chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Show me ___ orange. A: an. We use 'an' before a word that begins with a vowel letter. 'Orange' begins with o.

chunks.text: Q: Who is the head of the family? A: Father. Father is the head of the family.
chunks.source: Father is the head of the family.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who pays school fees for the children? A: Father. Father pays school fees.
chunks.source: Father pays school fees.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does mother do? A: She takes care of the family, cooks and cleans the home.. Mother takes care of the family, cooks and cleans the home.
chunks.source: Mother takes care of the family, cooks and cleans the home.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How do children help at home? A: They wash the dishes and sweep the compound.. Children wash the dishes, clean the house and sweep the compound.
chunks.source: Children wash the dishes, clean the house and sweep the compound.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The dog has a puppy. puppy - ___ A: puppies. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: puppies.
chunks.source: Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: puppies.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our baby is sick. baby - ___ A: babies. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: babies.
chunks.source: Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: babies.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The young lady is smart. lady - ___ A: ladies. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: ladies.
chunks.source: Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: ladies.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The knife has cut my finger. knife - ___ A: knives. Words ending in -fe change to -ves: knives.
chunks.source: Words ending in -fe change to -ves: knives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: That leaf is green. leaf - ___ A: leaves. Words ending in -f change to -ves: leaves.
chunks.source: Words ending in -f change to -ves: leaves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Daddy bought a loaf of bread. loaf - ___ A: loaves. Words ending in -f change to -ves: loaves.
chunks.source: Words ending in -f change to -ves: loaves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: That man has a good wife. man - ___ A: men. 'Men' is the plural of 'man'.
chunks.source: 'Men' is the plural of 'man'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: That man has a good wife. wife - ___ A: wives. Words ending in -fe change to -ves: wives.
chunks.source: Words ending in -fe change to -ves: wives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each word with its plural form. A: puppy: puppies; baby: babies; knife: knives; leaf: leaves. puppy-puppies, baby-babies, knife-knives, leaf-leaves.
chunks.source: puppy-puppies, baby-babies, knife-knives, leaf-leaves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: pot - ___ A: pots. Add -s: pots.
chunks.source: Add -s: pots.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: teacher - ___ A: teachers. Add -s: teachers.
chunks.source: Add -s: teachers.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: lorry - ___ A: lorries. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: lorries.
chunks.source: Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: lorries.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Tom and Jerry ___ cakes. A: have. Use 'have' with many people.
chunks.source: Use 'have' with many people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The boy is ___ to the house. (run) A: running. Use 'is' + verb-ing: is running. Double the n: running.
chunks.source: Use 'is' + verb-ing: is running. Double the n: running.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I am ___ a rope with my friends. (skip) A: skipping. Use 'am' + verb-ing: am skipping.
chunks.source: Use 'am' + verb-ing: am skipping.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We are ___ now. (dig) A: digging. Use 'are' + verb-ing: are digging.
chunks.source: Use 'are' + verb-ing: are digging.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I like ___. (swim) A: swimming. After 'like', use verb-ing: swimming.
chunks.source: After 'like', use verb-ing: swimming.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The baby ___ every night. (cry) A: cries. 'Every night' means always. With he/she, change y to -ies: cries.
chunks.source: 'Every night' means always. With he/she, change y to -ies: cries.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She ___ fish daily. (fry) A: fries. 'Daily' means always. With she, change y to -ies: fries.
chunks.source: 'Daily' means always. With she, change y to -ies: fries.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mummy ___ her baby every evening. (carry) A: carries. 'Every evening' means always. With she, change y to -ies: carries.
chunks.source: 'Every evening' means always. With she, change y to -ies: carries.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mummy ___ food every day. (cook) A: cooks. 'Every day' means always. With she, add -s: cooks.
chunks.source: 'Every day' means always. With she, add -s: cooks.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She ___ to town every Friday. (move) A: moves. 'Every Friday' means always. With she, add -s: moves.
chunks.source: 'Every Friday' means always. With she, add -s: moves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Daddy ___ his car every morning. (drive) A: drives. 'Every morning' means always. With he, add -s: drives.
chunks.source: 'Every morning' means always. With he, add -s: drives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each verb with its past tense. A: walk: walked; dance: danced; wash: washed; cook: cooked; pay: paid; boil: boiled. walk-walked, dance-danced, wash-washed, cook-cooked, pay-paid, boil-boiled.
chunks.source: walk-walked, dance-danced, wash-washed, cook-cooked, pay-paid, boil-boiled.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each verb with its past tense. A: cry: cried; dry: dried; fly: flew. cry-cried, dry-dried, fly-flew.
chunks.source: cry-cried, dry-dried, fly-flew.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The baby ___ loudly last night. (cry) A: cried. 'Last night' means the past. The past of 'cry' is 'cried'.
chunks.source: 'Last night' means the past. The past of 'cry' is 'cried'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He ___ to drive a car yesterday. (try) A: tried. 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'try' is 'tried'.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'try' is 'tried'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My uncle ___ two ladies last year. (marry) A: married. 'Last year' means the past. The past of 'marry' is 'married'.
chunks.source: 'Last year' means the past. The past of 'marry' is 'married'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I ___ my homework neatly. A: do. Use 'do' with I.
chunks.source: Use 'do' with I.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Joan and Mary ___ their work quickly. A: do. Use 'do' with many people.
chunks.source: Use 'do' with many people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She ___ her work well. A: does. Use 'does' with she.
chunks.source: Use 'does' with she.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Tom ___ his modelling daily. A: does. Use 'does' with he.
chunks.source: Use 'does' with he.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mary ___ not at home yesterday. A: was. 'Yesterday' means the past. Use 'was' with one person.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' means the past. Use 'was' with one person.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The bird is flying ___ the tree. (under, over, in, near) A: over. The bird is flying over the tree.
chunks.source: The bird is flying over the tree.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The fish is ___ the dish. (under, over, in, on) A: in. The fish is in the dish.
chunks.source: The fish is in the dish.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The cat is ___ the ball. (under, in, near, on) A: near. The cat is near the ball.
chunks.source: The cat is near the ball.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The snake is ___ the bed. (under, over, in, on) A: under. The snake is under the bed.
chunks.source: The snake is under the bed.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is an adjective? 'That cup is dirty.' A: dirty. 'Dirty' describes the cup. Describing words are adjectives.
chunks.source: 'Dirty' describes the cup. Describing words are adjectives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is an adjective? 'Jonah is a fat boy.' A: fat. 'Fat' describes Jonah. Describing words are adjectives.
chunks.source: 'Fat' describes Jonah. Describing words are adjectives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is an adjective? 'Golola is a strong man.' A: strong. 'Strong' describes the man. Describing words are adjectives.
chunks.source: 'Strong' describes the man. Describing words are adjectives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is an adjective? 'The wet shirt is down.' A: wet. 'Wet' describes the shirt. Describing words are adjectives.
chunks.source: 'Wet' describes the shirt. Describing words are adjectives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is an adjective? 'Pigs are fat animals.' A: fat. 'Fat' describes the pigs. Describing words are adjectives.
chunks.source: 'Fat' describes the pigs. Describing words are adjectives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: taller - ___ A: shorter. 'Shorter' is the opposite of 'taller'.
chunks.source: 'Shorter' is the opposite of 'taller'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: longest - ___ A: shortest. 'Shortest' is the opposite of 'longest'.
chunks.source: 'Shortest' is the opposite of 'longest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Sort the words into Comparative and Superlative. A: Comparative: shorter,thinner,smarter,hotter; Superlative: shortest,thinnest,smartest,hottest. Comparatives end in -er and compare two. Superlatives end in -est and compare many.
chunks.source: Comparatives end in -er and compare two. Superlatives end in -est and compare many.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each word with its comparative. A: short: shorter; thin: thinner; smart: smarter; hot: hotter. short-shorter, thin-thinner, smart-smarter, hot-hotter.
chunks.source: short-shorter, thin-thinner, smart-smarter, hot-hotter.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Musa has come late to school. late - ___ A: early. 'Early' is the opposite of 'late'.
chunks.source: 'Early' is the opposite of 'late'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The girl has long hair. long - ___ A: short. 'Short' is the opposite of 'long'.
chunks.source: 'Short' is the opposite of 'long'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mukisa is shorter than Malcom. shorter - ___ A: taller. 'Taller' is the opposite of 'shorter'.
chunks.source: 'Taller' is the opposite of 'shorter'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: man - ___ A: woman. 'Woman' is the opposite of 'man'.
chunks.source: 'Woman' is the opposite of 'man'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: girl - ___ A: boy. 'Boy' is the opposite of 'girl'.
chunks.source: 'Boy' is the opposite of 'girl'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. A: I have a book, a pencil and a rubber.. Use a comma to separate things in a list.
chunks.source: Use a comma to separate things in a list.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. A: Mary has ice cream, soda and safi juice.. Use a comma to separate things in a list.
chunks.source: Use a comma to separate things in a list.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correctly written sentence. A: I was born in April.. 'I' is always capital. Months begin with a capital letter: April.
chunks.source: 'I' is always capital. Months begin with a capital letter: April.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correctly written sentence. A: Today is Friday.. Days of the week begin with a capital letter: Friday.
chunks.source: Days of the week begin with a capital letter: Friday.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. A: What is your name?. A question ends with a question mark. A sentence begins with a capital letter.
chunks.source: A question ends with a question mark. A sentence begins with a capital letter.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correctly written sentence. A: Her name is Justine.. Names begin with a capital letter: Justine.
chunks.source: Names begin with a capital letter: Justine.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correctly written sentence. A: Kampala is a big city.. Place names begin with a capital letter: Kampala.
chunks.source: Place names begin with a capital letter: Kampala.

chunks.text: Q: Match each word with its short form. A: School: Sch; Doctor: Dr; Hospital: Hosp; Road: Rd; Number: No.. School-Sch, Doctor-Dr, Hospital-Hosp, Road-Rd, Number-No.
chunks.source: School-Sch, Doctor-Dr, Hospital-Hosp, Road-Rd, Number-No.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each word with its short form. A: January: Jan; September: Sept; August: Aug; Thursday: Thu. January-Jan, September-Sept, August-Aug, Thursday-Thu.
chunks.source: January-Jan, September-Sept, August-Aug, Thursday-Thu.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each short form with its full form. A: H/M: Headmaster; Mr.: Mister; Dr.: Doctor; Tr.: Teacher. H/M-Headmaster, Mr.-Mister, Dr.-Doctor, Tr.-Teacher.
chunks.source: H/M-Headmaster, Mr.-Mister, Dr.-Doctor, Tr.-Teacher.

chunks.text: Q: Match each word with its short form. A: I am: I'm; Doctor: Dr.; January: Jan.. I am-I'm, Doctor-Dr., January-Jan.
chunks.source: I am-I'm, Doctor-Dr., January-Jan.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: His ___ is sick. (son, sun) A: son. 'Son' is a boy child. 'Sun' is in the sky.
chunks.source: 'Son' is a boy child. 'Sun' is in the sky.

chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence: riding / a / He / is / bicycle. A: He, is, riding, a, bicycle.. He is riding a bicycle.
chunks.source: He is riding a bicycle.

chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence: a / goat / has / She. A: She, has, a, goat.. She has a goat.
chunks.source: She has a goat.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence: Jane / ball / has. A: Jane, has, a, ball.. Jane has a ball.
chunks.source: Jane has a ball.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence: big / Our / is / house. A: Our, house, is, big.. Our house is big.
chunks.source: Our house is big.

chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence: writing / My / is / father. A: My, father, is, writing.. My father is writing.
chunks.source: My father is writing.

chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence: book / A / on / is / a / chair. A: A, book, is, on, a, chair.. A book is on a chair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: When does grandmother go to the garden? A: Every Monday. Grandmother goes to the garden every Monday.
chunks.source: Grandmother goes to the garden every Monday.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Grandfather ___ the crops during the dry season. A: waters. Grandfather waters the crops.
chunks.source: Grandfather waters the crops.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Grandmother sells the harvested crops to get ___. A: money. She sells the crops to get money.
chunks.source: She sells the crops to get money.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who harvests the crops? A: The grandchildren. The grandchildren harvest the crops.
chunks.source: The grandchildren harvest the crops.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name one crop grandmother plants in the garden. A: beans. She plants beans, maize and cassava.
chunks.source: She plants beans, maize and cassava.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where does Bob keep his toys? A: in a cupboard. Bob has a cupboard full of toys.
chunks.source: Bob has a cupboard full of toys.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Bob likes his ___ most. A: train. The toy he likes most is the train.
chunks.source: The toy he likes most is the train.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the oldest toy? A: the bear. The oldest toy is the bear.
chunks.source: The oldest toy is the bear.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why does Bob like the train most? A: because it is new. He likes the train because it is new.
chunks.source: He likes the train because it is new.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The bus is yellow. A: True. The bus is yellow.
chunks.source: The bus is yellow.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the title of the story. A: Jet the Dog. The title is 'Jet the Dog'.
chunks.source: The title is 'Jet the Dog'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How old is Rita? A: six. Rita is six years old.
chunks.source: Rita is six years old.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rita lives with her father and ___. A: mother. She lives with her father and mother.
chunks.source: She lives with her father and mother.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does the dog do? A: guards the home. The dog guards the home.
chunks.source: The dog guards the home.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who feeds the dog? A: Rita's brother. Rita's brother feeds the dog.
chunks.source: Rita's brother feeds the dog.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The cat caught a mouse. mouse - ___ A: mice. The plural of 'mouse' is 'mice'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'mouse' is 'mice'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mr. Mukasa is a strong man. man - ___ A: men. The plural of 'man' is 'men'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'man' is 'men'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: An ox is used for ploughing. ox - ___ A: oxen. The plural of 'ox' is 'oxen'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'ox' is 'oxen'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A goose is sitting on the tree. goose - ___ A: geese. The plural of 'goose' is 'geese'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'goose' is 'geese'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: teeth - ___ (singular) A: tooth. The singular of 'teeth' is 'tooth'.
chunks.source: The singular of 'teeth' is 'tooth'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: oxen - ___ (singular) A: ox. The singular of 'oxen' is 'ox'.
chunks.source: The singular of 'oxen' is 'ox'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: children - ___ (singular) A: child. The singular of 'children' is 'child'.
chunks.source: The singular of 'children' is 'child'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: women - ___ (singular) A: woman. The singular of 'women' is 'woman'.
chunks.source: The singular of 'women' is 'woman'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: These are ___. (bench) A: benches. Words ending in ch add -es: benches.
chunks.source: Words ending in ch add -es: benches.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We have four ___ in our kitchen. (knife) A: knives. Words ending in -fe change to -ves: knives.
chunks.source: Words ending in -fe change to -ves: knives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mr. Musoke bought six ___ last year. (lorry) A: lorries. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: lorries.
chunks.source: Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: lorries.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each word with its plural form. A: mouse: mice; man: men; ox: oxen; goose: geese. mouse-mice, man-men, ox-oxen, goose-geese.
chunks.source: mouse-mice, man-men, ox-oxen, goose-geese.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A cow lives in a kraal. A lion lives in a ___. A: den. A lion lives in a den.
chunks.source: A lion lives in a den.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A driver drives a car. A ___ flies an aeroplane. A: pilot. A pilot flies an aeroplane.
chunks.source: A pilot flies an aeroplane.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ___ of Buganda is very rich. (queen - male) A: king. The male of a queen is a king.
chunks.source: The male of a queen is a king.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ___ is brave. (lioness - male) A: lion. The male of a lioness is a lion.
chunks.source: The male of a lioness is a lion.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We get meat from a ___. (cow - male) A: bull. The male of a cow is a bull.

chunks.text: Q: Match each female word with its male word. A: bitch: dog; princess: prince; tigress: tiger; she: he. bitch-dog, princess-prince, tigress-tiger, she-he.
chunks.source: bitch-dog, princess-prince, tigress-tiger, she-he.

chunks.text: Q: That is Martha's dress. It is ___. A: hers. Use 'hers' for what belongs to a girl.
chunks.source: Use 'hers' for what belongs to a girl.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Those are my books. They are ___. A: mine. Use 'mine' for what belongs to me.
chunks.source: Use 'mine' for what belongs to me.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: This is our classroom. It is ___. A: ours. Use 'ours' for what belongs to us.
chunks.source: Use 'ours' for what belongs to us.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He ___ under the tree yesterday. (sit) A: sat. 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'sit' is 'sat'.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'sit' is 'sat'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The teacher ___ the books in the shelf last week. (put) A: put. 'Last week' means the past. The past of 'put' is 'put'.
chunks.source: 'Last week' means the past. The past of 'put' is 'put'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My father ___ to Nairobi last year. (drive) A: drove. 'Last year' means the past. The past of 'drive' is 'drove'.
chunks.source: 'Last year' means the past. The past of 'drive' is 'drove'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct sentence. A: They do my homework daily.. Use 'do' with they.
chunks.source: Use 'do' with they.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct sentence. A: Tom does neat work always.. Use 'does' with he.
chunks.source: Use 'does' with he.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct sentence. A: I do my class work so well.. Use 'do' with I.
chunks.source: Use 'do' with I.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mark is ___ than Molly. (short) A: shorter. Use -er to compare two: shorter.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Here is a ___ ruler. (short) A: short. No comparing here. Use the word itself: short.
chunks.source: No comparing here. Use the word itself: short.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Namuli is the ___ girl in our class. (fat) A: fattest. Use -est to compare many: fattest.
chunks.source: Use -est to compare many: fattest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: This water is as cold as ___. A: ice. We say 'as cold as ice'.
chunks.source: We say 'as cold as ice'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My blouse is as ___ as snow. A: white. We say 'as white as snow'.
chunks.source: We say 'as white as snow'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our chalkboard is as black as ___. A: charcoal. We say 'as black as charcoal'.
chunks.source: We say 'as black as charcoal'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Thin, ___, thinnest A: thinner. thin - thinner - thinnest.
chunks.source: thin - thinner - thinnest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Smart, smarter, ___ A: smartest. smart - smarter - smartest.
chunks.source: smart - smarter - smartest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ___, hotter, hottest A: hot. hot - hotter - hottest.
chunks.source: hot - hotter - hottest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. A: Is this your book?. A question ends with a question mark.
chunks.source: A question ends with a question mark.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. A: Mariam has a dress, shoes, a bag and a skirt.. Use a comma to separate things in a list.
chunks.source: Use a comma to separate things in a list.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My father was born in September. Short form: ___ A: Sept.. The short form of 'September' is 'Sept.'.
chunks.source: The short form of 'September' is 'Sept.'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Thursday is the fifth day of the week. Short form: ___ A: Thu.. The short form of 'Thursday' is 'Thu.'.
chunks.source: The short form of 'Thursday' is 'Thu.'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Jonah cannot play with me. Short form: ___ A: can't. The short form of 'cannot' is "can't".

chunks.source: 'Every Sunday' means always. With she, add -es: goes.

chunks.text: Q: Christine ___ in her book every Wednesday. (write) A: writes. 'Every Wednesday' means always. With she, add -s: writes.
chunks.source: 'Every Wednesday' means always. With she, add -s: writes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He ___ the Bible every Saturday. (read) A: reads. 'Every Saturday' means always. With he, add -s: reads.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She ___ her homework every evening. (do) A: does. With she, 'do' becomes 'does'.
chunks.source: With she, 'do' becomes 'does'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They ___ their tests every end of a topic. (do) A: do. With they, use 'do' (no -s).
chunks.source: With they, use 'do' (no -s).

chunks.text: Q: He ___ the room every morning. (sweep) A: sweeps. 'Every morning' means always. With he, add -s: sweeps.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He ___ back home last night. (walk) A: walked. 'Last night' means the past. The past of 'walk' is 'walked'.
chunks.source: 'Last night' means the past. The past of 'walk' is 'walked'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mother ___ a cake yesterday. (bake) A: baked. 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'bake' is 'baked'.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'bake' is 'baked'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Esther ___ an old woman yesterday. (help) A: helped. 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'help' is 'helped'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She ___ at me yesterday. (look) A: looked. 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'look' is 'looked'.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'look' is 'looked'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They ___ to their new place. (move) A: moved. The past of 'move' is 'moved'.
chunks.source: The past of 'move' is 'moved'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Musa goes to school ___ a taxi. A: by. We travel 'by' taxi, 'by' bus, 'by' car.
chunks.source: We travel 'by' taxi, 'by' bus, 'by' car.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The police officer is looking ___ the soldier. A: at. We look 'at' a person.
chunks.source: We look 'at' a person.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Gloria comes to school ___ foot. A: on. We come 'on' foot when we walk.
chunks.source: We come 'on' foot when we walk.

chunks.text: Q: long, ___, longest A: longer. long - longer - longest.

chunks.text: Q: ___, colder, coldest A: cold. cold - colder - coldest.

chunks.text: Q: quick - ___ A: slow. 'Slow' is the opposite of 'quick'.
chunks.source: 'Slow' is the opposite of 'quick'.

chunks.text: Q: wet - ___ A: dry. 'Dry' is the opposite of 'wet'.

chunks.source: 'Cold' is the opposite of 'hot'.

chunks.text: Q: James has a clean shirt. clean - ___ A: dirty. 'Dirty' is the opposite of 'clean'.

chunks.source: 'Tall' is the opposite of 'short'.

chunks.text: Q: Daniel's shirt is wet. wet - ___ A: dry. 'Dry' is the opposite of 'wet'.
chunks.source: 'Dry' is the opposite of 'wet'.

chunks.text: Q: hand + bag = ___ A: handbag. Join the two words: handbag.
chunks.source: Join the two words: handbag.

chunks.text: Q: tea + time = ___ A: teatime. Join the two words: teatime.

chunks.subject: English

chunks.text: Q: A vase for flowers is called a ___. A: flower vase. A vase for flowers is a flower vase.

chunks.text: Q: A small pot with ink in it is called an ___. A: inkpot. A small pot for ink is an inkpot.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A board which is black is called a ___. A: blackboard. A black board is a blackboard.

chunks.text: Q: The dog has a puppy. puppy - ___ A: puppies. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: puppies.
chunks.source: Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: puppies.

chunks.text: Q: Our baby is sick. baby - ___ A: babies. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: babies.

chunks.text: Q: The young lady is smart. lady - ___ A: ladies. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: ladies.
chunks.source: Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: ladies.

chunks.text: Q: The knife has cut my finger. knife - ___ A: knives. Words ending in -fe change to -ves: knives.

chunks.text: Q: The boy is ___ to the house. (run) A: running. Use 'is' + verb-ing: is running. Double the n: running.
chunks.source: Use 'is' + verb-ing: is running. Double the n: running.

chunks.text: Q: I am ___ a rope with my friends. (skip) A: skipping. Use 'am' + verb-ing: am skipping.
chunks.source: Use 'am' + verb-ing: am skipping.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We are ___ now. (dig) A: digging. Use 'are' + verb-ing: are digging.
chunks.source: Use 'are' + verb-ing: are digging.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I like ___. (swim) A: swimming. After 'like', use verb-ing: swimming.
chunks.source: After 'like', use verb-ing: swimming.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The baby ___ every night. (cry) A: cries. 'Every night' means always. With he/she, change y to -ies: cries.

chunks.text: Q: She ___ fish daily. (fry) A: fries. 'Daily' means always. With she, change y to -ies: fries.

chunks.text: Q: Mummy ___ food every day. (cook) A: cooks. 'Every day' means always. With she, add -s: cooks.

chunks.text: Q: He ___ to drive a car yesterday. (try) A: tried. 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'try' is 'tried'.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'try' is 'tried'.

chunks.text: Q: My uncle ___ two ladies last year. (marry) A: married. 'Last year' means the past. The past of 'marry' is 'married'.

chunks.source: 'Shortest' is the opposite of 'longest'.

chunks.source: The plural of 'ox' is 'oxen'.

chunks.text: Q: teeth - ___ (singular) A: tooth. The singular of 'teeth' is 'tooth'.

chunks.text: Q: Mark is ___ than Molly. (short) A: shorter. Use -er to compare two: shorter.

chunks.text: Q: Namuli is the ___ girl in our class. (fat) A: fattest. Use -est to compare many: fattest.

chunks.text: Q: Show me an orange. A: True. We use 'an' before a word that begins with a vowel letter. 'Orange' begins with o.

chunks.text: Q: Mary ate an apple. A: True. 'Apple' begins with the vowel letter a, so we use 'an'.

chunks.text: Q: Tom has a new toy car. A: True. 'New' begins with the consonant letter n, so we use 'a'.

chunks.text: Q: I can see an elephant. A: True. 'Elephant' begins with the vowel letter e, so we use 'an'.

chunks.text: Q: I have an apple. A: True. 'Apple' begins with the vowel letter a, so we use 'an'.

chunks.text: Q: Our classes are very big. (class) A: True. The plural of 'class' is 'classes'.

chunks.text: Q: brush - brushes A: True. Words ending in sh add -es: brushes.

chunks.text: Q: Mary is a good girl. She is a good girl. A: True. Use 'She' for a girl.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He is milking a cow. (milk) A: True. Use 'is' + verb-ing for what is happening now: is milking.
chunks.source: Use 'is' + verb-ing for what is happening now: is milking.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The girls are reading story books. (read) A: True. Use 'are' + verb-ing: are reading.
chunks.source: Use 'are' + verb-ing: are reading.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Deborah goes to church every Sunday. (go) A: True. 'Every Sunday' means always. With she, add -es: goes.
chunks.source: 'Every Sunday' means always. With she, add -es: goes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Tom plays with the ball every day. (play) A: True. 'Every day' means always. With he, add -s: plays.
chunks.source: 'Every day' means always. With he, add -s: plays.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Christine writes in her book every Wednesday. (write) A: True. 'Every Wednesday' means always. With she, add -s: writes.
chunks.source: 'Every Wednesday' means always. With she, add -s: writes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He reads the Bible every Saturday. (read) A: True. 'Every Saturday' means always. With he, add -s: reads.
chunks.source: 'Every Saturday' means always. With he, add -s: reads.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She does her homework every evening. (do) A: True. With she, 'do' becomes 'does'.
chunks.source: With she, 'do' becomes 'does'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They do their tests every end of a topic. (do) A: True. With they, use 'do' (no -s).
chunks.source: With they, use 'do' (no -s).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He sweeps the room every morning. (sweep) A: True. 'Every morning' means always. With he, add -s: sweeps.
chunks.source: 'Every morning' means always. With he, add -s: sweeps.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He walked back home last night. (walk) A: True. 'Last night' means the past. The past of 'walk' is 'walked'.
chunks.source: 'Last night' means the past. The past of 'walk' is 'walked'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mother baked a cake yesterday. (bake) A: True. 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'bake' is 'baked'.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'bake' is 'baked'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Esther helped an old woman yesterday. (help) A: True. 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'help' is 'helped'.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'help' is 'helped'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She looked at me yesterday. (look) A: True. 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'look' is 'looked'.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'look' is 'looked'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They moved to their new place. (move) A: True. The past of 'move' is 'moved'.
chunks.source: The past of 'move' is 'moved'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The girls were reading their books. A: True. Use 'were' with many (plural) people.
chunks.source: Use 'were' with many (plural) people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Was he a good boy? A: True. Use 'Was' to ask about one person in the past.
chunks.source: Use 'Was' to ask about one person in the past.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My shirt was very nice. A: True. Use 'was' with one thing in the past.
chunks.source: Use 'was' with one thing in the past.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Were they learning English? A: True. Use 'Were' to ask about many people in the past.
chunks.source: Use 'Were' to ask about many people in the past.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Musa goes to school by a taxi. A: True. We travel 'by' taxi, 'by' bus, 'by' car.
chunks.source: We travel 'by' taxi, 'by' bus, 'by' car.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The police officer is looking at the soldier. A: True. We look 'at' a person.
chunks.source: We look 'at' a person.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Gloria comes to school on foot. A: True. We come 'on' foot when we walk.
chunks.source: We come 'on' foot when we walk.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: long, longer, longest A: True. long - longer - longest.
chunks.source: long - longer - longest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: old, older, oldest A: True. old - older - oldest.
chunks.source: old - older - oldest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: cold, colder, coldest A: True. cold - colder - coldest.
chunks.source: cold - colder - coldest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: quick - slow A: True. 'Slow' is the opposite of 'quick'.
chunks.source: 'Slow' is the opposite of 'quick'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: wet - dry A: True. 'Dry' is the opposite of 'wet'.
chunks.source: 'Dry' is the opposite of 'wet'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: thin - thick A: True. 'Thick' is the opposite of 'thin'.
chunks.source: 'Thick' is the opposite of 'thin'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: wrong - right A: True. 'Right' is the opposite of 'wrong'.
chunks.source: 'Right' is the opposite of 'wrong'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: hot - cold A: True. 'Cold' is the opposite of 'hot'.
chunks.source: 'Cold' is the opposite of 'hot'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: James has a clean shirt. clean - dirty A: True. 'Dirty' is the opposite of 'clean'.
chunks.source: 'Dirty' is the opposite of 'clean'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our school has tall buildings. tall - short A: True. 'Short' is the opposite of 'tall'.
chunks.source: 'Short' is the opposite of 'tall'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She has a bag full of books. full - empty A: True. 'Empty' is the opposite of 'full'.
chunks.source: 'Empty' is the opposite of 'full'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My father is a poor man. poor - rich A: True. 'Rich' is the opposite of 'poor'.
chunks.source: 'Rich' is the opposite of 'poor'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The short boy is in the house. short - tall A: True. 'Tall' is the opposite of 'short'.
chunks.source: 'Tall' is the opposite of 'short'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Daniel's shirt is wet. wet - dry A: True. 'Dry' is the opposite of 'wet'.
chunks.source: 'Dry' is the opposite of 'wet'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: hand + bag = handbag A: True. Join the two words: handbag.
chunks.source: Join the two words: handbag.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: tea + time = teatime A: True. Join the two words: teatime.
chunks.source: Join the two words: teatime.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ear + ring = earring A: True. Join the two words: earring.
chunks.source: Join the two words: earring.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A vase for flowers is called a flower vase. A: True. A vase for flowers is a flower vase.
chunks.source: A vase for flowers is a flower vase.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A small pot with ink in it is called an inkpot. A: True. A small pot for ink is an inkpot.
chunks.source: A small pot for ink is an inkpot.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A board which is black is called a blackboard. A: True. A black board is a blackboard.
chunks.source: A black board is a blackboard.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The dog has a puppy. puppy - puppies A: True. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: puppies.
chunks.source: Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: puppies.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our baby is sick. baby - babies A: True. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: babies.
chunks.source: Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: babies.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The young lady is smart. lady - ladies A: True. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: ladies.
chunks.source: Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: ladies.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The knife has cut my finger. knife - knives A: True. Words ending in -fe change to -ves: knives.
chunks.source: Words ending in -fe change to -ves: knives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: That leaf is green. leaf - leaves A: True. Words ending in -f change to -ves: leaves.
chunks.source: Words ending in -f change to -ves: leaves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: That man has a good wife. man - men A: True. 'Men' is the plural of 'man'.
chunks.source: 'Men' is the plural of 'man'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: That man has a good wife. wife - wives A: True. Words ending in -fe change to -ves: wives.
chunks.source: Words ending in -fe change to -ves: wives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: pot - pots A: True. Add -s: pots.
chunks.source: Add -s: pots.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: teacher - teachers A: True. Add -s: teachers.
chunks.source: Add -s: teachers.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: lorry - lorries A: True. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: lorries.
chunks.source: Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: lorries.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Tom and Jerry have cakes. A: True. Use 'have' with many people.
chunks.source: Use 'have' with many people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The boy is running to the house. (run) A: True. Use 'is' + verb-ing: is running. Double the n: running.
chunks.source: Use 'is' + verb-ing: is running. Double the n: running.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I am skipping a rope with my friends. (skip) A: True. Use 'am' + verb-ing: am skipping.
chunks.source: Use 'am' + verb-ing: am skipping.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We are digging now. (dig) A: True. Use 'are' + verb-ing: are digging.
chunks.source: Use 'are' + verb-ing: are digging.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I like swimming. (swim) A: True. After 'like', use verb-ing: swimming.
chunks.source: After 'like', use verb-ing: swimming.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The baby cries every night. (cry) A: True. 'Every night' means always. With he/she, change y to -ies: cries.
chunks.source: 'Every night' means always. With he/she, change y to -ies: cries.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She fries fish daily. (fry) A: True. 'Daily' means always. With she, change y to -ies: fries.
chunks.source: 'Daily' means always. With she, change y to -ies: fries.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mummy carries her baby every evening. (carry) A: True. 'Every evening' means always. With she, change y to -ies: carries.
chunks.source: 'Every evening' means always. With she, change y to -ies: carries.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mummy cooks food every day. (cook) A: True. 'Every day' means always. With she, add -s: cooks.
chunks.source: 'Every day' means always. With she, add -s: cooks.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She moves to town every Friday. (move) A: True. 'Every Friday' means always. With she, add -s: moves.
chunks.source: 'Every Friday' means always. With she, add -s: moves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Daddy drives his car every morning. (drive) A: True. 'Every morning' means always. With he, add -s: drives.
chunks.source: 'Every morning' means always. With he, add -s: drives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The baby cried loudly last night. (cry) A: True. 'Last night' means the past. The past of 'cry' is 'cried'.
chunks.source: 'Last night' means the past. The past of 'cry' is 'cried'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He tried to drive a car yesterday. (try) A: True. 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'try' is 'tried'.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'try' is 'tried'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My uncle married two ladies last year. (marry) A: True. 'Last year' means the past. The past of 'marry' is 'married'.
chunks.source: 'Last year' means the past. The past of 'marry' is 'married'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I do my homework neatly. A: True. Use 'do' with I.
chunks.source: Use 'do' with I.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Joan and Mary do their work quickly. A: True. Use 'do' with many people.
chunks.source: Use 'do' with many people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She does her work well. A: True. Use 'does' with she.
chunks.source: Use 'does' with she.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Tom does his modelling daily. A: True. Use 'does' with he.
chunks.source: Use 'does' with he.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mary was not at home yesterday. A: True. 'Yesterday' means the past. Use 'was' with one person.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' means the past. Use 'was' with one person.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: taller - shorter A: True. 'Shorter' is the opposite of 'taller'.
chunks.source: 'Shorter' is the opposite of 'taller'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: longest - shortest A: True. 'Shortest' is the opposite of 'longest'.
chunks.source: 'Shortest' is the opposite of 'longest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Musa has come late to school. late - early A: True. 'Early' is the opposite of 'late'.
chunks.source: 'Early' is the opposite of 'late'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The girl has long hair. long - short A: True. 'Short' is the opposite of 'long'.
chunks.source: 'Short' is the opposite of 'long'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mukisa is shorter than Malcom. shorter - taller A: True. 'Taller' is the opposite of 'shorter'.
chunks.source: 'Taller' is the opposite of 'shorter'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: man - woman A: True. 'Woman' is the opposite of 'man'.
chunks.source: 'Woman' is the opposite of 'man'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: girl - boy A: True. 'Boy' is the opposite of 'girl'.
chunks.source: 'Boy' is the opposite of 'girl'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The cat caught a mouse. mouse - mice A: True. The plural of 'mouse' is 'mice'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'mouse' is 'mice'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mr. Mukasa is a strong man. man - men A: True. The plural of 'man' is 'men'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'man' is 'men'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: An ox is used for ploughing. ox - oxen A: True. The plural of 'ox' is 'oxen'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'ox' is 'oxen'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A goose is sitting on the tree. goose - geese A: True. The plural of 'goose' is 'geese'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'goose' is 'geese'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: teeth - tooth (singular) A: True. The singular of 'teeth' is 'tooth'.
chunks.source: The singular of 'teeth' is 'tooth'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: oxen - ox (singular) A: True. The singular of 'oxen' is 'ox'.
chunks.source: The singular of 'oxen' is 'ox'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: children - child (singular) A: True. The singular of 'children' is 'child'.
chunks.source: The singular of 'children' is 'child'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: women - woman (singular) A: True. The singular of 'women' is 'woman'.
chunks.source: The singular of 'women' is 'woman'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: These are benches. (bench) A: True. Words ending in ch add -es: benches.
chunks.source: Words ending in ch add -es: benches.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We have four knives in our kitchen. (knife) A: True. Words ending in -fe change to -ves: knives.
chunks.source: Words ending in -fe change to -ves: knives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mr. Musoke bought six lorries last year. (lorry) A: True. Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: lorries.
chunks.source: Words ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: lorries.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The king of Buganda is very rich. (queen - male) A: True. The male of a queen is a king.
chunks.source: The male of a queen is a king.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The lion is brave. (lioness - male) A: True. The male of a lioness is a lion.
chunks.source: The male of a lioness is a lion.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We get meat from a bull. (cow - male) A: True. The male of a cow is a bull.
chunks.source: The male of a cow is a bull.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He married under the tree yesterday. (sit) A: False. 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'sit' is 'sat'.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' means the past. The past of 'sit' is 'sat'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The teacher baked the books in the shelf last week. (put) A: False. 'Last week' means the past. The past of 'put' is 'put'.
chunks.source: 'Last week' means the past. The past of 'put' is 'put'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My father {'walk': 'walked', 'dance': 'danced', 'wash': 'washed', 'cook': 'cooked', 'pay': 'paid', 'boil': 'boiled'} to Nairobi last year. (drive) A: False. 'Last year' means the past. The past of 'drive' is 'drove'.
chunks.source: 'Last year' means the past. The past of 'drive' is 'drove'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mark is hot than Molly. (short) A: False. Use -er to compare two: shorter.
chunks.source: Use -er to compare two: shorter.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Here is a {'long': 'longer', 'old': 'older', 'cold': 'colder'} ruler. (short) A: False. No comparing here. Use the word itself: short.
chunks.source: No comparing here. Use the word itself: short.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Namuli is the short girl in our class. (fat) A: False. Use -est to compare many: fattest.
chunks.source: Use -est to compare many: fattest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: This water is as cold as hot. A: False. We say 'as cold as ice'.
chunks.source: We say 'as cold as ice'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My blouse is as {'Comparative': ['shorter', 'thinner', 'smarter', 'hotter'], 'Superlative': ['shortest', 'thinnest', 'smartest', 'hottest']} as snow. A: False. We say 'as white as snow'.
chunks.source: We say 'as white as snow'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our chalkboard is as black as white. A: False. We say 'as black as charcoal'.
chunks.source: We say 'as black as charcoal'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Thin, shorter, thinnest A: False. thin - thinner - thinnest.
chunks.source: thin - thinner - thinnest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Smart, smarter, shorter A: False. smart - smarter - smartest.
chunks.source: smart - smarter - smartest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: thinner, hotter, hottest A: False. hot - hotter - hottest.
chunks.source: hot - hotter - hottest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My father was born in September. Short form: {"Let's": 'Let us', 'Dec.': 'December', "Won't": 'Will not'} A: False. The short form of 'September' is 'Sept.'.
chunks.source: The short form of 'September' is 'Sept.'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Thursday is the fifth day of the week. Short form: {"Let's": 'Let us', 'Dec.': 'December', "Won't": 'Will not'} A: False. The short form of 'Thursday' is 'Thu.'.
chunks.source: The short form of 'Thursday' is 'Thu.'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Jonah cannot play with me. Short form: {'H/M': 'Headmaster', 'Mr.': 'Mister', 'Dr.': 'Doctor', 'Tr.': 'Teacher'} A: False. The short form of 'cannot' is "can't".
chunks.source: The short form of 'cannot' is "can't".

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A egg is in the nest. A: False. We use 'an' before a word that begins with a vowel letter. 'Egg' begins with e.
chunks.source: We use 'an' before a word that begins with a vowel letter. 'Egg' begins with e.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Has she got a pen? A: True. Use 'Has' with she.
chunks.source: Use 'Has' with she.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The bird is flying under the tree. (under, over, in, near) A: False. The bird is flying over the tree.
chunks.source: The bird is flying over the tree.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The fish is in the dish. (under, over, in, on) A: True. The fish is in the dish.
chunks.source: The fish is in the dish.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The cat is under the ball. (under, in, near, on) A: False. The cat is near the ball.
chunks.source: The cat is near the ball.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The snake is under the bed. (under, over, in, on) A: True. The snake is under the bed.
chunks.source: The snake is under the bed.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: His sun is sick. (son, sun) A: False. 'Son' is a boy child. 'Sun' is in the sky.
chunks.source: 'Son' is a boy child. 'Sun' is in the sky.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A cow lives in a kraal. A lion lives in a den. A: True. A lion lives in a den.
chunks.source: A lion lives in a den.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A driver drives a car. A sailor flies an aeroplane. A: False. A pilot flies an aeroplane.
chunks.source: A pilot flies an aeroplane.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A ship sails on water. A: True. 'Ship' is a boat. 'Sheep' is an animal.
chunks.source: 'Ship' is a boat. 'Sheep' is an animal.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We get meet from animals. A: False. 'Meat' is food. 'Meet' is to see someone.
chunks.source: 'Meat' is food. 'Meet' is to see someone.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My grandmother always sit on the mat. A: True. 'Sit' is the doing word. 'Seat' is a chair.
chunks.source: 'Sit' is the doing word. 'Seat' is a chair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Show me a orange. A: False. We use 'an' before a word that begins with a vowel letter. 'Orange' begins with o.
chunks.source: We use 'an' before a word that begins with a vowel letter. 'Orange' begins with o.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Bring me An book. A: False. We use 'a' before a word that begins with a consonant letter. 'Book' begins with b.
chunks.source: We use 'a' before a word that begins with a consonant letter. 'Book' begins with b.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Bring me An axe. A: False. We use 'an' before a word that begins with a vowel letter. 'Axe' begins with a.
chunks.source: We use 'an' before a word that begins with a vowel letter. 'Axe' begins with a.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mother has a orange. A: False. 'Orange' begins with the vowel letter o, so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'Orange' begins with the vowel letter o, so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She is playing with An doll. A: False. 'Doll' begins with the consonant letter d, so we use 'a'.
chunks.source: 'Doll' begins with the consonant letter d, so we use 'a'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mary ate a apple. A: False. 'Apple' begins with the vowel letter a, so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'Apple' begins with the vowel letter a, so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Tom has An new toy car. A: False. 'New' begins with the consonant letter n, so we use 'a'.
chunks.source: 'New' begins with the consonant letter n, so we use 'a'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I can see An elephant. A: False. 'Elephant' begins with the vowel letter e, so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'Elephant' begins with the vowel letter e, so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I have An apple. A: False. 'Apple' begins with the vowel letter a, so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'Apple' begins with the vowel letter a, so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He has An umbrella. A: False. 'Umbrella' begins with the vowel letter u, so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'Umbrella' begins with the vowel letter u, so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: a arrow A: False. 'Arrow' begins with the vowel letter a.
