chunks.text: Q: How many fingers do 2 children have? ___ A: 20. Each child has 10 fingers, so 2 children have 20 fingers.
chunks.source: Each child has 10 fingers, so 2 children have 20 fingers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the product of 3 and 2? A: 6. 3 x 2 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many days make a week? A: 7. There are 7 days in a week.
chunks.source: There are 7 days in a week.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the missing number: 5, 6, 7, ____? A: 8. Count on from 5: 5, 6, 7, 8.
chunks.source: Count on from 5: 5, 6, 7, 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the missing number: 13, 14, ____?, 16 A: 15. Count on: 13, 14, 15, 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the missing number: 15, ____?, 17, 18 A: 16. Count on: 15, 16, 17, 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the number after 18: 18, ____? A: 19. The number after 18 is 19.
chunks.source: The number after 18 is 19.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the number before 16: ____?, 16 A: 15. The number before 16 is 15.
chunks.source: The number before 16 is 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the next number: 12, 14, 16, ____? A: 18. The numbers go up in twos: 12, 14, 16, 18.
chunks.source: The numbers go up in twos: 12, 14, 16, 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the number symbol for eight: ____? A: 8. The number symbol for eight is 8.
chunks.source: The number symbol for eight is 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the number symbol that comes just after 9: ____? A: 10. The number after 9 is 10.
chunks.source: The number after 9 is 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the number that comes just after 17: ____? A: 18. The number after 17 is 18.
chunks.source: The number after 17 is 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 41 in words: ____? A: forty-one. 41 is written as forty-one.
chunks.source: 41 is written as forty-one.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the number between 90 and 92: ____? A: 91. Count: 90, 91, 92.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Things found in a set are called ____?. A: members. Things found in a set are called members.
chunks.source: Things found in a set are called members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A group of cups is a set of ____?. A: cups. The set is made of cups.
chunks.source: The set is made of cups.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A set of 2 birds has ____? members. A: 2. Count the birds: there are 2 members.
chunks.source: Count the birds: there are 2 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A set of 0 balls has ____? members. A: 0. There are no balls, so there are 0 members.
chunks.source: There are no balls, so there are 0 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3 books + 2 books = ____? books A: 5. 3 + 2 = 5 books.
chunks.source: 3 + 2 = 5 books.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9 sticks + 1 stick = ____? sticks A: 10. 9 + 1 = 10 sticks.
chunks.source: 9 + 1 = 10 sticks.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6 chairs + 3 chairs = ____? chairs A: 9. 6 + 3 = 9 chairs.
chunks.source: 6 + 3 = 9 chairs.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4 books plus 3 books equals ____? A: 7. 4 + 3 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is four and six more? ____? A: 10. 4 + 6 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Jane has 3 green skirts and 5 blue skirts. How many skirts has Jane altogether? ____? A: 8. 3 + 5 = 8 skirts altogether.
chunks.source: 3 + 5 = 8 skirts altogether.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is thirty and five more? ____? A: 35. 30 + 5 = 35.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6 - 4 = ____? A: 2. 6 take away 4 leaves 2.
chunks.source: 6 take away 4 leaves 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10 - 7 = ____? A: 3. 10 take away 7 leaves 3.
chunks.source: 10 take away 7 leaves 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 12 - 8 = ____? A: 4. 12 take away 8 leaves 4.
chunks.source: 12 take away 8 leaves 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8 - 3 = ____? A: 5. 8 take away 3 leaves 5.
chunks.source: 8 take away 3 leaves 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9 takeaway 2 equals ____? A: 7. 9 - 2 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Seven takeaway four equals ____? A: 3. 7 - 4 = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Three remove two we get ____? A: 1. 3 - 2 = 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is eight minus two? ____? A: 6. 8 - 2 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Daddy bought 12 apples. He gave 6 apples to Peter. How many apples did he remain with? ____? A: 6. 12 - 6 = 6 apples remained.
chunks.source: 12 - 6 = 6 apples remained.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many tens are in 18? ____? A: 1. 18 has 1 ten and 8 ones.
chunks.source: 18 has 1 ten and 8 ones.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many ones are in 28? ____? A: 8. 28 has 2 tens and 8 ones.
chunks.source: 28 has 2 tens and 8 ones.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4 tens 2 ones = ____? A: 42. 4 tens is 40, plus 2 ones is 42.
chunks.source: 4 tens is 40, plus 2 ones is 42.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1 ten 3 ones = ____? A: 13. 1 ten is 10, plus 3 ones is 13.
chunks.source: 1 ten is 10, plus 3 ones is 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Expand 29: 29 = 20 + ____? A: 9. 29 is 2 tens and 9 ones, so 29 = 20 + 9.
chunks.source: 29 is 2 tens and 9 ones, so 29 = 20 + 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Expand 63: 63 = 60 + ____? A: 3. 63 is 6 tens and 3 ones, so 63 = 60 + 3.
chunks.source: 63 is 6 tens and 3 ones, so 63 = 60 + 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1 kg = ____? grams A: 1000. There are 1000 grams in 1 kilogram.
chunks.source: There are 1000 grams in 1 kilogram.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mother sold 14kg of rice and father sold 12kg of rice. How many kg of rice were sold altogether? ____? A: 26. 14 + 12 = 26 kg sold altogether.
chunks.source: 14 + 12 = 26 kg sold altogether.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2 litres + 2 litres = ____? litres A: 4. 2 + 2 = 4 litres.
chunks.source: 2 + 2 = 4 litres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9 litres + 10 litres = ____? litres A: 19. 9 + 10 = 19 litres.
chunks.source: 9 + 10 = 19 litres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6 litres - 4 litres = ____? litres A: 2. 6 - 4 = 2 litres.
chunks.source: 6 - 4 = 2 litres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9 litres - 3 litres = ____? litres A: 6. 9 - 3 = 6 litres.
chunks.source: 9 - 3 = 6 litres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: I had 9 litres of tomato sauce. I used 2 litres. How many litres remained? ____? A: 7. 9 - 2 = 7 litres remained.
chunks.source: 9 - 2 = 7 litres remained.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A pot holds ____? water than a glass. (more or less) A: more. A pot is bigger, so it holds more water than a glass.
chunks.source: A pot is bigger, so it holds more water than a glass.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.source: 600 + 300 = 900 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.source: 500 + 400 = 900 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.source: 100 + 500 = 600 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.source: 700 - 600 = 100 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.source: 400 - 100 = 300 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.source: 900 - 700 = 200 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Henry bought a pencil at 500 shillings and a book at 400 shillings. How much did he pay altogether? ____? A: 900. 500 + 400 = 900 shillings altogether.
chunks.source: 500 + 400 = 900 shillings altogether.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: I had 300 shillings and mother added me 500 shillings. How much money do I have now? ____? A: 800. 300 + 500 = 800 shillings.
chunks.source: 300 + 500 = 800 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 12 ÷ 2 = ____? A: 6. 12 shared between 2 gives 6 each.
chunks.source: 12 shared between 2 gives 6 each.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 18 ÷ 2 = ____? A: 9. 18 shared between 2 gives 9 each.
chunks.source: 18 shared between 2 gives 9 each.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 20 ÷ 2 = ____? A: 10. 20 shared between 2 gives 10 each.
chunks.source: 20 shared between 2 gives 10 each.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.source: 2 groups of 2: 2 + 2 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8 x 3 = ____? A: 24. 8 groups of 3: 3 added 8 times is 24.
chunks.source: 8 groups of 3: 3 added 8 times is 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A stool has 3 legs. How many legs do 4 stools have? ____? A: 12. 4 stools x 3 legs = 12 legs.
chunks.source: 4 stools x 3 legs = 12 legs.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many fingers do 2 children have? ____? A: 20. Each child has 10 fingers, so 2 children have 20 fingers.
chunks.source: Each child has 10 fingers, so 2 children have 20 fingers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ is a place where we go to learn. A: school. A school is a place where we go to learn.
chunks.source: A school is a place where we go to learn.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We go to school to ____. A: learn. We go to school to learn new things.
chunks.source: We go to school to learn new things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two things found on our way to school. A: trees, cars (answers may vary - e.g., shops, houses, flowers). On our way to school we may see trees, cars, shops, houses and flowers.
chunks.source: On our way to school we may see trees, cars, shops, houses and flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: At school we are taught by ____. A: teachers. Teachers teach us at school.
chunks.source: Teachers teach us at school.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which things do we find in a classroom? A: pencil and chair. We find pencils and chairs in a classroom.
chunks.source: We find pencils and chairs in a classroom.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who heads a school? A: head teacher. The head teacher heads a school.
chunks.source: The head teacher heads a school.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write your school motto. A: Answers vary (write your own school motto). Every school has its own motto.
chunks.source: Every school has its own motto.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match people at school to their places of work. A: Head teacher: office; Teacher: classroom; Cook: kitchen; Nurse: sick bay; Guard: gate. Head teacher works in the office, Teacher in the classroom, Cook in the kitchen, Nurse in the sick bay, Guard at the gate.
chunks.source: Head teacher works in the office, Teacher in the classroom, Cook in the kitchen, Nurse in the sick bay, Guard at the gate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name these ways of keeping the school clean. A: mopping, sweeping. We keep the school clean by mopping and sweeping.
chunks.source: We keep the school clean by mopping and sweeping.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which are school symbols? A: school uniform and school flag. The school uniform and school flag are school symbols.
chunks.source: The school uniform and school flag are school symbols.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tick the dangers on our way to school. A: Dog bite, car knock. Dog bites and car knocks are dangers. A uniform is not dangerous.
chunks.source: Dog bites and car knocks are dangers. A uniform is not dangerous.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any two school needs. A: books, pencils (answers may vary - e.g., desks, chalk). Schools need books, pencils, desks and chalk.
chunks.source: Schools need books, pencils, desks and chalk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which are holy books? A: Quran and Bible. The Quran and the Bible are holy books.
chunks.source: The Quran and the Bible are holy books.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a home? A: A home is a place where we live.. A home is a place where we live with our family.
chunks.source: A home is a place where we live with our family.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two things which make up a home. A: father, mother (answers may vary - e.g., children, house). A home is made up of family members like father, mother and children.
chunks.source: A home is made up of family members like father, mother and children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A group of people related by blood or marriage is called a ____. A: family. A family is a group of people related by blood or marriage.
chunks.source: A family is a group of people related by blood or marriage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the two types of families. A: Nuclear family, extended family. The two types of families are nuclear family and extended family.
chunks.source: The two types of families are nuclear family and extended family.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name these basic needs of a family. A: food, shelter, clothing. The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.
chunks.source: The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name these parts of a house. (a, b, c, d) A: a: roof, b: window, c: door, d: wall. The parts are: a-roof, b-window, c-door, d-wall.
chunks.source: The parts are: a-roof, b-window, c-door, d-wall.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two things found in a sitting room. A: chairs, table (answers may vary - e.g., TV, sofa). In a sitting room we find chairs, tables, TV and sofa.
chunks.source: In a sitting room we find chairs, tables, TV and sofa.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name these houses. A: hut, flats (storeyed house). The houses are a hut and flats (storeyed house).
chunks.source: The houses are a hut and flats (storeyed house).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which are building materials? A: bricks and stones. Bricks and stones are building materials.
chunks.source: Bricks and stones are building materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which animal guards our home? A: dog. A dog guards our home.
chunks.source: A dog guards our home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Circle places where we find wild animals. A: forest, water. We find wild animals in the forest and in water.
chunks.source: We find wild animals in the forest and in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write out only domestic animals. A: Domestic: Cow,Cat; Wild: Lion,Snake. Cow and Cat are domestic animals. Lion and Snake are wild animals.
chunks.source: Cow and Cat are domestic animals. Lion and Snake are wild animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Muslims pray ____ times a day. A: five. Muslims pray five times a day.
chunks.source: Muslims pray five times a day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A young lion is called a ____. A: cub. A young lion is called a cub.
chunks.source: A young lion is called a cub.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ is a group of people living and working together. A: community. A community is a group of people living and working together.
chunks.source: A community is a group of people living and working together.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two people found in our community. A: teacher, doctor (answers may vary - e.g., farmer, nurse). In our community we find teachers, doctors, farmers and nurses.
chunks.source: In our community we find teachers, doctors, farmers and nurses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match people with their work. A: Teacher: teaches children; Doctor: treats sick people; Carpenter: make furniture; Shop keeper: sells in a shop; Farmer: grows food. Teacher teaches children, Doctor treats sick people, Carpenter makes furniture, Shop keeper sells in a shop, Farmer grows food.
chunks.source: Teacher teaches children, Doctor treats sick people, Carpenter makes furniture, Shop keeper sells in a shop, Farmer grows food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two needs of a community. A: water, schools (answers may vary - e.g., hospitals, roads). A community needs water, schools, hospitals and roads.
chunks.source: A community needs water, schools, hospitals and roads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List down any three important features in our community. A: school, hospital, market (answers may vary). Important features include school, hospital and market.
chunks.source: Important features include school, hospital and market.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write their places of work: Doctor, Teacher, Shop keeper, Mechanic. A: Doctor: hospital, Teacher: school, Shop keeper: shop, Mechanic: garage. Doctor works in hospital, Teacher in school, Shop keeper in shop, Mechanic in garage.
chunks.source: Doctor works in hospital, Teacher in school, Shop keeper in shop, Mechanic in garage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any two activities done in our community. A: farming, trading (answers may vary). Activities include farming, trading and building.
chunks.source: Activities include farming, trading and building.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which people work in our community? A: policeman, nurse and teacher. Policeman, nurse and teacher work in our community.
chunks.source: Policeman, nurse and teacher work in our community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Underline only the places of work. A: Hospital, market, shop. Hospital, market and shop are places of work.
chunks.source: Hospital, market and shop are places of work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any four things we use to keep our body clean. A: water, soap, towel, toothbrush (answers may vary). We use water, soap, towel and toothbrush to keep clean.
chunks.source: We use water, soap, towel and toothbrush to keep clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The cleanliness of the body and the things we use to clean is called ____. A: personal hygiene. Personal hygiene is the cleanliness of the body.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene is the cleanliness of the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we brush our teeth? A: To keep our teeth clean and healthy.. We brush our teeth to keep them clean and prevent decay.
chunks.source: We brush our teeth to keep them clean and prevent decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match these body parts to their senses. A: Eyes: seeing; Ears: hearing; Nose: smelling; Tongue: tasting; Skin: feeling. Eyes-seeing, Ears-hearing, Nose-smelling, Tongue-tasting, Skin-feeling.
chunks.source: Eyes-seeing, Ears-hearing, Nose-smelling, Tongue-tasting, Skin-feeling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which immunisable disease causes lameness? A: polio. Polio causes lameness.
chunks.source: Polio causes lameness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Underline only immunisable diseases. A: polio, measles. Polio and measles are immunisable diseases.
chunks.source: Polio and measles are immunisable diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name these body parts. A: eyes, hand, leg/foot (see pictures). The body parts shown are eyes, hand and leg.
chunks.source: The body parts shown are eyes, hand and leg.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is the giving of a vaccine to a person in order to prevent a certain disease. A: immunization. Immunization is giving a vaccine to prevent disease.
chunks.source: Immunization is giving a vaccine to prevent disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a sign of measles? A: rash (red spots) on the body. Measles causes a rash (red spots) on the body.
chunks.source: Measles causes a rash (red spots) on the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write true or untrue: We use the skin for feeling. A: True. True. We use the skin for feeling.
chunks.source: True. We use the skin for feeling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write true or untrue: We should keep our finger nails long. A: False. Untrue. We should keep our finger nails short and clean.
chunks.source: Untrue. We should keep our finger nails short and clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write true or untrue: Tetanus is an immunisable disease. A: True. True. Tetanus is an immunisable disease.
chunks.source: True. Tetanus is an immunisable disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name this thing we use to cut our finger nails. A: nail cutter. We use a nail cutter to cut finger nails.
chunks.source: We use a nail cutter to cut finger nails.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why we wash our hands after visiting the toilets. A: To kill germs and prevent diseases.. We wash hands to kill germs.
chunks.source: We wash hands to kill germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ died for our sins. A: Jesus. Jesus died for our sins.
chunks.source: Jesus died for our sins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write a word with the 'ea' sound. A: head (answers may vary - e.g., bread, read, eat, ear). Words with 'ea' sound: head, bread, read, eat.
chunks.source: Words with 'ea' sound: head, bread, read, eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete: We use ____ for hearing. A: ears. We use ears for hearing.
chunks.source: We use ears for hearing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete: ____ teach pupils to read and write. A: Teachers. Teachers teach pupils.
chunks.source: Teachers teach pupils.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which are types of weather? A: rainy and sunny. Rainy and sunny are types of weather.
chunks.source: Rainy and sunny are types of weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Arrange to make a correct sentence: rainy / day / It / is / a. A: It, is, a, rainy, day. It is a rainy day.
chunks.source: It is a rainy day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Arrange to make a correct sentence: give / us / water / Rain. A: Rain, gives, us, water. Rain gives us water.
chunks.source: Rain gives us water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Arrange to make a correct sentence: four / types / are / There / weather / of. A: There, are, four, types, of, weather. There are four types of weather.
chunks.source: There are four types of weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Arrange to make a correct sentence: wind / The / blowing / is. A: The, wind, is, blowing. The wind is blowing.
chunks.source: The wind is blowing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete: ____ is the change in ____ of a given ____ at a particular ____. (atmosphere, time, place) A: Weather, atmosphere, place, time. Weather is the change in atmosphere of a given place at a particular time.
chunks.source: Weather is the change in atmosphere of a given place at a particular time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete: There are ____ types of weather. These are: cloudy, ____, rainy and ____. The sun, ____, wind and cloud cover are the four elements of weather. A: four, sunny, windy, rain. Four types: cloudy, sunny, rainy, windy. Elements: sun, rain, wind, cloud cover.
chunks.source: Four types: cloudy, sunny, rainy, windy. Elements: sun, rain, wind, cloud cover.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which weather word is found in the word puzzle? A: windy. The word 'windy' is in the puzzle.
chunks.source: The word 'windy' is in the puzzle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Underline the things that cause accidents: food, razorblade, sun. A: razorblade. A razorblade can cause accidents.
chunks.source: A razorblade can cause accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Underline the things that cause accidents: cup, broken bottle, electricity. A: broken bottle, electricity. Broken bottles and electricity cause accidents.
chunks.source: Broken bottles and electricity cause accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Underline the things that cause accidents: pen, fire, ruler. A: fire. Fire causes accidents.
chunks.source: Fire causes accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Form words with: o, Wh_en, ose. A: ox, when, nose (answers may vary). Form words like ox, when, nose.
chunks.source: Form words like ox, when, nose.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Arrange to make a correct sentence: play / Don't / with / objects / sharp. A: Don't, play, with, sharp, objects. Don't play with sharp objects.
chunks.source: Don't play with sharp objects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Arrange to make a correct sentence: brush / I / everyday / my / teeth. A: I, brush, my, teeth, everyday. I brush my teeth everyday.
chunks.source: I brush my teeth everyday.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Arrange to make a correct sentence: zebra / crossing / We / the / road / cross / at / the. A: We, cross, the, road, at, the, zebra, crossing. We cross the road at the zebra crossing.
chunks.source: We cross the road at the zebra crossing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which things can cause accidents? A: broken bottles and razor blade. Broken bottles and razor blades cause accidents.
chunks.source: Broken bottles and razor blades cause accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Arrange these sentences to form a good story. A: One day John and Moses were playing football., Moses stepped on a broken bottle., It cut his foot badly., His mother took him to the hospital.. Order: playing → stepped on bottle → cut foot → hospital.
chunks.source: Order: playing → stepped on bottle → cut foot → hospital.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gaps: Our teacher told us not to play with sharp objects because they ____ us. We should not play with ____ because it burns. ____ causes electric shock. It is not good to ____ trees because we can ____ down. (climb, fall, electricity, fire, cut) A: cut, fire, electricity, climb, fall. Sharp objects cut us. Fire burns. Electricity causes shock. Don't climb trees, you can fall.
chunks.source: Sharp objects cut us. Fire burns. Electricity causes shock. Don't climb trees, you can fall.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the missing letters: s____oking, sun d___ying, ti____ning. A: smoking, drying, tinning. Food preservation: smoking, sun drying, tinning.
chunks.source: Food preservation: smoking, sun drying, tinning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Join to form words: ood, ind, anket. A: food, wind, blanket. food (f+ood), wind (w+ind), blanket (bl+anket).
chunks.source: food (f+ood), wind (w+ind), blanket (bl+anket).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Find things we eat from the word puzzle. A: posho, beans, peas, banana. The foods in the puzzle are posho, beans, peas and banana.
chunks.source: The foods in the puzzle are posho, beans, peas and banana.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Sources of food are places where we get food. We get food from the garden, ____, market, ____ and animals. We get cassava, ____, bananas and ____ from the garden. We get ____ from water. People buy rice, bread, biscuits from the ____. (farm, shop, fish, yams, potatoes, water) A: farm, water, yams, potatoes, fish, shop. Sources: garden, farm, market, water, animals, shop.
chunks.source: Sources: garden, farm, market, water, animals, shop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Arrange these sentences to form a food story. A: I light the charcoal stove., I put the water in the kettle., I put the kettle on a charcoal stove., When it is ready, I pour it in my cup., Then I take my tea.. Order: light stove → put water → put kettle → pour → drink.
chunks.source: Order: light stove → put water → put kettle → pour → drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is the movement of people and their goods from one place to another. A: Transport. Transport means moving people and goods from one place to another.
chunks.source: Transport means moving people and goods from one place to another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is the quickest type of transport. A: Air transport. Aeroplanes fly fast in the sky.
chunks.source: Aeroplanes fly fast in the sky.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is the slowest type of transport. A: Railway transport. Trains on rails move slowly.
chunks.source: Trains on rails move slowly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is the commonest type of transport. A: Road transport. Cars and buses on roads are seen everywhere.
chunks.source: Cars and buses on roads are seen everywhere.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which is the quickest type of transport? A: Air transport. Aeroplanes fly very fast.
chunks.source: Aeroplanes fly very fast.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which is the slowest type of transport? A: Railway transport. Trains move slowly on rails.
chunks.source: Trains move slowly on rails.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the four types of transport. A: Air transport, Water transport, Railway transport, Road transport. The four types are air, water, railway and road.
chunks.source: The four types are air, water, railway and road.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is a means of road transport? A: Car. Cars move on roads.
chunks.source: Cars move on roads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A person who moves along the road is called a ____. A: pedestrian. A pedestrian walks along the road.
chunks.source: A pedestrian walks along the road.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ is a person who moves in the vehicle. A: passenger. A passenger sits inside the vehicle.
chunks.source: A passenger sits inside the vehicle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Select all means of road transport. A: Car, Bicycle, Bus, Motorcycle, Lorry. Cars, bicycles, buses, motorcycles and lorries move on roads.
chunks.source: Cars, bicycles, buses, motorcycles and lorries move on roads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name three animals used for transport. A: Camel, Donkey, Horse. Camels, donkeys and horses carry people and goods.
chunks.source: Camels, donkeys and horses carry people and goods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which animal is shown in the picture? A: Camel. The picture shows a camel.
chunks.source: The picture shows a camel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which animal is shown in the picture? A: Horse. The picture shows a horse.
chunks.source: The picture shows a horse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name three means of water transport. A: Canoe, Boat, Ship, Ferry. Canoes, boats, ships and ferries move on water.
chunks.source: Canoes, boats, ships and ferries move on water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which is a means of water transport? A: Canoe. A canoe moves on water.
chunks.source: A canoe moves on water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which is a means of water transport? A: Ship. A ship is a big boat on water.
chunks.source: A ship is a big boat on water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which is a means of air transport? A: Helicopter. A helicopter flies in the air.
chunks.source: A helicopter flies in the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two means of air transport. A: Aeroplane, Helicopter. Aeroplanes and helicopters fly in the air.
chunks.source: Aeroplanes and helicopters fly in the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write two means of railway transport. A: Train, Tram. Trains and trams run on rails.
chunks.source: Trains and trams run on rails.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A train moves on a ____. A: railway line. Trains run on railway lines.
chunks.source: Trains run on railway lines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which is shown in the picture? A: Train. The picture shows a train.
chunks.source: The picture shows a train.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match these people to their work. A: Pilot: flies an aeroplane; Driver: drives a car; Sailor: sails a ship; Cyclist: rides a bicycle. Each person operates a different means of transport.
chunks.source: Each person operates a different means of transport.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ flies an aeroplane. A: pilot. A pilot flies an aeroplane.
chunks.source: A pilot flies an aeroplane.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ sails a ship. A: sailor. A sailor sails a ship.
chunks.source: A sailor sails a ship.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ drives a car. A: driver. A driver drives a car.
chunks.source: A driver drives a car.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match these means of transport to their places. A: Aeroplane: airport; Train: railway station; Ship: harbour; Taxi: taxi park; Boat: landing site. Each means of transport is found at its own place.
chunks.source: Each means of transport is found at its own place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A train is found at the ____. A: railway station. Trains stop at railway stations.
chunks.source: Trains stop at railway stations.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We find aeroplanes at the ____. A: airport. Aeroplanes take off from airports.
chunks.source: Aeroplanes take off from airports.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A camel rider rides a ____. A: camel. A camel rider sits on a camel.
chunks.source: A camel rider sits on a camel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A donkey rider rides a ____. A: donkey. A donkey rider sits on a donkey.
chunks.source: A donkey rider sits on a donkey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give four uses of transport. A: To carry people, To carry food, To carry animals, To carry water. Transport carries people, food, animals and water.
chunks.source: Transport carries people, food, animals and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A taxi carries passengers. True or False? A: True. Taxis carry people from place to place.
chunks.source: Taxis carry people from place to place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Select the safe ways of crossing the road. A: Cross the road carefully, Follow traffic signs. Cross carefully and follow signs to be safe.
chunks.source: Cross carefully and follow signs to be safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We should cross on the zebra crossing. True or False? A: True. The zebra crossing is the safe place to cross.
chunks.source: The zebra crossing is the safe place to cross.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tick the unsafe ways of using the road. A: Playing on the road, Throwing stones to moving vehicles. Playing on roads and throwing stones are dangerous.
chunks.source: Playing on roads and throwing stones are dangerous.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Playing on the road is safe. True or False? A: False. Playing on the road is very dangerous.
chunks.source: Playing on the road is very dangerous.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which road sign do children use to cross the road? A: Zebra crossing. Children cross at the zebra crossing.
chunks.source: Children cross at the zebra crossing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does this road sign mean? A: Humps ahead. The sign warns of humps on the road.
chunks.source: The sign warns of humps on the road.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ are symbols which guide us on the road. A: Road signs. Road signs show us what to do.
chunks.source: Road signs show us what to do.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which traffic light tells drivers to stop? A: Red. Red means stop.
chunks.source: Red means stop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which traffic light means go? A: Green. Green means go.
chunks.source: Green means go.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which traffic light means get ready? A: Orange. Orange means get ready.
chunks.source: Orange means get ready.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match traffic lights to their meanings. A: Red: stop; Orange: get ready; Green: go. Red stops, orange gets ready, green goes.
chunks.source: Red stops, orange gets ready, green goes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention four dangerous things on the road. A: Nails, Broken bottles, Stones, Potholes. Nails, broken bottles, stones and potholes are dangerous.
chunks.source: Nails, broken bottles, stones and potholes are dangerous.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Broken bottles on the road are dangerous. True or False? A: True. Broken bottles can cut feet and tyres.
chunks.source: Broken bottles can cut feet and tyres.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name three people who help in traffic. A: Policemen, Teachers, Traffic warden. Police, teachers and wardens help us on roads.
chunks.source: Police, teachers and wardens help us on roads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ transport is the quickest type of transport. A: Air. Air transport by aeroplane is fastest.
chunks.source: Air transport by aeroplane is fastest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the cheapest type of transport? A: Road transport. Road transport costs the least.
chunks.source: Road transport costs the least.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the most expensive type of transport? A: Air transport. Flying by aeroplane costs the most.
chunks.source: Flying by aeroplane costs the most.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the missing letters: W___ter A: Water. W-A-T-E-R spells water.
chunks.source: W-A-T-E-R spells water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the missing letters: rai___w___y A: railway. R-A-I-L-W-A-Y spells railway.
chunks.source: R-A-I-L-W-A-Y spells railway.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the missing letters: r___ ___d A: road. R-O-A-D spells road.
chunks.source: R-O-A-D spells road.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Water transport is commonly used in our community. True or False? A: False. Most people use road transport.
chunks.source: Most people use road transport.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is the movement of people and their goods from one place to another. A: Transport. This is the definition of transport.
chunks.source: This is the definition of transport.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is transport useful to people? Give three ways. A: To carry people, To carry food, To carry building materials. Transport moves people, food and materials.
chunks.source: Transport moves people, food and materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is transport? A: The movement of people and their goods from one place to another. Transport moves people and goods.
chunks.source: Transport moves people and goods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A person who walks along the road is a ____. A: pedestrian. Pedestrians walk on foot.
chunks.source: Pedestrians walk on foot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Boats move on ____. A: water. Boats float on water.
chunks.source: Boats float on water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one way of using the road safely. A: Cross on the zebra crossing. The zebra crossing is safe.
chunks.source: The zebra crossing is safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are crafts? A: Things we make from local materials using our hands. Crafts are handmade things.
chunks.source: Crafts are handmade things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ makes pots. A: potter. A potter makes pots from clay.
chunks.source: A potter makes pots from clay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two things we make at school. A: Basket, Mat, Ball, Hat. We weave baskets, mats and make balls and hats.
chunks.source: We weave baskets, mats and make balls and hats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match these materials to their sources. A: Papyrus: swamp; Sisal: sisal plant; Clay: swamp; Palm leaves: palm tree. Materials come from plants and earth.
chunks.source: Materials come from plants and earth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do we get papyrus? A: Swamp. Papyrus grows in swampy areas.
chunks.source: Papyrus grows in swampy areas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do we get clay? A: swamp. Clay is dug from the ground near swamps.
chunks.source: Clay is dug from the ground near swamps.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name three things made from banana fibres. A: Mat, Hat, Bag, Rope. Mats, hats, bags and ropes are made from banana fibres.
chunks.source: Mats, hats, bags and ropes are made from banana fibres.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: From which plant do we get banana fibres? A: Banana plant. Banana fibres come from banana plants.
chunks.source: Banana fibres come from banana plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We use a mat for ____. A: sitting on. We sit on mats.
chunks.source: We sit on mats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name four things made from clay. A: Pot, Cup, Plate, Charcoal stove. Pots, cups, plates and stoves are made from clay.
chunks.source: Pots, cups, plates and stoves are made from clay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A person who makes things from clay is called a ____. A: potter. A potter shapes clay into pots.
chunks.source: A potter shapes clay into pots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We make pots from clay. True or False? A: True. Clay is shaped into pots.
chunks.source: Clay is shaped into pots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two things made from animal skins. A: Bags, Shoes, Belts, Drums. Bags, shoes, belts and drums use animal skins.
chunks.source: Bags, shoes, belts and drums use animal skins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: From which animal do we get wool? A: Sheep. Wool comes from sheep.
chunks.source: Wool comes from sheep.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is shown in the picture? A: Drum. The picture shows a drum.
chunks.source: The picture shows a drum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We get wool from cows. True or False? A: False. Wool comes from sheep, not cows.
chunks.source: Wool comes from sheep, not cows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name five things made from wood. A: Chair, Table, Bench, Bed, Door. Chairs, tables, benches, beds and doors are wooden.
chunks.source: Chairs, tables, benches, beds and doors are wooden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which is made from wood? A: Chair. Chairs are made from wood.
chunks.source: Chairs are made from wood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give three uses of things we make. A: For sitting, For decoration, For playing, For carrying water. We sit on, decorate with, play with and carry water in them.
chunks.source: We sit on, decorate with, play with and carry water in them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is used for sleeping on. A: bed. We sleep on beds.
chunks.source: We sleep on beds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is used for fetching water. A: pot. Pots carry water.
chunks.source: Pots carry water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match things to materials they are made from. A: Chair: wood; Drum: animal skins; Mat: palm leaves; Pot: clay. Each thing is made from its material.
chunks.source: Each thing is made from its material.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two reasons why people make crafts. A: To sell and get money, For decoration. People sell crafts and use them to decorate.
chunks.source: People sell crafts and use them to decorate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write two things we make for sitting on. A: Stool, Chair, Bench. Stools, chairs and benches are for sitting.
chunks.source: Stools, chairs and benches are for sitting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tick the reasons for keeping peace and security. A: To be friendly to one another, To live in a good environment, To protect children's rights. Peace brings friendship, good environment and protects children.
chunks.source: Peace brings friendship, good environment and protects children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We keep peace to live in a good environment. True or False? A: True. Peace makes our home good.
chunks.source: Peace makes our home good.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention two causes of insecurity at home. A: Fighting, Quarreling, Using bad words. Fighting, quarreling and bad words bring insecurity.
chunks.source: Fighting, quarreling and bad words bring insecurity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Circle the bad games children should not play. A: Fighting, Throwing stones. Fighting and throwing stones are bad.
chunks.source: Fighting and throwing stones are bad.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name three people who keep peace at school. A: Teacher, Policeman, Prefect. Teachers, police and prefects keep peace.
chunks.source: Teachers, police and prefects keep peace.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who keeps children safe in class? A: Teacher. The teacher keeps children safe in class.
chunks.source: The teacher keeps children safe in class.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Underline the causes of insecurity at school. A: Fighting, Using bad words, Not respecting others. Fighting, bad words and disrespect cause insecurity.
chunks.source: Fighting, bad words and disrespect cause insecurity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give three ways of keeping peace at school. A: Playing good games, Obeying school rules, Sharing with others. Good games, rules and sharing bring peace.
chunks.source: Good games, rules and sharing bring peace.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which can we share with friends? A: Apples, Books, Pencils. We share food and books.
chunks.source: We share food and books.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention three people who keep peace in the community. A: Policeman, Teacher, Parents. Police, teachers and parents keep peace.
chunks.source: Police, teachers and parents keep peace.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tick the causes of insecurity in a community. A: Poverty, Quarrelling, Stealing. Poverty, quarrels and stealing cause insecurity.
chunks.source: Poverty, quarrels and stealing cause insecurity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Teachers give ____ and counseling. A: guidance. Teachers guide children.
chunks.source: Teachers guide children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Police keep ____ and order. A: law. Police keep law and order.
chunks.source: Police keep law and order.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match people to their tools. A: Hunter: spear; Priest: bible; Soldier: gun; Policeman: gun. Each person uses their tool.
chunks.source: Each person uses their tool.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write four importances of keeping peace. A: Friendship, Freedom of speech, Protects property, Love and respect. Peace brings friendship, freedom, safety and love.
chunks.source: Peace brings friendship, freedom, safety and love.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention four people who bring insecurity. A: Thieves, Kidnappers, Drunkards, Idle people. Thieves, kidnappers and others bring fear.
chunks.source: Thieves, kidnappers and others bring fear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention three effects of insecurity. A: People become fearful, Loss of property, School dropouts. Insecurity causes fear, loss and dropouts.
chunks.source: Insecurity causes fear, loss and dropouts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do we report bad people? A: Police. We report to the police.
chunks.source: We report to the police.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Peace is living in ____ with others. A: harmony. Harmony means living well together.
chunks.source: Harmony means living well together.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Underline the people who cause insecurity. A: Thieves, Kidnappers. Thieves and kidnappers cause fear.
chunks.source: Thieves and kidnappers cause fear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do policemen help in keeping peace? A: They protect people and property. Police protect us.
chunks.source: Police protect us.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write the word correctly: pceea A: peace. P-E-A-C-E spells peace.
chunks.source: P-E-A-C-E spells peace.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write the word correctly: ritysecu A: security. S-E-C-U-R-I-T-Y spells security.
chunks.source: S-E-C-U-R-I-T-Y spells security.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write the word correctly: oeby A: obey. O-B-E-Y spells obey.
chunks.source: O-B-E-Y spells obey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write the word correctly: rmnyoha A: harmony. H-A-R-M-O-N-Y spells harmony.
chunks.source: H-A-R-M-O-N-Y spells harmony.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention two importances of keeping peace. A: To live in a good environment, To protect children's rights. Peace gives good life and protects children.
chunks.source: Peace gives good life and protects children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is shown in the picture? A: School uniform. The picture shows school uniform.
chunks.source: The picture shows school uniform.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Put the traffic lights in order from top to bottom. A: Red, Orange, Green. Red is on top, orange in the middle, green at the bottom.
chunks.source: Red is on top, orange in the middle, green at the bottom.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Order these from slowest to quickest. A: Railway transport, Water transport, Road transport, Air transport. Railway is slowest, air is quickest.
chunks.source: Railway is slowest, air is quickest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sort these into the correct type of transport. A: Air: Aeroplane,Helicopter; Water: Canoe,Ship,Boat; Road: Car,Bus,Bicycle. Aeroplanes fly, boats float, cars drive on roads.
chunks.source: Aeroplanes fly, boats float, cars drive on roads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sort into safe and unsafe ways of using the road. A: Safe: Cross on zebra crossing,Follow traffic signs; Unsafe: Play on the road,Throw stones. Safe ways protect us, unsafe ways hurt us.
chunks.source: Safe ways protect us, unsafe ways hurt us.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Put these in order of importance for peace at home. A: Love one another, Help one another, Share with others. Love comes first, then helping and sharing.
chunks.source: Love comes first, then helping and sharing.

chunks.text: Q: Which of these are school rules? (Choose all correct) A: Do not fight, Do not shout in class, Keep the compound clean. Do not fight, Do not shout in class, Run in class, Keep the compound clean
chunks.source: Do not fight, Do not shout in class, Run in class, Keep the compound clean

chunks.text: Q: Match the things in the classroom to their uses. A: Tables: writing; Chairs: sitting; Chalk: writing on the chalkboard; Broom: sweeping the classroom; Duster: cleaning the chalkboard. chunks.source: Tables are for writing, chairs are for sitting, chalk is for writing on the chalkboard, brooms sweep, dusters clean the board.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which things do we use to keep our school clean? (Choose all correct) A: Brooms, Water, Soap, Waste bins. Brooms, Water, Soap, Waste bins, Pillow, Television
chunks.source: Brooms, Water, Soap, Waste bins, Pillow, Television

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do we keep our school clean? A: By sweeping the compound and classroom. By sweeping the compound and classroom, By throwing rubbish anywhere, By writing on walls, By breaking chairs
chunks.source: By sweeping the compound and classroom, By throwing rubbish anywhere, By writing on walls, By breaking chairs

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A school motto encourages us to ____. A: work hard. The school motto encourages us to work hard.
chunks.source: The school motto encourages us to work hard.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which are school activities? (Choose all correct) A: Writing, Reading, Sweeping, Playing. Writing, Reading, Sweeping, Playing, Sleeping at home, Driving a car

chunks.text: Q: Match the animals to their homes. A: Dog: kennel; Pig: sty; Lion: den; Bird: nest; Cow: kraal; Horse: stable; Bee: hive. A dog stays in a kennel, a pig in a sty, a lion in a den, a bird in a nest, a cow in a kraal, a horse in a stable, a bee in a hive.

chunks.text: Q: Why do we need cooks at school? A: to cook food for children. Cooks cook food for the children.
chunks.source: Cooks cook food for the children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match the people at school to their work. A: Cooks: cook food for children; Teachers: teach children; Cleaners: clean the school. Cooks cook food, teachers teach children and cleaners clean the school.
chunks.source: Cooks cook food, teachers teach children and cleaners clean the school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match the people to their place of work. A: Cooks: kitchen; Head teacher: office; Nurse: sick bay; Teachers: classroom. Cooks work in the kitchen, the head teacher in the office, the nurse in the sick bay and teachers in the classroom.
chunks.source: Cooks work in the kitchen, the head teacher in the office, the nurse in the sick bay and teachers in the classroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match the school workers to their work. A: Bursar: collects school fees; Typist: types school work; Librarian: lends out books. The bursar collects fees, the typist types work and the librarian lends books.
chunks.source: The bursar collects fees, the typist types work and the librarian lends books.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing found on the school signpost. A: the school name. The school name is on the signpost.
chunks.source: The school name is on the signpost.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one symbol of the school. A: flag. The school flag is a symbol of the school.
chunks.source: The school flag is a symbol of the school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the person who collects school fees in your school. A: bursar. The bursar collects school fees.
chunks.source: The bursar collects school fees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one group of people found at school. A: pupils. Pupils are found at school.
chunks.source: Pupils are found at school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one important person found at school. A: teacher. Teachers are important people at school.
chunks.source: Teachers are important people at school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need balls at school? A: for playing. Balls are for playing games.
chunks.source: Balls are for playing games.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one play material used at school. A: ball. A ball is a play material.
chunks.source: A ball is a play material.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one game played at your school. A: football. Football is a game played at school.
chunks.source: Football is a game played at school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing you can share with your friend. A: books. We can share books with friends.
chunks.source: We can share books with friends.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing you put on before going to school. A: uniform. We put on our uniform before going to school.
chunks.source: We put on our uniform before going to school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do school children put on uniforms? A: to look smart. Uniforms make school children look smart.
chunks.source: Uniforms make school children look smart.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is a clock useful in a classroom? A: It tells us the time. A clock tells us the time in class.
chunks.source: A clock tells us the time in class.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing you see on your way to school. A: trees. We see trees on the way to school.
chunks.source: We see trees on the way to school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do we call a person who drives a school van? A: driver. A driver drives the school van.
chunks.source: A driver drives the school van.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these things are found in a classroom? (Choose all that apply.) A: book, table, ruler. A book, a table and a ruler are found in a classroom. A hoe is used in the garden.
chunks.source: A book, a table and a ruler are found in a classroom. A hoe is used in the garden.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A headteacher heads a school. A: True. The headteacher is the head of a school.
chunks.source: The headteacher is the head of a school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: We go to school to learn. A: True. Children go to school to learn.
chunks.source: Children go to school to learn.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A broom is used for writing. A: False. A broom is used for sweeping, not writing.
chunks.source: A broom is used for sweeping, not writing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The nurse cares for sick children at school. A: True. The nurse cares for sick children.
chunks.source: The nurse cares for sick children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: We put rubbish in the dustbin. A: True. Rubbish goes in the dustbin.
chunks.source: Rubbish goes in the dustbin.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Cooks teach children at school. A: False. Cooks cook food. Teachers teach children.
chunks.source: Cooks cook food. Teachers teach children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Cups, plates and spoons are ___. A: utensils. Cups, plates and spoons are utensils.
chunks.source: Cups, plates and spoons are utensils.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Forks, knives and spoons are ___. A: cutlery. Forks, knives and spoons are cutlery.
chunks.source: Forks, knives and spoons are cutlery.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Chairs, tables, bed and cupboard are ___. A: furniture. Chairs, tables, bed and cupboard are furniture.
chunks.source: Chairs, tables, bed and cupboard are furniture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: We get beef from a ___. A: cow. We get beef from a cow.
chunks.source: We get beef from a cow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: At home, there is a big ___ in the sitting room for us to watch news. A: television. We watch news on the television.
chunks.source: We watch news on the television.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: All the ___ and cutlery are kept in the kitchen. A: utensils. Utensils are kept in the kitchen.
chunks.source: Utensils are kept in the kitchen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: There are two big ___ in the bedroom. A: beds. We sleep on beds in the bedroom.
chunks.source: We sleep on beds in the bedroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing in the sitting room we sit on. A: chair. We sit on a chair in the sitting room.
chunks.source: We sit on a chair in the sitting room.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are found in the sitting room? (Choose all that apply.) A: mat, table, radio. A mat, a table and a radio are found in the sitting room.
chunks.source: A mat, a table and a radio are found in the sitting room.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are found in the kitchen? (Choose all that apply.) A: plate, spoon. A plate and a spoon are found in the kitchen.
chunks.source: A plate and a spoon are found in the kitchen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing found in the kitchen. A: saucepan. A saucepan is found in the kitchen.
chunks.source: A saucepan is found in the kitchen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing found in the bedroom. A: bed. A bed is found in the bedroom.
chunks.source: A bed is found in the bedroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one room found in a house. A: bedroom. A bedroom is a room in a house.
chunks.source: A bedroom is a room in a house.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: From which room of a house do people bathe? A: bathroom. People bathe in the bathroom.
chunks.source: People bathe in the bathroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the building at home where people sleep. A: house. People sleep in a house.
chunks.source: People sleep in a house.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing found in a bathroom. A: soap. Soap is found in the bathroom.
chunks.source: Soap is found in the bathroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are found in a bathroom? (Choose all that apply.) A: soap, water. Soap and water are found in the bathroom.
chunks.source: Soap and water are found in the bathroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a home? A: A home is a place where a family lives. A home is a place where a family lives.
chunks.source: A home is a place where a family lives.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a temporary house. A: hut. A hut is a temporary house.
chunks.source: A hut is a temporary house.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one part of a house. A: door. A door is part of a house.
chunks.source: A door is part of a house.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of a house. A: for shelter. A house gives us shelter.
chunks.source: A house gives us shelter.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who cooks food at home? A: mother. The mother cooks food at home.
chunks.source: The mother cooks food at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who buys food at home? A: mother. The mother buys food at home.
chunks.source: The mother buys food at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who breastfeeds a baby at home? A: mother. The mother breastfeeds the baby.
chunks.source: The mother breastfeeds the baby.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we use to cook food. A: saucepan. We cook food in a saucepan.
chunks.source: We cook food in a saucepan.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which animal guards our home? A: dog. A dog guards our home.
chunks.source: A dog guards our home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need a dog at home? A: to guard our home. A dog guards our home.
chunks.source: A dog guards our home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people keep dogs? A: To guard their homes. People keep dogs to guard their homes.
chunks.source: People keep dogs to guard their homes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one domestic animal kept at home. A: cow. A cow is a domestic animal kept at home.
chunks.source: A cow is a domestic animal kept at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people keep cows at home? A: to get milk. People keep cows to get milk.
chunks.source: People keep cows to get milk.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A cow gives us ___ and ___. A: milk and beef. A cow gives us milk and beef.
chunks.source: A cow gives us milk and beef.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one bird kept at home for eggs. A: hen. A hen is kept at home for eggs.
chunks.source: A hen is kept at home for eggs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people keep hens at home? A: to get eggs. People keep hens to get eggs.
chunks.source: People keep hens to get eggs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people keep rabbits at home? A: to get meat. People keep rabbits to get meat.
chunks.source: People keep rabbits to get meat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people keep domestic animals? A: for food. People keep domestic animals for food and other products.
chunks.source: People keep domestic animals for food and other products.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do people care for their animals at home? A: by feeding them. We care for animals by feeding them.
chunks.source: We care for animals by feeding them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one way of caring for a dog at home. A: by feeding it. We care for a dog by feeding it.
chunks.source: We care for a dog by feeding it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A broom is used for ___ at home. A: sweeping. A broom is used for sweeping at home.
chunks.source: A broom is used for sweeping at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing used to clean a house. A: broom. A broom is used to clean a house.
chunks.source: A broom is used to clean a house.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these should a clean home have? (Choose all that apply.) A: toilet, kitchen. A clean home should have a toilet and a kitchen.
chunks.source: A clean home should have a toilet and a kitchen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one material used to make pots. A: clay. Pots are made from clay.
chunks.source: Pots are made from clay.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of pots at home. A: for cooking. Pots are used for cooking at home.
chunks.source: Pots are used for cooking at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are found at home? (Choose all that apply.) A: Spoon, Fork, Knife. A spoon, a fork and a knife are found at home.
chunks.source: A spoon, a fork and a knife are found at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one item used for writing. A: pencil. We write with a pencil.
chunks.source: We write with a pencil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are members of a family? (Choose all that apply.) A: father, sister. A father and a sister are members of a family.
chunks.source: A father and a sister are members of a family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are members of a nuclear family? (Choose all that apply.) A: Brother. A brother is a member of a nuclear family.
chunks.source: A brother is a member of a nuclear family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are members of a nuclear family? (Choose all that apply.) A: father, mother. A father and a mother are members of a nuclear family.
chunks.source: A father and a mother are members of a nuclear family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a nuclear family? A: a family with parents and their own children. A nuclear family has parents and their own children only.
chunks.source: A nuclear family has parents and their own children only.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A ___ heads a family. A: father. A father heads a family.
chunks.source: A father heads a family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match the people at home with their roles. A: father: pays school fees; mother: cooks food; children: fetch water. The father pays school fees, the mother cooks food and the children fetch water.
chunks.source: The father pays school fees, the mother cooks food and the children fetch water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match the things found at home with their uses. A: mat: for sitting on; bed: for sleeping on; charcoal stove: for cooking; knife: for peeling; broom: for sweeping. A mat is for sitting, a bed for sleeping, a stove for cooking, a knife for peeling and a broom for sweeping.
chunks.source: A mat is for sitting, a bed for sleeping, a stove for cooking, a knife for peeling and a broom for sweeping.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one way children help at home. A: sweeping the compound. Children help by sweeping the compound.
chunks.source: Children help by sweeping the compound.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we call a place where people or animals stay? A: home. A home is a place where people or animals stay.
chunks.source: A home is a place where people or animals stay.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are found in the dining room? (Choose all that apply.) A: Bench, table, cup, plate. A bench, a table, a cup and a plate are found in the dining room.
chunks.source: A bench, a table, a cup and a plate are found in the dining room.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A dog guards our home. A: True. A dog guards our home.

chunks.text: Q: We get milk from a cow. A: True. A cow gives us milk.
chunks.source: A cow gives us milk.

chunks.source: A broom is used for sweeping.
