chunks.source: Forks, knives and spoons are cutlery.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A father heads a family. A: True. A father heads a family.
chunks.source: A father heads a family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: We sleep in the kitchen. A: False. We sleep in the bedroom, not the kitchen.
chunks.source: We sleep in the bedroom, not the kitchen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match the people with their places of work. A: Teacher: school; Doctor: hospital; Farmer: farm; Carpenter: workshop. A teacher works at school, a doctor at the hospital, a farmer on the farm and a carpenter in the workshop.
chunks.source: A teacher works at school, a doctor at the hospital, a farmer on the farm and a carpenter in the workshop.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: ___ grows maize and bananas and keeps animals. A: farmer. A farmer grows maize and bananas and keeps animals.
chunks.source: A farmer grows maize and bananas and keeps animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: ___ polishes and mends shoes. A: cobbler. A cobbler polishes and mends shoes.
chunks.source: A cobbler polishes and mends shoes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: ___ treats sick people. A: doctor. A doctor treats sick people.
chunks.source: A doctor treats sick people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: ___ makes chairs, beds and cupboards. A: carpenter. A carpenter makes chairs, beds and cupboards.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes chairs, beds and cupboards.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: ___ sells fruits, vegetables and food. A: market vendor. A market vendor sells fruits, vegetables and food.
chunks.source: A market vendor sells fruits, vegetables and food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A ___ is a group of people living and working together. A: community. A community is a group of people living and working together.
chunks.source: A community is a group of people living and working together.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we call a group of people living or working together? A: community. We call them a community.
chunks.source: We call them a community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What work does Mr. Kasule do? A: He is a farmer. Mr. Kasule is a farmer. He grows crops and keeps animals.
chunks.source: Mr. Kasule is a farmer. He grows crops and keeps animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a doctor do? A: treats sick people. A doctor treats sick people.
chunks.source: A doctor treats sick people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mr. ___ mends shoes. A: Mugarula. Mr. Mugarula mends shoes.
chunks.source: Mr. Mugarula mends shoes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does Mr. Opio do? A: cuts people's hair. Mr. Opio cuts people's hair. He is a barber.
chunks.source: Mr. Opio cuts people's hair. He is a barber.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match the people in a community to their work. A: Doctor: treats sick people; Policeman: keeps law and order; Barber: cuts people's hair; Pastor: preaches in church. A doctor treats the sick, a policeman keeps law and order, a barber cuts hair and a pastor preaches in church.
chunks.source: A doctor treats the sick, a policeman keeps law and order, a barber cuts hair and a pastor preaches in church.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match the workers to their work. A: Carpenter: makes furniture; Doctor: treats sick people; Barber: cuts hair; Farmer: grows crops and keeps animals. A carpenter makes furniture, a doctor treats the sick, a barber cuts hair and a farmer grows crops.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes furniture, a doctor treats the sick, a barber cuts hair and a farmer grows crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who makes furniture in our community? A: carpenter. A carpenter makes furniture.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes furniture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need a bank in our community? A: to keep our money safe. We keep our money safe in a bank.
chunks.source: We keep our money safe in a bank.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one important place in the community where people keep their money. A: bank. People keep money in a bank.
chunks.source: People keep money in a bank.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people go to hospital? A: for treatment. Sick people go to hospital for treatment.
chunks.source: Sick people go to hospital for treatment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one person who works in a hospital. A: doctor. A doctor works in a hospital.
chunks.source: A doctor works in a hospital.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do sick people go for treatment? A: hospital. Sick people go to hospital.
chunks.source: Sick people go to hospital.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do people go for praying? A: church. People go to church for praying.
chunks.source: People go to church for praying.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do people buy food? A: market. People buy food in the market.
chunks.source: People buy food in the market.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are important places in our community? (Choose all that apply.) A: bank, church, school. A bank, a church and a school are important places in a community.
chunks.source: A bank, a church and a school are important places in a community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one important place where people go for shopping. A: market. People go to the market for shopping.
chunks.source: People go to the market for shopping.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we buy from a market. A: food. We buy food from a market.
chunks.source: We buy food from a market.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one importance of a market in a community. A: We buy food there. A market is important because we buy food there.
chunks.source: A market is important because we buy food there.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one activity done by people in a community. A: farming. Farming is an activity done in a community.
chunks.source: Farming is an activity done in a community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one important place found in our community. A: school. A school is an important place in a community.
chunks.source: A school is an important place in a community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one duty of a teacher in a community. A: to teach children. A teacher teaches children in a community.
chunks.source: A teacher teaches children in a community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need doctors in a community? A: to treat sick people. Doctors treat sick people in a community.
chunks.source: Doctors treat sick people in a community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one cultural activity done by people in a community. A: dancing. Dancing is a cultural activity.
chunks.source: Dancing is a cultural activity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one cultural ceremony carried out in our community. A: wedding. A wedding is a cultural ceremony.
chunks.source: A wedding is a cultural ceremony.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the main activity of fishermen? A: fishing. Fishermen catch fish.
chunks.source: Fishermen catch fish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the main activity of farmers? A: farming. Farmers grow crops.
chunks.source: Farmers grow crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A doctor treats sick people. A: True. A doctor treats sick people.
chunks.source: A doctor treats sick people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A bank keeps our money safe. A: True. A bank keeps our money safe.
chunks.source: A bank keeps our money safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A carpenter makes furniture. A: True. A carpenter makes furniture.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes furniture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A community is a group of people living together. A: True. A community is a group of people living and working together.
chunks.source: A community is a group of people living and working together.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these do we use to clean our body? (Choose all that apply.) A: soap, comb, toothbrush, water. Soap, a comb, a toothbrush and water clean our body.
chunks.source: Soap, a comb, a toothbrush and water clean our body.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: ___ is the cleanliness of our body. A: personal hygiene. Personal hygiene is the cleanliness of our body.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene is the cleanliness of our body.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which one is NOT a disease? A: head. Malaria, diarrhoea and mumps are diseases. The head is a body part.
chunks.source: Malaria, diarrhoea and mumps are diseases. The head is a body part.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one way we keep our body clean. A: bathing. Bathing keeps our body clean.
chunks.source: Bathing keeps our body clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: We use ___ and ___ to brush our teeth. A: toothbrush and toothpaste. We use a toothbrush and toothpaste to brush our teeth.
chunks.source: We use a toothbrush and toothpaste to brush our teeth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which body part do we use for seeing? A: eyes. We see with our eyes.
chunks.source: We see with our eyes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the body part used for smelling. A: nose. We smell with our nose.
chunks.source: We smell with our nose.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the body part used for walking. A: legs. We walk with our legs.
chunks.source: We walk with our legs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which body part do we use for tasting food? A: tongue. We taste food with our tongue.
chunks.source: We taste food with our tongue.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one body part found on the head. A: eyes. Eyes are found on the head.
chunks.source: Eyes are found on the head.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we use for biting? A: teeth. We bite with our teeth.
chunks.source: We bite with our teeth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: We use a ___ and water to brush our teeth. A: toothpaste. We use toothpaste and water to brush our teeth.
chunks.source: We use toothpaste and water to brush our teeth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we use to brush our teeth. A: toothbrush. We brush our teeth with a toothbrush.
chunks.source: We brush our teeth with a toothbrush.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we brush our teeth after a meal? A: to keep our teeth clean. Brushing removes food and keeps teeth clean.
chunks.source: Brushing removes food and keeps teeth clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of caring for your teeth. A: by brushing them. We care for our teeth by brushing them.
chunks.source: We care for our teeth by brushing them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do you keep your hands clean? A: by washing them with soap and water. Washing with soap and water keeps hands clean.
chunks.source: Washing with soap and water keeps hands clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we wash our hands before eating food? A: to remove germs. Washing removes germs from our hands.
chunks.source: Washing removes germs from our hands.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people wash their hands after picking rubbish? A: to remove germs. Rubbish has germs, so we wash our hands.
chunks.source: Rubbish has germs, so we wash our hands.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we wash our hands after visiting the toilet? A: to remove germs. We wash our hands to remove germs.
chunks.source: We wash our hands to remove germs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we wash fruits before eating them? A: to remove germs. Fruits may have germs, so we wash them.
chunks.source: Fruits may have germs, so we wash them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do people do before eating food? A: wash their hands. People wash their hands before eating.
chunks.source: People wash their hands before eating.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one danger of not bathing daily. A: smelling bad. Not bathing makes us smell bad.
chunks.source: Not bathing makes us smell bad.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one danger of having a dirty body. A: diseases. A dirty body can bring diseases.
chunks.source: A dirty body can bring diseases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are toilets kept clean? A: by washing them. We keep toilets clean by washing them.
chunks.source: We keep toilets clean by washing them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are used to clean the latrine? (Choose all that apply.) A: soap, broom. Soap and a broom are used to clean the latrine.
chunks.source: Soap and a broom are used to clean the latrine.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one common disease. A: malaria. Malaria is a common disease.
chunks.source: Malaria is a common disease.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are common diseases? (Choose all that apply.) A: malaria, measles. Malaria and measles are common diseases.
chunks.source: Malaria and measles are common diseases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one immunisable disease. A: measles. Measles is an immunisable disease.
chunks.source: Measles is an immunisable disease.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are immunisable diseases? (Choose all that apply.) A: polio, measles. Polio and measles are immunisable diseases.
chunks.source: Polio and measles are immunisable diseases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one disease without a cure. A: AIDS. AIDS has no cure.
chunks.source: AIDS has no cure.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are ways of controlling diseases? (Choose all that apply.) A: boiling water for drinking, cleaning toilets. Boiling drinking water and cleaning toilets control diseases.
chunks.source: Boiling drinking water and cleaning toilets control diseases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do people keep mosquitoes away from their homes? A: by sleeping under mosquito nets. Sleeping under mosquito nets keeps mosquitoes away.
chunks.source: Sleeping under mosquito nets keeps mosquitoes away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of caring for your eyes. A: by washing them. We care for our eyes by washing them.
chunks.source: We care for our eyes by washing them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one body exercise children can do in the playground. A: skipping. Skipping is a good body exercise.
chunks.source: Skipping is a good body exercise.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these do you do after waking up? (Choose all that apply.) A: brushing teeth, bathing, washing face. After waking up we brush our teeth, bathe and wash our face.
chunks.source: After waking up we brush our teeth, bathe and wash our face.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: We wash our hands before eating food. A: True. We wash our hands before eating.
chunks.source: We wash our hands before eating.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Brushing our teeth keeps them clean. A: True. Brushing keeps our teeth clean.
chunks.source: Brushing keeps our teeth clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A dirty body can cause diseases. A: True. A dirty body can bring diseases.
chunks.source: A dirty body can bring diseases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Boiling drinking water controls diseases. A: True. Boiling water kills germs.
chunks.source: Boiling water kills germs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one use of the sun to people. A: It gives us light. The sun gives us light.
chunks.source: The sun gives us light.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which element of weather helps people to dry clothes? A: sunshine. Sunshine dries our clothes.
chunks.source: Sunshine dries our clothes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one danger of too much sunshine. A: It can make people sick. Too much sunshine can make people sick.
chunks.source: Too much sunshine can make people sick.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one danger of too much rain. A: floods. Too much rain causes floods.
chunks.source: Too much rain causes floods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one danger of floods. A: They destroy crops. Floods destroy crops and homes.
chunks.source: Floods destroy crops and homes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do we call the state of the atmosphere of a place at a given time? A: weather. We call it weather.
chunks.source: We call it weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to moving air? A: wind. Moving air is called wind.
chunks.source: Moving air is called wind.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one element of weather. A: rain. Rain is an element of weather.
chunks.source: Rain is an element of weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one type of weather. A: rainy. Rainy is a type of weather.
chunks.source: Rainy is a type of weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which element of weather is used for winnowing? A: wind. Wind is used for winnowing.
chunks.source: Wind is used for winnowing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which element of weather gives us light? A: sun. The sun gives us light.
chunks.source: The sun gives us light.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the element of weather we need when harvesting crops. A: sunshine. We need sunshine when harvesting crops.
chunks.source: We need sunshine when harvesting crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which season do farmers plant their crops? A: wet season. Farmers plant crops in the wet season.
chunks.source: Farmers plant crops in the wet season.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which season do farmers commonly harvest their crops? A: dry season. Farmers harvest crops in the dry season.
chunks.source: Farmers harvest crops in the dry season.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the two seasons we have. A: wet and dry seasons. We have the wet season and the dry season.
chunks.source: We have the wet season and the dry season.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one activity people do in the dry season. A: harvesting crops. People harvest crops in the dry season.
chunks.source: People harvest crops in the dry season.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one activity farmers do in the wet season. A: planting crops. Farmers plant crops in the wet season.
chunks.source: Farmers plant crops in the wet season.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which season do farmers water their crops? A: dry season. Farmers water crops in the dry season.
chunks.source: Farmers water crops in the dry season.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match the weather to its use. A: Windy: winnowing; Rainy: harvesting water; Sunny: drying seeds. Windy weather is for winnowing, rainy weather for harvesting water and sunny weather for drying seeds.
chunks.source: Windy weather is for winnowing, rainy weather for harvesting water and sunny weather for drying seeds.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we use on a rainy day. A: umbrella. We use an umbrella on a rainy day.
chunks.source: We use an umbrella on a rainy day.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we use to protect ourselves in rainy weather. A: raincoat. A raincoat protects us in rainy weather.
chunks.source: A raincoat protects us in rainy weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these do we use to manage rainy weather? (Choose all that apply.) A: umbrella, gumboots, raincoat. An umbrella, gumboots and a raincoat manage rainy weather.
chunks.source: An umbrella, gumboots and a raincoat manage rainy weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one weather condition where people wear sweaters. A: cold weather. People wear sweaters in cold weather.
chunks.source: People wear sweaters in cold weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one activity done during sunny weather. A: drying clothes. We dry clothes during sunny weather.
chunks.source: We dry clothes during sunny weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which clouds give us rain? A: Nimbus clouds. Nimbus clouds give us rain.
chunks.source: Nimbus clouds give us rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing that uses wind to work. A: kite. A kite uses wind to fly.
chunks.source: A kite uses wind to fly.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Wind is moving air. A: True. Wind is moving air.
chunks.source: Wind is moving air.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The sun gives us light. A: True. The sun gives us light.
chunks.source: The sun gives us light.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Farmers plant crops in the wet season. A: True. Farmers plant in the wet season.
chunks.source: Farmers plant in the wet season.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Rain gives us water. A: True. Rain gives us water.
chunks.source: Rain gives us water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these can cause accidents? (Choose all that apply.) A: razorblade, snake. A razorblade and a snake can cause accidents.
chunks.source: A razorblade and a snake can cause accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What accident is caused by broken glass? A: cuts. Broken glass causes cuts.
chunks.source: Broken glass causes cuts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What accident is caused by fire? A: burns. Fire causes burns.
chunks.source: Fire causes burns.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a sharp object. A: knife. A knife is a sharp object.
chunks.source: A knife is a sharp object.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one dangerous object. A: knife. A knife is dangerous.
chunks.source: A knife is dangerous.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one item that can cause harm to your body. A: razorblade. A razorblade can harm our body.
chunks.source: A razorblade can harm our body.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one dangerous object in the kitchen. A: knife. A knife in the kitchen is dangerous.
chunks.source: A knife in the kitchen is dangerous.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one accident at home. A: burns. Burns are accidents at home.
chunks.source: Burns are accidents at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one common accident at school. A: falling down. Falling down is a common accident at school.
chunks.source: Falling down is a common accident at school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one object that causes cuts at home. A: razorblade. A razorblade causes cuts at home.
chunks.source: A razorblade causes cuts at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one cause of accidents. A: fire. Fire is a cause of accidents.
chunks.source: Fire is a cause of accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one material we can use to stop fire. A: water. We use water to stop fire.
chunks.source: We use water to stop fire.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which name is given to the sudden happening that causes harm to the body? A: accident. We call it an accident.
chunks.source: We call it an accident.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one effect of accidents. A: injuries. Accidents cause injuries.
chunks.source: Accidents cause injuries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can children prevent accidents at school? A: by following school rules. Following school rules prevents accidents.
chunks.source: Following school rules prevents accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one traffic road sign. A: zebra crossing. A zebra crossing is a traffic road sign.
chunks.source: A zebra crossing is a traffic road sign.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do traffic road signs show drivers? A: They show drivers what to do on the road. Road signs show drivers what to do.
chunks.source: Road signs show drivers what to do.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing used to give first aid. A: bandage. A bandage is used to give first aid.
chunks.source: A bandage is used to give first aid.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A knife can cause cuts. A: True. A knife can cause cuts.
chunks.source: A knife can cause cuts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Fire can cause burns. A: True. Fire can cause burns.
chunks.source: Fire can cause burns.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: We use water to stop fire. A: True. Water stops fire.
chunks.source: Water stops fire.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one role of children in a family. A: to help with housework. Children help with housework.
chunks.source: Children help with housework.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one role of a mother in a family. A: to cook food. A mother cooks food for the family.
chunks.source: A mother cooks food for the family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one role of a father in a family. A: to pay school fees. A father pays school fees.
chunks.source: A father pays school fees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do mothers show love to their children? A: by caring for them. Mothers show love by caring for their children.
chunks.source: Mothers show love by caring for their children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which type of family do we find grandfather, uncle and aunt? A: extended family. An extended family has grandparents, uncles and aunts.
chunks.source: An extended family has grandparents, uncles and aunts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one member of an extended family. A: grandfather. A grandfather is in an extended family.
chunks.source: A grandfather is in an extended family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way children can show respect to elders. A: by greeting them. Greeting elders shows respect.
chunks.source: Greeting elders shows respect.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are ways of respecting parents? (Choose all that apply.) A: by greeting, by doing house work. Greeting parents and doing house work show respect.
chunks.source: Greeting parents and doing house work show respect.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are basic needs of a family? (Choose all that apply.) A: food, shelter. Food and shelter are basic needs.
chunks.source: Food and shelter are basic needs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one basic need of people. A: food. Food is a basic need.
chunks.source: Food is a basic need.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one group of people who need help from others. A: the sick. The sick need help from others.
chunks.source: The sick need help from others.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can you show love to other children? A: by sharing with them. We show love by sharing with others.
chunks.source: We show love by sharing with others.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: We should respect our elders. A: True. We should respect our elders.
chunks.source: We should respect our elders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Food and shelter are basic needs. A: True. Food and shelter are basic needs.
chunks.source: Food and shelter are basic needs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: An extended family has grandparents and uncles. A: True. An extended family is a big family.
chunks.source: An extended family is a big family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one place where people get food. A: market. People get food from the market.
chunks.source: People get food from the market.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are sources of food? (Choose all that apply.) A: garden, shops, market. A garden, shops and a market are sources of food.
chunks.source: A garden, shops and a market are sources of food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one source of food. A: garden. A garden is a source of food.
chunks.source: A garden is a source of food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing that gives us food. A: plants. Plants give us food.
chunks.source: Plants give us food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people eat food? A: to grow strong. People eat food to grow strong and healthy.
chunks.source: People eat food to grow strong and healthy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: We get food from the market. A: True. We buy food in the market.
chunks.source: We buy food in the market.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: People eat food to grow strong. A: True. Food makes us grow strong.
chunks.source: Food makes us grow strong.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one means of transport. A: car. A car is a means of transport.
chunks.source: A car is a means of transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which animal is used for transport? A: donkey. A donkey is used for transport.
chunks.source: A donkey is used for transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one animal that can be used for transport. A: donkey. A donkey can be used for transport.
chunks.source: A donkey can be used for transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one domestic animal used in transport. A: horse. A horse is used in transport.
chunks.source: A horse is used in transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one animal used for transport. A: camel. A camel is used for transport.
chunks.source: A camel is used for transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these animals are used for transport? (Choose all that apply.) A: horse, camel. A horse and a camel are used for transport.
chunks.source: A horse and a camel are used for transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match the means of transport to the correct type. A: Trains: railway transport; Cars: road transport; Aeroplanes: air transport; Boats: water transport. Trains use railway transport, cars use road transport, aeroplanes use air transport and boats use water transport.
chunks.source: Trains use railway transport, cars use road transport, aeroplanes use air transport and boats use water transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match the people to the means of transport. A: Captain: ship; Driver: bus; Cyclist: bicycle; Pilot: aeroplane. A captain sails a ship, a driver drives a bus, a cyclist rides a bicycle and a pilot flies an aeroplane.
chunks.source: A captain sails a ship, a driver drives a bus, a cyclist rides a bicycle and a pilot flies an aeroplane.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one means of water transport. A: boat. A boat is a means of water transport.
chunks.source: A boat is a means of water transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one means of road transport. A: car. A car is a means of road transport.
chunks.source: A car is a means of road transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one way children come to school. A: walking. Some children walk to school.
chunks.source: Some children walk to school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one means of air transport. A: aeroplane. An aeroplane is a means of air transport.
chunks.source: An aeroplane is a means of air transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one means of transport in your area. A: bicycle. A bicycle is a common means of transport.
chunks.source: A bicycle is a common means of transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is a donkey important to people? A: It is used for transport. A donkey carries people and loads.
chunks.source: A donkey carries people and loads.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A boat is a means of water transport. A: True. A boat moves on water.
chunks.source: A boat moves on water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A car is a means of road transport. A: True. A car moves on the road.
chunks.source: A car moves on the road.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: An aeroplane flies in the air. A: True. An aeroplane flies in the air.
chunks.source: An aeroplane flies in the air.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one material used to make pots. A: clay. Pots are made from clay.
chunks.source: Pots are made from clay.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do we get clay from? A: from the soil. We get clay from the soil.
chunks.source: We get clay from the soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one thing we make from clay. A: pot. We make pots from clay.
chunks.source: We make pots from clay.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one item made from animal hides. A: shoes. Shoes are made from animal hides.
chunks.source: Shoes are made from animal hides.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing made from banana fibres. A: rope. Ropes are made from banana fibres.
chunks.source: Ropes are made from banana fibres.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing made out of wood. A: chair. Chairs are made out of wood.
chunks.source: Chairs are made out of wood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing made by a carpenter. A: chair. A carpenter makes chairs.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes chairs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match the garden tools with the work they do. A: Panga: for cutting small trees; Hoe: for digging; Axe: for cutting big trees; Rake: for collecting rubbish. A panga cuts small trees, a hoe digs, an axe cuts big trees and a rake collects rubbish.
chunks.source: A panga cuts small trees, a hoe digs, an axe cuts big trees and a rake collects rubbish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the use of a hoe? A: For digging. A hoe is used for digging.
chunks.source: A hoe is used for digging.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which tool do we use when digging? A: hoe. We use a hoe for digging.
chunks.source: We use a hoe for digging.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one garden tool you know. A: hoe. A hoe is a garden tool.
chunks.source: A hoe is a garden tool.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing children make at home. A: doll. Children make dolls at home.
chunks.source: Children make dolls at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we make at school. A: basket. We make baskets at school.
chunks.source: We make baskets at school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: We make pots from clay. A: True. Pots are made from clay.
chunks.source: Pots are made from clay.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A hoe is used for digging. A: True. A hoe digs the soil.
chunks.source: A hoe digs the soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is environment? A: things surrounding us. Environment means the things surrounding us.
chunks.source: Environment means the things surrounding us.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing found in our environment. A: trees. Trees are found in our environment.
chunks.source: Trees are found in our environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one use of trees to people. A: They give us shade. Trees give us shade.
chunks.source: Trees give us shade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one activity that damages our environment. A: cutting down trees. Cutting down trees damages our environment.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees damages our environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these activities spoil our environment? (Choose all that apply.) A: burning bush, over grazing, pollution, cutting down trees, building in wetland. Burning bush, over grazing, pollution, cutting down trees and building in wetland spoil our environment.
chunks.source: Burning bush, over grazing, pollution, cutting down trees and building in wetland spoil our environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which of these activities damage our environment? (Choose all that apply.) A: Cutting trees, Burning grass. Cutting trees and burning grass damage our environment.
chunks.source: Cutting trees and burning grass damage our environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one way of conserving the environment. A: planting trees. Planting trees conserves the environment.
chunks.source: Planting trees conserves the environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one way of keeping our compound clean. A: sweeping. Sweeping keeps our compound clean.
chunks.source: Sweeping keeps our compound clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one source of water. A: rain. Rain is a source of water.
chunks.source: Rain is a source of water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the main source of water? A: rainfall. Rainfall is the main source of water.
chunks.source: Rainfall is the main source of water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the main source of water? A: rainfall. Rainfall is the main source of water.
chunks.source: Rainfall is the main source of water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one natural source of water. A: rivers. Rivers are a natural source of water.
chunks.source: Rivers are a natural source of water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one artificial source of water. A: boreholes. Boreholes are an artificial source of water.
chunks.source: Boreholes are an artificial source of water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of water to people. A: for drinking. We use water for drinking.
chunks.source: We use water for drinking.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match the things to their importance. A: Water bodies: sources of water; Soil: farming; Houses: shelter; Pencils: writing. Water bodies are sources of water, soil is for farming, houses for shelter and pencils for writing.
chunks.source: Water bodies are sources of water, soil is for farming, houses for shelter and pencils for writing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one way of caring for plants. A: by watering them. We care for plants by watering them.
chunks.source: We care for plants by watering them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Cutting down trees damages our environment. A: True. Cutting trees harms our environment.
chunks.source: Cutting trees harms our environment.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write and punctuate the sentence correctly: moslems go for prayers on Friday. -> ___ A: Moslems go for prayers on Friday.. Use capitals for names, places and months; use commas in lists.
chunks.source: Use capitals for names, places and months; use commas in lists.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write and punctuate the sentence correctly: I want to buy oranges pawpaws mangoes and apples. -> ___ A: I want to buy oranges, pawpaws, mangoes and apples.. Use capitals for names, places and months; use commas in lists.
chunks.source: Use capitals for names, places and months; use commas in lists.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly? A: Where is my pencil?. Questions start with a capital letter and end with ?.
chunks.source: Questions start with a capital letter and end with ?.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write out the adjective in the sentence: Denis has a dirty uniform. -> ___ A: dirty. 'dirty' describes the noun.
chunks.source: 'dirty' describes the noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write out the adjective in the sentence: Clever children don't shout in class. -> ___ A: Clever. 'Clever' describes the noun.
chunks.source: 'Clever' describes the noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange these adjectives from one to many: happiest, happy, happier. A: happy, happier, happiest. Happy, happier, happiest.
chunks.source: Happy, happier, happiest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the comparison table: beautiful, more beautiful, ___ A: most beautiful. Beautiful uses more/most; tall adds -er/-est.
chunks.source: Beautiful uses more/most; tall adds -er/-est.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the comparison table: tall, ___, tallest A: taller. Beautiful uses more/most; tall adds -er/-est.
chunks.source: Beautiful uses more/most; tall adds -er/-est.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: big, bigger, ___ A: biggest. Big doubles the g: biggest.
chunks.source: Big doubles the g: biggest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: tall, ___, tallest A: taller. Tall adds -er: taller.
chunks.source: Tall adds -er: taller.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: thin, ___, ___ A: thinner, thinnest. Thin doubles the n: thinner, thinnest.
chunks.source: Thin doubles the n: thinner, thinnest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: ___, shorter, ___ A: short, shortest. Short, shorter, shortest.
chunks.source: Short, shorter, shortest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: heavy, ___, heaviest A: heavier. Heavy changes y to i: heavier.
chunks.source: Heavy changes y to i: heavier.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: ___, darker, darkest A: dark. Dark, darker, darkest.
chunks.source: Dark, darker, darkest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct adjective: Musa is the ___ boy in class. (tall) A: tallest. The correct form is 'tallest'.
chunks.source: The correct form is 'tallest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct adjective: That box is ___ than mine. (heavy) A: heavier. The correct form is 'heavier'.
chunks.source: The correct form is 'heavier'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct adjective: An elephant is the ___ animal. (fat) A: fattest. The correct form is 'fattest'.
chunks.source: The correct form is 'fattest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct adjective: He is the ___ boy in our village. (poor) A: poorest. The correct form is 'poorest'.
chunks.source: The correct form is 'poorest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using 'than': Mary's handwriting is bad. Tom's handwriting is very bad. -> ___ A: Tom's handwriting is worse than Mary's.. Bad becomes worse in comparisons.
chunks.source: Bad becomes worse in comparisons.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'cheaper': A pen is cheap. A book is expensive. -> ___ A: A pen is cheaper than a book.. Cheap adds -er: cheaper.
chunks.source: Cheap adds -er: cheaper.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'My mother': My father is fat. My mother is fatter. -> ___ A: My mother is fatter than my father.. Fat doubles the t: fatter.
chunks.source: Fat doubles the t: fatter.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using 'than': Mary is tall. Tom is very tall. -> ___ A: Tom is taller than Mary.. Tall adds -er: taller.
chunks.source: Tall adds -er: taller.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange from one to many: hottest, hot, hotter. A: hot, hotter, hottest. Hot, hotter, hottest.
chunks.source: Hot, hotter, hottest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Put each adjective under the correct heading. A: One: big,tall,happy; Two (comparative): bigger,taller,happier; Many (superlative): biggest,tallest,happiest. One = plain word; two adds -er; many adds -est.
chunks.source: One = plain word; two adds -er; many adds -est.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct comparative: This box is ___ than that one. (heavy) A: heavier. Heavy changes y to i: heavier.
chunks.source: Heavy changes y to i: heavier.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Tick all the adjectives. A: dirty, clever, tall, happy. Dirty, clever, tall and happy describe things.
chunks.source: Dirty, clever, tall and happy describe things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: I saw an old woman yesterday. -> ___ A: young. The opposite is 'young'.
chunks.source: The opposite is 'young'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: Where are the lazy boys? -> ___ A: hardworking. The opposite is 'hardworking'.
chunks.source: The opposite is 'hardworking'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: Juma has a dirty bag. -> ___ A: clean. The opposite is 'clean'.
chunks.source: The opposite is 'clean'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'fat': ___ A: thin. The opposite of 'fat' is 'thin'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'fat' is 'thin'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'weak': ___ A: strong. The opposite of 'weak' is 'strong'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'weak' is 'strong'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'taller': ___ A: shorter. The opposite of 'taller' is 'shorter'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'taller' is 'shorter'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'smooth': ___ A: rough. The opposite of 'smooth' is 'rough'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'smooth' is 'rough'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'heavy': ___ A: light. The opposite of 'heavy' is 'light'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'heavy' is 'light'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'poor': ___ A: rich. The opposite of 'poor' is 'rich'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'poor' is 'rich'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: My shoes are new. -> ___ A: old. The opposite is 'old'.
chunks.source: The opposite is 'old'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: My uniform is dirty. -> ___ A: clean. The opposite is 'clean'.
chunks.source: The opposite is 'clean'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: My father is poor. -> ___ A: rich. The opposite is 'rich'.
chunks.source: The opposite is 'rich'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each word to its opposite. A: fat: thin; weak: strong; heavy: light; poor: rich; dirty: clean; new: old. Opposites are words with reverse meanings.
chunks.source: Opposites are words with reverse meanings.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The opposite of 'smooth' is 'rough'. A: True. Smooth and rough are opposites.
chunks.source: Smooth and rough are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in short: Let us -> ___ A: let's. The short form is 'let's'.
chunks.source: The short form is 'let's'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in short: Cannot -> ___ A: can't. The short form is 'can't'.
chunks.source: The short form is 'can't'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in short: Doctor -> ___ A: Dr.. The short form is 'Dr.'.
chunks.source: The short form is 'Dr.'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in short: Teacher -> ___ A: Tr.. The short form is 'Tr.'.
chunks.source: The short form is 'Tr.'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in short: Wednesday -> ___ A: Wed.. The short form is 'Wed.'.
chunks.source: The short form is 'Wed.'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in short: October -> ___ A: Oct.. The short form is 'Oct.'.
chunks.source: The short form is 'Oct.'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Dec. -> ___ A: December. The full word is 'December'.
chunks.source: The full word is 'December'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Sch. -> ___ A: School. The full word is 'School'.
chunks.source: The full word is 'School'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each word to its short form. A: Let us: let's; Cannot: can't; Doctor: Dr.; Wednesday: Wed.; October: Oct.. Short forms drop letters and use a full stop or apostrophe.
chunks.source: Short forms drop letters and use a full stop or apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct questioning word: ___ bag is this? A: Whose. The correct word is 'Whose'.
chunks.source: The correct word is 'Whose'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct questioning word: ___ many children are shouting? A: How. The correct word is 'How'.
chunks.source: The correct word is 'How'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct questioning word: ___ they know your name? A: Do. The correct word is 'Do'.
chunks.source: The correct word is 'Do'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct questioning word: ___ she go to school every day? A: Does. The correct word is 'Does'.
chunks.source: The correct word is 'Does'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct questioning word: ___ they going to church today? A: Are. The correct word is 'Are'.
chunks.source: The correct word is 'Are'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct questioning word: ___ that your mother? A: Is. The correct word is 'Is'.
chunks.source: The correct word is 'Is'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct questioning word: ___ these your books? A: Are. The correct word is 'Are'.
chunks.source: The correct word is 'Are'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct questioning word: ___ is her school? A: Where. The correct word is 'Where'.
chunks.source: The correct word is 'Where'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each question word to its use. A: Who: asks about a person; Where: asks about a place; When: asks about time; What: asks about a thing. Who = person, where = place, when = time, what = thing.
chunks.source: Who = person, where = place, when = time, what = thing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We use 'Whose' to ask about the owner of something. A: True. Whose bag is this? = Who owns this bag?
chunks.source: Whose bag is this? = Who owns this bag?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences using 'and': Mary has a dress. Anna has a dress. -> ___ A: Mary and Anna have dresses.. Use 'and' to join the two ideas.
chunks.source: Use 'and' to join the two ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences using 'and': Ali went to the shop. Ali bought a matchbox. -> ___ A: Ali went to the shop and bought a matchbox.. Use 'and' to join the two ideas.
chunks.source: Use 'and' to join the two ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences using 'and': Mark is a good boy. Richard is a good boy. -> ___ A: Mark and Richard are good boys.. Use 'and' to join the two ideas.
chunks.source: Use 'and' to join the two ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences using 'and': Tim has a shirt. Tim has a coat. -> ___ A: Tim has a shirt and a coat.. Use 'and' to join the two ideas.
chunks.source: Use 'and' to join the two ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences using 'and': Ivan was absent. Rose was absent. -> ___ A: Ivan and Rose were absent.. Use 'and' to join the two ideas.
chunks.source: Use 'and' to join the two ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed (join using 'but'): Bosco ate a lot of food. He did not get satisfied. -> ___ A: Bosco ate a lot of food but he did not get satisfied.. 'But' joins two different ideas.
chunks.source: 'But' joins two different ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed (join using 'and'): Mummy is tall. Daddy is tall. -> ___ A: Mummy and Daddy are tall.. 'And' joins two same ideas.
chunks.source: 'And' joins two same ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed (use 'because'): I cannot go to school. It is raining heavily. -> ___ A: I cannot go to school because it is raining heavily.. 'Because' gives the reason.
chunks.source: 'Because' gives the reason.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences as instructed (use 'but'): Alice has a pencil. She did not write. -> ___ A: Alice has a pencil but she did not write.. Use 'but' to join them.
chunks.source: Use 'but' to join them.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences as instructed (use 'because'): Moses did not come to school. He was very sick. -> ___ A: Moses did not come to school because he was very sick.. Use 'because' to join them.
chunks.source: Use 'because' to join them.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences as instructed (use 'who'): This is the girl. She ate my food. -> ___ A: This is the girl who ate my food.. Use 'who' to join them.
chunks.source: Use 'who' to join them.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences as instructed (use 'children'): The child is playing. (Begin: The children...) -> ___ A: The children are playing.. Use 'children' to join them.
chunks.source: Use 'children' to join them.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences as instructed (use 'and'): Tom is here. Bob is here. -> ___ A: Tom and Bob are here.. Use 'and' to join them.
chunks.source: Use 'and' to join them.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using 'but': Musa is short. Ali is tall. -> ___ A: Musa is short but Ali is tall.. 'But' joins different ideas.
chunks.source: 'But' joins different ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using 'because': He cannot build a big house. He is poor. -> ___ A: He cannot build a big house because he is poor.. 'Because' gives the reason.
chunks.source: 'Because' gives the reason.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using 'and': Mary has a book. Mary has a pencil. -> ___ A: Mary has a book and a pencil.. 'And' joins the two things.
chunks.source: 'And' joins the two things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using 'but': Paul is short. Mary is tall. -> ___ A: Paul is short but Mary is tall.. 'But' joins different ideas.
chunks.source: 'But' joins different ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using 'because': The girl fell down. She was running. -> ___ A: The girl fell down because she was running.. 'Because' gives the reason.
chunks.source: 'Because' gives the reason.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using 'and': I have a pencil. I have a book. -> ___ A: I have a pencil and a book.. 'And' joins the two things.
chunks.source: 'And' joins the two things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using 'and': Ali is in P.2 W. Jane is in P.2 W. -> ___ A: Ali and Jane are in P.2 W.. 'And' joins the two names.
chunks.source: 'And' joins the two names.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct joining word: I was sick ___ I went to the doctor. A: so. 'So' shows the result of being sick.
chunks.source: 'So' shows the result of being sick.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence: balls / we / fibres / banana / make / from. A: We, make, balls, from, banana, fibres. We make balls from banana fibres.
chunks.source: We make balls from banana fibres.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence: market / Sarah / is / to / going / the. A: Sarah, is, going, to, the, market. Sarah is going to the market.
chunks.source: Sarah is going to the market.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the sentences to make a good story. A: I wake up at six o'clock., I say my prayer., I go to the bathroom to bathe., I dress up to go to school., I arrive at school at 7.30 a.m.. First wake up, then pray, bathe, dress and go to school.
chunks.source: First wake up, then pray, bathe, dress and go to school.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence: children / school / going / are / The / to. A: The, children, are, going, to, school. The children are going to school.
chunks.source: The children are going to school.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence: Writing / teacher / on / Our / is / blackboard / the. A: Our, teacher, is, Writing, on, the, blackboard. Our teacher is writing on the blackboard.
chunks.source: Our teacher is writing on the blackboard.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence: colour / The / of / grey / my / white / is / uniform / and. A: The, colour, of, my, uniform, is, white, and, grey. The colour of my uniform is white and grey.
chunks.source: The colour of my uniform is white and grey.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Put each joining word under the correct use. A: Same ideas (and): and,both,too; Different ideas (but): but; Reason (because): because,so. And joins same ideas; but joins different ideas; because and so show reason and result.
chunks.source: And joins same ideas; but joins different ideas; because and so show reason and result.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gap with 'some' or 'any': She doesn't have ___ money. A: any. We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.
chunks.source: We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gap with 'some' or 'any': Are there ___ flowers in the vase? A: any. We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.
chunks.source: We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gap with 'some' or 'any': Moses has ___ mangoes. A: some. We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.
chunks.source: We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gap with 'some' or 'any': There is ___ sugar in the bowl. A: some. We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.
chunks.source: We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gap with 'some' or 'any': There isn't ___ salt in this soup. A: any. We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.
chunks.source: We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gap with 'some' or 'any': Is there ___ ink in the pen? A: any. We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.
chunks.source: We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gap with 'some' or 'any': The boys have ___ colours. A: some. We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.
chunks.source: We use 'some' in telling sentences and 'any' in questions and negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gap: ___ do children use to write? A: What. The correct word is 'What'.
chunks.source: The correct word is 'What'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gap: Put ___ pencils in the tin. A: some. The correct word is 'some'.
chunks.source: The correct word is 'some'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gap: He has ___ money in the bank. A: some. The correct word is 'some'.
chunks.source: The correct word is 'some'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gap: ___ takes you to school in the morning? A: Who. The correct word is 'Who'.
chunks.source: The correct word is 'Who'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gap: Is there ___ water in the pot? A: any. The correct word is 'any'.
chunks.source: The correct word is 'any'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We use 'any' in questions and negative sentences. A: True. Is there any water? There isn't any food.
chunks.source: Is there any water? There isn't any food.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'was' or 'were': The boat ___ on water. A: was. Was goes with one person or thing; were goes with many.
chunks.source: Was goes with one person or thing; were goes with many.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'was' or 'were': They ___ making mats. A: were. Was goes with one person or thing; were goes with many.
chunks.source: Was goes with one person or thing; were goes with many.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'was' or 'were': Musa ___ playing with his toys. A: was. Was goes with one person or thing; were goes with many.
chunks.source: Was goes with one person or thing; were goes with many.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We use 'were' with many people, as in 'They were happy'. A: True. Were goes with you, we and they.
chunks.source: Were goes with you, we and they.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct tense: Alex is ___ to school. (run) A: running. Is/am/are + verb-ing: running.
chunks.source: Is/am/are + verb-ing: running.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct tense: Tom and Allan are ___ to you. (wave) A: waving. Is/am/are + verb-ing: waving.
chunks.source: Is/am/are + verb-ing: waving.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct tense: I am ___ now. (pray) A: praying. Is/am/are + verb-ing: praying.
chunks.source: Is/am/are + verb-ing: praying.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'is' or 'are' correctly: The girls ___ going to school. A: are. Girls = many, so we use 'are'.
chunks.source: Girls = many, so we use 'are'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct tense: The teacher is ___ her children. (teach) A: teaching. Is + verb-ing: teaching.
chunks.source: Is + verb-ing: teaching.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct tense: Sherinah and Priva are ___ netball. (play) A: playing. Are + verb-ing: playing.
chunks.source: Are + verb-ing: playing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: The children are ___ a song. (sing) A: singing. Are + verb-ing: singing.
chunks.source: Are + verb-ing: singing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct present continuous sentence. A: She is reading a book.. She goes with 'is' + verb-ing.
chunks.source: She goes with 'is' + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for many: tables, chairs, desks are ___ A: furniture. They are all 'furniture'.
chunks.source: They are all 'furniture'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for many: pawpaws, oranges are ___ A: fruits. They are all 'fruits'.
chunks.source: They are all 'fruits'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for many: red, blue, pink, black are ___ A: colours. They are all 'colours'.
chunks.source: They are all 'colours'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for many: Tuesday, Thursday, Monday are ___ A: days. They are all 'days'.
chunks.source: They are all 'days'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined group of words: Dogs, cats, sheep, elephants, lions and tigers are all ___ A: animals. They are all 'animals'.
chunks.source: They are all 'animals'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined group of words: Apples, mangoes, pineapples and oranges are all ___ A: fruits. They are all 'fruits'.
chunks.source: They are all 'fruits'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Put each word under the correct group name. A: Furniture: tables,chairs,desks; Fruits: mangoes,oranges,pawpaws; Colours: red,blue,black; Days: Monday,Tuesday,Friday. Each group has one name for many words.
chunks.source: Each group has one name for many words.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Answer in a full sentence: Are these desks? -> ___ A: Yes, they are.. These -> they are. This -> it is.
chunks.source: These -> they are. This -> it is.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Answer in a full sentence: Is this a chair? -> ___ A: Yes, it is.. These -> they are. This -> it is.
chunks.source: These -> they are. This -> it is.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Answer in a full sentence: What is this? -> ___ A: This is a desk.. These -> they are. This -> it is.
chunks.source: These -> they are. This -> it is.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct answer: Are these balls? A: Yes, they are.. These goes with they are.
chunks.source: These goes with they are.

chunks.text: Q: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a story. A: Jojo wanted to have a chair., So, Jojo went to a carpenter., He asked the carpenter to make one for him., The carpenter told him to pay some money to help him buy the materials., The carpenter bought timber and nails and made a good chair for him.. Jojo wants a chair, visits the carpenter, asks, pays, and gets the chair.

chunks.text: Q: What is a set? A: A group of things. A set is a group of things put together.
chunks.source: A set is a group of things put together.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Things found in a set are called ___. A: members. Each thing in a set is called a member.
chunks.source: Each thing in a set is called a member.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which is the symbol of an empty set? A: Ø. The symbol Ø (or { }) stands for an empty set.
chunks.source: The symbol Ø (or { }) stands for an empty set.

chunks.text: Q: Look at the symbol in the picture. What is its name? A: intersection. The symbol ∩ means intersection, the common part of two sets.

chunks.source: Name a set by what is inside it; a, e, i, o, u are vowels.

chunks.text: Q: Set B has ___ members. A: 3. Set B holds 3 cups.

chunks.source: Set A holds 5 girls.

chunks.text: Q: Which set has more members? A: Set A. Set A has 5 members and set B has 3.
chunks.source: Set A has 5 members and set B has 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many members are there altogether? A: 8. 5 girls and 3 cups make 8 members.
chunks.source: 5 girls and 3 cups make 8 members.

chunks.text: Q: Which set comes first in ascending order? A: Set C. Set C has 1 member, the fewest of all.

chunks.text: Q: Which set comes second in ascending order? A: Set A. Set A has 3 members, the next fewest after set C.

chunks.text: Q: How many members are in set B? A: 5. Set B has 5 members.

chunks.text: Q: How many members are there altogether? A: 13. 3 + 5 + 1 + 4 = 13 members.

chunks.text: Q: Denis weighs 22 kg and Molly weighs 36 kg. Find their total mass.? A: 58. 22 + 36 = 58 kg.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one part found on the head of an insect: ____. A: antenna. Insects have antennae, eyes and mouthparts on the head.
chunks.source: Insects have antennae, eyes and mouthparts on the head.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one item used in cleaning a bedroom: ____. A: broom. We use a broom to sweep the floor and keep the bedroom clean.
chunks.source: We use a broom to sweep the floor and keep the bedroom clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one danger of playing with hot water: ____. A: You can burn your skin.. Hot water can burn the skin and make painful wounds.
chunks.source: Hot water can burn the skin and make painful wounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The picture shows a clay pot. How is this item useful at home? ____. A: It is used for storing drinking water.. A clay pot keeps drinking water clean and cool at home.
chunks.source: A clay pot keeps drinking water clean and cool at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one health activity we do before eating food: ____. A: washing our hands. Washing hands before eating removes germs that cause diseases.
chunks.source: Washing hands before eating removes germs that cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of making water safe for drinking: ____. A: boiling. Boiling water kills the germs that cause diseases.
chunks.source: Boiling water kills the germs that cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the second stage in the life cycle of a cockroach: ____. A: nymph. A cockroach grows from an egg into a nymph and then into an adult.
chunks.source: A cockroach grows from an egg into a nymph and then into an adult.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one material people use to give first aid (1): ____. A: bandage. A bandage is used to cover a wound when giving first aid.
chunks.source: A bandage is used to cover a wound when giving first aid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one material people use to give first aid (2): ____. A: plaster. A plaster is used to cover a small cut when giving first aid.
chunks.source: A plaster is used to cover a small cut when giving first aid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are goats grouped under living things? ____. A: Goats breathe and move.. Goats are living things because they breathe, move, feed and grow.
chunks.source: Goats are living things because they breathe, move, feed and grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one fruit tree found in your school compound (1): ____. A: mango tree. A mango tree is a fruit tree that grows mangoes.
chunks.source: A mango tree is a fruit tree that grows mangoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one fruit tree found in your school compound (2): ____. A: orange tree. An orange tree is a fruit tree that grows oranges.
chunks.source: An orange tree is a fruit tree that grows oranges.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we wash our hands after picking rubbish? ____. A: To remove germs and prevent diseases.. Rubbish has germs, so we wash our hands to stay healthy.
chunks.source: Rubbish has germs, so we wash our hands to stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do people care for domestic animals (1)? ____. A: feeding them. We care for domestic animals by giving them food to eat.
chunks.source: We care for domestic animals by giving them food to eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do people care for domestic animals (2)? ____. A: giving them clean water. We care for domestic animals by giving them clean water to drink.
chunks.source: We care for domestic animals by giving them clean water to drink.

chunks.text: Q: The picture shows fish over fire. Name this method of food preservation: ____. A: smoking. Smoking dries fish over fire so it stays good for a long time.
chunks.source: Smoking dries fish over fire so it stays good for a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The picture shows the sun drying beans. Name this method of food preservation: ____. A: drying. Drying in the sun removes water from food so it stays good for a long time.
chunks.source: Drying in the sun removes water from food so it stays good for a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one importance of insects to people: ____. A: Bees give us honey.. Some insects are useful; bees give us sweet honey.
chunks.source: Some insects are useful; bees give us sweet honey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one danger of poor feeding in children: ____. A: It causes malnutrition.. Children who do not eat well become weak and sick.
chunks.source: Children who do not eat well become weak and sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write the use of wings to an insect: ____. A: Wings help the insect to fly.. Insects use their wings to fly from place to place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one item used in managing rainy weather: ____. A: umbrella. An umbrella keeps us dry when it rains.
chunks.source: An umbrella keeps us dry when it rains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one farm activity done in a dry season: ____. A: weeding. In the dry season farmers weed their gardens.
chunks.source: In the dry season farmers weed their gardens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Of what use is the nose to a P.2 child? ____. A: The nose is used for smelling.. We use the nose to smell things around us.
chunks.source: We use the nose to smell things around us.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one use of a house to people: ____. A: A house gives us shelter.. A house protects us from rain, sun and thieves.
chunks.source: A house protects us from rain, sun and thieves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one good eating habit: ____. A: washing hands before eating. Washing hands before eating keeps germs away from our food.
chunks.source: Washing hands before eating keeps germs away from our food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do people care for their plants in the garden (1)? ____. A: watering them. Plants need water to grow well.
chunks.source: Plants need water to grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do people care for their plants in the garden (2)? ____. A: weeding. Removing weeds helps garden plants grow well.
chunks.source: Removing weeds helps garden plants grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we eat food (1)? ____. A: to get energy. Food gives our bodies energy to play and work.
chunks.source: Food gives our bodies energy to play and work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we eat food (2)? ____. A: to grow. Food helps our bodies grow big and strong.
chunks.source: Food helps our bodies grow big and strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one correct way of controlling diseases (1): ____. A: immunisation. Immunisation protects children from killer diseases.
chunks.source: Immunisation protects children from killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one correct way of controlling diseases (2): ____. A: keeping our surroundings clean. A clean home and compound keep diseases away.
chunks.source: A clean home and compound keep diseases away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one element of weather (2): ____. A: sunshine. Sunshine is the light and heat we get from the sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of wind to people (1): ____. A: drying clothes. Wind helps our wet clothes dry faster.

chunks.text: Q: Give one use of wind to people (2): ____. A: winnowing. Farmers use wind to winnow, separating grain from chaff.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we do that damages our environment: ____. A: cutting down trees. Cutting down trees without planting new ones damages our environment.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees without planting new ones damages our environment.

chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we can do to make our environment safe and good: ____. A: planting trees. Planting trees keeps our environment safe and beautiful.
chunks.source: Planting trees keeps our environment safe and beautiful.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each road sign to its correct name: (a) black-and-white striped sign, (b) sign with a bumpy road, (c) sign with an exclamation mark (!), (d) sign with two children. A: (a) black-and-white striped sign: Zebra crossing; (b) sign with a bumpy road: Humps ahead; (c) sign with an exclamation mark (!): Danger ahead; (d) sign with two children: School ahead. Road signs warn drivers: zebra crossing is for people to cross, humps slow cars, ! means danger, children means a school is near.
chunks.source: Road signs warn drivers: zebra crossing is for people to cross, humps slow cars, ! means danger, children means a school is near.
