chunks.source: People tell morning, afternoon and evening by where the sun is in the sky.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One natural thing used to tell time is rainy weather. True or False? A: False. People tell morning, afternoon and evening by where the sun is in the sky.
chunks.source: People tell morning, afternoon and evening by where the sun is in the sky.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wind is useful to people because it ____. A: dries our clothes. Wind moves air and helps wet clothes dry fast on the line.
chunks.source: Wind moves air and helps wet clothes dry fast on the line.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wind is useful to people because it dries our clothes. True or False? A: True. Wind moves air and helps wet clothes dry fast on the line.
chunks.source: Wind moves air and helps wet clothes dry fast on the line.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ weather helps people to play with a kite. A: Windy. A kite needs moving air to lift it up into the sky.
chunks.source: A kite needs moving air to lift it up into the sky.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: wind weather helps people to play with a kite. True or False? A: False. A kite needs moving air to lift it up into the sky.
chunks.source: A kite needs moving air to lift it up into the sky.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one danger of too much rainfall: ____. (i) A: floods. Too much rain fills rivers and floods homes and gardens.
chunks.source: Too much rain fills rivers and floods homes and gardens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One danger of too much rainfall is floods. True or False? A: True. Too much rain fills rivers and floods homes and gardens.
chunks.source: Too much rain fills rivers and floods homes and gardens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another danger of too much rainfall: ____. (ii) A: destroying crops. Heavy rain can wash away crops and break houses.
chunks.source: Heavy rain can wash away crops and break houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another danger of too much rainfall? the sun. True or False? A: False. Heavy rain can wash away crops and break houses.
chunks.source: Heavy rain can wash away crops and break houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one season of the year: ____. (i) A: rainy season. In the rainy season it rains almost every day.
chunks.source: In the rainy season it rains almost every day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One season of the year is rainy season. True or False? A: True. In the rainy season it rains almost every day.
chunks.source: In the rainy season it rains almost every day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write another season of the year: ____. (ii) A: dry season. In the dry season there is sunshine and little rain.
chunks.source: In the dry season there is sunshine and little rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write another season of the year? windy weather. True or False? A: False. In the dry season there is sunshine and little rain.
chunks.source: In the dry season there is sunshine and little rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the item shown in the picture that we use to protect ourselves in rainy weather: ____. A: umbrella. An umbrella keeps rain off our bodies when we walk in the rain.
chunks.source: An umbrella keeps rain off our bodies when we walk in the rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The item shown in the picture that we use to protect ourselves in rainy weather is umbrella. True or False? A: True. An umbrella keeps rain off our bodies when we walk in the rain.
chunks.source: An umbrella keeps rain off our bodies when we walk in the rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The sun is useful to people because it gives us ____. A: light. Sunlight lights our world during the day so we can see.
chunks.source: Sunlight lights our world during the day so we can see.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The sun is useful to people because it gives us rain. True or False? A: False. Sunlight lights our world during the day so we can see.
chunks.source: Sunlight lights our world during the day so we can see.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one type of weather shown in the picture: ____. A: rainy. When drops fall from clouds, the weather is rainy.
chunks.source: When drops fall from clouds, the weather is rainy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One type of weather shown in the picture is rainy. True or False? A: True. When drops fall from clouds, the weather is rainy.
chunks.source: When drops fall from clouds, the weather is rainy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another type of weather shown in the picture: ____. A: sunny. When the sun shines brightly, the weather is sunny.
chunks.source: When the sun shines brightly, the weather is sunny.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another type of weather shown in the picture? drought. True or False? A: False. When the sun shines brightly, the weather is sunny.
chunks.source: When the sun shines brightly, the weather is sunny.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name a third type of weather shown in the picture: ____. A: windy. When air moves fast and bends trees, the weather is windy.
chunks.source: When air moves fast and bends trees, the weather is windy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name a third type of weather shown in the picture? windy. True or False? A: True. When air moves fast and bends trees, the weather is windy.
chunks.source: When air moves fast and bends trees, the weather is windy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one element of weather: ____. A: rain. Rain is one of the elements of weather, along with sun and wind.
chunks.source: Rain is one of the elements of weather, along with sun and wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one element of weather: floods. True or False? A: False. Rain is one of the elements of weather, along with sun and wind.
chunks.source: Rain is one of the elements of weather, along with sun and wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The element of weather that moves things is ____. A: wind. Wind is moving air that can push leaves and clothes.
chunks.source: Wind is moving air that can push leaves and clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The element of weather that moves things is wind. True or False? A: True. Wind is moving air that can push leaves and clothes.
chunks.source: Wind is moving air that can push leaves and clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of water to people: ____. A: drinking. People drink water every day to stay alive and healthy.
chunks.source: People drink water every day to stay alive and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of water to people is washing. True or False? A: False. People drink water every day to stay alive and healthy.
chunks.source: People drink water every day to stay alive and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one source of water for washing clothes: ____. A: a well. We fetch water for washing from a well, a borehole or a tap.
chunks.source: We fetch water for washing from a well, a borehole or a tap.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One source of water for washing clothes is a well. True or False? A: True. We fetch water for washing from a well, a borehole or a tap.
chunks.source: We fetch water for washing from a well, a borehole or a tap.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of water to people: ____. (a) A: drinking. People drink water to live.
chunks.source: People drink water to live.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of water to people is rivers. True or False? A: False. People drink water to live.
chunks.source: People drink water to live.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another use of water to people: ____. (b) A: cooking. We use water to cook food like rice and beans.
chunks.source: We use water to cook food like rice and beans.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another use of water to people? cooking. True or False? A: True. We use water to cook food like rice and beans.
chunks.source: We use water to cook food like rice and beans.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of water to people: ____. A: drinking. We must drink water every day to stay alive.
chunks.source: We must drink water every day to stay alive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of water to people is boiling. True or False? A: False. We must drink water every day to stay alive.
chunks.source: We must drink water every day to stay alive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The main source of water is ____. A: rain. Rain fills rivers, wells and lakes with water.
chunks.source: Rain fills rivers, wells and lakes with water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The main source of water is rain. True or False? A: True. Rain fills rivers, wells and lakes with water.
chunks.source: Rain fills rivers, wells and lakes with water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one use of water: ____. A: drinking. We drink water to stay alive and healthy.
chunks.source: We drink water to stay alive and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one use of water: jerrycan. True or False? A: False. We drink water to stay alive and healthy.
chunks.source: We drink water to stay alive and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one source of water: ____. (i) A: rain. Rain is a source of water we collect.
chunks.source: Rain is a source of water we collect.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one source of water: rain. True or False? A: True. Rain is a source of water we collect.
chunks.source: Rain is a source of water we collect.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify another source of water: ____. (ii) A: well. We fetch water from a well.
chunks.source: We fetch water from a well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify another source of water: jerrycan. True or False? A: False. We fetch water from a well.
chunks.source: We fetch water from a well.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a school? A: a place where children go to learn. A school is a place where children go to learn to read, write and count.
chunks.source: A school is a place where children go to learn to read, write and count.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need class rules? A: to keep order in the classroom. Class rules help us behave well and keep order in the classroom.
chunks.source: Class rules help us behave well and keep order in the classroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing a school can buy from the neighbourhood. A: food. A school buys food, firewood and other things from the neighbourhood.
chunks.source: A school buys food, firewood and other things from the neighbourhood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one item used to clean our classroom. A: broom. We use brooms, mops and dusters to clean the classroom.
chunks.source: We use brooms, mops and dusters to clean the classroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another item used to clean our classroom. A: mop. We use brooms, mops and dusters to clean the classroom.
chunks.source: We use brooms, mops and dusters to clean the classroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one school symbol found on a school uniform. A: school badge. School symbols on a uniform are the school badge, school motto and school colours.
chunks.source: School symbols on a uniform are the school badge, school motto and school colours.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another school symbol found on a school uniform. A: school motto. School symbols on a uniform are the school badge, school motto and school colours.
chunks.source: School symbols on a uniform are the school badge, school motto and school colours.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing used to locate our school. A: signpost. A signpost and the school flag help people locate our school.
chunks.source: A signpost and the school flag help people locate our school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing used to locate our school. A: school flag. A signpost and the school flag help people locate our school.
chunks.source: A signpost and the school flag help people locate our school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing teachers use to teach children. A: chalk. Teachers use chalk, books, charts and pens to teach children.
chunks.source: Teachers use chalk, books, charts and pens to teach children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing teachers use to teach children. A: books. Teachers use chalk, books, charts and pens to teach children.
chunks.source: Teachers use chalk, books, charts and pens to teach children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the tool used at school to change lessons. A: bell. The bell is rung at school to show that lessons have changed.
chunks.source: The bell is rung at school to show that lessons have changed.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is a school important in a community? A: children get education. A school is important because children get education there.
chunks.source: A school is important because children get education there.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match each person to their correct workplace. A: Teacher: school; Doctor: hospital; Farmer: garden; Carpenter: factory. Teachers work at school, doctors at the hospital, farmers in the garden and carpenters in a factory.
chunks.source: Teachers work at school, doctors at the hospital, farmers in the garden and carpenters in a factory.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do we find the headmaster in a school? A: office. The headmaster stays in the school office.
chunks.source: The headmaster stays in the school office.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which school symbol helps people to locate our school? A: signpost. The school signpost is put along the road to help people locate the school.
chunks.source: The school signpost is put along the road to help people locate the school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one thing a school gets from its neighbourhood. A: food. A school gets food, water and firewood from its neighbourhood.
chunks.source: A school gets food, water and firewood from its neighbourhood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one cause of problems between a school and its neighbourhood. A: noise made by children. Noise made by children can cause problems between a school and its neighbourhood.
chunks.source: Noise made by children can cause problems between a school and its neighbourhood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match each person to their correct workplace. A: librarian: library; nurse: sick bay; headteacher: office; cooks: kitchen. The librarian works in the library, the nurse in the sick bay, the headteacher in the office and the cooks in the kitchen.
chunks.source: The librarian works in the library, the nurse in the sick bay, the headteacher in the office and the cooks in the kitchen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the importance of school symbols? A: they make our school different from others. School symbols make our school different from other schools.
chunks.source: School symbols make our school different from other schools.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do you come to school? A: to get education. We come to school to get education and learn new things.
chunks.source: We come to school to get education and learn new things.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one importance of a school sign post. A: it helps people locate the school. The school sign post helps people locate the school.
chunks.source: The school sign post helps people locate the school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one cause of problems between the school and the neighbourhood. A: children destroying crops in the neighbourhood. When school children destroy crops in the neighbourhood, it causes problems.
chunks.source: When school children destroy crops in the neighbourhood, it causes problems.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one activity done by children at school. A: playing. Children learn, play and sing at school.
chunks.source: Children learn, play and sing at school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we use to locate our school. A: signpost. A signpost and the school flag help people locate our school.
chunks.source: A signpost and the school flag help people locate our school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing teachers use to teach children. A: chalkboard. Teachers use the chalkboard, charts, books and chalk to teach children.
chunks.source: Teachers use the chalkboard, charts, books and chalk to teach children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing teachers use to teach children. A: charts. Teachers use the chalkboard, charts, books and chalk to teach children.
chunks.source: Teachers use the chalkboard, charts, books and chalk to teach children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is a school important to its neighbourhood? A: it educates children of the neighbourhood. A school is important to its neighbourhood because it educates the children there.
chunks.source: A school is important to its neighbourhood because it educates the children there.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where can you find the nurse in a school? A: sick bay. The nurse is found in the sick bay where sick children are treated.
chunks.source: The nurse is found in the sick bay where sick children are treated.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where can you find the librarian in a school? A: library. The librarian is found in the library where books are kept.
chunks.source: The librarian is found in the library where books are kept.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where can you find the headmaster in a school? A: office. The headmaster is found in the school office.
chunks.source: The headmaster is found in the school office.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do cleaners keep our school clean? A: by sweeping the classrooms. Cleaners keep our school clean by sweeping classrooms and mopping floors.
chunks.source: Cleaners keep our school clean by sweeping classrooms and mopping floors.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How else do cleaners keep our school clean? A: by mopping the floors. Cleaners keep our school clean by sweeping classrooms and mopping floors.
chunks.source: Cleaners keep our school clean by sweeping classrooms and mopping floors.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one activity done at school. A: reading. Children read, write and play at school.
chunks.source: Children read, write and play at school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give another activity done at school. A: writing. Children read, write and play at school.
chunks.source: Children read, write and play at school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need cleaners in a school? A: to keep the school clean. We need cleaners in a school to keep the school clean and healthy.
chunks.source: We need cleaners in a school to keep the school clean and healthy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do children go to learn? A: school. Children go to school to learn to read, write and count.
chunks.source: Children go to school to learn to read, write and count.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one thing children use for writing. A: pencil. Children use pencils and pens for writing in their books.
chunks.source: Children use pencils and pens for writing in their books.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing found on the school sign post. A: school name. The school name is written on the school sign post.
chunks.source: The school name is written on the school sign post.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one school symbol. A: school flag. School symbols are the school flag, school badge, school motto and school anthem.
chunks.source: School symbols are the school flag, school badge, school motto and school anthem.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Draw and name any one thing found in a classroom. A: desk. We find desks, chairs, chalkboards and books in a classroom.
chunks.source: We find desks, chairs, chalkboards and books in a classroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of preventing problems between the school and neighbourhood. A: by respecting people's property in the neighbourhood. We prevent problems by respecting people's property and keeping noise down.
chunks.source: We prevent problems by respecting people's property and keeping noise down.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we go to school? A: to learn to read and write. We go to school to learn to read, write and count.
chunks.source: We go to school to learn to read, write and count.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any one example of a flag. A: national flag. Examples of flags are the national flag and the school flag.
chunks.source: Examples of flags are the national flag and the school flag.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Choose the people found at school. A: teacher, children, librarian. Teachers, children and the librarian are found at school.
chunks.source: Teachers, children and the librarian are found at school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are school symbols? A: things that make a school different from others. School symbols are things that make a school different from other schools.
chunks.source: School symbols are things that make a school different from other schools.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the story about? A: school symbols. The story is about school symbols like the badge, motto, uniform, flag and anthem.
chunks.source: The story is about school symbols like the badge, motto, uniform, flag and anthem.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one symbol listed in the story. A: school badge. The story lists the school badge, school motto, school uniform, school address, school flag and school anthem.
chunks.source: The story lists the school badge, school motto, school uniform, school address, school flag and school anthem.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the use of a school signpost. A: it directs people to the school. A school signpost directs people to the school.
chunks.source: A school signpost directs people to the school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which school symbol makes children look smart? A: school uniform. The school uniform makes children look different and smart.
chunks.source: The school uniform makes children look different and smart.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: I am found at school. All school books are kept inside me. What am I? A: library. The library is found at school and all school books are kept inside it.
chunks.source: The library is found at school and all school books are kept inside it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: I am black and have the shape of a rectangle. Teachers write on me. You clean me with a duster. What am I? A: blackboard. The blackboard is black and rectangle-shaped. Teachers write on it and we clean it with a duster.
chunks.source: The blackboard is black and rectangle-shaped. Teachers write on it and we clean it with a duster.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: I sit in the office with a machine in front of me. I type letters and exams for the school. Who am I? A: secretary. The secretary sits in the office and types letters and exams for the school.
chunks.source: The secretary sits in the office and types letters and exams for the school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one member of an extended family. A: uncle. An extended family has parents, children and other relatives like uncles, aunts, cousins and grandparents.
chunks.source: An extended family has parents, children and other relatives like uncles, aunts, cousins and grandparents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one important place in a community where people go for treatment. A: hospital. Sick people go to the hospital or clinic for treatment.
chunks.source: Sick people go to the hospital or clinic for treatment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are cultural practices important to people? A: they bring people together. Cultural practices like naming and weddings bring people together and make them happy.
chunks.source: Cultural practices like naming and weddings bring people together and make them happy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one item found in a bedroom. A: bed. We find beds, blankets, pillows and clothes in a bedroom.
chunks.source: We find beds, blankets, pillows and clothes in a bedroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another item found in a bedroom. A: blanket. We find beds, blankets, pillows and clothes in a bedroom.
chunks.source: We find beds, blankets, pillows and clothes in a bedroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are markets important to people? A: people buy and sell things there. Markets are important because people buy and sell things there.
chunks.source: Markets are important because people buy and sell things there.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one role of children at home. A: sweeping the compound. Children help at home by sweeping, washing utensils and fetching water.
chunks.source: Children help at home by sweeping, washing utensils and fetching water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give another role of children at home. A: washing utensils. Children help at home by sweeping, washing utensils and fetching water.
chunks.source: Children help at home by sweeping, washing utensils and fetching water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do people keep their money safely? A: bank. People keep their money safely in a bank.
chunks.source: People keep their money safely in a bank.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we keep dogs at home? A: to guard our homes. We keep dogs at home to guard our homes and keep thieves away.
chunks.source: We keep dogs at home to guard our homes and keep thieves away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one activity done by people in our community. A: farming. People in our community do farming, trading, building and fishing.
chunks.source: People in our community do farming, trading, building and fishing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another activity done by people in our community. A: trading. People in our community do farming, trading, building and fishing.
chunks.source: People in our community do farming, trading, building and fishing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one basic need of a family. A: food. The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.
chunks.source: The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a nuclear family? A: a family of father, mother and their children. A nuclear family is made of the father, mother and their children.
chunks.source: A nuclear family is made of the father, mother and their children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How useful are builders in a community? A: they build houses for us. Builders are useful because they build houses, schools and shops for us.
chunks.source: Builders are useful because they build houses, schools and shops for us.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which type of family do we find uncles? A: extended family. We find uncles, aunts and cousins in an extended family.
chunks.source: We find uncles, aunts and cousins in an extended family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need flowers in our homes? A: to make our homes beautiful. Flowers make our homes beautiful and give a good smell.
chunks.source: Flowers make our homes beautiful and give a good smell.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is culture? A: the way of life of people. Culture is the way of life of people, like their food, dress and dances.
chunks.source: Culture is the way of life of people, like their food, dress and dances.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one duty of children at home. A: fetching water. Children help at home by fetching water, sweeping and washing utensils.
chunks.source: Children help at home by fetching water, sweeping and washing utensils.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one activity carried out in a community. A: fishing. People in a community do farming, trading, fishing and building.
chunks.source: People in a community do farming, trading, fishing and building.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need doctors in a community? A: to treat sick people. Doctors treat sick people in our community.
chunks.source: Doctors treat sick people in our community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one basic need of a family. A: shelter. The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.
chunks.source: The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to a group of people related by blood or marriage? A: family. A group of people related by blood or marriage is called a family.
chunks.source: A group of people related by blood or marriage is called a family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one role of a father at home. A: providing basic needs. A father provides the basic needs of the family like food and school fees.
chunks.source: A father provides the basic needs of the family like food and school fees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down one common ceremony that takes place at home. A: wedding. Common ceremonies at home are weddings and naming ceremonies.
chunks.source: Common ceremonies at home are weddings and naming ceremonies.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down another common ceremony that takes place at home. A: naming ceremony. Common ceremonies at home are weddings and naming ceremonies.
chunks.source: Common ceremonies at home are weddings and naming ceremonies.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are domestic animals? A: animals kept at home. Domestic animals are animals kept at home, like cows, goats, dogs and hens.
chunks.source: Domestic animals are animals kept at home, like cows, goats, dogs and hens.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of cows to us. A: they give us milk. Cows give us milk, meat and skins.
chunks.source: Cows give us milk, meat and skins.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one member of an extended family. A: aunt. An extended family has parents, children and other relatives like uncles, aunts, cousins and grandparents.
chunks.source: An extended family has parents, children and other relatives like uncles, aunts, cousins and grandparents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the role of a mother at home? A: cooking food for the family. A mother cooks food and cares for the children at home.
chunks.source: A mother cooks food and cares for the children at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people keep dogs at home? A: to guard our homes. People keep dogs at home to guard the home and keep thieves away.
chunks.source: People keep dogs at home to guard the home and keep thieves away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of a house to us. A: we live in it. A house gives us shelter. We live and sleep in it.
chunks.source: A house gives us shelter. We live and sleep in it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is a carpenter important in a community? A: he makes furniture for us. A carpenter is important because he makes furniture like tables and chairs for us.
chunks.source: A carpenter is important because he makes furniture like tables and chairs for us.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one cultural practice in the community. A: naming. Cultural practices in the community are naming, weddings and circumcision.
chunks.source: Cultural practices in the community are naming, weddings and circumcision.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which room of the house do we bathe from? A: bathroom. We bathe in the bathroom of the house.
chunks.source: We bathe in the bathroom of the house.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Choose one thing that we find in a kitchen. A: saucepan. We find saucepans and basins in a kitchen. A television is found in the sitting room.
chunks.source: We find saucepans and basins in a kitchen. A television is found in the sitting room.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one role of children at home. A: washing clothes. Children help at home by washing clothes, sweeping and fetching water.
chunks.source: Children help at home by washing clothes, sweeping and fetching water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to a group of people related by blood or marriage? A: family. A group of people related by blood or marriage is called a family.
chunks.source: A group of people related by blood or marriage is called a family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one basic need of a family. A: clothing. The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.
chunks.source: The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which type of family do we find a grandmother? A: extended family. We find grandmothers, uncles and cousins in an extended family.
chunks.source: We find grandmothers, uncles and cousins in an extended family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one activity done by people in our community. A: building. People in our community do building, fishing, farming and trading.
chunks.source: People in our community do building, fishing, farming and trading.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write another activity done by people in our community. A: fishing. People in our community do building, fishing, farming and trading.
chunks.source: People in our community do building, fishing, farming and trading.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Choose two religious leaders in our community. A: pastors, reverends. Pastors and reverends are religious leaders in our community.
chunks.source: Pastors and reverends are religious leaders in our community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a cultural practice. A: naming. Naming and weddings are examples of cultural practices.
chunks.source: Naming and weddings are examples of cultural practices.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give another example of a cultural practice. A: wedding. Naming and weddings are examples of cultural practices.
chunks.source: Naming and weddings are examples of cultural practices.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the importance of cultural practices. A: they unite people. Cultural practices are important because they unite people.
chunks.source: Cultural practices are important because they unite people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match each person to their correct work. A: Doctors: treat sick people; Teachers: teach children; Police woman: keeps law and order. Doctors treat sick people, teachers teach children and the police keep law and order.
chunks.source: Doctors treat sick people, teachers teach children and the police keep law and order.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can you care for a baby at home? A: by feeding the baby. We care for a baby by feeding, bathing and carrying it.
chunks.source: We care for a baby by feeding, bathing and carrying it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A ___ is a group of people related by blood or marriage. A: family. A family is a group of people related by blood or marriage.
chunks.source: A family is a group of people related by blood or marriage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing found in a home. A: cup. We find cups, televisions and baskets in a home.
chunks.source: We find cups, televisions and baskets in a home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing found in a home. A: television. We find cups, televisions and baskets in a home.
chunks.source: We find cups, televisions and baskets in a home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one more thing found in a home. A: basket. We find cups, televisions and baskets in a home.
chunks.source: We find cups, televisions and baskets in a home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one room found in a good house. A: bedroom. A good house has a bedroom, kitchen, sitting room and bathroom.
chunks.source: A good house has a bedroom, kitchen, sitting room and bathroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another room found in a good house. A: kitchen. A good house has a bedroom, kitchen, sitting room and bathroom.
chunks.source: A good house has a bedroom, kitchen, sitting room and bathroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is a father important in a home? A: he provides for the family. A father is important because he provides food and pays school fees for the family.
chunks.source: A father is important because he provides food and pays school fees for the family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one important place found in the community. A: church. Churches and mosques are important places of worship in the community.
chunks.source: Churches and mosques are important places of worship in the community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another important place found in the community. A: mosque. Churches and mosques are important places of worship in the community.
chunks.source: Churches and mosques are important places of worship in the community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Choose two things found in a bathroom. A: soap, water. We find soap and water in a bathroom. We use them to wash our bodies.
chunks.source: We find soap and water in a bathroom. We use them to wash our bodies.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one role of children at home. A: mopping the house. Children help at home by mopping the house, sweeping and fetching water.
chunks.source: Children help at home by mopping the house, sweeping and fetching water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need a dog at home? A: to keep thieves away. We keep a dog at home to keep thieves away and guard the home.
chunks.source: We keep a dog at home to keep thieves away and guard the home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one person found at home. A: father. Father, mother, brothers and sisters are people found at home.
chunks.source: Father, mother, brothers and sisters are people found at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another person found at home. A: brother. Father, mother, brothers and sisters are people found at home.
chunks.source: Father, mother, brothers and sisters are people found at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of water at home. A: for cooking. We use water at home for cooking, drinking, washing and bathing.
chunks.source: We use water at home for cooking, drinking, washing and bathing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one role of a barber in our community. A: he cuts people's hair. A barber cuts people's hair in our community.
chunks.source: A barber cuts people's hair in our community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the work of religious leaders in our community? A: they lead prayers. Religious leaders lead prayers and teach people to do good.
chunks.source: Religious leaders lead prayers and teach people to do good.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do deaf people communicate to others? A: by using sign language. Deaf people communicate by using sign language with their hands.
chunks.source: Deaf people communicate by using sign language with their hands.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any one importance of a hospital in the community. A: sick people get treatment there. A hospital is important because sick people get treatment there.
chunks.source: A hospital is important because sick people get treatment there.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to a family where we find the mother, father, children and uncles? A: extended family. A family with the mother, father, children and uncles is an extended family.
chunks.source: A family with the mother, father, children and uncles is an extended family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match each worker to their correct work. A: Carpenters: make furniture; Barbers: cut hair; Nurses: take care of sick people; Traders: buy and sell things. Carpenters make furniture, barbers cut hair, nurses take care of sick people and traders buy and sell things.
chunks.source: Carpenters make furniture, barbers cut hair, nurses take care of sick people and traders buy and sell things.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a family? A: a group of people related by blood or marriage. A family is a group of people related by blood or marriage.
chunks.source: A family is a group of people related by blood or marriage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The mother to my mother is my ___. A: grandmother. The mother to my mother is my grandmother.
chunks.source: The mother to my mother is my grandmother.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: My uncle's children are my ___. A: cousins. The children of my uncle are my cousins.
chunks.source: The children of my uncle are my cousins.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: A daughter to my brother is my ___. A: niece. The daughter to my brother is my niece.
chunks.source: The daughter to my brother is my niece.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Your sister's son is your ___. A: nephew. The son of my sister is my nephew.
chunks.source: The son of my sister is my nephew.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who heads a family? A: father. The father heads the family.
chunks.source: The father heads the family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Choose the cultural practices from the list. A: circumcision, introduction, wedding, naming. Circumcision, introduction, wedding and naming are cultural practices.
chunks.source: Circumcision, introduction, wedding and naming are cultural practices.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which part of the body do we use to breathe and smell? A: nose. We use the nose to breathe and smell.
chunks.source: We use the nose to breathe and smell.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: We use the ___ to taste our food. A: tongue. We use the tongue to taste our food.
chunks.source: We use the tongue to taste our food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we bathe? A: to keep our bodies clean. We bathe to keep our bodies clean and healthy.
chunks.source: We bathe to keep our bodies clean and healthy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why people brush their teeth. A: to remove dirt from the teeth. We brush our teeth to remove dirt and keep them strong.
chunks.source: We brush our teeth to remove dirt and keep them strong.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the poem about? A: personal hygiene. The poem is about personal hygiene: brushing teeth, washing hands and keeping clean.
chunks.source: The poem is about personal hygiene: brushing teeth, washing hands and keeping clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the title of the poem? A: Personal hygiene. The title of the poem is Personal hygiene.
chunks.source: The title of the poem is Personal hygiene.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one thing we do for personal hygiene. A: brush our teeth. For personal hygiene we brush our teeth, wash our hands and cut our nails short.
chunks.source: For personal hygiene we brush our teeth, wash our hands and cut our nails short.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do we keep our bodies fit? A: by exercising our bodies. We keep our bodies fit by exercising and having enough rest.
chunks.source: We keep our bodies fit by exercising and having enough rest.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which word is not a body part? Teeth, Ears, Razorblade, Toes. A: razorblade. Teeth, ears and toes are body parts. A razorblade is a tool.
chunks.source: Teeth, ears and toes are body parts. A razorblade is a tool.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match each body part to its correct use. A: eyes: used for seeing things; ears: used for hearing; nose: used for smelling and breathing; teeth: used for biting and chewing food. The eyes are for seeing, the ears for hearing, the nose for smelling and breathing, and the teeth for biting and chewing food.
chunks.source: The eyes are for seeing, the ears for hearing, the nose for smelling and breathing, and the teeth for biting and chewing food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one source of food. A: garden. We get food from the garden, market, shop and farm.
chunks.source: We get food from the garden, market, shop and farm.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another source of food. A: market. We get food from the garden, market, shop and farm.
chunks.source: We get food from the garden, market, shop and farm.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which season is planting of crops mostly done by farmers? A: rainy season. Farmers plant crops in the rainy season because crops need water to grow.
chunks.source: Farmers plant crops in the rainy season because crops need water to grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which farmers care for their crops. A: by weeding them. Farmers care for crops by weeding, watering and spraying them.
chunks.source: Farmers care for crops by weeding, watering and spraying them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is a hoe useful to a farmer? A: for digging the garden. A hoe is used for digging the garden and weeding crops.
chunks.source: A hoe is used for digging the garden and weeding crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which season do most farmers harvest their crops? A: dry season. Farmers harvest crops in the dry season and plant in the rainy season.
chunks.source: Farmers harvest crops in the dry season and plant in the rainy season.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Arrange these sentences to form a meaningful story: (a) She sent Tom and Jerry to the market. (b) They bought rice and meat. (c) Mummy wanted to prepare lunch. (d) And they had a wonderful lunch. (e) She prepared the food. A: Mummy wanted to prepare lunch., She sent Tom and Jerry to the market., They bought rice and meat., She prepared the food., And they had a wonderful lunch.. First mummy wanted to prepare lunch, then she sent Tom and Jerry to the market, they bought rice and meat, she prepared the food, and they had a wonderful lunch.
chunks.source: First mummy wanted to prepare lunch, then she sent Tom and Jerry to the market, they bought rice and meat, she prepared the food, and they had a wonderful lunch.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is food? A: something good to eat or drink. Food is something good to eat or drink.
chunks.source: Food is something good to eat or drink.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List one place where people can get food. A: shop. People get food from the shop, market, garden and farm.
chunks.source: People get food from the shop, market, garden and farm.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which food is got from water? A: fish. Fish is got from water in lakes and rivers.
chunks.source: Fish is got from water in lakes and rivers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a balanced diet? A: a meal with all classes of food in the right amounts. A balanced diet is a meal with all the classes of food in their right amounts.
chunks.source: A balanced diet is a meal with all the classes of food in their right amounts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Arrange these sentences to make the story of planting: (a) When the plants are fully grown, they are harvested and sold. (b) When the land is ready, the farmer sows seeds. (c) As plants grow, the farmer weeds and sprays them. (d) Then make the land ready for sowing seeds. (e) After sowing seeds, plants will start to grow. (f) First you have to clear the bushy land. A: First you have to clear the bushy land., Then make the land ready for sowing seeds., When the land is ready, the farmer sows seeds., After sowing seeds, plants will start to grow., As plants grow, the farmer weeds and sprays them., When the plants are fully grown, they are harvested and sold.. First clear the bushy land, make it ready, sow seeds, plants grow, weed and spray them, then harvest and sell.
chunks.source: First clear the bushy land, make it ready, sow seeds, plants grow, weed and spray them, then harvest and sell.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which type of weather causes floods? A: rainy weather. Heavy rain causes floods. Sunshine makes people sweat.
chunks.source: Heavy rain causes floods. Sunshine makes people sweat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which type of weather makes people sweat? A: sunny weather. Hot sunshine makes people sweat. Heavy rain causes floods.
chunks.source: Hot sunshine makes people sweat. Heavy rain causes floods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we can get from a swamp. A: clay. We get clay, papyrus and water from a swamp.
chunks.source: We get clay, papyrus and water from a swamp.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of trees at home. A: for shade. Trees at home give us shade, fruits and firewood.
chunks.source: Trees at home give us shade, fruits and firewood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which element of weather causes soil erosion? A: rain. Heavy rain washes away the top soil. This is called soil erosion.
chunks.source: Heavy rain washes away the top soil. This is called soil erosion.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How important are lakes and rivers to people? A: they give us water. Lakes and rivers give us water and fish.
chunks.source: Lakes and rivers give us water and fish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we carry umbrellas on a rainy day? A: to protect ourselves from rain. We carry umbrellas on a rainy day so that we do not get wet.
chunks.source: We carry umbrellas on a rainy day so that we do not get wet.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which type of weather helps in winnowing seeds? A: windy weather. Wind helps in winnowing seeds because it blows away the light husks.
chunks.source: Wind helps in winnowing seeds because it blows away the light husks.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any one material we can get from a swamp. A: papyrus. We get clay and papyrus from a swamp.
chunks.source: We get clay and papyrus from a swamp.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way people can care for plants in a compound. A: by watering them. We care for plants by watering them and weeding around them.
chunks.source: We care for plants by watering them and weeding around them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we use to manage sunny weather. A: wearing a hat. We manage sunny weather by wearing hats and staying in the shade.
chunks.source: We manage sunny weather by wearing hats and staying in the shade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing we use to manage sunny weather. A: staying in the shade. We manage sunny weather by wearing hats and staying in the shade.
chunks.source: We manage sunny weather by wearing hats and staying in the shade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one animal that lives in water. A: fish. Fish, frogs and crocodiles live in water.
chunks.source: Fish, frogs and crocodiles live in water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one way of caring for plants. A: by weeding them. We care for plants by weeding, watering and mulching them.
chunks.source: We care for plants by weeding, watering and mulching them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one plant found at home. A: flowers. We find flowers and fruit trees planted at home.
chunks.source: We find flowers and fruit trees planted at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another plant found at home. A: fruit trees. We find flowers and fruit trees planted at home.
chunks.source: We find flowers and fruit trees planted at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do people manage rainy weather? A: by using umbrellas. People manage rainy weather by using umbrellas and wearing raincoats.
chunks.source: People manage rainy weather by using umbrellas and wearing raincoats.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which type of weather causes people to sweat? A: sunny weather. Sunny weather is hot and makes people sweat.
chunks.source: Sunny weather is hot and makes people sweat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do we keep our environment clean? A: by sweeping the compound. We keep our environment clean by sweeping the compound and planting trees.
chunks.source: We keep our environment clean by sweeping the compound and planting trees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one item used to clean our environment. A: broom. We use brooms, rakes and wheelbarrows to clean our environment.
chunks.source: We use brooms, rakes and wheelbarrows to clean our environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one play object made from banana fibres. A: ball. People make play objects like balls and dolls from banana fibres.
chunks.source: People make play objects like balls and dolls from banana fibres.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one building material got from shops. A: nails. We buy nails, cement, iron sheets and timber from shops for building.
chunks.source: We buy nails, cement, iron sheets and timber from shops for building.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another building material got from shops. A: cement. We buy nails, cement, iron sheets and timber from shops for building.
chunks.source: We buy nails, cement, iron sheets and timber from shops for building.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we can buy from a carpenter. A: table. A carpenter makes tables, chairs, beds and doors.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes tables, chairs, beds and doors.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing we can buy from a carpenter. A: chair. A carpenter makes tables, chairs, beds and doors.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes tables, chairs, beds and doors.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of balls. A: for playing. Balls are used for playing games like football.
chunks.source: Balls are used for playing games like football.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of a basket. A: for carrying things. A basket is used for carrying things like food and clothes.
chunks.source: A basket is used for carrying things like food and clothes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one play object. A: ball. Play objects are things children play with, like balls and dolls.
chunks.source: Play objects are things children play with, like balls and dolls.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do we get nails for building houses? A: from shops. We buy nails, cement and iron sheets from shops.
chunks.source: We buy nails, cement and iron sheets from shops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing made by a carpenter. A: door. A carpenter makes doors, beds, tables and chairs.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes doors, beds, tables and chairs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing made by a carpenter. A: bed. A carpenter makes doors, beds, tables and chairs.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes doors, beds, tables and chairs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of mats. A: for sitting on. Mats are used for sitting on and sleeping on.
chunks.source: Mats are used for sitting on and sleeping on.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of ropes. A: for tying things. Ropes are used for tying things together.
chunks.source: Ropes are used for tying things together.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one material that we use to make mats. A: papyrus. We use papyrus and banana fibres to make mats.
chunks.source: We use papyrus and banana fibres to make mats.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which building material is got from soil? A: clay. Clay is got from the soil. People use it to make bricks and pots.
chunks.source: Clay is got from the soil. People use it to make bricks and pots.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one play object we make. A: balls. We make play objects like balls and dolls from banana fibres and cloth.
chunks.source: We make play objects like balls and dolls from banana fibres and cloth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another play object we make. A: dolls. We make play objects like balls and dolls from banana fibres and cloth.
chunks.source: We make play objects like balls and dolls from banana fibres and cloth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing made by a carpenter. A: stool. A carpenter makes stools, cupboards, tables and chairs.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes stools, cupboards, tables and chairs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing made by a carpenter. A: cupboard. A carpenter makes stools, cupboards, tables and chairs.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes stools, cupboards, tables and chairs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we make for playing with. A: skipping ropes. We make skipping ropes, kites, balls and dolls for playing.
chunks.source: We make skipping ropes, kites, balls and dolls for playing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing we make for playing with. A: kites. We make skipping ropes, kites, balls and dolls for playing.
chunks.source: We make skipping ropes, kites, balls and dolls for playing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the source of banana fibres. A: banana stems. Banana fibres come from banana stems.
chunks.source: Banana fibres come from banana stems.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which important place do we find aeroplanes? A: airport. Aeroplanes are found at the airport.
chunks.source: Aeroplanes are found at the airport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which domestic animal is kept for transport? A: donkey. Donkeys and horses are kept for transport. They carry luggage.
chunks.source: Donkeys and horses are kept for transport. They carry luggage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Choose one means of railway transport. A: train. A train is a means of railway transport. It moves on rails.
chunks.source: A train is a means of railway transport. It moves on rails.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of a horse to people. A: for transport. Horses are used for transport. They carry people and luggage.
chunks.source: Horses are used for transport. They carry people and luggage.

chunks.subject: Social
