chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing a school can buy from the neighbourhood. A: food. A school buys food, firewood and other things from the neighbourhood.
chunks.source: A school buys food, firewood and other things from the neighbourhood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one item used to clean our classroom. A: broom. We use brooms, mops and dusters to clean the classroom.
chunks.source: We use brooms, mops and dusters to clean the classroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another item used to clean our classroom. A: mop. We use brooms, mops and dusters to clean the classroom.
chunks.source: We use brooms, mops and dusters to clean the classroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one school symbol found on a school uniform. A: school badge. School symbols on a uniform are the school badge, school motto and school colours.
chunks.source: School symbols on a uniform are the school badge, school motto and school colours.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another school symbol found on a school uniform. A: school motto. School symbols on a uniform are the school badge, school motto and school colours.
chunks.source: School symbols on a uniform are the school badge, school motto and school colours.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing used to locate our school. A: signpost. A signpost and the school flag help people locate our school.
chunks.source: A signpost and the school flag help people locate our school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing used to locate our school. A: school flag. A signpost and the school flag help people locate our school.
chunks.source: A signpost and the school flag help people locate our school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing teachers use to teach children. A: chalk. Teachers use chalk, books, charts and pens to teach children.
chunks.source: Teachers use chalk, books, charts and pens to teach children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing teachers use to teach children. A: books. Teachers use chalk, books, charts and pens to teach children.
chunks.source: Teachers use chalk, books, charts and pens to teach children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the tool used at school to change lessons. A: bell. The bell is rung at school to show that lessons have changed.
chunks.source: The bell is rung at school to show that lessons have changed.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is a school important in a community? A: children get education. A school is important because children get education there.
chunks.source: A school is important because children get education there.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do we find the headmaster in a school? A: office. The headmaster stays in the school office.
chunks.source: The headmaster stays in the school office.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which school symbol helps people to locate our school? A: signpost. The school signpost is put along the road to help people locate the school.
chunks.source: The school signpost is put along the road to help people locate the school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one thing a school gets from its neighbourhood. A: food. A school gets food, water and firewood from its neighbourhood.
chunks.source: A school gets food, water and firewood from its neighbourhood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one cause of problems between a school and its neighbourhood. A: noise made by children. Noise made by children can cause problems between a school and its neighbourhood.
chunks.source: Noise made by children can cause problems between a school and its neighbourhood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do you come to school? A: to get education. We come to school to get education and learn new things.
chunks.source: We come to school to get education and learn new things.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one activity done by children at school. A: playing. Children learn, play and sing at school.
chunks.source: Children learn, play and sing at school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we use to locate our school. A: signpost. A signpost and the school flag help people locate our school.
chunks.source: A signpost and the school flag help people locate our school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing teachers use to teach children. A: chalkboard. Teachers use the chalkboard, charts, books and chalk to teach children.
chunks.source: Teachers use the chalkboard, charts, books and chalk to teach children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing teachers use to teach children. A: charts. Teachers use the chalkboard, charts, books and chalk to teach children.
chunks.source: Teachers use the chalkboard, charts, books and chalk to teach children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where can you find the nurse in a school? A: sick bay. The nurse is found in the sick bay where sick children are treated.
chunks.source: The nurse is found in the sick bay where sick children are treated.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where can you find the librarian in a school? A: library. The librarian is found in the library where books are kept.
chunks.source: The librarian is found in the library where books are kept.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where can you find the headmaster in a school? A: office. The headmaster is found in the school office.
chunks.source: The headmaster is found in the school office.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do cleaners keep our school clean? A: by sweeping the classrooms. Cleaners keep our school clean by sweeping classrooms and mopping floors.
chunks.source: Cleaners keep our school clean by sweeping classrooms and mopping floors.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How else do cleaners keep our school clean? A: by mopping the floors. Cleaners keep our school clean by sweeping classrooms and mopping floors.
chunks.source: Cleaners keep our school clean by sweeping classrooms and mopping floors.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one activity done at school. A: reading. Children read, write and play at school.
chunks.source: Children read, write and play at school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give another activity done at school. A: writing. Children read, write and play at school.
chunks.source: Children read, write and play at school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need cleaners in a school? A: to keep the school clean. We need cleaners in a school to keep the school clean and healthy.
chunks.source: We need cleaners in a school to keep the school clean and healthy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do children go to learn? A: school. Children go to school to learn to read, write and count.
chunks.source: Children go to school to learn to read, write and count.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one thing children use for writing. A: pencil. Children use pencils and pens for writing in their books.
chunks.source: Children use pencils and pens for writing in their books.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing found on the school sign post. A: school name. The school name is written on the school sign post.
chunks.source: The school name is written on the school sign post.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one school symbol. A: school flag. School symbols are the school flag, school badge, school motto and school anthem.
chunks.source: School symbols are the school flag, school badge, school motto and school anthem.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Draw and name any one thing found in a classroom. A: desk. We find desks, chairs, chalkboards and books in a classroom.
chunks.source: We find desks, chairs, chalkboards and books in a classroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any one example of a flag. A: national flag. Examples of flags are the national flag and the school flag.
chunks.source: Examples of flags are the national flag and the school flag.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the story about? A: school symbols. The story is about school symbols like the badge, motto, uniform, flag and anthem.
chunks.source: The story is about school symbols like the badge, motto, uniform, flag and anthem.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one symbol listed in the story. A: school badge. The story lists the school badge, school motto, school uniform, school address, school flag and school anthem.
chunks.source: The story lists the school badge, school motto, school uniform, school address, school flag and school anthem.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which school symbol makes children look smart? A: school uniform. The school uniform makes children look different and smart.
chunks.source: The school uniform makes children look different and smart.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: I am found at school. All school books are kept inside me. What am I? A: library. The library is found at school and all school books are kept inside it.
chunks.source: The library is found at school and all school books are kept inside it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: I am black and have the shape of a rectangle. Teachers write on me. You clean me with a duster. What am I? A: blackboard. The blackboard is black and rectangle-shaped. Teachers write on it and we clean it with a duster.
chunks.source: The blackboard is black and rectangle-shaped. Teachers write on it and we clean it with a duster.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: I sit in the office with a machine in front of me. I type letters and exams for the school. Who am I? A: secretary. The secretary sits in the office and types letters and exams for the school.
chunks.source: The secretary sits in the office and types letters and exams for the school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one member of an extended family. A: uncle. An extended family has parents, children and other relatives like uncles, aunts, cousins and grandparents.
chunks.source: An extended family has parents, children and other relatives like uncles, aunts, cousins and grandparents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one important place in a community where people go for treatment. A: hospital. Sick people go to the hospital or clinic for treatment.
chunks.source: Sick people go to the hospital or clinic for treatment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are cultural practices important to people? A: they bring people together. Cultural practices like naming and weddings bring people together and make them happy.
chunks.source: Cultural practices like naming and weddings bring people together and make them happy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one item found in a bedroom. A: bed. We find beds, blankets, pillows and clothes in a bedroom.
chunks.source: We find beds, blankets, pillows and clothes in a bedroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another item found in a bedroom. A: blanket. We find beds, blankets, pillows and clothes in a bedroom.
chunks.source: We find beds, blankets, pillows and clothes in a bedroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one role of children at home. A: sweeping the compound. Children help at home by sweeping, washing utensils and fetching water.
chunks.source: Children help at home by sweeping, washing utensils and fetching water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give another role of children at home. A: washing utensils. Children help at home by sweeping, washing utensils and fetching water.
chunks.source: Children help at home by sweeping, washing utensils and fetching water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do people keep their money safely? A: bank. People keep their money safely in a bank.
chunks.source: People keep their money safely in a bank.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we keep dogs at home? A: to guard our homes. We keep dogs at home to guard our homes and keep thieves away.
chunks.source: We keep dogs at home to guard our homes and keep thieves away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one activity done by people in our community. A: farming. People in our community do farming, trading, building and fishing.
chunks.source: People in our community do farming, trading, building and fishing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another activity done by people in our community. A: trading. People in our community do farming, trading, building and fishing.
chunks.source: People in our community do farming, trading, building and fishing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one basic need of a family. A: food. The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.
chunks.source: The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How useful are builders in a community? A: they build houses for us. Builders are useful because they build houses, schools and shops for us.
chunks.source: Builders are useful because they build houses, schools and shops for us.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which type of family do we find uncles? A: extended family. We find uncles, aunts and cousins in an extended family.
chunks.source: We find uncles, aunts and cousins in an extended family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need flowers in our homes? A: to make our homes beautiful. Flowers make our homes beautiful and give a good smell.
chunks.source: Flowers make our homes beautiful and give a good smell.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one duty of children at home. A: fetching water. Children help at home by fetching water, sweeping and washing utensils.
chunks.source: Children help at home by fetching water, sweeping and washing utensils.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one activity carried out in a community. A: fishing. People in a community do farming, trading, fishing and building.
chunks.source: People in a community do farming, trading, fishing and building.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need doctors in a community? A: to treat sick people. Doctors treat sick people in our community.
chunks.source: Doctors treat sick people in our community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one basic need of a family. A: shelter. The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.
chunks.source: The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to a group of people related by blood or marriage? A: family. A group of people related by blood or marriage is called a family.
chunks.source: A group of people related by blood or marriage is called a family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one role of a father at home. A: providing basic needs. A father provides the basic needs of the family like food and school fees.
chunks.source: A father provides the basic needs of the family like food and school fees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down one common ceremony that takes place at home. A: wedding. Common ceremonies at home are weddings and naming ceremonies.
chunks.source: Common ceremonies at home are weddings and naming ceremonies.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down another common ceremony that takes place at home. A: naming ceremony. Common ceremonies at home are weddings and naming ceremonies.
chunks.source: Common ceremonies at home are weddings and naming ceremonies.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are domestic animals? A: animals kept at home. Domestic animals are animals kept at home, like cows, goats, dogs and hens.
chunks.source: Domestic animals are animals kept at home, like cows, goats, dogs and hens.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of cows to us. A: they give us milk. Cows give us milk, meat and skins.
chunks.source: Cows give us milk, meat and skins.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one member of an extended family. A: aunt. An extended family has parents, children and other relatives like uncles, aunts, cousins and grandparents.
chunks.source: An extended family has parents, children and other relatives like uncles, aunts, cousins and grandparents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the role of a mother at home? A: cooking food for the family. A mother cooks food and cares for the children at home.
chunks.source: A mother cooks food and cares for the children at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people keep dogs at home? A: to guard our homes. People keep dogs at home to guard the home and keep thieves away.
chunks.source: People keep dogs at home to guard the home and keep thieves away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of a house to us. A: we live in it. A house gives us shelter. We live and sleep in it.
chunks.source: A house gives us shelter. We live and sleep in it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is a carpenter important in a community? A: he makes furniture for us. A carpenter is important because he makes furniture like tables and chairs for us.
chunks.source: A carpenter is important because he makes furniture like tables and chairs for us.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one cultural practice in the community. A: naming. Cultural practices in the community are naming, weddings and circumcision.
chunks.source: Cultural practices in the community are naming, weddings and circumcision.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which room of the house do we bathe from? A: bathroom. We bathe in the bathroom of the house.
chunks.source: We bathe in the bathroom of the house.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one role of children at home. A: washing clothes. Children help at home by washing clothes, sweeping and fetching water.
chunks.source: Children help at home by washing clothes, sweeping and fetching water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to a group of people related by blood or marriage? A: family. A group of people related by blood or marriage is called a family.
chunks.source: A group of people related by blood or marriage is called a family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one basic need of a family. A: clothing. The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.
chunks.source: The basic needs of a family are food, shelter and clothing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which type of family do we find a grandmother? A: extended family. We find grandmothers, uncles and cousins in an extended family.
chunks.source: We find grandmothers, uncles and cousins in an extended family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one activity done by people in our community. A: building. People in our community do building, fishing, farming and trading.
chunks.source: People in our community do building, fishing, farming and trading.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write another activity done by people in our community. A: fishing. People in our community do building, fishing, farming and trading.
chunks.source: People in our community do building, fishing, farming and trading.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a cultural practice. A: naming. Naming and weddings are examples of cultural practices.
chunks.source: Naming and weddings are examples of cultural practices.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give another example of a cultural practice. A: wedding. Naming and weddings are examples of cultural practices.
chunks.source: Naming and weddings are examples of cultural practices.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the importance of cultural practices. A: they unite people. Cultural practices are important because they unite people.
chunks.source: Cultural practices are important because they unite people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can you care for a baby at home? A: by feeding the baby. We care for a baby by feeding, bathing and carrying it.
chunks.source: We care for a baby by feeding, bathing and carrying it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing found in a home. A: cup. We find cups, televisions and baskets in a home.
chunks.source: We find cups, televisions and baskets in a home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing found in a home. A: television. We find cups, televisions and baskets in a home.
chunks.source: We find cups, televisions and baskets in a home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one more thing found in a home. A: basket. We find cups, televisions and baskets in a home.
chunks.source: We find cups, televisions and baskets in a home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one room found in a good house. A: bedroom. A good house has a bedroom, kitchen, sitting room and bathroom.
chunks.source: A good house has a bedroom, kitchen, sitting room and bathroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another room found in a good house. A: kitchen. A good house has a bedroom, kitchen, sitting room and bathroom.
chunks.source: A good house has a bedroom, kitchen, sitting room and bathroom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is a father important in a home? A: he provides for the family. A father is important because he provides food and pays school fees for the family.
chunks.source: A father is important because he provides food and pays school fees for the family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one important place found in the community. A: church. Churches and mosques are important places of worship in the community.
chunks.source: Churches and mosques are important places of worship in the community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another important place found in the community. A: mosque. Churches and mosques are important places of worship in the community.
chunks.source: Churches and mosques are important places of worship in the community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one role of children at home. A: mopping the house. Children help at home by mopping the house, sweeping and fetching water.
chunks.source: Children help at home by mopping the house, sweeping and fetching water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need a dog at home? A: to keep thieves away. We keep a dog at home to keep thieves away and guard the home.
chunks.source: We keep a dog at home to keep thieves away and guard the home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one person found at home. A: father. Father, mother, brothers and sisters are people found at home.
chunks.source: Father, mother, brothers and sisters are people found at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another person found at home. A: brother. Father, mother, brothers and sisters are people found at home.
chunks.source: Father, mother, brothers and sisters are people found at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of water at home. A: for cooking. We use water at home for cooking, drinking, washing and bathing.
chunks.source: We use water at home for cooking, drinking, washing and bathing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one role of a barber in our community. A: he cuts people's hair. A barber cuts people's hair in our community.
chunks.source: A barber cuts people's hair in our community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the work of religious leaders in our community? A: they lead prayers. Religious leaders lead prayers and teach people to do good.
chunks.source: Religious leaders lead prayers and teach people to do good.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do deaf people communicate to others? A: by using sign language. Deaf people communicate by using sign language with their hands.
chunks.source: Deaf people communicate by using sign language with their hands.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any one importance of a hospital in the community. A: sick people get treatment there. A hospital is important because sick people get treatment there.
chunks.source: A hospital is important because sick people get treatment there.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to a family where we find the mother, father, children and uncles? A: extended family. A family with the mother, father, children and uncles is an extended family.
chunks.source: A family with the mother, father, children and uncles is an extended family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who heads a family? A: father. The father heads the family.
chunks.source: The father heads the family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which part of the body do we use to breathe and smell? A: nose. We use the nose to breathe and smell.
chunks.source: We use the nose to breathe and smell.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we bathe? A: to keep our bodies clean. We bathe to keep our bodies clean and healthy.
chunks.source: We bathe to keep our bodies clean and healthy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the poem about? A: personal hygiene. The poem is about personal hygiene: brushing teeth, washing hands and keeping clean.
chunks.source: The poem is about personal hygiene: brushing teeth, washing hands and keeping clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the title of the poem? A: Personal hygiene. The title of the poem is Personal hygiene.
chunks.source: The title of the poem is Personal hygiene.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one thing we do for personal hygiene. A: brush our teeth. For personal hygiene we brush our teeth, wash our hands and cut our nails short.
chunks.source: For personal hygiene we brush our teeth, wash our hands and cut our nails short.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do we keep our bodies fit? A: by exercising our bodies. We keep our bodies fit by exercising and having enough rest.
chunks.source: We keep our bodies fit by exercising and having enough rest.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one source of food. A: garden. We get food from the garden, market, shop and farm.
chunks.source: We get food from the garden, market, shop and farm.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another source of food. A: market. We get food from the garden, market, shop and farm.
chunks.source: We get food from the garden, market, shop and farm.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which farmers care for their crops. A: by weeding them. Farmers care for crops by weeding, watering and spraying them.
chunks.source: Farmers care for crops by weeding, watering and spraying them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is a hoe useful to a farmer? A: for digging the garden. A hoe is used for digging the garden and weeding crops.
chunks.source: A hoe is used for digging the garden and weeding crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List one place where people can get food. A: shop. People get food from the shop, market, garden and farm.
chunks.source: People get food from the shop, market, garden and farm.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which food is got from water? A: fish. Fish is got from water in lakes and rivers.
chunks.source: Fish is got from water in lakes and rivers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we can get from a swamp. A: clay. We get clay, papyrus and water from a swamp.
chunks.source: We get clay, papyrus and water from a swamp.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of trees at home. A: for shade. Trees at home give us shade, fruits and firewood.
chunks.source: Trees at home give us shade, fruits and firewood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which element of weather causes soil erosion? A: rain. Heavy rain washes away the top soil. This is called soil erosion.
chunks.source: Heavy rain washes away the top soil. This is called soil erosion.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How important are lakes and rivers to people? A: they give us water. Lakes and rivers give us water and fish.
chunks.source: Lakes and rivers give us water and fish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we carry umbrellas on a rainy day? A: to protect ourselves from rain. We carry umbrellas on a rainy day so that we do not get wet.
chunks.source: We carry umbrellas on a rainy day so that we do not get wet.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any one material we can get from a swamp. A: papyrus. We get clay and papyrus from a swamp.
chunks.source: We get clay and papyrus from a swamp.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way people can care for plants in a compound. A: by watering them. We care for plants by watering them and weeding around them.
chunks.source: We care for plants by watering them and weeding around them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we use to manage sunny weather. A: wearing a hat. We manage sunny weather by wearing hats and staying in the shade.
chunks.source: We manage sunny weather by wearing hats and staying in the shade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing we use to manage sunny weather. A: staying in the shade. We manage sunny weather by wearing hats and staying in the shade.
chunks.source: We manage sunny weather by wearing hats and staying in the shade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one animal that lives in water. A: fish. Fish, frogs and crocodiles live in water.
chunks.source: Fish, frogs and crocodiles live in water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one way of caring for plants. A: by weeding them. We care for plants by weeding, watering and mulching them.
chunks.source: We care for plants by weeding, watering and mulching them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one plant found at home. A: flowers. We find flowers and fruit trees planted at home.
chunks.source: We find flowers and fruit trees planted at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another plant found at home. A: fruit trees. We find flowers and fruit trees planted at home.
chunks.source: We find flowers and fruit trees planted at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do people manage rainy weather? A: by using umbrellas. People manage rainy weather by using umbrellas and wearing raincoats.
chunks.source: People manage rainy weather by using umbrellas and wearing raincoats.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which type of weather causes people to sweat? A: sunny weather. Sunny weather is hot and makes people sweat.
chunks.source: Sunny weather is hot and makes people sweat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do we keep our environment clean? A: by sweeping the compound. We keep our environment clean by sweeping the compound and planting trees.
chunks.source: We keep our environment clean by sweeping the compound and planting trees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one item used to clean our environment. A: broom. We use brooms, rakes and wheelbarrows to clean our environment.
chunks.source: We use brooms, rakes and wheelbarrows to clean our environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one play object made from banana fibres. A: ball. People make play objects like balls and dolls from banana fibres.
chunks.source: People make play objects like balls and dolls from banana fibres.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one building material got from shops. A: nails. We buy nails, cement, iron sheets and timber from shops for building.
chunks.source: We buy nails, cement, iron sheets and timber from shops for building.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another building material got from shops. A: cement. We buy nails, cement, iron sheets and timber from shops for building.
chunks.source: We buy nails, cement, iron sheets and timber from shops for building.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we can buy from a carpenter. A: table. A carpenter makes tables, chairs, beds and doors.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes tables, chairs, beds and doors.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing we can buy from a carpenter. A: chair. A carpenter makes tables, chairs, beds and doors.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes tables, chairs, beds and doors.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of balls. A: for playing. Balls are used for playing games like football.
chunks.source: Balls are used for playing games like football.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of a basket. A: for carrying things. A basket is used for carrying things like food and clothes.
chunks.source: A basket is used for carrying things like food and clothes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one play object. A: ball. Play objects are things children play with, like balls and dolls.
chunks.source: Play objects are things children play with, like balls and dolls.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do we get nails for building houses? A: from shops. We buy nails, cement and iron sheets from shops.
chunks.source: We buy nails, cement and iron sheets from shops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing made by a carpenter. A: door. A carpenter makes doors, beds, tables and chairs.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes doors, beds, tables and chairs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing made by a carpenter. A: bed. A carpenter makes doors, beds, tables and chairs.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes doors, beds, tables and chairs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of mats. A: for sitting on. Mats are used for sitting on and sleeping on.
chunks.source: Mats are used for sitting on and sleeping on.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of ropes. A: for tying things. Ropes are used for tying things together.
chunks.source: Ropes are used for tying things together.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one material that we use to make mats. A: papyrus. We use papyrus and banana fibres to make mats.
chunks.source: We use papyrus and banana fibres to make mats.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which building material is got from soil? A: clay. Clay is got from the soil. People use it to make bricks and pots.
chunks.source: Clay is got from the soil. People use it to make bricks and pots.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one play object we make. A: balls. We make play objects like balls and dolls from banana fibres and cloth.
chunks.source: We make play objects like balls and dolls from banana fibres and cloth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another play object we make. A: dolls. We make play objects like balls and dolls from banana fibres and cloth.
chunks.source: We make play objects like balls and dolls from banana fibres and cloth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing made by a carpenter. A: stool. A carpenter makes stools, cupboards, tables and chairs.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes stools, cupboards, tables and chairs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing made by a carpenter. A: cupboard. A carpenter makes stools, cupboards, tables and chairs.
chunks.source: A carpenter makes stools, cupboards, tables and chairs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing we make for playing with. A: skipping ropes. We make skipping ropes, kites, balls and dolls for playing.
chunks.source: We make skipping ropes, kites, balls and dolls for playing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name another thing we make for playing with. A: kites. We make skipping ropes, kites, balls and dolls for playing.
chunks.source: We make skipping ropes, kites, balls and dolls for playing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the source of banana fibres. A: banana stems. Banana fibres come from banana stems.
chunks.source: Banana fibres come from banana stems.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which important place do we find aeroplanes? A: airport. Aeroplanes are found at the airport.
chunks.source: Aeroplanes are found at the airport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which domestic animal is kept for transport? A: donkey. Donkeys and horses are kept for transport. They carry luggage.
chunks.source: Donkeys and horses are kept for transport. They carry luggage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of a horse to people. A: for transport. Horses are used for transport. They carry people and luggage.
chunks.source: Horses are used for transport. They carry people and luggage.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'pupil' mean? A: child who goes to school. 'pupil' means child who goes to school.
chunks.source: 'pupil' means child who goes to school.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'wall around school'? A: fence. wall around school — that is 'fence'.
chunks.source: wall around school — that is 'fence'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'room where pupils learn'? A: classroom. room where pupils learn — that is 'classroom'.
chunks.source: room where pupils learn — that is 'classroom'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'water' mean? A: liquid we drink. 'water' means liquid we drink.
chunks.source: 'water' means liquid we drink.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: The ___ smiles. A: teacher. The word is 'teacher': The teacher smiles.
chunks.source: The word is 'teacher': The teacher smiles.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'map' mean? A: drawing of places. 'map' means drawing of places.
chunks.source: 'map' means drawing of places.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'library' mean? A: room with many books. 'library' means room with many books.
chunks.source: 'library' means room with many books.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'playground' mean? A: open area for play. 'playground' means open area for play.
chunks.source: 'playground' means open area for play.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'office' mean? A: room where teachers work. 'office' means room where teachers work.
chunks.source: 'office' means room where teachers work.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'pages with stories'? A: books. pages with stories — that is 'books'.
chunks.source: pages with stories — that is 'books'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'sign that means something'? A: symbol. sign that means something — that is 'symbol'.
chunks.source: sign that means something — that is 'symbol'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'fence' mean? A: wall around school. 'fence' means wall around school.
chunks.source: 'fence' means wall around school.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Her ___ shines. A: badge. The word is 'badge': Her badge shines.
chunks.source: The word is 'badge': Her badge shines.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'narrow way for walking'? A: path. narrow way for walking — that is 'path'.
chunks.source: narrow way for walking — that is 'path'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'small sign on uniform'? A: badge. small sign on uniform — that is 'badge'.
chunks.source: small sign on uniform — that is 'badge'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'person who teaches'? A: teacher. person who teaches — that is 'teacher'.
chunks.source: person who teaches — that is 'teacher'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'books' mean? A: pages with stories. 'books' means pages with stories.
chunks.source: 'books' means pages with stories.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'special clothes for school'? A: uniform. special clothes for school — that is 'uniform'.
chunks.source: special clothes for school — that is 'uniform'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'room where teachers work'? A: office. room where teachers work — that is 'office'.
chunks.source: room where teachers work — that is 'office'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'path' mean? A: narrow way for walking. 'path' means narrow way for walking.
chunks.source: 'path' means narrow way for walking.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'to do something for someone'? A: help. to do something for someone — that is 'help'.
chunks.source: to do something for someone — that is 'help'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'police' mean? A: people who keep us safe. 'police' means people who keep us safe.
chunks.source: 'police' means people who keep us safe.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: The ___ plants maize. A: farmer. The word is 'farmer': The farmer plants maize.
chunks.source: The word is 'farmer': The farmer plants maize.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'sister' mean? A: a girl with the same parents. 'sister' means a girl with the same parents.
chunks.source: 'sister' means a girl with the same parents.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'a place to buy things'? A: shop. a place to buy things — that is 'shop'.
chunks.source: a place to buy things — that is 'shop'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'people who keep us safe'? A: police. people who keep us safe — that is 'police'.
chunks.source: people who keep us safe — that is 'police'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'father' mean? A: the man who cares for you. 'father' means the man who cares for you.
chunks.source: 'father' means the man who cares for you.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: ___ works in the garden. A: father. The word is 'father': Father works in the garden.
chunks.source: The word is 'father': Father works in the garden.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: The ___ direct traffic. A: police. The word is 'police': The police direct traffic.
chunks.source: The word is 'police': The police direct traffic.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: ___ cooks matooke. A: mother. The word is 'mother': Mother cooks matooke.
chunks.source: The word is 'mother': Mother cooks matooke.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'market' mean? A: a big place with many sellers. 'market' means a big place with many sellers.
chunks.source: 'market' means a big place with many sellers.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: His ___ plays football. A: brother. The word is 'brother': His brother plays football.
chunks.source: The word is 'brother': His brother plays football.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'a girl with the same parents'? A: sister. a girl with the same parents — that is 'sister'.
chunks.source: a girl with the same parents — that is 'sister'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Her ___ helps with the baby. A: sister. The word is 'sister': Her sister helps with the baby.
chunks.source: The word is 'sister': Her sister helps with the baby.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'greet' mean? A: to say hello politely. 'greet' means to say hello politely.
chunks.source: 'greet' means to say hello politely.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: The ___ gives medicine. A: nurse. The word is 'nurse': The nurse gives medicine.
chunks.source: The word is 'nurse': The nurse gives medicine.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'house' mean? A: the building where a family lives. 'house' means the building where a family lives.
chunks.source: 'house' means the building where a family lives.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Kato shows ___ to father. A: respect. The word is 'respect': Kato shows respect to father.
chunks.source: The word is 'respect': Kato shows respect to father.

chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed: My father's car is old. It is fast. (Begin: Although) -> ___ A: Although my father's car is old, it is fast.. Although joins opposite ideas.

chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed: Okot went to the market. He bought a new watch. (Use 'and') -> ___ A: Okot went to the market and bought a new watch.. And joins two actions.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate the sentence correctly: Peter is both my friend and a brother -> ___ A: Peter is both my friend and a brother.. The correct sentence is: Peter is both my friend and a brother.
chunks.source: The correct sentence is: Peter is both my friend and a brother.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate the sentence correctly: We aren't going to do all the work now -> ___ A: We aren't going to do all the work now.. The correct sentence is: We aren't going to do all the work now.
chunks.source: The correct sentence is: We aren't going to do all the work now.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate the sentence correctly: Kampala is the capital city of Uganda. -> ___ A: Kampala is the capital city of Uganda.. The correct sentence is: Kampala is the capital city of Uganda.
chunks.source: The correct sentence is: Kampala is the capital city of Uganda.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate the sentence: my teacher is mr Sali -> ___ A: My teacher is Mr. Sali.. Begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. Names take capitals.
chunks.source: Begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. Names take capitals.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate the sentence: Ruth and amina are friends -> ___ A: Ruth and Amina are friends.. Names begin with capital letters.
chunks.source: Names begin with capital letters.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate the sentence: why are you shouting -> ___ A: Why are you shouting?. A question begins with a capital letter and ends with a question mark.
chunks.source: A question begins with a capital letter and ends with a question mark.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate correctly: i shall be there on Tuesday -> ___ A: I shall be there on Tuesday.. Begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop.
chunks.source: Begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate correctly: atim went to Nairobi last week -> ___ A: Atim went to Nairobi last week.. Names begin with capital letters.
chunks.source: Names begin with capital letters.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate the sentence: peter and ali are good boys -> ___ A: Peter and Ali are good boys.. Names begin with capital letters.
chunks.source: Names begin with capital letters.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: My mother ___ a bag everyday to work. (carry) A: carries. With he/she/it we add s: carry -> carries. 'Now' needs is + ing.
chunks.source: With he/she/it we add s: carry -> carries. 'Now' needs is + ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: The teachers ___ us from Monday to Friday. (teach) A: teach. With he/she/it we add s: teach -> teach. 'Now' needs is + ing.
chunks.source: With he/she/it we add s: teach -> teach. 'Now' needs is + ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: Stella ___ her pen for milk every day. (cry) A: cries. With he/she/it we add s: cry -> cries. 'Now' needs is + ing.
chunks.source: With he/she/it we add s: cry -> cries. 'Now' needs is + ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: The school bus ___ the pupils now. (take) A: is taking. With he/she/it we add s: take -> is taking. 'Now' needs is + ing.
chunks.source: With he/she/it we add s: take -> is taking. 'Now' needs is + ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: Daddy ___ for us every morning. (pray) A: prays. With he/she/it we add s: pray -> prays. 'Now' needs is + ing.
chunks.source: With he/she/it we add s: pray -> prays. 'Now' needs is + ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: The thief is ___ my friend's bag. (steal) A: stealing. With he/she/it we add s: steal -> stealing. 'Now' needs is + ing.
chunks.source: With he/she/it we add s: steal -> stealing. 'Now' needs is + ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: Akol ___ the truth everyday. (tell) A: tells. With he/she/it we add s: tell -> tells. 'Now' needs is + ing.
chunks.source: With he/she/it we add s: tell -> tells. 'Now' needs is + ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: Their cat ___ all the food they give it. (eat) A: eats. With he/she/it we add s: eat -> eats. 'Now' needs is + ing.
chunks.source: With he/she/it we add s: eat -> eats. 'Now' needs is + ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: Annet ___ porridge at breaktime. (take) A: takes. With he/she/it we add s: take -> takes. 'Now' needs is + ing.
chunks.source: With he/she/it we add s: take -> takes. 'Now' needs is + ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb: The P.3 pupils are ___ story books in their classroom. (read) A: reading. Present continuous = are + reading.
chunks.source: Present continuous = are + reading.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb: My sister ___ to her school by taxi every day. (go) A: goes. With she we add s: goes.
chunks.source: With she we add s: goes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: Sarah is ___ netball. (play) A: playing. Present continuous = is + playing.
chunks.source: Present continuous = is + playing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: Muthoni ___ her teeth every morning. (brush) A: brushes. With she we add es: brushes.
chunks.source: With she we add es: brushes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed: The doctor treated the sick man. (Use 'is treating') -> ___ A: The doctor is treating the sick man.. Present continuous = is + treating.
chunks.source: Present continuous = is + treating.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: The teacher is ___ on the chalkboard. (write) A: writing. Present continuous = is + writing.
chunks.source: Present continuous = is + writing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: It ___ heavily yesterday morning. (rain) A: rained. Past tense of 'rain' is 'rained'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'rain' is 'rained'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: My daddy ___ me a new mathematical set. (buy) A: bought. Past tense of 'buy' is 'bought'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'buy' is 'bought'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: Atim told me that Opio ___ her a pencil. (give) A: gave. Past tense of 'give' is 'gave'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'give' is 'gave'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: The dog ___ the rabbit yesterday. (chase) A: chased. Past tense of 'chase' is 'chased'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'chase' is 'chased'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: Our classroom was ___ last week. (paint) A: painted. Past tense of 'paint' is 'painted'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'paint' is 'painted'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: The tailor ___ my new dress at home. (bring) A: brought. Past tense of 'bring' is 'brought'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'bring' is 'brought'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: We ___ a lion yesterday. (see) A: saw. Past tense of 'see' is 'saw'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'see' is 'saw'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: I ___ that novel last Monday. (read) A: read. Past tense of 'read' is 'read'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'read' is 'read'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: We ___ him very well. (understand) A: understood. Past tense of 'understand' is 'understood'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'understand' is 'understood'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: They ___ a lot of food at the wedding party. (eat) A: ate. Past tense of 'eat' is 'ate'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'eat' is 'ate'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: The woodman ___ down the tallest tree. (cut) A: cut. Past tense of 'cut' is 'cut'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'cut' is 'cut'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: Kasubi ___ his car very fast yesterday morning. (drive) A: drove. Past tense of 'drive' is 'drove'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'drive' is 'drove'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: He ___ me at the end of the term. (punish) A: punished. Past tense of 'punish' is 'punished'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'punish' is 'punished'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: He ___ cleaning the class when the teacher came. (is) A: was. Past tense of 'is' is 'was'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'is' is 'was'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: The dogs ___ barking at the thief last night. (are) A: were. Past tense of 'are' is 'were'. Look for yesterday or last.
chunks.source: Past tense of 'are' is 'were'. Look for yesterday or last.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed: We are eating food now. (End: yesterday.) -> ___ A: We ate food yesterday.. Yesterday needs the past tense: ate.
chunks.source: Yesterday needs the past tense: ate.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: Mother ___ food yesterday. (cook) A: cooked. Yesterday needs the past tense: cooked.
chunks.source: Yesterday needs the past tense: cooked.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: Jackie lost ___ new pen last week. (she) A: her. We use 'her' for something belonging to Jackie.
chunks.source: We use 'her' for something belonging to Jackie.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: A friend of ___ has gone to town. (me) A: mine. A friend of mine = my friend.
chunks.source: A friend of mine = my friend.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: Timothy saw five ___ and reported to the police station. (thief) A: thieves. The plural of thief is thieves.
chunks.source: The plural of thief is thieves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: How many ___ are in this sub-county? (hill) A: hills. The plural of hill is hills.
chunks.source: The plural of hill is hills.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: Sarah has written four ___ today. (compose) A: compositions. The plural of composition is compositions.
chunks.source: The plural of composition is compositions.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: tomato -> ___ A: tomatoes. The plural of tomato is tomatoes.
chunks.source: The plural of tomato is tomatoes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: monkey -> ___ A: monkeys. The plural of monkey is monkeys.
chunks.source: The plural of monkey is monkeys.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: chief -> ___ A: chiefs. The plural of chief is chiefs.
chunks.source: The plural of chief is chiefs.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: toy -> ___ A: toys. The plural of toy is toys.
chunks.source: The plural of toy is toys.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: bench -> ___ A: benches. The plural of bench is benches.
chunks.source: The plural of bench is benches.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: child -> ___ A: children. The plural of child is children.
chunks.source: The plural of child is children.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed: A bee is an insect. (Begin: Bees) -> ___ A: Bees are insects.. Bees are plural, so we use 'are'.
chunks.source: Bees are plural, so we use 'are'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: My ___ are all wrapped. (book) A: books. The plural of book is books.
chunks.source: The plural of book is books.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed: A book is useful. (Begin: Books) -> ___ A: Books are useful.. Books are plural, so we use 'are'.
chunks.source: Books are plural, so we use 'are'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: That supermarket is ___ than our shop. (big) A: bigger. The comparative of big is bigger.
chunks.source: The comparative of big is bigger.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: An ostrich is the ___ bird in the world. (fast) A: fastest. The superlative of fast is fastest.
chunks.source: The superlative of fast is fastest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in a correct word: Musoke likes running more ___ singing. A: than. More ... than compares two things.
chunks.source: More ... than compares two things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed: Your dog was very slow. It did not catch me. (Use 'too ... to') -> ___ A: Your dog was too slow to catch me.. Too ... to shows the dog could not catch.
chunks.source: Too ... to shows the dog could not catch.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed: I like writing. I like reading more. (Use 'than') -> ___ A: I like reading more than writing.. More ... than compares.
chunks.source: More ... than compares.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed: Sunshine is important. Rain is important. (Use 'as ... as') -> ___ A: Sunshine is as important as rain.. As ... as compares equals.
chunks.source: As ... as compares equals.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is the adjective in this sentence: Maurice has a beautiful dress. -> ___ A: beautiful. Beautiful describes the dress, so it is the adjective.
chunks.source: Beautiful describes the dress, so it is the adjective.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: Matovu is ___ than Mubiru. (tall) A: taller. The comparative of tall is taller.
chunks.source: The comparative of tall is taller.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: Alex is ___ than Ben. (tall) A: taller. The comparative of tall is taller.
chunks.source: The comparative of tall is taller.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gap: She is older ___ my brother. A: than. Older ... than compares.
chunks.source: Older ... than compares.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed: A cat is small. A rat is smaller. (Use 'than') -> ___ A: A rat is smaller than a cat.. Smaller ... than compares.
chunks.source: Smaller ... than compares.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: big / ___ / biggest A: bigger. Big, bigger, biggest.
chunks.source: Big, bigger, biggest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: ___ / better / best A: good. Good, better, best.
chunks.source: Good, better, best.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: short / shorter / ___ A: shortest. Short, shorter, shortest.
chunks.source: Short, shorter, shortest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How many parishes make up Tanda town council? A: four. The passage says Tanda has four parishes.
chunks.source: The passage says Tanda has four parishes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: In which direction is Ndolwa parish? A: north. The passage says Ndolwa parish is in the north.
chunks.source: The passage says Ndolwa parish is in the north.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the main activity of people in Ndolwa parish? A: farming. People in Ndolwa parish farm because their land is fertile.
chunks.source: People in Ndolwa parish farm because their land is fertile.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: People in Kavule parish are cattle keepers. A: True. The passage says people in Kavule parish are cattle keepers.
chunks.source: The passage says people in Kavule parish are cattle keepers.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: There are fewer people in Amuso parish because of the ___. A: thick forest. The thick forest keeps people away from Amuso parish.
chunks.source: The thick forest keeps people away from Amuso parish.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: In which village did Biire live? A: Nsoga. The story begins in a village called Nsoga.
chunks.source: The story begins in a village called Nsoga.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What was Biire's work? A: potter. Biire was a potter; he made pots out of clay.
chunks.source: Biire was a potter; he made pots out of clay.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Biire's magic house had no door. A: True. The passage says the magic house had no door.
chunks.source: The passage says the magic house had no door.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ___ heard Biire saying the magic words. A: fox. A mad fox heard the magic words.
chunks.source: A mad fox heard the magic words.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What did the fox do inside Biire's house? A: ate all Biire's food and stole his pots. The fox ate all the food and stole the pots.
chunks.source: The fox ate all the food and stole the pots.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the main source of water? A: rain. The passage says the main source of water is rain.
chunks.source: The passage says the main source of water is rain.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We grow rice and yams in ___ because there is a lot of water. A: swamps. Swamps hold a lot of water for rice and yams.
chunks.source: Swamps hold a lot of water for rice and yams.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fishermen get fish from lakes. A: True. The passage says fishermen get fish from lakes.
chunks.source: The passage says fishermen get fish from lakes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do cooks at school use water for? A: cooking meals. Cooks use water for cooking meals.
chunks.source: Cooks use water for cooking meals.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is a lake in Uganda? A: Lake Victoria. Lake Victoria is named as a lake in Uganda.
chunks.source: Lake Victoria is named as a lake in Uganda.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where does the writer always go to watch boats sailing? A: lakeside. The writer goes to the lakeside to watch boats.
chunks.source: The writer goes to the lakeside to watch boats.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fishermen catch fish with fishnets. A: True. The poem says fishermen carry fishnets and catch fish.
chunks.source: The poem says fishermen carry fishnets and catch fish.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The poem was written by ___. A: Matovu Isaac. The writer's name is at the end: Matovu Isaac.
chunks.source: The writer's name is at the end: Matovu Isaac.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How many stanzas does the poem have? A: two. The poem has two stanzas: the lakeside and the forest.
chunks.source: The poem has two stanzas: the lakeside and the forest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which stanza talks about the forest? A: the second. The second stanza talks about the forest.
chunks.source: The second stanza talks about the forest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct word: What did Mary ___? A: do. After 'did' we use the base verb: do.
chunks.source: After 'did' we use the base verb: do.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: Ali ___ his father yesterday. (greet) A: greeted. Yesterday needs the past tense: greeted.
chunks.source: Yesterday needs the past tense: greeted.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: Did you ___ in the morning? (prayed) A: pray. After 'did' we use the base verb: pray.
chunks.source: After 'did' we use the base verb: pray.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: Peter ___ a nice shirt last week. (wear) A: wore. The past tense of wear is wore.
chunks.source: The past tense of wear is wore.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the verb in brackets correctly: What did Tom ___? (wrote) A: write. After 'did' we use the base verb: write.
chunks.source: After 'did' we use the base verb: write.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Put these sentences in the correct order to make a good story: 'The beef was bad.' / 'The shopkeeper refunded his money.' / 'Tom went to the shop.' / 'He returned the beef to the shop.' / 'He bought a tin of beef.' A: Tom went to the shop., He bought a tin of beef., The beef was bad., He returned the beef to the shop., The shopkeeper refunded his money.. Tom went to the shop, bought beef, found it bad, returned it and got his money back.
chunks.source: Tom went to the shop, bought beef, found it bad, returned it and got his money back.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets: The farmer ___ in his garden yesterday. (dig) A: dug. The correct form of 'dig' here is 'dug'.
chunks.source: The correct form of 'dig' here is 'dug'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets: We ___ tea last week. (drink) A: drank. The correct form of 'drink' here is 'drank'.
chunks.source: The correct form of 'drink' here is 'drank'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets: The headmaster ___ Nairobi yesterday. (leave) A: left. The correct form of 'leave' here is 'left'.
chunks.source: The correct form of 'leave' here is 'left'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets: The pupils ___ matooke and meat last Friday. (eat) A: ate. The correct form of 'eat' here is 'ate'.
chunks.source: The correct form of 'eat' here is 'ate'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets: Nalumu ___ the sweetest cake. (choose) A: chose. The correct form of 'choose' here is 'chose'.
chunks.source: The correct form of 'choose' here is 'chose'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets: Ritah has ___ my pen. (take) A: taken. The correct form of 'take' here is 'taken'.
chunks.source: The correct form of 'take' here is 'taken'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets: Why have you ___ my food? (eat) A: eaten. The correct form of 'eat' here is 'eaten'.
chunks.source: The correct form of 'eat' here is 'eaten'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets: Mr. Kintu has ___ us science. (teach) A: taught. The correct form of 'teach' here is 'taught'.
chunks.source: The correct form of 'teach' here is 'taught'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets: The teacher has ___ to the pupils. (speak) A: spoken. The correct form of 'speak' here is 'spoken'.
chunks.source: The correct form of 'speak' here is 'spoken'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets: My father has ___ a new car. (buy) A: bought. The correct form of 'buy' here is 'bought'.
chunks.source: The correct form of 'buy' here is 'bought'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets: Jalia has ___ all the dishes. (drop) A: dropped. The correct form of 'drop' here is 'dropped'.
chunks.source: The correct form of 'drop' here is 'dropped'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets: He has ___ to the market. (go) A: gone. The correct form of 'go' here is 'gone'.
chunks.source: The correct form of 'go' here is 'gone'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets: Mercy ___ her finger last night. (cut) A: cut. The correct form of 'cut' here is 'cut'.
chunks.source: The correct form of 'cut' here is 'cut'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Put these sentences in the correct order to make a good story: 'She dared to go there alone.' / 'Jane got a stick and killed it.' / 'Mother sent Halima to the well to fetch water.' / 'As they walked to the well, they saw a snake.' / 'Halima called her friend Jane to escort her.' A: Mother sent Halima to the well to fetch water., Halima called her friend Jane to escort her., As they walked to the well, they saw a snake., Jane got a stick and killed it., She dared to go there alone.. Mother sent Halima, Halima called Jane, they saw a snake, Jane killed it, then she went alone.
chunks.source: Mother sent Halima, Halima called Jane, they saw a snake, Jane killed it, then she went alone.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the verb: Our nurse has ___ the sick boy to the hospital. (take) A: taken. After has we use the past participle: taken.
chunks.source: After has we use the past participle: taken.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: The sun was shining ___. (bright) A: brightly. An adverb tells how: brightly.
chunks.source: An adverb tells how: brightly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: We kept your pen ___. (safe) A: safe. Here 'safe' describes the pen, so we keep the adjective.
chunks.source: Here 'safe' describes the pen, so we keep the adjective.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: Most newspapers are published ___. (day) A: daily. Day becomes the adverb daily.
chunks.source: Day becomes the adverb daily.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: He ___ welcomed me to his home. (happy) A: happily. An adverb tells how: happily.
chunks.source: An adverb tells how: happily.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: You must spell your name ___. (correct) A: correctly. An adverb tells how: correctly.
chunks.source: An adverb tells how: correctly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: The door was ___ open. (wide) A: wide. Here 'wide' describes the door, so we keep the adjective.
chunks.source: Here 'wide' describes the door, so we keep the adjective.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word: When it was raining, we walked ___ and went to the dining. (slow) A: slowly. An adverb tells how: slowly.
chunks.source: An adverb tells how: slowly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct word: How many brothers do you ___? A: have. We use 'have' with you.
chunks.source: We use 'have' with you.

chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct word: How many children ___ Musa have? A: do. We use 'do' to ask a question: How many children do Musa have?
chunks.source: We use 'do' to ask a question: How many children do Musa have?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct word: Karugaba ___ six sisters. A: has. We use 'has' with he/she/Karugaba.
chunks.source: We use 'has' with he/she/Karugaba.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct word: How old is your eldest ___? A: brother. The eldest child among brothers is a brother.
chunks.source: The eldest child among brothers is a brother.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct word: How many members are in your ___? A: family. Members belong to a family.
chunks.source: Members belong to a family.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write as instructed: The boy is playing in the rain. (Use: boys) -> ___ A: The boys are playing in the rain.. Boys are plural, so we use 'are'.
chunks.source: Boys are plural, so we use 'are'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in with has or have: Why ___ you beaten him? A: have. We use 'have' with you.
chunks.source: We use 'have' with you.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in with has or have: Dorah ___ a nice dress. A: has. We use 'has' with she/Dorah.
chunks.source: We use 'has' with she/Dorah.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in with has or have: My teacher ___ collected all the books. A: has. We use 'has' with he/she/teacher.
chunks.source: We use 'has' with he/she/teacher.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in with has or have: They ___ gone to Masaka. A: have. We use 'have' with they.
chunks.source: We use 'have' with they.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How many people are taking part in the dialogue? A: two. Musa and Sayid are talking: two people.
chunks.source: Musa and Sayid are talking: two people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who planted cabbages and egg plants? A: Musa. Musa says he planted cabbages and egg plants.
chunks.source: Musa says he planted cabbages and egg plants.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Sayid decided to keep bees this year. A: True. Sayid says: I decided to keep bees this year.
chunks.source: Sayid says: I decided to keep bees this year.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: By keeping bees, you get ___ which you can sell. A: honey. Bees give honey to sell.
chunks.source: Bees give honey to sell.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What will Sayid send Musa tomorrow? A: some honey. Sayid will send Musa some honey tomorrow.
chunks.source: Sayid will send Musa some honey tomorrow.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who is talking in the story? A: Nakate. The story begins: My name is Nakate.
chunks.source: The story begins: My name is Nakate.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is Nakate's mother's work? A: nurse. Her mother is a nurse.
chunks.source: Her mother is a nurse.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Nakate's father is a farmer. A: True. The passage says her father is a farmer.
chunks.source: The passage says her father is a farmer.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Nakate's sister ___ sweeps the compound. A: Nakyanzi. Her sister Nakyanzi sweeps the compound.
chunks.source: Her sister Nakyanzi sweeps the compound.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: When does the mother share out the work? A: during holidays. Mother shares work during holidays.
chunks.source: Mother shares work during holidays.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence: 'is' / 'A' / 'snail' / 'slower' / 'than' / 'a' / 'fly' A: A, snail, is, slower, than, a, fly. A snail is slower than a fly.
chunks.source: A snail is slower than a fly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence: 'leopard' / 'fast' / 'is' / 'A' / 'animal' / 'a' A: A, leopard, is, a, fast, animal. A leopard is a fast animal.
chunks.source: A leopard is a fast animal.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence: 'beautiful' / 'ostrich' / 'bird' / 'An' / 'is' / 'a' A: An, ostrich, is, a, beautiful, bird. An ostrich is a beautiful bird.
chunks.source: An ostrich is a beautiful bird.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Put these sentences in the correct order to make a good story: 'He warned him to stop eating rotten fruits.' / 'He was taken to the hospital.' / 'One day, he fell ill.' / 'Mugisha was well known for eating rotten fruits.' / 'The doctor told him that he had diarrhoea.' A: Mugisha was well known for eating rotten fruits., One day, he fell ill., He was taken to the hospital., The doctor told him that he had diarrhoea., He warned him to stop eating rotten fruits.. Mugisha ate rotten fruits, fell ill, went to hospital, the doctor warned him.
chunks.source: Mugisha ate rotten fruits, fell ill, went to hospital, the doctor warned him.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a meaningful sentence: 'playing' / 'my' / 'football' / 'is' / 'sister' A: My, sister, is, playing, football. My sister is playing football.
chunks.source: My sister is playing football.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a meaningful sentence: 'go' / 'on' / 'school' / 'foot' / 'to' / 'I' A: I, go, to, school, on, foot. I go to school on foot.
chunks.source: I go to school on foot.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in the correct order: 'fast' / 'she' / 'runner' / 'is' / 'a' A: She, is, a, fast, runner. She is a fast runner.
chunks.source: She is a fast runner.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in the correct order: 'Mr.' / 'is' / 'father' / 'my' / 'Musisi' A: Mr., Musisi, is, my, father. Mr. Musisi is my father.
chunks.source: Mr. Musisi is my father.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in the correct order: 'girl' / 'Susan' / 'an' / 'is' / 'obedient' A: Susan, is, an, obedient, girl. Susan is an obedient girl.
chunks.source: Susan is an obedient girl.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange to make a correct sentence: 'flower' / 'this' / 'a' / 'is' A: This, is, a, flower. This is a flower.
chunks.source: This is a flower.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange to make a correct sentence: 'friend' / 'a' / 'my' / 'teacher' / 'is' A: My, teacher, is, a, friend. My teacher is a friend.
chunks.source: My teacher is a friend.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Answer true or false: I shall make an alarm when I'm in danger. A: True. It is true: we make an alarm when in danger.
chunks.source: It is true: we make an alarm when in danger.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Answer true or false: A dog is bigger than a cow. A: False. It is false: a cow is bigger than a dog.
chunks.source: It is false: a cow is bigger than a dog.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Answer true or false: We have to report wrong doers to our elders. A: True. It is true: we report wrong doers to our elders.
chunks.source: It is true: we report wrong doers to our elders.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: A buffalo is ___ than an elephant. (big) A: bigger. The comparative of big is bigger.
chunks.source: The comparative of big is bigger.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: A giraffe is ___ than a goat. (tall) A: taller. The comparative of tall is taller.
chunks.source: The comparative of tall is taller.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: A rabbit is ___ than a goat. (small) A: smaller. The comparative of small is smaller.
