chunks.text: Q: One importance of first aid is to ____. A: save life. First aid saves the life of an injured person.
chunks.source: First aid saves the life of an injured person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another importance of first aid is to ____. A: reduce pain. First aid reduces the pain of the injured person.
chunks.source: First aid reduces the pain of the injured person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ is one sharp object that can cause harm to the body. A: razor blade. Sharp objects like razor blades can cut the skin and cause harm.
chunks.source: Sharp objects like razor blades can cut the skin and cause harm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One common disease in our sub-county is ____. A: malaria. Malaria is a common disease spread by mosquitoes.
chunks.source: Malaria is a common disease spread by mosquitoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another common disease in our sub-county is ____. A: diarrhoea. Diarrhoea is a common disease caused by dirty water and food.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea is a common disease caused by dirty water and food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way of preventing common diseases is ____. A: keeping our environment clean. A clean environment keeps germs away and prevents diseases.
chunks.source: A clean environment keeps germs away and prevents diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another way of preventing common diseases is ____. A: immunisation. Immunisation protects us from many diseases.
chunks.source: Immunisation protects us from many diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The soil layer marked A in the diagram is ____. A: topsoil. In the diagram, A is the top layer of the soil profile, called topsoil.
chunks.source: In the diagram, A is the top layer of the soil profile, called topsoil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The soil layer marked B in the diagram is ____. A: subsoil. In the diagram, B is the middle layer, called subsoil.
chunks.source: In the diagram, B is the middle layer, called subsoil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way soil is formed is by ____. A: the breaking down of rocks. Rocks break into small pieces over a long time to form soil.
chunks.source: Rocks break into small pieces over a long time to form soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way of keeping soil fertile is by ____. A: adding manure. Manure adds humus to the soil and makes it fertile.
chunks.source: Manure adds humus to the soil and makes it fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ is used to trim finger nails. A: nail cutter. A nail cutter is used to trim finger nails and keep them short and clean.
chunks.source: A nail cutter is used to trim finger nails and keep them short and clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We should brush our teeth after every meal to ____. A: remove food remains. Brushing removes food remains so the teeth do not rot.
chunks.source: Brushing removes food remains so the teeth do not rot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The first item in the diagram, used in keeping our bodies clean, is a ____. A: sponge. A sponge is used for scrubbing dirt from the body when bathing.
chunks.source: A sponge is used for scrubbing dirt from the body when bathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The second item in the diagram, used in keeping our bodies clean, is ____. A: soap. Soap kills germs on the skin when we bathe.
chunks.source: Soap kills germs on the skin when we bathe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Put these sentences about the water cycle in the correct order: 'The clouds become heavy and fall as rain.' / 'The sun heats water in the water body.' / 'The water vapour condenses to form nimbus clouds.' / 'The water evaporates into the atmosphere.' A: The sun heats water in the water body., The water evaporates into the atmosphere., The water vapour condenses to form nimbus clouds., The clouds become heavy and fall as rain.. The sun heats water, it evaporates into the air, forms clouds, and then falls back as rain.
chunks.source: The sun heats water, it evaporates into the air, forms clouds, and then falls back as rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One object made out of local materials is a ____. A: mat. Mats are woven from local materials like banana fibres.
chunks.source: Mats are woven from local materials like banana fibres.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another object made out of local materials is a ____. A: basket. Baskets are woven from local plant materials.
chunks.source: Baskets are woven from local plant materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One local material used to make local objects is ____. A: banana fibres. Banana fibres are used to weave mats, ropes and baskets.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are used to weave mats, ropes and baskets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another local material used to make local objects is ____. A: clay. Clay is used to make pots and stoves.
chunks.source: Clay is used to make pots and stoves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The garden tool shown in the diagram is a ____. A: hoe. The diagram shows a hoe used for digging.
chunks.source: The diagram shows a hoe used for digging.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The hoe is useful to a farmer for ____. A: digging the soil. A hoe is used for digging and tilling the soil in the garden.
chunks.source: A hoe is used for digging and tilling the soil in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We can take care of the hoe by ____. A: cleaning it after use. Cleaning the hoe after use stops it from rusting.
chunks.source: Cleaning the hoe after use stops it from rusting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We can also take care of the hoe by ____. A: keeping it in a cool dry place. Keeping tools in a cool dry place stops them from rusting.
chunks.source: Keeping tools in a cool dry place stops them from rusting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the animals to their homes: cow, pig, lion, dog. A: Cow: byre; Pig: pigsty; Lion: den; Dog: kennel. A cow lives in a byre, a pig in a pigsty, a lion in a den and a dog in a kennel.
chunks.source: A cow lives in a byre, a pig in a pigsty, a lion in a den and a dog in a kennel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One common insect is the ____. A: housefly. The housefly is a common insect found in our homes.
chunks.source: The housefly is a common insect found in our homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another common insect is the ____. A: mosquito. The mosquito is a common insect that spreads malaria.
chunks.source: The mosquito is a common insect that spreads malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of insects to people is that bees give us ____. A: honey. Bees make honey, which people eat.
chunks.source: Bees make honey, which people eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another use of insects to people is that they ____. A: pollinate flowers. Insects carry pollen from flower to flower, helping plants make seeds.
chunks.source: Insects carry pollen from flower to flower, helping plants make seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We eat food to ____. A: get energy. Food gives our bodies energy to work, grow and stay healthy.
chunks.source: Food gives our bodies energy to work, grow and stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should some food be cooked before eating it? A: To kill germs and make it soft. Cooking kills germs in food and makes it soft and easy to eat.
chunks.source: Cooking kills germs in food and makes it soft and easy to eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The best food for babies of one month is ____. A: breast milk. Breast milk has everything a small baby needs to grow.
chunks.source: Breast milk has everything a small baby needs to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One class of food is ____. A: proteins. Proteins, carbohydrates and vitamins are classes of food.
chunks.source: Proteins, carbohydrates and vitamins are classes of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One material used to make the mortar and pestle is ____. A: wood. Mortars and pestles are made from wood or stone.
chunks.source: Mortars and pestles are made from wood or stone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One food stuff prepared using the mortar and pestle is ____. A: millet flour. Millet grains are pounded in a mortar to make flour.
chunks.source: Millet grains are pounded in a mortar to make flour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another food stuff prepared using the mortar and pestle is ____. A: groundnut paste. Groundnuts are pounded in a mortar to make paste.
chunks.source: Groundnuts are pounded in a mortar to make paste.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should the mortar and pestle be kept clean? A: To stop germs from getting into our food. Dirty tools put germs into our food and make us sick.
chunks.source: Dirty tools put germs into our food and make us sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Soil erosion is the ____ of fertile soil by wind or running water. A: carrying away. Soil erosion carries away the fertile topsoil.
chunks.source: Soil erosion carries away the fertile topsoil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One agent of soil erosion is ____. A: running water. Running water carries soil away from the land.
chunks.source: Running water carries soil away from the land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another agent of soil erosion is ____. A: wind. Strong wind blows soil away from the land.
chunks.source: Strong wind blows soil away from the land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We can control soil erosion in our home compound by ____. A: planting grass. Grass holds the soil so it is not washed away.
chunks.source: Grass holds the soil so it is not washed away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The material shown in the diagram, kept in a first aid box, is a ____. A: razor blade. A razor blade is kept in the first aid box for cutting bandages.
chunks.source: A razor blade is kept in the first aid box for cutting bandages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The razor blade is useful to people for ____. A: cutting bandages. A first aider uses a razor blade to cut bandages and plasters.
chunks.source: A first aider uses a razor blade to cut bandages and plasters.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One accident which can be caused by carelessly using a razor blade is ____. A: cuts. A razor blade is very sharp and can cut the skin.
chunks.source: A razor blade is very sharp and can cut the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A first aid box is useful to a first aider because it ____. A: keeps first aid items together. The first aid box keeps all first aid items in one safe place.
chunks.source: The first aid box keeps all first aid items in one safe place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One material which can be made from sisal is ____. A: rope. Sisal fibres are used to make ropes and mats.
chunks.source: Sisal fibres are used to make ropes and mats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a soil profile. Which layer of soil is marked W? A: Topsoil. W points to the top layer of the soil profile, which is called topsoil.
chunks.source: W points to the top layer of the soil profile, which is called topsoil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One danger of heavy rainfall in the environment is ____. A: floods. Heavy rainfall causes floods that destroy crops and houses.
chunks.source: Heavy rainfall causes floods that destroy crops and houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Brooms are used in our classes for ____. A: sweeping. Brooms sweep dirt from the classroom floor.
chunks.source: Brooms sweep dirt from the classroom floor.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One common characteristic of insects is that they have ____. A: six legs. All insects have six legs and three body parts.
chunks.source: All insects have six legs and three body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One group of people who help in traffic is the ____. A: traffic police. Traffic police control vehicles and people on the road.
chunks.source: Traffic police control vehicles and people on the road.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One danger of cutting down many trees in the environment is ____. A: soil erosion. Trees hold the soil; without them, rain washes the soil away.
chunks.source: Trees hold the soil; without them, rain washes the soil away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a home of an animal. Name it: ____. A: nest. The picture shows a bird's nest made of twigs and grass.
chunks.source: The picture shows a bird's nest made of twigs and grass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One common fuel used for cooking at home is ____. A: charcoal. Charcoal is burnt to cook food at home.
chunks.source: Charcoal is burnt to cook food at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it dangerous to play near a cooking place? A: You can get burnt by fire or hot water. Fire and hot water at a cooking place can burn children who play near it.
chunks.source: Fire and hot water at a cooking place can burn children who play near it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The main body part of an insect on which the legs are attached is the ____. A: thorax. The six legs of an insect are attached to the middle part called the thorax.
chunks.source: The six legs of an insect are attached to the middle part called the thorax.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We can prevent food from getting contaminated by ____. A: keeping it covered. Covering food keeps germs and flies away from it.
chunks.source: Covering food keeps germs and flies away from it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we wash our hands after picking rubbish? A: To remove germs from our hands. Rubbish has germs, so we wash our hands after touching it.
chunks.source: Rubbish has germs, so we wash our hands after touching it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a spider not considered to be an insect? A: It has eight legs, not six. Insects have six legs, but a spider has eight legs, so it is not an insect.
chunks.source: Insects have six legs, but a spider has eight legs, so it is not an insect.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Farmers can control soil erosion in their gardens by ____. A: mulching. Mulching covers the soil so rain does not wash it away.
chunks.source: Mulching covers the soil so rain does not wash it away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One good health practice you know is ____. A: bathing daily. Bathing daily keeps our bodies clean and healthy.
chunks.source: Bathing daily keeps our bodies clean and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A zebra crossing is useful to pedestrians for ____. A: crossing the road safely. Cars stop to let people cross safely at a zebra crossing.
chunks.source: Cars stop to let people cross safely at a zebra crossing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One danger of diarrhoea to a patient is ____. A: dehydration. Diarrhoea makes the body lose a lot of water.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea makes the body lose a lot of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is clay soil the best soil to use when making pots? A: It sticks together well and can be shaped. Clay soil sticks together, so it can be shaped into pots.
chunks.source: Clay soil sticks together, so it can be shaped into pots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The item shown in the diagram is a toothbrush. How is it useful in promoting personal hygiene? A: It is used for brushing teeth. A toothbrush cleans our teeth and keeps them healthy.
chunks.source: A toothbrush cleans our teeth and keeps them healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One property of air is that air has ____. A: weight. Air has weight and takes up space.
chunks.source: Air has weight and takes up space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Farmers spray crops in the garden to ____. A: kill pests. Spraying kills pests that destroy crops in the garden.
chunks.source: Spraying kills pests that destroy crops in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Farmers keep garden tools in a cool dry place to ____. A: stop them from rusting. Wet tools rust, so they are kept in a cool dry place.
chunks.source: Wet tools rust, so they are kept in a cool dry place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A toilet is useful to people for ____. A: getting rid of human waste. A toilet keeps our waste in one safe place and stops diseases.
chunks.source: A toilet keeps our waste in one safe place and stops diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is one childhood immunisable disease. A: Measles. Measles is prevented by immunization in childhood.
chunks.source: Measles is prevented by immunization in childhood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One source of food is ____. A: the garden. We grow food crops in the garden.
chunks.source: We grow food crops in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One item we use in the kitchen is a ____. A: saucepan. A saucepan is used for cooking food in the kitchen.
chunks.source: A saucepan is used for cooking food in the kitchen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Strong winds are dangerous to plants because they ____. A: break them. Strong winds break branches and uproot plants.
chunks.source: Strong winds break branches and uproot plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Water is useful during germination because it ____. A: helps the seed to germinate. Seeds need water to start growing.
chunks.source: Seeds need water to start growing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Oxygen gas is useful to people for ____. A: breathing. People breathe in oxygen to stay alive.
chunks.source: People breathe in oxygen to stay alive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way people can care for their eyes is by ____. A: washing them with clean water. Clean water keeps our eyes healthy.
chunks.source: Clean water keeps our eyes healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which material is made from banana fibres? A: Mat. Banana fibres are woven to make mats.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are woven to make mats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A P.3 pupil can help to control the spread of malaria at home by ____. A: sleeping under a mosquito net. Sleeping under a mosquito net stops mosquitoes from biting you.
chunks.source: Sleeping under a mosquito net stops mosquitoes from biting you.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way of keeping food safe is by ____. A: covering it. Covering food keeps germs and flies away.
chunks.source: Covering food keeps germs and flies away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The parts of the insect marked X are the legs. They are useful to the insect for ____. A: walking. The insect uses its legs for walking and moving about.
chunks.source: The insect uses its legs for walking and moving about.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One item at home used for grinding millet is a ____. A: mortar. A mortar and pestle are used to pound millet into flour.
chunks.source: A mortar and pestle are used to pound millet into flour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way we can keep ourselves safe from accidents at home is by ____. A: not playing with sharp objects. Staying away from dangerous things keeps us safe from accidents.
chunks.source: Staying away from dangerous things keeps us safe from accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do animals move from one place to another? A: To look for food, water and shelter. Animals move to find food, water and safe homes.
chunks.source: Animals move to find food, water and safe homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is an antelope grouped under living things? A: It moves, feeds, grows and reproduces. Living things move, feed, grow and reproduce, and an antelope does all these.
chunks.source: Living things move, feed, grow and reproduce, and an antelope does all these.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One reason why people make mats is for ____. A: sitting on. Mats are used for sitting and sleeping on.
chunks.source: Mats are used for sitting and sleeping on.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An accident is a bad thing that happens ____. A: without being planned. Accidents happen suddenly and nobody plans them.
chunks.source: Accidents happen suddenly and nobody plans them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One cause of accidents on the road is ____. A: over speeding. Driving too fast causes accidents on the road.
chunks.source: Driving too fast causes accidents on the road.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One effect of an accident to a person is ____. A: injury. Accidents cause injuries like cuts and broken bones.
chunks.source: Accidents cause injuries like cuts and broken bones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another effect of an accident to a person is ____. A: death. Serious accidents can cause death.
chunks.source: Serious accidents can cause death.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One component of the environment, apart from air, is ____. A: water. Water, soil, plants and animals are parts of the environment.
chunks.source: Water, soil, plants and animals are parts of the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The component of air with 0.03% is carbon dioxide. It is useful to plants for ____. A: making food. Plants use carbon dioxide to make food.
chunks.source: Plants use carbon dioxide to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One property of air is that air ____. A: has weight. Air has weight, as shown by the balloon test.
chunks.source: Air has weight, as shown by the balloon test.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another property of air is that air ____. A: occupies space. Air takes up space wherever it is.
chunks.source: Air takes up space wherever it is.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wind is ____. A: moving air. Wind is air that is moving from one place to another.
chunks.source: Wind is air that is moving from one place to another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One element of weather, apart from wind, is ____. A: rainfall. Rainfall is an element of weather.
chunks.source: Rainfall is an element of weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another element of weather, apart from wind, is ____. A: sunshine. Sunshine is an element of weather.
chunks.source: Sunshine is an element of weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way of managing rainy weather is by ____. A: using an umbrella. An umbrella keeps us dry in rainy weather.
chunks.source: An umbrella keeps us dry in rainy weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The cycle shown in the diagram is the ____. A: water cycle. The water cycle is how water moves from water bodies to the air and back as rain.
chunks.source: The water cycle is how water moves from water bodies to the air and back as rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The sun is useful in the water cycle because it ____. A: heats water to evaporate. The sun heats water in lakes and rivers, and the water rises into the air.
chunks.source: The sun heats water in lakes and rivers, and the water rises into the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The process taking place at Q in the diagram is ____. A: evaporation. At Q, water changes into vapour and rises into the air. This is evaporation.
chunks.source: At Q, water changes into vapour and rises into the air. This is evaporation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The clouds that give us rain are ____ clouds. A: nimbus. Nimbus clouds are heavy with water and give us rain.
chunks.source: Nimbus clouds are heavy with water and give us rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of food in the body is to ____. A: give us energy. Food gives our bodies energy to work and play.
chunks.source: Food gives our bodies energy to work and play.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One danger of poor feeding is ____. A: poor growth. Children who do not eat well do not grow well.
chunks.source: Children who do not eat well do not grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One source of food in our division is the ____. A: garden. We grow food crops in the garden.
chunks.source: We grow food crops in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another source of food in our division is the ____. A: market. We buy food from the market.
chunks.source: We buy food from the market.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The item shown in the diagram is a ____. A: fire extinguisher. A fire extinguisher is used to put out fire.
chunks.source: A fire extinguisher is used to put out fire.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of a fire extinguisher in a school is to ____. A: put out fire. It puts out small fires before they spread in the school.
chunks.source: It puts out small fires before they spread in the school.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part of air found in a fire extinguisher is ____. A: carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it puts out fire.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it puts out fire.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In a school, the ____ can use the fire extinguisher. A: teachers. Trained adults like teachers use the fire extinguisher safely.
chunks.source: Trained adults like teachers use the fire extinguisher safely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A duck is grouped as a domestic bird because it ____. A: is kept by people at home. Domestic birds live with people and are cared for by them.
chunks.source: Domestic birds live with people and are cared for by them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One other example of a domestic bird, apart from a duck, is the ____. A: hen. A hen is a domestic bird kept at home for eggs and meat.
chunks.source: A hen is a domestic bird kept at home for eggs and meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of domestic birds to people is that they give us ____. A: eggs. Domestic birds like hens give us eggs to eat.
chunks.source: Domestic birds like hens give us eggs to eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another use of domestic birds to people is that they give us ____. A: meat. Domestic birds give us meat to eat.
chunks.source: Domestic birds give us meat to eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A family is a group of people who ____. A: live together and are related. A family is made of people who are related and live together.
chunks.source: A family is made of people who are related and live together.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One type of a family is the ____ family. A: nuclear. A nuclear family has parents and their children only.
chunks.source: A nuclear family has parents and their children only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One member of a family is the ____. A: father. The father is a member of the family.
chunks.source: The father is a member of the family.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another member of a family is the ____. A: mother. The mother is a member of the family.
chunks.source: The mother is a member of the family.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sand soil is useful for ____. A: building houses. Sand is mixed with cement to build houses.
chunks.source: Sand is mixed with cement to build houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Clay soil is useful for ____. A: making pots. Clay sticks together and can be shaped into pots.
chunks.source: Clay sticks together and can be shaped into pots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One organism that stays in soil is the ____. A: earthworm. Earthworms live in the soil and make it fertile.
chunks.source: Earthworms live in the soil and make it fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is loam soil the best for plant growth? A: It has humus, water and air that plants need. Loam soil has humus, water and air, which plants need to grow well.
chunks.source: Loam soil has humus, water and air, which plants need to grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The sun is useful in the environment because it gives us ____. A: light and heat. The sun gives light during the day and heat that warms us.
chunks.source: The sun gives light during the day and heat that warms us.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One danger of the sun is that it can ____. A: burn our skin. Too much sunshine can burn our skin.
chunks.source: Too much sunshine can burn our skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The best weather for winnowing seeds is ____ weather. A: windy. Wind blows away the light chaff from seeds during winnowing.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light chaff from seeds during winnowing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The best weather for drying harvested crops is ____ weather. A: sunny. Sunshine dries the harvested crops.
chunks.source: Sunshine dries the harvested crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The garden tool labelled D in the diagram is a ____. A: panga. In the diagram, D is a panga used for cutting grass and bushes.
chunks.source: In the diagram, D is a panga used for cutting grass and bushes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Garden tool A (rake) is useful to farmers for ____. A: levelling soil. A rake is used to level soil and gather rubbish in the garden.
chunks.source: A rake is used to level soil and gather rubbish in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Garden tool B (watering can) is useful to farmers for ____. A: watering crops. A watering can pours water on crops.
chunks.source: A watering can pours water on crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Garden tool C (hoe) is useful to farmers for ____. A: digging the soil. A hoe is used for digging and tilling the soil.
chunks.source: A hoe is used for digging and tilling the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Domestic animals are animals that ____. A: are kept by people. Domestic animals live with people at home.
chunks.source: Domestic animals live with people at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The domestic animal kept for wool production is the ____. A: sheep. Sheep give us wool for making clothes.
chunks.source: Sheep give us wool for making clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One product made from skins or hides is a ____. A: drum. Drums can be made from animal skins or hides.
chunks.source: Drums can be made from animal skins or hides.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Animal wastes are useful to farmers because they ____. A: are used as manure. Animal wastes rot to form manure that makes soil fertile.
chunks.source: Animal wastes rot to form manure that makes soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the animals to how they move: fish, snake, frog, man. A: Fish: Swimming; Snake: Slithering; Frog: Jumping; Man: Walking. Fish swim, snakes slither, frogs jump and people walk.
chunks.source: Fish swim, snakes slither, frogs jump and people walk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: First aid is the first help given to ____. A: a sick or injured person. First aid is quick help given before the doctor comes.
chunks.source: First aid is quick help given before the doctor comes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One reason we give first aid is to ____. A: save life. First aid saves the life of an injured person.
chunks.source: First aid saves the life of an injured person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another reason we give first aid is to ____. A: reduce pain. First aid reduces the pain of the injured person.
chunks.source: First aid reduces the pain of the injured person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One item used in giving first aid is a ____. A: bandage. A bandage is used to cover wounds.
chunks.source: A bandage is used to cover wounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One childhood immunisable disease is ____. A: polio. Polio is prevented by immunization in childhood.
chunks.source: Polio is prevented by immunization in childhood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another childhood immunisable disease is ____. A: measles. Measles is prevented by immunization in childhood.
chunks.source: Measles is prevented by immunization in childhood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Children are taken for immunization to the ____. A: health centre. Nurses at the health centre immunize children.
chunks.source: Nurses at the health centre immunize children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One group of people who carry out immunization is ____. A: health workers. Health workers give immunization to children.
chunks.source: Health workers give immunization to children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ is one useful insect. A: bee. A bee is a useful insect because it gives us honey.
chunks.source: A bee is a useful insect because it gives us honey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does a leopard move from one place to another? A: To look for food. Animals move from place to place to look for food and water.
chunks.source: Animals move from place to place to look for food and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A toilet is useful in a school for ____. A: getting rid of waste. Toilets keep the school clean and free from germs.
chunks.source: Toilets keep the school clean and free from germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a cockroach grouped under insects? A: It has six legs and three body parts. All insects have six legs and three body parts, and a cockroach has these.
chunks.source: All insects have six legs and three body parts, and a cockroach has these.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One danger of growing crops near anthills is that ____. A: termites destroy the crops. Termites from anthills eat and destroy crops grown near them.
chunks.source: Termites from anthills eat and destroy crops grown near them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of a plant is used to make food? A: Leaf. The green leaf makes food for the plant using sunlight.
chunks.source: The green leaf makes food for the plant using sunlight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is one childhood immunisable disease. A: Polio. Polio is a childhood disease prevented by immunization.
chunks.source: Polio is a childhood disease prevented by immunization.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Shadows are shortest at ____. A: midday. At midday the sun is overhead, so shadows are shortest.
chunks.source: At midday the sun is overhead, so shadows are shortest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which item is made from animal skin? A: Drum. Drums can be made from animal skin stretched over wood.
chunks.source: Drums can be made from animal skin stretched over wood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A dog is useful in a home because it ____. A: guards the home. Dogs bark at strangers and guard our homes.
chunks.source: Dogs bark at strangers and guard our homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A hen uses its beak for ____. A: picking food. Hens pick grains from the ground with their beaks.
chunks.source: Hens pick grains from the ground with their beaks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Soil erosion is the carrying away of ____ by wind or water. A: topsoil. Wind and running water carry away the fertile topsoil.
chunks.source: Wind and running water carry away the fertile topsoil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of mulching a garden is to ____. A: keep water in the soil. Mulching keeps water in the soil and stops weeds from growing.
chunks.source: Mulching keeps water in the soil and stops weeds from growing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from mulching, we can care for crops in the garden by ____. A: weeding the garden. Weeding removes weeds that compete with crops for food and water.
chunks.source: Weeding removes weeds that compete with crops for food and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is an ostrich unable to fly? A: It is too heavy and its wings are weak. An ostrich is very heavy and its wings are too weak to lift it.
chunks.source: An ostrich is very heavy and its wings are too weak to lift it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Floods are dangerous in an area because they ____. A: destroy crops and houses. Floods wash away crops and destroy houses.
chunks.source: Floods wash away crops and destroy houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are pedestrians advised to cross a busy road at a zebra crossing? A: Cars stop to let them cross safely. At a zebra crossing, drivers stop to let people cross the road safely.
chunks.source: At a zebra crossing, drivers stop to let people cross the road safely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One danger of poor feeding to a child is ____. A: weakness. Children who do not eat well become weak.
chunks.source: Children who do not eat well become weak.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One source of food is ____. A: plants. We get food like fruits and vegetables from plants.
chunks.source: We get food like fruits and vegetables from plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is loam soil the best for crop growing? A: It has humus, water and air. Loam soil has humus, water and air, which crops need to grow well.
chunks.source: Loam soil has humus, water and air, which crops need to grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Nimbus clouds are important in our sub-county because they ____. A: give us rain. Nimbus clouds bring rain for our crops.
chunks.source: Nimbus clouds bring rain for our crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The main natural source of heat and light is the ____. A: sun. The sun gives us heat and light every day.
chunks.source: The sun gives us heat and light every day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Water is important in a kitchen for ____. A: cooking and cleaning. In the kitchen we use water for cooking food and washing utensils.
chunks.source: In the kitchen we use water for cooking food and washing utensils.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The local tool shown in the diagram is a basket. What is one use of it to a crop farmer? A: Carrying harvested crops. Farmers use baskets to carry harvested crops from the garden.
chunks.source: Farmers use baskets to carry harvested crops from the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The component of air that helps a candle to burn is ____. A: oxygen. Oxygen supports burning, so a candle needs it to keep burning.
chunks.source: Oxygen supports burning, so a candle needs it to keep burning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Farmers can control pests in the garden by ____. A: spraying the crops. Spraying kills pests that destroy crops in the garden.
chunks.source: Spraying kills pests that destroy crops in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The best season for planting seeds is the ____ season. A: wet. Seeds need water to grow, so we plant them in the wet season.
chunks.source: Seeds need water to grow, so we plant them in the wet season.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should children not play near sharp objects? A: Sharp objects can cut them. Sharp objects can cut children and hurt them.
chunks.source: Sharp objects can cut children and hurt them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The item shown in the diagram is a razor blade. What is its use to people? A: Cutting things like bandages. A razor blade is used to cut things like bandages in first aid.
chunks.source: A razor blade is used to cut things like bandages in first aid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: People can care for domestic animals at home by ____. A: giving them food and clean water. Domestic animals need good food, clean water and shelter.
chunks.source: Domestic animals need good food, clean water and shelter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One crop grown in the swamps is ____. A: rice. Rice grows well in swampy areas with a lot of water.
chunks.source: Rice grows well in swampy areas with a lot of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One type of life cycle is ____. A: complete life cycle. In a complete life cycle, the insect passes through egg, larva, pupa and adult stages.
chunks.source: In a complete life cycle, the insect passes through egg, larva, pupa and adult stages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A rain gauge is useful at a weather station for ____. A: measuring rainfall. A rain gauge measures the amount of rainfall.
chunks.source: A rain gauge measures the amount of rainfall.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The sun is shining on a tree. Where is the shadow of the tree formed? A: On the side away from the sun. A shadow is always formed on the side away from the light.
chunks.source: A shadow is always formed on the side away from the light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One item that can be used to keep the environment clean is a ____. A: broom. Brooms sweep dirt and keep the environment clean.
chunks.source: Brooms sweep dirt and keep the environment clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do fish move from one side of a river to another? A: To look for food. Fish move about to look for food in the water.
chunks.source: Fish move about to look for food in the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One element of weather is ____. A: wind. Wind is moving air and is an element of weather.
chunks.source: Wind is moving air and is an element of weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way of controlling malaria at home is by ____. A: sleeping under a mosquito net. Mosquito nets stop mosquitoes from biting us at night.
chunks.source: Mosquito nets stop mosquitoes from biting us at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One time when you are supposed to wash hands is ____. A: before eating food. We wash our hands before eating so germs do not get into our food.
chunks.source: We wash our hands before eating so germs do not get into our food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a fruit is a ____. A: mango. A mango is a sweet fruit we eat.
chunks.source: A mango is a sweet fruit we eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The instrument shown in the diagram, used to preserve food, is a ____. A: fridge. A fridge keeps food cold so it stays fresh for a long time.
chunks.source: A fridge keeps food cold so it stays fresh for a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One food stuff preserved in a fridge is ____. A: milk. Milk is kept in the fridge so it does not go bad.
chunks.source: Milk is kept in the fridge so it does not go bad.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another food stuff preserved in a fridge is ____. A: meat. Meat is kept in the fridge to stay fresh.
chunks.source: Meat is kept in the fridge to stay fresh.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is food preserved? A: To keep it for a long time without going bad. Preserved food stays fresh for a long time.
chunks.source: Preserved food stays fresh for a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Air is a ____ of gases. A: mixture. Air is a mixture of gases like oxygen, carbon dioxide and nitrogen.
chunks.source: Air is a mixture of gases like oxygen, carbon dioxide and nitrogen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One component of air is ____. A: oxygen. Oxygen is the part of air we breathe in.
chunks.source: Oxygen is the part of air we breathe in.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another component of air is ____. A: carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is the part of air that plants use to make food.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide is the part of air that plants use to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One property of air is that air ____. A: has weight. Air has weight, as shown by the balloon test.
chunks.source: Air has weight, as shown by the balloon test.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The body organ shown in the diagram is the ____. A: eye. The eye is the sense organ we use for seeing.
chunks.source: The eye is the sense organ we use for seeing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One other body organ, apart from the eye, is the ____. A: ear. The ear is the sense organ we use for hearing.
chunks.source: The ear is the sense organ we use for hearing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One disease that affects the eye is ____. A: trachoma. Trachoma is a disease that makes the eyes red and painful.
chunks.source: Trachoma is a disease that makes the eyes red and painful.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We can take care of our eyes by ____. A: washing them with clean water. Washing our eyes with clean water keeps them healthy.
chunks.source: Washing our eyes with clean water keeps them healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a maize plant referred to as a flowering plant? A: Because it produces flowers. Maize produces flowers, so it is called a flowering plant.
chunks.source: Maize produces flowers, so it is called a flowering plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of leaves to plants is to ____. A: make food. Green leaves make food for the plant.
chunks.source: Green leaves make food for the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another use of leaves to plants is for ____. A: breathing. Leaves take in air that the plant needs.
chunks.source: Leaves take in air that the plant needs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Plants with weak stems climb others to ____. A: get sunlight. Climbing plants reach up to get sunlight for making food.
chunks.source: Climbing plants reach up to get sunlight for making food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An accident is a sudden bad event that ____. A: is not planned. Accidents happen suddenly and nobody plans them.
chunks.source: Accidents happen suddenly and nobody plans them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One common accident is ____. A: burns. Burns from fire or hot water are common accidents.
chunks.source: Burns from fire or hot water are common accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another common accident is ____. A: cuts. Cuts from sharp objects are common accidents.
chunks.source: Cuts from sharp objects are common accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: You can help a friend who has got an accident by ____. A: taking them to a hospital. Take the injured friend to hospital for treatment.
chunks.source: Take the injured friend to hospital for treatment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The wild animal shown in the diagram is a ____. A: crocodile. A crocodile lives in rivers and is a wild animal.
chunks.source: A crocodile lives in rivers and is a wild animal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The crocodile uses its ____ to hold its food. A: teeth. A crocodile holds its food with its strong teeth.
chunks.source: A crocodile holds its food with its strong teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The danger of a crocodile to people is that it ____. A: bites and kills people. A crocodile is dangerous because it can bite and kill people.
chunks.source: A crocodile is dangerous because it can bite and kill people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of a crocodile to people is that its skin is used to make ____. A: leather shoes and bags. Crocodile skin is used to make leather shoes and bags.
chunks.source: Crocodile skin is used to make leather shoes and bags.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: People need a balanced diet to ____. A: stay healthy and strong. A balanced diet keeps our bodies healthy and strong.
chunks.source: A balanced diet keeps our bodies healthy and strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We eat food to ____. A: get energy. Food gives our bodies energy to work and play.
chunks.source: Food gives our bodies energy to work and play.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it dangerous to eat food with unwashed hands? A: Germs on the hands get into the food and make us sick. Dirty hands put germs into food, and the germs make us sick.
chunks.source: Dirty hands put germs into food, and the germs make us sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One disease that is a result of poor feeding is ____. A: kwashiorkor. Kwashiorkor is caused by lack of proteins in food.
chunks.source: Kwashiorkor is caused by lack of proteins in food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: People need a toothbrush for ____. A: brushing their teeth. A toothbrush cleans our teeth.
chunks.source: A toothbrush cleans our teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We should bathe daily to ____. A: remove dirt and germs from our bodies. Bathing daily removes dirt and germs and keeps us healthy.
chunks.source: Bathing daily removes dirt and germs and keeps us healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Ironing clothes is useful because it ____. A: makes clothes neat and kills germs. Ironing makes clothes look neat and the heat kills germs.
chunks.source: Ironing makes clothes look neat and the heat kills germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It is dangerous to wear dirty clothes because they ____. A: can cause skin diseases. Dirty clothes carry germs that cause skin diseases.
chunks.source: Dirty clothes carry germs that cause skin diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The garden tool shown in the diagram is an ____. A: axe. The diagram shows an axe used for cutting wood.
chunks.source: The diagram shows an axe used for cutting wood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The axe is important to a farmer for ____. A: cutting wood and trees. Farmers use axes to cut wood for firewood and building.
chunks.source: Farmers use axes to cut wood for firewood and building.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We can take care of the axe by ____. A: keeping it in a cool dry place. Keeping the axe in a cool dry place stops it from rusting.
chunks.source: Keeping the axe in a cool dry place stops it from rusting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We can also take care of the axe by ____. A: cleaning it after use. Cleaning the axe after use stops it from rusting.
chunks.source: Cleaning the axe after use stops it from rusting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One item you can use to protect yourself from sunny weather is a ____. A: hat. A hat protects our head from strong sunshine.
chunks.source: A hat protects our head from strong sunshine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wind is useful to a farmer for ____. A: winnowing seeds. Wind blows away the light chaff when farmers winnow seeds.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light chaff when farmers winnow seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way too much rainfall is dangerous in an area is that it causes ____. A: floods. Too much rain causes floods.
chunks.source: Too much rain causes floods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another way too much rainfall is dangerous is that it ____. A: destroys crops. Heavy rain destroys crops in the gardens.
chunks.source: Heavy rain destroys crops in the gardens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Children are taken for immunization to ____. A: protect them from killer diseases. Immunization protects children from diseases like polio and measles.
chunks.source: Immunization protects children from diseases like polio and measles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Picture A shows a child who cannot walk well and uses a stick. Which disease is the child suffering from? A: Polio. Polio makes the legs weak, so the child cannot walk well.
chunks.source: Polio makes the legs weak, so the child cannot walk well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Picture B shows a child with red spots on the body. Which disease is the child suffering from? A: Measles. Measles causes red spots on the body.
chunks.source: Measles causes red spots on the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The above diseases (polio and measles) can be controlled by ____. A: immunization. Immunization protects children from polio and measles.
chunks.source: Immunization protects children from polio and measles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One item used in the kitchen to cook food is a ____. A: saucepan. A saucepan is used for cooking food in the kitchen.
chunks.source: A saucepan is used for cooking food in the kitchen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another item used in the kitchen to cook food is a ____. A: frying pan. A frying pan is used for frying food.
chunks.source: A frying pan is used for frying food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way of caring for the items found in the kitchen is by ____. A: washing them after use. Washing kitchen items after use keeps them clean.
chunks.source: Washing kitchen items after use keeps them clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another way of caring for kitchen items is by ____. A: keeping them in a clean dry place. Keeping kitchen items in a clean dry place stops them from rusting.
chunks.source: Keeping kitchen items in a clean dry place stops them from rusting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The soil animal shown in the diagram is an ____. A: earthworm. An earthworm lives in the soil.
chunks.source: An earthworm lives in the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The earthworm is useful to soil because it ____. A: helps to make the soil fertile. Earthworms dig in the soil and add humus, making the soil fertile.
chunks.source: Earthworms dig in the soil and add humus, making the soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One other component of soil, apart from earthworms, is ____. A: humus. Humus, water and air are components of soil.
chunks.source: Humus, water and air are components of soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Farmers can maintain soil fertility by ____. A: adding manure. Manure adds humus to the soil and keeps it fertile.
chunks.source: Manure adds humus to the soil and keeps it fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the way of moving to the animal: flying, hopping, slithering, swimming. A: Flying: bird; Hopping: grasshopper; Slithering: snake; Swimming: fish. Birds fly, grasshoppers hop, snakes slither and fish swim.
chunks.source: Birds fly, grasshoppers hop, snakes slither and fish swim.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One common disease is ____. A: malaria. Malaria is a common disease spread by mosquitoes.
chunks.source: Malaria is a common disease spread by mosquitoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another common disease is ____. A: flu. Flu is a common disease that affects the nose and throat.
chunks.source: Flu is a common disease that affects the nose and throat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way we can prevent malaria in our homes is by ____. A: sleeping under mosquito nets. Mosquito nets stop mosquitoes from biting us at night.
chunks.source: Mosquito nets stop mosquitoes from biting us at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another way we can prevent malaria in our homes is by ____. A: clearing bushes around the home. Clearing bushes removes places where mosquitoes hide and breed.
chunks.source: Clearing bushes removes places where mosquitoes hide and breed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The body organ for smelling is the ____. A: nose. The nose is the body organ we use for smelling.
chunks.source: The nose is the body organ we use for smelling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a broom useful to people? A: It is used for sweeping. A broom is used for sweeping dirt from the house and compound.
chunks.source: A broom is used for sweeping dirt from the house and compound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One role of a mother at home is ____. A: cooking food for the family. A mother cooks food and cares for the children at home.
chunks.source: A mother cooks food and cares for the children at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A zebra crossing helps pedestrians to ____. A: cross the road safely. A zebra crossing is a safe place marked on the road for people to cross.
chunks.source: A zebra crossing is a safe place marked on the road for people to cross.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is a danger of too much sunshine? A: It dries up crops. Too much sunshine dries up crops and water sources.
chunks.source: Too much sunshine dries up crops and water sources.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: At home, banana fibres can be used to make ____. A: ropes. Banana fibres are strong and can be twisted into ropes.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are strong and can be twisted into ropes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the main source of light energy in our environment? A: the sun. The sun gives us light during the day.
chunks.source: The sun gives us light during the day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A chameleon protects itself by ____. A: changing its colour. A chameleon changes its colour to hide from its enemies.
chunks.source: A chameleon changes its colour to hide from its enemies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The garden tool shown above is useful to farmers because it is used for ____. A: digging. Farmers use garden tools like the hoe for digging in the garden.
chunks.source: Farmers use garden tools like the hoe for digging in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is a danger of accidents to the human body? A: They cause injuries. Accidents can hurt our bodies and cause injuries.
chunks.source: Accidents can hurt our bodies and cause injuries.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To keep my bedroom clean, I ____. A: sweep it. Sweeping the bedroom removes dirt and keeps it clean.
chunks.source: Sweeping the bedroom removes dirt and keeps it clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these objects can float on water? A: a leaf. Light objects like a leaf stay on top of water and float.
chunks.source: Light objects like a leaf stay on top of water and float.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A meal with all food values in the correct amount is called a ____. A: balanced diet. A balanced diet has all food values in the right amounts to keep us healthy.
chunks.source: A balanced diet has all food values in the right amounts to keep us healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We prevent milk from going bad by ____. A: boiling it. Boiling milk kills germs so it does not go bad quickly.
chunks.source: Boiling milk kills germs so it does not go bad quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are earthworms useful in the soil? A: They make the soil loose. Earthworms dig tunnels that make the soil loose so air and water can enter.
chunks.source: Earthworms dig tunnels that make the soil loose so air and water can enter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is a disease which has no cure. A: HIV/AIDS. HIV/AIDS has no cure, so we must protect ourselves from it.
chunks.source: HIV/AIDS has no cure, so we must protect ourselves from it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wild animals are dangerous because they ____. A: can kill and eat people. Wild animals like lions can attack and kill people.
chunks.source: Wild animals like lions can attack and kill people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We care for crops in the garden by ____. A: weeding the garden. Weeding removes unwanted plants so crops can grow well.
chunks.source: Weeding removes unwanted plants so crops can grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is a component of air? A: oxygen. Air is made of gases like oxygen, nitrogen and carbon dioxide.
chunks.source: Air is made of gases like oxygen, nitrogen and carbon dioxide.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Nimbus clouds are useful to farmers because they ____. A: bring rain. Nimbus clouds bring the rain that crops need to grow.
chunks.source: Nimbus clouds bring the rain that crops need to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these domestic animals has two legs? A: hen. A hen is a domestic bird and birds have two legs.
chunks.source: A hen is a domestic bird and birds have two legs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the first aid for a nose bleed? A: pinch the nose and lean forward. Pinching the nose and leaning forward helps stop the bleeding.
chunks.source: Pinching the nose and leaning forward helps stop the bleeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ is used in the kitchen. A: saucepan. A saucepan is used for cooking food in the kitchen.
chunks.source: A saucepan is used for cooking food in the kitchen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where is a shadow formed when an object blocks light? A: on the side away from the light. A shadow forms on the side of the object that is away from the light.
chunks.source: A shadow forms on the side of the object that is away from the light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is carbon dioxide used in a fire extinguisher? A: It puts out fire. Carbon dioxide puts out fire because fire cannot burn in it.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide puts out fire because fire cannot burn in it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We make water safe for drinking by ____. A: boiling it. Boiling water kills the germs that cause diseases.
chunks.source: Boiling water kills the germs that cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We care for domestic birds by ____. A: feeding them. Domestic birds need food, water and shelter to stay healthy.
chunks.source: Domestic birds need food, water and shelter to stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ lives in water. A: fish. A fish lives and breathes in water.
chunks.source: A fish lives and breathes in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is a basic need of people? A: food. Food is a basic need because we cannot live without eating.
chunks.source: Food is a basic need because we cannot live without eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: I can help a sick friend at school by ____. A: taking them to the nurse. The school nurse treats pupils who are sick at school.
chunks.source: The school nurse treats pupils who are sick at school.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Harvested water can be used for ____. A: washing clothes. Rain water collected at home can be used for washing and cleaning.
chunks.source: Rain water collected at home can be used for washing and cleaning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Bees make ____. A: honey. Bees make honey, which people eat as food.
chunks.source: Bees make honey, which people eat as food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is an element of weather? A: rainfall. Rainfall, sunshine, wind and temperature are elements of weather.
chunks.source: Rainfall, sunshine, wind and temperature are elements of weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Trees are useful in a school compound because they give ____. A: shade. Trees give shade where pupils can rest on hot days.
chunks.source: Trees give shade where pupils can rest on hot days.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We keep the environment safe by ____. A: planting trees. Planting trees keeps the air clean and the soil safe.
chunks.source: Planting trees keeps the air clean and the soil safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A housefly is dangerous because it ____. A: spreads diseases. A housefly carries germs from dirt to our food and makes us sick.
chunks.source: A housefly carries germs from dirt to our food and makes us sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Soil profile is ____. A: the arrangement of soil layers. Soil profile shows how the layers of soil lie one above another.
chunks.source: Soil profile shows how the layers of soil lie one above another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A latrine is useful at home because we ____ in it. A: pass out faeces. A latrine is a clean and safe place for passing out faeces.
chunks.source: A latrine is a clean and safe place for passing out faeces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Trees are important because they give us ____. A: fruits. Trees give us fruits, shade, firewood and clean air.
chunks.source: Trees give us fruits, shade, firewood and clean air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which tool is used for harvesting bananas and sugarcanes? A: panga. A panga is a sharp tool used for cutting bananas and sugarcanes.
chunks.source: A panga is a sharp tool used for cutting bananas and sugarcanes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ and ____ are sources of water. A: Rivers and lakes. Rivers, lakes, wells and rain are sources of water.
chunks.source: Rivers, lakes, wells and rain are sources of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Water is useful to people for ____ and ____. A: drinking and cooking. People use water for drinking, cooking, washing and bathing.
chunks.source: People use water for drinking, cooking, washing and bathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ and ____ are immunizable diseases. A: Measles and polio. Measles and polio can be stopped by giving children vaccines.
chunks.source: Measles and polio can be stopped by giving children vaccines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where can immunization be carried out? A: at a health centre. Health workers give vaccines at health centres.
chunks.source: Health workers give vaccines at health centres.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ immunize children. A: Health workers. Health workers like nurses give vaccines to children.
chunks.source: Health workers like nurses give vaccines to children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mulching is ____. A: covering the soil with dry plant materials. Mulching means covering the soil around crops with dry grass or leaves.
chunks.source: Mulching means covering the soil around crops with dry grass or leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Farmers mulch their gardens to ____ and ____. A: keep water in the soil and stop weeds from growing. Mulches keep water in the soil and stop weeds from growing.
chunks.source: Mulches keep water in the soil and stop weeds from growing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ can be used for mulching. A: Dry grass. Dry grass, dry leaves and banana fibres can be used as mulches.
chunks.source: Dry grass, dry leaves and banana fibres can be used as mulches.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each animal to its habitat: cow, spider, lion, termite. A: cow: byre; spider: cobweb; lion: den; termite: anthill. A cow lives in a byre, a spider in a cobweb, a lion in a den and a termite in an anthill.
chunks.source: A cow lives in a byre, a spider in a cobweb, a lion in a den and a termite in an anthill.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Soil erosion is dangerous in the garden because it ____. A: carries away the fertile top soil. Soil erosion washes away the top soil where crops get food.
chunks.source: Soil erosion washes away the top soil where crops get food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Farmers control soil erosion in the school compound by ____. A: planting grass. Grass holds the soil together so it is not washed away.
chunks.source: Grass holds the soil together so it is not washed away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In hilly areas, farmers control soil erosion by ____. A: terracing. Terracing makes steps on hills so water does not wash the soil away fast.
chunks.source: Terracing makes steps on hills so water does not wash the soil away fast.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is a danger of soil erosion? A: It washes away fertile soil. Soil erosion carries away the fertile soil that crops need.
chunks.source: Soil erosion carries away the fertile soil that crops need.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part of the insect labeled Y is the ____. A: antenna. The antenna is found on the head of an insect and is used for feeling.
chunks.source: The antenna is found on the head of an insect and is used for feeling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Part X (the legs) is useful for ____ and part Z (the wings) is useful for ____. A: walking and flying. An insect uses its legs for walking and its wings for flying.
chunks.source: An insect uses its legs for walking and its wings for flying.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of an insect is the thorax? A: the middle part where the legs and wings are joined. The thorax is the middle part of an insect where the legs and wings are attached.
chunks.source: The thorax is the middle part of an insect where the legs and wings are attached.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Group these foodstuffs into Go food and Grow food: cassava, beans, rice, meat. A: Go food: cassava,rice; Grow food: beans,meat. Cassava and rice give us energy (Go food). Beans and meat build our bodies (Grow food).
chunks.source: Cassava and rice give us energy (Go food). Beans and meat build our bodies (Grow food).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ and ____ are common accidents at home. A: Burns and cuts. Burns and cuts happen often at home.
chunks.source: Burns and cuts happen often at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One cause of accidents at school is ____. A: playing rough games. Playing rough games at school can cause falls and injuries.
chunks.source: Playing rough games at school can cause falls and injuries.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A person who has got an accident is called a ____. A: casualty. A casualty is a person who is hurt in an accident.
chunks.source: A casualty is a person who is hurt in an accident.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are domestic animals? A: cow, goat, hen. Cows, goats and hens are kept at home, so they are domestic animals.
chunks.source: Cows, goats and hens are kept at home, so they are domestic animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Domestic animals are useful to people because they give us ____ and ____. A: milk and meat. Domestic animals give us milk, meat, eggs and skins.
chunks.source: Domestic animals give us milk, meat, eggs and skins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Air is ____. A: a mixture of gases. Air is made of gases like oxygen, nitrogen and carbon dioxide.
chunks.source: Air is made of gases like oxygen, nitrogen and carbon dioxide.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which component of air is used for extinguishing fire? A: carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide puts out fire, so it is used in fire extinguishers.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide puts out fire, so it is used in fire extinguishers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which component of air is needed for burning? A: oxygen. Things need oxygen to burn.
chunks.source: Things need oxygen to burn.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The two balloons show that air ____. A: occupies space. The inflated balloon is bigger because the air inside takes up space.
chunks.source: The inflated balloon is bigger because the air inside takes up space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We preserve food to ____. A: keep it for a long time. Preserved food stays good for a long time without going bad.
chunks.source: Preserved food stays good for a long time without going bad.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each food to how it is preserved in villages: beans, fish, ground nuts. A: beans: sun-drying; fish: smoking; ground nuts: sun-drying. Beans and ground nuts are preserved by sun-drying; fish is preserved by smoking.
chunks.source: Beans and ground nuts are preserved by sun-drying; fish is preserved by smoking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The plant shown in the diagram is a ____. A: maize plant. The diagram shows a maize plant with its parts.
chunks.source: The diagram shows a maize plant with its parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part marked K is the ____. A: grains. The grains grow on the cob of the maize plant.
chunks.source: The grains grow on the cob of the maize plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The grains are useful to people because we ____. A: eat them as food. Maize grains are ground into flour to make posho.
chunks.source: Maize grains are ground into flour to make posho.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We care for the maize plant by ____. A: watering it. Watering and weeding help the maize plant grow well.
chunks.source: Watering and weeding help the maize plant grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Poor feeding can cause ____ and ____. A: diseases and poor growth. Children who do not feed well get sick and do not grow well.
chunks.source: Children who do not feed well get sick and do not grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A child who does not feed well has ____ and ____. A: a big stomach and a thin body. Poorly fed children have swollen stomachs and thin bodies.
chunks.source: Poorly fed children have swollen stomachs and thin bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ is a useful insect and a ____ is a harmful insect. A: bee, mosquito. Bees give us honey so they are useful; mosquitoes spread malaria so they are harmful.
chunks.source: Bees give us honey so they are useful; mosquitoes spread malaria so they are harmful.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Birds are useful to people because they give us ____ and ____. A: meat and eggs. We get meat and eggs from birds like hens.
chunks.source: We get meat and eggs from birds like hens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: At school we make ____ for playing. A: balls. Pupils make balls from banana fibres for playing.
chunks.source: Pupils make balls from banana fibres for playing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Balls are made from ____. A: banana fibres. Banana fibres are used to make balls at school.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are used to make balls at school.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We get banana fibres from ____. A: banana plants. Banana fibres come from the stems of banana plants.
chunks.source: Banana fibres come from the stems of banana plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from playing, things we make at school are important because they ____. A: help us learn. Making things at school helps pupils learn new skills.
chunks.source: Making things at school helps pupils learn new skills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we call the study of living and non-living things? A: Science. Science is the study of living things and non-living things.
chunks.source: Science is the study of living things and non-living things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The main natural source of water is ____. A: rain. Rain is the main natural source of water on earth.
chunks.source: Rain is the main natural source of water on earth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An accident is ____. A: something bad that happens without planning. An accident is a bad thing that happens suddenly without planning.
chunks.source: An accident is a bad thing that happens suddenly without planning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we wash our hands with clean water and soap? A: to kill germs. Soap and clean water kill the germs on our hands.
chunks.source: Soap and clean water kill the germs on our hands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of soil is good for growing crops? A: loam soil. Loam soil has sand, clay and humus mixed well, so crops grow well in it.
chunks.source: Loam soil has sand, clay and humus mixed well, so crops grow well in it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which animal lives in water? A: fish. A fish lives in water and breathes in water.
chunks.source: A fish lives in water and breathes in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Animals move from one place to another to look for ____. A: food. Animals move to look for food, water and shelter.
chunks.source: Animals move to look for food, water and shelter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Air is important because we ____ it. A: breathe. We breathe in air to stay alive.
chunks.source: We breathe in air to stay alive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ clouds give us rain. A: Nimbus. Nimbus clouds are dark clouds that bring rain.
chunks.source: Nimbus clouds are dark clouds that bring rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is a type of weather? A: rainy. Rainy, sunny, windy and cloudy are types of weather.
chunks.source: Rainy, sunny, windy and cloudy are types of weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Bees are important to man because they give us ____. A: honey. Bees make honey which people eat.
chunks.source: Bees make honey which people eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of accident is most likely to happen if you play with fire? A: burns. Playing with fire causes burns on the body.
chunks.source: Playing with fire causes burns on the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows that air ____. A: occupies space. The diagram shows air taking up space inside the balloon.
chunks.source: The diagram shows air taking up space inside the balloon.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We breathe in ____. A: oxygen. Oxygen is the part of air that our bodies need.
chunks.source: Oxygen is the part of air that our bodies need.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is a layer of soil. A: Topsoil. Topsoil, subsoil and parent rock are layers of soil.
chunks.source: Topsoil, subsoil and parent rock are layers of soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We keep our environment clean by ____. A: sweeping the compound. Sweeping removes dirt and keeps the environment clean.
chunks.source: Sweeping removes dirt and keeps the environment clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is an example of a natural change? A: day and night. Day and night change on their own without people causing them.
chunks.source: Day and night change on their own without people causing them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: We boil drinking water to ____. A: kill germs. Boiling kills the germs in water that cause diseases.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs in water that cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which gas is used to preserve soft drinks like soda? A: carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is put in sodas to preserve them.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide is put in sodas to preserve them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is a common disease. A: Malaria. Malaria is a common disease spread by mosquitoes.
chunks.source: Malaria is a common disease spread by mosquitoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: ____ is a component of the environment. A: Plants. Plants, animals, water, soil and air are components of the environment.
chunks.source: Plants, animals, water, soil and air are components of the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is a product got from clay? A: a pot. Clay soil is used to make pots and bricks.
chunks.source: Clay soil is used to make pots and bricks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ____ is a wild animal. A: lion. A lion lives in the wild and is not kept at home.
chunks.source: A lion lives in the wild and is not kept at home.

chunks.subject: Science
