chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: Anita is the ___ girl in Primary Four. (smart) A: smartest. Use the superlative with 'the'.
chunks.source: Use the superlative with 'the'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: The gardener was so ___ that he asked for some water to drink. (thirst) A: thirsty. 'Thirst' becomes the adjective 'thirsty'.
chunks.source: 'Thirst' becomes the adjective 'thirsty'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using …as…as…: The juice is very cold. It is like ice. ___ A: The juice is as cold as ice.. 'As ... as' shows two things are equal.
chunks.source: 'As ... as' shows two things are equal.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using …more handsome…: Renny is handsome. Richard is very handsome. ___ A: Richard is more handsome than Renny.. Use the comparative with 'than'.
chunks.source: Use the comparative with 'than'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: read, write, study, learn A: learn, read, study, write. Alphabetical order: l comes before r, r before s, s before w.
chunks.source: Alphabetical order: l comes before r, r before s, s before w.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: house, mosque, temple, church A: church, house, mosque, temple. Compare first letters: c, h, m, t.
chunks.source: Compare first letters: c, h, m, t.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: Literacy, English, Science, Mathematics A: English, Literacy, Mathematics, Science. Compare first letters: E, L, M, S.
chunks.source: Compare first letters: E, L, M, S.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: hen, parrot, duck, eagle A: duck, eagle, hen, parrot. Compare first letters: d, e, h, p.
chunks.source: Compare first letters: d, e, h, p.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: class, church, cell, cold A: cell, church, class, cold. All start with 'c'; compare second letters: e, h, l, o.
chunks.source: All start with 'c'; compare second letters: e, h, l, o.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: rise, ring, ride, ripe A: ride, ring, ripe, rise. All start with 'ri'; compare third letters: d, n, p, s.
chunks.source: All start with 'ri'; compare third letters: d, n, p, s.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: send, sit, stand, scent A: scent, send, sit, stand. Compare: sc, se, si, st — second letters c, e, i, t.
chunks.source: Compare: sc, se, si, st — second letters c, e, i, t.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: Xavier, Amos, Peter, Zaitun A: Amos, Peter, Xavier, Zaitun. Compare first letters: A, P, X, Z.
chunks.source: Compare first letters: A, P, X, Z.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: Rwanda, Zaire, Uganda, Kenya A: Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda, Zaire. Compare first letters: K, R, U, Z.
chunks.source: Compare first letters: K, R, U, Z.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: meat, mean, meet, meal A: meal, mean, meat, meet. All start with 'mea'/'mee'; compare: meal, mean, meat, meet.
chunks.source: All start with 'mea'/'mee'; compare: meal, mean, meat, meet.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: tin, teacher, torch, tank A: tank, teacher, tin, torch. Compare: ta, te, ti, to — second letters a, e, i, o.
chunks.source: Compare: ta, te, ti, to — second letters a, e, i, o.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange in alphabetical order: square, circle, triangle, oval A: circle, oval, square, triangle. Compare first letters: c, o, s, t.
chunks.source: Compare first letters: c, o, s, t.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange in alphabetical order: dentist, mechanic, optician, nurse A: dentist, mechanic, nurse, optician. Compare first letters: d, m, n, o.
chunks.source: Compare first letters: d, m, n, o.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct pronoun: Amos did the work ___ . (he) A: himself. Use the reflexive pronoun when the doer and receiver are the same.
chunks.source: Use the reflexive pronoun when the doer and receiver are the same.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct pronoun: They always cross the road ___ . (them) A: themselves. 'They' takes the reflexive 'themselves'.
chunks.source: 'They' takes the reflexive 'themselves'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct pronoun: She goes to the well ___ . (she) A: herself. 'She' takes the reflexive 'herself'.
chunks.source: 'She' takes the reflexive 'herself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct pronoun: Those clothes are ___ . (me) A: mine. Use the possessive pronoun 'mine' after 'are'.
chunks.source: Use the possessive pronoun 'mine' after 'are'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct pronoun: We should attempt the questions ___ . (us) A: ourselves. 'We' takes the reflexive 'ourselves'.
chunks.source: 'We' takes the reflexive 'ourselves'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: The teacher beat our friends yesterday. ___ A: The teacher beat them yesterday.. 'Our friends' becomes 'them'.
chunks.source: 'Our friends' becomes 'them'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: She will not see Rinah, Jackie and I. ___ A: She will not see us.. 'Rinah, Jackie and I' becomes 'us'.
chunks.source: 'Rinah, Jackie and I' becomes 'us'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: John is stealing your snacks. ___ A: He is stealing your snacks.. 'John' becomes 'he'.
chunks.source: 'John' becomes 'he'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: Roritah is mad. ___ A: She is mad.. 'Roritah' becomes 'she'.
chunks.source: 'Roritah' becomes 'she'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: That cat ate the rat. ___ A: It ate the rat.. An animal becomes 'it'.
chunks.source: An animal becomes 'it'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: Ann, Lukia and I played well. ___ A: We played well.. 'Ann, Lukia and I' becomes 'we'.
chunks.source: 'Ann, Lukia and I' becomes 'we'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: They did the work alone. ___ A: They did the work themselves.. 'Alone' becomes the reflexive 'themselves'.
chunks.source: 'Alone' becomes the reflexive 'themselves'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: She painted this beautiful picture ___ . (self) A: herself. 'She' takes the reflexive 'herself'.
chunks.source: 'She' takes the reflexive 'herself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using …belongs…: That ruler is mine. ___ A: That ruler belongs to me.. 'Belongs to' shows ownership.
chunks.source: 'Belongs to' shows ownership.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: The children ___ food every evening. (carry) A: carry. Present simple for habits: base verb with plural subject.
chunks.source: Present simple for habits: base verb with plural subject.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Shanita always ___ soccer. (play) A: plays. Add -s for he/she/it in present simple.
chunks.source: Add -s for he/she/it in present simple.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: He ___ up at six o’clock. (wake) A: wakes. Add -s for he/she/it in present simple.
chunks.source: Add -s for he/she/it in present simple.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: They sometimes ___ their grandparents. (visit) A: visit. Base verb with plural subject 'they'.
chunks.source: Base verb with plural subject 'they'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who are the people conversing? ___ A: Desire and George. The dialogue is between Desire and George.
chunks.source: The dialogue is between Desire and George.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the conversation about? ___ A: A trip to Kasese. They talk about George's trip to Kasese.
chunks.source: They talk about George's trip to Kasese.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who went for the trip? ___ A: George. George went to Kasese; Desire stayed home.
chunks.source: George went to Kasese; Desire stayed home.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How many people are in the conversation? A: Two. Desire and George are talking.
chunks.source: Desire and George are talking.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two places George visited in Kasese. ___ A: Rwenzori National Game Park and Mt. Rwenzori. He visited the game park, salt mine, copper mine and the mountain.
chunks.source: He visited the game park, salt mine, copper mine and the mountain.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which mountain is found in Kasese district according to the conversation? ___ A: Mt. Rwenzori. George mentions Mt. Rwenzori itself.
chunks.source: George mentions Mt. Rwenzori itself.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: George enjoyed the trip to Kasese. A: True. He said 'Excellent. We enjoyed so much.'
chunks.source: He said 'Excellent. We enjoyed so much.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why didn't Desire go for the trip? ___ A: His mother had no money. Desire's mother had no money.
chunks.source: Desire's mother had no money.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the title of the conversation? ___ A: A trip to Kasese. The conversation is titled 'A trip to Kasese'.
chunks.source: The conversation is titled 'A trip to Kasese'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who is being talked about? ___ A: Bogere. The story is about Bogere.
chunks.source: The story is about Bogere.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where did Bogere stay? ___ A: In Katikamu village. He lived in a village called Katikamu.
chunks.source: He lived in a village called Katikamu.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why was Bogere known by the women and children? ___ A: Because of his muscular body. They knew him because of his muscular body.
chunks.source: They knew him because of his muscular body.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Identify two adjectives in the story. ___ A: muscular, humble. The story uses adjectives like muscular, humble, kind, strong, old, young.
chunks.source: The story uses adjectives like muscular, humble, kind, strong, old, young.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why did the old people like Bogere very much? ___ A: He fetched water and firewood for them. He used to fetch water and firewood for old people.
chunks.source: He used to fetch water and firewood for old people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who attacked the village? A: A group of young men. A group of young men attacked the village.
chunks.source: A group of young men attacked the village.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How did Bogere save his village? ___ A: He fought the attackers and scared them away. He fought them until they ran off.
chunks.source: He fought them until they ran off.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why were the young men scared? ___ A: Because Bogere was very strong. They discovered that he was very strong.
chunks.source: They discovered that he was very strong.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the title of the story. ___ A: The strongest man in Katikamu. The story is titled 'The strongest man in Katikamu'.
chunks.source: The story is titled 'The strongest man in Katikamu'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: The thief jumped ___ the fence. A: over. Jump across something: jump over.
chunks.source: Jump across something: jump over.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: The cow is sleeping ___ the tree shade. A: under. Under the shade of the tree.
chunks.source: Under the shade of the tree.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: Do not lean ___ that wall, it’s very weak. A: against. Lean against a wall.
chunks.source: Lean against a wall.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: Aren’t you ashamed ___ your conduct? A: of. 'Ashamed of' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'Ashamed of' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: Bob is sure ___ his success in future. A: of. 'Sure of' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'Sure of' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: The hunter aimed ___ the animal. A: at. Aim at a target.
chunks.source: Aim at a target.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: Kamujje was accused ___ stealing the old man’s fruits. A: of. 'Accused of' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'Accused of' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: William prefers a sweater ___ a coat. A: to. 'Prefer X to Y' uses 'to'.
chunks.source: 'Prefer X to Y' uses 'to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: He is jealous ___ his brother’s success. A: of. 'Jealous of' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'Jealous of' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: May I introduce you ___ Mrs. Mugabi? A: to. 'Introduce to' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'Introduce to' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the most suitable word: The twins shared the apples ___ themselves. A: among. Share with more than two: 'among'.
chunks.source: Share with more than two: 'among'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the most suitable word: It is not a good habit to quarrel ___ neighbours. A: with. Quarrel with someone.
chunks.source: Quarrel with someone.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the most suitable word: The bitch with its puppies was lying in its ___. A: kennel. A dog's house is called a kennel.
chunks.source: A dog's house is called a kennel.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange the words to make a meaningful sentence: waited / have / I / an / for / hour A: I, have, waited, for, an, hour. Present perfect: I have waited for an hour.
chunks.source: Present perfect: I have waited for an hour.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange the words to make a meaningful sentence: by / herself / Tamara / school / went / to A: Tamara, went, to, school, by, herself. Tamara went to school by herself.
chunks.source: Tamara went to school by herself.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange the words to make a meaningful sentence: train / have / you / by / ever / travelled? A: Have, you, ever, travelled, by, train?. Present perfect question: Have you ever travelled by train?
chunks.source: Present perfect question: Have you ever travelled by train?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite replacing the underlined word with its opposite: All our tables are very rough. ___ A: All our tables are very smooth.. The opposite of 'rough' is 'smooth'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'rough' is 'smooth'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite replacing the underlined word with its opposite: Nakachwa is stronger than her brother. ___ A: Nakachwa is weaker than her brother.. The opposite of 'stronger' is 'weaker'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'stronger' is 'weaker'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite replacing the underlined word with its opposite: Jessica has to buy some apples today. ___ A: Jessica has to sell some apples today.. The opposite of 'buy' is 'sell'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'buy' is 'sell'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite beginning with “What”: My father is a very tall man. ___ A: What a very tall man my father is!. 'What a ...!' makes an exclamation.
chunks.source: 'What a ...!' makes an exclamation.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a suitable question for this answer: She goes to school on foot. ___ A: How does she go to school?. Ask 'How' about the way she travels.
chunks.source: Ask 'How' about the way she travels.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the passage about? ___ A: Body parts. The passage is about body parts.
chunks.source: The passage is about body parts.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who is wonderful in his creation? ___ A: God. God is very wonderful in his creation.
chunks.source: God is very wonderful in his creation.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How did God create people? ___ A: With a lot of care and love. He created people with care and love.
chunks.source: He created people with care and love.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where do we find the eyes and ears? ___ A: On the head. On the head we find the eyes and ears.
chunks.source: On the head we find the eyes and ears.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which part enables people to see? A: The eyes. The eyes enable us to see.
chunks.source: The eyes enable us to see.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How is the mouth useful? ___ A: It enables us to talk and eat. The mouth is for talking and eating.
chunks.source: The mouth is for talking and eating.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: According to the passage, what do footballers need to kick a ball? ___ A: Legs. The legs enable footballers to kick the ball.
chunks.source: The legs enable footballers to kick the ball.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why should you protect the body parts? ___ A: Because God created them with a purpose. God created them with a purpose, and they can be damaged.
chunks.source: God created them with a purpose, and they can be damaged.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give another word to mean “talk”. ___ A: speak. The mouth enables us to talk and eat.
chunks.source: The mouth enables us to talk and eat.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give another word to mean “created”. ___ A: made. God created people.
chunks.source: God created people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who is the writer of the poem? ___ A: Murungi Maxine. The poem is by Murungi Maxine.
chunks.source: The poem is by Murungi Maxine.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the poem about? ___ A: Good news about the coming rain. The poem is about the good news of coming rain.
chunks.source: The poem is about the good news of coming rain.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the writer waiting to get? ___ A: Rain. They are soon getting rain.
chunks.source: They are soon getting rain.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How many stanzas are shown? ___ A: Four. The poem has four stanzas.
chunks.source: The poem has four stanzas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What will the rain chase away in stanza one? ___ A: The dust and the heat. Gone will be the dust and the heat.
chunks.source: Gone will be the dust and the heat.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How are crops useful to farmers? ___ A: For food and to sell. Farmers plant crops for food and to sell.
chunks.source: Farmers plant crops for food and to sell.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How many crops have been mentioned? ___ A: Four. Maize, beans, soya and millet are mentioned.
chunks.source: Maize, beans, soya and millet are mentioned.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give two uses of water at home. ___ A: For animals to drink and for people to use. Water is for animals to drink and for people to use at home.
chunks.source: Water is for animals to drink and for people to use at home.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How old is the writer? A: Nine years. The writer is nine years old.
chunks.source: The writer is nine years old.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which birds were lazy? A: The chickens. The chickens were lazy and noisy.
chunks.source: The chickens were lazy and noisy.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why did the birds agree to chase away the chickens? ___ A: Because the chickens were lazy and noisy. The chickens were making the forest noisy.
chunks.source: The chickens were making the forest noisy.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: According to the passage, who was sent to tell the chickens to leave the forest? ___ A: Mr. Eagle and three other strong birds. Mr. Eagle and three strong birds were sent.
chunks.source: Mr. Eagle and three strong birds were sent.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where did the chickens feel good? ___ A: At the river. They came across a river and felt good.
chunks.source: They came across a river and felt good.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do you think mother chicken scratched the ground? ___ A: To find food for the hungry chicks. She scratched the ground to find food for the chicks.
chunks.source: She scratched the ground to find food for the chicks.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What was in the metallic box? ___ A: Something very shiny. Inside the box was something very shiny.
chunks.source: Inside the box was something very shiny.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why did the king order the servants to build a special home for the chickens? ___ A: To reward the chickens for their good work. The king wanted to reward their good work.
chunks.source: The king wanted to reward their good work.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What good thing did the chickens do? ___ A: They found the queen's stolen golden ring. They found the queen's golden ring.
chunks.source: They found the queen's golden ring.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where does Omara live? ___ A: In Aloi, Lira District. Omara lives with his aunt in Aloi in Lira District.
chunks.source: Omara lives with his aunt in Aloi in Lira District.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: With whom does Omara stay? A: With his aunt. He lives with his aunt.
chunks.source: He lives with his aunt.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: According to the passage, what does Omara call Otim? ___ A: His uncle. Otim is his uncle.
chunks.source: Otim is his uncle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Whom did Omara go to Kampala with? ___ A: Kizza. He went with his uncle's friend Kizza.
chunks.source: He went with his uncle's friend Kizza.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where did Omara and Kizza have their lunch? ___ A: At the restaurant. Kizza took Omara to a restaurant for a meal.
chunks.source: Kizza took Omara to a restaurant for a meal.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where do you think Omara went after leaving the restaurant? ___ A: For a walk around Kampala city. He decided to take a walk around Kampala city.
chunks.source: He decided to take a walk around Kampala city.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who directed Omara when he went out of the restaurant? ___ A: The waiter. He asked the waiter to direct him.
chunks.source: He asked the waiter to direct him.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: When Omara left the bakery, where did he go? ___ A: Back to the restaurant. He walked back to the restaurant.
chunks.source: He walked back to the restaurant.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Suggest a suitable title for the passage. ___ A: Omara visits Kampala. The story is about Omara's visit to Kampala.
chunks.source: The story is about Omara's visit to Kampala.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is the adverb in: “The monkey ate the banana hurriedly.” A: hurriedly. An adverb tells us how the action was done.
chunks.source: An adverb tells us how the action was done.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is the adverb in: “Muddu slept soundly at night.” A: soundly. An adverb tells us how he slept.
chunks.source: An adverb tells us how he slept.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is the adverb in: “Kwesiga was hurt badly in the accident.” A: badly. An adverb tells us how he was hurt.
chunks.source: An adverb tells us how he was hurt.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is the adverb in: “Humble children speak softly.” A: softly. An adverb tells us how they speak.
chunks.source: An adverb tells us how they speak.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is the adverb in: “I can’t see clearly.” A: clearly. An adverb tells us how you see.
chunks.source: An adverb tells us how you see.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is the adverb in: “The old lady walked slowly across the road.” A: slowly. An adverb tells us how she walked.
chunks.source: An adverb tells us how she walked.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is the adverb in: “They live happily with their parents.” A: happily. An adverb tells us how they live.
chunks.source: An adverb tells us how they live.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is the adverb in: “Did you understand properly?” A: properly. An adverb tells us how you understood.
chunks.source: An adverb tells us how you understood.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Cheap ___ A: cheaply. Add -ly to form the adverb.
chunks.source: Add -ly to form the adverb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Poor ___ A: poorly. Add -ly to form the adverb.
chunks.source: Add -ly to form the adverb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Quiet ___ A: quietly. Add -ly; 'quiet' keeps its spelling.
chunks.source: Add -ly; 'quiet' keeps its spelling.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Patient ___ A: patiently. Add -ly to form the adverb.
chunks.source: Add -ly to form the adverb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Beautiful ___ A: beautifully. Add -ly to form the adverb.
chunks.source: Add -ly to form the adverb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Careful ___ A: carefully. Add -ly to form the adverb.
chunks.source: Add -ly to form the adverb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: lazy ___ A: lazily. Change y to i, then add -ly.
chunks.source: Change y to i, then add -ly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: easy ___ A: easily. Change y to i, then add -ly.
chunks.source: Change y to i, then add -ly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: noisy ___ A: noisily. Change y to i, then add -ly.
chunks.source: Change y to i, then add -ly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: busy ___ A: busily. Change y to i, then add -ly.
chunks.source: Change y to i, then add -ly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: day ___ A: daily. 'Day' becomes 'daily'.
chunks.source: 'Day' becomes 'daily'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: The thief was ___ beaten. (bad) A: badly. Use the adverb 'badly' to describe how he was beaten.
chunks.source: Use the adverb 'badly' to describe how he was beaten.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: I think we can ___ do this work. (easy) A: easily. Use the adverb 'easily' to describe how we can do it.
chunks.source: Use the adverb 'easily' to describe how we can do it.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: They ___ asked for permission from the teacher. (humble) A: humbly. Use the adverb 'humbly'.
chunks.source: Use the adverb 'humbly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Wabwa died ___ . (sudden) A: suddenly. Add -ly: suddenly.
chunks.source: Add -ly: suddenly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Daddy ___ answered him back. (angry) A: angrily. Add -ily: angrily.
chunks.source: Add -ily: angrily.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: It was ___ marked. (clear) A: clearly. Add -ly: clearly.
chunks.source: Add -ly: clearly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: That man is ___ sick. (mental) A: mentally. Add -ly: mentally.
chunks.source: Add -ly: mentally.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Suzan ___ dressed for the ceremony. (decent) A: decently. Add -ly: decently.
chunks.source: Add -ly: decently.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: They took their books to the teacher ___. (immediate) A: immediately. 'Immediate' becomes 'immediately'.
chunks.source: 'Immediate' becomes 'immediately'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is the adverb in: “The man acted cruelly with the child.” A: cruelly. An adverb tells us how he acted.
chunks.source: An adverb tells us how he acted.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is the adverb in: “The child hugged the mother immediately.” A: immediately. An adverb tells us when/how she hugged.
chunks.source: An adverb tells us when/how she hugged.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is the adverb in: “Don’t run too fast.” A: fast. 'Fast' tells us how to run.
chunks.source: 'Fast' tells us how to run.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word is the adverb in: “Somebody knocked at the door loudly.” A: loudly. An adverb tells us how they knocked.
chunks.source: An adverb tells us how they knocked.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Kind ___ A: kindly. Add -ly to form the adverb.
chunks.source: Add -ly to form the adverb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Usual ___ A: usually. Add -ly: usually.
chunks.source: Add -ly: usually.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Rude ___ A: rudely. Add -ly: rudely.
chunks.source: Add -ly: rudely.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: hurry ___ A: hurriedly. Change y to i, add -ly: hurriedly.
chunks.source: Change y to i, add -ly: hurriedly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: merry ___ A: merrily. Change y to i, add -ly: merrily.
chunks.source: Change y to i, add -ly: merrily.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with a suitable adverb: The cheetah jumped over the kob ___. (swift) A: swiftly. Add -ly: swiftly.
chunks.source: Add -ly: swiftly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with a suitable adverb: The doctor was called ___ for the patient in a critical condition. (immediate) A: immediately. 'Immediate' becomes 'immediately'.
chunks.source: 'Immediate' becomes 'immediately'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with a suitable adverb: The workers got their salary ___. (month) A: monthly. 'Month' becomes 'monthly'.
chunks.source: 'Month' becomes 'monthly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with a suitable adverb: He speaks English ___. (fluent) A: fluently. Add -ly: fluently.
chunks.source: Add -ly: fluently.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with a suitable adverb: She sings ___. (sweet) A: sweetly. Add -ly: sweetly.
chunks.source: Add -ly: sweetly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: She crossed the road ___ and got an accident. (care) A: carelessly. Use the adverb 'carelessly' to describe how she crossed.
chunks.source: Use the adverb 'carelessly' to describe how she crossed.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with “some” or “any”: I don’t want ___ book in my bag. A: any. Use 'any' in negative sentences.
chunks.source: Use 'any' in negative sentences.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with “some” or “any”: She has ___ stones in the wheelbarrow. A: some. Use 'some' in affirmative sentences.
chunks.source: Use 'some' in affirmative sentences.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with “some” or “any”: They have bought ___ meat today. A: some. Use 'some' in affirmative sentences.
chunks.source: Use 'some' in affirmative sentences.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with “some” or “any”: Daddy is waiting for ___ money from the shopkeeper. A: some. Use 'some' in affirmative sentences.
chunks.source: Use 'some' in affirmative sentences.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with “some” or “any”: There were ___ children at the party. A: some. Use 'some' in affirmative sentences.
chunks.source: Use 'some' in affirmative sentences.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the most suitable word: There wasn’t ___ sugar left in the bowl. A: any. Use 'any' in negative sentences.
chunks.source: Use 'any' in negative sentences.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Mummy has ___ some eggs. (fry) A: fried. Present perfect: has + past participle. 'Fry' → 'fried'.
chunks.source: Present perfect: has + past participle. 'Fry' → 'fried'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: The bees ___ my brother yesterday. (sting) A: stung. 'Sting' is irregular: sting → stung → stung.
chunks.source: 'Sting' is irregular: sting → stung → stung.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Monica has ___ the compound very well. (sweep) A: swept. 'Sweep' is irregular: sweep → swept → swept.
chunks.source: 'Sweep' is irregular: sweep → swept → swept.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: The boy ___ down on the mat. (lie) A: lay. 'Lie' (rest) is irregular: lie → lay → lain.
chunks.source: 'Lie' (rest) is irregular: lie → lay → lain.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Our time keeper has ___ the bell. (ring) A: rung. 'Ring' is irregular: ring → rang → rung.
chunks.source: 'Ring' is irregular: ring → rang → rung.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Who has ___ my book on the floor? (put) A: put. 'Put' is the same in all forms.
chunks.source: 'Put' is the same in all forms.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Her baby has been ___ by hot water. (burn) A: burnt. 'Burn' → 'burnt' (or 'burned').
chunks.source: 'Burn' → 'burnt' (or 'burned').

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: They have ___ nicely. (sing) A: sung. 'Sing' is irregular: sing → sang → sung.
chunks.source: 'Sing' is irregular: sing → sang → sung.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: David never ___ for permission before going outside. (ask) A: asked. Regular verb: add -ed.
chunks.source: Regular verb: add -ed.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Paul has ___ my soda. (drink) A: drunk. 'Drink' is irregular: drink → drank → drunk.
chunks.source: 'Drink' is irregular: drink → drank → drunk.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: The pupils have ___ English. (speak) A: spoken. 'Speak' is irregular: speak → spoke → spoken.
chunks.source: 'Speak' is irregular: speak → spoke → spoken.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Amina has ___ a car. (drive) A: driven. 'Drive' is irregular: drive → drove → driven.
chunks.source: 'Drive' is irregular: drive → drove → driven.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: She has ___ well. (write) A: written. 'Write' is irregular: write → wrote → written.
chunks.source: 'Write' is irregular: write → wrote → written.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: The school choir has ___ a nice song at the assembly. (sing) A: sung. Present perfect: has + past participle. 'Sing' → 'sung'.
chunks.source: Present perfect: has + past participle. 'Sing' → 'sung'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to the negative form: They sold some mangoes. ___ A: They did not sell any mangoes.. Past simple negative: did not + verb. 'Some' becomes 'any'.
chunks.source: Past simple negative: did not + verb. 'Some' becomes 'any'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to the negative form: Monica heard the baby crying. ___ A: Monica did not hear the baby crying.. Past simple negative: did not + verb.
chunks.source: Past simple negative: did not + verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to the negative form: We ate some food at the party. ___ A: We did not eat any food at the party.. Past simple negative: did not + verb. 'Some' becomes 'any'.
chunks.source: Past simple negative: did not + verb. 'Some' becomes 'any'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to the negative form: The teacher marked our books. ___ A: The teacher did not mark our books.. Past simple negative: did not + verb.
chunks.source: Past simple negative: did not + verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to the negative form: He played football yesterday. ___ A: He did not play football yesterday.. Past simple negative: did not + verb.
chunks.source: Past simple negative: did not + verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using …did not…: Mummy gave me some money for transport. ___ A: Mummy did not give me any money for transport.. Past negative: did not + base verb; 'some' becomes 'any'.
chunks.source: Past negative: did not + base verb; 'some' becomes 'any'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to the interrogative form: She was cooking food. ___ A: Was she cooking food?. Move 'was' to the front for questions.
chunks.source: Move 'was' to the front for questions.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to the interrogative form: Anita sang nicely. ___ A: Did Anita sing nicely?. Past simple questions start with 'Did'.
chunks.source: Past simple questions start with 'Did'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to the interrogative form: The teacher taught us very well. ___ A: Did the teacher teach us very well?. Past simple questions start with 'Did' + base verb.
chunks.source: Past simple questions start with 'Did' + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to the interrogative form: Daddy was driving his car. ___ A: Was Daddy driving his car?. Move 'was' to the front for questions.
chunks.source: Move 'was' to the front for questions.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to the interrogative form: The policemen arrested the thief. ___ A: Did the policemen arrest the thief?. Past simple questions start with 'Did' + base verb.
chunks.source: Past simple questions start with 'Did' + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: We are ___ now. (plan) A: planning. Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing. Double the n in 'plan'.
chunks.source: Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing. Double the n in 'plan'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Mutebi is ___ his bicycle now. (ride) A: riding. Present continuous: is + verb-ing. Drop the e in 'ride'.
chunks.source: Present continuous: is + verb-ing. Drop the e in 'ride'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: I am ___ now. (eat) A: eating. Present continuous: am + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Present continuous: am + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: They are ___ now. (revise) A: revising. Present continuous: are + verb-ing. Drop the e.
chunks.source: Present continuous: are + verb-ing. Drop the e.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: The baby is ___ with a doll. (play) A: playing. Present continuous: is + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Present continuous: is + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: The baby cries every night, ___? A: doesn't it. Present simple positive takes negative tag: doesn't it.
chunks.source: Present simple positive takes negative tag: doesn't it.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: He wrote well, ___? A: didn't he. Past simple positive takes negative tag: didn't he.
chunks.source: Past simple positive takes negative tag: didn't he.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: They do not write well, ___? A: do they. Negative statement takes positive tag: do they.
chunks.source: Negative statement takes positive tag: do they.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: We are learning, ___? A: aren't we. 'Are' positive takes negative tag: aren't we.
chunks.source: 'Are' positive takes negative tag: aren't we.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: I am happy, ___? A: aren't I. 'I am' takes the special tag 'aren't I'.
chunks.source: 'I am' takes the special tag 'aren't I'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: I am not sad, ___? A: am I. 'I am not' takes the positive tag 'am I'.
chunks.source: 'I am not' takes the positive tag 'am I'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: The dog is barking, ___? A: isn't it. Positive statement takes negative tag: isn't it.
chunks.source: Positive statement takes negative tag: isn't it.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: The girl was sick, ___? A: wasn't she. Past 'was' positive takes negative tag: wasn't she.
chunks.source: Past 'was' positive takes negative tag: wasn't she.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: They were not around, ___? A: were they. Negative statement takes positive tag: were they.
chunks.source: Negative statement takes positive tag: were they.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: She was not beaten, ___? A: was she. Negative statement takes positive tag: was she.
chunks.source: Negative statement takes positive tag: was she.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply a suitable question tag: We write our work neatly, ___? A: don't we. Present simple positive takes negative tag.
chunks.source: Present simple positive takes negative tag.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the source of knowledge? ___ A: The fear of the Lord. The poem says the fear of the Lord is the source of knowledge.
chunks.source: The poem says the fear of the Lord is the source of knowledge.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who says that the fear of the parents is the source of success? ___ A: The poet. The poet says, 'The fear of the parents is the source of success, I say.'
chunks.source: The poet says, 'The fear of the parents is the source of success, I say.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why should one be humble before God? ___ A: Because the humble ones are blessed. The poem says the humble ones are blessed.
chunks.source: The poem says the humble ones are blessed.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What will happen to your children when you grow up? ___ A: They will also be humble and blessed. The poem says they will also be humble and blessed.
chunks.source: The poem says they will also be humble and blessed.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What should be your daily word? ___ A: Sorry. The poem says 'Sorry should be your daily word'.
chunks.source: The poem says 'Sorry should be your daily word'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What cools anger? ___ A: Sorry. The poem says 'sorry cools the anger'.
chunks.source: The poem says 'sorry cools the anger'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does God do to those who say sorry? ___ A: God blesses them. The poem says 'God blesses those who say sorry'.
chunks.source: The poem says 'God blesses those who say sorry'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What cools hunger? ___ A: Food. The poem says 'As food cools the hunger'.
chunks.source: The poem says 'As food cools the hunger'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who wrote this poem? ___ A: Mukasa Desire. The poem is by Mukasa Desire.
chunks.source: The poem is by Mukasa Desire.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the story about? ___ A: A disobedient boy called Tony. The story is about Tony, a disobedient boy.
chunks.source: The story is about Tony, a disobedient boy.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: In which school is Tony? ___ A: Lugazi Primary School. Tony is in primary four at Lugazi Primary School.
chunks.source: Tony is in primary four at Lugazi Primary School.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What did Tony decide to do instead of washing plates? ___ A: He went to play with his friends. He went to play at the neighbouring home.
chunks.source: He went to play at the neighbouring home.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where did Tony go to play? ___ A: At the neighbouring home. He played with friends at the neighbouring home.
chunks.source: He played with friends at the neighbouring home.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why was Tony punished by his father? ___ A: For not washing the plates. His father punished him for not washing the plates.
chunks.source: His father punished him for not washing the plates.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Tony apologised to his father. A: False. The story says he could not even apologise.
chunks.source: The story says he could not even apologise.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who was caught stealing food at night? ___ A: Tony. Tony stole food from the cupboard at night.
chunks.source: Tony stole food from the cupboard at night.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: For how many hours did Tony play? ___ A: Three hours. After three hours Tony went back home.
chunks.source: After three hours Tony went back home.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What did Tony steal from the cupboard? ___ A: Food. He stole food his mother had kept in the cupboard.
chunks.source: He stole food his mother had kept in the cupboard.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the title of the story? ___ A: The disobedient boy. The story is titled 'The disobedient boy'.
chunks.source: The story is titled 'The disobedient boy'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …too…to…: The cow is very old. It cannot give us enough milk. ___ A: The cow is too old to give us enough milk.. 'Too + adjective + to' shows something is impossible.
chunks.source: 'Too + adjective + to' shows something is impossible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …too…to…: The car is very old. It cannot carry a heavy load. ___ A: The car is too old to carry a heavy load.. 'Too + adjective + to' shows something is impossible.
chunks.source: 'Too + adjective + to' shows something is impossible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …too…to…: The donkey is very weak. It cannot lift the load up the mountain. ___ A: The donkey is too weak to lift the load up the mountain.. 'Too + adjective + to' shows something is impossible.
chunks.source: 'Too + adjective + to' shows something is impossible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …too…to…: He was very ill. He could not speak clearly. ___ A: He was too ill to speak clearly.. 'Too + adjective + to' shows something is impossible.
chunks.source: 'Too + adjective + to' shows something is impossible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …too…to…: He was slow. He did not finish the exercise. ___ A: He was too slow to finish the exercise.. 'Too + adjective + to' shows something is impossible.
chunks.source: 'Too + adjective + to' shows something is impossible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite as one sentence using …too…to…: The teacher was very excited. He could not speak properly. ___ A: The teacher was too excited to speak properly.. 'Too + adjective + to' shows impossibility.
chunks.source: 'Too + adjective + to' shows impossibility.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …enough to…: Alupo is very strong. He will lift the sack alone. ___ A: Alupo is strong enough to lift the sack alone.. 'Adjective + enough + to' shows something is possible.
chunks.source: 'Adjective + enough + to' shows something is possible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …enough to…: Doreen is very clever. She will get a first grade. ___ A: Doreen is clever enough to get a first grade.. 'Adjective + enough + to' shows something is possible.
chunks.source: 'Adjective + enough + to' shows something is possible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …enough to…: She is very old. She can walk through the town alone. ___ A: She is old enough to walk through the town alone.. 'Adjective + enough + to' shows something is possible.
chunks.source: 'Adjective + enough + to' shows something is possible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …enough to…: He is very skilled. He can repair a computer. ___ A: He is skilled enough to repair a computer.. 'Adjective + enough + to' shows something is possible.
chunks.source: 'Adjective + enough + to' shows something is possible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …enough to…: He is quite tall. He can touch the ceiling. ___ A: He is tall enough to touch the ceiling.. 'Adjective + enough + to' shows something is possible.
chunks.source: 'Adjective + enough + to' shows something is possible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …so…that…: A lion is very dangerous. Everybody fears it. ___ A: A lion is so dangerous that everybody fears it.. 'So + adjective + that' shows a result.
chunks.source: 'So + adjective + that' shows a result.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …so…that…: Mukunde’s wedding was very interesting. The visitors didn’t want to go home. ___ A: Mukunde’s wedding was so interesting that the visitors didn’t want to go home.. 'So + adjective + that' shows a result.
chunks.source: 'So + adjective + that' shows a result.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …so…that…: The dog is very fierce. All the children fear it. ___ A: The dog is so fierce that all the children fear it.. 'So + adjective + that' shows a result.
chunks.source: 'So + adjective + that' shows a result.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …so…that…: Mulondo is very honest. Everybody respects him. ___ A: Mulondo is so honest that everybody respects him.. 'So + adjective + that' shows a result.
chunks.source: 'So + adjective + that' shows a result.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …so…that…: Grace was very hardworking. She was able to pass the test. ___ A: Grace was so hardworking that she was able to pass the test.. 'So + adjective + that' shows a result.
chunks.source: 'So + adjective + that' shows a result.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using …so…that…: The pupils are very clever. They can score high marks. ___ A: The pupils are so clever that they can score high marks.. 'So + adjective + that' shows a result.
chunks.source: 'So + adjective + that' shows a result.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write using …prefer…to…: Janet likes reading more than writing. ___ A: Janet prefers reading to writing.. 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.
chunks.source: 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write using …prefer…to…: I like Uganda more than other countries. ___ A: I prefer Uganda to other countries.. 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.
chunks.source: 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write using …prefer…to…: Children like day schools more than boarding schools. ___ A: Children prefer day schools to boarding schools.. 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.
chunks.source: 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write using …prefer…to…: She likes singing more than dancing. ___ A: She prefers singing to dancing.. 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.
chunks.source: 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write using …prefer…to…: I like poems but I like riddles much more. ___ A: I prefer riddles to poems.. 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.
chunks.source: 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using …prefers…: She loves swimming more than skipping. ___ A: She prefers swimming to skipping.. 'Prefers X to Y' means liking X more.
chunks.source: 'Prefers X to Y' means liking X more.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …either…or…: They may go and watch a movie. They may stay at home. ___ A: They may either go and watch a movie or stay at home.. 'Either...or' gives two choices.
chunks.source: 'Either...or' gives two choices.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …either…or…: She can sing. She can dance. ___ A: She can either sing or dance.. 'Either...or' gives two choices.
chunks.source: 'Either...or' gives two choices.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …either…or…: You can eat. You can drink. ___ A: You can either eat or drink.. 'Either...or' gives two choices.
chunks.source: 'Either...or' gives two choices.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …neither…nor…: It is not deep. It is not salty. ___ A: It is neither deep nor salty.. 'Neither...nor' joins two negatives.
chunks.source: 'Neither...nor' joins two negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …neither…nor…: He did not play. He did not warm up. ___ A: He neither played nor warmed up.. 'Neither...nor' joins two negatives.
chunks.source: 'Neither...nor' joins two negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …neither…nor…: The dog could not sleep. It could not bark. ___ A: The dog could neither sleep nor bark.. 'Neither...nor' joins two negatives.
chunks.source: 'Neither...nor' joins two negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using: Neither …nor…: Janat did not eat food. Nancy did not eat food. ___ A: Neither Janat nor Nancy ate food.. 'Neither...nor' joins two negatives.
chunks.source: 'Neither...nor' joins two negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite as one sentence using …and…: English is an interesting subject. Mathematics is an interesting subject. ___ A: English and Mathematics are interesting subjects.. Join with 'and'; the verb becomes plural 'are'.
chunks.source: Join with 'and'; the verb becomes plural 'are'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using …but…: Sarah has a swollen eye. She comes to school. ___ A: Sarah has a swollen eye, but she comes to school.. 'But' joins contrasting ideas.
chunks.source: 'But' joins contrasting ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite beginning with “Although”: Kelly worked hard. Kelly failed the exams. ___ A: Although Kelly worked hard, she failed the exams.. 'Although' shows a surprising result.
chunks.source: 'Although' shows a surprising result.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using …in order to…: She wakes up early. She reaches school in time. ___ A: She wakes up early in order to reach school in time.. 'In order to' shows purpose.
chunks.source: 'In order to' shows purpose.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using …who…: Here is the doctor. He treated my baby sister. ___ A: Here is the doctor who treated my baby sister.. 'Who' joins sentences about people.
chunks.source: 'Who' joins sentences about people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using …whose…: Here comes the man. His son broke the glass window. ___ A: Here comes the man whose son broke the glass window.. 'Whose' shows belonging.
chunks.source: 'Whose' shows belonging.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange the sentences to make a meaningful story: (a) They apologized to the teacher that they were very sorry. (b) The class teacher sent for them at once. (c) Two naughty boys fought yesterday. (d) He reported them to their class teacher, Mr. Magezi. (e) A prefect saw them from a distance. A: Two naughty boys fought yesterday., A prefect saw them from a distance., He reported them to their class teacher, Mr. Magezi., The class teacher sent for them at once., They apologized to the teacher that they were very sorry.. First the fight, then the prefect saw, reported, teacher called, apology.
chunks.source: First the fight, then the prefect saw, reported, teacher called, apology.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange the sentences to make a meaningful story: (a) I returned home happily and kept them in my school bag. (b) I thanked her and quickly went to the supermarket to buy all my requirements. (c) She looked at it carefully and gave me twenty thousand shillings. (d) I wrote down my shopping list and gave it to my mother. (e) It was my shopping day yesterday. A: It was my shopping day yesterday., I wrote down my shopping list and gave it to my mother., She looked at it carefully and gave me twenty thousand shillings., I thanked her and quickly went to the supermarket to buy all my requirements., I returned home happily and kept them in my school bag.. First the shopping day, then the list, the money, the shopping, going home.
chunks.source: First the shopping day, then the list, the money, the shopping, going home.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box (always, language, greet, supposed, watch, care, roles, listen, responsibility, children): Good ___ are like gold. A: children. Good children are like gold.
chunks.source: Good children are like gold.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: When a child behaves well and shows ___, even the elder people will trust them. A: responsibility. Behaving well shows responsibility.
chunks.source: Behaving well shows responsibility.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: They have to ___ to their parents’ instructions and obey them by heart. A: listen. Listen to instructions.
chunks.source: Listen to instructions.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: They should also carry out their ___ in time. A: roles. Carry out their duties/roles.
chunks.source: Carry out their duties/roles.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: If your parent tells you to take ___ of the baby, ensure the baby is fed and bathed. A: care. Take care of the baby.
chunks.source: Take care of the baby.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: Wait for the baby to sleep but ___ the baby because it may wake up. A: watch. Watch the baby.
chunks.source: Watch the baby.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: If you are ___ to cook, do it before you go to play. A: supposed. If you are supposed to cook.
chunks.source: If you are supposed to cook.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: When visitors come home, ___ them and find out how you can help them. A: greet. Greet the visitors.
chunks.source: Greet the visitors.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: Use polite ___ and avoid talking rudely to them. A: language. Use polite language.
chunks.source: Use polite language.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: A good child will ___ be liked by everybody. A: always. Will always be liked.
chunks.source: Will always be liked.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct collective noun: The tourists were attacked by a ___ of lions. A: pride. A group of lions is called a pride.
chunks.source: A group of lions is called a pride.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct collective noun: We have two ___ of furniture in our house. A: suites. A group of furniture is called a suite.
chunks.source: A group of furniture is called a suite.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct collective noun: Mr. Mubiru has the biggest ___ of cattle in the whole village. A: herd. A group of cattle is called a herd.
chunks.source: A group of cattle is called a herd.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct collective noun: A ___ of sheep is quite expensive to look after. A: flock. A group of sheep is called a flock.
chunks.source: A group of sheep is called a flock.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: Suzan cooks food every day. ___ A: Food is cooked by Suzan every day.. Present simple passive: is/are + past participle.
chunks.source: Present simple passive: is/are + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: The children break the windows every day. ___ A: The windows are broken by the children every day.. Plural subject takes 'are' + past participle.
chunks.source: Plural subject takes 'are' + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: The goat ate all the grass. ___ A: All the grass was eaten by the goat.. Past simple passive: was/were + past participle.
chunks.source: Past simple passive: was/were + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: He drove the bus. ___ A: The bus was driven by him.. Past simple passive: was + past participle.
chunks.source: Past simple passive: was + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: Luke is carrying a jerry can. ___ A: A jerry can is being carried by Luke.. Present continuous passive: is/are + being + past participle.
chunks.source: Present continuous passive: is/are + being + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: We are playing netball. ___ A: Netball is being played by us.. Present continuous passive: is + being + past participle.
chunks.source: Present continuous passive: is + being + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: Betty has hidden your bag. ___ A: Your bag has been hidden by Betty.. Present perfect passive: has/have + been + past participle.
chunks.source: Present perfect passive: has/have + been + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: The babies have eaten the food. ___ A: The food has been eaten by the babies.. Present perfect passive: has + been + past participle.
chunks.source: Present perfect passive: has + been + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: She will draw a map. ___ A: A map will be drawn by her.. Future passive: will + be + past participle.
chunks.source: Future passive: will + be + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: We shall carry the books. ___ A: The books shall be carried by us.. Future passive: shall + be + past participle.
chunks.source: Future passive: shall + be + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: The teacher will be keeping the books. ___ A: The books will be being kept by the teacher.. Future continuous passive: will + be + being + past participle.
chunks.source: Future continuous passive: will + be + being + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: Poni was teaching English. ___ A: English was being taught by Poni.. Past continuous passive: was/were + being + past participle.
chunks.source: Past continuous passive: was/were + being + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: The dogs were eating the bones. ___ A: The bones were being eaten by the dogs.. Past continuous passive: were + being + past participle.
chunks.source: Past continuous passive: were + being + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: The children were playing basketball. ___ A: Basketball was being played by the children.. Past continuous passive: was + being + past participle.
chunks.source: Past continuous passive: was + being + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: My uncle sold some eggs. ___ A: Some eggs were sold by my uncle.. Past simple passive: were + past participle.
chunks.source: Past simple passive: were + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: We were preparing supper. ___ A: Supper was being prepared by us.. Past continuous passive: was + being + past participle.
chunks.source: Past continuous passive: was + being + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: He bought a new shirt. ___ A: A new shirt was bought by him.. Past simple passive: was + past participle.
chunks.source: Past simple passive: was + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from active to passive voice: Jane was peeling cassava. ___ A: Cassava was being peeled by Jane.. Past continuous passive: was + being + past participle.
chunks.source: Past continuous passive: was + being + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite beginning with “A very nice …”: Mr. Mukasa made a very nice chair. ___ A: A very nice chair was made by Mr. Mukasa.. Past simple passive: was + past participle.
chunks.source: Past simple passive: was + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite beginning with “A letter”: Nakato is writing a letter. ___ A: A letter is being written by Nakato.. Present continuous passive: is + being + past participle.
chunks.source: Present continuous passive: is + being + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: sch ___ A: school. 'sch' is short for 'school'.
chunks.source: 'sch' is short for 'school'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: i.e. ___ A: that is. 'i.e.' means 'that is'.
chunks.source: 'i.e.' means 'that is'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: e.g. ___ A: for example. 'e.g.' means 'for example'.
chunks.source: 'e.g.' means 'for example'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: rd. ___ A: road. 'rd.' is short for 'road'.
chunks.source: 'rd.' is short for 'road'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: co. ___ A: company. 'co.' is short for 'company'.
chunks.source: 'co.' is short for 'company'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: st. ___ A: saint. 'st.' is short for 'saint'.
chunks.source: 'st.' is short for 'saint'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Dr ___ A: Doctor. 'Dr' is short for 'Doctor'.
chunks.source: 'Dr' is short for 'Doctor'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: mt. ___ A: mount. 'mt.' is short for 'mount' (mountain).
chunks.source: 'mt.' is short for 'mount' (mountain).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Ltd ___ A: Limited. 'Ltd' is short for 'Limited'.
chunks.source: 'Ltd' is short for 'Limited'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: H.E. ___ A: His Excellency. 'H.E.' means 'His Excellency', used for presidents.
chunks.source: 'H.E.' means 'His Excellency', used for presidents.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the contraction in full: She can’t come today. ___ A: She cannot come today.. 'can't' is the short form of 'cannot'.
chunks.source: 'can't' is the short form of 'cannot'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the contraction in full: They won’t keep quiet. ___ A: They will not keep quiet.. 'won't' is the short form of 'will not'.
chunks.source: 'won't' is the short form of 'will not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the contraction in full: We shan’t do that work. ___ A: We shall not do that work.. 'shan't' is the short form of 'shall not'.
chunks.source: 'shan't' is the short form of 'shall not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the contraction in full: I’ll sing with my sister. ___ A: I will sing with my sister.. 'll' is the short form of 'will'.
chunks.source: 'll' is the short form of 'will'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the contraction in full: He isn’t happy. ___ A: He is not happy.. 'isn't' is the short form of 'is not'.
chunks.source: 'isn't' is the short form of 'is not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the contraction in full: The children aren’t well behaved. ___ A: The children are not well behaved.. 'aren't' is the short form of 'are not'.
chunks.source: 'aren't' is the short form of 'are not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: e.t.c. ___ A: etcetera. 'e.t.c.' means 'and so on'.
chunks.source: 'e.t.c.' means 'and so on'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: R.S.V.P. ___ A: Reply if you please. R.S.V.P. asks guests to reply to an invitation.
chunks.source: R.S.V.P. asks guests to reply to an invitation.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Via ___ A: by way of. 'Via' means going through a place.
chunks.source: 'Via' means going through a place.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: p.m. ___ A: afternoon. 'p.m.' means after noon.
chunks.source: 'p.m.' means after noon.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: a.m. ___ A: morning. 'a.m.' means before noon.
chunks.source: 'a.m.' means before noon.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Ave. ___ A: Avenue. 'Ave.' is short for 'Avenue'.
chunks.source: 'Ave.' is short for 'Avenue'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Rd. ___ A: Road. 'Rd.' is short for 'Road'.
chunks.source: 'Rd.' is short for 'Road'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Co. ___ A: Company. 'Co.' is short for 'Company'.
chunks.source: 'Co.' is short for 'Company'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Rev. ___ A: Reverend. 'Rev.' is a title for a pastor.
chunks.source: 'Rev.' is a title for a pastor.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: C/o ___ A: care of. 'C/o' means 'care of' on letters.
chunks.source: 'C/o' means 'care of' on letters.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: UNEB ___ A: Uganda National Examinations Board. UNEB sets national examinations in Uganda.
chunks.source: UNEB sets national examinations in Uganda.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: UPE ___ A: Universal Primary Education. UPE is free primary education in Uganda.
chunks.source: UPE is free primary education in Uganda.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: P.L.E. ___ A: Primary Leaving Examination. PLE is the final primary examination.
chunks.source: PLE is the final primary examination.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: P.S.V. ___ A: Public Service Vehicle. PSV carries passengers for payment.
chunks.source: PSV carries passengers for payment.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Can’t ___ A: cannot. 'Can't' is the short form of 'cannot'.
chunks.source: 'Can't' is the short form of 'cannot'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: won’t ___ A: will not. 'Won't' is the short form of 'will not'.
chunks.source: 'Won't' is the short form of 'will not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Shan’t ___ A: shall not. 'Shan't' is the short form of 'shall not'.
chunks.source: 'Shan't' is the short form of 'shall not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: I’ve ___ A: I have. 've' is the short form of 'have'.
chunks.source: 've' is the short form of 'have'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: Rev. ___ A: Reverend. 'Rev.' is a title for a pastor.
chunks.source: 'Rev.' is a title for a pastor.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: Feb. ___ A: February. 'Feb.' is the second month.
chunks.source: 'Feb.' is the second month.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: e.g. ___ A: for example. 'e.g.' means 'for example'.
chunks.source: 'e.g.' means 'for example'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write beginning with “Unless”: If I work hard, I will pass the examination. ___ A: Unless I work hard, I will not pass the examination.. 'Unless' means 'if not', so the second part becomes negative.
chunks.source: 'Unless' means 'if not', so the second part becomes negative.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write beginning with “Unless”: If Joan comes on Monday, Peter will be happy. ___ A: Unless Joan comes on Monday, Peter will not be happy.. 'Unless' means 'if not', so the result becomes negative.
chunks.source: 'Unless' means 'if not', so the result becomes negative.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write beginning with “Unless”: If we do not eat, we shall die. ___ A: Unless we eat, we shall die.. 'Unless we eat' already carries the negative idea.
chunks.source: 'Unless we eat' already carries the negative idea.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write beginning with “Unless”: If Katamba does not come, Peter will not pray. ___ A: Unless Katamba comes, Peter will not pray.. 'Unless Katamba comes' means 'if Katamba does not come'.
chunks.source: 'Unless Katamba comes' means 'if Katamba does not come'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write beginning with “Unless”: If the teacher does not beat me, I will not tell my mother. ___ A: Unless the teacher beats me, I will not tell my mother.. 'Unless the teacher beats me' means 'if the teacher does not beat me'.
chunks.source: 'Unless the teacher beats me' means 'if the teacher does not beat me'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: Direct “am” → Indirect ___ A: was. In indirect speech, present 'am' becomes past 'was'.
chunks.source: In indirect speech, present 'am' becomes past 'was'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: Direct ___ → Indirect “go” A: come. 'Come' in direct speech becomes 'go' in indirect speech.
chunks.source: 'Come' in direct speech becomes 'go' in indirect speech.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: Direct “today” → Indirect ___ A: that day. 'Today' becomes 'that day' in indirect speech.
chunks.source: 'Today' becomes 'that day' in indirect speech.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: Direct ___ → Indirect “then” A: now. 'Now' becomes 'then' in indirect speech.
chunks.source: 'Now' becomes 'then' in indirect speech.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: Direct “Yesterday” → Indirect ___ A: the day before. 'Yesterday' becomes 'the day before' in indirect speech.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' becomes 'the day before' in indirect speech.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from direct to indirect speech: Mary said, “I am eating now.” ___ A: Mary said that she was eating then.. Move one step back: am → was, now → then, I → she.
chunks.source: Move one step back: am → was, now → then, I → she.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from direct to indirect speech: “I love her so much”, Jack says. ___ A: Jack says that he loves her so much.. With present 'says', the tense stays the same; I → he.
chunks.source: With present 'says', the tense stays the same; I → he.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change from direct to indirect speech: “We have written the letter,” the teacher said. ___ A: The teacher said that they had written the letter.. Move one step back: have written → had written, we → they.
chunks.source: Move one step back: have written → had written, we → they.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the ordinal number: three ___ A: third. 'Three' → 'third' (3rd).
chunks.source: 'Three' → 'third' (3rd).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the ordinal number: four ___ A: fourth. 'Four' → 'fourth' (4th).
chunks.source: 'Four' → 'fourth' (4th).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the ordinal number: nine ___ A: ninth. 'Nine' → 'ninth' (9th); drop the e.
chunks.source: 'Nine' → 'ninth' (9th); drop the e.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the ordinal number: twelve ___ A: twelfth. 'Twelve' → 'twelfth' (12th); ve becomes f.
chunks.source: 'Twelve' → 'twelfth' (12th); ve becomes f.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the ordinal number: forty ___ A: fortieth. 'Forty' → 'fortieth' (40th); y becomes ie.
chunks.source: 'Forty' → 'fortieth' (40th); y becomes ie.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the cardinal number: fortieth ___ A: forty. 'Fortieth' → 'forty' (40).
chunks.source: 'Fortieth' → 'forty' (40).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the cardinal number: thirtieth ___ A: thirty. 'Thirtieth' → 'thirty' (30).
chunks.source: 'Thirtieth' → 'thirty' (30).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: She ___ late yesterday. (come) A: came. 'Come' is irregular: come → came → come.
chunks.source: 'Come' is irregular: come → came → come.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Suzan ___ well last weekend. (write) A: wrote. 'Write' is irregular: write → wrote → written.
chunks.source: 'Write' is irregular: write → wrote → written.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: I used abusive language but the teacher ___ me. (forgive) A: forgave. 'Forgive' is irregular: forgive → forgave → forgiven.
chunks.source: 'Forgive' is irregular: forgive → forgave → forgiven.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: We shall ___ them tomorrow. (see) A: see. Future simple: shall/will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: shall/will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: It will ___ that bone. (break) A: break. Future simple: will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: Joan ___ us next Sunday. (visit) A: will visit. Future simple: will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: Mother ___ care of our uncle’s wife. (take) A: will take. Future simple: will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: I ___ my homework after supper. (do) A: shall do. Use 'shall' with I and we.
chunks.source: Use 'shall' with I and we.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: The teachers ___ harder next term. (work) A: will work. Future simple: will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: We ___ the village meeting. (attend) A: shall attend. Use 'shall' with I and we.
chunks.source: Use 'shall' with I and we.

chunks.subject: English
