chunks.text: Q: What was Sam doing when his mother called him? ___ A: He was completing his work. Sam was completing his work when his mother called.
chunks.source: Sam was completing his work when his mother called.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What was mother peeling when she called Sam? ___ A: Potatoes. She was peeling potatoes when she called Sam.
chunks.source: She was peeling potatoes when she called Sam.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What was Sam's sister doing while Sam was completing his work? ___ A: She was mopping. His sister was mopping while mother was peeling potatoes.
chunks.source: His sister was mopping while mother was peeling potatoes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where was Judith going when she heard Sam's mother calling him? ___ A: To the market. Judith was going to the market.
chunks.source: Judith was going to the market.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What was Judith going to buy? ___ A: A kilogram of meat. She was going to buy a kilogram of meat.
chunks.source: She was going to buy a kilogram of meat.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who were holding the dialogue? A: Judith and Sam. The dialogue is between Judith and Sam.
chunks.source: The dialogue is between Judith and Sam.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Sam was riding a bicycle when his mother called him. A: False. Sam was completing his work, not riding a bicycle.
chunks.source: Sam was completing his work, not riding a bicycle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who was serving food? ___ A: Nobody. Nobody was serving food; mother was peeling potatoes.
chunks.source: Nobody was serving food; mother was peeling potatoes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: When was Sam completing his work? ___ A: Last evening. It was last evening when his mother called.
chunks.source: It was last evening when his mother called.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why was Judith going to the market? ___ A: To buy a kilogram of meat. She was going to buy a kilogram of meat.
chunks.source: She was going to buy a kilogram of meat.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the notice about? ___ A: A football match. The notice is about a football match.
chunks.source: The notice is about a football match.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which schools are participating? ___ A: Kitebi and Mother Care. Kitebi Vs Mother Care are playing.
chunks.source: Kitebi Vs Mother Care are playing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: When will the match take place? ___ A: 29th October, 2013. The match is on 29th October, 2013.
chunks.source: The match is on 29th October, 2013.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where will the match take place? ___ A: Wankulukuku playground. The venue is Wankulukuku playground.
chunks.source: The venue is Wankulukuku playground.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: At what time will the match start? ___ A: 2:00 pm. The time is 2:00 pm - 5:00 pm.
chunks.source: The time is 2:00 pm - 5:00 pm.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: At what time will the match end? ___ A: 5:00 pm. The time is 2:00 pm - 5:00 pm.
chunks.source: The time is 2:00 pm - 5:00 pm.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How much will Nalubwama and her mother pay to watch the match? ___ A: 10000 shillings. Two adults at 5000 shillings each pay 10000 shillings.
chunks.source: Two adults at 5000 shillings each pay 10000 shillings.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How much will children pay to watch the match? A: Free. Children enter free.
chunks.source: Children enter free.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who was invited? ___ A: Everyone. The notice says 'Come one, come all'.
chunks.source: The notice says 'Come one, come all'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who wrote the notice? ___ A: The games master of Kitebi Primary School. It was written by the games master, Kitebi Primary School.
chunks.source: It was written by the games master, Kitebi Primary School.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who organized the elections? ___ A: Ms. Nambi. The patron, Ms. Nambi, organized elections.
chunks.source: The patron, Ms. Nambi, organized elections.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How many people contested for the presidency? ___ A: Three. There were three candidates for President.
chunks.source: There were three candidates for President.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who wrote the story? ___ A: Kabazaire Daniel. The story is by Kabazaire Daniel.
chunks.source: The story is by Kabazaire Daniel.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: In which class is the writer? A: P.4N. The writer is in P.4N.
chunks.source: The writer is in P.4N.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do you think Kabazaire tried to rig the votes? ___ A: To make his candidate win. He wanted Pathot Degesh to win the presidency.
chunks.source: He wanted Pathot Degesh to win the presidency.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who saw Kabazaire rigging the votes? ___ A: Mr. Mbuye. Mr. Mbuye saw him and they beat him.
chunks.source: Mr. Mbuye saw him and they beat him.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who won the presidency? ___ A: Pathot Degesh. His president had gone through.
chunks.source: His president had gone through.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why did Kabazaire promise never to participate in politics? ___ A: Because he was beaten for rigging votes. They beat him terribly for rigging votes.
chunks.source: They beat him terribly for rigging votes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Suggest a suitable title for the story. ___ A: The school elections. The story is about school elections.
chunks.source: The story is about school elections.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: Andrea ___ with her friends when the brother called her. (play) A: was playing. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: We ___ our cassava garden while our father was picking coffee. (weed) A: were weeding. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: As I ___ through the bush, I saw a snake. (walk) A: was walking. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: Pauline ___ for her uncle when a taxi knocked her. (wait) A: was waiting. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: Mother ___ supper when the visitors arrived. (prepare) A: was preparing. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: Padhe and Pudhu ___ the garden all day long. (dig) A: were digging. Double the g: digging.
chunks.source: Double the g: digging.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: I fell down while I ___ to school. (run) A: was running. Double the n: running.
chunks.source: Double the n: running.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: The power went off while they ___ television. (watch) A: were watching. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write beginning with “As”: I was playing. I hurt myself. ___ A: As I was playing, I hurt myself.. 'As' joins the two actions; comma after the first part.
chunks.source: 'As' joins the two actions; comma after the first part.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write using …while…: We were working. She was playing. ___ A: We were working while she was playing.. 'While' joins two actions happening together.
chunks.source: 'While' joins two actions happening together.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write beginning with “While”: We were working. She was playing. ___ A: While we were working, she was playing.. Start with 'While' and add a comma.
chunks.source: Start with 'While' and add a comma.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write beginning with “While”: Eve was singing. Ruth was reading. ___ A: While Eve was singing, Ruth was reading.. Start with 'While' and add a comma.
chunks.source: Start with 'While' and add a comma.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite as one sentence using …while…: The boys were playing. The teacher entered the classroom. ___ A: The boys were playing while the teacher entered the classroom.. 'While' joins an ongoing action and a short one.
chunks.source: 'While' joins an ongoing action and a short one.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: The teacher expected ___ from all her pupils. (obey) A: obedience. 'Obey' becomes the noun 'obedience'.
chunks.source: 'Obey' becomes the noun 'obedience'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: Crowds watched the ___ of the queen from Entebbe. (arrive) A: arrival. 'Arrive' becomes the noun 'arrival'.
chunks.source: 'Arrive' becomes the noun 'arrival'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: Benja sent Peter an ___ to all his pupils. (invite) A: invitation. 'Invite' becomes the noun 'invitation'.
chunks.source: 'Invite' becomes the noun 'invitation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: “___ is power” is a well-known saying. (know) A: Knowledge. 'Know' becomes the noun 'knowledge'.
chunks.source: 'Know' becomes the noun 'knowledge'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: We watched the ___ of the plant with interest. (grow) A: growth. 'Grow' becomes the noun 'growth'.
chunks.source: 'Grow' becomes the noun 'growth'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: The children’s ___ at the theatre was excellent. (behave) A: behaviour. 'Behave' becomes the noun 'behaviour'.
chunks.source: 'Behave' becomes the noun 'behaviour'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: The ___ took place at St. Peter’s church. (marry) A: marriage. 'Marry' becomes the noun 'marriage'.
chunks.source: 'Marry' becomes the noun 'marriage'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: The boy wrote an excellent ___ about dogs. (compose) A: composition. 'Compose' becomes the noun 'composition'.
chunks.source: 'Compose' becomes the noun 'composition'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: ___ is the key to success. (educate) A: Education. 'Educate' becomes the noun 'Education'.
chunks.source: 'Educate' becomes the noun 'Education'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write the sentence with correct punctuation: this s my mummy’s car ___ A: This is my mummy's car.. Start with a capital letter and use an apostrophe in 's.
chunks.source: Start with a capital letter and use an apostrophe in 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write the sentence with correct punctuation: this s my mummy’s car Do you stay near the lake? A: False. Start with a capital letter and use an apostrophe in 's.
chunks.source: Start with a capital letter and use an apostrophe in 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write the sentence with correct punctuation: how easy this activity is ___ A: How easy this activity is!. Exclamations end with an exclamation mark.
chunks.source: Exclamations end with an exclamation mark.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write the sentence with correct punctuation: how easy this activity is Do you stay near the lake? A: False. Exclamations end with an exclamation mark.
chunks.source: Exclamations end with an exclamation mark.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write the sentence with correct punctuation: what is your teachers name ___ A: What is your teacher's name?. Use an apostrophe to show belonging.
chunks.source: Use an apostrophe to show belonging.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write the sentence with correct punctuation: what is your teachers name How easy this activity is! A: False. Use an apostrophe to show belonging.
chunks.source: Use an apostrophe to show belonging.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the masculine of: Bride ___ A: bridegroom. The masculine of 'bride' is 'bridegroom'.
chunks.source: The masculine of 'bride' is 'bridegroom'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the masculine of: Bride landlady A: False. The masculine of 'bride' is 'bridegroom'.
chunks.source: The masculine of 'bride' is 'bridegroom'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the feminine of: nephew ___ A: niece. The feminine of 'nephew' is 'niece'.
chunks.source: The feminine of 'nephew' is 'niece'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the feminine of: nephew abstract A: False. The feminine of 'nephew' is 'niece'.
chunks.source: The feminine of 'nephew' is 'niece'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the feminine of: landlord ___ A: landlady. The feminine of 'landlord' is 'landlady'.
chunks.source: The feminine of 'landlord' is 'landlady'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the feminine of: landlord bridegroom A: False. The feminine of 'landlord' is 'landlady'.
chunks.source: The feminine of 'landlord' is 'landlady'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the masculine of: Widow ___ A: widower. The masculine of 'widow' is 'widower'.
chunks.source: The masculine of 'widow' is 'widower'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the masculine of: Widow abstract A: False. The masculine of 'widow' is 'widower'.
chunks.source: The masculine of 'widow' is 'widower'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the feminine of: Prince ___ A: princess. The feminine of 'prince' is 'princess'.

chunks.source: 'Thirtieth' → 'thirty' (30).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: She wrote late yesterday. (come) A: False. 'Come' is irregular: come → came → come.
chunks.source: 'Come' is irregular: come → came → come.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Suzan wrote well last weekend. (write) A: True. 'Write' is irregular: write → wrote → written.
chunks.source: 'Write' is irregular: write → wrote → written.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: I used abusive language but the teacher came me. (forgive) A: False. 'Forgive' is irregular: forgive → forgave → forgiven.
chunks.source: 'Forgive' is irregular: forgive → forgave → forgiven.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: We shall ___ them tomorrow. (see) A: see. Future simple: shall/will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: shall/will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: We shall break them tomorrow. (see) A: False. Future simple: shall/will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: shall/will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: It will ___ that bone. (break) A: break. Future simple: will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: It will shall attend that bone. (break) A: False. Future simple: will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: Joan ___ us next Sunday. (visit) A: will visit. Future simple: will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: Joan shall do us next Sunday. (visit) A: False. Future simple: will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: Mother ___ care of our uncle’s wife. (take) A: will take. Future simple: will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: Mother will work care of our uncle’s wife. (take) A: False. Future simple: will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: I ___ my homework after supper. (do) A: shall do. Use 'shall' with I and we.
chunks.source: Use 'shall' with I and we.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: I see my homework after supper. (do) A: False. Use 'shall' with I and we.
chunks.source: Use 'shall' with I and we.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: The teachers ___ harder next term. (work) A: will work. Future simple: will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: The teachers will visit harder next term. (work) A: False. Future simple: will + base verb.
chunks.source: Future simple: will + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: We ___ the village meeting. (attend) A: shall attend. Use 'shall' with I and we.
chunks.source: Use 'shall' with I and we.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete in future simple tense: We will take the village meeting. (attend) A: False. Use 'shall' with I and we.
chunks.source: Use 'shall' with I and we.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: Andrea ___ with her friends when the brother called her. (play) A: was playing. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: Andrea We were working while she was playing. with her friends when the brother called her. (play) A: False. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: We ___ our cassava garden while our father was picking coffee. (weed) A: were weeding. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: We was preparing our cassava garden while our father was picking coffee. (weed) A: False. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: As I ___ through the bush, I saw a snake. (walk) A: was walking. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: As I were weeding through the bush, I saw a snake. (walk) A: False. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: Pauline ___ for her uncle when a taxi knocked her. (wait) A: was waiting. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: Pauline was playing for her uncle when a taxi knocked her. (wait) A: False. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: Mother ___ supper when the visitors arrived. (prepare) A: was preparing. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: Mother was waiting supper when the visitors arrived. (prepare) A: False. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: Padhe and Pudhu ___ the garden all day long. (dig) A: were digging. Double the g: digging.
chunks.source: Double the g: digging.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: Padhe and Pudhu While Eve was singing, Ruth was reading. the garden all day long. (dig) A: False. Double the g: digging.
chunks.source: Double the g: digging.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: I fell down while I ___ to school. (run) A: was running. Double the n: running.
chunks.source: Double the n: running.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: I fell down while I The boys were playing while the teacher entered the classroom. to school. (run) A: False. Double the n: running.
chunks.source: Double the n: running.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: The power went off while they ___ television. (watch) A: were watching. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change the verb to past continuous: The power went off while they As I was playing, I hurt myself. television. (watch) A: False. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: The teacher expected ___ from all her pupils. (obey) A: obedience. 'Obey' becomes the noun 'obedience'.
chunks.source: 'Obey' becomes the noun 'obedience'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: The teacher expected Knowledge from all her pupils. (obey) A: False. 'Obey' becomes the noun 'obedience'.
chunks.source: 'Obey' becomes the noun 'obedience'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: Crowds watched the ___ of the queen from Entebbe. (arrive) A: arrival. 'Arrive' becomes the noun 'arrival'.
chunks.source: 'Arrive' becomes the noun 'arrival'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: Crowds watched the invitation of the queen from Entebbe. (arrive) A: False. 'Arrive' becomes the noun 'arrival'.
chunks.source: 'Arrive' becomes the noun 'arrival'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: Benja sent Peter an ___ to all his pupils. (invite) A: invitation. 'Invite' becomes the noun 'invitation'.
chunks.source: 'Invite' becomes the noun 'invitation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: Benja sent Peter an growth to all his pupils. (invite) A: False. 'Invite' becomes the noun 'invitation'.
chunks.source: 'Invite' becomes the noun 'invitation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: “___ is power” is a well-known saying. (know) A: Knowledge. 'Know' becomes the noun 'knowledge'.
chunks.source: 'Know' becomes the noun 'knowledge'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: “arrival is power” is a well-known saying. (know) A: False. 'Know' becomes the noun 'knowledge'.
chunks.source: 'Know' becomes the noun 'knowledge'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: We watched the ___ of the plant with interest. (grow) A: growth. 'Grow' becomes the noun 'growth'.
chunks.source: 'Grow' becomes the noun 'growth'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: We watched the Education of the plant with interest. (grow) A: False. 'Grow' becomes the noun 'growth'.
chunks.source: 'Grow' becomes the noun 'growth'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: The children’s ___ at the theatre was excellent. (behave) A: behaviour. 'Behave' becomes the noun 'behaviour'.
chunks.source: 'Behave' becomes the noun 'behaviour'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: The children’s growth at the theatre was excellent. (behave) A: False. 'Behave' becomes the noun 'behaviour'.
chunks.source: 'Behave' becomes the noun 'behaviour'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: The ___ took place at St. Peter’s church. (marry) A: marriage. 'Marry' becomes the noun 'marriage'.
chunks.source: 'Marry' becomes the noun 'marriage'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: The behaviour took place at St. Peter’s church. (marry) A: False. 'Marry' becomes the noun 'marriage'.
chunks.source: 'Marry' becomes the noun 'marriage'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: The boy wrote an excellent ___ about dogs. (compose) A: composition. 'Compose' becomes the noun 'composition'.
chunks.source: 'Compose' becomes the noun 'composition'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the noun formed from the word in brackets: The boy wrote an excellent invitation about dogs. (compose) A: False. 'Compose' becomes the noun 'composition'.
chunks.source: 'Compose' becomes the noun 'composition'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: ___ is the key to success. (educate) A: Education. 'Educate' becomes the noun 'Education'.
chunks.source: 'Educate' becomes the noun 'Education'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: growth is the key to success. (educate) A: False. 'Educate' becomes the noun 'Education'.
chunks.source: 'Educate' becomes the noun 'Education'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the masculine of: Bride ___ A: bridegroom. The masculine of 'bride' is 'bridegroom'.
chunks.source: The masculine of 'bride' is 'bridegroom'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the feminine of: nephew ___ A: niece. The feminine of 'nephew' is 'niece'.
chunks.source: The feminine of 'nephew' is 'niece'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the feminine of: landlord ___ A: landlady. The feminine of 'landlord' is 'landlady'.
chunks.source: The feminine of 'landlord' is 'landlady'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the masculine of: Widow ___ A: widower. The masculine of 'widow' is 'widower'.
chunks.source: The masculine of 'widow' is 'widower'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the feminine of: Prince ___ A: princess. The feminine of 'prince' is 'princess'.
chunks.source: The feminine of 'prince' is 'princess'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the feminine of: ram ___ A: ewe. The feminine of 'ram' is 'ewe'.
chunks.source: The feminine of 'ram' is 'ewe'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the most suitable word: The ___ does not have any bread for sale today. A: baker. The baker sells bread.
chunks.source: The baker sells bread.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural of: tooth ___ A: teeth. 'Tooth' is irregular: tooth → teeth.
chunks.source: 'Tooth' is irregular: tooth → teeth.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural of: Passer-by ___ A: Passers-by. For compound words, make the main word plural: Passers-by.
chunks.source: For compound words, make the main word plural: Passers-by.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural of: calf ___ A: calves. Words ending in -f often change f to v and add -es.
chunks.source: Words ending in -f often change f to v and add -es.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural of: Valley ___ A: Valleys. After a vowel + y, just add -s.
chunks.source: After a vowel + y, just add -s.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural of: Chief ___ A: Chiefs. Most words ending in -f just add -s: chiefs.
chunks.source: Most words ending in -f just add -s: chiefs.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the plural of the word in brackets: I need two ___ of sugar for my tea. (teaspoonful) A: teaspoonfuls. Make the main word plural: teaspoonfuls.
chunks.source: Make the main word plural: teaspoonfuls.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the plural of the word in brackets: He bought two ___ from the market. (mouse-trap) A: mouse-traps. Make the main word plural: mouse-traps.
chunks.source: Make the main word plural: mouse-traps.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the plural of the word in brackets: How many ___ are in the shed? (sheep) A: sheep. 'Sheep' is the same in singular and plural.
chunks.source: 'Sheep' is the same in singular and plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the plural of the word in brackets: We usually collect five ___ of eggs from our poultry farm every day. (tray) A: trays. After a vowel + y, add -s: trays.
chunks.source: After a vowel + y, add -s: trays.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: How many ___ does Mr. Kakande have on his farm? (calf) A: calves. 'Calf' → 'calves': f becomes v + es.
chunks.source: 'Calf' → 'calves': f becomes v + es.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of the underlined word: He ate a mango for lunch. ___ A: mangoes. 'Mango' → 'mangoes': add -es after o.
chunks.source: 'Mango' → 'mangoes': add -es after o.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of the underlined word: There is a sheep in the field. ___ A: sheep. 'Sheep' is the same in singular and plural.
chunks.source: 'Sheep' is the same in singular and plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct degree of the word in brackets: Mirembe is the ___ girl in their family. (beautiful) A: most beautiful. Use the superlative with 'the' when comparing more than two.
chunks.source: Use the superlative with 'the' when comparing more than two.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct degree of the word in brackets: Masaka road is ___ than Jinja road. (wide) A: wider. Use the comparative with 'than' when comparing two things.
chunks.source: Use the comparative with 'than' when comparing two things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct degree of the word in brackets: She has the ___ handwriting in our class. (good) A: best. 'Good' is irregular: good → better → best.
chunks.source: 'Good' is irregular: good → better → best.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct degree of the word in brackets: John is ___ than his brother Ronald. (bright) A: brighter. Comparing two people with 'than' needs the comparative.
chunks.source: Comparing two people with 'than' needs the comparative.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct degree of the word in brackets: Please add me ___ tea. (much) A: more. 'Much' is irregular: much → more → most.
chunks.source: 'Much' is irregular: much → more → most.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct degree of the word in brackets: A python is ___ than a lizard. (dangerous) A: more dangerous. Long adjectives use 'more' for the comparative.
chunks.source: Long adjectives use 'more' for the comparative.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join using …than…: Saul is clever. Samuel is not clever. ___ A: Saul is cleverer than Samuel.. 'Than' compares two people; use the comparative form.
chunks.source: 'Than' compares two people; use the comparative form.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: Katumba is ___ than his brother Saleh. (clever) A: cleverer. Comparing two people with 'than' needs the comparative.
chunks.source: Comparing two people with 'than' needs the comparative.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: Anita is the ___ girl in Primary Four. (smart) A: smartest. Use the superlative with 'the'.
chunks.source: Use the superlative with 'the'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: The gardener was so ___ that he asked for some water to drink. (thirst) A: thirsty. 'Thirst' becomes the adjective 'thirsty'.
chunks.source: 'Thirst' becomes the adjective 'thirsty'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct pronoun: Amos did the work ___ . (he) A: himself. Use the reflexive pronoun when the doer and receiver are the same.
chunks.source: Use the reflexive pronoun when the doer and receiver are the same.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct pronoun: They always cross the road ___ . (them) A: themselves. 'They' takes the reflexive 'themselves'.
chunks.source: 'They' takes the reflexive 'themselves'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct pronoun: She goes to the well ___ . (she) A: herself. 'She' takes the reflexive 'herself'.
chunks.source: 'She' takes the reflexive 'herself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct pronoun: Those clothes are ___ . (me) A: mine. Use the possessive pronoun 'mine' after 'are'.
chunks.source: Use the possessive pronoun 'mine' after 'are'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct pronoun: We should attempt the questions ___ . (us) A: ourselves. 'We' takes the reflexive 'ourselves'.
chunks.source: 'We' takes the reflexive 'ourselves'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: The teacher beat our friends yesterday. ___ A: The teacher beat them yesterday.. 'Our friends' becomes 'them'.
chunks.source: 'Our friends' becomes 'them'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: She will not see Rinah, Jackie and I. ___ A: She will not see us.. 'Rinah, Jackie and I' becomes 'us'.
chunks.source: 'Rinah, Jackie and I' becomes 'us'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: John is stealing your snacks. ___ A: He is stealing your snacks.. 'John' becomes 'he'.
chunks.source: 'John' becomes 'he'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: Roritah is mad. ___ A: She is mad.. 'Roritah' becomes 'she'.
chunks.source: 'Roritah' becomes 'she'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: That cat ate the rat. ___ A: It ate the rat.. An animal becomes 'it'.
chunks.source: An animal becomes 'it'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: Ann, Lukia and I played well. ___ A: We played well.. 'Ann, Lukia and I' becomes 'we'.
chunks.source: 'Ann, Lukia and I' becomes 'we'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Replace the underlined words with a pronoun: They did the work alone. ___ A: They did the work themselves.. 'Alone' becomes the reflexive 'themselves'.
chunks.source: 'Alone' becomes the reflexive 'themselves'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: She painted this beautiful picture ___ . (self) A: herself. 'She' takes the reflexive 'herself'.
chunks.source: 'She' takes the reflexive 'herself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using …belongs…: That ruler is mine. ___ A: That ruler belongs to me.. 'Belongs to' shows ownership.
chunks.source: 'Belongs to' shows ownership.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: The thief jumped ___ the fence. A: over. Jump across something: jump over.
chunks.source: Jump across something: jump over.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: The cow is sleeping ___ the tree shade. A: under. Under the shade of the tree.
chunks.source: Under the shade of the tree.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: Do not lean ___ that wall, it’s very weak. A: against. Lean against a wall.
chunks.source: Lean against a wall.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: Aren’t you ashamed ___ your conduct? A: of. 'Ashamed of' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'Ashamed of' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: Bob is sure ___ his success in future. A: of. 'Sure of' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'Sure of' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: The hunter aimed ___ the animal. A: at. Aim at a target.
chunks.source: Aim at a target.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: Kamujje was accused ___ stealing the old man’s fruits. A: of. 'Accused of' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'Accused of' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: William prefers a sweater ___ a coat. A: to. 'Prefer X to Y' uses 'to'.
chunks.source: 'Prefer X to Y' uses 'to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: He is jealous ___ his brother’s success. A: of. 'Jealous of' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'Jealous of' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the correct preposition: May I introduce you ___ Mrs. Mugabi? A: to. 'Introduce to' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'Introduce to' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the most suitable word: The twins shared the apples ___ themselves. A: among. Share with more than two: 'among'.
chunks.source: Share with more than two: 'among'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the most suitable word: It is not a good habit to quarrel ___ neighbours. A: with. Quarrel with someone.
chunks.source: Quarrel with someone.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Cheap ___ A: cheaply. Add -ly to form the adverb.
chunks.source: Add -ly to form the adverb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Poor ___ A: poorly. Add -ly to form the adverb.
chunks.source: Add -ly to form the adverb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Quiet ___ A: quietly. Add -ly; 'quiet' keeps its spelling.
chunks.source: Add -ly; 'quiet' keeps its spelling.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Patient ___ A: patiently. Add -ly to form the adverb.
chunks.source: Add -ly to form the adverb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Beautiful ___ A: beautifully. Add -ly to form the adverb.
chunks.source: Add -ly to form the adverb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Careful ___ A: carefully. Add -ly to form the adverb.
chunks.source: Add -ly to form the adverb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: lazy ___ A: lazily. Change y to i, then add -ly.
chunks.source: Change y to i, then add -ly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: easy ___ A: easily. Change y to i, then add -ly.
chunks.source: Change y to i, then add -ly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: noisy ___ A: noisily. Change y to i, then add -ly.
chunks.source: Change y to i, then add -ly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: busy ___ A: busily. Change y to i, then add -ly.
chunks.source: Change y to i, then add -ly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: day ___ A: daily. 'Day' becomes 'daily'.
chunks.source: 'Day' becomes 'daily'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: The thief was ___ beaten. (bad) A: badly. Use the adverb 'badly' to describe how he was beaten.
chunks.source: Use the adverb 'badly' to describe how he was beaten.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: I think we can ___ do this work. (easy) A: easily. Use the adverb 'easily' to describe how we can do it.
chunks.source: Use the adverb 'easily' to describe how we can do it.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: They ___ asked for permission from the teacher. (humble) A: humbly. Use the adverb 'humbly'.
chunks.source: Use the adverb 'humbly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Wabwa died ___ . (sudden) A: suddenly. Add -ly: suddenly.
chunks.source: Add -ly: suddenly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Daddy ___ answered him back. (angry) A: angrily. Add -ily: angrily.
chunks.source: Add -ily: angrily.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: It was ___ marked. (clear) A: clearly. Add -ly: clearly.
chunks.source: Add -ly: clearly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: That man is ___ sick. (mental) A: mentally. Add -ly: mentally.
chunks.source: Add -ly: mentally.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Suzan ___ dressed for the ceremony. (decent) A: decently. Add -ly: decently.
chunks.source: Add -ly: decently.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: They took their books to the teacher ___. (immediate) A: immediately. 'Immediate' becomes 'immediately'.
chunks.source: 'Immediate' becomes 'immediately'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Kind ___ A: kindly. Add -ly to form the adverb.
chunks.source: Add -ly to form the adverb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Usual ___ A: usually. Add -ly: usually.
chunks.source: Add -ly: usually.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: Rude ___ A: rudely. Add -ly: rudely.
chunks.source: Add -ly: rudely.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: hurry ___ A: hurriedly. Change y to i, add -ly: hurriedly.
chunks.source: Change y to i, add -ly: hurriedly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form an adverb from: merry ___ A: merrily. Change y to i, add -ly: merrily.
chunks.source: Change y to i, add -ly: merrily.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with a suitable adverb: The cheetah jumped over the kob ___. (swift) A: swiftly. Add -ly: swiftly.
chunks.source: Add -ly: swiftly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with a suitable adverb: The doctor was called ___ for the patient in a critical condition. (immediate) A: immediately. 'Immediate' becomes 'immediately'.
chunks.source: 'Immediate' becomes 'immediately'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with a suitable adverb: The workers got their salary ___. (month) A: monthly. 'Month' becomes 'monthly'.
chunks.source: 'Month' becomes 'monthly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with a suitable adverb: He speaks English ___. (fluent) A: fluently. Add -ly: fluently.
chunks.source: Add -ly: fluently.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with a suitable adverb: She sings ___. (sweet) A: sweetly. Add -ly: sweetly.
chunks.source: Add -ly: sweetly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: She crossed the road ___ and got an accident. (care) A: carelessly. Use the adverb 'carelessly' to describe how she crossed.
chunks.source: Use the adverb 'carelessly' to describe how she crossed.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Mummy has ___ some eggs. (fry) A: fried. Present perfect: has + past participle. 'Fry' → 'fried'.
chunks.source: Present perfect: has + past participle. 'Fry' → 'fried'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: The bees ___ my brother yesterday. (sting) A: stung. 'Sting' is irregular: sting → stung → stung.
chunks.source: 'Sting' is irregular: sting → stung → stung.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Monica has ___ the compound very well. (sweep) A: swept. 'Sweep' is irregular: sweep → swept → swept.
chunks.source: 'Sweep' is irregular: sweep → swept → swept.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: The boy ___ down on the mat. (lie) A: lay. 'Lie' (rest) is irregular: lie → lay → lain.
chunks.source: 'Lie' (rest) is irregular: lie → lay → lain.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Our time keeper has ___ the bell. (ring) A: rung. 'Ring' is irregular: ring → rang → rung.
chunks.source: 'Ring' is irregular: ring → rang → rung.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Who has ___ my book on the floor? (put) A: put. 'Put' is the same in all forms.
chunks.source: 'Put' is the same in all forms.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Her baby has been ___ by hot water. (burn) A: burnt. 'Burn' → 'burnt' (or 'burned').
chunks.source: 'Burn' → 'burnt' (or 'burned').

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: They have ___ nicely. (sing) A: sung. 'Sing' is irregular: sing → sang → sung.
chunks.source: 'Sing' is irregular: sing → sang → sung.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: David never ___ for permission before going outside. (ask) A: asked. Regular verb: add -ed.
chunks.source: Regular verb: add -ed.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Paul has ___ my soda. (drink) A: drunk. 'Drink' is irregular: drink → drank → drunk.
chunks.source: 'Drink' is irregular: drink → drank → drunk.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: The pupils have ___ English. (speak) A: spoken. 'Speak' is irregular: speak → spoke → spoken.
chunks.source: 'Speak' is irregular: speak → spoke → spoken.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Amina has ___ a car. (drive) A: driven. 'Drive' is irregular: drive → drove → driven.
chunks.source: 'Drive' is irregular: drive → drove → driven.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: She has ___ well. (write) A: written. 'Write' is irregular: write → wrote → written.
chunks.source: 'Write' is irregular: write → wrote → written.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: The school choir has ___ a nice song at the assembly. (sing) A: sung. Present perfect: has + past participle. 'Sing' → 'sung'.
chunks.source: Present perfect: has + past participle. 'Sing' → 'sung'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: We are ___ now. (plan) A: planning. Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing. Double the n in 'plan'.
chunks.source: Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing. Double the n in 'plan'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: Mutebi is ___ his bicycle now. (ride) A: riding. Present continuous: is + verb-ing. Drop the e in 'ride'.
chunks.source: Present continuous: is + verb-ing. Drop the e in 'ride'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: I am ___ now. (eat) A: eating. Present continuous: am + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Present continuous: am + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the correct form of the word in brackets: They are ___ now. (revise) A: revising. Present continuous: are + verb-ing. Drop the e.
chunks.source: Present continuous: are + verb-ing. Drop the e.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the word in brackets correctly: The baby is ___ with a doll. (play) A: playing. Present continuous: is + verb-ing.
chunks.source: Present continuous: is + verb-ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: The baby cries every night, ___? A: doesn't it. Present simple positive takes negative tag: doesn't it.
chunks.source: Present simple positive takes negative tag: doesn't it.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: He wrote well, ___? A: didn't he. Past simple positive takes negative tag: didn't he.
chunks.source: Past simple positive takes negative tag: didn't he.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: They do not write well, ___? A: do they. Negative statement takes positive tag: do they.
chunks.source: Negative statement takes positive tag: do they.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: We are learning, ___? A: aren't we. 'Are' positive takes negative tag: aren't we.
chunks.source: 'Are' positive takes negative tag: aren't we.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: I am happy, ___? A: aren't I. 'I am' takes the special tag 'aren't I'.
chunks.source: 'I am' takes the special tag 'aren't I'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: I am not sad, ___? A: am I. 'I am not' takes the positive tag 'am I'.
chunks.source: 'I am not' takes the positive tag 'am I'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: The dog is barking, ___? A: isn't it. Positive statement takes negative tag: isn't it.
chunks.source: Positive statement takes negative tag: isn't it.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: The girl was sick, ___? A: wasn't she. Past 'was' positive takes negative tag: wasn't she.
chunks.source: Past 'was' positive takes negative tag: wasn't she.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: They were not around, ___? A: were they. Negative statement takes positive tag: were they.
chunks.source: Negative statement takes positive tag: were they.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: She was not beaten, ___? A: was she. Negative statement takes positive tag: was she.
chunks.source: Negative statement takes positive tag: was she.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply a suitable question tag: We write our work neatly, ___? A: don't we. Present simple positive takes negative tag.
chunks.source: Present simple positive takes negative tag.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write using …prefer…to…: Janet likes reading more than writing. ___ A: Janet prefers reading to writing.. 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.
chunks.source: 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write using …prefer…to…: She likes singing more than dancing. ___ A: She prefers singing to dancing.. 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.
chunks.source: 'Prefer X to Y' means liking X more than Y.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using …prefers…: She loves swimming more than skipping. ___ A: She prefers swimming to skipping.. 'Prefers X to Y' means liking X more.
chunks.source: 'Prefers X to Y' means liking X more.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box (always, language, greet, supposed, watch, care, roles, listen, responsibility, children): Good ___ are like gold. A: children. Good children are like gold.
chunks.source: Good children are like gold.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: When a child behaves well and shows ___, even the elder people will trust them. A: responsibility. Behaving well shows responsibility.
chunks.source: Behaving well shows responsibility.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: They have to ___ to their parents’ instructions and obey them by heart. A: listen. Listen to instructions.
chunks.source: Listen to instructions.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: They should also carry out their ___ in time. A: roles. Carry out their duties/roles.
chunks.source: Carry out their duties/roles.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: If your parent tells you to take ___ of the baby, ensure the baby is fed and bathed. A: care. Take care of the baby.
chunks.source: Take care of the baby.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: Wait for the baby to sleep but ___ the baby because it may wake up. A: watch. Watch the baby.
chunks.source: Watch the baby.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: If you are ___ to cook, do it before you go to play. A: supposed. If you are supposed to cook.
chunks.source: If you are supposed to cook.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: When visitors come home, ___ them and find out how you can help them. A: greet. Greet the visitors.
chunks.source: Greet the visitors.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: Use polite ___ and avoid talking rudely to them. A: language. Use polite language.
chunks.source: Use polite language.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the letter with a word from the box: A good child will ___ be liked by everybody. A: always. Will always be liked.
chunks.source: Will always be liked.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: sch ___ A: school. 'sch' is short for 'school'.
chunks.source: 'sch' is short for 'school'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: i.e. ___ A: that is. 'i.e.' means 'that is'.
chunks.source: 'i.e.' means 'that is'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: e.g. ___ A: for example. 'e.g.' means 'for example'.
chunks.source: 'e.g.' means 'for example'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: rd. ___ A: road. 'rd.' is short for 'road'.
chunks.source: 'rd.' is short for 'road'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: co. ___ A: company. 'co.' is short for 'company'.
chunks.source: 'co.' is short for 'company'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: st. ___ A: saint. 'st.' is short for 'saint'.
chunks.source: 'st.' is short for 'saint'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Dr ___ A: Doctor. 'Dr' is short for 'Doctor'.
chunks.source: 'Dr' is short for 'Doctor'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: mt. ___ A: mount. 'mt.' is short for 'mount' (mountain).
chunks.source: 'mt.' is short for 'mount' (mountain).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Ltd ___ A: Limited. 'Ltd' is short for 'Limited'.
chunks.source: 'Ltd' is short for 'Limited'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: H.E. ___ A: His Excellency. 'H.E.' means 'His Excellency', used for presidents.
chunks.source: 'H.E.' means 'His Excellency', used for presidents.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the contraction in full: She can’t come today. ___ A: She cannot come today.. 'can't' is the short form of 'cannot'.
chunks.source: 'can't' is the short form of 'cannot'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the contraction in full: They won’t keep quiet. ___ A: They will not keep quiet.. 'won't' is the short form of 'will not'.
chunks.source: 'won't' is the short form of 'will not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the contraction in full: He isn’t happy. ___ A: He is not happy.. 'isn't' is the short form of 'is not'.
chunks.source: 'isn't' is the short form of 'is not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: e.t.c. ___ A: etcetera. 'e.t.c.' means 'and so on'.
chunks.source: 'e.t.c.' means 'and so on'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: R.S.V.P. ___ A: Reply if you please. R.S.V.P. asks guests to reply to an invitation.
chunks.source: R.S.V.P. asks guests to reply to an invitation.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Via ___ A: by way of. 'Via' means going through a place.
chunks.source: 'Via' means going through a place.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: p.m. ___ A: afternoon. 'p.m.' means after noon.
chunks.source: 'p.m.' means after noon.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: a.m. ___ A: morning. 'a.m.' means before noon.
chunks.source: 'a.m.' means before noon.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Ave. ___ A: Avenue. 'Ave.' is short for 'Avenue'.
chunks.source: 'Ave.' is short for 'Avenue'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Rd. ___ A: Road. 'Rd.' is short for 'Road'.
chunks.source: 'Rd.' is short for 'Road'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Co. ___ A: Company. 'Co.' is short for 'Company'.
chunks.source: 'Co.' is short for 'Company'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Rev. ___ A: Reverend. 'Rev.' is a title for a pastor.
chunks.source: 'Rev.' is a title for a pastor.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: C/o ___ A: care of. 'C/o' means 'care of' on letters.
chunks.source: 'C/o' means 'care of' on letters.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: UNEB ___ A: Uganda National Examinations Board. UNEB sets national examinations in Uganda.
chunks.source: UNEB sets national examinations in Uganda.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: UPE ___ A: Universal Primary Education. UPE is free primary education in Uganda.
chunks.source: UPE is free primary education in Uganda.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: P.L.E. ___ A: Primary Leaving Examination. PLE is the final primary examination.
chunks.source: PLE is the final primary examination.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: P.S.V. ___ A: Public Service Vehicle. PSV carries passengers for payment.
chunks.source: PSV carries passengers for payment.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: M = {the first four letters of the alphabet}. List all the members of set M. A: a, b, c, d. The first four letters of the alphabet are a, b, c and d.
chunks.source: The first four letters of the alphabet are a, b, c and d.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that X = {a, b, g} and Y = {t, a, b, l, e}. How many members make the union set? A: 6. The union is {a, b, g, t, l, e}, which has 6 members.
chunks.source: The union is {a, b, g, t, l, e}, which has 6 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set K = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}. How many members are in set K? A: 5. Counting the members 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 gives 5.
chunks.source: Counting the members 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 gives 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the sets below. (a) The picture shows cups in a set. A set of ___ cups. A: 5. There are 5 cups in the picture.
chunks.source: There are 5 cups in the picture.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the sets below. (b) The picture shows chairs in a set. A set of ___ chairs. A: 10. There are 10 chairs in the picture.
chunks.source: There are 10 chairs in the picture.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set K = {t, e, a} and L = {a, t, e}. Set K and L are ___ sets. A: equal. Both sets have exactly the same members, so they are equal sets.
chunks.source: Both sets have exactly the same members, so they are equal sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the Venn diagram below (P and R). (a) List the members of set P. A: g, o, a, t. Set P contains g, o, a and t.
chunks.source: Set P contains g, o, a and t.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the Venn diagram below (P and R). (b) Find P ∩ R. A: a, t. The letters in both P and R are a and t.
chunks.source: The letters in both P and R are a and t.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the Venn diagram below (P and R). (c) How many members are in P ∪ R? A: 5. P ∪ R = {g, o, a, t, e}, which has 5 members.
chunks.source: P ∪ R = {g, o, a, t, e}, which has 5 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: K = {the first five letters of the English alphabet}. List the members of set K. A: a, b, c, d, e. The first five letters are a, b, c, d and e.
chunks.source: The first five letters are a, b, c, d and e.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set M = {triangle, square, circle, school bag} and set G = {circle, school bag}, as shown in the pictures. Write the common members of set M and set G. A: circle, school bag. Circle and school bag appear in both sets.
chunks.source: Circle and school bag appear in both sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (i) G = {18, 19, 20, 26} and H = {26, 18, 20, 19}. Set G and H are ___ sets. A: equal. Both sets have exactly the same members, so they are equal sets.
chunks.source: Both sets have exactly the same members, so they are equal sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (ii) R = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} and P = {a, b, c, d, e}. P and R are ___ sets. A: equivalent. Both sets have 5 members but different members, so they are equivalent sets.
chunks.source: Both sets have 5 members but different members, so they are equivalent sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (b) Set N = {boys who have seven eyes each}. Set N = ? A: empty set. No boy has seven eyes, so the set has no members: it is an empty set.
chunks.source: No boy has seven eyes, so the set has no members: it is an empty set.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that K = {1, 2, 3} and L = {2, 1, 3}. Set K and L are ___ sets. A: equal. Both sets have the same members, so they are equal sets.
chunks.source: Both sets have the same members, so they are equal sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The Venn diagram shows set R with members 1, 2, 3 and 4. How many members has set R? A: 4. Counting the members gives 4.
chunks.source: Counting the members gives 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set R = {oval, triangle, square} and set S = {p, a, i, n}, as shown in the pictures. Set R and S are ___ sets. A: not equivalent. R has 3 members and S has 4 members, so they are not equivalent sets.
chunks.source: R has 3 members and S has 4 members, so they are not equivalent sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set X = {p, l, a, n, t} and Y = {c, l, a, i, m}. Find X ∩ Y. A: l, a. The letters in both sets are l and a.
chunks.source: The letters in both sets are l and a.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The Venn diagram shows A = {3, 4, 1, 2} and B = {1, 2, 5, 6}. Find A ∪ B. A: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Putting all different members together gives {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}.
chunks.source: Putting all different members together gives {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If set P = {a, b, c}, how many elements has set P? A: 3. P has 3 members.
chunks.source: P has 3 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set K = {0, 1, 2} and set L = {1, 2, 4}. (i) Find K ∩ L. A: 1, 2. 1 and 2 are in both sets.
chunks.source: 1 and 2 are in both sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set K = {0, 1, 2} and set L = {1, 2, 4}. (ii) Find K ∪ L. A: 0, 1, 2, 4. All different members together are {0, 1, 2, 4}.
chunks.source: All different members together are {0, 1, 2, 4}.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the set symbol '∩'. A: intersection. The symbol ∩ means intersection.
chunks.source: The symbol ∩ means intersection.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the set symbol '∪'. A: union. The symbol ∪ means union.
chunks.source: The symbol ∪ means union.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the set symbol '='. A: equal to. The symbol = means equal to.
chunks.source: The symbol = means equal to.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the set symbol '≠'. A: not equal to. The symbol ≠ means not equal to.
chunks.source: The symbol ≠ means not equal to.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that K = {1, 2, 3}, find the number of elements in set K. A: 3. K has 3 members.
chunks.source: K has 3 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If M = {ball, bench, bag} and N = {bag, bench, ball} as shown in the pictures, describe the relationship between set M and set N. A: They are equal sets. Both sets have exactly the same members, so they are equal sets.
chunks.source: Both sets have exactly the same members, so they are equal sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: H = {whole numbers between 10 and 18}. (a)(i) List all the members of set H. A: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. The whole numbers after 10 up to 18 are 11 to 17.
chunks.source: The whole numbers after 10 up to 18 are 11 to 17.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: G = {odd numbers between 10 and 20}. (a)(ii) List all the members of set G. A: 11, 13, 15, 17, 19. The odd numbers between 10 and 20 are 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19.
chunks.source: The odd numbers between 10 and 20 are 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.source: H − G = {12, 14, 16}, which has 3 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: R = {all months of the year with 30 days}. Find the members of set R. A: April, June, September, November. The months with 30 days are April, June, September and November.
chunks.source: The months with 30 days are April, June, September and November.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that set A = {a, b, c, d}, find n(A). A: 4. Set A has 4 members, so n(A) = 4.
chunks.source: Set A has 4 members, so n(A) = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that R = {e, x, a, m}, find n(R). A: 4. R has 4 members, so n(R) = 4.
chunks.source: R has 4 members, so n(R) = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that W = {d, o, g} and X = {d, o, n, k, e, y}. (b) Find W ∩ X. A: d, o. The letters in both sets are d and o.
chunks.source: The letters in both sets are d and o.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that W = {d, o, g} and X = {d, o, n, k, e, y}. (c) How many members are in W ∪ X? A: 7. W ∪ X = {d, o, g, n, k, e, y}, which has 7 members.
chunks.source: W ∪ X = {d, o, g, n, k, e, y}, which has 7 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the missing counting numbers: ___, 1994, 1995, 1996, 1997, 1998, 1999, ___. A: 1993, 2000. The numbers count up by one, so 1993 comes before 1994 and 2000 comes after 1999.
chunks.source: The numbers count up by one, so 1993 comes before 1994 and 2000 comes after 1999.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 24 in Roman numerals. A: XXIV. 20 is XX and 4 is IV, so 24 is XXIV.
chunks.source: 20 is XX and 4 is IV, so 24 is XXIV.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A sign post shows 256 kilometres to Mbale. (a) Write the distance to Mbale in words. A: Two hundred fifty-six kilometres. 256 is read as two hundred fifty-six.
chunks.source: 256 is read as two hundred fifty-six.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A sign post shows 256 kilometres to Mbale. (b) Expand 256 using place values. A: 200 + 50 + 6. 256 = 200 + 50 + 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A sign post shows 256 kilometres to Mbale. (c) Round off 256 to the nearest hundred. A: 300. 256 is closer to 300 than to 200.
chunks.source: 256 is closer to 300 than to 200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the Roman numeral for 10. A: X. In Roman numerals, X means 10.
chunks.source: In Roman numerals, X means 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 'four thousand two hundred' in figures. A: 4200. Four thousand two hundred is 4200.
chunks.source: Four thousand two hundred is 4200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the digits 4, 9, 1. (a)(i) Form the smallest three-digit number. A: 149. Putting the smallest digit first gives 149.
chunks.source: Putting the smallest digit first gives 149.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the digits 4, 9, 1. (a)(ii) Form the biggest three-digit number. A: 941. Putting the biggest digit first gives 941.
chunks.source: Putting the biggest digit first gives 941.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the digits 4, 9, 1. (b) Write the smallest three-digit number, 149, in words. A: One hundred forty-nine. 149 is read as one hundred forty-nine.
chunks.source: 149 is read as one hundred forty-nine.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the sum of the values of 3 and 2 in 4352? A: 350. The value of 3 is 300 and the value of 2 is 50; 300 + 50 = 350.
chunks.source: The value of 3 is 300 and the value of 2 is 50; 300 + 50 = 350.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Joanita has 15 pencils. Express the number of pencils she has in Roman numerals. A: XV. 10 is X and 5 is V, so 15 is XV.
chunks.source: 10 is X and 5 is V, so 15 is XV.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write down the expanded number: (2 × 100) + (9 × 10) + (3 × 1). A: 293. 200 + 90 + 3 = 293.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (a) What number is shown on the abacus below? (Hundreds, Tens, Ones) A: 243. 2 hundreds, 4 tens and 3 ones make 243.
chunks.source: 2 hundreds, 4 tens and 3 ones make 243.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (b) Write the number 243 shown on the abacus in words. A: Two hundred forty-three. 243 is read as two hundred forty-three.
chunks.source: 243 is read as two hundred forty-three.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (c) Multiply the value of 2 by the value of 3 in the number 243 shown on the abacus. A: 600. The value of 2 is 200 and the value of 3 is 3; 200 × 3 = 600.
chunks.source: The value of 2 is 200 and the value of 3 is 3; 200 × 3 = 600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the single number that has been expanded to get 5000 + 800 + 7. A: 5807. 5000 + 800 + 7 = 5807.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Kasirye eats 24 apples per day. Write the number of apples in Roman numerals. A: XXIV. 24 is XXIV in Roman numerals.
chunks.source: 24 is XXIV in Roman numerals.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the abacus below (Thousands, Hundreds, Tens, Ones). What number is shown on the abacus? A: 2403. 2 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 3 ones make 2403.
chunks.source: 2 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 3 ones make 2403.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 160 in words. A: One hundred sixty. 160 is read as one hundred sixty.
chunks.source: 160 is read as one hundred sixty.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What number is shown on the abacus? (Hundreds, Tens, Ones) A: 521. 5 hundreds, 2 tens and 1 one make 521.
chunks.source: 5 hundreds, 2 tens and 1 one make 521.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the numerals 521 shown on the abacus above in words. A: Five hundred twenty-one. 521 is read as five hundred twenty-one.
chunks.source: 521 is read as five hundred twenty-one.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 20 in Roman numerals. A: XX. 10 is X, so 20 is XX.
chunks.source: 10 is X, so 20 is XX.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the place value of 2 in the number 624? A: tens. The 2 is in the tens place.
chunks.source: The 2 is in the tens place.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the place value of each digit in 243? A: 2: hundreds, 4: tens, 3: ones. In 243, 2 is hundreds, 4 is tens and 3 is ones.
chunks.source: In 243, 2 is hundreds, 4 is tens and 3 is ones.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the values of the digits in the number 48,359. A: 40000, 8000, 300, 50, 9. 4 is 40000, 8 is 8000, 3 is 300, 5 is 50 and 9 is 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Expand 390 in value form. A: 300 + 90. 390 = 300 + 90.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the number expanded below: 3 hundreds + 7 tens + 5 ones. A: 375. 300 + 70 + 5 = 375.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the digits 5, 3, 9. (a) Form the largest 3-digit number using the digits above. A: 953. Putting the biggest digit first gives 953.
chunks.source: Putting the biggest digit first gives 953.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the digits 5, 3, 9. (b) Form the smallest 3-digit number using the digits above. A: 359. Putting the smallest digit first gives 359.
chunks.source: Putting the smallest digit first gives 359.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the digits 5, 3, 9. (c) Find the sum of the smallest and the largest number formed above. A: 1312. 359 + 953 = 1312.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Expand 384 using values. A: 300 + 80 + 4. 384 = 300 + 80 + 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the value of 2 in 9246. A: 200. The 2 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 200.
chunks.source: The 2 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What number has been expanded to give (6 x 1000) + (8 x 100) + (4 x 10) + (9 x 1)? A: 6849. 6000 + 800 + 40 + 9 = 6849.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the number 6849 in words. A: Six thousand eight hundred forty-nine. 6849 is read as six thousand eight hundred forty-nine.
chunks.source: 6849 is read as six thousand eight hundred forty-nine.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the digits 5, 2 and 4. (a) Form the biggest numeral using the above digits. A: 542. Putting the biggest digit first gives 542.
chunks.source: Putting the biggest digit first gives 542.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the digits 5, 2 and 4. (b) Form the smallest numeral. A: 245. Putting the smallest digit first gives 245.
chunks.source: Putting the smallest digit first gives 245.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the digits 5, 2 and 4. (c) Find the sum of the smallest and largest numeral formed. A: 787. 245 + 542 = 787.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write XVII in Hindu-Arabic numerals. A: 17. XVII = 10 + 5 + 1 + 1 = 17.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which number is represented in the place value of hundreds on the abacus below? (TH, H, T, O) A: 2. There are 2 beads on the hundreds spike.
chunks.source: There are 2 beads on the hundreds spike.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 19 in Roman numerals. A: XIX. 10 is X and 9 is IX, so 19 is XIX.
chunks.source: 10 is X and 9 is IX, so 19 is XIX.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 946 in expanded form. A: 900 + 40 + 6. 946 = 900 + 40 + 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Round off 147 to the nearest ten. A: 150. 147 is closer to 150 than to 140.
chunks.source: 147 is closer to 150 than to 140.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Subtract: 30 − 19 = ___ A: 11. 30 take away 19 leaves 11.
chunks.source: 30 take away 19 leaves 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Match only one operation on the left with the operation on the right that has the same answer. A: 29 × 0: 30 − 30; 11 + 7: 2 × 9. 29 × 0 = 0 and 30 − 30 = 0; 11 + 7 = 18 and 2 × 9 = 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that a = 80 and b = 60. Find the value of a + b. A: 140. 80 + 60 = 140.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that a = 80 and b = 60. Find the value of (a ÷ 2) + b. A: 100. 80 ÷ 2 = 40, and 40 + 60 = 100.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that a = 80 and b = 60. Find the value of a − b. A: 20. 80 − 60 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Nakato has 315 mangoes, Kiiza has 426 mangoes and Babirye has 246 mangoes. How many mangoes do the three have altogether? A: 987. 315 + 426 + 246 = 987 mangoes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Add: 9 beads + 10 beads = ___ beads. A: 19. 9 + 10 = 19 beads.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Out of 1298 pupils in a school, 572 pupils are boys. The rest are girls. Find the number of girls in the school. A: 726. 1298 − 572 = 726 girls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mary had 123 ripe mangoes in the basket and some raw mangoes. Altogether they were 245 mangoes. How many raw mangoes were in the basket? A: 122. 245 − 123 = 122 raw mangoes.
chunks.source: 245 − 123 = 122 raw mangoes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Ritah is 6 years younger than her sister. Her sister is 10 years old. (a) How old is Ritah? A: 4. 10 − 6 = 4 years old.
chunks.source: 10 − 6 = 4 years old.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Ritah is 4 years old and her sister is 10 years old. (b) What is their total age? A: 14. 4 + 10 = 14 years.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Ritah is 4 and her sister is 10. (c) How old will each be in 3 years' time from now? A: Ritah 7, sister 13. 4 + 3 = 7 and 10 + 3 = 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mugabe packed 25 phones in a box. How many phones were packed in 3 similar boxes? A: 75. 3 × 25 = 75 phones.
chunks.source: 3 × 25 = 75 phones.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Sserugo had 346 cows on the farm. He bought 758 more cows. How many cows does he have on his farm now? A: 1104. 346 + 758 = 1104 cows.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Gloria had 105 pencils. She shared them among five children. How many pencils did each child get? A: 21. 105 ÷ 5 = 21 pencils.
chunks.source: 105 ÷ 5 = 21 pencils.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Maria had 216 goats but lost 19 goats to thieves. How many goats did she remain with? A: 197. 216 − 19 = 197 goats.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Share 24 mangoes by 6. How many mangoes does each get? A: 4. 24 ÷ 6 = 4 mangoes.
chunks.source: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 mangoes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Subtract: 11 from 22. A: 11. 22 − 11 = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3240 books were shared equally by 8 schools. How many books did each school get? A: 405. 3240 ÷ 8 = 405 books.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Match each operation with its answer. A: 2 + 3: 5; 4 − 2: 2; 6 × 6: 36; 1 × 1: 1. 2+3=5, 4−2=2, 6×6=36 and 1×1=1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A class has 32 boys and 47 girls. Find the total number of pupils in the class. A: 79. 32 + 47 = 79 pupils.
chunks.source: 32 + 47 = 79 pupils.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the difference of 88 and 25. A: 63. 88 − 25 = 63.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Add 5 + 4 using the number line below. A: 9. Start at 5 and jump 4 forward to land on 9.
chunks.source: Start at 5 and jump 4 forward to land on 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the number line to work out: 10 − 6 = ___. A: 4. Start at 10 and count back 6 to land on 4.
chunks.source: Start at 10 and count back 6 to land on 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the number line to work out: 2 × 4 = ___. A: 8. Two groups of 4 make 8.
chunks.source: Two groups of 4 make 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out using repeated addition: 4 × 3 = ___. A: 12. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A farmer had 340 goats and sold 120 goats. How many goats remained? A: 220. 340 − 120 = 220 goats.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use >, < or = to complete: 2 + 4 ___ 0 × 6. A: >. 6 > 0.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use >, < or = to complete: 3 × 4 ___ 6 + 6. A: =. 12 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use >, < or = to complete: 9 ÷ 3 ___ 10 ÷ 2. A: <. 3 < 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a school of 2748 pupils, 53 pupils were absent on a certain day. How many pupils were present on that day? A: 2695. 2748 − 53 = 2695 pupils.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use <, > or = to fill in correctly: 3 + 2 ___ 3 × 2. A: <. 5 < 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use <, > or = to fill in correctly: 7 × 2 ___ 2 × 7. A: =. 14 = 14.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use <, > or = to fill in correctly: 20 − 2 ___ 20 ÷ 2. A: >. 18 > 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A trader had 6 boxes each containing 12 balls. How many balls did the trader have altogether? A: 72. 6 × 12 = 72 balls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: List all the multiples of 4 less than 16. A: 4, 8, 12. Counting in fours gives 4, 8 and 12 before 16.
chunks.source: Counting in fours gives 4, 8 and 12 before 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the sum of the first four odd numbers. A: 16. 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16.

chunks.subject: Math
