chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 2, 6, 10, 14, ___. A: 18. Each number is 4 more than the one before, so 14 + 4 = 18.
chunks.source: Each number is 4 more than the one before, so 14 + 4 = 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: List down all multiples of 5 between 0 and 25. A: 5, 10, 15, 20. Counting in fives between 0 and 25 gives 5, 10, 15 and 20.
chunks.source: Counting in fives between 0 and 25 gives 5, 10, 15 and 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the value of a in the magic square. (Top row: 10, a, 8; middle: 5, 7, b; bottom: c, d, 4. Every row, column and diagonal adds to the same total.) A: 3. The diagonal 10 + 7 + 4 = 21, so 10 + a + 8 = 21 gives a = 3.
chunks.source: The diagonal 10 + 7 + 4 = 21, so 10 + a + 8 = 21 gives a = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the value of b in the magic square. (Every row, column and diagonal adds to 21.) A: 9. 5 + 7 + b = 21, so b = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the value of c in the magic square. (Every row, column and diagonal adds to 21.) A: 6. 10 + 5 + c = 21, so c = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the value of d in the magic square. (Every row, column and diagonal adds to 21.) A: 11. c + d + 4 = 21 with c = 6, so d = 11.
chunks.source: c + d + 4 = 21 with c = 6, so d = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the missing numbers in the sequence: 5, 6, 8, 11, 15, 20, ___, ___. A: 26, 33. The differences grow by one each time (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), so 20 + 6 = 26 and 26 + 7 = 33.
chunks.source: The differences grow by one each time (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), so 20 + 6 = 26 and 26 + 7 = 33.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Circle the even numbers: 1, 2, 5, 4, 3, 7. A: 2, 4. 2 and 4 are the even numbers in the list.
chunks.source: 2 and 4 are the even numbers in the list.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the missing numbers: 0, 2, 4, 6, ___, ___. A: 8, 10. Counting in twos gives 8 and then 10.
chunks.source: Counting in twos gives 8 and then 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the sum of the first 4 even numbers. A: 20. 2 + 4 + 6 + 8 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 4, 6, 8, 10, ___. A: 12. Each number is 2 more than the one before, so 10 + 2 = 12.
chunks.source: Each number is 2 more than the one before, so 10 + 2 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the number represented by letter a in the sequence: 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, a. a = ___ A: 77. Each number is 11 more, so 66 + 11 = 77.
chunks.source: Each number is 11 more, so 66 + 11 = 77.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of 6 and 9. A: 18. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18; multiples of 9: 9, 18. The smallest common one is 18.
chunks.source: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18; multiples of 9: 9, 18. The smallest common one is 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: 1 stool → 3 legs, 2 stools → 6 legs, 3 stools → ___ legs. How many legs do 3 stools have? A: 9. Each stool has 3 legs, so 3 × 3 = 9 legs.
chunks.source: Each stool has 3 legs, so 3 × 3 = 9 legs.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: 1 stool → 3 legs, 2 stools → 6 legs, ___ stools → 15 legs. How many stools have 15 legs? A: 5. 15 ÷ 3 = 5 stools.
chunks.source: 15 ÷ 3 = 5 stools.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In the magic square below, the three numbers in every row, column and diagonal add to 12. The top-left box is empty. What number goes in the top-left box? A: 7. The top row has 0 and 5, so 12 − 0 − 5 = 7.
chunks.source: The top row has 0 and 5, so 12 − 0 − 5 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In the magic square below (every line adds to 12), the middle-right box is empty. What number goes in the middle-right box? A: 6. The middle row has 2 and 4, so 12 − 2 − 4 = 6.
chunks.source: The middle row has 2 and 4, so 12 − 2 − 4 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In the magic square below (every line adds to 12), the bottom-left box is empty. What number goes in the bottom-left box? A: 3. The first column has 7 and 2, so 12 − 7 − 2 = 3.
chunks.source: The first column has 7 and 2, so 12 − 7 − 2 = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In the magic square below (every line adds to 12), the bottom-middle box is empty. What number goes in the bottom-middle box? A: 8. The second column has 0 and 4, so 12 − 0 − 4 = 8.
chunks.source: The second column has 0 and 4, so 12 − 0 − 4 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the missing number in the sequence: 1, 5, 9, 13, ___. A: 17. Each number is 4 more, so 13 + 4 = 17.
chunks.source: Each number is 4 more, so 13 + 4 = 17.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: List the multiples of 6 less than 20. A: 6, 12, 18. Counting in sixes gives 6, 12 and 18 before 20.
chunks.source: Counting in sixes gives 6, 12 and 18 before 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A water tank was 11/15 full of water. 4/15 was used for watering seedlings in the nursery bed. What fraction of the water remained in the tank? A: 7/15. 11/15 take away 4/15 leaves 7/15 of the water.
chunks.source: 11/15 take away 4/15 leaves 7/15 of the water.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 10 3/5 to an improper fraction. A: 53/5. 10 × 5 + 3 = 53, so it becomes 53/5.
chunks.source: 10 × 5 + 3 = 53, so it becomes 53/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram below carefully. (i) Write down the shaded fraction. A: 4/5. 4 out of the 5 equal parts are shaded.
chunks.source: 4 out of the 5 equal parts are shaded.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram below carefully. (ii) Write the unshaded fraction in words. A: one fifth. 1 out of 5 parts is not shaded, which is one fifth.
chunks.source: 1 out of 5 parts is not shaded, which is one fifth.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A class has 40 pupils. 2/5 of them are boys and the rest are girls. How many girls are in that class? A: 24. 2/5 of 40 is 16 boys, so 40 − 16 = 24 girls.
chunks.source: 2/5 of 40 is 16 boys, so 40 − 16 = 24 girls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the sum of 3/7 and 2/7. A: 5/7. 3/7 + 2/7 = 5/7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write a quarter in figures. A: 1/4. A quarter is one part out of four, written 1/4.
chunks.source: A quarter is one part out of four, written 1/4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a P.4 Blue class there are 60 pupils. 2/3 of them are girls and the rest are boys. (a) Find the fraction of boys in the class. A: 1/3. 1 − 2/3 = 1/3 are boys.
chunks.source: 1 − 2/3 = 1/3 are boys.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a P.4 Blue class there are 60 pupils. 2/3 of them are girls. (b) How many girls are in the class? A: 40. 2/3 of 60 = 40 girls.
chunks.source: 2/3 of 60 = 40 girls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a P.4 Blue class there are 60 pupils. 2/3 of them are girls. (c) How many boys are in the class? A: 20. 60 − 40 = 20 boys.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Musa ate 7/15 of the cake and Namugga ate 4/15 of the cake. (a) What fraction of the cake did they eat altogether? A: 11/15. 7/15 + 4/15 = 11/15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Musa ate 7/15 of the cake and Namugga ate 4/15 of the cake. (b) What fraction of the cake remained? A: 4/15. 15/15 − 11/15 = 4/15 remained.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the fraction that is unshaded in the triangle diagram below. A: 6/9. 6 of the 9 small triangles are not shaded.
chunks.source: 6 of the 9 small triangles are not shaded.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the shaded fraction of the figure below. A: 3/8. 3 out of the 8 equal parts are shaded.
chunks.source: 3 out of the 8 equal parts are shaded.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Three children shared apples: Agnes got 2/5, Bob got 1/5 and Juma got the rest. (a) What fraction did Agnes and Bob get? A: 3/5. 2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Three children shared apples: Agnes got 2/5, Bob got 1/5 and Juma got the rest. (b) What fraction was given to Juma? A: 2/5. 1 − 3/5 = 2/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Agnes got 2/5, Bob got 1/5 and Juma got 2/5 of the apples. (c) If the total number of apples was 20, how many apples did Bob get? A: 4. 1/5 of 20 = 4 apples.
chunks.source: 1/5 of 20 = 4 apples.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 3 1/4 as an improper fraction. A: 13/4. 3 × 4 + 1 = 13, so it becomes 13/4.
chunks.source: 3 × 4 + 1 = 13, so it becomes 13/4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a class of 90 pupils, 1/3 of them are girls and the rest are boys. (a) Find the fraction of boys in the class. A: 2/3. 1 − 1/3 = 2/3 are boys.
chunks.source: 1 − 1/3 = 2/3 are boys.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a class of 90 pupils, 1/3 of them are girls and the rest are boys. (b) How many boys are there in the class? A: 60. 2/3 of 90 = 60 boys.
chunks.source: 2/3 of 90 = 60 boys.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a class of 90 pupils, 1/3 are girls (30) and the rest are boys (60). (c) How many more boys than girls are there in the class? A: 30. 60 − 30 = 30 more boys.
chunks.source: 60 − 30 = 30 more boys.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the total of 4/9 and 3/9. A: 7/9. 4/9 + 3/9 = 7/9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 5 1/3 as an improper fraction. A: 16/3. 5 × 3 + 1 = 16, so it becomes 16/3.
chunks.source: 5 × 3 + 1 = 16, so it becomes 16/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a rectangular flower garden. (a) Find the value of a. A: 10. Side a is opposite the 10m side, and opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.
chunks.source: Side a is opposite the 10m side, and opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a rectangular flower garden. (a) Find the value of b. A: 8. Side b is opposite the 8m side, and opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.
chunks.source: Side b is opposite the 8m side, and opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a rectangular flower garden 10m by 8m. (b) Calculate the area occupied by the flower garden. A: 80. Area = 10 × 8 = 80 square metres.
chunks.source: Area = 10 × 8 = 80 square metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a rectangular flower garden 10m by 8m. (c) Amos walked round the garden once. What total distance did he cover altogether? A: 36. Perimeter = 10 + 8 + 10 + 8 = 36 metres.
chunks.source: Perimeter = 10 + 8 + 10 + 8 = 36 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name shape (ii) shown below. A: oval. The flat closed curved shape is an oval.
chunks.source: The flat closed curved shape is an oval.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name any one 4-sided shape. A: square. A square has four sides.
chunks.source: A square has four sides.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Patel walked once round a plot with sides 10m, 5m, 20m and 5m. What distance did he cover? A: 40. 10 + 5 + 20 + 5 = 40 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the size of angle P. (A 40° angle is marked inside a right angle.) A: 50. 90 − 40 = 50 degrees.
chunks.source: 90 − 40 = 50 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the size of angle X. (A 50° angle and X are on a straight line.) A: 130. 180 − 50 = 130 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the size of angle y. (A right angle is split into 30°, 40° and y°.) A: 20. 90 − 30 − 40 = 20 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the total distance around the rectangle below (7m by 3m). A: 20. 7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name shape (ii) shown below. A: triangle. The flat shape with three straight sides is a triangle.
chunks.source: The flat shape with three straight sides is a triangle.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the rectangle figure below (10cm by 4cm). (a)(i) Find the value of a. A: 10. Side a is opposite the 10cm side, so a = 10cm.
chunks.source: Side a is opposite the 10cm side, so a = 10cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the rectangle figure below (10cm by 4cm). (a)(ii) Find the value of b. A: 4. Side b is opposite the 4cm side, so b = 4cm.
chunks.source: Side b is opposite the 4cm side, so b = 4cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the rectangle figure below (10cm by 4cm). (b) Work out the area of the figure. A: 40. Area = 10 × 4 = 40 square centimetres.
chunks.source: Area = 10 × 4 = 40 square centimetres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the shape below. A: triangle. The shape has three straight sides, so it is a triangle.
chunks.source: The shape has three straight sides, so it is a triangle.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the perimeter of a square garden whose side is 7 metres. A: 28. 4 × 7 = 28 metres.
chunks.source: 4 × 7 = 28 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the area of the figure below. (A 3 by 3 grid of squares.) A: 9. There are 9 unit squares, so the area is 9 square units.
chunks.source: There are 9 unit squares, so the area is 9 square units.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name shape (i) shown below. A: kite. The four-sided shape with two pairs of equal adjacent sides is a kite.
chunks.source: The four-sided shape with two pairs of equal adjacent sides is a kite.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many lines of folding symmetry does the rectangle figure below have? A: 2. A rectangle folds in half lengthwise and widthwise, so 2 lines.
chunks.source: A rectangle folds in half lengthwise and widthwise, so 2 lines.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Below is a rectangle 6cm by 8cm. (a) What is the length of the rectangle? A: 8. The longer side of the rectangle is 8cm.
chunks.source: The longer side of the rectangle is 8cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Below is a rectangle 6cm by 8cm. (b) Calculate the perimeter of the rectangle. A: 28. 2 × (8 + 6) = 28cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the shape below. A: rectangle. The four-sided shape with right angles is a rectangle.
chunks.source: The four-sided shape with right angles is a rectangle.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the figure shown below. A: trapezium. The four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides is a trapezium.
chunks.source: The four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides is a trapezium.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the solid shape shown below. A: cube. The shape has six equal square faces, so it is a cube.
chunks.source: The shape has six equal square faces, so it is a cube.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name shape (i) shown below. A: cone. The shape has a circular base and comes to a point, so it is a cone.
chunks.source: The shape has a circular base and comes to a point, so it is a cone.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name shape (i) shown below. A: cylinder. The solid with two circular faces is a cylinder.
chunks.source: The solid with two circular faces is a cylinder.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name shape (ii) shown below. A: cube. The solid with six square faces is a cube.
chunks.source: The solid with six square faces is a cube.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the shape drawn below. A: cone. The shape with a circular base and a point is a cone.
chunks.source: The shape with a circular base and a point is a cone.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the shape below (6cm by 3cm by 4cm). (a) Name the shape. A: cuboid. The box-shaped solid with rectangular faces is a cuboid.
chunks.source: The box-shaped solid with rectangular faces is a cuboid.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the cuboid below. (b)(i) How many vertices does it have? A: 8. A cuboid has 8 corners (vertices).
chunks.source: A cuboid has 8 corners (vertices).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A class prefect recorded books of four girls using tallies, as shown in the table. How many books did Grace have? A: 15. Grace has three groups of five tallies, which is 15.
chunks.source: Grace has three groups of five tallies, which is 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The prefect recorded: Joan 7 books, Angella 8 books, Grace 15 books, Ritah 12 books. How many books did the prefect count altogether? A: 42. 7 + 8 + 15 + 12 = 42 books.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Nakato has 315 mangoes, Kiiza has 426 mangoes and Babirye has 246 mangoes. The table is missing one name and one number. Which person has 426 mangoes? A: Kiiza. The question says Kiiza has 426 mangoes.
chunks.source: The question says Kiiza has 426 mangoes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Nakato has 315 mangoes, Kiiza has 426 mangoes and Babirye has 246 mangoes. How many mangoes does Babirye have? A: 246. The question says Babirye has 246 mangoes.
chunks.source: The question says Babirye has 246 mangoes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: One fruit picture represents 10 fruits. How many fruit pictures are needed to represent 40 fruits? A: 4. 40 ÷ 10 = 4 pictures.
chunks.source: 40 ÷ 10 = 4 pictures.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: One fruit picture represents 10 fruits. How many fruit pictures are needed to represent 90 fruits? A: 9. 90 ÷ 10 = 9 pictures.
chunks.source: 90 ÷ 10 = 9 pictures.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: One fruit picture represents 10 fruits. How many fruit pictures are needed to represent 60 fruits? A: 6. 60 ÷ 10 = 6 pictures.
chunks.source: 60 ÷ 10 = 6 pictures.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: One ball picture represents 5 balls. How many balls are represented by the 5 ball pictures shown? A: 25. 5 × 5 = 25 balls.
chunks.source: 5 × 5 = 25 balls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The bar graph below shows the number of pupils who played games in P.4. (a) How many pupils played football? A: 30. The football bar reaches 30.
chunks.source: The football bar reaches 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The bar graph below shows the number of pupils who played games in P.4. (b) Which games are played by the same number of pupils? A: Football and Tennis. Football and Tennis both have bars reaching 30.
chunks.source: Football and Tennis both have bars reaching 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The bar graph below shows the number of pupils who played games in P.4. (c) Find the total number of pupils who played all the four games. A: 105. 30 + 20 + 25 + 30 = 105 pupils.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the pictograph below (Monday has 3 balls; Tuesday to Friday have none). (a) How many days were used for playing football? A: 1. Only Monday has balls, so football was played on 1 day.
chunks.source: Only Monday has balls, so football was played on 1 day.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the pictograph below. (b) Which day had the biggest number of balls played? A: Monday. Monday has 3 balls, more than any other day.
chunks.source: Monday has 3 balls, more than any other day.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the pictograph below. (d) Write the first day on the pictograph. A: Monday. The first row of the pictograph is Monday.
chunks.source: The first row of the pictograph is Monday.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: One book picture stands for 6 books. How many books are represented by the 4 book pictures shown? A: 24. 4 × 6 = 24 books.
chunks.source: 4 × 6 = 24 books.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The pictograph shows flowers planted each month (one flower picture = 5 flowers): February 3, March 2, April 4, May 3, June 1. (a) In which month were the most flowers planted? A: April. April has 4 flower pictures, more than any other month.
chunks.source: April has 4 flower pictures, more than any other month.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The pictograph shows flowers planted each month (one flower picture = 5 flowers). (b) How many flowers were planted in March? A: 10. 2 pictures × 5 = 10 flowers.
chunks.source: 2 pictures × 5 = 10 flowers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The pictograph shows flowers planted each month (one flower picture = 5 flowers). (c) In which two months were the same number of flowers planted? A: February and May. February and May both have 3 flower pictures.
chunks.source: February and May both have 3 flower pictures.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The pictograph shows flowers planted each month (one flower picture = 5 flowers): February 3, March 2, April 4, May 3, June 1. (d) Find the total number of flowers planted for all the five months. A: 65. (3 + 2 + 4 + 3 + 1) × 5 = 13 × 5 = 65 flowers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: One tree picture stands for 10 trees. How many trees are represented by the 4 tree pictures shown? A: 40. 4 × 10 = 40 trees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the pictograph below (one stool picture = 10 stools): Tom 3, Jane 5, Ali 2, Shadia 3. (a) Who has the highest number of stools? A: Jane. Jane has 5 stool pictures, more than anyone else.
chunks.source: Jane has 5 stool pictures, more than anyone else.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the pictograph below (one stool picture = 10 stools). (b) Which two pupils have the same number of stools? A: Tom and Shadia. Tom and Shadia both have 3 stool pictures.
chunks.source: Tom and Shadia both have 3 stool pictures.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the pictograph below (one stool picture = 10 stools): Tom 3, Jane 5, Ali 2, Shadia 3. (c) How many stools do they have altogether? A: 130. (3 + 5 + 2 + 3) × 10 = 13 × 10 = 130 stools.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The pictograph below shows balls of each colour (one ball picture = 2 balls): Blue 3, Yellow 1, Red 5, Green 4, Orange 2. (a) Which colour has the highest number of balls? A: Red. Red has 5 ball pictures, more than any other colour.
chunks.source: Red has 5 ball pictures, more than any other colour.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The pictograph below shows balls of each colour (one ball picture = 2 balls). (b) ___ has 2 balls. A: Yellow. Yellow has 1 picture, and 1 × 2 = 2 balls.
chunks.source: Yellow has 1 picture, and 1 × 2 = 2 balls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The pictograph below shows balls of each colour (one ball picture = 2 balls): Blue 3, Yellow 1, Red 5, Green 4, Orange 2. (c) Find the total number of balls in the school. A: 30. (3 + 1 + 5 + 4 + 2) × 2 = 15 × 2 = 30 balls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What number is shown by the tallies below? A: 19. Three groups of five plus four singles make 19.
chunks.source: Three groups of five plus four singles make 19.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The cost of a hot dog is Sh. 4000. How many coins of 500 shillings does Tom need in order to buy the hot dog? A: 8. 4000 ÷ 500 = 8 coins.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mukasa saves money using three tins: 4 coins of 1000 shillings, 6 coins of 500 shillings and 10 coins of 200 shillings. (a) How much money does Mukasa save altogether? A: 9000. 4000 + 3000 + 2000 = 9000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mukasa saved 9000 shillings. (b) If he spends Sh. 5000 and keeps the rest, how much does he keep? A: 4000. 9000 − 5000 = 4000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Subtract correctly: Sh. 5,000 − Sh. 3,000. A: 2000. 5000 − 3000 = 2000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Opio bought 3kg of sugar at Sh. 2,000 per kg. How much was spent on sugar? A: 6000. 3 × 2000 = 6000 shillings.
chunks.source: 3 × 2000 = 6000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Opio bought 2 books at Sh. 1,000 per book. How much was spent on books? A: 2000. 2 × 1000 = 2000 shillings.
chunks.source: 2 × 1000 = 2000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Opio bought 4 rulers at Sh. 5,000 each. How much was spent on rulers? A: 20000. 4 × 5000 = 20000 shillings.
chunks.source: 4 × 5000 = 20000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Opio bought 6 sweets at Sh. 200 each. How much was spent on sweets? A: 1200. 6 × 200 = 1200 shillings.
chunks.source: 6 × 200 = 1200 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Opio spent Sh. 6000 on sugar, Sh. 2000 on books, Sh. 20000 on rulers and Sh. 1200 on sweets. Find his total expenditure. A: 29200. 6000 + 2000 + 20000 + 1200 = 29200 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A trader has Sh. 9500. He sells his mangoes for Sh. 2500. How much money does he have altogether? A: 12000. 9500 + 2500 = 12000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Supermarket prices: 1kg rice Sh. 3600, 1kg sugar Sh. 3000, 1 packet biscuits Sh. 1000, 1 bar soap Sh. 800. (c) What was the most expensive item? A: rice. Sh. 3600 is the highest price, for rice.
chunks.source: Sh. 3600 is the highest price, for rice.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Supermarket prices: 1kg rice Sh. 3600, 1kg sugar Sh. 3000, 1 packet biscuits Sh. 1000, 1 bar soap Sh. 800. (d) What was the cheapest item? A: bar of soap. Sh. 800 is the lowest price, for the bar of soap.
chunks.source: Sh. 800 is the lowest price, for the bar of soap.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Supermarket prices: 1kg rice Sh. 3600, 1 packet biscuits Sh. 1000. (e) How much did Kato pay for 2kg of rice and one packet of biscuits? A: 8200. 2 × 3600 = 7200, plus 1000 = 8200 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A mathematical set costs Sh. 3000. How much will nine similar mathematical sets cost? A: 27000. 9 × 3000 = 27000 shillings.
chunks.source: 9 × 3000 = 27000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Katwere bought a cake at Sh. 2500 and she bought bread at Sh. 2500. How much money did she spend altogether? A: 5000. 2500 + 2500 = 5000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If 1kg of sugar costs Sh. 3500, what is the cost of 2kg? A: 7000. 2 × 3500 = 7000 shillings.
chunks.source: 2 × 3500 = 7000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The cost of 3 pens is Sh. 1,500. Find the cost of one pen. A: 500. 1500 ÷ 3 = 500 shillings.
chunks.source: 1500 ÷ 3 = 500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many five hundred shilling coins can be got from 2,000 shillings? A: 4. 2000 ÷ 500 = 4 coins.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Rhona's shopping list: ruler Sh. 1,000; box file Sh. 4,500; school bag Sh. 15,000; notebook Sh. 3,000; counter book Sh. 7,000. (a) Which is the most expensive item? A: School bag. Sh. 15,000 is the highest price.
chunks.source: Sh. 15,000 is the highest price.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Rhona's shopping list. (b) Find the cost of a box file and a ruler altogether. A: 5500. 4500 + 1000 = 5500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Rhona had a five thousand shillings note and bought a box file at Sh. 4,500. (c) How much was her balance? A: 500. 5000 − 4500 = 500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A pen costs Sh. 1200. What is the cost of 3 similar pens? A: 3600. 3 × 1200 = 3600 shillings.
chunks.source: 3 × 1200 = 3600 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: P.4 pupils bought: a pen at Sh. 1200, a mathematical set at Sh. 1800, a ruler at Sh. 500. (a) What is the most expensive item from the list? A: Mathematical set. Sh. 1800 is the highest price.
chunks.source: Sh. 1800 is the highest price.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: P.4 pupils bought a pen at Sh. 1200 and a ruler at Sh. 500. (b) How much did the pupil pay for a pen and a ruler? A: 1700. 1200 + 500 = 1700 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: P.4 pupils bought: a pen at Sh. 1200, a mathematical set at Sh. 1800, a ruler at Sh. 500. (c) Work out the total cost of all the 3 items. A: 3500. 1200 + 1800 + 500 = 3500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Julius has 4 coins of five hundred shillings. How much money does Julius have altogether? A: 2000. 4 × 500 = 2000 shillings.
chunks.source: 4 × 500 = 2000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mrs. Kampi's stall: pineapple Sh. 3000, banana Sh. 300, mango Sh. 1000, tomato Sh. 500. (a) Which item costs the least amount of money? A: Banana. Sh. 300 is the lowest price, for the banana.
chunks.source: Sh. 300 is the lowest price, for the banana.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mrs. Kampi's stall: pineapple Sh. 3000, banana Sh. 300, mango Sh. 1000. (b) How much money will Mrs. Kampi get from one who buys a pineapple, a mango and a banana? A: 4300. 3000 + 1000 + 300 = 4300 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mrs. Kampi's stall: tomato Sh. 500. (c) Find the total amount of money needed to buy four tomatoes. A: 2000. 4 × 500 = 2000 shillings.
chunks.source: 4 × 500 = 2000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: After buying a geometry set for Sh. 3,700, Mukasa was given a balance of Sh. 1,300. How much money did he give the shopkeeper? A: 5000. 3700 + 1300 = 5000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the time shown on the digital clock face (7:20) in words. A: Twenty minutes past seven. 7:20 is twenty minutes after seven o'clock.
chunks.source: 7:20 is twenty minutes after seven o'clock.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A baby is 84 days old. What is his age in weeks? A: 12. 84 ÷ 7 = 12 weeks.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (i) 60 minutes ___ 1 hour. Use 'is greater than', 'is less than' or 'is equal to'. A: is equal to. 60 minutes is exactly the same as 1 hour.
chunks.source: 60 minutes is exactly the same as 1 hour.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (ii) 2 weeks ___ 7 days. Use 'is greater than', 'is less than' or 'is equal to'. A: is greater than. 2 weeks is 14 days, which is more than 7 days.
chunks.source: 2 weeks is 14 days, which is more than 7 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (iii) 10 months ___ 1 year. Use 'is greater than', 'is less than' or 'is equal to'. A: is less than. 1 year is 12 months, which is more than 10 months.
chunks.source: 1 year is 12 months, which is more than 10 months.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Add: 4 hours 20 minutes + 3 hours 35 minutes. A: 7 hours 55 minutes. 4 + 3 = 7 hours and 20 + 35 = 55 minutes.
chunks.source: 4 + 3 = 7 hours and 20 + 35 = 55 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Tell the time shown on clock (a). A: Nine o'clock. The short hand points at 9 and the long hand at 12, so it is nine o'clock.
chunks.source: The short hand points at 9 and the long hand at 12, so it is nine o'clock.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Tell the time shown on clock (b). A: Half past three. The short hand is at 3 and the long hand at 6, so it is half past three.
chunks.source: The short hand is at 3 and the long hand at 6, so it is half past three.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Tell the time shown on the clock face below. A: A quarter past seven. The short hand is past 7 and the long hand is at 3, so it is a quarter past seven.
chunks.source: The short hand is past 7 and the long hand is at 3, so it is a quarter past seven.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (a) Express 4 weeks in days. A: 28. 4 × 7 = 28 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (d) Write the fifth month of the year. A: May. The months go January, February, March, April, May.
chunks.source: The months go January, February, March, April, May.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the time shown on the clock face below. (The clock uses Roman numerals.) A: Twenty minutes past eight. The short hand is past 8 and the long hand is at 4, so it is twenty minutes past eight.
chunks.source: The short hand is past 8 and the long hand is at 4, so it is twenty minutes past eight.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Kamau spent 42 days in Kenya. How many weeks did he spend in Kenya? A: 6. 42 ÷ 7 = 6 weeks.
chunks.source: 42 ÷ 7 = 6 weeks.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Tell the time shown on the clock below. A: Ten minutes past six. The short hand is past 6 and the long hand is at 2, so it is ten minutes past six.
chunks.source: The short hand is past 6 and the long hand is at 2, so it is ten minutes past six.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If 60 minutes = 1 hour, how many hours are there in 180 minutes? A: 3. 180 ÷ 60 = 3 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: 7 weeks 3 days + 5 weeks 2 days. A: 12 weeks 5 days. 7 + 5 = 12 weeks and 3 + 2 = 5 days.
chunks.source: 7 + 5 = 12 weeks and 3 + 2 = 5 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: 6 weeks 3 days + 1 week 5 days. A: 8 weeks 1 day. 6 + 1 = 7 weeks and 3 + 5 = 8 days = 1 week 1 day, so 8 weeks 1 day.
chunks.source: 6 + 1 = 7 weeks and 3 + 5 = 8 days = 1 week 1 day, so 8 weeks 1 day.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many days are there in 4 weeks? A: 28. 4 × 7 = 28 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: 6 hours 30 minutes + 2 hours 40 minutes. A: 9 hours 10 minutes. 6 + 2 = 8 hours and 30 + 40 = 70 minutes = 1 hour 10 minutes, so 9 hours 10 minutes.
chunks.source: 6 + 2 = 8 hours and 30 + 40 = 70 minutes = 1 hour 10 minutes, so 9 hours 10 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many hours are there in 120 minutes? A: 2. 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Tell the morning time shown on the clock face below. A: A quarter past three. The short hand is past 3 and the long hand is at 3, so it is a quarter past three.
chunks.source: The short hand is past 3 and the long hand is at 3, so it is a quarter past three.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the month of the year with the least number of days. A: February. February has 28 days (29 in a leap year), fewer than any other month.
chunks.source: February has 28 days (29 in a leap year), fewer than any other month.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 2 weeks to days. A: 14. 2 × 7 = 14 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (a) How many minutes make one hour? A: 60. One hour has 60 minutes.
chunks.source: One hour has 60 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (b) Tell the time shown on the clock below. A: Half past twelve. The short hand is at 12 and the long hand at 6, so it is half past twelve.
chunks.source: The short hand is at 12 and the long hand at 6, so it is half past twelve.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Convert 5 weeks into days. A: 35. 5 × 7 = 35 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a food store there are three bags: rice 13kg, posho 15kg and millet 12kg. Find the total mass of the three bags in kilogrammes. A: 40. 13 + 15 + 12 = 40 kilogrammes.
chunks.source: 13 + 15 + 12 = 40 kilogrammes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Container A holds 6000 litres and container B holds 4000 litres. Write the difference in litres of the two containers in words. A: Two thousand litres. 6000 − 4000 = 2000 litres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Subtract: 7 litres 700 millilitres − 2 litres 500 millilitres. A: 5L 200mL. 7L − 2L = 5L and 700mL − 500mL = 200mL.
chunks.source: 7L − 2L = 5L and 700mL − 500mL = 200mL.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Peter weighs 39kg and Florence weighs 21kg. Who is heavier? A: Peter. 39kg is more than 21kg, so Peter is heavier.
chunks.source: 39kg is more than 21kg, so Peter is heavier.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the map: Home — 100m — Borehole — 200m — (300m) — Shop. (a) How far is the borehole (the water source) from the home? A: 100. The map shows 100 metres from home to the borehole.
chunks.source: The map shows 100 metres from home to the borehole.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the map: Home — 100m — Borehole — 200m + 300m — Shop. (b) Write the direct distance from the borehole to the shop in words. A: Five hundred metres. 200 + 300 = 500 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the map: Home — 100m — Borehole — 200m + 300m — Shop. (c) What distance will one cover travelling from the home to the shop via the borehole? A: 600. 100 + 200 + 300 = 600 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many half-litre cups are in a 5-litre jerrycan? A: 10. 5 ÷ 1/2 = 10 cups.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: 5m 35cm + 1m 14cm. A: 6m 49cm. 5 + 1 = 6m and 35 + 14 = 49cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows the road between three homes in a triangle: Henry's to Kato's 18m, Henry's to Mary's 13m, Kato's to Mary's 20m. (a) Find the distance Henry will cover if he goes to Mary's home and continues to Kato's home. A: 33. 13 + 20 = 33 metres.
chunks.source: 13 + 20 = 33 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows the road between three homes in a triangle: Henry's to Kato's 18m, Henry's to Mary's 13m, Kato's to Mary's 20m. (b) If Henry's cow walks around the three homes, calculate in metres the distance covered by the cow. A: 51. 18 + 13 + 20 = 51 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Take away: 363 litres − 139 litres = ___ litres. A: 224. 363 − 139 = 224 litres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 7kg to grams. A: 7000. 1kg = 1000g, so 7kg = 7000g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mugenyi weighs 24kg and Mangeni weighs 8kg heavier than Mugenyi. (a) What is Mangeni's weight? A: 32. 24 + 8 = 32kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mugenyi weighs 24kg and Mangeni weighs 32kg. (b) Find their total weight. A: 56. 24 + 32 = 56kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 3 metres to centimetres. A: 300. 1m = 100cm, so 3m = 300cm.
chunks.source: 1m = 100cm, so 3m = 300cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Moses weighs 70kg and Sarah weighs 60kg. By how many kilogrammes is Moses heavier than Sarah? A: 10. 70 − 60 = 10kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the map below: Greenhill Buwaate — 12km — Kireka — 8km — Kibuli Mosque — 5km — Kampala city. (a) How far is Kireka from Greenhill Buwaate? A: 12. The map shows 12km between them.
chunks.source: The map shows 12km between them.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the map below. (c) Find the distance from Kibuli Mosque to Greenhill Buwaate via Kireka. A: 20. 8 + 12 = 20km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Simplify: 4b + 2b − b. A: 5b. 4b + 2b = 6b, and 6b − b = 5b.
chunks.source: 4b + 2b = 6b, and 6b − b = 5b.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out and fill in correctly: ___ + 6 = 13. A: 7. 13 − 6 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve the equation: P − 4 = 7. A: 11. 7 + 4 = 11, so P = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve the equation: m + 5 = 9. A: 4. 9 − 5 = 4, so m = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve the equation: y/3 = 2. A: 6. 2 × 3 = 6, so y = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the value of a: a × 4 = 12. A: 3. 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so a = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Simplify: 4e + e. A: 5e. 4e + 1e = 5e.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that a = 2, b = 4 and c = 5, find the value of a + b + c. A: 11. 2 + 4 + 5 = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that a = 2, b = 4 and c = 5, find the value of c − a. A: 3. 5 − 2 = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the missing number in the box: 312 − ___ = 301. A: 11. 312 − 301 = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Think of a number, subtract 9 from it and the difference is 12. What is the number? A: 21. 12 + 9 = 21.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Simplify: 9 cups + 6 cups − 4 cups. A: 11 cups. 9 + 6 − 4 = 11 cups.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the number in the box: ___ − 3 = 97. A: 100. 97 + 3 = 100.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Simplify: 4 cats + 3 cats + 2 cats. A: 9 cats. 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 cats.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the missing number: ___ + 10 = 19. A: 9. 19 − 10 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the missing number: 6 × ___ = 18. A: 3. 18 ÷ 6 = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the missing number: ___ ÷ 2 = 10. A: 20. 10 × 2 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Fill the box with the missing number: ___ − 12 = 18. A: 30. 18 + 12 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is M = {the first four letters of the alphabet}. List all the members of set M. A: a, b, c, d. The first four letters of the alphabet are a, b, c and d.
chunks.source: The first four letters of the alphabet are a, b, c and d.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that X = {a, b, g} and Y = {t, a, b, l, e}. How many members make the union set? A: 6. The union is {a, b, g, t, l, e}, which has 6 members.
chunks.source: The union is {a, b, g, t, l, e}, which has 6 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Set K = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}. How many members are in set K? A: 5. Counting the members 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 gives 5.
chunks.source: Counting the members 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 gives 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the sets below. (a) The picture shows cups in a set. A set of ____? cups. A: 5. There are 5 cups in the picture.
chunks.source: There are 5 cups in the picture.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the sets below. (b) The picture shows chairs in a set. A set of ____? chairs. A: 10. There are 10 chairs in the picture.
chunks.source: There are 10 chairs in the picture.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set K = {t, e, a} and L = {a, t, e}. Set K and L are ____? sets. A: equal. Both sets have exactly the same members, so they are equal sets.
chunks.source: Both sets have exactly the same members, so they are equal sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the Venn diagram below (P and R). (a) List the members of set P. A: g, o, a, t. Set P contains g, o, a and t.
chunks.source: Set P contains g, o, a and t.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the Venn diagram below (P and R). (b) Find P ∩ R. A: a, t. The letters in both P and R are a and t.
chunks.source: The letters in both P and R are a and t.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the Venn diagram below (P and R). (c) How many members are in P ∪ R? A: 5. P ∪ R = {g, o, a, t, e}, which has 5 members.
chunks.source: P ∪ R = {g, o, a, t, e}, which has 5 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is K = {the first five letters of the English alphabet}. List the members of set K. A: a, b, c, d, e. The first five letters are a, b, c, d and e.
chunks.source: The first five letters are a, b, c, d and e.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Set M = {triangle, square, circle, school bag} and set G = {circle, school bag}, as shown in the pictures. Write the common members of set M and set G. A: circle, school bag. Circle and school bag appear in both sets.
chunks.source: Circle and school bag appear in both sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (i) G = {18, 19, 20, 26} and H = {26, 18, 20, 19}. Set G and H are ____? sets. A: equal. Both sets have exactly the same members, so they are equal sets.
chunks.source: Both sets have exactly the same members, so they are equal sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: (ii) R = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} and P = {a, b, c, d, e}. P and R are ____? sets. A: equivalent. Both sets have 5 members but different members, so they are equivalent sets.
chunks.source: Both sets have 5 members but different members, so they are equivalent sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is (b) Set N = {boys who have seven eyes each}. Set N = ? A: empty set. No boy has seven eyes, so the set has no members: it is an empty set.
chunks.source: No boy has seven eyes, so the set has no members: it is an empty set.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that K = {1, 2, 3} and L = {2, 1, 3}. Set K and L are ____? sets. A: equal. Both sets have the same members, so they are equal sets.
chunks.source: Both sets have the same members, so they are equal sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The Venn diagram shows set R with members 1, 2, 3 and 4. How many members has set R? A: 4. Counting the members gives 4.
chunks.source: Counting the members gives 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set R = {oval, triangle, square} and set S = {p, a, i, n}, as shown in the pictures. Set R and S are ____? sets. A: not equivalent. R has 3 members and S has 4 members, so they are not equivalent sets.
chunks.source: R has 3 members and S has 4 members, so they are not equivalent sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Set X = {p, l, a, n, t} and Y = {c, l, a, i, m}. Find X ∩ Y. A: l, a. The letters in both sets are l and a.
chunks.source: The letters in both sets are l and a.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If set P = {a, b, c}, how many elements has set P? A: 3. P has 3 members.
chunks.source: P has 3 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Set K = {0, 1, 2} and set L = {1, 2, 4}. (i) Find K ∩ L. A: 1, 2. 1 and 2 are in both sets.
chunks.source: 1 and 2 are in both sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Set K = {0, 1, 2} and set L = {1, 2, 4}. (ii) Find K ∪ L. A: 0, 1, 2, 4. All different members together are {0, 1, 2, 4}.
chunks.source: All different members together are {0, 1, 2, 4}.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name the set symbol '∩'. A: intersection. The symbol ∩ means intersection.
chunks.source: The symbol ∩ means intersection.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name the set symbol '∪'. A: union. The symbol ∪ means union.
chunks.source: The symbol ∪ means union.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name the set symbol '='. A: equal to. The symbol = means equal to.
chunks.source: The symbol = means equal to.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name the set symbol '≠'. A: not equal to. The symbol ≠ means not equal to.
chunks.source: The symbol ≠ means not equal to.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that K = {1, 2, 3}, find the number of elements in set K. A: 3. K has 3 members.
chunks.source: K has 3 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If M = {ball, bench, bag} and N = {bag, bench, ball} as shown in the pictures, describe the relationship between set M and set N. A: They are equal sets. Both sets have exactly the same members, so they are equal sets.
chunks.source: Both sets have exactly the same members, so they are equal sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is G = {odd numbers between 10 and 20}. (a)(ii) List all the members of set G. A: 11, 13, 15, 17, 19. The odd numbers between 10 and 20 are 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19.
chunks.source: The odd numbers between 10 and 20 are 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.source: H − G = {12, 14, 16}, which has 3 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is R = {all months of the year with 30 days}. Find the members of set R. A: April, June, September, November. The months with 30 days are April, June, September and November.
chunks.source: The months with 30 days are April, June, September and November.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that set A = {a, b, c, d}, find n(A). A: 4. Set A has 4 members, so n(A) = 4.
chunks.source: Set A has 4 members, so n(A) = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that R = {e, x, a, m}, find n(R). A: 4. R has 4 members, so n(R) = 4.
chunks.source: R has 4 members, so n(R) = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that W = {d, o, g} and X = {d, o, n, k, e, y}. (b) Find W ∩ X. A: d, o. The letters in both sets are d and o.
chunks.source: The letters in both sets are d and o.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that W = {d, o, g} and X = {d, o, n, k, e, y}. (c) How many members are in W ∪ X? A: 7. W ∪ X = {d, o, g, n, k, e, y}, which has 7 members.
chunks.source: W ∪ X = {d, o, g, n, k, e, y}, which has 7 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Express 24 in Roman numerals. A: XXIV. 20 is XX and 4 is IV, so 24 is XXIV.
chunks.source: 20 is XX and 4 is IV, so 24 is XXIV.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A sign post shows 256 kilometres to Mbale. (a) Write the distance to Mbale in words. A: Two hundred fifty-six kilometres. 256 is read as two hundred fifty-six.
chunks.source: 256 is read as two hundred fifty-six.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A sign post shows 256 kilometres to Mbale. (b) Expand 256 using place values. A: 200 + 50 + 6. 256 = 200 + 50 + 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A sign post shows 256 kilometres to Mbale. (c) Round off 256 to the nearest hundred. A: 300. 256 is closer to 300 than to 200.
chunks.source: 256 is closer to 300 than to 200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write the Roman numeral for 10. A: X. In Roman numerals, X means 10.
chunks.source: In Roman numerals, X means 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write 'four thousand two hundred' in figures. A: 4200. Four thousand two hundred is 4200.
chunks.source: Four thousand two hundred is 4200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the digits 4, 9, 1. (a)(i) Form the smallest three-digit number. A: 149. Putting the smallest digit first gives 149.
chunks.source: Putting the smallest digit first gives 149.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the digits 4, 9, 1. (a)(ii) Form the biggest three-digit number. A: 941. Putting the biggest digit first gives 941.
chunks.source: Putting the biggest digit first gives 941.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the digits 4, 9, 1. (b) Write the smallest three-digit number, 149, in words. A: One hundred forty-nine. 149 is read as one hundred forty-nine.
chunks.source: 149 is read as one hundred forty-nine.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What is the sum of the values of 3 and 2 in 4352? A: 350. The value of 3 is 300 and the value of 2 is 50; 300 + 50 = 350.
chunks.source: The value of 3 is 300 and the value of 2 is 50; 300 + 50 = 350.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Joanita has 15 pencils. Express the number of pencils she has in Roman numerals. A: XV. 10 is X and 5 is V, so 15 is XV.
chunks.source: 10 is X and 5 is V, so 15 is XV.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write down the expanded number: (2 × 100) + (9 × 10) + (3 × 1). A: 293. 200 + 90 + 3 = 293.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is (a) What number is shown on the abacus below? (Hundreds, Tens, Ones) A: 243. 2 hundreds, 4 tens and 3 ones make 243.
chunks.source: 2 hundreds, 4 tens and 3 ones make 243.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is (b) Write the number 243 shown on the abacus in words. A: Two hundred forty-three. 243 is read as two hundred forty-three.
chunks.source: 243 is read as two hundred forty-three.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is (c) Multiply the value of 2 by the value of 3 in the number 243 shown on the abacus. A: 600. The value of 2 is 200 and the value of 3 is 3; 200 × 3 = 600.
chunks.source: The value of 2 is 200 and the value of 3 is 3; 200 × 3 = 600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write the single number that has been expanded to get 5000 + 800 + 7. A: 5807. 5000 + 800 + 7 = 5807.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Kasirye eats 24 apples per day. Write the number of apples in Roman numerals. A: XXIV. 24 is XXIV in Roman numerals.
chunks.source: 24 is XXIV in Roman numerals.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the abacus below (Thousands, Hundreds, Tens, Ones). What number is shown on the abacus? A: 2403. 2 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 3 ones make 2403.
chunks.source: 2 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 3 ones make 2403.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write 160 in words. A: One hundred sixty. 160 is read as one hundred sixty.
chunks.source: 160 is read as one hundred sixty.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What number is shown on the abacus? (Hundreds, Tens, Ones) A: 521. 5 hundreds, 2 tens and 1 one make 521.
chunks.source: 5 hundreds, 2 tens and 1 one make 521.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write the numerals 521 shown on the abacus above in words. A: Five hundred twenty-one. 521 is read as five hundred twenty-one.
chunks.source: 521 is read as five hundred twenty-one.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write 20 in Roman numerals. A: XX. 10 is X, so 20 is XX.
chunks.source: 10 is X, so 20 is XX.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What is the place value of 2 in the number 624? A: tens. The 2 is in the tens place.
chunks.source: The 2 is in the tens place.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write the values of the digits in the number 48,359. A: 40000, 8000, 300, 50, 9. 4 is 40000, 8 is 8000, 3 is 300, 5 is 50 and 9 is 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Expand 390 in value form. A: 300 + 90. 390 = 300 + 90.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the number expanded below: 3 hundreds + 7 tens + 5 ones. A: 375. 300 + 70 + 5 = 375.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the digits 5, 3, 9. (a) Form the largest 3-digit number using the digits above. A: 953. Putting the biggest digit first gives 953.
chunks.source: Putting the biggest digit first gives 953.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the digits 5, 3, 9. (b) Form the smallest 3-digit number using the digits above. A: 359. Putting the smallest digit first gives 359.
chunks.source: Putting the smallest digit first gives 359.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the digits 5, 3, 9. (c) Find the sum of the smallest and the largest number formed above. A: 1312. 359 + 953 = 1312.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Expand 384 using values. A: 300 + 80 + 4. 384 = 300 + 80 + 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the value of 2 in 9246. A: 200. The 2 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 200.
chunks.source: The 2 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What number has been expanded to give (6 x 1000) + (8 x 100) + (4 x 10) + (9 x 1)? A: 6849. 6000 + 800 + 40 + 9 = 6849.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write the number 6849 in words. A: Six thousand eight hundred forty-nine. 6849 is read as six thousand eight hundred forty-nine.
chunks.source: 6849 is read as six thousand eight hundred forty-nine.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the digits 5, 2 and 4. (a) Form the biggest numeral using the above digits. A: 542. Putting the biggest digit first gives 542.
chunks.source: Putting the biggest digit first gives 542.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the digits 5, 2 and 4. (b) Form the smallest numeral. A: 245. Putting the smallest digit first gives 245.
chunks.source: Putting the smallest digit first gives 245.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the digits 5, 2 and 4. (c) Find the sum of the smallest and largest numeral formed. A: 787. 245 + 542 = 787.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write XVII in Hindu-Arabic numerals. A: 17. XVII = 10 + 5 + 1 + 1 = 17.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Which number is represented in the place value of hundreds on the abacus below? (TH, H, T, O) A: 2. There are 2 beads on the hundreds spike.
chunks.source: There are 2 beads on the hundreds spike.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write 4000 + 900 + 6 as a single number. A: 4906. 4000 + 900 + 6 = 4906.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write 19 in Roman numerals. A: XIX. 10 is X and 9 is IX, so 19 is XIX.
chunks.source: 10 is X and 9 is IX, so 19 is XIX.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write 946 in expanded form. A: 900 + 40 + 6. 946 = 900 + 40 + 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Round off 147 to the nearest ten. A: 150. 147 is closer to 150 than to 140.
chunks.source: 147 is closer to 150 than to 140.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Subtract: 30 − 19 = ____? A: 11. 30 take away 19 leaves 11.
chunks.source: 30 take away 19 leaves 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that a = 80 and b = 60. Find the value of a + b. A: 140. 80 + 60 = 140.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that a = 80 and b = 60. Find the value of (a ÷ 2) + b. A: 100. 80 ÷ 2 = 40, and 40 + 60 = 100.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that a = 80 and b = 60. Find the value of a − b. A: 20. 80 − 60 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Subtract: 152 from 700. A: 548. 700 − 152 = 548.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Nakato has 315 mangoes, Kiiza has 426 mangoes and Babirye has 246 mangoes. How many mangoes do the three have altogether? A: 987. 315 + 426 + 246 = 987 mangoes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If a = 40, b = 60 and c = 30, find the value of (a + b) − c. A: 70. (40 + 60) − 30 = 100 − 30 = 70.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Add: 9 beads + 10 beads = ____? beads. A: 19. 9 + 10 = 19 beads.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Out of 1298 pupils in a school, 572 pupils are boys. The rest are girls. Find the number of girls in the school. A: 726. 1298 − 572 = 726 girls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mary had 123 ripe mangoes in the basket and some raw mangoes. Altogether they were 245 mangoes. How many raw mangoes were in the basket? A: 122. 245 − 123 = 122 raw mangoes.
chunks.source: 245 − 123 = 122 raw mangoes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Ritah is 6 years younger than her sister. Her sister is 10 years old. (a) How old is Ritah? A: 4. 10 − 6 = 4 years old.
chunks.source: 10 − 6 = 4 years old.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Ritah is 4 years old and her sister is 10 years old. (b) What is their total age? A: 14. 4 + 10 = 14 years.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Ritah is 4 and her sister is 10. (c) How old will each be in 3 years' time from now? A: Ritah 7, sister 13. 4 + 3 = 7 and 10 + 3 = 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mugabe packed 25 phones in a box. How many phones were packed in 3 similar boxes? A: 75. 3 × 25 = 75 phones.
chunks.source: 3 × 25 = 75 phones.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Sserugo had 346 cows on the farm. He bought 758 more cows. How many cows does he have on his farm now? A: 1104. 346 + 758 = 1104 cows.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Gloria had 105 pencils. She shared them among five children. How many pencils did each child get? A: 21. 105 ÷ 5 = 21 pencils.
chunks.source: 105 ÷ 5 = 21 pencils.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Maria had 216 goats but lost 19 goats to thieves. How many goats did she remain with? A: 197. 216 − 19 = 197 goats.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Share 24 mangoes by 6. How many mangoes does each get? A: 4. 24 ÷ 6 = 4 mangoes.
chunks.source: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 mangoes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Subtract: 11 from 22. A: 11. 22 − 11 = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 3240 books were shared equally by 8 schools. How many books did each school get? A: 405. 3240 ÷ 8 = 405 books.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A class has 32 boys and 47 girls. Find the total number of pupils in the class. A: 79. 32 + 47 = 79 pupils.
chunks.source: 32 + 47 = 79 pupils.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the difference of 88 and 25. A: 63. 88 − 25 = 63.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Add 5 + 4 using the number line below. A: 9. Start at 5 and jump 4 forward to land on 9.
chunks.source: Start at 5 and jump 4 forward to land on 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the number line to work out: 10 − 6 = ____?. A: 4. Start at 10 and count back 6 to land on 4.
chunks.source: Start at 10 and count back 6 to land on 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the number line to work out: 2 × 4 = ____?. A: 8. Two groups of 4 make 8.
chunks.source: Two groups of 4 make 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out using repeated addition: 4 × 3 = ____?. A: 12. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A farmer had 340 goats and sold 120 goats. How many goats remained? A: 220. 340 − 120 = 220 goats.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a school of 2748 pupils, 53 pupils were absent on a certain day. How many pupils were present on that day? A: 2695. 2748 − 53 = 2695 pupils.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A trader had 6 boxes each containing 12 balls. How many balls did the trader have altogether? A: 72. 6 × 12 = 72 balls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the sum of the first four odd numbers. A: 16. 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 2, 6, 10, 14, ____?. A: 18. Each number is 4 more than the one before, so 14 + 4 = 18.
chunks.source: Each number is 4 more than the one before, so 14 + 4 = 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the value of a in the magic square. (Top row: 10, a, 8; middle: 5, 7, b; bottom: c, d, 4. Every row, column and diagonal adds to the same total.) A: 3. The diagonal 10 + 7 + 4 = 21, so 10 + a + 8 = 21 gives a = 3.
chunks.source: The diagonal 10 + 7 + 4 = 21, so 10 + a + 8 = 21 gives a = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the value of b in the magic square. (Every row, column and diagonal adds to 21.) A: 9. 5 + 7 + b = 21, so b = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the value of c in the magic square. (Every row, column and diagonal adds to 21.) A: 6. 10 + 5 + c = 21, so c = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the value of d in the magic square. (Every row, column and diagonal adds to 21.) A: 11. c + d + 4 = 21 with c = 6, so d = 11.
chunks.source: c + d + 4 = 21 with c = 6, so d = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the sum of the first 4 even numbers. A: 20. 2 + 4 + 6 + 8 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 4, 6, 8, 10, ____?. A: 12. Each number is 2 more than the one before, so 10 + 2 = 12.
chunks.source: Each number is 2 more than the one before, so 10 + 2 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the number represented by letter a in the sequence: 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, a. a = ____? A: 77. Each number is 11 more, so 66 + 11 = 77.
chunks.source: Each number is 11 more, so 66 + 11 = 77.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of 6 and 9. A: 18. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18; multiples of 9: 9, 18. The smallest common one is 18.
chunks.source: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18; multiples of 9: 9, 18. The smallest common one is 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: 1 stool → 3 legs, 2 stools → 6 legs, 3 stools → ____? legs. How many legs do 3 stools have? A: 9. Each stool has 3 legs, so 3 × 3 = 9 legs.
chunks.source: Each stool has 3 legs, so 3 × 3 = 9 legs.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: 1 stool → 3 legs, 2 stools → 6 legs, ____? stools → 15 legs. How many stools have 15 legs? A: 5. 15 ÷ 3 = 5 stools.
chunks.source: 15 ÷ 3 = 5 stools.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In the magic square below, the three numbers in every row, column and diagonal add to 12. The top-left box is empty. What number goes in the top-left box? A: 7. The top row has 0 and 5, so 12 − 0 − 5 = 7.
chunks.source: The top row has 0 and 5, so 12 − 0 − 5 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In the magic square below (every line adds to 12), the middle-right box is empty. What number goes in the middle-right box? A: 6. The middle row has 2 and 4, so 12 − 2 − 4 = 6.
chunks.source: The middle row has 2 and 4, so 12 − 2 − 4 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In the magic square below (every line adds to 12), the bottom-left box is empty. What number goes in the bottom-left box? A: 3. The first column has 7 and 2, so 12 − 7 − 2 = 3.
chunks.source: The first column has 7 and 2, so 12 − 7 − 2 = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In the magic square below (every line adds to 12), the bottom-middle box is empty. What number goes in the bottom-middle box? A: 8. The second column has 0 and 4, so 12 − 0 − 4 = 8.
chunks.source: The second column has 0 and 4, so 12 − 0 − 4 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the missing number in the sequence: 1, 5, 9, 13, ____?. A: 17. Each number is 4 more, so 13 + 4 = 17.
chunks.source: Each number is 4 more, so 13 + 4 = 17.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A water tank was 11/15 full of water. 4/15 was used for watering seedlings in the nursery bed. What fraction of the water remained in the tank? A: 7/15. 11/15 take away 4/15 leaves 7/15 of the water.
chunks.source: 11/15 take away 4/15 leaves 7/15 of the water.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Change 10 3/5 to an improper fraction. A: 53/5. 10 × 5 + 3 = 53, so it becomes 53/5.
chunks.source: 10 × 5 + 3 = 53, so it becomes 53/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the diagram below carefully. (i) Write down the shaded fraction. A: 4/5. 4 out of the 5 equal parts are shaded.
chunks.source: 4 out of the 5 equal parts are shaded.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the diagram below carefully. (ii) Write the unshaded fraction in words. A: one fifth. 1 out of 5 parts is not shaded, which is one fifth.
chunks.source: 1 out of 5 parts is not shaded, which is one fifth.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A class has 40 pupils. 2/5 of them are boys and the rest are girls. How many girls are in that class? A: 24. 2/5 of 40 is 16 boys, so 40 − 16 = 24 girls.
chunks.source: 2/5 of 40 is 16 boys, so 40 − 16 = 24 girls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the sum of 3/7 and 2/7. A: 5/7. 3/7 + 2/7 = 5/7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write a quarter in figures. A: 1/4. A quarter is one part out of four, written 1/4.
chunks.source: A quarter is one part out of four, written 1/4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a P.4 Blue class there are 60 pupils. 2/3 of them are girls and the rest are boys. (a) Find the fraction of boys in the class. A: 1/3. 1 − 2/3 = 1/3 are boys.
chunks.source: 1 − 2/3 = 1/3 are boys.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a P.4 Blue class there are 60 pupils. 2/3 of them are girls. (b) How many girls are in the class? A: 40. 2/3 of 60 = 40 girls.
chunks.source: 2/3 of 60 = 40 girls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a P.4 Blue class there are 60 pupils. 2/3 of them are girls. (c) How many boys are in the class? A: 20. 60 − 40 = 20 boys.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Musa ate 7/15 of the cake and Namugga ate 4/15 of the cake. (a) What fraction of the cake did they eat altogether? A: 11/15. 7/15 + 4/15 = 11/15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Musa ate 7/15 of the cake and Namugga ate 4/15 of the cake. (b) What fraction of the cake remained? A: 4/15. 15/15 − 11/15 = 4/15 remained.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write the fraction that is unshaded in the triangle diagram below. A: 6/9. 6 of the 9 small triangles are not shaded.
chunks.source: 6 of the 9 small triangles are not shaded.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write the shaded fraction of the figure below. A: 3/8. 3 out of the 8 equal parts are shaded.
chunks.source: 3 out of the 8 equal parts are shaded.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Three children shared apples: Agnes got 2/5, Bob got 1/5 and Juma got the rest. (a) What fraction did Agnes and Bob get? A: 3/5. 2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Three children shared apples: Agnes got 2/5, Bob got 1/5 and Juma got the rest. (b) What fraction was given to Juma? A: 2/5. 1 − 3/5 = 2/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Agnes got 2/5, Bob got 1/5 and Juma got 2/5 of the apples. (c) If the total number of apples was 20, how many apples did Bob get? A: 4. 1/5 of 20 = 4 apples.
chunks.source: 1/5 of 20 = 4 apples.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Change 3 1/4 as an improper fraction. A: 13/4. 3 × 4 + 1 = 13, so it becomes 13/4.
chunks.source: 3 × 4 + 1 = 13, so it becomes 13/4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a class of 90 pupils, 1/3 of them are girls and the rest are boys. (a) Find the fraction of boys in the class. A: 2/3. 1 − 1/3 = 2/3 are boys.
chunks.source: 1 − 1/3 = 2/3 are boys.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a class of 90 pupils, 1/3 of them are girls and the rest are boys. (b) How many boys are there in the class? A: 60. 2/3 of 90 = 60 boys.
chunks.source: 2/3 of 90 = 60 boys.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a class of 90 pupils, 1/3 are girls (30) and the rest are boys (60). (c) How many more boys than girls are there in the class? A: 30. 60 − 30 = 30 more boys.
chunks.source: 60 − 30 = 30 more boys.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the total of 4/9 and 3/9. A: 7/9. 4/9 + 3/9 = 7/9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write 5 1/3 as an improper fraction. A: 16/3. 5 × 3 + 1 = 16, so it becomes 16/3.
chunks.source: 5 × 3 + 1 = 16, so it becomes 16/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The diagram below shows a rectangular flower garden. (a) Find the value of a. A: 10. Side a is opposite the 10m side, and opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.
chunks.source: Side a is opposite the 10m side, and opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The diagram below shows a rectangular flower garden. (a) Find the value of b. A: 8. Side b is opposite the 8m side, and opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.
chunks.source: Side b is opposite the 8m side, and opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The diagram shows a rectangular flower garden 10m by 8m. (b) Calculate the area occupied by the flower garden. A: 80. Area = 10 × 8 = 80 square metres.
chunks.source: Area = 10 × 8 = 80 square metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The diagram shows a rectangular flower garden 10m by 8m. (c) Amos walked round the garden once. What total distance did he cover altogether? A: 36. Perimeter = 10 + 8 + 10 + 8 = 36 metres.
chunks.source: Perimeter = 10 + 8 + 10 + 8 = 36 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name shape (ii) shown below. A: oval. The flat closed curved shape is an oval.
chunks.source: The flat closed curved shape is an oval.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Patel walked once round a plot with sides 10m, 5m, 20m and 5m. What distance did he cover? A: 40. 10 + 5 + 20 + 5 = 40 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the size of angle P. (A 40° angle is marked inside a right angle.) A: 50. 90 − 40 = 50 degrees.
chunks.source: 90 − 40 = 50 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the size of angle X. (A 50° angle and X are on a straight line.) A: 130. 180 − 50 = 130 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the size of angle y. (A right angle is split into 30°, 40° and y°.) A: 20. 90 − 30 − 40 = 20 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the total distance around the rectangle below (7m by 3m). A: 20. 7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name shape (ii) shown below. A: triangle. The flat shape with three straight sides is a triangle.
chunks.source: The flat shape with three straight sides is a triangle.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the rectangle figure below (10cm by 4cm). (a)(i) Find the value of a. A: 10. Side a is opposite the 10cm side, so a = 10cm.
chunks.source: Side a is opposite the 10cm side, so a = 10cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the rectangle figure below (10cm by 4cm). (a)(ii) Find the value of b. A: 4. Side b is opposite the 4cm side, so b = 4cm.
chunks.source: Side b is opposite the 4cm side, so b = 4cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the rectangle figure below (10cm by 4cm). (b) Work out the area of the figure. A: 40. Area = 10 × 4 = 40 square centimetres.
chunks.source: Area = 10 × 4 = 40 square centimetres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name the shape below. A: triangle. The shape has three straight sides, so it is a triangle.
chunks.source: The shape has three straight sides, so it is a triangle.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the perimeter of a square garden whose side is 7 metres. A: 28. 4 × 7 = 28 metres.
chunks.source: 4 × 7 = 28 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the area of the figure below. (A 3 by 3 grid of squares.) A: 9. There are 9 unit squares, so the area is 9 square units.
chunks.source: There are 9 unit squares, so the area is 9 square units.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name shape (i) shown below. A: kite. The four-sided shape with two pairs of equal adjacent sides is a kite.
chunks.source: The four-sided shape with two pairs of equal adjacent sides is a kite.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many lines of folding symmetry does the rectangle figure below have? A: 2. A rectangle folds in half lengthwise and widthwise, so 2 lines.
chunks.source: A rectangle folds in half lengthwise and widthwise, so 2 lines.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Below is a rectangle 6cm by 8cm. (a) What is the length of the rectangle? A: 8. The longer side of the rectangle is 8cm.
chunks.source: The longer side of the rectangle is 8cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Below is a rectangle 6cm by 8cm. (b) Calculate the perimeter of the rectangle. A: 28. 2 × (8 + 6) = 28cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name the shape below. A: rectangle. The four-sided shape with right angles is a rectangle.
chunks.source: The four-sided shape with right angles is a rectangle.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name the figure shown below. A: trapezium. The four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides is a trapezium.
chunks.source: The four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides is a trapezium.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name the solid shape shown below. A: cube. The shape has six equal square faces, so it is a cube.
chunks.source: The shape has six equal square faces, so it is a cube.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name shape (i) shown below. A: cone. The shape has a circular base and comes to a point, so it is a cone.
chunks.source: The shape has a circular base and comes to a point, so it is a cone.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name shape (i) shown below. A: cylinder. The solid with two circular faces is a cylinder.
chunks.source: The solid with two circular faces is a cylinder.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name shape (ii) shown below. A: cube. The solid with six square faces is a cube.
chunks.source: The solid with six square faces is a cube.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name the shape drawn below. A: cone. The shape with a circular base and a point is a cone.
chunks.source: The shape with a circular base and a point is a cone.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the shape below (6cm by 3cm by 4cm). (a) Name the shape. A: cuboid. The box-shaped solid with rectangular faces is a cuboid.
chunks.source: The box-shaped solid with rectangular faces is a cuboid.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the cuboid below. (b)(i) How many vertices does it have? A: 8. A cuboid has 8 corners (vertices).
chunks.source: A cuboid has 8 corners (vertices).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A class prefect recorded books of four girls using tallies, as shown in the table. How many books did Grace have? A: 15. Grace has three groups of five tallies, which is 15.
chunks.source: Grace has three groups of five tallies, which is 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The prefect recorded: Joan 7 books, Angella 8 books, Grace 15 books, Ritah 12 books. How many books did the prefect count altogether? A: 42. 7 + 8 + 15 + 12 = 42 books.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Nakato has 315 mangoes, Kiiza has 426 mangoes and Babirye has 246 mangoes. The table is missing one name and one number. Which person has 426 mangoes? A: Kiiza. The question says Kiiza has 426 mangoes.
chunks.source: The question says Kiiza has 426 mangoes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Nakato has 315 mangoes, Kiiza has 426 mangoes and Babirye has 246 mangoes. How many mangoes does Babirye have? A: 246. The question says Babirye has 246 mangoes.
chunks.source: The question says Babirye has 246 mangoes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is One fruit picture represents 10 fruits. How many fruit pictures are needed to represent 40 fruits? A: 4. 40 ÷ 10 = 4 pictures.
chunks.source: 40 ÷ 10 = 4 pictures.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is One fruit picture represents 10 fruits. How many fruit pictures are needed to represent 90 fruits? A: 9. 90 ÷ 10 = 9 pictures.
chunks.source: 90 ÷ 10 = 9 pictures.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is One fruit picture represents 10 fruits. How many fruit pictures are needed to represent 60 fruits? A: 6. 60 ÷ 10 = 6 pictures.
chunks.source: 60 ÷ 10 = 6 pictures.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is One ball picture represents 5 balls. How many balls are represented by the 5 ball pictures shown? A: 25. 5 × 5 = 25 balls.
chunks.source: 5 × 5 = 25 balls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The bar graph below shows the number of pupils who played games in P.4. (a) How many pupils played football? A: 30. The football bar reaches 30.
chunks.source: The football bar reaches 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The bar graph below shows the number of pupils who played games in P.4. (b) Which games are played by the same number of pupils? A: Football and Tennis. Football and Tennis both have bars reaching 30.
chunks.source: Football and Tennis both have bars reaching 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The bar graph below shows the number of pupils who played games in P.4. (c) Find the total number of pupils who played all the four games. A: 105. 30 + 20 + 25 + 30 = 105 pupils.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the pictograph below (Monday has 3 balls; Tuesday to Friday have none). (a) How many days were used for playing football? A: 1. Only Monday has balls, so football was played on 1 day.
chunks.source: Only Monday has balls, so football was played on 1 day.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the pictograph below. (b) Which day had the biggest number of balls played? A: Monday. Monday has 3 balls, more than any other day.
chunks.source: Monday has 3 balls, more than any other day.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the pictograph below. (d) Write the first day on the pictograph. A: Monday. The first row of the pictograph is Monday.
chunks.source: The first row of the pictograph is Monday.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is One book picture stands for 6 books. How many books are represented by the 4 book pictures shown? A: 24. 4 × 6 = 24 books.
chunks.source: 4 × 6 = 24 books.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The pictograph shows flowers planted each month (one flower picture = 5 flowers): February 3, March 2, April 4, May 3, June 1. (a) In which month were the most flowers planted? A: April. April has 4 flower pictures, more than any other month.
chunks.source: April has 4 flower pictures, more than any other month.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The pictograph shows flowers planted each month (one flower picture = 5 flowers). (b) How many flowers were planted in March? A: 10. 2 pictures × 5 = 10 flowers.
chunks.source: 2 pictures × 5 = 10 flowers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The pictograph shows flowers planted each month (one flower picture = 5 flowers). (c) In which two months were the same number of flowers planted? A: February and May. February and May both have 3 flower pictures.
chunks.source: February and May both have 3 flower pictures.

chunks.subject: Math
