chunks.text: Q: What is The pictograph shows flowers planted each month (one flower picture = 5 flowers): February 3, March 2, April 4, May 3, June 1. (d) Find the total number of flowers planted for all the five months. A: 65. (3 + 2 + 4 + 3 + 1) × 5 = 13 × 5 = 65 flowers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is One tree picture stands for 10 trees. How many trees are represented by the 4 tree pictures shown? A: 40. 4 × 10 = 40 trees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the pictograph below (one stool picture = 10 stools): Tom 3, Jane 5, Ali 2, Shadia 3. (a) Who has the highest number of stools? A: Jane. Jane has 5 stool pictures, more than anyone else.
chunks.source: Jane has 5 stool pictures, more than anyone else.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the pictograph below (one stool picture = 10 stools). (b) Which two pupils have the same number of stools? A: Tom and Shadia. Tom and Shadia both have 3 stool pictures.
chunks.source: Tom and Shadia both have 3 stool pictures.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the pictograph below (one stool picture = 10 stools): Tom 3, Jane 5, Ali 2, Shadia 3. (c) How many stools do they have altogether? A: 130. (3 + 5 + 2 + 3) × 10 = 13 × 10 = 130 stools.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The pictograph below shows balls of each colour (one ball picture = 2 balls): Blue 3, Yellow 1, Red 5, Green 4, Orange 2. (a) Which colour has the highest number of balls? A: Red. Red has 5 ball pictures, more than any other colour.
chunks.source: Red has 5 ball pictures, more than any other colour.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The pictograph below shows balls of each colour (one ball picture = 2 balls). (b) ____? has 2 balls. A: Yellow. Yellow has 1 picture, and 1 × 2 = 2 balls.
chunks.source: Yellow has 1 picture, and 1 × 2 = 2 balls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The pictograph below shows balls of each colour (one ball picture = 2 balls): Blue 3, Yellow 1, Red 5, Green 4, Orange 2. (c) Find the total number of balls in the school. A: 30. (3 + 1 + 5 + 4 + 2) × 2 = 15 × 2 = 30 balls.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What number is shown by the tallies below? A: 19. Three groups of five plus four singles make 19.
chunks.source: Three groups of five plus four singles make 19.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The cost of a hot dog is Sh. 4000. How many coins of 500 shillings does Tom need in order to buy the hot dog? A: 8. 4000 ÷ 500 = 8 coins.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mukasa saves money using three tins: 4 coins of 1000 shillings, 6 coins of 500 shillings and 10 coins of 200 shillings. (a) How much money does Mukasa save altogether? A: 9000. 4000 + 3000 + 2000 = 9000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mukasa saved 9000 shillings. (b) If he spends Sh. 5000 and keeps the rest, how much does he keep? A: 4000. 9000 − 5000 = 4000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Subtract correctly: Sh. 5,000 − Sh. 3,000. A: 2000. 5000 − 3000 = 2000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Opio bought 3kg of sugar at Sh. 2,000 per kg. How much was spent on sugar? A: 6000. 3 × 2000 = 6000 shillings.
chunks.source: 3 × 2000 = 6000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Opio bought 2 books at Sh. 1,000 per book. How much was spent on books? A: 2000. 2 × 1000 = 2000 shillings.
chunks.source: 2 × 1000 = 2000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Opio bought 4 rulers at Sh. 5,000 each. How much was spent on rulers? A: 20000. 4 × 5000 = 20000 shillings.
chunks.source: 4 × 5000 = 20000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Opio bought 6 sweets at Sh. 200 each. How much was spent on sweets? A: 1200. 6 × 200 = 1200 shillings.
chunks.source: 6 × 200 = 1200 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Opio spent Sh. 6000 on sugar, Sh. 2000 on books, Sh. 20000 on rulers and Sh. 1200 on sweets. Find his total expenditure. A: 29200. 6000 + 2000 + 20000 + 1200 = 29200 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A trader has Sh. 9500. He sells his mangoes for Sh. 2500. How much money does he have altogether? A: 12000. 9500 + 2500 = 12000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Supermarket prices: 1kg rice Sh. 3600, 1kg sugar Sh. 3000, 1 packet biscuits Sh. 1000, 1 bar soap Sh. 800. (c) What was the most expensive item? A: rice. Sh. 3600 is the highest price, for rice.
chunks.source: Sh. 3600 is the highest price, for rice.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Supermarket prices: 1kg rice Sh. 3600, 1kg sugar Sh. 3000, 1 packet biscuits Sh. 1000, 1 bar soap Sh. 800. (d) What was the cheapest item? A: bar of soap. Sh. 800 is the lowest price, for the bar of soap.
chunks.source: Sh. 800 is the lowest price, for the bar of soap.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Supermarket prices: 1kg rice Sh. 3600, 1 packet biscuits Sh. 1000. (e) How much did Kato pay for 2kg of rice and one packet of biscuits? A: 8200. 2 × 3600 = 7200, plus 1000 = 8200 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A mathematical set costs Sh. 3000. How much will nine similar mathematical sets cost? A: 27000. 9 × 3000 = 27000 shillings.
chunks.source: 9 × 3000 = 27000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Katwere bought a cake at Sh. 2500 and she bought bread at Sh. 2500. How much money did she spend altogether? A: 5000. 2500 + 2500 = 5000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If 1kg of sugar costs Sh. 3500, what is the cost of 2kg? A: 7000. 2 × 3500 = 7000 shillings.
chunks.source: 2 × 3500 = 7000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The cost of 3 pens is Sh. 1,500. Find the cost of one pen. A: 500. 1500 ÷ 3 = 500 shillings.
chunks.source: 1500 ÷ 3 = 500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many five hundred shilling coins can be got from 2,000 shillings? A: 4. 2000 ÷ 500 = 4 coins.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Rhona's shopping list: ruler Sh. 1,000; box file Sh. 4,500; school bag Sh. 15,000; notebook Sh. 3,000; counter book Sh. 7,000. (a) Which is the most expensive item? A: School bag. Sh. 15,000 is the highest price.
chunks.source: Sh. 15,000 is the highest price.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Rhona's shopping list. (b) Find the cost of a box file and a ruler altogether. A: 5500. 4500 + 1000 = 5500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Rhona had a five thousand shillings note and bought a box file at Sh. 4,500. (c) How much was her balance? A: 500. 5000 − 4500 = 500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A pen costs Sh. 1200. What is the cost of 3 similar pens? A: 3600. 3 × 1200 = 3600 shillings.
chunks.source: 3 × 1200 = 3600 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is P.4 pupils bought: a pen at Sh. 1200, a mathematical set at Sh. 1800, a ruler at Sh. 500. (a) What is the most expensive item from the list? A: Mathematical set. Sh. 1800 is the highest price.
chunks.source: Sh. 1800 is the highest price.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is P.4 pupils bought a pen at Sh. 1200 and a ruler at Sh. 500. (b) How much did the pupil pay for a pen and a ruler? A: 1700. 1200 + 500 = 1700 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is P.4 pupils bought: a pen at Sh. 1200, a mathematical set at Sh. 1800, a ruler at Sh. 500. (c) Work out the total cost of all the 3 items. A: 3500. 1200 + 1800 + 500 = 3500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Julius has 4 coins of five hundred shillings. How much money does Julius have altogether? A: 2000. 4 × 500 = 2000 shillings.
chunks.source: 4 × 500 = 2000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mrs. Kampi's stall: pineapple Sh. 3000, banana Sh. 300, mango Sh. 1000, tomato Sh. 500. (a) Which item costs the least amount of money? A: Banana. Sh. 300 is the lowest price, for the banana.
chunks.source: Sh. 300 is the lowest price, for the banana.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mrs. Kampi's stall: pineapple Sh. 3000, banana Sh. 300, mango Sh. 1000. (b) How much money will Mrs. Kampi get from one who buys a pineapple, a mango and a banana? A: 4300. 3000 + 1000 + 300 = 4300 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mrs. Kampi's stall: tomato Sh. 500. (c) Find the total amount of money needed to buy four tomatoes. A: 2000. 4 × 500 = 2000 shillings.
chunks.source: 4 × 500 = 2000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is After buying a geometry set for Sh. 3,700, Mukasa was given a balance of Sh. 1,300. How much money did he give the shopkeeper? A: 5000. 3700 + 1300 = 5000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write the time shown on the digital clock face (7:20) in words. A: Twenty minutes past seven. 7:20 is twenty minutes after seven o'clock.
chunks.source: 7:20 is twenty minutes after seven o'clock.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A baby is 84 days old. What is his age in weeks? A: 12. 84 ÷ 7 = 12 weeks.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Add: 4 hours 20 minutes + 3 hours 35 minutes. A: 7 hours 55 minutes. 4 + 3 = 7 hours and 20 + 35 = 55 minutes.
chunks.source: 4 + 3 = 7 hours and 20 + 35 = 55 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Tell the time shown on clock (a). A: Nine o'clock. The short hand points at 9 and the long hand at 12, so it is nine o'clock.
chunks.source: The short hand points at 9 and the long hand at 12, so it is nine o'clock.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Tell the time shown on clock (b). A: Half past three. The short hand is at 3 and the long hand at 6, so it is half past three.
chunks.source: The short hand is at 3 and the long hand at 6, so it is half past three.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Tell the time shown on the clock face below. A: A quarter past seven. The short hand is past 7 and the long hand is at 3, so it is a quarter past seven.
chunks.source: The short hand is past 7 and the long hand is at 3, so it is a quarter past seven.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is (a) Express 4 weeks in days. A: 28. 4 × 7 = 28 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is (d) Write the fifth month of the year. A: May. The months go January, February, March, April, May.
chunks.source: The months go January, February, March, April, May.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write the time shown on the clock face below. (The clock uses Roman numerals.) A: Twenty minutes past eight. The short hand is past 8 and the long hand is at 4, so it is twenty minutes past eight.
chunks.source: The short hand is past 8 and the long hand is at 4, so it is twenty minutes past eight.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Kamau spent 42 days in Kenya. How many weeks did he spend in Kenya? A: 6. 42 ÷ 7 = 6 weeks.
chunks.source: 42 ÷ 7 = 6 weeks.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Tell the time shown on the clock below. A: Ten minutes past six. The short hand is past 6 and the long hand is at 2, so it is ten minutes past six.
chunks.source: The short hand is past 6 and the long hand is at 2, so it is ten minutes past six.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If 60 minutes = 1 hour, how many hours are there in 180 minutes? A: 3. 180 ÷ 60 = 3 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 7 weeks 3 days + 5 weeks 2 days. A: 12 weeks 5 days. 7 + 5 = 12 weeks and 3 + 2 = 5 days.
chunks.source: 7 + 5 = 12 weeks and 3 + 2 = 5 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 6 weeks 3 days + 1 week 5 days. A: 8 weeks 1 day. 6 + 1 = 7 weeks and 3 + 5 = 8 days = 1 week 1 day, so 8 weeks 1 day.
chunks.source: 6 + 1 = 7 weeks and 3 + 5 = 8 days = 1 week 1 day, so 8 weeks 1 day.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many days are there in 4 weeks? A: 28. 4 × 7 = 28 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 6 hours 30 minutes + 2 hours 40 minutes. A: 9 hours 10 minutes. 6 + 2 = 8 hours and 30 + 40 = 70 minutes = 1 hour 10 minutes, so 9 hours 10 minutes.
chunks.source: 6 + 2 = 8 hours and 30 + 40 = 70 minutes = 1 hour 10 minutes, so 9 hours 10 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many hours are there in 120 minutes? A: 2. 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Tell the morning time shown on the clock face below. A: A quarter past three. The short hand is past 3 and the long hand is at 3, so it is a quarter past three.
chunks.source: The short hand is past 3 and the long hand is at 3, so it is a quarter past three.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write the month of the year with the least number of days. A: February. February has 28 days (29 in a leap year), fewer than any other month.
chunks.source: February has 28 days (29 in a leap year), fewer than any other month.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Express 2 weeks to days. A: 14. 2 × 7 = 14 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is (a) How many minutes make one hour? A: 60. One hour has 60 minutes.
chunks.source: One hour has 60 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is (b) Tell the time shown on the clock below. A: Half past twelve. The short hand is at 12 and the long hand at 6, so it is half past twelve.
chunks.source: The short hand is at 12 and the long hand at 6, so it is half past twelve.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Convert 5 weeks into days. A: 35. 5 × 7 = 35 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a food store there are three bags: rice 13kg, posho 15kg and millet 12kg. Find the total mass of the three bags in kilogrammes. A: 40. 13 + 15 + 12 = 40 kilogrammes.
chunks.source: 13 + 15 + 12 = 40 kilogrammes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Container A holds 6000 litres and container B holds 4000 litres. Write the difference in litres of the two containers in words. A: Two thousand litres. 6000 − 4000 = 2000 litres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Subtract: 7 litres 700 millilitres − 2 litres 500 millilitres. A: 5L 200mL. 7L − 2L = 5L and 700mL − 500mL = 200mL.
chunks.source: 7L − 2L = 5L and 700mL − 500mL = 200mL.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Peter weighs 39kg and Florence weighs 21kg. Who is heavier? A: Peter. 39kg is more than 21kg, so Peter is heavier.
chunks.source: 39kg is more than 21kg, so Peter is heavier.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the map: Home — 100m — Borehole — 200m — (300m) — Shop. (a) How far is the borehole (the water source) from the home? A: 100. The map shows 100 metres from home to the borehole.
chunks.source: The map shows 100 metres from home to the borehole.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the map: Home — 100m — Borehole — 200m + 300m — Shop. (b) Write the direct distance from the borehole to the shop in words. A: Five hundred metres. 200 + 300 = 500 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the map: Home — 100m — Borehole — 200m + 300m — Shop. (c) What distance will one cover travelling from the home to the shop via the borehole? A: 600. 100 + 200 + 300 = 600 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many half-litre cups are in a 5-litre jerrycan? A: 10. 5 ÷ 1/2 = 10 cups.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 5m 35cm + 1m 14cm. A: 6m 49cm. 5 + 1 = 6m and 35 + 14 = 49cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The diagram shows the road between three homes in a triangle: Henry's to Kato's 18m, Henry's to Mary's 13m, Kato's to Mary's 20m. (a) Find the distance Henry will cover if he goes to Mary's home and continues to Kato's home. A: 33. 13 + 20 = 33 metres.
chunks.source: 13 + 20 = 33 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The diagram shows the road between three homes in a triangle: Henry's to Kato's 18m, Henry's to Mary's 13m, Kato's to Mary's 20m. (b) If Henry's cow walks around the three homes, calculate in metres the distance covered by the cow. A: 51. 18 + 13 + 20 = 51 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Take away: 363 litres − 139 litres = ____? litres. A: 224. 363 − 139 = 224 litres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Change 7kg to grams. A: 7000. 1kg = 1000g, so 7kg = 7000g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mugenyi weighs 24kg and Mangeni weighs 8kg heavier than Mugenyi. (a) What is Mangeni's weight? A: 32. 24 + 8 = 32kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mugenyi weighs 24kg and Mangeni weighs 32kg. (b) Find their total weight. A: 56. 24 + 32 = 56kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Express 3 metres to centimetres. A: 300. 1m = 100cm, so 3m = 300cm.
chunks.source: 1m = 100cm, so 3m = 300cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Moses weighs 70kg and Sarah weighs 60kg. By how many kilogrammes is Moses heavier than Sarah? A: 10. 70 − 60 = 10kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the map below: Greenhill Buwaate — 12km — Kireka — 8km — Kibuli Mosque — 5km — Kampala city. (a) How far is Kireka from Greenhill Buwaate? A: 12. The map shows 12km between them.
chunks.source: The map shows 12km between them.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the map below. (c) Find the distance from Kibuli Mosque to Greenhill Buwaate via Kireka. A: 20. 8 + 12 = 20km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Simplify: 4b + 2b − b. A: 5b. 4b + 2b = 6b, and 6b − b = 5b.
chunks.source: 4b + 2b = 6b, and 6b − b = 5b.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out and fill in correctly: ____? + 6 = 13. A: 7. 13 − 6 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve the equation: P − 4 = 7. A: 11. 7 + 4 = 11, so P = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve the equation: m + 5 = 9. A: 4. 9 − 5 = 4, so m = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve the equation: y/3 = 2. A: 6. 2 × 3 = 6, so y = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out the value of a: a × 4 = 12. A: 3. 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so a = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Simplify: 4e + e. A: 5e. 4e + 1e = 5e.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve: g + 4 = 8. A: 4. 8 − 4 = 4, so g = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve: e − 3 = 7. A: 10. 7 + 3 = 10, so e = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve: 2z = 18. A: 9. 18 ÷ 2 = 9, so z = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve: m + 4 = 9. A: 5. 9 − 4 = 5, so m = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that a = 2, b = 4 and c = 5, find the value of a + b + c. A: 11. 2 + 4 + 5 = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that a = 2, b = 4 and c = 5, find the value of c − a. A: 3. 5 − 2 = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the missing number in the box: 312 − ____? = 301. A: 11. 312 − 301 = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Think of a number, subtract 9 from it and the difference is 12. What is the number? A: 21. 12 + 9 = 21.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Simplify: 9 cups + 6 cups − 4 cups. A: 11 cups. 9 + 6 − 4 = 11 cups.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve: x + 3 = 7. A: 4. 7 − 3 = 4, so x = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the number in the box: ____? − 3 = 97. A: 100. 97 + 3 = 100.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Simplify: 4 cats + 3 cats + 2 cats. A: 9 cats. 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 cats.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the missing number: ____? + 10 = 19. A: 9. 19 − 10 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the missing number: 6 × ____? = 18. A: 3. 18 ÷ 6 = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the missing number: ____? ÷ 2 = 10. A: 20. 10 × 2 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Fill the box with the missing number: ____? − 12 = 18. A: 30. 18 + 12 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 35 in words. ___ A: Thirty five. 35 = 30 + 5, which is written as 'Thirty five'.
chunks.source: 35 = 30 + 5, which is written as 'Thirty five'.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Anita had shs. 1,000 and bought 2 pencils at shs. 300 each. How much money did she remain with? shs. ___ A: 400. 2 pencils cost 2 x shs. 300 = shs. 600. Then shs. 1,000 - shs. 600 = shs. 400.
chunks.source: 2 pencils cost 2 x shs. 300 = shs. 600. Then shs. 1,000 - shs. 600 = shs. 400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the missing number in the sequence: 20, 24, 28, 32, ___. ___ A: 36. Each number is 4 more than the one before it: 32 + 4 = 36.
chunks.source: Each number is 4 more than the one before it: 32 + 4 = 36.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Convert 8 kilograms into grammes. ___ A: 8000. 1 kg = 1,000 g, so 8 kg = 8 x 1,000 = 8,000 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Reduce 20/30 to its simplest form. ___ A: 2/3. Divide the top and bottom by 10: 20/30 = 2/3.
chunks.source: Divide the top and bottom by 10: 20/30 = 2/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A basket contains 20 mangoes and 3/5 of them are ripe. How many mangoes are ripe? ___ A: 12. 20 divided by 5 = 4, and 4 x 3 = 12 ripe mangoes.
chunks.source: 20 divided by 5 = 4, and 4 x 3 = 12 ripe mangoes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set A is made up of the days of the week that begin with the letter S. How many members are in set A? A: 2. Saturday and Sunday begin with S, so set A has 2 members.
chunks.source: Saturday and Sunday begin with S, so set A has 2 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set K = {c, a, t} and L = {a, b, c, d}. List the members of K and L that are common to both sets (K ∩ L). ___ A: a, c. The letters found in both sets are a and c.
chunks.source: The letters found in both sets are a and c.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 2, 5, 8, 11, ___. ___ A: 14. Each number is 3 more than the one before it: 11 + 3 = 14.
chunks.source: Each number is 3 more than the one before it: 11 + 3 = 14.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a test, Joseph got 15 marks out of 25 marks. How many marks did he fail? ___ A: 10. 25 - 15 = 10 marks failed.
chunks.source: 25 - 15 = 10 marks failed.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: One tomato costs shs. 300. How much will Francis pay for 4 similar tomatoes? shs. ___ A: 1200. 4 x shs. 300 = shs. 1,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many days are in 4 weeks? ___ A: 28. 1 week = 7 days, so 4 x 7 = 28 days.
chunks.source: 1 week = 7 days, so 4 x 7 = 28 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a factor of 18? A: 6. 18 ÷ 6 = 3 with no remainder, so 6 is a factor of 18.
chunks.source: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 with no remainder, so 6 is a factor of 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The teacher gave 2/6 of a pancake to her daughter and 3/6 to her son. What fraction of the pancake did the two children get altogether? ___ A: 5/6. 2/6 + 3/6 = 5/6 of the pancake.
chunks.source: 2/6 + 3/6 = 5/6 of the pancake.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If P = 10, m = 6 and q = 3, find the value of P × q. ___ A: 30. P × q = 10 × 3 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Okello is 10 years old and 100 cm tall. Akena is 8 years old and 110 cm tall. Who is taller? ___ A: Akena. Akena is 110 cm tall and Okello is 100 cm tall, so Akena is taller.
chunks.source: Akena is 110 cm tall and Okello is 100 cm tall, so Akena is taller.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the product of 13 and 3. ___ A: 39. 13 x 3 = 39. (10 x 3 = 30 and 3 x 3 = 9, then 30 + 9 = 39.)

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use 'greater than' or 'less than' to complete the statement: 1/4 ___ 1/2. A: less than. 1/4 is smaller than 1/2, so the answer is 'less than'.
chunks.source: 1/4 is smaller than 1/2, so the answer is 'less than'.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many months are in 4 years? ___ A: 48. 1 year = 12 months, so 4 x 12 = 48 months.
chunks.source: 1 year = 12 months, so 4 x 12 = 48 months.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 2/3 of 24 mangoes? ___ A: 16. 24 ÷ 3 = 8, and 8 x 2 = 16 mangoes.
chunks.source: 24 ÷ 3 = 8, and 8 x 2 = 16 mangoes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 35 in words. ____? A: Thirty five. 35 = 30 + 5, which is written as 'Thirty five'.
chunks.source: 35 = 30 + 5, which is written as 'Thirty five'.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Anita had shs. 1,000 and bought 2 pencils at shs. 300 each. How much money did she remain with? shs. ____? A: 400. 2 pencils cost 2 x shs. 300 = shs. 600. Then shs. 1,000 - shs. 600 = shs. 400.
chunks.source: 2 pencils cost 2 x shs. 300 = shs. 600. Then shs. 1,000 - shs. 600 = shs. 400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the missing number in the sequence: 20, 24, 28, 32, ____?. ____? A: 36. Each number is 4 more than the one before it: 32 + 4 = 36.
chunks.source: Each number is 4 more than the one before it: 32 + 4 = 36.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Convert 8 kilograms into grammes. ____? A: 8000. 1 kg = 1,000 g, so 8 kg = 8 x 1,000 = 8,000 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Reduce 20/30 to its simplest form. ____? A: 2/3. Divide the top and bottom by 10: 20/30 = 2/3.
chunks.source: Divide the top and bottom by 10: 20/30 = 2/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A basket contains 20 mangoes and 3/5 of them are ripe. How many mangoes are ripe? ____? A: 12. 20 divided by 5 = 4, and 4 x 3 = 12 ripe mangoes.
chunks.source: 20 divided by 5 = 4, and 4 x 3 = 12 ripe mangoes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set K = {c, a, t} and L = {a, b, c, d}. List the members of K and L that are common to both sets (K ∩ L). ____? A: a, c. The letters found in both sets are a and c.
chunks.source: The letters found in both sets are a and c.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 2, 5, 8, 11, ____?. ____? A: 14. Each number is 3 more than the one before it: 11 + 3 = 14.
chunks.source: Each number is 3 more than the one before it: 11 + 3 = 14.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a test, Joseph got 15 marks out of 25 marks. How many marks did he fail? ____? A: 10. 25 - 15 = 10 marks failed.
chunks.source: 25 - 15 = 10 marks failed.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: One tomato costs shs. 300. How much will Francis pay for 4 similar tomatoes? shs. ____? A: 1200. 4 x shs. 300 = shs. 1,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many days are in 4 weeks? ____? A: 28. 1 week = 7 days, so 4 x 7 = 28 days.
chunks.source: 1 week = 7 days, so 4 x 7 = 28 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The teacher gave 2/6 of a pancake to her daughter and 3/6 to her son. What fraction of the pancake did the two children get altogether? ____? A: 5/6. 2/6 + 3/6 = 5/6 of the pancake.
chunks.source: 2/6 + 3/6 = 5/6 of the pancake.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If P = 10, m = 6 and q = 3, find the value of P × q. ____? A: 30. P × q = 10 × 3 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Okello is 10 years old and 100 cm tall. Akena is 8 years old and 110 cm tall. Who is taller? ____? A: Akena. Akena is 110 cm tall and Okello is 100 cm tall, so Akena is taller.
chunks.source: Akena is 110 cm tall and Okello is 100 cm tall, so Akena is taller.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the product of 13 and 3. ____? A: 39. 13 x 3 = 39. (10 x 3 = 30 and 3 x 3 = 9, then 30 + 9 = 39.)

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many months are in 4 years? ____? A: 48. 1 year = 12 months, so 4 x 12 = 48 months.
chunks.source: 1 year = 12 months, so 4 x 12 = 48 months.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 2/3 of 24 mangoes? ____? A: 16. 24 ÷ 3 = 8, and 8 x 2 = 16 mangoes.
chunks.source: 24 ÷ 3 = 8, and 8 x 2 = 16 mangoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one domestic animal that gives us milk. A: cow. A cow is a domestic animal that gives us milk.
chunks.source: A cow is a domestic animal that gives us milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What deficiency disease causes swelling of the neck? A: goitre. Goitre is caused by lack of iodine, and it makes the neck swell.
chunks.source: Goitre is caused by lack of iodine, and it makes the neck swell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do most people in the city get food? A: They buy it from markets and shops. People in towns do not farm, so they buy their food from markets and shops.
chunks.source: People in towns do not farm, so they buy their food from markets and shops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is sugar important in ORS? A: It gives the body energy and helps it absorb water and salts. Sugar in ORS gives energy and helps the body take in the water and salts it lost.
chunks.source: Sugar in ORS gives energy and helps the body take in the water and salts it lost.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are flowers useful to bees? A: Bees get nectar (food) from flowers. Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers, which is their food.
chunks.source: Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers, which is their food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important to wash hands after eating food? A: To remove germs and dirt and prevent diseases. Washing hands removes germs that can make us sick.
chunks.source: Washing hands removes germs that can make us sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are ears useful to a dog? A: They are used for hearing. A dog uses its ears to hear sounds around it.
chunks.source: A dog uses its ears to hear sounds around it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which component of soil makes the soil fertile? A: humus. Humus is decayed plant and animal matter that makes soil fertile.
chunks.source: Humus is decayed plant and animal matter that makes soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of plant roots. Identify any one plant with such roots. A: maize. Maize has fibrous roots, like the many thin roots shown in the diagram.
chunks.source: Maize has fibrous roots, like the many thin roots shown in the diagram.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger of diseases to people. A: They can cause death. Diseases make people weak and can kill them.
chunks.source: Diseases make people weak and can kill them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one way farmers can stop rats from destroying stored food. A: Store food in tightly closed containers. Rats cannot reach food kept in sealed tins or containers.
chunks.source: Rats cannot reach food kept in sealed tins or containers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are termites similar to wasps in the way they live? A: They live in colonies (groups). Both termites and wasps are social insects that live together in colonies.
chunks.source: Both termites and wasps are social insects that live together in colonies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of controlling houseflies at home. A: Keep the home clean and cover food. Houseflies breed in dirt, so a clean home with covered food keeps them away.
chunks.source: Houseflies breed in dirt, so a clean home with covered food keeps them away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the importance of a micropyle to a bean seed? A: It lets water (and air) into the seed during germination. The micropyle is a tiny hole through which water enters the seed so it can germinate.
chunks.source: The micropyle is a tiny hole through which water enters the seed so it can germinate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which food value is needed most by people who make bricks? A: carbohydrates. Brick makers do hard work, so they need carbohydrates, the energy-giving food value.
chunks.source: Brick makers do hard work, so they need carbohydrates, the energy-giving food value.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do first aiders need a first aid box? A: To keep first aid items for giving quick first aid. A first aid box keeps bandages and other items ready for emergencies.
chunks.source: A first aid box keeps bandages and other items ready for emergencies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can P.4 children keep their classroom clean? A: By sweeping it daily and putting rubbish in the dustbin. Sweeping every day and using a dustbin keeps the classroom clean.
chunks.source: Sweeping every day and using a dustbin keeps the classroom clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one importance of banana fibres to school children. A: They are used to make ropes and balls. School children use banana fibres to make ropes, balls and mats.
chunks.source: School children use banana fibres to make ropes, balls and mats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for people to preserve food? A: To keep it for future use and prevent hunger. Preserved food lasts longer, so people have food even in the dry season.
chunks.source: Preserved food lasts longer, so people have food even in the dry season.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the item below. Give the importance of the item to a school child. A: They protect the feet and keep them dry in wet, muddy weather. Gumboots keep a school child's feet dry and safe in rain and mud.
chunks.source: Gumboots keep a school child's feet dry and safe in rain and mud.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one effect of drought to people. A: It causes hunger and famine. Drought dries crops and water sources, so people go hungry.
chunks.source: Drought dries crops and water sources, so people go hungry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of killing germs and vectors in our clothes. A: Ironing the clothes. The heat of ironing kills germs and vectors hiding in clothes.
chunks.source: The heat of ironing kills germs and vectors hiding in clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one childhood immunisable disease in our community. A: polio. Polio is one of the diseases children are immunised against.
chunks.source: Polio is one of the diseases children are immunised against.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the human body organ. Name the body organ shown. A: stomach. The diagram shows the stomach, the bag-like organ where food is churned.
chunks.source: The diagram shows the stomach, the bag-like organ where food is churned.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one function of the above part of the body. A: It digests food (churns and mixes food with digestive juices). The stomach churns food and mixes it with juices to digest it.
chunks.source: The stomach churns food and mixes it with juices to digest it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do some schools have gardens? A: To grow food and teach pupils farming. School gardens give food and help pupils learn how to farm.
chunks.source: School gardens give food and help pupils learn how to farm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which instrument is used by health workers to find the body temperature of a patient? A: thermometer. A thermometer measures how hot or cold the body is.
chunks.source: A thermometer measures how hot or cold the body is.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one natural change in the environment. A: rainfall. Rainfall is a change in nature that happens on its own.
chunks.source: Rainfall is a change in nature that happens on its own.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one group of people who control the flow of traffic on our roads. A: traffic police. Traffic police direct cars and people on the roads.
chunks.source: Traffic police direct cars and people on the roads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should people eat a balanced diet? A: To get all food values and stay healthy. A balanced diet has every food value the body needs to grow well.
chunks.source: A balanced diet has every food value the body needs to grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the animal. How is part X useful to the animal above? A: It helps the fish to swim. Part X is the tail, which pushes the fish through water when swimming.
chunks.source: Part X is the tail, which pushes the fish through water when swimming.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A garden tool used for peeling is called a ___. A: knife. A knife is the garden tool used for peeling fruits and food.
chunks.source: A knife is the garden tool used for peeling fruits and food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the difference between air and wind. A: Air is still, while wind is moving air. Wind is simply air that is moving from one place to another.
chunks.source: Wind is simply air that is moving from one place to another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one way of saving energy at home. A: Switch off lights and appliances that are not in use. Switching off unused lights saves electricity at home.
chunks.source: Switching off unused lights saves electricity at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of caring for toilets at school. A: Clean them daily with water and disinfectant. Daily cleaning keeps school toilets free from germs and smell.
chunks.source: Daily cleaning keeps school toilets free from germs and smell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which sense enables people to tell that there is sugar in tea? A: the sense of taste (tongue). The tongue tastes the sweetness of sugar in tea.
chunks.source: The tongue tastes the sweetness of sugar in tea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the item below. How is the item useful to people? A: It protects the head from strong sunshine. A cap shades the head and face from hot sunshine.
chunks.source: A cap shades the head and face from hot sunshine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do dogs move from one place to another? A: To look for food, water and shelter. Dogs move around searching for food, water and a safe place.
chunks.source: Dogs move around searching for food, water and a safe place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the importance of earthworms in the soil. A: They make the soil fertile and let air into it. Earthworms burrow through soil, letting in air, and their droppings add humus.
chunks.source: Earthworms burrow through soil, letting in air, and their droppings add humus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one local material that is used to build permanent houses. A: bricks. Bricks are local materials used to build strong, permanent houses.
chunks.source: Bricks are local materials used to build strong, permanent houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two dangers of accidents to people. A: They cause death; they cause injuries and disability. Accidents can kill people or leave them injured and disabled.
chunks.source: Accidents can kill people or leave them injured and disabled.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State two ways in which people can prevent accidents at home. A: Keep sharp objects out of children's reach; handle fire and hot things carefully. Keeping dangers away from children and being careful with fire prevents home accidents.
chunks.source: Keeping dangers away from children and being careful with fire prevents home accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How many teeth make up the first set? A: 20. The first set of teeth, called milk teeth, is made up of 20 teeth.
chunks.source: The first set of teeth, called milk teeth, is made up of 20 teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of teeth when eating food. A: To cut, bite and chew (break food into small pieces). Teeth break food into small pieces so it is easy to swallow and digest.
chunks.source: Teeth break food into small pieces so it is easy to swallow and digest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one disorder of teeth. A: tooth decay (cavities). Tooth decay is a disorder where teeth develop holes and pain.
chunks.source: Tooth decay is a disorder where teeth develop holes and pain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way people at home can take care of their teeth. A: Brush the teeth every day. Brushing daily removes food remains that cause tooth decay.
chunks.source: Brushing daily removes food remains that cause tooth decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is photosynthesis? A: The process by which green plants make their own food using sunlight. In photosynthesis, green plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food.
chunks.source: In photosynthesis, green plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of a plant carries out photosynthesis? A: the leaves. Leaves contain chlorophyll, so they are the parts that carry out photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Leaves contain chlorophyll, so they are the parts that carry out photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is chlorophyll important during photosynthesis? A: It traps (absorbs) sunlight needed for photosynthesis. Chlorophyll is the green colouring that traps sunlight for the plant to make food.
chunks.source: Chlorophyll is the green colouring that traps sunlight for the plant to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from photosynthesis, name one other process that takes place in plants. A: transpiration. Plants also carry out transpiration, the loss of water through leaves.
chunks.source: Plants also carry out transpiration, the loss of water through leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any two processes involved in the formation of rain. A: evaporation; condensation. Water evaporates into vapour, then condenses into clouds that bring rain.
chunks.source: Water evaporates into vapour, then condenses into clouds that bring rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is too much rainfall dangerous to our environment? A: It causes floods that destroy crops, houses and roads. Heavy rain brings floods which wash away crops and damage property.
chunks.source: Heavy rain brings floods which wash away crops and damage property.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of the sun in rain formation. A: It heats water, causing evaporation. The sun's heat turns water in lakes and rivers into vapour.
chunks.source: The sun's heat turns water in lakes and rivers into vapour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any two diseases that result from poor feeding. A: kwashiorkor; marasmus. Kwashiorkor and marasmus are deficiency diseases caused by poor feeding.
chunks.source: Kwashiorkor and marasmus are deficiency diseases caused by poor feeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one sign of poor feeding among children. A: A thin body (or swollen belly, brown hair). Poorly fed children become very thin or develop swollen bellies.
chunks.source: Poorly fed children become very thin or develop swollen bellies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one way people in your family get food. A: By buying it from the market (or by farming). Families get food by buying from markets or growing it in gardens.
chunks.source: Families get food by buying from markets or growing it in gardens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the life cycle of a butterfly. Name stage marked L on the diagram. A: pupa (chrysalis). Stage L is the pupa, the resting stage inside a cocoon-like case.
chunks.source: Stage L is the pupa, the resting stage inside a cocoon-like case.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is stage N dangerous to people? A: The eggs hatch into caterpillars that destroy people's crops. Stage N is the egg; the caterpillars that hatch from them eat and destroy crops.
chunks.source: Stage N is the egg; the caterpillars that hatch from them eat and destroy crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the stages above is useful to farmers? A: Stage M (the adult butterfly) because it pollinates crops. The adult butterfly moves pollen between flowers, helping crops form fruits.
chunks.source: The adult butterfly moves pollen between flowers, helping crops form fruits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any other insect that undergoes a life cycle like the one above. A: housefly (or mosquito, bee). Like the butterfly, the housefly undergoes complete metamorphosis: egg, larva, pupa, adult.
chunks.source: Like the butterfly, the housefly undergoes complete metamorphosis: egg, larva, pupa, adult.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any two ways water gets contaminated at home. A: Using dirty containers; leaving water uncovered. Dirty containers and uncovered water let germs get into drinking water.
chunks.source: Dirty containers and uncovered water let germs get into drinking water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one danger of drinking contaminated water. A: It causes water-borne diseases like cholera and typhoid. Germs in dirty water cause diseases such as cholera, typhoid and diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Germs in dirty water cause diseases such as cholera, typhoid and diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one method you would use to make water safe for drinking. A: boiling. Boiling kills the germs in water, making it safe to drink.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs in water, making it safe to drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is fuel? A: Anything that is burnt to produce heat or energy. Fuel, like firewood or charcoal, is burnt to give heat and energy.
chunks.source: Fuel, like firewood or charcoal, is burnt to give heat and energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two fuels commonly found in the kitchen. A: firewood; charcoal. Firewood and charcoal are common kitchen fuels used for cooking.
chunks.source: Firewood and charcoal are common kitchen fuels used for cooking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one way of saving energy at home. A: Use energy-saving bulbs (or switch off unused lights). Energy-saving bulbs use less electricity at home.
chunks.source: Energy-saving bulbs use less electricity at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a wild bird. A: eagle (or kite, weaver bird). An eagle is a wild bird that lives in forests and hunts for food.
chunks.source: An eagle is a wild bird that lives in forests and hunts for food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one domestic animal which does not give us meat. A: donkey. A donkey is kept for carrying loads, not for meat.
chunks.source: A donkey is kept for carrying loads, not for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any two ways of caring for domestic animals. A: Feed them well; treat them when they are sick. Domestic animals need good feeding and treatment when sick.
chunks.source: Domestic animals need good feeding and treatment when sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the second layer of soil profile. A: sub soil. Below the top soil lies the second layer, called sub soil.
chunks.source: Below the top soil lies the second layer, called sub soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is top soil suitable for plant growth? A: It contains a lot of humus, so it is fertile. Top soil is rich in humus, which feeds growing plants.
chunks.source: Top soil is rich in humus, which feeds growing plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any two human activities that can damage soil. A: deforestation; overgrazing (or bush burning). Cutting down trees and overgrazing leave soil bare and easily washed away.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees and overgrazing leave soil bare and easily washed away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is AIDS dangerous to people? A: It kills people and has no cure. AIDS weakens the body's defence and has no cure, so it kills.
chunks.source: AIDS weakens the body's defence and has no cure, so it kills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two ways of caring for AIDS patients. A: Feed them well; give them their medicine and love. AIDS patients need good food, medicine and comfort.
chunks.source: AIDS patients need good food, medicine and comfort.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one way pupils can protect themselves from HIV/AIDS. A: Abstain from sex (or avoid sharing sharp objects). Pupils protect themselves by abstaining from sex and not sharing sharp objects.
chunks.source: Pupils protect themselves by abstaining from sex and not sharing sharp objects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the items used to keep our bodies clean. Name any one part of the body that is cared for using item marked C. A: the teeth (mouth). Item C is a toothbrush, used to clean the teeth.
chunks.source: Item C is a toothbrush, used to clean the teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one hygiene activity that is done using item marked A. A: bathing (washing the body). Item A is a sponge, used for bathing the body.
chunks.source: Item A is a sponge, used for bathing the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is item B useful to people? A: It is used for shaving (cutting hair). Item B is a razor blade, used for shaving hair.
chunks.source: Item B is a razor blade, used for shaving hair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one source of item marked A. A: the sea. Item A is a sponge; natural sponges are sea animals got from the sea.
chunks.source: Item A is a sponge; natural sponges are sea animals got from the sea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the part of a flower to the correct function. A: stigma: receives pollen grains; ovary: holds the ovules; anthers: produce pollen grains; petals: attract pollinators. The stigma receives pollen, the ovary holds ovules, anthers make pollen and petals attract pollinators.
chunks.source: The stigma receives pollen, the ovary holds ovules, anthers make pollen and petals attract pollinators.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of a wind vane. A: It shows the direction of wind. A wind vane points to where the wind is coming from.
chunks.source: A wind vane points to where the wind is coming from.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of an anemometer. A: It measures the speed of wind. An anemometer tells how fast the wind is blowing.
chunks.source: An anemometer tells how fast the wind is blowing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should a rain gauge be placed in an open place? A: So that buildings and trees do not block rain from entering it. In the open, the rain gauge collects all the rain that falls.
chunks.source: In the open, the rain gauge collects all the rain that falls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one activity that farmers can do in windy weather. A: winnowing. Farmers use wind to winnow, blowing away chaff from grain.
chunks.source: Farmers use wind to winnow, blowing away chaff from grain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the experiment. What is the experiment about? A: To show that air (oxygen) is needed for burning. Covering a burning candle with a glass shows that burning needs air.
chunks.source: Covering a burning candle with a glass shows that burning needs air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What will happen to the candle after some time? A: The flame will go out (stop burning). Once the oxygen in the glass is used up, the candle stops burning.
chunks.source: Once the oxygen in the glass is used up, the candle stops burning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any other process that uses the same gas as burning. A: breathing (respiration). Like burning, breathing uses oxygen from air.
chunks.source: Like burning, breathing uses oxygen from air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which gas can be used to stop things from burning? A: carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it puts out fire.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it puts out fire.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one infant immunisable disease. A: polio. Polio is one of the diseases babies are immunised against.
chunks.source: Polio is one of the diseases babies are immunised against.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the use of earthworms in the soil? A: They let air into the soil and make it fertile. Earthworms burrow through soil letting in air, and their droppings add humus.
chunks.source: Earthworms burrow through soil letting in air, and their droppings add humus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way are teeth useful during digestion of food? A: They break food into small pieces (chewing). Teeth chew food into small pieces so it is easy to swallow and digest.
chunks.source: Teeth chew food into small pieces so it is easy to swallow and digest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of seeds undergoes epigeal germination? A: bean seeds. In epigeal germination the cotyledons come above the ground, as in beans.
chunks.source: In epigeal germination the cotyledons come above the ground, as in beans.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the plant. Of what use is structure marked S to the plant? A: The leaves make food for the plant through photosynthesis. Structure S is the leaves, which trap sunlight to make food for the plant.
chunks.source: Structure S is the leaves, which trap sunlight to make food for the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does sand soil easily lose water? A: It has large particles with large air spaces, so water drains through fast. Water passes quickly through the big spaces between sand particles.
chunks.source: Water passes quickly through the big spaces between sand particles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one advantage of weeding to farmers. A: It removes weeds that compete with crops for nutrients. Weeding stops weeds from stealing water and nutrients from crops.
chunks.source: Weeding stops weeds from stealing water and nutrients from crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you help in saving electricity at home and school? A: By switching off lights and appliances when not in use. Switching off unused lights and machines saves electricity.
chunks.source: Switching off unused lights and machines saves electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a mosquito grouped under living things? A: Because it carries out life processes like breathing, feeding and reproducing. A mosquito breathes, feeds, moves and reproduces, so it is a living thing.
chunks.source: A mosquito breathes, feeds, moves and reproduces, so it is a living thing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way can you help to improve soil fertility? A: By adding manure (or mulching). Manure adds humus to soil, making it fertile.
chunks.source: Manure adds humus to soil, making it fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the bird's head. The wattle is the fleshy flap that hangs ___. A: below the beak. The wattle is the red fleshy skin hanging below the bird's beak.
chunks.source: The wattle is the red fleshy skin hanging below the bird's beak.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do plants like mangoes reduce their rate of transpiration during the dry season? A: They shed (drop) their leaves. With fewer leaves, mango trees lose less water in the dry season.
chunks.source: With fewer leaves, mango trees lose less water in the dry season.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a shed put at the top of a nursery bed? A: To protect young seedlings from strong sunshine and heavy rain. The shed shades tender seedlings from harsh sun and rain.
chunks.source: The shed shades tender seedlings from harsh sun and rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the human body organ where urine is stored before it is removed from the body. A: urinary bladder. Urine collects in the urinary bladder before it is passed out.
chunks.source: Urine collects in the urinary bladder before it is passed out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is massive cutting down of trees dangerous to our environment? A: It causes soil erosion and drought, and destroys homes of animals. Without trees, soil is washed away, rain reduces and animals lose shelter.
chunks.source: Without trees, soil is washed away, rain reduces and animals lose shelter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why would you advise poultry farmers using free range not to live near forests? A: Wild animals and birds of prey from the forest can eat the poultry. Predators like kites and wild cats from forests attack free-range birds.
chunks.source: Predators like kites and wild cats from forests attack free-range birds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger you may get for failing to wash your clothes. A: You can get skin diseases (or body odour). Dirty clothes carry germs that cause skin diseases.
chunks.source: Dirty clothes carry germs that cause skin diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way can you help in controlling diarrhea at home? A: By drinking clean boiled water (or washing hands, covering food). Clean water and clean hands stop the germs that cause diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Clean water and clean hands stop the germs that cause diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the kettle. Name the substance labeled K. A: steam (water vapour). K labels the steam rising from the boiling water in the kettle.
chunks.source: K labels the steam rising from the boiling water in the kettle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which form of energy leads to formation of substance K? A: heat energy. Heat from the stove boils the water, forming steam.
chunks.source: Heat from the stove boils the water, forming steam.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one disease spread by a vector that feeds on faeces. A: cholera (or dysentery, typhoid). The housefly feeds on faeces and spreads cholera to our food.
chunks.source: The housefly feeds on faeces and spreads cholera to our food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one danger of polio to infants. A: It causes lameness (paralysis) or death. Polio attacks the nerves and can leave a child's legs lame.
chunks.source: Polio attacks the nerves and can leave a child's legs lame.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do children get infected with worms? A: By eating dirty food, drinking dirty water, or walking barefoot. Worm eggs in dirty food, water or soil enter children's bodies.
chunks.source: Worm eggs in dirty food, water or soil enter children's bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one type of poultry. A: chicken (or duck, turkey). A chicken is a common type of poultry kept at home.
chunks.source: A chicken is a common type of poultry kept at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the figure. Calculate the volume of the figure. A: 24 cubic centimetres (24 cm³). Volume = length × width × height = 4 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm = 24 cm³.
chunks.source: Volume = length × width × height = 4 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm = 24 cm³.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do people eat food? A: To get energy, grow and stay healthy. Food gives the body energy to work and materials to grow.
chunks.source: Food gives the body energy to work and materials to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are people discouraged from carelessly playing with razor blades? A: They can cut and injure themselves. Razor blades are very sharp and can cause deep cuts.
chunks.source: Razor blades are very sharp and can cause deep cuts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one natural change in the environment. A: growth (or rainfall, death). Growth is a natural change that happens in living things on their own.
chunks.source: Growth is a natural change that happens in living things on their own.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The outer covering of a bean seed is called the ___. A: seed coat (testa). The seed coat (testa) covers and protects the inside of a bean seed.
chunks.source: The seed coat (testa) covers and protects the inside of a bean seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you separate passion fruit juice from its seeds? A: By sieving (filtering) it. Pouring the juice through a sieve leaves the seeds behind.
chunks.source: Pouring the juice through a sieve leaves the seeds behind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the kind of honey bee commonly found near flowers. A: worker bee. Worker bees fly from flower to flower collecting nectar.
chunks.source: Worker bees fly from flower to flower collecting nectar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it dangerous to keep poison in open places at home? A: Children and animals may swallow it and die. Poison in the open can be mistaken for food and kill.
chunks.source: Poison in the open can be mistaken for food and kill.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do farmers care for their crops during drought? A: By irrigating (watering) them (or mulching). Farmers water their crops by irrigation when there is no rain.
chunks.source: Farmers water their crops by irrigation when there is no rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Rubbish in the classroom is disposed in a ___. A: dustbin. A dustbin is the container where classroom rubbish is thrown.
chunks.source: A dustbin is the container where classroom rubbish is thrown.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one advantage of keeping records to farmers. A: It helps them know their profits and losses (plan better). Records show a farmer how the farm is doing.
chunks.source: Records show a farmer how the farm is doing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do farmers control crop pests in their gardens? A: By spraying pesticides (or weeding, crop rotation). Spraying kills the pests that attack crops.
chunks.source: Spraying kills the pests that attack crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way can children and their teachers use shadows in their environment? A: To tell time. The length and direction of shadows show the time of day.
chunks.source: The length and direction of shadows show the time of day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is a nuclear family different from an extended family? A: A nuclear family has only parents and children, while an extended family includes other relatives. Extended families add grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins.
chunks.source: Extended families add grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can crop farmers make good use of wind? A: For winnowing (separating grain from chaff). Wind blows away light chaff, leaving clean grain.
chunks.source: Wind blows away light chaff, leaving clean grain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do animals make movements? A: To look for food, water, shelter and mates, and to escape danger. Animals move to find what they need and to run from danger.
chunks.source: Animals move to find what they need and to run from danger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two examples of domestic animals. A: cow; goat. Cows and goats are domestic animals kept at home.
chunks.source: Cows and goats are domestic animals kept at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two insects eaten by people. A: white ants (termites); grasshoppers. In Uganda, people eat roasted white ants and grasshoppers.
chunks.source: In Uganda, people eat roasted white ants and grasshoppers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the internal parts of an egg. Name the part labeled K. A: albumen (egg white). K points to the albumen, the clear white part of the egg.
chunks.source: K points to the albumen, the clear white part of the egg.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part labeled X. A: yolk. X points to the yolk, the yellow part that feeds the growing chick.
chunks.source: X points to the yolk, the yellow part that feeds the growing chick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part of the egg that develops into a chick is the ___. A: embryo. The tiny embryo on the yolk grows into the chick.
chunks.source: The tiny embryo on the yolk grows into the chick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is structure labelled M useful to poultry farmers? A: It is the shell, which protects the inside of the egg from damage. M is the hard shell that keeps the egg safe until it hatches or is sold.
chunks.source: M is the hard shell that keeps the egg safe until it hatches or is sold.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any two breeds of rabbits. A: New Zealand White; Californian. New Zealand White and Californian are common rabbit breeds.
chunks.source: New Zealand White and Californian are common rabbit breeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one disease that affects rabbits. A: coccidiosis. Coccidiosis is a common disease that kills rabbits.
chunks.source: Coccidiosis is a common disease that kills rabbits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do farmers control rabbit diseases? A: By vaccinating them and keeping hutches clean. Vaccination and clean hutches keep rabbits healthy.
chunks.source: Vaccination and clean hutches keep rabbits healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange the sentences to describe the steps of rain formation in order. A: The sun heats water in lakes and the vegetation., Evaporation and transpiration takes place., Water vapour rises up and condenses to form nimbus clouds., The nimbus clouds become heavy and fall as rain.. First the sun heats water, then vapour rises and condenses into clouds, which fall as rain.
chunks.source: First the sun heats water, then vapour rises and condenses into clouds, which fall as rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the experiment. Which component of air supports the process in X? A: oxygen. X shows a burning candle, and burning needs oxygen.
chunks.source: X shows a burning candle, and burning needs oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why did the candle continue burning in Y? A: Because air (oxygen) could still enter under the raised glass. The glass in Y is raised, so fresh air keeps reaching the flame.
chunks.source: The glass in Y is raised, so fresh air keeps reaching the flame.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why did the candle stop burning as shown in Z? A: Because the sealed glass used up all the oxygen inside. In Z the glass is sealed, so once the oxygen is used up the flame dies.
chunks.source: In Z the glass is sealed, so once the oxygen is used up the flame dies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does the above experiment show about air? A: That air supports burning (air contains oxygen). The experiment proves that burning needs oxygen from air.
chunks.source: The experiment proves that burning needs oxygen from air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write ORS in full. A: Oral Rehydration Salts. ORS stands for Oral Rehydration Salts.
chunks.source: ORS stands for Oral Rehydration Salts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one solute used in making of ORS. A: salt (or sugar). Salt is dissolved in water when making ORS.
chunks.source: Salt is dissolved in water when making ORS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is ORS useful to a person suffering from diarrhea? A: It replaces the water and salts lost from the body. Diarrhoea removes water and salts; ORS puts them back.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea removes water and salts; ORS puts them back.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important to wash hands before preparing ORS locally? A: To avoid putting germs into the ORS. Dirty hands would contaminate the ORS with germs.
chunks.source: Dirty hands would contaminate the ORS with germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is photosynthesis? A: The process by which green plants make their own food using sunlight. Green plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food.
chunks.source: Green plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one raw material needed by plants to carry out photosynthesis. A: carbon dioxide (or water, sunlight). Plants take in carbon dioxide from air to make food.
chunks.source: Plants take in carbon dioxide from air to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write the food made by plants during photosynthesis. A: starch (glucose). Photosynthesis produces glucose, which plants store as starch.
chunks.source: Photosynthesis produces glucose, which plants store as starch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the gas released by plants during photosynthesis. A: oxygen. Plants release oxygen into the air during photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants release oxygen into the air during photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the human digestive system. Name the part labelled G. A: stomach. G points to the stomach, the bag-like organ in the digestive system.
chunks.source: G points to the stomach, the bag-like organ in the digestive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part labelled E. A: liver. E points to the liver, the large organ above the stomach.
chunks.source: E points to the liver, the large organ above the stomach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is part F useful during digestion? A: It stores bile, which breaks down fats. F is the gall bladder; it keeps bile that digests fats in food.
chunks.source: F is the gall bladder; it keeps bile that digests fats in food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you improve on the normal functioning of your digestive system? A: By eating a balanced diet and drinking enough water (and exercising). Good food, enough water and exercise keep digestion working well.
chunks.source: Good food, enough water and exercise keep digestion working well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two items found in a first aid box. A: bandage; plaster (or scissors, antiseptic). A first aid box keeps bandages and plasters for treating injuries.
chunks.source: A first aid box keeps bandages and plasters for treating injuries.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are causalities taken to hospitals or health centres? A: To get proper medical treatment. Hospitals have doctors and medicine to treat casualties properly.
chunks.source: Hospitals have doctors and medicine to treat casualties properly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you assist your friend who has fallen in a pit latrine? A: Call adults (or older people) for help immediately. A child should not enter a pit latrine but quickly call adults to rescue.
chunks.source: A child should not enter a pit latrine but quickly call adults to rescue.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the weather chart. Write one crop farming activity that may be carried out in condition A. A: planting. Condition A is rainy, which is good for planting crops.
chunks.source: Condition A is rainy, which is good for planting crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one crop farming activity that may be carried out in condition C. A: drying harvested crops (or harvesting). Condition C is sunny, good for drying crops.
chunks.source: Condition C is sunny, good for drying crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which weather condition is suitable for winnowing? A: condition B (windy). Winnowing needs wind to blow away chaff, so windy condition B suits it.
chunks.source: Winnowing needs wind to blow away chaff, so windy condition B suits it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the advantage of weather condition D to our environment. A: Clouds bring rain (and cool the environment). Condition D is cloudy, and clouds bring the rain crops need.
chunks.source: Condition D is cloudy, and clouds bring the rain crops need.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the garden tool. Identify the garden tool shown. A: sickle. The curved blade tool shown is a sickle.
chunks.source: The curved blade tool shown is a sickle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the above garden tool useful to farmers? A: It is used for cutting grass and harvesting crops. Farmers use the sickle to cut grass and harvest rice.
chunks.source: Farmers use the sickle to cut grass and harvest rice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do you care for such garden tools at home? Give two ways. A: Clean them after use; oil and sharpen them, and store in a dry place. Cleaning, oiling and safe storage keep garden tools in good condition.
chunks.source: Cleaning, oiling and safe storage keep garden tools in good condition.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the vectors to the diseases they spread. A: Tsetse fly: sleeping sickness; Housefly: cholera; Female anopheles mosquito: malaria; Rat fleas: plague. Tsetse flies spread sleeping sickness, houseflies spread cholera, female anopheles spread malaria and rat fleas spread plague.
chunks.source: Tsetse flies spread sleeping sickness, houseflies spread cholera, female anopheles spread malaria and rat fleas spread plague.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one food stuff rich in carbohydrates. A: posho (maize meal) (or rice, cassava). Posho is rich in carbohydrates, the energy-giving food value.
chunks.source: Posho is rich in carbohydrates, the energy-giving food value.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which deficiency disease can a child suffer from if he/she lacks enough carbohydrates? A: marasmus. Lack of energy foods (carbohydrates) causes marasmus.
chunks.source: Lack of energy foods (carbohydrates) causes marasmus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from carbohydrates, name other two food values required in our bodies. A: proteins; vitamins. Besides carbohydrates, our bodies need proteins and vitamins.
chunks.source: Besides carbohydrates, our bodies need proteins and vitamins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is soil erosion? A: The removal (washing away) of top soil. Soil erosion is when running water or wind carries away the top soil.
chunks.source: Soil erosion is when running water or wind carries away the top soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one cause of soil erosion. A: running water (or wind, deforestation). Fast-running water washes away top soil.
chunks.source: Fast-running water washes away top soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can erosion be controlled on a school compound? A: By planting grass and trees (or mulching). Grass and trees hold the soil so it is not washed away.
chunks.source: Grass and trees hold the soil so it is not washed away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can erosion be controlled in a garden on hilly land? A: By terracing (or contour ploughing). Terraces slow down running water on hills.
chunks.source: Terraces slow down running water on hills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the method of measuring. Which kind of objects are measured using the method shown? A: irregular objects (like stones). The displacement method measures the volume of irregular objects that sink.
chunks.source: The displacement method measures the volume of irregular objects that sink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name container marked Z. A: measuring cylinder. Z is a measuring cylinder, marked to show volume.
chunks.source: Z is a measuring cylinder, marked to show volume.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The stone displaced 20 cc of water and has a density of 3 g/cc. Calculate its mass. A: 60 grammes (60 g). Mass = density × volume = 3 g/cc × 20 cc = 60 g.
chunks.source: Mass = density × volume = 3 g/cc × 20 cc = 60 g.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one faecal disease. A: cholera (or dysentery, typhoid). Cholera is a faecal disease spread through dirty faeces.
chunks.source: Cholera is a faecal disease spread through dirty faeces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way a P.5 child can prepare eggs for eating. A: By boiling (or frying) them. Eggs can be boiled or fried before eating.
chunks.source: Eggs can be boiled or fried before eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one role of a mother in a home. A: Cooking food for the family (or caring for children). A mother cooks and cares for the children at home.
chunks.source: A mother cooks and cares for the children at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are grasshoppers dangerous to farmers? A: They eat and destroy crops. Grasshoppers feed on crop leaves, destroying farmers' harvests.
chunks.source: Grasshoppers feed on crop leaves, destroying farmers' harvests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one use of banana fibres at school. A: Making ropes (or balls, mats). Banana fibres are woven into ropes and balls at school.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are woven into ropes and balls at school.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the item drawn below. How useful is the item to people at home? A: It is used for fetching and storing water. The jerrycan is used to carry and keep water at home.
chunks.source: The jerrycan is used to carry and keep water at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the body organ used for seeing. A: the eyes. We see with our eyes.
chunks.source: We see with our eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one source of water. A: rain (or wells, rivers, springs, boreholes). Rain is a natural source of water.
chunks.source: Rain is a natural source of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of a plant is used for sucking water from the ground? A: the roots. Roots suck water and nutrients from the soil.
chunks.source: Roots suck water and nutrients from the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one animal at home that produces milk. A: cow (or goat). A cow at home gives the family milk.
chunks.source: A cow at home gives the family milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are some metallic tools painted? A: To prevent rusting. Paint covers metal so air and water cannot rust it.
chunks.source: Paint covers metal so air and water cannot rust it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which gas is needed by plants during photosynthesis? A: carbon dioxide. Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air to make food.
chunks.source: Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of shadows to people. A: They help people tell time. People use the length and direction of shadows to know the time.
chunks.source: People use the length and direction of shadows to know the time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you prevent tape worm infection? A: By eating well-cooked meat (and washing hands). Tapeworms come from half-cooked meat, so cook meat well.
chunks.source: Tapeworms come from half-cooked meat, so cook meat well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of soil which is rough and with large particles. A: sand soil. Sand soil feels rough because its particles are large.
chunks.source: Sand soil feels rough because its particles are large.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of strong wind. A: It destroys houses and crops (or spreads fire). Strong wind can blow off roofs and flatten crops.
chunks.source: Strong wind can blow off roofs and flatten crops.

chunks.subject: Science
