chunks.text: Q: Name any one agent of soil erosion. A: running water (or wind). Running water is an agent that washes soil away.
chunks.source: Running water is an agent that washes soil away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of not brushing your teeth after every meal. A: It causes tooth decay. Food remains rot teeth when not brushed off.
chunks.source: Food remains rot teeth when not brushed off.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does a stone sink when thrown in water? A: Because it is denser (heavier) than water. A stone is denser than water, so it sinks.
chunks.source: A stone is denser than water, so it sinks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one characteristic of an insect. A: It has six legs (or three body parts). Insects have six legs and three body parts.
chunks.source: Insects have six legs and three body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the garden tool below. How is the garden tool useful to farmers? A: It is used for digging and weeding. The hoe is used to dig soil and remove weeds.
chunks.source: The hoe is used to dig soil and remove weeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How many legs has a spider? A: eight. A spider has eight legs.
chunks.source: A spider has eight legs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one harmful plant in the environment. A: thorn apple (or stinging nettle). The thorn apple is a harmful, poisonous plant.
chunks.source: The thorn apple is a harmful, poisonous plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of showing that air occupies space. A: Trap air in a container, e.g. push an upside-down cup into water. Air trapped in the cup occupies space and stops water from filling it.
chunks.source: Air trapped in the cup occupies space and stops water from filling it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a perennial crop. A: coffee (or bananas, tea, mangoes). Coffee lives for many years, so it is a perennial crop.
chunks.source: Coffee lives for many years, so it is a perennial crop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one vector that breeds in water. A: mosquito. Mosquitoes lay their eggs and breed in stagnant water.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes lay their eggs and breed in stagnant water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one thing made out of clay at home. A: a pot (or cup, plate, stove). Clay is moulded into pots used at home.
chunks.source: Clay is moulded into pots used at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram. Give the use of the body organ marked Y. A: The brain controls the body (thinking, senses and movement). Y marks the brain, which controls all body activities.
chunks.source: Y marks the brain, which controls all body activities.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way are rats dangerous to people? A: They destroy stored food and spread diseases. Rats eat stored food and spread diseases like plague.
chunks.source: Rats eat stored food and spread diseases like plague.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one danger of electricity in our homes. A: It can shock and kill people (or cause fires). Careless handling of electricity causes shocks and fires.
chunks.source: Careless handling of electricity causes shocks and fires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of food in our body. A: It gives us energy (or builds the body). Food gives the body energy to work and play.
chunks.source: Food gives the body energy to work and play.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important to cross the road carefully? A: To avoid being knocked by vehicles (accidents). Careful crossing prevents road accidents.
chunks.source: Careful crossing prevents road accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of a school garden. A: It provides food for the school (and teaches farming). School gardens grow food used in school meals.
chunks.source: School gardens grow food used in school meals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of caring for crops in the garden. A: Weeding (or watering, spraying). Weeding removes weeds that compete with crops.
chunks.source: Weeding removes weeds that compete with crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way people can control the spread of dysentery in the community. A: By using latrines properly (and drinking clean water). Proper latrine use stops faeces spreading dysentery.
chunks.source: Proper latrine use stops faeces spreading dysentery.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the animal. How does the animal above move from one place to another? A: It crawls (slithers). The snake has no legs, so it crawls on its belly.
chunks.source: The snake has no legs, so it crawls on its belly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should rabbit hutches be cleaned regularly? A: To prevent diseases. Dirty hutches breed germs that make rabbits sick.
chunks.source: Dirty hutches breed germs that make rabbits sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the weather instrument used to measure the amount of rain received in an area. A: rain gauge. A rain gauge collects and measures rainfall.
chunks.source: A rain gauge collects and measures rainfall.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one component of air. A: oxygen (or nitrogen, carbon dioxide). Oxygen is one of the gases found in air.
chunks.source: Oxygen is one of the gases found in air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way a P.4 child can prevent him/herself from getting AIDS. A: Avoid sharing sharp objects (or abstain from sex). Not sharing razor blades and needles protects children from HIV.
chunks.source: Not sharing razor blades and needles protects children from HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is weather? A: The daily condition of the atmosphere (in a place). Weather is how the atmosphere is each day: sunny, rainy, windy or cloudy.
chunks.source: Weather is how the atmosphere is each day: sunny, rainy, windy or cloudy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the element of weather which people use to water their crops. A: rainfall (rain). Rain waters crops in the garden.
chunks.source: Rain waters crops in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the element of weather which people use to winnow harvested crops. A: wind. Wind blows away chaff when winnowing.
chunks.source: Wind blows away chaff when winnowing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one material used to manage weather. A: An umbrella (or raincoat) is used to manage rainy weather. We cannot change weather, but we manage it, e.g. with umbrellas in rain.
chunks.source: We cannot change weather, but we manage it, e.g. with umbrellas in rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the food store. Name the food store shown above. A: granary. The raised store for keeping harvested food is called a granary.
chunks.source: The raised store for keeping harvested food is called a granary.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one material used to make the above store. A: grass (or banana fibres, wood, poles). Granaries are thatched with grass and built with poles.
chunks.source: Granaries are thatched with grass and built with poles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name part marked W. A: legs (supports, poles). W points to the legs that raise the granary off the ground.
chunks.source: W points to the legs that raise the granary off the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is part marked Y useful on the food store? A: The thatched roof (Y) protects the food from rain and sunshine. Y is the roof, which keeps rain and sun off the stored food.
chunks.source: Y is the roof, which keeps rain and sun off the stored food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is wind? A: Moving air. Wind is air moving from one place to another.
chunks.source: Wind is air moving from one place to another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can wind be useful to people? Give two ways. A: For winnowing; for drying clothes (or sailing boats, running windmills). Wind is useful for winnowing grain and drying clothes.
chunks.source: Wind is useful for winnowing grain and drying clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is wind dangerous to people? A: Strong wind destroys houses and crops. Strong wind blows off roofs and flattens crops.
chunks.source: Strong wind blows off roofs and flattens crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the method of planting. Name the above method of planting. A: row planting. The crops are planted in straight rows, so it is row planting.
chunks.source: The crops are planted in straight rows, so it is row planting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any two advantages of using the above method of planting. A: It makes weeding easy; it makes harvesting easy (proper spacing). Rows give crops space and make weeding and harvesting easy.
chunks.source: Rows give crops space and make weeding and harvesting easy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the above method, write one other method of planting. A: broadcasting. Broadcasting is scattering seeds over the garden.
chunks.source: Broadcasting is scattering seeds over the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is an extended family? A: A family made up of parents, children and other relatives living together. An extended family includes grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins.
chunks.source: An extended family includes grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two groups of people found in an extended family. A: grandparents; uncles and aunts (or cousins). Grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins live in an extended family.
chunks.source: Grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins live in an extended family.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which a nuclear family can become an extended family. A: When relatives like grandparents come to live with them. If grandparents or uncles join the home, it becomes extended.
chunks.source: If grandparents or uncles join the home, it becomes extended.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the split bean seed. Name part marked Q. A: cotyledon. Q points to the cotyledon, the food store of the seed.
chunks.source: Q points to the cotyledon, the food store of the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name part marked R. A: embryo. R points to the embryo, the young plant inside the seed.
chunks.source: R points to the embryo, the young plant inside the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of part marked P. A: It protects the inner parts of the seed (seed coat/testa). P is the testa, which covers and protects the seed.
chunks.source: P is the testa, which covers and protects the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of germination does the bean seed above undergo? A: epigeal germination. Bean cotyledons come above the ground, which is epigeal germination.
chunks.source: Bean cotyledons come above the ground, which is epigeal germination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the animals in A with their habitats in B. A: Bird: Nest; Dog: Kennel; Rabbit: Hutch; Cow: Kraal. Birds live in nests, dogs in kennels, rabbits in hutches and cows in kraals.
chunks.source: Birds live in nests, dogs in kennels, rabbits in hutches and cows in kraals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the human tooth. Name the type of tooth drawn above. A: molar. The broad, flat-topped tooth drawn is a molar.
chunks.source: The broad, flat-topped tooth drawn is a molar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the region marked M. A: crown. M marks the crown, the top part of the tooth above the gum.
chunks.source: M marks the crown, the top part of the tooth above the gum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the above tooth useful when eating? A: It grinds and crushes food. Molars have broad tops for grinding food.
chunks.source: Molars have broad tops for grinding food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way in which people can protect their teeth from decay. A: Brush teeth regularly (or avoid sugary foods). Regular brushing removes food that rots teeth.
chunks.source: Regular brushing removes food that rots teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two sources of food. A: plants; animals. We get food from plants and from animals.
chunks.source: We get food from plants and from animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which food value is obtained from eating fruits? A: vitamins. Fruits give us vitamins, which protect us from diseases.
chunks.source: Fruits give us vitamins, which protect us from diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which deficiency disease is as a result of lack of carbohydrates in the body? A: marasmus. Without enough carbohydrates, the body lacks energy and marasmus develops.
chunks.source: Without enough carbohydrates, the body lacks energy and marasmus develops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two components of the first aid box. A: bandage; plaster (or scissors, antiseptic, cotton wool). A first aid box keeps bandages and plasters for emergencies.
chunks.source: A first aid box keeps bandages and plasters for emergencies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State two reasons why first aid should be given. A: To save life; to prevent the injury from getting worse (reduce pain). First aid saves life and stops injuries worsening before the doctor comes.
chunks.source: First aid saves life and stops injuries worsening before the doctor comes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of wood fuel used at home. A: firewood; charcoal. Firewood and charcoal are wood fuels burnt at home.
chunks.source: Firewood and charcoal are wood fuels burnt at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one use of paraffin at home. A: It is used in lamps for lighting (or in stoves for cooking). Paraffin burns in lamps to give light at home.
chunks.source: Paraffin burns in lamps to give light at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of the sun. A: It gives us light and heat (or dries things, helps plants make food). The sun gives light and warmth to the earth.
chunks.source: The sun gives light and warmth to the earth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the passage about the water cycle with the correct words. A: heats, atmosphere, condenses, rain. The sun heats water; vapour rises to the atmosphere, condenses into clouds, and falls as rain.
chunks.source: The sun heats water; vapour rises to the atmosphere, condenses into clouds, and falls as rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the life cycle of a cockroach. Name the stage marked A. A: eggs. A points to the eggs, the first stage of the cockroach life cycle.
chunks.source: A points to the eggs, the first stage of the cockroach life cycle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the stage marked B. A: nymph. B points to the nymph, the young cockroach.
chunks.source: B points to the nymph, the young cockroach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from a cockroach, name any other insect that undergoes the above life cycle. A: grasshopper (or locust). Like the cockroach, the grasshopper has incomplete metamorphosis.
chunks.source: Like the cockroach, the grasshopper has incomplete metamorphosis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger of cockroaches at home. A: They spread diseases (contaminate food). Cockroaches carry germs that contaminate food and cause diseases.
chunks.source: Cockroaches carry germs that contaminate food and cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify two causes of dehydration. A: diarrhoea; vomiting (or too little drinking water, too much sweating). Diarrhoea and vomiting make the body lose a lot of water.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea and vomiting make the body lose a lot of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two signs of dehydration in children. A: sunken eyes; dry mouth and tongue (weakness, little urine). Dehydrated children have sunken eyes and dry mouths.
chunks.source: Dehydrated children have sunken eyes and dry mouths.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a dog protect itself? A: It barks and bites. A dog barks loudly and bites to scare away enemies.
chunks.source: A dog barks loudly and bites to scare away enemies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a chameleon protect itself? A: It changes colour to hide (camouflage). A chameleon changes its skin colour to match its surroundings.
chunks.source: A chameleon changes its skin colour to match its surroundings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two uses of wild animals to people. A: They attract tourists (income); they are a source of food (meat). Wild animals bring tourists who pay money, and some give meat.
chunks.source: Wild animals bring tourists who pay money, and some give meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one part of the human body organ that is found on the head. A: the eye (or ear, nose, mouth). The eyes are body organs found on the head.
chunks.source: The eyes are body organs found on the head.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way family members may care for an HIV/AIDS patient. A: Feed them well (or give medicine, comfort them). Family members care for patients by feeding and comforting them.
chunks.source: Family members care for patients by feeding and comforting them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of an annual crop. A: maize (or beans, tomatoes). Maize grows and is harvested within one year, so it is annual.
chunks.source: Maize grows and is harvested within one year, so it is annual.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one component of soil. A: humus (or air, water, sand, clay). Humus is one of the components that make up soil.
chunks.source: Humus is one of the components that make up soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one importance of keeping our bodies clean. A: It prevents diseases (or makes us smart). Clean bodies are free from germs that cause diseases.
chunks.source: Clean bodies are free from germs that cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of showing that air exerts pressure. A: Suck air out of a plastic bottle and see it crash (or blow up a balloon). Removing air from a bottle lets outside air pressure crash it.
chunks.source: Removing air from a bottle lets outside air pressure crash it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the disease vector that spreads malaria. A: female anopheles mosquito. The female anopheles mosquito spreads malaria when it bites.
chunks.source: The female anopheles mosquito spreads malaria when it bites.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one danger of the sun. A: Too much sunshine causes sunburn (or dries crops, causes drought). Strong sunshine can burn the skin.
chunks.source: Strong sunshine can burn the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one example of a natural change in the environment. A: germination (or rainfall, growth). Germination is a natural change that happens on its own.
chunks.source: Germination is a natural change that happens on its own.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from a hen, name one other domestic bird. A: duck (or turkey, pigeon). A duck is a domestic bird kept at home.
chunks.source: A duck is a domestic bird kept at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way people can care for insects such as bees. A: By not destroying their hives (or planting flowers for them). Protecting beehives keeps bees safe.
chunks.source: Protecting beehives keeps bees safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the soil profile. Identify the layer marked X. A: parent rock (bedrock). X marks the bottom layer of the soil profile, the parent rock.
chunks.source: X marks the bottom layer of the soil profile, the parent rock.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The soil layer that contains a lot of humus is the ___. A: top soil. Top soil holds the most humus, which is why plants grow well in it.
chunks.source: Top soil holds the most humus, which is why plants grow well in it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of keeping food free from germs. A: Cover it (or keep it in clean containers). Covering food stops germs and flies reaching it.
chunks.source: Covering food stops germs and flies reaching it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of a dog to people in a home. A: It guards the home (provides security). Dogs bark at strangers and guard the home.
chunks.source: Dogs bark at strangers and guard the home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the garden tool. How do people care for the above garden tool? A: Clean it after use, oil it and store it in a dry place. The hoe is cleaned, oiled and kept dry to stop rust.
chunks.source: The hoe is cleaned, oiled and kept dry to stop rust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one example of an insect without wings. A: ant (or termite, silverfish). Ants are insects that have no wings.
chunks.source: Ants are insects that have no wings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of controlling pests in a garden. A: Spraying pesticides (or weeding, crop rotation). Spraying kills pests that attack crops.
chunks.source: Spraying kills pests that attack crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one living component in the environment. A: plants (or animals). Plants are living components of the environment.
chunks.source: Plants are living components of the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is clearing bushes near your home useful to family members? A: It removes hiding places for dangerous animals and vectors. Cleared bushes leave no hiding place for snakes and mosquitoes.
chunks.source: Cleared bushes leave no hiding place for snakes and mosquitoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is cutting down of trees a danger to the environment? A: It causes soil erosion and drought. Without trees, soil washes away and rain reduces.
chunks.source: Without trees, soil washes away and rain reduces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one item used to keep our bodies clean. A: sponge (or soap, toothbrush, towel). A sponge is used for bathing the body.
chunks.source: A sponge is used for bathing the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one disadvantage of heavy rainfall to people. A: It causes floods that destroy crops and houses. Heavy rain brings floods which damage property.
chunks.source: Heavy rain brings floods which damage property.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one local material made from banana fibres. A: rope (or mat, ball). Banana fibres are woven into ropes.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are woven into ropes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a domestic bird. A: hen (or duck, turkey). A hen is a common domestic bird.
chunks.source: A hen is a common domestic bird.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of grasshoppers to people. A: They are eaten as food (source of proteins). People roast and eat grasshoppers.
chunks.source: People roast and eat grasshoppers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of avoiding accidents at home. A: Keep sharp objects out of children's reach (or handle fire carefully). Keeping dangers away prevents home accidents.
chunks.source: Keeping dangers away prevents home accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of germination does a bean seed undergo? A: epigeal germination. Bean cotyledons rise above the ground: epigeal germination.
chunks.source: Bean cotyledons rise above the ground: epigeal germination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of avoiding accidents at home. A: Mop up spilt water so floors are not slippery (or keep medicines away from children). Dry, clean floors prevent falls at home.
chunks.source: Dry, clean floors prevent falls at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mr. Kalumbe's family has parents, grandparents and biological children. Which kind of family is this? A: extended family. With grandparents included, it is an extended family.
chunks.source: With grandparents included, it is an extended family.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the habitat shown. Which animal stays in the habitat shown below? A: spider. The web is a spider's habitat.
chunks.source: The web is a spider's habitat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one common sign of a crop damaged by pests. A: leaves with holes (or wilting, yellow leaves). Pests chew leaves, leaving holes.
chunks.source: Pests chew leaves, leaving holes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To what class of food does cassava belong? A: carbohydrates (energy-giving foods). Cassava gives energy, so it belongs to carbohydrates.
chunks.source: Cassava gives energy, so it belongs to carbohydrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of caring for wild animals. A: Protect their habitats (or stop poaching). Keeping forests safe protects wild animals.
chunks.source: Keeping forests safe protects wild animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should you group a maize plant under living things? A: Because it carries out life processes (grows, breathes, reproduces). Maize grows, breathes and reproduces, so it is living.
chunks.source: Maize grows, breathes and reproduces, so it is living.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the sun, give any other natural source of energy. A: wind (or running water, wood). Wind is a natural source of energy.
chunks.source: Wind is a natural source of energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one childhood immunisable disease. A: measles (or polio, tuberculosis). Measles is immunised against in childhood.
chunks.source: Measles is immunised against in childhood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do you group tomatoes under annual crops? A: Because they grow and are harvested within one year. Tomatoes complete their life in one season.
chunks.source: Tomatoes complete their life in one season.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one activity where clay soil is used as a raw-material. A: Making pots (or bricks, cups). Clay soil is moulded into pots.
chunks.source: Clay soil is moulded into pots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of a cow to people at home. A: It gives us milk (or meat, manure). Cows provide families with milk.
chunks.source: Cows provide families with milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do we call a meal that contains all food values in their correct amount? A: a balanced diet. A balanced diet has every food value in the right amount.
chunks.source: A balanced diet has every food value in the right amount.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two classes of food that make up a balanced diet. A: carbohydrates; proteins (or vitamins). Carbohydrates and proteins are classes of food in a balanced diet.
chunks.source: Carbohydrates and proteins are classes of food in a balanced diet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What food value do we get from eating beans? A: proteins. Beans are rich in proteins, which build the body.
chunks.source: Beans are rich in proteins, which build the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the fish. Name the part labeled with letter A. A: tail (caudal fin). A points to the tail of the fish.
chunks.source: A points to the tail of the fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part labeled with letter B. A: mouth. B points to the mouth of the fish.
chunks.source: B points to the mouth of the fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part of a fish used for smelling food in water is the ___. A: nostrils. A fish smells food in water with its nostrils.
chunks.source: A fish smells food in water with its nostrils.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of fish to people. A: It is eaten as food (source of proteins). Fish gives people proteins when eaten.
chunks.source: Fish gives people proteins when eaten.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two common accidents at home. A: burns; cuts (or falls, poisoning). Burns and cuts are common home accidents.
chunks.source: Burns and cuts are common home accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one cause of accidents at home. A: carelessness (or slippery floors, open fire). Carelessness causes many home accidents.
chunks.source: Carelessness causes many home accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What first aid is given to someone with burns? A: Pour clean cold water on the burn (and cover loosely). Cold water cools a burn and reduces pain.
chunks.source: Cold water cools a burn and reduces pain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the garden tools in A to their uses in B. A: Wheelbarrow: carrying rubbish and manure; Watering can: watering plants; Forked hoe: breaking stony and hard soil; Axe: splitting firewood. A wheelbarrow carries loads, a watering can waters plants, a forked hoe breaks hard soil and an axe splits firewood.
chunks.source: A wheelbarrow carries loads, a watering can waters plants, a forked hoe breaks hard soil and an axe splits firewood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one source of water in our community. A: a well (or borehole, spring, river). Wells give communities water.
chunks.source: Wells give communities water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of water to people. A: drinking (or cooking, washing). People need water for drinking.
chunks.source: People need water for drinking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one way of making water safe for drinking. A: boiling (or filtering, chlorinating). Boiling kills germs in water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger of having stagnant water near our homes. A: It breeds mosquitoes (which spread malaria). Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the shoot system of a flowering plant. Name the part of the shoot labeled with letter A. A: stem. A points to the stem, which holds the plant upright.
chunks.source: A points to the stem, which holds the plant upright.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part of the shoot labeled with letter C. A: flower. C points to the flower at the top of the shoot.
chunks.source: C points to the flower at the top of the shoot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two uses of part B to a plant. A: It makes food through photosynthesis; it loses excess water (transpiration). B is the leaf: it makes food and gives off excess water.
chunks.source: B is the leaf: it makes food and gives off excess water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the life cycle of a cockroach: Eggs → Nymph → ___. A: adult. The nymph grows into an adult cockroach, completing the cycle.
chunks.source: The nymph grows into an adult cockroach, completing the cycle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of lifecycle shown above. A: incomplete metamorphosis. Eggs → nymph → adult, without a pupa, is incomplete metamorphosis.
chunks.source: Eggs → nymph → adult, without a pupa, is incomplete metamorphosis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the life cycle above, mention one other type of insect life cycle. A: complete metamorphosis. The other type is complete metamorphosis (egg → larva → pupa → adult).
chunks.source: The other type is complete metamorphosis (egg → larva → pupa → adult).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are domestic animals? A: Animals kept at home by people. Domestic animals live with people and are cared for by them.
chunks.source: Domestic animals live with people and are cared for by them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of domestic animals that provide people with milk. A: cow; goat. Cows and goats give people milk.
chunks.source: Cows and goats give people milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way people can care for their domestic animals. A: Feed them well (or treat them when sick, house them). Good feeding keeps domestic animals healthy.
chunks.source: Good feeding keeps domestic animals healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two materials used in building a house. A: bricks; cement (or sand, iron sheets, timber). Bricks and cement are used to build houses.
chunks.source: Bricks and cement are used to build houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two places where people can get building materials. A: shops (hardware); swamps for sand (or forests for timber). People buy materials from shops or collect sand and timber locally.
chunks.source: People buy materials from shops or collect sand and timber locally.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In one sentence, write the meaning of personal hygiene. A: Keeping the body and its surroundings clean. Personal hygiene means keeping yourself and your things clean.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene means keeping yourself and your things clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any two things we use to promote personal hygiene. A: soap; toothbrush (or sponge, towel, water). Soap and toothbrushes keep our bodies clean.
chunks.source: Soap and toothbrushes keep our bodies clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of personal hygiene. A: It prevents diseases. Being clean keeps germs away and prevents diseases.
chunks.source: Being clean keeps germs away and prevents diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the natural change. What name is given to the natural change shown above? A: the water cycle (rain formation). The diagram shows the water cycle: water rises, forms clouds and falls as rain.
chunks.source: The diagram shows the water cycle: water rises, forms clouds and falls as rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the process that takes place at B. A: evaporation. B shows water vapour rising: evaporation.
chunks.source: B shows water vapour rising: evaporation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the process that takes place at C. A: condensation. C shows vapour forming clouds: condensation.
chunks.source: C shows vapour forming clouds: condensation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are plants useful in the natural change above? A: They release water vapour (transpiration), helping rain formation. Plants give off vapour which joins the water cycle.
chunks.source: Plants give off vapour which joins the water cycle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Briefly explain the term mulching. A: Covering soil around crops with dry plant materials. Mulching means spreading dry grass or leaves over soil.
chunks.source: Mulching means spreading dry grass or leaves over soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do farmers mulch their gardens? Give two reasons. A: To keep moisture in the soil; to stop weeds from growing (control soil erosion). Mulch keeps soil wet and stops weeds.
chunks.source: Mulch keeps soil wet and stops weeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can mulching be a danger to crops in the garden? A: It can hide pests that attack crops (or cause rotting). Pests hide in mulch and damage crops.
chunks.source: Pests hide in mulch and damage crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the weather chart. Identify the type of weather shown in A. A: sunny weather. A shows the sun drying crops: sunny weather.
chunks.source: A shows the sun drying crops: sunny weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the type of weather shown in B. A: rainy weather. B shows a child with an umbrella in rain: rainy weather.
chunks.source: B shows a child with an umbrella in rain: rainy weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which the type of weather in B is useful to a crop farmer. A: It provides water for crops to grow. Rain gives crops the water they need.
chunks.source: Rain gives crops the water they need.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way of protecting ourselves from weather B. A: By using an umbrella (or wearing a raincoat, gumboots). Umbrellas protect us from rain.
chunks.source: Umbrellas protect us from rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the food value in mangoes that keeps the body healthy is ___. A: vitamins. Mangoes give vitamins, which keep the body healthy.
chunks.source: Mangoes give vitamins, which keep the body healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the source of proteins is ___. A: beans (or meat, fish, eggs). Beans are a source of proteins.
chunks.source: Beans are a source of proteins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the source of carbohydrates is ___, and their use in the body is ___. A: posho (maize); they give the body energy. Posho gives carbohydrates, which give the body energy.
chunks.source: Posho gives carbohydrates, which give the body energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange the steps of making O.R.S in the correct order. A: Wash your hands with clean water and soap., Measure one litre of drinking water into a clean container., Measure one leveled teaspoonful of salt and eight of sugar into the drinking water., Stir until all the salt and sugar dissolve.. First wash hands, then measure water, add salt and sugar, and stir until dissolved.
chunks.source: First wash hands, then measure water, add salt and sugar, and stir until dissolved.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one staple food that is processed using a mortar and a pestle. A: cassava (or millet, sorghum). Cassava flour is pounded using a mortar and pestle.
chunks.source: Cassava flour is pounded using a mortar and pestle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one material that people may use to clean their teeth. A: toothbrush (or chewing stick, toothpaste). A toothbrush is used to clean teeth.
chunks.source: A toothbrush is used to clean teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do farmers protect their crops from being destroyed by drought? A: By irrigating them (or mulching). Irrigation gives crops water when there is no rain.
chunks.source: Irrigation gives crops water when there is no rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of preventing faecal diseases at school. A: Use latrines properly (or wash hands after visiting the latrine). Proper latrine use stops faecal diseases spreading.
chunks.source: Proper latrine use stops faecal diseases spreading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do people put scare crows in their gardens? A: To scare away birds that eat crops. Scarecrows frighten birds away from crops.
chunks.source: Scarecrows frighten birds away from crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is a leopard dangerous to people? A: It can attack and kill people (and their animals). Leopards are wild cats that can attack people.
chunks.source: Leopards are wild cats that can attack people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the living component of the environment which gives us timber. A: trees (plants). Trees give us timber used for building.
chunks.source: Trees give us timber used for building.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one natural factor that destroys our environment. A: drought (or floods, lightning). Drought is a natural factor that destroys crops and vegetation.
chunks.source: Drought is a natural factor that destroys crops and vegetation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A tool you can use to clean a house is a ___. A: broom. A broom is used for sweeping and cleaning the house.
chunks.source: A broom is used for sweeping and cleaning the house.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are forests useful to birds? A: They give birds shelter (homes) and food. Birds build nests and find food in forests.
chunks.source: Birds build nests and find food in forests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do people control malaria in their homes? A: By sleeping under mosquito nets (or spraying, draining stagnant water). Mosquito nets stop malaria-spreading mosquitoes biting at night.
chunks.source: Mosquito nets stop malaria-spreading mosquitoes biting at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is heavy rainfall dangerous to people? A: It causes floods that destroy homes and crops. Heavy rain brings floods which damage property.
chunks.source: Heavy rain brings floods which damage property.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one social insect. A: termite (or bee, ant, wasp). Termites live together in colonies, so they are social insects.
chunks.source: Termites live together in colonies, so they are social insects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one plant that gives us fibre for making balls. A: banana (banana fibres). Banana fibres are woven into balls.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are woven into balls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do people prevent spread of HIV/AIDS in their communities? A: By abstaining from sex and not sharing sharp objects (faithfulness). Avoiding the ways HIV spreads stops it in the community.
chunks.source: Avoiding the ways HIV spreads stops it in the community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one source of heat energy in our environment. A: the sun (or fire, charcoal). The sun is the main natural source of heat.
chunks.source: The sun is the main natural source of heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one area in a home that requires constant cleaning. A: the kitchen (or latrine, bathroom). The kitchen must be cleaned constantly to keep food safe.
chunks.source: The kitchen must be cleaned constantly to keep food safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one other relative in an extended family. A: grandmother (or uncle, aunt, cousin). Grandmothers are relatives in an extended family.
chunks.source: Grandmothers are relatives in an extended family.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of weather encourages people to wear sweaters? A: cold weather. People wear sweaters when the weather is cold.
chunks.source: People wear sweaters when the weather is cold.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one immunisable disease. A: measles (or polio, tuberculosis). Measles is prevented by immunisation.
chunks.source: Measles is prevented by immunisation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study part of a flower. The stigma is the part at the ___. A: top (tip) of the style. The stigma is the sticky tip at the top where pollen lands.
chunks.source: The stigma is the sticky tip at the top where pollen lands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one role of a mother at home. A: Cooking food (or caring for children). A mother cooks for the family.
chunks.source: A mother cooks for the family.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do farmers mulch their gardens? A: To keep moisture in the soil (and stop weeds). Mulch keeps soil wet and stops weeds growing.
chunks.source: Mulch keeps soil wet and stops weeds growing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one animal which lives in soil. A: earthworm (or termite, mole). Earthworms live in the soil.
chunks.source: Earthworms live in the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are bean plants grouped under flowering plants? A: Because they produce flowers. Bean plants bear flowers, so they are flowering plants.
chunks.source: Bean plants bear flowers, so they are flowering plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one material that people use to keep the toilets clean. A: disinfectant (or water, soap, brush). Disinfectant kills germs in toilets.
chunks.source: Disinfectant kills germs in toilets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of soap at school. A: Washing hands (or bathing, washing clothes). Soap is used for washing hands at school.
chunks.source: Soap is used for washing hands at school.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of controlling the spread of malaria at home. A: Sleep under mosquito nets (or drain stagnant water). Nets stop mosquitoes biting at night.
chunks.source: Nets stop mosquitoes biting at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of preventing skin diseases. A: Keep the body clean (bathe daily). Bathing daily keeps skin free from germs.
chunks.source: Bathing daily keeps skin free from germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A garden tool used for cutting trees is called ___. A: an axe (or panga). An axe cuts down trees.
chunks.source: An axe cuts down trees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one importance of eating a balanced diet. A: It keeps us healthy (prevents deficiency diseases). A balanced diet gives all food values for good health.
chunks.source: A balanced diet gives all food values for good health.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of skins and hides of animals to people. A: Making shoes (or bags, belts, drums). Skins are made into leather shoes and bags.
chunks.source: Skins are made into leather shoes and bags.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can injuries of cuts be prevented at home? A: Handle sharp objects carefully (keep them away from children). Careful handling of knives and blades prevents cuts.
chunks.source: Careful handling of knives and blades prevents cuts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do houseflies lay their eggs? A: On rotting matter (faeces, rubbish). Houseflies lay eggs on faeces and rotting rubbish.
chunks.source: Houseflies lay eggs on faeces and rotting rubbish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the roots of plants. Name one plant with the kind of roots shown above. A: beans (or groundnuts, soya). The roots have nodules, which are found on legumes like beans.
chunks.source: The roots have nodules, which are found on legumes like beans.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A kitten is a young one of a domestic animal. Name that animal. A: cat. A kitten is a baby cat.
chunks.source: A kitten is a baby cat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for school children to wear shoes? A: To protect their feet from injury and infection (jiggers). Shoes protect feet from cuts and jiggers.
chunks.source: Shoes protect feet from cuts and jiggers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the life cycle: Eggs → ___ → Adult. A: larva. A larva (like a maggot or caterpillar) hatches from the egg and later becomes an adult. Some insects have a nymph instead.
chunks.source: A larva (like a maggot or caterpillar) hatches from the egg and later becomes an adult. Some insects have a nymph instead.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of carbon dioxide. A: Plants use it in photosynthesis (or it puts out fire, in fizzy drinks). Green plants need carbon dioxide to make food.
chunks.source: Green plants need carbon dioxide to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one plant that has thorns on its stem or leaves. A: rose (or cactus, acacia). The rose has thorns on its stem.
chunks.source: The rose has thorns on its stem.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from water, give any other two components of soil. A: humus; air (or sand, clay). Besides water, soil contains humus and air.
chunks.source: Besides water, soil contains humus and air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one farming practice that can keep water (moisture) in the soil. A: mulching. Mulching covers soil and keeps moisture in.
chunks.source: Mulching covers soil and keeps moisture in.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of water at home. A: drinking (or cooking, washing). Water at home is used for drinking.
chunks.source: Water at home is used for drinking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do people preserve food? A: To keep it for future use (prevent wastage and hunger). Preserved food lasts so people eat even when food is scarce.
chunks.source: Preserved food lasts so people eat even when food is scarce.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from refrigeration, give two other ways of preserving food. A: drying; salting (or smoking). Drying and salting keep food from going bad.
chunks.source: Drying and salting keep food from going bad.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is refrigeration not common in rural areas? A: Because there is no electricity (and fridges are expensive). Most rural homes have no power for fridges.
chunks.source: Most rural homes have no power for fridges.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the sense organ for tasting. A: the tongue. We taste with the tongue.
chunks.source: We taste with the tongue.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of caring for the organ you have named above. A: Brush the tongue when brushing teeth (or avoid very hot food). Cleaning the tongue keeps it healthy.
chunks.source: Cleaning the tongue keeps it healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write two other senses in the human body. A: sight; hearing (or smell, touch). Besides taste, we have sight and hearing.
chunks.source: Besides taste, we have sight and hearing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the types of weather in A to the correct activities in B. A: Rainy weather: harvesting water; Windy weather: winnowing seeds; Sunny weather: drying harvested crops. Rainy weather is for harvesting water, windy for winnowing and sunny for drying crops.
chunks.source: Rainy weather is for harvesting water, windy for winnowing and sunny for drying crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the above types of weather can we manage by putting on gumboots? A: rainy weather. Gumboots protect feet in rainy, muddy weather.
chunks.source: Gumboots protect feet in rainy, muddy weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which month in a year has the least number of days? A: February. February has 28 days (29 in a leap year), the least of all months.
chunks.source: February has 28 days (29 in a leap year), the least of all months.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the season in which farmers plant their seeds. A: the rainy (wet) season. Farmers plant when the rains come.
chunks.source: Farmers plant when the rains come.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the rectangle (3 cm by 7 cm). Give the length and the width of the rectangle. A: Length 7 cm; Width 3 cm. The longer side (7 cm) is the length and the shorter (3 cm) is the width.
chunks.source: The longer side (7 cm) is the length and the shorter (3 cm) is the width.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the foodstuffs. Name the food stuff marked B. A: sugarcane. B shows sugarcane stalks.
chunks.source: B shows sugarcane stalks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the food value got from foodstuff marked A. A: vitamins. A is a mango, which gives vitamins.
chunks.source: A is a mango, which gives vitamins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one tool that can be used to peel foodstuff B for eating. A: a knife. A knife peels the hard cover of sugarcane.
chunks.source: A knife peels the hard cover of sugarcane.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should foodstuff A be washed properly before eating it? A: To remove germs and dirt (it is eaten raw). Mangoes are eaten raw, so washing removes germs.
chunks.source: Mangoes are eaten raw, so washing removes germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a chameleon protect itself from enemies? A: It changes colour to hide (camouflage). Colour change hides the chameleon from enemies.
chunks.source: Colour change hides the chameleon from enemies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a dog protect itself from enemies? A: It barks and bites. A dog scares enemies by barking and biting.
chunks.source: A dog scares enemies by barking and biting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a hen protect itself from enemies? A: It runs away and hides (or flies a short distance). A hen escapes danger by running and hiding.
chunks.source: A hen escapes danger by running and hiding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one way domestic animals can be dangerous to people. A: They can bite or kick people (spread diseases). Animals like dogs can bite people.
chunks.source: Animals like dogs can bite people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the item in the first aid box. Give the use of this item in giving first aid. A: It covers small cuts and wounds (plaster). A plaster covers small wounds to keep germs out.
chunks.source: A plaster covers small wounds to keep germs out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one quality of a good first aider. A: kindness (or calmness, quick to act, knowledgeable). A good first aider stays calm and acts quickly.
chunks.source: A good first aider stays calm and acts quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two reasons for giving first aid to people who have got accidents. A: To save life; to stop the injury getting worse (reduce pain). First aid saves life and prevents worse harm.
chunks.source: First aid saves life and prevents worse harm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the disease caused by HIV. A: AIDS. HIV causes AIDS.
chunks.source: HIV causes AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is HIV spread from one person to another? A: Through unprotected sex (or sharing sharp objects, blood transfusion). HIV spreads mainly through unprotected sex.
chunks.source: HIV spreads mainly through unprotected sex.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way a school child can protect him/herself from getting HIV. A: Avoid sharing sharp objects (abstain from sex). Not sharing blades and needles protects children.
chunks.source: Not sharing blades and needles protects children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one way of caring for people with HIV. A: Feed them well (or comfort them, give medicine). Good food and comfort help people with HIV.
chunks.source: Good food and comfort help people with HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two uses of shadows to people. A: They help tell time; they give shade (coolness). Shadows show time and give cool shade.
chunks.source: Shadows show time and give cool shade.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which direction will the shadow of an object be if the sun is in the West? A: to the East. Shadows fall opposite the sun, so a western sun casts shadows east.
chunks.source: Shadows fall opposite the sun, so a western sun casts shadows east.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: At what time of the day are shadows shortest? A: midday (noon). At midday the sun is overhead, so shadows are shortest.
chunks.source: At midday the sun is overhead, so shadows are shortest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the garden tools below. Name the garden tools shown. A: trowel; axe. The tools shown are a trowel and an axe.
chunks.source: The tools shown are a trowel and an axe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one tool which can be cared for by sharpening. A: axe (or panga, knife, hoe). An axe is kept sharp by sharpening.
chunks.source: An axe is kept sharp by sharpening.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one tool which can be cared for by oiling moving parts. A: wheelbarrow (or secateurs). A wheelbarrow's moving parts are oiled.
chunks.source: A wheelbarrow's moving parts are oiled.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the sun useful in the water cycle? A: It heats water, causing evaporation. The sun's heat turns water into vapour.
chunks.source: The sun's heat turns water into vapour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are trees useful in the water cycle? A: They release water vapour (transpiration), helping rain formation. Trees add vapour to air through transpiration.
chunks.source: Trees add vapour to air through transpiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one human activity which can affect the water cycle. A: deforestation (cutting down trees). Cutting trees reduces vapour and rain.
chunks.source: Cutting trees reduces vapour and rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one way people can make use of rainwater. A: Harvest it for drinking and home use (or irrigation). Rainwater can be collected in tanks for home use.
chunks.source: Rainwater can be collected in tanks for home use.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the gaps about germination with the correct words. A: seedling (young plant), epigeal, water, plumule. A seed grows into a seedling; the two germinations are hypogeal and epigeal; seeds need water; the plumule becomes the shoot.
chunks.source: A seed grows into a seedling; the two germinations are hypogeal and epigeal; seeds need water; the plumule becomes the shoot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one material or thing found in a bedroom. A: a bed (or blanket, pillow). A bed is found in a bedroom.
chunks.source: A bed is found in a bedroom.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part of the body used for smelling. A: Nose. The nose contains smell receptors that detect odours in the air around us.
chunks.source: The nose contains smell receptors that detect odours in the air around us.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of preparing cassava before eating. A: Peel off the outer skin and boil it until soft. Cassava roots must be peeled and cooked by boiling, steaming or roasting to make them soft and safe to eat.
chunks.source: Cassava roots must be peeled and cooked by boiling, steaming or roasting to make them soft and safe to eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do bees visit flowers? A: To collect nectar and pollen for food. Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers as food, and as they move they carry pollen that helps plants reproduce.
chunks.source: Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers as food, and as they move they carry pollen that helps plants reproduce.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we iron clothes before wearing them? A: To kill germs and make the clothes look neat. The heat of the iron kills germs and lice hiding in clothes and removes creases so clothes look smart.
chunks.source: The heat of the iron kills germs and lice hiding in clothes and removes creases so clothes look smart.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Draw a diagram of a simple leaf in the space below. A: A drawing of a simple leaf: one undivided flat blade (lamina) joined by a stalk (petiole), with a midrib and side veins. A simple leaf has a single undivided blade attached to the stem by a stalk, with veins spreading from a midrib.
chunks.source: A simple leaf has a single undivided blade attached to the stem by a stalk, with veins spreading from a midrib.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the gas used to put out fire. A: Carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it is used in fire extinguishers to put out fires.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it is used in fire extinguishers to put out fires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one role of children in a home. A: Sweeping the compound (or fetching water, or washing utensils). Children help at home by doing light work such as sweeping, fetching water and washing utensils.
chunks.source: Children help at home by doing light work such as sweeping, fetching water and washing utensils.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are earthworms important in the soil? A: They burrow through the soil, letting in air and water, and their droppings make the soil fertile. Earthworm tunnels aerate the soil so roots get air and water, and worm waste adds nutrients that feed plants.
chunks.source: Earthworm tunnels aerate the soil so roots get air and water, and worm waste adds nutrients that feed plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: "It refers to the general cleanliness of the place where we live." Write one word for the above statement. A: Sanitation. Sanitation means keeping our homes, surroundings and environment clean and free from dirt and germs.
chunks.source: Sanitation means keeping our homes, surroundings and environment clean and free from dirt and germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is fire useful at school? A: It is used for cooking food and boiling drinking water. At school, fire is mainly used in the kitchen to cook meals and to boil water so it is safe to drink.
chunks.source: At school, fire is mainly used in the kitchen to cook meals and to boil water so it is safe to drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one use of sisal material at school. A: Making ropes (or mats, or scrubbing brushes). Sisal fibres are strong and tough, so they are used to make ropes, mats and scrubbing brushes.
chunks.source: Sisal fibres are strong and tough, so they are used to make ropes, mats and scrubbing brushes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Joan likes sharing sharp body cutting objects with her friends. How is this practice dangerous to their health? A: They can spread HIV/AIDS and tetanus through shared blood on the objects. Sharing razors, blades or needles can transfer infected blood from one person to another, spreading diseases like HIV/AIDS and tetanus.
chunks.source: Sharing razors, blades or needles can transfer infected blood from one person to another, spreading diseases like HIV/AIDS and tetanus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which human organ has the same function as the gills of a fish? A: The lungs. Just as gills take oxygen from water for the fish, the lungs take oxygen from air for the human body.
chunks.source: Just as gills take oxygen from water for the fish, the lungs take oxygen from air for the human body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you control the spread of diarrhea at home? A: Boil drinking water and wash hands with soap before eating. Diarrhoea germs spread through dirty water and dirty hands, so boiling water and handwashing stop them.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea germs spread through dirty water and dirty hands, so boiling water and handwashing stop them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below shows parts of an egg. Use it to answer questions 15 and 16.
15. Name part marked X on the diagram above. A: Egg white (albumen). X points to the clear part surrounding the yolk, which is called the egg white or albumen.
chunks.source: X points to the clear part surrounding the yolk, which is called the egg white or albumen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. Identify one animal at home that produces eggs. A: Hen (chicken). The hen is the common home bird that lays the eggs people eat.
chunks.source: The hen is the common home bird that lays the eggs people eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way can windy weather be helpful to people? A: It is used for winnowing grain and for drying clothes and crops. Wind helps farmers separate grain from chaff during winnowing and dries clothes and harvested crops faster.
chunks.source: Wind helps farmers separate grain from chaff during winnowing and dries clothes and harvested crops faster.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are some metallic tools painted? A: To prevent them from rusting. Paint covers the metal so air and water cannot reach it, which stops rust from forming.
chunks.source: Paint covers the metal so air and water cannot reach it, which stops rust from forming.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens to water when it is heated? A: It boils and changes into steam (water vapour). Heating makes water evaporate faster, and at boiling point it turns into steam, an invisible gas.
chunks.source: Heating makes water evaporate faster, and at boiling point it turns into steam, an invisible gas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one use of food in the body. A: It gives the body energy (or builds the body, or protects the body against diseases). Food gives us energy for work and play, builds our body tissues, and protects us from diseases.
chunks.source: Food gives us energy for work and play, builds our body tissues, and protects us from diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it dangerous to cross the road carelessly? A: You can be knocked down by a moving vehicle and get badly hurt or killed. Careless crossing causes road accidents because drivers may not be able to stop in time.
chunks.source: Careless crossing causes road accidents because drivers may not be able to stop in time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below shows a cabbage plant. Use it to answer question 22.
22. How is part labeled B useful to people? A: It is eaten as a vegetable (food). Part B is the cabbage head made of leaves, which people cook and eat as a vegetable.
chunks.source: Part B is the cabbage head made of leaves, which people cook and eat as a vegetable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the gas given off by plants during photosynthesis. A: Oxygen. During photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen into the air.
chunks.source: During photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen into the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one material used for constructing a permanent house. A: Bricks (or cement, or iron sheets, or timber). Permanent houses are built with strong, long-lasting materials such as bricks, cement and iron sheets.
chunks.source: Permanent houses are built with strong, long-lasting materials such as bricks, cement and iron sheets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. Draw the shadow of the object below in the right position. (The diagram shows a bottle with the sun shining from the top right.) A: A dark bottle-shaped shadow drawn on the ground on the side away from the sun (to the lower left of the bottle). A shadow always forms on the opposite side of the light source, so the bottle's shadow falls away from the sun.
chunks.source: A shadow always forms on the opposite side of the light source, so the bottle's shadow falls away from the sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one foodstuff we get from a lake. A: Fish. Lakes are a source of fish, which is an important body-building food for people.
chunks.source: Lakes are a source of fish, which is an important body-building food for people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By what process are nimbus clouds formed? A: Condensation. Water vapour cools high in the sky and condenses into tiny droplets that join to form nimbus clouds.
chunks.source: Water vapour cools high in the sky and condenses into tiny droplets that join to form nimbus clouds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do people lock their houses at night? A: To keep thieves out and protect the family and property (for security). Locking doors at night stops thieves from entering and keeps everyone inside safe.
chunks.source: Locking doors at night stops thieves from entering and keeps everyone inside safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is wind? A: Wind is moving air. When air moves from one place to another, we feel it as wind.
chunks.source: When air moves from one place to another, we feel it as wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of a bean seed stores food? A: The cotyledon. The cotyledons are the two fleshy halves of a bean seed that store food for the young plant.
chunks.source: The cotyledons are the two fleshy halves of a bean seed that store food for the young plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it bad to share a towel with other people? A: It spreads skin diseases and germs from one person to another. Towels pick up sweat and germs from the body, so sharing them passes skin infections between people.
chunks.source: Towels pick up sweat and germs from the body, so sharing them passes skin infections between people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one way you can save energy at home. A: Switch off lights and electrical appliances when not in use. Turning off unused bulbs and machines saves electricity and reduces the power bill.
chunks.source: Turning off unused bulbs and machines saves electricity and reduces the power bill.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you help a person who is dehydrated? A: Give them ORS solution or plenty of clean fluids to drink. A dehydrated person has lost body water, so giving ORS or clean water replaces the lost fluids and salts.
chunks.source: A dehydrated person has lost body water, so giving ORS or clean water replaces the lost fluids and salts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 34. Fill in the missing stage.
Egg -> larva -> _______ -> adult A: Pupa. Insects with complete metamorphosis develop in four stages: egg, larva, pupa, then adult.
chunks.source: Insects with complete metamorphosis develop in four stages: egg, larva, pupa, then adult.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way you can care for insects like bees. A: Do not destroy their hives; plant flowers for them to feed on. Bees need safe homes and flowers for nectar, so we protect their hives and avoid spraying chemicals near them.
chunks.source: Bees need safe homes and flowers for nectar, so we protect their hives and avoid spraying chemicals near them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one health habit you can teach your young brother or sister to do. A: Washing hands with soap before eating (or brushing teeth daily, or bathing daily). Teaching young children to wash hands, brush teeth and bathe daily keeps them free from diseases.
chunks.source: Teaching young children to wash hands, brush teeth and bathe daily keeps them free from diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you prevent worms from entering your body? A: Wear shoes, wash hands with soap, and drink boiled water. Worms enter through bare feet, dirty hands and dirty water, so shoes, handwashing and boiled water block them.
chunks.source: Worms enter through bare feet, dirty hands and dirty water, so shoes, handwashing and boiled water block them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way people make use of rain water. A: Collecting it in tanks for drinking, washing and watering plants. Rain water is harvested from roofs into tanks and used for domestic work and farming.
chunks.source: Rain water is harvested from roofs into tanks and used for domestic work and farming.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What advice can you give to a person who has lice in the hair? A: Shave or treat the hair with lice medicine, and wash all combs, towels and bedding. Lice are killed by shaving the hair or using medicated shampoo, and washing everything the hair touches stops them spreading.
chunks.source: Lice are killed by shaving the hair or using medicated shampoo, and washing everything the hair touches stops them spreading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. What does the experiment below prove about soil? (A lump of soil is dropped in water and bubbles rise up.) A: It proves that soil contains air. When the soil lump is put in water, trapped air escapes as bubbles, showing that soil has air in it.
chunks.source: When the soil lump is put in water, trapped air escapes as bubbles, showing that soil has air in it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 41. Match items in list A with those in list B.
A: Forked hoe, Knapsack sprayer, Trowel, Fertilizers
B: transplanting seedlings, improve on soil fertility, spraying herbicides, digging hard ground
a) Forked hoe
b) Knapsack sprayer
c) Trowel
d) Fertilizers A: Fertilizers: improve on soil fertility; Forked hoe: digging hard ground; Knapsack sprayer: spraying herbicides; Trowel: transplanting seedlings. Each garden tool has its work: the forked hoe breaks hard ground, the knapsack sprayer sprays chemicals, the trowel moves seedlings, and fertilizers feed the soil.
chunks.source: Each garden tool has its work: the forked hoe breaks hard ground, the knapsack sprayer sprays chemicals, the trowel moves seedlings, and fertilizers feed the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 42. a) Name any two materials used in cleaning our bodies.
b) Give one disease that we get due to poor personal hygiene.
c) How can you promote personal hygiene? A: a) Water and soap (also: sponge, towel, toothbrush). b) Scabies (or ringworms, or diarrhoea). c) By bathing daily, brushing teeth, washing hands and keeping clothes clean. We clean our bodies with water, soap and a sponge; poor body cleanliness causes skin diseases like scabies; daily washing habits promote personal hygiene.
chunks.source: We clean our bodies with water, soap and a sponge; poor body cleanliness causes skin diseases like scabies; daily washing habits promote personal hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 43. a) Give any one way we can make water safe for drinking.
b) Write any two ways in which water sources may get contaminated.
c) Name any one natural source of water. A: a) By boiling it. b) Dumping rubbish near the source; animals drinking and defecating in it. c) Spring (or river, lake, rain, well). Boiling kills germs in water; water sources get dirty from waste and animals; natural sources include springs, rivers and lakes.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs in water; water sources get dirty from waste and animals; natural sources include springs, rivers and lakes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 44. The diagram below shows part of the human body. Use it to answer question 44.
a) Name the body organs marked T and S.
b) Give any one use of organ marked T.
c) How can you care for the organ marked R above? A: a) T is the brain; S is the stomach. b) The brain controls the body and is used for thinking and remembering. c) Avoid smoking and dusty air; do breathing exercises. T marks the brain in the head, S marks the stomach in the belly, and R marks the lungs, which stay healthy with clean air and exercise.
chunks.source: T marks the brain in the head, S marks the stomach in the belly, and R marks the lungs, which stay healthy with clean air and exercise.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 45. a) State any two reasons for giving first aid to accident victims.
b) Write any two items that are found in a first aid box. A: a) To save life and to reduce pain (also: to prevent the injury from getting worse). b) Bandage and iodine (also: scissors, cotton wool, painkillers, spirit). First aid keeps an injured person alive and comfortable before the doctor comes, using items like bandages and antiseptics from the first aid box.
chunks.source: First aid keeps an injured person alive and comfortable before the doctor comes, using items like bandages and antiseptics from the first aid box.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 46. The diagram below is of a food store found in village homes. Use it to answer the questions below.
a) Name the food store shown above.
b) How are structures marked K important on the food store above?
c) Identify any two crops that can be stored in the food store above. A: a) Granary. b) K are the raised legs/supports; they lift the store off the ground so pests like rats cannot reach the grain and dampness cannot spoil it. c) Maize and beans (also: millet, sorghum, cassava, groundnuts). A granary is a raised village food store; its legs keep grain safe from pests and moisture, and it stores dry crops like maize and beans.
chunks.source: A granary is a raised village food store; its legs keep grain safe from pests and moisture, and it stores dry crops like maize and beans.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 47. a) Give any two food values that make up a balanced diet.
b) Write any two diseases caused by poor feeding. A: a) Carbohydrates and proteins (also: vitamins, fats, minerals). b) Kwashiorkor and marasmus (also: anaemia, goitre, rickets). A balanced diet contains all food values like carbohydrates and proteins; lacking them causes deficiency diseases such as kwashiorkor and marasmus.
chunks.source: A balanced diet contains all food values like carbohydrates and proteins; lacking them causes deficiency diseases such as kwashiorkor and marasmus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 48. The diagram below shows part of a plant. Use it to answer the questions that follow.
a) Name the part of the plant shown above.
b) What is the importance of the part shown above to a plant?
c) Name part marked V and X on the diagram above. A: a) Flower. b) It is the reproductive part; it makes seeds and fruits so new plants can grow. c) V is the sepal; X is the petal. The flower is where reproduction happens in a plant; its colourful petals attract insects and its sepals protect the bud.
chunks.source: The flower is where reproduction happens in a plant; its colourful petals attract insects and its sepals protect the bud.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 49. a) Write two insects which are useful to people.
b) State any one danger of insects to people.
c) Identify any one characteristic of insects. A: a) Bees and butterflies (also: ladybird beetles). b) Some sting or bite people; some spread diseases; some destroy crops. c) They have six legs (also: three body parts; a pair of antennae). Useful insects like bees give honey and pollinate crops, but insects can also sting, spread disease or eat crops; all insects have six legs.
chunks.source: Useful insects like bees give honey and pollinate crops, but insects can also sting, spread disease or eat crops; all insects have six legs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 50. a) Name the part of a fish which it uses for:
(i) smelling
(ii) breathing
(iii) feeding
b) Give any one reason why people catch fish. A: a) (i) Nostrils; (ii) Gills; (iii) Mouth. b) For food (also: to earn money by selling). A fish smells with its nostrils, breathes with its gills and feeds with its mouth; people catch fish mainly as food.
chunks.source: A fish smells with its nostrils, breathes with its gills and feeds with its mouth; people catch fish mainly as food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 51. The diagram below shows a tooth. Use it to answer the questions that follow.
a) Name the part marked B and C.
b) Which part of a tooth is the hardest?
c) How is the tooth in the diagram above useful to people? A: a) B is the crown; C is the root. b) The enamel. c) It is used for biting and cutting food (it is an incisor). The crown is the visible top of the tooth and the root fixes it in the gum; enamel is the hardest part; incisors bite and cut food.
chunks.source: The crown is the visible top of the tooth and the root fixes it in the gum; enamel is the hardest part; incisors bite and cut food.
