chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 52. Apart from extended family, name any other type of family in your area.
b) Write any two groups of people found in an extended family.
a) Give the member of a family who breast feeds the baby at home. A: Nuclear family. b) Uncles and aunts (also: cousins, grandparents). a) Mother. A nuclear family has parents and their children only; extended families include uncles, aunts, cousins and grandparents; the mother breastfeeds the baby.
chunks.source: A nuclear family has parents and their children only; extended families include uncles, aunts, cousins and grandparents; the mother breastfeeds the baby.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 53. a) Give any two examples of pests that attack crops in the garden.
b) How can you control pests in a crop garden? (give two ways) A: a) Aphids and caterpillars (also: weevils, termites, cutworms). b) By spraying with pesticides and by practising crop rotation (also: weeding, hand-picking pests). Pests like aphids and caterpillars damage crops, and farmers control them by spraying, weeding and rotating crops.
chunks.source: Pests like aphids and caterpillars damage crops, and farmers control them by spraying, weeding and rotating crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 54. The picture below shows a health facility in our area. Use it to answer the questions below.
b) Identify any two groups of people that work in the above facility.
c) Which group of people are carried to the facility above?
d) Write any one way you would take care of a person who is in the facility above. A: b) Doctors and nurses. c) Patients (sick people). d) By giving them food and medicine and keeping them clean (also: visiting and comforting them). A hospital employs doctors and nurses who treat patients brought in by ambulance; we care for the sick by feeding them, giving medicine and keeping them clean.
chunks.source: A hospital employs doctors and nurses who treat patients brought in by ambulance; we care for the sick by feeding them, giving medicine and keeping them clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55. a) Draw and name any two materials used in cleaning kitchen utensils. A: Two labelled drawings, e.g. a scrubbing brush labelled 'scrubbing brush' and a scouring pad (steel wool) labelled 'scouring pad' (also: sponge, sisal fibre, sand, detergent). Kitchen utensils are cleaned with materials like scrubbing brushes, scouring pads, sponges and sisal that scrub off dirt.
chunks.source: Kitchen utensils are cleaned with materials like scrubbing brushes, scouring pads, sponges and sisal that scrub off dirt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 56. Name any one component of soil. A: Air (also: water, humus, rock particles, living organisms). Soil is made of rock particles, humus, water, air and living organisms.
chunks.source: Soil is made of rock particles, humus, water, air and living organisms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 57. Which part of the human body is used for feeling? A: The skin. The skin all over our body feels touch, heat, cold and pain.
chunks.source: The skin all over our body feels touch, heat, cold and pain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 58. Why is a bean plant grouped under flowering plants? A: Because it produces flowers (which develop into fruits with seeds). Flowering plants reproduce by making flowers, and the bean plant produces flowers, so it belongs to this group.
chunks.source: Flowering plants reproduce by making flowers, and the bean plant produces flowers, so it belongs to this group.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 59. How can you control soil erosion in a school compound? A: By planting grass and trees (also: mulching, terracing). Plant cover holds the soil together so running water cannot wash it away.
chunks.source: Plant cover holds the soil together so running water cannot wash it away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 60. Why are garden tools kept in cool dry places after use? A: To prevent them from rusting. Cool dry places keep air and moisture away from metal tools, so they do not rust.
chunks.source: Cool dry places keep air and moisture away from metal tools, so they do not rust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below is of a human tooth. Study it and answer question 61.
61. Name the above tooth. A: Canine (eye tooth). The pointed tooth used for tearing food is called a canine.
chunks.source: The pointed tooth used for tearing food is called a canine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 62. Write ORS in full. A: Oral Rehydration Salts. ORS is a mixture of salt and sugar dissolved in clean water, given to people who have lost body fluids.
chunks.source: ORS is a mixture of salt and sugar dissolved in clean water, given to people who have lost body fluids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 63. How is heavy rainfall dangerous to people? A: It causes floods that destroy crops and houses and can drown people and animals. Too much rain makes rivers overflow, flooding homes and gardens and sweeping away people and animals.
chunks.source: Too much rain makes rivers overflow, flooding homes and gardens and sweeping away people and animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 64. How are foods rich in proteins important to a seven year old boy? A: They build his body and help him grow. Proteins are body-building foods that make muscles and help children grow strong.
chunks.source: Proteins are body-building foods that make muscles and help children grow strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 65. Why should we cover leftover food at home? A: To prevent flies, dust and germs from contaminating it. Covering food keeps off flies and dust that carry germs which cause diseases.
chunks.source: Covering food keeps off flies and dust that carry germs which cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 66. Why should we keep our bodies clean? A: To prevent diseases and smell good. Clean bodies do not carry germs that cause skin diseases, and they do not smell bad.
chunks.source: Clean bodies do not carry germs that cause skin diseases, and they do not smell bad.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 67. Give any one use of water at home. A: For drinking (also: cooking, washing, bathing). Water at home is used for drinking, cooking food, washing clothes and bathing.
chunks.source: Water at home is used for drinking, cooking food, washing clothes and bathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 68. Why is the heart important in the human body? A: It pumps blood to all parts of the body. The heart pushes blood carrying food and oxygen to every part of the body.
chunks.source: The heart pushes blood carrying food and oxygen to every part of the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below is of a bird. Use it to answer questions 69 and 70.
69. Name part marked with letter Y. A: Comb. Y points to the red fleshy crest on top of the cock's head, which is called the comb.
chunks.source: Y points to the red fleshy crest on top of the cock's head, which is called the comb.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 70. By use of an arrow and letter X, show the part which is used to pick food. A: An arrow marked X pointing to the beak. The bird picks its food using its hard pointed beak.
chunks.source: The bird picks its food using its hard pointed beak.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 71. Give any one way a P.2 child can cross a busy road safely. A: By using the zebra crossing (also: holding an adult's hand; looking left, right and left again). Children cross safely at marked crossings and with an adult, after checking that no vehicle is coming.
chunks.source: Children cross safely at marked crossings and with an adult, after checking that no vehicle is coming.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 72. In the space below, draw one item used to manage sunny weather. A: A drawing of an umbrella (or a wide hat, or sunglasses) labelled with its name. An umbrella or hat gives shade and protects us from the hot sun.
chunks.source: An umbrella or hat gives shade and protects us from the hot sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 73. Name any one disease that we can control by boiling water for drinking at home. A: Cholera (also: typhoid, diarrhoea, dysentery). Boiling kills the germs in water that cause water-borne diseases like cholera and typhoid.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs in water that cause water-borne diseases like cholera and typhoid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 74. State the first aid for a burn. A: Pour clean cold water on the burn and cover it with a clean cloth. Cold water cools the burn and reduces pain, and a clean cover keeps germs away.
chunks.source: Cold water cools the burn and reduces pain, and a clean cover keeps germs away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 75. In the space provided below, draw a diagram to show network leaf venation. A: A drawing of a leaf with veins branching like a net from a central midrib. In network venation, veins spread from the midrib and branch again like a fishing net.
chunks.source: In network venation, veins spread from the midrib and branch again like a fishing net.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 76. Looking at the watery stool of a patient, how can you tell that the person has dysentery? A: The stool contains blood. Dysentery is a disease of the intestines whose watery stool is mixed with blood.
chunks.source: Dysentery is a disease of the intestines whose watery stool is mixed with blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 77. How are stars useful to people? A: They give light at night and help travellers find direction. Stars light the night sky and people long used them to find their way when travelling.
chunks.source: Stars light the night sky and people long used them to find their way when travelling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 78. Why should people close doors and windows early in the evening? A: To prevent mosquitoes from entering the house (and spreading malaria). Mosquitoes enter homes in the evening, so closing doors and windows early keeps them out.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes enter homes in the evening, so closing doors and windows early keeps them out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 79. How are rat guards useful on a granary? A: They prevent rats from climbing up into the granary. Rat guards are wide discs fixed on the granary legs that stop rats climbing up to eat the stored grain.
chunks.source: Rat guards are wide discs fixed on the granary legs that stop rats climbing up to eat the stored grain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 80. Why is it dangerous to stay with domestic animals in the same house? A: Animals spread diseases and dirt to people. Domestic animals carry germs, fleas and dirt that can make people sick when they share living space.
chunks.source: Domestic animals carry germs, fleas and dirt that can make people sick when they share living space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 81. Give the importance of chlorophyll during photosynthesis. A: It traps sunlight energy used to make food. Chlorophyll is the green colouring that captures energy from sunlight so the plant can make food.
chunks.source: Chlorophyll is the green colouring that captures energy from sunlight so the plant can make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 82. Give any one use of electricity at home. A: For lighting the house (also: ironing, cooking, charging phones). Electricity at home is mainly used to give light and to run appliances like irons and cookers.
chunks.source: Electricity at home is mainly used to give light and to run appliances like irons and cookers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 83. Mention any one use of carbon dioxide to people. A: It is used in fire extinguishers (also: in making sodas and soft drinks). Carbon dioxide puts out fires and is also pumped into sodas to make them fizzy.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide puts out fires and is also pumped into sodas to make them fizzy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 84. Give any one way people use bricks in our community. A: For building houses and walls. Bricks are strong building blocks used to put up houses, schools and walls.
chunks.source: Bricks are strong building blocks used to put up houses, schools and walls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 85. Name the staple food drawn below. A: Bananas (matooke). The drawing shows a bunch of bananas, which is the staple food (matooke) in many Ugandan homes.
chunks.source: The drawing shows a bunch of bananas, which is the staple food (matooke) in many Ugandan homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 86. Why should every classroom have a dustbin? A: For proper disposal of rubbish to keep the classroom clean. A dustbin collects waste paper and dirt so the classroom stays clean and healthy.
chunks.source: A dustbin collects waste paper and dirt so the classroom stays clean and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 87. How do farmers preserve maize after harvesting? A: By drying it in the sun and storing it in a granary or sacks. Maize is sun-dried to remove moisture and then kept in a dry granary or sacks so it does not rot.
chunks.source: Maize is sun-dried to remove moisture and then kept in a dry granary or sacks so it does not rot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 88. State any one way in which people may damage the environment. A: By cutting down trees carelessly (also: bush burning, dumping rubbish, swamp drainage). Deforestation and other bad practices destroy the environment that people depend on.
chunks.source: Deforestation and other bad practices destroy the environment that people depend on.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 89. Give any one way we can care for our eyes. A: By not touching them with dirty hands and washing the face with clean water. Dirty hands put germs into the eyes, so we keep hands and face clean to protect our sight.
chunks.source: Dirty hands put germs into the eyes, so we keep hands and face clean to protect our sight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 90. How is the structure below useful to a spider? A: It traps insects which the spider eats as food. The spider spins a sticky web that catches flying insects, giving the spider its food.
chunks.source: The spider spins a sticky web that catches flying insects, giving the spider its food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 91. State any one way of controlling the spread of germs at home. A: By washing hands with soap (also: using a clean latrine, covering food). Germs spread through dirty hands, so washing them stops germs reaching food and mouths.
chunks.source: Germs spread through dirty hands, so washing them stops germs reaching food and mouths.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 92. How are plants useful to animals? A: Plants give animals food, oxygen and shelter. Animals eat plants, breathe the oxygen plants release, and shelter under them.
chunks.source: Animals eat plants, breathe the oxygen plants release, and shelter under them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 93. Draw the garden tool used to harvest cereals. A: A drawing of a sickle: a curved metal blade with a short wooden handle, labelled 'sickle'. A sickle is the curved hand tool farmers swing to cut cereal stems at harvest.
chunks.source: A sickle is the curved hand tool farmers swing to cut cereal stems at harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 94. What is soil erosion? A: Soil erosion is the carrying away of top soil by running water or wind. When rain or wind removes the fertile top layer of soil, we call it soil erosion.
chunks.source: When rain or wind removes the fertile top layer of soil, we call it soil erosion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 95. Write down any one item that can be used in water harvesting at home. A: A jerrycan (also: tank, drum, gutter, basin). Water harvesting collects rain water in containers like jerrycans, drums and tanks.
chunks.source: Water harvesting collects rain water in containers like jerrycans, drums and tanks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 96. (a) State any two ways of maintaining proper sanitation at home.
(b) Name any two diseases that can be spread through poor sanitation. A: (a) Sweeping the compound and disposing of rubbish properly; using a clean latrine. (b) Cholera and diarrhoea (also: typhoid, dysentery). Good sanitation means a clean compound and proper waste disposal; poor sanitation spreads diseases like cholera and diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Good sanitation means a clean compound and proper waste disposal; poor sanitation spreads diseases like cholera and diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 97. (a) What do the following worms feed on in the human body?
(i) Hook worms
(ii) Tape worms
(b) Besides the above worms, mention one other worm which affects the human body.
(c) How can worms be prevented? A: (a) (i) Hook worms feed on blood; (ii) Tape worms feed on digested food in the intestines. (b) Roundworms (ascaris). (c) By wearing shoes, washing hands, drinking boiled water and using a latrine. Hook worms suck blood while tape worms absorb digested food; roundworms also attack people; cleanliness and shoes keep worms away.
chunks.source: Hook worms suck blood while tape worms absorb digested food; roundworms also attack people; cleanliness and shoes keep worms away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 98. (a) What is a resource?
(b) State any one use of electricity at home.
(c) How can electricity be dangerous to people at home?
(d) State one way of saving electricity as an energy resource. A: (a) A resource is anything in the environment that people use to meet their needs. (b) For lighting. (c) It can shock, burn or start fires. (d) By switching off appliances when not in use. Resources are useful things like water and electricity; electricity lights homes but can shock or burn; switching off saves it.
chunks.source: Resources are useful things like water and electricity; electricity lights homes but can shock or burn; switching off saves it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 99. (a) How do we use the item below at home? (The diagram shows a razor blade.)
(b) Why do we brush our teeth after every meal?
(c) Name any two diseases spread as a result of poor personal hygiene. A: (a) For shaving hair (also: for cutting). (b) To remove food particles and prevent tooth decay. (c) Scabies and ringworms (also: cholera, diarrhoea). A razor blade shaves hair; brushing after meals removes food that rots teeth; poor hygiene brings diseases like scabies.
chunks.source: A razor blade shaves hair; brushing after meals removes food that rots teeth; poor hygiene brings diseases like scabies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 100. (a) Give the importance of these parts to a plant.
(i) Leaves
(ii) Roots
(b) Write down any two uses of stems to people. A: (a) Leaves make food for the plant (photosynthesis); roots absorb water and mineral salts and anchor the plant. (b) For firewood and building (also: sugarcane stems give sugar; stems are eaten as food). Leaves cook food for the plant using sunlight while roots drink water and hold the plant firm; stems give people wood and food.
chunks.source: Leaves cook food for the plant using sunlight while roots drink water and hold the plant firm; stems give people wood and food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 101. The diagram below shows one of the properties of air. Use it to answer the questions that follow. (A balance with an inflated balloon on one side and a deflated balloon on the other; the inflated side goes down.)
(a) Which property of air is shown above?
(b) What is air?
(c) Which part of air helps burning to take place?
(d) What name is given to moving air? A: (a) Air has weight. (b) Air is a mixture of gases. (c) Oxygen. (d) Wind. The inflated balloon is heavier and pulls its side down, proving air has weight; air is a mixture of gases including oxygen, and moving air is wind.
chunks.source: The inflated balloon is heavier and pulls its side down, proving air has weight; air is a mixture of gases including oxygen, and moving air is wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 102. (a) State any two causes of accidents on our roads today.
(b) Why are accident victims given first aid? (give two reasons) A: (a) Over-speeding and drunk driving (also: careless crossing, bad roads). (b) To save life and reduce pain (also: to stop the injury worsening). Speeding and drunk driving cause road accidents; first aid keeps victims alive and comfortable before medical help arrives.
chunks.source: Speeding and drunk driving cause road accidents; first aid keeps victims alive and comfortable before medical help arrives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 103. (a) Write down any one cause of dehydration.
(b) Why are dehydrated people given plenty of drinking water?
(c) Identify any two materials used in the making of oral rehydration solution (ORS) at home. A: (a) Diarrhoea (also: vomiting, drinking too little water). (b) To replace the water lost from the body. (c) Salt and sugar (dissolved in clean boiled water). Diarrhoea drains water from the body, so victims drink plenty of water; ORS made from salt and sugar replaces lost fluids and salts.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea drains water from the body, so victims drink plenty of water; ORS made from salt and sugar replaces lost fluids and salts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 104. (a) Why are termites called social insects?
(b) Name the habitat for termites.
(c) How are termites dangerous to crop farmers?
(d) Besides termites, name any other example of social insects. A: (a) Because they live together in organized colonies. (b) Anthills (termitaria). (c) They destroy crops. (d) Bees (also: ants, wasps). Termites are social because they live and work together in colonies inside anthills; they eat crops, like bees and ants they are social insects.
chunks.source: Termites are social because they live and work together in colonies inside anthills; they eat crops, like bees and ants they are social insects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 105. The diagram below is of a flower.
(a) Name parts marked N and T.
(b) By use of an arrow and letter P, show the part that produces pollen grains.
(c) What is the main work of a flower to a plant? A: (a) N is the stigma; T is the ovary. (b) An arrow marked P pointing to an anther (the pollen-bearing tip of a stamen). (c) Reproduction - it makes seeds and fruits. The stigma (N) receives pollen and the ovary (T) holds the ovules; anthers produce pollen grains; the flower's main work is reproduction.
chunks.source: The stigma (N) receives pollen and the ovary (T) holds the ovules; anthers produce pollen grains; the flower's main work is reproduction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 106. (a) Name any one food we can get from these places;
(i) Forests
(ii) Swamps
(iii) Rivers
(b) Give any one tool we can use to collect food from the river. A: (a) (i) Forests: wild fruits (also: mushrooms, honey); (ii) Swamps: papyrus (also: fish); (iii) Rivers: fish. (b) Fishing net (also: hook, basket trap). Forests give wild fruits, swamps give papyrus and fish, rivers give fish, which people catch with nets and hooks.
chunks.source: Forests give wild fruits, swamps give papyrus and fish, rivers give fish, which people catch with nets and hooks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 107. Match the body organs in A to their functions in B correctly.
A: Kidney, Liver, Stomach, Brain
B: stores food for some time, stores information, produces bile, filters blood
a) Kidney
b) Liver
c) Stomach
d) Brain A: Brain: stores information.; Kidney: filters blood.; Liver: produces bile.; Stomach: stores food for some time.. The kidney cleans blood, the liver makes bile for digestion, the stomach holds food, and the brain stores what we learn.
chunks.source: The kidney cleans blood, the liver makes bile for digestion, the stomach holds food, and the brain stores what we learn.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 108. (a) Apart from the extended family, name any one other type of family in Uganda.
(b) Give any one role of the following people in a family.
(i) Children
(ii) Mother
(a) Write any one advantage of an extended family. A: (a) Nuclear family. (b) (i) Children: do house chores; (ii) Mother: cooks food and cares for children. (a) It is easy to manage (also: unity; fewer quarrels). A nuclear family is parents and children only; children help with chores while the mother cooks and cares; small families are easy to manage.
chunks.source: A nuclear family is parents and children only; children help with chores while the mother cooks and cares; small families are easy to manage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 109. (a) What are vectors?
(b) Name any one vector commonly found in pit latrines.
(c) Give any two ways in which the above vector can be controlled. A: (a) Vectors are animals that spread diseases to people. (b) Housefly. (c) By covering the latrine hole and spraying with insecticide (also: proper disposal of faeces). Vectors carry disease germs from dirty places to people; houseflies breed in pit latrines; covering holes and spraying control them.
chunks.source: Vectors carry disease germs from dirty places to people; houseflies breed in pit latrines; covering holes and spraying control them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 110. Use the words provided in the box to complete the passage below. (Word box: sun, condensed, clouds, evaporation, water vapour)
The water cycle.
During rain formation, the _______ heats water bodies like oceans, lakes, seas, rivers, swamps to cause _______. The _______ rises up to the sky and is _______ to form nimbus clouds. The droplets of water from clouds then fall down as rain. The water flows and collects in water bodies and the cycle continues. A: The sun heats water bodies to cause evaporation. The water vapour rises and is condensed to form nimbus clouds. The sun's heat evaporates water into vapour, which rises, cools and condenses into clouds that later fall as rain.
chunks.source: The sun's heat evaporates water into vapour, which rises, cools and condenses into clouds that later fall as rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1) Name any one type of soil you know. A: Loam soil (also: sand soil, clay soil). There are three main types of soil: sand, clay and loam, and loam is the most fertile.
chunks.source: There are three main types of soil: sand, clay and loam, and loam is the most fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2) How does regular bathing control the spread of skin diseases? A: It removes dirt and germs from the skin. Bathing washes away sweat, dirt and germs that cause skin diseases.
chunks.source: Bathing washes away sweat, dirt and germs that cause skin diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3) Identify any one way strong wind can be dangerous to a crop farmer. A: It can destroy crops (also: it blows away top soil). Strong wind breaks crop stems and can blow away the fertile top soil from gardens.
chunks.source: Strong wind breaks crop stems and can blow away the fertile top soil from gardens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4) Write any one common accident at school. A: Falling down (also: cuts, burns, bruises). Children at school commonly get hurt by falling while playing or running.
chunks.source: Children at school commonly get hurt by falling while playing or running.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5) How are the ears important to a person? A: They are used for hearing. The ears collect sound waves so we can hear voices, music and warnings.
chunks.source: The ears collect sound waves so we can hear voices, music and warnings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6) Give one way the part below is useful to a plant. (The diagram shows leaves.) A: They make food for the plant (photosynthesis). Leaves use sunlight, air and water to make food that feeds the whole plant.
chunks.source: Leaves use sunlight, air and water to make food that feeds the whole plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7) Why is a balanced diet needed by every person? A: It gives the body all the food values needed for growth and good health. A balanced diet contains carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins and minerals that keep every person healthy.
chunks.source: A balanced diet contains carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins and minerals that keep every person healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8) Identify any one way people take care of domestic animals at home. A: By feeding them well (also: housing them, treating them when sick). Domestic animals stay healthy when they are given enough food, clean shelter and treatment.
chunks.source: Domestic animals stay healthy when they are given enough food, clean shelter and treatment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 9) Give one way water sources can be contaminated. A: By dumping rubbish near the source (also: animals defecating in it). Waste and animal droppings wash into water sources and pollute them with germs.
chunks.source: Waste and animal droppings wash into water sources and pollute them with germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10) Draw and name any one item used to manage rainy weather. A: A labelled drawing of an umbrella (or raincoat, or gumboots). Umbrellas, raincoats and gumboots protect us from rain during rainy weather.
chunks.source: Umbrellas, raincoats and gumboots protect us from rain during rainy weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11) How can you keep proper personal hygiene? A: By bathing daily, brushing teeth and washing hands with soap. Daily washing of the body, teeth and hands keeps germs away and promotes personal hygiene.
chunks.source: Daily washing of the body, teeth and hands keeps germs away and promotes personal hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12) In the space provided below, draw a diagram to show air has weight. A: A drawing of a balance with an inflated balloon on one side and a deflated balloon on the other, the inflated side hanging lower. The inflated balloon is heavier because air has weight, so its side of the balance goes down.
chunks.source: The inflated balloon is heavier because air has weight, so its side of the balance goes down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 13) Mention any one way mulching is useful to farmers. A: It keeps moisture in the soil (also: it controls weeds; it rots to add fertility). Mulch covers the soil so water does not evaporate quickly and weeds cannot grow.
chunks.source: Mulch covers the soil so water does not evaporate quickly and weeds cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14) Why do people eat food? A: To get energy and to grow. Food gives the body energy for work and nutrients for growth.
chunks.source: Food gives the body energy for work and nutrients for growth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15) How is the larva stage of a butterfly dangerous to crop farmers? A: It eats and destroys the leaves of crops. Butterfly larvae (caterpillars) feed on crop leaves, damaging the farmer's harvest.
chunks.source: Butterfly larvae (caterpillars) feed on crop leaves, damaging the farmer's harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16) Name any one disease spread by a housefly. A: Cholera (also: typhoid, dysentery, diarrhoea). Houseflies carry germs from faeces to food, spreading diseases like cholera.
chunks.source: Houseflies carry germs from faeces to food, spreading diseases like cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below is a garden tool. Use it to answer questions 17 and 18.
17) Identify one use of the above garden tool to people. A: For carrying loads like manure, harvested crops and soil. A wheelbarrow is a garden tool with one wheel used to transport heavy loads around the farm.
chunks.source: A wheelbarrow is a garden tool with one wheel used to transport heavy loads around the farm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18) How can the above tool be cared for? A: By cleaning it after use, oiling the moving parts and keeping it in a dry place. Cleaning and oiling prevent rust, and dry storage keeps the wheelbarrow strong for long use.
chunks.source: Cleaning and oiling prevent rust, and dry storage keeps the wheelbarrow strong for long use.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19) How do farmers benefit from nimbus clouds? A: They bring rain which waters the crops. Nimbus are rain clouds, and farmers depend on their rain for crops to grow well.
chunks.source: Nimbus are rain clouds, and farmers depend on their rain for crops to grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 20) With the help of a pencil, draw an arrow to show the part used for flying. (The diagram shows a housefly.) A: An arrow pointing to the wings. The housefly flies using its pair of wings.
chunks.source: The housefly flies using its pair of wings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21) State any one reason why first aid is given to casualties. A: To save the life of the casualty (also: to reduce pain). Quick first aid keeps an injured person alive until proper medical help arrives.
chunks.source: Quick first aid keeps an injured person alive until proper medical help arrives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22) Draw and name any play material made from banana fibres. A: A labelled drawing of a doll (or ball) made from banana fibres. Banana fibres are woven into playthings like dolls and balls for children.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are woven into playthings like dolls and balls for children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23) Identify any one activity a farmer carries out during the wet season. A: Planting crops. Farmers plant their crops in the wet season when there is enough rain for seeds to grow.
chunks.source: Farmers plant their crops in the wet season when there is enough rain for seeds to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 24) How are proteins important to human bodies? A: They build the body and help it grow. Proteins are body-building foods that make muscles, skin and blood.
chunks.source: Proteins are body-building foods that make muscles, skin and blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25) How are swamps useful to people? A: They provide papyrus, fish and water (also: clay for crafts). Swamps give people papyrus for mats, fish for food and water for animals.
chunks.source: Swamps give people papyrus for mats, fish for food and water for animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26) In which one way do people manage sunny weather? A: By wearing a hat and staying in the shade. Hats, shade and light clothes protect people from the hot sun.
chunks.source: Hats, shade and light clothes protect people from the hot sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27) Mention any one manmade change in the environment. A: Deforestation (also: road construction, building towns, swamp drainage). People change the environment by cutting forests, building roads and draining swamps.
chunks.source: People change the environment by cutting forests, building roads and draining swamps.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28) Give any one danger of the animal shown below to farmers. (The diagram shows a rat.) A: It eats and destroys stored crops and growing crops. Rats feed on maize and other crops in gardens and granaries, causing great losses to farmers.
chunks.source: Rats feed on maize and other crops in gardens and granaries, causing great losses to farmers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29) How are living components of soil important? A: They decompose dead matter and make the soil fertile (also: earthworms aerate the soil). Living things in soil break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients that feed crops.
chunks.source: Living things in soil break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients that feed crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30) Give any one responsibility of a child at home. A: Sweeping the compound (also: fetching water, washing utensils). Children help at home by doing chores like sweeping and fetching water.
chunks.source: Children help at home by doing chores like sweeping and fetching water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31) Give a reason why a cow is grouped under living things. A: Because it breathes, feeds, grows and reproduces. Living things carry out life processes like breathing and feeding, and a cow does all of these.
chunks.source: Living things carry out life processes like breathing and feeding, and a cow does all of these.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32) How is a housefly able to spread faecal disease? A: It carries germs on its legs and body from faeces to uncovered food. A housefly picks germs from faeces on its hairy legs and drops them on food that people eat.
chunks.source: A housefly picks germs from faeces on its hairy legs and drops them on food that people eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33) Write any one way you can care for the AIDS patients. A: By feeding them well and giving them their medicine (also: counselling and comforting them). AIDS patients need good food, proper medicine and love to stay strong.
chunks.source: AIDS patients need good food, proper medicine and love to stay strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34) Give one way the sun can be used as a source of energy. A: Through solar panels that make electricity (also: for drying crops and clothes). The sun's energy is trapped by solar panels to make electricity and used directly for drying.
chunks.source: The sun's energy is trapped by solar panels to make electricity and used directly for drying.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35) How are shadows formed? A: They are formed when an opaque object blocks light. Light travels straight, so when an object blocks it, a dark shadow appears behind the object.
chunks.source: Light travels straight, so when an object blocks it, a dark shadow appears behind the object.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 36) In one sentence, write the meaning of the word transplanting. A: Transplanting is the transfer of seedlings from the nursery bed to the main garden. Young plants are first raised in a nursery, then moved to where they will grow fully.
chunks.source: Young plants are first raised in a nursery, then moved to where they will grow fully.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 37) Why is it a good practice to wash hands with clean water and soap after visiting a latrine? A: To remove germs picked from the latrine. Latrines harbour germs, so washing with soap and clean water removes them from the hands.
chunks.source: Latrines harbour germs, so washing with soap and clean water removes them from the hands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38) Why are dehydrated people given ORS? A: To replace the water and salts lost from their bodies. ORS restores the fluids and body salts lost through diarrhoea or vomiting.
chunks.source: ORS restores the fluids and body salts lost through diarrhoea or vomiting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39) Name the component of air that supports burning. A: Oxygen. Oxygen is the part of air that supports burning; things burn only where oxygen is present.
chunks.source: Oxygen is the part of air that supports burning; things burn only where oxygen is present.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40) Identify any one plant that has the roots shown below. (The diagram shows prop roots growing from the stem.) A: Maize (also: sorghum). The diagram shows prop (stilt) roots that grow from the stem into the soil, as seen on maize plants.
chunks.source: The diagram shows prop (stilt) roots that grow from the stem into the soil, as seen on maize plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 41) The diagram below shows the arrangement of soil layers. Use it to answer the questions that follow:-
a) Name the layers marked B and D.
b) Why is layer A usually black and dark?
c) Describe any one way of keeping soil fertile. A: a) B is the subsoil; D is the bedrock. b) Layer A is black and dark because it contains humus (rotted plant and animal matter). c) By adding manure and mulching (also: practising crop rotation). Soil has layers: dark topsoil rich in humus, then subsoil, weathered rock and hard bedrock; manure and mulch keep it fertile.
chunks.source: Soil has layers: dark topsoil rich in humus, then subsoil, weathered rock and hard bedrock; manure and mulch keep it fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 42a) Briefly explain the term photosynthesis.
b) How is chlorophyll useful in the above process?
c) Give a reason why plants are able to carry out photosynthesis during day time.
d) Name the food that is made during the process of photosynthesis. A: a) Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants make their own food using sunlight. b) Chlorophyll traps sunlight energy needed for the process. c) Sunlight needed for photosynthesis is only available during day time. d) Starch (glucose). Green plants cook food from water and carbon dioxide using sunlight trapped by chlorophyll, making starch during the day.
chunks.source: Green plants cook food from water and carbon dioxide using sunlight trapped by chlorophyll, making starch during the day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 43) What is air?
b) Apart from carbondioxide, give any other two components of air.
c) How is carbondioxide useful in a soda factory? A: Air is a mixture of gases. b) Oxygen and nitrogen (also: rare gases, water vapour). c) It makes the drinks fizzy. Air contains oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide and other gases; soda factories pump carbon dioxide into drinks to make them fizzy.
chunks.source: Air contains oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide and other gases; soda factories pump carbon dioxide into drinks to make them fizzy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 44) The diagram below shows a fish. Use it to answer the questions that follow.
a) Name the parts labelled.
i) Y
ii) X
b) How is part W useful to a fish?
c) Name the habitat of the above animal. A: a) Y is the dorsal fin; X is the gills. b) W (the mouth) is used for feeding. c) Water (lakes, rivers, ponds). The dorsal fin steadies the fish, the gills are for breathing, the mouth takes in food, and fish live in water.
chunks.source: The dorsal fin steadies the fish, the gills are for breathing, the mouth takes in food, and fish live in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 45) Germination is the growing of a seed into a seedling.
a) Write any two conditions needed for germination to take place.
b) Write any one example of a crop that undergoes the following types of germination:-
i) epigeal germination
ii) hypogeal germination A: a) Moisture (water) and warmth (also: air/oxygen). b) i) Beans undergo epigeal germination; ii) Maize undergoes hypogeal germination. Seeds need water, warmth and air to sprout; in beans the cotyledons come above ground (epigeal) while in maize they stay below (hypogeal).
chunks.source: Seeds need water, warmth and air to sprout; in beans the cotyledons come above ground (epigeal) while in maize they stay below (hypogeal).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 46a) Identify any two items we can use to promote good sanitation at your school.
b) Write any two activities a P.4 child can do to promote sanitation at a school. A: a) Brooms and dustbins (also: rakes, slashes). b) Sweeping the compound and slashing the bushes. Brooms, dustbins and rakes are sanitation tools, and children use them when sweeping and slashing at school.
chunks.source: Brooms, dustbins and rakes are sanitation tools, and children use them when sweeping and slashing at school.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 47) Match the garden tools to their uses correctly.
Garden tool: A hoe, A rake, A trowel, A watering can, A garden fork
Use: watering plants, transplanting seedlings, pruning, collecting rubbish, weeding
a) A hoe
b) A rake
c) A watering can
d) A trowel A: A hoe: weeding; A rake: collecting rubbish; A trowel: transplanting seedlings; A watering can: watering plants. A hoe digs and weeds, a rake gathers rubbish, a watering can waters plants, and a trowel lifts seedlings for transplanting.
chunks.source: A hoe digs and weeds, a rake gathers rubbish, a watering can waters plants, and a trowel lifts seedlings for transplanting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 48) Why are bees grouped under social insects?
b) Apart from bees, give one other social insect.
c) How are bees useful to the following:
a) people
b) plants A: Bees live together in organized colonies. b) Ants (also: termites, wasps). c) a) People: they get honey; b) Plants: bees pollinate flowers. Bees are social because they live and work together in a hive; they give people honey and help plants by carrying pollen.
chunks.source: Bees are social because they live and work together in a hive; they give people honey and help plants by carrying pollen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 49) Study the life cycle below and answer questions that follow:-
a) Name stage marked P.
b) Name the vector shown in the above lifecycle.
c) Write one disease spread by the above vector.
d) How can the disease mentioned in number (c) above be prevented? A: a) Nymph. b) Cockroach. c) Cholera (also: typhoid, dysentery, diarrhoea). d) By keeping proper sanitation and covering food. The cockroach life cycle is egg, nymph, adult; stage P is the nymph; cockroaches spread cholera, which proper sanitation prevents.
chunks.source: The cockroach life cycle is egg, nymph, adult; stage P is the nymph; cockroaches spread cholera, which proper sanitation prevents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 50) Give the food value got from eating the following food stuffs.
i) fish
ii) pineapple
b) Write one use of food to the human body.
c) Identify one example of food that can be preserved by smoking. A: i) Fish gives proteins; ii) Pineapple gives vitamins. b) Food gives the body energy. c) Fish (also: meat). Fish builds the body with proteins and pineapple protects with vitamins; smoking preserves fish and meat.
chunks.source: Fish builds the body with proteins and pineapple protects with vitamins; smoking preserves fish and meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 51a) What name is given to moving air?
b) Given any two components of air.
c) Identify any one danger of air. A: a) Wind. b) Oxygen and carbon dioxide (also: nitrogen). c) It can spread diseases and destroy property (also: it dries crops). Moving air is wind; air contains oxygen and carbon dioxide; strong wind spreads germs and damages things.
chunks.source: Moving air is wind; air contains oxygen and carbon dioxide; strong wind spreads germs and damages things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 52a) A flower is a reproductive part of a plant. Draw the female part of a flower.
b) What happens to the following parts after fertilization?
i) Ovary
ii) Ovules
c) Why are some petals brightly coloured? A: a) A drawing of the pistil: a central stalk with a sticky stigma on top, a style and a swollen ovary at the base, labelled 'pistil'. b) i) The ovary becomes a fruit; ii) The ovules become seeds. c) To attract pollinators (insects). The female part (pistil) receives pollen; after fertilization the ovary swells into a fruit and ovules become seeds; bright petals attract insects.
chunks.source: The female part (pistil) receives pollen; after fertilization the ovary swells into a fruit and ovules become seeds; bright petals attract insects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 53a) In one sentence, give the meaning of the term accident.
b) Give any two causes of accidents on Ugandan roads.
c) Mention one way in which the above causes can be prevented. A: a) An accident is an unexpected bad event that causes injury or damage. b) Over-speeding and drunk driving (also: careless crossing). c) By obeying traffic rules. Accidents happen suddenly and hurt people; speeding and drunk driving cause them; following road rules prevents them.
chunks.source: Accidents happen suddenly and hurt people; speeding and drunk driving cause them; following road rules prevents them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 54a) Write any two causes of soil erosion.
b) How can erosion be controlled in a garden? (give two ways) A: a) Deforestation and overgrazing (also: bush burning). b) By mulching and terracing (also: planting trees). Cutting trees and overgrazing expose soil to erosion, which mulching, terracing and tree planting control.
chunks.source: Cutting trees and overgrazing expose soil to erosion, which mulching, terracing and tree planting control.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 55) The steps below show a wrong order of making O.R.S. Rearrange them correctly.
1) Stir the mixture until the solutes dissolve.
2) Measure 1 litre of drinking water into a clean container.
3) Wash your hands with clean water and soap.
4) Measure eight levelled tea spoonfuls of sugar and one of salt into the container. A: Wash your hands with clean water and soap, Measure 1 litre of drinking water into a clean container, Measure eight levelled tea spoonfuls of sugar and one of salt into the container, Stir the mixture until the solutes dissolve. To make ORS, first wash hands, then measure clean water, add the correct sugar and salt, and finally stir to dissolve.
chunks.source: To make ORS, first wash hands, then measure clean water, add the correct sugar and salt, and finally stir to dissolve.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1. Name any one dicotyledonous plant commonly grown for food. A: Beans (or groundnuts, soya beans, peas). Beans are dicotyledonous plants with two seed leaves, commonly grown for food.
chunks.source: Beans are dicotyledonous plants with two seed leaves, commonly grown for food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2. How is photosynthesis in plants useful to animals? A: Plants give out oxygen during photosynthesis, which animals need for breathing. During photosynthesis plants release oxygen into the air, and animals breathe in that oxygen to stay alive.
chunks.source: During photosynthesis plants release oxygen into the air, and animals breathe in that oxygen to stay alive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3. Give any one way you can improve soil fertility in the school garden. A: By adding manure (or fertilizers, or mulching). Manure and fertilizers add nutrients to the soil, making it fertile for crops to grow well.
chunks.source: Manure and fertilizers add nutrients to the soil, making it fertile for crops to grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4. Write the importance of washing mango fruits before eating them. A: To remove dirt, germs and chemicals that can make us sick. Fruits can carry dust, germs and spray chemicals, so washing them keeps us from falling sick.
chunks.source: Fruits can carry dust, germs and spray chemicals, so washing them keeps us from falling sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5. Identify any one danger caused by strong wind. A: It can blow off roofs of houses (or uproot trees, or spread fires). Strong wind has great force that can tear off roofs, knock down trees and spread fires quickly.
chunks.source: Strong wind has great force that can tear off roofs, knock down trees and spread fires quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6. Which mosquito spreads malaria germs? A: The female anopheles mosquito. Only the female anopheles mosquito carries and spreads the germs that cause malaria.
chunks.source: Only the female anopheles mosquito carries and spreads the germs that cause malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7. Why should a rain gauge be placed in an open place? A: So that trees or buildings do not block rain from falling into it. A rain gauge must catch all the rain falling from the sky, so nothing should shelter it.
chunks.source: A rain gauge must catch all the rain falling from the sky, so nothing should shelter it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8. Give any one way you can care for your tongue. A: By brushing it daily (or avoiding very hot food and drinks). Brushing the tongue removes germs and food remains, keeping the mouth clean and healthy.
chunks.source: Brushing the tongue removes germs and food remains, keeping the mouth clean and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below shows a nursery bed. Use it to answer question 9.
9. How is part marked W important on a nursery bed? A: It provides shade to the young seedlings (protects them from strong sunshine). W is the thatched shade over the nursery bed; young seedlings are delicate and need shelter from harsh sun.
chunks.source: W is the thatched shade over the nursery bed; young seedlings are delicate and need shelter from harsh sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10. In which way can electricity be dangerous to people? A: It can shock and electrocute people, causing injury or death (or start fires). Electricity passing through the body causes dangerous shocks, and faulty wires can start fires.
chunks.source: Electricity passing through the body causes dangerous shocks, and faulty wires can start fires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11. Write one activity you can carry out to reduce houseflies at home. A: Keep the compound clean and dispose of rubbish properly (or cover food, or spray with insecticide). Houseflies breed in dirt and rubbish, so a clean home gives them nowhere to multiply.
chunks.source: Houseflies breed in dirt and rubbish, so a clean home gives them nowhere to multiply.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12. Name the male reproductive cells of a flowering plant. A: Pollen grains. Pollen grains are produced in the anthers and are the male reproductive cells of flowering plants.
chunks.source: Pollen grains are produced in the anthers and are the male reproductive cells of flowering plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 13. How can a farmer increase the proper working of the garden tool below? (The diagram shows a panga.) A: By sharpening it (keeping the blade sharp; also oiling it to prevent rust). A panga cuts well only when its blade is sharp, so regular sharpening keeps it working properly.
chunks.source: A panga cuts well only when its blade is sharp, so regular sharpening keeps it working properly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14. Identify the body sense responsible for finding out the sweetness of juice. A: The sense of taste. The tongue carries taste buds that detect sweet, sour, salty and bitter tastes.
chunks.source: The tongue carries taste buds that detect sweet, sour, salty and bitter tastes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15. Draw a diagram of a simple leaf in the space below. A: A drawing of a simple leaf: one undivided flat blade (lamina) joined by a stalk (petiole), with a midrib and side veins. A simple leaf has a single undivided blade attached to the stem by a stalk, with veins spreading from a midrib.
chunks.source: A simple leaf has a single undivided blade attached to the stem by a stalk, with veins spreading from a midrib.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. Give any one danger of electricity at home. A: It can cause electric shock, burns or death (or start a fire). Faulty wires and sockets at home can shock anyone who touches them and can start fires.
chunks.source: Faulty wires and sockets at home can shock anyone who touches them and can start fires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 17. Name any one animal whose habitat is a burrow. A: A rabbit (or rat, or mole). Rabbits dig and live in underground tunnels called burrows.
chunks.source: Rabbits dig and live in underground tunnels called burrows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18. Write any one way you can protect yourself from coldness on a rainy day. A: Wear warm/heavy clothes (or stay indoors). Warm clothes trap body heat and keep the cold out on a rainy day.
chunks.source: Warm clothes trap body heat and keep the cold out on a rainy day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19. Give one way in which plants can reduce the rate of transpiration. A: By shedding their leaves (or having small leaves, or a thick waxy cuticle). Leaves lose water through transpiration, so dropping leaves in the dry season cuts water loss.
chunks.source: Leaves lose water through transpiration, so dropping leaves in the dry season cuts water loss.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below shows a fish. Use it to answer question 20.
20. Use letter P to show the part used to detect sound waves in water. A: P is placed on the lateral line (the line of tiny dots running along the side of the fish). The lateral line senses vibrations and sound waves in water, helping the fish detect movement around it.
chunks.source: The lateral line senses vibrations and sound waves in water, helping the fish detect movement around it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21. Why is it important for us to bathe daily? A: To remove dirt, sweat and germs from the body and prevent diseases and bad smell. Daily bathing washes away germs and sweat that cause skin diseases and body odour.
chunks.source: Daily bathing washes away germs and sweat that cause skin diseases and body odour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22. What is the danger of having bushes near our homes? A: They hide dangerous animals like snakes and mosquitoes (or thieves). Bushes give hiding places to snakes, mosquitoes and thieves near the home.
chunks.source: Bushes give hiding places to snakes, mosquitoes and thieves near the home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23. Give one reason why bees visit flowers. A: To collect nectar (and pollen) for food. Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers as food, and carry pollen that helps plants reproduce.
chunks.source: Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers as food, and carry pollen that helps plants reproduce.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below shows a common plant. Use it to answer questions 24 and 25.
24. Name part marked X on the plant above. A: The stem. X points to the tall jointed stalk of the sugarcane, which is its stem.
chunks.source: X points to the tall jointed stalk of the sugarcane, which is its stem.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. Identify the common product that can be got from the plant above. A: Sugar. Sugarcane stems are crushed to extract juice from which sugar is made.
chunks.source: Sugarcane stems are crushed to extract juice from which sugar is made.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26. How can people protect themselves from worm infestation? A: Wear shoes, wash hands with soap, and drink boiled water (also: deworm regularly). Worms enter through bare feet, dirty hands and dirty water, so shoes, handwashing and boiled water block them.
chunks.source: Worms enter through bare feet, dirty hands and dirty water, so shoes, handwashing and boiled water block them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27. Why do some Ugandans keep ducks at their homes? A: For eggs and meat as food (or to earn money by selling them). Ducks are kept as poultry for their eggs and meat, which feed the family or earn income.
chunks.source: Ducks are kept as poultry for their eggs and meat, which feed the family or earn income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28. Give one human activity that destroys habitats of wild animals. A: Deforestation/cutting down trees (or bush burning, or draining swamps). When forests are cut down, wild animals lose the homes and food they depend on.
chunks.source: When forests are cut down, wild animals lose the homes and food they depend on.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29. What is the danger of throwing stones at a bee hive? A: The bees will become angry and sting you. Disturbing a hive makes bees defend it by stinging the attacker, which is very painful.
chunks.source: Disturbing a hive makes bees defend it by stinging the attacker, which is very painful.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30. Which food value prevents kwashiorkor in children? A: Proteins. Kwashiorkor is caused by lack of proteins in the diet, so protein foods prevent it.
chunks.source: Kwashiorkor is caused by lack of proteins in the diet, so protein foods prevent it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31. Give one way of preserving food for a long time. A: Drying (or smoking, salting, refrigeration, canning). Removing water by drying stops germs from growing, so food lasts longer.
chunks.source: Removing water by drying stops germs from growing, so food lasts longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32. In which way is the water cycle important in our environment? A: It brings rainfall that gives us water for drinking and farming. The water cycle keeps water moving from the sky to the land, giving rain for crops and wells.
chunks.source: The water cycle keeps water moving from the sky to the land, giving rain for crops and wells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33. Write one crop growing practice which adds humus to the soil. A: Mulching (or adding manure, or crop rotation). Mulch rots into humus, which feeds the soil and holds water for crops.
chunks.source: Mulch rots into humus, which feeds the soil and holds water for crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34. Name the non-curable disease which can be spread through sharing body piercing tools. A: HIV/AIDS. Sharing piercing tools can transfer infected blood, spreading HIV/AIDS which has no cure.
chunks.source: Sharing piercing tools can transfer infected blood, spreading HIV/AIDS which has no cure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35. Which element of weather provides heat to people? A: Sunshine (the sun). The sun's rays warm the earth and give heat to people and all living things.
chunks.source: The sun's rays warm the earth and give heat to people and all living things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below shows an insect. Use it to answer questions 36 and 37.
36. Which stage of the life cycle of an insect is shown above? A: The adult (imago) stage. The insect shown has fully developed wings and body parts, which is the final adult stage.
chunks.source: The insect shown has fully developed wings and body parts, which is the final adult stage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 37. What danger will the insect have if parts marked M are blocked? A: It will not be able to breathe and will suffocate and die. M marks the spiracles, the tiny breathing holes on the insect's abdomen; blocking them stops breathing.
chunks.source: M marks the spiracles, the tiny breathing holes on the insect's abdomen; blocking them stops breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38. How are wild animals dangerous to people? A: They can attack and kill people (or destroy crops, or spread diseases). Wild animals like lions and snakes can attack humans and destroy their crops.
chunks.source: Wild animals like lions and snakes can attack humans and destroy their crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. Give any one thing that is given to patients in a hospital. A: Medicine/drugs (or food, or injections). Doctors give patients medicine to treat their sickness in hospital.
chunks.source: Doctors give patients medicine to treat their sickness in hospital.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. Name one domestic animal that gives us a lot of milk. A: A cow. Cows are the main domestic animals kept for large amounts of milk.
chunks.source: Cows are the main domestic animals kept for large amounts of milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 41. (a) Identify any two materials that can be used to build a permanent house.
(i)
(ii)
(b) Why do people build houses?
(c) Give any one way of caring for a house. A: a) (i) Bricks (ii) Cement (also: iron sheets, timber). b) For shelter and protection from rain, sunshine, cold, thieves and wild animals. c) By sweeping/cleaning it daily (also: repairing broken parts, painting). Permanent houses are built with strong materials like bricks and cement; they shelter people, and cleaning and repairs keep them in good condition.
chunks.source: Permanent houses are built with strong materials like bricks and cement; they shelter people, and cleaning and repairs keep them in good condition.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 42. (a) Give the use of these tools during first aid.
(i) spirit (the bottle)
(ii) scissors
(b) How is first aid useful to casualty?
(c) Give one quality of a good first aider. A: a) (i) Spirit is used to clean and sterilize wounds (it kills germs). (ii) Scissors are used for cutting bandages and dressings (or cutting clothes around a wound). b) It saves life, reduces pain and stops the injury from getting worse. c) Being calm and gentle (also: quick, kind, knowledgeable). Spirit disinfects wounds while scissors cut dressings to size; first aid keeps the casualty alive and comfortable before the doctor comes.
chunks.source: Spirit disinfects wounds while scissors cut dressings to size; first aid keeps the casualty alive and comfortable before the doctor comes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 43. (a) What is harvesting?
(b) Why is the dry season the best for harvesting seed crops?
(c) How can a farmer prevent rats from destroying his crops in the granary?
(d) Draw and name any one garden tool used for harvesting crops. A: a) Harvesting is the collecting of mature crops from the garden. b) Crops dry well and do not rot since there is no rain to spoil them. c) By keeping the granary clean, using traps, and storing grain in rat-proof containers. d) A labelled drawing of e.g. a sickle labelled 'sickle' (or panga, or hoe). Mature crops are gathered in the dry season when they cannot rot; granaries must be kept rat-proof; harvest tools like sickles cut crops.
chunks.source: Mature crops are gathered in the dry season when they cannot rot; granaries must be kept rat-proof; harvest tools like sickles cut crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 44. (a) Give any one different way soil may be useful to termites and people.
(i) Termites
(ii) People
(b) Name one organism that helps in soil formation by decomposition.
(c) Which component of soil is needed by plants during photosynthesis? A: a) (i) Termites: they live in the soil and build their mounds in it. (ii) People: they grow crops in the soil (also: make bricks). b) Bacteria (also: fungi, earthworms). c) Water (also: mineral salts). Termites make homes in soil while people farm it; decomposers like bacteria break down dead matter to form soil; plants take water from soil for photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Termites make homes in soil while people farm it; decomposers like bacteria break down dead matter to form soil; plants take water from soil for photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 45. (a) Why should people observe proper personal hygiene?
(b) Give the use of these materials in promoting personal hygiene.
(i) soap
(ii) towel
(c) Identify any one disease that people can get due to poor personal hygiene. A: a) To prevent diseases and stay healthy. b) (i) Soap is used for washing the body and clothes to remove dirt and germs. (ii) A towel is used for drying the body after bathing. c) Scabies (also: ringworms, diarrhoea, cholera). Clean bodies keep germs away; soap washes, towels dry; dirty habits bring skin and diarrhoeal diseases.
chunks.source: Clean bodies keep germs away; soap washes, towels dry; dirty habits bring skin and diarrhoeal diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 46. (a) Write any one way non-flowering plants reproduce.
(b) Give one example of non-flowering plants.
(c) How are non-flowering plants useful to people?
(i)
(ii) A: a) By means of spores (conifers reproduce by seeds in cones). b) Ferns (also: mosses, pines). c) (i) They are used as medicine. (ii) They provide timber and beautify the environment (also: some are eaten). Non-flowering plants like ferns reproduce with spores and still serve people as medicine, timber and decoration.
chunks.source: Non-flowering plants like ferns reproduce with spores and still serve people as medicine, timber and decoration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagrams below show things we make at home.
(a) Give the use of each of the items above.
A
B
(b) Write one material used to make item (B) above.
(c) How can a P.4 pupil benefit from making the items above? A: a) A (broom) is used for sweeping; B (basket) is used for carrying and storing things. b) Sisal (also: palm leaves, bamboo, reeds). c) He/she can sell them to earn money (also: learns a useful hand skill). Brooms sweep homes and baskets carry goods; both are woven from plant fibres, and making them earns income.
chunks.source: Brooms sweep homes and baskets carry goods; both are woven from plant fibres, and making them earns income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 48. (a) Write two activities that can lead to contamination of water sources.
(i)
(ii)
(b) Why is it dangerous to drink contaminated water?
(c) How can water be made safe for drinking? A: a) (i) Dumping rubbish near the water source. (ii) Animals drinking and defecating in the water (also: washing clothes or bathing in it). b) It contains germs that cause diarrhoeal diseases. c) By boiling it (also: filtering, treating with chlorine). Waste and animals dirty water sources; dirty water carries disease germs; boiling kills the germs.
chunks.source: Waste and animals dirty water sources; dirty water carries disease germs; boiling kills the germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 49. Study the diagram below and use it to answer question 49. (1 litre of drinking water + 8 teaspoonfuls of sugar + 1 teaspoonful of salt = solution)
(a) Name the solution made above.
(b) How is the solution above useful to people?
(c) Give the reason why the following are necessary in the above solution
(i) salt
(ii) sugar A: a) Oral Rehydration Salts solution (ORS). b) It replaces lost body water and salts in dehydrated people (it treats diarrhoea). c) (i) Salt replaces the body salts lost during diarrhoea. (ii) Sugar gives energy and helps the body absorb the water and salts. Mixing the right amounts of salt and sugar in clean water makes ORS, which saves dehydrated people by replacing lost fluids and salts.
chunks.source: Mixing the right amounts of salt and sugar in clean water makes ORS, which saves dehydrated people by replacing lost fluids and salts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 50. (a) Give any two ways in which insects spread germs to people.
(i)
(ii)
(b) Apart from insects, give any other disease vector.
(c) How are vectors different from pests? A: a) (i) By biting people and injecting germs. (ii) By carrying germs on their bodies and legs onto food. b) Rats (also: snails, dogs). c) Vectors carry and spread disease germs to people, while pests destroy crops and property. Insects move germs by bites and dirty feet; other vectors include rats; vectors spread disease whereas pests cause damage.
chunks.source: Insects move germs by bites and dirty feet; other vectors include rats; vectors spread disease whereas pests cause damage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 51. (a) Write any one use of food in the body.
(b) Why do children need a lot of proteins in their diet?
(c) Which class of food is most needed by brick makers?
(d) Give one sign of poor feeding among children. A: a) It gives the body energy (also: builds the body, protects against diseases). b) For proper growth of their bodies. c) Carbohydrates (energy-giving foods), because brick making is heavy work. d) Thin, stunted growth (also: swollen belly, brown thin hair). Food gives energy, proteins build growing bodies, hard workers need energy foods, and poor feeding shows in thin weak bodies.
chunks.source: Food gives energy, proteins build growing bodies, hard workers need energy foods, and poor feeding shows in thin weak bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below shows weather instruments.
(a) Name the instruments shown above.
A
B
(b) Which element of weather enables the instruments above to work?
(c) How are the above instruments similar? A: a) A: Anemometer; B: Windsock. b) Wind. c) Both are wind instruments used to detect/measure wind. The anemometer measures wind speed and the windsock shows wind direction; both only work when wind blows.
chunks.source: The anemometer measures wind speed and the windsock shows wind direction; both only work when wind blows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 53. (a) Which system of a flowering plant develops from the radicle?
(b) State the function of these parts to a germinating bean seed.
(i) micropyle
(ii) cotyledon
(c) Identify any one factor that can fail a seed to germinate. A: a) The root system. b) (i) The micropyle lets water and air into the seed for germination. (ii) The cotyledon stores food for the germinating seed. c) Lack of moisture (also: lack of warmth, lack of air, or a dead seed). The radicle becomes the root; the micropyle admits water and air while the cotyledon feeds the young plant; seeds fail without water, warmth or air.
chunks.source: The radicle becomes the root; the micropyle admits water and air while the cotyledon feeds the young plant; seeds fail without water, warmth or air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 54. Match the body organs to their correct functions.
Body organ: (i) Heart, (ii) Kidney, (iii) Brain, (iv) Liver
Function: regulating blood sugars, storing information, pumping blood, filtering blood
(i) Heart -
(ii) Kidney -
(iii) Brain -
(iv) Liver - A: Heart: pumping blood; Kidney: filtering blood; Brain: storing information; Liver: regulating blood sugars. The heart pumps blood round the body, the kidneys filter blood, the brain stores information, and the liver regulates blood sugar.
chunks.source: The heart pumps blood round the body, the kidneys filter blood, the brain stores information, and the liver regulates blood sugar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 55. (a) How are shadows formed?
(b) At which time of the day is the shadow shortest?
(c) Give one use of shadows to children.
(d) Draw the shadow for the object below. (The diagram shows a tin with the sun shining from the top right.) A: a) Shadows are formed when an opaque object blocks light; the shadow falls on the opposite side of the light source. b) At midday (around 12 noon) when the sun is directly overhead. c) Children use shadows for playing shadow games (also: for telling time). d) A drawing of the tin's shadow on the ground on the side away from the sun (below and to the left of the tin). Light blocked by an object casts a shadow opposite the light; noon sun gives the shortest shadow; children play with shadows.
chunks.source: Light blocked by an object casts a shadow opposite the light; noon sun gives the shortest shadow; children play with shadows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 111. Which element of weather do people use for winnowing? A: Wind. Wind blows away the light chaff while the heavy grain falls down during winnowing.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light chaff while the heavy grain falls down during winnowing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 112. State any one way of keeping water sources clean. A: Do not dump rubbish near water sources (also: fence them off, keep animals away). Keeping dirt, rubbish and animals away from water sources keeps the water clean and safe.
chunks.source: Keeping dirt, rubbish and animals away from water sources keeps the water clean and safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 113. How are feathers useful to a bird? A: They help the bird to fly (also: keep the bird warm). Feathers give the wings shape for flight and trap warmth around the bird's body.
chunks.source: Feathers give the wings shape for flight and trap warmth around the bird's body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 114. Identify the deficiency disease caused due to lack of vitamin C in the diet. A: Scurvy. Lack of vitamin C in food causes scurvy, with bleeding gums and weak body.
chunks.source: Lack of vitamin C in food causes scurvy, with bleeding gums and weak body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 115. Name one crop that can be harvested using the garden tool below. (The diagram shows a hoe.) A: Cassava (or groundnuts, or sweet potatoes). A hoe digs up root crops like cassava, groundnuts and sweet potatoes at harvest.
chunks.source: A hoe digs up root crops like cassava, groundnuts and sweet potatoes at harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 116. How can a P.4 child protect him/herself from getting HIV/AIDS? A: By not sharing sharp body-cutting objects (also: avoiding bad touches, abstaining). HIV spreads through infected blood and body fluids, so children must never share razors, blades or needles.
chunks.source: HIV spreads through infected blood and body fluids, so children must never share razors, blades or needles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 117. The diagram below shows part of a flower.
Use an arrow and letter N to show the part that receives pollen grains. A: N points to the stigma (the sticky top of the carpel). Pollen grains land and stick on the stigma, the top part of the female flower part shown.
chunks.source: Pollen grains land and stick on the stigma, the top part of the female flower part shown.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 118. Give any one way of keeping your beddings clean. A: Wash them regularly (also: air them in sunshine). Regular washing removes sweat, dirt and germs from beddings.
chunks.source: Regular washing removes sweat, dirt and germs from beddings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 119. Why are farmers advised to leave enough space between rows when planting? A: So that crops get enough sunlight, air and nutrients (also: for easy weeding). Crowded plants compete for light and food, so spacing lets each plant grow well.
chunks.source: Crowded plants compete for light and food, so spacing lets each plant grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 120. State any one danger of wild birds to people. A: They eat and destroy crops in gardens (also: they can spread diseases). Wild birds like weaver birds feed on cereals and can destroy a farmer's harvest.
chunks.source: Wild birds like weaver birds feed on cereals and can destroy a farmer's harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 121. How is poor personal hygiene dangerous to people? A: It causes diseases like skin diseases and diarrhoea. Dirty bodies and surroundings breed germs that make people sick.
chunks.source: Dirty bodies and surroundings breed germs that make people sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 122. Identify any one human activity that can change the environment. A: Deforestation/cutting down trees (also: building, farming, bush burning). Cutting forests changes rainfall, soil and homes of animals in an area.
chunks.source: Cutting forests changes rainfall, soil and homes of animals in an area.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 123. Draw a diagram of a simple leaf and show the midrib. A: A drawing of a simple leaf: one undivided flat blade (lamina) with a central midrib running from the stalk to the tip, and side veins. A simple leaf has one blade with a strong central vein called the midrib.
chunks.source: A simple leaf has one blade with a strong central vein called the midrib.

chunks.subject: Science
