chunks.text: Q: 124. How do you care for your eyes? A: Wash them with clean water (also: avoid dusty and smoky places, do not read in dim light). Clean water removes dirt from eyes, and good light protects them from strain.
chunks.source: Clean water removes dirt from eyes, and good light protects them from strain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below shows a child suffering from a common disease.
125. How can the disease in the child above be prevented among children? A: By immunizing/vaccinating children against measles (also: keeping the sick child away from others). The child has measles, shown by the rash; vaccination protects children from catching it.
chunks.source: The child has measles, shown by the rash; vaccination protects children from catching it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 126. Which gas is needed by plants during photosynthesis? A: Carbon dioxide. Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air and use it with water to make food.
chunks.source: Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air and use it with water to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 127. What first aid can be given to a person with a burn? A: Pour cold clean water on the burn (also: cover it with a clean cloth). Cold water cools the burn and reduces pain and damage to the skin.
chunks.source: Cold water cools the burn and reduces pain and damage to the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 128. Name one harmful insect in the environment. A: A mosquito (also: housefly, tsetse fly). Mosquitoes spread malaria, making them harmful to people.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes spread malaria, making them harmful to people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 129. Give any one way of controlling pests in a maize garden. A: By spraying with pesticides (also: weeding, crop rotation, hand-picking pests). Pesticides kill the insects that attack maize in the garden.
chunks.source: Pesticides kill the insects that attack maize in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 130. Write any one use of food in the body. A: It gives the body energy (also: builds the body, protects against diseases). Food gives us energy for work and play, builds our body tissues, and protects us from diseases.
chunks.source: Food gives us energy for work and play, builds our body tissues, and protects us from diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 131. Which part of a seed grows into the root system? A: The radicle. The radicle is the first part to grow out of a germinating seed and develops into the roots.
chunks.source: The radicle is the first part to grow out of a germinating seed and develops into the roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 132. Give one way of managing rainy weather. A: Carry an umbrella or wear a raincoat (also: stay indoors). Umbrellas and raincoats keep us dry when it rains.
chunks.source: Umbrellas and raincoats keep us dry when it rains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 133. How are claws useful to a cat? A: For catching and holding prey (also: for climbing, for protection). A cat's sharp claws grip prey and help it climb and defend itself.
chunks.source: A cat's sharp claws grip prey and help it climb and defend itself.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 134. Why do people close windows and doors early in the evening? A: To keep out mosquitoes (also: thieves, cold). Mosquitoes enter homes in the evening, so closing doors and windows keeps them out.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes enter homes in the evening, so closing doors and windows keeps them out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 135. State one sign of food poisoning in people. A: Vomiting (also: diarrhoea, stomach pain). Spoilt food upsets the stomach, causing vomiting and diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Spoilt food upsets the stomach, causing vomiting and diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 136. How are earthquakes dangerous to people? A: They destroy buildings and can kill people. Shaking ground topples houses and buries people under falling walls.
chunks.source: Shaking ground topples houses and buries people under falling walls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 137. Give one use of very heavy clothes to people who wear them. A: They keep the body warm. Heavy clothes trap body heat and protect against cold weather.
chunks.source: Heavy clothes trap body heat and protect against cold weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 138. Identify any one way of preserving groundnuts after harvesting? A: By drying them in the sunshine. Dried groundnuts do not rot, so they keep for a long time.
chunks.source: Dried groundnuts do not rot, so they keep for a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 139. How can a P.4 pupil avoid having a bad breath? A: By brushing teeth daily (also: rinsing the mouth after eating). Brushing removes food remains and germs that cause bad smell in the mouth.
chunks.source: Brushing removes food remains and germs that cause bad smell in the mouth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 140. Write one type of germination. A: Epigeal germination (also: hypogeal germination). In epigeal germination the cotyledons come above the ground; in hypogeal they stay below.
chunks.source: In epigeal germination the cotyledons come above the ground; in hypogeal they stay below.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 141. Why are pain killers important to a casualty? A: They reduce the casualty's pain. Pain killers ease suffering so the injured person feels comfortable.
chunks.source: Pain killers ease suffering so the injured person feels comfortable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 142. Give one way of controlling soil erosion in a compound. A: By planting grass (also: planting trees, mulching). Grass roots hold the soil together so rain cannot wash it away.
chunks.source: Grass roots hold the soil together so rain cannot wash it away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below shows a tapeworm. Use it to answer question 143.
143. How are the structures marked P useful to a tapeworm? A: They help the tapeworm attach itself to the walls of the host's intestines (they are hooks and suckers). P marks the hooks and suckers on the tapeworm's head, which grip the intestinal wall so it is not pushed out.
chunks.source: P marks the hooks and suckers on the tapeworm's head, which grip the intestinal wall so it is not pushed out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 144. How is a nest useful to a bird? A: The bird lays its eggs and raises its young in it (it gives shelter). Nests keep eggs and chicks safe and warm until they can fly.
chunks.source: Nests keep eggs and chicks safe and warm until they can fly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 145. Apart from drinking water, name one other item used in the preparation of ORS locally. A: Salt (or sugar). Local ORS is made from clean water mixed with salt and sugar.
chunks.source: Local ORS is made from clean water mixed with salt and sugar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 146. What is the danger of cutting down trees on a large scale in an area? A: It causes soil erosion and drought (also: destroys habitats of wild animals). Without trees, rain washes soil away and the land becomes dry and bare.
chunks.source: Without trees, rain washes soil away and the land becomes dry and bare.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 147. Name any one insect without wings. A: An ant (also: termite, silverfish). Ants are insects with six legs but no wings.
chunks.source: Ants are insects with six legs but no wings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 148. Write down any one product of a cow that gives us proteins. A: Milk (also: beef/meat). Milk is rich in proteins that build our bodies.
chunks.source: Milk is rich in proteins that build our bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 149. How are tree shades useful to people? A: They give cool resting places (protect people from strong sunshine). Tree shade cools the air and shelters people from harsh sun.
chunks.source: Tree shade cools the air and shelters people from harsh sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 150. Why is a tsetse fly grouped under vectors? A: Because it spreads/transmits disease germs (sleeping sickness) to people and animals. Tsetse flies carry the germs of sleeping sickness from one animal to another.
chunks.source: Tsetse flies carry the germs of sleeping sickness from one animal to another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 151. a) Give the difference between wind and air.
b) Write any one importance of wind to a crop farmer.
c) How are the following gases useful to people?
(i) Oxygen
(ii) Carbon dioxide A: a) Air is still, while wind is moving air. b) It helps in pollination and seed dispersal (also: it is used for winnowing). c) (i) Oxygen is used for breathing/respiration. (ii) Carbon dioxide is used by plants to make food (also: used in fire extinguishers). Still air becomes wind when it moves; wind helps farmers with pollination and winnowing; we breathe oxygen while plants use carbon dioxide.
chunks.source: Still air becomes wind when it moves; wind helps farmers with pollination and winnowing; we breathe oxygen while plants use carbon dioxide.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below shows vertical arrangement of soil layers. Use it to answer the questions that follow.
a) What name is given to the above vertical arrangement of soil layers?
b) Name any one organism found in layer B.
c) Identify layer marked C.
d) Where can we observe the above arrangement in the environment? A: a) Soil profile. b) Earthworm (also: bacteria, fungi, termites). c) Subsoil. d) In a pit where soil has been dug (also: on a cliff or roadside cutting). The vertical layers form the soil profile: topsoil (B) with living organisms, subsoil (C), and parent rock below; it shows wherever soil is cut open.
chunks.source: The vertical layers form the soil profile: topsoil (B) with living organisms, subsoil (C), and parent rock below; it shows wherever soil is cut open.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 153. a) Write any two diarrhoeal diseases spread by houseflies.
(i)
(ii)
b) How can the above diseases be controlled in a community?
c) How are diarrhoeal diseases dangerous to people? A: a) (i) Cholera (ii) Typhoid (also: dysentery, diarrhoea). b) By proper disposal of rubbish and faeces, covering food, and spraying flies. c) They cause dehydration and can kill people. Flies carry germs from waste to food, spreading cholera and typhoid; cleanliness controls them; they kill through water loss.
chunks.source: Flies carry germs from waste to food, spreading cholera and typhoid; cleanliness controls them; they kill through water loss.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 154. a) What is sanitation?
b) Give one importance of maintaining proper sanitation in an area.
c) Write two activities you can do to keep your classroom clean.
(i)
(ii) A: a) Sanitation is the general cleanliness of the place where we live. b) It prevents diseases in the community. c) (i) Sweeping the classroom (ii) Mopping the floor (also: dusting, arranging desks). A clean living place keeps germs away; classrooms stay clean through sweeping and mopping.
chunks.source: A clean living place keeps germs away; classrooms stay clean through sweeping and mopping.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below shows a food store. Use it to answer question 155.
d) Name the food store shown above.
e) Identify any one example of a crop kept in such a store.
f) Write the importance of part marked L and M on the store above.
L
M A: d) Granary. e) Maize (also: beans, millet, sorghum). f) L: the roof protects the stored grain from rain and wetness. M: the raised legs lift the store off the ground so rats cannot reach the grain and dampness cannot spoil it. A granary stores dry crops; its roof keeps rain out and its raised legs keep rats and dampness away.
chunks.source: A granary stores dry crops; its roof keeps rain out and its raised legs keep rats and dampness away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 156. a) State the function of each of the following types of teeth.
(i) Canines
(ii) Incisors
b) Give two ways of keeping our teeth healthy.
(i)
(ii) A: a) (i) Canines tear food. (ii) Incisors bite and cut food. b) (i) Brushing teeth daily. (ii) Avoiding too many sweets (also: visiting the dentist). Canines tear and incisors cut; daily brushing and less sugar keep teeth healthy.
chunks.source: Canines tear and incisors cut; daily brushing and less sugar keep teeth healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 157. a) In which way is heavy rainfall dangerous to people?
b) Give two processes involved in rainfall formation.
(i)
(ii)
c) How is the sun important in the process of rain formation? A: a) It causes floods that destroy property and kill people. b) (i) Evaporation (ii) Condensation. c) The sun heats water bodies, causing evaporation that starts the cycle. Heavy rain floods land; rain forms when evaporated vapour condenses; the sun drives evaporation.
chunks.source: Heavy rain floods land; rain forms when evaporated vapour condenses; the sun drives evaporation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below shows a life cycle of an insect. Use it to answer the questions that follow.
a) What do we call the stage marked C on the diagram above.
b) Name the type of life cycle shown above.
c) Identify two insects that undergo the life cycle above.
(i)
(ii) A: a) The adult (imago) stage. b) Incomplete metamorphosis. c) (i) Cockroach (ii) Grasshopper (also: termite, locust). C is the adult cockroach; the cycle egg-nymph-adult has no pupa, so it is incomplete metamorphosis, as in cockroaches and grasshoppers.
chunks.source: C is the adult cockroach; the cycle egg-nymph-adult has no pupa, so it is incomplete metamorphosis, as in cockroaches and grasshoppers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 159. Complete the table below correctly.
BODY ORGAN | FUNCTION
Heart | ______
______ | To filter blood.
Brain | ______
______ | To taste food. A: Heart - To pump blood; Kidney - To filter blood; Brain - To store information (controls the body); Tongue - To taste food. Each organ has its work: the heart pumps, kidneys filter, the brain remembers and controls, the tongue tastes.
chunks.source: Each organ has its work: the heart pumps, kidneys filter, the brain remembers and controls, the tongue tastes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 160. a) What is a nuclear family?
b) Apart from parents and their own children, name one other person found in an extended family.
c) Give two roles of parents in a family.
(i)
(ii) A: a) A nuclear family is made up of parents and their own children only. b) An uncle or aunt (also: grandparent, cousin). c) (i) Providing food for the family. (ii) Paying school fees (also: guiding children, providing shelter). Nuclear families are parents plus children; extended families add relatives; parents feed, shelter and educate children.
chunks.source: Nuclear families are parents plus children; extended families add relatives; parents feed, shelter and educate children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: 161. a) Write any one dangerous object found on roads.
b) Name any two groups of people who help in traffic.
(i)
(ii)
c) How can road accidents be controlled in our district? A: a) Broken bottles (also: nails, stones). b) (i) Traffic police (ii) Road safety marshals. c) By obeying traffic rules and driving carefully (also: repairing bad roads). Sharp objects endanger road users; police and marshals guide traffic; careful driving prevents accidents.
chunks.source: Sharp objects endanger road users; police and marshals guide traffic; careful driving prevents accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: The diagram below shows part of the human body.
a) Identify the parts marked N and K.
N
K
b) Name the part of the human body shown above. A: a) N: Toes; K: Foot. b) The leg. N points to the toes and K to the foot on the lower leg shown.
chunks.source: N points to the toes and K to the foot on the lower leg shown.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one cereal crop. A: Maize. Maize is a cereal crop whose grains we grind into flour for food.
chunks.source: Maize is a cereal crop whose grains we grind into flour for food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do farmers mulch their gardens? A: To keep moisture in the soil. Mulch covers the soil so water does not dry up quickly and weeds do not grow.
chunks.source: Mulch covers the soil so water does not dry up quickly and weeds do not grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one food stuff which can be preserved by smoking. A: Fish. Smoking removes water from fish or meat so germs cannot grow on it.
chunks.source: Smoking removes water from fish or meat so germs cannot grow on it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important to iron clothes after washing? A: To kill germs in the clothes. The heat of the iron kills germs hiding in clothes and makes them look neat.
chunks.source: The heat of the iron kills germs hiding in clothes and makes them look neat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the importance of a rain gauge at a weather station? A: To measure the amount of rainfall. A rain gauge collects rain water so we can measure how much rain fell.
chunks.source: A rain gauge collects rain water so we can measure how much rain fell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is ORS useful to a dehydrated person? A: It replaces the water and salts lost from the body. ORS gives back the water and body salts lost through diarrhoea or vomiting.
chunks.source: ORS gives back the water and body salts lost through diarrhoea or vomiting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are wasps grouped under social insects? A: Because they live together in colonies. Social insects live and work together in a colony, like wasps, bees, ants and termites.
chunks.source: Social insects live and work together in a colony, like wasps, bees, ants and termites.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one raw material plants need to make their own food. A: Water. Plants use water, carbon dioxide and sunlight to make food during photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants use water, carbon dioxide and sunlight to make food during photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should P.4 children wear shoes in school? A: To protect their feet from injuries and germs. Shoes protect feet from cuts, thorns and germs like jiggers that enter through bare feet.
chunks.source: Shoes protect feet from cuts, thorns and germs like jiggers that enter through bare feet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are children protected from measles? A: By immunisation (vaccination). Children get the measles vaccine so their bodies can fight measles germs.
chunks.source: Children get the measles vaccine so their bodies can fight measles germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do children make materials like mats and baskets? A: To sell them and get money. Mats and baskets can be sold to earn money and can also be used at home.
chunks.source: Mats and baskets can be sold to earn money and can also be used at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one cause of accidents on the road. A: Over speeding. Fast and careless driving causes many road accidents.
chunks.source: Fast and careless driving causes many road accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one function of the organ below. A: It digests food. The stomach churns food and mixes it with digestive juices.
chunks.source: The stomach churns food and mixes it with digestive juices.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one product made from animal hides. A: Shoes. Animal hides are made into leather for shoes, bags and belts.
chunks.source: Animal hides are made into leather for shoes, bags and belts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the sun contribute to the formation of rainfall? A: It heats water bodies causing evaporation. The sun's heat turns water into vapour (evaporation), which later cools to form rain.
chunks.source: The sun's heat turns water into vapour (evaporation), which later cools to form rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do bees visit flowers? A: To collect nectar. Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers to make honey.
chunks.source: Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers to make honey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which description fits a canine tooth? A: A long, pointed tooth for tearing food. Canine teeth are pointed and tear food; dogs have strong canines.
chunks.source: Canine teeth are pointed and tear food; dogs have strong canines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are monkeys grouped under pests? A: Because they destroy crops. Monkeys raid gardens and eat or spoil farmers' crops, so they are pests.
chunks.source: Monkeys raid gardens and eat or spoil farmers' crops, so they are pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of wind. A: It can blow off roofs of houses. Strong wind can destroy houses and crops and spread germs.
chunks.source: Strong wind can destroy houses and crops and spread germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is yellow fever spread among people? A: Through the bite of an infected mosquito. Yellow fever spreads when an infected (tiger) mosquito bites a person.
chunks.source: Yellow fever spreads when an infected (tiger) mosquito bites a person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which component of air supports burning? A: Oxygen. Oxygen in air helps things to burn; without it a fire goes off.
chunks.source: Oxygen in air helps things to burn; without it a fire goes off.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do some people harvest rain water? A: To have water for home use. Harvested rain water is stored and used for drinking, cooking and washing.
chunks.source: Harvested rain water is stored and used for drinking, cooking and washing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is chlorophyll important to plants? A: It traps sunlight for photosynthesis. Chlorophyll is the green colouring that traps sunlight so plants can make food.
chunks.source: Chlorophyll is the green colouring that traps sunlight so plants can make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one item used to promote oral health. A: Toothbrush. A toothbrush removes food remains from teeth to keep them healthy.
chunks.source: A toothbrush removes food remains from teeth to keep them healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are gills useful to a fish? A: They are used for breathing. Fish breathe through gills, which take in oxygen dissolved in water.
chunks.source: Fish breathe through gills, which take in oxygen dissolved in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way farmers in hilly areas control soil erosion. A: Terracing. Terraces are steps cut across hills so soil is not washed away.
chunks.source: Terraces are steps cut across hills so soil is not washed away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are people advised to bathe regularly? A: To remove dirt and germs from the body. Bathing removes dirt, sweat and germs so we stay clean and healthy.
chunks.source: Bathing removes dirt, sweat and germs so we stay clean and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one danger of poor feeding to people. A: It causes deficiency diseases. Poor feeding weakens the body and causes deficiency diseases like kwashiorkor.
chunks.source: Poor feeding weakens the body and causes deficiency diseases like kwashiorkor.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How dangerous is it to live with domestic animals in the same room? A: Very dangerous. Animals can spread diseases and parasites to people sharing the same room.
chunks.source: Animals can spread diseases and parasites to people sharing the same room.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why can't mushrooms make their own food? A: Because they have no chlorophyll. Mushrooms lack the green chlorophyll needed to trap sunlight for making food.
chunks.source: Mushrooms lack the green chlorophyll needed to trap sunlight for making food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is breast milk the best food for babies? A: It has all the nutrients a baby needs. Breast milk contains all the food values a baby needs and protects against diseases.
chunks.source: Breast milk contains all the food values a baby needs and protects against diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the animal below useful to people at home? A: It catches rats and mice. Cats catch rats and mice that spoil our food at home.
chunks.source: Cats catch rats and mice that spoil our food at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why would a cockroach die if its abdomen is kept in water for some time? A: Because its breathing holes are on the abdomen. A cockroach breathes through tiny holes (spiracles) on its abdomen; water blocks them and it suffocates.
chunks.source: A cockroach breathes through tiny holes (spiracles) on its abdomen; water blocks them and it suffocates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of soil holds water for the longest time? A: Clay soil. Clay soil has tiny particles packed tightly, so it holds water longest.
chunks.source: Clay soil has tiny particles packed tightly, so it holds water longest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one natural habitat of wild animals. A: Forest. Wild animals live in natural places like forests where they find food and shelter.
chunks.source: Wild animals live in natural places like forests where they find food and shelter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do chameleons change colours? A: To hide from their enemies. Chameleons change colour to match the environment (camouflage) and catch prey unnoticed.
chunks.source: Chameleons change colour to match the environment (camouflage) and catch prey unnoticed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which set of teeth is found in the mouth of a four year old boy? A: Milk teeth. Young children have milk teeth, which later fall out and are replaced by permanent teeth.
chunks.source: Young children have milk teeth, which later fall out and are replaced by permanent teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which item is used to give first aid to a casualty? A: Bandage. A bandage covers wounds to stop bleeding and keep germs out.
chunks.source: A bandage covers wounds to stop bleeding and keep germs out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should people eat food containing all food values every day? A: To keep the body healthy. Every food value does a special job, so we need all of them daily to stay healthy.
chunks.source: Every food value does a special job, so we need all of them daily to stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part of a plant that sucks water from the ground. A: Roots. Roots grow into the soil and suck up water and mineral salts for the plant.
chunks.source: Roots grow into the soil and suck up water and mineral salts for the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Name one insect which cannot be eaten. A: Housefly. Houseflies carry germs from dirty places, so they are not eaten.
chunks.source: Houseflies carry germs from dirty places, so they are not eaten.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name another insect which cannot be eaten. A: Mosquito. Mosquitoes spread diseases like malaria, so they are not eaten.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes spread diseases like malaria, so they are not eaten.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Name one insect without wings. A: Ant. Ants are insects that have no wings.
chunks.source: Ants are insects that have no wings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Name another insect without wings. A: Flea. Fleas are wingless insects that jump onto animals.
chunks.source: Fleas are wingless insects that jump onto animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Briefly explain the term soil erosion. A: The washing away of top soil by running water or wind. Soil erosion is when wind or running water carries away the fertile top soil.
chunks.source: Soil erosion is when wind or running water carries away the fertile top soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Name one agent of soil erosion. A: Running water. Fast-running water washes soil away.
chunks.source: Fast-running water washes soil away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Name another agent of soil erosion. A: Wind. Strong wind blows loose soil away.
chunks.source: Strong wind blows loose soil away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How is soil erosion dangerous to soil? A: It removes the fertile top soil. Erosion carries away the fertile top layer, leaving poor soil for crops.
chunks.source: Erosion carries away the fertile top layer, leaving poor soil for crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Why do people drain swamps in the environment? A: To get land for farming and settlement. People drain swamps to create land for growing crops and building homes.
chunks.source: People drain swamps to create land for growing crops and building homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Write one effect of swamp drainage on the environment. A: It destroys the habitat of swamp animals. Draining swamps destroys the homes of swamp creatures and plants.
chunks.source: Draining swamps destroys the homes of swamp creatures and plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Write one effect of overgrazing on the environment. A: It leaves the land bare leading to soil erosion. Too many animals eat all the grass, leaving bare soil that washes away.
chunks.source: Too many animals eat all the grass, leaving bare soil that washes away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give one way of controlling floods in the environment. A: By planting trees. Trees slow down running water and drainage channels carry excess water away safely.
chunks.source: Trees slow down running water and drainage channels carry excess water away safely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the part marked M on the maize grain. A: Plumule. The plumule is the young shoot of the embryo; it grows into the shoot system.
chunks.source: The plumule is the young shoot of the embryo; it grows into the shoot system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the part marked N on the maize grain. A: Cotyledon. The cotyledon passes food from the endosperm to the embryo.
chunks.source: The cotyledon passes food from the endosperm to the embryo.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) How is part marked O useful to a maize grain? A: It develops into the root system after germination. The radicle grows into roots that absorb water and mineral salts for the seedling.
chunks.source: The radicle grows into roots that absorb water and mineral salts for the seedling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Why is the maize grain above classified under fruits? A: Because it developed from the ovary wall of a flower. A maize grain is a fruit (caryopsis); its seed coat is fused with the fruit wall.
chunks.source: A maize grain is a fruit (caryopsis); its seed coat is fused with the fruit wall.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Give any one way HIV/AIDS is spread among people. A: Through unprotected sex with an infected person. HIV spreads mainly through unprotected sex with an infected person.
chunks.source: HIV spreads mainly through unprotected sex with an infected person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) How can a pupil protect him/herself from HIV/AIDS? A: By abstaining from sex. Abstaining from sex keeps a pupil safe from HIV infection.
chunks.source: Abstaining from sex keeps a pupil safe from HIV infection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give one danger of HIV to people. A: It weakens the body's immunity. HIV destroys the body's defence, so the person easily gets sick and can die.
chunks.source: HIV destroys the body's defence, so the person easily gets sick and can die.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) Write one way of caring for HIV/AIDS patients. A: By giving them proper food and medicine. Good food and medicine keep HIV/AIDS patients strong and comfortable.
chunks.source: Good food and medicine keep HIV/AIDS patients strong and comfortable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Name one artificial source of light. A: Electric bulb. An electric bulb gives light made by people, not by nature.
chunks.source: An electric bulb gives light made by people, not by nature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name another artificial source of light. A: Candle. A candle is a man-made source of light.
chunks.source: A candle is a man-made source of light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give one example of an item which uses electricity to work. A: Television. A television needs electricity to work.
chunks.source: A television needs electricity to work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give one importance of saving energy at home. A: To reduce electricity bills. Using less electricity means paying less money.
chunks.source: Using less electricity means paying less money.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name stage A in the life cycle of the vector. A: Adult. Stage A is the fully grown adult cockroach.
chunks.source: Stage A is the fully grown adult cockroach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name stage C in the life cycle of the vector. A: Nymph. Stage C is the young cockroach (nymph) that looks like a small adult.
chunks.source: Stage C is the young cockroach (nymph) that looks like a small adult.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Name one disease spread by the above insect. A: Cholera. Cockroaches carry germs that cause cholera and typhoid.
chunks.source: Cockroaches carry germs that cause cholera and typhoid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How can we control the spread of the disease named above? A: By covering food and killing cockroaches. Keeping food covered and homes clean stops cockroaches from spreading germs.
chunks.source: Keeping food covered and homes clean stops cockroaches from spreading germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the animals in A to their habitats in B. A: dog: kennel; man: house; fish: water body; rabbit: hutch. Dogs live in kennels, people in houses, fish in water bodies and rabbits in hutches.
chunks.source: Dogs live in kennels, people in houses, fish in water bodies and rabbits in hutches.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Write any one root system in plants. A: Taproot system. A taproot system has one main root growing deep with small side roots.
chunks.source: A taproot system has one main root growing deep with small side roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one use of roots to a plant. A: They absorb water and mineral salts from the soil. Roots suck up water and nutrients the plant needs.
chunks.source: Roots suck up water and nutrients the plant needs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another use of roots to a plant. A: They hold the plant firmly in the soil. Roots anchor the plant so wind cannot blow it away.
chunks.source: Roots anchor the plant so wind cannot blow it away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Which part of a bean seed develops into a root system? A: Radicle. The radicle is the young root of the embryo; it grows into the root system.
chunks.source: The radicle is the young root of the embryo; it grows into the root system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Give one reason why farmers mulch their gardens. A: To keep moisture in the soil. Mulch stops water from drying up quickly in the garden.
chunks.source: Mulch stops water from drying up quickly in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Name one material used for mulching. A: Dry grass. Dry grass is spread on soil as mulch.
chunks.source: Dry grass is spread on soil as mulch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Name another material used for mulching. A: Dry leaves. Dry leaves also make good mulch.
chunks.source: Dry leaves also make good mulch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give one way in which mulching may be dangerous in the garden. A: It can hide pests that attack crops. Pests can hide in mulch and then attack the crops.
chunks.source: Pests can hide in mulch and then attack the crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What does the above experiment show about soil? A: That soil contains air. Bubbles rise from the lump of soil in water, showing air was trapped inside.
chunks.source: Bubbles rise from the lump of soil in water, showing air was trapped inside.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Apart from air, write one other component of soil. A: Water. Soil also contains water, humus, mineral salts and living organisms.
chunks.source: Soil also contains water, humus, mineral salts and living organisms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Apart from air, write another component of soil. A: Humus. Humus is the decayed matter in soil that makes it fertile.
chunks.source: Humus is the decayed matter in soil that makes it fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How is air useful in soil? A: It helps plant roots to breathe. Roots need air in the soil for breathing (respiration).
chunks.source: Roots need air in the soil for breathing (respiration).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the element of weather got from nimbus clouds. A: Rainfall. Nimbus clouds are dark rain-bearing clouds.
chunks.source: Nimbus clouds are dark rain-bearing clouds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) How is the element named in (a) useful to a crop farmer? A: It provides water for crops to grow. Rain gives crops the water they need to grow well.
chunks.source: Rain gives crops the water they need to grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give one danger caused by too much sunshine in our environment. A: It dries up crops and causes drought. Too much sunshine withers crops and dries water sources.
chunks.source: Too much sunshine withers crops and dries water sources.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) How can the danger given above be managed? A: By irrigation. Watering crops (irrigation) saves them when sunshine is too much.
chunks.source: Watering crops (irrigation) saves them when sunshine is too much.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Which garden tool is used for harvesting root crops? A: Fork hoe. A fork hoe digs out root crops like cassava without cutting them.
chunks.source: A fork hoe digs out root crops like cassava without cutting them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Which garden tool is used for watering crops? A: Watering can. A watering can sprinkles water on crops.
chunks.source: A watering can sprinkles water on crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give one way a slasher can be dangerous to the person using it. A: It can cut the user. A slasher has a sharp blade that can injure the user.
chunks.source: A slasher has a sharp blade that can injure the user.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How can one take care of a slasher? A: By cleaning it after use and keeping it in a dry place. Cleaning and keeping tools dry prevents rust.
chunks.source: Cleaning and keeping tools dry prevents rust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Define the term personal hygiene. A: The keeping of our bodies and the things we use clean. Personal hygiene means keeping our body, clothes and surroundings clean.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene means keeping our body, clothes and surroundings clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Name one activity used to keep our hair neat and clean. A: Washing the hair. Washing removes dirt and oil from hair.
chunks.source: Washing removes dirt and oil from hair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Name another activity used to keep our hair neat and clean. A: Combing the hair. Combing keeps hair tidy and neat.
chunks.source: Combing keeps hair tidy and neat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give one importance of maintaining proper personal hygiene. A: It prevents diseases. Clean bodies keep germs away so we do not fall sick.
chunks.source: Clean bodies keep germs away so we do not fall sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the vector involved in the 4Fs cycle. A: Housefly. The housefly carries germs from faeces to food in the 4Fs chain.
chunks.source: The housefly carries germs from faeces to food in the 4Fs chain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Identify one disease spread through 4Fs. A: Cholera. The 4Fs (faeces, flies, food, fingers) spread cholera.
chunks.source: The 4Fs (faeces, flies, food, fingers) spread cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Identify another disease spread through 4Fs. A: Typhoid. Typhoid also spreads through the 4Fs chain.
chunks.source: Typhoid also spreads through the 4Fs chain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give one way of controlling the spread of diseases by the insect vector in (a) above. A: By covering food properly. Covered food keeps houseflies and their germs away.
chunks.source: Covered food keeps houseflies and their germs away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one material that can be used to build a house. A: Bricks. Bricks are strong materials used to build walls of houses.
chunks.source: Bricks are strong materials used to build walls of houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a pit latrine useful in a home? A: It is used for disposing human faeces. A pit latrine keeps faeces in one safe place so diseases do not spread.
chunks.source: A pit latrine keeps faeces in one safe place so diseases do not spread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which human body part is used for seeing? A: Eye. We see with our eyes.
chunks.source: We see with our eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do most flowering plants reproduce? A: Through seeds. Most flowering plants make seeds which grow into new plants.
chunks.source: Most flowering plants make seeds which grow into new plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way clouds are useful to people in the environment. A: They bring rain. Clouds give us rain which waters crops.
chunks.source: Clouds give us rain which waters crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest one way you would prevent garden tools from rusting. A: By oiling them. Oil keeps water and air away from metal so it does not rust.
chunks.source: Oil keeps water and air away from metal so it does not rust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can people control soil erosion in a school compound? A: By planting grass. Grass holds the soil so running water cannot wash it away.
chunks.source: Grass holds the soil so running water cannot wash it away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one object that can cause wounds. A: Nail. Sharp objects like nails can cut the skin and cause wounds.
chunks.source: Sharp objects like nails can cut the skin and cause wounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which seed is an example of epigeal germination? A: Bean seed. In epigeal germination the cotyledons are carried above the ground, as in beans.
chunks.source: In epigeal germination the cotyledons are carried above the ground, as in beans.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can an individual manage sunny weather? A: By staying in a shade. Shade protects us from too much sunshine.
chunks.source: Shade protects us from too much sunshine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should pedestrians cross a busy road at a zebra crossing? A: Because it is safe. Drivers stop for pedestrians at a zebra crossing.
chunks.source: Drivers stop for pedestrians at a zebra crossing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest any one way people can care for domestic animals. A: By feeding them well. Well-fed animals stay healthy and strong.
chunks.source: Well-fed animals stay healthy and strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is too much sunshine dangerous to a crop farmer? A: It dries up crops. Too much sunshine withers crops and leads to poor harvests.
chunks.source: Too much sunshine withers crops and leads to poor harvests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way can you control the spread of malaria at home? A: By sleeping under a mosquito net. A mosquito net stops mosquitoes from biting us at night.
chunks.source: A mosquito net stops mosquitoes from biting us at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way school children use water. A: For drinking. Children drink water to stay healthy.
chunks.source: Children drink water to stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one importance of food to the body. A: It gives the body energy. Food gives us energy to work and play.
chunks.source: Food gives us energy to work and play.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do you clean your body using soap? A: To remove dirt and kill germs. Soap removes dirt and kills germs on the skin.
chunks.source: Soap removes dirt and kills germs on the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the insect above. A: Grasshopper. The insect with long jumping hind legs is a grasshopper.
chunks.source: The insect with long jumping hind legs is a grasshopper.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one use of plants to animals. A: They provide food to animals. Animals eat plants and plant products.
chunks.source: Animals eat plants and plant products.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should people wash fruits before eating them? A: To remove germs and chemicals. Fruits may carry germs and spray chemicals that make us sick.
chunks.source: Fruits may carry germs and spray chemicals that make us sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which layer of the soil profile is the subsoil? A: Subsoil. The subsoil is the layer just below the topsoil.
chunks.source: The subsoil is the layer just below the topsoil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important to keep water sources such as wells clean? A: To prevent water-borne diseases. Dirty water carries germs that cause diseases like cholera.
chunks.source: Dirty water carries germs that cause diseases like cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one way a farmer can control pests in a maize garden. A: By spraying with pesticides. Pesticides kill pests that attack crops.
chunks.source: Pesticides kill pests that attack crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you use banana fibres at home? A: For making ropes. Banana fibres are strong and can be twisted into ropes and mats.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are strong and can be twisted into ropes and mats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the crop growing practice where unwanted plants are removed from the garden. A: Weeding. Weeding is removing unwanted plants (weeds) from the garden.
chunks.source: Weeding is removing unwanted plants (weeds) from the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the type of soil used for making pots. A: Clay soil. Clay soil sticks together and holds shape, good for pots.
chunks.source: Clay soil sticks together and holds shape, good for pots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a P.4 child keep his/her finger nails clean? A: By cutting them short and washing hands. Short clean nails do not hide dirt and germs.
chunks.source: Short clean nails do not hide dirt and germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of trees found in the school compound. A: They provide shade. Trees give shade where pupils rest.
chunks.source: Trees give shade where pupils rest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the component of soil that plants use during photosynthesis. A: Water. Plants take water from the soil to make food.
chunks.source: Plants take water from the soil to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do crop farmers use rabbit droppings? A: As manure. Rabbit droppings decay into manure that makes soil fertile.
chunks.source: Rabbit droppings decay into manure that makes soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of electricity at home. A: It can shock a person. Touching naked wires can give a dangerous electric shock.
chunks.source: Touching naked wires can give a dangerous electric shock.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you prevent meat from going bad? A: By smoking it. Smoking removes water from meat so germs cannot grow.
chunks.source: Smoking removes water from meat so germs cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the method you can use to control cockroaches at home. A: Spraying with insecticides. Insecticides kill cockroaches in the house.
chunks.source: Insecticides kill cockroaches in the house.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is too much sunshine dangerous to crop farmers? A: It dries up crops. Too much sunshine causes drought and poor harvests.
chunks.source: Too much sunshine causes drought and poor harvests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one animal that lives in water. A: Fish. Fish live and breathe in water.
chunks.source: Fish live and breathe in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one source of food. A: Plants. Plants give us food like fruits, vegetables and grains.
chunks.source: Plants give us food like fruits, vegetables and grains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one use of stones to people in our community. A: For building houses. Stones are used to build strong houses and walls.
chunks.source: Stones are used to build strong houses and walls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do parents protect their children from polio? A: By immunisation. The polio vaccine protects children from polio.
chunks.source: The polio vaccine protects children from polio.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one farming activity commonly done during a wet season. A: Planting. Farmers plant crops when the rains come.
chunks.source: Farmers plant crops when the rains come.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Of what use is part marked A to people? A: It is used for wrapping food. Banana leaves are used to wrap and steam food like matooke.
chunks.source: Banana leaves are used to wrap and steam food like matooke.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name one condition necessary for rusting to take place. A: Oxygen (air). Rusting needs both air and water on iron.
chunks.source: Rusting needs both air and water on iron.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name another condition necessary for rusting to take place. A: Water (moisture). Rusting needs both water and air on iron.
chunks.source: Rusting needs both water and air on iron.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) How can people prevent their tools from rusting? A: By painting them. Paint keeps air and water away from the metal.
chunks.source: Paint keeps air and water away from the metal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Write down one danger of rusting. A: It weakens tools. Rust eats metal so tools become weak and break.
chunks.source: Rust eats metal so tools become weak and break.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is pollination? A: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower. Pollination must happen before a flower can make fruits and seeds.
chunks.source: Pollination must happen before a flower can make fruits and seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) State one type of pollination. A: Self pollination. In self pollination, pollen moves within the same flower.
chunks.source: In self pollination, pollen moves within the same flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) State another type of pollination. A: Cross pollination. In cross pollination, pollen moves from one flower to another.
chunks.source: In cross pollination, pollen moves from one flower to another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Name the bright coloured structures that attract pollinators in flowers. A: Petals. Bright petals attract insects like bees to flowers.
chunks.source: Bright petals attract insects like bees to flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is the experiment about? A: To show that oxygen supports burning. The candle under test goes off when oxygen is used up.
chunks.source: The candle under test goes off when oxygen is used up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Why did the candle go off in B? A: Because it lacked oxygen. The burning candle used up the oxygen around it and went off.
chunks.source: The burning candle used up the oxygen around it and went off.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Which gas is produced as the candle burns in A? A: Carbon dioxide. Burning produces carbon dioxide gas.
chunks.source: Burning produces carbon dioxide gas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) Give any one use of fire to people. A: For cooking food. Fire gives heat used for cooking.
chunks.source: Fire gives heat used for cooking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the process marked A on the diagram. A: Evaporation. A is evaporation: the sun heats water and it rises as vapour.
chunks.source: A is evaporation: the sun heats water and it rises as vapour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the process marked B on the diagram. A: Condensation. B is condensation: vapour cools and forms clouds.
chunks.source: B is condensation: vapour cools and forms clouds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) What is the importance of the sun in the process above? A: It provides heat that causes evaporation. The sun's heat turns water into vapour.
chunks.source: The sun's heat turns water into vapour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) What scientific name is given to all the processes above? A: The water cycle. Evaporation, condensation and rain together form the water cycle.
chunks.source: Evaporation, condensation and rain together form the water cycle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Name one class of food. A: Proteins. Proteins build the body; other classes are carbohydrates and vitamins.
chunks.source: Proteins build the body; other classes are carbohydrates and vitamins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name another class of food. A: Carbohydrates. Carbohydrates give the body energy.
chunks.source: Carbohydrates give the body energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one danger of poor feeding to a child. A: Kwashiorkor. Lack of proteins causes kwashiorkor in children.
chunks.source: Lack of proteins causes kwashiorkor in children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another danger of poor feeding to a child. A: Marasmus. Lack of enough food causes marasmus.
chunks.source: Lack of enough food causes marasmus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Which local material is used to make ropes? A: Banana fibres. Banana fibres are twisted to make strong ropes.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are twisted to make strong ropes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Which local material is used to make mats? A: Palm leaves. Palm leaves are woven into mats.
chunks.source: Palm leaves are woven into mats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Identify the tool used for sweeping. A: Broom. A broom is used for sweeping.
chunks.source: A broom is used for sweeping.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Identify the tool used for slashing. A: Slasher. A slasher cuts grass and bushes.
chunks.source: A slasher cuts grass and bushes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Write one example of a useful insect. A: Bee. Bees give us honey and pollinate flowers.
chunks.source: Bees give us honey and pollinate flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Write another example of a useful insect. A: Butterfly. Butterflies pollinate flowers.
chunks.source: Butterflies pollinate flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give any one example of a harmful insect. A: Mosquito. Mosquitoes spread malaria.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes spread malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How can people care for useful insects? A: By not killing them. We protect useful insects by keeping their habitats safe.
chunks.source: We protect useful insects by keeping their habitats safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What are perennial crops? A: Crops that take more than a year to mature and yield for many years. Perennial crops like coffee stay in the garden for years.
chunks.source: Perennial crops like coffee stay in the garden for years.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Mention one example of a perennial crop. A: Coffee. Coffee is a perennial crop harvested year after year.
chunks.source: Coffee is a perennial crop harvested year after year.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Mention another example of a perennial crop. A: Bananas. Banana plants keep producing for years.
chunks.source: Banana plants keep producing for years.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Why would you classify simsim as an annual crop? A: Because it completes its life cycle within one season. Annual crops grow and are harvested within one year.
chunks.source: Annual crops grow and are harvested within one year.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name one item found in a first aid box. A: Bandage. A bandage is kept in a first aid box for covering wounds.
chunks.source: A bandage is kept in a first aid box for covering wounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name another item found in a first aid box. A: Plaster. Plasters cover small cuts.
chunks.source: Plasters cover small cuts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Why should accident victims be given first aid? A: To save their lives. First aid keeps the victim alive before a doctor comes.
chunks.source: First aid keeps the victim alive before a doctor comes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How can people control and prevent accidents at home? A: By keeping dangerous objects out of children's reach. Sharp and poisonous things kept away cannot harm children.
chunks.source: Sharp and poisonous things kept away cannot harm children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) State one example of a domestic bird. A: Chicken. Chickens are common domestic birds.
chunks.source: Chickens are common domestic birds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) State another example of a domestic bird. A: Duck. Ducks are also kept at home.
chunks.source: Ducks are also kept at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Write one thing people get from domestic birds. A: Eggs. Hens lay eggs we eat.
chunks.source: Hens lay eggs we eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Write another thing people get from domestic birds. A: Meat. We get meat from chickens and ducks.
chunks.source: We get meat from chickens and ducks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Which garden tool is used for weeding? A: Hoe. A hoe is used to dig out weeds.
chunks.source: A hoe is used to dig out weeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Which garden tool is used for cutting trees? A: Axe. An axe cuts down trees.
chunks.source: An axe cuts down trees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) State one way of caring for garden tools. A: Cleaning them after use. Clean tools last longer.
chunks.source: Clean tools last longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) State another way of caring for garden tools. A: Keeping them in a dry place. Dry storage prevents rust.
chunks.source: Dry storage prevents rust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) How is the sun important to people? A: It gives us light. Sunlight lights our day.
chunks.source: Sunlight lights our day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) How else is the sun important to people? A: It gives us heat. The sun warms us and helps plants make food.
chunks.source: The sun warms us and helps plants make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give any one importance of shadows to people. A: They help us to tell time. Shadows move as the sun moves, showing time.
chunks.source: Shadows move as the sun moves, showing time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) State one danger of the sun. A: It can cause sunburn. Too much sunshine burns the skin.
chunks.source: Too much sunshine burns the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Give one importance of a sick bay at school. A: Sick pupils get first aid there. A sick bay is where ill pupils rest and get help.
chunks.source: A sick bay is where ill pupils rest and get help.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name one group of people who work in a sick bay. A: Nurses. Nurses treat sick people in a sick bay.
chunks.source: Nurses treat sick people in a sick bay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Identify any one material found in a sick bay. A: Bandages. Bandages are kept in a sick bay for wounds.
chunks.source: Bandages are kept in a sick bay for wounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Name any one place in your community which has a similar function as a sick bay. A: Hospital. A hospital treats sick people like a sick bay.
chunks.source: A hospital treats sick people like a sick bay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is personal hygiene? A: The keeping of our bodies clean. Personal hygiene means keeping our body clean every day.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene means keeping our body clean every day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) State any one danger of poor personal hygiene. A: It causes diseases. Dirty bodies attract germs that cause diseases.
chunks.source: Dirty bodies attract germs that cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(i) What can you do to promote personal hygiene? A: Bathing daily. Daily bathing keeps the body clean.
chunks.source: Daily bathing keeps the body clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(ii) What else can you do to promote personal hygiene? A: Washing hands before eating. Clean hands keep germs out of food.
chunks.source: Clean hands keep germs out of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the vectors with the diseases they spread. A: Female anopheles mosquito: malaria; Tsetse fly: sleeping sickness; Black fly: river blindness; Housefly: diarrhoea. Female anopheles spreads malaria, tsetse fly sleeping sickness, black fly river blindness and housefly diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Female anopheles spreads malaria, tsetse fly sleeping sickness, black fly river blindness and housefly diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a dicotyledonous seed. A: Bean seed. Bean seeds have two cotyledons.
chunks.source: Bean seeds have two cotyledons.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one domestic animal that gives us milk. A: Cow. Cows give us milk.
chunks.source: Cows give us milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one component of soil. A: Water. Soil is made of water, air, humus and mineral salts.
chunks.source: Soil is made of water, air, humus and mineral salts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of shadows to people. A: They help us to tell time. Shadows change with the sun's movement.
chunks.source: Shadows change with the sun's movement.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one material used to make a kite used for playing. A: Polythene paper. Kites are made from light paper, sticks and strings.
chunks.source: Kites are made from light paper, sticks and strings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we iron clothes? A: To kill germs in them. Ironing kills germs and makes clothes neat.
chunks.source: Ironing kills germs and makes clothes neat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one place where harvested crops can be stored. A: Granary. A granary is a store for harvested crops.
chunks.source: A granary is a store for harvested crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which item is used to keep our bodies clean? A: Soap. Soap removes dirt and germs from the body.
chunks.source: Soap removes dirt and germs from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a maize grain called a fruit? A: Because it developed from the ovary wall of a flower. A maize grain is a caryopsis fruit with the seed coat fused to the fruit wall.
chunks.source: A maize grain is a caryopsis fruit with the seed coat fused to the fruit wall.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is wind? A: Moving air. Wind is air moving from one place to another.
chunks.source: Wind is air moving from one place to another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the plant fibre used for making balls. A: Banana fibres. Banana fibres are rolled to make balls.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are rolled to make balls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from cirrus, name any other type of clouds. A: Cumulus. Cloud types include cirrus, cumulus, stratus and nimbus.
chunks.source: Cloud types include cirrus, cumulus, stratus and nimbus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the root system drawn above. A: Taproot system. The diagram shows one main root with side roots: a taproot system.
chunks.source: The diagram shows one main root with side roots: a taproot system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one example of a plant with the above type of root system. A: Bean plant. Beans and mangoes have taproot systems.
chunks.source: Beans and mangoes have taproot systems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we call the young plant in the garden? A: Seedling. A young plant is called a seedling.
chunks.source: A young plant is called a seedling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which some plants climb others. A: By tendrils. Climbing plants hold others using tendrils.
chunks.source: Climbing plants hold others using tendrils.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do flowering plants reproduce? A: By seeds. Flowering plants make seeds that grow into new plants.
chunks.source: Flowering plants make seeds that grow into new plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does the experiment below show? A: Transpiration in plants. Water drops on the polythene show the plant gives off water vapour.
chunks.source: Water drops on the polythene show the plant gives off water vapour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one common accident at home. A: Burns. Burns from fire or hot things are common at home.
chunks.source: Burns from fire or hot things are common at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the sanitation material we use for putting on plates to dry. A: Rack. A plate rack holds plates to dry.
chunks.source: A plate rack holds plates to dry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one natural change in the environment. A: Rainfall. Natural changes include rainfall, drought and floods.
chunks.source: Natural changes include rainfall, drought and floods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of caring for our teeth. A: Brushing teeth daily. Brushing removes food remains that rot teeth.
chunks.source: Brushing removes food remains that rot teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one type of soil. A: Clay soil. Soil types are clay, sand and loam.
chunks.source: Soil types are clay, sand and loam.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of leaf shown in the diagram. A: Trifoliate leaf. The leaf has three leaflets: a trifoliate leaf.
chunks.source: The leaf has three leaflets: a trifoliate leaf.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a dog important at home? A: It guards our home. Dogs bark at and chase away thieves and wild animals.
chunks.source: Dogs bark at and chase away thieves and wild animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are beans called annual crops? A: Because they complete their life cycle in one season. Annual crops mature and are harvested within one year.
chunks.source: Annual crops mature and are harvested within one year.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of leaves to plants. A: They make food for the plant. Leaves trap sunlight to make food.
chunks.source: Leaves trap sunlight to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one activity done to clean our bodies. A: Bathing. Bathing cleans the whole body.
chunks.source: Bathing cleans the whole body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are pests? A: Living organisms that destroy crops. Pests are creatures that damage crops and animals.
chunks.source: Pests are creatures that damage crops and animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the structure drawn in the diagram below. A: A nursery bed. The diagram shows a nursery bed with a shade where seedlings are raised.
chunks.source: The diagram shows a nursery bed with a shade where seedlings are raised.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of germination do beans undergo? A: Epigeal germination. Beans carry their cotyledons above the ground.
chunks.source: Beans carry their cotyledons above the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one method used in growing plants. A: Planting seeds. We grow plants by planting seeds or seedlings.
chunks.source: We grow plants by planting seeds or seedlings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of wind. A: It blows off roofs. Strong wind destroys roofs and crops.
chunks.source: Strong wind destroys roofs and crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to a male part of a flower? A: Stamen. The stamen is the male part that makes pollen.
chunks.source: The stamen is the male part that makes pollen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are people encouraged to boil water for drinking? A: To kill germs. Boiling kills germs in water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of a dust bin in your classroom. A: It keeps the classroom clean. Rubbish in a dustbin keeps the class tidy.
chunks.source: Rubbish in a dustbin keeps the class tidy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one insect that protects itself by stinging. A: Bee. Bees sting to protect themselves.
chunks.source: Bees sting to protect themselves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one type of leaf venation. A: Netted venation. Leaf veins can be netted or parallel.
chunks.source: Leaf veins can be netted or parallel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one place where houseflies lay their eggs. A: On rotting matter. Houseflies lay eggs on faeces and rotting rubbish.
chunks.source: Houseflies lay eggs on faeces and rotting rubbish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of plants to people. A: They give us food. Plants give food, medicine, timber and shade.
chunks.source: Plants give food, medicine, timber and shade.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is seed germination? A: The development of a seed into a young plant. Germination is when a seed starts to grow into a seedling.
chunks.source: Germination is when a seed starts to grow into a seedling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one condition needed for seeds to germinate. A: Water (moisture). Seeds need water, warmth and air to germinate.
chunks.source: Seeds need water, warmth and air to germinate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another condition needed for seeds to germinate. A: Warmth. Seeds need warmth, water and air to germinate.
chunks.source: Seeds need warmth, water and air to germinate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Mention any one type of germination. A: Epigeal germination. Types are epigeal and hypogeal germination.
chunks.source: Types are epigeal and hypogeal germination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is personal hygiene? A: The keeping of our bodies clean. Personal hygiene is keeping our body clean every day.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene is keeping our body clean every day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one way of promoting personal hygiene. A: Bathing daily. Daily bathing keeps us clean.
chunks.source: Daily bathing keeps us clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another way of promoting personal hygiene. A: Brushing teeth. Brushing keeps teeth clean and healthy.
chunks.source: Brushing keeps teeth clean and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) State any one danger of not promoting personal hygiene. A: It causes diseases. Poor hygiene lets germs make us sick.
chunks.source: Poor hygiene lets germs make us sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Name part marked A on the flowering plant. A: Flower. Part A is the flower.
chunks.source: Part A is the flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name part marked C on the flowering plant. A: Fruit. Part C is the fruit.
chunks.source: Part C is the fruit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Name the system of the plant marked X. A: Shoot system. X is the shoot system: stem, leaves, flowers above ground.
chunks.source: X is the shoot system: stem, leaves, flowers above ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Name the system of the plant marked Y. A: Root system. Y is the root system below the ground.
chunks.source: Y is the root system below the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Give one example of pests which attack crops in the garden. A: Weevils. Weevils bore into grains and crops.
chunks.source: Weevils bore into grains and crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give another example of pests which attack crops in the garden. A: Locusts. Locusts eat up whole gardens.
chunks.source: Locusts eat up whole gardens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Mention any one way of controlling pests in the garden. A: By spraying with pesticides. Pesticides kill crop pests.
chunks.source: Pesticides kill crop pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Mention any one disease of crops. A: Blight. Blight attacks leaves of crops like tomatoes.
chunks.source: Blight attacks leaves of crops like tomatoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Name one crop grown in a nursery bed. A: Tomatoes. Tomato seedlings are raised in nursery beds.
chunks.source: Tomato seedlings are raised in nursery beds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name another crop grown in a nursery bed. A: Cabbages. Cabbage seedlings are raised in nursery beds.
chunks.source: Cabbage seedlings are raised in nursery beds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give any one way of caring for crops in a nursery bed. A: Watering them. Seedlings need water to grow.
chunks.source: Seedlings need water to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Why is transplanting of seedlings done in the evening? A: To prevent wilting. Evenings are cool, so seedlings do not lose much water.
chunks.source: Evenings are cool, so seedlings do not lose much water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Mention one crop growing practice. A: Planting. Planting is putting seeds or seedlings in soil.
chunks.source: Planting is putting seeds or seedlings in soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Mention another crop growing practice. A: Weeding. Weeding removes unwanted plants.
chunks.source: Weeding removes unwanted plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one example of leafy vegetables. A: Cabbage. Cabbage leaves are eaten as vegetables.
chunks.source: Cabbage leaves are eaten as vegetables.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another example of leafy vegetables. A: Spinach. Spinach leaves are eaten as vegetables.
chunks.source: Spinach leaves are eaten as vegetables.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Name part marked W on the flower. A: Petal. W is a petal.
chunks.source: W is a petal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name part marked Y on the flower. A: Filament. Y is the filament holding the anther.
chunks.source: Y is the filament holding the anther.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) What does part Z develop into after fertilization? A: A fruit. The ovary (Z) grows into a fruit.
chunks.source: The ovary (Z) grows into a fruit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) State any one importance of flowers to people. A: They are used for decoration. Beautiful flowers decorate homes and ceremonies.
chunks.source: Beautiful flowers decorate homes and ceremonies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is pollination? A: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma. Pollination must happen before fruits and seeds form.
chunks.source: Pollination must happen before fruits and seeds form.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one type of pollination. A: Self pollination. Self pollination happens within one flower.
chunks.source: Self pollination happens within one flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another type of pollination. A: Cross pollination. Cross pollination happens between two flowers.
chunks.source: Cross pollination happens between two flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Which insect pollinates flowers at night? A: Moth. Moths visit flowers at night to pollinate them.
chunks.source: Moths visit flowers at night to pollinate them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What are perennial crops? A: Crops that take more than a year to mature and yield for many years. Perennials like coffee stay productive for years.
chunks.source: Perennials like coffee stay productive for years.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one example of a perennial crop. A: Coffee. Coffee yields for many years.
chunks.source: Coffee yields for many years.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another example of a perennial crop. A: Tea. Tea is harvested for many years.
chunks.source: Tea is harvested for many years.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Name any one method used to harvest perennial crops. A: Hand picking. Coffee and tea are picked by hand.
chunks.source: Coffee and tea are picked by hand.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What name is given to the food made by plants during photosynthesis? A: Starch. Plants make starch (glucose) as food.
chunks.source: Plants make starch (glucose) as food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one raw material needed by plants to make their food. A: Water. Plants need water and carbon dioxide to make food.
chunks.source: Plants need water and carbon dioxide to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another raw material needed by plants to make their food. A: Carbon dioxide. Plants take carbon dioxide from the air.
