chunks.source: Plants take carbon dioxide from the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Mention any one condition needed by plants to make their own food. A: Sunlight. Sunlight gives energy for photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Sunlight gives energy for photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the weather in A to the correct activities in B. A: Rainy weather: Harvesting water; Windy weather: Winnowing seeds; Sunny weather: Drying harvested crops. Rainy weather is for harvesting water, windy weather for winnowing seeds, sunny weather for drying crops.
chunks.source: Rainy weather is for harvesting water, windy weather for winnowing seeds, sunny weather for drying crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Which of the above weather can be managed by putting on gumboots? A: Rainy weather. We wear gumboots in rainy weather to walk in mud.
chunks.source: We wear gumboots in rainy weather to walk in mud.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Give one type of stem. A: Erect stem. Erect stems stand upright like maize.
chunks.source: Erect stems stand upright like maize.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give another type of stem. A: Weak stem. Weak stems cannot stand alone, e.g. pumpkins.
chunks.source: Weak stems cannot stand alone, e.g. pumpkins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Mention one use of stems to people. A: Firewood. Stems are cut for firewood.
chunks.source: Stems are cut for firewood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Mention another use of stems to people. A: Building. Stems give timber for building.
chunks.source: Stems give timber for building.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Mention one source of water. A: Wells. Wells are dug sources of water.
chunks.source: Wells are dug sources of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Mention another source of water. A: Rivers. Rivers are natural sources of water.
chunks.source: Rivers are natural sources of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give any one use of water at home. A: For drinking. We drink water to live.
chunks.source: We drink water to live.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Write down any one way of making water safe for drinking at home. A: By boiling. Boiling kills germs in water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is air? A: A mixture of gases. Air is made of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen and others.
chunks.source: Air is made of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen and others.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Mention one gas found in air. A: Oxygen. Air contains oxygen which we breathe.
chunks.source: Air contains oxygen which we breathe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Mention another gas found in air. A: Carbon dioxide. Air contains carbon dioxide which plants use.
chunks.source: Air contains carbon dioxide which plants use.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) State any one property of air. A: Air occupies space. Air takes up space and has weight.
chunks.source: Air takes up space and has weight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the first garden tool below. A: Watering can. The first tool is a watering can for watering crops.
chunks.source: The first tool is a watering can for watering crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the second garden tool below. A: Axe. The second tool is an axe for cutting trees.
chunks.source: The second tool is an axe for cutting trees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one way of caring for garden tools. A: Cleaning them after use. Clean tools last longer.
chunks.source: Clean tools last longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another way of caring for garden tools. A: Oiling the metal parts. Oil stops metal tools from rusting.
chunks.source: Oil stops metal tools from rusting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one body organ used for hearing. A: Ear. We hear with our ears.
chunks.source: We hear with our ears.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the suitable time for transplanting seedlings. A: In the evening. Evenings are cool so seedlings do not wilt.
chunks.source: Evenings are cool so seedlings do not wilt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is personal hygiene? A: The keeping of our bodies clean. Personal hygiene means keeping our body clean.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene means keeping our body clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one disease of the teeth. A: Tooth decay. Tooth decay rots teeth.
chunks.source: Tooth decay rots teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it good to plant trees in the compound? A: To get shade. Trees give shade and control soil erosion.
chunks.source: Trees give shade and control soil erosion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a P.4 pupil protect his food from contamination? A: By covering it. Covered food keeps germs and flies away.
chunks.source: Covered food keeps germs and flies away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of leaf shown below. A: Simple leaf. The leaf has a single blade: a simple leaf.
chunks.source: The leaf has a single blade: a simple leaf.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one item used to promote sanitation. A: Broom. A broom sweeps dirt away.
chunks.source: A broom sweeps dirt away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down the cause of night blindness in people. A: Lack of vitamin A. Without vitamin A, people cannot see at night.
chunks.source: Without vitamin A, people cannot see at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which vector spreads cholera? A: Housefly. Houseflies carry cholera germs to food.
chunks.source: Houseflies carry cholera germs to food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is an accident? A: A sudden bad happening that causes injury. Accidents happen without warning and hurt people.
chunks.source: Accidents happen without warning and hurt people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of germination the maize grain undergo. A: Hypogeal germination. Maize keeps its cotyledon below the ground.
chunks.source: Maize keeps its cotyledon below the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one type of blood. A: Blood group O. Blood types include groups A, B, AB and O.
chunks.source: Blood types include groups A, B, AB and O.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of diarrhoeal diseases? A: Cholera. Cholera causes severe diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Cholera causes severe diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one raw material for photosynthesis. A: Water. Plants use water to make food.
chunks.source: Plants use water to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List down one use of food in the body. A: It gives the body energy. Food gives energy to work and play.
chunks.source: Food gives energy to work and play.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which mineral salt is needed in the body to prevent anaemia? A: Iron. Iron makes blood and prevents anaemia.
chunks.source: Iron makes blood and prevents anaemia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of tooth shown below. A: Molar. The broad flat tooth for grinding is a molar.
chunks.source: The broad flat tooth for grinding is a molar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is sanitation? A: The keeping of our environment clean. Sanitation means keeping our surroundings clean.
chunks.source: Sanitation means keeping our surroundings clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do plants with weak stems climb others? A: To get sunlight. Climbers rise to reach sunlight.
chunks.source: Climbers rise to reach sunlight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do we call the green colouring matter in the leaf? A: Chlorophyll. Chlorophyll makes leaves green.
chunks.source: Chlorophyll makes leaves green.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write S.S.S in full. A: Salt Sugar Solution. SSS is a home drink for replacing lost body fluids.
chunks.source: SSS is a home drink for replacing lost body fluids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one common accident at school. A: Falls. Pupils often fall and get hurt at school.
chunks.source: Pupils often fall and get hurt at school.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one animal protein. A: Meat. Meat, eggs and milk are animal proteins.
chunks.source: Meat, eggs and milk are animal proteins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way a P.4 pupil can promote oral health. A: Brushing teeth. Brushing keeps teeth clean and strong.
chunks.source: Brushing keeps teeth clean and strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a germ? A: A tiny living organism that causes disease. Germs are so small we cannot see them.
chunks.source: Germs are so small we cannot see them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way we keep our bodies clean. A: By bathing. Bathing cleans the body.
chunks.source: Bathing cleans the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part marked Y on the root below. A: Root nodules. Y points to root nodules that keep nitrogen-fixing bacteria.
chunks.source: Y points to root nodules that keep nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of roots to the plants. A: They absorb water and mineral salts. Roots take in water and nutrients for the plant.
chunks.source: Roots take in water and nutrients for the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does blood go to the lungs? A: To pick up oxygen. Blood collects oxygen in the lungs.
chunks.source: Blood collects oxygen in the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one sign of goitre. A: Swollen neck. Goitre swells the neck from lack of iodine.
chunks.source: Goitre swells the neck from lack of iodine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one danger of poor sanitation in the environment. A: It causes diseases. Dirty environments breed germs.
chunks.source: Dirty environments breed germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are carrots propagated? A: By seeds. Carrots are grown from seeds.
chunks.source: Carrots are grown from seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one example of a non-communicable disease. A: Diabetes. Diabetes cannot spread from person to person.
chunks.source: Diabetes cannot spread from person to person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which body organ protects the brain? A: Skull. The skull is the hard bone covering the brain.
chunks.source: The skull is the hard bone covering the brain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do tape worms enter our bodies? A: Through eating undercooked infected meat. Tapeworms in half-cooked meat enter our intestines.
chunks.source: Tapeworms in half-cooked meat enter our intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one disease that can be got due to poor personal hygiene. A: Cholera. Poor hygiene spreads cholera.
chunks.source: Poor hygiene spreads cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do we call a female part of the flower? A: Pistil. The pistil is the female part of a flower.
chunks.source: The pistil is the female part of a flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The nose is to people while _______________ is to leaves. A: Stomata. Leaves breathe through tiny stomata.
chunks.source: Leaves breathe through tiny stomata.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one place where germs are got. A: In dirty places. Germs live in latrines, rubbish pits and dirty water.
chunks.source: Germs live in latrines, rubbish pits and dirty water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is pollination? A: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma. Pollination must happen before fruits and seeds form.
chunks.source: Pollination must happen before fruits and seeds form.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) State any one type of pollination. A: Self pollination. Self pollination happens within one flower.
chunks.source: Self pollination happens within one flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Name the insect that pollinates flowers at night. A: Moth. Moths visit flowers at night.
chunks.source: Moths visit flowers at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) What helps the insect named above to reach the flowers at night? A: The sweet smell of the flowers. Moths are attracted by the scent of flowers.
chunks.source: Moths are attracted by the scent of flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Why do we wash our hands with soap after visiting the latrine? A: To remove germs. Soap kills germs picked up in the latrine.
chunks.source: Soap kills germs picked up in the latrine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give one reason why finger nails should be kept short. A: To prevent dirt and germs hiding under them. Long nails hide dirt that carries germs.
chunks.source: Long nails hide dirt that carries germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(i) List down one item used to promote personal hygiene. A: Soap. Soap cleans the body.
chunks.source: Soap cleans the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(ii) List down another item used to promote personal hygiene. A: Toothbrush. A toothbrush cleans teeth.
chunks.source: A toothbrush cleans teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (i) Why do people eat food? Give one reason. A: To get energy. Food gives energy to work.
chunks.source: Food gives energy to work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (ii) Why do people eat food? Give a second reason. A: To grow. Food builds our bodies so we grow.
chunks.source: Food builds our bodies so we grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (iii) Why do people eat food? Give a third reason. A: To stay healthy and fight diseases. Food protects the body against diseases.
chunks.source: Food protects the body against diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (iv) Why do people eat food? Give a fourth reason. A: To repair worn-out body parts. Food replaces damaged body parts.
chunks.source: Food replaces damaged body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is germination? A: The development of a seed into a young plant. Germination is a seed starting to grow.
chunks.source: Germination is a seed starting to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) How is rusting similar to germination? A: Both need water and air to take place. Rusting and germination both require moisture and oxygen.
chunks.source: Rusting and germination both require moisture and oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give the function of water during germination. A: It softens the seed coat. Water softens the testa so the embryo can grow out.
chunks.source: Water softens the testa so the embryo can grow out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) Write down one factor that can lead to seed dormancy. A: Lack of water. Dry seeds stay dormant until they get water.
chunks.source: Dry seeds stay dormant until they get water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the classes of food to the diseases below. A: Proteins: Kwashiorkor; Vitamin B1: Beriberi; Vitamin D: Rickets; Vitamin A: Night blindness. Lack of proteins causes kwashiorkor, vitamin B1 beriberi, vitamin D rickets and vitamin A night blindness.
chunks.source: Lack of proteins causes kwashiorkor, vitamin B1 beriberi, vitamin D rickets and vitamin A night blindness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (i) Write 4Fs in full: F number 1. A: Faeces. The first F is faeces.
chunks.source: The first F is faeces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (ii) Write 4Fs in full: F number 2. A: Flies. The second F is flies.
chunks.source: The second F is flies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (iii) Write 4Fs in full: F number 3. A: Food. The third F is food.
chunks.source: The third F is food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (iv) Write 4Fs in full: F number 4. A: Fingers. The fourth F is fingers.
chunks.source: The fourth F is fingers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is dehydration? A: The loss of a lot of water and salts from the body. Dehydration happens after diarrhoea or vomiting.
chunks.source: Dehydration happens after diarrhoea or vomiting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give one sign of a dehydrated person. A: Sunken eyes. Dehydrated people have sunken eyes and a dry mouth.
chunks.source: Dehydrated people have sunken eyes and a dry mouth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Why is ORS given to a person with severe burns? A: To replace the water lost from the body. Burns make the body lose a lot of water.
chunks.source: Burns make the body lose a lot of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) How is sugar in ORS solution important to a dehydrated person? A: It gives energy to the body. Sugar in ORS gives the weak body energy.
chunks.source: Sugar in ORS gives the weak body energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the body part that protects the lungs. A: Rib cage. The ribs form a cage around the lungs.
chunks.source: The ribs form a cage around the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one function of the brain. A: It controls body activities. The brain tells body parts what to do.
chunks.source: The brain tells body parts what to do.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another function of the brain. A: It stores memory. The brain remembers things.
chunks.source: The brain remembers things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Write the vector that spreads trachoma to people. A: Housefly. Houseflies spread trachoma to the eyes.
chunks.source: Houseflies spread trachoma to the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) How is a dust bin important in a classroom? A: It keeps the classroom clean. Rubbish goes into the dustbin.
chunks.source: Rubbish goes into the dustbin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one activity done to promote sanitation. A: Sweeping. Sweeping removes dirt.
chunks.source: Sweeping removes dirt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another activity done to promote sanitation. A: Mopping. Mopping cleans floors.
chunks.source: Mopping cleans floors.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) List down one quality of a hygienic home. A: It has a clean compound. A hygienic home is clean inside and outside.
chunks.source: A hygienic home is clean inside and outside.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (i) Write the 3Ds in full: D number 1. A: Dirt. The first D is dirt.
chunks.source: The first D is dirt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (ii) Write the 3Ds in full: D number 2. A: Disease. Dirt brings disease.
chunks.source: Dirt brings disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (iii) Write the 3Ds in full: D number 3. A: Death. Disease can lead to death.
chunks.source: Disease can lead to death.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give any one way we can prevent typhoid in our homes. A: By boiling drinking water. Boiled water has no typhoid germs.
chunks.source: Boiled water has no typhoid germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Apart from brushing the teeth, give one way we can care for our teeth. A: Avoiding sugary foods. Sweets rot teeth.
chunks.source: Sweets rot teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Apart from brushing the teeth, give another way we can care for our teeth. A: Visiting the dentist. The dentist checks and treats teeth.
chunks.source: The dentist checks and treats teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) How are canine teeth important to dogs? A: For tearing meat. Dogs tear meat with sharp canines.
chunks.source: Dogs tear meat with sharp canines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Name one set of the teeth. A: Milk teeth. The two sets are milk teeth and permanent teeth.
chunks.source: The two sets are milk teeth and permanent teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is weather? A: The daily condition of the atmosphere. Weather tells whether a day is rainy or sunny.
chunks.source: Weather tells whether a day is rainy or sunny.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) How is sunny weather important to a farmer? A: It helps to dry harvested crops. Farmers dry crops in sunshine.
chunks.source: Farmers dry crops in sunshine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(i) Write down one element of weather. A: Rainfall. Rainfall is an element of weather.
chunks.source: Rainfall is an element of weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(ii) Write down another element of weather. A: Sunshine. Sunshine is an element of weather.
chunks.source: Sunshine is an element of weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Which part of a flower develops into a fruit? A: Ovary. The ovary grows into a fruit after fertilization.
chunks.source: The ovary grows into a fruit after fertilization.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Name part marked C. A: Petal. C points to a petal.
chunks.source: C points to a petal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(i) Give one function of a flower to man. A: For decoration. Flowers beautify homes and ceremonies.
chunks.source: Flowers beautify homes and ceremonies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(ii) Give another function of a flower to man. A: For making perfumes. Flowers give sweet smells for perfumes.
chunks.source: Flowers give sweet smells for perfumes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is transpiration? A: The loss of water vapour from plant leaves. Plants give off water vapour through leaves.
chunks.source: Plants give off water vapour through leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one factor that can affect the rate of transpiration. A: Temperature. Hot days increase transpiration.
chunks.source: Hot days increase transpiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another factor that can affect the rate of transpiration. A: Wind. Wind carries vapour away, increasing transpiration.
chunks.source: Wind carries vapour away, increasing transpiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How is transpiration important to a plant? A: It cools the plant. Transpiration cools the plant like sweating cools us.
chunks.source: Transpiration cools the plant like sweating cools us.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the type of air that supports burning. A: Oxygen. Oxygen helps things to burn.
chunks.source: Oxygen helps things to burn.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) How is wind important in the environment? A: It brings rain. Wind moves clouds that bring rain.
chunks.source: Wind moves clouds that bring rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(i) List down one project you know. A: Poultry keeping. Keeping chickens is a common project.
chunks.source: Keeping chickens is a common project.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(ii) List down another project you know. A: Vegetable growing. Growing vegetables is a common project.
chunks.source: Growing vegetables is a common project.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one domestic animal that gives us milk. A: cow. A cow is a domestic animal that gives us milk.
chunks.source: A cow is a domestic animal that gives us milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A cow is a domestic animal that gives us milk. A: True. A cow is a domestic animal that gives us milk.
chunks.source: A cow is a domestic animal that gives us milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What deficiency disease causes swelling of the neck? A: goitre. Goitre is caused by lack of iodine, and it makes the neck swell.
chunks.source: Goitre is caused by lack of iodine, and it makes the neck swell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: cow is caused by lack of iodine, and it makes the neck swell. A: False. Goitre is caused by lack of iodine, and it makes the neck swell.
chunks.source: Goitre is caused by lack of iodine, and it makes the neck swell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are ears useful to a dog? A: They are used for hearing. A dog uses its ears to hear sounds around it.
chunks.source: A dog uses its ears to hear sounds around it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A dog uses its ears to hear sounds around it. A: True. A dog uses its ears to hear sounds around it.
chunks.source: A dog uses its ears to hear sounds around it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which component of soil makes the soil fertile? A: humus. Humus is decayed plant and animal matter that makes soil fertile.
chunks.source: Humus is decayed plant and animal matter that makes soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: winnowing is decayed plant and animal matter that makes soil fertile. A: False. Humus is decayed plant and animal matter that makes soil fertile.
chunks.source: Humus is decayed plant and animal matter that makes soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of plant roots. Identify any one plant with such roots. A: maize. Maize has fibrous roots, like the many thin roots shown in the diagram.
chunks.source: Maize has fibrous roots, like the many thin roots shown in the diagram.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Maize has fibrous roots, like the many thin roots shown in the diagram. A: True. Maize has fibrous roots, like the many thin roots shown in the diagram.
chunks.source: Maize has fibrous roots, like the many thin roots shown in the diagram.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger of diseases to people. A: They can cause death. Diseases make people weak and can kill them.
chunks.source: Diseases make people weak and can kill them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The answer to "Give any one danger of diseases to people." is "housefly (or mosquito, bee)". A: False. Diseases make people weak and can kill them.
chunks.source: Diseases make people weak and can kill them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are termites similar to wasps in the way they live? A: They live in colonies (groups). Both termites and wasps are social insects that live together in colonies.
chunks.source: Both termites and wasps are social insects that live together in colonies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Both termites and wasps are social insects that live together in colonies. A: True. Both termites and wasps are social insects that live together in colonies.
chunks.source: Both termites and wasps are social insects that live together in colonies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which food value is needed most by people who make bricks? A: carbohydrates. Brick makers do hard work, so they need carbohydrates, the energy-giving food value.
chunks.source: Brick makers do hard work, so they need carbohydrates, the energy-giving food value.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Brick makers do hard work, so they need thermometer, the energy-giving food value. A: False. Brick makers do hard work, so they need carbohydrates, the energy-giving food value.
chunks.source: Brick makers do hard work, so they need carbohydrates, the energy-giving food value.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one effect of drought to people. A: It causes hunger and famine. Drought dries crops and water sources, so people go hungry.
chunks.source: Drought dries crops and water sources, so people go hungry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Drought dries crops and water sources, so people go hungry. A: True. Drought dries crops and water sources, so people go hungry.
chunks.source: Drought dries crops and water sources, so people go hungry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of killing germs and vectors in our clothes. A: Ironing the clothes. The heat of ironing kills germs and vectors hiding in clothes.
chunks.source: The heat of ironing kills germs and vectors hiding in clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The answer to "Give any one way of killing germs and vectors in our clothes." is "tooth decay (cavities)". A: False. The heat of ironing kills germs and vectors hiding in clothes.
chunks.source: The heat of ironing kills germs and vectors hiding in clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one childhood immunisable disease in our community. A: polio. Polio is one of the diseases children are immunised against.
chunks.source: Polio is one of the diseases children are immunised against.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Polio is one of the diseases children are immunised against. A: True. Polio is one of the diseases children are immunised against.
chunks.source: Polio is one of the diseases children are immunised against.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the human body organ. Name the body organ shown. A: stomach. The diagram shows the stomach, the bag-like organ where food is churned.
chunks.source: The diagram shows the stomach, the bag-like organ where food is churned.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows the thermometer, the bag-like organ where food is churned. A: False. The diagram shows the stomach, the bag-like organ where food is churned.
chunks.source: The diagram shows the stomach, the bag-like organ where food is churned.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which instrument is used by health workers to find the body temperature of a patient? A: thermometer. A thermometer measures how hot or cold the body is.
chunks.source: A thermometer measures how hot or cold the body is.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A thermometer measures how hot or cold the body is. A: True. A thermometer measures how hot or cold the body is.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which deficiency disease can a child suffer from if he/she lacks enough carbohydrates? A: marasmus. Lack of energy foods (carbohydrates) causes marasmus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one cause of soil erosion. A: running water (or wind, deforestation). Fast-running water washes away top soil.
chunks.source: Fast-running water washes away top soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fast-running water washes away top soil. A: True. Fast-running water washes away top soil.
chunks.source: Fast-running water washes away top soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can erosion be controlled in a garden on hilly land? A: By terracing (or contour ploughing). Terraces slow down running water on hills.

chunks.text: Q: The answer to "How can erosion be controlled in a garden on hilly land?" is "carbon dioxide (or water, sunlight)". A: False. Terraces slow down running water on hills.

chunks.text: Q: Study the method of measuring. Which kind of objects are measured using the method shown? A: irregular objects (like stones). The displacement method measures the volume of irregular objects that sink.

chunks.text: Q: The displacement method measures the volume of irregular objects that sink. A: True. The displacement method measures the volume of irregular objects that sink.

chunks.text: Q: The stone displaced 20 cc of water and has a density of 3 g/cc. Calculate its mass. A: 60 grammes (60 g). Mass = density × volume = 3 g/cc × 20 cc = 60 g.

chunks.source: Cholera is a faecal disease spread through dirty faeces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way a P.5 child can prepare eggs for eating. A: By boiling (or frying) them. Eggs can be boiled or fried before eating.

chunks.text: Q: Eggs can be boiled or fried before eating. A: True. Eggs can be boiled or fried before eating.

chunks.text: Q: How are grasshoppers dangerous to farmers? A: They eat and destroy crops. Grasshoppers feed on crop leaves, destroying farmers' harvests.
chunks.source: Grasshoppers feed on crop leaves, destroying farmers' harvests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The answer to "How are grasshoppers dangerous to farmers?" is "thorn apple (or stinging nettle)". A: False. Grasshoppers feed on crop leaves, destroying farmers' harvests.

chunks.text: Q: Write any one use of banana fibres at school. A: Making ropes (or balls, mats). Banana fibres are woven into ropes and balls at school.

chunks.text: Q: Which part of a plant is used for sucking water from the ground? A: the roots. Roots suck water and nutrients from the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. Give any one thing that is given to patients in a hospital. A: Medicine/drugs (or food, or injections). Doctors give patients medicine to treat their sickness in hospital.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. Name one domestic animal that gives us a lot of milk. A: A cow. Cows are the main domestic animals kept for large amounts of milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 111. Which element of weather do people use for winnowing? A: Wind. Wind blows away the light chaff while the heavy grain falls down during winnowing.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light chaff while the heavy grain falls down during winnowing.

chunks.text: Q: 126. Which gas is needed by plants during photosynthesis? A: Carbon dioxide. Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air and use it with water to make food.

chunks.text: Q: 135. State one sign of food poisoning in people. A: Vomiting (also: diarrhoea, stomach pain). Spoilt food upsets the stomach, causing vomiting and diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 140. Write one type of germination. A: Epigeal germination (also: hypogeal germination). In epigeal germination the cotyledons come above the ground; in hypogeal they stay below.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 145. Apart from drinking water, name one other item used in the preparation of ORS locally. A: Salt (or sugar). Local ORS is made from clean water mixed with salt and sugar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are monkeys grouped under pests? A: Because they destroy crops. Monkeys raid gardens and eat or spoil farmers' crops, so they are pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which component of air supports burning? A: Oxygen. Oxygen in air helps things to burn; without it a fire goes off.

chunks.text: Q: Oxygen in air helps things to burn; without it a fire goes off. A: True. Oxygen in air helps things to burn; without it a fire goes off.

chunks.text: Q: How is chlorophyll important to plants? A: It traps sunlight for photosynthesis. Chlorophyll is the green colouring that traps sunlight so plants can make food.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: State the difference between a map and a picture. A: A map is drawn as seen from above, while a picture is drawn as seen from the side.. Maps give a top view; pictures show objects from the side.
chunks.source: Maps give a top view; pictures show objects from the side.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Mention any four qualities of a good map. A: Title, key, scale, compass direction.. A good map has a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.
chunks.source: A good map has a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Why are symbols used on a map? A: To represent many features in a small space and make the map easy to read.. Symbols stand for real features so the map is not crowded.
chunks.source: Symbols stand for real features so the map is not crowded.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: In which direction does the compass needle always rest? A: It always points to the north (rests in the north-south direction).. The compass needle is a magnet that always points north.
chunks.source: The compass needle is a magnet that always points north.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: What problem does a map reader face if the map lacks a key? A: The reader cannot understand what the symbols on the map mean.. The key explains the meaning of symbols.
chunks.source: The key explains the meaning of symbols.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: List down any four groups of people who use a compass. A: Pilots, sailors, soldiers, surveyors.. People who travel or find directions use a compass.
chunks.source: People who travel or find directions use a compass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: What are cardinal points on a compass? A: The four main points: North, South, East and West.. Cardinal points are the four main directions.
chunks.source: Cardinal points are the four main directions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Identify the four major points of a compass. A: North, South, East, West.. These are the cardinal points of a compass.
chunks.source: These are the cardinal points of a compass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: What are the points which lie between cardinal points? A: Semi-cardinal points, for example North East and South West.. They lie between the four main points.
chunks.source: They lie between the four main points.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: List down any three ways of locating places. A: By using a map, by using a compass direction, and by using landmarks.. Places can be found with a map, a compass or known landmarks.
chunks.source: Places can be found with a map, a compass or known landmarks.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: What was the commonest way of finding direction long ago? A: By using the sun (it rises in the east and sets in the west).. Long ago people used the sun to find direction.
chunks.source: Long ago people used the sun to find direction.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the major latitude marked 0 degrees on a map. A: The Equator.. The Equator is the latitude marked 0 degrees.
chunks.source: The Equator is the latitude marked 0 degrees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Why is the Equator marked 0 degrees on the map? A: It is the starting line from which other latitudes are measured north and south.. All other latitudes are measured from the Equator.
chunks.source: All other latitudes are measured from the Equator.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Mention any three ways of locating places on a map. A: By using the key, by using the scale, and by using the compass direction.. The key, scale and compass help us read a map.
chunks.source: The key, scale and compass help us read a map.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Sarah was moving to school in the morning and she saw the sun directly on her face. In which direction was she facing? A: East.. The sun rises in the east in the morning.
chunks.source: The sun rises in the east in the morning.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the country which borders Uganda to the south west. A: Rwanda.. Rwanda borders Uganda to the south west.
chunks.source: Rwanda borders Uganda to the south west.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the district which is found in Lake Victoria. A: Kalangala district.. Kalangala is made of islands in Lake Victoria.
chunks.source: Kalangala is made of islands in Lake Victoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why Kampala city has many people. A: There are many jobs and good social services in the city.. People move to Kampala to look for jobs.
chunks.source: People move to Kampala to look for jobs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: How is Kampala useful to the people of Uganda as a city? A: It is the capital city and the centre of trade, government and transport.. Kampala is the capital city of Uganda.
chunks.source: Kampala is the capital city of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: How many divisions make up Kampala district? A: Five divisions.. Kampala has five divisions.
chunks.source: Kampala has five divisions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Which body is responsible for Kampala district? A: Kampala Capital City Authority (KCCA).. KCCA runs the affairs of Kampala.
chunks.source: KCCA runs the affairs of Kampala.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: What title is given to the political head of Kampala? A: Lord Mayor.. The political head of Kampala is the Lord Mayor.
chunks.source: The political head of Kampala is the Lord Mayor.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Give two reasons why Kampala is divided into divisions. A: For easy administration; to bring services nearer to the people.. Divisions make it easier to govern the city.
chunks.source: Divisions make it easier to govern the city.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: State three factors that have attracted many people to Kampala. A: Many jobs, good schools and hospitals, and better social services.. People move to Kampala for jobs and services.
chunks.source: People move to Kampala for jobs and services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name any four municipalities (divisions) of Kampala. A: Kawempe, Makindye, Rubaga, Nakawa.. Kampala has five divisions; any four are correct.
chunks.source: Kampala has five divisions; any four are correct.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the biggest division of Kampala and the most industrialized division. A: Biggest: Kawempe; most industrialized: Nakawa.. Kawempe is the biggest division and Nakawa has many industries.
chunks.source: Kawempe is the biggest division and Nakawa has many industries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: In which division of Kampala do we find (i) the Police Headquarters (ii) the Kasubi tombs (iii) Parliament (iv) Lake Victoria? A: (i) Nakawa (ii) Rubaga (iii) Central (iv) Makindye.. Police Headquarters is at Naguru in Nakawa; Kasubi tombs are in Rubaga; Parliament is in Central; Lake Victoria touches Makindye at Ggaba.
chunks.source: Police Headquarters is at Naguru in Nakawa; Kasubi tombs are in Rubaga; Parliament is in Central; Lake Victoria touches Makindye at Ggaba.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Identify any three problems facing people who live in Kampala. A: Traffic jams, high cost of living, unemployment.. City life has problems like traffic and high prices.
chunks.source: City life has problems like traffic and high prices.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name two lakes crossed by the Equator in Uganda. A: Lake Victoria and Lake George.. The Equator crosses Lake Victoria and Lake George.
chunks.source: The Equator crosses Lake Victoria and Lake George.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name any two districts which are crossed by the Equator. A: Mpigi and Masaka.. The Equator passes through Mpigi and Masaka districts.
chunks.source: The Equator passes through Mpigi and Masaka districts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: What title is given to (i) the head of a municipality in Kampala (ii) the head of civil servants in Kampala City (iii) the head of KCCA (iv) the political head of a district like Mukono? A: (i) Mayor (ii) Executive Director (iii) Executive Director (iv) District Chairperson (LCV Chairperson).. Municipalities are headed by mayors; KCCA staff are headed by the Executive Director; districts are headed by the LCV Chairperson.
chunks.source: Municipalities are headed by mayors; KCCA staff are headed by the Executive Director; districts are headed by the LCV Chairperson.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name two important places in Kampala. A: Parliament of Uganda and the Uganda Museum.. Kampala has the Parliament and the Uganda Museum.
chunks.source: Kampala has the Parliament and the Uganda Museum.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: State four problems faced by people in Kampala when looking for basic needs. A: High cost of living, unemployment, poor housing, overcrowding.. Getting food, shelter and other needs in the city is hard.
chunks.source: Getting food, shelter and other needs in the city is hard.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name any three small towns found in Kampala. A: Bwaise, Katwe, Ntinda.. Kampala has small towns like Bwaise, Katwe and Ntinda.
chunks.source: Kampala has small towns like Bwaise, Katwe and Ntinda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the drawing of an object as seen from aside? A: A picture.. A picture shows an object as seen from the side.
chunks.source: A picture shows an object as seen from the side.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: In which direction is the sun in the evening? A: In the west.. The sun sets in the west in the evening.
chunks.source: The sun sets in the west in the evening.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a semi-cardinal point on a compass. A: North East.. North East is a semi-cardinal point.
chunks.source: North East is a semi-cardinal point.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Give any one cardinal point of a compass. A: North.. North is a cardinal point.
chunks.source: North is a cardinal point.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Mention the importance of a compass direction. A: It helps us to find direction.. Compass directions show the way.
chunks.source: Compass directions show the way.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Mention the element of a map that helps us to understand it. A: The key.. The key explains the map.
chunks.source: The key explains the map.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the map symbol drawn below: 0 10 km 20 km. A: The scale.. That symbol is the scale of the map.
chunks.source: That symbol is the scale of the map.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: How is a picture similar to a map? A: Both are drawings.. Pictures and maps are both drawings.
chunks.source: Pictures and maps are both drawings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Give one element of a good map. A: A title.. A title is an element of a good map.
chunks.source: A title is an element of a good map.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the capital city of Uganda. A: Kampala.. Kampala is the capital of Uganda.
chunks.source: Kampala is the capital of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are physical features? A: Natural landforms and water bodies on the earth's surface, like hills, mountains, lakes and rivers.. Physical features are natural features of the land.
chunks.source: Physical features are natural features of the land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any four examples of physical features in your district. A: Hills, mountains, lakes, rivers.. Physical features include hills, mountains, lakes and rivers.
chunks.source: Physical features include hills, mountains, lakes and rivers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are there no landslides in Kampala? A: Kampala has no steep mountains; landslides happen on steep mountain slopes.. Landslides occur on steep slopes, which Kampala lacks.
chunks.source: Landslides occur on steep slopes, which Kampala lacks.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State the uses of physical features. A: They are sources of water; they attract tourists; lakes provide fish; they help in rainfall formation.. Physical features give water, fish, tourism and rain.
chunks.source: Physical features give water, fish, tourism and rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two ways how people have misused physical features today. A: Draining swamps; cutting down forests on hills.. Swamp drainage and deforestation misuse physical features.
chunks.source: Swamp drainage and deforestation misuse physical features.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define the following terms: (i) Relief (ii) Plateau (iii) Altitude (iv) Landforms. A: (i) Relief: the ups and downs (height and shape) of the land. (ii) Plateau: a flat raised area of land. (iii) Altitude: the height of a place above sea level. (iv) Landforms: the natural shapes of the land surface, like hills and valleys.. Relief is about height and shape; a plateau is flat raised land; altitude is height above sea level.
chunks.source: Relief is about height and shape; a plateau is flat raised land; altitude is height above sea level.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any three waterfalls along River Nile. A: Murchison Falls, Karuma Falls, Ripon Falls.. Famous Nile waterfalls include Murchison and Karuma.
chunks.source: Famous Nile waterfalls include Murchison and Karuma.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the highest points of these mountains: (i) Mt Rwenzori (ii) Mt Elgon (iii) Mt Mufumbiro. A: (i) Margherita peak (ii) Wagagai peak (iii) Muhavura peak.. Each mountain has a highest peak.
chunks.source: Each mountain has a highest peak.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any four ways of protecting physical features. A: Avoid deforestation; control soil erosion; avoid draining swamps; avoid polluting lakes and rivers.. Protect features by planting trees and keeping water clean.
chunks.source: Protect features by planting trees and keeping water clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any two economic activities carried out on plateau land. A: Crop growing and animal grazing.. Flat plateau land is good for farming and grazing.
chunks.source: Flat plateau land is good for farming and grazing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any two lakes found in Kampala district. A: Lake Victoria and Kabaka's lake.. Kampala has Lake Victoria and the man-made Kabaka's lake.
chunks.source: Kampala has Lake Victoria and the man-made Kabaka's lake.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which man-made lake is found in Kampala? A: Kabaka's lake.. Kabaka's lake was dug by the Kabaka's men.
chunks.source: Kabaka's lake was dug by the Kabaka's men.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two dangers of physical features. A: Floods from lakes and rivers; landslides on steep mountains.. Water bodies flood and steep slopes slide.
chunks.source: Water bodies flood and steep slopes slide.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State two ways of caring for physical features. A: Planting trees on hills; not dumping waste in lakes and rivers.. Plant trees and keep water bodies clean.
chunks.source: Plant trees and keep water bodies clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two problems faced by lakes and rivers. A: Pollution and silting.. Lakes and rivers suffer from pollution and silting.
chunks.source: Lakes and rivers suffer from pollution and silting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two problems faced by people living around lakes and rivers. A: Floods and water-borne diseases.. People near water face floods and diseases.
chunks.source: People near water face floods and diseases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: On which hill in Kampala do we find radio and television masts? A: Kololo hill.. Masts stand on Kololo hill.
chunks.source: Masts stand on Kololo hill.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is the peak of Mt. Rwenzori snow-capped? A: It is very high, so it is very cold at the top.. High altitude means very low temperatures.
chunks.source: High altitude means very low temperatures.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What feature is formed between two or more hills? A: A valley.. Low land between hills is a valley.
chunks.source: Low land between hills is a valley.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State two importance of hills to people. A: They attract tourists; they are good sites for communication masts.. Hills bring tourists and carry masts.
chunks.source: Hills bring tourists and carry masts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two dangers of hills. A: Landslides; difficulty in building roads and transport.. Hills can slide and are hard to travel on.
chunks.source: Hills can slide and are hard to travel on.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can valleys be dangerous to people? A: They flood during heavy rains.. Water collects in valleys and floods them.
chunks.source: Water collects in valleys and floods them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any two hills in Kampala. A: Kololo and Nakasero.. Kampala is built on hills like Kololo and Nakasero.
chunks.source: Kampala is built on hills like Kololo and Nakasero.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are waterfalls important to Ugandans? A: They attract tourists; they are used to generate hydro-electricity.. Waterfalls bring tourists and electricity.
chunks.source: Waterfalls bring tourists and electricity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define the term weather. A: The condition of the atmosphere of a place at a given time.. Weather is the day-to-day state of the air.
chunks.source: Weather is the day-to-day state of the air.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any four types of weather. A: Sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy.. Weather can be sunny, cloudy, rainy or windy.
chunks.source: Weather can be sunny, cloudy, rainy or windy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any three weather makers. A: The sun, wind and clouds.. The sun, wind and clouds make weather.
chunks.source: The sun, wind and clouds make weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down any two weather changes. A: Changes in temperature; changes in rainfall.. Weather changes like hot to cold, dry to wet.
chunks.source: Weather changes like hot to cold, dry to wet.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What term is used to mean the study of weather conditions? A: Meteorology.. Meteorology is the study of weather.
chunks.source: Meteorology is the study of weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do we call people who study and tell us about the weather conditions of a particular place? A: Meteorologists.. Meteorologists study the weather.
chunks.source: Meteorologists study the weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is weather forecasting? A: The telling of the expected weather conditions of a place in advance.. Forecasting tells the coming weather.
chunks.source: Forecasting tells the coming weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of weather forecasting. A: It helps farmers plan their activities and people prepare for bad weather.. Forecasts help farmers and travellers prepare.
chunks.source: Forecasts help farmers and travellers prepare.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which district do we find the biggest meteorological centre? A: Wakiso (at Entebbe).. The biggest weather centre is at Entebbe in Wakiso.
chunks.source: The biggest weather centre is at Entebbe in Wakiso.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is temperature? (b) State the units used to measure temperature. (c) Which instrument is used to measure temperature of an area? (d) Mention any one liquid used in thermometers. A: Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a place. (b) Degrees Celsius. (c) A thermometer. (d) Mercury.. Temperature is hotness or coldness, measured in degrees Celsius with a thermometer using mercury.
chunks.source: Temperature is hotness or coldness, measured in degrees Celsius with a thermometer using mercury.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one advantage of using mercury in thermometers. (b) State two advantages of using alcohol over mercury. A: (a) Mercury expands evenly and does not stick to glass. (b) Alcohol is cheaper and safer than mercury.. Mercury gives true readings; alcohol is cheap and safe.
chunks.source: Mercury gives true readings; alcohol is cheap and safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which instrument is used to measure the amount of sunshine in an area? A: A sunshine recorder.. The sunshine recorder measures sunshine.
chunks.source: The sunshine recorder measures sunshine.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two uses of sunshine. A: Drying harvested crops; giving light and warmth.. Sunshine dries crops and warms us.
chunks.source: Sunshine dries crops and warms us.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify the three types of rainfall. A: Relief (orographic) rainfall, convectional rainfall, cyclonic (frontal) rainfall.. The three types are relief, convectional and cyclonic.
chunks.source: The three types are relief, convectional and cyclonic.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List down any two processes of rain formation. A: Evaporation and condensation.. Water evaporates, then vapour condenses into rain.
chunks.source: Water evaporates, then vapour condenses into rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the instrument used to measure the amount of rainfall received in an area. (b) What is the importance of a rain gauge to a farmer? (c) Why is a rain gauge placed in a flat open place? (d) Why is a rain gauge placed 30cm above the ground? (e) What is the importance of a rain gauge at a weather station? A: (a) A rain gauge. (b) It helps the farmer know the amount of rainfall. (c) To avoid splashes from the ground. (d) To prevent splash water from entering it. (e) To record rainfall for weather study.. A rain gauge measures rain; it is placed in the open, 30cm high, to get true readings.
chunks.source: A rain gauge measures rain; it is placed in the open, 30cm high, to get true readings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is rainfall measured in millimetres? A: Because the amount of rainfall received is usually small.. Rainfall amounts are small, so we use millimetres.
chunks.source: Rainfall amounts are small, so we use millimetres.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why does Kabale receive orographic (relief) rainfall? A: It has hills which force moist wind to rise, cool and form rain.. Hills in Kabale force wind up to make rain.
chunks.source: Hills in Kabale force wind up to make rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What type of rainfall is received in Kalangala and Kampala districts? A: Convectional rainfall.. Areas near Lake Victoria get convectional rainfall.
chunks.source: Areas near Lake Victoria get convectional rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of rainfall received in flat areas. A: Convectional rainfall.. Flat, hot areas get convectional rainfall.
chunks.source: Flat, hot areas get convectional rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define wind. A: Moving air.. Wind is air in motion.
chunks.source: Wind is air in motion.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any three characteristics of wind. A: It has direction, speed and strength.. Wind has direction, speed and strength.
chunks.source: Wind has direction, speed and strength.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Outline any two importance of wind to man. (b) State any two dangers of wind. A: (a) Winnowing crops and drying clothes. (b) It destroys roofs and spreads fires.. Wind helps winnowing but destroys houses.
chunks.source: Wind helps winnowing but destroys houses.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the instrument which (i) shows the direction of wind (ii) measures the speed of wind (iii) shows the strength of wind. A: (i) Wind vane (ii) Anemometer (iii) Wind sock.. Wind vane for direction, anemometer for speed, wind sock for strength.
chunks.source: Wind vane for direction, anemometer for speed, wind sock for strength.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any four types of clouds. (b) How are nimbus clouds useful to farmers? A: Cirrus, cumulus, stratus, nimbus. Nimbus clouds bring rain for crops.. Cloud types include cirrus and nimbus; nimbus brings rain.
chunks.source: Cloud types include cirrus and nimbus; nimbus brings rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name (i) the nearest clouds (ii) the highest clouds. A: (i) Stratus (ii) Cirrus.. Stratus clouds are lowest; cirrus are highest.
chunks.source: Stratus clouds are lowest; cirrus are highest.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two uses of clouds to man. A: They bring rain; they give shade from the sun.. Clouds give rain and shade.
chunks.source: Clouds give rain and shade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State two dangers of clouds to man. A: Heavy clouds cause floods; they bring lightning.. Clouds can cause floods and lightning.
chunks.source: Clouds can cause floods and lightning.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is a Stevenson screen painted white? A: To reflect heat.. White paint reflects heat away.
chunks.source: White paint reflects heat away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any two instruments kept in a Stevenson screen. A: Maximum and minimum thermometers.. The screen holds the maximum and minimum thermometers.
chunks.source: The screen holds the maximum and minimum thermometers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the use of louvers on a Stevenson screen? A: To allow free circulation of air.. Louvers let air flow through the screen.
chunks.source: Louvers let air flow through the screen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Apart from weather instruments, which other item is kept in a Stevenson screen? A: Nothing else; only weather instruments are kept in it.. A Stevenson screen holds only weather instruments.
chunks.source: A Stevenson screen holds only weather instruments.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is a Stevenson screen built with wood? A: Wood is a bad conductor of heat.. Wood does not pass heat easily.
chunks.source: Wood does not pass heat easily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a Stevenson screen? A: A wooden box in which delicate weather instruments are kept.. It is a wooden box for weather instruments.
chunks.source: It is a wooden box for weather instruments.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a weather station? A: A place where weather is studied and recorded.. Weather stations study and record weather.
chunks.source: Weather stations study and record weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is a clinical thermometer not kept in a Stevenson screen? A: It measures the temperature of the human body, not the air.. A clinical thermometer is for body temperature.
chunks.source: A clinical thermometer is for body temperature.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why a rain gauge is not kept in a Stevenson screen. A: It must be in an open place to collect rain.. A rain gauge needs open sky to catch rain.
chunks.source: A rain gauge needs open sky to catch rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the instrument which (i) shows the amount of water vapour in the atmosphere (ii) shows the pressure of air (iii) shows the sunshine received in a day. A: (i) Hygrometer (ii) Barometer (iii) Sunshine recorder.. Hygrometer for vapour, barometer for pressure, sunshine recorder for sunshine.
chunks.source: Hygrometer for vapour, barometer for pressure, sunshine recorder for sunshine.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two dangers of rain. (b) State any two importance of rain. A: (a) Floods and destruction of crops. (b) It helps crops grow and fills water sources.. Rain can flood but also waters crops.
chunks.source: Rain can flood but also waters crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is it dangerous to settle in swamps? A: Swamps flood and harbour disease-carrying mosquitoes.. Swamps flood and breed mosquitoes.
chunks.source: Swamps flood and breed mosquitoes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way soil erosion is controlled in our school compound. A: By planting grass.. Planted grass holds the soil.
chunks.source: Planted grass holds the soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are nimbus clouds important to farmers? A: They bring rain for crops.. Nimbus clouds bring the rain farmers need.
chunks.source: Nimbus clouds bring the rain farmers need.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is Lake Victoria important to the people of Kampala and Wakiso? A: It is a source of water and fish.. The lake gives water and fish.
chunks.source: The lake gives water and fish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which landform is good for constructing roads? A: Plains (flat land).. Flat land is best for roads.
chunks.source: Flat land is best for roads.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one way of managing rainy weather. A: Using an umbrella.. Umbrellas protect us in rain.
chunks.source: Umbrellas protect us in rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does drought cause shortage of food in a community? A: Crops dry up and animals die.. Drought kills crops and animals.
chunks.source: Drought kills crops and animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which element of weather is responsible for the water increase in Lake Victoria? A: Rainfall.. Rainfall raises the lake's water.
chunks.source: Rainfall raises the lake's water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can we protect ourselves from sunny weather? A: By wearing a hat or staying in the shade.. Hats and shade protect from sun.
chunks.source: Hats and shade protect from sun.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one danger of living near Lake Victoria. A: Floods.. Lake areas flood.
chunks.source: Lake areas flood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are donkeys useful to people in mountainous areas? A: They carry loads.. Donkeys carry loads in mountains.
chunks.source: Donkeys carry loads in mountains.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one type of rainfall received in Uganda. A: Convectional rainfall.. Uganda receives convectional rainfall.
chunks.source: Uganda receives convectional rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is Lake Victoria important to people? A: It is a source of fish and water.. The lake gives fish and water.
chunks.source: The lake gives fish and water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do school children manage rainy weather? A: By using umbrellas and raincoats.. Umbrellas and raincoats manage rain.
chunks.source: Umbrellas and raincoats manage rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is a rain gauge important at a weather station? A: It measures the amount of rainfall.. A rain gauge measures rain.
chunks.source: A rain gauge measures rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the building material got from hills. A: Stones.. Stones come from hills.
chunks.source: Stones come from hills.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is Lake Victoria helpful to the people in our district? A: It provides fish and water.. The lake gives fish and water.
chunks.source: The lake gives fish and water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What problem do people living in hilly areas face? A: Poor transport and landslides.. Hills make transport hard and slide.
chunks.source: Hills make transport hard and slide.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are nimbus clouds useful to farmers? A: They bring rain for crops.. Nimbus clouds bring rain.
chunks.source: Nimbus clouds bring rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one physical feature in your district or division. A: A hill.. Hills are physical features.
chunks.source: Hills are physical features.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one danger caused by too much rainfall. A: Floods.. Too much rain causes floods.
chunks.source: Too much rain causes floods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which physical feature covers the largest part of your district? A: Plains (flat land).. Flat plains cover most of the district.
chunks.source: Flat plains cover most of the district.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) Name any one type of rainfall. b) Which weather instrument is used to measure rainfall? c) Why is the instrument named above placed in an open flat area? d) How is rainfall useful in our homes? A: a) Convectional rainfall. b) A rain gauge. c) To collect the true amount of rainfall. d) It gives water for domestic use.. A rain gauge measures rain in the open; rain gives home water.
chunks.source: A rain gauge measures rain in the open; rain gives home water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) What name is given to the natural landforms of an area? b) How are rivers important to people? c) Give any one way in which people can care for rivers. A: a) Physical features. b) They provide fish and water. c) By not dumping waste in them.. Landforms are physical features; rivers give fish and water.
chunks.source: Landforms are physical features; rivers give fish and water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) What are physical features? b) Give any two physical features found in our district. c) How is soil erosion controlled in mountain areas? A: a) Natural landforms and water bodies. b) Hills; lakes. c) By terracing.. Physical features are natural; terracing stops erosion on mountains.
chunks.source: Physical features are natural; terracing stops erosion on mountains.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) Name the weather condition which is managed by using an umbrella. b) Mention two elements of weather. c) Why is it important to have a weather station in a school? A: a) Rainy weather. b) Rainfall and temperature. c) To study the weather.. Umbrellas manage rain; weather stations study weather.
chunks.source: Umbrellas manage rain; weather stations study weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) What are physical features? b) Give any two importance of physical features. c) State any one way of caring for physical features. A: a) Natural landforms and water bodies on the earth's surface. b) They provide water; they attract tourists. c) By planting trees.. Physical features give water and tourism; plant trees to care for them.
chunks.source: Physical features give water and tourism; plant trees to care for them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is vegetation? A: The plant cover of an area.. Vegetation is the plants covering an area.
chunks.source: Vegetation is the plants covering an area.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List down the two types of vegetation. A: Natural vegetation and planted vegetation.. Vegetation is either natural or planted.
chunks.source: Vegetation is either natural or planted.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is natural vegetation different from planted vegetation? A: Natural vegetation grows on its own, while planted vegetation is grown by man.. Natural grows alone; planted is grown by people.
chunks.source: Natural grows alone; planted is grown by people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Outline any four examples of natural vegetation in Uganda. A: Forests, swamps, grasslands, bushes.. Natural vegetation includes forests, swamps and grasslands.
chunks.source: Natural vegetation includes forests, swamps and grasslands.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two uses of vegetation to man. A: Source of timber; grazing for animals.. Vegetation gives timber and grass for animals.
chunks.source: Vegetation gives timber and grass for animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down two human activities that negatively affect vegetation and two that positively affect it. A: Negative: deforestation, bush burning. Positive: afforestation, agro-forestry.. Cutting and burning harm vegetation; planting trees helps it.
chunks.source: Cutting and burning harm vegetation; planting trees helps it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State two ways how people care for vegetation. A: Planting trees; avoiding bush burning.. Plant trees and do not burn bushes.
chunks.source: Plant trees and do not burn bushes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What type of wood is got from planted forests? A: Soft wood.. Planted forests give soft wood.
chunks.source: Planted forests give soft wood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of trees that provide hard wood timber. A: Mvule and mahogany.. Mvule and mahogany give hard wood.
chunks.source: Mvule and mahogany give hard wood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of soft wood trees. A: Pine and cypress.. Pine and cypress are soft wood trees.
chunks.source: Pine and cypress are soft wood trees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any three ways of protecting forests. A: Afforestation; avoiding bush burning; making by-laws against deforestation.. Protect forests by planting trees and stopping fires.
chunks.source: Protect forests by planting trees and stopping fires.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any three problems facing wetlands. A: Drainage of swamps; pollution; over-harvesting of papyrus.. Wetlands suffer from drainage and pollution.
chunks.source: Wetlands suffer from drainage and pollution.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two reasons why man cuts down trees. A: To get timber; to get firewood and charcoal; to clear land for farming.. Trees are cut for timber, fuel and farmland.
chunks.source: Trees are cut for timber, fuel and farmland.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which district is Mabira natural forest? A: Buikwe district.. Mabira forest is in Buikwe district.
chunks.source: Mabira forest is in Buikwe district.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any three importance of forests to man. A: Source of timber; they attract rainfall; home of wild animals.. Forests give timber, rain and homes for animals.
chunks.source: Forests give timber, rain and homes for animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List down any three examples of natural forests. A: Mabira, Budongo, Kibale.. Uganda's natural forests include Mabira and Budongo.
chunks.source: Uganda's natural forests include Mabira and Budongo.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List down any three examples of planted forests. A: Lendu, Nyabyeya, Mafuga.. Planted forests include Lendu and Nyabyeya.
chunks.source: Planted forests include Lendu and Nyabyeya.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a swamp? A: A waterlogged area with vegetation.. A swamp is a wet area with plants.
chunks.source: A swamp is a wet area with plants.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the most swampy lake in Uganda. A: Lake Kyoga.. Lake Kyoga is the most swampy lake.
chunks.source: Lake Kyoga is the most swampy lake.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is Lake Kyoga swampy? A: It is shallow.. Kyoga is shallow, so swamps grow in it.
chunks.source: Kyoga is shallow, so swamps grow in it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is Lake Kyoga shallow? A: Silt has filled it up over time.. Deposits of silt have made Kyoga shallow.
chunks.source: Deposits of silt have made Kyoga shallow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two values of swamps to people. A: Source of raw materials like papyrus and clay; fishing.. Swamps give papyrus, clay and fish.
chunks.source: Swamps give papyrus, clay and fish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the commonest fish caught from most swamps. A: Mudfish.. Mudfish is common in swamps.
chunks.source: Mudfish is common in swamps.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two dangers of swamps. A: They harbour mosquitoes that spread malaria; they flood.. Swamps breed mosquitoes and flood.
chunks.source: Swamps breed mosquitoes and flood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which type of vegetation covers the largest part of Uganda? A: Savannah grassland.. Savannah grassland covers most of Uganda.
chunks.source: Savannah grassland covers most of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention three uses of swamps to people. A: Fishing; source of clay and papyrus; water for animals.. Swamps give fish, clay, papyrus and water.
chunks.source: Swamps give fish, clay, papyrus and water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two ways we can care for swamps in our district. A: Avoid draining them; avoid dumping waste in them.. Do not drain swamps or dump waste in them.
chunks.source: Do not drain swamps or dump waste in them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one swamp you know. A: Lubigi swamp.. Lubigi is a well-known swamp near Kampala.
chunks.source: Lubigi is a well-known swamp near Kampala.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a forest? A: A large area covered with trees.. A forest is a large area of trees.
chunks.source: A forest is a large area of trees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the two types of forests you know. A: Natural forests and planted forests.. Forests are natural or planted.
chunks.source: Forests are natural or planted.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State the type of wood got from (i) natural forests (ii) planted forests. A: (i) Hard wood (ii) Soft wood.. Natural forests give hard wood; planted forests give soft wood.
chunks.source: Natural forests give hard wood; planted forests give soft wood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List two tree species planted in forests. A: Pine and eucalyptus.. Pine and eucalyptus are planted in forests.
chunks.source: Pine and eucalyptus are planted in forests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give three products got from soft wood. A: Paper; furniture; poles.. Soft wood is used for paper, furniture and poles.
chunks.source: Soft wood is used for paper, furniture and poles.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define the following terms: (i) Deforestation (ii) Afforestation (iii) Re-afforestation (iv) Agro-forestry (v) Environmental degradation. A: (i) Deforestation: cutting down trees without replacing them. (ii) Afforestation: planting trees where there were none. (iii) Re-afforestation: replanting trees where they were cut. (iv) Agro-forestry: growing trees alongside crops. (v) Environmental degradation: the destruction of the natural environment.. Deforestation is cutting; afforestation is planting; agro-forestry mixes trees and crops.
chunks.source: Deforestation is cutting; afforestation is planting; agro-forestry mixes trees and crops.

chunks.subject: Social
