chunks.text: Q: Give two uses of grasslands to man. A: Grazing for animals; thatching houses.. Grasslands give pasture and thatch.
chunks.source: Grasslands give pasture and thatch.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give four uses of vegetation. A: Source of food; source of timber; grazing for animals; medicine.. Vegetation gives food, timber, pasture and medicine.
chunks.source: Vegetation gives food, timber, pasture and medicine.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the body responsible for protection of the environment. A: NEMA (National Environment Management Authority).. NEMA protects the environment in Uganda.
chunks.source: NEMA protects the environment in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List four factors affecting vegetation in your district. A: Rainfall, soil type, human activities, temperature.. Rain, soil, people and temperature affect vegetation.
chunks.source: Rain, soil, people and temperature affect vegetation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the two types of crops. A: Food crops and cash crops.. Crops are grown for food or for sale.
chunks.source: Crops are grown for food or for sale.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are cash crops? A: Crops grown mainly for sale.. Cash crops are grown to be sold.
chunks.source: Cash crops are grown to be sold.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the two types of cash crops. A: Traditional cash crops and non-traditional cash crops.. Cash crops are traditional or non-traditional.
chunks.source: Cash crops are traditional or non-traditional.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give four examples of cash crops. A: Coffee, cotton, tea, tobacco.. Coffee, cotton, tea and tobacco are cash crops.
chunks.source: Coffee, cotton, tea and tobacco are cash crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are traditional cash crops? A: Cash crops that have been grown for a long time, like coffee and cotton.. Traditional cash crops like coffee were grown long ago.
chunks.source: Traditional cash crops like coffee were grown long ago.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of non-traditional cash crops. A: Flowers and vanilla.. Flowers and vanilla are non-traditional cash crops.
chunks.source: Flowers and vanilla are non-traditional cash crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match each crop to its product: (i) Coffee (ii) Tea (iii) Tobacco (iv) Cotton (v) Cocoa (vi) Pyrethrum (vii) Simsim (viii) Palm oil. A: Coffee: coffee powder for drinks; Tea: tea leaves for drinks; Tobacco: cigarettes; Cotton: clothes; Cocoa: chocolate; Pyrethrum: insecticides; Simsim: cooking oil; Palm oil: cooking oil and soap. Coffee gives drinks, tobacco gives cigarettes, cotton gives clothes, cocoa gives chocolate.
chunks.source: Coffee gives drinks, tobacco gives cigarettes, cotton gives clothes, cocoa gives chocolate.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are natural resources? A: Things found in nature that people use, like land, water and forests.. Natural resources are useful things from nature.
chunks.source: Natural resources are useful things from nature.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one natural resource in your district. A: Land.. Land is a natural resource.
chunks.source: Land is a natural resource.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are renewable resources? A: Resources that can be replaced naturally, like trees and water.. Renewable resources grow back or return.
chunks.source: Renewable resources grow back or return.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one renewable resource. A: Trees.. Trees grow back, so they are renewable.
chunks.source: Trees grow back, so they are renewable.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify one way in which land is used in your district. A: Farming.. Land is used for farming.
chunks.source: Land is used for farming.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can swamps be helpful to builders? A: They provide clay for making bricks.. Builders get clay for bricks from swamps.
chunks.source: Builders get clay for bricks from swamps.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down one common crop that grows well in swampy areas. A: Rice.. Rice grows well in swampy areas.
chunks.source: Rice grows well in swampy areas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do people in your district misuse natural resources? A: Deforestation; overfishing; polluting water sources.. People misuse resources by cutting trees and polluting water.
chunks.source: People misuse resources by cutting trees and polluting water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one way a farmer can maintain soil fertility in a hilly area. A: Terracing.. Terracing stops soil from washing away on hills.
chunks.source: Terracing stops soil from washing away on hills.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why people should be encouraged to carry out afforestation. A: To get more timber and firewood, and to attract rainfall.. Planting trees gives wood and brings rain.
chunks.source: Planting trees gives wood and brings rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one example of a craft object. A: A basket.. Baskets are craft objects.
chunks.source: Baskets are craft objects.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do farmers harvest crops in dry season? A: So that the crops do not rot in the rain.. Dry season keeps harvested crops from rotting.
chunks.source: Dry season keeps harvested crops from rotting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is clay useful in our community? A: It is used for making pots and bricks.. Clay makes pots and bricks.
chunks.source: Clay makes pots and bricks.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why should we plant trees in our school compound? A: For shade and fresh air.. Trees give shade and fresh air.
chunks.source: Trees give shade and fresh air.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do farmers plant crops in the wet season? A: To get enough water for the crops.. Wet season gives crops water.
chunks.source: Wet season gives crops water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we call a waterlogged area with vegetation? A: A swamp.. A swamp is waterlogged with plants.
chunks.source: A swamp is waterlogged with plants.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which domestic animals are kept for meat only? A: Pigs.. Pigs are kept mainly for meat.
chunks.source: Pigs are kept mainly for meat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger of draining swampy areas. A: It destroys water sources.. Draining swamps destroys water.
chunks.source: Draining swamps destroys water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write NFA in full. A: National Forestry Authority.. NFA is the National Forestry Authority.
chunks.source: NFA is the National Forestry Authority.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Crops grown mainly for sale are known as what? A: Crops grown mainly for sale.. Cash crops are grown to be sold.
chunks.source: Cash crops are grown to be sold.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which building material is got from swamps? A: Clay.. Clay comes from swamps.
chunks.source: Clay comes from swamps.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are swamps useful to people in our district? A: They provide clay, papyrus and fish.. Swamps give clay, papyrus and fish.
chunks.source: Swamps give clay, papyrus and fish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need trees and grass planted in our school compound? A: For shade and beauty.. Trees and grass give shade and beauty.
chunks.source: Trees and grass give shade and beauty.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What term is used to mean the plant cover of an area that is grown by man? A: Planted vegetation.. Man-grown plant cover is planted vegetation.
chunks.source: Man-grown plant cover is planted vegetation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write NEMA in full. A: National Environment Management Authority.. NEMA protects the environment.
chunks.source: NEMA protects the environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way people in our district have destroyed the environment. A: Deforestation.. Cutting trees destroys the environment.
chunks.source: Cutting trees destroys the environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people carry out deforestation? A: To get timber, firewood and farmland.. People cut trees for wood and land.
chunks.source: People cut trees for wood and land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people keep domestic animals? A: For milk, meat and eggs.. Animals give milk, meat and eggs.
chunks.source: Animals give milk, meat and eggs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why people grow crops. A: To get food.. Crops give food.
chunks.source: Crops give food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) In which two ways is vegetation important to people? b) Give one use of vegetation to farmers. c) State any one danger of vegetation. A: a) Source of timber; it attracts rainfall. b) Grazing for animals. c) It harbours dangerous animals like snakes.. Vegetation gives timber and rain; it feeds animals but hides snakes.
chunks.source: Vegetation gives timber and rain; it feeds animals but hides snakes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) State any one example of vegetation that gives people food. b) Why do we need trees in our school compound? c) How do we care for the vegetation in our school compound? A: a) Banana plants. b) For shade. c) By watering them.. Food plants feed us; trees give shade; water them.
chunks.source: Food plants feed us; trees give shade; water them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) Mention any one place where wild animals are kept. b) Give any two uses of wild animals. c) How are wild animals dangerous to people? A: a) A game park. b) They attract tourists; for education. c) They attack people.. Game parks keep wild animals; they bring tourists but can attack.
chunks.source: Game parks keep wild animals; they bring tourists but can attack.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) What are cash crops? b) Give any two examples of cash crops grown by the people in our district. c) Why do people grow cash crops? A: a) Crops grown mainly for sale. b) Coffee; cotton. c) To earn money.. Cash crops are sold to earn money.
chunks.source: Cash crops are sold to earn money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define the following terms: (i) Ethnic group (ii) Tribe (iii) Clan (iv) Kingdom (v) Lineage (vi) Family (vii) Totem. A: (i) Ethnic group: a large group of tribes with related languages and origin. (ii) Tribe: a group of people with the same language, culture and origin. (iii) Clan: a group of families with a common ancestor. (iv) Kingdom: a large traditional area ruled by a king. (v) Lineage: a line of descendants from a common ancestor. (vi) Family: people related by blood or marriage. (vii) Totem: an animal or object respected as a clan symbol.. Ethnic group is biggest; tribe shares language; clan shares an ancestor; totem is a clan symbol.
chunks.source: Ethnic group is biggest; tribe shares language; clan shares an ancestor; totem is a clan symbol.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down the four ethnic groups of Uganda. A: Bantu, Nilotics, Nilo-Hamites, Hamites.. Uganda has four main ethnic groups.
chunks.source: Uganda has four main ethnic groups.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give four reasons why ethnic groups migrated from their homelands. A: Search for fertile land; search for water and pasture; wars; drought and famine.. They moved looking for land, water and peace.
chunks.source: They moved looking for land, water and peace.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the cradle land of these groups: (i) Bantu (ii) Nilotics (iii) Nilo-Hamites (iv) Hamites. A: (i) Cameroon highlands (ii) Bahr-el-Ghazal in South Sudan (iii) Ethiopian highlands (iv) Ethiopia.. Each group has a cradle land where it came from.
chunks.source: Each group has a cradle land where it came from.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two tribes under (i) Bantu (ii) Nilotics (iii) Nilo-Hamites (iv) Hamites. A: (i) Baganda, Basoga (ii) Acholi, Langi (iii) Iteso, Karamojong (iv) Bahima, Batutsi.. Baganda are Bantu; Acholi are Nilotics; Iteso are Nilo-Hamites; Bahima are Hamites.
chunks.source: Baganda are Bantu; Acholi are Nilotics; Iteso are Nilo-Hamites; Bahima are Hamites.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two effects of ethnic migrations. A: Intermarriage between tribes; spread of new languages and crops.. Migration mixed tribes and spread new things.
chunks.source: Migration mixed tribes and spread new things.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Outline any four problems faced by ethnic groups on their way to Uganda. A: Attacks by wild animals; hunger; diseases; hostile tribes.. The journey was hard: animals, hunger, disease, enemies.
chunks.source: The journey was hard: animals, hunger, disease, enemies.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the language spoken by the following tribes: (i) Bagisu (ii) Iteso (iii) Bakiga (iv) Acholi (v) Karamojong (vi) Baganda. A: (i) Lugisu (ii) Ateso (iii) Rukiga (iv) Acholi (v) Ngakarimojong (vi) Luganda.. Each tribe speaks its own language.
chunks.source: Each tribe speaks its own language.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are the Baganda and Bagisu related? A: They are both Bantu.. Both belong to the Bantu ethnic group.
chunks.source: Both belong to the Bantu ethnic group.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the titles given to the cultural leaders of (i) Acholi (ii) Iteso (iii) Tooro (iv) Basoga. A: (i) Rwot (ii) Emorimor (iii) Omukama (iv) Kyabazinga.. Acholi have the Rwot; Tooro have the Omukama; Basoga have the Kyabazinga.
chunks.source: Acholi have the Rwot; Tooro have the Omukama; Basoga have the Kyabazinga.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give three symbols of a clan. A: Totem, clan name, and clan taboos.. Clans have totems, names and taboos.
chunks.source: Clans have totems, names and taboos.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a legend? A: A traditional story of long ago that may not be true.. Legends are old traditional stories.
chunks.source: Legends are old traditional stories.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two legends told by the Bantu. A: Kintu and Nambi; the bead and the spear.. Famous Bantu legends are Kintu and the bead and spear.
chunks.source: Famous Bantu legends are Kintu and the bead and spear.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What lesson do we learn from the story of the bead and the spear? A: We should avoid greed and live peacefully with others.. The story teaches against greed.
chunks.source: The story teaches against greed.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the brother of Nambi who was kind. A: Kayikuzi.. Kayikuzi, Nambi's brother, was kind to Kintu.
chunks.source: Kayikuzi, Nambi's brother, was kind to Kintu.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does the name (i) Walumbe mean (ii) Kayikuzi mean? A: (i) Death (ii) The digger.. Walumbe means death; Kayikuzi means the digger.
chunks.source: Walumbe means death; Kayikuzi means the digger.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define the following terms: (i) Migration (ii) Rural-urban migration (iii) Urban-rural migration. A: (i) Migration: the movement of people from one place to another to settle. (ii) Rural-urban migration: movement of people from villages to towns. (iii) Urban-rural migration: movement of people from towns to villages.. Migration is moving to settle; rural-urban is village to town.
chunks.source: Migration is moving to settle; rural-urban is village to town.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two causes of rural-urban migration. A: Search for jobs; better social services in towns.. People move to towns for jobs and services.
chunks.source: People move to towns for jobs and services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List four problems faced by people in towns. A: Overcrowding; slums; unemployment; high cost of living.. Towns have crowds, slums and high prices.
chunks.source: Towns have crowds, slums and high prices.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a slum? A: A crowded poor area with poor houses in a town.. Slums are poor crowded parts of towns.
chunks.source: Slums are poor crowded parts of towns.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two dangers of slums. A: Diseases; crime.. Slums spread disease and crime.
chunks.source: Slums spread disease and crime.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What should the government do to encourage rural-urban migration? A: Provide more jobs and better services in towns.. Jobs and services pull people to towns.
chunks.source: Jobs and services pull people to towns.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two types of family. A: Nuclear family and extended family.. Families are nuclear or extended.
chunks.source: Families are nuclear or extended.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a nuclear family? A: A small family of father, mother and their children.. A nuclear family has parents and their children.
chunks.source: A nuclear family has parents and their children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List two advantages of a nuclear family. A: It is easy to provide basic needs; there are fewer quarrels.. Small families are easy to feed and keep peaceful.
chunks.source: Small families are easy to feed and keep peaceful.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two disadvantages of an extended family. A: It is hard to feed many people; there are quarrels over property.. Big families are hard to feed and quarrel over property.
chunks.source: Big families are hard to feed and quarrel over property.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who heads a family? A: The father.. The father heads the family.
chunks.source: The father heads the family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the duty of a head of a family? (give two) A: Providing basic needs; protecting the family.. The head provides needs and protects the family.
chunks.source: The head provides needs and protects the family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two duties of children at home. A: Helping with housework; respecting parents.. Children help at home and respect parents.
chunks.source: Children help at home and respect parents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is population? A: The number of people living in an area.. Population is the number of people in an area.
chunks.source: Population is the number of people in an area.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is population distribution? A: The way people are spread in an area.. Distribution shows how people are spread.
chunks.source: Distribution shows how people are spread.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any four causes of population growth. A: High birth rate; low death rate; immigration; early marriages.. More births and fewer deaths grow population.
chunks.source: More births and fewer deaths grow population.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is population growth? A: The increase in the number of people in an area.. Population growth is increase in numbers.
chunks.source: Population growth is increase in numbers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any three causes of population growth. A: High birth rate; immigration; better medical care.. Births, immigration and good health care grow numbers.
chunks.source: Births, immigration and good health care grow numbers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give three dangers of high population. A: Overcrowding; land shortage; unemployment.. Too many people bring crowds and land shortage.
chunks.source: Too many people bring crowds and land shortage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List any three advantages of a high population in an area. A: Large market; enough labour; high tax collection.. Many people give market, labour and taxes.
chunks.source: Many people give market, labour and taxes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is population density? A: The number of people per square kilometre.. Density is people per square kilometre.
chunks.source: Density is people per square kilometre.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two advantages of low population in an area. A: Enough land; less competition for services.. Few people means enough land and services.
chunks.source: Few people means enough land and services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List any two disadvantages of a low population in an area. A: Shortage of labour; small market.. Few people means little labour and market.
chunks.source: Few people means little labour and market.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is over population? A: When the number of people is more than the resources can support.. Over population means too many people for the resources.
chunks.source: Over population means too many people for the resources.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Suggest any three ways of checking population growth in an area. A: Family planning; educating girls; discouraging early marriages.. Family planning and education slow growth.
chunks.source: Family planning and education slow growth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List any four natural hazards that can lead to population decrease in an area. A: Drought, floods, earthquakes, landslides.. Drought, floods and quakes kill people.
chunks.source: Drought, floods and quakes kill people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is population census? A: The official counting of people in a country.. A census is the official counting of people.
chunks.source: A census is the official counting of people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any four reasons why the government carries out population census. A: To plan for services; to know the number of people; to plan the budget; to know population growth.. Census helps planning for services and budgets.
chunks.source: Census helps planning for services and budgets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who is an enumerator? A: A person who counts people during a census.. Enumerators count people in a census.
chunks.source: Enumerators count people in a census.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List any four items collected by enumerators during population census. A: Name, age, sex, tribe.. Enumerators record name, age, sex and tribe.
chunks.source: Enumerators record name, age, sex and tribe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why does the government carry out population census after every ten years? A: To update population records and know the current population.. Census every ten years keeps records up to date.
chunks.source: Census every ten years keeps records up to date.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define population structure. A: The composition of the population by age and sex.. Structure shows ages and sexes of the people.
chunks.source: Structure shows ages and sexes of the people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List any four problems faced by enumerators during population census. A: Bad weather; uncooperative people; hard-to-reach areas; insecurity.. Enumerators face weather, rude people and bad roads.
chunks.source: Enumerators face weather, rude people and bad roads.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to a home and its surroundings? A: A homestead.. A home with its surroundings is a homestead.
chunks.source: A home with its surroundings is a homestead.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one role of a family head. A: Providing basic needs for the family.. The head provides for the family.
chunks.source: The head provides for the family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why most people in towns do not keep cows. A: There is not enough land and space.. Towns lack space for cows.
chunks.source: Towns lack space for cows.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one cultural practice in your district. A: Circumcision.. Circumcision is a cultural practice.
chunks.source: Circumcision is a cultural practice.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write any one cultural practice in your district. A: Circumcision.. Circumcision is a cultural practice.
chunks.source: Circumcision is a cultural practice.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any one member of an extended family. A: An uncle.. An uncle is in the extended family.
chunks.source: An uncle is in the extended family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why some areas have more people than others. A: Better jobs and services.. Jobs and services attract people.
chunks.source: Jobs and services attract people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What lesson do we learn from the story of Walumbe and Nambi? A: We should obey instructions; disobedience brings suffering.. The story teaches obedience.
chunks.source: The story teaches obedience.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What term is used to mean a home and its surroundings? A: A homestead.. A home and surroundings is a homestead.
chunks.source: A home and surroundings is a homestead.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the tribe in our district that practises circumcision. A: The Bagisu.. The Bagisu practise circumcision.
chunks.source: The Bagisu practise circumcision.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did a bee help Kintu? A: It guided him on his journey.. A bee showed Kintu the way.
chunks.source: A bee showed Kintu the way.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What lesson do we learn from the story of Kintu and Nambi? A: Hard work pays.. Kintu's story teaches hard work.
chunks.source: Kintu's story teaches hard work.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a homestead? A: A home and its surroundings.. A homestead is a home with its surroundings.
chunks.source: A homestead is a home with its surroundings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How was a bee helpful to Kintu? A: It guided him on his journey.. A bee showed Kintu the way.
chunks.source: A bee showed Kintu the way.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people fence their homes? A: For security.. Fences protect homes.
chunks.source: Fences protect homes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way customs are important to the people in our district. A: They unite people and preserve culture.. Customs unite and keep culture.
chunks.source: Customs unite and keep culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one responsibility of a child in a home. A: Respecting parents and helping at home.. Children respect and help.
chunks.source: Children respect and help.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one duty of the head of a family. A: Providing basic needs for the family.. The head provides needs.
chunks.source: The head provides needs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) What do we call a group of people related by blood or marriage? b) Mention any one member of an extended family. c) Write two problems families face when getting their needs. A: a) A family. b) An uncle. c) Poverty; unemployment.. A family is blood or marriage relations; they face poverty and joblessness.
chunks.source: A family is blood or marriage relations; they face poverty and joblessness.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) What name is given to the stories of long ago? b) Give two examples of the stories of long ago. c) What do we learn from the stories of long ago? A: a) Legends. b) Kintu and Nambi; the bead and the spear. c) Our culture and history.. Legends are old stories that teach culture.
chunks.source: Legends are old stories that teach culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) Give the meaning of migration. b) Give two reasons why people migrate from rural areas to urban areas. c) How can rural-urban migration lead to food shortage? A: a) The movement of people from one place to another to settle. b) Search for jobs; better services in towns. c) Few people are left to farm.. Migration is moving to settle; towns pull people, leaving farms empty.
chunks.source: Migration is moving to settle; towns pull people, leaving farms empty.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) What are legends? b) Give any two examples of legends. c) How are legends important to people? A: a) Traditional stories of long ago. b) Kintu and Nambi; the bead and the spear. c) They teach our culture.. Legends are old stories that teach culture.
chunks.source: Legends are old stories that teach culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) Give two reasons why towns have more people than villages. b) State two problems faced by people who live in towns. A: a) More jobs; better services. b) Overcrowding; slums.. Towns have jobs and services but also crowds and slums.
chunks.source: Towns have jobs and services but also crowds and slums.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) Name one member of a nuclear family. b) State one problem faced by families today. c) Write down any one role of the parents in a family. d) Give one advantage of living in a nuclear family. A: a) Mother. b) Poverty. c) Providing basic needs. d) It is easy to provide basic needs.. A nuclear family is father, mother and children; it is easy to provide for.
chunks.source: A nuclear family is father, mother and children; it is easy to provide for.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: a) Name one type of a house. b) Why do people build houses? c) Give two materials used for building a house. A: a) A grass-thatched house. b) For shelter. c) Bricks and iron sheets.. Houses give shelter; they are built with bricks and iron sheets.
chunks.source: Houses give shelter; they are built with bricks and iron sheets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the official responsible for payment of civil servants in the district. A: The Chief Administrative Officer (CAO).. The CAO pays civil servants in the district.
chunks.source: The CAO pays civil servants in the district.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How many members make up the Local Council committee? A: Nine members.. An LC committee has nine members.
chunks.source: An LC committee has nine members.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the executive committee of the L.C responsible for the welfare of children in the district. A: The Vice Chairperson.. The Vice Chairperson looks after children's welfare.
chunks.source: The Vice Chairperson looks after children's welfare.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the title of the person who heads the Local Council V committee. A: District Chairperson (LCV Chairperson).. The LCV committee is headed by the District Chairperson.
chunks.source: The LCV committee is headed by the District Chairperson.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define the term decentralization. A: The sharing of power between the central government and local governments.. Decentralization shares power with local governments.
chunks.source: Decentralization shares power with local governments.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why districts are divided into sub-counties. A: For easy administration.. Sub-counties make governing easier.
chunks.source: Sub-counties make governing easier.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which body is responsible for running all the activities in Kampala? A: Kampala Capital City Authority (KCCA).. KCCA runs Kampala.
chunks.source: KCCA runs Kampala.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the current Lord Mayor of Kampala. A: Erias Lukwago.. The Lord Mayor of Kampala is Erias Lukwago.
chunks.source: The Lord Mayor of Kampala is Erias Lukwago.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Under which Ministry is the Local Council? A: Ministry of Local Government.. Local councils fall under the Ministry of Local Government.
chunks.source: Local councils fall under the Ministry of Local Government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define by-laws. A: Laws made by local councils.. By-laws are local laws.
chunks.source: By-laws are local laws.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the title of the President's representative in Kampala. A: The Minister for Kampala.. The President is represented in Kampala by the Minister for Kampala.
chunks.source: The President is represented in Kampala by the Minister for Kampala.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the body responsible for the activities in the district. A: The District Council (LCV).. The District Council runs district activities.
chunks.source: The District Council runs district activities.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one duty of KCCA. A: Maintaining roads and collecting garbage in Kampala.. KCCA keeps Kampala's roads and garbage.
chunks.source: KCCA keeps Kampala's roads and garbage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do you elect leaders in your school? A: To lead pupils and help keep discipline.. School leaders lead and keep discipline.
chunks.source: School leaders lead and keep discipline.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any one municipality (division) in Kampala. A: Kawempe.. Kawempe is a division of Kampala.
chunks.source: Kawempe is a division of Kampala.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the officials responsible for the following activities in the district: (i) Political head of the district who chairs district meetings (ii) Responsible for all civil servants in the district (iii) Improving the standard of education and heading all schools (iv) Responsible for all medical departments (v) Represents the President in the district (vi) Advises farmers on how to look after their livestock. A: (i) District Chairperson (ii) Chief Administrative Officer (iii) District Education Officer (iv) District Health Officer (v) Resident District Commissioner (vi) District Veterinary Officer.. District leaders: Chairperson, CAO, DEO, DHO, RDC, DVO.
chunks.source: District leaders: Chairperson, CAO, DEO, DHO, RDC, DVO.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write these abbreviations in full: (i) D.P.C (ii) D.F.O (iii) D.A.O. A: (i) District Police Commander (ii) District Fisheries Officer (iii) District Agricultural Officer.. DPC is police, DFO is fisheries, DAO is agriculture.
chunks.source: DPC is police, DFO is fisheries, DAO is agriculture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State the duty of the District Planner in your district. A: Planning the development projects of the district.. The planner plans district development.
chunks.source: The planner plans district development.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one role played by the Local Council 1 committee. A: Keeping law and order in the village.. LC1 keeps law and order.
chunks.source: LC1 keeps law and order.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is the L.C.I Vice Chairperson useful to children in your community? A: He protects the welfare and rights of children.. The Vice Chairperson looks after children.
chunks.source: The Vice Chairperson looks after children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are religious leaders important in our community? A: They guide people morally and preach peace.. Religious leaders guide and unite people.
chunks.source: Religious leaders guide and unite people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What type of leaders are reverends and priests? A: Religious leaders.. Reverends and priests are religious leaders.
chunks.source: Reverends and priests are religious leaders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which local council official is in charge of children's rights? A: The Vice Chairperson.. The Vice Chairperson handles children's rights.
chunks.source: The Vice Chairperson handles children's rights.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is our district divided into divisions or town councils? A: For easy administration.. Divisions make governing easy.
chunks.source: Divisions make governing easy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does the colour red represent on the Uganda flag? A: Brotherhood (the blood that unites all Ugandans).. Red stands for brotherhood.
chunks.source: Red stands for brotherhood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is the Vice Chairman of L.C.I important to children? A: He protects the welfare of children.. The Vice Chairman looks after children.
chunks.source: The Vice Chairman looks after children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one group of law enforcers in your district. A: The police.. The police enforce the law.
chunks.source: The police enforce the law.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for law and order to be kept in your district? A: For people to live in peace.. Law and order bring peace.
chunks.source: Law and order bring peace.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: If there was an outbreak of cholera in your district, which district officer would you report to? A: The District Health Officer (DHO).. The DHO handles health matters.
chunks.source: The DHO handles health matters.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State the major duty of the police in your district. A: Keeping law and order.. The police keep law and order.
chunks.source: The police keep law and order.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of prisons in your district. A: Keeping law breakers and reforming them.. Prisons keep and reform criminals.
chunks.source: Prisons keep and reform criminals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give the title of the highest person in Uganda's prisons. A: Commissioner General of Prisons.. Prisons are headed by the Commissioner General.
chunks.source: Prisons are headed by the Commissioner General.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What title is given to a person who heads Parliament? A: The Speaker.. Parliament is headed by the Speaker.
chunks.source: Parliament is headed by the Speaker.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Write the following abbreviations in full: (i) U.P.D.F (ii) I.G.P (iii) ISO (iv) LDU. A: (i) Uganda People's Defence Force (ii) Inspector General of Police (iii) Internal Security Organisation (iv) Local Defence Unit.. UPDF is the army; IGP heads the police.
chunks.source: UPDF is the army; IGP heads the police.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Identify any two sections of the police in Uganda. A: Traffic police and CID (Criminal Investigations Department).. Police sections include traffic and CID.
chunks.source: Police sections include traffic and CID.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Which department of police is responsible for (i) putting out fires (ii) controlling riots (iii) investigating crimes? A: (i) Fire brigade (ii) Field Force Unit (iii) CID.. Fire brigade puts out fires; FFU controls riots; CID investigates crimes.
chunks.source: Fire brigade puts out fires; FFU controls riots; CID investigates crimes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Define the term commercial centres. A: Places where buying and selling take place.. Commercial centres are trading places.
chunks.source: Commercial centres are trading places.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one commercial centre you know. A: Owino market.. Owino is a big commercial centre.
chunks.source: Owino is a big commercial centre.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What are social services? A: Services provided by the government to meet people's needs.. Social services meet people's needs.
chunks.source: Social services meet people's needs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name any one social service provided by the district council in your area. A: Maintaining roads.. The district council maintains roads.
chunks.source: The district council maintains roads.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What social service is provided by schools? A: Education.. Schools provide education.
chunks.source: Schools provide education.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Write U.S.E in full. A: Universal Secondary Education.. USE means Universal Secondary Education.
chunks.source: USE means Universal Secondary Education.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Suggest one problem faced by U.P.E schools today. A: Overcrowding in classes.. UPE schools have too many pupils.
chunks.source: UPE schools have too many pupils.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What type of modern communication is used by people in your district today? A: Mobile phones.. People use mobile phones today.
chunks.source: People use mobile phones today.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Define amenities. A: Facilities that make life comfortable.. Amenities are useful comfortable facilities.
chunks.source: Amenities are useful comfortable facilities.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name any one amenity found in your school. A: Toilets.. Toilets are amenities in a school.
chunks.source: Toilets are amenities in a school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why are traffic lights important on the roads? A: They control traffic and prevent accidents.. Traffic lights control cars and stop accidents.
chunks.source: Traffic lights control cars and stop accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How are feeder roads helpful to farmers? A: They help farmers transport produce to markets.. Feeder roads take produce to markets.
chunks.source: Feeder roads take produce to markets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name one type of road you know. A: Tarmac road.. Tarmac is a type of road.
chunks.source: Tarmac is a type of road.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State one way of caring for social services. A: Cleaning them and not vandalizing them.. Keep services clean and unbroken.
chunks.source: Keep services clean and unbroken.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why do you need a post office in your district? A: To send and receive letters and parcels.. Post offices handle letters and parcels.
chunks.source: Post offices handle letters and parcels.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name the place where the following services can be got from: (i) Education services (ii) Communication services (iii) Security services (iv) Transport services. A: (i) School (ii) Post office (iii) Police station (iv) Taxi park.. Schools give education; police give security.
chunks.source: Schools give education; police give security.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How does the community benefit from the school? A: Their children get education.. Schools educate the community's children.
chunks.source: Schools educate the community's children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Write U.R.A in full. A: Uganda Revenue Authority.. URA collects taxes in Uganda.
chunks.source: URA collects taxes in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Which body in Uganda is responsible for collecting taxes? A: Uganda Revenue Authority (URA).. URA collects taxes.
chunks.source: URA collects taxes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Write VAT in full. A: Value Added Tax.. VAT is Value Added Tax.
chunks.source: VAT is Value Added Tax.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for the citizens to pay taxes? A: To enable the government to provide services.. Taxes help government give services.
chunks.source: Taxes help government give services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What are imports? A: Goods bought from other countries.. Imports come from other countries.
chunks.source: Imports come from other countries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name one major export of Uganda. A: Coffee.. Coffee is Uganda's major export.
chunks.source: Coffee is Uganda's major export.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Which major port handles the imports and exports of Uganda? A: Mombasa port.. Uganda uses Mombasa port in Kenya.
chunks.source: Uganda uses Mombasa port in Kenya.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important to have a school budget? A: To plan how school money is spent.. A budget plans spending.
chunks.source: A budget plans spending.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State one duty of the school bursar. A: Keeping the school's money safely.. The bursar keeps school money.
chunks.source: The bursar keeps school money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Identify one part of the budget. A: Income.. A budget has income and expenditure.
chunks.source: A budget has income and expenditure.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How does Uganda benefit from tourists? A: They bring foreign exchange.. Tourists bring money into Uganda.
chunks.source: Tourists bring money into Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State four sources of government income. A: Taxes, tourism, loans, donations.. Government gets money from taxes and tourism.
chunks.source: Government gets money from taxes and tourism.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name one means of road transport used in our area. A: A bicycle.. Bicycles are a common means of road transport.
chunks.source: Bicycles are a common means of road transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give the meaning of the term communication. A: The sending and receiving of messages.. Communication is sharing messages.
chunks.source: Communication is sharing messages.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State the ministry responsible for all schools in Uganda. A: Ministry of Education and Sports.. Schools fall under the Ministry of Education and Sports.
chunks.source: Schools fall under the Ministry of Education and Sports.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why soldiers wear uniforms. A: To be easily identified.. Uniforms make soldiers easy to identify.
chunks.source: Uniforms make soldiers easy to identify.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State one local material used to make balls. A: Banana fibres.. Balls are made from banana fibres.
chunks.source: Balls are made from banana fibres.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How can children help to keep security at school? A: By reporting strangers and wrongdoers.. Children keep security by reporting.
chunks.source: Children keep security by reporting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: In which way are prefects important in a school? A: They help to keep discipline.. Prefects keep discipline in school.
chunks.source: Prefects keep discipline in school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What is a project? A: A planned activity done to earn money or meet a need.. A project is planned work to earn a living.
chunks.source: A project is planned work to earn a living.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why do parents escort their children to school? A: To protect them from danger on the way.. Parents protect children on the way.
chunks.source: Parents protect children on the way.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of preventing conflicts between a school and its neighbourhood. A: By respecting neighbours and keeping peace.. Respect and peace prevent conflicts.
chunks.source: Respect and peace prevent conflicts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How can school children benefit from the Uganda museum? A: By learning about the past and culture.. The museum teaches history and culture.
chunks.source: The museum teaches history and culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How are markets important in our community? A: They are places for buying and selling goods.. Markets are for buying and selling.
chunks.source: Markets are for buying and selling.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How is traffic police important on our roads? A: They control traffic and prevent accidents.. Traffic police control cars and stop accidents.
chunks.source: Traffic police control cars and stop accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give one symbol of a school that encourages children to work hard. A: The school motto.. The motto encourages hard work.
chunks.source: The motto encourages hard work.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why do school children go for tours? A: To learn new things.. Tours teach new things.
chunks.source: Tours teach new things.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one item made by a potter. A: A pot.. Potters make pots.
chunks.source: Potters make pots.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why should a school have a sick bay? A: To treat sick pupils.. A sick bay treats sick pupils.
chunks.source: A sick bay treats sick pupils.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How can we keep security at home? A: By locking doors and fencing the home.. Locks and fences keep homes secure.
chunks.source: Locks and fences keep homes secure.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of making our environment clean. A: Proper disposal of rubbish.. Dispose of rubbish properly.
chunks.source: Dispose of rubbish properly.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give any one economic activity carried out in your division or sub-county. A: Farming.. Farming is an economic activity.
chunks.source: Farming is an economic activity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State any one problem the government faces in providing services to its people. A: Lack of enough money.. The government lacks enough money.
chunks.source: The government lacks enough money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why is air transport used to carry flowers and vegetables from Uganda to America? A: Because they get spoiled quickly.. Air transport is fast for perishable goods.
chunks.source: Air transport is fast for perishable goods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How does a community benefit from the school? A: Their children get education.. Schools educate the community's children.
chunks.source: Schools educate the community's children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How can we control accidents while using the road? A: By obeying traffic rules.. Traffic rules prevent accidents.
chunks.source: Traffic rules prevent accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How important is a hospital in your district? A: It treats the sick.. Hospitals treat sick people.
chunks.source: Hospitals treat sick people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How is a class register useful in a school? A: It is used for recording attendance.. Registers record who is present.
chunks.source: Registers record who is present.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State any one group of people who provide social services to us. A: The government.. The government provides services.
chunks.source: The government provides services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of a market to a crop farmer in your district. A: Selling farm produce.. Farmers sell produce in markets.
chunks.source: Farmers sell produce in markets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How is the Uganda Museum important to school children? A: It teaches them about culture and history.. The museum teaches history.
chunks.source: The museum teaches history.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name any one economic activity carried out by farmers. A: Crop growing.. Farmers grow crops.
chunks.source: Farmers grow crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Which department of the police guides drivers? A: Traffic police.. Traffic police guide drivers.
chunks.source: Traffic police guide drivers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need radios in our homes? A: To get news and information.. Radios give news.
chunks.source: Radios give news.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: On which side of the road should pedestrians walk? A: On the right side of the road.. Pedestrians walk on the right.
chunks.source: Pedestrians walk on the right.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Which symbol of a school is found on your uniform? A: The school badge.. The badge is on the uniform.
chunks.source: The badge is on the uniform.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How do people save electricity at home? A: By switching off lights that are not in use.. Switch off unused lights.
chunks.source: Switch off unused lights.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Define the term project. A: A planned activity done to earn money.. Projects are planned to earn a living.
chunks.source: Projects are planned to earn a living.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Which title is given to the person who heads a school? A: The headteacher.. A school is headed by the headteacher.
chunks.source: A school is headed by the headteacher.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name the district official in charge of treating animals. A: The Veterinary Officer.. The Veterinary Officer treats animals.
chunks.source: The Veterinary Officer treats animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What is child abuse? A: The mistreatment of children.. Child abuse is mistreating children.
chunks.source: Child abuse is mistreating children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State any one benefit the school gets from the community. A: The community supports the school with labour and materials.. Communities support their schools.
chunks.source: Communities support their schools.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give the meaning of child abuse. A: The mistreating of children.. Child abuse mistreats children.
chunks.source: Child abuse mistreats children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a basic need. A: Food.. Food is a basic need.
chunks.source: Food is a basic need.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How can we protect our water sources? A: By not dumping waste in them.. Keep waste out of water.
chunks.source: Keep waste out of water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why are markets important to people? A: They are places for buying and selling.. Markets are for trade.
chunks.source: Markets are for trade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give the importance of peace and security. A: People live and work in peace.. Peace lets people work happily.
chunks.source: Peace lets people work happily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How do school rules and regulations promote order and discipline in a school? A: They guide the behaviour of pupils.. Rules guide how pupils behave.
chunks.source: Rules guide how pupils behave.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need teachers in a community? A: To educate children.. Teachers educate children.
chunks.source: Teachers educate children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Mention one way we can keep our money safe from thieves. A: By keeping it in a bank.. Banks keep money safe.
chunks.source: Banks keep money safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why should every school have a flag? A: For identity and patriotism.. A flag gives the school identity.
chunks.source: A flag gives the school identity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why some people fail to get their basic needs. A: Poverty.. Poverty stops people getting needs.
chunks.source: Poverty stops people getting needs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How does the police keep law and order? A: By arresting law breakers and patrolling.. Police arrest criminals and patrol.
chunks.source: Police arrest criminals and patrol.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) Give any one cause of child abuse. b) State any two ways children's rights are abused in our district. c) Write one way of controlling child abuse. A: a) Poverty. b) Child labour; denying children education. c) Reporting abusers to the police or LC.. Poverty causes abuse; children are overworked and denied school; report abusers.
chunks.source: Poverty causes abuse; children are overworked and denied school; report abusers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) What term is used to mean the movement of people or goods from one place to another? b) Write any one safe way of using the road. c) Why are road signs put on busy roads? A: a) Transport. b) Walking on the right side of the road. c) To guide road users and prevent accidents.. Transport moves people and goods; road signs guide and protect.
chunks.source: Transport moves people and goods; road signs guide and protect.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Match the raw materials to the product correctly: (a) Cotton (b) Papyrus (c) Clay (d) Tobacco. A: Cotton: clothes; Papyrus: mats; Clay: pots; Tobacco: cigarettes. Cotton makes clothes, papyrus makes mats, clay makes pots, tobacco makes cigarettes.
chunks.source: Cotton makes clothes, papyrus makes mats, clay makes pots, tobacco makes cigarettes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) What are economic activities? b) Mention any one importance of social activities in your district. c) Give one reason why people work. d) State one problem people face at their work places. A: a) Activities people do to earn a living. b) They unite people. c) To earn a living. d) Low pay.. Economic activities earn a living; social activities unite people.
chunks.source: Economic activities earn a living; social activities unite people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) What is child abuse? b) State any two dangers of child abuse. c) Give any one way children can be protected from abuse. A: a) The mistreatment of children. b) Injuries; death. c) By reporting abusers to the police.. Abuse mistreats children, injures them; report abusers.
chunks.source: Abuse mistreats children, injures them; report abusers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) How do communities benefit schools around them? b) Give two reasons why schools should be fenced. A: a) They provide land and labour to the school. b) For security; to keep animals out.. Communities give land and labour; fences give security.
chunks.source: Communities give land and labour; fences give security.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) Name two basic needs of a family. b) Give two reasons why some families lack basic needs. A: a) Food and shelter. b) Poverty; unemployment.. Food and shelter are basic needs; poverty denies them.
chunks.source: Food and shelter are basic needs; poverty denies them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Match correctly: (a) Cotton (b) Sisal (c) Milk (d) Sugarcane. A: Cotton: clothes; Sisal: ropes; Milk: ghee; Sugarcane: sugar. Cotton makes clothes, sisal makes ropes, milk makes ghee, sugarcane makes sugar.
chunks.source: Cotton makes clothes, sisal makes ropes, milk makes ghee, sugarcane makes sugar.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) What is transport? b) Which type of transport is commonly used in our district? c) Why is air transport used by few people in our district? d) Give one means of transport used on railway lines. A: a) The movement of people or goods from one place to another. b) Road transport. c) It is expensive. d) A train.. Transport moves people and goods; road is common; air is costly.
chunks.source: Transport moves people and goods; road is common; air is costly.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) What are social services? b) Write any two social services the government provides to Uganda. c) Mention any one problem the government faces when providing social services to people. A: a) Services provided by the government to meet people's needs. b) Education; health services. c) Lack of enough money.. Social services meet needs; money is the main problem.
chunks.source: Social services meet needs; money is the main problem.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Match list A to B correctly: Meteorology, Dentist, Cobbler, Mechanic. A: Meteorology: the study of weather changes; Dentist: treats teeth; Cobbler: mends shoes; Mechanic: repairs machines. Meteorology studies weather; a dentist treats teeth; a cobbler mends shoes; a mechanic repairs machines.
chunks.source: Meteorology studies weather; a dentist treats teeth; a cobbler mends shoes; a mechanic repairs machines.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) What are basic needs? b) Give any two examples of basic needs. c) Why do some people fail to get basic needs? A: a) Things we cannot live without. b) Food; shelter. c) Because of poverty.. Basic needs are must-haves; poverty denies them.
chunks.source: Basic needs are must-haves; poverty denies them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) What are social activities? b) Give any two examples of social activities. c) Give the importance of social activities. A: a) Activities people do together for enjoyment. b) Games; dancing. c) They unite people.. Social activities are done together and unite people.
chunks.source: Social activities are done together and unite people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) State any two causes of accidents at home. b) How can we avoid accidents at home? c) Why are accidents very bad? A: a) Careless handling of fire; slippery floors. b) By being careful. c) They cause injuries and death.. Fire and slippery floors cause accidents; be careful.
chunks.source: Fire and slippery floors cause accidents; be careful.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table correctly: Soft wood, Clay, (raw material for cigarettes), (raw material for papyrus mats). A: Soft wood: furniture; Clay: pots; Tobacco: cigarettes; Papyrus: mats. Soft wood makes furniture, clay makes pots, tobacco makes cigarettes, papyrus makes mats.
chunks.source: Soft wood makes furniture, clay makes pots, tobacco makes cigarettes, papyrus makes mats.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) Give any two forms of child abuse. b) Write two rights every child must enjoy. A: a) Beating children; child labour. b) The right to education; the right to health.. Abuse includes beating and child labour; children have rights to education and health.
chunks.source: Abuse includes beating and child labour; children have rights to education and health.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) Write one source of water in your sub-county. b) Why should water sources be protected? c) State any two ways in which people destroy water sources. A: a) A borehole. b) To keep the water clean and safe. c) Dumping waste in them; washing in them.. Boreholes give water; keep them clean.
chunks.source: Boreholes give water; keep them clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: a) Mention any two examples of traditional means of communication. b) How is a radio useful to people? c) State any one advantage of modern means of communication. A: a) Drums; smoke signals. b) It gives news and information. c) They are fast.. Drums and smoke are traditional; radios give news; modern means are fast.
chunks.source: Drums and smoke are traditional; radios give news; modern means are fast.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Mention any four qualities of a good map. A: Title, key, scale, compass direction.. A good map has a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.
chunks.source: A good map has a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Mention any four qualities of a good map. A: False. A good map has a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.
chunks.source: A good map has a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: List down any four groups of people who use a compass. A: Pilots, sailors, soldiers, surveyors.. People who travel or find directions use a compass.
chunks.source: People who travel or find directions use a compass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: List down any four groups of people who use a compass. A: False. People who travel or find directions use a compass.
chunks.source: People who travel or find directions use a compass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Identify the four major points of a compass. A: North, South, East, West.. These are the cardinal points of a compass.
chunks.source: These are the cardinal points of a compass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Identify the four major points of a compass. A: False. These are the cardinal points of a compass.
chunks.source: These are the cardinal points of a compass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the major latitude marked 0 degrees on a map. A: The Equator.. The Equator is the latitude marked 0 degrees.
chunks.source: The Equator is the latitude marked 0 degrees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the major latitude marked 0 degrees on a map. A: False. The Equator is the latitude marked 0 degrees.
chunks.source: The Equator is the latitude marked 0 degrees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Sarah was moving to school in the morning and she saw the sun directly on her face. In which direction was she facing? A: East.. The sun rises in the east in the morning.
chunks.source: The sun rises in the east in the morning.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Sarah was moving to school in the morning and she saw the sun directly on her face. In which direction was she facing? A: False. The sun rises in the east in the morning.
chunks.source: The sun rises in the east in the morning.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the country which borders Uganda to the south west. A: Rwanda.. Rwanda borders Uganda to the south west.
chunks.source: Rwanda borders Uganda to the south west.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the country which borders Uganda to the south west. A: False. Rwanda borders Uganda to the south west.
chunks.source: Rwanda borders Uganda to the south west.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
