chunks.text: Q: Mention any four qualities of a good map. A: Title, key, scale, compass direction.. A good map has a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.
chunks.source: A good map has a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: List down any four groups of people who use a compass. A: Pilots, sailors, soldiers, surveyors.. People who travel or find directions use a compass.
chunks.source: People who travel or find directions use a compass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Identify the four major points of a compass. A: North, South, East, West.. These are the cardinal points of a compass.
chunks.source: These are the cardinal points of a compass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the major latitude marked 0 degrees on a map. A: The Equator.. The Equator is the latitude marked 0 degrees.
chunks.source: The Equator is the latitude marked 0 degrees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Sarah was moving to school in the morning and she saw the sun directly on her face. In which direction was she facing? A: East.. The sun rises in the east in the morning.
chunks.source: The sun rises in the east in the morning.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the country which borders Uganda to the south west. A: Rwanda.. Rwanda borders Uganda to the south west.
chunks.source: Rwanda borders Uganda to the south west.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the district which is found in Lake Victoria. A: Kalangala district.. Kalangala is made of islands in Lake Victoria.
chunks.source: Kalangala is made of islands in Lake Victoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: How many divisions make up Kampala district? A: Five divisions.. Kampala has five divisions.
chunks.source: Kampala has five divisions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Which body is responsible for Kampala district? A: Kampala Capital City Authority (KCCA).. KCCA runs the affairs of Kampala.
chunks.source: KCCA runs the affairs of Kampala.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: What title is given to the political head of Kampala? A: Lord Mayor.. The political head of Kampala is the Lord Mayor.
chunks.source: The political head of Kampala is the Lord Mayor.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name any four municipalities (divisions) of Kampala. A: Kawempe, Makindye, Rubaga, Nakawa.. Kampala has five divisions; any four are correct.
chunks.source: Kampala has five divisions; any four are correct.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the biggest division of Kampala and the most industrialized division. A: Biggest: Kawempe; most industrialized: Nakawa.. Kawempe is the biggest division and Nakawa has many industries.
chunks.source: Kawempe is the biggest division and Nakawa has many industries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name two lakes crossed by the Equator in Uganda. A: Lake Victoria and Lake George.. The Equator crosses Lake Victoria and Lake George.
chunks.source: The Equator crosses Lake Victoria and Lake George.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name any two districts which are crossed by the Equator. A: Mpigi and Masaka.. The Equator passes through Mpigi and Masaka districts.
chunks.source: The Equator passes through Mpigi and Masaka districts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name any three small towns found in Kampala. A: Bwaise, Katwe, Ntinda.. Kampala has small towns like Bwaise, Katwe and Ntinda.
chunks.source: Kampala has small towns like Bwaise, Katwe and Ntinda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the drawing of an object as seen from aside? A: A picture.. A picture shows an object as seen from the side.
chunks.source: A picture shows an object as seen from the side.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: In which direction is the sun in the evening? A: In the west.. The sun sets in the west in the evening.
chunks.source: The sun sets in the west in the evening.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a semi-cardinal point on a compass. A: North East.. North East is a semi-cardinal point.
chunks.source: North East is a semi-cardinal point.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Give any one cardinal point of a compass. A: North.. North is a cardinal point.
chunks.source: North is a cardinal point.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Mention the element of a map that helps us to understand it. A: The key.. The key explains the map.
chunks.source: The key explains the map.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the map symbol drawn below: 0 10 km 20 km. A: The scale.. That symbol is the scale of the map.
chunks.source: That symbol is the scale of the map.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: How is a picture similar to a map? A: Both are drawings.. Pictures and maps are both drawings.
chunks.source: Pictures and maps are both drawings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Give one element of a good map. A: A title.. A title is an element of a good map.
chunks.source: A title is an element of a good map.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the capital city of Uganda. A: Kampala.. Kampala is the capital of Uganda.
chunks.source: Kampala is the capital of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any four examples of physical features in your district. A: Hills, mountains, lakes, rivers.. Physical features include hills, mountains, lakes and rivers.
chunks.source: Physical features include hills, mountains, lakes and rivers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any two economic activities carried out on plateau land. A: Crop growing and animal grazing.. Flat plateau land is good for farming and grazing.
chunks.source: Flat plateau land is good for farming and grazing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any two lakes found in Kampala district. A: Lake Victoria and Kabaka's lake.. Kampala has Lake Victoria and the man-made Kabaka's lake.
chunks.source: Kampala has Lake Victoria and the man-made Kabaka's lake.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which man-made lake is found in Kampala? A: Kabaka's lake.. Kabaka's lake was dug by the Kabaka's men.
chunks.source: Kabaka's lake was dug by the Kabaka's men.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two problems faced by lakes and rivers. A: Pollution and silting.. Lakes and rivers suffer from pollution and silting.
chunks.source: Lakes and rivers suffer from pollution and silting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two problems faced by people living around lakes and rivers. A: Floods and water-borne diseases.. People near water face floods and diseases.
chunks.source: People near water face floods and diseases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: On which hill in Kampala do we find radio and television masts? A: Kololo hill.. Masts stand on Kololo hill.
chunks.source: Masts stand on Kololo hill.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What feature is formed between two or more hills? A: A valley.. Low land between hills is a valley.
chunks.source: Low land between hills is a valley.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can valleys be dangerous to people? A: They flood during heavy rains.. Water collects in valleys and floods them.
chunks.source: Water collects in valleys and floods them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any two hills in Kampala. A: Kololo and Nakasero.. Kampala is built on hills like Kololo and Nakasero.
chunks.source: Kampala is built on hills like Kololo and Nakasero.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any four types of weather. A: Sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy.. Weather can be sunny, cloudy, rainy or windy.
chunks.source: Weather can be sunny, cloudy, rainy or windy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any three weather makers. A: The sun, wind and clouds.. The sun, wind and clouds make weather.
chunks.source: The sun, wind and clouds make weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What term is used to mean the study of weather conditions? A: Meteorology.. Meteorology is the study of weather.
chunks.source: Meteorology is the study of weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do we call people who study and tell us about the weather conditions of a particular place? A: Meteorologists.. Meteorologists study the weather.
chunks.source: Meteorologists study the weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which district do we find the biggest meteorological centre? A: Wakiso (at Entebbe).. The biggest weather centre is at Entebbe in Wakiso.
chunks.source: The biggest weather centre is at Entebbe in Wakiso.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which instrument is used to measure the amount of sunshine in an area? A: A sunshine recorder.. The sunshine recorder measures sunshine.
chunks.source: The sunshine recorder measures sunshine.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List down any two processes of rain formation. A: Evaporation and condensation.. Water evaporates, then vapour condenses into rain.
chunks.source: Water evaporates, then vapour condenses into rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What type of rainfall is received in Kalangala and Kampala districts? A: Convectional rainfall.. Areas near Lake Victoria get convectional rainfall.
chunks.source: Areas near Lake Victoria get convectional rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of rainfall received in flat areas. A: Convectional rainfall.. Flat, hot areas get convectional rainfall.
chunks.source: Flat, hot areas get convectional rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define wind. A: Moving air.. Wind is air in motion.
chunks.source: Wind is air in motion.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name (i) the nearest clouds (ii) the highest clouds. A: (i) Stratus (ii) Cirrus.. Stratus clouds are lowest; cirrus are highest.
chunks.source: Stratus clouds are lowest; cirrus are highest.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is a Stevenson screen painted white? A: To reflect heat.. White paint reflects heat away.
chunks.source: White paint reflects heat away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any two instruments kept in a Stevenson screen. A: Maximum and minimum thermometers.. The screen holds the maximum and minimum thermometers.
chunks.source: The screen holds the maximum and minimum thermometers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way soil erosion is controlled in our school compound. A: By planting grass.. Planted grass holds the soil.
chunks.source: Planted grass holds the soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are nimbus clouds important to farmers? A: They bring rain for crops.. Nimbus clouds bring the rain farmers need.
chunks.source: Nimbus clouds bring the rain farmers need.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which landform is good for constructing roads? A: Plains (flat land).. Flat land is best for roads.
chunks.source: Flat land is best for roads.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one way of managing rainy weather. A: Using an umbrella.. Umbrellas protect us in rain.
chunks.source: Umbrellas protect us in rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which element of weather is responsible for the water increase in Lake Victoria? A: Rainfall.. Rainfall raises the lake's water.
chunks.source: Rainfall raises the lake's water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one danger of living near Lake Victoria. A: Floods.. Lake areas flood.
chunks.source: Lake areas flood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are donkeys useful to people in mountainous areas? A: They carry loads.. Donkeys carry loads in mountains.
chunks.source: Donkeys carry loads in mountains.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one type of rainfall received in Uganda. A: Convectional rainfall.. Uganda receives convectional rainfall.
chunks.source: Uganda receives convectional rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do school children manage rainy weather? A: By using umbrellas and raincoats.. Umbrellas and raincoats manage rain.
chunks.source: Umbrellas and raincoats manage rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the building material got from hills. A: Stones.. Stones come from hills.
chunks.source: Stones come from hills.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is Lake Victoria helpful to the people in our district? A: It provides fish and water.. The lake gives fish and water.
chunks.source: The lake gives fish and water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What problem do people living in hilly areas face? A: Poor transport and landslides.. Hills make transport hard and slide.
chunks.source: Hills make transport hard and slide.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are nimbus clouds useful to farmers? A: They bring rain for crops.. Nimbus clouds bring rain.
chunks.source: Nimbus clouds bring rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one physical feature in your district or division. A: A hill.. Hills are physical features.
chunks.source: Hills are physical features.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one danger caused by too much rainfall. A: Floods.. Too much rain causes floods.
chunks.source: Too much rain causes floods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which physical feature covers the largest part of your district? A: Plains (flat land).. Flat plains cover most of the district.
chunks.source: Flat plains cover most of the district.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List down the two types of vegetation. A: Natural vegetation and planted vegetation.. Vegetation is either natural or planted.
chunks.source: Vegetation is either natural or planted.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Outline any four examples of natural vegetation in Uganda. A: Forests, swamps, grasslands, bushes.. Natural vegetation includes forests, swamps and grasslands.
chunks.source: Natural vegetation includes forests, swamps and grasslands.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State two ways how people care for vegetation. A: Planting trees; avoiding bush burning.. Plant trees and do not burn bushes.
chunks.source: Plant trees and do not burn bushes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What type of wood is got from planted forests? A: Soft wood.. Planted forests give soft wood.
chunks.source: Planted forests give soft wood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of trees that provide hard wood timber. A: Mvule and mahogany.. Mvule and mahogany give hard wood.
chunks.source: Mvule and mahogany give hard wood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of soft wood trees. A: Pine and cypress.. Pine and cypress are soft wood trees.
chunks.source: Pine and cypress are soft wood trees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which district is Mabira natural forest? A: Buikwe district.. Mabira forest is in Buikwe district.
chunks.source: Mabira forest is in Buikwe district.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List down any three examples of natural forests. A: Mabira, Budongo, Kibale.. Uganda's natural forests include Mabira and Budongo.
chunks.source: Uganda's natural forests include Mabira and Budongo.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List down any three examples of planted forests. A: Lendu, Nyabyeya, Mafuga.. Planted forests include Lendu and Nyabyeya.
chunks.source: Planted forests include Lendu and Nyabyeya.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a swamp? A: A waterlogged area with vegetation.. A swamp is a wet area with plants.
chunks.source: A swamp is a wet area with plants.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the most swampy lake in Uganda. A: Lake Kyoga.. Lake Kyoga is the most swampy lake.
chunks.source: Lake Kyoga is the most swampy lake.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is Lake Kyoga swampy? A: It is shallow.. Kyoga is shallow, so swamps grow in it.
chunks.source: Kyoga is shallow, so swamps grow in it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the commonest fish caught from most swamps. A: Mudfish.. Mudfish is common in swamps.
chunks.source: Mudfish is common in swamps.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which type of vegetation covers the largest part of Uganda? A: Savannah grassland.. Savannah grassland covers most of Uganda.
chunks.source: Savannah grassland covers most of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one swamp you know. A: Lubigi swamp.. Lubigi is a well-known swamp near Kampala.
chunks.source: Lubigi is a well-known swamp near Kampala.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the two types of forests you know. A: Natural forests and planted forests.. Forests are natural or planted.
chunks.source: Forests are natural or planted.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List two tree species planted in forests. A: Pine and eucalyptus.. Pine and eucalyptus are planted in forests.
chunks.source: Pine and eucalyptus are planted in forests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give three products got from soft wood. A: Paper; furniture; poles.. Soft wood is used for paper, furniture and poles.
chunks.source: Soft wood is used for paper, furniture and poles.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two uses of grasslands to man. A: Grazing for animals; thatching houses.. Grasslands give pasture and thatch.
chunks.source: Grasslands give pasture and thatch.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the body responsible for protection of the environment. A: NEMA (National Environment Management Authority).. NEMA protects the environment in Uganda.
chunks.source: NEMA protects the environment in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the two types of crops. A: Food crops and cash crops.. Crops are grown for food or for sale.
chunks.source: Crops are grown for food or for sale.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are cash crops? A: Crops grown mainly for sale.. Cash crops are grown to be sold.
chunks.source: Cash crops are grown to be sold.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give four examples of cash crops. A: Coffee, cotton, tea, tobacco.. Coffee, cotton, tea and tobacco are cash crops.
chunks.source: Coffee, cotton, tea and tobacco are cash crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of non-traditional cash crops. A: Flowers and vanilla.. Flowers and vanilla are non-traditional cash crops.
chunks.source: Flowers and vanilla are non-traditional cash crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one natural resource in your district. A: Land.. Land is a natural resource.
chunks.source: Land is a natural resource.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one renewable resource. A: Trees.. Trees grow back, so they are renewable.
chunks.source: Trees grow back, so they are renewable.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify one way in which land is used in your district. A: Farming.. Land is used for farming.
chunks.source: Land is used for farming.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down one common crop that grows well in swampy areas. A: Rice.. Rice grows well in swampy areas.
chunks.source: Rice grows well in swampy areas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do people in your district misuse natural resources? A: Deforestation; overfishing; polluting water sources.. People misuse resources by cutting trees and polluting water.
chunks.source: People misuse resources by cutting trees and polluting water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one way a farmer can maintain soil fertility in a hilly area. A: Terracing.. Terracing stops soil from washing away on hills.
chunks.source: Terracing stops soil from washing away on hills.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one example of a craft object. A: A basket.. Baskets are craft objects.
chunks.source: Baskets are craft objects.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why should we plant trees in our school compound? A: For shade and fresh air.. Trees give shade and fresh air.
chunks.source: Trees give shade and fresh air.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we call a waterlogged area with vegetation? A: A swamp.. A swamp is waterlogged with plants.
chunks.source: A swamp is waterlogged with plants.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which domestic animals are kept for meat only? A: Pigs.. Pigs are kept mainly for meat.
chunks.source: Pigs are kept mainly for meat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger of draining swampy areas. A: It destroys water sources.. Draining swamps destroys water.
chunks.source: Draining swamps destroys water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write NFA in full. A: National Forestry Authority.. NFA is the National Forestry Authority.
chunks.source: NFA is the National Forestry Authority.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Crops grown mainly for sale are known as what? A: Crops grown mainly for sale.. Cash crops are grown to be sold.
chunks.source: Cash crops are grown to be sold.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which building material is got from swamps? A: Clay.. Clay comes from swamps.
chunks.source: Clay comes from swamps.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need trees and grass planted in our school compound? A: For shade and beauty.. Trees and grass give shade and beauty.
chunks.source: Trees and grass give shade and beauty.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What term is used to mean the plant cover of an area that is grown by man? A: Planted vegetation.. Man-grown plant cover is planted vegetation.
chunks.source: Man-grown plant cover is planted vegetation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write NEMA in full. A: National Environment Management Authority.. NEMA protects the environment.
chunks.source: NEMA protects the environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way people in our district have destroyed the environment. A: Deforestation.. Cutting trees destroys the environment.
chunks.source: Cutting trees destroys the environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people keep domestic animals? A: For milk, meat and eggs.. Animals give milk, meat and eggs.
chunks.source: Animals give milk, meat and eggs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why people grow crops. A: To get food.. Crops give food.
chunks.source: Crops give food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down the four ethnic groups of Uganda. A: Bantu, Nilotics, Nilo-Hamites, Hamites.. Uganda has four main ethnic groups.
chunks.source: Uganda has four main ethnic groups.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are the Baganda and Bagisu related? A: They are both Bantu.. Both belong to the Bantu ethnic group.
chunks.source: Both belong to the Bantu ethnic group.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the brother of Nambi who was kind. A: Kayikuzi.. Kayikuzi, Nambi's brother, was kind to Kintu.
chunks.source: Kayikuzi, Nambi's brother, was kind to Kintu.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does the name (i) Walumbe mean (ii) Kayikuzi mean? A: (i) Death (ii) The digger.. Walumbe means death; Kayikuzi means the digger.
chunks.source: Walumbe means death; Kayikuzi means the digger.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two dangers of slums. A: Diseases; crime.. Slums spread disease and crime.
chunks.source: Slums spread disease and crime.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two types of family. A: Nuclear family and extended family.. Families are nuclear or extended.
chunks.source: Families are nuclear or extended.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who heads a family? A: The father.. The father heads the family.
chunks.source: The father heads the family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two duties of children at home. A: Helping with housework; respecting parents.. Children help at home and respect parents.
chunks.source: Children help at home and respect parents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give three dangers of high population. A: Overcrowding; land shortage; unemployment.. Too many people bring crowds and land shortage.
chunks.source: Too many people bring crowds and land shortage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List any two disadvantages of a low population in an area. A: Shortage of labour; small market.. Few people means little labour and market.
chunks.source: Few people means little labour and market.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List any four natural hazards that can lead to population decrease in an area. A: Drought, floods, earthquakes, landslides.. Drought, floods and quakes kill people.
chunks.source: Drought, floods and quakes kill people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List any four items collected by enumerators during population census. A: Name, age, sex, tribe.. Enumerators record name, age, sex and tribe.
chunks.source: Enumerators record name, age, sex and tribe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to a home and its surroundings? A: A homestead.. A home with its surroundings is a homestead.
chunks.source: A home with its surroundings is a homestead.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one cultural practice in your district. A: Circumcision.. Circumcision is a cultural practice.
chunks.source: Circumcision is a cultural practice.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write any one cultural practice in your district. A: Circumcision.. Circumcision is a cultural practice.
chunks.source: Circumcision is a cultural practice.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any one member of an extended family. A: An uncle.. An uncle is in the extended family.
chunks.source: An uncle is in the extended family.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why some areas have more people than others. A: Better jobs and services.. Jobs and services attract people.
chunks.source: Jobs and services attract people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What term is used to mean a home and its surroundings? A: A homestead.. A home and surroundings is a homestead.
chunks.source: A home and surroundings is a homestead.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the tribe in our district that practises circumcision. A: The Bagisu.. The Bagisu practise circumcision.
chunks.source: The Bagisu practise circumcision.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What lesson do we learn from the story of Kintu and Nambi? A: Hard work pays.. Kintu's story teaches hard work.
chunks.source: Kintu's story teaches hard work.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a homestead? A: A home and its surroundings.. A homestead is a home with its surroundings.
chunks.source: A homestead is a home with its surroundings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people fence their homes? A: For security.. Fences protect homes.
chunks.source: Fences protect homes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the official responsible for payment of civil servants in the district. A: The Chief Administrative Officer (CAO).. The CAO pays civil servants in the district.
chunks.source: The CAO pays civil servants in the district.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How many members make up the Local Council committee? A: Nine members.. An LC committee has nine members.
chunks.source: An LC committee has nine members.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the executive committee of the L.C responsible for the welfare of children in the district. A: The Vice Chairperson.. The Vice Chairperson looks after children's welfare.
chunks.source: The Vice Chairperson looks after children's welfare.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the title of the person who heads the Local Council V committee. A: District Chairperson (LCV Chairperson).. The LCV committee is headed by the District Chairperson.
chunks.source: The LCV committee is headed by the District Chairperson.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why districts are divided into sub-counties. A: For easy administration.. Sub-counties make governing easier.
chunks.source: Sub-counties make governing easier.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which body is responsible for running all the activities in Kampala? A: Kampala Capital City Authority (KCCA).. KCCA runs Kampala.
chunks.source: KCCA runs Kampala.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the current Lord Mayor of Kampala. A: Erias Lukwago.. The Lord Mayor of Kampala is Erias Lukwago.
chunks.source: The Lord Mayor of Kampala is Erias Lukwago.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Under which Ministry is the Local Council? A: Ministry of Local Government.. Local councils fall under the Ministry of Local Government.
chunks.source: Local councils fall under the Ministry of Local Government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define by-laws. A: Laws made by local councils.. By-laws are local laws.
chunks.source: By-laws are local laws.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the title of the President's representative in Kampala. A: The Minister for Kampala.. The President is represented in Kampala by the Minister for Kampala.
chunks.source: The President is represented in Kampala by the Minister for Kampala.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the body responsible for the activities in the district. A: The District Council (LCV).. The District Council runs district activities.
chunks.source: The District Council runs district activities.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any one municipality (division) in Kampala. A: Kawempe.. Kawempe is a division of Kampala.
chunks.source: Kawempe is a division of Kampala.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What type of leaders are reverends and priests? A: Religious leaders.. Reverends and priests are religious leaders.
chunks.source: Reverends and priests are religious leaders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which local council official is in charge of children's rights? A: The Vice Chairperson.. The Vice Chairperson handles children's rights.
chunks.source: The Vice Chairperson handles children's rights.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is our district divided into divisions or town councils? A: For easy administration.. Divisions make governing easy.
chunks.source: Divisions make governing easy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one group of law enforcers in your district. A: The police.. The police enforce the law.
chunks.source: The police enforce the law.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: If there was an outbreak of cholera in your district, which district officer would you report to? A: The District Health Officer (DHO).. The DHO handles health matters.
chunks.source: The DHO handles health matters.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State the major duty of the police in your district. A: Keeping law and order.. The police keep law and order.
chunks.source: The police keep law and order.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give the title of the highest person in Uganda's prisons. A: Commissioner General of Prisons.. Prisons are headed by the Commissioner General.
chunks.source: Prisons are headed by the Commissioner General.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What title is given to a person who heads Parliament? A: The Speaker.. Parliament is headed by the Speaker.
chunks.source: Parliament is headed by the Speaker.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one commercial centre you know. A: Owino market.. Owino is a big commercial centre.
chunks.source: Owino is a big commercial centre.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name any one social service provided by the district council in your area. A: Maintaining roads.. The district council maintains roads.
chunks.source: The district council maintains roads.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What social service is provided by schools? A: Education.. Schools provide education.
chunks.source: Schools provide education.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Write U.S.E in full. A: Universal Secondary Education.. USE means Universal Secondary Education.
chunks.source: USE means Universal Secondary Education.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Suggest one problem faced by U.P.E schools today. A: Overcrowding in classes.. UPE schools have too many pupils.
chunks.source: UPE schools have too many pupils.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What type of modern communication is used by people in your district today? A: Mobile phones.. People use mobile phones today.
chunks.source: People use mobile phones today.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Define amenities. A: Facilities that make life comfortable.. Amenities are useful comfortable facilities.
chunks.source: Amenities are useful comfortable facilities.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name any one amenity found in your school. A: Toilets.. Toilets are amenities in a school.
chunks.source: Toilets are amenities in a school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name one type of road you know. A: Tarmac road.. Tarmac is a type of road.
chunks.source: Tarmac is a type of road.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How does the community benefit from the school? A: Their children get education.. Schools educate the community's children.
chunks.source: Schools educate the community's children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Write U.R.A in full. A: Uganda Revenue Authority.. URA collects taxes in Uganda.
chunks.source: URA collects taxes in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Which body in Uganda is responsible for collecting taxes? A: Uganda Revenue Authority (URA).. URA collects taxes.
chunks.source: URA collects taxes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Write VAT in full. A: Value Added Tax.. VAT is Value Added Tax.
chunks.source: VAT is Value Added Tax.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What are imports? A: Goods bought from other countries.. Imports come from other countries.
chunks.source: Imports come from other countries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name one major export of Uganda. A: Coffee.. Coffee is Uganda's major export.
chunks.source: Coffee is Uganda's major export.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Which major port handles the imports and exports of Uganda? A: Mombasa port.. Uganda uses Mombasa port in Kenya.
chunks.source: Uganda uses Mombasa port in Kenya.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State one duty of the school bursar. A: Keeping the school's money safely.. The bursar keeps school money.
chunks.source: The bursar keeps school money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Identify one part of the budget. A: Income.. A budget has income and expenditure.
chunks.source: A budget has income and expenditure.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How does Uganda benefit from tourists? A: They bring foreign exchange.. Tourists bring money into Uganda.
chunks.source: Tourists bring money into Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State four sources of government income. A: Taxes, tourism, loans, donations.. Government gets money from taxes and tourism.
chunks.source: Government gets money from taxes and tourism.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name one means of road transport used in our area. A: A bicycle.. Bicycles are a common means of road transport.
chunks.source: Bicycles are a common means of road transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State the ministry responsible for all schools in Uganda. A: Ministry of Education and Sports.. Schools fall under the Ministry of Education and Sports.
chunks.source: Schools fall under the Ministry of Education and Sports.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why soldiers wear uniforms. A: To be easily identified.. Uniforms make soldiers easy to identify.
chunks.source: Uniforms make soldiers easy to identify.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State one local material used to make balls. A: Banana fibres.. Balls are made from banana fibres.
chunks.source: Balls are made from banana fibres.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How can children help to keep security at school? A: By reporting strangers and wrongdoers.. Children keep security by reporting.
chunks.source: Children keep security by reporting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: In which way are prefects important in a school? A: They help to keep discipline.. Prefects keep discipline in school.
chunks.source: Prefects keep discipline in school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give one symbol of a school that encourages children to work hard. A: The school motto.. The motto encourages hard work.
chunks.source: The motto encourages hard work.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why do school children go for tours? A: To learn new things.. Tours teach new things.
chunks.source: Tours teach new things.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one item made by a potter. A: A pot.. Potters make pots.
chunks.source: Potters make pots.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why should a school have a sick bay? A: To treat sick pupils.. A sick bay treats sick pupils.
chunks.source: A sick bay treats sick pupils.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of making our environment clean. A: Proper disposal of rubbish.. Dispose of rubbish properly.
chunks.source: Dispose of rubbish properly.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give any one economic activity carried out in your division or sub-county. A: Farming.. Farming is an economic activity.
chunks.source: Farming is an economic activity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State any one problem the government faces in providing services to its people. A: Lack of enough money.. The government lacks enough money.
chunks.source: The government lacks enough money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why is air transport used to carry flowers and vegetables from Uganda to America? A: Because they get spoiled quickly.. Air transport is fast for perishable goods.
chunks.source: Air transport is fast for perishable goods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How does a community benefit from the school? A: Their children get education.. Schools educate the community's children.
chunks.source: Schools educate the community's children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How can we control accidents while using the road? A: By obeying traffic rules.. Traffic rules prevent accidents.
chunks.source: Traffic rules prevent accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How important is a hospital in your district? A: It treats the sick.. Hospitals treat sick people.
chunks.source: Hospitals treat sick people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State any one group of people who provide social services to us. A: The government.. The government provides services.
chunks.source: The government provides services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of a market to a crop farmer in your district. A: Selling farm produce.. Farmers sell produce in markets.
chunks.source: Farmers sell produce in markets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name any one economic activity carried out by farmers. A: Crop growing.. Farmers grow crops.
chunks.source: Farmers grow crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Which department of the police guides drivers? A: Traffic police.. Traffic police guide drivers.
chunks.source: Traffic police guide drivers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need radios in our homes? A: To get news and information.. Radios give news.
chunks.source: Radios give news.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Which symbol of a school is found on your uniform? A: The school badge.. The badge is on the uniform.
chunks.source: The badge is on the uniform.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Which title is given to the person who heads a school? A: The headteacher.. A school is headed by the headteacher.
chunks.source: A school is headed by the headteacher.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name the district official in charge of treating animals. A: The Veterinary Officer.. The Veterinary Officer treats animals.
chunks.source: The Veterinary Officer treats animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What is child abuse? A: The mistreatment of children.. Child abuse is mistreating children.
chunks.source: Child abuse is mistreating children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give the meaning of child abuse. A: The mistreating of children.. Child abuse mistreats children.
chunks.source: Child abuse mistreats children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a basic need. A: Food.. Food is a basic need.
chunks.source: Food is a basic need.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need teachers in a community? A: To educate children.. Teachers educate children.
chunks.source: Teachers educate children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Why should every school have a flag? A: For identity and patriotism.. A flag gives the school identity.
chunks.source: A flag gives the school identity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why some people fail to get their basic needs. A: Poverty.. Poverty stops people getting needs.
chunks.source: Poverty stops people getting needs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Mention any four qualities of a good map. A: Title, key, scale, compass direction.. A good map has a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.
chunks.source: A good map has a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: List down any four groups of people who use a compass. A: Pilots, sailors, soldiers, surveyors.. People who travel or find directions use a compass.
chunks.source: People who travel or find directions use a compass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Identify the four major points of a compass. A: North, South, East, West.. These are the cardinal points of a compass.
chunks.source: These are the cardinal points of a compass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the major latitude marked 0 degrees on a map. A: The Equator.. The Equator is the latitude marked 0 degrees.
chunks.source: The Equator is the latitude marked 0 degrees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Sarah was moving to school in the morning and she saw the sun directly on her face. In which direction was she facing? A: East.. The sun rises in the east in the morning.
chunks.source: The sun rises in the east in the morning.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the country which borders Uganda to the south west. A: Rwanda.. Rwanda borders Uganda to the south west.
chunks.source: Rwanda borders Uganda to the south west.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the district which is found in Lake Victoria. A: Kalangala district.. Kalangala is made of islands in Lake Victoria.
chunks.source: Kalangala is made of islands in Lake Victoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: How many divisions make up Kampala district? A: Five divisions.. Kampala has five divisions.
chunks.source: Kampala has five divisions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Which body is responsible for Kampala district? A: Kampala Capital City Authority (KCCA).. KCCA runs the affairs of Kampala.
chunks.source: KCCA runs the affairs of Kampala.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: What title is given to the political head of Kampala? A: Lord Mayor.. The political head of Kampala is the Lord Mayor.
chunks.source: The political head of Kampala is the Lord Mayor.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name any four municipalities (divisions) of Kampala. A: Kawempe, Makindye, Rubaga, Nakawa.. Kampala has five divisions; any four are correct.
chunks.source: Kampala has five divisions; any four are correct.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the biggest division of Kampala and the most industrialized division. A: Biggest: Kawempe; most industrialized: Nakawa.. Kawempe is the biggest division and Nakawa has many industries.
chunks.source: Kawempe is the biggest division and Nakawa has many industries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name two lakes crossed by the Equator in Uganda. A: Lake Victoria and Lake George.. The Equator crosses Lake Victoria and Lake George.
chunks.source: The Equator crosses Lake Victoria and Lake George.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name any two districts which are crossed by the Equator. A: Mpigi and Masaka.. The Equator passes through Mpigi and Masaka districts.
chunks.source: The Equator passes through Mpigi and Masaka districts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name any three small towns found in Kampala. A: Bwaise, Katwe, Ntinda.. Kampala has small towns like Bwaise, Katwe and Ntinda.
chunks.source: Kampala has small towns like Bwaise, Katwe and Ntinda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the drawing of an object as seen from aside? A: A picture.. A picture shows an object as seen from the side.
chunks.source: A picture shows an object as seen from the side.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: In which direction is the sun in the evening? A: In the west.. The sun sets in the west in the evening.
chunks.source: The sun sets in the west in the evening.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a semi-cardinal point on a compass. A: North East.. North East is a semi-cardinal point.
chunks.source: North East is a semi-cardinal point.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Give any one cardinal point of a compass. A: North.. North is a cardinal point.
chunks.source: North is a cardinal point.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Mention the element of a map that helps us to understand it. A: The key.. The key explains the map.
chunks.source: The key explains the map.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the map symbol drawn below: 0 10 km 20 km. A: The scale.. That symbol is the scale of the map.
chunks.source: That symbol is the scale of the map.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: How is a picture similar to a map? A: Both are drawings.. Pictures and maps are both drawings.
chunks.source: Pictures and maps are both drawings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Give one element of a good map. A: A title.. A title is an element of a good map.
chunks.source: A title is an element of a good map.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Our District in Uganda
chunks.text: Q: Name the capital city of Uganda. A: Kampala.. Kampala is the capital of Uganda.
chunks.source: Kampala is the capital of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any four examples of physical features in your district. A: Hills, mountains, lakes, rivers.. Physical features include hills, mountains, lakes and rivers.
chunks.source: Physical features include hills, mountains, lakes and rivers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any two economic activities carried out on plateau land. A: Crop growing and animal grazing.. Flat plateau land is good for farming and grazing.
chunks.source: Flat plateau land is good for farming and grazing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any two lakes found in Kampala district. A: Lake Victoria and Kabaka's lake.. Kampala has Lake Victoria and the man-made Kabaka's lake.
chunks.source: Kampala has Lake Victoria and the man-made Kabaka's lake.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which man-made lake is found in Kampala? A: Kabaka's lake.. Kabaka's lake was dug by the Kabaka's men.
chunks.source: Kabaka's lake was dug by the Kabaka's men.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two problems faced by lakes and rivers. A: Pollution and silting.. Lakes and rivers suffer from pollution and silting.
chunks.source: Lakes and rivers suffer from pollution and silting.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'shaped like a circle'? A: round. shaped like a circle — that is 'round'.
chunks.source: shaped like a circle — that is 'round'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'soft' mean? A: easy to press. 'soft' means easy to press.
chunks.source: 'soft' means easy to press.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'tall' mean? A: high in height. 'tall' means high in height.
chunks.source: 'tall' means high in height.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'oval' mean? A: egg shaped. 'oval' means egg shaped.
chunks.source: 'oval' means egg shaped.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'having great length'? A: long. having great length — that is 'long'.
chunks.source: having great length — that is 'long'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'colour' mean? A: the hue of something. 'colour' means the hue of something.
chunks.source: 'colour' means the hue of something.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: The book is ___. A: rectangular. The word is 'rectangular': The book is rectangular.
chunks.source: The word is 'rectangular': The book is rectangular.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'small in height'? A: short. small in height — that is 'short'.
chunks.source: small in height — that is 'short'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'even surface'? A: smooth. even surface — that is 'smooth'.
chunks.source: even surface — that is 'smooth'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: The shirt has a bright ___. A: colour. The word is 'colour': The shirt has a bright colour.
chunks.source: The word is 'colour': The shirt has a bright colour.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'smooth' mean? A: even surface. 'smooth' means even surface.
chunks.source: 'smooth' means even surface.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'darkest colour'? A: black. darkest colour — that is 'black'.
chunks.source: darkest colour — that is 'black'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'kind' mean? A: nice, caring. 'kind' means nice, caring.
chunks.source: 'kind' means nice, caring.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: She looks ___. A: smart. The word is 'smart': She looks smart.
chunks.source: The word is 'smart': She looks smart.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: He is ___. A: kind. The word is 'kind': He is kind.
chunks.source: The word is 'kind': He is kind.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'easy to press'? A: soft. easy to press — that is 'soft'.
chunks.source: easy to press — that is 'soft'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: The soil is ___. A: brown. The word is 'brown': The soil is brown.
chunks.source: The word is 'brown': The soil is brown.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'round' mean? A: shaped like a circle. 'round' means shaped like a circle.
chunks.source: 'round' means shaped like a circle.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'hard' mean? A: firm, not soft. 'hard' means firm, not soft.
chunks.source: 'hard' means firm, not soft.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: The rock is ___. A: hard. The word is 'hard': The rock is hard.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: anitas uncle has left for nairobi ___ A: Anita's uncle has left for Nairobi.. Names of people and places begin with capital letters. Use an apostrophe for possession: Anita's.
chunks.source: Names of people and places begin with capital letters. Use an apostrophe for possession: Anita's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: tracy joan and mercy visited queen Elizabeth national park ___ A: Tracy, Joan and Mercy visited Queen Elizabeth National Park.. Put commas between names in a list. Capitalize names of people and parks.
chunks.source: Put commas between names in a list. Capitalize names of people and parks.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: this is the teachers desk it is not marias ___ A: This is the teacher's desk; it is not Maria's.. Start with a capital letter. Use apostrophes for possession: teacher's, Maria's.
chunks.source: Start with a capital letter. Use apostrophes for possession: teacher's, Maria's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: why did you dodge my lesson the teacher asked her ___ A: 'Why did you dodge my lesson?' the teacher asked her.. A direct question goes inside quotation marks and ends with a question mark.
chunks.source: A direct question goes inside quotation marks and ends with a question mark.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: Paul said i am going to study very hard this year ___ A: Paul said, "I am going to study very hard this year.". Put a comma after 'said' and the spoken words inside quotation marks.
chunks.source: Put a comma after 'said' and the spoken words inside quotation marks.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly? A: Our teacher will wed next Friday.. Sentences begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. Days of the week are capitalized.
chunks.source: Sentences begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. Days of the week are capitalized.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: you shouldn't behave like that ___ A: You shouldn't behave like that.. Begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. shouldn't already has its apostrophe.
chunks.source: Begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. shouldn't already has its apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: why have you hidden toms shirt ___ A: Why have you hidden Tom's shirt?. It is a question, so end with a question mark. Tom's needs an apostrophe.
chunks.source: It is a question, so end with a question mark. Tom's needs an apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: the childrens exercise books are being marked by mr tumbo ___ A: The children's exercise books are being marked by Mr. Tumbo.. Capitalize the first word. children's needs an apostrophe. Mr. has a full stop.
chunks.source: Capitalize the first word. children's needs an apostrophe. Mr. has a full stop.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: The movie we watched yesterday is known as home alone ___ A: The movie we watched yesterday is known as "Home Alone".. Titles of movies begin with capital letters and go inside quotation marks.
chunks.source: Titles of movies begin with capital letters and go inside quotation marks.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: Have you seen Hillarys new bicycle ___ A: Have you seen Hillary's new bicycle?. Hillary's needs an apostrophe for possession. It is a question.
chunks.source: Hillary's needs an apostrophe for possession. It is a question.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: You wont watch TV if you dont complete the homework ___ A: You won't watch TV if you don't complete the homework.. won't and don't need apostrophes where letters are missing.
chunks.source: won't and don't need apostrophes where letters are missing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: We always pray in Jesus name ___ A: We always pray in Jesus' name.. For names ending in s, add only an apostrophe: Jesus'.
chunks.source: For names ending in s, add only an apostrophe: Jesus'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: The name of Mrs Musoke dog was micky ___ A: The name of Mrs. Musoke's dog was Micky.. Mrs. takes a full stop. Musoke's needs an apostrophe. Pet names are capitalized.
chunks.source: Mrs. takes a full stop. Musoke's needs an apostrophe. Pet names are capitalized.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: I cant live without you ___ A: I can't live without you.. can't needs an apostrophe. Begin with a capital I and end with a full stop.
chunks.source: can't needs an apostrophe. Begin with a capital I and end with a full stop.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which sentences are punctuated correctly? (Choose all that apply) A: Anita's uncle has left for Nairobi., Have you seen Hillary's new bicycle?. Correct sentences begin with capitals, use apostrophes for possession, and end properly.
chunks.source: Correct sentences begin with capitals, use apostrophes for possession, and end properly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': What ___ ugly man he is! A: an. 'an' is used before words that begin with a vowel sound, like 'ugly'.
chunks.source: 'an' is used before words that begin with a vowel sound, like 'ugly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I eat ___ apple every day. A: an. 'an' comes before vowel sounds. 'apple' begins with a vowel sound.
chunks.source: 'an' comes before vowel sounds. 'apple' begins with a vowel sound.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': ___ blanket is made of wool. A: A. 'A' is used to talk about any one thing of its kind.
chunks.source: 'A' is used to talk about any one thing of its kind.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ___ Nile is the longest river in Africa. A: the. 'the' is used with names of rivers, like the Nile.
chunks.source: 'the' is used with names of rivers, like the Nile.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': We shall finish the work in less than ___ hour. A: an. 'hour' begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'hour' begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Kampala is ___ capital city of Uganda. A: the. 'the' is used because there is only one capital city.
chunks.source: 'the' is used because there is only one capital city.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': It was ___ unwise decision to take that route. A: an. 'unwise' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'unwise' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which is ___ oldest university in East Africa? A: the. 'the' is used with superlatives like 'oldest'.
chunks.source: 'the' is used with superlatives like 'oldest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': ___ hoe is a very useful garden tool. A: A. We use 'a' to talk about any one hoe in general.
chunks.source: We use 'a' to talk about any one hoe in general.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': Can ___ cock lay ___ egg? A: a, an. 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cock'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'.
chunks.source: 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cock'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ___ elephant is one of ___ biggest animals on land. A: The, the. 'The elephant' names the animal; 'the biggest' is a superlative, so both take 'the'.
chunks.source: 'The elephant' names the animal; 'the biggest' is a superlative, so both take 'the'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': Is seven ___ even number? A: an. 'even' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'even' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': Would you like ___ cup of tea or ___ orange? A: a, an. 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cup'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'orange'.
chunks.source: 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cup'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'orange'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She will either marry ___ European or ___ Egyptian. A: a, an. 'European' begins with a 'y' consonant sound, so 'a'; 'Egyptian' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an'.
chunks.source: 'European' begins with a 'y' consonant sound, so 'a'; 'Egyptian' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': I prefer ___ egg to ___ samosa. A: an, a. 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'; 'a' before the consonant sound in 'samosa'.
chunks.source: 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'; 'a' before the consonant sound in 'samosa'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Sort these phrases by the correct article. A: a: a cup,a European,a blanket; an: an apple,an hour,an egg. 'a' before consonant sounds; 'an' before vowel sounds. 'European' begins with a 'y' sound.
chunks.source: 'a' before consonant sounds; 'an' before vowel sounds. 'European' begins with a 'y' sound.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: True or False: We say 'an university' because 'u' is a vowel. A: False. We say 'a university' because it begins with a 'y' consonant sound.
chunks.source: We say 'a university' because it begins with a 'y' consonant sound.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: radio ___ A: radios. Words ending in a vowel + o simply add -s: radio -> radios.
chunks.source: Words ending in a vowel + o simply add -s: radio -> radios.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: piano ___ A: pianos. Words ending in a vowel + o simply add -s: piano -> pianos.
chunks.source: Words ending in a vowel + o simply add -s: piano -> pianos.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the plural of 'leaf'? A: leaves. Nouns ending in -f or -fe change to -ves: leaf -> leaves.
chunks.source: Nouns ending in -f or -fe change to -ves: leaf -> leaves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: shelf ___ A: shelves. Nouns ending in -f change to -ves: shelf -> shelves.
chunks.source: Nouns ending in -f change to -ves: shelf -> shelves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: guest-of-honour ___ A: guests-of-honour. In compound nouns, the main word takes the plural: guests-of-honour.
chunks.source: In compound nouns, the main word takes the plural: guests-of-honour.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: a group of flowers ___ A: bouquet. A group of flowers held together is called a bouquet.
chunks.source: A group of flowers held together is called a bouquet.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A group of thieves is called a: A: gang. A group of thieves or robbers is called a gang.
chunks.source: A group of thieves or robbers is called a gang.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: the people watching a game ___ A: spectators. People who watch a game or match are called spectators.
chunks.source: People who watch a game or match are called spectators.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: the people walking on foot ___ A: pedestrians. People walking on foot, not in a vehicle, are pedestrians.
chunks.source: People walking on foot, not in a vehicle, are pedestrians.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: books, papers, pens, pencils, files and rulers ___ A: stationery. Writing materials like pens, paper and books are called stationery.
chunks.source: Writing materials like pens, paper and books are called stationery.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct form: His ___ was so clear that everyone understood. (explain) ___ A: explanation. The noun form of 'explain' is 'explanation'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'explain' is 'explanation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct form: He went out without getting ___ from the teacher. (permit) ___ A: permission. The noun form of 'permit' is 'permission'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'permit' is 'permission'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct form: The little girl made a very wise ___. (decide) ___ A: decision. The noun form of 'decide' is 'decision'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'decide' is 'decision'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The old man died of ___. (hungry) A: hunger. The noun form of 'hungry' is 'hunger'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'hungry' is 'hunger'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct form: There is widespread ___ in this country. (poor) ___ A: poverty. The noun form of 'poor' is 'poverty'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'poor' is 'poverty'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Sort these nouns by how they form their plural. A: add -s: radios,pianos; change -f to -ves: leaves,shelves; plural in the middle: guests-of-honour,passers-by. radio/piano add -s; leaf/shelf change -f to -ves; compound nouns pluralize the main word.
chunks.source: radio/piano add -s; leaf/shelf change -f to -ves; compound nouns pluralize the main word.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: The pupils ___ classes daily. (attend) ___ A: attend. With 'they' we use the base verb: attend.
chunks.source: With 'they' we use the base verb: attend.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My father ___ me to school every day. (drive) A: drives. With he/she/it we add -s: drives.
chunks.source: With he/she/it we add -s: drives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: I ___ posho to rice. (prefer) ___ A: prefer. With 'I' we use the base verb: prefer.
chunks.source: With 'I' we use the base verb: prefer.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Alice ___ her bag to school every day. (carry) A: carries. Verbs ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: carries.
chunks.source: Verbs ending in consonant + y change y to -ies: carries.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: She ___ us English every Friday. (teach) ___ A: teaches. With she we add -es after ch: teaches.
chunks.source: With she we add -es after ch: teaches.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: The priest preaches to the congregation every morning. ___ A: Does the priest preach to the congregation every morning?. Use 'Does' with singular subjects and return the verb to base form: preach.
chunks.source: Use 'Does' with singular subjects and return the verb to base form: preach.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: Those ladies dress decently. ___ A: Do those ladies dress decently?. Use 'Do' with plural subjects.
chunks.source: Use 'Do' with plural subjects.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: The maid feeds the baby. ___ A: Does the maid feed the baby?. Use 'Does' and change 'feeds' back to 'feed'.
chunks.source: Use 'Does' and change 'feeds' back to 'feed'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: True or False: 'Do Lillian and Ella plays netball?' is correct. A: False. With 'Do' the verb stays in base form: 'Do Lillian and Ella play netball?'
chunks.source: With 'Do' the verb stays in base form: 'Do Lillian and Ella play netball?'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: Becky revises her notes every week. ___ A: Does Becky revise her notes every week?. Use 'Does' and change 'revises' to 'revise'.
chunks.source: Use 'Does' and change 'revises' to 'revise'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: Ezra buys milk from the dairy, ___? ___ A: doesn't he. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: doesn't he?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: doesn't he?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: The children fetch water every weekend, ___? ___ A: don't they. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: don't they?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: don't they?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: My father pays our school fees, ___? ___ A: doesn't he. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: doesn't he?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: doesn't he?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The market vendors don't sell clothes, ___? A: do they. A negative sentence takes a positive tag: do they?
chunks.source: A negative sentence takes a positive tag: do they?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: Our teacher doesn't come on Saturday, ___? ___ A: does he. A negative sentence takes a positive tag: does he?
chunks.source: A negative sentence takes a positive tag: does he?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: I ___ my notes now. (revise) ___ A: am revising. Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing. With 'I' use 'am revising'.
chunks.source: Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing. With 'I' use 'am revising'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He ___ the car in the garage. (park) A: is parking. With 'he' use 'is' + verb-ing: is parking.
chunks.source: With 'he' use 'is' + verb-ing: is parking.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: The mechanic ___ the bicycle. (repair) ___ A: is repairing. Use 'is repairing' for an action happening now.
chunks.source: Use 'is repairing' for an action happening now.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Our teacher ___ a meeting now. (hold) ___ A: is holding. 'hold' doubles the 'd' before -ing: holding. Our teacher = is holding.
chunks.source: 'hold' doubles the 'd' before -ing: holding. Our teacher = is holding.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: The pilot ___ the aeroplane. (fly) ___ A: is flying. With 'the pilot' use 'is flying'.
chunks.source: With 'the pilot' use 'is flying'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: She is preparing breakfast. ___ A: Is she preparing breakfast?. Swap the subject and the helping verb: Is she...?
chunks.source: Swap the subject and the helping verb: Is she...?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: True or False: 'Are the babies crying?' is the correct question form of 'The babies are crying.' A: True. Yes. Swap 'are' and the subject: Are the babies crying?
chunks.source: Yes. Swap 'are' and the subject: Are the babies crying?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: Hannah is wearing a blue dress. ___ A: Is Hannah wearing a blue dress?. Move 'is' before the subject: Is Hannah...?
chunks.source: Move 'is' before the subject: Is Hannah...?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: Charles is not driving a car. ___ A: Is Charles driving a car?. In questions we usually drop 'not': Is Charles driving a car?
chunks.source: In questions we usually drop 'not': Is Charles driving a car?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: They are sowing seeds, ___? ___ A: aren't they. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: aren't they?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: aren't they?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The teacher is not coming, ___? A: is he. A negative sentence takes a positive tag: is he?
chunks.source: A negative sentence takes a positive tag: is he?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: I am going to church today, ___? ___ A: aren't I. 'I am' takes the special tag 'aren't I'.
chunks.source: 'I am' takes the special tag 'aren't I'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: It is raining now, ___? ___ A: isn't it. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: isn't it?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: isn't it?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: She ___ my food. (eat) ___ A: has eaten. Present perfect: has/have + past participle. She has eaten.
chunks.source: Present perfect: has/have + past participle. She has eaten.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The boys ___ their books. (take) A: have taken. With 'they' use 'have' + past participle: have taken.
chunks.source: With 'they' use 'have' + past participle: have taken.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Anita ___ the compound. (sweep) ___ A: has swept. Anita = she: has swept.
chunks.source: Anita = she: has swept.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: John ___ his father's property. (sell) ___ A: has sold. John = he: has sold.
chunks.source: John = he: has sold.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: I ___ a snake under my bed. (see) ___ A: have seen. With 'I' use 'have seen'.
chunks.source: With 'I' use 'have seen'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: They have bought a big piece of land. ___ A: Have they bought a big piece of land?. Move 'have' before the subject.
chunks.source: Move 'have' before the subject.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: The maid has not fed the baby. ___ A: Has the maid fed the baby?. Move 'has' to the front and drop 'not'.
chunks.source: Move 'has' to the front and drop 'not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: The little boy has broken the cup. ___ A: Has the little boy broken the cup?. Move 'has' before the subject.
chunks.source: Move 'has' before the subject.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: The baby has woken up, ___? ___ A: hasn't it. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: hasn't it?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: hasn't it?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Timothy has not yet arrived, ___? A: has he. A negative sentence takes a positive tag: has he?
chunks.source: A negative sentence takes a positive tag: has he?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: My friends have visited me, ___? ___ A: haven't they. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: haven't they?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: haven't they?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: He ___ singing to dancing. (prefer) ___ A: preferred. Past simple of 'prefer' doubles the 'r': preferred.
chunks.source: Past simple of 'prefer' doubles the 'r': preferred.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Milly ___ a new house. (buy) A: bought. 'buy' is irregular: buy -> bought.
chunks.source: 'buy' is irregular: buy -> bought.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: My balloon ___ last Friday. (burst) ___ A: burst. 'burst' stays the same in the past: burst.
chunks.source: 'burst' stays the same in the past: burst.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: I ___ a thief last night. (see) ___ A: saw. Past of 'see' is 'saw'.
chunks.source: Past of 'see' is 'saw'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Have you ___ your books? (keep) A: kept. After 'have' use the past participle: kept.
chunks.source: After 'have' use the past participle: kept.

chunks.subject: English
