chunks.text: Q: Change to negative: We went with him to the party last Saturday. ___ A: We did not go with him to the party last Saturday.. Use 'did not' + base verb: did not go.
chunks.source: Use 'did not' + base verb: did not go.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to negative: Maria gave me a notebook. ___ A: Maria did not give me a notebook.. Use 'did not' + base verb: did not give.
chunks.source: Use 'did not' + base verb: did not give.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: True or False: 'Tina did not told me the truth.' is correct. A: False. After 'did not' use the base verb: 'Tina did not tell me the truth.'
chunks.source: After 'did not' use the base verb: 'Tina did not tell me the truth.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to negative: I lent him some money. ___ A: I did not lend him any money.. Use 'did not lend'; 'some' becomes 'any' in negatives.
chunks.source: Use 'did not lend'; 'some' becomes 'any' in negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: We read a novel last week. ___ A: Did we read a novel last week?. Start with 'Did' and use the base verb 'read'.
chunks.source: Start with 'Did' and use the base verb 'read'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: He forgot to hand in his book for marking. ___ A: Did he forget to hand in his book for marking?. Start with 'Did' and use 'forget'.
chunks.source: Start with 'Did' and use 'forget'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: She bought a new car last month. ___ A: Did she buy a new car last month?. Start with 'Did' and change 'bought' back to 'buy'.
chunks.source: Start with 'Did' and change 'bought' back to 'buy'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: They began the exercise in the morning. ___ A: Did they begin the exercise in the morning?. Start with 'Did'; 'began' returns to 'begin'.
chunks.source: Start with 'Did'; 'began' returns to 'begin'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Mary was ___ a novel. (read) ___ A: reading. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing: was reading.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing: was reading.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Alice ___ with her friends when the teacher called her. (play) A: was playing. Alice = she: was playing.
chunks.source: Alice = she: was playing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: As I ___ through the bush, I stepped on a snake. (walk) ___ A: was walking. With 'I' use 'was walking'.
chunks.source: With 'I' use 'was walking'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: I fell down while I ___ to school. (run) ___ A: was running. 'run' doubles the 'n': was running.
chunks.source: 'run' doubles the 'n': was running.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Ceasar ___ a bicycle when I met him. (ride) ___ A: was riding. Ceasar = he: was riding.
chunks.source: Ceasar = he: was riding.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: Janat was cleaning the house when the visitors came. ___ A: Was Janat cleaning the house when the visitors came?. Move 'was' before the subject.
chunks.source: Move 'was' before the subject.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: Were the girls decorating the room. ___ A: Were the girls decorating the room?. It is already a question; end with a question mark: Were the girls decorating the room?
chunks.source: It is already a question; end with a question mark: Were the girls decorating the room?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: True or False: 'Was Tina sleeping when I arrived?' is the correct question form. A: True. Yes. Move 'was' before the subject: Was Tina sleeping...?
chunks.source: Yes. Move 'was' before the subject: Was Tina sleeping...?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: The boys were watching a movie. ___ A: Were the boys watching a movie?. Move 'were' before the subject.
chunks.source: Move 'were' before the subject.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: Our teachers were not present. ___ A: Were our teachers present?. Move 'were' to the front and drop 'not'.
chunks.source: Move 'were' to the front and drop 'not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: They go to the gym almost ___ . (day) ___ A: daily. 'day' becomes the adverb 'daily'.
chunks.source: 'day' becomes the adverb 'daily'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why are you walking ___? (slow) A: slowly. Add -ly to the adjective: slowly.
chunks.source: Add -ly to the adjective: slowly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: He treated the little boy ___ . (cruel) ___ A: cruelly. 'cruel' becomes 'cruelly' (y changes to i before -ly).
chunks.source: 'cruel' becomes 'cruelly' (y changes to i before -ly).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: She ___ walked through the forest at night. (courage) ___ A: courageously. 'courage' becomes 'courageously'.
chunks.source: 'courage' becomes 'courageously'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Maria always takes her meals ___. (hurry) A: hurriedly. 'hurry' becomes 'hurriedly' (y changes to i).
chunks.source: 'hurry' becomes 'hurriedly' (y changes to i).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: We ___ said our prayers before going to bed. (quiet) ___ A: quietly. 'quiet' becomes 'quietly'.
chunks.source: 'quiet' becomes 'quietly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: We visit the zoo ___ a month. (two) ___ A: twice. 'two' becomes 'twice' for times.
chunks.source: 'two' becomes 'twice' for times.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our football team ___ wins the trophy. (occasion) A: occasionally. 'occasion' becomes 'occasionally'.
chunks.source: 'occasion' becomes 'occasionally'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: Christians go to church ___ a week. (one) ___ A: once. 'one' becomes 'once' for times.
chunks.source: 'one' becomes 'once' for times.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: The visitors were ___ welcomed. (warm) ___ A: warmly. 'warm' becomes 'warmly'.
chunks.source: 'warm' becomes 'warmly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: True or False: 'It has been raining heavy since last night.' is correct. A: False. We need the adverb 'heavily': 'It has been raining heavily since last night.'
chunks.source: We need the adverb 'heavily': 'It has been raining heavily since last night.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: The lousy boy has ___ written his work. (careless) ___ A: carelessly. 'careless' becomes 'carelessly'.
chunks.source: 'careless' becomes 'carelessly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: He entered the room ___ and took our toys. (steal) ___ A: stealthily. 'steal' gives the adverb 'stealthily' (quietly and secretly).
chunks.source: 'steal' gives the adverb 'stealthily' (quietly and secretly).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: Our teachers always advise us to dress ___. (decent) ___ A: decently. 'decent' becomes 'decently'.
chunks.source: 'decent' becomes 'decently'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: All the pupils were ___ involved in the exercise. (active) A: actively. 'active' becomes 'actively'.
chunks.source: 'active' becomes 'actively'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which of these words are adverbs? (Choose all that apply) A: slowly, quietly, heavily. Adverbs often end in -ly: slowly, quietly, heavily.
chunks.source: Adverbs often end in -ly: slowly, quietly, heavily.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: junior ___ A: senior. 'junior' and 'senior' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'junior' and 'senior' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: modern ___ A: ancient. 'modern' and 'ancient' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'modern' and 'ancient' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the opposite of 'literate'? A: illiterate. Add the prefix 'il-': illiterate.
chunks.source: Add the prefix 'il-': illiterate.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: possible ___ A: impossible. Add the prefix 'im-': impossible.
chunks.source: Add the prefix 'im-': impossible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: host ___ A: guest. The host invites; the guest is invited.
chunks.source: The host invites; the guest is invited.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the opposite of 'bachelor'? A: spinster. A bachelor is an unmarried man; a spinster is an unmarried woman.
chunks.source: A bachelor is an unmarried man; a spinster is an unmarried woman.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: busy ___ A: idle. 'busy' and 'idle' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'busy' and 'idle' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: wild ___ A: tame. A wild animal lives freely; a tame one is gentle with people.
chunks.source: A wild animal lives freely; a tame one is gentle with people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each word with its opposite. A: junior: senior; modern: ancient; literate: illiterate; possible: impossible; host: guest; bachelor: spinster; busy: idle; wild: tame. Opposites: junior-senior, modern-ancient, literate-illiterate, possible-impossible, host-guest, bachelor-spinster, busy-idle, wild-tame.
chunks.source: Opposites: junior-senior, modern-ancient, literate-illiterate, possible-impossible, host-guest, bachelor-spinster, busy-idle, wild-tame.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'absence': His absence at the party was a misfortune. ___ A: presence. 'absence' and 'presence' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'absence' and 'presence' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'strong': The strong man pulled me. ___ A: weak. 'strong' and 'weak' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'strong' and 'weak' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They reached before dawn. The opposite of 'dawn' is: A: dusk. Dawn is sunrise; dusk is sunset.
chunks.source: Dawn is sunrise; dusk is sunset.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'princess': The princess visited our school. ___ A: prince. 'princess' and 'prince' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'princess' and 'prince' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'nephews': I don't have any nephews. ___ A: nieces. Nephews are sons of siblings; nieces are daughters.
chunks.source: Nephews are sons of siblings; nieces are daughters.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each word with its opposite. A: absence: presence; strong: weak; dawn: dusk; princess: prince; active: passive; cruel: kind. Opposites: absence-presence, strong-weak, dawn-dusk, princess-prince, active-passive, cruel-kind.
chunks.source: Opposites: absence-presence, strong-weak, dawn-dusk, princess-prince, active-passive, cruel-kind.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'landlord': Have you talked to the landlord? ___ A: tenant. The landlord owns the house; the tenant rents it.
chunks.source: The landlord owns the house; the tenant rents it.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'obedient': The obedient pupils will be rewarded. ___ A: disobedient. Add the prefix 'dis-': disobedient.
chunks.source: Add the prefix 'dis-': disobedient.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'heir': He has not yet chosen an heir. ___ A: heiress. An heir is male; an heiress is female.
chunks.source: An heir is male; an heiress is female.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'because': Rebecca is beautiful. She won the beauty contest. ___ A: Rebecca won the beauty contest because she is beautiful.. 'because' gives the reason.
chunks.source: 'because' gives the reason.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'and': Jesca did not pass the test. Elina did not pass the test. ___ A: Jesca and Elina did not pass the test.. 'and' joins two similar ideas.
chunks.source: 'and' joins two similar ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'either...or': You can hand in your work today. You can hand in your work tomorrow. ___ A: You can hand in your work either today or tomorrow.. 'either...or' shows a choice.
chunks.source: 'either...or' shows a choice.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'Either': Moses is allowed to come in. Simon is allowed to come in. ___ A: Either Moses or Simon is allowed to come in.. Begin: Either Moses or Simon...
chunks.source: Begin: Either Moses or Simon...

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'Neither': Sarah does not eat meat every day. Janet does not eat meat every day. ___ A: Neither Sarah nor Janet eats meat every day.. 'Neither...nor' joins two negatives; the verb becomes singular: eats.
chunks.source: 'Neither...nor' joins two negatives; the verb becomes singular: eats.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Faridah is very hardworking. All teachers like her. (Join with 'so...that') A: Faridah is so hardworking that all teachers like her.. The pattern is 'so + adjective + that'.
chunks.source: The pattern is 'so + adjective + that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'too...to': The water is very dirty. We cannot drink it. ___ A: The water is too dirty to drink.. 'too...to' means more than enough: too dirty to drink.
chunks.source: 'too...to' means more than enough: too dirty to drink.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'Although': Mr. Mate is a mechanic but he cannot drive a lorry. ___ A: Although Mr. Mate is a mechanic, he cannot drive a lorry.. 'Although' begins the surprising fact.
chunks.source: 'Although' begins the surprising fact.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'although': She won the race. She was not given a prize. ___ A: She won the race although she was not given a prize.. 'although' joins a surprising contrast.
chunks.source: 'although' joins a surprising contrast.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'prefer': I like reading newspapers more than novels. ___ A: I prefer reading newspapers to novels.. 'prefer X to Y' is the pattern.
chunks.source: 'prefer X to Y' is the pattern.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Janet was reading the Bible as Jona was revising his notes. (Begin with 'While') A: While Janet was reading the Bible, Jona was revising his notes.. 'While' begins the longer background action.
chunks.source: 'While' begins the longer background action.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'than': I prefer travelling to watching movies. ___ A: I like travelling more than watching movies.. 'prefer X to Y' = 'like X more than Y'.
chunks.source: 'prefer X to Y' = 'like X more than Y'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'When': As Jolly was laughing, a fly flew into her mouth. ___ A: When Jolly was laughing, a fly flew into her mouth.. 'When' can replace 'As' here.
chunks.source: 'When' can replace 'As' here.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'as': Kintu was slashing the compound. Nakintu was sweeping. ___ A: Kintu was slashing the compound as Nakintu was sweeping.. 'as' joins two actions happening together.
chunks.source: 'as' joins two actions happening together.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'As': The headteacher was addressing us. The sick girl fell down. ___ A: As the headteacher was addressing us, the sick girl fell down.. 'As' begins the background action.
chunks.source: 'As' begins the background action.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'after': Mondo completed the exercise. He went for break. ___ A: Mondo went for break after he completed the exercise.. The first action goes after 'after'.
chunks.source: The first action goes after 'after'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'After': Magezi finished his homework. He went to sleep. ___ A: After Magezi finished his homework, he went to sleep.. 'After' begins with the earlier action.
chunks.source: 'After' begins with the earlier action.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: True or False: 'Neither Sarah nor Janet eats meat.' has the correct verb. A: True. Yes. With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject: eats.
chunks.source: Yes. With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject: eats.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Joan writes so ___ that every pupil in our class admires her. (good) ___ A: well. The adverb form of 'good' is 'well'.
chunks.source: The adverb form of 'good' is 'well'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: The ___ of the headmaster surprised every child in the school compound. (arrive) ___ A: arrival. The noun form of 'arrive' is 'arrival'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'arrive' is 'arrival'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: We are ___ on the verandah to wait for the weather to clear. (sit) ___ A: sitting. Present continuous: are + sitting.
chunks.source: Present continuous: are + sitting.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Most children in this school do not speak local languages because the parents have not helped ___. (they) ___ A: them. The object form of 'they' is 'them'.
chunks.source: The object form of 'they' is 'them'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Rajab was the ___ out of the forty pupils in the class. (twelve) ___ A: twelfth. The ordinal of 'twelve' is 'twelfth'.
chunks.source: The ordinal of 'twelve' is 'twelfth'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Has any teacher taught you about ___ this term? (punctuate) ___ A: punctuation. The noun form of 'punctuate' is 'punctuation'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'punctuate' is 'punctuation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: The driver could not see ___ during the rain. (clear) ___ A: clearly. The adverb form of 'clear' is 'clearly'.
chunks.source: The adverb form of 'clear' is 'clearly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: How many glasses has the child ___? (breake) ___ A: broken. Past participle of 'break' is 'broken'.
chunks.source: Past participle of 'break' is 'broken'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Jacob likes neither sweets ___ biscuits. ___ A: nor. 'neither...nor' is the pair.
chunks.source: 'neither...nor' is the pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: ___ the boys were playing football, the girls were mopping the main hall. ___ A: While. 'While' joins two actions happening at the same time.
chunks.source: 'While' joins two actions happening at the same time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Our teacher is ___ open minded woman. ___ A: an. 'an' before the vowel sound in 'open'.
chunks.source: 'an' before the vowel sound in 'open'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: Reply, replay, repay, pay A: pay, repay, replay, Reply. Compare letter by letter: pay, repay, replay, Reply.
chunks.source: Compare letter by letter: pay, repay, replay, Reply.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: English, China, German, French A: China, English, French, German. Alphabetical: C, E, F, G.
chunks.source: Alphabetical: C, E, F, G.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'nearer': The tourist feared to move nearer the lion in the game reserve. ___ A: farther. 'nearer' and 'farther' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'nearer' and 'farther' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'departure': We must be at the main gate before the departure of the guest of honour. ___ A: arrival. 'departure' and 'arrival' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'departure' and 'arrival' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form a correct sentence: newspaper our every teacher a buys day. ___ A: Our teacher buys a newspaper every day.. Start with the subject: Our teacher...
chunks.source: Start with the subject: Our teacher...

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form a correct sentence: my return story book did not Hilda. ___ A: Hilda did not return my story book.. Start with the subject: Hilda...
chunks.source: Start with the subject: Hilda...

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite giving the plural of 'turkey': The turkey we bought in school should be used for practical lessons. ___ A: The turkeys we bought in school should be used for practical lessons.. turkey -> turkeys.
chunks.source: turkey -> turkeys.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite giving the plural of 'louse': The louse on his head could not allow him to sleep. ___ A: The lice on his head could not allow him to sleep.. louse -> lice (irregular).
chunks.source: louse -> lice (irregular).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: mangoes, oranges, apples, watermelon and pineapples ___ A: fruits. These are all fruits.
chunks.source: These are all fruits.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: people who grow crops and look after animals ___ A: farmers. People who grow crops and keep animals are farmers.
chunks.source: People who grow crops and keep animals are farmers.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'always': We usually travel to Ntawo by bus. ___ A: We always travel to Ntawo by bus.. Replace 'usually' with 'always'.
chunks.source: Replace 'usually' with 'always'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'Although': The P.2 pupils did not have rafia-skirts but they danced very well. ___ A: Although the P.2 pupils did not have rafia-skirts, they danced very well.. 'Although' begins the surprising fact.
chunks.source: 'Although' begins the surprising fact.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'too...to': The shopkeeper was very busy. He could not attend to me. ___ A: The shopkeeper was too busy to attend to me.. 'too...to' joins the two ideas.
chunks.source: 'too...to' joins the two ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'any': There is some food in the cooking pot. ___ A: There is not any food in the cooking pot.. 'some' becomes 'any' in negatives.
chunks.source: 'some' becomes 'any' in negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'because': My mother wanted to go out of the house. My mother needed an umbrella. ___ A: My mother needed an umbrella because she wanted to go out of the house.. 'because' gives the reason.
chunks.source: 'because' gives the reason.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'either': I will drink soda or mineral water. ___ A: I will drink either soda or mineral water.. 'either...or' shows a choice.
chunks.source: 'either...or' shows a choice.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'Birds': A bird lives in a nest. ___ A: Birds live in nests.. Make everything plural: Birds live in nests.
chunks.source: Make everything plural: Birds live in nests.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'prefer': Samilla likes local music more than poems. ___ A: Samilla prefers local music to poems.. 'like more than' = 'prefer...to'.
chunks.source: 'like more than' = 'prefer...to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'immediately': We went back home. We planted our seeds. ___ A: Immediately we went back home, we planted our seeds.. 'immediately' joins two quick actions.
chunks.source: 'immediately' joins two quick actions.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'reached': The guest of honour arrived at school very early. ___ A: The guest of honour reached school very early.. 'reached' replaces 'arrived at'.
chunks.source: 'reached' replaces 'arrived at'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'While': The music was playing. The children were dancing. ___ A: While the music was playing, the children were dancing.. 'While' begins the background action.
chunks.source: 'While' begins the background action.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'enough': I am very strong. I can kill a big snake. ___ A: I am strong enough to kill a big snake.. 'enough to' joins the ideas.
chunks.source: 'enough to' joins the ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'in order to': Sean went to the market. He wanted to buy some fruits. ___ A: Sean went to the market in order to buy some fruits.. 'in order to' shows purpose.
chunks.source: 'in order to' shows purpose.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'Both': The class prefect was elected. The assistant was also elected. ___ A: Both the class prefect and the assistant were elected.. 'Both...and' joins two subjects; the verb is plural: were.
chunks.source: 'Both...and' joins two subjects; the verb is plural: were.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Sarah went to hospital in ___ to get treatment. ___ A: order. 'in order to' shows purpose.
chunks.source: 'in order to' shows purpose.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: We ___ been invited to Sweden by our cousins. ___ A: have. Present perfect: have been invited.
chunks.source: Present perfect: have been invited.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Neither Paul ___ Peter went to the garage. ___ A: nor. 'Neither...nor' is the pair.
chunks.source: 'Neither...nor' is the pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Mrs. Kadogo spoke to us ___. (rude) ___ A: rudely. The adverb of 'rude' is 'rudely'.
chunks.source: The adverb of 'rude' is 'rudely'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Sarah received an ___ letter from Joan. (invite) ___ A: invitation. The noun form of 'invite' is 'invitation'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'invite' is 'invitation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Ten ___ were caught stealing cassava. (thief) ___ A: thieves. thief -> thieves.
chunks.source: thief -> thieves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: My grandmother ___ in the bedroom now. (to be) ___ A: is. With 'she' use 'is'.
chunks.source: With 'she' use 'is'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: Zebra, hippo, ape, lion A: ape, hippo, lion, Zebra. Alphabetical: a, h, l, z.
chunks.source: Alphabetical: a, h, l, z.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: community, came, culture, cite A: came, cite, community, culture. ca < ci < co < cu.
chunks.source: ca < ci < co < cu.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: behaviour, belt, begin, before A: before, begin, behaviour, belt. bef < beg < beh < bel.
chunks.source: bef < beg < beh < bel.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite giving the plural of 'tooth': Penny's tooth needed to be removed. ___ A: Penny's teeth needed to be removed.. tooth -> teeth.
chunks.source: tooth -> teeth.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite giving the plural of 'diary': I have lost my diary. ___ A: I have lost my diaries.. diary -> diaries (y to i).
chunks.source: diary -> diaries (y to i).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite giving the plural of 'luggage': Ben was told to off load the entire luggage. ___ A: Ben was told to off load the entire luggage.. 'luggage' has no plural; it stays the same.
chunks.source: 'luggage' has no plural; it stays the same.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'obedient': The obedient girl was given an award. ___ A: disobedient. Add the prefix 'dis-': disobedient.
chunks.source: Add the prefix 'dis-': disobedient.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'badly': Her letters are badly formed. ___ A: well. 'badly' and 'well' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'badly' and 'well' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: members who attended the church service ___ A: congregation. Church members at a service are a congregation.
chunks.source: Church members at a service are a congregation.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: the three young ducks ___ A: ducklings. Young ducks are ducklings.
chunks.source: Young ducks are ducklings.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: a brother to my father ___ A: uncle. Your father's brother is your uncle.
chunks.source: Your father's brother is your uncle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'in order to': Benabana wants to get treatment. She must go to the hospital. ___ A: Benabana must go to the hospital in order to get treatment.. 'in order to' shows purpose.
chunks.source: 'in order to' shows purpose.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'prefer': Jonathan likes models. Jonathan likes flowers more. ___ A: Jonathan prefers flowers to models.. 'like more than' = 'prefer...to'.
chunks.source: 'like more than' = 'prefer...to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'too...to': The box is very heavy. Musa cannot lift it. ___ A: The box is too heavy for Musa to lift.. 'too...to' joins the ideas.
chunks.source: 'too...to' joins the ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'belong': That is our home. ___ A: That home belongs to us.. 'belongs to' shows ownership.
chunks.source: 'belongs to' shows ownership.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: End with 'did he?': The teacher marked our books, didn't he? ___ A: The teacher did not mark our books, did he?. Change to negative; the tag becomes positive.
chunks.source: Change to negative; the tag becomes positive.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'such...that': Mary is very hardworking. All teachers admire her. ___ A: Mary is such a hardworking girl that all teachers admire her.. 'such a' + adjective + noun + 'that'.
chunks.source: 'such a' + adjective + noun + 'that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'any': There is some water in the tank. ___ A: There is not any water in the tank.. 'some' becomes 'any' in negatives.
chunks.source: 'some' becomes 'any' in negatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'A friend': My friend will visit me in the evening. ___ A: A friend of mine will visit me in the evening.. 'A friend of mine' = my friend.
chunks.source: 'A friend of mine' = my friend.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'because': Atim was happy. She received a prize for being smart all the time. ___ A: Atim was happy because she received a prize for being smart all the time.. 'because' gives the reason.
chunks.source: 'because' gives the reason.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'While': I cut myself as I was digging. ___ A: While I was digging, I cut myself.. 'While' begins the background action.
chunks.source: 'While' begins the background action.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate correctly: have you been to tororo ___ A: Have you been to Tororo?. Capitalize the first word and the place name; end with a question mark.
chunks.source: Capitalize the first word and the place name; end with a question mark.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'but': Baby Yukana fell down. She didn't cry. ___ A: Baby Yukana fell down but she didn't cry.. 'but' joins a contrast.
chunks.source: 'but' joins a contrast.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'and': I bought an envelope. I also bought a stamp. ___ A: I bought an envelope and a stamp.. 'and' joins two things.
chunks.source: 'and' joins two things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Aren't ___ ashamed of behaving badly in public? ___ A: you. 'Aren't you' is the question tag pair.
chunks.source: 'Aren't you' is the question tag pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Our neighbour's son ate ___ apple and sweet bananas at the party. ___ A: an. 'an' before the vowel sound in 'apple'.
chunks.source: 'an' before the vowel sound in 'apple'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: John likes swimming and so ___ Peter. ___ A: does. 'so does Peter' agrees with the first sentence.
chunks.source: 'so does Peter' agrees with the first sentence.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: This jacket is thick ___ to make me warm in this cold weather. ___ A: enough. 'enough to' follows the adjective.
chunks.source: 'enough to' follows the adjective.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: The farmer drove his ___ of cattle to the grazing ground very early in the morning. ___ A: herd. A group of cattle is a herd.
chunks.source: A group of cattle is a herd.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: It is difficult to walk ___ both in the dark and during heavy rain. (quick) ___ A: quickly. The adverb of 'quick' is 'quickly'.
chunks.source: The adverb of 'quick' is 'quickly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Musa always ___ to the radio to get current news. (listen) ___ A: listens. Musa = he: listens.
chunks.source: Musa = he: listens.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: The blind man knocked ___ against the wall while walking out of the main hall. (him) ___ A: himself. The reflexive pronoun of 'him' is 'himself'.
chunks.source: The reflexive pronoun of 'him' is 'himself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: wiper, saddle, brakes, indicator A: brakes, indicator, saddle, wiper. Alphabetical: b, i, s, w.
chunks.source: Alphabetical: b, i, s, w.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in alphabetical order: chief, bigger, travel, luggage A: bigger, chief, luggage, travel. Alphabetical: b, c, l, t.
chunks.source: Alphabetical: b, c, l, t.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange to form a correct sentence: telling at good she story is. ___ A: She is good at telling story.. Start with the subject: She is...
chunks.source: Start with the subject: She is...

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange to form a correct sentence: a helpful and are doctors in teachers community. ___ A: Doctors and teachers are helpful in a community.. Start with the subjects: Doctors and teachers...
chunks.source: Start with the subjects: Doctors and teachers...

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: the people who cannot see ___ A: blind. People who cannot see are blind.
chunks.source: People who cannot see are blind.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: our head of country ___ A: president. The head of a country is the president.
chunks.source: The head of a country is the president.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: cars, buses, taxis and lorries ___ A: vehicles. These are all vehicles.
chunks.source: These are all vehicles.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite giving the plural of 'tyre': The tyre bust due to high speed. ___ A: The tyres bust due to high speed.. tyre -> tyres.
chunks.source: tyre -> tyres.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite giving the plural of 'houses': He sprayed the houses to prevent common diseases. ___ A: He sprayed the houses to prevent common diseases.. 'houses' is already plural.
chunks.source: 'houses' is already plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite giving the plural of 'thief': The notorious thief should be arrested by the police. ___ A: The notorious thieves should be arrested by the police.. thief -> thieves.
chunks.source: thief -> thieves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'too...to': The farmer was weak. He couldn't carry a full bag of maize. ___ A: The farmer was too weak to carry a full bag of maize.. 'too...to' joins the ideas.
chunks.source: 'too...to' joins the ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'in order to': He reads newspapers daily. He wants to get information. ___ A: He reads newspapers daily in order to get information.. 'in order to' shows purpose.
chunks.source: 'in order to' shows purpose.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'as soon as': The visitor sat on a chair. Namuli greeted him. ___ A: As soon as the visitor sat on a chair, Namuli greeted him.. 'as soon as' shows quick sequence.
chunks.source: 'as soon as' shows quick sequence.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'while': The little girl fell sick. She was going to the village. ___ A: The little girl fell sick while she was going to the village.. 'while' joins actions at the same time.
chunks.source: 'while' joins actions at the same time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'because': Bemba needs money. He wants to travel to Arusha. ___ A: Bemba needs money because he wants to travel to Arusha.. 'because' gives the reason.
chunks.source: 'because' gives the reason.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'an': Bitu wrote a very interesting poem. ___ A: Bitu wrote an interesting poem.. 'an' before the vowel sound in 'interesting'.
chunks.source: 'an' before the vowel sound in 'interesting'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'Both': Godfrey is hardworking. Timothy is hardworking. ___ A: Both Godfrey and Timothy are hardworking.. 'Both...and' joins two subjects.
chunks.source: 'Both...and' joins two subjects.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: That phone belongs to him. It is ___. ___ A: his. The possessive pronoun is 'his'.
chunks.source: The possessive pronoun is 'his'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'Although': The weather was very bad but we travelled. ___ A: Although the weather was very bad, we travelled.. 'Although' begins the surprising fact.
chunks.source: 'Although' begins the surprising fact.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'enough to': My son is mature. He can start school. ___ A: My son is mature enough to start school.. 'enough to' joins the ideas.
chunks.source: 'enough to' joins the ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Add the question tag: Peter is a Ugandan, ___? ___ A: isn't he. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: isn't he?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: isn't he?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate correctly: joan lives in nigeria. ___ A: Joan lives in Nigeria.. Capitalize names of people and countries; end with a full stop.
chunks.source: Capitalize names of people and countries; end with a full stop.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who was going to Mityana? A: Kabugo. Kabugo was the one travelling to Mityana.
chunks.source: Kabugo was the one travelling to Mityana.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why was Kabugo going to Mityana? ___ A: To attend an introduction ceremony. He had to attend an introduction ceremony.
chunks.source: He had to attend an introduction ceremony.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The taxi stopped because it got a puncture. A: True. Yes. After 10 km the taxi got a puncture.
chunks.source: Yes. After 10 km the taxi got a puncture.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What did Kabugo borrow for the rest of the journey? ___ A: a bicycle. He borrowed a bicycle.
chunks.source: He borrowed a bicycle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What happened to the bicycle near Mityana town? A: He crashed into a lorry and bent the wheel.. He crashed into the back of a lorry.
chunks.source: He crashed into the back of a lorry.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which radio aired the programme? A: Radio Solo FM 73.3. The notice names Radio Solo FM 73.3.
chunks.source: The notice names Radio Solo FM 73.3.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who presents the last programme? ___ A: Peace. The mid-night caller is by Peace.
chunks.source: The mid-night caller is by Peace.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The Music club night is presented at 7:00 p.m. A: True. Yes, Music club night is at 07:00 p.m. to 08:00 p.m.
chunks.source: Yes, Music club night is at 07:00 p.m. to 08:00 p.m.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What programme does Lubowa Martin present? ___ A: Talk of the Nation. Lubowa Martin presents Talk of the Nation.
chunks.source: Lubowa Martin presents Talk of the Nation.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: At what time is the National News? A: 8:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.. National News by Night Mpora is at 8:00 p.m.
chunks.source: National News by Night Mpora is at 8:00 p.m.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which class visited Mr. Walusimbi's garage? ___ A: Primary Five. The Primary Five pupils visited.
chunks.source: The Primary Five pupils visited.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where is the garage found? A: At Kavule along Kampala-Bombo Road. The garage is at Kavule.
chunks.source: The garage is at Kavule.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a jack used for? ___ A: To hold vehicles while removing flat tyres or changing wheels. A jack holds the vehicle up.
chunks.source: A jack holds the vehicle up.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The first thing the pupils saw at the garage was a jack. A: False. The first thing they saw was a toolbox.
chunks.source: The first thing they saw was a toolbox.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why did the pupils visit the garage? A: To learn about equipment used in vehicle repair. Their aim was to learn.
chunks.source: Their aim was to learn.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is a source of information? A: Newspapers. Newspapers are a great source of information.
chunks.source: Newspapers are a great source of information.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What are people who sell newspapers called? ___ A: vendors. Vendors sell newspapers.
chunks.source: Vendors sell newspapers.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The Observer is published every day. A: False. The Observer is published twice a week.
chunks.source: The Observer is published twice a week.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name one newspaper written in a local language. ___ A: Bukedde. Bukedde, Rupiny and Etop are in local languages.
chunks.source: Bukedde, Rupiny and Etop are in local languages.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where are newspapers mainly sold? A: In urban areas. Newspapers are mainly sold in urban areas.
chunks.source: Newspapers are mainly sold in urban areas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete sensibly: If I were the headteacher, ___. A: I would punish latecomers.. After 'If I were', use 'would': I would...
chunks.source: After 'If I were', use 'would': I would...

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete sensibly: If father gets money, ___. A: he will buy a car.. After 'If + present', use 'will': he will...
chunks.source: After 'If + present', use 'will': he will...

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete sensibly: If aunt comes today, ___. A: we shall be happy.. After 'If + present', use 'shall/will'.
chunks.source: After 'If + present', use 'shall/will'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete sensibly: If I were a nurse, ___. A: I would treat the sick.. After 'If I were', use 'would'.
chunks.source: After 'If I were', use 'would'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete sensibly: If my mother buys a car, ___. A: she will drive us to school.. After 'If + present', use 'will'.
chunks.source: After 'If + present', use 'will'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite beginning with 'If': When I get money, I shall visit my relatives. ___ A: If I get money, I shall visit my relatives.. 'When' becomes 'If'; the rest stays the same.
chunks.source: 'When' becomes 'If'; the rest stays the same.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite beginning with 'If': Father will buy a taxi when he gets money. ___ A: If father gets money, he will buy a taxi.. Begin with the 'if' clause: If father gets money...
chunks.source: Begin with the 'if' clause: If father gets money...

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite beginning with 'If': When you behave well, you will go to heaven. ___ A: If you behave well, you will go to heaven.. 'When' becomes 'If'.
chunks.source: 'When' becomes 'If'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite beginning with 'If': My grandmother will be happy when we visit her. ___ A: If we visit her, my grandmother will be happy.. The condition comes first: If we visit her...
chunks.source: The condition comes first: If we visit her...

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete sensibly: If I were a bird, ___. A: I would fly high in the sky.. After 'If I were', use 'would'.
chunks.source: After 'If I were', use 'would'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete sensibly: If we had an aeroplane, ___. A: we would travel to many countries.. After 'If + past', use 'would'.
chunks.source: After 'If + past', use 'would'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'unless': If I go to the village, I will bring many fruits. ___ A: Unless I go to the village, I will not bring many fruits.. 'Unless' = 'if not': change 'will' to 'will not'.
chunks.source: 'Unless' = 'if not': change 'will' to 'will not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'unless': If you don't share eats, we shall not play with you. ___ A: Unless you share eats, we shall not play with you.. 'Unless you share' = 'if you don't share'.
chunks.source: 'Unless you share' = 'if you don't share'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'unless': If you dodge classes, you will not be promoted. ___ A: Unless you dodge classes, you will be promoted.. Remove both negatives: 'unless' + positive result.
chunks.source: Remove both negatives: 'unless' + positive result.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'unless': If it rains, I will not go to the market. ___ A: Unless it rains, I will go to the market.. 'Unless it rains' = 'if it does not rain'.
chunks.source: 'Unless it rains' = 'if it does not rain'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'unless': If you don't dress smartly, you will not come with us. ___ A: Unless you dress smartly, you will not come with us.. Drop 'don't': Unless you dress smartly...
chunks.source: Drop 'don't': Unless you dress smartly...

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each country with its nationality. A: Uganda: Ugandan; Netherlands: Dutch; China: Chinese; America: American; Kenya: Kenyan; Nigeria: Nigerian; Switzerland: Swiss; Rwanda: Rwandan. Uganda-Ugandan, Netherlands-Dutch, China-Chinese, America-American, Kenya-Kenyan, Nigeria-Nigerian, Switzerland-Swiss, Rwanda-Rwandan.
chunks.source: Uganda-Ugandan, Netherlands-Dutch, China-Chinese, America-American, Kenya-Kenyan, Nigeria-Nigerian, Switzerland-Swiss, Rwanda-Rwandan.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each country with its nationality. A: Ghana: Ghanaian; Germany: German; Portugal: Portuguese; Tanzania: Tanzanian; Senegal: Senegalese. Ghana-Ghanaian, Germany-German, Portugal-Portuguese, Tanzania-Tanzanian, Senegal-Senegalese.
chunks.source: Ghana-Ghanaian, Germany-German, Portugal-Portuguese, Tanzania-Tanzanian, Senegal-Senegalese.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: Uganda -> ___ ___ A: Ugandan. People from Uganda are Ugandans.
chunks.source: People from Uganda are Ugandans.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A person from the Netherlands is: A: Dutch. People from the Netherlands are called Dutch.
chunks.source: People from the Netherlands are called Dutch.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: China -> ___ ___ A: Chinese. People from China are Chinese.
chunks.source: People from China are Chinese.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A person from America is: A: American. People from America are Americans.
chunks.source: People from America are Americans.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: Switzerland -> ___ ___ A: Swiss. People from Switzerland are Swiss.
chunks.source: People from Switzerland are Swiss.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: Portugal -> ___ ___ A: Portuguese. People from Portugal are Portuguese.
chunks.source: People from Portugal are Portuguese.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'for whom': I dug the garden for the lady. The lady did not thank me. ___ A: The lady for whom I dug the garden did not thank me.. Join with 'for whom' in the middle.
chunks.source: Join with 'for whom' in the middle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'whose': That is the man. His wife died in the car accident. ___ A: That is the man whose wife died in the car accident.. 'whose' shows possession.
chunks.source: 'whose' shows possession.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'in which': That is the village. Many people were killed in that village. ___ A: That is the village in which many people were killed.. 'in which' refers to the village.
chunks.source: 'in which' refers to the village.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'where': I do not remember the place. I met the old woman. ___ A: I do not remember the place where I met the old woman.. 'where' refers to a place.
chunks.source: 'where' refers to a place.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The boy stole the food. He has been arrested. (Use 'who') A: The boy who stole the food has been arrested.. 'who' refers to a person doing the action.
chunks.source: 'who' refers to a person doing the action.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'with whom': That is the man. I arrived at school with him. ___ A: That is the man with whom I arrived at school.. 'with whom' refers to the man.
chunks.source: 'with whom' refers to the man.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'in which': That is the house. I sleep in it. ___ A: That is the house in which I sleep.. 'in which' refers to the house.
chunks.source: 'in which' refers to the house.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I met an old lady yesterday. Her bag had been stolen. (Use 'whose') A: I met an old lady yesterday whose bag had been stolen.. 'whose' shows the bag belongs to her.
chunks.source: 'whose' shows the bag belongs to her.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'about whom': This is the teacher. Many books have been written about him. ___ A: This is the teacher about whom many books have been written.. 'about whom' refers to the teacher.
chunks.source: 'about whom' refers to the teacher.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'whom': The doctor travelled with the patient. The patient was yelling loudly. ___ A: The patient whom the doctor travelled with was yelling loudly.. 'whom' refers to the patient receiving the action.
chunks.source: 'whom' refers to the patient receiving the action.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: From ___ bookshop did you buy that book? A: which. 'which' is used for choosing from known things.
chunks.source: 'which' is used for choosing from known things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: That is the man ___ cat was stolen. A: whose. 'whose' shows possession.
chunks.source: 'whose' shows possession.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: May you suggest a day ___ we can meet? A: when. 'when' refers to a day/time.
chunks.source: 'when' refers to a day/time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the name of the school ___ your brother goes to? A: which. 'which' refers to the school.
chunks.source: 'which' refers to the school.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Those are the desks ___ legs broke off. A: whose. 'whose' shows the legs belong to the desks.
chunks.source: 'whose' shows the legs belong to the desks.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct pronoun: That is the teacher ___ teaches us mathematics. ___ A: who. 'who' refers to a person.
chunks.source: 'who' refers to a person.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct pronoun: This is the cow ___ we bought from Kenya. ___ A: which. 'which' refers to an animal.
chunks.source: 'which' refers to an animal.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct pronoun: ___ car was stolen? ___ A: Whose. 'Whose' asks about the owner.
chunks.source: 'Whose' asks about the owner.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is another name for a personal letter? ___ A: a friendly letter. Personal letters are also called friendly letters.
chunks.source: Personal letters are also called friendly letters.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do we write personal letters? A: To tell friends and relatives about good or bad things. We write to share news with friends and relatives.
chunks.source: We write to share news with friends and relatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who is the addressee? ___ A: The person to whom the letter is written. The addressee receives the letter.
chunks.source: The addressee receives the letter.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You should read the letter through before posting it. A: True. Yes, to make sure there is no mistake.
chunks.source: Yes, to make sure there is no mistake.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What should a posted letter bear? A: A postage stamp. All posted letters should bear a postage stamp.
chunks.source: All posted letters should bear a postage stamp.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to passive: Akello learns music. ___ A: Music is learnt by Akello.. Passive: is + past participle + by.
chunks.source: Passive: is + past participle + by.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to passive: Kato plays football. ___ A: Football is played by Kato.. Passive: is played by Kato.
chunks.source: Passive: is played by Kato.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to passive: Lions eat other animals. ___ A: Other animals are eaten by lions.. Plural subject: are eaten.
chunks.source: Plural subject: are eaten.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to passive: I am writing a letter. A: A letter is being written by me.. Present continuous passive: is being + written.
chunks.source: Present continuous passive: is being + written.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to passive: They are carrying firewood. ___ A: Firewood is being carried by them.. Present continuous passive: is being carried.
chunks.source: Present continuous passive: is being carried.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to passive: Moses is repairing a radio. ___ A: A radio is being repaired by Moses.. Present continuous passive: is being repaired.
chunks.source: Present continuous passive: is being repaired.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to passive: They are beating me. ___ A: I am being beaten by them.. 'me' becomes 'I': I am being beaten.
chunks.source: 'me' becomes 'I': I am being beaten.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to passive: He has cleaned the table. A: The table has been cleaned by him.. Present perfect passive: has been cleaned.
chunks.source: Present perfect passive: has been cleaned.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to passive: Ugandans have built nice houses. ___ A: Nice houses have been built by Ugandans.. Present perfect passive: have been built.
chunks.source: Present perfect passive: have been built.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to passive: Mary has written a letter. ___ A: A letter has been written by Mary.. Present perfect passive: has been written.
chunks.source: Present perfect passive: has been written.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to passive: I have broken the cup. ___ A: The cup has been broken by me.. Present perfect passive: has been broken.
chunks.source: Present perfect passive: has been broken.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: True or False: 'A letter is wrote by me.' is the correct passive of 'I write a letter.' A: False. The past participle is 'written': 'A letter is written by me.'
chunks.source: The past participle is 'written': 'A letter is written by me.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which sentences are in the passive voice? (Choose all that apply) A: Music is learnt by Akello., The cup has been broken by me.. Passive voice uses be + past participle: is learnt, has been broken.
chunks.source: Passive voice uses be + past participle: is learnt, has been broken.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who wrote the letter? ___ A: Ninsiima Tracy. The letter is signed Ninsiima Tracy.
chunks.source: The letter is signed Ninsiima Tracy.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How old is the writer? A: Twelve. It is her twelfth birthday party.
chunks.source: It is her twelfth birthday party.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where was the party held? ___ A: At their home at Bugembe. The party was at their home at Bugembe.
chunks.source: The party was at their home at Bugembe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The party began at 7:00 p.m. A: False. The celebrations began at 12:00 p.m.
chunks.source: The celebrations began at 12:00 p.m.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: To whom was the letter written? ___ A: Merisa. The letter begins 'Dear Merisa'.
chunks.source: The letter begins 'Dear Merisa'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: Micheal is the ___ boy in our class. (good) ___ A: best. The superlative of 'good' is 'best'.
chunks.source: The superlative of 'good' is 'best'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: Joseph is ___ than Richard. (heavy) ___ A: heavier. heavy -> heavier (y to i).
chunks.source: heavy -> heavier (y to i).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: The box is ___ than that box. (light) ___ A: lighter. light -> lighter.
chunks.source: light -> lighter.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My house is ___ than yours. (near) A: nearer. near -> nearer.
chunks.source: near -> nearer.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: Which is the ___ building in Nairobi? (tall) ___ A: tallest. The superlative of 'tall' is 'tallest'.
chunks.source: The superlative of 'tall' is 'tallest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: Peter is ___ than George. (weak) ___ A: weaker. weak -> weaker.
chunks.source: weak -> weaker.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: Mary is the ___ girl in our class. (short) ___ A: shortest. The superlative of 'short' is 'shortest'.
chunks.source: The superlative of 'short' is 'shortest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Please give me ___ milk. (much) A: more. The comparative of 'much' is 'more'.
chunks.source: The comparative of 'much' is 'more'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: What is the ___ news? (late) ___ A: latest. The superlative of 'late' is 'latest'.
chunks.source: The superlative of 'late' is 'latest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: I came ___ than you. (early) ___ A: earlier. early -> earlier (y to i).
chunks.source: early -> earlier (y to i).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: He is the ___ of the twins. (old) ___ A: older. With two people, use the comparative: older.
chunks.source: With two people, use the comparative: older.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: This flower is ___ than that flower. (beautiful) A: more beautiful. Long adjectives use 'more': more beautiful.
chunks.source: Long adjectives use 'more': more beautiful.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: His mother is ___ today. (well) ___ A: better. The comparative of 'well' is 'better'.
chunks.source: The comparative of 'well' is 'better'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: James is the ___ of the two boys. (clever) ___ A: cleverer. With two people, use the comparative: cleverer.
chunks.source: With two people, use the comparative: cleverer.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join in order of adjectives: I solved fifteen good numbers. ___ A: I solved fifteen good numbers.. Order: number (fifteen) before opinion (good).
chunks.source: Order: number (fifteen) before opinion (good).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join in order of adjectives: The tree is large. It is green. It is wonderful. It was cut down. ___ A: The wonderful large green tree was cut down.. Order: opinion (wonderful), size (large), colour (green).
chunks.source: Order: opinion (wonderful), size (large), colour (green).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join in order of adjectives: She brought several slim young ignorant black Ugandan children. ___ A: She brought several ignorant slim young black Ugandan children.. Order: number, opinion, size, age, colour, origin.
chunks.source: Order: number, opinion, size, age, colour, origin.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join in order of adjectives: He was given a big new red Indian cotton shirt. ___ A: He was given a big new red Indian cotton shirt.. Order: size, age, colour, origin, material.
chunks.source: Order: size, age, colour, origin, material.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with 'as...as': James is hardworking. Sarah is hardworking. ___ A: James is as hardworking as Sarah.. 'as...as' shows equality.
chunks.source: 'as...as' shows equality.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A bus is fast. A taxi is very fast. The bus is ___ fast ___ the taxi. A: not as, as. 'not as...as' shows the bus is slower.
chunks.source: 'not as...as' shows the bus is slower.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: True or False: 'She is more taller than me.' is correct. A: False. Use one comparative form only: 'She is taller than me.'
chunks.source: Use one comparative form only: 'She is taller than me.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: He will take an oath, ___? ___ A: won't he. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't he?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't he?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: They will fix the poles, ___? ___ A: won't they. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't they?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't they?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: We shall call him, ___? ___ A: shan't we. 'shall' takes 'shan't we'.
chunks.source: 'shall' takes 'shan't we'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: The baby will cry, ___? ___ A: won't it. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't it?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't it?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: I shall go to school, ___? ___ A: shan't I. 'I shall' takes 'shan't I'.
chunks.source: 'I shall' takes 'shan't I'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Luwedde is ___ than Gaberialla. (thin) ___ A: thinner. Short adjectives double the final consonant: thin -> thinner.
chunks.source: Short adjectives double the final consonant: thin -> thinner.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: If I ___ to the radio, I would tell you the whole story. (listen) ___ A: listened. After 'If + past', use 'would': If I listened... I would tell.
chunks.source: After 'If + past', use 'would': If I listened... I would tell.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Tel: ___ A: Telephone. 'Tel.' is short for 'Telephone'.
chunks.source: 'Tel.' is short for 'Telephone'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: I'll ___ A: I will. 'I'll' is the contraction of 'I will'.
chunks.source: 'I'll' is the contraction of 'I will'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'more': Primary Five pupils prefer Gmail to Yahoo. ___ A: Primary Five pupils like Gmail more than Yahoo.. 'prefer X to Y' = 'like X more than Y'.
chunks.source: 'prefer X to Y' = 'like X more than Y'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'who': That is the boy. He failed to name a single shape during the Mathematics lesson. ___ A: That is the boy who failed to name a single shape during the Mathematics lesson.. 'who' refers to the boy.
chunks.source: 'who' refers to the boy.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'Unless': If you don't use crayons, your picture will not look nice. ___ A: Unless you use crayons, your picture will not look nice.. 'Unless' = 'if not'.
chunks.source: 'Unless' = 'if not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'What': Our new nurse is a very smart lady. ___ A: What a very smart lady our new nurse is!. Exclamation pattern: What + a + adjective + noun!
chunks.source: Exclamation pattern: What + a + adjective + noun!

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'if': Mega will go to the post office. She will buy some stamps. ___ A: If Mega goes to the post office, she will buy some stamps.. If + present, will + verb.
chunks.source: If + present, will + verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'which': Here is the gun. The thief used it to shoot the padlock. ___ A: Here is the gun which the thief used to shoot the padlock.. 'which' refers to the gun.
chunks.source: 'which' refers to the gun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Add the question tag: She will come today, ___ she? ___ A: won't. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't she?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't she?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: ___ whom did you travel to Nairobi? ___ A: With. 'With whom' asks about a companion.
chunks.source: 'With whom' asks about a companion.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: ___ he revises his notes, he won't get good marks. ___ A: Unless. 'Unless' = 'if not'.
chunks.source: 'Unless' = 'if not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Teachers are very ___ people. (care) ___ A: careful. The adjective form is 'careful'.
chunks.source: The adjective form is 'careful'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Daddy's windscreen has been ___ by George. (clean) ___ A: cleaned. Passive: has been + past participle: has been cleaned.
chunks.source: Passive: has been + past participle: has been cleaned.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Babirye is ___ than her elder brother. (wise) ___ A: wiser. Short adjectives add -er: wise -> wiser.
chunks.source: Short adjectives add -er: wise -> wiser.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Mr. ___ A: Mister. 'Mr.' is short for 'Mister'.
chunks.source: 'Mr.' is short for 'Mister'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: e-mail ___ A: electronic mail. 'e-mail' means 'electronic mail'.
chunks.source: 'e-mail' means 'electronic mail'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: End with 'by Didi': Didi swept the classroom. ___ A: The classroom was swept by Didi.. Passive: was + swept + by Didi.
chunks.source: Passive: was + swept + by Didi.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'as...as': Lucas is very calm. His father is very calm. ___ A: Lucas is as calm as his father.. 'as...as' shows equality.
chunks.source: 'as...as' shows equality.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'How': It is always good to tell the truth. ___ A: How good it is to tell the truth!. Exclamation: How + adjective!
chunks.source: Exclamation: How + adjective!

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'What': He wrote a very nice letter. ___ A: What a nice letter he wrote!. Exclamation: What + a + adjective + noun!
chunks.source: Exclamation: What + a + adjective + noun!

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'than': Malinga is clever. Moses is cleverer. ___ A: Moses is cleverer than Malinga.. Comparative + than.
chunks.source: Comparative + than.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'which': This is the hospital. It was built last year. ___ A: This is the hospital which was built last year.. 'which' refers to the hospital.
chunks.source: 'which' refers to the hospital.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Have you seen the boy ___ the teacher was looking for? ___ A: whom. 'whom' refers to the boy receiving the action.
chunks.source: 'whom' refers to the boy receiving the action.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: The red book is bigger ___ the green one. ___ A: than. Comparative + than.
chunks.source: Comparative + than.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Old men are said to be ___ than young men. (wise) ___ A: wiser. wise -> wiser.
chunks.source: wise -> wiser.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Simon is a very ___ boy because he didn't hand in his work for marking. (care) ___ A: careless. 'careless' means not careful.
chunks.source: 'careless' means not careful.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Feb. ___ A: February. 'Feb.' is short for 'February'.
chunks.source: 'Feb.' is short for 'February'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: a.m. ___ A: ante meridiem. 'a.m.' means 'ante meridiem' (before noon).
chunks.source: 'a.m.' means 'ante meridiem' (before noon).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: won't ___ A: will not. 'won't' is the contraction of 'will not'.
chunks.source: 'won't' is the contraction of 'will not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'than': I like driving but I like repairing vehicles more. ___ A: I like repairing vehicles more than driving.. 'more...than' shows comparison.
chunks.source: 'more...than' shows comparison.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'If': When you open the boot, the luggage will fall down. ___ A: If you open the boot, the luggage will fall down.. 'When' becomes 'If'.
chunks.source: 'When' becomes 'If'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'which': This is the story. I told you about it. ___ A: This is the story which I told you about.. 'which' refers to the story.
chunks.source: 'which' refers to the story.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'A glass': Opio broke a glass. ___ A: A glass was broken by Opio.. Passive: was + broken + by Opio.
chunks.source: Passive: was + broken + by Opio.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'whose': This is the driver. His key got lost yesterday. ___ A: This is the driver whose key got lost yesterday.. 'whose' shows the key belongs to him.
chunks.source: 'whose' shows the key belongs to him.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join with 'not as...as': A bus is fast. A taxi is very fast. ___ A: A bus is not as fast as a taxi.. 'not as...as' shows the bus is slower.
chunks.source: 'not as...as' shows the bus is slower.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'What': He is a tall boy. ___ A: What a tall boy he is!. Exclamation: What + a + adjective + noun!
chunks.source: Exclamation: What + a + adjective + noun!

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'needn't have': It was not necessary for him to go to school. ___ A: He needn't have gone to school.. 'needn't have' + past participle: needn't have gone.
chunks.source: 'needn't have' + past participle: needn't have gone.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'must': He had to improve on his spellings. ___ A: He must improve on his spellings.. 'had to' becomes 'must' + base verb.
chunks.source: 'had to' becomes 'must' + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'should': We need to keep our promise. ___ A: We should keep our promise.. 'need to' becomes 'should' + base verb.
chunks.source: 'need to' becomes 'should' + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'The food': The maid needn't have thrown away the food. ___ A: The food needn't have been thrown away.. Passive: needn't have been thrown away.
chunks.source: Passive: needn't have been thrown away.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'ought': We should be exemplary to others. ___ A: We ought to be exemplary to others.. 'should' becomes 'ought to'.
chunks.source: 'should' becomes 'ought to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I can't fast when I am sick. I ___ be fooling myself. (Use 'must' or 'can't') A: must. It is certain, so use 'must'.
chunks.source: It is certain, so use 'must'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'must' or 'can't': He is not a Ugandan. He ___ be a presidential candidate. ___ A: can't. It is impossible, so use 'can't'.
chunks.source: It is impossible, so use 'can't'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'must' or 'can't': She dresses expensively. Her father ___ be a rich man. ___ A: must. It is almost certain, so use 'must'.
chunks.source: It is almost certain, so use 'must'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He ___ be at the university. He is still young. (Use 'must' or 'can't') A: can't. It is impossible, so use 'can't'.
chunks.source: It is impossible, so use 'can't'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'must' or 'can't': She is making a wide smile. She ___ be happy to see us. ___ A: must. It is almost certain, so use 'must'.
chunks.source: It is almost certain, so use 'must'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'ought' or 'should': Prices of commodities ___ be lowered soon. ___ A: ought to. Use 'ought to' + base verb.
chunks.source: Use 'ought to' + base verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'ought' or 'should': You ___ to complain about it. ___ A: ought. 'ought to complain' gives advice.
chunks.source: 'ought to complain' gives advice.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you think I ___ do? (Use 'ought' or 'should') A: should. Asking for advice: 'should'.
chunks.source: Asking for advice: 'should'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'ought' or 'should': One ___ to be friendly to the neighbours. ___ A: ought. 'ought to' gives moral advice.
chunks.source: 'ought to' gives moral advice.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'ought' or 'should': You ___ sweep the classroom before you go home. ___ A: should. Giving advice: 'should'.
chunks.source: Giving advice: 'should'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate correctly: I did not come to school he said because I was sick. ___ A: "I did not come to school," he said, "because I was sick.". Direct speech goes in quotation marks with commas.
chunks.source: Direct speech goes in quotation marks with commas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'Mother asked': 'Betty, what are you doing now?' mother asked. ___ A: Mother asked Betty what she was doing then.. Reported question: asked + what + she was doing then.
chunks.source: Reported question: asked + what + she was doing then.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He wanted to know from me if I had never been to London. (End: '...?' he asked me.) A: "Have you never been to London?" he asked me.. Change the reported question back to direct speech.
chunks.source: Change the reported question back to direct speech.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'He said': He said, 'I have finished all the work.' ___ A: He said that he had finished all the work.. Present perfect becomes past perfect: had finished.
chunks.source: Present perfect becomes past perfect: had finished.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'wanted to know': 'Have you cleaned the classroom?' asked the teacher. ___ A: The teacher wanted to know whether I had cleaned the classroom.. Reported question with 'whether' + past perfect.
chunks.source: Reported question with 'whether' + past perfect.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'The host said': 'I do not expect him today,' the host said. ___ A: The host said that he did not expect him that day.. 'today' becomes 'that day' in reported speech.
chunks.source: 'today' becomes 'that day' in reported speech.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: 'Everybody must be very quiet,' the teacher said. (Begin: The teacher said...) A: The teacher said that everybody had to be very quiet.. 'must' becomes 'had to' in reported speech.
chunks.source: 'must' becomes 'had to' in reported speech.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'Mother told': 'Come and share with me this chicken, Shivon,' mother said. ___ A: Mother told Shivon to come and share the chicken with her.. Reported command: told + person + to + verb.
chunks.source: Reported command: told + person + to + verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with '"Will you...?"': The guest wanted to know whether I would sit at the dining table with them. ___ A: "Will you sit at the dining table with us?" the guest asked.. Change reported speech back to a direct question.
chunks.source: Change reported speech back to a direct question.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'The teacher': 'The earth goes round the sun,' the teacher taught us. ___ A: The teacher told us that the earth goes round the sun.. Universal truths stay in the present tense.
chunks.source: Universal truths stay in the present tense.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: True or False: In reported speech, 'today' usually becomes 'that day'. A: True. Yes. Time words shift back: today -> that day.
chunks.source: Yes. Time words shift back: today -> that day.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He spoke ___ me yesterday. A: to. 'speak to' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'speak to' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: I am tired ___ walking. ___ A: of. 'tired of' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'tired of' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: You boys, you must settle it ___ yourselves. ___ A: among. 'among' is used for more than two people.
chunks.source: 'among' is used for more than two people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The burglar jumped ___ the wall. A: over. He jumped 'over' the wall.
chunks.source: He jumped 'over' the wall.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: He died ___ his country. ___ A: for. 'die for' means to give one's life for something.
chunks.source: 'die for' means to give one's life for something.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: I am fond ___ music. ___ A: of. 'fond of' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'fond of' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The letter was written ___ me by that man. A: to. The letter was written 'to' me.
chunks.source: The letter was written 'to' me.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: It is ten o'clock ___ my watch. ___ A: by. 'by my watch' means according to my watch.
chunks.source: 'by my watch' means according to my watch.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: I will sit ___ my desk and write all notes. ___ A: at. 'sit at' a desk is correct.
chunks.source: 'sit at' a desk is correct.

chunks.subject: English
