chunks.text: Q: Do not cry ___ spilt milk. A: over. The saying is 'cry over spilt milk'.
chunks.source: The saying is 'cry over spilt milk'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: The cup was put ___ the table for everybody to see. ___ A: on. 'on the table' is correct.
chunks.source: 'on the table' is correct.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: Do not lean ___ the wall. ___ A: against. 'lean against' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'lean against' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He lives ___ the post office. A: near. 'near' shows a place close by.
chunks.source: 'near' shows a place close by.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: Do not put it ___ the bed because they will not see it. ___ A: under. 'under the bed' hides it.
chunks.source: 'under the bed' hides it.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: They swam ___ the river and caught fish. ___ A: across. 'across' is used for crossing water.
chunks.source: 'across' is used for crossing water.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My opinion differs ___ yours. A: from. 'differ from' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'differ from' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: He hardly parts ___ money. ___ A: with. 'part with' means to give away.
chunks.source: 'part with' means to give away.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: They should act ___ my behalf. ___ A: on. 'on behalf of' is the saying.
chunks.source: 'on behalf of' is the saying.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He presided ___ the meeting. A: over. 'preside over' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'preside over' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: Those good ideas originated ___ him. ___ A: from. 'originate from' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'originate from' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The gulf war started ___ 1986. A: in. 'in' is used with years.
chunks.source: 'in' is used with years.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: I have been sick ___ last Monday. ___ A: since. 'since' is used with a starting point in time.
chunks.source: 'since' is used with a starting point in time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: They have lived in Kenya ___ a decade. ___ A: for. 'for' is used with a period of time.
chunks.source: 'for' is used with a period of time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Peter has been waiting ___ her. ___ A: for. 'wait for' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'wait for' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our school opened ___ 1987. A: in. 'in' is used with years.
chunks.source: 'in' is used with years.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: He will have died ___ next week. ___ A: by. 'by' means not later than.
chunks.source: 'by' means not later than.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: They were in Kabale ___ ten o'clock. ___ A: at. 'at' is used with exact times.
chunks.source: 'at' is used with exact times.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We learn science ___ Friday. A: on. 'on' is used with days.
chunks.source: 'on' is used with days.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: He often leaves ___ the afternoon. ___ A: in. 'in the afternoon' is correct.
chunks.source: 'in the afternoon' is correct.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: He is interested ___ reading newspapers. ___ A: in. 'interested in' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'interested in' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: She met me ___ the way. ___ A: on. 'on the way' is the saying.
chunks.source: 'on the way' is the saying.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The train arrived ___ time. A: on. 'on time' means punctual.
chunks.source: 'on time' means punctual.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: He came ___ bus. ___ A: by. We travel 'by' bus.
chunks.source: We travel 'by' bus.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Somebody is knocking ___ the door. ___ A: at. 'knock at the door' is correct.
chunks.source: 'knock at the door' is correct.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are prepositions? (Choose all that apply) A: to, over, against. Prepositions show relationships: to, over, against.
chunks.source: Prepositions show relationships: to, over, against.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the passage about? A: Ways of keeping money. The passage describes old and new ways of keeping money.
chunks.source: The passage describes old and new ways of keeping money.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mention one way people kept money in the past. ___ A: In pots under beds. Some used pots hidden under beds.
chunks.source: Some used pots hidden under beds.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Keeping money in grass roofs was safe. A: False. It was not safe because the houses often caught fire.
chunks.source: It was not safe because the houses often caught fire.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the addition given by banks called? ___ A: interest. Banks give an addition called interest.
chunks.source: Banks give an addition called interest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How do people keep money today? A: In banks. Today people keep money in banks.
chunks.source: Today people keep money in banks.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: When did the father hear the alarm? ___ A: Late in the night. It was late in the night.
chunks.source: It was late in the night.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who was making the loud, violent noise? A: The boarding pupils. The pupils in the boarding section were making noise.
chunks.source: The pupils in the boarding section were making noise.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What was the father's job? ___ A: A security officer. He was a security officer.
chunks.source: He was a security officer.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The neighbours rushed the father to hospital. A: True. Yes, the neighbours rushed him to hospital.
chunks.source: Yes, the neighbours rushed him to hospital.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What happened after the father recovered? A: He was appointed chairman of the security committee. He became chairman of the security committee.
chunks.source: He became chairman of the security committee.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: We travelled to Ntawo ___ bus for our tour. ___ A: by. We travel 'by' bus.
chunks.source: We travel 'by' bus.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Aine is good ___ writing letters. ___ A: at. 'good at' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'good at' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Tabitha lives ___ Mpigi along Masaka road. ___ A: at. 'at' is used for small places like Mpigi.
chunks.source: 'at' is used for small places like Mpigi.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'must': You have to charge your phone when the battery is low. ___ A: You must charge your phone when the battery is low.. 'have to' becomes 'must'.
chunks.source: 'have to' becomes 'must'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: The bees moved from one flower ___ another looking for nectar. ___ A: to. 'from...to' is the pair.
chunks.source: 'from...to' is the pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'You must': Clean the kennel weekly. ___ A: You must clean the kennel weekly.. 'must' gives a strong order.
chunks.source: 'must' gives a strong order.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: you shouldn't behave like that ___ A: You shouldn't behave like that.. Begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. shouldn't already has its apostrophe.
chunks.source: Begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. shouldn't already has its apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: you shouldn't behave like that Have you seen Hillary's new bicycle? A: False. Begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. shouldn't already has its apostrophe.
chunks.source: Begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. shouldn't already has its apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: I cant live without you ___ A: I can't live without you.. can't needs an apostrophe. Begin with a capital I and end with a full stop.
chunks.source: can't needs an apostrophe. Begin with a capital I and end with a full stop.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: I cant live without you You shouldn't behave like that. A: False. can't needs an apostrophe. Begin with a capital I and end with a full stop.
chunks.source: can't needs an apostrophe. Begin with a capital I and end with a full stop.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': What ___ ugly man he is! A: an. 'an' is used before words that begin with a vowel sound, like 'ugly'.
chunks.source: 'an' is used before words that begin with a vowel sound, like 'ugly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': What a, an ugly man he is! A: False. 'an' is used before words that begin with a vowel sound, like 'ugly'.
chunks.source: 'an' is used before words that begin with a vowel sound, like 'ugly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': ___ blanket is made of wool. A: A. 'A' is used to talk about any one thing of its kind.
chunks.source: 'A' is used to talk about any one thing of its kind.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': {'a': ['a cup', 'a European', 'a blanket'], 'an': ['an apple', 'an hour', 'an egg']} blanket is made of wool. A: False. 'A' is used to talk about any one thing of its kind.
chunks.source: 'A' is used to talk about any one thing of its kind.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': We shall finish the work in less than ___ hour. A: an. 'hour' begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'hour' begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': We shall finish the work in less than A hour. A: False. 'hour' begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'hour' begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': It was ___ unwise decision to take that route. A: an. 'unwise' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'unwise' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': It was the unwise decision to take that route. A: False. 'unwise' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'unwise' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': ___ hoe is a very useful garden tool. A: A. We use 'a' to talk about any one hoe in general.
chunks.source: We use 'a' to talk about any one hoe in general.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': an hoe is a very useful garden tool. A: False. We use 'a' to talk about any one hoe in general.
chunks.source: We use 'a' to talk about any one hoe in general.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': Can ___ cock lay ___ egg? A: a, an. 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cock'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'.
chunks.source: 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cock'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': Can A cock lay A egg? A: False. 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cock'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'.
chunks.source: 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cock'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': Is seven ___ even number? A: an. 'even' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'even' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': Is seven a, an even number? A: False. 'even' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'even' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': Would you like ___ cup of tea or ___ orange? A: a, an. 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cup'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'orange'.
chunks.source: 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cup'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'orange'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': Would you like The, the cup of tea or The, the orange? A: False. 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cup'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'orange'.
chunks.source: 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cup'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'orange'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': I prefer ___ egg to ___ samosa. A: an, a. 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'; 'a' before the consonant sound in 'samosa'.
chunks.source: 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'; 'a' before the consonant sound in 'samosa'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': I prefer an egg to an samosa. A: False. 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'; 'a' before the consonant sound in 'samosa'.
chunks.source: 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'; 'a' before the consonant sound in 'samosa'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: radio ___ A: radios. Words ending in a vowel + o simply add -s: radio -> radios.
chunks.source: Words ending in a vowel + o simply add -s: radio -> radios.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: radio fruits A: False. Words ending in a vowel + o simply add -s: radio -> radios.
chunks.source: Words ending in a vowel + o simply add -s: radio -> radios.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: piano ___ A: pianos. Words ending in a vowel + o simply add -s: piano -> pianos.

chunks.source: 'originate from' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct preposition: Those good ideas originated near him. near A: False. 'originate from' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'originate from' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: I have been sick ___ last Monday. ___ A: since. 'since' is used with a starting point in time.
chunks.source: 'since' is used with a starting point in time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: I have been sick on last Monday. on A: False. 'since' is used with a starting point in time.
chunks.source: 'since' is used with a starting point in time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: They have lived in Kenya ___ a decade. ___ A: for. 'for' is used with a period of time.
chunks.source: 'for' is used with a period of time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: They have lived in Kenya from a decade. from A: False. 'for' is used with a period of time.
chunks.source: 'for' is used with a period of time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Peter has been waiting ___ her. ___ A: for. 'wait for' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'wait for' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Peter has been waiting at her. at A: False. 'wait for' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'wait for' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: He will have died ___ next week. ___ A: by. 'by' means not later than.
chunks.source: 'by' means not later than.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: He will have died in next week. in A: False. 'by' means not later than.
chunks.source: 'by' means not later than.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: They were in Kabale ___ ten o'clock. ___ A: at. 'at' is used with exact times.
chunks.source: 'at' is used with exact times.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: They were in Kabale by ten o'clock. by A: False. 'at' is used with exact times.
chunks.source: 'at' is used with exact times.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: He often leaves ___ the afternoon. ___ A: in. 'in the afternoon' is correct.
chunks.source: 'in the afternoon' is correct.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: He often leaves against the afternoon. against A: False. 'in the afternoon' is correct.
chunks.source: 'in the afternoon' is correct.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: He is interested ___ reading newspapers. ___ A: in. 'interested in' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'interested in' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: He is interested under reading newspapers. under A: False. 'interested in' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'interested in' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: She met me ___ the way. ___ A: on. 'on the way' is the saying.
chunks.source: 'on the way' is the saying.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: She met me against the way. against A: False. 'on the way' is the saying.
chunks.source: 'on the way' is the saying.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: He came ___ bus. ___ A: by. We travel 'by' bus.
chunks.source: We travel 'by' bus.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: He came under bus. under A: False. We travel 'by' bus.
chunks.source: We travel 'by' bus.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Somebody is knocking ___ the door. ___ A: at. 'knock at the door' is correct.
chunks.source: 'knock at the door' is correct.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Somebody is knocking since the door. since A: False. 'knock at the door' is correct.
chunks.source: 'knock at the door' is correct.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: We travelled to Ntawo ___ bus for our tour. ___ A: by. We travel 'by' bus.
chunks.source: We travel 'by' bus.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: We travelled to Ntawo in bus for our tour. in A: False. We travel 'by' bus.
chunks.source: We travel 'by' bus.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Aine is good ___ writing letters. ___ A: at. 'good at' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'good at' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Aine is good with writing letters. with A: False. 'good at' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'good at' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Tabitha lives ___ Mpigi along Masaka road. ___ A: at. 'at' is used for small places like Mpigi.
chunks.source: 'at' is used for small places like Mpigi.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Tabitha lives by Mpigi along Masaka road. by A: False. 'at' is used for small places like Mpigi.
chunks.source: 'at' is used for small places like Mpigi.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: The bees moved from one flower ___ another looking for nectar. ___ A: to. 'from...to' is the pair.
chunks.source: 'from...to' is the pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: The bees moved from one flower in another looking for nectar. in A: False. 'from...to' is the pair.
chunks.source: 'from...to' is the pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: you shouldn't behave like that ___ A: You shouldn't behave like that.. Begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. shouldn't already has its apostrophe.
chunks.source: Begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. shouldn't already has its apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate this sentence correctly: I cant live without you ___ A: I can't live without you.. can't needs an apostrophe. Begin with a capital I and end with a full stop.
chunks.source: can't needs an apostrophe. Begin with a capital I and end with a full stop.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': What ___ ugly man he is! A: an. 'an' is used before words that begin with a vowel sound, like 'ugly'.
chunks.source: 'an' is used before words that begin with a vowel sound, like 'ugly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': ___ blanket is made of wool. A: A. 'A' is used to talk about any one thing of its kind.
chunks.source: 'A' is used to talk about any one thing of its kind.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': We shall finish the work in less than ___ hour. A: an. 'hour' begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'hour' begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': It was ___ unwise decision to take that route. A: an. 'unwise' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'unwise' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': ___ hoe is a very useful garden tool. A: A. We use 'a' to talk about any one hoe in general.
chunks.source: We use 'a' to talk about any one hoe in general.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': Can ___ cock lay ___ egg? A: a, an. 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cock'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'.
chunks.source: 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cock'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': Is seven ___ even number? A: an. 'even' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.
chunks.source: 'even' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': Would you like ___ cup of tea or ___ orange? A: a, an. 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cup'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'orange'.
chunks.source: 'a' before the consonant sound in 'cup'; 'an' before the vowel sound in 'orange'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'a', 'an' or 'the': I prefer ___ egg to ___ samosa. A: an, a. 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'; 'a' before the consonant sound in 'samosa'.
chunks.source: 'an' before the vowel sound in 'egg'; 'a' before the consonant sound in 'samosa'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: radio ___ A: radios. Words ending in a vowel + o simply add -s: radio -> radios.
chunks.source: Words ending in a vowel + o simply add -s: radio -> radios.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: piano ___ A: pianos. Words ending in a vowel + o simply add -s: piano -> pianos.
chunks.source: Words ending in a vowel + o simply add -s: piano -> pianos.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: shelf ___ A: shelves. Nouns ending in -f change to -ves: shelf -> shelves.
chunks.source: Nouns ending in -f change to -ves: shelf -> shelves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: guest-of-honour ___ A: guests-of-honour. In compound nouns, the main word takes the plural: guests-of-honour.
chunks.source: In compound nouns, the main word takes the plural: guests-of-honour.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: a group of flowers ___ A: bouquet. A group of flowers held together is called a bouquet.
chunks.source: A group of flowers held together is called a bouquet.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: the people watching a game ___ A: spectators. People who watch a game or match are called spectators.
chunks.source: People who watch a game or match are called spectators.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: the people walking on foot ___ A: pedestrians. People walking on foot, not in a vehicle, are pedestrians.
chunks.source: People walking on foot, not in a vehicle, are pedestrians.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: books, papers, pens, pencils, files and rulers ___ A: stationery. Writing materials like pens, paper and books are called stationery.
chunks.source: Writing materials like pens, paper and books are called stationery.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct form: His ___ was so clear that everyone understood. (explain) ___ A: explanation. The noun form of 'explain' is 'explanation'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'explain' is 'explanation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct form: He went out without getting ___ from the teacher. (permit) ___ A: permission. The noun form of 'permit' is 'permission'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'permit' is 'permission'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct form: The little girl made a very wise ___. (decide) ___ A: decision. The noun form of 'decide' is 'decision'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'decide' is 'decision'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct form: There is widespread ___ in this country. (poor) ___ A: poverty. The noun form of 'poor' is 'poverty'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'poor' is 'poverty'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: The pupils ___ classes daily. (attend) ___ A: attend. With 'they' we use the base verb: attend.
chunks.source: With 'they' we use the base verb: attend.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: I ___ posho to rice. (prefer) ___ A: prefer. With 'I' we use the base verb: prefer.
chunks.source: With 'I' we use the base verb: prefer.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: She ___ us English every Friday. (teach) ___ A: teaches. With she we add -es after ch: teaches.
chunks.source: With she we add -es after ch: teaches.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: Those ladies dress decently. ___ A: Do those ladies dress decently?. Use 'Do' with plural subjects.
chunks.source: Use 'Do' with plural subjects.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: Ezra buys milk from the dairy, ___? ___ A: doesn't he. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: doesn't he?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: doesn't he?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: The children fetch water every weekend, ___? ___ A: don't they. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: don't they?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: don't they?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: My father pays our school fees, ___? ___ A: doesn't he. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: doesn't he?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: doesn't he?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: Our teacher doesn't come on Saturday, ___? ___ A: does he. A negative sentence takes a positive tag: does he?
chunks.source: A negative sentence takes a positive tag: does he?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: I ___ my notes now. (revise) ___ A: am revising. Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing. With 'I' use 'am revising'.
chunks.source: Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing. With 'I' use 'am revising'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: The mechanic ___ the bicycle. (repair) ___ A: is repairing. Use 'is repairing' for an action happening now.
chunks.source: Use 'is repairing' for an action happening now.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Our teacher ___ a meeting now. (hold) ___ A: is holding. 'hold' doubles the 'd' before -ing: holding. Our teacher = is holding.
chunks.source: 'hold' doubles the 'd' before -ing: holding. Our teacher = is holding.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: The pilot ___ the aeroplane. (fly) ___ A: is flying. With 'the pilot' use 'is flying'.
chunks.source: With 'the pilot' use 'is flying'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: She is preparing breakfast. ___ A: Is she preparing breakfast?. Swap the subject and the helping verb: Is she...?
chunks.source: Swap the subject and the helping verb: Is she...?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: Charles is not driving a car. ___ A: Is Charles driving a car?. In questions we usually drop 'not': Is Charles driving a car?
chunks.source: In questions we usually drop 'not': Is Charles driving a car?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: They are sowing seeds, ___? ___ A: aren't they. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: aren't they?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: aren't they?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: I am going to church today, ___? ___ A: aren't I. 'I am' takes the special tag 'aren't I'.
chunks.source: 'I am' takes the special tag 'aren't I'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: It is raining now, ___? ___ A: isn't it. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: isn't it?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: isn't it?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: She ___ my food. (eat) ___ A: has eaten. Present perfect: has/have + past participle. She has eaten.
chunks.source: Present perfect: has/have + past participle. She has eaten.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Anita ___ the compound. (sweep) ___ A: has swept. Anita = she: has swept.
chunks.source: Anita = she: has swept.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: John ___ his father's property. (sell) ___ A: has sold. John = he: has sold.
chunks.source: John = he: has sold.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: I ___ a snake under my bed. (see) ___ A: have seen. With 'I' use 'have seen'.
chunks.source: With 'I' use 'have seen'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: The baby has woken up, ___? ___ A: hasn't it. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: hasn't it?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: hasn't it?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: My friends have visited me, ___? ___ A: haven't they. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: haven't they?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: haven't they?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: He ___ singing to dancing. (prefer) ___ A: preferred. Past simple of 'prefer' doubles the 'r': preferred.
chunks.source: Past simple of 'prefer' doubles the 'r': preferred.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: My balloon ___ last Friday. (burst) ___ A: burst. 'burst' stays the same in the past: burst.
chunks.source: 'burst' stays the same in the past: burst.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: I ___ a thief last night. (see) ___ A: saw. Past of 'see' is 'saw'.
chunks.source: Past of 'see' is 'saw'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Mary was ___ a novel. (read) ___ A: reading. Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing: was reading.
chunks.source: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing: was reading.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: As I ___ through the bush, I stepped on a snake. (walk) ___ A: was walking. With 'I' use 'was walking'.
chunks.source: With 'I' use 'was walking'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: I fell down while I ___ to school. (run) ___ A: was running. 'run' doubles the 'n': was running.
chunks.source: 'run' doubles the 'n': was running.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Ceasar ___ a bicycle when I met him. (ride) ___ A: was riding. Ceasar = he: was riding.
chunks.source: Ceasar = he: was riding.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to interrogative: Our teachers were not present. ___ A: Were our teachers present?. Move 'were' to the front and drop 'not'.
chunks.source: Move 'were' to the front and drop 'not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: They go to the gym almost ___ . (day) ___ A: daily. 'day' becomes the adverb 'daily'.
chunks.source: 'day' becomes the adverb 'daily'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: He treated the little boy ___ . (cruel) ___ A: cruelly. 'cruel' becomes 'cruelly' (y changes to i before -ly).
chunks.source: 'cruel' becomes 'cruelly' (y changes to i before -ly).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: She ___ walked through the forest at night. (courage) ___ A: courageously. 'courage' becomes 'courageously'.
chunks.source: 'courage' becomes 'courageously'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: We ___ said our prayers before going to bed. (quiet) ___ A: quietly. 'quiet' becomes 'quietly'.
chunks.source: 'quiet' becomes 'quietly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: We visit the zoo ___ a month. (two) ___ A: twice. 'two' becomes 'twice' for times.
chunks.source: 'two' becomes 'twice' for times.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: Christians go to church ___ a week. (one) ___ A: once. 'one' becomes 'once' for times.
chunks.source: 'one' becomes 'once' for times.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: The visitors were ___ welcomed. (warm) ___ A: warmly. 'warm' becomes 'warmly'.
chunks.source: 'warm' becomes 'warmly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: The lousy boy has ___ written his work. (careless) ___ A: carelessly. 'careless' becomes 'carelessly'.
chunks.source: 'careless' becomes 'carelessly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: He entered the room ___ and took our toys. (steal) ___ A: stealthily. 'steal' gives the adverb 'stealthily' (quietly and secretly).
chunks.source: 'steal' gives the adverb 'stealthily' (quietly and secretly).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the adverb: Our teachers always advise us to dress ___. (decent) ___ A: decently. 'decent' becomes 'decently'.
chunks.source: 'decent' becomes 'decently'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: junior ___ A: senior. 'junior' and 'senior' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'junior' and 'senior' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: modern ___ A: ancient. 'modern' and 'ancient' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'modern' and 'ancient' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: possible ___ A: impossible. Add the prefix 'im-': impossible.
chunks.source: Add the prefix 'im-': impossible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: host ___ A: guest. The host invites; the guest is invited.
chunks.source: The host invites; the guest is invited.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: busy ___ A: idle. 'busy' and 'idle' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'busy' and 'idle' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: wild ___ A: tame. A wild animal lives freely; a tame one is gentle with people.
chunks.source: A wild animal lives freely; a tame one is gentle with people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'absence': His absence at the party was a misfortune. ___ A: presence. 'absence' and 'presence' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'absence' and 'presence' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'strong': The strong man pulled me. ___ A: weak. 'strong' and 'weak' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'strong' and 'weak' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'princess': The princess visited our school. ___ A: prince. 'princess' and 'prince' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'princess' and 'prince' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'nephews': I don't have any nephews. ___ A: nieces. Nephews are sons of siblings; nieces are daughters.
chunks.source: Nephews are sons of siblings; nieces are daughters.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'landlord': Have you talked to the landlord? ___ A: tenant. The landlord owns the house; the tenant rents it.
chunks.source: The landlord owns the house; the tenant rents it.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'obedient': The obedient pupils will be rewarded. ___ A: disobedient. Add the prefix 'dis-': disobedient.
chunks.source: Add the prefix 'dis-': disobedient.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'heir': He has not yet chosen an heir. ___ A: heiress. An heir is male; an heiress is female.
chunks.source: An heir is male; an heiress is female.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Joan writes so ___ that every pupil in our class admires her. (good) ___ A: well. The adverb form of 'good' is 'well'.
chunks.source: The adverb form of 'good' is 'well'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: The ___ of the headmaster surprised every child in the school compound. (arrive) ___ A: arrival. The noun form of 'arrive' is 'arrival'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'arrive' is 'arrival'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: We are ___ on the verandah to wait for the weather to clear. (sit) ___ A: sitting. Present continuous: are + sitting.
chunks.source: Present continuous: are + sitting.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Rajab was the ___ out of the forty pupils in the class. (twelve) ___ A: twelfth. The ordinal of 'twelve' is 'twelfth'.
chunks.source: The ordinal of 'twelve' is 'twelfth'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Has any teacher taught you about ___ this term? (punctuate) ___ A: punctuation. The noun form of 'punctuate' is 'punctuation'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'punctuate' is 'punctuation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: The driver could not see ___ during the rain. (clear) ___ A: clearly. The adverb form of 'clear' is 'clearly'.
chunks.source: The adverb form of 'clear' is 'clearly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: How many glasses has the child ___? (breake) ___ A: broken. Past participle of 'break' is 'broken'.
chunks.source: Past participle of 'break' is 'broken'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Jacob likes neither sweets ___ biscuits. ___ A: nor. 'neither...nor' is the pair.
chunks.source: 'neither...nor' is the pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: ___ the boys were playing football, the girls were mopping the main hall. ___ A: While. 'While' joins two actions happening at the same time.
chunks.source: 'While' joins two actions happening at the same time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Our teacher is ___ open minded woman. ___ A: an. 'an' before the vowel sound in 'open'.
chunks.source: 'an' before the vowel sound in 'open'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'nearer': The tourist feared to move nearer the lion in the game reserve. ___ A: farther. 'nearer' and 'farther' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'nearer' and 'farther' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'departure': We must be at the main gate before the departure of the guest of honour. ___ A: arrival. 'departure' and 'arrival' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'departure' and 'arrival' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: mangoes, oranges, apples, watermelon and pineapples ___ A: fruits. These are all fruits.
chunks.source: These are all fruits.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: people who grow crops and look after animals ___ A: farmers. People who grow crops and keep animals are farmers.
chunks.source: People who grow crops and keep animals are farmers.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Begin with 'Birds': A bird lives in a nest. ___ A: Birds live in nests.. Make everything plural: Birds live in nests.
chunks.source: Make everything plural: Birds live in nests.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Sarah went to hospital in ___ to get treatment. ___ A: order. 'in order to' shows purpose.
chunks.source: 'in order to' shows purpose.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: We ___ been invited to Sweden by our cousins. ___ A: have. Present perfect: have been invited.
chunks.source: Present perfect: have been invited.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Neither Paul ___ Peter went to the garage. ___ A: nor. 'Neither...nor' is the pair.
chunks.source: 'Neither...nor' is the pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Mrs. Kadogo spoke to us ___. (rude) ___ A: rudely. The adverb of 'rude' is 'rudely'.
chunks.source: The adverb of 'rude' is 'rudely'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Sarah received an ___ letter from Joan. (invite) ___ A: invitation. The noun form of 'invite' is 'invitation'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'invite' is 'invitation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Ten ___ were caught stealing cassava. (thief) ___ A: thieves. thief -> thieves.
chunks.source: thief -> thieves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: My grandmother ___ in the bedroom now. (to be) ___ A: is. With 'she' use 'is'.
chunks.source: With 'she' use 'is'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite giving the plural of 'diary': I have lost my diary. ___ A: I have lost my diaries.. diary -> diaries (y to i).
chunks.source: diary -> diaries (y to i).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'obedient': The obedient girl was given an award. ___ A: disobedient. Add the prefix 'dis-': disobedient.
chunks.source: Add the prefix 'dis-': disobedient.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of 'badly': Her letters are badly formed. ___ A: well. 'badly' and 'well' are opposites.
chunks.source: 'badly' and 'well' are opposites.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: members who attended the church service ___ A: congregation. Church members at a service are a congregation.
chunks.source: Church members at a service are a congregation.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: the three young ducks ___ A: ducklings. Young ducks are ducklings.
chunks.source: Young ducks are ducklings.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: a brother to my father ___ A: uncle. Your father's brother is your uncle.
chunks.source: Your father's brother is your uncle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate correctly: have you been to tororo ___ A: Have you been to Tororo?. Capitalize the first word and the place name; end with a question mark.
chunks.source: Capitalize the first word and the place name; end with a question mark.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Aren't ___ ashamed of behaving badly in public? ___ A: you. 'Aren't you' is the question tag pair.
chunks.source: 'Aren't you' is the question tag pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: Our neighbour's son ate ___ apple and sweet bananas at the party. ___ A: an. 'an' before the vowel sound in 'apple'.
chunks.source: 'an' before the vowel sound in 'apple'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: John likes swimming and so ___ Peter. ___ A: does. 'so does Peter' agrees with the first sentence.
chunks.source: 'so does Peter' agrees with the first sentence.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: This jacket is thick ___ to make me warm in this cold weather. ___ A: enough. 'enough to' follows the adjective.
chunks.source: 'enough to' follows the adjective.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: The farmer drove his ___ of cattle to the grazing ground very early in the morning. ___ A: herd. A group of cattle is a herd.
chunks.source: A group of cattle is a herd.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: It is difficult to walk ___ both in the dark and during heavy rain. (quick) ___ A: quickly. The adverb of 'quick' is 'quickly'.
chunks.source: The adverb of 'quick' is 'quickly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Musa always ___ to the radio to get current news. (listen) ___ A: listens. Musa = he: listens.
chunks.source: Musa = he: listens.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: The blind man knocked ___ against the wall while walking out of the main hall. (him) ___ A: himself. The reflexive pronoun of 'him' is 'himself'.
chunks.source: The reflexive pronoun of 'him' is 'himself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: the people who cannot see ___ A: blind. People who cannot see are blind.
chunks.source: People who cannot see are blind.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: our head of country ___ A: president. The head of a country is the president.
chunks.source: The head of a country is the president.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a single word for: cars, buses, taxis and lorries ___ A: vehicles. These are all vehicles.
chunks.source: These are all vehicles.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite with 'an': Bitu wrote a very interesting poem. ___ A: Bitu wrote an interesting poem.. 'an' before the vowel sound in 'interesting'.
chunks.source: 'an' before the vowel sound in 'interesting'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Add the question tag: Peter is a Ugandan, ___? ___ A: isn't he. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: isn't he?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: isn't he?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Punctuate correctly: joan lives in nigeria. ___ A: Joan lives in Nigeria.. Capitalize names of people and countries; end with a full stop.
chunks.source: Capitalize names of people and countries; end with a full stop.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: Uganda -> ___ ___ A: Ugandan. People from Uganda are Ugandans.
chunks.source: People from Uganda are Ugandans.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: China -> ___ ___ A: Chinese. People from China are Chinese.
chunks.source: People from China are Chinese.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: Switzerland -> ___ ___ A: Swiss. People from Switzerland are Swiss.
chunks.source: People from Switzerland are Swiss.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: Portugal -> ___ ___ A: Portuguese. People from Portugal are Portuguese.
chunks.source: People from Portugal are Portuguese.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct pronoun: That is the teacher ___ teaches us mathematics. ___ A: who. 'who' refers to a person.
chunks.source: 'who' refers to a person.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct pronoun: This is the cow ___ we bought from Kenya. ___ A: which. 'which' refers to an animal.
chunks.source: 'which' refers to an animal.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct pronoun: ___ car was stolen? ___ A: Whose. 'Whose' asks about the owner.
chunks.source: 'Whose' asks about the owner.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: Micheal is the ___ boy in our class. (good) ___ A: best. The superlative of 'good' is 'best'.
chunks.source: The superlative of 'good' is 'best'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: Joseph is ___ than Richard. (heavy) ___ A: heavier. heavy -> heavier (y to i).
chunks.source: heavy -> heavier (y to i).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: The box is ___ than that box. (light) ___ A: lighter. light -> lighter.
chunks.source: light -> lighter.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: Which is the ___ building in Nairobi? (tall) ___ A: tallest. The superlative of 'tall' is 'tallest'.
chunks.source: The superlative of 'tall' is 'tallest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: Peter is ___ than George. (weak) ___ A: weaker. weak -> weaker.
chunks.source: weak -> weaker.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: Mary is the ___ girl in our class. (short) ___ A: shortest. The superlative of 'short' is 'shortest'.
chunks.source: The superlative of 'short' is 'shortest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: What is the ___ news? (late) ___ A: latest. The superlative of 'late' is 'latest'.
chunks.source: The superlative of 'late' is 'latest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: I came ___ than you. (early) ___ A: earlier. early -> earlier (y to i).
chunks.source: early -> earlier (y to i).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: He is the ___ of the twins. (old) ___ A: older. With two people, use the comparative: older.
chunks.source: With two people, use the comparative: older.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: His mother is ___ today. (well) ___ A: better. The comparative of 'well' is 'better'.
chunks.source: The comparative of 'well' is 'better'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete with the correct degree: James is the ___ of the two boys. (clever) ___ A: cleverer. With two people, use the comparative: cleverer.
chunks.source: With two people, use the comparative: cleverer.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join in order of adjectives: I solved fifteen good numbers. ___ A: I solved fifteen good numbers.. Order: number (fifteen) before opinion (good).
chunks.source: Order: number (fifteen) before opinion (good).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: He will take an oath, ___? ___ A: won't he. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't he?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't he?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: They will fix the poles, ___? ___ A: won't they. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't they?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't they?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: We shall call him, ___? ___ A: shan't we. 'shall' takes 'shan't we'.
chunks.source: 'shall' takes 'shan't we'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: The baby will cry, ___? ___ A: won't it. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't it?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't it?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Supply the question tag: I shall go to school, ___? ___ A: shan't I. 'I shall' takes 'shan't I'.
chunks.source: 'I shall' takes 'shan't I'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Luwedde is ___ than Gaberialla. (thin) ___ A: thinner. Short adjectives double the final consonant: thin -> thinner.
chunks.source: Short adjectives double the final consonant: thin -> thinner.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: If I ___ to the radio, I would tell you the whole story. (listen) ___ A: listened. After 'If + past', use 'would': If I listened... I would tell.
chunks.source: After 'If + past', use 'would': If I listened... I would tell.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Tel: ___ A: Telephone. 'Tel.' is short for 'Telephone'.
chunks.source: 'Tel.' is short for 'Telephone'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: I'll ___ A: I will. 'I'll' is the contraction of 'I will'.
chunks.source: 'I'll' is the contraction of 'I will'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Add the question tag: She will come today, ___ she? ___ A: won't. Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't she?
chunks.source: Positive sentence takes a negative tag: won't she?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: ___ whom did you travel to Nairobi? ___ A: With. 'With whom' asks about a companion.
chunks.source: 'With whom' asks about a companion.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: ___ he revises his notes, he won't get good marks. ___ A: Unless. 'Unless' = 'if not'.
chunks.source: 'Unless' = 'if not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Teachers are very ___ people. (care) ___ A: careful. The adjective form is 'careful'.
chunks.source: The adjective form is 'careful'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete correctly: Babirye is ___ than her elder brother. (wise) ___ A: wiser. Short adjectives add -er: wise -> wiser.
chunks.source: Short adjectives add -er: wise -> wiser.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Mr. ___ A: Mister. 'Mr.' is short for 'Mister'.
chunks.source: 'Mr.' is short for 'Mister'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: e-mail ___ A: electronic mail. 'e-mail' means 'electronic mail'.
chunks.source: 'e-mail' means 'electronic mail'.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is a set? A: A collection of well-defined objects. A set is a group of objects that are clearly described.
chunks.source: A set is a group of objects that are clearly described.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is the empty set symbol? A: ∅. The empty set has no members and is written as ∅ or {}.
chunks.source: The empty set has no members and is written as ∅ or {}.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that K = {z, e, r, o}, find n(K). A: 4. n(K) counts the members of set K, and there are 4 of them.
chunks.source: n(K) counts the members of set K, and there are 4 of them.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If D = {m, a, n, g, o} and E = {o, r, a, n, g, e}, find D ∩ E. A: {a, n, g, o}. D ∩ E keeps only the members found in both sets: a, n, g and o.
chunks.source: D ∩ E keeps only the members found in both sets: a, n, g and o.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If D = {m, a, n, g, o} and E = {o, r, a, n, g, e}, find n(D ∪ E). A: 7. D ∪ E = {m, a, n, g, o, r, e}, which has 7 members.
chunks.source: D ∪ E = {m, a, n, g, o, r, e}, which has 7 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the probability of tossing a coin and a head showing up? A: 1/2. A coin has 2 faces and only 1 is a head, so the probability is 1/2.
chunks.source: A coin has 2 faces and only 1 is a head, so the probability is 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set F = {even numbers less than 10}. Which of these are members of set F? A: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8. The even numbers less than 10 are 0, 2, 4, 6 and 8.
chunks.source: The even numbers less than 10 are 0, 2, 4, 6 and 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: F = {prime numbers from 2 to 11} and G = {even numbers less than 10}. How many members are in F ∪ G? A: 9. F ∪ G = {0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11}, which has 9 members.
chunks.source: F ∪ G = {0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11}, which has 9 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: F = {prime numbers from 2 to 11} and G = {even numbers less than 10}. Find n(G − F). A: 4. G − F = {0, 4, 6, 8}, which has 4 members.
chunks.source: G − F = {0, 4, 6, 8}, which has 4 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a box there are 5 blue pens, 3 red pens and 7 black pens. If a pen is picked at random, what is the probability of picking a black pen? A: 7/15. There are 15 pens in total and 7 are black, so the probability is 7/15.
chunks.source: There are 15 pens in total and 7 are black, so the probability is 7/15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a box there are 5 blue pens, 3 red pens and 7 black pens. If a pen is picked at random, what is the probability of picking a red pen? A: 1/5. There are 15 pens in total and 3 are red, so the probability is 3/15 = 1/5.
chunks.source: There are 15 pens in total and 3 are red, so the probability is 3/15 = 1/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a box there are 5 blue pens, 3 red pens and 7 black pens. If a pen is picked at random, what is the probability of picking a blue pen? A: 1/3. There are 15 pens in total and 5 are blue, so the probability is 5/15 = 1/3.
chunks.source: There are 15 pens in total and 5 are blue, so the probability is 5/15 = 1/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If a die is tossed once, what is the probability of a prime number showing up? A: 1/2. The prime numbers on a die are 2, 3 and 5, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2.
chunks.source: The prime numbers on a die are 2, 3 and 5, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If a die is tossed once, what is the probability of a number less than 5 showing up? A: 2/3. The numbers less than 5 are 1, 2, 3 and 4, so the probability is 4/6 = 2/3.
chunks.source: The numbers less than 5 are 1, 2, 3 and 4, so the probability is 4/6 = 2/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If a die is tossed once, what is the probability of a 3 showing up? A: 1/6. A die has 6 faces and only one of them is a 3, so the probability is 1/6.
chunks.source: A die has 6 faces and only one of them is a 3, so the probability is 1/6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In the Venn diagram below, which region is A − B? A: The part of A that does not overlap B. A − B keeps the members of A that are not in B.
chunks.source: A − B keeps the members of A that are not in B.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the set symbol: ⊄ A: not a subset of. The symbol ⊄ means the first set is not a subset of the second set.
chunks.source: The symbol ⊄ means the first set is not a subset of the second set.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Describe the shaded region in the Venn diagram below. A: W − X. Only the ring part of W is shaded, so the region is W − X.
chunks.source: Only the ring part of W is shaded, so the region is W − X.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the Venn diagram below. How many members are in set D′? A: 2. All members shown are 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7. D = {0, 2, 5, 7}, so D′ = {1, 3}, which has 2 members.
chunks.source: All members shown are 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7. D = {0, 2, 5, 7}, so D′ = {1, 3}, which has 2 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the Venn diagram below. Find n(C ∩ D). A: 1. Only the number 2 is in both C and D, so n(C ∩ D) = 1.
chunks.source: Only the number 2 is in both C and D, so n(C ∩ D) = 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the Venn diagram below. Find n(C ∩ D)′. A: 5. C ∩ D = {2}, and out of the 6 members shown, 5 are not in it.
chunks.source: C ∩ D = {2}, and out of the 6 members shown, 5 are not in it.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the Venn diagram below. How many subsets does set D only have? A: 8. D only = {5, 7, 0} has 3 members, and a 3-member set has 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 subsets.
chunks.source: D only = {5, 7, 0} has 3 members, and a 3-member set has 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 subsets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Set G = {cat, dog, rabbit}. Find n(G). A: 3. Set G has 3 members.
chunks.source: Set G has 3 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the Venn diagram below. Find P ∪ Q. A: {hen, sheep, duck, cow, goat}. P ∪ Q joins all members without repeating: hen, sheep, duck, cow and goat.
chunks.source: P ∪ Q joins all members without repeating: hen, sheep, duck, cow and goat.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the Venn diagram below. Write the members of set Q. A: {sheep, duck, cow, goat}. Set Q contains sheep, duck, cow and goat.
chunks.source: Set Q contains sheep, duck, cow and goat.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the Venn diagram below. Find n(Q − P). A: 2. Q − P = {cow, goat}, which has 2 members.
chunks.source: Q − P = {cow, goat}, which has 2 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the number of subsets in set K = {cat, cow, rat}. A: 8. 2³ = 8 subsets.
chunks.source: 2³ = 8 subsets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a group, 30 children enjoy milk (M), 25 enjoy porridge (P) and 5 enjoy both. Use the Venn diagram. How many enjoy ONLY milk? A: 25. 30 − 5 = 25.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a group, 30 children enjoy milk (M), 25 enjoy porridge (P) and 5 enjoy both. Use the Venn diagram. How many enjoy ONLY porridge? A: 20. 25 − 5 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a group, 30 children enjoy milk, 25 enjoy porridge and 5 enjoy both. How many children do NOT enjoy milk? A: 20. Total = 25 + 5 + 20 = 50, so 50 − 30 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The Venn diagram shows the union of P and Q shaded. What does P ∪ Q contain? A: All members of P and all members of Q. The union joins every member of both sets.
chunks.source: The union joins every member of both sets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The Venn diagram shows B = {9, 10, 4, 5} and A = {4, 5, 6, 7, 8}. How many subsets does the set B only have? A: 4. B only = {9, 10}, which has 2² = 4 subsets.
chunks.source: B only = {9, 10}, which has 2² = 4 subsets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the Venn diagram. List all the elements in P − Q. A: {8, 9, 10}. P − Q = {8, 9, 10}.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the Venn diagram. List all the elements in P ∩ Q. A: {1, 3}. P ∩ Q = {1, 3}.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the Venn diagram. Find n(P ∪ Q). A: 9. P ∪ Q has 3 + 2 + 4 = 9 members.
chunks.source: P ∪ Q has 3 + 2 + 4 = 9 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 312,015 in words. A: Three hundred twelve thousand fifteen. 312,015 is read as three hundred twelve thousand fifteen.
chunks.source: 312,015 is read as three hundred twelve thousand fifteen.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 139 in Roman numerals. A: CXXXIX. 139 = 100 + 30 + 9, which is C + XXX + IX.
chunks.source: 139 = 100 + 30 + 9, which is C + XXX + IX.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the place value of 3 in 3,207? A: Thousands. The 3 is in the fourth position from the right, so its place value is thousands.
chunks.source: The 3 is in the fourth position from the right, so its place value is thousands.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the value of 3 in 3,201. A: 3000. The 3 stands for 3 thousands, which is 3,000.
chunks.source: The 3 stands for 3 thousands, which is 3,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 'one million one thousand one' in figures. A: 1001001. One million one thousand one is written as 1,001,001.
chunks.source: One million one thousand one is written as 1,001,001.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Expand 3463.4 using powers of 10. A: (3 × 10³) + (4 × 10²) + (6 × 10¹) + (3 × 10⁰) + (4 × 10⁻¹). Each digit is multiplied by 10 raised to the power of its position.
chunks.source: Each digit is multiplied by 10 raised to the power of its position.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Round off 438 to the nearest hundred. A: 400. 438 is closer to 400 than to 500, so it rounds to 400.
chunks.source: 438 is closer to 400 than to 500, so it rounds to 400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Convert XLIV to Hindu-Arabic numerals. A: 44. XLIV = (50 − 10) + (5 − 1) = 40 + 4 = 44.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Grandfather is 99 years old. Express his age in Roman numerals. A: XCIX. 99 = (100 − 10) + (10 − 1) = XC + IX.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the digits 4, 6, 1 and 2, form the biggest number. A: 6421. Arranging the digits from biggest to smallest gives 6,421.
chunks.source: Arranging the digits from biggest to smallest gives 6,421.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the digits 4, 6, 1 and 2, form the smallest number. A: 1246. Arranging the digits from smallest to biggest gives 1,246.
chunks.source: Arranging the digits from smallest to biggest gives 1,246.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the digits 4, 6, 1 and 2, find the sum of the largest and smallest numbers formed. A: 7667. 6,421 + 1,246 = 7,667.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the digits 4, 6, 1 and 2, find the difference between the largest and smallest numbers formed. A: 5175. 6,421 − 1,246 = 5,175.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Round off 3,878 to the nearest ten. A: 3880. 3,878 is closer to 3,880 than to 3,870.
chunks.source: 3,878 is closer to 3,880 than to 3,870.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The abacus below shows a number. Write it in Roman numerals. A: XXXIV. The abacus shows 34, which is XXXIV in Roman numerals.
chunks.source: The abacus shows 34, which is XXXIV in Roman numerals.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the place value of 6 in 369. A: tens. The 6 is in the tens place.
chunks.source: The 6 is in the tens place.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write XLIX in Hindu Arabic numerals. A: 49. XL = 40 and IX = 9, so XLIX = 49.
chunks.source: XL = 40 and IX = 9, so XLIX = 49.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Round off 6,273 to the nearest hundred. A: 6300. 6,273 is closer to 6,300 than to 6,200.
chunks.source: 6,273 is closer to 6,300 than to 6,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 4,621 in words. A: Four thousand six hundred twenty-one. 4,621 = four thousand six hundred twenty-one.
chunks.source: 4,621 = four thousand six hundred twenty-one.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the value of 2 in the number 4,621? A: 20. The 2 is in the tens place, so its value is 20.
chunks.source: The 2 is in the tens place, so its value is 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 'six hundred twenty nine' in figures. A: 629. Six hundred twenty nine = 629.
chunks.source: Six hundred twenty nine = 629.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Identify the place value of 6 in the number 1,620. A: hundreds. The 6 is in the hundreds place.
chunks.source: The 6 is in the hundreds place.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What number has been expanded to give 3,000 + 90 + 500 + 7? A: 3597. 3,000 + 500 + 90 + 7 = 3,597.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Round off 246 to the nearest ten. A: 250. 246 is closer to 250 than to 240.
chunks.source: 246 is closer to 250 than to 240.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Kagimu reads a story of 145 words. How many words will he read if he reads 5 such stories? A: 725. 145 × 5 = 725 words.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The difference between two numbers is 305. If the smaller number is 267, find the bigger number. A: 572. 267 + 305 = 572.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: 3 + 2 = ___ (finite 4) A: 1. 3 + 2 = 5, and 5 in finite 4 is 1.
chunks.source: 3 + 2 = 5, and 5 in finite 4 is 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: 3 − 5 = ___ (finite 7) A: 5. 3 − 5 = −2, and −2 in finite 7 is 5.
chunks.source: 3 − 5 = −2, and −2 in finite 7 is 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The average weight of 3 boys is 53 kg. Find their total weight. A: 159. 53 × 3 = 159 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the place value of 2 in 234₅? A: Twenty-fives. In base five the positions are ones, fives, twenty-fives, so the 2 stands for twenty-fives.
chunks.source: In base five the positions are ones, fives, twenty-fives, so the 2 stands for twenty-fives.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the numbers 4, 6, 4 and 10, find the mode. A: 4. The number 4 appears twice, more than any other, so the mode is 4.
chunks.source: The number 4 appears twice, more than any other, so the mode is 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the numbers 4, 6, 4 and 10, find the mean. A: 6. (4 + 6 + 4 + 10) ÷ 4 = 24 ÷ 4 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the numbers 4, 6, 4 and 10, find the range. A: 6. 10 − 4 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the numbers 4, 6, 4 and 10, find the median. A: 5. Arranged in order: 4, 4, 6, 10. The middle two are 4 and 6, so the median is (4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5.
chunks.source: Arranged in order: 4, 4, 6, 10. The middle two are 4 and 6, so the median is (4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Subtract: 234₇ − 25₇ A: 206₇. 234₇ − 25₇ = 206₇.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: John had some cows on his farm. He sold 18 cows and remained with 92 cows. How many cows did he have at first? A: 110. 18 + 92 = 110.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mukasa scored 98, 95, 92, 95 and 100 in his mid-term exams. Work out his average mark. A: 96. (98 + 95 + 92 + 95 + 100) ÷ 5 = 480 ÷ 5 = 96.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: At a wedding, 3,617 women, 2,398 men and 954 children attended. How many adults attended altogether? A: 6015. 3,617 + 2,398 = 6,015.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: At a wedding, 6,969 guests attended and each was served 2 sodas. How many sodas were served? A: 13938. 6,969 × 2 = 13,938.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 12₅ into base ten. A: 7. 12₅ = (1 × 5) + 2 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the product of seventy-two and fifteen. A: 1080. 72 × 15 = 1,080.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A pupil scored 4, 5, 6, 4, 7 and 4 in homework. Find his average mark. A: 5. (4 + 5 + 6 + 4 + 7 + 4) ÷ 6 = 30 ÷ 6 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Convert 24₅ to base ten. A: 14. 24₅ = (2 × 5) + 4 = 14.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Share 903 sweets equally among Akrah, Joel and Olive. How many sweets do Akrah and Olive get altogether? A: 602. 903 ÷ 3 = 301 each, so 301 × 2 = 602.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: At a party there were 470 adults and 520 children. Find the total number of guests. A: 990. 470 + 520 = 990.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: At a party there were 470 adults and 520 children. How many more children than adults attended? A: 50. 520 − 470 = 50.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: At a party 990 guests attended but there were sodas for only 900 guests. How many guests missed sodas? A: 90. 990 − 900 = 90.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1 school bag costs sh. 1,500. Find the cost of 5 similar school bags. A: 7500. 1,500 × 5 = 7,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5 books cost sh. 2,500. How much will Mary pay for 3 similar books? A: 1500. One book costs 2,500 ÷ 5 = 500, so 3 books cost 1,500.
chunks.source: One book costs 2,500 ÷ 5 = 500, so 3 books cost 1,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The cost of 2 pencils is sh. 800. What is the cost of 6 similar pencils? A: 2400. One pencil costs 800 ÷ 2 = 400, so 6 pencils cost 2,400.
chunks.source: One pencil costs 800 ÷ 2 = 400, so 6 pencils cost 2,400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Joan bought a radio at sh. 50,000 and sold it at a loss of sh. 5,000. What was the selling price? A: 45000. 50,000 − 5,000 = 45,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Bony went to the market with sh. 8,000 and bought: 3 mangoes at sh. 800 each, a heap of four oranges at sh. 2,000, and 3 apples at sh. 1,200 each. How much did he spend altogether? A: 8000. (3 × 800) + 2,000 + (3 × 1,200) = 2,400 + 2,000 + 3,600 = 8,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Bony went to the market with sh. 8,000 and spent sh. 8,000. Find his change. A: 0. 8,000 − 8,000 = 0.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Katongole bought a T.V. at sh. 45,500 and later sold it at sh. 50,000. How much profit did he make? A: 4500. 50,000 − 45,500 = 4,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: It costs sh. 4,000 to travel from Kampala to Jinja and sh. 7,000 from Jinja to Mbale. How much will one person pay for the journey from Kampala to Mbale? A: 11000. 4,000 + 7,000 = 11,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: It costs sh. 11,000 for one person to travel from Kampala to Mbale. If 5 people are travelling, how much will they pay altogether? A: 55000. 11,000 × 5 = 55,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Okoth sold a goat at sh. 85,000 and made a loss of sh. 13,000. How much did she buy the goat? A: 98000. 85,000 + 13,000 = 98,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Complete the shopping list: Sugar, 4 kg at sh. 2,400 per kg. What is the total cost of the sugar? A: 9600. 4 × 2,400 = 9,600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Complete the shopping list: Bread costs sh. 3,500 per loaf and the total for bread is sh. 7,000. How many loaves were bought? A: 2. 7,000 ÷ 3,500 = 2 loaves.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A shopping list totals sh. 9,600 for sugar, sh. 7,000 for bread and sh. 400 for salt. What is the grand total? A: 17000. 9,600 + 7,000 + 400 = 17,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Kalungi paid sh. 17,000 from a sh. 20,000 note. What balance did he receive? A: 3000. 20,000 − 17,000 = 3,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A book costs sh. 300. Find the cost of four similar books. A: 1200. 300 × 4 = 1,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mugisha bought a bull at sh. 250,000 and later sold it at sh. 320,000. How much profit did he make? A: 70000. 320,000 − 250,000 = 70,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5 books cost sh. 2,000. Find the cost of 8 similar books. A: 3200. One book costs 2,000 ÷ 5 = 400, so 8 books cost 3,200.
chunks.source: One book costs 2,000 ÷ 5 = 400, so 8 books cost 3,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A man bought 2 kg of sugar at sh. 3,200 per kg, 1/2 litre of cooking oil at sh. 4,000 a litre, and 4 kg of Irish potatoes at sh. 6,000. How much money did he spend? A: 14400. (2 × 3,200) + (1/2 × 4,000) + 6,000 = 6,400 + 2,000 + 6,000 = 14,400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A man went to the market with sh. 20,000 and spent sh. 14,400. How much money did he remain with? A: 5600. 20,000 − 14,400 = 5,600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Musa sold a pair of trousers at sh. 16,000, making a profit of sh. 4,000. How much did he buy the pair of trousers? A: 12000. 16,000 − 4,000 = 12,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Martha's bill: 2 dozen books cost sh. 12,000. What was the unit cost per dozen? A: 6000. 12,000 ÷ 2 = 6,000 per dozen.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Martha's bill: 1 1/2 dozen pens at sh. 4,000 per dozen. What was the amount for the pens? A: 6000. 1 1/2 × 4,000 = 6,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Martha's bill: rulers cost sh. 600 each and the amount for rulers was sh. 2,400. How many rulers did she buy? A: 4. 2,400 ÷ 600 = 4 rulers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Martha's bill: 3 rubbers cost sh. 2,250. What was the unit cost of one rubber? A: 750. 2,250 ÷ 3 = 750.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Martha spent sh. 12,000 on books, sh. 6,000 on pens, sh. 2,400 on rulers and sh. 2,250 on rubbers. What was her total expenditure? A: 22650. 12,000 + 6,000 + 2,400 + 2,250 = 22,650.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Martha spent sh. 22,650 and remained with sh. 2,350. How much money did she have at first? A: 25000. 22,650 + 2,350 = 25,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A shirt costs sh. 4,000. How many shirts can a person buy with sh. 32,000? A: 8. 32,000 ÷ 4,000 = 8 shirts.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Calvin bought a mathematical set at sh. 2,500 and later sold it at a loss of sh. 500. How much did he sell the mathematical set? A: 2000. 2,500 − 500 = 2,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A kilogram of salt costs sh. 800. How much will a person pay for 750 g of salt? A: 600. 750 g = 3/4 kg, so 3/4 × 800 = 600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A shopkeeper made a profit of sh. 7,600 after selling a box of milk at sh. 39,200. What was the buying price of the box of milk? A: 31600. 39,200 − 7,600 = 31,600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The cost of an exercise book is sh. 1,000. Find the cost of a dozen similar books. A: 12000. 1,000 × 12 = 12,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A cup's buying price is sh. 1,500 and its selling price is sh. 1,800. Find the profit made. A: 300. 1,800 − 1,500 = 300.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1 kg of sugar costs sh. 5,500 and 1 litre of milk costs sh. 2,400. Find the total cost of 2 kg of sugar and 3 litres of milk. A: 18200. (2 × 5,500) + (3 × 2,400) = 11,000 + 7,200 = 18,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Clare had sh. 20,000 and bought 3 loaves of bread at sh. 4,500 each. Find her change. A: 6500. 20,000 − 13,500 = 6,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The 5 children who enjoy both drinks each got sh. 1,000. How much money did they get altogether? A: 5000. 5 × 1,000 = 5,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Paul bought 2 pens at sh. 1,500 each, 6 books at sh. 500 each and a geometry set at sh. 2,800. Find his total expenditure. A: 8800. 3,000 + 3,000 + 2,800 = 8,800.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Paul spent sh. 8,800 and got sh. 1,200 change. How much money did he go with? A: 10000. 8,800 + 1,200 = 10,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Privah had a five thousand shilling note and bought 2 kg of sugar at sh. 2,400 per kg. What was her change? A: 200. 5,000 − 4,800 = 200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Tinah collected: 20 notes of sh. 1,000, 10 coins of sh. 500 and 30 coins of sh. 200. Find her total collection. A: 31000. 20,000 + 5,000 + 6,000 = 31,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Liz collected: 10 notes of sh. 1,000, 30 coins of sh. 500 and 15 coins of sh. 200. Find her total collection. A: 28000. 10,000 + 15,000 + 3,000 = 28,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 3? 65, 72, 83, 94 A: 72. 7 + 2 = 9, and 9 is divisible by 3, so 72 is divisible by 3.
chunks.source: 7 + 2 = 9, and 9 is divisible by 3, so 72 is divisible by 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the product of the next two missing numbers: 2, 3, 5, 7, ___, ___ A: 143. The sequence lists prime numbers, so the next two are 11 and 13, and 11 × 13 = 143.
chunks.source: The sequence lists prime numbers, so the next two are 11 and 13, and 11 × 13 = 143.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the square of 7? A: 49. 7² = 7 × 7 = 49.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the square root of 121. A: 11. 11 × 11 = 121, so √121 = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: List all the factors of 36 by selecting them. A: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. The factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18 and 36.
chunks.source: The factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18 and 36.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 5, 6, 8, 11, 15, ___ A: 20. The differences grow by 1 each time (1, 2, 3, 4), so the next difference is 5 and 15 + 5 = 20.
chunks.source: The differences grow by 1 each time (1, 2, 3, 4), so the next difference is 5 and 15 + 5 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: (½ of 18) + (¼ of 16) A: 13. ½ of 18 is 9 and ¼ of 16 is 4, so 9 + 4 = 13.
chunks.source: ½ of 18 is 9 and ¼ of 16 is 4, so 9 + 4 = 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the GCF of 32 and 48? A: 16. The greatest number that divides both 32 and 48 is 16.
chunks.source: The greatest number that divides both 32 and 48 is 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If y² = 81, find the value of y. A: 9. 9 × 9 = 81, so y = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the LCM of 16 and 24. A: 48. The smallest number both 16 and 24 divide into is 48.
chunks.source: The smallest number both 16 and 24 divide into is 48.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the figure shown below. A: Cube. All edges are equal and marked the same, so the figure is a cube.
chunks.source: All edges are equal and marked the same, so the figure is a cube.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the volume of the figure shown below. A: 216. Volume = 6 × 6 × 6 = 216 cm³.
chunks.source: Volume = 6 × 6 × 6 = 216 cm³.

chunks.subject: Math
