chunks.text: Q: Find the missing numbers in the factor tree of 18 below. Write them from top to bottom, separated by a comma. A: 9, 3. 18 = 2 × 9 and 9 = 3 × 3, so the missing numbers are 9 and 3.
chunks.source: 18 = 2 × 9 and 9 = 3 × 3, so the missing numbers are 9 and 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 213 ___ 312 A: <. 213 is smaller than 312.
chunks.source: 213 is smaller than 312.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: ¾ of 16 ___ ⅔ of 18 A: =. ¾ of 16 = 12 and ⅔ of 18 = 12, so they are equal.
chunks.source: ¾ of 16 = 12 and ⅔ of 18 = 12, so they are equal.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 2 m ___ 150 cm A: >. 2 m = 200 cm, which is more than 150 cm.
chunks.source: 2 m = 200 cm, which is more than 150 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: XCV ___ C A: <. XCV = 95 and C = 100, so 95 < 100.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 16, 21, 26, 31, 36, ___ A: 41. Each number is 5 more than the one before, so 36 + 5 = 41.
chunks.source: Each number is 5 more than the one before, so 36 + 5 = 41.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The cards show 8, 12 and 6. Find the lowest common multiple of the numbers. A: 24. The smallest number all three divide into is 24.
chunks.source: The smallest number all three divide into is 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: List all the factors of 12. A: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
chunks.source: The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the greatest common factor of 8 and 6. A: 2. The biggest number dividing both 8 and 6 is 2.
chunks.source: The biggest number dividing both 8 and 6 is 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the sum of the first three prime numbers. A: 10. 2 + 3 + 5 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The Venn diagram shows prime factors of x and y. Find the value of y. A: 18. y = 2 × 3 × 3 = 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The Venn diagram shows prime factors of x and y. Find the value of x. A: 30. x = 2 × 3 × 5 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The Venn diagram shows prime factors of x and y. Find the GCF of Fx and Fy. A: 6. GCF = 2 × 3 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 20, 16, 12, 8, ___ A: 4. Each number drops by 4, so 8 − 4 = 4.
chunks.source: Each number drops by 4, so 8 − 4 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the lowest common multiple of 8 and 6. A: 24. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24... of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24. LCM = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the mixed number 3 2/4, match each part to its name. A: 2,numerator, 4,denominator, 3,whole number. In 3 2/4, the 3 is the whole number, 2 is the numerator and 4 is the denominator.
chunks.source: In 3 2/4, the 3 is the whole number, 2 is the numerator and 4 is the denominator.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 3 2/4 as an improper fraction. A: 14/4. 3 2/4 = (3 × 4 + 2)/4 = 14/4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A driver covered 1/3 of his journey of 72 km. What distance did he cover? A: 24. 1/3 of 72 = 72 ÷ 3 = 24 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the missing number: 3/5 = 12/__ A: 20. 3 × 4 = 12, so 5 × 4 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A grid has 12 equal squares. To show 3/4 of the grid, how many squares must be shaded? A: 9. 3/4 of 12 = 9 squares.
chunks.source: 3/4 of 12 = 9 squares.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 32/3 as a mixed fraction. A: 10 2/3. 32 ÷ 3 = 10 remainder 2, so 32/3 = 10 2/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use <, > or = to compare: 18/24 ___ 6/8 A: =. 18/24 = 3/4 and 6/8 = 3/4, so they are equal.
chunks.source: 18/24 = 3/4 and 6/8 = 3/4, so they are equal.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: On a farm of 30 animals, 3/5 of them are cows and the rest are goats. How many cows are on the farm? A: 18. 3/5 of 30 = 18 cows.
chunks.source: 3/5 of 30 = 18 cows.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: On a farm of 30 animals, 3/5 of them are cows and the rest are goats. How many goats are on the farm? A: 12. 30 − 18 = 12 goats.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: On a farm of 30 animals, 3/5 of them are cows and the rest are goats. What fraction of the animals are goats? A: 2/5. 1 − 3/5 = 2/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: On a farm of 30 animals, 3/5 of them are cows and the rest are goats. How many more cows than goats are on the farm? A: 6. 18 − 12 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a P.5 class of 50 pupils, 3/10 of them were absent and the rest were present. What fraction of the class was present? A: 7/10. 1 − 3/10 = 7/10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a P.5 class of 50 pupils, 3/10 of them were absent. How many pupils were absent? A: 15. 3/10 of 50 = 15 pupils.
chunks.source: 3/10 of 50 = 15 pupils.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a P.5 class of 50 pupils, 3/10 were absent and the rest were present. How many more pupils were present than absent? A: 20. Present = 35 and absent = 15, so 35 − 15 = 20.
chunks.source: Present = 35 and absent = 15, so 35 − 15 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arrange these fractions in descending order: 5/6, 2/3, 1/4, 3/4 A: 5/6, 3/4, 2/3, 1/4. From biggest to smallest: 5/6, 3/4, 2/3, 1/4.
chunks.source: From biggest to smallest: 5/6, 3/4, 2/3, 1/4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 3/4 ___ 6/8 A: =. 6/8 simplifies to 3/4, so they are equal.
chunks.source: 6/8 simplifies to 3/4, so they are equal.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 2/3 ___ 5/6 A: <. 2/3 = 4/6, which is less than 5/6.
chunks.source: 2/3 = 4/6, which is less than 5/6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 1/3 ___ 1/4 A: >. When numerators are the same, the smaller denominator gives the bigger fraction.
chunks.source: When numerators are the same, the smaller denominator gives the bigger fraction.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 13/13 as a mixed fraction. A: 1. 13/13 = 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 1/2 kg as grams. A: 500. 1 kg = 1,000 g, so 1/2 kg = 500 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 2 4/5 to an improper fraction. A: 14/5. 2 4/5 = (2 × 5 + 4)/5 = 14/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arrange 4.4, 0.4, 4.04 and 0.04 in ascending order. A: 0.04, 0.4, 4.04, 4.4. From smallest to biggest: 0.04, 0.4, 4.04, 4.4.
chunks.source: From smallest to biggest: 0.04, 0.4, 4.04, 4.4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many half-litre bottles of milk can be got from a container of 20 litres? A: 40. 20 ÷ 1/2 = 40 bottles.
chunks.source: 20 ÷ 1/2 = 40 bottles.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 1/2 ___ 4/8 A: =. 4/8 simplifies to 1/2.
chunks.source: 4/8 simplifies to 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 1/3 ___ 1/2 A: <. 1/3 is smaller than 1/2.
chunks.source: 1/3 is smaller than 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 3/4 ___ 6/12 A: >. 3/4 = 9/12, which is bigger than 6/12.
chunks.source: 3/4 = 9/12, which is bigger than 6/12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in ascending order: 1/2, 1/4, 1/3 A: 1/4, 1/3, 1/2. From smallest to biggest: 1/4, 1/3, 1/2.
chunks.source: From smallest to biggest: 1/4, 1/3, 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in descending order: 5/6, 1/2, 2/3 A: 5/6, 2/3, 1/2. From biggest to smallest: 5/6, 2/3, 1/2.
chunks.source: From biggest to smallest: 5/6, 2/3, 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a class of 48 pupils, 3/4 of them eat meat and the rest eat fish. What fraction of the class eats fish? A: 1/4. 1 − 3/4 = 1/4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a class of 48 pupils, 3/4 of them eat meat. How many children eat meat? A: 36. 3/4 of 48 = 36.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a class of 48 pupils, 3/4 eat meat and the rest eat fish. How many more children eat meat than fish? A: 24. Meat eaters = 36 and fish eaters = 12, so 36 − 12 = 24.
chunks.source: Meat eaters = 36 and fish eaters = 12, so 36 − 12 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mary ate 1/2 of the sugar cane on Monday and 2/5 on Tuesday. What fraction did she remain with? A: 1/10. 1/2 + 2/5 = 9/10, so 1 − 9/10 = 1/10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in descending order: 0.2, 0.6, 0.8, 0.4 A: 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2. From biggest to smallest: 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2.
chunks.source: From biggest to smallest: 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A mother shared 36 pieces of watermelon: Mark got 1/3, Mike got 1/4 and Moses got the rest. How many pieces did Mark get? A: 12. 1/3 of 36 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A mother shared 36 pieces of watermelon: Mark got 1/3, Mike got 1/4 and Moses got the rest. How many pieces did Mike get? A: 9. 1/4 of 36 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A mother shared 36 pieces of watermelon: Mark got 1/3, Mike got 1/4 and Moses got the rest. How many pieces did Moses get? A: 15. 36 − 12 − 9 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 0.5 as a reduced proper fraction. A: 1/2. 0.5 = 5/10 = 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 15/2 as a mixed number. A: 7 1/2. 15 ÷ 2 = 7 remainder 1, so 7 1/2.
chunks.source: 15 ÷ 2 = 7 remainder 1, so 7 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in ascending order: 1/4, 1/2, 1/5 A: 1/5, 1/4, 1/2. Smallest to biggest: 1/5, 1/4, 1/2.
chunks.source: Smallest to biggest: 1/5, 1/4, 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Bianca gave 3/7 of an apple to Benita, 1/7 to Mellisa and the rest to Davita. What fraction did Davita get? A: 3/7. 1 − 3/7 − 1/7 = 3/7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: An Omni bus had 15 seats. If 3/5 were occupied, how many free seats were in the bus? A: 6. 3/5 of 15 = 9 occupied, so 15 − 9 = 6 free.
chunks.source: 3/5 of 15 = 9 occupied, so 15 − 9 = 6 free.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a class of 70 pupils, 3/5 are girls and the rest are boys. Find the fraction of boys. A: 2/5. 1 − 3/5 = 2/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a class of 70 pupils, 3/5 are girls and the rest are boys. How many boys are there? A: 28. 2/5 of 70 = 28.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a class of 70 pupils, 3/5 are girls and the rest are boys. How many girls are there? A: 42. 3/5 of 70 = 42.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 1/2 as a decimal fraction. A: 0.5. 1/2 = 0.5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in descending order: 1/3, 1/2, 1/4 A: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4. Biggest to smallest: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4.
chunks.source: Biggest to smallest: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Group these fractions: 3/4, 7/3, 2/7, 9/4 A: Proper: 3/4,2/7; Improper: 7/3,9/4. Proper fractions have a smaller top than bottom.
chunks.source: Proper fractions have a smaller top than bottom.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the value of angle y in the diagram below. A: 28. y = 90° − 62° = 28°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the value of angle k in the diagram below. A: 40. k = 180° − 50° − 90° = 40°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: An equilateral triangle has sides of 6 cm. Find its perimeter. A: 18. 6 × 3 = 18 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the area of the shaded triangle in the rectangle below (base 12 dm, height 8 dm). A: 48. Area = 1/2 × 12 × 8 = 48 dm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many lines of symmetry does a semicircle have? A: 1. Only the vertical line through the middle works.
chunks.source: Only the vertical line through the middle works.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a right angle split into m and 15°. Find the value of 2m. A: 150. m = 90° − 15° = 75°, so 2m = 150°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The right-angled triangle below has angles k and 43°. Find k. A: 47. k = 90° − 43° = 47°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The triangle below has angles 40°, p and 75°. Find p. A: 65. p = 180° − 40° − 75° = 65°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The angles 131° and m sit on a straight line. Find m. A: 49. m = 180° − 131° = 49°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The cuboid below measures 15 hm by 10 hm by 3 hm, with the front face shaded. Work out the area of the shaded portion. A: 45. 15 × 3 = 45 hm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The cuboid below measures 15 hm by 10 hm by 3 hm. Calculate its volume. A: 450. 15 × 10 × 3 = 450 hm³.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many edges does a cuboid have? A: 12. A cuboid has 12 edges.
chunks.source: A cuboid has 12 edges.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The arrow on the number line below starts at −1 and ends at +3. What integer does the arrowhead point to? A: 3. The arrowhead lands on +3.
chunks.source: The arrowhead lands on +3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the integers in descending order: −3, 3, 0, 2, 1, −1, −4 A: 3, 2, 1, 0, −1, −3, −4. From biggest to smallest: 3, 2, 1, 0, −1, −3, −4.
chunks.source: From biggest to smallest: 3, 2, 1, 0, −1, −3, −4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: −3 ___ 3 A: <. −3 is less than 3.
chunks.source: −3 is less than 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: −7 ___ −6 A: <. −7 is further from zero on the negative side, so −7 < −6.
chunks.source: −7 is further from zero on the negative side, so −7 < −6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 0 ___ −2 A: >. 0 is greater than any negative number.
chunks.source: 0 is greater than any negative number.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use a number line to work out: 2 − 3 + +6 A: 5. 2 − 3 = −1 and −1 + 6 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the median of the integers: 0, −3, 4, −3, −2, 5, −5 A: −2. In order: −5, −3, −3, −2, 0, 4, 5. The middle value is −2.
chunks.source: In order: −5, −3, −3, −2, 0, 4, 5. The middle value is −2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use a number line to work out: 2 × 4 A: 8. 2 × 4 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the range of the integers: −2, 0, 4, −5, 3 A: 9. 4 − (−5) = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the inverse (opposite) of +6. A: −6. The opposite of +6 is −6.
chunks.source: The opposite of +6 is −6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Aminah jumped 4 metres backwards and then 9 metres forward. How far is she now from her original place? A: 5. −4 + 9 = 5 metres forward.
chunks.source: −4 + 9 = 5 metres forward.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the integer represented by the arrowhead b on the number line below. A: -2. The arrowhead lands on −2.
chunks.source: The arrowhead lands on −2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that a = −4 and b = 6, find the value of a + b. A: 2. −4 + 6 = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in descending order: −4, +4, 0, +9 A: +9, +4, 0, −4. From biggest to smallest: +9, +4, 0, −4.
chunks.source: From biggest to smallest: +9, +4, 0, −4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Group these integers: −3, 5, 0, −7, 2, −1 A: Positive: 5,2; Negative: -3,-7,-1; Zero: 0. Positives are 5 and 2, negatives are −3, −7 and −1, and 0 is zero.
chunks.source: Positives are 5 and 2, negatives are −3, −7 and −1, and 0 is zero.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: John bought 22 cows. How many cows do the tallies below represent? A: 22. The tallies count 22.
chunks.source: The tallies count 22.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The bar graph below shows marks: Joy 80, Mary 70, John 60, David 70, Jane 60. Who scored the highest mark? A: Joy. Joy's bar is the tallest at 80 marks.
chunks.source: Joy's bar is the tallest at 80 marks.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The bar graph below shows marks: Joy 80, Mary 70, John 60, David 70, Jane 60. Which marks are the modal marks? A: 60, 70. Both 60 and 70 appear twice, so both are modal.
chunks.source: Both 60 and 70 appear twice, so both are modal.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The bar graph below shows marks: Joy 80, Mary 70, John 60, David 70, Jane 60. How many more marks did Mary get than Jane? A: 10. 70 − 60 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The bar graph below shows marks: Joy 80, Mary 70, John 60, David 70, Jane 60. Find the total marks of Mary, Joy and John. A: 210. 70 + 80 + 60 = 210.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: One picture represents 12 trees. How many trees do 2 such pictures represent? A: 24. 12 × 2 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the tally table. The Posho row shows 5 groups of five tallies. What is the frequency for Posho? A: 25. 5 × 5 = 25.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the tally table. Rice has a frequency of 10. How many tally marks should be drawn for Rice? A: 10. The tally marks must equal the frequency, 10.
chunks.source: The tally marks must equal the frequency, 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: One chair picture represents 6 chairs. How many pictures are needed to represent 24 chairs? A: 4. 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The graph shows litres of milk sold: Mon 30, Tue 40, Wed 30, Thu 35, Fri 50. Which two days had the same number of litres sold? A: Monday and Wednesday. Both Monday and Wednesday sold 30 litres.
chunks.source: Both Monday and Wednesday sold 30 litres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The graph shows litres of milk sold: Mon 30, Tue 40, Wed 30, Thu 35, Fri 50. How many litres were sold on Thursday? A: 35. Thursday's bar reaches 35.
chunks.source: Thursday's bar reaches 35.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The graph shows litres of milk sold: Mon 30, Tue 40, Wed 30, Thu 35, Fri 50. How many litres were sold on Tuesday and Friday altogether? A: 90. 40 + 50 = 90.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Wangwe's scores: Mathematics 95, English 70, Science 90, Social studies 85. How many subjects did Wangwe write? A: 4. There are 4 subjects in the table.
chunks.source: There are 4 subjects in the table.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Wangwe's scores: Mathematics 95, English 70, Science 90, Social studies 85. In which subject did he score highest? A: Mathematics. 95 is the biggest score.
chunks.source: 95 is the biggest score.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Wangwe's scores: Mathematics 95, English 70, Science 90, Social studies 85. In which subject did he score lowest? A: English. 70 is the smallest score.
chunks.source: 70 is the smallest score.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Wangwe's scores: Mathematics 95, English 70, Science 90, Social studies 85. Find the difference between the highest and the lowest scores. A: 25. 95 − 70 = 25.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Wangwe's scores: Mathematics 95, English 70, Science 90, Social studies 85. Find his total mark in all subjects. A: 340. 95 + 70 + 90 + 85 = 340.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: It started raining at 2:20 am and stopped at 8:10 am. How long did the rain take? A: 5 hours 50 minutes. From 2:20 to 8:10 is 5 hours 50 minutes.
chunks.source: From 2:20 to 8:10 is 5 hours 50 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A forty-minute lesson started at 8:10 am. At what time did it end? A: 8:50 am. 8:10 + 40 minutes = 8:50 am.
chunks.source: 8:10 + 40 minutes = 8:50 am.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the distance a driver covers at 15 kilometres per hour for 3 hours. A: 45. Distance = speed × time = 15 × 3 = 45 km.
chunks.source: Distance = speed × time = 15 × 3 = 45 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A cyclist covered a journey of 100 km at a speed of 40 km/h. How long did it take him? A: 2.5. Time = distance ÷ speed = 100 ÷ 40 = 2.5 hours.
chunks.source: Time = distance ÷ speed = 100 ÷ 40 = 2.5 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Alupo travelled from Kitgum to Luweero, a distance of 616 km, in 7 hours. Find her average speed. A: 88. Speed = 616 ÷ 7 = 88 km/h.
chunks.source: Speed = 616 ÷ 7 = 88 km/h.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A dance competition started at 8:00 am and ended at 9:10 am. How long did the dance take? A: 1 hour 10 minutes. From 8:00 to 9:10 is 1 hour 10 minutes.
chunks.source: From 8:00 to 9:10 is 1 hour 10 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many minutes are in 1 1/2 hours? A: 90. 1 1/2 × 60 = 90 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A motorist travelled at 70 km/h for 3 hours. What distance did he cover? A: 210. 70 × 3 = 210 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Add: 4 hours 25 minutes + 1 hour 46 minutes A: 6 hours 11 minutes. 25 + 46 = 71 minutes = 1 hour 11 minutes, so 4 + 1 + 1 = 6 hours 11 minutes.
chunks.source: 25 + 46 = 71 minutes = 1 hour 11 minutes, so 4 + 1 + 1 = 6 hours 11 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Tell the time shown on the clock face. A: 7:20. The hour hand is past 7 and the minute hand is on 4, so it is 7:20.
chunks.source: The hour hand is past 7 and the minute hand is on 4, so it is 7:20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the number of minutes in an hour. A: 60. One hour has 60 minutes.
chunks.source: One hour has 60 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What time is shown on the clock face below? A: 8:00. The hour hand points at 8 and the minute hand at 12, so it is 8:00.
chunks.source: The hour hand points at 8 and the minute hand at 12, so it is 8:00.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many 1/4 litre bottles are in a 2 litre jerrycan? A: 8. 2 ÷ 1/4 = 8 bottles.
chunks.source: 2 ÷ 1/4 = 8 bottles.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Okoth's baby was born weighing 5 kg. How many grams was the baby? A: 5000. 1 kg = 1,000 g, so 5 kg = 5,000 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 4.75 metres in centimetres. A: 475. 1 m = 100 cm, so 4.75 × 100 = 475 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The area of a rectangle is 42 cm² and its length is 7 cm. Find its width. A: 6. Width = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 cm.
chunks.source: Width = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The area of a rectangle is 42 cm² and its length is 7 cm. Calculate its perimeter. A: 26. Width = 6 cm, so perimeter = 2 × (7 + 6) = 26 cm.
chunks.source: Width = 6 cm, so perimeter = 2 × (7 + 6) = 26 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 2 metres to centimetres. A: 200. 2 × 100 = 200 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 4.2 km in metres. A: 4200. 4.2 × 1,000 = 4,200 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Subtract: 4 kg 427 g − 2 kg 609 g A: 1 kg 818 g. Borrow 1 kg: 3 kg 1,427 g − 2 kg 609 g = 1 kg 818 g.
chunks.source: Borrow 1 kg: 3 kg 1,427 g − 2 kg 609 g = 1 kg 818 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The perimeter of a square playground is 36 cm. Find the length of its sides. A: 9. 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The perimeter of a square playground is 36 cm. Work out its area. A: 81. Side = 9 cm, so area = 9 × 9 = 81 cm².
chunks.source: Side = 9 cm, so area = 9 × 9 = 81 cm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 2,000 ml into litres. A: 2. 1,000 ml = 1 litre, so 2,000 ml = 2 litres.
chunks.source: 1,000 ml = 1 litre, so 2,000 ml = 2 litres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Calculate the area of the outer rectangle shown below. A: 84. Area = 12 × 7 = 84 cm².
chunks.source: Area = 12 × 7 = 84 cm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the area of the inner rectangle shown below. A: 24. Area = 6 × 4 = 24 cm².
chunks.source: Area = 6 × 4 = 24 cm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the area of the shaded part shown below? A: 60. 84 − 24 = 60 cm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the cuboid below. How many vertices does it have? A: 8. A cuboid has 8 vertices.
chunks.source: A cuboid has 8 vertices.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the cuboid below. How many edges does it have? A: 12. A cuboid has 12 edges.
chunks.source: A cuboid has 12 edges.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the cuboid below. How many faces does it have? A: 6. A cuboid has 6 faces.
chunks.source: A cuboid has 6 faces.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Calculate the area of the shaded (top) face of the cuboid below. A: 45. Area = 9 × 5 = 45 cm².
chunks.source: Area = 9 × 5 = 45 cm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the volume of the cuboid below. A: 270. Volume = 9 × 5 × 6 = 270 cm³.
chunks.source: Volume = 9 × 5 × 6 = 270 cm³.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the total surface area of the cuboid below. A: 258. 2 × (45 + 54 + 30) = 258 cm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the figure below. Find the value of X. A: 9. X = 6 + 3 = 9 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the figure below. Find the value of Y. A: 8. Y = 12 − 4 = 8 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the perimeter of the figure below. A: 42. Perimeter = 2 × (12 + 9) = 42 cm.
chunks.source: Perimeter = 2 × (12 + 9) = 42 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the area of the figure below. A: 84. Area = (12 × 9) − (8 × 3) = 108 − 24 = 84 cm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Calculate the area of the triangle below. A: 40. Area = 1/2 × 10 × 8 = 40 dm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The area of the rectangle below is 40 cm² and its length is 8 cm. Find its width. A: 5. Width = 40 ÷ 8 = 5 cm.
chunks.source: Width = 40 ÷ 8 = 5 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The area of the rectangle below is 40 cm² and its length is 8 cm. Work out its perimeter. A: 26. Width = 5 cm, so perimeter = 2 × (8 + 5) = 26 cm.
chunks.source: Width = 5 cm, so perimeter = 2 × (8 + 5) = 26 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the area of the trapezium below. A: 69. Area = 1/2 × (8 + 15) × 6 = 69 cm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the area of the shaded part below. A: 74. Rectangle = 110 cm² and triangle = 36 cm², so shaded = 110 − 36 = 74 cm².
chunks.source: Rectangle = 110 cm² and triangle = 36 cm², so shaded = 110 − 36 = 74 cm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The volume of the cuboid below is 120 m³. Find the value of h. A: 5. h = 120 ÷ (6 × 4) = 5 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The cuboid below measures 6 m by 4 m by 5 m. Work out its total surface area. A: 148. 2 × (24 + 30 + 20) = 148 m².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Calculate the area of the shaded (top) face of the cuboid below. A: 24. Area = 6 × 4 = 24 m².
chunks.source: Area = 6 × 4 = 24 m².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the area of the figure below? (Each small square = 1 cm²) A: 15. There are 15 unit squares, so the area is 15 cm².
chunks.source: There are 15 unit squares, so the area is 15 cm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In the circle below, lines are drawn from the centre Y to the circumference. What is such a line called? A: radius. A line from the centre to the circumference is a radius.
chunks.source: A line from the centre to the circumference is a radius.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If the diameter of a circle is 8 cm, find its radius. A: 4. Radius = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.
chunks.source: Radius = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a rectangular swimming pool 75 m by 50 m. If Mary walks around the pool once, what distance will she cover? A: 250. Perimeter = 2 × (75 + 50) = 250 m.
chunks.source: Perimeter = 2 × (75 + 50) = 250 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 12,500 grammes into kilogrammes. A: 12.5. 12,500 ÷ 1,000 = 12.5 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Jessy filled a 1,000 litre container using a 250 litre container. How many times did he fill the small container? A: 4. 1,000 ÷ 250 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The distance from P to Q is 100 cm. If Angela's stride is 20 cm long, how many strides will she make from P to Q? A: 5. 100 ÷ 20 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the area of the shaded region: a 20 dm by 6 dm rectangle with an 8 dm by 4 dm rectangle cut out. A: 88. (20 × 6) − (8 × 4) = 120 − 32 = 88 dm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 7 metres to centimetres. A: 700. 7 × 100 = 700 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many half-litre bottles can fill a 20-litre jerrycan? A: 40. 20 ÷ 1/2 = 40.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The rectangle below is 14 dm by 6 dm. Double its perimeter. A: 80. Perimeter = 2 × (14 + 6) = 40 dm, doubled = 80 dm.
chunks.source: Perimeter = 2 × (14 + 6) = 40 dm, doubled = 80 dm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Simplify: 2b − b + 3b A: 4b. 2b − b + 3b = 4b.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that x = 2, y = 3 and z = 4, find the value of x + y + z. A: 9. 2 + 3 + 4 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that x = 2, y = 3 and z = 4, find the value of xyz. A: 24. 2 × 3 × 4 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that x = 2, y = 3 and z = 4, find the value of xy + z. A: 10. (2 × 3) + 4 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that x = 2, y = 3 and z = 4, find the value of yz ÷ (x + z). A: 2. (3 × 4) ÷ (2 + 4) = 12 ÷ 6 = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: I think of a number, add 6 to it and the answer is 13. What is the number? A: 7. 13 − 6 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Collect like terms: 2x + 4y + 3x + y A: 5x + 5y. 2x + 3x = 5x and 4y + y = 5y.
chunks.source: 2x + 3x = 5x and 4y + y = 5y.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Collect like terms: 4m + 2n − m + n A: 3m + 3n. 4m − m = 3m and 2n + n = 3n.
chunks.source: 4m − m = 3m and 2n + n = 3n.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Collect like terms: 7k − 2p + k + 6p A: 8k + 4p. 7k + k = 8k and −2p + 6p = 4p.
chunks.source: 7k + k = 8k and −2p + 6p = 4p.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The area of a rectangle is 60 cm² and its length is 12 cm. Find its width. A: 5. Width = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 cm.
chunks.source: Width = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The area of a rectangle is 60 cm² and its length is 12 cm. Work out its perimeter. A: 34. Width = 5 cm, so perimeter = 2 × (12 + 5) = 34 cm.
chunks.source: Width = 5 cm, so perimeter = 2 × (12 + 5) = 34 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that x² = 36, find the value of x. A: 6. 6 × 6 = 36, so x = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve: 2x + 3x = 20 A: 4. 5x = 20, so x = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve: 4x − 2 + x = 8 A: 2. 5x = 10, so x = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve: 3n − 4 = n A: 2. 2n = 4, so n = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What number, when divided by 3, gives 5 as the answer? A: 15. 5 × 3 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The perimeter of a rectangle is 26 dm and its length is 7 dm. Find its width. A: 6. Width = (26 − 14) ÷ 2 = 6 dm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The perimeter of a rectangle is 26 dm and its length is 7 dm. Calculate its area. A: 42. Width = 6 dm, so area = 7 × 6 = 42 dm².
chunks.source: Width = 6 dm, so area = 7 × 6 = 42 dm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The area of a square garden is 144 m². Find the length of its sides. A: 12. 12 × 12 = 144, so each side is 12 m.
chunks.source: 12 × 12 = 144, so each side is 12 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The area of a square garden is 144 m². Work out the total distance round the garden. A: 48. Side = 12 m, so perimeter = 4 × 12 = 48 m.
chunks.source: Side = 12 m, so perimeter = 4 × 12 = 48 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the missing number: 2/3 = __/12 A: 8. 3 × 4 = 12, so 2 × 4 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve: 2p + p − 7 = 5 A: 4. 3p = 12, so p = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that a = 12, b = 20 and c = 15, find the value of 2a. A: 24. 2 × 12 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that a = 12, b = 20 and c = 15, find the value of (a + b) − c. A: 17. (12 + 20) − 15 = 17.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that a = 12 and b = 20, find the value of b ÷ 4. A: 5. 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The figure below is a rectangle with AB = 2y and DC = 12 dm. Find the value of y. A: 6. Opposite sides are equal, so 2y = 12 and y = 6.
chunks.source: Opposite sides are equal, so 2y = 12 and y = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The figure below is a rectangle with AD = k and BC = 8 dm. Find the value of k. A: 8. Opposite sides are equal, so k = 8.
chunks.source: Opposite sides are equal, so k = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Atim is 4 years older than Otim. Their total age is 20 years. How old is Atim? A: 12. Otim is 8 and Atim is 8 + 4 = 12.
chunks.source: Otim is 8 and Atim is 8 + 4 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that p = 10, q = 30 and r = 20, find the value of p + q. A: 40. 10 + 30 = 40.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that p = 10, q = 30 and r = 20, find the value of q + r. A: 50. 30 + 20 = 50.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that p = 10 and q = 30, find the value of q ÷ p. A: 3. 30 ÷ 10 = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Simplify: 5d + 3d + d A: 9d. 5 + 3 + 1 = 9, so 9d.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Collect like terms and simplify: 2y + p + 3y A: 5y + p. 2y + 3y = 5y, so 5y + p.
chunks.source: 2y + 3y = 5y, so 5y + p.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that e = 6, find the value of (2e) + (e × e). A: 48. 12 + 36 = 48.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Think of a number, add 4 to it, and the result becomes 11. Find the number. A: 7. 11 − 4 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that K = {z, e, r, o}, find n(K). A: 4. n(K) counts the members of set K, and there are 4 of them.
chunks.source: n(K) counts the members of set K, and there are 4 of them.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If D = {m, a, n, g, o} and E = {o, r, a, n, g, e}, find D ∩ E. A: {a, n, g, o}. D ∩ E keeps only the members found in both sets: a, n, g and o.
chunks.source: D ∩ E keeps only the members found in both sets: a, n, g and o.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If D = {m, a, n, g, o} and E = {o, r, a, n, g, e}, find n(D ∪ E). A: 7. D ∪ E = {m, a, n, g, o, r, e}, which has 7 members.
chunks.source: D ∪ E = {m, a, n, g, o, r, e}, which has 7 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What is the probability of tossing a coin and a head showing up? A: 1/2. A coin has 2 faces and only 1 is a head, so the probability is 1/2.
chunks.source: A coin has 2 faces and only 1 is a head, so the probability is 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is F = {prime numbers from 2 to 11} and G = {even numbers less than 10}. How many members are in F ∪ G? A: 9. F ∪ G = {0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11}, which has 9 members.
chunks.source: F ∪ G = {0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11}, which has 9 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is F = {prime numbers from 2 to 11} and G = {even numbers less than 10}. Find n(G − F). A: 4. G − F = {0, 4, 6, 8}, which has 4 members.
chunks.source: G − F = {0, 4, 6, 8}, which has 4 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a box there are 5 blue pens, 3 red pens and 7 black pens. If a pen is picked at random, what is the probability of picking a black pen? A: 7/15. There are 15 pens in total and 7 are black, so the probability is 7/15.
chunks.source: There are 15 pens in total and 7 are black, so the probability is 7/15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a box there are 5 blue pens, 3 red pens and 7 black pens. If a pen is picked at random, what is the probability of picking a red pen? A: 1/5. There are 15 pens in total and 3 are red, so the probability is 3/15 = 1/5.
chunks.source: There are 15 pens in total and 3 are red, so the probability is 3/15 = 1/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a box there are 5 blue pens, 3 red pens and 7 black pens. If a pen is picked at random, what is the probability of picking a blue pen? A: 1/3. There are 15 pens in total and 5 are blue, so the probability is 5/15 = 1/3.
chunks.source: There are 15 pens in total and 5 are blue, so the probability is 5/15 = 1/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If a die is tossed once, what is the probability of a prime number showing up? A: 1/2. The prime numbers on a die are 2, 3 and 5, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2.
chunks.source: The prime numbers on a die are 2, 3 and 5, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If a die is tossed once, what is the probability of a number less than 5 showing up? A: 2/3. The numbers less than 5 are 1, 2, 3 and 4, so the probability is 4/6 = 2/3.
chunks.source: The numbers less than 5 are 1, 2, 3 and 4, so the probability is 4/6 = 2/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If a die is tossed once, what is the probability of a 3 showing up? A: 1/6. A die has 6 faces and only one of them is a 3, so the probability is 1/6.
chunks.source: A die has 6 faces and only one of them is a 3, so the probability is 1/6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the Venn diagram below. How many members are in set D′? A: 2. All members shown are 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7. D = {0, 2, 5, 7}, so D′ = {1, 3}, which has 2 members.
chunks.source: All members shown are 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7. D = {0, 2, 5, 7}, so D′ = {1, 3}, which has 2 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the Venn diagram below. Find n(C ∩ D). A: 1. Only the number 2 is in both C and D, so n(C ∩ D) = 1.
chunks.source: Only the number 2 is in both C and D, so n(C ∩ D) = 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the Venn diagram below. Find n(C ∩ D)′. A: 5. C ∩ D = {2}, and out of the 6 members shown, 5 are not in it.
chunks.source: C ∩ D = {2}, and out of the 6 members shown, 5 are not in it.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the Venn diagram below. How many subsets does set D only have? A: 8. D only = {5, 7, 0} has 3 members, and a 3-member set has 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 subsets.
chunks.source: D only = {5, 7, 0} has 3 members, and a 3-member set has 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 subsets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Set G = {cat, dog, rabbit}. Find n(G). A: 3. Set G has 3 members.
chunks.source: Set G has 3 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the Venn diagram below. Find P ∪ Q. A: {hen, sheep, duck, cow, goat}. P ∪ Q joins all members without repeating: hen, sheep, duck, cow and goat.
chunks.source: P ∪ Q joins all members without repeating: hen, sheep, duck, cow and goat.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the Venn diagram below. Write the members of set Q. A: {sheep, duck, cow, goat}. Set Q contains sheep, duck, cow and goat.
chunks.source: Set Q contains sheep, duck, cow and goat.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the Venn diagram below. Find n(Q − P). A: 2. Q − P = {cow, goat}, which has 2 members.
chunks.source: Q − P = {cow, goat}, which has 2 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the number of subsets in set K = {cat, cow, rat}. A: 8. 2³ = 8 subsets.
chunks.source: 2³ = 8 subsets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a group, 30 children enjoy milk (M), 25 enjoy porridge (P) and 5 enjoy both. Use the Venn diagram. How many enjoy ONLY milk? A: 25. 30 − 5 = 25.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a group, 30 children enjoy milk (M), 25 enjoy porridge (P) and 5 enjoy both. Use the Venn diagram. How many enjoy ONLY porridge? A: 20. 25 − 5 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a group, 30 children enjoy milk, 25 enjoy porridge and 5 enjoy both. How many children do NOT enjoy milk? A: 20. Total = 25 + 5 + 20 = 50, so 50 − 30 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The Venn diagram shows B = {9, 10, 4, 5} and A = {4, 5, 6, 7, 8}. How many subsets does the set B only have? A: 4. B only = {9, 10}, which has 2² = 4 subsets.
chunks.source: B only = {9, 10}, which has 2² = 4 subsets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the Venn diagram. List all the elements in P − Q. A: {8, 9, 10}. P − Q = {8, 9, 10}.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the Venn diagram. List all the elements in P ∩ Q. A: {1, 3}. P ∩ Q = {1, 3}.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the Venn diagram. Find n(P ∪ Q). A: 9. P ∪ Q has 3 + 2 + 4 = 9 members.
chunks.source: P ∪ Q has 3 + 2 + 4 = 9 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Express 139 in Roman numerals. A: CXXXIX. 139 = 100 + 30 + 9, which is C + XXX + IX.
chunks.source: 139 = 100 + 30 + 9, which is C + XXX + IX.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the value of 3 in 3,201. A: 3000. The 3 stands for 3 thousands, which is 3,000.
chunks.source: The 3 stands for 3 thousands, which is 3,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write 'one million one thousand one' in figures. A: 1001001. One million one thousand one is written as 1,001,001.
chunks.source: One million one thousand one is written as 1,001,001.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Round off 438 to the nearest hundred. A: 400. 438 is closer to 400 than to 500, so it rounds to 400.
chunks.source: 438 is closer to 400 than to 500, so it rounds to 400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Convert XLIV to Hindu-Arabic numerals. A: 44. XLIV = (50 − 10) + (5 − 1) = 40 + 4 = 44.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Grandfather is 99 years old. Express his age in Roman numerals. A: XCIX. 99 = (100 − 10) + (10 − 1) = XC + IX.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the number that has been expanded as (7 × 10⁴) + (2 × 10²) + (8 × 10⁰). A: 70208. (7 × 10⁴) + (2 × 10²) + (8 × 10⁰) = 70,000 + 200 + 8 = 70,208.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the digits 4, 6, 1 and 2, form the biggest number. A: 6421. Arranging the digits from biggest to smallest gives 6,421.
chunks.source: Arranging the digits from biggest to smallest gives 6,421.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the digits 4, 6, 1 and 2, form the smallest number. A: 1246. Arranging the digits from smallest to biggest gives 1,246.
chunks.source: Arranging the digits from smallest to biggest gives 1,246.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the digits 4, 6, 1 and 2, find the sum of the largest and smallest numbers formed. A: 7667. 6,421 + 1,246 = 7,667.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the digits 4, 6, 1 and 2, find the difference between the largest and smallest numbers formed. A: 5175. 6,421 − 1,246 = 5,175.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Round off 3,878 to the nearest ten. A: 3880. 3,878 is closer to 3,880 than to 3,870.
chunks.source: 3,878 is closer to 3,880 than to 3,870.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The abacus below shows a number. Write it in Roman numerals. A: XXXIV. The abacus shows 34, which is XXXIV in Roman numerals.
chunks.source: The abacus shows 34, which is XXXIV in Roman numerals.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write XLIX in Hindu Arabic numerals. A: 49. XL = 40 and IX = 9, so XLIX = 49.
chunks.source: XL = 40 and IX = 9, so XLIX = 49.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Round off 6,273 to the nearest hundred. A: 6300. 6,273 is closer to 6,300 than to 6,200.
chunks.source: 6,273 is closer to 6,300 than to 6,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What is the value of 2 in the number 4,621? A: 20. The 2 is in the tens place, so its value is 20.
chunks.source: The 2 is in the tens place, so its value is 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write 'six hundred twenty nine' in figures. A: 629. Six hundred twenty nine = 629.
chunks.source: Six hundred twenty nine = 629.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What number has been expanded to give 3,000 + 90 + 500 + 7? A: 3597. 3,000 + 500 + 90 + 7 = 3,597.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Round off 246 to the nearest ten. A: 250. 246 is closer to 250 than to 240.
chunks.source: 246 is closer to 250 than to 240.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Kagimu reads a story of 145 words. How many words will he read if he reads 5 such stories? A: 725. 145 × 5 = 725 words.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The difference between two numbers is 305. If the smaller number is 267, find the bigger number. A: 572. 267 + 305 = 572.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: 3 + 2 = ____? (finite 4) A: 1. 3 + 2 = 5, and 5 in finite 4 is 1.
chunks.source: 3 + 2 = 5, and 5 in finite 4 is 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: 3 − 5 = ____? (finite 7) A: 5. 3 − 5 = −2, and −2 in finite 7 is 5.
chunks.source: 3 − 5 = −2, and −2 in finite 7 is 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The average weight of 3 boys is 53 kg. Find their total weight. A: 159. 53 × 3 = 159 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the average of 8, 3, 0, 2 and 7. A: 4. (8 + 3 + 0 + 2 + 7) ÷ 5 = 20 ÷ 5 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the numbers 4, 6, 4 and 10, find the mode. A: 4. The number 4 appears twice, more than any other, so the mode is 4.
chunks.source: The number 4 appears twice, more than any other, so the mode is 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the numbers 4, 6, 4 and 10, find the mean. A: 6. (4 + 6 + 4 + 10) ÷ 4 = 24 ÷ 4 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the numbers 4, 6, 4 and 10, find the range. A: 6. 10 − 4 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the numbers 4, 6, 4 and 10, find the median. A: 5. Arranged in order: 4, 4, 6, 10. The middle two are 4 and 6, so the median is (4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5.
chunks.source: Arranged in order: 4, 4, 6, 10. The middle two are 4 and 6, so the median is (4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Add: 231₅ + 22₅ A: 303₅. 231₅ + 22₅ = 303₅.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Subtract: 234₇ − 25₇ A: 206₇. 234₇ − 25₇ = 206₇.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 70 + 24 A: 94. 70 + 24 = 94.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is John had some cows on his farm. He sold 18 cows and remained with 92 cows. How many cows did he have at first? A: 110. 18 + 92 = 110.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mukasa scored 98, 95, 92, 95 and 100 in his mid-term exams. Work out his average mark. A: 96. (98 + 95 + 92 + 95 + 100) ÷ 5 = 480 ÷ 5 = 96.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is At a wedding, 3,617 women, 2,398 men and 954 children attended. How many adults attended altogether? A: 6015. 3,617 + 2,398 = 6,015.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is At a wedding, 6,969 guests attended and each was served 2 sodas. How many sodas were served? A: 13938. 6,969 × 2 = 13,938.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Subtract: 441₅ − 132₅ A: 304₅. 441₅ − 132₅ = 304₅.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Change 12₅ into base ten. A: 7. 12₅ = (1 × 5) + 2 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Add: 6 + 4 A: 10. 6 + 4 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the product of seventy-two and fifteen. A: 1080. 72 × 15 = 1,080.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A pupil scored 4, 5, 6, 4, 7 and 4 in homework. Find his average mark. A: 5. (4 + 5 + 6 + 4 + 7 + 4) ÷ 6 = 30 ÷ 6 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Subtract: 404₅ − 131₅ A: 223₅. 404₅ − 131₅ = 223₅.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Convert 24₅ to base ten. A: 14. 24₅ = (2 × 5) + 4 = 14.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Share 903 sweets equally among Akrah, Joel and Olive. How many sweets do Akrah and Olive get altogether? A: 602. 903 ÷ 3 = 301 each, so 301 × 2 = 602.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is At a party there were 470 adults and 520 children. Find the total number of guests. A: 990. 470 + 520 = 990.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is At a party there were 470 adults and 520 children. How many more children than adults attended? A: 50. 520 − 470 = 50.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is At a party 990 guests attended but there were sodas for only 900 guests. How many guests missed sodas? A: 90. 990 − 900 = 90.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 1 school bag costs sh. 1,500. Find the cost of 5 similar school bags. A: 7500. 1,500 × 5 = 7,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 5 books cost sh. 2,500. How much will Mary pay for 3 similar books? A: 1500. One book costs 2,500 ÷ 5 = 500, so 3 books cost 1,500.
chunks.source: One book costs 2,500 ÷ 5 = 500, so 3 books cost 1,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The cost of 2 pencils is sh. 800. What is the cost of 6 similar pencils? A: 2400. One pencil costs 800 ÷ 2 = 400, so 6 pencils cost 2,400.
chunks.source: One pencil costs 800 ÷ 2 = 400, so 6 pencils cost 2,400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Joan bought a radio at sh. 50,000 and sold it at a loss of sh. 5,000. What was the selling price? A: 45000. 50,000 − 5,000 = 45,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Bony went to the market with sh. 8,000 and bought: 3 mangoes at sh. 800 each, a heap of four oranges at sh. 2,000, and 3 apples at sh. 1,200 each. How much did he spend altogether? A: 8000. (3 × 800) + 2,000 + (3 × 1,200) = 2,400 + 2,000 + 3,600 = 8,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Bony went to the market with sh. 8,000 and spent sh. 8,000. Find his change. A: 0. 8,000 − 8,000 = 0.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Katongole bought a T.V. at sh. 45,500 and later sold it at sh. 50,000. How much profit did he make? A: 4500. 50,000 − 45,500 = 4,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is It costs sh. 4,000 to travel from Kampala to Jinja and sh. 7,000 from Jinja to Mbale. How much will one person pay for the journey from Kampala to Mbale? A: 11000. 4,000 + 7,000 = 11,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is It costs sh. 11,000 for one person to travel from Kampala to Mbale. If 5 people are travelling, how much will they pay altogether? A: 55000. 11,000 × 5 = 55,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Okoth sold a goat at sh. 85,000 and made a loss of sh. 13,000. How much did she buy the goat? A: 98000. 85,000 + 13,000 = 98,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Complete the shopping list: Sugar, 4 kg at sh. 2,400 per kg. What is the total cost of the sugar? A: 9600. 4 × 2,400 = 9,600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Complete the shopping list: Bread costs sh. 3,500 per loaf and the total for bread is sh. 7,000. How many loaves were bought? A: 2. 7,000 ÷ 3,500 = 2 loaves.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A shopping list totals sh. 9,600 for sugar, sh. 7,000 for bread and sh. 400 for salt. What is the grand total? A: 17000. 9,600 + 7,000 + 400 = 17,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Kalungi paid sh. 17,000 from a sh. 20,000 note. What balance did he receive? A: 3000. 20,000 − 17,000 = 3,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A book costs sh. 300. Find the cost of four similar books. A: 1200. 300 × 4 = 1,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mugisha bought a bull at sh. 250,000 and later sold it at sh. 320,000. How much profit did he make? A: 70000. 320,000 − 250,000 = 70,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 5 books cost sh. 2,000. Find the cost of 8 similar books. A: 3200. One book costs 2,000 ÷ 5 = 400, so 8 books cost 3,200.
chunks.source: One book costs 2,000 ÷ 5 = 400, so 8 books cost 3,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A man bought 2 kg of sugar at sh. 3,200 per kg, 1/2 litre of cooking oil at sh. 4,000 a litre, and 4 kg of Irish potatoes at sh. 6,000. How much money did he spend? A: 14400. (2 × 3,200) + (1/2 × 4,000) + 6,000 = 6,400 + 2,000 + 6,000 = 14,400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A man went to the market with sh. 20,000 and spent sh. 14,400. How much money did he remain with? A: 5600. 20,000 − 14,400 = 5,600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Musa sold a pair of trousers at sh. 16,000, making a profit of sh. 4,000. How much did he buy the pair of trousers? A: 12000. 16,000 − 4,000 = 12,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Martha's bill: 2 dozen books cost sh. 12,000. What was the unit cost per dozen? A: 6000. 12,000 ÷ 2 = 6,000 per dozen.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Martha's bill: 1 1/2 dozen pens at sh. 4,000 per dozen. What was the amount for the pens? A: 6000. 1 1/2 × 4,000 = 6,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Martha's bill: rulers cost sh. 600 each and the amount for rulers was sh. 2,400. How many rulers did she buy? A: 4. 2,400 ÷ 600 = 4 rulers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Martha's bill: 3 rubbers cost sh. 2,250. What was the unit cost of one rubber? A: 750. 2,250 ÷ 3 = 750.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Martha spent sh. 12,000 on books, sh. 6,000 on pens, sh. 2,400 on rulers and sh. 2,250 on rubbers. What was her total expenditure? A: 22650. 12,000 + 6,000 + 2,400 + 2,250 = 22,650.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Martha spent sh. 22,650 and remained with sh. 2,350. How much money did she have at first? A: 25000. 22,650 + 2,350 = 25,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A shirt costs sh. 4,000. How many shirts can a person buy with sh. 32,000? A: 8. 32,000 ÷ 4,000 = 8 shirts.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Calvin bought a mathematical set at sh. 2,500 and later sold it at a loss of sh. 500. How much did he sell the mathematical set? A: 2000. 2,500 − 500 = 2,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A kilogram of salt costs sh. 800. How much will a person pay for 750 g of salt? A: 600. 750 g = 3/4 kg, so 3/4 × 800 = 600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A shopkeeper made a profit of sh. 7,600 after selling a box of milk at sh. 39,200. What was the buying price of the box of milk? A: 31600. 39,200 − 7,600 = 31,600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The cost of an exercise book is sh. 1,000. Find the cost of a dozen similar books. A: 12000. 1,000 × 12 = 12,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A cup's buying price is sh. 1,500 and its selling price is sh. 1,800. Find the profit made. A: 300. 1,800 − 1,500 = 300.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 1 kg of sugar costs sh. 5,500 and 1 litre of milk costs sh. 2,400. Find the total cost of 2 kg of sugar and 3 litres of milk. A: 18200. (2 × 5,500) + (3 × 2,400) = 11,000 + 7,200 = 18,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Clare had sh. 20,000 and bought 3 loaves of bread at sh. 4,500 each. Find her change. A: 6500. 20,000 − 13,500 = 6,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The 5 children who enjoy both drinks each got sh. 1,000. How much money did they get altogether? A: 5000. 5 × 1,000 = 5,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Paul bought 2 pens at sh. 1,500 each, 6 books at sh. 500 each and a geometry set at sh. 2,800. Find his total expenditure. A: 8800. 3,000 + 3,000 + 2,800 = 8,800.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Paul spent sh. 8,800 and got sh. 1,200 change. How much money did he go with? A: 10000. 8,800 + 1,200 = 10,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Privah had a five thousand shilling note and bought 2 kg of sugar at sh. 2,400 per kg. What was her change? A: 200. 5,000 − 4,800 = 200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Tinah collected: 20 notes of sh. 1,000, 10 coins of sh. 500 and 30 coins of sh. 200. Find her total collection. A: 31000. 20,000 + 5,000 + 6,000 = 31,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Liz collected: 10 notes of sh. 1,000, 30 coins of sh. 500 and 15 coins of sh. 200. Find her total collection. A: 28000. 10,000 + 15,000 + 3,000 = 28,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the product of the next two missing numbers: 2, 3, 5, 7, ____?, ____? A: 143. The sequence lists prime numbers, so the next two are 11 and 13, and 11 × 13 = 143.
chunks.source: The sequence lists prime numbers, so the next two are 11 and 13, and 11 × 13 = 143.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What is the square of 7? A: 49. 7² = 7 × 7 = 49.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the square root of 121. A: 11. 11 × 11 = 121, so √121 = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 5, 6, 8, 11, 15, ____? A: 20. The differences grow by 1 each time (1, 2, 3, 4), so the next difference is 5 and 15 + 5 = 20.
chunks.source: The differences grow by 1 each time (1, 2, 3, 4), so the next difference is 5 and 15 + 5 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: (½ of 18) + (¼ of 16) A: 13. ½ of 18 is 9 and ¼ of 16 is 4, so 9 + 4 = 13.
chunks.source: ½ of 18 is 9 and ¼ of 16 is 4, so 9 + 4 = 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What is the GCF of 32 and 48? A: 16. The greatest number that divides both 32 and 48 is 16.
chunks.source: The greatest number that divides both 32 and 48 is 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If y² = 81, find the value of y. A: 9. 9 × 9 = 81, so y = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the LCM of 16 and 24. A: 48. The smallest number both 16 and 24 divide into is 48.
chunks.source: The smallest number both 16 and 24 divide into is 48.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name the figure shown below. A: Cube. All edges are equal and marked the same, so the figure is a cube.
chunks.source: All edges are equal and marked the same, so the figure is a cube.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the volume of the figure shown below. A: 216. Volume = 6 × 6 × 6 = 216 cm³.
chunks.source: Volume = 6 × 6 × 6 = 216 cm³.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the missing numbers in the factor tree of 18 below. Write them from top to bottom, separated by a comma. A: 9, 3. 18 = 2 × 9 and 9 = 3 × 3, so the missing numbers are 9 and 3.
chunks.source: 18 = 2 × 9 and 9 = 3 × 3, so the missing numbers are 9 and 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 213 ____? 312 A: <. 213 is smaller than 312.
chunks.source: 213 is smaller than 312.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: ¾ of 16 ____? ⅔ of 18 A: =. ¾ of 16 = 12 and ⅔ of 18 = 12, so they are equal.
chunks.source: ¾ of 16 = 12 and ⅔ of 18 = 12, so they are equal.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 2 m ____? 150 cm A: >. 2 m = 200 cm, which is more than 150 cm.
chunks.source: 2 m = 200 cm, which is more than 150 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: XCV ____? C A: <. XCV = 95 and C = 100, so 95 < 100.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 16, 21, 26, 31, 36, ____? A: 41. Each number is 5 more than the one before, so 36 + 5 = 41.
chunks.source: Each number is 5 more than the one before, so 36 + 5 = 41.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The cards show 8, 12 and 6. Find the lowest common multiple of the numbers. A: 24. The smallest number all three divide into is 24.
chunks.source: The smallest number all three divide into is 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the greatest common factor of 8 and 6. A: 2. The biggest number dividing both 8 and 6 is 2.
chunks.source: The biggest number dividing both 8 and 6 is 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the sum of the first three prime numbers. A: 10. 2 + 3 + 5 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The Venn diagram shows prime factors of x and y. Find the value of y. A: 18. y = 2 × 3 × 3 = 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The Venn diagram shows prime factors of x and y. Find the value of x. A: 30. x = 2 × 3 × 5 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The Venn diagram shows prime factors of x and y. Find the GCF of Fx and Fy. A: 6. GCF = 2 × 3 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 20, 16, 12, 8, ____? A: 4. Each number drops by 4, so 8 − 4 = 4.
chunks.source: Each number drops by 4, so 8 − 4 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out the lowest common multiple of 8 and 6. A: 24. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24... of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24. LCM = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Express 3 2/4 as an improper fraction. A: 14/4. 3 2/4 = (3 × 4 + 2)/4 = 14/4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A driver covered 1/3 of his journey of 72 km. What distance did he cover? A: 24. 1/3 of 72 = 72 ÷ 3 = 24 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the missing number: 3/5 = 12/__ A: 20. 3 × 4 = 12, so 5 × 4 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write 32/3 as a mixed fraction. A: 10 2/3. 32 ÷ 3 = 10 remainder 2, so 32/3 = 10 2/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use <, > or = to compare: 18/24 ____? 6/8 A: =. 18/24 = 3/4 and 6/8 = 3/4, so they are equal.
chunks.source: 18/24 = 3/4 and 6/8 = 3/4, so they are equal.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is On a farm of 30 animals, 3/5 of them are cows and the rest are goats. How many cows are on the farm? A: 18. 3/5 of 30 = 18 cows.
chunks.source: 3/5 of 30 = 18 cows.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is On a farm of 30 animals, 3/5 of them are cows and the rest are goats. How many goats are on the farm? A: 12. 30 − 18 = 12 goats.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is On a farm of 30 animals, 3/5 of them are cows and the rest are goats. What fraction of the animals are goats? A: 2/5. 1 − 3/5 = 2/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is On a farm of 30 animals, 3/5 of them are cows and the rest are goats. How many more cows than goats are on the farm? A: 6. 18 − 12 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a P.5 class of 50 pupils, 3/10 of them were absent and the rest were present. What fraction of the class was present? A: 7/10. 1 − 3/10 = 7/10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a P.5 class of 50 pupils, 3/10 of them were absent. How many pupils were absent? A: 15. 3/10 of 50 = 15 pupils.
chunks.source: 3/10 of 50 = 15 pupils.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a P.5 class of 50 pupils, 3/10 were absent and the rest were present. How many more pupils were present than absent? A: 20. Present = 35 and absent = 15, so 35 − 15 = 20.
chunks.source: Present = 35 and absent = 15, so 35 − 15 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 3/4 ____? 6/8 A: =. 6/8 simplifies to 3/4, so they are equal.
chunks.source: 6/8 simplifies to 3/4, so they are equal.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 2/3 ____? 5/6 A: <. 2/3 = 4/6, which is less than 5/6.
chunks.source: 2/3 = 4/6, which is less than 5/6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 1/3 ____? 1/4 A: >. When numerators are the same, the smaller denominator gives the bigger fraction.
chunks.source: When numerators are the same, the smaller denominator gives the bigger fraction.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Express 13/13 as a mixed fraction. A: 1. 13/13 = 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Express 1/2 kg as grams. A: 500. 1 kg = 1,000 g, so 1/2 kg = 500 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Change 2 4/5 to an improper fraction. A: 14/5. 2 4/5 = (2 × 5 + 4)/5 = 14/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 1/4 of (20 − 4) A: 4. 20 − 4 = 16 and 1/4 of 16 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: (10 + 30) of 1/5 A: 8. 10 + 30 = 40 and 1/5 of 40 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many half-litre bottles of milk can be got from a container of 20 litres? A: 40. 20 ÷ 1/2 = 40 bottles.
chunks.source: 20 ÷ 1/2 = 40 bottles.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 1/2 ____? 4/8 A: =. 4/8 simplifies to 1/2.
chunks.source: 4/8 simplifies to 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 1/3 ____? 1/2 A: <. 1/3 is smaller than 1/2.
chunks.source: 1/3 is smaller than 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 3/4 ____? 6/12 A: >. 3/4 = 9/12, which is bigger than 6/12.
chunks.source: 3/4 = 9/12, which is bigger than 6/12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a class of 48 pupils, 3/4 of them eat meat and the rest eat fish. What fraction of the class eats fish? A: 1/4. 1 − 3/4 = 1/4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a class of 48 pupils, 3/4 of them eat meat. How many children eat meat? A: 36. 3/4 of 48 = 36.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a class of 48 pupils, 3/4 eat meat and the rest eat fish. How many more children eat meat than fish? A: 24. Meat eaters = 36 and fish eaters = 12, so 36 − 12 = 24.
chunks.source: Meat eaters = 36 and fish eaters = 12, so 36 − 12 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mary ate 1/2 of the sugar cane on Monday and 2/5 on Tuesday. What fraction did she remain with? A: 1/10. 1/2 + 2/5 = 9/10, so 1 − 9/10 = 1/10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A mother shared 36 pieces of watermelon: Mark got 1/3, Mike got 1/4 and Moses got the rest. How many pieces did Mark get? A: 12. 1/3 of 36 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A mother shared 36 pieces of watermelon: Mark got 1/3, Mike got 1/4 and Moses got the rest. How many pieces did Mike get? A: 9. 1/4 of 36 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A mother shared 36 pieces of watermelon: Mark got 1/3, Mike got 1/4 and Moses got the rest. How many pieces did Moses get? A: 15. 36 − 12 − 9 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write 0.5 as a reduced proper fraction. A: 1/2. 0.5 = 5/10 = 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Express 15/2 as a mixed number. A: 7 1/2. 15 ÷ 2 = 7 remainder 1, so 7 1/2.
chunks.source: 15 ÷ 2 = 7 remainder 1, so 7 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Bianca gave 3/7 of an apple to Benita, 1/7 to Mellisa and the rest to Davita. What fraction did Davita get? A: 3/7. 1 − 3/7 − 1/7 = 3/7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is An Omni bus had 15 seats. If 3/5 were occupied, how many free seats were in the bus? A: 6. 3/5 of 15 = 9 occupied, so 15 − 9 = 6 free.
chunks.source: 3/5 of 15 = 9 occupied, so 15 − 9 = 6 free.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a class of 70 pupils, 3/5 are girls and the rest are boys. Find the fraction of boys. A: 2/5. 1 − 3/5 = 2/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a class of 70 pupils, 3/5 are girls and the rest are boys. How many boys are there? A: 28. 2/5 of 70 = 28.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In a class of 70 pupils, 3/5 are girls and the rest are boys. How many girls are there? A: 42. 3/5 of 70 = 42.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Express 1/2 as a decimal fraction. A: 0.5. 1/2 = 0.5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the value of angle y in the diagram below. A: 28. y = 90° − 62° = 28°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the value of angle k in the diagram below. A: 40. k = 180° − 50° − 90° = 40°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is An equilateral triangle has sides of 6 cm. Find its perimeter. A: 18. 6 × 3 = 18 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the area of the shaded triangle in the rectangle below (base 12 dm, height 8 dm). A: 48. Area = 1/2 × 12 × 8 = 48 dm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many lines of symmetry does a semicircle have? A: 1. Only the vertical line through the middle works.
chunks.source: Only the vertical line through the middle works.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The diagram shows a right angle split into m and 15°. Find the value of 2m. A: 150. m = 90° − 15° = 75°, so 2m = 150°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The right-angled triangle below has angles k and 43°. Find k. A: 47. k = 90° − 43° = 47°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The triangle below has angles 40°, p and 75°. Find p. A: 65. p = 180° − 40° − 75° = 65°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The angles 131° and m sit on a straight line. Find m. A: 49. m = 180° − 131° = 49°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The cuboid below measures 15 hm by 10 hm by 3 hm, with the front face shaded. Work out the area of the shaded portion. A: 45. 15 × 3 = 45 hm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The cuboid below measures 15 hm by 10 hm by 3 hm. Calculate its volume. A: 450. 15 × 10 × 3 = 450 hm³.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many edges does a cuboid have? A: 12. A cuboid has 12 edges.
chunks.source: A cuboid has 12 edges.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The arrow on the number line below starts at −1 and ends at +3. What integer does the arrowhead point to? A: 3. The arrowhead lands on +3.
chunks.source: The arrowhead lands on +3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: −3 ____? 3 A: <. −3 is less than 3.
chunks.source: −3 is less than 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: −7 ____? −6 A: <. −7 is further from zero on the negative side, so −7 < −6.
chunks.source: −7 is further from zero on the negative side, so −7 < −6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare using <, > or =: 0 ____? −2 A: >. 0 is greater than any negative number.
chunks.source: 0 is greater than any negative number.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: −2 + +6 A: 4. −2 + 6 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 3 − +7 A: −4. 3 − 7 = −4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 4 × −6 A: −24. 4 × −6 = −24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use a number line to work out: 2 − 3 + +6 A: 5. 2 − 3 = −1 and −1 + 6 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 3 × −4 A: −12. 3 × −4 = −12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: +3 + −7 A: −4. 3 − 7 = −4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the median of the integers: 0, −3, 4, −3, −2, 5, −5 A: −2. In order: −5, −3, −3, −2, 0, 4, 5. The middle value is −2.
chunks.source: In order: −5, −3, −3, −2, 0, 4, 5. The middle value is −2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use a number line to work out: 2 × 4 A: 8. 2 × 4 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the range of the integers: −2, 0, 4, −5, 3 A: 9. 4 − (−5) = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Simplify: −3 − −3 A: 0. −3 + 3 = 0.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out the inverse (opposite) of +6. A: −6. The opposite of +6 is −6.
chunks.source: The opposite of +6 is −6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Aminah jumped 4 metres backwards and then 9 metres forward. How far is she now from her original place? A: 5. −4 + 9 = 5 metres forward.
chunks.source: −4 + 9 = 5 metres forward.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write the integer represented by the arrowhead b on the number line below. A: -2. The arrowhead lands on −2.
chunks.source: The arrowhead lands on −2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that a = −4 and b = 6, find the value of a + b. A: 2. −4 + 6 = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is John bought 22 cows. How many cows do the tallies below represent? A: 22. The tallies count 22.
chunks.source: The tallies count 22.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The bar graph below shows marks: Joy 80, Mary 70, John 60, David 70, Jane 60. How many more marks did Mary get than Jane? A: 10. 70 − 60 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The bar graph below shows marks: Joy 80, Mary 70, John 60, David 70, Jane 60. Find the total marks of Mary, Joy and John. A: 210. 70 + 80 + 60 = 210.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is One picture represents 12 trees. How many trees do 2 such pictures represent? A: 24. 12 × 2 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the tally table. The Posho row shows 5 groups of five tallies. What is the frequency for Posho? A: 25. 5 × 5 = 25.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the tally table. Rice has a frequency of 10. How many tally marks should be drawn for Rice? A: 10. The tally marks must equal the frequency, 10.
chunks.source: The tally marks must equal the frequency, 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is One chair picture represents 6 chairs. How many pictures are needed to represent 24 chairs? A: 4. 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The graph shows litres of milk sold: Mon 30, Tue 40, Wed 30, Thu 35, Fri 50. How many litres were sold on Thursday? A: 35. Thursday's bar reaches 35.
chunks.source: Thursday's bar reaches 35.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The graph shows litres of milk sold: Mon 30, Tue 40, Wed 30, Thu 35, Fri 50. How many litres were sold on Tuesday and Friday altogether? A: 90. 40 + 50 = 90.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Wangwe's scores: Mathematics 95, English 70, Science 90, Social studies 85. How many subjects did Wangwe write? A: 4. There are 4 subjects in the table.
chunks.source: There are 4 subjects in the table.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Wangwe's scores: Mathematics 95, English 70, Science 90, Social studies 85. Find the difference between the highest and the lowest scores. A: 25. 95 − 70 = 25.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Wangwe's scores: Mathematics 95, English 70, Science 90, Social studies 85. Find his total mark in all subjects. A: 340. 95 + 70 + 90 + 85 = 340.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is It started raining at 2:20 am and stopped at 8:10 am. How long did the rain take? A: 5 hours 50 minutes. From 2:20 to 8:10 is 5 hours 50 minutes.
chunks.source: From 2:20 to 8:10 is 5 hours 50 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A forty-minute lesson started at 8:10 am. At what time did it end? A: 8:50 am. 8:10 + 40 minutes = 8:50 am.
chunks.source: 8:10 + 40 minutes = 8:50 am.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the distance a driver covers at 15 kilometres per hour for 3 hours. A: 45. Distance = speed × time = 15 × 3 = 45 km.
chunks.source: Distance = speed × time = 15 × 3 = 45 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A cyclist covered a journey of 100 km at a speed of 40 km/h. How long did it take him? A: 2.5. Time = distance ÷ speed = 100 ÷ 40 = 2.5 hours.
chunks.source: Time = distance ÷ speed = 100 ÷ 40 = 2.5 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: There are 158 pupils in P.4. If there are 74 girls in the class, how many boys are in the class? ____? A: 84. 158 − 74 = 84 boys.

chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 7, 12, 17, 22, ____? A: 27. Add 5 each time: 22 + 5 = 27.

chunks.text: Q: A book costs sh. 3,500. Find the cost of 3 similar books = sh. ____? A: 10500. 3 × 3,500 = 10,500 shillings.

chunks.text: Q: Simplify: +3 + (−7) = ____? A: -4. Start at +3 on the number line and move 7 steps down to reach −4.

chunks.text: Q: Find the missing number in the sequence: 1, 4, 9, 16, ____? A: 25. These are square numbers (1², 2², 3², 4²), so the next is 5² = 25.

chunks.text: Q: Express 10/3 as a mixed number = ____? A: 3 1/3. 10 ÷ 3 = 3 remainder 1, so 10/3 = 3 1/3.

chunks.text: Q: Why does oil settle at the top when mixed with water? ____ A: Because oil is less dense than water. Oil is less dense (lighter) than water, so it floats and settles on top.

chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange the following sentences to show how rain is formed: 'The evaporated water condenses to form nimbus clouds' / 'The sun heats water body.' / 'When the clouds become heavy, they fall as rain drops.' / 'The water evaporates.' A: The sun heats water body., The water evaporates., The evaporated water condenses to form nimbus clouds., When the clouds become heavy, they fall as rain drops.. The sun heats water, it evaporates, vapour condenses into clouds, and heavy clouds fall as rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one item used for sweeping. A: Broom. A broom is used to sweep dirt and dust from floors and compounds.
chunks.source: A broom is used to sweep dirt and dust from floors and compounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How should you care for your hair? A: Wash it regularly and comb it. Washing removes dirt and germs, and combing keeps hair neat.
chunks.source: Washing removes dirt and germs, and combing keeps hair neat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are people encouraged to wash hands after using the latrine? A: To remove germs and prevent the spread of diseases. Hands pick up germs in the latrine, and washing removes them.
chunks.source: Hands pick up germs in the latrine, and washing removes them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows parts of a leaf. Which part attaches the leaf onto the plant? A: Petiole (leaf stalk). The petiole, also called the leaf stalk, joins the leaf blade to the stem of the plant.
chunks.source: The petiole, also called the leaf stalk, joins the leaf blade to the stem of the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a beak useful to birds? A: Birds use their beaks to pick up and eat food. Birds have no hands, so they use their beaks to pick food.
chunks.source: Birds have no hands, so they use their beaks to pick food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should cooked food be covered? A: To protect it from germs, flies and dust. Covering food keeps germs, flies and dust from landing on it.
chunks.source: Covering food keeps germs, flies and dust from landing on it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these shows that air exerts pressure? A: A balloon tied over the mouth of a bottle swells up when the bottle is put in hot water. The warm air inside the bottle expands and pushes upwards, inflating the balloon. This push is air pressure.
chunks.source: The warm air inside the bottle expands and pushes upwards, inflating the balloon. This push is air pressure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the act of mulching promote soil fertility? A: Mulches decay and add humus, which makes the soil fertile. Dead plant materials rot and add humus to the soil.
chunks.source: Dead plant materials rot and add humus to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do tape worms enter our body? A: By eating raw or half-cooked meat containing tapeworm cysts. Tapeworm cysts live in uncooked meat and grow in our intestines.
chunks.source: Tapeworm cysts live in uncooked meat and grow in our intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a bean seed said to be a dicotyledonous seed? A: Because it has two cotyledons. 'Di' means two, and a bean seed has two seed leaves (cotyledons).
chunks.source: 'Di' means two, and a bean seed has two seed leaves (cotyledons).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one effect of accidents to people. A: Accidents cause injuries. Accidents can injure, disable or even kill people.
chunks.source: Accidents can injure, disable or even kill people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a mango plant said to be a perennial crop? A: Because it lives and produces for many years (more than two years). Perennial crops live for more than two growing seasons.
chunks.source: Perennial crops live for more than two growing seasons.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.source: The pointed tooth shown is a canine, used for tearing food.
