chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you care for a blind person in your community? A: By guiding them when walking and helping them with daily tasks. Blind people need help to move around safely.
chunks.source: Blind people need help to move around safely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do people prefer keeping rabbits to some animals like cows? A: Rabbits need little space and little food, so they are cheap to keep. Rabbits eat little and need only a small hutch.
chunks.source: Rabbits eat little and need only a small hutch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a primary five child differentiate sand soil from clay soil? A: Sand soil feels rough and coarse while clay soil feels smooth and sticky. Rubbing the soil between the fingers shows the difference.
chunks.source: Rubbing the soil between the fingers shows the difference.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one use of a child health card to a mother. A: It records the child's immunisation dates and growth. The card reminds the mother when to take the child for immunisation.
chunks.source: The card reminds the mother when to take the child for immunisation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the clouds that may indicate that it is about to rain. A: Nimbus clouds. Dark nimbus clouds are a sign that rain is coming.
chunks.source: Dark nimbus clouds are a sign that rain is coming.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do farmers carry out crop rotation? A: To keep the soil fertile and to control crop pests and diseases. Changing crops each season rests the soil and breaks pest cycles.
chunks.source: Changing crops each season rests the soil and breaks pest cycles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of spending resources wisely. A: By buying only what is needed. Spending only on what is needed avoids waste.
chunks.source: Spending only on what is needed avoids waste.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one advantage of breast feeding to a mother. A: It helps the mother's womb return to its normal size after birth. Breast feeding also helps the mother recover quickly after giving birth.
chunks.source: Breast feeding also helps the mother recover quickly after giving birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one danger of plants. A: Some plants are poisonous when eaten. Some plants have poison or thorns that can harm people.
chunks.source: Some plants have poison or thorns that can harm people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a wild bird. A: Weaver bird. Weaver birds live in the wild and are not kept by people.
chunks.source: Weaver birds live in the wild and are not kept by people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does mulching reduce soil erosion on a flat land? A: Mulches cover the soil and slow down running water, so soil is not carried away. The mulch cover breaks the speed of flowing water.
chunks.source: The mulch cover breaks the speed of flowing water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a weaning child said to be a vulnerable person? A: A weaning child is changing from breast milk to other foods and can easily suffer from poor feeding. Weaning is a delicate stage when the child needs proper new foods.
chunks.source: Weaning is a delicate stage when the child needs proper new foods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the ileum adapted to the absorption of digested food? A: The ileum is long and has many villi that increase the surface area for absorption. Villi are tiny finger-like parts that absorb digested food.
chunks.source: Villi are tiny finger-like parts that absorb digested food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does water pass through sand soil easily? A: Because sand soil has large particles with large spaces between them. Big spaces between sand particles let water flow through fast.
chunks.source: Big spaces between sand particles let water flow through fast.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the propagation of beans different from that of cassava? A: Beans are grown from seeds while cassava is grown from stem cuttings. Beans use seeds; cassava uses pieces of stem.
chunks.source: Beans use seeds; cassava uses pieces of stem.

chunks.source: Carbon dioxide covers the fire and cuts off the air it needs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one way of keeping our classroom clean. A: By sweeping the classroom every day. Daily sweeping removes dust and litter.
chunks.source: Daily sweeping removes dust and litter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does keeping fish in a pond help to control malaria in a home? A: Fish eat mosquito larvae in the water, so fewer mosquitoes breed. Fewer mosquito larvae grow into adult mosquitoes.
chunks.source: Fewer mosquito larvae grow into adult mosquitoes.

chunks.text: Q: Name the part of the digestive system that produces gastric juice. A: Stomach. The walls of the stomach produce gastric juice which digests food.
chunks.source: The walls of the stomach produce gastric juice which digests food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows part of the digestive system. What is the function of part labelled R during digestion? A: It (the liver) produces bile juice which helps to digest fats. R points to the liver, which makes bile.
chunks.source: R points to the liver, which makes bile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can the above system be kept healthy? A: By eating a balanced diet and drinking clean water. Good feeding keeps the digestive system working well.
chunks.source: Good feeding keeps the digestive system working well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write 4Fs in full. A: Flies, Fingers, Faeces and Food. The 4Fs are the four ways germs spread: Flies, Fingers, Faeces and Food.
chunks.source: The 4Fs are the four ways germs spread: Flies, Fingers, Faeces and Food.

chunks.source: The 4Fs are the four ways germs spread: Flies, Fingers, Faeces and Food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any two diseases that are spread through the 4Fs. A: Cholera and dysentery. The 4Fs spread diarrhoeal diseases like cholera and dysentery.
chunks.source: The 4Fs spread diarrhoeal diseases like cholera and dysentery.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any two diseases that are spread through the 4Fs. A: Cholera and dysentery. The 4Fs spread diarrhoeal diseases like cholera and dysentery.
chunks.source: The 4Fs spread diarrhoeal diseases like cholera and dysentery.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one way in which you can control the spread of the diseases you have given in (b) above. A: By using latrines properly to dispose of faeces. Proper disposal of faeces stops germs from spreading.
chunks.source: Proper disposal of faeces stops germs from spreading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one example of a root tuber crop. A: Cassava. Cassava stores food in its swollen roots.
chunks.source: Cassava stores food in its swollen roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one example of a stem tuber crop. A: Irish potato. The Irish potato is a swollen underground stem.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one pest that destroys root tubers. A: Mole rats. Mole rats dig and eat root tubers like cassava.
chunks.source: Mole rats dig and eat root tubers like cassava.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can pests of tuber crops be controlled? A: By spraying the crops with pesticides. Pesticides kill the pests that attack the crops.
chunks.source: Pesticides kill the pests that attack the crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two exotic breeds of rabbits. A: New Zealand White and Californian. These are common exotic rabbit breeds kept in Uganda.
chunks.source: These are common exotic rabbit breeds kept in Uganda.

chunks.source: These are common exotic rabbit breeds kept in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one disease which commonly attacks both rabbits and poultry. A: Coccidiosis. Coccidiosis attacks rabbits and also poultry.
chunks.source: Coccidiosis attacks rabbits and also poultry.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.source: Coccidiosis attacks rabbits and also poultry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it advisable for rabbit farmers to keep rabbit houses clean and dry? A: To prevent diseases from attacking the rabbits. Dirty, damp houses breed germs that make rabbits sick.
chunks.source: Dirty, damp houses breed germs that make rabbits sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one way in which HIV/AIDS spreads. A: Through having unprotected sex with an infected person. Unprotected sex is the main way HIV spreads.
chunks.source: Unprotected sex is the main way HIV spreads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write ABC in full as used in the control of HIV/AIDS. A: Abstinence, Being faithful and Condom use. ABC is the well-known HIV prevention message.
chunks.source: ABC is the well-known HIV prevention message.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one effect of HIV/AIDS to an individual. A: It weakens the body's immunity, making the person fall sick easily. HIV destroys the body's defence against diseases.
chunks.source: HIV destroys the body's defence against diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you care for HIV/AIDS patients? A: By giving them good food, love and taking them to hospital for treatment. Patients need good feeding, love and medicine.
chunks.source: Patients need good feeding, love and medicine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two insects eaten by people in your community. A: Grasshoppers and white ants. Grasshoppers and white ants are commonly eaten in Uganda.
chunks.source: Grasshoppers and white ants are commonly eaten in Uganda.

chunks.text: Q: Mention any two insects eaten by people in your community. A: Grasshoppers and white ants. Grasshoppers and white ants are commonly eaten in Uganda.
chunks.source: Grasshoppers and white ants are commonly eaten in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two dangerous insects in the environment. A: Mosquitoes and tsetse flies. Mosquitoes spread malaria and tsetse flies spread sleeping sickness.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes spread malaria and tsetse flies spread sleeping sickness.

chunks.text: Q: Give any two dangerous insects in the environment. A: Mosquitoes and tsetse flies. Mosquitoes spread malaria and tsetse flies spread sleeping sickness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a shadow formed? A: A shadow is formed when an opaque object blocks light from passing through. Light cannot pass through the object, leaving a dark shape behind it.
chunks.source: Light cannot pass through the object, leaving a dark shape behind it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can shadows be helpful to people in the environment? A: Shadows give shade on sunny days. Standing in a shadow keeps you cool.
chunks.source: Standing in a shadow keeps you cool.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: When are shadows longest? A: In the morning and in the evening. When the sun is low, shadows stretch out long.
chunks.source: When the sun is low, shadows stretch out long.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows the sun on the left and a tree. On which side of the tree should its shadow be drawn? A: To the right of the tree. A shadow forms on the opposite side of the light source; the sun is on the left, so the shadow falls to the right.
chunks.source: A shadow forms on the opposite side of the light source; the sun is on the left, so the shadow falls to the right.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a rain gauge useful at a weather station? A: It measures the amount of rainfall. A rain gauge collects and measures rain.
chunks.source: A rain gauge collects and measures rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a wind vane useful at a weather station? A: It shows the direction of wind. The wind vane turns to point where the wind comes from.
chunks.source: The wind vane turns to point where the wind comes from.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a barometer useful at a weather station? A: It measures air pressure. A barometer measures the pressure of the air.
chunks.source: A barometer measures the pressure of the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a barometer useful at a weather station? A: It measures air pressure. A barometer measures the pressure of the air.
chunks.source: A barometer measures the pressure of the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a rain gauge usually placed in an open space? A: So that buildings or trees do not block the rain from entering it. In the open, all the falling rain can enter the gauge.
chunks.source: In the open, all the falling rain can enter the gauge.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one component of the environment. A: Plants. Plants are living components of the environment.
chunks.source: Plants are living components of the environment.

chunks.source: Plants are living components of the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why people keep birds at home. A: To get eggs and meat. Birds like chicken give us eggs and meat.
chunks.source: Birds like chicken give us eggs and meat.

chunks.source: Birds like chicken give us eggs and meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are gills of a fish similar to spiracles of an insect? A: Both are breathing organs. Gills and spiracles are both used for breathing.
chunks.source: Gills and spiracles are both used for breathing.

chunks.text: Q: How are gills of a fish similar to spiracles of an insect? A: Both are breathing organs. Gills and spiracles are both used for breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention the type of feeds given to birds for egg production. A: Layers mash. Layers mash is the special feed for laying birds.
chunks.source: Layers mash is the special feed for laying birds.

chunks.text: Q: Mention the type of feeds given to birds for egg production. A: Layers mash. Layers mash is the special feed for laying birds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are dust bins useful in a class room? A: They are used for collecting rubbish to keep the classroom clean. Rubbish goes into the dustbin instead of the floor.
chunks.source: Rubbish goes into the dustbin instead of the floor.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do people wash fruits like mangoes before eating them? A: To remove dirt and germs from them. Fruits can carry dirt and germs on their skins.
chunks.source: Fruits can carry dirt and germs on their skins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one advantage of planting trees in a compound. A: Trees provide shade in the compound. Trees give shade and fresh air.
chunks.source: Trees give shade and fresh air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the use of the garden tool shown below. (An axe is shown.) A: It is used for cutting down trees. An axe cuts trees for firewood and timber.
chunks.source: An axe cuts trees for firewood and timber.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do insects like bees and wasps have stings? A: To protect themselves from enemies. The sting is their weapon for defence.
chunks.source: The sting is their weapon for defence.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.source: The sting is their weapon for defence.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one condition necessary for seed germination. A: Water. Seeds need water (moisture) to germinate.
chunks.source: Seeds need water (moisture) to germinate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way do people control the spread of malaria in their homes? A: By sleeping under treated mosquito nets. Nets stop mosquitoes from biting at night.
chunks.source: Nets stop mosquitoes from biting at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do parents take their children for immunization? A: To protect them against immunisable diseases. Immunisation protects children from killer diseases.
chunks.source: Immunisation protects children from killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is anemometer useful at a weather station? A: It measures the speed of wind. An anemometer has cups that spin to measure how fast wind blows.
chunks.source: An anemometer has cups that spin to measure how fast wind blows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why farmers mulch their garden. A: To keep water in the soil. Mulch stops water from drying out of the soil.
chunks.source: Mulch stops water from drying out of the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the habitat for a fish. A: Water. Fish live in water.
chunks.source: Fish live in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the habitat for a fish. A: Water. Fish live in water.
chunks.source: Fish live in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a spider not considered to be an insect? A: Because it has eight legs while insects have six legs. Insects have six legs; spiders have eight.
chunks.source: Insects have six legs; spiders have eight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write the use of splints to a first aider. A: Splints are used to keep broken bones in position. A splint supports a broken bone so it does not move.
chunks.source: A splint supports a broken bone so it does not move.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a poultry farmer improve on his/her local breeds of chicken? A: By cross breeding local chicken with exotic breeds. Cross breeding mixes good qualities of both breeds.
chunks.source: Cross breeding mixes good qualities of both breeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a cockroach. Briefly describe any one danger of the above insect to people. A: Cockroaches contaminate our food and spread diseases. Cockroaches carry germs onto food and cause diseases like cholera.
chunks.source: Cockroaches carry germs onto food and cause diseases like cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one activity you can do to keep your body clean. A: Bathing every day. Bathing removes dirt and sweat from the body.
chunks.source: Bathing removes dirt and sweat from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one activity you can do to keep your body clean. A: Bathing every day. Bathing removes dirt and sweat from the body.
chunks.source: Bathing removes dirt and sweat from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do dogs help in protecting our homes? A: They bark to alert us and chase away thieves. Dogs bark at strangers and scare thieves away.
chunks.source: Dogs bark at strangers and scare thieves away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one danger of drinking unboiled water. A: It may contain germs that cause diseases like cholera. Unboiled water can carry germs.
chunks.source: Unboiled water can carry germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the rearing of bees useful to a crop farmer? A: Bees help to pollinate the farmer's crops. Bees carry pollen as they visit flowers.
chunks.source: Bees carry pollen as they visit flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List down any one example of perennial crops grown in Uganda. A: Mango. Mango trees live and produce for many years.
chunks.source: Mango trees live and produce for many years.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List down any one example of perennial crops grown in Uganda. A: Mango. Mango trees live and produce for many years.
chunks.source: Mango trees live and produce for many years.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the putting of humps on roads help to control accidents on Uganda roads? A: Humps force drivers to reduce speed. Slow vehicles cause fewer accidents.
chunks.source: Slow vehicles cause fewer accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do poultry farmers debeak their birds? A: To stop them from pecking and injuring one another. Debeaked birds cannot peck each other badly.
chunks.source: Debeaked birds cannot peck each other badly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger of windy weather in our environment. A: Strong wind can blow off roofs of houses. Strong wind destroys buildings and crops.
chunks.source: Strong wind destroys buildings and crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the main function of the kidney in the human body. A: To remove waste products from the blood. The kidney filters blood and forms urine.
chunks.source: The kidney filters blood and forms urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the main source of heat and light in our environment? A: The sun. The sun gives us heat and light.
chunks.source: The sun gives us heat and light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the main source of heat and light in our environment? A: The sun. The sun gives us heat and light.
chunks.source: The sun gives us heat and light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows part of a split bean seed. Give the function of part marked M to the seed. A: It protects the inner parts of the seed. M points to the testa (seed coat), which covers and protects the seed.
chunks.source: M points to the testa (seed coat), which covers and protects the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is too much sunshine dangerous to a crop farmer? A: It dries up the crops in the garden. Too much sun withers crops.
chunks.source: Too much sun withers crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way a poultry farmer can benefit from egg shells. A: Crushed egg shells are fed to birds to give them calcium. Egg shells are rich in calcium for strong shells.
chunks.source: Egg shells are rich in calcium for strong shells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the use of soap control the spread of germs to people? A: Soap kills germs on our hands and body. Washing with soap removes and kills germs.
chunks.source: Washing with soap removes and kills germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the danger of failing to brush teeth to an individual. A: It causes tooth decay. Dirty teeth rot and smell badly.
chunks.source: Dirty teeth rot and smell badly.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.source: Dirty teeth rot and smell badly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do mosquitoes fly from one place to another? A: To look for food (blood to suck). Mosquitoes move around searching for blood.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes move around searching for blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one advantage of putting litter in a poultry house. A: It keeps the poultry house warm. Litter also absorbs droppings and keeps birds comfortable.
chunks.source: Litter also absorbs droppings and keeps birds comfortable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the picture of a child shown below. Name the immunisable disease that could have affected the child in the diagram above. A: Polio. The child has a wasted leg and uses a walking stick, a sign of polio.
chunks.source: The child has a wasted leg and uses a walking stick, a sign of polio.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are vitamins grouped under protective foods? A: Because they protect our bodies against diseases. Protective foods defend the body from illness.
chunks.source: Protective foods defend the body from illness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are windows useful on a house? A: They allow fresh air and light into the house. Windows let in air and light.
chunks.source: Windows let in air and light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is air? A: Air is a mixture of gases. Air is made of nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and other gases.
chunks.source: Air is made of nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and other gases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two components of air. A: Oxygen and carbon dioxide. Air contains oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen and others.
chunks.source: Air contains oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen and others.

chunks.source: Air contains oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen and others.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which component of air supports burning? A: Oxygen. Fires need oxygen to keep burning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are people with diarrhoea given ORS? A: To replace the water and salts lost from the body. Diarrhoea removes water and salts, which ORS replaces.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea removes water and salts, which ORS replaces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the value of washing hands before preparing O.R.S? A: To stop germs from getting into the ORS. Clean hands keep the ORS safe to drink.
chunks.source: Clean hands keep the ORS safe to drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do people first taste the O.R.S before giving it to the patient? A: To make sure it is properly mixed. Tasting checks that it is not too salty or too plain.
chunks.source: Tasting checks that it is not too salty or too plain.

chunks.text: Q: Write any two common accidents at home. A: Burns and cuts. Burns and cuts happen easily at home.
chunks.source: Burns and cuts happen easily at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Describe any two ways in which you can care for a casualty. A: Give first aid and take the casualty to hospital. A casualty needs first aid and then hospital care.
chunks.source: A casualty needs first aid and then hospital care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two examples of poultry. A: Chicken and ducks. Chicken and ducks are common poultry birds.
chunks.source: Chicken and ducks are common poultry birds.

chunks.source: Poultry need good food and protection from diseases.

chunks.text: Q: Name any one process in plants that helps in the formation of rainfall. A: Transpiration. Plants release water vapour through transpiration.

chunks.source: Heat from the sun turns water into vapour.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.source: Floods destroy property and drown crops.

chunks.source: Soil also contains water, humus and mineral particles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are vectors? A: Vectors are living things that spread diseases to people. Mosquitoes and houseflies are examples of vectors.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes and houseflies are examples of vectors.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the vector that spreads cholera. A: Housefly. Houseflies carry cholera germs onto food.
chunks.source: Houseflies carry cholera germs onto food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention two ways people can control vectors in their homes. A: By spraying homes with insecticides and keeping the home clean. Spraying kills vectors and cleanliness removes their breeding places.
chunks.source: Spraying kills vectors and cleanliness removes their breeding places.

chunks.text: Q: Match the animals in A with their products in B. A: (i) Sheep (ii) Turkey (iii) Rabbit (iv) Pig. B: eggs, wool, milk, fur, pork. A: Sheep: wool; Turkey: eggs; Rabbit: fur; Pig: pork. Sheep give wool, turkeys give eggs, rabbits give fur and pigs give pork. Milk is the extra word.
chunks.source: Sheep give wool, turkeys give eggs, rabbits give fur and pigs give pork. Milk is the extra word.

chunks.source: Calcium makes egg shells hard.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagrams show containers found at home: A is a jerrycan and B is a pot. Give any one advantage of container A over container B. A: A jerrycan has a tight lid, so the water in it stays clean. The lid keeps dirt and germs out of the water.
chunks.source: The lid keeps dirt and germs out of the water.

chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of carrying out crop rotation. A: It helps to keep the soil fertile. Rotating crops rests the soil.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.source: Small pieces of food are easier to digest.

chunks.text: Q: Why should schools have projects like poultry keeping? A: To get eggs and meat, and to teach pupils farming skills. School projects give food and practical skills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the first aid terms in A with their meanings in B. A: Burn, Fracture, Scald, Dislocation. B: injury on skin caused by wet heat; break or crack in a bone; injury on skin caused by dry heat; movement of a bone from its position at a joint. A: Burn: injury on skin caused by dry heat; Scald: injury on skin caused by wet heat; Fracture: break or crack in a bone; Dislocation: movement of a bone from its position at a joint. A burn comes from dry heat, a scald from wet heat, a fracture is a broken bone and a dislocation is a bone moved from its joint.
chunks.source: A burn comes from dry heat, a scald from wet heat, a fracture is a broken bone and a dislocation is a bone moved from its joint.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is egestion? A: Egestion is the removal of undigested waste (faeces) from the body. Undigested food leaves the body as faeces.
chunks.source: Undigested food leaves the body as faeces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is an accident? A: An accident is a sudden unexpected happening that causes injury or damage. Accidents happen suddenly and without warning.
chunks.source: Accidents happen suddenly and without warning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one safety precaution when using electricity at home. A: Never touch electric switches or sockets with wet hands. Water and electricity are a dangerous mix.
chunks.source: Water and electricity are a dangerous mix.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two qualities of a good First Aider. A: A good first aider is kind and quick to act. First aiders must be caring and fast.
chunks.source: First aiders must be caring and fast.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: People keep their different body parts clean in different ways. Give any two ways we keep our bodies clean. A: Bathing daily and brushing our teeth. Bathing and brushing teeth keep the body clean.
chunks.source: Bathing and brushing teeth keep the body clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two dangers of not keeping your body clean. A: It causes bad body smell and skin diseases. Dirt causes smell and skin infections.
chunks.source: Dirt causes smell and skin infections.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do people get infected with tapeworms? A: By eating raw or half-cooked meat containing tapeworm cysts. Cysts in uncooked meat grow into tapeworms in people.
chunks.source: Cysts in uncooked meat grow into tapeworms in people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can tapeworm infestation be controlled? A: By eating well-cooked meat and deworming regularly. Cooked meat has no live cysts, and deworming kills worms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is germination? A: Germination is the process by which a seed grows into a seedling. A seed sprouts and grows into a young plant.
chunks.source: A seed sprouts and grows into a young plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides water, name one other condition necessary for seed germination. A: Warmth. Seeds also need warmth and air.
chunks.source: Seeds also need warmth and air.

chunks.text: Q: How is water important during germination? A: Water softens the seed coat so the seed can sprout. Softening lets the young root break out.
chunks.source: Softening lets the young root break out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one factor that may fail a seed to germinate. A: Lack of water. Dry seeds cannot germinate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is soil erosion? A: Soil erosion is the carrying away of top soil by water or wind. Top soil is removed by running water or wind.
chunks.source: Top soil is removed by running water or wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two non-living agents of soil erosion. A: Water and wind. Running water and wind carry soil away.
chunks.source: Running water and wind carry soil away.

chunks.text: Q: How is soil erosion dangerous to crop farmers? A: It carries away the fertile top soil, so crops grow poorly. Without top soil, crops lack nutrients.

A: Put the salt and sand in a container and add water., Stir to dissolve the salt., Filter to remove sand from the solution., Boil the solution to dryness.. First add water, then stir, then filter out the sand, and finally boil to get the salt.

chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for crop farmers to weed their gardens regularly? A: To stop weeds from competing with crops for nutrients and water. Weeds steal food and water from crops.
chunks.source: Weeds steal food and water from crops.

chunks.text: Q: Identify one way of caring for insects. A: By giving bees clean hives and protecting them from enemies. Useful insects like bees need good hives.
chunks.source: Useful insects like bees need good hives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do objects weigh less in water than on land? A: Because water exerts an upward push (upthrust) on them. Upthrust pushes objects up, making them feel lighter.
chunks.source: Upthrust pushes objects up, making them feel lighter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a kidney important in a human body? A: It removes waste products from the blood. The kidney filters blood and forms urine.
chunks.source: The kidney filters blood and forms urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is de-beaking important in poultry keeping? A: It stops birds from pecking and injuring one another. Debeaked birds cannot hurt each other.
chunks.source: Debeaked birds cannot hurt each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way does slashing around our homes help in controlling malaria? ____ A: It destroys hiding and breeding places of mosquitoes.. Mosquitoes hide and breed in bushy places; slashing removes them.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes hide and breed in bushy places; slashing removes them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a house. How is part labeled R (the window) useful to the people who stay in such a house? ____ A: It allows fresh air and light to enter the house.. Windows let in fresh air and daylight and let out bad air.
chunks.source: Windows let in fresh air and daylight and let out bad air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one activity you can carry out to keep your bedroom clean. ____ A: Sweeping the floor daily.. A clean bedroom needs sweeping, dusting and arranging beddings.

chunks.source: Safety rules, like not playing with sharp objects, prevent accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What advice would you give to a friend with a bad breath? ____ A: Brush the teeth every day and visit a dentist.. Bad breath is reduced by brushing teeth daily and treating sick teeth.
chunks.source: Bad breath is reduced by brushing teeth daily and treating sick teeth.

chunks.source: Pesticides kill crop pests; other ways include weeding and crop rotation.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a) List any two examples of useful insects: (i) ____ (ii) ____ A: Honey bees and butterflies. Useful insects help people; bees give honey and butterflies help pollinate flowers.
chunks.source: Useful insects help people; bees give honey and butterflies help pollinate flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) Give two ways of caring for insects: (i) ____ (ii) ____ A: By not killing useful insects and by protecting their habitats.. We care for insects by protecting their homes and avoiding harmful sprays.
chunks.source: We care for insects by protecting their homes and avoiding harmful sprays.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a) Briefly explain the term crop rotation. ____ A: Crop rotation is the growing of different crops on the same piece of land in turns.. Instead of growing the same crop every season, a farmer changes crops each season.
chunks.source: Instead of growing the same crop every season, a farmer changes crops each season.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) Why are legumes included in a crop rotation cycle? ____ A: Because legumes add nitrogen to the soil.. Legumes have root nodules with bacteria that fix nitrogen into the soil.
chunks.source: Legumes have root nodules with bacteria that fix nitrogen into the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c) How is crop rotation important to a farmer? Give two ways: (i) ____ (ii) ____ A: It keeps the soil fertile and controls crop pests and diseases.. Changing crops keeps soil rich and breaks the life cycle of pests.
chunks.source: Changing crops keeps soil rich and breaks the life cycle of pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a) Why is it important to feed a family on a balanced diet? ____ A: A balanced diet keeps the body healthy and protects it from deficiency diseases.. A balanced diet has all food values the body needs to grow and stay healthy.
chunks.source: A balanced diet has all food values the body needs to grow and stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b) Write any two food values in a balanced diet: (i) ____ (ii) ____ A: Carbohydrates and proteins. A balanced diet contains carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, fats and mineral salts.
chunks.source: A balanced diet contains carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, fats and mineral salts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c) How can drought affect a family's feeding in rural areas? ____ A: Drought kills crops, so families get little food to eat.. Without rain, crops fail and families face hunger.
chunks.source: Without rain, crops fail and families face hunger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a) Give one example of plants that can be used as: (i) plant fibre ____ (ii) medicinal plant ____ A: (i) Cotton (ii) Aloe vera. Cotton gives plant fibre for cloth; aloe vera is used as medicine.
chunks.source: Cotton gives plant fibre for cloth; aloe vera is used as medicine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a) What are enzymes? ____ A: Enzymes are chemicals in the body that speed up digestion of food.. Enzymes break down food faster in the digestive system.
chunks.source: Enzymes break down food faster in the digestive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b) Name one enzyme found in the following parts of the digestive system: (i) mouth ____ (ii) duodenum ____ A: (i) Salivary amylase (ii) Lipase (pancreatic enzymes). The mouth has salivary amylase; the duodenum receives pancreatic enzymes like lipase.
chunks.source: The mouth has salivary amylase; the duodenum receives pancreatic enzymes like lipase.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c) State one disorder of the digestive system. ____ A: Constipation. Disorders of the digestive system include constipation, diarrhoea and ulcers.
chunks.source: Disorders of the digestive system include constipation, diarrhoea and ulcers.

chunks.text: Q: 45(c) State one disorder of the digestive system. ___ A: Constipation. Disorders of the digestive system include constipation, diarrhoea and ulcers.
chunks.source: Disorders of the digestive system include constipation, diarrhoea and ulcers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) The diagram below shows the positions of some human body organs. Name the organs marked: (i) X ____ (ii) Y ____ A: (i) X: lungs (ii) Y: nose. X points to the lungs in the chest; Y points to the nose where air enters.
chunks.source: X points to the lungs in the chest; Y points to the nose where air enters.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) How is the function of Y different from that of X? ____ A: Y (the nose) cleans, warms and moistens air entering the body, while X (the lungs) exchange gases by taking in oxygen and removing carbon dioxide.. The nose prepares air; the lungs do the exchange of gases.
chunks.source: The nose prepares air; the lungs do the exchange of gases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c) How can you keep the organ marked X (the lungs) in good working condition? ____ A: By avoiding smoking and dusty air, and doing breathing exercises.. Clean air and exercise keep the lungs healthy.
chunks.source: Clean air and exercise keep the lungs healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) Apart from B.C.G vaccine, give other two vaccines administered to babies: (i) ____ (ii) ____ A: Polio vaccine and DPT vaccine. Babies also receive polio vaccine and DPT against killer diseases.
chunks.source: Babies also receive polio vaccine and DPT against killer diseases.

chunks.text: Q: 47(a) Apart from B.C.G vaccine, give other two vaccines administered to babies: (i) ___ (ii) ___ A: Polio vaccine and DPT vaccine. Babies also receive polio vaccine and DPT against killer diseases.

chunks.source: Babies also receive polio vaccine and DPT against killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b) Why is B.C.G vaccine administered at birth? ____ A: To protect the baby against tuberculosis early in life.. BCG protects newborn babies against tuberculosis (TB).
chunks.source: BCG protects newborn babies against tuberculosis (TB).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) What advice can you give to Mr. Lutu whose children are suffering from measles? ____ A: Take the children to the nearest health centre for treatment.. Sick children should be taken to a health worker quickly.
chunks.source: Sick children should be taken to a health worker quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a) Identify any two harmful materials of soil: (i) ____ (ii) ____ A: Broken glass and polythene bags. Harmful materials like broken glass, polythene and sharp metals spoil soil.
chunks.source: Harmful materials like broken glass, polythene and sharp metals spoil soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b) Give one importance of a compost pile in a home of a farmer. ____ A: It provides manure that makes soil fertile.. Compost manure from the pile adds nutrients to the soil.
chunks.source: Compost manure from the pile adds nutrients to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c) State one disadvantage of artificial fertilizers. ____ A: They are expensive and can spoil the soil if used for a long time.. Artificial fertilizers cost money and may harm soil living things.
chunks.source: Artificial fertilizers cost money and may harm soil living things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a) Give two examples of worms which commonly attack people: (i) ____ (ii) ____ A: Tapeworms and roundworms. Common worms in people include tapeworms, roundworms and hookworms.
chunks.source: Common worms in people include tapeworms, roundworms and hookworms.

chunks.text: Q: 49(a) Give two examples of worms which commonly attack people: (i) ___ (ii) ___ A: Tapeworms and roundworms. Common worms in people include tapeworms, roundworms and hookworms.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.source: Common worms in people include tapeworms, roundworms and hookworms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) Name any two examples of ecto-parasites which depend on people: (i) ____ (ii) ____ A: Lice and fleas. Ecto-parasites live on the body; examples are lice, fleas, ticks and bedbugs.
chunks.source: Ecto-parasites live on the body; examples are lice, fleas, ticks and bedbugs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) Name any two examples of ecto-parasites which depend on people: (i) ___ (ii) ___ A: Lice and fleas. Ecto-parasites live on the body; examples are lice, fleas, ticks and bedbugs.
chunks.source: Ecto-parasites live on the body; examples are lice, fleas, ticks and bedbugs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a) Give the meaning of the term communicable diseases. ____ A: Communicable diseases are diseases that spread from one person to another.. They move from a sick person to a healthy person.
chunks.source: They move from a sick person to a healthy person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b) How is diarrhea as a communicable disease spread? ____ A: It spreads through eating contaminated food or drinking dirty water.. Germs from faeces get into food and water and cause diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Germs from faeces get into food and water and cause diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c) Why is ORS given to patients who have diarrhoeal diseases? ____ A: ORS replaces the water and salts lost from the body.. Diarrhoea removes water and salts; ORS puts them back.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea removes water and salts; ORS puts them back.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(d) Why are school children advised to abstain from sex? ____ A: To avoid HIV/AIDS and early pregnancies.. Abstaining keeps children safe from HIV and early pregnancy.
chunks.source: Abstaining keeps children safe from HIV and early pregnancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a) Sanitation is the general cleanliness of the environment. Mention any two ways children keep the school compound clean: (i) ____ (ii) ____ A: Sweeping the compound and picking up rubbish. Children keep school clean by sweeping, slashing and putting rubbish in dustbins.
chunks.source: Children keep school clean by sweeping, slashing and putting rubbish in dustbins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b) How does smoking improve on the cleanliness of a pit latrine? ____ A: The smoke kills germs and drives away flies that spread diseases.. Smoke in a latrine chases flies and reduces bad smell.
chunks.source: Smoke in a latrine chases flies and reduces bad smell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c) Give one advantage of a VIP latrine over an ordinary pit latrine. ____ A: A VIP latrine has a vent pipe that removes bad smell and keeps away flies.. The vent pipe of a VIP latrine takes away smell and traps flies.
chunks.source: The vent pipe of a VIP latrine takes away smell and traps flies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52 Match the following nutritional diseases to their causes: (i) Kwashiorkor (ii) Scurvy (iii) Rickets (iv) Anaemia ____ A: Kwashiorkor: Lack of enough proteins; Scurvy: Lack of enough vitamin C; Rickets: Lack of enough vitamin D; Anaemia: Lack of enough iron. Each deficiency disease is caused by lack of a certain food value: proteins, vitamin C, vitamin D and iron.
chunks.source: Each deficiency disease is caused by lack of a certain food value: proteins, vitamin C, vitamin D and iron.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a) List down any two breeds of rabbits kept in Uganda: (i) ____ (ii) ____ A: New Zealand White and Californian. Common rabbit breeds in Uganda include New Zealand White, Californian and Chinchilla.
chunks.source: Common rabbit breeds in Uganda include New Zealand White, Californian and Chinchilla.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) How do rabbit farmers control the spread of rabbit diseases on their farms? ____ A: By keeping hutches clean and isolating sick rabbits.. Clean hutches and separating sick rabbits stop diseases spreading.
chunks.source: Clean hutches and separating sick rabbits stop diseases spreading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c) Why do some farmers prefer keeping rabbits to other animals like cows? ____ A: Rabbits need little space and little food, and they multiply fast.. Rabbits are cheap to keep and produce many young ones quickly.
chunks.source: Rabbits are cheap to keep and produce many young ones quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a) Mention any one man-made change in the environment. ____ A: Building roads. People change the environment by building roads, houses and cutting down forests.
chunks.source: People change the environment by building roads, houses and cutting down forests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b) How are floods dangerous in the environment? ____ A: Floods destroy crops, homes and spread diseases.. Too much water destroys property and brings water-borne diseases.
chunks.source: Too much water destroys property and brings water-borne diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) Which type of weather enables farmers to winnow their seeds? ____ A: Windy weather. Wind blows away light chaff when farmers winnow seeds.
chunks.source: Wind blows away light chaff when farmers winnow seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) Which type of weather enables farmers to winnow their seeds? ___ A: Windy weather. Wind blows away light chaff when farmers winnow seeds.

chunks.text: Q: 54(d) Why do people use umbrellas when walking under rain? ____ A: To protect themselves from getting wet.. Umbrellas keep rain off our bodies and clothes.

chunks.source: A compass shows direction using a magnetic needle that points north.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one block mountain in Uganda. A: Mt. Rwenzori. Mt. Rwenzori is a block mountain formed by faulting.
chunks.source: Mt. Rwenzori is a block mountain formed by faulting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way landslides can affect transport in highland areas. A: They block roads and destroy them. Landslides cover roads with soil and rocks so vehicles cannot pass.
chunks.source: Landslides cover roads with soil and rocks so vehicles cannot pass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one economic importance of keeping domestic animals. A: They give milk, meat and income. Domestic animals give us milk, meat, eggs and money when sold.
chunks.source: Domestic animals give us milk, meat, eggs and money when sold.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are hills important during road construction? A: Hills provide stones and murram for building roads. Stones and murram got from hills are used to make strong roads.
chunks.source: Stones and murram got from hills are used to make strong roads.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do farmers in highlands control soil erosion? A: by terracing and contour ploughing. Terraces slow down running water so it does not carry away the soil.
chunks.source: Terraces slow down running water so it does not carry away the soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is the short grass around our school compound very important? A: It controls soil erosion. Short grass holds the soil together and stops wind and water from carrying it away.
chunks.source: Short grass holds the soil together and stops wind and water from carrying it away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What general name is given to all lines of longitudes? A: meridians. All lines of longitude are called meridians.
chunks.source: All lines of longitude are called meridians.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How were the rift valleys formed? A: by faulting. Rift valleys were formed when the land between faults sank due to tension forces in the earth's crust.
chunks.source: Rift valleys were formed when the land between faults sank due to tension forces in the earth's crust.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is vegetation used to improve on the health of Ugandans? A: Vegetation gives medicine, fruits and fresh air. Trees give us medicine, fruits, firewood and clean air to breathe.
chunks.source: Trees give us medicine, fruits, firewood and clean air to breathe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State two ways people have destroyed the vegetation in some parts of Uganda. A: deforestation and charcoal burning. People destroy vegetation by cutting down trees without planting new ones and by burning charcoal.
chunks.source: People destroy vegetation by cutting down trees without planting new ones and by burning charcoal.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way the government of Uganda can protect the vegetation. A: by planting trees (afforestation) and making laws against deforestation. The government can protect vegetation by planting more trees and punishing those who destroy forests.
chunks.source: The government can protect vegetation by planting more trees and punishing those who destroy forests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do farmers benefit from vegetation? A: They get firewood, timber, fruits and medicine from it. Farmers get firewood for cooking, timber for building and fruits for food from vegetation.
chunks.source: Farmers get firewood for cooking, timber for building and fruits for food from vegetation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match each type of farming to its correct description. A: Dairy farming: The keeping of cattle for milk production.; Plantation farming: The growing of one perennial crop on a large scale.; Mixed farming: The growing of crops and keeping of animals on the same piece of land.; Subsistence farming: The growing of crops for home use.. Dairy farming is keeping cattle for milk, plantation farming grows one perennial crop on a large scale, mixed farming combines crops and animals, and subsistence farming grows crops for home use.
chunks.source: Dairy farming is keeping cattle for milk, plantation farming grows one perennial crop on a large scale, mixed farming combines crops and animals, and subsistence farming grows crops for home use.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is rural – urban migration? A: the movement of people from villages to towns. Rural-urban migration is when people leave villages to go and live in towns.
chunks.source: Rural-urban migration is when people leave villages to go and live in towns.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Apart from a cow, name another domestic animal kept for milk. A: a goat. Apart from a cow, a goat is also kept for milk.
chunks.source: Apart from a cow, a goat is also kept for milk.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two reasons why people practise rural – urban migration. A: They look for jobs and better social services. People move to towns to find jobs, good schools and hospitals.
chunks.source: People move to towns to find jobs, good schools and hospitals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can domestic animals be dangerous to people? A: They spread diseases and destroy crops. Domestic animals can spread diseases to people and eat or destroy people's crops.
chunks.source: Domestic animals can spread diseases to people and eat or destroy people's crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why Kampala has more people than other districts. A: Kampala is the capital city with many jobs and industries. Kampala has more people because it is the capital city with many jobs, industries and social services.
chunks.source: Kampala has more people because it is the capital city with many jobs, industries and social services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can overcrowding be controlled on a map? A: by using symbols. Symbols are used on maps to show many features in a small space without overcrowding.
chunks.source: Symbols are used on maps to show many features in a small space without overcrowding.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one element of a good map. A: a title. A good map must have a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.
chunks.source: A good map must have a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one way of conserving the environment. A: by planting trees. Planting trees replaces those cut down and keeps the environment green.
chunks.source: Planting trees replaces those cut down and keeps the environment green.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any one volcanic mountain in Uganda. A: Mt. Elgon. Mt. Elgon is a volcanic mountain formed by volcanicity.
chunks.source: Mt. Elgon is a volcanic mountain formed by volcanicity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are the shores of L. Victoria densely populated? A: because of fishing, fertile soils and trade. Many people live near Lake Victoria because they fish, farm on fertile soils and trade.
chunks.source: Many people live near Lake Victoria because they fish, farm on fertile soils and trade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are latitudes important to a map reader? A: They help a map reader to locate places. Latitudes help a map reader find the exact position of a place on a map.
chunks.source: Latitudes help a map reader find the exact position of a place on a map.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is land taken to be the most important resource? A: Land is used for farming, settlement and building. Land is the most important resource because we farm on it, build houses on it and get minerals from it.
chunks.source: Land is the most important resource because we farm on it, build houses on it and get minerals from it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do terraces help in controlling soil erosion in hilly areas? A: They slow down running water. Terraces are steps cut across slopes that slow down water so it does not wash away soil.
chunks.source: Terraces are steps cut across slopes that slow down water so it does not wash away soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one means of transport used by children when coming to school. A: walking. Many children walk to school.
chunks.source: Many children walk to school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which type of natural vegetation covers the largest part of Uganda? A: savanna vegetation. Savanna vegetation covers the largest part of Uganda.
chunks.source: Savanna vegetation covers the largest part of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write any one product got from hard wood timber. A: furniture. Hard wood timber from natural forests is used to make furniture.
chunks.source: Hard wood timber from natural forests is used to make furniture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are mountains important to our country? A: They attract tourists, bring rainfall and give minerals. Mountains are important because they attract tourists, help in rain formation and have minerals.
chunks.source: Mountains are important because they attract tourists, help in rain formation and have minerals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is migration? A: the movement of people from one place to another. Migration is the movement of people from one place to another to settle.
chunks.source: Migration is the movement of people from one place to another to settle.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one way phosphates promote agriculture in Uganda. A: Phosphates are used to make fertilizers. Phosphates from Tororo are used to make artificial fertilizers that make crops grow well.
chunks.source: Phosphates from Tororo are used to make artificial fertilizers that make crops grow well.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a swamp? A: a waterlogged area with vegetation growing in it. A swamp is a low lying area covered with water where plants like papyrus grow.
chunks.source: A swamp is a low lying area covered with water where plants like papyrus grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two items obtained from a swamp. A: fish and clay. People get fish, clay for making pots and papyrus from swamps.
chunks.source: People get fish, clay for making pots and papyrus from swamps.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are some people destroying swamps today? A: to get land for farming and settlement. Some people drain swamps to create land for farming, building houses and industries.
chunks.source: Some people drain swamps to create land for farming, building houses and industries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What term is used to mean the number of people living in an area per square kilometre? A: population density. Population density is the number of people living in an area per square kilometre.
chunks.source: Population density is the number of people living in an area per square kilometre.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two reasons why urban areas have many people. A: There are many jobs and good social services in urban areas. Towns have many people because of jobs in industries and good schools and hospitals.
chunks.source: Towns have many people because of jobs in industries and good schools and hospitals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do some people move from villages to towns? A: to look for jobs and better social services. People move from villages to towns to find jobs and better schools and hospitals.
chunks.source: People move from villages to towns to find jobs and better schools and hospitals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one similarity between poaching and smuggling. A: Both are illegal activities. Poaching and smuggling are both against the law.
chunks.source: Poaching and smuggling are both against the law.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why most hunters keep dogs in their homes. A: Dogs give them security and help them to hunt. Hunters keep dogs for security at home and to help catch wild animals when hunting.
chunks.source: Hunters keep dogs for security at home and to help catch wild animals when hunting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are most tourists who go to game parks given security? A: to protect them from wild animals and thieves. Tourists are given security to protect them from dangerous wild animals and robbers.
chunks.source: Tourists are given security to protect them from dangerous wild animals and robbers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the neighbouring country of Uganda in the North. A: South Sudan. South Sudan is the country in the north of Uganda.
chunks.source: South Sudan is the country in the north of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one importance of vegetation to man. A: Vegetation brings rainfall and gives timber. Vegetation is important because it helps in rain formation and gives us timber and firewood.
chunks.source: Vegetation is important because it helps in rain formation and gives us timber and firewood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the line of longitude marked 180o. A: the International Date Line. The line of longitude marked 180 degrees is the International Date Line.
chunks.source: The line of longitude marked 180 degrees is the International Date Line.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is grass useful to builders? A: Grass is used for thatching houses. Builders use grass to thatch roofs of houses.
chunks.source: Builders use grass to thatch roofs of houses.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does brick making affect the land? A: Brick making destroys vegetation and leaves pits in the land. Digging soil for bricks destroys vegetation and leaves ugly pits that degrade the land.
chunks.source: Digging soil for bricks destroys vegetation and leaves ugly pits that degrade the land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one major problem facing game parks in Uganda. A: poaching. Poaching, the illegal killing of wild animals, is a major problem facing game parks.
chunks.source: Poaching, the illegal killing of wild animals, is a major problem facing game parks.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one tributary of R. Nile in Uganda. A: River Achwa. River Achwa is a tributary of the River Nile in Uganda.
chunks.source: River Achwa is a tributary of the River Nile in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Apart from gold, which other mineral is mined from Karamoja region. A: limestone. Apart from gold, limestone is also mined in Karamoja.
chunks.source: Apart from gold, limestone is also mined in Karamoja.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which National organization is in charge of forests in Uganda? A: National Forestry Authority (NFA). The National Forestry Authority is in charge of forests in Uganda.
chunks.source: The National Forestry Authority is in charge of forests in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State two economic importance of forests in Uganda. A: Forests give timber and attract tourists. Forests are economically important because they give timber for sale and attract tourists.
chunks.source: Forests are economically important because they give timber for sale and attract tourists.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can forests be conserved? A: by planting more trees (afforestation). Forests can be conserved by planting more trees and stopping illegal cutting.
chunks.source: Forests can be conserved by planting more trees and stopping illegal cutting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State two economic activities done in swampy areas. A: fishing and farming. People in swampy areas carry out fishing and growing of crops like yams and sugarcane.
chunks.source: People in swampy areas carry out fishing and growing of crops like yams and sugarcane.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are floods dangerous to people in our community? A: Floods destroy crops, houses and kill people. Floods are dangerous because they destroy crops and houses and can drown people and animals.
chunks.source: Floods are dangerous because they destroy crops and houses and can drown people and animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which one way can rivers be a problem to people? A: Rivers cause floods that destroy crops and houses. Rivers can be a problem when they flood and destroy people's crops and homes.
chunks.source: Rivers can be a problem when they flood and destroy people's crops and homes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of lines of longitudes and latitude to a map reader. A: They help a map reader to locate places. Lines of longitude and latitude help a map reader find the exact location of a place.
chunks.source: Lines of longitude and latitude help a map reader find the exact location of a place.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one effect of overgrazing to the environment. A: It causes soil erosion. Overgrazing leaves the land bare so wind and water easily carry away the soil.
chunks.source: Overgrazing leaves the land bare so wind and water easily carry away the soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the use of map symbols to a map reader. A: Map symbols represent real features and reduce overcrowding on a map. Map symbols stand for real things like rivers and roads so the map is not overcrowded.
chunks.source: Map symbols stand for real things like rivers and roads so the map is not overcrowded.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Apart from Kalangala, name another Island district in Uganda. A: Buvuma. Apart from Kalangala, Buvuma is another island district in Uganda.
chunks.source: Apart from Kalangala, Buvuma is another island district in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why people in Kapchorwa rear donkeys. A: Donkeys are used for transport in the hilly areas. People in Kapchorwa rear donkeys to carry loads in the hilly areas where vehicles cannot go.
chunks.source: People in Kapchorwa rear donkeys to carry loads in the hilly areas where vehicles cannot go.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the capital city of the neighbouring country of Uganda to the South West? A: Kigali. Kigali is the capital city of Rwanda, the neighbouring country in the south west of Uganda.
chunks.source: Kigali is the capital city of Rwanda, the neighbouring country in the south west of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why Kampala has many people. A: Kampala is the capital city with many jobs and industries. Kampala has many people because it is the capital with many jobs and social services.
chunks.source: Kampala has many people because it is the capital with many jobs and social services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is limestone important to builders in Uganda? A: Limestone is used to make cement. Limestone is important to builders because it is used to make cement for building houses.
chunks.source: Limestone is important to builders because it is used to make cement for building houses.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What type of wood is got from natural forests? A: hard wood. Hard wood is got from natural forests.
chunks.source: Hard wood is got from natural forests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mary was facing North, she turned at an angle of 900 clock wise, what was her new direction? A: East. Turning 90 degrees clockwise from North faces East.
chunks.source: Turning 90 degrees clockwise from North faces East.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How many countries border Uganda? A: five. Five countries border Uganda: Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, DR Congo and South Sudan.
chunks.source: Five countries border Uganda: Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, DR Congo and South Sudan.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is Uganda called a land locked country? A: Uganda is surrounded by land with no sea coast. Uganda is called landlocked because it has no direct access to the sea.
chunks.source: Uganda is called landlocked because it has no direct access to the sea.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two problems Uganda faces as a landlocked country. A: High transport costs and depending on neighbours for sea routes. As a landlocked country Uganda pays high transport costs and depends on neighbours to reach the sea.
chunks.source: As a landlocked country Uganda pays high transport costs and depends on neighbours to reach the sea.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the lakes in Uganda crossed by the equator. A: Lake Victoria and Lake George. The equator crosses Lake Victoria and Lake George in Uganda.
chunks.source: The equator crosses Lake Victoria and Lake George in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the largest lake in Uganda. A: Lake Victoria. Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Uganda.
chunks.source: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two importance of lakes to the people. A: Lakes give fish and are used for transport. Lakes are important because people get fish from them and use them for water transport.
chunks.source: Lakes are important because people get fish from them and use them for water transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are areas round L.Victoria densily populated? A: because of fishing and fertile soils. Areas round Lake Victoria are densely populated because people fish and farm on fertile soils there.
chunks.source: Areas round Lake Victoria are densely populated because people fish and farm on fertile soils there.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is transport? A: the movement of people and goods from one place to another. Transport is the movement of people and goods from one place to another.
chunks.source: Transport is the movement of people and goods from one place to another.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention two types of transport used in Uganda. A: road transport and water transport. The main types of transport in Uganda are road, water, railway and air transport.
chunks.source: The main types of transport in Uganda are road, water, railway and air transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match each material to what is made from it. A: Tobacco: cigarettes; Cotton: clothes; Sisal: mats; Charcoal: wood. Tobacco makes cigarettes, cotton makes clothes, sisal makes mats, and charcoal is made from wood.
chunks.source: Tobacco makes cigarettes, cotton makes clothes, sisal makes mats, and charcoal is made from wood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why does River Katonga flow form L.George to L.Victoria? A: River Katonga flows from a higher to a lower altitude. River Katonga flows from Lake George to Lake Victoria because Lake George is at a higher altitude.
chunks.source: River Katonga flows from Lake George to Lake Victoria because Lake George is at a higher altitude.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Apart from sand mining, mention another economic activity carried out on L.Victoria. A: fishing. Apart from sand mining, fishing is another economic activity carried out on Lake Victoria.
chunks.source: Apart from sand mining, fishing is another economic activity carried out on Lake Victoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way land is used in Uganda. A: Land is used for farming. Land in Uganda is used for farming, settlement and building.
chunks.source: Land in Uganda is used for farming, settlement and building.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are physical features? A: Physical features are natural landforms on the earth's surface. Physical features are natural things like mountains, hills, valleys, lakes and rivers found on land.
chunks.source: Physical features are natural things like mountains, hills, valleys, lakes and rivers found on land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why water transport is difficult on some parts of river Nile. A: because of waterfalls and rapids. Water transport is difficult on some parts of the Nile because of waterfalls like Murchison Falls and rapids.
chunks.source: Water transport is difficult on some parts of the Nile because of waterfalls like Murchison Falls and rapids.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define the term: Delta. A: a fan-shaped area of land formed at the mouth of a river by deposited soil. A delta is formed when a river deposits soil at its mouth.
chunks.source: A delta is formed when a river deposits soil at its mouth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define the term: Estuary. A: the wide mouth of a river where it meets a lake or sea. An estuary is the wide mouth of a river where fresh water mixes with lake or sea water.
chunks.source: An estuary is the wide mouth of a river where fresh water mixes with lake or sea water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of controlling soil erosion in mountainous areas. A: by terracing. Terracing controls soil erosion in mountainous areas by slowing down running water.
chunks.source: Terracing controls soil erosion in mountainous areas by slowing down running water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are escarpments? A: steep slopes at the sides of a rift valley. Escarpments are the steep sides of a rift valley formed by faulting.
chunks.source: Escarpments are the steep sides of a rift valley formed by faulting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: On which lake is port Butiaba? A: Lake Albert. Port Butiaba is found on Lake Albert.
chunks.source: Port Butiaba is found on Lake Albert.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the deepest lake in Uganda. A: Lake Bunyonyi. Lake Bunyonyi is the deepest lake in Uganda.
chunks.source: Lake Bunyonyi is the deepest lake in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why the slopes of some mountains have very many people. A: because of fertile soils and good rainfall. Mountain slopes have many people because the soils are fertile and rainfall is reliable for farming.
chunks.source: Mountain slopes have many people because the soils are fertile and rainfall is reliable for farming.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does altitude affect the climate of an area? A: The higher the altitude, the cooler the climate. Altitude affects climate because temperature falls as height above sea level increases.
chunks.source: Altitude affects climate because temperature falls as height above sea level increases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is Lake Victoria similar to lake Kyoga in terms of formation? A: Both were formed by downwarping. Lake Victoria and Lake Kyoga are similar because both were formed by downwarping.
chunks.source: Lake Victoria and Lake Kyoga are similar because both were formed by downwarping.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the mineral found around L. Albert. A: crude oil. Crude oil (petroleum) is found around Lake Albert.
chunks.source: Crude oil (petroleum) is found around Lake Albert.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which physical feature covers the largest part of Uganda? A: the plateau. The plateau covers the largest part of Uganda.
chunks.source: The plateau covers the largest part of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is Road construction difficult in Kabale and Bundibugyo districts? A: because the areas are hilly and mountainous. Road construction is difficult in Kabale and Bundibugyo because the land is hilly and mountainous.
chunks.source: Road construction is difficult in Kabale and Bundibugyo because the land is hilly and mountainous.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who was the first European explorer to see Mt. Elgon? A: Joseph Thomson. Joseph Thomson was the first European explorer to see Mt. Elgon.
chunks.source: Joseph Thomson was the first European explorer to see Mt. Elgon.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who was the first European explorer to see the River Nile? A: John Hanning Speke. John Hanning Speke was the first European explorer to see the River Nile (its source).
chunks.source: John Hanning Speke was the first European explorer to see the River Nile (its source).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who was the first European explorer to see Mt. Rwenzori? A: Henry Morton Stanley. Henry Morton Stanley was the first European explorer to see Mt. Rwenzori.
chunks.source: Henry Morton Stanley was the first European explorer to see Mt. Rwenzori.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who was the first European explorer to see Lake Albert? A: Sir Samuel Baker. Sir Samuel Baker was the first European explorer to see Lake Albert.
chunks.source: Sir Samuel Baker was the first European explorer to see Lake Albert.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How was Mt. Rwenzori formed? A: by faulting. Mt. Rwenzori was formed by faulting, which pushed up a block of land.
chunks.source: Mt. Rwenzori was formed by faulting, which pushed up a block of land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is altitude? A: the height of land above sea level. Altitude is the height of a place above sea level.
chunks.source: Altitude is the height of a place above sea level.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is the highest peak of Mt. Rwenzori snow capped? A: because it is very high and therefore very cold. The peak of Mt. Rwenzori is snow capped because its great height makes it very cold.
chunks.source: The peak of Mt. Rwenzori is snow capped because its great height makes it very cold.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What type of mountain is Mt. Elgon? A: a volcanic mountain. Mt. Elgon is a volcanic mountain formed by volcanicity.
chunks.source: Mt. Elgon is a volcanic mountain formed by volcanicity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two characteristics of rift valley lakes. A: They are salty and long and narrow. Rift valley lakes are salty and are long, narrow and deep.
chunks.source: Rift valley lakes are salty and are long, narrow and deep.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the most swampy lake in Uganda. A: Lake Kyoga. Lake Kyoga is the most swampy lake in Uganda.
chunks.source: Lake Kyoga is the most swampy lake in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are rift valley lakes salty? A: because they have no outlet and lose water by evaporation. Rift valley lakes are salty because they have no outlet, so salts collect as water evaporates.
chunks.source: Rift valley lakes are salty because they have no outlet, so salts collect as water evaporates.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is vegetation? A: the plant cover of an area. Vegetation is the plant cover of an area, both natural and planted.
chunks.source: Vegetation is the plant cover of an area, both natural and planted.

chunks.subject: Social
