chunks.text: Q: What is deforestation? A: the cutting down of trees without replacing them. Deforestation is the cutting down of trees on a large scale without planting new ones.
chunks.source: Deforestation is the cutting down of trees on a large scale without planting new ones.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one cause of deforestation. A: charcoal burning. Charcoal burning is a major cause of deforestation in Uganda.
chunks.source: Charcoal burning is a major cause of deforestation in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any four factors that influence vegetation distribution. A: rainfall, altitude, soils and human activities. Vegetation distribution is influenced by rainfall, altitude, soils and human activities.
chunks.source: Vegetation distribution is influenced by rainfall, altitude, soils and human activities.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is natural vegetation? A: plants that grow on their own without being planted by man. Natural vegetation grows by itself without being planted by people.
chunks.source: Natural vegetation grows by itself without being planted by people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two ways in which people destroy vegetation in Uganda. A: through deforestation and charcoal burning. People destroy vegetation by cutting down trees and burning charcoal.
chunks.source: People destroy vegetation by cutting down trees and burning charcoal.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of natural vegetation suitable for climbing animals. A: tropical rainforest. Tropical rainforest has tall trees suitable for climbing animals like monkeys.
chunks.source: Tropical rainforest has tall trees suitable for climbing animals like monkeys.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is agro-forestry? A: the growing of crops and trees on the same piece of land. Agro-forestry is growing crops together with trees on the same land.
chunks.source: Agro-forestry is growing crops together with trees on the same land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two uses of forests to a farmer. A: Forests give firewood and timber. Forests are useful to a farmer because they give firewood, timber, fruits and medicine.
chunks.source: Forests are useful to a farmer because they give firewood, timber, fruits and medicine.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one problem facing natural forests in Uganda. A: deforestation. Deforestation is a major problem facing natural forests in Uganda.
chunks.source: Deforestation is a major problem facing natural forests in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two causes of swamp drainage. A: farming and settlement. Swamps are drained to create land for farming and settlement.
chunks.source: Swamps are drained to create land for farming and settlement.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the two types of vegetation. A: natural vegetation and planted vegetation. The two types of vegetation are natural vegetation and planted vegetation.
chunks.source: The two types of vegetation are natural vegetation and planted vegetation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a tree species found in natural forests. A: mvule. Mvule is a tree species found in natural forests.
chunks.source: Mvule is a tree species found in natural forests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any two natural forests found in Uganda. A: Mabira and Budongo. Mabira and Budongo are natural forests found in Uganda.
chunks.source: Mabira and Budongo are natural forests found in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which type of natural vegetation covers the largest part of Uganda? A: savanna vegetation. Savanna vegetation covers the largest part of Uganda.
chunks.source: Savanna vegetation covers the largest part of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List down any three types of natural vegetation. A: savanna, tropical rainforest and montane vegetation. The main types of natural vegetation are savanna, tropical rainforest and montane vegetation.
chunks.source: The main types of natural vegetation are savanna, tropical rainforest and montane vegetation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write any one characteristic of tropical rain forests. A: It has tall evergreen trees. Tropical rainforests have tall evergreen trees with a thick canopy.
chunks.source: Tropical rainforests have tall evergreen trees with a thick canopy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What type of wood is got from planted forests? A: soft wood. Soft wood is got from planted forests.
chunks.source: Soft wood is got from planted forests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are most game parks in Uganda found in Savanna vegetation? A: because savanna has grass for wild animals to graze. Most game parks are in savanna because the grass feeds grazing animals and the open land makes animals easy to see.
chunks.source: Most game parks are in savanna because the grass feeds grazing animals and the open land makes animals easy to see.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are swamps? A: waterlogged areas where plants like papyrus grow. Swamps are low areas covered with water where swamp plants grow.
chunks.source: Swamps are low areas covered with water where swamp plants grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one problem facing swamps? A: drainage for farming and settlement. Swamps face the problem of being drained for farming and settlement.
chunks.source: Swamps face the problem of being drained for farming and settlement.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a resource? A: anything that is useful to man. A resource is anything that is useful to man.
chunks.source: A resource is anything that is useful to man.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why should a tourist coming to Uganda be given a map of Uganda? A: so that the tourist can easily find places of interest. A tourist should be given a map to easily locate tourist attractions in Uganda.
chunks.source: A tourist should be given a map to easily locate tourist attractions in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any three problems facing the tourism industry. A: poaching, poor roads and insecurity. The tourism industry faces poaching, poor roads, insecurity and few hotels.
chunks.source: The tourism industry faces poaching, poor roads, insecurity and few hotels.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is poaching? A: the illegal killing of wild animals. Poaching is the illegal killing of wild animals in game parks.
chunks.source: Poaching is the illegal killing of wild animals in game parks.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is poaching dangerous to the tourism industry? A: Poaching reduces the wild animals tourists come to see. Poaching is dangerous to tourism because it kills the animals tourists pay to see.
chunks.source: Poaching is dangerous to tourism because it kills the animals tourists pay to see.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mountain gorillas A: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park. Bwindi Impenetrable National Park is famous for mountain gorillas.
chunks.source: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park is famous for mountain gorillas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Ostriches A: Kidepo Valley National Park. Kidepo Valley National Park is famous for ostriches.
chunks.source: Kidepo Valley National Park is famous for ostriches.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Crocodiles A: Murchison Falls National Park. Murchison Falls National Park is famous for crocodiles.
chunks.source: Murchison Falls National Park is famous for crocodiles.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the largest game park in Uganda? A: Murchison Falls National Park. Murchison Falls National Park is the largest game park in Uganda.
chunks.source: Murchison Falls National Park is the largest game park in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is fishing? A: the catching of fish from water bodies. Fishing is the catching of fish from lakes, rivers and ponds.
chunks.source: Fishing is the catching of fish from lakes, rivers and ponds.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write any two problems facing the fishing industry. A: overfishing and water pollution. The fishing industry faces overfishing, water pollution and use of bad fishing methods.
chunks.source: The fishing industry faces overfishing, water pollution and use of bad fishing methods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the biggest and commonest fish in Uganda. A: Nile perch. Nile perch is the biggest and commonest fish in Uganda.
chunks.source: Nile perch is the biggest and commonest fish in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the most common method of preserving fish? A: smoking. Smoking is the most common method of preserving fish in Uganda.
chunks.source: Smoking is the most common method of preserving fish in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we call things that are useful to man and exist on their own? A: natural resources. Things that are useful to man and exist on their own are called natural resources.
chunks.source: Things that are useful to man and exist on their own are called natural resources.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Limestone A: cement. Limestone is used to make cement.
chunks.source: Limestone is used to make cement.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Phosphates A: fertilizers. Phosphates are used to make fertilizers.
chunks.source: Phosphates are used to make fertilizers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Crude oil A: fuel (petrol and diesel). Crude oil is refined into fuel like petrol, diesel and paraffin.
chunks.source: Crude oil is refined into fuel like petrol, diesel and paraffin.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Natural gas A: cooking fuel. Natural gas is used as fuel for cooking and lighting.
chunks.source: Natural gas is used as fuel for cooking and lighting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give three major natural resources in Uganda. A: land, water and minerals. The major natural resources in Uganda are land, water, minerals, vegetation and wildlife.
chunks.source: The major natural resources in Uganda are land, water, minerals, vegetation and wildlife.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the most important natural resources in Uganda? A: land. Land is the most important natural resource in Uganda.
chunks.source: Land is the most important natural resource in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two ways in which man destroys natural resources. A: through deforestation and pollution. Man destroys natural resources through deforestation, poaching and pollution.
chunks.source: Man destroys natural resources through deforestation, poaching and pollution.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List down the two types of natural resources. A: renewable and non-renewable resources. The two types of natural resources are renewable and non-renewable resources.
chunks.source: The two types of natural resources are renewable and non-renewable resources.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is tourism? A: the movement of people from place to place for pleasure. Tourism is the movement of people from one place to another for leisure and enjoyment.
chunks.source: Tourism is the movement of people from one place to another for leisure and enjoyment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is tourism called an industry? A: because it creates jobs and earns income like other industries. Tourism is called an industry because it employs many people and earns the country income.
chunks.source: Tourism is called an industry because it employs many people and earns the country income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List down any four tourist attractions found in Uganda. A: national parks, lakes, mountains and the source of the Nile. Uganda's tourist attractions include national parks, lakes, mountains, the source of the Nile and culture.
chunks.source: Uganda's tourist attractions include national parks, lakes, mountains, the source of the Nile and culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way the problem of water shortage can be solved in Karamoja. A: by building valley dams and drilling boreholes. Water shortage in Karamoja can be solved by building valley dams and drilling boreholes.
chunks.source: Water shortage in Karamoja can be solved by building valley dams and drilling boreholes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which type of rainfall is received around forested areas? A: relief rainfall. Forested highland areas receive relief rainfall when winds are forced to rise over hills.
chunks.source: Forested highland areas receive relief rainfall when winds are forced to rise over hills.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the delicate weather instrument found in a weather station. A: a barometer. A barometer is the delicate weather instrument found in a weather station.
chunks.source: A barometer is the delicate weather instrument found in a weather station.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is wind useful to a farmer? A: Wind is used for winnowing and sailing. Wind is useful to a farmer for winnowing grains and it can also turn windmills.
chunks.source: Wind is useful to a farmer for winnowing grains and it can also turn windmills.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What type of climate covers the largest part of Uganda? A: tropical climate. Tropical climate covers the largest part of Uganda.
chunks.source: Tropical climate covers the largest part of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two factors which affect the climate of Uganda. A: latitude and altitude. The climate of Uganda is affected by latitude, altitude, distance from water bodies and vegetation.
chunks.source: The climate of Uganda is affected by latitude, altitude, distance from water bodies and vegetation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one human activity that improves on the climate of an area. A: planting trees. Planting trees improves the climate of an area because trees help in rain formation.
chunks.source: Planting trees improves the climate of an area because trees help in rain formation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do water bodies improve the climate of an area? A: Water bodies cause evaporation which brings rainfall. Water bodies improve the climate because water evaporates from them and falls back as rain.
chunks.source: Water bodies improve the climate because water evaporates from them and falls back as rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How has drought affected people in most parts of Uganda? A: Drought causes famine and death of animals. Drought has affected people by causing famine, death of animals and water shortage.
chunks.source: Drought has affected people by causing famine, death of animals and water shortage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one way vegetation influences the climate of a given area. A: Vegetation helps in rain formation. Vegetation influences climate because forests help in the formation of rainfall.
chunks.source: Vegetation influences climate because forests help in the formation of rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is weather? A: the daily condition of the atmosphere. Weather is the daily condition of the atmosphere at a given place and time.
chunks.source: Weather is the daily condition of the atmosphere at a given place and time.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two elements of weather. A: temperature and rainfall. Elements of weather include temperature, rainfall, wind, sunshine and humidity.
chunks.source: Elements of weather include temperature, rainfall, wind, sunshine and humidity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one bad effect of weather. A: Floods destroy crops. Bad effects of weather include floods that destroy crops and houses, and drought that causes famine.
chunks.source: Bad effects of weather include floods that destroy crops and houses, and drought that causes famine.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is climate? A: the average weather condition of an area over a long time. Climate is the average weather condition of an area recorded for a long period of time.
chunks.source: Climate is the average weather condition of an area recorded for a long period of time.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which units is rainfall measured? A: millimetres. Rainfall is measured in millimetres using a rain gauge.
chunks.source: Rainfall is measured in millimetres using a rain gauge.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What was the hottest month? A: May. May was the hottest month with 25 degrees Celsius.
chunks.source: May was the hottest month with 25 degrees Celsius.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the wettest month? A: March. March was the wettest month with 250 millimetres of rainfall.
chunks.source: March was the wettest month with 250 millimetres of rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Find the temperature range. A: 5 degrees Celsius. The temperature range is 5 degrees Celsius (25 minus 20).
chunks.source: The temperature range is 5 degrees Celsius (25 minus 20).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How many rainy seasons are shown on the graph? A: two. Two rainy seasons are shown on the graph.
chunks.source: Two rainy seasons are shown on the graph.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do nomadic pastoralists move from one place to another? A: in search of water and pasture for their animals. Nomadic pastoralists move from place to place looking for water and pasture for their cattle.
chunks.source: Nomadic pastoralists move from place to place looking for water and pasture for their cattle.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one problem faced by crop farmers. A: drought. Crop farmers face problems like drought, pests and diseases.
chunks.source: Crop farmers face problems like drought, pests and diseases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can crop farming be made possible in dry areas? A: through irrigation. Crop farming can be made possible in dry areas through irrigation.
chunks.source: Crop farming can be made possible in dry areas through irrigation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What type of farming is practised by most people in Uganda? A: subsistence farming. Most people in Uganda practise subsistence farming.
chunks.source: Most people in Uganda practise subsistence farming.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does climate affect the way people dress? A: People in hot areas wear light clothes and those in cold areas wear heavy clothes. Climate affects dressing because people wear light clothes in hot areas and warm clothes in cold areas.
chunks.source: Climate affects dressing because people wear light clothes in hot areas and warm clothes in cold areas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one factor of climate. A: latitude. Latitude is one factor of climate; others are altitude, vegetation and distance from water bodies.
chunks.source: Latitude is one factor of climate; others are altitude, vegetation and distance from water bodies.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down the four types of climate. A: equatorial, tropical, semi-arid and montane climate. The four types of climate in Uganda are equatorial, tropical, semi-arid and montane climate.
chunks.source: The four types of climate in Uganda are equatorial, tropical, semi-arid and montane climate.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any four factors that influence the climate of an area. A: latitude, altitude, distance from water bodies and vegetation. The climate of an area is influenced by latitude, altitude, distance from water bodies and vegetation.
chunks.source: The climate of an area is influenced by latitude, altitude, distance from water bodies and vegetation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one advantage of growing crops by irrigation. A: Crops can be grown even in the dry season. An advantage of irrigation is that crops can be grown all year round, even without rain.
chunks.source: An advantage of irrigation is that crops can be grown all year round, even without rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Suggest the main economic activity carried out in the semi-arid areas of Uganda. A: nomadic pastoralism. The main economic activity in semi-arid areas of Uganda is nomadic pastoralism (cattle keeping).
chunks.source: The main economic activity in semi-arid areas of Uganda is nomadic pastoralism (cattle keeping).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is the equatorial climate described as hot and wet throughout the year? A: because it is near the equator where the sun is overhead all year. The equatorial climate is hot and wet throughout the year because the area is near the equator with overhead sun and daily convectional rainfall.
chunks.source: The equatorial climate is hot and wet throughout the year because the area is near the equator with overhead sun and daily convectional rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why most parts of Uganda have tropical climate. A: because Uganda lies on a plateau which cools the equatorial heat. Most parts of Uganda have tropical climate because the high plateau modifies the hot equatorial climate.
chunks.source: Most parts of Uganda have tropical climate because the high plateau modifies the hot equatorial climate.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is Mbale cooler than Kampala? A: because Mbale is at a higher altitude than Kampala. Mbale is cooler than Kampala because it is at a higher altitude near Mt. Elgon.
chunks.source: Mbale is cooler than Kampala because it is at a higher altitude near Mt. Elgon.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the two elements of weather shown on the table above. A: temperature and rainfall. The two elements of weather shown on the table are temperature and rainfall.
chunks.source: The two elements of weather shown on the table are temperature and rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which month has the highest rainfall? A: March. March has the highest rainfall of 250 millimetres.
chunks.source: March has the highest rainfall of 250 millimetres.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What was the highest temperature? A: 25 degrees Celsius. The highest temperature was 25 degrees Celsius.
chunks.source: The highest temperature was 25 degrees Celsius.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are natural resources? A: gifts of nature that are useful to man. Natural resources are useful things provided by nature, like land, water and minerals.
chunks.source: Natural resources are useful things provided by nature, like land, water and minerals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are slopes of mountains in Uganda densely populated? A: because of fertile volcanic soils and reliable rainfall. Mountain slopes are densely populated because their soils are fertile and rainfall is good for farming.
chunks.source: Mountain slopes are densely populated because their soils are fertile and rainfall is good for farming.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does limestone promote the construction industry? A: Limestone is used to make cement. Limestone promotes the construction industry because it is used to make cement for building.
chunks.source: Limestone promotes the construction industry because it is used to make cement for building.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is specialization? A: concentrating on what one does best. Specialization means concentrating on the work one does best.
chunks.source: Specialization means concentrating on the work one does best.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a natural resource. A: land. Land is an example of a natural resource.
chunks.source: Land is an example of a natural resource.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is land regarded as a major resource? A: because it is used for farming, settlement and many other activities. Land is a major resource because we farm on it, build on it and get minerals from it.
chunks.source: Land is a major resource because we farm on it, build on it and get minerals from it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any two minerals for making artificial fertilizers i) ii) A: phosphates and potash. Phosphates and potash are minerals used to make artificial fertilizers.
chunks.source: Phosphates and potash are minerals used to make artificial fertilizers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which Ministry in Uganda is responsible for protecting natural resources? A: the Ministry of Water and Environment. The Ministry of Water and Environment is responsible for protecting natural resources in Uganda.
chunks.source: The Ministry of Water and Environment is responsible for protecting natural resources in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Suggest any two ways in which NEMA can protect our environment. i) ii) A: by planting trees and enforcing laws against pollution. NEMA can protect the environment by planting trees and punishing people who pollute.
chunks.source: NEMA can protect the environment by planting trees and punishing people who pollute.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is there a cement industry in Tororo? A: because there are limestone deposits in Tororo. There is a cement industry in Tororo because limestone, used to make cement, is found there.
chunks.source: There is a cement industry in Tororo because limestone, used to make cement, is found there.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is wind called a resource? A: because it is a free gift of nature that is useful to man. Wind is called a resource because it is a free gift of nature used to generate electricity and for sailing.
chunks.source: Wind is called a resource because it is a free gift of nature used to generate electricity and for sailing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one human activity that can lead to land degradation. A: deforestation. Deforestation, overgrazing and poor farming can lead to land degradation.
chunks.source: Deforestation, overgrazing and poor farming can lead to land degradation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down one importance of human labour. A: Human labour provides the workforce that does all work. Human labour is important because people do all the work in farms, factories and offices.
chunks.source: Human labour is important because people do all the work in farms, factories and offices.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which traditional rulers are important to Uganda. A: They promote culture and unite people. Traditional rulers are important because they promote culture and unite their people.
chunks.source: Traditional rulers are important because they promote culture and unite their people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which discovery helped early man to live in caves? A: the discovery of fire. The discovery of fire helped early man to live in caves because fire gave warmth and kept away wild animals.
chunks.source: The discovery of fire helped early man to live in caves because fire gave warmth and kept away wild animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why some Bantu tribes were able to form kingdoms. A: because they had strong leaders and lived in unity. Some Bantu tribes formed kingdoms because they had strong leaders and lived in unity.
chunks.source: Some Bantu tribes formed kingdoms because they had strong leaders and lived in unity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why should children be taught legends? A: to preserve history and learn morals. Children should be taught legends to preserve the history of their people and learn good morals.
chunks.source: Children should be taught legends to preserve the history of their people and learn good morals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why should family members work together? A: so that they develop faster. Family members should work together so that work is done faster and the family develops.
chunks.source: Family members should work together so that work is done faster and the family develops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are the Baganda similar to Bakiga in terms of ethnicity? A: Both are Bantu. The Baganda are similar to the Bakiga because both belong to the Bantu ethnic group.
chunks.source: The Baganda are similar to the Bakiga because both belong to the Bantu ethnic group.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one symbol of a clan. A: a totem. A totem is one symbol of a clan.
chunks.source: A totem is one symbol of a clan.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are names important to children? A: Names give children identity. Names are important to children because they give them identity and show which clan they belong to.
chunks.source: Names are important to children because they give them identity and show which clan they belong to.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are cultural practices important in our community? A: Cultural practices unite people. Cultural practices are important because they unite people and preserve their identity.
chunks.source: Cultural practices are important because they unite people and preserve their identity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one role of a clan head / leader. A: The clan head settles disputes. A clan head settles disputes among clan members and keeps clan culture.
chunks.source: A clan head settles disputes among clan members and keeps clan culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are cultural leaders important in our country? A: Cultural leaders promote culture and settle disputes. Cultural leaders are important because they promote culture and settle disputes among their people.
chunks.source: Cultural leaders are important because they promote culture and settle disputes among their people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are social activities? A: activities that people do together in a community. Social activities are activities people do together, like games, dances and ceremonies.
chunks.source: Social activities are activities people do together, like games, dances and ceremonies.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of social activities. A: football and traditional dances. Examples of social activities are football, traditional dances and weddings.
chunks.source: Examples of social activities are football, traditional dances and weddings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are social activities useful in our community? A: They promote unity and cooperation. Social activities are useful because they promote unity, cooperation and friendship in the community.
chunks.source: Social activities are useful because they promote unity, cooperation and friendship in the community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one economic contribution of the Bachwezi in Uganda. A: They introduced long-horned cattle. An economic contribution of the Bachwezi was introducing long-horned cattle in Uganda.
chunks.source: An economic contribution of the Bachwezi was introducing long-horned cattle in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is it good for children to attend cultural ceremonies? A: so that they learn their culture. It is good for children to attend cultural ceremonies so that they learn their culture.
chunks.source: It is good for children to attend cultural ceremonies so that they learn their culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do most people prefer having a nuclear family today? A: because it is cheaper to care for a small family. Most people prefer a nuclear family today because it is cheaper and easier to care for.
chunks.source: Most people prefer a nuclear family today because it is cheaper and easier to care for.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did early man get his food? A: through hunting and gathering. Early man got his food through hunting wild animals and gathering fruits.
chunks.source: Early man got his food through hunting wild animals and gathering fruits.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one symbol of a clan. A: a totem. A totem, like an animal or object, is a symbol of a clan.
chunks.source: A totem, like an animal or object, is a symbol of a clan.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one kingdom in Uganda today. A: Buganda. Buganda is one kingdom in Uganda today.
chunks.source: Buganda is one kingdom in Uganda today.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two importance of kingdoms in Uganda. A: Kingdoms promote culture and attract tourists. Kingdoms are important because they promote culture and attract tourists.
chunks.source: Kingdoms are important because they promote culture and attract tourists.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do kingdoms get their new leaders? A: through hereditary (kings inherit the throne). Kingdoms get new leaders through hereditary, where the son inherits from the father.
chunks.source: Kingdoms get new leaders through hereditary, where the son inherits from the father.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is culture? A: the way of life of people. Culture is the way of life of people, including their language, food, dress and customs.
chunks.source: Culture is the way of life of people, including their language, food, dress and customs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two examples of culture. A: language and traditional dances. Examples of culture are language, traditional dances, dress and food.
chunks.source: Examples of culture are language, traditional dances, dress and food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important to preserve our culture? A: to keep our identity. It is important to preserve our culture to keep our identity and unity.
chunks.source: It is important to preserve our culture to keep our identity and unity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How useful are social activities to our community? A: They promote unity in the community. Social activities are useful because they bring people together and promote unity.
chunks.source: Social activities are useful because they bring people together and promote unity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are kingdoms useful to our country today? A: Kingdoms promote culture and tourism. Kingdoms are useful to our country because they preserve culture and attract tourists who bring income.
chunks.source: Kingdoms are useful to our country because they preserve culture and attract tourists who bring income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one lesson we learn from the legend of Gipiir and Labong. A: Disunity brings suffering. The lesson from the legend of Gipiir and Labong is that disunity brings suffering, so people should live in peace.
chunks.source: The lesson from the legend of Gipiir and Labong is that disunity brings suffering, so people should live in peace.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is an ethic group? A: a group of people with the same origin, language and culture. An ethnic group is a group of people who share the same origin, language and culture.
chunks.source: An ethnic group is a group of people who share the same origin, language and culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one common characteristics of ethnic groups. A: They speak the same language. A common characteristic of ethnic groups is that members speak the same language and share the same culture.
chunks.source: A common characteristic of ethnic groups is that members speak the same language and share the same culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two reasons why ethnic groups migrate from their original homeland. A: They fled wars and searched for fertile land. Ethnic groups migrated from their homeland because of wars, drought and the search for fertile land and pasture.
chunks.source: Ethnic groups migrated from their homeland because of wars, drought and the search for fertile land and pasture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How has the Uganda Museum promoted the economic development in Uganda? A: by attracting tourists. The Uganda Museum has promoted economic development by attracting tourists who bring income.
chunks.source: The Uganda Museum has promoted economic development by attracting tourists who bring income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a family? A: a group of people related by blood, marriage or adoption. A family is a group of people related by blood, marriage or adoption living together.
chunks.source: A family is a group of people related by blood, marriage or adoption living together.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important to be a member of a family? A: to get love, care and support. It is important to be a member of a family to get love, care and support.
chunks.source: It is important to be a member of a family to get love, care and support.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way people become members of their families. A: through birth, marriage or adoption. People become members of families through birth, marriage or adoption.
chunks.source: People become members of families through birth, marriage or adoption.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do some families carry out farming? A: to get food and income. Some families carry out farming to get food and earn income.
chunks.source: Some families carry out farming to get food and earn income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What lesson do you learn from the story of Gipiir and Labong? A: People should live in peace and unity. The lesson from Gipiir and Labong is that people should avoid division and live in peace.
chunks.source: The lesson from Gipiir and Labong is that people should avoid division and live in peace.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the meaning of Stone Age sites. A: places where remains of early man like stone tools were found. Stone Age sites are places where remains of early man, such as stone tools, were discovered.
chunks.source: Stone Age sites are places where remains of early man, such as stone tools, were discovered.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is Pubungu remembered in the history of Uganda? A: Pubungu was the entry point of the Luo into Uganda. Pubungu is remembered because it was where the Luo entered Uganda during their migration.
chunks.source: Pubungu is remembered because it was where the Luo entered Uganda during their migration.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two problems faced by people living in urban areas. A: overcrowding and unemployment. People in urban areas face problems like overcrowding, unemployment and high crime.
chunks.source: People in urban areas face problems like overcrowding, unemployment and high crime.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How were the Bantu politically organised? A: in kingdoms and chiefdoms. The Bantu were politically organised in kingdoms and chiefdoms under kings and chiefs.
chunks.source: The Bantu were politically organised in kingdoms and chiefdoms under kings and chiefs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did the size of Bunyoro Kitara Empire contribute to its collapse? A: It was too large to be controlled. The size of Bunyoro Kitara Empire contributed to its collapse because it was too large for the king to control.
chunks.source: The size of Bunyoro Kitara Empire contributed to its collapse because it was too large for the king to control.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define a norm. A: an accepted behaviour in a community. A norm is an accepted way of behaving in a community.
chunks.source: A norm is an accepted way of behaving in a community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define barter trade. A: the exchange of goods for goods. Barter trade is the exchange of goods for other goods without using money.
chunks.source: Barter trade is the exchange of goods for other goods without using money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why did the people of pre- colonial times use barter trade? A: because there was no money. People of pre-colonial times used barter trade because money had not yet been introduced.
chunks.source: People of pre-colonial times used barter trade because money had not yet been introduced.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is culture important in our community? A: Culture unites people. Culture is important in our community because it unites people and gives them identity.
chunks.source: Culture is important in our community because it unites people and gives them identity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why didn’t the Karimojong form a kingdom? A: because they were nomads without central leadership. The Karimojong did not form a kingdom because they were nomadic pastoralists without a central leader.
chunks.source: The Karimojong did not form a kingdom because they were nomadic pastoralists without a central leader.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do Ugandans benefit from the establishment of a Museum? A: They learn history and it attracts tourists. Ugandans benefit from a museum because they learn their history and tourists bring income.
chunks.source: Ugandans benefit from a museum because they learn their history and tourists bring income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is Africa regarded as a cradle land of man? A: because the earliest remains of man were found in Africa. Africa is regarded as the cradle land of man because the oldest remains of early man were found here.
chunks.source: Africa is regarded as the cradle land of man because the oldest remains of early man were found here.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one source of history. A: oral traditions. Oral traditions, fossils and written records are sources of history.
chunks.source: Oral traditions, fossils and written records are sources of history.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one economic importance of Stone Age sites to the people around them. A: They attract tourists who bring income. Stone Age sites are economically important because they attract tourists.
chunks.source: Stone Age sites are economically important because they attract tourists.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two ways early man obtained food. A: by hunting and gathering. Early man obtained food by hunting wild animals and gathering wild fruits.
chunks.source: Early man obtained food by hunting wild animals and gathering wild fruits.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did farming help early man to live a settled life? A: Farming gave constant food so man stopped moving. Farming helped early man live a settled life because it provided a steady supply of food.
chunks.source: Farming helped early man live a settled life because it provided a steady supply of food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define an ethnic group. A: a group of people with the same origin, language and culture. An ethnic group is a group of people sharing the same origin, language and culture.
chunks.source: An ethnic group is a group of people sharing the same origin, language and culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two causes of the Bantu migration to Uganda. A: search for fertile land and fleeing wars. The Bantu migrated to Uganda in search of fertile land and to flee wars and drought.
chunks.source: The Bantu migrated to Uganda in search of fertile land and to flee wars and drought.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way the Christian Missionaries promoted agriculture in Uganda. A: They introduced new crops like cotton. The Christian missionaries promoted agriculture by introducing new crops such as cotton and teaching better farming methods.
chunks.source: The Christian missionaries promoted agriculture by introducing new crops such as cotton and teaching better farming methods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why did the Arabs practise slave trade? A: They needed labour for their plantations and it was profitable. The Arabs practised slave trade because they needed slaves to work on plantations and selling slaves earned them a lot of money.
chunks.source: The Arabs practised slave trade because they needed slaves to work on plantations and selling slaves earned them a lot of money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a nation? A: a group of people living in a defined area under one government. A nation is a group of people living together in a defined area under one government.
chunks.source: A nation is a group of people living together in a defined area under one government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which people helped to form Uganda as a nation? A: The British colonialists and Ugandan traditional leaders. The British colonialists together with Ugandan traditional leaders helped to form Uganda as a nation.
chunks.source: The British colonialists together with Ugandan traditional leaders helped to form Uganda as a nation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did Dr. Albert Cook help in improving on the health services in Uganda? A: He built Mengo Hospital. Dr. Albert Cook helped improve health services by building Mengo Hospital in 1901.
chunks.source: Dr. Albert Cook helped improve health services by building Mengo Hospital in 1901.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did Kenneth Borup contribute to the economic development of Uganda? A: He introduced cotton growing in Uganda. Kenneth Borup contributed to economic development by introducing cotton growing in Uganda.
chunks.source: Kenneth Borup contributed to economic development by introducing cotton growing in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why King Muteesa I invited missionaries to Buganda. A: He wanted guns and to learn reading and writing. King Muteesa I invited missionaries because he wanted guns for protection and to learn reading and writing.
chunks.source: King Muteesa I invited missionaries because he wanted guns for protection and to learn reading and writing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why did the Arabs come to Uganda? A: to trade. The Arabs came to Uganda to trade.
chunks.source: The Arabs came to Uganda to trade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two items brought by the Arabs to Uganda. A: cloth and guns. The Arabs brought cloth, guns, beads and mirrors to Uganda.
chunks.source: The Arabs brought cloth, guns, beads and mirrors to Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is the crested crane drawn while standing on one leg? A: to show that Uganda is moving forward. The crested crane is drawn standing on one leg to show that Uganda is moving forward.
chunks.source: The crested crane is drawn standing on one leg to show that Uganda is moving forward.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why did the colonialists introduce cash crop growing? A: to get raw materials for their industries. The colonialists introduced cash crop growing to get raw materials for British industries.
chunks.source: The colonialists introduced cash crop growing to get raw materials for British industries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which body in Uganda works like the legislative council during colonial rule? A: Parliament. Parliament works like the legislative council did during colonial rule.
chunks.source: Parliament works like the legislative council did during colonial rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did the coming of the Arabs promote trade in Uganda? A: They introduced new trade goods and expanded trade. The coming of the Arabs promoted trade because they brought new goods like cloth and guns and opened new trade routes.
chunks.source: The coming of the Arabs promoted trade because they brought new goods like cloth and guns and opened new trade routes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one way missionaries promoted education in Uganda. A: They built schools. Missionaries promoted education by building schools where Ugandans learnt reading and writing.
chunks.source: Missionaries promoted education by building schools where Ugandans learnt reading and writing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why did the British decide to give the lost counties of Buyaga and Bugangayizi to Buganda? A: as a reward for Buganda's help against Bunyoro. The British gave the lost counties of Buyaga and Bugangayizi to Buganda as a reward for helping them defeat Bunyoro.
chunks.source: The British gave the lost counties of Buyaga and Bugangayizi to Buganda as a reward for helping them defeat Bunyoro.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: When is the Uganda flag flown at half-mast? A: during national mourning. The Uganda flag is flown at half-mast when the nation is mourning a dead hero or leader.
chunks.source: The Uganda flag is flown at half-mast when the nation is mourning a dead hero or leader.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is George Kakoma remembered in the history of Uganda? A: He composed the Uganda national anthem. George Kakoma is remembered because he composed the Uganda national anthem.
chunks.source: George Kakoma is remembered because he composed the Uganda national anthem.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is English used as an official language in Uganda? A: because of British colonial rule. English is used as an official language in Uganda because of British colonial rule and it unites people of different tribes.
chunks.source: English is used as an official language in Uganda because of British colonial rule and it unites people of different tribes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a nation? A: a group of people living in a defined area under one government. A nation is a country of people living together in a defined area under one government.
chunks.source: A nation is a country of people living together in a defined area under one government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention two symbols of Uganda as a nation. A: the national flag and the national anthem. Two symbols of Uganda as a nation are the national flag and the national anthem.
chunks.source: Two symbols of Uganda as a nation are the national flag and the national anthem.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which type of nation is Uganda? A: an independent republic. Uganda is an independent republic.
chunks.source: Uganda is an independent republic.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match each British colonial leader to what he is remembered for. A: Sir Walter Coutts: The last British Governor of Uganda.; Sir Hesketh Bell: Promoted higher education in Uganda.; Sir Philip Mitchell: The first British governor of Uganda.; Sir Andrew Cohen: Exiled Mutesa II.. Sir Walter Coutts was the last British governor, Sir Hesketh Bell promoted higher education, Sir Philip Mitchell was the first British governor, and Sir Andrew Cohen exiled Mutesa II.
chunks.source: Sir Walter Coutts was the last British governor, Sir Hesketh Bell promoted higher education, Sir Philip Mitchell was the first British governor, and Sir Andrew Cohen exiled Mutesa II.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is indirect rule as used by the British in Uganda? A: ruling through local leaders. Indirect rule was the British system of ruling Uganda through local kings and chiefs.
chunks.source: Indirect rule was the British system of ruling Uganda through local kings and chiefs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two reasons why the British used indirect rule. A: It was cheap and it avoided resistance. The British used indirect rule because it was cheap and it reduced resistance from Africans.
chunks.source: The British used indirect rule because it was cheap and it reduced resistance from Africans.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did the Africans benefit from indirect rule? A: Africans kept their leaders and got jobs and education. Africans benefited from indirect rule because they kept their own leaders and got jobs and education.
chunks.source: Africans benefited from indirect rule because they kept their own leaders and got jobs and education.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why did Ugandans form political parties in early 1950s? A: to demand independence. Ugandans formed political parties in the early 1950s to demand independence from Britain.
chunks.source: Ugandans formed political parties in the early 1950s to demand independence from Britain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for Uganda cranes going for a football match in Egypt to carry the national flag? A: to show that they represent Uganda. It is important for the Uganda Cranes to carry the national flag so that people know they represent Uganda.
chunks.source: It is important for the Uganda Cranes to carry the national flag so that people know they represent Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the bird in the middle of the Uganda national flag? A: the crested crane. The bird in the middle of the Uganda national flag is the crested crane.
chunks.source: The bird in the middle of the Uganda national flag is the crested crane.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does black symbolize on the Uganda national flag? A: the African people. Black on the Uganda flag symbolizes the African people.
chunks.source: Black on the Uganda flag symbolizes the African people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does yellow symbolize on the Uganda national flag? A: sunshine. Yellow on the Uganda flag symbolizes sunshine.
chunks.source: Yellow on the Uganda flag symbolizes sunshine.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does red symbolize on the Uganda national flag? A: African brotherhood. Red on the Uganda flag symbolizes African brotherhood.
chunks.source: Red on the Uganda flag symbolizes African brotherhood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who raised the national flag for the first time in Uganda? A: Major Kanuti Akorimo. Major Kanuti Akorimo raised the national flag for the first time in Uganda on 9th October 1962.
chunks.source: Major Kanuti Akorimo raised the national flag for the first time in Uganda on 9th October 1962.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which flag in Uganda was lowered on 9th Oct 1962? A: the Union Jack. The Union Jack, the British flag, was lowered on 9th October 1962.
chunks.source: The Union Jack, the British flag, was lowered on 9th October 1962.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who declared Uganda a British protectorate? A: Sir Gerald Portal. Sir Gerald Portal declared Uganda a British protectorate in 1894.
chunks.source: Sir Gerald Portal declared Uganda a British protectorate in 1894.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which year was Uganda declared a British protectorate? A: 1894. Uganda was declared a British protectorate in 1894.
chunks.source: Uganda was declared a British protectorate in 1894.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is the Uganda flag sometimes flown at half – mast? A: when the nation is mourning. The Uganda flag is flown at half-mast when the nation is mourning a great leader or hero.
chunks.source: The Uganda flag is flown at half-mast when the nation is mourning a great leader or hero.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why does Uganda use English as her official language? A: because of colonial rule and to unite different tribes. Uganda uses English as the official language because of British colonial rule and because it unites many tribes.
chunks.source: Uganda uses English as the official language because of British colonial rule and because it unites many tribes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the national language for Kenya and Tanzania? A: Kiswahili. Kiswahili is the national language for Kenya and Tanzania.
chunks.source: Kiswahili is the national language for Kenya and Tanzania.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define trade. A: the buying and selling of goods. Trade is the buying and selling of goods and services.
chunks.source: Trade is the buying and selling of goods and services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What was the major reason for the coming of missionaries to Uganda? A: to spread Christianity. The major reason for the coming of missionaries to Uganda was to spread Christianity.
chunks.source: The major reason for the coming of missionaries to Uganda was to spread Christianity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did Kenneth Borup contribute to economic development of Uganda? A: He introduced cotton growing in Uganda. Kenneth Borup contributed to economic development by introducing cotton growing in Uganda.
chunks.source: Kenneth Borup contributed to economic development by introducing cotton growing in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why was Bishop Hannington killed in Busoga? A: on the orders of Kabaka Mwanga. Bishop Hannington was killed in Busoga on the orders of Kabaka Mwanga, who feared Europeans.
chunks.source: Bishop Hannington was killed in Busoga on the orders of Kabaka Mwanga, who feared Europeans.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How helpful was Captain Lugard to the Kingdom of Toro? A: He helped to restore the Toro kingdom. Captain Lugard was helpful to Toro because he helped restore the Toro kingdom under Kasagama.
chunks.source: Captain Lugard was helpful to Toro because he helped restore the Toro kingdom under Kasagama.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the political event that took place in Uganda in 1894. A: Uganda was declared a British protectorate. The political event that took place in Uganda in 1894 was the declaration of the British protectorate.
chunks.source: The political event that took place in Uganda in 1894 was the declaration of the British protectorate.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write IBEACO in full. A: Imperial British East Africa Company. IBEACO stands for Imperial British East Africa Company.
chunks.source: IBEACO stands for Imperial British East Africa Company.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State the major reason why IBEACO withdrew its activities from Uganda. A: because it went bankrupt. IBEACO withdrew its activities from Uganda because it went bankrupt and lacked money.
chunks.source: IBEACO withdrew its activities from Uganda because it went bankrupt and lacked money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State the reason why Egypt wanted to colonise Uganda. A: to control the source of the River Nile. Egypt wanted to colonise Uganda in order to control the source of the River Nile.
chunks.source: Egypt wanted to colonise Uganda in order to control the source of the River Nile.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why many poachers hunt elephants in game parks. A: to get ivory. Many poachers hunt elephants in game parks to get ivory from their tusks.
chunks.source: Many poachers hunt elephants in game parks to get ivory from their tusks.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How were dhows useful to early Arab traders? A: Dhows carried their goods across the Indian Ocean. Dhows were useful to early Arab traders because they carried trade goods across the Indian Ocean.
chunks.source: Dhows were useful to early Arab traders because they carried trade goods across the Indian Ocean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who were the first group of foreigners to come to Uganda? A: the Arabs. The Arabs were the first group of foreigners to come to Uganda.
chunks.source: The Arabs were the first group of foreigners to come to Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State the reason why it was difficult to stop slave trade in Uganda. A: because Africans collaborated with the Arabs and it was profitable. It was difficult to stop slave trade because some Africans helped the Arabs and selling slaves was very profitable.
chunks.source: It was difficult to stop slave trade because some Africans helped the Arabs and selling slaves was very profitable.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How was R. Nile responsible for the coming of European explorers? A: because they wanted to find its source. The River Nile was responsible for the coming of European explorers because they wanted to find its source.
chunks.source: The River Nile was responsible for the coming of European explorers because they wanted to find its source.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why did HM Stanley circumnavigate L. Victoria? A: to prove that Lake Victoria was the source of the Nile. H.M. Stanley circumnavigated Lake Victoria to prove that it was the source of the River Nile.
chunks.source: H.M. Stanley circumnavigated Lake Victoria to prove that it was the source of the River Nile.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two reasons why Kabaka Muteesa I invited Missionaries. A: He wanted guns and education. Kabaka Muteesa I invited missionaries because he wanted guns for protection and to learn reading and writing.
chunks.source: Kabaka Muteesa I invited missionaries because he wanted guns for protection and to learn reading and writing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How was the Royal Geographical Society important in the coming of explorers to Uganda? A: It sponsored and funded the explorers. The Royal Geographical Society was important because it sponsored and paid for the explorers' journeys.
chunks.source: The Royal Geographical Society was important because it sponsored and paid for the explorers' journeys.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a nation? A: a group of people living in a defined area under one government. A nation is a group of people living together in a defined area under one government.
chunks.source: A nation is a group of people living together in a defined area under one government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two reasons why the British used indirect rule in Uganda. A: It was cheap and it avoided resistance. The British used indirect rule because it was cheap to run and it reduced African resistance.
chunks.source: The British used indirect rule because it was cheap to run and it reduced African resistance.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How were Omukama Kabalega and Kabaka Mwanga similar in terms of their reaction towards the British rule? A: Both resisted British rule. Omukama Kabalega and Kabaka Mwanga were similar because both resisted British colonial rule.
chunks.source: Omukama Kabalega and Kabaka Mwanga were similar because both resisted British colonial rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why was the IBEACO sent to Uganda? A: to trade and administer the area. The IBEACO was sent to Uganda to carry out trade and administer the territory.
chunks.source: The IBEACO was sent to Uganda to carry out trade and administer the territory.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why was Uganda called a protectorate? A: because Britain protected and controlled Uganda. Uganda was called a protectorate because Britain protected and controlled it without fully colonising it.
chunks.source: Uganda was called a protectorate because Britain protected and controlled it without fully colonising it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What was the major cause of Lamogi rebellion in Acholi land? A: the British attempt to disarm the Acholi. The major cause of the Lamogi rebellion was the British attempt to disarm the Acholi people.
chunks.source: The major cause of the Lamogi rebellion was the British attempt to disarm the Acholi people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write LEGCO in full. A: Legislative Council. LEGCO stands for Legislative Council.
chunks.source: LEGCO stands for Legislative Council.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did the first Ugandans join LEGCO A: They were nominated (appointed) by the governor. The first Ugandans joined LEGCO through nomination by the British governor.
chunks.source: The first Ugandans joined LEGCO through nomination by the British governor.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why was it difficult for the British to capture the North Eastern part of Uganda? A: because the Karimojong were fierce and the area was dry with little wealth. It was difficult for the British to capture North Eastern Uganda because the Karimojong fiercely resisted and the dry area had little economic value.
chunks.source: It was difficult for the British to capture North Eastern Uganda because the Karimojong fiercely resisted and the dry area had little economic value.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did Semei Kakungulu extend the British rule in Eastern Uganda? A: by defeating local chiefs and bringing them under British rule. Semei Kakungulu extended British rule in Eastern Uganda by defeating and subduing local chiefs.
chunks.source: Semei Kakungulu extended British rule in Eastern Uganda by defeating and subduing local chiefs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why the British signed the 1900 Buganda Agreement. A: to establish British control over Buganda. The British signed the 1900 Buganda Agreement to establish their control over Buganda.
chunks.source: The British signed the 1900 Buganda Agreement to establish their control over Buganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who was the father to King Daudi Chwa II? A: Kabaka Mwanga II. Kabaka Mwanga II was the father of King Daudi Chwa II.
chunks.source: Kabaka Mwanga II was the father of King Daudi Chwa II.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the British official who signed the 1900 Buganda Agreement on behalf of the British government. A: Sir Harry Johnston. Sir Harry Johnston signed the 1900 Buganda Agreement on behalf of the British government.
chunks.source: Sir Harry Johnston signed the 1900 Buganda Agreement on behalf of the British government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which method of administration was mostly used in Uganda by the colonialists? A: indirect rule. Indirect rule was the method of administration mostly used by the colonialists in Uganda.
chunks.source: Indirect rule was the method of administration mostly used by the colonialists in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did sir Hesketh Bell contribute to the economic development of Uganda? A: He encouraged the growing of cash crops. Sir Hesketh Bell contributed to economic development by encouraging Ugandans to grow cash crops.
chunks.source: Sir Hesketh Bell contributed to economic development by encouraging Ugandans to grow cash crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two reasons why the British introduced cash crops in Uganda. A: to get raw materials and raise tax revenue. The British introduced cash crops to get raw materials for their industries and to raise tax money.
chunks.source: The British introduced cash crops to get raw materials for their industries and to raise tax money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you understand by the term independence? A: freedom from colonial rule (self-rule). Independence means freedom from colonial rule, when a country rules itself.
chunks.source: Independence means freedom from colonial rule, when a country rules itself.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What title was given to the leader of government between 1962 – 1966? A: Prime Minister. The leader of government between 1962 and 1966 was called the Prime Minister.
chunks.source: The leader of government between 1962 and 1966 was called the Prime Minister.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who was the first vice president of Uganda? A: William Nadiope. William Nadiope was the first vice president of Uganda.
chunks.source: William Nadiope was the first vice president of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did the 1967 constitution affect the kingdoms in Uganda? A: It abolished the kingdoms. The 1967 constitution abolished the kingdoms in Uganda.
chunks.source: The 1967 constitution abolished the kingdoms in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who became the first executive president of Uganda? A: Milton Obote. Milton Obote became the first executive president of Uganda.
chunks.source: Milton Obote became the first executive president of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which year was Uganda declared a republic? A: 1967. Uganda was declared a republic in 1967.
chunks.source: Uganda was declared a republic in 1967.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: To which country was Kabaka Mutesa II exiled during the 1966 Buganda crisis? A: Britain. Kabaka Mutesa II was exiled to Britain during the 1966 Buganda crisis.
chunks.source: Kabaka Mutesa II was exiled to Britain during the 1966 Buganda crisis.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write UPDF in full A: Uganda People's Defence Force. UPDF stands for Uganda People's Defence Force.
chunks.source: UPDF stands for Uganda People's Defence Force.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention the two political parties that made an alliance to win the 1962 general elections? A: UPC and Kabaka Yekka (KY). UPC and Kabaka Yekka made an alliance to win the 1962 general elections.
chunks.source: UPC and Kabaka Yekka made an alliance to win the 1962 general elections.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the president of Uganda who brought back the dead body of Edward Mutesa II from Britain? A: Idi Amin. Idi Amin brought back the dead body of Edward Mutesa II from Britain.
chunks.source: Idi Amin brought back the dead body of Edward Mutesa II from Britain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where was Kabaka Edward Mutesa II buried? A: at Kasubi tombs. Kabaka Edward Mutesa II was buried at Kasubi tombs.
chunks.source: Kabaka Edward Mutesa II was buried at Kasubi tombs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two characteristics of a nation. A: It has defined boundaries and its own government. Characteristics of a nation are defined boundaries, a government, a population and sovereignty.
chunks.source: Characteristics of a nation are defined boundaries, a government, a population and sovereignty.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the president of Uganda who took over power through a military coup? A: Idi Amin. Idi Amin took over power through a military coup in 1971.
chunks.source: Idi Amin took over power through a military coup in 1971.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which president of Uganda exiled Asians from Uganda? A: Idi Amin. Idi Amin exiled Asians from Uganda in 1972.
chunks.source: Idi Amin exiled Asians from Uganda in 1972.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write UNLF in full A: Uganda National Liberation Front. UNLF stands for Uganda National Liberation Front.
chunks.source: UNLF stands for Uganda National Liberation Front.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which president of Uganda ruled for the shortest period of time? A: Yusuf Lule. Yusuf Lule ruled for the shortest period of time (68 days).
chunks.source: Yusuf Lule ruled for the shortest period of time (68 days).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the president of Uganda who has ruled for the longest period of time? A: Yoweri Kaguta Museveni. Yoweri Kaguta Museveni has ruled Uganda for the longest period of time.
chunks.source: Yoweri Kaguta Museveni has ruled Uganda for the longest period of time.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do Ugandans remember on the 26th January every year? A: the NRM Liberation Day. On 26th January Ugandans remember the NRM Liberation Day.
chunks.source: On 26th January Ugandans remember the NRM Liberation Day.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which political party took over government in 1986? A: the National Resistance Movement (NRM). The National Resistance Movement took over government in 1986.
chunks.source: The National Resistance Movement took over government in 1986.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write IGG in full. A: Inspector General of Government. IGG stands for Inspector General of Government.
chunks.source: IGG stands for Inspector General of Government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why was IGG’s office formed? A: to fight corruption. The IGG's office was formed to fight corruption in Uganda.
chunks.source: The IGG's office was formed to fight corruption in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two private universities in Uganda? A: Kampala International University and Uganda Christian University. Private universities in Uganda include Kampala International University and Uganda Christian University.
chunks.source: Private universities in Uganda include Kampala International University and Uganda Christian University.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two reasons why Uganda should be recognized as an independent nation. A: It has its own flag, anthem and government. Uganda should be recognized as independent because it has its own flag, anthem, government and constitution.
chunks.source: Uganda should be recognized as independent because it has its own flag, anthem, government and constitution.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any two government universities in Uganda. A: Makerere University and Kyambogo University. Government universities in Uganda include Makerere University and Kyambogo University.
chunks.source: Government universities in Uganda include Makerere University and Kyambogo University.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write UPE in full. A: Universal Primary Education. UPE stands for Universal Primary Education.
chunks.source: UPE stands for Universal Primary Education.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write USE in full. A: Universal Secondary Education. USE stands for Universal Secondary Education.
chunks.source: USE stands for Universal Secondary Education.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write AGOA in full. A: African Growth and Opportunity Act. AGOA stands for African Growth and Opportunity Act.
chunks.source: AGOA stands for African Growth and Opportunity Act.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the president who was over thrown by Y. K Museveni. A: Tito Okello. Tito Okello was the president overthrown by Y.K. Museveni.
chunks.source: Tito Okello was the president overthrown by Y.K. Museveni.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which political party in Uganda won the general elections of 1962? A: the Uganda People's Congress (UPC). The Uganda People's Congress won the general elections of 1962 (in alliance with KY).
chunks.source: The Uganda People's Congress won the general elections of 1962 (in alliance with KY).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write the day and the year Uganda attained her independence. A: 9th October 1962. Uganda attained her independence on 9th October 1962.
chunks.source: Uganda attained her independence on 9th October 1962.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who was the first chief minister of Uganda? A: Benedicto Kiwanuka. Benedicto Kiwanuka was the first chief minister of Uganda.
chunks.source: Benedicto Kiwanuka was the first chief minister of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who was the first prime minister of Uganda? A: Milton Obote. Milton Obote was the first prime minister of Uganda.
chunks.source: Milton Obote was the first prime minister of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who was the first president of Uganda? A: Sir Edward Mutesa II. Sir Edward Mutesa II was the first president of Uganda.
chunks.source: Sir Edward Mutesa II was the first president of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What caused the 1966 Buganda crisis? A: the power struggle between Obote and Mutesa II. The 1966 Buganda crisis was caused by the power struggle between Obote and Kabaka Mutesa II, ending with the army attacking the palace.
chunks.source: The 1966 Buganda crisis was caused by the power struggle between Obote and Kabaka Mutesa II, ending with the army attacking the palace.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any three attributes of Uganda as a nation? A: the national flag, the national anthem and the coat of arms. Three attributes of Uganda as a nation are the national flag, the national anthem and the coat of arms.
chunks.source: Three attributes of Uganda as a nation are the national flag, the national anthem and the coat of arms.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which country in Africa is known as the pearl of Africa? A: Uganda. Uganda is the country in Africa known as the pearl of Africa.
chunks.source: Uganda is the country in Africa known as the pearl of Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the British prime minister who referred to Uganda as the pearl of Africa? A: Winston Churchill. Winston Churchill, the British prime minister, referred to Uganda as the pearl of Africa.
chunks.source: Winston Churchill, the British prime minister, referred to Uganda as the pearl of Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How many stanzas does the Uganda national anthem have? A: three. The Uganda national anthem has three stanzas.
chunks.source: The Uganda national anthem has three stanzas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down the first line of the second stanza of the Uganda national anthem. A: Oh Uganda! the land of freedom.. The first line of the second stanza of the Uganda national anthem is 'Oh Uganda! the land of freedom.'
chunks.source: The first line of the second stanza of the Uganda national anthem is 'Oh Uganda! the land of freedom.'

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who designed the Uganda national flag? A: Grace Ibingira. Grace Ibingira designed the Uganda national flag.
chunks.source: Grace Ibingira designed the Uganda national flag.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one sentence about GW Kakoma. A: George William Kakoma composed the Uganda national anthem.. George William Kakoma composed Uganda's national anthem in 1962.
chunks.source: George William Kakoma composed Uganda's national anthem in 1962.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How should a true Ugandan behave when the national anthem is being sung? A: stand at attention and sing along. A true Ugandan should stand at attention and sing along when the national anthem is being sung.
chunks.source: A true Ugandan should stand at attention and sing along when the national anthem is being sung.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: When is only one stanza of the national anthem sung? A: on brief occasions like school assembly. Only one stanza of the national anthem is sung on brief occasions such as school assembly.
chunks.source: Only one stanza of the national anthem is sung on brief occasions such as school assembly.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: When are all the three stanza’s sung? A: on great national celebrations like Independence Day. All the three stanzas are sung on great national celebrations such as Independence Day.
chunks.source: All the three stanzas are sung on great national celebrations such as Independence Day.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: When was the Uganda national anthem first sung? A: on 9th October 1962. The Uganda national anthem was first sung on 9th October 1962, Independence Day.
chunks.source: The Uganda national anthem was first sung on 9th October 1962, Independence Day.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two occasions on which the national anthem may be sung? A: on Independence Day and at school assembly. The national anthem may be sung on Independence Day and at school assembly.
chunks.source: The national anthem may be sung on Independence Day and at school assembly.

chunks.subject: Social
