chunks.text: Q: What message do we get from the first stanza of the Uganda national anthem? A: Ugandans put their future in God's hands. The message from the first stanza is that Ugandans lay their future in God's hands and love their country.
chunks.source: The message from the first stanza is that Ugandans lay their future in God's hands and love their country.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for Ugandans to show respect to the national anthem when being sung? A: to show patriotism and love for the country. It is important to respect the national anthem because it shows patriotism and love for Uganda.
chunks.source: It is important to respect the national anthem because it shows patriotism and love for Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does the Uganda police help to reduce crime in the country? A: by arresting criminals and patrolling. The Uganda police helps reduce crime by arresting criminals and patrolling towns.
chunks.source: The Uganda police helps reduce crime by arresting criminals and patrolling towns.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one way a school can encourage the community around it to promote sanitation. A: by organizing cleaning days and providing dustbins. A school can encourage sanitation by organizing community cleaning days and providing dustbins.
chunks.source: A school can encourage sanitation by organizing community cleaning days and providing dustbins.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do industries promote development in an area? A: Industries create jobs and produce goods. Industries promote development by creating jobs and producing goods for people.
chunks.source: Industries promote development by creating jobs and producing goods for people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one reason why Port Mombasa is important to Uganda. A: Uganda's imports and exports pass through Port Mombasa. Port Mombasa is important to Uganda because, as a landlocked country, Uganda's goods pass through it.
chunks.source: Port Mombasa is important to Uganda because, as a landlocked country, Uganda's goods pass through it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the importance of caring for the social service centres. A: to keep people healthy and educated. Caring for social service centres is important because they keep people healthy and educated.
chunks.source: Caring for social service centres is important because they keep people healthy and educated.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one cause of street children in Uganda. A: poverty. Poverty is one cause of street children in Uganda.
chunks.source: Poverty is one cause of street children in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do prefects help to maintain order in a school? A: by keeping order and reporting wrongdoers. Prefects help maintain order by keeping discipline and reporting wrongdoers to teachers.
chunks.source: Prefects help maintain order by keeping discipline and reporting wrongdoers to teachers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do traders benefit the people in a community? A: Traders provide goods to the people. Traders benefit the people by bringing goods nearer to them.
chunks.source: Traders benefit the people by bringing goods nearer to them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one weapon used by security organs to maintain peace in an area. A: a gun. A gun is one weapon used by security organs to maintain peace.
chunks.source: A gun is one weapon used by security organs to maintain peace.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why the government is creating many districts in Uganda. A: to bring services nearer to the people. The government is creating many districts to bring services nearer to the people.
chunks.source: The government is creating many districts to bring services nearer to the people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are political leaders got in our country? A: through elections. Political leaders in our country are got through elections by voters.
chunks.source: Political leaders in our country are got through elections by voters.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give anyone example of a voluntary leader. A: a youth leader. A youth leader is an example of a voluntary leader.
chunks.source: A youth leader is an example of a voluntary leader.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are the following leaders important in our country? Religious leaders: A: They preach morals and unite people. Religious leaders are important because they preach good morals and unite people.
chunks.source: Religious leaders are important because they preach good morals and unite people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one symbol of a school found on the school badge. A: the school motto. The school motto is one symbol of a school found on the school badge.
chunks.source: The school motto is one symbol of a school found on the school badge.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can commercial banks help farmers to develop? A: by giving loans to farmers. Commercial banks help farmers by giving them loans to buy seeds and equipment.
chunks.source: Commercial banks help farmers by giving them loans to buy seeds and equipment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are children advised to stand upright when singing the school Anthem? A: to show respect for the anthem. Children should stand upright when singing the anthem to show respect for it.
chunks.source: Children should stand upright when singing the anthem to show respect for it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is a veterinary officer important to farmers? A: by treating sick animals. A veterinary officer is important to farmers because he treats their sick animals.
chunks.source: A veterinary officer is important to farmers because he treats their sick animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How has the government of Uganda tried to solve the problem of water shortage in Karamoja region? A: by building valley dams and drilling boreholes. The government has tried to solve water shortage in Karamoja by building valley dams and drilling boreholes.
chunks.source: The government has tried to solve water shortage in Karamoja by building valley dams and drilling boreholes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why child abuse should be stopped in Uganda. A: because it harms children. Child abuse should be stopped because it harms children physically and mentally.
chunks.source: Child abuse should be stopped because it harms children physically and mentally.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one way the police keeps law and order. A: by patrolling and arresting law breakers. The police keeps law and order by patrolling areas and arresting law breakers.
chunks.source: The police keeps law and order by patrolling areas and arresting law breakers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can a school control indiscipline among children? A: through punishments and guidance. A school can control indiscipline through punishments and guidance and counselling.
chunks.source: A school can control indiscipline through punishments and guidance and counselling.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one social service providers in our community. A: a hospital. A hospital is one social service provider in our community.
chunks.source: A hospital is one social service provider in our community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do some people fail to get better social services? A: because of poverty and long distances. Some people fail to get better social services because of poverty and long distances to service centres.
chunks.source: Some people fail to get better social services because of poverty and long distances to service centres.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which social service is provided by soldiers in our country? A: security. Soldiers provide security as a social service in our country.
chunks.source: Soldiers provide security as a social service in our country.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why the government provides social services to its citizens. A: to improve the welfare of citizens. The government provides social services to improve the welfare of its citizens.
chunks.source: The government provides social services to improve the welfare of its citizens.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match each worker to what they do. A: Judges: settle disputes / cases; Carpenters: make furniture; Police officers: keep law and order; Medical doctors: treat sick people. Judges settle disputes, carpenters make furniture, police officers keep law and order, and medical doctors treat sick people.
chunks.source: Judges settle disputes, carpenters make furniture, police officers keep law and order, and medical doctors treat sick people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are basic needs of man? A: food, shelter and clothing. The basic needs of man are food, shelter and clothing.
chunks.source: The basic needs of man are food, shelter and clothing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two basic needs of people. A: food and shelter. Two basic needs of people are food and shelter.
chunks.source: Two basic needs of people are food and shelter.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one factor that has enabled some people get their basic needs easily. A: having a job that earns income. Some people get their basic needs easily because they have jobs that earn them income.
chunks.source: Some people get their basic needs easily because they have jobs that earn them income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who is a leader? A: a person who guides and directs others. A leader is a person who guides and directs other people.
chunks.source: A leader is a person who guides and directs other people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two qualities of a good leader. A: honest and hardworking. Two qualities of a good leader are honesty and hard work.
chunks.source: Two qualities of a good leader are honesty and hard work.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need leaders in our community? A: to guide and organize the community. We need leaders to guide, organize and unite the community.
chunks.source: We need leaders to guide, organize and unite the community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for the government to tarmac most roads in Uganda? A: to make transport easy and promote development. It is important for the government to tarmac roads to make transport easy and promote development.
chunks.source: It is important for the government to tarmac roads to make transport easy and promote development.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one way we get prefects at school. A: through elections by pupils. We get prefects at school through elections by pupils.
chunks.source: We get prefects at school through elections by pupils.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one importance of a constitution to a country like Uganda. A: It guides how the country is governed. A constitution is important because it guides how the country is governed and protects people's rights.
chunks.source: A constitution is important because it guides how the country is governed and protects people's rights.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one school facility which the community around it can use. A: the playground. The playground is one school facility which the community around it can use.
chunks.source: The playground is one school facility which the community around it can use.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is a speaker of parliament useful in the parliament? A: He controls debates in parliament. The speaker of parliament is useful because he controls debates and keeps order in parliament.
chunks.source: The speaker of parliament is useful because he controls debates and keeps order in parliament.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one importance of a field to a P.5 child. A: It is used for games and sports. A field is important to a P.5 child because it is used for games and sports.
chunks.source: A field is important to a P.5 child because it is used for games and sports.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way farmers are useful to our industries. A: Farmers provide raw materials to industries. Farmers are useful to industries because they supply raw materials like cotton and sugarcane.
chunks.source: Farmers are useful to industries because they supply raw materials like cotton and sugarcane.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How has the government of Uganda tried to control cattle rustling in Karamoja region? A: through disarmament and deploying the army. The government has tried to control cattle rustling in Karamoja through disarmament and deploying the army.
chunks.source: The government has tried to control cattle rustling in Karamoja through disarmament and deploying the army.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way we can care for our social service centres. A: by cleaning them and not vandalizing them. We can care for social service centres by cleaning them and not destroying their property.
chunks.source: We can care for social service centres by cleaning them and not destroying their property.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is child abuse? A: the mistreatment of children. Child abuse is the mistreatment of children.
chunks.source: Child abuse is the mistreatment of children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can child abuse be controlled in Uganda? A: through strict laws and sensitization. Child abuse can be controlled through strict laws and sensitizing people about children's rights.
chunks.source: Child abuse can be controlled through strict laws and sensitizing people about children's rights.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two causes of child abuse. A: poverty and drunkenness. Two causes of child abuse are poverty and drunkenness of parents.
chunks.source: Two causes of child abuse are poverty and drunkenness of parents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How has the government of Uganda tried to improve the lives of people in rural areas? A: by building roads, schools and hospitals. The government has tried to improve rural lives by building roads, schools, hospitals and extending electricity.
chunks.source: The government has tried to improve rural lives by building roads, schools, hospitals and extending electricity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is an economic activity? A: work done to earn a living. An economic activity is work done by people to earn a living.
chunks.source: An economic activity is work done by people to earn a living.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people carry out economic activities? A: to earn a living. People carry out economic activities to earn a living.
chunks.source: People carry out economic activities to earn a living.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of social services provided by the government to its people. A: education and health services. Two social services provided by the government are education and health services.
chunks.source: Two social services provided by the government are education and health services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why does the government of Uganda provide social services to its citizens? A: to improve the welfare of citizens. The government provides social services to improve the welfare of its citizens.
chunks.source: The government provides social services to improve the welfare of its citizens.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one social service provider. A: a school. A school is one social service provider.
chunks.source: A school is one social service provider.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does insecurity affect people in our country? A: Insecurity kills people and scares away investors. Insecurity affects people because it kills, destroys property and scares away investors.
chunks.source: Insecurity affects people because it kills, destroys property and scares away investors.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do some families fail to get basic needs? A: because of poverty and unemployment. Some families fail to get basic needs because of poverty and unemployment.
chunks.source: Some families fail to get basic needs because of poverty and unemployment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How has URA contributed to the development of Uganda? A: by collecting taxes used for development. URA has contributed to development by collecting taxes which the government uses to build roads and schools.
chunks.source: URA has contributed to development by collecting taxes which the government uses to build roads and schools.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one animal that provides security in our homes. A: a dog. A dog is an animal that provides security in our homes.
chunks.source: A dog is an animal that provides security in our homes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one problem faced by political leaders while doing their work. A: opposition from rivals. Political leaders face problems like opposition from rivals and lack of enough funds.
chunks.source: Political leaders face problems like opposition from rivals and lack of enough funds.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the biggest government hospital in Uganda. A: Mulago Hospital. Mulago Hospital is the biggest government hospital in Uganda.
chunks.source: Mulago Hospital is the biggest government hospital in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why should a class be with a sweeping rota? A: so that cleaning work is shared. A class should have a sweeping rota so that cleaning work is shared among all pupils.
chunks.source: A class should have a sweeping rota so that cleaning work is shared among all pupils.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way a school manages the waste materials. A: by using dustbins. A school manages waste materials by providing dustbins and burning rubbish.
chunks.source: A school manages waste materials by providing dustbins and burning rubbish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one disadvantage of a zebra crossing on busy roads. A: It slows down traffic. A disadvantage of a zebra crossing on busy roads is that it slows down traffic.
chunks.source: A disadvantage of a zebra crossing on busy roads is that it slows down traffic.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What title is given to a person who heads bank of Uganda? A: Governor. The person who heads the Bank of Uganda is called the Governor.
chunks.source: The person who heads the Bank of Uganda is called the Governor.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are there few people who read newspapers in Uganda? A: because of illiteracy and poverty. Few people read newspapers in Uganda because of illiteracy and poverty.
chunks.source: Few people read newspapers in Uganda because of illiteracy and poverty.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How has the government of Uganda tried to reduce the rate of illiteracy? A: through UPE and adult literacy programmes. The government has tried to reduce illiteracy through UPE and adult literacy programmes.
chunks.source: The government has tried to reduce illiteracy through UPE and adult literacy programmes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need markets in our community? A: for buying and selling goods. We need markets in our community for buying and selling goods.
chunks.source: We need markets in our community for buying and selling goods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is it dangerous for a child to move alone from home to school? A: because of kidnappers and accidents. It is dangerous for a child to move alone because of kidnappers and road accidents.
chunks.source: It is dangerous for a child to move alone because of kidnappers and road accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What effect do people get from road accidents? A: death and injuries. Road accidents cause death and serious injuries to people.
chunks.source: Road accidents cause death and serious injuries to people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way one can become a leader in Uganda. A: through elections. One can become a leader in Uganda through elections.
chunks.source: One can become a leader in Uganda through elections.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do some people practise child abuse? A: because of poverty and ignorance. Some people practise child abuse because of poverty and ignorance of children's rights.
chunks.source: Some people practise child abuse because of poverty and ignorance of children's rights.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does a nurse promote the health of children in a school? A: by treating sick children and teaching health. A nurse promotes children's health by treating sick children and teaching about cleanliness.
chunks.source: A nurse promotes children's health by treating sick children and teaching about cleanliness.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do very few Ugandans use air transport? A: because air transport is very expensive. Very few Ugandans use air transport because it is very expensive.
chunks.source: Very few Ugandans use air transport because it is very expensive.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State two examples of social services provided by the government. A: schools and hospitals. Two examples of social services are schools and hospitals.
chunks.source: Two examples of social services are schools and hospitals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two problems faced by the government in providing social services. A: lack of enough money and corruption. The government faces lack of enough money and corruption in providing social services.
chunks.source: The government faces lack of enough money and corruption in providing social services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do farmers need good road netwok? A: to transport their produce to markets. Farmers need a good road network to transport their produce to markets easily.
chunks.source: Farmers need a good road network to transport their produce to markets easily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who is a citizen? A: a member of a country with rights and duties. A citizen is a person who is a legal member of a country.
chunks.source: A citizen is a person who is a legal member of a country.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can democracy be practiced in your school? A: by electing prefects. Democracy can be practiced in school by electing prefects through voting.
chunks.source: Democracy can be practiced in school by electing prefects through voting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which group of people introduced democracy in the world? A: the Greeks. The Greeks introduced democracy in the world.
chunks.source: The Greeks introduced democracy in the world.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two ways in which democracy is practiced in Uganda today? A: through regular elections and parliament. Democracy is practiced in Uganda through regular elections and through parliament.
chunks.source: Democracy is practiced in Uganda through regular elections and through parliament.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is an election? A: the choosing of leaders by voting. An election is the choosing of leaders by voting.
chunks.source: An election is the choosing of leaders by voting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why should there be regular elections in Uganda? A: to choose good leaders and remove bad ones. There should be regular elections so that people can choose good leaders and remove bad ones.
chunks.source: There should be regular elections so that people can choose good leaders and remove bad ones.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a by – election? A: an election held to fill a vacant seat. A by-election is an election held to fill a seat that becomes vacant between general elections.
chunks.source: A by-election is an election held to fill a seat that becomes vacant between general elections.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two types of elections? A: general elections and by-elections. Two types of elections are general elections and by-elections.
chunks.source: Two types of elections are general elections and by-elections.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two methods of elections? A: secret ballot and lining up behind candidates. Two methods of elections are secret ballot and lining up behind candidates.
chunks.source: Two methods of elections are secret ballot and lining up behind candidates.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a polling station? A: a place where people go to vote. A polling station is a place where people go to cast their votes.
chunks.source: A polling station is a place where people go to cast their votes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who is a presiding officer? A: the person in charge of a polling station. A presiding officer is the person in charge of a polling station.
chunks.source: A presiding officer is the person in charge of a polling station.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which body in Uganda is responsible for supervising and organizing general elections? A: the Electoral Commission. The Electoral Commission is responsible for supervising and organizing general elections in Uganda.
chunks.source: The Electoral Commission is responsible for supervising and organizing general elections in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two examples of election officials? A: the presiding officer and polling assistants. Examples of election officials are the presiding officer and polling assistants.
chunks.source: Examples of election officials are the presiding officer and polling assistants.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is voting by proxy? A: voting on behalf of another person. Voting by proxy is voting on behalf of another person who cannot be present.
chunks.source: Voting by proxy is voting on behalf of another person who cannot be present.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a government? A: the group of people who rule a country. A government is the group of people who rule and manage a country.
chunks.source: A government is the group of people who rule and manage a country.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Suggest any two reasons why the government of Uganda has created more districts? A: to bring services nearer to the people and create jobs. The government has created more districts to bring services nearer to the people and create jobs.
chunks.source: The government has created more districts to bring services nearer to the people and create jobs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Under which ministry are the local governments? A: the Ministry of Local Government. Local governments are under the Ministry of Local Government.
chunks.source: Local governments are under the Ministry of Local Government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two arms of a democratic government? A: the executive and the legislature. Two arms of a democratic government are the executive and the legislature (and the judiciary).
chunks.source: Two arms of a democratic government are the executive and the legislature (and the judiciary).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: To which organ of the government do the civil servants belong? A: the executive. Civil servants belong to the executive organ of the government.
chunks.source: Civil servants belong to the executive organ of the government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the main role of the Uganda People’s Defence Forces? A: to defend and protect Uganda. The main role of the Uganda People's Defence Forces is to defend and protect Uganda.
chunks.source: The main role of the Uganda People's Defence Forces is to defend and protect Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is the legislative important to the judiciary? A: The legislature makes the laws that the judiciary interprets. The legislature is important to the judiciary because it makes the laws which the judiciary interprets and enforces.
chunks.source: The legislature is important to the judiciary because it makes the laws which the judiciary interprets and enforces.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who heads the executive arm of the government? A: the President. The President heads the executive arm of the government.
chunks.source: The President heads the executive arm of the government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which organ of the government makes laws in Uganda? A: Parliament (the legislature). Parliament, the legislature, is the organ of government that makes laws in Uganda.
chunks.source: Parliament, the legislature, is the organ of government that makes laws in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name any two groups of people under the legislature. A: elected MPs and special interest group representatives. Groups of people under the legislature include elected Members of Parliament and special interest group representatives.
chunks.source: Groups of people under the legislature include elected Members of Parliament and special interest group representatives.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two special groups of people represented in the parliament. A: women and the youth. Special groups represented in parliament include women, the youth, workers, soldiers and people with disabilities.
chunks.source: Special groups represented in parliament include women, the youth, workers, soldiers and people with disabilities.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention the two types of government? A: the central government and local governments. The two types of government are the central government and local governments.
chunks.source: The two types of government are the central government and local governments.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the work of the Sergeant at arms in the parliament? A: to keep order and security in parliament. The Sergeant at arms keeps order and security in parliament.
chunks.source: The Sergeant at arms keeps order and security in parliament.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the work of the Clerk to parliament? A: to record the proceedings of parliament. The Clerk to parliament records the proceedings of parliament.
chunks.source: The Clerk to parliament records the proceedings of parliament.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a bill? A: a proposed law. A bill is a proposed law before parliament.
chunks.source: A bill is a proposed law before parliament.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: When does a bill become a law? A: when it is signed by the President. A bill becomes a law when it is signed by the President.
chunks.source: A bill becomes a law when it is signed by the President.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What term is given to the recorded proceedings in the parliament? A: the Hansard. The Hansard is the term given to the recorded proceedings in parliament.
chunks.source: The Hansard is the term given to the recorded proceedings in parliament.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does one become a member of parliament in Uganda today? A: by being elected by voters in a constituency. One becomes a member of parliament by being elected by voters in a constituency.
chunks.source: One becomes a member of parliament by being elected by voters in a constituency.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a constituency? A: an area represented by a Member of Parliament. A constituency is an area represented by a Member of Parliament.
chunks.source: A constituency is an area represented by a Member of Parliament.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What title is given to the head of the judiciary? A: the Chief Justice. The Chief Justice is the head of the judiciary.
chunks.source: The Chief Justice is the head of the judiciary.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State the minimum educational level for a person to qualify to become a member of Parliament A: Advanced level (Senior Six). The minimum educational level for a Member of Parliament is Advanced level.
chunks.source: The minimum educational level for a Member of Parliament is Advanced level.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the highest court in Uganda? A: the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court is the highest court in Uganda.
chunks.source: The Supreme Court is the highest court in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is the judiciary similar to the local council I in terms of their work? A: Both settle disputes among people. The judiciary is similar to the local council I because both settle disputes among people.
chunks.source: The judiciary is similar to the local council I because both settle disputes among people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who is the highest civil servant in any ministry? A: the Permanent Secretary. The Permanent Secretary is the highest civil servant in any ministry.
chunks.source: The Permanent Secretary is the highest civil servant in any ministry.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two uses of radios to people? A: for news and education. Two uses of radios to people are getting news and education.
chunks.source: Two uses of radios to people are getting news and education.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is it difficult to use televisions in most rural areas of Uganda? A: because of lack of electricity. It is difficult to use televisions in most rural areas because of lack of electricity.
chunks.source: It is difficult to use televisions in most rural areas because of lack of electricity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two modern means of communication. A: mobile phones and the internet. Two modern means of communication are mobile phones and the internet.
chunks.source: Two modern means of communication are mobile phones and the internet.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any three sources of government revenue? A: taxes, loans and foreign aid. Three sources of government revenue are taxes, loans and foreign aid.
chunks.source: Three sources of government revenue are taxes, loans and foreign aid.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State the difference between excise duty and customs duty? A: Excise duty is tax on locally made goods while customs duty is tax on imports and exports. Excise duty is paid on goods made within the country while customs duty is paid on goods imported or exported.
chunks.source: Excise duty is paid on goods made within the country while customs duty is paid on goods imported or exported.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one activity on which the government spends her revenue? A: building roads. The government spends her revenue on activities like building roads, schools and hospitals.
chunks.source: The government spends her revenue on activities like building roads, schools and hospitals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is smuggling? A: the illegal importation or exportation of goods. Smuggling is the illegal importation or exportation of goods without paying taxes.
chunks.source: Smuggling is the illegal importation or exportation of goods without paying taxes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write URA in full. A: Uganda Revenue Authority. URA stands for Uganda Revenue Authority.
chunks.source: URA stands for Uganda Revenue Authority.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are children’s rights? A: the right to education, health and protection. Children's rights include the right to education, health care, food and protection.
chunks.source: Children's rights include the right to education, health care, food and protection.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two causes of child abuse? A: poverty and drunkenness. Two causes of child abuse are poverty and drunkenness of parents.
chunks.source: Two causes of child abuse are poverty and drunkenness of parents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What title is given to the central governments’ representative in the district? A: the Resident District Commissioner (RDC). The Resident District Commissioner is the central government's representative in the district.
chunks.source: The Resident District Commissioner is the central government's representative in the district.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two ways in which one can become a citizen of Uganda? A: by birth and by registration. One can become a citizen of Uganda by birth, registration, naturalization or adoption.
chunks.source: One can become a citizen of Uganda by birth, registration, naturalization or adoption.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is decentralization? A: the sharing of power from the central government to local governments. Decentralization is the sharing of power and responsibilities from the central government to local governments.
chunks.source: Decentralization is the sharing of power and responsibilities from the central government to local governments.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two levels of decentralization. A: the central government and local governments. The two levels of decentralization are the central government and local governments.
chunks.source: The two levels of decentralization are the central government and local governments.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who is a civil servant? A: a person employed by the government. A civil servant is a person employed by the government to provide services.
chunks.source: A civil servant is a person employed by the government to provide services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write CAO in full. A: Chief Administrative Officer. CAO stands for Chief Administrative Officer.
chunks.source: CAO stands for Chief Administrative Officer.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write RDC in full. A: Resident District Commissioner. RDC stands for Resident District Commissioner.
chunks.source: RDC stands for Resident District Commissioner.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State the level at which the local government begins? A: at the village level (LC1). Local government begins at the village level, the LC1.
chunks.source: Local government begins at the village level, the LC1.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a pilot use to find direction? A: a compass. A compass shows direction using a magnetic needle that points north.
chunks.source: A compass shows direction using a magnetic needle that points north.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a pilot use to find direction? A: False. A compass shows direction using a magnetic needle that points north.
chunks.source: A compass shows direction using a magnetic needle that points north.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one block mountain in Uganda. A: Mt. Rwenzori. Mt. Rwenzori is a block mountain formed by faulting.
chunks.source: Mt. Rwenzori is a block mountain formed by faulting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one block mountain in Uganda. A: False. Mt. Rwenzori is a block mountain formed by faulting.
chunks.source: Mt. Rwenzori is a block mountain formed by faulting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do farmers in highlands control soil erosion? A: by terracing and contour ploughing. Terraces slow down running water so it does not carry away the soil.
chunks.source: Terraces slow down running water so it does not carry away the soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do farmers in highlands control soil erosion? A: False. Terraces slow down running water so it does not carry away the soil.
chunks.source: Terraces slow down running water so it does not carry away the soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is the short grass around our school compound very important? A: It controls soil erosion. Short grass holds the soil together and stops wind and water from carrying it away.
chunks.source: Short grass holds the soil together and stops wind and water from carrying it away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is the short grass around our school compound very important? A: False. Short grass holds the soil together and stops wind and water from carrying it away.
chunks.source: Short grass holds the soil together and stops wind and water from carrying it away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What general name is given to all lines of longitudes? A: meridians. All lines of longitude are called meridians.
chunks.source: All lines of longitude are called meridians.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What general name is given to all lines of longitudes? A: False. All lines of longitude are called meridians.
chunks.source: All lines of longitude are called meridians.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How were the rift valleys formed? A: by faulting. Rift valleys were formed when the land between faults sank due to tension forces in the earth's crust.
chunks.source: Rift valleys were formed when the land between faults sank due to tension forces in the earth's crust.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How were the rift valleys formed? A: False. Rift valleys were formed when the land between faults sank due to tension forces in the earth's crust.
chunks.source: Rift valleys were formed when the land between faults sank due to tension forces in the earth's crust.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State two ways people have destroyed the vegetation in some parts of Uganda. A: deforestation and charcoal burning. People destroy vegetation by cutting down trees without planting new ones and by burning charcoal.
chunks.source: People destroy vegetation by cutting down trees without planting new ones and by burning charcoal.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State two ways people have destroyed the vegetation in some parts of Uganda. A: False. People destroy vegetation by cutting down trees without planting new ones and by burning charcoal.
chunks.source: People destroy vegetation by cutting down trees without planting new ones and by burning charcoal.

chunks.text: Q: Apart from a cow, name another domestic animal kept for milk. A: a goat. Apart from a cow, a goat is also kept for milk.
chunks.source: Apart from a cow, a goat is also kept for milk.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Apart from a cow, name another domestic animal kept for milk. A: False. Apart from a cow, a goat is also kept for milk.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can overcrowding be controlled on a map? A: by using symbols. Symbols are used on maps to show many features in a small space without overcrowding.
chunks.source: Symbols are used on maps to show many features in a small space without overcrowding.

chunks.text: Q: How can overcrowding be controlled on a map? A: False. Symbols are used on maps to show many features in a small space without overcrowding.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one element of a good map. A: a title. A good map must have a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.
chunks.source: A good map must have a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one element of a good map. A: False. A good map must have a title, a key, a scale and a compass direction.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one way of conserving the environment. A: by planting trees. Planting trees replaces those cut down and keeps the environment green.

chunks.text: Q: Mention any one way of conserving the environment. A: False. Planting trees replaces those cut down and keeps the environment green.

chunks.text: Q: Name any one volcanic mountain in Uganda. A: Mt. Elgon. Mt. Elgon is a volcanic mountain formed by volcanicity.

chunks.text: Q: Name any one volcanic mountain in Uganda. A: False. Mt. Elgon is a volcanic mountain formed by volcanicity.

chunks.text: Q: How do terraces help in controlling soil erosion in hilly areas? A: They slow down running water. Terraces are steps cut across slopes that slow down water so it does not wash away soil.

chunks.text: Q: How do terraces help in controlling soil erosion in hilly areas? A: False. Terraces are steps cut across slopes that slow down water so it does not wash away soil.

chunks.text: Q: Mention one means of transport used by children when coming to school. A: walking. Many children walk to school.

chunks.text: Q: Mention one means of transport used by children when coming to school. A: False. Many children walk to school.

chunks.text: Q: Which type of natural vegetation covers the largest part of Uganda? A: savanna vegetation. Savanna vegetation covers the largest part of Uganda.

chunks.text: Q: Which type of natural vegetation covers the largest part of Uganda? A: False. Savanna vegetation covers the largest part of Uganda.

chunks.text: Q: Write any one product got from hard wood timber. A: furniture. Hard wood timber from natural forests is used to make furniture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write any one product got from hard wood timber. A: False. Hard wood timber from natural forests is used to make furniture.

chunks.text: Q: Give any two items obtained from a swamp. A: fish and clay. People get fish, clay for making pots and papyrus from swamps.

chunks.text: Q: Give any two items obtained from a swamp. A: False. People get fish, clay for making pots and papyrus from swamps.

chunks.text: Q: What term is used to mean the number of people living in an area per square kilometre? A: population density. Population density is the number of people living in an area per square kilometre.

chunks.text: Q: Name the line of longitude marked 180o. A: the International Date Line. The line of longitude marked 180 degrees is the International Date Line.

chunks.text: Q: Apart from gold, which other mineral is mined from Karamoja region. A: False. Apart from gold, limestone is also mined in Karamoja.

chunks.text: Q: Which National organization is in charge of forests in Uganda? A: National Forestry Authority (NFA). The National Forestry Authority is in charge of forests in Uganda.

chunks.text: Q: Which National organization is in charge of forests in Uganda? A: False. The National Forestry Authority is in charge of forests in Uganda.
