chunks.source: Nouns ending in -sh take -es in the plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: bench → ___ A: benches. Nouns ending in -ch take -es in the plural.
chunks.source: Nouns ending in -ch take -es in the plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: patch → ___ A: patches. Nouns ending in -ch take -es in the plural.
chunks.source: Nouns ending in -ch take -es in the plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: baby → ___ A: babies. Nouns ending in consonant + y change y to -ies.
chunks.source: Nouns ending in consonant + y change y to -ies.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: city → ___ A: cities. Nouns ending in consonant + y change y to -ies.
chunks.source: Nouns ending in consonant + y change y to -ies.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: thief → ___ A: thieves. Some nouns ending in -f change f to -ves.
chunks.source: Some nouns ending in -f change f to -ves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: loaf → ___ A: loaves. Some nouns ending in -f change f to -ves.
chunks.source: Some nouns ending in -f change f to -ves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: leaf → ___ A: leaves. Some nouns ending in -f change f to -ves.
chunks.source: Some nouns ending in -f change f to -ves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: shelf → ___ A: shelves. Some nouns ending in -f change f to -ves.
chunks.source: Some nouns ending in -f change f to -ves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: scarf → ___ A: scarves. Some nouns ending in -f change f to -ves.
chunks.source: Some nouns ending in -f change f to -ves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: calf → ___ A: calves. Some nouns ending in -f change f to -ves.
chunks.source: Some nouns ending in -f change f to -ves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: mouse → ___ A: mice. 'Mouse' has an irregular plural: 'mice'.
chunks.source: 'Mouse' has an irregular plural: 'mice'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: child → ___ A: children. 'Child' has an irregular plural: 'children'.
chunks.source: 'Child' has an irregular plural: 'children'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: tooth → ___ A: teeth. 'Tooth' has an irregular plural: 'teeth'.
chunks.source: 'Tooth' has an irregular plural: 'teeth'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: foot → ___ A: feet. 'Foot' has an irregular plural: 'feet'.
chunks.source: 'Foot' has an irregular plural: 'feet'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: man → ___ A: men. 'Man' has an irregular plural: 'men'.
chunks.source: 'Man' has an irregular plural: 'men'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: woman → ___ A: women. 'Woman' has an irregular plural: 'women'.
chunks.source: 'Woman' has an irregular plural: 'women'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: sheep → ___ A: sheep. 'Sheep' has the same form in singular and plural.
chunks.source: 'Sheep' has the same form in singular and plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: ox → ___ A: oxen. 'Ox' has an irregular plural: 'oxen'.
chunks.source: 'Ox' has an irregular plural: 'oxen'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: cactus → ___ A: cacti. 'Cactus' changes -us to -i in the plural.
chunks.source: 'Cactus' changes -us to -i in the plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: syllabus → ___ A: syllabi. 'Syllabus' changes -us to -i in the plural.
chunks.source: 'Syllabus' changes -us to -i in the plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: analysis → ___ A: analyses. 'Analysis' changes -is to -es in the plural.
chunks.source: 'Analysis' changes -is to -es in the plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: crisis → ___ A: crises. 'Crisis' changes -is to -es in the plural.
chunks.source: 'Crisis' changes -is to -es in the plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: chief → ___ A: chiefs. Nouns ending in -f after a vowel just add -s.
chunks.source: Nouns ending in -f after a vowel just add -s.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: belief → ___ A: beliefs. Nouns ending in -f after a vowel just add -s.
chunks.source: Nouns ending in -f after a vowel just add -s.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: handkerchief → ___ A: handkerchiefs. Nouns ending in -f after a vowel just add -s.
chunks.source: Nouns ending in -f after a vowel just add -s.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: mother-in-law → ___ A: mothers-in-law. In hyphenated nouns, pluralize the main word.
chunks.source: In hyphenated nouns, pluralize the main word.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: father-in-law → ___ A: fathers-in-law. In hyphenated nouns, pluralize the main word.
chunks.source: In hyphenated nouns, pluralize the main word.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: passer-by → ___ A: passers-by. In hyphenated nouns, pluralize the main word.
chunks.source: In hyphenated nouns, pluralize the main word.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence giving the plural of 'diary': His diary is very expensive. ___ A: His diaries are very expensive.. Change 'diary' to 'diaries' and 'is' to 'are'.
chunks.source: Change 'diary' to 'diaries' and 'is' to 'are'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence giving the plural of 'calf': Please, look after that calf. ___ A: Please, look after those calves.. Change 'calf' to 'calves' and 'that' to 'those'.
chunks.source: Change 'calf' to 'calves' and 'that' to 'those'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence giving the plural of 'referee': The national referee has been suspended. ___ A: The national referees have been suspended.. Change 'referee' to 'referees' and 'has' to 'have'.
chunks.source: Change 'referee' to 'referees' and 'has' to 'have'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence ending with '... mammals.': A duck is not a flying mammal. ___ A: Ducks are not flying mammals.. Make both 'duck' and 'mammal' plural.
chunks.source: Make both 'duck' and 'mammal' plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the doll of the child → ___ A: the child's doll. Use 's to show one child owns the doll.
chunks.source: Use 's to show one child owns the doll.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the shoes of the woman → ___ A: the woman's shoes. Use 's to show one woman owns the shoes.
chunks.source: Use 's to show one woman owns the shoes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the tail of the puppy → ___ A: the puppy's tail. Use 's to show the puppy owns the tail.
chunks.source: Use 's to show the puppy owns the tail.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the horns of the buffalo → ___ A: the buffalo's horns. Use 's to show the buffalo owns the horns.
chunks.source: Use 's to show the buffalo owns the horns.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the boundaries of Uganda → ___ A: Uganda's boundaries. Use 's with names of places.
chunks.source: Use 's with names of places.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the smooth voice of Suzan → ___ A: Suzan's smooth voice. Use 's with people's names.
chunks.source: Use 's with people's names.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the ring of the princess → ___ A: the princess's ring. Use 's to show the princess owns the ring.
chunks.source: Use 's to show the princess owns the ring.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the house of my niece → ___ A: my niece's house. Use 's to show the niece owns the house.
chunks.source: Use 's to show the niece owns the house.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the cubs of the lioness → ___ A: the lioness's cubs. Use 's to show the lioness owns the cubs.
chunks.source: Use 's to show the lioness owns the cubs.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the feathers of the bird → ___ A: the bird's feathers. Use 's to show the bird owns the feathers.
chunks.source: Use 's to show the bird owns the feathers.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: dresses for ladies → ___ A: ladies' dresses. With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.
chunks.source: With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: uniform for policemen → ___ A: policemen's uniforms. 'Policemen' is already plural, so add 's.
chunks.source: 'Policemen' is already plural, so add 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: talons of eagles → ___ A: eagles' talons. With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.
chunks.source: With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: a house belonging to Moses → ___ A: Moses's house. Use 's with people's names.
chunks.source: Use 's with people's names.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: food for visitors → ___ A: visitors' food. With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.
chunks.source: With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: books belonging to pupils → ___ A: pupils' books. With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.
chunks.source: With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: toys for children → ___ A: children's toys. 'Children' is already plural, so add 's.
chunks.source: 'Children' is already plural, so add 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: money for workers → ___ A: workers' money. With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.
chunks.source: With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ______ driving licence had expired. (motorist) A: motorist's. One motorist owns the licence, so add 's.
chunks.source: One motorist owns the licence, so add 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ______ feet were covered with sores. (pedestrians) A: pedestrians'. Many pedestrians: the plural ends in s, so add only the apostrophe.
chunks.source: Many pedestrians: the plural ends in s, so add only the apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We failed to read the ______ signature. (chairman) A: chairman's. One chairman owns the signature, so add 's.
chunks.source: One chairman owns the signature, so add 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ______ concert was interesting. (children) A: children's. 'Children' is already plural, so add 's.
chunks.source: 'Children' is already plural, so add 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Many ______ hats were blown off by the strong wind. (people) A: people's. 'People' is already plural, so add 's.
chunks.source: 'People' is already plural, so add 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The boxer beat ______ badly yesterday. (I) A: me. After a verb, use the object pronoun 'me'.
chunks.source: After a verb, use the object pronoun 'me'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The guide has taken ______ around the lake. (we) A: us. After a verb, use the object pronoun 'us'.
chunks.source: After a verb, use the object pronoun 'us'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The manager will blame ______ for the loss. (you) A: you. After a verb, use the object pronoun 'you'.
chunks.source: After a verb, use the object pronoun 'you'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The wardens punished ______ for misbehaviour. (she) A: her. After a verb, use the object pronoun 'her'.
chunks.source: After a verb, use the object pronoun 'her'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Did the referee cheat ______ during the match? (they) A: them. After a verb, use the object pronoun 'them'.
chunks.source: After a verb, use the object pronoun 'them'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I shall borrow a novel from ______ tomorrow. (he) A: him. After a preposition, use the object pronoun 'him'.
chunks.source: After a preposition, use the object pronoun 'him'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mr. Pianos wished ______ a safe journey. (they) A: them. After a verb, use the object pronoun 'them'.
chunks.source: After a verb, use the object pronoun 'them'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The shopkeeper sold ______ some sugar last week. (I) A: me. Use 'me' as the indirect object.
chunks.source: Use 'me' as the indirect object.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The shepherds hid ______ mousetraps. (they) A: their. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'their'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'their'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The cat shook ______ tail. (it) A: its. Before a noun, use 'its' (no apostrophe).
chunks.source: Before a noun, use 'its' (no apostrophe).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The driver drank all ______ milk. (he) A: his. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'his'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'his'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I decided to enlarge the entrance to ______ kitchen. (I) A: my. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'my'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'my'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: These are ______ orchards. (we) A: our. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'our'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'our'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Are these ______ reams of paper or not? (you) A: your. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'your'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'your'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He has dirtied ______ shoes, hasn't he? (they) A: their. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'their'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'their'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The teacher fed the sheep and ______ lambs. (it) A: its. Before a noun, use 'its' (no apostrophe).
chunks.source: Before a noun, use 'its' (no apostrophe).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: None of ______ brothers is courageous. (you) A: your. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'your'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'your'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The cheetah injured ______ when it was running. (it) A: itself. The action goes back to the doer: use 'itself'.
chunks.source: The action goes back to the doer: use 'itself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We blamed ______ for not buying the equipment. (we) A: ourselves. The action goes back to the doers: use 'ourselves'.
chunks.source: The action goes back to the doers: use 'ourselves'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: This girl dirtied ______ in the muddy water. (she) A: herself. The action goes back to the doer: use 'herself'.
chunks.source: The action goes back to the doer: use 'herself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I baked the cake all by ______. (I) A: myself. 'By myself' means 'alone'.
chunks.source: 'By myself' means 'alone'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She taught ______ to play the piano. (she) A: herself. The action goes back to the doer: use 'herself'.
chunks.source: The action goes back to the doer: use 'herself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You don't seem ______ this morning. (you) A: yourself. 'Yourself' is the reflexive form of 'you'.
chunks.source: 'Yourself' is the reflexive form of 'you'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They had the whole plate of food to ______. (they) A: themselves. The reflexive form of 'they' is 'themselves'.
chunks.source: The reflexive form of 'they' is 'themselves'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A friend of ______ has been arrested for forgery. (I) A: mine. After 'a friend of', use the possessive pronoun 'mine'.
chunks.source: After 'a friend of', use the possessive pronoun 'mine'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If the cobbler isn't careful, he is likely to hurt ______ while mending the boots. (he) A: himself. The action goes back to the doer: use 'himself'.
chunks.source: The action goes back to the doer: use 'himself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Is that the van ______ transports newspapers upcountry? A: that. Use the relative pronoun 'that' for things.
chunks.source: Use the relative pronoun 'that' for things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The casualties ______ vehicle overturned were taken to hospital. A: whose. Use 'whose' to show possession for people.
chunks.source: Use 'whose' to show possession for people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Road transport is cheaper ______ water transport. A: than. Use 'than' after a comparative adjective like 'cheaper'.
chunks.source: Use 'than' after a comparative adjective like 'cheaper'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: This test is ______ simple that no one will fail it. A: so. The pattern is 'so ... that' to show result.
chunks.source: The pattern is 'so ... that' to show result.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our chairman was ______ interested nor against the programme. A: neither. The pair is 'neither ... nor'.
chunks.source: The pair is 'neither ... nor'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ______ we learn crafts at school, we may not be useful citizens in future. A: Unless. 'Unless' means 'if ... not'.
chunks.source: 'Unless' means 'if ... not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ______ the manager nor the chief accountant could explain the theft. A: Neither. The pair is 'neither ... nor'.
chunks.source: The pair is 'neither ... nor'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Hardly has the doctor arrived ______ the patient died. A: when. The pair is 'hardly ... when'.
chunks.source: The pair is 'hardly ... when'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... because ...": "As the motorist was approaching a black spot, he reduced the speed." ___ A: The motorist reduced the speed because he was approaching a black spot.. 'Because' introduces the reason.
chunks.source: 'Because' introduces the reason.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "In spite of the fact that ...": "Jovita is a very tall girl. She can't touch the ceiling." ___ A: In spite of the fact that Jovita is a very tall girl, she can't touch the ceiling.. 'In spite of the fact that' shows contrast.
chunks.source: 'In spite of the fact that' shows contrast.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences as one using "... which ...": "This is the newspaper. I bought it at one hundred shillings." ___ A: This is the newspaper which I bought at one hundred shillings.. 'Which' joins the sentences and replaces 'it'.
chunks.source: 'Which' joins the sentences and replaces 'it'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "Not only ... but also ...": "The mechanic repaired the car. He also painted it." ___ A: The mechanic not only repaired the car but also painted it.. 'Not only ... but also' joins two similar ideas.
chunks.source: 'Not only ... but also' joins two similar ideas.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... and so ...": "Both Kato and Wasswa performed very well in the examination." ___ A: Kato performed very well in the examination and so did Wasswa.. 'And so did' avoids repeating the verb.
chunks.source: 'And so did' avoids repeating the verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... not only ...": "Mr. Kasozi is a teacher and a tailor." ___ A: Mr. Kasozi is not only a teacher but also a tailor.. 'Not only ... but also' joins two nouns.
chunks.source: 'Not only ... but also' joins two nouns.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "As soon as ...": "No sooner had the accident occurred than the villagers gathered." ___ A: As soon as the accident occurred, the villagers gathered.. 'As soon as' means the same as 'no sooner ... than'.
chunks.source: 'As soon as' means the same as 'no sooner ... than'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... but ...": "In spite of the fact that the debate started early, it ended very late." ___ A: The debate started early but it ended very late.. 'But' shows the contrast simply.
chunks.source: 'But' shows the contrast simply.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... because ...": "The chef did not report on duty as he was ill." ___ A: The chef did not report on duty because he was ill.. 'Because' replaces 'as' to show reason.
chunks.source: 'Because' replaces 'as' to show reason.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences as one using "... either ... or ...": "Our mother may go to town tomorrow. Our mother may go to school tomorrow." ___ A: Our mother may go either to town or to school tomorrow.. 'Either ... or' shows a choice between two.
chunks.source: 'Either ... or' shows a choice between two.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "Although ...": "It had rained heavily but the children went swimming." ___ A: Although it had rained heavily, the children went swimming.. 'Although' replaces 'but' to show contrast.
chunks.source: 'Although' replaces 'but' to show contrast.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... as soon as ...": "Hardly had the carpenter finished varnishing the table when he sold it off." ___ A: The carpenter sold it off as soon as he finished varnishing the table.. 'As soon as' means the same as 'hardly ... when'.
chunks.source: 'As soon as' means the same as 'hardly ... when'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... because ...": "The traffic officer stopped the car so as to check the driver's licence." ___ A: The traffic officer stopped the car because he wanted to check the driver's licence.. 'Because he wanted to' explains the purpose.
chunks.source: 'Because he wanted to' explains the purpose.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "Not only ... but also ...": "Mr. Kasozi is a trader. Mr. Kasozi is also a carpenter." ___ A: Mr. Kasozi is not only a trader but also a carpenter.. 'Not only ... but also' joins two nouns.
chunks.source: 'Not only ... but also' joins two nouns.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "Whereas ...": "We are children but we need protection." ___ A: Whereas we are children, we need protection.. 'Whereas' replaces 'but' to show contrast.
chunks.source: 'Whereas' replaces 'but' to show contrast.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "Immediately ...": "No sooner had we entered the room than the thief knocked at the door." ___ A: Immediately we entered the room, the thief knocked at the door.. 'Immediately' means the same as 'no sooner ... than'.
chunks.source: 'Immediately' means the same as 'no sooner ... than'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "In spite of the fact that ...": "The officer advised us to plant trees but we didn't care." ___ A: In spite of the fact that the officer advised us to plant trees, we didn't care.. 'In spite of the fact that' shows contrast.
chunks.source: 'In spite of the fact that' shows contrast.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ___ honest man helped the poor family. A: An. Use 'an' before a vowel sound, like the silent h in 'honest'.
chunks.source: Use 'an' before a vowel sound, like the silent h in 'honest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She plays ___ piano very well. A: the. Use 'the' with musical instruments.
chunks.source: Use 'the' with musical instruments.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Kampala is ___ capital city of Uganda. A: the. Use 'the' when there is only one of something.
chunks.source: Use 'the' when there is only one of something.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He is ___ European teacher. A: a. Use 'a' before a consonant sound; 'European' starts with a 'y' sound.
chunks.source: Use 'a' before a consonant sound; 'European' starts with a 'y' sound.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I saw ___ owl in the tree last night. A: an. Use 'an' before a vowel sound.
chunks.source: Use 'an' before a vowel sound.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My father is ___ engineer. A: an. Use 'an' before a vowel sound.
chunks.source: Use 'an' before a vowel sound.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We stayed at ___ hotel near the lake. A: a. Use 'a' before a consonant sound for something not specific.
chunks.source: Use 'a' before a consonant sound for something not specific.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ___ honesty is the best policy. A: No article. Abstract nouns like 'honesty' take no article in general statements.
chunks.source: Abstract nouns like 'honesty' take no article in general statements.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: By the time Kayimu arrived at the bus park, most buses ______. (leave) A: had left. Use the past perfect ('had left') for the earlier of two past actions.
chunks.source: Use the past perfect ('had left') for the earlier of two past actions.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The timekeeper has just ______ the morning bell. (ring) A: rung. 'Ring, rang, rung': use 'rung' after 'has'.
chunks.source: 'Ring, rang, rung': use 'rung' after 'has'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My entire family will ______ to Nairobi for a tour. (travel) A: travel. After 'will', use the base form of the verb.
chunks.source: After 'will', use the base form of the verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... since ...": "The sun is shining brightly. It started shining in the morning." ___ A: The sun has been shining brightly since morning.. Use the present perfect continuous with 'since' for an action that started in the past and continues.
chunks.source: Use the present perfect continuous with 'since' for an action that started in the past and continues.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She ______ him for thirty minutes. (blame) A: has been blaming. Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.
chunks.source: Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The pupils ______ since morning. (walk) A: have been walking. Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.
chunks.source: Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The shopkeeper ______ fruits since she went to the city. (sell) A: has been selling. Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.
chunks.source: Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The drivers ______ their taxis since morning. (drive) A: have been driving. Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.
chunks.source: Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We ______ our books for the last two weeks. (revise) A: have been revising. Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.
chunks.source: Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She ___ to school every day. A: goes. With 'she' in the present simple, add -s to the verb.
chunks.source: With 'she' in the present simple, add -s to the verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They ___ football now. A: are playing. 'Now' shows the present continuous: 'are playing'.
chunks.source: 'Now' shows the present continuous: 'are playing'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He ___ his homework already. A: has finished. 'Already' with a finished action uses the present perfect: 'has finished'.
chunks.source: 'Already' with a finished action uses the present perfect: 'has finished'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We ___ to Kampala tomorrow. A: will travel. 'Tomorrow' shows the future: 'will travel'.
chunks.source: 'Tomorrow' shows the future: 'will travel'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She ___ the bus yesterday. A: missed. 'Yesterday' shows the past simple: 'missed'.
chunks.source: 'Yesterday' shows the past simple: 'missed'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How many ______ boxes have been bought here? (triangle) A: triangular. 'Triangular' is the adjective form of 'triangle'.
chunks.source: 'Triangular' is the adjective form of 'triangle'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Driving ______ is the major cause of accidents in Uganda. (reckless) A: recklessly. Use the adverb 'recklessly' to describe how they drive.
chunks.source: Use the adverb 'recklessly' to describe how they drive.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ______ you walk, the sooner you will reach town. (fast) A: faster. The pattern 'the ... the ...' needs comparatives: 'the faster'.
chunks.source: The pattern 'the ... the ...' needs comparatives: 'the faster'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The dogs barked ______ at the stranger. (angry) A: angrily. Use the adverb 'angrily' to describe how they barked.
chunks.source: Use the adverb 'angrily' to describe how they barked.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My parents were born in the ______ area of south-western Uganda. (mountain) A: mountainous. 'Mountainous' is the adjective form of 'mountain'.
chunks.source: 'Mountainous' is the adjective form of 'mountain'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... than ...": "Rose is beautiful. Stellah is very beautiful." ___ A: Stellah is more beautiful than Rose.. Use 'more ... than' to compare.
chunks.source: Use 'more ... than' to compare.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences as one using "... not as ...": "Amolo is two metres tall. Amolata is three metres tall." ___ A: Amolo is not as tall as Amolata.. 'Not as ... as' compares two things.
chunks.source: 'Not as ... as' compares two things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... always ...": "The teacher marks our books every day." ___ A: The teacher always marks our books.. 'Always' replaces 'every day'.
chunks.source: 'Always' replaces 'every day'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... always ...": "He writes the social studies notes every day." ___ A: He always writes the social studies notes.. 'Always' replaces 'every day'.
chunks.source: 'Always' replaces 'every day'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences as one using "... too ... to ...": "That family was very big. That lady could not feed it alone." ___ A: That family was too big for that lady to feed alone.. The pattern 'too ... to' shows something is impossible.
chunks.source: The pattern 'too ... to' shows something is impossible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join the sentences as one using "... too ... to ...": "My computer is very slow. It cannot open in the first two minutes." ___ A: My computer is too slow to open in the first two minutes.. The pattern 'too ... to' shows something is impossible.
chunks.source: The pattern 'too ... to' shows something is impossible.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... so ... that ...": "My room is too small to accommodate five guests." ___ A: My room is so small that it cannot accommodate five guests.. 'So ... that' replaces 'too ... to'.
chunks.source: 'So ... that' replaces 'too ... to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Babies depend ______ milk most of the time. A: on. We say 'depend on'.
chunks.source: We say 'depend on'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Akampa's house is next ______ mine. A: to. We say 'next to'.
chunks.source: We say 'next to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Is it true that our school librarian is related ______ the headteacher? A: to. We say 'related to'.
chunks.source: We say 'related to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The spectators started arguing ______ themselves when Mubiru scored. A: among. Use 'among' for more than two people.
chunks.source: Use 'among' for more than two people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I wonder why many people are suffering ______ flu nowadays. A: from. We say 'suffer from' an illness.
chunks.source: We say 'suffer from' an illness.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She is very good ______ mathematics. A: at. We say 'good at' a subject.
chunks.source: We say 'good at' a subject.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The book is ______ the table. A: on. Use 'on' for something resting on a surface.
chunks.source: Use 'on' for something resting on a surface.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They arrived ______ Kampala in the evening. A: in. Use 'in' with towns and cities.
chunks.source: Use 'in' with towns and cities.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "Ann said that ...": "I am revising my social studies notes now," Ann said. ___ A: Ann said that she was revising her social studies notes then.. In reported speech, 'I' becomes 'she', 'am revising' becomes 'was revising', and 'now' becomes 'then'.
chunks.source: In reported speech, 'I' becomes 'she', 'am revising' becomes 'was revising', and 'now' becomes 'then'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "The headteacher said that ...": "The guest is coming to address the gathering today," said the headteacher. ___ A: The headteacher said that the guest was coming to address the gathering that day.. In reported speech, 'is coming' becomes 'was coming' and 'today' becomes 'that day'.
chunks.source: In reported speech, 'is coming' becomes 'was coming' and 'today' becomes 'that day'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "The head teacher said that ...": "The inspector of schools will visit our school tomorrow," said the head teacher. ___ A: The head teacher said that the inspector of schools would visit their school the next day.. In reported speech, 'will' becomes 'would' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.
chunks.source: In reported speech, 'will' becomes 'would' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct reported speech: "I am hungry," said Tom. A: Tom said that he was hungry.. In reported speech, 'I' becomes 'he' and 'am' becomes 'was'.
chunks.source: In reported speech, 'I' becomes 'he' and 'am' becomes 'was'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence: "By whom were the funny pictures in the newspaper drawn?" (Give one word for "By whom".) ___ A: Who drew the funny pictures in the newspaper?. The active form of 'were drawn' is 'drew'; 'by whom' becomes 'who'.
chunks.source: The active form of 'were drawn' is 'drew'; 'by whom' becomes 'who'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "All the school ...": "Daniella has repaired all the school furniture." ___ A: All the school furniture has been repaired by Daniella.. Present perfect passive: 'has been repaired'. The object becomes the subject.
chunks.source: Present perfect passive: 'has been repaired'. The object becomes the subject.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "The pupils ...": "The headteacher is addressing the pupils." ___ A: The pupils are being addressed by the headteacher.. Present continuous passive: 'are being addressed'.
chunks.source: Present continuous passive: 'are being addressed'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence in the passive: "The dog bit the boy." ___ A: The boy was bitten by the dog.. Past simple passive: 'was bitten'. The object becomes the subject.
chunks.source: Past simple passive: 'was bitten'. The object becomes the subject.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct passive form: "She writes a letter." A: A letter is written by her.. Present simple passive: 'is written'.
chunks.source: Present simple passive: 'is written'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence in the passive: "They will build a new classroom." ___ A: A new classroom will be built by them.. Future passive: 'will be built'.
chunks.source: Future passive: 'will be built'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "Unless ...": "My father will not pay me a visit if he does not get enough money." ___ A: My father will not pay me a visit unless he gets enough money.. 'Unless' means 'if ... not', so remove the negative.
chunks.source: 'Unless' means 'if ... not', so remove the negative.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "I would ...": "If I listen to the news, I will learn something." ___ A: I would learn something if I listened to the news.. Second conditional: 'would' + past simple in the if-clause.
chunks.source: Second conditional: 'would' + past simple in the if-clause.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... would ...": "I have the money but I will not buy anything." ___ A: Even though I have the money, I would not buy anything.. 'Would' softens the refusal.
chunks.source: 'Would' softens the refusal.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ______ you write a good application letter, you will not be given that job. A: Unless. 'Unless' means 'if ... not'.
chunks.source: 'Unless' means 'if ... not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "I would go ...": "If mummy returns home early, I will go for choir practice." ___ A: I would go for choir practice if mummy returned home early.. Second conditional: 'would' + past simple in the if-clause.
chunks.source: Second conditional: 'would' + past simple in the if-clause.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: "If it rains, we ___ at home." Choose the correct word. A: will stay. First conditional: 'if' + present simple, then 'will'.
chunks.source: First conditional: 'if' + present simple, then 'will'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write two separate sentences: "John did not attend today's debate due to his illness." ___ A: John did not attend today's debate. He was ill.. 'Due to his illness' becomes a second sentence: 'He was ill'.
chunks.source: 'Due to his illness' becomes a second sentence: 'He was ill'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join as one sentence without using "who" or "and": "Audi is a tall girl. She is beautiful. She is brown." ___ A: Audi is a tall, beautiful, brown girl.. Join the adjectives with commas before the noun.
chunks.source: Join the adjectives with commas before the noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "It is ...": "Watching football on a projector screen is very interesting." ___ A: It is very interesting to watch football on a projector screen.. 'It is ... to ...' replaces the -ing subject.
chunks.source: 'It is ... to ...' replaces the -ing subject.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Join as one sentence using "... enough ...": "The traffic officer was very kind. He assisted the learners to cross the road." ___ A: The traffic officer was kind enough to assist the learners to cross the road.. The pattern is 'adjective + enough + to'.
chunks.source: The pattern is 'adjective + enough + to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... belongs ...": "Abigail is the owner of that goat." ___ A: That goat belongs to Abigail.. 'Belongs to' replaces 'is the owner of'.
chunks.source: 'Belongs to' replaces 'is the owner of'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... succeeded ...": "My father managed to write a good composition." ___ A: My father succeeded in writing a good composition.. 'Succeed in' replaces 'manage to'.
chunks.source: 'Succeed in' replaces 'manage to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form a suitable question for the statement: "There are three hundred national referees in Sweden." ___ A: How many national referees are there in Sweden?. Use 'How many' to ask about a number.
chunks.source: Use 'How many' to ask about a number.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... in order to ...": "That mechanic repaired the car very well because he wanted to please his master." ___ A: That mechanic repaired the car very well in order to please his master.. 'In order to' replaces 'because he wanted to'.
chunks.source: 'In order to' replaces 'because he wanted to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write two separate sentences: "This is the magazine which had very interesting articles." ___ A: This is the magazine. It had very interesting articles.. Split the relative clause into its own sentence.
chunks.source: Split the relative clause into its own sentence.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... related to ...": "Joshua is Lydia's relative." ___ A: Joshua is related to Lydia.. 'Is related to' replaces 'is ...'s relative'.
chunks.source: 'Is related to' replaces 'is ...'s relative'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... reach ...": "Jjagwa arrived at the garage before the heavy rain." ___ A: Jjagwa reached the garage before the heavy rain.. 'Reached' replaces 'arrived at'.
chunks.source: 'Reached' replaces 'arrived at'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... owns ...": "That house belongs to Janet." ___ A: Janet owns that house.. 'Owns' replaces 'belongs to', and the subject changes.
chunks.source: 'Owns' replaces 'belongs to', and the subject changes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Form a suitable question for the statement: "My grandfather has three bakeries." ___ A: How many bakeries does your grandfather have?. Use 'How many' to ask about a number.
chunks.source: Use 'How many' to ask about a number.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... arrived ...": "The police reached the crime scene after two hours." ___ A: The police arrived at the crime scene after two hours.. 'Arrived at' replaces 'reached'.
chunks.source: 'Arrived at' replaces 'reached'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... so as ...": "Agute went to the internet café. He wanted to read about plant species." ___ A: Agute went to the internet café so as to read about plant species.. 'So as to' replaces 'wanted to' to show purpose.
chunks.source: 'So as to' replaces 'wanted to' to show purpose.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite as one sentence: "What a good presentation the primary six pupils made!" ___ A: The primary six pupils made a very good presentation.. Change the exclamation into a statement.
chunks.source: Change the exclamation into a statement.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite as one sentence without using "which" or "and": "Jeff received a watch. It was made of gold. It was expensive." ___ A: Jeff received an expensive watch made of gold.. Join the describing words before the noun.
chunks.source: Join the describing words before the noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence beginning "How dangerous ...!": "It is very dangerous to take laws in one's own hand." ___ A: How dangerous it is to take laws in one's own hand!. 'How' + adjective starts an exclamation.
chunks.source: 'How' + adjective starts an exclamation.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match each word with its opposite: guilty, interesting, exit, left. A: guilty: innocent; interesting: boring; exit: entrance; left: right. Guilty-innocent, interesting-boring, exit-entrance, left-right.
chunks.source: Guilty-innocent, interesting-boring, exit-entrance, left-right.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Put each noun under the correct kind: Kampala, book, flock, honesty, team, courage, Jinja, chair. A: Proper nouns: Kampala,Jinja; Common nouns: book,chair; Collective nouns: flock,team; Abstract nouns: honesty,courage. Kampala and Jinja are proper nouns; book and chair are common nouns; flock and team are collective nouns; honesty and courage are abstract nouns.
chunks.source: Kampala and Jinja are proper nouns; book and chair are common nouns; flock and team are collective nouns; honesty and courage are abstract nouns.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which of these words are abstract nouns? A: honesty, courage, kindness, friendship. Abstract nouns name ideas or feelings: honesty, courage, kindness, friendship.
chunks.source: Abstract nouns name ideas or feelings: honesty, courage, kindness, friendship.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which sentences use the correct plural forms? A: The children are playing., The mice are in the hole.. 'Children' and 'mice' are the correct irregular plurals.
chunks.source: 'Children' and 'mice' are the correct irregular plurals.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The plural of 'sheep' is 'sheeps'. A: False. 'Sheep' has the same form in singular and plural.
chunks.source: 'Sheep' has the same form in singular and plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The word 'furniture' does not have a plural form. A: True. 'Furniture' is uncountable; we say 'pieces of furniture'.
chunks.source: 'Furniture' is uncountable; we say 'pieces of furniture'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The opposite of 'ancient' is 'modern'. A: True. 'Ancient' means very old; 'modern' means new.
chunks.source: 'Ancient' means very old; 'modern' means new.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence: tailor / a / needle / have / a / must / every / day A: Every, tailor, must, have, a, needle, every, day. The correct sentence is: 'Every tailor must have a needle every day.'
chunks.source: The correct sentence is: 'Every tailor must have a needle every day.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence: birth / given / to / my / twins / has / sister A: My, sister, has, given, birth, to, twins. The correct sentence is: 'My sister has given birth to twins.'
chunks.source: The correct sentence is: 'My sister has given birth to twins.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence: lends / usually / neighbour / our / car / his / us A: Our, neighbour, usually, lends, us, his, car. The correct sentence is: 'Our neighbour usually lends us his car.'
chunks.source: The correct sentence is: 'Our neighbour usually lends us his car.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence: nor / the / neither / doctor / the / has / nurse / come A: Neither, the, doctor, nor, the, nurse, has, come. The correct sentence is: 'Neither the doctor nor the nurse has come.'
chunks.source: The correct sentence is: 'Neither the doctor nor the nurse has come.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence: concert / what / is / lively / what / this / a A: What, a, lively, concert, this, is. The correct sentence is: 'What a lively concert this is!'
chunks.source: The correct sentence is: 'What a lively concert this is!'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence: very / bad / lies / to / tell / it / is / teachers / to A: It, is, very, bad, to, tell, lies, to, teachers. The correct sentence is: 'It is very bad to tell lies to teachers.'
chunks.source: The correct sentence is: 'It is very bad to tell lies to teachers.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words to form a correct sentence: sent / cyclist / the / reckless / was / to / prison A: The, reckless, cyclist, was, sent, to, prison. The correct sentence is: 'The reckless cyclist was sent to prison.'
chunks.source: The correct sentence is: 'The reckless cyclist was sent to prison.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in alphabetical order: Sunshine, sunny, shining, shone A: shone, shining, sunny, Sunshine. Alphabetical order: shone, shining, sunny, Sunshine.
chunks.source: Alphabetical order: shone, shining, sunny, Sunshine.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in alphabetical order: Tamia, Jovita, Jonathan, Teko A: Jonathan, Jovita, Tamia, Teko. Alphabetical order: Jonathan, Jovita, Tamia, Teko.
chunks.source: Alphabetical order: Jonathan, Jovita, Tamia, Teko.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in alphabetical order: foods, feeds, feed, freedom A: feed, feeds, foods, freedom. Alphabetical order: feed, feeds, foods, freedom.
chunks.source: Alphabetical order: feed, feeds, foods, freedom.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in alphabetical order: abuse, agree, apart, ashame A: abuse, agree, apart, ashame. Alphabetical order: abuse, agree, apart, ashame.
chunks.source: Alphabetical order: abuse, agree, apart, ashame.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where did the accident take place? A: At a zebra crossing. The passage begins: 'I witnessed an accident at a zebra crossing.'
chunks.source: The passage begins: 'I witnessed an accident at a zebra crossing.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What was the reckless driver doing when the accident happened? A: Talking on a mobile phone. The passage says the driver 'had been talking on a mobile phone'.
chunks.source: The passage says the driver 'had been talking on a mobile phone'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The writer's mother is a nurse. A: True. The passage says: 'My mother, being a nurse, rushed over to give him first aid.'
chunks.source: The passage says: 'My mother, being a nurse, rushed over to give him first aid.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The taxi driver managed to escape. A: False. The passage says: 'The taxi driver tried to escape, but some youths stopped him.'
chunks.source: The passage says: 'The taxi driver tried to escape, but some youths stopped him.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The writer wrote the taxi ___ number on a piece of paper. A: registration. The writer 'took note of the taxi registration number'.
chunks.source: The writer 'took note of the taxi registration number'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What did the police do to the reckless driver? A: They arrested him and took his driving permit.. The police 'confiscated the reckless driver's driving permit and arrested him'.
chunks.source: The police 'confiscated the reckless driver's driving permit and arrested him'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What almost hit Nababi? A: A speeding car. The passage begins: 'A car zoomed past. It missed Nababi by inches.'
chunks.source: The passage begins: 'A car zoomed past. It missed Nababi by inches.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What should vehicles do when the traffic light turns red? A: Stop. Mother says: 'When the light turns red, the vehicles will stop.'
chunks.source: Mother says: 'When the light turns red, the vehicles will stop.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Nababi's mother says it is safe to cross the road at a roundabout. A: False. Mother says: 'You should not cross the road at a roundabout just like that. It is very dangerous.'
chunks.source: Mother says: 'You should not cross the road at a roundabout just like that. It is very dangerous.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A ___ is a set of rules on how motorists and pedestrians should use the road safely. A: Highway Code. Mother explains: 'A Highway Code is a set of rules on how motorists and pedestrians should use the road safely.'
chunks.source: Mother explains: 'A Highway Code is a set of rules on how motorists and pedestrians should use the road safely.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do some drivers cause many accidents? A: They speed even where there are road humps.. The passage says such drivers 'speed even where we have road humps'.
chunks.source: The passage says such drivers 'speed even where we have road humps'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Nababi promised her mother that she would always be careful. A: True. Nababi says: 'I promise you, mother, I will be very careful.'
chunks.source: Nababi says: 'I promise you, mother, I will be very careful.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who had an accident according to the dialogue? A: Jane, the head prefect. Mariam says: 'Jane, our head prefect, had an accident this morning.'
chunks.source: Mariam says: 'Jane, our head prefect, had an accident this morning.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What knocked Jane down? A: A speeding motorcycle. Mariam says: 'A speeding motorcycle knocked her down.'
chunks.source: Mariam says: 'A speeding motorcycle knocked her down.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: To which hospital was Jane taken? A: Mengo Hospital. Mariam says Jane was 'rushed to Mengo Hospital by an ambulance'.
chunks.source: Mariam says Jane was 'rushed to Mengo Hospital by an ambulance'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Jane looked right, left and right again before crossing the road. A: False. Mariam says: 'Not at all! She was in a hurry.'
chunks.source: Mariam says: 'Not at all! She was in a hurry.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Jane is the school's head ___. A: prefect. The dialogue calls Jane 'our head prefect'.
chunks.source: The dialogue calls Jane 'our head prefect'.

chunks.subject: English
