chunks.source: Nouns ending in -f after a vowel just add -s.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: handkerchief → ___ A: handkerchiefs. Nouns ending in -f after a vowel just add -s.
chunks.source: Nouns ending in -f after a vowel just add -s.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: mother-in-law → ___ A: mothers-in-law. In hyphenated nouns, pluralize the main word.
chunks.source: In hyphenated nouns, pluralize the main word.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: father-in-law → ___ A: fathers-in-law. In hyphenated nouns, pluralize the main word.
chunks.source: In hyphenated nouns, pluralize the main word.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the plural form of the given word: passer-by → ___ A: passers-by. In hyphenated nouns, pluralize the main word.
chunks.source: In hyphenated nouns, pluralize the main word.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence giving the plural of 'diary': His diary is very expensive. ___ A: His diaries are very expensive.. Change 'diary' to 'diaries' and 'is' to 'are'.
chunks.source: Change 'diary' to 'diaries' and 'is' to 'are'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence giving the plural of 'calf': Please, look after that calf. ___ A: Please, look after those calves.. Change 'calf' to 'calves' and 'that' to 'those'.
chunks.source: Change 'calf' to 'calves' and 'that' to 'those'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence ending with '... mammals.': A duck is not a flying mammal. ___ A: Ducks are not flying mammals.. Make both 'duck' and 'mammal' plural.
chunks.source: Make both 'duck' and 'mammal' plural.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the doll of the child → ___ A: the child's doll. Use 's to show one child owns the doll.
chunks.source: Use 's to show one child owns the doll.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the shoes of the woman → ___ A: the woman's shoes. Use 's to show one woman owns the shoes.
chunks.source: Use 's to show one woman owns the shoes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the tail of the puppy → ___ A: the puppy's tail. Use 's to show the puppy owns the tail.
chunks.source: Use 's to show the puppy owns the tail.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the horns of the buffalo → ___ A: the buffalo's horns. Use 's to show the buffalo owns the horns.
chunks.source: Use 's to show the buffalo owns the horns.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the boundaries of Uganda → ___ A: Uganda's boundaries. Use 's with names of places.
chunks.source: Use 's with names of places.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the smooth voice of Suzan → ___ A: Suzan's smooth voice. Use 's with people's names.
chunks.source: Use 's with people's names.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the ring of the princess → ___ A: the princess's ring. Use 's to show the princess owns the ring.
chunks.source: Use 's to show the princess owns the ring.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the house of my niece → ___ A: my niece's house. Use 's to show the niece owns the house.
chunks.source: Use 's to show the niece owns the house.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the cubs of the lioness → ___ A: the lioness's cubs. Use 's to show the lioness owns the cubs.
chunks.source: Use 's to show the lioness owns the cubs.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: the feathers of the bird → ___ A: the bird's feathers. Use 's to show the bird owns the feathers.
chunks.source: Use 's to show the bird owns the feathers.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: dresses for ladies → ___ A: ladies' dresses. With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.
chunks.source: With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: uniform for policemen → ___ A: policemen's uniforms. 'Policemen' is already plural, so add 's.
chunks.source: 'Policemen' is already plural, so add 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: talons of eagles → ___ A: eagles' talons. With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.
chunks.source: With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: a house belonging to Moses → ___ A: Moses's house. Use 's with people's names.
chunks.source: Use 's with people's names.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: food for visitors → ___ A: visitors' food. With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.
chunks.source: With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: books belonging to pupils → ___ A: pupils' books. With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.
chunks.source: With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: toys for children → ___ A: children's toys. 'Children' is already plural, so add 's.
chunks.source: 'Children' is already plural, so add 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite using the possessive form: money for workers → ___ A: workers' money. With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.
chunks.source: With plural nouns ending in s, add only the apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ______ driving licence had expired. (motorist) A: motorist's. One motorist owns the licence, so add 's.
chunks.source: One motorist owns the licence, so add 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ______ feet were covered with sores. (pedestrians) A: pedestrians'. Many pedestrians: the plural ends in s, so add only the apostrophe.
chunks.source: Many pedestrians: the plural ends in s, so add only the apostrophe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We failed to read the ______ signature. (chairman) A: chairman's. One chairman owns the signature, so add 's.
chunks.source: One chairman owns the signature, so add 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ______ concert was interesting. (children) A: children's. 'Children' is already plural, so add 's.
chunks.source: 'Children' is already plural, so add 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Many ______ hats were blown off by the strong wind. (people) A: people's. 'People' is already plural, so add 's.
chunks.source: 'People' is already plural, so add 's.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The boxer beat ______ badly yesterday. (I) A: me. After a verb, use the object pronoun 'me'.
chunks.source: After a verb, use the object pronoun 'me'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The guide has taken ______ around the lake. (we) A: us. After a verb, use the object pronoun 'us'.
chunks.source: After a verb, use the object pronoun 'us'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The manager will blame ______ for the loss. (you) A: you. After a verb, use the object pronoun 'you'.
chunks.source: After a verb, use the object pronoun 'you'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The wardens punished ______ for misbehaviour. (she) A: her. After a verb, use the object pronoun 'her'.
chunks.source: After a verb, use the object pronoun 'her'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Did the referee cheat ______ during the match? (they) A: them. After a verb, use the object pronoun 'them'.
chunks.source: After a verb, use the object pronoun 'them'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I shall borrow a novel from ______ tomorrow. (he) A: him. After a preposition, use the object pronoun 'him'.
chunks.source: After a preposition, use the object pronoun 'him'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mr. Pianos wished ______ a safe journey. (they) A: them. After a verb, use the object pronoun 'them'.
chunks.source: After a verb, use the object pronoun 'them'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The shopkeeper sold ______ some sugar last week. (I) A: me. Use 'me' as the indirect object.
chunks.source: Use 'me' as the indirect object.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The shepherds hid ______ mousetraps. (they) A: their. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'their'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'their'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The cat shook ______ tail. (it) A: its. Before a noun, use 'its' (no apostrophe).
chunks.source: Before a noun, use 'its' (no apostrophe).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The driver drank all ______ milk. (he) A: his. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'his'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'his'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I decided to enlarge the entrance to ______ kitchen. (I) A: my. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'my'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'my'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: These are ______ orchards. (we) A: our. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'our'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'our'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Are these ______ reams of paper or not? (you) A: your. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'your'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'your'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He has dirtied ______ shoes, hasn't he? (they) A: their. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'their'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'their'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The teacher fed the sheep and ______ lambs. (it) A: its. Before a noun, use 'its' (no apostrophe).
chunks.source: Before a noun, use 'its' (no apostrophe).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: None of ______ brothers is courageous. (you) A: your. Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'your'.
chunks.source: Before a noun, use the possessive adjective 'your'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The cheetah injured ______ when it was running. (it) A: itself. The action goes back to the doer: use 'itself'.
chunks.source: The action goes back to the doer: use 'itself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We blamed ______ for not buying the equipment. (we) A: ourselves. The action goes back to the doers: use 'ourselves'.
chunks.source: The action goes back to the doers: use 'ourselves'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: This girl dirtied ______ in the muddy water. (she) A: herself. The action goes back to the doer: use 'herself'.
chunks.source: The action goes back to the doer: use 'herself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I baked the cake all by ______. (I) A: myself. 'By myself' means 'alone'.
chunks.source: 'By myself' means 'alone'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She taught ______ to play the piano. (she) A: herself. The action goes back to the doer: use 'herself'.
chunks.source: The action goes back to the doer: use 'herself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You don't seem ______ this morning. (you) A: yourself. 'Yourself' is the reflexive form of 'you'.
chunks.source: 'Yourself' is the reflexive form of 'you'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They had the whole plate of food to ______. (they) A: themselves. The reflexive form of 'they' is 'themselves'.
chunks.source: The reflexive form of 'they' is 'themselves'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A friend of ______ has been arrested for forgery. (I) A: mine. After 'a friend of', use the possessive pronoun 'mine'.
chunks.source: After 'a friend of', use the possessive pronoun 'mine'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If the cobbler isn't careful, he is likely to hurt ______ while mending the boots. (he) A: himself. The action goes back to the doer: use 'himself'.
chunks.source: The action goes back to the doer: use 'himself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Is that the van ______ transports newspapers upcountry? A: that. Use the relative pronoun 'that' for things.
chunks.source: Use the relative pronoun 'that' for things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The casualties ______ vehicle overturned were taken to hospital. A: whose. Use 'whose' to show possession for people.
chunks.source: Use 'whose' to show possession for people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Road transport is cheaper ______ water transport. A: than. Use 'than' after a comparative adjective like 'cheaper'.
chunks.source: Use 'than' after a comparative adjective like 'cheaper'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: This test is ______ simple that no one will fail it. A: so. The pattern is 'so ... that' to show result.
chunks.source: The pattern is 'so ... that' to show result.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our chairman was ______ interested nor against the programme. A: neither. The pair is 'neither ... nor'.
chunks.source: The pair is 'neither ... nor'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ______ we learn crafts at school, we may not be useful citizens in future. A: Unless. 'Unless' means 'if ... not'.
chunks.source: 'Unless' means 'if ... not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ______ the manager nor the chief accountant could explain the theft. A: Neither. The pair is 'neither ... nor'.
chunks.source: The pair is 'neither ... nor'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Hardly has the doctor arrived ______ the patient died. A: when. The pair is 'hardly ... when'.
chunks.source: The pair is 'hardly ... when'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: By the time Kayimu arrived at the bus park, most buses ______. (leave) A: had left. Use the past perfect ('had left') for the earlier of two past actions.
chunks.source: Use the past perfect ('had left') for the earlier of two past actions.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The timekeeper has just ______ the morning bell. (ring) A: rung. 'Ring, rang, rung': use 'rung' after 'has'.
chunks.source: 'Ring, rang, rung': use 'rung' after 'has'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My entire family will ______ to Nairobi for a tour. (travel) A: travel. After 'will', use the base form of the verb.
chunks.source: After 'will', use the base form of the verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She ______ him for thirty minutes. (blame) A: has been blaming. Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.
chunks.source: Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The pupils ______ since morning. (walk) A: have been walking. Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.
chunks.source: Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The shopkeeper ______ fruits since she went to the city. (sell) A: has been selling. Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.
chunks.source: Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The drivers ______ their taxis since morning. (drive) A: have been driving. Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.
chunks.source: Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We ______ our books for the last two weeks. (revise) A: have been revising. Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.
chunks.source: Use the present perfect continuous for an action continuing over time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How many ______ boxes have been bought here? (triangle) A: triangular. 'Triangular' is the adjective form of 'triangle'.
chunks.source: 'Triangular' is the adjective form of 'triangle'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Driving ______ is the major cause of accidents in Uganda. (reckless) A: recklessly. Use the adverb 'recklessly' to describe how they drive.
chunks.source: Use the adverb 'recklessly' to describe how they drive.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ______ you walk, the sooner you will reach town. (fast) A: faster. The pattern 'the ... the ...' needs comparatives: 'the faster'.
chunks.source: The pattern 'the ... the ...' needs comparatives: 'the faster'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The dogs barked ______ at the stranger. (angry) A: angrily. Use the adverb 'angrily' to describe how they barked.
chunks.source: Use the adverb 'angrily' to describe how they barked.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My parents were born in the ______ area of south-western Uganda. (mountain) A: mountainous. 'Mountainous' is the adjective form of 'mountain'.
chunks.source: 'Mountainous' is the adjective form of 'mountain'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Babies depend ______ milk most of the time. A: on. We say 'depend on'.
chunks.source: We say 'depend on'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Akampa's house is next ______ mine. A: to. We say 'next to'.
chunks.source: We say 'next to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Is it true that our school librarian is related ______ the headteacher? A: to. We say 'related to'.
chunks.source: We say 'related to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The spectators started arguing ______ themselves when Mubiru scored. A: among. Use 'among' for more than two people.
chunks.source: Use 'among' for more than two people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I wonder why many people are suffering ______ flu nowadays. A: from. We say 'suffer from' an illness.
chunks.source: We say 'suffer from' an illness.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She is very good ______ mathematics. A: at. We say 'good at' a subject.
chunks.source: We say 'good at' a subject.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The book is ______ the table. A: on. Use 'on' for something resting on a surface.
chunks.source: Use 'on' for something resting on a surface.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They arrived ______ Kampala in the evening. A: in. Use 'in' with towns and cities.
chunks.source: Use 'in' with towns and cities.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence ending with "... does she?": "Kalipo likes dancing, doesn't she?" ___ A: Kalipo likes dancing, does she?. Follow the instruction: end with 'does she?'.
chunks.source: Follow the instruction: end with 'does she?'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Candidates need a lot of revisionrevision exercises for practice. (revise) A: True. The noun form of 'revise' is 'revision'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'revise' is 'revision'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: There was a lot of confusionconfusion at the rally. (confuse) A: True. The noun form of 'confuse' is 'confusion'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'confuse' is 'confusion'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: His conversionconversion to Islam led him to great wealth. (convert) A: True. 'Convert' becomes 'conversion' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Convert' becomes 'conversion' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: When all the trees were cut down, soil erosionerosion increased in the area. (erode) A: True. The noun form of 'erode' is 'erosion'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'erode' is 'erosion'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The girl did not get permissionpermission to go to the market. (permit) A: True. The noun form of 'permit' is 'permission'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'permit' is 'permission'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: There is little provisionprovision of food in the desert areas. (provide) A: True. 'Provide' becomes 'provision' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Provide' becomes 'provision' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The separationseparation between husband and wife makes children suffer. (separate) A: True. The noun form of 'separate' is 'separation'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'separate' is 'separation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I was given a lot of encouragementencouragement when I lost my new toy car. (encourage) A: True. 'Encourage' becomes 'encouragement' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Encourage' becomes 'encouragement' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Wars and racism bring extreme hatredhatred among citizens. (hate) A: True. The noun form of 'hate' is 'hatred'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'hate' is 'hatred'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: All animals need protectionprotection against illegal hunters. (protect) A: True. The noun form of 'protect' is 'protection'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'protect' is 'protection'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The teacher told us to do correctionscorrections in our books. (correct) A: True. 'Correct' becomes 'corrections' (plural) as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Correct' becomes 'corrections' (plural) as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Sarah was given a prize because of her determinationdetermination to win. (determine) A: True. 'Determine' becomes 'determination' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Determine' becomes 'determination' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The oppositionopposition party has no support from the public. (oppose) A: True. The noun form of 'oppose' is 'opposition'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'oppose' is 'opposition'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We have to pay attentionattention in class. (attend) A: True. 'Attend' becomes 'attention' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Attend' becomes 'attention' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is your occupationoccupation these days? (occupy) A: True. 'Occupy' becomes 'occupation' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Occupy' becomes 'occupation' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The revenue authority deals with tax collectioncollection in the country. (collect) A: True. The noun form of 'collect' is 'collection'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'collect' is 'collection'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: DictationDictation exercise is not easy for me in class. (dictate) A: True. 'Dictate' becomes 'dictation' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Dictate' becomes 'dictation' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Tethering an animal is a hindrancehindrance to its freedom of movement. (hinder) A: True. 'Hinder' becomes 'hindrance' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Hinder' becomes 'hindrance' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Ebonyi made a suitable choicechoice of dress. (choose) A: True. The noun form of 'choose' is 'choice'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'choose' is 'choice'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The headmaster apologized for his absenceabsence. (absent) A: True. 'Absent' becomes 'absence' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Absent' becomes 'absence' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Even wild animals need securitysecurity all the time. (secure) A: True. 'Secure' becomes 'security' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Secure' becomes 'security' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He did not succeed because of his pridepride. (proud) A: True. The noun form of 'proud' is 'pride'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'proud' is 'pride'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: PunctualityPunctuality can lead to success in business. (punctual) A: True. 'Punctual' becomes 'punctuality' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Punctual' becomes 'punctuality' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The matron received us with pleasurepleasure. (please) A: True. 'Please' becomes 'pleasure' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Please' becomes 'pleasure' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: God wants people to say the truththe truth all the time. (true) A: True. The noun form of 'true' is 'truth'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'true' is 'truth'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You need to understand the realityreality of life. (real) A: True. 'Real' becomes 'reality' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Real' becomes 'reality' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She was very dirty because of povertypoverty. (poor) A: True. 'Poor' becomes 'poverty' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Poor' becomes 'poverty' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He was chosen to be the guest of honour due to his generositygenerosity. (generous) A: True. 'Generous' becomes 'generosity' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Generous' becomes 'generosity' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Kato was not chosen as head boy because of his shabbinessshabbiness. (shabby) A: True. 'Shabby' becomes 'shabbiness' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Shabby' becomes 'shabbiness' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We are looking for safetysafety as we put up the security light. (safe) A: True. 'Safe' becomes 'safety' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Safe' becomes 'safety' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The pupil was given a front seatseat because of his stubbornness. (sit) A: True. 'Sit' becomes 'seat' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Sit' becomes 'seat' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Due to the disappointmentdisappointment at the party, I left very fast. (disappoint) A: True. 'Disappoint' becomes 'disappointment' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Disappoint' becomes 'disappointment' as a noun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The stranger was tired, so he was advised to take a restrest. (rest) A: True. 'Rest' is both a verb and a noun.
chunks.source: 'Rest' is both a verb and a noun.

chunks.subject: English

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... belongs ...": "Abigail is the owner of that goat." John did not attend today's debate. He was ill. A: False. 'Belongs to' replaces 'is the owner of'.

chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... related to ...": "Joshua is Lydia's relative." That mechanic repaired the car very well in order to please his master. A: False. 'Is related to' replaces 'is ...'s relative'.

chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence using "... owns ...": "That house belongs to Janet." Jeff received an expensive watch made of gold. A: False. 'Owns' replaces 'belongs to', and the subject changes.
chunks.source: 'Owns' replaces 'belongs to', and the subject changes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rewrite the sentence ending with "... does she?": "Kalipo likes dancing, doesn't she?" We need health centres in our community, don't we? A: False. Follow the instruction: end with 'does she?'.

chunks.text: Q: Candidates need a lot of determinationdetermination exercises for practice. (revise) A: False. The noun form of 'revise' is 'revision'.

chunks.text: Q: His explanationexplanation to Islam led him to great wealth. (convert) A: False. 'Convert' becomes 'conversion' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: Wars and racism bring extreme erosionerosion among citizens. (hate) A: False. The noun form of 'hate' is 'hatred'.

chunks.text: Q: Sarah was given a prize because of her separationseparation to win. (determine) A: False. 'Determine' becomes 'determination' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: We have to pay friendshipfriendship in class. (attend) A: False. 'Attend' becomes 'attention' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: What is your choicechoice these days? (occupy) A: False. 'Occupy' becomes 'occupation' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: The revenue authority deals with tax the truththe truth in the country. (collect) A: False. The noun form of 'collect' is 'collection'.

chunks.text: Q: permissionpermission exercise is not easy for me in class. (dictate) A: False. 'Dictate' becomes 'dictation' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Dictate' becomes 'dictation' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: Tethering an animal is a shabbinessshabbiness to its freedom of movement. (hinder) A: False. 'Hinder' becomes 'hindrance' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Hinder' becomes 'hindrance' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: Ebonyi made a suitable sadnesssadness of dress. (choose) A: False. The noun form of 'choose' is 'choice'.

chunks.text: Q: The headmaster apologized for his explanationexplanation. (absent) A: False. 'Absent' becomes 'absence' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: Even wild animals need arrivalarrival all the time. (secure) A: False. 'Secure' becomes 'security' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: He did not succeed because of his determinationdetermination. (proud) A: False. The noun form of 'proud' is 'pride'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'proud' is 'pride'.

chunks.text: Q: occupationoccupation can lead to success in business. (punctual) A: False. 'Punctual' becomes 'punctuality' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Punctual' becomes 'punctuality' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: The matron received us with kindnesskindness. (please) A: False. 'Please' becomes 'pleasure' as a noun.
chunks.source: 'Please' becomes 'pleasure' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: God wants people to say conversionconversion all the time. (true) A: False. The noun form of 'true' is 'truth'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'true' is 'truth'.

chunks.text: Q: He was chosen to be the guest of honour due to his abilityability. (generous) A: False. 'Generous' becomes 'generosity' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: Kato was not chosen as head boy because of his choicechoice. (shabby) A: False. 'Shabby' becomes 'shabbiness' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: We are looking for wisdomwisdom as we put up the security light. (safe) A: False. 'Safe' becomes 'safety' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: The pupil was given a front collectioncollection because of his stubbornness. (sit) A: False. 'Sit' becomes 'seat' as a noun.

chunks.text: Q: The stranger was tired, so he was advised to take a salesale. (rest) A: False. 'Rest' is both a verb and a noun.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that P = {vowel letters}. Find the number of subsets that can be formed from set P. A: 32. P has 5 members; subsets = 2^5 = 32.
chunks.source: P has 5 members; subsets = 2^5 = 32.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given n(A) = 15, n(B) = 25 and n(A intersect B) = 5: how many members are in A only? A: 10. 15 - 5 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given n(A) = 15, n(B) = 25 and n(A intersect B) = 5: how many members are in B only? A: 20. 25 - 5 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given n(A) = 15, n(B) = 25, n(A intersect B) = 5 and n(universe) = 55: find n(A union B)'. A: 20. n(A union B) = 10 + 5 + 20 = 35; 55 - 35 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 409,049 in words. A: Four hundred nine thousand, forty-nine. 409,049 = four hundred nine thousand, forty-nine.
chunks.source: 409,049 = four hundred nine thousand, forty-nine.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Subtract 102_five from 242_five, and give your answer in base ten. A: 45. 242_five = 72 and 102_five = 27 in base ten; 72 - 27 = 45.
chunks.source: 242_five = 72 and 102_five = 27 in base ten; 72 - 27 = 45.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Round off 389 to the nearest hundreds. A: 400. 389 is closest to 400.
chunks.source: 389 is closest to 400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What number has been expanded as (5 x 10^1) + (8 x 10^0) + (3 x 10^-1)? A: 58.3. 50 + 8 + 0.3 = 58.3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 58.3 in words. A: fifty-eight point three. 58.3 = fifty-eight point three.
chunks.source: 58.3 = fifty-eight point three.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Add: 416 + 22 A: 438. Add the two numbers: 416 + 22 = 438.
chunks.source: Add the two numbers: 416 + 22 = 438.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Subtract: 754 - 239 A: 515. 754 minus 239 equals 515.
chunks.source: 754 minus 239 equals 515.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Share 2727 apples between 9 boys. How many will each one get? A: 303. 2727 divided by 9 equals 303.
chunks.source: 2727 divided by 9 equals 303.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the difference between 268 and 143? A: 125. Difference means subtraction: 268 - 143 = 125.
chunks.source: Difference means subtraction: 268 - 143 = 125.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Simplify: 3 + 4 x 2 A: 11. Multiply first: 4 x 2 = 8, then add: 3 + 8 = 11.
chunks.source: Multiply first: 4 x 2 = 8, then add: 3 + 8 = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A truck can carry 80 bags of millet in one trip. How many bags can it carry in 96 trips? A: 7680. 80 x 96 = 7680 bags.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: At a party 4896 people were each served with a bottle of soda. If each crate of soda contains 24 bottles, how many crates of soda were served? A: 204. 4896 divided by 24 equals 204 crates.
chunks.source: 4896 divided by 24 equals 204 crates.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Each crate of soda costs sh.24,000. 204 crates were served at a party. How much money was used to buy all the crates? A: 4896000. 204 x 24,000 = 4,896,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Patrick had 20 coins of sh.500 and 65 coins of sh.200 in his saving box. If he wanted 1000-shilling notes from the total amount, how many notes would he get? A: 23. 20 x 500 = 10,000 and 65 x 200 = 13,000; total 23,000; 23,000 / 1,000 = 23 notes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A bus carried 59 passengers per trip. How many passengers will the bus carry if it makes 12 trips? A: 708. 59 x 12 = 708 passengers.
chunks.source: 59 x 12 = 708 passengers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: There are 30 eggs in one tray. How many trays will be required to pack 330 eggs? A: 11. 330 divided by 30 equals 11 trays.
chunks.source: 330 divided by 30 equals 11 trays.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A radio uses batteries of 1.5 volts. For the radio to work, it requires 12 volts. How many such batteries will the radio require? A: 8. 12 divided by 1.5 equals 8 batteries.
chunks.source: 12 divided by 1.5 equals 8 batteries.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A pair of batteries costs sh.1,000. How much money is needed to buy 8 batteries? A: 4000. 8 batteries = 4 pairs; 4 x 1,000 = 4,000 shillings.
chunks.source: 8 batteries = 4 pairs; 4 x 1,000 = 4,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Ssempijja's poultry produces 3000 eggs in a day. If eggs are packed in trays of 30 eggs each, how many trays are produced in a week? A: 700. 3000 / 30 = 100 trays per day; 100 x 7 = 700 trays per week.
chunks.source: 3000 / 30 = 100 trays per day; 100 x 7 = 700 trays per week.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A taxi carries 14 passengers while a bus carries 59 passengers. If the two vehicles make two journeys each, how many passengers will they carry altogether? A: 146. (14 + 59) x 2 = 73 x 2 = 146 passengers.
chunks.source: (14 + 59) x 2 = 73 x 2 = 146 passengers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A bus left Kampala for Masaka with 60 passengers. At Mpigi 15 got out, at Buwama 8 boarded, and at Lukaya 12 got out. How many passengers reached Masaka? A: 41. 60 - 15 + 8 - 12 = 41 passengers.
chunks.source: 60 - 15 + 8 - 12 = 41 passengers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 41 passengers reached Masaka town, each paying sh.8,000. How much money was collected? A: 328000. 41 x 8,000 = 328,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Sort into Even and Odd: 7, 12, 19, 24, 31, 40 A: Even: 12,24,40; Odd: 7,19,31. Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.
chunks.source: Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Sort into Multiple of 3 and Not a multiple of 3: 12, 14, 15, 20, 21, 25 A: Multiple of 3: 12,15,21; Not a multiple of 3: 14,20,25. 12, 15, 21 divide by 3; 14, 20, 25 do not.
chunks.source: 12, 15, 21 divide by 3; 14, 20, 25 do not.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the number line to multiply: 3 x 2 = A: 6. 3 x 2 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Peter had three silos of 124016 kg, 31419 kg and 214602 kg of beans. How many kg did he have altogether? A: 370037. 124016 + 31419 + 214602 = 370037 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 2, 3, 5, 7, _____ A: 11. These are prime numbers in order; the next prime after 7 is 11.
chunks.source: These are prime numbers in order; the next prime after 7 is 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the GCF of 12 and 16. A: 4. The factors of 12 are 1,2,3,4,6,12 and of 16 are 1,2,4,8,16; the greatest common factor is 4.
chunks.source: The factors of 12 are 1,2,3,4,6,12 and of 16 are 1,2,4,8,16; the greatest common factor is 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Prime factorize 64 using set notation. A: {2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2}. 64 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2, written in set notation as {2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2}.
chunks.source: 64 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2, written in set notation as {2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2}.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which of these numbers are prime? A: 2, 7, 11. 2, 7 and 11 have only two factors.
chunks.source: 2, 7 and 11 have only two factors.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The volume of a cube is 27 dm^3. Find the length of each side. A: 3. The cube root of 27 is 3.
chunks.source: The cube root of 27 is 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which of these are multiples of 8 less than 50? A: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48 (56 is not less than 50).
chunks.source: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48 (56 is not less than 50).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The sum of 3 consecutive counting numbers is 63. Find the numbers. A: 20, 21, 22. 63 / 3 = 21, the middle number; the numbers are 20, 21, 22.
chunks.source: 63 / 3 = 21, the middle number; the numbers are 20, 21, 22.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The sum of 3 consecutive counting numbers is 63. Work out the range of the numbers. A: 2. The numbers are 20, 21, 22; range = 22 - 20 = 2.
chunks.source: The numbers are 20, 21, 22; range = 22 - 20 = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The LCM of two numbers is 120. Their GCF is 10. One of the numbers is 40. Find the other number. A: 30. LCM x GCF = product of the numbers: 120 x 10 = 1200; 1200 / 40 = 30.
chunks.source: LCM x GCF = product of the numbers: 120 x 10 = 1200; 1200 / 40 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A bell rings every 30 minutes and another every 40 minutes. They ring together at 8:45 a.m. After how many hours will they ring together again? A: 2. LCM of 30 and 40 is 120 minutes, which is 2 hours.
chunks.source: LCM of 30 and 40 is 120 minutes, which is 2 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A bell rings every 30 minutes and another every 40 minutes. They ring together at 8:45 a.m. At what time will they ring together again? A: 10:45 a.m.. They ring together every 2 hours, so next at 8:45 + 2 hours = 10:45 a.m.
chunks.source: They ring together every 2 hours, so next at 8:45 + 2 hours = 10:45 a.m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Fatuma arranged apples in heaps of 12 and Fahad in heaps of 9, both arranging an equal total number. How many heaps did Fatuma and Fahad arrange altogether? A: 7. LCM of 12 and 9 is 36; Fatuma made 36/12 = 3 heaps and Fahad 36/9 = 4 heaps; 3 + 4 = 7.
chunks.source: LCM of 12 and 9 is 36; Fatuma made 36/12 = 3 heaps and Fahad 36/9 = 4 heaps; 3 + 4 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Fatuma arranged apples in heaps of 12 and Fahad in heaps of 9, both arranging an equal total number. What was the total number of apples arranged by the two? A: 72. Each arranged 36 apples (LCM of 12 and 9), so together 36 + 36 = 72.
chunks.source: Each arranged 36 apples (LCM of 12 and 9), so together 36 + 36 = 72.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The area of a square is 144 cm^2. Find the length of each side of the square. A: 12. The square root of 144 is 12, so each side is 12 cm.
chunks.source: The square root of 144 is 12, so each side is 12 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The area of a square is 144 cm^2. Calculate the perimeter of the square. A: 48. Each side is 12 cm; perimeter = 4 x 12 = 48 cm.
chunks.source: Each side is 12 cm; perimeter = 4 x 12 = 48 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the Venn diagram showing prime factors of 24 and B. Find the value of B. A: 108. B = 2^2 x 3^2 x 3^1 = 4 x 9 x 3 = 108.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the Venn diagram showing prime factors of 24 and B. Find the value of A (the overlap). A: 4. The overlap contains 2^2, so A = 4. Check: F24 = 2 x 4 x 3 = 24.
chunks.source: The overlap contains 2^2, so A = 4. Check: F24 = 2 x 4 x 3 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the Venn diagram showing prime factors of 24 and B. Calculate the GCF of 24 and B. A: 12. 24 = 2^3 x 3 and B = 2^2 x 3^3; common factors give 2^2 x 3 = 12.
chunks.source: 24 = 2^3 x 3 and B = 2^2 x 3^3; common factors give 2^2 x 3 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the Venn diagram showing prime factors of 24 and B. Calculate the LCM of 24 and B. A: 216. 24 = 2^3 x 3, B = 2^2 x 3^3; LCM = 2^3 x 3^3 = 8 x 27 = 216.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the smallest number of mangoes that can be shared between 12 girls and 15 boys with no remainder. A: 60. LCM of 12 and 15 is 60.
chunks.source: LCM of 12 and 15 is 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number: 1, 3, 6, 11, 18, _____ A: 29. Differences 2,3,5,7 are prime; next is 11; 18+11=29.
chunks.source: Differences 2,3,5,7 are prime; next is 11; 18+11=29.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: 2/3 + 4/7 A: 26/21. Common denominator 21: 14/21 + 12/21 = 26/21.
chunks.source: Common denominator 21: 14/21 + 12/21 = 26/21.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which of these fractions are equal to 1/2? A: 2/4, 3/6, 4/8. 2/4, 3/6 and 4/8 all simplify to 1/2.
chunks.source: 2/4, 3/6 and 4/8 all simplify to 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: 2/3 x 4/5 A: 8/15. Multiply tops and bottoms: 8/15.
chunks.source: Multiply tops and bottoms: 8/15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A rope is 8 m long. It is cut into small pieces of 0.2 m. How many pieces will be obtained? A: 40. 8 / 0.2 = 40 pieces.
chunks.source: 8 / 0.2 = 40 pieces.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A boy cut his sugar cane into 4 parts. He gave one part to his 3 friends to share equally. What fraction of the sugar cane did each friend get? A: 1/12. 1/4 divided by 3 = 1/12.
chunks.source: 1/4 divided by 3 = 1/12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mugisha ate 2/5 of his cake in the morning, gave half of the remainder to a friend, and ate the rest in the afternoon. What fraction did he eat in the afternoon? A: 3/10. Remainder after morning: 3/5; half given away: 3/10; left for afternoon: 3/10.
chunks.source: Remainder after morning: 3/5; half given away: 3/10; left for afternoon: 3/10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A teacher has 20 blue markers and 15 red ones. Find the ratio of red to blue markers. A: 3:4. 15:20 simplifies to 3:4.
chunks.source: 15:20 simplifies to 3:4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The ratio of rulers to pupils is 2:3. If there are 39 pupils, how many rulers are there? A: 26. 39/3 = 13; 13 x 2 = 26 rulers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Increase sh.1200 in the ratio 4:3. A: 1600. 1200 x 4/3 = 1600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Increase sh.1200 in the ratio 9:4. A: 2700. 1200 x 9/4 = 2700.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Increase sh.1200 in the ratio 5:1. A: 6000. 1200 x 5 = 6000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Decrease 400 kg in the ratio 3:5. A: 240. 400 x 3/5 = 240 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Decrease 400 kg in the ratio 7:10. A: 280. 400 x 7/10 = 280 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Juma, Jimmy and John bought a ball at 24,000/= in the ratio 1:2:3 respectively. How much did each contribute? (Juma, Jimmy, John) A: 4000, 8000, 12000. 6 parts = 24,000; one part = 4,000; so 4,000, 8,000, 12,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: White and black colour are mixed in the ratio 5:2 to make grey. How many kg of black are needed with 25 kg of white? A: 10. 25/5 = 5; 5 x 2 = 10 kg of black.
chunks.source: 25/5 = 5; 5 x 2 = 10 kg of black.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 16 boys can sweep the compound in 5 minutes. How many boys can do the same work in 20 minutes? A: 4. Total work = 16 x 5 = 80 boy-minutes; 80/20 = 4 boys.
chunks.source: Total work = 16 x 5 = 80 boy-minutes; 80/20 = 4 boys.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5% of a number is 120. What is the number? A: 2400. 120/5 = 24; 24 x 100 = 2400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Increase 30 bottles by 10%. A: 33. 10% of 30 = 3; 30 + 3 = 33.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Wele's pay is 24,000/=. He received an increment of 30%. What is his increment? A: 7200. 30% of 24,000 = 7,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A company retrenched 28% of its 280 workers. How many workers were retained? A: 201.6. 72% retained: 0.72 x 280 = 201.6 (the source numbers do not give a whole number).
chunks.source: 72% retained: 0.72 x 280 = 201.6 (the source numbers do not give a whole number).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A mechanic bought a motorcycle at sh.600,000 and sold it at sh.480,000. Find his percentage loss. A: 20. Loss = 120,000; 120,000/600,000 x 100 = 20%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A canteen attendant buys a dozen books at 2400/= and gets a profit of sh.50 from each book. Find her percentage profit on each book. A: 25. Cost per book = 200; 50/200 x 100 = 25%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Wambata borrowed sh.2,400,000 from a bank at 20% per year for 16 months. How much interest did he pay? A: 640000. 2,400,000 x 0.2 x 16/12 = 640,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Wambata borrowed sh.2,400,000 at 20% per year for 16 months. What total amount did he pay to the bank? A: 3040000. 2,400,000 + 640,000 = 3,040,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 5 1/6 to an improper fraction. A: 31/6. (5 x 6 + 1)/6 = 31/6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A father shared one million shillings among Peter, Mark and Solomon in the ratio 1:4:5. How much did Mark and Solomon get altogether? A: 900000. 10 parts = 1,000,000; one part = 100,000; Mark + Solomon = 9 parts = 900,000.
chunks.source: 10 parts = 1,000,000; one part = 100,000; Mark + Solomon = 9 parts = 900,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How much more money did Mark get than Peter? (Ratio 1:4:5 of one million.) A: 300000. Mark - Peter = 3 parts = 300,000.
chunks.source: Mark - Peter = 3 parts = 300,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the numbers: 6, 4, 5, 6, 2, 3, 0 and 6. Find the mode. A: 6. 6 appears most often (3 times), so the mode is 6.
chunks.source: 6 appears most often (3 times), so the mode is 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the numbers: 6, 4, 5, 6, 2, 3, 0 and 6. Find the median. A: 4.5. Arranged: 0,2,3,4,5,6,6,6; median = (4+5)/2 = 4.5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given the numbers: 6, 4, 5, 6, 2, 3, 0 and 6. Find the range. A: 6. Range = 6 - 0 = 6.
chunks.source: Range = 6 - 0 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in ascending order: 6, 4, 5, 6, 2, 3, 0, 6 A: 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6, 6. Smallest to largest: 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6, 6.
chunks.source: Smallest to largest: 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6, 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The median of 5 consecutive positive integers is 12. What are the numbers? A: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. The median is the middle number, so the numbers are 10, 11, 12, 13, 14.
chunks.source: The median is the middle number, so the numbers are 10, 11, 12, 13, 14.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The median of 5 consecutive positive integers is 12. Find their range. A: 4. The numbers are 10 to 14; range = 14 - 10 = 4.
chunks.source: The numbers are 10 to 14; range = 14 - 10 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The average age of 120 pupils in a class is 12 years. What is their total age? A: 1440. Total = average x number = 12 x 120 = 1440 years.
chunks.source: Total = average x number = 12 x 120 = 1440 years.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The average of x, 3x, 7x, 4x and 0 is 6. Find x. A: 2. (15x)/5 = 6; 3x = 6; x = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: John's average mark in 3 tests is 60% and in 2 other tests is 90%. What is his average in the 5 tests? A: 72. (3x60 + 2x90)/5 = 360/5 = 72%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Premier League points: Chelsea 80, Arsenal 73, Man U 72, Man City 70, Liverpool 68, Everton 62. Which club is in first position? A: Chelsea. Chelsea has the most points (80).
chunks.source: Chelsea has the most points (80).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arsenal has 73 points and Everton 62 points. How many more points does Arsenal have than Everton? A: 11. 73 - 62 = 11 points.
chunks.source: 73 - 62 = 11 points.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The number of brothers of 20 pupils: 2 appears 6 times, 3 appears 4 times, 4 appears 5 times, 5 appears 4 times, 6 appears once. Find the mode. A: 2. 2 appears most often (6 times).
chunks.source: 2 appears most often (6 times).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The number of brothers of 20 pupils ranges from 2 to 6. What is the range? A: 4. 6 - 2 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 20 pupils have brothers: six have 2, four have 3, five have 4, four have 5, one has 6. Calculate the mean. A: 3.5. (12+12+20+20+6)/20 = 70/20 = 3.5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The pie chart shows how Mr. James spends sh.15,000 daily: Food 1/5, Savings 3/15, Rent 5/15, Others 4/15. How much does he save daily? A: 3000. 3/15 x 15,000 = 3,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mr. James spends sh.15,000 daily: Food 1/5, Savings 3/15, Rent 5/15, Others 4/15. How much more does he spend on rent than food? A: 2000. (5/15 - 3/15) x 15,000 = 2,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change the savings fraction 3/15 to degrees for a pie chart. A: 72. 3/15 x 360 = 72 degrees.
chunks.source: 3/15 x 360 = 72 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The pie chart shows tribes in Kampala: Baganda 108 degrees, Bakiga 54 degrees, Banyonkole 54 degrees, Basoga y degrees, Others y degrees. Find the value of y. A: 72. 108 + 54 + 54 + 2y = 360; 2y = 144; y = 72.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Kampala has 18 million people. The pie chart shows Baganda 108 degrees. How many are Baganda? A: 5400000. 108/360 x 18,000,000 = 5,400,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Kampala has 18 million people. The pie chart shows Bakiga 54 degrees. How many are Bakiga? A: 2700000. 54/360 x 18,000,000 = 2,700,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Kampala has 18 million people. The pie chart shows Basoga 72 degrees. How many are Basoga? A: 3600000. 72/360 x 18,000,000 = 3,600,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In the Kampala tribes pie chart, Others take up 72 degrees. What fraction represents other tribes? A: 1/5. 72/360 simplifies to 1/5.
chunks.source: 72/360 simplifies to 1/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 30% of phones in Alice's shop are Nokia. What angle represents Nokia on a pie chart? A: 108. 30/100 x 360 = 108 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A farmer has 635 goats, 948 cows and 215 sheep. Find the range of the animals on the farm. A: 733. 948 - 215 = 733.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in descending order: 60, 40, 200 A: 200, 60, 40. Largest to smallest: 200, 60, 40.
chunks.source: Largest to smallest: 200, 60, 40.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The pie chart shows how a man spends sh.360,000: Investment 80 degrees, Medical care 90 degrees, Books 54 degrees, Savings x degrees. Find x. A: 136. 360 - 80 - 90 - 54 = 136 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express the sector for medical care (90 degrees) as a percentage. A: 25. 90/360 x 100 = 25%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How much more money does the man spend on investment (80 degrees) than books (54 degrees) out of sh.360,000? A: 26000. (80-54)/360 x 360,000 = 26,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many 200/= coins make up 4600/=? A: 23. 4600 divided by 200 equals 23.
chunks.source: 4600 divided by 200 equals 23.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the number of 5000/= bank notes that John will pay for a radio that costs sh.90,000. A: 18. 90,000 / 5,000 = 18 notes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Kirimutu has bank notes numbered from RA439619 to RA439718. How many bank notes does he have? A: 100. 439718 - 439619 + 1 = 100 notes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the amount of money in a bundle of sh.1000 notes numbered from KY11100 to KY11199. A: 100000. There are 100 notes (11199 - 11100 + 1); 100 x 1000 = 100,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Sekyanzi picked a bundle of 10,000/= notes numbered PM000260 to PM000289. Notes PM000272 to PM000282 were forged. Find the number of banknotes that were not counterfeit. A: 19. Total 30 notes; forged 11 (282-272+1); 30 - 11 = 19 genuine.
chunks.source: Total 30 notes; forged 11 (282-272+1); 30 - 11 = 19 genuine.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many bank notes were counterfeit in the bundle numbered PM000260 to PM000289 if notes PM000272 to PM000282 were forged? A: 11. 282 - 272 + 1 = 11 notes were forged.
chunks.source: 282 - 272 + 1 = 11 notes were forged.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What was the value of the forged money if 11 counterfeit notes of 10,000/= each were found? A: 110000. 11 x 10,000 = 110,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The cost of 3 pens is 1000/=. How much will I pay for a dozen of such pens? A: 4000. A dozen is 12 pens = 4 sets of 3; 4 x 1000 = 4000.
chunks.source: A dozen is 12 pens = 4 sets of 3; 4 x 1000 = 4000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The cost of a ream of papers is double the price of a text book. How much more do I pay for the ream if the text book costs 7000/=? A: 7000. Ream = 2 x 7000 = 14,000; difference = 14,000 - 7,000 = 7,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Jimmy bought 2.5 kg of cow peas at sh.2000 per kg, 2 tins of charcoal at sh.7000 each, and 500 g of salt at sh.4500 per kg. How much did he spend on all the items? A: 21250. 5000 + 14,000 + 2,250 = 21,250 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Jimmy spent sh.21,250 but had only sh.20,000. How much was his change (negative means short)? A: -1250. 20,000 - 21,250 = -1,250, so he is short by 1,250 shillings.
chunks.source: 20,000 - 21,250 = -1,250, so he is short by 1,250 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study Tim Tom's shopping bill: Sugar costs sh.1200 per kg and the amount paid was sh.4800. What quantity of sugar was bought? A: 4. 4800 / 1200 = 4 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study Tim Tom's shopping bill: 4 kg of millet at sh.1700 per kg. What was the amount? A: 6800. 4 x 1700 = 6800 shillings.
chunks.source: 4 x 1700 = 6800 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study Tim Tom's shopping bill: 1.5 L of paraffin cost sh.18,000. What was the unit price per litre? A: 12000. 18,000 / 1.5 = 12,000 shillings per litre.
chunks.source: 18,000 / 1.5 = 12,000 shillings per litre.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study Tim Tom's shopping bill: 750 g of maize flour at sh.4000 per kg. What was the amount? A: 3000. 750 g = 0.75 kg; 0.75 x 4000 = 3000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study Tim Tom's shopping bill: soap at sh.2000 per bar, amount paid sh.1000. What quantity was bought? A: 0.5. 1000 / 2000 = 0.5 bar (half a bar).
chunks.source: 1000 / 2000 = 0.5 bar (half a bar).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Tim Tom's bill: Sugar 4800, Millet 6800, Paraffin 18000, Maize flour 3000, Soap 1000. What was the total amount? A: 33600. 4800 + 6800 + 18,000 + 3000 + 1000 = 33,600 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The forex bureau sells 1 Euro at 1720 shillings. I have 430,000 shillings. How much do I have in Euros? A: 250. 430,000 / 1720 = 250 Euros.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Johnson sold his phone to an English man at 420 pounds sterling. The bureau buys 1 pound at 2600 shillings. How much did he get in Uganda shillings? A: 1092000. 420 x 2600 = 1,092,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The bureau sells 1 Kenya shilling at 22 Uganda shillings. How much in Uganda shillings does one pay to buy Ksh 170? A: 3740. 170 x 22 = 3740 shillings.
chunks.source: 170 x 22 = 3740 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The bureau sells 1 US dollar at 2000 shillings. How much in Uganda shillings does one pay to buy US $420? A: 840000. 420 x 2000 = 840,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The bureau sells 1 Euro at 1720 shillings. How much in Uganda shillings does one pay to buy Euro 110? A: 189200. 110 x 1720 = 189,200 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A tray of 30 eggs costs sh.9000. How many eggs can one buy with sh.155,100? A: 517. Each egg costs 300; 155,100/300 = 517 eggs.
chunks.source: Each egg costs 300; 155,100/300 = 517 eggs.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A father had two 50,000-shilling notes, five 5,000-shilling notes and ten 500-shilling coins. How much money did he have altogether? A: 130000. 100,000 + 25,000 + 5,000 = 130,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A father had sh.130,000 and bought a watch at sh.56,500. How much money did he remain with? A: 73500. 130,000 - 56,500 = 73,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many minutes are in 2 hours? A: 120. 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 2 hours = 120 minutes.
chunks.source: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 2 hours = 120 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use >, < or = : 12 hours _____ 12000 minutes A: <. 12 hours = 720 minutes, which is less than 12000 minutes.
chunks.source: 12 hours = 720 minutes, which is less than 12000 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use >, < or = : 180 minutes _____ (2 + 1) hours A: =. 2 + 1 = 3 hours = 180 minutes.
chunks.source: 2 + 1 = 3 hours = 180 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use >, < or = : 110 minutes _____ 1100 seconds A: >. 110 minutes = 6600 seconds, which is greater than 1100 seconds.
chunks.source: 110 minutes = 6600 seconds, which is greater than 1100 seconds.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use >, < or = : 3600 seconds _____ 1 hour A: =. 3600 seconds equals exactly 1 hour.
chunks.source: 3600 seconds equals exactly 1 hour.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use >, < or = : 2 days _____ 24 hours A: >. 2 days = 48 hours, which is greater than 24 hours.
chunks.source: 2 days = 48 hours, which is greater than 24 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many hours are there between 3:15 a.m. and 10:30 a.m.? A: 7 hours 15 minutes. From 3:15 to 10:15 is 7 hours, plus 15 more minutes = 7 hours 15 minutes.
chunks.source: From 3:15 to 10:15 is 7 hours, plus 15 more minutes = 7 hours 15 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many hours are there between 11:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.? A: 5. From 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. is 5 hours.
chunks.source: From 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. is 5 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many hours are there between 7:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m.? A: 8. From 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. is 8 hours.
chunks.source: From 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. is 8 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: An examination started at 8:30 a.m. and ended at 10:30 a.m. For how many seconds did the exam last? A: 7200. The exam lasted 2 hours = 120 minutes = 7200 seconds.
chunks.source: The exam lasted 2 hours = 120 minutes = 7200 seconds.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the distance covered by an airplane in 4 hours at 600 km/hr. A: 2400. Distance = speed x time = 600 x 4 = 2400 km.
chunks.source: Distance = speed x time = 600 x 4 = 2400 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Sam takes 40 minutes to cover a distance at a speed of 60 km/hr. How long is the distance he covers? A: 40. 40 minutes = 2/3 hour; distance = 60 x 2/3 = 40 km.
chunks.source: 40 minutes = 2/3 hour; distance = 60 x 2/3 = 40 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A bus moves at a speed of 160 km/hr. What distance does it cover in 1/2 hour? A: 80 km. 160 x 1/2 = 80 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How long will it take a traveller to move a distance of 350 m at a speed of 70 m/hour? A: 5. Time = distance / speed = 350 / 70 = 5 hours.
chunks.source: Time = distance / speed = 350 / 70 = 5 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A car moving at 70 km/hr covers a 350 km journey. How many more hours will it take if its average speed is reduced to 50 km/hr? A: 2. 350/70 = 5 hours; 350/50 = 7 hours; 7 - 5 = 2 more hours.
chunks.source: 350/70 = 5 hours; 350/50 = 7 hours; 7 - 5 = 2 more hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: At what speed should a ship move to reach a landing site 320 km away in 4 hours? A: 80. Speed = distance / time = 320 / 4 = 80 km/hr.
chunks.source: Speed = distance / time = 320 / 4 = 80 km/hr.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Kiprotich took 30 minutes to run a distance of 2 km. What was his average speed in km/hr? A: 4. 30 minutes = 1/2 hour; speed = 2 / 0.5 = 4 km/hr.
chunks.source: 30 minutes = 1/2 hour; speed = 2 / 0.5 = 4 km/hr.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 180 km/hr in m/second. A: 50. 180 km/hr = 180,000 m / 3600 s = 50 m/s.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Convert 20 m/second to km/hr. A: 72. 20 m/s = 20 x 3600 / 1000 = 72 km/hr.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A trip to Entebbe beach took 4 hours at 45 km/hr; the return took 6 hours. Calculate the average speed for the whole journey. A: 36. Distance each way = 180 km; total 360 km in 10 hours; 360/10 = 36 km/hr.
chunks.source: Distance each way = 180 km; total 360 km in 10 hours; 360/10 = 36 km/hr.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the journey graph of the flight from Entebbe to Cape Town. What distance did the plane cover after resting? A: 800. After resting at 1200 km, the plane flew to 2000 km; 2000 - 1200 = 800 km.
chunks.source: After resting at 1200 km, the plane flew to 2000 km; 2000 - 1200 = 800 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the journey graph of the flight from Entebbe to Cape Town. At what time did the plane arrive at Cape Town? A: 2 p.m.. The graph line reaches 2000 km at 2 p.m.
chunks.source: The graph line reaches 2000 km at 2 p.m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the journey graph of the flight from Entebbe to Cape Town. Identify the scale on the vertical axis. A: 200 km. Each division on the vertical axis represents 200 km.
chunks.source: Each division on the vertical axis represents 200 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the journey graph of the flight from Entebbe to Cape Town. What is the distance from Entebbe to Zimbabwe? A: 1200. The plane rested in Zimbabwe at the 1200 km mark.
chunks.source: The plane rested in Zimbabwe at the 1200 km mark.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the journey graph of the flight from Entebbe to Cape Town. Calculate the average speed for the whole journey. A: 333.33. Total distance 2000 km in 6 hours (8 a.m. to 2 p.m.); 2000/6 = 333.33 km/hr.
chunks.source: Total distance 2000 km in 6 hours (8 a.m. to 2 p.m.); 2000/6 = 333.33 km/hr.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Joanita started driving at 8:00 and stopped at 11:00, as shown on the clock faces. Find the time she took driving. A: 3. 11:00 - 8:00 = 3 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The distance between Kibuli and Buwaate is 15 km and Kamuntu takes 45 minutes. At what speed in km/hr does he cover the distance? A: 20. 45 min = 3/4 hr; 15 / 0.75 = 20 km/hr.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Match each measurement to its conversion. A: 2.7 km,2700 m, 2.45 m,245 cm, 4 kg,4000 g, 3217 m,3.217 km. Multiply or divide by 1000 (or 100) as needed.
chunks.source: Multiply or divide by 1000 (or 100) as needed.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Convert 4 km to centimetres. A: 400000. 4 km = 4000 m = 400,000 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 2800 cm to metres. A: 28. 2800 / 100 = 28 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A house fly covered 150 mm. What is this distance in centimetres? A: 15. 150 / 10 = 15 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Convert 7 m^2 to square centimetres. A: 70000. 7 x 10,000 = 70,000 cm^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: 450 kg + 350 g. Give your answer in grams. A: 450350. 450 kg = 450,000 g; 450,000 + 350 = 450,350 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Subtract 150 g from 6 kg. Give your answer in grams. A: 5850. 6 kg = 6000 g; 6000 - 150 = 5850 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 6.045 kg to grams. A: 6045. 6.045 x 1000 = 6045 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A box weighs 56,000 g. What is its weight in kg? A: 56. 56,000 / 1000 = 56 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A container carries 1200 kg of beans. How many packets of 200 g can be poured into the container? A: 6000. 1200 kg = 1,200,000 g; 1,200,000 / 200 = 6000 packets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Naigaga prepares 17,000 millilitres of juice daily. How many 1-litre bottles does she prepare? A: 17. 17,000 ml = 17 litres, so 17 bottles.
chunks.source: 17,000 ml = 17 litres, so 17 bottles.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A bus used 20 1/2 litres of diesel. How many millilitres were they? A: 20500. 20.5 x 1000 = 20,500 ml.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many cups of 250 cm^3 can be obtained from a five litre jerrycan? A: 20. 5 litres = 5000 cm^3; 5000/250 = 20 cups.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: 49 m 65 cm + 30 m 55 cm. A: 80 m 20 cm. 79 m 120 cm = 80 m 20 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many 200 g packets of salt can be got from 3.2 kg of salt? A: 16. 3200/200 = 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The diameter of a circle is 14 cm. Find its circumference. (Use pi = 22/7) A: 44. Circumference = pi x d = 22/7 x 14 = 44 cm.
chunks.source: Circumference = pi x d = 22/7 x 14 = 44 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the area of a circle whose radius is 35 dm? (Take pi = 22/7) A: 3850. Area = pi x r^2 = 22/7 x 35 x 35 = 3850 dm^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In triangle ABC, AB = 12 cm, AC = 16 cm. CE is the altitude to AB with CE = 10 cm. Find the length of the altitude BD to side AC. A: 7.5. Area = 1/2 x 12 x 10 = 60; also = 1/2 x 16 x BD; BD = 120/16 = 7.5 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The volume of a cuboid is 48 litres. Its base is 80 cm by 120 cm. Find the value of x (the height). A: 5. 48 litres = 48,000 cm^3; x = 48,000/(80x120) = 5 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A cuboid is 80 cm by 120 cm by 5 cm. Calculate the total surface area. A: 21200. 2(80x120 + 80x5 + 120x5) = 2(9600+400+600) = 21,200 cm^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A box B measures 32 cm by 18 cm by 25 cm. How many 3 cm cubes (C) can be packed in box B? A: 480. 10 x 6 x 8 = 480 cubes fit along each side.
chunks.source: 10 x 6 x 8 = 480 cubes fit along each side.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A box B measures 32 cm by 18 cm by 25 cm. How many layers of 3 cm cubes can be made in box B? A: 8. 25/3 = 8 full layers.
chunks.source: 25/3 = 8 full layers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Calculate the area of the L-shaped figure below. (Left column 5 cm wide; top-right part 5 cm wide and 2 cm tall; step down 4 cm.) A: 40. Big rectangle 10x6 = 60 minus the missing 5x4 = 20; 60 - 20 = 40 cm^2.
chunks.source: Big rectangle 10x6 = 60 minus the missing 5x4 = 20; 60 - 20 = 40 cm^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the area of the shaded part. The outer rectangle is 10 m by 8 m and the inner white rectangle is 6 m by 5 m. A: 50. Outer 80 minus inner 30 = 50 m^2.
chunks.source: Outer 80 minus inner 30 = 50 m^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out the perimeter of the outer rectangular figure (10 m by 8 m). A: 36. 2 x (10 + 8) = 36 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Calculate the area of the whole rectangular figure (10 m by 8 m). A: 80. 10 x 8 = 80 m^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which of these angles are acute? A: 30 degrees, 45 degrees, 60 degrees. Acute angles are less than 90 degrees.
chunks.source: Acute angles are less than 90 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: From the cuboid ABCDEFGH below, identify one pair of skew lines. A: AB and CG. AB and CG never meet and are not parallel, so they are skew.
chunks.source: AB and CG never meet and are not parallel, so they are skew.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the value of y. (A straight line with 40 degrees, y degrees and a right angle between two rays.) A: 50. 40 + 90 + y = 180; y = 50.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In the isosceles triangle, the base angles are (x+40) degrees and 2(x+5) degrees. Find the value of the angle marked K at the apex. A: 40. x + 40 = 2(x + 5) gives x = 30; base angles are 70 each; K = 180 - 140 = 40.
chunks.source: x + 40 = 2(x + 5) gives x = 30; base angles are 70 each; K = 180 - 140 = 40.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Two parallel lines are cut by a zigzag. The given angles are 40 degrees and 30 degrees. What is the value of W at the bend? A: 70. Draw a line through the bend parallel to the two lines; W = 40 + 30 = 70.
chunks.source: Draw a line through the bend parallel to the two lines; W = 40 + 30 = 70.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the isosceles triangle with base extended to form an exterior angle of 120 degrees. Find angle Q. A: 60. The interior base angle r = 180 - 120 = 60; the triangle is isosceles, so Q = r = 60.
chunks.source: The interior base angle r = 180 - 120 = 60; the triangle is isosceles, so Q = r = 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. The marked angle at the top is 120 degrees and 3y is the angle on the same side below. Find y. A: 20. 3y and 120 are supplementary (same-side); 3y = 60; y = 20.
chunks.source: 3y and 120 are supplementary (same-side); 3y = 60; y = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The interior angle of a regular polygon is twice its exterior angle. Find its interior angle sum. A: 720. Exterior = 60, so 6 sides; sum = (6-2) x 180 = 720.
chunks.source: Exterior = 60, so 6 sides; sum = (6-2) x 180 = 720.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The exterior angle of a regular polygon is 40 degrees. What is its interior angle sum? A: 1260. Sides = 360/40 = 9; sum = (9-2) x 180 = 1260.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The interior angle of a regular polygon is 120 more than its exterior angle. Calculate the exterior angle. A: 30. Let exterior = e; e + (e + 120) = 180; e = 30.
chunks.source: Let exterior = e; e + (e + 120) = 180; e = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The interior angle of a regular polygon is 120 more than its exterior angle. How many sides has the polygon? A: 12. Exterior = 30; sides = 360/30 = 12.
chunks.source: Exterior = 30; sides = 360/30 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The interior angle of a regular polygon is 120 more than its exterior angle. Work out its interior angle sum. A: 1800. 12 sides; (12-2) x 180 = 1800.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Two parallel lines with a triangle between them: the bottom angle is 120 degrees. Find X (alternate interior angle at the top). A: 60. The interior base angle is 180 - 120 = 60; X is alternate interior to it, so X = 60.
chunks.source: The interior base angle is 180 - 120 = 60; X is alternate interior to it, so X = 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A ladder 10 m long leans against a wall with its foot 8 m from the wall. What is the height of the wall? A: 6. h^2 + 8^2 = 10^2; h^2 = 36; h = 6 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that (x + 40) degrees and 2(x + 5) degrees are supplementary angles. Find the value of x. A: 43.33. 3x + 50 = 180; 3x = 130; x = 130/3 = 43.33.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Two parallel rays stand on a horizontal line. The angles at the left ray are 3x (outside) and 2x (inside). Find x. A: 36. 3x + 2x = 180; x = 36.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the value of y in the zigzag figure between two parallel lines (120 degrees on the left, 130 degrees on the right). A: 110. Draw a line through the peak parallel to both; y = (180-120) + (180-130) = 110.
chunks.source: Draw a line through the peak parallel to both; y = (180-120) + (180-130) = 110.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the polygon whose interior angle sum is 1080 degrees. A: octagon. (n-2) x 180 = 1080; n = 8, an octagon.
chunks.source: (n-2) x 180 = 1080; n = 8, an octagon.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In the triangle, the apex is 60 degrees, the left base angle is 40 degrees, and the exterior angle at the right base is 2x. Find x. A: 50. Exterior angle = sum of opposite interiors: 2x = 100; x = 50.
chunks.source: Exterior angle = sum of opposite interiors: 2x = 100; x = 50.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The area of a triangular garden is 60 m^2. If the base is 12 m, find the height. A: 10. Height = 2 x 60 / 12 = 10 m.
chunks.source: Height = 2 x 60 / 12 = 10 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the value of angle marked y in the isosceles triangle with apex 50 degrees. A: 65. Base angles are equal: (180 - 50)/2 = 65 degrees.
chunks.source: Base angles are equal: (180 - 50)/2 = 65 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the cuboid 8 cm by 6 cm by 5 cm. Find the perimeter of the shaded base. A: 28. 2 x (8 + 6) = 28 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the total surface area of the cuboid 8 cm by 6 cm by 5 cm. A: 236. 2(48 + 40 + 30) = 236 cm^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Temperatures for 5 days: -3, 0, +1, -4, +5 degrees C. Find the range. A: 9. 5 - (-4) = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Identify the integer shown by the arrow on the number line below. (Arrow from +5 pointing left to +2.) A: 2. The arrowhead lands on +2.
chunks.source: The arrowhead lands on +2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write down the mathematical sentence shown on the number line below. (Start at -11, four jumps of +3.) A: -11 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 1. Start at -11 and add 3 four times to reach +1.
chunks.source: Start at -11 and add 3 four times to reach +1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the number line: arrow X goes from -4 to +4. Identify the integer at the arrowhead of X. A: 4. The arrowhead of X lands on +4.
chunks.source: The arrowhead of X lands on +4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the number line: arrow Y goes from -1 to -4. Identify the integer at the arrowhead of Y. A: -4. The arrowhead of Y lands on -4.
chunks.source: The arrowhead of Y lands on -4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the number line: arrow Z goes from +1 to -1. Identify the integer at the arrowhead of Z. A: -1. The arrowhead of Z lands on -1.
chunks.source: The arrowhead of Z lands on -1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Study the number line: dashed arrow k goes from +1 to +4. Identify the integer at the arrowhead of k. A: 4. The arrowhead of k lands on +4.
chunks.source: The arrowhead of k lands on +4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve and give the solution set: 2y > 4 A: y > 2. Divide both sides by 2: y > 2.
chunks.source: Divide both sides by 2: y > 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The temperature on top of a mountain was 3 degrees C at noon. It dropped by 10 degrees C. What was the final temperature? A: -7. 3 - 10 = -7 degrees C.
chunks.source: 3 - 10 = -7 degrees C.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve: n - - 7 = 7 A: 0. n + 7 = 7, so n = 0.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve: 2x < 6 A: x < 3. Divide both sides by 2: x < 3.
chunks.source: Divide both sides by 2: x < 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the following integers in ascending order: -2, 4, 8, 3, -1, 0 A: -2, -1, 0, 3, 4, 8. From smallest to largest: -2, -1, 0, 3, 4, 8.
chunks.source: From smallest to largest: -2, -1, 0, 3, 4, 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use >, < or = to compare: -3 _____ +1 A: <. -3 is less than +1.
chunks.source: -3 is less than +1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Arrange in ascending order: -2, +3, +4, -4, -5, +2 A: -5, -4, -2, +2, +3, +4. From smallest to largest: -5, -4, -2, +2, +3, +4.
chunks.source: From smallest to largest: -5, -4, -2, +2, +3, +4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve: -3x + 5 < 8 and give the solution set. A: x > -1. -3x < 3; dividing by -3 flips the sign: x > -1.
chunks.source: -3x < 3; dividing by -3 flips the sign: x > -1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out +4 - +7 using a number line. A: -3. Start at +4, move 7 left to reach -3.
chunks.source: Start at +4, move 7 left to reach -3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: I think of a number, multiply it by 4 and subtract 5; the result is greater than 3. Find the least possible whole number. A: 3. 4n - 5 > 3; 4n > 8; n > 2; the least whole number is 3.
chunks.source: 4n - 5 > 3; 4n > 8; n > 2; the least whole number is 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Hailstone -50 degrees C, water 24 degrees C. What is the difference? A: 74. 24 - (-50) = 74.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In an interview, 3 points are awarded for every correct answer and 2 points subtracted for each wrong answer. There were 10 questions. What was the final score for one who answered 7 correctly? A: 15. 7 x 3 = 21; 3 x 2 = 6; 21 - 6 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The sum of 4 consecutive integers is 46. Find the numbers. A: 10, 11, 12, 13. 46/4 = 11.5, the middle; the numbers are 10, 11, 12, 13.
chunks.source: 46/4 = 11.5, the middle; the numbers are 10, 11, 12, 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the number line: arrow b goes from 0 to +6 and dashed arrow c goes from +6 to -5. Write the integer for arrow c. A: -11. Arrow c jumps 11 to the left: -11.
chunks.source: Arrow c jumps 11 to the left: -11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Use the number line: arrow b goes from 0 to +6. Write the integer for arrow b. A: 6. Arrow b jumps 6 to the right: +6.
chunks.source: Arrow b jumps 6 to the right: +6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the subtraction statement for the arrows: from +6 subtract 11 to reach -5. A: 6 - 11 = -5. Start at +6, subtract 11, land at -5.
chunks.source: Start at +6, subtract 11, land at -5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve: p - 2 = 4 A: 6. Add 2 to both sides: p = 6.
chunks.source: Add 2 to both sides: p = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If x = 2, find the value of 5 - 2x A: 1. 5 - 2(2) = 5 - 4 = 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Remove the brackets: 4(1 - 3b) A: 4 - 12b. Multiply each term inside by 4: 4 - 12b.
chunks.source: Multiply each term inside by 4: 4 - 12b.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Simplify: 2b + 4a + b - 2a A: 2a + 3b. Combine a terms: 4a - 2a = 2a; combine b terms: 2b + b = 3b.
chunks.source: Combine a terms: 4a - 2a = 2a; combine b terms: 2b + b = 3b.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve: x - 3 = 5 A: 8. Add 3 to both sides: x = 8.
chunks.source: Add 3 to both sides: x = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If a = 2, b = 1 and c = 1/2, calculate ab/c. A: 4. (2 x 1) / (1/2) = 2 x 2 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the value of (bc + ac)/a given that a = 1, b = 0 and c = 3. A: 3. (0 + 3)/1 = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Simplify: 3x - (2 + x) A: 2x - 2. 3x - 2 - x = 2x - 2.

chunks.subject: Math
