chunks.text: Q: The figure is a rectangle with length (2x+1) cm and width (x+3) cm (opposite sides equal). The other width is marked (2x-1) cm. Find the perimeter. A: 16. 2x + 1 = x + 3 gives x = 2; sides 5 cm and 3 cm; perimeter = 16 cm.
chunks.source: 2x + 1 = x + 3 gives x = 2; sides 5 cm and 3 cm; perimeter = 16 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The figure is a rectangle with length (2x+1) cm and width (x+3) cm (opposite sides equal). Find its area. A: 15. x = 2; area = 5 x 3 = 15 cm^2.
chunks.source: x = 2; area = 5 x 3 = 15 cm^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Kirya is 3 times as old as his daughter. Their ages add up to 72 years. How old is the daughter? A: 18. Let the daughter be x: x + 3x = 72; x = 18.
chunks.source: Let the daughter be x: x + 3x = 72; x = 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In the triangle, the altitude to the 12 cm base is 6 cm, and the altitude to side x is 8 cm. Find x. A: 9. Area = 1/2 x 12 x 6 = 36 = 1/2 x 8x; x = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The isosceles triangle has equal sides (2x-2) cm and (x+4) cm. Find x. A: 6. 2x - 2 = x + 4; x = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A parent bought three bags at sh.K, sh.(K-600) and sh.2K. Write an algebraic expression for the total cost. A: 4K - 600. K + (K - 600) + 2K = 4K - 600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If K = sh.1650, find the total cost of the three bags (expression 4K - 600). A: 6000. 4 x 1650 - 600 = 6000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that P = {vowel letters}. Find the number of subsets that can be formed from set P. A: 32. P has 5 members; subsets = 2^5 = 32.
chunks.source: P has 5 members; subsets = 2^5 = 32.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given n(A) = 15, n(B) = 25 and n(A intersect B) = 5: how many members are in A only? A: 10. 15 - 5 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write 409,049 in words. A: Four hundred nine thousand, forty-nine. 409,049 = four hundred nine thousand, forty-nine.
chunks.source: 409,049 = four hundred nine thousand, forty-nine.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Subtract 102_five from 242_five, and give your answer in base ten. A: 45. 242_five = 72 and 102_five = 27 in base ten; 72 - 27 = 45.
chunks.source: 242_five = 72 and 102_five = 27 in base ten; 72 - 27 = 45.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What number has been expanded as (5 x 10^1) + (8 x 10^0) + (3 x 10^-1)? A: 58.3. 50 + 8 + 0.3 = 58.3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write 58.3 in words. A: fifty-eight point three. 58.3 = fifty-eight point three.
chunks.source: 58.3 = fifty-eight point three.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Add: 416 + 22 A: 438. Add the two numbers: 416 + 22 = 438.
chunks.source: Add the two numbers: 416 + 22 = 438.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Subtract: 754 - 239 A: 515. 754 minus 239 equals 515.
chunks.source: 754 minus 239 equals 515.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What is the difference between 268 and 143? A: 125. Difference means subtraction: 268 - 143 = 125.
chunks.source: Difference means subtraction: 268 - 143 = 125.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Simplify: 3 + 4 x 2 A: 11. Multiply first: 4 x 2 = 8, then add: 3 + 8 = 11.
chunks.source: Multiply first: 4 x 2 = 8, then add: 3 + 8 = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is At a party 4896 people were each served with a bottle of soda. If each crate of soda contains 24 bottles, how many crates of soda were served? A: 204. 4896 divided by 24 equals 204 crates.
chunks.source: 4896 divided by 24 equals 204 crates.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Each crate of soda costs sh.24,000. 204 crates were served at a party. How much money was used to buy all the crates? A: 4896000. 204 x 24,000 = 4,896,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Patrick had 20 coins of sh.500 and 65 coins of sh.200 in his saving box. If he wanted 1000-shilling notes from the total amount, how many notes would he get? A: 23. 20 x 500 = 10,000 and 65 x 200 = 13,000; total 23,000; 23,000 / 1,000 = 23 notes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is There are 30 eggs in one tray. How many trays will be required to pack 330 eggs? A: 11. 330 divided by 30 equals 11 trays.
chunks.source: 330 divided by 30 equals 11 trays.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A radio uses batteries of 1.5 volts. For the radio to work, it requires 12 volts. How many such batteries will the radio require? A: 8. 12 divided by 1.5 equals 8 batteries.
chunks.source: 12 divided by 1.5 equals 8 batteries.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A pair of batteries costs sh.1,000. How much money is needed to buy 8 batteries? A: 4000. 8 batteries = 4 pairs; 4 x 1,000 = 4,000 shillings.
chunks.source: 8 batteries = 4 pairs; 4 x 1,000 = 4,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A taxi carries 14 passengers while a bus carries 59 passengers. If the two vehicles make two journeys each, how many passengers will they carry altogether? A: 146. (14 + 59) x 2 = 73 x 2 = 146 passengers.
chunks.source: (14 + 59) x 2 = 73 x 2 = 146 passengers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A bus left Kampala for Masaka with 60 passengers. At Mpigi 15 got out, at Buwama 8 boarded, and at Lukaya 12 got out. How many passengers reached Masaka? A: 41. 60 - 15 + 8 - 12 = 41 passengers.
chunks.source: 60 - 15 + 8 - 12 = 41 passengers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 41 passengers reached Masaka town, each paying sh.8,000. How much money was collected? A: 328000. 41 x 8,000 = 328,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the number line to multiply: 3 x 2 = A: 6. 3 x 2 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Peter had three silos of 124016 kg, 31419 kg and 214602 kg of beans. How many kg did he have altogether? A: 370037. 124016 + 31419 + 214602 = 370037 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 2, 3, 5, 7, ____?__ A: 11. These are prime numbers in order; the next prime after 7 is 11.
chunks.source: These are prime numbers in order; the next prime after 7 is 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The sum of 3 consecutive counting numbers is 63. Find the numbers. A: 20, 21, 22. 63 / 3 = 21, the middle number; the numbers are 20, 21, 22.
chunks.source: 63 / 3 = 21, the middle number; the numbers are 20, 21, 22.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The sum of 3 consecutive counting numbers is 63. Work out the range of the numbers. A: 2. The numbers are 20, 21, 22; range = 22 - 20 = 2.
chunks.source: The numbers are 20, 21, 22; range = 22 - 20 = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The LCM of two numbers is 120. Their GCF is 10. One of the numbers is 40. Find the other number. A: 30. LCM x GCF = product of the numbers: 120 x 10 = 1200; 1200 / 40 = 30.
chunks.source: LCM x GCF = product of the numbers: 120 x 10 = 1200; 1200 / 40 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A bell rings every 30 minutes and another every 40 minutes. They ring together at 8:45 a.m. After how many hours will they ring together again? A: 2. LCM of 30 and 40 is 120 minutes, which is 2 hours.
chunks.source: LCM of 30 and 40 is 120 minutes, which is 2 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A bell rings every 30 minutes and another every 40 minutes. They ring together at 8:45 a.m. At what time will they ring together again? A: 10:45 a.m.. They ring together every 2 hours, so next at 8:45 + 2 hours = 10:45 a.m.
chunks.source: They ring together every 2 hours, so next at 8:45 + 2 hours = 10:45 a.m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Fatuma arranged apples in heaps of 12 and Fahad in heaps of 9, both arranging an equal total number. How many heaps did Fatuma and Fahad arrange altogether? A: 7. LCM of 12 and 9 is 36; Fatuma made 36/12 = 3 heaps and Fahad 36/9 = 4 heaps; 3 + 4 = 7.
chunks.source: LCM of 12 and 9 is 36; Fatuma made 36/12 = 3 heaps and Fahad 36/9 = 4 heaps; 3 + 4 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Fatuma arranged apples in heaps of 12 and Fahad in heaps of 9, both arranging an equal total number. What was the total number of apples arranged by the two? A: 72. Each arranged 36 apples (LCM of 12 and 9), so together 36 + 36 = 72.
chunks.source: Each arranged 36 apples (LCM of 12 and 9), so together 36 + 36 = 72.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The area of a square is 144 cm^2. Find the length of each side of the square. A: 12. The square root of 144 is 12, so each side is 12 cm.
chunks.source: The square root of 144 is 12, so each side is 12 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The area of a square is 144 cm^2. Calculate the perimeter of the square. A: 48. Each side is 12 cm; perimeter = 4 x 12 = 48 cm.
chunks.source: Each side is 12 cm; perimeter = 4 x 12 = 48 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the Venn diagram showing prime factors of 24 and B. Find the value of B. A: 108. B = 2^2 x 3^2 x 3^1 = 4 x 9 x 3 = 108.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the Venn diagram showing prime factors of 24 and B. Find the value of A (the overlap). A: 4. The overlap contains 2^2, so A = 4. Check: F24 = 2 x 4 x 3 = 24.
chunks.source: The overlap contains 2^2, so A = 4. Check: F24 = 2 x 4 x 3 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the Venn diagram showing prime factors of 24 and B. Calculate the GCF of 24 and B. A: 12. 24 = 2^3 x 3 and B = 2^2 x 3^3; common factors give 2^2 x 3 = 12.
chunks.source: 24 = 2^3 x 3 and B = 2^2 x 3^3; common factors give 2^2 x 3 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the Venn diagram showing prime factors of 24 and B. Calculate the LCM of 24 and B. A: 216. 24 = 2^3 x 3, B = 2^2 x 3^3; LCM = 2^3 x 3^3 = 8 x 27 = 216.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the smallest number of mangoes that can be shared between 12 girls and 15 boys with no remainder. A: 60. LCM of 12 and 15 is 60.
chunks.source: LCM of 12 and 15 is 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 2/3 + 4/7 A: 26/21. Common denominator 21: 14/21 + 12/21 = 26/21.
chunks.source: Common denominator 21: 14/21 + 12/21 = 26/21.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 2/3 x 4/5 A: 8/15. Multiply tops and bottoms: 8/15.
chunks.source: Multiply tops and bottoms: 8/15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 3/4 divided by 9/8 A: 2/3. 3/4 x 8/9 = 24/36 = 2/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A rope is 8 m long. It is cut into small pieces of 0.2 m. How many pieces will be obtained? A: 40. 8 / 0.2 = 40 pieces.
chunks.source: 8 / 0.2 = 40 pieces.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A boy cut his sugar cane into 4 parts. He gave one part to his 3 friends to share equally. What fraction of the sugar cane did each friend get? A: 1/12. 1/4 divided by 3 = 1/12.
chunks.source: 1/4 divided by 3 = 1/12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mugisha ate 2/5 of his cake in the morning, gave half of the remainder to a friend, and ate the rest in the afternoon. What fraction did he eat in the afternoon? A: 3/10. Remainder after morning: 3/5; half given away: 3/10; left for afternoon: 3/10.
chunks.source: Remainder after morning: 3/5; half given away: 3/10; left for afternoon: 3/10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A teacher has 20 blue markers and 15 red ones. Find the ratio of red to blue markers. A: 3:4. 15:20 simplifies to 3:4.
chunks.source: 15:20 simplifies to 3:4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The ratio of rulers to pupils is 2:3. If there are 39 pupils, how many rulers are there? A: 26. 39/3 = 13; 13 x 2 = 26 rulers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Increase sh.1200 in the ratio 4:3. A: 1600. 1200 x 4/3 = 1600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Increase sh.1200 in the ratio 9:4. A: 2700. 1200 x 9/4 = 2700.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Increase sh.1200 in the ratio 5:1. A: 6000. 1200 x 5 = 6000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Decrease 400 kg in the ratio 3:5. A: 240. 400 x 3/5 = 240 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Decrease 400 kg in the ratio 7:10. A: 280. 400 x 7/10 = 280 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Juma, Jimmy and John bought a ball at 24,000/= in the ratio 1:2:3 respectively. How much did each contribute? (Juma, Jimmy, John) A: 4000, 8000, 12000. 6 parts = 24,000; one part = 4,000; so 4,000, 8,000, 12,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is White and black colour are mixed in the ratio 5:2 to make grey. How many kg of black are needed with 25 kg of white? A: 10. 25/5 = 5; 5 x 2 = 10 kg of black.
chunks.source: 25/5 = 5; 5 x 2 = 10 kg of black.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 16 boys can sweep the compound in 5 minutes. How many boys can do the same work in 20 minutes? A: 4. Total work = 16 x 5 = 80 boy-minutes; 80/20 = 4 boys.
chunks.source: Total work = 16 x 5 = 80 boy-minutes; 80/20 = 4 boys.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 5% of a number is 120. What is the number? A: 2400. 120/5 = 24; 24 x 100 = 2400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Increase 30 bottles by 10%. A: 33. 10% of 30 = 3; 30 + 3 = 33.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Wele's pay is 24,000/=. He received an increment of 30%. What is his increment? A: 7200. 30% of 24,000 = 7,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A company retrenched 28% of its 280 workers. How many workers were retained? A: 201.6. 72% retained: 0.72 x 280 = 201.6 (the source numbers do not give a whole number).
chunks.source: 72% retained: 0.72 x 280 = 201.6 (the source numbers do not give a whole number).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A mechanic bought a motorcycle at sh.600,000 and sold it at sh.480,000. Find his percentage loss. A: 20. Loss = 120,000; 120,000/600,000 x 100 = 20%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A canteen attendant buys a dozen books at 2400/= and gets a profit of sh.50 from each book. Find her percentage profit on each book. A: 25. Cost per book = 200; 50/200 x 100 = 25%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Wambata borrowed sh.2,400,000 from a bank at 20% per year for 16 months. How much interest did he pay? A: 640000. 2,400,000 x 0.2 x 16/12 = 640,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Wambata borrowed sh.2,400,000 at 20% per year for 16 months. What total amount did he pay to the bank? A: 3040000. 2,400,000 + 640,000 = 3,040,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Change 5 1/6 to an improper fraction. A: 31/6. (5 x 6 + 1)/6 = 31/6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A father shared one million shillings among Peter, Mark and Solomon in the ratio 1:4:5. How much did Mark and Solomon get altogether? A: 900000. 10 parts = 1,000,000; one part = 100,000; Mark + Solomon = 9 parts = 900,000.
chunks.source: 10 parts = 1,000,000; one part = 100,000; Mark + Solomon = 9 parts = 900,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How much more money did Mark get than Peter? (Ratio 1:4:5 of one million.) A: 300000. Mark - Peter = 3 parts = 300,000.
chunks.source: Mark - Peter = 3 parts = 300,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the numbers: 6, 4, 5, 6, 2, 3, 0 and 6. Find the mode. A: 6. 6 appears most often (3 times), so the mode is 6.
chunks.source: 6 appears most often (3 times), so the mode is 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the numbers: 6, 4, 5, 6, 2, 3, 0 and 6. Find the median. A: 4.5. Arranged: 0,2,3,4,5,6,6,6; median = (4+5)/2 = 4.5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given the numbers: 6, 4, 5, 6, 2, 3, 0 and 6. Find the range. A: 6. Range = 6 - 0 = 6.
chunks.source: Range = 6 - 0 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The median of 5 consecutive positive integers is 12. What are the numbers? A: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. The median is the middle number, so the numbers are 10, 11, 12, 13, 14.
chunks.source: The median is the middle number, so the numbers are 10, 11, 12, 13, 14.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The median of 5 consecutive positive integers is 12. Find their range. A: 4. The numbers are 10 to 14; range = 14 - 10 = 4.
chunks.source: The numbers are 10 to 14; range = 14 - 10 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find Lucy's mean mark: MTC 80%, ENG 60%, SST 20%, SCIE 40%. A: 50. (80+60+20+40)/4 = 200/4 = 50%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The average age of 120 pupils in a class is 12 years. What is their total age? A: 1440. Total = average x number = 12 x 120 = 1440 years.
chunks.source: Total = average x number = 12 x 120 = 1440 years.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The average of x, 3x, 7x, 4x and 0 is 6. Find x. A: 2. (15x)/5 = 6; 3x = 6; x = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is John's average mark in 3 tests is 60% and in 2 other tests is 90%. What is his average in the 5 tests? A: 72. (3x60 + 2x90)/5 = 360/5 = 72%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Arsenal has 73 points and Everton 62 points. How many more points does Arsenal have than Everton? A: 11. 73 - 62 = 11 points.
chunks.source: 73 - 62 = 11 points.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The number of brothers of 20 pupils: 2 appears 6 times, 3 appears 4 times, 4 appears 5 times, 5 appears 4 times, 6 appears once. Find the mode. A: 2. 2 appears most often (6 times).
chunks.source: 2 appears most often (6 times).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The number of brothers of 20 pupils ranges from 2 to 6. What is the range? A: 4. 6 - 2 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 20 pupils have brothers: six have 2, four have 3, five have 4, four have 5, one has 6. Calculate the mean. A: 3.5. (12+12+20+20+6)/20 = 70/20 = 3.5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The pie chart shows how Mr. James spends sh.15,000 daily: Food 1/5, Savings 3/15, Rent 5/15, Others 4/15. How much does he save daily? A: 3000. 3/15 x 15,000 = 3,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Mr. James spends sh.15,000 daily: Food 1/5, Savings 3/15, Rent 5/15, Others 4/15. How much more does he spend on rent than food? A: 2000. (5/15 - 3/15) x 15,000 = 2,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Change the savings fraction 3/15 to degrees for a pie chart. A: 72. 3/15 x 360 = 72 degrees.
chunks.source: 3/15 x 360 = 72 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The pie chart shows tribes in Kampala: Baganda 108 degrees, Bakiga 54 degrees, Banyonkole 54 degrees, Basoga y degrees, Others y degrees. Find the value of y. A: 72. 108 + 54 + 54 + 2y = 360; 2y = 144; y = 72.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Kampala has 18 million people. The pie chart shows Baganda 108 degrees. How many are Baganda? A: 5400000. 108/360 x 18,000,000 = 5,400,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Kampala has 18 million people. The pie chart shows Bakiga 54 degrees. How many are Bakiga? A: 2700000. 54/360 x 18,000,000 = 2,700,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Kampala has 18 million people. The pie chart shows Basoga 72 degrees. How many are Basoga? A: 3600000. 72/360 x 18,000,000 = 3,600,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In the Kampala tribes pie chart, Others take up 72 degrees. What fraction represents other tribes? A: 1/5. 72/360 simplifies to 1/5.
chunks.source: 72/360 simplifies to 1/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 30% of phones in Alice's shop are Nokia. What angle represents Nokia on a pie chart? A: 108. 30/100 x 360 = 108 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A farmer has 635 goats, 948 cows and 215 sheep. Find the range of the animals on the farm. A: 733. 948 - 215 = 733.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The pie chart shows how a man spends sh.360,000: Investment 80 degrees, Medical care 90 degrees, Books 54 degrees, Savings x degrees. Find x. A: 136. 360 - 80 - 90 - 54 = 136 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Express the sector for medical care (90 degrees) as a percentage. A: 25. 90/360 x 100 = 25%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How much more money does the man spend on investment (80 degrees) than books (54 degrees) out of sh.360,000? A: 26000. (80-54)/360 x 360,000 = 26,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many 200/= coins make up 4600/=? A: 23. 4600 divided by 200 equals 23.
chunks.source: 4600 divided by 200 equals 23.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the number of 5000/= bank notes that John will pay for a radio that costs sh.90,000. A: 18. 90,000 / 5,000 = 18 notes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Kirimutu has bank notes numbered from RA439619 to RA439718. How many bank notes does he have? A: 100. 439718 - 439619 + 1 = 100 notes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the amount of money in a bundle of sh.1000 notes numbered from KY11100 to KY11199. A: 100000. There are 100 notes (11199 - 11100 + 1); 100 x 1000 = 100,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Sekyanzi picked a bundle of 10,000/= notes numbered PM000260 to PM000289. Notes PM000272 to PM000282 were forged. Find the number of banknotes that were not counterfeit. A: 19. Total 30 notes; forged 11 (282-272+1); 30 - 11 = 19 genuine.
chunks.source: Total 30 notes; forged 11 (282-272+1); 30 - 11 = 19 genuine.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many bank notes were counterfeit in the bundle numbered PM000260 to PM000289 if notes PM000272 to PM000282 were forged? A: 11. 282 - 272 + 1 = 11 notes were forged.
chunks.source: 282 - 272 + 1 = 11 notes were forged.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What was the value of the forged money if 11 counterfeit notes of 10,000/= each were found? A: 110000. 11 x 10,000 = 110,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The cost of 3 pens is 1000/=. How much will I pay for a dozen of such pens? A: 4000. A dozen is 12 pens = 4 sets of 3; 4 x 1000 = 4000.
chunks.source: A dozen is 12 pens = 4 sets of 3; 4 x 1000 = 4000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The cost of a ream of papers is double the price of a text book. How much more do I pay for the ream if the text book costs 7000/=? A: 7000. Ream = 2 x 7000 = 14,000; difference = 14,000 - 7,000 = 7,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Jimmy bought 2.5 kg of cow peas at sh.2000 per kg, 2 tins of charcoal at sh.7000 each, and 500 g of salt at sh.4500 per kg. How much did he spend on all the items? A: 21250. 5000 + 14,000 + 2,250 = 21,250 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Jimmy spent sh.21,250 but had only sh.20,000. How much was his change (negative means short)? A: -1250. 20,000 - 21,250 = -1,250, so he is short by 1,250 shillings.
chunks.source: 20,000 - 21,250 = -1,250, so he is short by 1,250 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study Tim Tom's shopping bill: Sugar costs sh.1200 per kg and the amount paid was sh.4800. What quantity of sugar was bought? A: 4. 4800 / 1200 = 4 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study Tim Tom's shopping bill: 4 kg of millet at sh.1700 per kg. What was the amount? A: 6800. 4 x 1700 = 6800 shillings.
chunks.source: 4 x 1700 = 6800 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study Tim Tom's shopping bill: 1.5 L of paraffin cost sh.18,000. What was the unit price per litre? A: 12000. 18,000 / 1.5 = 12,000 shillings per litre.
chunks.source: 18,000 / 1.5 = 12,000 shillings per litre.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study Tim Tom's shopping bill: 750 g of maize flour at sh.4000 per kg. What was the amount? A: 3000. 750 g = 0.75 kg; 0.75 x 4000 = 3000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study Tim Tom's shopping bill: soap at sh.2000 per bar, amount paid sh.1000. What quantity was bought? A: 0.5. 1000 / 2000 = 0.5 bar (half a bar).
chunks.source: 1000 / 2000 = 0.5 bar (half a bar).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Tim Tom's bill: Sugar 4800, Millet 6800, Paraffin 18000, Maize flour 3000, Soap 1000. What was the total amount? A: 33600. 4800 + 6800 + 18,000 + 3000 + 1000 = 33,600 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The forex bureau sells 1 Euro at 1720 shillings. I have 430,000 shillings. How much do I have in Euros? A: 250. 430,000 / 1720 = 250 Euros.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Johnson sold his phone to an English man at 420 pounds sterling. The bureau buys 1 pound at 2600 shillings. How much did he get in Uganda shillings? A: 1092000. 420 x 2600 = 1,092,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The bureau sells 1 Kenya shilling at 22 Uganda shillings. How much in Uganda shillings does one pay to buy Ksh 170? A: 3740. 170 x 22 = 3740 shillings.
chunks.source: 170 x 22 = 3740 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The bureau sells 1 US dollar at 2000 shillings. How much in Uganda shillings does one pay to buy US $420? A: 840000. 420 x 2000 = 840,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The bureau sells 1 Euro at 1720 shillings. How much in Uganda shillings does one pay to buy Euro 110? A: 189200. 110 x 1720 = 189,200 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A tray of 30 eggs costs sh.9000. How many eggs can one buy with sh.155,100? A: 517. Each egg costs 300; 155,100/300 = 517 eggs.
chunks.source: Each egg costs 300; 155,100/300 = 517 eggs.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A father had two 50,000-shilling notes, five 5,000-shilling notes and ten 500-shilling coins. How much money did he have altogether? A: 130000. 100,000 + 25,000 + 5,000 = 130,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A father had sh.130,000 and bought a watch at sh.56,500. How much money did he remain with? A: 73500. 130,000 - 56,500 = 73,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many minutes are in 2 hours? A: 120. 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 2 hours = 120 minutes.
chunks.source: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 2 hours = 120 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many hours are there between 3:15 a.m. and 10:30 a.m.? A: 7 hours 15 minutes. From 3:15 to 10:15 is 7 hours, plus 15 more minutes = 7 hours 15 minutes.
chunks.source: From 3:15 to 10:15 is 7 hours, plus 15 more minutes = 7 hours 15 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many hours are there between 11:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.? A: 5. From 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. is 5 hours.
chunks.source: From 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. is 5 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many hours are there between 7:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m.? A: 8. From 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. is 8 hours.
chunks.source: From 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. is 8 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is An examination started at 8:30 a.m. and ended at 10:30 a.m. For how many seconds did the exam last? A: 7200. The exam lasted 2 hours = 120 minutes = 7200 seconds.
chunks.source: The exam lasted 2 hours = 120 minutes = 7200 seconds.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the distance covered by an airplane in 4 hours at 600 km/hr. A: 2400. Distance = speed x time = 600 x 4 = 2400 km.
chunks.source: Distance = speed x time = 600 x 4 = 2400 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Sam takes 40 minutes to cover a distance at a speed of 60 km/hr. How long is the distance he covers? A: 40. 40 minutes = 2/3 hour; distance = 60 x 2/3 = 40 km.
chunks.source: 40 minutes = 2/3 hour; distance = 60 x 2/3 = 40 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How long will it take a traveller to move a distance of 350 m at a speed of 70 m/hour? A: 5. Time = distance / speed = 350 / 70 = 5 hours.
chunks.source: Time = distance / speed = 350 / 70 = 5 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A car moving at 70 km/hr covers a 350 km journey. How many more hours will it take if its average speed is reduced to 50 km/hr? A: 2. 350/70 = 5 hours; 350/50 = 7 hours; 7 - 5 = 2 more hours.
chunks.source: 350/70 = 5 hours; 350/50 = 7 hours; 7 - 5 = 2 more hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is At what speed should a ship move to reach a landing site 320 km away in 4 hours? A: 80. Speed = distance / time = 320 / 4 = 80 km/hr.
chunks.source: Speed = distance / time = 320 / 4 = 80 km/hr.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Kiprotich took 30 minutes to run a distance of 2 km. What was his average speed in km/hr? A: 4. 30 minutes = 1/2 hour; speed = 2 / 0.5 = 4 km/hr.
chunks.source: 30 minutes = 1/2 hour; speed = 2 / 0.5 = 4 km/hr.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Express 180 km/hr in m/second. A: 50. 180 km/hr = 180,000 m / 3600 s = 50 m/s.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Convert 20 m/second to km/hr. A: 72. 20 m/s = 20 x 3600 / 1000 = 72 km/hr.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A trip to Entebbe beach took 4 hours at 45 km/hr; the return took 6 hours. Calculate the average speed for the whole journey. A: 36. Distance each way = 180 km; total 360 km in 10 hours; 360/10 = 36 km/hr.
chunks.source: Distance each way = 180 km; total 360 km in 10 hours; 360/10 = 36 km/hr.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the journey graph of the flight from Entebbe to Cape Town. What distance did the plane cover after resting? A: 800. After resting at 1200 km, the plane flew to 2000 km; 2000 - 1200 = 800 km.
chunks.source: After resting at 1200 km, the plane flew to 2000 km; 2000 - 1200 = 800 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the journey graph of the flight from Entebbe to Cape Town. At what time did the plane arrive at Cape Town? A: 2 p.m.. The graph line reaches 2000 km at 2 p.m.
chunks.source: The graph line reaches 2000 km at 2 p.m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the journey graph of the flight from Entebbe to Cape Town. Identify the scale on the vertical axis. A: 200 km. Each division on the vertical axis represents 200 km.
chunks.source: Each division on the vertical axis represents 200 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the journey graph of the flight from Entebbe to Cape Town. What is the distance from Entebbe to Zimbabwe? A: 1200. The plane rested in Zimbabwe at the 1200 km mark.
chunks.source: The plane rested in Zimbabwe at the 1200 km mark.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the journey graph of the flight from Entebbe to Cape Town. Calculate the average speed for the whole journey. A: 333.33. Total distance 2000 km in 6 hours (8 a.m. to 2 p.m.); 2000/6 = 333.33 km/hr.
chunks.source: Total distance 2000 km in 6 hours (8 a.m. to 2 p.m.); 2000/6 = 333.33 km/hr.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Joanita started driving at 8:00 and stopped at 11:00, as shown on the clock faces. Find the time she took driving. A: 3. 11:00 - 8:00 = 3 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The distance between Kibuli and Buwaate is 15 km and Kamuntu takes 45 minutes. At what speed in km/hr does he cover the distance? A: 20. 45 min = 3/4 hr; 15 / 0.75 = 20 km/hr.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Convert 4 km to centimetres. A: 400000. 4 km = 4000 m = 400,000 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Change 2800 cm to metres. A: 28. 2800 / 100 = 28 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A house fly covered 150 mm. What is this distance in centimetres? A: 15. 150 / 10 = 15 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Convert 7 m^2 to square centimetres. A: 70000. 7 x 10,000 = 70,000 cm^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Change 0.36 km^2 to square metres. A: 360000. 0.36 x 1,000,000 = 360,000 m^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Express 13000 g as kg. A: 13. 13000 / 1000 = 13 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 450 kg + 350 g. Give your answer in grams. A: 450350. 450 kg = 450,000 g; 450,000 + 350 = 450,350 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Subtract 150 g from 6 kg. Give your answer in grams. A: 5850. 6 kg = 6000 g; 6000 - 150 = 5850 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Change 6.045 kg to grams. A: 6045. 6.045 x 1000 = 6045 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A box weighs 56,000 g. What is its weight in kg? A: 56. 56,000 / 1000 = 56 kg.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A container carries 1200 kg of beans. How many packets of 200 g can be poured into the container? A: 6000. 1200 kg = 1,200,000 g; 1,200,000 / 200 = 6000 packets.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Naigaga prepares 17,000 millilitres of juice daily. How many 1-litre bottles does she prepare? A: 17. 17,000 ml = 17 litres, so 17 bottles.
chunks.source: 17,000 ml = 17 litres, so 17 bottles.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A bus used 20 1/2 litres of diesel. How many millilitres were they? A: 20500. 20.5 x 1000 = 20,500 ml.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is How many cups of 250 cm^3 can be obtained from a five litre jerrycan? A: 20. 5 litres = 5000 cm^3; 5000/250 = 20 cups.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out: 49 m 65 cm + 30 m 55 cm. A: 80 m 20 cm. 79 m 120 cm = 80 m 20 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The diameter of a circle is 14 cm. Find its circumference. (Use pi = 22/7) A: 44. Circumference = pi x d = 22/7 x 14 = 44 cm.
chunks.source: Circumference = pi x d = 22/7 x 14 = 44 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is What is the area of a circle whose radius is 35 dm? (Take pi = 22/7) A: 3850. Area = pi x r^2 = 22/7 x 35 x 35 = 3850 dm^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In triangle ABC, AB = 12 cm, AC = 16 cm. CE is the altitude to AB with CE = 10 cm. Find the length of the altitude BD to side AC. A: 7.5. Area = 1/2 x 12 x 10 = 60; also = 1/2 x 16 x BD; BD = 120/16 = 7.5 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The volume of a cuboid is 48 litres. Its base is 80 cm by 120 cm. Find the value of x (the height). A: 5. 48 litres = 48,000 cm^3; x = 48,000/(80x120) = 5 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A cuboid is 80 cm by 120 cm by 5 cm. Calculate the total surface area. A: 21200. 2(80x120 + 80x5 + 120x5) = 2(9600+400+600) = 21,200 cm^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A box B measures 32 cm by 18 cm by 25 cm. How many 3 cm cubes (C) can be packed in box B? A: 480. 10 x 6 x 8 = 480 cubes fit along each side.
chunks.source: 10 x 6 x 8 = 480 cubes fit along each side.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A box B measures 32 cm by 18 cm by 25 cm. How many layers of 3 cm cubes can be made in box B? A: 8. 25/3 = 8 full layers.
chunks.source: 25/3 = 8 full layers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Calculate the area of the L-shaped figure below. (Left column 5 cm wide; top-right part 5 cm wide and 2 cm tall; step down 4 cm.) A: 40. Big rectangle 10x6 = 60 minus the missing 5x4 = 20; 60 - 20 = 40 cm^2.
chunks.source: Big rectangle 10x6 = 60 minus the missing 5x4 = 20; 60 - 20 = 40 cm^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the area of the shaded part. The outer rectangle is 10 m by 8 m and the inner white rectangle is 6 m by 5 m. A: 50. Outer 80 minus inner 30 = 50 m^2.
chunks.source: Outer 80 minus inner 30 = 50 m^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out the perimeter of the outer rectangular figure (10 m by 8 m). A: 36. 2 x (10 + 8) = 36 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Calculate the area of the whole rectangular figure (10 m by 8 m). A: 80. 10 x 8 = 80 m^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the value of y. (A straight line with 40 degrees, y degrees and a right angle between two rays.) A: 50. 40 + 90 + y = 180; y = 50.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In the isosceles triangle, the base angles are (x+40) degrees and 2(x+5) degrees. Find the value of the angle marked K at the apex. A: 40. x + 40 = 2(x + 5) gives x = 30; base angles are 70 each; K = 180 - 140 = 40.
chunks.source: x + 40 = 2(x + 5) gives x = 30; base angles are 70 each; K = 180 - 140 = 40.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Two parallel lines are cut by a zigzag. The given angles are 40 degrees and 30 degrees. What is the value of W at the bend? A: 70. Draw a line through the bend parallel to the two lines; W = 40 + 30 = 70.
chunks.source: Draw a line through the bend parallel to the two lines; W = 40 + 30 = 70.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the isosceles triangle with base extended to form an exterior angle of 120 degrees. Find angle Q. A: 60. The interior base angle r = 180 - 120 = 60; the triangle is isosceles, so Q = r = 60.
chunks.source: The interior base angle r = 180 - 120 = 60; the triangle is isosceles, so Q = r = 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. The marked angle at the top is 120 degrees and 3y is the angle on the same side below. Find y. A: 20. 3y and 120 are supplementary (same-side); 3y = 60; y = 20.
chunks.source: 3y and 120 are supplementary (same-side); 3y = 60; y = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The interior angle of a regular polygon is twice its exterior angle. Find its interior angle sum. A: 720. Exterior = 60, so 6 sides; sum = (6-2) x 180 = 720.
chunks.source: Exterior = 60, so 6 sides; sum = (6-2) x 180 = 720.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The exterior angle of a regular polygon is 40 degrees. What is its interior angle sum? A: 1260. Sides = 360/40 = 9; sum = (9-2) x 180 = 1260.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The interior angle of a regular polygon is 120 more than its exterior angle. Calculate the exterior angle. A: 30. Let exterior = e; e + (e + 120) = 180; e = 30.
chunks.source: Let exterior = e; e + (e + 120) = 180; e = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The interior angle of a regular polygon is 120 more than its exterior angle. How many sides has the polygon? A: 12. Exterior = 30; sides = 360/30 = 12.
chunks.source: Exterior = 30; sides = 360/30 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The interior angle of a regular polygon is 120 more than its exterior angle. Work out its interior angle sum. A: 1800. 12 sides; (12-2) x 180 = 1800.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Two parallel lines with a triangle between them: the bottom angle is 120 degrees. Find X (alternate interior angle at the top). A: 60. The interior base angle is 180 - 120 = 60; X is alternate interior to it, so X = 60.
chunks.source: The interior base angle is 180 - 120 = 60; X is alternate interior to it, so X = 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A ladder 10 m long leans against a wall with its foot 8 m from the wall. What is the height of the wall? A: 6. h^2 + 8^2 = 10^2; h^2 = 36; h = 6 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Given that (x + 40) degrees and 2(x + 5) degrees are supplementary angles. Find the value of x. A: 43.33. 3x + 50 = 180; 3x = 130; x = 130/3 = 43.33.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Two parallel rays stand on a horizontal line. The angles at the left ray are 3x (outside) and 2x (inside). Find x. A: 36. 3x + 2x = 180; x = 36.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the value of y in the zigzag figure between two parallel lines (120 degrees on the left, 130 degrees on the right). A: 110. Draw a line through the peak parallel to both; y = (180-120) + (180-130) = 110.
chunks.source: Draw a line through the peak parallel to both; y = (180-120) + (180-130) = 110.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Name the polygon whose interior angle sum is 1080 degrees. A: octagon. (n-2) x 180 = 1080; n = 8, an octagon.
chunks.source: (n-2) x 180 = 1080; n = 8, an octagon.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In the triangle, the apex is 60 degrees, the left base angle is 40 degrees, and the exterior angle at the right base is 2x. Find x. A: 50. Exterior angle = sum of opposite interiors: 2x = 100; x = 50.
chunks.source: Exterior angle = sum of opposite interiors: 2x = 100; x = 50.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The area of a triangular garden is 60 m^2. If the base is 12 m, find the height. A: 10. Height = 2 x 60 / 12 = 10 m.
chunks.source: Height = 2 x 60 / 12 = 10 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the value of angle marked y in the isosceles triangle with apex 50 degrees. A: 65. Base angles are equal: (180 - 50)/2 = 65 degrees.
chunks.source: Base angles are equal: (180 - 50)/2 = 65 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the cuboid 8 cm by 6 cm by 5 cm. Find the perimeter of the shaded base. A: 28. 2 x (8 + 6) = 28 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the total surface area of the cuboid 8 cm by 6 cm by 5 cm. A: 236. 2(48 + 40 + 30) = 236 cm^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Identify the integer shown by the arrow on the number line below. (Arrow from +5 pointing left to +2.) A: 2. The arrowhead lands on +2.
chunks.source: The arrowhead lands on +2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the number line: arrow X goes from -4 to +4. Identify the integer at the arrowhead of X. A: 4. The arrowhead of X lands on +4.
chunks.source: The arrowhead of X lands on +4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the number line: arrow Y goes from -1 to -4. Identify the integer at the arrowhead of Y. A: -4. The arrowhead of Y lands on -4.
chunks.source: The arrowhead of Y lands on -4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the number line: arrow Z goes from +1 to -1. Identify the integer at the arrowhead of Z. A: -1. The arrowhead of Z lands on -1.
chunks.source: The arrowhead of Z lands on -1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Study the number line: dashed arrow k goes from +1 to +4. Identify the integer at the arrowhead of k. A: 4. The arrowhead of k lands on +4.
chunks.source: The arrowhead of k lands on +4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve and give the solution set: 2y > 4 A: y > 2. Divide both sides by 2: y > 2.
chunks.source: Divide both sides by 2: y > 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The temperature on top of a mountain was 3 degrees C at noon. It dropped by 10 degrees C. What was the final temperature? A: -7. 3 - 10 = -7 degrees C.
chunks.source: 3 - 10 = -7 degrees C.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve: n - - 7 = 7 A: 0. n + 7 = 7, so n = 0.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve: 2x < 6 A: x < 3. Divide both sides by 2: x < 3.
chunks.source: Divide both sides by 2: x < 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve: -3x + 5 < 8 and give the solution set. A: x > -1. -3x < 3; dividing by -3 flips the sign: x > -1.
chunks.source: -3x < 3; dividing by -3 flips the sign: x > -1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Work out +4 - +7 using a number line. A: -3. Start at +4, move 7 left to reach -3.
chunks.source: Start at +4, move 7 left to reach -3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is I think of a number, multiply it by 4 and subtract 5; the result is greater than 3. Find the least possible whole number. A: 3. 4n - 5 > 3; 4n > 8; n > 2; the least whole number is 3.
chunks.source: 4n - 5 > 3; 4n > 8; n > 2; the least whole number is 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In an interview, 3 points are awarded for every correct answer and 2 points subtracted for each wrong answer. There were 10 questions. What was the final score for one who answered 7 correctly? A: 15. 7 x 3 = 21; 3 x 2 = 6; 21 - 6 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The sum of 4 consecutive integers is 46. Find the numbers. A: 10, 11, 12, 13. 46/4 = 11.5, the middle; the numbers are 10, 11, 12, 13.
chunks.source: 46/4 = 11.5, the middle; the numbers are 10, 11, 12, 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the number line: arrow b goes from 0 to +6 and dashed arrow c goes from +6 to -5. Write the integer for arrow c. A: -11. Arrow c jumps 11 to the left: -11.
chunks.source: Arrow c jumps 11 to the left: -11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Use the number line: arrow b goes from 0 to +6. Write the integer for arrow b. A: 6. Arrow b jumps 6 to the right: +6.
chunks.source: Arrow b jumps 6 to the right: +6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Write the subtraction statement for the arrows: from +6 subtract 11 to reach -5. A: 6 - 11 = -5. Start at +6, subtract 11, land at -5.
chunks.source: Start at +6, subtract 11, land at -5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve: p - 2 = 4 A: 6. Add 2 to both sides: p = 6.
chunks.source: Add 2 to both sides: p = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If x = 2, find the value of 5 - 2x A: 1. 5 - 2(2) = 5 - 4 = 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Remove the brackets: 4(1 - 3b) A: 4 - 12b. Multiply each term inside by 4: 4 - 12b.
chunks.source: Multiply each term inside by 4: 4 - 12b.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Simplify: 2b + 4a + b - 2a A: 2a + 3b. Combine a terms: 4a - 2a = 2a; combine b terms: 2b + b = 3b.
chunks.source: Combine a terms: 4a - 2a = 2a; combine b terms: 2b + b = 3b.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve: x - 3 = 5 A: 8. Add 3 to both sides: x = 8.
chunks.source: Add 3 to both sides: x = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve: 3x - 5 = 7 A: 4. 3x = 12; x = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If a = 2, b = 1 and c = 1/2, calculate ab/c. A: 4. (2 x 1) / (1/2) = 2 x 2 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Find the value of (bc + ac)/a given that a = 1, b = 0 and c = 3. A: 3. (0 + 3)/1 = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve: 3p - 6 = 18 + p A: 12. 2p = 24; p = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Simplify: 3x - (2 + x) A: 2x - 2. 3x - 2 - x = 2x - 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The figure is a rectangle with length (2x+1) cm and width (x+3) cm (opposite sides equal). The other width is marked (2x-1) cm. Find the perimeter. A: 16. 2x + 1 = x + 3 gives x = 2; sides 5 cm and 3 cm; perimeter = 16 cm.
chunks.source: 2x + 1 = x + 3 gives x = 2; sides 5 cm and 3 cm; perimeter = 16 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The figure is a rectangle with length (2x+1) cm and width (x+3) cm (opposite sides equal). Find its area. A: 15. x = 2; area = 5 x 3 = 15 cm^2.
chunks.source: x = 2; area = 5 x 3 = 15 cm^2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Kirya is 3 times as old as his daughter. Their ages add up to 72 years. How old is the daughter? A: 18. Let the daughter be x: x + 3x = 72; x = 18.
chunks.source: Let the daughter be x: x + 3x = 72; x = 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is In the triangle, the altitude to the 12 cm base is 6 cm, and the altitude to side x is 8 cm. Find x. A: 9. Area = 1/2 x 12 x 6 = 36 = 1/2 x 8x; x = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is The isosceles triangle has equal sides (2x-2) cm and (x+4) cm. Find x. A: 6. 2x - 2 = x + 4; x = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is Solve: 3k - 2 = 142 A: 48. 3k = 144; k = 48.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is A parent bought three bags at sh.K, sh.(K-600) and sh.2K. Write an algebraic expression for the total cost. A: 4K - 600. K + (K - 600) + 2K = 4K - 600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is If K = sh.1650, find the total cost of the three bags (expression 4K - 600). A: 6000. 4 x 1650 - 600 = 6000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Round off 4,467 to the nearest hundred: ___ A: 4500. The tens digit is 6, so round up: 4,467 rounds to 4,500.
chunks.source: The tens digit is 6, so round up: 4,467 rounds to 4,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Joan read XLIX pages of a book. How many pages did she read in Hindu Arabic numerals? ___ A: 49. XL = 40 and IX = 9, so XLIX = 49.
chunks.source: XL = 40 and IX = 9, so XLIX = 49.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the place value of 6 in 463.21? A: tens. 6 is in the second place to the left of the decimal point, so its place value is tens.
chunks.source: 6 is in the second place to the left of the decimal point, so its place value is tens.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the HCF of 12 and 16: ___ A: 4. Factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12; factors of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The highest common factor is 4.
chunks.source: Factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12; factors of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The highest common factor is 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the LCM of 30 and 40: ___ A: 120. Prime factors: 30 = 2 x 3 x 5, 40 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 5. LCM = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 = 120.
chunks.source: Prime factors: 30 = 2 x 3 x 5, 40 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 5. LCM = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 = 120.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the square root of 256: ___ A: 16. 16 x 16 = 256, so the square root of 256 is 16.
chunks.source: 16 x 16 = 256, so the square root of 256 is 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the square root of 196: A: 14. 14 x 14 = 196, so the square root of 196 is 14.
chunks.source: 14 x 14 = 196, so the square root of 196 is 14.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the missing number in the sequence: 10, 19, 18, 27, 26, ___ A: 35. The pattern alternates: +9, -1. 26 + 9 = 35.
chunks.source: The pattern alternates: +9, -1. 26 + 9 = 35.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 110, 130, 150, 170, ___ A: 190. Each number increases by 20, so 170 + 20 = 190.
chunks.source: Each number increases by 20, so 170 + 20 = 190.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The sum of two consecutive numbers is 9. Find the larger number: ___ A: 5. 4 + 5 = 9, so the larger number is 5.
chunks.source: 4 + 5 = 9, so the larger number is 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that set K is the set of vowel letters, find n(K): ___ A: 5. The vowels are a, e, i, o, u, so n(K) = 5.
chunks.source: The vowels are a, e, i, o, u, so n(K) = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a class of 50 pupils, 30 like Mathematics, 25 like English and 2 like neither. How many pupils like both subjects? ___ A: 7. 30 + 25 + 2 - 50 = 7 pupils like both.
chunks.source: 30 + 25 + 2 - 50 = 7 pupils like both.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: (1/4 of 1/3) divided by 1/12: ___ A: 1. 1/4 of 1/3 = 1/12, and 1/12 divided by 1/12 = 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 45% into a fraction in its lowest terms: ___ A: 9/20. 45/100 simplifies to 9/20.
chunks.source: 45/100 simplifies to 9/20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that a = 2/3 and b = 1/4, find the value of a minus b: ___ A: 5/12. 2/3 - 1/4 = 8/12 - 3/12 = 5/12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Convert 3 1/3 to an improper fraction: ___ A: 10/3. 3 x 3 + 1 = 10, so 3 1/3 = 10/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Joan, Juliet and Alice shared sh. 12,000 in the ratio 2:3:1. What fraction of the money did Alice get? A: 1/6. Total parts = 2 + 3 + 1 = 6, so Alice got 1/6 of the money.
chunks.source: Total parts = 2 + 3 + 1 = 6, so Alice got 1/6 of the money.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The cost of 4 pens is sh. 2,000. Find the cost of 3 similar pens: ___ A: 1500. One pen costs 2,000 / 4 = 500 shillings, so 3 pens cost 1,500 shillings.
chunks.source: One pen costs 2,000 / 4 = 500 shillings, so 3 pens cost 1,500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: John bought a dozen counter books at sh. 36,000 and sold each book at sh. 4,000. How much profit did he make? ___ A: 12000. Selling price = 12 x 4,000 = 48,000. Profit = 48,000 - 36,000 = 12,000 shillings.
chunks.source: Selling price = 12 x 4,000 = 48,000. Profit = 48,000 - 36,000 = 12,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: By selling an article at sh. 3,500, a trader made a loss of sh. 1,000. At what price did he buy the article? ___ A: 4500. Buying price = selling price + loss = 3,500 + 1,000 = 4,500 shillings.
chunks.source: Buying price = selling price + loss = 3,500 + 1,000 = 4,500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many 200 shilling coins make up sh. 4,600? ___ A: 23. 4,600 / 200 = 23 coins.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Nantale buys 8 books for sh. 48,000. How much will 9 similar books cost? ___ A: 54000. One book costs 48,000 / 8 = 6,000 shillings, so 9 books cost 54,000 shillings.
chunks.source: One book costs 48,000 / 8 = 6,000 shillings, so 9 books cost 54,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A lorry covered a distance of 300 km in 5 hours. What was its average speed? ___ A: 60. Speed = distance / time = 300 / 5 = 60 km/h.
chunks.source: Speed = distance / time = 300 / 5 = 60 km/h.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A motorist covers a journey at 60 km/h for 3 hours 30 minutes. Calculate the distance covered by the motorist: ___ A: 210. Distance = speed x time = 60 x 3.5 = 210 km.
chunks.source: Distance = speed x time = 60 x 3.5 = 210 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 1342 hours in the 12-hour clock system: ___ A: 1:42 p.m.. 1342 hours is 42 minutes past 1 p.m.
chunks.source: 1342 hours is 42 minutes past 1 p.m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A bus arrived at Bwera at 10:30 a.m. and left at 10:45 a.m. For how long did the bus stay at Bwera? ___ A: 15 minutes. 10:45 - 10:30 = 15 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How long is it from 10:30 a.m. to 11:50 a.m.? ___ A: 80 minutes. From 10:30 to 11:50 is 1 hour 20 minutes, which is 80 minutes.
chunks.source: From 10:30 to 11:50 is 1 hour 20 minutes, which is 80 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Makmot scored 40, 85, 60, 55 and 70 in a series of tests. Find the median score: ___ A: 60. In order: 40, 55, 60, 70, 85. The middle value is 60.
chunks.source: In order: 40, 55, 60, 70, 85. The middle value is 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A girl scored 4, 3, 4, 5 and 8 points in a game. Find the range of the points: ___ A: 5. Range = highest - lowest = 8 - 3 = 5.
chunks.source: Range = highest - lowest = 8 - 3 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Ndahura's birthday will be celebrated next week. What is the probability that the day starts with the letter T? A: 2/7. Tuesday and Thursday start with T, so the probability is 2/7.
chunks.source: Tuesday and Thursday start with T, so the probability is 2/7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Add: -4 + 7: ___ A: 3. Start at -4 on the number line and move 7 steps up: -4 + 7 = 3.
chunks.source: Start at -4 on the number line and move 7 steps up: -4 + 7 = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the range of the integers: 3, -4, 0, -7, 5 and 6: ___ A: 13. Range = highest - lowest = 6 - (-7) = 13.
chunks.source: Range = highest - lowest = 6 - (-7) = 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve: K + K = 18. Find the value of K: ___ A: 9. 2K = 18, so K = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Simplify: 2k + 3p - k - p A: k + 2p. 2k - k = k and 3p - p = 2p, so the answer is k + 2p.
chunks.source: 2k - k = k and 3p - p = 2p, so the answer is k + 2p.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 7 metres to centimetres: ___ A: 700. 1 m = 100 cm, so 7 m = 700 cm.
chunks.source: 1 m = 100 cm, so 7 m = 700 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Convert 1 3/5 kg to grams: ___ A: 1600. 1 3/5 kg = 8/5 kg = 1.6 kg, and 1.6 x 1000 = 1600 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many half litres are in a 10 litre jerrycan? A: 20. 10 / 0.5 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many faces does a cuboid have? ___ A: 6. A cuboid has 6 faces.
chunks.source: A cuboid has 6 faces.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Round off 4,467 to the nearest hundred: ____? A: 4500. The tens digit is 6, so round up: 4,467 rounds to 4,500.
chunks.source: The tens digit is 6, so round up: 4,467 rounds to 4,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Joan read XLIX pages of a book. How many pages did she read in Hindu Arabic numerals? ____? A: 49. XL = 40 and IX = 9, so XLIX = 49.
chunks.source: XL = 40 and IX = 9, so XLIX = 49.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the HCF of 12 and 16: ____? A: 4. Factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12; factors of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The highest common factor is 4.
chunks.source: Factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12; factors of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The highest common factor is 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the LCM of 30 and 40: ____? A: 120. Prime factors: 30 = 2 x 3 x 5, 40 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 5. LCM = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 = 120.
chunks.source: Prime factors: 30 = 2 x 3 x 5, 40 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 5. LCM = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 = 120.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the square root of 256: ____? A: 16. 16 x 16 = 256, so the square root of 256 is 16.
chunks.source: 16 x 16 = 256, so the square root of 256 is 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the missing number in the sequence: 10, 19, 18, 27, 26, ____? A: 35. The pattern alternates: +9, -1. 26 + 9 = 35.
chunks.source: The pattern alternates: +9, -1. 26 + 9 = 35.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the next number in the sequence: 110, 130, 150, 170, ____? A: 190. Each number increases by 20, so 170 + 20 = 190.
chunks.source: Each number increases by 20, so 170 + 20 = 190.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The sum of two consecutive numbers is 9. Find the larger number: ____? A: 5. 4 + 5 = 9, so the larger number is 5.
chunks.source: 4 + 5 = 9, so the larger number is 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that set K is the set of vowel letters, find n(K): ____? A: 5. The vowels are a, e, i, o, u, so n(K) = 5.
chunks.source: The vowels are a, e, i, o, u, so n(K) = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a class of 50 pupils, 30 like Mathematics, 25 like English and 2 like neither. How many pupils like both subjects? ____? A: 7. 30 + 25 + 2 - 50 = 7 pupils like both.
chunks.source: 30 + 25 + 2 - 50 = 7 pupils like both.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Work out: (1/4 of 1/3) divided by 1/12: ____? A: 1. 1/4 of 1/3 = 1/12, and 1/12 divided by 1/12 = 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 45% into a fraction in its lowest terms: ____? A: 9/20. 45/100 simplifies to 9/20.
chunks.source: 45/100 simplifies to 9/20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Given that a = 2/3 and b = 1/4, find the value of a minus b: ____? A: 5/12. 2/3 - 1/4 = 8/12 - 3/12 = 5/12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Convert 3 1/3 to an improper fraction: ____? A: 10/3. 3 x 3 + 1 = 10, so 3 1/3 = 10/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The cost of 4 pens is sh. 2,000. Find the cost of 3 similar pens: ____? A: 1500. One pen costs 2,000 / 4 = 500 shillings, so 3 pens cost 1,500 shillings.
chunks.source: One pen costs 2,000 / 4 = 500 shillings, so 3 pens cost 1,500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: John bought a dozen counter books at sh. 36,000 and sold each book at sh. 4,000. How much profit did he make? ____? A: 12000. Selling price = 12 x 4,000 = 48,000. Profit = 48,000 - 36,000 = 12,000 shillings.
chunks.source: Selling price = 12 x 4,000 = 48,000. Profit = 48,000 - 36,000 = 12,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: By selling an article at sh. 3,500, a trader made a loss of sh. 1,000. At what price did he buy the article? ____? A: 4500. Buying price = selling price + loss = 3,500 + 1,000 = 4,500 shillings.
chunks.source: Buying price = selling price + loss = 3,500 + 1,000 = 4,500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many 200 shilling coins make up sh. 4,600? ____? A: 23. 4,600 / 200 = 23 coins.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Nantale buys 8 books for sh. 48,000. How much will 9 similar books cost? ____? A: 54000. One book costs 48,000 / 8 = 6,000 shillings, so 9 books cost 54,000 shillings.
chunks.source: One book costs 48,000 / 8 = 6,000 shillings, so 9 books cost 54,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A lorry covered a distance of 300 km in 5 hours. What was its average speed? ____? A: 60. Speed = distance / time = 300 / 5 = 60 km/h.
chunks.source: Speed = distance / time = 300 / 5 = 60 km/h.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A motorist covers a journey at 60 km/h for 3 hours 30 minutes. Calculate the distance covered by the motorist: ____? A: 210. Distance = speed x time = 60 x 3.5 = 210 km.
chunks.source: Distance = speed x time = 60 x 3.5 = 210 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Express 1342 hours in the 12-hour clock system: ____? A: 1:42 p.m.. 1342 hours is 42 minutes past 1 p.m.
chunks.source: 1342 hours is 42 minutes past 1 p.m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A bus arrived at Bwera at 10:30 a.m. and left at 10:45 a.m. For how long did the bus stay at Bwera? ____? A: 15 minutes. 10:45 - 10:30 = 15 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How long is it from 10:30 a.m. to 11:50 a.m.? ____? A: 80 minutes. From 10:30 to 11:50 is 1 hour 20 minutes, which is 80 minutes.
chunks.source: From 10:30 to 11:50 is 1 hour 20 minutes, which is 80 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Makmot scored 40, 85, 60, 55 and 70 in a series of tests. Find the median score: ____? A: 60. In order: 40, 55, 60, 70, 85. The middle value is 60.
chunks.source: In order: 40, 55, 60, 70, 85. The middle value is 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A girl scored 4, 3, 4, 5 and 8 points in a game. Find the range of the points: ____? A: 5. Range = highest - lowest = 8 - 3 = 5.
chunks.source: Range = highest - lowest = 8 - 3 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Add: -4 + 7: ____? A: 3. Start at -4 on the number line and move 7 steps up: -4 + 7 = 3.
chunks.source: Start at -4 on the number line and move 7 steps up: -4 + 7 = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the range of the integers: 3, -4, 0, -7, 5 and 6: ____? A: 13. Range = highest - lowest = 6 - (-7) = 13.
chunks.source: Range = highest - lowest = 6 - (-7) = 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Solve: K + K = 18. Find the value of K: ____? A: 9. 2K = 18, so K = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Change 7 metres to centimetres: ____? A: 700. 1 m = 100 cm, so 7 m = 700 cm.
chunks.source: 1 m = 100 cm, so 7 m = 700 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Convert 1 3/5 kg to grams: ____? A: 1600. 1 3/5 kg = 8/5 kg = 1.6 kg, and 1.6 x 1000 = 1600 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many faces does a cuboid have? ____? A: 6. A cuboid has 6 faces.
chunks.source: A cuboid has 6 faces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one example of a fungus: ____. A: mushroom. Fungi are living things that feed on dead matter; mushroom, yeast and mould are common examples.
chunks.source: Fungi are living things that feed on dead matter; mushroom, yeast and mould are common examples.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one activity supported by the air property 'air exerts pressure': ____. A: inflating a balloon (or a bicycle tyre). Air inside a balloon pushes on its walls; this pressure is what keeps the balloon inflated.
chunks.source: Air inside a balloon pushes on its walls; this pressure is what keeps the balloon inflated.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A bat differs from all other mammals because it ____. A: can fly (it is the only mammal that can fly). Bats have wings and are the only mammals capable of true flight.
chunks.source: Bats have wings and are the only mammals capable of true flight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The bee which does most of the duties in a beehive is the ____. A: worker bee. Worker bees clean the hive, feed the young, collect nectar and guard the hive.
chunks.source: Worker bees clean the hive, feed the young, collect nectar and guard the hive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a fertilized egg. The part marked X is the ____. A: yolk. The yolk is the yellow central part of the egg that feeds the growing chick.
chunks.source: The yolk is the yellow central part of the egg that feeds the growing chick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Part R of the egg is suitable for gaseous exchange because it ____. A: has tiny pores that let air pass in and out. The eggshell has tiny holes (pores) through which oxygen enters and carbon dioxide leaves.
chunks.source: The eggshell has tiny holes (pores) through which oxygen enters and carbon dioxide leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way you can help your class monitor to promote sanitation in class is to ____. A: sweep and mop the classroom regularly. A clean classroom has fewer germs and keeps all learners healthy.
chunks.source: A clean classroom has fewer germs and keeps all learners healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way through which heat travels is ____. A: conduction. Heat travels by conduction in solids, by convection in fluids and by radiation through space.
chunks.source: Heat travels by conduction in solids, by convection in fluids and by radiation through space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A cat is helpful to a crop farmer because it ____. A: kills rats that destroy crops. Cats hunt rats and mice that would otherwise eat growing and stored crops.
chunks.source: Cats hunt rats and mice that would otherwise eat growing and stored crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of cow dung to people is ____. A: it is used as manure. Cow dung adds nutrients to the soil and can also be dried and used as fuel.
chunks.source: Cow dung adds nutrients to the soil and can also be dried and used as fuel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides a toothbrush, one other material used in the promotion of oral health is ____. A: toothpaste. Toothpaste contains fluoride, which strengthens teeth and prevents decay.
chunks.source: Toothpaste contains fluoride, which strengthens teeth and prevents decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a glass of cold water from a fridge. The process that led to the formation of water droplets on the glass is ____. A: condensation. Water vapour in the air touched the cold glass, cooled and changed into liquid droplets.
chunks.source: Water vapour in the air touched the cold glass, cooled and changed into liquid droplets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Learners use the displacement method of measurement when measuring the volume of ____. A: irregular objects. An irregular object is lowered into water and the volume of water it pushes aside equals its volume.
chunks.source: An irregular object is lowered into water and the volume of water it pushes aside equals its volume.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wetlands promote the spread of malaria because they ____. A: are breeding places for mosquitoes. Stagnant water in wetlands is where mosquitoes lay their eggs.
chunks.source: Stagnant water in wetlands is where mosquitoes lay their eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Farmers should be encouraged to use correct farming methods in order to ____. A: get high crop yields and protect the soil. Good methods like mulching and crop rotation keep the soil fertile and increase harvests.
chunks.source: Good methods like mulching and crop rotation keep the soil fertile and increase harvests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A lion is different from an antelope in the way they feed because the lion is a ____ while the antelope is a herbivore. A: carnivore. Lions eat flesh (meat) while antelopes feed on grass and plants.
chunks.source: Lions eat flesh (meat) while antelopes feed on grass and plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A parent's excessive drinking of alcohol affects the family because ____. A: money meant for family needs is wasted on alcohol. Alcohol abuse drains family income and can lead to neglect and quarrels at home.
chunks.source: Alcohol abuse drains family income and can lead to neglect and quarrels at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The major component of air in the atmosphere is ____. A: nitrogen. Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air we breathe.
chunks.source: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air we breathe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One item that can be used to harvest resources such as water is a ____. A: tank. Roof tanks, drums and jerrycans store rainwater harvested from roofs.
chunks.source: Roof tanks, drums and jerrycans store rainwater harvested from roofs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a wingless insect is a ____. A: flea. Fleas, lice and silverfish are insects that have no wings.
chunks.source: Fleas, lice and silverfish are insects that have no wings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One healthy lifestyle that can help you fight skin diseases is ____. A: bathing the body daily. Washing removes dirt and germs that cause skin infections.
chunks.source: Washing removes dirt and germs that cause skin infections.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A piece of paper floats on water because it is ____ than water. A: less dense (lighter). Objects that are less dense than water float on it.
chunks.source: Objects that are less dense than water float on it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The main product obtained from a cow is ____. A: milk. Likely answer: milk. The diagram was not extractable, but cows are mainly kept for milk (and meat).
chunks.source: Likely answer: milk. The diagram was not extractable, but cows are mainly kept for milk (and meat).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The common way through which HIV is spread is through ____. A: unprotected sexual intercourse. HIV passes through body fluids, most commonly during unprotected sex.
chunks.source: HIV passes through body fluids, most commonly during unprotected sex.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Clay soil is the most suitable for making pots because it is ____. A: sticky and holds its shape when moulded. Clay has fine particles that stick together when wet and harden when baked.
chunks.source: Clay has fine particles that stick together when wet and harden when baked.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A farmer can know that his cow is on heat when it ____. A: becomes restless and bellows (moos loudly). A cow on heat is restless, mounts other cows and has a mucus discharge from the vulva.
chunks.source: A cow on heat is restless, mounts other cows and has a mucus discharge from the vulva.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from drinking, one use of water to a school child is ____. A: washing (bathing). Water is also needed for washing, cleaning and cooking.
chunks.source: Water is also needed for washing, cleaning and cooking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The sound of a child singing reaches a person 200 metres away through ____. A: air. Sound travels from the singer through the air to the listener's ears.
chunks.source: Sound travels from the singer through the air to the listener's ears.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Freezing is regarded as a physical change because ____. A: no new substance is formed and it is reversible. Ice can melt back into water, so freezing forms no new substance.
chunks.source: Ice can melt back into water, so freezing forms no new substance.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One element of Primary Health Care (P.H.C.) is ____. A: immunization. P.H.C. elements include immunization, safe water, sanitation and nutrition education.
chunks.source: P.H.C. elements include immunization, safe water, sanitation and nutrition education.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Boiling water for drinking controls the spread of diarrhoeal diseases because boiling ____. A: kills the germs in the water. Heat kills the germs that cause diarrhoea, making the water safe to drink.
chunks.source: Heat kills the germs that cause diarrhoea, making the water safe to drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One agent of soil erosion is ____. A: running water. Running water and wind carry away the top fertile soil.
chunks.source: Running water and wind carry away the top fertile soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Echoes can be reduced in cinema halls by ____. A: fixing soft materials like curtains and carpets on the walls. Soft surfaces absorb sound instead of reflecting it back as echoes.
chunks.source: Soft surfaces absorb sound instead of reflecting it back as echoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The organ of hearing in insects is the ____. A: antennae. Insects detect sound vibrations with their antennae.
chunks.source: Insects detect sound vibrations with their antennae.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The type of weather suitable for winnowing is ____ weather. A: windy. Wind blows away the light husks while the heavy grain falls down.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light husks while the heavy grain falls down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One activity that can destroy habitats of wild animals is ____. A: deforestation. Cutting down forests removes the homes and food of wild animals.
chunks.source: Cutting down forests removes the homes and food of wild animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One importance of heat from the sun is ____. A: drying clothes and harvested crops. The sun's heat dries our clothes and helps preserve harvested crops.
chunks.source: The sun's heat dries our clothes and helps preserve harvested crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a building material (a brick). The natural resource from which it is made is ____. A: clay (soil). Bricks are moulded from clay soil and then baked so they harden.
chunks.source: Bricks are moulded from clay soil and then baked so they harden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way people abuse drugs is ____. A: taking an overdose. Drug abuse includes taking an overdose and taking drugs without a doctor's advice.
chunks.source: Drug abuse includes taking an overdose and taking drugs without a doctor's advice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The seed shown in the diagram is dispersed by ____. A: wind. Likely answer: wind. The seed appears to have wing-like structures that let wind carry it.
chunks.source: Likely answer: wind. The seed appears to have wing-like structures that let wind carry it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the items in list A with those in list B correctly: Insecticides, Acaricides, Pesticides, herbicides. A: Insecticides: insect vectors; Acaricides: ticks; Pesticides: pests; herbicides: weeds. Insecticides kill insect vectors, acaricides kill ticks, pesticides kill pests and herbicides kill weeds.
chunks.source: Insecticides kill insect vectors, acaricides kill ticks, pesticides kill pests and herbicides kill weeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one type of chicken reared in Uganda: ____. A: layers. Layers are kept for eggs and broilers are kept for meat in Uganda.
chunks.source: Layers are kept for eggs and broilers are kept for meat in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another type of chicken reared in Uganda: ____. A: broilers. Broilers grow fast and are kept for meat.
chunks.source: Broilers grow fast and are kept for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The system of poultry keeping commonly used by most rural farmers is ____. A: free range. Rural farmers let chickens roam freely to find their own food.
chunks.source: Rural farmers let chickens roam freely to find their own food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The system of poultry keeping commonly used by most commercial farmers is ____. A: deep litter. Commercial farmers keep many birds indoors on the floor (deep litter) or in cages.
chunks.source: Commercial farmers keep many birds indoors on the floor (deep litter) or in cages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a respiratory system. The part marked Y is the ____. A: trachea (windpipe). The trachea is the tube that carries air from the nose to the lungs.
chunks.source: The trachea is the tube that carries air from the nose to the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part marked Z is the ____. A: nostrils (nose). Air enters the respiratory system through the nostrils.
chunks.source: Air enters the respiratory system through the nostrils.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The process that takes place in part labelled X is ____. A: gaseous exchange (breathing). In the lungs, oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.
chunks.source: In the lungs, oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way the above respiratory system can be kept healthy is to ____. A: avoid smoking. Smoke damages the lungs; exercise and clean air keep them healthy.
chunks.source: Smoke damages the lungs; exercise and clean air keep them healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one childhood immunisable disease caused by a virus: ____. A: polio. Polio and measles are viral diseases prevented by immunization.
chunks.source: Polio and measles are viral diseases prevented by immunization.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one childhood immunisable disease caused by bacteria: ____. A: tuberculosis. Tuberculosis, whooping cough and diphtheria are bacterial diseases prevented by immunization.
chunks.source: Tuberculosis, whooping cough and diphtheria are bacterial diseases prevented by immunization.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Immunization is important to people because it ____. A: protects them against killer diseases. Vaccines build immunity so the body can fight disease germs.
chunks.source: Vaccines build immunity so the body can fight disease germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A P.6 child can help promote immunization in the community by ____. A: encouraging parents to take young children for immunization. Reminding neighbours about immunization days helps protect all children.
chunks.source: Reminding neighbours about immunization days helps protect all children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the animals: goose, fish, lizard, rabbit, frog, bat. One similarity among all the animals above is that they all ____. A: are vertebrates (have backbones). All these animals have a backbone, so they are all vertebrates.
chunks.source: All these animals have a backbone, so they are all vertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A rabbit is different from a fish because the rabbit ____. A: breathes with lungs and lives on land, while a fish breathes with gills and lives in water. Rabbits are land mammals with lungs; fish are water animals with gills.
chunks.source: Rabbits are land mammals with lungs; fish are water animals with gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: From the list above, one animal that has fur on its body is the ____. A: rabbit. Rabbits and bats are mammals, and mammals have fur or hair.
chunks.source: Rabbits and bats are mammals, and mammals have fur or hair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: From the list above, another animal that has fur on its body is the ____. A: bat. Bats are mammals, so their bodies are covered with fur.
chunks.source: Bats are mammals, so their bodies are covered with fur.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a musical instrument. It belongs to the ____ group of musical instruments. A: percussion. Drums are percussion instruments because sound is made by hitting them.
chunks.source: Drums are percussion instruments because sound is made by hitting them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The instrument above produces sound by ____. A: beating (hitting) the stretched skin. Hitting the tight skin makes it vibrate and produce sound.
