chunks.source: Hitting the tight skin makes it vibrate and produce sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The animal product used to make part X is ____. A: skin (hide/leather). Drum skins are made from animal hide stretched tightly over the drum.
chunks.source: Drum skins are made from animal hide stretched tightly over the drum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One factor that can affect the pitch of sound produced by the instrument above is ____. A: the tightness of the skin. A tighter skin vibrates faster and gives a higher pitch.
chunks.source: A tighter skin vibrates faster and gives a higher pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The importance of stomata to a plant is for ____. A: gaseous exchange. Stomata are tiny holes in leaves through which gases and water vapour pass.
chunks.source: Stomata are tiny holes in leaves through which gases and water vapour pass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Some plants shed their leaves in the dry season to ____. A: reduce water loss. Without leaves, the plant loses less water by transpiration.
chunks.source: Without leaves, the plant loses less water by transpiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One condition needed by plants to grow well is ____. A: water. Plants need water, sunlight, air and fertile soil to grow well.
chunks.source: Plants need water, sunlight, air and fertile soil to grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another condition needed by plants to grow well is ____. A: sunlight. Plants use sunlight to make food by photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants use sunlight to make food by photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The instrument used to measure rainfall is a ____. A: rain gauge. A rain gauge collects rain so its depth can be measured.
chunks.source: A rain gauge collects rain so its depth can be measured.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Rainfall is measured in ____. A: millimetres. The depth of collected rain is read in millimetres (mm).
chunks.source: The depth of collected rain is read in millimetres (mm).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One other weather instrument is the ____. A: thermometer. A thermometer measures temperature; other instruments include the anemometer and wind vane.
chunks.source: A thermometer measures temperature; other instruments include the anemometer and wind vane.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another weather instrument is the ____. A: anemometer. An anemometer measures the speed of wind.
chunks.source: An anemometer measures the speed of wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following items is used to clean the school compound? A: Broom. A broom is used for sweeping the compound clean.
chunks.source: A broom is used for sweeping the compound clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A school compound should be kept clean to ____. A: prevent the spread of diseases. A clean compound has fewer germs and looks beautiful.
chunks.source: A clean compound has fewer germs and looks beautiful.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One component of a clean home is ____. A: a clean latrine. A clean home has a clean latrine, a clean kitchen and proper rubbish disposal.
chunks.source: A clean home has a clean latrine, a clean kitchen and proper rubbish disposal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another component of a clean home is ____. A: a clean kitchen. Food must be prepared in a clean place to avoid contamination.
chunks.source: Food must be prepared in a clean place to avoid contamination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One component of a balanced diet is ____. A: carbohydrates. A balanced diet has carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, fats, minerals, fibre and water.
chunks.source: A balanced diet has carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, fats, minerals, fibre and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: People are advised to eat a balanced diet in order to ____. A: grow well and stay healthy. A balanced diet gives the body all nutrients and prevents deficiency diseases.
chunks.source: A balanced diet gives the body all nutrients and prevents deficiency diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One sign of poor feeding in children is ____. A: a thin body. Poorly fed children become thin, have swollen bellies or brown hair.
chunks.source: Poorly fed children become thin, have swollen bellies or brown hair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another sign of poor feeding in children is ____. A: a swollen belly. Kwashiorkor causes the belly to swell in poorly fed children.
chunks.source: Kwashiorkor causes the belly to swell in poorly fed children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a saucepan with water on fire. The use of hole marked A is to ____. A: let in air to support burning. Air entering through hole A provides oxygen so the charcoal burns well.
chunks.source: Air entering through hole A provides oxygen so the charcoal burns well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The use of hole marked B is to ____. A: put in charcoal. Charcoal is pushed into the stove through hole B.
chunks.source: Charcoal is pushed into the stove through hole B.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The fuel used by the stove above is ____. A: charcoal. The stove burns charcoal to heat the saucepan.
chunks.source: The stove burns charcoal to heat the saucepan.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The above stove helps to conserve the environment because it ____. A: uses less charcoal, so fewer trees are cut down. An improved stove wastes less heat, saving charcoal and trees.
chunks.source: An improved stove wastes less heat, saving charcoal and trees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from sun drying, one other method of food preservation is ____. A: salting. Salting, smoking, refrigeration and tinning also preserve food.
chunks.source: Salting, smoking, refrigeration and tinning also preserve food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from sun drying, another method of food preservation is ____. A: smoking. Smoking removes water from food so germs cannot grow in it.
chunks.source: Smoking removes water from food so germs cannot grow in it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One foodstuff that is preserved by sun drying is ____. A: cassava. Cassava, maize, beans and fish are commonly sun dried.
chunks.source: Cassava, maize, beans and fish are commonly sun dried.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another foodstuff that is preserved by sun drying is ____. A: maize. Drying maize grains in the sun keeps them for a long time.
chunks.source: Drying maize grains in the sun keeps them for a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One item needed by a person going to harvest honey is ____. A: a bee veil. A veil, smoker, overall and gloves protect the harvester from stings.
chunks.source: A veil, smoker, overall and gloves protect the harvester from stings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another item needed by a person going to harvest honey is ____. A: a smoker. Smoke calms the bees so honey can be harvested safely.
chunks.source: Smoke calms the bees so honey can be harvested safely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The best time for harvesting honey is ____. A: in the evening (at night). Bees are less active and docile in the cool of the evening.
chunks.source: Bees are less active and docile in the cool of the evening.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: This is the best time because ____. A: bees are less active and docile. Calm bees sting less, so harvesting is safer.
chunks.source: Calm bees sting less, so harvesting is safer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One importance of soil is ____. A: it supports plant growth. Soil holds plants and gives them water and nutrients.
chunks.source: Soil holds plants and gives them water and nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another importance of soil is ____. A: it is used for building. Soil is used to make bricks and to smear houses.
chunks.source: Soil is used to make bricks and to smear houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One harmful material on soil is ____. A: polythene (plastics). Polythene, chemicals and broken glass harm the soil.
chunks.source: Polythene, chemicals and broken glass harm the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One effect of the harmful material named above on the soil is that it ____. A: prevents air and water from entering the soil. Buried polythene blocks air and water, killing soil organisms.
chunks.source: Buried polythene blocks air and water, killing soil organisms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write PIASCY in full: ____. A: Presidential Initiative on AIDS Strategy for Communication to the Youth. PIASCY is a programme that teaches the youth about HIV/AIDS.
chunks.source: PIASCY is a programme that teaches the youth about HIV/AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One importance of PIASCY in schools is ____. A: it sensitizes pupils about HIV/AIDS. PIASCY teaches pupils how HIV spreads and how to avoid it.
chunks.source: PIASCY teaches pupils how HIV spreads and how to avoid it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another importance of PIASCY in schools is ____. A: it promotes abstinence among the youth. PIASCY encourages the youth to abstain from sex until marriage.
chunks.source: PIASCY encourages the youth to abstain from sex until marriage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one HIV/AIDS message for your school: ____. A: Abstain from sex. Abstinence, faithfulness and avoiding sharing sharp objects protect against HIV.
chunks.source: Abstinence, faithfulness and avoiding sharing sharp objects protect against HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one liquid that can float on water: ____. A: oil (paraffin). Oil is less dense than water, so it floats on top of it.
chunks.source: Oil is less dense than water, so it floats on top of it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one word that refers to the physical change of state from vapour to water: ____. A: condensation. Condensation is the change of water vapour into liquid water on cooling.
chunks.source: Condensation is the change of water vapour into liquid water on cooling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of managing wastes in the environment: ____. A: sorting and recycling waste. Sorting rubbish and recycling keeps the environment clean and reduces pollution.
chunks.source: Sorting rubbish and recycling keeps the environment clean and reduces pollution.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which immunisable disease in children is fought using the BCG vaccine? ____. A: tuberculosis. The BCG vaccine given at birth protects babies against tuberculosis.
chunks.source: The BCG vaccine given at birth protects babies against tuberculosis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a tool. What is the use of the above tool to crop farmers? A: watering crops (seedlings). A watering can is used to sprinkle water on crops and young seedlings.
chunks.source: A watering can is used to sprinkle water on crops and young seedlings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of bees in a hive that mate with the queen bee: ____. A: drones. Drones are the male bees whose duty is to mate with the queen.
chunks.source: Drones are the male bees whose duty is to mate with the queen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one structural difference between arteries and veins: ____. A: arteries have thick walls while veins have thin walls. Arteries carry blood under high pressure so their walls are thick; veins have thin walls and valves.
chunks.source: Arteries carry blood under high pressure so their walls are thick; veins have thin walls and valves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do some plants like pumpkins climb other plants? ____. A: to get enough sunlight. Climbing plants grow up supports so their leaves can reach sunlight for photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Climbing plants grow up supports so their leaves can reach sunlight for photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a P.6 pupil prevent himself/herself from getting infected with HIV/AIDS? ____. A: by abstaining from sex. Abstinence keeps pupils safe from HIV infection.
chunks.source: Abstinence keeps pupils safe from HIV infection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the component of air used in stopping fire outbreak: ____. A: carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so fire extinguishers release it to put out fires.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so fire extinguishers release it to put out fires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one organ which is damaged when an individual over-depends on alcohol: ____. A: liver. Too much alcohol damages the liver and can cause liver disease.
chunks.source: Too much alcohol damages the liver and can cause liver disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one cause of dehydration among children: ____. A: diarrhoea. Diarrhoea and vomiting make the body lose a lot of water.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea and vomiting make the body lose a lot of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which element of weather is measured using a hygrometer? ____. A: humidity. A hygrometer measures the amount of water vapour (humidity) in the air.
chunks.source: A hygrometer measures the amount of water vapour (humidity) in the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the human body organ found in the head that helps us to remember things: ____. A: brain. The brain controls thinking, memory and all body activities.
chunks.source: The brain controls thinking, memory and all body activities.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one danger of having poor shelter: ____. A: the family is exposed to bad weather. A leaking or weak shelter lets in rain and cold, which can make the family sick.
chunks.source: A leaking or weak shelter lets in rain and cold, which can make the family sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one component of soil: ____. A: humus. Soil is made of humus, air, water and small rock particles.
chunks.source: Soil is made of humus, air, water and small rock particles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one content of a first aid box: ____. A: bandage. A first aid box contains bandages, cotton wool, antiseptic and painkillers.
chunks.source: A first aid box contains bandages, cotton wool, antiseptic and painkillers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one disorder of the digestive system: ____. A: constipation. Constipation, diarrhoea and indigestion are disorders of the digestive system.
chunks.source: Constipation, diarrhoea and indigestion are disorders of the digestive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Layers should be fed on feeds containing enough calcium for ____. A: formation of strong eggshells. Calcium makes the shells of eggs hard and strong.
chunks.source: Calcium makes the shells of eggs hard and strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a plant with parts A, B and C. Which letter shows the structure used by the plant to take in water? ____. A: C. Roots (marked C) absorb water and mineral salts from the soil.
chunks.source: Roots (marked C) absorb water and mineral salts from the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are fire extinguishers painted with bright colours? ____. A: so that they can be easily seen (located). Bright colours make extinguishers easy to find during a fire emergency.
chunks.source: Bright colours make extinguishers easy to find during a fire emergency.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for people to keep their bodies clean? ____. A: to prevent diseases. A clean body has fewer germs that cause diseases.
chunks.source: A clean body has fewer germs that cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one way in which people can destroy their environment: ____. A: deforestation. Cutting down trees and bush burning destroy the environment.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees and bush burning destroy the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a leguminous crop: ____. A: beans. Beans, groundnuts, peas and soya beans are leguminous crops that add nitrogen to soil.
chunks.source: Beans, groundnuts, peas and soya beans are leguminous crops that add nitrogen to soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way in which people can manage rainy weather: ____. A: using umbrellas. Umbrellas, raincoats and gumboots protect people from rain.
chunks.source: Umbrellas, raincoats and gumboots protect people from rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Insects have three main body parts. Give any one of them: ____. A: head. An insect's body has a head, thorax and abdomen.
chunks.source: An insect's body has a head, thorax and abdomen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one activity done at school to prevent the spread of faecal diseases: ____. A: washing hands after visiting the latrine. Washing hands kills germs picked from the latrine.
chunks.source: Washing hands kills germs picked from the latrine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a poultry farmer prevent diseases that attack poultry? ____. A: by vaccinating the birds. Vaccination builds immunity against poultry diseases.
chunks.source: Vaccination builds immunity against poultry diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one insect that stings: ____. A: bee. Bees and wasps sting to defend themselves.
chunks.source: Bees and wasps sting to defend themselves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one natural cause of changes in the environment: ____. A: floods. Floods, drought, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions change the environment naturally.
chunks.source: Floods, drought, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions change the environment naturally.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do clouds bring changes in temperature? ____. A: they block the sun's heat from reaching the earth, making it cooler. Clouds act like a shade, reducing the sunshine that warms the ground.
chunks.source: Clouds act like a shade, reducing the sunshine that warms the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the sense organ that helps one to detect a dog barking: ____. A: ear. The ear detects sound such as a dog barking.
chunks.source: The ear detects sound such as a dog barking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one source of water: ____. A: rain. Rain, wells, boreholes and rivers are sources of water.
chunks.source: Rain, wells, boreholes and rivers are sources of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of energy possessed by a moving object: ____. A: kinetic energy. Anything that moves has kinetic energy.
chunks.source: Anything that moves has kinetic energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the deficiency disease the person in the diagram is suffering from: ____. A: goitre. The swollen neck (goitre) is caused by lack of iodine in the diet.
chunks.source: The swollen neck (goitre) is caused by lack of iodine in the diet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one element of Primary Health Care: ____. A: immunization. Immunization, safe water and sanitation are elements of Primary Health Care.
chunks.source: Immunization, safe water and sanitation are elements of Primary Health Care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can we prevent accidents that happen in our classrooms? ____. A: by keeping the floor dry and desks well arranged. A tidy, dry classroom with no running prevents falls and injuries.
chunks.source: A tidy, dry classroom with no running prevents falls and injuries.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does boiling make water safe for drinking? ____. A: it kills the germs in the water. Heat destroys the germs that cause water-borne diseases.
chunks.source: Heat destroys the germs that cause water-borne diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one effect of alcohol to an individual: ____. A: it damages the liver. Alcohol can damage the liver and make a person lose self-control.
chunks.source: Alcohol can damage the liver and make a person lose self-control.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should a school have a first aid box? ____. A: to give first aid to injured pupils. A first aid box provides quick treatment before a casualty reaches hospital.
chunks.source: A first aid box provides quick treatment before a casualty reaches hospital.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In one sentence, give the meaning of the term 'plant propagation': ____. A: the process of growing new plants from seeds or plant parts. Propagation is how new plants are produced, e.g. from seeds, suckers or cuttings.
chunks.source: Propagation is how new plants are produced, e.g. from seeds, suckers or cuttings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the banana plant propagated? ____. A: by suckers. Bananas grow from suckers that shoot from the base of the parent plant.
chunks.source: Bananas grow from suckers that shoot from the base of the parent plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is cassava propagated? ____. A: by stem cuttings. Pieces of cassava stem planted in soil grow into new plants.
chunks.source: Pieces of cassava stem planted in soil grow into new plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one plant that produces fibre: ____. A: cotton. Cotton, sisal and flax give fibres used for cloth and ropes.
chunks.source: Cotton, sisal and flax give fibres used for cloth and ropes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why animals move from one place to another: ____. A: to look for food. Animals move to find food, water, shelter, mates and to escape danger.
chunks.source: Animals move to find food, water, shelter, mates and to escape danger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another reason why animals move from one place to another: ____. A: to escape from danger. Animals run away from enemies that want to eat them.
chunks.source: Animals run away from enemies that want to eat them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a snake move? ____. A: by slithering (crawling). A snake has no legs, so it slides along the ground by slithering.
chunks.source: A snake has no legs, so it slides along the ground by slithering.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a frog move? ____. A: by hopping (jumping). A frog jumps with its strong hind legs and can also swim.
chunks.source: A frog jumps with its strong hind legs and can also swim.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List one foodstuff that can be preserved by smoking: ____. A: fish. Fish and meat are preserved by smoking over fire.
chunks.source: Fish and meat are preserved by smoking over fire.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List one foodstuff that can be preserved by sun drying: ____. A: cassava. Cassava, maize and beans are dried in the sun for storage.
chunks.source: Cassava, maize and beans are dried in the sun for storage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List one foodstuff that can be preserved by pasteurization: ____. A: milk. Milk is heated gently (pasteurized) to kill germs and keep longer.
chunks.source: Milk is heated gently (pasteurized) to kill germs and keep longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one importance of preserving food: ____. A: to keep food for a long time. Preserved food does not go bad quickly, so it is available in scarce seasons.
chunks.source: Preserved food does not go bad quickly, so it is available in scarce seasons.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down the first thing you would do when preparing ORS at home: ____. A: wash your hands and the utensils. Clean hands and clean utensils keep germs out of the ORS.
chunks.source: Clean hands and clean utensils keep germs out of the ORS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one material used in making ORS: ____. A: sugar. ORS is made by dissolving sugar and salt in clean boiled water.
chunks.source: ORS is made by dissolving sugar and salt in clean boiled water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another material used in making ORS: ____. A: salt. Salt replaces the body salts lost during diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Salt replaces the body salts lost during diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is ORS useful to a dehydrated person? ____. A: it replaces the water and salts lost from the body. ORS rehydrates the body by replacing lost fluids and salts.
chunks.source: ORS rehydrates the body by replacing lost fluids and salts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a musical instrument. Name the musical instrument above: ____. A: xylophone. A xylophone is made of wooden bars of different lengths arranged in order.
chunks.source: A xylophone is made of wooden bars of different lengths arranged in order.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the instrument above produce sound? ____. A: by hitting the bars with mallets (sticks). Striking a bar makes it vibrate and produce sound.
chunks.source: Striking a bar makes it vibrate and produce sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the bar which will produce the lowest pitch: ____. A: E. Likely answer: E. The longest bar vibrates slowest and gives the lowest pitch; E appears to be the longest bar.
chunks.source: Likely answer: E. The longest bar vibrates slowest and gives the lowest pitch; E appears to be the longest bar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which group of musical instruments does it belong? ____. A: percussion. The xylophone is a percussion instrument because sound is made by hitting it.
chunks.source: The xylophone is a percussion instrument because sound is made by hitting it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the role of the human heart: ____. A: to pump blood to all parts of the body. The heart pumps blood carrying oxygen and food to every body part.
chunks.source: The heart pumps blood carrying oxygen and food to every body part.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the blood component that transports oxygen to all body parts: ____. A: red blood cells. Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to all body parts.
chunks.source: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to all body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which you can increase the amount of blood in your body: ____. A: eating foods rich in iron such as meat and green vegetables. Iron helps the body make more red blood cells.
chunks.source: Iron helps the body make more red blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another way in which you can increase the amount of blood in your body: ____. A: drinking plenty of fluids. Fluids increase the liquid part of blood.
chunks.source: Fluids increase the liquid part of blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one disease that results from active smoking: ____. A: lung cancer. Smoking damages the lungs and can cause lung cancer.
chunks.source: Smoking damages the lungs and can cause lung cancer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why people smoke: ____. A: peer pressure. Some people start smoking because friends influence them.
chunks.source: Some people start smoking because friends influence them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another reason why people smoke: ____. A: to relieve stress. Some people wrongly believe smoking reduces stress.
chunks.source: Some people wrongly believe smoking reduces stress.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one life skill that can safeguard you against smoking: ____. A: assertiveness (saying no). Being assertive helps you refuse cigarettes confidently.
chunks.source: Being assertive helps you refuse cigarettes confidently.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagrams show garden tools. Name the garden tool marked A: ____. A: hoe. A hoe is used for digging and weeding in the garden.
chunks.source: A hoe is used for digging and weeding in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the garden tool marked B: ____. A: axe. An axe is used for cutting wood.
chunks.source: An axe is used for cutting wood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of tool marked B at home: ____. A: splitting firewood. The axe splits logs into firewood for cooking.
chunks.source: The axe splits logs into firewood for cooking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way of caring for garden tool A: ____. A: clean it after use and keep it in a dry place. Cleaning and dry storage prevent the hoe from rusting.
chunks.source: Cleaning and dry storage prevent the hoe from rusting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write AIDS in full: ____. A: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome. AIDS is the disease caused by HIV when body immunity is destroyed.
chunks.source: AIDS is the disease caused by HIV when body immunity is destroyed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write HIV in full: ____. A: Human Immunodeficiency Virus. HIV is the virus that causes AIDS.
chunks.source: HIV is the virus that causes AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is PIASCY useful to school children? ____. A: it sensitizes them about HIV/AIDS. PIASCY teaches school children how HIV spreads and how to avoid it.
chunks.source: PIASCY teaches school children how HIV spreads and how to avoid it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one PIASCY message: ____. A: Abstain from sex. Abstinence messages protect school children from HIV.
chunks.source: Abstinence messages protect school children from HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is of the reproductive system of a woman. Name the part marked A: ____. A: uterus (womb). The uterus is where the baby grows during pregnancy.
chunks.source: The uterus is where the baby grows during pregnancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part marked C: ____. A: vagina (birth canal). The vagina is the passage through which the baby is born.
chunks.source: The vagina is the passage through which the baby is born.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of the part marked with letter A: ____. A: it holds and nourishes the growing baby. The foetus develops inside the uterus until birth.
chunks.source: The foetus develops inside the uterus until birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one sexually transmitted disease that attacks the system above: ____. A: gonorrhoea. Gonorrhoea, syphilis and HIV attack the reproductive system.
chunks.source: Gonorrhoea, syphilis and HIV attack the reproductive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do hookworms enter our bodies? ____. A: through the feet (they penetrate bare skin). Hookworm larvae in soil enter through bare feet.
chunks.source: Hookworm larvae in soil enter through bare feet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one danger of hookworms to people: ____. A: they cause anaemia. Hookworms suck blood, making the person anaemic and weak.
chunks.source: Hookworms suck blood, making the person anaemic and weak.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one health habit that can help people to avoid worm infestation: ____. A: wearing shoes. Shoes stop hookworms entering through the feet.
chunks.source: Shoes stop hookworms entering through the feet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down another health habit that can help people to avoid worm infestation: ____. A: washing hands before eating. Clean hands keep worm eggs out of food.
chunks.source: Clean hands keep worm eggs out of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one material farmers use to mulch a garden: ____. A: dry grass. Dry grass, banana leaves and coffee husks are used as mulch.
chunks.source: Dry grass, banana leaves and coffee husks are used as mulch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another material farmers use to mulch a garden: ____. A: banana leaves. Banana leaves spread on soil keep moisture and stop weeds.
chunks.source: Banana leaves spread on soil keep moisture and stop weeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one importance of mulching: ____. A: it keeps moisture in the soil. Mulch covers soil so water does not evaporate quickly.
chunks.source: Mulch covers soil so water does not evaporate quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another importance of mulching: ____. A: it controls weeds. Mulch blocks sunlight so weeds cannot grow.
chunks.source: Mulch blocks sunlight so weeds cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the diseases in A to B correctly: Yellow fever, Malaria, Sleeping sickness, Dysentery. A: Yellow fever: virus; Malaria: plasmodium; Sleeping sickness: trypanosomes; Dysentery: amoeba. Yellow fever is caused by a virus, malaria by plasmodium, sleeping sickness by trypanosomes and dysentery by amoeba.
chunks.source: Yellow fever is caused by a virus, malaria by plasmodium, sleeping sickness by trypanosomes and dysentery by amoeba.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is food taboo? ____. A: a belief (custom) that forbids people from eating certain foods. Some cultures forbid eating foods like eggs or chicken.
chunks.source: Some cultures forbid eating foods like eggs or chicken.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does food taboo lead to malnutritional diseases? ____. A: people miss important nutrients found in the forbidden foods. Avoiding nutritious foods can cause deficiency diseases.
chunks.source: Avoiding nutritious foods can cause deficiency diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one advantage of food taboo: ____. A: it preserves culture (customs). Food taboos keep some cultural practices alive.
chunks.source: Food taboos keep some cultural practices alive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one effect of poor feeding to babies: ____. A: stunted growth. Poorly fed babies do not grow well and fall sick easily.
chunks.source: Poorly fed babies do not grow well and fall sick easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the instrument we can use to see bacteria: ____. A: microscope. Bacteria are too small to see, so we use a microscope.
chunks.source: Bacteria are too small to see, so we use a microscope.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way in which bacteria are useful to people: ____. A: they are used to make yoghurt and cheese. Some bacteria ferment milk into yoghurt and help decompose waste.
chunks.source: Some bacteria ferment milk into yoghurt and help decompose waste.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State another way in which bacteria are useful to people: ____. A: they decompose dead matter (adding humus to soil). Decomposer bacteria rot dead plants and animals, enriching the soil.
chunks.source: Decomposer bacteria rot dead plants and animals, enriching the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are bacteria different from yeast in terms of reproduction? ____. A: bacteria reproduce by binary fission while yeast reproduces by budding. Bacteria split into two equal parts; yeast grows a small bud that breaks off.
chunks.source: Bacteria split into two equal parts; yeast grows a small bud that breaks off.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of wood fuel commonly used by people in Uganda: ____. A: firewood. Firewood and charcoal are the common wood fuels used in Uganda.
chunks.source: Firewood and charcoal are the common wood fuels used in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Root crops store their food in the roots. Suggest one way people prepare such foodstuffs for eating: ____. A: boiling (peeling and boiling). Root crops like cassava are peeled and boiled before eating.
chunks.source: Root crops like cassava are peeled and boiled before eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which state of matter are the molecules closely attached together? ____. A: solid. In solids the particles are packed closely and only vibrate in position.
chunks.source: In solids the particles are packed closely and only vibrate in position.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one sound storage device that can produce sound in a computer: ____. A: flash disk. Flash disks, CDs and memory cards store sound that a computer can play.
chunks.source: Flash disks, CDs and memory cards store sound that a computer can play.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Eyes, brain, ears, stomach, urinary bladder, heart, lungs, liver and kidneys are major body organs. State one function of the kidneys: ____. A: they filter waste materials from the blood. The kidneys remove waste and excess water from blood as urine.
chunks.source: The kidneys remove waste and excess water from blood as urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the garden tool drawn below: ____. A: spade. A spade is used for digging and lifting soil.
chunks.source: A spade is used for digging and lifting soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one type of poultry commonly kept in Uganda today: ____. A: layers. Layers (for eggs), broilers (for meat) and local chicken are kept in Uganda.
chunks.source: Layers (for eggs), broilers (for meat) and local chicken are kept in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one negative effect of bush burning to the environment: ____. A: it destroys soil fertility. Bush burning kills soil organisms and burns the humus in soil.
chunks.source: Bush burning kills soil organisms and burns the humus in soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one behaviour or habit that can maintain good working conditions of the digestive system: ____. A: chewing food well. Chewing food properly and eating on time keep the digestive system working well.
chunks.source: Chewing food properly and eating on time keep the digestive system working well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which stage in the life cycle of a mosquito is very dangerous to human life? ____. A: the adult stage. The adult female mosquito bites people and spreads malaria.
chunks.source: The adult female mosquito bites people and spreads malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way of controlling intestinal worms in people: ____. A: deworming regularly. Taking deworming tablets kills intestinal worms.
chunks.source: Taking deworming tablets kills intestinal worms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagrams show two different charcoal stoves (sigiri). How does the use of stove A conserve our environment? A: it uses less charcoal, so fewer trees are cut down. An improved stove saves charcoal, which saves the trees charcoal is made from.
chunks.source: An improved stove saves charcoal, which saves the trees charcoal is made from.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down the weapon that can be used by a wasp to defend itself from its enemies: ____. A: its sting. A wasp stings its enemies to defend itself.
chunks.source: A wasp stings its enemies to defend itself.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An accident is a sudden happening that causes harm to the body. Describe one effect of accidents to people: ____. A: they cause injuries (and can cause death). Accidents injure the body and may leave a person disabled.
chunks.source: Accidents injure the body and may leave a person disabled.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The immunisation schedule in Uganda is free and mandatory. Identify one group of people who must be immunised: ____. A: children under five (infants). Babies and young children are immunised against killer diseases.
chunks.source: Babies and young children are immunised against killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows an animal kept at home. Give one common product people who keep such animals can get: ____. A: meat. Rabbits are kept for meat and also give skins and manure.
chunks.source: Rabbits are kept for meat and also give skins and manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does smoking tobacco affect the lungs of people who smoke? ____. A: it damages the lungs (and can cause lung cancer). Tobacco smoke destroys lung tissue and can cause lung cancer.
chunks.source: Tobacco smoke destroys lung tissue and can cause lung cancer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Soil is the top layer of the earth's surface. How does it help people in our community to survive? ____. A: it supports the crops we eat. People grow food crops in soil, which feeds the community.
chunks.source: People grow food crops in soil, which feeds the community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Air is a mixture of gases. What term is given to air in motion? ____. A: wind. Moving air is called wind.
chunks.source: Moving air is called wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from water, name one other item people use to keep their bodies clean: ____. A: soap. Soap removes dirt and germs from the body.
chunks.source: Soap removes dirt and germs from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one food processing method in which yeast plays a big role: ____. A: baking (bread making). Yeast makes dough rise when baking bread.
chunks.source: Yeast makes dough rise when baking bread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: During the preparation of ORS, sugar and salt are dissolved in the water. Give one use of sugar to the patient who drinks ORS: ____. A: it gives the patient energy. Sugar in ORS provides energy to the weak patient.
chunks.source: Sugar in ORS provides energy to the weak patient.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Light and heat from the sun is known as sunshine. State one use of the light to plants in the environment: ____. A: for photosynthesis (making food). Plants use sunlight to make their food.
chunks.source: Plants use sunlight to make their food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one way of killing germs in water: ____. A: boiling. Boiling kills the germs in water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which kind of blood cells are attacked by plasmodium that causes malaria fever? ____. A: red blood cells. Malaria parasites destroy red blood cells, causing fever and anaemia.
chunks.source: Malaria parasites destroy red blood cells, causing fever and anaemia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Farmers carry out different practices on their farms. What is gap-filling as used in crop farming? ____. A: replacing dead seedlings (planting where seeds failed to germinate). Gap-filling keeps the plant population correct in the garden.
chunks.source: Gap-filling keeps the plant population correct in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a burning candle. What type of change does the wax undergo when the candle is burning? ____. A: physical change. The wax melts, which is a physical change because no new substance is formed.
chunks.source: The wax melts, which is a physical change because no new substance is formed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write HIV in full: ____. A: Human Immunodeficiency Virus. HIV is the virus that causes AIDS.
chunks.source: HIV is the virus that causes AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one communicable disease that spreads through air: ____. A: tuberculosis. Tuberculosis, influenza and measles spread through the air.
chunks.source: Tuberculosis, influenza and measles spread through the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are locusts dangerous to plants? ____. A: they eat and destroy crops. Swarms of locusts feed on green plants and can clear whole gardens.
chunks.source: Swarms of locusts feed on green plants and can clear whole gardens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one disorder of the human teeth: ____. A: tooth decay (dental caries). Tooth decay and misaligned teeth are disorders of the teeth.
chunks.source: Tooth decay and misaligned teeth are disorders of the teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Petero started a simple tree planting project at home. Describe one importance of the project he started to his family: ____. A: it provides firewood (fruits, shade and income). Trees give the family firewood, fruits, timber and fresh air.
chunks.source: Trees give the family firewood, fruits, timber and fresh air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the deficiency disease due to lack of vitamin A: ____. A: night blindness. Lack of vitamin A makes it hard to see at night.
chunks.source: Lack of vitamin A makes it hard to see at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a snail regarded as an invertebrate? ____. A: because it has no backbone. Animals without backbones are called invertebrates.
chunks.source: Animals without backbones are called invertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of soil whose texture is rough and has large particles: ____. A: sandy soil. Sandy soil has large rough particles and drains water fast.
chunks.source: Sandy soil has large rough particles and drains water fast.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of change takes place when a plant bears fruits? ____. A: biological change. Fruiting involves growth, which is a biological change.
chunks.source: Fruiting involves growth, which is a biological change.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way people can protect themselves against rainy weather: ____. A: using umbrellas. Umbrellas and raincoats keep people dry in the rain.
chunks.source: Umbrellas and raincoats keep people dry in the rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one similarity between burning and rusting: ____. A: both need oxygen (and both are chemical changes). Burning and rusting both use oxygen and form new substances.
chunks.source: Burning and rusting both use oxygen and form new substances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a maize grain. Name the part marked with letter P: ____. A: embryo (radicle - the part that develops into the root system). Likely answer: the embryo (radicle). The label P points to the lower pointed part of the grain where the embryo sits; the radicle grows into the root.
chunks.source: Likely answer: the embryo (radicle). The label P points to the lower pointed part of the grain where the embryo sits; the radicle grows into the root.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the diseases with the vectors that spread them correctly: Malaria, Bilharzia, Elephantiasis, River blindness. A: Malaria: Anopheles mosquito; Bilharzia: Water snail; Elephantiasis: Culex mosquito; River blindness: Black fly. Malaria is spread by the Anopheles mosquito, bilharzia by water snails, elephantiasis by the Culex mosquito and river blindness by the black fly.
chunks.source: Malaria is spread by the Anopheles mosquito, bilharzia by water snails, elephantiasis by the Culex mosquito and river blindness by the black fly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is Primary Health Care? ____. A: essential health care made available to all people. Primary Health Care brings basic health services within reach of every community.
chunks.source: Primary Health Care brings basic health services within reach of every community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one element of PHC: ____. A: immunization. PHC elements include immunization, safe water, sanitation and nutrition education.
chunks.source: PHC elements include immunization, safe water, sanitation and nutrition education.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down another element of PHC: ____. A: provision of safe water. Safe water prevents water-borne diseases.
chunks.source: Safe water prevents water-borne diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one activity in which an individual can promote PHC in the community where he/she lives: ____. A: encouraging people to use latrines. Using latrines and keeping the environment clean promotes community health.
chunks.source: Using latrines and keeping the environment clean promotes community health.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A stone of 98g was lowered into a measuring cylinder and the water level rose from 18ml to 32ml. Find the volume of the stone: ____. A: 14 ml. Volume = 32 ml - 18 ml = 14 ml of water displaced.
chunks.source: Volume = 32 ml - 18 ml = 14 ml of water displaced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why did the stone sink in water? ____. A: because it is denser than water. Objects denser than water sink in it.
chunks.source: Objects denser than water sink in it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one substance that can float on water: ____. A: wood. Wood is less dense than water so it floats.
chunks.source: Wood is less dense than water so it floats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows an insect that is a delicacy in Central Uganda. Name it: ____. A: nsenene (grasshopper). Nsenene is the edible grasshopper enjoyed as a delicacy in Central Uganda.
chunks.source: Nsenene is the edible grasshopper enjoyed as a delicacy in Central Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one characteristic of the above insect: ____. A: it has six legs. Like all insects, nsenene has six legs and three body parts.
chunks.source: Like all insects, nsenene has six legs and three body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one food for the above insect: ____. A: grass (leaves). Nsenene feeds on grass and green leaves.
chunks.source: Nsenene feeds on grass and green leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which form of energy do people use to catch many of them for business or sale? ____. A: light energy. Bright lights are used at night to attract nsenene for catching.
chunks.source: Bright lights are used at night to attract nsenene for catching.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is breast feeding? ____. A: feeding a baby on breast milk. Breast milk is the best food for babies.
chunks.source: Breast milk is the best food for babies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Describe one advantage of bottle feeding to a working class mother: ____. A: the baby can be fed by another person while she is at work. Expressed milk in a bottle lets another caregiver feed the baby.
chunks.source: Expressed milk in a bottle lets another caregiver feed the baby.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of weaning food: ____. A: porridge. Weaning foods like porridge and mashed bananas are introduced gradually.
chunks.source: Weaning foods like porridge and mashed bananas are introduced gradually.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another example of weaning food: ____. A: mashed bananas. Soft mashed foods are easy for babies to swallow.
chunks.source: Soft mashed foods are easy for babies to swallow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is soil erosion? ____. A: the carrying away of top soil by water or wind. Running water and wind remove the fertile top soil.
chunks.source: Running water and wind remove the fertile top soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one type of soil erosion: ____. A: sheet erosion. Sheet, rill and gully erosion are types of soil erosion.
chunks.source: Sheet, rill and gully erosion are types of soil erosion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another type of soil erosion: ____. A: gully erosion. Gully erosion cuts deep channels in the land.
chunks.source: Gully erosion cuts deep channels in the land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one cause of soil erosion in the environment: ____. A: deforestation. Cutting trees leaves soil bare so rain washes it away.
chunks.source: Cutting trees leaves soil bare so rain washes it away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why people keep goats in Uganda: ____. A: for meat. Goats are kept for meat, milk and income.
chunks.source: Goats are kept for meat, milk and income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another reason why people keep goats in Uganda: ____. A: for milk. Goat milk is drunk and sold.
chunks.source: Goat milk is drunk and sold.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one breed of goats kept in Uganda: ____. A: Boer. Boer, Mubende and Small East African are goat breeds in Uganda.
chunks.source: Boer, Mubende and Small East African are goat breeds in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one disease that attacks both goats and sheep: ____. A: anthrax. Anthrax attacks goats, sheep and cattle.
chunks.source: Anthrax attacks goats, sheep and cattle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: On the medical instrument below (a clinical thermometer), the part that prevents back flow of mercury is marked ____. A: K. The kink (marked K) stops mercury flowing back into the bulb so the reading stays.
chunks.source: The kink (marked K) stops mercury flowing back into the bulb so the reading stays.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the role of the above instrument to a doctor? ____. A: to measure body temperature. A clinical thermometer tells the doctor whether a patient has fever.
chunks.source: A clinical thermometer tells the doctor whether a patient has fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of part marked with letter K: ____. A: it prevents the back flow of mercury. The kink holds the mercury in place so the temperature can be read.
chunks.source: The kink holds the mercury in place so the temperature can be read.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does the doctor shake the above instrument before using it? ____. A: to bring the mercury below 35 degrees (to reset it). Shaking returns the mercury to the bulb for a fresh reading.
chunks.source: Shaking returns the mercury to the bulb for a fresh reading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is immunity? ____. A: the ability of the body to fight diseases. Immunity protects the body against disease germs.
chunks.source: Immunity protects the body against disease germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one type of immunity: ____. A: natural immunity. Natural immunity is inborn; artificial immunity comes from vaccines.
chunks.source: Natural immunity is inborn; artificial immunity comes from vaccines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a person acquire the type of immunity you have named above? ____. A: by birth (it is inherited from parents). Natural immunity is passed from parents to children.
chunks.source: Natural immunity is passed from parents to children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one place in our community where we take children for immunization: ____. A: health centre. Children are immunised at health centres and hospitals.
chunks.source: Children are immunised at health centres and hospitals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the animal that breathes through moist skin is the ____. A: earthworm. Earthworms breathe through their moist skins.
chunks.source: Earthworms breathe through their moist skins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the breathing organ of a housefly is the ____. A: spiracles. Insects breathe through tiny holes called spiracles.
chunks.source: Insects breathe through tiny holes called spiracles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the animal that breathes through gills is the ____. A: fish. Fish breathe in water using gills.
chunks.source: Fish breathe in water using gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the breathing organ of a cow is the ____. A: lungs. Cows, like all mammals, breathe with lungs.
chunks.source: Cows, like all mammals, breathe with lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one example of root crops in the environment: ____. A: cassava. Cassava and sweet potatoes store food in their roots.
chunks.source: Cassava and sweet potatoes store food in their roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another example of root crops in the environment: ____. A: sweet potatoes. Sweet potatoes are root tubers eaten boiled or roasted.
chunks.source: Sweet potatoes are root tubers eaten boiled or roasted.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one disease that attacks root crops: ____. A: cassava mosaic. Cassava mosaic disease makes cassava leaves mottled and reduces yields.
chunks.source: Cassava mosaic disease makes cassava leaves mottled and reduces yields.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Describe one way farmers can preserve harvested root crops for a long time: ____. A: drying them in the sun. Sun-dried cassava chips keep for a long time.
chunks.source: Sun-dried cassava chips keep for a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of the kidney: ____. A: it filters waste materials from the blood. The kidneys remove waste as urine.
chunks.source: The kidneys remove waste as urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of the brain: ____. A: it controls all body activities (thinking and memory). The brain is the control centre of the body.
chunks.source: The brain is the control centre of the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one way of caring for the human eyes: ____. A: washing the face with clean water. Clean water removes dust that irritates the eyes.
chunks.source: Clean water removes dust that irritates the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one disease that attacks the human eyes: ____. A: trachoma. Trachoma and conjunctivitis attack the eyes.
chunks.source: Trachoma and conjunctivitis attack the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a diurnal insect (active in day time): ____. A: housefly. Houseflies and bees are active during the day.
chunks.source: Houseflies and bees are active during the day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a nocturnal insect (active in the night): ____. A: mosquito. Mosquitoes and moths are active at night.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes and moths are active at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one use of insects to people: ____. A: bees give honey. Bees give honey and pollinate crops.
chunks.source: Bees give honey and pollinate crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one danger of insects to people: ____. A: they spread diseases. Mosquitoes and houseflies spread diseases like malaria and cholera.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes and houseflies spread diseases like malaria and cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of the seed develops into the shoot system? ____. A: plumule. The plumule grows upward into the shoot while the radicle becomes the root.
chunks.source: The plumule grows upward into the shoot while the radicle becomes the root.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being used as food, give one use of seeds to people and other animals: ____. A: planting. Seeds are planted to grow new crops.
chunks.source: Seeds are planted to grow new crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being used as food, give another use of seeds to people and other animals: ____. A: making oil. Seeds like simsim and groundnuts are pressed for cooking oil.
chunks.source: Seeds like simsim and groundnuts are pressed for cooking oil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What scientific term is given to the ability of a seed to germinate or grow? ____. A: viability. Viability is the ability of a seed to germinate.
chunks.source: Viability is the ability of a seed to germinate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is of a human ear. Where does part labelled J lead to? ____. A: the middle ear (ear drum). The auditory canal (J) leads inward to the ear drum of the middle ear.
chunks.source: The auditory canal (J) leads inward to the ear drum of the middle ear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one part of the ear found in the outer ear: ____. A: pinna. The pinna is the outer flap that collects sound.
chunks.source: The pinna is the outer flap that collects sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one part of the ear found in the middle ear: ____. A: ear drum (ossicles). The middle ear has the ear drum and three tiny bones (ossicles).
chunks.source: The middle ear has the ear drum and three tiny bones (ossicles).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which form of energy does the organ above respond in order to function? ____. A: sound energy. The ear detects sound energy.
chunks.source: The ear detects sound energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one poisonous fungus: ____. A: toadstool. Toadstools are poisonous fungi that look like mushrooms but are harmful when eaten.
chunks.source: Toadstools are poisonous fungi that look like mushrooms but are harmful when eaten.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one domestic animal that neither gives us milk nor meat: ____. A: dog. Dogs are kept for security, not for milk or meat.
chunks.source: Dogs are kept for security, not for milk or meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way in which people can use rabbit urine and dung at home: ____. A: as manure in the garden. Rabbit droppings and urine add nutrients to the soil.
chunks.source: Rabbit droppings and urine add nutrients to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the mineral salt that helps in strengthening of our teeth and bones: ____. A: calcium. Calcium builds strong teeth and bones; it is found in milk.
chunks.source: Calcium builds strong teeth and bones; it is found in milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows roots of a legume. Name the part marked P: ____. A: root nodule. Root nodules on legumes contain bacteria that fix nitrogen into the soil.
chunks.source: Root nodules on legumes contain bacteria that fix nitrogen into the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from bees, mention any other social insect: ____. A: termites. Termites and ants live together in large organised colonies.
chunks.source: Termites and ants live together in large organised colonies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a mosquito similar to reptiles in terms of reproduction? ____. A: both lay eggs. Mosquitoes and reptiles reproduce by laying eggs.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes and reptiles reproduce by laying eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it not good to cut down trees without planting new ones? ____. A: it causes deforestation (loss of rainfall and soil erosion). Cutting trees without replacement destroys forests and brings drought.
chunks.source: Cutting trees without replacement destroys forests and brings drought.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which plant leaves can be useful to people: ____. A: as vegetables. Leaves like cabbage are eaten as vegetables; others are used for mulching.
chunks.source: Leaves like cabbage are eaten as vegetables; others are used for mulching.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one example of dental disorders: ____. A: tooth decay. Tooth decay (cavities) is a common dental disorder.
chunks.source: Tooth decay (cavities) is a common dental disorder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one type of energy you know: ____. A: heat energy. Heat, light, sound and kinetic energy are types of energy.
chunks.source: Heat, light, sound and kinetic energy are types of energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens to a piece of cheese left outside on a sunny day? ____. A: it melts. Heat from the sun melts the cheese.
chunks.source: Heat from the sun melts the cheese.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one advantage of bottle feeding to the mother: ____. A: she can rest or do other work while another person feeds the baby. Bottle feeding lets a caregiver feed the baby when the mother is busy.
chunks.source: Bottle feeding lets a caregiver feed the baby when the mother is busy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way we can care for wild animals: ____. A: by protecting forests (their natural habitats). Wild animals survive when their homes are not destroyed.
chunks.source: Wild animals survive when their homes are not destroyed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one plant habitat: ____. A: garden. Gardens, forests and swamps are places where plants grow.
chunks.source: Gardens, forests and swamps are places where plants grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one reason why farmers sow their seeds during the wet season: ____. A: so that the seeds get enough water to germinate. Seeds need water to germinate and grow.
chunks.source: Seeds need water to germinate and grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part that protects the gills of a fish from mechanical injuries: ____. A: operculum (gill cover). The hard gill cover shields the delicate gills.
chunks.source: The hard gill cover shields the delicate gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the missing word to complete the life cycle of a cockroach: Eggs -> ____ -> Adult. A: nymph. A cockroach hatches into a nymph, which grows into an adult. (The diagram was vector-drawn and not extractable.)
chunks.source: A cockroach hatches into a nymph, which grows into an adult. (The diagram was vector-drawn and not extractable.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one disease that people who live in a home without a latrine are likely to suffer from: ____. A: cholera. Without a latrine, faeces spread germs that cause cholera and diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Without a latrine, faeces spread germs that cause cholera and diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is free range system of keeping poultry not common in the capital city of Uganda? ____. A: there is no enough space (and birds may be stolen). Towns have small plots, so free-ranging birds would stray and cause dirt.
chunks.source: Towns have small plots, so free-ranging birds would stray and cause dirt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part of blood which carries oxygen to all body parts: ____. A: red blood cells. Red blood cells pick oxygen from the lungs and deliver it everywhere.
chunks.source: Red blood cells pick oxygen from the lungs and deliver it everywhere.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is bush burning as a method of clearing land discouraged? ____. A: it destroys soil fertility and kills soil organisms. Fire burns humus and beneficial organisms in the soil.
chunks.source: Fire burns humus and beneficial organisms in the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can the dangers of drought be controlled in Uganda? ____. A: by irrigation (and planting trees). Irrigation gives crops water when rain fails; trees attract rain.
chunks.source: Irrigation gives crops water when rain fails; trees attract rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part of a plant from which seeds are formed: ____. A: flower (ovary). After pollination, the flower's ovary develops into fruits with seeds.
chunks.source: After pollination, the flower's ovary develops into fruits with seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does water pass through sandy soil faster than clay soil? ____. A: sandy soil has large particles with large air spaces. Big spaces between sand particles let water drain through quickly.
chunks.source: Big spaces between sand particles let water drain through quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one way in which people may prepare cassava for eating: ____. A: boiling. Cassava is peeled and boiled before eating.
chunks.source: Cassava is peeled and boiled before eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one breed of goats reared in Uganda: ____. A: Boer. Boer, Mubende and Small East African goats are reared in Uganda.
chunks.source: Boer, Mubende and Small East African goats are reared in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a garden tool. How is the above garden tool useful to farmers? A: for loosening soil (and weeding). A hand fork loosens soil and removes weeds around crops.
chunks.source: A hand fork loosens soil and removes weeds around crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of an object that floats on water: ____. A: wood. Wood is less dense than water, so it floats.
chunks.source: Wood is less dense than water, so it floats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the digestive juice which is added to food in the mouth: ____. A: saliva. Saliva moistens food and starts digesting starch.
chunks.source: Saliva moistens food and starts digesting starch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one insect vector that may spread more than one disease to people: ____. A: mosquito. Mosquitoes spread malaria, elephantiasis and yellow fever.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes spread malaria, elephantiasis and yellow fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is of a charcoal stove of clay. Of what importance is the hole marked M when using the stove above? A: it lets in air to support burning (and is used to put in charcoal and remove ash). The opening admits oxygen for burning and charcoal is fed through it.
chunks.source: The opening admits oxygen for burning and charcoal is fed through it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one thing we can make from sisal: ____. A: ropes. Sisal fibres are twisted into ropes, mats and baskets.
chunks.source: Sisal fibres are twisted into ropes, mats and baskets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one problem of poor personal hygiene: ____. A: bad body smell. Poor hygiene causes bad smell and skin diseases.
chunks.source: Poor hygiene causes bad smell and skin diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one economic importance of mosquitoes to people: ____. A: their larvae are food for fish (which people keep for food and income). Likely answer: mosquito larvae feed fish, and fish farming earns income. (Best-effort answer; the booklet gives no key.)
chunks.source: Likely answer: mosquito larvae feed fish, and fish farming earns income. (Best-effort answer; the booklet gives no key.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which element of PHC helps to control rapid population growth? ____. A: family planning. Family planning helps families have the number of children they can care for.
chunks.source: Family planning helps families have the number of children they can care for.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What should a rabbit farmer do to prevent his rabbits from catching diseases? ____. A: vaccinate them (and keep the hutches clean). Vaccination and clean hutches keep rabbits healthy.
chunks.source: Vaccination and clean hutches keep rabbits healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How many pairs of legs has a spider? ____. A: four pairs. Spiders are arachnids with eight legs in four pairs.
chunks.source: Spiders are arachnids with eight legs in four pairs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a percussion musical instrument: ____. A: drum. Drums and xylophones are played by hitting them.
chunks.source: Drums and xylophones are played by hitting them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the practice 'No spitting in public' prevent and control the spread of common diseases? ____. A: it stops germs in saliva (like TB germs) from spreading to others. Spitting spreads germs through the air to people nearby.
chunks.source: Spitting spreads germs through the air to people nearby.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one use of the urinary bladder: ____. A: it stores urine. Urine made by the kidneys is stored in the bladder before release.
chunks.source: Urine made by the kidneys is stored in the bladder before release.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one use of the stomach: ____. A: it churns and digests food. The stomach mixes food with juices to digest it.
chunks.source: The stomach mixes food with juices to digest it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one functional similarity between the ear and the brain: ____. A: both receive and send messages (impulses) through nerves. Likely answer: both work with nerves carrying messages. The ear sends sound messages to the brain, which interprets them.
chunks.source: Likely answer: both work with nerves carrying messages. The ear sends sound messages to the brain, which interprets them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one habit that may endanger or bring trouble to the human liver: ____. A: excessive drinking of alcohol. Too much alcohol damages the liver.
chunks.source: Too much alcohol damages the liver.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows an experiment carried out on a plant (a potted plant covered with polythene paper). What was the experiment about? ____. A: transpiration. The experiment shows that leaves give off water (transpiration), which collects on the polythene.
chunks.source: The experiment shows that leaves give off water (transpiration), which collects on the polythene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the purpose of the polythene paper in the experiment above? ____. A: to trap (collect) the water vapour given off by the leaves. The polythene traps water vapour so it can be seen as droplets.
chunks.source: The polythene traps water vapour so it can be seen as droplets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one factor that determines the rate of the above process: ____. A: temperature. High temperature, wind, light and low humidity increase transpiration.
chunks.source: High temperature, wind, light and low humidity increase transpiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another factor that determines the rate of the above process: ____. A: humidity. Dry air (low humidity) makes transpiration faster.
chunks.source: Dry air (low humidity) makes transpiration faster.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which season of the year do farmers usually mulch their gardens? ____. A: dry season. Mulch keeps soil moisture during the dry season.
chunks.source: Mulch keeps soil moisture during the dry season.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one reason why farmers mulch their gardens: ____. A: to keep moisture in the soil. Mulch stops water evaporating from the soil.
chunks.source: Mulch stops water evaporating from the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention another reason why farmers mulch their gardens: ____. A: to control weeds. Mulch blocks sunlight so weeds cannot grow.
chunks.source: Mulch blocks sunlight so weeds cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one disadvantage of mulching a school garden: ____. A: it hides pests (and can make crops rot). Pests hide under mulch and attack crops unnoticed.
chunks.source: Pests hide under mulch and attack crops unnoticed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a thermometer. What name is given to the thermometer above? ____. A: clinical thermometer. A clinical thermometer is used to measure body temperature.
chunks.source: A clinical thermometer is used to measure body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of part marked with letter R: ____. A: it prevents the back flow of mercury. The kink (R) holds mercury in place so the reading can be taken.
chunks.source: The kink (R) holds mercury in place so the reading can be taken.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the liquid commonly used in the above thermometer: ____. A: mercury. Mercury expands evenly with heat, making it good for thermometers.
chunks.source: Mercury expands evenly with heat, making it good for thermometers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a doctor sterilize the above thermometer after use? ____. A: by dipping it in methylated spirit (antiseptic). Spirit kills the germs on the thermometer.
chunks.source: Spirit kills the germs on the thermometer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A farmer recorded how many times a goat and a rabbit ate each food. What was the most favourable food for the rabbit? ____. A: sweet potato leaves. The rabbit ate sweet potato leaves 4 times, more than any other food.
chunks.source: The rabbit ate sweet potato leaves 4 times, more than any other food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What was the most favourable food for the goat? ____. A: sweet potato leaves, grass leaves and maize leaves (tied at 3 times each). Likely answer: the goat ate sweet potato leaves, grass leaves and maize leaves 3 times each - a three-way tie.
chunks.source: Likely answer: the goat ate sweet potato leaves, grass leaves and maize leaves 3 times each - a three-way tie.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What was the least favourable food for the rabbit? ____. A: sorghum leaves. The rabbit ate sorghum leaves 0 times.
chunks.source: The rabbit ate sorghum leaves 0 times.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: If the farmer was to use only one type of food, which one would be the most favourable for both the goat and the rabbit? ____. A: sweet potato leaves. Sweet potato leaves scored highest in total (4 + 3 = 7).
chunks.source: Sweet potato leaves scored highest in total (4 + 3 = 7).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are babies grouped under vulnerable groups of people? ____. A: because their immunity is low (they cannot care for themselves). Babies fall sick easily and depend on others for care.
chunks.source: Babies fall sick easily and depend on others for care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from babies, name one other vulnerable group of people: ____. A: pregnant women. Pregnant women, the elderly and the sick need special care.
chunks.source: Pregnant women, the elderly and the sick need special care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from babies, name another vulnerable group of people: ____. A: the elderly. Old people have weak bodies and need support.
chunks.source: Old people have weak bodies and need support.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should school children be encouraged to feed on fruits and vegetables? ____. A: they provide vitamins that protect the body against diseases. Vitamins in fruits and vegetables keep children healthy.
chunks.source: Vitamins in fruits and vegetables keep children healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a musical instrument. To which group of musical instruments does the above instrument belong? ____. A: string instruments. The adungu (bow harp) makes sound with vibrating strings.
chunks.source: The adungu (bow harp) makes sound with vibrating strings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the strings will produce the highest pitch? ____. A: a. Likely answer: a. The shortest string vibrates fastest and gives the highest pitch.
chunks.source: Likely answer: a. The shortest string vibrates fastest and gives the highest pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the strings will produce the lowest pitch? ____. A: c. Likely answer: c. The longest string vibrates slowest and gives the lowest pitch.
chunks.source: Likely answer: c. The longest string vibrates slowest and gives the lowest pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
