chunks.text: Q: If you want string C to produce a higher pitched sound, what will you do? ____. A: shorten (tighten) the string. A shorter, tighter string vibrates faster and sounds higher.
chunks.source: A shorter, tighter string vibrates faster and sounds higher.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one disorder of the digestive system: ____. A: constipation. Constipation and diarrhoea are disorders of the digestive system.
chunks.source: Constipation and diarrhoea are disorders of the digestive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another disorder of the digestive system: ____. A: diarrhoea. Diarrhoea is the frequent passing of watery stool.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea is the frequent passing of watery stool.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one disease that attacks the digestive system: ____. A: cholera. Cholera and dysentery attack the digestive system.
chunks.source: Cholera and dysentery attack the digestive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another disease that attacks the digestive system: ____. A: dysentery. Dysentery causes bloody diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Dysentery causes bloody diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one craft material got from swamps: ____. A: papyrus. Papyrus, clay and palm leaves are got from swamps for crafts.
chunks.source: Papyrus, clay and palm leaves are got from swamps for crafts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another craft material got from swamps: ____. A: clay. Swamp clay is used for pottery and crafts.
chunks.source: Swamp clay is used for pottery and crafts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from getting craft materials from swamps, give one other use of swamps to people: ____. A: fishing. Swamps provide fish and are a source of water.
chunks.source: Swamps provide fish and are a source of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way can swamps be protected from destruction? ____. A: by avoiding draining them (not dumping waste in them). Swamps survive when people do not drain or pollute them.
chunks.source: Swamps survive when people do not drain or pollute them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one source of food in your community: ____. A: gardens. Gardens and markets are sources of food.
chunks.source: Gardens and markets are sources of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another source of food in your community: ____. A: markets. Food is bought from markets and shops.
chunks.source: Food is bought from markets and shops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is food useful in the human body? Give one way: ____. A: it gives the body energy. Food gives energy and builds the body.
chunks.source: Food gives energy and builds the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is food useful in the human body? Give another way: ____. A: it helps the body to grow. Body-building foods make children grow.
chunks.source: Body-building foods make children grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are germs? ____. A: tiny living things that cause diseases. Germs are so small they can only be seen with a microscope.
chunks.source: Germs are so small they can only be seen with a microscope.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one place where germs are found: ____. A: latrines. Germs live in latrines, rubbish pits and dirty places.
chunks.source: Germs live in latrines, rubbish pits and dirty places.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which germs can be spread: ____. A: through the air. Germs spread through air, dirty water, food and insect vectors.
chunks.source: Germs spread through air, dirty water, food and insect vectors.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another way in which germs can be spread: ____. A: through contaminated water (and food). Drinking dirty water spreads germs like cholera.
chunks.source: Drinking dirty water spreads germs like cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one type of immunity: ____. A: natural immunity. Natural immunity is inborn; artificial immunity comes from vaccines.
chunks.source: Natural immunity is inborn; artificial immunity comes from vaccines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one role of a P.6 child in the immunization program: ____. A: encouraging parents to take babies for immunization. Children can remind adults about immunization days.
chunks.source: Children can remind adults about immunization days.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one disease controlled by immunizing using DPT vaccine: ____. A: diphtheria. DPT protects against diphtheria, whooping cough (pertussis) and tetanus.
chunks.source: DPT protects against diphtheria, whooping cough (pertussis) and tetanus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention another disease controlled by immunizing using DPT vaccine: ____. A: tetanus. Tetanus causes painful muscle stiffness.
chunks.source: Tetanus causes painful muscle stiffness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a parasite worm (tapeworm). Name part labeled H: ____. A: hooks. The tapeworm's head (scolex) has hooks for gripping the intestines.
chunks.source: The tapeworm's head (scolex) has hooks for gripping the intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of part labeled G: ____. A: sucker - for attaching to the intestinal wall. Suckers hold the tapeworm firmly to the intestines.
chunks.source: Suckers hold the tapeworm firmly to the intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do human beings get infected by tape worms? ____. A: by eating undercooked meat containing tapeworm cysts. Half-cooked pork or beef with cysts passes tapeworms to people.
chunks.source: Half-cooked pork or beef with cysts passes tapeworms to people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can tape worm infestation be controlled? ____. A: by cooking meat properly (and deworming regularly). Well-cooked meat has no live cysts; deworming kills the worms.
chunks.source: Well-cooked meat has no live cysts; deworming kills the worms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Germination, burning, melting and evaporation are common changes in the environment. Which of the above changes is a biological change? ____. A: germination. Germination involves a living seed growing, so it is biological.
chunks.source: Germination involves a living seed growing, so it is biological.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one of the above changes that produces a new substance: ____. A: burning. Burning and germination form new substances; melting and evaporation do not.
chunks.source: Burning and germination form new substances; melting and evaporation do not.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another of the above changes that produces a new substance: ____. A: germination. A seedling is a new substance formed from the seed.
chunks.source: A seedling is a new substance formed from the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is evaporation similar to melting? ____. A: both are physical changes (no new substance is formed). Both can be reversed and form no new substance.
chunks.source: Both can be reversed and form no new substance.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which first aid is administered by applying cold water on the affected part? ____. A: burns (and scalds). Cold water cools a burn and stops it going deeper.
chunks.source: Cold water cools a burn and stops it going deeper.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the use of cotton wool in first aid management: ____. A: cleaning wounds. Cotton wool wipes dirt from wounds gently.
chunks.source: Cotton wool wipes dirt from wounds gently.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the use of a bandage in first aid management: ____. A: covering (and tying) wounds. A bandage covers wounds and holds dressings in place.
chunks.source: A bandage covers wounds and holds dressings in place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What first aid can you give to a young child who has swallowed rat poison? ____. A: give plenty of milk (or water) to drink and rush the child to hospital. Milk dilutes the poison; the child needs a doctor urgently.
chunks.source: Milk dilutes the poison; the child needs a doctor urgently.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides water, give one other item used in cleaning our feet: ____. A: soap. Soap removes dirt and germs from the feet.
chunks.source: Soap removes dirt and germs from the feet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the element of weather suitable for removing moisture from harvested cereals: ____. A: sunshine (heat). The sun's heat dries harvested cereals.
chunks.source: The sun's heat dries harvested cereals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does the bird with the beak below feed on? ____. A: flesh (meat). The strong hooked beak is for tearing flesh; such birds are birds of prey.
chunks.source: The strong hooked beak is for tearing flesh; such birds are birds of prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way is crop rotation important to a farmer? ____. A: it controls crop pests and diseases (and keeps soil fertile). Changing crops breaks pest cycles and balances soil nutrients.
chunks.source: Changing crops breaks pest cycles and balances soil nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which gumboots are useful to people during rainy weather: ____. A: they protect the feet from cold dirty water. Gumboots keep feet dry and protect against germs in muddy water.
chunks.source: Gumboots keep feet dry and protect against germs in muddy water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one vaccine given to infants at the age of six weeks: ____. A: DPT. At six weeks babies receive DPT and polio vaccines.
chunks.source: At six weeks babies receive DPT and polio vaccines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the fruit below adapted to its mode of dispersal? ____. A: it is light with feathery hairs (pappus) so wind can carry it. The feathery pappus acts like a parachute, letting wind disperse the fruit.
chunks.source: The feathery pappus acts like a parachute, letting wind disperse the fruit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A solid block of mass 24g was dropped in an overflow can and displaces 12cm3 of water into a measuring cylinder. Find the density of the solid block: ____. A: 2 g/cm3. Density = mass / volume = 24g / 12cm3 = 2 g/cm3.
chunks.source: Density = mass / volume = 24g / 12cm3 = 2 g/cm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which blood vessel transports deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs? ____. A: pulmonary artery. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation.
chunks.source: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a soil profile? ____. A: the vertical arrangement of soil layers (horizons). A soil profile shows the layers of soil from top to bottom.
chunks.source: A soil profile shows the layers of soil from top to bottom.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a mother control and prevent burns at home? ____. A: by keeping hot objects away from children. Keeping fires, hot water and charcoal stoves out of children's reach prevents burns.
chunks.source: Keeping fires, hot water and charcoal stoves out of children's reach prevents burns.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of serving food in clean containers: ____. A: to prevent contamination (germs getting into food). Clean containers keep germs out of food.
chunks.source: Clean containers keep germs out of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of controlling poultry vices on a farm: ____. A: debeaking. Debeaking stops birds pecking each other; enough space and feed also help.
chunks.source: Debeaking stops birds pecking each other; enough space and feed also help.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows part of a plant. The axillary bud grows from the ____. A: leaf axil (the angle between the leaf and the stem). The axillary bud sits in the axil where the leaf joins the stem.
chunks.source: The axillary bud sits in the axil where the leaf joins the stem.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is sorting clothes important to a person washing? ____. A: to stop colours running (and to wash whites separately). Sorting keeps white clothes from being stained by coloured ones.
chunks.source: Sorting keeps white clothes from being stained by coloured ones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a garden tool. State the function of the above garden tool to a farmer: ____. A: cutting (clearing bushes and cutting wood). A panga is used for cutting wood and clearing bushes.
chunks.source: A panga is used for cutting wood and clearing bushes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one danger of electricity at home: ____. A: electric shock. Touching naked wires can shock or even kill a person.
chunks.source: Touching naked wires can shock or even kill a person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Use the diagram of a tape worm. Name part marked K: ____. A: head (scolex). The scolex (head) has hooks and suckers for attaching to the intestines.
chunks.source: The scolex (head) has hooks and suckers for attaching to the intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it easier to control AIDS than controlling malaria? ____. A: AIDS can be avoided by behaviour change, while mosquitoes are hard to eliminate. Abstinence and faithfulness stop HIV; mosquitoes breed everywhere and are hard to wipe out.
chunks.source: Abstinence and faithfulness stop HIV; mosquitoes breed everywhere and are hard to wipe out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are snakes similar to weaver birds in the way they reproduce? ____. A: both lay eggs. Snakes and weaver birds reproduce by laying eggs.
chunks.source: Snakes and weaver birds reproduce by laying eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are coffee and tea grouped under perennial crops? ____. A: because they live and produce for many years. Perennial crops stay in the garden producing for several years.
chunks.source: Perennial crops stay in the garden producing for several years.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from decomposition, how else can soil be formed? ____. A: by weathering of rocks. Rocks break down into small particles that form soil.
chunks.source: Rocks break down into small particles that form soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one place where the soil profile can be seen properly: ____. A: in a deep pit. The soil layers are clearly visible on the walls of a deep pit.
chunks.source: The soil layers are clearly visible on the walls of a deep pit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of soil used in filtration of water: ____. A: sandy soil. Water passes through sand, leaving dirt behind.
chunks.source: Water passes through sand, leaving dirt behind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is of a charcoal box (charcoal iron). Why is part marked X not made up of iron? ____. A: because iron conducts heat and would burn the hand (wood is a poor conductor). The handle (X) is made of wood, which does not conduct heat to the hand.
chunks.source: The handle (X) is made of wood, which does not conduct heat to the hand.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is wax important in the auditory canal? ____. A: it traps dust and germs. Ear wax catches dust and germs before they reach the ear drum.
chunks.source: Ear wax catches dust and germs before they reach the ear drum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which property of air enables a P.6 child to drink soda from a bottle using a straw? ____. A: air exerts pressure. Sucking removes air from the straw and air pressure pushes the soda up.
chunks.source: Sucking removes air from the straw and air pressure pushes the soda up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one advantage of a VIP latrine: ____. A: it controls bad smell (and flies). The vent pipe of a VIP latrine carries away smell and traps flies.
chunks.source: The vent pipe of a VIP latrine carries away smell and traps flies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one sign of crop damage by pests: ____. A: holes in leaves. Pests chew leaves leaving holes, and cut stems.
chunks.source: Pests chew leaves leaving holes, and cut stems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it a good practice for a pupil to wash his/her clothing and beddings? ____. A: to kill germs and lice (and prevent diseases). Washing removes germs, lice and dirt from clothes and beddings.
chunks.source: Washing removes germs, lice and dirt from clothes and beddings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are warm blooded animals? ____. A: animals whose body temperature stays constant. Mammals and birds keep a constant body temperature.
chunks.source: Mammals and birds keep a constant body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is cassava grouped under root tubers? ____. A: because it stores food in swollen roots. Cassava's thick roots store starch, making them tubers.
chunks.source: Cassava's thick roots store starch, making them tubers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way you can separate beans from bean husks: ____. A: winnowing. Wind blows away the light husks while heavy beans fall down.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light husks while heavy beans fall down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the reproduction of a mushroom different from that of bacteria? ____. A: a mushroom reproduces by spores while bacteria reproduce by binary fission. Mushrooms release spores; bacteria split into two.
chunks.source: Mushrooms release spores; bacteria split into two.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way you can maintain the normal functioning of your respiratory system: ____. A: avoid smoking. Smoke damages the lungs; exercise keeps them strong.
chunks.source: Smoke damages the lungs; exercise keeps them strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is distilled water not good for drinking? ____. A: because it lacks mineral salts. Distillation removes the useful mineral salts water should contain.
chunks.source: Distillation removes the useful mineral salts water should contain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the role of the liver during digestion? ____. A: it produces bile. Bile breaks large fat droplets into small ones.
chunks.source: Bile breaks large fat droplets into small ones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a space left in soda bottles? ____. A: to allow for expansion of the soda (gases). Soda expands when warm; the space stops the bottle bursting.
chunks.source: Soda expands when warm; the space stops the bottle bursting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of caring for sheep: ____. A: deworming them regularly. Deworming, shelter and dipping keep sheep healthy.
chunks.source: Deworming, shelter and dipping keep sheep healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match the animals in list A to their habitats in list B correctly: Dog, Cattle, Pig, Lion. A: Dog: Kennel; Cattle: Kraal; Pig: Sty; Lion: Den. Dogs live in kennels, cattle in kraals, pigs in sties and lions in dens.
chunks.source: Dogs live in kennels, cattle in kraals, pigs in sties and lions in dens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is food preservation? ____. A: methods of keeping food from going bad. Preservation stops germs growing in food so it keeps longer.
chunks.source: Preservation stops germs growing in food so it keeps longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from sun drying, mention one other local method of food preservation: ____. A: salting. Salting, smoking and frying are local preservation methods.
chunks.source: Salting, smoking and frying are local preservation methods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from sun drying, mention another local method of food preservation: ____. A: smoking. Smoking removes water so germs cannot grow.
chunks.source: Smoking removes water so germs cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do farmers preserve food? ____. A: to keep it for future use (and avoid wastage). Preserved food is available in seasons of scarcity.
chunks.source: Preserved food is available in seasons of scarcity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a housefly. Give the role of part Q to the insect: ____. A: breathing (gaseous exchange through spiracles). Part Q (spiracles on the abdomen) lets air in and out for breathing.
chunks.source: Part Q (spiracles on the abdomen) lets air in and out for breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the role of part P to the insect: ____. A: flying. Part P (the wing) is used for flight.
chunks.source: Part P (the wing) is used for flight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can the above organism be controlled in pit latrines? ____. A: by keeping the latrine hole covered (and spraying insecticide). Covering the hole and spraying kill or keep away houseflies.
chunks.source: Covering the hole and spraying kill or keep away houseflies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What problem is the insect most likely to face if parts labelled R were cut off? ____. A: it would not be able to smell (detect food and danger). Part R (antennae) senses smell; without them the fly cannot find food.
chunks.source: Part R (antennae) senses smell; without them the fly cannot find food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are crop pests? ____. A: organisms that destroy crops. Pests like locusts and weevils damage growing crops.
chunks.source: Pests like locusts and weevils damage growing crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of crop pests in the garden: ____. A: locusts. Locusts, weevils and caterpillars are crop pests.
chunks.source: Locusts, weevils and caterpillars are crop pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another example of crop pests in the garden: ____. A: weevils. Weevils attack stored and growing crops.
chunks.source: Weevils attack stored and growing crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one way of controlling garden crop pests: ____. A: spraying with pesticides. Pesticides kill crop pests.
chunks.source: Pesticides kill crop pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one disease of the human teeth: ____. A: tooth decay. Tooth decay is a disease that makes holes in teeth.
chunks.source: Tooth decay is a disease that makes holes in teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one disorder of the human teeth: ____. A: misaligned teeth. Likely answer: misaligned teeth. (Best-effort; the booklet gives no key.)
chunks.source: Likely answer: misaligned teeth. (Best-effort; the booklet gives no key.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do you prevent the teeth disease identified above? Give one way: ____. A: brushing teeth regularly. Brushing removes food remains that cause decay.
chunks.source: Brushing removes food remains that cause decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do you prevent the teeth disease identified above? Give another way: ____. A: avoiding sugary foods. Sugar feeds the germs that rot teeth.
chunks.source: Sugar feeds the germs that rot teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows the female reproductive organ. Name the part marked X: ____. A: ovary. The ovary produces eggs (ova).
chunks.source: The ovary produces eggs (ova).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part marked Y: ____. A: vagina (birth canal). The vagina is the passage through which the baby is born.
chunks.source: The vagina is the passage through which the baby is born.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By use of letter N, show the part where fertilization takes place. Fertilization takes place in the ____. A: fallopian tube (oviduct). The egg meets the sperm in the fallopian tube.
chunks.source: The egg meets the sperm in the fallopian tube.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one disease which affects the above organ: ____. A: gonorrhoea. Gonorrhoea and syphilis attack the reproductive system.
chunks.source: Gonorrhoea and syphilis attack the reproductive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write AIDS in full: ____. A: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome. AIDS is the disease caused by HIV.
chunks.source: AIDS is the disease caused by HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What germ causes AIDS among people? ____. A: virus (HIV). The Human Immunodeficiency Virus causes AIDS.
chunks.source: The Human Immunodeficiency Virus causes AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: As a pupil in Primary Six, how can you avoid getting AIDS? ____. A: by abstaining from sex. Abstinence keeps pupils safe from HIV.
chunks.source: Abstinence keeps pupils safe from HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one PIASCY message that can protect school going children from contracting HIV/AIDS: ____. A: Abstain from sex. Abstinence messages protect school children from HIV.
chunks.source: Abstinence messages protect school children from HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides proteins, name one other food value: ____. A: carbohydrates. Carbohydrates, vitamins, fats and minerals are other food values.
chunks.source: Carbohydrates, vitamins, fats and minerals are other food values.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the use of proteins to children: ____. A: for growth and repair of the body. Proteins build muscles and repair worn-out tissues.
chunks.source: Proteins build muscles and repair worn-out tissues.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one effect of poor nutrition to infants: ____. A: stunted growth. Poorly fed infants do not grow well.
chunks.source: Poorly fed infants do not grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write another effect of poor nutrition to infants: ____. A: kwashiorkor. Lack of protein causes kwashiorkor with a swollen belly.
chunks.source: Lack of protein causes kwashiorkor with a swollen belly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a thermometer. Name the kind of thermometer shown above: ____. A: maximum and minimum thermometer. It records the highest and lowest temperatures of the day.
chunks.source: It records the highest and lowest temperatures of the day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the use of the above thermometer at a weather station: ____. A: to measure the highest and lowest temperatures of the day. Weather stations record daily temperature extremes with it.
chunks.source: Weather stations record daily temperature extremes with it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from mercury, name one other liquid used in the above thermometer: ____. A: alcohol. Alcohol is also used in thermometers as it expands with heat.
chunks.source: Alcohol is also used in thermometers as it expands with heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one difference between the above thermometer and a clinical thermometer: ____. A: it has no kink (and measures maximum and minimum temperature) while a clinical thermometer has a kink and measures body temperature. The max-min thermometer has no kink; the clinical one has a kink to hold the reading.
chunks.source: The max-min thermometer has no kink; the clinical one has a kink to hold the reading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who is a first aider? ____. A: a person trained to give first aid. A first aider gives quick help before a doctor arrives.
chunks.source: A first aider gives quick help before a doctor arrives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are first aiders necessary in a school? ____. A: to give quick help to injured pupils. First aiders treat injuries immediately at school.
chunks.source: First aiders treat injuries immediately at school.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the first aid for nose bleeding: ____. A: pinch the nose and lean forward (apply a cold compress). Pinching stops the bleeding; leaning forward stops blood flowing down the throat.
chunks.source: Pinching stops the bleeding; leaning forward stops blood flowing down the throat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should casualties at times be taken to hospital? ____. A: for proper treatment by a doctor. Some injuries need a doctor's care beyond first aid.
chunks.source: Some injuries need a doctor's care beyond first aid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides floods, identify one natural change that can displace people: ____. A: drought. Drought, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions displace people.
chunks.source: Drought, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions displace people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides floods, identify another natural change that can displace people: ____. A: earthquakes. Earthquakes destroy homes, forcing people to move.
chunks.source: Earthquakes destroy homes, forcing people to move.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from displacing people, write one other effect of natural changes: ____. A: they destroy crops and property. Floods and droughts destroy farms and houses.
chunks.source: Floods and droughts destroy farms and houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of controlling floods in your area: ____. A: digging drainage channels (and planting trees). Drainage carries excess water away; trees reduce runoff.
chunks.source: Drainage carries excess water away; trees reduce runoff.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a fish. Which organ of the fish is protected by structure marked H? ____. A: gills. The operculum (H) covers and protects the gills.
chunks.source: The operculum (H) covers and protects the gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part marked L: ____. A: dorsal fin. The dorsal fin is on the back of the fish.
chunks.source: The dorsal fin is on the back of the fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is part labelled K useful to the above animal? ____. A: for swimming (pushing the fish forward and steering). The tail (caudal fin) pushes the fish through water.
chunks.source: The tail (caudal fin) pushes the fish through water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the above animal able to live in water? ____. A: it has gills for breathing and a streamlined body with fins for swimming. Gills take oxygen from water; the streamlined shape and fins aid movement.
chunks.source: Gills take oxygen from water; the streamlined shape and fins aid movement.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides paraffin, mention one fuel used in our homes: ____. A: firewood. Firewood and charcoal are common home fuels.
chunks.source: Firewood and charcoal are common home fuels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides paraffin, mention another fuel used in our homes: ____. A: charcoal. Charcoal is burnt in stoves for cooking.
chunks.source: Charcoal is burnt in stoves for cooking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one danger of using paraffin at home: ____. A: it can cause fire (and poisoning if drunk). Paraffin catches fire easily and is poisonous.
chunks.source: Paraffin catches fire easily and is poisonous.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one way of saving energy at home: ____. A: switching off lights (and appliances) not in use. Unused lights waste electricity.
chunks.source: Unused lights waste electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do bees swarm? Give one reason: ____. A: overcrowding in the hive. Likely answer: overcrowding. (Best-effort; the booklet gives no key.)
chunks.source: Likely answer: overcrowding. (Best-effort; the booklet gives no key.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do bees swarm? Give another reason: ____. A: emergence of a new queen. Likely answer: when a new queen emerges, part of the colony leaves with the old queen. (Best-effort.)
chunks.source: Likely answer: when a new queen emerges, part of the colony leaves with the old queen. (Best-effort.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you prevent bees from swarming? ____. A: by providing enough space (and harvesting honey regularly). Roomy hives and regular harvests keep bees settled.
chunks.source: Roomy hives and regular harvests keep bees settled.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is bee farming regarded as a business? ____. A: because honey is sold for income. Honey and wax earn the farmer money.
chunks.source: Honey and wax earn the farmer money.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can milk be preserved? ____. A: by boiling (and refrigeration). Boiling kills germs in milk so it keeps longer.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs in milk so it keeps longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one product got from milk: ____. A: ghee. Ghee, butter, yoghurt and cheese are made from milk.
chunks.source: Ghee, butter, yoghurt and cheese are made from milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention another product got from milk: ____. A: yoghurt. Milk is fermented to make yoghurt.
chunks.source: Milk is fermented to make yoghurt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from a cow, give one other animal that gives milk: ____. A: goat. Goats also give milk for drinking.
chunks.source: Goats also give milk for drinking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one component of soil that can also be used by animals for breathing: ____. A: Air. Soil has tiny air spaces between its particles, and soil animals such as earthworms breathe this air.
chunks.source: Soil has tiny air spaces between its particles, and soil animals such as earthworms breathe this air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do farmers keep poultry such as chicken? A: To get eggs and meat for food and income. Chickens give families eggs and meat, which can be eaten or sold for money.
chunks.source: Chickens give families eggs and meat, which can be eaten or sold for money.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Describe one way you help a person who is unable to see (a blind man). A: By guiding him, holding his hand when crossing the road. A blind person cannot see dangers on the road, so guiding him by the hand keeps him safe.
chunks.source: A blind person cannot see dangers on the road, so guiding him by the hand keeps him safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the spiny ant eater, mention one other example of monotremes: ____. A: Duck-billed platypus. The duck-billed platypus is a mammal that lays eggs, just like the spiny ant eater.
chunks.source: The duck-billed platypus is a mammal that lays eggs, just like the spiny ant eater.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The human body is made up of many organs. Give any one use of the brain as an organ in the human body. A: It controls all body activities and stores information. The brain is the control centre of the body; it also stores what we learn.
chunks.source: The brain is the control centre of the body; it also stores what we learn.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mary collected water from the well. She filtered and later boiled it. What do you think she was going to use the water for? A: For drinking. Filtering and boiling remove dirt and kill germs, making water safe to drink.
chunks.source: Filtering and boiling remove dirt and kill germs, making water safe to drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: There are many natural changes in our environment such as floods, drought, landslides and earthquakes. Give any one effect of such natural changes. A: They destroy crops, homes and property, and can kill people and animals. Natural disasters damage what people have built and the crops they depend on.
chunks.source: Natural disasters damage what people have built and the crops they depend on.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides saving life, state any one importance of giving first aid to a casualty. A: It reduces pain and stops the injury from getting worse. Quick first aid eases the victim's pain and prevents a small injury from becoming serious.
chunks.source: Quick first aid eases the victim's pain and prevents a small injury from becoming serious.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Calculate the volume of the cuboid shown below (length 5mm, width 2mm, height 6mm): ____. A: 60 cubic millimetres (60mm3). Volume of a cuboid = length x width x height = 5 x 2 x 6 = 60mm3.
chunks.source: Volume of a cuboid = length x width x height = 5 x 2 x 6 = 60mm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a tadpole similar to a fish? A: Both breathe using gills. Tadpoles live in water and, like fish, take in dissolved oxygen through gills.
chunks.source: Tadpoles live in water and, like fish, take in dissolved oxygen through gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How dangerous are cockroaches to people? A: They walk on food and spread germs that cause diseases such as diarrhoea. Cockroaches carry germs from dirty places onto uncovered food, spreading sickness.
chunks.source: Cockroaches carry germs from dirty places onto uncovered food, spreading sickness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following items is used to clean our body? A: Sponge. A sponge is rubbed on the body with soap and water to remove dirt.
chunks.source: A sponge is rubbed on the body with soap and water to remove dirt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the stage in the life cycle of a bee that is able to swarm: ____. A: Adult stage. Swarming is done by a group of adult bees that leave the hive with a queen to start a new colony.
chunks.source: Swarming is done by a group of adult bees that leave the hive with a queen to start a new colony.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is proper ventilation important in a hutch in rabbit keeping? A: It lets in fresh air and removes heat and bad smells that cause diseases. Stale, smelly air in a hutch makes rabbits sick, so fresh air must keep flowing through.
chunks.source: Stale, smelly air in a hutch makes rabbits sick, so fresh air must keep flowing through.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sweets and biscuits are a delicacy for children all over the world. Describe any one danger of eating many of them. A: They cause tooth decay. Sugar left on the teeth feeds germs that eat into the teeth and form holes.
chunks.source: Sugar left on the teeth feeds germs that eat into the teeth and form holes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Immunity is the body's ability to fight against disease causing germs. State any one way people can get immunity. A: Through immunization (vaccination). Vaccines train the body to fight specific germs before the real disease attacks.
chunks.source: Vaccines train the body to fight specific germs before the real disease attacks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A mushroom is a common fungus that many Ugandans eat as sauce. How does a mushroom itself feed? A: It absorbs dissolved food from dead and decaying matter. Mushrooms cannot make their own food, so they feed saprophytically on rotting matter.
chunks.source: Mushrooms cannot make their own food, so they feed saprophytically on rotting matter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are people advised to brush their teeth after every meal? A: To remove food remains that would rot the teeth. Food left between teeth decays and forms acids that eat into the teeth.
chunks.source: Food left between teeth decays and forms acids that eat into the teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The sun is found high up in the sky. State one way people can use the heat from it at home. A: For drying clothes and food crops. The sun's heat evaporates water, which dries wet clothes and harvested crops.
chunks.source: The sun's heat evaporates water, which dries wet clothes and harvested crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A mammal is a warm-blooded vertebrate animal distinguished by the possession of fur or hair. Give any one example of such an animal: ____. A: Cow. A cow has hair on its body, gives birth to live calves and feeds them on milk.
chunks.source: A cow has hair on its body, gives birth to live calves and feeds them on milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does heat travel through solids? A: By conduction. In solids, heat moves from particle to particle without the particles themselves moving.
chunks.source: In solids, heat moves from particle to particle without the particles themselves moving.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain the way the process of photosynthesis in plants makes the environment/atmosphere clean. A: Plants take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen, which keeps the air clean. During photosynthesis plants remove carbon dioxide from the air and release fresh oxygen for breathing.
chunks.source: During photosynthesis plants remove carbon dioxide from the air and release fresh oxygen for breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Describe any one way in which people in a community can carry out maintenance of water sources. A: By regularly cleaning and slashing around the water source. Clearing bushes and rubbish around a well or spring stops dirt and germs from entering the water.
chunks.source: Clearing bushes and rubbish around a well or spring stops dirt and germs from entering the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The experiment above shows that air exerts pressure. How can this property of air be used in our daily life? A: It is used when pumping air into bicycle tyres or sucking liquids through a straw. Air pressure pushes on surfaces; we use it to inflate tyres and to draw liquid up a straw.
chunks.source: Air pressure pushes on surfaces; we use it to inflate tyres and to draw liquid up a straw.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does poultry keeping in a given family help to control kwashiorkor among the children there? A: It provides eggs and meat, which are protein-rich body-building foods. Kwashiorkor is caused by lack of proteins, and eggs and meat from chickens supply proteins.
chunks.source: Kwashiorkor is caused by lack of proteins, and eggs and meat from chickens supply proteins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The garden tool above is a hoe. Describe one way a farmer can take care of it. A: By cleaning it after use and oiling the metal part to prevent rusting. A hoe lasts longer if it is cleaned, kept dry and oiled so the metal does not rust.
chunks.source: A hoe lasts longer if it is cleaned, kept dry and oiled so the metal does not rust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cite the element of primary health care that may be used to control population growth: ____. A: Family planning. Family planning helps families choose the number of children they can care for.
chunks.source: Family planning helps families choose the number of children they can care for.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are the roots shown in the diagram important to a maize plant? A: They absorb water and mineral salts from the soil and anchor the plant firmly. Roots take in water and nutrients for the plant and hold it upright in the soil.
chunks.source: Roots take in water and nutrients for the plant and hold it upright in the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do nimbus clouds contribute to high crop yields in a village food path? A: They bring rainfall, which provides water for the crops to grow well. Nimbus clouds are rain-bearing clouds, and rain waters the crops for a good harvest.
chunks.source: Nimbus clouds are rain-bearing clouds, and rain waters the crops for a good harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the gestation period of a doe (female rabbit)? A: About 30 days (one month). A doe carries her pregnancy for about a month before giving birth to bunnies.
chunks.source: A doe carries her pregnancy for about a month before giving birth to bunnies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the importance of a dustbin in our classroom at Greenhill Academy. A: It keeps the classroom clean by collecting rubbish. A dustbin gives rubbish a proper place instead of the floor.
chunks.source: A dustbin gives rubbish a proper place instead of the floor.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Of what importance are earthworms to a farmer? A: They burrow through the soil, letting in air and water, and their droppings add fertility. Earthworm tunnels aerate the soil and their waste enriches it for crops.
chunks.source: Earthworm tunnels aerate the soil and their waste enriches it for crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Kawudha prepared matooke, covered it with banana leaves, added water and put it on fire. After 36 minutes the water was gone and the food started burning. Where had the water she had poured in the food gone? A: It had evaporated (changed into invisible water vapour). Heat changed the liquid water into water vapour, which escaped into the air.
chunks.source: Heat changed the liquid water into water vapour, which escaped into the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The outer covering of the bean seed shown in the diagram is called the ____. A: Testa. The testa is the tough outer skin that protects the inside of the seed.
chunks.source: The testa is the tough outer skin that protects the inside of the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we wash our hands when preparing ORS? A: To avoid putting germs from our hands into the ORS. Dirty hands would contaminate the ORS and make the sick person worse.
chunks.source: Dirty hands would contaminate the ORS and make the sick person worse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Communicable diseases are diseases that can be spread from one person to another. Give any one example: ____. A: Tuberculosis. Tuberculosis spreads through the air when an infected person coughs.
chunks.source: Tuberculosis spreads through the air when an infected person coughs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is carbon dioxide used in fire extinguishers? A: It does not support burning and cuts off the supply of oxygen to the fire. Fire needs oxygen to burn; carbon dioxide blankets the fire and puts it out.
chunks.source: Fire needs oxygen to burn; carbon dioxide blankets the fire and puts it out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Honey is a product that apiary farmers regularly harvest from bee hives and sell or eat. State the food value we get from eating honey: ____. A: Energy. Honey is rich in sugars, which the body burns to release energy.
chunks.source: Honey is rich in sugars, which the body burns to release energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How useful are stomata to a plant? A: They allow gaseous exchange: carbon dioxide enters and oxygen and water vapour leave. Stomata are tiny openings on leaves through which gases pass in and out.
chunks.source: Stomata are tiny openings on leaves through which gases pass in and out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one biological change that takes place in animals: ____. A: Growth. Growth is a biological change because a young animal develops into an adult and cannot change back.
chunks.source: Growth is a biological change because a young animal develops into an adult and cannot change back.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the season in which cereal crop farmers are advised to harvest their crops: ____. A: Dry season. Crops harvested in the dry season stay dry and do not rot.
chunks.source: Crops harvested in the dry season stay dry and do not rot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for farmers to harvest their cereal crops in the dry season? A: So that the grains stay dry, do not rot or grow mould, and store well. Wet grains rot and grow mould, but dry grains keep safely in the granary.
chunks.source: Wet grains rot and grow mould, but dry grains keep safely in the granary.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cereal crop farmers carry out many activities during the 'caring stage'. Name any one of them: ____. A: Weeding. Weeding removes unwanted plants that compete with the crops for nutrients.
chunks.source: Weeding removes unwanted plants that compete with the crops for nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another activity cereal crop farmers carry out during the 'caring stage': ____. A: Thinning. Thinning removes extra seedlings so the remaining crops get enough space and nutrients.
chunks.source: Thinning removes extra seedlings so the remaining crops get enough space and nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Accidents are sudden happenings that cause harm to the body. Outline any one example of accidents: ____. A: Road accident. A road accident happens suddenly and can injure people.
chunks.source: A road accident happens suddenly and can injure people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Outline another example of accidents: ____. A: Burns. Burns from fire or hot objects happen suddenly and injure the body.
chunks.source: Burns from fire or hot objects happen suddenly and injure the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Describe any one effect of accidents on an individual/person. A: They cause injuries and pain to the body. Accidents hurt the body, causing wounds, pain and suffering.
chunks.source: Accidents hurt the body, causing wounds, pain and suffering.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Describe another effect of accidents on an individual/person. A: They can cause permanent disability or death. Serious accidents may cripple a person for life or even kill them.
chunks.source: Serious accidents may cripple a person for life or even kill them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the displacement method. Name the part marked X: ____. A: Spout. The spout is the outlet of the displacement can through which displaced water flows into the measuring cylinder.
chunks.source: The spout is the outlet of the displacement can through which displaced water flows into the measuring cylinder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part marked Q in the diagram: ____. A: Thread. The thread is tied to the irregular object so it can be lowered into the water.
chunks.source: The thread is tied to the irregular object so it can be lowered into the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one common example of an irregular object whose volume can be found in the same way: ____. A: Stone. A stone has no regular shape, so its volume is found by the displacement method.
chunks.source: A stone has no regular shape, so its volume is found by the displacement method.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the volume of the displaced water collected in cylinder W? ____. A: 20cc (20cm3). The displaced water rose to the 20cc mark in the measuring cylinder, so its volume is 20cc.
chunks.source: The displaced water rose to the 20cc mark in the measuring cylinder, so its volume is 20cc.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: Match each vector in A with the disease it spreads in B.
A: (i) Housefly, (ii) Tsetsefly, (iii) Rats fleas, (iv) Fresh water snails
B: Bilharzia, Trachoma, Elephantiasis, Plague, Sleeping sickness A: Housefly: Trachoma; Tsetsefly: Sleeping sickness; Rats fleas: Plague; Fresh water snails: Bilharzia. Houseflies spread trachoma, tsetseflies spread sleeping sickness, rat fleas spread plague and fresh water snails spread bilharzia.
chunks.source: Houseflies spread trachoma, tsetseflies spread sleeping sickness, rat fleas spread plague and fresh water snails spread bilharzia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Briefly explain the term soil erosion. A: Soil erosion is the washing or blowing away of the top fertile soil by agents such as running water and wind. The top soil, which is the most fertile, is carried away, leaving poor soil behind.
chunks.source: The top soil, which is the most fertile, is carried away, leaving poor soil behind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from running water, mention one other agent of soil erosion: ____. A: Wind. Strong wind blows away loose top soil, especially where there is no plant cover.
chunks.source: Strong wind blows away loose top soil, especially where there is no plant cover.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention another agent of soil erosion apart from running water: ____. A: Animals. Animals walking and grazing loosen the soil, making it easy to wash away.
chunks.source: Animals walking and grazing loosen the soil, making it easy to wash away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one method of controlling soil erosion in the compound at home/school. A: By planting grass or trees to hold the soil. Plant roots hold the soil firmly so it is not washed away.
chunks.source: Plant roots hold the soil firmly so it is not washed away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which body system is responsible for the breakage of food into soluble substances? ____. A: Digestive system. The digestive system breaks food into tiny soluble particles the body can absorb.
chunks.source: The digestive system breaks food into tiny soluble particles the body can absorb.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from teeth, mention one other organ in the digestive system: ____. A: Stomach. The stomach churns food and mixes it with digestive juices.
chunks.source: The stomach churns food and mixes it with digestive juices.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention another organ in the digestive system apart from teeth: ____. A: Small intestine. Digested food is absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.
chunks.source: Digested food is absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Teeth are some of the important organs in the body. What is the use of teeth when eating? A: They cut and grind food into small pieces for easy swallowing. Teeth break big lumps of food into small pieces that are easy to swallow and digest.
chunks.source: Teeth break big lumps of food into small pieces that are easy to swallow and digest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Steps taken when preparing ORS locally are listed above. Identify the solute: ____. A: Sugar and salt. The solute is the substance that dissolves; here both sugar and salt dissolve in the water.
chunks.source: The solute is the substance that dissolves; here both sugar and salt dissolve in the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the solvent from the ORS experiment: ____. A: Water. The solvent is the liquid in which other substances dissolve.
chunks.source: The solvent is the liquid in which other substances dissolve.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the solution from the ORS experiment: ____. A: ORS (the mixture of sugar, salt and water). The solution is the uniform mixture formed after the solute dissolves in the solvent.
chunks.source: The solution is the uniform mixture formed after the solute dissolves in the solvent.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What would be the danger if the one making the ORS did not wash his hands with water and soap first? A: Germs from the dirty hands would contaminate the ORS and cause more sickness. Unwashed hands carry germs that would enter the ORS and infect the sick person.
chunks.source: Unwashed hands carry germs that would enter the ORS and infect the sick person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does cross-breeding improve on local breeds of chicken? A: It produces birds that grow faster, lay more eggs and resist diseases better. Cross-breeding combines the good qualities of local and exotic breeds in the offspring.
chunks.source: Cross-breeding combines the good qualities of local and exotic breeds in the offspring.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides free range system, mention one method of keeping poultry birds: ____. A: Deep litter system. In the deep litter system birds move freely on a floor covered with litter.
chunks.source: In the deep litter system birds move freely on a floor covered with litter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention another method of keeping poultry birds besides free range system: ____. A: Battery cage system. In the battery cage system birds are kept in small individual cages.
chunks.source: In the battery cage system birds are kept in small individual cages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention a third method of keeping poultry birds besides free range system: ____. A: Fold system. In the fold system a small movable house is shifted to fresh ground daily.
chunks.source: In the fold system a small movable house is shifted to fresh ground daily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the flowering plant. Name the part labeled X: ____. A: Shoot system. The shoot system is made up of all the parts of the plant above the ground.
chunks.source: The shoot system is made up of all the parts of the plant above the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part labeled Y in the diagram: ____. A: Root system. The root system is made up of all the roots below the ground.
chunks.source: The root system is made up of all the roots below the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one importance of part P (the flower) to the plant. A: It helps the plant to reproduce by developing into seeds and fruits. Flowers are the reproductive parts; after pollination they form seeds and fruits.
chunks.source: Flowers are the reproductive parts; after pollination they form seeds and fruits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the by-product that part K (the leaf) produces during photosynthesis: ____. A: Oxygen. During photosynthesis leaves take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen as a by-product.
chunks.source: During photosynthesis leaves take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen as a by-product.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does yeast reproduce? A: By budding. In budding, a small outgrowth (bud) forms on the yeast cell, grows and breaks off.
chunks.source: In budding, a small outgrowth (bud) forms on the yeast cell, grows and breaks off.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides yeast, mention one other example of fungi: ____. A: Mushroom. A mushroom is a large fungus that grows on decaying matter.
chunks.source: A mushroom is a large fungus that grows on decaying matter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention another example of fungi besides yeast: ____. A: Mould. Mould is a fungus that grows on stale food such as bread.
chunks.source: Mould is a fungus that grows on stale food such as bread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Describe one way in which fungi can be harmful to people. A: Some fungi cause diseases such as ringworm, and some mushrooms are poisonous. Harmful fungi attack the skin or poison people who eat them.
chunks.source: Harmful fungi attack the skin or poison people who eat them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is an ostrich unable to fly (flightless)? A: It has a very heavy body and wings that are too small to lift it. An ostrich's big heavy body cannot be lifted by its small wings.
chunks.source: An ostrich's big heavy body cannot be lifted by its small wings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from an ostrich, mention one other bird which cannot fly: ____. A: Penguin. Penguins have flippers for swimming instead of wings for flying.
chunks.source: Penguins have flippers for swimming instead of wings for flying.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention another bird which cannot fly apart from an ostrich: ____. A: Emu. The emu is a large flightless bird like the ostrich.
chunks.source: The emu is a large flightless bird like the ostrich.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can wild birds like the ostriches be useful to people in a country where they are? A: They attract tourists, which brings income to the country. People pay to see ostriches in the wild, earning the country foreign income.
chunks.source: People pay to see ostriches in the wild, earning the country foreign income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way plants in our environment can be conserved. A: By planting more trees and avoiding bush burning. Planting trees replaces those cut down, and avoiding fires protects vegetation.
chunks.source: Planting trees replaces those cut down, and avoiding fires protects vegetation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do plants depend on animals? A: Animals help in pollination and seed dispersal, and their droppings add manure to the soil. Bees pollinate flowers, animals carry seeds, and dung enriches the soil.
chunks.source: Bees pollinate flowers, animals carry seeds, and dung enriches the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one use of plants to animals: ____. A: Plants provide food to animals. Herbivores feed directly on plants for their food.
chunks.source: Herbivores feed directly on plants for their food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify another use of plants to animals: ____. A: Plants provide shelter to animals. Trees give shade and hiding places to wild and domestic animals.
chunks.source: Trees give shade and hiding places to wild and domestic animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one animal fibre that can be got from sheep and goats: ____. A: Wool. Sheep are sheared to get wool, a soft animal fibre.
chunks.source: Sheep are sheared to get wool, a soft animal fibre.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Goat farmers in Uganda usually find it hard when their goats die of diseases. Name any one disease that can kill goats: ____. A: Anthrax. Anthrax is a deadly disease that kills goats and other livestock quickly.
chunks.source: Anthrax is a deadly disease that kills goats and other livestock quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way goat farmers in Uganda can protect their goats against the disease you have named above. A: By vaccinating the goats regularly. Vaccination builds immunity so the goats resist the disease.
chunks.source: Vaccination builds immunity so the goats resist the disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: From which external part of a goat does the goat farmer get milk? ____. A: Udder. Milk is drawn from the udder of a female goat.
chunks.source: Milk is drawn from the udder of a female goat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram above shows a local tool (charcoal flat iron) used at home. How is the tool useful at home? A: It is used for ironing (pressing) clothes. The hot flat iron smooths wrinkles out of clothes.
chunks.source: The hot flat iron smooths wrinkles out of clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is part marked J (the handle) made out of a material that does not conduct heat? A: So that the person holding it does not get burnt. A handle that does not conduct heat stays cool while the iron is hot.
chunks.source: A handle that does not conduct heat stays cool while the iron is hot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain the use of holes marked K when the tool is in use. A: They let in air (oxygen) to keep the charcoal burning and let out smoke. Charcoal needs a steady supply of air to keep burning inside the iron.
chunks.source: Charcoal needs a steady supply of air to keep burning inside the iron.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one common fuel used in the tool above: ____. A: Charcoal. Burning charcoal inside the iron produces the heat for ironing.
chunks.source: Burning charcoal inside the iron produces the heat for ironing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: People are encouraged to wash hands after visiting the latrine. Write down one material we use to wash hands which is in solid state: ____. A: Soap. Soap is a solid that we rub on our hands with water.
chunks.source: Soap is a solid that we rub on our hands with water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one material we use to wash hands which is in liquid state: ____. A: Water. Water is the liquid we use to rinse our hands.
chunks.source: Water is the liquid we use to rinse our hands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Describe any one danger that may come as a result of not keeping our bodies, clothing and beddings clean. A: It leads to skin diseases and bad body smell. Dirt on the body and clothes breeds germs that cause skin infections.
chunks.source: Dirt on the body and clothes breeds germs that cause skin infections.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from washing and bathing, state any other one activity that school children do to keep clean. A: Brushing their teeth. Brushing removes food remains and keeps the mouth clean and fresh.
chunks.source: Brushing removes food remains and keeps the mouth clean and fresh.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of cattle that is useful in the production of yoghurt: ____. A: Dairy cattle. Yoghurt is made from milk, and dairy cattle are kept for milk production.
chunks.source: Yoghurt is made from milk, and dairy cattle are kept for milk production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a family fight deficiency diseases among its members? A: By feeding on a balanced diet. A balanced diet supplies all food values, so no deficiency disease develops.
chunks.source: A balanced diet supplies all food values, so no deficiency disease develops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from insects, state any other group of arthropods: ____. A: Arachnids. Arachnids such as spiders and ticks have eight legs and two body parts.
chunks.source: Arachnids such as spiders and ticks have eight legs and two body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the process through which water turns into ice: ____. A: Freezing. When water is cooled below 0C, it freezes into ice.
chunks.source: When water is cooled below 0C, it freezes into ice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it necessary for farmers to carry out sorting before planting seeds? A: To select only healthy, viable seeds and remove damaged or bad ones. Good seeds germinate well while bad ones would waste space in the garden.
chunks.source: Good seeds germinate well while bad ones would waste space in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one activity that school children can do to promote sanitation. A: Sweeping the classroom and compound. Sweeping removes dirt and rubbish, keeping the school environment clean.
chunks.source: Sweeping removes dirt and rubbish, keeping the school environment clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger of air to people. A: It carries germs that cause airborne diseases. Air can transport disease germs from sick people to healthy ones.
chunks.source: Air can transport disease germs from sick people to healthy ones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the component of soil formed as a result of decomposition: ____. A: Humus. Humus is the dark material formed when dead plants and animals rot.
chunks.source: Humus is the dark material formed when dead plants and animals rot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can farmers control overcrowding of crops in their gardens? A: By thinning and proper spacing of the crops. Thinning removes extra plants so the rest get enough nutrients and light.
chunks.source: Thinning removes extra plants so the rest get enough nutrients and light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the lungs, what other organ does a frog use for breathing? ____. A: Skin. A frog also breathes through its moist skin when in water.
chunks.source: A frog also breathes through its moist skin when in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part of a tooth that contains sensory nerves: ____. A: Pulp. The pulp is the soft centre of the tooth with nerves and blood vessels.
chunks.source: The pulp is the soft centre of the tooth with nerves and blood vessels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down the process that helps in the circulation of air in the house: ____. A: Ventilation. Ventilation is the free movement of fresh air in and out of a house.
chunks.source: Ventilation is the free movement of fresh air in and out of a house.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the equipment drawn above (a chicken drinker) useful at a poultry farm? A: It provides clean drinking water to the chickens at all times. Chickens need a steady supply of clean water to stay healthy and productive.
chunks.source: Chickens need a steady supply of clean water to stay healthy and productive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one form of energy which is produced when a drum is hit: ____. A: Sound energy. Hitting the drum makes it vibrate, producing sound.
chunks.source: Hitting the drum makes it vibrate, producing sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a rat similar to a cow in terms of reproduction? A: Both give birth to live young ones. Rats and cows are both mammals, so they do not lay eggs.
chunks.source: Rats and cows are both mammals, so they do not lay eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it dangerous to apply sugar on a fresh wound on your skin? A: It attracts germs and flies, which cause infection of the wound. Sugar feeds germs, so a sugared wound easily becomes infected.
chunks.source: Sugar feeds germs, so a sugared wound easily becomes infected.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why a breast feeding mother should drink a lot of fluids. A: To produce enough breast milk for the baby. Breast milk is mostly water, so the mother needs plenty of fluids to make it.
chunks.source: Breast milk is mostly water, so the mother needs plenty of fluids to make it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of thermometer is used to measure both the highest and lowest temperatures of the day? A: Maximum and minimum thermometer. This special thermometer records the day's highest and lowest temperatures.
chunks.source: This special thermometer records the day's highest and lowest temperatures.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one factor which promotes quick breeding of bacteria: ____. A: Warmth. Bacteria multiply fastest in warm conditions.
chunks.source: Bacteria multiply fastest in warm conditions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the component of air that keeps candle A burning: ____. A: Oxygen. Oxygen supports burning; without it the candle flame goes out.
chunks.source: Oxygen supports burning; without it the candle flame goes out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The gas produced at point Z is carbon dioxide. Which plant process makes use of this gas? A: Photosynthesis. Plants take in carbon dioxide to make food during photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants take in carbon dioxide to make food during photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does a chameleon keep changing its body colour from place to place as it moves? A: To camouflage (hide) itself from enemies and from its prey. Matching its surroundings hides the chameleon from predators and prey.
chunks.source: Matching its surroundings hides the chameleon from predators and prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way are geckos able to control the spread of malaria at home? A: They eat mosquitoes, which spread malaria. Geckos feed on mosquitoes, reducing the insects that transmit malaria.
chunks.source: Geckos feed on mosquitoes, reducing the insects that transmit malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are the stomata of leaves similar in function to the human lungs? A: Both are used for gaseous exchange (breathing). Stomata let gases in and out of leaves just as lungs do for the body.
chunks.source: Stomata let gases in and out of leaves just as lungs do for the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way of controlling soil erosion in hilly areas. A: By terracing the hillsides. Terraces are steps cut across slopes that slow down running water.
chunks.source: Terraces are steps cut across slopes that slow down running water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for people to harvest water during the rainy season? A: To store it for use during the dry season. Rainy-season water is stored in tanks for the dry months when water is scarce.
chunks.source: Rainy-season water is stored in tanks for the dry months when water is scarce.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why laying boxes in a poultry house should be kept in dark places. A: Hens feel safe and comfortable laying eggs in quiet, dark places. Darkness gives laying hens privacy, so they lay more eggs.
chunks.source: Darkness gives laying hens privacy, so they lay more eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the first aid for a bite from a poisonous snake. A: Keep the victim calm and rush him or her to hospital immediately. Quick hospital treatment with antivenom saves the victim's life.
chunks.source: Quick hospital treatment with antivenom saves the victim's life.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the body temperature of a bird different from that of a fish? A: A bird's body temperature stays constant while a fish's changes with the surroundings. Birds are warm-blooded but fish are cold-blooded.
chunks.source: Birds are warm-blooded but fish are cold-blooded.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What advice would you give to a crop farmer to ensure that his garden soil has enough nitrogen? A: Plant legumes or apply nitrogenous fertilizers. Legumes add nitrogen to the soil and fertilizers supply it directly.
chunks.source: Legumes add nitrogen to the soil and fertilizers supply it directly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the absence of iodine in the human body harmful to one's health? A: It causes goitre (swelling of the neck). Without iodine the thyroid gland swells, forming a goitre.
chunks.source: Without iodine the thyroid gland swells, forming a goitre.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one activity that a cattle farmer can do to improve on milk production in his Friesian cows. A: Feed them well on nutritious pastures and give clean water. Well-fed cows produce more milk.
chunks.source: Well-fed cows produce more milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the liver an important organ of the human body? A: It removes poisonous substances from the blood. The liver cleans the blood by breaking down harmful substances.
chunks.source: The liver cleans the blood by breaking down harmful substances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of change occurs when a mango fruit rots? ____. A: Chemical change. Rotting forms new substances and cannot be reversed, so it is a chemical change.
chunks.source: Rotting forms new substances and cannot be reversed, so it is a chemical change.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which a housefly is different from a spider. A: A housefly has six legs while a spider has eight legs. Houseflies are insects with six legs; spiders are arachnids with eight legs.
chunks.source: Houseflies are insects with six legs; spiders are arachnids with eight legs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one problem that may be faced by a P.6 child who does not brush his or her teeth after a meal. A: Tooth decay. Food remains rot the teeth, forming painful holes.
chunks.source: Food remains rot the teeth, forming painful holes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Decanted water is said to be clean water. Why are people discouraged from drinking it? A: It may still contain disease-causing germs. Decantation removes dirt but does not kill germs.
chunks.source: Decantation removes dirt but does not kill germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one advantage of proper prescription of a drug before using it. A: It prevents taking the wrong drug or wrong dose. A prescription ensures the right drug in the right amount.
chunks.source: A prescription ensures the right drug in the right amount.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why would the seeds in the experiment fail to germinate after 9 days? A: The ice made the conditions too cold; seeds need warmth to germinate. Seeds need warmth, air and moisture; ice removed the warmth.
chunks.source: Seeds need warmth, air and moisture; ice removed the warmth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one sign of Kwashiorkor in children: ____. A: Swollen belly. Kwashiorkor makes the belly swell and the hair turn brownish.
chunks.source: Kwashiorkor makes the belly swell and the hair turn brownish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the molar tooth. Name the part marked A: ____. A: Enamel. The enamel is the hard white outer covering of the crown.
chunks.source: The enamel is the hard white outer covering of the crown.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part marked C in the diagram: ____. A: Dentine. Dentine is the layer just beneath the enamel.
chunks.source: Dentine is the layer just beneath the enamel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the above tooth important during digestion of food? A: It grinds food into small pieces for easy swallowing and digestion. Molars crush and grind food so it can be swallowed and digested easily.
chunks.source: Molars crush and grind food so it can be swallowed and digested easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which the above tooth is adapted to its function. A: It has a broad, rough surface for grinding food. The wide rough crown is perfect for crushing and grinding.
chunks.source: The wide rough crown is perfect for crushing and grinding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one activity that a farmer does before planting seeds: ____. A: Clearing the land. Bushes and weeds must be cleared before seeds are planted.
chunks.source: Bushes and weeds must be cleared before seeds are planted.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another activity that a farmer does before planting seeds: ____. A: Ploughing (digging) the land. Digging loosens the soil so seeds can be planted easily.
chunks.source: Digging loosens the soil so seeds can be planted easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are farmers encouraged to carry out crop rotation? A: To maintain soil fertility and control pests and diseases. Different crops use different nutrients, and rotation breaks pest cycles.
chunks.source: Different crops use different nutrients, and rotation breaks pest cycles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is wind useful to a cereal farmer who has harvested her crops? A: It helps in winnowing (separating grains from chaff). Wind blows away the light chaff, leaving the heavy clean grains.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light chaff, leaving the heavy clean grains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of chicken kept for egg production: ____. A: Layers. Layers are chickens specially kept for laying eggs.
chunks.source: Layers are chickens specially kept for laying eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of chicken kept for meat production: ____. A: Broilers. Broilers grow very fast and are kept for meat.
chunks.source: Broilers grow very fast and are kept for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
