chunks.text: Q: Write one exotic breed of chicken kept for egg production: ____. A: White Leghorn. The White Leghorn is a famous exotic layer breed.
chunks.source: The White Leghorn is a famous exotic layer breed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write another exotic breed of chicken kept for egg production: ____. A: Rhode Island Red. Rhode Island Red is another exotic breed good for laying eggs.
chunks.source: Rhode Island Red is another exotic breed good for laying eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List A has ferns, liverworts and mosses. List B has puff balls, toadstools and mould. Give one similarity between organisms in list A and those in list B. A: Both reproduce by means of spores. Neither group produces seeds; both use spores for reproduction.
chunks.source: Neither group produces seeds; both use spores for reproduction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are organisms in list A different from those in list B? A: Organisms in list A are plants that make their own food, while those in list B are fungi that do not. List A are green plants; list B are fungi which feed on other matter.
chunks.source: List A are green plants; list B are fungi which feed on other matter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one danger of organisms in list B to people. A: Some are poisonous and some cause diseases. Poisonous toadstools can kill, and moulds spoil food.
chunks.source: Poisonous toadstools can kill, and moulds spoil food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are conifers different from plants in list A in terms of reproduction? A: Conifers reproduce by means of seeds while plants in list A reproduce by spores. Conifers bear cones with seeds; ferns and mosses have no seeds.
chunks.source: Conifers bear cones with seeds; ferns and mosses have no seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one example of a diarrhoeal disease in people: ____. A: Cholera. Cholera causes severe diarrhoea and spreads through dirty water.
chunks.source: Cholera causes severe diarrhoea and spreads through dirty water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of protecting yourself from getting diarrhoeal diseases. A: By drinking boiled water. Boiling kills the germs that cause diarrhoeal diseases.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs that cause diarrhoeal diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another way of protecting yourself from getting diarrhoeal diseases. A: By washing hands before eating. Clean hands stop germs from entering food.
chunks.source: Clean hands stop germs from entering food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of caring for a sick person. A: By giving them the prescribed medicine on time. Sick people recover faster when they take their medicine properly.
chunks.source: Sick people recover faster when they take their medicine properly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a cow regarded as a domestic animal? A: Because it is kept and cared for by people at home. Domestic animals live with people who feed and protect them.
chunks.source: Domestic animals live with people who feed and protect them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one domestic animal that is kept only for meat production and neither for milk nor for its skin: ____. A: Pig. Pigs are reared mainly for pork.
chunks.source: Pigs are reared mainly for pork.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do you care for such animals? Give one way. A: By feeding them well. Well-fed pigs grow fast and stay healthy.
chunks.source: Well-fed pigs grow fast and stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another way of caring for such animals. A: By vaccinating and treating them against diseases. Healthy pigs need protection from diseases.
chunks.source: Healthy pigs need protection from diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one disease spread by mosquitoes to people: ____. A: Malaria. Female anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria.
chunks.source: Female anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one disease spread by house flies to people: ____. A: Cholera. Houseflies carry germs from faeces to food, spreading cholera.
chunks.source: Houseflies carry germs from faeces to food, spreading cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the disease spread by a rabid dog to people: ____. A: Rabies. A bite from a rabid dog transmits the deadly rabies virus.
chunks.source: A bite from a rabid dog transmits the deadly rabies virus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way people in the community can control the spread of diseases by mosquitoes. A: By draining stagnant water where mosquitoes breed. Without stagnant water, mosquitoes have nowhere to breed.
chunks.source: Without stagnant water, mosquitoes have nowhere to breed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In one sentence, give the meaning of the term transpiration. A: Transpiration is the loss of water as vapour from the leaves of plants. Plants give off excess water through their leaves as vapour.
chunks.source: Plants give off excess water through their leaves as vapour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one factor that can increase the rate of transpiration: ____. A: High temperature. Heat makes water evaporate faster from the leaves.
chunks.source: Heat makes water evaporate faster from the leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention another factor that can increase the rate of transpiration: ____. A: Wind. Wind carries away water vapour, so leaves lose more water.
chunks.source: Wind carries away water vapour, so leaves lose more water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the process of transpiration useful in the environment? A: It releases water vapour into the air, which helps in the formation of rainfall. Transpiration adds moisture to the atmosphere for rain formation.
chunks.source: Transpiration adds moisture to the atmosphere for rain formation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the kettle and cold-water bottle. What do the arrows labelled with letter Y represent? A: Heat from the fire. The arrows show heat rising from the fire to boil the water in the kettle.
chunks.source: The arrows show heat rising from the fire to boil the water in the kettle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the physical process taking place at Z: ____. A: Condensation. At Z, water vapour cools on the cold bottle and turns back into liquid.
chunks.source: At Z, water vapour cools on the cold bottle and turns back into liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are the water droplets formed on the bottle? A: The steam (water vapour) cooled and condensed on the cold surface of the bottle. Cold surfaces make water vapour change into liquid droplets.
chunks.source: Cold surfaces make water vapour change into liquid droplets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the natural process represented by the above diagram: ____. A: Water cycle. The diagram models evaporation, condensation and precipitation like in nature.
chunks.source: The diagram models evaporation, condensation and precipitation like in nature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: Match the type of mammal in A with its example in B.
A: (i) Primate, (ii) Pouched mammal, (iii) Chiroptera, (iv) Rodent
B: wallaby, bat, mouse, monkey A: Primate: monkey; Pouched mammal: wallaby; chiroptera: bat; rodent: mouse. Monkeys are primates, wallabies are pouched mammals, bats are chiroptera and mice are rodents.
chunks.source: Monkeys are primates, wallabies are pouched mammals, bats are chiroptera and mice are rodents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from B.C.G vaccine, give any one other vaccine administered to babies: ____. A: Polio vaccine. Babies receive polio vaccine to protect them against polio.
chunks.source: Babies receive polio vaccine to protect them against polio.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another vaccine administered to babies apart from B.C.G: ____. A: DPT vaccine. DPT protects babies against diphtheria, whooping cough and tetanus.
chunks.source: DPT protects babies against diphtheria, whooping cough and tetanus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is B.C.G vaccine administered to babies? A: To protect them against tuberculosis. BCG gives babies immunity against TB.
chunks.source: BCG gives babies immunity against TB.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What advice can you give to Mr. Lule whose child is suffering from measles? A: Take the child to a health centre for treatment immediately. Measles needs proper medical care to avoid complications.
chunks.source: Measles needs proper medical care to avoid complications.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one feature found on a child health card: ____. A: The child's immunization record. The card records every vaccine the child receives.
chunks.source: The card records every vaccine the child receives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention another feature found on a child health card: ____. A: The child's growth (weight) chart. The card shows the child's weight over time to track growth.
chunks.source: The card shows the child's weight over time to track growth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a child health card useful to health workers? A: It helps them monitor the child's growth and immunization status. Health workers read the card to know which vaccines and care a child still needs.
chunks.source: Health workers read the card to know which vaccines and care a child still needs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a family participate in the immunization programme? A: By taking their children for immunization on the scheduled days. Families must bring babies to health centres when vaccines are due.
chunks.source: Families must bring babies to health centres when vaccines are due.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one component of blood: ____. A: Red blood cells. Red blood cells carry oxygen around the body.
chunks.source: Red blood cells carry oxygen around the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another component of blood: ____. A: White blood cells. White blood cells fight disease germs in the body.
chunks.source: White blood cells fight disease germs in the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of haemoglobin in blood. A: It carries oxygen to all parts of the body. Haemoglobin in red blood cells picks up oxygen for the body.
chunks.source: Haemoglobin in red blood cells picks up oxygen for the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way we can increase the volume of blood in our bodies. A: By eating foods rich in iron. Iron is used to make more red blood cells.
chunks.source: Iron is used to make more red blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the digestive juice produced by the pancreas: ____. A: Pancreatic juice. The pancreas releases pancreatic juice into the small intestine.
chunks.source: The pancreas releases pancreatic juice into the small intestine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the digestive juice produced by the stomach: ____. A: Gastric juice. The stomach walls produce gastric juice to digest food.
chunks.source: The stomach walls produce gastric juice to digest food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where does absorption of digested food take place in the alimentary canal? A: In the small intestine (ileum). Digested food passes into the blood through the walls of the ileum.
chunks.source: Digested food passes into the blood through the walls of the ileum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way of promoting the good working conditions of the digestive system. A: By eating a balanced diet and drinking enough water. Good food and water keep the digestive organs working smoothly.
chunks.source: Good food and water keep the digestive organs working smoothly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram above shows some food being cooked. Identify the fuel being used to cook this food: ____. A: Firewood. The fire under the cooking pots is made from firewood.
chunks.source: The fire under the cooking pots is made from firewood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which physical process is shown at X (the rising vapour above the food)? A: Evaporation. Heat changes the water in the food into steam, which rises.
chunks.source: Heat changes the water in the food into steam, which rises.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should such food be wrapped with banana leaves? A: To keep it clean and to retain heat and flavour. Banana leaves protect the food from dirt and keep it hot.
chunks.source: Banana leaves protect the food from dirt and keep it hot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason for cooking food before it is eaten. A: To kill germs in the food. Heat destroys disease germs that may be in raw food.
chunks.source: Heat destroys disease germs that may be in raw food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of soil suitable for making glasses: ____. A: Sand soil. Glass is made from silica, which is found in sand soil.
chunks.source: Glass is made from silica, which is found in sand soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To what group of flowering plants does sorghum belong? A: Monocotyledonous plants (monocots). Sorghum is a cereal with one seed leaf, like maize and rice.
chunks.source: Sorghum is a cereal with one seed leaf, like maize and rice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are minerals grouped under non-renewable resources? A: Because they cannot be replaced once they are used up. Minerals take millions of years to form, so they are used up forever.
chunks.source: Minerals take millions of years to form, so they are used up forever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The outer covering of the bean seed shown in the diagram is called the ____. A: Testa. The testa is the protective outer skin of the seed.
chunks.source: The testa is the protective outer skin of the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one danger a weaning child may get: ____. A: Malnutrition (kwashiorkor). Children weaned onto poor foods may suffer protein deficiency.
chunks.source: Children weaned onto poor foods may suffer protein deficiency.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way a crop farmer can prevent destruction of his root crops by monkeys. A: By guarding the garden and scaring the monkeys away. A farmer watching the garden can chase monkeys before they dig up crops.
chunks.source: A farmer watching the garden can chase monkeys before they dig up crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do people in rural areas obtain their food? A: By growing their own crops and rearing animals. Rural families farm the land to produce their food.
chunks.source: Rural families farm the land to produce their food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How would a farmer protect his goats and sheep from bad weather? A: By housing them in a shelter. A shelter keeps goats and sheep dry and warm in bad weather.
chunks.source: A shelter keeps goats and sheep dry and warm in bad weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides chicken, mention one other type of poultry kept in Uganda: ____. A: Ducks. Ducks are common poultry birds reared alongside chickens.
chunks.source: Ducks are common poultry birds reared alongside chickens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: As a P.6 child, state any one activity that can help you avoid drugs of dependence. A: Joining good peer groups and playing healthy games. Busy children with good friends avoid bad company and drugs.
chunks.source: Busy children with good friends avoid bad company and drugs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one recommended method of catching fish in Uganda: ____. A: Net fishing. Fishing nets are the approved way of catching mature fish.
chunks.source: Fishing nets are the approved way of catching mature fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one activity that can be carried out to prevent the spread of diarrhoeal diseases at home. A: Boiling drinking water. Boiled water is germ-free and safe to drink.
chunks.source: Boiled water is germ-free and safe to drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the insect. Which part of the insect is used for communication? A: Antennae. Insects use their antennae to sense smells and communicate with each other.
chunks.source: Insects use their antennae to sense smells and communicate with each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of caring for wild animals. A: By protecting forests, which are their natural homes. Wild animals survive when their habitats are not destroyed.
chunks.source: Wild animals survive when their habitats are not destroyed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one foodstuff that is prepared by peeling: ____. A: Matooke. Matooke must be peeled before it is cooked.
chunks.source: Matooke must be peeled before it is cooked.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are reptiles and fish similar in their way of reproduction? A: Both lay eggs. Reptiles and fish reproduce by laying eggs that hatch outside the body.
chunks.source: Reptiles and fish reproduce by laying eggs that hatch outside the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following best describes the molar tooth of an adult person? A: It has a broad, rough surface for grinding food. Molars are wide and rough so they can crush and grind food.
chunks.source: Molars are wide and rough so they can crush and grind food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram above shows two types of beehives, X and Y. Give one advantage of beehive X over Y. A: Honey can be harvested and the hive inspected without destroying the combs. The modern hive X has movable frames, so combs stay intact during harvest.
chunks.source: The modern hive X has movable frames, so combs stay intact during harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which state of matter does heat travel by conduction? ____. A: Solid state. Conduction needs closely packed particles, found in solids.
chunks.source: Conduction needs closely packed particles, found in solids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one activity done by a community to protect water sources from contamination. A: Fencing the water source. A fence keeps animals and people from dirtying the water source.
chunks.source: A fence keeps animals and people from dirtying the water source.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one practice that controls the spread of diseases among rabbits. A: Isolating sick rabbits from healthy ones. Sick rabbits are separated so they do not infect the rest.
chunks.source: Sick rabbits are separated so they do not infect the rest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a baby acquire natural immunity? A: Through breastfeeding (mother's milk). A mother's first milk gives the baby ready-made protection against diseases.
chunks.source: A mother's first milk gives the baby ready-made protection against diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is cholera grouped under communicable diseases? A: Because it can spread from one person to another. Cholera germs pass from infected people to others through dirty water and food.
chunks.source: Cholera germs pass from infected people to others through dirty water and food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of a basket as a garden tool. A: For carrying harvested crops from the garden. Baskets are used to carry produce home after harvest.
chunks.source: Baskets are used to carry produce home after harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one place where a soil profile can be properly seen or observed by a class: ____. A: In a deep pit. The layers of soil are clearly visible on the walls of a deep pit.
chunks.source: The layers of soil are clearly visible on the walls of a deep pit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one disease that people can mistake for being HIV/AIDS: ____. A: Tuberculosis. TB causes weight loss and weakness just like AIDS.
chunks.source: TB causes weight loss and weakness just like AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a child health card important to a doctor? A: It shows the child's health and immunization history. The doctor reads the card to know what care the child has received.
chunks.source: The doctor reads the card to know what care the child has received.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a cassava plant propagated? A: By planting stem cuttings. Pieces of cassava stem are buried in the soil to grow new plants.
chunks.source: Pieces of cassava stem are buried in the soil to grow new plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do farmers harvest cereal crops in the dry season? A: So that the grains stay dry and do not rot. Dry grains keep well in storage without going bad.
chunks.source: Dry grains keep well in storage without going bad.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it advisable for pupils to iron their school uniform after washing them? A: The heat kills germs and lice in the uniform. Ironing with a hot iron destroys germs hiding in the cloth.
chunks.source: Ironing with a hot iron destroys germs hiding in the cloth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why farmers castrate their young male pigs. A: To make them grow bigger and fatten faster. Castrated pigs put on weight quickly instead of wasting energy.
chunks.source: Castrated pigs put on weight quickly instead of wasting energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does rotational grazing control the spread of tick-borne diseases? A: Ticks left in the empty paddock die of starvation without animals to feed on. Moving animals away breaks the tick life cycle because ticks cannot find blood.
chunks.source: Moving animals away breaks the tick life cycle because ticks cannot find blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which group of fruits does the fruit shown in the diagram belong? A: Simple fruits. The fruit develops from a single flower ovary, making it a simple fruit.
chunks.source: The fruit develops from a single flower ovary, making it a simple fruit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one habit that promotes oral health: ____. A: Brushing teeth regularly. Regular brushing removes food remains and prevents tooth decay.
chunks.source: Regular brushing removes food remains and prevents tooth decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of electricity at school: ____. A: For lighting classrooms. Electric lights brighten classrooms for reading.
chunks.source: Electric lights brighten classrooms for reading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of natural changes in the environment: ____. A: Rainfall. Rainfall is a natural change that happens without people's control.
chunks.source: Rainfall is a natural change that happens without people's control.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one disease of the respiratory system: ____. A: Tuberculosis. TB attacks the lungs, which are part of the respiratory system.
chunks.source: TB attacks the lungs, which are part of the respiratory system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does sound travel fastest in solids? A: Because particles in solids are very closely packed together. Closely packed particles pass vibrations to each other very quickly.
chunks.source: Closely packed particles pass vibrations to each other very quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the best way of preventing the bad effects of measles among infants in Uganda. A: Immunization (vaccination). The measles vaccine protects babies before they catch the disease.
chunks.source: The measles vaccine protects babies before they catch the disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of domestic animals: ____. A: Cow. Cows are kept at home and cared for by people.
chunks.source: Cows are kept at home and cared for by people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another example of domestic animals: ____. A: Goat. Goats are common domestic animals in Ugandan homes.
chunks.source: Goats are common domestic animals in Ugandan homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one characteristic of living things: ____. A: They breathe. All living things take in air for respiration.
chunks.source: All living things take in air for respiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another characteristic of living things: ____. A: They reproduce. Living things produce young ones of their own kind.
chunks.source: Living things produce young ones of their own kind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In one sentence, write the meaning of accidents. A: Accidents are sudden happenings that cause harm to the body. An accident is unexpected and injures the body.
chunks.source: An accident is unexpected and injures the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a burn different from a scald? A: A burn is caused by dry heat while a scald is caused by wet heat such as hot water or steam. Fire and hot metals cause burns; boiling water and steam cause scalds.
chunks.source: Fire and hot metals cause burns; boiling water and steam cause scalds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: As a P.6 child, what first aid would you give to a person who is burnt by porridge? A: Cool the burnt area immediately with clean cold water. Cold water soothes the scald and stops the burning from going deeper.
chunks.source: Cold water soothes the scald and stops the burning from going deeper.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write P.H.C in full: ____. A: Primary Health Care. PHC stands for Primary Health Care.
chunks.source: PHC stands for Primary Health Care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one principle of P.H.C: ____. A: Community participation. Communities must take part in planning their own health care.
chunks.source: Communities must take part in planning their own health care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one element of P.H.C: ____. A: Immunization. Immunization protects communities against killer diseases.
chunks.source: Immunization protects communities against killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify another element of P.H.C: ____. A: Provision of safe water. Safe water prevents water-borne diseases in the community.
chunks.source: Safe water prevents water-borne diseases in the community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the blood vessels. Identify the blood vessel labelled P: ____. A: Artery. P has thick walls and a narrow lumen, which are features of an artery.
chunks.source: P has thick walls and a narrow lumen, which are features of an artery.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the blood vessel labelled Q: ____. A: Vein. Q has valves and thin walls, which are features of a vein.
chunks.source: Q has valves and thin walls, which are features of a vein.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of valves in blood vessel Q. A: They prevent the backflow of blood. Valves make sure blood flows in one direction only.
chunks.source: Valves make sure blood flows in one direction only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one structural difference between P and Q. A: P (artery) has thick muscular walls and a narrow lumen, while Q (vein) has thin walls and a wide lumen. Arteries need thick walls to withstand high pressure; veins do not.
chunks.source: Arteries need thick walls to withstand high pressure; veins do not.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who breastfeeds a child/baby at home? A: The mother. Mothers feed their babies on breast milk.
chunks.source: Mothers feed their babies on breast milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one disadvantage of breastfeeding to the mother. A: The mother needs extra food and may become weak. Producing milk drains the mother's energy and nutrients.
chunks.source: Producing milk drains the mother's energy and nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another disadvantage of breastfeeding to the mother. A: It takes up much of the mother's time. Frequent feeding leaves the mother little time for other work.
chunks.source: Frequent feeding leaves the mother little time for other work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one advantage of bottle feeding. A: Anybody can feed the baby, giving the mother rest. Bottle feeding frees the mother because others can help.
chunks.source: Bottle feeding frees the mother because others can help.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why people in Uganda keep cattle: ____. A: For milk. Cattle provide milk for the family and for sale.
chunks.source: Cattle provide milk for the family and for sale.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one type of cattle: ____. A: Dairy cattle. Dairy cattle are kept mainly for milk production.
chunks.source: Dairy cattle are kept mainly for milk production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention another type of cattle: ____. A: Beef cattle. Beef cattle are kept mainly for meat.
chunks.source: Beef cattle are kept mainly for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the body shape of a typical dairy cow? A: Triangular. A dairy cow's body is wedge-shaped: narrow at the front and wide at the rear, unlike the rectangular beef cow.
chunks.source: A dairy cow's body is wedge-shaped: narrow at the front and wide at the rear, unlike the rectangular beef cow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mark left dirty pond water to settle, then poured off the clear water as shown. What method of preparing clean water is shown above? A: Decantation. Decantation is pouring off the clear liquid after the dirt has settled.
chunks.source: Decantation is pouring off the clear liquid after the dirt has settled.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the clear water obtained using the method in (a) above not safe for drinking? A: It may still contain disease-causing germs. Decantation removes dirt but does not kill germs.
chunks.source: Decantation removes dirt but does not kill germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of making the water in Pot B safe for drinking. A: By boiling it. Boiling kills all the germs in the water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills all the germs in the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another way of making the water in Pot B safe for drinking. A: By filtering it. Filtering removes the remaining tiny dirt particles.
chunks.source: Filtering removes the remaining tiny dirt particles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is heat different from temperature? A: Heat is a form of energy while temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body. Heat is energy in transit; temperature measures how hot or cold something is.
chunks.source: Heat is energy in transit; temperature measures how hot or cold something is.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one effect of heat on matter: ____. A: It causes expansion. Heated matter expands and takes up more space.
chunks.source: Heated matter expands and takes up more space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State another effect of heat on matter: ____. A: It causes change of state (e.g. melting). Heat can change solids to liquids and liquids to gases.
chunks.source: Heat can change solids to liquids and liquids to gases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do telephone wires appear loose at some times of the day? A: They expand and sag during the hot part of the day. Heat makes the metal wires expand and hang loosely.
chunks.source: Heat makes the metal wires expand and hang loosely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the classification table. Identify the group of vertebrates marked X: ____. A: Cold-blooded vertebrates. X branches into fish, amphibians and reptiles, which are all cold-blooded.
chunks.source: X branches into fish, amphibians and reptiles, which are all cold-blooded.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the group of vertebrates marked Y: ____. A: Warm-blooded vertebrates. Y branches into birds and mammals, which keep a constant body temperature.
chunks.source: Y branches into birds and mammals, which keep a constant body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the group of vertebrates marked S: ____. A: Birds. S is the warm-blooded group with feathers that lay eggs.
chunks.source: S is the warm-blooded group with feathers that lay eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being vertebrates, mention any other similarity among groups of organisms labelled P, Q and R. A: They are all cold-blooded. Fish, amphibians and reptiles all have body temperatures that change with the environment.
chunks.source: Fish, amphibians and reptiles all have body temperatures that change with the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one intestinal worm in children: ____. A: Tapeworm. Tapeworms live in the intestines and steal digested food.
chunks.source: Tapeworms live in the intestines and steal digested food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another intestinal worm in children: ____. A: Roundworm. Roundworms are common intestinal worms in children.
chunks.source: Roundworms are common intestinal worms in children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which intestinal worms enter our bodies. A: Through eating food contaminated with worm eggs. Worm eggs on dirty food hatch inside the intestines.
chunks.source: Worm eggs on dirty food hatch inside the intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest any one way of preventing the spread of worms in children. A: By washing hands before eating. Clean hands stop worm eggs from reaching the mouth.
chunks.source: Clean hands stop worm eggs from reaching the mouth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: Match each deficiency disease in A with its cause in B.
A: (i) Night blindness, (ii) Kwashiorkor, (iii) Scurvy, (iv) Marasmus
B: Lack of carbohydrates in the diet, Lack of Vitamin A in the diet, Lack of vitamin C in the diet, Lack of proteins in the diet A: Night blindness: Lack of Vitamin A in the diet.; Kwashiorkor: Lack of proteins in the diet.; Scurvy: Lack of vitamin C in the diet.; Marasmus: Lack of carbohydrates in the diet.. Night blindness comes from lack of vitamin A, kwashiorkor from lack of proteins, scurvy from lack of vitamin C and marasmus from lack of carbohydrates.
chunks.source: Night blindness comes from lack of vitamin A, kwashiorkor from lack of proteins, scurvy from lack of vitamin C and marasmus from lack of carbohydrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the latrine. Identify the type of latrine drawn above: ____. A: VIP latrine (Ventilated Improved Pit latrine). The vent pipe on the latrine identifies it as a VIP latrine.
chunks.source: The vent pipe on the latrine identifies it as a VIP latrine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What process is taking place at part labelled X (the pit)? A: Decomposition of faeces. In the pit, bacteria break down the faeces into harmless matter.
chunks.source: In the pit, bacteria break down the faeces into harmless matter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the above type of latrine control the spread of diarrhoeal diseases? A: The vent pipe traps flies and reduces bad smell, so flies cannot carry germs to food. Fewer flies and no smell mean germs are not carried from the latrine to homes.
chunks.source: Fewer flies and no smell mean germs are not carried from the latrine to homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one advantage of the above latrine over an ordinary pit latrine. A: It has no bad smell and fewer flies. The vent pipe carries away smell and traps flies.
chunks.source: The vent pipe carries away smell and traps flies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the experiment with the measuring cylinder. Identify part K: ____. A: Stone (an irregular object). K is the irregular object tied with a thread and immersed in water.
chunks.source: K is the irregular object tied with a thread and immersed in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Find the volume of K: ____. A: 22cm³ (37ml − 15ml). Volume = final level − initial level = 37ml − 15ml = 22ml = 22cm³. (Readings are approximate from the diagram.)
chunks.source: Volume = final level − initial level = 37ml − 15ml = 22ml = 22cm³. (Readings are approximate from the diagram.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Work out the density of K if its mass is 60g: ____. A: 2.7g/cm³. Density = mass ÷ volume = 60g ÷ 22cm³ ≈ 2.7g/cm³.
chunks.source: Density = mass ÷ volume = 60g ÷ 22cm³ ≈ 2.7g/cm³.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the mushroom. Name the part marked X: ____. A: Cap (pileus). The cap is the umbrella-like top of the mushroom.
chunks.source: The cap is the umbrella-like top of the mushroom.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part marked Y in the diagram: ____. A: Gills. The gills are the thin plates under the cap that produce spores.
chunks.source: The gills are the thin plates under the cap that produce spores.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the mushroom reproduce? A: By means of spores. The gills release tiny spores which grow into new mushrooms.
chunks.source: The gills release tiny spores which grow into new mushrooms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the mushroom feed? A: It absorbs dissolved food from dead and decaying matter. Mushrooms feed saprophytically since they cannot make their own food.
chunks.source: Mushrooms feed saprophytically since they cannot make their own food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the water cycle. Name the process labelled B: ____. A: Evaporation. At B, heat from the sun changes water into vapour that rises.
chunks.source: At B, heat from the sun changes water into vapour that rises.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the process labelled D: ____. A: Condensation. At D, water vapour cools high up and forms clouds.
chunks.source: At D, water vapour cools high up and forms clouds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of the sun in the natural cycle above. A: It provides the heat that causes evaporation of water. Without the sun's heat, water would not evaporate to start the cycle.
chunks.source: Without the sun's heat, water would not evaporate to start the cycle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you help in maintaining the above cycle in your environment? A: By planting trees and protecting water sources. Trees release vapour and protect the sources that feed the cycle.
chunks.source: Trees release vapour and protect the sources that feed the cycle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one body organ that helps a P.6 child to taste food: ____. A: Tongue. The tongue has taste buds that detect the taste of food.
chunks.source: The tongue has taste buds that detect the taste of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can soil erosion be controlled in a school compound? A: By planting grass to hold the soil. Grass roots hold the soil firmly so it is not washed away.
chunks.source: Grass roots hold the soil firmly so it is not washed away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way in which water can be made safe for drinking at home. A: By boiling it. Boiling kills the germs in water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is rusting considered to be a chemical change? A: Because a new substance (rust) is formed and the change cannot be reversed. Rusting creates a completely new substance that cannot turn back into iron.
chunks.source: Rusting creates a completely new substance that cannot turn back into iron.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one disadvantage of using the traditional beehive shown above. A: It is difficult to inspect the hive and harvest honey without destroying the combs. The fixed combs of a traditional hive break during harvest, giving less honey.
chunks.source: The fixed combs of a traditional hive break during harvest, giving less honey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do farmers propagate Irish potatoes? A: By planting tubers. Irish potatoes are grown from the tubers themselves.
chunks.source: Irish potatoes are grown from the tubers themselves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger of rearing many chickens in a small poultry house. A: Diseases spread easily among the crowded birds. Overcrowding lets diseases and parasites pass quickly from bird to bird.
chunks.source: Overcrowding lets diseases and parasites pass quickly from bird to bird.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can an alcoholic parent affect children's education in a family? A: He or she wastes money on alcohol instead of paying school fees. Money spent on alcohol is not available for fees and books.
chunks.source: Money spent on alcohol is not available for fees and books.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way is the spread of dysentery different from the spread of tuberculosis? A: Dysentery spreads through contaminated food and water while tuberculosis spreads through air. Dysentery germs enter through the mouth; TB germs are breathed in.
chunks.source: Dysentery germs enter through the mouth; TB germs are breathed in.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the best way for preserving apples? A: Refrigeration. Cold storage slows down the rotting of fruits like apples.
chunks.source: Cold storage slows down the rotting of fruits like apples.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a baby with X at the mouth. How is the vaccine administered through part X important to the baby? A: It protects the baby against polio. The oral polio vaccine given through the mouth guards the baby against polio.
chunks.source: The oral polio vaccine given through the mouth guards the baby against polio.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of wind in the environment. A: It destroys crops and buildings. Strong wind blows down crops and damages houses.
chunks.source: Strong wind blows down crops and damages houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mr. Muwonge was advised by a doctor to eat more foods rich in iron. State the deficiency disease Mr. Muwonge was suffering from: ____. A: Anaemia. Lack of iron causes anaemia, a shortage of healthy red blood cells.
chunks.source: Lack of iron causes anaemia, a shortage of healthy red blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a spider depend on its cobweb to feed? A: It traps insects in the web and then eats them. Flying insects get stuck in the sticky web for the spider to eat.
chunks.source: Flying insects get stuck in the sticky web for the spider to eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a musical drum. Name the domestic animal from which part A (the drum skin) is got: ____. A: Cow. Drum skins are made from the hide of a cow.
chunks.source: Drum skins are made from the hide of a cow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the first step in washing clothes: ____. A: Sorting the clothes. Clothes are sorted by colour and dirtiness before washing.
chunks.source: Clothes are sorted by colour and dirtiness before washing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a sugarcane not regarded as a stem tuber? A: Because it does not develop a swollen underground stem for storing food. A stem tuber is a swollen underground stem like the Irish potato; sugarcane has none.
chunks.source: A stem tuber is a swollen underground stem like the Irish potato; sugarcane has none.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens to the volume of water when frozen? A: It increases. Water expands when it freezes into ice.
chunks.source: Water expands when it freezes into ice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of grasshoppers to people. A: They are eaten as food. Grasshoppers (nsenene) are a popular seasonal delicacy.
chunks.source: Grasshoppers (nsenene) are a popular seasonal delicacy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a sickle useful to a cattle farmer who carries out zero grazing? A: It is used for cutting grass to feed the cattle. Zero-grazing farmers cut pasture with a sickle and carry it to the animals.
chunks.source: Zero-grazing farmers cut pasture with a sickle and carry it to the animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one method of harvesting cassava: ____. A: By uprooting. Cassava roots are pulled out of the soil by uprooting the plant.
chunks.source: Cassava roots are pulled out of the soil by uprooting the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one type of chicken: ____. A: Layers. Layers are chickens kept for egg production.
chunks.source: Layers are chickens kept for egg production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way in which the reproduction of a bean plant is similar to that of a pine tree. A: Both reproduce by means of seeds. Beans and pines both produce seeds that grow into new plants.
chunks.source: Beans and pines both produce seeds that grow into new plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the fertilization in birds different from that in amphibians? A: Birds have internal fertilization while amphibians have external fertilization. In birds the sperm meets the egg inside the body; in amphibians they meet in water.
chunks.source: In birds the sperm meets the egg inside the body; in amphibians they meet in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do hyenas move in the same places with lions? A: To feed on the leftovers of the lions' prey. Hyenas scavenge the remains of animals killed by lions.
chunks.source: Hyenas scavenge the remains of animals killed by lions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way people can make good use of plant resources. A: By planting trees and using plant products sustainably. Planting trees replaces what is cut and keeps resources available.
chunks.source: Planting trees replaces what is cut and keeps resources available.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the main purpose of including legumes in the crop rotation cycle? A: They add nitrogen to the soil. Legumes fix nitrogen from the air into the soil for the next crops.
chunks.source: Legumes fix nitrogen from the air into the soil for the next crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the component of soil that helps to make soil: ____. A: Living organisms. Likely answer: living organisms such as bacteria and earthworms break down dead matter and rock particles, helping to form soil.
chunks.source: Likely answer: living organisms such as bacteria and earthworms break down dead matter and rock particles, helping to form soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one material used to make local salt: ____. A: Ash (from burnt plants). Local salt is traditionally made from plant ash.
chunks.source: Local salt is traditionally made from plant ash.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one advantage of using solar energy in our homes. A: It is free and does not pollute the environment. Sunlight costs nothing and produces no smoke.
chunks.source: Sunlight costs nothing and produces no smoke.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: During the preparation of food, salt may be added. Give any one importance of the salt added to food. A: It adds taste to the food. Salt improves the flavour of food.
chunks.source: Salt improves the flavour of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does heat travel through gases? A: By convection. In gases, heat moves with the rising warm currents.
chunks.source: In gases, heat moves with the rising warm currents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one importance of a dust bin in a school: ____. A: It keeps the school clean by collecting rubbish. Rubbish goes into the dustbin instead of littering the compound.
chunks.source: Rubbish goes into the dustbin instead of littering the compound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you control mosquitoes in your bedroom? A: By sleeping under a mosquito net. A treated net stops mosquitoes from biting at night.
chunks.source: A treated net stops mosquitoes from biting at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one economic importance of plant fibres. A: They are used to make ropes, mats and baskets for sale. Plant fibres provide raw material for crafts that earn income.
chunks.source: Plant fibres provide raw material for crafts that earn income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the tooth. Name the part labelled A: ____. A: Crown. The crown is the upper visible part of the tooth.
chunks.source: The crown is the upper visible part of the tooth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are plasmodia germs spread by female anopheles mosquitoes dangerous to the human circulatory system? A: They destroy red blood cells, causing anaemia. Plasmodia attack and burst red blood cells, weakening the blood.
chunks.source: Plasmodia attack and burst red blood cells, weakening the blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Anderson's body temperature is 38C. What first aid can Anderson be given? A: Sponge his body with lukewarm water to cool him down. Sponging removes excess heat from a feverish body.
chunks.source: Sponging removes excess heat from a feverish body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which ticks affect the health of goats on a farm. A: They suck blood, making the goats anaemic. Ticks drain blood and can spread tick-borne diseases.
chunks.source: Ticks drain blood and can spread tick-borne diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the male reproductive cell of a mammal: ____. A: Sperm. The sperm is the male cell that fertilizes the egg.
chunks.source: The sperm is the male cell that fertilizes the egg.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is cannibalism as used in poultry management? A: It is a vice where birds peck and eat one another. Cannibalism starts when birds peck at each other's feathers and flesh.
chunks.source: Cannibalism starts when birds peck at each other's feathers and flesh.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one cause of the above poultry vice: ____. A: Overcrowding. Crowded birds get stressed and start pecking each other.
chunks.source: Crowded birds get stressed and start pecking each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down another cause of the above poultry vice: ____. A: Lack of enough food. Hungry birds peck at each other searching for food.
chunks.source: Hungry birds peck at each other searching for food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way can the above vice affect the poultry farmer? A: Birds injure and kill each other, causing losses to the farmer. Dead and injured birds mean fewer eggs and less income.
chunks.source: Dead and injured birds mean fewer eggs and less income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the flowering plant. From what part of the seed does part K (the root) develop? A: Radicle. The radicle is the first part of the embryo to grow out and form the root.
chunks.source: The radicle is the first part of the embryo to grow out and form the root.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of flowering plant is shown above? A: Dicotyledonous plant (dicot). The plant has a taproot system, which is a feature of dicots.
chunks.source: The plant has a taproot system, which is a feature of dicots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason for your answer in (b) above. A: It has a taproot system. Taproots grow from dicot seeds, unlike the fibrous roots of monocots.
chunks.source: Taproots grow from dicot seeds, unlike the fibrous roots of monocots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is part N (the leaves) important to the plant? A: Leaves make food for the plant through photosynthesis. Leaves trap sunlight to manufacture food for the whole plant.
chunks.source: Leaves trap sunlight to manufacture food for the whole plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from ordinary pit latrines, write down any other one type of latrine: ____. A: VIP latrine. A VIP latrine has a vent pipe that removes smell and flies.
chunks.source: A VIP latrine has a vent pipe that removes smell and flies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of caring for an ordinary pit latrine. A: By cleaning it regularly. Regular cleaning keeps the latrine hygienic.
chunks.source: Regular cleaning keeps the latrine hygienic.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another way of caring for an ordinary pit latrine. A: By keeping the squat hole covered. A covered hole stops flies from entering and smells from escaping.
chunks.source: A covered hole stops flies from entering and smells from escaping.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one disease associated with poor use of latrines: ____. A: Cholera. Faeces near homes spread cholera germs to food and water.
chunks.source: Faeces near homes spread cholera germs to food and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one set of teeth in humans: ____. A: Milk teeth (deciduous teeth). Milk teeth are the first set that falls out in childhood.
chunks.source: Milk teeth are the first set that falls out in childhood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the other set of teeth in humans: ____. A: Permanent teeth. Permanent teeth replace milk teeth and last into adulthood.
chunks.source: Permanent teeth replace milk teeth and last into adulthood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which mineral salt is responsible for the development of healthy teeth? ____. A: Calcium. Calcium hardens the teeth and bones.
chunks.source: Calcium hardens the teeth and bones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write the danger of continuous use of sugary foods to the teeth. A: It causes tooth decay. Sugar feeds germs that eat into the teeth.
chunks.source: Sugar feeds germs that eat into the teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a method of separating mixtures. Name the method used above: ____. A: Filtration. Passing pond water through filter paper to trap dirt is filtration.
chunks.source: Passing pond water through filter paper to trap dirt is filtration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one impurity removed by using the above method: ____. A: Mud (dirt particles). The filter paper traps mud and sand from the pond water.
chunks.source: The filter paper traps mud and sand from the pond water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The solid material trapped on the filter paper is called the ____. A: Residue. The residue is the solid left behind on the filter paper.
chunks.source: The residue is the solid left behind on the filter paper.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one danger of drinking water marked L. A: It may still contain germs that cause diseases. Filtration removes dirt but does not kill germs.
chunks.source: Filtration removes dirt but does not kill germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do bacteria reproduce? A: By binary fission (dividing into two). One bacterium splits into two identical new bacteria.
chunks.source: One bacterium splits into two identical new bacteria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which bacteria are harmful: A: They cause diseases. Disease-causing bacteria make people and animals sick.
chunks.source: Disease-causing bacteria make people and animals sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which bacteria are useful: A: They help in the decomposition of dead matter. Bacteria rot dead matter, returning nutrients to the soil.
chunks.source: Bacteria rot dead matter, returning nutrients to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can the presence of bacteria be controlled in our bodies? A: By observing personal hygiene and taking prescribed antibiotics. Cleanliness keeps bacteria away and antibiotics kill them inside the body.
chunks.source: Cleanliness keeps bacteria away and antibiotics kill them inside the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: Match the items in A to those in B correctly.
A: Mass, Weight, Volume, Density
B: the space occupied by an object, the force exerted on an object by gravitational force, mass per unit volume, the quantity of matter in an object A: Mass: the quantity of matter in an object.; Weight: the force exerted on an object by gravitational force.; Volume: the space occupied by an object.; Density: mass per unit volume.. Mass is the quantity of matter, weight is the pull of gravity, volume is space occupied and density is mass per unit volume.
chunks.source: Mass is the quantity of matter, weight is the pull of gravity, volume is space occupied and density is mass per unit volume.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from wind, give one other agent of seed dispersal: ____. A: Animals. Animals carry seeds on their fur or in their droppings.
chunks.source: Animals carry seeds on their fur or in their droppings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one characteristic of seeds dispersed by wind: ____. A: They are light. Light seeds are easily carried away by wind.
chunks.source: Light seeds are easily carried away by wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Outline any one importance of seed dispersal. A: It reduces competition for nutrients among seedlings. Spread-out seeds do not fight for the same water and nutrients.
chunks.source: Spread-out seeds do not fight for the same water and nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Outline another importance of seed dispersal. A: It helps plants to colonize new areas. Dispersal lets plants grow in new places far from the parent.
chunks.source: Dispersal lets plants grow in new places far from the parent.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: Arrange the following statements properly to explain how the volume of an irregular object is obtained.
(a) A thread is tied to an irregular object.
(b) Volume is got by subtracting 1st level from 2nd level.
(c) An irregular object is then immersed in a measuring cylinder with water.
(d) The level of water rises from 1st level to 2nd level. A: A thread is tied to an irregular object., An irregular object is then immersed in a measuring cylinder with water., The level of water rises from 1st level to 2nd level., Volume is got by subtracting 1st level from 2nd level.. First tie the thread, then immerse the object, watch the level rise, and finally subtract the first level from the second.
chunks.source: First tie the thread, then immerse the object, watch the level rise, and finally subtract the first level from the second.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is pitch different from volume in relation to sound energy? A: Pitch is the highness or lowness of sound while volume is the loudness or softness of sound. Pitch describes how high a sound is; volume describes how loud it is.
chunks.source: Pitch describes how high a sound is; volume describes how loud it is.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one factor that affects the pitch of sound: ____. A: Length of the vibrating object. Shorter strings vibrate faster and produce a higher pitch.
chunks.source: Shorter strings vibrate faster and produce a higher pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention another factor that affects the pitch of sound: ____. A: Tension (tightness) of the vibrating object. Tighter strings produce a higher pitch.
chunks.source: Tighter strings produce a higher pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one animal that uses echoes to locate its food: ____. A: Bat. Bats use echoes to find insects in the dark.
chunks.source: Bats use echoes to find insects in the dark.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a balanced diet? A: A diet containing all food values in their right amounts. A balanced diet gives the body every nutrient it needs.
chunks.source: A balanced diet gives the body every nutrient it needs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write the deficiency disease associated with lack of enough carbohydrates: ____. A: Marasmus. Without enough carbohydrates the body wastes away (marasmus).
chunks.source: Without enough carbohydrates the body wastes away (marasmus).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write the deficiency disease associated with lack of enough proteins: ____. A: Kwashiorkor. Without enough proteins children develop kwashiorkor.
chunks.source: Without enough proteins children develop kwashiorkor.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can scurvy be prevented among children? A: By feeding them fruits rich in vitamin C. Fruits like oranges supply the vitamin C that prevents scurvy.
chunks.source: Fruits like oranges supply the vitamin C that prevents scurvy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the human body organs. Name the body organ represented by Y: ____. A: Lungs. Y points to the lungs in the chest.
chunks.source: Y points to the lungs in the chest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the body organ represented by X: ____. A: Stomach. X points to the stomach in the abdomen.
chunks.source: X points to the stomach in the abdomen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way is the organ represented by letter A (the brain) important to a child writing examinations? A: It stores information and helps the child remember what was read. The brain keeps memories, so the child can recall lessons in the exam.
chunks.source: The brain keeps memories, so the child can recall lessons in the exam.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the main function of organ Z (the heart) in the body. A: It pumps blood to all parts of the body. The heart pushes blood around the body without stopping.
chunks.source: The heart pushes blood around the body without stopping.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of honey bees is usually seen around flower gardens? A: Worker bees. Worker bees fly from flower to flower collecting nectar.
chunks.source: Worker bees fly from flower to flower collecting nectar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one thing bees get from flowers: ____. A: Nectar. Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers to make honey.
chunks.source: Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers to make honey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State another thing bees get from flowers: ____. A: Pollen. Bees also collect pollen, which they use as food.
chunks.source: Bees also collect pollen, which they use as food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one importance of bees to flowering plants. A: They help in pollination. As bees move, they carry pollen from flower to flower.
chunks.source: As bees move, they carry pollen from flower to flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows heat transfer through matter. Name the circular movement marked N: ____. A: Convection current. The circular movement of the heated water is a convection current.
chunks.source: The circular movement of the heated water is a convection current.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the source of heat used above: ____. A: Burning charcoal. The charcoal stove supplies the heat.
chunks.source: The charcoal stove supplies the heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part of the charcoal stove that takes out warm air: ____. A: Air holes (vents). Likely answer: the air holes let warm air and smoke escape from the stove.
chunks.source: Likely answer: the air holes let warm air and smoke escape from the stove.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What can one do to reduce the burning charcoal? A: Close the stove door and air holes to cut off the air supply. Less air reaching the charcoal slows down its burning.
chunks.source: Less air reaching the charcoal slows down its burning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one element of weather that favours maize harvesting: ____. A: Sunshine. Sunshine dries the maize for safe harvesting and storage.
chunks.source: Sunshine dries the maize for safe harvesting and storage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a maize farmer benefit from the element of weather in (a) above? A: It dries the maize grains so they store well without rotting. Dry grains keep safely in the granary.
chunks.source: Dry grains keep safely in the granary.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the element of weather given in (a) above, mention any other one element of weather that favours farmers' activities: ____. A: Rainfall. Rainfall provides the water crops need to grow.
chunks.source: Rainfall provides the water crops need to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention another element of weather that favours farmers' activities: ____. A: Wind. Wind helps in winnowing harvested grains.
chunks.source: Wind helps in winnowing harvested grains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the young one of a cat? ____. A: Kitten. A baby cat is called a kitten.
chunks.source: A baby cat is called a kitten.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way can heat be useful to man? A: For cooking food. Heat from fire cooks our food.
chunks.source: Heat from fire cooks our food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one physical process involved in the formation of clouds: ____. A: Condensation. Water vapour condenses high in the sky to form clouds.
chunks.source: Water vapour condenses high in the sky to form clouds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the body organ which stores information: ____. A: Brain. The brain keeps everything we learn and remember.
chunks.source: The brain keeps everything we learn and remember.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a duck billed platypus called a mammal yet it reproduces by laying eggs? A: Because it has fur and suckles its young on milk. Like all mammals, the platypus feeds its babies on milk.
chunks.source: Like all mammals, the platypus feeds its babies on milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way of preventing metals from rusting. A: By painting them. Paint covers metal so air and water cannot reach it.
chunks.source: Paint covers metal so air and water cannot reach it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does slashing around the compound help to control the spread of malaria? A: It destroys the bushy hiding and breeding places of mosquitoes. Mosquitoes rest and breed in bushes near homes.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes rest and breed in bushes near homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is an extended family? A: A family made up of parents, children, grandparents and other relatives living together. An extended family includes relatives beyond parents and children.
chunks.source: An extended family includes relatives beyond parents and children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of soil does not keep water for long? ____. A: Sand soil. Water drains quickly through the large particles of sand soil.
chunks.source: Water drains quickly through the large particles of sand soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a nocturnal animal: ____. A: Bat. Bats are active at night and rest during the day.
chunks.source: Bats are active at night and rest during the day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one body part where a thermometer is fixed to take the temperature: ____. A: Armpit. The thermometer is placed in the armpit to read body temperature.
chunks.source: The thermometer is placed in the armpit to read body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one advantage of paddock grazing in goat keeping. A: It controls the spread of diseases among the goats. Moving goats between paddocks breaks the cycle of parasites.
chunks.source: Moving goats between paddocks breaks the cycle of parasites.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a tongue useful in the digestion process? A: It rolls food into a bolus and pushes it down for swallowing. The tongue shapes chewed food into a ball for easy swallowing.
chunks.source: The tongue shapes chewed food into a ball for easy swallowing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens to a plant if it is planted in a vase in a dark room which has a small window to let in light? A: It grows bending towards the light from the window. Plants grow towards light to trap it for photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants grow towards light to trap it for photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should food kept for future use be properly covered? A: To prevent contamination by germs, dust and flies. Covered food stays clean and safe for later eating.
chunks.source: Covered food stays clean and safe for later eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A spoon left in hot tea becomes hot up to the handle. Which process of heat transfer does this show? A: Conduction. Heat travels through the solid metal spoon by conduction.
chunks.source: Heat travels through the solid metal spoon by conduction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can effects of floods be controlled in the environment? A: By planting trees and digging drainage channels. Trees slow running water and channels carry it away safely.
chunks.source: Trees slow running water and channels carry it away safely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest one way of maintaining the digestive system in good working condition. A: By eating a balanced diet. Good food keeps all digestive organs working smoothly.
chunks.source: Good food keeps all digestive organs working smoothly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way can a poultry farmer control poultry diseases in the poultry house? A: By vaccinating the birds. Vaccines protect chickens against killer diseases.
chunks.source: Vaccines protect chickens against killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What activity can be done by a primary six boy in order to promote environmental sanitation? A: Sweeping the compound. Sweeping removes dirt and keeps the surroundings clean.
chunks.source: Sweeping removes dirt and keeps the surroundings clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is friction? A: Friction is the force that opposes motion between two surfaces in contact. Friction resists sliding, which is why things slow down and stop.
chunks.source: Friction resists sliding, which is why things slow down and stop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should teeth be brushed after a meal? A: To remove food remains that cause tooth decay. Leftover food rots the teeth if not brushed away.
chunks.source: Leftover food rots the teeth if not brushed away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is castration important in livestock farming? A: It makes animals grow fat quickly and controls unwanted breeding. Castrated males fatten faster and cannot breed anyhow.
chunks.source: Castrated males fatten faster and cannot breed anyhow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the picture below. Name the type of family shown: ____. A: Extended family. Likely answer: the picture shows many adults and children together, like grandparents, parents and children.
chunks.source: Likely answer: the picture shows many adults and children together, like grandparents, parents and children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of change occurs when a leopard dies of an illness? ____. A: Biological change. Death and decay of a living thing is a biological change.
chunks.source: Death and decay of a living thing is a biological change.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do some plants reduce the rate of transpiration? A: By shedding their leaves. Without leaves, a plant loses very little water.
chunks.source: Without leaves, a plant loses very little water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can wind be useful in the environment? A: It helps in seed dispersal and winnowing of grains. Wind carries seeds to new places and cleans harvested grains.
chunks.source: Wind carries seeds to new places and cleans harvested grains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why a nurse shakes the thermometer before taking the temperature reading. A: To bring the mercury level below the normal mark. Shaking returns the mercury down for a fresh correct reading.
chunks.source: Shaking returns the mercury down for a fresh correct reading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one product from a Marino sheep: ____. A: Wool. Merino sheep are famous for their fine wool.
chunks.source: Merino sheep are famous for their fine wool.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one soil pollutant: ____. A: Polythene bags. Polythene bags dumped in soil pollute it.
chunks.source: Polythene bags dumped in soil pollute it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can water promote personal hygiene? A: It is used for bathing, washing clothes and cleaning the body. We need water for washing ourselves and our clothes.
chunks.source: We need water for washing ourselves and our clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the bird's foot. Identify the type of foot shown: ____. A: Scratching foot. The strong toes of a domestic fowl are adapted for scratching the ground.
chunks.source: The strong toes of a domestic fowl are adapted for scratching the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do birds with such kind of foot feed on? A: Seeds and grains scratched from the soil. Scratching feet dig up seeds, grains and small insects from the ground.
chunks.source: Scratching feet dig up seeds, grains and small insects from the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are enzymes? A: Enzymes are chemical substances in the body that speed up digestion. Enzymes break down food faster inside the digestive system.
chunks.source: Enzymes break down food faster inside the digestive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from having a latrine, name any one other item a healthy home should have: ____. A: A bathroom. A healthy home needs a bathroom for bathing.
chunks.source: A healthy home needs a bathroom for bathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way conduction of heat is applied in our daily life. A: Ironing clothes with a hot flat iron. The hot iron passes heat to the clothes by conduction.
chunks.source: The hot iron passes heat to the clothes by conduction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one advantage of biological changes in the environment. A: They lead to growth of living things and add fertility to the soil through decay. Growth and decomposition keep life and soil fertility going.
chunks.source: Growth and decomposition keep life and soil fertility going.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the plant in the diagram below get support in order to get enough sunlight? A: It climbs up a support using its tendrils. Tendrils coil around a support and pull the plant up towards light.
chunks.source: Tendrils coil around a support and pull the plant up towards light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does planting trees control soil erosion in the compound? A: Their roots hold the soil firmly together. Tree roots grip the soil so running water cannot wash it away.
chunks.source: Tree roots grip the soil so running water cannot wash it away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one material used for making composite manure: ____. A: Animal droppings. Animal droppings rot into rich composite manure.
chunks.source: Animal droppings rot into rich composite manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Define volume of an object. A: Volume is the amount of space occupied by an object. Volume tells how much space something takes up.
chunks.source: Volume tells how much space something takes up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can the volume of an irregular object be found? A: By the displacement method: immersing it in water in a measuring cylinder. The rise in water level equals the volume of the object.
chunks.source: The rise in water level equals the volume of the object.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List down any one example of irregular objects: ____. A: Stone. A stone has no regular shape.
chunks.source: A stone has no regular shape.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List down another example of irregular objects: ____. A: Key. A key's shape is not regular.
chunks.source: A key's shape is not regular.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one characteristic of living things: ____. A: They feed. All living things take in food for energy.
chunks.source: All living things take in food for energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State another characteristic of living things: ____. A: They grow. Living things increase in size as they develop.
chunks.source: Living things increase in size as they develop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one major group of living things: ____. A: Plants. Plants are one major group of living things.
chunks.source: Plants are one major group of living things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another major group of living things: ____. A: Animals. Animals are the other major group of living things.
chunks.source: Animals are the other major group of living things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the human body system. Name the part labeled G: ____. A: Trachea (wind pipe). The trachea is the tube that carries air to the lungs.
chunks.source: The trachea is the tube that carries air to the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part labeled F: ____. A: Bronchus. The bronchus branches from the trachea into each lung.
chunks.source: The bronchus branches from the trachea into each lung.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which system of the body does the diagram belong? A: Respiratory system. These organs are all used in breathing.
chunks.source: These organs are all used in breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one bad health practice that may affect proper functioning of the system. A: Smoking. Smoke damages the lungs and air passages.
chunks.source: Smoke damages the lungs and air passages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which component of air is used by plants to make food? ____. A: Carbon dioxide. Plants take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Other than the component named above, name any two other components of air. A: Oxygen and nitrogen. Air also contains oxygen and nitrogen.
chunks.source: Air also contains oxygen and nitrogen.

chunks.subject: Science
