chunks.text: Q: How does planting of many trees in the environment help to reduce the component named in 44(a) above? A: Trees absorb carbon dioxide during photosynthesis. Growing trees take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen.
chunks.source: Growing trees take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one product got from poultry farming: ____. A: Eggs. Poultry farms produce eggs for food and sale.
chunks.source: Poultry farms produce eggs for food and sale.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is poultry farming important to a baking industry? A: It provides the eggs used in baking. Bakers need a steady supply of eggs for cakes and bread.
chunks.source: Bakers need a steady supply of eggs for cakes and bread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it not advisable to keep turkeys together with chicken in the same room? A: Turkeys can spread diseases to the chicken. Turkeys carry infections like blackhead that kill chickens.
chunks.source: Turkeys carry infections like blackhead that kill chickens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one disease of poultry: ____. A: Newcastle disease. Newcastle disease kills chickens in large numbers.
chunks.source: Newcastle disease kills chickens in large numbers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is dehydration? A: Dehydration is the loss of a lot of water from the body. When the body loses too much water, it becomes dehydrated.
chunks.source: When the body loses too much water, it becomes dehydrated.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one cause of dehydration: ____. A: Diarrhoea. Diarrhoea drains a lot of water from the body.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea drains a lot of water from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State another cause of dehydration: ____. A: Vomiting. Vomiting also removes water from the body.
chunks.source: Vomiting also removes water from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest one way you can prevent one from becoming dehydrated. A: By drinking a lot of fluids and giving ORS. Replacing lost water with drinks or ORS prevents dehydration.
chunks.source: Replacing lost water with drinks or ORS prevents dehydration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text:
Q: Match the changes that take place in the environment in A with their descriptions in B.
A: (i) Flood, (ii) Drought, (iii) Landslides, (iv) Earth quake
B: Abrupt falling of a mass of soil covering another area, Sudden shaking of the earth which takes short time, Much amount of water occupying an area of land, Long period without water (rain) A: Flood: Much amount of water occupying an area of land.; Drought: Long period without water (rain); Landslides: Abrupt falling of a mass of soil covering another area; Earth quake: Sudden shaking of the earth which takes short time. A flood is too much water, a drought is too little rain, a landslide is falling soil and an earthquake is shaking ground.
chunks.source: A flood is too much water, a drought is too little rain, a landslide is falling soil and an earthquake is shaking ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are carnivorous mammals? A: Mammals that feed on flesh. Carnivorous mammals hunt and eat other animals.
chunks.source: Carnivorous mammals hunt and eat other animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one characteristic of carnivorous mammals: ____. A: They have sharp pointed canines for tearing flesh. Sharp canines tear meat from prey.
chunks.source: Sharp canines tear meat from prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State another characteristic of carnivorous mammals: ____. A: They have strong claws for holding prey. Strong claws grip struggling prey.
chunks.source: Strong claws grip struggling prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a carnivorous mammal: ____. A: Lion. The lion is a well-known flesh-eating mammal.
chunks.source: The lion is a well-known flesh-eating mammal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who is a casualty? A: A casualty is a person who is injured in an accident. Anyone hurt in an accident is called a casualty.
chunks.source: Anyone hurt in an accident is called a casualty.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two reasons for giving first aid. A: To save life and to prevent the injury from getting worse. First aid keeps the victim alive and stops injuries worsening.
chunks.source: First aid keeps the victim alive and stops injuries worsening.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one example of a first aid kit: ____. A: Bandage. A bandage is used to cover wounds.
chunks.source: A bandage is used to cover wounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one effect of heat on matter: ____. A: It causes expansion. Heated matter expands.
chunks.source: Heated matter expands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State another effect of heat on matter: ____. A: It causes change of state. Heat can melt solids and boil liquids.
chunks.source: Heat can melt solids and boil liquids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is sunny weather important in the environment? A: It gives light and warmth that plants need to make food. Sunshine powers photosynthesis in plants.
chunks.source: Sunshine powers photosynthesis in plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is windy weather important in the environment? A: Wind helps in seed dispersal and in winnowing grains. Wind spreads seeds and cleans harvested grains.
chunks.source: Wind spreads seeds and cleans harvested grains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: During which weather can a Campbell sunshine recorder be used? A: Sunny weather. The recorder needs sunshine to burn its readings.
chunks.source: The recorder needs sunshine to burn its readings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does wind help to dry wet clothes? A: It carries away water vapour from the clothes. Wind removes the vapour so more water evaporates.
chunks.source: Wind removes the vapour so more water evaporates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one type of family: ____. A: Nuclear family. A nuclear family has parents and their children only.
chunks.source: A nuclear family has parents and their children only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another type of family: ____. A: Extended family. An extended family includes grandparents and other relatives.
chunks.source: An extended family includes grandparents and other relatives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one role of a father at home: ____. A: He provides the basic needs of the family. Fathers work to feed, clothe and house the family.
chunks.source: Fathers work to feed, clothe and house the family.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State another role of a father at home: ____. A: He protects the family. Fathers keep the family safe from harm.
chunks.source: Fathers keep the family safe from harm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of changes of state. Name the state of matter labeled Q: ____. A: Solid. Sublimation changes Q directly into gas, so Q is a solid.
chunks.source: Sublimation changes Q directly into gas, so Q is a solid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the state of matter labeled P: ____. A: Liquid. Condensation changes gas into P, so P is a liquid.
chunks.source: Condensation changes gas into P, so P is a liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention the process of change of state of matter labeled M: ____. A: Evaporation. M changes liquid P into gas.
chunks.source: M changes liquid P into gas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention the process of change of state of matter labeled N: ____. A: Freezing. N changes liquid P into solid Q, which is freezing. (Read from the diagram's arrow directions.)
chunks.source: N changes liquid P into solid Q, which is freezing. (Read from the diagram's arrow directions.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one type of root: ____. A: Taproot. A taproot grows straight down from the seed.
chunks.source: A taproot grows straight down from the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another type of root: ____. A: Fibrous root. Fibrous roots spread out in many thin branches.
chunks.source: Fibrous roots spread out in many thin branches.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way are roots useful to plants? A: They absorb water and mineral salts from the soil. Roots take in what the plant needs from the soil.
chunks.source: Roots take in what the plant needs from the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way are roots useful to animals? A: Some animals feed on roots. Animals like rabbits eat roots such as carrots.
chunks.source: Animals like rabbits eat roots such as carrots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one garden tool used in land preparation: ____. A: Hoe. A hoe digs and breaks the soil.
chunks.source: A hoe digs and breaks the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name another garden tool used in land preparation: ____. A: Spade. A spade cuts and turns the soil.
chunks.source: A spade cuts and turns the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name a third garden tool used in land preparation: ____. A: Rake. A rake levels the dug soil.
chunks.source: A rake levels the dug soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is transplanting usually done in the evening? A: To reduce water loss so the seedlings do not wilt. Evening coolness lets seedlings settle without wilting.
chunks.source: Evening coolness lets seedlings settle without wilting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the best soil for growing crops: ____ A: Loam soil. Loam soil has sand, clay and humus mixed, so it holds water and air and is fertile.
chunks.source: Loam soil has sand, clay and humus mixed, so it holds water and air and is fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the function of gills on a mushroom: ____ A: They produce (and release) spores. The gills under the cap of a mushroom make the tiny spores used for reproduction.
chunks.source: The gills under the cap of a mushroom make the tiny spores used for reproduction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a spur useful to a cock? ____ A: For fighting (protection/defence). A cock uses its sharp spurs to fight enemies and protect itself.
chunks.source: A cock uses its sharp spurs to fight enemies and protect itself.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one property of air: ____ A: Air occupies space. Air takes up space, has weight and exerts pressure even though we cannot see it.
chunks.source: Air takes up space, has weight and exerts pressure even though we cannot see it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the organisms found in root nodules of legumes: ____ A: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria (Rhizobium). Tiny bacteria living in the root nodules of beans and other legumes fix nitrogen from the air into the soil.
chunks.source: Tiny bacteria living in the root nodules of beans and other legumes fix nitrogen from the air into the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the blood vessel marked with letter I in the diagram: ____ A: Vein. Likely answer: vessel I has a wide lumen and thin wall, which is how a vein is drawn (arteries have thick walls and narrow lumens).
chunks.source: Likely answer: vessel I has a wide lumen and thin wall, which is how a vein is drawn (arteries have thick walls and narrow lumens).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one function of blood vessels in the body: ____ A: They transport (carry) blood around the body. Blood vessels carry blood with oxygen, food and waste materials to and from all body parts.
chunks.source: Blood vessels carry blood with oxygen, food and waste materials to and from all body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which form of energy is produced by vibrations of an object? ____ A: Sound energy. When an object vibrates, it produces sound energy.
chunks.source: When an object vibrates, it produces sound energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the reptile in the diagram protect itself? ____ A: It changes its body colour to camouflage (blend) with the surroundings. The chameleon in the diagram changes colour to match its environment so enemies cannot see it.
chunks.source: The chameleon in the diagram changes colour to match its environment so enemies cannot see it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one organ damaged by excessive alcoholism: ____ A: Liver. Too much alcohol damages the liver (and also the brain and stomach).
chunks.source: Too much alcohol damages the liver (and also the brain and stomach).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of an essential drug: ____ A: Paracetamol (Panadol). Essential drugs are safe, affordable and always needed medicines such as paracetamol.
chunks.source: Essential drugs are safe, affordable and always needed medicines such as paracetamol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way bacteria are useful in the environment: ____ A: They decompose (rot) dead plants and animals. Bacteria break down dead matter, returning nutrients to the soil; some also fix nitrogen.
chunks.source: Bacteria break down dead matter, returning nutrients to the soil; some also fix nitrogen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is clay soil able to retain water much longer than any other type of soil? ____ A: Because it has the smallest (finest) particles packed closely together. Clay has very tiny particles with tiny air spaces, so water is trapped and drains very slowly.
chunks.source: Clay has very tiny particles with tiny air spaces, so water is trapped and drains very slowly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of maintaining soil fertility: ____ A: Mulching. Adding manure or mulch, crop rotation and bush fallowing keep the soil fertile.
chunks.source: Adding manure or mulch, crop rotation and bush fallowing keep the soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is water called a universal solvent? ____ A: Because it dissolves many substances. Water can dissolve very many things such as salt and sugar, so it is called a universal solvent.
chunks.source: Water can dissolve very many things such as salt and sugar, so it is called a universal solvent.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one way we can save electricity at home: ____ A: Switch off lights and appliances when not in use. Turning off bulbs, TV and other appliances when not needed saves electricity.
chunks.source: Turning off bulbs, TV and other appliances when not needed saves electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of an annual crop: ____ A: Maize. Annual crops grow and are harvested within one year, e.g. maize, beans, groundnuts.
chunks.source: Annual crops grow and are harvested within one year, e.g. maize, beans, groundnuts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of energy is possessed by a leaf falling from a tree? ____ A: Kinetic energy. A moving (falling) leaf has kinetic energy, the energy of a moving object.
chunks.source: A moving (falling) leaf has kinetic energy, the energy of a moving object.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the substance that exists in the three states of matter: ____ A: Water. Water exists as ice (solid), liquid water, and steam (gas).
chunks.source: Water exists as ice (solid), liquid water, and steam (gas).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the standard units for measuring mass: ____ A: Kilograms (kg). Mass is measured in kilograms; small masses in grams.
chunks.source: Mass is measured in kilograms; small masses in grams.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why sugar dissolves in water: ____ A: Because sugar is soluble in water. Sugar dissolves because it is soluble and water is a good solvent.
chunks.source: Sugar dissolves because it is soluble and water is a good solvent.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one method of harvesting crops: ____ A: Hand picking. Crops are harvested by hand picking, uprooting, cutting or digging.
chunks.source: Crops are harvested by hand picking, uprooting, cutting or digging.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is salt added to food during cooking? ____ A: To add taste (flavour) to the food. Salt makes food tasty and also helps preserve it.
chunks.source: Salt makes food tasty and also helps preserve it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one sign of dehydration in babies: ____ A: Sunken eyes. A dehydrated baby has sunken eyes, a dry mouth, a sunken soft spot on the head, or passes little urine.
chunks.source: A dehydrated baby has sunken eyes, a dry mouth, a sunken soft spot on the head, or passes little urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one method of making alcohol: ____ A: Fermentation. Alcohol is made by fermentation (and concentrated by distillation).
chunks.source: Alcohol is made by fermentation (and concentrated by distillation).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do houseflies lay their eggs in decaying matter? ____ A: So that the larvae (maggots) find food when they hatch. Decaying matter is food for the young maggots that hatch from the eggs.
chunks.source: Decaying matter is food for the young maggots that hatch from the eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the blood cell that carries oxygen around the body: ____ A: Red blood cell. The red blood cell contains haemoglobin which carries oxygen to all body parts.
chunks.source: The red blood cell contains haemoglobin which carries oxygen to all body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one method of storing sound: ____ A: Recording (on tape, CD, phone or flash disk). Sound can be stored by recording it on tapes, CDs, phones or memory cards.
chunks.source: Sound can be stored by recording it on tapes, CDs, phones or memory cards.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from a drum, give any other example of a percussion musical instrument: ____ A: Xylophone. Percussion instruments are played by hitting or shaking, e.g. xylophone, jembe, bell, rattles.
chunks.source: Percussion instruments are played by hitting or shaking, e.g. xylophone, jembe, bell, rattles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one disease spread through poor sanitation: ____ A: Cholera. Poor sanitation spreads cholera, typhoid, dysentery and diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Poor sanitation spreads cholera, typhoid, dysentery and diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the mollusc in the diagram below: ____ A: Snail. The animal in the diagram with a coiled shell is a snail, which is a mollusc.
chunks.source: The animal in the diagram with a coiled shell is a snail, which is a mollusc.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a liquid that floats on water: ____ A: Oil (cooking oil). Oil, paraffin and petrol are less dense than water, so they float on it.
chunks.source: Oil, paraffin and petrol are less dense than water, so they float on it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we cook food before eating it? ____ A: To kill germs in the food. Cooking kills germs and also makes food soft and easy to digest.
chunks.source: Cooking kills germs and also makes food soft and easy to digest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write ORS in full: ____ A: Oral Rehydration Salts. ORS stands for Oral Rehydration Salts, given to replace water lost in diarrhoea.
chunks.source: ORS stands for Oral Rehydration Salts, given to replace water lost in diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does heat travel through solids? ____ A: By conduction. Heat moves through solids by conduction, e.g. along a metal spoon in hot tea.
chunks.source: Heat moves through solids by conduction, e.g. along a metal spoon in hot tea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one cause of road traffic accidents in Uganda: ____ A: Over speeding. Accidents are caused by over speeding, drunk driving, bad roads and careless driving.
chunks.source: Accidents are caused by over speeding, drunk driving, bad roads and careless driving.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one advantage of breast feeding to a woman: ____ A: It helps the mother's womb return to its normal size. Breast feeding helps the uterus contract back, delays another pregnancy and is free.
chunks.source: Breast feeding helps the uterus contract back, delays another pregnancy and is free.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of having too much wax in the ears: ____ A: It causes deafness (loss of hearing). Too much wax blocks the ear canal and can cause deafness or earache.
chunks.source: Too much wax blocks the ear canal and can cause deafness or earache.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of too much sunshine in the environment: ____ A: It causes drought (dries up water sources and crops). Too much sunshine causes drought, dries water sources and can damage the skin.
chunks.source: Too much sunshine causes drought, dries water sources and can damage the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of a vacuum flask at home: ____ A: It keeps hot drinks hot and cold drinks cold. A vacuum (thermos) flask keeps hot things hot and cold things cold for a long time.
chunks.source: A vacuum (thermos) flask keeps hot things hot and cold things cold for a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one good eating habit: ____ A: Washing hands before eating. Good eating habits include washing hands, chewing food well and eating a balanced diet.
chunks.source: Good eating habits include washing hands, chewing food well and eating a balanced diet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What name is given to such information written on a packet of drugs (as shown in the diagram)? ____ A: Prescription (dosage instructions). The instructions on a drug packet telling how the drug should be taken are called a prescription.
chunks.source: The instructions on a drug packet telling how the drug should be taken are called a prescription.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give any one reason why such information is important to patients: ____ A: It helps the patient take the correct dose (and avoid overdose). Dosage information helps patients take the right amount of drug at the right time.
chunks.source: Dosage information helps patients take the right amount of drug at the right time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How many times a day is the patient supposed to take the drug? ____ A: Three times a day. The packet is marked 2x3, meaning 2 tablets taken 3 times a day.
chunks.source: The packet is marked 2x3, meaning 2 tablets taken 3 times a day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) The patient took the drug in the morning; for how many hours should the patient wait before taking the drug again? ____ A: 8 hours. Three doses a day means one dose every 8 hours (24 divided by 3).
chunks.source: Three doses a day means one dose every 8 hours (24 divided by 3).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is immunity? ____ A: The ability of the body to resist (fight) diseases. Immunity is the body's power to fight disease-causing germs.
chunks.source: Immunity is the body's power to fight disease-causing germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Name the type of immunity acquired through recovery from illness: ____ A: Natural immunity. Immunity got after recovering from a disease is called natural immunity.
chunks.source: Immunity got after recovering from a disease is called natural immunity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Name the type of immunity acquired through immunization: ____ A: Artificial immunity. Immunity got through vaccines (immunization) is called artificial immunity.
chunks.source: Immunity got through vaccines (immunization) is called artificial immunity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give any one example of an immunisable disease: ____ A: Measles. Immunisable diseases include measles, polio, tuberculosis, tetanus and whooping cough.
chunks.source: Immunisable diseases include measles, polio, tuberculosis, tetanus and whooping cough.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What are chemical changes? ____ A: Changes in which a new substance is formed. In a chemical change a completely new substance is formed and the change cannot be reversed easily.
chunks.source: In a chemical change a completely new substance is formed and the change cannot be reversed easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give any one characteristic of chemical changes: ____ A: They are irreversible (a new substance is formed). Chemical changes cannot be reversed and may produce heat, light or gas.
chunks.source: Chemical changes cannot be reversed and may produce heat, light or gas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(i) Give one example of a chemical change: ____ A: Burning (combustion). Examples of chemical changes: burning, rusting, rotting, cooking food, digestion.
chunks.source: Examples of chemical changes: burning, rusting, rotting, cooking food, digestion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(ii) Give another example of a chemical change: ____ A: Rusting of iron. Other examples: rotting of fruits, souring of milk, baking.
chunks.source: Other examples: rotting of fruits, souring of milk, baking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) In the classification chart, which group of animals is indicated by letter X? ____ A: Warm-blooded vertebrates. X groups birds and mammals together, and both are warm-blooded vertebrates.
chunks.source: X groups birds and mammals together, and both are warm-blooded vertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) In the classification chart, which group of animals is indicated by letter Y? ____ A: Mammals. Y is grouped with birds under X (warm-blooded), so Y is mammals.
chunks.source: Y is grouped with birds under X (warm-blooded), so Y is mammals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give any one characteristic of the animal in group K: ____ A: It breathes through gills. K is fish (grouped with reptiles and amphibians as cold-blooded); fish live in water and breathe through gills.
chunks.source: K is fish (grouped with reptiles and amphibians as cold-blooded); fish live in water and breathe through gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Mention any one example of an amphibian: ____ A: Frog. Amphibians live partly in water and partly on land, e.g. frog, toad.
chunks.source: Amphibians live partly in water and partly on land, e.g. frog, toad.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) State one effect of heat gain on matter: ____ A: Matter expands (increases in size). When matter gains heat it expands, melts, evaporates or rises in temperature.
chunks.source: When matter gains heat it expands, melts, evaporates or rises in temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) State another effect of heat gain on matter: ____ A: Matter melts (solid changes to liquid). Heat gain can melt solids, boil liquids or expand gases.
chunks.source: Heat gain can melt solids, boil liquids or expand gases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one way in which people use heat: ____ A: For cooking food. People use heat for cooking, warming the house, drying clothes and ironing.
chunks.source: People use heat for cooking, warming the house, drying clothes and ironing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another way in which people use heat: ____ A: For warming the house. Heat is also used for drying harvested crops and warming bath water.
chunks.source: Heat is also used for drying harvested crops and warming bath water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Why is a cassava plant called a root tuber? ____ A: Because it stores food in its (swollen) roots. Cassava is a root tuber because its thick roots store food for the plant.
chunks.source: Cassava is a root tuber because its thick roots store food for the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Apart from cassava, give one other example of a root tuber: ____ A: Sweet potato. Root tubers include sweet potatoes and carrots.
chunks.source: Root tubers include sweet potatoes and carrots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another example of a root tuber: ____ A: Carrot. Carrots are also swollen roots that store food.
chunks.source: Carrots are also swollen roots that store food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give any one disease which affects cassava plants: ____ A: Cassava mosaic disease. Cassava is attacked by cassava mosaic disease (and cassava brown streak disease).
chunks.source: Cassava is attacked by cassava mosaic disease (and cassava brown streak disease).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Give the meaning of the term personal hygiene: ____ A: Keeping the body (and its surroundings) clean. Personal hygiene means keeping your body clean to stay healthy.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene means keeping your body clean to stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one way of promoting personal hygiene: ____ A: Bathing the body daily. Brushing teeth, washing hands, cutting nails short and bathing keep one clean.
chunks.source: Brushing teeth, washing hands, cutting nails short and bathing keep one clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another way of promoting personal hygiene: ____ A: Brushing the teeth (after meals). Wearing clean clothes and washing hands before eating also promote hygiene.
chunks.source: Wearing clean clothes and washing hands before eating also promote hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Name any one item used to promote good personal hygiene: ____ A: Soap. Items like soap, toothbrush, towel and nail cutters promote personal hygiene.
chunks.source: Items like soap, toothbrush, towel and nail cutters promote personal hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) In the diagram of the human ear, name the part marked M: ____ A: Eardrum (tympanic membrane). M points to the eardrum, the thin skin at the end of the ear canal that vibrates with sound.
chunks.source: M points to the eardrum, the thin skin at the end of the ear canal that vibrates with sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) In the diagram of the human ear, name the part marked P: ____ A: Cochlea. P points to the snail-shaped cochlea in the inner ear where sound messages start.
chunks.source: P points to the snail-shaped cochlea in the inner ear where sound messages start.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give the function of the part of the ear marked N: ____ A: It balances air pressure on both sides of the eardrum. N is the Eustachian tube; it keeps air pressure equal on both sides of the eardrum.
chunks.source: N is the Eustachian tube; it keeps air pressure equal on both sides of the eardrum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) The part of the ear responsible for balancing the body is the ____ A: Semicircular canals. The semicircular canals in the inner ear help the body to balance.
chunks.source: The semicircular canals in the inner ear help the body to balance.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Mention one characteristic of mammals: ____ A: They give birth to live young ones. Mammals give birth to live young, feed them on milk, have hair or fur, and are warm-blooded.
chunks.source: Mammals give birth to live young, feed them on milk, have hair or fur, and are warm-blooded.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Mention another characteristic of mammals: ____ A: They feed their young on milk (have mammary glands). Female mammals produce milk to feed their babies.
chunks.source: Female mammals produce milk to feed their babies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) State one example of a marine (sea) mammal: ____ A: Whale. Marine mammals live in the sea but breathe air, e.g. whale, dolphin, seal.
chunks.source: Marine mammals live in the sea but breathe air, e.g. whale, dolphin, seal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) State another example of a marine (sea) mammal: ____ A: Dolphin. Dolphins are intelligent sea mammals that breathe through a blowhole.
chunks.source: Dolphins are intelligent sea mammals that breathe through a blowhole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each term in Part A with its correct meaning in Part B. Part A: Volume, Pitch, Frequency, Echo. Part B: number of vibrations per second; reflected sound; loudness or softness of sound; highness or lowness of sound. A: Volume: loudness or softness of sound; Pitch: highness or lowness of sound; Frequency: number of vibrations per second; Echo: reflected sound. Volume means loudness or softness of sound; pitch means highness or lowness; frequency is the number of vibrations per second; echo is reflected sound.
chunks.source: Volume means loudness or softness of sound; pitch means highness or lowness; frequency is the number of vibrations per second; echo is reflected sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each garden tool (A-D) in the diagram with its correct use from the list. List: For collecting rubbish; For spraying crops; For turning manure; For transplanting seedlings; For cutting tree stumps; For cutting tree branches. A: Tool A: For spraying crops; Tool B: For cutting tree branches; Tool C: For collecting rubbish; Tool D: For transplanting seedlings. Tool A is a sprayer (spraying crops), B is a hand saw (cutting tree branches), C is a rake (collecting rubbish), D is a hand trowel (transplanting seedlings).
chunks.source: Tool A is a sprayer (spraying crops), B is a hand saw (cutting tree branches), C is a rake (collecting rubbish), D is a hand trowel (transplanting seedlings).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Write down one exotic breed of goat kept in Uganda: ____ A: Toggenburg. Exotic goat breeds kept in Uganda include Toggenburg, Saanen, Boer and Anglo-Nubian.
chunks.source: Exotic goat breeds kept in Uganda include Toggenburg, Saanen, Boer and Anglo-Nubian.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Write down another exotic breed of goat kept in Uganda: ____ A: Saanen. Saanen goats are white dairy goats.
chunks.source: Saanen goats are white dairy goats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) How long is the gestation period of a nanny (female goat)? ____ A: 5 months (about 150 days). A nanny goat carries its pregnancy for about 5 months.
chunks.source: A nanny goat carries its pregnancy for about 5 months.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give any one way of caring for a pregnant goat: ____ A: Feed it well (with nutritious feeds). A pregnant goat should be well fed, kept in a clean dry house and handled gently.
chunks.source: A pregnant goat should be well fed, kept in a clean dry house and handled gently.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the component of air used for: (i) respiration: ____ A: Oxygen. Oxygen in air is used for respiration (breathing).
chunks.source: Oxygen in air is used for respiration (breathing).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the component of air used for: (ii) putting out fire: ____ A: Carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it is used to put out fire.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it is used to put out fire.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) State one danger of wind to people: ____ A: It spreads diseases. Strong wind destroys crops and houses, spreads diseases and causes accidents.
chunks.source: Strong wind destroys crops and houses, spreads diseases and causes accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) State another danger of wind to people: ____ A: It destroys (blows off) houses and crops. Strong winds blow off roofs and break trees.
chunks.source: Strong winds blow off roofs and break trees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) An irregular stone on a string was lowered into container A with water; displaced water was collected in container B. Name container A: ____ A: Overflow can (displacement can / Eureka can). Container A is the overflow (displacement) can; the displaced water flows into container B, the measuring cylinder.
chunks.source: Container A is the overflow (displacement) can; the displaced water flows into container B, the measuring cylinder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name container B: ____ A: Measuring cylinder. Container B collects and measures the displaced water.
chunks.source: Container B collects and measures the displaced water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) What is the volume of the irregular object? ____ A: 10 cc (10 cm3). The volume of the object equals the volume of displaced water, which reads 10 cc in container B.
chunks.source: The volume of the object equals the volume of displaced water, which reads 10 cc in container B.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Calculate the density of the irregular object if its mass is 60 g: ____ A: 6 g/cm3. Density = mass / volume = 60 g / 10 cc = 6 g/cm3.
chunks.source: Density = mass / volume = 60 g / 10 cc = 6 g/cm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Name one poisonous substance found in tobacco: ____ A: Nicotine. Tobacco contains nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide, which are poisonous.
chunks.source: Tobacco contains nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide, which are poisonous.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name another poisonous substance found in tobacco: ____ A: Tar. Tar from tobacco smoke coats the lungs and can cause cancer.
chunks.source: Tar from tobacco smoke coats the lungs and can cause cancer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) State one effect of cigarette smoking by pregnant women on their unborn babies: ____ A: Low birth weight (premature birth). Smoking in pregnancy can cause miscarriage, premature birth and low birth weight babies.
chunks.source: Smoking in pregnancy can cause miscarriage, premature birth and low birth weight babies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) State another effect of cigarette smoking by pregnant women on their unborn babies: ____ A: Miscarriage (loss of the pregnancy). The poisons in smoke reach the unborn baby through the mother's blood.
chunks.source: The poisons in smoke reach the unborn baby through the mother's blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the reflected sound? ____ A: Echo. Sound that bounces back off a surface is called an echo.
chunks.source: Sound that bounces back off a surface is called an echo.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one characteristic of living things: ____ A: They breathe (respire). Living things breathe, feed, grow, reproduce, move and respond to changes.
chunks.source: Living things breathe, feed, grow, reproduce, move and respond to changes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of canine tooth to carnivorous animals: ____ A: For tearing flesh (meat). Carnivores use their sharp pointed canines to tear meat.
chunks.source: Carnivores use their sharp pointed canines to tear meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the best food for babies below six months: ____ A: Breast milk. Babies below six months should feed on breast milk only.
chunks.source: Babies below six months should feed on breast milk only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which vaccine is immunized to infants against tuberculosis? ____ A: BCG. BCG vaccine protects infants against tuberculosis (TB).
chunks.source: BCG vaccine protects infants against tuberculosis (TB).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the item used to promote sanitation drawn below: ____ A: Toothbrush. The drawn item is a toothbrush, used for cleaning teeth.
chunks.source: The drawn item is a toothbrush, used for cleaning teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the above item used by people to promote personal hygiene? ____ A: For brushing (cleaning) the teeth. A toothbrush is used to brush teeth and keep the mouth clean.
chunks.source: A toothbrush is used to brush teeth and keep the mouth clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the habitat of earth worms: ____ A: Soil. Earthworms live in the soil.
chunks.source: Earthworms live in the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which invertebrate lives in the human alimentary canal? ____ A: Tapeworm. Tapeworms (and roundworms) are invertebrates that live in the human gut.
chunks.source: Tapeworms (and roundworms) are invertebrates that live in the human gut.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a snake move from one place to another? ____ A: By crawling (slithering). A snake wriggles (slithers) its long body to crawl.
chunks.source: A snake wriggles (slithers) its long body to crawl.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are teeth important during digestion of food? ____ A: They break (cut and chew) food into small pieces. Teeth cut, tear and grind food into small pieces for easy swallowing and digestion.
chunks.source: Teeth cut, tear and grind food into small pieces for easy swallowing and digestion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one example of an intestinal worm in human beings: ____ A: Roundworm. Intestinal worms include roundworms, tapeworms and hookworms.
chunks.source: Intestinal worms include roundworms, tapeworms and hookworms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why can't a feather sink in water? ____ A: Because it is light (less dense than water). A feather is very light and traps air, so it floats on water.
chunks.source: A feather is very light and traps air, so it floats on water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one vulnerable group of people in your community: ____ A: Babies (infants). Vulnerable groups include babies, pregnant women, the elderly and the sick.
chunks.source: Vulnerable groups include babies, pregnant women, the elderly and the sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one device used to store sound: ____ A: Tape recorder. Sound can be stored on tape recorders, CDs, phones, radios and flash disks.
chunks.source: Sound can be stored on tape recorders, CDs, phones, radios and flash disks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the transport system of the human body: ____ A: Circulatory (blood) system. The circulatory system transports blood, food, oxygen and waste around the body.
chunks.source: The circulatory system transports blood, food, oxygen and waste around the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The soft feather covering a chick's body is called a ____ feather A: Down. Down feathers are soft and fluffy and keep the chick warm.
chunks.source: Down feathers are soft and fluffy and keep the chick warm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of ventilation on a living house for people: ____ A: It allows fresh air into the house (and removes bad air). Ventilation brings in fresh air and takes out warm stale air and smoke.
chunks.source: Ventilation brings in fresh air and takes out warm stale air and smoke.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one natural source of sound in the environment: ____ A: Thunder. Natural sources of sound include thunder, flowing water, wind and animals.
chunks.source: Natural sources of sound include thunder, flowing water, wind and animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the function of the blood cell drawn in the diagram below: ____ A: It carries oxygen around the body. The drawn disc-shaped cell is a red blood cell, which carries oxygen to all body parts. (Vector-drawn diagram; no usable image file.)
chunks.source: The drawn disc-shaped cell is a red blood cell, which carries oxygen to all body parts. (Vector-drawn diagram; no usable image file.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What food value is got from eating legumes? ____ A: Proteins. Legumes such as beans, peas and groundnuts give the body proteins for growth.
chunks.source: Legumes such as beans, peas and groundnuts give the body proteins for growth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the type of soil with the highest capillarity: ____ A: Clay soil. Clay soil has the smallest particles, so water rises highest in it by capillarity.
chunks.source: Clay soil has the smallest particles, so water rises highest in it by capillarity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one solute used in the making of ORS: ____ A: Sugar. ORS is made by dissolving sugar and salt in clean boiled water.
chunks.source: ORS is made by dissolving sugar and salt in clean boiled water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one weather instrument: ____ A: Thermometer. Weather instruments include the thermometer, rain gauge, wind vane and barometer.
chunks.source: Weather instruments include the thermometer, rain gauge, wind vane and barometer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the instrument used to detect body temperature: ____ A: Thermometer (clinical thermometer). A clinical thermometer measures body temperature.
chunks.source: A clinical thermometer measures body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is sound energy produced? ____ A: By vibrations of objects. Sound is produced when objects vibrate.
chunks.source: Sound is produced when objects vibrate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of an amphibian: ____ A: Frog. Amphibians include frogs and toads.
chunks.source: Amphibians include frogs and toads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which body organ filters blood? ____ A: Kidney. The kidneys filter waste materials out of the blood to make urine.
chunks.source: The kidneys filter waste materials out of the blood to make urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of feathers to birds: ____ A: For flying. Feathers help birds to fly and also keep them warm.
chunks.source: Feathers help birds to fly and also keep them warm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one bird with the foot in the diagram: ____ A: Duck. The webbed foot in the diagram belongs to swimming birds such as a duck or goose.
chunks.source: The webbed foot in the diagram belongs to swimming birds such as a duck or goose.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name part marked B on the foot in the diagram: ____ A: Web (webbing between the toes). B points to the skin (web) joining the toes, which helps the bird swim.
chunks.source: B points to the skin (web) joining the toes, which helps the bird swim.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one characteristic of insects: ____ A: They have six legs. Insects have six legs, three body parts and a pair of antennae.
chunks.source: Insects have six legs, three body parts and a pair of antennae.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one common disease at home: ____ A: Malaria. Common home diseases include malaria, flu, cough and diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Common home diseases include malaria, flu, cough and diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one sign of soil erosion in an area: ____ A: Gullies (channels) in the soil. Signs of erosion include gullies, exposed plant roots and bare stony land.
chunks.source: Signs of erosion include gullies, exposed plant roots and bare stony land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one reproductive cell in flowering plants: ____ A: Pollen grain. The male reproductive cell is the pollen grain; the female one is the ovule (ovum).
chunks.source: The male reproductive cell is the pollen grain; the female one is the ovule (ovum).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a cell? ____ A: The smallest (basic) unit of a living thing. A cell is the smallest building block of all living things.
chunks.source: A cell is the smallest building block of all living things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do people drink alcohol? ____ A: For pleasure (to enjoy themselves). People drink alcohol for leisure, to socialize or to feel happy.
chunks.source: People drink alcohol for leisure, to socialize or to feel happy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which body organ balances the body in its right posture? ____ A: The ear (semicircular canals). The semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.
chunks.source: The semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the difference between mass and weight: ____ A: Mass is the amount of matter in an object (constant); weight is the pull of gravity on the object (changes). Mass is measured in kilograms and never changes; weight is measured in newtons and changes with gravity.
chunks.source: Mass is measured in kilograms and never changes; weight is measured in newtons and changes with gravity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one crop growing practice: ____ A: Weeding. Crop growing practices include planting, weeding, mulching, spraying and harvesting.
chunks.source: Crop growing practices include planting, weeding, mulching, spraying and harvesting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Give one characteristic of mammals: ____ A: They give birth to live young ones. Mammals give birth to live young, suckle them, have hair and are warm-blooded.
chunks.source: Mammals give birth to live young, suckle them, have hair and are warm-blooded.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give another characteristic of mammals: ____ A: They have hair (fur) on their bodies. All mammals have some hair or fur on their bodies.
chunks.source: All mammals have some hair or fur on their bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one difference between mammals and birds: ____ A: Mammals give birth to live young ones while birds lay eggs. Mammals have hair and give birth; birds have feathers and lay eggs.
chunks.source: Mammals have hair and give birth; birds have feathers and lay eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another difference between mammals and birds: ____ A: Mammals have hair (fur) while birds have feathers. Mammals feed young on milk from mammary glands; birds feed young on regurgitated food.
chunks.source: Mammals feed young on milk from mammary glands; birds feed young on regurgitated food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) In the diagrams about states of matter, name the state of matter marked B: ____ A: Liquid. B shows particles fairly close but not tightly packed, which is the liquid state.
chunks.source: B shows particles fairly close but not tightly packed, which is the liquid state.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name the state of matter marked C: ____ A: Gas (gaseous state). C shows particles far apart and scattered, which is the gaseous state.
chunks.source: C shows particles far apart and scattered, which is the gaseous state.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Which substance makes up the state of matter B above? ____ A: Water. Likely answer: the liquid shown is water, the commonest liquid used in such diagrams.
chunks.source: Likely answer: the liquid shown is water, the commonest liquid used in such diagrams.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How does heat travel through the state of matter marked C? ____ A: By convection. Heat travels through gases (and liquids) by convection currents.
chunks.source: Heat travels through gases (and liquids) by convection currents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Name one type of bird found in our environment: ____ A: Hen (chicken). Common birds include hens, ducks, doves, pigeons and eagles.
chunks.source: Common birds include hens, ducks, doves, pigeons and eagles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name another type of bird found in our environment: ____ A: Duck. Ducks are water birds with webbed feet.
chunks.source: Ducks are water birds with webbed feet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Why are birds grouped as warm blooded? ____ A: Because their body temperature remains constant (does not change with the environment). Birds keep a constant body temperature whatever the weather.
chunks.source: Birds keep a constant body temperature whatever the weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Apart from birds, name the other group of warm blooded vertebrates: ____ A: Mammals. The two warm-blooded vertebrate groups are birds and mammals.
chunks.source: The two warm-blooded vertebrate groups are birds and mammals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Who is a casualty? ____ A: A person injured (hurt) in an accident. A casualty is someone who has been hurt in an accident and needs first aid.
chunks.source: A casualty is someone who has been hurt in an accident and needs first aid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one reason for giving first aid to casualties: ____ A: To save life. First aid saves life, reduces pain and prevents the injury from getting worse.
chunks.source: First aid saves life, reduces pain and prevents the injury from getting worse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another reason for giving first aid to casualties: ____ A: To reduce pain. First aid also stops bleeding and prevents further harm.
chunks.source: First aid also stops bleeding and prevents further harm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Name the first aid material drawn below: ____ A: Gloves (protective gloves). The drawn material is a pair of gloves worn to protect the first aider from germs.
chunks.source: The drawn material is a pair of gloves worn to protect the first aider from germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) A stone of mass 60 g was immersed in water and displaced 20 cc of water. What does the displaced water represent? ____ A: The volume of the stone. The volume of displaced water equals the volume of the immersed object.
chunks.source: The volume of displaced water equals the volume of the immersed object.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Why did the stone sink in water in the measuring cylinder? ____ A: Because it is denser than water. Objects denser than water sink in it.
chunks.source: Objects denser than water sink in it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) Calculate the density of the stone: ____ A: 3 g/cm3. Density = mass / volume = 60 g / 20 cc = 3 g/cm3.
chunks.source: Density = mass / volume = 60 g / 20 cc = 3 g/cm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Give one example of an annual crop: ____ A: Maize. Annual crops mature within one year, e.g. maize, beans, groundnuts, sorghum.
chunks.source: Annual crops mature within one year, e.g. maize, beans, groundnuts, sorghum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give another example of an annual crop: ____ A: Beans. Beans are legumes harvested within months of planting.
chunks.source: Beans are legumes harvested within months of planting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one example of a perennial crop: ____ A: Coffee. Perennial crops live for many years, e.g. coffee, bananas, tea, sugarcane.
chunks.source: Perennial crops live for many years, e.g. coffee, bananas, tea, sugarcane.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another example of a perennial crop: ____ A: Bananas. Banana plants keep producing bunches for many years.
chunks.source: Banana plants keep producing bunches for many years.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What are vertebrates? ____ A: Animals with a backbone (spine). Vertebrates are animals that have a backbone.
chunks.source: Vertebrates are animals that have a backbone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Name one example of a vertebrate: ____ A: Cow. Examples: cow, goat, fish, bird, frog, snake, human being.
chunks.source: Examples: cow, goat, fish, bird, frog, snake, human being.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Name another example of a vertebrate: ____ A: Fish. Fish have backbones too.
chunks.source: Fish have backbones too.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give any one characteristic of vertebrates: ____ A: They have a backbone. All vertebrates possess a backbone (vertebral column).
chunks.source: All vertebrates possess a backbone (vertebral column).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Name the root system marked P: ____ A: Fibrous root system. P shows many thin roots of almost equal size spreading from the stem base: a fibrous root system.
chunks.source: P shows many thin roots of almost equal size spreading from the stem base: a fibrous root system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name the root system marked Q: ____ A: Taproot system. Q shows one main root with side roots and nodules: a taproot system.
chunks.source: Q shows one main root with side roots and nodules: a taproot system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one example of a plant with the root system marked P: ____ A: Maize. Fibrous roots are found in maize, sorghum, millet, rice and grasses.
chunks.source: Fibrous roots are found in maize, sorghum, millet, rice and grasses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give one example of a plant with the root system marked Q: ____ A: Beans. Taproots are found in beans, groundnuts and other legumes.
chunks.source: Taproots are found in beans, groundnuts and other legumes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the group of vertebrates where human beings belong: ____ A: Mammals. Human beings are mammals.
chunks.source: Human beings are mammals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Apart from human beings, name one other vertebrate in the group named in (a): ____ A: Cow. Other mammals: cow, goat, dog, cat, bat, whale.
chunks.source: Other mammals: cow, goat, dog, cat, bat, whale.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Name another vertebrate in the same group: ____ A: Goat. Goats are mammals kept for milk and meat.
chunks.source: Goats are mammals kept for milk and meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Name the example of a flying mammal: ____ A: Bat. The bat is the only mammal that can truly fly.
chunks.source: The bat is the only mammal that can truly fly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Give one use of the human ear to the body: ____ A: For hearing (sound). The ear is used for hearing and for balancing the body.
chunks.source: The ear is used for hearing and for balancing the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give another use of the human ear to the body: ____ A: For balancing the body. The semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.
chunks.source: The semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) In the diagram of the mammalian ear, name part labeled X: ____ A: Pinna (outer ear). X points to the pinna, the outer flap that collects sound waves.
chunks.source: X points to the pinna, the outer flap that collects sound waves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Name part labeled Y: ____ A: Eardrum (tympanic membrane). Y points to the eardrum at the end of the ear canal.
chunks.source: Y points to the eardrum at the end of the ear canal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Give one type of weather: ____ A: Sunny. Types of weather: sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy.
chunks.source: Types of weather: sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give another type of weather: ____ A: Rainy. Rain falls from dark clouds.
chunks.source: Rain falls from dark clouds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Name the weather condition that favours winnowing of cereals: ____ A: Windy. Wind blows away the light chaff, leaving the heavy grains.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light chaff, leaving the heavy grains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How is a rain gauge useful to a crop farmer? ____ A: It measures the amount of rainfall. A rain gauge tells the farmer how much rain has fallen, helping plan planting.
chunks.source: A rain gauge tells the farmer how much rain has fallen, helping plan planting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) How does sound move? ____ A: In the form of waves (through a medium). Sound travels as waves through air, water or solids.
chunks.source: Sound travels as waves through air, water or solids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Why can't sound travel through a vacuum? ____ A: Because there is no matter (particles) to vibrate. Sound needs particles to vibrate through; a vacuum has none.
chunks.source: Sound needs particles to vibrate through; a vacuum has none.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) In which state of matter does sound travel fastest? ____ A: Solid. Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids, slowest in gases.
chunks.source: Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids, slowest in gases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Give one reason why farmers rear chicken: ____ A: For eggs. Farmers keep chicken for eggs, meat and income.
chunks.source: Farmers keep chicken for eggs, meat and income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give another reason why farmers rear chicken: ____ A: For meat. Chicken meat is a source of protein and income.
chunks.source: Chicken meat is a source of protein and income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Mention one type of chicken reared by farmers: ____ A: Layers. Layers are kept for eggs; broilers for meat.
chunks.source: Layers are kept for eggs; broilers for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Mention another type of chicken reared by farmers: ____ A: Broilers. Broilers grow fast and are kept for meat.
chunks.source: Broilers grow fast and are kept for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Mention one pest which attacks crops in the garden: ____ A: Weevils. Crop pests include weevils, stalk borers, aphids, cutworms and termites.
chunks.source: Crop pests include weevils, stalk borers, aphids, cutworms and termites.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Mention another pest which attacks crops in the garden: ____ A: Stalk borers. Stalk borers tunnel into cereal stems.
chunks.source: Stalk borers tunnel into cereal stems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give any one way in which pests are dangerous to crops: ____ A: They eat (destroy) the crops. Pests eat crops and reduce harvests.
chunks.source: Pests eat crops and reduce harvests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How can a farmer control pests in the garden? ____ A: By spraying with pesticides. Pests are controlled by spraying pesticides, crop rotation and weeding.
chunks.source: Pests are controlled by spraying pesticides, crop rotation and weeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Moses observed a mango fruit with his five senses. Fill in the missing body structure: Fruity smell is observed by sense of smell using (i) ____ A: Nose. We smell with the nose.
chunks.source: We smell with the nose.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Red colour is observed by sense of sight using (ii) ____ A: Eyes. We see with the eyes.
chunks.source: We see with the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sound made when the mango drops is observed by sense of hearing using (iii) ____ A: Ears. We hear with the ears.
chunks.source: We hear with the ears.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sweet taste is observed by sense of taste using (iv) ____ A: Tongue. We taste with the tongue.
chunks.source: We taste with the tongue.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one vector which is involved in the 4Fs disease path: ____ A: Housefly. The housefly carries germs through the 4Fs: faeces, fingers, flies and food.
chunks.source: The housefly carries germs through the 4Fs: faeces, fingers, flies and food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are farmers encouraged to clean the habitats of their domestic animals? ____ A: To kill (remove) parasites and germs that cause diseases. Clean habitats keep animals free from parasites and diseases.
chunks.source: Clean habitats keep animals free from parasites and diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are blood vessels important in the body? ____ A: They transport (carry) blood around the body. Blood vessels carry oxygen, food and waste in the blood to all body parts.
chunks.source: Blood vessels carry oxygen, food and waste in the blood to all body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way of controlling tape worm infestation in humans: ____ A: Deworming regularly. Tapeworms are controlled by deworming, cooking meat properly and using latrines.
chunks.source: Tapeworms are controlled by deworming, cooking meat properly and using latrines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a non-renewable resource: ____ A: Petroleum (crude oil). Non-renewable resources cannot be replaced once used up, e.g. petroleum, coal, minerals.
chunks.source: Non-renewable resources cannot be replaced once used up, e.g. petroleum, coal, minerals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the garden tool shown in the diagram: ____ A: Hand fork (garden fork). The small forked tool in the diagram is a hand fork, used for light digging and weeding.
chunks.source: The small forked tool in the diagram is a hand fork, used for light digging and weeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of caring for garden tools: ____ A: Clean them after use. Garden tools are cared for by cleaning, oiling metal parts, sharpening and keeping them dry.
chunks.source: Garden tools are cared for by cleaning, oiling metal parts, sharpening and keeping them dry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of energy is possessed by a bat in flight? ____ A: Kinetic energy. A flying bat is moving, so it has kinetic energy.
chunks.source: A flying bat is moving, so it has kinetic energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one animal fibre: ____ A: Wool. Animal fibres include wool (from sheep), silk and mohair.
chunks.source: Animal fibres include wool (from sheep), silk and mohair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one economic importance of rearing bees to people: ____ A: People get honey to eat and sell. Bees give honey and beeswax, which bring income.
chunks.source: Bees give honey and beeswax, which bring income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a rabbit grouped under mammals? ____ A: Because it gives birth to live young ones. Rabbits give birth, suckle their young and have hair, so they are mammals.
chunks.source: Rabbits give birth, suckle their young and have hair, so they are mammals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from sugar, name any other substance used to make Oral Rehydration Solution: ____ A: Salt. ORS is made of sugar and salt dissolved in clean boiled water.
chunks.source: ORS is made of sugar and salt dissolved in clean boiled water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one farming practice used by crop farmers to maintain soil fertility: ____ A: Crop rotation. Crop rotation, mulching, manuring and bush fallowing keep soil fertile.
chunks.source: Crop rotation, mulching, manuring and bush fallowing keep soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of food eaten by the bird with the beak shown in the diagram: ____ A: Nectar. The long curved beak is for sucking nectar from flowers.
chunks.source: The long curved beak is for sucking nectar from flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the above bird adapted to its mode of feeding? ____ A: It has a long curved beak for sucking nectar from flowers. The bird's long thin curved beak reaches deep into flowers to suck nectar.
chunks.source: The bird's long thin curved beak reaches deep into flowers to suck nectar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way in which a latrine is useful in a home: ____ A: For proper disposal of faeces. Latrines keep faeces away from people, preventing diseases like cholera.
chunks.source: Latrines keep faeces away from people, preventing diseases like cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the component of blood which is destroyed by HIV: ____ A: White blood cells. HIV attacks and destroys white blood cells, weakening the body's defence.
chunks.source: HIV attacks and destroys white blood cells, weakening the body's defence.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one factor which favours the breeding of bacteria: ____ A: Warmth. Bacteria breed fast where there is warmth, moisture and food.
chunks.source: Bacteria breed fast where there is warmth, moisture and food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can people in the community control the spread of water borne diseases? ____ A: By boiling drinking water. Boiling water, proper sanitation and protecting wells control water-borne diseases.
chunks.source: Boiling water, proper sanitation and protecting wells control water-borne diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one difference between a mosquito and a spider: ____ A: A mosquito is an insect (has six legs) while a spider is an arachnid (has eight legs). Mosquitoes have six legs, three body parts and wings; spiders have eight legs, two body parts and no wings.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes have six legs, three body parts and wings; spiders have eight legs, two body parts and no wings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where does gaseous exchange take place in the human body? ____ A: In the lungs (air sacs). Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged in the tiny air sacs of the lungs.
chunks.source: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged in the tiny air sacs of the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we call the number of vibrations produced by an object per second? ____ A: Frequency. Frequency is the number of vibrations per second, measured in hertz.
chunks.source: Frequency is the number of vibrations per second, measured in hertz.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the importance of ventilators on a house? ____ A: They allow fresh air into the house. Ventilators let in fresh air and let out warm stale air and smoke.
chunks.source: Ventilators let in fresh air and let out warm stale air and smoke.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a root tuber: ____ A: Cassava. Root tubers include cassava, sweet potatoes and carrots.
chunks.source: Root tubers include cassava, sweet potatoes and carrots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can poultry farmers control cannibalism on their farms? ____ A: By debeaking the birds. Debeaking, proper feeding and avoiding overcrowding stop birds pecking each other.
chunks.source: Debeaking, proper feeding and avoiding overcrowding stop birds pecking each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which weather instrument is used to measure the speed of wind? ____ A: Anemometer. An anemometer has spinning cups that measure how fast wind blows.
chunks.source: An anemometer has spinning cups that measure how fast wind blows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one danger of drought in the environment: ____ A: Crops dry up (famine). Drought kills crops and animals and causes famine and lack of water.
chunks.source: Drought kills crops and animals and causes famine and lack of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the larva of a housefly useful to people? ____ A: Maggots are used as feed for chicken and fish. Housefly larvae (maggots) are rich in protein and feed poultry and fish.
chunks.source: Housefly larvae (maggots) are rich in protein and feed poultry and fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one sanitary activity that children can do to keep the school compound clean: ____ A: Sweeping the compound. Children can sweep, slash grass and pick rubbish to keep the school clean.
chunks.source: Children can sweep, slash grass and pick rubbish to keep the school clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name part marked with letter K on the bean seed: ____ A: Cotyledon. K points to the cotyledon, the food store of the bean seed.
chunks.source: K points to the cotyledon, the food store of the bean seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is part marked Y useful to the seed during germination? ____ A: It allows water to enter the seed. Y is the micropyle, the tiny hole through which water enters the germinating seed.
chunks.source: Y is the micropyle, the tiny hole through which water enters the germinating seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one factor one should consider when selecting a site for a house: ____ A: Well-drained land. A house site should be well-drained, near water, secure and away from swamps.
chunks.source: A house site should be well-drained, near water, secure and away from swamps.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one physical process that helps in rain formation: ____ A: Evaporation. Evaporation lifts water into the sky and condensation forms the clouds that give rain.
chunks.source: Evaporation lifts water into the sky and condensation forms the clouds that give rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way are termites dangerous to crop farmers? ____ A: They eat (destroy) crops. Termites eat crops, wooden buildings and stored harvests.
chunks.source: Termites eat crops, wooden buildings and stored harvests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of the human ear helps the body to balance? ____ A: Semicircular canals. The three semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.
chunks.source: The three semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one reason why loam soil is good in crop growing: ____ A: It is fertile (rich in humus). Loam is fertile, holds water well and still drains and lets air in.
chunks.source: Loam is fertile, holds water well and still drains and lets air in.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which element of weather is needed for the preservation of harvested seeds and grains? ____ A: Sunshine (sun heat). Sunshine dries harvested seeds and grains so they can be stored without rotting.
chunks.source: Sunshine dries harvested seeds and grains so they can be stored without rotting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is blood carried by the pulmonary vein different from that carried by the pulmonary artery? ____ A: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood while the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood. The pulmonary vein brings oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the heart; the pulmonary artery takes oxygen-poor blood to the lungs.
chunks.source: The pulmonary vein brings oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the heart; the pulmonary artery takes oxygen-poor blood to the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one common accident at home: ____ A: Burns. Common home accidents: burns, scalds, cuts, falls, poisoning.
chunks.source: Common home accidents: burns, scalds, cuts, falls, poisoning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is water not recommended in putting out petrol fire? ____ A: Because petrol floats on water and the fire spreads. Petrol is lighter than water, so water only spreads the burning petrol.
chunks.source: Petrol is lighter than water, so water only spreads the burning petrol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Apart from amphibians, state two other groups of cold-blooded vertebrates: ____ A: Reptiles and fish. Cold-blooded vertebrates are fish, amphibians and reptiles.
chunks.source: Cold-blooded vertebrates are fish, amphibians and reptiles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give any one example of an amphibian: ____ A: Toad. Amphibians include frogs and toads.
chunks.source: Amphibians include frogs and toads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How do amphibians reproduce? ____ A: By laying eggs (in water). Amphibians lay eggs in water, which hatch into tadpoles.
chunks.source: Amphibians lay eggs in water, which hatch into tadpoles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) In one sentence, explain the term pollination: ____ A: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower. Pollination is how pollen moves from the male part to the female part of a flower.
chunks.source: Pollination is how pollen moves from the male part to the female part of a flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Mention one type of pollination: ____ A: Self pollination. The two types are self pollination and cross pollination.
chunks.source: The two types are self pollination and cross pollination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Mention another type of pollination: ____ A: Cross pollination. In cross pollination, pollen moves from one flower to another.
chunks.source: In cross pollination, pollen moves from one flower to another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Name any one agent of pollination: ____ A: Bees (insects). Agents of pollination: insects, wind, water, birds and animals.
chunks.source: Agents of pollination: insects, wind, water, birds and animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) State the importance of a safety pin when giving First Aid: ____ A: For fastening bandages. A safety pin holds bandages firmly in place.
chunks.source: A safety pin holds bandages firmly in place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) State the importance of cotton wool when giving First Aid: ____ A: For cleaning wounds. Cotton wool is used to clean wounds and apply medicine.
chunks.source: Cotton wool is used to clean wounds and apply medicine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give any one importance of giving First Aid to an accident victim: ____ A: To save life. First aid saves life and stops injuries from getting worse.
chunks.source: First aid saves life and stops injuries from getting worse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Mention one factor considered when giving First Aid: ____ A: The safety of the first aider and the casualty. Consider safety first, then how serious the injury is.
chunks.source: Consider safety first, then how serious the injury is.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the blood cell drawn below: ____ A: Red blood cell. The round disc-shaped cell drawn is a red blood cell.
chunks.source: The round disc-shaped cell drawn is a red blood cell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) How is the blood cell shown in the diagram above useful to the body? ____ A: It carries oxygen to all body parts. Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to every part of the body.
chunks.source: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to every part of the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) Mention two diseases which attack the red blood cell: ____ A: Malaria and sickle cell anaemia. Malaria parasites and sickle cell disease attack red blood cells.
chunks.source: Malaria parasites and sickle cell disease attack red blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
