chunks.text: Q: (a) What is food preservation? ____ A: Keeping food from going bad (for future use). Food preservation stops food from rotting so it can be used later.
chunks.source: Food preservation stops food from rotting so it can be used later.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Mention one way of preserving meat: ____ A: Salting. Meat is preserved by salting, smoking, drying or freezing.
chunks.source: Meat is preserved by salting, smoking, drying or freezing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Mention another way of preserving meat: ____ A: Smoking. Smoke dries meat and keeps germs away.
chunks.source: Smoke dries meat and keeps germs away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Why are people encouraged to preserve their food? ____ A: To avoid wastage (and have food in times of scarcity). Preserved food lasts longer and is available when fresh food is scarce.
chunks.source: Preserved food lasts longer and is available when fresh food is scarce.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) In the diagram of a fish, name part marked B: ____ A: Tail fin (caudal fin). B points to the tail fin, which pushes the fish forward in water.
chunks.source: B points to the tail fin, which pushes the fish forward in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name part marked C: ____ A: Gills. C points to the gills, which the fish uses for breathing in water.
chunks.source: C points to the gills, which the fish uses for breathing in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Which part does a fish use to protect itself from enemies? ____ A: Scales. The hard overlapping scales cover and protect the fish's body.
chunks.source: The hard overlapping scales cover and protect the fish's body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give any one use of fish to people: ____ A: Fish is eaten as food (source of protein). People eat fish, sell it for income and use its bones for feed.
chunks.source: People eat fish, sell it for income and use its bones for feed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Write one duty of a worker bee in a hive: ____ A: Collecting nectar (and pollen). Worker bees collect nectar and pollen, make honey, clean the hive and guard it.
chunks.source: Worker bees collect nectar and pollen, make honey, clean the hive and guard it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Write another duty of a worker bee in a hive: ____ A: Making honey. Workers also feed the queen and the young bees.
chunks.source: Workers also feed the queen and the young bees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Apart from worker bees, name any other type of bee in the hive: ____ A: Queen bee. A hive has the queen, workers and drones.
chunks.source: A hive has the queen, workers and drones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) How can apiarists prevent their bees from swarming? ____ A: By providing enough space in the hive (and removing queen cells). Bees swarm when crowded; more space and regular harvesting prevent it.
chunks.source: Bees swarm when crowded; more space and regular harvesting prevent it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) How is cassava harvested? ____ A: By uprooting. Cassava tubers are pulled out of the soil by uprooting the plant.
chunks.source: Cassava tubers are pulled out of the soil by uprooting the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) How is coffee harvested? ____ A: By hand picking. Ripe coffee berries are picked by hand.
chunks.source: Ripe coffee berries are picked by hand.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Mention one way of controlling crop pests in a garden: ____ A: Spraying with pesticides. Pests are controlled by spraying, crop rotation, weeding and hand picking.
chunks.source: Pests are controlled by spraying, crop rotation, weeding and hand picking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Mention another way of controlling crop pests in a garden: ____ A: Crop rotation. Changing crops each season breaks the life cycle of pests.
chunks.source: Changing crops each season breaks the life cycle of pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Give the meaning of the term drug abuse: ____ A: Using drugs wrongly (in a harmful way). Drug abuse is the wrong use of drugs, e.g. taking overdose or drugs for pleasure.
chunks.source: Drug abuse is the wrong use of drugs, e.g. taking overdose or drugs for pleasure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give the meaning of the term drug misuse: ____ A: Using a drug for the wrong purpose (not following instructions). Drug misuse is using medicine wrongly, e.g. wrong dose or wrong illness.
chunks.source: Drug misuse is using medicine wrongly, e.g. wrong dose or wrong illness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) State any one effect of drug dependence to an individual: ____ A: Poor health (mental illness). Drug dependence ruins health, causes madness, poverty and school dropout.
chunks.source: Drug dependence ruins health, causes madness, poverty and school dropout.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) How can you help your friend who smokes to stop the habit? ____ A: Advise (encourage) him to stop smoking. Counsel the friend, keep him busy and away from smokers.
chunks.source: Counsel the friend, keep him busy and away from smokers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Give the meaning of the word immunity: ____ A: The ability of the body to resist (fight) diseases. Immunity is the body's power to fight germs.
chunks.source: Immunity is the body's power to fight germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one way in which a child can acquire immunity: ____ A: Through immunization (vaccination). Children get immunity through vaccination, recovery from illness, or from the mother.
chunks.source: Children get immunity through vaccination, recovery from illness, or from the mother.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another way in which a child can acquire immunity: ____ A: Through recovery from an illness. After recovering from a disease, the body remembers how to fight it.
chunks.source: After recovering from a disease, the body remembers how to fight it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (e) Give any one way in which a person's body immunity can be increased: ____ A: By eating a balanced diet. Good feeding, immunization and exercise strengthen immunity.
chunks.source: Good feeding, immunization and exercise strengthen immunity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) In the diagram of the human digestive system, name part marked P: ____ A: Oesophagus (gullet). P is the tube carrying food from the mouth to the stomach: the oesophagus.
chunks.source: P is the tube carrying food from the mouth to the stomach: the oesophagus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name part marked Q: ____ A: Stomach. Q is the bag-like stomach where food is churned and mixed with juices.
chunks.source: Q is the bag-like stomach where food is churned and mixed with juices.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give the digestive juice produced by part marked S: ____ A: Bile. S is the liver, which produces bile juice.
chunks.source: S is the liver, which produces bile juice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How can you maintain the proper working of the system shown in the diagram? ____ A: By eating a balanced diet. Eat balanced meals, drink clean water, deworm regularly and avoid alcohol.
chunks.source: Eat balanced meals, drink clean water, deworm regularly and avoid alcohol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Write one method of making alcohol: ____ A: Fermentation. Alcohol is made by fermentation of sugary juices (note: the booklet prints "meaning" but means "making").
chunks.source: Alcohol is made by fermentation of sugary juices (note: the booklet prints "meaning" but means "making").

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) State one reason why some people drink alcohol: ____ A: For pleasure. Some drink for leisure, to socialize or to forget problems.
chunks.source: Some drink for leisure, to socialize or to forget problems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) State another reason why some people drink alcohol: ____ A: To socialize with friends. Others drink to feel brave or to cope with stress.
chunks.source: Others drink to feel brave or to cope with stress.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Mention one medical instrument which uses alcohol to function: ____ A: Clinical thermometer. Some clinical thermometers use alcohol instead of mercury.
chunks.source: Some clinical thermometers use alcohol instead of mercury.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Name one percussion musical instrument: ____ A: Drum. Percussion instruments are hit or shaken: drum, xylophone, bell.
chunks.source: Percussion instruments are hit or shaken: drum, xylophone, bell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name one string musical instrument: ____ A: Guitar. String instruments have strings that are plucked or bowed: guitar, harp, violin.
chunks.source: String instruments have strings that are plucked or bowed: guitar, harp, violin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Mention any one method of storing sound: ____ A: Recording. Sound is stored by recording on tapes, CDs or phones.
chunks.source: Sound is stored by recording on tapes, CDs or phones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give any one factor which affects the pitch of sound: ____ A: The length of the vibrating object. Pitch is affected by the length, thickness and tightness of the vibrating object.
chunks.source: Pitch is affected by the length, thickness and tightness of the vibrating object.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Give one example of an exotic breed of cattle: ____ A: Friesian. Exotic cattle breeds: Friesian, Jersey, Guernsey, Ayrshire.
chunks.source: Exotic cattle breeds: Friesian, Jersey, Guernsey, Ayrshire.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give another example of an exotic breed of cattle: ____ A: Jersey. Jersey cows give milk rich in butterfat.
chunks.source: Jersey cows give milk rich in butterfat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) How are draught cattle useful to farmers? ____ A: For ploughing (and pulling carts). Draught cattle pull ploughs and carts on the farm.
chunks.source: Draught cattle pull ploughs and carts on the farm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) State one way of controlling internal parasites in cattle: ____ A: Deworming (drenching). Internal parasites (worms) are controlled by regular deworming.
chunks.source: Internal parasites (worms) are controlled by regular deworming.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Which term is used to describe the loss of water and mineral salts from the body? ____ A: Dehydration. Losing too much water and salts from the body is called dehydration.
chunks.source: Losing too much water and salts from the body is called dehydration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Mention one sign of dehydration: ____ A: Sunken eyes. Signs: sunken eyes, dry mouth, great thirst, passing little urine.
chunks.source: Signs: sunken eyes, dry mouth, great thirst, passing little urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Mention another sign of dehydration: ____ A: Dry mouth (great thirst). The patient feels very thirsty and the tongue is dry.
chunks.source: The patient feels very thirsty and the tongue is dry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) What advice is given to a friend who is dehydrated? ____ A: Drink ORS (plenty of fluids). A dehydrated person should drink oral rehydration salts and plenty of fluids.
chunks.source: A dehydrated person should drink oral rehydration salts and plenty of fluids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one item used for sweeping: ____ A: Broom. A broom is used for sweeping floors and compounds.
chunks.source: A broom is used for sweeping floors and compounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one member of a nuclear family: ____ A: Father. A nuclear family is made of father, mother and their children.
chunks.source: A nuclear family is made of father, mother and their children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from use of chemicals, give any other way of controlling pests in a garden: ____ A: Crop rotation. Pests can also be controlled by crop rotation, weeding, hand picking and proper spacing.
chunks.source: Pests can also be controlled by crop rotation, weeding, hand picking and proper spacing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part of the flower which attracts pollinators is the ____ A: Petals. The bright colourful petals attract insects and other pollinators to the flower.
chunks.source: The bright colourful petals attract insects and other pollinators to the flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of transpiration to plants: ____ A: It cools the plant. Transpiration cools the plant and pulls water and minerals up from the roots.
chunks.source: Transpiration cools the plant and pulls water and minerals up from the roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How important is nitrogen to legumes? ____ A: It is used to make proteins (for growth). Nitrogen is needed to form proteins that build the plant body.
chunks.source: Nitrogen is needed to form proteins that build the plant body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the eggs, mention any other dormant stage in the life cycle of a butterfly: ____ A: Pupa. The dormant (resting) stages are the egg and the pupa.
chunks.source: The dormant (resting) stages are the egg and the pupa.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are the standard units for measuring mass? ____ A: Kilograms (kg). Mass is measured in kilograms.
chunks.source: Mass is measured in kilograms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of keeping the body clean: ____ A: Bathing daily. Bathing, brushing teeth and washing hands keep the body clean.
chunks.source: Bathing, brushing teeth and washing hands keep the body clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do mulches help to control the growth of weeds in a garden? ____ A: They cover weeds and block sunlight from reaching them. A thick layer of mulch buries weeds and stops sunlight, so weeds cannot grow.
chunks.source: A thick layer of mulch buries weeds and stops sunlight, so weeds cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of an annual crop: ____ A: Maize. Annual crops mature in one year: maize, beans, groundnuts.
chunks.source: Annual crops mature in one year: maize, beans, groundnuts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the use of the garden tool shown above (a sickle) to farmers: ____ A: For cutting grass (and harvesting crops). A sickle is used for cutting grass and harvesting crops like rice and millet.
chunks.source: A sickle is used for cutting grass and harvesting crops like rice and millet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one exotic breed of goats that provides people with mohair: ____ A: Angora. Angora goats produce mohair, a soft silky fibre.
chunks.source: Angora goats produce mohair, a soft silky fibre.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way an apiarist can control the swarming of bees: ____ A: By removing queen cells (providing enough space). Swarming is controlled by giving bees more space, removing extra queen cells and harvesting regularly.
chunks.source: Swarming is controlled by giving bees more space, removing extra queen cells and harvesting regularly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from killing germs, how else is hydrochloric acid important in the stomach? ____ A: It provides good conditions for digestive enzymes to work. Hydrochloric acid makes the stomach acidic so enzymes can digest food well.
chunks.source: Hydrochloric acid makes the stomach acidic so enzymes can digest food well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why can't a spider be trapped by its own cobweb? ____ A: Because its legs are oily (the web does not stick to them). Likely answer: the spider's legs have an oily coating so the sticky web cannot trap them.
chunks.source: Likely answer: the spider's legs have an oily coating so the sticky web cannot trap them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way AIDS can be spread from one person to another: ____ A: Through unprotected sexual intercourse. AIDS spreads through unprotected sex, sharing sharp instruments and infected blood.
chunks.source: AIDS spreads through unprotected sex, sharing sharp instruments and infected blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one play material made from banana fibres: ____ A: Dolls. Banana fibres are woven into dolls, balls and ropes for play.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are woven into dolls, balls and ropes for play.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write P.H.C in full: ____ A: Primary Health Care. PHC stands for Primary Health Care.
chunks.source: PHC stands for Primary Health Care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention the type of root system shown in the diagram above: ____ A: Taproot system. The diagram shows one main root with side roots: a taproot system.
chunks.source: The diagram shows one main root with side roots: a taproot system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the heart of a bird different from that of a reptile? ____ A: A bird's heart has four (completely divided) chambers while a reptile's heart has three (partly divided) chambers. Birds have four-chambered hearts; most reptiles have three-chambered hearts.
chunks.source: Birds have four-chambered hearts; most reptiles have three-chambered hearts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of plastics in the environment: ____ A: They pollute the environment (block drainage). Plastics litter the land, block water channels and kill animals that swallow them.
chunks.source: Plastics litter the land, block water channels and kill animals that swallow them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one danger of plants: ____ A: Some plants are poisonous. Some plants are poisonous, have thorns or harbour dangerous animals.
chunks.source: Some plants are poisonous, have thorns or harbour dangerous animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does it mean to classify animals? ____ A: Grouping animals with similar characteristics together. Classification means putting animals with the same features in one group.
chunks.source: Classification means putting animals with the same features in one group.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one sign of a compound fracture: ____ A: The broken bone sticks out through the skin. In a compound fracture the broken bone pierces the skin and there is bleeding.
chunks.source: In a compound fracture the broken bone pierces the skin and there is bleeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of change is the boiling of an egg? ____ A: Chemical change. Boiling an egg forms a new substance and cannot be reversed: a chemical change.
chunks.source: Boiling an egg forms a new substance and cannot be reversed: a chemical change.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does a plant die when salty water has been poured on its roots? ____ A: Because salt draws water out of the plant (the roots cannot absorb water). Salt makes water move out of the roots by osmosis, so the plant dries and dies.
chunks.source: Salt makes water move out of the roots by osmosis, so the plant dries and dies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention the source of papyrus used in making mats: ____ A: Swamps (wetlands). Papyrus reeds grow in swamps and are used for mats and crafts.
chunks.source: Papyrus reeds grow in swamps and are used for mats and crafts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do birds keep their feathers clean and smooth? ____ A: By preening (using their beaks). Birds preen, arranging their feathers with the beak and oiling them.
chunks.source: Birds preen, arranging their feathers with the beak and oiling them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of the sun to the environment: ____ A: It gives light and heat. The sun gives light and warmth and helps green plants make food.
chunks.source: The sun gives light and warmth and helps green plants make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention the food value obtained from eating honey: ____ A: Carbohydrates. Honey is rich in carbohydrates, which give the body energy.
chunks.source: Honey is rich in carbohydrates, which give the body energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which season do farmers irrigate their crops? ____ A: Dry season. Crops are watered (irrigated) in the dry season when there is no rain.
chunks.source: Crops are watered (irrigated) in the dry season when there is no rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What germ causes haemophilus influenza b? ____ A: Bacteria. Haemophilus influenzae is a bacterium.
chunks.source: Haemophilus influenzae is a bacterium.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does keeping fish in a pond help to control malaria in a home? ____ A: Fish eat mosquito larvae. Fish feed on the mosquito larvae (wigglers) in water, stopping mosquitoes from breeding.
chunks.source: Fish feed on the mosquito larvae (wigglers) in water, stopping mosquitoes from breeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the two containers (A and B) has more heat? ____ A: Container B. Container B holds more hot water, so it contains more heat energy.
chunks.source: Container B holds more hot water, so it contains more heat energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason for your answer in question 35 above (which container has more heat): ____ A: Because it contains more (a greater quantity of) hot water. More hot water means more heat energy stored.
chunks.source: More hot water means more heat energy stored.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one importance of rain to crops: ____ A: It provides water for crops to grow. Rain gives crops the water they need to grow well.
chunks.source: Rain gives crops the water they need to grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one group of people considered to be vulnerable: ____ A: Babies. Vulnerable groups: babies, pregnant women, the elderly, the sick.
chunks.source: Vulnerable groups: babies, pregnant women, the elderly, the sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which property of air enables a person to suck soda with a straw? ____ A: Air pressure (air exerts pressure). Air pressure pushes the soda up the straw when air is sucked out.
chunks.source: Air pressure pushes the soda up the straw when air is sucked out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is culling different from vaccination? ____ A: Culling is killing (removing) sick animals while vaccination is giving medicine to prevent disease. Culling removes diseased animals by killing them; vaccination protects healthy ones with a vaccine.
chunks.source: Culling removes diseased animals by killing them; vaccination protects healthy ones with a vaccine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name any one communicable disease caused by a fungus: ____ A: Ringworm. Fungal communicable diseases include ringworm and athlete's foot.
chunks.source: Fungal communicable diseases include ringworm and athlete's foot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) State the body organ affected by the disease mentioned in (a) above: ____ A: Skin. Ringworm attacks the skin.
chunks.source: Ringworm attacks the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(i) Give one way of preventing the spread of ringworm: ____ A: Avoid sharing clothes and towels. Prevent ringworm by keeping skin clean and dry and not sharing personal items.
chunks.source: Prevent ringworm by keeping skin clean and dry and not sharing personal items.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(ii) Give another way of preventing the spread of ringworm: ____ A: Keep the skin clean and dry. Wash the body well and keep the skin dry.
chunks.source: Wash the body well and keep the skin dry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is seed dormancy? ____ A: The state in which a seed cannot germinate (resting stage). Seed dormancy is when a seed stays alive but cannot sprout even in good conditions.
chunks.source: Seed dormancy is when a seed stays alive but cannot sprout even in good conditions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one factor that may cause seed dormancy: ____ A: Hard seed coat. A very hard seed coat or an immature embryo can cause dormancy.
chunks.source: A very hard seed coat or an immature embryo can cause dormancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another factor that may cause seed dormancy: ____ A: Immature embryo. If the young plant inside is not fully grown, the seed stays dormant.
chunks.source: If the young plant inside is not fully grown, the seed stays dormant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) How important is water during seed germination? ____ A: It softens the seed coat (and activates enzymes). Water softens the testa and starts the chemical processes of germination.
chunks.source: Water softens the testa and starts the chemical processes of germination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Select from the table the correct function of each organ. Table - Organ | Function (wrong order): Liver | Balances the level of water in the body; Kidney | Stores iron; Heart | Excretes carbon dioxide; Lungs | Pumps blood in the body. A: Liver: Stores iron; Kidney: Balances the level of water in the body; Heart: Pumps blood in the body; Lungs: Excretes carbon dioxide. Liver stores iron; kidney balances body water; heart pumps blood; lungs excrete carbon dioxide.
chunks.source: Liver stores iron; kidney balances body water; heart pumps blood; lungs excrete carbon dioxide.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) In the diagram of an insect, name part marked X: ____ A: Antenna (antennae). X points to the antenna, the insect's feeler on its head.
chunks.source: X points to the antenna, the insect's feeler on its head.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) State the function of part Z to an insect: ____ A: It is used for breathing (has spiracles). Likely answer: Z is the abdomen, which carries the breathing holes (spiracles).
chunks.source: Likely answer: Z is the abdomen, which carries the breathing holes (spiracles).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Which part of an insect balances it when flying? ____ A: Wings. Likely answer: the wings keep the insect steady and balanced in flight.
chunks.source: Likely answer: the wings keep the insect steady and balanced in flight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) Give any one characteristic of insects: ____ A: They have six legs. Insects have six legs, three body parts and one pair of antennae.
chunks.source: Insects have six legs, three body parts and one pair of antennae.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Apart from cassava and beet roots, give one other example of a root tuber: ____ A: Sweet potato. Root tubers: sweet potatoes, carrots.
chunks.source: Root tubers: sweet potatoes, carrots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give another example of a root tuber: ____ A: Carrot. Carrots store food in their swollen roots.
chunks.source: Carrots store food in their swollen roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Mention any one viral disease of cassava: ____ A: Cassava mosaic disease. Cassava mosaic is a virus disease spread by whiteflies.
chunks.source: Cassava mosaic is a virus disease spread by whiteflies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give any one way cassava is harvested: ____ A: By uprooting. Cassava is harvested by pulling (uprooting) the plant from the soil.
chunks.source: Cassava is harvested by pulling (uprooting) the plant from the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) In the diagrams of teeth, name the type of tooth marked S: ____ A: Molar. S is broad and flat with a wide crown: a molar.
chunks.source: S is broad and flat with a wide crown: a molar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name the type of tooth marked T: ____ A: Canine. T is sharp and pointed: a canine.
chunks.source: T is sharp and pointed: a canine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) State the function of the tooth marked S: ____ A: For grinding (crushing) food. Molars grind and crush food into small pieces.
chunks.source: Molars grind and crush food into small pieces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) State the function of the tooth marked T: ____ A: For tearing food. Canines are sharp and pointed for tearing meat.
chunks.source: Canines are sharp and pointed for tearing meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What causes ear canker? ____ A: Mites (ear mites). Likely answer: ear canker in rabbits is caused by tiny mites (parasites) in the ear.
chunks.source: Likely answer: ear canker in rabbits is caused by tiny mites (parasites) in the ear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Apart from ear canker, mention one other disease of rabbits: ____ A: Coccidiosis. Likely answer: other rabbit diseases include coccidiosis and snuffles (pneumonia).
chunks.source: Likely answer: other rabbit diseases include coccidiosis and snuffles (pneumonia).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Mention another disease of rabbits: ____ A: Snuffles (pneumonia). Likely answer: snuffles is a respiratory disease of rabbits.
chunks.source: Likely answer: snuffles is a respiratory disease of rabbits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Name any one exotic breed of rabbits kept in Uganda: ____ A: New Zealand White. Likely answer: exotic rabbit breeds include New Zealand White and Californian.
chunks.source: Likely answer: exotic rabbit breeds include New Zealand White and Californian.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What do we call the act of suckling milk from the breasts? ____ A: Breast feeding. Suckling milk from the mother's breasts is called breast feeding.
chunks.source: Suckling milk from the mother's breasts is called breast feeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) State one advantage of a baby suckling milk from its mother's breasts: ____ A: The baby gets all the nutrients it needs. Breast milk has all nutrients, protects against diseases and is free.
chunks.source: Breast milk has all nutrients, protects against diseases and is free.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) State another advantage of a baby suckling milk from its mother's breasts: ____ A: It protects the baby against diseases. Breast milk gives the baby immunity against infections.
chunks.source: Breast milk gives the baby immunity against infections.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give any one disadvantage of a baby suckling milk from its mother's breasts: ____ A: An infected mother can pass diseases (e.g. HIV) to the baby. If the mother is sick, e.g. with HIV, the baby may catch it through breast milk.
chunks.source: If the mother is sick, e.g. with HIV, the baby may catch it through breast milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is photosynthesis? ____ A: The process by which green plants make food. Photosynthesis is how green plants use sunlight to make their own food.
chunks.source: Photosynthesis is how green plants use sunlight to make their own food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Mention one raw material needed by plants during photosynthesis: ____ A: Carbon dioxide. Plants need carbon dioxide and water to make food in sunlight.
chunks.source: Plants need carbon dioxide and water to make food in sunlight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Mention another raw material needed by plants during photosynthesis: ____ A: Water. Roots absorb the water used in photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Roots absorb the water used in photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give any one way in which plants use starch made during photosynthesis: ____ A: For growth (as food / stored for energy). Plants use starch for growth and store the rest as food.
chunks.source: Plants use starch for growth and store the rest as food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) In the diagram of a thermos flask, name part labeled B: ____ A: Outer case (metal/plastic cover). Likely answer: B points to the outer protective case of the flask.
chunks.source: Likely answer: B points to the outer protective case of the flask.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name part labeled D: ____ A: Base (insulating pad). Likely answer: D points to the base on which the flask stands.
chunks.source: Likely answer: D points to the base on which the flask stands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: (b) Mention any one material from which part C is made: ____ A: Glass. C is the double-walled glass bottle with a vacuum between the walls.
chunks.source: C is the double-walled glass bottle with a vacuum between the walls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Why is part A made out of an insulator? ____ A: To prevent heat loss (or gain) by conduction. A is the cork/stopper; being an insulator it stops heat escaping through the mouth.
chunks.source: A is the cork/stopper; being an insulator it stops heat escaping through the mouth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Give one way vectors spread germs that cause diseases: ____ A: Through bites. Vectors spread germs by biting people or by contaminating food.
chunks.source: Vectors spread germs by biting people or by contaminating food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give another way vectors spread germs that cause diseases: ____ A: By contaminating food. Houseflies carry germs on their bodies onto our food.
chunks.source: Houseflies carry germs on their bodies onto our food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Mention one disease whose germs are spread by vectors: ____ A: Malaria. Vector-spread diseases: malaria, cholera, typhoid, sleeping sickness.
chunks.source: Vector-spread diseases: malaria, cholera, typhoid, sleeping sickness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Mention another disease whose germs are spread by vectors: ____ A: Cholera. Houseflies spread cholera germs onto food.
chunks.source: Houseflies spread cholera germs onto food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention four classes of vertebrates: ____ A: Fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds (and mammals - any four). Vertebrates are grouped into fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.
chunks.source: Vertebrates are grouped into fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Give one way soil loses its fertility: ____ A: Soil erosion. Soil loses fertility through erosion, leaching, over-cultivation and bush burning.
chunks.source: Soil loses fertility through erosion, leaching, over-cultivation and bush burning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give another way soil loses its fertility: ____ A: Leaching. Heavy rain washes nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach.
chunks.source: Heavy rain washes nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Mention one way of preventing soil from losing its fertility: ____ A: Mulching. Mulching, crop rotation, terracing and manuring protect soil fertility.
chunks.source: Mulching, crop rotation, terracing and manuring protect soil fertility.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Mention another way of preventing soil from losing its fertility: ____ A: Crop rotation. Planting different crops each season keeps the soil rich.
chunks.source: Planting different crops each season keeps the soil rich.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name any one place where bacteria are found: ____ A: In the soil. Bacteria are found in soil, air, water and decaying matter.
chunks.source: Bacteria are found in soil, air, water and decaying matter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one way in which bacteria are useful in the environment: ____ A: They decompose dead matter. Bacteria rot dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.
chunks.source: Bacteria rot dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another way in which bacteria are useful in the environment: ____ A: They fix nitrogen in the soil (help make yoghurt). Some bacteria fix nitrogen for plants; others are used to make yoghurt.
chunks.source: Some bacteria fix nitrogen for plants; others are used to make yoghurt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) What name is given to the substances that kill/prevent the growth of bacteria? ____ A: Antibiotics. Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria or stop them growing.
chunks.source: Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria or stop them growing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the steps of separating a mixture of sand and salt in the correct order. Steps: Stir until all the salt dissolves; Boil the salt solution to dryness; Put the mixture in a container and add water; Filter the mixture. A: Put the mixture in a container and add water., Stir until all the salt dissolves, Filter the mixture., Boil the salt solution to dryness. First add water to dissolve the salt, stir, filter out the sand, then boil the filtrate to get the salt back.
chunks.source: First add water to dissolve the salt, stir, filter out the sand, then boil the filtrate to get the salt back.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one play material made from banana fibres: ____ A: Dolls. Banana fibres are woven into dolls, balls and ropes for children to play with.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are woven into dolls, balls and ropes for children to play with.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one effect of alcoholism to a community: ____ A: Poverty. Alcoholism brings poverty, violence, accidents and broken families to a community.
chunks.source: Alcoholism brings poverty, violence, accidents and broken families to a community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are babies grouped under vulnerable groups of people? ____ A: Because they cannot care for (protect) themselves. Babies are helpless and their bodies are weak against diseases, so they need special care.
chunks.source: Babies are helpless and their bodies are weak against diseases, so they need special care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of a tool used at home, name part marked B: ____ A: Mortar. B points to the bowl (mortar); A is the pestle used for pounding inside it.
chunks.source: B points to the bowl (mortar); A is the pestle used for pounding inside it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State what would happen if a clinical thermometer is sterilized by boiling: ____ A: It would break (the glass would crack). Boiling makes the mercury expand suddenly and crack the thin glass tube.
chunks.source: Boiling makes the mercury expand suddenly and crack the thin glass tube.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are foliage leaves useful to an onion? ____ A: They make food for the plant (photosynthesis). The green leaves of an onion trap sunlight to make food.
chunks.source: The green leaves of an onion trap sunlight to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one way you would reduce egg eating on a poultry farm: ____ A: Debeak the birds. Debeaking, collecting eggs often and feeding the birds well reduce egg eating.
chunks.source: Debeaking, collecting eggs often and feeding the birds well reduce egg eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of silting to aquatic animals: ____ A: It kills them (covers their breeding places). Silt covers breeding grounds and removes oxygen, killing fish and other water animals.
chunks.source: Silt covers breeding grounds and removes oxygen, killing fish and other water animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following shows that air has weight? A: An inflated balloon weighs more than a deflated one. Air has weight: a balloon full of air is heavier than an empty one.
chunks.source: Air has weight: a balloon full of air is heavier than an empty one.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it a good practice to wear shoes especially when walking outside the house? ____ A: To protect the feet from injuries (and jiggers). Shoes protect feet from cuts, thorns, jiggers and hookworms.
chunks.source: Shoes protect feet from cuts, thorns, jiggers and hookworms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which disease of the eyes is spread by a housefly? ____ A: Trachoma. Houseflies spread trachoma, a disease that damages the eyes.
chunks.source: Houseflies spread trachoma, a disease that damages the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one characteristic of physical changes: ____ A: They are reversible (no new substance is formed). In physical changes no new substance is formed and the change can be reversed.
chunks.source: In physical changes no new substance is formed and the change can be reversed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does over-grazing affect the soil? ____ A: It exposes the soil to erosion. Over-grazing removes plant cover, leaving bare soil that wind and water wash away.
chunks.source: Over-grazing removes plant cover, leaving bare soil that wind and water wash away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which water borne disease affects the liver resulting to liver cancer? ____ A: Bilharzia (schistosomiasis). Bilharzia worms damage the liver and can lead to liver cancer.
chunks.source: Bilharzia worms damage the liver and can lead to liver cancer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the liquid marked Y in the diagram (a boy put water and oil in a container): ____ A: Water. Oil floats on water; Y marks the lower layer, which is water. (The extracted image file P614141315img.jpg is blank/unusable, so no image is attached.)
chunks.source: Oil floats on water; Y marks the lower layer, which is water. (The extracted image file P614141315img.jpg is blank/unusable, so no image is attached.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is millet and sorghum propagated? ____ A: By planting seeds. Millet and sorghum are grown by sowing their seeds.
chunks.source: Millet and sorghum are grown by sowing their seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one difference between a toad and a frog: ____ A: A toad has dry rough skin while a frog has smooth moist skin. Toads have warty dry skin and walk; frogs have smooth wet skin and jump.
chunks.source: Toads have warty dry skin and walk; frogs have smooth wet skin and jump.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one factor you would consider before selecting a site for house: ____ A: Well-drained land. Choose land that is well-drained, near clean water, secure and not in a swamp.
chunks.source: Choose land that is well-drained, near clean water, secure and not in a swamp.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are children in a family protected against any deficiency disease? ____ A: By feeding them a balanced diet. A balanced diet gives all food values and prevents deficiency diseases.
chunks.source: A balanced diet gives all food values and prevents deficiency diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one function of the human kidney: ____ A: It filters waste materials from the blood (forms urine). The kidneys clean the blood by removing waste as urine.
chunks.source: The kidneys clean the blood by removing waste as urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the garden tool drawn in the diagram below: ____ A: Garden fork (digging fork). The long-handled forked tool is a garden (digging) fork.
chunks.source: The long-handled forked tool is a garden (digging) fork.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one use of the above garden tool to a farmer: ____ A: For digging (loosening) the soil. A garden fork digs and loosens soil and turns manure.
chunks.source: A garden fork digs and loosens soil and turns manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write PIASCY in full: ____ A: Presidential Initiative on AIDS Strategy for Communication to Youth. PIASCY is Uganda's Presidential Initiative on AIDS Strategy for Communication to Youth.
chunks.source: PIASCY is Uganda's Presidential Initiative on AIDS Strategy for Communication to Youth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one characteristic of essential drugs: ____ A: They are affordable (cheap). Essential drugs are affordable, available, safe and effective.
chunks.source: Essential drugs are affordable, available, safe and effective.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way babies acquire natural immunity: ____ A: Through breast milk (from the mother). Babies get natural immunity from the mother through breast milk (and during birth).
chunks.source: Babies get natural immunity from the mother through breast milk (and during birth).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one danger of sharing your handkerchief with another person: ____ A: It spreads diseases (e.g. flu, cough). Sharing handkerchiefs spreads cough, flu and other germs.
chunks.source: Sharing handkerchiefs spreads cough, flu and other germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are schools encouraged to have a school garden? ____ A: To teach pupils farming skills (and get food). School gardens teach farming, provide food and income for the school.
chunks.source: School gardens teach farming, provide food and income for the school.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does malaria affect the circulatory system? ____ A: It destroys red blood cells (causing anaemia). Malaria parasites attack red blood cells, reducing blood and causing anaemia.
chunks.source: Malaria parasites attack red blood cells, reducing blood and causing anaemia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of pollination illustrated below: ____ A: Self pollination. The arrows show pollen moving within the same flower: self pollination.
chunks.source: The arrows show pollen moving within the same flower: self pollination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a stem tuber: ____ A: Irish potato. Stem tubers include Irish potatoes and yams.
chunks.source: Stem tubers include Irish potatoes and yams.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a crustacean: ____ A: Crab. Crustaceans have hard shells: crab, lobster, prawn.
chunks.source: Crustaceans have hard shells: crab, lobster, prawn.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a crop farmer reduce overcrowding of plants in a garden? ____ A: By thinning (proper spacing). Thinning removes extra seedlings so the rest get enough space, light and nutrients.
chunks.source: Thinning removes extra seedlings so the rest get enough space, light and nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of energy is possessed by water at 100C? ____ A: Heat energy. Boiling water at 100C contains a lot of heat energy.
chunks.source: Boiling water at 100C contains a lot of heat energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: How does the cork on a vacuum flask help to prevent heat gain or loss? ____ A: It is a poor conductor (insulator) of heat. The cork does not conduct heat, so heat cannot escape or enter through the mouth.
chunks.source: The cork does not conduct heat, so heat cannot escape or enter through the mouth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the legume store above: ____ A: Granary. The raised grass-thatched store in the diagram is a granary for keeping grains and legumes.
chunks.source: The raised grass-thatched store in the diagram is a granary for keeping grains and legumes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: As a farmer, how would you protect your metallic tools from getting rusty? ____ A: By oiling them (keeping them dry). Oil, paint or grease keeps water and air away from metal so it does not rust.
chunks.source: Oil, paint or grease keeps water and air away from metal so it does not rust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one message that may be said to children during a health parade: ____ A: Wash your hands before eating. Health parade messages: wash hands, brush teeth, cut nails, keep clean.
chunks.source: Health parade messages: wash hands, brush teeth, cut nails, keep clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How has the government of Uganda helped in the control of tuberculosis? ____ A: By immunizing children with BCG (and giving free treatment). The government gives free BCG immunization and free TB treatment.
chunks.source: The government gives free BCG immunization and free TB treatment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which group of musical instruments does the instrument drawn below belong? ____ A: String (musical) instruments. The drawn instrument has a string stretched over a bridge: a string instrument.
chunks.source: The drawn instrument has a string stretched over a bridge: a string instrument.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the use of natural fertilizers friendly to the environment? ____ A: They do not pollute the environment (they rot and improve the soil). Natural fertilizers like manure rot into the soil without poisoning water or killing useful organisms.
chunks.source: Natural fertilizers like manure rot into the soil without poisoning water or killing useful organisms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) A farmer recorded how many times his goat and rabbit ate each food. What was the most favourable food for the rabbit? ____ A: Sweet potatoes (eaten 4 times). The rabbit ate sweet potatoes 4 times, more than any other food.
chunks.source: The rabbit ate sweet potatoes 4 times, more than any other food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) What was the most favourable food for the goat? ____ A: Sweet potatoes, grass and maize leaves (3 times each - a tie). The goat ate sweet potatoes, grass and maize leaves 3 times each: a three-way tie.
chunks.source: The goat ate sweet potatoes, grass and maize leaves 3 times each: a three-way tie.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) What was the least favourable food for the rabbit? ____ A: Sorghum leaves (eaten 0 times). The rabbit never ate sorghum leaves.
chunks.source: The rabbit never ate sorghum leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) If the farmer was to use only one type of food, which one would be most favourable for both the goat and the rabbit? ____ A: Sweet potatoes (7 times in total). Sweet potatoes: 4 (rabbit) + 3 (goat) = 7, the highest combined total.
chunks.source: Sweet potatoes: 4 (rabbit) + 3 (goat) = 7, the highest combined total.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Apart from carbon dioxide, name one other part (component) of air: ____ A: Oxygen. Air is made of nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, water vapour and dust.
chunks.source: Air is made of nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, water vapour and dust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name another part (component) of air: ____ A: Nitrogen. Nitrogen makes up the largest part of air.
chunks.source: Nitrogen makes up the largest part of air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give one use of carbon dioxide to people: ____ A: For putting out fire. Carbon dioxide puts out fires, is used by plants to make food, and makes drinks fizzy.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide puts out fires, is used by plants to make food, and makes drinks fizzy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give another use of carbon dioxide to people: ____ A: In photosynthesis (by plants). Plants need carbon dioxide to make food.
chunks.source: Plants need carbon dioxide to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) A P.6 class boiled well water and did the experiment shown. Identify the method used to clean the water: ____ A: Filtration. Pouring water through filter paper to remove dirt is called filtration.
chunks.source: Pouring water through filter paper to remove dirt is called filtration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) What scientific name is given to the substance labeled T? ____ A: Residue. T is the dirt trapped on the filter paper: the residue.
chunks.source: T is the dirt trapped on the filter paper: the residue.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) What scientific name is given to the substance labeled K? ____ A: Filtrate. K is the clean liquid collected below: the filtrate.
chunks.source: K is the clean liquid collected below: the filtrate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Why would you encourage a thirsty P.6 child to drink the water labeled K? ____ A: Because it is clean (filtered and boiled) and safe to drink. K was boiled and filtered, so it is free from dirt and germs.
chunks.source: K was boiled and filtered, so it is free from dirt and germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Give the element of P.H.C responsible for controlling of over population: ____ A: Family planning. Family planning is the PHC element that controls overpopulation.
chunks.source: Family planning is the PHC element that controls overpopulation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give the element of P.H.C responsible for controlling of bad body odour: ____ A: Personal hygiene. Personal hygiene keeps the body clean and free from bad smell.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene keeps the body clean and free from bad smell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(iii) Give the element of P.H.C responsible for controlling killer diseases among children: ____ A: Immunization. Immunization protects children against the killer diseases.
chunks.source: Immunization protects children against the killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Write one activity you can do to promote PHC in school: ____ A: Health parade (general cleaning). Health parades, cleaning the compound and health talks promote PHC.
chunks.source: Health parades, cleaning the compound and health talks promote PHC.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What kind of food is eaten by the bird in the diagram? ____ A: Flesh (meat). The hooked beak is for tearing flesh: the bird eats meat.
chunks.source: The hooked beak is for tearing flesh: the bird eats meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) To which group of birds does it belong? ____ A: Birds of prey. Eagles, hawks and kites with hooked beaks are birds of prey.
chunks.source: Eagles, hawks and kites with hooked beaks are birds of prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Name any one bird that has a beak like the one drawn above: ____ A: Eagle. Eagles, hawks and kites have strong hooked beaks.
chunks.source: Eagles, hawks and kites have strong hooked beaks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) State any one danger of the bird you have named in (c) above to people: ____ A: It eats (steals) people's chicken. Birds of prey snatch chickens and chicks from homes.
chunks.source: Birds of prey snatch chickens and chicks from homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Which first aid is administered by applying cold water on the affected part? ____ A: First aid for burns (and scalds). Cold water cools burns and scalds and reduces pain.
chunks.source: Cold water cools burns and scalds and reduces pain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Give the use of cotton (wool) in first aid management: ____ A: For cleaning wounds. Cotton wool cleans wounds before dressing.
chunks.source: Cotton wool cleans wounds before dressing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Give the use of a bandage in first aid management: ____ A: For holding dressings in place (covering wounds). Bandages hold dressings and support injured parts.
chunks.source: Bandages hold dressings and support injured parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) What first aid can you give to a young child who has swallowed rat poison? ____ A: Give plenty of milk (or water) and rush the child to hospital. Give milk to dilute the poison and take the child to hospital at once.
chunks.source: Give milk to dilute the poison and take the child to hospital at once.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Name the type of blood vessel drawn above: ____ A: Vein. The vessel has valves (W) that stop backflow: it is a vein.
chunks.source: The vessel has valves (W) that stop backflow: it is a vein.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give a reason why blood carried by the above blood vessel flows at a low pressure: ____ A: Because it is flowing back to the heart (it has lost pressure in the capillaries). After passing through the tiny capillaries, blood pressure drops, so veins carry blood at low pressure.
chunks.source: After passing through the tiny capillaries, blood pressure drops, so veins carry blood at low pressure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give the importance of structures marked W in the blood vessel above: ____ A: They prevent the backflow of blood. W are valves; they let blood flow one way towards the heart and stop it flowing back.
chunks.source: W are valves; they let blood flow one way towards the heart and stop it flowing back.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The arrows showing the direction of blood flow in the vein above should point: A: Toward the heart. Veins carry blood towards the heart, in the direction their valves open.
chunks.source: Veins carry blood towards the heart, in the direction their valves open.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each item in List A with its correct match in List B. List A: Chameleon, Kangaroo, Whale, Tilapia. List B: external fertilization; camouflages for defence; pouch for carrying young ones; layer of fats (blubber). A: Chameleon: camouflages for defence; Kangaroo: pouch for carrying young ones; Whale: layer of fats (blubber); Tilapia: external fertilization. Chameleon camouflages; kangaroo carries young in a pouch; whale has blubber; tilapia fertilizes eggs outside the body.
chunks.source: Chameleon camouflages; kangaroo carries young in a pouch; whale has blubber; tilapia fertilizes eggs outside the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What is near drowning? ____ A: A situation where a person almost drowns (but is rescued alive). Near drowning is when someone nearly dies in water but survives.
chunks.source: Near drowning is when someone nearly dies in water but survives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) State any one cause of near drowning: ____ A: Falling into deep water (inability to swim). Near drowning is caused by falling into water, swimming in deep water or cramps.
chunks.source: Near drowning is caused by falling into water, swimming in deep water or cramps.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Which first aid is given to a near drowned victim who has been removed from water? ____ A: Artificial respiration (mouth to mouth). Give artificial respiration to restore breathing.
chunks.source: Give artificial respiration to restore breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) How does the use of a life jacket while travelling on water help to prevent near drowning? ____ A: It keeps the person floating on water. A life jacket keeps one afloat even if they cannot swim.
chunks.source: A life jacket keeps one afloat even if they cannot swim.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Where does absorption of alcohol take place in the human digestive system? ____ A: In the stomach. Alcohol is absorbed into the blood mainly through the stomach walls.
chunks.source: Alcohol is absorbed into the blood mainly through the stomach walls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give one reason why vitamins and mineral salts are not digested in any part of the digestive system: ____ A: Because they are already in a simple form (they do not need digestion). Vitamins and mineral salts are already simple, so they are absorbed directly.
chunks.source: Vitamins and mineral salts are already simple, so they are absorbed directly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(i) Give one adaptation of the ileum that enables it to absorb digested food: ____ A: It is long (coiled) to increase surface area. The ileum is very long and has finger-like villi, giving a large surface for absorption.
chunks.source: The ileum is very long and has finger-like villi, giving a large surface for absorption.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(ii) Give another adaptation of the ileum that enables it to absorb digested food: ____ A: It has villi (finger-like projections). Villi greatly increase the absorbing surface of the ileum.
chunks.source: Villi greatly increase the absorbing surface of the ileum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Identify any one insect that contaminates our food: ____ A: Housefly. Houseflies land on faeces then on food, contaminating it.
chunks.source: Houseflies land on faeces then on food, contaminating it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Write any one example of a disease spread through contaminated food: ____ A: Cholera. Contaminated food spreads cholera, typhoid and dysentery.
chunks.source: Contaminated food spreads cholera, typhoid and dysentery.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(i) Suggest one way you would prevent contamination of food by the vector named in (a) above: ____ A: Cover food (properly). Cover food, kill flies and keep the surroundings clean.
chunks.source: Cover food, kill flies and keep the surroundings clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c)(ii) Suggest another way you would prevent contamination of food by the vector: ____ A: Kill houseflies (keep the home clean). Spray or trap flies and dispose of rubbish properly.
chunks.source: Spray or trap flies and dispose of rubbish properly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) Apart from paddock grazing, give one other system of grazing cattle: ____ A: Zero grazing. Grazing systems: paddock, zero grazing, tethering, herding (free range), strip grazing.
chunks.source: Grazing systems: paddock, zero grazing, tethering, herding (free range), strip grazing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Give another system of grazing cattle: ____ A: Tethering. In tethering, an animal is tied with a rope to graze in one spot.
chunks.source: In tethering, an animal is tied with a rope to graze in one spot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) How does paddock grazing help to reduce tick borne diseases on a farm? ____ A: Ticks die (starve) when paddocks are rested, breaking their life cycle. Resting paddocks leaves ticks without animals to feed on, so they die.
chunks.source: Resting paddocks leaves ticks without animals to feed on, so they die.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Give one disadvantage of paddock system of grazing cattle: ____ A: It is expensive (needs fencing and large land). Paddocks need a lot of land and money for fencing and water.
chunks.source: Paddocks need a lot of land and money for fencing and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) Why do people feel hotter when dressed in black on hot days than when dressed in white? ____ A: Because black absorbs heat while white reflects it. Black clothes absorb the sun's heat; white clothes reflect it away.
chunks.source: Black clothes absorb the sun's heat; white clothes reflect it away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(i) Name one source of heat used for cooking food at home: ____ A: Firewood. Heat for cooking comes from firewood, charcoal, paraffin, gas or electricity.
chunks.source: Heat for cooking comes from firewood, charcoal, paraffin, gas or electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b)(ii) Name another source of heat used for cooking food at home: ____ A: Charcoal. Charcoal burns with steady heat in stoves.
chunks.source: Charcoal burns with steady heat in stoves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Identify any one food value that provides heat to the body: ____ A: Carbohydrates. Carbohydrates (and fats) are burnt in the body to release heat and energy.
chunks.source: Carbohydrates (and fats) are burnt in the body to release heat and energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(i) In the diagram of an insect, name part marked O: ____ A: Thorax. O points to the middle segment of the insect's body: the thorax. (The answer line in the booklet is mislabeled Q, but the question asks for O and P.)
chunks.source: O points to the middle segment of the insect's body: the thorax. (The answer line in the booklet is mislabeled Q, but the question asks for O and P.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a)(ii) Name part marked P: ____ A: Antenna (antennae). P points to the feeler on the head: the antenna.
chunks.source: P points to the feeler on the head: the antenna.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) How is part marked P useful to an insect? ____ A: For feeling and smelling (it is a sense organ). The antennae are sense organs for touch and smell.
chunks.source: The antennae are sense organs for touch and smell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Why do you think the insect in the diagram is a female? ____ A: Because it has an ovipositor (for laying eggs). The diagram shows an ovipositor at the abdomen tip, which only females have.
chunks.source: The diagram shows an ovipositor at the abdomen tip, which only females have.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (a) What name is given to the thermometer above? ____ A: Clinical thermometer. The thermometer with a kink for measuring body temperature is a clinical thermometer.
chunks.source: The thermometer with a kink for measuring body temperature is a clinical thermometer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (b) Give the function of part marked with letter R: ____ A: It prevents mercury from flowing back (so the reading can be taken). R is the kink (constriction) that stops mercury returning to the bulb after use.
chunks.source: R is the kink (constriction) that stops mercury returning to the bulb after use.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (c) Name the liquid commonly used in the above thermometer: ____ A: Mercury. Clinical thermometers commonly use mercury.
chunks.source: Clinical thermometers commonly use mercury.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: (d) How does a doctor sterilize the above thermometer after use? ____ A: By wiping it with a disinfectant (methylated spirit). The thermometer is wiped with disinfectant, never boiled.
chunks.source: The thermometer is wiped with disinfectant, never boiled.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a fungus? A: mushroom. Fungi are living things that feed on dead matter; mushroom, yeast and mould are common examples.
chunks.source: Fungi are living things that feed on dead matter; mushroom, yeast and mould are common examples.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The bee which does most of the duties in a beehive is the ___. A: worker bee. Worker bees clean the hive, feed the young, collect nectar and guard the hive.
chunks.source: Worker bees clean the hive, feed the young, collect nectar and guard the hive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a fertilized egg. The part marked X is the ___. A: yolk. The yolk is the yellow central part of the egg that feeds the growing chick.
chunks.source: The yolk is the yellow central part of the egg that feeds the growing chick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way through which heat travels is ___. A: conduction. Heat travels by conduction in solids, by convection in fluids and by radiation through space.
chunks.source: Heat travels by conduction in solids, by convection in fluids and by radiation through space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A cat is helpful to a crop farmer because it ___. A: kills rats that destroy crops. Cats hunt rats and mice that would otherwise eat growing and stored crops.
chunks.source: Cats hunt rats and mice that would otherwise eat growing and stored crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of cow dung to people is ___. A: it is used as manure. Cow dung adds nutrients to the soil and can also be dried and used as fuel.
chunks.source: Cow dung adds nutrients to the soil and can also be dried and used as fuel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides a toothbrush, which of the following is another material used in the promotion of oral health? A: toothpaste. Toothpaste contains fluoride, which strengthens teeth and prevents decay.
chunks.source: Toothpaste contains fluoride, which strengthens teeth and prevents decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a glass of cold water from a fridge. The process that led to the formation of water droplets on the glass is ___. A: condensation. Water vapour in the air touched the cold glass, cooled and changed into liquid droplets.
chunks.source: Water vapour in the air touched the cold glass, cooled and changed into liquid droplets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Learners use the displacement method of measurement when measuring the volume of ___. A: irregular objects. An irregular object is lowered into water and the volume of water it pushes aside equals its volume.
chunks.source: An irregular object is lowered into water and the volume of water it pushes aside equals its volume.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wetlands promote the spread of malaria because they ___. A: are breeding places for mosquitoes. Stagnant water in wetlands is where mosquitoes lay their eggs.
chunks.source: Stagnant water in wetlands is where mosquitoes lay their eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A lion is different from an antelope in the way they feed because the lion is a ___ while the antelope is a herbivore. A: carnivore. Lions eat flesh (meat) while antelopes feed on grass and plants.
chunks.source: Lions eat flesh (meat) while antelopes feed on grass and plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The major component of air in the atmosphere is ___. A: nitrogen. Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air we breathe.
chunks.source: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air we breathe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One item that can be used to harvest resources such as water is a ___. A: tank. Roof tanks, drums and jerrycans store rainwater harvested from roofs.
chunks.source: Roof tanks, drums and jerrycans store rainwater harvested from roofs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a wingless insect is a ___. A: flea. Fleas, lice and silverfish are insects that have no wings.
chunks.source: Fleas, lice and silverfish are insects that have no wings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One healthy lifestyle that can help you fight skin diseases is ___. A: bathing the body daily. Washing removes dirt and germs that cause skin infections.
chunks.source: Washing removes dirt and germs that cause skin infections.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A piece of paper floats on water because it is ___ than water. A: less dense (lighter). Objects that are less dense than water float on it.
chunks.source: Objects that are less dense than water float on it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The main product obtained from a cow is ___. A: milk. Likely answer: milk. The diagram was not extractable, but cows are mainly kept for milk (and meat).
chunks.source: Likely answer: milk. The diagram was not extractable, but cows are mainly kept for milk (and meat).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The common way through which HIV is spread is through ___. A: unprotected sexual intercourse. HIV passes through body fluids, most commonly during unprotected sex.
chunks.source: HIV passes through body fluids, most commonly during unprotected sex.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from drinking, which of the following is an use of water to a school child? A: washing (bathing). Water is also needed for washing, cleaning and cooking.
chunks.source: Water is also needed for washing, cleaning and cooking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The sound of a child singing reaches a person 200 metres away through ___. A: air. Sound travels from the singer through the air to the listener's ears.
chunks.source: Sound travels from the singer through the air to the listener's ears.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One element of Primary Health Care (P.H.C.) is ___. A: immunization. P.H.C. elements include immunization, safe water, sanitation and nutrition education.
chunks.source: P.H.C. elements include immunization, safe water, sanitation and nutrition education.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One agent of soil erosion is ___. A: running water. Running water and wind carry away the top fertile soil.
chunks.source: Running water and wind carry away the top fertile soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The organ of hearing in insects is the ___. A: antennae. Insects detect sound vibrations with their antennae.
chunks.source: Insects detect sound vibrations with their antennae.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The type of weather suitable for winnowing is ___ weather. A: windy. Wind blows away the light husks while the heavy grain falls down.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light husks while the heavy grain falls down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One activity that can destroy habitats of wild animals is ___. A: deforestation. Cutting down forests removes the homes and food of wild animals.
chunks.source: Cutting down forests removes the homes and food of wild animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One importance of heat from the sun is ___. A: drying clothes and harvested crops. The sun's heat dries our clothes and helps preserve harvested crops.
chunks.source: The sun's heat dries our clothes and helps preserve harvested crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a building material (a brick). The natural resource from which it is made is ___. A: clay (soil). Bricks are moulded from clay soil and then baked so they harden.
chunks.source: Bricks are moulded from clay soil and then baked so they harden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way people abuse drugs is ___. A: taking an overdose. Drug abuse includes taking an overdose and taking drugs without a doctor's advice.
chunks.source: Drug abuse includes taking an overdose and taking drugs without a doctor's advice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The seed shown in the diagram is dispersed by ___. A: wind. Likely answer: wind. The seed appears to have wing-like structures that let wind carry it.
chunks.source: Likely answer: wind. The seed appears to have wing-like structures that let wind carry it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a type of chicken reared in Uganda? A: layers. Layers are kept for eggs and broilers are kept for meat in Uganda.
chunks.source: Layers are kept for eggs and broilers are kept for meat in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another type of chicken reared in Uganda? A: broilers. Broilers grow fast and are kept for meat.
chunks.source: Broilers grow fast and are kept for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The system of poultry keeping commonly used by most rural farmers is ___. A: free range. Rural farmers let chickens roam freely to find their own food.
chunks.source: Rural farmers let chickens roam freely to find their own food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The system of poultry keeping commonly used by most commercial farmers is ___. A: deep litter. Commercial farmers keep many birds indoors on the floor (deep litter) or in cages.
chunks.source: Commercial farmers keep many birds indoors on the floor (deep litter) or in cages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a respiratory system. The part marked Y is the ___. A: trachea (windpipe). The trachea is the tube that carries air from the nose to the lungs.
chunks.source: The trachea is the tube that carries air from the nose to the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part marked Z is the ___. A: nostrils (nose). Air enters the respiratory system through the nostrils.
chunks.source: Air enters the respiratory system through the nostrils.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The process that takes place in part labelled X is ___. A: gaseous exchange (breathing). In the lungs, oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.
chunks.source: In the lungs, oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way the above respiratory system can be kept healthy is to ___. A: avoid smoking. Smoke damages the lungs; exercise and clean air keep them healthy.
chunks.source: Smoke damages the lungs; exercise and clean air keep them healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a childhood immunisable disease caused by a virus? A: polio. Polio and measles are viral diseases prevented by immunization.
chunks.source: Polio and measles are viral diseases prevented by immunization.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a childhood immunisable disease caused by bacteria? A: tuberculosis. Tuberculosis, whooping cough and diphtheria are bacterial diseases prevented by immunization.
chunks.source: Tuberculosis, whooping cough and diphtheria are bacterial diseases prevented by immunization.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Immunization is important to people because it ___. A: protects them against killer diseases. Vaccines build immunity so the body can fight disease germs.
chunks.source: Vaccines build immunity so the body can fight disease germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the animals: goose, fish, lizard, rabbit, frog, bat. One similarity among all the animals above is that they all ___. A: are vertebrates (have backbones). All these animals have a backbone, so they are all vertebrates.
chunks.source: All these animals have a backbone, so they are all vertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: From the list above, one animal that has fur on its body is the ___. A: rabbit. Rabbits and bats are mammals, and mammals have fur or hair.
chunks.source: Rabbits and bats are mammals, and mammals have fur or hair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: From the list above, another animal that has fur on its body is the ___. A: bat. Bats are mammals, so their bodies are covered with fur.
chunks.source: Bats are mammals, so their bodies are covered with fur.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a musical instrument. It belongs to the ___ group of musical instruments. A: percussion. Drums are percussion instruments because sound is made by hitting them.
