chunks.source: Drums are percussion instruments because sound is made by hitting them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The instrument above produces sound by ___. A: beating (hitting) the stretched skin. Hitting the tight skin makes it vibrate and produce sound.
chunks.source: Hitting the tight skin makes it vibrate and produce sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The animal product used to make part X is ___. A: skin (hide/leather). Drum skins are made from animal hide stretched tightly over the drum.
chunks.source: Drum skins are made from animal hide stretched tightly over the drum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One factor that can affect the pitch of sound produced by the instrument above is ___. A: the tightness of the skin. A tighter skin vibrates faster and gives a higher pitch.
chunks.source: A tighter skin vibrates faster and gives a higher pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The importance of stomata to a plant is for ___. A: gaseous exchange. Stomata are tiny holes in leaves through which gases and water vapour pass.
chunks.source: Stomata are tiny holes in leaves through which gases and water vapour pass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Some plants shed their leaves in the dry season to ___. A: reduce water loss. Without leaves, the plant loses less water by transpiration.
chunks.source: Without leaves, the plant loses less water by transpiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One condition needed by plants to grow well is ___. A: water. Plants need water, sunlight, air and fertile soil to grow well.
chunks.source: Plants need water, sunlight, air and fertile soil to grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another condition needed by plants to grow well is ___. A: sunlight. Plants use sunlight to make food by photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants use sunlight to make food by photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The instrument used to measure rainfall is a ___. A: rain gauge. A rain gauge collects rain so its depth can be measured.
chunks.source: A rain gauge collects rain so its depth can be measured.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Rainfall is measured in ___. A: millimetres. The depth of collected rain is read in millimetres (mm).
chunks.source: The depth of collected rain is read in millimetres (mm).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One other weather instrument is the ___. A: thermometer. A thermometer measures temperature; other instruments include the anemometer and wind vane.
chunks.source: A thermometer measures temperature; other instruments include the anemometer and wind vane.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another weather instrument is the ___. A: anemometer. An anemometer measures the speed of wind.
chunks.source: An anemometer measures the speed of wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A school compound should be kept clean to ___. A: prevent the spread of diseases. A clean compound has fewer germs and looks beautiful.
chunks.source: A clean compound has fewer germs and looks beautiful.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One component of a clean home is ___. A: a clean latrine. A clean home has a clean latrine, a clean kitchen and proper rubbish disposal.
chunks.source: A clean home has a clean latrine, a clean kitchen and proper rubbish disposal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another component of a clean home is ___. A: a clean kitchen. Food must be prepared in a clean place to avoid contamination.
chunks.source: Food must be prepared in a clean place to avoid contamination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One component of a balanced diet is ___. A: carbohydrates. A balanced diet has carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, fats, minerals, fibre and water.
chunks.source: A balanced diet has carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, fats, minerals, fibre and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: People are advised to eat a balanced diet in order to ___. A: grow well and stay healthy. A balanced diet gives the body all nutrients and prevents deficiency diseases.
chunks.source: A balanced diet gives the body all nutrients and prevents deficiency diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One sign of poor feeding in children is ___. A: a thin body. Poorly fed children become thin, have swollen bellies or brown hair.
chunks.source: Poorly fed children become thin, have swollen bellies or brown hair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another sign of poor feeding in children is ___. A: a swollen belly. Kwashiorkor causes the belly to swell in poorly fed children.
chunks.source: Kwashiorkor causes the belly to swell in poorly fed children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The use of hole marked B is to ___. A: put in charcoal. Charcoal is pushed into the stove through hole B.
chunks.source: Charcoal is pushed into the stove through hole B.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The fuel used by the stove above is ___. A: charcoal. The stove burns charcoal to heat the saucepan.
chunks.source: The stove burns charcoal to heat the saucepan.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from sun drying, which of the following is another method of food preservation? A: salting. Salting, smoking, refrigeration and tinning also preserve food.
chunks.source: Salting, smoking, refrigeration and tinning also preserve food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from sun drying, which of the following is another method of food preservation? A: smoking. Smoking removes water from food so germs cannot grow in it.
chunks.source: Smoking removes water from food so germs cannot grow in it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One foodstuff that is preserved by sun drying is ___. A: cassava. Cassava, maize, beans and fish are commonly sun dried.
chunks.source: Cassava, maize, beans and fish are commonly sun dried.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another foodstuff that is preserved by sun drying is ___. A: maize. Drying maize grains in the sun keeps them for a long time.
chunks.source: Drying maize grains in the sun keeps them for a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One item needed by a person going to harvest honey is ___. A: a bee veil. A veil, smoker, overall and gloves protect the harvester from stings.
chunks.source: A veil, smoker, overall and gloves protect the harvester from stings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another item needed by a person going to harvest honey is ___. A: a smoker. Smoke calms the bees so honey can be harvested safely.
chunks.source: Smoke calms the bees so honey can be harvested safely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The best time for harvesting honey is ___. A: in the evening (at night). Bees are less active and docile in the cool of the evening.
chunks.source: Bees are less active and docile in the cool of the evening.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One importance of soil is ___. A: it supports plant growth. Soil holds plants and gives them water and nutrients.
chunks.source: Soil holds plants and gives them water and nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another importance of soil is ___. A: it is used for building. Soil is used to make bricks and to smear houses.
chunks.source: Soil is used to make bricks and to smear houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One harmful material on soil is ___. A: polythene (plastics). Polythene, chemicals and broken glass harm the soil.
chunks.source: Polythene, chemicals and broken glass harm the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One importance of PIASCY in schools is ___. A: it sensitizes pupils about HIV/AIDS. PIASCY teaches pupils how HIV spreads and how to avoid it.
chunks.source: PIASCY teaches pupils how HIV spreads and how to avoid it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one HIV/AIDS message for your school: ___. A: Abstain from sex. Abstinence, faithfulness and avoiding sharing sharp objects protect against HIV.
chunks.source: Abstinence, faithfulness and avoiding sharing sharp objects protect against HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a liquid that can float on water? A: oil (paraffin). Oil is less dense than water, so it floats on top of it.
chunks.source: Oil is less dense than water, so it floats on top of it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one word that refers to the physical change of state from vapour to water: ___. A: condensation. Condensation is the change of water vapour into liquid water on cooling.
chunks.source: Condensation is the change of water vapour into liquid water on cooling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of managing wastes in the environment? A: sorting and recycling waste. Sorting rubbish and recycling keeps the environment clean and reduces pollution.
chunks.source: Sorting rubbish and recycling keeps the environment clean and reduces pollution.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which immunisable disease in children is fought using the BCG vaccine? A: tuberculosis. The BCG vaccine given at birth protects babies against tuberculosis.
chunks.source: The BCG vaccine given at birth protects babies against tuberculosis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a tool. What is the use of the above tool to crop farmers? A: watering crops (seedlings). A watering can is used to sprinkle water on crops and young seedlings.
chunks.source: A watering can is used to sprinkle water on crops and young seedlings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of bees in a hive that mate with the queen bee? A: drones. Drones are the male bees whose duty is to mate with the queen.
chunks.source: Drones are the male bees whose duty is to mate with the queen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do some plants like pumpkins climb other plants? A: to get enough sunlight. Climbing plants grow up supports so their leaves can reach sunlight for photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Climbing plants grow up supports so their leaves can reach sunlight for photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a P.6 pupil prevent himself/herself from getting infected with HIV/AIDS? A: by abstaining from sex. Abstinence keeps pupils safe from HIV infection.
chunks.source: Abstinence keeps pupils safe from HIV infection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the component of air used in stopping fire outbreak? A: carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so fire extinguishers release it to put out fires.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so fire extinguishers release it to put out fires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an organ which is damaged when an individual over-depends on alcohol? A: liver. Too much alcohol damages the liver and can cause liver disease.
chunks.source: Too much alcohol damages the liver and can cause liver disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a cause of dehydration among children? A: diarrhoea. Diarrhoea and vomiting make the body lose a lot of water.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea and vomiting make the body lose a lot of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which element of weather is measured using a hygrometer? A: humidity. A hygrometer measures the amount of water vapour (humidity) in the air.
chunks.source: A hygrometer measures the amount of water vapour (humidity) in the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the human body organ found in the head that helps us to remember things? A: brain. The brain controls thinking, memory and all body activities.
chunks.source: The brain controls thinking, memory and all body activities.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a component of soil? A: humus. Soil is made of humus, air, water and small rock particles.
chunks.source: Soil is made of humus, air, water and small rock particles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one content of a first aid box: ___. A: bandage. A first aid box contains bandages, cotton wool, antiseptic and painkillers.
chunks.source: A first aid box contains bandages, cotton wool, antiseptic and painkillers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disorder of the digestive system? A: constipation. Constipation, diarrhoea and indigestion are disorders of the digestive system.
chunks.source: Constipation, diarrhoea and indigestion are disorders of the digestive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Layers should be fed on feeds containing enough calcium for ___. A: formation of strong eggshells. Calcium makes the shells of eggs hard and strong.
chunks.source: Calcium makes the shells of eggs hard and strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a plant with parts A, B and C. Which letter shows the structure used by the plant to take in water? A: C. Roots (marked C) absorb water and mineral salts from the soil.
chunks.source: Roots (marked C) absorb water and mineral salts from the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for people to keep their bodies clean? A: to prevent diseases. A clean body has fewer germs that cause diseases.
chunks.source: A clean body has fewer germs that cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one way in which people can destroy their environment: ___. A: deforestation. Cutting down trees and bush burning destroy the environment.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees and bush burning destroy the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a leguminous crop? A: beans. Beans, groundnuts, peas and soya beans are leguminous crops that add nitrogen to soil.
chunks.source: Beans, groundnuts, peas and soya beans are leguminous crops that add nitrogen to soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way in which people can manage rainy weather? A: using umbrellas. Umbrellas, raincoats and gumboots protect people from rain.
chunks.source: Umbrellas, raincoats and gumboots protect people from rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Insects have three main body parts. Give any one of them: ___. A: head. An insect's body has a head, thorax and abdomen.
chunks.source: An insect's body has a head, thorax and abdomen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a poultry farmer prevent diseases that attack poultry? A: by vaccinating the birds. Vaccination builds immunity against poultry diseases.
chunks.source: Vaccination builds immunity against poultry diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one insect that stings: ___. A: bee. Bees and wasps sting to defend themselves.
chunks.source: Bees and wasps sting to defend themselves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a natural cause of changes in the environment? A: floods. Floods, drought, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions change the environment naturally.
chunks.source: Floods, drought, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions change the environment naturally.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the sense organ that helps one to detect a dog barking? A: ear. The ear detects sound such as a dog barking.
chunks.source: The ear detects sound such as a dog barking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a source of water? A: rain. Rain, wells, boreholes and rivers are sources of water.
chunks.source: Rain, wells, boreholes and rivers are sources of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of energy possessed by a moving object? A: kinetic energy. Anything that moves has kinetic energy.
chunks.source: Anything that moves has kinetic energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the deficiency disease the person in the diagram is suffering from? A: goitre. The swollen neck (goitre) is caused by lack of iodine in the diet.
chunks.source: The swollen neck (goitre) is caused by lack of iodine in the diet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an element of Primary Health Care? A: immunization. Immunization, safe water and sanitation are elements of Primary Health Care.
chunks.source: Immunization, safe water and sanitation are elements of Primary Health Care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an effect of alcohol to an individual? A: it damages the liver. Alcohol can damage the liver and make a person lose self-control.
chunks.source: Alcohol can damage the liver and make a person lose self-control.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the banana plant propagated? A: by suckers. Bananas grow from suckers that shoot from the base of the parent plant.
chunks.source: Bananas grow from suckers that shoot from the base of the parent plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is cassava propagated? A: by stem cuttings. Pieces of cassava stem planted in soil grow into new plants.
chunks.source: Pieces of cassava stem planted in soil grow into new plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a plant that produces fibre? A: cotton. Cotton, sisal and flax give fibres used for cloth and ropes.
chunks.source: Cotton, sisal and flax give fibres used for cloth and ropes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a reason why animals move from one place to another? A: to look for food. Animals move to find food, water, shelter, mates and to escape danger.
chunks.source: Animals move to find food, water, shelter, mates and to escape danger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another reason why animals move from one place to another? A: to escape from danger. Animals run away from enemies that want to eat them.
chunks.source: Animals run away from enemies that want to eat them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a snake move? A: by slithering (crawling). A snake has no legs, so it slides along the ground by slithering.
chunks.source: A snake has no legs, so it slides along the ground by slithering.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a frog move? A: by hopping (jumping). A frog jumps with its strong hind legs and can also swim.
chunks.source: A frog jumps with its strong hind legs and can also swim.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List one foodstuff that can be preserved by smoking: ___. A: fish. Fish and meat are preserved by smoking over fire.
chunks.source: Fish and meat are preserved by smoking over fire.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List one foodstuff that can be preserved by sun drying: ___. A: cassava. Cassava, maize and beans are dried in the sun for storage.
chunks.source: Cassava, maize and beans are dried in the sun for storage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List one foodstuff that can be preserved by pasteurization: ___. A: milk. Milk is heated gently (pasteurized) to kill germs and keep longer.
chunks.source: Milk is heated gently (pasteurized) to kill germs and keep longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a material used in making ORS? A: sugar. ORS is made by dissolving sugar and salt in clean boiled water.
chunks.source: ORS is made by dissolving sugar and salt in clean boiled water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another material used in making ORS? A: salt. Salt replaces the body salts lost during diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Salt replaces the body salts lost during diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a musical instrument. Name the musical instrument above: ___. A: xylophone. A xylophone is made of wooden bars of different lengths arranged in order.
chunks.source: A xylophone is made of wooden bars of different lengths arranged in order.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the bar which will produce the lowest pitch? A: E. Likely answer: E. The longest bar vibrates slowest and gives the lowest pitch; E appears to be the longest bar.
chunks.source: Likely answer: E. The longest bar vibrates slowest and gives the lowest pitch; E appears to be the longest bar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which group of musical instruments does it belong? A: percussion. The xylophone is a percussion instrument because sound is made by hitting it.
chunks.source: The xylophone is a percussion instrument because sound is made by hitting it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the blood component that transports oxygen to all body parts? A: red blood cells. Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to all body parts.
chunks.source: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to all body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another way in which you can increase the amount of blood in your body? A: drinking plenty of fluids. Fluids increase the liquid part of blood.
chunks.source: Fluids increase the liquid part of blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one disease that results from active smoking: ___. A: lung cancer. Smoking damages the lungs and can cause lung cancer.
chunks.source: Smoking damages the lungs and can cause lung cancer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a reason why people smoke? A: peer pressure. Some people start smoking because friends influence them.
chunks.source: Some people start smoking because friends influence them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another reason why people smoke? A: to relieve stress. Some people wrongly believe smoking reduces stress.
chunks.source: Some people wrongly believe smoking reduces stress.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a life skill that can safeguard you against smoking? A: assertiveness (saying no). Being assertive helps you refuse cigarettes confidently.
chunks.source: Being assertive helps you refuse cigarettes confidently.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagrams show garden tools. Name the garden tool marked A: ___. A: hoe. A hoe is used for digging and weeding in the garden.
chunks.source: A hoe is used for digging and weeding in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the garden tool marked B? A: axe. An axe is used for cutting wood.
chunks.source: An axe is used for cutting wood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an use of tool marked B at home? A: splitting firewood. The axe splits logs into firewood for cooking.
chunks.source: The axe splits logs into firewood for cooking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write AIDS in full: ___. A: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome. AIDS is the disease caused by HIV when body immunity is destroyed.
chunks.source: AIDS is the disease caused by HIV when body immunity is destroyed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write HIV in full: ___. A: Human Immunodeficiency Virus. HIV is the virus that causes AIDS.
chunks.source: HIV is the virus that causes AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is PIASCY useful to school children? A: it sensitizes them about HIV/AIDS. PIASCY teaches school children how HIV spreads and how to avoid it.
chunks.source: PIASCY teaches school children how HIV spreads and how to avoid it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one PIASCY message: ___. A: Abstain from sex. Abstinence messages protect school children from HIV.
chunks.source: Abstinence messages protect school children from HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is of the reproductive system of a woman. Name the part marked A: ___. A: uterus (womb). The uterus is where the baby grows during pregnancy.
chunks.source: The uterus is where the baby grows during pregnancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the part marked C? A: vagina (birth canal). The vagina is the passage through which the baby is born.
chunks.source: The vagina is the passage through which the baby is born.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a sexually transmitted disease that attacks the system above? A: gonorrhoea. Gonorrhoea, syphilis and HIV attack the reproductive system.
chunks.source: Gonorrhoea, syphilis and HIV attack the reproductive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a danger of hookworms to people? A: they cause anaemia. Hookworms suck blood, making the person anaemic and weak.
chunks.source: Hookworms suck blood, making the person anaemic and weak.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one health habit that can help people to avoid worm infestation: ___. A: wearing shoes. Shoes stop hookworms entering through the feet.
chunks.source: Shoes stop hookworms entering through the feet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down another health habit that can help people to avoid worm infestation: ___. A: washing hands before eating. Clean hands keep worm eggs out of food.
chunks.source: Clean hands keep worm eggs out of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a material farmers use to mulch a garden? A: dry grass. Dry grass, banana leaves and coffee husks are used as mulch.
chunks.source: Dry grass, banana leaves and coffee husks are used as mulch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another material farmers use to mulch a garden? A: banana leaves. Banana leaves spread on soil keep moisture and stop weeds.
chunks.source: Banana leaves spread on soil keep moisture and stop weeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another importance of mulching? A: it controls weeds. Mulch blocks sunlight so weeds cannot grow.
chunks.source: Mulch blocks sunlight so weeds cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an advantage of food taboo? A: it preserves culture (customs). Food taboos keep some cultural practices alive.
chunks.source: Food taboos keep some cultural practices alive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an effect of poor feeding to babies? A: stunted growth. Poorly fed babies do not grow well and fall sick easily.
chunks.source: Poorly fed babies do not grow well and fall sick easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the instrument we can use to see bacteria? A: microscope. Bacteria are too small to see, so we use a microscope.
chunks.source: Bacteria are too small to see, so we use a microscope.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of wood fuel commonly used by people in Uganda? A: firewood. Firewood and charcoal are the common wood fuels used in Uganda.
chunks.source: Firewood and charcoal are the common wood fuels used in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Root crops store their food in the roots. Suggest one way people prepare such foodstuffs for eating: ___. A: boiling (peeling and boiling). Root crops like cassava are peeled and boiled before eating.
chunks.source: Root crops like cassava are peeled and boiled before eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which state of matter are the molecules closely attached together? A: solid. In solids the particles are packed closely and only vibrate in position.
chunks.source: In solids the particles are packed closely and only vibrate in position.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a sound storage device that can produce sound in a computer? A: flash disk. Flash disks, CDs and memory cards store sound that a computer can play.
chunks.source: Flash disks, CDs and memory cards store sound that a computer can play.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the garden tool drawn below? A: spade. A spade is used for digging and lifting soil.
chunks.source: A spade is used for digging and lifting soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a type of poultry commonly kept in Uganda today? A: layers. Layers (for eggs), broilers (for meat) and local chicken are kept in Uganda.
chunks.source: Layers (for eggs), broilers (for meat) and local chicken are kept in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a negative effect of bush burning to the environment? A: it destroys soil fertility. Bush burning kills soil organisms and burns the humus in soil.
chunks.source: Bush burning kills soil organisms and burns the humus in soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a behaviour or habit that can maintain good working conditions of the digestive system? A: chewing food well. Chewing food properly and eating on time keep the digestive system working well.
chunks.source: Chewing food properly and eating on time keep the digestive system working well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which stage in the life cycle of a mosquito is very dangerous to human life? A: the adult stage. The adult female mosquito bites people and spreads malaria.
chunks.source: The adult female mosquito bites people and spreads malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of controlling intestinal worms in people? A: deworming regularly. Taking deworming tablets kills intestinal worms.
chunks.source: Taking deworming tablets kills intestinal worms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down the weapon that can be used by a wasp to defend itself from its enemies: ___. A: its sting. A wasp stings its enemies to defend itself.
chunks.source: A wasp stings its enemies to defend itself.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The immunisation schedule in Uganda is free and mandatory. Identify one group of people who must be immunised: ___. A: children under five (infants). Babies and young children are immunised against killer diseases.
chunks.source: Babies and young children are immunised against killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows an animal kept at home. Give one common product people who keep such animals can get: ___. A: meat. Rabbits are kept for meat and also give skins and manure.
chunks.source: Rabbits are kept for meat and also give skins and manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Air is a mixture of gases. What term is given to air in motion? A: wind. Moving air is called wind.
chunks.source: Moving air is called wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from water, which of the following is another item people use to keep their bodies clean? A: soap. Soap removes dirt and germs from the body.
chunks.source: Soap removes dirt and germs from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a food processing method in which yeast plays a big role? A: baking (bread making). Yeast makes dough rise when baking bread.
chunks.source: Yeast makes dough rise when baking bread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: During the preparation of ORS, sugar and salt are dissolved in the water. Give one use of sugar to the patient who drinks ORS: ___. A: it gives the patient energy. Sugar in ORS provides energy to the weak patient.
chunks.source: Sugar in ORS provides energy to the weak patient.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Light and heat from the sun is known as sunshine. State one use of the light to plants in the environment: ___. A: for photosynthesis (making food). Plants use sunlight to make their food.
chunks.source: Plants use sunlight to make their food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of killing germs in water? A: boiling. Boiling kills the germs in water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which kind of blood cells are attacked by plasmodium that causes malaria fever? A: red blood cells. Malaria parasites destroy red blood cells, causing fever and anaemia.
chunks.source: Malaria parasites destroy red blood cells, causing fever and anaemia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a burning candle. What type of change does the wax undergo when the candle is burning? A: physical change. The wax melts, which is a physical change because no new substance is formed.
chunks.source: The wax melts, which is a physical change because no new substance is formed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write HIV in full: ___. A: Human Immunodeficiency Virus. HIV is the virus that causes AIDS.
chunks.source: HIV is the virus that causes AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a communicable disease that spreads through air? A: tuberculosis. Tuberculosis, influenza and measles spread through the air.
chunks.source: Tuberculosis, influenza and measles spread through the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are locusts dangerous to plants? A: they eat and destroy crops. Swarms of locusts feed on green plants and can clear whole gardens.
chunks.source: Swarms of locusts feed on green plants and can clear whole gardens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one disorder of the human teeth: ___. A: tooth decay (dental caries). Tooth decay and misaligned teeth are disorders of the teeth.
chunks.source: Tooth decay and misaligned teeth are disorders of the teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the deficiency disease due to lack of vitamin A? A: night blindness. Lack of vitamin A makes it hard to see at night.
chunks.source: Lack of vitamin A makes it hard to see at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a snail regarded as an invertebrate? A: because it has no backbone. Animals without backbones are called invertebrates.
chunks.source: Animals without backbones are called invertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of soil whose texture is rough and has large particles? A: sandy soil. Sandy soil has large rough particles and drains water fast.
chunks.source: Sandy soil has large rough particles and drains water fast.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of change takes place when a plant bears fruits? A: biological change. Fruiting involves growth, which is a biological change.
chunks.source: Fruiting involves growth, which is a biological change.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way people can protect themselves against rainy weather? A: using umbrellas. Umbrellas and raincoats keep people dry in the rain.
chunks.source: Umbrellas and raincoats keep people dry in the rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one element of PHC: ___. A: immunization. PHC elements include immunization, safe water, sanitation and nutrition education.
chunks.source: PHC elements include immunization, safe water, sanitation and nutrition education.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down another element of PHC: ___. A: provision of safe water. Safe water prevents water-borne diseases.
chunks.source: Safe water prevents water-borne diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an activity in which an individual can promote PHC in the community where he/she lives? A: encouraging people to use latrines. Using latrines and keeping the environment clean promotes community health.
chunks.source: Using latrines and keeping the environment clean promotes community health.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A stone of 98g was lowered into a measuring cylinder and the water level rose from 18ml to 32ml. Find the volume of the stone: ___. A: 14 ml. Volume = 32 ml - 18 ml = 14 ml of water displaced.
chunks.source: Volume = 32 ml - 18 ml = 14 ml of water displaced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a substance that can float on water? A: wood. Wood is less dense than water so it floats.
chunks.source: Wood is less dense than water so it floats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows an insect that is a delicacy in Central Uganda. Name it: ___. A: nsenene (grasshopper). Nsenene is the edible grasshopper enjoyed as a delicacy in Central Uganda.
chunks.source: Nsenene is the edible grasshopper enjoyed as a delicacy in Central Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a characteristic of the above insect? A: it has six legs. Like all insects, nsenene has six legs and three body parts.
chunks.source: Like all insects, nsenene has six legs and three body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a food for the above insect? A: grass (leaves). Nsenene feeds on grass and green leaves.
chunks.source: Nsenene feeds on grass and green leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which form of energy do people use to catch many of them for business or sale? A: light energy. Bright lights are used at night to attract nsenene for catching.
chunks.source: Bright lights are used at night to attract nsenene for catching.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of weaning food? A: porridge. Weaning foods like porridge and mashed bananas are introduced gradually.
chunks.source: Weaning foods like porridge and mashed bananas are introduced gradually.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another example of weaning food? A: mashed bananas. Soft mashed foods are easy for babies to swallow.
chunks.source: Soft mashed foods are easy for babies to swallow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a type of soil erosion? A: sheet erosion. Sheet, rill and gully erosion are types of soil erosion.
chunks.source: Sheet, rill and gully erosion are types of soil erosion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another type of soil erosion? A: gully erosion. Gully erosion cuts deep channels in the land.
chunks.source: Gully erosion cuts deep channels in the land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a cause of soil erosion in the environment? A: deforestation. Cutting trees leaves soil bare so rain washes it away.
chunks.source: Cutting trees leaves soil bare so rain washes it away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a reason why people keep goats in Uganda? A: for meat. Goats are kept for meat, milk and income.
chunks.source: Goats are kept for meat, milk and income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another reason why people keep goats in Uganda? A: for milk. Goat milk is drunk and sold.
chunks.source: Goat milk is drunk and sold.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a breed of goats kept in Uganda? A: Boer. Boer, Mubende and Small East African are goat breeds in Uganda.
chunks.source: Boer, Mubende and Small East African are goat breeds in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease that attacks both goats and sheep? A: anthrax. Anthrax attacks goats, sheep and cattle.
chunks.source: Anthrax attacks goats, sheep and cattle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: On the medical instrument below (a clinical thermometer), the part that prevents back flow of mercury is marked ___. A: K. The kink (marked K) stops mercury flowing back into the bulb so the reading stays.
chunks.source: The kink (marked K) stops mercury flowing back into the bulb so the reading stays.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the role of the above instrument to a doctor? A: to measure body temperature. A clinical thermometer tells the doctor whether a patient has fever.
chunks.source: A clinical thermometer tells the doctor whether a patient has fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a type of immunity? A: natural immunity. Natural immunity is inborn; artificial immunity comes from vaccines.
chunks.source: Natural immunity is inborn; artificial immunity comes from vaccines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a place in our community where we take children for immunization? A: health centre. Children are immunised at health centres and hospitals.
chunks.source: Children are immunised at health centres and hospitals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the animal that breathes through moist skin is the ___. A: earthworm. Earthworms breathe through their moist skins.
chunks.source: Earthworms breathe through their moist skins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the breathing organ of a housefly is the ___. A: spiracles. Insects breathe through tiny holes called spiracles.
chunks.source: Insects breathe through tiny holes called spiracles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the animal that breathes through gills is the ___. A: fish. Fish breathe in water using gills.
chunks.source: Fish breathe in water using gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the breathing organ of a cow is the ___. A: lungs. Cows, like all mammals, breathe with lungs.
chunks.source: Cows, like all mammals, breathe with lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of root crops in the environment? A: cassava. Cassava and sweet potatoes store food in their roots.
chunks.source: Cassava and sweet potatoes store food in their roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another example of root crops in the environment? A: sweet potatoes. Sweet potatoes are root tubers eaten boiled or roasted.
chunks.source: Sweet potatoes are root tubers eaten boiled or roasted.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease that attacks root crops? A: cassava mosaic. Cassava mosaic disease makes cassava leaves mottled and reduces yields.
chunks.source: Cassava mosaic disease makes cassava leaves mottled and reduces yields.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Describe one way farmers can preserve harvested root crops for a long time: ___. A: drying them in the sun. Sun-dried cassava chips keep for a long time.
chunks.source: Sun-dried cassava chips keep for a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease that attacks the human eyes? A: trachoma. Trachoma and conjunctivitis attack the eyes.
chunks.source: Trachoma and conjunctivitis attack the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a diurnal insect (active in day time)? A: housefly. Houseflies and bees are active during the day.
chunks.source: Houseflies and bees are active during the day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a nocturnal insect (active in the night)? A: mosquito. Mosquitoes and moths are active at night.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes and moths are active at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an use of insects to people? A: bees give honey. Bees give honey and pollinate crops.
chunks.source: Bees give honey and pollinate crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a danger of insects to people? A: they spread diseases. Mosquitoes and houseflies spread diseases like malaria and cholera.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes and houseflies spread diseases like malaria and cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of the seed develops into the shoot system? A: plumule. The plumule grows upward into the shoot while the radicle becomes the root.
chunks.source: The plumule grows upward into the shoot while the radicle becomes the root.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being used as food, which of the following is an use of seeds to people and other animals? A: planting. Seeds are planted to grow new crops.
chunks.source: Seeds are planted to grow new crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being used as food, which of the following is another use of seeds to people and other animals? A: making oil. Seeds like simsim and groundnuts are pressed for cooking oil.
chunks.source: Seeds like simsim and groundnuts are pressed for cooking oil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What scientific term is given to the ability of a seed to germinate or grow? A: viability. Viability is the ability of a seed to germinate.
chunks.source: Viability is the ability of a seed to germinate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is of a human ear. Where does part labelled J lead to? A: the middle ear (ear drum). The auditory canal (J) leads inward to the ear drum of the middle ear.
chunks.source: The auditory canal (J) leads inward to the ear drum of the middle ear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a part of the ear found in the outer ear? A: pinna. The pinna is the outer flap that collects sound.
chunks.source: The pinna is the outer flap that collects sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a part of the ear found in the middle ear? A: ear drum (ossicles). The middle ear has the ear drum and three tiny bones (ossicles).
chunks.source: The middle ear has the ear drum and three tiny bones (ossicles).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which form of energy does the organ above respond in order to function? A: sound energy. The ear detects sound energy.
chunks.source: The ear detects sound energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a poisonous fungus? A: toadstool. Toadstools are poisonous fungi that look like mushrooms but are harmful when eaten.
chunks.source: Toadstools are poisonous fungi that look like mushrooms but are harmful when eaten.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a domestic animal that neither gives us milk nor meat? A: dog. Dogs are kept for security, not for milk or meat.
chunks.source: Dogs are kept for security, not for milk or meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way in which people can use rabbit urine and dung at home? A: as manure in the garden. Rabbit droppings and urine add nutrients to the soil.
chunks.source: Rabbit droppings and urine add nutrients to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the mineral salt that helps in strengthening of our teeth and bones? A: calcium. Calcium builds strong teeth and bones; it is found in milk.
chunks.source: Calcium builds strong teeth and bones; it is found in milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows roots of a legume. Name the part marked P: ___. A: root nodule. Root nodules on legumes contain bacteria that fix nitrogen into the soil.
chunks.source: Root nodules on legumes contain bacteria that fix nitrogen into the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from bees, which of the following is another social insect? A: termites. Termites and ants live together in large organised colonies.
chunks.source: Termites and ants live together in large organised colonies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a mosquito similar to reptiles in terms of reproduction? A: both lay eggs. Mosquitoes and reptiles reproduce by laying eggs.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes and reptiles reproduce by laying eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way in which plant leaves can be useful to people? A: as vegetables. Leaves like cabbage are eaten as vegetables; others are used for mulching.
chunks.source: Leaves like cabbage are eaten as vegetables; others are used for mulching.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of dental disorders? A: tooth decay. Tooth decay (cavities) is a common dental disorder.
chunks.source: Tooth decay (cavities) is a common dental disorder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one type of energy you know: ___. A: heat energy. Heat, light, sound and kinetic energy are types of energy.
chunks.source: Heat, light, sound and kinetic energy are types of energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens to a piece of cheese left outside on a sunny day? A: it melts. Heat from the sun melts the cheese.
chunks.source: Heat from the sun melts the cheese.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a plant habitat? A: garden. Gardens, forests and swamps are places where plants grow.
chunks.source: Gardens, forests and swamps are places where plants grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the part that protects the gills of a fish from mechanical injuries? A: operculum (gill cover). The hard gill cover shields the delicate gills.
chunks.source: The hard gill cover shields the delicate gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the missing word to complete the life cycle of a cockroach: Eggs -> ___ -> Adult. A: nymph. A cockroach hatches into a nymph, which grows into an adult. (The diagram was vector-drawn and not extractable.)
chunks.source: A cockroach hatches into a nymph, which grows into an adult. (The diagram was vector-drawn and not extractable.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease that people who live in a home without a latrine are likely to suffer from? A: cholera. Without a latrine, faeces spread germs that cause cholera and diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Without a latrine, faeces spread germs that cause cholera and diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the part of blood which carries oxygen to all body parts? A: red blood cells. Red blood cells pick oxygen from the lungs and deliver it everywhere.
chunks.source: Red blood cells pick oxygen from the lungs and deliver it everywhere.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can the dangers of drought be controlled in Uganda? A: by irrigation (and planting trees). Irrigation gives crops water when rain fails; trees attract rain.
chunks.source: Irrigation gives crops water when rain fails; trees attract rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the part of a plant from which seeds are formed? A: flower (ovary). After pollination, the flower's ovary develops into fruits with seeds.
chunks.source: After pollination, the flower's ovary develops into fruits with seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way in which people may prepare cassava for eating? A: boiling. Cassava is peeled and boiled before eating.
chunks.source: Cassava is peeled and boiled before eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one breed of goats reared in Uganda: ___. A: Boer. Boer, Mubende and Small East African goats are reared in Uganda.
chunks.source: Boer, Mubende and Small East African goats are reared in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a garden tool. How is the above garden tool useful to farmers? A: for loosening soil (and weeding). A hand fork loosens soil and removes weeds around crops.
chunks.source: A hand fork loosens soil and removes weeds around crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of an object that floats on water? A: wood. Wood is less dense than water, so it floats.
chunks.source: Wood is less dense than water, so it floats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the digestive juice which is added to food in the mouth? A: saliva. Saliva moistens food and starts digesting starch.
chunks.source: Saliva moistens food and starts digesting starch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an insect vector that may spread more than one disease to people? A: mosquito. Mosquitoes spread malaria, elephantiasis and yellow fever.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes spread malaria, elephantiasis and yellow fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a thing we can make from sisal? A: ropes. Sisal fibres are twisted into ropes, mats and baskets.
chunks.source: Sisal fibres are twisted into ropes, mats and baskets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a problem of poor personal hygiene? A: bad body smell. Poor hygiene causes bad smell and skin diseases.
chunks.source: Poor hygiene causes bad smell and skin diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which element of PHC helps to control rapid population growth? A: family planning. Family planning helps families have the number of children they can care for.
chunks.source: Family planning helps families have the number of children they can care for.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How many pairs of legs has a spider? A: four pairs. Spiders are arachnids with eight legs in four pairs.
chunks.source: Spiders are arachnids with eight legs in four pairs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a percussion musical instrument? A: drum. Drums and xylophones are played by hitting them.
chunks.source: Drums and xylophones are played by hitting them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one use of the urinary bladder: ___. A: it stores urine. Urine made by the kidneys is stored in the bladder before release.
chunks.source: Urine made by the kidneys is stored in the bladder before release.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one use of the stomach: ___. A: it churns and digests food. The stomach mixes food with juices to digest it.
chunks.source: The stomach mixes food with juices to digest it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a habit that may endanger or bring trouble to the human liver? A: excessive drinking of alcohol. Too much alcohol damages the liver.
chunks.source: Too much alcohol damages the liver.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows an experiment carried out on a plant (a potted plant covered with polythene paper). What was the experiment about? A: transpiration. The experiment shows that leaves give off water (transpiration), which collects on the polythene.
chunks.source: The experiment shows that leaves give off water (transpiration), which collects on the polythene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a factor that determines the rate of the above process? A: temperature. High temperature, wind, light and low humidity increase transpiration.
chunks.source: High temperature, wind, light and low humidity increase transpiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another factor that determines the rate of the above process? A: humidity. Dry air (low humidity) makes transpiration faster.
chunks.source: Dry air (low humidity) makes transpiration faster.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which season of the year do farmers usually mulch their gardens? A: dry season. Mulch keeps soil moisture during the dry season.
chunks.source: Mulch keeps soil moisture during the dry season.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another reason why farmers mulch their gardens? A: to control weeds. Mulch blocks sunlight so weeds cannot grow.
chunks.source: Mulch blocks sunlight so weeds cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a thermometer. What name is given to the thermometer above? A: clinical thermometer. A clinical thermometer is used to measure body temperature.
chunks.source: A clinical thermometer is used to measure body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the liquid commonly used in the above thermometer? A: mercury. Mercury expands evenly with heat, making it good for thermometers.
chunks.source: Mercury expands evenly with heat, making it good for thermometers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A farmer recorded how many times a goat and a rabbit ate each food. What was the most favourable food for the rabbit? A: sweet potato leaves. The rabbit ate sweet potato leaves 4 times, more than any other food.
chunks.source: The rabbit ate sweet potato leaves 4 times, more than any other food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What was the least favourable food for the rabbit? A: sorghum leaves. The rabbit ate sorghum leaves 0 times.
chunks.source: The rabbit ate sorghum leaves 0 times.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: If the farmer was to use only one type of food, which one would be the most favourable for both the goat and the rabbit? A: sweet potato leaves. Sweet potato leaves scored highest in total (4 + 3 = 7).
chunks.source: Sweet potato leaves scored highest in total (4 + 3 = 7).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from babies, which of the following is another vulnerable group of people? A: pregnant women. Pregnant women, the elderly and the sick need special care.
chunks.source: Pregnant women, the elderly and the sick need special care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from babies, which of the following is another vulnerable group of people? A: the elderly. Old people have weak bodies and need support.
chunks.source: Old people have weak bodies and need support.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a musical instrument. To which group of musical instruments does the above instrument belong? A: string instruments. The adungu (bow harp) makes sound with vibrating strings.
chunks.source: The adungu (bow harp) makes sound with vibrating strings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the strings will produce the highest pitch? A: a. Likely answer: a. The shortest string vibrates fastest and gives the highest pitch.
chunks.source: Likely answer: a. The shortest string vibrates fastest and gives the highest pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the strings will produce the lowest pitch? A: c. Likely answer: c. The longest string vibrates slowest and gives the lowest pitch.
chunks.source: Likely answer: c. The longest string vibrates slowest and gives the lowest pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: If you want string C to produce a higher pitched sound, what will you do? A: shorten (tighten) the string. A shorter, tighter string vibrates faster and sounds higher.
chunks.source: A shorter, tighter string vibrates faster and sounds higher.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disorder of the digestive system? A: constipation. Constipation and diarrhoea are disorders of the digestive system.
chunks.source: Constipation and diarrhoea are disorders of the digestive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another disorder of the digestive system? A: diarrhoea. Diarrhoea is the frequent passing of watery stool.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea is the frequent passing of watery stool.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease that attacks the digestive system? A: cholera. Cholera and dysentery attack the digestive system.
chunks.source: Cholera and dysentery attack the digestive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another disease that attacks the digestive system? A: dysentery. Dysentery causes bloody diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Dysentery causes bloody diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a craft material got from swamps? A: papyrus. Papyrus, clay and palm leaves are got from swamps for crafts.
chunks.source: Papyrus, clay and palm leaves are got from swamps for crafts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another craft material got from swamps? A: clay. Swamp clay is used for pottery and crafts.
chunks.source: Swamp clay is used for pottery and crafts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from getting craft materials from swamps, which of the following is another use of swamps to people? A: fishing. Swamps provide fish and are a source of water.
chunks.source: Swamps provide fish and are a source of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a source of food in your community? A: gardens. Gardens and markets are sources of food.
chunks.source: Gardens and markets are sources of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another source of food in your community? A: markets. Food is bought from markets and shops.
chunks.source: Food is bought from markets and shops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is food useful in the human body? Give one way? A: it gives the body energy. Food gives energy and builds the body.
chunks.source: Food gives energy and builds the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a place where germs are found? A: latrines. Germs live in latrines, rubbish pits and dirty places.
chunks.source: Germs live in latrines, rubbish pits and dirty places.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way in which germs can be spread? A: through the air. Germs spread through air, dirty water, food and insect vectors.
chunks.source: Germs spread through air, dirty water, food and insect vectors.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another way in which germs can be spread? A: through contaminated water (and food). Drinking dirty water spreads germs like cholera.
chunks.source: Drinking dirty water spreads germs like cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a type of immunity? A: natural immunity. Natural immunity is inborn; artificial immunity comes from vaccines.
chunks.source: Natural immunity is inborn; artificial immunity comes from vaccines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease controlled by immunizing using DPT vaccine? A: diphtheria. DPT protects against diphtheria, whooping cough (pertussis) and tetanus.
chunks.source: DPT protects against diphtheria, whooping cough (pertussis) and tetanus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another disease controlled by immunizing using DPT vaccine? A: tetanus. Tetanus causes painful muscle stiffness.
chunks.source: Tetanus causes painful muscle stiffness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a parasite worm (tapeworm). Name part labeled H: ___. A: hooks. The tapeworm's head (scolex) has hooks for gripping the intestines.
chunks.source: The tapeworm's head (scolex) has hooks for gripping the intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Germination, burning, melting and evaporation are common changes in the environment. Which of the above changes is a biological change? A: germination. Germination involves a living seed growing, so it is biological.
chunks.source: Germination involves a living seed growing, so it is biological.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an of the above changes that produces a new substance? A: burning. Burning and germination form new substances; melting and evaporation do not.
chunks.source: Burning and germination form new substances; melting and evaporation do not.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another of the above changes that produces a new substance? A: germination. A seedling is a new substance formed from the seed.
chunks.source: A seedling is a new substance formed from the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which first aid is administered by applying cold water on the affected part? A: burns (and scalds). Cold water cools a burn and stops it going deeper.
chunks.source: Cold water cools a burn and stops it going deeper.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the use of cotton wool in first aid management? A: cleaning wounds. Cotton wool wipes dirt from wounds gently.
chunks.source: Cotton wool wipes dirt from wounds gently.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the use of a bandage in first aid management? A: covering (and tying) wounds. A bandage covers wounds and holds dressings in place.
chunks.source: A bandage covers wounds and holds dressings in place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides water, which of the following is another item used in cleaning our feet? A: soap. Soap removes dirt and germs from the feet.
chunks.source: Soap removes dirt and germs from the feet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the element of weather suitable for removing moisture from harvested cereals? A: sunshine (heat). The sun's heat dries harvested cereals.
chunks.source: The sun's heat dries harvested cereals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does the bird with the beak below feed on? A: flesh (meat). The strong hooked beak is for tearing flesh; such birds are birds of prey.
chunks.source: The strong hooked beak is for tearing flesh; such birds are birds of prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a vaccine given to infants at the age of six weeks? A: DPT. At six weeks babies receive DPT and polio vaccines.
chunks.source: At six weeks babies receive DPT and polio vaccines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A solid block of mass 24g was dropped in an overflow can and displaces 12cm3 of water into a measuring cylinder. Find the density of the solid block: ___. A: 2 g/cm3. Density = mass / volume = 24g / 12cm3 = 2 g/cm3.
chunks.source: Density = mass / volume = 24g / 12cm3 = 2 g/cm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which blood vessel transports deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs? A: pulmonary artery. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation.
chunks.source: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of controlling poultry vices on a farm? A: debeaking. Debeaking stops birds pecking each other; enough space and feed also help.
chunks.source: Debeaking stops birds pecking each other; enough space and feed also help.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a danger of electricity at home? A: electric shock. Touching naked wires can shock or even kill a person.
chunks.source: Touching naked wires can shock or even kill a person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Use the diagram of a tape worm. Name part marked K: ___. A: head (scolex). The scolex (head) has hooks and suckers for attaching to the intestines.
chunks.source: The scolex (head) has hooks and suckers for attaching to the intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are snakes similar to weaver birds in the way they reproduce? A: both lay eggs. Snakes and weaver birds reproduce by laying eggs.
chunks.source: Snakes and weaver birds reproduce by laying eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from decomposition, how else can soil be formed? A: by weathering of rocks. Rocks break down into small particles that form soil.
chunks.source: Rocks break down into small particles that form soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a place where the soil profile can be seen properly? A: in a deep pit. The soil layers are clearly visible on the walls of a deep pit.
chunks.source: The soil layers are clearly visible on the walls of a deep pit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of soil used in filtration of water? A: sandy soil. Water passes through sand, leaving dirt behind.
chunks.source: Water passes through sand, leaving dirt behind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is wax important in the auditory canal? A: it traps dust and germs. Ear wax catches dust and germs before they reach the ear drum.
chunks.source: Ear wax catches dust and germs before they reach the ear drum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which property of air enables a P.6 child to drink soda from a bottle using a straw? A: air exerts pressure. Sucking removes air from the straw and air pressure pushes the soda up.
chunks.source: Sucking removes air from the straw and air pressure pushes the soda up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one sign of crop damage by pests: ___. A: holes in leaves. Pests chew leaves leaving holes, and cut stems.
chunks.source: Pests chew leaves leaving holes, and cut stems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way you can separate beans from bean husks? A: winnowing. Wind blows away the light husks while heavy beans fall down.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light husks while heavy beans fall down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way you can maintain the normal functioning of your respiratory system? A: avoid smoking. Smoke damages the lungs; exercise keeps them strong.
chunks.source: Smoke damages the lungs; exercise keeps them strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is distilled water not good for drinking? A: because it lacks mineral salts. Distillation removes the useful mineral salts water should contain.
chunks.source: Distillation removes the useful mineral salts water should contain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the role of the liver during digestion? A: it produces bile. Bile breaks large fat droplets into small ones.
chunks.source: Bile breaks large fat droplets into small ones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of caring for sheep? A: deworming them regularly. Deworming, shelter and dipping keep sheep healthy.
chunks.source: Deworming, shelter and dipping keep sheep healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from sun drying, which of the following is another local method of food preservation? A: salting. Salting, smoking and frying are local preservation methods.
chunks.source: Salting, smoking and frying are local preservation methods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from sun drying, which of the following is another local method of food preservation? A: smoking. Smoking removes water so germs cannot grow.
chunks.source: Smoking removes water so germs cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a housefly. Give the role of part Q to the insect: ___. A: breathing (gaseous exchange through spiracles). Part Q (spiracles on the abdomen) lets air in and out for breathing.
chunks.source: Part Q (spiracles on the abdomen) lets air in and out for breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the role of part P to the insect? A: flying. Part P (the wing) is used for flight.
chunks.source: Part P (the wing) is used for flight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are crop pests? A: organisms that destroy crops. Pests like locusts and weevils damage growing crops.
chunks.source: Pests like locusts and weevils damage growing crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of crop pests in the garden? A: locusts. Locusts, weevils and caterpillars are crop pests.
chunks.source: Locusts, weevils and caterpillars are crop pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another example of crop pests in the garden? A: weevils. Weevils attack stored and growing crops.
chunks.source: Weevils attack stored and growing crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one way of controlling garden crop pests: ___. A: spraying with pesticides. Pesticides kill crop pests.
chunks.source: Pesticides kill crop pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease of the human teeth? A: tooth decay. Tooth decay is a disease that makes holes in teeth.
chunks.source: Tooth decay is a disease that makes holes in teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disorder of the human teeth? A: misaligned teeth. Likely answer: misaligned teeth. (Best-effort; the booklet gives no key.)
chunks.source: Likely answer: misaligned teeth. (Best-effort; the booklet gives no key.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do you prevent the teeth disease identified above? Give one way? A: brushing teeth regularly. Brushing removes food remains that cause decay.
chunks.source: Brushing removes food remains that cause decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do you prevent the teeth disease identified above? Give another way? A: avoiding sugary foods. Sugar feeds the germs that rot teeth.
chunks.source: Sugar feeds the germs that rot teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows the female reproductive organ. Name the part marked X: ___. A: ovary. The ovary produces eggs (ova).
chunks.source: The ovary produces eggs (ova).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the part marked Y? A: vagina (birth canal). The vagina is the passage through which the baby is born.
chunks.source: The vagina is the passage through which the baby is born.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By use of letter N, show the part where fertilization takes place. Fertilization takes place in the ___. A: fallopian tube (oviduct). The egg meets the sperm in the fallopian tube.
chunks.source: The egg meets the sperm in the fallopian tube.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease which affects the above organ? A: gonorrhoea. Gonorrhoea and syphilis attack the reproductive system.
chunks.source: Gonorrhoea and syphilis attack the reproductive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write AIDS in full: ___. A: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome. AIDS is the disease caused by HIV.
chunks.source: AIDS is the disease caused by HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What germ causes AIDS among people? A: virus (HIV). The Human Immunodeficiency Virus causes AIDS.
chunks.source: The Human Immunodeficiency Virus causes AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: As a pupil in Primary Six, how can you avoid getting AIDS? A: by abstaining from sex. Abstinence keeps pupils safe from HIV.
chunks.source: Abstinence keeps pupils safe from HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one PIASCY message that can protect school going children from contracting HIV/AIDS: ___. A: Abstain from sex. Abstinence messages protect school children from HIV.
chunks.source: Abstinence messages protect school children from HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides proteins, which of the following is another food value? A: carbohydrates. Carbohydrates, vitamins, fats and minerals are other food values.
chunks.source: Carbohydrates, vitamins, fats and minerals are other food values.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one effect of poor nutrition to infants: ___. A: stunted growth. Poorly fed infants do not grow well.
chunks.source: Poorly fed infants do not grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write another effect of poor nutrition to infants: ___. A: kwashiorkor. Lack of protein causes kwashiorkor with a swollen belly.
chunks.source: Lack of protein causes kwashiorkor with a swollen belly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a thermometer. Name the kind of thermometer shown above: ___. A: maximum and minimum thermometer. It records the highest and lowest temperatures of the day.
chunks.source: It records the highest and lowest temperatures of the day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from mercury, which of the following is another liquid used in the above thermometer? A: alcohol. Alcohol is also used in thermometers as it expands with heat.
chunks.source: Alcohol is also used in thermometers as it expands with heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides floods, which of the following is a natural change that can displace people? A: drought. Drought, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions displace people.
chunks.source: Drought, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions displace people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides floods, which of the following is another natural change that can displace people? A: earthquakes. Earthquakes destroy homes, forcing people to move.
chunks.source: Earthquakes destroy homes, forcing people to move.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from displacing people, write one other effect of natural changes: ___. A: they destroy crops and property. Floods and droughts destroy farms and houses.
chunks.source: Floods and droughts destroy farms and houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a fish. Which organ of the fish is protected by structure marked H? A: gills. The operculum (H) covers and protects the gills.
chunks.source: The operculum (H) covers and protects the gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the part marked L? A: dorsal fin. The dorsal fin is on the back of the fish.
chunks.source: The dorsal fin is on the back of the fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides paraffin, which of the following is a fuel used in our homes? A: firewood. Firewood and charcoal are common home fuels.
chunks.source: Firewood and charcoal are common home fuels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides paraffin, which of the following is another fuel used in our homes? A: charcoal. Charcoal is burnt in stoves for cooking.
chunks.source: Charcoal is burnt in stoves for cooking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do bees swarm? Give one reason? A: overcrowding in the hive. Likely answer: overcrowding. (Best-effort; the booklet gives no key.)
chunks.source: Likely answer: overcrowding. (Best-effort; the booklet gives no key.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do bees swarm? Give another reason? A: emergence of a new queen. Likely answer: when a new queen emerges, part of the colony leaves with the old queen. (Best-effort.)
chunks.source: Likely answer: when a new queen emerges, part of the colony leaves with the old queen. (Best-effort.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can milk be preserved? A: by boiling (and refrigeration). Boiling kills germs in milk so it keeps longer.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs in milk so it keeps longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a product got from milk? A: ghee. Ghee, butter, yoghurt and cheese are made from milk.
chunks.source: Ghee, butter, yoghurt and cheese are made from milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another product got from milk? A: yoghurt. Milk is fermented to make yoghurt.
chunks.source: Milk is fermented to make yoghurt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from a cow, which of the following is another animal that gives milk? A: goat. Goats also give milk for drinking.
chunks.source: Goats also give milk for drinking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a component of soil that can also be used by animals for breathing? A: Air. Soil has tiny air spaces between its particles, and soil animals such as earthworms breathe this air.
chunks.source: Soil has tiny air spaces between its particles, and soil animals such as earthworms breathe this air.

chunks.subject: Science
