chunks.text: Q: Apart from the spiny ant eater, which of the following is another example of monotremes? A: Duck-billed platypus. The duck-billed platypus is a mammal that lays eggs, just like the spiny ant eater.
chunks.source: The duck-billed platypus is a mammal that lays eggs, just like the spiny ant eater.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mary collected water from the well. She filtered and later boiled it. What do you think she was going to use the water for? A: For drinking. Filtering and boiling remove dirt and kill germs, making water safe to drink.
chunks.source: Filtering and boiling remove dirt and kill germs, making water safe to drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Calculate the volume of the cuboid shown below (length 5mm, width 2mm, height 6mm): ___. A: 60 cubic millimetres (60mm3). Volume of a cuboid = length x width x height = 5 x 2 x 6 = 60mm3.
chunks.source: Volume of a cuboid = length x width x height = 5 x 2 x 6 = 60mm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a tadpole similar to a fish? A: Both breathe using gills. Tadpoles live in water and, like fish, take in dissolved oxygen through gills.
chunks.source: Tadpoles live in water and, like fish, take in dissolved oxygen through gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the stage in the life cycle of a bee that is able to swarm? A: Adult stage. Swarming is done by a group of adult bees that leave the hive with a queen to start a new colony.
chunks.source: Swarming is done by a group of adult bees that leave the hive with a queen to start a new colony.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A mammal is a warm-blooded vertebrate animal distinguished by the possession of fur or hair. Give any one example of such an animal: ___. A: Cow. A cow has hair on its body, gives birth to live calves and feeds them on milk.
chunks.source: A cow has hair on its body, gives birth to live calves and feeds them on milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does heat travel through solids? A: By conduction. In solids, heat moves from particle to particle without the particles themselves moving.
chunks.source: In solids, heat moves from particle to particle without the particles themselves moving.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cite the element of primary health care that may be used to control population growth: ___. A: Family planning. Family planning helps families choose the number of children they can care for.
chunks.source: Family planning helps families choose the number of children they can care for.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the gestation period of a doe (female rabbit)? A: About 30 days (one month). A doe carries her pregnancy for about a month before giving birth to bunnies.
chunks.source: A doe carries her pregnancy for about a month before giving birth to bunnies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The outer covering of the bean seed shown in the diagram is called the ___. A: Testa. The testa is the tough outer skin that protects the inside of the seed.
chunks.source: The testa is the tough outer skin that protects the inside of the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Communicable diseases are diseases that can be spread from one person to another. Give any one example: ___. A: Tuberculosis. Tuberculosis spreads through the air when an infected person coughs.
chunks.source: Tuberculosis spreads through the air when an infected person coughs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Honey is a product that apiary farmers regularly harvest from bee hives and sell or eat. State the food value we get from eating honey: ___. A: Energy. Honey is rich in sugars, which the body burns to release energy.
chunks.source: Honey is rich in sugars, which the body burns to release energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a biological change that takes place in animals? A: Growth. Growth is a biological change because a young animal develops into an adult and cannot change back.
chunks.source: Growth is a biological change because a young animal develops into an adult and cannot change back.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the season in which cereal crop farmers are advised to harvest their crops? A: Dry season. Crops harvested in the dry season stay dry and do not rot.
chunks.source: Crops harvested in the dry season stay dry and do not rot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cereal crop farmers carry out many activities during the 'caring stage'. Name any one of them: ___. A: Weeding. Weeding removes unwanted plants that compete with the crops for nutrients.
chunks.source: Weeding removes unwanted plants that compete with the crops for nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another activity cereal crop farmers carry out during the 'caring stage'? A: Thinning. Thinning removes extra seedlings so the remaining crops get enough space and nutrients.
chunks.source: Thinning removes extra seedlings so the remaining crops get enough space and nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Accidents are sudden happenings that cause harm to the body. Outline any one example of accidents: ___. A: Road accident. A road accident happens suddenly and can injure people.
chunks.source: A road accident happens suddenly and can injure people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Outline another example of accidents: ___. A: Burns. Burns from fire or hot objects happen suddenly and injure the body.
chunks.source: Burns from fire or hot objects happen suddenly and injure the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the displacement method. Name the part marked X: ___. A: Spout. The spout is the outlet of the displacement can through which displaced water flows into the measuring cylinder.
chunks.source: The spout is the outlet of the displacement can through which displaced water flows into the measuring cylinder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the part marked Q in the diagram? A: Thread. The thread is tied to the irregular object so it can be lowered into the water.
chunks.source: The thread is tied to the irregular object so it can be lowered into the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a common example of an irregular object whose volume can be found in the same way? A: Stone. A stone has no regular shape, so its volume is found by the displacement method.
chunks.source: A stone has no regular shape, so its volume is found by the displacement method.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the volume of the displaced water collected in cylinder W? A: 20cc (20cm3). The displaced water rose to the 20cc mark in the measuring cylinder, so its volume is 20cc.
chunks.source: The displaced water rose to the 20cc mark in the measuring cylinder, so its volume is 20cc.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from running water, which of the following is another agent of soil erosion? A: Wind. Strong wind blows away loose top soil, especially where there is no plant cover.
chunks.source: Strong wind blows away loose top soil, especially where there is no plant cover.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another agent of soil erosion apart from running water? A: Animals. Animals walking and grazing loosen the soil, making it easy to wash away.
chunks.source: Animals walking and grazing loosen the soil, making it easy to wash away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which body system is responsible for the breakage of food into soluble substances? A: Digestive system. The digestive system breaks food into tiny soluble particles the body can absorb.
chunks.source: The digestive system breaks food into tiny soluble particles the body can absorb.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from teeth, which of the following is another organ in the digestive system? A: Stomach. The stomach churns food and mixes it with digestive juices.
chunks.source: The stomach churns food and mixes it with digestive juices.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another organ in the digestive system apart from teeth? A: Small intestine. Digested food is absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.
chunks.source: Digested food is absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Steps taken when preparing ORS locally are listed above. Identify the solute: ___. A: Sugar and salt. The solute is the substance that dissolves; here both sugar and salt dissolve in the water.
chunks.source: The solute is the substance that dissolves; here both sugar and salt dissolve in the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the solvent from the ORS experiment? A: Water. The solvent is the liquid in which other substances dissolve.
chunks.source: The solvent is the liquid in which other substances dissolve.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides free range system, which of the following is a method of keeping poultry birds? A: Deep litter system. In the deep litter system birds move freely on a floor covered with litter.
chunks.source: In the deep litter system birds move freely on a floor covered with litter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another method of keeping poultry birds besides free range system? A: Battery cage system. In the battery cage system birds are kept in small individual cages.
chunks.source: In the battery cage system birds are kept in small individual cages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a third method of keeping poultry birds besides free range system? A: Fold system. In the fold system a small movable house is shifted to fresh ground daily.
chunks.source: In the fold system a small movable house is shifted to fresh ground daily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the flowering plant. Name the part labeled X: ___. A: Shoot system. The shoot system is made up of all the parts of the plant above the ground.
chunks.source: The shoot system is made up of all the parts of the plant above the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the part labeled Y in the diagram? A: Root system. The root system is made up of all the roots below the ground.
chunks.source: The root system is made up of all the roots below the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the by-product that part K (the leaf) produces during photosynthesis? A: Oxygen. During photosynthesis leaves take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen as a by-product.
chunks.source: During photosynthesis leaves take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen as a by-product.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does yeast reproduce? A: By budding. In budding, a small outgrowth (bud) forms on the yeast cell, grows and breaks off.
chunks.source: In budding, a small outgrowth (bud) forms on the yeast cell, grows and breaks off.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides yeast, which of the following is another example of fungi? A: Mushroom. A mushroom is a large fungus that grows on decaying matter.
chunks.source: A mushroom is a large fungus that grows on decaying matter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another example of fungi besides yeast? A: Mould. Mould is a fungus that grows on stale food such as bread.
chunks.source: Mould is a fungus that grows on stale food such as bread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from an ostrich, which of the following is another bird which cannot fly? A: Penguin. Penguins have flippers for swimming instead of wings for flying.
chunks.source: Penguins have flippers for swimming instead of wings for flying.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another bird which cannot fly apart from an ostrich? A: Emu. The emu is a large flightless bird like the ostrich.
chunks.source: The emu is a large flightless bird like the ostrich.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an use of plants to animals? A: Plants provide food to animals. Herbivores feed directly on plants for their food.
chunks.source: Herbivores feed directly on plants for their food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another use of plants to animals? A: Plants provide shelter to animals. Trees give shade and hiding places to wild and domestic animals.
chunks.source: Trees give shade and hiding places to wild and domestic animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an animal fibre that can be got from sheep and goats? A: Wool. Sheep are sheared to get wool, a soft animal fibre.
chunks.source: Sheep are sheared to get wool, a soft animal fibre.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Goat farmers in Uganda usually find it hard when their goats die of diseases. Name any one disease that can kill goats: ___. A: Anthrax. Anthrax is a deadly disease that kills goats and other livestock quickly.
chunks.source: Anthrax is a deadly disease that kills goats and other livestock quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way goat farmers in Uganda can protect their goats against the disease you have named above? A: By vaccinating the goats regularly. Vaccination builds immunity so the goats resist the disease.
chunks.source: Vaccination builds immunity so the goats resist the disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: From which external part of a goat does the goat farmer get milk? A: Udder. Milk is drawn from the udder of a female goat.
chunks.source: Milk is drawn from the udder of a female goat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a common fuel used in the tool above? A: Charcoal. Burning charcoal inside the iron produces the heat for ironing.
chunks.source: Burning charcoal inside the iron produces the heat for ironing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: People are encouraged to wash hands after visiting the latrine. Write down one material we use to wash hands which is in solid state: ___. A: Soap. Soap is a solid that we rub on our hands with water.
chunks.source: Soap is a solid that we rub on our hands with water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one material we use to wash hands which is in liquid state: ___. A: Water. Water is the liquid we use to rinse our hands.
chunks.source: Water is the liquid we use to rinse our hands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from washing and bathing, which of the following is another one activity that school children do to keep clean? A: Brushing their teeth. Brushing removes food remains and keeps the mouth clean and fresh.
chunks.source: Brushing removes food remains and keeps the mouth clean and fresh.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of cattle that is useful in the production of yoghurt? A: Dairy cattle. Yoghurt is made from milk, and dairy cattle are kept for milk production.
chunks.source: Yoghurt is made from milk, and dairy cattle are kept for milk production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from insects, which of the following is another group of arthropods? A: Arachnids. Arachnids such as spiders and ticks have eight legs and two body parts.
chunks.source: Arachnids such as spiders and ticks have eight legs and two body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the process through which water turns into ice? A: Freezing. When water is cooled below 0C, it freezes into ice.
chunks.source: When water is cooled below 0C, it freezes into ice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the component of soil formed as a result of decomposition? A: Humus. Humus is the dark material formed when dead plants and animals rot.
chunks.source: Humus is the dark material formed when dead plants and animals rot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the lungs, what other organ does a frog use for breathing? A: Skin. A frog also breathes through its moist skin when in water.
chunks.source: A frog also breathes through its moist skin when in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the part of a tooth that contains sensory nerves? A: Pulp. The pulp is the soft centre of the tooth with nerves and blood vessels.
chunks.source: The pulp is the soft centre of the tooth with nerves and blood vessels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down the process that helps in the circulation of air in the house: ___. A: Ventilation. Ventilation is the free movement of fresh air in and out of a house.
chunks.source: Ventilation is the free movement of fresh air in and out of a house.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a form of energy which is produced when a drum is hit? A: Sound energy. Hitting the drum makes it vibrate, producing sound.
chunks.source: Hitting the drum makes it vibrate, producing sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of thermometer is used to measure both the highest and lowest temperatures of the day? A: Maximum and minimum thermometer. This special thermometer records the day's highest and lowest temperatures.
chunks.source: This special thermometer records the day's highest and lowest temperatures.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a factor which promotes quick breeding of bacteria? A: Warmth. Bacteria multiply fastest in warm conditions.
chunks.source: Bacteria multiply fastest in warm conditions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the component of air that keeps candle A burning? A: Oxygen. Oxygen supports burning; without it the candle flame goes out.
chunks.source: Oxygen supports burning; without it the candle flame goes out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The gas produced at point Z is carbon dioxide. Which plant process makes use of this gas? A: Photosynthesis. Plants take in carbon dioxide to make food during photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants take in carbon dioxide to make food during photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of controlling soil erosion in hilly areas? A: By terracing the hillsides. Terraces are steps cut across slopes that slow down running water.
chunks.source: Terraces are steps cut across slopes that slow down running water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of change occurs when a mango fruit rots? A: Chemical change. Rotting forms new substances and cannot be reversed, so it is a chemical change.
chunks.source: Rotting forms new substances and cannot be reversed, so it is a chemical change.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one sign of Kwashiorkor in children: ___. A: Swollen belly. Kwashiorkor makes the belly swell and the hair turn brownish.
chunks.source: Kwashiorkor makes the belly swell and the hair turn brownish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the molar tooth. Name the part marked A: ___. A: Enamel. The enamel is the hard white outer covering of the crown.
chunks.source: The enamel is the hard white outer covering of the crown.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the part marked C in the diagram? A: Dentine. Dentine is the layer just beneath the enamel.
chunks.source: Dentine is the layer just beneath the enamel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an activity that a farmer does before planting seeds? A: Clearing the land. Bushes and weeds must be cleared before seeds are planted.
chunks.source: Bushes and weeds must be cleared before seeds are planted.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another activity that a farmer does before planting seeds? A: Ploughing (digging) the land. Digging loosens the soil so seeds can be planted easily.
chunks.source: Digging loosens the soil so seeds can be planted easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of chicken kept for egg production? A: Layers. Layers are chickens specially kept for laying eggs.
chunks.source: Layers are chickens specially kept for laying eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of chicken kept for meat production? A: Broilers. Broilers grow very fast and are kept for meat.
chunks.source: Broilers grow very fast and are kept for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one exotic breed of chicken kept for egg production: ___. A: White Leghorn. The White Leghorn is a famous exotic layer breed.
chunks.source: The White Leghorn is a famous exotic layer breed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write another exotic breed of chicken kept for egg production: ___. A: Rhode Island Red. Rhode Island Red is another exotic breed good for laying eggs.
chunks.source: Rhode Island Red is another exotic breed good for laying eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one example of a diarrhoeal disease in people: ___. A: Cholera. Cholera causes severe diarrhoea and spreads through dirty water.
chunks.source: Cholera causes severe diarrhoea and spreads through dirty water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of protecting yourself from getting diarrhoeal diseases? A: By drinking boiled water. Boiling kills the germs that cause diarrhoeal diseases.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs that cause diarrhoeal diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another way of protecting yourself from getting diarrhoeal diseases? A: By washing hands before eating. Clean hands stop germs from entering food.
chunks.source: Clean hands stop germs from entering food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a domestic animal that is kept only for meat production and neither for milk nor for its skin? A: Pig. Pigs are reared mainly for pork.
chunks.source: Pigs are reared mainly for pork.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do you care for such animals? Give one way.? A: By feeding them well. Well-fed pigs grow fast and stay healthy.
chunks.source: Well-fed pigs grow fast and stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease spread by mosquitoes to people? A: Malaria. Female anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria.
chunks.source: Female anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease spread by house flies to people? A: Cholera. Houseflies carry germs from faeces to food, spreading cholera.
chunks.source: Houseflies carry germs from faeces to food, spreading cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the disease spread by a rabid dog to people? A: Rabies. A bite from a rabid dog transmits the deadly rabies virus.
chunks.source: A bite from a rabid dog transmits the deadly rabies virus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a factor that can increase the rate of transpiration? A: High temperature. Heat makes water evaporate faster from the leaves.
chunks.source: Heat makes water evaporate faster from the leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another factor that can increase the rate of transpiration? A: Wind. Wind carries away water vapour, so leaves lose more water.
chunks.source: Wind carries away water vapour, so leaves lose more water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the kettle and cold-water bottle. What do the arrows labelled with letter Y represent? A: Heat from the fire. The arrows show heat rising from the fire to boil the water in the kettle.
chunks.source: The arrows show heat rising from the fire to boil the water in the kettle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the physical process taking place at Z? A: Condensation. At Z, water vapour cools on the cold bottle and turns back into liquid.
chunks.source: At Z, water vapour cools on the cold bottle and turns back into liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the natural process represented by the above diagram? A: Water cycle. The diagram models evaporation, condensation and precipitation like in nature.
chunks.source: The diagram models evaporation, condensation and precipitation like in nature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from B.C.G vaccine, which of the following is an other vaccine administered to babies? A: Polio vaccine. Babies receive polio vaccine to protect them against polio.
chunks.source: Babies receive polio vaccine to protect them against polio.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another vaccine administered to babies apart from B.C.G? A: DPT vaccine. DPT protects babies against diphtheria, whooping cough and tetanus.
chunks.source: DPT protects babies against diphtheria, whooping cough and tetanus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is B.C.G vaccine administered to babies? A: To protect them against tuberculosis. BCG gives babies immunity against TB.
chunks.source: BCG gives babies immunity against TB.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a feature found on a child health card? A: The child's immunization record. The card records every vaccine the child receives.
chunks.source: The card records every vaccine the child receives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another feature found on a child health card? A: The child's growth (weight) chart. The card shows the child's weight over time to track growth.
chunks.source: The card shows the child's weight over time to track growth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a component of blood? A: Red blood cells. Red blood cells carry oxygen around the body.
chunks.source: Red blood cells carry oxygen around the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another component of blood? A: White blood cells. White blood cells fight disease germs in the body.
chunks.source: White blood cells fight disease germs in the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the digestive juice produced by the pancreas? A: Pancreatic juice. The pancreas releases pancreatic juice into the small intestine.
chunks.source: The pancreas releases pancreatic juice into the small intestine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the digestive juice produced by the stomach? A: Gastric juice. The stomach walls produce gastric juice to digest food.
chunks.source: The stomach walls produce gastric juice to digest food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where does absorption of digested food take place in the alimentary canal? A: In the small intestine (ileum). Digested food passes into the blood through the walls of the ileum.
chunks.source: Digested food passes into the blood through the walls of the ileum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram above shows some food being cooked. Identify the fuel being used to cook this food: ___. A: Firewood. The fire under the cooking pots is made from firewood.
chunks.source: The fire under the cooking pots is made from firewood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which physical process is shown at X (the rising vapour above the food)? A: Evaporation. Heat changes the water in the food into steam, which rises.
chunks.source: Heat changes the water in the food into steam, which rises.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of soil suitable for making glasses? A: Sand soil. Glass is made from silica, which is found in sand soil.
chunks.source: Glass is made from silica, which is found in sand soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To what group of flowering plants does sorghum belong? A: Monocotyledonous plants (monocots). Sorghum is a cereal with one seed leaf, like maize and rice.
chunks.source: Sorghum is a cereal with one seed leaf, like maize and rice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The outer covering of the bean seed shown in the diagram is called the ___. A: Testa. The testa is the protective outer skin of the seed.
chunks.source: The testa is the protective outer skin of the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one danger a weaning child may get: ___. A: Malnutrition (kwashiorkor). Children weaned onto poor foods may suffer protein deficiency.
chunks.source: Children weaned onto poor foods may suffer protein deficiency.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides chicken, which of the following is another type of poultry kept in Uganda? A: Ducks. Ducks are common poultry birds reared alongside chickens.
chunks.source: Ducks are common poultry birds reared alongside chickens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a recommended method of catching fish in Uganda? A: Net fishing. Fishing nets are the approved way of catching mature fish.
chunks.source: Fishing nets are the approved way of catching mature fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an activity that can be carried out to prevent the spread of diarrhoeal diseases at home? A: Boiling drinking water. Boiled water is germ-free and safe to drink.
chunks.source: Boiled water is germ-free and safe to drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a foodstuff that is prepared by peeling? A: Matooke. Matooke must be peeled before it is cooked.
chunks.source: Matooke must be peeled before it is cooked.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are reptiles and fish similar in their way of reproduction? A: Both lay eggs. Reptiles and fish reproduce by laying eggs that hatch outside the body.
chunks.source: Reptiles and fish reproduce by laying eggs that hatch outside the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which state of matter does heat travel by conduction? A: Solid state. Conduction needs closely packed particles, found in solids.
chunks.source: Conduction needs closely packed particles, found in solids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an activity done by a community to protect water sources from contamination? A: Fencing the water source. A fence keeps animals and people from dirtying the water source.
chunks.source: A fence keeps animals and people from dirtying the water source.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a baby acquire natural immunity? A: Through breastfeeding (mother's milk). A mother's first milk gives the baby ready-made protection against diseases.
chunks.source: A mother's first milk gives the baby ready-made protection against diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a place where a soil profile can be properly seen or observed by a class? A: In a deep pit. The layers of soil are clearly visible on the walls of a deep pit.
chunks.source: The layers of soil are clearly visible on the walls of a deep pit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease that people can mistake for being HIV/AIDS? A: Tuberculosis. TB causes weight loss and weakness just like AIDS.
chunks.source: TB causes weight loss and weakness just like AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a cassava plant propagated? A: By planting stem cuttings. Pieces of cassava stem are buried in the soil to grow new plants.
chunks.source: Pieces of cassava stem are buried in the soil to grow new plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which group of fruits does the fruit shown in the diagram belong? A: Simple fruits. The fruit develops from a single flower ovary, making it a simple fruit.
chunks.source: The fruit develops from a single flower ovary, making it a simple fruit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a habit that promotes oral health? A: Brushing teeth regularly. Regular brushing removes food remains and prevents tooth decay.
chunks.source: Regular brushing removes food remains and prevents tooth decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an use of electricity at school? A: For lighting classrooms. Electric lights brighten classrooms for reading.
chunks.source: Electric lights brighten classrooms for reading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of natural changes in the environment? A: Rainfall. Rainfall is a natural change that happens without people's control.
chunks.source: Rainfall is a natural change that happens without people's control.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease of the respiratory system? A: Tuberculosis. TB attacks the lungs, which are part of the respiratory system.
chunks.source: TB attacks the lungs, which are part of the respiratory system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the best way of preventing the bad effects of measles among infants in Uganda? A: Immunization (vaccination). The measles vaccine protects babies before they catch the disease.
chunks.source: The measles vaccine protects babies before they catch the disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of domestic animals? A: Cow. Cows are kept at home and cared for by people.
chunks.source: Cows are kept at home and cared for by people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another example of domestic animals? A: Goat. Goats are common domestic animals in Ugandan homes.
chunks.source: Goats are common domestic animals in Ugandan homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a characteristic of living things? A: They breathe. All living things take in air for respiration.
chunks.source: All living things take in air for respiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another characteristic of living things? A: They reproduce. Living things produce young ones of their own kind.
chunks.source: Living things produce young ones of their own kind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write P.H.C in full: ___. A: Primary Health Care. PHC stands for Primary Health Care.
chunks.source: PHC stands for Primary Health Care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a principle of P.H.C? A: Community participation. Communities must take part in planning their own health care.
chunks.source: Communities must take part in planning their own health care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an element of P.H.C? A: Immunization. Immunization protects communities against killer diseases.
chunks.source: Immunization protects communities against killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another element of P.H.C? A: Provision of safe water. Safe water prevents water-borne diseases in the community.
chunks.source: Safe water prevents water-borne diseases in the community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the blood vessels. Identify the blood vessel labelled P: ___. A: Artery. P has thick walls and a narrow lumen, which are features of an artery.
chunks.source: P has thick walls and a narrow lumen, which are features of an artery.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the blood vessel labelled Q? A: Vein. Q has valves and thin walls, which are features of a vein.
chunks.source: Q has valves and thin walls, which are features of a vein.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who breastfeeds a child/baby at home? A: The mother. Mothers feed their babies on breast milk.
chunks.source: Mothers feed their babies on breast milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a reason why people in Uganda keep cattle? A: For milk. Cattle provide milk for the family and for sale.
chunks.source: Cattle provide milk for the family and for sale.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a type of cattle? A: Dairy cattle. Dairy cattle are kept mainly for milk production.
chunks.source: Dairy cattle are kept mainly for milk production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another type of cattle? A: Beef cattle. Beef cattle are kept mainly for meat.
chunks.source: Beef cattle are kept mainly for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mark left dirty pond water to settle, then poured off the clear water as shown. What method of preparing clean water is shown above? A: Decantation. Decantation is pouring off the clear liquid after the dirt has settled.
chunks.source: Decantation is pouring off the clear liquid after the dirt has settled.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of making the water in Pot B safe for drinking? A: By boiling it. Boiling kills all the germs in the water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills all the germs in the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another way of making the water in Pot B safe for drinking? A: By filtering it. Filtering removes the remaining tiny dirt particles.
chunks.source: Filtering removes the remaining tiny dirt particles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an effect of heat on matter? A: It causes expansion. Heated matter expands and takes up more space.
chunks.source: Heated matter expands and takes up more space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the classification table. Identify the group of vertebrates marked X: ___. A: Cold-blooded vertebrates. X branches into fish, amphibians and reptiles, which are all cold-blooded.
chunks.source: X branches into fish, amphibians and reptiles, which are all cold-blooded.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the group of vertebrates marked Y? A: Warm-blooded vertebrates. Y branches into birds and mammals, which keep a constant body temperature.
chunks.source: Y branches into birds and mammals, which keep a constant body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the group of vertebrates marked S? A: Birds. S is the warm-blooded group with feathers that lay eggs.
chunks.source: S is the warm-blooded group with feathers that lay eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being vertebrates, which of the following is another similarity among groups of organisms labelled P, Q and R? A: They are all cold-blooded. Fish, amphibians and reptiles all have body temperatures that change with the environment.
chunks.source: Fish, amphibians and reptiles all have body temperatures that change with the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an intestinal worm in children? A: Tapeworm. Tapeworms live in the intestines and steal digested food.
chunks.source: Tapeworms live in the intestines and steal digested food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another intestinal worm in children? A: Roundworm. Roundworms are common intestinal worms in children.
chunks.source: Roundworms are common intestinal worms in children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What process is taking place at part labelled X (the pit)? A: Decomposition of faeces. In the pit, bacteria break down the faeces into harmless matter.
chunks.source: In the pit, bacteria break down the faeces into harmless matter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the experiment with the measuring cylinder. Identify part K: ___. A: Stone (an irregular object). K is the irregular object tied with a thread and immersed in water.
chunks.source: K is the irregular object tied with a thread and immersed in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Find the volume of K: ___. A: 22cm³ (37ml − 15ml). Volume = final level − initial level = 37ml − 15ml = 22ml = 22cm³. (Readings are approximate from the diagram.)
chunks.source: Volume = final level − initial level = 37ml − 15ml = 22ml = 22cm³. (Readings are approximate from the diagram.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Work out the density of K if its mass is 60g: ___. A: 2.7g/cm³. Density = mass ÷ volume = 60g ÷ 22cm³ ≈ 2.7g/cm³.
chunks.source: Density = mass ÷ volume = 60g ÷ 22cm³ ≈ 2.7g/cm³.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the mushroom. Name the part marked X: ___. A: Cap (pileus). The cap is the umbrella-like top of the mushroom.
chunks.source: The cap is the umbrella-like top of the mushroom.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the part marked Y in the diagram? A: Gills. The gills are the thin plates under the cap that produce spores.
chunks.source: The gills are the thin plates under the cap that produce spores.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the mushroom reproduce? A: By means of spores. The gills release tiny spores which grow into new mushrooms.
chunks.source: The gills release tiny spores which grow into new mushrooms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the water cycle. Name the process labelled B: ___. A: Evaporation. At B, heat from the sun changes water into vapour that rises.
chunks.source: At B, heat from the sun changes water into vapour that rises.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the process labelled D? A: Condensation. At D, water vapour cools high up and forms clouds.
chunks.source: At D, water vapour cools high up and forms clouds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a body organ that helps a P.6 child to taste food? A: Tongue. The tongue has taste buds that detect the taste of food.
chunks.source: The tongue has taste buds that detect the taste of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way in which water can be made safe for drinking at home? A: By boiling it. Boiling kills the germs in water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do farmers propagate Irish potatoes? A: By planting tubers. Irish potatoes are grown from the tubers themselves.
chunks.source: Irish potatoes are grown from the tubers themselves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the best way for preserving apples? A: Refrigeration. Cold storage slows down the rotting of fruits like apples.
chunks.source: Cold storage slows down the rotting of fruits like apples.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a danger of wind in the environment? A: It destroys crops and buildings. Strong wind blows down crops and damages houses.
chunks.source: Strong wind blows down crops and damages houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mr. Muwonge was advised by a doctor to eat more foods rich in iron. State the deficiency disease Mr. Muwonge was suffering from: ___. A: Anaemia. Lack of iron causes anaemia, a shortage of healthy red blood cells.
chunks.source: Lack of iron causes anaemia, a shortage of healthy red blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a musical drum. Name the domestic animal from which part A (the drum skin) is got: ___. A: Cow. Drum skins are made from the hide of a cow.
chunks.source: Drum skins are made from the hide of a cow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the first step in washing clothes? A: Sorting the clothes. Clothes are sorted by colour and dirtiness before washing.
chunks.source: Clothes are sorted by colour and dirtiness before washing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens to the volume of water when frozen? A: It increases. Water expands when it freezes into ice.
chunks.source: Water expands when it freezes into ice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an use of grasshoppers to people? A: They are eaten as food. Grasshoppers (nsenene) are a popular seasonal delicacy.
chunks.source: Grasshoppers (nsenene) are a popular seasonal delicacy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a method of harvesting cassava? A: By uprooting. Cassava roots are pulled out of the soil by uprooting the plant.
chunks.source: Cassava roots are pulled out of the soil by uprooting the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a type of chicken? A: Layers. Layers are chickens kept for egg production.
chunks.source: Layers are chickens kept for egg production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the component of soil that helps to make soil? A: Living organisms. Likely answer: living organisms such as bacteria and earthworms break down dead matter and rock particles, helping to form soil.
chunks.source: Likely answer: living organisms such as bacteria and earthworms break down dead matter and rock particles, helping to form soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one material used to make local salt: ___. A: Ash (from burnt plants). Local salt is traditionally made from plant ash.
chunks.source: Local salt is traditionally made from plant ash.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does heat travel through gases? A: By convection. In gases, heat moves with the rising warm currents.
chunks.source: In gases, heat moves with the rising warm currents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the tooth. Name the part labelled A: ___. A: Crown. The crown is the upper visible part of the tooth.
chunks.source: The crown is the upper visible part of the tooth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the male reproductive cell of a mammal? A: Sperm. The sperm is the male cell that fertilizes the egg.
chunks.source: The sperm is the male cell that fertilizes the egg.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one cause of the above poultry vice: ___. A: Overcrowding. Crowded birds get stressed and start pecking each other.
chunks.source: Crowded birds get stressed and start pecking each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down another cause of the above poultry vice: ___. A: Lack of enough food. Hungry birds peck at each other searching for food.
chunks.source: Hungry birds peck at each other searching for food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the flowering plant. From what part of the seed does part K (the root) develop? A: Radicle. The radicle is the first part of the embryo to grow out and form the root.
chunks.source: The radicle is the first part of the embryo to grow out and form the root.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of flowering plant is shown above? A: Dicotyledonous plant (dicot). The plant has a taproot system, which is a feature of dicots.
chunks.source: The plant has a taproot system, which is a feature of dicots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a reason for your answer in (b) above? A: It has a taproot system. Taproots grow from dicot seeds, unlike the fibrous roots of monocots.
chunks.source: Taproots grow from dicot seeds, unlike the fibrous roots of monocots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from ordinary pit latrines, write down any other one type of latrine: ___. A: VIP latrine. A VIP latrine has a vent pipe that removes smell and flies.
chunks.source: A VIP latrine has a vent pipe that removes smell and flies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of caring for an ordinary pit latrine? A: By cleaning it regularly. Regular cleaning keeps the latrine hygienic.
chunks.source: Regular cleaning keeps the latrine hygienic.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease associated with poor use of latrines? A: Cholera. Faeces near homes spread cholera germs to food and water.
chunks.source: Faeces near homes spread cholera germs to food and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a set of teeth in humans? A: Milk teeth (deciduous teeth). Milk teeth are the first set that falls out in childhood.
chunks.source: Milk teeth are the first set that falls out in childhood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the other set of teeth in humans? A: Permanent teeth. Permanent teeth replace milk teeth and last into adulthood.
chunks.source: Permanent teeth replace milk teeth and last into adulthood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which mineral salt is responsible for the development of healthy teeth? A: Calcium. Calcium hardens the teeth and bones.
chunks.source: Calcium hardens the teeth and bones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a method of separating mixtures. Name the method used above: ___. A: Filtration. Passing pond water through filter paper to trap dirt is filtration.
chunks.source: Passing pond water through filter paper to trap dirt is filtration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an impurity removed by using the above method? A: Mud (dirt particles). The filter paper traps mud and sand from the pond water.
chunks.source: The filter paper traps mud and sand from the pond water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The solid material trapped on the filter paper is called the ___. A: Residue. The residue is the solid left behind on the filter paper.
chunks.source: The residue is the solid left behind on the filter paper.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way in which bacteria are harmful:? A: They cause diseases. Disease-causing bacteria make people and animals sick.
chunks.source: Disease-causing bacteria make people and animals sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from wind, which of the following is another agent of seed dispersal? A: Animals. Animals carry seeds on their fur or in their droppings.
chunks.source: Animals carry seeds on their fur or in their droppings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one characteristic of seeds dispersed by wind: ___. A: They are light. Light seeds are easily carried away by wind.
chunks.source: Light seeds are easily carried away by wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a factor that affects the pitch of sound? A: Length of the vibrating object. Shorter strings vibrate faster and produce a higher pitch.
chunks.source: Shorter strings vibrate faster and produce a higher pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one animal that uses echoes to locate its food: ___. A: Bat. Bats use echoes to find insects in the dark.
chunks.source: Bats use echoes to find insects in the dark.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write the deficiency disease associated with lack of enough carbohydrates: ___. A: Marasmus. Without enough carbohydrates the body wastes away (marasmus).
chunks.source: Without enough carbohydrates the body wastes away (marasmus).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write the deficiency disease associated with lack of enough proteins: ___. A: Kwashiorkor. Without enough proteins children develop kwashiorkor.
chunks.source: Without enough proteins children develop kwashiorkor.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the human body organs. Name the body organ represented by Y: ___. A: Lungs. Y points to the lungs in the chest.
chunks.source: Y points to the lungs in the chest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the body organ represented by X? A: Stomach. X points to the stomach in the abdomen.
chunks.source: X points to the stomach in the abdomen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of honey bees is usually seen around flower gardens? A: Worker bees. Worker bees fly from flower to flower collecting nectar.
chunks.source: Worker bees fly from flower to flower collecting nectar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a thing bees get from flowers? A: Nectar. Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers to make honey.
chunks.source: Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers to make honey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another thing bees get from flowers? A: Pollen. Bees also collect pollen, which they use as food.
chunks.source: Bees also collect pollen, which they use as food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an importance of bees to flowering plants? A: They help in pollination. As bees move, they carry pollen from flower to flower.
chunks.source: As bees move, they carry pollen from flower to flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows heat transfer through matter. Name the circular movement marked N: ___. A: Convection current. The circular movement of the heated water is a convection current.
chunks.source: The circular movement of the heated water is a convection current.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the source of heat used above? A: Burning charcoal. The charcoal stove supplies the heat.
chunks.source: The charcoal stove supplies the heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the part of the charcoal stove that takes out warm air? A: Air holes (vents). Likely answer: the air holes let warm air and smoke escape from the stove.
chunks.source: Likely answer: the air holes let warm air and smoke escape from the stove.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one element of weather that favours maize harvesting: ___. A: Sunshine. Sunshine dries the maize for safe harvesting and storage.
chunks.source: Sunshine dries the maize for safe harvesting and storage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the element of weather given in (a) above, which of the following is another one element of weather that favours farmers' activities? A: Rainfall. Rainfall provides the water crops need to grow.
chunks.source: Rainfall provides the water crops need to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another element of weather that favours farmers' activities? A: Wind. Wind helps in winnowing harvested grains.
chunks.source: Wind helps in winnowing harvested grains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the young one of a cat? A: Kitten. A baby cat is called a kitten.
chunks.source: A baby cat is called a kitten.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way can heat be useful to man? A: For cooking food. Heat from fire cooks our food.
chunks.source: Heat from fire cooks our food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a physical process involved in the formation of clouds? A: Condensation. Water vapour condenses high in the sky to form clouds.
chunks.source: Water vapour condenses high in the sky to form clouds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the body organ which stores information? A: Brain. The brain keeps everything we learn and remember.
chunks.source: The brain keeps everything we learn and remember.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of preventing metals from rusting? A: By painting them. Paint covers metal so air and water cannot reach it.
chunks.source: Paint covers metal so air and water cannot reach it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of soil does not keep water for long? A: Sand soil. Water drains quickly through the large particles of sand soil.
chunks.source: Water drains quickly through the large particles of sand soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a nocturnal animal? A: Bat. Bats are active at night and rest during the day.
chunks.source: Bats are active at night and rest during the day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a body part where a thermometer is fixed to take the temperature? A: Armpit. The thermometer is placed in the armpit to read body temperature.
chunks.source: The thermometer is placed in the armpit to read body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way can a poultry farmer control poultry diseases in the poultry house? A: By vaccinating the birds. Vaccines protect chickens against killer diseases.
chunks.source: Vaccines protect chickens against killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What activity can be done by a primary six boy in order to promote environmental sanitation? A: Sweeping the compound. Sweeping removes dirt and keeps the surroundings clean.
chunks.source: Sweeping removes dirt and keeps the surroundings clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the picture below. Name the type of family shown: ___. A: Extended family. Likely answer: the picture shows many adults and children together, like grandparents, parents and children.
chunks.source: Likely answer: the picture shows many adults and children together, like grandparents, parents and children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of change occurs when a leopard dies of an illness? A: Biological change. Death and decay of a living thing is a biological change.
chunks.source: Death and decay of a living thing is a biological change.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do some plants reduce the rate of transpiration? A: By shedding their leaves. Without leaves, a plant loses very little water.
chunks.source: Without leaves, a plant loses very little water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a product from a Marino sheep? A: Wool. Merino sheep are famous for their fine wool.
chunks.source: Merino sheep are famous for their fine wool.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a soil pollutant? A: Polythene bags. Polythene bags dumped in soil pollute it.
chunks.source: Polythene bags dumped in soil pollute it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the bird's foot. Identify the type of foot shown: ___. A: Scratching foot. The strong toes of a domestic fowl are adapted for scratching the ground.
chunks.source: The strong toes of a domestic fowl are adapted for scratching the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from having a latrine, which of the following is an other item a healthy home should have? A: A bathroom. A healthy home needs a bathroom for bathing.
chunks.source: A healthy home needs a bathroom for bathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a material used for making composite manure? A: Animal droppings. Animal droppings rot into rich composite manure.
chunks.source: Animal droppings rot into rich composite manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List down any one example of irregular objects: ___. A: Stone. A stone has no regular shape.
chunks.source: A stone has no regular shape.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List down another example of irregular objects: ___. A: Key. A key's shape is not regular.
chunks.source: A key's shape is not regular.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a characteristic of living things? A: They feed. All living things take in food for energy.
chunks.source: All living things take in food for energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another characteristic of living things? A: They grow. Living things increase in size as they develop.
chunks.source: Living things increase in size as they develop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a major group of living things? A: Plants. Plants are one major group of living things.
chunks.source: Plants are one major group of living things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another major group of living things? A: Animals. Animals are the other major group of living things.
chunks.source: Animals are the other major group of living things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the human body system. Name the part labeled G: ___. A: Trachea (wind pipe). The trachea is the tube that carries air to the lungs.
chunks.source: The trachea is the tube that carries air to the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the part labeled F? A: Bronchus. The bronchus branches from the trachea into each lung.
chunks.source: The bronchus branches from the trachea into each lung.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which system of the body does the diagram belong? A: Respiratory system. These organs are all used in breathing.
chunks.source: These organs are all used in breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a bad health practice that may affect proper functioning of the system? A: Smoking. Smoke damages the lungs and air passages.
chunks.source: Smoke damages the lungs and air passages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which component of air is used by plants to make food? A: Carbon dioxide. Plants take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a product got from poultry farming? A: Eggs. Poultry farms produce eggs for food and sale.
chunks.source: Poultry farms produce eggs for food and sale.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one disease of poultry: ___. A: Newcastle disease. Newcastle disease kills chickens in large numbers.
chunks.source: Newcastle disease kills chickens in large numbers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a cause of dehydration? A: Diarrhoea. Diarrhoea drains a lot of water from the body.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea drains a lot of water from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another cause of dehydration? A: Vomiting. Vomiting also removes water from the body.
chunks.source: Vomiting also removes water from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are carnivorous mammals? A: Mammals that feed on flesh. Carnivorous mammals hunt and eat other animals.
chunks.source: Carnivorous mammals hunt and eat other animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a carnivorous mammal? A: Lion. The lion is a well-known flesh-eating mammal.
chunks.source: The lion is a well-known flesh-eating mammal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a first aid kit? A: Bandage. A bandage is used to cover wounds.
chunks.source: A bandage is used to cover wounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an effect of heat on matter? A: It causes expansion. Heated matter expands.
chunks.source: Heated matter expands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another effect of heat on matter? A: It causes change of state. Heat can melt solids and boil liquids.
chunks.source: Heat can melt solids and boil liquids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: During which weather can a Campbell sunshine recorder be used? A: Sunny weather. The recorder needs sunshine to burn its readings.
chunks.source: The recorder needs sunshine to burn its readings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a type of family? A: Nuclear family. A nuclear family has parents and their children only.
chunks.source: A nuclear family has parents and their children only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another type of family? A: Extended family. An extended family includes grandparents and other relatives.
chunks.source: An extended family includes grandparents and other relatives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another role of a father at home? A: He protects the family. Fathers keep the family safe from harm.
chunks.source: Fathers keep the family safe from harm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of changes of state. Name the state of matter labeled Q: ___. A: Solid. Sublimation changes Q directly into gas, so Q is a solid.
chunks.source: Sublimation changes Q directly into gas, so Q is a solid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the state of matter labeled P? A: Liquid. Condensation changes gas into P, so P is a liquid.
chunks.source: Condensation changes gas into P, so P is a liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the process of change of state of matter labeled M? A: Evaporation. M changes liquid P into gas.
chunks.source: M changes liquid P into gas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the process of change of state of matter labeled N? A: Freezing. N changes liquid P into solid Q, which is freezing. (Read from the diagram's arrow directions.)
chunks.source: N changes liquid P into solid Q, which is freezing. (Read from the diagram's arrow directions.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a type of root? A: Taproot. A taproot grows straight down from the seed.
chunks.source: A taproot grows straight down from the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another type of root? A: Fibrous root. Fibrous roots spread out in many thin branches.
chunks.source: Fibrous roots spread out in many thin branches.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way are roots useful to animals? A: Some animals feed on roots. Animals like rabbits eat roots such as carrots.
chunks.source: Animals like rabbits eat roots such as carrots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a garden tool used in land preparation? A: Hoe. A hoe digs and breaks the soil.
chunks.source: A hoe digs and breaks the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another garden tool used in land preparation? A: Spade. A spade cuts and turns the soil.
chunks.source: A spade cuts and turns the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a third garden tool used in land preparation? A: Rake. A rake levels the dug soil.
chunks.source: A rake levels the dug soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the best soil for growing crops? A: Loam soil. Loam soil has sand, clay and humus mixed, so it holds water and air and is fertile.
chunks.source: Loam soil has sand, clay and humus mixed, so it holds water and air and is fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the function of gills on a mushroom? A: They produce (and release) spores. The gills under the cap of a mushroom make the tiny spores used for reproduction.
chunks.source: The gills under the cap of a mushroom make the tiny spores used for reproduction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a spur useful to a cock? A: For fighting (protection/defence). A cock uses its sharp spurs to fight enemies and protect itself.
chunks.source: A cock uses its sharp spurs to fight enemies and protect itself.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a property of air? A: Air occupies space. Air takes up space, has weight and exerts pressure even though we cannot see it.
chunks.source: Air takes up space, has weight and exerts pressure even though we cannot see it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the organisms found in root nodules of legumes? A: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria (Rhizobium). Tiny bacteria living in the root nodules of beans and other legumes fix nitrogen from the air into the soil.
chunks.source: Tiny bacteria living in the root nodules of beans and other legumes fix nitrogen from the air into the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the blood vessel marked with letter I in the diagram? A: Vein. Likely answer: vessel I has a wide lumen and thin wall, which is how a vein is drawn (arteries have thick walls and narrow lumens).
chunks.source: Likely answer: vessel I has a wide lumen and thin wall, which is how a vein is drawn (arteries have thick walls and narrow lumens).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which form of energy is produced by vibrations of an object? A: Sound energy. When an object vibrates, it produces sound energy.
chunks.source: When an object vibrates, it produces sound energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an organ damaged by excessive alcoholism? A: Liver. Too much alcohol damages the liver (and also the brain and stomach).
chunks.source: Too much alcohol damages the liver (and also the brain and stomach).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of an essential drug? A: Paracetamol (Panadol). Essential drugs are safe, affordable and always needed medicines such as paracetamol.
chunks.source: Essential drugs are safe, affordable and always needed medicines such as paracetamol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of maintaining soil fertility? A: Mulching. Adding manure or mulch, crop rotation and bush fallowing keep the soil fertile.
chunks.source: Adding manure or mulch, crop rotation and bush fallowing keep the soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is water called a universal solvent? A: Because it dissolves many substances. Water can dissolve very many things such as salt and sugar, so it is called a universal solvent.
chunks.source: Water can dissolve very many things such as salt and sugar, so it is called a universal solvent.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of an annual crop? A: Maize. Annual crops grow and are harvested within one year, e.g. maize, beans, groundnuts.
chunks.source: Annual crops grow and are harvested within one year, e.g. maize, beans, groundnuts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of energy is possessed by a leaf falling from a tree? A: Kinetic energy. A moving (falling) leaf has kinetic energy, the energy of a moving object.
chunks.source: A moving (falling) leaf has kinetic energy, the energy of a moving object.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the substance that exists in the three states of matter? A: Water. Water exists as ice (solid), liquid water, and steam (gas).
chunks.source: Water exists as ice (solid), liquid water, and steam (gas).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the standard units for measuring mass? A: Kilograms (kg). Mass is measured in kilograms; small masses in grams.
chunks.source: Mass is measured in kilograms; small masses in grams.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a method of harvesting crops? A: Hand picking. Crops are harvested by hand picking, uprooting, cutting or digging.
chunks.source: Crops are harvested by hand picking, uprooting, cutting or digging.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a sign of dehydration in babies? A: Sunken eyes. A dehydrated baby has sunken eyes, a dry mouth, a sunken soft spot on the head, or passes little urine.
chunks.source: A dehydrated baby has sunken eyes, a dry mouth, a sunken soft spot on the head, or passes little urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a method of making alcohol? A: Fermentation. Alcohol is made by fermentation (and concentrated by distillation).
chunks.source: Alcohol is made by fermentation (and concentrated by distillation).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the blood cell that carries oxygen around the body? A: Red blood cell. The red blood cell contains haemoglobin which carries oxygen to all body parts.
chunks.source: The red blood cell contains haemoglobin which carries oxygen to all body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from a drum, which of the following is another example of a percussion musical instrument? A: Xylophone. Percussion instruments are played by hitting or shaking, e.g. xylophone, jembe, bell, rattles.
chunks.source: Percussion instruments are played by hitting or shaking, e.g. xylophone, jembe, bell, rattles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease spread through poor sanitation? A: Cholera. Poor sanitation spreads cholera, typhoid, dysentery and diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Poor sanitation spreads cholera, typhoid, dysentery and diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the mollusc in the diagram below? A: Snail. The animal in the diagram with a coiled shell is a snail, which is a mollusc.
chunks.source: The animal in the diagram with a coiled shell is a snail, which is a mollusc.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a liquid that floats on water? A: Oil (cooking oil). Oil, paraffin and petrol are less dense than water, so they float on it.
chunks.source: Oil, paraffin and petrol are less dense than water, so they float on it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write ORS in full: ___. A: Oral Rehydration Salts. ORS stands for Oral Rehydration Salts, given to replace water lost in diarrhoea.
chunks.source: ORS stands for Oral Rehydration Salts, given to replace water lost in diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does heat travel through solids? A: By conduction. Heat moves through solids by conduction, e.g. along a metal spoon in hot tea.
chunks.source: Heat moves through solids by conduction, e.g. along a metal spoon in hot tea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a cause of road traffic accidents in Uganda? A: Over speeding. Accidents are caused by over speeding, drunk driving, bad roads and careless driving.
chunks.source: Accidents are caused by over speeding, drunk driving, bad roads and careless driving.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a good eating habit? A: Washing hands before eating. Good eating habits include washing hands, chewing food well and eating a balanced diet.
chunks.source: Good eating habits include washing hands, chewing food well and eating a balanced diet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to such information written on a packet of drugs (as shown in the diagram)? A: Prescription (dosage instructions). The instructions on a drug packet telling how the drug should be taken are called a prescription.
chunks.source: The instructions on a drug packet telling how the drug should be taken are called a prescription.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How many times a day is the patient supposed to take the drug? A: Three times a day. The packet is marked 2x3, meaning 2 tablets taken 3 times a day.
chunks.source: The packet is marked 2x3, meaning 2 tablets taken 3 times a day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The patient took the drug in the morning; for how many hours should the patient wait before taking the drug again? A: 8 hours. Three doses a day means one dose every 8 hours (24 divided by 3).
chunks.source: Three doses a day means one dose every 8 hours (24 divided by 3).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of immunity acquired through recovery from illness? A: Natural immunity. Immunity got after recovering from a disease is called natural immunity.
chunks.source: Immunity got after recovering from a disease is called natural immunity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of immunity acquired through immunization? A: Artificial immunity. Immunity got through vaccines (immunization) is called artificial immunity.
chunks.source: Immunity got through vaccines (immunization) is called artificial immunity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of an immunisable disease? A: Measles. Immunisable diseases include measles, polio, tuberculosis, tetanus and whooping cough.
chunks.source: Immunisable diseases include measles, polio, tuberculosis, tetanus and whooping cough.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a chemical change? A: Burning (combustion). Examples of chemical changes: burning, rusting, rotting, cooking food, digestion.
chunks.source: Examples of chemical changes: burning, rusting, rotting, cooking food, digestion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another example of a chemical change? A: Rusting of iron. Other examples: rotting of fruits, souring of milk, baking.
chunks.source: Other examples: rotting of fruits, souring of milk, baking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the classification chart, which group of animals is indicated by letter X? A: Warm-blooded vertebrates. X groups birds and mammals together, and both are warm-blooded vertebrates.
chunks.source: X groups birds and mammals together, and both are warm-blooded vertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the classification chart, which group of animals is indicated by letter Y? A: Mammals. Y is grouped with birds under X (warm-blooded), so Y is mammals.
chunks.source: Y is grouped with birds under X (warm-blooded), so Y is mammals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a characteristic of the animal in group K? A: It breathes through gills. K is fish (grouped with reptiles and amphibians as cold-blooded); fish live in water and breathe through gills.
chunks.source: K is fish (grouped with reptiles and amphibians as cold-blooded); fish live in water and breathe through gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of an amphibian? A: Frog. Amphibians live partly in water and partly on land, e.g. frog, toad.
chunks.source: Amphibians live partly in water and partly on land, e.g. frog, toad.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an effect of heat gain on matter? A: Matter expands (increases in size). When matter gains heat it expands, melts, evaporates or rises in temperature.
chunks.source: When matter gains heat it expands, melts, evaporates or rises in temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way in which people use heat? A: For cooking food. People use heat for cooking, warming the house, drying clothes and ironing.
chunks.source: People use heat for cooking, warming the house, drying clothes and ironing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another way in which people use heat? A: For warming the house. Heat is also used for drying harvested crops and warming bath water.
chunks.source: Heat is also used for drying harvested crops and warming bath water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from cassava, which of the following is another example of a root tuber? A: Sweet potato. Root tubers include sweet potatoes and carrots.
chunks.source: Root tubers include sweet potatoes and carrots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another example of a root tuber? A: Carrot. Carrots are also swollen roots that store food.
chunks.source: Carrots are also swollen roots that store food.

chunks.subject: Science
