chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease which affects cassava plants? A: Cassava mosaic disease. Cassava is attacked by cassava mosaic disease (and cassava brown streak disease).
chunks.source: Cassava is attacked by cassava mosaic disease (and cassava brown streak disease).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of promoting personal hygiene? A: Bathing the body daily. Brushing teeth, washing hands, cutting nails short and bathing keep one clean.
chunks.source: Brushing teeth, washing hands, cutting nails short and bathing keep one clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another way of promoting personal hygiene? A: Brushing the teeth (after meals). Wearing clean clothes and washing hands before eating also promote hygiene.
chunks.source: Wearing clean clothes and washing hands before eating also promote hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an item used to promote good personal hygiene? A: Soap. Items like soap, toothbrush, towel and nail cutters promote personal hygiene.
chunks.source: Items like soap, toothbrush, towel and nail cutters promote personal hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of the human ear, name the part marked M: ___. A: Eardrum (tympanic membrane). M points to the eardrum, the thin skin at the end of the ear canal that vibrates with sound.
chunks.source: M points to the eardrum, the thin skin at the end of the ear canal that vibrates with sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of the human ear, name the part marked P: ___. A: Cochlea. P points to the snail-shaped cochlea in the inner ear where sound messages start.
chunks.source: P points to the snail-shaped cochlea in the inner ear where sound messages start.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part of the ear responsible for balancing the body is the ___. A: Semicircular canals. The semicircular canals in the inner ear help the body to balance.
chunks.source: The semicircular canals in the inner ear help the body to balance.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a marine (sea) mammal? A: Whale. Marine mammals live in the sea but breathe air, e.g. whale, dolphin, seal.
chunks.source: Marine mammals live in the sea but breathe air, e.g. whale, dolphin, seal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another example of a marine (sea) mammal? A: Dolphin. Dolphins are intelligent sea mammals that breathe through a blowhole.
chunks.source: Dolphins are intelligent sea mammals that breathe through a blowhole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one exotic breed of goat kept in Uganda: ___. A: Toggenburg. Exotic goat breeds kept in Uganda include Toggenburg, Saanen, Boer and Anglo-Nubian.
chunks.source: Exotic goat breeds kept in Uganda include Toggenburg, Saanen, Boer and Anglo-Nubian.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down another exotic breed of goat kept in Uganda: ___. A: Saanen. Saanen goats are white dairy goats.
chunks.source: Saanen goats are white dairy goats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How long is the gestation period of a nanny (female goat)? A: 5 months (about 150 days). A nanny goat carries its pregnancy for about 5 months.
chunks.source: A nanny goat carries its pregnancy for about 5 months.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the component of air used for: (i) respiration? A: Oxygen. Oxygen in air is used for respiration (breathing).
chunks.source: Oxygen in air is used for respiration (breathing).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the component of air used for: (ii) putting out fire? A: Carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it is used to put out fire.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it is used to put out fire.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a danger of wind to people? A: It spreads diseases. Strong wind destroys crops and houses, spreads diseases and causes accidents.
chunks.source: Strong wind destroys crops and houses, spreads diseases and causes accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a container B? A: Measuring cylinder. Container B collects and measures the displaced water.
chunks.source: Container B collects and measures the displaced water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the volume of the irregular object? A: 10 cc (10 cm3). The volume of the object equals the volume of displaced water, which reads 10 cc in container B.
chunks.source: The volume of the object equals the volume of displaced water, which reads 10 cc in container B.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Calculate the density of the irregular object if its mass is 60 g: ___. A: 6 g/cm3. Density = mass / volume = 60 g / 10 cc = 6 g/cm3.
chunks.source: Density = mass / volume = 60 g / 10 cc = 6 g/cm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a poisonous substance found in tobacco? A: Nicotine. Tobacco contains nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide, which are poisonous.
chunks.source: Tobacco contains nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide, which are poisonous.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another poisonous substance found in tobacco? A: Tar. Tar from tobacco smoke coats the lungs and can cause cancer.
chunks.source: Tar from tobacco smoke coats the lungs and can cause cancer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an effect of cigarette smoking by pregnant women on their unborn babies? A: Low birth weight (premature birth). Smoking in pregnancy can cause miscarriage, premature birth and low birth weight babies.
chunks.source: Smoking in pregnancy can cause miscarriage, premature birth and low birth weight babies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another effect of cigarette smoking by pregnant women on their unborn babies? A: Miscarriage (loss of the pregnancy). The poisons in smoke reach the unborn baby through the mother's blood.
chunks.source: The poisons in smoke reach the unborn baby through the mother's blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the reflected sound? A: Echo. Sound that bounces back off a surface is called an echo.
chunks.source: Sound that bounces back off a surface is called an echo.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a characteristic of living things? A: They breathe (respire). Living things breathe, feed, grow, reproduce, move and respond to changes.
chunks.source: Living things breathe, feed, grow, reproduce, move and respond to changes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the importance of canine tooth to carnivorous animals? A: For tearing flesh (meat). Carnivores use their sharp pointed canines to tear meat.
chunks.source: Carnivores use their sharp pointed canines to tear meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the best food for babies below six months? A: Breast milk. Babies below six months should feed on breast milk only.
chunks.source: Babies below six months should feed on breast milk only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which vaccine is immunized to infants against tuberculosis? A: BCG. BCG vaccine protects infants against tuberculosis (TB).
chunks.source: BCG vaccine protects infants against tuberculosis (TB).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the item used to promote sanitation drawn below? A: Toothbrush. The drawn item is a toothbrush, used for cleaning teeth.
chunks.source: The drawn item is a toothbrush, used for cleaning teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the above item used by people to promote personal hygiene? A: For brushing (cleaning) the teeth. A toothbrush is used to brush teeth and keep the mouth clean.
chunks.source: A toothbrush is used to brush teeth and keep the mouth clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the habitat of earth worms? A: Soil. Earthworms live in the soil.
chunks.source: Earthworms live in the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which invertebrate lives in the human alimentary canal? A: Tapeworm. Tapeworms (and roundworms) are invertebrates that live in the human gut.
chunks.source: Tapeworms (and roundworms) are invertebrates that live in the human gut.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a snake move from one place to another? A: By crawling (slithering). A snake wriggles (slithers) its long body to crawl.
chunks.source: A snake wriggles (slithers) its long body to crawl.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of an intestinal worm in human beings? A: Roundworm. Intestinal worms include roundworms, tapeworms and hookworms.
chunks.source: Intestinal worms include roundworms, tapeworms and hookworms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a vulnerable group of people in your community? A: Babies (infants). Vulnerable groups include babies, pregnant women, the elderly and the sick.
chunks.source: Vulnerable groups include babies, pregnant women, the elderly and the sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a device used to store sound? A: Tape recorder. Sound can be stored on tape recorders, CDs, phones, radios and flash disks.
chunks.source: Sound can be stored on tape recorders, CDs, phones, radios and flash disks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the transport system of the human body? A: Circulatory (blood) system. The circulatory system transports blood, food, oxygen and waste around the body.
chunks.source: The circulatory system transports blood, food, oxygen and waste around the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The soft feather covering a chick's body is called a ___ feather. A: Down. Down feathers are soft and fluffy and keep the chick warm.
chunks.source: Down feathers are soft and fluffy and keep the chick warm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a natural source of sound in the environment? A: Thunder. Natural sources of sound include thunder, flowing water, wind and animals.
chunks.source: Natural sources of sound include thunder, flowing water, wind and animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What food value is got from eating legumes? A: Proteins. Legumes such as beans, peas and groundnuts give the body proteins for growth.
chunks.source: Legumes such as beans, peas and groundnuts give the body proteins for growth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of soil with the highest capillarity? A: Clay soil. Clay soil has the smallest particles, so water rises highest in it by capillarity.
chunks.source: Clay soil has the smallest particles, so water rises highest in it by capillarity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a solute used in the making of ORS? A: Sugar. ORS is made by dissolving sugar and salt in clean boiled water.
chunks.source: ORS is made by dissolving sugar and salt in clean boiled water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a weather instrument? A: Thermometer. Weather instruments include the thermometer, rain gauge, wind vane and barometer.
chunks.source: Weather instruments include the thermometer, rain gauge, wind vane and barometer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the instrument used to detect body temperature? A: Thermometer (clinical thermometer). A clinical thermometer measures body temperature.
chunks.source: A clinical thermometer measures body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is sound energy produced? A: By vibrations of objects. Sound is produced when objects vibrate.
chunks.source: Sound is produced when objects vibrate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of an amphibian? A: Frog. Amphibians include frogs and toads.
chunks.source: Amphibians include frogs and toads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which body organ filters blood? A: Kidney. The kidneys filter waste materials out of the blood to make urine.
chunks.source: The kidneys filter waste materials out of the blood to make urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an use of feathers to birds? A: For flying. Feathers help birds to fly and also keep them warm.
chunks.source: Feathers help birds to fly and also keep them warm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a bird with the foot in the diagram? A: Duck. The webbed foot in the diagram belongs to swimming birds such as a duck or goose.
chunks.source: The webbed foot in the diagram belongs to swimming birds such as a duck or goose.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a part marked B on the foot in the diagram? A: Web (webbing between the toes). B points to the skin (web) joining the toes, which helps the bird swim.
chunks.source: B points to the skin (web) joining the toes, which helps the bird swim.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a characteristic of insects? A: They have six legs. Insects have six legs, three body parts and a pair of antennae.
chunks.source: Insects have six legs, three body parts and a pair of antennae.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a common disease at home? A: Malaria. Common home diseases include malaria, flu, cough and diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Common home diseases include malaria, flu, cough and diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a sign of soil erosion in an area? A: Gullies (channels) in the soil. Signs of erosion include gullies, exposed plant roots and bare stony land.
chunks.source: Signs of erosion include gullies, exposed plant roots and bare stony land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a reproductive cell in flowering plants? A: Pollen grain. The male reproductive cell is the pollen grain; the female one is the ovule (ovum).
chunks.source: The male reproductive cell is the pollen grain; the female one is the ovule (ovum).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do people drink alcohol? A: For pleasure (to enjoy themselves). People drink alcohol for leisure, to socialize or to feel happy.
chunks.source: People drink alcohol for leisure, to socialize or to feel happy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which body organ balances the body in its right posture? A: The ear (semicircular canals). The semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.
chunks.source: The semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a crop growing practice? A: Weeding. Crop growing practices include planting, weeding, mulching, spraying and harvesting.
chunks.source: Crop growing practices include planting, weeding, mulching, spraying and harvesting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagrams about states of matter, name the state of matter marked B: ___. A: Liquid. B shows particles fairly close but not tightly packed, which is the liquid state.
chunks.source: B shows particles fairly close but not tightly packed, which is the liquid state.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the state of matter marked C? A: Gas (gaseous state). C shows particles far apart and scattered, which is the gaseous state.
chunks.source: C shows particles far apart and scattered, which is the gaseous state.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which substance makes up the state of matter B above? A: Water. Likely answer: the liquid shown is water, the commonest liquid used in such diagrams.
chunks.source: Likely answer: the liquid shown is water, the commonest liquid used in such diagrams.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does heat travel through the state of matter marked C? A: By convection. Heat travels through gases (and liquids) by convection currents.
chunks.source: Heat travels through gases (and liquids) by convection currents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a type of bird found in our environment? A: Hen (chicken). Common birds include hens, ducks, doves, pigeons and eagles.
chunks.source: Common birds include hens, ducks, doves, pigeons and eagles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another type of bird found in our environment? A: Duck. Ducks are water birds with webbed feet.
chunks.source: Ducks are water birds with webbed feet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from birds, which of the following is the other group of warm blooded vertebrates? A: Mammals. The two warm-blooded vertebrate groups are birds and mammals.
chunks.source: The two warm-blooded vertebrate groups are birds and mammals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a reason for giving first aid to casualties? A: To save life. First aid saves life, reduces pain and prevents the injury from getting worse.
chunks.source: First aid saves life, reduces pain and prevents the injury from getting worse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another reason for giving first aid to casualties? A: To reduce pain. First aid also stops bleeding and prevents further harm.
chunks.source: First aid also stops bleeding and prevents further harm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the first aid material drawn below? A: Gloves (protective gloves). The drawn material is a pair of gloves worn to protect the first aider from germs.
chunks.source: The drawn material is a pair of gloves worn to protect the first aider from germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A stone of mass 60 g was immersed in water and displaced 20 cc of water. What does the displaced water represent? A: The volume of the stone. The volume of displaced water equals the volume of the immersed object.
chunks.source: The volume of displaced water equals the volume of the immersed object.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Calculate the density of the stone: ___. A: 3 g/cm3. Density = mass / volume = 60 g / 20 cc = 3 g/cm3.
chunks.source: Density = mass / volume = 60 g / 20 cc = 3 g/cm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of an annual crop? A: Maize. Annual crops mature within one year, e.g. maize, beans, groundnuts, sorghum.
chunks.source: Annual crops mature within one year, e.g. maize, beans, groundnuts, sorghum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another example of an annual crop? A: Beans. Beans are legumes harvested within months of planting.
chunks.source: Beans are legumes harvested within months of planting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a perennial crop? A: Coffee. Perennial crops live for many years, e.g. coffee, bananas, tea, sugarcane.
chunks.source: Perennial crops live for many years, e.g. coffee, bananas, tea, sugarcane.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another example of a perennial crop? A: Bananas. Banana plants keep producing bunches for many years.
chunks.source: Banana plants keep producing bunches for many years.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are vertebrates? A: Animals with a backbone (spine). Vertebrates are animals that have a backbone.
chunks.source: Vertebrates are animals that have a backbone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a vertebrate? A: Cow. Examples: cow, goat, fish, bird, frog, snake, human being.
chunks.source: Examples: cow, goat, fish, bird, frog, snake, human being.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another example of a vertebrate? A: Fish. Fish have backbones too.
chunks.source: Fish have backbones too.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a characteristic of vertebrates? A: They have a backbone. All vertebrates possess a backbone (vertebral column).
chunks.source: All vertebrates possess a backbone (vertebral column).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the root system marked P? A: Fibrous root system. P shows many thin roots of almost equal size spreading from the stem base: a fibrous root system.
chunks.source: P shows many thin roots of almost equal size spreading from the stem base: a fibrous root system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the root system marked Q? A: Taproot system. Q shows one main root with side roots and nodules: a taproot system.
chunks.source: Q shows one main root with side roots and nodules: a taproot system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a plant with the root system marked P? A: Maize. Fibrous roots are found in maize, sorghum, millet, rice and grasses.
chunks.source: Fibrous roots are found in maize, sorghum, millet, rice and grasses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a plant with the root system marked Q? A: Beans. Taproots are found in beans, groundnuts and other legumes.
chunks.source: Taproots are found in beans, groundnuts and other legumes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the group of vertebrates where human beings belong? A: Mammals. Human beings are mammals.
chunks.source: Human beings are mammals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from human beings, which of the following is another vertebrate in the group named in (a)? A: Cow. Other mammals: cow, goat, dog, cat, bat, whale.
chunks.source: Other mammals: cow, goat, dog, cat, bat, whale.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another vertebrate in the same group? A: Goat. Goats are mammals kept for milk and meat.
chunks.source: Goats are mammals kept for milk and meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the example of a flying mammal? A: Bat. The bat is the only mammal that can truly fly.
chunks.source: The bat is the only mammal that can truly fly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an use of the human ear to the body? A: For hearing (sound). The ear is used for hearing and for balancing the body.
chunks.source: The ear is used for hearing and for balancing the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another use of the human ear to the body? A: For balancing the body. The semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.
chunks.source: The semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of the mammalian ear, name part labeled X: ___. A: Pinna (outer ear). X points to the pinna, the outer flap that collects sound waves.
chunks.source: X points to the pinna, the outer flap that collects sound waves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a part labeled Y? A: Eardrum (tympanic membrane). Y points to the eardrum at the end of the ear canal.
chunks.source: Y points to the eardrum at the end of the ear canal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a type of weather? A: Sunny. Types of weather: sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy.
chunks.source: Types of weather: sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another type of weather? A: Rainy. Rain falls from dark clouds.
chunks.source: Rain falls from dark clouds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the weather condition that favours winnowing of cereals? A: Windy. Wind blows away the light chaff, leaving the heavy grains.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light chaff, leaving the heavy grains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which state of matter does sound travel fastest? A: Solid. Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids, slowest in gases.
chunks.source: Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids, slowest in gases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a reason why farmers rear chicken? A: For eggs. Farmers keep chicken for eggs, meat and income.
chunks.source: Farmers keep chicken for eggs, meat and income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another reason why farmers rear chicken? A: For meat. Chicken meat is a source of protein and income.
chunks.source: Chicken meat is a source of protein and income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a type of chicken reared by farmers? A: Layers. Layers are kept for eggs; broilers for meat.
chunks.source: Layers are kept for eggs; broilers for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another type of chicken reared by farmers? A: Broilers. Broilers grow fast and are kept for meat.
chunks.source: Broilers grow fast and are kept for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a pest which attacks crops in the garden? A: Weevils. Crop pests include weevils, stalk borers, aphids, cutworms and termites.
chunks.source: Crop pests include weevils, stalk borers, aphids, cutworms and termites.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another pest which attacks crops in the garden? A: Stalk borers. Stalk borers tunnel into cereal stems.
chunks.source: Stalk borers tunnel into cereal stems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way in which pests are dangerous to crops? A: They eat (destroy) the crops. Pests eat crops and reduce harvests.
chunks.source: Pests eat crops and reduce harvests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a farmer control pests in the garden? A: By spraying with pesticides. Pests are controlled by spraying pesticides, crop rotation and weeding.
chunks.source: Pests are controlled by spraying pesticides, crop rotation and weeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Moses observed a mango fruit with his five senses. Fill in the missing body structure: Fruity smell is observed by sense of smell using (i) ___. A: Nose. We smell with the nose.
chunks.source: We smell with the nose.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Red colour is observed by sense of sight using (ii) ___. A: Eyes. We see with the eyes.
chunks.source: We see with the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sound made when the mango drops is observed by sense of hearing using (iii) ___. A: Ears. We hear with the ears.
chunks.source: We hear with the ears.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sweet taste is observed by sense of taste using (iv) ___. A: Tongue. We taste with the tongue.
chunks.source: We taste with the tongue.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a vector which is involved in the 4Fs disease path? A: Housefly. The housefly carries germs through the 4Fs: faeces, fingers, flies and food.
chunks.source: The housefly carries germs through the 4Fs: faeces, fingers, flies and food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of controlling tape worm infestation in humans? A: Deworming regularly. Tapeworms are controlled by deworming, cooking meat properly and using latrines.
chunks.source: Tapeworms are controlled by deworming, cooking meat properly and using latrines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a non-renewable resource? A: Petroleum (crude oil). Non-renewable resources cannot be replaced once used up, e.g. petroleum, coal, minerals.
chunks.source: Non-renewable resources cannot be replaced once used up, e.g. petroleum, coal, minerals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the garden tool shown in the diagram? A: Hand fork (garden fork). The small forked tool in the diagram is a hand fork, used for light digging and weeding.
chunks.source: The small forked tool in the diagram is a hand fork, used for light digging and weeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of caring for garden tools? A: Clean them after use. Garden tools are cared for by cleaning, oiling metal parts, sharpening and keeping them dry.
chunks.source: Garden tools are cared for by cleaning, oiling metal parts, sharpening and keeping them dry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of energy is possessed by a bat in flight? A: Kinetic energy. A flying bat is moving, so it has kinetic energy.
chunks.source: A flying bat is moving, so it has kinetic energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an animal fibre? A: Wool. Animal fibres include wool (from sheep), silk and mohair.
chunks.source: Animal fibres include wool (from sheep), silk and mohair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from sugar, which of the following is another substance used to make Oral Rehydration Solution? A: Salt. ORS is made of sugar and salt dissolved in clean boiled water.
chunks.source: ORS is made of sugar and salt dissolved in clean boiled water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a farming practice used by crop farmers to maintain soil fertility? A: Crop rotation. Crop rotation, mulching, manuring and bush fallowing keep soil fertile.
chunks.source: Crop rotation, mulching, manuring and bush fallowing keep soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of food eaten by the bird with the beak shown in the diagram? A: Nectar. The long curved beak is for sucking nectar from flowers.
chunks.source: The long curved beak is for sucking nectar from flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way in which a latrine is useful in a home? A: For proper disposal of faeces. Latrines keep faeces away from people, preventing diseases like cholera.
chunks.source: Latrines keep faeces away from people, preventing diseases like cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the component of blood which is destroyed by HIV? A: White blood cells. HIV attacks and destroys white blood cells, weakening the body's defence.
chunks.source: HIV attacks and destroys white blood cells, weakening the body's defence.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a factor which favours the breeding of bacteria? A: Warmth. Bacteria breed fast where there is warmth, moisture and food.
chunks.source: Bacteria breed fast where there is warmth, moisture and food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can people in the community control the spread of water borne diseases? A: By boiling drinking water. Boiling water, proper sanitation and protecting wells control water-borne diseases.
chunks.source: Boiling water, proper sanitation and protecting wells control water-borne diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where does gaseous exchange take place in the human body? A: In the lungs (air sacs). Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged in the tiny air sacs of the lungs.
chunks.source: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged in the tiny air sacs of the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we call the number of vibrations produced by an object per second? A: Frequency. Frequency is the number of vibrations per second, measured in hertz.
chunks.source: Frequency is the number of vibrations per second, measured in hertz.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a root tuber? A: Cassava. Root tubers include cassava, sweet potatoes and carrots.
chunks.source: Root tubers include cassava, sweet potatoes and carrots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can poultry farmers control cannibalism on their farms? A: By debeaking the birds. Debeaking, proper feeding and avoiding overcrowding stop birds pecking each other.
chunks.source: Debeaking, proper feeding and avoiding overcrowding stop birds pecking each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which weather instrument is used to measure the speed of wind? A: Anemometer. An anemometer has spinning cups that measure how fast wind blows.
chunks.source: An anemometer has spinning cups that measure how fast wind blows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one danger of drought in the environment: ___. A: Crops dry up (famine). Drought kills crops and animals and causes famine and lack of water.
chunks.source: Drought kills crops and animals and causes famine and lack of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a sanitary activity that children can do to keep the school compound clean? A: Sweeping the compound. Children can sweep, slash grass and pick rubbish to keep the school clean.
chunks.source: Children can sweep, slash grass and pick rubbish to keep the school clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a part marked with letter K on the bean seed? A: Cotyledon. K points to the cotyledon, the food store of the bean seed.
chunks.source: K points to the cotyledon, the food store of the bean seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a factor one should consider when selecting a site for a house? A: Well-drained land. A house site should be well-drained, near water, secure and away from swamps.
chunks.source: A house site should be well-drained, near water, secure and away from swamps.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a physical process that helps in rain formation? A: Evaporation. Evaporation lifts water into the sky and condensation forms the clouds that give rain.
chunks.source: Evaporation lifts water into the sky and condensation forms the clouds that give rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way are termites dangerous to crop farmers? A: They eat (destroy) crops. Termites eat crops, wooden buildings and stored harvests.
chunks.source: Termites eat crops, wooden buildings and stored harvests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of the human ear helps the body to balance? A: Semicircular canals. The three semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.
chunks.source: The three semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which element of weather is needed for the preservation of harvested seeds and grains? A: Sunshine (sun heat). Sunshine dries harvested seeds and grains so they can be stored without rotting.
chunks.source: Sunshine dries harvested seeds and grains so they can be stored without rotting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a common accident at home? A: Burns. Common home accidents: burns, scalds, cuts, falls, poisoning.
chunks.source: Common home accidents: burns, scalds, cuts, falls, poisoning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from amphibians, which of the following is a two other groups of cold-blooded vertebrates? A: Reptiles and fish. Cold-blooded vertebrates are fish, amphibians and reptiles.
chunks.source: Cold-blooded vertebrates are fish, amphibians and reptiles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of an amphibian? A: Toad. Amphibians include frogs and toads.
chunks.source: Amphibians include frogs and toads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do amphibians reproduce? A: By laying eggs (in water). Amphibians lay eggs in water, which hatch into tadpoles.
chunks.source: Amphibians lay eggs in water, which hatch into tadpoles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a type of pollination? A: Self pollination. The two types are self pollination and cross pollination.
chunks.source: The two types are self pollination and cross pollination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another type of pollination? A: Cross pollination. In cross pollination, pollen moves from one flower to another.
chunks.source: In cross pollination, pollen moves from one flower to another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an agent of pollination? A: Bees (insects). Agents of pollination: insects, wind, water, birds and animals.
chunks.source: Agents of pollination: insects, wind, water, birds and animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the importance of a safety pin when giving First Aid? A: For fastening bandages. A safety pin holds bandages firmly in place.
chunks.source: A safety pin holds bandages firmly in place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the importance of cotton wool when giving First Aid? A: For cleaning wounds. Cotton wool is used to clean wounds and apply medicine.
chunks.source: Cotton wool is used to clean wounds and apply medicine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an importance of giving First Aid to an accident victim? A: To save life. First aid saves life and stops injuries from getting worse.
chunks.source: First aid saves life and stops injuries from getting worse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the blood cell drawn below? A: Red blood cell. The round disc-shaped cell drawn is a red blood cell.
chunks.source: The round disc-shaped cell drawn is a red blood cell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a two diseases which attack the red blood cell? A: Malaria and sickle cell anaemia. Malaria parasites and sickle cell disease attack red blood cells.
chunks.source: Malaria parasites and sickle cell disease attack red blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of preserving meat? A: Salting. Meat is preserved by salting, smoking, drying or freezing.
chunks.source: Meat is preserved by salting, smoking, drying or freezing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another way of preserving meat? A: Smoking. Smoke dries meat and keeps germs away.
chunks.source: Smoke dries meat and keeps germs away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of a fish, name part marked B: ___. A: Tail fin (caudal fin). B points to the tail fin, which pushes the fish forward in water.
chunks.source: B points to the tail fin, which pushes the fish forward in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a part marked C? A: Gills. C points to the gills, which the fish uses for breathing in water.
chunks.source: C points to the gills, which the fish uses for breathing in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part does a fish use to protect itself from enemies? A: Scales. The hard overlapping scales cover and protect the fish's body.
chunks.source: The hard overlapping scales cover and protect the fish's body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one duty of a worker bee in a hive: ___. A: Collecting nectar (and pollen). Worker bees collect nectar and pollen, make honey, clean the hive and guard it.
chunks.source: Worker bees collect nectar and pollen, make honey, clean the hive and guard it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write another duty of a worker bee in a hive: ___. A: Making honey. Workers also feed the queen and the young bees.
chunks.source: Workers also feed the queen and the young bees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from worker bees, which of the following is another type of bee in the hive? A: Queen bee. A hive has the queen, workers and drones.
chunks.source: A hive has the queen, workers and drones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is cassava harvested? A: By uprooting. Cassava tubers are pulled out of the soil by uprooting the plant.
chunks.source: Cassava tubers are pulled out of the soil by uprooting the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is coffee harvested? A: By hand picking. Ripe coffee berries are picked by hand.
chunks.source: Ripe coffee berries are picked by hand.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of controlling crop pests in a garden? A: Spraying with pesticides. Pests are controlled by spraying, crop rotation, weeding and hand picking.
chunks.source: Pests are controlled by spraying, crop rotation, weeding and hand picking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another way of controlling crop pests in a garden? A: Crop rotation. Changing crops each season breaks the life cycle of pests.
chunks.source: Changing crops each season breaks the life cycle of pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an effect of drug dependence to an individual? A: Poor health (mental illness). Drug dependence ruins health, causes madness, poverty and school dropout.
chunks.source: Drug dependence ruins health, causes madness, poverty and school dropout.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way in which a child can acquire immunity? A: Through immunization (vaccination). Children get immunity through vaccination, recovery from illness, or from the mother.
chunks.source: Children get immunity through vaccination, recovery from illness, or from the mother.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another way in which a child can acquire immunity? A: Through recovery from an illness. After recovering from a disease, the body remembers how to fight it.
chunks.source: After recovering from a disease, the body remembers how to fight it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way in which a person's body immunity can be increased? A: By eating a balanced diet. Good feeding, immunization and exercise strengthen immunity.
chunks.source: Good feeding, immunization and exercise strengthen immunity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of the human digestive system, name part marked P: ___. A: Oesophagus (gullet). P is the tube carrying food from the mouth to the stomach: the oesophagus.
chunks.source: P is the tube carrying food from the mouth to the stomach: the oesophagus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a part marked Q? A: Stomach. Q is the bag-like stomach where food is churned and mixed with juices.
chunks.source: Q is the bag-like stomach where food is churned and mixed with juices.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the digestive juice produced by part marked S? A: Bile. S is the liver, which produces bile juice.
chunks.source: S is the liver, which produces bile juice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you maintain the proper working of the system shown in the diagram? A: By eating a balanced diet. Eat balanced meals, drink clean water, deworm regularly and avoid alcohol.
chunks.source: Eat balanced meals, drink clean water, deworm regularly and avoid alcohol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one method of making alcohol: ___. A: Fermentation. Alcohol is made by fermentation of sugary juices (note: the booklet prints "meaning" but means "making").
chunks.source: Alcohol is made by fermentation of sugary juices (note: the booklet prints "meaning" but means "making").

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a reason why some people drink alcohol? A: For pleasure. Some drink for leisure, to socialize or to forget problems.
chunks.source: Some drink for leisure, to socialize or to forget problems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another reason why some people drink alcohol? A: To socialize with friends. Others drink to feel brave or to cope with stress.
chunks.source: Others drink to feel brave or to cope with stress.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a medical instrument which uses alcohol to function? A: Clinical thermometer. Some clinical thermometers use alcohol instead of mercury.
chunks.source: Some clinical thermometers use alcohol instead of mercury.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a percussion musical instrument? A: Drum. Percussion instruments are hit or shaken: drum, xylophone, bell.
chunks.source: Percussion instruments are hit or shaken: drum, xylophone, bell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a string musical instrument? A: Guitar. String instruments have strings that are plucked or bowed: guitar, harp, violin.
chunks.source: String instruments have strings that are plucked or bowed: guitar, harp, violin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a method of storing sound? A: Recording. Sound is stored by recording on tapes, CDs or phones.
chunks.source: Sound is stored by recording on tapes, CDs or phones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of an exotic breed of cattle? A: Friesian. Exotic cattle breeds: Friesian, Jersey, Guernsey, Ayrshire.
chunks.source: Exotic cattle breeds: Friesian, Jersey, Guernsey, Ayrshire.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another example of an exotic breed of cattle? A: Jersey. Jersey cows give milk rich in butterfat.
chunks.source: Jersey cows give milk rich in butterfat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are draught cattle useful to farmers? A: For ploughing (and pulling carts). Draught cattle pull ploughs and carts on the farm.
chunks.source: Draught cattle pull ploughs and carts on the farm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of controlling internal parasites in cattle? A: Deworming (drenching). Internal parasites (worms) are controlled by regular deworming.
chunks.source: Internal parasites (worms) are controlled by regular deworming.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which term is used to describe the loss of water and mineral salts from the body? A: Dehydration. Losing too much water and salts from the body is called dehydration.
chunks.source: Losing too much water and salts from the body is called dehydration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a sign of dehydration? A: Sunken eyes. Signs: sunken eyes, dry mouth, great thirst, passing little urine.
chunks.source: Signs: sunken eyes, dry mouth, great thirst, passing little urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another sign of dehydration? A: Dry mouth (great thirst). The patient feels very thirsty and the tongue is dry.
chunks.source: The patient feels very thirsty and the tongue is dry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What advice is given to a friend who is dehydrated? A: Drink ORS (plenty of fluids). A dehydrated person should drink oral rehydration salts and plenty of fluids.
chunks.source: A dehydrated person should drink oral rehydration salts and plenty of fluids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an item used for sweeping? A: Broom. A broom is used for sweeping floors and compounds.
chunks.source: A broom is used for sweeping floors and compounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a member of a nuclear family? A: Father. A nuclear family is made of father, mother and their children.
chunks.source: A nuclear family is made of father, mother and their children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from use of chemicals, which of the following is another way of controlling pests in a garden? A: Crop rotation. Pests can also be controlled by crop rotation, weeding, hand picking and proper spacing.
chunks.source: Pests can also be controlled by crop rotation, weeding, hand picking and proper spacing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part of the flower which attracts pollinators is the ___. A: Petals. The bright colourful petals attract insects and other pollinators to the flower.
chunks.source: The bright colourful petals attract insects and other pollinators to the flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an importance of transpiration to plants? A: It cools the plant. Transpiration cools the plant and pulls water and minerals up from the roots.
chunks.source: Transpiration cools the plant and pulls water and minerals up from the roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the eggs, which of the following is another dormant stage in the life cycle of a butterfly? A: Pupa. The dormant (resting) stages are the egg and the pupa.
chunks.source: The dormant (resting) stages are the egg and the pupa.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are the standard units for measuring mass? A: Kilograms (kg). Mass is measured in kilograms.
chunks.source: Mass is measured in kilograms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of keeping the body clean? A: Bathing daily. Bathing, brushing teeth and washing hands keep the body clean.
chunks.source: Bathing, brushing teeth and washing hands keep the body clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of an annual crop? A: Maize. Annual crops mature in one year: maize, beans, groundnuts.
chunks.source: Annual crops mature in one year: maize, beans, groundnuts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an exotic breed of goats that provides people with mohair? A: Angora. Angora goats produce mohair, a soft silky fibre.
chunks.source: Angora goats produce mohair, a soft silky fibre.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way AIDS can be spread from one person to another? A: Through unprotected sexual intercourse. AIDS spreads through unprotected sex, sharing sharp instruments and infected blood.
chunks.source: AIDS spreads through unprotected sex, sharing sharp instruments and infected blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a play material made from banana fibres? A: Dolls. Banana fibres are woven into dolls, balls and ropes for play.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are woven into dolls, balls and ropes for play.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write P.H.C in full: ___. A: Primary Health Care. PHC stands for Primary Health Care.
chunks.source: PHC stands for Primary Health Care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of root system shown in the diagram above? A: Taproot system. The diagram shows one main root with side roots: a taproot system.
chunks.source: The diagram shows one main root with side roots: a taproot system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one danger of plants: ___. A: Some plants are poisonous. Some plants are poisonous, have thorns or harbour dangerous animals.
chunks.source: Some plants are poisonous, have thorns or harbour dangerous animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of change is the boiling of an egg? A: Chemical change. Boiling an egg forms a new substance and cannot be reversed: a chemical change.
chunks.source: Boiling an egg forms a new substance and cannot be reversed: a chemical change.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the source of papyrus used in making mats? A: Swamps (wetlands). Papyrus reeds grow in swamps and are used for mats and crafts.
chunks.source: Papyrus reeds grow in swamps and are used for mats and crafts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do birds keep their feathers clean and smooth? A: By preening (using their beaks). Birds preen, arranging their feathers with the beak and oiling them.
chunks.source: Birds preen, arranging their feathers with the beak and oiling them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an importance of the sun to the environment? A: It gives light and heat. The sun gives light and warmth and helps green plants make food.
chunks.source: The sun gives light and warmth and helps green plants make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the food value obtained from eating honey? A: Carbohydrates. Honey is rich in carbohydrates, which give the body energy.
chunks.source: Honey is rich in carbohydrates, which give the body energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which season do farmers irrigate their crops? A: Dry season. Crops are watered (irrigated) in the dry season when there is no rain.
chunks.source: Crops are watered (irrigated) in the dry season when there is no rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What germ causes haemophilus influenza b? A: Bacteria. Haemophilus influenzae is a bacterium.
chunks.source: Haemophilus influenzae is a bacterium.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does keeping fish in a pond help to control malaria in a home? A: Fish eat mosquito larvae. Fish feed on the mosquito larvae (wigglers) in water, stopping mosquitoes from breeding.
chunks.source: Fish feed on the mosquito larvae (wigglers) in water, stopping mosquitoes from breeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the two containers (A and B) has more heat? A: Container B. Container B holds more hot water, so it contains more heat energy.
chunks.source: Container B holds more hot water, so it contains more heat energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a group of people considered to be vulnerable? A: Babies. Vulnerable groups: babies, pregnant women, the elderly, the sick.
chunks.source: Vulnerable groups: babies, pregnant women, the elderly, the sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which property of air enables a person to suck soda with a straw? A: Air pressure (air exerts pressure). Air pressure pushes the soda up the straw when air is sucked out.
chunks.source: Air pressure pushes the soda up the straw when air is sucked out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a communicable disease caused by a fungus? A: Ringworm. Fungal communicable diseases include ringworm and athlete's foot.
chunks.source: Fungal communicable diseases include ringworm and athlete's foot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the body organ affected by the disease mentioned in (a) above? A: Skin. Ringworm attacks the skin.
chunks.source: Ringworm attacks the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of preventing the spread of ringworm? A: Avoid sharing clothes and towels. Prevent ringworm by keeping skin clean and dry and not sharing personal items.
chunks.source: Prevent ringworm by keeping skin clean and dry and not sharing personal items.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a factor that may cause seed dormancy? A: Hard seed coat. A very hard seed coat or an immature embryo can cause dormancy.
chunks.source: A very hard seed coat or an immature embryo can cause dormancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another factor that may cause seed dormancy? A: Immature embryo. If the young plant inside is not fully grown, the seed stays dormant.
chunks.source: If the young plant inside is not fully grown, the seed stays dormant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of an insect, name part marked X: ___. A: Antenna (antennae). X points to the antenna, the insect's feeler on its head.
chunks.source: X points to the antenna, the insect's feeler on its head.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of an insect balances it when flying? A: Wings. Likely answer: the wings keep the insect steady and balanced in flight.
chunks.source: Likely answer: the wings keep the insect steady and balanced in flight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a characteristic of insects? A: They have six legs. Insects have six legs, three body parts and one pair of antennae.
chunks.source: Insects have six legs, three body parts and one pair of antennae.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from cassava and beet roots, which of the following is another example of a root tuber? A: Sweet potato. Root tubers: sweet potatoes, carrots.
chunks.source: Root tubers: sweet potatoes, carrots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another example of a root tuber? A: Carrot. Carrots store food in their swollen roots.
chunks.source: Carrots store food in their swollen roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a viral disease of cassava? A: Cassava mosaic disease. Cassava mosaic is a virus disease spread by whiteflies.
chunks.source: Cassava mosaic is a virus disease spread by whiteflies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way cassava is harvested? A: By uprooting. Cassava is harvested by pulling (uprooting) the plant from the soil.
chunks.source: Cassava is harvested by pulling (uprooting) the plant from the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagrams of teeth, name the type of tooth marked S: ___. A: Molar. S is broad and flat with a wide crown: a molar.
chunks.source: S is broad and flat with a wide crown: a molar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of tooth marked T? A: Canine. T is sharp and pointed: a canine.
chunks.source: T is sharp and pointed: a canine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the function of the tooth marked S? A: For grinding (crushing) food. Molars grind and crush food into small pieces.
chunks.source: Molars grind and crush food into small pieces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the function of the tooth marked T? A: For tearing food. Canines are sharp and pointed for tearing meat.
chunks.source: Canines are sharp and pointed for tearing meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What causes ear canker? A: Mites (ear mites). Likely answer: ear canker in rabbits is caused by tiny mites (parasites) in the ear.
chunks.source: Likely answer: ear canker in rabbits is caused by tiny mites (parasites) in the ear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from ear canker, which of the following is another disease of rabbits? A: Coccidiosis. Likely answer: other rabbit diseases include coccidiosis and snuffles (pneumonia).
chunks.source: Likely answer: other rabbit diseases include coccidiosis and snuffles (pneumonia).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another disease of rabbits? A: Snuffles (pneumonia). Likely answer: snuffles is a respiratory disease of rabbits.
chunks.source: Likely answer: snuffles is a respiratory disease of rabbits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an exotic breed of rabbits kept in Uganda? A: New Zealand White. Likely answer: exotic rabbit breeds include New Zealand White and Californian.
chunks.source: Likely answer: exotic rabbit breeds include New Zealand White and Californian.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we call the act of suckling milk from the breasts? A: Breast feeding. Suckling milk from the mother's breasts is called breast feeding.
chunks.source: Suckling milk from the mother's breasts is called breast feeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a raw material needed by plants during photosynthesis? A: Carbon dioxide. Plants need carbon dioxide and water to make food in sunlight.
chunks.source: Plants need carbon dioxide and water to make food in sunlight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another raw material needed by plants during photosynthesis? A: Water. Roots absorb the water used in photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Roots absorb the water used in photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of a thermos flask, name part labeled B: ___. A: Outer case (metal/plastic cover). Likely answer: B points to the outer protective case of the flask.
chunks.source: Likely answer: B points to the outer protective case of the flask.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a part labeled D? A: Base (insulating pad). Likely answer: D points to the base on which the flask stands.
chunks.source: Likely answer: D points to the base on which the flask stands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a material from which part C is made? A: Glass. C is the double-walled glass bottle with a vacuum between the walls.
chunks.source: C is the double-walled glass bottle with a vacuum between the walls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way vectors spread germs that cause diseases? A: Through bites. Vectors spread germs by biting people or by contaminating food.
chunks.source: Vectors spread germs by biting people or by contaminating food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another way vectors spread germs that cause diseases? A: By contaminating food. Houseflies carry germs on their bodies onto our food.
chunks.source: Houseflies carry germs on their bodies onto our food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a disease whose germs are spread by vectors? A: Malaria. Vector-spread diseases: malaria, cholera, typhoid, sleeping sickness.
chunks.source: Vector-spread diseases: malaria, cholera, typhoid, sleeping sickness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another disease whose germs are spread by vectors? A: Cholera. Houseflies spread cholera germs onto food.
chunks.source: Houseflies spread cholera germs onto food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way soil loses its fertility? A: Soil erosion. Soil loses fertility through erosion, leaching, over-cultivation and bush burning.
chunks.source: Soil loses fertility through erosion, leaching, over-cultivation and bush burning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another way soil loses its fertility? A: Leaching. Heavy rain washes nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach.
chunks.source: Heavy rain washes nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way of preventing soil from losing its fertility? A: Mulching. Mulching, crop rotation, terracing and manuring protect soil fertility.
chunks.source: Mulching, crop rotation, terracing and manuring protect soil fertility.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another way of preventing soil from losing its fertility? A: Crop rotation. Planting different crops each season keeps the soil rich.
chunks.source: Planting different crops each season keeps the soil rich.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a place where bacteria are found? A: In the soil. Bacteria are found in soil, air, water and decaying matter.
chunks.source: Bacteria are found in soil, air, water and decaying matter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a way in which bacteria are useful in the environment? A: They decompose dead matter. Bacteria rot dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.
chunks.source: Bacteria rot dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the substances that kill/prevent the growth of bacteria? A: Antibiotics. Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria or stop them growing.
chunks.source: Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria or stop them growing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a play material made from banana fibres? A: Dolls. Banana fibres are woven into dolls, balls and ropes for children to play with.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are woven into dolls, balls and ropes for children to play with.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an effect of alcoholism to a community? A: Poverty. Alcoholism brings poverty, violence, accidents and broken families to a community.
chunks.source: Alcoholism brings poverty, violence, accidents and broken families to a community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of a tool used at home, name part marked B: ___. A: Mortar. B points to the bowl (mortar); A is the pestle used for pounding inside it.
chunks.source: B points to the bowl (mortar); A is the pestle used for pounding inside it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one way you would reduce egg eating on a poultry farm: ___. A: Debeak the birds. Debeaking, collecting eggs often and feeding the birds well reduce egg eating.
chunks.source: Debeaking, collecting eggs often and feeding the birds well reduce egg eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which disease of the eyes is spread by a housefly? A: Trachoma. Houseflies spread trachoma, a disease that damages the eyes.
chunks.source: Houseflies spread trachoma, a disease that damages the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which water borne disease affects the liver resulting to liver cancer? A: Bilharzia (schistosomiasis). Bilharzia worms damage the liver and can lead to liver cancer.
chunks.source: Bilharzia worms damage the liver and can lead to liver cancer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the liquid marked Y in the diagram (a boy put water and oil in a container)? A: Water. Oil floats on water; Y marks the lower layer, which is water. (The extracted image file P614141315img.jpg is blank/unusable, so no image is attached.)
chunks.source: Oil floats on water; Y marks the lower layer, which is water. (The extracted image file P614141315img.jpg is blank/unusable, so no image is attached.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is millet and sorghum propagated? A: By planting seeds. Millet and sorghum are grown by sowing their seeds.
chunks.source: Millet and sorghum are grown by sowing their seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a factor you would consider before selecting a site for house? A: Well-drained land. Choose land that is well-drained, near clean water, secure and not in a swamp.
chunks.source: Choose land that is well-drained, near clean water, secure and not in a swamp.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the garden tool drawn in the diagram below? A: Garden fork (digging fork). The long-handled forked tool is a garden (digging) fork.
chunks.source: The long-handled forked tool is a garden (digging) fork.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an use of the above garden tool to a farmer? A: For digging (loosening) the soil. A garden fork digs and loosens soil and turns manure.
chunks.source: A garden fork digs and loosens soil and turns manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one characteristic of essential drugs: ___. A: They are affordable (cheap). Essential drugs are affordable, available, safe and effective.
chunks.source: Essential drugs are affordable, available, safe and effective.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of pollination illustrated below? A: Self pollination. The arrows show pollen moving within the same flower: self pollination.
chunks.source: The arrows show pollen moving within the same flower: self pollination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a stem tuber? A: Irish potato. Stem tubers include Irish potatoes and yams.
chunks.source: Stem tubers include Irish potatoes and yams.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of a crustacean? A: Crab. Crustaceans have hard shells: crab, lobster, prawn.
chunks.source: Crustaceans have hard shells: crab, lobster, prawn.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a crop farmer reduce overcrowding of plants in a garden? A: By thinning (proper spacing). Thinning removes extra seedlings so the rest get enough space, light and nutrients.
chunks.source: Thinning removes extra seedlings so the rest get enough space, light and nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of energy is possessed by water at 100C? A: Heat energy. Boiling water at 100C contains a lot of heat energy.
chunks.source: Boiling water at 100C contains a lot of heat energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the legume store above? A: Granary. The raised grass-thatched store in the diagram is a granary for keeping grains and legumes.
chunks.source: The raised grass-thatched store in the diagram is a granary for keeping grains and legumes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one message that may be said to children during a health parade: ___. A: Wash your hands before eating. Health parade messages: wash hands, brush teeth, cut nails, keep clean.
chunks.source: Health parade messages: wash hands, brush teeth, cut nails, keep clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which group of musical instruments does the instrument drawn below belong? A: String (musical) instruments. The drawn instrument has a string stretched over a bridge: a string instrument.
chunks.source: The drawn instrument has a string stretched over a bridge: a string instrument.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A farmer recorded how many times his goat and rabbit ate each food. What was the most favourable food for the rabbit? A: Sweet potatoes (eaten 4 times). The rabbit ate sweet potatoes 4 times, more than any other food.
chunks.source: The rabbit ate sweet potatoes 4 times, more than any other food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What was the least favourable food for the rabbit? A: Sorghum leaves (eaten 0 times). The rabbit never ate sorghum leaves.
chunks.source: The rabbit never ate sorghum leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from carbon dioxide, which of the following is another part (component) of air? A: Oxygen. Air is made of nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, water vapour and dust.
chunks.source: Air is made of nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, water vapour and dust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another part (component) of air? A: Nitrogen. Nitrogen makes up the largest part of air.
chunks.source: Nitrogen makes up the largest part of air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an use of carbon dioxide to people? A: For putting out fire. Carbon dioxide puts out fires, is used by plants to make food, and makes drinks fizzy.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide puts out fires, is used by plants to make food, and makes drinks fizzy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another use of carbon dioxide to people? A: In photosynthesis (by plants). Plants need carbon dioxide to make food.
chunks.source: Plants need carbon dioxide to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A P.6 class boiled well water and did the experiment shown. Identify the method used to clean the water: ___. A: Filtration. Pouring water through filter paper to remove dirt is called filtration.
chunks.source: Pouring water through filter paper to remove dirt is called filtration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What scientific name is given to the substance labeled T? A: Residue. T is the dirt trapped on the filter paper: the residue.
chunks.source: T is the dirt trapped on the filter paper: the residue.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What scientific name is given to the substance labeled K? A: Filtrate. K is the clean liquid collected below: the filtrate.
chunks.source: K is the clean liquid collected below: the filtrate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the element of P.H.C responsible for controlling of over population? A: Family planning. Family planning is the PHC element that controls overpopulation.
chunks.source: Family planning is the PHC element that controls overpopulation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the element of P.H.C responsible for controlling of bad body odour? A: Personal hygiene. Personal hygiene keeps the body clean and free from bad smell.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene keeps the body clean and free from bad smell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the element of P.H.C responsible for controlling killer diseases among children? A: Immunization. Immunization protects children against the killer diseases.
chunks.source: Immunization protects children against the killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one activity you can do to promote PHC in school: ___. A: Health parade (general cleaning). Health parades, cleaning the compound and health talks promote PHC.
chunks.source: Health parades, cleaning the compound and health talks promote PHC.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What kind of food is eaten by the bird in the diagram? A: Flesh (meat). The hooked beak is for tearing flesh: the bird eats meat.
chunks.source: The hooked beak is for tearing flesh: the bird eats meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which group of birds does it belong? A: Birds of prey. Eagles, hawks and kites with hooked beaks are birds of prey.
chunks.source: Eagles, hawks and kites with hooked beaks are birds of prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a bird that has a beak like the one drawn above? A: Eagle. Eagles, hawks and kites have strong hooked beaks.
chunks.source: Eagles, hawks and kites have strong hooked beaks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a danger of the bird you have named in (c) above to people? A: It eats (steals) people's chicken. Birds of prey snatch chickens and chicks from homes.
chunks.source: Birds of prey snatch chickens and chicks from homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the use of cotton (wool) in first aid management? A: For cleaning wounds. Cotton wool cleans wounds before dressing.
chunks.source: Cotton wool cleans wounds before dressing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the type of blood vessel drawn above? A: Vein. The vessel has valves (W) that stop backflow: it is a vein.
chunks.source: The vessel has valves (W) that stop backflow: it is a vein.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which first aid is given to a near drowned victim who has been removed from water? A: Artificial respiration (mouth to mouth). Give artificial respiration to restore breathing.
chunks.source: Give artificial respiration to restore breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where does absorption of alcohol take place in the human digestive system? A: In the stomach. Alcohol is absorbed into the blood mainly through the stomach walls.
chunks.source: Alcohol is absorbed into the blood mainly through the stomach walls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another adaptation of the ileum that enables it to absorb digested food? A: It has villi (finger-like projections). Villi greatly increase the absorbing surface of the ileum.
chunks.source: Villi greatly increase the absorbing surface of the ileum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an insect that contaminates our food? A: Housefly. Houseflies land on faeces then on food, contaminating it.
chunks.source: Houseflies land on faeces then on food, contaminating it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one example of a disease spread through contaminated food: ___. A: Cholera. Contaminated food spreads cholera, typhoid and dysentery.
chunks.source: Contaminated food spreads cholera, typhoid and dysentery.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest one way you would prevent contamination of food by the vector named in (a) above: ___. A: Cover food (properly). Cover food, kill flies and keep the surroundings clean.
chunks.source: Cover food, kill flies and keep the surroundings clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from paddock grazing, which of the following is another system of grazing cattle? A: Zero grazing. Grazing systems: paddock, zero grazing, tethering, herding (free range), strip grazing.
chunks.source: Grazing systems: paddock, zero grazing, tethering, herding (free range), strip grazing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another system of grazing cattle? A: Tethering. In tethering, an animal is tied with a rope to graze in one spot.
chunks.source: In tethering, an animal is tied with a rope to graze in one spot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a source of heat used for cooking food at home? A: Firewood. Heat for cooking comes from firewood, charcoal, paraffin, gas or electricity.
chunks.source: Heat for cooking comes from firewood, charcoal, paraffin, gas or electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another source of heat used for cooking food at home? A: Charcoal. Charcoal burns with steady heat in stoves.
chunks.source: Charcoal burns with steady heat in stoves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a food value that provides heat to the body? A: Carbohydrates. Carbohydrates (and fats) are burnt in the body to release heat and energy.
chunks.source: Carbohydrates (and fats) are burnt in the body to release heat and energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of an insect, name part marked O: ___. A: Thorax. O points to the middle segment of the insect's body: the thorax. (The answer line in the booklet is mislabeled Q, but the question asks for O and P.)
chunks.source: O points to the middle segment of the insect's body: the thorax. (The answer line in the booklet is mislabeled Q, but the question asks for O and P.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a part marked P? A: Antenna (antennae). P points to the feeler on the head: the antenna.
chunks.source: P points to the feeler on the head: the antenna.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the thermometer above? A: Clinical thermometer. The thermometer with a kink for measuring body temperature is a clinical thermometer.
chunks.source: The thermometer with a kink for measuring body temperature is a clinical thermometer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is the liquid commonly used in the above thermometer? A: Mercury. Clinical thermometers commonly use mercury.
chunks.source: Clinical thermometers commonly use mercury.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mushroom is an example of a fungus. A: True. Fungi are living things that feed on dead matter; mushroom, yeast and mould are common examples.
chunks.source: Fungi are living things that feed on dead matter; mushroom, yeast and mould are common examples.

chunks.subject: Science
