chunks.text: Q: The bee which does most of the duties in a beehive is not the worker bee. A: False. Worker bees clean the hive, feed the young, collect nectar and guard the hive.
chunks.source: Worker bees clean the hive, feed the young, collect nectar and guard the hive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a fertilized egg. The part marked X is the yolk. A: True. The yolk is the yellow central part of the egg that feeds the growing chick.
chunks.source: The yolk is the yellow central part of the egg that feeds the growing chick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way through which heat travels is not conduction. A: False. Heat travels by conduction in solids, by convection in fluids and by radiation through space.
chunks.source: Heat travels by conduction in solids, by convection in fluids and by radiation through space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A cat is helpful to a crop farmer because it kills rats that destroy crops. A: True. Cats hunt rats and mice that would otherwise eat growing and stored crops.
chunks.source: Cats hunt rats and mice that would otherwise eat growing and stored crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of cow dung to people is not it is used as manure. A: False. Cow dung adds nutrients to the soil and can also be dried and used as fuel.
chunks.source: Cow dung adds nutrients to the soil and can also be dried and used as fuel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides a toothbrush, one other material used in the promotion of oral health is toothpaste. A: True. Toothpaste contains fluoride, which strengthens teeth and prevents decay.
chunks.source: Toothpaste contains fluoride, which strengthens teeth and prevents decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a glass of cold water from a fridge. The process that led to the formation of water droplets on the glass is not condensation. A: False. Water vapour in the air touched the cold glass, cooled and changed into liquid droplets.
chunks.source: Water vapour in the air touched the cold glass, cooled and changed into liquid droplets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wetlands promote the spread of malaria because they are breeding places for mosquitoes. A: True. Stagnant water in wetlands is where mosquitoes lay their eggs.
chunks.source: Stagnant water in wetlands is where mosquitoes lay their eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A lion is not different from an antelope in the way they feed because the lion is a carnivore while the antelope is a herbivore. A: False. Lions eat flesh (meat) while antelopes feed on grass and plants.
chunks.source: Lions eat flesh (meat) while antelopes feed on grass and plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The major component of air in the atmosphere is nitrogen. A: True. Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air we breathe.
chunks.source: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air we breathe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One item that cannot be used to harvest resources such as water is a tank. A: False. Roof tanks, drums and jerrycans store rainwater harvested from roofs.
chunks.source: Roof tanks, drums and jerrycans store rainwater harvested from roofs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a wingless insect is a flea. A: True. Fleas, lice and silverfish are insects that have no wings.
chunks.source: Fleas, lice and silverfish are insects that have no wings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One healthy lifestyle that cannot help you fight skin diseases is bathing the body daily. A: False. Washing removes dirt and germs that cause skin infections.
chunks.source: Washing removes dirt and germs that cause skin infections.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A piece of paper floats on water because it is less dense (lighter) than water. A: True. Objects that are less dense than water float on it.
chunks.source: Objects that are less dense than water float on it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The main product obtained from a cow is not milk. A: False. Likely answer: milk. The diagram was not extractable, but cows are mainly kept for milk (and meat).
chunks.source: Likely answer: milk. The diagram was not extractable, but cows are mainly kept for milk (and meat).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The common way through which HIV is spread is through unprotected sexual intercourse. A: True. HIV passes through body fluids, most commonly during unprotected sex.
chunks.source: HIV passes through body fluids, most commonly during unprotected sex.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from drinking, one use of water to a school child is not washing (bathing). A: False. Water is also needed for washing, cleaning and cooking.
chunks.source: Water is also needed for washing, cleaning and cooking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One element of Primary Health Care (P.H.C.) is immunization. A: True. P.H.C. elements include immunization, safe water, sanitation and nutrition education.
chunks.source: P.H.C. elements include immunization, safe water, sanitation and nutrition education.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One agent of soil erosion is not running water. A: False. Running water and wind carry away the top fertile soil.
chunks.source: Running water and wind carry away the top fertile soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The organ of hearing in insects is the antennae. A: True. Insects detect sound vibrations with their antennae.
chunks.source: Insects detect sound vibrations with their antennae.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The type of weather suitable for winnowing is not windy weather. A: False. Wind blows away the light husks while the heavy grain falls down.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light husks while the heavy grain falls down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One activity that can destroy habitats of wild animals is deforestation. A: True. Cutting down forests removes the homes and food of wild animals.
chunks.source: Cutting down forests removes the homes and food of wild animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One importance of heat from the sun is not drying clothes and harvested crops. A: False. The sun's heat dries our clothes and helps preserve harvested crops.
chunks.source: The sun's heat dries our clothes and helps preserve harvested crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a building material (a brick). The natural resource from which it is made is clay (soil). A: True. Bricks are moulded from clay soil and then baked so they harden.
chunks.source: Bricks are moulded from clay soil and then baked so they harden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way people abuse drugs is not taking an overdose. A: False. Drug abuse includes taking an overdose and taking drugs without a doctor's advice.
chunks.source: Drug abuse includes taking an overdose and taking drugs without a doctor's advice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The seed shown in the diagram is dispersed by wind. A: True. Likely answer: wind. The seed appears to have wing-like structures that let wind carry it.
chunks.source: Likely answer: wind. The seed appears to have wing-like structures that let wind carry it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Layers is not a type of chicken reared in Uganda. A: False. Layers are kept for eggs and broilers are kept for meat in Uganda.
chunks.source: Layers are kept for eggs and broilers are kept for meat in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Broilers is another type of chicken reared in Uganda. A: True. Broilers grow fast and are kept for meat.
chunks.source: Broilers grow fast and are kept for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The system of poultry keeping commonly used by most rural farmers is not free range. A: False. Rural farmers let chickens roam freely to find their own food.
chunks.source: Rural farmers let chickens roam freely to find their own food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The system of poultry keeping commonly used by most commercial farmers is deep litter. A: True. Commercial farmers keep many birds indoors on the floor (deep litter) or in cages.
chunks.source: Commercial farmers keep many birds indoors on the floor (deep litter) or in cages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a respiratory system. The part marked Y is not the trachea (windpipe). A: False. The trachea is the tube that carries air from the nose to the lungs.
chunks.source: The trachea is the tube that carries air from the nose to the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part marked Z is the nostrils (nose). A: True. Air enters the respiratory system through the nostrils.
chunks.source: Air enters the respiratory system through the nostrils.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The process that takes place in part labelled X is not gaseous exchange (breathing). A: False. In the lungs, oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.
chunks.source: In the lungs, oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way the above respiratory system can be kept healthy is to avoid smoking. A: True. Smoke damages the lungs; exercise and clean air keep them healthy.
chunks.source: Smoke damages the lungs; exercise and clean air keep them healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Polio is not a childhood immunisable disease caused by a virus. A: False. Polio and measles are viral diseases prevented by immunization.
chunks.source: Polio and measles are viral diseases prevented by immunization.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tuberculosis is a childhood immunisable disease caused by bacteria. A: True. Tuberculosis, whooping cough and diphtheria are bacterial diseases prevented by immunization.
chunks.source: Tuberculosis, whooping cough and diphtheria are bacterial diseases prevented by immunization.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Immunization is not important to people because it protects them against killer diseases. A: False. Vaccines build immunity so the body can fight disease germs.
chunks.source: Vaccines build immunity so the body can fight disease germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the animals: goose, fish, lizard, rabbit, frog, bat. One similarity among all the animals above is that they all are vertebrates (have backbones). A: True. All these animals have a backbone, so they are all vertebrates.
chunks.source: All these animals have a backbone, so they are all vertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: From the list above, one animal that has not fur on its body is the rabbit. A: False. Rabbits and bats are mammals, and mammals have fur or hair.
chunks.source: Rabbits and bats are mammals, and mammals have fur or hair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: From the list above, another animal that has fur on its body is the bat. A: True. Bats are mammals, so their bodies are covered with fur.
chunks.source: Bats are mammals, so their bodies are covered with fur.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The animal product used to make part X is not skin (hide/leather). A: False. Drum skins are made from animal hide stretched tightly over the drum.
chunks.source: Drum skins are made from animal hide stretched tightly over the drum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One factor that can affect the pitch of sound produced by the instrument above is the tightness of the skin. A: True. A tighter skin vibrates faster and gives a higher pitch.
chunks.source: A tighter skin vibrates faster and gives a higher pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The importance of stomata to a plant is not for gaseous exchange. A: False. Stomata are tiny holes in leaves through which gases and water vapour pass.
chunks.source: Stomata are tiny holes in leaves through which gases and water vapour pass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One condition needed by plants to grow well is water. A: True. Plants need water, sunlight, air and fertile soil to grow well.
chunks.source: Plants need water, sunlight, air and fertile soil to grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another condition needed by plants to grow well is not sunlight. A: False. Plants use sunlight to make food by photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants use sunlight to make food by photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The instrument used to measure rainfall is a rain gauge. A: True. A rain gauge collects rain so its depth can be measured.
chunks.source: A rain gauge collects rain so its depth can be measured.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Rainfall is not measured in millimetres. A: False. The depth of collected rain is read in millimetres (mm).
chunks.source: The depth of collected rain is read in millimetres (mm).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One other weather instrument is the thermometer. A: True. A thermometer measures temperature; other instruments include the anemometer and wind vane.
chunks.source: A thermometer measures temperature; other instruments include the anemometer and wind vane.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another weather instrument is not the anemometer. A: False. An anemometer measures the speed of wind.
chunks.source: An anemometer measures the speed of wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A school compound should be kept clean to prevent the spread of diseases. A: True. A clean compound has fewer germs and looks beautiful.
chunks.source: A clean compound has fewer germs and looks beautiful.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One component of a clean home is not a clean latrine. A: False. A clean home has a clean latrine, a clean kitchen and proper rubbish disposal.
chunks.source: A clean home has a clean latrine, a clean kitchen and proper rubbish disposal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another component of a clean home is a clean kitchen. A: True. Food must be prepared in a clean place to avoid contamination.
chunks.source: Food must be prepared in a clean place to avoid contamination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One component of a balanced diet is not carbohydrates. A: False. A balanced diet has carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, fats, minerals, fibre and water.
chunks.source: A balanced diet has carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, fats, minerals, fibre and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: People are advised to eat a balanced diet in order to grow well and stay healthy. A: True. A balanced diet gives the body all nutrients and prevents deficiency diseases.
chunks.source: A balanced diet gives the body all nutrients and prevents deficiency diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One sign of poor feeding in children is not a thin body. A: False. Poorly fed children become thin, have swollen bellies or brown hair.
chunks.source: Poorly fed children become thin, have swollen bellies or brown hair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another sign of poor feeding in children is a swollen belly. A: True. Kwashiorkor causes the belly to swell in poorly fed children.
chunks.source: Kwashiorkor causes the belly to swell in poorly fed children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The use of hole marked B is not to put in charcoal. A: False. Charcoal is pushed into the stove through hole B.
chunks.source: Charcoal is pushed into the stove through hole B.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The fuel used by the stove above is charcoal. A: True. The stove burns charcoal to heat the saucepan.
chunks.source: The stove burns charcoal to heat the saucepan.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from sun drying, one other method of food preservation is not salting. A: False. Salting, smoking, refrigeration and tinning also preserve food.
chunks.source: Salting, smoking, refrigeration and tinning also preserve food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from sun drying, another method of food preservation is smoking. A: True. Smoking removes water from food so germs cannot grow in it.
chunks.source: Smoking removes water from food so germs cannot grow in it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One foodstuff that is not preserved by sun drying is cassava. A: False. Cassava, maize, beans and fish are commonly sun dried.
chunks.source: Cassava, maize, beans and fish are commonly sun dried.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another foodstuff that is preserved by sun drying is maize. A: True. Drying maize grains in the sun keeps them for a long time.
chunks.source: Drying maize grains in the sun keeps them for a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One item needed by a person going to harvest honey is not a bee veil. A: False. A veil, smoker, overall and gloves protect the harvester from stings.
chunks.source: A veil, smoker, overall and gloves protect the harvester from stings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another item needed by a person going to harvest honey is a smoker. A: True. Smoke calms the bees so honey can be harvested safely.
chunks.source: Smoke calms the bees so honey can be harvested safely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The best time for harvesting honey is not in the evening (at night). A: False. Bees are less active and docile in the cool of the evening.
chunks.source: Bees are less active and docile in the cool of the evening.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One importance of soil is it supports plant growth. A: True. Soil holds plants and gives them water and nutrients.
chunks.source: Soil holds plants and gives them water and nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Another importance of soil is not it is used for building. A: False. Soil is used to make bricks and to smear houses.
chunks.source: Soil is used to make bricks and to smear houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One harmful material on soil is polythene (plastics). A: True. Polythene, chemicals and broken glass harm the soil.
chunks.source: Polythene, chemicals and broken glass harm the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One importance of PIASCY in schools is not it sensitizes pupils about HIV/AIDS. A: False. PIASCY teaches pupils how HIV spreads and how to avoid it.
chunks.source: PIASCY teaches pupils how HIV spreads and how to avoid it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Oil (paraffin) is a liquid that can float on water. A: True. Oil is less dense than water, so it floats on top of it.
chunks.source: Oil is less dense than water, so it floats on top of it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sorting and recycling waste is not a way of managing wastes in the environment. A: False. Sorting rubbish and recycling keeps the environment clean and reduces pollution.
chunks.source: Sorting rubbish and recycling keeps the environment clean and reduces pollution.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Drones is the type of bees in a hive that mate with the queen bee. A: True. Drones are the male bees whose duty is to mate with the queen.
chunks.source: Drones are the male bees whose duty is to mate with the queen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Carbon dioxide is not the component of air used in stopping fire outbreak. A: False. Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so fire extinguishers release it to put out fires.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so fire extinguishers release it to put out fires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Liver is an organ which is damaged when an individual over-depends on alcohol. A: True. Too much alcohol damages the liver and can cause liver disease.
chunks.source: Too much alcohol damages the liver and can cause liver disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Diarrhoea is not a cause of dehydration among children. A: False. Diarrhoea and vomiting make the body lose a lot of water.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea and vomiting make the body lose a lot of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Brain is the human body organ found in the head that helps us to remember things. A: True. The brain controls thinking, memory and all body activities.
chunks.source: The brain controls thinking, memory and all body activities.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Humus is not a component of soil. A: False. Soil is made of humus, air, water and small rock particles.
chunks.source: Soil is made of humus, air, water and small rock particles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Constipation is a disorder of the digestive system. A: True. Constipation, diarrhoea and indigestion are disorders of the digestive system.
chunks.source: Constipation, diarrhoea and indigestion are disorders of the digestive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Layers should not be fed on feeds containing enough calcium for formation of strong eggshells. A: False. Calcium makes the shells of eggs hard and strong.
chunks.source: Calcium makes the shells of eggs hard and strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one way in which people can destroy their environment: deforestation. A: True. Cutting down trees and bush burning destroy the environment.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees and bush burning destroy the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Beans is not an example of a leguminous crop. A: False. Beans, groundnuts, peas and soya beans are leguminous crops that add nitrogen to soil.
chunks.source: Beans, groundnuts, peas and soya beans are leguminous crops that add nitrogen to soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Using umbrellas is a way in which people can manage rainy weather. A: True. Umbrellas, raincoats and gumboots protect people from rain.
chunks.source: Umbrellas, raincoats and gumboots protect people from rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Insects have not three main body parts. Give any one of them: head. A: False. An insect's body has a head, thorax and abdomen.
chunks.source: An insect's body has a head, thorax and abdomen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Floods is a natural cause of changes in the environment. A: True. Floods, drought, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions change the environment naturally.
chunks.source: Floods, drought, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions change the environment naturally.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Ear is not the sense organ that helps one to detect a dog barking. A: False. The ear detects sound such as a dog barking.
chunks.source: The ear detects sound such as a dog barking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Rain is a source of water. A: True. Rain, wells, boreholes and rivers are sources of water.
chunks.source: Rain, wells, boreholes and rivers are sources of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Kinetic energy is not the type of energy possessed by a moving object. A: False. Anything that moves has kinetic energy.
chunks.source: Anything that moves has kinetic energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Goitre is the deficiency disease the person in the diagram is suffering from. A: True. The swollen neck (goitre) is caused by lack of iodine in the diet.
chunks.source: The swollen neck (goitre) is caused by lack of iodine in the diet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Immunization is not an element of Primary Health Care. A: False. Immunization, safe water and sanitation are elements of Primary Health Care.
chunks.source: Immunization, safe water and sanitation are elements of Primary Health Care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It damages the liver is an effect of alcohol to an individual. A: True. Alcohol can damage the liver and make a person lose self-control.
chunks.source: Alcohol can damage the liver and make a person lose self-control.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cotton is not a plant that produces fibre. A: False. Cotton, sisal and flax give fibres used for cloth and ropes.
chunks.source: Cotton, sisal and flax give fibres used for cloth and ropes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To look for food is a reason why animals move from one place to another. A: True. Animals move to find food, water, shelter, mates and to escape danger.
chunks.source: Animals move to find food, water, shelter, mates and to escape danger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To escape from danger is not another reason why animals move from one place to another. A: False. Animals run away from enemies that want to eat them.
chunks.source: Animals run away from enemies that want to eat them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List one foodstuff that can be preserved by smoking: fish. A: True. Fish and meat are preserved by smoking over fire.
chunks.source: Fish and meat are preserved by smoking over fire.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List one foodstuff that cannot be preserved by sun drying: cassava. A: False. Cassava, maize and beans are dried in the sun for storage.
chunks.source: Cassava, maize and beans are dried in the sun for storage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List one foodstuff that can be preserved by pasteurization: milk. A: True. Milk is heated gently (pasteurized) to kill germs and keep longer.
chunks.source: Milk is heated gently (pasteurized) to kill germs and keep longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sugar is not a material used in making ORS. A: False. ORS is made by dissolving sugar and salt in clean boiled water.
chunks.source: ORS is made by dissolving sugar and salt in clean boiled water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Salt is another material used in making ORS. A: True. Salt replaces the body salts lost during diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Salt replaces the body salts lost during diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: E is not the bar which will produce the lowest pitch. A: False. Likely answer: E. The longest bar vibrates slowest and gives the lowest pitch; E appears to be the longest bar.
chunks.source: Likely answer: E. The longest bar vibrates slowest and gives the lowest pitch; E appears to be the longest bar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Red blood cells is the blood component that transports oxygen to all body parts. A: True. Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to all body parts.
chunks.source: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to all body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Drinking plenty of fluids is not another way in which you can increase the amount of blood in your body. A: False. Fluids increase the liquid part of blood.
chunks.source: Fluids increase the liquid part of blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Peer pressure is a reason why people smoke. A: True. Some people start smoking because friends influence them.
chunks.source: Some people start smoking because friends influence them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To relieve stress is not another reason why people smoke. A: False. Some people wrongly believe smoking reduces stress.
chunks.source: Some people wrongly believe smoking reduces stress.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Assertiveness (saying no) is a life skill that can safeguard you against smoking. A: True. Being assertive helps you refuse cigarettes confidently.
chunks.source: Being assertive helps you refuse cigarettes confidently.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Axe is not the garden tool marked B. A: False. An axe is used for cutting wood.
chunks.source: An axe is used for cutting wood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Splitting firewood is an use of tool marked B at home. A: True. The axe splits logs into firewood for cooking.
chunks.source: The axe splits logs into firewood for cooking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is not of the reproductive system of a woman. Name the part marked A: uterus (womb). A: False. The uterus is where the baby grows during pregnancy.
chunks.source: The uterus is where the baby grows during pregnancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Vagina (birth canal) is the part marked C. A: True. The vagina is the passage through which the baby is born.
chunks.source: The vagina is the passage through which the baby is born.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Gonorrhoea is not a sexually transmitted disease that attacks the system above. A: False. Gonorrhoea, syphilis and HIV attack the reproductive system.
chunks.source: Gonorrhoea, syphilis and HIV attack the reproductive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They cause anaemia is a danger of hookworms to people. A: True. Hookworms suck blood, making the person anaemic and weak.
chunks.source: Hookworms suck blood, making the person anaemic and weak.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one health habit that cannot help people to avoid worm infestation: wearing shoes. A: False. Shoes stop hookworms entering through the feet.
chunks.source: Shoes stop hookworms entering through the feet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down another health habit that can help people to avoid worm infestation: washing hands before eating. A: True. Clean hands keep worm eggs out of food.
chunks.source: Clean hands keep worm eggs out of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Dry grass is not a material farmers use to mulch a garden. A: False. Dry grass, banana leaves and coffee husks are used as mulch.
chunks.source: Dry grass, banana leaves and coffee husks are used as mulch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Banana leaves is another material farmers use to mulch a garden. A: True. Banana leaves spread on soil keep moisture and stop weeds.
chunks.source: Banana leaves spread on soil keep moisture and stop weeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It controls weeds is not another importance of mulching. A: False. Mulch blocks sunlight so weeds cannot grow.
chunks.source: Mulch blocks sunlight so weeds cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It preserves culture (customs) is an advantage of food taboo. A: True. Food taboos keep some cultural practices alive.
chunks.source: Food taboos keep some cultural practices alive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Stunted growth is not an effect of poor feeding to babies. A: False. Poorly fed babies do not grow well and fall sick easily.
chunks.source: Poorly fed babies do not grow well and fall sick easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Microscope is the instrument we can use to see bacteria. A: True. Bacteria are too small to see, so we use a microscope.
chunks.source: Bacteria are too small to see, so we use a microscope.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Firewood is not an example of wood fuel commonly used by people in Uganda. A: False. Firewood and charcoal are the common wood fuels used in Uganda.
chunks.source: Firewood and charcoal are the common wood fuels used in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Flash disk is a sound storage device that can produce sound in a computer. A: True. Flash disks, CDs and memory cards store sound that a computer can play.
chunks.source: Flash disks, CDs and memory cards store sound that a computer can play.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Spade is not the garden tool drawn below. A: False. A spade is used for digging and lifting soil.
chunks.source: A spade is used for digging and lifting soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Layers is a type of poultry commonly kept in Uganda today. A: True. Layers (for eggs), broilers (for meat) and local chicken are kept in Uganda.
chunks.source: Layers (for eggs), broilers (for meat) and local chicken are kept in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It destroys soil fertility is not a negative effect of bush burning to the environment. A: False. Bush burning kills soil organisms and burns the humus in soil.
chunks.source: Bush burning kills soil organisms and burns the humus in soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Chewing food well is a behaviour or habit that can maintain good working conditions of the digestive system. A: True. Chewing food properly and eating on time keep the digestive system working well.
chunks.source: Chewing food properly and eating on time keep the digestive system working well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Deworming regularly is not a way of controlling intestinal worms in people. A: False. Taking deworming tablets kills intestinal worms.
chunks.source: Taking deworming tablets kills intestinal worms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down the weapon that can be used by a wasp to defend itself from its enemies: its sting. A: True. A wasp stings its enemies to defend itself.
chunks.source: A wasp stings its enemies to defend itself.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The immunisation schedule in Uganda is not free and mandatory. Identify one group of people who must be immunised: children under five (infants). A: False. Babies and young children are immunised against killer diseases.
chunks.source: Babies and young children are immunised against killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows an animal kept at home. Give one common product people who keep such animals can get: meat. A: True. Rabbits are kept for meat and also give skins and manure.
chunks.source: Rabbits are kept for meat and also give skins and manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Baking (bread making) is not a food processing method in which yeast plays a big role. A: False. Yeast makes dough rise when baking bread.
chunks.source: Yeast makes dough rise when baking bread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: During the preparation of ORS, sugar and salt are dissolved in the water. Give one use of sugar to the patient who drinks ORS: it gives the patient energy. A: True. Sugar in ORS provides energy to the weak patient.
chunks.source: Sugar in ORS provides energy to the weak patient.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Light and heat from the sun is not known as sunshine. State one use of the light to plants in the environment: for photosynthesis (making food). A: False. Plants use sunlight to make their food.
chunks.source: Plants use sunlight to make their food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Boiling is a way of killing germs in water. A: True. Boiling kills the germs in water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tuberculosis is not a communicable disease that spreads through air. A: False. Tuberculosis, influenza and measles spread through the air.
chunks.source: Tuberculosis, influenza and measles spread through the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Night blindness is the deficiency disease due to lack of vitamin A. A: True. Lack of vitamin A makes it hard to see at night.
chunks.source: Lack of vitamin A makes it hard to see at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sandy soil is not the type of soil whose texture is rough and has large particles. A: False. Sandy soil has large rough particles and drains water fast.
chunks.source: Sandy soil has large rough particles and drains water fast.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Using umbrellas is a way people can protect themselves against rainy weather. A: True. Umbrellas and raincoats keep people dry in the rain.
chunks.source: Umbrellas and raincoats keep people dry in the rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Encouraging people to use latrines is not an activity in which an individual can promote PHC in the community where he/she lives. A: False. Using latrines and keeping the environment clean promotes community health.
chunks.source: Using latrines and keeping the environment clean promotes community health.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A stone of 98g was lowered into a measuring cylinder and the water level rose from 18ml to 32ml. Find the volume of the stone: 14 ml. A: True. Volume = 32 ml - 18 ml = 14 ml of water displaced.
chunks.source: Volume = 32 ml - 18 ml = 14 ml of water displaced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wood is not a substance that can float on water. A: False. Wood is less dense than water so it floats.
chunks.source: Wood is less dense than water so it floats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows an insect that is a delicacy in Central Uganda. Name it: nsenene (grasshopper). A: True. Nsenene is the edible grasshopper enjoyed as a delicacy in Central Uganda.
chunks.source: Nsenene is the edible grasshopper enjoyed as a delicacy in Central Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It has six legs is not a characteristic of the above insect. A: False. Like all insects, nsenene has six legs and three body parts.
chunks.source: Like all insects, nsenene has six legs and three body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Grass (leaves) is a food for the above insect. A: True. Nsenene feeds on grass and green leaves.
chunks.source: Nsenene feeds on grass and green leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Porridge is not an example of weaning food. A: False. Weaning foods like porridge and mashed bananas are introduced gradually.
chunks.source: Weaning foods like porridge and mashed bananas are introduced gradually.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mashed bananas is another example of weaning food. A: True. Soft mashed foods are easy for babies to swallow.
chunks.source: Soft mashed foods are easy for babies to swallow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sheet erosion is not a type of soil erosion. A: False. Sheet, rill and gully erosion are types of soil erosion.
chunks.source: Sheet, rill and gully erosion are types of soil erosion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Gully erosion is another type of soil erosion. A: True. Gully erosion cuts deep channels in the land.
chunks.source: Gully erosion cuts deep channels in the land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Deforestation is not a cause of soil erosion in the environment. A: False. Cutting trees leaves soil bare so rain washes it away.
chunks.source: Cutting trees leaves soil bare so rain washes it away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For meat is a reason why people keep goats in Uganda. A: True. Goats are kept for meat, milk and income.
chunks.source: Goats are kept for meat, milk and income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For milk is not another reason why people keep goats in Uganda. A: False. Goat milk is drunk and sold.
chunks.source: Goat milk is drunk and sold.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Boer is a breed of goats kept in Uganda. A: True. Boer, Mubende and Small East African are goat breeds in Uganda.
chunks.source: Boer, Mubende and Small East African are goat breeds in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Anthrax is not a disease that attacks both goats and sheep. A: False. Anthrax attacks goats, sheep and cattle.
chunks.source: Anthrax attacks goats, sheep and cattle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: On the medical instrument below (a clinical thermometer), the part that prevents back flow of mercury is marked K. A: True. The kink (marked K) stops mercury flowing back into the bulb so the reading stays.
chunks.source: The kink (marked K) stops mercury flowing back into the bulb so the reading stays.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Natural immunity is not a type of immunity. A: False. Natural immunity is inborn; artificial immunity comes from vaccines.
chunks.source: Natural immunity is inborn; artificial immunity comes from vaccines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Health centre is a place in our community where we take children for immunization. A: True. Children are immunised at health centres and hospitals.
chunks.source: Children are immunised at health centres and hospitals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the animal that breathes through moist skin is not the earthworm. A: False. Earthworms breathe through their moist skins.
chunks.source: Earthworms breathe through their moist skins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the breathing organ of a housefly is the spiracles. A: True. Insects breathe through tiny holes called spiracles.
chunks.source: Insects breathe through tiny holes called spiracles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the animal that breathes through gills is not the fish. A: False. Fish breathe in water using gills.
chunks.source: Fish breathe in water using gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the table: the breathing organ of a cow is the lungs. A: True. Cows, like all mammals, breathe with lungs.
chunks.source: Cows, like all mammals, breathe with lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cassava is not an example of root crops in the environment. A: False. Cassava and sweet potatoes store food in their roots.
chunks.source: Cassava and sweet potatoes store food in their roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sweet potatoes is another example of root crops in the environment. A: True. Sweet potatoes are root tubers eaten boiled or roasted.
chunks.source: Sweet potatoes are root tubers eaten boiled or roasted.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cassava mosaic is not a disease that attacks root crops. A: False. Cassava mosaic disease makes cassava leaves mottled and reduces yields.
chunks.source: Cassava mosaic disease makes cassava leaves mottled and reduces yields.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Describe one way farmers can preserve harvested root crops for a long time: drying them in the sun. A: True. Sun-dried cassava chips keep for a long time.
chunks.source: Sun-dried cassava chips keep for a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Trachoma is not a disease that attacks the human eyes. A: False. Trachoma and conjunctivitis attack the eyes.
chunks.source: Trachoma and conjunctivitis attack the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Housefly is an example of a diurnal insect (active in day time). A: True. Houseflies and bees are active during the day.
chunks.source: Houseflies and bees are active during the day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mosquito is not an example of a nocturnal insect (active in the night). A: False. Mosquitoes and moths are active at night.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes and moths are active at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Bees give honey is an use of insects to people. A: True. Bees give honey and pollinate crops.
chunks.source: Bees give honey and pollinate crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They spread diseases is not a danger of insects to people. A: False. Mosquitoes and houseflies spread diseases like malaria and cholera.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes and houseflies spread diseases like malaria and cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Pinna is a part of the ear found in the outer ear. A: True. The pinna is the outer flap that collects sound.
chunks.source: The pinna is the outer flap that collects sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Ear drum (ossicles) is not a part of the ear found in the middle ear. A: False. The middle ear has the ear drum and three tiny bones (ossicles).
chunks.source: The middle ear has the ear drum and three tiny bones (ossicles).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Toadstool is a poisonous fungus. A: True. Toadstools are poisonous fungi that look like mushrooms but are harmful when eaten.
chunks.source: Toadstools are poisonous fungi that look like mushrooms but are harmful when eaten.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Dog is not a domestic animal that neither gives us milk nor meat. A: False. Dogs are kept for security, not for milk or meat.
chunks.source: Dogs are kept for security, not for milk or meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: As manure in the garden is a way in which people can use rabbit urine and dung at home. A: True. Rabbit droppings and urine add nutrients to the soil.
chunks.source: Rabbit droppings and urine add nutrients to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Calcium is not the mineral salt that helps in strengthening of our teeth and bones. A: False. Calcium builds strong teeth and bones; it is found in milk.
chunks.source: Calcium builds strong teeth and bones; it is found in milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: As vegetables is a way in which plant leaves can be useful to people. A: True. Leaves like cabbage are eaten as vegetables; others are used for mulching.
chunks.source: Leaves like cabbage are eaten as vegetables; others are used for mulching.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tooth decay is not an example of dental disorders. A: False. Tooth decay (cavities) is a common dental disorder.
chunks.source: Tooth decay (cavities) is a common dental disorder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Garden is a plant habitat. A: True. Gardens, forests and swamps are places where plants grow.
chunks.source: Gardens, forests and swamps are places where plants grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Operculum (gill cover) is not the part that protects the gills of a fish from mechanical injuries. A: False. The hard gill cover shields the delicate gills.
chunks.source: The hard gill cover shields the delicate gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cholera is a disease that people who live in a home without a latrine are likely to suffer from. A: True. Without a latrine, faeces spread germs that cause cholera and diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Without a latrine, faeces spread germs that cause cholera and diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Red blood cells is not the part of blood which carries oxygen to all body parts. A: False. Red blood cells pick oxygen from the lungs and deliver it everywhere.
chunks.source: Red blood cells pick oxygen from the lungs and deliver it everywhere.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Flower (ovary) is the part of a plant from which seeds are formed. A: True. After pollination, the flower's ovary develops into fruits with seeds.
chunks.source: After pollination, the flower's ovary develops into fruits with seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Boiling is not a way in which people may prepare cassava for eating. A: False. Cassava is peeled and boiled before eating.
chunks.source: Cassava is peeled and boiled before eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wood is an example of an object that floats on water. A: True. Wood is less dense than water, so it floats.
chunks.source: Wood is less dense than water, so it floats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Saliva is not the digestive juice which is added to food in the mouth. A: False. Saliva moistens food and starts digesting starch.
chunks.source: Saliva moistens food and starts digesting starch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mosquito is an insect vector that may spread more than one disease to people. A: True. Mosquitoes spread malaria, elephantiasis and yellow fever.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes spread malaria, elephantiasis and yellow fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Ropes is not a thing we can make from sisal. A: False. Sisal fibres are twisted into ropes, mats and baskets.
chunks.source: Sisal fibres are twisted into ropes, mats and baskets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Bad body smell is a problem of poor personal hygiene. A: True. Poor hygiene causes bad smell and skin diseases.
chunks.source: Poor hygiene causes bad smell and skin diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Drum is not an example of a percussion musical instrument. A: False. Drums and xylophones are played by hitting them.
chunks.source: Drums and xylophones are played by hitting them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Excessive drinking of alcohol is a habit that may endanger or bring trouble to the human liver. A: True. Too much alcohol damages the liver.
chunks.source: Too much alcohol damages the liver.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Temperature is not a factor that determines the rate of the above process. A: False. High temperature, wind, light and low humidity increase transpiration.
chunks.source: High temperature, wind, light and low humidity increase transpiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Humidity is another factor that determines the rate of the above process. A: True. Dry air (low humidity) makes transpiration faster.
chunks.source: Dry air (low humidity) makes transpiration faster.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To control weeds is not another reason why farmers mulch their gardens. A: False. Mulch blocks sunlight so weeds cannot grow.
chunks.source: Mulch blocks sunlight so weeds cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mercury is the liquid commonly used in the above thermometer. A: True. Mercury expands evenly with heat, making it good for thermometers.
chunks.source: Mercury expands evenly with heat, making it good for thermometers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Constipation is not a disorder of the digestive system. A: False. Constipation and diarrhoea are disorders of the digestive system.
chunks.source: Constipation and diarrhoea are disorders of the digestive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Diarrhoea is another disorder of the digestive system. A: True. Diarrhoea is the frequent passing of watery stool.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea is the frequent passing of watery stool.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cholera is not a disease that attacks the digestive system. A: False. Cholera and dysentery attack the digestive system.
chunks.source: Cholera and dysentery attack the digestive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Dysentery is another disease that attacks the digestive system. A: True. Dysentery causes bloody diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Dysentery causes bloody diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Papyrus is not a craft material got from swamps. A: False. Papyrus, clay and palm leaves are got from swamps for crafts.
chunks.source: Papyrus, clay and palm leaves are got from swamps for crafts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Clay is another craft material got from swamps. A: True. Swamp clay is used for pottery and crafts.
chunks.source: Swamp clay is used for pottery and crafts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Gardens is not a source of food in your community. A: False. Gardens and markets are sources of food.
chunks.source: Gardens and markets are sources of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Markets is another source of food in your community. A: True. Food is bought from markets and shops.
chunks.source: Food is bought from markets and shops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is not food useful in the human body? Give one way: it gives the body energy. A: False. Food gives energy and builds the body.
chunks.source: Food gives energy and builds the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Latrines is a place where germs are found. A: True. Germs live in latrines, rubbish pits and dirty places.
chunks.source: Germs live in latrines, rubbish pits and dirty places.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Through the air is not a way in which germs can be spread. A: False. Germs spread through air, dirty water, food and insect vectors.
chunks.source: Germs spread through air, dirty water, food and insect vectors.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Through contaminated water (and food) is another way in which germs can be spread. A: True. Drinking dirty water spreads germs like cholera.
chunks.source: Drinking dirty water spreads germs like cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Natural immunity is not a type of immunity. A: False. Natural immunity is inborn; artificial immunity comes from vaccines.
chunks.source: Natural immunity is inborn; artificial immunity comes from vaccines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Diphtheria is a disease controlled by immunizing using DPT vaccine. A: True. DPT protects against diphtheria, whooping cough (pertussis) and tetanus.
chunks.source: DPT protects against diphtheria, whooping cough (pertussis) and tetanus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tetanus is not another disease controlled by immunizing using DPT vaccine. A: False. Tetanus causes painful muscle stiffness.
chunks.source: Tetanus causes painful muscle stiffness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Burning is an of the above changes that produces a new substance. A: True. Burning and germination form new substances; melting and evaporation do not.
chunks.source: Burning and germination form new substances; melting and evaporation do not.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Germination is not another of the above changes that produces a new substance. A: False. A seedling is a new substance formed from the seed.
chunks.source: A seedling is a new substance formed from the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cleaning wounds is the use of cotton wool in first aid management. A: True. Cotton wool wipes dirt from wounds gently.
chunks.source: Cotton wool wipes dirt from wounds gently.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Covering (and tying) wounds is not the use of a bandage in first aid management. A: False. A bandage covers wounds and holds dressings in place.
chunks.source: A bandage covers wounds and holds dressings in place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sunshine (heat) is the element of weather suitable for removing moisture from harvested cereals. A: True. The sun's heat dries harvested cereals.
chunks.source: The sun's heat dries harvested cereals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: DPT is not a vaccine given to infants at the age of six weeks. A: False. At six weeks babies receive DPT and polio vaccines.
chunks.source: At six weeks babies receive DPT and polio vaccines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A solid block of mass 24g was dropped in an overflow can and displaces 12cm3 of water into a measuring cylinder. Find the density of the solid block: 2 g/cm3. A: True. Density = mass / volume = 24g / 12cm3 = 2 g/cm3.
chunks.source: Density = mass / volume = 24g / 12cm3 = 2 g/cm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Debeaking is not a way of controlling poultry vices on a farm. A: False. Debeaking stops birds pecking each other; enough space and feed also help.
chunks.source: Debeaking stops birds pecking each other; enough space and feed also help.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Electric shock is a danger of electricity at home. A: True. Touching naked wires can shock or even kill a person.
chunks.source: Touching naked wires can shock or even kill a person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In a deep pit is not a place where the soil profile can be seen properly. A: False. The soil layers are clearly visible on the walls of a deep pit.
chunks.source: The soil layers are clearly visible on the walls of a deep pit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sandy soil is the type of soil used in filtration of water. A: True. Water passes through sand, leaving dirt behind.
chunks.source: Water passes through sand, leaving dirt behind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Winnowing is not a way you can separate beans from bean husks. A: False. Wind blows away the light husks while heavy beans fall down.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light husks while heavy beans fall down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Avoid smoking is a way you can maintain the normal functioning of your respiratory system. A: True. Smoke damages the lungs; exercise keeps them strong.
chunks.source: Smoke damages the lungs; exercise keeps them strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Deworming them regularly is not a way of caring for sheep. A: False. Deworming, shelter and dipping keep sheep healthy.
chunks.source: Deworming, shelter and dipping keep sheep healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Flying is the role of part P to the insect. A: True. Part P (the wing) is used for flight.
chunks.source: Part P (the wing) is used for flight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Locusts is not an example of crop pests in the garden. A: False. Locusts, weevils and caterpillars are crop pests.
chunks.source: Locusts, weevils and caterpillars are crop pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Weevils is another example of crop pests in the garden. A: True. Weevils attack stored and growing crops.
chunks.source: Weevils attack stored and growing crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tooth decay is not a disease of the human teeth. A: False. Tooth decay is a disease that makes holes in teeth.
chunks.source: Tooth decay is a disease that makes holes in teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Misaligned teeth is a disorder of the human teeth. A: True. Likely answer: misaligned teeth. (Best-effort; the booklet gives no key.)
chunks.source: Likely answer: misaligned teeth. (Best-effort; the booklet gives no key.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Vagina (birth canal) is not the part marked Y. A: False. The vagina is the passage through which the baby is born.
chunks.source: The vagina is the passage through which the baby is born.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Gonorrhoea is a disease which affects the above organ. A: True. Gonorrhoea and syphilis attack the reproductive system.
chunks.source: Gonorrhoea and syphilis attack the reproductive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one PIASCY message that cannot protect school going children from contracting HIV/AIDS: Abstain from sex. A: False. Abstinence messages protect school children from HIV.
chunks.source: Abstinence messages protect school children from HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides floods, identify one natural change that can displace people: drought. A: True. Drought, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions displace people.
chunks.source: Drought, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions displace people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides floods, identify another natural change that cannot displace people: earthquakes. A: False. Earthquakes destroy homes, forcing people to move.
chunks.source: Earthquakes destroy homes, forcing people to move.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Dorsal fin is the part marked L. A: True. The dorsal fin is on the back of the fish.
chunks.source: The dorsal fin is on the back of the fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Ghee is not a product got from milk. A: False. Ghee, butter, yoghurt and cheese are made from milk.
chunks.source: Ghee, butter, yoghurt and cheese are made from milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Yoghurt is another product got from milk. A: True. Milk is fermented to make yoghurt.
chunks.source: Milk is fermented to make yoghurt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Air is not a component of soil that can also be used by animals for breathing. A: False. Soil has tiny air spaces between its particles, and soil animals such as earthworms breathe this air.
chunks.source: Soil has tiny air spaces between its particles, and soil animals such as earthworms breathe this air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Adult stage is the stage in the life cycle of a bee that is able to swarm. A: True. Swarming is done by a group of adult bees that leave the hive with a queen to start a new colony.
chunks.source: Swarming is done by a group of adult bees that leave the hive with a queen to start a new colony.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A mammal is not a warm-blooded vertebrate animal distinguished by the possession of fur or hair. Give any one example of such an animal: Cow. A: False. A cow has hair on its body, gives birth to live calves and feeds them on milk.
chunks.source: A cow has hair on its body, gives birth to live calves and feeds them on milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The outer covering of the bean seed shown in the diagram is called the Testa. A: True. The testa is the tough outer skin that protects the inside of the seed.
chunks.source: The testa is the tough outer skin that protects the inside of the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Communicable diseases are not diseases that can be spread from one person to another. Give any one example: Tuberculosis. A: False. Tuberculosis spreads through the air when an infected person coughs.
chunks.source: Tuberculosis spreads through the air when an infected person coughs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Honey is a product that apiary farmers regularly harvest from bee hives and sell or eat. State the food value we get from eating honey: Energy. A: True. Honey is rich in sugars, which the body burns to release energy.
chunks.source: Honey is rich in sugars, which the body burns to release energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Growth is not a biological change that takes place in animals. A: False. Growth is a biological change because a young animal develops into an adult and cannot change back.
chunks.source: Growth is a biological change because a young animal develops into an adult and cannot change back.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Dry season is the season in which cereal crop farmers are advised to harvest their crops. A: True. Crops harvested in the dry season stay dry and do not rot.
chunks.source: Crops harvested in the dry season stay dry and do not rot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Thinning is not another activity cereal crop farmers carry out during the 'caring stage'. A: False. Thinning removes extra seedlings so the remaining crops get enough space and nutrients.
chunks.source: Thinning removes extra seedlings so the remaining crops get enough space and nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Accidents are sudden happenings that cause harm to the body. Outline any one example of accidents: Road accident. A: True. A road accident happens suddenly and can injure people.
chunks.source: A road accident happens suddenly and can injure people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Thread is not the part marked Q in the diagram. A: False. The thread is tied to the irregular object so it can be lowered into the water.
chunks.source: The thread is tied to the irregular object so it can be lowered into the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Stone is a common example of an irregular object whose volume can be found in the same way. A: True. A stone has no regular shape, so its volume is found by the displacement method.
chunks.source: A stone has no regular shape, so its volume is found by the displacement method.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Animals is not another agent of soil erosion apart from running water. A: False. Animals walking and grazing loosen the soil, making it easy to wash away.
chunks.source: Animals walking and grazing loosen the soil, making it easy to wash away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Small intestine is another organ in the digestive system apart from teeth. A: True. Digested food is absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.
chunks.source: Digested food is absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Steps taken when preparing ORS locally are not listed above. Identify the solute: Sugar and salt. A: False. The solute is the substance that dissolves; here both sugar and salt dissolve in the water.
chunks.source: The solute is the substance that dissolves; here both sugar and salt dissolve in the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Water is the solvent from the ORS experiment. A: True. The solvent is the liquid in which other substances dissolve.
chunks.source: The solvent is the liquid in which other substances dissolve.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Battery cage system is not another method of keeping poultry birds besides free range system. A: False. In the battery cage system birds are kept in small individual cages.
chunks.source: In the battery cage system birds are kept in small individual cages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fold system is a third method of keeping poultry birds besides free range system. A: True. In the fold system a small movable house is shifted to fresh ground daily.
chunks.source: In the fold system a small movable house is shifted to fresh ground daily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Root system is not the part labeled Y in the diagram. A: False. The root system is made up of all the roots below the ground.
chunks.source: The root system is made up of all the roots below the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Oxygen is the by-product that part K (the leaf) produces during photosynthesis. A: True. During photosynthesis leaves take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen as a by-product.
chunks.source: During photosynthesis leaves take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen as a by-product.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mould is not another example of fungi besides yeast. A: False. Mould is a fungus that grows on stale food such as bread.
chunks.source: Mould is a fungus that grows on stale food such as bread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Emu is another bird which cannot fly apart from an ostrich. A: True. The emu is a large flightless bird like the ostrich.
chunks.source: The emu is a large flightless bird like the ostrich.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Plants provide food to animals is not an use of plants to animals. A: False. Herbivores feed directly on plants for their food.
chunks.source: Herbivores feed directly on plants for their food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Plants provide shelter to animals is another use of plants to animals. A: True. Trees give shade and hiding places to wild and domestic animals.
chunks.source: Trees give shade and hiding places to wild and domestic animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wool is not an animal fibre that can be got from sheep and goats. A: False. Sheep are sheared to get wool, a soft animal fibre.
chunks.source: Sheep are sheared to get wool, a soft animal fibre.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Goat farmers in Uganda usually find it hard when their goats die of diseases. Name any one disease that can kill goats: Anthrax. A: True. Anthrax is a deadly disease that kills goats and other livestock quickly.
chunks.source: Anthrax is a deadly disease that kills goats and other livestock quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By vaccinating the goats regularly is not a way goat farmers in Uganda can protect their goats against the disease you have named above. A: False. Vaccination builds immunity so the goats resist the disease.
chunks.source: Vaccination builds immunity so the goats resist the disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Charcoal is a common fuel used in the tool above. A: True. Burning charcoal inside the iron produces the heat for ironing.
chunks.source: Burning charcoal inside the iron produces the heat for ironing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: People are not encouraged to wash hands after visiting the latrine. Write down one material we use to wash hands which is in solid state: Soap. A: False. Soap is a solid that we rub on our hands with water.
chunks.source: Soap is a solid that we rub on our hands with water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one material we use to wash hands which is in liquid state: Water. A: True. Water is the liquid we use to rinse our hands.
chunks.source: Water is the liquid we use to rinse our hands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Dairy cattle is not the type of cattle that is useful in the production of yoghurt. A: False. Yoghurt is made from milk, and dairy cattle are kept for milk production.
chunks.source: Yoghurt is made from milk, and dairy cattle are kept for milk production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Freezing is the process through which water turns into ice. A: True. When water is cooled below 0C, it freezes into ice.
chunks.source: When water is cooled below 0C, it freezes into ice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Humus is not the component of soil formed as a result of decomposition. A: False. Humus is the dark material formed when dead plants and animals rot.
chunks.source: Humus is the dark material formed when dead plants and animals rot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Pulp is the part of a tooth that contains sensory nerves. A: True. The pulp is the soft centre of the tooth with nerves and blood vessels.
chunks.source: The pulp is the soft centre of the tooth with nerves and blood vessels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sound energy is not a form of energy which is produced when a drum is hit. A: False. Hitting the drum makes it vibrate, producing sound.
chunks.source: Hitting the drum makes it vibrate, producing sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Warmth is a factor which promotes quick breeding of bacteria. A: True. Bacteria multiply fastest in warm conditions.
chunks.source: Bacteria multiply fastest in warm conditions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Oxygen is not the component of air that keeps candle A burning. A: False. Oxygen supports burning; without it the candle flame goes out.
chunks.source: Oxygen supports burning; without it the candle flame goes out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By terracing the hillsides is a way of controlling soil erosion in hilly areas. A: True. Terraces are steps cut across slopes that slow down running water.
chunks.source: Terraces are steps cut across slopes that slow down running water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Dentine is not the part marked C in the diagram. A: False. Dentine is the layer just beneath the enamel.
chunks.source: Dentine is the layer just beneath the enamel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Clearing the land is an activity that a farmer does before planting seeds. A: True. Bushes and weeds must be cleared before seeds are planted.
chunks.source: Bushes and weeds must be cleared before seeds are planted.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Ploughing (digging) the land is not another activity that a farmer does before planting seeds. A: False. Digging loosens the soil so seeds can be planted easily.
chunks.source: Digging loosens the soil so seeds can be planted easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Layers is the type of chicken kept for egg production. A: True. Layers are chickens specially kept for laying eggs.
chunks.source: Layers are chickens specially kept for laying eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Broilers is not the type of chicken kept for meat production. A: False. Broilers grow very fast and are kept for meat.
chunks.source: Broilers grow very fast and are kept for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By drinking boiled water is a way of protecting yourself from getting diarrhoeal diseases. A: True. Boiling kills the germs that cause diarrhoeal diseases.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs that cause diarrhoeal diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By washing hands before eating is not another way of protecting yourself from getting diarrhoeal diseases. A: False. Clean hands stop germs from entering food.
chunks.source: Clean hands stop germs from entering food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Pig is a domestic animal that is kept only for meat production and neither for milk nor for its skin. A: True. Pigs are reared mainly for pork.
chunks.source: Pigs are reared mainly for pork.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Malaria is not a disease spread by mosquitoes to people. A: False. Female anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria.
chunks.source: Female anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cholera is a disease spread by house flies to people. A: True. Houseflies carry germs from faeces to food, spreading cholera.
chunks.source: Houseflies carry germs from faeces to food, spreading cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Rabies is not the disease spread by a rabid dog to people. A: False. A bite from a rabid dog transmits the deadly rabies virus.
chunks.source: A bite from a rabid dog transmits the deadly rabies virus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: High temperature is a factor that can increase the rate of transpiration. A: True. Heat makes water evaporate faster from the leaves.
chunks.source: Heat makes water evaporate faster from the leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wind is not another factor that can increase the rate of transpiration. A: False. Wind carries away water vapour, so leaves lose more water.
chunks.source: Wind carries away water vapour, so leaves lose more water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Condensation is the physical process taking place at Z. A: True. At Z, water vapour cools on the cold bottle and turns back into liquid.
chunks.source: At Z, water vapour cools on the cold bottle and turns back into liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Water cycle is not the natural process represented by the above diagram. A: False. The diagram models evaporation, condensation and precipitation like in nature.
chunks.source: The diagram models evaporation, condensation and precipitation like in nature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: DPT vaccine is another vaccine administered to babies apart from B.C.G. A: True. DPT protects babies against diphtheria, whooping cough and tetanus.
chunks.source: DPT protects babies against diphtheria, whooping cough and tetanus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The child's immunization record is not a feature found on a child health card. A: False. The card records every vaccine the child receives.
chunks.source: The card records every vaccine the child receives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The child's growth (weight) chart is another feature found on a child health card. A: True. The card shows the child's weight over time to track growth.
chunks.source: The card shows the child's weight over time to track growth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Red blood cells is not a component of blood. A: False. Red blood cells carry oxygen around the body.
chunks.source: Red blood cells carry oxygen around the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: White blood cells is another component of blood. A: True. White blood cells fight disease germs in the body.
chunks.source: White blood cells fight disease germs in the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Pancreatic juice is not the digestive juice produced by the pancreas. A: False. The pancreas releases pancreatic juice into the small intestine.
chunks.source: The pancreas releases pancreatic juice into the small intestine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Gastric juice is the digestive juice produced by the stomach. A: True. The stomach walls produce gastric juice to digest food.
chunks.source: The stomach walls produce gastric juice to digest food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sand soil is not the type of soil suitable for making glasses. A: False. Glass is made from silica, which is found in sand soil.
chunks.source: Glass is made from silica, which is found in sand soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The outer covering of the bean seed shown in the diagram is called the Testa. A: True. The testa is the protective outer skin of the seed.
chunks.source: The testa is the protective outer skin of the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Net fishing is not a recommended method of catching fish in Uganda. A: False. Fishing nets are the approved way of catching mature fish.
chunks.source: Fishing nets are the approved way of catching mature fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Boiling drinking water is an activity that can be carried out to prevent the spread of diarrhoeal diseases at home. A: True. Boiled water is germ-free and safe to drink.
chunks.source: Boiled water is germ-free and safe to drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Matooke is not a foodstuff that is prepared by peeling. A: False. Matooke must be peeled before it is cooked.
chunks.source: Matooke must be peeled before it is cooked.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fencing the water source is an activity done by a community to protect water sources from contamination. A: True. A fence keeps animals and people from dirtying the water source.
chunks.source: A fence keeps animals and people from dirtying the water source.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In a deep pit is not a place where a soil profile can be properly seen or observed by a class. A: False. The layers of soil are clearly visible on the walls of a deep pit.
chunks.source: The layers of soil are clearly visible on the walls of a deep pit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tuberculosis is a disease that people can mistake for being HIV/AIDS. A: True. TB causes weight loss and weakness just like AIDS.
chunks.source: TB causes weight loss and weakness just like AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Brushing teeth regularly is not a habit that promotes oral health. A: False. Regular brushing removes food remains and prevents tooth decay.
chunks.source: Regular brushing removes food remains and prevents tooth decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For lighting classrooms is an use of electricity at school. A: True. Electric lights brighten classrooms for reading.
chunks.source: Electric lights brighten classrooms for reading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Rainfall is not an example of natural changes in the environment. A: False. Rainfall is a natural change that happens without people's control.
chunks.source: Rainfall is a natural change that happens without people's control.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tuberculosis is a disease of the respiratory system. A: True. TB attacks the lungs, which are part of the respiratory system.
chunks.source: TB attacks the lungs, which are part of the respiratory system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Immunization (vaccination) is not the best way of preventing the bad effects of measles among infants in Uganda. A: False. The measles vaccine protects babies before they catch the disease.
chunks.source: The measles vaccine protects babies before they catch the disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cow is an example of domestic animals. A: True. Cows are kept at home and cared for by people.
chunks.source: Cows are kept at home and cared for by people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Goat is not another example of domestic animals. A: False. Goats are common domestic animals in Ugandan homes.
chunks.source: Goats are common domestic animals in Ugandan homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They breathe is a characteristic of living things. A: True. All living things take in air for respiration.
chunks.source: All living things take in air for respiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They reproduce is not another characteristic of living things. A: False. Living things produce young ones of their own kind.
chunks.source: Living things produce young ones of their own kind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Community participation is a principle of P.H.C. A: True. Communities must take part in planning their own health care.
chunks.source: Communities must take part in planning their own health care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Immunization is not an element of P.H.C. A: False. Immunization protects communities against killer diseases.
