chunks.source: Immunization protects communities against killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Provision of safe water is another element of P.H.C. A: True. Safe water prevents water-borne diseases in the community.
chunks.source: Safe water prevents water-borne diseases in the community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Vein is not the blood vessel labelled Q. A: False. Q has valves and thin walls, which are features of a vein.
chunks.source: Q has valves and thin walls, which are features of a vein.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For milk is a reason why people in Uganda keep cattle. A: True. Cattle provide milk for the family and for sale.
chunks.source: Cattle provide milk for the family and for sale.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Dairy cattle is not a type of cattle. A: False. Dairy cattle are kept mainly for milk production.
chunks.source: Dairy cattle are kept mainly for milk production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Beef cattle is another type of cattle. A: True. Beef cattle are kept mainly for meat.
chunks.source: Beef cattle are kept mainly for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By boiling it is not a way of making the water in Pot B safe for drinking. A: False. Boiling kills all the germs in the water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills all the germs in the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By filtering it is another way of making the water in Pot B safe for drinking. A: True. Filtering removes the remaining tiny dirt particles.
chunks.source: Filtering removes the remaining tiny dirt particles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It causes expansion is not an effect of heat on matter. A: False. Heated matter expands and takes up more space.
chunks.source: Heated matter expands and takes up more space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Warm-blooded vertebrates is the group of vertebrates marked Y. A: True. Y branches into birds and mammals, which keep a constant body temperature.
chunks.source: Y branches into birds and mammals, which keep a constant body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Birds is not the group of vertebrates marked S. A: False. S is the warm-blooded group with feathers that lay eggs.
chunks.source: S is the warm-blooded group with feathers that lay eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tapeworm is an intestinal worm in children. A: True. Tapeworms live in the intestines and steal digested food.
chunks.source: Tapeworms live in the intestines and steal digested food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Roundworm is not another intestinal worm in children. A: False. Roundworms are common intestinal worms in children.
chunks.source: Roundworms are common intestinal worms in children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Work out the density of K if its mass is 60g: 2.7g/cm³. A: True. Density = mass ÷ volume = 60g ÷ 22cm³ ≈ 2.7g/cm³.
chunks.source: Density = mass ÷ volume = 60g ÷ 22cm³ ≈ 2.7g/cm³.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Gills is not the part marked Y in the diagram. A: False. The gills are the thin plates under the cap that produce spores.
chunks.source: The gills are the thin plates under the cap that produce spores.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Condensation is the process labelled D. A: True. At D, water vapour cools high up and forms clouds.
chunks.source: At D, water vapour cools high up and forms clouds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tongue is not a body organ that helps a P.6 child to taste food. A: False. The tongue has taste buds that detect the taste of food.
chunks.source: The tongue has taste buds that detect the taste of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By boiling it is a way in which water can be made safe for drinking at home. A: True. Boiling kills the germs in water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It destroys crops and buildings is not a danger of wind in the environment. A: False. Strong wind blows down crops and damages houses.
chunks.source: Strong wind blows down crops and damages houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mr. Muwonge was advised by a doctor to eat more foods rich in iron. State the deficiency disease Mr. Muwonge was suffering from: Anaemia. A: True. Lack of iron causes anaemia, a shortage of healthy red blood cells.
chunks.source: Lack of iron causes anaemia, a shortage of healthy red blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a musical drum. Name the domestic animal from which part A (the drum skin) is not got: Cow. A: False. Drum skins are made from the hide of a cow.
chunks.source: Drum skins are made from the hide of a cow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sorting the clothes is the first step in washing clothes. A: True. Clothes are sorted by colour and dirtiness before washing.
chunks.source: Clothes are sorted by colour and dirtiness before washing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They are eaten as food is not an use of grasshoppers to people. A: False. Grasshoppers (nsenene) are a popular seasonal delicacy.
chunks.source: Grasshoppers (nsenene) are a popular seasonal delicacy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By uprooting is a method of harvesting cassava. A: True. Cassava roots are pulled out of the soil by uprooting the plant.
chunks.source: Cassava roots are pulled out of the soil by uprooting the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Layers is not a type of chicken. A: False. Layers are chickens kept for egg production.
chunks.source: Layers are chickens kept for egg production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Living organisms is the component of soil that helps to make soil. A: True. Likely answer: living organisms such as bacteria and earthworms break down dead matter and rock particles, helping to form soil.
chunks.source: Likely answer: living organisms such as bacteria and earthworms break down dead matter and rock particles, helping to form soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sperm is not the male reproductive cell of a mammal. A: False. The sperm is the male cell that fertilizes the egg.
chunks.source: The sperm is the male cell that fertilizes the egg.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It has a taproot system is a reason for your answer in (b) above. A: True. Taproots grow from dicot seeds, unlike the fibrous roots of monocots.
chunks.source: Taproots grow from dicot seeds, unlike the fibrous roots of monocots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By cleaning it regularly is not a way of caring for an ordinary pit latrine. A: False. Regular cleaning keeps the latrine hygienic.
chunks.source: Regular cleaning keeps the latrine hygienic.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cholera is a disease associated with poor use of latrines. A: True. Faeces near homes spread cholera germs to food and water.
chunks.source: Faeces near homes spread cholera germs to food and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Milk teeth (deciduous teeth) is not a set of teeth in humans. A: False. Milk teeth are the first set that falls out in childhood.
chunks.source: Milk teeth are the first set that falls out in childhood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Permanent teeth is the other set of teeth in humans. A: True. Permanent teeth replace milk teeth and last into adulthood.
chunks.source: Permanent teeth replace milk teeth and last into adulthood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mud (dirt particles) is not an impurity removed by using the above method. A: False. The filter paper traps mud and sand from the pond water.
chunks.source: The filter paper traps mud and sand from the pond water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The solid material trapped on the filter paper is called the Residue. A: True. The residue is the solid left behind on the filter paper.
chunks.source: The residue is the solid left behind on the filter paper.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They cause diseases is not a way in which bacteria are harmful:. A: False. Disease-causing bacteria make people and animals sick.
chunks.source: Disease-causing bacteria make people and animals sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one characteristic of seeds dispersed by wind: They are light. A: True. Light seeds are easily carried away by wind.
chunks.source: Light seeds are easily carried away by wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Length of the vibrating object is not a factor that affects the pitch of sound. A: False. Shorter strings vibrate faster and produce a higher pitch.
chunks.source: Shorter strings vibrate faster and produce a higher pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Stomach is the body organ represented by X. A: True. X points to the stomach in the abdomen.
chunks.source: X points to the stomach in the abdomen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Nectar is not a thing bees get from flowers. A: False. Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers to make honey.
chunks.source: Bees suck sweet nectar from flowers to make honey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Pollen is another thing bees get from flowers. A: True. Bees also collect pollen, which they use as food.
chunks.source: Bees also collect pollen, which they use as food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They help in pollination is not an importance of bees to flowering plants. A: False. As bees move, they carry pollen from flower to flower.
chunks.source: As bees move, they carry pollen from flower to flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Burning charcoal is the source of heat used above. A: True. The charcoal stove supplies the heat.
chunks.source: The charcoal stove supplies the heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Air holes (vents) is not the part of the charcoal stove that takes out warm air. A: False. Likely answer: the air holes let warm air and smoke escape from the stove.
chunks.source: Likely answer: the air holes let warm air and smoke escape from the stove.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wind is another element of weather that favours farmers' activities. A: True. Wind helps in winnowing harvested grains.
chunks.source: Wind helps in winnowing harvested grains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Condensation is not a physical process involved in the formation of clouds. A: False. Water vapour condenses high in the sky to form clouds.
chunks.source: Water vapour condenses high in the sky to form clouds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Brain is the body organ which stores information. A: True. The brain keeps everything we learn and remember.
chunks.source: The brain keeps everything we learn and remember.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By painting them is not a way of preventing metals from rusting. A: False. Paint covers metal so air and water cannot reach it.
chunks.source: Paint covers metal so air and water cannot reach it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Bat is an example of a nocturnal animal. A: True. Bats are active at night and rest during the day.
chunks.source: Bats are active at night and rest during the day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Armpit is not a body part where a thermometer is fixed to take the temperature. A: False. The thermometer is placed in the armpit to read body temperature.
chunks.source: The thermometer is placed in the armpit to read body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wool is a product from a Marino sheep. A: True. Merino sheep are famous for their fine wool.
chunks.source: Merino sheep are famous for their fine wool.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Polythene bags is not a soil pollutant. A: False. Polythene bags dumped in soil pollute it.
chunks.source: Polythene bags dumped in soil pollute it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from having a latrine, name any one other item a healthy home should have: A bathroom. A: True. A healthy home needs a bathroom for bathing.
chunks.source: A healthy home needs a bathroom for bathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Animal droppings is not a material used for making composite manure. A: False. Animal droppings rot into rich composite manure.
chunks.source: Animal droppings rot into rich composite manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They feed is a characteristic of living things. A: True. All living things take in food for energy.
chunks.source: All living things take in food for energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They grow is not another characteristic of living things. A: False. Living things increase in size as they develop.
chunks.source: Living things increase in size as they develop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Plants is a major group of living things. A: True. Plants are one major group of living things.
chunks.source: Plants are one major group of living things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Animals is not another major group of living things. A: False. Animals are the other major group of living things.
chunks.source: Animals are the other major group of living things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Bronchus is the part labeled F. A: True. The bronchus branches from the trachea into each lung.
chunks.source: The bronchus branches from the trachea into each lung.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Smoking is not a bad health practice that may affect proper functioning of the system. A: False. Smoke damages the lungs and air passages.
chunks.source: Smoke damages the lungs and air passages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Eggs is a product got from poultry farming. A: True. Poultry farms produce eggs for food and sale.
chunks.source: Poultry farms produce eggs for food and sale.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Diarrhoea is not a cause of dehydration. A: False. Diarrhoea drains a lot of water from the body.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea drains a lot of water from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Vomiting is another cause of dehydration. A: True. Vomiting also removes water from the body.
chunks.source: Vomiting also removes water from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Lion is not an example of a carnivorous mammal. A: False. The lion is a well-known flesh-eating mammal.
chunks.source: The lion is a well-known flesh-eating mammal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Bandage is an example of a first aid kit. A: True. A bandage is used to cover wounds.
chunks.source: A bandage is used to cover wounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It causes expansion is not an effect of heat on matter. A: False. Heated matter expands.
chunks.source: Heated matter expands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It causes change of state is another effect of heat on matter. A: True. Heat can melt solids and boil liquids.
chunks.source: Heat can melt solids and boil liquids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Nuclear family is not a type of family. A: False. A nuclear family has parents and their children only.
chunks.source: A nuclear family has parents and their children only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Extended family is another type of family. A: True. An extended family includes grandparents and other relatives.
chunks.source: An extended family includes grandparents and other relatives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: He protects the family is not another role of a father at home. A: False. Fathers keep the family safe from harm.
chunks.source: Fathers keep the family safe from harm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Liquid is the state of matter labeled P. A: True. Condensation changes gas into P, so P is a liquid.
chunks.source: Condensation changes gas into P, so P is a liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Evaporation is not the process of change of state of matter labeled M. A: False. M changes liquid P into gas.
chunks.source: M changes liquid P into gas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Freezing is the process of change of state of matter labeled N. A: True. N changes liquid P into solid Q, which is freezing. (Read from the diagram's arrow directions.)
chunks.source: N changes liquid P into solid Q, which is freezing. (Read from the diagram's arrow directions.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Taproot is not a type of root. A: False. A taproot grows straight down from the seed.
chunks.source: A taproot grows straight down from the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fibrous root is another type of root. A: True. Fibrous roots spread out in many thin branches.
chunks.source: Fibrous roots spread out in many thin branches.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Hoe is not a garden tool used in land preparation. A: False. A hoe digs and breaks the soil.
chunks.source: A hoe digs and breaks the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Spade is another garden tool used in land preparation. A: True. A spade cuts and turns the soil.
chunks.source: A spade cuts and turns the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Rake is not a third garden tool used in land preparation. A: False. A rake levels the dug soil.
chunks.source: A rake levels the dug soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Loam soil is the best soil for growing crops. A: True. Loam soil has sand, clay and humus mixed, so it holds water and air and is fertile.
chunks.source: Loam soil has sand, clay and humus mixed, so it holds water and air and is fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They produce (and release) spores is not the function of gills on a mushroom. A: False. The gills under the cap of a mushroom make the tiny spores used for reproduction.
chunks.source: The gills under the cap of a mushroom make the tiny spores used for reproduction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Air occupies space is a property of air. A: True. Air takes up space, has weight and exerts pressure even though we cannot see it.
chunks.source: Air takes up space, has weight and exerts pressure even though we cannot see it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria (Rhizobium) is not the organisms found in root nodules of legumes. A: False. Tiny bacteria living in the root nodules of beans and other legumes fix nitrogen from the air into the soil.
chunks.source: Tiny bacteria living in the root nodules of beans and other legumes fix nitrogen from the air into the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Vein is the blood vessel marked with letter I in the diagram. A: True. Likely answer: vessel I has a wide lumen and thin wall, which is how a vein is drawn (arteries have thick walls and narrow lumens).
chunks.source: Likely answer: vessel I has a wide lumen and thin wall, which is how a vein is drawn (arteries have thick walls and narrow lumens).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Liver is not an organ damaged by excessive alcoholism. A: False. Too much alcohol damages the liver (and also the brain and stomach).
chunks.source: Too much alcohol damages the liver (and also the brain and stomach).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Paracetamol (Panadol) is an example of an essential drug. A: True. Essential drugs are safe, affordable and always needed medicines such as paracetamol.
chunks.source: Essential drugs are safe, affordable and always needed medicines such as paracetamol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mulching is not a way of maintaining soil fertility. A: False. Adding manure or mulch, crop rotation and bush fallowing keep the soil fertile.
chunks.source: Adding manure or mulch, crop rotation and bush fallowing keep the soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Maize is an example of an annual crop. A: True. Annual crops grow and are harvested within one year, e.g. maize, beans, groundnuts.
chunks.source: Annual crops grow and are harvested within one year, e.g. maize, beans, groundnuts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Water is not the substance that exists in the three states of matter. A: False. Water exists as ice (solid), liquid water, and steam (gas).
chunks.source: Water exists as ice (solid), liquid water, and steam (gas).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Kilograms (kg) is the standard units for measuring mass. A: True. Mass is measured in kilograms; small masses in grams.
chunks.source: Mass is measured in kilograms; small masses in grams.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Hand picking is not a method of harvesting crops. A: False. Crops are harvested by hand picking, uprooting, cutting or digging.
chunks.source: Crops are harvested by hand picking, uprooting, cutting or digging.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sunken eyes is a sign of dehydration in babies. A: True. A dehydrated baby has sunken eyes, a dry mouth, a sunken soft spot on the head, or passes little urine.
chunks.source: A dehydrated baby has sunken eyes, a dry mouth, a sunken soft spot on the head, or passes little urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fermentation is not a method of making alcohol. A: False. Alcohol is made by fermentation (and concentrated by distillation).
chunks.source: Alcohol is made by fermentation (and concentrated by distillation).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Red blood cell is the blood cell that carries oxygen around the body. A: True. The red blood cell contains haemoglobin which carries oxygen to all body parts.
chunks.source: The red blood cell contains haemoglobin which carries oxygen to all body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cholera is not a disease spread through poor sanitation. A: False. Poor sanitation spreads cholera, typhoid, dysentery and diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Poor sanitation spreads cholera, typhoid, dysentery and diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Snail is the mollusc in the diagram below. A: True. The animal in the diagram with a coiled shell is a snail, which is a mollusc.
chunks.source: The animal in the diagram with a coiled shell is a snail, which is a mollusc.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.text: Q: Oil (cooking oil) is not an example of a liquid that floats on water. A: False. Oil, paraffin and petrol are less dense than water, so they float on it.
chunks.source: Oil, paraffin and petrol are less dense than water, so they float on it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Over speeding is a cause of road traffic accidents in Uganda. A: True. Accidents are caused by over speeding, drunk driving, bad roads and careless driving.
chunks.source: Accidents are caused by over speeding, drunk driving, bad roads and careless driving.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Washing hands before eating is not a good eating habit. A: False. Good eating habits include washing hands, chewing food well and eating a balanced diet.
chunks.source: Good eating habits include washing hands, chewing food well and eating a balanced diet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Natural immunity is the type of immunity acquired through recovery from illness. A: True. Immunity got after recovering from a disease is called natural immunity.
chunks.source: Immunity got after recovering from a disease is called natural immunity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Artificial immunity is not the type of immunity acquired through immunization. A: False. Immunity got through vaccines (immunization) is called artificial immunity.
chunks.source: Immunity got through vaccines (immunization) is called artificial immunity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Measles is an example of an immunisable disease. A: True. Immunisable diseases include measles, polio, tuberculosis, tetanus and whooping cough.
chunks.source: Immunisable diseases include measles, polio, tuberculosis, tetanus and whooping cough.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Burning (combustion) is not an example of a chemical change. A: False. Examples of chemical changes: burning, rusting, rotting, cooking food, digestion.
chunks.source: Examples of chemical changes: burning, rusting, rotting, cooking food, digestion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Rusting of iron is another example of a chemical change. A: True. Other examples: rotting of fruits, souring of milk, baking.
chunks.source: Other examples: rotting of fruits, souring of milk, baking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It breathes through gills is not a characteristic of the animal in group K. A: False. K is fish (grouped with reptiles and amphibians as cold-blooded); fish live in water and breathe through gills.
chunks.source: K is fish (grouped with reptiles and amphibians as cold-blooded); fish live in water and breathe through gills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Frog is an example of an amphibian. A: True. Amphibians live partly in water and partly on land, e.g. frog, toad.
chunks.source: Amphibians live partly in water and partly on land, e.g. frog, toad.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Matter expands (increases in size) is not an effect of heat gain on matter. A: False. When matter gains heat it expands, melts, evaporates or rises in temperature.
chunks.source: When matter gains heat it expands, melts, evaporates or rises in temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For cooking food is a way in which people use heat. A: True. People use heat for cooking, warming the house, drying clothes and ironing.
chunks.source: People use heat for cooking, warming the house, drying clothes and ironing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For warming the house is not another way in which people use heat. A: False. Heat is also used for drying harvested crops and warming bath water.
chunks.source: Heat is also used for drying harvested crops and warming bath water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Carrot is another example of a root tuber. A: True. Carrots are also swollen roots that store food.
chunks.source: Carrots are also swollen roots that store food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cassava mosaic disease is not a disease which affects cassava plants. A: False. Cassava is attacked by cassava mosaic disease (and cassava brown streak disease).
chunks.source: Cassava is attacked by cassava mosaic disease (and cassava brown streak disease).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Bathing the body daily is a way of promoting personal hygiene. A: True. Brushing teeth, washing hands, cutting nails short and bathing keep one clean.
chunks.source: Brushing teeth, washing hands, cutting nails short and bathing keep one clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Brushing the teeth (after meals) is not another way of promoting personal hygiene. A: False. Wearing clean clothes and washing hands before eating also promote hygiene.
chunks.source: Wearing clean clothes and washing hands before eating also promote hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Soap is an item used to promote good personal hygiene. A: True. Items like soap, toothbrush, towel and nail cutters promote personal hygiene.
chunks.source: Items like soap, toothbrush, towel and nail cutters promote personal hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part of the ear responsible for balancing the body is not the Semicircular canals. A: False. The semicircular canals in the inner ear help the body to balance.
chunks.source: The semicircular canals in the inner ear help the body to balance.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Whale is an example of a marine (sea) mammal. A: True. Marine mammals live in the sea but breathe air, e.g. whale, dolphin, seal.
chunks.source: Marine mammals live in the sea but breathe air, e.g. whale, dolphin, seal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Dolphin is not another example of a marine (sea) mammal. A: False. Dolphins are intelligent sea mammals that breathe through a blowhole.
chunks.source: Dolphins are intelligent sea mammals that breathe through a blowhole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Oxygen is the component of air used for: (i) respiration. A: True. Oxygen in air is used for respiration (breathing).
chunks.source: Oxygen in air is used for respiration (breathing).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Carbon dioxide is not the component of air used for: (ii) putting out fire. A: False. Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it is used to put out fire.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it is used to put out fire.

chunks.text: Q: It spreads diseases is a danger of wind to people. A: True. Strong wind destroys crops and houses, spreads diseases and causes accidents.
chunks.source: Strong wind destroys crops and houses, spreads diseases and causes accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Measuring cylinder is not a container B. A: False. Container B collects and measures the displaced water.
chunks.source: Container B collects and measures the displaced water.

chunks.text: Q: Calculate the density of the irregular object if its mass is 60 g: 6 g/cm3. A: True. Density = mass / volume = 60 g / 10 cc = 6 g/cm3.
chunks.source: Density = mass / volume = 60 g / 10 cc = 6 g/cm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Nicotine is not a poisonous substance found in tobacco. A: False. Tobacco contains nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide, which are poisonous.
chunks.source: Tobacco contains nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide, which are poisonous.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tar is another poisonous substance found in tobacco. A: True. Tar from tobacco smoke coats the lungs and can cause cancer.
chunks.source: Tar from tobacco smoke coats the lungs and can cause cancer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Low birth weight (premature birth) is not an effect of cigarette smoking by pregnant women on their unborn babies. A: False. Smoking in pregnancy can cause miscarriage, premature birth and low birth weight babies.
chunks.source: Smoking in pregnancy can cause miscarriage, premature birth and low birth weight babies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Miscarriage (loss of the pregnancy) is another effect of cigarette smoking by pregnant women on their unborn babies. A: True. The poisons in smoke reach the unborn baby through the mother's blood.
chunks.source: The poisons in smoke reach the unborn baby through the mother's blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They breathe (respire) is not a characteristic of living things. A: False. Living things breathe, feed, grow, reproduce, move and respond to changes.
chunks.source: Living things breathe, feed, grow, reproduce, move and respond to changes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For tearing flesh (meat) is the importance of canine tooth to carnivorous animals. A: True. Carnivores use their sharp pointed canines to tear meat.
chunks.source: Carnivores use their sharp pointed canines to tear meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Breast milk is not the best food for babies below six months. A: False. Babies below six months should feed on breast milk only.
chunks.source: Babies below six months should feed on breast milk only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Toothbrush is the item used to promote sanitation drawn below. A: True. The drawn item is a toothbrush, used for cleaning teeth.
chunks.source: The drawn item is a toothbrush, used for cleaning teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Soil is not the habitat of earth worms. A: False. Earthworms live in the soil.
chunks.source: Earthworms live in the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Roundworm is an example of an intestinal worm in human beings. A: True. Intestinal worms include roundworms, tapeworms and hookworms.
chunks.source: Intestinal worms include roundworms, tapeworms and hookworms.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.source: Vulnerable groups include babies, pregnant women, the elderly and the sick.

chunks.source: Sound can be stored on tape recorders, CDs, phones, radios and flash disks.

chunks.text: Q: Circulatory (blood) system is not the transport system of the human body. A: False. The circulatory system transports blood, food, oxygen and waste around the body.
chunks.source: The circulatory system transports blood, food, oxygen and waste around the body.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.source: Down feathers are soft and fluffy and keep the chick warm.

chunks.text: Q: Thunder is not a natural source of sound in the environment. A: False. Natural sources of sound include thunder, flowing water, wind and animals.
chunks.source: Natural sources of sound include thunder, flowing water, wind and animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Clay soil is the type of soil with the highest capillarity. A: True. Clay soil has the smallest particles, so water rises highest in it by capillarity.
chunks.source: Clay soil has the smallest particles, so water rises highest in it by capillarity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sugar is not a solute used in the making of ORS. A: False. ORS is made by dissolving sugar and salt in clean boiled water.
chunks.source: ORS is made by dissolving sugar and salt in clean boiled water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Thermometer is a weather instrument. A: True. Weather instruments include the thermometer, rain gauge, wind vane and barometer.
chunks.source: Weather instruments include the thermometer, rain gauge, wind vane and barometer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Thermometer (clinical thermometer) is not the instrument used to detect body temperature. A: False. A clinical thermometer measures body temperature.
chunks.source: A clinical thermometer measures body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Frog is an example of an amphibian. A: True. Amphibians include frogs and toads.
chunks.source: Amphibians include frogs and toads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For flying is not an use of feathers to birds. A: False. Feathers help birds to fly and also keep them warm.
chunks.source: Feathers help birds to fly and also keep them warm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Duck is a bird with the foot in the diagram. A: True. The webbed foot in the diagram belongs to swimming birds such as a duck or goose.
chunks.source: The webbed foot in the diagram belongs to swimming birds such as a duck or goose.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Web (webbing between the toes) is not a part marked B on the foot in the diagram. A: False. B points to the skin (web) joining the toes, which helps the bird swim.
chunks.source: B points to the skin (web) joining the toes, which helps the bird swim.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They have six legs is a characteristic of insects. A: True. Insects have six legs, three body parts and a pair of antennae.
chunks.source: Insects have six legs, three body parts and a pair of antennae.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Malaria is not a common disease at home. A: False. Common home diseases include malaria, flu, cough and diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Common home diseases include malaria, flu, cough and diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Gullies (channels) in the soil is a sign of soil erosion in an area. A: True. Signs of erosion include gullies, exposed plant roots and bare stony land.
chunks.source: Signs of erosion include gullies, exposed plant roots and bare stony land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Pollen grain is not a reproductive cell in flowering plants. A: False. The male reproductive cell is the pollen grain; the female one is the ovule (ovum).
chunks.source: The male reproductive cell is the pollen grain; the female one is the ovule (ovum).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Weeding is a crop growing practice. A: True. Crop growing practices include planting, weeding, mulching, spraying and harvesting.
chunks.source: Crop growing practices include planting, weeding, mulching, spraying and harvesting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Gas (gaseous state) is not the state of matter marked C. A: False. C shows particles far apart and scattered, which is the gaseous state.
chunks.source: C shows particles far apart and scattered, which is the gaseous state.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Hen (chicken) is a type of bird found in our environment. A: True. Common birds include hens, ducks, doves, pigeons and eagles.
chunks.source: Common birds include hens, ducks, doves, pigeons and eagles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Duck is not another type of bird found in our environment. A: False. Ducks are water birds with webbed feet.
chunks.source: Ducks are water birds with webbed feet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To save life is a reason for giving first aid to casualties. A: True. First aid saves life, reduces pain and prevents the injury from getting worse.
chunks.source: First aid saves life, reduces pain and prevents the injury from getting worse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To reduce pain is not another reason for giving first aid to casualties. A: False. First aid also stops bleeding and prevents further harm.
chunks.source: First aid also stops bleeding and prevents further harm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Gloves (protective gloves) is the first aid material drawn below. A: True. The drawn material is a pair of gloves worn to protect the first aider from germs.
chunks.source: The drawn material is a pair of gloves worn to protect the first aider from germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Maize is not an example of an annual crop. A: False. Annual crops mature within one year, e.g. maize, beans, groundnuts, sorghum.
chunks.source: Annual crops mature within one year, e.g. maize, beans, groundnuts, sorghum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Beans is another example of an annual crop. A: True. Beans are legumes harvested within months of planting.
chunks.source: Beans are legumes harvested within months of planting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Coffee is not an example of a perennial crop. A: False. Perennial crops live for many years, e.g. coffee, bananas, tea, sugarcane.
chunks.source: Perennial crops live for many years, e.g. coffee, bananas, tea, sugarcane.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Bananas is another example of a perennial crop. A: True. Banana plants keep producing bunches for many years.
chunks.source: Banana plants keep producing bunches for many years.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cow is not an example of a vertebrate. A: False. Examples: cow, goat, fish, bird, frog, snake, human being.
chunks.source: Examples: cow, goat, fish, bird, frog, snake, human being.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fish is another example of a vertebrate. A: True. Fish have backbones too.
chunks.source: Fish have backbones too.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They have a backbone is not a characteristic of vertebrates. A: False. All vertebrates possess a backbone (vertebral column).
chunks.source: All vertebrates possess a backbone (vertebral column).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fibrous root system is the root system marked P. A: True. P shows many thin roots of almost equal size spreading from the stem base: a fibrous root system.
chunks.source: P shows many thin roots of almost equal size spreading from the stem base: a fibrous root system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Taproot system is not the root system marked Q. A: False. Q shows one main root with side roots and nodules: a taproot system.
chunks.source: Q shows one main root with side roots and nodules: a taproot system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Maize is an example of a plant with the root system marked P. A: True. Fibrous roots are found in maize, sorghum, millet, rice and grasses.
chunks.source: Fibrous roots are found in maize, sorghum, millet, rice and grasses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Beans is not an example of a plant with the root system marked Q. A: False. Taproots are found in beans, groundnuts and other legumes.
chunks.source: Taproots are found in beans, groundnuts and other legumes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mammals is the group of vertebrates where human beings belong. A: True. Human beings are mammals.
chunks.source: Human beings are mammals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Goat is not another vertebrate in the same group. A: False. Goats are mammals kept for milk and meat.
chunks.source: Goats are mammals kept for milk and meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Bat is the example of a flying mammal. A: True. The bat is the only mammal that can truly fly.
chunks.source: The bat is the only mammal that can truly fly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For hearing (sound) is not an use of the human ear to the body. A: False. The ear is used for hearing and for balancing the body.
chunks.source: The ear is used for hearing and for balancing the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For balancing the body is another use of the human ear to the body. A: True. The semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.
chunks.source: The semicircular canals in the inner ear keep the body balanced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Eardrum (tympanic membrane) is not a part labeled Y. A: False. Y points to the eardrum at the end of the ear canal.
chunks.source: Y points to the eardrum at the end of the ear canal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sunny is a type of weather. A: True. Types of weather: sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy.
chunks.source: Types of weather: sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Rainy is not another type of weather. A: False. Rain falls from dark clouds.
chunks.source: Rain falls from dark clouds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Windy is the weather condition that favours winnowing of cereals. A: True. Wind blows away the light chaff, leaving the heavy grains.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light chaff, leaving the heavy grains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For eggs is not a reason why farmers rear chicken. A: False. Farmers keep chicken for eggs, meat and income.
chunks.source: Farmers keep chicken for eggs, meat and income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For meat is another reason why farmers rear chicken. A: True. Chicken meat is a source of protein and income.
chunks.source: Chicken meat is a source of protein and income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Layers is not a type of chicken reared by farmers. A: False. Layers are kept for eggs; broilers for meat.
chunks.source: Layers are kept for eggs; broilers for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Broilers is another type of chicken reared by farmers. A: True. Broilers grow fast and are kept for meat.
chunks.source: Broilers grow fast and are kept for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Weevils is not a pest which attacks crops in the garden. A: False. Crop pests include weevils, stalk borers, aphids, cutworms and termites.
chunks.source: Crop pests include weevils, stalk borers, aphids, cutworms and termites.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Stalk borers is another pest which attacks crops in the garden. A: True. Stalk borers tunnel into cereal stems.
chunks.source: Stalk borers tunnel into cereal stems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They eat (destroy) the crops is not a way in which pests are dangerous to crops. A: False. Pests eat crops and reduce harvests.
chunks.source: Pests eat crops and reduce harvests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Moses observed a mango fruit with his five senses. Fill in the missing body structure: Fruity smell is observed by sense of smell using (i) Nose. A: True. We smell with the nose.
chunks.source: We smell with the nose.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Red colour is not observed by sense of sight using (ii) Eyes. A: False. We see with the eyes.
chunks.source: We see with the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sound made when the mango drops is observed by sense of hearing using (iii) Ears. A: True. We hear with the ears.
chunks.source: We hear with the ears.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sweet taste is not observed by sense of taste using (iv) Tongue. A: False. We taste with the tongue.
chunks.source: We taste with the tongue.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Housefly is a vector which is involved in the 4Fs disease path. A: True. The housefly carries germs through the 4Fs: faeces, fingers, flies and food.
chunks.source: The housefly carries germs through the 4Fs: faeces, fingers, flies and food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Deworming regularly is not a way of controlling tape worm infestation in humans. A: False. Tapeworms are controlled by deworming, cooking meat properly and using latrines.
chunks.source: Tapeworms are controlled by deworming, cooking meat properly and using latrines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Petroleum (crude oil) is an example of a non-renewable resource. A: True. Non-renewable resources cannot be replaced once used up, e.g. petroleum, coal, minerals.
chunks.source: Non-renewable resources cannot be replaced once used up, e.g. petroleum, coal, minerals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Hand fork (garden fork) is not the garden tool shown in the diagram. A: False. The small forked tool in the diagram is a hand fork, used for light digging and weeding.
chunks.source: The small forked tool in the diagram is a hand fork, used for light digging and weeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Clean them after use is a way of caring for garden tools. A: True. Garden tools are cared for by cleaning, oiling metal parts, sharpening and keeping them dry.
chunks.source: Garden tools are cared for by cleaning, oiling metal parts, sharpening and keeping them dry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wool is not an animal fibre. A: False. Animal fibres include wool (from sheep), silk and mohair.
chunks.source: Animal fibres include wool (from sheep), silk and mohair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Crop rotation is a farming practice used by crop farmers to maintain soil fertility. A: True. Crop rotation, mulching, manuring and bush fallowing keep soil fertile.
chunks.source: Crop rotation, mulching, manuring and bush fallowing keep soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Nectar is not the type of food eaten by the bird with the beak shown in the diagram. A: False. The long curved beak is for sucking nectar from flowers.
chunks.source: The long curved beak is for sucking nectar from flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For proper disposal of faeces is a way in which a latrine is useful in a home. A: True. Latrines keep faeces away from people, preventing diseases like cholera.
chunks.source: Latrines keep faeces away from people, preventing diseases like cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: White blood cells is not the component of blood which is destroyed by HIV. A: False. HIV attacks and destroys white blood cells, weakening the body's defence.
chunks.source: HIV attacks and destroys white blood cells, weakening the body's defence.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Warmth is a factor which favours the breeding of bacteria. A: True. Bacteria breed fast where there is warmth, moisture and food.
chunks.source: Bacteria breed fast where there is warmth, moisture and food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cassava is not an example of a root tuber. A: False. Root tubers include cassava, sweet potatoes and carrots.
chunks.source: Root tubers include cassava, sweet potatoes and carrots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sweeping the compound is a sanitary activity that children can do to keep the school compound clean. A: True. Children can sweep, slash grass and pick rubbish to keep the school clean.
chunks.source: Children can sweep, slash grass and pick rubbish to keep the school clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cotyledon is not a part marked with letter K on the bean seed. A: False. K points to the cotyledon, the food store of the bean seed.
chunks.source: K points to the cotyledon, the food store of the bean seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Well-drained land is a factor one should consider when selecting a site for a house. A: True. A house site should be well-drained, near water, secure and away from swamps.
chunks.source: A house site should be well-drained, near water, secure and away from swamps.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Evaporation is not a physical process that helps in rain formation. A: False. Evaporation lifts water into the sky and condensation forms the clouds that give rain.
chunks.source: Evaporation lifts water into the sky and condensation forms the clouds that give rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Burns is a common accident at home. A: True. Common home accidents: burns, scalds, cuts, falls, poisoning.
chunks.source: Common home accidents: burns, scalds, cuts, falls, poisoning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Toad is not an example of an amphibian. A: False. Amphibians include frogs and toads.
chunks.source: Amphibians include frogs and toads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Self pollination is a type of pollination. A: True. The two types are self pollination and cross pollination.
chunks.source: The two types are self pollination and cross pollination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cross pollination is not another type of pollination. A: False. In cross pollination, pollen moves from one flower to another.
chunks.source: In cross pollination, pollen moves from one flower to another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Bees (insects) is an agent of pollination. A: True. Agents of pollination: insects, wind, water, birds and animals.
chunks.source: Agents of pollination: insects, wind, water, birds and animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For fastening bandages is not the importance of a safety pin when giving First Aid. A: False. A safety pin holds bandages firmly in place.
chunks.source: A safety pin holds bandages firmly in place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For cleaning wounds is the importance of cotton wool when giving First Aid. A: True. Cotton wool is used to clean wounds and apply medicine.
chunks.source: Cotton wool is used to clean wounds and apply medicine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To save life is not an importance of giving First Aid to an accident victim. A: False. First aid saves life and stops injuries from getting worse.
chunks.source: First aid saves life and stops injuries from getting worse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Red blood cell is the blood cell drawn below. A: True. The round disc-shaped cell drawn is a red blood cell.
chunks.source: The round disc-shaped cell drawn is a red blood cell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Malaria and sickle cell anaemia is not a two diseases which attack the red blood cell. A: False. Malaria parasites and sickle cell disease attack red blood cells.
chunks.source: Malaria parasites and sickle cell disease attack red blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Salting is a way of preserving meat. A: True. Meat is preserved by salting, smoking, drying or freezing.
chunks.source: Meat is preserved by salting, smoking, drying or freezing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Smoking is not another way of preserving meat. A: False. Smoke dries meat and keeps germs away.
chunks.source: Smoke dries meat and keeps germs away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Gills is a part marked C. A: True. C points to the gills, which the fish uses for breathing in water.
chunks.source: C points to the gills, which the fish uses for breathing in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Spraying with pesticides is not a way of controlling crop pests in a garden. A: False. Pests are controlled by spraying, crop rotation, weeding and hand picking.
chunks.source: Pests are controlled by spraying, crop rotation, weeding and hand picking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Crop rotation is another way of controlling crop pests in a garden. A: True. Changing crops each season breaks the life cycle of pests.
chunks.source: Changing crops each season breaks the life cycle of pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Poor health (mental illness) is not an effect of drug dependence to an individual. A: False. Drug dependence ruins health, causes madness, poverty and school dropout.
chunks.source: Drug dependence ruins health, causes madness, poverty and school dropout.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Through immunization (vaccination) is a way in which a child can acquire immunity. A: True. Children get immunity through vaccination, recovery from illness, or from the mother.
chunks.source: Children get immunity through vaccination, recovery from illness, or from the mother.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Through recovery from an illness is not another way in which a child can acquire immunity. A: False. After recovering from a disease, the body remembers how to fight it.
chunks.source: After recovering from a disease, the body remembers how to fight it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By eating a balanced diet is a way in which a person's body immunity can be increased. A: True. Good feeding, immunization and exercise strengthen immunity.
chunks.source: Good feeding, immunization and exercise strengthen immunity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Stomach is not a part marked Q. A: False. Q is the bag-like stomach where food is churned and mixed with juices.
chunks.source: Q is the bag-like stomach where food is churned and mixed with juices.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Bile is the digestive juice produced by part marked S. A: True. S is the liver, which produces bile juice.
chunks.source: S is the liver, which produces bile juice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For pleasure is not a reason why some people drink alcohol. A: False. Some drink for leisure, to socialize or to forget problems.
chunks.source: Some drink for leisure, to socialize or to forget problems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To socialize with friends is another reason why some people drink alcohol. A: True. Others drink to feel brave or to cope with stress.
chunks.source: Others drink to feel brave or to cope with stress.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Clinical thermometer is not a medical instrument which uses alcohol to function. A: False. Some clinical thermometers use alcohol instead of mercury.
chunks.source: Some clinical thermometers use alcohol instead of mercury.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Drum is a percussion musical instrument. A: True. Percussion instruments are hit or shaken: drum, xylophone, bell.
chunks.source: Percussion instruments are hit or shaken: drum, xylophone, bell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Guitar is not a string musical instrument. A: False. String instruments have strings that are plucked or bowed: guitar, harp, violin.
chunks.source: String instruments have strings that are plucked or bowed: guitar, harp, violin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Recording is a method of storing sound. A: True. Sound is stored by recording on tapes, CDs or phones.
chunks.source: Sound is stored by recording on tapes, CDs or phones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Friesian is not an example of an exotic breed of cattle. A: False. Exotic cattle breeds: Friesian, Jersey, Guernsey, Ayrshire.
chunks.source: Exotic cattle breeds: Friesian, Jersey, Guernsey, Ayrshire.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Jersey is another example of an exotic breed of cattle. A: True. Jersey cows give milk rich in butterfat.
chunks.source: Jersey cows give milk rich in butterfat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Deworming (drenching) is not a way of controlling internal parasites in cattle. A: False. Internal parasites (worms) are controlled by regular deworming.
chunks.source: Internal parasites (worms) are controlled by regular deworming.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sunken eyes is a sign of dehydration. A: True. Signs: sunken eyes, dry mouth, great thirst, passing little urine.
chunks.source: Signs: sunken eyes, dry mouth, great thirst, passing little urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Dry mouth (great thirst) is not another sign of dehydration. A: False. The patient feels very thirsty and the tongue is dry.
chunks.source: The patient feels very thirsty and the tongue is dry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Broom is an item used for sweeping. A: True. A broom is used for sweeping floors and compounds.
chunks.source: A broom is used for sweeping floors and compounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: Father is not a member of a nuclear family. A: False. A nuclear family is made of father, mother and their children.
chunks.source: A nuclear family is made of father, mother and their children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part of the flower which attracts pollinators is the Petals. A: True. The bright colourful petals attract insects and other pollinators to the flower.
chunks.source: The bright colourful petals attract insects and other pollinators to the flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It cools the plant is not an importance of transpiration to plants. A: False. Transpiration cools the plant and pulls water and minerals up from the roots.
chunks.source: Transpiration cools the plant and pulls water and minerals up from the roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Bathing daily is a way of keeping the body clean. A: True. Bathing, brushing teeth and washing hands keep the body clean.
chunks.source: Bathing, brushing teeth and washing hands keep the body clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Maize is not an example of an annual crop. A: False. Annual crops mature in one year: maize, beans, groundnuts.
chunks.source: Annual crops mature in one year: maize, beans, groundnuts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Angora is an exotic breed of goats that provides people with mohair. A: True. Angora goats produce mohair, a soft silky fibre.
chunks.source: Angora goats produce mohair, a soft silky fibre.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Through unprotected sexual intercourse is not a way AIDS can be spread from one person to another. A: False. AIDS spreads through unprotected sex, sharing sharp instruments and infected blood.
chunks.source: AIDS spreads through unprotected sex, sharing sharp instruments and infected blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Dolls is a play material made from banana fibres. A: True. Banana fibres are woven into dolls, balls and ropes for play.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are woven into dolls, balls and ropes for play.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Taproot system is not the type of root system shown in the diagram above. A: False. The diagram shows one main root with side roots: a taproot system.
chunks.source: The diagram shows one main root with side roots: a taproot system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one danger of plants: Some plants are poisonous. A: True. Some plants are poisonous, have thorns or harbour dangerous animals.
chunks.source: Some plants are poisonous, have thorns or harbour dangerous animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Swamps (wetlands) is not the source of papyrus used in making mats. A: False. Papyrus reeds grow in swamps and are used for mats and crafts.
chunks.source: Papyrus reeds grow in swamps and are used for mats and crafts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It gives light and heat is an importance of the sun to the environment. A: True. The sun gives light and warmth and helps green plants make food.
chunks.source: The sun gives light and warmth and helps green plants make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Carbohydrates is not the food value obtained from eating honey. A: False. Honey is rich in carbohydrates, which give the body energy.
chunks.source: Honey is rich in carbohydrates, which give the body energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Babies is a group of people considered to be vulnerable. A: True. Vulnerable groups: babies, pregnant women, the elderly, the sick.
chunks.source: Vulnerable groups: babies, pregnant women, the elderly, the sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Ringworm is not a communicable disease caused by a fungus. A: False. Fungal communicable diseases include ringworm and athlete's foot.
chunks.source: Fungal communicable diseases include ringworm and athlete's foot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Skin is the body organ affected by the disease mentioned in (a) above. A: True. Ringworm attacks the skin.
chunks.source: Ringworm attacks the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Avoid sharing clothes and towels is not a way of preventing the spread of ringworm. A: False. Prevent ringworm by keeping skin clean and dry and not sharing personal items.
chunks.source: Prevent ringworm by keeping skin clean and dry and not sharing personal items.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Hard seed coat is a factor that may cause seed dormancy. A: True. A very hard seed coat or an immature embryo can cause dormancy.
chunks.source: A very hard seed coat or an immature embryo can cause dormancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Immature embryo is not another factor that may cause seed dormancy. A: False. If the young plant inside is not fully grown, the seed stays dormant.
chunks.source: If the young plant inside is not fully grown, the seed stays dormant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They have six legs is a characteristic of insects. A: True. Insects have six legs, three body parts and one pair of antennae.
chunks.source: Insects have six legs, three body parts and one pair of antennae.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Carrot is not another example of a root tuber. A: False. Carrots store food in their swollen roots.
chunks.source: Carrots store food in their swollen roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cassava mosaic disease is a viral disease of cassava. A: True. Cassava mosaic is a virus disease spread by whiteflies.
chunks.source: Cassava mosaic is a virus disease spread by whiteflies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By uprooting is not a way cassava is harvested. A: False. Cassava is harvested by pulling (uprooting) the plant from the soil.
chunks.source: Cassava is harvested by pulling (uprooting) the plant from the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Canine is the type of tooth marked T. A: True. T is sharp and pointed: a canine.
chunks.source: T is sharp and pointed: a canine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For grinding (crushing) food is not the function of the tooth marked S. A: False. Molars grind and crush food into small pieces.
chunks.source: Molars grind and crush food into small pieces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For tearing food is the function of the tooth marked T. A: True. Canines are sharp and pointed for tearing meat.
chunks.source: Canines are sharp and pointed for tearing meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Snuffles (pneumonia) is not another disease of rabbits. A: False. Likely answer: snuffles is a respiratory disease of rabbits.
chunks.source: Likely answer: snuffles is a respiratory disease of rabbits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: New Zealand White is an exotic breed of rabbits kept in Uganda. A: True. Likely answer: exotic rabbit breeds include New Zealand White and Californian.
chunks.source: Likely answer: exotic rabbit breeds include New Zealand White and Californian.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Carbon dioxide is not a raw material needed by plants during photosynthesis. A: False. Plants need carbon dioxide and water to make food in sunlight.
chunks.source: Plants need carbon dioxide and water to make food in sunlight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Water is another raw material needed by plants during photosynthesis. A: True. Roots absorb the water used in photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Roots absorb the water used in photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: Base (insulating pad) is not a part labeled D. A: False. Likely answer: D points to the base on which the flask stands.
chunks.source: Likely answer: D points to the base on which the flask stands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Science at Home and in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: Glass is a material from which part C is made. A: True. C is the double-walled glass bottle with a vacuum between the walls.
chunks.source: C is the double-walled glass bottle with a vacuum between the walls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Through bites is not a way vectors spread germs that cause diseases. A: False. Vectors spread germs by biting people or by contaminating food.
chunks.source: Vectors spread germs by biting people or by contaminating food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By contaminating food is another way vectors spread germs that cause diseases. A: True. Houseflies carry germs on their bodies onto our food.
chunks.source: Houseflies carry germs on their bodies onto our food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Malaria is not a disease whose germs are spread by vectors. A: False. Vector-spread diseases: malaria, cholera, typhoid, sleeping sickness.
chunks.source: Vector-spread diseases: malaria, cholera, typhoid, sleeping sickness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cholera is another disease whose germs are spread by vectors. A: True. Houseflies spread cholera germs onto food.
chunks.source: Houseflies spread cholera germs onto food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Soil erosion is not a way soil loses its fertility. A: False. Soil loses fertility through erosion, leaching, over-cultivation and bush burning.
chunks.source: Soil loses fertility through erosion, leaching, over-cultivation and bush burning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Leaching is another way soil loses its fertility. A: True. Heavy rain washes nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach.
chunks.source: Heavy rain washes nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mulching is not a way of preventing soil from losing its fertility. A: False. Mulching, crop rotation, terracing and manuring protect soil fertility.
chunks.source: Mulching, crop rotation, terracing and manuring protect soil fertility.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Crop rotation is another way of preventing soil from losing its fertility. A: True. Planting different crops each season keeps the soil rich.
chunks.source: Planting different crops each season keeps the soil rich.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the soil is not a place where bacteria are found. A: False. Bacteria are found in soil, air, water and decaying matter.
chunks.source: Bacteria are found in soil, air, water and decaying matter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: They decompose dead matter is a way in which bacteria are useful in the environment. A: True. Bacteria rot dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.
chunks.source: Bacteria rot dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Dolls is not a play material made from banana fibres. A: False. Banana fibres are woven into dolls, balls and ropes for children to play with.
chunks.source: Banana fibres are woven into dolls, balls and ropes for children to play with.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Poverty is an effect of alcoholism to a community. A: True. Alcoholism brings poverty, violence, accidents and broken families to a community.
chunks.source: Alcoholism brings poverty, violence, accidents and broken families to a community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one way you would not reduce egg eating on a poultry farm: Debeak the birds. A: False. Debeaking, collecting eggs often and feeding the birds well reduce egg eating.
chunks.source: Debeaking, collecting eggs often and feeding the birds well reduce egg eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Water is the liquid marked Y in the diagram (a boy put water and oil in a container). A: True. Oil floats on water; Y marks the lower layer, which is water. (The extracted image file P614141315img.jpg is blank/unusable, so no image is attached.)
chunks.source: Oil floats on water; Y marks the lower layer, which is water. (The extracted image file P614141315img.jpg is blank/unusable, so no image is attached.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Well-drained land is not a factor you would consider before selecting a site for house. A: False. Choose land that is well-drained, near clean water, secure and not in a swamp.
chunks.source: Choose land that is well-drained, near clean water, secure and not in a swamp.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Garden fork (digging fork) is the garden tool drawn in the diagram below. A: True. The long-handled forked tool is a garden (digging) fork.
chunks.source: The long-handled forked tool is a garden (digging) fork.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For digging (loosening) the soil is not an use of the above garden tool to a farmer. A: False. A garden fork digs and loosens soil and turns manure.
chunks.source: A garden fork digs and loosens soil and turns manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one characteristic of essential drugs: They are affordable (cheap). A: True. Essential drugs are affordable, available, safe and effective.
chunks.source: Essential drugs are affordable, available, safe and effective.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Self pollination is not the type of pollination illustrated below. A: False. The arrows show pollen moving within the same flower: self pollination.
chunks.source: The arrows show pollen moving within the same flower: self pollination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Irish potato is an example of a stem tuber. A: True. Stem tubers include Irish potatoes and yams.
chunks.source: Stem tubers include Irish potatoes and yams.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Crab is not an example of a crustacean. A: False. Crustaceans have hard shells: crab, lobster, prawn.
chunks.source: Crustaceans have hard shells: crab, lobster, prawn.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Granary is the legume store above. A: True. The raised grass-thatched store in the diagram is a granary for keeping grains and legumes.
chunks.source: The raised grass-thatched store in the diagram is a granary for keeping grains and legumes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Nitrogen is not another part (component) of air. A: False. Nitrogen makes up the largest part of air.
chunks.source: Nitrogen makes up the largest part of air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For putting out fire is an use of carbon dioxide to people. A: True. Carbon dioxide puts out fires, is used by plants to make food, and makes drinks fizzy.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide puts out fires, is used by plants to make food, and makes drinks fizzy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In photosynthesis (by plants) is not another use of carbon dioxide to people. A: False. Plants need carbon dioxide to make food.
chunks.source: Plants need carbon dioxide to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Family planning is the element of P.H.C responsible for controlling of over population. A: True. Family planning is the PHC element that controls overpopulation.
chunks.source: Family planning is the PHC element that controls overpopulation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Personal hygiene is not the element of P.H.C responsible for controlling of bad body odour. A: False. Personal hygiene keeps the body clean and free from bad smell.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene keeps the body clean and free from bad smell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Immunization is the element of P.H.C responsible for controlling killer diseases among children. A: True. Immunization protects children against the killer diseases.
chunks.source: Immunization protects children against the killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one activity you cannot do to promote PHC in school: Health parade (general cleaning). A: False. Health parades, cleaning the compound and health talks promote PHC.
chunks.source: Health parades, cleaning the compound and health talks promote PHC.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Eagle is a bird that has a beak like the one drawn above. A: True. Eagles, hawks and kites have strong hooked beaks.
chunks.source: Eagles, hawks and kites have strong hooked beaks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It eats (steals) people's chicken is not a danger of the bird you have named in (c) above to people. A: False. Birds of prey snatch chickens and chicks from homes.
chunks.source: Birds of prey snatch chickens and chicks from homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For cleaning wounds is the use of cotton (wool) in first aid management. A: True. Cotton wool cleans wounds before dressing.
chunks.source: Cotton wool cleans wounds before dressing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Vein is not the type of blood vessel drawn above. A: False. The vessel has valves (W) that stop backflow: it is a vein.
chunks.source: The vessel has valves (W) that stop backflow: it is a vein.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: It has villi (finger-like projections) is another adaptation of the ileum that enables it to absorb digested food. A: True. Villi greatly increase the absorbing surface of the ileum.
chunks.source: Villi greatly increase the absorbing surface of the ileum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Housefly is not an insect that contaminates our food. A: False. Houseflies land on faeces then on food, contaminating it.
chunks.source: Houseflies land on faeces then on food, contaminating it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest one way you would prevent contamination of food by the vector named in (a) above: Cover food (properly). A: True. Cover food, kill flies and keep the surroundings clean.
chunks.source: Cover food, kill flies and keep the surroundings clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tethering is not another system of grazing cattle. A: False. In tethering, an animal is tied with a rope to graze in one spot.
chunks.source: In tethering, an animal is tied with a rope to graze in one spot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Firewood is a source of heat used for cooking food at home. A: True. Heat for cooking comes from firewood, charcoal, paraffin, gas or electricity.
chunks.source: Heat for cooking comes from firewood, charcoal, paraffin, gas or electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Charcoal is not another source of heat used for cooking food at home. A: False. Charcoal burns with steady heat in stoves.
chunks.source: Charcoal burns with steady heat in stoves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Carbohydrates is a food value that provides heat to the body. A: True. Carbohydrates (and fats) are burnt in the body to release heat and energy.
chunks.source: Carbohydrates (and fats) are burnt in the body to release heat and energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Antenna (antennae) is not a part marked P. A: False. P points to the feeler on the head: the antenna.
chunks.source: P points to the feeler on the head: the antenna.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mercury is the liquid commonly used in the above thermometer. A: True. Clinical thermometers commonly use mercury.
chunks.source: Clinical thermometers commonly use mercury.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one river which flows into Lake Victoria: ____. A: River Kagera. River Kagera is the largest river that flows into Lake Victoria.
chunks.source: River Kagera is the largest river that flows into Lake Victoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is central Tanzania not good for cattle keeping? ____. A: It is infested with tsetse flies which spread sleeping sickness to cattle. Tsetse flies bite cattle and spread diseases, so cattle cannot thrive there.
chunks.source: Tsetse flies bite cattle and spread diseases, so cattle cannot thrive there.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why monkeys live in forests: ____. A: Forests provide them with food and shelter. Monkeys eat fruits and leaves from forest trees and hide from enemies among the trees.
chunks.source: Monkeys eat fruits and leaves from forest trees and hide from enemies among the trees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which the vegetation in a compound helps to control soil erosion: ____. A: The roots hold the soil together. Plant roots bind the soil so running water cannot easily wash it away.
chunks.source: Plant roots bind the soil so running water cannot easily wash it away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why many lions are found in savannah vegetation: ____. A: Savannah has many grazing animals for lions to prey on. Lions are carnivores; the savannah grassland supports large herds of antelopes and zebras which lions hunt.
chunks.source: Lions are carnivores; the savannah grassland supports large herds of antelopes and zebras which lions hunt.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is rainy weather important to farmers? ____. A: Rain provides the water needed by crops to grow. Crops need water to germinate and grow, and rain supplies it.
chunks.source: Crops need water to germinate and grow, and rain supplies it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How has drought affected people in most parts of East Africa? ____. A: It has caused crop failure and famine. Without rain, crops dry up and animals die, leading to hunger.
chunks.source: Without rain, crops dry up and animals die, leading to hunger.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The table shows monthly rainfall of 80mm to 230mm and temperatures of 24 to 26 degrees Celsius all year. What type of climate is shown above? ____. A: Equatorial climate. Temperatures are high and fairly uniform all year, with rainfall in every month.
chunks.source: Temperatures are high and fairly uniform all year, with rainfall in every month.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same climatic table, which activity can be done by farmers in the month of January? ____. A: Harvesting. January receives little rain, so farmers harvest and dry their crops.
chunks.source: January receives little rain, so farmers harvest and dry their crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one element of weather which makes people sweat: ____. A: High temperature (heat). When the temperature is high, the body sweats to cool down.
chunks.source: When the temperature is high, the body sweats to cool down.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two problems facing the fishing industry in East Africa: ____. A: Overfishing and water pollution. Catching too many fish reduces stocks, and pollution kills fish.
chunks.source: Catching too many fish reduces stocks, and pollution kills fish.

chunks.subject: Social
