chunks.text: Q: Mention any two ways of preserving fish: ____. A: Smoking and sun drying. Removing water from fish by smoking, drying or salting stops it from rotting.
chunks.source: Removing water from fish by smoking, drying or salting stops it from rotting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two major resources found in East Africa: ____. A: Minerals and forests. East Africa is rich in minerals, forests, water bodies and wildlife.
chunks.source: East Africa is rich in minerals, forests, water bodies and wildlife.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State two major problems facing the mining industry in East Africa: ____. A: Lack of capital and poor transport. Mining needs a lot of money and good roads, which are lacking.
chunks.source: Mining needs a lot of money and good roads, which are lacking.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do the prevailing winds influence the climate of East Africa? ____. A: They determine the rainfall received in an area. Winds blowing from the sea bring rain, while dry winds bring dry conditions.
chunks.source: Winds blowing from the sea bring rain, while dry winds bring dry conditions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the stage of a river that is suitable for the construction of electric dams: ____. A: The young stage. Waterfalls, which provide falling water for power, occur in the young stage of a river.
chunks.source: Waterfalls, which provide falling water for power, occur in the young stage of a river.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can rainfall be dangerous to people? ____. A: It causes floods which destroy crops and homes. Too much rain leads to floods that kill people and destroy property.
chunks.source: Too much rain leads to floods that kill people and destroy property.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do the people of Kabale adapt to the cool climatic conditions? ____. A: By wearing heavy warm clothes. Kabale is cold, so people wear warm clothes and build warm houses.
chunks.source: Kabale is cold, so people wear warm clothes and build warm houses.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are the Turkana and the Karimojong similar in terms of their activities? ____. A: Both practise pastoralism. The Turkana of Kenya and the Karimojong of Uganda are both cattle keepers.
chunks.source: The Turkana of Kenya and the Karimojong of Uganda are both cattle keepers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two human activities that have led to the destruction of the environment: ____. A: Deforestation and bush burning. Cutting down trees and burning bushes destroy the environment.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees and burning bushes destroy the environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State two ways of conserving the environment: ____. A: Afforestation and proper disposal of waste. Planting trees and dumping rubbish properly protect the environment.
chunks.source: Planting trees and dumping rubbish properly protect the environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does tourism contribute towards the government revenue? ____. A: Tourists pay fees and bring foreign exchange. Money spent by tourists adds to government income.
chunks.source: Money spent by tourists adds to government income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the largest climatic zone of Uganda: ____. A: The tropical climatic zone. Most of Uganda has a tropical climate with wet and dry seasons.
chunks.source: Most of Uganda has a tropical climate with wet and dry seasons.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two characteristics of equatorial climate: ____. A: High temperatures throughout the year and heavy rainfall throughout the year. Equatorial areas are hot and wet all year round.
chunks.source: Equatorial areas are hot and wet all year round.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does climate influence vegetation distribution in an area? ____. A: Areas with heavy rainfall have thick forests while dry areas have grassland. The amount of rain determines whether forests or grasslands grow.
chunks.source: The amount of rain determines whether forests or grasslands grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one human activity that can destroy our environment: ____. A: Deforestation. Cutting down trees destroys forests and animal homes.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees destroys forests and animal homes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention the major cash crop that was introduced by the Arabs along the coast of East Africa: ____. A: Cloves. Arabs introduced clove growing, especially in Zanzibar.
chunks.source: Arabs introduced clove growing, especially in Zanzibar.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one weather instrument that can be kept in the Stevenson screen: ____. A: A thermometer. Maximum and minimum thermometers are kept in the Stevenson screen.
chunks.source: Maximum and minimum thermometers are kept in the Stevenson screen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify one problem that is faced by people who live around hilly and mountainous areas: ____. A: Soil erosion. Steep slopes make soil wash away easily.
chunks.source: Steep slopes make soil wash away easily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the physical feature that crosses at least five East African countries: ____. A: The Rift Valley. The Rift Valley runs through many East African countries.
chunks.source: The Rift Valley runs through many East African countries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason for controlling soil erosion in mountainous areas: ____. A: To keep the soil fertile. Erosion washes away the fertile top soil needed by crops.
chunks.source: Erosion washes away the fertile top soil needed by crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one disadvantage of using traditional methods of fishing: ____. A: They catch few fish. Hooks and baskets catch less fish than modern nets.
chunks.source: Hooks and baskets catch less fish than modern nets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can people protect lakes as natural resources? ____. A: By not dumping waste into them. Keeping lakes clean and avoiding overfishing protects them.
chunks.source: Keeping lakes clean and avoiding overfishing protects them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one importance of planting grass in the school compound: ____. A: It controls soil erosion. Grass holds the soil and makes the compound beautiful.
chunks.source: Grass holds the soil and makes the compound beautiful.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the biggest water mass that neighbours East Africa in the east: ____. A: The Indian Ocean. The Indian Ocean lies to the east of East Africa.
chunks.source: The Indian Ocean lies to the east of East Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one tributary of the River Nile in Uganda: ____. A: River Achwa. The Achwa joins the Nile in northern Uganda.
chunks.source: The Achwa joins the Nile in northern Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one factor that can influence the climate of an area: ____. A: Altitude. High places are cooler; areas near the equator are hotter.
chunks.source: High places are cooler; areas near the equator are hotter.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is farming? ____. A: The growing of crops and rearing of animals. Farming includes crop growing and animal rearing.
chunks.source: Farming includes crop growing and animal rearing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one problem that is faced by farmers in Uganda today: ____. A: Pests and diseases. Pests destroy crops and little rain causes poor harvests.
chunks.source: Pests destroy crops and little rain causes poor harvests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two ways in which farming creates employment: ____. A: It provides jobs on farms and raw materials for industries. People work on farms, and factories employ people to process farm produce.
chunks.source: People work on farms, and factories employ people to process farm produce.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is tourism referred to as an industry? ____. A: Because it generates income and employs people. Like other industries, tourism creates jobs and earns money.
chunks.source: Like other industries, tourism creates jobs and earns money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two problems that are faced by the tourism industry in our country: ____. A: Poaching and poor roads. Killing of wild animals and bad roads discourage tourists.
chunks.source: Killing of wild animals and bad roads discourage tourists.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any invisible export of Uganda to Kenya and Rwanda: ____. A: Tourism. Tourists from Kenya and Rwanda spend money in Uganda without carrying goods.
chunks.source: Tourists from Kenya and Rwanda spend money in Uganda without carrying goods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the major occupation of the Turkana people in Kenya? ____. A: Pastoralism. The Turkana keep cattle, goats and sheep in the dry lands of Kenya.
chunks.source: The Turkana keep cattle, goats and sheep in the dry lands of Kenya.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are the Bagisu similar to the Chagga in their location? ____. A: Both live on the slopes of mountains. The Bagisu live on Mt. Elgon and the Chagga on Mt. Kilimanjaro.
chunks.source: The Bagisu live on Mt. Elgon and the Chagga on Mt. Kilimanjaro.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Apart from human activity, give any one other factor that determines the vegetation of an area: ____. A: Climate. The amount of rainfall decides what plants grow in an area.
chunks.source: The amount of rainfall decides what plants grow in an area.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is soil erosion controlled in Kabale? ____. A: By terracing. Farmers in Kabale make terraces across hills to slow running water.
chunks.source: Farmers in Kabale make terraces across hills to slow running water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why Mountain Rwenzori is snow capped throughout the year: ____. A: Because of its high altitude. Very high mountains are cold enough for snow all year.
chunks.source: Very high mountains are cold enough for snow all year.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one characteristic of Rift Valley lakes: ____. A: They are long and narrow. Rift Valley lakes like Albert and Tanganyika are long, narrow and deep.
chunks.source: Rift Valley lakes like Albert and Tanganyika are long, narrow and deep.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do farmers benefit from agro-based industries? ____. A: They get market for their produce. Factories buy crops from farmers as raw materials.
chunks.source: Factories buy crops from farmers as raw materials.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the water body that joins Lake George to Lake Edward: ____. A: The Kazinga Channel. The Kazinga Channel connects the two lakes.
chunks.source: The Kazinga Channel connects the two lakes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one reason why Stone Age sites are economically important to a country: ____. A: They attract tourists who bring foreign exchange. Visitors pay to see historical sites, earning the country money.
chunks.source: Visitors pay to see historical sites, earning the country money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is a rain gauge placed on a raised place? ____. A: To prevent splashes from the ground. Raising it stops splashing water from entering and gives true readings.
chunks.source: Raising it stops splashing water from entering and gives true readings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is dairy farming? ____. A: The rearing of cattle for milk production. Dairy farmers keep cows mainly to get milk.
chunks.source: Dairy farmers keep cows mainly to get milk.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is Hima similar to Tororo in terms of Uganda's economic development? ____. A: Both have cement factories. Hima and Tororo both produce cement from limestone.
chunks.source: Hima and Tororo both produce cement from limestone.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one factor that favours the proper growth of Arabica coffee on the slopes of Mountain Elgon: ____. A: Fertile volcanic soils. Volcanic soils on Mt. Elgon are rich and good for coffee.
chunks.source: Volcanic soils on Mt. Elgon are rich and good for coffee.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the main economic activity carried out in the equatorial rain forests: ____. A: Lumbering. People cut timber trees in the rain forests.
chunks.source: People cut timber trees in the rain forests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two characteristics of equatorial rain forests: ____. A: Tall evergreen trees and a dense canopy. The trees stay green all year and their tops form a thick cover.
chunks.source: The trees stay green all year and their tops form a thick cover.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do trees in equatorial rain forests grow tall? ____. A: To compete for sunlight. Trees grow tall to reach sunlight above the dense canopy.
chunks.source: Trees grow tall to reach sunlight above the dense canopy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is fishing? ____. A: The catching of fish from water bodies. Fishing is harvesting fish from lakes, rivers and seas.
chunks.source: Fishing is harvesting fish from lakes, rivers and seas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two traditional methods of fishing used on Ugandan lakes: ____. A: Use of baskets and hooks. Fishermen traditionally used baskets, hooks and spears.
chunks.source: Fishermen traditionally used baskets, hooks and spears.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one problem facing the fishing industry in Uganda today: ____. A: Overfishing. Catching too many fish reduces the fish stock.
chunks.source: Catching too many fish reduces the fish stock.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one example of sustainable use of the environment: ____. A: Afforestation. Planting trees replaces those cut down, keeping the environment safe.
chunks.source: Planting trees replaces those cut down, keeping the environment safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does the government benefit from the mining of crude oil? ____. A: It earns revenue. Oil money adds to government income.
chunks.source: Oil money adds to government income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is meant by the term land degradation? ____. A: The destruction of land. Land degradation is the loss of the land's fertility and usefulness.
chunks.source: Land degradation is the loss of the land's fertility and usefulness.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is pastoralism mainly carried out in Karamoja but not Kampala? ____. A: Karamoja is dry with grass suitable for grazing. Karamoja's semi-arid grassland suits cattle, while Kampala is a built-up city.
chunks.source: Karamoja's semi-arid grassland suits cattle, while Kampala is a built-up city.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are places near the Equator hotter than those far away? ____. A: The sun's rays strike directly overhead. Near the equator the sun is overhead, giving more heat.
chunks.source: Near the equator the sun is overhead, giving more heat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is the government of Uganda encouraging people to grow a lot of non-traditional cash crops? ____. A: To earn more foreign exchange. New cash crops like flowers bring more export money.
chunks.source: New cash crops like flowers bring more export money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do Osukuru hills promote the building industry in Uganda? ____. A: They have limestone used to make cement. Limestone from Osukuru hills is used in cement factories.
chunks.source: Limestone from Osukuru hills is used in cement factories.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being cloudy or windy, give any one other change of weather: ____. A: Rainy. Weather can change to rainy or sunny.
chunks.source: Weather can change to rainy or sunny.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one of the reasons why tourists should be given game rangers every time they visit a game park: ____. A: For protection. Rangers protect tourists from wild animals.
chunks.source: Rangers protect tourists from wild animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why does Kalangala district receive convectional rainfall? ____. A: It is surrounded by Lake Victoria which gives a lot of evaporation. Water evaporates from the lake, rises, cools and falls as rain.
chunks.source: Water evaporates from the lake, rises, cools and falls as rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention the major tourist attraction found in Bwindi and Mgahinga national parks: ____. A: Mountain gorillas. Tourists visit Bwindi and Mgahinga to see mountain gorillas.
chunks.source: Tourists visit Bwindi and Mgahinga to see mountain gorillas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is environment? ____. A: Our surroundings. The environment includes air, water, soil, plants, animals and buildings around us.
chunks.source: The environment includes air, water, soil, plants, animals and buildings around us.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention two types of environment you know: ____. A: Natural environment and man-made environment. Forests and lakes are natural; roads and buildings are man-made.
chunks.source: Forests and lakes are natural; roads and buildings are man-made.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can the extension of electricity in rural areas reduce the rate at which people cut down trees for wood? ____. A: People will use electricity instead of firewood. With electricity for cooking and lighting, fewer trees are cut.
chunks.source: With electricity for cooking and lighting, fewer trees are cut.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: In which one way can accidents be reduced on Lake Victoria? ____. A: By wearing life jackets when travelling on the lake. Life jackets keep people afloat if a boat capsizes.
chunks.source: Life jackets keep people afloat if a boat capsizes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Apart from water, write any other item transported using pipelines: ____. A: Crude oil (petroleum). Pipelines also carry petroleum products and natural gas.
chunks.source: Pipelines also carry petroleum products and natural gas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give the meaning of the term communication: ____. A: The sending and receiving of information. Communication is how people share news, ideas and messages.
chunks.source: Communication is how people share news, ideas and messages.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State any two importance of mobile phone companies operating in Uganda: ____. A: They provide employment and make communication easy. Phone companies employ many people and let Ugandans call and message each other easily.
chunks.source: Phone companies employ many people and let Ugandans call and message each other easily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one mobile phone company operating in Uganda: ____. A: MTN Uganda. MTN and Airtel are mobile phone companies operating in Uganda.
chunks.source: MTN and Airtel are mobile phone companies operating in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What is transport? ____. A: The movement of people and goods from one place to another. Transport carries people and things by road, rail, water or air.
chunks.source: Transport carries people and things by road, rail, water or air.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State two reasons why there are many road accidents in Uganda today: ____. A: Over speeding and drunk driving. Drivers who speed or drink cause many accidents.
chunks.source: Drivers who speed or drink cause many accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: In which way can road accidents be controlled in Uganda? ____. A: By enforcing traffic rules. Police can punish over speeding and drunk drivers to make roads safer.
chunks.source: Police can punish over speeding and drunk drivers to make roads safer.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one advantage of traditional means of transport over modern means: ____. A: They are cheap and do not need fuel. Walking or using donkeys costs nothing, unlike cars that need fuel.
chunks.source: Walking or using donkeys costs nothing, unlike cars that need fuel.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why is a radio station regarded as an important place in our community today? ____. A: It spreads news and information to people. Radio stations educate and inform the community through programmes.
chunks.source: Radio stations educate and inform the community through programmes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What part of the Uganda Coat of Arms represents Uganda's traditional communication? ____. A: The drum. In the past, drums were used to send messages, so the drum appears on the coat of arms.
chunks.source: In the past, drums were used to send messages, so the drum appears on the coat of arms.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How is a bell important in a school community? ____. A: It signals time for lessons and breaks. The bell tells pupils when lessons begin and end.
chunks.source: The bell tells pupils when lessons begin and end.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Apart from a television, give two other forms of mass media: ____. A: Radio and newspapers. Radio and newspapers also pass information to many people.
chunks.source: Radio and newspapers also pass information to many people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why televisions are not commonly used in rural areas: ____. A: There is no electricity. Most rural homes lack electricity to power television sets.
chunks.source: Most rural homes lack electricity to power television sets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State any one way television stations promote employment opportunities to people: ____. A: They employ journalists and presenters. Television stations give jobs to reporters, presenters and technicians.
chunks.source: Television stations give jobs to reporters, presenters and technicians.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being expensive, give another reason why air transport is not used by many people in Uganda: ____. A: There are few airports. Uganda has few airports, so air transport is not common.
chunks.source: Uganda has few airports, so air transport is not common.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name any one inland port found on Lake Victoria in Kenya: ____. A: Kisumu. Kisumu is a major inland port on Lake Victoria in Kenya.
chunks.source: Kisumu is a major inland port on Lake Victoria in Kenya.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which explorer followed the River Nile from its mouth? ____. A: John Hanning Speke. Speke traced the River Nile and proved that Lake Victoria is its source.
chunks.source: Speke traced the River Nile and proved that Lake Victoria is its source.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which missionary contributed to the economic development of Uganda? ____. A: Alexander Mackay. Mackay taught Africans farming and technical skills like carpentry and printing.
chunks.source: Mackay taught Africans farming and technical skills like carpentry and printing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why explorers came to Uganda: ____. A: To find the source of the River Nile. European explorers wanted to discover where the River Nile begins.
chunks.source: European explorers wanted to discover where the River Nile begins.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why were political parties formed in the early 1950s? ____. A: To demand independence (self-rule). Africans formed parties to unite and demand freedom from colonial rule.
chunks.source: Africans formed parties to unite and demand freedom from colonial rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State any one characteristic of colonial administration: ____. A: It used harsh laws and force. Colonial rulers forced Africans to obey through harsh punishments.
chunks.source: Colonial rulers forced Africans to obey through harsh punishments.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why was slave trade regarded as an evil practice in East Africa? ____. A: It caused suffering and loss of lives. People were captured, chained and many died; families were broken.
chunks.source: People were captured, chained and many died; families were broken.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one positive effect of colonial rule in Uganda: ____. A: Colonialists built roads, schools and hospitals. The colonial government constructed infrastructure like roads and schools.
chunks.source: The colonial government constructed infrastructure like roads and schools.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name the British governor who was responsible for the Kabaka crisis in Buganda in 1953: ____. A: Sir Andrew Cohen. Governor Cohen exiled Kabaka Muteesa II in 1953, causing the crisis.
chunks.source: Governor Cohen exiled Kabaka Muteesa II in 1953, causing the crisis.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why did the British advise Ugandans to have national symbols before 9th October 1962? ____. A: So that Uganda would have symbols of an independent nation. A new nation needs a flag, an anthem and a coat of arms to show its identity.
chunks.source: A new nation needs a flag, an anthem and a coat of arms to show its identity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why did the British use direct rule in some parts of Uganda? ____. A: Because those areas had no strong centralized kingdoms. Where there were no kings to rule through, the British ruled directly.
chunks.source: Where there were no kings to rule through, the British ruled directly.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State one way how formal education contributed to the success of missionary work in Uganda: ____. A: It enabled Africans to read the Bible. Schools taught reading and writing, so converts could read the Bible themselves.
chunks.source: Schools taught reading and writing, so converts could read the Bible themselves.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How did the 1966 constitution affect kingdoms in Uganda? ____. A: It abolished the kingdoms. The 1966 constitution ended the traditional kingdoms in Uganda.
chunks.source: The 1966 constitution ended the traditional kingdoms in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How was IBEACo useful to Christian missionaries in Uganda? ____. A: It gave them protection. The company provided armed protection to missionaries as they worked.
chunks.source: The company provided armed protection to missionaries as they worked.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who were the founders of Bunyoro Kitara Kingdom? ____. A: The Bachwezi. The Bachwezi founded the Bunyoro Kitara Kingdom.
chunks.source: The Bachwezi founded the Bunyoro Kitara Kingdom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State any two causes of the downfall of Bunyoro Kitara: ____. A: The Luo invasion and internal conflicts. The Luo attacked the kingdom and the Bachwezi also quarrelled among themselves.
chunks.source: The Luo attacked the kingdom and the Bachwezi also quarrelled among themselves.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name the African country that tried to colonise Uganda: ____. A: Egypt. Egypt, under the Khedive, tried to extend its rule into Uganda through Equatoria.
chunks.source: Egypt, under the Khedive, tried to extend its rule into Uganda through Equatoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How was River Nile responsible for the coming of early explorers to Uganda? ____. A: They came to find its source. Explorers followed the Nile inland to discover where it begins.
chunks.source: Explorers followed the Nile inland to discover where it begins.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why are the Bachwezi economically remembered in the history of Uganda? ____. A: They introduced long-horned cattle. The Bachwezi brought long-horned cattle which improved livestock keeping.
chunks.source: The Bachwezi brought long-horned cattle which improved livestock keeping.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How important were clan heads in the pre-colonial societies? ____. A: They settled disputes and led their clans. Clan heads kept order and guided their people before colonial rule.
chunks.source: Clan heads kept order and guided their people before colonial rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which European missionary brought a printing press to Uganda? ____. A: Alexander Mackay. Mackay brought the first printing press and taught printing.
chunks.source: Mackay brought the first printing press and taught printing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who was the last king of the Bachwezi? ____. A: King Wamala. Wamala was the last ruler of the Bachwezi before the Luo took over.
chunks.source: Wamala was the last ruler of the Bachwezi before the Luo took over.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who signed the 1900 Buganda Agreement on behalf of Buganda Kingdom? ____. A: Sir Apollo Kaggwa. Kaggwa, a Buganda regent, signed for the kingdom.
chunks.source: Kaggwa, a Buganda regent, signed for the kingdom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who signed the 1900 Buganda Agreement on behalf of the British government? ____. A: Sir Harry Johnston. Johnston signed the agreement for Britain.
chunks.source: Johnston signed the agreement for Britain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: In which two ways did the Arabs contribute to the development of East Africa? ____. A: They introduced new crops and promoted trade. Arabs brought new crops like cloves and rice and developed trade along the coast.
chunks.source: Arabs brought new crops like cloves and rice and developed trade along the coast.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give two reasons why slave trade took long to end in East Africa: ____. A: The Arabs resisted its end and it was very profitable. Slave traders fought abolition because the trade made them rich.
chunks.source: Slave traders fought abolition because the trade made them rich.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which political party was formed by I.K. Musaazi? ____. A: Uganda National Congress (UNC). Musaazi formed the UNC, Uganda's first political party.
chunks.source: Musaazi formed the UNC, Uganda's first political party.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name any one form of tax that was introduced by the 1900 Buganda Agreement: ____. A: Hut tax. The agreement introduced hut tax and gun tax in Buganda.
chunks.source: The agreement introduced hut tax and gun tax in Buganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name the British official who declared Uganda a British Protectorate: ____. A: Sir Gerald Portal. Portal declared Uganda a British protectorate in 1894.
chunks.source: Portal declared Uganda a British protectorate in 1894.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What attitude did Chief Awich of Payera have towards the British? ____. A: He resisted the British. Chief Awich fought against British colonial rule.
chunks.source: Chief Awich fought against British colonial rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State the tribal group of people that ruled Bunyoro-Kitara after the Bachwezi: ____. A: The Luo. The Luo, led by the Babiito clan, took over from the Bachwezi.
chunks.source: The Luo, led by the Babiito clan, took over from the Bachwezi.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give any evidence to show that the Portuguese were once at the East African coast: ____. A: Fort Jesus in Mombasa. The Portuguese built Fort Jesus and the Vasco da Gama pillar at Malindi.
chunks.source: The Portuguese built Fort Jesus and the Vasco da Gama pillar at Malindi.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How did the coming of Arabs promote the agricultural sector in East Africa? ____. A: They introduced new crops like cloves and rice. Arabs brought cloves, rice and new farming methods.
chunks.source: Arabs brought cloves, rice and new farming methods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why H.M. Stanley is associated with the coming of missionaries in Uganda: ____. A: He wrote a letter inviting missionaries to Uganda. Stanley's letter to England led to missionaries being sent to Buganda.
chunks.source: Stanley's letter to England led to missionaries being sent to Buganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give the main reason why IBEACo withdrew from Uganda: ____. A: It had run bankrupt. The company lost money and could not continue administering Uganda.
chunks.source: The company lost money and could not continue administering Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How did the Berlin Conference of 1884 and 1885 affect the people of East Africa? ____. A: It led to the partition of East Africa. Europeans divided Africa among themselves without asking Africans.
chunks.source: Europeans divided Africa among themselves without asking Africans.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who was the leader of the Maji Maji rebellion in Tanganyika? ____. A: Kinjeketile Ngwale. Kinjeketile led the Maji Maji rebellion against German rule.
chunks.source: Kinjeketile led the Maji Maji rebellion against German rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State any two major causes of the Maji Maji rebellion: ____. A: Forced cotton growing and heavy taxes. Germans forced Africans to grow cotton and taxed them heavily.
chunks.source: Germans forced Africans to grow cotton and taxed them heavily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give any one result of the Maji Maji rebellion: ____. A: Many Africans were killed. The Germans crushed the rebellion and thousands died.
chunks.source: The Germans crushed the rebellion and thousands died.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which political party led Uganda to self rule in 1961? ____. A: Democratic Party (DP). The DP won the 1961 elections and Ben Kiwanuka became chief minister.
chunks.source: The DP won the 1961 elections and Ben Kiwanuka became chief minister.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who was the founder of the Democratic Party? ____. A: Ben Kiwanuka. Ben Kiwanuka founded the Democratic Party.
chunks.source: Ben Kiwanuka founded the Democratic Party.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How was U.P.C able to win the 1962 general elections? ____. A: By forming an alliance with Kabaka Yekka. UPC joined with KY to defeat the DP in 1962.
chunks.source: UPC joined with KY to defeat the DP in 1962.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who was the leader of U.P.C at the time of independence? ____. A: Dr. Apollo Milton Obote. Obote led UPC and became Uganda's first prime minister.
chunks.source: Obote led UPC and became Uganda's first prime minister.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Write LEGCo in full: ____. A: Legislative Council. LEGCo was the law-making body in colonial Uganda.
chunks.source: LEGCo was the law-making body in colonial Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Apart from making laws, give another reason why LEGCo was formed in Uganda in 1921: ____. A: To advise the governor. LEGCo advised the colonial governor on ruling Uganda.
chunks.source: LEGCo advised the colonial governor on ruling Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why the land given to the Kabaka of Buganda during the 1900 Buganda Agreement was called mailo land: ____. A: It was measured in square miles. Mailo comes from 'mile'; the land was measured in square miles.
chunks.source: Mailo comes from 'mile'; the land was measured in square miles.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which group of foreigners introduced the idea of selling people as slaves? ____. A: The Arabs. Arab traders started the slave trade in East Africa.
chunks.source: Arab traders started the slave trade in East Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How was Zanzibar economically important to the Arabs? ____. A: It was the centre of the slave trade. Arabs used Zanzibar as their main trading base for slaves and cloves.
chunks.source: Arabs used Zanzibar as their main trading base for slaves and cloves.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Write IBEACo in full: ____. A: Imperial British East Africa Company. IBEACo was the British trading company that ruled Uganda before the protectorate.
chunks.source: IBEACo was the British trading company that ruled Uganda before the protectorate.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How did missionary work improve the lives of Africans? ____. A: They built schools and hospitals. Missionaries provided education and health care.
chunks.source: Missionaries provided education and health care.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How was Germany punished by the League of Nations after World War I? ____. A: Her colonies were taken away. Germany lost all her colonies, which were shared as mandates.
chunks.source: Germany lost all her colonies, which were shared as mandates.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name any one tribe from Uganda that participated in the Long Distance Trade: ____. A: The Nyamwezi. The Nyamwezi were great traders in the long distance trade.
chunks.source: The Nyamwezi were great traders in the long distance trade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why Christian missionaries built mission stations on hills: ____. A: For security. Hills were safe places from which enemies could be seen from far.
chunks.source: Hills were safe places from which enemies could be seen from far.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Mention the first political party in Uganda: ____. A: Uganda National Congress (UNC). The UNC, formed by I.K. Musaazi, was Uganda's first party.
chunks.source: The UNC, formed by I.K. Musaazi, was Uganda's first party.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How was the work of LegCo similar to that of Parliament of Uganda today? ____. A: Both make laws. LEGCo made laws in colonial times, as Parliament does today.
chunks.source: LEGCo made laws in colonial times, as Parliament does today.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give the main reason for the calling of the Berlin Conference of 1884-1885: ____. A: To partition Africa peacefully. European powers wanted to share Africa without fighting each other.
chunks.source: European powers wanted to share Africa without fighting each other.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State any two European countries that attended the Berlin Conference of 1884-1885: ____. A: Britain and Germany. Many European powers, including Britain, Germany, France and Portugal, attended.
chunks.source: Many European powers, including Britain, Germany, France and Portugal, attended.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why didn't African leaders attend the 1884-1885 Berlin Conference? ____. A: They were not invited. Europeans did not invite or recognize African leaders.
chunks.source: Europeans did not invite or recognize African leaders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: In which East African country was the Maji Maji rebellion fought? ____. A: Tanzania. The Maji Maji rebellion was fought in Tanganyika against German rule.
chunks.source: The Maji Maji rebellion was fought in Tanganyika against German rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give any two factors which forced the people of Tanzania to demand for their freedom: ____. A: Forced labour and heavy taxes. Germans forced Africans to work and taxed them heavily.
chunks.source: Germans forced Africans to work and taxed them heavily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why was African resistance towards colonial rule defeated? ____. A: Africans had inferior weapons. Europeans had guns while Africans had spears and arrows.
chunks.source: Europeans had guns while Africans had spears and arrows.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Match the people in list A with their contributions in list B correctly: Harry Johnstone, Chaille Long, Dr. Albert Cook, Alexander Mackay. A: Harry Johnstone: Led a Scientific mission to Mt. Kilimanjaro; Chaille Long: discovered Lake Kyoga; Dr. Albert Cook: built Mengo Hospital; Alexander Mackay: Was the leader of C.M.S in Uganda. Harry Johnstone led a scientific mission to Mt. Kilimanjaro; Chaille Long discovered Lake Kyoga; Dr. Albert Cook built Mengo Hospital; Alexander Mackay led the Church Missionary Society in Uganda.
chunks.source: Harry Johnstone led a scientific mission to Mt. Kilimanjaro; Chaille Long discovered Lake Kyoga; Dr. Albert Cook built Mengo Hospital; Alexander Mackay led the Church Missionary Society in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does the fencing of a school promote its security? ____. A: It keeps away strangers and stray animals. A fence stops intruders and animals from entering the school compound freely.
chunks.source: A fence stops intruders and animals from entering the school compound freely.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In which way does security promote development in an area? ____. A: People invest without fear of losing their property. When an area is secure, people build businesses and invest because their property is safe.
chunks.source: When an area is secure, people build businesses and invest because their property is safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one way in which high population promotes industrialization: ____. A: It provides a large market for industrial goods. Many people buy the goods that industries produce, so industries grow.
chunks.source: Many people buy the goods that industries produce, so industries grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do people in a constituency benefit from their representatives in parliament? ____. A: Their representatives present their problems and needs in parliament. MPs speak for their people and help bring services to their areas.
chunks.source: MPs speak for their people and help bring services to their areas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why should every community have a midwife? ____. A: To help mothers deliver babies safely. Midwives are trained to handle childbirth and reduce deaths of mothers and babies.
chunks.source: Midwives are trained to handle childbirth and reduce deaths of mothers and babies.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is population distribution? ____. A: The way people are spread over an area. Some areas have many people while others have few; that pattern is population distribution.
chunks.source: Some areas have many people while others have few; that pattern is population distribution.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two factors that influence population distribution in East Africa: ____. A: Climate and soil fertility. People settle where the climate is good, soils are fertile and jobs exist.
chunks.source: People settle where the climate is good, soils are fertile and jobs exist.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one effect of immigration to Kampala city: ____. A: Overcrowding. Many people moving into Kampala make it crowded and strain services.
chunks.source: Many people moving into Kampala make it crowded and strain services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are human rights? ____. A: The freedoms and benefits every person deserves. Human rights are things like the right to life and education that belong to everyone.
chunks.source: Human rights are things like the right to life and education that belong to everyone.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two human rights known to you: ____. A: The right to life and the right to education. Everyone has the right to live and to go to school.
chunks.source: Everyone has the right to live and to go to school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why citizens should know their rights: ____. A: To protect themselves from abuse. People who know their rights can defend themselves when mistreated.
chunks.source: People who know their rights can defend themselves when mistreated.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write in full the ruling political party in Uganda: ____. A: National Resistance Movement (NRM). The NRM is the party currently ruling Uganda.
chunks.source: The NRM is the party currently ruling Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the ruling party, name any two political parties operating in Uganda today: ____. A: Forum for Democratic Change (FDC) and Democratic Party (DP). Uganda has many parties, including FDC, DP and UPC.
chunks.source: Uganda has many parties, including FDC, DP and UPC.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one challenge the government may face in providing social services to its people: ____. A: Limited funds. The government may not have enough money to build schools and hospitals for everyone.
chunks.source: The government may not have enough money to build schools and hospitals for everyone.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can the Uganda police help to reduce crime in our community today? ____. A: By arresting criminals. Police patrol and arrest law-breakers, which scares away criminals.
chunks.source: Police patrol and arrest law-breakers, which scares away criminals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one way religious leaders may help in keeping peace and security in our community: ____. A: By preaching peace and settling disputes. Religious leaders teach people to live peacefully and help solve quarrels.
chunks.source: Religious leaders teach people to live peacefully and help solve quarrels.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Child abuse is the physical maltreatment of a child. Give one effect of child abuse: ____. A: It can cause death or serious injuries. Abused children may be injured, traumatized or even killed.
chunks.source: Abused children may be injured, traumatized or even killed.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one problem of high population density in an area: ____. A: Congestion. Too many people in a small area leads to crowding and land shortage.
chunks.source: Too many people in a small area leads to crowding and land shortage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one role of the Electoral Commission in a democratic state: ____. A: To organize and conduct elections. The Electoral Commission registers voters and runs elections.
chunks.source: The Electoral Commission registers voters and runs elections.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Aggrey is a Ugandan boy whose grandfather was Tanzanian. In which way did he become a citizen of Tanzania? ____. A: By descent. A person can become a citizen through a parent or grandparent from that country.
chunks.source: A person can become a citizen through a parent or grandparent from that country.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Kaberamaido district has 3600 people and covers 40 square kilometres. Find its population density: ____. A: 90 people per square kilometre. Population density equals total people divided by area: 3600 divided by 40 equals 90.
chunks.source: Population density equals total people divided by area: 3600 divided by 40 equals 90.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one disadvantage of sparse population: ____. A: It is difficult to provide social services. When people are few and scattered, building schools and hospitals for them is costly.
chunks.source: When people are few and scattered, building schools and hospitals for them is costly.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one disadvantage of high population density: ____. A: Congestion and land shortage. Too many people in a small area causes crowding.
chunks.source: Too many people in a small area causes crowding.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can the government help to control rapid population growth in a country? ____. A: By promoting family planning. Teaching people to have fewer children slows population growth.
chunks.source: Teaching people to have fewer children slows population growth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are social services? ____. A: Services provided by the government to improve people's welfare. Schools, hospitals and clean water are social services.
chunks.source: Schools, hospitals and clean water are social services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two social service providers found in Mulago hospital: ____. A: Doctors and nurses. Doctors treat patients and nurses care for them.
chunks.source: Doctors treat patients and nurses care for them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can the government help to make medical services better in Uganda? ____. A: By building more hospitals and training more health workers. More hospitals and trained workers improve health care.
chunks.source: More hospitals and trained workers improve health care.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of leaders that we get through elections: ____. A: Elected leaders. Leaders chosen by voting are called elected leaders.
chunks.source: Leaders chosen by voting are called elected leaders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two examples of elected leaders: ____. A: Members of Parliament and LC chairpersons. MPs and local council leaders are elected by the people.
chunks.source: MPs and local council leaders are elected by the people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one way leaders can be useful to their people: ____. A: They bring services to their people. Good leaders speak for their people and attract development.
chunks.source: Good leaders speak for their people and attract development.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are social service centres? ____. A: Places where social services are provided, like schools and hospitals. People go to social service centres to get education, treatment and water.
chunks.source: People go to social service centres to get education, treatment and water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify one importance of conducting a population census in a country: ____. A: It helps the government to plan for the people. Knowing the number of people helps the government provide enough services.
chunks.source: Knowing the number of people helps the government provide enough services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Education is a common social service everywhere in the world. Explain the importance of education: ____. A: It gives people knowledge and skills. Education teaches reading, writing and skills for work.
chunks.source: Education teaches reading, writing and skills for work.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is democracy exercised in a school community? ____. A: Through electing prefects and leaders. Pupils vote for their leaders, which is democracy in school.
chunks.source: Pupils vote for their leaders, which is democracy in school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does corruption affect the development of a country? ____. A: It slows development. Corrupt officials steal money meant for roads, schools and hospitals.
chunks.source: Corrupt officials steal money meant for roads, schools and hospitals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one disadvantage of smuggling in a country like Uganda: ____. A: The government loses tax revenue. Smuggled goods pay no tax, so the government gets less money.
chunks.source: Smuggled goods pay no tax, so the government gets less money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is child abuse? ____. A: The mistreatment of children. Beating, overworking or neglecting children is child abuse.
chunks.source: Beating, overworking or neglecting children is child abuse.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one form of child abuse: ____. A: Beating. Common forms of child abuse include beating, child labour and neglect.
chunks.source: Common forms of child abuse include beating, child labour and neglect.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one way in which we can reduce the rate of child abuse in our community today: ____. A: By reporting abusers to the police. Punishing abusers scares others from abusing children.
chunks.source: Punishing abusers scares others from abusing children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are by-laws? ____. A: Laws made by local councils. Local councils make by-laws to govern their areas.
chunks.source: Local councils make by-laws to govern their areas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who makes the by-laws? ____. A: Local councils. Elected local council leaders make by-laws.
chunks.source: Elected local council leaders make by-laws.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two importance of by-laws in our community: ____. A: They maintain order and promote hygiene. By-laws keep peace and ensure clean surroundings.
chunks.source: By-laws keep peace and ensure clean surroundings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is the Judiciary an important arm of a democratic government? ____. A: It interprets laws and settles disputes. Courts punish law-breakers and solve quarrels fairly.
chunks.source: Courts punish law-breakers and solve quarrels fairly.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one disadvantage of a high population to a country like Uganda: ____. A: It strains social services. Many people share few schools, hospitals and little land.
chunks.source: Many people share few schools, hospitals and little land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is 8th March celebrated worldwide every year? ____. A: It is International Women's Day. The world honours the achievements of women on 8th March.
chunks.source: The world honours the achievements of women on 8th March.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the democratic leader elected in a school: ____. A: The head prefect. Pupils elect the head prefect to lead them.
chunks.source: Pupils elect the head prefect to lead them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one responsibility of a child at home: ____. A: Helping with housework. Children should help at home and obey their parents.
chunks.source: Children should help at home and obey their parents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down any two causes of child abuse: ____. A: Poverty and alcoholism. Poor, drunk or quarrelling parents may abuse their children.
chunks.source: Poor, drunk or quarrelling parents may abuse their children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the official at the district in charge of children's rights: ____. A: The District Probation Officer. This officer protects the rights of children in the district.
chunks.source: This officer protects the rights of children in the district.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why Ugandans pay taxes to the government: ____. A: To enable the government to provide services. Tax money builds roads, schools and hospitals.
chunks.source: Tax money builds roads, schools and hospitals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one duty of the Uganda Revenue Authority (URA): ____. A: To collect taxes. URA collects taxes on behalf of the government.
chunks.source: URA collects taxes on behalf of the government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one reason why some Ugandans don't want to pay taxes: ____. A: Taxes are too high. Some people feel taxes are high or the money is misused.
chunks.source: Some people feel taxes are high or the money is misused.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which ministry is in charge of the activities of the Uganda Revenue Authority? ____. A: The Ministry of Finance. URA works under the Ministry of Finance.
chunks.source: URA works under the Ministry of Finance.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a budget? ____. A: A plan of income and expenditure. A budget shows how money will be got and spent.
chunks.source: A budget shows how money will be got and spent.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for a school to make a budget? ____. A: To plan spending and avoid wastage. A budget helps the school use its money wisely.
chunks.source: A budget helps the school use its money wisely.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two types of budget: ____. A: Surplus budget and deficit budget. A surplus budget has income more than spending; a deficit budget has spending more than income.
chunks.source: A surplus budget has income more than spending; a deficit budget has spending more than income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one indicator of democracy in East African countries: ____. A: Holding free and fair elections. Regular elections show that people choose their leaders.
chunks.source: Regular elections show that people choose their leaders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a social activity: ____. A: Football. People play, dance and celebrate together in social activities.
chunks.source: People play, dance and celebrate together in social activities.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Democracy means government of the people, by the people and for the people. What do 'of the people', 'by the people' and 'for the people' mean? ____. A: Of the people: government belongs to the people; by the people: leaders are chosen by the people; for the people: government works for the people's benefit. Democracy is power belonging to the people, exercised through leaders they choose, for their own good.
chunks.source: Democracy is power belonging to the people, exercised through leaders they choose, for their own good.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The table shows three houses: Ephesians (8000 sq km, 10 million people), Galatians (120000 sq km, 8 million people), Romans (24000 sq km, 12 million people). Which house has the biggest population? ____. A: Romans. Romans has 12 million people, more than the others.
chunks.source: Romans has 12 million people, more than the others.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same table, what is the size of house Romans? ____. A: 24000 square kilometres. The table shows Romans covers 24,000 square kilometres.
chunks.source: The table shows Romans covers 24,000 square kilometres.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same table, which house has the least population density? ____. A: Galatians. Galatians has the lowest density of 66 people per square kilometre.
chunks.source: Galatians has the lowest density of 66 people per square kilometre.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same table, calculate the population density of Galatians: ____. A: 67 people per square kilometre. Density equals people divided by area: 8,000,000 divided by 120,000 is about 67.
chunks.source: Density equals people divided by area: 8,000,000 divided by 120,000 is about 67.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The three arms of government are Legislature, Executive and Judiciary. In which arm of government would you place lawyers? ____. A: The Judiciary. Lawyers work in courts, which are part of the Judiciary.
chunks.source: Lawyers work in courts, which are part of the Judiciary.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the main duty of the Legislature arm? ____. A: To make laws. Parliament, the Legislature, makes the country's laws.
chunks.source: Parliament, the Legislature, makes the country's laws.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one group of people under the Executive arm of government: ____. A: Ministers. The President and ministers form the Executive.
chunks.source: The President and ministers form the Executive.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a Bill as used in Parliament? ____. A: A proposed law. A Bill is a suggestion for a new law discussed in Parliament.
chunks.source: A Bill is a suggestion for a new law discussed in Parliament.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one river which flows into Lake Victoria: ____. A: River Kagera. River Kagera is the largest river that flows into Lake Victoria.
chunks.source: River Kagera is the largest river that flows into Lake Victoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one river which flows into Lake Victoria: Smoking and sun drying_. A: False. River Kagera is the largest river that flows into Lake Victoria.
chunks.source: River Kagera is the largest river that flows into Lake Victoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The table shows monthly rainfall of 80mm to 230mm and temperatures of 24 to 26 degrees Celsius all year. What type of climate is shown above? ____. A: Equatorial climate. Temperatures are high and fairly uniform all year, with rainfall in every month.
chunks.source: Temperatures are high and fairly uniform all year, with rainfall in every month.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The table shows monthly rainfall of 80mm to 230mm and temperatures of 24 to 26 degrees Celsius all year. What type of climate is shown above? Forests provide them with food and shelter_. A: False. Temperatures are high and fairly uniform all year, with rainfall in every month.
chunks.source: Temperatures are high and fairly uniform all year, with rainfall in every month.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same climatic table, which activity can be done by farmers in the month of January? ____. A: Harvesting. January receives little rain, so farmers harvest and dry their crops.
chunks.source: January receives little rain, so farmers harvest and dry their crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same climatic table, which activity can be done by farmers in the month of January? They are long and narrow_. A: False. January receives little rain, so farmers harvest and dry their crops.
chunks.source: January receives little rain, so farmers harvest and dry their crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one element of weather which makes people sweat: ____. A: High temperature (heat). When the temperature is high, the body sweats to cool down.
chunks.source: When the temperature is high, the body sweats to cool down.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one element of weather which makes people sweat: The catching of fish from water bodies_. A: False. When the temperature is high, the body sweats to cool down.
chunks.source: When the temperature is high, the body sweats to cool down.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two problems facing the fishing industry in East Africa: ____. A: Overfishing and water pollution. Catching too many fish reduces stocks, and pollution kills fish.
chunks.source: Catching too many fish reduces stocks, and pollution kills fish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two problems facing the fishing industry in East Africa: Soil erosion_. A: False. Catching too many fish reduces stocks, and pollution kills fish.
chunks.source: Catching too many fish reduces stocks, and pollution kills fish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two ways of preserving fish: ____. A: Smoking and sun drying. Removing water from fish by smoking, drying or salting stops it from rotting.
chunks.source: Removing water from fish by smoking, drying or salting stops it from rotting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two ways of preserving fish: For protection_. A: False. Removing water from fish by smoking, drying or salting stops it from rotting.
chunks.source: Removing water from fish by smoking, drying or salting stops it from rotting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two major resources found in East Africa: ____. A: Minerals and forests. East Africa is rich in minerals, forests, water bodies and wildlife.
chunks.source: East Africa is rich in minerals, forests, water bodies and wildlife.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two major resources found in East Africa: They determine the rainfall received in an area_. A: False. East Africa is rich in minerals, forests, water bodies and wildlife.
chunks.source: East Africa is rich in minerals, forests, water bodies and wildlife.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the stage of a river that is suitable for the construction of electric dams: ____. A: The young stage. Waterfalls, which provide falling water for power, occur in the young stage of a river.
chunks.source: Waterfalls, which provide falling water for power, occur in the young stage of a river.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the stage of a river that is suitable for the construction of electric dams: Mountain gorillas_. A: False. Waterfalls, which provide falling water for power, occur in the young stage of a river.
chunks.source: Waterfalls, which provide falling water for power, occur in the young stage of a river.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do the people of Kabale adapt to the cool climatic conditions? ____. A: By wearing heavy warm clothes. Kabale is cold, so people wear warm clothes and build warm houses.
chunks.source: Kabale is cold, so people wear warm clothes and build warm houses.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do the people of Kabale adapt to the cool climatic conditions? River Achwa_. A: False. Kabale is cold, so people wear warm clothes and build warm houses.
chunks.source: Kabale is cold, so people wear warm clothes and build warm houses.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are the Turkana and the Karimojong similar in terms of their activities? ____. A: Both practise pastoralism. The Turkana of Kenya and the Karimojong of Uganda are both cattle keepers.
chunks.source: The Turkana of Kenya and the Karimojong of Uganda are both cattle keepers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are the Turkana and the Karimojong similar in terms of their activities? It has caused crop failure and famine_. A: False. The Turkana of Kenya and the Karimojong of Uganda are both cattle keepers.
chunks.source: The Turkana of Kenya and the Karimojong of Uganda are both cattle keepers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two human activities that have led to the destruction of the environment: ____. A: Deforestation and bush burning. Cutting down trees and burning bushes destroy the environment.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees and burning bushes destroy the environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two human activities that have led to the destruction of the environment: Equatorial climate_. A: False. Cutting down trees and burning bushes destroy the environment.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees and burning bushes destroy the environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the largest climatic zone of Uganda: ____. A: The tropical climatic zone. Most of Uganda has a tropical climate with wet and dry seasons.
chunks.source: Most of Uganda has a tropical climate with wet and dry seasons.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the largest climatic zone of Uganda: River Achwa_. A: False. Most of Uganda has a tropical climate with wet and dry seasons.
chunks.source: Most of Uganda has a tropical climate with wet and dry seasons.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one human activity that can destroy our environment: ____. A: Deforestation. Cutting down trees destroys forests and animal homes.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees destroys forests and animal homes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one human activity that can destroy our environment: Our surroundings_. A: False. Cutting down trees destroys forests and animal homes.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees destroys forests and animal homes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention the major cash crop that was introduced by the Arabs along the coast of East Africa: ____. A: Cloves. Arabs introduced clove growing, especially in Zanzibar.
chunks.source: Arabs introduced clove growing, especially in Zanzibar.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention the major cash crop that was introduced by the Arabs along the coast of East Africa: Soil erosion_. A: False. Arabs introduced clove growing, especially in Zanzibar.
chunks.source: Arabs introduced clove growing, especially in Zanzibar.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one weather instrument that can be kept in the Stevenson screen: ____. A: A thermometer. Maximum and minimum thermometers are kept in the Stevenson screen.
chunks.source: Maximum and minimum thermometers are kept in the Stevenson screen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one weather instrument that can be kept in the Stevenson screen: Poaching and poor roads_. A: False. Maximum and minimum thermometers are kept in the Stevenson screen.
chunks.source: Maximum and minimum thermometers are kept in the Stevenson screen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify one problem that is faced by people who live around hilly and mountainous areas: ____. A: Soil erosion. Steep slopes make soil wash away easily.
chunks.source: Steep slopes make soil wash away easily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify one problem that is faced by people who live around hilly and mountainous areas: Mountain gorillas_. A: False. Steep slopes make soil wash away easily.
chunks.source: Steep slopes make soil wash away easily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the physical feature that crosses at least five East African countries: ____. A: The Rift Valley. The Rift Valley runs through many East African countries.
chunks.source: The Rift Valley runs through many East African countries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the physical feature that crosses at least five East African countries: Lack of capital and poor transport_. A: False. The Rift Valley runs through many East African countries.
chunks.source: The Rift Valley runs through many East African countries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason for controlling soil erosion in mountainous areas: ____. A: To keep the soil fertile. Erosion washes away the fertile top soil needed by crops.
chunks.source: Erosion washes away the fertile top soil needed by crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason for controlling soil erosion in mountainous areas: Deforestation and bush burning_. A: False. Erosion washes away the fertile top soil needed by crops.
chunks.source: Erosion washes away the fertile top soil needed by crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one disadvantage of using traditional methods of fishing: ____. A: They catch few fish. Hooks and baskets catch less fish than modern nets.
chunks.source: Hooks and baskets catch less fish than modern nets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one disadvantage of using traditional methods of fishing: Lack of capital and poor transport_. A: False. Hooks and baskets catch less fish than modern nets.
chunks.source: Hooks and baskets catch less fish than modern nets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one importance of planting grass in the school compound: ____. A: It controls soil erosion. Grass holds the soil and makes the compound beautiful.
chunks.source: Grass holds the soil and makes the compound beautiful.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one importance of planting grass in the school compound: They have limestone used to make cement_. A: False. Grass holds the soil and makes the compound beautiful.
chunks.source: Grass holds the soil and makes the compound beautiful.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the biggest water mass that neighbours East Africa in the east: ____. A: The Indian Ocean. The Indian Ocean lies to the east of East Africa.
chunks.source: The Indian Ocean lies to the east of East Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the biggest water mass that neighbours East Africa in the east: The destruction of land_. A: False. The Indian Ocean lies to the east of East Africa.
chunks.source: The Indian Ocean lies to the east of East Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one tributary of the River Nile in Uganda: ____. A: River Achwa. The Achwa joins the Nile in northern Uganda.
chunks.source: The Achwa joins the Nile in northern Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one tributary of the River Nile in Uganda: Because it generates income and employs people_. A: False. The Achwa joins the Nile in northern Uganda.
chunks.source: The Achwa joins the Nile in northern Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one factor that can influence the climate of an area: ____. A: Altitude. High places are cooler; areas near the equator are hotter.
chunks.source: High places are cooler; areas near the equator are hotter.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one factor that can influence the climate of an area: The sun's rays strike directly overhead_. A: False. High places are cooler; areas near the equator are hotter.
chunks.source: High places are cooler; areas near the equator are hotter.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one problem that is faced by farmers in Uganda today: ____. A: Pests and diseases. Pests destroy crops and little rain causes poor harvests.
chunks.source: Pests destroy crops and little rain causes poor harvests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one problem that is faced by farmers in Uganda today: Lumbering_. A: False. Pests destroy crops and little rain causes poor harvests.
chunks.source: Pests destroy crops and little rain causes poor harvests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two problems that are faced by the tourism industry in our country: ____. A: Poaching and poor roads. Killing of wild animals and bad roads discourage tourists.
chunks.source: Killing of wild animals and bad roads discourage tourists.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two problems that are faced by the tourism industry in our country: High temperature (heat)_. A: False. Killing of wild animals and bad roads discourage tourists.
chunks.source: Killing of wild animals and bad roads discourage tourists.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any invisible export of Uganda to Kenya and Rwanda: ____. A: Tourism. Tourists from Kenya and Rwanda spend money in Uganda without carrying goods.
chunks.source: Tourists from Kenya and Rwanda spend money in Uganda without carrying goods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any invisible export of Uganda to Kenya and Rwanda: It provides jobs on farms and raw materials for industries_. A: False. Tourists from Kenya and Rwanda spend money in Uganda without carrying goods.
chunks.source: Tourists from Kenya and Rwanda spend money in Uganda without carrying goods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the major occupation of the Turkana people in Kenya? ____. A: Pastoralism. The Turkana keep cattle, goats and sheep in the dry lands of Kenya.
chunks.source: The Turkana keep cattle, goats and sheep in the dry lands of Kenya.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the major occupation of the Turkana people in Kenya? They attract tourists who bring foreign exchange_. A: False. The Turkana keep cattle, goats and sheep in the dry lands of Kenya.
chunks.source: The Turkana keep cattle, goats and sheep in the dry lands of Kenya.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Apart from human activity, give any one other factor that determines the vegetation of an area: ____. A: Climate. The amount of rainfall decides what plants grow in an area.
chunks.source: The amount of rainfall decides what plants grow in an area.
