chunks.source: Tourists visit Bwindi and Mgahinga to see mountain gorillas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is environment? ____. A: Our surroundings. The environment includes air, water, soil, plants, animals and buildings around us.
chunks.source: The environment includes air, water, soil, plants, animals and buildings around us.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention two types of environment you know: ____. A: Natural environment and man-made environment. Forests and lakes are natural; roads and buildings are man-made.
chunks.source: Forests and lakes are natural; roads and buildings are man-made.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Apart from water, write any other item transported using pipelines: ____. A: Crude oil (petroleum). Pipelines also carry petroleum products and natural gas.
chunks.source: Pipelines also carry petroleum products and natural gas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one mobile phone company operating in Uganda: ____. A: MTN Uganda. MTN and Airtel are mobile phone companies operating in Uganda.
chunks.source: MTN and Airtel are mobile phone companies operating in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State two reasons why there are many road accidents in Uganda today: ____. A: Over speeding and drunk driving. Drivers who speed or drink cause many accidents.
chunks.source: Drivers who speed or drink cause many accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: In which way can road accidents be controlled in Uganda? ____. A: By enforcing traffic rules. Police can punish over speeding and drunk drivers to make roads safer.
chunks.source: Police can punish over speeding and drunk drivers to make roads safer.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What part of the Uganda Coat of Arms represents Uganda's traditional communication? ____. A: The drum. In the past, drums were used to send messages, so the drum appears on the coat of arms.
chunks.source: In the past, drums were used to send messages, so the drum appears on the coat of arms.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Apart from a television, give two other forms of mass media: ____. A: Radio and newspapers. Radio and newspapers also pass information to many people.
chunks.source: Radio and newspapers also pass information to many people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why televisions are not commonly used in rural areas: ____. A: There is no electricity. Most rural homes lack electricity to power television sets.
chunks.source: Most rural homes lack electricity to power television sets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State any one way television stations promote employment opportunities to people: ____. A: They employ journalists and presenters. Television stations give jobs to reporters, presenters and technicians.
chunks.source: Television stations give jobs to reporters, presenters and technicians.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being expensive, give another reason why air transport is not used by many people in Uganda: ____. A: There are few airports. Uganda has few airports, so air transport is not common.
chunks.source: Uganda has few airports, so air transport is not common.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name any one inland port found on Lake Victoria in Kenya: ____. A: Kisumu. Kisumu is a major inland port on Lake Victoria in Kenya.
chunks.source: Kisumu is a major inland port on Lake Victoria in Kenya.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which explorer followed the River Nile from its mouth? ____. A: John Hanning Speke. Speke traced the River Nile and proved that Lake Victoria is its source.
chunks.source: Speke traced the River Nile and proved that Lake Victoria is its source.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which missionary contributed to the economic development of Uganda? ____. A: Alexander Mackay. Mackay taught Africans farming and technical skills like carpentry and printing.
chunks.source: Mackay taught Africans farming and technical skills like carpentry and printing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why were political parties formed in the early 1950s? ____. A: To demand independence (self-rule). Africans formed parties to unite and demand freedom from colonial rule.
chunks.source: Africans formed parties to unite and demand freedom from colonial rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name the British governor who was responsible for the Kabaka crisis in Buganda in 1953: ____. A: Sir Andrew Cohen. Governor Cohen exiled Kabaka Muteesa II in 1953, causing the crisis.
chunks.source: Governor Cohen exiled Kabaka Muteesa II in 1953, causing the crisis.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How did the 1966 constitution affect kingdoms in Uganda? ____. A: It abolished the kingdoms. The 1966 constitution ended the traditional kingdoms in Uganda.
chunks.source: The 1966 constitution ended the traditional kingdoms in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How was IBEACo useful to Christian missionaries in Uganda? ____. A: It gave them protection. The company provided armed protection to missionaries as they worked.
chunks.source: The company provided armed protection to missionaries as they worked.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who were the founders of Bunyoro Kitara Kingdom? ____. A: The Bachwezi. The Bachwezi founded the Bunyoro Kitara Kingdom.
chunks.source: The Bachwezi founded the Bunyoro Kitara Kingdom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name the African country that tried to colonise Uganda: ____. A: Egypt. Egypt, under the Khedive, tried to extend its rule into Uganda through Equatoria.
chunks.source: Egypt, under the Khedive, tried to extend its rule into Uganda through Equatoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why are the Bachwezi economically remembered in the history of Uganda? ____. A: They introduced long-horned cattle. The Bachwezi brought long-horned cattle which improved livestock keeping.
chunks.source: The Bachwezi brought long-horned cattle which improved livestock keeping.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which European missionary brought a printing press to Uganda? ____. A: Alexander Mackay. Mackay brought the first printing press and taught printing.
chunks.source: Mackay brought the first printing press and taught printing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who was the last king of the Bachwezi? ____. A: King Wamala. Wamala was the last ruler of the Bachwezi before the Luo took over.
chunks.source: Wamala was the last ruler of the Bachwezi before the Luo took over.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who signed the 1900 Buganda Agreement on behalf of Buganda Kingdom? ____. A: Sir Apollo Kaggwa. Kaggwa, a Buganda regent, signed for the kingdom.
chunks.source: Kaggwa, a Buganda regent, signed for the kingdom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who signed the 1900 Buganda Agreement on behalf of the British government? ____. A: Sir Harry Johnston. Johnston signed the agreement for Britain.
chunks.source: Johnston signed the agreement for Britain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which political party was formed by I.K. Musaazi? ____. A: Uganda National Congress (UNC). Musaazi formed the UNC, Uganda's first political party.
chunks.source: Musaazi formed the UNC, Uganda's first political party.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name any one form of tax that was introduced by the 1900 Buganda Agreement: ____. A: Hut tax. The agreement introduced hut tax and gun tax in Buganda.
chunks.source: The agreement introduced hut tax and gun tax in Buganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name the British official who declared Uganda a British Protectorate: ____. A: Sir Gerald Portal. Portal declared Uganda a British protectorate in 1894.
chunks.source: Portal declared Uganda a British protectorate in 1894.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What attitude did Chief Awich of Payera have towards the British? ____. A: He resisted the British. Chief Awich fought against British colonial rule.
chunks.source: Chief Awich fought against British colonial rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State the tribal group of people that ruled Bunyoro-Kitara after the Bachwezi: ____. A: The Luo. The Luo, led by the Babiito clan, took over from the Bachwezi.
chunks.source: The Luo, led by the Babiito clan, took over from the Bachwezi.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give any evidence to show that the Portuguese were once at the East African coast: ____. A: Fort Jesus in Mombasa. The Portuguese built Fort Jesus and the Vasco da Gama pillar at Malindi.
chunks.source: The Portuguese built Fort Jesus and the Vasco da Gama pillar at Malindi.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give the main reason why IBEACo withdrew from Uganda: ____. A: It had run bankrupt. The company lost money and could not continue administering Uganda.
chunks.source: The company lost money and could not continue administering Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who was the leader of the Maji Maji rebellion in Tanganyika? ____. A: Kinjeketile Ngwale. Kinjeketile led the Maji Maji rebellion against German rule.
chunks.source: Kinjeketile led the Maji Maji rebellion against German rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give any one result of the Maji Maji rebellion: ____. A: Many Africans were killed. The Germans crushed the rebellion and thousands died.
chunks.source: The Germans crushed the rebellion and thousands died.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which political party led Uganda to self rule in 1961? ____. A: Democratic Party (DP). The DP won the 1961 elections and Ben Kiwanuka became chief minister.
chunks.source: The DP won the 1961 elections and Ben Kiwanuka became chief minister.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who was the founder of the Democratic Party? ____. A: Ben Kiwanuka. Ben Kiwanuka founded the Democratic Party.
chunks.source: Ben Kiwanuka founded the Democratic Party.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who was the leader of U.P.C at the time of independence? ____. A: Dr. Apollo Milton Obote. Obote led UPC and became Uganda's first prime minister.
chunks.source: Obote led UPC and became Uganda's first prime minister.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Write LEGCo in full: ____. A: Legislative Council. LEGCo was the law-making body in colonial Uganda.
chunks.source: LEGCo was the law-making body in colonial Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Apart from making laws, give another reason why LEGCo was formed in Uganda in 1921: ____. A: To advise the governor. LEGCo advised the colonial governor on ruling Uganda.
chunks.source: LEGCo advised the colonial governor on ruling Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which group of foreigners introduced the idea of selling people as slaves? ____. A: The Arabs. Arab traders started the slave trade in East Africa.
chunks.source: Arab traders started the slave trade in East Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Write IBEACo in full: ____. A: Imperial British East Africa Company. IBEACo was the British trading company that ruled Uganda before the protectorate.
chunks.source: IBEACo was the British trading company that ruled Uganda before the protectorate.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How did missionary work improve the lives of Africans? ____. A: They built schools and hospitals. Missionaries provided education and health care.
chunks.source: Missionaries provided education and health care.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How was Germany punished by the League of Nations after World War I? ____. A: Her colonies were taken away. Germany lost all her colonies, which were shared as mandates.
chunks.source: Germany lost all her colonies, which were shared as mandates.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name any one tribe from Uganda that participated in the Long Distance Trade: ____. A: The Nyamwezi. The Nyamwezi were great traders in the long distance trade.
chunks.source: The Nyamwezi were great traders in the long distance trade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why Christian missionaries built mission stations on hills: ____. A: For security. Hills were safe places from which enemies could be seen from far.
chunks.source: Hills were safe places from which enemies could be seen from far.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Mention the first political party in Uganda: ____. A: Uganda National Congress (UNC). The UNC, formed by I.K. Musaazi, was Uganda's first party.
chunks.source: The UNC, formed by I.K. Musaazi, was Uganda's first party.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How was the work of LegCo similar to that of Parliament of Uganda today? ____. A: Both make laws. LEGCo made laws in colonial times, as Parliament does today.
chunks.source: LEGCo made laws in colonial times, as Parliament does today.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give the main reason for the calling of the Berlin Conference of 1884-1885: ____. A: To partition Africa peacefully. European powers wanted to share Africa without fighting each other.
chunks.source: European powers wanted to share Africa without fighting each other.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State any two European countries that attended the Berlin Conference of 1884-1885: ____. A: Britain and Germany. Many European powers, including Britain, Germany, France and Portugal, attended.
chunks.source: Many European powers, including Britain, Germany, France and Portugal, attended.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why didn't African leaders attend the 1884-1885 Berlin Conference? ____. A: They were not invited. Europeans did not invite or recognize African leaders.
chunks.source: Europeans did not invite or recognize African leaders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: In which East African country was the Maji Maji rebellion fought? ____. A: Tanzania. The Maji Maji rebellion was fought in Tanganyika against German rule.
chunks.source: The Maji Maji rebellion was fought in Tanganyika against German rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give any two factors which forced the people of Tanzania to demand for their freedom: ____. A: Forced labour and heavy taxes. Germans forced Africans to work and taxed them heavily.
chunks.source: Germans forced Africans to work and taxed them heavily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why was African resistance towards colonial rule defeated? ____. A: Africans had inferior weapons. Europeans had guns while Africans had spears and arrows.
chunks.source: Europeans had guns while Africans had spears and arrows.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two factors that influence population distribution in East Africa: ____. A: Climate and soil fertility. People settle where the climate is good, soils are fertile and jobs exist.
chunks.source: People settle where the climate is good, soils are fertile and jobs exist.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one effect of immigration to Kampala city: ____. A: Overcrowding. Many people moving into Kampala make it crowded and strain services.
chunks.source: Many people moving into Kampala make it crowded and strain services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why citizens should know their rights: ____. A: To protect themselves from abuse. People who know their rights can defend themselves when mistreated.
chunks.source: People who know their rights can defend themselves when mistreated.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write in full the ruling political party in Uganda: ____. A: National Resistance Movement (NRM). The NRM is the party currently ruling Uganda.
chunks.source: The NRM is the party currently ruling Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one challenge the government may face in providing social services to its people: ____. A: Limited funds. The government may not have enough money to build schools and hospitals for everyone.
chunks.source: The government may not have enough money to build schools and hospitals for everyone.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can the Uganda police help to reduce crime in our community today? ____. A: By arresting criminals. Police patrol and arrest law-breakers, which scares away criminals.
chunks.source: Police patrol and arrest law-breakers, which scares away criminals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one problem of high population density in an area: ____. A: Congestion. Too many people in a small area leads to crowding and land shortage.
chunks.source: Too many people in a small area leads to crowding and land shortage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one role of the Electoral Commission in a democratic state: ____. A: To organize and conduct elections. The Electoral Commission registers voters and runs elections.
chunks.source: The Electoral Commission registers voters and runs elections.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Aggrey is a Ugandan boy whose grandfather was Tanzanian. In which way did he become a citizen of Tanzania? ____. A: By descent. A person can become a citizen through a parent or grandparent from that country.
chunks.source: A person can become a citizen through a parent or grandparent from that country.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Kaberamaido district has 3600 people and covers 40 square kilometres. Find its population density: ____. A: 90 people per square kilometre. Population density equals total people divided by area: 3600 divided by 40 equals 90.
chunks.source: Population density equals total people divided by area: 3600 divided by 40 equals 90.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one disadvantage of high population density: ____. A: Congestion and land shortage. Too many people in a small area causes crowding.
chunks.source: Too many people in a small area causes crowding.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can the government help to control rapid population growth in a country? ____. A: By promoting family planning. Teaching people to have fewer children slows population growth.
chunks.source: Teaching people to have fewer children slows population growth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two social service providers found in Mulago hospital: ____. A: Doctors and nurses. Doctors treat patients and nurses care for them.
chunks.source: Doctors treat patients and nurses care for them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of leaders that we get through elections: ____. A: Elected leaders. Leaders chosen by voting are called elected leaders.
chunks.source: Leaders chosen by voting are called elected leaders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is democracy exercised in a school community? ____. A: Through electing prefects and leaders. Pupils vote for their leaders, which is democracy in school.
chunks.source: Pupils vote for their leaders, which is democracy in school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does corruption affect the development of a country? ____. A: It slows development. Corrupt officials steal money meant for roads, schools and hospitals.
chunks.source: Corrupt officials steal money meant for roads, schools and hospitals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one disadvantage of smuggling in a country like Uganda: ____. A: The government loses tax revenue. Smuggled goods pay no tax, so the government gets less money.
chunks.source: Smuggled goods pay no tax, so the government gets less money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is child abuse? ____. A: The mistreatment of children. Beating, overworking or neglecting children is child abuse.
chunks.source: Beating, overworking or neglecting children is child abuse.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one form of child abuse: ____. A: Beating. Common forms of child abuse include beating, child labour and neglect.
chunks.source: Common forms of child abuse include beating, child labour and neglect.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are by-laws? ____. A: Laws made by local councils. Local councils make by-laws to govern their areas.
chunks.source: Local councils make by-laws to govern their areas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who makes the by-laws? ____. A: Local councils. Elected local council leaders make by-laws.
chunks.source: Elected local council leaders make by-laws.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one disadvantage of a high population to a country like Uganda: ____. A: It strains social services. Many people share few schools, hospitals and little land.
chunks.source: Many people share few schools, hospitals and little land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is 8th March celebrated worldwide every year? ____. A: It is International Women's Day. The world honours the achievements of women on 8th March.
chunks.source: The world honours the achievements of women on 8th March.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the democratic leader elected in a school: ____. A: The head prefect. Pupils elect the head prefect to lead them.
chunks.source: Pupils elect the head prefect to lead them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one responsibility of a child at home: ____. A: Helping with housework. Children should help at home and obey their parents.
chunks.source: Children should help at home and obey their parents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down any two causes of child abuse: ____. A: Poverty and alcoholism. Poor, drunk or quarrelling parents may abuse their children.
chunks.source: Poor, drunk or quarrelling parents may abuse their children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the official at the district in charge of children's rights: ____. A: The District Probation Officer. This officer protects the rights of children in the district.
chunks.source: This officer protects the rights of children in the district.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one duty of the Uganda Revenue Authority (URA): ____. A: To collect taxes. URA collects taxes on behalf of the government.
chunks.source: URA collects taxes on behalf of the government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one reason why some Ugandans don't want to pay taxes: ____. A: Taxes are too high. Some people feel taxes are high or the money is misused.
chunks.source: Some people feel taxes are high or the money is misused.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which ministry is in charge of the activities of the Uganda Revenue Authority? ____. A: The Ministry of Finance. URA works under the Ministry of Finance.
chunks.source: URA works under the Ministry of Finance.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two types of budget: ____. A: Surplus budget and deficit budget. A surplus budget has income more than spending; a deficit budget has spending more than income.
chunks.source: A surplus budget has income more than spending; a deficit budget has spending more than income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one indicator of democracy in East African countries: ____. A: Holding free and fair elections. Regular elections show that people choose their leaders.
chunks.source: Regular elections show that people choose their leaders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a social activity: ____. A: Football. People play, dance and celebrate together in social activities.
chunks.source: People play, dance and celebrate together in social activities.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The table shows three houses: Ephesians (8000 sq km, 10 million people), Galatians (120000 sq km, 8 million people), Romans (24000 sq km, 12 million people). Which house has the biggest population? ____. A: Romans. Romans has 12 million people, more than the others.
chunks.source: Romans has 12 million people, more than the others.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same table, what is the size of house Romans? ____. A: 24000 square kilometres. The table shows Romans covers 24,000 square kilometres.
chunks.source: The table shows Romans covers 24,000 square kilometres.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same table, which house has the least population density? ____. A: Galatians. Galatians has the lowest density of 66 people per square kilometre.
chunks.source: Galatians has the lowest density of 66 people per square kilometre.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same table, calculate the population density of Galatians: ____. A: 67 people per square kilometre. Density equals people divided by area: 8,000,000 divided by 120,000 is about 67.
chunks.source: Density equals people divided by area: 8,000,000 divided by 120,000 is about 67.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The three arms of government are Legislature, Executive and Judiciary. In which arm of government would you place lawyers? ____. A: The Judiciary. Lawyers work in courts, which are part of the Judiciary.
chunks.source: Lawyers work in courts, which are part of the Judiciary.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the main duty of the Legislature arm? ____. A: To make laws. Parliament, the Legislature, makes the country's laws.
chunks.source: Parliament, the Legislature, makes the country's laws.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one group of people under the Executive arm of government: ____. A: Ministers. The President and ministers form the Executive.
chunks.source: The President and ministers form the Executive.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a Bill as used in Parliament? ____. A: A proposed law. A Bill is a suggestion for a new law discussed in Parliament.
chunks.source: A Bill is a suggestion for a new law discussed in Parliament.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one river which flows into Lake Victoria: River Kagera_. A: True. River Kagera is the largest river that flows into Lake Victoria.
chunks.source: River Kagera is the largest river that flows into Lake Victoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The table shows monthly rainfall of 80mm to 230mm and temperatures of 24 to 26 degrees Celsius all year. What type of climate is shown above? Equatorial climate_. A: True. Temperatures are high and fairly uniform all year, with rainfall in every month.
chunks.source: Temperatures are high and fairly uniform all year, with rainfall in every month.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same climatic table, which activity can be done by farmers in the month of January? Harvesting_. A: True. January receives little rain, so farmers harvest and dry their crops.
chunks.source: January receives little rain, so farmers harvest and dry their crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one element of weather which makes people sweat: High temperature (heat)_. A: True. When the temperature is high, the body sweats to cool down.
chunks.source: When the temperature is high, the body sweats to cool down.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two problems facing the fishing industry in East Africa: Overfishing and water pollution_. A: True. Catching too many fish reduces stocks, and pollution kills fish.
chunks.source: Catching too many fish reduces stocks, and pollution kills fish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two ways of preserving fish: Smoking and sun drying_. A: True. Removing water from fish by smoking, drying or salting stops it from rotting.
chunks.source: Removing water from fish by smoking, drying or salting stops it from rotting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two major resources found in East Africa: Minerals and forests_. A: True. East Africa is rich in minerals, forests, water bodies and wildlife.
chunks.source: East Africa is rich in minerals, forests, water bodies and wildlife.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the stage of a river that is suitable for the construction of electric dams: The young stage_. A: True. Waterfalls, which provide falling water for power, occur in the young stage of a river.
chunks.source: Waterfalls, which provide falling water for power, occur in the young stage of a river.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do the people of Kabale adapt to the cool climatic conditions? By wearing heavy warm clothes_. A: True. Kabale is cold, so people wear warm clothes and build warm houses.
chunks.source: Kabale is cold, so people wear warm clothes and build warm houses.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are the Turkana and the Karimojong similar in terms of their activities? Both practise pastoralism_. A: True. The Turkana of Kenya and the Karimojong of Uganda are both cattle keepers.
chunks.source: The Turkana of Kenya and the Karimojong of Uganda are both cattle keepers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two human activities that have led to the destruction of the environment: Deforestation and bush burning_. A: True. Cutting down trees and burning bushes destroy the environment.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees and burning bushes destroy the environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the largest climatic zone of Uganda: The tropical climatic zone_. A: True. Most of Uganda has a tropical climate with wet and dry seasons.
chunks.source: Most of Uganda has a tropical climate with wet and dry seasons.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one human activity that can destroy our environment: Deforestation_. A: True. Cutting down trees destroys forests and animal homes.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees destroys forests and animal homes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention the major cash crop that was introduced by the Arabs along the coast of East Africa: Cloves_. A: True. Arabs introduced clove growing, especially in Zanzibar.
chunks.source: Arabs introduced clove growing, especially in Zanzibar.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one weather instrument that can be kept in the Stevenson screen: A thermometer_. A: True. Maximum and minimum thermometers are kept in the Stevenson screen.
chunks.source: Maximum and minimum thermometers are kept in the Stevenson screen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify one problem that is faced by people who live around hilly and mountainous areas: Soil erosion_. A: True. Steep slopes make soil wash away easily.
chunks.source: Steep slopes make soil wash away easily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the physical feature that crosses at least five East African countries: The Rift Valley_. A: True. The Rift Valley runs through many East African countries.
chunks.source: The Rift Valley runs through many East African countries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason for controlling soil erosion in mountainous areas: To keep the soil fertile_. A: True. Erosion washes away the fertile top soil needed by crops.
chunks.source: Erosion washes away the fertile top soil needed by crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one disadvantage of using traditional methods of fishing: They catch few fish_. A: True. Hooks and baskets catch less fish than modern nets.
chunks.source: Hooks and baskets catch less fish than modern nets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one importance of planting grass in the school compound: It controls soil erosion_. A: True. Grass holds the soil and makes the compound beautiful.
chunks.source: Grass holds the soil and makes the compound beautiful.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the biggest water mass that neighbours East Africa in the east: The Indian Ocean_. A: True. The Indian Ocean lies to the east of East Africa.
chunks.source: The Indian Ocean lies to the east of East Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one tributary of the River Nile in Uganda: River Achwa_. A: True. The Achwa joins the Nile in northern Uganda.
chunks.source: The Achwa joins the Nile in northern Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one factor that can influence the climate of an area: Altitude_. A: True. High places are cooler; areas near the equator are hotter.
chunks.source: High places are cooler; areas near the equator are hotter.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one problem that is faced by farmers in Uganda today: Pests and diseases_. A: True. Pests destroy crops and little rain causes poor harvests.
chunks.source: Pests destroy crops and little rain causes poor harvests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two problems that are faced by the tourism industry in our country: Poaching and poor roads_. A: True. Killing of wild animals and bad roads discourage tourists.
chunks.source: Killing of wild animals and bad roads discourage tourists.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any invisible export of Uganda to Kenya and Rwanda: Tourism_. A: True. Tourists from Kenya and Rwanda spend money in Uganda without carrying goods.
chunks.source: Tourists from Kenya and Rwanda spend money in Uganda without carrying goods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the major occupation of the Turkana people in Kenya? Pastoralism_. A: True. The Turkana keep cattle, goats and sheep in the dry lands of Kenya.
chunks.source: The Turkana keep cattle, goats and sheep in the dry lands of Kenya.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Apart from human activity, give any one other factor that determines the vegetation of an area: Climate_. A: True. The amount of rainfall decides what plants grow in an area.
chunks.source: The amount of rainfall decides what plants grow in an area.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is soil erosion controlled in Kabale? By terracing_. A: True. Farmers in Kabale make terraces across hills to slow running water.
chunks.source: Farmers in Kabale make terraces across hills to slow running water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why Mountain Rwenzori is snow capped throughout the year: Because of its high altitude_. A: True. Very high mountains are cold enough for snow all year.
chunks.source: Very high mountains are cold enough for snow all year.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one characteristic of Rift Valley lakes: They are long and narrow_. A: True. Rift Valley lakes like Albert and Tanganyika are long, narrow and deep.
chunks.source: Rift Valley lakes like Albert and Tanganyika are long, narrow and deep.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the water body that joins Lake George to Lake Edward: The Kazinga Channel_. A: True. The Kazinga Channel connects the two lakes.
chunks.source: The Kazinga Channel connects the two lakes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is Hima similar to Tororo in terms of Uganda's economic development? Both have cement factories_. A: True. Hima and Tororo both produce cement from limestone.
chunks.source: Hima and Tororo both produce cement from limestone.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one factor that favours the proper growth of Arabica coffee on the slopes of Mountain Elgon: Fertile volcanic soils_. A: True. Volcanic soils on Mt. Elgon are rich and good for coffee.
chunks.source: Volcanic soils on Mt. Elgon are rich and good for coffee.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the main economic activity carried out in the equatorial rain forests: Lumbering_. A: True. People cut timber trees in the rain forests.
chunks.source: People cut timber trees in the rain forests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do trees in equatorial rain forests grow tall? To compete for sunlight_. A: True. Trees grow tall to reach sunlight above the dense canopy.
chunks.source: Trees grow tall to reach sunlight above the dense canopy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two traditional methods of fishing used on Ugandan lakes: Use of baskets and hooks_. A: True. Fishermen traditionally used baskets, hooks and spears.
chunks.source: Fishermen traditionally used baskets, hooks and spears.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one problem facing the fishing industry in Uganda today: Overfishing_. A: True. Catching too many fish reduces the fish stock.
chunks.source: Catching too many fish reduces the fish stock.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one example of sustainable use of the environment: Afforestation_. A: True. Planting trees replaces those cut down, keeping the environment safe.
chunks.source: Planting trees replaces those cut down, keeping the environment safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does the government benefit from the mining of crude oil? It earns revenue_. A: True. Oil money adds to government income.
chunks.source: Oil money adds to government income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is meant by the term land degradation? The destruction of land_. A: True. Land degradation is the loss of the land's fertility and usefulness.
chunks.source: Land degradation is the loss of the land's fertility and usefulness.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is the government of Uganda encouraging people to grow a lot of non-traditional cash crops? To earn more foreign exchange_. A: True. New cash crops like flowers bring more export money.
chunks.source: New cash crops like flowers bring more export money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being cloudy or windy, give any one other change of weather: Rainy_. A: True. Weather can change to rainy or sunny.
chunks.source: Weather can change to rainy or sunny.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one of the reasons why tourists should be given game rangers every time they visit a game park: For protection_. A: True. Rangers protect tourists from wild animals.
chunks.source: Rangers protect tourists from wild animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention the major tourist attraction found in Bwindi and Mgahinga national parks: Mountain gorillas_. A: True. Tourists visit Bwindi and Mgahinga to see mountain gorillas.
chunks.source: Tourists visit Bwindi and Mgahinga to see mountain gorillas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is environment? Our surroundings_. A: True. The environment includes air, water, soil, plants, animals and buildings around us.
chunks.source: The environment includes air, water, soil, plants, animals and buildings around us.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention two types of environment you know: Natural environment and man-made environment_. A: True. Forests and lakes are natural; roads and buildings are man-made.
chunks.source: Forests and lakes are natural; roads and buildings are man-made.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Apart from water, write any other item transported using pipelines: Crude oil (petroleum)_. A: True. Pipelines also carry petroleum products and natural gas.
chunks.source: Pipelines also carry petroleum products and natural gas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one mobile phone company operating in Uganda: MTN Uganda_. A: True. MTN and Airtel are mobile phone companies operating in Uganda.
chunks.source: MTN and Airtel are mobile phone companies operating in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State two reasons why there are many road accidents in Uganda today: Over speeding and drunk driving_. A: True. Drivers who speed or drink cause many accidents.
chunks.source: Drivers who speed or drink cause many accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: In which way can road accidents be controlled in Uganda? By enforcing traffic rules_. A: True. Police can punish over speeding and drunk drivers to make roads safer.
chunks.source: Police can punish over speeding and drunk drivers to make roads safer.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What part of the Uganda Coat of Arms represents Uganda's traditional communication? The drum_. A: True. In the past, drums were used to send messages, so the drum appears on the coat of arms.
chunks.source: In the past, drums were used to send messages, so the drum appears on the coat of arms.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Apart from a television, give two other forms of mass media: Radio and newspapers_. A: True. Radio and newspapers also pass information to many people.
chunks.source: Radio and newspapers also pass information to many people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why televisions are not commonly used in rural areas: There is no electricity_. A: True. Most rural homes lack electricity to power television sets.
chunks.source: Most rural homes lack electricity to power television sets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State any one way television stations promote employment opportunities to people: They employ journalists and presenters_. A: True. Television stations give jobs to reporters, presenters and technicians.
chunks.source: Television stations give jobs to reporters, presenters and technicians.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being expensive, give another reason why air transport is not used by many people in Uganda: There are few airports_. A: True. Uganda has few airports, so air transport is not common.
chunks.source: Uganda has few airports, so air transport is not common.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name any one inland port found on Lake Victoria in Kenya: Kisumu_. A: True. Kisumu is a major inland port on Lake Victoria in Kenya.
chunks.source: Kisumu is a major inland port on Lake Victoria in Kenya.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which explorer followed the River Nile from its mouth? John Hanning Speke_. A: True. Speke traced the River Nile and proved that Lake Victoria is its source.
chunks.source: Speke traced the River Nile and proved that Lake Victoria is its source.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which missionary contributed to the economic development of Uganda? Alexander Mackay_. A: True. Mackay taught Africans farming and technical skills like carpentry and printing.
chunks.source: Mackay taught Africans farming and technical skills like carpentry and printing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why were political parties formed in the early 1950s? To demand independence (self-rule)_. A: True. Africans formed parties to unite and demand freedom from colonial rule.
chunks.source: Africans formed parties to unite and demand freedom from colonial rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name the British governor who was responsible for the Kabaka crisis in Buganda in 1953: Sir Andrew Cohen_. A: True. Governor Cohen exiled Kabaka Muteesa II in 1953, causing the crisis.
chunks.source: Governor Cohen exiled Kabaka Muteesa II in 1953, causing the crisis.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How did the 1966 constitution affect kingdoms in Uganda? It abolished the kingdoms_. A: True. The 1966 constitution ended the traditional kingdoms in Uganda.
chunks.source: The 1966 constitution ended the traditional kingdoms in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How was IBEACo useful to Christian missionaries in Uganda? It gave them protection_. A: True. The company provided armed protection to missionaries as they worked.
chunks.source: The company provided armed protection to missionaries as they worked.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who were the founders of Bunyoro Kitara Kingdom? The Bachwezi_. A: True. The Bachwezi founded the Bunyoro Kitara Kingdom.
chunks.source: The Bachwezi founded the Bunyoro Kitara Kingdom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name the African country that tried to colonise Uganda: Egypt_. A: True. Egypt, under the Khedive, tried to extend its rule into Uganda through Equatoria.
chunks.source: Egypt, under the Khedive, tried to extend its rule into Uganda through Equatoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why are the Bachwezi economically remembered in the history of Uganda? They introduced long-horned cattle_. A: True. The Bachwezi brought long-horned cattle which improved livestock keeping.
chunks.source: The Bachwezi brought long-horned cattle which improved livestock keeping.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which European missionary brought a printing press to Uganda? Alexander Mackay_. A: True. Mackay brought the first printing press and taught printing.
chunks.source: Mackay brought the first printing press and taught printing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who was the last king of the Bachwezi? King Wamala_. A: True. Wamala was the last ruler of the Bachwezi before the Luo took over.
chunks.source: Wamala was the last ruler of the Bachwezi before the Luo took over.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who signed the 1900 Buganda Agreement on behalf of Buganda Kingdom? Sir Apollo Kaggwa_. A: True. Kaggwa, a Buganda regent, signed for the kingdom.
chunks.source: Kaggwa, a Buganda regent, signed for the kingdom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who signed the 1900 Buganda Agreement on behalf of the British government? Sir Harry Johnston_. A: True. Johnston signed the agreement for Britain.
chunks.source: Johnston signed the agreement for Britain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which political party was formed by I.K. Musaazi? Uganda National Congress (UNC)_. A: True. Musaazi formed the UNC, Uganda's first political party.
chunks.source: Musaazi formed the UNC, Uganda's first political party.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name any one form of tax that was introduced by the 1900 Buganda Agreement: Hut tax_. A: True. The agreement introduced hut tax and gun tax in Buganda.
chunks.source: The agreement introduced hut tax and gun tax in Buganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name the British official who declared Uganda a British Protectorate: Sir Gerald Portal_. A: True. Portal declared Uganda a British protectorate in 1894.
chunks.source: Portal declared Uganda a British protectorate in 1894.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What attitude did Chief Awich of Payera have towards the British? He resisted the British_. A: True. Chief Awich fought against British colonial rule.
chunks.source: Chief Awich fought against British colonial rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State the tribal group of people that ruled Bunyoro-Kitara after the Bachwezi: The Luo_. A: True. The Luo, led by the Babiito clan, took over from the Bachwezi.
chunks.source: The Luo, led by the Babiito clan, took over from the Bachwezi.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give any evidence to show that the Portuguese were once at the East African coast: Fort Jesus in Mombasa_. A: True. The Portuguese built Fort Jesus and the Vasco da Gama pillar at Malindi.
chunks.source: The Portuguese built Fort Jesus and the Vasco da Gama pillar at Malindi.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give the main reason why IBEACo withdrew from Uganda: It had run bankrupt_. A: True. The company lost money and could not continue administering Uganda.
chunks.source: The company lost money and could not continue administering Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who was the leader of the Maji Maji rebellion in Tanganyika? Kinjeketile Ngwale_. A: True. Kinjeketile led the Maji Maji rebellion against German rule.
chunks.source: Kinjeketile led the Maji Maji rebellion against German rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give any one result of the Maji Maji rebellion: Many Africans were killed_. A: True. The Germans crushed the rebellion and thousands died.
chunks.source: The Germans crushed the rebellion and thousands died.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which political party led Uganda to self rule in 1961? Democratic Party (DP)_. A: True. The DP won the 1961 elections and Ben Kiwanuka became chief minister.
chunks.source: The DP won the 1961 elections and Ben Kiwanuka became chief minister.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who was the founder of the Democratic Party? Ben Kiwanuka_. A: True. Ben Kiwanuka founded the Democratic Party.
chunks.source: Ben Kiwanuka founded the Democratic Party.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who was the leader of U.P.C at the time of independence? Dr. Apollo Milton Obote_. A: True. Obote led UPC and became Uganda's first prime minister.
chunks.source: Obote led UPC and became Uganda's first prime minister.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Write LEGCo in full: Legislative Council_. A: True. LEGCo was the law-making body in colonial Uganda.
chunks.source: LEGCo was the law-making body in colonial Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Apart from making laws, give another reason why LEGCo was formed in Uganda in 1921: To advise the governor_. A: True. LEGCo advised the colonial governor on ruling Uganda.
chunks.source: LEGCo advised the colonial governor on ruling Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which group of foreigners introduced the idea of selling people as slaves? The Arabs_. A: True. Arab traders started the slave trade in East Africa.
chunks.source: Arab traders started the slave trade in East Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Write IBEACo in full: Imperial British East Africa Company_. A: True. IBEACo was the British trading company that ruled Uganda before the protectorate.
chunks.source: IBEACo was the British trading company that ruled Uganda before the protectorate.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How did missionary work improve the lives of Africans? They built schools and hospitals_. A: True. Missionaries provided education and health care.
chunks.source: Missionaries provided education and health care.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How was Germany punished by the League of Nations after World War I? Her colonies were taken away_. A: True. Germany lost all her colonies, which were shared as mandates.
chunks.source: Germany lost all her colonies, which were shared as mandates.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name any one tribe from Uganda that participated in the Long Distance Trade: The Nyamwezi_. A: True. The Nyamwezi were great traders in the long distance trade.
chunks.source: The Nyamwezi were great traders in the long distance trade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why Christian missionaries built mission stations on hills: For security_. A: True. Hills were safe places from which enemies could be seen from far.
chunks.source: Hills were safe places from which enemies could be seen from far.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Mention the first political party in Uganda: Uganda National Congress (UNC)_. A: True. The UNC, formed by I.K. Musaazi, was Uganda's first party.
chunks.source: The UNC, formed by I.K. Musaazi, was Uganda's first party.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: How was the work of LegCo similar to that of Parliament of Uganda today? Both make laws_. A: True. LEGCo made laws in colonial times, as Parliament does today.
chunks.source: LEGCo made laws in colonial times, as Parliament does today.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give the main reason for the calling of the Berlin Conference of 1884-1885: To partition Africa peacefully_. A: True. European powers wanted to share Africa without fighting each other.
chunks.source: European powers wanted to share Africa without fighting each other.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: State any two European countries that attended the Berlin Conference of 1884-1885: Britain and Germany_. A: True. Many European powers, including Britain, Germany, France and Portugal, attended.
chunks.source: Many European powers, including Britain, Germany, France and Portugal, attended.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why didn't African leaders attend the 1884-1885 Berlin Conference? They were not invited_. A: True. Europeans did not invite or recognize African leaders.
chunks.source: Europeans did not invite or recognize African leaders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: In which East African country was the Maji Maji rebellion fought? Tanzania_. A: True. The Maji Maji rebellion was fought in Tanganyika against German rule.
chunks.source: The Maji Maji rebellion was fought in Tanganyika against German rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Give any two factors which forced the people of Tanzania to demand for their freedom: Forced labour and heavy taxes_. A: True. Germans forced Africans to work and taxed them heavily.
chunks.source: Germans forced Africans to work and taxed them heavily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why was African resistance towards colonial rule defeated? Africans had inferior weapons_. A: True. Europeans had guns while Africans had spears and arrows.
chunks.source: Europeans had guns while Africans had spears and arrows.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two factors that influence population distribution in East Africa: Climate and soil fertility_. A: True. People settle where the climate is good, soils are fertile and jobs exist.
chunks.source: People settle where the climate is good, soils are fertile and jobs exist.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one effect of immigration to Kampala city: Overcrowding_. A: True. Many people moving into Kampala make it crowded and strain services.
chunks.source: Many people moving into Kampala make it crowded and strain services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why citizens should know their rights: To protect themselves from abuse_. A: True. People who know their rights can defend themselves when mistreated.
chunks.source: People who know their rights can defend themselves when mistreated.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write in full the ruling political party in Uganda: National Resistance Movement (NRM)_. A: True. The NRM is the party currently ruling Uganda.
chunks.source: The NRM is the party currently ruling Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one challenge the government may face in providing social services to its people: Limited funds_. A: True. The government may not have enough money to build schools and hospitals for everyone.
chunks.source: The government may not have enough money to build schools and hospitals for everyone.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can the Uganda police help to reduce crime in our community today? By arresting criminals_. A: True. Police patrol and arrest law-breakers, which scares away criminals.
chunks.source: Police patrol and arrest law-breakers, which scares away criminals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one problem of high population density in an area: Congestion_. A: True. Too many people in a small area leads to crowding and land shortage.
chunks.source: Too many people in a small area leads to crowding and land shortage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one role of the Electoral Commission in a democratic state: To organize and conduct elections_. A: True. The Electoral Commission registers voters and runs elections.
chunks.source: The Electoral Commission registers voters and runs elections.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Aggrey is a Ugandan boy whose grandfather was Tanzanian. In which way did he become a citizen of Tanzania? By descent_. A: True. A person can become a citizen through a parent or grandparent from that country.
chunks.source: A person can become a citizen through a parent or grandparent from that country.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Kaberamaido district has 3600 people and covers 40 square kilometres. Find its population density: 90 people per square kilometre_. A: True. Population density equals total people divided by area: 3600 divided by 40 equals 90.
chunks.source: Population density equals total people divided by area: 3600 divided by 40 equals 90.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one disadvantage of high population density: Congestion and land shortage_. A: True. Too many people in a small area causes crowding.
chunks.source: Too many people in a small area causes crowding.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can the government help to control rapid population growth in a country? By promoting family planning_. A: True. Teaching people to have fewer children slows population growth.
chunks.source: Teaching people to have fewer children slows population growth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two social service providers found in Mulago hospital: Doctors and nurses_. A: True. Doctors treat patients and nurses care for them.
chunks.source: Doctors treat patients and nurses care for them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of leaders that we get through elections: Elected leaders_. A: True. Leaders chosen by voting are called elected leaders.
chunks.source: Leaders chosen by voting are called elected leaders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is democracy exercised in a school community? Through electing prefects and leaders_. A: True. Pupils vote for their leaders, which is democracy in school.
chunks.source: Pupils vote for their leaders, which is democracy in school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does corruption affect the development of a country? It slows development_. A: True. Corrupt officials steal money meant for roads, schools and hospitals.
chunks.source: Corrupt officials steal money meant for roads, schools and hospitals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one disadvantage of smuggling in a country like Uganda: The government loses tax revenue_. A: True. Smuggled goods pay no tax, so the government gets less money.
chunks.source: Smuggled goods pay no tax, so the government gets less money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is child abuse? The mistreatment of children_. A: True. Beating, overworking or neglecting children is child abuse.
chunks.source: Beating, overworking or neglecting children is child abuse.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one form of child abuse: Beating_. A: True. Common forms of child abuse include beating, child labour and neglect.
chunks.source: Common forms of child abuse include beating, child labour and neglect.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are by-laws? Laws made by local councils_. A: True. Local councils make by-laws to govern their areas.
chunks.source: Local councils make by-laws to govern their areas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who makes the by-laws? Local councils_. A: True. Elected local council leaders make by-laws.
chunks.source: Elected local council leaders make by-laws.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one disadvantage of a high population to a country like Uganda: It strains social services_. A: True. Many people share few schools, hospitals and little land.
chunks.source: Many people share few schools, hospitals and little land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is 8th March celebrated worldwide every year? It is International Women's Day_. A: True. The world honours the achievements of women on 8th March.
chunks.source: The world honours the achievements of women on 8th March.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the democratic leader elected in a school: The head prefect_. A: True. Pupils elect the head prefect to lead them.
chunks.source: Pupils elect the head prefect to lead them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one responsibility of a child at home: Helping with housework_. A: True. Children should help at home and obey their parents.
chunks.source: Children should help at home and obey their parents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down any two causes of child abuse: Poverty and alcoholism_. A: True. Poor, drunk or quarrelling parents may abuse their children.
chunks.source: Poor, drunk or quarrelling parents may abuse their children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the official at the district in charge of children's rights: The District Probation Officer_. A: True. This officer protects the rights of children in the district.
chunks.source: This officer protects the rights of children in the district.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one duty of the Uganda Revenue Authority (URA): To collect taxes_. A: True. URA collects taxes on behalf of the government.
chunks.source: URA collects taxes on behalf of the government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one reason why some Ugandans don't want to pay taxes: Taxes are too high_. A: True. Some people feel taxes are high or the money is misused.
chunks.source: Some people feel taxes are high or the money is misused.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which ministry is in charge of the activities of the Uganda Revenue Authority? The Ministry of Finance_. A: True. URA works under the Ministry of Finance.
chunks.source: URA works under the Ministry of Finance.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two types of budget: Surplus budget and deficit budget_. A: True. A surplus budget has income more than spending; a deficit budget has spending more than income.
chunks.source: A surplus budget has income more than spending; a deficit budget has spending more than income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one indicator of democracy in East African countries: Holding free and fair elections_. A: True. Regular elections show that people choose their leaders.
chunks.source: Regular elections show that people choose their leaders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a social activity: Football_. A: True. People play, dance and celebrate together in social activities.
chunks.source: People play, dance and celebrate together in social activities.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The table shows three houses: Ephesians (8000 sq km, 10 million people), Galatians (120000 sq km, 8 million people), Romans (24000 sq km, 12 million people). Which house has the biggest population? Romans_. A: True. Romans has 12 million people, more than the others.
chunks.source: Romans has 12 million people, more than the others.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same table, what is the size of house Romans? 24000 square kilometres_. A: True. The table shows Romans covers 24,000 square kilometres.
chunks.source: The table shows Romans covers 24,000 square kilometres.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same table, which house has the least population density? Galatians_. A: True. Galatians has the lowest density of 66 people per square kilometre.
chunks.source: Galatians has the lowest density of 66 people per square kilometre.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same table, calculate the population density of Galatians: 67 people per square kilometre_. A: True. Density equals people divided by area: 8,000,000 divided by 120,000 is about 67.
chunks.source: Density equals people divided by area: 8,000,000 divided by 120,000 is about 67.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The three arms of government are Legislature, Executive and Judiciary. In which arm of government would you place lawyers? The Judiciary_. A: True. Lawyers work in courts, which are part of the Judiciary.
chunks.source: Lawyers work in courts, which are part of the Judiciary.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the main duty of the Legislature arm? To make laws_. A: True. Parliament, the Legislature, makes the country's laws.
chunks.source: Parliament, the Legislature, makes the country's laws.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one group of people under the Executive arm of government: Ministers_. A: True. The President and ministers form the Executive.
chunks.source: The President and ministers form the Executive.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a Bill as used in Parliament? A proposed law_. A: True. A Bill is a suggestion for a new law discussed in Parliament.
chunks.source: A Bill is a suggestion for a new law discussed in Parliament.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one river which flows into Lake Victoria: Equatorial climate_. A: False. River Kagera is the largest river that flows into Lake Victoria.
chunks.source: River Kagera is the largest river that flows into Lake Victoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The table shows monthly rainfall of 80mm to 230mm and temperatures of 24 to 26 degrees Celsius all year. What type of climate is shown above? River Kagera_. A: False. Temperatures are high and fairly uniform all year, with rainfall in every month.
chunks.source: Temperatures are high and fairly uniform all year, with rainfall in every month.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Using the same climatic table, which activity can be done by farmers in the month of January? River Kagera_. A: False. January receives little rain, so farmers harvest and dry their crops.
chunks.source: January receives little rain, so farmers harvest and dry their crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write one element of weather which makes people sweat: River Kagera_. A: False. When the temperature is high, the body sweats to cool down.
chunks.source: When the temperature is high, the body sweats to cool down.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any two problems facing the fishing industry in East Africa: River Kagera_. A: False. Catching too many fish reduces stocks, and pollution kills fish.
chunks.source: Catching too many fish reduces stocks, and pollution kills fish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two ways of preserving fish: River Kagera_. A: False. Removing water from fish by smoking, drying or salting stops it from rotting.
chunks.source: Removing water from fish by smoking, drying or salting stops it from rotting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two major resources found in East Africa: River Kagera_. A: False. East Africa is rich in minerals, forests, water bodies and wildlife.
chunks.source: East Africa is rich in minerals, forests, water bodies and wildlife.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the stage of a river that is suitable for the construction of electric dams: River Kagera_. A: False. Waterfalls, which provide falling water for power, occur in the young stage of a river.
chunks.source: Waterfalls, which provide falling water for power, occur in the young stage of a river.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do the people of Kabale adapt to the cool climatic conditions? River Kagera_. A: False. Kabale is cold, so people wear warm clothes and build warm houses.
chunks.source: Kabale is cold, so people wear warm clothes and build warm houses.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are the Turkana and the Karimojong similar in terms of their activities? River Kagera_. A: False. The Turkana of Kenya and the Karimojong of Uganda are both cattle keepers.
chunks.source: The Turkana of Kenya and the Karimojong of Uganda are both cattle keepers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two human activities that have led to the destruction of the environment: River Kagera_. A: False. Cutting down trees and burning bushes destroy the environment.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees and burning bushes destroy the environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the largest climatic zone of Uganda: River Kagera_. A: False. Most of Uganda has a tropical climate with wet and dry seasons.
chunks.source: Most of Uganda has a tropical climate with wet and dry seasons.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one human activity that can destroy our environment: River Kagera_. A: False. Cutting down trees destroys forests and animal homes.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees destroys forests and animal homes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention the major cash crop that was introduced by the Arabs along the coast of East Africa: River Kagera_. A: False. Arabs introduced clove growing, especially in Zanzibar.
chunks.source: Arabs introduced clove growing, especially in Zanzibar.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one weather instrument that can be kept in the Stevenson screen: River Kagera_. A: False. Maximum and minimum thermometers are kept in the Stevenson screen.
chunks.source: Maximum and minimum thermometers are kept in the Stevenson screen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify one problem that is faced by people who live around hilly and mountainous areas: River Kagera_. A: False. Steep slopes make soil wash away easily.
chunks.source: Steep slopes make soil wash away easily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the physical feature that crosses at least five East African countries: River Kagera_. A: False. The Rift Valley runs through many East African countries.
chunks.source: The Rift Valley runs through many East African countries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason for controlling soil erosion in mountainous areas: River Kagera_. A: False. Erosion washes away the fertile top soil needed by crops.
chunks.source: Erosion washes away the fertile top soil needed by crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one disadvantage of using traditional methods of fishing: River Kagera_. A: False. Hooks and baskets catch less fish than modern nets.
chunks.source: Hooks and baskets catch less fish than modern nets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State one importance of planting grass in the school compound: River Kagera_. A: False. Grass holds the soil and makes the compound beautiful.
chunks.source: Grass holds the soil and makes the compound beautiful.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the biggest water mass that neighbours East Africa in the east: River Kagera_. A: False. The Indian Ocean lies to the east of East Africa.
chunks.source: The Indian Ocean lies to the east of East Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one tributary of the River Nile in Uganda: River Kagera_. A: False. The Achwa joins the Nile in northern Uganda.
chunks.source: The Achwa joins the Nile in northern Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one factor that can influence the climate of an area: River Kagera_. A: False. High places are cooler; areas near the equator are hotter.
chunks.source: High places are cooler; areas near the equator are hotter.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Mention one problem that is faced by farmers in Uganda today: River Kagera_. A: False. Pests destroy crops and little rain causes poor harvests.
chunks.source: Pests destroy crops and little rain causes poor harvests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two problems that are faced by the tourism industry in our country: River Kagera_. A: False. Killing of wild animals and bad roads discourage tourists.
chunks.source: Killing of wild animals and bad roads discourage tourists.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Identify any invisible export of Uganda to Kenya and Rwanda: River Kagera_. A: False. Tourists from Kenya and Rwanda spend money in Uganda without carrying goods.
chunks.source: Tourists from Kenya and Rwanda spend money in Uganda without carrying goods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the major occupation of the Turkana people in Kenya? River Kagera_. A: False. The Turkana keep cattle, goats and sheep in the dry lands of Kenya.
chunks.source: The Turkana keep cattle, goats and sheep in the dry lands of Kenya.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Apart from human activity, give any one other factor that determines the vegetation of an area: River Kagera_. A: False. The amount of rainfall decides what plants grow in an area.
chunks.source: The amount of rainfall decides what plants grow in an area.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is soil erosion controlled in Kabale? River Kagera_. A: False. Farmers in Kabale make terraces across hills to slow running water.
chunks.source: Farmers in Kabale make terraces across hills to slow running water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why Mountain Rwenzori is snow capped throughout the year: River Kagera_. A: False. Very high mountains are cold enough for snow all year.
chunks.source: Very high mountains are cold enough for snow all year.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one characteristic of Rift Valley lakes: River Kagera_. A: False. Rift Valley lakes like Albert and Tanganyika are long, narrow and deep.
chunks.source: Rift Valley lakes like Albert and Tanganyika are long, narrow and deep.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the water body that joins Lake George to Lake Edward: River Kagera_. A: False. The Kazinga Channel connects the two lakes.
chunks.source: The Kazinga Channel connects the two lakes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is Hima similar to Tororo in terms of Uganda's economic development? River Kagera_. A: False. Hima and Tororo both produce cement from limestone.
chunks.source: Hima and Tororo both produce cement from limestone.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any one factor that favours the proper growth of Arabica coffee on the slopes of Mountain Elgon: River Kagera_. A: False. Volcanic soils on Mt. Elgon are rich and good for coffee.
chunks.source: Volcanic soils on Mt. Elgon are rich and good for coffee.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give the main economic activity carried out in the equatorial rain forests: River Kagera_. A: False. People cut timber trees in the rain forests.
chunks.source: People cut timber trees in the rain forests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do trees in equatorial rain forests grow tall? River Kagera_. A: False. Trees grow tall to reach sunlight above the dense canopy.
chunks.source: Trees grow tall to reach sunlight above the dense canopy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give any two traditional methods of fishing used on Ugandan lakes: River Kagera_. A: False. Fishermen traditionally used baskets, hooks and spears.
chunks.source: Fishermen traditionally used baskets, hooks and spears.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: State any one problem facing the fishing industry in Uganda today: River Kagera_. A: False. Catching too many fish reduces the fish stock.
chunks.source: Catching too many fish reduces the fish stock.

chunks.subject: Social
