chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'the ceremony where two people get married'? A: wedding. the ceremony where two people get married — that is 'wedding'.
chunks.source: the ceremony where two people get married — that is 'wedding'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'decided beforehand; not by accident'? A: planned. decided beforehand; not by accident — that is 'planned'.
chunks.source: decided beforehand; not by accident — that is 'planned'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'wedding' mean? A: the ceremony where two people get married. 'wedding' means the ceremony where two people get married.
chunks.source: 'wedding' means the ceremony where two people get married.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Our ___ totem is the lion; we do not eat lion meat. A: clan. The word is 'clan': Our clan totem is the lion; we do not eat lion meat.
chunks.source: The word is 'clan': Our clan totem is the lion; we do not eat lion meat.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'groom' mean? A: the man getting married. 'groom' means the man getting married.
chunks.source: 'groom' means the man getting married.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: My ___ drives a boda boda in Kampala. A: uncle. The word is 'uncle': My uncle drives a boda boda in Kampala.
chunks.source: The word is 'uncle': My uncle drives a boda boda in Kampala.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'a group of families with a common ancestor'? A: clan. a group of families with a common ancestor — that is 'clan'.
chunks.source: a group of families with a common ancestor — that is 'clan'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: My ___ sings in the church choir. A: niece. The word is 'niece': My niece sings in the church choir.
chunks.source: The word is 'niece': My niece sings in the church choir.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: ___ makes a family stay together in hard times. A: love. The word is 'love': Love makes a family stay together in hard times.
chunks.source: The word is 'love': Love makes a family stay together in hard times.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: My ___ helps with homework. A: step sister. The word is 'step sister': My step sister helps with homework.
chunks.source: The word is 'step sister': My step sister helps with homework.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: My ___ shares my room. A: step brother. The word is 'step brother': My step brother shares my room.
chunks.source: The word is 'step brother': My step brother shares my room.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'a sister of your father or mother'? A: auntie. a sister of your father or mother — that is 'auntie'.
chunks.source: a sister of your father or mother — that is 'auntie'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: My ___ Peter goes to my school. A: cousin. The word is 'cousin': My cousin Peter goes to my school.
chunks.source: The word is 'cousin': My cousin Peter goes to my school.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'grandparent' mean? A: a parent of your father or mother. 'grandparent' means a parent of your father or mother.
chunks.source: 'grandparent' means a parent of your father or mother.

chunks.subject: Theme

chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: The ___ wore a seatbelt. A: passenger. The word is 'passenger': The passenger wore a seatbelt.
chunks.source: The word is 'passenger': The passenger wore a seatbelt.

chunks.subject: Theme

chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'visible gas from fire used as a sign'? A: smoke. visible gas from fire used as a sign — that is 'smoke'.
chunks.source: visible gas from fire used as a sign — that is 'smoke'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'whistle' mean? A: a small device that makes a sharp sound. 'whistle' means a small device that makes a sharp sound.
chunks.source: 'whistle' means a small device that makes a sharp sound.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: The ___ arrived quickly. A: telegram. The word is 'telegram': The telegram arrived quickly.
chunks.source: The word is 'telegram': The telegram arrived quickly.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'smoke' mean? A: visible gas from fire used as a sign. 'smoke' means visible gas from fire used as a sign.
chunks.source: 'smoke' means visible gas from fire used as a sign.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: A ___ carries fuel from the coast inland. A: pipeline. The word is 'pipeline': A pipeline carries fuel from the coast inland.
chunks.source: The word is 'pipeline': A pipeline carries fuel from the coast inland.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'the movement of vehicles and people on roads'? A: traffic. the movement of vehicles and people on roads — that is 'traffic'.
chunks.source: the movement of vehicles and people on roads — that is 'traffic'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: The ___ blocked the road. A: accident. The word is 'accident': The accident blocked the road.
chunks.source: The word is 'accident': The accident blocked the road.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: The ___ ran to the next village. A: messenger. The word is 'messenger': The messenger ran to the next village.
chunks.source: The word is 'messenger': The messenger ran to the next village.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'a traditional sailing vessel with lateen sails'? A: dhow. a traditional sailing vessel with lateen sails — that is 'dhow'.
chunks.source: a traditional sailing vessel with lateen sails — that is 'dhow'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'the movement of people or goods from one place to another'? A: transport. the movement of people or goods from one place to another — that is 'transport'.
chunks.source: the movement of people or goods from one place to another — that is 'transport'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'messenger' mean? A: a person who carries a message. 'messenger' means a person who carries a message.
chunks.source: 'messenger' means a person who carries a message.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'trumpet' mean? A: a long metal instrument blown for signals. 'trumpet' means a long metal instrument blown for signals.
chunks.source: 'trumpet' means a long metal instrument blown for signals.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'railway' mean? A: tracks for trains to carry passengers and goods. 'railway' means tracks for trains to carry passengers and goods.
chunks.source: 'railway' means tracks for trains to carry passengers and goods.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'a written message sent by post'? A: letter. a written message sent by post — that is 'letter'.
chunks.source: a written message sent by post — that is 'letter'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: Transport and Communication in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'alarm' mean? A: a warning of danger. 'alarm' means a warning of danger.
chunks.source: 'alarm' means a warning of danger.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'the elected head of state in a republic'? A: president. the elected head of state in a republic — that is 'president'.
chunks.source: the elected head of state in a republic — that is 'president'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'journey' mean? A: a long trip from one place to another. 'journey' means a long trip from one place to another.
chunks.source: 'journey' means a long trip from one place to another.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'president' mean? A: the elected head of state in a republic. 'president' means the elected head of state in a republic.
chunks.source: 'president' means the elected head of state in a republic.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Local chiefs organised ___. A: resistance. The word is 'resistance': Local chiefs organised resistance.
chunks.source: The word is 'resistance': Local chiefs organised resistance.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Uganda practices ___ with regular elections. A: democracy. The word is 'democracy': Uganda practices democracy with regular elections.
chunks.source: The word is 'democracy': Uganda practices democracy with regular elections.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'the system of managing a colony'? A: administration. the system of managing a colony — that is 'administration'.
chunks.source: the system of managing a colony — that is 'administration'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Paying taxes is a ___ of citizenship. A: responsibility. The word is 'responsibility': Paying taxes is a responsibility of citizenship.
chunks.source: The word is 'responsibility': Paying taxes is a responsibility of citizenship.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'a system of faith and worship'? A: religion. a system of faith and worship — that is 'religion'.
chunks.source: a system of faith and worship — that is 'religion'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'a country with an elected president'? A: republic. a country with an elected president — that is 'republic'.
chunks.source: a country with an elected president — that is 'republic'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'a drawing that shows where places are'? A: map. a drawing that shows where places are — that is 'map'.
chunks.source: a drawing that shows where places are — that is 'map'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'electoral commission' mean? A: the body that organises elections. 'electoral commission' means the body that organises elections.
chunks.source: 'electoral commission' means the body that organises elections.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: ___ rule began after the explorers. A: colonial. The word is 'colonial': Colonial rule began after the explorers.
chunks.source: The word is 'colonial': Colonial rule began after the explorers.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'the top official representing the colonial power'? A: governor. the top official representing the colonial power — that is 'governor'.
chunks.source: the top official representing the colonial power — that is 'governor'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'responsibility' mean? A: a duty to contribute to society. 'responsibility' means a duty to contribute to society.
chunks.source: 'responsibility' means a duty to contribute to society.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'citizen' mean? A: a legal member of a country. 'citizen' means a legal member of a country.
chunks.source: 'citizen' means a legal member of a country.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'religion' mean? A: a system of faith and worship. 'religion' means a system of faith and worship.
chunks.source: 'religion' means a system of faith and worship.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'citizenship' mean? A: the status of being a citizen. 'citizenship' means the status of being a citizen.
chunks.source: 'citizenship' means the status of being a citizen.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'the right to act without oppression'? A: freedom. the right to act without oppression — that is 'freedom'.
chunks.source: the right to act without oppression — that is 'freedom'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What does 'rebellion' mean? A: an armed uprising against rulers. 'rebellion' means an armed uprising against rulers.
chunks.source: 'rebellion' means an armed uprising against rulers.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.unit: The Road to Independence in East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'relating to a country controlling another territory'? A: colonial. relating to a country controlling another territory — that is 'colonial'.
chunks.source: relating to a country controlling another territory — that is 'colonial'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'pollution' mean? A: harmful substances added to air, water or soil. 'pollution' means harmful substances added to air, water or soil.
chunks.source: 'pollution' means harmful substances added to air, water or soil.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'acting with care for consequences on others and nature'? A: responsible. acting with care for consequences on others and nature — that is 'responsible'.
chunks.source: acting with care for consequences on others and nature — that is 'responsible'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'harmful substances added to air, water or soil'? A: pollution. harmful substances added to air, water or soil — that is 'pollution'.
chunks.source: harmful substances added to air, water or soil — that is 'pollution'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: This ___ must fix the mistakes of the past. A: generation. The word is 'generation': This generation must fix the mistakes of the past.
chunks.source: The word is 'generation': This generation must fix the mistakes of the past.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: We must respect ___ and not pollute the rivers. A: nature. The word is 'nature': We must respect nature and not pollute the rivers.
chunks.source: The word is 'nature': We must respect nature and not pollute the rivers.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'community' mean? A: people living together in one area. 'community' means people living together in one area.
chunks.source: 'community' means people living together in one area.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'disease' mean? A: illness caused by germs or unhealthy conditions. 'disease' means illness caused by germs or unhealthy conditions.
chunks.source: 'disease' means illness caused by germs or unhealthy conditions.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'volunteer' mean? A: person who offers time and effort without pay. 'volunteer' means person who offers time and effort without pay.
chunks.source: 'volunteer' means person who offers time and effort without pay.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Proper ___ pipes keep the borehole water clean. A: sewage. The word is 'sewage': Proper sewage pipes keep the borehole water clean.
chunks.source: The word is 'sewage': Proper sewage pipes keep the borehole water clean.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'energy' mean? A: power used for cooking, lighting and machines. 'energy' means power used for cooking, lighting and machines.
chunks.source: 'energy' means power used for cooking, lighting and machines.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'organised effort to promote a cause'? A: campaign. organised effort to promote a cause — that is 'campaign'.
chunks.source: organised effort to promote a cause — that is 'campaign'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Amina became a ___ for the Saturday clean-up. A: volunteer. The word is 'volunteer': Amina became a volunteer for the Saturday clean-up.
chunks.source: The word is 'volunteer': Amina became a volunteer for the Saturday clean-up.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'the physical world including plants, animals, landscapes'? A: nature. the physical world including plants, animals, landscapes — that is 'nature'.
chunks.source: the physical world including plants, animals, landscapes — that is 'nature'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Gully ___ has cut deep channels across the garden. A: erosion. The word is 'erosion': Gully erosion has cut deep channels across the garden.
chunks.source: The word is 'erosion': Gully erosion has cut deep channels across the garden.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Our ___ gives us food, water and firewood. A: environment. The word is 'environment': Our environment gives us food, water and firewood.
chunks.source: The word is 'environment': Our environment gives us food, water and firewood.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'damage' mean? A: harm that makes something less valuable or useful. 'damage' means harm that makes something less valuable or useful.
chunks.source: 'damage' means harm that makes something less valuable or useful.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'long period with little or no rain'? A: drought. long period with little or no rain — that is 'drought'.
chunks.source: long period with little or no rain — that is 'drought'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'clean' mean? A: free from dirt, waste or germs. 'clean' means free from dirt, waste or germs.
chunks.source: 'clean' means free from dirt, waste or germs.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'solution' mean? A: a way to solve a problem. 'solution' means a way to solve a problem.
chunks.source: 'solution' means a way to solve a problem.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Factory ___ turned the stream water brown and smelly. A: pollution. The word is 'pollution': Factory pollution turned the stream water brown and smelly.
chunks.source: The word is 'pollution': Factory pollution turned the stream water brown and smelly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The schools will break ___ for holidays next week. A: off. 'Break off' means to stop work so as to begin a holiday.
chunks.source: 'Break off' means to stop work so as to begin a holiday.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We shall travel to the village next holidays, ___? A: shan't we. A positive sentence with 'shall' takes the negative tag 'shan't we?'.
chunks.source: A positive sentence with 'shall' takes the negative tag 'shan't we?'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The village ___ Kyangwa was born has developed greatly. A: where. 'Where' is the relative pronoun we use for places.
chunks.source: 'Where' is the relative pronoun we use for places.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I prefer studying in rural schools to ___ ones. A: urban. The opposite of 'rural' is 'urban'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'rural' is 'urban'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They will travel ___ train from Kampala to Kigali. A: by. We use 'by' for means of transport: by train, by bus, by car.
chunks.source: We use 'by' for means of transport: by train, by bus, by car.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My brother will spend his ___ in Durban. (vacate) A: vacation. The noun form of 'vacate' is 'vacation'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'vacate' is 'vacation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: When ___ the timetable for exams going to be out? (be) A: is. 'Timetable' is singular, so we use 'is'.
chunks.source: 'Timetable' is singular, so we use 'is'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Katuutu visited her grandfather ___ last year. (two) A: twice. The adverb form of 'two' is 'twice' (two times).
chunks.source: The adverb form of 'two' is 'twice' (two times).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our teachers are ___ to give us a test. (plan) A: planning. After 'are' we use the -ing form: 'are planning'.
chunks.source: After 'are' we use the -ing form: 'are planning'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Of the three holidays, third term is the ___. (long) A: longest. We use the superlative 'longest' when comparing three or more.
chunks.source: We use the superlative 'longest' when comparing three or more.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The children enjoyed a long holiday during winter. (Give one word for: 'enjoyed a long holiday' ___) A: vacationed. 'To vacation' means to spend a holiday.
chunks.source: 'To vacation' means to spend a holiday.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The second term will start in May. (Give one word for: 'The second term' ___) A: It. 'It' replaces the singular noun phrase 'The second term'.
chunks.source: 'It' replaces the singular noun phrase 'The second term'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Holiday makers should have a clear list of planned activities. (Give one word for: 'a clear list of planned activities' ___) A: itinerary. An 'itinerary' is a planned list of activities for a journey.
chunks.source: An 'itinerary' is a planned list of activities for a journey.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The P.7 pupils will read hard for their P.L.E. (Re-write using: ….going to ___)  A: The P.7 pupils are going to read hard for their P.L.E.. 'Will' changes to 'are going to' for a future plan.
chunks.source: 'Will' changes to 'are going to' for a future plan.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Jane will help her parents during the vacation, wont she? (Re-write and end: …'will she?' ___)  A: Jane will help her parents during the vacation, will she?. The tag must be opposite to the main sentence: the main part is positive, so the tag is 'will she?'.
chunks.source: The tag must be opposite to the main sentence: the main part is positive, so the tag is 'will she?'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The Headteacher said that the candidates had done their examinations the previous day. (Re-write ending: '___ ,' said the Headteacher.) A: "The candidates did their examinations yesterday," said the Headteacher.. In direct speech: 'had done' becomes 'did' and 'the previous day' becomes 'yesterday'.
chunks.source: In direct speech: 'had done' becomes 'did' and 'the previous day' becomes 'yesterday'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The policeman will arrest the wrong doers. (Begin: The wrong doers ___)  A: The wrong doers will be arrested by the policeman.. Active to passive: the object becomes the subject, add 'will be' + past participle.
chunks.source: Active to passive: the object becomes the subject, add 'will be' + past participle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Juliet is admired because of her beauty. (Re-write and end: …beautiful. ___) A: Juliet is admired because she is beautiful.. 'Because of her beauty' can be written as 'because she is beautiful'.
chunks.source: 'Because of her beauty' can be written as 'because she is beautiful'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: There is little water remaining, ___? (Supply a suitable question tag.) A: is there?. 'Little' is negative in meaning, so the tag is positive: 'is there?'.
chunks.source: 'Little' is negative in meaning, so the tag is positive: 'is there?'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The letter was written by the boy. (Begin: The boy ___)  A: The boy wrote the letter.. Passive to active: 'was written' becomes 'wrote', and 'the boy' becomes the subject.
chunks.source: Passive to active: 'was written' becomes 'wrote', and 'the boy' becomes the subject.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The boys play football during the holidays. (Begin: Football ___)  A: Football is played by the boys during the holidays.. Active to passive: the object 'football' becomes the subject.
chunks.source: Active to passive: the object 'football' becomes the subject.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The program is written by the secretary. (Begin: The secretary ___)  A: The secretary writes the program.. Passive to active: 'is written' becomes 'writes'.
chunks.source: Passive to active: 'is written' becomes 'writes'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange the sentences to form a good story about holidays: (a) However, resting does not simply mean being idle or not working at all. (b) They may also include visiting relatives and friends during this period. (c) Since this would be very difficult to fulfil when we are at school. (d) It only means doing activities that help your body and mind relax. (e) That is why we should always have holidays at the end of every term. (f) Why do you think so? (g) Most pupils believe that this period is indeed very good for us. (h) Such activities include camping, swimming and touring important places. (i) I think so because holidays enable us to rest. (j) Every school child needs a holiday. A: Every school child needs a holiday., Most pupils believe that this period is indeed very good for us., Why do you think so?, I think so because holidays enable us to rest., However, resting does not simply mean being idle or not working at all., It only means doing activities that help your body and mind relax., Such activities include camping, swimming and touring important places., They may also include visiting relatives and friends during this period., Since this would be very difficult to fulfil when we are at school., That is why we should always have holidays at the end of every term.. A good story begins with the topic, gives opinions and reasons, then explains and ends with a conclusion.
chunks.source: A good story begins with the topic, gives opinions and reasons, then explains and ends with a conclusion.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What ___ exciting holiday it was! A: an. Before a vowel sound we use 'an': 'an exciting holiday'.
chunks.source: Before a vowel sound we use 'an': 'an exciting holiday'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We ought ___ work hard so as to improve. A: to. 'Ought' is followed by 'to': 'ought to work'.
chunks.source: 'Ought' is followed by 'to': 'ought to work'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Sandra will pass the test, ___, she? A: won't. A positive sentence with 'will' takes the negative tag 'won't she?'.
chunks.source: A positive sentence with 'will' takes the negative tag 'won't she?'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If I had seen him in the holiday, he ___ have given me some money. A: would. In a third conditional: 'If I had seen…, he would have given…'.
chunks.source: In a third conditional: 'If I had seen…, he would have given…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: It was ___ an interesting journey that everybody enjoyed. A: such. The pattern is 'such + a/an + adjective + noun + that…'.
chunks.source: The pattern is 'such + a/an + adjective + noun + that…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Jemba ___ his parents every morning. (greet) A: greets. With 'every morning' (present habit) we use the present simple: 'greets'.
chunks.source: With 'every morning' (present habit) we use the present simple: 'greets'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Hellen was a ___ pupil because of her work. (succeed) A: successful. We need an adjective: the adjective form of 'succeed' is 'successful'.
chunks.source: We need an adjective: the adjective form of 'succeed' is 'successful'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If we ___ our notes, we would have passed the test. (revise) A: had revised. Third conditional: 'If we had revised…, we would have passed…'.
chunks.source: Third conditional: 'If we had revised…, we would have passed…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: All my clothes were ___ during my vacation. (tear) A: torn. The past participle of 'tear' is 'torn': 'were torn'.
chunks.source: The past participle of 'tear' is 'torn': 'were torn'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The lazy boy ___ his uniform last holiday. (dirty) A: dirtied. With 'last holiday' we use the past simple: 'dirtied'.
chunks.source: With 'last holiday' we use the past simple: 'dirtied'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: It is not good to play cards during class hours. (Re-write and begin: Playing ___)  A: Playing cards during class hours is not good.. 'It is not good to play…' can be rewritten with the gerund as subject: 'Playing… is not good.'
chunks.source: 'It is not good to play…' can be rewritten with the gerund as subject: 'Playing… is not good.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: "I will work hard in my examinations next term," said Enid. (Re-write beginning: Enid said ___)  A: Enid said that she would work hard in her examinations the following term.. In reported speech: 'will' → 'would', 'my' → 'her', 'next term' → 'the following term'.
chunks.source: In reported speech: 'will' → 'would', 'my' → 'her', 'next term' → 'the following term'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If we get our holidays, we shall go to the beach. (Re-write beginning: If we had ___)  A: If we had got our holidays, we would have gone to the beach.. First conditional becomes third conditional: 'If we had got…, we would have gone…'.
chunks.source: First conditional becomes third conditional: 'If we had got…, we would have gone…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Takuba will visit his parents if he gets the bus fare. (Re-write using: …unless ___)  A: Takuba will not visit his parents unless he gets the bus fare.. 'If he gets…' can be rewritten as 'unless he gets…' with a negative main clause.
chunks.source: 'If he gets…' can be rewritten as 'unless he gets…' with a negative main clause.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I was sick but I enjoyed the holiday. (Begin: Even though ___)  A: Even though I was sick, I enjoyed the holiday.. 'But' showing contrast can be rewritten with 'Even though'.
chunks.source: 'But' showing contrast can be rewritten with 'Even though'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Peter did not enjoy the holiday. Deborah did not enjoy the holiday. (Begin: Neither ___ nor ___)  A: Neither Peter nor Deborah enjoyed the holiday.. Two negative sentences join with 'Neither… nor…'.
chunks.source: Two negative sentences join with 'Neither… nor…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We ate a lot of eggs during December holidays. (Begin: A lot of ___)  A: A lot of eggs were eaten by us during December holidays.. Active to passive: 'a lot of eggs' becomes the subject.
chunks.source: Active to passive: 'a lot of eggs' becomes the subject.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: His money that he had to pay to travel by plane was stolen. (Give one word for: 'money that he had to pay to travel by plane' ___) A: fare. Money paid to travel by plane is called the 'fare'.
chunks.source: Money paid to travel by plane is called the 'fare'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The children did tiresome regular tasks during the holiday. (Give one word for: 'tiresome regular tasks' ___) A: chores. Regular household tasks are called 'chores'.
chunks.source: Regular household tasks are called 'chores'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Their trip to the zoo was exciting. (Give one word for: 'exciting' ___) A: thrilling. Another word for 'exciting' is 'thrilling'.
chunks.source: Another word for 'exciting' is 'thrilling'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'fare' and 'fair' in sentences to show their difference in meaning. (Write two sentences: ___)  A: I paid the bus fare to Kampala. The judge was fair to everyone.. 'Fare' is money paid for travel; 'fair' means just or beautiful.
chunks.source: 'Fare' is money paid for travel; 'fair' means just or beautiful.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Kate: 'Good afternoon, Derrick.' Derrick: ___ A: Good afternoon, Kate.. We reply to a greeting with the same greeting.
chunks.source: We reply to a greeting with the same greeting.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Kate: 'How do you always spend your holidays?' Derrick: ___ A: I always spend my holidays helping my parents in the shop.. Answer the question about how he spends holidays; the next line shows he helps in the shop.
chunks.source: Answer the question about how he spends holidays; the next line shows he helps in the shop.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Kate: 'Helping your parents in the shop! What kind of shop is it?' Derrick: ___ A: It is a retail shop.. Kate's next line says 'It is a retail shop!', so Derrick said that.
chunks.source: Kate's next line says 'It is a retail shop!', so Derrick said that.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Kate: 'It is a retail shop! What do you use to measure sugar?' Derrick: ___ A: I use a weighing scale.. Kate's next line says 'A weighing scale!', so Derrick said that.
chunks.source: Kate's next line says 'A weighing scale!', so Derrick said that.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Kate: 'A weighing scale! How much is a kilo of sugar?' Derrick: ___ A: A kilo of sugar is three thousand shillings.. Kate's next line says 'Three thousand shillings!', so Derrick said that.
chunks.source: Kate's next line says 'Three thousand shillings!', so Derrick said that.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Derrick: 'What about you Kate, how do you spend your holidays?' Kate: ___ A: I spend my holidays visiting relatives and touring important places.. Derrick's next line repeats 'Visiting relatives and touring important places!', so Kate said that.
chunks.source: Derrick's next line repeats 'Visiting relatives and touring important places!', so Kate said that.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Derrick: 'Visiting relatives and touring important places! Whom do you normally travel with?' Kate: ___ A: I normally travel with my parents.. Derrick's next line says 'With your parents!', so Kate said that.
chunks.source: Derrick's next line says 'With your parents!', so Kate said that.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Derrick: 'With your parents! How do you normally travel to Kasese?' Kate: ___ A: I normally travel to Kasese by bus.. Derrick's next line says 'By bus!', so Kate said that.
chunks.source: Derrick's next line says 'By bus!', so Kate said that.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Derrick: 'By bus! For how long do you stay at your grandmother's home?' Kate: ___ A: I stay at my grandmother's home for a fortnight.. Derrick's next line says 'A fortnight!', so Kate said that.
chunks.source: Derrick's next line says 'A fortnight!', so Kate said that.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Derrick: 'A fortnight! Goodbye Kate.' Kate: ___ A: Goodbye, Derrick.. Reply to 'Goodbye' with 'Goodbye'.
chunks.source: Reply to 'Goodbye' with 'Goodbye'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Sumaya has written a ___ letter. (friend) A: friendly. We need an adjective: the adjective form of 'friend' is 'friendly'.
chunks.source: We need an adjective: the adjective form of 'friend' is 'friendly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My father is ___ to write to me next week. (like) A: likely. 'Likely' means 'probably going to': 'is likely to write'.
chunks.source: 'Likely' means 'probably going to': 'is likely to write'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: His letter had a good ___. (introduce) A: introduction. The noun form of 'introduce' is 'introduction'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'introduce' is 'introduction'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Joan received a ___ letter from Paul. (person) A: personal. The adjective form of 'person' is 'personal'.
chunks.source: The adjective form of 'person' is 'personal'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I received a letter from my ___ friend. (Ghana) A: Ghanaian. A person from Ghana is 'Ghanaian'.
chunks.source: A person from Ghana is 'Ghanaian'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: There were ___ any letters in the mail box. A: hardly. 'Hardly any' means 'almost no': 'There were hardly any letters'.
chunks.source: 'Hardly any' means 'almost no': 'There were hardly any letters'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We ___ writing letters to our friends. A: enjoy. We need a verb: 'We enjoy writing letters'.
chunks.source: We need a verb: 'We enjoy writing letters'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Sofia writes letters ___ her friends every weekend. A: to. We write letters 'to' friends.
chunks.source: We write letters 'to' friends.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Neither the teacher ___ the pupil wrote a good letter. A: nor. 'Neither… nor…' is the correct pair.
chunks.source: 'Neither… nor…' is the correct pair.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He did not reply ___ my letter. A: to. We 'reply to' a letter.
chunks.source: We 'reply to' a letter.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: Informal ___ A: formal. The opposite of 'informal' is 'formal'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'informal' is 'formal'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: Friendly ___ A: unfriendly. The opposite of 'friendly' is 'unfriendly'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'friendly' is 'unfriendly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We may visit our relatives tomorrow. (Re-write using: …likely ___)  A: We are likely to visit our relatives tomorrow.. 'May' can be rewritten as 'are likely to'.
chunks.source: 'May' can be rewritten as 'are likely to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: There was almost no water in the tank. (Re-write using: …any ___)  A: There was hardly any water in the tank.. 'Almost no' can be rewritten as 'hardly any'.
chunks.source: 'Almost no' can be rewritten as 'hardly any'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The letter Monica wrote was not as good as mine. (Re-write using: …than ___)  A: My letter was better than the letter Monica wrote.. 'Not as good as' becomes 'better than' when reversed.
chunks.source: 'Not as good as' becomes 'better than' when reversed.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Kansiime is writing a personal letter. (Begin: A personal ___)  A: A personal letter is being written by Kansiime.. Active to passive in the present continuous.
chunks.source: Active to passive in the present continuous.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I have never seen a person as lucky as you are. (Re-write using: …luckiest ___)  A: You are the luckiest person I have ever seen.. 'As lucky as' becomes the superlative 'luckiest'.
chunks.source: 'As lucky as' becomes the superlative 'luckiest'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She sat under the mango tree. (Re-write using: …is ___)  A: She is sitting under the mango tree.. Past simple 'sat' becomes present continuous 'is sitting'.
chunks.source: Past simple 'sat' becomes present continuous 'is sitting'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We write letters to our parents every time we get holidays. (Begin: Whenever ___)  A: Whenever we get holidays, we write letters to our parents.. 'Every time' can be replaced by 'Whenever'.
chunks.source: 'Every time' can be replaced by 'Whenever'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: An informal letter is not as easy as a formal one. (Re-write using: A formal letter ___)  A: A formal letter is easier than an informal one.. 'Not as easy as' becomes 'easier than' when reversed.
chunks.source: 'Not as easy as' becomes 'easier than' when reversed.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the words in the box to complete the letter: [sincerely, choice, invite, reply, expected, 10th March, 2015, sports, Leah, function, place, guest]. 'Dear ___.'  A: Leah. The letter is addressed to Leah; 'Dear Leah,'.
chunks.source: The letter is addressed to Leah; 'Dear Leah,'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the words in the box to complete the letter: [sincerely, choice, invite, reply, expected, 10th March, 2015, sports, Leah, function, place, guest]. '…where did you put as your first ___?'  A: choice. 'First choice' means the first thing one chooses.
chunks.source: 'First choice' means the first thing one chooses.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the words in the box to complete the letter: [sincerely, choice, invite, reply, expected, 10th March, 2015, sports, Leah, function, place, guest]. 'I have written this letter to ___ you to our school Album Launch…'  A: invite. To 'invite' someone means to ask them to come.
chunks.source: To 'invite' someone means to ask them to come.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the words in the box to complete the letter: [sincerely, choice, invite, reply, expected, 10th March, 2015, sports, Leah, function, place, guest]. 'The ___ will take ___ at Theatre Labonita.'  A: function, place. The 'function' (event) will take 'place' (happen) at Theatre Labonita.
chunks.source: The 'function' (event) will take 'place' (happen) at Theatre Labonita.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the words in the box to complete the letter: [sincerely, choice, invite, reply, expected, 10th March, 2015, sports, Leah, function, place, guest]. 'The ___ of honour is ___ to be the Minister of Education and ___.'  A: guest, expected, sports. The 'guest of honour' is 'expected' to be the Minister of Education and Sports.
chunks.source: The 'guest of honour' is 'expected' to be the Minister of Education and Sports.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the words in the box to complete the letter: [sincerely, choice, invite, reply, expected, 10th March, 2015, sports, Leah, function, place, guest]. 'Please ___ soon to confirm your coming.'  A: reply. We ask someone to 'reply' to confirm.
chunks.source: We ask someone to 'reply' to confirm.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use the words in the box to complete the letter: [sincerely, choice, invite, reply, expected, 10th March, 2015, sports, Leah, function, place, guest]. 'Yours ___.'  A: sincerely. An informal letter ends with 'Yours sincerely'.
chunks.source: An informal letter ends with 'Yours sincerely'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The letter was ___ to the headteacher. (address) A: addressed. Passive: 'was addressed'. The past participle of 'address' is 'addressed'.
chunks.source: Passive: 'was addressed'. The past participle of 'address' is 'addressed'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Whenever I post a letter, I pay the ___ fee. (post) A: postage. The noun for the cost of posting is 'postage'.
chunks.source: The noun for the cost of posting is 'postage'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I ended my letter to the class teacher with 'yours ___.' (faith) A: faithfully. A formal letter ends with 'yours faithfully'.
chunks.source: A formal letter ends with 'yours faithfully'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We ___ write formal letters to our teachers. (usual) A: usually. We need an adverb: 'usually write'.
chunks.source: We need an adverb: 'usually write'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The headteacher's ___ is complicated. (sign) A: signature. The noun form of 'sign' is 'signature'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'sign' is 'signature'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The new pupils will get their ___ letters tomorrow. (admit) A: admission. Letters that admit pupils are 'admission letters'.
chunks.source: Letters that admit pupils are 'admission letters'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: There were only four ___ who applied for the job. (apply) A: applicants. People who apply are 'applicants'.
chunks.source: People who apply are 'applicants'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: His letter lacked a proper ___. (salute) A: salutation. The noun form of 'salute' is 'salutation'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'salute' is 'salutation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The letter was ___ signed by the manager. (office) A: officially. We need an adverb: 'officially signed'.
chunks.source: We need an adverb: 'officially signed'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ___ a letter is easier than flying an aeroplane. (write) A: Writing. The gerund 'Writing' is the subject of the sentence.
chunks.source: The gerund 'Writing' is the subject of the sentence.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Kungu's ___ was misplaced at the post office. (apply) A: application. The noun form of 'apply' is 'application'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'apply' is 'application'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The letter she received yesterday was ___ in black ink. (to write) A: written. Passive: 'was written'.
chunks.source: Passive: 'was written'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Baraza received his ___ letter to the party last week. (invite) A: invitation. The noun form of 'invite' is 'invitation'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'invite' is 'invitation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Jesca ___ the best pupil in the letter writing competition last term. (to be) A: was. 'Last term' needs the past simple: 'was'.
chunks.source: 'Last term' needs the past simple: 'was'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The P.7 pupils always write their letters ___. (care) A: carefully. We need an adverb: 'write carefully'.
chunks.source: We need an adverb: 'write carefully'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: Pamella's handwriting was legible. ___ A: illegible. The opposite of 'legible' is 'illegible'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'legible' is 'illegible'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: Formal letters are good to write. ___ A: bad. The opposite of 'good' is 'bad'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'good' is 'bad'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: He wrote his salutation as 'Dear Madam'. ___ A: Dear Sir. The opposite salutation is 'Dear Sir'.
chunks.source: The opposite salutation is 'Dear Sir'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: Rev. ___ A: Reverend. 'Rev.' is short for 'Reverend'.
chunks.source: 'Rev.' is short for 'Reverend'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: I.O.U ___ A: I Owe You. 'I.O.U' stands for 'I Owe You'.
chunks.source: 'I.O.U' stands for 'I Owe You'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: PP ___ A: per procurationem (on behalf of). 'PP' means 'per procurationem', i.e. signing on behalf of someone.
chunks.source: 'PP' means 'per procurationem', i.e. signing on behalf of someone.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: CC ___ A: Carbon Copy. 'CC' stands for 'Carbon Copy'.
chunks.source: 'CC' stands for 'Carbon Copy'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: Re ___ A: regarding. In letters, 'Re' means 'regarding' (about).
chunks.source: In letters, 'Re' means 'regarding' (about).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: e-mail ___ A: electronic mail. 'E-mail' is short for 'electronic mail'.
chunks.source: 'E-mail' is short for 'electronic mail'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: Hon. ___ A: Honourable. 'Hon.' is short for 'Honourable'.
chunks.source: 'Hon.' is short for 'Honourable'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: Prof. ___ A: Professor. 'Prof.' is short for 'Professor'.
chunks.source: 'Prof.' is short for 'Professor'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: w.e.f ___ A: with effect from. 'w.e.f' stands for 'with effect from'.
chunks.source: 'w.e.f' stands for 'with effect from'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: RSVP ___ A: Répondez s'il vous plaît (please reply). 'RSVP' is French for 'please reply'.
chunks.source: 'RSVP' is French for 'please reply'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the abbreviation in full: P.O ___ A: Post Office. 'P.O' is short for 'Post Office'.
chunks.source: 'P.O' is short for 'Post Office'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The letter was not legible. (Re-write using: …barely ___)  A: The letter was barely legible.. 'Not legible' can be rewritten as 'barely legible'.
chunks.source: 'Not legible' can be rewritten as 'barely legible'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: When he got a pen, he wrote a letter. (Use: …hardly ___)  A: Hardly had he got a pen when he wrote a letter.. 'When… wrote' becomes 'Hardly had… when…'.
chunks.source: 'When… wrote' becomes 'Hardly had… when…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She bought a stamp as soon as he reached the post office. (Use: scarcely ___)  A: Scarcely had he reached the post office when she bought a stamp.. 'As soon as' becomes 'Scarcely had… when…'.
chunks.source: 'As soon as' becomes 'Scarcely had… when…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Kimuli followed the teacher immediately he left the class. (Re-write beginning: Barely ___)  A: Barely had he left the class when Kimuli followed the teacher.. 'Immediately' becomes 'Barely had… when…'.
chunks.source: 'Immediately' becomes 'Barely had… when…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Immediately he wrote the letter, he posted it. (Begin: No sooner ___)  A: No sooner had he written the letter than he posted it.. 'Immediately' becomes 'No sooner had… than…'.
chunks.source: 'Immediately' becomes 'No sooner had… than…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange the sentences to make a good composition about 'Letter Writing': (a) Informal letters are written to relatives and friends. (b) In addition, we discussed several reasons why people write letters. (c) Last week, our teacher of English taught us about letter writing. (d) Lastly, people write letters either to apologise or to order for goods and services. (e) One of them is to apply for jobs or vacancies. (f) These are informal and formal letters. (g) While formal letters are written to office bearers. (h) The other is to invite somebody to a function. (i) Such as headteachers, bank managers and District Education Officers. A: Last week, our teacher of English taught us about letter writing., In addition, we discussed several reasons why people write letters., The other is to invite somebody to a function., One of them is to apply for jobs or vacancies., Lastly, people write letters either to apologise or to order for goods and services., These are informal and formal letters., Informal letters are written to relatives and friends., While formal letters are written to office bearers., Such as headteachers, bank managers and District Education Officers.. Begin with what happened, list the reasons, name the types, then give details.
chunks.source: Begin with what happened, list the reasons, name the types, then give details.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ___ was so easy that everybody passed it. (examine) A: examination. The noun form of 'examine' is 'examination'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'examine' is 'examination'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We look forward to ___ our end of term exams. (sit) A: sitting. After 'look forward to' we use the -ing form: 'sitting'.
chunks.source: After 'look forward to' we use the -ing form: 'sitting'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ___ to the examination room is narrow. (enter) A: entrance. The noun form of 'enter' is 'entrance'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'enter' is 'entrance'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He failed the question because he didn't read the ___. (instruct) A: instructions. The noun form of 'instruct' is 'instructions'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'instruct' is 'instructions'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The candidates will attend the ___. (brief) A: briefing. The noun form of 'brief' is 'briefing'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'brief' is 'briefing'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: His ___ in the examinations was a surprise. (fail) A: failure. The noun form of 'fail' is 'failure'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'fail' is 'failure'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The boys entered the room ___. (silent) A: silently. We need an adverb: 'entered silently'.
chunks.source: We need an adverb: 'entered silently'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: None of the candidates has paid the ___ fee. (register) A: registration. The noun form of 'register' is 'registration'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'register' is 'registration'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They did the test ___. (silent) A: silently. We need an adverb: 'did the test silently'.
chunks.source: We need an adverb: 'did the test silently'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Her ___ in the examination was attributed to hard work. (succeed) A: success. The noun form of 'succeed' is 'success'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'succeed' is 'success'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We are looking ___ to touring the city. A: forward. The phrase is 'looking forward to'.
chunks.source: The phrase is 'looking forward to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You must revise your work or ___ you will fail the examinations. A: else. The phrase is 'or else' (otherwise).
chunks.source: The phrase is 'or else' (otherwise).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He read his notes ___ to pass his examinations. A: carefully. He read his notes 'carefully' in order to pass.
chunks.source: He read his notes 'carefully' in order to pass.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: All pupils wrote the test without any difficulty. (Give one word for: 'without any difficulty' ___) A: easily. 'Without any difficulty' means 'easily'.
chunks.source: 'Without any difficulty' means 'easily'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We wrote our signed names carefully. (Give one word for: 'signed names' ___) A: signatures. 'Signed names' are 'signatures'.
chunks.source: 'Signed names' are 'signatures'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The man who supervised the examination was very kind. (Give one word for: 'man who supervised the examination' ___) A: invigilator. A person who supervises an examination is an 'invigilator'.
chunks.source: A person who supervises an examination is an 'invigilator'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The officials who set and mark examinations were called for a seminar. (Give one word for: 'officials who set and mark examinations' ___) A: examiners. People who set and mark examinations are 'examiners'.
chunks.source: People who set and mark examinations are 'examiners'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The pupils who were taking an examination were checked at the entrance. (Give one word for: 'pupils who were taking an examination' ___) A: candidates. Pupils taking an examination are 'candidates'.
chunks.source: Pupils taking an examination are 'candidates'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of the underlined word: We received the examination timetable yesterday. ___ A: timetables. The plural of 'timetable' is 'timetables'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'timetable' is 'timetables'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of the underlined word: They checked for his file name in the index. ___ A: indices. The plural of 'index' is 'indices' (or 'indexes').
chunks.source: The plural of 'index' is 'indices' (or 'indexes').

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Musana scored good marks because he answered questions in an accurate way. (Re-write ending: …accurately. ___)  A: Musana scored good marks because he answered questions accurately.. 'In an accurate way' becomes the adverb 'accurately'.
chunks.source: 'In an accurate way' becomes the adverb 'accurately'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If you don't keep quiet, I will throw you out of the examination room. (Re-write using: …or else ___)  A: Keep quiet or else I will throw you out of the examination room.. 'If you don't…' can be rewritten as an order + 'or else'.
chunks.source: 'If you don't…' can be rewritten as an order + 'or else'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The headteacher will brief the candidates soon. (Re-write using: …looking forward ___)  A: The headteacher is looking forward to briefing the candidates soon.. 'Will brief' becomes 'is looking forward to briefing'.
chunks.source: 'Will brief' becomes 'is looking forward to briefing'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You should read the instructions or else you won't understand. (Use: If ___)  A: If you don't read the instructions, you won't understand.. 'Or else' becomes a negative 'if' clause.
chunks.source: 'Or else' becomes a negative 'if' clause.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: All the candidates didn't fail the examinations. (Re-write using: None ___)  A: None of the candidates failed the examinations.. 'All… didn't' becomes 'None of…'.
chunks.source: 'All… didn't' becomes 'None of…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If the inspector gets a vehicle, he will visit our school. (Use: …unless ___)  A: Unless the inspector gets a vehicle, he will not visit our school.. 'If' becomes 'unless' with a negative main clause.
chunks.source: 'If' becomes 'unless' with a negative main clause.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The science examination was very easy. The pass mark was raised. (Join using: …so…that ___)  A: The science examination was so easy that the pass mark was raised.. Join with 'so + adjective + that'.
chunks.source: Join with 'so + adjective + that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He performs carefully. (Use: …careful ___)  A: He is careful in his performance.. The adverb 'carefully' becomes the adjective 'careful'.
chunks.source: The adverb 'carefully' becomes the adjective 'careful'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mr. Omonya taught us very well. We did not pass the test. (Re-write using: …although ___)  A: Although Mr. Omonya taught us very well, we did not pass the test.. Join two contrasting sentences with 'although'.
chunks.source: Join two contrasting sentences with 'although'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: When you cheat the examination, you will be disqualified. (Begin: If ___)  A: If you cheat the examination, you will be disqualified.. 'When' (on condition) can be replaced by 'If'.
chunks.source: 'When' (on condition) can be replaced by 'If'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We gave our answer sheets to the supervisor. He sealed them in an envelope. (Begin: Having ___)  A: Having been given our answer sheets, the supervisor sealed them in an envelope.. 'Having been given…' shows the first action happened before the second.
chunks.source: 'Having been given…' shows the first action happened before the second.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the UNEB instructions and answer: Where was the information above extracted? ___ A: The Uganda National Examinations Board Primary Leaving Examination Paper of English.. The instructions come from the UNEB PLE English paper.
chunks.source: The instructions come from the UNEB PLE English paper.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the UNEB instructions and answer: For which subject are the above instructions? ___ A: English. The instructions are for the English paper.
chunks.source: The instructions are for the English paper.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the UNEB instructions and answer: How many sections does an English examination paper consist? ___ A: Two. The paper has two sections: A and B.
chunks.source: The paper has two sections: A and B.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the UNEB instructions and answer: What will happen to a candidate who writes poorly? ___ A: The candidate may lose marks.. Handwriting that cannot be read may lead to loss of marks.
chunks.source: Handwriting that cannot be read may lead to loss of marks.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the UNEB instructions and answer: Which kind of ink is only allowed in writing answers? ___ A: Blue or black ball-point pen or ink.. Instruction 3 says blue or black ball-point pen or ink.
chunks.source: Instruction 3 says blue or black ball-point pen or ink.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the UNEB instructions and answer: Which body is responsible for setting and marking examinations in Uganda? ___ A: The Uganda National Examinations Board (UNEB).. UNEB sets and marks examinations in Uganda.
chunks.source: UNEB sets and marks examinations in Uganda.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the UNEB instructions and answer: What does instruction six tell the candidates to do? ___ A: Not to fill in anything in the boxes shown 'For Examiners use only' and those inside the question paper.. Instruction 6 forbids writing in the examiners' boxes.
chunks.source: Instruction 6 forbids writing in the examiners' boxes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the UNEB instructions and answer: Which two instructions are quite similar? ___ A: Instructions 4 and 5.. Instruction 4 (unnecessary changes) and instruction 5 (unreadable handwriting) both warn about losing marks.
chunks.source: Instruction 4 (unnecessary changes) and instruction 5 (unreadable handwriting) both warn about losing marks.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ___ checked the candidates before entering the examination room. (invigilate) A: invigilator. The noun form of 'invigilate' is 'invigilator'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'invigilate' is 'invigilator'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A relative of ___ failed the examinations. (she) A: hers. After 'of' we use the possessive pronoun 'hers'.
chunks.source: After 'of' we use the possessive pronoun 'hers'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: All the visitors were given comfortable ___. (sit) A: seats. The noun form of 'sit' is 'seat'; plural 'seats'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'sit' is 'seat'; plural 'seats'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Wahib passed in ___ one. (divide) A: division. The noun form of 'divide' is 'division'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'divide' is 'division'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The candidates were found ___ examinations. (cheat) A: cheating. After 'were found' we use the -ing form: 'were found cheating'.
chunks.source: After 'were found' we use the -ing form: 'were found cheating'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The examination cheats were ___. (disqualify) A: disqualified. Passive: 'were disqualified'.
chunks.source: Passive: 'were disqualified'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Nalule was advised to stop ___ examination papers. (dirty) A: dirtying. After 'stop' we use the -ing form: 'stop dirtying'.
chunks.source: After 'stop' we use the -ing form: 'stop dirtying'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We must prepare ___ for the forthcoming examinations. (self) A: ourselves. The reflexive pronoun for 'we' is 'ourselves'.
chunks.source: The reflexive pronoun for 'we' is 'ourselves'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: All the answers should be written ___. (correct) A: correctly. We need an adverb: 'written correctly'.
chunks.source: We need an adverb: 'written correctly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Examiners are looking forward to ___ examinations next week. (mark) A: marking. After 'look forward to' we use the -ing form.
chunks.source: After 'look forward to' we use the -ing form.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: Their success in the test was a surprise. ___ A: failure. The opposite of 'success' is 'failure'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'success' is 'failure'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: Most pupils passed P.L.E last year. ___ A: failed. The opposite of 'passed' is 'failed'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'passed' is 'failed'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: Juliet's work is really tidy. ___ A: untidy. The opposite of 'tidy' is 'untidy'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'tidy' is 'untidy'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: The arrival of the scout scared the invigilator. ___ A: departure. The opposite of 'arrival' is 'departure'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'arrival' is 'departure'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: Her work was complete by the time the bell rang. ___ A: incomplete. The opposite of 'complete' is 'incomplete'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'complete' is 'incomplete'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The girls performed well. The boys performed poorly. (Re-write beginning: Whereas ___)  A: Whereas the girls performed well, the boys performed poorly.. 'Whereas' joins two contrasting sentences.
chunks.source: 'Whereas' joins two contrasting sentences.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Cheating is likely to lead to disqualification of our school. (Re-write using: …could ___)  A: Cheating could lead to disqualification of our school.. 'Is likely to' can be rewritten as 'could'.
chunks.source: 'Is likely to' can be rewritten as 'could'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: In spite of Aboke's sickness, she came for the examination. (Re-write using: …although ___)  A: Although Aboke was sick, she came for the examination.. 'In spite of' + noun becomes 'although' + clause.
chunks.source: 'In spite of' + noun becomes 'although' + clause.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Although the candidates were given more time, they didn't complete the work. (Begin: Despite ___)  A: Despite being given more time, the candidates didn't complete the work.. 'Although' + clause becomes 'Despite' + -ing.
chunks.source: 'Although' + clause becomes 'Despite' + -ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The pass mark was high. The pupils passed mathematics. (Re-write beginning: Although ___)  A: Although the pass mark was high, the pupils passed mathematics.. Join contrasting sentences with 'Although'.
chunks.source: Join contrasting sentences with 'Although'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: This pen belongs to Maria. (Re-write beginning: Maria ___)  A: Maria owns this pen.. 'Belongs to Maria' becomes 'Maria owns'.
chunks.source: 'Belongs to Maria' becomes 'Maria owns'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: This room is theirs. (Re-write using: …their ___)  A: This is their room.. 'Is theirs' becomes 'is their room'.
chunks.source: 'Is theirs' becomes 'is their room'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You failed the English paper. Didn't you? (Re-write and end: …did you? ___)  A: You failed the English paper, did you?. The tag must be opposite: the sentence is positive, so the tag is 'did you?'.
chunks.source: The tag must be opposite: the sentence is positive, so the tag is 'did you?'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the PLE 2012 timetable and answer: For which year is the above examination timetable? ___ A: 2012. The timetable is for PLE November 2012.
chunks.source: The timetable is for PLE November 2012.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the PLE 2012 timetable and answer: What took place on 2nd November? ___ A: Briefing of candidates by the Headteacher.. On Tuesday 2nd November there was the briefing of candidates.
chunks.source: On Tuesday 2nd November there was the briefing of candidates.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the PLE 2012 timetable and answer: On which date did the examinations begin? ___ A: 3rd November. The first papers (Social Studies, English) were on Wednesday 3rd November.
chunks.source: The first papers (Social Studies, English) were on Wednesday 3rd November.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the PLE 2012 timetable and answer: Which subject was done on Thursday afternoon? ___ A: Basic Science and Health Education. Thursday afternoon: Basic Science and Health Education.
chunks.source: Thursday afternoon: Basic Science and Health Education.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the PLE 2012 timetable and answer: How long did the Mathematics paper take? ___ A: 2 hours 30 minutes. The Mathematics paper took 2 hrs 30 min.
chunks.source: The Mathematics paper took 2 hrs 30 min.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the PLE 2012 timetable and answer: Who briefed the candidates? ___ A: The Headteacher. The briefing was done by the Headteacher.
chunks.source: The briefing was done by the Headteacher.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the PLE 2012 timetable and answer: How long did the briefing take? ___ A: 2 hours. The briefing took 2 hours.
chunks.source: The briefing took 2 hours.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the PLE 2012 timetable and answer: How many subjects are shown on the timetable? ___ A: Four. The subjects are Social Studies, English, Mathematics, and Basic Science and Health Education.
chunks.source: The subjects are Social Studies, English, Mathematics, and Basic Science and Health Education.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the PLE 2012 timetable and answer: Which examination took the longest time? ___ A: Mathematics. Mathematics took 2 hrs 30 min, the longest.
chunks.source: Mathematics took 2 hrs 30 min, the longest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: It was ___ that the prices of sugar would rise. (forecast) A: forecast. 'Forecast' is the same in the past participle: 'was forecast'.
chunks.source: 'Forecast' is the same in the past participle: 'was forecast'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The T.V. was ___ in to Bukedde. (tune) A: tuned. Passive: 'was tuned in to Bukedde'.
chunks.source: Passive: 'was tuned in to Bukedde'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The prefect in charge of ___ is very jolly. (entertain) A: entertainment. The noun form of 'entertain' is 'entertainment'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'entertain' is 'entertainment'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The news was ___ by radio star. (broadcast) A: broadcast. 'Broadcast' is the same in the past participle: 'was broadcast'.
chunks.source: 'Broadcast' is the same in the past participle: 'was broadcast'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: There are several forms of electronic ___. (medium) A: media. The plural of 'medium' is 'media'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'medium' is 'media'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Tel. ___ A: Telephone. 'Tel.' is short for 'Telephone'.
chunks.source: 'Tel.' is short for 'Telephone'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: TV ___ A: Television. 'TV' is short for 'Television'.
chunks.source: 'TV' is short for 'Television'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Advert ___ A: Advertisement. 'Advert' is short for 'Advertisement'.
chunks.source: 'Advert' is short for 'Advertisement'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: CD ___ A: Compact Disc. 'CD' is short for 'Compact Disc'.
chunks.source: 'CD' is short for 'Compact Disc'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: DVD ___ A: Digital Versatile Disc. 'DVD' is short for 'Digital Versatile Disc'.
chunks.source: 'DVD' is short for 'Digital Versatile Disc'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Vol. ___ A: Volume. 'Vol.' is short for 'Volume'.
chunks.source: 'Vol.' is short for 'Volume'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Joan is a good presenter. Cathy is also a good presenter. (Join using: …and so ___)  A: Joan is a good presenter, and so is Cathy.. Join with 'and so' + inversion: 'and so is Cathy'.
chunks.source: Join with 'and so' + inversion: 'and so is Cathy'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If I have a CD player, I will buy many CDs. (Use: …would have ___)  A: If I had had a CD player, I would have bought many CDs.. First conditional becomes third conditional.
chunks.source: First conditional becomes third conditional.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You needn't have switched off the DVD. (Use: …necessary ___)  A: It was not necessary for you to switch off the DVD.. 'Needn't have' means 'it was not necessary'.
chunks.source: 'Needn't have' means 'it was not necessary'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I don't like listening to gospel music. (Re-write using: …hate ___)  A: I hate listening to gospel music.. 'Don't like' becomes 'hate'.
chunks.source: 'Don't like' becomes 'hate'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Ojamba bought a radio yet it was not necessary. (Use: …didn't have ___)  A: Ojamba didn't have to buy a radio.. 'It was not necessary to buy' becomes 'didn't have to buy'.
chunks.source: 'It was not necessary to buy' becomes 'didn't have to buy'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the advertisement and answer: What is the advertisement about? ___ A: The sale of used vehicles by Uganda Communications Network.. UCN is selling off used vehicles.
chunks.source: UCN is selling off used vehicles.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the advertisement and answer: Where did it appear? ___ A: In the Sun newspaper.. The advertisement appeared in the Sun newspaper.
chunks.source: The advertisement appeared in the Sun newspaper.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the advertisement and answer: When did it appear? ___ A: June 12th 2012. It appeared in the Sun newspaper of June 12th 2012.
chunks.source: It appeared in the Sun newspaper of June 12th 2012.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the advertisement and answer: For how many days was the sale meant to last? ___ A: Seven days. From 25/07/2012 to 31/07/2012 is seven days.
chunks.source: From 25/07/2012 to 31/07/2012 is seven days.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the advertisement and answer: How many vehicles were on sale? ___ A: Four. Toyota Land Cruiser, Prado, Toyota Rav 4 and Spacio.
chunks.source: Toyota Land Cruiser, Prado, Toyota Rav 4 and Spacio.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the advertisement and answer: When was the advertisement written? ___ A: 10th June 2012. The advertisement is dated 10/06/2012.
chunks.source: The advertisement is dated 10/06/2012.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the advertisement and answer: How long will the sale last each day? ___ A: Seven hours (9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.). The sale runs from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. daily.
chunks.source: The sale runs from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. daily.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the advertisement and answer: Where will the sale take place? ___ A: Kamwokya. The venue of the sale is Kamwokya.
chunks.source: The venue of the sale is Kamwokya.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the advertisement and answer: Write UCN in full. ___ A: Uganda Communications Network. UCN stands for Uganda Communications Network.
chunks.source: UCN stands for Uganda Communications Network.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the advertisement and answer: The sale of used vehicles will begin on ___. A: Friday, July 25, 2012. The sale begins on Friday, July 25, 2012.
chunks.source: The sale begins on Friday, July 25, 2012.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: The pupils left the room after the teacher's arrival. ___ A: departure. The opposite of 'arrival' is 'departure'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'arrival' is 'departure'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: The exercise was passed by the majority. ___ A: minority. The opposite of 'majority' is 'minority'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'majority' is 'minority'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: The woman was found innocent. ___ A: guilty. The opposite of 'innocent' is 'guilty'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'innocent' is 'guilty'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: Jane was cruel to her horse. ___ A: kind. The opposite of 'cruel' is 'kind'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'cruel' is 'kind'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: He scattered his friend's clothes. ___ A: gathered. The opposite of 'scattered' is 'gathered'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'scattered' is 'gathered'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: The MC blamed the choir for their performance. ___ A: praised. The opposite of 'blamed' is 'praised'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'blamed' is 'praised'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: He got a permanent job. ___ A: temporary. The opposite of 'permanent' is 'temporary'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'permanent' is 'temporary'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: It is legal to hunt in game parks. ___ A: illegal. The opposite of 'legal' is 'illegal'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'legal' is 'illegal'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: A Toyota moves faster than a Peugeot. ___ A: slower. The opposite of 'faster' is 'slower'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'faster' is 'slower'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: Their descendants were literate. ___ A: illiterate. The opposite of 'literate' is 'illiterate'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'literate' is 'illiterate'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: My father is a person who sells meat. ___ A: butcher. A person who sells meat is a 'butcher'.
chunks.source: A person who sells meat is a 'butcher'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: I bought my book from a woman who writes poems. ___ A: poet. A person who writes poems is a 'poet'.
chunks.source: A person who writes poems is a 'poet'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: Daddy bought my stationery from the man who sells stationery. ___ A: stationer. A person who sells stationery is a 'stationer'.
chunks.source: A person who sells stationery is a 'stationer'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: The doctor who attends to eye diseases is kind. ___ A: ophthalmologist. A doctor who treats eye diseases is an 'ophthalmologist' (eye doctor).
chunks.source: A doctor who treats eye diseases is an 'ophthalmologist' (eye doctor).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: Katongole is a person who writes news for Red Pepper. ___ A: journalist. A person who writes news is a 'journalist'.
chunks.source: A person who writes news is a 'journalist'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in alphabetical order: ally, alive, alto, allow ___ A: alive, ally, allow, alto. Compare letter by letter: alive, ally, allow, alto.
chunks.source: Compare letter by letter: alive, ally, allow, alto.

chunks.subject: English
