chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in alphabetical order: wake, want, wag, warrant ___ A: wag, wake, want, warrant. Compare letter by letter: wag, wake, want, warrant.
chunks.source: Compare letter by letter: wag, wake, want, warrant.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in alphabetical order: glory, glass, glorify, gland ___ A: gland, glass, glorify, glory. Compare letter by letter: gland, glass, glorify, glory.
chunks.source: Compare letter by letter: gland, glass, glorify, glory.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in alphabetical order: temperature, temperate, temporary, temple ___ A: temperate, temperature, temple, temporary. Compare letter by letter: temperate, temperature, temple, temporary.
chunks.source: Compare letter by letter: temperate, temperature, temple, temporary.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in alphabetical order: year, yeah, yearn, yeast ___ A: yeah, year, yearn, yeast. Compare letter by letter: yeah, year, yearn, yeast.
chunks.source: Compare letter by letter: yeah, year, yearn, yeast.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The innocent girl carried out an ___ (abort) A: abortion. The noun form of 'abort' is 'abortion'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'abort' is 'abortion'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fred's ___ took place in the village. (marry) A: marriage. The noun form of 'marry' is 'marriage'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'marry' is 'marriage'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The rapist was ___ last week. (convict) A: convicted. Passive: 'was convicted'.
chunks.source: Passive: 'was convicted'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Discipline should be ___ in all schools. (force) A: enforced. Passive: 'should be enforced'.
chunks.source: Passive: 'should be enforced'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Pupils should be ___ to their teachers. (obey) A: obedient. The adjective form of 'obey' is 'obedient'.
chunks.source: The adjective form of 'obey' is 'obedient'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The rioters were all ___ last week. (prison) A: imprisoned. Passive: 'were imprisoned' (put in prison).
chunks.source: Passive: 'were imprisoned' (put in prison).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He died due to serious ___ he sustained. (injure) A: injuries. The noun form of 'injure' is 'injury'; plural 'injuries'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'injure' is 'injury'; plural 'injuries'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: freedom ___ A: slavery. The opposite of 'freedom' is 'slavery'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'freedom' is 'slavery'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: life ___ A: death. The opposite of 'life' is 'death'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'life' is 'death'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: refuse ___ A: accept. The opposite of 'refuse' is 'accept'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'refuse' is 'accept'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: peace ___ A: war. The opposite of 'peace' is 'war'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'peace' is 'war'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: obedient ___ A: disobedient. The opposite of 'obedient' is 'disobedient'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'obedient' is 'disobedient'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: respect ___ A: disrespect. The opposite of 'respect' is 'disrespect'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'respect' is 'disrespect'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: sugar-daddy ___ A: sugar-mummy. The opposite of 'sugar-daddy' is 'sugar-mummy'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'sugar-daddy' is 'sugar-mummy'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: capture ___ A: release. The opposite of 'capture' is 'release'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'capture' is 'release'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: secure ___ A: insecure. The opposite of 'secure' is 'insecure'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'secure' is 'insecure'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: comfort ___ A: discomfort. The opposite of 'comfort' is 'discomfort'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'comfort' is 'discomfort'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The woman battered her step-child. (Re-write using: …..accused of ___)  A: The woman was accused of battering her step-child.. 'Battered' becomes 'was accused of battering'.
chunks.source: 'Battered' becomes 'was accused of battering'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The man has gone to court. His son was arrested. (Join using: …whose ___)  A: The man whose son was arrested has gone to court.. Join with the relative pronoun 'whose'.
chunks.source: Join with the relative pronoun 'whose'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The boys will be tried in court. They threw stones at policemen. (Join using: …who ___)  A: The boys who threw stones at policemen will be tried in court.. Join with the relative pronoun 'who'.
chunks.source: Join with the relative pronoun 'who'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The sugar-daddy was arrested. He was caught defiling a school girl. (Join using: …because ___)  A: The sugar-daddy was arrested because he was caught defiling a school girl.. Join the cause and effect with 'because'.
chunks.source: Join the cause and effect with 'because'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Bangi: 'Good morning, Omara.' Omara: ___ A: Good morning, Bangi.. Reply to a greeting with the same greeting.
chunks.source: Reply to a greeting with the same greeting.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Bangi: 'I am going to the police station.' Omara: ___ A: Where are you going?. Ask where he is going; the answer is 'the police station'.
chunks.source: Ask where he is going; the answer is 'the police station'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Bangi: 'I am going to see Mr. Kapare. The police arrested him.' Omara: ___ A: Why was he arrested?. Ask why he was arrested; the answer is that he mistreats his children.
chunks.source: Ask why he was arrested; the answer is that he mistreats his children.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Bangi: 'The villagers say that he mistreats his children.' Omara: ___ A: That is very bad.. React to the bad news.
chunks.source: React to the bad news.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the dialogue. Bangi: 'It is a serious matter indeed. He should know that it is a crime to mistreat children.' Omara: ___ A: You are right.. Agree with Bangi.
chunks.source: Agree with Bangi.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We should mulch the soil to protect it against soil ___. (erode) A: erosion. The noun form of 'erode' is 'erosion'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'erode' is 'erosion'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We learnt about ___ of the environment. (conserve) A: conservation. The noun form of 'conserve' is 'conservation'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'conserve' is 'conservation'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our village has good natural ___. (drain) A: drainage. The noun form of 'drain' is 'drainage'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'drain' is 'drainage'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Over ___ destroys the environment. (graze) A: overgrazing. 'Over' + grazing = 'overgrazing'.
chunks.source: 'Over' + grazing = 'overgrazing'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: All the garbage should be well ___ of. (dispose) A: disposed. 'Dispose of' needs the past participle: 'disposed'.
chunks.source: 'Dispose of' needs the past participle: 'disposed'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a word to mean: flora ___ A: plants. 'Flora' means the plants of an area.
chunks.source: 'Flora' means the plants of an area.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a word to mean: fauna ___ A: animals. 'Fauna' means the animals of an area.
chunks.source: 'Fauna' means the animals of an area.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a word to mean: degradation ___ A: destruction. 'Degradation' means gradual damage or destruction.
chunks.source: 'Degradation' means gradual damage or destruction.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give a word to mean: conserve ___ A: protect. 'Conserve' means to protect or preserve.
chunks.source: 'Conserve' means to protect or preserve.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The terraces broke down. They were not well made. (Re-write using: …so ___)  A: The terraces were so badly made that they broke down.. Join with 'so + adverb + that'.
chunks.source: Join with 'so + adverb + that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If we are to get rain, we must conserve our forests. (Re-write using: …in order to ___)  A: We must conserve our forests in order to get rain.. 'If we are to get rain' becomes 'in order to get rain'.
chunks.source: 'If we are to get rain' becomes 'in order to get rain'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Namata hurried home after school. She wanted to burn the rubbish at home. (Join using: …since ___)  A: Namata hurried home after school since she wanted to burn the rubbish at home.. Join the cause with 'since'.
chunks.source: Join the cause with 'since'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We cut down all the trees. We did not have more rain. (Begin: If we had ___)  A: If we had not cut down all the trees, we would have had more rain.. Third conditional: 'If we had not cut…, we would have had…'.
chunks.source: Third conditional: 'If we had not cut…, we would have had…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If you don't practice good farming methods, you will get poor crop yields. (Re-write using: …unless ___)  A: Unless you practice good farming methods, you will get poor crop yields.. 'If you don't…' becomes 'Unless you…'.
chunks.source: 'If you don't…' becomes 'Unless you…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mulching is a good farming method. Crop rotation is also a good farming method. (Join using: …as well as ___)  A: Mulching as well as crop rotation is a good farming method.. Join with 'as well as'.
chunks.source: Join with 'as well as'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Too much smoke causes air ___ in a place. (pollute) A: pollution. The noun form of 'pollute' is 'pollution'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'pollute' is 'pollution'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ___ protection is the keeping of the environment safe. A: Environmental. 'Environmental protection' is the full phrase.
chunks.source: 'Environmental protection' is the full phrase.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: People in Kigezi dig terraces so as to control soil ___. (erode) A: erosion. The noun form of 'erode' is 'erosion'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'erode' is 'erosion'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Smoking may ___ our lives. (danger) A: endanger. The verb form of 'danger' is 'endanger'.
chunks.source: The verb form of 'danger' is 'endanger'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We must ___ all the swamps to avoid floods. (drainage) A: drain. The verb form of 'drainage' is 'drain'.
chunks.source: The verb form of 'drainage' is 'drain'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Jenifer Musisi has advised residents of Kampala to stop ___ garbage. A: dumping. We 'dump' garbage in wrong places.
chunks.source: We 'dump' garbage in wrong places.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We need to dispose ___ the rubbish in the right places. A: of. The phrase is 'dispose of'.
chunks.source: The phrase is 'dispose of'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The forests have been cut ___, we are likely to face a drought. A: down. The phrasal verb is 'cut down'.
chunks.source: The phrasal verb is 'cut down'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ___ we build terraces, the soil will erode. A: Unless. 'Unless we build…' means 'if we do not build…'.
chunks.source: 'Unless we build…' means 'if we do not build…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We had to rotate crops ___ to maintain soil fertility. A: so as. The phrase is 'so as to'.
chunks.source: The phrase is 'so as to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: Garbage ___ A: garbage. 'Garbage' is uncountable; the plural is the same.
chunks.source: 'Garbage' is uncountable; the plural is the same.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: Dustbin ___ A: dustbins. The plural of 'dustbin' is 'dustbins'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'dustbin' is 'dustbins'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the plural of: Mosquito ___ A: mosquitoes. The plural of 'mosquito' is 'mosquitoes'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'mosquito' is 'mosquitoes'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: People of Karamoja faced a long period of dry weather last year. (Give one word for: 'a long period of dry weather' ___) A: drought. A long period of dry weather is a 'drought'.
chunks.source: A long period of dry weather is a 'drought'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The animals in Budongo forest are dangerous. (Give one word for: 'The animals in Budongo forest' ___) A: wildlife. Wild animals of an area are 'wildlife'.
chunks.source: Wild animals of an area are 'wildlife'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The forests have been cut. We shall not have rain. (Re-write using: …since ___)  A: Since the forests have been cut, we shall not have rain.. Join the cause with 'since'.
chunks.source: Join the cause with 'since'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Everybody admires the Queen because she is beautiful. (Re-write using: …due to ___)  A: Everybody admires the Queen due to her beauty.. 'Because she is beautiful' becomes 'due to her beauty'.
chunks.source: 'Because she is beautiful' becomes 'due to her beauty'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Farmers practice crop rotation. They want to get better yields. (Begin: In order ___)  A: In order to get better yields, farmers practice crop rotation.. 'They want to get…' becomes 'In order to get…'.
chunks.source: 'They want to get…' becomes 'In order to get…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We cut down all the trees. We didn't have more rain. (Begin: If we had ___)  A: If we had not cut down all the trees, we would have had more rain.. Third conditional.
chunks.source: Third conditional.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If I see him, I will tell him to come to your office. (Re-write using: …saw ___)  A: If I saw him, I would tell him to come to your office.. First conditional becomes second conditional.
chunks.source: First conditional becomes second conditional.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Your animals will get lost if you don't tag them. (Begin: Unless ___)  A: Unless you tag your animals, they will get lost.. 'If you don't…' becomes 'Unless you…'.
chunks.source: 'If you don't…' becomes 'Unless you…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our tap was spoilt. We did not have clean water. (Join using: …so ___)  A: Our tap was spoilt so we did not have clean water.. Join cause and effect with 'so'.
chunks.source: Join cause and effect with 'so'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The farmers watered their crops but all the same they dried up. (Re-write using: …although ___)  A: Although the farmers watered their crops, they dried up.. 'But all the same' becomes 'although'.
chunks.source: 'But all the same' becomes 'although'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-arrange the sentences to form a good story about the environment: (a) The environment includes forests, wetlands, lakes and rivers. (b) As a result farmers can no longer harvest good yield. (c) In the end, the future generation will enjoy the beauty of this country. (d) There are a number of environmental problems facing Ugandans today. (e) Thirdly, overgrazing and soil erosion have reduced manure. (f) About the danger of the uncontrolled use of the environment. (g) First of all, some forests and wetlands are now farming areas. (h) The greatest one being poor conservation of environment. (i) Secondly, people do not practice the best methods of farming. (j) There is no doubt, therefore, we have to educate everybody. A: The environment includes forests, wetlands, lakes and rivers., There are a number of environmental problems facing Ugandans today., The greatest one being poor conservation of environment., About the danger of the uncontrolled use of the environment., First of all, some forests and wetlands are now farming areas., Secondly, people do not practice the best methods of farming., Thirdly, overgrazing and soil erosion have reduced manure., As a result farmers can no longer harvest good yield., There is no doubt, therefore, we have to educate everybody., In the end, the future generation will enjoy the beauty of this country.. Begin with the topic, state the problems in order, then give the solution and end with hope.
chunks.source: Begin with the topic, state the problems in order, then give the solution and end with hope.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Cultural ___ is so interesting. (marry) A: marriage. The noun form of 'marry' is 'marriage'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'marry' is 'marriage'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I bought my ___ gown from Winna Classic. (bride) A: bridal. The adjective form of 'bride' is 'bridal'.
chunks.source: The adjective form of 'bride' is 'bridal'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Before his ___, he had to produce his birth certificate. (baptize) A: baptism. The noun form of 'baptize' is 'baptism'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'baptize' is 'baptism'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Neither my father nor my mother attended the ___ of the chief. (bury) A: burial. The noun form of 'bury' is 'burial'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'bury' is 'burial'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The couple was given a nice ___ ring. (engage) A: engagement. The noun form of 'engage' is 'engagement'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'engage' is 'engagement'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: The bride was smartly dressed. ___ A: shabbily. The opposite of 'smartly' is 'shabbily'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'smartly' is 'shabbily'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: The best man looked organized. ___ A: disorganized. The opposite of 'organized' is 'disorganized'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'organized' is 'disorganized'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: The heir should be understanding. ___ A: misunderstanding. The opposite of 'understanding' is 'misunderstanding'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'understanding' is 'misunderstanding'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: The widow stays in a hut. ___ A: widower. The male form of 'widow' is 'widower'.
chunks.source: The male form of 'widow' is 'widower'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: The mourners sat around the place in the ground where a dead person is buried. ___ A: grave. A place where a dead person is buried is a 'grave'.
chunks.source: A place where a dead person is buried is a 'grave'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: The child whose parents are dead got a bursary. ___ A: orphan. A child whose parents are dead is an 'orphan'.
chunks.source: A child whose parents are dead is an 'orphan'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: A box in which a dead body is placed for burial should be durable. ___ A: coffin. A box for a dead body is a 'coffin'.
chunks.source: A box for a dead body is a 'coffin'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: The people attending the burial looked sad. ___ A: mourners. People attending a burial are 'mourners'.
chunks.source: People attending a burial are 'mourners'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: He is a man who lost his wife. ___ A: widower. A man who lost his wife is a 'widower'.
chunks.source: A man who lost his wife is a 'widower'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: The brides were given a collection of flowers. ___ A: bouquet. A collection of flowers is a 'bouquet'.
chunks.source: A collection of flowers is a 'bouquet'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'salon' in a meaningful sentence to show its meaning. ___ A: My sister went to the beauty salon to plait her hair.. 'Salon' is a place for hair and beauty care.
chunks.source: 'Salon' is a place for hair and beauty care.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'saloon' in a meaningful sentence to show its meaning. ___ A: The saloon car carried five passengers.. 'Saloon' is a type of car.
chunks.source: 'Saloon' is a type of car.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The woman is my aunt. She was the bride. (Join using: …who ___)  A: The woman who was the bride is my aunt.. Join with the relative pronoun 'who'.
chunks.source: Join with the relative pronoun 'who'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The teachers did not go to the wedding. The pupils did not go to the wedding. (Re-write using: Neither ___)  A: Neither the teachers nor the pupils went to the wedding.. Join two negatives with 'Neither… nor…'.
chunks.source: Join two negatives with 'Neither… nor…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He has never gone to his ancestral grounds. He was chosen to be the heir. (Begin: Despite ___)  A: Despite never having gone to his ancestral grounds, he was chosen to be the heir.. 'Despite' + -ing replaces 'has never gone'.
chunks.source: 'Despite' + -ing replaces 'has never gone'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ___ my aunt nor my uncle attended the burial. A: Neither. The pair is 'Neither… nor…'.
chunks.source: The pair is 'Neither… nor…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mutosi died ___ Typhoid fever. A: of. We 'die of' a disease.
chunks.source: We 'die of' a disease.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The thief ___ broke into the shop was killed. A: who. 'Who' refers to a person.
chunks.source: 'Who' refers to a person.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Many guests preferred self service ___ being served by others. A: to. We 'prefer… to…'.
chunks.source: We 'prefer… to…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The best man looked handsome ___ did the bridegroom. A: so. The pattern is 'so did' (inversion).
chunks.source: The pattern is 'so did' (inversion).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I prefer religious marriage to ___ one. (culture) A: cultural. The adjective form of 'culture' is 'cultural'.
chunks.source: The adjective form of 'culture' is 'cultural'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The chief was buried at their ___ home. (ancestor) A: ancestral. The adjective form of 'ancestor' is 'ancestral'.
chunks.source: The adjective form of 'ancestor' is 'ancestral'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: John's ___ took place in the village. (marry) A: marriage. The noun form of 'marry' is 'marriage'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'marry' is 'marriage'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The bride was putting on a golden ___ ring. (engage) A: engagement. The noun form of 'engage' is 'engagement'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'engage' is 'engagement'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The bride was smartly dressed in her ___ gown. (bride) A: bridal. The adjective form of 'bride' is 'bridal'.
chunks.source: The adjective form of 'bride' is 'bridal'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We should be ___ to the orphans. (sympathy) A: sympathetic. The adjective form of 'sympathy' is 'sympathetic'.
chunks.source: The adjective form of 'sympathy' is 'sympathetic'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: People attending the burial were rowdy. ___ A: mourners. People attending a burial are 'mourners'.
chunks.source: People attending a burial are 'mourners'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: The box for carrying a dead body was very expensive. ___ A: coffin. A box for a dead body is a 'coffin'.
chunks.source: A box for a dead body is a 'coffin'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: The man who is marrying looks smart. ___ A: bridegroom. A man who is marrying is the 'bridegroom'.
chunks.source: A man who is marrying is the 'bridegroom'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: The wife and husband walked gently to the altar. ___ A: couple. 'The wife and husband' are a 'couple'.
chunks.source: 'The wife and husband' are a 'couple'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: Kadoma was the person who succeeded the late Kasolo. ___ A: heir. A person who succeeds another is the 'heir'.
chunks.source: A person who succeeds another is the 'heir'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: The children who lost their parents need special care. ___ A: orphans. Children who lost their parents are 'orphans'.
chunks.source: Children who lost their parents are 'orphans'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for the underlined words: The brides were holding a beautiful collection of flowers. ___ A: bouquets. Collections of flowers are 'bouquets'.
chunks.source: Collections of flowers are 'bouquets'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence using 'salon' to show its meaning. ___ A: She works in a hair salon in town.. 'Salon' is a place for hair and beauty care.
chunks.source: 'Salon' is a place for hair and beauty care.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence using 'saloon' to show its meaning. ___ A: He bought a new saloon car.. 'Saloon' is a type of car.
chunks.source: 'Saloon' is a type of car.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: bridesmaid ___ A: best man. The male counterpart of a 'bridesmaid' is the 'best man'.
chunks.source: The male counterpart of a 'bridesmaid' is the 'best man'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: bride ___ A: bridegroom. The male form of 'bride' is 'bridegroom'.
chunks.source: The male form of 'bride' is 'bridegroom'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: heir ___ A: heiress. The female form of 'heir' is 'heiress'.
chunks.source: The female form of 'heir' is 'heiress'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: widow ___ A: widower. The male form of 'widow' is 'widower'.
chunks.source: The male form of 'widow' is 'widower'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of: monogamy ___ A: polygamy. The opposite of 'monogamy' is 'polygamy'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'monogamy' is 'polygamy'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The President attended the wedding. The Prime Minister attended the wedding. (Join using: Both ___)  A: Both the President and the Prime Minister attended the wedding.. Join with 'Both… and…'.
chunks.source: Join with 'Both… and…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The bride does not have a job. The groom does not have a job. (Re-write using: Neither ___)  A: Neither the bride nor the groom has a job.. Join two negatives with 'Neither… nor…'.
chunks.source: Join two negatives with 'Neither… nor…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I don't often dream about dead bodies. (Re-write using: …seldom ___)  A: I seldom dream about dead bodies.. 'Don't often' becomes 'seldom'.
chunks.source: 'Don't often' becomes 'seldom'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The food was cold. The guests enjoyed the food. (Begin: Despite ___)  A: Despite the cold food, the guests enjoyed it.. 'Despite' + noun phrase.
chunks.source: 'Despite' + noun phrase.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The bridegroom will arrive after the guests have had lunch. (Re-write using: …by the time ___)  A: By the time the guests have had lunch, the bridegroom will have arrived.. 'After' becomes 'By the time' + future perfect.
chunks.source: 'After' becomes 'By the time' + future perfect.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He realised his mistake after he had offended his wife several times. (Begin: By the ___)  A: By the time he realised his mistake, he had offended his wife several times.. 'After' becomes 'By the time'.
chunks.source: 'After' becomes 'By the time'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: There were a few cakes in the box. (Use: …hardly ___)  A: There were hardly any cakes in the box.. 'A few' becomes 'hardly any'.
chunks.source: 'A few' becomes 'hardly any'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The girls were working ___ in the kitchen. (noise) A: noisily. The adverb form of 'noise' is 'noisily'.
chunks.source: The adverb form of 'noise' is 'noisily'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rubogo walks ___ than Rubulwa. (hurry) A: more hurriedly. The comparative adverb is 'more hurriedly'.
chunks.source: The comparative adverb is 'more hurriedly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The lazy girl left the room ___ as the teacher was busy writing. (stealthy) A: stealthily. The adverb form of 'stealthy' is 'stealthily'.
chunks.source: The adverb form of 'stealthy' is 'stealthily'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Namususwa played ___ and scored a goal. (active) A: actively. The adverb form of 'active' is 'actively'.
chunks.source: The adverb form of 'active' is 'actively'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She goes to the market ___ a week. (two) A: twice. 'Two' as an adverb of frequency is 'twice'.
chunks.source: 'Two' as an adverb of frequency is 'twice'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Maradona ___ scored the goal. (skill) A: skillfully. The adverb form of 'skill' is 'skillfully'.
chunks.source: The adverb form of 'skill' is 'skillfully'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Balinda sat ___ in an arm chair as if he was a king. (comfortable) A: comfortably. The adverb form of 'comfortable' is 'comfortably'.
chunks.source: The adverb form of 'comfortable' is 'comfortably'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: Nakawuka failed the test because she did it proudly. ___ A: humbly. The opposite of 'proudly' is 'humbly'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'proudly' is 'humbly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: The man beat his daughter mercifully. ___ A: mercilessly. The opposite of 'mercifully' is 'mercilessly'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'mercifully' is 'mercilessly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: We could not hear because he spoke softly. ___ A: loudly. The opposite of 'softly' is 'loudly'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'softly' is 'loudly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: All the children did the exercise badly. ___ A: well. The opposite of 'badly' is 'well'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'badly' is 'well'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: The police saluted respectfully as the president passed. ___ A: disrespectfully. The opposite of 'respectfully' is 'disrespectfully'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'respectfully' is 'disrespectfully'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write using the correct adverb order: The minister went (to Mbale, yesterday, hurriedly). ___ A: The minister went hurriedly to Mbale yesterday.. Adverb order: manner, place, time.
chunks.source: Adverb order: manner, place, time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write using the correct adverb order: The school choir sang (at the party, nicely, last week). ___ A: The school choir sang nicely at the party last week.. Adverb order: manner, place, time.
chunks.source: Adverb order: manner, place, time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Re-write using the correct adverb order: The teachers walked (to school, last evening, slowly). ___ A: The teachers walked slowly to school last evening.. Adverb order: manner, place, time.
chunks.source: Adverb order: manner, place, time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The Deputy spoke with confidence. (Give one word for: 'with confidence' ___) A: confidently. 'With confidence' = 'confidently'.
chunks.source: 'With confidence' = 'confidently'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The worriers fought without aim. (Give one word for: 'without aim' ___) A: aimlessly. 'Without aim' = 'aimlessly'.
chunks.source: 'Without aim' = 'aimlessly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: All of a sudden, she gave birth. (Give one word for: 'All of a sudden' ___) A: suddenly. 'All of a sudden' = 'suddenly'.
chunks.source: 'All of a sudden' = 'suddenly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The soldiers fought like heroes. (Give one word for: 'like heroes' ___) A: heroically. 'Like heroes' = 'heroically'.
chunks.source: 'Like heroes' = 'heroically'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We welcomed her mother by cheering. (Give one word for: 'by cheering' ___) A: cheerfully. 'By cheering' = 'cheerfully'.
chunks.source: 'By cheering' = 'cheerfully'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The exercise was ___ hard for us to do. A: too. The pattern is 'too + adjective + to'.
chunks.source: The pattern is 'too + adjective + to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He has ___ money to buy an aeroplane. A: enough. The pattern is 'enough + noun + to'.
chunks.source: The pattern is 'enough + noun + to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: James was ___ tired that he could not speak. A: so. The pattern is 'so + adjective + that'.
chunks.source: The pattern is 'so + adjective + that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: She was ___ a clever teacher that she came early. A: such. The pattern is 'such + a/an + adjective + noun + that'.
chunks.source: The pattern is 'such + a/an + adjective + noun + that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The head monitor came early ___ to sweep the classroom. A: enough. The pattern is 'adjective + enough + to'.
chunks.source: The pattern is 'adjective + enough + to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The children woke up early ___ they could complete their homework. A: so that. The purpose pattern is 'so that'.
chunks.source: The purpose pattern is 'so that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They cleared the garden ___ to plant crops. A: in order. The purpose pattern is 'in order to'.
chunks.source: The purpose pattern is 'in order to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He was very intelligent. He got a bursary from the district. (Join using: such a …that ___)  A: He was such an intelligent boy that he got a bursary from the district.. Use 'such a/an + adjective + noun + that'.
chunks.source: Use 'such a/an + adjective + noun + that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The train was not very fast. It did not reach the town in time. (Use: …too…to ___)  A: The train was too slow to reach the town in time.. 'Not very fast' becomes 'too slow to'.
chunks.source: 'Not very fast' becomes 'too slow to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: This song is very interesting. I can't stop listening to it. (Join using: …so…that ___)  A: This song is so interesting that I can't stop listening to it.. Join with 'so + adjective + that'.
chunks.source: Join with 'so + adjective + that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The chief will buy a bicycle next year. He is saving money this year. (Join using: …so as ___)  A: The chief is saving money this year so as to buy a bicycle next year.. Show purpose with 'so as to'.
chunks.source: Show purpose with 'so as to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mustafa went to Japan. He wanted to buy a new car. (Begin: In order to ___)  A: In order to buy a new car, Mustafa went to Japan.. Show purpose with 'In order to'.
chunks.source: Show purpose with 'In order to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He works hard. He wants to pass exams. (Use: …such that ___)  A: He works hard such that he will pass exams.. Show result with 'such that'.
chunks.source: Show result with 'such that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Amanda speaks English all the time. She wants to become perfect. (Re-write using: …in order that ___)  A: Amanda speaks English all the time in order that she becomes perfect.. Show purpose with 'in order that'.
chunks.source: Show purpose with 'in order that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The book ___ is lying on the table is mine. A: which. 'Which' is used for things.
chunks.source: 'Which' is used for things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The boy ___ was knocked down by a lorry is now in hospital. A: who. 'Who' is used for people.
chunks.source: 'Who' is used for people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The girl to ___ the minister gave the prize was in P.7. A: whom. After a preposition we use 'whom'.
chunks.source: After a preposition we use 'whom'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The woman ___ car broke down walked to town. A: whose. 'Whose' shows possession.
chunks.source: 'Whose' shows possession.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The joke at ___ I laughed was rather silly. A: which. After a preposition for things we use 'which'.
chunks.source: After a preposition for things we use 'which'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I haven't seen the boy ___ suitcase was stolen. A: whose. 'Whose' shows possession.
chunks.source: 'Whose' shows possession.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Musiime, ___ became the head prefect, made serious campaigns. A: who. 'Who' is used for people.
chunks.source: 'Who' is used for people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Opio's brother is a Minister. Opio is a kind man. (Join using: …whose ___)  A: Opio, whose brother is a Minister, is a kind man.. Join with 'whose' for possession.
chunks.source: Join with 'whose' for possession.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Karim won the independence rally. Karim is my uncle. (Re-write using: …who ___)  A: Karim, who won the independence rally, is my uncle.. Join with 'who' for people.
chunks.source: Join with 'who' for people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I joined this school with a boy. The boy has run mad. (Join using: …whom ___)  A: The boy with whom I joined this school has run mad.. After a preposition we use 'whom'.
chunks.source: After a preposition we use 'whom'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The car belongs to my friend. It got an accident. (Re-write using: …which ___)  A: The car, which belongs to my friend, got an accident.. Join with 'which' for things.
chunks.source: Join with 'which' for things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: This is the place. The orphans stay here. (Join using: …where ___)  A: This is the place where the orphans stay.. Join with 'where' for places.
chunks.source: Join with 'where' for places.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Joan is the girl. I gave her my book. (Re-write using: …whom ___)  A: Joan is the girl to whom I gave my book.. After a preposition we use 'whom'.
chunks.source: After a preposition we use 'whom'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He bought the furniture last week. It is already broken. (Join using: …that ___)  A: The furniture that he bought last week is already broken.. Join with 'that'.
chunks.source: Join with 'that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He is a famous leader about whom many books have been written. (Write as two separate sentences. ___)  A: He is a famous leader. Many books have been written about him.. Split the relative clause into its own sentence.
chunks.source: Split the relative clause into its own sentence.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Jane said that she was going to sweep the room then. (Begin: Jane said, "___")  A: Jane said, "I am going to sweep the room now.". In direct speech: 'she' → 'I', 'was' → 'am', 'then' → 'now'.
chunks.source: In direct speech: 'she' → 'I', 'was' → 'am', 'then' → 'now'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: "Why were you late last week?" the teacher asked Sandra. (Re-write using: …wanted to know ___)  A: The teacher wanted to know why Sandra had been late the previous week.. In reported speech: past simple → past perfect, 'last week' → 'the previous week'.
chunks.source: In reported speech: past simple → past perfect, 'last week' → 'the previous week'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why asked the stranger are you against me (Re-write and punctuate the sentence correctly. ___)  A: "Why are you against me?" asked the stranger.. Direct speech needs quotation marks and a question mark.
chunks.source: Direct speech needs quotation marks and a question mark.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: "Judith, go and see the doctor," said my uncle. (Begin: My uncle told ___)  A: My uncle told Judith to go and see the doctor.. A command becomes 'told + person + to + verb'.
chunks.source: A command becomes 'told + person + to + verb'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: "I wrote this letter myself," said Joshua. (Begin: Joshua said ___)  A: Joshua said that he had written that letter himself.. In reported speech: 'wrote' → 'had written', 'this' → 'that'.
chunks.source: In reported speech: 'wrote' → 'had written', 'this' → 'that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The teacher told the pupils to keep quiet. (Rewrite in direct speech: ___)  A: The teacher said, "Keep quiet.". A reported command becomes direct: 'Keep quiet.'
chunks.source: A reported command becomes direct: 'Keep quiet.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: "Are you the boy who won a scholarship?" asked the DEO. (Begin: The DEO asked ___)  A: The DEO asked whether I was the boy who had won a scholarship.. A yes/no question becomes 'asked whether/if' with past tenses.
chunks.source: A yes/no question becomes 'asked whether/if' with past tenses.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: "I will donate money to the poor," said the Minister. (Re-write beginning: The minister said ___)  A: The minister said that he would donate money to the poor.. In reported speech: 'will' → 'would'.
chunks.source: In reported speech: 'will' → 'would'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The man said, "I am sick today." (Write into reported speech: ___)  A: The man said that he was sick that day.. In reported speech: 'am' → 'was', 'today' → 'that day'.
chunks.source: In reported speech: 'am' → 'was', 'today' → 'that day'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: "They are going to Entebbe now," said the girl. (Begin: The girl ___)  A: The girl said that they were going to Entebbe then.. In reported speech: 'are' → 'were', 'now' → 'then'.
chunks.source: In reported speech: 'are' → 'were', 'now' → 'then'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: It was not necessary for the headmaster to come. (Re-write using: …needn't have ___)  A: The headmaster needn't have come.. 'It was not necessary to come' = 'needn't have come'.
chunks.source: 'It was not necessary to come' = 'needn't have come'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You needn't worry about the sickness of your brother. (Use: …necessary ___)  A: It is not necessary for you to worry about the sickness of your brother.. 'Needn't' becomes 'it is not necessary'.
chunks.source: 'Needn't' becomes 'it is not necessary'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Lwere must repeat P.7 if he is to pass the exams. (Re-write using: …will have ___)  A: Lwere will have to repeat P.7 if he is to pass the exams.. 'Must' becomes 'will have to'.
chunks.source: 'Must' becomes 'will have to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: It was not necessary for Lobojo to return to the teacher. (Use: …didn't have ___)  A: Lobojo didn't have to return to the teacher.. 'It was not necessary' becomes 'didn't have to'.
chunks.source: 'It was not necessary' becomes 'didn't have to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The lazy boy must go to school. (Use: …had to ___)  A: The lazy boy had to go to school.. 'Must' in the past becomes 'had to'.
chunks.source: 'Must' in the past becomes 'had to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: There is no need for the boys to water the flowers. (Re-write using: …needn't ___)  A: The boys needn't water the flowers.. 'There is no need' becomes 'needn't'.
chunks.source: 'There is no need' becomes 'needn't'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: School children needn't have reached school late. (Use: …didn't need ___)  A: School children didn't need to reach school late.. 'Needn't have' becomes 'didn't need to'.
chunks.source: 'Needn't have' becomes 'didn't need to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You don't need to repeat the exercise. (Begin: There is ___)  A: There is no need to repeat the exercise.. 'Don't need to' becomes 'There is no need to'.
chunks.source: 'Don't need to' becomes 'There is no need to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He is to eat all the stale food. (Write into past tense: ___)  A: He was to eat all the stale food.. Change 'is to' to 'was to' in the past.
chunks.source: Change 'is to' to 'was to' in the past.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We should go to church every Sunday. (Re-write using: …ought ___)  A: We ought to go to church every Sunday.. 'Should' becomes 'ought to'.
chunks.source: 'Should' becomes 'ought to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: There was no need for him to go away but all the same he went. (Use: …needn't ___)  A: He needn't have gone away but all the same he went.. 'There was no need' (past) becomes 'needn't have'.
chunks.source: 'There was no need' (past) becomes 'needn't have'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You needn't feed the baby because it is satisfied. (Re-write using: …unnecessary ___)  A: It is unnecessary for you to feed the baby because it is satisfied.. 'Needn't' becomes 'it is unnecessary'.
chunks.source: 'Needn't' becomes 'it is unnecessary'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The pupils stood up immediately they saw the class teacher. (Begin: As soon as ___)  A: As soon as the pupils saw the class teacher, they stood up.. 'Immediately' becomes 'As soon as'.
chunks.source: 'Immediately' becomes 'As soon as'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Immediately I reached school, it started raining. (Begin: No sooner ___)  A: No sooner had I reached school than it started raining.. 'Immediately' becomes 'No sooner had… than…'.
chunks.source: 'Immediately' becomes 'No sooner had… than…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They had just passed the spot when a grenade exploded. (Re-write using: Hardly ___)  A: Hardly had they passed the spot when a grenade exploded.. 'Had just… when' becomes 'Hardly had… when…'.
chunks.source: 'Had just… when' becomes 'Hardly had… when…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He ran away when his father came back. (Re-write using: Hardly ___)  A: Hardly had his father come back when he ran away.. 'When' becomes 'Hardly had… when…'.
chunks.source: 'When' becomes 'Hardly had… when…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: No sooner had Grace reached home than he begun abusing the maid. (Begin: Immediately ___)  A: Immediately Grace reached home, he begun abusing the maid.. 'No sooner had… than' becomes 'Immediately'.
chunks.source: 'No sooner had… than' becomes 'Immediately'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Having sung the song, the choir left the stage. (Re-write using: …as soon as ___)  A: As soon as the choir had sung the song, they left the stage.. 'Having sung' becomes 'As soon as… had sung'.
chunks.source: 'Having sung' becomes 'As soon as… had sung'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He entered the courtroom. He said his prayer before he entered. (Begin: By the time ___)  A: By the time he entered the courtroom, he had said his prayer.. The earlier action uses the past perfect.
chunks.source: The earlier action uses the past perfect.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Aisha will go away before Mary returns from school. (Re-write using: …by the time ___)  A: By the time Mary returns from school, Aisha will have gone away.. Use 'By the time' with the future perfect.
chunks.source: Use 'By the time' with the future perfect.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He removed his shoes before he entered the mosque. (Use: …after ___)  A: He entered the mosque after he had removed his shoes.. 'Before' becomes 'after' with reversed order.
chunks.source: 'Before' becomes 'after' with reversed order.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He said a prayer before entering the court-room. (Begin: After ___)  A: After saying a prayer, he entered the court-room.. 'Before entering' becomes 'After saying' with reversed order.
chunks.source: 'Before entering' becomes 'After saying' with reversed order.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We ate supper after saying the Lord's Prayer. (Re-write using: …before ___)  A: We said the Lord's Prayer before eating supper.. 'After' becomes 'before' with reversed order.
chunks.source: 'After' becomes 'before' with reversed order.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: It started raining at midday. It is still raining. (Re-write using: …since ___)  A: It has been raining since midday.. Use the present perfect continuous with 'since'.
chunks.source: Use the present perfect continuous with 'since'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He has not seen his cousin for one year. (Re-write and end: …ago. ___)  A: He last saw his cousin one year ago.. 'Has not seen for one year' becomes 'last saw… ago'.
chunks.source: 'Has not seen for one year' becomes 'last saw… ago'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I have not met my aunt for two years now. (Begin: It is ___)  A: It is two years since I met my aunt.. Use 'It is + time + since'.
chunks.source: Use 'It is + time + since'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They met each other two weeks ago. (Use: …for ___)  A: They have not met each other for two weeks.. 'Two weeks ago' becomes 'for two weeks' with the present perfect negative.
chunks.source: 'Two weeks ago' becomes 'for two weeks' with the present perfect negative.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Achieng will reach Tororo before sunset. (Begin: By sunset ___)  A: By sunset, Achieng will have reached Tororo.. Use 'By sunset' with the future perfect.
chunks.source: Use 'By sunset' with the future perfect.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The police came but the money had been already stolen. (Re-write using: …by the ___)  A: By the time the police came, the money had already been stolen.. Use 'By the time' with the past perfect.
chunks.source: Use 'By the time' with the past perfect.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The pupils stood up immediately they saw the headteacher. (Re-write using: …as soon ___)  A: As soon as the pupils saw the headteacher, they stood up.. 'Immediately' becomes 'As soon as'.
chunks.source: 'Immediately' becomes 'As soon as'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: As soon as the teacher reached school, the headmaster called them to his office. (Use: …no sooner ___)  A: No sooner had the teacher reached school than the headmaster called them to his office.. 'As soon as' becomes 'No sooner had… than…'.
chunks.source: 'As soon as' becomes 'No sooner had… than…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Kamagu went to bed immediately he felt sleepy. (Re-write beginning: Hardly ___)  A: Hardly had Kamagu felt sleepy when he went to bed.. 'Immediately' becomes 'Hardly had… when…'.
chunks.source: 'Immediately' becomes 'Hardly had… when…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The moment Kula heard the bell, he stopped writing. (Re-write using: Scarcely ___)  A: Scarcely had Kula heard the bell when he stopped writing.. 'The moment' becomes 'Scarcely had… when…'.
chunks.source: 'The moment' becomes 'Scarcely had… when…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Having sung the welcome song, the choir left the stage. (Begin: Immediately ___)  A: Immediately the choir had sung the welcome song, they left the stage.. 'Having sung' becomes 'Immediately… had sung'.
chunks.source: 'Having sung' becomes 'Immediately… had sung'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Everybody stood up as soon as the chief guest arrived. (Re-write beginning: Barely ___)  A: Barely had the chief guest arrived when everybody stood up.. 'As soon as' becomes 'Barely had… when…'.
chunks.source: 'As soon as' becomes 'Barely had… when…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I will go away before the aeroplane lands. (Re-write beginning: By the time ___)  A: By the time the aeroplane lands, I will have gone away.. Use 'By the time' with the future perfect.
chunks.source: Use 'By the time' with the future perfect.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Paul passed the examination yet he was not clever. (Begin: Although ___)  A: Although Paul was not clever, he passed the examination.. 'Yet' becomes 'Although'.
chunks.source: 'Yet' becomes 'Although'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Kamau is a rich man but he doesn't send his children to school. (Re-write using: …in spite ___)  A: In spite of being a rich man, Kamau doesn't send his children to school.. 'But' becomes 'In spite of' + -ing.
chunks.source: 'But' becomes 'In spite of' + -ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The food was very delicious. Nobody ate it. (Re-write beginning: Eventhough ___)  A: Eventhough the food was very delicious, nobody ate it.. Join contrasting sentences with 'Eventhough'.
chunks.source: Join contrasting sentences with 'Eventhough'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Ritah is lame but she runs very fast. (Use: …despite ___)  A: Despite being lame, Ritah runs very fast.. 'But' becomes 'Despite' + -ing.
chunks.source: 'But' becomes 'Despite' + -ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Although the teacher taught very well, I didn't understand. (Re-write using: …but ___)  A: The teacher taught very well but I didn't understand.. 'Although' becomes 'but'.
chunks.source: 'Although' becomes 'but'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Namale writes very fast. She doesn't make mistakes. (Begin: However ___)  A: Namale writes very fast; however, she doesn't make mistakes.. Join contrasting sentences with 'however'.
chunks.source: Join contrasting sentences with 'however'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He is very clever but he failed the test. (Begin: Clever ___)  A: Clever as he is, he failed the test.. Use the pattern 'adjective + as + subject + verb'.
chunks.source: Use the pattern 'adjective + as + subject + verb'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I don't admire her though she is beautiful. (Use: …nevertheless ___)  A: She is beautiful; nevertheless, I don't admire her.. 'Though' becomes 'nevertheless'.
chunks.source: 'Though' becomes 'nevertheless'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The old man had a fractured leg but he continued with the journey. (Use: …although ___)  A: Although the old man had a fractured leg, he continued with the journey.. 'But' becomes 'Although'.
chunks.source: 'But' becomes 'Although'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Joyce was sick but she went to school. (Re-write beginning: In spite of ___)  A: In spite of being sick, Joyce went to school.. 'But' becomes 'In spite of' + -ing.
chunks.source: 'But' becomes 'In spite of' + -ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: John slapped the boy. John kicked the boy. (Begin: Not only ___)  A: Not only did John slap the boy, but he also kicked him.. Use 'Not only did… but also'.
chunks.source: Use 'Not only did… but also'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Racheal is sitting for exams. Edson is also sitting for exams. (Re-write beginning: Both ___)  A: Both Racheal and Edson are sitting for exams.. Join with 'Both… and…'.
chunks.source: Join with 'Both… and…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The cow doesn't eat bones. The goat doesn't eat bones. (Re-write using: Neither ___)  A: Neither the cow nor the goat eats bones.. Join two negatives with 'Neither… nor…'.
chunks.source: Join two negatives with 'Neither… nor…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rose enjoys reading novels. Rose enjoys reading magazines. (Join using: …either…or ___)  A: Rose enjoys reading either novels or magazines.. Join with 'either… or…'.
chunks.source: Join with 'either… or…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I can write well using both hands. (Re-write using: …either ___)  A: I can write well using either hand.. 'Both hands' becomes 'either hand'.
chunks.source: 'Both hands' becomes 'either hand'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My grandfather couldn't write. He couldn't read. (Re-write using: …neither ___)  A: My grandfather could neither write nor read.. Join two negatives with 'neither… nor…'.
chunks.source: Join two negatives with 'neither… nor…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Edson is good at dancing. Edson is good at singing. (Join using: …both ___)  A: Edson is good at both dancing and singing.. Join with 'both… and…'.
chunks.source: Join with 'both… and…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Tang doesn't speak well. Moro doesn't speak well. (Join using: …and neither ___)  A: Tang doesn't speak well, and neither does Moro.. Add 'and neither does' for agreement.
chunks.source: Add 'and neither does' for agreement.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Pamella performed well. Rebecca also performed well. (Join using: …and so ___)  A: Pamella performed well, and so did Rebecca.. Add 'and so did' for agreement.
chunks.source: Add 'and so did' for agreement.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mondo is likely to have stolen the teacher's money. Melabu is likely to have stolen the teacher's money. (Begin: Either ___)  A: Either Mondo or Melabu is likely to have stolen the teacher's money.. Join with 'Either… or…'.
chunks.source: Join with 'Either… or…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Ssozi may go to the zoo. Sarah may go to the zoo. (Begin: Either ___)  A: Either Ssozi or Sarah may go to the zoo.. Join with 'Either… or…'.
chunks.source: Join with 'Either… or…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Neither Mary nor Tom arrived late for the morning lessons. (Begin: Both ___)  A: Both Mary and Tom arrived in time for the morning lessons.. 'Neither… arrived late' means both arrived in time.
chunks.source: 'Neither… arrived late' means both arrived in time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Cows provide people with milk. Goats provide people with milk. (Re-write using: …as well as ___)  A: Cows as well as goats provide people with milk.. Join with 'as well as'.
chunks.source: Join with 'as well as'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Both Hassan and Tonny don't eat mutton. (Use: Neither ___)  A: Neither Hassan nor Tonny eats mutton.. 'Both… don't' becomes 'Neither… nor…'.
chunks.source: 'Both… don't' becomes 'Neither… nor…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mark swept the classroom. Mark mopped the classroom. (Begin: Not only ___)  A: Not only did Mark sweep the classroom, but he also mopped it.. Use 'Not only did… but also'.
chunks.source: Use 'Not only did… but also'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Sharon will eat the pancake. Sharon will eat the doughnut. (Join using: …either…or ___)  A: Sharon will eat either the pancake or the doughnut.. Join with 'either… or…'.
chunks.source: Join with 'either… or…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We sell second hand vehicles in our shop. We sell spare parts in our shop. (Re-write using: …as well as ___)  A: We sell second hand vehicles as well as spare parts in our shop.. Join with 'as well as'.
chunks.source: Join with 'as well as'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I like eating cabbage more than Sukuma wiki. (Use: …prefer ___)  A: I prefer eating cabbage to Sukuma wiki.. 'Like… more than' becomes 'prefer… to…'.
chunks.source: 'Like… more than' becomes 'prefer… to…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The old man is very weak. He cannot walk thirty kilometres. (Join using: …too…to ___)  A: The old man is too weak to walk thirty kilometres.. Join with 'too + adjective + to'.
chunks.source: Join with 'too + adjective + to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Amina is very lazy. Amina cannot do the work. (Re-write using: …so…that ___)  A: Amina is so lazy that she cannot do the work.. Join with 'so + adjective + that'.
chunks.source: Join with 'so + adjective + that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The water was very deep. We could not swim in it. (Join using: …enough to ___)  A: The water was not shallow enough for us to swim in.. 'Very deep' (cannot swim) becomes 'not shallow enough to swim in'.
chunks.source: 'Very deep' (cannot swim) becomes 'not shallow enough to swim in'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The compound is very large. It can accommodate a hundred celebrants. (Join using: …such…that ___)  A: It is such a large compound that it can accommodate a hundred celebrants.. Join with 'such a + adjective + noun + that'.
chunks.source: Join with 'such a + adjective + noun + that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The letter was read to him. The letter was translated to him. (Use: …not only ___)  A: The letter was not only read to him but also translated.. Use 'not only… but also'.
chunks.source: Use 'not only… but also'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Deborah has ear-rings on both ears. (Re-write using: …either ___)  A: Deborah has ear-rings on either ear.. 'Both ears' becomes 'either ear'.
chunks.source: 'Both ears' becomes 'either ear'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You and I will slash the compound tomorrow. (Re-write beginning: Both ___)  A: Both you and I will slash the compound tomorrow.. Join with 'Both… and…'.
chunks.source: Join with 'Both… and…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Both Hellen and Samson are clever. (Use: …as well as ___)  A: Hellen as well as Samson is clever.. 'Both… and' becomes 'as well as' (verb agrees with the first subject).
chunks.source: 'Both… and' becomes 'as well as' (verb agrees with the first subject).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If our team ___ the match next week, we would be the champions. (win) A: won. Second conditional: 'If our team won…, we would be…'.
chunks.source: Second conditional: 'If our team won…, we would be…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The Minister ___ our school if the headteacher invites her. (visit) A: will visit. First conditional: 'if… invites…, will visit'.
chunks.source: First conditional: 'if… invites…, will visit'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The accident ___ if the driver had been careful. (not to happen) A: would not have happened. Third conditional: 'would not have happened'.
chunks.source: Third conditional: 'would not have happened'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He will go shopping if he ___ the money. (get) A: gets. First conditional: 'if he gets…'.
chunks.source: First conditional: 'if he gets…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Paul would not ask us if he ___ the answer. (know) A: knew. Second conditional: 'if he knew…'.
chunks.source: Second conditional: 'if he knew…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If you had gone to school, you ___ the magician. (to see) A: would have seen. Third conditional: 'would have seen'.
chunks.source: Third conditional: 'would have seen'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Unless he wakes up early, he ___ the bus. (find) A: will not find. 'Unless… wakes' means if he does not wake early, he will not find the bus.
chunks.source: 'Unless… wakes' means if he does not wake early, he will not find the bus.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He will buy a car only if he ___ hard. (work) A: works. First conditional: 'if he works…'.
chunks.source: First conditional: 'if he works…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Konde would be surprised if he ___ Okitui next year. (meet) A: met. Second conditional: 'if he met…'.
chunks.source: Second conditional: 'if he met…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We would have been happy if our teacher ___ the race. (to win) A: had won. Third conditional: 'if… had won…'.
chunks.source: Third conditional: 'if… had won…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If she becomes happy, she will dance for us. (Use: …unless ___)  A: Unless she becomes happy, she will not dance for us.. 'If' becomes 'unless' with a negative main clause.
chunks.source: 'If' becomes 'unless' with a negative main clause.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If you don't write well, you will fail this paper. (Re-write using: …or else ___)  A: Write well or else you will fail this paper.. 'If you don't…' becomes a command + 'or else'.
chunks.source: 'If you don't…' becomes a command + 'or else'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If I visit Kidepo National Park, I will see many crocodiles. (Begin: If I had ___)  A: If I had visited Kidepo National Park, I would have seen many crocodiles.. First conditional becomes third conditional.
chunks.source: First conditional becomes third conditional.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The Education Manager won't visit our school unless he gets a vehicle. (Re-write using: …only if ___)  A: The Education Manager will visit our school only if he gets a vehicle.. 'Won't… unless' becomes 'will… only if'.
chunks.source: 'Won't… unless' becomes 'will… only if'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I will come with you to Apac if you invite me. (Re-write using: …would ___)  A: I would come with you to Apac if you invited me.. First conditional becomes second conditional.
chunks.source: First conditional becomes second conditional.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Unless you listen attentively, you won't get the teacher's explanation. (Begin: If ___)  A: If you don't listen attentively, you won't get the teacher's explanation.. 'Unless' becomes 'if… don't'.
chunks.source: 'Unless' becomes 'if… don't'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If I get time, I shall pay you a visit. (Re-write using: …when ___)  A: When I get time, I shall pay you a visit.. 'If' (condition) can become 'when' (time).
chunks.source: 'If' (condition) can become 'when' (time).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The teacher did not see the boy. He did not punish him. (Begin: If the teacher ___)  A: If the teacher had seen the boy, he would have punished him.. Two past negatives become a third conditional.
chunks.source: Two past negatives become a third conditional.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I would have made a mistake if the matron hadn't warned me. (Write as two separate sentences: ___)  A: I would have made a mistake. The matron warned me.. Split into two sentences: the result and the condition.
chunks.source: Split into two sentences: the result and the condition.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The teacher will come in time. He will give us a test. (Re-write beginning: If ___)  A: If the teacher comes in time, he will give us a test.. Join as a first conditional.
chunks.source: Join as a first conditional.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If the teacher ___ seen me, he would have punished me. A: had. Third conditional: 'If the teacher had seen…'.
chunks.source: Third conditional: 'If the teacher had seen…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ___ you revise hard, you will not get good marks. A: Unless. 'Unless you revise…' means 'if you do not revise…'.
chunks.source: 'Unless you revise…' means 'if you do not revise…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If we went to school late, we ___ find the gate closed. A: would. Second conditional: '…we would find…'.
chunks.source: Second conditional: '…we would find…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They will get good marks ___ they write well. A: if. First conditional: '…if they write well'.
chunks.source: First conditional: '…if they write well'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You should wake up early ___ you won't find the bus. A: or else. 'Or else' warns of a bad result.
chunks.source: 'Or else' warns of a bad result.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If the driver had been careful, the accident ___ happened. A: would not have. Third conditional: 'would not have happened'.
chunks.source: Third conditional: 'would not have happened'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If it rains, we shall plough our garden. (Re-write using: …rained ___)  A: If it rained, we would plough our garden.. First conditional becomes second conditional.
chunks.source: First conditional becomes second conditional.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Candidates have to work hard in order to pass P.L.E. (Begin: Unless ___)  A: Unless candidates work hard, they will not pass P.L.E.. 'Have to' becomes 'unless… will not'.
chunks.source: 'Have to' becomes 'unless… will not'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If you don't come to school early, you will be punished. (Re-write using: …or else ___)  A: Come to school early or else you will be punished.. 'If you don't…' becomes a command + 'or else'.
chunks.source: 'If you don't…' becomes a command + 'or else'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I didn't buy a new pair of shoes. I didn't have enough money. (Join beginning: If ___)  A: If I had had enough money, I would have bought a new pair of shoes.. Two past negatives become a third conditional.
chunks.source: Two past negatives become a third conditional.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If Moses works hard, he will pass the examinations. (Use: …as long as ___)  A: Moses will pass the examinations as long as he works hard.. 'If' becomes 'as long as'.
chunks.source: 'If' becomes 'as long as'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Nekesa didn't change her behaviors. She didn't get a bursary. (Begin: Had ___)  A: Had Nekesa changed her behaviors, she would have got a bursary.. 'If… hadn't' becomes 'Had…'.
chunks.source: 'If… hadn't' becomes 'Had…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If she gets time, she will pay you a visit. (Use: …when ___)  A: When she gets time, she will pay you a visit.. 'If' becomes 'when'.
chunks.source: 'If' becomes 'when'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Jemba will not go abroad. He will get a passport first. (Re-write using: Unless ___)  A: Unless Jemba gets a passport, he will not go abroad.. 'Will not… first' becomes 'unless'.
chunks.source: 'Will not… first' becomes 'unless'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If the prefect had caught me, he would have reported me to the matron. (Write as two separate sentences: ___)  A: The prefect did not catch me. He did not report me to the matron.. Split into two sentences.
chunks.source: Split into two sentences.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If I am invited, I will attend the wedding. (Re-write using: …without ___)  A: Without an invitation, I will not attend the wedding.. 'If I am invited' becomes 'without an invitation' with a negative.
chunks.source: 'If I am invited' becomes 'without an invitation' with a negative.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: God will not exalt you if you don't humble yourself. (Re-write using: …only if ___)  A: God will exalt you only if you humble yourself.. 'Will not… if' becomes 'will… only if'.
chunks.source: 'Will not… if' becomes 'will… only if'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If you don't listen attentively, you won't get the teacher's explanation. (Re-write using: …would have ___)  A: If you had not listened attentively, you would not have got the teacher's explanation.. First conditional becomes third conditional.
chunks.source: First conditional becomes third conditional.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Willy is likely to cry if he fails the exams. (Re-write and end: …would cry. ___)  A: If Willy failed the exams, he would cry.. 'Is likely to' becomes the second conditional.
chunks.source: 'Is likely to' becomes the second conditional.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They will fail to understand the instructions unless they pay attention to their teachers. (Re-write using: …if ___)  A: They will fail to understand the instructions if they don't pay attention to their teachers.. 'Unless' becomes 'if… don't'.
chunks.source: 'Unless' becomes 'if… don't'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: To ___ teacher did you give your book? A: which. 'Which' is used for choice among teachers.
chunks.source: 'Which' is used for choice among teachers.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The dog ___ tail was cut off died in serious pain. A: whose. 'Whose' shows possession.
chunks.source: 'Whose' shows possession.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The soldier with ___ I went to Somalia was promoted immediately. A: whom. After a preposition we use 'whom'.
chunks.source: After a preposition we use 'whom'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The girl ___ performed very well was given a bursary. A: who. 'Who' is used for people.
chunks.source: 'Who' is used for people.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: One ought to respect ___ before others. A: oneself. The reflexive pronoun for 'one' is 'oneself'.
chunks.source: The reflexive pronoun for 'one' is 'oneself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He was punished because of ___ bad manners. (he) A: his. The possessive adjective for 'he' is 'his'.
chunks.source: The possessive adjective for 'he' is 'his'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A friend of ___ was given a prize. (they) A: theirs. After 'of' we use the possessive pronoun 'theirs'.
chunks.source: After 'of' we use the possessive pronoun 'theirs'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The book she took was not ___. (she) A: hers. The possessive pronoun for 'she' is 'hers'.
chunks.source: The possessive pronoun for 'she' is 'hers'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: "This pen is not ___, " he replied. (me) A: mine. The possessive pronoun for 'me' is 'mine'.
chunks.source: The possessive pronoun for 'me' is 'mine'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The teacher of ___ has graduated today. (we) A: ours. The possessive pronoun for 'we' is 'ours'.
chunks.source: The possessive pronoun for 'we' is 'ours'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mwidu is the owner of that car. (Re-write using: …belongs ___)  A: That car belongs to Mwidu.. 'Is the owner of' becomes 'belongs to'.
chunks.source: 'Is the owner of' becomes 'belongs to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Opondo's brother will visit us next week. (Re-write and begin: A brother of ___)  A: A brother of Opondo's will visit us next week.. 'Opondo's brother' becomes 'A brother of Opondo's'.
chunks.source: 'Opondo's brother' becomes 'A brother of Opondo's'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Majorie will come to our school tomorrow. You met her son yesterday. (Join using: …whose ___)  A: Majorie, whose son you met yesterday, will come to our school tomorrow.. Join with 'whose' for possession.
chunks.source: Join with 'whose' for possession.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Joyce Bond is a great musician. Many books have been written about her. (Re-write using: …whom ___)  A: Joyce Bond, about whom many books have been written, is a great musician.. Use 'about whom' for the relative clause.
chunks.source: Use 'about whom' for the relative clause.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Here comes the man. He married my sister. (Use: …who ___)  A: Here comes the man who married my sister.. Join with 'who'.
chunks.source: Join with 'who'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: That is the hospital. Kenzo was born in that hospital. (Join using: …which ___)  A: That is the hospital in which Kenzo was born.. Use 'in which' for the place.
chunks.source: Use 'in which' for the place.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: This is the month. James was born in this month. (Re-write using: …when ___)  A: This is the month when James was born.. Use 'when' for time.
chunks.source: Use 'when' for time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The girl to whom I gave my red pen has gone away. (Write as two separate sentences: ___)  A: I gave my red pen to the girl. The girl has gone away.. Split into two simple sentences.
chunks.source: Split into two simple sentences.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The man has been arrested. I saw him at the park. (Join using: …whom ___)  A: The man whom I saw at the park has been arrested.. Join with 'whom'.
chunks.source: Join with 'whom'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Football is their favourite game. (Re-write and end: …theirs. ___)  A: Football is the favourite game of theirs.. 'Their favourite game' becomes 'the favourite game of theirs'.
chunks.source: 'Their favourite game' becomes 'the favourite game of theirs'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You need to keep your bags by yourselves. (Begin: One ___)  A: One needs to keep one's bags by oneself.. 'You/your/yourselves' becomes 'one/one's/oneself'.
chunks.source: 'You/your/yourselves' becomes 'one/one's/oneself'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: To whom does that pen belong? (Re-write using: …owns ___)  A: Who owns that pen?. 'Belong to' becomes 'own'.
chunks.source: 'Belong to' becomes 'own'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The dog is chasing the thief. (Re-write beginning: The thief ___)  A: The thief is being chased by the dog.. Present continuous passive: 'is being chased'.
chunks.source: Present continuous passive: 'is being chased'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The teacher rides a new bicycle everyday. (Begin: A new bicycle ___)  A: A new bicycle is ridden by the teacher everyday.. Present simple passive: 'is ridden'.
chunks.source: Present simple passive: 'is ridden'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The bus is being surrounded by monkeys. (Re-write beginning: Monkeys ___)  A: Monkeys are surrounding the bus.. Passive to active in the present continuous.
chunks.source: Passive to active in the present continuous.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: My umbrella was blown off by a strong wind. (Re-write and end: …my umbrella. ___)  A: A strong wind blew off my umbrella.. Passive to active: 'blew off'.
chunks.source: Passive to active: 'blew off'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A lorry has knocked down my brother. (Re-write and end: …a lorry. ___)  A: My brother has been knocked down by a lorry.. Present perfect passive: 'has been knocked down'.
chunks.source: Present perfect passive: 'has been knocked down'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The headgirl will record the number of desks in the classroom. (Begin: The number ___)  A: The number of desks in the classroom will be recorded by the headgirl.. Future passive: 'will be recorded'.
chunks.source: Future passive: 'will be recorded'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Did Mary carry the text books? (Re-write beginning: Were ___)  A: Were the text books carried by Mary?. Past simple passive question: 'Were… carried?'.
chunks.source: Past simple passive question: 'Were… carried?'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The trip to the zoo was organised by the class teacher. (Re-write and end: …the trip to the zoo. ___)  A: The class teacher organised the trip to the zoo.. Passive to active: 'organised'.
