chunks.source: Passive to active: 'organised'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Bruno will be drawing pictures on the chalkboard. (Begin: Pictures ___)  A: Pictures will be being drawn by Bruno on the chalkboard.. Future continuous passive: 'will be being drawn'.
chunks.source: Future continuous passive: 'will be being drawn'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Several books have been written by Mr. Wavamunno. (Begin: Mr. Wavamunno ___)  A: Mr. Wavamunno has written several books.. Passive to active in the present perfect.
chunks.source: Passive to active in the present perfect.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: They will take care of you. (Begin: You will ___)  A: You will be taken care of by them.. Future passive with the phrasal verb 'take care of'.
chunks.source: Future passive with the phrasal verb 'take care of'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who abused our good friend? (Begin: By whom ___)  A: By whom was our good friend abused?. Passive question: 'By whom was… abused?'.
chunks.source: Passive question: 'By whom was… abused?'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Serena swept the dirty room. (Re-write and end: …Serena. ___)  A: The dirty room was swept by Serena.. Past simple passive: 'was swept'.
chunks.source: Past simple passive: 'was swept'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Juma brought a new Japanese car. (Re-write beginning: A new Japanese ___)  A: A new Japanese car was brought by Juma.. Past simple passive: 'was brought'.
chunks.source: Past simple passive: 'was brought'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Baskets are woven by Natalie. (Re-write and end: …baskets. ___)  A: Natalie weaves baskets.. Passive to active: 'weaves'.
chunks.source: Passive to active: 'weaves'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The pupils of Primary Seven ___ ready for their examinations. A: are. 'Pupils' is plural, so we use 'are'.
chunks.source: 'Pupils' is plural, so we use 'are'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Writing your work ___ ink makes it look neat. A: in. We write 'in ink'.
chunks.source: We write 'in ink'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: That is the farmer from ___ farm I bought a calf. A: whose. 'Whose' shows possession.
chunks.source: 'Whose' shows possession.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: ___ is the difference between these two books. A: What. We ask 'What is the difference…?'.
chunks.source: We ask 'What is the difference…?'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Kadoma and his sister ___ waste time telling stories, mustn't they? A: don't. The tag 'mustn't they?' follows a negative main clause with 'don't'.
chunks.source: The tag 'mustn't they?' follows a negative main clause with 'don't'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ___ box will be kept by the priest. (wood) A: wooden. The adjective form of 'wood' is 'wooden'.
chunks.source: The adjective form of 'wood' is 'wooden'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mukweje ___ his cousin for nothing last night. (beat) A: beat. 'Last night' needs the past simple; the past of 'beat' is 'beat'.
chunks.source: 'Last night' needs the past simple; the past of 'beat' is 'beat'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: One ___ has just boarded the bus to Mbale. (Congo) A: Congolese. A person from Congo is 'Congolese'.
chunks.source: A person from Congo is 'Congolese'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Having ___ this letter, you can now buy a postage stamp. (write) A: written. After 'having' we use the past participle: 'written'.
chunks.source: After 'having' we use the past participle: 'written'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The ___ man in the line did not get any food. (two) A: second. The ordinal of 'two' is 'second'.
chunks.source: The ordinal of 'two' is 'second'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We should get ready to meet the ___ Member of Parliament today. (honour) A: honourable. The adjective form of 'honour' is 'honourable'.
chunks.source: The adjective form of 'honour' is 'honourable'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Kendo was punished because of ___ to his mother. (lie) A: lying. After 'because of' we use the -ing form.
chunks.source: After 'because of' we use the -ing form.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: During the drought most households were hit by the ___ famine in their life. (bad) A: worst. Superlative: 'the worst famine'.
chunks.source: Superlative: 'the worst famine'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The bad man in our neighbourhood ___ our grass in the compound last week. (burn) A: burnt. 'Last week' needs the past simple: 'burnt'.
chunks.source: 'Last week' needs the past simple: 'burnt'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Most passengers ___ escaped death when the bus overturned. (narrow) A: narrowly. The adverb form of 'narrow' is 'narrowly'.
chunks.source: The adverb form of 'narrow' is 'narrowly'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'burn' in your own sentence to show its meaning. ___ A: The farmers burn the rubbish after harvesting.. 'Burn' means to destroy by fire.
chunks.source: 'Burn' means to destroy by fire.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'bun' in your own sentence to show its meaning. ___ A: She ate a sweet bun for breakfast.. 'Bun' is a small sweet bread.
chunks.source: 'Bun' is a small sweet bread.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The thieves hid away from the chief. (Re-write giving the plural of 'chief': ___)  A: The thieves hid away from the chiefs.. The plural of 'chief' is 'chiefs'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'chief' is 'chiefs'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Okere rears the nice looking goose. (Re-write giving the plural of 'goose': ___)  A: Okere rears the nice looking geese.. The plural of 'goose' is 'geese'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'goose' is 'geese'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The half-sister will be happy to see us. (Re-write giving the plural of 'half-sister': ___)  A: The half-sisters will be happy to see us.. The plural of 'half-sister' is 'half-sisters'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'half-sister' is 'half-sisters'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in alphabetical order: bullet, cooking, brush, cooker ___ A: brush, bullet, cooker, cooking. Compare letter by letter: brush, bullet, cooker, cooking.
chunks.source: Compare letter by letter: brush, bullet, cooker, cooking.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words in alphabetical order: dress, drink, dream, driver ___ A: dream, dress, drink, driver. Compare letter by letter: dream, dress, drink, driver.
chunks.source: Compare letter by letter: dream, dress, drink, driver.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: The class monitor has left all the doors closed. ___ A: open. The opposite of 'closed' is 'open'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'closed' is 'open'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: Our sub-county is densely populated. ___ A: sparsely. The opposite of 'densely' is 'sparsely'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'densely' is 'sparsely'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: By sunset all the guests had arrived. ___ A: departed. The opposite of 'arrived' is 'departed'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'arrived' is 'departed'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for: The flesh of a sheep is very delicious. ___ A: mutton. The flesh of a sheep is 'mutton'.
chunks.source: The flesh of a sheep is 'mutton'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one word for: Angellico was punished for coming to school after the expected time. ___ A: late. 'After the expected time' means 'late'.
chunks.source: 'After the expected time' means 'late'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: As soon as it started raining, the farmers planted their crops. (Give one word for 'as soon as': ___)  A: Immediately it started raining, the farmers planted their crops.. 'As soon as' means 'immediately'.
chunks.source: 'As soon as' means 'immediately'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words into a correct sentence: book, My, this, me, for, sent, uncle ___ A: My, uncle, sent, this, book, for, me. Subject + verb + object: My uncle sent this book for me.
chunks.source: Subject + verb + object: My uncle sent this book for me.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the words into a correct sentence: is, the, do, know, time, what, you ___ A: Do, you, know, what, the, time, is?. A polite question: Do you know what the time is?
chunks.source: A polite question: Do you know what the time is?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: That prefect will be rewarded. He has worked hard to promote discipline. (Re-write using: …who ___)  A: That prefect, who has worked hard to promote discipline, will be rewarded.. Join with the relative pronoun 'who'.
chunks.source: Join with the relative pronoun 'who'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Good neighbours are needed in our community. Hard working parents are also needed in our community. (Re-write using: …and so ___)  A: Good neighbours are needed in our community, and so are hard working parents.. Add 'and so are' for agreement.
chunks.source: Add 'and so are' for agreement.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The papyrus was very dry. The papyrus was not dirty. (Re-write using: …but ___)  A: The papyrus was very dry but it was not dirty.. Join contrasting sentences with 'but'.
chunks.source: Join contrasting sentences with 'but'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Katete could not read the poor handwriting. He did not understand the letter. (Re-write using: …because ___)  A: Katete did not understand the letter because he could not read the poor handwriting.. Join cause and effect with 'because'.
chunks.source: Join cause and effect with 'because'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How much does a litre of milk cost? (Re-write beginning: What ___?)  A: What is the price of a litre of milk?. 'How much does… cost?' becomes 'What is the price of…?'.
chunks.source: 'How much does… cost?' becomes 'What is the price of…?'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: People who are rich take their children to good schools. (Re-write beginning: The ___)  A: The rich take their children to good schools.. 'People who are rich' becomes 'The rich'.
chunks.source: 'People who are rich' becomes 'The rich'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: May I go home and help my mother? (Re-write using: I would ___)  A: I would like to go home and help my mother.. 'May I…?' becomes 'I would like to…'.
chunks.source: 'May I…?' becomes 'I would like to…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: "These garden tools were bought last term," said the head teacher. (Re-write using: …said that ___)  A: The head teacher said that those garden tools had been bought the previous term.. In reported speech: 'were bought' → 'had been bought', 'last term' → 'the previous term'.
chunks.source: In reported speech: 'were bought' → 'had been bought', 'last term' → 'the previous term'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our bodies should be kept clean, so we shall not fall sick. (Re-write using: …or else ___)  A: Our bodies should be kept clean or else we shall fall sick.. 'So' becomes 'or else' with the opposite result.
chunks.source: 'So' becomes 'or else' with the opposite result.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: That is a very bright idea. (Re-write using: …is! ___)  A: How bright that idea is!. Use the exclamation pattern 'How + adjective…!'.
chunks.source: Use the exclamation pattern 'How + adjective…!'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The fishmonger started selling fish three days ago. He is still selling fish. (Re-write using: …for ___)  A: The fishmonger has been selling fish for three days.. Use the present perfect continuous with 'for'.
chunks.source: Use the present perfect continuous with 'for'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Having put up our school sign post, the parents addressed the pupils. (Re-write using: …after ___)  A: After the parents had put up our school sign post, they addressed the pupils.. 'Having put up' becomes 'After… had put up'.
chunks.source: 'Having put up' becomes 'After… had put up'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I am more interested in English than in music. (Re-write using: …enjoy ___)  A: I enjoy English more than music.. 'Am more interested in' becomes 'enjoy… more than'.
chunks.source: 'Am more interested in' becomes 'enjoy… more than'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: It isn't far from here to the health center, is it? (Re-write using: …isn't it? ___)  A: It is far from here to the health center, isn't it?. Change the tag to 'isn't it?' with a positive main clause.
chunks.source: Change the tag to 'isn't it?' with a positive main clause.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: All those who borrowed books from the librarian are needed by the class teacher. (Re-write using: …to whom ___)  A: All those to whom the librarian lent books are needed by the class teacher.. 'Borrowed from the librarian' becomes 'to whom the librarian lent'.
chunks.source: 'Borrowed from the librarian' becomes 'to whom the librarian lent'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Molist became very weak because he ate very little food. (Re-write using: The ___ the ___)  A: The less food Molist ate, the weaker he became.. Use the pattern 'The… the…'.
chunks.source: Use the pattern 'The… the…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: All the eggs in the cupboard were not good. (Re-write using: None ___)  A: None of the eggs in the cupboard was good.. 'All… were not' becomes 'None of… was'.
chunks.source: 'All… were not' becomes 'None of… was'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The school team looks forward to winning the match. (Re-write using: …will ___)  A: The school team will win the match.. 'Looks forward to winning' becomes 'will win'.
chunks.source: 'Looks forward to winning' becomes 'will win'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: You will not attend the family meeting. You get permission from your father. (Begin: Unless ___)  A: Unless you get permission from your father, you will not attend the family meeting.. Join with 'Unless'.
chunks.source: Join with 'Unless'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: There is need for the farm house to be cleaned. (Re-write using: …needs ___)  A: The farm house needs to be cleaned.. 'There is need for' becomes 'needs to be'.
chunks.source: 'There is need for' becomes 'needs to be'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Safiri and answer: Where did Safiri go for her Primary studies? ___ A: Ndogo Primary School. Safiri started school at Ndogo Primary School.
chunks.source: Safiri started school at Ndogo Primary School.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Safiri and answer: Who is Safiri's father? ___ A: Mr. Mulefu. Her father is Mr. Mulefu.
chunks.source: Her father is Mr. Mulefu.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Safiri and answer: How did the teachers show love to Safiri? ___ A: They decided to pay for her school fees.. The teachers paid her fees.
chunks.source: The teachers paid her fees.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Safiri and answer: What did Safiri do so as not to disappoint the teachers? ___ A: She did not let them down; she became even more intelligent.. She worked hard and became even more intelligent.
chunks.source: She worked hard and became even more intelligent.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Safiri and answer: How did the Sub-County chief help Safiri? ___ A: He asked every man in the area to contribute for the girl's fees.. The chief asked men to contribute fees.
chunks.source: The chief asked men to contribute fees.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Safiri and answer: In which district does Safiri live? ___ A: Kigoto district. Safiri lives in Kigoto district.
chunks.source: Safiri lives in Kigoto district.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Safiri and answer: Why do you think Kyente Secondary School still remembers Safiri? ___ A: Because she became the head girl in Senior Two, which had never happened in that school.. She was the first Senior Two head girl.
chunks.source: She was the first Senior Two head girl.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Safiri and answer: Give a word to mean 'behaviour'. ___ A: conduct. 'Behaviour' means 'conduct'.
chunks.source: 'Behaviour' means 'conduct'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Safiri and answer: Give a word to mean 'chosen'. ___ A: selected. 'Chosen' means 'selected'.
chunks.source: 'Chosen' means 'selected'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Safiri and answer: Suggest a suitable title for the story. ___ A: Safiri's Success. The story is about Safiri's success through hard work.
chunks.source: The story is about Safiri's success through hard work.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The first European missionaries arrived ___ Uganda around 1877 – 1897. A: in. We 'arrive in' a country.
chunks.source: We 'arrive in' a country.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: He had ___ entered the hotel when the hotelier welcomed him. A: hardly. 'Had hardly… when' is the correct pattern.
chunks.source: 'Had hardly… when' is the correct pattern.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: All the ___ were closed so our maid could not buy any meat. A: shops. 'Shops' were closed, so she could not buy meat.
chunks.source: 'Shops' were closed, so she could not buy meat.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: It has rained heavily ___ the last two weeks. A: for. We use 'for' with a period of time.
chunks.source: We use 'for' with a period of time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Since the news was boring, my father ___ off the radio and went to sleep. A: switched. The phrasal verb is 'switch off'.
chunks.source: The phrasal verb is 'switch off'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: I was ___ with my grandmother in Kisoro when I heard the good news about travelling to UK. (holiday) A: holidaying. The verb form of 'holiday' is 'holidaying'.
chunks.source: The verb form of 'holiday' is 'holidaying'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The lorry from Soroti was ___ loaded of all the vehicles. (heavy) A: heavily. We need an adverb: 'heavily loaded'.
chunks.source: We need an adverb: 'heavily loaded'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: It was ___ who volunteered to clean the village well. (they) A: they. After 'It was' we use the subject pronoun 'they'.
chunks.source: After 'It was' we use the subject pronoun 'they'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The lineman used the ___ lead to tap electricity while repairing my uncle's phone. (extend) A: extension. The noun form of 'extend' is 'extension'.
chunks.source: The noun form of 'extend' is 'extension'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our class teacher's penpal is a ___. (Madagascar) A: Malagasy. A person from Madagascar is 'Malagasy'.
chunks.source: A person from Madagascar is 'Malagasy'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Aunt Joveta is yet to celebrate her ___ birthday. (fifty) A: fiftieth. The ordinal of 'fifty' is 'fiftieth'.
chunks.source: The ordinal of 'fifty' is 'fiftieth'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Primary four girls have modelled ___ objects from their artwork. (life) A: lifelike. 'Lifelike' means looking like real life.
chunks.source: 'Lifelike' means looking like real life.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: During time for clubs and societies, he usually finds himself taking on a ___ lesson. (work) A: work. 'Work' is used as an adjective: 'a work lesson'.
chunks.source: 'Work' is used as an adjective: 'a work lesson'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The Kampala – Masaka highway is being ___ in order to reduce accidents. (broad) A: broadened. The verb form of 'broad' is 'broaden'; passive: 'being broadened'.
chunks.source: The verb form of 'broad' is 'broaden'; passive: 'being broadened'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Some boys were ___ from the examination owing to stubbornness. (continue) A: discontinued. Passive: 'were discontinued' (stopped/removed).
chunks.source: Passive: 'were discontinued' (stopped/removed).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: Hon. ___ A: Honourable. 'Hon.' is short for 'Honourable'.
chunks.source: 'Hon.' is short for 'Honourable'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write in full: asap ___ A: as soon as possible. 'asap' stands for 'as soon as possible'.
chunks.source: 'asap' stands for 'as soon as possible'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mother is exchanging banter with a person who owns and manages a restaurant. (Give one word for: 'a person who owns and manages a restaurant' ___) A: restaurateur. A person who owns and manages a restaurant is a 'restaurateur'.
chunks.source: A person who owns and manages a restaurant is a 'restaurateur'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: While the teachers went for a meeting, we revised our notes in a silent way. (Re-write using one word for 'in a silent way': ___)  A: While the teachers went for a meeting, we revised our notes silently.. 'In a silent way' = 'silently'.
chunks.source: 'In a silent way' = 'silently'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Apart from yarn, the tailor had a thimble in his container. (Re-write giving one word for 'apart from': ___)  A: Besides yarn, the tailor had a thimble in his container.. 'Apart from' means 'besides'.
chunks.source: 'Apart from' means 'besides'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Sarah brought an abacus for the Mathematics lesson. (Re-write giving the plural of 'abacus': ___)  A: Sarah brought abacuses for the Mathematics lesson.. The plural of 'abacus' is 'abacuses'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'abacus' is 'abacuses'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The fire chief reached the scene an hour later after the factory had been burnt-out. (Re-write giving the plural of 'chief': ___)  A: The fire chiefs reached the scene an hour later after the factory had been burnt-out.. The plural of 'chief' is 'chiefs'.
chunks.source: The plural of 'chief' is 'chiefs'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'date' in a sentence to show its meaning. ___ A: What is today's date?. 'Date' is the day of the month.
chunks.source: 'Date' is the day of the month.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Use 'debt' in a sentence to show its meaning. ___ A: He paid his debt yesterday.. 'Debt' is money owed to someone.
chunks.source: 'Debt' is money owed to someone.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rearrange the words to form a correct sentence: library, How, is, a, useful ___ A: How, useful, a, library, is!. Exclamation: How useful a library is!
chunks.source: Exclamation: How useful a library is!

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rearrange the words to form a correct sentence: holiday, most, term's, interesting, was, the, Last ___ A: Last, term's, holiday, was, the, most, interesting. Last term's holiday was the most interesting.
chunks.source: Last term's holiday was the most interesting.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rearrange the words in alphabetical order: newspaper, magazine, brochure, journal ___ A: brochure, journal, magazine, newspaper. Compare first letters: b, j, m, n.
chunks.source: Compare first letters: b, j, m, n.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rearrange the words in alphabetical order: grandmother, niece, grandfather, nephew ___ A: grandfather, grandmother, nephew, niece. Compare letter by letter: grandfather, grandmother, nephew, niece.
chunks.source: Compare letter by letter: grandfather, grandmother, nephew, niece.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined word: At JK shop, second-hand ovens are sold expensively. ___ A: cheaply. The opposite of 'expensively' is 'cheaply'.
chunks.source: The opposite of 'expensively' is 'cheaply'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give the opposite of the underlined words: My little brother is being chased by your funny white bullock. ___ A: My big brother is being chased by your funny black bullock.. 'Little' → 'big', 'white' → 'black'.
chunks.source: 'Little' → 'big', 'white' → 'black'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The tailor is likely to patch my torn shirt at 2:00p.m. The tailor is likely to patch my torn shirt at 3:00p.m. (Re-write as one sentence using: …either ___)  A: The tailor is likely to patch my torn shirt at either 2:00p.m. or 3:00p.m.. Join with 'either… or…'.
chunks.source: Join with 'either… or…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Cyclists are advised to wear helmets. This may help protect their heads. (Re-write beginning: In order to ___)  A: In order to protect their heads, cyclists are advised to wear helmets.. Show purpose with 'In order to'.
chunks.source: Show purpose with 'In order to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The stranger asked me the way to the church. (Re-write using: …inquire ___)  A: The stranger inquired about the way to the church.. 'Asked the way' becomes 'inquired about the way'.
chunks.source: 'Asked the way' becomes 'inquired about the way'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A friend of mine lent this book to me. (Re-write beginning: I was ___)  A: I was lent this book by a friend of mine.. Active to passive: 'I was lent'.
chunks.source: Active to passive: 'I was lent'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The mad man continued eating dirty food. The mad man's stomach pained more and more. (Re-write using: The ___ the ___)  A: The more dirty food the mad man ate, the more his stomach pained.. Use the pattern 'The… the…'.
chunks.source: Use the pattern 'The… the…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who will be cleaning the blackboard tonight? (Re-write beginning: By whom ___)  A: By whom will the blackboard be cleaned tonight?. Passive question: 'By whom will… be cleaned?'.
chunks.source: Passive question: 'By whom will… be cleaned?'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The rainfall was very gentle. We walked back home in it. (Re-write using: …such…that ___)  A: It was such a gentle rainfall that we walked back home in it.. Join with 'such a + adjective + noun + that'.
chunks.source: Join with 'such a + adjective + noun + that'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: That tailor did not have any cloths. The tailor did not make any face mask for me. (Re-write beginning: Had ___)  A: Had that tailor had any cloths, he would have made a face mask for me.. 'If… hadn't' becomes 'Had…'.
chunks.source: 'If… hadn't' becomes 'Had…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The visitor was sitting on a wooden stool. A nail pricked the visitor's pair of trousers. (Re-write beginning: Sitting ___)  A: Sitting on a wooden stool, the visitor's pair of trousers was pricked by a nail.. Use the participle 'Sitting' with passive voice.
chunks.source: Use the participle 'Sitting' with passive voice.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mary enjoys listening to pop music. Mary enjoys listening to gospel music more. (Re-write using: …would rather ___)  A: Mary would rather listen to gospel music than pop music.. Use 'would rather… than…'.
chunks.source: Use 'would rather… than…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Our parents and teachers love disciplined children. (Re-write beginning: What ___)  A: What our parents and teachers love are disciplined children.. Use the 'What' cleft sentence.
chunks.source: Use the 'What' cleft sentence.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The pair of scissors was too blunt to be used for cutting the garment. (Rewrite as two separate sentences: ___)  A: The pair of scissors was too blunt. It could not be used for cutting the garment.. Split into two sentences.
chunks.source: Split into two sentences.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The chairperson of the debate will speak before the secretary announces the results of today's debate. (Re-write beginning: By the time ___)  A: By the time the secretary announces the results of today's debate, the chairperson of the debate will have spoken.. Use 'By the time' with the future perfect.
chunks.source: Use 'By the time' with the future perfect.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Some scholars are more interested in playing games than in training in MDD. (Re-write using: …better than ___)  A: Some scholars like playing games better than training in MDD.. 'More interested in' becomes 'like… better than'.
chunks.source: 'More interested in' becomes 'like… better than'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The baker baked nice biscuits then he baked brown bread. (Re-write using: …besides ___)  A: Besides baking nice biscuits, the baker baked brown bread.. 'Then' becomes 'Besides' + -ing.
chunks.source: 'Then' becomes 'Besides' + -ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The new inspector of schools does not know Kiswahili. The new inspector of schools does not know French. (Re-write using: …neither ___)  A: The new inspector of schools knows neither Kiswahili nor French.. Join two negatives with 'neither… nor…'.
chunks.source: Join two negatives with 'neither… nor…'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The doctor made a phone call having loaded enough airtime on his phone. (Re-write using: …before ___)  A: Before the doctor made a phone call, he had loaded enough airtime on his phone.. 'Having loaded' becomes 'Before… had loaded'.
chunks.source: 'Having loaded' becomes 'Before… had loaded'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why did he disturb you during the English lesson? (Re-write using: …necessary…? ___)  A: Was it necessary for him to disturb you during the English lesson?. 'Why did…' becomes 'Was it necessary…?'.
chunks.source: 'Why did…' becomes 'Was it necessary…?'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: We took our torn shoes to the cobbler. The cobbler has not come for work today. (Re-write using: …whom ___)  A: The cobbler to whom we took our torn shoes has not come for work today.. Use 'to whom'.
chunks.source: Use 'to whom'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: "Class, has Mr. Okoik come for his morning lesson?" asked the head teacher. (Re-write using: …wanted ___)  A: The head teacher wanted to know whether Mr. Okoik had come for his morning lesson.. In reported speech: use 'wanted to know whether' with past perfect.
chunks.source: In reported speech: use 'wanted to know whether' with past perfect.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Kofi and answer: What is the passage about? ___ A: Kofi, a boy who worked hard, bought a TV set, saved money and returned to school.. The passage tells Kofi's story of hard work and success.
chunks.source: The passage tells Kofi's story of hard work and success.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Kofi and answer: How did the uncle appreciate Kofi's effort? ___ A: He gave him a token of one hundred fifty-five thousand shillings.. The uncle gave Kofi 155,000 shillings.
chunks.source: The uncle gave Kofi 155,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Kofi and answer: What made Kofi drop out of school? ___ A: His parents died of cancer before he could complete primary five.. His parents died and he could not afford school.
chunks.source: His parents died and he could not afford school.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Kofi and answer: Mention Kofi's uncle's occupation. ___ A: Fishing. The uncle fished in the nearby river.
chunks.source: The uncle fished in the nearby river.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Kofi and answer: Why did he decide to start saving sixty thousand shillings? ___ A: To raise money enough for school fees.. He saved to pay his school fees.
chunks.source: He saved to pay his school fees.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Kofi and answer: What made Kofi's home crowded? ___ A: The TV set; people came to watch news and Nigerian movies.. Villagers crowded his home to watch TV.
chunks.source: Villagers crowded his home to watch TV.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Kofi and answer: What lesson do you learn from this passage? ___ A: Hard work and determination pay.. Kofi's hard work helped him return to school.
chunks.source: Kofi's hard work helped him return to school.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Kofi and answer: Give a single word for 'dawn'. ___ A: sunrise. 'Dawn' means 'sunrise'.
chunks.source: 'Dawn' means 'sunrise'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Kofi and answer: Give a single word for 'throng'. ___ A: crowd. 'Throng' means 'crowd'.
chunks.source: 'Throng' means 'crowd'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage about Kofi and answer: Suggest a suitable title for the passage. ___ A: Kofi's Determination. The story shows Kofi's determination.
chunks.source: The story shows Kofi's determination.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the shopping list and answer: What is the information above about? ___ A: Bulamu Bushra's shopping from Kalerwe market.. The list shows items Bushra bought.
chunks.source: The list shows items Bushra bought.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the shopping list and answer: From where were the items bought? ___ A: Kalerwe market. The items were bought from Kalerwe market.
chunks.source: The items were bought from Kalerwe market.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the shopping list and answer: On which day were the items purchased? ___ A: A day before Easter Sunday. She was sent a day before Easter Sunday.
chunks.source: She was sent a day before Easter Sunday.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the shopping list and answer: How many items were bought? ___ A: Ten. There are ten items on the list.
chunks.source: There are ten items on the list.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the shopping list and answer: Who bought the items? ___ A: Bulamu Bushra. Bulamu Bushra was sent to buy the items.
chunks.source: Bulamu Bushra was sent to buy the items.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the shopping list and answer: How much was spent on toothpaste? ___ A: 10,000 shillings. Two tablets at 5,000 shillings each = 10,000.
chunks.source: Two tablets at 5,000 shillings each = 10,000.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the shopping list and answer: Which item cost thirty-three thousand five hundred? ___ A: Fresh fish. Fresh fish cost 33,500 shillings.
chunks.source: Fresh fish cost 33,500 shillings.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the shopping list and answer: In which quantity is charcoal sold? ___ A: A tin. Charcoal is sold by the tin.
chunks.source: Charcoal is sold by the tin.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the shopping list and answer: If you bought two watermelons, how much change would you get from a fifty thousand shilling note? ___ A: 43,000 shillings. Two watermelons cost 7,000; 50,000 - 7,000 = 43,000.
chunks.source: Two watermelons cost 7,000; 50,000 - 7,000 = 43,000.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Study the shopping list and answer: Who received the above shopping? ___ A: Her father. She presented the shopping to her father.
chunks.source: She presented the shopping to her father.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Rearrange the sentences to form a good composition about the carpenter: (a) At last our head teacher was appreciative to the carpenter. (b) Next, he sawed it into pieces and joined them with nails and a hammer. (c) 'How many desks do you need?' the carpenter asked the head teacher. (d) First, the carpenter used a plane to smooth the wood. (e) When this year commenced, pupils joined new classes. (f) The head teacher immediately reached the nearby carpenter. (g) Then he varnished the desks that he had made. (h) Unfortunately, pupils in P.5 did not have enough desks. (i) He told the carpenter that the pupils did not have enough desks. (j) 'Twelve desks, please,' replied the head teacher. A: When this year commenced, pupils joined new classes., Unfortunately, pupils in P.5 did not have enough desks., The head teacher immediately reached the nearby carpenter., He told the carpenter that the pupils did not have enough desks., 'How many desks do you need?' the carpenter asked the head teacher., 'Twelve desks, please,' replied the head teacher., First, the carpenter used a plane to smooth the wood., Next, he sawed it into pieces and joined them with nails and a hammer., Then he varnished the desks that he had made., At last our head teacher was appreciative to the carpenter.. Follow the order: problem, visit, order, work in steps, thanks.
chunks.source: Follow the order: problem, visit, order, work in steps, thanks.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: When did Lukunyanga's school break up for holidays? A: 24th November. The school closed on 24th November, before the official date.
chunks.source: The school closed on 24th November, before the official date.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Lukunyanga's school closed earlier than other schools. A: True. It was the first school to break up.
chunks.source: It was the first school to break up.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Lukunyanga travelled to Seeta Town by ___. A: motorcycle. He used a motorcycle from Namilyango to Seeta Town.
chunks.source: He used a motorcycle from Namilyango to Seeta Town.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: What was Lukunyanga's position in class? A: third. He was the third out of sixty pupils.
chunks.source: He was the third out of sixty pupils.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Lukunyanga was promoted to Primary Seven. A: True. He gave the report card with joy because he had been promoted.
chunks.source: He gave the report card with joy because he had been promoted.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Lukunyanga visited his relatives in ___ District. A: Luweero. After Christmas he visited relatives in Luweero District.
chunks.source: After Christmas he visited relatives in Luweero District.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Where did Lukunyanga bank his school fees? A: Tropical Bank. He took the money to Tropical Bank.
chunks.source: He took the money to Tropical Bank.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Lukunyanga helped his father in the garden for four weeks. A: True. He kept off studies for the first four weeks to help his father.
chunks.source: He kept off studies for the first four weeks to help his father.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Lukunyanga's village is called ___. A: Kyebando. His village was Kyebando in Kampala District.
chunks.source: His village was Kyebando in Kampala District.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Why did the school close early? A: financial problems. Because of financial shortages in the school.
chunks.source: Because of financial shortages in the school.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Who invented the telephone? A: A.G. Bell. The telephone was invented by A.G. Bell in 1876.
chunks.source: The telephone was invented by A.G. Bell in 1876.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: The aeroplane was invented in America. A: True. The Wright Brothers invented it in America.
chunks.source: The Wright Brothers invented it in America.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: The radio was invented in ___ by Marconi. A: 1912. Marconi invented the radio in 1912.
chunks.source: Marconi invented the radio in 1912.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: What did the Wright Brothers invent? A: the aeroplane. The Wright Brothers invented the aeroplane in 1903.
chunks.source: The Wright Brothers invented the aeroplane in 1903.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: The television was invented by A.G. Bell. A: False. The television was invented by J.L. Baird.
chunks.source: The television was invented by J.L. Baird.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: The television was invented in ___ by J.L. Baird. A: England. J.L. Baird invented the television in England in 1926.
chunks.source: J.L. Baird invented the television in England in 1926.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: What do radio presenters use in the studios? A: microphones and earphones. Presenters use microphones and earphones.
chunks.source: Presenters use microphones and earphones.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Radios use electricity or dry cells to produce sound. A: True. The passage says radios use electricity or dry cells.
chunks.source: The passage says radios use electricity or dry cells.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: The knobs are used for ___ in to different stations. A: tuning. The knobs are used for tuning in to different stations.
chunks.source: The knobs are used for tuning in to different stations.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Which invention came first? A: the telephone. The telephone (1876) came before the aeroplane, radio and television.
chunks.source: The telephone (1876) came before the aeroplane, radio and television.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: What is the name of the village in the story? A: Nyakibale. The story is about Nyakibale Village.
chunks.source: The story is about Nyakibale Village.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: The animals died due to lack of food and water. A: True. Animals died due to lack of food and water.
chunks.source: Animals died due to lack of food and water.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Mr. Papayeko is the ___ elder. A: village. Mr. Papayeko was the village elder.
chunks.source: Mr. Papayeko was the village elder.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: What did the villagers agree to do at the meeting? A: plant many trees. They agreed to plant many trees to attract rain.
chunks.source: They agreed to plant many trees to attract rain.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Leo promised to give a thousand tree seedlings. A: True. Leo, a forest officer, promised a thousand seedlings.
chunks.source: Leo, a forest officer, promised a thousand seedlings.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: The villagers gathered at the ___ square. A: market. They gathered at the market square.
chunks.source: They gathered at the market square.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Why did the animals die? A: lack of food and water. The drought caused lack of food and water.
chunks.source: The drought caused lack of food and water.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: The people saw the rain as a miracle. A: True. When it finally rained, the people saw it as a miracle.
chunks.source: When it finally rained, the people saw it as a miracle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Read the passage and answer: Mujuni said the ___ must be annoyed. A: ancestors. Mujuni said the ancestors must be annoyed.
chunks.source: Mujuni said the ancestors must be annoyed.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Given that A = {b, d, f, h} and B = {a, b, c, d, e}, list the elements of A union B (A ∪ B). A: {a, b, c, d, e, f, h}. Union means all the elements from both sets, written once each.
chunks.source: Union means all the elements from both sets, written once each.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. If M = {2, 3, 4, 5}, how many subsets does set M have? A: 16. A set with n elements has 2^n subsets; 2^4 = 16.
chunks.source: A set with n elements has 2^n subsets; 2^4 = 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. A set has 31 proper subsets. How many elements does the set have? A: 5. Proper subsets = 2^n − 1, so 2^n = 32 and n = 5.
chunks.source: Proper subsets = 2^n − 1, so 2^n = 32 and n = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. Given that the universal set is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}, A = {2, 4, 6} and B = {4, 5, 6, 7}, find (A ∪ B)' (the complement of A union B). A: {1, 3}. A ∪ B = {2, 4, 5, 6, 7}, so the elements left in the universal set are 1 and 3.
chunks.source: A ∪ B = {2, 4, 5, 6, 7}, so the elements left in the universal set are 1 and 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. Given n(A) = 25, n(B) = 20 and n(A ∪ B) = 35, find n(A ∩ B) (A intersection B). A: 10. n(A ∩ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∪ B) = 25 + 20 − 35 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. In a class of 30 pupils, y like English only, 10 like both English and French, 7 like French only and 4 like neither language. How many pupils like English only? A: 9. y + 10 + 7 + 4 = 30, so y = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. In the class above, what is the probability of choosing a pupil who likes only one language? A: 8/15. Only one language = 9 + 7 = 16 pupils out of 30, which simplifies to 8/15.
chunks.source: Only one language = 9 + 7 = 16 pupils out of 30, which simplifies to 8/15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. In a class of 60 pupils, 30 took part in football, y took part in volleyball only, 10 took part in both games and 2y took part in neither. Find the value of y. A: 10. (30 − 10) + 10 + y + 2y = 60, so 3y = 30 and y = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. Using the value of y above, how many pupils took part in neither football nor volleyball? A: 20. Neither = 2y = 2 × 10 = 20.
chunks.source: Neither = 2y = 2 × 10 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. At a party of 2x guests, 19 ate meat, 13 ate fish, 9 ate both and x ate neither. What is the probability that a guest chosen at random ate neither meat nor fish? A: 1/2. 2x = 10 + 9 + 4 + x gives x = 23, so 23 of 46 guests ate nothing, which is 1/2.
chunks.source: 2x = 10 + 9 + 4 + x gives x = 23, so 23 of 46 guests ate nothing, which is 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 11. Given that set Q has 15 proper subsets, find n(Q) (the number of elements in Q). A: 4. 2^n − 1 = 15, so 2^n = 16 and n = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 12. In a group of players, 32 like tennis, 7 like football only, y like both games and 5 like neither. If 27 players like football, how many players are in the group altogether? A: 44. y = 27 − 7 = 20; total = 32 + 7 + 5 = 44.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 13. What is the probability of choosing a player who likes netball from the group above? A: 0. Nobody in the group plays netball, so the probability is 0.
chunks.source: Nobody in the group plays netball, so the probability is 0.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 14. In a Venn diagram, 40 pupils like mathematics (M) and some like English (E), while t like both. The regions are: M only = 2t + 10, both = t, E only = 3t − 5, neither = 3. Find the value of t. A: 10. (2t + 10) + t = 40, so 3t = 30 and t = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 15. Using t = 10 above, how many pupils like English? A: 35. English = t + (3t − 5) = 10 + 25 = 35.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 16. Using the same Venn diagram, how many pupils are there altogether? A: 68. 40 + 25 + 3 = 68.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 17. At a party, 2y guests ate beef only, 14 ate chicken only, (y + 7) ate both and (y − 1) ate none. If 29 guests did not eat chicken, find y. A: 10. 2y + (y − 1) = 29, so 3y = 30 and y = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 18. How many guests attended the party above? A: 60. 20 + 14 + 17 + 9 = 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 19. At Okello's birthday party, 16 guests took water, 30 took soda and 10 took both. How many guests took only one type of drink? A: 26. (16 − 10) + (30 − 10) = 6 + 20 = 26.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 20. How many guests attended Okello's party? A: 36. 6 + 10 + 20 = 36.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 21. Given X = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} and Y = {1, 3, 5, 7, 9}, find n(Y − X). A: 2. Y − X = {7, 9}, which has 2 elements.
chunks.source: Y − X = {7, 9}, which has 2 elements.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 22. Given that set Y = {all prime numbers less than 12}, find n(Y). A: 5. Y = {2, 3, 5, 7, 11}, which has 5 members.
chunks.source: Y = {2, 3, 5, 7, 11}, which has 5 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 23. In a home of 8 people, 5 like eating meat and 6 like eating fish. If everyone who eats only one dish is given 3 eggs, how many eggs are served? A: 15. Both = 5 + 6 − 8 = 3; only one dish = 8 − 3 = 5; eggs = 5 × 3 = 15.
chunks.source: Both = 5 + 6 − 8 = 3; only one dish = 8 − 3 = 5; eggs = 5 × 3 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 24. A Venn diagram shows boys who play volleyball (V) and tennis (T): 5 play volleyball only, 4 play both, 3 play tennis only. How many play only one game? A: 8. Only one game = 5 + 3 = 8.
chunks.source: Only one game = 5 + 3 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. What is the place value of 3 in the number 3,564? A: thousands. The 3 is in the fourth position from the right, the thousands place.
chunks.source: The 3 is in the fourth position from the right, the thousands place.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Write 111,111 in words. A: One hundred eleven thousand one hundred eleven. Read the thousands part first, then the rest.
chunks.source: Read the thousands part first, then the rest.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. Write 'four hundred four thousand forty four' in figures. A: 404044. 404 thousand and 44 ones make 404,044.
chunks.source: 404 thousand and 44 ones make 404,044.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. Convert XCIV to Hindu-Arabic numerals. A: 94. XC = 90 and IV = 4, so XCIV = 94.
chunks.source: XC = 90 and IV = 4, so XCIV = 94.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. My father was born in MCMLXXV and my mother in MCMLXXXIX. What is the difference between their ages, in Hindu-Arabic numerals? A: 14. 1975 and 1989 differ by 14 years.
chunks.source: 1975 and 1989 differ by 14 years.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. Express 409 in Roman numerals. A: CDIX. 400 = CD and 9 = IX, so 409 = CDIX.
chunks.source: 400 = CD and 9 = IX, so 409 = CDIX.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. What is the place value of 0 in the number 203four? A: fours. In base four the positions are ones, fours, sixteens; 0 is in the fours place.
chunks.source: In base four the positions are ones, fours, sixteens; 0 is in the fours place.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. Change 23four to base ten. A: 11. (2 × 4) + 3 = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. Express 52 in base three. A: 1221₃. 52 = 1×27 + 2×9 + 2×3 + 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. Change 201four to base three. A: 1020₃. 201four = 33 in base ten, and 33 = 1×27 + 0×9 + 2×3 + 0.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 11. Work out 401five − 344five. A: 2₅. 401five = 101 and 344five = 99 in base ten; 101 − 99 = 2.
chunks.source: 401five = 101 and 344five = 99 in base ten; 101 − 99 = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 12. Find the value of x if 211x = 112four. A: 3. 112four = 22 in base ten; 2x² + x + 1 = 22 gives x = 3.
chunks.source: 112four = 22 in base ten; 2x² + x + 1 = 22 gives x = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 13. How many hands and fingers are needed to count 48? A: 9 hands and 3 fingers. Each hand has 5 fingers; 48 ÷ 5 = 9 remainder 3.
chunks.source: Each hand has 5 fingers; 48 ÷ 5 = 9 remainder 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 14. Find the difference between the value of 3 and the place value of 4 in the number 73,946. A: 2990. Value of 3 = 3,000; place value of 4 = tens = 10; 3,000 − 10 = 2,990.
chunks.source: Value of 3 = 3,000; place value of 4 = tens = 10; 3,000 − 10 = 2,990.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 15. Multiply 101two × 11two. A: 1111₂. 101two = 5 and 11two = 3 in base ten; 5 × 3 = 15 = 1111two.
chunks.source: 101two = 5 and 11two = 3 in base ten; 5 × 3 = 15 = 1111two.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 16. Using the digits 5, 0 and 3, form the smallest three-digit numeral. A: 305. The smallest hundreds digit (not zero) is 3, then 0, then 5.
chunks.source: The smallest hundreds digit (not zero) is 3, then 0, then 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 17. Find the difference between the largest and the smallest numeral formed from 5, 0 and 3. A: 225. 530 − 305 = 225.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 18. Round off 23,456 to the nearest hundred. A: 23500. The tens digit is 5, so round up to 23,500.
chunks.source: The tens digit is 5, so round up to 23,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 19. Round off 456.27 to the nearest whole number. A: 456. The first decimal is 2, which is less than 5, so round down.
chunks.source: The first decimal is 2, which is less than 5, so round down.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 20. Write 500 in standard form (scientific notation). A: 5 x 10^2. 500 = 5 × 100 = 5 × 10².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 21. Write 30.45 in standard form (scientific notation). A: 3.045 x 10^1. 30.45 = 3.045 × 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 22. Write 0.00204 in standard form (scientific notation). A: 2.04 x 10^-3. 0.00204 = 2.04 × 10⁻³.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 23. Write the number whose scientific notation is 6.45 × 10³. A: 6450. Move the point 3 places to the right.
chunks.source: Move the point 3 places to the right.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 24. Write the number whose scientific notation is 3.9 × 10⁻². A: 0.039. Move the point 2 places to the left.
chunks.source: Move the point 2 places to the left.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 25. Express CXCVI as Hindu-Arabic numerals. A: 196. C + XC + VI = 100 + 90 + 6 = 196.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 26. Round off 47 to the nearest ten. A: 50. The ones digit 7 is 5 or more, so round up.
chunks.source: The ones digit 7 is 5 or more, so round up.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 27. Express 43five as a binary number (base two). A: 10111₂. 43five = 23 in base ten, and 23 = 16 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 10111two.
chunks.source: 43five = 23 in base ten, and 23 = 16 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 10111two.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 28. Write the number whose scientific notation is 8.61 × 10⁻². A: 0.0861. Move the point 2 places to the left.
chunks.source: Move the point 2 places to the left.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 29. Work out 303five − 22five. A: 231₅. 303five = 78 and 22five = 12 in base ten; 78 − 12 = 66 = 231five.
chunks.source: 303five = 78 and 22five = 12 in base ten; 78 − 12 = 66 = 231five.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 31. If 103x = 28ten, find the value of x. A: 5. x² + 3 = 28, so x² = 25 and x = 5.
chunks.source: x² + 3 = 28, so x² = 25 and x = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 32. Using the number 3,418: what is the place value of 4? A: hundreds. The 4 is third from the right, in the hundreds place.
chunks.source: The 4 is third from the right, in the hundreds place.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 33. Find the value of 4 in 3,418. A: 400. 4 hundreds = 400.
chunks.source: 4 hundreds = 400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 34. Write 'forty three thousand forty' in numerals. A: 43040. 43 thousand = 43,000; add 40 to get 43,040.
chunks.source: 43 thousand = 43,000; add 40 to get 43,040.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 35. Write XLV in Hindu-Arabic numerals. A: 45. XL = 40 and V = 5, so XLV = 45.
chunks.source: XL = 40 and V = 5, so XLV = 45.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 36. Find the unknown base: 112three = 22b. A: 6. 112three = 14 in base ten; 2b + 2 = 14 gives b = 6.
chunks.source: 112three = 14 in base ten; 2b + 2 = 14 gives b = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 38. Write CXL in Hindu-Arabic numerals. A: 140. C = 100 and XL = 40, so CXL = 140.
chunks.source: C = 100 and XL = 40, so CXL = 140.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 39. Write 90,098 in words. A: Ninety thousand ninety eight. 90 thousand and 98.
chunks.source: 90 thousand and 98.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 40. What is the place value of 3 in 3,468,428? A: millions. The 3 is in the millions position.
chunks.source: The 3 is in the millions position.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 41. Find the base n if 21n = 1001two. A: 4. 1001two = 9 in base ten; 2n + 1 = 9 gives n = 4.
chunks.source: 1001two = 9 in base ten; 2n + 1 = 9 gives n = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 42. Write 64 in Roman numerals. A: LXIV. 60 = LX and 4 = IV, so 64 = LXIV.
chunks.source: 60 = LX and 4 = IV, so 64 = LXIV.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 43. Write 'eleven thousand, one hundred eleven' in figures. A: 11111. 11,000 + 111 = 11,111.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 44. Change 103five to base ten (decimal). A: 28. (1 × 25) + (0 × 5) + 3 = 28.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 45. Express 13,400 in scientific notation (standard form). A: 1.34 x 10^4. 13,400 = 1.34 × 10,000 = 1.34 × 10⁴.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 46. Express MCDXC in Hindu-Arabic numerals. A: 1490. M = 1,000, CD = 400 and XC = 90, so 1,490.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 47. Express XXIX in Hindu-Arabic numerals. A: 29. XX = 20 and IX = 9, so 29.
chunks.source: XX = 20 and IX = 9, so 29.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 48. Change 120three to base five. A: 30₅. 120three = 15 in base ten, and 15 = 3 × 5 + 0 = 30five.
chunks.source: 120three = 15 in base ten, and 15 = 3 × 5 + 0 = 30five.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 49. Find the expanded number: (2 × 5²) + (3 × 5¹) + (4 × 5⁰). A: 69. 50 + 15 + 4 = 69.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 50. Correct 99.998 to 2 decimal places. A: 100.00. The third decimal is 8, so round up to 100.00.
chunks.source: The third decimal is 8, so round up to 100.00.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 52. Write 70,603 in words. A: Seventy thousand six hundred three. 70 thousand and 603.
chunks.source: 70 thousand and 603.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 54. Match each Roman numeral to its Hindu-Arabic value. A: CXCVI: 196; XCIV: 94; XLIV: 44; CDIX: 409. Break each Roman numeral into parts: C=100, XC=90, IV=4.
chunks.source: Break each Roman numeral into parts: C=100, XC=90, IV=4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Use the distributive property to work out (48 × 2.5) + (2.5 × 52). A: 250. 2.5 × (48 + 52) = 2.5 × 100 = 250.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. Use the distributive property to work out (16 ÷ 5) + (3 ÷ 5). A: 3.8. (16 + 3) ÷ 5 = 19 ÷ 5 = 3.8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. A taxi carries 14 passengers and a bus carries 29. If both make 3 journeys each, how many passengers do they carry altogether? A: 129. (14 + 29) × 3 = 43 × 3 = 129.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. Given that p ★ y = py + 8, evaluate 3 ★ 4. A: 20. (3 × 4) + 8 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. Using p ★ y = py + 8, evaluate 6 ★ 8. A: 56. (6 × 8) + 8 = 56.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. Work out 4 + 6 ÷ 2. A: 7. Divide first: 4 + 3 = 7.
chunks.source: Divide first: 4 + 3 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. Work out the square root of 196. A: 14. 14 × 14 = 196.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. Work out the square root of 1.44. A: 1.2. 1.2 × 1.2 = 1.44.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 11. The area of a square is 144 m². Find its perimeter. A: 48 m. Each side is 12 m, so the perimeter is 4 × 12 = 48 m.
chunks.source: Each side is 12 m, so the perimeter is 4 × 12 = 48 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 12. A water meter read 234,689 units at the start of the month and 234,788 at the end. How many units were used? A: 99. 234,788 − 234,689 = 99.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 13. If each unit costs sh. 500, how much is paid for the month above? A: 49500. 99 × 500 = 49,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 14. A farmer collects 15,600 eggs a day and packs them in trays of 30. Her vehicle carries 40 trays per trip. How many trips does she need? A: 13. 15,600 ÷ 30 = 520 trays; 520 ÷ 40 = 13 trips.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 15. Work out 42five × 3. A: 231₅. 42five = 22 in base ten; 22 × 3 = 66 = 231five.
chunks.source: 42five = 22 in base ten; 22 × 3 = 66 = 231five.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 17. Damalie picks 28 mangoes every day. How many will she pick in 9 days? A: 252. 28 × 9 = 252.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 19. A trader withdrew 5,000-shilling notes numbered BT 8182010 to BT 8182199. How much money did he withdraw? A: 950000. 190 notes × 5,000 = 950,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 21. Use the distributive property to work out (10 × 3.5) + (6.5 × 10). A: 100. 10 × (3.5 + 6.5) = 10 × 10 = 100.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 22. Multiply 490 × 1/2. A: 245. Half of 490 is 245.
chunks.source: Half of 490 is 245.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 23. What is the sum of 49 and 243? A: 292. 49 + 243 = 292.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 24. Work out the square root of 2.56. A: 1.6. 1.6 × 1.6 = 2.56.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 25. Work out 8 + 8 ÷ 4. A: 10. Divide first: 8 + 2 = 10.
chunks.source: Divide first: 8 + 2 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 26. Use the distributive property to work out (489 × 13) − (489 × 3). A: 4890. 489 × (13 − 3) = 489 × 10 = 4,890.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 29. If twice a number is 16, what is half the number? A: 4. The number is 8, and half of 8 is 4.
chunks.source: The number is 8, and half of 8 is 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 30. Musa has 150 mangoes. He can sell them in heaps of 5 for sh. 800 or heaps of 3 for sh. 500. Which option fetches more money? A: Heaps of 3. Heaps of 5: 30 × 800 = 24,000; heaps of 3: 50 × 500 = 25,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 31. How much more money does the better option fetch above? A: 1000. 25,000 − 24,000 = 1,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Find the next number in the sequence: 2, 3, 5, 7, ___. A: 11. These are prime numbers; the next prime after 7 is 11.
chunks.source: These are prime numbers; the next prime after 7 is 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. Find the next number in the sequence: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, ___. A: 21. The differences grow by 1 (2, 3, 4, 5), so add 6 to 15.
chunks.source: The differences grow by 1 (2, 3, 4, 5), so add 6 to 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. What is the smallest number which leaves remainder 5 when divided by 8 or by 9? A: 77. LCM of 8 and 9 is 72; 72 + 5 = 77.
chunks.source: LCM of 8 and 9 is 72; 72 + 5 = 77.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. The GCF of two numbers is 6 and their LCM is 72. If one number is 24, find the other. A: 18. Other = (6 × 72) ÷ 24 = 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. Find the LCM of 6, 8 and 9. A: 72. 72 = 2³ × 3² covers 6, 8 and 9.
chunks.source: 72 = 2³ × 3² covers 6, 8 and 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. Find the missing number: 4, 6, 8, 9, ___. A: 10. These are composite numbers in order; after 9 comes 10.
chunks.source: These are composite numbers in order; after 9 comes 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. What is the product of the first and the fifth even number? A: 20. 2 × 10 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. Work out the cube root of 64. A: 4. 4 × 4 × 4 = 64.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. Buses to Arua leave every 40 minutes and buses to Mbarara every 50 minutes. Both leave at 6:00 a.m. When do they next leave together? A: 9:20 a.m.. LCM of 40 and 50 is 200 minutes = 3 h 20 min; 6:00 + 3:20 = 9:20.
chunks.source: LCM of 40 and 50 is 200 minutes = 3 h 20 min; 6:00 + 3:20 = 9:20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 11. Three bells ring every 60, 45 and 30 minutes. All ring at 9:00 a.m. After how many minutes do they ring together again? A: 180. LCM of 60, 45 and 30 is 180.
chunks.source: LCM of 60, 45 and 30 is 180.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 12. At what time do the bells above ring together again? A: 12:00 noon. 180 minutes = 3 hours; 9:00 + 3:00 = 12:00.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 13. The LCM of two numbers is 84 and their GCF is 7. If one number is 14, find the other. A: 42. Other = (84 × 7) ÷ 14 = 42.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 14. Prime factorise 639 and write your answer in set notation. A: {3, 3, 71}. 639 = 9 × 71 = 3 × 3 × 71.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 15. Find the next two numbers: 1, 3, 6, 11, 18, ___, ___. A: 29, 42. Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7 (primes); next differences 11 and 13.
chunks.source: Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7 (primes); next differences 11 and 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 17. Prime factorise 18 and write your answer in power (superscript) form. A: 2 x 3^2. 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 = 2 × 3².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 18. A parent shared some apples among 6 boys and 1 apple remained. Sharing the same apples among 4 girls, 1 apple also remained. Find the least number of apples. A: 13. LCM of 6 and 4 is 12; 12 + 1 = 13.
chunks.source: LCM of 6 and 4 is 12; 12 + 1 = 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 19. Find the next number: 36, 34, 31, 26, 19, ___. A: 8. Differences are −2, −3, −5, −7 (primes); next is −11, so 19 − 11 = 8.
chunks.source: Differences are −2, −3, −5, −7 (primes); next is −11, so 19 − 11 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 20. Find the smallest number of pencils that 24 pupils or 18 pupils can share equally, leaving 3 pencils in each case. A: 75. LCM of 24 and 18 is 72; 72 + 3 = 75.
chunks.source: LCM of 24 and 18 is 72; 72 + 3 = 75.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 21. Find the next two numbers: 2, 4, 7, 12, 19, ___, ___. A: 30, 43. Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7 (primes); next differences 11 and 13.
chunks.source: Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7 (primes); next differences 11 and 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 22. Find all the prime factors of 30. A: 2, 3, 5. 30 = 2 × 3 × 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 23. Find the next number: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ___. A: 36. These are square numbers; 6² = 36.
chunks.source: These are square numbers; 6² = 36.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 24. Prime factorise 36 and write your answer in product form. A: 2 x 2 x 3 x 3. 36 = 4 × 9 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 25. Find the next number: 2, 4, 7, 12, 19, ___. A: 30. Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7 (primes); 19 + 11 = 30.
chunks.source: Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7 (primes); 19 + 11 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 26. Find the sum of the prime numbers between 20 and 30. A: 52. 23 + 29 = 52.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 27. Find the next number: 0, 2, 5, 10, 17, 28, ___. A: 41. Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 (primes); 28 + 13 = 41.
chunks.source: Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 (primes); 28 + 13 = 41.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 28. Find the sum of all prime numbers between 50 and 60. A: 112. 53 + 59 = 112.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 29. Find the LCM of 6 and 9. A: 18. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18; of 9: 9, 18.
chunks.source: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18; of 9: 9, 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 30. Put each number in the correct group: 2367, 814, 6425, 7282, 1001, 901938. A: Divisible by 11: 814,7282,1001; Not divisible by 11: 2367,6425,901938. Use the divisibility rule for 11 on each number.
chunks.source: Use the divisibility rule for 11 on each number.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. Sarah covered 20 km, which was 1/4 of her journey. How long was the journey? A: 80 km. 20 × 4 = 80.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. The ratio of boys to girls is 4:2. If there are 40 girls, how many boys are there? A: 80. 4:2 = 2:1, so boys = 2 × 40 = 80.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. Otim had 30 km still to cover after travelling 3/5 of the journey. How long was the whole journey? A: 75 km. 2/5 of the journey = 30 km, so the whole = 30 × 5/2 = 75.
chunks.source: 2/5 of the journey = 30 km, so the whole = 30 × 5/2 = 75.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. In a school, 3/4 of the pupils who sat PLE passed. If 30 failed, how many passed? A: 90. 1/4 = 30, so 3/4 = 90.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. What percentage of the pupils failed in the question above? A: 25. 1/4 = 25%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. Add 4.05 + 11.4 + 2.3. A: 17.75. Line up the decimal points and add.
chunks.source: Line up the decimal points and add.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. Osman spent 1/4 of his salary on food, 1/3 of the remainder on debts and saved sh. 3,600. What is his monthly salary? A: 7200. Food = 1/4, debts = 1/4, saved = 1/2 = 3,600, so salary = 7,200.
chunks.source: Food = 1/4, debts = 1/4, saved = 1/2 = 3,600, so salary = 7,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 11. How much did Osman spend on debts above? A: 1800. 1/4 of 7,200 = 1,800.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 13. Tap A fills a tank in 9 minutes, B in 12 and C in 18. How long if all three are opened together? A: 4 minutes. 1/9 + 1/12 + 1/18 = 1/4 of the tank per minute.
chunks.source: 1/9 + 1/12 + 1/18 = 1/4 of the tank per minute.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 14. The cost of 4 rulers is sh. 2,400. What is the cost of 6 similar rulers? A: 3600. One ruler = 600; 6 × 600 = 3,600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 16. A tank was 2/3 full. When 1/4 of the water was drawn, 2,500 litres remained. What is the tank's full capacity? A: 5000 litres. Water left = 2/3 − 1/6 = 1/2 of the tank = 2,500, so full = 5,000.
chunks.source: Water left = 2/3 − 1/6 = 1/2 of the tank = 2,500, so full = 5,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 17. In P.7, 1/4 of the pupils like science, 2/3 of the remainder like mathematics and the rest (33 pupils) like English. How many pupils are in P.7? A: 132. English = 1 − 1/4 − 1/2 = 1/4 = 33, so total = 132.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 18. 12 men can build a classroom in 5 days. How many men are needed to build it in 10 days? A: 6. 12 × 5 = 60 man-days; 60 ÷ 10 = 6 men.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 20. A pot has 5 1/2 litres of water. How many half-litre bottles can it fill? A: 11. 5.5 ÷ 0.5 = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 21. A tap pours 40 litres in 5 minutes. How long (in hours) will it take to fill a 1,080-litre tank? A: 2.25. 8 litres per minute; 1,080 ÷ 8 = 135 minutes = 2.25 hours.
chunks.source: 8 litres per minute; 1,080 ÷ 8 = 135 minutes = 2.25 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 22. 2/3 of Peter's salary equals 3/4 of Mary's salary of sh. 120,000. Find Peter's salary. A: 135000. 3/4 of 120,000 = 90,000; Peter's = 90,000 × 3/2 = 135,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 23. Kato, Mukasa and Musoke shared money in the ratio 2:3:5. Musoke got sh. 1,500 more than Kato. How much money was shared? A: 5000. 3 parts = 1,500, so 1 part = 500; total = 10 × 500 = 5,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 24. How much did each of Kato, Mukasa and Musoke get above? A: 1000, 1500, 2500. One part = 500; Kato = 1,000, Mukasa = 1,500, Musoke = 2,500.
chunks.source: One part = 500; Kato = 1,000, Mukasa = 1,500, Musoke = 2,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 25. A and B shared money in the ratio 3:4. If A got sh. 12,000, how much was shared? A: 28000. One part = 4,000; total = 7 × 4,000 = 28,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 26. How much did B get above? A: 16000. 4 × 4,000 = 16,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 27. A tank was 1/4 full. When half the water was drawn, 6,000 litres remained. What is the full capacity? A: 48000 litres. Remaining = 1/8 of the tank = 6,000, so full = 48,000.
chunks.source: Remaining = 1/8 of the tank = 6,000, so full = 48,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 28. Change 33 1/3% to a common fraction. A: 1/3. 33 1/3 ÷ 100 = 1/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 29. Express the ratio 1:8 as a percentage. A: 11.11. 1:8 means 1 out of 9; 1/9 = 11.11%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 30. Express 30 cm as a percentage of 2 metres. A: 15%. 30/200 = 15%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 32. 16% of a number is 900. What is the number? A: 5625. 900 ÷ 0.16 = 5,625.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 33. A school has 800 pupils; 45% are girls. How many boys are there? A: 440. Girls = 360; boys = 800 − 360 = 440.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 34. After spending 30% of his income, a man was left with sh. 210,000. What is his income? A: 300000. 70% = 210,000, so 100% = 300,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 35. How much did he spend above? A: 90000. 30% of 300,000 = 90,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 37. A radio costing sh. 90,000 was increased by 30%. What is the new price? A: 117000. 90,000 × 1.3 = 117,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 39. What amount, increased by 20%, becomes sh. 1,440? A: 1200. 1,440 ÷ 1.2 = 1,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 40. After selling an article at sh. 21,000, a trader made a profit of 20%. What was the cost price? A: 17500. 21,000 ÷ 1.2 = 17,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 41. A teacher's salary was decreased by 20% to sh. 120,000. What was it before? A: 150000. 120,000 ÷ 0.8 = 150,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 42. Kato sold shoes at sh. 45,000 at a loss of 10%. What was the cost price? A: 50000. 45,000 ÷ 0.9 = 50,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 43. How much money did Kato lose above? A: 5000. 50,000 − 45,000 = 5,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 44. A farmer's cattle rose from 800 to 1,200. By what percentage did they increase? A: 50%. (1,200 − 800) ÷ 800 = 50%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 45. When 240 is decreased to 192, what is the percentage decrease? A: 20%. (240 − 192) ÷ 240 = 20%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 46. A trader bought 30 books at sh. 24,000. At what price did he sell each book if he made a loss of 20%? A: 640. Cost each = 800; 800 × 0.8 = 640.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 47. A 100 kg bag of rice costs sh. 80,000. At what price per kg must it be sold for a 30% profit? A: 1040. Cost per kg = 800; 800 × 1.3 = 1,040.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 48. A radio marked sh. 60,000 is sold at a 15% discount. How much does the customer pay? A: 51000. 60,000 × 0.85 = 51,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 49. A man paid sh. 28,000 for an article marked sh. 32,000. What was the percentage discount? A: 12.5%. (32,000 − 28,000) ÷ 32,000 = 12.5%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 50. Wasswa paid sh. 18,000 for a handbag after a 10% discount. What was the marked price? A: 20000. 18,000 ÷ 0.9 = 20,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 51. Okello bought a car at sh. 2,500,000 and sold it to Otim at 20% profit. Otim sold it to Kato at 15% loss. How much did Kato pay? A: 2550000. Otim paid 3,000,000; Kato paid 3,000,000 × 0.85 = 2,550,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 52. 14 litres of milk, which is 40% more than the water, was used to make tea. How much tea was prepared? A: 24. Water = 14 ÷ 1.4 = 10 litres; tea = 14 + 10 = 24.
chunks.source: Water = 14 ÷ 1.4 = 10 litres; tea = 14 + 10 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 53. A man spent 20% of his salary on food, 10% on transport, 40% on medical care and the rest on rent. What percentage went to rent? A: 30. 100 − 20 − 10 − 40 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 54. If he earns sh. 800,000, how much does he spend on medical care? A: 320000. 40% of 800,000 = 320,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 55. How much more is spent on food than on transport above? A: 80000. 10% of 800,000 = 80,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 56. Mary banked sh. 500,000 at 12% simple interest per year. How much interest did she earn after 2 years? A: 120000. 500,000 × 0.12 × 2 = 120,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 57. A man borrowed sh. 120,000 at 8% per year and paid sh. 7,200 interest. For how long was the loan? A: 9 months. 7,200 ÷ (120,000 × 0.08) = 0.75 years = 9 months.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 58. Out of 120 students who did a test, 1/3 were girls. How many girls did the test? A: 40. 120 ÷ 3 = 40.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 59. If 40% of the boys failed and 55% of the girls passed above, how many students passed? A: 70. Boys passed = 60% of 80 = 48; girls passed = 55% of 40 = 22; total = 70.
chunks.source: Boys passed = 60% of 80 = 48; girls passed = 55% of 40 = 22; total = 70.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 60. When sh. 400 is increased by x%, it becomes sh. 500. Find x. A: 25. (500 − 400) ÷ 400 = 25%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 61. David borrowed sh. 500,000 at 20% per year. What was the simple interest after 9 months? A: 75000. 500,000 × 0.2 × 0.75 = 75,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 62. At what rate will sh. 480,000 give sh. 2,400 interest in 2 months? A: 3. 2,400 ÷ (480,000 × 2/12) = 3%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 63. Florence cut 12 bars of soap into quarter pieces. How many small pieces did she get? A: 48. 12 × 4 = 48.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 65. Express 0.16 as a fraction in its lowest term. A: 4/25. 0.16 = 16/100 = 4/25.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 66. A woman deposited sh. 360,000 at 5% per year. After how long will she get sh. 10,500 interest? A: 7 months. 10,500 ÷ (360,000 × 0.05) = 0.583 years = 7 months.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 67. A boy had 20 km still to cover after travelling 3/4 of the journey. How long was the journey? A: 80 km. 1/4 of the journey = 20 km, so the whole = 80 km.
chunks.source: 1/4 of the journey = 20 km, so the whole = 80 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 68. Timothy bought a radio at sh. 280,000 and sold it to Willy at 20% profit. How much profit did Timothy make? A: 56000. 20% of 280,000 = 56,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 69. Willy sold the radio to Moses at 5% loss. How much did Moses pay? A: 319200. Willy paid 336,000; Moses paid 336,000 × 0.95 = 319,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 71. Write 8 1/3% as a fraction in its simplest form. A: 1/12. 8 1/3 ÷ 100 = 25/300 = 1/12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 72. Tea is sold in 3/4 kg packets. How many packets can be made from 24 kg? A: 32. 24 ÷ 3/4 = 32.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 73. A man spends 75% of his salary and saves sh. 180,000. Find his salary. A: 720000. 25% = 180,000, so 100% = 720,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 74. In a class, 3/4 of the pupils are boys and the rest are girls. What fraction are girls? A: 1/4. 1 − 3/4 = 1/4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 75. If there are 18 girls in the class above, how many boys are there? A: 54. Total = 72; boys = 72 − 18 = 54.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 76. Find the total number of pupils in the class above. A: 72. 18 × 4 = 72.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 77. In a basket, 5/8 of the apples are red, 1/6 are yellow and the rest are green. What fraction are green? A: 5/24. 1 − 5/8 − 1/6 = 5/24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 78. If there are 60 green apples in the basket above, how many apples are there altogether? A: 288. 60 ÷ 5/24 = 288.
