chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 80. Musoke's salary fell from sh. 240,000 to sh. 192,000. Find the percentage decrease. A: 20. (240,000 − 192,000) ÷ 240,000 = 20%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 81. Jane and Barbra shared sh. 904,000 in the ratio 5:3. How much more did Jane get than Barbra? A: 226000. One part = 113,000; difference = 2 × 113,000 = 226,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 82. Omut scored 16 marks out of 20. Express his mark as a percentage. A: 80. 16/20 = 80%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 83. In the ratio 2:3, Namu has 6 litres of milk. How many litres has Bagaga? A: 9. One part = 3 litres; Bagaga = 3 × 3 = 9.
chunks.source: One part = 3 litres; Bagaga = 3 × 3 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 84. Juma bought a goat at sh. 142,000 and sold it at 10% profit. Find the profit. A: 14200. 10% of 142,000 = 14,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 85. What was the selling price of Juma's goat? A: 156200. 142,000 + 14,200 = 156,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 86. A basket was sold at sh. 2,500 making a profit of sh. 500. Find the percentage profit. A: 25. Cost = 2,000; 500/2,000 = 25%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 90. Agatha, Angella and Angel shared dollars in the ratio 5:2:3. Agatha got 50 dollars more than Angel. How many dollars were shared? A: 250. 2 parts = 50, so 1 part = 25; total = 10 × 25 = 250.
chunks.source: 2 parts = 50, so 1 part = 25; total = 10 × 25 = 250.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 91. How many dollars did Angella get above? A: 50. 2 × 25 = 50.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 92. Sumaya sold a bicycle for sh. 170,000 making a profit of sh. 35,000. At what price did she buy the bicycle? A: 135000. 170,000 − 35,000 = 135,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 93. Share 40 bananas between Alice and Brenda in the ratio 2:3. How many does each get? A: 16, 24. One part = 8; Alice = 16, Brenda = 24.
chunks.source: One part = 8; Alice = 16, Brenda = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 94. Namagga spent sh. 20,000 making 50 chapatis and sold each at sh. 500. What was her percentage profit? A: 25%. Sales = 25,000; profit = 5,000; 5,000/20,000 = 25%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 95. Express 2/3 as a decimal, correct to 2 decimal places. A: 0.67. 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666…, which rounds to 0.67.
chunks.source: 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666…, which rounds to 0.67.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 96. 2% of Kiirya's salary is sh. 10,000. How much does he spend on basic needs (45% of his salary)? A: 225000. Salary = 500,000; 45% of 500,000 = 225,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 97. How much does Kiirya save above? A: 275000. 55% of 500,000 = 275,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 98. Seven boys can build a house in 9 days. How long will 21 boys take at the same rate? A: 3 days. 7 × 9 = 63 man-days; 63 ÷ 21 = 3 days.
chunks.source: 7 × 9 = 63 man-days; 63 ÷ 21 = 3 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 99. In a class of 40 pupils, 1/4 are girls. How many boys are there? A: 30. Girls = 10; boys = 40 − 10 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 100. Change 3/5 into a decimal. A: 0.6. 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 101. If 6 men can dig a pit latrine in 8 days, how long will 4 men take? A: 12 days. 6 × 8 = 48 man-days; 48 ÷ 4 = 12 days.
chunks.source: 6 × 8 = 48 man-days; 48 ÷ 4 = 12 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 102. 30 bottles of soda took 20 minutes to cool in a fridge. How long will 10 bottles take in the same fridge? A: 20 minutes. Cooling time does not change with fewer bottles.
chunks.source: Cooling time does not change with fewer bottles.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 105. After a 10% increase, Akello's salary is sh. 10,450. What was his original salary? A: 9500. 10,450 ÷ 1.1 = 9,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 106. The interest on sh. 20,000 for 2 years is sh. 1,200. Find the simple interest rate per year. A: 3. 1,200 ÷ (20,000 × 2) = 3%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 107. The ratio of men to women in a village is 5:7. If there are 63 women, how many adults are there in the village? A: 108. One part = 9; men = 45; total = 108.
chunks.source: One part = 9; men = 45; total = 108.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 108. How many more men are needed above to make the ratio 1:1? A: 18. 63 − 45 = 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 109. Okello sold a turkey for sh. 55,000 making a profit of sh. 9,500. How much did he buy it for? A: 45500. 55,000 − 9,500 = 45,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 111. Annet, Babra and Christine imported cars in the ratio 3:2:1. If Annet imported 48 cars, what is the total number of cars imported? A: 96. One part = 16; total = 6 × 16 = 96.
chunks.source: One part = 16; total = 6 × 16 = 96.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Simplify −6 − +6. A: -12. Going down 6 more from −6 gives −12.
chunks.source: Going down 6 more from −6 gives −12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Simplify −2 − −7. A: 5. Subtracting a negative is adding: −2 + 7 = 5.
chunks.source: Subtracting a negative is adding: −2 + 7 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. Arrange in descending order: +3, −8, 0, −1, +1. A: +3, +1, 0, -1, -8. Positive numbers first, then zero, then negatives.
chunks.source: Positive numbers first, then zero, then negatives.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. What integer is 8 steps to the right of −3? A: 5. −3 + 8 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. Work out (+4) × (−3). A: -12. Positive times negative gives negative: 4 × 3 = 12.
chunks.source: Positive times negative gives negative: 4 × 3 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. Moses put ice at −15°C, boiled it to 100°C, then let it cool by 60°C. What is the difference in temperature between the ice (−15°C) and the water he drank? A: 55°C. He drank it at 40°C; 40 − (−15) = 55.
chunks.source: He drank it at 40°C; 40 − (−15) = 55.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. In an interview, 2 marks are given for a correct answer and 1 mark deducted for a wrong one. A candidate got 5 correct and 3 wrong. What is the score? A: 7. (5 × 2) − 3 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. What is the score of a candidate who got 15 correct out of 20 questions above? A: 25. (15 × 2) − 5 = 25.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. A teacher gives 2 marks for a correct answer and subtracts 1 for a wrong one in a 20-question test. A pupil got 18 correct. What mark did the pupil get? A: 34. (18 × 2) − 2 = 34.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 11. A pupil got 25 marks in the test above. How many answers were correct? A: 15. 2c − (20 − c) = 25 gives 3c = 45, so c = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 12. Work out 2 − 3 (finite 5). A: 4. −1 in finite 5 is 4.
chunks.source: −1 in finite 5 is 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 13. Work out 5 + 6 + 4 (finite 7). A: 1. 15 ÷ 7 leaves remainder 1.
chunks.source: 15 ÷ 7 leaves remainder 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 14. Solve 2y − 3 = 3 (finite 5). A: 3. 2y = 6, so y = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 15. Solve 2(2p − 1) = 4 (finite 7). A: 5. 4p = 6 (finite 7); p = 5 works since 4 × 5 = 20 = 6.
chunks.source: 4p = 6 (finite 7); p = 5 works since 4 × 5 = 20 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 17. Divide 3 ÷ 5 (finite 12). A: 3. 3 × 5 = 15 = 3 (finite 12).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 18. Today is Wednesday. What day of the week will it be after 46 days? A: Sunday. 46 ÷ 7 leaves 4; Wednesday + 4 = Sunday.
chunks.source: 46 ÷ 7 leaves 4; Wednesday + 4 = Sunday.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 19. Today is Monday. What day of the week was it 54 days ago? A: Wednesday. 54 ÷ 7 leaves 5; 5 days before Monday is Wednesday.
chunks.source: 54 ÷ 7 leaves 5; 5 days before Monday is Wednesday.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 20. Today is Wednesday 14th June. What day of the week will it be on 29th August the same year? A: Tuesday. 76 days later; 76 ÷ 7 leaves 6; Wednesday + 6 = Tuesday.
chunks.source: 76 days later; 76 ÷ 7 leaves 6; Wednesday + 6 = Tuesday.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 21. A boy was born 81 months ago. It is January now. In which month was he born? A: April. 81 ÷ 12 leaves 9; 9 months before January is April.
chunks.source: 81 ÷ 12 leaves 9; 9 months before January is April.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 22. It is 4:30 a.m. now. What time of the day will it be after 66 hours? A: 10:30 p.m.. 66 ÷ 24 leaves 18 hours; 4:30 + 18 h = 10:30 p.m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 23. What is the least number of cows which leaves remainder 3 when divided by 4 and remainder 7 when divided by 8? A: 7. 7 ÷ 8 leaves 7, and 7 ÷ 4 leaves 3.
chunks.source: 7 ÷ 8 leaves 7, and 7 ÷ 4 leaves 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 24. A watch loses 5 seconds every hour. How many minutes does it lose in 2 days? A: 4. 48 × 5 = 240 seconds = 4 minutes.
chunks.source: 48 × 5 = 240 seconds = 4 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 25. A watch loses 5 seconds per hour. In how many hours will it lose 2 minutes? A: 24 hours. 120 ÷ 5 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 26. Solve 2y − 3 = 4 (finite 5). A: 1. 2y = 7 = 2 (finite 5), so y = 1.
chunks.source: 2y = 7 = 2 (finite 5), so y = 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 27. Work out −3 − 8. A: -11. Going down 8 more from −3 gives −11.
chunks.source: Going down 8 more from −3 gives −11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 29. Use the number line to work out −8 + +6. A: -2. Start at −8 and move 6 steps right to −2.
chunks.source: Start at −8 and move 6 steps right to −2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 30. Work out −4 + −2. A: -6. Going down 2 more from −4 gives −6.
chunks.source: Going down 2 more from −4 gives −6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 31. Simplify −5 + −7. A: -12. Going down 7 more from −5 gives −12.
chunks.source: Going down 7 more from −5 gives −12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 33. Arrange starting with the largest: 3, 0, −2, 5, −4. A: 5, 3, 0, -2, -4. Positives first, then zero, then negatives.
chunks.source: Positives first, then zero, then negatives.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 34. Simplify −4 − +7. A: -11. Going down 7 more from −4 gives −11.
chunks.source: Going down 7 more from −4 gives −11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 35. Express 0, −3, +4, −7, +5, +7 in ascending order. A: -7, -3, 0, +4, +5, +7. Start with the most negative.
chunks.source: Start with the most negative.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 36. Work out 3 + 1 (finite 7). A: 4. 3 + 1 = 4, which is less than 7.
chunks.source: 3 + 1 = 4, which is less than 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 37. If y + 2 = 1 (finite 3), find y. A: 2. 2 + 2 = 4 = 1 (finite 3).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 38. If today is Monday, what day of the week will it be after 38 days? A: Thursday. 38 ÷ 7 leaves 3; Monday + 3 = Thursday.
chunks.source: 38 ÷ 7 leaves 3; Monday + 3 = Thursday.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Two coins are tossed at once. What is the probability that a head and a tail show on top? A: 1/2. Outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT; 2 out of 4 give one head and one tail.
chunks.source: Outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT; 2 out of 4 give one head and one tail.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. A bag has 15 pens; 4 are red and the rest blue. What is the probability of picking a blue pen? A: 11/15. 11 blue pens out of 15.
chunks.source: 11 blue pens out of 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. A basket has 3 rotten eggs and 6 good ones. What is the probability of picking a rotten egg? A: 1/3. 3 rotten out of 9 eggs = 1/3.
chunks.source: 3 rotten out of 9 eggs = 1/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. A team's chance of winning a game is 3/5. If the team plays 15 games, how many games is it expected to lose? A: 6. Lose 2/5 of 15 = 6.
chunks.source: Lose 2/5 of 15 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. What is the probability that Mr. Musoke's birthday falls on a day starting with the letter S? A: 2/7. Saturday and Sunday start with S: 2 out of 7 days.
chunks.source: Saturday and Sunday start with S: 2 out of 7 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. A football team can win, draw or lose a match. What is the probability that it will win a match? A: 1/3. One winning outcome out of three.
chunks.source: One winning outcome out of three.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. A die is tossed once. What is the probability that a prime number appears on top? A: 1/2. Primes 2, 3, 5: 3 out of 6 = 1/2.
chunks.source: Primes 2, 3, 5: 3 out of 6 = 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. What is the probability that a composite number shows up on the die above? A: 1/3. Composites 4, 6: 2 out of 6 = 1/3.
chunks.source: Composites 4, 6: 2 out of 6 = 1/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. What is the probability that a 5 shows up on the die above? A: 1/6. One 5 out of 6 faces.
chunks.source: One 5 out of 6 faces.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. What is the probability that a number less than 4 shows up on the die above? A: 1/2. 1, 2, 3: 3 out of 6 = 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 11. Pupils scored: 50 (2 pupils), k (6 pupils), 45 (3 pupils), 80 (4 pupils). How many pupils did the test? A: 15. 2 + 6 + 3 + 4 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 12. If the mean mark above was 61, find the value of k. A: 60. (100 + 6k + 135 + 320) ÷ 15 = 61 gives k = 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 13. What was the range of the marks above? A: 35. 80 − 45 = 35.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 14. Find the median mark above. A: 60. The 8th mark in order is 60.
chunks.source: The 8th mark in order is 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 15. The mean of the numbers 7, 9, 5, x + 2 and 6 is 8. Find the value of x. A: 11. Total = 40; x + 2 = 13, so x = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 16. Work out the range of the numbers above. A: 8. The numbers run from 5 to 13; range = 8.
chunks.source: The numbers run from 5 to 13; range = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 17. The average age of 3 girls is 11 years. One of the girls is 12 years old. Find the average age of the other two girls. A: 10.5. Total = 33; others = 21; 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 18. The average age of 8 pupils is 15 years. If pupils aged 10 and 14 leave the group, what is the average age of the remaining pupils? A: 16. Total = 120; rest = 96 ÷ 6 = 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 19. The average weight of 14 pupils is 50 kg. When the teacher joins, the average becomes 51 kg. What is the teacher's weight? A: 65 kg. 15 × 51 − 14 × 50 = 65.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 20. The average weight of 3 boys is 32 kg. When a fourth boy joins, the average becomes 40 kg. Find the weight of the fourth boy. A: 64. 4 × 40 − 3 × 32 = 64.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 21. Find the mean of 6, 5x, 2 and 7x. A: 3x + 2. (8 + 12x) ÷ 4 = 3x + 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 22. Sumaya's homework marks: 2, 5, 7, 3, 10, 4, 7, 11, 8, 3. Find her median mark. A: 6. Ordered: 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 7, 7, 8, 10, 11; median = (5 + 7) ÷ 2 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 23. What is the probability that Sumaya scored a mark above her mean mark? A: 1/2. Mean = 6; marks above 6: 7, 7, 8, 10, 11 = 5 out of 10.
chunks.source: Mean = 6; marks above 6: 7, 7, 8, 10, 11 = 5 out of 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 24. Marks scored: 70 (3 pupils), 40 (4 pupils), 30 (2 pupils), 50 (1 pupil). How many pupils did the test? A: 10. 3 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 25. Find the mean mark above. A: 48. (210 + 160 + 60 + 50) ÷ 10 = 48.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 26. Find the mean of y − 2, y, y − 4 and y − 6. A: y - 3. (4y − 12) ÷ 4 = y − 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 27. The mean mark of 1, 3, 4, 5, t, 8 and 13 is 6. Find the value of t. A: 8. Total = 42; t = 42 − 34 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 28. Find the median mark above. A: 5. Ordered: 1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 8, 13; middle = 5.
chunks.source: Ordered: 1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 8, 13; middle = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 29. Children recorded: 2 aged 9, 1 aged 11, 4 aged 12, 1 aged 13, 1 aged 18. How many children were recorded altogether? A: 9. 2 + 1 + 4 + 1 + 1 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 30. Find the range of the ages above. A: 9. 18 − 9 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 31. What is the modal frequency above? A: 4. The highest frequency is 4 (age 12).
chunks.source: The highest frequency is 4 (age 12).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 32. Find the mean age above. A: 12. (18 + 11 + 48 + 13 + 18) ÷ 9 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 33. If one picture represents 7 balls, how many pictures are needed to represent 42 balls? A: 6. 42 ÷ 7 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 34. A man spends 1/4 of his income on rent and 4/9 of the remainder on food, and saves sh. 360,000. What fraction of his income does he save? A: 5/12. 1 − 1/4 − 1/3 = 5/12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 35. What is his income above? A: 864000. 5/12 = 360,000, so income = 864,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 36. Express 5 m/sec in km/hr. A: 18. 5 × 3.6 = 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 37. Change 72 km/hr to m/sec. A: 20. 72 × 5/18 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 38. Joshua 70, Joan 40, Jane 50, Joseph 30. Work out the median mark. A: 45. Ordered: 30, 40, 50, 70; median = (40 + 50) ÷ 2 = 45.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 39. Calculate the mean mark above. A: 47.5. 190 ÷ 4 = 47.5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 40. A pie chart shows land use: beans 25%, maize 40%, millet 20%, potatoes y%. Find y. A: 15. 100 − 25 − 40 − 20 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 41. If 1,200 sq.m is used for potatoes above, what is the total area of the land? A: 8000. 15% = 1,200, so total = 8,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 42. Express the land used for potatoes as degrees of the pie chart. A: 54. 15% of 360° = 54°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 43. Find the mean of n, 3n − 5 and 2n − 7. A: 2n - 4. (6n − 12) ÷ 3 = 2n − 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 44. Isma scored 21 goals and Damalie scored 12. Find the range of their scores. A: 9. 21 − 12 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 45. Jane is 9 years old and Peter is 2 years older than Jane. Find their mean age. A: 10. (9 + 11) ÷ 2 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 46. A bag has 10 blue and 5 red pens. What is the probability of picking a red pen at random? A: 1/3. 5 red out of 15 = 1/3.
chunks.source: 5 red out of 15 = 1/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 47. Marks: 35 (2 pupils), 40 (3 pupils), 50 (2 pupils), 70 (2 pupils), 90 (1 pupil). What was the modal mark? A: 40. 40 has the highest frequency (3).
chunks.source: 40 has the highest frequency (3).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 48. Find the range of the marks above. A: 55. 90 − 35 = 55.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 49. Work out the mean mark above. A: 52. (70 + 120 + 100 + 140 + 90) ÷ 10 = 52.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 50. Ashaba's marks: 2 (twice), 3, 4, 5 (twice), 6. What is the probability that she scored 5 marks? A: 2/7. 2 fives out of 7 marks.
chunks.source: 2 fives out of 7 marks.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 51. The ages of immunised children were recorded (30 children). How many children were immunised during the week? A: 30. Count all the ages: 30.
chunks.source: Count all the ages: 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 52. What was the modal age above? A: 6. Age 6 appears 10 times, more than any other.
chunks.source: Age 6 appears 10 times, more than any other.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 53. Calculate the average age of the children aged above 7 above. A: 9. Ages 8, 9, 10 appear 3 times each: (24 + 27 + 30) ÷ 9 = 9.
chunks.source: Ages 8, 9, 10 appear 3 times each: (24 + 27 + 30) ÷ 9 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 54. The average mass of 3 pupils is 35 kg. When a fourth pupil joins, the average becomes 40 kg. Find the mass of the fourth pupil. A: 55. 4 × 40 − 3 × 35 = 55.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 55. Ann's marks: 4 (twice), 7, 6 (4 times), 7, 8 (twice). What is the probability that she scored a 6? A: 2/5. 4 sixes out of 10 marks = 2/5.
chunks.source: 4 sixes out of 10 marks = 2/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 56. Points A(−3, 3), B(−3, −3), C(4, −3) are joined to form a triangle. Find the length of BC in units. A: 7. From x = −3 to x = 4 is 7 units.
chunks.source: From x = −3 to x = 4 is 7 units.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 57. A picture represents 9 carrots. How many pictures can represent 63 carrots? A: 7. 63 ÷ 9 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Haruna bought: rice 2 kg (sh. 8,800), meat (sh. 5,000 at sh. 10,000 per kg), soap 3 bars at sh. 7,000 per bar. What was his total expenditure? A: 34800. 8,800 + 5,000 + 21,000 = 34,800.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. If Haruna remained with sh. 50,000 as his balance, how much money did he have at first? A: 84800. 34,800 + 50,000 = 84,800.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. A tourist has 600 US dollars (buying rate sh. 2,500) and 400 Kenya shillings (buying rate sh. 18). How much in Uganda shillings can he get? A: 1507200. 600 × 2,500 + 400 × 18 = 1,507,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. Sarah has sh. 900,000. How many US dollars can she get at the selling rate of sh. 3,000? A: 300. 900,000 ÷ 3,000 = 300.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. Namutebi bought: 3 bars of soap at sh. 3,500; 2 1/2 litres of milk at sh. 1,500 per half litre; 250 g of sugar at sh. 4,200 per kg. How much did she spend altogether? A: 19050. 10,500 + 7,500 + 1,050 = 19,050.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. If Namutebi went to the market with sh. 20,000, what was her change? A: 950. 20,000 − 19,050 = 950.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. Amos bought: 2 pineapples at sh. 2,000 each; 0.5 kg of sugar at sh. 3,200 per kg; 1 1/2 kg of meat at sh. 8,000 per kg; 1 bunch of matooke at sh. 18,000. How much did he spend altogether? A: 35600. 4,000 + 1,600 + 12,000 + 18,000 = 35,600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. A maid bought: 10 books at sh. 600; 5 pencils (sh. 1,500 total); 5 pens at sh. 200; 3 rulers at sh. 500. What was the total cost? A: 10000. 6,000 + 1,500 + 1,000 + 1,500 = 10,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. If the maid above was given a 10% discount, how much did she pay? A: 9000. 10,000 × 0.9 = 9,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. Namagga bought: a tin of charcoal sh. 3,000; 2 packets of flour at sh. 5,500 each; 1 1/2 litres of cooking oil at sh. 4,000 per litre. Find her total expenditure. A: 20000. 3,000 + 11,000 + 6,000 = 20,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 11. A school has 41 P.7 pupils. How much examination fee is collected at sh. 22,000 each? A: 902000. 41 × 22,000 = 902,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 12. Okiror pays for a P5 day scholar (sh. 72,000), a P6 day scholar (sh. 85,000) and a P7 boarder (sh. 216,000). How much does he pay to the school? A: 373000. 72,000 + 85,000 + 216,000 = 373,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 13. One pair of jeans costs sh. 9,000 and one busuuti costs sh. 35,000. Find the cost of 2 jeans and 3 busuuti. A: 123000. 18,000 + 105,000 = 123,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 14. Atim bought 4 pens at sh. 500 each, a geometry set at sh. 2,500 and 2 rulers at sh. 1,000 each. How much did she pay altogether? A: 6500. 2,000 + 2,500 + 2,000 = 6,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 15. Walter bought 2 geometry sets (sh. 2,500 each), 6 rulers (sh. 1,000 each) and 10 pencils (sh. 1,800 a dozen), and got a 20% discount. What did he actually pay? A: 10000. 5,000 + 6,000 + 1,500 = 12,500; 12,500 × 0.8 = 10,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Study the figure (right-angled triangle ABC with AB = 6 dm, BD = 4 dm, DC = 5 dm). Find the area of the unshaded triangle ADC. A: 15. 1/2 × 5 × 6 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Calculate the area of triangle ABC in the figure. A: 27. 1/2 × 9 × 6 = 27.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. Calculate the perimeter of triangle ADC in the figure (AD = 7 dm, AC = 10 dm). A: 22. 7 + 5 + 10 = 22.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. In the diagram, line AB is parallel to line CD. Find the value of m. A: 40. m and 40° are alternate interior angles.
chunks.source: m and 40° are alternate interior angles.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. Find the bearing of town M from town K. (The diagram shows 030° measured clockwise from north at K to M.) A: 030. Bearings are measured clockwise from north; it is 030°.
chunks.source: Bearings are measured clockwise from north; it is 030°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. Find the area of a circle whose circumference is 132 cm. (Use π = 22/7.) A: 1386 cm². r = 132 ÷ (2 × 22/7) = 21; area = 22/7 × 21² = 1,386.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. Find the distance around the triangle with sides 8 cm, 10 cm and 12 cm. A: 30 cm. 8 + 10 + 12 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. Find the supplement of (40 − y)°. A: 140 + y. 180 − (40 − y) = 140 + y.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. The interior angle of a regular polygon is 36° more than its exterior angle. Find the exterior angle. A: 72. 180 − 2e = 36, so e = 72.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. Name the regular polygon above. A: pentagon. 360 ÷ 72 = 5 sides.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 11. Calculate the interior angle sum of the polygon above. A: 540. (5 − 2) × 180 = 540.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 12. Calculate the area of a circle of radius 5 cm. (Use π = 3.14.) A: 78.5 cm². 3.14 × 25 = 78.5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 13. Work out the circumference of a circle of diameter 28 cm. (Use π = 22/7.) A: 88. 22/7 × 28 = 88.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 14. A rhombus has diagonals 10 cm and 24 cm. Calculate the length of one side. A: 13. √(5² + 12²) = 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 15. Find the perimeter of the rhombus above. A: 52. 4 × 13 = 52.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 16. How many right angles does a regular hexagon have? A: 0. Each interior angle is 120°, so none is 90°.
chunks.source: Each interior angle is 120°, so none is 90°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 17. A regular hexagon has side 4 cm. Calculate its perimeter. A: 24. 6 × 4 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Add: 5 weeks 4 days + 2 weeks 6 days. A: 8 weeks 3 days. 7 weeks 10 days = 8 weeks 3 days.
chunks.source: 7 weeks 10 days = 8 weeks 3 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. A forty-minute lesson started at 9:30 a.m. At what time did the lesson end? A: 10:10 a.m.. 9:30 + 0:40 = 10:10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. A driver moved a distance of 180 km in 1 1/2 hours. At what speed was he moving? A: 120 km/hr. 180 ÷ 1.5 = 120.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. A meeting which lasted 1 1/3 hours ended at 5:10 p.m. What time did it start? A: 3:50 p.m.. 5:10 − 1:20 = 3:50.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. Mr. Mawanda walked 1,800 metres in 18 minutes. Find his average speed in km/hr. A: 6 km/hr. 100 m/min = 6 km/h.
chunks.source: 100 m/min = 6 km/h.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. Study the distance–time graph. Find the motorist's speed from home to town N. A: 40. 80 km in 2 hours = 40 km/h.
chunks.source: 80 km in 2 hours = 40 km/h.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. At what time did the motorist leave town N on the graph? A: 10:30 a.m.. The flat part ends at 10:30 a.m.
chunks.source: The flat part ends at 10:30 a.m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. Calculate the average speed for the whole journey on the graph. A: 30. 120 km in 4 hours = 30 km/h.
chunks.source: 120 km in 4 hours = 30 km/h.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. A motorist covered 360 km in 3 hours from home to town A, then continued to town B at 90 km/h for 2 hours. How far is town B from town A? A: 180. 90 × 2 = 180.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. Work out the average speed for the whole journey above. A: 108. 540 km ÷ 5 h = 108 km/h.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 11. How long does a train moving at 48 km/hr take to cover a distance of 36 km? A: 45 minutes. 36 ÷ 48 = 0.75 h = 45 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 12. A motorist left town A at 9:15 a.m. driving at 80 km/hr and reached town B at 11:45 a.m. How long did the journey take? A: 2.5 hours. 11:45 − 9:15 = 2 h 30 min.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 13. How far is town B from town A above? A: 200. 80 × 2.5 = 200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 14. If his car uses 3 litres of fuel for every 40 km, how many litres are needed for the journey above? A: 15. 200 ÷ 40 × 3 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 15. Add: 6 weeks 4 days + 2 weeks 5 days. A: 9 weeks 2 days. 8 weeks 9 days = 9 weeks 2 days.
chunks.source: 8 weeks 9 days = 9 weeks 2 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 16. Musoke covered a distance of 25 km in 30 minutes. Calculate his speed in km/hr. A: 50 km/hr. 25 km in half an hour = 50 km/h.
chunks.source: 25 km in half an hour = 50 km/h.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 17. A football match ended at 12:50 a.m. Express this time in the 24-hour clock. A: 00:50. 12:50 a.m. = 00:50.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 18. Express 36 km/hr in metres per second. A: 10. 36 × 5/18 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 19. A bus timetable shows: Tororo 0 km (departs 9:00), Iganga 60 km, Jinja 100 km, Kampala 150 km (arrives 21:25). Find the distance between Iganga and Kampala. A: 90. 150 − 60 = 90.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 20. How long did the bus rest at Jinja? (Arrived 19:10, departed 19:40.) A: 30 minutes. 19:40 − 19:10 = 30 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 21. How long did the whole Tororo–Kampala trip take? A: 12 hours 25 minutes. 21:25 − 9:00 = 12 h 25 min.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 22. Find the total time the bus spent resting. (Iganga rest 35 min, Jinja rest 30 min.) A: 1 hour 5 minutes. 35 + 30 = 65 minutes.
chunks.source: 35 + 30 = 65 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 23. A meeting which started at 11:50 a.m. ended at 1:00 p.m. How long did the meeting last? A: 1 hour 10 minutes. 11:50 → 1:00 is 1 h 10 min.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 24. Mulero had to cover 147 km in 3 1/2 hours at a constant speed. At what speed was he driving? A: 42. 147 ÷ 3.5 = 42.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 25. What distance was Mulero left with after driving for 2 hours above? A: 63. 147 − 84 = 63.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 26. An examination began at 7:35 a.m. and lasted 2 1/2 hours. At what time did it end? A: 10:05 a.m.. 7:35 + 2:30 = 10:05.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 27. A baby started sleeping at 9:10 a.m. and woke up at 1:40 p.m. For how long did she sleep? A: 4 hours 30 minutes. 9:10 → 1:40 is 4 h 30 min.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 28. Kato (80 km/hr) and Wasswa (60 km/hr) left Kampala for Masaka at the same time. How far apart were they after the first 30 minutes? A: 10. 40 − 30 = 10 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 29. If both left at 9:00 a.m., at what time did Kato arrive at Masaka (120 km away)? A: 10:30 a.m.. 120 ÷ 80 = 1.5 h; 9:00 + 1:30 = 10:30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 30. How long did Kato wait at Masaka before Wasswa arrived? A: 30 minutes. Wasswa took 2 h, arriving at 11:00; 11:00 − 10:30 = 30 min.
chunks.source: Wasswa took 2 h, arriving at 11:00; 11:00 − 10:30 = 30 min.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 31. A school van was driven at 80 km/hr from 8:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. Find the distance it covered. A: 240. 80 × 3 = 240.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 32. How long did the return journey above take at 96 km/hr? A: 2.5 hours. 240 ÷ 96 = 2.5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. The base area of a cube is 49 cm². Calculate the volume of the cube. A: 343 cm³. Side = 7 cm; volume = 7³ = 343 cm³.
chunks.source: Side = 7 cm; volume = 7³ = 343 cm³.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Cylindrical tins (diameter 6 cm, height 14 cm) are packed into a box 18 cm × 42 cm × 20 cm. How many tins fit in the first layer? A: 21. (18 ÷ 6) × (42 ÷ 6) = 3 × 7 = 21.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. How many layers of tins can be packed in the box above? A: 1. 20 ÷ 14 = 1 remainder.
chunks.source: 20 ÷ 14 = 1 remainder.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. Find the volume of the empty space after packing the tins. (Use π = 22/7.) A: 6804. Box = 15,120; tins = 21 × 396 = 8,316; space = 6,804 cm³.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. The cost of 1 kg of rice is sh. 3,600. Find the cost of 250 grams of rice. A: 900. 250 g = 1/4 kg; 3,600 ÷ 4 = 900.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. A milkman sells milk in quarter-litre cups. How many cups can he sell from a ten-litre jerrycan? A: 40. 10 ÷ 1/4 = 40.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. A bicycle wheel has diameter 35 cm. How many revolutions does it make to cover 22 metres? (Use π = 22/7.) A: 20. Circumference = 110 cm = 1.1 m; 22 ÷ 1.1 = 20.
chunks.source: Circumference = 110 cm = 1.1 m; 22 ÷ 1.1 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. Express 1.5 km into metres. A: 1500. 1.5 × 1,000 = 1,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. Kamatu bought 700 g of salt at sh. 500 a kilogram. How much did he actually pay? A: 350. 0.7 × 500 = 350.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. Calculate the volume of a cube whose width is 12 cm. A: 1728. 12³ = 1,728 cm³.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 11. The diagram shows a rectangle 6 m by 4 m. Kipromo ran round it three times. What total distance did he cover? A: 60. Perimeter = 20 m; 3 × 20 = 60 m.
chunks.source: Perimeter = 20 m; 3 × 20 = 60 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. The age of Ben is thrice that of Ali. If Ali is 12 years old, how old is Ben? A: 36. 3 × 12 = 36.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Given that a = −3 and b = 4, find the value of 2b − 2a. A: 14. 8 − (−6) = 14.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. The sum of 3 consecutive even numbers is 24. If the largest number is k, find the three numbers. A: 6, 8, 10. k − 4, k − 2, k; 3k − 6 = 24 gives k = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. The rectangle has its two shorter sides marked equal: (3y − 5) cm and (y + 5) cm. Find y. A: 5. 3y − 5 = y + 5 gives y = 5.
chunks.source: 3y − 5 = y + 5 gives y = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. Find the area of the rectangle above (the longer side is (4y + 6) cm). A: 260. Sides are 10 cm and 26 cm; 10 × 26 = 260 cm².
chunks.source: Sides are 10 cm and 26 cm; 10 × 26 = 260 cm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. Simplify 9k − 4y − 3k + 5y. A: 6k + y. 9k − 3k = 6k; −4y + 5y = y.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. Given that p = 4 and r = −3, find the value of (3p + r) ÷ r. A: -3. (12 − 3) ÷ (−3) = −3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. Simplify (y + 6)/2 + (y − 2)/5. A: (7y + 26)/10. Common denominator 10: (5y + 30 + 2y − 4)/10.
chunks.source: Common denominator 10: (5y + 30 + 2y − 4)/10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 11. Solve the inequality −6 ≤ −3(k − 2). A: k ≤ 4. 2 ≥ k − 2, so k ≤ 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 12. Simplify 5p − q − p − 2q. A: 4p - 3q. 5p − p = 4p; −q − 2q = −3q.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 17. Simplify a⁶ × a² ÷ a³. A: a^5. a^(6+2−3) = a⁵.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 18. The sum of 3 consecutive odd numbers is 87. Find the numbers. A: 27, 29, 31. Middle = 87 ÷ 3 = 29.
chunks.source: Middle = 87 ÷ 3 = 29.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 19. Work out the range of the numbers above. A: 4. 31 − 27 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 22. Remove the brackets and simplify: 8(m − 1) + 3(m + 2). A: 11m - 2. 8m − 8 + 3m + 6 = 11m − 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 24. Given that a = 5 and b = 2, find the value of 2ba/5. A: 4. (2 × 2 × 5) ÷ 5 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 25. Find the value of d if 2d ÷ 4 = 8. A: 16. 2d = 32, so d = 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 27. Find the first 2 values of n if 4 − 3n ≤ 13. A: -3, -2. −3n ≤ 9 gives n ≥ −3; first two: −3, −2.
chunks.source: −3n ≤ 9 gives n ≥ −3; first two: −3, −2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 28. The sum of three consecutive numbers is 96. Find the numbers. A: 31, 32, 33. Middle = 96 ÷ 3 = 32.
chunks.source: Middle = 96 ÷ 3 = 32.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.source: 3a − 3 − 2a + 4 = 3 gives a = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 31. Wanyama is 3 years younger than his elder sister Nasirumbi. In 15 years time, their total age will be 49 years. How old is Wanyama? A: 8. (x + 15) + (x + 18) = 49 gives x = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 32. The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 54 and the first number is y. Find the value of y. A: 16. y + (y + 2) + (y + 4) = 54 gives y = 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 33. Work out the range of the numbers above. A: 4. The numbers are 16, 18, 20; 20 − 16 = 4.
chunks.source: The numbers are 16, 18, 20; 20 − 16 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 34. Given that a = −4 and b = −3, work out b(a − b). A: 3. −3 × (−4 + 3) = −3 × (−1) = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 36. Solve the inequality 3(x + 4) < 5x − 2. A: x > 7. 3x + 12 < 5x − 2 gives 14 < 2x.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 40. Kasiri is 3 years old and his mother is 25 years old. How old will the mother be when Kasiri is 25? A: 47. The difference is 22 years; 25 + 22 = 47.
chunks.source: The difference is 22 years; 25 + 22 = 47.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 41. Moses and Janet got (3y − 8) apples altogether. If Janet got y apples and Moses got (y − 2) apples, what is the value of y? A: 6. y + (y − 2) = 3y − 8 gives y = 6.
chunks.source: y + (y − 2) = 3y − 8 gives y = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 42. Three children aged (x + 3), (3x − 10) and (2x + 5) have a total age of 34 years. How old is each child? A: 9, 8, 17. 6x − 2 = 34 gives x = 6; ages 9, 8, 17.
chunks.source: 6x − 2 = 34 gives x = 6; ages 9, 8, 17.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 43. Ham is 4 years younger than Tom, and Sam is 4 years older than Tom. In 10 years time, the sum of their ages will be 63 years. How old is Tom now? A: 11. (x − 4 + 10) + (x + 10) + (x + 4 + 10) = 63 gives x = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 44. Find the difference between Sam's and Ham's ages after ten years above. A: 8. Sam − Ham = 8 always.
chunks.source: Sam − Ham = 8 always.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 3. A set has 31 proper subsets. How many elements does the set have? A: 5. Proper subsets = 2^n − 1, so 2^n = 32 and n = 5.
chunks.source: Proper subsets = 2^n − 1, so 2^n = 32 and n = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 4. Given that the universal set is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}, A = {2, 4, 6} and B = {4, 5, 6, 7}, find (A ∪ B)' (the complement of A union B). A: {1, 3}. A ∪ B = {2, 4, 5, 6, 7}, so the elements left in the universal set are 1 and 3.
chunks.source: A ∪ B = {2, 4, 5, 6, 7}, so the elements left in the universal set are 1 and 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 6. In a class of 30 pupils, y like English only, 10 like both English and French, 7 like French only and 4 like neither language. How many pupils like English only? A: 9. y + 10 + 7 + 4 = 30, so y = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 8. In a class of 60 pupils, 30 took part in football, y took part in volleyball only, 10 took part in both games and 2y took part in neither. Find the value of y. A: 10. (30 − 10) + 10 + y + 2y = 60, so 3y = 30 and y = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 9. Using the value of y above, how many pupils took part in neither football nor volleyball? A: 20. Neither = 2y = 2 × 10 = 20.
chunks.source: Neither = 2y = 2 × 10 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 11. Given that set Q has 15 proper subsets, find n(Q) (the number of elements in Q). A: 4. 2^n − 1 = 15, so 2^n = 16 and n = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 12. In a group of players, 32 like tennis, 7 like football only, y like both games and 5 like neither. If 27 players like football, how many players are in the group altogether? A: 44. y = 27 − 7 = 20; total = 32 + 7 + 5 = 44.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 13. What is the probability of choosing a player who likes netball from the group above? A: 0. Nobody in the group plays netball, so the probability is 0.
chunks.source: Nobody in the group plays netball, so the probability is 0.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 14. In a Venn diagram, 40 pupils like mathematics (M) and some like English (E), while t like both. The regions are: M only = 2t + 10, both = t, E only = 3t − 5, neither = 3. Find the value of t. A: 10. (2t + 10) + t = 40, so 3t = 30 and t = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 15. Using t = 10 above, how many pupils like English? A: 35. English = t + (3t − 5) = 10 + 25 = 35.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 16. Using the same Venn diagram, how many pupils are there altogether? A: 68. 40 + 25 + 3 = 68.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 17. At a party, 2y guests ate beef only, 14 ate chicken only, (y + 7) ate both and (y − 1) ate none. If 29 guests did not eat chicken, find y. A: 10. 2y + (y − 1) = 29, so 3y = 30 and y = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 18. How many guests attended the party above? A: 60. 20 + 14 + 17 + 9 = 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 19. At Okello's birthday party, 16 guests took water, 30 took soda and 10 took both. How many guests took only one type of drink? A: 26. (16 − 10) + (30 − 10) = 6 + 20 = 26.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 20. How many guests attended Okello's party? A: 36. 6 + 10 + 20 = 36.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 21. Given X = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} and Y = {1, 3, 5, 7, 9}, find n(Y − X). A: 2. Y − X = {7, 9}, which has 2 elements.
chunks.source: Y − X = {7, 9}, which has 2 elements.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 22. Given that set Y = {all prime numbers less than 12}, find n(Y). A: 5. Y = {2, 3, 5, 7, 11}, which has 5 members.
chunks.source: Y = {2, 3, 5, 7, 11}, which has 5 members.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 23. In a home of 8 people, 5 like eating meat and 6 like eating fish. If everyone who eats only one dish is given 3 eggs, how many eggs are served? A: 15. Both = 5 + 6 − 8 = 3; only one dish = 8 − 3 = 5; eggs = 5 × 3 = 15.
chunks.source: Both = 5 + 6 − 8 = 3; only one dish = 8 − 3 = 5; eggs = 5 × 3 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 24. A Venn diagram shows boys who play volleyball (V) and tennis (T): 5 play volleyball only, 4 play both, 3 play tennis only. How many play only one game? A: 8. Only one game = 5 + 3 = 8.
chunks.source: Only one game = 5 + 3 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 1. What is the place value of 3 in the number 3,564? A: thousands. The 3 is in the fourth position from the right, the thousands place.
chunks.source: The 3 is in the fourth position from the right, the thousands place.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 3. Write 'four hundred four thousand forty four' in figures. A: 404044. 404 thousand and 44 ones make 404,044.
chunks.source: 404 thousand and 44 ones make 404,044.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 7. What is the place value of 0 in the number 203four? A: fours. In base four the positions are ones, fours, sixteens; 0 is in the fours place.
chunks.source: In base four the positions are ones, fours, sixteens; 0 is in the fours place.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 13. How many hands and fingers are needed to count 48? A: 9 hands and 3 fingers. Each hand has 5 fingers; 48 ÷ 5 = 9 remainder 3.
chunks.source: Each hand has 5 fingers; 48 ÷ 5 = 9 remainder 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 14. Find the difference between the value of 3 and the place value of 4 in the number 73,946. A: 2990. Value of 3 = 3,000; place value of 4 = tens = 10; 3,000 − 10 = 2,990.
chunks.source: Value of 3 = 3,000; place value of 4 = tens = 10; 3,000 − 10 = 2,990.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 16. Using the digits 5, 0 and 3, form the smallest three-digit numeral. A: 305. The smallest hundreds digit (not zero) is 3, then 0, then 5.
chunks.source: The smallest hundreds digit (not zero) is 3, then 0, then 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 17. Find the difference between the largest and the smallest numeral formed from 5, 0 and 3. A: 225. 530 − 305 = 225.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 18. Round off 23,456 to the nearest hundred. A: 23500. The tens digit is 5, so round up to 23,500.
chunks.source: The tens digit is 5, so round up to 23,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 19. Round off 456.27 to the nearest whole number. A: 456. The first decimal is 2, which is less than 5, so round down.
chunks.source: The first decimal is 2, which is less than 5, so round down.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 20. Write 500 in standard form (scientific notation). A: 5 x 10^2. 500 = 5 × 100 = 5 × 10².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 21. Write 30.45 in standard form (scientific notation). A: 3.045 x 10^1. 30.45 = 3.045 × 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 22. Write 0.00204 in standard form (scientific notation). A: 2.04 x 10^-3. 0.00204 = 2.04 × 10⁻³.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 23. Write the number whose scientific notation is 6.45 × 10³. A: 6450. Move the point 3 places to the right.
chunks.source: Move the point 3 places to the right.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 24. Write the number whose scientific notation is 3.9 × 10⁻². A: 0.039. Move the point 2 places to the left.
chunks.source: Move the point 2 places to the left.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 26. Round off 47 to the nearest ten. A: 50. The ones digit 7 is 5 or more, so round up.
chunks.source: The ones digit 7 is 5 or more, so round up.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 28. Write the number whose scientific notation is 8.61 × 10⁻². A: 0.0861. Move the point 2 places to the left.
chunks.source: Move the point 2 places to the left.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 31. If 103x = 28ten, find the value of x. A: 5. x² + 3 = 28, so x² = 25 and x = 5.
chunks.source: x² + 3 = 28, so x² = 25 and x = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 32. Using the number 3,418: what is the place value of 4? A: hundreds. The 4 is third from the right, in the hundreds place.
chunks.source: The 4 is third from the right, in the hundreds place.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 33. Find the value of 4 in 3,418. A: 400. 4 hundreds = 400.
chunks.source: 4 hundreds = 400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 34. Write 'forty three thousand forty' in numerals. A: 43040. 43 thousand = 43,000; add 40 to get 43,040.
chunks.source: 43 thousand = 43,000; add 40 to get 43,040.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 36. Find the unknown base: 112three = 22b. A: 6. 112three = 14 in base ten; 2b + 2 = 14 gives b = 6.
chunks.source: 112three = 14 in base ten; 2b + 2 = 14 gives b = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 39. Write 90,098 in words. A: Ninety thousand ninety eight. 90 thousand and 98.
chunks.source: 90 thousand and 98.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 40. What is the place value of 3 in 3,468,428? A: millions. The 3 is in the millions position.
chunks.source: The 3 is in the millions position.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 41. Find the base n if 21n = 1001two. A: 4. 1001two = 9 in base ten; 2n + 1 = 9 gives n = 4.
chunks.source: 1001two = 9 in base ten; 2n + 1 = 9 gives n = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 43. Write 'eleven thousand, one hundred eleven' in figures. A: 11111. 11,000 + 111 = 11,111.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 44. Change 103five to base ten (decimal). A: 28. (1 × 25) + (0 × 5) + 3 = 28.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 45. Express 13,400 in scientific notation (standard form). A: 1.34 x 10^4. 13,400 = 1.34 × 10,000 = 1.34 × 10⁴.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 48. Change 120three to base five. A: 30₅. 120three = 15 in base ten, and 15 = 3 × 5 + 0 = 30five.
chunks.source: 120three = 15 in base ten, and 15 = 3 × 5 + 0 = 30five.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 49. Find the expanded number: (2 × 5²) + (3 × 5¹) + (4 × 5⁰). A: 69. 50 + 15 + 4 = 69.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 50. Correct 99.998 to 2 decimal places. A: 100.00. The third decimal is 8, so round up to 100.00.
chunks.source: The third decimal is 8, so round up to 100.00.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 52. Write 70,603 in words. A: Seventy thousand six hundred three. 70 thousand and 603.
chunks.source: 70 thousand and 603.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 2. Use the distributive property to work out (48 × 2.5) + (2.5 × 52). A: 250. 2.5 × (48 + 52) = 2.5 × 100 = 250.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 3. Use the distributive property to work out (16 ÷ 5) + (3 ÷ 5). A: 3.8. (16 + 3) ÷ 5 = 19 ÷ 5 = 3.8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 4. A taxi carries 14 passengers and a bus carries 29. If both make 3 journeys each, how many passengers do they carry altogether? A: 129. (14 + 29) × 3 = 43 × 3 = 129.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 5. Given that p ★ y = py + 8, evaluate 3 ★ 4. A: 20. (3 × 4) + 8 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 6. Using p ★ y = py + 8, evaluate 6 ★ 8. A: 56. (6 × 8) + 8 = 56.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 7. Work out 4 + 6 ÷ 2. A: 7. Divide first: 4 + 3 = 7.
chunks.source: Divide first: 4 + 3 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 8. Work out the square root of 196. A: 14. 14 × 14 = 196.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 9. Work out the square root of 1.44. A: 1.2. 1.2 × 1.2 = 1.44.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 10. Work out the square root of 5 4/9. A: 2 1/3. 5 4/9 = 49/9, and √(49/9) = 7/3 = 2 1/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 12. A water meter read 234,689 units at the start of the month and 234,788 at the end. How many units were used? A: 99. 234,788 − 234,689 = 99.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 13. If each unit costs sh. 500, how much is paid for the month above? A: 49500. 99 × 500 = 49,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 17. Damalie picks 28 mangoes every day. How many will she pick in 9 days? A: 252. 28 × 9 = 252.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 21. Use the distributive property to work out (10 × 3.5) + (6.5 × 10). A: 100. 10 × (3.5 + 6.5) = 10 × 10 = 100.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 22. Multiply 490 × 1/2. A: 245. Half of 490 is 245.
chunks.source: Half of 490 is 245.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 23. What is the sum of 49 and 243? A: 292. 49 + 243 = 292.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 24. Work out the square root of 2.56. A: 1.6. 1.6 × 1.6 = 2.56.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 25. Work out 8 + 8 ÷ 4. A: 10. Divide first: 8 + 2 = 10.
chunks.source: Divide first: 8 + 2 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 26. Use the distributive property to work out (489 × 13) − (489 × 3). A: 4890. 489 × (13 − 3) = 489 × 10 = 4,890.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 29. If twice a number is 16, what is half the number? A: 4. The number is 8, and half of 8 is 4.
chunks.source: The number is 8, and half of 8 is 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 31. How much more money does the better option fetch above? A: 1000. 25,000 − 24,000 = 1,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 32. Divide 24 ÷ 3. A: 8. 3 × 8 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Find the next number in the sequence: 2, 3, 5, 7, ____?. A: 11. These are prime numbers; the next prime after 7 is 11.
chunks.source: These are prime numbers; the next prime after 7 is 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. Find the next number in the sequence: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, ____?. A: 21. The differences grow by 1 (2, 3, 4, 5), so add 6 to 15.
chunks.source: The differences grow by 1 (2, 3, 4, 5), so add 6 to 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 4. What is the smallest number which leaves remainder 5 when divided by 8 or by 9? A: 77. LCM of 8 and 9 is 72; 72 + 5 = 77.
chunks.source: LCM of 8 and 9 is 72; 72 + 5 = 77.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. Find the missing number: 4, 6, 8, 9, ____?. A: 10. These are composite numbers in order; after 9 comes 10.
chunks.source: These are composite numbers in order; after 9 comes 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 8. What is the product of the first and the fifth even number? A: 20. 2 × 10 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 11. Three bells ring every 60, 45 and 30 minutes. All ring at 9:00 a.m. After how many minutes do they ring together again? A: 180. LCM of 60, 45 and 30 is 180.
chunks.source: LCM of 60, 45 and 30 is 180.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 12. At what time do the bells above ring together again? A: 12:00 noon. 180 minutes = 3 hours; 9:00 + 3:00 = 12:00.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 13. The LCM of two numbers is 84 and their GCF is 7. If one number is 14, find the other. A: 42. Other = (84 × 7) ÷ 14 = 42.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 14. Prime factorise 639 and write your answer in set notation. A: {3, 3, 71}. 639 = 9 × 71 = 3 × 3 × 71.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 15. Find the next two numbers: 1, 3, 6, 11, 18, ____?, ____?. A: 29, 42. Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7 (primes); next differences 11 and 13.
chunks.source: Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7 (primes); next differences 11 and 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 17. Prime factorise 18 and write your answer in power (superscript) form. A: 2 x 3^2. 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 = 2 × 3².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 18. A parent shared some apples among 6 boys and 1 apple remained. Sharing the same apples among 4 girls, 1 apple also remained. Find the least number of apples. A: 13. LCM of 6 and 4 is 12; 12 + 1 = 13.
chunks.source: LCM of 6 and 4 is 12; 12 + 1 = 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 19. Find the next number: 36, 34, 31, 26, 19, ____?. A: 8. Differences are −2, −3, −5, −7 (primes); next is −11, so 19 − 11 = 8.
chunks.source: Differences are −2, −3, −5, −7 (primes); next is −11, so 19 − 11 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 20. Find the smallest number of pencils that 24 pupils or 18 pupils can share equally, leaving 3 pencils in each case. A: 75. LCM of 24 and 18 is 72; 72 + 3 = 75.
chunks.source: LCM of 24 and 18 is 72; 72 + 3 = 75.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 21. Find the next two numbers: 2, 4, 7, 12, 19, ____?, ____?. A: 30, 43. Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7 (primes); next differences 11 and 13.
chunks.source: Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7 (primes); next differences 11 and 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 22. Find all the prime factors of 30. A: 2, 3, 5. 30 = 2 × 3 × 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 23. Find the next number: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ____?. A: 36. These are square numbers; 6² = 36.
chunks.source: These are square numbers; 6² = 36.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 25. Find the next number: 2, 4, 7, 12, 19, ____?. A: 30. Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7 (primes); 19 + 11 = 30.
chunks.source: Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7 (primes); 19 + 11 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 26. Find the sum of the prime numbers between 20 and 30. A: 52. 23 + 29 = 52.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 27. Find the next number: 0, 2, 5, 10, 17, 28, ____?. A: 41. Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 (primes); 28 + 13 = 41.
chunks.source: Differences are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 (primes); 28 + 13 = 41.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 28. Find the sum of all prime numbers between 50 and 60. A: 112. 53 + 59 = 112.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 29. Find the LCM of 6 and 9. A: 18. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18; of 9: 9, 18.
chunks.source: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18; of 9: 9, 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 7. In a school, 3/4 of the pupils who sat PLE passed. If 30 failed, how many passed? A: 90. 1/4 = 30, so 3/4 = 90.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 8. What percentage of the pupils failed in the question above? A: 25. 1/4 = 25%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 9. Add 4.05 + 11.4 + 2.3. A: 17.75. Line up the decimal points and add.
chunks.source: Line up the decimal points and add.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 10. Osman spent 1/4 of his salary on food, 1/3 of the remainder on debts and saved sh. 3,600. What is his monthly salary? A: 7200. Food = 1/4, debts = 1/4, saved = 1/2 = 3,600, so salary = 7,200.
chunks.source: Food = 1/4, debts = 1/4, saved = 1/2 = 3,600, so salary = 7,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 11. How much did Osman spend on debts above? A: 1800. 1/4 of 7,200 = 1,800.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 14. The cost of 4 rulers is sh. 2,400. What is the cost of 6 similar rulers? A: 3600. One ruler = 600; 6 × 600 = 3,600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 17. In P.7, 1/4 of the pupils like science, 2/3 of the remainder like mathematics and the rest (33 pupils) like English. How many pupils are in P.7? A: 132. English = 1 − 1/4 − 1/2 = 1/4 = 33, so total = 132.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 19. Increase sh. 5,000 in the ratio 5:4. A: 6250. 5,000 × 5/4 = 6,250.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 20. A pot has 5 1/2 litres of water. How many half-litre bottles can it fill? A: 11. 5.5 ÷ 0.5 = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 21. A tap pours 40 litres in 5 minutes. How long (in hours) will it take to fill a 1,080-litre tank? A: 2.25. 8 litres per minute; 1,080 ÷ 8 = 135 minutes = 2.25 hours.
chunks.source: 8 litres per minute; 1,080 ÷ 8 = 135 minutes = 2.25 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 23. Kato, Mukasa and Musoke shared money in the ratio 2:3:5. Musoke got sh. 1,500 more than Kato. How much money was shared? A: 5000. 3 parts = 1,500, so 1 part = 500; total = 10 × 500 = 5,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 24. How much did each of Kato, Mukasa and Musoke get above? A: 1000, 1500, 2500. One part = 500; Kato = 1,000, Mukasa = 1,500, Musoke = 2,500.
chunks.source: One part = 500; Kato = 1,000, Mukasa = 1,500, Musoke = 2,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 25. A and B shared money in the ratio 3:4. If A got sh. 12,000, how much was shared? A: 28000. One part = 4,000; total = 7 × 4,000 = 28,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 26. How much did B get above? A: 16000. 4 × 4,000 = 16,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 29. Express the ratio 1:8 as a percentage. A: 11.11. 1:8 means 1 out of 9; 1/9 = 11.11%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 33. A school has 800 pupils; 45% are girls. How many boys are there? A: 440. Girls = 360; boys = 800 − 360 = 440.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 34. After spending 30% of his income, a man was left with sh. 210,000. What is his income? A: 300000. 70% = 210,000, so 100% = 300,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 35. How much did he spend above? A: 90000. 30% of 300,000 = 90,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 37. A radio costing sh. 90,000 was increased by 30%. What is the new price? A: 117000. 90,000 × 1.3 = 117,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 39. What amount, increased by 20%, becomes sh. 1,440? A: 1200. 1,440 ÷ 1.2 = 1,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 41. A teacher's salary was decreased by 20% to sh. 120,000. What was it before? A: 150000. 120,000 ÷ 0.8 = 150,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 42. Kato sold shoes at sh. 45,000 at a loss of 10%. What was the cost price? A: 50000. 45,000 ÷ 0.9 = 50,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 43. How much money did Kato lose above? A: 5000. 50,000 − 45,000 = 5,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 47. A 100 kg bag of rice costs sh. 80,000. At what price per kg must it be sold for a 30% profit? A: 1040. Cost per kg = 800; 800 × 1.3 = 1,040.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 50. Wasswa paid sh. 18,000 for a handbag after a 10% discount. What was the marked price? A: 20000. 18,000 ÷ 0.9 = 20,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 52. 14 litres of milk, which is 40% more than the water, was used to make tea. How much tea was prepared? A: 24. Water = 14 ÷ 1.4 = 10 litres; tea = 14 + 10 = 24.
chunks.source: Water = 14 ÷ 1.4 = 10 litres; tea = 14 + 10 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 53. A man spent 20% of his salary on food, 10% on transport, 40% on medical care and the rest on rent. What percentage went to rent? A: 30. 100 − 20 − 10 − 40 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 54. If he earns sh. 800,000, how much does he spend on medical care? A: 320000. 40% of 800,000 = 320,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 55. How much more is spent on food than on transport above? A: 80000. 10% of 800,000 = 80,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 57. A man borrowed sh. 120,000 at 8% per year and paid sh. 7,200 interest. For how long was the loan? A: 9 months. 7,200 ÷ (120,000 × 0.08) = 0.75 years = 9 months.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 58. Out of 120 students who did a test, 1/3 were girls. How many girls did the test? A: 40. 120 ÷ 3 = 40.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 59. If 40% of the boys failed and 55% of the girls passed above, how many students passed? A: 70. Boys passed = 60% of 80 = 48; girls passed = 55% of 40 = 22; total = 70.
chunks.source: Boys passed = 60% of 80 = 48; girls passed = 55% of 40 = 22; total = 70.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 60. When sh. 400 is increased by x%, it becomes sh. 500. Find x. A: 25. (500 − 400) ÷ 400 = 25%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 62. At what rate will sh. 480,000 give sh. 2,400 interest in 2 months? A: 3. 2,400 ÷ (480,000 × 2/12) = 3%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 63. Florence cut 12 bars of soap into quarter pieces. How many small pieces did she get? A: 48. 12 × 4 = 48.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 66. A woman deposited sh. 360,000 at 5% per year. After how long will she get sh. 10,500 interest? A: 7 months. 10,500 ÷ (360,000 × 0.05) = 0.583 years = 7 months.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 69. Willy sold the radio to Moses at 5% loss. How much did Moses pay? A: 319200. Willy paid 336,000; Moses paid 336,000 × 0.95 = 319,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 72. Tea is sold in 3/4 kg packets. How many packets can be made from 24 kg? A: 32. 24 ÷ 3/4 = 32.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 74. In a class, 3/4 of the pupils are boys and the rest are girls. What fraction are girls? A: 1/4. 1 − 3/4 = 1/4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 75. If there are 18 girls in the class above, how many boys are there? A: 54. Total = 72; boys = 72 − 18 = 54.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 76. Find the total number of pupils in the class above. A: 72. 18 × 4 = 72.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 77. In a basket, 5/8 of the apples are red, 1/6 are yellow and the rest are green. What fraction are green? A: 5/24. 1 − 5/8 − 1/6 = 5/24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 78. If there are 60 green apples in the basket above, how many apples are there altogether? A: 288. 60 ÷ 5/24 = 288.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 80. Musoke's salary fell from sh. 240,000 to sh. 192,000. Find the percentage decrease. A: 20. (240,000 − 192,000) ÷ 240,000 = 20%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 81. Jane and Barbra shared sh. 904,000 in the ratio 5:3. How much more did Jane get than Barbra? A: 226000. One part = 113,000; difference = 2 × 113,000 = 226,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 82. Omut scored 16 marks out of 20. Express his mark as a percentage. A: 80. 16/20 = 80%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 83. In the ratio 2:3, Namu has 6 litres of milk. How many litres has Bagaga? A: 9. One part = 3 litres; Bagaga = 3 × 3 = 9.
chunks.source: One part = 3 litres; Bagaga = 3 × 3 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 84. Juma bought a goat at sh. 142,000 and sold it at 10% profit. Find the profit. A: 14200. 10% of 142,000 = 14,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 85. What was the selling price of Juma's goat? A: 156200. 142,000 + 14,200 = 156,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 86. A basket was sold at sh. 2,500 making a profit of sh. 500. Find the percentage profit. A: 25. Cost = 2,000; 500/2,000 = 25%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 90. Agatha, Angella and Angel shared dollars in the ratio 5:2:3. Agatha got 50 dollars more than Angel. How many dollars were shared? A: 250. 2 parts = 50, so 1 part = 25; total = 10 × 25 = 250.
chunks.source: 2 parts = 50, so 1 part = 25; total = 10 × 25 = 250.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 91. How many dollars did Angella get above? A: 50. 2 × 25 = 50.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 92. Sumaya sold a bicycle for sh. 170,000 making a profit of sh. 35,000. At what price did she buy the bicycle? A: 135000. 170,000 − 35,000 = 135,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 93. Share 40 bananas between Alice and Brenda in the ratio 2:3. How many does each get? A: 16, 24. One part = 8; Alice = 16, Brenda = 24.
chunks.source: One part = 8; Alice = 16, Brenda = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 95. Express 2/3 as a decimal, correct to 2 decimal places. A: 0.67. 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666…, which rounds to 0.67.
chunks.source: 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666…, which rounds to 0.67.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 96. 2% of Kiirya's salary is sh. 10,000. How much does he spend on basic needs (45% of his salary)? A: 225000. Salary = 500,000; 45% of 500,000 = 225,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 97. How much does Kiirya save above? A: 275000. 55% of 500,000 = 275,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 99. In a class of 40 pupils, 1/4 are girls. How many boys are there? A: 30. Girls = 10; boys = 40 − 10 = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 100. Change 3/5 into a decimal. A: 0.6. 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 101. If 6 men can dig a pit latrine in 8 days, how long will 4 men take? A: 12 days. 6 × 8 = 48 man-days; 48 ÷ 4 = 12 days.
chunks.source: 6 × 8 = 48 man-days; 48 ÷ 4 = 12 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 105. After a 10% increase, Akello's salary is sh. 10,450. What was his original salary? A: 9500. 10,450 ÷ 1.1 = 9,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 106. The interest on sh. 20,000 for 2 years is sh. 1,200. Find the simple interest rate per year. A: 3. 1,200 ÷ (20,000 × 2) = 3%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 107. The ratio of men to women in a village is 5:7. If there are 63 women, how many adults are there in the village? A: 108. One part = 9; men = 45; total = 108.
chunks.source: One part = 9; men = 45; total = 108.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 108. How many more men are needed above to make the ratio 1:1? A: 18. 63 − 45 = 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 109. Okello sold a turkey for sh. 55,000 making a profit of sh. 9,500. How much did he buy it for? A: 45500. 55,000 − 9,500 = 45,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 111. Annet, Babra and Christine imported cars in the ratio 3:2:1. If Annet imported 48 cars, what is the total number of cars imported? A: 96. One part = 16; total = 6 × 16 = 96.
chunks.source: One part = 16; total = 6 × 16 = 96.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 1. Simplify −6 − +6. A: -12. Going down 6 more from −6 gives −12.
chunks.source: Going down 6 more from −6 gives −12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 2. Simplify −2 − −7. A: 5. Subtracting a negative is adding: −2 + 7 = 5.
chunks.source: Subtracting a negative is adding: −2 + 7 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 3. Simplify −8 − −8. A: 0. −8 + 8 = 0.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 5. What integer is 8 steps to the right of −3? A: 5. −3 + 8 = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 6. Work out (+4) × (−3). A: -12. Positive times negative gives negative: 4 × 3 = 12.
chunks.source: Positive times negative gives negative: 4 × 3 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 8. In an interview, 2 marks are given for a correct answer and 1 mark deducted for a wrong one. A candidate got 5 correct and 3 wrong. What is the score? A: 7. (5 × 2) − 3 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 9. What is the score of a candidate who got 15 correct out of 20 questions above? A: 25. (15 × 2) − 5 = 25.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 10. A teacher gives 2 marks for a correct answer and subtracts 1 for a wrong one in a 20-question test. A pupil got 18 correct. What mark did the pupil get? A: 34. (18 × 2) − 2 = 34.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 11. A pupil got 25 marks in the test above. How many answers were correct? A: 15. 2c − (20 − c) = 25 gives 3c = 45, so c = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 12. Work out 2 − 3 (finite 5). A: 4. −1 in finite 5 is 4.
chunks.source: −1 in finite 5 is 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 13. Work out 5 + 6 + 4 (finite 7). A: 1. 15 ÷ 7 leaves remainder 1.
chunks.source: 15 ÷ 7 leaves remainder 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 14. Solve 2y − 3 = 3 (finite 5). A: 3. 2y = 6, so y = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 15. Solve 2(2p − 1) = 4 (finite 7). A: 5. 4p = 6 (finite 7); p = 5 works since 4 × 5 = 20 = 6.
chunks.source: 4p = 6 (finite 7); p = 5 works since 4 × 5 = 20 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 16. Solve 3(x − 2) = 1 (finite 5). A: 4. 3x = 7 = 2 (finite 5); 3 × 4 = 12 = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 17. Divide 3 ÷ 5 (finite 12). A: 3. 3 × 5 = 15 = 3 (finite 12).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 20. Today is Wednesday 14th June. What day of the week will it be on 29th August the same year? A: Tuesday. 76 days later; 76 ÷ 7 leaves 6; Wednesday + 6 = Tuesday.
chunks.source: 76 days later; 76 ÷ 7 leaves 6; Wednesday + 6 = Tuesday.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 23. What is the least number of cows which leaves remainder 3 when divided by 4 and remainder 7 when divided by 8? A: 7. 7 ÷ 8 leaves 7, and 7 ÷ 4 leaves 3.
chunks.source: 7 ÷ 8 leaves 7, and 7 ÷ 4 leaves 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 24. A watch loses 5 seconds every hour. How many minutes does it lose in 2 days? A: 4. 48 × 5 = 240 seconds = 4 minutes.
chunks.source: 48 × 5 = 240 seconds = 4 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 26. Solve 2y − 3 = 4 (finite 5). A: 1. 2y = 7 = 2 (finite 5), so y = 1.
chunks.source: 2y = 7 = 2 (finite 5), so y = 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 27. Work out −3 − 8. A: -11. Going down 8 more from −3 gives −11.
chunks.source: Going down 8 more from −3 gives −11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 29. Use the number line to work out −8 + +6. A: -2. Start at −8 and move 6 steps right to −2.
chunks.source: Start at −8 and move 6 steps right to −2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 30. Work out −4 + −2. A: -6. Going down 2 more from −4 gives −6.
chunks.source: Going down 2 more from −4 gives −6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 31. Simplify −5 + −7. A: -12. Going down 7 more from −5 gives −12.
chunks.source: Going down 7 more from −5 gives −12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 32. Simplify 30 − 20. A: 10. 30 − 20 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 34. Simplify −4 − +7. A: -11. Going down 7 more from −4 gives −11.
chunks.source: Going down 7 more from −4 gives −11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 36. Work out 3 + 1 (finite 7). A: 4. 3 + 1 = 4, which is less than 7.
chunks.source: 3 + 1 = 4, which is less than 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 37. If y + 2 = 1 (finite 3), find y. A: 2. 2 + 2 = 4 = 1 (finite 3).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 4. A team's chance of winning a game is 3/5. If the team plays 15 games, how many games is it expected to lose? A: 6. Lose 2/5 of 15 = 6.
chunks.source: Lose 2/5 of 15 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 7. A die is tossed once. What is the probability that a prime number appears on top? A: 1/2. Primes 2, 3, 5: 3 out of 6 = 1/2.
chunks.source: Primes 2, 3, 5: 3 out of 6 = 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 8. What is the probability that a composite number shows up on the die above? A: 1/3. Composites 4, 6: 2 out of 6 = 1/3.
chunks.source: Composites 4, 6: 2 out of 6 = 1/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 9. What is the probability that a 5 shows up on the die above? A: 1/6. One 5 out of 6 faces.
chunks.source: One 5 out of 6 faces.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 10. What is the probability that a number less than 4 shows up on the die above? A: 1/2. 1, 2, 3: 3 out of 6 = 1/2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 11. Pupils scored: 50 (2 pupils), k (6 pupils), 45 (3 pupils), 80 (4 pupils). How many pupils did the test? A: 15. 2 + 6 + 3 + 4 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 12. If the mean mark above was 61, find the value of k. A: 60. (100 + 6k + 135 + 320) ÷ 15 = 61 gives k = 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 13. What was the range of the marks above? A: 35. 80 − 45 = 35.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 14. Find the median mark above. A: 60. The 8th mark in order is 60.
chunks.source: The 8th mark in order is 60.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 15. The mean of the numbers 7, 9, 5, x + 2 and 6 is 8. Find the value of x. A: 11. Total = 40; x + 2 = 13, so x = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 16. Work out the range of the numbers above. A: 8. The numbers run from 5 to 13; range = 8.
chunks.source: The numbers run from 5 to 13; range = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 17. The average age of 3 girls is 11 years. One of the girls is 12 years old. Find the average age of the other two girls. A: 10.5. Total = 33; others = 21; 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 18. The average age of 8 pupils is 15 years. If pupils aged 10 and 14 leave the group, what is the average age of the remaining pupils? A: 16. Total = 120; rest = 96 ÷ 6 = 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 20. The average weight of 3 boys is 32 kg. When a fourth boy joins, the average becomes 40 kg. Find the weight of the fourth boy. A: 64. 4 × 40 − 3 × 32 = 64.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 21. Find the mean of 6, 5x, 2 and 7x. A: 3x + 2. (8 + 12x) ÷ 4 = 3x + 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 22. Sumaya's homework marks: 2, 5, 7, 3, 10, 4, 7, 11, 8, 3. Find her median mark. A: 6. Ordered: 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 7, 7, 8, 10, 11; median = (5 + 7) ÷ 2 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 23. What is the probability that Sumaya scored a mark above her mean mark? A: 1/2. Mean = 6; marks above 6: 7, 7, 8, 10, 11 = 5 out of 10.
chunks.source: Mean = 6; marks above 6: 7, 7, 8, 10, 11 = 5 out of 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 24. Marks scored: 70 (3 pupils), 40 (4 pupils), 30 (2 pupils), 50 (1 pupil). How many pupils did the test? A: 10. 3 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 25. Find the mean mark above. A: 48. (210 + 160 + 60 + 50) ÷ 10 = 48.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 26. Find the mean of y − 2, y, y − 4 and y − 6. A: y - 3. (4y − 12) ÷ 4 = y − 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 27. The mean mark of 1, 3, 4, 5, t, 8 and 13 is 6. Find the value of t. A: 8. Total = 42; t = 42 − 34 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 28. Find the median mark above. A: 5. Ordered: 1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 8, 13; middle = 5.
chunks.source: Ordered: 1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 8, 13; middle = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 29. Children recorded: 2 aged 9, 1 aged 11, 4 aged 12, 1 aged 13, 1 aged 18. How many children were recorded altogether? A: 9. 2 + 1 + 4 + 1 + 1 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 30. Find the range of the ages above. A: 9. 18 − 9 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 31. What is the modal frequency above? A: 4. The highest frequency is 4 (age 12).
chunks.source: The highest frequency is 4 (age 12).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 32. Find the mean age above. A: 12. (18 + 11 + 48 + 13 + 18) ÷ 9 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 33. If one picture represents 7 balls, how many pictures are needed to represent 42 balls? A: 6. 42 ÷ 7 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 34. A man spends 1/4 of his income on rent and 4/9 of the remainder on food, and saves sh. 360,000. What fraction of his income does he save? A: 5/12. 1 − 1/4 − 1/3 = 5/12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 35. What is his income above? A: 864000. 5/12 = 360,000, so income = 864,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 36. Express 5 m/sec in km/hr. A: 18. 5 × 3.6 = 18.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 37. Change 72 km/hr to m/sec. A: 20. 72 × 5/18 = 20.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 38. Joshua 70, Joan 40, Jane 50, Joseph 30. Work out the median mark. A: 45. Ordered: 30, 40, 50, 70; median = (40 + 50) ÷ 2 = 45.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 39. Calculate the mean mark above. A: 47.5. 190 ÷ 4 = 47.5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 40. A pie chart shows land use: beans 25%, maize 40%, millet 20%, potatoes y%. Find y. A: 15. 100 − 25 − 40 − 20 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 41. If 1,200 sq.m is used for potatoes above, what is the total area of the land? A: 8000. 15% = 1,200, so total = 8,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 42. Express the land used for potatoes as degrees of the pie chart. A: 54. 15% of 360° = 54°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 43. Find the mean of n, 3n − 5 and 2n − 7. A: 2n - 4. (6n − 12) ÷ 3 = 2n − 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 44. Isma scored 21 goals and Damalie scored 12. Find the range of their scores. A: 9. 21 − 12 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 45. Jane is 9 years old and Peter is 2 years older than Jane. Find their mean age. A: 10. (9 + 11) ÷ 2 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 47. Marks: 35 (2 pupils), 40 (3 pupils), 50 (2 pupils), 70 (2 pupils), 90 (1 pupil). What was the modal mark? A: 40. 40 has the highest frequency (3).
chunks.source: 40 has the highest frequency (3).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 48. Find the range of the marks above. A: 55. 90 − 35 = 55.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 49. Work out the mean mark above. A: 52. (70 + 120 + 100 + 140 + 90) ÷ 10 = 52.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 50. Ashaba's marks: 2 (twice), 3, 4, 5 (twice), 6. What is the probability that she scored 5 marks? A: 2/7. 2 fives out of 7 marks.
