chunks.source: 2 fives out of 7 marks.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 51. The ages of immunised children were recorded (30 children). How many children were immunised during the week? A: 30. Count all the ages: 30.
chunks.source: Count all the ages: 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 52. What was the modal age above? A: 6. Age 6 appears 10 times, more than any other.
chunks.source: Age 6 appears 10 times, more than any other.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 53. Calculate the average age of the children aged above 7 above. A: 9. Ages 8, 9, 10 appear 3 times each: (24 + 27 + 30) ÷ 9 = 9.
chunks.source: Ages 8, 9, 10 appear 3 times each: (24 + 27 + 30) ÷ 9 = 9.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 54. The average mass of 3 pupils is 35 kg. When a fourth pupil joins, the average becomes 40 kg. Find the mass of the fourth pupil. A: 55. 4 × 40 − 3 × 35 = 55.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 55. Ann's marks: 4 (twice), 7, 6 (4 times), 7, 8 (twice). What is the probability that she scored a 6? A: 2/5. 4 sixes out of 10 marks = 2/5.
chunks.source: 4 sixes out of 10 marks = 2/5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 56. Points A(−3, 3), B(−3, −3), C(4, −3) are joined to form a triangle. Find the length of BC in units. A: 7. From x = −3 to x = 4 is 7 units.
chunks.source: From x = −3 to x = 4 is 7 units.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 57. A picture represents 9 carrots. How many pictures can represent 63 carrots? A: 7. 63 ÷ 9 = 7.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 1. Haruna bought: rice 2 kg (sh. 8,800), meat (sh. 5,000 at sh. 10,000 per kg), soap 3 bars at sh. 7,000 per bar. What was his total expenditure? A: 34800. 8,800 + 5,000 + 21,000 = 34,800.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 2. If Haruna remained with sh. 50,000 as his balance, how much money did he have at first? A: 84800. 34,800 + 50,000 = 84,800.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 3. A tourist has 600 US dollars (buying rate sh. 2,500) and 400 Kenya shillings (buying rate sh. 18). How much in Uganda shillings can he get? A: 1507200. 600 × 2,500 + 400 × 18 = 1,507,200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 4. Sarah has sh. 900,000. How many US dollars can she get at the selling rate of sh. 3,000? A: 300. 900,000 ÷ 3,000 = 300.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 5. Namutebi bought: 3 bars of soap at sh. 3,500; 2 1/2 litres of milk at sh. 1,500 per half litre; 250 g of sugar at sh. 4,200 per kg. How much did she spend altogether? A: 19050. 10,500 + 7,500 + 1,050 = 19,050.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 6. If Namutebi went to the market with sh. 20,000, what was her change? A: 950. 20,000 − 19,050 = 950.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 7. Amos bought: 2 pineapples at sh. 2,000 each; 0.5 kg of sugar at sh. 3,200 per kg; 1 1/2 kg of meat at sh. 8,000 per kg; 1 bunch of matooke at sh. 18,000. How much did he spend altogether? A: 35600. 4,000 + 1,600 + 12,000 + 18,000 = 35,600.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 8. A maid bought: 10 books at sh. 600; 5 pencils (sh. 1,500 total); 5 pens at sh. 200; 3 rulers at sh. 500. What was the total cost? A: 10000. 6,000 + 1,500 + 1,000 + 1,500 = 10,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 9. If the maid above was given a 10% discount, how much did she pay? A: 9000. 10,000 × 0.9 = 9,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 10. Namagga bought: a tin of charcoal sh. 3,000; 2 packets of flour at sh. 5,500 each; 1 1/2 litres of cooking oil at sh. 4,000 per litre. Find her total expenditure. A: 20000. 3,000 + 11,000 + 6,000 = 20,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 11. A school has 41 P.7 pupils. How much examination fee is collected at sh. 22,000 each? A: 902000. 41 × 22,000 = 902,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 12. Okiror pays for a P5 day scholar (sh. 72,000), a P6 day scholar (sh. 85,000) and a P7 boarder (sh. 216,000). How much does he pay to the school? A: 373000. 72,000 + 85,000 + 216,000 = 373,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 13. One pair of jeans costs sh. 9,000 and one busuuti costs sh. 35,000. Find the cost of 2 jeans and 3 busuuti. A: 123000. 18,000 + 105,000 = 123,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 14. Atim bought 4 pens at sh. 500 each, a geometry set at sh. 2,500 and 2 rulers at sh. 1,000 each. How much did she pay altogether? A: 6500. 2,000 + 2,500 + 2,000 = 6,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 15. Walter bought 2 geometry sets (sh. 2,500 each), 6 rulers (sh. 1,000 each) and 10 pencils (sh. 1,800 a dozen), and got a 20% discount. What did he actually pay? A: 10000. 5,000 + 6,000 + 1,500 = 12,500; 12,500 × 0.8 = 10,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 1. Study the figure (right-angled triangle ABC with AB = 6 dm, BD = 4 dm, DC = 5 dm). Find the area of the unshaded triangle ADC. A: 15. 1/2 × 5 × 6 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 2. Calculate the area of triangle ABC in the figure. A: 27. 1/2 × 9 × 6 = 27.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 3. Calculate the perimeter of triangle ADC in the figure (AD = 7 dm, AC = 10 dm). A: 22. 7 + 5 + 10 = 22.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 4. In the diagram, line AB is parallel to line CD. Find the value of m. A: 40. m and 40° are alternate interior angles.
chunks.source: m and 40° are alternate interior angles.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 5. Find the bearing of town M from town K. (The diagram shows 030° measured clockwise from north at K to M.) A: 030. Bearings are measured clockwise from north; it is 030°.
chunks.source: Bearings are measured clockwise from north; it is 030°.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 8. Find the supplement of (40 − y)°. A: 140 + y. 180 − (40 − y) = 140 + y.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 9. The interior angle of a regular polygon is 36° more than its exterior angle. Find the exterior angle. A: 72. 180 − 2e = 36, so e = 72.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 10. Name the regular polygon above. A: pentagon. 360 ÷ 72 = 5 sides.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 11. Calculate the interior angle sum of the polygon above. A: 540. (5 − 2) × 180 = 540.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 13. Work out the circumference of a circle of diameter 28 cm. (Use π = 22/7.) A: 88. 22/7 × 28 = 88.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 14. A rhombus has diagonals 10 cm and 24 cm. Calculate the length of one side. A: 13. √(5² + 12²) = 13.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 15. Find the perimeter of the rhombus above. A: 52. 4 × 13 = 52.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 17. A regular hexagon has side 4 cm. Calculate its perimeter. A: 24. 6 × 4 = 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 1. Add: 5 weeks 4 days + 2 weeks 6 days. A: 8 weeks 3 days. 7 weeks 10 days = 8 weeks 3 days.
chunks.source: 7 weeks 10 days = 8 weeks 3 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 6. Study the distance–time graph. Find the motorist's speed from home to town N. A: 40. 80 km in 2 hours = 40 km/h.
chunks.source: 80 km in 2 hours = 40 km/h.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 7. At what time did the motorist leave town N on the graph? A: 10:30 a.m.. The flat part ends at 10:30 a.m.
chunks.source: The flat part ends at 10:30 a.m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 8. Calculate the average speed for the whole journey on the graph. A: 30. 120 km in 4 hours = 30 km/h.
chunks.source: 120 km in 4 hours = 30 km/h.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 9. A motorist covered 360 km in 3 hours from home to town A, then continued to town B at 90 km/h for 2 hours. How far is town B from town A? A: 180. 90 × 2 = 180.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 10. Work out the average speed for the whole journey above. A: 108. 540 km ÷ 5 h = 108 km/h.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 12. A motorist left town A at 9:15 a.m. driving at 80 km/hr and reached town B at 11:45 a.m. How long did the journey take? A: 2.5 hours. 11:45 − 9:15 = 2 h 30 min.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 13. How far is town B from town A above? A: 200. 80 × 2.5 = 200.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 14. If his car uses 3 litres of fuel for every 40 km, how many litres are needed for the journey above? A: 15. 200 ÷ 40 × 3 = 15.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 15. Add: 6 weeks 4 days + 2 weeks 5 days. A: 9 weeks 2 days. 8 weeks 9 days = 9 weeks 2 days.
chunks.source: 8 weeks 9 days = 9 weeks 2 days.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 17. A football match ended at 12:50 a.m. Express this time in the 24-hour clock. A: 00:50. 12:50 a.m. = 00:50.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 18. Express 36 km/hr in metres per second. A: 10. 36 × 5/18 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 19. A bus timetable shows: Tororo 0 km (departs 9:00), Iganga 60 km, Jinja 100 km, Kampala 150 km (arrives 21:25). Find the distance between Iganga and Kampala. A: 90. 150 − 60 = 90.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 20. How long did the bus rest at Jinja? (Arrived 19:10, departed 19:40.) A: 30 minutes. 19:40 − 19:10 = 30 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 21. How long did the whole Tororo–Kampala trip take? A: 12 hours 25 minutes. 21:25 − 9:00 = 12 h 25 min.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 22. Find the total time the bus spent resting. (Iganga rest 35 min, Jinja rest 30 min.) A: 1 hour 5 minutes. 35 + 30 = 65 minutes.
chunks.source: 35 + 30 = 65 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 23. A meeting which started at 11:50 a.m. ended at 1:00 p.m. How long did the meeting last? A: 1 hour 10 minutes. 11:50 → 1:00 is 1 h 10 min.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 24. Mulero had to cover 147 km in 3 1/2 hours at a constant speed. At what speed was he driving? A: 42. 147 ÷ 3.5 = 42.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 25. What distance was Mulero left with after driving for 2 hours above? A: 63. 147 − 84 = 63.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 26. An examination began at 7:35 a.m. and lasted 2 1/2 hours. At what time did it end? A: 10:05 a.m.. 7:35 + 2:30 = 10:05.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 27. A baby started sleeping at 9:10 a.m. and woke up at 1:40 p.m. For how long did she sleep? A: 4 hours 30 minutes. 9:10 → 1:40 is 4 h 30 min.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 28. Kato (80 km/hr) and Wasswa (60 km/hr) left Kampala for Masaka at the same time. How far apart were they after the first 30 minutes? A: 10. 40 − 30 = 10 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 29. If both left at 9:00 a.m., at what time did Kato arrive at Masaka (120 km away)? A: 10:30 a.m.. 120 ÷ 80 = 1.5 h; 9:00 + 1:30 = 10:30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 30. How long did Kato wait at Masaka before Wasswa arrived? A: 30 minutes. Wasswa took 2 h, arriving at 11:00; 11:00 − 10:30 = 30 min.
chunks.source: Wasswa took 2 h, arriving at 11:00; 11:00 − 10:30 = 30 min.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 31. A school van was driven at 80 km/hr from 8:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. Find the distance it covered. A: 240. 80 × 3 = 240.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 32. How long did the return journey above take at 96 km/hr? A: 2.5 hours. 240 ÷ 96 = 2.5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 2. Cylindrical tins (diameter 6 cm, height 14 cm) are packed into a box 18 cm × 42 cm × 20 cm. How many tins fit in the first layer? A: 21. (18 ÷ 6) × (42 ÷ 6) = 3 × 7 = 21.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 3. How many layers of tins can be packed in the box above? A: 1. 20 ÷ 14 = 1 remainder.
chunks.source: 20 ÷ 14 = 1 remainder.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 4. Find the volume of the empty space after packing the tins. (Use π = 22/7.) A: 6804. Box = 15,120; tins = 21 × 396 = 8,316; space = 6,804 cm³.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 6. A milkman sells milk in quarter-litre cups. How many cups can he sell from a ten-litre jerrycan? A: 40. 10 ÷ 1/4 = 40.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 8. Express 1.5 km into metres. A: 1500. 1.5 × 1,000 = 1,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 9. Kamatu bought 700 g of salt at sh. 500 a kilogram. How much did he actually pay? A: 350. 0.7 × 500 = 350.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 10. Calculate the volume of a cube whose width is 12 cm. A: 1728. 12³ = 1,728 cm³.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 11. The diagram shows a rectangle 6 m by 4 m. Kipromo ran round it three times. What total distance did he cover? A: 60. Perimeter = 20 m; 3 × 20 = 60 m.
chunks.source: Perimeter = 20 m; 3 × 20 = 60 m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 1. The age of Ben is thrice that of Ali. If Ali is 12 years old, how old is Ben? A: 36. 3 × 12 = 36.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 2. Given that a = −3 and b = 4, find the value of 2b − 2a. A: 14. 8 − (−6) = 14.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 3. The sum of 3 consecutive even numbers is 24. If the largest number is k, find the three numbers. A: 6, 8, 10. k − 4, k − 2, k; 3k − 6 = 24 gives k = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 4. The rectangle has its two shorter sides marked equal: (3y − 5) cm and (y + 5) cm. Find y. A: 5. 3y − 5 = y + 5 gives y = 5.
chunks.source: 3y − 5 = y + 5 gives y = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 5. Find the area of the rectangle above (the longer side is (4y + 6) cm). A: 260. Sides are 10 cm and 26 cm; 10 × 26 = 260 cm².
chunks.source: Sides are 10 cm and 26 cm; 10 × 26 = 260 cm².

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 6. Simplify 9k − 4y − 3k + 5y. A: 6k + y. 9k − 3k = 6k; −4y + 5y = y.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 7. Given that p = 4 and r = −3, find the value of (3p + r) ÷ r. A: -3. (12 − 3) ÷ (−3) = −3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 9. Simplify 5p − (−3 + p). A: 4p + 3. 5p + 3 − p = 4p + 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 10. Simplify (y + 6)/2 + (y − 2)/5. A: (7y + 26)/10. Common denominator 10: (5y + 30 + 2y − 4)/10.
chunks.source: Common denominator 10: (5y + 30 + 2y − 4)/10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 11. Solve the inequality −6 ≤ −3(k − 2). A: k ≤ 4. 2 ≥ k − 2, so k ≤ 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 12. Simplify 5p − q − p − 2q. A: 4p - 3q. 5p − p = 4p; −q − 2q = −3q.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 13. Solve 2^x = 32. A: 5. 32 = 2⁵, so x = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 14. Solve 3^y ÷ 3 = 81. A: 5. 3^(y−1) = 3⁴, so y = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 15. Solve 5^n × 5^n = 25. A: 1. 5^(2n) = 5², so n = 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 16. Simplify 4² × 4³ ÷ 4⁴. A: 4. 4^(2+3−4) = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 17. Simplify a⁶ × a² ÷ a³. A: a^5. a^(6+2−3) = a⁵.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 18. The sum of 3 consecutive odd numbers is 87. Find the numbers. A: 27, 29, 31. Middle = 87 ÷ 3 = 29.
chunks.source: Middle = 87 ÷ 3 = 29.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 19. Work out the range of the numbers above. A: 4. 31 − 27 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 20. Solve 2(p − 3) = 0. A: 3. p − 3 = 0, so p = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 21. Solve 2y − 8 ≤ y + 2. A: y ≤ 10. y ≤ 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 22. Remove the brackets and simplify: 8(m − 1) + 3(m + 2). A: 11m - 2. 8m − 8 + 3m + 6 = 11m − 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 23. Solve 3m − 5 = 7. A: 4. 3m = 12, so m = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 24. Given that a = 5 and b = 2, find the value of 2ba/5. A: 4. (2 × 2 × 5) ÷ 5 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 25. Find the value of d if 2d ÷ 4 = 8. A: 16. 2d = 32, so d = 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 26. Solve (2m)/3 + m/3 = 5. A: 5. 3m/3 = m = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 27. Find the first 2 values of n if 4 − 3n ≤ 13. A: -3, -2. −3n ≤ 9 gives n ≥ −3; first two: −3, −2.
chunks.source: −3n ≤ 9 gives n ≥ −3; first two: −3, −2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 28. The sum of three consecutive numbers is 96. Find the numbers. A: 31, 32, 33. Middle = 96 ÷ 3 = 32.
chunks.source: Middle = 96 ÷ 3 = 32.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 29. Solve 3y − 2 = 7. A: 3. 3y = 9, so y = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 30. Solve 3(a − 1) − 2(a − 2) = 3. A: 2. 3a − 3 − 2a + 4 = 3 gives a = 2.
chunks.source: 3a − 3 − 2a + 4 = 3 gives a = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 31. Wanyama is 3 years younger than his elder sister Nasirumbi. In 15 years time, their total age will be 49 years. How old is Wanyama? A: 8. (x + 15) + (x + 18) = 49 gives x = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 32. The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 54 and the first number is y. Find the value of y. A: 16. y + (y + 2) + (y + 4) = 54 gives y = 16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 33. Work out the range of the numbers above. A: 4. The numbers are 16, 18, 20; 20 − 16 = 4.
chunks.source: The numbers are 16, 18, 20; 20 − 16 = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 34. Given that a = −4 and b = −3, work out b(a − b). A: 3. −3 × (−4 + 3) = −3 × (−1) = 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 36. Solve the inequality 3(x + 4) < 5x − 2. A: x > 7. 3x + 12 < 5x − 2 gives 14 < 2x.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 37. Solve 8 − 2x = 4. A: 2. 2x = 4, so x = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 38. Simplify 3(y − 4) − 2(y − 3). A: y - 6. 3y − 12 − 2y + 6 = y − 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 39. Evaluate 2(a − b) if a = −3 and b = 2. A: -10. 2 × (−5) = −10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 40. Kasiri is 3 years old and his mother is 25 years old. How old will the mother be when Kasiri is 25? A: 47. The difference is 22 years; 25 + 22 = 47.
chunks.source: The difference is 22 years; 25 + 22 = 47.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 41. Moses and Janet got (3y − 8) apples altogether. If Janet got y apples and Moses got (y − 2) apples, what is the value of y? A: 6. y + (y − 2) = 3y − 8 gives y = 6.
chunks.source: y + (y − 2) = 3y − 8 gives y = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 42. Three children aged (x + 3), (3x − 10) and (2x + 5) have a total age of 34 years. How old is each child? A: 9, 8, 17. 6x − 2 = 34 gives x = 6; ages 9, 8, 17.
chunks.source: 6x − 2 = 34 gives x = 6; ages 9, 8, 17.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 43. Ham is 4 years younger than Tom, and Sam is 4 years older than Tom. In 10 years time, the sum of their ages will be 63 years. How old is Tom now? A: 11. (x − 4 + 10) + (x + 10) + (x + 4 + 10) = 63 gives x = 11.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 44. Find the difference between Sam's and Ham's ages after ten years above. A: 8. Sam − Ham = 8 always.
chunks.source: Sam − Ham = 8 always.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Work out: 1 2/3 divided by 5/6. A: 2. 1 2/3 = 5/3. 5/3 divided by 5/6 = 5/3 x 6/5 = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.source: Common denominator 24: 8/24 - 21/24 + 18/24 = 5/24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. Akiki planted half of his garden with maize and intercropped 3/8 of the planted maize with beans. What fraction of the shamba was left with only maize? A: 5/16. Maize left with only maize = 1/2 x (1 - 3/8) = 1/2 x 5/8 = 5/16.
chunks.source: Maize left with only maize = 1/2 x (1 - 3/8) = 1/2 x 5/8 = 5/16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. If 3/4 of a cake weighs 450 grammes, find the weight of the whole cake in grammes. A: 600. 1/4 of the cake weighs 450/3 = 150 g. The whole cake weighs 150 x 4 = 600 g.
chunks.source: 1/4 of the cake weighs 450/3 = 150 g. The whole cake weighs 150 x 4 = 600 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. 7/8 of the fruits in a basket are mangoes, 1/3 of the remainder are oranges and 24 are apples. What fraction of the fruits are oranges? A: 1/24. The remainder is 1/8 of the basket. Oranges = 1/3 x 1/8 = 1/24.
chunks.source: The remainder is 1/8 of the basket. Oranges = 1/3 x 1/8 = 1/24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. How many fruits are in the basket in question 9 above altogether? A: 288. Apples = 1/8 - 1/24 = 1/12 of the basket. 24 x 12 = 288.
chunks.source: Apples = 1/8 - 1/24 = 1/12 of the basket. 24 x 12 = 288.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Simplify: 5m - 3n + m - 2n. A: 6m - 5n. 5m + m = 6m and -3n - 2n = -5n.
chunks.source: 5m + m = 6m and -3n - 2n = -5n.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Given that c = b squared and b = -4, evaluate 3b - c. A: -28. c = (-4) squared = 16. 3(-4) - 16 = -12 - 16 = -28.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. The mean of 2, y + 1, 0 and 4 is 3. Find the value of y. A: 5. (y + 7)/4 = 3, so y + 7 = 12 and y = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. Solve: 2k divided by 8 = 1. Find the value of k. A: 4. 2k/8 = 1, so k/4 = 1 and k = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. Solve the inequality: 12 <= 9 - 3x. A: x <= -1. 3 <= -3x, so x <= -1. The sign flips when dividing by a negative number.
chunks.source: 3 <= -3x, so x <= -1. The sign flips when dividing by a negative number.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. Solve: -2X < 4. A: X > -2. Divide by -2 and flip the sign: X > -2.
chunks.source: Divide by -2 and flip the sign: X > -2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. The probability that Messi scores a penalty is 4/5. If he missed 3 penalties, how many penalties did he score? A: 12. He missed 1/5 of the penalties. Total = 3 x 5 = 15, so he scored 15 - 3 = 12.
chunks.source: He missed 1/5 of the penalties. Total = 3 x 5 = 15, so he scored 15 - 3 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. In a test, 2 pupils scored 70, 1 pupil scored 90, 3 pupils scored m and 4 pupils scored 60. How many pupils did the test? A: 10. 2 + 1 + 3 + 4 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. If their average score was 71, which mark was scored by the 3 pupils in question 2 above? A: 80. Total marks = 71 x 10 = 710. Known marks = 2x70 + 90 + 4x60 = 470. 3m = 240, so m = 80.
chunks.source: Total marks = 71 x 10 = 710. Known marks = 2x70 + 90 + 4x60 = 470. 3m = 240, so m = 80.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. In a pie chart, first grade = 2p + 30 degrees, second grade = 3p + 40 degrees and third grade = 4p + 20 degrees. Find the value of p. A: 30. 9p + 90 = 360, so 9p = 270 and p = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. If 27 candidates passed in first grade in question 4 above, how many candidates sat the exams? A: 108. First grade = 2x30 + 30 = 90 degrees. 27 x 360/90 = 108.
chunks.source: First grade = 2x30 + 30 = 90 degrees. 27 x 360/90 = 108.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. The scores 80, 75, 90, 60 and 85 had frequencies 1, 1, 2, 1 and 1. What is the modal score? A: 90. 90 has the highest frequency, which is 2.
chunks.source: 90 has the highest frequency, which is 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. Find the mean of the scores in question 6 above. A: 80. (80 + 75 + 2x90 + 60 + 85)/6 = 480/6 = 80.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. Find the median of: 3, -2, 6, 7, 0, -5, 1. A: 1. In order: -5, -2, 0, 1, 3, 6, 7. The middle value is 1.
chunks.source: In order: -5, -2, 0, 1, 3, 6, 7. The middle value is 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. A die was tossed once. What is the probability that a square number showed up? A: 1/3. The square numbers on a die are 1 and 4, so the probability is 2/6 = 1/3.
chunks.source: The square numbers on a die are 1 and 4, so the probability is 2/6 = 1/3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. A motorist travelled at a speed of 80 km/h for 2 hours 15 minutes. Calculate the distance covered in kilometres. A: 180. Distance = 80 x 2.25 = 180 km.
chunks.source: Distance = 80 x 2.25 = 180 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Bells for upper and lower primary are rung at intervals of 40 minutes and 30 minutes. After how long will the two bells ring together again? A: 120 minutes. The LCM of 40 and 30 is 120, so they ring together again after 120 minutes.
chunks.source: The LCM of 40 and 30 is 120, so they ring together again after 120 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. The two bells were first rung together at 10:30 a.m. At what time will they ring together again? A: 12:30 p.m.. 10:30 a.m. + 2 hours = 12:30 p.m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. A meeting ended at 12:25 p.m. after lasting 2 hours 35 minutes. At what time did the meeting start? A: 9:50 a.m.. 12:25 - 2:35 = 9:50 a.m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. A cargo plane flew at 300 km/h for 2 1/2 hours and then at 240 km/h for 45 minutes. Work out the total distance covered. A: 930. 300 x 2.5 = 750 km and 240 x 0.75 = 180 km. Total = 930 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. A lorry covers a distance of 60 km in one hour. What distance will it cover in 80 minutes at the same speed? A: 80. 60 x 80/60 = 80 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. A vehicle travelled for 4 hours at 60 km/h from Kuno to Budi, then returned at 80 km/h. How long did the return journey take? A: 3 hours. Distance = 4 x 60 = 240 km. Time = 240/80 = 3 hours.
chunks.source: Distance = 4 x 60 = 240 km. Time = 240/80 = 3 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. A taxi covered a distance of 360 km in 2 hours 15 minutes. Calculate its average speed in km/h. A: 160. Speed = 360/2.25 = 160 km/h.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. Besigye left Kasangati at 7:20 p.m. and reached Wandegeya at 10:30 p.m. How long did the journey take? A: 3 hours 10 minutes. 10:30 - 7:20 = 3 hours 10 minutes.
chunks.source: 10:30 - 7:20 = 3 hours 10 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. Given that r = -6 and t = 4, find the value of t squared + r squared. A: 52. t squared = 16 and r squared = 36. 16 + 36 = 52.
chunks.source: t squared = 16 and r squared = 36. 16 + 36 = 52.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Write 496 in Roman numerals. A: CDXCVI. 496 = 400 + 90 + 6 = CD + XC + VI.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Given that m = (5 x 100) + (9 x 10 to the power -2), find the value of m. A: 500.09. (5 x 100) + (9 x 0.01) = 500 + 0.09 = 500.09.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. Work out 211 in base three minus 12 in base three, giving the answer in base three. A: 122₃. 211 in base three = 22, 12 in base three = 5. 22 - 5 = 17 = 122 in base three.
chunks.source: 211 in base three = 22, 12 in base three = 5. 22 - 5 = 17 = 122 in base three.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. Change 21 in base three to a binary base. A: 111₂. 21 in base three = 7 in base ten = 111 in binary.
chunks.source: 21 in base three = 7 in base ten = 111 in binary.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. Doctor Kuwala had 35 notes of money numbered consecutively from AK004624 to the last note. Find the number written on the last note. A: AK004658. 4624 + 35 - 1 = 4658, so the last note is AK004658.
chunks.source: 4624 + 35 - 1 = 4658, so the last note is AK004658.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. A set has 32 subsets. How many elements does the set have? A: 5. 2 to the power 5 = 32, so the set has 5 elements.
chunks.source: 2 to the power 5 = 32, so the set has 5 elements.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. Express in figures: one million, one thousand, one. A: 1001001. One million = 1,000,000 and one thousand and one = 1,001. Together: 1,001,001.
chunks.source: One million = 1,000,000 and one thousand and one = 1,001. Together: 1,001,001.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. What Hindu Arabic numeral is represented by the Roman numeral DCLXVI? A: 666. D = 500, C = 100, L = 50, X = 10, V = 5, I = 1. Total = 666.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. Change 16 in base ten into octal base. A: 20₈. 16 = 2 x 8 + 0, so 16 in base ten = 20 in base eight.
chunks.source: 16 = 2 x 8 + 0, so 16 in base ten = 20 in base eight.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Aminah had fifty-thousand-shilling notes numbered consecutively from DC 2819238 to DC 2819282. How much money did he have altogether? A: 2250000. 2819282 - 2819238 + 1 = 45 notes. 45 x 50,000 = 2,250,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Kibalama went to the market with sh. 40,000 and spent sh. 30,500. Calculate his change. A: 9500. 40,000 - 30,500 = 9,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. A trader bought 5 trays of eggs at sh. 12,000 each and sold each tray at sh. 15,000. How much profit did the trader make? A: 15000. Profit per tray = 3,000. 5 x 3,000 = 15,000.
chunks.source: Profit per tray = 3,000. 5 x 3,000 = 15,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. Calculate the percentage profit in question 3 above. A: 25%. 15,000/60,000 x 100 = 25%.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. One Kenya shilling was equivalent to Ug. sh. 28.2. Find the Kenya shillings equivalent of Ug. sh. 1833. A: 65. 1833/28.2 = 65.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. The price of shoes was sh. 15,000 and increased by 40%. What is the new price of the shoes? A: 21000. 15,000 x 1.4 = 21,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. Muddu bought 1/2 kg of sugar at sh. 3,000 per kg, 500 g of salt at sh. 1,000 per kg, 3 bars of soap at sh. 6,000 each and 4 kg of maize flour at sh. 1,600 per kg. How much money did she spend? A: 26400. 1,500 + 500 + 18,000 + 6,400 = 26,400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. Muddu remained with a change of sh. 3,680. How much money did he have at the beginning? A: 30080. 26,400 + 3,680 = 30,080.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. A tourist sold 200 US dollars and 400 Kenya shillings to a bank. The bank's buying rates were $1 = Ug. sh. 2,500 and Ksh 1 = Ug. sh. 27. How much Uganda currency did she get? A: 510800. 200 x 2,500 + 400 x 27 = 500,000 + 10,800 = 510,800.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Find the next two numbers in the sequence: 37, 26, 17, 10, ___, ___. A: 5, 2. The differences are 11, 9, 7, so the next differences are 5 and 3: 10 - 5 = 5, 5 - 3 = 2.
chunks.source: The differences are 11, 9, 7, so the next differences are 5 and 3: 10 - 5 = 5, 5 - 3 = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Find the next number in the sequence: 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, ___. A: 8. The pattern is +1, +2, +1, +2, so the next step is +1: 7 + 1 = 8.
chunks.source: The pattern is +1, +2, +1, +2, so the next step is +1: 7 + 1 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. Give the next number in the sequence: 1, 6, 15, 28, 45, ___. A: 66. The differences are 5, 9, 13, 17, so the next difference is 21: 45 + 21 = 66.
chunks.source: The differences are 5, 9, 13, 17, so the next difference is 21: 45 + 21 = 66.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. Find the next two numbers in the sequence: 3, 5, 8, 13, ___, ___. A: 20, 29. The differences are 2, 3, 5, so the next differences are 7 and 9: 13 + 7 = 20, 20 + 9 = 29.
chunks.source: The differences are 2, 3, 5, so the next differences are 7 and 9: 13 + 7 = 20, 20 + 9 = 29.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. Write the next two numbers in the sequence: 3, 7, 11, 15, ___, ___. A: 19, 23. The numbers go up by 4 each time: 15 + 4 = 19, 19 + 4 = 23.
chunks.source: The numbers go up by 4 each time: 15 + 4 = 19, 19 + 4 = 23.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Find the interior angle sum of a polygon with 7 sides. A: 900. (7 - 2) x 180 = 900 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. The volume of a cylinder is 1540 cm cubed. Find the height of the cylinder if the radius is 7 cm. (Take pi = 22/7). A: 10. Volume = pi x r x r x h. 1540 = 22/7 x 7 x 7 x h = 154 x h, so h = 10 cm.
chunks.source: Volume = pi x r x r x h. 1540 = 22/7 x 7 x 7 x h = 154 x h, so h = 10 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. Two supplementary angles are in the ratio 5:4. Find the size of the larger angle. A: 100. Supplementary angles add to 180. Larger = 5/9 x 180 = 100 degrees.
chunks.source: Supplementary angles add to 180. Larger = 5/9 x 180 = 100 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. How many sides has a polygon whose exterior angle is 45 degrees? A: 8. 360/45 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. The interior angle to the exterior angle of a regular polygon is 3:2. Find the size of the exterior angle. A: 72. Interior + exterior = 180. Exterior = 2/5 x 180 = 72 degrees.
chunks.source: Interior + exterior = 180. Exterior = 2/5 x 180 = 72 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Use the distributive property to work out: (72 divided by 4) + (28 divided by 4). A: 25. (72 + 28)/4 = 100/4 = 25.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Convert 1 1/2 litres into millilitres. A: 1500. 1 litre = 1,000 ml. 1.5 x 1,000 = 1,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. A bus covered a distance of 720 km in 10 hours. Give the distance in metres. A: 720000. 1 km = 1,000 m. 720 x 1,000 = 720,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Work out: 1 2/3 divided by 5/6.? A: 2. 1 2/3 = 5/3. 5/3 divided by 5/6 = 5/3 x 6/5 = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.source: Common denominator 24: 8/24 - 21/24 + 18/24 = 5/24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. Akiki planted half of his garden with maize and intercropped 3/8 of the planted maize with beans. What fraction of the shamba was left with only maize?? A: 5/16. Maize left with only maize = 1/2 x (1 - 3/8) = 1/2 x 5/8 = 5/16.
chunks.source: Maize left with only maize = 1/2 x (1 - 3/8) = 1/2 x 5/8 = 5/16.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. If 3/4 of a cake weighs 450 grammes, find the weight of the whole cake in grammes.? A: 600. 1/4 of the cake weighs 450/3 = 150 g. The whole cake weighs 150 x 4 = 600 g.
chunks.source: 1/4 of the cake weighs 450/3 = 150 g. The whole cake weighs 150 x 4 = 600 g.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. 7/8 of the fruits in a basket are mangoes, 1/3 of the remainder are oranges and 24 are apples. What fraction of the fruits are oranges?? A: 1/24. The remainder is 1/8 of the basket. Oranges = 1/3 x 1/8 = 1/24.
chunks.source: The remainder is 1/8 of the basket. Oranges = 1/3 x 1/8 = 1/24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 10. How many fruits are in the basket in question 9 above altogether?? A: 288. Apples = 1/8 - 1/24 = 1/12 of the basket. 24 x 12 = 288.
chunks.source: Apples = 1/8 - 1/24 = 1/12 of the basket. 24 x 12 = 288.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Simplify: 5m - 3n + m - 2n.? A: 6m - 5n. 5m + m = 6m and -3n - 2n = -5n.
chunks.source: 5m + m = 6m and -3n - 2n = -5n.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Given that c = b squared and b = -4, evaluate 3b - c.? A: -28. c = (-4) squared = 16. 3(-4) - 16 = -12 - 16 = -28.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. The mean of 2, y + 1, 0 and 4 is 3. Find the value of y.? A: 5. (y + 7)/4 = 3, so y + 7 = 12 and y = 5.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. Solve: 2k divided by 8 = 1. Find the value of k.? A: 4. 2k/8 = 1, so k/4 = 1 and k = 4.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. Solve the inequality: 12 <= 9 - 3x.? A: x <= -1. 3 <= -3x, so x <= -1. The sign flips when dividing by a negative number.
chunks.source: 3 <= -3x, so x <= -1. The sign flips when dividing by a negative number.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 9. Solve: -2X < 4.? A: X > -2. Divide by -2 and flip the sign: X > -2.
chunks.source: Divide by -2 and flip the sign: X > -2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. The probability that Messi scores a penalty is 4/5. If he missed 3 penalties, how many penalties did he score?? A: 12. He missed 1/5 of the penalties. Total = 3 x 5 = 15, so he scored 15 - 3 = 12.
chunks.source: He missed 1/5 of the penalties. Total = 3 x 5 = 15, so he scored 15 - 3 = 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. In a test, 2 pupils scored 70, 1 pupil scored 90, 3 pupils scored m and 4 pupils scored 60. How many pupils did the test?? A: 10. 2 + 1 + 3 + 4 = 10.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. If their average score was 71, which mark was scored by the 3 pupils in question 2 above?? A: 80. Total marks = 71 x 10 = 710. Known marks = 2x70 + 90 + 4x60 = 470. 3m = 240, so m = 80.
chunks.source: Total marks = 71 x 10 = 710. Known marks = 2x70 + 90 + 4x60 = 470. 3m = 240, so m = 80.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. In a pie chart, first grade = 2p + 30 degrees, second grade = 3p + 40 degrees and third grade = 4p + 20 degrees. Find the value of p.? A: 30. 9p + 90 = 360, so 9p = 270 and p = 30.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. If 27 candidates passed in first grade in question 4 above, how many candidates sat the exams?? A: 108. First grade = 2x30 + 30 = 90 degrees. 27 x 360/90 = 108.
chunks.source: First grade = 2x30 + 30 = 90 degrees. 27 x 360/90 = 108.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. The scores 80, 75, 90, 60 and 85 had frequencies 1, 1, 2, 1 and 1. What is the modal score?? A: 90. 90 has the highest frequency, which is 2.
chunks.source: 90 has the highest frequency, which is 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. Find the mean of the scores in question 6 above.? A: 80. (80 + 75 + 2x90 + 60 + 85)/6 = 480/6 = 80.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. Find the median of: 3, -2, 6, 7, 0, -5, 1.? A: 1. In order: -5, -2, 0, 1, 3, 6, 7. The middle value is 1.
chunks.source: In order: -5, -2, 0, 1, 3, 6, 7. The middle value is 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. A motorist travelled at a speed of 80 km/h for 2 hours 15 minutes. Calculate the distance covered in kilometres.? A: 180. Distance = 80 x 2.25 = 180 km.
chunks.source: Distance = 80 x 2.25 = 180 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Bells for upper and lower primary are rung at intervals of 40 minutes and 30 minutes. After how long will the two bells ring together again?? A: 120 minutes. The LCM of 40 and 30 is 120, so they ring together again after 120 minutes.
chunks.source: The LCM of 40 and 30 is 120, so they ring together again after 120 minutes.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. The two bells were first rung together at 10:30 a.m. At what time will they ring together again?? A: 12:30 p.m.. 10:30 a.m. + 2 hours = 12:30 p.m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. A meeting ended at 12:25 p.m. after lasting 2 hours 35 minutes. At what time did the meeting start?? A: 9:50 a.m.. 12:25 - 2:35 = 9:50 a.m.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. A cargo plane flew at 300 km/h for 2 1/2 hours and then at 240 km/h for 45 minutes. Work out the total distance covered.? A: 930. 300 x 2.5 = 750 km and 240 x 0.75 = 180 km. Total = 930 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. A lorry covers a distance of 60 km in one hour. What distance will it cover in 80 minutes at the same speed?? A: 80. 60 x 80/60 = 80 km.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. A vehicle travelled for 4 hours at 60 km/h from Kuno to Budi, then returned at 80 km/h. How long did the return journey take?? A: 3 hours. Distance = 4 x 60 = 240 km. Time = 240/80 = 3 hours.
chunks.source: Distance = 4 x 60 = 240 km. Time = 240/80 = 3 hours.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. A taxi covered a distance of 360 km in 2 hours 15 minutes. Calculate its average speed in km/h.? A: 160. Speed = 360/2.25 = 160 km/h.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. Given that r = -6 and t = 4, find the value of t squared + r squared.? A: 52. t squared = 16 and r squared = 36. 16 + 36 = 52.
chunks.source: t squared = 16 and r squared = 36. 16 + 36 = 52.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Write 496 in Roman numerals.? A: CDXCVI. 496 = 400 + 90 + 6 = CD + XC + VI.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Given that m = (5 x 100) + (9 x 10 to the power -2), find the value of m.? A: 500.09. (5 x 100) + (9 x 0.01) = 500 + 0.09 = 500.09.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. Work out 211 in base three minus 12 in base three, giving the answer in base three.? A: 122₃. 211 in base three = 22, 12 in base three = 5. 22 - 5 = 17 = 122 in base three.
chunks.source: 211 in base three = 22, 12 in base three = 5. 22 - 5 = 17 = 122 in base three.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. Change 21 in base three to a binary base.? A: 111₂. 21 in base three = 7 in base ten = 111 in binary.
chunks.source: 21 in base three = 7 in base ten = 111 in binary.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. Doctor Kuwala had 35 notes of money numbered consecutively from AK004624 to the last note. Find the number written on the last note.? A: AK004658. 4624 + 35 - 1 = 4658, so the last note is AK004658.
chunks.source: 4624 + 35 - 1 = 4658, so the last note is AK004658.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. A set has 32 subsets. How many elements does the set have?? A: 5. 2 to the power 5 = 32, so the set has 5 elements.
chunks.source: 2 to the power 5 = 32, so the set has 5 elements.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. Express in figures: one million, one thousand, one.? A: 1001001. One million = 1,000,000 and one thousand and one = 1,001. Together: 1,001,001.
chunks.source: One million = 1,000,000 and one thousand and one = 1,001. Together: 1,001,001.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Aminah had fifty-thousand-shilling notes numbered consecutively from DC 2819238 to DC 2819282. How much money did he have altogether?? A: 2250000. 2819282 - 2819238 + 1 = 45 notes. 45 x 50,000 = 2,250,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Kibalama went to the market with sh. 40,000 and spent sh. 30,500. Calculate his change.? A: 9500. 40,000 - 30,500 = 9,500.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. A trader bought 5 trays of eggs at sh. 12,000 each and sold each tray at sh. 15,000. How much profit did the trader make?? A: 15000. Profit per tray = 3,000. 5 x 3,000 = 15,000.
chunks.source: Profit per tray = 3,000. 5 x 3,000 = 15,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 5. One Kenya shilling was equivalent to Ug. sh. 28.2. Find the Kenya shillings equivalent of Ug. sh. 1833.? A: 65. 1833/28.2 = 65.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 6. The price of shoes was sh. 15,000 and increased by 40%. What is the new price of the shoes?? A: 21000. 15,000 x 1.4 = 21,000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 7. Muddu bought 1/2 kg of sugar at sh. 3,000 per kg, 500 g of salt at sh. 1,000 per kg, 3 bars of soap at sh. 6,000 each and 4 kg of maize flour at sh. 1,600 per kg. How much money did she spend?? A: 26400. 1,500 + 500 + 18,000 + 6,400 = 26,400.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 8. Muddu remained with a change of sh. 3,680. How much money did he have at the beginning?? A: 30080. 26,400 + 3,680 = 30,080.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Find the next two numbers in the sequence: 37, 26, 17, 10, ____?, ____?. A: 5, 2. The differences are 11, 9, 7, so the next differences are 5 and 3: 10 - 5 = 5, 5 - 3 = 2.
chunks.source: The differences are 11, 9, 7, so the next differences are 5 and 3: 10 - 5 = 5, 5 - 3 = 2.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Find the next number in the sequence: 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, ____?. A: 8. The pattern is +1, +2, +1, +2, so the next step is +1: 7 + 1 = 8.
chunks.source: The pattern is +1, +2, +1, +2, so the next step is +1: 7 + 1 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. Give the next number in the sequence: 1, 6, 15, 28, 45, ____?. A: 66. The differences are 5, 9, 13, 17, so the next difference is 21: 45 + 21 = 66.
chunks.source: The differences are 5, 9, 13, 17, so the next difference is 21: 45 + 21 = 66.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. Find the next two numbers in the sequence: 3, 5, 8, 13, ____?, ____?. A: 20, 29. The differences are 2, 3, 5, so the next differences are 7 and 9: 13 + 7 = 20, 20 + 9 = 29.
chunks.source: The differences are 2, 3, 5, so the next differences are 7 and 9: 13 + 7 = 20, 20 + 9 = 29.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Find the interior angle sum of a polygon with 7 sides.? A: 900. (7 - 2) x 180 = 900 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. The volume of a cylinder is 1540 cm cubed. Find the height of the cylinder if the radius is 7 cm. (Take pi = 22/7).? A: 10. Volume = pi x r x r x h. 1540 = 22/7 x 7 x 7 x h = 154 x h, so h = 10 cm.
chunks.source: Volume = pi x r x r x h. 1540 = 22/7 x 7 x 7 x h = 154 x h, so h = 10 cm.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 3. Two supplementary angles are in the ratio 5:4. Find the size of the larger angle.? A: 100. Supplementary angles add to 180. Larger = 5/9 x 180 = 100 degrees.
chunks.source: Supplementary angles add to 180. Larger = 5/9 x 180 = 100 degrees.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 4. How many sides has a polygon whose exterior angle is 45 degrees?? A: 8. 360/45 = 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 2. Use the distributive property to work out: (72 divided by 4) + (28 divided by 4).? A: 25. (72 + 28)/4 = 100/4 = 25.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1. Convert 1 1/2 litres into millilitres.? A: 1500. 1 litre = 1,000 ml. 1.5 x 1,000 = 1,500.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1. Mention the class of food that is necessary for steaming up a pregnant cow. A: Concentrates (dairy meal). Steaming up means feeding a pregnant cow extra rich feeds before calving so she has energy for the calf and for milk production.
chunks.source: Steaming up means feeding a pregnant cow extra rich feeds before calving so she has energy for the calf and for milk production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2. Give one way man has used the process of condensation. A: In distillation to obtain pure water from salty or impure water. When vapour is cooled it condenses into liquid; this is used in distillation to collect pure water.
chunks.source: When vapour is cooled it condenses into liquid; this is used in distillation to collect pure water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3. Point out one substance needed by plants during photosynthesis and germination. A: Water. Water is a raw material for photosynthesis and it softens the seed coat so the seed can germinate.
chunks.source: Water is a raw material for photosynthesis and it softens the seed coat so the seed can germinate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4. The diagram shows a farming practice used to care for seedlings after transplanting. Why does a farmer provide shelter to the seedling after transplanting? A: To protect the seedlings from strong sunshine and heat until their roots recover. Transplanted seedlings have weak roots and can easily wilt; shelter reduces water loss and heat stress.
chunks.source: Transplanted seedlings have weak roots and can easily wilt; shelter reduces water loss and heat stress.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5. How is the movement of the larva stage of a mosquito different from that of the adult mosquito? A: The larva wriggles (swims) in water while the adult mosquito flies in air. A mosquito larva (wriggler) lives in water and moves by wriggling its body, while the adult has wings and flies.
chunks.source: A mosquito larva (wriggler) lives in water and moves by wriggling its body, while the adult has wings and flies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6. Which method of obtaining wood for timber involves cutting a tree at an angle to a stump level? A: Coppicing. In coppicing the tree is cut near the stump level so that new shoots grow from the stump.
chunks.source: In coppicing the tree is cut near the stump level so that new shoots grow from the stump.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7. Name one of the long bones found below the knee. A: Tibia (shin bone). The tibia and fibula are the long bones of the lower leg, below the knee.
chunks.source: The tibia and fibula are the long bones of the lower leg, below the knee.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8. Point out one activity that can be done during community clean up campaign. A: Slashing bushes (collecting litter). Slashing bushes, sweeping and collecting rubbish keep the community clean and healthy.
chunks.source: Slashing bushes, sweeping and collecting rubbish keep the community clean and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 9. Why doesn't wood burn to ash during the making of charcoal? A: The supply of oxygen is limited (cut off). Charcoal is made by heating wood with little oxygen, so the wood carbonises instead of burning completely to ash.
chunks.source: Charcoal is made by heating wood with little oxygen, so the wood carbonises instead of burning completely to ash.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10. Which system of poultry keeping keeps eggs away from layers? A: Battery cage system. In battery cages the floor slopes so that laid eggs roll away from the hen.
chunks.source: In battery cages the floor slopes so that laid eggs roll away from the hen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11. How is reproduction of a moss plant different from that of a maize plant? A: A moss plant reproduces by spores while a maize plant reproduces by seeds. Mosses are non-flowering plants that use spores; maize is a flowering plant that produces seeds.
chunks.source: Mosses are non-flowering plants that use spores; maize is a flowering plant that produces seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12. Which substance is suitable for sterilizing a clinical thermometer? A: Methylated spirit (surgical spirit). Methylated spirit kills germs on the thermometer without damaging it.
chunks.source: Methylated spirit kills germs on the thermometer without damaging it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 13. Why should one wash hands before preparing sugar salt solution? A: To prevent germs and dirt from the hands contaminating the solution. Dirty hands can introduce germs into the solution that a sick person will drink.
chunks.source: Dirty hands can introduce germs into the solution that a sick person will drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14. What term is used to describe the upward movement of water through soil? A: Capillarity. Capillarity is the movement of water upwards through tiny spaces in the soil.
chunks.source: Capillarity is the movement of water upwards through tiny spaces in the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15. How do double silvered walls in a thermos flask prevent heat loss? A: They reflect heat (radiation) back into the flask. The shiny silvered surfaces reflect radiant heat, reducing heat loss by radiation.
chunks.source: The shiny silvered surfaces reflect radiant heat, reducing heat loss by radiation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. Why are farmers encouraged to harvest rain water? A: To store water for use during the dry season. Harvested rain water can be used for animals, crops and domestic work when rains fail.
chunks.source: Harvested rain water can be used for animals, crops and domestic work when rains fail.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 17. How is the awareness of communicable diseases important in our community? A: It helps people to prevent and control the spread of diseases. When people know how diseases spread, they can take steps to protect themselves and others.
chunks.source: When people know how diseases spread, they can take steps to protect themselves and others.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18. To which group of succulent fruits do tomatoes belong? A: Berries. Tomatoes are succulent fruits with many seeds inside, so they are classified as berries.
chunks.source: Tomatoes are succulent fruits with many seeds inside, so they are classified as berries.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19. Apart from drying clothes, why should clothes be hanged on a line in the sunshine on a hot day? A: The sunshine kills germs on the clothes. Ultraviolet rays from the sun kill germs, keeping the clothes hygienic.
chunks.source: Ultraviolet rays from the sun kill germs, keeping the clothes hygienic.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 20. How is propagation of bananas similar to that of pineapples? A: Both are propagated by suckers. Bananas and pineapples are both planted using suckers, a vegetative method.
chunks.source: Bananas and pineapples are both planted using suckers, a vegetative method.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21. Which method of making water safe for drinking is commonly used by National Water and Sewerage Corporation? A: Chlorination. NWSC adds chlorine to water to kill germs before supplying it to homes.
chunks.source: NWSC adds chlorine to water to kill germs before supplying it to homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22. Which vector spreads the filarial worm that causes river blindness? A: Black fly (Simulium). The black fly bites people and transmits the filarial worm that causes river blindness.
chunks.source: The black fly bites people and transmits the filarial worm that causes river blindness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23. State the importance of screening blood before transfusion. A: To make sure the blood is free from germs and diseases before giving it to a patient. Screening checks that donated blood has no infections such as HIV before transfusion.
chunks.source: Screening checks that donated blood has no infections such as HIV before transfusion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 24. Point out one method of controlling weeds in a garden. A: Uprooting (digging them out). Weeds can be controlled by uprooting, mulching or spraying herbicides.
chunks.source: Weeds can be controlled by uprooting, mulching or spraying herbicides.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. What do ticks feed on? A: Blood. Ticks are external parasites that suck blood from animals.
chunks.source: Ticks are external parasites that suck blood from animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26. State the role of ligaments in a human skeleton. A: They join bones to bones at joints. Ligaments are tough tissues that hold bones together where they meet.
chunks.source: Ligaments are tough tissues that hold bones together where they meet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27. The diagram shows a health habit practised by people in the community. Name the health habit shown in the diagram. A: Cutting fingernails short (keeping hands clean). The diagram shows hands with short clean fingernails, a habit that keeps germs away.
chunks.source: The diagram shows hands with short clean fingernails, a habit that keeps germs away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28. How does the health habit above prevent the spread of diarrhoeal diseases? A: It removes germs and dirt from under the fingernails so they cannot contaminate food and water. Germs that cause diarrhoea hide under long dirty nails; short clean nails cannot carry them to food.
chunks.source: Germs that cause diarrhoea hide under long dirty nails; short clean nails cannot carry them to food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29. Why can't tilapia survive long on land? A: It breathes through gills which can only absorb oxygen from water. Fish gills extract dissolved oxygen from water; on land they collapse and the fish cannot breathe.
chunks.source: Fish gills extract dissolved oxygen from water; on land they collapse and the fish cannot breathe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30. Besides absorption of digested food, what other process takes place in the ileum? A: Completion of digestion (final digestion of food). Digestive juices in the ileum finish breaking down food before the digested food is absorbed.
chunks.source: Digestive juices in the ileum finish breaking down food before the digested food is absorbed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31. Why are lactating cows fed on dairy meal? A: To increase milk production. Dairy meal is rich in nutrients that help a milking cow produce more milk.
chunks.source: Dairy meal is rich in nutrients that help a milking cow produce more milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32. Give one similarity between sound and light energy. A: Both are forms of energy. Sound and light are both forms of energy and both travel in waves.
chunks.source: Sound and light are both forms of energy and both travel in waves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33. Point out one way of keeping the respiratory system in good health condition. A: Avoid smoking. Avoiding smoking, dusty places and doing exercise keep the breathing organs healthy.
chunks.source: Avoiding smoking, dusty places and doing exercise keep the breathing organs healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34. Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker than that of the right ventricle? A: The left ventricle pumps blood to the whole body, so it needs more force. Blood must travel a long distance round the body, so the left ventricle has thicker, stronger muscles.
chunks.source: Blood must travel a long distance round the body, so the left ventricle has thicker, stronger muscles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35. Why should girls who have started experiencing menstruation cycles abstain from sex? A: To avoid teenage pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases. After menstruation starts, a girl can conceive; abstaining protects her from pregnancy and infections.
chunks.source: After menstruation starts, a girl can conceive; abstaining protects her from pregnancy and infections.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 36. Apart from determining the colour of the skin, how else is melanin important to the body? A: It protects the skin from the sun's ultraviolet rays. Melanin absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays, shielding the skin from sun damage.
chunks.source: Melanin absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays, shielding the skin from sun damage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38. Name the device that protects appliances from the effects of too much current flow. A: Fuse. A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when too much current flows, protecting appliances.
chunks.source: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when too much current flows, protecting appliances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. Why is salt added to food during cooking? A: To add taste (flavour) to the food. Salt improves the taste of food and also helps preserve it.
chunks.source: Salt improves the taste of food and also helps preserve it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. Which immunisable disease makes limbs of infants very thin and paralyzed? A: Polio. Polio attacks the nerves and can leave a child's limbs thin and paralysed; it is prevented by immunisation.
chunks.source: Polio attacks the nerves and can leave a child's limbs thin and paralysed; it is prevented by immunisation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a) Study the diagram of the animal below. To which group of vertebrates does the animal above belong? A: Reptiles. A snake is a cold-blooded vertebrate with scales that lays eggs, so it belongs to the reptiles.
chunks.source: A snake is a cold-blooded vertebrate with scales that lays eggs, so it belongs to the reptiles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) Name the part marked Y on the diagram of the animal. A: Fangs. The snake's mouth has sharp fangs used for biting and injecting venom into prey.
chunks.source: The snake's mouth has sharp fangs used for biting and injecting venom into prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c)(i) Give the function of the part marked X on the diagram of the animal. A: For seeing (sight). Part X is the eye, which the snake uses to see its surroundings and prey.
chunks.source: Part X is the eye, which the snake uses to see its surroundings and prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c)(ii) Give the function of the part marked Z on the diagram of the animal. A: For smelling (detecting scent). Part Z is the forked tongue, which the snake flicks out to pick up scents from the air.
chunks.source: Part Z is the forked tongue, which the snake flicks out to pick up scents from the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a) What is food preservation? A: The keeping of food in good condition for a long time without going bad. Food preservation uses methods that stop germs from growing so food stays safe to eat longer.
chunks.source: Food preservation uses methods that stop germs from growing so food stays safe to eat longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) Point out one traditional method of preserving meat in your homes. A: Smoking (sun drying). Smoking or sun drying removes water from meat so germs cannot grow on it.
chunks.source: Smoking or sun drying removes water from meat so germs cannot grow on it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c) How is the preservation of millet similar to that of cassava? A: Both are preserved by sun drying. Millet grains and cassava chips are both dried in the sun to remove water.
chunks.source: Millet grains and cassava chips are both dried in the sun to remove water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(d) Name the fungus that commonly grows on food items that are not properly dried. A: Mould. Mould grows on damp, poorly dried foods and makes them unsafe to eat.
chunks.source: Mould grows on damp, poorly dried foods and makes them unsafe to eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(i) Give the meaning of the term condensation. A: The change of a gas into a liquid on cooling. When vapour is cooled, its particles slow down and form a liquid.
chunks.source: When vapour is cooled, its particles slow down and form a liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(ii) Give the meaning of the term evaporation. A: The change of a liquid into a gas (vapour) on heating. When a liquid is heated, its particles gain energy and escape as gas.
chunks.source: When a liquid is heated, its particles gain energy and escape as gas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(iii) Give the meaning of the term melting. A: The change of a solid into a liquid on heating. Heating a solid makes its particles move apart until it becomes liquid.
chunks.source: Heating a solid makes its particles move apart until it becomes liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(iv) Give the meaning of the term convection. A: The transfer of heat through liquids and gases by the movement of the heated particles. In convection, warm less-dense fluid rises while cool denser fluid sinks, carrying heat along.
chunks.source: In convection, warm less-dense fluid rises while cool denser fluid sinks, carrying heat along.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a)(i) Study the diagram of the human arm. Name the type of bone marked X. A: Long bone. The humerus of the upper arm is a long bone.
chunks.source: The humerus of the upper arm is a long bone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a)(ii) Name the type of bone marked Z on the diagram of the human arm. A: Long bone. The radius and ulna of the forearm are long bones.
chunks.source: The radius and ulna of the forearm are long bones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b) Which of the labeled muscles contracts to lift a load? A: Muscle B (the biceps). When lifting, the biceps on the front of the upper arm contracts and pulls the forearm up.
chunks.source: When lifting, the biceps on the front of the upper arm contracts and pulls the forearm up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c) What type of movable joint is E on the diagram of the human arm? A: Hinge joint. The elbow moves in one direction only, like a door hinge.
chunks.source: The elbow moves in one direction only, like a door hinge.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a) How do fish reproduce? A: By laying eggs which are fertilized externally in water. A female fish lays eggs in water and the male sheds sperms over them outside the body.
chunks.source: A female fish lays eggs in water and the male sheds sperms over them outside the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(i) In which way do fish help to improve health of people in the community? A: They are eaten as food rich in proteins. Fish provide proteins and other food values that keep people healthy.
chunks.source: Fish provide proteins and other food values that keep people healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(ii) Give another way in which fish help to improve health of people in the community. A: Some fish eat mosquito larvae, controlling malaria. Larvivorous fish feed on mosquito larvae in water, reducing malaria mosquitoes.
chunks.source: Larvivorous fish feed on mosquito larvae in water, reducing malaria mosquitoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c) Point out one other group of vertebrates whose eggs are fertilized like those of fish. A: Amphibians. Amphibians such as frogs also lay eggs in water where they are fertilized externally.
chunks.source: Amphibians such as frogs also lay eggs in water where they are fertilized externally.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) Name one viral disease among the six childhood immunisable diseases. A: Measles (polio). Measles and polio are viral diseases prevented by childhood immunisation.
chunks.source: Measles and polio are viral diseases prevented by childhood immunisation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) How is such a disease in 46(a) above spread? A: Through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes. Measles spreads through droplets in the air from an infected person.
chunks.source: Measles spreads through droplets in the air from an infected person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c) Point out one way of controlling the diseases mentioned in 46(a) above. A: By immunisation (vaccination). Vaccinating children protects them against the immunisable diseases.
chunks.source: Vaccinating children protects them against the immunisable diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(d) How are ventilators important in a living house? A: They allow fresh air in and let out warm stale air. Ventilators keep air moving through the house so it stays cool and fresh.
chunks.source: Ventilators keep air moving through the house so it stays cool and fresh.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) What is incubation? A: The keeping of fertilized eggs warm until they hatch. During incubation eggs are kept at the right warmth for the chicks to develop.
chunks.source: During incubation eggs are kept at the right warmth for the chicks to develop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b) Give one advantage of artificial incubation in poultry management. A: Many chicks can be hatched at once. An incubator can warm very many eggs at the same time, unlike a broody hen.
chunks.source: An incubator can warm very many eggs at the same time, unlike a broody hen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) Of what importance is litter in the poultry house? A: It keeps the poultry house warm and absorbs droppings. Litter on the floor keeps birds warm and soaks up droppings so the house stays dry.
chunks.source: Litter on the floor keeps birds warm and soaks up droppings so the house stays dry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(d) Mention one factor that may make a fertilized egg fail to hatch. A: Lack of enough warmth (improper temperature). Eggs need steady warmth to develop; without it the embryo dies.
chunks.source: Eggs need steady warmth to develop; without it the embryo dies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a) In which type of digestion is food broken down by enzymes? A: Chemical digestion. Enzymes chemically break food into tiny soluble particles the body can absorb.
chunks.source: Enzymes chemically break food into tiny soluble particles the body can absorb.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b) Of what importance are teeth in our mouth during digestion? A: They cut, tear and grind food into small pieces. Teeth carry out physical digestion, making food pieces small enough to swallow and digest.
chunks.source: Teeth carry out physical digestion, making food pieces small enough to swallow and digest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c) Why doesn't digestion of carbohydrates take place in the stomach? A: There are no enzymes for digesting carbohydrates in the stomach. Carbohydrate digestion starts in the mouth and is completed in the ileum; the stomach only digests proteins.
chunks.source: Carbohydrate digestion starts in the mouth and is completed in the ileum; the stomach only digests proteins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(d) Point out one disorder of the digestive system. A: Constipation (diarrhoea). Constipation, diarrhoea, peptic ulcers and appendicitis are disorders of digestion.
chunks.source: Constipation, diarrhoea, peptic ulcers and appendicitis are disorders of digestion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(i) Study the diagram of a burning candle. Name the type of change that occurs in the part marked U. A: Chemical change. Part U is the burning wick; burning produces new substances (smoke, gases), so it is chemical.
chunks.source: Part U is the burning wick; burning produces new substances (smoke, gases), so it is chemical.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(ii) Name the type of change that occurs in the part marked X on the burning candle. A: Physical change. Part X is the melting wax; melting forms no new substance, so it is physical.
chunks.source: Part X is the melting wax; melting forms no new substance, so it is physical.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) Give one characteristic of the type of change marked X above. A: It is reversible (no new substance is formed). Physical changes can be reversed, e.g. melted wax can solidify again.
chunks.source: Physical changes can be reversed, e.g. melted wax can solidify again.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c) Give one change in the environment caused by human activities. A: Deforestation (pollution). People change the environment through deforestation, pollution and swamp drainage.
chunks.source: People change the environment through deforestation, pollution and swamp drainage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a) Match the item in list A with the correct item in list B. lungs → ____. A: Carbon dioxide. The lungs remove carbon dioxide from the body during breathing out.
chunks.source: The lungs remove carbon dioxide from the body during breathing out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b) Match the item in list A with the correct item in list B. kidney → ____. A: Urine. The kidneys filter blood and produce urine.
chunks.source: The kidneys filter blood and produce urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c) Match the item in list A with the correct item in list B. liver → ____. A: Bile pigment. The liver produces bile, whose pigment colours urine and faeces.
chunks.source: The liver produces bile, whose pigment colours urine and faeces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(d) Match the item in list A with the correct item in list B. skin → ____. A: Sweat. The skin excretes excess water, salts and urea as sweat.
chunks.source: The skin excretes excess water, salts and urea as sweat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a) Give one reason why steaming up is done on an animal farm. A: To prepare the pregnant cow for calving and increase milk production after birth. Extra feeds before calving build the cow's body reserves for milk production.
chunks.source: Extra feeds before calving build the cow's body reserves for milk production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b) Give one reason why shearing is done on an animal farm. A: To obtain wool from sheep. Shearing is the cutting of wool from sheep for sale or use.
chunks.source: Shearing is the cutting of wool from sheep for sale or use.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c) Give one reason why docking is done on an animal farm. A: To prevent dirt and faeces from collecting on the tail (for hygiene). A short tail stays clean and makes mating easier in sheep.
chunks.source: A short tail stays clean and makes mating easier in sheep.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(d) Give one reason why dipping cattle is done on an animal farm. A: To kill ticks and other external parasites. Dipping in acaricide kills ticks that spread diseases to cattle.
chunks.source: Dipping in acaricide kills ticks that spread diseases to cattle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a) Who is an adolescent? A: A young person between childhood and adulthood (about 10 to 19 years). Adolescence is the stage of growth between childhood and adulthood.
chunks.source: Adolescence is the stage of growth between childhood and adulthood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b) Point out one primary sex characteristic that occurs in adolescent girls. A: Beginning of menstruation (maturation of the reproductive organs). Primary sex characteristics involve the reproductive organs becoming mature.
chunks.source: Primary sex characteristics involve the reproductive organs becoming mature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(c)(i) Give one secondary sexual characteristic that occurs in both female and male adolescents. A: Growth of pubic hair. Both boys and girls grow pubic hair as a secondary sex characteristic.
chunks.source: Both boys and girls grow pubic hair as a secondary sex characteristic.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(c)(ii) Give another secondary sexual characteristic that occurs in both female and male adolescents. A: Growth of hair in the armpits. Hair under the arms appears in both sexes during adolescence.
chunks.source: Hair under the arms appears in both sexes during adolescence.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a) What causes AIDS? A: HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus). AIDS is caused by HIV, which weakens the body's defence against diseases.
chunks.source: AIDS is caused by HIV, which weakens the body's defence against diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) How is AIDS commonly spread among adults? A: Through unprotected sexual intercourse. HIV passes from one adult to another mainly through unprotected sex.
chunks.source: HIV passes from one adult to another mainly through unprotected sex.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c) State one common sign to both AIDS and measles patients. A: Skin rash. Both AIDS and measles patients can develop rashes on the skin.
chunks.source: Both AIDS and measles patients can develop rashes on the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(d) Point out one way a P.7 child can prevent himself or herself from getting AIDS. A: By abstaining from sex. Abstinence keeps a school child completely safe from sexually transmitted HIV.
chunks.source: Abstinence keeps a school child completely safe from sexually transmitted HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a) Study the diagram. Name the body system represented by the diagram above. A: The breathing (respiratory) system. The diagram is a model showing the windpipe, lungs and diaphragm used in breathing.
chunks.source: The diagram is a model showing the windpipe, lungs and diaphragm used in breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b) What does the part marked M represent? A: The windpipe (trachea). In the model, the tube M stands for the windpipe through which air passes.
chunks.source: In the model, the tube M stands for the windpipe through which air passes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) What would happen to the part marked K if N is pushed upwards? A: Air would be forced out of K (the balloons would deflate). Pushing N up reduces the space in the jar, squeezing air out of K, just like breathing out.
chunks.source: Pushing N up reduces the space in the jar, squeezing air out of K, just like breathing out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(d) Point out one habit which is destructive to the body system above. A: Smoking. Smoking damages the lungs and air passages of the breathing system.
chunks.source: Smoking damages the lungs and air passages of the breathing system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a) Study the diagrams of spawns of amphibians. Which amphibian lays eggs marked A? A: Frog. Frogs lay their eggs in a mass or clump in water, as shown in A.
chunks.source: Frogs lay their eggs in a mass or clump in water, as shown in A.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(i) Give one importance of the jelly on the eggs marked B. A: It protects the eggs from enemies (predators). The jelly coat shields the eggs from animals that would eat them.
chunks.source: The jelly coat shields the eggs from animals that would eat them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(ii) Give another importance of the jelly on the eggs marked B. A: It keeps the eggs moist (prevents them from drying). The jelly holds water around the eggs so they do not dry out.
chunks.source: The jelly holds water around the eggs so they do not dry out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c) How is breathing of a tadpole different from that of its adult? A: A tadpole breathes through gills in water while the adult frog breathes through lungs (and moist skin). Tadpoles live in water and use gills; adult frogs live partly on land and use lungs.
chunks.source: Tadpoles live in water and use gills; adult frogs live partly on land and use lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1. Name the domestic animal whose house is made of wire mesh. A: Rabbit. Rabbits are kept in hutches, which are houses made of wire mesh.
chunks.source: Rabbits are kept in hutches, which are houses made of wire mesh.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2. What general name is given to the plumule and radicle of a germinating bean? A: Embryo. The plumule and radicle together form the embryo, the young plant inside the seed.
chunks.source: The plumule and radicle together form the embryo, the young plant inside the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3. What type of skeleton does a millipede have? A: Exoskeleton. A millipede's hard body covering is a skeleton found outside its body.
chunks.source: A millipede's hard body covering is a skeleton found outside its body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4. Name the mineral salt that helps in the formation of blood in the human body. A: Iron. Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in red blood cells.
chunks.source: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in red blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5. How are the hairy bodies of a housefly able to carry germs that spread diseases? A: Germs stick to the hairs on its body and legs. The hairs on a housefly's body trap germs, which the fly then drops on food.
chunks.source: The hairs on a housefly's body trap germs, which the fly then drops on food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6. What form of energy is a moving vehicle on the road? A: Kinetic energy. Any moving object possesses kinetic energy.
chunks.source: Any moving object possesses kinetic energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7. Give a reason why nutritious feeds should be given to cattle. A: For proper growth and increased production (milk and meat). Well-fed cattle grow fast, resist diseases and produce more milk and meat.
chunks.source: Well-fed cattle grow fast, resist diseases and produce more milk and meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8. How is reproduction in mammals different from that in amphibians? A: Mammals give birth to live young while amphibians lay eggs. Mammals develop their young inside the body; amphibians lay eggs in water.
chunks.source: Mammals develop their young inside the body; amphibians lay eggs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 9. Which term refers to the inability of a seed to germinate under normal conditions? A: Seed dormancy. A dormant seed stays alive but will not germinate even when conditions are right.
