chunks.source: A dormant seed stays alive but will not germinate even when conditions are right.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10. The diagram is a mushroom. State the use of the part marked Q. A: It protects the gills (where spores are produced). Part Q is the cap (pileus), which shields the spore-producing gills underneath.
chunks.source: Part Q is the cap (pileus), which shields the spore-producing gills underneath.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11. Why is it good to immunize children with anti-rabies vaccine? A: To protect them against rabies (in case of dog bites). The vaccine prepares the child's body to fight the rabies virus from an animal bite.
chunks.source: The vaccine prepares the child's body to fight the rabies virus from an animal bite.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12. Give one reason why electricians should wear helmets. A: To protect their heads from injury. Helmets shield electricians from falling objects and head injuries at work.
chunks.source: Helmets shield electricians from falling objects and head injuries at work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 13. Why should young boys avoid drug abuse? A: Drugs damage their health and ruin their future. Drug abuse harms the body and brain and can destroy a young person's education and life.
chunks.source: Drug abuse harms the body and brain and can destroy a young person's education and life.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14. Give one way crop rotation helps a farmer to control crop diseases. A: It breaks the life cycle of crop pests and diseases. When a different crop is planted, the pests and germs that attacked the first crop starve.
chunks.source: When a different crop is planted, the pests and germs that attacked the first crop starve.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15. How does wringing method ease drying of washed clothes? A: It squeezes (removes) water from the clothes. Wringing forces out most of the water so the remaining little water dries fast.
chunks.source: Wringing forces out most of the water so the remaining little water dries fast.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. Write the type of venation shown by the diagram. A: Parallel venation. The leaf veins run side by side from base to tip, which is parallel venation.
chunks.source: The leaf veins run side by side from base to tip, which is parallel venation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 17. Mention any one example of wingless insects. A: Silverfish (louse). Silverfish, lice and fleas are insects that have no wings.
chunks.source: Silverfish, lice and fleas are insects that have no wings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18. State one way of preventing appendicitis digestive disease. A: Eating foods rich in roughage (fibre). Roughage keeps food moving through the gut and prevents blockages.
chunks.source: Roughage keeps food moving through the gut and prevents blockages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19. What name is given to the substance that makes up an exoskeleton of an insect? A: Chitin. The hard outer covering of insects is made of chitin.
chunks.source: The hard outer covering of insects is made of chitin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 20. Give any one importance of ossicles during the process of hearing. A: They amplify (increase) sound vibrations. The three tiny ossicles pass on and strengthen vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear.
chunks.source: The three tiny ossicles pass on and strengthen vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21. The diagram shows an insect. State the function of the part marked G. A: For smelling. Part G is an antenna (feeler), which the insect uses to smell and feel.
chunks.source: Part G is an antenna (feeler), which the insect uses to smell and feel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22. Why would the insect above die when the whole of its abdomen is dipped in oil? A: Its spiracles (breathing holes) would be blocked, so it cannot breathe. Insects breathe through spiracles on the abdomen; oil seals them and the insect suffocates.
chunks.source: Insects breathe through spiracles on the abdomen; oil seals them and the insect suffocates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23. Name one appliance used at home that changes electric energy to heat energy. A: Flat iron (electric kettle). A flat iron uses electricity to produce heat for ironing clothes.
chunks.source: A flat iron uses electricity to produce heat for ironing clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 24. Give one activity the community can do to reduce accidental fires. A: Avoid bush burning. Avoiding careless bush burning and sensitising people prevents accidental fires.
chunks.source: Avoiding careless bush burning and sensitising people prevents accidental fires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. How do birds use claws for protection? A: They scratch their enemies with claws. Birds defend themselves by scratching attackers with their sharp claws.
chunks.source: Birds defend themselves by scratching attackers with their sharp claws.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26. Name one activity carried by farmers to remove excess seedlings from the garden. A: Thinning. Thinning is the removal of extra seedlings so the remaining ones grow well.
chunks.source: Thinning is the removal of extra seedlings so the remaining ones grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27. The diagram shows bicycle handles with grips that are used to increase friction. State the function of grips in increasing friction. A: They provide a firm grip and prevent the hands from slipping. The rough grips increase friction between the hands and the handles so they do not slip.
chunks.source: The rough grips increase friction between the hands and the handles so they do not slip.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28. Give one way in which salt is important in food preservation. A: It removes water from food, preventing germs from growing. Salt draws water out of food (dehydration); without water, germs cannot grow.
chunks.source: Salt draws water out of food (dehydration); without water, germs cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29. Name one internal parasite which results from feeding cattle on dirty pasture. A: Liver fluke (tapeworm). Cattle pick up worm eggs from dirty pasture and develop internal parasites like liver flukes.
chunks.source: Cattle pick up worm eggs from dirty pasture and develop internal parasites like liver flukes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30. To which group of invertebrates do snails belong? A: Molluscs. Snails are soft-bodied invertebrates with shells, grouped as molluscs.
chunks.source: Snails are soft-bodied invertebrates with shells, grouped as molluscs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31. How does intercropping control soil erosion? A: The crops cover the soil, reducing the speed of running water. A good crop cover protects the soil from direct raindrops and slows runoff.
chunks.source: A good crop cover protects the soil from direct raindrops and slows runoff.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32. What happens when a translucent object is placed in a path of light? A: Some light passes through (a faint shadow is formed). Translucent materials allow part of the light through, unlike opaque objects.
chunks.source: Translucent materials allow part of the light through, unlike opaque objects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33. State any one example of radiation in nature. A: Sunshine (solar radiation). The sun gives out heat and light as radiation.
chunks.source: The sun gives out heat and light as radiation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34. Give one factor to be considered when storing cereals. A: The store should be dry and well ventilated (grains must be well dried). Dry, airy stores prevent moisture, mould and pests from spoiling cereals.
chunks.source: Dry, airy stores prevent moisture, mould and pests from spoiling cereals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35. What feature enables birds to overcome resistance in air during flight? A: Streamlined body. A streamlined shape lets the bird cut through air with little resistance.
chunks.source: A streamlined shape lets the bird cut through air with little resistance.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 36. State one physical change in girls during puberty. A: Enlargement of the breasts (broadening of hips). During puberty a girl's body changes shape as it matures.
chunks.source: During puberty a girl's body changes shape as it matures.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 37. Why is breast feeding very important in family planning? A: It delays the return of menstruation, spacing the children naturally. Exclusive breastfeeding delays ovulation, giving natural child spacing.
chunks.source: Exclusive breastfeeding delays ovulation, giving natural child spacing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38. Which component of air is needed for photosynthesis to take place? A: Carbon dioxide. Green plants take in carbon dioxide from the air to make food.
chunks.source: Green plants take in carbon dioxide from the air to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. Name the organisms found in the root nodules of a plant. A: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria (rhizobium). These bacteria live in legume root nodules and fix nitrogen into the soil.
chunks.source: These bacteria live in legume root nodules and fix nitrogen into the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. Give one reason why children who get bad scalds are immediately taken to hospitals. A: To get proper treatment and prevent infection. Bad scalds need quick medical care to stop infection and further damage.
chunks.source: Bad scalds need quick medical care to stop infection and further damage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a) Name the mineral salt that prevents tooth decay in human beings. A: Fluoride. Fluoride strengthens the teeth and protects them from decay.
chunks.source: Fluoride strengthens the teeth and protects them from decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) Write any one cause of tooth decay in human beings. A: Eating too many sugary foods (not brushing teeth). Germs act on sugary food remains on teeth and produce acids that cause decay.
chunks.source: Germs act on sugary food remains on teeth and produce acids that cause decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c)(i) State one practice carried out by people to prevent tooth decay. A: Brushing teeth regularly. Regular brushing removes food remains and germs from teeth.
chunks.source: Regular brushing removes food remains and germs from teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c)(ii) State another practice carried out by people to prevent tooth decay. A: Avoid eating too many sweets (visit a dentist regularly). Less sugar means fewer acids attacking the teeth.
chunks.source: Less sugar means fewer acids attacking the teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a) How is sound recorded on a piece of paper reproduced? A: By playing it on a sound-reproducing device (record player). Recorded sound is played back through a device that turns the recording into sound again.
chunks.source: Recorded sound is played back through a device that turns the recording into sound again.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) Name one way of storing sound. A: On tapes (CDs, records, memory cards). Sound can be stored on tapes, CDs, records and memory cards.
chunks.source: Sound can be stored on tapes, CDs, records and memory cards.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c)(i) Mention one sound reproduction device. A: Radio. A radio reproduces sound from broadcasts or recordings.
chunks.source: A radio reproduces sound from broadcasts or recordings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c)(ii) Mention another sound reproduction device. A: Gramophone (record player). A gramophone plays sound stored on records.
chunks.source: A gramophone plays sound stored on records.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a) Study the diagram. Name the method of harvesting trees in agroforestry shown in the diagram. A: Coppicing. The diagram shows a stump with a new shoot growing, which is coppicing.
chunks.source: The diagram shows a stump with a new shoot growing, which is coppicing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b) State one importance of harvesting trees in agroforestry using the above method. A: The stump grows new shoots, so trees can be harvested repeatedly. Coppicing allows regrowth, saving the cost and time of replanting.
chunks.source: Coppicing allows regrowth, saving the cost and time of replanting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c)(i) Give one way in which crops benefit from trees when they are grown together. A: Trees provide shade to crops. Tree shade protects crops from too much sunshine.
chunks.source: Tree shade protects crops from too much sunshine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c)(ii) Give another way in which crops benefit from trees when they are grown together. A: Fallen leaves add manure to the soil. Leaves from trees rot and enrich the soil for crops.
chunks.source: Leaves from trees rot and enrich the soil for crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a)(i) Give one reason why farmers weed their crops. A: To reduce competition for nutrients, water and sunlight. Weeds steal food, water and light from crops, so removing them helps crops grow.
chunks.source: Weeds steal food, water and light from crops, so removing them helps crops grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a)(ii) Give another reason why farmers weed their crops. A: To prevent weeds from harbouring crop pests and diseases. Weeds can hide pests and germs that attack crops.
chunks.source: Weeds can hide pests and germs that attack crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b)(i) State one advantage of weeds to farmers. A: They rot to add manure (humus) to the soil. When weeds die and rot, they enrich the soil.
chunks.source: When weeds die and rot, they enrich the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b)(ii) State another advantage of weeds to farmers. A: Some weeds are used as animal feeds (vegetables). Certain weeds serve as feed for animals or food for people.
chunks.source: Certain weeds serve as feed for animals or food for people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a) Name the poisonous and cancerous substance found in tobacco smoke. A: Nicotine. Nicotine in tobacco smoke is poisonous and addictive, and tar in the smoke causes cancer.
chunks.source: Nicotine in tobacco smoke is poisonous and addictive, and tar in the smoke causes cancer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(i) Name one respiratory disease which results from smoking of tobacco. A: Lung cancer. Smoking damages the lungs and can cause lung cancer.
chunks.source: Smoking damages the lungs and can cause lung cancer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(ii) Name another respiratory disease which results from smoking of tobacco. A: Bronchitis. Tobacco smoke inflames the air passages, causing bronchitis.
chunks.source: Tobacco smoke inflames the air passages, causing bronchitis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) State the difference between density and mass. A: Mass is the amount of matter in an object while density is mass per unit volume. Mass measures how much matter is present; density compares that mass to the space it occupies.
chunks.source: Mass measures how much matter is present; density compares that mass to the space it occupies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) Name the instrument used to measure the density of liquids. A: Hydrometer. A hydrometer floats in a liquid to show its density.
chunks.source: A hydrometer floats in a liquid to show its density.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c) The density of a stone is 6 grams per cubic centimeter. Its mass is 48 grams. Find its volume. A: 8 cm³. Volume = mass ÷ density = 48 ÷ 6 = 8 cm³.
chunks.source: Volume = mass ÷ density = 48 ÷ 6 = 8 cm³.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(i) Apart from broken bottles, give one other dangerous object in the school compound. A: Nails (sharp metals). Nails, rusty tins and thorns can injure pupils in the compound.
chunks.source: Nails, rusty tins and thorns can injure pupils in the compound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(ii) Give another dangerous object found in the school compound apart from broken bottles. A: Rusty tins. Rusty tins can cut the skin and cause tetanus.
chunks.source: Rusty tins can cut the skin and cause tetanus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b) State one way of controlling dangers caused by broken bottles. A: Collect and dispose of them properly (bury them). Picking up and safely burying broken bottles removes the danger.
chunks.source: Picking up and safely burying broken bottles removes the danger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) Give one disease germ that can enter the body through cuts on the skin. A: Tetanus germs. Tetanus bacteria enter through wounds and cause lockjaw.
chunks.source: Tetanus bacteria enter through wounds and cause lockjaw.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(i) Apart from fast flowing water, mention one other agent of soil erosion. A: Wind. Strong wind blows away loose topsoil.
chunks.source: Strong wind blows away loose topsoil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(ii) Mention another agent of soil erosion apart from fast flowing water. A: Animals (man). Animals and people loosen soil through overgrazing and digging.
chunks.source: Animals and people loosen soil through overgrazing and digging.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b)(i) State one way soil erosion affects food production. A: It carries away fertile topsoil, making the soil infertile. Without fertile topsoil, crops grow poorly and yields fall.
chunks.source: Without fertile topsoil, crops grow poorly and yields fall.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b)(ii) State another way soil erosion affects food production. A: It destroys (washes away) crops. Running water can uproot and carry away growing crops.
chunks.source: Running water can uproot and carry away growing crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(i) Write one activity that helps to control the spread of diarrhoeal diseases in a home. A: Washing hands after visiting the latrine. Clean hands cannot carry diarrhoea germs to food and mouths.
chunks.source: Clean hands cannot carry diarrhoea germs to food and mouths.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(ii) Write another activity that helps to control the spread of diarrhoeal diseases in a home. A: Boiling drinking water. Boiling kills the germs in water that cause diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs in water that cause diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) How does proper management of wastes make a home healthy? A: It removes breeding places for germs and disease vectors. Properly disposed wastes cannot breed flies or grow germs.
chunks.source: Properly disposed wastes cannot breed flies or grow germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c) State one way in which a convectional pit latrine contributes to the promotion of sanitation. A: It keeps faeces away from people and flies, preventing contamination. Faeces safely buried in a latrine cannot spread germs to food and water.
chunks.source: Faeces safely buried in a latrine cannot spread germs to food and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(i) Study the diagram of the urinary system of a human being. State the function of the part marked S. A: It carries urine out of the body. Part S is the urethra, the tube through which urine leaves the body.
chunks.source: Part S is the urethra, the tube through which urine leaves the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(ii) State the function of the part marked R on the urinary system. A: It carries urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder. Part R is the ureter, joining each kidney to the bladder.
chunks.source: Part R is the ureter, joining each kidney to the bladder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b) In which way does the kidney regulate the amount of water and salts in blood? A: By removing excess water and salts as urine (reabsorbing what the body needs). The kidney filters blood, keeping needed water and salts and excreting the excess.
chunks.source: The kidney filters blood, keeping needed water and salts and excreting the excess.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c) Give any one sign and symptom of diseases of the urinary system. A: Painful urination (blood in urine). Infections of the urinary system cause pain when passing urine.
chunks.source: Infections of the urinary system cause pain when passing urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(i) Write down one factor that leads to alcoholism. A: Peer pressure. Friends can push a person into drinking alcohol.
chunks.source: Friends can push a person into drinking alcohol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(ii) Write down another factor that leads to alcoholism. A: Stress (idleness). Worried or idle people may turn to alcohol for comfort.
chunks.source: Worried or idle people may turn to alcohol for comfort.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(i) State one health problem caused by alcohol to the family. A: Poverty (money wasted on alcohol). Money spent on alcohol leaves the family without basics.
chunks.source: Money spent on alcohol leaves the family without basics.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(ii) State another health problem caused by alcohol to the family. A: Domestic violence (broken families). Drinking often leads to fights and family breakups.
chunks.source: Drinking often leads to fights and family breakups.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(i) State the function of the ligament in the human skeleton. A: It joins bones to bones at joints. Ligaments hold bones together where they meet.
chunks.source: Ligaments hold bones together where they meet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(ii) State the function of the tendon in the human skeleton. A: It joins muscles to bones. Tendons attach muscles to bones so movement is possible.
chunks.source: Tendons attach muscles to bones so movement is possible.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b) Give one example of a long bone in a human skeleton. A: Femur (thigh bone). The femur is the longest bone in the human body.
chunks.source: The femur is the longest bone in the human body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(c) Name one disease that affects a human skeleton. A: Rickets. Rickets weakens and bends the bones of children lacking vitamin D.
chunks.source: Rickets weakens and bends the bones of children lacking vitamin D.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a) Match the component with its function. Fuse → ____. A: Breaks the circuit due to much current. A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when current is too high.
chunks.source: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when current is too high.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) Match the component with its function. Ammeter → ____. A: Measures amount of electricity used. The ammeter is the component that measures electricity in the circuit.
chunks.source: The ammeter is the component that measures electricity in the circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c) Match the component with its function. Voltmeter → ____. A: Measures the voltage in the circuit. A voltmeter measures the voltage (push) in a circuit.
chunks.source: A voltmeter measures the voltage (push) in a circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(d) Match the component with its function. Switch → ____. A: Breaks the circuit at user's wish. A switch opens or closes the circuit whenever the user wants.
chunks.source: A switch opens or closes the circuit whenever the user wants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a) Name the type of lens that is commonly used to correct myopia eye defect. A: Concave (diverging) lens. A concave lens diverges light rays before they enter a short-sighted eye.
chunks.source: A concave lens diverges light rays before they enter a short-sighted eye.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b) Why is a myopic person advised to wear glasses with diverging lens? A: To diverge light rays so that the image forms on the retina. In myopia the image forms in front of the retina; diverging lenses push it back onto the retina.
chunks.source: In myopia the image forms in front of the retina; diverging lenses push it back onto the retina.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c)(i) Apart from washing eyes with water and soap, give one other way of caring for the human eye. A: Avoid reading in dim light. Reading in poor light strains the eyes.
chunks.source: Reading in poor light strains the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c)(ii) Give another way of caring for the human eye apart from washing eyes with water and soap. A: Do not look directly at bright light (eat foods rich in vitamin A). Bright light can damage the eyes; vitamin A keeps them healthy.
chunks.source: Bright light can damage the eyes; vitamin A keeps them healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a) Name the organism that causes candidiasis. A: Candida (a fungus). Candidiasis is caused by the fungus Candida albicans.
chunks.source: Candidiasis is caused by the fungus Candida albicans.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b) Give one sign of candidiasis infection in females. A: Itching in the private parts (smelly discharge). Candidiasis causes itching and discharge in the private parts.
chunks.source: Candidiasis causes itching and discharge in the private parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c)(i) State one way of preventing candidiasis infection in females. A: Keep the private parts clean and dry. Cleanliness and dryness stop the fungus from growing.
chunks.source: Cleanliness and dryness stop the fungus from growing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c)(ii) State another way of preventing candidiasis infection in females. A: Avoid sharing underwear (wear clean dry underwear). Sharing underwear can pass the infection from person to person.
chunks.source: Sharing underwear can pass the infection from person to person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1. What happens to matter when it is heated? A: It expands (its particles move faster and spread out). Heating makes particles gain energy, move faster and push apart, so matter expands.
chunks.source: Heating makes particles gain energy, move faster and push apart, so matter expands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2. Why are weaning babies said to be vulnerable? A: They can easily become malnourished (when moved from breast milk to other foods). During weaning the baby's diet changes, and poor feeding can quickly cause malnutrition.
chunks.source: During weaning the baby's diet changes, and poor feeding can quickly cause malnutrition.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3. The diagram shows an animal farm practice. Name it. A: Docking. The diagram shows a sheep whose tail is shortened; cutting the tail is called docking.
chunks.source: The diagram shows a sheep whose tail is shortened; cutting the tail is called docking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4. Why is it necessary for plants to lose water through transpiration? A: It cools the plant and pulls water and mineral salts up from the roots. Water lost from leaves creates a pull that draws more water and dissolved salts up the stem.
chunks.source: Water lost from leaves creates a pull that draws more water and dissolved salts up the stem.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5. Mention one role of a mother in a home. A: Cooking food for the family (caring for children). A mother prepares meals and cares for the children in a home.
chunks.source: A mother prepares meals and cares for the children in a home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6. How do other crops benefit from the growing of legumes in a garden? A: Legumes add nitrogen to the soil. Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in legume roots enrich the soil for other crops.
chunks.source: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in legume roots enrich the soil for other crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7. Give any one behaviour that made Mustapha, a livestock farmer, suspect that his cow is on heat. A: The cow mounts other cows (restlessness, bellowing). A cow on heat becomes restless, bellows and mounts others.
chunks.source: A cow on heat becomes restless, bellows and mounts others.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8. Where in the alimentary canal does the absorption of water take place? A: In the colon (large intestine). The large intestine absorbs water from undigested food remains.
chunks.source: The large intestine absorbs water from undigested food remains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 9. How important is a screen on a VIP latrine? A: It traps flies (prevents flies from entering and leaving the latrine). The screen on the vent pipe catches flies so they cannot spread germs.
chunks.source: The screen on the vent pipe catches flies so they cannot spread germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10. Give one way in which air is used for transport. A: Aeroplanes move through air. Aeroplanes fly in air to carry people and goods.
chunks.source: Aeroplanes fly in air to carry people and goods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11. How do forests help in reducing the effect of global warming? A: Trees absorb carbon dioxide from the air. Carbon dioxide traps heat; trees remove it during photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide traps heat; trees remove it during photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12. Give one way in which the tools below are helpful to a casualty. A: They support a casualty with an injured leg to walk (aid movement). The crutches help an injured person move without putting weight on the hurt leg.
chunks.source: The crutches help an injured person move without putting weight on the hurt leg.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 13. How do we call static electricity in nature? A: Lightning. Lightning is a giant spark of static electricity in the sky.
chunks.source: Lightning is a giant spark of static electricity in the sky.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14. Write HIV in full. A: Human Immunodeficiency Virus. HIV is the virus that causes AIDS.
chunks.source: HIV is the virus that causes AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15. Why is a magnet placed under a paper able to attract pins on the paper? A: Magnetic force passes through the paper. Magnetism passes through non-magnetic materials like paper.
chunks.source: Magnetism passes through non-magnetic materials like paper.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. The diagram is of a housefly. How is the larva useful to humans? A: The larva (maggot) is used as feed for poultry and fish. Housefly maggots are rich in protein and are fed to chickens and fish.
chunks.source: Housefly maggots are rich in protein and are fed to chickens and fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 17. How important are halteres to an insect? A: They balance the insect during flight. Halteres are small knobbed structures that keep a flying insect steady.
chunks.source: Halteres are small knobbed structures that keep a flying insect steady.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18. What first aid is appropriate for a person with fever? A: Sponge the body with cold water (give plenty of fluids). Sponging cools the body and brings the temperature down.
chunks.source: Sponging cools the body and brings the temperature down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19. Why are there few houseflies in a VIP latrine? A: The screen traps the flies inside (the dark interior keeps them out). Flies entering the vent pipe are trapped by the screen and die.
chunks.source: Flies entering the vent pipe are trapped by the screen and die.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 20. Name one commonly abused drug. A: Alcohol (marijuana). Alcohol, marijuana and tobacco are commonly abused drugs.
chunks.source: Alcohol, marijuana and tobacco are commonly abused drugs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21. Which fuel is commonly used for cooking in villages? A: Firewood. Most village homes cook using firewood.
chunks.source: Most village homes cook using firewood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22. Which part of the body is affected by scabies? A: The skin. Scabies is a skin infection that causes itching.
chunks.source: Scabies is a skin infection that causes itching.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23. What is hibernation? A: A long deep sleep that some animals take during cold or unfavourable conditions. Animals like bats hibernate to survive seasons with little food.
chunks.source: Animals like bats hibernate to survive seasons with little food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 24. Mabira placed a bowl of water under the sun and noted the level. In the evening, he was surprised to find that the water level had gone low. State why it was so. A: Some of the water evaporated due to the sun's heat. Heat from the sun changed some water into vapour, lowering the level.
chunks.source: Heat from the sun changed some water into vapour, lowering the level.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. Mention one food stuff suitable for brick makers. A: Posho. Brick makers do heavy work and need energy-giving foods like posho.
chunks.source: Brick makers do heavy work and need energy-giving foods like posho.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26. Give a reason for your answer in (25) above. A: It gives them energy to do the heavy work. Brick making needs a lot of energy, which carbohydrate foods supply.
chunks.source: Brick making needs a lot of energy, which carbohydrate foods supply.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27. How is family planning important to a nation like Uganda? A: It controls population growth. Family planning helps the nation manage its growing population.
chunks.source: Family planning helps the nation manage its growing population.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28. Explain the term drowning. A: Dying due to lack of air when water fills the lungs. When water enters the lungs, air cannot reach them and the person dies.
chunks.source: When water enters the lungs, air cannot reach them and the person dies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29. Give one energy change that takes place in a bulb as it gives light. A: Electrical energy changes to light (and heat) energy. A bulb converts the electrical energy it receives into light energy.
chunks.source: A bulb converts the electrical energy it receives into light energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30. How can you increase milk production in a dairy cow? A: By feeding it well (on dairy meal). Good feeding, especially with dairy meal, raises milk yield.
chunks.source: Good feeding, especially with dairy meal, raises milk yield.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31. What can one use to put out petrol fire? A: Foam fire extinguisher (sand). Foam or sand smothers a petrol fire; water would spread it.
chunks.source: Foam or sand smothers a petrol fire; water would spread it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32. If a box of mass 25g is immersed in an overflow can and it displaces 5cc of water, find its density. A: 5 g/cc. Density = mass ÷ volume = 25 ÷ 5 = 5 g/cm³.
chunks.source: Density = mass ÷ volume = 25 ÷ 5 = 5 g/cm³.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33. Why is bush fallowing an important practice in farming? A: It allows the soil to regain fertility. Resting the land lets natural plants restore nutrients to the soil.
chunks.source: Resting the land lets natural plants restore nutrients to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34. How can the problem of anaemia be immediately solved in bleeding patients? A: By blood transfusion. Giving blood quickly replaces what the bleeding patient has lost.
chunks.source: Giving blood quickly replaces what the bleeding patient has lost.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35. Give one way in which air is bad to human health. A: Polluted air causes respiratory diseases. Dirty air breathed in can cause cough, asthma and lung diseases.
chunks.source: Dirty air breathed in can cause cough, asthma and lung diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 36. Draw a diagram showing regular reflection. Describe what the diagram should show. A: Parallel incident rays striking a smooth surface and reflecting as parallel rays. In regular reflection, parallel rays hitting a smooth shiny surface bounce off still parallel.
chunks.source: In regular reflection, parallel rays hitting a smooth shiny surface bounce off still parallel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 37. To which group of birds does the one below belong? A: Birds of prey. The eagle's hooked beak and sharp eyes show it is a bird of prey.
chunks.source: The eagle's hooked beak and sharp eyes show it is a bird of prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38. How is the strong sharp hooked beak important to the above bird? A: For tearing flesh (meat) of its prey. The hooked beak grips and rips the flesh of captured prey.
chunks.source: The hooked beak grips and rips the flesh of captured prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. What name is given to the path taken by the flow of electrons? A: A circuit (electric circuit). Electrons flow along a complete path called a circuit.
chunks.source: Electrons flow along a complete path called a circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. Why is it necessary to sleep under a mosquito net? A: To prevent mosquito bites (and malaria). The net blocks mosquitoes from biting a sleeping person.
chunks.source: The net blocks mosquitoes from biting a sleeping person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(i) Name one type of chicken reared in Uganda. A: Layers. Layers are chickens kept for laying eggs.
chunks.source: Layers are chickens kept for laying eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(ii) Name another type of chicken reared in Uganda. A: Broilers. Broilers are chickens kept for meat.
chunks.source: Broilers are chickens kept for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(i) Give a reason for which the layers named in (a) above are kept. A: For laying eggs. Layers produce eggs for sale and eating.
chunks.source: Layers produce eggs for sale and eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(ii) Give a reason for which the broilers named in (a) above are kept. A: For meat production. Broilers grow fast and are slaughtered for meat.
chunks.source: Broilers grow fast and are slaughtered for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42. Complete the table: The vaccine given against polio is ____. A: Polio vaccine (OPV). Polio vaccine drops are given by mouth to prevent polio.
chunks.source: Polio vaccine drops are given by mouth to prevent polio.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42. Complete the table: The site where the DPT vaccine (for tetanus) is given is ____. A: Left thigh (left upper leg). DPT injections are given into the left thigh of babies.
chunks.source: DPT injections are given into the left thigh of babies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42. Complete the table: The disease prevented by the BCG vaccine is ____. A: Tuberculosis (TB). BCG vaccine, given on the right upper arm, prevents tuberculosis.
chunks.source: BCG vaccine, given on the right upper arm, prevents tuberculosis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42. Complete the table: The site where the measles vaccine is given is ____. A: Left upper arm. The measles injection is given on the left upper arm.
chunks.source: The measles injection is given on the left upper arm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a) Study the diagram. Name the method of making magnets shown in the diagram. A: Electrical method. Passing electric current through a coil round a soft iron bar magnetises it.
chunks.source: Passing electric current through a coil round a soft iron bar magnetises it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b) What form of energy is used in the making of the magnet? A: Electrical energy. Current from the cell flows through the coil to magnetise the nail.
chunks.source: Current from the cell flows through the coil to magnetise the nail.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c) What happens to the pins when the switch is turned off? A: They fall off (drop down). The soft iron is a temporary magnet; it loses magnetism once the current stops.
chunks.source: The soft iron is a temporary magnet; it loses magnetism once the current stops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(d) Name the pole on which the pins are attached. A: North pole. The pins hang from one pole of the electromagnet.
chunks.source: The pins hang from one pole of the electromagnet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a) Study the diagram of a mammalian ear. What collective name is given to P? A: Ossicles. P points to the three tiny bones (hammer, anvil, stirrup) called ossicles.
chunks.source: P points to the three tiny bones (hammer, anvil, stirrup) called ossicles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b) In which way is Q important in the process of hearing? A: It vibrates when sound waves hit it, passing the vibrations to the ossicles. Q is the eardrum; it picks up sound vibrations and passes them inward.
chunks.source: Q is the eardrum; it picks up sound vibrations and passes them inward.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c) State the function of D in the mammalian ear. A: It changes sound vibrations into impulses sent to the brain. D is the cochlea, which converts vibrations into nerve messages.
chunks.source: D is the cochlea, which converts vibrations into nerve messages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(d) What would happen if one's ear drum got torn? A: One would become deaf (cannot hear well). A torn eardrum cannot pass vibrations, so hearing is lost.
chunks.source: A torn eardrum cannot pass vibrations, so hearing is lost.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a) Give one example of livestock you know. A: Cattle (goats). Cattle, goats, sheep, pigs and poultry are livestock.
chunks.source: Cattle, goats, sheep, pigs and poultry are livestock.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b) Why do you think rearing livestock can help in reducing poverty? A: Livestock can be sold for income (and provide food for the family). Selling animals and their products brings money to the home.
chunks.source: Selling animals and their products brings money to the home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c) Mention one problem faced by livestock farmers. A: Diseases (lack of feeds, thieves). Animal diseases kill livestock and cause losses to farmers.
chunks.source: Animal diseases kill livestock and cause losses to farmers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(d) How has the problem in (c) above been solved? A: By vaccinating animals (treating sick animals). Vaccination protects animals from diseases; sick ones are treated.
chunks.source: Vaccination protects animals from diseases; sick ones are treated.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) How is alcohol made in your community? A: By fermenting sugary substances (bananas, millet, cassava). Local alcohol is brewed by fermenting sugary plant materials.
chunks.source: Local alcohol is brewed by fermenting sugary plant materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) Which type of alcohol is commonly used as a fuel? A: Ethanol. Ethanol burns well and is used as a fuel.
chunks.source: Ethanol burns well and is used as a fuel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c) In which part of the alimentary canal is alcohol absorbed? A: Stomach. Alcohol is absorbed through the walls of the stomach into the blood.
chunks.source: Alcohol is absorbed through the walls of the stomach into the blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(d) How is alcohol dangerous to an individual? A: It damages body organs (the liver) and affects judgment. Too much alcohol harms the liver and makes people behave badly.
chunks.source: Too much alcohol harms the liver and makes people behave badly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) Study the diagram of a human kidney. Name the part marked B. A: Ureter. Part B is the tube carrying urine from the kidney to the bladder.
chunks.source: Part B is the tube carrying urine from the kidney to the bladder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b) What process takes place in the part marked A? A: Filtration of blood. In the cortex (A), blood is filtered to remove waste products.
chunks.source: In the cortex (A), blood is filtered to remove waste products.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) Name any disease that affects the system shown in the diagram above. A: Kidney stones (nephritis). Kidney stones and nephritis are diseases of the urinary system.
chunks.source: Kidney stones and nephritis are diseases of the urinary system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(d) Write down one way of caring for the kidney and the urinary system. A: Drink plenty of clean water. Enough water helps the kidneys flush out wastes easily.
chunks.source: Enough water helps the kidneys flush out wastes easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(i) One of the functions of the skeleton is to protect delicate parts of the body. State how the lungs are protected. A: By the rib cage. The ribs form a cage around the lungs and heart.
chunks.source: The ribs form a cage around the lungs and heart.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(ii) State how the spinal cord is protected by the skeleton. A: By the backbone (vertebral column). The vertebrae surround and protect the spinal cord.
chunks.source: The vertebrae surround and protect the spinal cord.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b) What food nutrient do poultry birds obtain from crushed animal bones? A: Calcium (mineral salts). Bones are rich in calcium, which birds need for strong bones and eggshells.
chunks.source: Bones are rich in calcium, which birds need for strong bones and eggshells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c) Mention one disease that affects the skeletal system. A: Rickets. Rickets softens and bends the bones of children.
chunks.source: Rickets softens and bends the bones of children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a) Given the organisms A (moss), B (yeast), C (fern), D (mushroom): How is A similar to C in reference to feeding? A: Both make their own food (are green plants). Moss and fern are green plants that photosynthesize.
chunks.source: Moss and fern are green plants that photosynthesize.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) Which of the organisms above is an odd man out? A: B (yeast). Yeast is unicellular while moss, fern and mushroom are multicellular.
chunks.source: Yeast is unicellular while moss, fern and mushroom are multicellular.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c) Give a reason for your answer in 49(b) above. A: It is unicellular while the rest are multicellular. Yeast is a single-celled organism; the others have many cells.
chunks.source: Yeast is a single-celled organism; the others have many cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(d) Mention one other organism that can be classified with D (mushroom). A: Mould (toadstool). Mould and toadstools are fungi like the mushroom.
chunks.source: Mould and toadstools are fungi like the mushroom.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a) Match the item with the correct one. Hydroelectricity → ____. A: Running water. Hydroelectricity is generated using running water.
chunks.source: Hydroelectricity is generated using running water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b) Match the item with the correct one. Solar electricity → ____. A: Sun. Solar electricity comes from the sun.
chunks.source: Solar electricity comes from the sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c) Match the item with the correct one. Thermal electricity → ____. A: Fuels. Thermal electricity is generated by burning fuels.
chunks.source: Thermal electricity is generated by burning fuels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(d) Match the item with the correct one. Electricity path → ____. A: Circuit. The path followed by electric current is a circuit.
chunks.source: The path followed by electric current is a circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a) Write STI in full. A: Sexually Transmitted Infection. STIs are infections passed from person to person through sex.
chunks.source: STIs are infections passed from person to person through sex.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b) Which STI is characterized by painful sores in the genitals, painful urination and pus discharge from the urethra or vagina? A: Gonorrhoea. Gonorrhoea causes sores, painful urination and pus discharge.
chunks.source: Gonorrhoea causes sores, painful urination and pus discharge.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c) What causes the STI mentioned in (b) above? A: Bacteria. Gonorrhoea is caused by bacteria.
chunks.source: Gonorrhoea is caused by bacteria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(d) How can a school going child avoid getting an STI? A: By abstaining from sex. Avoiding sex completely keeps a school child safe from STIs.
chunks.source: Avoiding sex completely keeps a school child safe from STIs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(i) Identify the type of change illustrated: melting of ice. A: Physical change. Melting forms no new substance, so it is physical.
chunks.source: Melting forms no new substance, so it is physical.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(ii) Identify the type of change illustrated: burning of a candle wick. A: Chemical change. Burning produces new substances, so it is chemical.
chunks.source: Burning produces new substances, so it is chemical.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(iii) Identify the type of change illustrated: development of breasts in girls. A: Biological change. Growth changes in living things are biological changes.
chunks.source: Growth changes in living things are biological changes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b) What type of sex characteristic in adolescents is (iii) above? A: Secondary sex characteristic. Breast development is a secondary sex characteristic of girls.
chunks.source: Breast development is a secondary sex characteristic of girls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a) The experiment below was performed by a P.4 class. What was the experiment intended to find out? A: To find the volume of the block (using the displacement method). The rise in water level shows the volume of the immersed block.
chunks.source: The rise in water level shows the volume of the immersed block.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) Name the method used in the experiment above. A: Displacement method. The volume of displaced water equals the volume of the object.
chunks.source: The volume of displaced water equals the volume of the object.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c) What volume of water was in the can? (2 marks) A: 45 cc. The level with the block is 65 cc; block volume = 5 × 2 × 2 = 20 cc; water = 65 − 20 = 45 cc.
chunks.source: The level with the block is 65 cc; block volume = 5 × 2 × 2 = 20 cc; water = 65 − 20 = 45 cc.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a) What is excretion? A: The removal of waste products from the body. Excretion gets rid of wastes the body does not need.
chunks.source: Excretion gets rid of wastes the body does not need.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b)(i) Name the organ responsible for the excretion of carbon dioxide. A: Lungs. The lungs breathe out carbon dioxide.
chunks.source: The lungs breathe out carbon dioxide.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b)(ii) Name the organ responsible for the excretion of urea. A: Kidneys. The kidneys filter urea from blood into urine.
chunks.source: The kidneys filter urea from blood into urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b)(iii) Name the organ responsible for the excretion of sweat. A: Skin. The skin releases sweat through sweat glands.
chunks.source: The skin releases sweat through sweat glands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a) Match the item with the correct one. Hydroelectricity → ____. A: Running water. Hydroelectricity is generated using running water.
chunks.source: Hydroelectricity is generated using running water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b) Match the item with the correct one. Solar electricity → ____. A: Sun. Solar electricity comes from the sun.
chunks.source: Solar electricity comes from the sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c) Match the item with the correct one. Thermal electricity → ____. A: Fuels. Thermal electricity is generated by burning fuels.
chunks.source: Thermal electricity is generated by burning fuels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(d) Match the item with the correct one. Electric path → ____. A: Circuit. The path followed by electric current is a circuit.
chunks.source: The path followed by electric current is a circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1. Give one example of a legume. A: Beans. Beans, peas and groundnuts are legumes.
chunks.source: Beans, peas and groundnuts are legumes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2. What is the use of a trowel to a crop farmer? A: For transplanting seedlings. A trowel is a small tool for lifting and planting seedlings.
chunks.source: A trowel is a small tool for lifting and planting seedlings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3. Give one reason why a spider is not an insect. A: It has eight legs (four pairs). Spiders have eight legs and two body parts, while insects have six legs and three body parts.
chunks.source: Spiders have eight legs and two body parts, while insects have six legs and three body parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4. How is a worker bee able to carry pollen on its body? A: Pollen sticks to its hairy body. The worker bee's hairy body traps pollen grains as it visits flowers.
chunks.source: The worker bee's hairy body traps pollen grains as it visits flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5. What does a mushroom use to reproduce? A: Spores. Mushrooms produce tiny spores that grow into new mushrooms.
chunks.source: Mushrooms produce tiny spores that grow into new mushrooms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6. What is the danger of not brushing your teeth regularly? A: Tooth decay. Food remains and germs left on teeth cause decay.
chunks.source: Food remains and germs left on teeth cause decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7. Why is copper called a good conductor? A: It allows heat and electricity to pass through it easily. Copper wires carry electric current well.
chunks.source: Copper wires carry electric current well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8. How is chlorophyll important in the process of photosynthesis? A: It traps sunlight energy. Chlorophyll, the green pigment, captures the sun's energy for making food.
chunks.source: Chlorophyll, the green pigment, captures the sun's energy for making food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 9. The diagram shows a foot of a bird. Name an example of a bird with this foot. A: Eagle (hawk, kite). Birds of prey like eagles have strong sharp claws for gripping prey.
chunks.source: Birds of prey like eagles have strong sharp claws for gripping prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10. How useful is the structure of this foot to the bird? A: For gripping and killing its prey (tearing flesh). The sharp claws hold prey firmly and tear its flesh.
chunks.source: The sharp claws hold prey firmly and tear its flesh.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11. How does a vacuum prevent heat loss in a flask? A: It prevents heat loss by conduction and convection. A vacuum has no particles to carry heat by conduction or convection.
chunks.source: A vacuum has no particles to carry heat by conduction or convection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12. What do we call a condition when a person cannot see objects that are far from him? A: Myopia (short sight). A short-sighted person sees near objects clearly but not distant ones.
chunks.source: A short-sighted person sees near objects clearly but not distant ones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 13. The diagram shows a type of a pulley system. How does it help to make work easy? A: It changes the direction of the effort (one pulls down to lift the load up). A single fixed pulley lets you pull downward, using your body weight to lift the load.
chunks.source: A single fixed pulley lets you pull downward, using your body weight to lift the load.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14. Which substance in the ear prevents dust from entering the organ? A: Wax. Ear wax traps dust and germs before they reach the inner ear.
chunks.source: Ear wax traps dust and germs before they reach the inner ear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15. Apart from charcoal and timber, name one practice that is a danger to trees. A: Bush burning (deforestation). Bush burning destroys trees and young seedlings.
chunks.source: Bush burning destroys trees and young seedlings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. How does a poultry farmer stop cannibalism among his birds? A: By debeaking. Cutting the beaks short stops birds from pecking and eating each other.
chunks.source: Cutting the beaks short stops birds from pecking and eating each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 17. Give an example of a stem tuber. A: Irish potato. The Irish potato is a swollen underground stem (tuber).
chunks.source: The Irish potato is a swollen underground stem (tuber).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18. How is the reproduction of a housefly different from that of a grasshopper? A: A housefly undergoes complete metamorphosis while a grasshopper undergoes incomplete metamorphosis. The housefly passes through egg, larva, pupa and adult; the grasshopper has no pupa stage.
chunks.source: The housefly passes through egg, larva, pupa and adult; the grasshopper has no pupa stage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19. Which type of plants have a parallel leaf venation? A: Monocots (monocotyledonous plants). Monocots like maize have parallel leaf veins.
chunks.source: Monocots like maize have parallel leaf veins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 20. What is the use of synovial fluid in a joint? A: It lubricates the joint (reduces friction). Synovial fluid oils the joint so bones move smoothly.
chunks.source: Synovial fluid oils the joint so bones move smoothly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21. Which organ in the body allows exchange of gases in blood? A: The lungs. In the lungs, oxygen enters blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.
chunks.source: In the lungs, oxygen enters blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22. What is the use of a urinary bladder? A: It stores urine. Urine from the kidneys collects in the bladder before it is passed out.
chunks.source: Urine from the kidneys collects in the bladder before it is passed out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23. What is the use of ORS to a sick child? A: It replaces water and salts lost during diarrhoea (prevents dehydration). Oral Rehydration Salts restore the fluids a sick child loses.
chunks.source: Oral Rehydration Salts restore the fluids a sick child loses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 24. Why does a piece of stone sink in water? A: It is denser than water. Objects denser than water sink in it.
chunks.source: Objects denser than water sink in it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. Which immunisable disease paralyses limbs of human beings? A: Polio. Polio can paralyse the limbs; immunisation prevents it.
chunks.source: Polio can paralyse the limbs; immunisation prevents it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26. What causes evaporation in a water cycle? A: Heat from the sun. The sun heats water bodies and turns water into vapour.
chunks.source: The sun heats water bodies and turns water into vapour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27. Which activity of sanitation will reduce the spread of malaria in a community? A: Draining stagnant water (slashing bushes). Removing stagnant water destroys mosquito breeding places.
chunks.source: Removing stagnant water destroys mosquito breeding places.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28. What is the danger of water snails to human beings? A: They spread bilharzia (schistosomiasis). Water snails carry the worms that cause bilharzia.
chunks.source: Water snails carry the worms that cause bilharzia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29. What is the use of prop roots on a maize plant? A: They give extra support to the plant. Prop roots hold the tall maize plant firmly in the soil.
chunks.source: Prop roots hold the tall maize plant firmly in the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30. What type of change needs heat to take place? A: Physical change. Physical changes like melting and evaporation need heat.
chunks.source: Physical changes like melting and evaporation need heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31. Give one reason why a mother must breastfeed her baby. A: Breast milk contains all food values the baby needs (and protects against diseases). Breast milk is the complete, safe food for a baby.
chunks.source: Breast milk is the complete, safe food for a baby.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32. How is a bat able to avoid hitting a rock at night? A: By producing echoes (echolocation). A bat sends out sound waves and listens to their echoes to detect obstacles.
chunks.source: A bat sends out sound waves and listens to their echoes to detect obstacles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33. Which practice of cultivation reduces soil erosion in hilly areas? A: Terracing (contour ploughing). Terraces slow down running water on slopes.
chunks.source: Terraces slow down running water on slopes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34. What is passive smoking? A: Breathing in smoke from other people's cigarettes. A non-smoker near smokers inhales their smoke.
chunks.source: A non-smoker near smokers inhales their smoke.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35. Why should garden tools be kept in a dry place? A: To prevent them from rusting. Moisture causes iron tools to rust.
chunks.source: Moisture causes iron tools to rust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 36. Why is human skin called an excretory organ? A: It removes sweat (excess water, salts and urea). The skin excretes wastes as sweat.
chunks.source: The skin excretes wastes as sweat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 37. Which part of a living house allows carbon dioxide out? A: The ventilators. Ventilators let stale air with carbon dioxide escape.
chunks.source: Ventilators let stale air with carbon dioxide escape.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38. What is the use of a nostril to a fish? A: For smelling. A fish uses its nostrils to detect scents in water.
chunks.source: A fish uses its nostrils to detect scents in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. Which blood vessels have valves? A: Veins. Valves in veins stop blood from flowing backwards.
chunks.source: Valves in veins stop blood from flowing backwards.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. How would the seed below be dispersed? A: By animals. The seed has hooks (spines) that stick to animal fur and are carried away.
chunks.source: The seed has hooks (spines) that stick to animal fur and are carried away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(i) Study the diagram of part of a germinating seed. Name the part marked i. A: Endosperm. Part i is the food store of the seed that feeds the embryo.
chunks.source: Part i is the food store of the seed that feeds the embryo.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(ii) Name the part marked ii on the germinating seed. A: Radicle. The radicle is the young root that grows out of the seed first.
chunks.source: The radicle is the young root that grows out of the seed first.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) What is the function of part Y on the germinating seed? A: It grows into the shoot (stem and leaves). Part Y is the plumule, which develops into the shoot of the new plant.
chunks.source: Part Y is the plumule, which develops into the shoot of the new plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c) Name one condition that would make a seed fail to germinate. A: Lack of moisture (air, warmth). Seeds need water, air and warmth to germinate.
chunks.source: Seeds need water, air and warmth to germinate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(i) Match the weather instrument with what it does. Windsock → ____. A: Strength of wind. A windsock shows how strong the wind is blowing.
chunks.source: A windsock shows how strong the wind is blowing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(ii) Match the weather instrument with what it does. Rain gauge → ____. A: How much it has rained. A rain gauge measures the amount of rainfall.
chunks.source: A rain gauge measures the amount of rainfall.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(iii) Match the weather instrument with what it does. Sixth's thermometer → ____. A: Temperature. Sixth's thermometer records maximum and minimum temperatures.
chunks.source: Sixth's thermometer records maximum and minimum temperatures.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(iv) Match the weather instrument with what it does. Barometer → ____. A: Atmospheric pressure. A barometer measures the pressure of the air.
chunks.source: A barometer measures the pressure of the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(i) Give the cause of kwashiorkor in the human body. A: Lack of proteins in the diet. Kwashiorkor is a deficiency disease caused by too little protein food.
chunks.source: Kwashiorkor is a deficiency disease caused by too little protein food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(ii) Give the cause of anaemia in the human body. A: Lack of iron in the diet. Without enough iron the body cannot make enough red blood cells.
chunks.source: Without enough iron the body cannot make enough red blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(i) Apart from refrigeration, give one other way of conserving fish. A: Smoking. Smoking dries fish and keeps it from going bad.
chunks.source: Smoking dries fish and keeps it from going bad.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(ii) Give another way of conserving fish apart from refrigeration. A: Sun drying (salting). Drying or salting removes water so germs cannot grow on fish.
chunks.source: Drying or salting removes water so germs cannot grow on fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a) Study the diagram. What is the method of magnetization called? A: Stroking method. Rubbing a magnet along a nail in one direction magnetises it.
chunks.source: Rubbing a magnet along a nail in one direction magnetises it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b) What would happen if point X of the nail is put at pole S? A: It would be attracted. Point X becomes a north pole, and unlike poles attract.
chunks.source: Point X becomes a north pole, and unlike poles attract.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c) Name one activity that would make a magnet lose its magnetism. A: Heating it strongly (hammering it). Strong heat or hammering disturbs the magnet's particles and weakens it.
chunks.source: Strong heat or hammering disturbs the magnet's particles and weakens it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(d) Which part of a radio uses a permanent magnet? A: The loudspeaker. The radio's loudspeaker contains a permanent magnet.
chunks.source: The radio's loudspeaker contains a permanent magnet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a) What are energy resources? A: Things from which energy can be obtained. Energy resources like the sun, water and fuels supply energy.
chunks.source: Energy resources like the sun, water and fuels supply energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b) What is the major source of energy on earth? A: The sun. Almost all energy on earth comes from the sun.
chunks.source: Almost all energy on earth comes from the sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c)(i) Give one way by which water can act as a resource. A: It is used to generate hydroelectricity. Running water turns turbines to make electricity.
chunks.source: Running water turns turbines to make electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c)(ii) Give another way by which water can act as a resource. A: It is used for drinking (irrigation, transport). Water is drunk by people and animals and used in farming.
chunks.source: Water is drunk by people and animals and used in farming.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a)(i) Name one type of pollination in flowering plants. A: Self pollination. In self pollination, pollen moves within the same flower.
chunks.source: In self pollination, pollen moves within the same flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a)(ii) Name another type of pollination in flowering plants. A: Cross pollination. In cross pollination, pollen moves from one flower to another.
chunks.source: In cross pollination, pollen moves from one flower to another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b)(i) What is the use of anthers during pollination? A: They produce pollen grains. The anthers make the pollen needed for pollination.
chunks.source: The anthers make the pollen needed for pollination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b)(ii) What is the use of the stigma during pollination? A: It receives pollen grains. Pollen lands and sticks on the stigma.
chunks.source: Pollen lands and sticks on the stigma.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) Study the diagram of a boy using a metallic bar to raise a bag of coffee. Which type of machine is he using? A: A lever. The metallic bar turning on a pivot is a lever.
chunks.source: The metallic bar turning on a pivot is a lever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b) What can he do to lift the sack more easily? A: Move the pivot (fulcrum) nearer to the load (use a longer bar). A longer effort arm makes the lever lift heavy loads more easily.
chunks.source: A longer effort arm makes the lever lift heavy loads more easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) Name the force that slows movement in moving parts of a machine. A: Friction. Friction opposes motion between touching surfaces.
chunks.source: Friction opposes motion between touching surfaces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(d) How is the force in (c) useful in our daily life? A: It enables us to walk without slipping (to grip things, to stop vehicles with brakes). Friction lets our feet grip the ground and brakes stop vehicles.
chunks.source: Friction lets our feet grip the ground and brakes stop vehicles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(i) Study the diagram of a ray of light on a smooth shiny surface Z. Name part X. A: Incident ray. Part X is the ray striking the surface.
chunks.source: Part X is the ray striking the surface.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(ii) Name part W on the diagram of a ray of light. A: Reflected ray. Part W is the ray bouncing off the surface.
chunks.source: Part W is the ray bouncing off the surface.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b) Name an instrument where the above principle is used. A: Periscope (plane mirror). A periscope uses reflection on plane mirrors to see over obstacles.
chunks.source: A periscope uses reflection on plane mirrors to see over obstacles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c) Show the angle of reflection on the diagram using the letter T. Describe where T should be placed. A: Between the reflected ray (W) and the normal. The angle of reflection is measured between the reflected ray and the normal.
chunks.source: The angle of reflection is measured between the reflected ray and the normal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a) What is First Aid? A: The first help given to a casualty before he or she is taken to hospital. First aid is immediate care that saves life before proper treatment.
chunks.source: First aid is immediate care that saves life before proper treatment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(i) Give one reason why an injured person may need first aid. A: To save life. Quick first aid can keep a casualty alive.
chunks.source: Quick first aid can keep a casualty alive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(ii) Give another reason why an injured person may need first aid. A: To reduce pain (prevent the injury from becoming worse). First aid eases pain and stops the injury worsening.
chunks.source: First aid eases pain and stops the injury worsening.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c) How is a splint useful to a person with fractured lower leg? A: It keeps the broken bones in position (immobilizes the fracture). A splint holds the broken leg still so the bones do not move.
chunks.source: A splint holds the broken leg still so the bones do not move.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a) What is teenage pregnancy? A: Pregnancy in girls below 20 years (13 to 19 years). When a teenage girl becomes pregnant, it is teenage pregnancy.
chunks.source: When a teenage girl becomes pregnant, it is teenage pregnancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(i) Apart from failure to have safe delivery, give one other danger of teenage pregnancy. A: Death of the mother. Teenage mothers face high risks, including death during birth.
chunks.source: Teenage mothers face high risks, including death during birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(ii) Give another danger of teenage pregnancy apart from failure to have safe delivery. A: Dropping out of school. Pregnant schoolgirls often leave school.
chunks.source: Pregnant schoolgirls often leave school.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c) How can a school prevent teenage pregnancies? A: By sensitizing pupils about the dangers (guidance and counselling). Teaching pupils the dangers helps them avoid early pregnancy.
chunks.source: Teaching pupils the dangers helps them avoid early pregnancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(i) How is castration important to a cattle farmer? A: It makes bulls calm and easy to handle (and they fatten faster). Castrated bulls (bullocks) are docile and good for work and beef.
chunks.source: Castrated bulls (bullocks) are docile and good for work and beef.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(ii) How is deworming important to a cattle farmer? A: It kills internal parasites (worms), keeping cattle healthy. Deworming removes worms so cattle grow well.
chunks.source: Deworming removes worms so cattle grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(i) Give one system used in grazing cattle. A: Paddocking. In paddocking, cattle graze in fenced portions of pasture in turn.
chunks.source: In paddocking, cattle graze in fenced portions of pasture in turn.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(ii) Give another system used in grazing cattle. A: Tethering (herding, zero grazing). Cattle can be tied with ropes, herded, or kept under zero grazing.
chunks.source: Cattle can be tied with ropes, herded, or kept under zero grazing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(i) Give one way of making water safe for drinking. A: Boiling. Boiling kills germs in water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(ii) Give another way of making water safe for drinking. A: Filtering (chlorination). Filtering removes dirt; chlorine kills germs.
chunks.source: Filtering removes dirt; chlorine kills germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(i) Write one way by which water can become impure. A: Dumping wastes in water sources. Wastes thrown into water make it dirty and unsafe.
chunks.source: Wastes thrown into water make it dirty and unsafe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(ii) Write another way by which water can become impure. A: Urinating or defecating near water sources. Human wastes near water sources wash germs into the water.
chunks.source: Human wastes near water sources wash germs into the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(i) Study the diagram of a simple electric circuit. Name the part marked T. A: Connecting wire. Part T is the wire joining the components of the circuit.
chunks.source: Part T is the wire joining the components of the circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(ii) Name the part marked R on the simple electric circuit. A: Bulb. Part R is the electric bulb that lights when current flows.
chunks.source: Part R is the electric bulb that lights when current flows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) If Q is closed, give one reason why R would not light. A: The cell (battery) is dead (the fuse S is blown, or there is a loose connection). Even with the switch closed, a flat cell or broken connection stops current.
chunks.source: Even with the switch closed, a flat cell or broken connection stops current.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c) How is S useful in the above circuit? A: It protects the circuit by breaking it when there is too much current (S is a fuse). The fuse melts and opens the circuit if current becomes dangerously high.
chunks.source: The fuse melts and opens the circuit if current becomes dangerously high.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(i) Study part of the human alimentary canal. Name part R. A: Gall bladder. Part R is the small sac under the liver that stores bile.
chunks.source: Part R is the small sac under the liver that stores bile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(ii) Give the function of part R of the alimentary canal. A: It stores bile. The gall bladder keeps bile until it is needed in digestion.
chunks.source: The gall bladder keeps bile until it is needed in digestion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b) Where does food go after P? A: To the ileum (small intestine). Part P is the duodenum; food moves on into the ileum for final digestion and absorption.
chunks.source: Part P is the duodenum; food moves on into the ileum for final digestion and absorption.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) Give one way of preventing constipation. A: Eat foods rich in roughage (fibre) and drink plenty of water. Roughage and water keep food moving through the gut.
chunks.source: Roughage and water keep food moving through the gut.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a)(i) The government of Uganda has stopped the use and manufacture of polythene bags. Give one reason why this was done. A: Polythene bags pollute the environment (they do not rot). Polythene litters the land and does not decay.
