chunks.source: Polythene litters the land and does not decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a)(ii) Give another reason why the use and manufacture of polythene bags was stopped. A: They block drainages, causing floods. Polythene bags choke water channels and cause flooding.
chunks.source: Polythene bags choke water channels and cause flooding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(i) Apart from controlling the spread of crop pests, give one other use of mulching a garden. A: It keeps moisture in the soil. Mulch covers the soil and reduces water loss by evaporation.
chunks.source: Mulch covers the soil and reduces water loss by evaporation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(ii) Give another use of mulching a garden apart from controlling the spread of crop pests. A: It controls soil erosion (adds manure when it rots). Mulch protects soil from runoff and rots into manure.
chunks.source: Mulch protects soil from runoff and rots into manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1. What is the use of small hair found in the nose? A: To trap dust and germs from inhaled air. Nasal hairs filter the air we breathe in.
chunks.source: Nasal hairs filter the air we breathe in.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2. Which immunisable disease causes lameness in children? A: Polio. Polio can paralyse children's legs, causing lameness.
chunks.source: Polio can paralyse children's legs, causing lameness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3. Why is a cockroach classified as an invertebrate? A: It has no backbone (spine). Invertebrates are animals without backbones.
chunks.source: Invertebrates are animals without backbones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4. What advice would you give to your fellow P.7 pupils about protection of the environment against polythene bags? A: Avoid using polythene bags (use paper or cloth bags instead). Refusing polythene bags reduces pollution of the environment.
chunks.source: Refusing polythene bags reduces pollution of the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5. Where in the alimentary canal does digestion of food end? A: In the ileum (small intestine). Digestion is completed in the ileum before absorption.
chunks.source: Digestion is completed in the ileum before absorption.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6. Gilamia touched a kettle full of water and found it to be hot. Which body sense enabled her to tell that the kettle was hot? A: The sense of touch (feeling). The skin feels heat through the sense of touch.
chunks.source: The skin feels heat through the sense of touch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7. The diagram shows three liquids with different densities. Which of the three liquids has the lowest density? A: Liquid P. The least dense liquid floats on top; P is the top layer.
chunks.source: The least dense liquid floats on top; P is the top layer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8. What is the role of chlorophyll during the process of photosynthesis? A: To trap sunlight energy. Chlorophyll captures light energy for making food.
chunks.source: Chlorophyll captures light energy for making food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 9. Kikojjo sprayed mosquitoes and Oniambe in the next room could smell the insecticide. What process enabled the smell of insecticide to reach Oniambe in the next room? A: Diffusion. Gas particles spread from where they are many to where they are few.
chunks.source: Gas particles spread from where they are many to where they are few.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10. Mention one example of a non-luminous object in the environment. A: The moon (a book, a table). Non-luminous objects do not give out their own light.
chunks.source: Non-luminous objects do not give out their own light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11. What practice is carried out by constructors to leave a room for expansion when building railway lines? A: Leaving small gaps between rails. Gaps allow the metal rails to expand on hot days without buckling.
chunks.source: Gaps allow the metal rails to expand on hot days without buckling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12. Apart from warmth, state any one other condition necessary for germination. A: Moisture (air/oxygen). Seeds also need water and air to germinate.
chunks.source: Seeds also need water and air to germinate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 13. Draw the image formed by a plane mirror using the characteristics of images formed by plane mirrors. Describe the image. A: An upright image of the same size, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front. Plane mirrors form upright, same-size images behind the mirror.
chunks.source: Plane mirrors form upright, same-size images behind the mirror.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14. How are seeds with hooks like black jack dispersed? A: By animals. Hooked seeds stick to animal fur and are carried away.
chunks.source: Hooked seeds stick to animal fur and are carried away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15. Nankya cannot see clearly when it is getting dark. What vitamin is deficient in her diet? A: Vitamin A. Lack of vitamin A causes night blindness.
chunks.source: Lack of vitamin A causes night blindness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. What is the difference between a sprain and a strain? A: A sprain is the tearing of ligaments while a strain is the tearing of muscles (tendons). Sprains affect ligaments at joints; strains affect muscles or tendons.
chunks.source: Sprains affect ligaments at joints; strains affect muscles or tendons.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 17. The diagram is of a pulley. What type of pulley is shown in the diagram? A: Movable pulley. The pulley block moves with the load, so it is a movable pulley.
chunks.source: The pulley block moves with the load, so it is a movable pulley.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18. Calculate the effort needed to raise the load shown in the diagram above. A: 25 kg. With a single movable pulley, effort = load ÷ 2 = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 kg.
chunks.source: With a single movable pulley, effort = load ÷ 2 = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 kg.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19. Suggest one way a P.7 candidate can promote personal hygiene. A: Bathing daily (brushing teeth, washing hands). Daily bathing keeps the body clean and healthy.
chunks.source: Daily bathing keeps the body clean and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21. How can a farmer improve on his local breeds of rabbits? A: By crossbreeding them with exotic breeds. Crossing local and exotic rabbits produces improved offspring.
chunks.source: Crossing local and exotic rabbits produces improved offspring.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22. Name the method that is used to measure the volume of irregular objects. A: Displacement method. The volume of displaced water equals the volume of the object.
chunks.source: The volume of displaced water equals the volume of the object.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23. Apart from BCG vaccine, mention the other vaccine administered to babies at birth. A: Polio vaccine (OPV). Newborns receive BCG and polio vaccine drops at birth.
chunks.source: Newborns receive BCG and polio vaccine drops at birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 24. How are viviparous animals different from oviparous animals? A: Viviparous animals give birth to live young while oviparous animals lay eggs. Viviparous young develop inside the mother; oviparous young develop in eggs.
chunks.source: Viviparous young develop inside the mother; oviparous young develop in eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. Name the excretory organ that suffers from hepatitis disease. A: The liver. Hepatitis is a disease of the liver.
chunks.source: Hepatitis is a disease of the liver.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26. Apart from faeces, mention any other material used in a bio-gas digester in production of bio gas. A: Urine (plant remains). Urine and plant wastes are also fed into a bio-gas digester.
chunks.source: Urine and plant wastes are also fed into a bio-gas digester.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27. How does the function of the ear drum differ from that of the Eustachian tube in the mammalian ear? A: The eardrum vibrates to pass sound while the Eustachian tube balances air pressure on both sides of the eardrum. The eardrum picks up vibrations; the Eustachian tube equalises pressure.
chunks.source: The eardrum picks up vibrations; the Eustachian tube equalises pressure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28. Which type of cattle has the body shape shown below? A: Dairy cattle. Dairy cattle have a triangular (wedge) body shape.
chunks.source: Dairy cattle have a triangular (wedge) body shape.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29. Magnets can help in separation of mixtures. Why can't a magnet separate nails from steel filings? A: Both nails and steel filings are magnetic (both are attracted by the magnet). A magnet cannot separate two materials that are both attracted to it.
chunks.source: A magnet cannot separate two materials that are both attracted to it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30. Name the disease caused by Onchocerca volvulus. A: River blindness. The Onchocerca worm causes river blindness.
chunks.source: The Onchocerca worm causes river blindness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31. Write HIV in full. A: Human Immunodeficiency Virus. HIV is the virus that causes AIDS.
chunks.source: HIV is the virus that causes AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32. Name the force which enables rain drops to fall from condensed clouds. A: Gravity. Gravity pulls rain drops down to the earth.
chunks.source: Gravity pulls rain drops down to the earth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33. What advice would you give Yokosan who wants to determine the amount of rainfall received in his home area? A: To use a rain gauge. A rain gauge measures the amount of rainfall.
chunks.source: A rain gauge measures the amount of rainfall.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34. Name the mineral from which tungsten is made. A: Wolframite. Tungsten is obtained from wolframite ore.
chunks.source: Tungsten is obtained from wolframite ore.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35. Define the term sex deviation. A: Abnormal sexual behaviour. Sex deviation is sexual behaviour that is not normal or acceptable.
chunks.source: Sex deviation is sexual behaviour that is not normal or acceptable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 36. Write down one principle of reflection of light. A: The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. A ray striking a surface bounces off at the same angle.
chunks.source: A ray striking a surface bounces off at the same angle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 37. Why are some objects like aeroplanes streamlined? A: To reduce air resistance. Streamlined shapes cut through air easily.
chunks.source: Streamlined shapes cut through air easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38. How are periscopes useful to submarines when in water? A: They enable people in the submarine to see objects above the water surface. A periscope rises above water so the crew can see without surfacing.
chunks.source: A periscope rises above water so the crew can see without surfacing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. Mention one example of a plant fibre. A: Cotton. Cotton fibres come from the cotton plant.
chunks.source: Cotton fibres come from the cotton plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. Name one method of storing sound. A: On tapes (CDs, records, memory cards). Sound can be stored on tapes, CDs and memory cards.
chunks.source: Sound can be stored on tapes, CDs and memory cards.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a) What is puberty? A: The stage when a child's body becomes sexually mature. At puberty the body changes and becomes able to reproduce.
chunks.source: At puberty the body changes and becomes able to reproduce.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(i) Give one body change common in adolescents during puberty. A: Growth of pubic hair. Both boys and girls grow pubic hair at puberty.
chunks.source: Both boys and girls grow pubic hair at puberty.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(ii) Give another body change common in adolescents during puberty. A: Growth of hair in the armpits. Hair under the arms appears in both sexes.
chunks.source: Hair under the arms appears in both sexes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c) Mention one emotional change common in adolescents. A: Mood swings (attraction to the opposite sex). Adolescents experience changing moods and new feelings.
chunks.source: Adolescents experience changing moods and new feelings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a) How is malaria spread? A: Through the bite of an infected female anopheles mosquito. The female anopheles mosquito injects malaria parasites when it bites.
chunks.source: The female anopheles mosquito injects malaria parasites when it bites.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) How does a fish help in controlling the above disease? A: It eats mosquito larvae in water. Fish feed on mosquito larvae, reducing the number of mosquitoes.
chunks.source: Fish feed on mosquito larvae, reducing the number of mosquitoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c)(i) Give one way through which people can get communicable diseases. A: Through contaminated water or food. Germs in dirty water and food cause diseases.
chunks.source: Germs in dirty water and food cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c)(ii) Give another way through which people can get communicable diseases. A: Through insect bites (body contact with an infected person). Bites and close contact pass germs between people.
chunks.source: Bites and close contact pass germs between people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(i) Study the diagrams of types of lenses. Name the lens marked (i). A: Concave lens. Lens (i) is thinner in the middle, so it is concave.
chunks.source: Lens (i) is thinner in the middle, so it is concave.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(ii) Name the lens marked (ii) on the diagrams of types of lenses. A: Convex lens. Lens (ii) is thicker in the middle, so it is convex.
chunks.source: Lens (ii) is thicker in the middle, so it is convex.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b) Complete the diagrams above to show the light rays after passing through the lenses. Describe what happens to the rays. A: Rays diverge (spread out) after the concave lens and converge (meet) after the convex lens. Concave lenses spread light rays; convex lenses bring them together.
chunks.source: Concave lenses spread light rays; convex lenses bring them together.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a) What is breast feeding? A: Feeding a baby on breast milk. Breastfeeding is giving a baby milk directly from the mother's breast.
chunks.source: Breastfeeding is giving a baby milk directly from the mother's breast.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b)(i) Outline one advantage of breast feeding to a mother. A: It is cheap (creates a bond between mother and child). Breast milk costs nothing and brings mother and baby close.
chunks.source: Breast milk costs nothing and brings mother and baby close.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b)(ii) Outline another advantage of breast feeding to a mother. A: It helps the uterus return to normal size (delays the next pregnancy). Breastfeeding helps the mother's body recover after birth.
chunks.source: Breastfeeding helps the mother's body recover after birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c) State the food value which is not available in breast milk. A: Iron. Breast milk lacks enough iron, so older babies need other foods.
chunks.source: Breast milk lacks enough iron, so older babies need other foods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a) Study the feeding relationship among living things. What name is given to the relationship above? A: Food chain. Grass → grasshopper → hen → man → bacteria shows feeding in a straight chain.
chunks.source: Grass → grasshopper → hen → man → bacteria shows feeding in a straight chain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(i) Which organism in the list above is referred to as a primary consumer? A: Grasshopper. The grasshopper feeds directly on the producer (grass).
chunks.source: The grasshopper feeds directly on the producer (grass).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(ii) Which organism in the list above is referred to as a decomposer? A: Bacteria. Bacteria break down dead organisms in the chain.
chunks.source: Bacteria break down dead organisms in the chain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c) Apart from food, give one other way animals depend on each other. A: For shelter (protection). Animals also depend on each other for shelter and protection.
chunks.source: Animals also depend on each other for shelter and protection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46. Complete the table: The vector that spreads cholera is ____. A: Housefly. Houseflies carry cholera germs from faeces to food.
chunks.source: Houseflies carry cholera germs from faeces to food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46. Complete the table: The disease spread by the water snail is ____. A: Bilharzia (schistosomiasis). Water snails host the worms that cause bilharzia.
chunks.source: Water snails host the worms that cause bilharzia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46. Complete the table: The vector that spreads sleeping sickness is ____. A: Tsetse fly. The tsetse fly transmits the germs that cause sleeping sickness.
chunks.source: The tsetse fly transmits the germs that cause sleeping sickness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46. Complete the table: The disease spread by the black fly is ____. A: River blindness. Black flies transmit the worm causing river blindness.
chunks.source: Black flies transmit the worm causing river blindness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) What term is used to describe the small living organisms which destroy crops in the garden? A: Pests. Pests are organisms that damage crops.
chunks.source: Pests are organisms that damage crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(i) Identify one example of a root crop pest. A: Mole rat. Mole rats eat root crops like cassava and sweet potatoes.
chunks.source: Mole rats eat root crops like cassava and sweet potatoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(ii) Identify another example of a root crop pest. A: Sweet potato weevil. Weevils bore into sweet potato roots.
chunks.source: Weevils bore into sweet potato roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) Suggest one way of controlling weeds in the garden. A: Uprooting them (mulching, spraying herbicides). Weeds can be uprooted, smothered with mulch or sprayed.
chunks.source: Weeds can be uprooted, smothered with mulch or sprayed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a) What name is given to the thick wall that separates the heart into the left and right side? A: Septum. The septum divides the heart into left and right halves.
chunks.source: The septum divides the heart into left and right halves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b) What name is given to the lower chambers of the heart? A: Ventricles. The two lower chambers that pump blood are the ventricles.
chunks.source: The two lower chambers that pump blood are the ventricles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c) What name is given to blood vessels that take away blood from the heart? A: Arteries. Arteries carry blood away from the heart to the body.
chunks.source: Arteries carry blood away from the heart to the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(d) Name the blood vessel that carries digested food from the ileum to the liver. A: Hepatic portal vein. The hepatic portal vein transports digested food to the liver.
chunks.source: The hepatic portal vein transports digested food to the liver.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a) Study the experiments shown. Name the type of soil marked A. A: Clay soil. Soil A lets the least water through, which is typical of clay soil.
chunks.source: Soil A lets the least water through, which is typical of clay soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) What was the experiment about? A: To find out which type of soil retains (holds) the most water. Water was poured through different soils to compare how much each holds.
chunks.source: Water was poured through different soils to compare how much each holds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c) Which type of soil has the highest water retention? A: Clay soil. Clay particles are tiny and hold water best.
chunks.source: Clay particles are tiny and hold water best.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(d) Mention any one way in which soil is formed. A: By weathering of rocks. Rocks break down over time to form soil.
chunks.source: Rocks break down over time to form soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50. Kembabazi weighs 80 kg and sits 3 metres from the fulcrum. How far from the pivot should her friend Babirye who weighs 60 kg sit in order to balance the see-saw as shown below? A: 4 metres. 80 × 3 = 60 × d, so d = 240 ÷ 60 = 4 m.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a) What are essential drugs? A: Drugs that satisfy the health needs of most people (and must always be available). Essential drugs are the basic medicines every health unit should stock.
chunks.source: Essential drugs are the basic medicines every health unit should stock.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(i) State one drug commonly abused in Uganda. A: Alcohol. Alcohol is the most commonly abused drug.
chunks.source: Alcohol is the most commonly abused drug.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(ii) State another drug commonly abused in Uganda. A: Marijuana (tobacco). Marijuana and tobacco are also commonly abused.
chunks.source: Marijuana and tobacco are also commonly abused.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c) What do we call the time when the drug is too old to be used by the patients? A: Expiry date. After the expiry date, a drug is no longer safe to use.
chunks.source: After the expiry date, a drug is no longer safe to use.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(i) Give one example of a chemical change. A: Burning of wood. Burning forms new substances, so it is chemical.
chunks.source: Burning forms new substances, so it is chemical.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(ii) Give another example of a chemical change. A: Rusting of iron. Rusting forms a new substance (rust).
chunks.source: Rusting forms a new substance (rust).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(i) Give one example of a biological change. A: Germination (growth). Growth changes in living things are biological.
chunks.source: Growth changes in living things are biological.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(ii) Give another example of a biological change. A: Growth of a baby into an adult. Development of living things is a biological change.
chunks.source: Development of living things is a biological change.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a) The skin is an excretory body organ in humans. Name one excretory product that the skin releases. A: Sweat. The skin releases excess water, salts and urea as sweat.
chunks.source: The skin releases excess water, salts and urea as sweat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b)(i) Besides excretion, state one other way in which the skin is important in the human body. A: It protects the inner body parts. The skin covers and shields delicate organs inside.
chunks.source: The skin covers and shields delicate organs inside.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b)(ii) State another way in which the skin is important in the human body besides excretion. A: It regulates body temperature. Sweating and shivering through the skin control body heat.
chunks.source: Sweating and shivering through the skin control body heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c) Give one viral infection that affects the human skin. A: Chicken pox (measles). Chicken pox is a viral disease that shows on the skin.
chunks.source: Chicken pox is a viral disease that shows on the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(i) Mention one enzyme that helps in digestion of food. A: Ptyalin (salivary amylase). Ptyalin in saliva starts digesting starch in the mouth.
chunks.source: Ptyalin in saliva starts digesting starch in the mouth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(ii) Mention another enzyme that helps in digestion of food. A: Pepsin. Pepsin in gastric juice digests proteins in the stomach.
chunks.source: Pepsin in gastric juice digests proteins in the stomach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b)(i) Where is saliva produced from? A: Salivary glands. Three pairs of salivary glands make saliva.
chunks.source: Three pairs of salivary glands make saliva.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b)(ii) Where is gastric juice produced from? A: Walls of the stomach (gastric glands). Glands in the stomach walls secrete gastric juice.
chunks.source: Glands in the stomach walls secrete gastric juice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a) Study the diagram of parts of the flower. Name the part marked X. A: Stigma. Part X is the top of the pistil that receives pollen.
chunks.source: Part X is the top of the pistil that receives pollen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(i) What will part Y develop into after fertilization? A: Fruit. Part Y is the ovary, which ripens into the fruit.
chunks.source: Part Y is the ovary, which ripens into the fruit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(ii) What will part Z develop into after fertilization? A: Seeds. Part Z represents the ovules, which become seeds.
chunks.source: Part Z represents the ovules, which become seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c) What is the difference between a fruit and a seed? A: A fruit is a ripened ovary containing seeds while a seed is a fertilized ovule that grows into a new plant. The fruit protects the seeds; the seed contains the embryo of the new plant.
chunks.source: The fruit protects the seeds; the seed contains the embryo of the new plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1. Why does a bedbug produce a very bad smell when it is touched? A: To scare away its enemies (for defence).. A bedbug releases a bad smell as a defence to frighten away animals that touch it.
chunks.source: A bedbug releases a bad smell as a defence to frighten away animals that touch it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2. Give any one way in which flowers are important to a plant. A: They help the plant to reproduce (they develop into seeds and fruits).. Flowers are the reproductive parts of a plant; after pollination they form seeds and fruits.
chunks.source: Flowers are the reproductive parts of a plant; after pollination they form seeds and fruits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3. Which deficiency disease in children has these signs and symptoms: swollen moon face, brownish hair and pot belly? A: Kwashiorkor.. Kwashiorkor is caused by lack of proteins in the diet and shows a swollen face, brownish hair and a pot belly.
chunks.source: Kwashiorkor is caused by lack of proteins in the diet and shows a swollen face, brownish hair and a pot belly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4. Write one common characteristic which is common in all arachnids. A: They have four pairs of walking legs (eight legs).. All arachnids such as spiders, ticks and scorpions have eight legs and their bodies are divided into two parts.
chunks.source: All arachnids such as spiders, ticks and scorpions have eight legs and their bodies are divided into two parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5. Why does sugar disappear when it is mixed in water? A: Sugar dissolves in water.. When sugar is mixed with water it dissolves, forming a solution, so it seems to disappear.
chunks.source: When sugar is mixed with water it dissolves, forming a solution, so it seems to disappear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6. Which property of air is demonstrated when air is pumped into a ball and it becomes bigger? A: Air occupies space.. The ball becomes bigger because the air pumped into it takes up space inside the ball.
chunks.source: The ball becomes bigger because the air pumped into it takes up space inside the ball.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7. How is the absence of vitamin D harmful to our health? A: It causes rickets (weak, soft bones).. Vitamin D helps the body to use calcium for strong bones; without it children develop rickets.
chunks.source: Vitamin D helps the body to use calcium for strong bones; without it children develop rickets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8. What is the importance of blood platelets in the body? A: They help blood to clot (stop bleeding).. When you are cut, platelets gather at the wound and make the blood clot so that bleeding stops.
chunks.source: When you are cut, platelets gather at the wound and make the blood clot so that bleeding stops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 9. Give one reason why a farmer should keep records of daily weather. A: To plan farming activities (for example, to know when to plant crops).. Weather records help a farmer decide the best time for planting, weeding and harvesting.
chunks.source: Weather records help a farmer decide the best time for planting, weeding and harvesting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10. Why is proper disposal of wastes important in a home? A: It prevents the spread of diseases.. Wastes left anyhow breed germs and vectors, so proper disposal keeps the home free from diseases.
chunks.source: Wastes left anyhow breed germs and vectors, so proper disposal keeps the home free from diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11. Which of the following animals: fish, frog, lizard, rat and a snail is warm blooded? A: Rat.. A rat is a mammal, and mammals are warm blooded; the other animals are cold blooded.
chunks.source: A rat is a mammal, and mammals are warm blooded; the other animals are cold blooded.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12. In the space provided below, draw a symbol of a switch. A: A switch symbol: a break in a straight wire with a short slanting line (lever) bridging the gap.. The switch symbol shows a wire with a small gap and a lever that can close the gap to complete the circuit.
chunks.source: The switch symbol shows a wire with a small gap and a lever that can close the gap to complete the circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 13. What type of energy is possessed by a stone resting on the table? A: Potential energy.. A stone resting above the ground has stored energy because of its position; this is potential energy.
chunks.source: A stone resting above the ground has stored energy because of its position; this is potential energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14. When water is heated it changes into steam. What is this process called? A: Evaporation.. Heating water changes it from liquid to gas (steam); this change of state is called evaporation.
chunks.source: Heating water changes it from liquid to gas (steam); this change of state is called evaporation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15. Name any one example of a perennial crop. A: Mango (any one: coffee, banana, avocado, orange).. Perennial crops live for many years; mango, coffee and banana are common examples.
chunks.source: Perennial crops live for many years; mango, coffee and banana are common examples.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. How does paddock system of grazing cattle control the spread of tick borne diseases? A: It breaks the life cycle of ticks (ticks starve and die while a paddock rests without cattle).. Moving cattle from paddock to paddock leaves ticks without animals to feed on, so the ticks die.
chunks.source: Moving cattle from paddock to paddock leaves ticks without animals to feed on, so the ticks die.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 17. Give any one reason why we should wring clothes before drying them. A: To remove excess water so that the clothes dry faster.. Wringing squeezes out most of the water, leaving less water to evaporate in the sun.
chunks.source: Wringing squeezes out most of the water, leaving less water to evaporate in the sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18. Write down any one part which makes the stamen on a flower. A: Anther (any one: filament).. The stamen is the male part of a flower and is made up of the anther and the filament.
chunks.source: The stamen is the male part of a flower and is made up of the anther and the filament.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19. Give one reason why a farmer should practice thinning of his crops. A: To reduce competition for nutrients, water and sunlight so that the remaining crops grow well.. Crowded seedlings compete for food and light; thinning gives each plant enough space to grow healthy.
chunks.source: Crowded seedlings compete for food and light; thinning gives each plant enough space to grow healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 20. Vultures, kites and crows were found feeding on rotting meat. What group of birds are these? A: Birds of prey.. Vultures, kites and crows feed on flesh, so they belong to the group called birds of prey.
chunks.source: Vultures, kites and crows feed on flesh, so they belong to the group called birds of prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21. Give any one special characteristic of the air we breathe in. A: It contains a lot of oxygen.. The air we breathe in is rich in oxygen, which the body needs to release energy from food.
chunks.source: The air we breathe in is rich in oxygen, which the body needs to release energy from food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22. What is the function of synovial fluid in the knee joint? A: It lubricates the joint (reduces friction between the bones).. Synovial fluid is like oil in the joint; it lets the bones move smoothly without rubbing.
chunks.source: Synovial fluid is like oil in the joint; it lets the bones move smoothly without rubbing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23. Give the main cause of fainting. A: Insufficient supply of blood (and oxygen) to the brain.. When the brain does not get enough blood and oxygen, a person faints.
chunks.source: When the brain does not get enough blood and oxygen, a person faints.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 24. Mention one service provided under ante-natal care. A: Immunising mothers against tetanus (any one: examining the mother, giving health education).. During ante-natal care, mothers are examined, immunised and taught how to care for themselves and the baby.
chunks.source: During ante-natal care, mothers are examined, immunised and taught how to care for themselves and the baby.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. Which blood vessel transports digested food from the ileum to the liver? A: Hepatic portal vein.. After absorption in the ileum, digested food is carried to the liver by the hepatic portal vein.
chunks.source: After absorption in the ileum, digested food is carried to the liver by the hepatic portal vein.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26. The diagram below shows a chalk box (5 cm by 4 cm by 6 cm). Find its volume. A: 120 cm3.. Volume = length x width x height = 6 cm x 5 cm x 4 cm = 120 cm3.
chunks.source: Volume = length x width x height = 6 cm x 5 cm x 4 cm = 120 cm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27. Study the animals given in list K (FISH, BIRD, FROG) and those in list M (MAN, WHALE, BAT). How are animals in list K similar to those in list M? A: They are all vertebrates (they all have backbones).. Fish, birds, frogs, man, whales and bats all have backbones, so they are all vertebrates.
chunks.source: Fish, birds, frogs, man, whales and bats all have backbones, so they are all vertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28. What is the source of energy in thermal electricity? A: Heat (from burning fuel such as coal, oil or peat).. Thermal electricity is generated using heat produced by burning fuels.
chunks.source: Thermal electricity is generated using heat produced by burning fuels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29. Why is it a bad practice for people to share a house with domestic animals? A: Animals can spread diseases and parasites to people.. Domestic animals carry germs, ticks and fleas which can easily pass to people sharing the house.
chunks.source: Domestic animals carry germs, ticks and fleas which can easily pass to people sharing the house.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30. State the use of a stretcher when giving First Aid to a victim with a fracture. A: To carry the casualty safely without worsening the fracture.. A stretcher keeps the injured part still while the victim is carried, so the fracture does not get worse.
chunks.source: A stretcher keeps the injured part still while the victim is carried, so the fracture does not get worse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31. How does a vent help to reduce smell in a VIP latrine? A: It lets out the bad smell (gases) from the pit.. The vent pipe carries smelly gases from the pit up into the air, away from the latrine users.
chunks.source: The vent pipe carries smelly gases from the pit up into the air, away from the latrine users.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32. Write down one danger of buying drugs from local shops or markets. A: The drugs may be expired or fake (any one: wrong drug, wrong dosage).. Drugs sold in markets may be expired, fake or wrongly measured, which can harm the patient.
chunks.source: Drugs sold in markets may be expired, fake or wrongly measured, which can harm the patient.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33. Name one material used to guard against electric shock. A: Rubber (any one: plastic, dry wood).. Insulators like rubber and plastic do not conduct electricity, so they protect people from electric shock.
chunks.source: Insulators like rubber and plastic do not conduct electricity, so they protect people from electric shock.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34. Draw prop roots in the space provided below. A: Prop roots grow out from the lower part of the stem and go down into the soil, supporting the plant (as in maize).. Prop roots are extra roots that grow from the stem above the ground to give the plant extra support.
chunks.source: Prop roots are extra roots that grow from the stem above the ground to give the plant extra support.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35. Which body system is commonly affected by polio? A: Nervous system.. Polio attacks the nerves, which is why it can cause paralysis of the limbs.
chunks.source: Polio attacks the nerves, which is why it can cause paralysis of the limbs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 36. State one process by which soil is formed. A: Weathering.. Soil is formed when rocks are broken down into small particles by weathering.
chunks.source: Soil is formed when rocks are broken down into small particles by weathering.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 37. Give one use of an axe at home. A: Splitting firewood (any one: cutting wood).. An axe is used at home mainly for splitting firewood into pieces.
chunks.source: An axe is used at home mainly for splitting firewood into pieces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38. What happens to the blood as it passes through the kidneys? A: Waste products (urea, excess water and salts) are removed from it.. The kidneys filter the blood, removing waste materials which leave the body as urine.
chunks.source: The kidneys filter the blood, removing waste materials which leave the body as urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. Study the diagram of a leaf below. What is part marked B? A: Petiole (leaf stalk).. Part B is the stalk that joins the leaf blade to the stem; it is called the petiole.
chunks.source: Part B is the stalk that joins the leaf blade to the stem; it is called the petiole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. Give one of the functions of the structures marked A on a leaf. A: They allow gaseous exchange (they let in carbon dioxide and release oxygen and water vapour).. The structures marked A are stomata, tiny openings through which gases move in and out of the leaf.
chunks.source: The structures marked A are stomata, tiny openings through which gases move in and out of the leaf.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a) Which bone joins the elbow and shoulder? A: Humerus.. The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm, joining the shoulder to the elbow.
chunks.source: The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm, joining the shoulder to the elbow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(i) Give one example of a voluntary muscle. A: Biceps (any one: triceps, arm or leg muscles).. Voluntary muscles are controlled by our will, for example the biceps we use to lift things.
chunks.source: Voluntary muscles are controlled by our will, for example the biceps we use to lift things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(ii) Give one example of an involuntary muscle. A: Heart (cardiac) muscle (any one: stomach muscles).. Involuntary muscles work without our control, like the heart muscle that beats on its own.
chunks.source: Involuntary muscles work without our control, like the heart muscle that beats on its own.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c) Give one use of muscles in the human body. A: They help the body to move (any one: they give the body shape, they protect body organs).. Muscles pull the bones so that the body can move from place to place.
chunks.source: Muscles pull the bones so that the body can move from place to place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a) Name one vector which spreads dysentery. A: Housefly.. Houseflies carry germs from faeces to food, spreading dysentery.
chunks.source: Houseflies carry germs from faeces to food, spreading dysentery.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) Write down one sign of dysentery. A: Passing out watery stool mixed with blood.. A person with dysentery passes frequent watery stool that contains blood.
chunks.source: A person with dysentery passes frequent watery stool that contains blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c)(i) Give one way of controlling and preventing the spread of dysentery. A: Proper disposal of faeces (using latrines).. Using latrines keeps faeces away from flies, which stops dysentery from spreading.
chunks.source: Using latrines keeps faeces away from flies, which stops dysentery from spreading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c)(ii) Give another way of controlling and preventing the spread of dysentery. A: Washing hands with soap after visiting the latrine and before eating.. Clean hands stop germs from reaching food and the mouth.
chunks.source: Clean hands stop germs from reaching food and the mouth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a) After it has rained, earthworms come out of their holes. Why do they come out? A: Their holes get filled with water, so they come out to breathe.. Earthworms breathe through their moist skin and cannot breathe under water, so they leave flooded holes.
chunks.source: Earthworms breathe through their moist skin and cannot breathe under water, so they leave flooded holes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(i) Give one reason why earthworms are very important in the soil. A: They aerate the soil (they make air spaces as they burrow).. As earthworms burrow, they open up the soil so that air and water can enter easily.
chunks.source: As earthworms burrow, they open up the soil so that air and water can enter easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(ii) Give another reason why earthworms are very important in the soil. A: Their droppings add fertility to the soil (any one: they improve drainage, they mix the soil).. Earthworm droppings are rich in plant nutrients, making the soil fertile.
chunks.source: Earthworm droppings are rich in plant nutrients, making the soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c) Why does an earthworm die if oil is poured on its body? A: Oil blocks the skin through which it breathes, so the earthworm suffocates.. An earthworm breathes through its moist skin; oil covers the skin and stops air from reaching it.
chunks.source: An earthworm breathes through its moist skin; oil covers the skin and stops air from reaching it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44. Match the items in list A with those in list B. List A: Heart, Kidney, Skin, Lung. List B: carbon dioxide, sensory organ, circulation of blood, urine. A: Heart - circulation of blood; Kidney - urine; Skin - sensory organ; Lung - carbon dioxide.. The heart pumps blood round the body, the kidney makes urine, the skin feels things, and the lungs remove carbon dioxide.
chunks.source: The heart pumps blood round the body, the kidney makes urine, the skin feels things, and the lungs remove carbon dioxide.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a) Name one vaccine which is given to the child at birth. A: BCG (any one: polio vaccine).. At birth, babies are given BCG against tuberculosis and polio drops.
chunks.source: At birth, babies are given BCG against tuberculosis and polio drops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b) Why is it important to take children for immunization? A: It protects children against immunisable (killer) diseases.. Immunisation makes the body able to fight diseases like polio, measles and tuberculosis.
chunks.source: Immunisation makes the body able to fight diseases like polio, measles and tuberculosis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c)(i) Give one way in which a child health card is important to the parents. A: It reminds parents of the date of the next immunisation.. The health card shows the immunisation schedule so parents know when to return to the clinic.
chunks.source: The health card shows the immunisation schedule so parents know when to return to the clinic.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c)(ii) Give another way in which a child health card is important to the parents. A: It keeps a record of the child's growth and health (immunisations received).. The card records the child's weight, growth and vaccines given, helping health workers follow the child's health.
chunks.source: The card records the child's weight, growth and vaccines given, helping health workers follow the child's health.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) How can you tell without looking at the roots, that a plant is a legume? A: It bears pods (its fruits are pods containing seeds).. Leguminous plants produce their seeds inside pods, for example beans and peas.
chunks.source: Leguminous plants produce their seeds inside pods, for example beans and peas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b)(i) Give one example of a crop which is a legume. A: Beans (any one: peas, groundnuts, soya beans).. Beans, peas and groundnuts are legumes because their seeds grow in pods.
chunks.source: Beans, peas and groundnuts are legumes because their seeds grow in pods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b)(ii) Give another example of a crop which is a legume. A: Peas (any one: groundnuts, soya beans, beans).. Peas are legumes whose seeds are carried in pods.
chunks.source: Peas are legumes whose seeds are carried in pods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c) How do legumes increase the fertility of the soil? A: They add nitrogen to the soil (nitrogen fixation by bacteria in their root nodules).. Bacteria in the root nodules of legumes change nitrogen from the air into a form plants can use, enriching the soil.
chunks.source: Bacteria in the root nodules of legumes change nitrogen from the air into a form plants can use, enriching the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) In which part of the plant does photosynthesis mainly take place? A: In the leaves.. Leaves have chlorophyll which traps sunlight, so most photosynthesis happens in the leaves.
chunks.source: Leaves have chlorophyll which traps sunlight, so most photosynthesis happens in the leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(i) Name one raw material which enables photosynthesis to take place. A: Carbon dioxide (any one: water).. Green plants use carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil to make food.
chunks.source: Green plants use carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(ii) Name another raw material which enables photosynthesis to take place. A: Water (any one: carbon dioxide).. Water absorbed by the roots is a raw material for making food in the leaves.
chunks.source: Water absorbed by the roots is a raw material for making food in the leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) State one way in which photosynthesis is useful to animals. A: It releases oxygen which animals breathe in (any one: it produces food eaten by animals).. During photosynthesis plants give out oxygen, which animals need for breathing.
chunks.source: During photosynthesis plants give out oxygen, which animals need for breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(i) Use the list (BEANS, RICE, CABBAGE, MILK, ORANGES): give one foodstuff that is a source of proteins. A: Beans (any one: milk).. Beans and milk are body-building foods because they contain proteins.
chunks.source: Beans and milk are body-building foods because they contain proteins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(ii) Give another foodstuff from the list that is a source of proteins. A: Milk (any one: beans).. Milk contains proteins needed for growth and repair of the body.
chunks.source: Milk contains proteins needed for growth and repair of the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b) How are cabbages useful in one's diet? A: They provide vitamins and roughage (they protect the body against diseases).. Cabbages are protective foods that supply vitamins and help digestion through roughage.
chunks.source: Cabbages are protective foods that supply vitamins and help digestion through roughage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c) Why would you regard the list of the foods given above as a balanced diet? A: It contains all classes of food (body-building, energy-giving and protective foods).. The list has proteins (beans, milk), carbohydrates (rice), and vitamins (cabbage, oranges), making a balanced diet.
chunks.source: The list has proteins (beans, milk), carbohydrates (rice), and vitamins (cabbage, oranges), making a balanced diet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a) What do we call a mixture of two or more metals? A: An alloy.. When two or more metals are melted and mixed together, the mixture is called an alloy.
chunks.source: When two or more metals are melted and mixed together, the mixture is called an alloy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) Give one example of a common mixture of metals. A: Brass (any one: bronze, steel).. Brass is an alloy made by mixing copper and zinc.
chunks.source: Brass is an alloy made by mixing copper and zinc.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c) How does heat move from one point to another in a metal? A: By conduction.. In metals, heat travels from the hot end to the cold end by conduction.
chunks.source: In metals, heat travels from the hot end to the cold end by conduction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(d) Apart from painting, give any other method of preventing a metallic object from rusting. A: Oiling (any one: galvanising, greasing).. Oiling keeps water and air away from the metal surface, so rusting does not take place.
chunks.source: Oiling keeps water and air away from the metal surface, so rusting does not take place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a) Use the diagram of the seed below. How is the seed in the diagram dispersed? A: By wind.. The seed has light fluffy hairs that let the wind carry it away from the parent plant.
chunks.source: The seed has light fluffy hairs that let the wind carry it away from the parent plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b) Give a reason to support your answer in question (a) above. A: The seed is light and has hairs (pappus) that help it to float in air.. Wind-dispersed seeds are light with parachute-like hairs so that wind can carry them far.
chunks.source: Wind-dispersed seeds are light with parachute-like hairs so that wind can carry them far.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c)(i) State two advantages of seed dispersal. A: It reduces competition for nutrients, light and water; it enables plants to colonise new areas (any two: it reduces the spread of pests and diseases).. When seeds scatter far, seedlings do not crowd near the parent plant and new areas get covered with plants.
chunks.source: When seeds scatter far, seedlings do not crowd near the parent plant and new areas get covered with plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(i) Give one way in which sound can be stored. A: Recording it on a cassette, CD or flash disk.. Sound can be stored by recording it on devices like cassettes, CDs and memory cards.
chunks.source: Sound can be stored by recording it on devices like cassettes, CDs and memory cards.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(ii) Give another way in which sound can be stored. A: Writing it in staff notation.. Music can be stored on paper using staff notation so that it can be read and played later.
chunks.source: Music can be stored on paper using staff notation so that it can be read and played later.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(i) Identify one way in which stored sound can be useful to people. A: For entertainment (any one: for communication, for education, for advertising).. Stored sound like music entertains people when it is played back.
chunks.source: Stored sound like music entertains people when it is played back.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(ii) Identify another way in which stored sound can be useful to people. A: For communication (any one: for education, for keeping records).. Recorded messages on radio pass information to many people.
chunks.source: Recorded messages on radio pass information to many people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(i) Mention one method of making magnets. A: Stroking (any one: electrical method, induction).. A piece of steel can be made into a magnet by stroking it with another magnet in one direction.
chunks.source: A piece of steel can be made into a magnet by stroking it with another magnet in one direction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(ii) Mention another method of making magnets. A: Electrical method (any one: induction).. Passing electricity through a coil wound round a nail makes the nail a magnet.
chunks.source: Passing electricity through a coil wound round a nail makes the nail a magnet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(i) Suggest one way of destroying a magnet. A: Heating it strongly (any one: hammering it, dropping it many times).. Strong heating makes a magnet lose its magnetism.
chunks.source: Strong heating makes a magnet lose its magnetism.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(ii) Suggest another way of destroying a magnet. A: Hammering it (any one: dropping it repeatedly).. Hammering disturbs the arrangement inside the magnet so it loses magnetism.
chunks.source: Hammering disturbs the arrangement inside the magnet so it loses magnetism.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(i) State one function of blood in the human body. A: It transports oxygen and digested food to body cells.. Blood carries oxygen from the lungs and food from the intestines to all parts of the body.
chunks.source: Blood carries oxygen from the lungs and food from the intestines to all parts of the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(ii) State another function of blood in the human body. A: It carries waste products to the excretory organs.. Blood collects waste like carbon dioxide and urea and takes them to the organs that remove them.
chunks.source: Blood collects waste like carbon dioxide and urea and takes them to the organs that remove them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(iii) State a third function of blood in the human body. A: It distributes heat round the body (any one: white blood cells fight germs, platelets help clotting).. Blood spreads heat so that all parts of the body stay warm.
chunks.source: Blood spreads heat so that all parts of the body stay warm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) How can one increase the volume of blood in the body? A: By eating iron-rich foods (a balanced diet).. Foods rich in iron help the body to make more blood.
chunks.source: Foods rich in iron help the body to make more blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(i) Below is a diagram of a clinical thermometer. Name the part labeled Y. A: Bulb.. Part Y is the bulb at the bottom of the thermometer which holds mercury and is placed against the body.
chunks.source: Part Y is the bulb at the bottom of the thermometer which holds mercury and is placed against the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(ii) Name the part labeled X. A: Constriction (kink).. Part X is the narrow constriction that stops mercury from flowing back so the temperature can be read.
chunks.source: Part X is the narrow constriction that stops mercury from flowing back so the temperature can be read.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b) Identify the importance of part marked X. A: It prevents mercury from flowing back into the bulb so that the temperature can be read.. The constriction breaks the mercury thread, keeping the reading in place after the thermometer is removed.
chunks.source: The constriction breaks the mercury thread, keeping the reading in place after the thermometer is removed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) Apart from the tongue, mention any one part of the human body where the clinical thermometer can be placed when measuring body temperature. A: Armpit.. A clinical thermometer can also be placed in the armpit to measure body temperature.
chunks.source: A clinical thermometer can also be placed in the armpit to measure body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a)(i) The table below shows the classification of animals. Name the group of animals marked S. A: Vertebrates.. Animals are first grouped into vertebrates (with backbones) and invertebrates (without backbones).
chunks.source: Animals are first grouped into vertebrates (with backbones) and invertebrates (without backbones).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a)(ii) Name the group of animals marked K. A: Invertebrates.. Invertebrates are animals without backbones, such as insects, spiders and worms.
chunks.source: Invertebrates are animals without backbones, such as insects, spiders and worms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(i) Give one example of an animal in the group: Molluscs. A: Snail (any one: slug, oyster).. Molluscs are soft-bodied invertebrates; the snail is a common example.
chunks.source: Molluscs are soft-bodied invertebrates; the snail is a common example.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(ii) Give one example of an animal in the group: Arachnids. A: Spider (any one: tick, scorpion).. Arachnids are eight-legged invertebrates such as spiders, ticks and scorpions.
chunks.source: Arachnids are eight-legged invertebrates such as spiders, ticks and scorpions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1. Mention any one component of soil. A: Humus (any one: air, water, mineral salts, living organisms).. Soil is made up of humus, air, water, mineral particles and living organisms.
chunks.source: Soil is made up of humus, air, water, mineral particles and living organisms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2. Mention any one function of the human skin. A: It protects the body against germs and injury (any one: it excretes sweat, it regulates body temperature, it feels touch).. The skin covers the body, keeping germs out and helping to control body temperature.
chunks.source: The skin covers the body, keeping germs out and helping to control body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3. Name one epidemic disease that can break out in your community with poor sanitation. A: Cholera (any one: typhoid, dysentery).. Poor sanitation lets germs spread quickly, causing epidemic diseases like cholera.
chunks.source: Poor sanitation lets germs spread quickly, causing epidemic diseases like cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4. Name the group of tuber crops to which a cocoyam belongs. A: Root tubers.. Cocoyam stores food in its swollen roots, so it belongs to the root tubers.
chunks.source: Cocoyam stores food in its swollen roots, so it belongs to the root tubers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5. State any one use of snakes to man. A: They eat rats and other pests (any one: their venom is used to make medicine, their skins are used).. Snakes control pests by feeding on rats that destroy crops and stored food.
chunks.source: Snakes control pests by feeding on rats that destroy crops and stored food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6. Identify any one part to look at when cleaning your teeth. A: Teeth and gums (any one: the tongue).. When cleaning the mouth, the teeth, gums and tongue should all be cleaned.
chunks.source: When cleaning the mouth, the teeth, gums and tongue should all be cleaned.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7. Name one type of mechanical energy. A: Kinetic energy (any one: potential energy).. Mechanical energy is the energy of movement and position: kinetic and potential energy.
chunks.source: Mechanical energy is the energy of movement and position: kinetic and potential energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8. State the reason why the rate of soil erosion is higher in mountainous areas. A: The slopes are steep, so running water moves fast and carries away soil.. On steep mountain slopes, rain water runs down quickly with force, washing soil away.
chunks.source: On steep mountain slopes, rain water runs down quickly with force, washing soil away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 9. State one reason why it is advisable that children participate in keeping their environment clean. A: It prevents the outbreak of diseases (any one: it teaches them good habits).. When children help to clean, germs and vectors are removed and diseases are prevented.
chunks.source: When children help to clean, germs and vectors are removed and diseases are prevented.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10. Identify the mineral missing in the diet of a child suffering from goitre. A: Iodine.. Goitre is caused by lack of iodine, which is needed by the thyroid gland.
chunks.source: Goitre is caused by lack of iodine, which is needed by the thyroid gland.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11. Name the state of matter in which a material with a ______ volume but no ______ shape belongs. A: Liquid.. Liquids have a fixed volume but take the shape of their container.
chunks.source: Liquids have a fixed volume but take the shape of their container.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12. State the function of the septum in the human heart. A: It separates the left side of the heart from the right side (it prevents oxygenated and deoxygenated blood from mixing).. The septum is a wall in the middle of the heart that keeps clean and dirty blood apart.
chunks.source: The septum is a wall in the middle of the heart that keeps clean and dirty blood apart.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14. Below is a drawing of a garden tool. Name the garden tool. A: Hoe.. The common garden tool used for digging and weeding is the hoe.
chunks.source: The common garden tool used for digging and weeding is the hoe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15. State the function of the garden tool. A: Digging and weeding.. A hoe is used to dig the soil and to remove weeds from the garden.
chunks.source: A hoe is used to dig the soil and to remove weeds from the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. Mention any one condition under which a mother may be stopped from breastfeeding the baby. A: When she is seriously sick (any one: when she has cracked, sore or bleeding nipples).. A mother who is very ill or has injured breasts may be advised to stop breastfeeding for a time.
chunks.source: A mother who is very ill or has injured breasts may be advised to stop breastfeeding for a time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 17. An alcoholic drink is labelled 40%. State what that means. A: It means the drink contains 40% alcohol.. The percentage on the label shows the amount of alcohol in the drink.
chunks.source: The percentage on the label shows the amount of alcohol in the drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18. Below is the structure of the root system in a plant. Name the type of roots in the plant above. A: Fibrous (adventitious) roots.. The roots spread out like fibres from the base of the stem; these are fibrous roots.
chunks.source: The roots spread out like fibres from the base of the stem; these are fibrous roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19. Identify the type of root system in the plant above. A: Fibrous root system.. A mass of thin, spreading roots forms a fibrous root system, common in cereals and grasses.
chunks.source: A mass of thin, spreading roots forms a fibrous root system, common in cereals and grasses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 20. State any one reason why immunization is considered as a Primary Health Care practice. A: It prevents diseases and is affordable and available to everyone.. Primary Health Care brings cheap, simple health services to all people, and immunisation prevents killer diseases.
chunks.source: Primary Health Care brings cheap, simple health services to all people, and immunisation prevents killer diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21. State one reason why physical methods of pest control are preferred to chemical methods. A: Chemicals are poisonous and pollute the environment (any one: chemicals are expensive, chemicals kill useful organisms).. Physical methods do not poison people, animals or the soil, unlike chemical sprays.
chunks.source: Physical methods do not poison people, animals or the soil, unlike chemical sprays.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22. State any one reason why it is advisable for men to be circumcised. A: It reduces the risk of contracting HIV and other sexually transmitted diseases (any one: it improves hygiene).. Circumcision lowers the chances of getting HIV and keeps the private parts clean.
chunks.source: Circumcision lowers the chances of getting HIV and keeps the private parts clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23. Mention any one way in which a health club in schools can reduce the outbreak of diseases in the school. A: By sensitising members on proper sanitation and hygiene.. Health clubs teach pupils to keep clean surroundings, which stops diseases from spreading.
chunks.source: Health clubs teach pupils to keep clean surroundings, which stops diseases from spreading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 24. Name the type of change that takes place when fruits ripen. A: Chemical change.. Ripening forms new substances in the fruit and cannot be reversed, so it is a chemical change.
chunks.source: Ripening forms new substances in the fruit and cannot be reversed, so it is a chemical change.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. State any one importance of bacteria to man. A: They decompose dead organic matter (any one: they help in digestion, they are used to make yoghurt, they fix nitrogen).. Bacteria break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.
chunks.source: Bacteria break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26. State how the hairy body of the ______ is important in spreading diseases. A: Housefly: its hairy body and legs trap germs which it carries to food.. The housefly's hairy body picks up germs from rubbish and faeces and drops them on food.
chunks.source: The housefly's hairy body picks up germs from rubbish and faeces and drops them on food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27. State why in resting an arm using an arm sling, the forearm and upper arm should be rested at 90 degrees. A: To keep the arm comfortable and well supported.. Resting the arm at a right angle in the sling supports the injured part and reduces pain.
chunks.source: Resting the arm at a right angle in the sling supports the injured part and reduces pain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28. Below is an instrument used to measure the temperature of a person (reading 42.0 degrees). Record the temperature of the person. A: 42.0 degrees Celsius.. The thermometer scale shows the person's temperature as 42.0 degrees Celsius.
chunks.source: The thermometer scale shows the person's temperature as 42.0 degrees Celsius.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29. State why the doctor said the person was not normal. A: Normal body temperature is 37 degrees Celsius, so 42.0 degrees shows a very high fever.. A temperature of 42 degrees is far above the normal 37 degrees, meaning the person is seriously ill.
chunks.source: A temperature of 42 degrees is far above the normal 37 degrees, meaning the person is seriously ill.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30. State why it is important to sprinkle water on plant materials when making compost manure. A: To make the materials rot (decompose) faster.. Moisture helps the tiny organisms that break down plant materials to work quickly.
chunks.source: Moisture helps the tiny organisms that break down plant materials to work quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31. State the role of plants in a food chain. A: They are producers (they make food for all other living things).. Plants make their own food by photosynthesis, so every food chain starts with plants.
chunks.source: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis, so every food chain starts with plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32. Name the muscular organ that separates the chest cavity from the abdomen in humans. A: Diaphragm.. The diaphragm is the sheet of muscle below the lungs that separates the chest from the abdomen.
chunks.source: The diaphragm is the sheet of muscle below the lungs that separates the chest from the abdomen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33. Mention any one importance of information gathered through a health survey in a community. A: It helps health workers to plan and solve community health problems.. A health survey shows which diseases are common so that health services can be planned well.
chunks.source: A health survey shows which diseases are common so that health services can be planned well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34. Identify any one human activity that results into ______ of water bodies. A: Dumping waste into water (any one: washing vehicles in the lake, releasing sewage).. Human activities like dumping rubbish pollute water bodies.
chunks.source: Human activities like dumping rubbish pollute water bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35. Name the group of arthropods to which ticks belong. A: Arachnids.. Ticks have eight legs like spiders and scorpions, so they are arachnids.
chunks.source: Ticks have eight legs like spiders and scorpions, so they are arachnids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 36. An organism has the following characteristics: cannot make its own food, reproduces by the use of spores, is made up of many cells. Name the group of living things to which it belongs. A: Fungi.. Fungi cannot make their own food, reproduce by spores and many are made of many cells, like mushrooms.
chunks.source: Fungi cannot make their own food, reproduce by spores and many are made of many cells, like mushrooms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 37. Apart from the magnetic method, mention any one method of storage and reproduction of sound. A: Staff notation (any one: optical recording on CDs).. Besides magnetic tapes, sound can be stored as written music (staff notation) or on compact discs.
chunks.source: Besides magnetic tapes, sound can be stored as written music (staff notation) or on compact discs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38. Name the type of immunity that a baby gets after being immunized. A: Artificial active immunity.. Vaccines make the baby's body produce its own defences, giving artificial active immunity.
chunks.source: Vaccines make the baby's body produce its own defences, giving artificial active immunity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. Name any one vaccine against COVID-19. A: AstraZeneca (any one: Pfizer, Moderna, Johnson and Johnson).. AstraZeneca was one of the vaccines used to protect people against COVID-19.
chunks.source: AstraZeneca was one of the vaccines used to protect people against COVID-19.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. State what you understand by the ______ of a simple machine. A: Efficiency: the comparison of the work a machine does (output) with the work put into it (input).. The efficiency of a machine tells how much of the effort put in is turned into useful work.
chunks.source: The efficiency of a machine tells how much of the effort put in is turned into useful work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a) Mention any two ways of promoting personal hygiene. A: Bathing every day; brushing teeth regularly (any two: washing hands with soap, cutting fingernails short).. Personal hygiene means keeping the body clean through bathing, brushing teeth and washing hands.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene means keeping the body clean through bathing, brushing teeth and washing hands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(i) State the importance of ironing while cleaning clothes. A: It kills germs in clothes (and makes them smart).. The heat of the iron kills germs hiding in clothes and removes wrinkles.
chunks.source: The heat of the iron kills germs hiding in clothes and removes wrinkles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(ii) State the importance of soaking while cleaning clothes. A: It softens and loosens dirt so that clothes become easy to wash.. Soaking in soapy water loosens dirt from the fibres before washing.
chunks.source: Soaking in soapy water loosens dirt from the fibres before washing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c) Identify any one disease that can be spread in a school due to poor cleanliness of beddings. A: Scabies (any one: ringworm).. Dirty beddings spread skin diseases like scabies among pupils.
chunks.source: Dirty beddings spread skin diseases like scabies among pupils.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(i) Mention one function of muscles. A: They help the body to move.. Muscles pull bones so the body can walk, run and lift things.
chunks.source: Muscles pull bones so the body can walk, run and lift things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(ii) Mention another function of muscles. A: They give the body shape (any one: they support the body, they protect internal organs).. Muscles cover the skeleton and give the body its shape.
chunks.source: Muscles cover the skeleton and give the body its shape.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) State what happens to the triceps when the forearm is folded. A: The triceps relaxes.. When the forearm folds, the biceps contracts to pull it up while the triceps relaxes.
chunks.source: When the forearm folds, the biceps contracts to pull it up while the triceps relaxes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) State what happens to the biceps when the forearm is folded. A: The biceps contracts.. The biceps shortens and pulls the forearm up when the arm folds.
chunks.source: The biceps shortens and pulls the forearm up when the arm folds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43. Match the internal organs in A to their functions in B. A: Kidney, Brain, Liver, Lungs. B: exchange of gases, produces bile, produces urine, stores information. A: Kidney - produces urine; Brain - stores information; Liver - produces bile; Lungs - exchange of gases.. The kidney makes urine, the brain stores information, the liver makes bile, and the lungs exchange gases.
chunks.source: The kidney makes urine, the brain stores information, the liver makes bile, and the lungs exchange gases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44. The following are processes that lead to hearing in humans. Arrange them in their correct order: (1) The cochlea changes the vibrations into nervous impulses. (2) The pinna receives sound vibrations and directs them to the eardrum. (3) Vibrations are transmitted through the ear ossicles to the inner ear. (4) Messages are sent through the auditory nerve to the brain for interpretation. A: 2, 3, 1, 4 (pinna receives sound; ossicles transmit vibrations; cochlea changes them to impulses; auditory nerve sends messages to the brain).. Sound is collected by the pinna, passed through the ossicles, changed to impulses in the cochlea, then sent to the brain.
chunks.source: Sound is collected by the pinna, passed through the ossicles, changed to impulses in the cochlea, then sent to the brain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(i) In a slum with poor latrines and polyethene litter, identify one environmental problem that can result. A: Outbreak of diseases (any one: pollution of the environment, poor drainage and flooding).. Poor latrines and littered polyethene bags cause diseases and pollute the slum environment.
chunks.source: Poor latrines and littered polyethene bags cause diseases and pollute the slum environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(ii) Identify another environmental problem that can result from this situation. A: Pollution from polyethene bags (any one: bad smell, blocked drainage).. Littered polyethene bags pollute the area and block water channels.
chunks.source: Littered polyethene bags pollute the area and block water channels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(i) Identify one way in which the people in the area above can control these environmental problems. A: Proper disposal of rubbish.. Collecting and disposing of rubbish properly keeps the environment clean.
chunks.source: Collecting and disposing of rubbish properly keeps the environment clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(ii) Identify another way in which the people in the area above can control these environmental problems. A: Constructing proper pit latrines (any one: digging drainage channels).. Proper latrines stop faeces from polluting the area and spreading diseases.
chunks.source: Proper latrines stop faeces from polluting the area and spreading diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
