chunks.text: Q: 46(a) Name the germ that causes COVID-19. A: Coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2).. COVID-19 is caused by a virus called coronavirus.
chunks.source: COVID-19 is caused by a virus called coronavirus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) Identify any one sign and symptom of COVID-19. A: Fever (any one: dry cough, difficulty in breathing, loss of taste or smell).. People with COVID-19 often develop fever, dry cough and difficulty in breathing.
chunks.source: People with COVID-19 often develop fever, dry cough and difficulty in breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c)(i) Mention one way of controlling the spread of COVID-19 in a school. A: Wearing face masks (any one: washing hands, keeping distance).. Face masks stop the virus from moving between people when they talk or cough.
chunks.source: Face masks stop the virus from moving between people when they talk or cough.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c)(ii) Mention another way of controlling the spread of COVID-19 in a school. A: Washing hands with soap and water (any one: avoiding sharing items, keeping social distance).. Clean hands remove the virus and stop it from entering the body.
chunks.source: Clean hands remove the virus and stop it from entering the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(i) Name the group of worms to which the hookworm belongs. A: Nematodes (roundworms).. Hookworms are round in cross-section, so they belong to the nematodes (roundworms).
chunks.source: Hookworms are round in cross-section, so they belong to the nematodes (roundworms).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(ii) Name the group of worms to which the tapeworm belongs. A: Cestodes (flatworms).. Tapeworms are flat and segmented, belonging to the cestodes (flatworms).
chunks.source: Tapeworms are flat and segmented, belonging to the cestodes (flatworms).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(i) Identify one way of controlling the spread of bilharzia in a community. A: Avoid swimming or wading in infected water.. Bilharzia worms enter the body through the skin in infected water, so people should avoid such water.
chunks.source: Bilharzia worms enter the body through the skin in infected water, so people should avoid such water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(ii) Identify another way of controlling the spread of bilharzia in a community. A: Proper disposal of faeces and urine (any one: killing water snails, drinking boiled water).. Proper sanitation stops bilharzia eggs from reaching water where snails live.
chunks.source: Proper sanitation stops bilharzia eggs from reaching water where snails live.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(i) Mention one practice that can prevent contamination of food in a school. A: Covering food (any one: proper food storage, washing hands before handling food).. Covered food is protected from flies and dust that carry germs.
chunks.source: Covered food is protected from flies and dust that carry germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(ii) Mention another practice that can prevent contamination of food in a school. A: Washing hands before handling food.. Clean hands stop germs from passing to food.
chunks.source: Clean hands stop germs from passing to food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b)(i) Name one disease that can be transmitted through contaminated food. A: Cholera (any one: typhoid, dysentery, food poisoning).. Contaminated food carries germs that cause diseases like cholera and typhoid.
chunks.source: Contaminated food carries germs that cause diseases like cholera and typhoid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b)(ii) Name another disease that can be transmitted through contaminated food. A: Typhoid (any one: dysentery).. Typhoid spreads when people eat food contaminated with faeces.
chunks.source: Typhoid spreads when people eat food contaminated with faeces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(i) Mention one ______ of keeping pigs. A: Intensive system (any one: semi-intensive, free range).. Pigs can be kept under the intensive system, where they are housed and fed, or other systems.
chunks.source: Pigs can be kept under the intensive system, where they are housed and fed, or other systems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(ii) Mention another ______ of keeping pigs. A: Free range system (any one: semi-intensive).. In the free range system, pigs roam and find some of their own food.
chunks.source: In the free range system, pigs roam and find some of their own food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(i) Identify one advantage of keeping pigs over keeping cattle. A: Pigs multiply faster and mature early.. A sow produces many piglets that grow quickly, while cattle take long to mature.
chunks.source: A sow produces many piglets that grow quickly, while cattle take long to mature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(ii) Identify another advantage of keeping pigs over keeping cattle. A: Pigs need less space and less capital to start (any one: pigs eat a variety of feeds).. Pig farming can start in a small space with little money compared to cattle keeping.
chunks.source: Pig farming can start in a small space with little money compared to cattle keeping.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(i) Apart from the free-range system, name one other method of keeping poultry. A: Deep litter system (any one: battery/cage system, fold system).. In the deep litter system, birds are kept inside a house on a thick layer of litter.
chunks.source: In the deep litter system, birds are kept inside a house on a thick layer of litter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(ii) Name another method of keeping poultry apart from the free-range system. A: Battery (cage) system.. In the battery system, birds are kept in individual cages.
chunks.source: In the battery system, birds are kept in individual cages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b) Explain why poultry easily get infected in the free-range system. A: They roam and mix with other birds and animals, picking up germs, worms and parasites.. Free-range birds move everywhere, meeting sick birds and vectors that infect them.
chunks.source: Free-range birds move everywhere, meeting sick birds and vectors that infect them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(i) Mention one method of extracting honey. A: Pressing (any one: centrifuging).. Honey combs can be pressed to squeeze out the honey.
chunks.source: Honey combs can be pressed to squeeze out the honey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(ii) Mention another method of extracting honey. A: Centrifuging.. A centrifuge spins the combs so that honey is thrown out without breaking them.
chunks.source: A centrifuge spins the combs so that honey is thrown out without breaking them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b) State the importance of the queen excluder in a Kenyan Top bar hive. A: It prevents the queen from entering the honey chamber (it keeps brood separate from honey).. The queen excluder stops the queen from laying eggs where honey is stored, keeping honey clean.
chunks.source: The queen excluder stops the queen from laying eggs where honey is stored, keeping honey clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b) State the importance of the top bar in a Kenyan Top bar hive. A: Bees build (attach) their combs on it.. The top bars give bees a place to hang their combs inside the hive.
chunks.source: The top bars give bees a place to hang their combs inside the hive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(i) Name one material that can be used to make compost manure in your community. A: Plant materials/leaves (any one: animal droppings, kitchen remains, ash).. Compost is made by rotting plant and animal materials such as leaves and droppings.
chunks.source: Compost is made by rotting plant and animal materials such as leaves and droppings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(ii) Name another material that can be used to make compost manure in your community. A: Animal droppings (any one: kitchen remains).. Animal waste rots together with plant materials to form rich compost manure.
chunks.source: Animal waste rots together with plant materials to form rich compost manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(i) Identify one advantage of organic manure over inorganic fertilizers. A: It improves soil structure (any one: it is cheap and easily available, it does not pollute the soil).. Organic manure adds humus which makes the soil soft and able to hold water.
chunks.source: Organic manure adds humus which makes the soil soft and able to hold water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(ii) Identify another advantage of organic manure over inorganic fertilizers. A: It releases nutrients slowly and lasts longer in the soil.. Unlike chemical fertilizers that wash away quickly, manure feeds plants over a long time.
chunks.source: Unlike chemical fertilizers that wash away quickly, manure feeds plants over a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a) Name the state of matter in which heat travels fastest by conduction. A: Solids.. Heat moves fastest by conduction in solids because their particles are closely packed.
chunks.source: Heat moves fastest by conduction in solids because their particles are closely packed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a) Name the state of matter in which heat travels fastest by convection. A: Liquids.. Convection currents carry heat through liquids (and gases) as the heated parts rise.
chunks.source: Convection currents carry heat through liquids (and gases) as the heated parts rise.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) Explain the reason why the inner walls of the glass in a vacuum flask are painted silver. A: The silver coating reflects heat back, reducing heat loss by radiation.. Shiny silver walls bounce heat back into the flask so the drink stays hot (or cold).
chunks.source: Shiny silver walls bounce heat back into the flask so the drink stays hot (or cold).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a) A machine lifts a load of 3000 N through a distance of 0.5 m when an effort of 1000 N is applied through a distance of 2 m. Calculate the mechanical advantage of the machine. A: 3.. Mechanical advantage = load / effort = 3000 N / 1000 N = 3.
chunks.source: Mechanical advantage = load / effort = 3000 N / 1000 N = 3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b) Calculate the velocity ratio of the machine. A: 4.. Velocity ratio = effort distance / load distance = 2 m / 0.5 m = 4.
chunks.source: Velocity ratio = effort distance / load distance = 2 m / 0.5 m = 4.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55. Match the plants in A with how they reproduce in B. A: Mango, Fern, Christmas tree, Algae. B: reproduces by fragmentation, produces seeds but without flowers, produces seeds and have flowers, reproduces by the use of spores. A: Mango - produces seeds and have flowers; Fern - reproduces by the use of spores; Christmas tree - produces seeds but without flowers; Algae - reproduces by fragmentation.. Mango is flowering, ferns use spores, Christmas trees are cone-bearing without flowers, and algae break into pieces.
chunks.source: Mango is flowering, ferns use spores, Christmas trees are cone-bearing without flowers, and algae break into pieces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1. Name the body organ commonly affected by scalds. A: Skin.. Scalds burn the skin, which is the organ that covers the body.
chunks.source: Scalds burn the skin, which is the organ that covers the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2. Which component of the environment enables man to produce hydro electricity? A: Water.. Hydro electricity is generated using fast-flowing water turning turbines.
chunks.source: Hydro electricity is generated using fast-flowing water turning turbines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3. Give any one example of a fossil fuel. A: Petroleum (any one: coal, natural gas).. Fossil fuels are formed from decayed organisms long ago; petroleum, coal and natural gas are examples.
chunks.source: Fossil fuels are formed from decayed organisms long ago; petroleum, coal and natural gas are examples.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4. Write any one way a family can care for its member who is HIV positive. A: Feeding them on a balanced diet (any one: showing them love, taking them for treatment).. Family members with HIV need good feeding, love and medical care to stay healthy.
chunks.source: Family members with HIV need good feeding, love and medical care to stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5. Give one way of preventing COVID-19 infections. A: Wearing a face mask (any one: washing hands, keeping social distance).. Face masks stop the virus from spreading between people.
chunks.source: Face masks stop the virus from spreading between people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6. Calculate the voltage of a torch that uses three dry cells. A: 4.5 V.. One dry cell gives 1.5 V, so three cells give 3 x 1.5 V = 4.5 V.
chunks.source: One dry cell gives 1.5 V, so three cells give 3 x 1.5 V = 4.5 V.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7. Write down any one way farmers can prevent and control rats from destroying their crops in the garden. A: Setting traps (any one: keeping cats, using rat guards).. Traps catch rats before they destroy crops in the garden.
chunks.source: Traps catch rats before they destroy crops in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8. State the first aid for a snake bite. A: Keep the casualty calm and rush them to hospital (any one: keep the bitten part still and below the heart).. A snake-bite victim should rest and be taken to hospital quickly for treatment.
chunks.source: A snake-bite victim should rest and be taken to hospital quickly for treatment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 9. Identify the disease vector that spreads nagana to cattle. A: Tsetse fly.. Nagana (trypanosomiasis) in cattle is spread by the bite of tsetse flies.
chunks.source: Nagana (trypanosomiasis) in cattle is spread by the bite of tsetse flies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10. The diagram below shows a second class lever machine (a wheelbarrow). Name the part labeled L. A: Load.. In a wheelbarrow, the load sits between the fulcrum (wheel) and the effort (handles); part L is the load.
chunks.source: In a wheelbarrow, the load sits between the fulcrum (wheel) and the effort (handles); part L is the load.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11. State any one natural method of family planning. A: Abstinence (any one: use of safe days, withdrawal).. Natural family planning uses no drugs or devices, for example abstaining or counting safe days.
chunks.source: Natural family planning uses no drugs or devices, for example abstaining or counting safe days.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12. Give any one advantage of modern bee hives over the traditional one. A: Honey is harvested easily without killing bees (any one: more honey is harvested, the hive is durable).. Modern hives like the top bar hive let farmers remove honey combs without destroying the colony.
chunks.source: Modern hives like the top bar hive let farmers remove honey combs without destroying the colony.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 13. The diagram below shows a magnetic field. Name pole a. A: South pole.. In the magnetic field diagram, pole a is the south pole (unlike poles attract).
chunks.source: In the magnetic field diagram, pole a is the south pole (unlike poles attract).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14. Vulnerable groups of people are those that can easily be harmed. Give one example of such a group of people. A: Children (any one: the elderly, the disabled, pregnant women).. Children, the elderly and the disabled need extra protection because they are easily harmed.
chunks.source: Children, the elderly and the disabled need extra protection because they are easily harmed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15. Write down one use of yeast to people. A: Baking bread (any one: brewing alcohol).. Yeast makes dough rise, so it is used in baking bread.
chunks.source: Yeast makes dough rise, so it is used in baking bread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. The diagram below shows a common latrine in urban schools. Give the use of part Q. A: It stores water used for flushing the latrine.. Part Q is the cistern (tank) which holds water that washes waste into the pit when flushed.
chunks.source: Part Q is the cistern (tank) which holds water that washes waste into the pit when flushed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 17. How are animals used as energy resources in our environment? A: They provide labour (for example, oxen pull ploughs); their dung is used to make biogas.. Animals give energy through the work they do and through biogas from their dung.
chunks.source: Animals give energy through the work they do and through biogas from their dung.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18. Apart from chicken, mention any one other domestic bird. A: Duck (any one: turkey, pigeon, goose).. Ducks, turkeys and pigeons are domestic birds kept like chicken.
chunks.source: Ducks, turkeys and pigeons are domestic birds kept like chicken.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19. Give one example of a long bone in the body. A: Femur (thigh bone) (any one: humerus).. The femur in the thigh is the longest bone in the body.
chunks.source: The femur in the thigh is the longest bone in the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 20. Identify the plant shoot response shown in the diagram below. A: Phototropism.. The shoot bends and grows towards light, which is the response called phototropism.
chunks.source: The shoot bends and grows towards light, which is the response called phototropism.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21. Oral health is the state of being free from any mouth and teeth infection or disorders. Name any one oral disease / infection. A: Tooth decay (any one: dental caries, mouth ulcers).. Tooth decay is a common oral disease caused by germs feeding on food remains in the mouth.
chunks.source: Tooth decay is a common oral disease caused by germs feeding on food remains in the mouth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22. Mention any one material that can be attracted by a magnet. A: Iron (any one: steel, nickel, cobalt).. Magnets attract magnetic materials such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt.
chunks.source: Magnets attract magnetic materials such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23. State any one way food gets contaminated at home. A: Leaving food uncovered (any one: handling food with dirty hands, using dirty utensils).. Uncovered food collects dust and is visited by flies that carry germs.
chunks.source: Uncovered food collects dust and is visited by flies that carry germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 24. Write down any one common sign of pest and disease damage in crops. A: Holes in leaves (any one: wilting, yellow spots, stunted growth).. Pests chew leaves leaving holes, which shows pest damage on crops.
chunks.source: Pests chew leaves leaving holes, which shows pest damage on crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. A towel is one of the materials used in promoting personal hygiene. How is it important? A: It is used for drying the body after bathing.. After bathing, a towel dries the body so that one stays clean and comfortable.
chunks.source: After bathing, a towel dries the body so that one stays clean and comfortable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26. Change 320 F into degrees Celsius. A: 160 degrees Celsius.. C = (F - 32) x 5/9 = (320 - 32) x 5/9 = 288 x 5/9 = 160 degrees Celsius.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27. State any one factor that can increase transpiration in plants. A: High temperature (any one: wind, low humidity, bright light).. Hot, windy and dry conditions make plants lose more water through transpiration.
chunks.source: Hot, windy and dry conditions make plants lose more water through transpiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28. What is leaching? A: It is the washing away of soil nutrients by running water.. When water drains through the soil, it carries dissolved nutrients away; this is leaching.
chunks.source: When water drains through the soil, it carries dissolved nutrients away; this is leaching.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29. Give one use of rocks in our environment. A: Building houses (any one: making roads, making sculptures).. Rocks and stones are used as building materials for houses and roads.
chunks.source: Rocks and stones are used as building materials for houses and roads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30. Which part of a seed produces the stem of a plant? A: Plumule.. During germination, the plumule grows upward and develops into the stem and leaves.
chunks.source: During germination, the plumule grows upward and develops into the stem and leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31. Identify the exotic breed of goats well known for producing large amounts of milk. A: Saanen (any one: Toggenburg, Alpine).. Saanen goats are exotic dairy goats famous for high milk production.
chunks.source: Saanen goats are exotic dairy goats famous for high milk production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32. Write down any one effect of poor feeding to people. A: Malnutrition (any one: stunted growth, deficiency diseases).. Poor feeding leads to malnutrition, where the body lacks the nutrients it needs.
chunks.source: Poor feeding leads to malnutrition, where the body lacks the nutrients it needs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33. State any one importance of air to plants. A: It provides carbon dioxide used in photosynthesis.. Plants take carbon dioxide from the air to make food during photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants take carbon dioxide from the air to make food during photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34. Study the life cycle of the insect below (egg -> r -> t -> adult). Name the stages marked r and t. A: r is the larva; t is the pupa.. In complete metamorphosis, the egg hatches into a larva (r), which then becomes a pupa (t) before the adult appears.
chunks.source: In complete metamorphosis, the egg hatches into a larva (r), which then becomes a pupa (t) before the adult appears.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35. Mention any one insect that undergoes the above life cycle. A: Housefly (any one: butterfly, mosquito, bee).. The housefly goes through egg, larva, pupa and adult stages (complete metamorphosis).
chunks.source: The housefly goes through egg, larva, pupa and adult stages (complete metamorphosis).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 36. Give any one precaution one should consider before taking any drug. A: Read the instructions (any one: take the correct dosage, check the expiry date).. Reading the label helps one take the right drug in the right amount safely.
chunks.source: Reading the label helps one take the right drug in the right amount safely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 37. Write down any one type of soil erosion. A: Sheet erosion (any one: rill, gully, splash erosion).. Sheet erosion washes away a thin uniform layer of topsoil.
chunks.source: Sheet erosion washes away a thin uniform layer of topsoil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38. What is the use of the human eyes when eating food? A: To see (identify) the food.. We use our eyes to see food, which also makes us feel like eating.
chunks.source: We use our eyes to see food, which also makes us feel like eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. Write down any one place where immunization of children can take place. A: Health centre (any one: hospital, school during outreach).. Children are immunised at health centres and hospitals, and sometimes at schools during outreach.
chunks.source: Children are immunised at health centres and hospitals, and sometimes at schools during outreach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. State any one difference between mass and weight. A: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and is constant, while weight is the pull of gravity and changes from place to place.. Mass is measured in kilograms and never changes, but weight in newtons is greater where gravity is stronger.
chunks.source: Mass is measured in kilograms and never changes, but weight in newtons is greater where gravity is stronger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a) Study the diagram of part of a plant below. Name the part marked X. A: Veins (leaf veins).. Part X shows the veins spreading through the leaf blade.
chunks.source: Part X shows the veins spreading through the leaf blade.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a) Name the part marked Y. A: Stalk (petiole).. Part Y is the stalk joining the leaf blade to the stem, called the petiole.
chunks.source: Part Y is the stalk joining the leaf blade to the stem, called the petiole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(i) Give the use of the stalk to the leaf. A: It holds the leaf to the stem (any one: it transports water and food to and from the leaf).. The stalk supports the leaf and carries materials between the leaf and the stem.
chunks.source: The stalk supports the leaf and carries materials between the leaf and the stem.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(ii) Give the use of the veins to the leaf. A: They transport water and manufactured food (any one: they support the leaf blade).. Veins carry water into the leaf and food out of it, and they hold the blade firm.
chunks.source: Veins carry water into the leaf and food out of it, and they hold the blade firm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a) Besides plasma, name one other component of blood. A: Red blood cells (any one: white blood cells, platelets).. Blood is made of plasma plus red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.
chunks.source: Blood is made of plasma plus red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b)(i) Write one material carried by plasma. A: Digested food (any one: water, hormones, urea, heat).. Plasma is the liquid part of blood that carries dissolved food, wastes and heat.
chunks.source: Plasma is the liquid part of blood that carries dissolved food, wastes and heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b)(ii) Write another material carried by plasma. A: Water (any one: hormones, waste products, heat).. Plasma also carries water, hormones and waste materials round the body.
chunks.source: Plasma also carries water, hormones and waste materials round the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c) How are malaria parasites dangerous to the circulatory system? A: They destroy red blood cells, causing anaemia.. Malaria parasites live in and burst red blood cells, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
chunks.source: Malaria parasites live in and burst red blood cells, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(i) Apart from wringing, give one activity involved in cleaning clothes locally. A: Soaking (any one: washing with soap, rinsing, ironing).. Soaking loosens dirt before the actual washing of clothes.
chunks.source: Soaking loosens dirt before the actual washing of clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(ii) Give another activity involved in cleaning clothes locally apart from wringing. A: Washing/rubbing with soap.. Rubbing with soap removes dirt and stains from the clothes.
chunks.source: Rubbing with soap removes dirt and stains from the clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b) Why is it important to wring clothes before spreading them under the sun? A: To remove excess water so that the clothes dry faster.. Wringing squeezes out water, leaving less water to evaporate in the sun.
chunks.source: Wringing squeezes out water, leaving less water to evaporate in the sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c) Write the use of soap when washing clothes. A: It removes dirt and stains from clothes.. Soap dissolves grease and loosens dirt so that it washes away with water.
chunks.source: Soap dissolves grease and loosens dirt so that it washes away with water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a) Study the diagram of part of the human alimentary canal below. Name the part marked with letter T. A: Lacteal.. Part T is the lacteal, the tiny vessel in the middle of the villus that absorbs fats.
chunks.source: Part T is the lacteal, the tiny vessel in the middle of the villus that absorbs fats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b) How is the part marked with letter R adapted to its function of food absorption? A: It has a large surface area, thin walls and a rich supply of blood capillaries.. Part R is a villus; its thin walls, many finger-like projections and dense capillaries let digested food pass into blood quickly.
chunks.source: Part R is a villus; its thin walls, many finger-like projections and dense capillaries let digested food pass into blood quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c)(i) Write down one disorder of the above system. Disorder: A: Constipation (any one: indigestion).. Constipation is a disorder of the alimentary canal where stool becomes hard and difficult to pass.
chunks.source: Constipation is a disorder of the alimentary canal where stool becomes hard and difficult to pass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c)(ii) Write down one disease of the above system. Disease: A: Dysentery (any one: cholera, typhoid).. Dysentery is a disease of the alimentary canal causing bloody diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Dysentery is a disease of the alimentary canal causing bloody diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(i) Identify one material used for harvesting water at home. A: Water tank (any one: jerrycan, drum, gutter).. Rain water from roofs is collected through gutters into tanks and jerrycans.
chunks.source: Rain water from roofs is collected through gutters into tanks and jerrycans.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(ii) Identify another material used for harvesting water at home. A: Jerrycan (any one: drum, gutter).. Jerrycans are used to collect and store harvested rain water at home.
chunks.source: Jerrycans are used to collect and store harvested rain water at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b) Why do people harvest water? A: To have water during the dry season (any one: for domestic use).. Harvested water is stored so that families have water even when it does not rain.
chunks.source: Harvested water is stored so that families have water even when it does not rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c) Name the natural cycle that helps in the production of harvested water. A: Water cycle (rain cycle).. Rain, which people harvest, comes through the water cycle of evaporation and condensation.
chunks.source: Rain, which people harvest, comes through the water cycle of evaporation and condensation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) In one sentence, show the meaning of 'seed dispersal'. A: Seed dispersal is the scattering of seeds away from the parent plant.. Seeds are carried away from the mother plant by wind, water, animals or explosion.
chunks.source: Seeds are carried away from the mother plant by wind, water, animals or explosion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) Give any one advantage of seed dispersal. A: It reduces competition for nutrients, light and water (any one: it enables plants to colonise new areas).. Scattered seeds grow without crowding near the parent plant.
chunks.source: Scattered seeds grow without crowding near the parent plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c)(i) Mention one seed dispersed by animals. A: Mango (any one: guava, orange, pawpaw).. Animals eat fruits like mangoes and drop the seeds far away.
chunks.source: Animals eat fruits like mangoes and drop the seeds far away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c)(ii) Mention another seed dispersed by animals. A: Guava (any one: orange).. Guava seeds pass through animals and grow where they are dropped.
chunks.source: Guava seeds pass through animals and grow where they are dropped.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) Why is there no problem playing with a child who is infected with HIV/AIDS in your community? A: HIV is not spread through casual play or touching.. Playing, touching and sharing toys do not transmit HIV from one child to another.
chunks.source: Playing, touching and sharing toys do not transmit HIV from one child to another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b) How is the engagement and participation in sports activities important in the fight against HIV/AIDS among school children? A: It keeps children occupied and teaches them to avoid risky behaviour.. Sports keep children busy with healthy activities and give chances to teach them about HIV/AIDS.
chunks.source: Sports keep children busy with healthy activities and give chances to teach them about HIV/AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) Name any one harmful traditional practice that may be done to school children in Uganda today. A: Female genital mutilation (any one: early/forced marriage).. Some harmful traditional practices like female genital mutilation and early marriage still affect children.
chunks.source: Some harmful traditional practices like female genital mutilation and early marriage still affect children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(d) Identify any one life skill that may help school children in the fight against HIV/AIDS. A: Assertiveness (any one: good decision-making, self-awareness).. Assertiveness helps children to say no to risky behaviour that spreads HIV.
chunks.source: Assertiveness helps children to say no to risky behaviour that spreads HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(i) Explain in one sentence how electricity can be used to make magnets. A: Passing an electric current through a coil wound round a piece of iron makes it a magnet (electromagnet).. Electricity flowing round an iron core lines up its magnetism, creating an electromagnet.
chunks.source: Electricity flowing round an iron core lines up its magnetism, creating an electromagnet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(ii) Explain in one sentence how magnets can be used to produce electricity. A: Moving a magnet in and out of a coil makes electricity flow in the coil (electromagnetic induction).. A changing magnetic field inside a coil pushes electrons, generating electricity as in generators.
chunks.source: A changing magnetic field inside a coil pushes electrons, generating electricity as in generators.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b)(i) The diagrams below show ways of making temporal magnets. Name method (i). A: Stroking.. One way of making a temporary magnet is stroking a steel bar with a magnet in one direction.
chunks.source: One way of making a temporary magnet is stroking a steel bar with a magnet in one direction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b)(ii) Name method (ii). A: Electrical method.. The second way uses electricity passed through a coil to magnetise the metal.
chunks.source: The second way uses electricity passed through a coil to magnetise the metal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(i) Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther head to the stigma. Apart from bees, mention one other insect that helps in transferring pollen grains. A: Butterfly (any one: moth, beetle, wasp).. Butterflies visit flowers for nectar and carry pollen from flower to flower.
chunks.source: Butterflies visit flowers for nectar and carry pollen from flower to flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(ii) Mention another insect that helps in transferring pollen grains apart from bees. A: Moth (any one: beetle).. Moths also move pollen between flowers as they feed.
chunks.source: Moths also move pollen between flowers as they feed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) What structures on the bee's body enables it to carry pollen grains? A: Pollen baskets (on its hind legs).. Bees pack pollen into special pollen baskets on their hind legs to carry it to the hive.
chunks.source: Bees pack pollen into special pollen baskets on their hind legs to carry it to the hive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c) Mention the product from pollen made by bees. A: Bee bread.. Bees mix pollen with honey to make bee bread, which feeds the young bees.
chunks.source: Bees mix pollen with honey to make bee bread, which feeds the young bees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a) Mention any one method of preserving skins and hides. A: Drying (any one: salting, smoking).. Skins and hides are dried or salted to stop them from rotting before processing.
chunks.source: Skins and hides are dried or salted to stop them from rotting before processing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(i) Write down one item got from processed skins and hides. A: Shoes (any one: bags, belts, jackets, drums).. Leather from processed hides is used to make shoes, bags and belts.
chunks.source: Leather from processed hides is used to make shoes, bags and belts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(ii) Write down another item got from processed skins and hides. A: Bags (any one: belts).. Leather goods like bags and belts come from processed skins and hides.
chunks.source: Leather goods like bags and belts come from processed skins and hides.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c) Give any one cattle parasite that may affect the quality of skins and hides. A: Ticks.. Ticks bite cattle and damage their skins, lowering the quality of hides.
chunks.source: Ticks bite cattle and damage their skins, lowering the quality of hides.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a) Study the diagram of the human skull below. Name the immovable joint at T. A: Suture (fixed/immovable joint).. The bones of the skull are joined by sutures, which are immovable joints.
chunks.source: The bones of the skull are joined by sutures, which are immovable joints.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(i) List down one organ protected by the above part of the skeleton. A: Brain.. The skull is a bony case that protects the delicate brain.
chunks.source: The skull is a bony case that protects the delicate brain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(ii) List down another organ protected by the above part of the skeleton. A: Eyes (any one: ears).. The skull also shields sense organs like the eyes and ears.
chunks.source: The skull also shields sense organs like the eyes and ears.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c) How is the joint marked by letter T different from the joint at S? A: The joint at T is immovable (fixed) while the joint at S is movable.. T is a suture that cannot move, but S is the jaw joint that moves when we talk and chew.
chunks.source: T is a suture that cannot move, but S is the jaw joint that moves when we talk and chew.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52. Match A with B. A: (i) rushing to hospital, (ii) fire, (iii) making an alarm, (iv) applying cold pad. B: causes accidents, management of accidents, giving first aid, calling for help from others. A: (i) rushing to hospital - management of accidents; (ii) fire - causes accidents; (iii) making an alarm - calling for help from others; (iv) applying cold pad - giving first aid.. Fire causes accidents, rushing victims to hospital manages accidents, alarms call for help, and cold pads give first aid.
chunks.source: Fire causes accidents, rushing victims to hospital manages accidents, alarms call for help, and cold pads give first aid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(i) Name one natural change that can displace people in an area. A: Floods (any one: drought, earthquake, landslide, volcanic eruption).. Floods destroy homes and force people to leave their area.
chunks.source: Floods destroy homes and force people to leave their area.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(ii) Name another natural change that can displace people in an area. A: Drought (any one: earthquake).. Long droughts destroy crops and force people to move in search of food and water.
chunks.source: Long droughts destroy crops and force people to move in search of food and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b)(i) State one effect of the natural changes named in (a) above. A: Loss of lives and property.. Natural disasters kill people and destroy houses and property.
chunks.source: Natural disasters kill people and destroy houses and property.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b)(ii) State another effect of the natural changes named in (a) above. A: Famine and homelessness (any one: outbreak of diseases).. After floods or drought, people lack food and shelter and diseases may break out.
chunks.source: After floods or drought, people lack food and shelter and diseases may break out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a) Study the diagrams of houses below. Name the type of house shown in diagram M. A: Permanent house.. House M is built with strong lasting materials, so it is a permanent house.
chunks.source: House M is built with strong lasting materials, so it is a permanent house.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b)(i) Mention one material used to construct house N. A: Grass (any one: mud, poles, banana fibres).. House N is a temporary house built from local materials like grass and mud.
chunks.source: House N is a temporary house built from local materials like grass and mud.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b)(ii) Mention another material used to construct house N. A: Mud (any one: poles).. Mud walls are common in temporary houses.
chunks.source: Mud walls are common in temporary houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) Give any one advantage of house M over house N. A: It is durable / lasts longer (any one: it resists bad weather, it is easy to keep clean).. A permanent house stands for many years while a temporary one needs frequent repair.
chunks.source: A permanent house stands for many years while a temporary one needs frequent repair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a) Name any one exotic breed of rabbits kept in Uganda. A: California white (any one: New Zealand white, Angora).. California white is an exotic rabbit breed kept in Uganda for meat.
chunks.source: California white is an exotic rabbit breed kept in Uganda for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b) Write down any one habit of rabbits you know. A: They burrow (any one: they feed on grass and vegetables).. Rabbits dig burrows in the ground where they live.
chunks.source: Rabbits dig burrows in the ground where they live.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c) Give any one rabbit disease that can attack poultry. A: Coccidiosis.. Coccidiosis attacks both rabbits and poultry, causing bloody diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Coccidiosis attacks both rabbits and poultry, causing bloody diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(d) State any one way in which rabbit farmers can keep their livestock healthy. A: Cleaning their hutches regularly (any one: proper feeding, vaccinating).. Clean hutches keep away germs that make rabbits sick.
chunks.source: Clean hutches keep away germs that make rabbits sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1. State one sign of pest attack on a crop. A: Holes in leaves (any one: wilting, yellow spots, stunted growth).. Pests chew parts of the crop, leaving holes in the leaves.
chunks.source: Pests chew parts of the crop, leaving holes in the leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2. In which state of matter does sound move fastest? A: Solids.. Sound travels fastest through solids because their particles are closely packed.
chunks.source: Sound travels fastest through solids because their particles are closely packed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3. Name the type of chicken kept for production of meat. A: Broilers.. Broilers are chickens specially kept for meat production.
chunks.source: Broilers are chickens specially kept for meat production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4. What role does the fuse play in an electric circuit? A: It protects appliances by breaking the circuit when too much current flows.. The fuse wire melts when current is too high, stopping the flow and saving appliances.
chunks.source: The fuse wire melts when current is too high, stopping the flow and saving appliances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5. State one way transpiration benefits a plant. A: It cools the plant (any one: it helps in the absorption of water and mineral salts).. As water evaporates from leaves, the plant cools down and more water is pulled up from the roots.
chunks.source: As water evaporates from leaves, the plant cools down and more water is pulled up from the roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6. The diagram below shows a property of magnets. State the property of magnets shown above. A: Like poles repel each other while unlike poles attract each other.. When two magnets face each other, same poles push apart and different poles pull together.
chunks.source: When two magnets face each other, same poles push apart and different poles pull together.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7. Give one activity done at school to promote sanitation. A: Sweeping the compound (any one: slashing, general cleaning, health parades).. Regular cleaning activities like sweeping keep the school free from germs.
chunks.source: Regular cleaning activities like sweeping keep the school free from germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8. State one way a cobweb is important to a spider. A: It traps insects for food.. The spider's web catches flying insects which the spider eats.
chunks.source: The spider's web catches flying insects which the spider eats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 9. In which way can man make good use of wax got from bees? A: Making candles (any one: making polish).. Beeswax is used to make candles and shoe polish.
chunks.source: Beeswax is used to make candles and shoe polish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10. Why do many crop farmers prefer growing annual crops to perennial crops? A: They mature and are harvested in a short time.. Annual crops complete their life in one season, giving farmers a quick harvest.
chunks.source: Annual crops complete their life in one season, giving farmers a quick harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11. How are valves important in the heart? A: They prevent the backflow of blood.. Valves in the heart allow blood to flow in one direction only.
chunks.source: Valves in the heart allow blood to flow in one direction only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12. Name the immunisable disease that causes stiffness of muscles. A: Tetanus.. Tetanus makes the muscles, especially of the jaw, become stiff.
chunks.source: Tetanus makes the muscles, especially of the jaw, become stiff.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 13. Why is evening the best time for transplanting seedlings? A: It is cool, so seedlings lose less water and establish well overnight.. Evening coolness reduces wilting and gives seedlings the night to recover.
chunks.source: Evening coolness reduces wilting and gives seedlings the night to recover.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14. Why is it not necessary to smoke a VIP latrine? A: The vent pipe removes the bad smell.. A VIP latrine has a vent that carries away smells, so smoking is not needed.
chunks.source: A VIP latrine has a vent that carries away smells, so smoking is not needed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15. How is the windsock at an airport important to a pilot? A: It shows the direction (and strength) of wind.. Pilots look at the windsock to know which way the wind blows before landing or taking off.
chunks.source: Pilots look at the windsock to know which way the wind blows before landing or taking off.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. Give a reason why the salivary amylase cannot continue digesting cooked starch even in the stomach. A: The acidic conditions in the stomach destroy it.. Salivary amylase works in the mouth, but stomach acid kills it so it stops working.
chunks.source: Salivary amylase works in the mouth, but stomach acid kills it so it stops working.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 17. State one way we can care for AIDS victims in our homes. A: Feeding them well on a balanced diet (any one: showing them love and care, counselling them).. AIDS victims need good nutrition, love and medical care to live longer.
chunks.source: AIDS victims need good nutrition, love and medical care to live longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18. The diagram below shows a movable joint. Name the type of movable joint shown above. A: Hinge joint.. The diagram shows a joint that moves in one direction like a door hinge, for example the knee.
chunks.source: The diagram shows a joint that moves in one direction like a door hinge, for example the knee.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19. State one way part marked P is important at a joint. A: It reduces friction between the bones (it allows smooth movement).. Part P (cartilage/synovial fluid) cushions the bones so they move smoothly without rubbing.
chunks.source: Part P (cartilage/synovial fluid) cushions the bones so they move smoothly without rubbing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 20. Apart from destroying crops, give any other effect of too much rain in the environment. A: It causes floods (any one: it causes soil erosion, it causes leaching).. Too much rain fills rivers and low areas, causing floods that destroy property.
chunks.source: Too much rain fills rivers and low areas, causing floods that destroy property.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21. State one way diarrhoeal diseases can be controlled in our communities. A: Drinking boiled water (any one: proper use of latrines, washing hands).. Boiling water kills the germs that cause diarrhoeal diseases.
chunks.source: Boiling water kills the germs that cause diarrhoeal diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22. Give one effect of alcoholism to the community. A: It leads to violence and poverty (any one: accidents, broken families).. Alcoholism causes fights, poverty and accidents in the community.
chunks.source: Alcoholism causes fights, poverty and accidents in the community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23. When making charcoal, why is the piled wood covered with soil? A: To limit air (oxygen) so that the wood does not burn completely into ash.. With little air, the wood chars slowly into charcoal instead of burning into ashes.
chunks.source: With little air, the wood chars slowly into charcoal instead of burning into ashes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 24. Why is it necessary to feed a malaria patient with green leafy vegetables? A: They are rich in iron, which helps to replace the blood destroyed by malaria.. Malaria destroys red blood cells, and iron from green vegetables helps the body make new blood.
chunks.source: Malaria destroys red blood cells, and iron from green vegetables helps the body make new blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. How does bush burning cause soil erosion? A: It destroys plant cover, leaving the soil bare and exposed to wind and running water.. Without plants to hold it, bare soil is easily carried away by wind and rain.
chunks.source: Without plants to hold it, bare soil is easily carried away by wind and rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26. Write down one characteristic of animal dispersed seeds. A: They have hooks that stick on animals (any one: they are fleshy and attractive, they have a sweet smell).. Some seeds have hooks that cling to animal fur so they are carried far.
chunks.source: Some seeds have hooks that cling to animal fur so they are carried far.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27. Draw a converging beam in the space below. A: Light rays drawn as straight lines meeting at one point (the focus).. A converging beam is a set of light rays that come together and meet at a point.
chunks.source: A converging beam is a set of light rays that come together and meet at a point.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28. State one reason why distilled water is not suitable for drinking. A: It lacks mineral salts needed by the body.. Distilled water has no dissolved minerals, so it does not supply the body's needs.
chunks.source: Distilled water has no dissolved minerals, so it does not supply the body's needs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29. Mention any one cause of improper growth of teeth. A: Lack of calcium in the diet (any one: poor feeding).. Teeth need calcium to grow strong; without it they grow poorly.
chunks.source: Teeth need calcium to grow strong; without it they grow poorly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30. Give a reason why water is added to the pit when making compost manure. A: To help the materials decompose (rot) faster.. Moisture helps the organisms that break down the materials to work quickly.
chunks.source: Moisture helps the organisms that break down the materials to work quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31. The diagram below shows an iron box. Why is part marked T made out of wood? A: Wood is a poor conductor of heat, so the handle stays cool.. The handle of a charcoal iron is made of wood because wood does not conduct heat to the hand.
chunks.source: The handle of a charcoal iron is made of wood because wood does not conduct heat to the hand.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32. How is the use of holes marked P different from that of holes marked W? A: Holes P let in fresh air to keep the charcoal burning, while holes W let out smoke.. Air enters through P to feed the fire, and smoke escapes through W.
chunks.source: Air enters through P to feed the fire, and smoke escapes through W.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33. Give the main reason why farmers pollard fruit trees. A: To encourage the growth of many branches (for firewood and easy harvesting).. Cutting back the top makes the tree grow many new branches.
chunks.source: Cutting back the top makes the tree grow many new branches.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34. Why is the use of biogas taken to be environmental friendly? A: It does not pollute the environment (it burns cleanly).. Biogas burns with a clean flame and uses animal waste, so it keeps the environment clean.
chunks.source: Biogas burns with a clean flame and uses animal waste, so it keeps the environment clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35. Give one way living things depend on non-living things. A: Plants need water, air and sunlight to make food.. Living things need non-living things like water, air and sunlight to survive.
chunks.source: Living things need non-living things like water, air and sunlight to survive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 36. Apart from dry lips, state any one other sign of dehydration in children. A: Sunken eyes (any one: dry skin, passing little urine).. A dehydrated child has sunken eyes and dry skin.
chunks.source: A dehydrated child has sunken eyes and dry skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 37. Why is dew formed at night? A: The air cools at night and water vapour condenses into droplets.. At night temperatures fall, so water vapour in the air turns into tiny dew drops on cool surfaces.
chunks.source: At night temperatures fall, so water vapour in the air turns into tiny dew drops on cool surfaces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38. State one problem faced by people who rear goats. A: Diseases and parasites (any one: theft, predators).. Goats suffer from diseases and worms, and they may be stolen.
chunks.source: Goats suffer from diseases and worms, and they may be stolen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. What role does oxygen play during respiration? A: It helps to break down food to release energy.. Oxygen burns digested food in the body cells, releasing energy.
chunks.source: Oxygen burns digested food in the body cells, releasing energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. Give one reason why some mothers bottle feed their babies instead of breast feeding. A: The mother may not produce enough milk (any one: the mother is sick or away at work).. Some mothers cannot breastfeed because of illness, work or low milk, so they use bottles.
chunks.source: Some mothers cannot breastfeed because of illness, work or low milk, so they use bottles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(i) State one sign of heat period in cattle. A: Mounting other cattle (any one: restlessness, bellowing, mucus discharge, loss of appetite).. A cow on heat mounts others and becomes restless, showing she is ready for mating.
chunks.source: A cow on heat mounts others and becomes restless, showing she is ready for mating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(ii) State another sign of heat period in cattle. A: Restlessness and bellowing.. Cows on heat move about restlessly and moo loudly.
chunks.source: Cows on heat move about restlessly and moo loudly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) What advice would you give to a farmer whose cow is on heat? A: Take the cow for mating (or call a veterinary doctor for artificial insemination).. A cow on heat should be served by a bull or inseminated so that she can conceive.
chunks.source: A cow on heat should be served by a bull or inseminated so that she can conceive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c) Give one reason why cattle keepers are advised to graze cows and bulls separately. A: To control breeding (to prevent unwanted mating).. Keeping bulls away from cows stops unplanned pregnancies and inbreeding.
chunks.source: Keeping bulls away from cows stops unplanned pregnancies and inbreeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(i) Write down one condition necessary for photosynthesis to take place. A: Sunlight (any one: chlorophyll, carbon dioxide, water).. Plants need sunlight energy to make food during photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants need sunlight energy to make food during photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(ii) Write down another condition necessary for photosynthesis to take place. A: Chlorophyll (any one: carbon dioxide).. Chlorophyll traps sunlight for the plant to use in making food.
chunks.source: Chlorophyll traps sunlight for the plant to use in making food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) Why can't photosynthesis take place at night? A: There is no sunlight at night.. Photosynthesis needs light energy, which is absent at night.
chunks.source: Photosynthesis needs light energy, which is absent at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c) In which way does photosynthesis benefit the environment? A: It releases oxygen and absorbs carbon dioxide, purifying the air.. Plants clean the air by taking in carbon dioxide and giving out oxygen.
chunks.source: Plants clean the air by taking in carbon dioxide and giving out oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a) The diagram below shows a kidney. Name part marked T. A: Ureter.. Part T is the tube that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder, called the ureter.
chunks.source: Part T is the tube that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder, called the ureter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b) How is part marked X important in the kidney? A: It carries blood into the kidney for filtration.. Part X (the renal artery) brings blood with waste products into the kidney to be cleaned.
chunks.source: Part X (the renal artery) brings blood with waste products into the kidney to be cleaned.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c) State one substance that gets reabsorbed into the body in part marked Y. A: Water (any one: glucose, mineral salts).. As urine flows through the tubules, useful substances like water and glucose are taken back into the blood.
chunks.source: As urine flows through the tubules, useful substances like water and glucose are taken back into the blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(d) Apart from excretion mention any other use of the kidney in the body. A: It regulates the amount of water and salts in the body (osmoregulation).. Besides removing waste, the kidney balances water and salts in the body.
chunks.source: Besides removing waste, the kidney balances water and salts in the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a) Give one reason why many poultry farmers in Uganda today prefer keeping exotic breeds of poultry. A: They grow fast and lay many eggs.. Exotic birds mature quickly and are more productive than local birds.
chunks.source: Exotic birds mature quickly and are more productive than local birds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b) State one problem faced by poultry farmers in Uganda. A: Outbreak of diseases (any one: expensive feeds, lack of market).. Diseases can kill many birds and cause big losses to poultry farmers.
chunks.source: Diseases can kill many birds and cause big losses to poultry farmers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c) Name the poultry disease that can be identified by blood stained diarrhoea and ruffled feathers. A: Coccidiosis.. Coccidiosis in poultry shows bloody diarrhoea and ruffled feathers.
chunks.source: Coccidiosis in poultry shows bloody diarrhoea and ruffled feathers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(d) Mention one way poultry diseases can be controlled. A: Vaccinating the birds (any one: proper hygiene, isolating sick birds).. Vaccination protects birds against killer poultry diseases.
chunks.source: Vaccination protects birds against killer poultry diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(i) State one way food can get contaminated. A: Leaving food uncovered (any one: handling food with dirty hands, using dirty utensils).. Uncovered food collects germs from flies and dust.
chunks.source: Uncovered food collects germs from flies and dust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(ii) State another way food can get contaminated. A: Handling food with dirty hands.. Dirty hands pass germs directly to food.
chunks.source: Dirty hands pass germs directly to food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b) Mention one disease a person can get if he eats contaminated food. A: Cholera (any one: typhoid, dysentery).. Contaminated food carries germs that cause cholera, typhoid and dysentery.
chunks.source: Contaminated food carries germs that cause cholera, typhoid and dysentery.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c) Give one reason why we need to cover food when cooking it. A: To prevent it from getting contaminated (and to cook faster).. Covering food keeps dirt out and keeps heat in so it cooks quickly.
chunks.source: Covering food keeps dirt out and keeps heat in so it cooks quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) The diagram below shows a doctor's prescription. How many tablets should the patient take in a day? A: 6 tablets (2 tablets three times a day).. The prescription directs the patient to take 2 tablets three times daily, which is 6 tablets a day.
chunks.source: The prescription directs the patient to take 2 tablets three times daily, which is 6 tablets a day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) Write down any one condition under which drugs should be stored. A: In a cool, dry place (any one: away from children).. Drugs kept in a cool dry place away from children remain safe and effective.
chunks.source: Drugs kept in a cool dry place away from children remain safe and effective.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c) Give one reason why drugs should be labeled. A: To show how they should be used (dosage) and their expiry date.. Labels tell the patient the correct dose and when the drug expires.
chunks.source: Labels tell the patient the correct dose and when the drug expires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(d) Apart from age and weight, give any other factor medical workers consider before prescribing a drug. A: The type of sickness (any one: the patient's medical history, allergies).. The doctor must know the disease and the patient's history before choosing a drug.
chunks.source: The doctor must know the disease and the patient's history before choosing a drug.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(i) Mention one cause of a short circuit in electricity. A: Naked wires touching each other (any one: overloading, faulty appliances).. When bare wires touch, current takes a shortcut, causing a short circuit.
chunks.source: When bare wires touch, current takes a shortcut, causing a short circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(ii) Mention another cause of a short circuit in electricity. A: Overloading the circuit.. Too many appliances on one circuit can cause a short circuit.
chunks.source: Too many appliances on one circuit can cause a short circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b) Write down one danger that can be brought by a short circuit. A: It can cause fire (any one: it destroys appliances, it causes electric shock).. Short circuits produce heat that can start fires and burn appliances.
chunks.source: Short circuits produce heat that can start fires and burn appliances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) In which way do people who install electricity guard against electric shocks? A: By using insulated wires and proper earthing.. Insulation and earthing stop electricity from reaching people.
chunks.source: Insulation and earthing stop electricity from reaching people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a) Give the main reason why our bodies carry out respiration. A: To release energy from food.. Respiration breaks down food in body cells to set free energy for work.
chunks.source: Respiration breaks down food in body cells to set free energy for work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b) Where does respiration take place in the body? A: In the body cells.. Food is broken down to release energy inside every living body cell.
chunks.source: Food is broken down to release energy inside every living body cell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c) What role does oxygen play during respiration? A: It helps to break down food to release energy.. Oxygen burns digested food in the cells, setting energy free.
chunks.source: Oxygen burns digested food in the cells, setting energy free.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(d) How does respiration affect the environment negatively? A: It releases carbon dioxide into the air.. Breathing out adds carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas, to the atmosphere.
chunks.source: Breathing out adds carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas, to the atmosphere.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a) What is thinning? A: The removal of excess seedlings from a nursery or garden bed.. Thinning means pulling out extra young plants so the rest have enough space.
chunks.source: Thinning means pulling out extra young plants so the rest have enough space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(i) Give one reason why farmers thin their crops. A: To reduce competition for nutrients, water and sunlight.. Thinning gives each plant enough space, food and light to grow well.
chunks.source: Thinning gives each plant enough space, food and light to grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(ii) Give another reason why farmers thin their crops. A: So that the remaining crops grow healthy and give a good harvest.. Well-spaced crops grow bigger and yield more.
chunks.source: Well-spaced crops grow bigger and yield more.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c) State one way farmers can make good use of thinned crops. A: They can be used as vegetables or animal feed (any one: they can be transplanted).. Thinned seedlings need not be wasted; they can feed animals or people.
chunks.source: Thinned seedlings need not be wasted; they can feed animals or people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a) The diagram below shows an experiment carried out in a science lesson. Name container marked W. A: Measuring cylinder.. Container W is a measuring cylinder used to measure the volume of water displaced by the stone.
chunks.source: Container W is a measuring cylinder used to measure the volume of water displaced by the stone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b) What was the experiment about? A: Finding the volume of a stone (an irregular object) by displacement.. The stone was lowered into water and the rise in water level showed its volume.
chunks.source: The stone was lowered into water and the rise in water level showed its volume.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c) Why did the teacher decide to use such a method? A: Because the stone has an irregular shape (it cannot be measured with a ruler).. Irregular objects have no simple length, width and height, so displacement is used.
chunks.source: Irregular objects have no simple length, width and height, so displacement is used.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(d) State the volume of the stone. A: The difference between the two water levels (final reading minus initial reading).. The volume of the stone equals the volume of water it displaces, read from the rise in level.
chunks.source: The volume of the stone equals the volume of water it displaces, read from the rise in level.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(i) Give one reason why we need to keep our bodies clean. A: To prevent diseases.. A clean body keeps away germs that cause diseases.
chunks.source: A clean body keeps away germs that cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(ii) Give another reason why we need to keep our bodies clean. A: To remove bad smell (any one: to look smart).. Bathing removes sweat and dirt that cause bad body smell.
chunks.source: Bathing removes sweat and dirt that cause bad body smell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b) How does the washing of clothes keep them clean? A: It removes dirt and germs from them.. Washing with soap and water takes dirt and germs out of clothes.
chunks.source: Washing with soap and water takes dirt and germs out of clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c) Mention one place where cleaned clothes can be kept. A: In a wardrobe (any one: drawer, suitcase).. Clean clothes are kept in wardrobes or drawers to stay clean.
chunks.source: Clean clothes are kept in wardrobes or drawers to stay clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a) The diagram below shows a type of pulley. Name the type of pulley. A: Single fixed pulley.. The diagram shows a pulley fixed in one position, which changes the direction of effort.
chunks.source: The diagram shows a pulley fixed in one position, which changes the direction of effort.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b) Through what distance did the effort move by the time the load reached point B? A: The same distance as the load moved (in a single fixed pulley, effort distance equals load distance).. With a fixed pulley, the rope moves equally on both sides, so effort and load cover the same distance.
chunks.source: With a fixed pulley, the rope moves equally on both sides, so effort and load cover the same distance.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(c) State one advantage of using such pulley. A: It changes the direction of effort, making work easier.. A fixed pulley lets one pull down to lift a load up, which is easier.
chunks.source: A fixed pulley lets one pull down to lift a load up, which is easier.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(d) Give one use of such a pulley in our daily life. A: Drawing water from a well (any one: raising a flag).. Fixed pulleys are used on wells to lift water and on flag poles.
chunks.source: Fixed pulleys are used on wells to lift water and on flag poles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a) Why is a frog able to live in water? A: It breathes through its moist skin (any one: it has webbed feet for swimming).. A frog can absorb oxygen from water through its moist skin.
chunks.source: A frog can absorb oxygen from water through its moist skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) Mention one way a frog is different from a toad. A: A frog has smooth, moist skin while a toad has rough, dry, warty skin.. Frogs live mostly in water but toads live mostly on land, and their skins differ.
chunks.source: Frogs live mostly in water but toads live mostly on land, and their skins differ.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c) Write down one characteristic of amphibians. A: They live part of their life in water and part on land (any one: they lay their eggs in water).. Amphibians like frogs start life in water and later live on land.
chunks.source: Amphibians like frogs start life in water and later live on land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(d) Toads spend most of their adult time on land. Why do they go in water? A: To lay their eggs (to breed).. Toads return to water to lay eggs, since their young develop in water.
chunks.source: Toads return to water to lay eggs, since their young develop in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a) Mention one place in a home where near drowning can take place. A: In a well (any one: swimming pool, water tank).. Open wells and pools at home are places where children can drown.
chunks.source: Open wells and pools at home are places where children can drown.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b) During first aid for near drowning, why is it necessary to press the chest hard? A: To force water out of the lungs (and help the victim to breathe).. Pressing the chest pushes swallowed water out so that air can enter the lungs.
chunks.source: Pressing the chest pushes swallowed water out so that air can enter the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) How can a young boy help a person who is near-drowning? A: By throwing them a rope or float (without jumping into the water).. A boy should extend a stick or throw something that floats, and call for help.
chunks.source: A boy should extend a stick or throw something that floats, and call for help.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(d) State one way of preventing near-drowning at home. A: Covering open wells (any one: fencing the pool, supervising children near water).. Covered wells and fenced pools keep children from falling into water.
chunks.source: Covered wells and fenced pools keep children from falling into water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a) How are the health parades important in a school? A: They help to check pupils' personal hygiene.. During health parades, teachers inspect cleanliness of pupils, encouraging good hygiene.
chunks.source: During health parades, teachers inspect cleanliness of pupils, encouraging good hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b) Write down one role of a health prefect in a school. A: Ensures the school compound is clean (any one: organises cleaning).. The health prefect leads pupils in keeping the school clean.
chunks.source: The health prefect leads pupils in keeping the school clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c) Apart from the sanitary prefect, mention any one other member of a school health committee. A: The headteacher (any one: class teacher, school nurse).. The school health committee includes teachers and the headteacher besides the sanitary prefect.
chunks.source: The school health committee includes teachers and the headteacher besides the sanitary prefect.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(d) Give one way we can care for the people with special needs in a community. A: By helping them with their needs (showing them love and care).. People with special needs should be assisted and treated with kindness.
chunks.source: People with special needs should be assisted and treated with kindness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1. Why does a bedbug produce a very bad smell when it is touched? A: To scare away its enemies (for defence).. A bedbug releases a bad smell as a defence to frighten away animals that touch it.
chunks.source: A bedbug releases a bad smell as a defence to frighten away animals that touch it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2. Give any one way in which flowers are important to a plant. A: They help the plant to reproduce (they develop into seeds and fruits).. Flowers are the reproductive parts of a plant; after pollination they form seeds and fruits.
chunks.source: Flowers are the reproductive parts of a plant; after pollination they form seeds and fruits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3. Which deficiency disease in children has these signs and symptoms: swollen moon face, brownish hair and pot belly? A: Kwashiorkor.. Kwashiorkor is caused by lack of proteins in the diet and shows a swollen face, brownish hair and a pot belly.
chunks.source: Kwashiorkor is caused by lack of proteins in the diet and shows a swollen face, brownish hair and a pot belly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4. Write one common characteristic which is common in all arachnids. A: They have four pairs of walking legs (eight legs).. All arachnids such as spiders, ticks and scorpions have eight legs and their bodies are divided into two parts.
chunks.source: All arachnids such as spiders, ticks and scorpions have eight legs and their bodies are divided into two parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5. Why does sugar disappear when it is mixed in water? A: Sugar dissolves in water.. When sugar is mixed with water it dissolves, forming a solution, so it seems to disappear.
chunks.source: When sugar is mixed with water it dissolves, forming a solution, so it seems to disappear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6. Which property of air is demonstrated when air is pumped into a ball and it becomes bigger? A: Air occupies space.. The ball becomes bigger because the air pumped into it takes up space inside the ball.
chunks.source: The ball becomes bigger because the air pumped into it takes up space inside the ball.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7. How is the absence of vitamin D harmful to our health? A: It causes rickets (weak, soft bones).. Vitamin D helps the body to use calcium for strong bones; without it children develop rickets.
chunks.source: Vitamin D helps the body to use calcium for strong bones; without it children develop rickets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8. What is the importance of blood platelets in the body? A: They help blood to clot (stop bleeding).. When you are cut, platelets gather at the wound and make the blood clot so that bleeding stops.
chunks.source: When you are cut, platelets gather at the wound and make the blood clot so that bleeding stops.

chunks.subject: Science
