chunks.text: Q: 9. Give one reason why a farmer should keep records of daily weather. A: To plan farming activities (for example, to know when to plant crops).. Weather records help a farmer decide the best time for planting, weeding and harvesting.
chunks.source: Weather records help a farmer decide the best time for planting, weeding and harvesting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10. Why is proper disposal of wastes important in a home? A: It prevents the spread of diseases.. Wastes left anyhow breed germs and vectors, so proper disposal keeps the home free from diseases.
chunks.source: Wastes left anyhow breed germs and vectors, so proper disposal keeps the home free from diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11. Which of the following animals: fish, frog, lizard, rat and a snail is warm blooded? A: Rat.. A rat is a mammal, and mammals are warm blooded; the other animals are cold blooded.
chunks.source: A rat is a mammal, and mammals are warm blooded; the other animals are cold blooded.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12. In the space provided below, draw a symbol of a switch. A: A switch symbol: a break in a straight wire with a short slanting line (lever) bridging the gap.. The switch symbol shows a wire with a small gap and a lever that can close the gap to complete the circuit.
chunks.source: The switch symbol shows a wire with a small gap and a lever that can close the gap to complete the circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 13. What type of energy is possessed by a stone resting on the table? A: Potential energy.. A stone resting above the ground has stored energy because of its position; this is potential energy.
chunks.source: A stone resting above the ground has stored energy because of its position; this is potential energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14. When water is heated it changes into steam. What is this process called? A: Evaporation.. Heating water changes it from liquid to gas (steam); this change of state is called evaporation.
chunks.source: Heating water changes it from liquid to gas (steam); this change of state is called evaporation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15. Name any one example of a perennial crop. A: Mango (any one: coffee, banana, avocado, orange).. Perennial crops live for many years; mango, coffee and banana are common examples.
chunks.source: Perennial crops live for many years; mango, coffee and banana are common examples.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. How does paddock system of grazing cattle control the spread of tick borne diseases? A: It breaks the life cycle of ticks (ticks starve and die while a paddock rests without cattle).. Moving cattle from paddock to paddock leaves ticks without animals to feed on, so the ticks die.
chunks.source: Moving cattle from paddock to paddock leaves ticks without animals to feed on, so the ticks die.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 17. Give any one reason why we should wring clothes before drying them. A: To remove excess water so that the clothes dry faster.. Wringing squeezes out most of the water, leaving less water to evaporate in the sun.
chunks.source: Wringing squeezes out most of the water, leaving less water to evaporate in the sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18. Write down any one part which makes the stamen on a flower. A: Anther (any one: filament).. The stamen is the male part of a flower and is made up of the anther and the filament.
chunks.source: The stamen is the male part of a flower and is made up of the anther and the filament.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19. Give one reason why a farmer should practice thinning of his crops. A: To reduce competition for nutrients, water and sunlight so that the remaining crops grow well.. Crowded seedlings compete for food and light; thinning gives each plant enough space to grow healthy.
chunks.source: Crowded seedlings compete for food and light; thinning gives each plant enough space to grow healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 20. Vultures, kites and crows were found feeding on rotting meat. What group of birds are these? A: Birds of prey.. Vultures, kites and crows feed on flesh, so they belong to the group called birds of prey.
chunks.source: Vultures, kites and crows feed on flesh, so they belong to the group called birds of prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21. Give any one special characteristic of the air we breathe in. A: It contains a lot of oxygen.. The air we breathe in is rich in oxygen, which the body needs to release energy from food.
chunks.source: The air we breathe in is rich in oxygen, which the body needs to release energy from food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22. What is the function of synovial fluid in the knee joint? A: It lubricates the joint (reduces friction between the bones).. Synovial fluid is like oil in the joint; it lets the bones move smoothly without rubbing.
chunks.source: Synovial fluid is like oil in the joint; it lets the bones move smoothly without rubbing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23. Give the main cause of fainting. A: Insufficient supply of blood (and oxygen) to the brain.. When the brain does not get enough blood and oxygen, a person faints.
chunks.source: When the brain does not get enough blood and oxygen, a person faints.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 24. Mention one service provided under ante-natal care. A: Immunising mothers against tetanus (any one: examining the mother, giving health education).. During ante-natal care, mothers are examined, immunised and taught how to care for themselves and the baby.
chunks.source: During ante-natal care, mothers are examined, immunised and taught how to care for themselves and the baby.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. Which blood vessel transports digested food from the ileum to the liver? A: Hepatic portal vein.. After absorption in the ileum, digested food is carried to the liver by the hepatic portal vein.
chunks.source: After absorption in the ileum, digested food is carried to the liver by the hepatic portal vein.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26. The diagram below shows a chalk box (5 cm by 4 cm by 6 cm). Find its volume. A: 120 cm3.. Volume = length x width x height = 6 cm x 5 cm x 4 cm = 120 cm3.
chunks.source: Volume = length x width x height = 6 cm x 5 cm x 4 cm = 120 cm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27. Study the animals given in list K (FISH, BIRD, FROG) and those in list M (MAN, WHALE, BAT). How are animals in list K similar to those in list M? A: They are all vertebrates (they all have backbones).. Fish, birds, frogs, man, whales and bats all have backbones, so they are all vertebrates.
chunks.source: Fish, birds, frogs, man, whales and bats all have backbones, so they are all vertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28. What is the source of energy in thermal electricity? A: Heat (from burning fuel such as coal, oil or peat).. Thermal electricity is generated using heat produced by burning fuels.
chunks.source: Thermal electricity is generated using heat produced by burning fuels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29. Why is it a bad practice for people to share a house with domestic animals? A: Animals can spread diseases and parasites to people.. Domestic animals carry germs, ticks and fleas which can easily pass to people sharing the house.
chunks.source: Domestic animals carry germs, ticks and fleas which can easily pass to people sharing the house.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30. State the use of a stretcher when giving First Aid to a victim with a fracture. A: To carry the casualty safely without worsening the fracture.. A stretcher keeps the injured part still while the victim is carried, so the fracture does not get worse.
chunks.source: A stretcher keeps the injured part still while the victim is carried, so the fracture does not get worse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31. How does a vent help to reduce smell in a VIP latrine? A: It lets out the bad smell (gases) from the pit.. The vent pipe carries smelly gases from the pit up into the air, away from the latrine users.
chunks.source: The vent pipe carries smelly gases from the pit up into the air, away from the latrine users.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32. Write down one danger of buying drugs from local shops or markets. A: The drugs may be expired or fake (any one: wrong drug, wrong dosage).. Drugs sold in markets may be expired, fake or wrongly measured, which can harm the patient.
chunks.source: Drugs sold in markets may be expired, fake or wrongly measured, which can harm the patient.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33. Name one material used to guard against electric shock. A: Rubber (any one: plastic, dry wood).. Insulators like rubber and plastic do not conduct electricity, so they protect people from electric shock.
chunks.source: Insulators like rubber and plastic do not conduct electricity, so they protect people from electric shock.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34. Draw prop roots in the space provided below. A: Prop roots grow out from the lower part of the stem and go down into the soil, supporting the plant (as in maize).. Prop roots are extra roots that grow from the stem above the ground to give the plant extra support.
chunks.source: Prop roots are extra roots that grow from the stem above the ground to give the plant extra support.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35. Which body system is commonly affected by polio? A: Nervous system.. Polio attacks the nerves, which is why it can cause paralysis of the limbs.
chunks.source: Polio attacks the nerves, which is why it can cause paralysis of the limbs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 36. State one process by which soil is formed. A: Weathering.. Soil is formed when rocks are broken down into small particles by weathering.
chunks.source: Soil is formed when rocks are broken down into small particles by weathering.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 37. Give one use of an axe at home. A: Splitting firewood (any one: cutting wood).. An axe is used at home mainly for splitting firewood into pieces.
chunks.source: An axe is used at home mainly for splitting firewood into pieces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38. What happens to the blood as it passes through the kidneys? A: Waste products (urea, excess water and salts) are removed from it.. The kidneys filter the blood, removing waste materials which leave the body as urine.
chunks.source: The kidneys filter the blood, removing waste materials which leave the body as urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. Study the diagram of a leaf below. What is part marked B? A: Petiole (leaf stalk).. Part B is the stalk that joins the leaf blade to the stem; it is called the petiole.
chunks.source: Part B is the stalk that joins the leaf blade to the stem; it is called the petiole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. Give one of the functions of the structures marked A on a leaf. A: They allow gaseous exchange (they let in carbon dioxide and release oxygen and water vapour).. The structures marked A are stomata, tiny openings through which gases move in and out of the leaf.
chunks.source: The structures marked A are stomata, tiny openings through which gases move in and out of the leaf.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1. Mention any one example of a childhood immunisable disease. A: Polio (any one: measles, tuberculosis, diphtheria, tetanus).. Childhood immunisable diseases like polio and measles are prevented by vaccination.
chunks.source: Childhood immunisable diseases like polio and measles are prevented by vaccination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2. Identify the part of the digestive system where alcohol is absorbed. A: Stomach.. Alcohol is absorbed mainly through the walls of the stomach into the blood.
chunks.source: Alcohol is absorbed mainly through the walls of the stomach into the blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3. In which way does the use of solar energy for cooking help to conserve the environment? A: It reduces the cutting down of trees for firewood.. Cooking with the sun saves trees, keeping forests that protect the environment.
chunks.source: Cooking with the sun saves trees, keeping forests that protect the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4. How are screws similar to wheels and axles in the way they simplify work? A: Both are simple machines that make work easier.. Screws and wheels-and-axles are simple machines that help people do work with less effort.
chunks.source: Screws and wheels-and-axles are simple machines that help people do work with less effort.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5. Name the type of germ which causes ringworm infection. A: Fungus.. Ringworm is a skin infection caused by a fungus, not a worm.
chunks.source: Ringworm is a skin infection caused by a fungus, not a worm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6. How is the cause of burns similar to that of scalds? A: Both are caused by heat.. Burns come from dry heat like fire, and scalds from wet heat like steam, but both are heat injuries.
chunks.source: Burns come from dry heat like fire, and scalds from wet heat like steam, but both are heat injuries.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7. Give one way in which reflection of light is useful to people. A: It enables us to see (any one: mirrors help us see behind, periscopes).. We see objects when light reflects off them into our eyes; mirrors use reflection too.
chunks.source: We see objects when light reflects off them into our eyes; mirrors use reflection too.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8. What term refers to the practice of growing crops and trees together on the same piece of land? A: Agroforestry.. Agroforestry is the growing of crops and trees together on the same land.
chunks.source: Agroforestry is the growing of crops and trees together on the same land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 9. In the diagram below, a plastic comb was rubbed against a woollen cloth and it was brought nearer to small pieces of paper. Why is the plastic comb able to attract the pieces of paper as shown above? A: The comb became electrically charged (static electricity).. Rubbing the comb charges it with static electricity, which then attracts the light paper pieces.
chunks.source: Rubbing the comb charges it with static electricity, which then attracts the light paper pieces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10. What form of energy is stored in a candle? A: Chemical energy.. A candle stores chemical energy in its wax, released as light and heat when it burns.
chunks.source: A candle stores chemical energy in its wax, released as light and heat when it burns.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11. Name the fungal-caused sexually transmitted disease which is spread through poor hygiene. A: Candidiasis.. Candidiasis is a fungal infection spread through poor hygiene.
chunks.source: Candidiasis is a fungal infection spread through poor hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12. Which method of heat transfer helps farmers to dry their harvested crops? A: Radiation.. The sun's heat reaches crops by radiation and dries them.
chunks.source: The sun's heat reaches crops by radiation and dries them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 13. Give one sign of pest and disease attack on tuber crops. A: Holes in the leaves (any one: rotting tubers, wilting).. Pests chew leaves leaving holes, and diseases rot the tubers.
chunks.source: Pests chew leaves leaving holes, and diseases rot the tubers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14. Identify one condition needed by bacteria to multiply. A: Warmth (any one: moisture, food, oxygen).. Bacteria multiply fast where it is warm and moist with food available.
chunks.source: Bacteria multiply fast where it is warm and moist with food available.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15. Give any one good effect of changes in the environment. A: Rain provides water for crops to grow.. Environmental changes like rainfall bring water needed by plants and animals.
chunks.source: Environmental changes like rainfall bring water needed by plants and animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. How can foot and mouth disease be controlled on a farm? A: Vaccinating the animals (any one: quarantine, restricting animal movement).. Vaccination and quarantine stop foot and mouth disease from spreading among animals.
chunks.source: Vaccination and quarantine stop foot and mouth disease from spreading among animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 17. Study the diagram below and answer the questions about it. How are structures marked X useful to the above organism? A: They help it to fly (wings).. The structures marked X are wings, which let the organism fly from place to place.
chunks.source: The structures marked X are wings, which let the organism fly from place to place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18. Which disease is spread by the above organism to people? A: Cholera (any one: typhoid, dysentery).. The organism (housefly) carries germs from faeces to food, spreading cholera and similar diseases.
chunks.source: The organism (housefly) carries germs from faeces to food, spreading cholera and similar diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19. How is the above organism similar to a maggot? A: The maggot is the larval stage that grows into the organism (both are stages of the housefly's life cycle).. A maggot develops through pupa into the adult organism, the housefly.
chunks.source: A maggot develops through pupa into the adult organism, the housefly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 20. Why should a pig sty have a slanting floor? A: So that urine and washing water drain out easily.. A slanting floor lets waste water flow out, keeping the sty clean and dry.
chunks.source: A slanting floor lets waste water flow out, keeping the sty clean and dry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21. Give one way in which music stored by staff notation can be reproduced. A: By singing or playing it on instruments.. Written music in staff notation can be read and performed by singers and instrumentalists.
chunks.source: Written music in staff notation can be read and performed by singers and instrumentalists.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22. In the space below, draw a vein and show the flow of blood in it. A: A blood vessel drawn with valves inside and an arrow showing blood flowing towards the heart.. Veins carry blood back to the heart and have valves that stop blood flowing backwards.
chunks.source: Veins carry blood back to the heart and have valves that stop blood flowing backwards.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23. Give one factor that leads to sickness in a home. A: Poor sanitation (any one: poor feeding).. Dirty homes breed germs that make family members sick.
chunks.source: Dirty homes breed germs that make family members sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 24. What type of root system does an onion plant have? A: Fibrous root system.. Onions have many thin spreading roots, which form a fibrous root system.
chunks.source: Onions have many thin spreading roots, which form a fibrous root system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. Apart from production of eggs (ova), mention one other use of the ovaries in the human body. A: They produce female hormones (oestrogen).. The ovaries also make hormones that bring about female body changes.
chunks.source: The ovaries also make hormones that bring about female body changes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26. How does a sweater help to keep a person warm during cold days? A: It traps warm air and prevents body heat from escaping.. A sweater holds a layer of warm air around the body, keeping heat in.
chunks.source: A sweater holds a layer of warm air around the body, keeping heat in.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27. Write down any one example of an animal fibre. A: Wool (any one: silk, fur).. Wool from sheep is an animal fibre used to make clothes.
chunks.source: Wool from sheep is an animal fibre used to make clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28. State the compass direction in which a freely suspended magnet will rest. A: North-south direction.. A freely hanging magnet always settles pointing north and south.
chunks.source: A freely hanging magnet always settles pointing north and south.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29. Give any one property of air in the diagram below. A: Air occupies space.. The diagram shows that air takes up space inside a container.
chunks.source: The diagram shows that air takes up space inside a container.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30. Which body sense is used by Phionah to know whether Alex has dressed perfume? A: Smell.. Perfume is detected by the nose, the organ of smell.
chunks.source: Perfume is detected by the nose, the organ of smell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31. Why is photosynthesis important to animals? A: It provides oxygen for breathing (and food for animals).. Animals depend on plants for the oxygen they breathe and the food they eat.
chunks.source: Animals depend on plants for the oxygen they breathe and the food they eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32. What process makes dew to disappear during hot days? A: Evaporation.. Heat turns dew drops into water vapour, which is evaporation.
chunks.source: Heat turns dew drops into water vapour, which is evaporation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33. What group of birds are vultures, kites and crows? A: Birds of prey.. Vultures, kites and crows feed on flesh, so they are birds of prey.
chunks.source: Vultures, kites and crows feed on flesh, so they are birds of prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34. Why does an insect die when its abdomen is placed in oil for some time? A: Oil blocks its breathing holes (spiracles), so it suffocates.. Insects breathe through tiny holes on the abdomen; oil covers them and stops air entering.
chunks.source: Insects breathe through tiny holes on the abdomen; oil covers them and stops air entering.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35. Give any one special characteristic of the air we breathe out. A: It contains a lot of carbon dioxide (any one: it is warm and moist).. Breathed-out air is rich in carbon dioxide produced in the body.
chunks.source: Breathed-out air is rich in carbon dioxide produced in the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 36. Find the density of an object whose mass is 19 g and volume is 5 cm3. A: 3.8 g/cm3.. Density = mass / volume = 19 g / 5 cm3 = 3.8 g/cm3.
chunks.source: Density = mass / volume = 19 g / 5 cm3 = 3.8 g/cm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 37. Why does smoke go up when firewood is burning? A: Smoke is hot and less dense than the surrounding air, so it rises.. Hot smoke is lighter than cool air, so it floats upward.
chunks.source: Hot smoke is lighter than cool air, so it floats upward.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38. Give one reason why drugs should be prescribed by health workers before they are used by sick people. A: To get the right drug and correct dosage (any one: to avoid misuse).. Health workers choose the correct medicine and amount for each sickness.
chunks.source: Health workers choose the correct medicine and amount for each sickness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. What feature enables a housefly to spread diseases? A: Its hairy body and legs trap germs.. Germs stick to the housefly's hairy body and legs and are carried to food.
chunks.source: Germs stick to the housefly's hairy body and legs and are carried to food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. Give any one characteristic of flowers which attract moths to visit them at night. A: They produce a sweet scent (any one: white petals visible at night).. Night flowers attract moths with strong sweet smells and pale petals.
chunks.source: Night flowers attract moths with strong sweet smells and pale petals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a) The diagram below shows a simple circuit. Study it carefully. Name the part marked with letter T. A: Bulb.. Part T is the bulb, which lights when the circuit is complete.
chunks.source: Part T is the bulb, which lights when the circuit is complete.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) Give the function of the part marked with letter M. A: It provides electricity (it is the source of power in the circuit).. Part M is the dry cell (battery) which pushes electric current round the circuit.
chunks.source: Part M is the dry cell (battery) which pushes electric current round the circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c) State any one energy change which takes place in an electric bulb when part labeled K is closed. A: Electrical energy changes to light and heat energy.. When the switch K is closed, current flows and the bulb turns electrical energy into light (and heat).
chunks.source: When the switch K is closed, current flows and the bulb turns electrical energy into light (and heat).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(d) Using an arrow, show the direction of the flow of electrons in the diagram above. A: Electrons flow from the negative terminal of the cell to the positive terminal round the circuit.. In a circuit, electrons move from the negative side of the battery, through the wires, to the positive side.
chunks.source: In a circuit, electrons move from the negative side of the battery, through the wires, to the positive side.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a) State the difference between endoskeleton and exoskeleton. A: An endoskeleton is found inside the body while an exoskeleton is found outside the body.. People have skeletons inside their bodies (endoskeleton), while insects wear theirs outside (exoskeleton).
chunks.source: People have skeletons inside their bodies (endoskeleton), while insects wear theirs outside (exoskeleton).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) State the protective function of the skull to the human skeleton. A: It protects the brain.. The skull is a hard bony case that shields the delicate brain from injury.
chunks.source: The skull is a hard bony case that shields the delicate brain from injury.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c)(i) Write one advantage of maintaining proper body posture. A: It prevents backache and deformity of the body.. Sitting and standing upright keeps the backbone in good shape.
chunks.source: Sitting and standing upright keeps the backbone in good shape.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c)(ii) Write another advantage of maintaining proper body posture. A: It allows proper breathing and blood flow (any one: one looks smart).. Good posture lets the lungs and heart work well.
chunks.source: Good posture lets the lungs and heart work well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a) Why do earthworms come out of the soil after it has rained? A: Their holes get filled with water, so they come out to breathe.. Earthworms breathe through moist skin and cannot breathe under water in flooded holes.
chunks.source: Earthworms breathe through moist skin and cannot breathe under water in flooded holes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(i) Give one way in which earthworms are useful to farmers. A: They aerate the soil (they make air spaces as they burrow).. Burrowing earthworms open up the soil so air and water enter easily.
chunks.source: Burrowing earthworms open up the soil so air and water enter easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(ii) Give another way in which earthworms are useful to farmers. A: Their droppings add fertility to the soil.. Earthworm droppings are rich in nutrients that feed crops.
chunks.source: Earthworm droppings are rich in nutrients that feed crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c) To which group of animals do earthworms belong? A: Annelids (segmented worms).. Earthworms have segmented bodies, so they belong to the annelids.
chunks.source: Earthworms have segmented bodies, so they belong to the annelids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a) The diagram below is an experiment performed by a P.7 class (copper rod with vaseline and clips, heated at one end). What is the experiment about? A: How heat travels through a metal (conduction).. The experiment shows heat moving along the copper rod from the hot end, melting vaseline at each clip.
chunks.source: The experiment shows heat moving along the copper rod from the hot end, melting vaseline at each clip.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b) What is the importance of vaseline in the experiment? A: It holds the clips in place (it melts when heat reaches it).. Vaseline sticks the clips to the rod; when heat arrives, it melts and the clip falls.
chunks.source: Vaseline sticks the clips to the rod; when heat arrives, it melts and the clip falls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c) What will happen to vaseline in clip 4 after some time? A: It will melt and the clip will fall.. Heat travels along the rod to clip 4, melting its vaseline last.
chunks.source: Heat travels along the rod to clip 4, melting its vaseline last.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(d) Give a reason for your answer. A: Heat travels from the hot end to the cold end of the rod by conduction.. Conduction carries heat along the metal until it reaches the last clip.
chunks.source: Conduction carries heat along the metal until it reaches the last clip.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(i) Mention one service provided to expectant mothers during ante-natal care. A: Immunising mothers against tetanus (any one: examining the mother, giving health education).. During ante-natal visits, mothers are examined, immunised and taught how to stay healthy.
chunks.source: During ante-natal visits, mothers are examined, immunised and taught how to stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(ii) Mention another service provided to expectant mothers during ante-natal care. A: Giving health education to the mothers.. Mothers learn about feeding, hygiene and preparing for safe delivery.
chunks.source: Mothers learn about feeding, hygiene and preparing for safe delivery.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b) Write down any one primary sex characteristic that is common in both boys and girls. A: Growth of pubic hair.. At puberty, both boys and girls grow hair in the pubic region.
chunks.source: At puberty, both boys and girls grow hair in the pubic region.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c) State any one role played by children in promoting PIASCY at school. A: They sensitise fellow pupils about the dangers of HIV/AIDS.. Children spread PIASCY messages by teaching others how to avoid HIV/AIDS.
chunks.source: Children spread PIASCY messages by teaching others how to avoid HIV/AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) The experiment below demonstrates the process of breathing in human beings (Y-shaped tube, balloon, bell jar, rubber sheet). What does the Y-shaped tube represent on the diagram above? A: The trachea and bronchi.. The Y-shaped tube stands for the windpipe (trachea) branching into the two bronchi.
chunks.source: The Y-shaped tube stands for the windpipe (trachea) branching into the two bronchi.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) What happens to the rubber sheet when it is pulled down? A: The balloons inflate (air is drawn in).. Pulling the rubber sheet down is like the diaphragm moving down; air rushes in and the balloons (lungs) inflate.
chunks.source: Pulling the rubber sheet down is like the diaphragm moving down; air rushes in and the balloons (lungs) inflate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c) Why is there an increase in the percentage of carbon dioxide we breathe out than the one we breathe in? A: Carbon dioxide is produced when food is broken down in the body.. Respiration in body cells releases carbon dioxide, which is then breathed out.
chunks.source: Respiration in body cells releases carbon dioxide, which is then breathed out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(d) Give the importance of cilia found in the nose during the process of breathing in. A: They trap dust and germs.. Tiny hairs (cilia) in the nose catch dust and germs so that clean air reaches the lungs.
chunks.source: Tiny hairs (cilia) in the nose catch dust and germs so that clean air reaches the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) What term refers to the deposition of eroded soil into water bodies? A: Silting (sedimentation).. When eroded soil settles in rivers and lakes, the process is called silting.
chunks.source: When eroded soil settles in rivers and lakes, the process is called silting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(i) In which way does uncontrolled bush burning degrade the environment? A: It destroys vegetation cover.. Burning kills plants, leaving the land bare and lifeless.
chunks.source: Burning kills plants, leaving the land bare and lifeless.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(ii) In which other way does uncontrolled bush burning degrade the environment? A: It kills soil organisms (any one: it causes soil erosion, it pollutes the air).. Fire kills useful organisms in the soil and leaves soil open to erosion.
chunks.source: Fire kills useful organisms in the soil and leaves soil open to erosion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) Give one way in which silting affects fish. A: It kills fish (it destroys their habitat and breeding grounds).. Silt fills water bodies, reducing oxygen and destroying where fish live and breed.
chunks.source: Silt fills water bodies, reducing oxygen and destroying where fish live and breed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a) The diagram below shows a method of grazing cattle. Identify the method of grazing cattle shown above. A: Paddock grazing.. The diagram shows cattle kept in fenced paddocks and moved from one to another.
chunks.source: The diagram shows cattle kept in fenced paddocks and moved from one to another.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b) State any one advantage of the above method of grazing cattle. A: It controls tick-borne diseases (any one: pasture is given time to rest and regrow).. Moving cattle between paddocks breaks the tick life cycle and lets grass recover.
chunks.source: Moving cattle between paddocks breaks the tick life cycle and lets grass recover.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c) How does paddock grazing help to control tick borne diseases? A: It breaks the life cycle of ticks (ticks starve and die while a paddock rests).. Ticks die when paddocks stay empty of cattle for some time.
chunks.source: Ticks die when paddocks stay empty of cattle for some time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(d) State one way in which colostrum is important to a newly born calf. A: It gives the calf protection against diseases (it contains antibodies).. The first milk, colostrum, gives the newborn calf immunity against infections.
chunks.source: The first milk, colostrum, gives the newborn calf immunity against infections.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a) How is a pineapple plant similar to a banana in the way they are propagated? A: Both are propagated by planting suckers.. Pineapples and bananas are both multiplied vegetatively using suckers, not seeds.
chunks.source: Pineapples and bananas are both multiplied vegetatively using suckers, not seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(i) Give one advantage of vegetative propagation over seed propagation. A: Plants mature faster (any one: plants are true to the parent type).. Vegetatively propagated plants fruit earlier than those grown from seeds.
chunks.source: Vegetatively propagated plants fruit earlier than those grown from seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(ii) Give another advantage of vegetative propagation over seed propagation. A: The new plants are exactly like the parent (any one: no seed dormancy).. Suckers and cuttings keep the good qualities of the parent plant.
chunks.source: Suckers and cuttings keep the good qualities of the parent plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) [second (b)] Which method of seed dispersal involves bursting/splitting of a pod violently due to long exposure to sun heat? A: Explosive mechanism.. Dry pods burst open in the sun's heat, flinging seeds away; this is the explosive mechanism.
chunks.source: Dry pods burst open in the sun's heat, flinging seeds away; this is the explosive mechanism.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50. The table below shows parts of a flowering plant; their functions are in the wrong order. Match the parts to their functions: Roots, Stem, Leaves, Flowers. Functions: absorb water and mineral salts, support the plant and transport materials, make food by photosynthesis, reproduction. A: Roots - absorb water and mineral salts; Stem - support the plant and transport materials; Leaves - make food by photosynthesis; Flowers - reproduction.. Roots absorb, stems support and transport, leaves make food, and flowers reproduce the plant.
chunks.source: Roots absorb, stems support and transport, leaves make food, and flowers reproduce the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 1. Mention any one example of a childhood immunisable disease. A: Polio. Polio is one of the killer diseases children are immunised against at health centres.
chunks.source: Polio is one of the killer diseases children are immunised against at health centres.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 2. Identify the part of the digestive system where alcohol is absorbed. A: Stomach. Alcohol passes through the walls of the stomach into the blood.
chunks.source: Alcohol passes through the walls of the stomach into the blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 3. In which way does the use of solar energy for cooking help to conserve the environment? A: It reduces the cutting down of trees for firewood. Solar cookers use heat from the sun, so fewer trees are cut for firewood and less smoke pollutes the air.
chunks.source: Solar cookers use heat from the sun, so fewer trees are cut for firewood and less smoke pollutes the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 4. How are screws similar to wheels and axles in the way they simplify work? A: Both reduce the effort needed to do work. A screw and a wheel and axle are both simple machines that multiply force so less effort is needed.
chunks.source: A screw and a wheel and axle are both simple machines that multiply force so less effort is needed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5. Name the type of germ which causes ringworm infection. A: Fungi. Ringworm is a skin infection caused by fungi, not by worms.
chunks.source: Ringworm is a skin infection caused by fungi, not by worms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 6. How is the cause of burns similar to that of scalds? A: Both are caused by heat. Burns are caused by dry heat while scalds are caused by wet heat such as steam or hot water.
chunks.source: Burns are caused by dry heat while scalds are caused by wet heat such as steam or hot water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 7. Give one way in which reflection of light is useful to people. A: It enables us to see ourselves in mirrors. A mirror reflects light to form our image, which helps us check our appearance.
chunks.source: A mirror reflects light to form our image, which helps us check our appearance.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 8. What term refers to the practice of growing crops and trees together on the same piece of land? A: Agroforestry. In agroforestry, crops and trees share the same land so farmers get food as well as wood or fruits.
chunks.source: In agroforestry, crops and trees share the same land so farmers get food as well as wood or fruits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 9. A plastic comb was rubbed against a woollen cloth and brought near small pieces of paper. Why is the plastic comb able to attract the pieces of paper? A: The comb became charged with static electricity when rubbed. Rubbing the comb on the woollen cloth charges it, and the charged comb attracts the light pieces of paper.
chunks.source: Rubbing the comb on the woollen cloth charges it, and the charged comb attracts the light pieces of paper.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 10. What form of energy is stored in a candle? A: Chemical energy. The wax in a candle stores chemical energy, which changes to heat and light energy when the candle burns.
chunks.source: The wax in a candle stores chemical energy, which changes to heat and light energy when the candle burns.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11. Name the fungal-caused sexually transmitted disease which is spread through poor hygiene. A: Candidiasis (thrush). Candidiasis is caused by a fungus and spreads through poor personal hygiene.
chunks.source: Candidiasis is caused by a fungus and spreads through poor personal hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 12. Which method of heat transfer helps farmers to dry their harvested crops? A: Convection. Warm air rises by convection, carrying moisture away from the crops so they dry faster.
chunks.source: Warm air rises by convection, carrying moisture away from the crops so they dry faster.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 13. Give one sign of pest and disease attack on tuber crops. A: Holes bored in the leaves or tubers. Pests chew holes in leaves and tubers, and diseases cause rotting or yellowing of the crop.
chunks.source: Pests chew holes in leaves and tubers, and diseases cause rotting or yellowing of the crop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 14. Identify one condition needed by bacteria to multiply. A: Warmth. Bacteria multiply fast in warm, moist places where food is available.
chunks.source: Bacteria multiply fast in warm, moist places where food is available.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 15. Give any one good effect of changes in the environment. A: Rainfall provides water for crops to grow. Seasonal changes such as rainfall bring water that helps plants grow well.
chunks.source: Seasonal changes such as rainfall bring water that helps plants grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 16. How can foot and mouth disease be controlled on a farm? A: By vaccinating the animals. Vaccination protects healthy animals, while infected ones should be isolated or slaughtered.
chunks.source: Vaccination protects healthy animals, while infected ones should be isolated or slaughtered.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 17. How are structures marked X useful to the above organism? A: They are used for walking and movement. The legs help the insect move from place to place in search of food.
chunks.source: The legs help the insect move from place to place in search of food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 18. Which disease is spread by the above organism to people? A: Cholera. Houseflies carry germs from faeces and rubbish onto food, spreading cholera and other diarrhoeal diseases.
chunks.source: Houseflies carry germs from faeces and rubbish onto food, spreading cholera and other diarrhoeal diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 19. How is the above organism similar to a maggot? A: Both are stages in the life cycle of a housefly. A maggot is the larva stage which grows into the adult housefly.
chunks.source: A maggot is the larva stage which grows into the adult housefly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 20. Why should a pig sty have a slanting floor? A: To allow urine and water to drain easily. A slanting floor lets urine and washing water flow out, keeping the sty clean and dry.
chunks.source: A slanting floor lets urine and washing water flow out, keeping the sty clean and dry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 21. Give one way in which music stored by staff notation can be reproduced. A: By singing the notes. The written notes can be sung or played on a musical instrument to reproduce the music.
chunks.source: The written notes can be sung or played on a musical instrument to reproduce the music.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 22. In the space below, draw a vein and show the flow of blood in it. A: A tube drawn with valves inside and an arrow pointing towards the heart. Veins carry blood towards the heart and have valves that prevent blood from flowing backwards.
chunks.source: Veins carry blood towards the heart and have valves that prevent blood from flowing backwards.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 23. Give one factor that leads to sickness in a home. A: Poor sanitation. Dirty surroundings breed germs and vectors that cause diseases.
chunks.source: Dirty surroundings breed germs and vectors that cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 24. What type of root system does an onion plant have? A: Fibrous (adventitious) root system. Onions grow many thin roots of equal size from the base of the bulb.
chunks.source: Onions grow many thin roots of equal size from the base of the bulb.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 25. Apart from production of eggs (ova), mention one other use of the ovaries in the human body. A: They produce female sex hormones (oestrogen). The ovaries release oestrogen, which controls the development of female body features.
chunks.source: The ovaries release oestrogen, which controls the development of female body features.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26. How does a sweater help to keep a person warm during cold days? A: It traps warm air around the body and prevents heat loss. The sweater is a poor conductor of heat, so body heat is kept in and cold air is kept out.
chunks.source: The sweater is a poor conductor of heat, so body heat is kept in and cold air is kept out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 27. Write down any one example of an animal fibre. A: Wool. Wool is obtained from sheep and is used to make sweaters and blankets.
chunks.source: Wool is obtained from sheep and is used to make sweaters and blankets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 28. State the compass direction in which a freely suspended magnet will rest. A: North–south direction. A freely suspended magnet always comes to rest pointing north and south because of the earth's magnetism.
chunks.source: A freely suspended magnet always comes to rest pointing north and south because of the earth's magnetism.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 29. Give any one property of air illustrated in the diagram. A: Air occupies space. Air takes up space, so it pushes water out of the way in the experiment.
chunks.source: Air takes up space, so it pushes water out of the way in the experiment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 30. Which body sense is used by Phionah to know whether Alex has dressed perfume? A: Sense of smell. The nose detects the scent of the perfume.
chunks.source: The nose detects the scent of the perfume.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 31. Why is photosynthesis important to animals? A: It releases oxygen needed by animals for respiration. Green plants give out oxygen during photosynthesis, which animals breathe in.
chunks.source: Green plants give out oxygen during photosynthesis, which animals breathe in.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 32. What process makes dew disappear during hot days? A: Evaporation. Heat from the sun changes the dew (liquid water) into water vapour.
chunks.source: Heat from the sun changes the dew (liquid water) into water vapour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 33. What group of birds are vultures, kites and crows? A: Scavenger birds. These birds feed on dead animals (carrion).
chunks.source: These birds feed on dead animals (carrion).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 34. Why does an insect die when its abdomen is placed in oil for some time? A: Oil blocks the spiracles and the insect suffocates. Insects breathe through spiracles on the abdomen; oil seals them so air cannot enter.
chunks.source: Insects breathe through spiracles on the abdomen; oil seals them so air cannot enter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 35. Give any one special characteristic of the air we breathe out. A: It contains more carbon dioxide than the air breathed in. Breathed-out air has about 4% carbon dioxide because oxygen is used up in the body.
chunks.source: Breathed-out air has about 4% carbon dioxide because oxygen is used up in the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 36. Find the density of an object whose mass is 19g and volume is 5cm³. A: 3.8 g/cm³. Density = mass ÷ volume = 19 ÷ 5 = 3.8 g/cm³.
chunks.source: Density = mass ÷ volume = 19 ÷ 5 = 3.8 g/cm³.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 37. Why does smoke go up when firewood is burning? A: Hot smoke is less dense than the surrounding air, so it rises. Heated smoke expands, becomes lighter than cool air, and rises by convection.
chunks.source: Heated smoke expands, becomes lighter than cool air, and rises by convection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 38. Give one reason why drugs should be prescribed by health workers before they are used by sick people. A: To ensure the correct drug and dosage is used. Health workers know the right drug and amount, which prevents harm from wrong or excess drugs.
chunks.source: Health workers know the right drug and amount, which prevents harm from wrong or excess drugs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 39. What feature enables a housefly to spread diseases? A: Its hairy legs and body carry germs. Germs stick to the hairs on the housefly's legs and body and are dropped onto food.
chunks.source: Germs stick to the hairs on the housefly's legs and body and are dropped onto food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 40. Give any one characteristic of flowers which attract moths to visit them at night. A: They produce a sweet scent at night. Night-blooming flowers give off a strong scent that guides moths to them in the dark.
chunks.source: Night-blooming flowers give off a strong scent that guides moths to them in the dark.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a) Name the part of the simple circuit marked with letter T. A: Bulb (electric lamp). The bulb is the part that gives light when current flows through the circuit.
chunks.source: The bulb is the part that gives light when current flows through the circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) Give the function of the part of the simple circuit marked with letter M. A: It provides electrical energy (current) to the circuit. The dry cell is the source of electricity that drives current round the circuit.
chunks.source: The dry cell is the source of electricity that drives current round the circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c) State any one energy change which takes place in an electric bulb when part labelled K is closed. A: Electrical energy changes to light and heat energy. When the switch K is closed, current flows and the bulb filament glows, giving out light and heat.
chunks.source: When the switch K is closed, current flows and the bulb filament glows, giving out light and heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(d) Using an arrow, show the direction of the flow of electrons in the circuit diagram. A: Electrons flow from the negative terminal of the cell through the wires to the positive terminal. In a circuit, electrons move from the negative terminal towards the positive terminal, opposite to conventional current.
chunks.source: In a circuit, electrons move from the negative terminal towards the positive terminal, opposite to conventional current.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a) State the difference between endoskeleton and exoskeleton. A: An endoskeleton is found inside the body while an exoskeleton is found outside the body. Humans have an endoskeleton (bones inside); insects have an exoskeleton (hard covering outside).
chunks.source: Humans have an endoskeleton (bones inside); insects have an exoskeleton (hard covering outside).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) State the protective function of the skull to the human skeleton. A: It protects the brain. The skull is a hard bony case that shields the delicate brain from injury.
chunks.source: The skull is a hard bony case that shields the delicate brain from injury.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c)(i) Write two advantages of maintaining proper body posture. (i) A: It prevents deformities of the body (e.g. a bent spine). Good posture keeps the spine straight and the body in proper shape.
chunks.source: Good posture keeps the spine straight and the body in proper shape.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c)(ii) Write two advantages of maintaining proper body posture. (ii) A: It prevents backache and allows body organs to work properly. Sitting and standing upright avoids strain on muscles and lets organs like the lungs expand fully.
chunks.source: Sitting and standing upright avoids strain on muscles and lets organs like the lungs expand fully.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a) Why do earthworms come out of the soil after it has rained? A: To avoid drowning as rainwater fills their burrows. Rainwater floods their tunnels, so earthworms move to the surface where they can get air.
chunks.source: Rainwater floods their tunnels, so earthworms move to the surface where they can get air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(i) Give two ways in which earthworms are useful to farmers. (i) A: They aerate the soil — their burrows let air and water reach plant roots. The tunnels made by earthworms allow air and water to move into the soil.
chunks.source: The tunnels made by earthworms allow air and water to move into the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(ii) Give two ways in which earthworms are useful to farmers. (ii) A: They improve soil fertility — their castings (droppings) enrich the soil. Earthworms eat dead leaves and their droppings add nutrients to the soil.
chunks.source: Earthworms eat dead leaves and their droppings add nutrients to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c) To which group of animals do earthworms belong? A: Invertebrates (segmented worms). Earthworms have no backbone, so they are invertebrates.
chunks.source: Earthworms have no backbone, so they are invertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a) The diagram shows an experiment with vaseline and clips on a copper rod heated at one end. What is the experiment about? A: Conduction of heat through solids (metals). The copper rod carries heat from the hot end to the cold end, melting the vaseline at each clip in turn.
chunks.source: The copper rod carries heat from the hot end to the cold end, melting the vaseline at each clip in turn.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b) What is the importance of vaseline in the experiment? A: It sticks the clips onto the copper rod. The vaseline holds the clips in place until heat melts it, showing that heat has reached that point.
chunks.source: The vaseline holds the clips in place until heat melts it, showing that heat has reached that point.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c) What will happen to vaseline in clip 4 after some time? A: It will melt and clip 4 will fall off. Heat conducted along the rod will eventually reach clip 4 and melt the vaseline holding it.
chunks.source: Heat conducted along the rod will eventually reach clip 4 and melt the vaseline holding it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(d) Give a reason for your answer in (c) above. A: Heat is conducted from the hot end of the copper rod to the cold end. Copper is a good conductor of heat, so heat travels along the rod until it reaches clip 4.
chunks.source: Copper is a good conductor of heat, so heat travels along the rod until it reaches clip 4.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(i) Mention any two services provided to expectant mothers during ante-natal care. (i) A: Checking the health and growth of the foetus and the mother. Health workers examine the mother and unborn baby to detect problems early.
chunks.source: Health workers examine the mother and unborn baby to detect problems early.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(ii) Mention any two services provided to expectant mothers during ante-natal care. (ii) A: Immunising the mother against tetanus. The tetanus vaccine protects both the mother and the newborn baby from tetanus infection.
chunks.source: The tetanus vaccine protects both the mother and the newborn baby from tetanus infection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b) Write down any one primary sex characteristic that is common in both boys and girls. A: Development (maturation) of the reproductive organs. At puberty, the reproductive organs of both boys and girls mature so that they can reproduce.
chunks.source: At puberty, the reproductive organs of both boys and girls mature so that they can reproduce.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c) State any one role played by children in promoting PIASCY at school. A: Educating fellow pupils about HIV/AIDS prevention (peer education). Children share PIASCY messages with their peers, encouraging abstinence and safe behaviour.
chunks.source: Children share PIASCY messages with their peers, encouraging abstinence and safe behaviour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) In the breathing experiment with the Y-shaped tube, balloon and bell jar, what does the Y-shaped tube represent? A: The trachea and bronchi (air passages). The Y-tube stands for the windpipe which branches into the two bronchi leading to the lungs.
chunks.source: The Y-tube stands for the windpipe which branches into the two bronchi leading to the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) What happens to the rubber sheet when it is pulled down? A: The balloons inflate as air rushes in. Pulling the sheet down increases the space in the jar, lowering the pressure so outside air rushes in — like breathing in.
chunks.source: Pulling the sheet down increases the space in the jar, lowering the pressure so outside air rushes in — like breathing in.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c) Why is there an increase in the percentage of carbon dioxide we breathe out than the one we breathe in? A: Oxygen is used up in the body during respiration, producing carbon dioxide as a waste product. Body cells burn food with oxygen and release carbon dioxide, which is then breathed out.
chunks.source: Body cells burn food with oxygen and release carbon dioxide, which is then breathed out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(d) Give the importance of cilia found in the nose during the process of breathing in. A: They trap dust and germs in mucus and sweep them away from the air passages. Cilia are tiny hairs that catch dirt in the mucus and move it out, so clean air enters the lungs.
chunks.source: Cilia are tiny hairs that catch dirt in the mucus and move it out, so clean air enters the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) What term refers to the deposition of eroded soil into water bodies? A: Silting (sedimentation). Eroded soil carried by running water settles at the bottom of lakes and rivers.
chunks.source: Eroded soil carried by running water settles at the bottom of lakes and rivers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(i) In which two ways does uncontrolled bush burning degrade the environment? (i) A: It destroys vegetation, leaving soil bare and open to erosion. Fire burns the plant cover that protects soil from wind and rain.
chunks.source: Fire burns the plant cover that protects soil from wind and rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(ii) In which two ways does uncontrolled bush burning degrade the environment? (ii) A: It kills useful soil organisms and reduces soil fertility. Intense heat destroys the living things that keep the soil fertile.
chunks.source: Intense heat destroys the living things that keep the soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) Give one way in which silting affects fish. A: Silt covers fish breeding grounds and suffocates fish eggs. Deposited silt buries the eggs and makes the water dirty, reducing oxygen for the fish.
chunks.source: Deposited silt buries the eggs and makes the water dirty, reducing oxygen for the fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a) Identify the method of grazing cattle shown in the diagram. A: Paddock grazing. The grazing land is divided into fenced paddocks and animals graze one paddock at a time.
chunks.source: The grazing land is divided into fenced paddocks and animals graze one paddock at a time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b) State any one advantage of the above method of grazing cattle. A: It allows pasture to regrow while animals graze other paddocks (prevents overgrazing). Resting each paddock in turn gives the grass time to recover.
chunks.source: Resting each paddock in turn gives the grass time to recover.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c) How does paddock grazing help to control tick-borne diseases? A: Resting a paddock breaks the tick life cycle, as ticks die without animals to feed on. Ticks left in an empty paddock starve to death, so fewer ticks attack the cattle when they return.
chunks.source: Ticks left in an empty paddock starve to death, so fewer ticks attack the cattle when they return.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(d) State one way in which colostrum is important to a newly born calf. A: It gives the calf immunity against diseases (contains antibodies). The first milk is rich in antibodies that protect the newborn calf from infections.
chunks.source: The first milk is rich in antibodies that protect the newborn calf from infections.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a) How is a pineapple plant similar to a banana in the way they are propagated? A: Both are propagated vegetatively by planting suckers. Pineapples and bananas both grow new plants from suckers rather than from seeds.
chunks.source: Pineapples and bananas both grow new plants from suckers rather than from seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(i) Give two advantages of vegetative propagation over seed propagation. (i) A: Plants mature faster and produce fruit earlier. A sucker or cutting is already a grown part of a plant, so it fruits sooner than a seedling.
chunks.source: A sucker or cutting is already a grown part of a plant, so it fruits sooner than a seedling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(ii) Give two advantages of vegetative propagation over seed propagation. (ii) A: The new plants keep the exact qualities of the parent plant. Vegetative propagation produces identical copies, unlike seeds whose offspring may vary.
chunks.source: Vegetative propagation produces identical copies, unlike seeds whose offspring may vary.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) Which method of seed dispersal involves bursting/splitting of a pod violently due to long exposure to sun heat? A: Explosive mechanism. Dry pods split open suddenly in the sun's heat, throwing the seeds away from the parent plant.
chunks.source: Dry pods split open suddenly in the sun's heat, throwing the seeds away from the parent plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a) Match the part of a flowering plant to its function: Leaves ___. A: Manufacture food for the plant. Leaves make food for the plant during photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Leaves make food for the plant during photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b) Match the part of a flowering plant to its function: Roots ___. A: Absorb plant nutrients from the soil. Roots grow into the soil and absorb water and mineral salts for the plant.
chunks.source: Roots grow into the soil and absorb water and mineral salts for the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c) Match the part of a flowering plant to its function: Stem ___. A: Transports water and mineral salts. The stem carries water and mineral salts from the roots to the leaves.
chunks.source: The stem carries water and mineral salts from the roots to the leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(d) Match the part of a flowering plant to its function: Flowers ___. A: Develop into fruits and seeds. After pollination and fertilization, flowers develop into fruits and seeds.
chunks.source: After pollination and fertilization, flowers develop into fruits and seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a) Name the waste material excreted by the liver. A: Bile pigments. The liver breaks down old red blood cells and excretes bile pigments with the bile.
chunks.source: The liver breaks down old red blood cells and excretes bile pigments with the bile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b) State the role of melanin pigment in the human skin. A: It protects the skin from strong sunshine (ultra-violet rays). Melanin absorbs the sun's ultra-violet rays, shielding the inner layers of the skin.
chunks.source: Melanin absorbs the sun's ultra-violet rays, shielding the inner layers of the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c) State two disorders of the human skin. (i) ___ A: Ringworm. Ringworm is a fungal infection that causes itchy round patches on the skin.
chunks.source: Ringworm is a fungal infection that causes itchy round patches on the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c) State two disorders of the human skin. (ii) ___ A: Scabies. Scabies is a skin infection caused by tiny mites that burrow into the skin.
chunks.source: Scabies is a skin infection caused by tiny mites that burrow into the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a) Give any one reason why light is regarded as a form of energy. A: It can do work, for example it enables green plants to make food. Energy is the ability to do work, and light does work by enabling sight and photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Energy is the ability to do work, and light does work by enabling sight and photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b) In which way do opaque materials affect light? A: They block light and do not allow it to pass through. Opaque materials stop light completely, so a shadow forms behind them.
chunks.source: Opaque materials stop light completely, so a shadow forms behind them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(c) The diagram below shows regular reflection of light. Study it carefully and find the value of g in degrees. A: 62 degrees. In regular reflection the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, so g is 62 degrees.
chunks.source: In regular reflection the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, so g is 62 degrees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a) Name any two examples of anti social behaviours among people in the community. (i) ___ A: Stealing (theft). Stealing harms others and breaks the peace of the community.
chunks.source: Stealing harms others and breaks the peace of the community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a) Name any two examples of anti social behaviours among people in the community. (ii) ___ A: Fighting. Fighting injures people and disturbs peace in the community.
chunks.source: Fighting injures people and disturbs peace in the community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) Mention any two effects of anti social behaviour to school children. (i) ___ A: Children copy the bad behaviour and become indisciplined. When adults behave badly, school children learn and copy those bad habits.
chunks.source: When adults behave badly, school children learn and copy those bad habits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) Mention any two effects of anti social behaviour to school children. (ii) ___ A: It disturbs peace and learning at school. Anti-social behaviour around schools makes the learning environment unsafe.
chunks.source: Anti-social behaviour around schools makes the learning environment unsafe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a) Name the type of a bee hive drawn below. A: A traditional bee hive. A traditional hive is the local type made from logs, bark or woven materials.
chunks.source: A traditional hive is the local type made from logs, bark or woven materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b) How is honey harvesting different from honey extraction? A: Harvesting is removing honeycombs from the hive, while extraction is removing honey from the honeycombs. Harvesting collects the combs from the hive; extraction separates the honey out of those combs.
chunks.source: Harvesting collects the combs from the hive; extraction separates the honey out of those combs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) Give two methods of honey extraction apart from centrifuging method. (i) ___ A: Pressing (squeezing) method. In the pressing method the honeycombs are squeezed to force the honey out.
chunks.source: In the pressing method the honeycombs are squeezed to force the honey out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) Give two methods of honey extraction apart from centrifuging method. (ii) ___ A: Floating (draining) method. In the floating method crushed combs are left so the honey drips out by itself.
chunks.source: In the floating method crushed combs are left so the honey drips out by itself.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a) Name the first set of teeth in babies. A: Milk teeth (deciduous teeth). Babies first grow milk teeth, which later fall out and are replaced by permanent teeth.
chunks.source: Babies first grow milk teeth, which later fall out and are replaced by permanent teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b) How are molars and pre molars adapted to their function? A: They have broad flat tops for grinding and crushing food. Molars and premolars have wide flat ridged surfaces that crush food into small pieces.
chunks.source: Molars and premolars have wide flat ridged surfaces that crush food into small pieces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c) Give two teeth disorders apart from broken teeth. (i) ___ A: Tooth decay (dental cavities). Germs acting on food remains on teeth cause decay and holes called cavities.
chunks.source: Germs acting on food remains on teeth cause decay and holes called cavities.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c) Give two teeth disorders apart from broken teeth. (ii) ___ A: Bleeding gums (gum disease). Poor cleaning of teeth makes the gums swell, sore and bleed.
chunks.source: Poor cleaning of teeth makes the gums swell, sore and bleed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one example of a wild bird. A: A crested crane. Wild birds like the crested crane live freely in swamps and forests.
chunks.source: Wild birds like the crested crane live freely in swamps and forests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of a fish has similar function as stomata on a plant? A: The gills. Gills take in dissolved oxygen for the fish, just as stomata take in air for the plant.
chunks.source: Gills take in dissolved oxygen for the fish, just as stomata take in air for the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of valves in the human heart. A: They prevent the backflow of blood. Valves open and close so that blood flows in one direction only.
chunks.source: Valves open and close so that blood flows in one direction only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is a smoker important to a person harvesting honey? A: It produces smoke that calms the bees. Smoke makes bees calm and less likely to sting during honey harvesting.
chunks.source: Smoke makes bees calm and less likely to sting during honey harvesting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is early sex dangerous to children at school? A: It leads to teenage pregnancy, HIV/AIDS infection and dropping out of school. Early sex exposes children to pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases, ending their schooling.
chunks.source: Early sex exposes children to pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases, ending their schooling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one way mosquitoes can be controlled without using chemicals. A: By sleeping under mosquito nets. Mosquito nets form a physical barrier that stops mosquitoes from biting people at night.
chunks.source: Mosquito nets form a physical barrier that stops mosquitoes from biting people at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one annual crop which is a cereal. A: Maize. Maize is a cereal crop that is planted and harvested within one year.
chunks.source: Maize is a cereal crop that is planted and harvested within one year.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a method of making water clean. Name the method of making water clean shown above. A: Filtration. In filtration, dirty water passes through a filter which traps the dirt particles.
chunks.source: In filtration, dirty water passes through a filter which traps the dirt particles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does mulching control soil erosion? A: Mulches cover the soil and slow down running water. A mulch cover breaks the force of rain and slows runoff, so soil is not washed away.
chunks.source: A mulch cover breaks the force of rain and slows runoff, so soil is not washed away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way in which a farmer can promote easy mating in sheep. A: By keeping the ram together with the ewes on heat. Putting the ram with ewes that are on heat makes mating take place easily.
chunks.source: Putting the ram with ewes that are on heat makes mating take place easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of bee is formed by feeding a grub on royal jelly in its life time? A: The queen bee. A grub fed on royal jelly throughout its life develops into a queen bee.
chunks.source: A grub fed on royal jelly throughout its life develops into a queen bee.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of using dry wood put on the handle of an iron box. A: Dry wood is a poor conductor of heat, so it protects the hand from burns. The wooden handle does not conduct heat from the hot iron box to the hand.
chunks.source: The wooden handle does not conduct heat from the hot iron box to the hand.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do insects with mandibles feed? A: They bite and chew their food. Mandibles are strong jaws that bite off and chew food.
chunks.source: Mandibles are strong jaws that bite off and chew food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which structure enables the trachea to open all the time? A: Rings of cartilage. Rings of cartilage hold the trachea open so that air passes through freely.
chunks.source: Rings of cartilage hold the trachea open so that air passes through freely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way the use of biogas conserves trees in the environment. A: It reduces the cutting down of trees for firewood. Families using biogas for cooking no longer cut trees for firewood.
chunks.source: Families using biogas for cooking no longer cut trees for firewood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a plant. Identify the plant drawn above. A: A cactus. The drawing shows a cactus, a plant with a thick fleshy stem and spines instead of leaves.
chunks.source: The drawing shows a cactus, a plant with a thick fleshy stem and spines instead of leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the above plant adapted to growing in very dry places? A: It has a thick fleshy stem that stores water, and spines that reduce water loss. The cactus stores water in its stem and its spines lose very little water to the air.
chunks.source: The cactus stores water in its stem and its spines lose very little water to the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way bacteria are useful in septic tanks. A: They break down (decompose) the sewage. Bacteria digest the solid waste in septic tanks into harmless liquid.
chunks.source: Bacteria digest the solid waste in septic tanks into harmless liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the energy change that takes place in a dry cell when the circuit is complete. A: Chemical energy to electrical energy. The chemicals inside the dry cell change into electricity when the circuit is complete.
chunks.source: The chemicals inside the dry cell change into electricity when the circuit is complete.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it not good to induce vomiting when one has taken poisons like paraffin? A: Vomiting makes the poison burn the gullet again and it may enter the lungs. Bringing paraffin up burns the throat a second time and the poison may enter the lungs.
chunks.source: Bringing paraffin up burns the throat a second time and the poison may enter the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a dairy farmer identify cows with mastitis infection during milking? A: The milk has clots or blood, and the udder is swollen and painful. Mastitis makes the udder swell and the milk watery with clots.
chunks.source: Mastitis makes the udder swell and the milk watery with clots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one milk breed of goat kept in Uganda. A: Saanen. Saanen is an exotic dairy goat breed kept in Uganda for milk.
chunks.source: Saanen is an exotic dairy goat breed kept in Uganda for milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it necessary to prepare land before the process of planting crops? A: To loosen the soil and remove weeds for proper germination. Prepared land lets seeds germinate easily and roots grow deep.
chunks.source: Prepared land lets seeds germinate easily and roots grow deep.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do plants use oxygen gas during germination process? A: Oxygen is used in respiration to release energy for germination. The germinating seed uses oxygen to release energy from stored food so it can grow.
chunks.source: The germinating seed uses oxygen to release energy from stored food so it can grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the body organ that enables human beings to watch a football match on a television. A: The eyes. We see the match on the television with our eyes.
chunks.source: We see the match on the television with our eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are filarial worms dangerous to people? A: They cause elephantiasis, which swells body parts. Filarial worms block the lymph vessels, causing the swelling called elephantiasis.
chunks.source: Filarial worms block the lymph vessels, causing the swelling called elephantiasis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the immunisable disease that causes paralysis of the limbs. A: Polio. The polio virus attacks the nerves and paralyses the limbs; it is prevented by immunisation.
chunks.source: The polio virus attacks the nerves and paralyses the limbs; it is prevented by immunisation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one way in which a magnet is important to a health worker. A: It is used to remove small iron pieces from a patient's eye. A health worker uses a magnet to pull tiny iron splinters out of the eye.
