chunks.source: A health worker uses a magnet to pull tiny iron splinters out of the eye.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which method of heat transfer helps us in ironing our clothes? A: Conduction. Heat moves by conduction from the hot iron box through to the clothes.
chunks.source: Heat moves by conduction from the hot iron box through to the clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are children advised to participate in P.E activities? A: To keep the body healthy and physically fit. P.E exercises the body, making children strong and healthy.
chunks.source: P.E exercises the body, making children strong and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to a male rabbit? A: A buck. A male rabbit is called a buck, while the female is called a doe.
chunks.source: A male rabbit is called a buck, while the female is called a doe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one way poultry farmers control egg eating in a poultry farm. A: By debeaking the layers. Debeaked birds cannot easily break and eat eggs.
chunks.source: Debeaked birds cannot easily break and eat eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which state of matter is porridge? A: Liquid state. Porridge flows like a liquid, so it is in the liquid state.
chunks.source: Porridge flows like a liquid, so it is in the liquid state.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does drought lead to lack of food in the environment? A: Crops dry up and fail without rain. Without rain, crops wither and die, so there is no food to harvest.
chunks.source: Without rain, crops wither and die, so there is no food to harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from using pesticides, how else can a farmer control pests in a maize garden? A: By practising crop rotation. Rotating crops breaks the life cycle of pests in the garden.
chunks.source: Rotating crops breaks the life cycle of pests in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way a short circuit can be prevented in a house. A: By using a fuse in the circuit. A fuse breaks the circuit when too much current flows through it.
chunks.source: A fuse breaks the circuit when too much current flows through it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way the skeletal system is important to the circulatory system. A: The ribcage protects the heart. Bones shield the heart, which is the main organ of the circulatory system.
chunks.source: Bones shield the heart, which is the main organ of the circulatory system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does refrigeration preserve milk? A: The cold slows down the growth of germs that sour milk. Low temperatures make germs inactive, so milk stays fresh for longer.
chunks.source: Low temperatures make germs inactive, so milk stays fresh for longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Primary Five pupils of Poyem P/S immersed a stone of mass 500g into water and it displaced 25cm3 of water in the measuring cylinder. Calculate the density of the stone. A: 20 g/cm3. Density = mass / volume = 500 g / 25 cm3 = 20 g/cm3.
chunks.source: Density = mass / volume = 500 g / 25 cm3 = 20 g/cm3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why biceps and triceps are called antagonist muscles. A: They work in opposite directions; when one contracts the other relaxes. The biceps bends the arm while the triceps straightens it, so they oppose each other.
chunks.source: The biceps bends the arm while the triceps straightens it, so they oppose each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) The following are components of an electric circuit: battery, fuse, switch, bulb. State the use of: (i) a fuse A: It breaks the circuit when too much current flows, protecting appliances. A fuse melts and breaks the circuit before too much current damages appliances.
chunks.source: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit before too much current damages appliances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) State the use of: (ii) a switch A: It opens and closes the circuit (puts the current on and off). A switch completes or breaks the path of current in a circuit.
chunks.source: A switch completes or breaks the path of current in a circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) State the use of: (iii) battery A: It provides the electrical energy that drives current round the circuit. The battery is the source of electrical energy in the circuit.
chunks.source: The battery is the source of electrical energy in the circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c) State the energy change that takes place in a bulb when a circuit is complete. A: Electrical energy to light and heat energy. The bulb changes electricity into light, and also gives off heat.
chunks.source: The bulb changes electricity into light, and also gives off heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a) Study the diagram below. Name the family planning method shown above. A: Tubal ligation. Tubal ligation is a permanent family planning method in which the oviducts are cut and tied.
chunks.source: Tubal ligation is a permanent family planning method in which the oviducts are cut and tied.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) How does the above method prevent pregnancies? A: The oviducts are cut and tied so eggs cannot meet the sperms. When the oviducts are blocked, the egg cannot meet sperms and fertilization cannot take place.
chunks.source: When the oviducts are blocked, the egg cannot meet sperms and fertilization cannot take place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c) Apart from the above method, give any one other permanent method of family planning. A: Vasectomy. Vasectomy is the permanent family planning method for men, in which the sperm ducts are cut and tied.
chunks.source: Vasectomy is the permanent family planning method for men, in which the sperm ducts are cut and tied.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(d) State one advantage of family planning. A: It enables parents to have only the number of children they can look after. Family planning lets a family raise the children it can feed, clothe and educate.
chunks.source: Family planning lets a family raise the children it can feed, clothe and educate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a) Mention any one crop that can be grown in wetlands. A: Rice. Rice grows well in the wet soils of wetlands.
chunks.source: Rice grows well in the wet soils of wetlands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b) Apart from growing crops mentioned above, give two other ways people destroy wetlands. (i) ___ A: By dumping rubbish in wetlands. Rubbish dumped in wetlands pollutes the water and kills wetland life.
chunks.source: Rubbish dumped in wetlands pollutes the water and kills wetland life.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b) Apart from growing crops mentioned above, give two other ways people destroy wetlands. (ii) ___ A: By digging clay for making bricks. Digging clay destroys the wetland soil and its plants.
chunks.source: Digging clay destroys the wetland soil and its plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c) Write one danger of staying near wetlands. A: People are exposed to mosquitoes and water-borne diseases. Wetlands breed mosquitoes and harbour germs that cause diseases.
chunks.source: Wetlands breed mosquitoes and harbour germs that cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a) The diagram below shows changes of states of matter. Name the physical process marked A. A: Sublimation. Sublimation is the change of a solid directly into a gas.
chunks.source: Sublimation is the change of a solid directly into a gas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a) Name the physical process marked B. A: Melting. Melting is the change of a solid into a liquid.
chunks.source: Melting is the change of a solid into a liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b) What happens to the following when water freezes: (i) Volume? A: It increases. Water expands when it freezes into ice, so its volume increases.
chunks.source: Water expands when it freezes into ice, so its volume increases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b) What happens to the following when water freezes: (ii) Mass? A: It remains the same. Freezing only changes the state of water, not the amount of matter in it.
chunks.source: Freezing only changes the state of water, not the amount of matter in it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a) How is a clinical thermometer important in our daily life? A: It measures body temperature to detect fever. A clinical thermometer shows whether a person has a fever and needs treatment.
chunks.source: A clinical thermometer shows whether a person has a fever and needs treatment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b) Mention one part of a human body where a clinical thermometer is placed to measure temperature. A: In the armpit. The thermometer is held in the armpit to read body temperature.
chunks.source: The thermometer is held in the armpit to read body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c) Why can't clinical thermometers be boiled as a way of sterilizing? A: The boiling heat would make the mercury expand and break the thermometer. Boiling would push the mercury beyond the scale and burst the glass tube.
chunks.source: Boiling would push the mercury beyond the scale and burst the glass tube.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c) Give a reason why alcohol is the best liquid to measure the lowest temperature. A: Alcohol has a very low freezing point. Alcohol stays liquid even in extreme cold, so it can measure very low temperatures.
chunks.source: Alcohol stays liquid even in extreme cold, so it can measure very low temperatures.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) Study the illustrations below (a new knife, and the same knife after seven months). Name the force that made the knife appear as seen in diagram C. A: Rusting. The knife reacted with air and water to form the brown substance called rust.
chunks.source: The knife reacted with air and water to form the brown substance called rust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) Apart from the danger shown above in the diagram, give any two other disadvantages of the force mentioned in (a) above. (i) ___ A: It weakens the metal so tools break easily. Rust eats away iron, making tools weak and likely to break.
chunks.source: Rust eats away iron, making tools weak and likely to break.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) Give any two other disadvantages of the force mentioned in (a) above. (ii) ___ A: It makes sharp tools blunt. A rusted knife loses its sharp edge and cannot cut well.
chunks.source: A rusted knife loses its sharp edge and cannot cut well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c) Write one way greasing prevents the force mentioned above. A: Grease covers the metal and keeps air and water away from it. A layer of grease stops air and water from reaching the iron, so rust cannot form.
chunks.source: A layer of grease stops air and water from reaching the iron, so rust cannot form.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) State any two types of manure. (i) ___ A: Compost manure. Compost manure is made from decayed plant and animal materials.
chunks.source: Compost manure is made from decayed plant and animal materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) State any two types of manure. (ii) ___ A: Farmyard manure. Farmyard manure is made from animal droppings and urine.
chunks.source: Farmyard manure is made from animal droppings and urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b) State one advantage of using artificial fertilizers over natural fertilizers. A: They act faster (are absorbed quickly by crops). Artificial fertilizers dissolve quickly so crops get nutrients within a short time.
chunks.source: Artificial fertilizers dissolve quickly so crops get nutrients within a short time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) Suggest one danger that can result from frequent use of artificial fertilizers. A: They can burn the crops and destroy living organisms in the soil. Too much artificial fertilizer makes the soil acidic and kills useful soil organisms.
chunks.source: Too much artificial fertilizer makes the soil acidic and kills useful soil organisms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48. Study the animals below and match correctly. (i) Kangaroo ___ A: Running away very fast. A kangaroo escapes enemies by hopping away very fast on its strong hind legs.
chunks.source: A kangaroo escapes enemies by hopping away very fast on its strong hind legs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(ii) Cat ___ A: Sharp claws. A cat defends itself and catches prey with its sharp claws.
chunks.source: A cat defends itself and catches prey with its sharp claws.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(iii) Porcupine ___ A: Use of spines. A porcupine protects itself with its sharp spines.
chunks.source: A porcupine protects itself with its sharp spines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(iv) Caterpillar ___ A: Prickly hair. A caterpillar keeps enemies away with its prickly irritating hair.
chunks.source: A caterpillar keeps enemies away with its prickly irritating hair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a) Which type of change takes place when a snake moults? A: Biological change. Moulting is a natural growth process in a living thing, which is a biological change.
chunks.source: Moulting is a natural growth process in a living thing, which is a biological change.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) Give two differences between physical and chemical changes. (i) ___ A: In a physical change no new substance is formed, while in a chemical change a new substance is formed. Physical changes only alter appearance, but chemical changes produce new substances.
chunks.source: Physical changes only alter appearance, but chemical changes produce new substances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) Give two differences between physical and chemical changes. (ii) ___ A: A physical change is reversible while a chemical change is irreversible. A physical change can be undone, but a chemical change cannot easily be reversed.
chunks.source: A physical change can be undone, but a chemical change cannot easily be reversed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c) How do snakes benefit from moulting? A: It allows the snake to grow (the tight old skin is removed). Shedding the old skin gives the growing snake room to increase in size.
chunks.source: Shedding the old skin gives the growing snake room to increase in size.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a) The diagram below shows a food chain: Maize plant, Grasshoppers, Birds, Bacteria. Which of the above components acts as: (i) Primary consumer A: Grasshoppers. Grasshoppers feed directly on the maize plant, so they are primary consumers.
chunks.source: Grasshoppers feed directly on the maize plant, so they are primary consumers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(ii) Decomposer A: Bacteria. Bacteria break down dead plants and animals in the food chain.
chunks.source: Bacteria break down dead plants and animals in the food chain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(iii) Secondary consumer A: Birds. Birds feed on the grasshoppers, so they are secondary consumers.
chunks.source: Birds feed on the grasshoppers, so they are secondary consumers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(iv) Producer A: Maize plant. The maize plant makes its own food, so it is the producer.
chunks.source: The maize plant makes its own food, so it is the producer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a) The diagram below shows an organism under invertebrates. To which group of invertebrates does the above organism belong? A: Arachnids. The organism (a tick) has eight legs and two body parts, which are features of arachnids.
chunks.source: The organism (a tick) has eight legs and two body parts, which are features of arachnids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b) How is part marked W important to the organism shown above? A: It is the mouthpart used for sucking blood from the host. The tick uses its mouthparts to pierce the skin and suck blood.
chunks.source: The tick uses its mouthparts to pierce the skin and suck blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c) Mention any one other organism in the group mentioned in (a) above apart from the one drawn above. A: A spider. Spiders are also arachnids with eight legs.
chunks.source: Spiders are also arachnids with eight legs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(d) Write one danger of the organism drawn above to human health. A: It sucks blood and spreads diseases such as relapsing fever. Ticks feed on human blood and transmit disease germs.
chunks.source: Ticks feed on human blood and transmit disease germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a) The diagram below shows a property of magnets. Identify the property of magnet shown in the diagram above. A: Like poles of magnets repel each other. When two like poles of magnets face each other, they push apart.
chunks.source: When two like poles of magnets face each other, they push apart.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b) State any two methods of making magnets. (i) ___ A: By stroking (single touch method). Stroking a steel bar repeatedly with a magnet in one direction makes it a magnet.
chunks.source: Stroking a steel bar repeatedly with a magnet in one direction makes it a magnet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b) State any two methods of making magnets. (ii) ___ A: By using electricity (electrical method). Passing current through a coil wound round an iron bar makes an electromagnet.
chunks.source: Passing current through a coil wound round an iron bar makes an electromagnet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(c) How can an electro magnet be made stronger? A: By increasing the number of coils (or increasing the current). More turns of wire round the core make the electromagnet stronger.
chunks.source: More turns of wire round the core make the electromagnet stronger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a) Study the intestinal worms below. Identify the worms marked: (i) P A: Tapeworm. The tapeworm is a long flat worm that lives in the intestines.
chunks.source: The tapeworm is a long flat worm that lives in the intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(ii) Q A: Roundworm. The roundworm is a round cylindrical worm found in the intestines.
chunks.source: The roundworm is a round cylindrical worm found in the intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) How does worm marked P enter the body? A: Through eating undercooked (half-cooked) meat. Tapeworm larvae in half-cooked meat develop into worms in the intestines.
chunks.source: Tapeworm larvae in half-cooked meat develop into worms in the intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c) State any one way of preventing worm marked Q. A: By washing hands before eating food. Washing hands removes roundworm eggs before they enter the mouth.
chunks.source: Washing hands removes roundworm eggs before they enter the mouth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a) List any two examples of scavenger birds. (i) ___ A: Marabou stork. The marabou stork feeds on dead animals and rubbish.
chunks.source: The marabou stork feeds on dead animals and rubbish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a) List any two examples of scavenger birds. (ii) ___ A: Vulture. Vultures feed on the flesh of dead animals.
chunks.source: Vultures feed on the flesh of dead animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b) How are scavenger birds important in the environment? A: They eat dead animals (carrion), keeping the environment clean. By removing carcasses, scavenger birds stop diseases from spreading.
chunks.source: By removing carcasses, scavenger birds stop diseases from spreading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) Apart from scavenger birds, give any one group of birds. A: Perching birds. Perching birds, like weaver birds, are another group of birds.
chunks.source: Perching birds, like weaver birds, are another group of birds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a) The diagram below shows types of teeth. Name the type of tooth shown: (i) A A: Incisor. Incisors are the flat front teeth used for cutting food.
chunks.source: Incisors are the flat front teeth used for cutting food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a)(ii) B A: Canine. Canines are the pointed teeth next to the incisors, used for tearing food.
chunks.source: Canines are the pointed teeth next to the incisors, used for tearing food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b) Give the use of the above type of teeth in man. (i) A A: For cutting and biting food. Incisors have sharp edges that cut food into pieces.
chunks.source: Incisors have sharp edges that cut food into pieces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(ii) B A: For tearing food. Canines are pointed so they tear tough food like meat.
chunks.source: Canines are pointed so they tear tough food like meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one example of a flowering plant. A: Maize. Maize is a flowering plant because it produces flowers that develop into grains.
chunks.source: Maize is a flowering plant because it produces flowers that develop into grains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which component of air supports burning? A: Oxygen. Oxygen in the air supports burning; things cannot burn without it.
chunks.source: Oxygen in the air supports burning; things cannot burn without it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one use of water in promoting personal hygiene. A: For bathing (washing the body). Bathing with clean water keeps the body clean and healthy.
chunks.source: Bathing with clean water keeps the body clean and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the type of poultry reared for egg production. A: Layers. Layers are chickens kept specially for laying eggs.
chunks.source: Layers are chickens kept specially for laying eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which element of weather helps in winnowing harvested crops? A: Wind. Wind blows away the light chaff from the heavier grains during winnowing.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the light chaff from the heavier grains during winnowing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows an example of a storage root crop. How is the above crop propagated? A: By planting stem cuttings. Cassava, the storage root crop shown, is propagated by planting pieces of its stem.
chunks.source: Cassava, the storage root crop shown, is propagated by planting pieces of its stem.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the above crop, mention any one other example of a root crop. A: Sweet potatoes. Sweet potatoes are root crops whose swollen roots store food.
chunks.source: Sweet potatoes are root crops whose swollen roots store food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does a drone bee die after mating a queen bee? A: Its reproductive organ is torn off during mating. The drone's abdomen bursts when mating ends, so the drone dies.
chunks.source: The drone's abdomen bursts when mating ends, so the drone dies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of immunity is acquired through taking breast milk? A: Natural passive immunity. The baby receives ready-made antibodies from the mother's milk without making them itself.
chunks.source: The baby receives ready-made antibodies from the mother's milk without making them itself.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the best method of making water safe for drinking. A: By boiling. Boiling kills all the germs in water, making it safe to drink.
chunks.source: Boiling kills all the germs in water, making it safe to drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a dustbin useful in a classroom? A: It keeps rubbish, helping to keep the classroom clean. A dustbin collects waste papers and dirt so the classroom stays clean.
chunks.source: A dustbin collects waste papers and dirt so the classroom stays clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which garden tool is used for light weeding? A: A hand fork. A hand fork is used to dig out small weeds near crops.
chunks.source: A hand fork is used to dig out small weeds near crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one characteristic of a housefly which makes it an insect. A: It has six legs. All insects, including the housefly, have six legs.
chunks.source: All insects, including the housefly, have six legs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of controlling mosquitoes at home. A: By draining stagnant water around the home. Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water, so draining it stops them from multiplying.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water, so draining it stops them from multiplying.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are canine teeth able to tear meat? A: They are sharp and pointed. The sharp pointed shape of canines lets them pierce and tear meat.
chunks.source: The sharp pointed shape of canines lets them pierce and tear meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a head of a tapeworm. Name the part marked K. A: Hooks. The head (scolex) of a tapeworm has hooks that grip the wall of the intestines.
chunks.source: The head (scolex) of a tapeworm has hooks that grip the wall of the intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the above intestinal worm enter our body? A: Through eating undercooked (half-cooked) meat. Tapeworm larvae in half-cooked pork or beef grow into worms in our intestines.
chunks.source: Tapeworm larvae in half-cooked pork or beef grow into worms in our intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one use of honey in industries. A: It is used for making sweets. Factories use honey as a sweetener in sweets and cough syrups.
chunks.source: Factories use honey as a sweetener in sweets and cough syrups.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which disease vector spreads relapsing fever to people? A: Ticks. Ticks bite people and pass on the germs that cause relapsing fever.
chunks.source: Ticks bite people and pass on the germs that cause relapsing fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a moth able to pollinate flowers at night? A: It visits flowers guided by their scent. Night flowers produce a strong scent that attracts moths to pollinate them.
chunks.source: Night flowers produce a strong scent that attracts moths to pollinate them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one reason why animals move from one place to another. A: To look for food. Animals move to places where they can find enough food to eat.
chunks.source: Animals move to places where they can find enough food to eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the difference between a vector and a germ. A: A vector carries and transmits germs, while a germ causes the disease. Vectors like mosquitoes spread germs, but it is the germ that makes a person sick.
chunks.source: Vectors like mosquitoes spread germs, but it is the germ that makes a person sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which food is important to the human body. A: It gives the body energy. Food provides energy that the body uses to work and play.
chunks.source: Food provides energy that the body uses to work and play.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do some objects sink in water? A: Because they are denser (heavier) than water. An object sinks when it is heavier than the same volume of water.
chunks.source: An object sinks when it is heavier than the same volume of water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a maize grain. Name the part marked Y. A: Embryo. The embryo is the young plant inside the maize grain that grows during germination.
chunks.source: The embryo is the young plant inside the maize grain that grows during germination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the function of part marked X to the maize grain above. A: It stores food used by the germinating seed. The endosperm stores starch that feeds the embryo until it can make its own food.
chunks.source: The endosperm stores starch that feeds the embryo until it can make its own food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is rain regarded as the main natural source of water on earth? A: All other natural sources like rivers, wells and springs are fed by rain. Rain fills rivers, lakes and underground water, so it is the mother of all water sources.
chunks.source: Rain fills rivers, lakes and underground water, so it is the mother of all water sources.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a safety pin useful when giving first aid to casualties? A: It fastens bandages and slings in place. A safety pin holds bandages firmly so they do not fall off the wound.
chunks.source: A safety pin holds bandages firmly so they do not fall off the wound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of the spur to a cock. A: It uses it for fighting and protection. A cock fights enemies and rivals using its sharp spurs.
chunks.source: A cock fights enemies and rivals using its sharp spurs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one vaccine given to babies at birth. A: BCG. BCG vaccine protects babies against tuberculosis and is given at birth.
chunks.source: BCG vaccine protects babies against tuberculosis and is given at birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from a leaf, name any one other object that floats on water. A: A piece of dry wood. Dry wood is less dense than water, so it floats.
chunks.source: Dry wood is less dense than water, so it floats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which rabbit disease causes wounds in their ears? A: Ear canker. Ear canker is a rabbit disease that causes sores and wounds in the ears.
chunks.source: Ear canker is a rabbit disease that causes sores and wounds in the ears.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one reason why a passion fruit plant climbs a mango plant. A: To get enough sunlight. Climbing up the mango plant lifts the passion fruit leaves into the sunlight.
chunks.source: Climbing up the mango plant lifts the passion fruit leaves into the sunlight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do earthworms die when oil is poured on them? A: Oil covers their skin so they cannot breathe. Earthworms breathe through their moist skin; oil blocks it and suffocates them.
chunks.source: Earthworms breathe through their moist skin; oil blocks it and suffocates them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one condition which makes bees swarm. A: Overcrowding in the hive. When the hive becomes too crowded, some bees leave with a new queen to form another colony.
chunks.source: When the hive becomes too crowded, some bees leave with a new queen to form another colony.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are plants not able to make their own food at night? A: There is no sunlight for photosynthesis. Photosynthesis needs sunlight, which is absent at night.
chunks.source: Photosynthesis needs sunlight, which is absent at night.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a body structure. Name the body structure shown in the diagram above. A: The heart. The diagram shows the heart, the muscular organ that pumps blood.
chunks.source: The diagram shows the heart, the muscular organ that pumps blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the above structure useful to the body? A: It pumps blood to all parts of the body. The heart pushes blood carrying food and oxygen round the body.
chunks.source: The heart pushes blood carrying food and oxygen round the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which group of insects do not live, move and work together? A: Solitary insects. Unlike social insects such as bees and termites, solitary insects live alone.
chunks.source: Unlike social insects such as bees and termites, solitary insects live alone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the weather instrument used to measure the amount of rainfall received in an area. A: A rain gauge. A rain gauge collects and measures the rain that falls in an area.
chunks.source: A rain gauge collects and measures the rain that falls in an area.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a) Name any two items found in a First Aid box. (i) ___ A: Bandage. A bandage is used to cover and protect wounds.
chunks.source: A bandage is used to cover and protect wounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a) Name any two items found in a First Aid box. (ii) ___ A: Plaster. A plaster covers small cuts to keep out dirt and germs.
chunks.source: A plaster covers small cuts to keep out dirt and germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) Give any two reasons why a casualty is given First Aid. (i) ___ A: To save life. Quick first aid can keep a casualty alive before the doctor arrives.
chunks.source: Quick first aid can keep a casualty alive before the doctor arrives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) Give any two reasons why a casualty is given First Aid. (ii) ___ A: To prevent the condition from becoming worse. First aid stops bleeding and pain from increasing before proper treatment.
chunks.source: First aid stops bleeding and pain from increasing before proper treatment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a) The diagram below shows a flower. Name the parts marked T and U. (i) T A: Anther. The anther is the part of the stamen that produces pollen grains.
chunks.source: The anther is the part of the stamen that produces pollen grains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(ii) U A: Stigma. The stigma is the top of the pistil that receives pollen grains.
chunks.source: The stigma is the top of the pistil that receives pollen grains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) Why is part marked V brightly coloured in some flowers? A: To attract pollinators (insects). Bright petals attract insects which carry pollen from flower to flower.
chunks.source: Bright petals attract insects which carry pollen from flower to flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c) What does part marked W develop into after fertilization? A: A fruit. After fertilization the ovary swells and develops into a fruit.
chunks.source: After fertilization the ovary swells and develops into a fruit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a) Name two solutes used to prepare Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS). (i) ___ A: Salt. Salt replaces the body salts lost during diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Salt replaces the body salts lost during diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a) Name two solutes used to prepare Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS). (ii) ___ A: Sugar. Sugar gives the body energy in the ORS mixture.
chunks.source: Sugar gives the body energy in the ORS mixture.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b) Why should a person preparing Oral Rehydration Solution wash his/her hands first? A: To prevent germs from entering the solution. Dirty hands would add germs to the ORS and make the patient sicker.
chunks.source: Dirty hands would add germs to the ORS and make the patient sicker.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c) Apart from giving Oral Rehydration Solution, state any one other way of treating a dehydrated patient. A: By putting the patient on a drip (intravenous fluids). A drip puts fluids directly into the blood of a severely dehydrated patient.
chunks.source: A drip puts fluids directly into the blood of a severely dehydrated patient.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44. In the table below, Part A shows body organs and Part B has functions of the body organs. Use the functions in Part B to match the body organs below. (i) Skin ___ A: For feeling. The skin feels touch, heat, cold and pain.
chunks.source: The skin feels touch, heat, cold and pain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(ii) Eye ___ A: For seeing. The eyes are used for seeing things around us.
chunks.source: The eyes are used for seeing things around us.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(iii) Tongue ___ A: For tasting. The tongue tastes the food we eat.
chunks.source: The tongue tastes the food we eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(iv) Nose ___ A: For smelling. The nose smells different scents in the air.
chunks.source: The nose smells different scents in the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a) Write down any two examples of food crops. (i) ___ A: Maize. Maize is a food crop grown for its grains which people eat.
chunks.source: Maize is a food crop grown for its grains which people eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a) Write down any two examples of food crops. (ii) ___ A: Beans. Beans are food crops grown for their protein-rich seeds.
chunks.source: Beans are food crops grown for their protein-rich seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b) State any two ways of controlling crop pests in the garden. (i) ___ A: By practising crop rotation. Crop rotation breaks the life cycle of pests in the garden.
chunks.source: Crop rotation breaks the life cycle of pests in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b) State any two ways of controlling crop pests in the garden. (ii) ___ A: By spraying crops with pesticides. Pesticides kill the pests that attack crops.
chunks.source: Pesticides kill the pests that attack crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) List down any two items used to keep our body clean. (i) ___ A: Soap. Soap removes dirt and germs from the body during bathing.
chunks.source: Soap removes dirt and germs from the body during bathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) List down any two items used to keep our body clean. (ii) ___ A: Clean water. Clean water rinses dirt and soap off the body.
chunks.source: Clean water rinses dirt and soap off the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) Give any two ways of keeping our body clean. (i) ___ A: By bathing daily. Daily bathing removes sweat, dirt and germs from the body.
chunks.source: Daily bathing removes sweat, dirt and germs from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) Give any two ways of keeping our body clean. (ii) ___ A: By brushing the teeth. Brushing removes food remains that rot the teeth.
chunks.source: Brushing removes food remains that rot the teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) The diagram below shows a farm practice commonly done by poultry farmers. Name the farm practice shown above. A: Debeaking. Debeaking is the trimming of the beaks of birds to control poultry vices.
chunks.source: Debeaking is the trimming of the beaks of birds to control poultry vices.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b) Mention any two poultry vices controlled by the above farm practice. (i) ___ A: Egg eating. Debeaked birds cannot easily break and eat eggs.
chunks.source: Debeaked birds cannot easily break and eat eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b) Mention any two poultry vices controlled by the above farm practice. (ii) ___ A: Feather pecking (cannibalism). Debeaking stops birds from pecking each other's feathers and flesh.
chunks.source: Debeaking stops birds from pecking each other's feathers and flesh.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) Apart from the above practice, state any one other way of controlling poultry vices in domestic birds. A: By providing enough feed and water. Well-fed birds have no reason to eat eggs or peck each other.
chunks.source: Well-fed birds have no reason to eat eggs or peck each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a) Write down any two types of germs. (i) ___ A: Bacteria. Bacteria are tiny germs that cause diseases like cholera.
chunks.source: Bacteria are tiny germs that cause diseases like cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a) Write down any two types of germs. (ii) ___ A: Viruses. Viruses are germs that cause diseases like measles and HIV/AIDS.
chunks.source: Viruses are germs that cause diseases like measles and HIV/AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b) State any one way in which germs enter our body. A: Through cuts and wounds. Germs enter the blood through open cuts on the skin.
chunks.source: Germs enter the blood through open cuts on the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c) Give any one way of preventing germs from entering our body. A: By covering cuts with a plaster. A plaster seals the cut so germs cannot enter.
chunks.source: A plaster seals the cut so germs cannot enter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a) Mention two methods of harvesting water. (i) ___ A: By using gutters (roof catchment). Gutters collect rain water from the roof into tanks.
chunks.source: Gutters collect rain water from the roof into tanks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a) Mention two methods of harvesting water. (ii) ___ A: By digging water holes. Water holes trap rain water for later use.
chunks.source: Water holes trap rain water for later use.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) State any one way in which a farmer uses water. A: For watering crops (irrigation). Farmers water crops during dry periods to keep them growing.
chunks.source: Farmers water crops during dry periods to keep them growing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c) Why is water important during germination? A: It softens the seed coat and activates the enzymes in the seed. Water makes the seed swell and starts the chemical processes of germination.
chunks.source: Water makes the seed swell and starts the chemical processes of germination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a) The diagram below shows an insect. Name parts marked P and R. (i) P A: Abdomen. The abdomen is the hind part of the insect's body.
chunks.source: The abdomen is the hind part of the insect's body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(ii) R A: Antenna. The antennae are feelers on the insect's head used for sensing.
chunks.source: The antennae are feelers on the insect's head used for sensing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b) State the function of part marked O to an insect. A: For seeing. The eyes (O) enable the insect to see its surroundings.
chunks.source: The eyes (O) enable the insect to see its surroundings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c) Which part of a fish has the same function as part marked S? A: Gills. Part S is the spiracle used for breathing, just as gills are used by fish for breathing.
chunks.source: Part S is the spiracle used for breathing, just as gills are used by fish for breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a) Mention any two diseases that attack rabbits. (i) ___ A: Coccidiosis. Coccidiosis is a deadly disease of rabbits that causes diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Coccidiosis is a deadly disease of rabbits that causes diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a) Mention any two diseases that attack rabbits. (ii) ___ A: Ear canker. Ear canker causes sores and wounds in rabbits' ears.
chunks.source: Ear canker causes sores and wounds in rabbits' ears.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b) Give any one way of preventing diseases in rabbits. A: By keeping the hutches clean. Clean hutches keep away the germs that cause rabbit diseases.
chunks.source: Clean hutches keep away the germs that cause rabbit diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c) Why should rabbits be given a block of salt to lick? A: To get mineral salts needed for a healthy body. Licking the salt block gives rabbits minerals for strong bones and good health.
chunks.source: Licking the salt block gives rabbits minerals for strong bones and good health.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a) Give any two pieces of information found on a child health card. (i) ___ A: The child's name. The health card records the name of the child for identification.
chunks.source: The health card records the name of the child for identification.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a) Give any two pieces of information found on a child health card. (ii) ___ A: The child's immunisation record. The card shows which vaccines the child has received and which are remaining.
chunks.source: The card shows which vaccines the child has received and which are remaining.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b) Give any one use of a child health card to each of the following people. (i) doctor A: It helps the doctor to know the child's immunisation history. The doctor reads the card to see which vaccines the child still needs.
chunks.source: The doctor reads the card to see which vaccines the child still needs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(ii) parent A: It reminds the parent when to take the child for the next immunisation. The parent follows the dates on the card for return visits.
chunks.source: The parent follows the dates on the card for return visits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a) Which type of soil is used for: (i) making pots A: Clay soil. Clay soil is sticky and can be moulded into pots.
chunks.source: Clay soil is sticky and can be moulded into pots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(ii) growing crops A: Loam soil. Loam soil is fertile and best for growing crops.
chunks.source: Loam soil is fertile and best for growing crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) State any one way how soil is formed. A: By weathering of rocks. Rocks break down into small particles that form soil.
chunks.source: Rocks break down into small particles that form soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c) Apart from soil, mention any one other component of the environment. A: Air. Air is another component of the environment around us.
chunks.source: Air is another component of the environment around us.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a) The diagram below shows part of the alimentary canal. Name the parts marked M and N. (i) M A: Oesophagus (gullet). The oesophagus carries chewed food from the mouth to the stomach.
chunks.source: The oesophagus carries chewed food from the mouth to the stomach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(ii) N A: Small intestine. The small intestine is where digestion ends and digested food is absorbed.
chunks.source: The small intestine is where digestion ends and digested food is absorbed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b) State the function of part marked O during digestion. A: It produces digestive juices (enzymes) that digest food. Part O (the pancreas) makes enzymes that break down food in the small intestine.
chunks.source: Part O (the pancreas) makes enzymes that break down food in the small intestine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) On the diagram of the alimentary canal above, which part should be labelled K (the stomach)? A: The wide muscular sac between the oesophagus and the small intestine. The stomach is the J-shaped sac where food is churned and mixed with enzymes.
chunks.source: The stomach is the J-shaped sac where food is churned and mixed with enzymes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a) What food deficiency disease is caused due to lack of each of the following food values in the body? (i) iodine A: Goitre. Lack of iodine causes the thyroid gland to swell, forming a goitre.
chunks.source: Lack of iodine causes the thyroid gland to swell, forming a goitre.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a)(ii) vitamin C A: Scurvy. Lack of vitamin C causes scurvy, with bleeding gums and weak joints.
chunks.source: Lack of vitamin C causes scurvy, with bleeding gums and weak joints.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b) Give any two modern methods of preserving food. (i) ___ A: Refrigeration. Refrigeration keeps food cold so germs cannot spoil it quickly.
chunks.source: Refrigeration keeps food cold so germs cannot spoil it quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b) Give any two modern methods of preserving food. (ii) ___ A: Canning (tinning). Canning seals food in airtight tins so it stays fresh for long.
chunks.source: Canning seals food in airtight tins so it stays fresh for long.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the human body organ that uses sound energy for its function. A: The ears. We hear sound with our ears.
chunks.source: We hear sound with our ears.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one importance of school demonstration gardens. A: They help pupils to learn farming practically. In demonstration gardens pupils practise what they learn about crops.
chunks.source: In demonstration gardens pupils practise what they learn about crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of life cycle does a tsetse fly undergo? A: Complete life cycle (complete metamorphosis). A tsetse fly passes through the egg, larva, pupa and adult stages.
chunks.source: A tsetse fly passes through the egg, larva, pupa and adult stages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should water for drinking be boiled at school? A: To kill the germs in it. Boiling destroys the germs that cause water-borne diseases.
chunks.source: Boiling destroys the germs that cause water-borne diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagrams below are of weather instruments A and B. Why is it advisable for the above instruments to be put in an open place? A: So that they can measure the true weather elements of the area. In an open place the instruments freely catch rain and wind without obstruction.
chunks.source: In an open place the instruments freely catch rain and wind without obstruction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the difference in the functions of weather instruments A and B. A: Instrument A measures the amount of rainfall while instrument B shows the direction of wind. A rain gauge collects rainfall, while a wind vane points to where the wind comes from.
chunks.source: A rain gauge collects rainfall, while a wind vane points to where the wind comes from.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one importance of having enough sleeping and resting time to a P.7 candidate during this COVID 19 period. A: It keeps the body healthy and strong to fight diseases. Enough rest builds the body's strength against infections like COVID-19.
chunks.source: Enough rest builds the body's strength against infections like COVID-19.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one condition necessary for poultry eggs to hatch properly. A: Warmth (suitable temperature). Eggs need steady warmth for the chick to develop inside.
chunks.source: Eggs need steady warmth for the chick to develop inside.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does prolonged breast feeding help in child spacing during this period of corona virus outbreak? A: It delays the mother's fertility and prevents pregnancy. Breast feeding for a long time naturally spaces births by delaying pregnancy.
chunks.source: Breast feeding for a long time naturally spaces births by delaying pregnancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should every home have a plate stand? A: To keep plates clean, dry and away from germs. A plate stand holds plates off the ground where they stay clean.
chunks.source: A plate stand holds plates off the ground where they stay clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a type of thermometer. Why is part Q made of a metal? A: Metal is a good conductor of heat, so it quickly passes heat to the liquid inside. The metal part conducts body heat fast to the thermometric liquid for a quick reading.
chunks.source: The metal part conducts body heat fast to the thermometric liquid for a quick reading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the importance of shaking the thermometer after use? A: To bring the mercury back below the constriction (reset it for the next reading). Shaking forces the mercury past the kink back into the bulb, ready for the next person.
chunks.source: Shaking forces the mercury past the kink back into the bulb, ready for the next person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part of the eye which receives images. A: The retina. Light images fall on the retina at the back of the eye.
chunks.source: Light images fall on the retina at the back of the eye.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does paddock system of grazing cattle control tick borne diseases? A: Cattle are moved away before ticks mature, breaking the tick life cycle. Rotating cattle between paddocks starves the ticks, which die without hosts.
chunks.source: Rotating cattle between paddocks starves the ticks, which die without hosts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the disease that is caused by corona virus in our communities today? A: COVID-19. COVID-19 is the disease caused by the corona virus spreading in communities.
chunks.source: COVID-19 is the disease caused by the corona virus spreading in communities.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one form of weather. A: Sunny. Sunny is one form of weather, alongside rainy, windy and cloudy.
chunks.source: Sunny is one form of weather, alongside rainy, windy and cloudy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should water be kept in a first aid box? A: For washing wounds. Clean water in the first aid box is used to wash dirt from wounds.
chunks.source: Clean water in the first aid box is used to wash dirt from wounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Use the diagram below to answer questions 18 and 19. Name the type of leaf venation in the diagram. A: Network (net) venation. The veins branch like a net across the leaf, which is network venation.
chunks.source: The veins branch like a net across the leaf, which is network venation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one crop with similar roots as the ones shown in the diagram. A: Beans. Beans have a taproot system like the roots shown in the diagram.
chunks.source: Beans have a taproot system like the roots shown in the diagram.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the body organ where gaseous exchange takes place. A: The lungs. Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged in the lungs during breathing.
chunks.source: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged in the lungs during breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one example of an animal that navigates by the use of echoes apart from bats. A: A dolphin. Dolphins send out sounds and listen to the echoes to find their way in water.
chunks.source: Dolphins send out sounds and listen to the echoes to find their way in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why weaning babies are said to be vulnerable? A: They no longer get the protective antibodies from breast milk. After weaning, babies lose the immunity passed through breast milk and fall sick easily.
chunks.source: After weaning, babies lose the immunity passed through breast milk and fall sick easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What form of energy is turned into hydro electricity? A: Kinetic energy (of running water). The moving water's kinetic energy turns turbines to make hydro electricity.
chunks.source: The moving water's kinetic energy turns turbines to make hydro electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the type of soil erosion that is caused by the rain drops as they hit the soil directly. A: Splash erosion. Falling raindrops splash soil particles away, which is called splash erosion.
chunks.source: Falling raindrops splash soil particles away, which is called splash erosion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one cause of eye defects. A: Looking directly at bright light (the sun). Staring at the sun damages the eyes and causes defects.
chunks.source: Staring at the sun damages the eyes and causes defects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What food value is got from eating fruits? A: Vitamins. Fruits are rich in vitamins that protect the body against diseases.
chunks.source: Fruits are rich in vitamins that protect the body against diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the difference between drowning and near drowning. A: In drowning the victim dies, while in near drowning the victim survives. Drowning ends in death, but a near-drowning victim is rescued alive.
chunks.source: Drowning ends in death, but a near-drowning victim is rescued alive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way can tins containing water be a danger in our environment? A: They act as breeding places for mosquitoes. Tins holding water give mosquitoes a place to lay their eggs.
chunks.source: Tins holding water give mosquitoes a place to lay their eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows an important body organ protected by the human skeleton. Write down one danger of damaging the above body organ. A: It may lead to death. The brain controls the whole body, so damaging it can kill a person.
chunks.source: The brain controls the whole body, so damaging it can kill a person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part of the skeleton that protects part marked X. A: The skull (cranium). The skull is the bony case that protects the brain.
chunks.source: The skull is the bony case that protects the brain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one mineral deficiency disease in infants. A: Anaemia (lack of iron). Babies lacking iron in food suffer from anaemia.
chunks.source: Babies lacking iron in food suffer from anaemia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the process by which water and mineral salts enter the plant roots. A: Osmosis. Water moves into root hairs from the soil by osmosis.
chunks.source: Water moves into root hairs from the soil by osmosis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a single fixed pulley similar to the first class lever? A: Both change the direction of the applied force, making work easier. A fixed pulley and a first-class lever both reverse the direction of effort.
chunks.source: A fixed pulley and a first-class lever both reverse the direction of effort.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the Alpine goats, give one other exotic breed of goat reared for milk production. A: Saanen. Saanen is another exotic dairy goat breed kept for milk.
chunks.source: Saanen is another exotic dairy goat breed kept for milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a switch useful in a circuit? A: It opens and closes the circuit. A switch puts the current on or off in a circuit.
chunks.source: A switch puts the current on or off in a circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one importance of health parades in a school. A: They promote cleanliness and smartness among pupils. Health parades encourage pupils to keep their bodies and clothes clean.
chunks.source: Health parades encourage pupils to keep their bodies and clothes clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is air called matter? A: Because it has weight and occupies space. Like all matter, air has weight and takes up space.
chunks.source: Like all matter, air has weight and takes up space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the space below, draw a simple serrated leaf. A: A leaf outline with a toothed (saw-like) edge, a stalk and a midrib with veins. A serrated leaf has a margin with sharp teeth like a saw blade.
chunks.source: A serrated leaf has a margin with sharp teeth like a saw blade.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the occurrence of lightning important to farmers? A: It helps to add nitrogen to the soil, making it fertile. Lightning makes nitrogen in the air dissolve in rain, which carries it into the soil.
chunks.source: Lightning makes nitrogen in the air dissolve in rain, which carries it into the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides stem tubers, give any two other plants with swollen storage organs. A: Carrots and sweet potatoes. Carrots and sweet potatoes store food in their swollen roots.
chunks.source: Carrots and sweet potatoes store food in their swollen roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41. Match the following animals to their ways of adaptation to the environment. (a) Chameleon ___ A: Camouflage. A chameleon changes its colour to hide from enemies.
chunks.source: A chameleon changes its colour to hide from enemies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) Millipede ___ A: Curling. A millipede curls into a ball to protect itself from enemies.
chunks.source: A millipede curls into a ball to protect itself from enemies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c) Hedgehog ___ A: Spines. A hedgehog's sharp spines keep enemies away.
chunks.source: A hedgehog's sharp spines keep enemies away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(d) Polar bear ___ A: Thick fur. A polar bear's thick fur keeps it warm in the cold.
chunks.source: A polar bear's thick fur keeps it warm in the cold.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a) Why is COVID 19 taken as a dangerous disease in Uganda today? A: It spreads very fast and kills many people. COVID-19 passes easily from person to person and has caused many deaths.
chunks.source: COVID-19 passes easily from person to person and has caused many deaths.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) State any two community related activities that have caused COVID 19 in our homes today. (i) ___ A: Attending crowded gatherings (burials, parties). Crowded gatherings bring infected and healthy people together, spreading the virus.
chunks.source: Crowded gatherings bring infected and healthy people together, spreading the virus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) State any two community related activities that have caused COVID 19 in our homes today. (ii) ___ A: Shaking hands and hugging. Body contact passes the virus from an infected person to a healthy one.
chunks.source: Body contact passes the virus from an infected person to a healthy one.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c) How are children able to control the high rate spread of COVID 19 in schools? A: By wearing face masks and washing hands regularly. Masks and hand washing stop the virus from moving between children.
chunks.source: Masks and hand washing stop the virus from moving between children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a) How can blindness be caused among people? A: Through eye infections such as trachoma. Untreated eye infections like trachoma can destroy sight.
chunks.source: Untreated eye infections like trachoma can destroy sight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b) How important are the following parts of the eye in the process of seeing? (i) optic nerves A: They carry image messages from the eye to the brain. The optic nerves pass what the eye sees to the brain for interpretation.
chunks.source: The optic nerves pass what the eye sees to the brain for interpretation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(ii) retina A: It receives the light images and forms the picture. Images from the lens fall on the retina, which starts the process of seeing.
chunks.source: Images from the lens fall on the retina, which starts the process of seeing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c) Give one eye disease. A: Trachoma. Trachoma is an eye infection that can lead to blindness if untreated.
chunks.source: Trachoma is an eye infection that can lead to blindness if untreated.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a) Outline two types of bee hives. (i) ___ A: Traditional hive. A traditional hive is the local type made from logs or woven materials.
chunks.source: A traditional hive is the local type made from logs or woven materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a) Outline two types of bee hives. (ii) ___ A: Box (modern) hive. A box hive is the modern type made of timber boxes.
chunks.source: A box hive is the modern type made of timber boxes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b) Give one advantage of growing flowering plants near a bee hive. A: Bees get nectar easily and make more honey. Nearby flowers give bees plenty of nectar for honey making.
chunks.source: Nearby flowers give bees plenty of nectar for honey making.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c) Identify one material bees collect from trees to repair hives. A: Propolis (bee glue). Bees collect the sticky propolis from tree buds to seal cracks in the hive.
chunks.source: Bees collect the sticky propolis from tree buds to seal cracks in the hive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a) Why can't sound travel through a vacuum? A: There are no particles in a vacuum to carry the sound vibrations. Sound needs a material medium whose particles vibrate; a vacuum has none.
chunks.source: Sound needs a material medium whose particles vibrate; a vacuum has none.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b) Give one way echoes are useful to pilots of ships. A: They help to detect obstacles and measure the depth of the sea. Echoes bouncing back tell the pilot how far objects or the sea bed are.
chunks.source: Echoes bouncing back tell the pilot how far objects or the sea bed are.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c) Write down one disadvantage of echoes in our environment. A: They disturb clear hearing and communication. Repeated echoes confuse listeners and spoil speeches and music.
chunks.source: Repeated echoes confuse listeners and spoil speeches and music.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(d) How are echoes prevented in theatres and halls? A: By fixing soft materials like curtains and cushions on the walls to absorb sound. Soft wall coverings absorb sound instead of reflecting it back as echoes.
chunks.source: Soft wall coverings absorb sound instead of reflecting it back as echoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46. Below are drawings of certain garden tools. Identify a correct statement from the list below to show the use of each tool to a farmer. (a) Tool A A: For collecting rubbish. Tool A (a rake) is used for collecting rubbish in the garden.
chunks.source: Tool A (a rake) is used for collecting rubbish in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) Tool B A: For spraying crops. Tool B (a spray pump) is used for spraying crops with pesticides.
chunks.source: Tool B (a spray pump) is used for spraying crops with pesticides.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c) Tool C A: For turning manure. Tool C (a garden fork) is used for turning manure.
chunks.source: Tool C (a garden fork) is used for turning manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(d) Tool D A: For transplanting seedlings. Tool D (a trowel) is used for transplanting seedlings.
chunks.source: Tool D (a trowel) is used for transplanting seedlings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) How are renewable resources different from non-renewable resources? A: Renewable resources can be replaced naturally, while non-renewable resources cannot be replaced once used up. Resources like trees grow again, but minerals like oil get finished forever.
chunks.source: Resources like trees grow again, but minerals like oil get finished forever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b) What type of energy is produced by the following: (i) Uranium A: Nuclear energy. Uranium atoms split to release nuclear energy.
chunks.source: Uranium atoms split to release nuclear energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(ii) Water waves A: Hydro electricity. Moving water turns turbines to produce hydro electricity.
chunks.source: Moving water turns turbines to produce hydro electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(iii) Sun A: Solar energy. The sun gives out solar energy which panels change into electricity.
chunks.source: The sun gives out solar energy which panels change into electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a) Name the electrical symbol shown below. A: A fuse. The symbol shown represents a fuse in a circuit diagram.
chunks.source: The symbol shown represents a fuse in a circuit diagram.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c) State one advantage of fuses. A: They protect appliances from damage by too much current. A fuse breaks the circuit before excess current destroys appliances.
chunks.source: A fuse breaks the circuit before excess current destroys appliances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(d) Mention any two reasons why a fuse may break or blow. (i) ___ A: Short circuit. A short circuit sends too much current through the fuse, blowing it.
chunks.source: A short circuit sends too much current through the fuse, blowing it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(d) Mention any two reasons why a fuse may break or blow. (ii) ___ A: Overloading the circuit. Connecting too many appliances overloads the circuit and blows the fuse.
chunks.source: Connecting too many appliances overloads the circuit and blows the fuse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a) Complete the table below correctly. (i) Light / sunlight -> ___ tropism A: Phototropism. Phototropism is the growth response of a plant towards light.
chunks.source: Phototropism is the growth response of a plant towards light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(ii) ___ -> Hydrotropism A: Water. Hydrotropism is the growth response of roots towards water.
chunks.source: Hydrotropism is the growth response of roots towards water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(iii) ___ -> Geotropism A: Gravity. Geotropism is the growth response of a plant towards gravity.
chunks.source: Geotropism is the growth response of a plant towards gravity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) State one way plants control water loss during long dry season. A: By shedding their leaves. Dropping leaves reduces the surface through which water is lost.
chunks.source: Dropping leaves reduces the surface through which water is lost.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a) What scientific term is used to refer to broken or cracked bone in the body? A: Fracture. Any break or crack in a bone is scientifically called a fracture.
chunks.source: Any break or crack in a bone is scientifically called a fracture.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b) Give one sign that can be used to identify a person with a cracked bone in his or her body. A: Swelling and severe pain at the injured part. A cracked bone swells and pains the victim when touched or moved.
chunks.source: A cracked bone swells and pains the victim when touched or moved.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c) State the first aid given to a person who has got a cracked bone. A: Tie a splint to keep the broken part still. A splint stops the broken bone from moving before the victim reaches hospital.
chunks.source: A splint stops the broken bone from moving before the victim reaches hospital.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(d) Name the type of broken bone shown in the diagram below. A: Simple fracture. In a simple fracture the bone breaks cleanly into two without piercing the skin.
chunks.source: In a simple fracture the bone breaks cleanly into two without piercing the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a) What do we call a mixture of two or more metals? A: An alloy. Metals mixed together form a stronger material called an alloy.
chunks.source: Metals mixed together form a stronger material called an alloy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b) Give one example of a common mixture of metals. A: Brass. Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc used for taps and ornaments.
chunks.source: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc used for taps and ornaments.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c) How does heat move from one point of a metal to another? A: By conduction. In metals, heat travels from the hot end to the cold end by conduction.
chunks.source: In metals, heat travels from the hot end to the cold end by conduction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(d) Apart from painting, give any other method of preventing metallic objects from rusting. A: By oiling (greasing). Oil covers the metal and keeps air and water away, so rust cannot form.
chunks.source: Oil covers the metal and keeps air and water away, so rust cannot form.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a) The diagrams below show percussion musical drums of three different sizes. Which drum will produce sound with the: (i) Highest pitch A: The smallest drum. A smaller drum skin vibrates faster, producing a higher pitch.
chunks.source: A smaller drum skin vibrates faster, producing a higher pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(ii) lowest pitch A: The biggest drum. A bigger drum skin vibrates more slowly, producing a lower pitch.
chunks.source: A bigger drum skin vibrates more slowly, producing a lower pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b) What makes the drum given in (a)(i) above produce a high pitch? A: Its small skin vibrates faster. Fast vibrations of the small drum skin produce a high-pitched sound.
chunks.source: Fast vibrations of the small drum skin produce a high-pitched sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(c) Apart from drums, mention any other percussion instrument that produces sound. A: A xylophone. A xylophone is struck to produce musical sound like a drum.
chunks.source: A xylophone is struck to produce musical sound like a drum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53. Study the list of common crops below: Millet, Tea, Beans, Cotton. (a) Which of the above crops is grown and harvested more than once? A: Tea. Tea is a perennial crop whose leaves are plucked many times over years.
chunks.source: Tea is a perennial crop whose leaves are plucked many times over years.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) Which of the crops above is a raw material to the textile industry? A: Cotton. Cotton fibres are spun into thread for making cloth.
chunks.source: Cotton fibres are spun into thread for making cloth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c) Mention two ways we can care for our crops. (i) ___ A: By weeding. Weeding removes unwanted plants that compete with crops.
chunks.source: Weeding removes unwanted plants that compete with crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c) Mention two ways we can care for our crops. (ii) ___ A: By spraying against pests. Spraying kills pests that would destroy the crops.
chunks.source: Spraying kills pests that would destroy the crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a) The diagram below shows one of the human body organs. Name the part labeled T. A: Renal pelvis. The renal pelvis collects urine from the kidney into the ureter.
chunks.source: The renal pelvis collects urine from the kidney into the ureter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b) State the difference between blood carried by vessel Y and blood carried by vessel Z. A: Vessel Y carries oxygenated blood with wastes to the kidney, while vessel Z carries filtered deoxygenated blood away from the kidney. The renal artery brings dirty oxygenated blood in, and the renal vein takes clean blood away.
chunks.source: The renal artery brings dirty oxygenated blood in, and the renal vein takes clean blood away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) Mention one disease that can cause the blockage of part P. A: Kidney stones. Kidney stones can block the ureter and stop urine from flowing.
chunks.source: Kidney stones can block the ureter and stop urine from flowing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) How can such blockage be avoided in humans? A: By drinking plenty of clean water. Enough water dilutes urine and flushes out substances that form stones.
chunks.source: Enough water dilutes urine and flushes out substances that form stones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a) Why is a knife regarded as a simple machine? A: Because it is a wedge that makes cutting work easier. A knife is a wedge, one of the six simple machines, which simplifies work.
chunks.source: A knife is a wedge, one of the six simple machines, which simplifies work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b) Give one advantage of machines to people. A: They make work easier and faster. Machines reduce the effort and time needed to do work.
chunks.source: Machines reduce the effort and time needed to do work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c) Find the weight at K. (A lever has 50kg at 8cm on one side of the fulcrum and K at 4cm on the other side.) A: 100 kg. 50 kg x 8 cm = K x 4 cm, so K = 400 / 4 = 100 kg.
chunks.source: 50 kg x 8 cm = K x 4 cm, so K = 400 / 4 = 100 kg.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention the class of food that is necessary for steaming up a pregnant cows. A: Proteins (body-building foods). Proteins build the calf's body and prepare the cow for milk production.
chunks.source: Proteins build the calf's body and prepare the cow for milk production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way man has used the process of condensation. A: To get pure water by distillation. In distillation, steam is condensed back into pure liquid water.
chunks.source: In distillation, steam is condensed back into pure liquid water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Point out one substance needed by plants during photosynthesis and germination. A: Water. Plants need water both to make food and to start germination.
chunks.source: Plants need water both to make food and to start germination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The farming practice below shows one of the care given to seedlings after transplanting. Why does a farmer provide shelter to the seedling after transplanting? A: To protect it from direct sunshine (prevent wilting). Shade keeps the tender seedling cool so it does not dry up and die.
chunks.source: Shade keeps the tender seedling cool so it does not dry up and die.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the movement of the larva stage of a mosquito different from that of the adult mosquito? A: The larva (wriggler) swims in water while the adult flies in air. Mosquito larvae live and wriggle in water, but adults fly about in the air.
chunks.source: Mosquito larvae live and wriggle in water, but adults fly about in the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which method of obtaining wood for timber involves cutting a tree at an angle to a stump level? A: Felling. In felling, the tree is cut at an angle so that it falls in the wanted direction.
chunks.source: In felling, the tree is cut at an angle so that it falls in the wanted direction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one of the long bones found below the knee. A: Tibia (shin bone). The tibia is the long bone of the lower leg below the knee.
chunks.source: The tibia is the long bone of the lower leg below the knee.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Point out one activity that can be done during community clean up campaign. A: Slashing bushes. Slashing overgrown bushes keeps the community clean and safe.
chunks.source: Slashing overgrown bushes keeps the community clean and safe.

chunks.subject: Science
