chunks.text: Q: Why doesn't wood burn to ash during the making of charcoal? A: Because the supply of air (oxygen) is limited. With little oxygen, wood chars into charcoal instead of burning fully to ash.
chunks.source: With little oxygen, wood chars into charcoal instead of burning fully to ash.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which system of poultry keeping keeps eggs away from layers? A: Battery (cage) system. In the battery system eggs roll away from the caged layers as soon as they are laid.
chunks.source: In the battery system eggs roll away from the caged layers as soon as they are laid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is reproduction of a moss plant different from that of a maize plant? A: A moss plant reproduces by spores while a maize plant reproduces by seeds. Mosses have no flowers or seeds; they multiply using tiny spores.
chunks.source: Mosses have no flowers or seeds; they multiply using tiny spores.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which substance is suitable for sterilizing a clinical thermometer? A: Methylated spirit (alcohol). Methylated spirit kills germs on the thermometer without damaging it.
chunks.source: Methylated spirit kills germs on the thermometer without damaging it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should one wash hands before preparing sugar salt solution? A: To prevent germs from entering the solution. Dirty hands would contaminate the solution given to the patient.
chunks.source: Dirty hands would contaminate the solution given to the patient.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What term is used to describe the upward movement of water through soil? A: Capillarity. Capillarity pulls water up through the tiny spaces in the soil.
chunks.source: Capillarity pulls water up through the tiny spaces in the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do double silvered walls in a thermos flask prevent heat loss? A: They reflect heat radiation back into the flask. The shiny silvered walls bounce heat rays back, keeping the contents hot.
chunks.source: The shiny silvered walls bounce heat rays back, keeping the contents hot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are farmers encouraged to harvest rain water? A: To have water for use during the dry season. Stored rain water helps farmers when rains fail.
chunks.source: Stored rain water helps farmers when rains fail.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the awareness of communicable diseases important in our community? A: It helps people to prevent and control their spread. Knowing how diseases spread helps the community to stop them.
chunks.source: Knowing how diseases spread helps the community to stop them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which group of succulent fruits do tomatoes belong? A: Berries. Tomatoes are berries because their fleshy wall encloses many seeds.
chunks.source: Tomatoes are berries because their fleshy wall encloses many seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from drying clothes, why should clothes be hanged on a line in the sunshine on a hot day? A: The sunshine kills germs in the clothes. Strong sunshine disinfects clothes by killing germs on them.
chunks.source: Strong sunshine disinfects clothes by killing germs on them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is propagation of bananas similar to that of pineapples? A: Both are propagated by suckers. Bananas and pineapples both grow from suckers shoots.
chunks.source: Bananas and pineapples both grow from suckers shoots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which method of making water safe for drinking is commonly used by national water and sewerage cooperation? A: Chlorination. National Water adds chlorine to kill germs in piped water.
chunks.source: National Water adds chlorine to kill germs in piped water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which vector spreads the filarial worm that cause river blindness? A: Blackfly. The blackfly bites people and spreads the worms that cause river blindness.
chunks.source: The blackfly bites people and spreads the worms that cause river blindness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of screening blood before transfusion. A: To prevent the spread of HIV/AIDS and other infections. Screened blood is free from germs that would infect the receiver.
chunks.source: Screened blood is free from germs that would infect the receiver.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Point out one method of controlling weeds in a garden. A: By uprooting (hand pulling). Pulling weeds out by hand removes them completely from the garden.
chunks.source: Pulling weeds out by hand removes them completely from the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do ticks feed on? A: Blood. Ticks suck blood from animals and people.
chunks.source: Ticks suck blood from animals and people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the role of ligaments in a human skeleton. A: They join bones to bones at joints. Ligaments are tough bands that hold bones together at joints.
chunks.source: Ligaments are tough bands that hold bones together at joints.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which disease makes rabbits have wounds in the ears? A: Ear canker. Ear canker causes sores and wounds in rabbits' ears.
chunks.source: Ear canker causes sores and wounds in rabbits' ears.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a health habit practised by people in the community. How does the health habit above prevent the spread of diarrhoeal diseases? A: Washing hands with soap removes the germs that cause diarrhoea. Clean hands cannot carry diarrhoea germs to food and mouths.
chunks.source: Clean hands cannot carry diarrhoea germs to food and mouths.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why can't tilapia survive long on land? A: It breathes through gills which need water to work. Tilapia's gills can only absorb oxygen from water, not from air.
chunks.source: Tilapia's gills can only absorb oxygen from water, not from air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides absorption of digested food, what other process takes place in the ileum? A: Digestion of food is completed there. Enzymes in the ileum finish breaking down food before it is absorbed.
chunks.source: Enzymes in the ileum finish breaking down food before it is absorbed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are lactating cows fed on dairy meal? A: To increase milk production. Dairy meal gives milking cows the nutrients needed to produce more milk.
chunks.source: Dairy meal gives milking cows the nutrients needed to produce more milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one similarity between sound and light energy? A: Both are forms of energy that travel in waves. Sound and light both move from place to place as waves.
chunks.source: Sound and light both move from place to place as waves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Point out one way of keeping the respiratory system in the good health condition. A: By avoiding smoking. Smoke damages the lungs, so avoiding it keeps the breathing system healthy.
chunks.source: Smoke damages the lungs, so avoiding it keeps the breathing system healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker than that of the right ventricle? A: It pumps blood to the whole body, a longer distance. The left ventricle needs a stronger muscle to push blood round the entire body.
chunks.source: The left ventricle needs a stronger muscle to push blood round the entire body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should girls who have started experiencing menstruation cycles abstain from sex? A: To avoid teenage pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases. After menstruation begins, sex can lead to pregnancy and infections.
chunks.source: After menstruation begins, sex can lead to pregnancy and infections.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from determining the colour of the skin, how else is melanin important to the body? A: It protects the skin from strong sunshine (ultra-violet rays). Melanin absorbs the sun's harmful rays, shielding the inner skin.
chunks.source: Melanin absorbs the sun's harmful rays, shielding the inner skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the device that protects appliances from the effects of too much current flow. A: A fuse. A fuse breaks the circuit when too much current flows, saving appliances.
chunks.source: A fuse breaks the circuit when too much current flows, saving appliances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is salt added to food during cooking? A: To make the food tasty. Salt adds flavour to food during cooking.
chunks.source: Salt adds flavour to food during cooking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which immunisable disease makes limbs of infants very thin and paralyzed? A: Polio. Polio attacks the nerves, making infants' limbs thin and paralysed; it is prevented by vaccine.
chunks.source: Polio attacks the nerves, making infants' limbs thin and paralysed; it is prevented by vaccine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41. Study the diagram below and answer the questions that follow. (a) To which group of vertebrates does the animal above belong? A: Fish. The animal has gills and fins, which are features of fish.
chunks.source: The animal has gills and fins, which are features of fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b) Name Y. A: Lateral line. The lateral line runs along the fish's body and senses vibrations in water.
chunks.source: The lateral line runs along the fish's body and senses vibrations in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c) Give the function of the parts below. (i) X A: For breathing (gaseous exchange). Part X (the gills) absorbs dissolved oxygen from water for the fish.
chunks.source: Part X (the gills) absorbs dissolved oxygen from water for the fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c)(ii) Z A: For movement (swimming). Part Z (the fins) pushes against water so the fish can swim.
chunks.source: Part Z (the fins) pushes against water so the fish can swim.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a) What is food preservation? A: It is the keeping of food from going bad. Food preservation treats food so it stays safe to eat for a long time.
chunks.source: Food preservation treats food so it stays safe to eat for a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b) Point out one traditional method of preserving meat in your homes. A: By smoking. Smoking dries meat with smoke so germs cannot spoil it.
chunks.source: Smoking dries meat with smoke so germs cannot spoil it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c) How is the preservation of millet similar to that of cassava? A: Both are preserved by sun drying. Millet grains and cassava chips are both dried in the sun for storage.
chunks.source: Millet grains and cassava chips are both dried in the sun for storage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(d) Name the fungus that commonly grows on food items that are not properly dried. A: Moulds. Moulds grow on damp, poorly dried foods and spoil them.
chunks.source: Moulds grow on damp, poorly dried foods and spoil them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43. Give the meaning of the following terms: (i) condensation A: The process by which vapour (gas) changes into liquid. When steam cools, it condenses into liquid water drops.
chunks.source: When steam cools, it condenses into liquid water drops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(ii) evaporation A: The process by which liquid changes into vapour (gas). When water is heated, it evaporates into invisible vapour.
chunks.source: When water is heated, it evaporates into invisible vapour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(iii) melting A: The process by which a solid changes into liquid. Ice melts into water when it is warmed.
chunks.source: Ice melts into water when it is warmed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(iv) convection A: The transfer of heat through fluids (liquids and gases). In convection, warm fluid rises and cool fluid sinks, carrying heat along.
chunks.source: In convection, warm fluid rises and cool fluid sinks, carrying heat along.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a) The diagram below shows a human arm. Name the type of bone: (i) X A: Humerus. The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm marked X.
chunks.source: The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm marked X.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a)(ii) Z A: Radius (and ulna). The radius and ulna are the two long bones of the forearm marked Z.
chunks.source: The radius and ulna are the two long bones of the forearm marked Z.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b) Which of the labeled muscles contracts to lift a load? A: The biceps. The biceps contracts and pulls the forearm up when lifting a load.
chunks.source: The biceps contracts and pulls the forearm up when lifting a load.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c) What type of movable joint is E? A: Hinge joint. The elbow (E) is a hinge joint that bends in one direction like a door hinge.
chunks.source: The elbow (E) is a hinge joint that bends in one direction like a door hinge.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a) How do fish reproduce? A: By laying eggs (which are fertilized externally). Female fish lay eggs in water and the male sheds sperms over them.
chunks.source: Female fish lay eggs in water and the male sheds sperms over them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b) In which two ways do fish help to improve health of people in the community? (i) ___ A: They provide protein food. Eating fish gives the body proteins for growth and repair.
chunks.source: Eating fish gives the body proteins for growth and repair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(ii) ___ A: They provide income to buy other needs. Selling fish earns money for medicine, food and school needs.
chunks.source: Selling fish earns money for medicine, food and school needs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c) Point out one other group of vertebrates whose eggs are fertilized like those of fish. A: Amphibians. Like fish, amphibians such as frogs lay eggs that are fertilized outside the body.
chunks.source: Like fish, amphibians such as frogs lay eggs that are fertilized outside the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) Name one viral disease among the six childhood immunisable diseases. A: Measles. Measles is a viral killer disease prevented by immunisation.
chunks.source: Measles is a viral killer disease prevented by immunisation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b) How is such a disease in 46(a) above spread? A: Through the air when the patient coughs or sneezes. Measles germs move in droplets through the air to healthy children.
chunks.source: Measles germs move in droplets through the air to healthy children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c) Point out one way of controlling the diseases mentioned in 46(a) above. A: By immunising children. Vaccination protects children against measles.
chunks.source: Vaccination protects children against measles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(d) How are ventilators important in a living house? A: They allow fresh air into the house. Ventilators bring in fresh air and remove stale air from the house.
chunks.source: Ventilators bring in fresh air and remove stale air from the house.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a) What is incubation? A: The keeping of eggs warm until they hatch. During incubation the hen (or machine) warms the eggs so chicks develop.
chunks.source: During incubation the hen (or machine) warms the eggs so chicks develop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b) Give one advantage of artificial incubation in poultry management. A: Many eggs can be hatched at the same time. An incubator hatches large numbers of chicks together, unlike one hen.
chunks.source: An incubator hatches large numbers of chicks together, unlike one hen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c) Of what importance is litter in the poultry house? A: It keeps the house warm and absorbs droppings. Litter insulates the floor and soaks up moisture from droppings.
chunks.source: Litter insulates the floor and soaks up moisture from droppings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(d) Mention one factor that may make a fertilized egg fail to hatch. A: Low temperature (too little warmth). Without enough warmth the chick inside cannot develop and hatch.
chunks.source: Without enough warmth the chick inside cannot develop and hatch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a) In which type of digestion is food broken down by enzymes? A: Chemical digestion. Enzymes chemically break food into simple soluble substances.
chunks.source: Enzymes chemically break food into simple soluble substances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b) Of what importance are teeth in our mouth during digestion? A: They break food into small pieces (mechanical digestion). Teeth cut and grind food so enzymes can act on it easily.
chunks.source: Teeth cut and grind food so enzymes can act on it easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c) Why doesn't digestion of carbohydrates take place in the stomach? A: The stomach has no enzyme that digests carbohydrates. Carbohydrate digestion starts in the mouth with saliva and continues in the small intestine, not the stomach.
chunks.source: Carbohydrate digestion starts in the mouth with saliva and continues in the small intestine, not the stomach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(d) Point out one disorder of the digestive system. A: Constipation. Constipation is difficulty in passing out solid waste.
chunks.source: Constipation is difficulty in passing out solid waste.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a) The diagram below is of a burning candle. Name the type of change that occurs in parts marked U and X. (i) U A: Physical change. At U the wax only melts, forming no new substance, which is a physical change.
chunks.source: At U the wax only melts, forming no new substance, which is a physical change.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(ii) X A: Chemical change. At X the wick burns, forming new substances (smoke, ash), which is a chemical change.
chunks.source: At X the wick burns, forming new substances (smoke, ash), which is a chemical change.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b) Give one characteristic of the type of change marked X above. A: A new substance is formed (it is irreversible). Chemical changes produce new substances and cannot easily be undone.
chunks.source: Chemical changes produce new substances and cannot easily be undone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c) Give one change in the environment caused by human activities. A: Deforestation. People cut down forests for farming and settlement, changing the environment.
chunks.source: People cut down forests for farming and settlement, changing the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50. Match the items in list A with those in B. (a) lungs ___ A: carbon dioxide. The lungs excrete carbon dioxide from the body during breathing.
chunks.source: The lungs excrete carbon dioxide from the body during breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b) kidney ___ A: urine. The kidneys filter blood and excrete urine.
chunks.source: The kidneys filter blood and excrete urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c) liver ___ A: bile pigment. The liver excretes bile pigments from broken red blood cells.
chunks.source: The liver excretes bile pigments from broken red blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(d) skin ___ A: sweat. The skin excretes sweat through the sweat glands.
chunks.source: The skin excretes sweat through the sweat glands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51. Give one reason why the following practices are done on an animal farm: (a) steaming up A: To increase milk production after calving. Steaming up feeds the pregnant cow well so it produces much milk after giving birth.
chunks.source: Steaming up feeds the pregnant cow well so it produces much milk after giving birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b) shearing A: To get wool from sheep. Shearing cuts the wool off sheep for sale and use.
chunks.source: Shearing cuts the wool off sheep for sale and use.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c) docking A: To keep the animal clean (prevent faeces from soiling the wool). Docking cuts the tail short so droppings do not dirty the animal's rear.
chunks.source: Docking cuts the tail short so droppings do not dirty the animal's rear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(d) dipping cattle A: To kill ticks on the cattle. Dipping bathes cattle in chemicals that kill ticks and prevent tick-borne diseases.
chunks.source: Dipping bathes cattle in chemicals that kill ticks and prevent tick-borne diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a) Who is an adolescent? A: A person between childhood and adulthood (about 10-19 years). Adolescence is the stage of growth between being a child and becoming an adult.
chunks.source: Adolescence is the stage of growth between being a child and becoming an adult.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b) Point out one primary sex characteristic that occurs in adolescent girls. A: The start of menstruation. Menstruation shows that the reproductive organs of the girl are maturing.
chunks.source: Menstruation shows that the reproductive organs of the girl are maturing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(c) Give two secondary sexual characteristics that occur in both female and male adolescents. (i) ___ A: Hair grows in the pubic region. Both boys and girls grow pubic hair during adolescence.
chunks.source: Both boys and girls grow pubic hair during adolescence.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(c) Give two secondary sexual characteristics that occur in both female and male adolescents. (ii) ___ A: Hair grows in the armpits. Armpit hair appears in both male and female adolescents.
chunks.source: Armpit hair appears in both male and female adolescents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a) What causes AIDS? A: HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus). AIDS is caused by the HIV virus which destroys the body's defence system.
chunks.source: AIDS is caused by the HIV virus which destroys the body's defence system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b) How is AIDS commonly spread among adults? A: Through unprotected sex. Having unprotected sex with an infected person spreads HIV.
chunks.source: Having unprotected sex with an infected person spreads HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c) State one common sign to both AIDS and measles patients. A: Skin rash. Both AIDS and measles patients can develop rashes on the skin.
chunks.source: Both AIDS and measles patients can develop rashes on the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(d) Point out one way a P.7 child can prevent himself or herself from getting AIDS. A: By abstaining from sex. Avoiding sex keeps a P.7 child safe from HIV infection.
chunks.source: Avoiding sex keeps a P.7 child safe from HIV infection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a) The diagram below shows one of the body systems. Name the body system represented by the diagram above. A: The breathing (respiratory) system. The diagram shows the organs used for breathing air in and out.
chunks.source: The diagram shows the organs used for breathing air in and out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b) What does part marked M represent? A: The windpipe (trachea). Part M is the tube that carries air to the lungs.
chunks.source: Part M is the tube that carries air to the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c) What would happen to part marked K if N is pushed upwards? A: Part K (the lungs) would deflate and air would be forced out. Pushing the diaphragm (N) up squeezes the lungs so air is breathed out.
chunks.source: Pushing the diaphragm (N) up squeezes the lungs so air is breathed out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(d) Point out one habit which is destructive to the body system above. A: Smoking. Smoking damages the lungs and air passages of the breathing system.
chunks.source: Smoking damages the lungs and air passages of the breathing system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a) The diagram below are of spawns of the amphibians. Which amphibian lays eggs marked A? A: A toad. Toads lay their eggs in long strings (spawn A), unlike frogs.
chunks.source: Toads lay their eggs in long strings (spawn A), unlike frogs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b) Give two importance of the jelly on the eggs marked B. (i) ___ A: It protects the eggs from enemies. The jelly coat shields the delicate eggs from harm.
chunks.source: The jelly coat shields the delicate eggs from harm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b) Give two importance of the jelly on the eggs marked B. (ii) ___ A: It keeps the eggs moist and holds them together. The jelly stops the eggs from drying and binds the spawn in a clump.
chunks.source: The jelly stops the eggs from drying and binds the spawn in a clump.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c) How is breathing of a tadpole different from that of its adult? A: A tadpole breathes through gills while the adult breathes through lungs (and moist skin). Tadpoles live in water and use gills; adult frogs use lungs on land.
chunks.source: Tadpoles live in water and use gills; adult frogs use lungs on land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the element of weather that helps crop farmers to carryout winnowing. A: Wind. Wind blows away the chaff from the heavier grain during winnowing.
chunks.source: Wind blows away the chaff from the heavier grain during winnowing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one fungal disease that affects the human skin. A: Ringworm. Ringworm is a fungal infection of the skin.
chunks.source: Ringworm is a fungal infection of the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is culling important in poultry management? A: It removes unproductive birds, reducing feed costs and disease spread.. Why would a farmer remove birds that do not lay well?
chunks.source: Why would a farmer remove birds that do not lay well?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below is of a fishing rod. Study and use it to answer questions 4 and 5. Name the class of levers to which the fishing rod belongs. A: Third class lever. In a fishing rod the effort is between the fulcrum and the load, making it a third-class lever.
chunks.source: In a fishing rod the effort is between the fulcrum and the load, making it a third-class lever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 5: The diagram shows a fishing rod. What is the load on the fishing rod? A: The load is the fish at the end of the line (the tip of the rod).. The load is whatever is being lifted, here the hooked fish.
chunks.source: The load is whatever is being lifted, here the hooked fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it not advisable to keep potted plants in a room where people live? A: Plants give out carbon dioxide at night, which pollutes the air in the room.. What gas do plants release in the dark?
chunks.source: What gas do plants release in the dark?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one disorder of the human digestive system. A: Constipation. Constipation is a common disorder of the digestive system.
chunks.source: Constipation is a common disorder of the digestive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the filament of an electric bulb coiled? A: To make it longer so it produces more light and lasts longer.. A longer filament gives more light. How does coiling help?
chunks.source: A longer filament gives more light. How does coiling help?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which part of an onion plant is food stored? A: In the bulb (the swollen underground stem).. An onion is a bulb; food is stored in its fleshy leaves.
chunks.source: An onion is a bulb; food is stored in its fleshy leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any way in which the fish benefits from its slippery body. A: It reduces friction, helping the fish to swim easily and escape predators.. How does slipperiness help in water?
chunks.source: How does slipperiness help in water?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the function of the cotyledon in the maize grain different from that in a bean seed? A: In maize the cotyledon absorbs food from the endosperm, while in beans the cotyledons store the food.. Maize has endosperm; beans store food in the cotyledons. What is the difference?
chunks.source: Maize has endosperm; beans store food in the cotyledons. What is the difference?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in school children benefit from a school garden. A: They get food / learn farming skills.. A school garden provides food and practical lessons.
chunks.source: A school garden provides food and practical lessons.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the importance of giving a person who has drunk paraffin fluids like milk to drink? A: Milk dilutes the paraffin and soothes the throat/stomach lining.. Why give milk after paraffin poisoning?
chunks.source: Why give milk after paraffin poisoning?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the best way of preventing childhood immunisable diseases. A: Immunization (vaccination).. Vaccines protect children against immunisable diseases.
chunks.source: Vaccines protect children against immunisable diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a human ear .Study and use it to answer questions 15 and 16. Name the part marked K. A: Cochlea. The cochlea converts sound vibrations into nerve impulses.
chunks.source: The cochlea converts sound vibrations into nerve impulses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a human ear .Study and use it to answer questions 15 and 16. State the function of the part marked L on the human ear above. A: It helps the body to balance (maintains body posture).. The semicircular canals detect head movement for balance.
chunks.source: The semicircular canals detect head movement for balance.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which disease vector spreads river blindness to people? A: Blackfly. The blackfly (Simulium) spreads river blindness.
chunks.source: The blackfly (Simulium) spreads river blindness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does painting help to prevent a metallic object from rusting? A: Paint keeps air and water away from the metal, preventing rusting.. What two things must reach iron for it to rust?
chunks.source: What two things must reach iron for it to rust?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of increasing the volume of blood in the human body. A: By drinking fluids / blood transfusion.. Fluids and transfusions raise blood volume.
chunks.source: Fluids and transfusions raise blood volume.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way are air sacs (alveoli) able to carry out gaseous exchange? A: They have thin walls and a large surface area for gaseous exchange.. Thin walls and many air sacs speed up diffusion.
chunks.source: Thin walls and many air sacs speed up diffusion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it more difficult to push a wheelbarrow uphill than downhill? A: More effort is needed to overcome gravity when moving uphill.. Going up means working against gravity.
chunks.source: Going up means working against gravity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from making alcohol, state any one other way in which distillation is useful to people. A: Purifying water / making clean drinking water.. Distillation gives pure water from dirty water.
chunks.source: Distillation gives pure water from dirty water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one factor to consider before sorting clothes for washing. A: Colour / fabric type / how dirty they are.. Sorting by colour and fabric protects clothes.
chunks.source: Sorting by colour and fabric protects clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a candle manufacturer benefit from bee keeping? A: He gets beeswax for making candles.. Beeswax is the raw material for candles.
chunks.source: Beeswax is the raw material for candles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from preventing teenage pregnancy, give one other reason why school girls are advised to abstain from sex. A: To avoid HIV/AIDS and other sexually transmitted infections.. Abstinence also protects against STIs.
chunks.source: Abstinence also protects against STIs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of moulting to an insect. A: It allows the insect to grow bigger.. The hard exoskeleton is shed so the insect can grow.
chunks.source: The hard exoskeleton is shed so the insect can grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the function of the cortex in the kidney? A: Filtration of blood (it filters waste from blood to form urine).. The cortex is where blood is filtered in the kidney.
chunks.source: The cortex is where blood is filtered in the kidney.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does buoyancy(upthrust) force affect the weight of objects in water? A: It makes objects weigh less in water than in air.. Upthrust pushes up against the weight.
chunks.source: Upthrust pushes up against the weight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a chameleon important to human beings? A: It eats crop pests (insects), protecting crops.. Chameleons feed on harmful insects.
chunks.source: Chameleons feed on harmful insects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one breed of goats kept for milk production. A: Saanen (or Toggenburg).. Saanen goats are famous dairy goats.
chunks.source: Saanen goats are famous dairy goats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a condition during the flow of electricity along electric wires. Study and use it to answer questions 31 and 32. Identify the electrical condition shown above. A: Short circuit (sparks are produced).. When bare wires touch, a short circuit causes sparks.
chunks.source: When bare wires touch, a short circuit causes sparks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a condition during the flow of electricity along electric wires. Study and use it to answer questions 31 and 32. Write any one cause of the above condition during flow of electric current A: Switch off the power / do not touch the wires; call an electrician.. Never touch sparking wires with bare hands.
chunks.source: Never touch sparking wires with bare hands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it not advisable to stop petrol fire using water? A: Water spreads the burning petrol / petrol floats on water.. Petrol floats, so water spreads the fire.
chunks.source: Petrol floats, so water spreads the fire.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way in which colostrum is important to a newly born calf. A: It gives the calf immunity (antibodies) against diseases.. Colostrum is rich in antibodies for the newborn.
chunks.source: Colostrum is rich in antibodies for the newborn.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What would you do to the garden where planted seeds failed to germinate? A: Gap fill / replant (sow again).. Failed seeds should be replaced by replanting.
chunks.source: Failed seeds should be replaced by replanting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does a clay-made charcoal stove use less charcoal than a metallic one? A: Clay is a poor conductor of heat, so less heat is lost.. Which material keeps heat in better?
chunks.source: Which material keeps heat in better?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one habit that helps to promote oral health. A: Brushing teeth after meals.. Brushing removes food that decays teeth.
chunks.source: Brushing removes food that decays teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the importance of a chimney on a kitchen? A: It lets out smoke (so the kitchen is not smoky).. A chimney carries smoke out of the kitchen.
chunks.source: A chimney carries smoke out of the kitchen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one reason why clay soil is used for making ceramics. A: It is plastic when wet and hard when baked.. Clay can be moulded then hardened by firing.
chunks.source: Clay can be moulded then hardened by firing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which part of a lens camera are images formed? A: On the film (or screen).. The lens focuses the image onto the film.
chunks.source: The lens focuses the image onto the film.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(1): Name the part on a house that performs the following functions, Lets fresh air into the house A: Window. Windows let fresh air into the house.
chunks.source: Windows let fresh air into the house.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(2): Name the part on a house that performs the following functions, Lets warm air out of the house A: Ventilator. Ventilators let warm air out near the roof.
chunks.source: Ventilators let warm air out near the roof.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b): By what process does heat travel through a saucepan placed on a gas cooker? A: Conduction. Heat travels through the metal saucepan by conduction.
chunks.source: Heat travels through the metal saucepan by conduction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c): State any one way in which insulators of heat are useful to people. A: They keep hot things hot and cold things cold (e.g. handles, flasks).. Insulators slow heat loss or gain.
chunks.source: Insulators slow heat loss or gain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(1): Name the parts marked X and Z. X A: Lid (cover). The lid covers the top of the hive.
chunks.source: The lid covers the top of the hive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(2): Name the parts marked X and Z. Z A: Entrance. Bees enter and leave through the entrance hole.
chunks.source: Bees enter and leave through the entrance hole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b): Sate any one function of the part marked Y on the beehive above. A: It separates the queen from the honey chamber / keeps the queen in the brood area.. The queen excluder confines the queen.
chunks.source: The queen excluder confines the queen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c): Identify the type of beehive shown above. A: Top-bar hive (Kenya top-bar hive).. The long box with top bars is a top-bar hive.
chunks.source: The long box with top bars is a top-bar hive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43: The table below shows parts of a flush toilet with their functions in the wrong order. Part Function of part Toilet seat Stores faeces and urine Bowl Stores water for flushing the toilet Cistern tank For the user to sit on when defecating Septic tank For depositing faeces and urine Match the parts to their function by re-writing the correct order. a) Toilet seat b) Bowl c) Cistern tank d) Septic tank A: Toilet seat: It is sat on; Bowl: Faeces and urine are deposited in it; Cistern: It stores water for flushing; Septic tank: It stores faeces and urine. Each part has a matching function in a flush toilet.
chunks.source: Each part has a matching function in a flush toilet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a): State what happened to sugar. A: The sugar dissolved (disappeared) in the water.. Sugar dissolves in water to form a solution.
chunks.source: Sugar dissolves in water to form a solution.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b): Why did sugar behave as stated in (a0 above? A: Because sugar is soluble in water.. Soluble substances dissolve in water.
chunks.source: Soluble substances dissolve in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c)(1): Identify the name given to the following substances in the above experiment. Sugar A: Solute. The dissolved substance is the solute.
chunks.source: The dissolved substance is the solute.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c)(2): Identify the name given to the following substances in the above experiment. Water A: Solvent. The liquid that dissolves is the solvent.
chunks.source: The liquid that dissolves is the solvent.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(1): Name any two examples of wedges. A: Axe. An axe blade is a wedge.
chunks.source: An axe blade is a wedge.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(2): Name any two examples of wedges. A: Knife. A knife blade is a wedge.
chunks.source: A knife blade is a wedge.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(1): Give any two ways in which a crop farmer uses wedges. A: Splitting firewood.. Wedges split wood easily.
chunks.source: Wedges split wood easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(2): Give any two ways in which a crop farmer uses wedges. A: Cutting (e.g. using a hoe or panga to dig/cut).. Wedge tools cut and dig.
chunks.source: Wedge tools cut and dig.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a): In which class of food does iodised salt belong? A: Protective food (minerals).. Iodised salt supplies iodine, a mineral.
chunks.source: Iodised salt supplies iodine, a mineral.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b): Name any one class of food which is not represented in the above list. A: Carbohydrates (energy-giving food).. The list lacks an energy-giving food.
chunks.source: The list lacks an energy-giving food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c): identify any one foodstuff you would advise a brick maker to eat. A: Posho / cassava / sweet potatoes (energy food).. A brick maker needs energy for hard work.
chunks.source: A brick maker needs energy for hard work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(d): How are oranges useful to human health? A: They provide vitamin C, which prevents scurvy.. Oranges are rich in vitamin C.
chunks.source: Oranges are rich in vitamin C.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(1): Name the blood vessels marked A and B. A A: Artery. Vessel A is thick-walled, carrying blood from the heart.
chunks.source: Vessel A is thick-walled, carrying blood from the heart.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(2): Name the blood vessels marked A and B. B A: Capillary. Vessel B is the tiny thin-walled vessel.
chunks.source: Vessel B is the tiny thin-walled vessel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b): State any one structural difference between blood vessel A and blood vessel C. A: A has thicker walls than C / A has a narrower lumen than C.. Arteries are thicker and narrower than veins.
chunks.source: Arteries are thicker and narrower than veins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c): Give any one function of blood vessel B during blood circulation. A: It allows exchange of materials between blood and body cells.. Capillaries link arteries to veins for exchange.
chunks.source: Capillaries link arteries to veins for exchange.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a): What germ causes gonorrhea in human beings? A: Bacteria (Neisseria gonorrhoeae).. Gonorrhoea is caused by bacteria.
chunks.source: Gonorrhoea is caused by bacteria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b)(1): Give any two signs of gonorrhea. A: Pain when urinating.. Burning urine is a sign of gonorrhoea.
chunks.source: Burning urine is a sign of gonorrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b)(2): Give any two signs of gonorrhea. A: Discharge of pus from the genitals.. Pus discharge is a sign of gonorrhoea.
chunks.source: Pus discharge is a sign of gonorrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c): State any one way of preventing gonorrhea in human beings. A: Abstain from sex / use a condom.. Avoiding unsafe sex prevents gonorrhoea.
chunks.source: Avoiding unsafe sex prevents gonorrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(1): Give any two ways in which drug dependence can affect an individual. A: It damages health (e.g. liver, brain).. Drugs harm the body organs.
chunks.source: Drugs harm the body organs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(2): Give any two ways in which drug dependence can affect an individual. A: It leads to poor school performance / crime.. Addiction disrupts school and behaviour.
chunks.source: Addiction disrupts school and behaviour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c)(1): State two ways in which an individual can avoid drug dependence. A: Avoid bad peer groups.. Good friends keep you from drugs.
chunks.source: Good friends keep you from drugs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c)(2): State two ways in which an individual can avoid drug dependence. A: Do not taste or experiment with drugs.. Refusing the first offer prevents addiction.
chunks.source: Refusing the first offer prevents addiction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(1): Mention any two chemicals used to treat water. A: Chlorine. Chlorine kills germs in water.
chunks.source: Chlorine kills germs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(2): Mention any two chemicals used to treat water. A: Alum. Alum helps dirt to settle in water treatment.
chunks.source: Alum helps dirt to settle in water treatment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b): Apart from using chemicals, state any one other method used to make water safe for drinking. A: Boiling. Boiling kills germs in water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c): Why is water obtained by filtration not good for drinking? A: Filtration does not kill germs.. Filtered water may still contain germs.
chunks.source: Filtered water may still contain germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(1): Apart from compost manure, mention any two other examples of natural fertilizers. A: Farmyard manure. Animal droppings are a natural fertilizer.
chunks.source: Animal droppings are a natural fertilizer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(2): Apart from compost manure, mention any two other examples of natural fertilizers. A: Green manure. Ploughed-in green plants enrich the soil.
chunks.source: Ploughed-in green plants enrich the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b): Why should water be sprinkled on a compost pit or heap? A: To speed up rotting (decomposition).. Moisture helps decomposers rot the heap.
chunks.source: Moisture helps decomposers rot the heap.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c): State any one advantage of using natural fertilizers over artificial fertilizers. A: They do not pollute the soil / they improve soil structure.. Natural fertilizers are eco-friendly.
chunks.source: Natural fertilizers are eco-friendly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a): Identify the device shown in the diagram above. A: Solar panel. The device traps sunlight to make electricity.
chunks.source: The device traps sunlight to make electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(1): Give any one reason why the above device is usually, placed on top of a house roof. A: To receive maximum sunlight.. Roofs are open to the sun all day.
chunks.source: Roofs are open to the sun all day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(2): Give any one reason why the above device is usually, painted black on the surface. A: Black absorbs the most heat/light energy.. Dark surfaces absorb more radiation.
chunks.source: Dark surfaces absorb more radiation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(c): Name any one electrical appliance that uses electricity produced by the above device. A: Bulb (lamp).. A bulb gives light from solar electricity.
chunks.source: A bulb gives light from solar electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a): Give any one reason why a passion fruit plant climbs others. A: To get sunlight for photosynthesis.. Climbing reaches light above other plants.
chunks.source: Climbing reaches light above other plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c): Apart from a passion fruit plant, name any one other plant that climbs others. A: Cucumber plant. Cucumbers climb using tendrils.
chunks.source: Cucumbers climb using tendrils.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b)(1): State any two ways how plants with weak stems climbs others. A: By using tendrils.. Tendrils coil around supports.
chunks.source: Tendrils coil around supports.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b)(2): State any two ways how plants with weak stems climbs others. A: By twining around the support.. Some stems wind around poles.
chunks.source: Some stems wind around poles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54: The table below shows groups of birds, type of food eaten and nature of their beaks. Study and complete it correctly. Group Type of food Nature of beak Climbing birds Strong pointed and chisel shaped beak. Flesh Strong sharp hooked beak Wading birds Long thin beak Swimming birds Fries, toads, frogs A: Climbing birds: Seeds; Birds of prey: Flesh; Wading birds: Fish, frogs and toads; Swimming birds: Water plants. Beak shape and food match the bird group: chisel beaks crack seeds, hooked beaks tear flesh, long thin beaks spear fish, broad flat beaks sieve water food.
chunks.source: Beak shape and food match the bird group: chisel beaks crack seeds, hooked beaks tear flesh, long thin beaks spear fish, broad flat beaks sieve water food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a)(1): Name the fungus used in the following, brewing of alcohol A: Yeast. Yeast ferments sugar to make alcohol.
chunks.source: Yeast ferments sugar to make alcohol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a)(2): Name the fungus used in the following, making of antibiotics A: Penicillium. Penicillium makes the antibiotic penicillin.
chunks.source: Penicillium makes the antibiotic penicillin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(2): State any two ways in which fungi are harmful to people. A: Some cause food to rot.. Moulds spoil stored food.
chunks.source: Moulds spoil stored food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(3): State any two ways in which fungi are harmful to people. A: Some cause diseases (e.g. ringworm).. Fungi cause skin infections.
chunks.source: Fungi cause skin infections.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of chicken purposely kept for egg production. A: Layers. Layers are chickens kept for egg production.
chunks.source: Layers are chickens kept for egg production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which vector spreads yellow fever to people? A: Female Aedes mosquito. The Aedes mosquito spreads yellow fever.
chunks.source: The Aedes mosquito spreads yellow fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one use of soap in promoting personal hygiene. A: Washing hands / bathing.. Soap removes germs and dirt from the body.
chunks.source: Soap removes germs and dirt from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a sea mammal. A: Whale (or dolphin).. Whales are mammals that live in the sea.
chunks.source: Whales are mammals that live in the sea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a stone being thrown using a catapult. Use it to answer question 5. What type of energy is possessed by the rubber band before the stone is released?. A: Potential (elastic) energy. The stretched rubber band stores elastic potential energy.
chunks.source: The stretched rubber band stores elastic potential energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which group of non-flowering plants reproduce by means of seeds? A: Gymnosperms. Gymnosperms (e.g. pines) are non-flowering but make seeds.
chunks.source: Gymnosperms (e.g. pines) are non-flowering but make seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the type of change that enables Primary Seven pupils to burn rubbish in a rubbish pit. A: Chemical change. Burning is a chemical change (new substances form).
chunks.source: Burning is a chemical change (new substances form).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention the component of soil that enables plants to carry out photosynthesis. A: Water. Water from soil is needed for photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Water from soil is needed for photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is transplanting of seedlings done in the evening? A: To reduce water loss (transpiration) / avoid harsh sunshine.. Evening is cool, so seedlings lose less water.
chunks.source: Evening is cool, so seedlings lose less water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are the ossicles useful during the process of hearing? A: They amplify sound vibrations to the inner ear.. The ossicles pass and strengthen vibrations.
chunks.source: The ossicles pass and strengthen vibrations.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 11: The diagram shows a white blood cell. Which part is the nucleus? A: The nucleus is the large dark-stained body inside the white blood cell.. The nucleus controls the cell.
chunks.source: The nucleus controls the cell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below is a white blood cell. Use it to answer questions 11 and 12. Give the function of the white blood cells in the body. A: They defend the body against germs (fight infection).. White blood cells engulf germs.
chunks.source: White blood cells engulf germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one activity done to keep food safe for more than one month. A: Drying / smoking / salting.. Drying removes water so food keeps longer.
chunks.source: Drying removes water so food keeps longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of controlling diarrheal diseases in the community. A: Boiling drinking water / proper latrine use.. Clean water and sanitation stop diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Clean water and sanitation stop diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which state of matter is smoke? A: Gas. Smoke is a mixture of gases and tiny solids in air.
chunks.source: Smoke is a mixture of gases and tiny solids in air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one primary sex change common in both adolescent boys and girls. A: Growth of pubic hair.. Both boys and girls grow pubic hair at puberty.
chunks.source: Both boys and girls grow pubic hair at puberty.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which a shopkeeper uses electricity. A: Lighting the shop / running a fridge.. Electricity lights and cools the shop.
chunks.source: Electricity lights and cools the shop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a hyena benefit from following a lion? A: It eats leftovers from the lion’s kill.. Hyenas scavenge what lions leave.
chunks.source: Hyenas scavenge what lions leave.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the difference in function between a tendon and a ligament at a joint. A: A tendon joins muscle to bone; a ligament joins bone to bone.. Tendons pull bones, ligaments hold joints.
chunks.source: Tendons pull bones, ligaments hold joints.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which regular medical check-ups are important to the human body. A: They detect diseases early for treatment.. Check-ups find sickness before it worsens.
chunks.source: Check-ups find sickness before it worsens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does debeaking help to control egg eating in chicken? A: It stops them pecking and eating eggs.. Debeaked birds cannot break eggshells.
chunks.source: Debeaked birds cannot break eggshells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from pregnant mothers, name one other group of people who are given TT vaccine. A: Women of childbearing age.. TT protects mothers and newborns from tetanus.
chunks.source: TT protects mothers and newborns from tetanus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which cattle disease makes animals to move in circles? A: Heartwater. Heartwater makes cattle circle and is tick-borne.
chunks.source: Heartwater makes cattle circle and is tick-borne.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of mucus found on the lining of the alimentary canal during digestion. A: It protects the walls from being digested.. Mucus shields the gut lining from acid and enzymes.
chunks.source: Mucus shields the gut lining from acid and enzymes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagrams below show two metallic ball rings. Study them and answer questions 25 and 26. What does the above experiment show about metals? A: Metals expand when heated.. The heated ball expanded and could not pass through the ring.
chunks.source: The heated ball expanded and could not pass through the ring.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagrams below show two metallic ball rings. Study them and answer questions 25 and 26. Why did the metallic ball in diagram B fail to pass through the ring? A: The ball expanded on heating.. Expansion made the ball too big for the ring.
chunks.source: Expansion made the ball too big for the ring.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should parents stop children from eating a lot of sweets? A: It is a vector that spreads sleeping sickness (to people and animals).. Tsetse flies transmit trypanosomiasis.
chunks.source: Tsetse flies transmit trypanosomiasis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a skunk protect itself against enemies? A: It keeps the body warm / protects organs.. Fat insulates and cushions the body.
chunks.source: Fat insulates and cushions the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of preventing burns and scalds at home. A: It is a compound leaf.. A mango leaf has many leaflets on one stalk.
chunks.source: A mango leaf has many leaflets on one stalk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do energy saving stoves help to conserve wood fuel? A: To prevent the spread of Newcastle disease.. Vaccination protects poultry from Newcastle.
chunks.source: Vaccination protects poultry from Newcastle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one condition favourable for soil to support good plant growth. A: It pollutes the air (smoke).. Burning rubbish releases harmful smoke.
chunks.source: Burning rubbish releases harmful smoke.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does decision making help school children to safeguard themselves against alcoholism? A: Deforestation leads to soil erosion / loss of rain.. Trees protect soil and attract rain.
chunks.source: Trees protect soil and attract rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure? A: It helps in breathing (it is the windpipe).. Air passes through the trachea to the lungs.
chunks.source: Air passes through the trachea to the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why animals move from one place to another. A: Through the bloodstream.. The heart pumps blood round the body.
chunks.source: The heart pumps blood round the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which group of people are easily harmed due to poor feeding? A: It helps the flower to be pollinated.. Scent and colour attract pollinators.
chunks.source: Scent and colour attract pollinators.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below is of an invertebrate in the mollusc group. Study it and use it to answer questions 36 and 37. Name the part marked W. A: Tentacle. The snail feels with its tentacles.
chunks.source: The snail feels with its tentacles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below is of an invertebrate in the mollusc group. Study it and use it to answer questions 36 and 37. State the function of substance marked X to the above mollusc during movement. A: It produces slime for smooth movement.. Mucus lubricates the snail’s path.
chunks.source: Mucus lubricates the snail’s path.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the skin, give one other body organ that makes use of light energy. A: It stores bile.. The gall bladder keeps bile from the liver.
chunks.source: The gall bladder keeps bile from the liver.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one characteristic that enables termites to build an anthill within a short period of time. A: It kills germs in food.. Stomach acid destroys many germs.
chunks.source: Stomach acid destroys many germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one principle of Primary Health Care P.H.C). A: On the retina.. Images form on the retina of the eye.
chunks.source: Images form on the retina of the eye.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a): Why is rusting called a chemical change? A: Because a new substance (rust) is formed.. Rusting creates iron oxide, which is different from iron.
chunks.source: Rusting creates iron oxide, which is different from iron.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(1): State two conditions necessary for rusting to take place. A: Oxygen (air).. Iron needs oxygen to rust.
chunks.source: Iron needs oxygen to rust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(2): State two conditions necessary for rusting to take place. A: Water (moisture).. Iron needs water to rust.
chunks.source: Iron needs water to rust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c): Give any one way in which rusting is important in the environment. A: It breaks down iron materials, returning iron to the soil.. Rusted iron adds minerals to soil.
chunks.source: Rusted iron adds minerals to soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a): Identify the method of storing music shown above A: Tonic solfa. The notes doh, ray, me show tonic solfa.
chunks.source: The notes doh, ray, me show tonic solfa.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b): Give any one way in which music stored using the above method can be reproduced. A: By singing the notes.. Tonic solfa is performed by singing.
chunks.source: Tonic solfa is performed by singing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c): Apart from the above method, mention any one other method of storing music. A: Staff notation. Music can also be written on lines and spaces.
chunks.source: Music can also be written on lines and spaces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(d): State the difference between pitch and volume of sound. A: Pitch is the highness or lowness of sound, while volume is the loudness or softness of sound.. Pitch and volume describe different qualities.
chunks.source: Pitch and volume describe different qualities.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(1): Give the importance of carrying out each of the following practices in sheep keeping. hoof trimming. A: It prevents lameness and foot rot.. Trimmed hooves keep sheep walking well.
chunks.source: Trimmed hooves keep sheep walking well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(2): Give the importance of carrying out each of the following practices in sheep keeping. docking. A: It prevents blowfly strike / makes mating easy.. A short tail stays clean.
chunks.source: A short tail stays clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(1): State any two ways of controlling tick borne diseases in sheep. A: Spraying with acaricide.. Acaricides kill ticks.
chunks.source: Acaricides kill ticks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(2): State any two ways of controlling tick borne diseases in sheep. A: Dipping the sheep.. Dips destroy ticks on the body.
chunks.source: Dips destroy ticks on the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a)(1): Write down any two causes of soil exhaustion. A: Overcultivation.. Growing crops without rest tires the soil.
chunks.source: Growing crops without rest tires the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a)(2): Write down any two causes of soil exhaustion. A: Soil erosion.. Erosion washes away fertile topsoil.
chunks.source: Erosion washes away fertile topsoil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b): Give any one characteristic that makes clays soil suitable for making ceramics. A: It is plastic (easily moulded) when wet.. Clay can be shaped then hardened.
chunks.source: Clay can be shaped then hardened.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c): Apart from making ceramics, state any one other way in which clay soil is useful to people. A: Making bricks.. Clay bricks build houses.
chunks.source: Clay bricks build houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45: The table below shows parts of a flower and their functions but in wrong order. Part of a flower Function of the part (i) Sepal receives pollen grains during pollination. (ii) Anther attracts insects for pollination (iii) Stigma protects the flower during bud stage (iv) Petal produces pollen grains. Match the parts of a flower in the table above with their functions correctly. (i) Sepal (ii) Anther (iii) Stigma (iv) Petal A: Sepal: It protects the flower bud; Anther: It produces pollen grains; Stigma: It receives pollen grains; Petal: It attracts insects for pollination. Each flower part matches its reproductive function.
chunks.source: Each flower part matches its reproductive function.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a): In which way does severe diarrhea lead to dehydration? A: The body loses a lot of water through the watery stool.. Frequent watery stool drains body fluids.
chunks.source: Frequent watery stool drains body fluids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b): State the importance of sugar when preparing Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS). A: It gives energy and helps the body absorb water and salts.. Sugar aids absorption in ORS.
chunks.source: Sugar aids absorption in ORS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c)(1): Apart from giving Oral Rehydration Solution, state any two other ways of rehydrating a patient with severe diarrhea. A: Giving plenty of fluids like fruit juice.. Juices replace lost water.
chunks.source: Juices replace lost water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c)(2): Apart from giving Oral Rehydration Solution, state any two other ways of rehydrating a patient with severe diarrhea. A: Giving porridge or soup.. Soft foods give fluids and energy.
chunks.source: Soft foods give fluids and energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(1): Name the group of crops to which each of the following crops belongs. bean crops A: Legumes. Beans fix nitrogen; they are legumes.
chunks.source: Beans fix nitrogen; they are legumes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(2): Name the group of crops to which each of the following crops belongs. rice crops A: Cereals. Rice is a cereal grain.
chunks.source: Rice is a cereal grain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(1): Give any two ways in which weeding is done in the garden. A: Digging them out with a hoe.. A hoe cuts weed roots.
chunks.source: A hoe cuts weed roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(2): Give any two ways in which weeding is done in the garden. A: Uprooting by hand.. Small weeds can be pulled.
chunks.source: Small weeds can be pulled.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a): Name the equipment in the diagram above. A: Bee catcher (swarm catcher).. The box traps a swarm of bees.
chunks.source: The box traps a swarm of bees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b): How is the above equipment useful to a bee keeper? A: It is used to catch swarms for stocking hives.. A catcher collects bees for a new hive.
chunks.source: A catcher collects bees for a new hive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c): What activity in bee keeping involves the use of the above equipment? A: Hiving / stocking a beehive.. The swarm is put into a hive.
chunks.source: The swarm is put into a hive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(d): Give any one reason why honey does not go bad yet it is food. A: It has very low moisture content.. Germs cannot grow in thick honey.
chunks.source: Germs cannot grow in thick honey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a): State the role of yeast during fermentation of alcohol. A: It ferments sugar into alcohol.. Yeast breaks down sugar, releasing alcohol.
chunks.source: Yeast breaks down sugar, releasing alcohol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(1): Apart from fermentation of alcohol, give any two other way in which yeast is useful to people. A: Baking bread (makes dough rise).. Yeast produces gas that lifts dough.
chunks.source: Yeast produces gas that lifts dough.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(2): Apart from fermentation of alcohol, give any two other way in which yeast is useful to people. A: Brewing beer.. Yeast ferments grain for beer.
chunks.source: Yeast ferments grain for beer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c): Which fungus is used to make antibiotic drugs? A: Penicillium. Penicillium mould makes penicillin.
chunks.source: Penicillium mould makes penicillin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(1): Give the importance of each of the following in a home, a rubbish pit A: For proper disposal of rubbish.. A pit keeps the home clean.
chunks.source: A pit keeps the home clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(2): Give the importance of each of the following in a home, a rack A: For drying utensils.. A rack keeps plates clean and dry.
chunks.source: A rack keeps plates clean and dry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(1): Mention any two other sanitary items that a home should have. A: Latrine. A latrine disposes of faeces safely.
chunks.source: A latrine disposes of faeces safely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(2): Mention any two other sanitary items that a home should have. A: Bathroom. A bathroom is for bathing.
chunks.source: A bathroom is for bathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a): Name the example of stem tuber marked Q. A: Irish potato. Q is the Irish potato plant.
chunks.source: Q is the Irish potato plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b): State any one characteristic common to all root tubers. A: They store food in their roots.. Root tubers swell with stored food.
chunks.source: Root tubers swell with stored food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c): In which way is the propagation of cassava different from that of a white yam? A: Cassava is planted by stem cuttings, while white yam is planted by tubers.. Cassava uses stems; yam uses tubers.
chunks.source: Cassava uses stems; yam uses tubers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(d): Why is a sugarcane plant not grouped under stem tubers yet it stores its food in the stem? A: It has no swollen tuber; it stores sugar in the stem.. Sugar cane stems are not tubers.
chunks.source: Sugar cane stems are not tubers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a): In which way is the function of a fuse different from that of a switch in an electric circuit? A: A fuse breaks the circuit automatically when current is too high, while a switch opens or closes the circuit manually.. Fuse protects; switch controls.
chunks.source: Fuse protects; switch controls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(1): Apart from a fuse and a switch, write down any two other components of an electric circuit. A: Bulb. A bulb uses electricity to give light.
chunks.source: A bulb uses electricity to give light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(2): Apart from a fuse and a switch, write down any two other components of an electric circuit. A: Dry cell (battery). A cell supplies electricity.
chunks.source: A cell supplies electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(c): State the main reason why the tungsten filament of an electric bulb is coiled. A: To make the filament longer so it gives more light.. A longer filament glows brighter.
chunks.source: A longer filament glows brighter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a): State any one way in which rocks contribute to the development of an area. A: They provide building stones for construction.. Stones build houses and roads.
chunks.source: Stones build houses and roads.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b): Apart from rocks, name any one other example of a non-renewable resource in the environment. A: Petroleum (crude oil).. Oil cannot be replaced once used.
chunks.source: Oil cannot be replaced once used.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c)(1): State any two ways of conserving non-renewable resources in the environment. A: Recycling materials.. Recycling reduces new extraction.
chunks.source: Recycling reduces new extraction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c)(2): State any two ways of conserving non-renewable resources in the environment. A: Using them sparingly.. Less use makes them last longer.
chunks.source: Less use makes them last longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(1): Name the parts marked B and C. B A: Bronchus. B branches from the trachea into the lung.
chunks.source: B branches from the trachea into the lung.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(2): Name the parts marked B and C. C A: Diaphragm. C is the breathing muscle.
chunks.source: C is the breathing muscle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b): What process takes place in part marked D? A: Gaseous exchange. Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged in the lungs.
chunks.source: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged in the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c): State any one way in which part marked A is adapted to its function. A: It has rings of cartilage that keep it open.. Cartilage stops the trachea collapsing.
chunks.source: Cartilage stops the trachea collapsing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a): State any one cause of rickets in children. A: Lack of vitamin D (or lack of sunlight).. Vitamin D needs sunshine for strong bones.
chunks.source: Vitamin D needs sunshine for strong bones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c)(1): Write down any two signs of rickets in a child. A: Bow legs.. Weak bones bend outward.
chunks.source: Weak bones bend outward.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c)(2): Write down any two signs of rickets in a child. A: Knock knees.. Knees touch while ankles part.
chunks.source: Knees touch while ankles part.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b): Give any one example of food you would give to a child to protect him/her against rickets. A: Milk. Milk provides vitamin D and calcium.
chunks.source: Milk provides vitamin D and calcium.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the body organ that enables a primary one pupil to sense the nice smell from the kitchen. A: Nose. The nose senses smells.
chunks.source: The nose senses smells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way of controlling mosquitoes at the larva stage. A: Oiling the water / draining stagnant water.. Oil suffocates mosquito larvae.
chunks.source: Oil suffocates mosquito larvae.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of change is destructive to iron and steel metals? A: Chemical change (rusting).. Rusting destroys iron and steel.
chunks.source: Rusting destroys iron and steel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the class of food recommended by Mr.Agaba who is a brick maker to eat. X A: Carbohydrates (energy-giving food).. A brick maker needs energy for heavy work.
chunks.source: A brick maker needs energy for heavy work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows blood vessels. Use it to answer questions 5 and 6. Identify the type of blood vessel shown above. A: Vein. The vessel has valves, which are found in veins.
chunks.source: The vessel has valves, which are found in veins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows blood vessels. Use it to answer questions 5 and 6. State function of structures marked X in the above blood vessel. A: They prevent the backflow of blood.. Valves keep blood flowing toward the heart.
chunks.source: Valves keep blood flowing toward the heart.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a swim bladder useful to a fish? A: It helps the fish to float (controls buoyancy).. The swim bladder fills with gas to rise or sink.
chunks.source: The swim bladder fills with gas to rise or sink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of a caterpillar has the same function as the hard shell of a snail? A: Its cuticle (exoskeleton).. The tough cuticle protects like a shell.
chunks.source: The tough cuticle protects like a shell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of some water that remains in a toilet bowl after flushing. A: It prevents bad smells from the septic tank.. Water seals out odours.
chunks.source: Water seals out odours.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does water exist in all three states of matter? A: Because temperature changes make it freeze, melt and evaporate.. Heat changes water’s state.
chunks.source: Heat changes water’s state.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below is of a property of sound. Use it to answer questions 11 and 12. State the property of sound shown above. A: Reflection of sound (echo).. Sound bounces off the wall back to the speaker.
chunks.source: Sound bounces off the wall back to the speaker.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below is of a property of sound. Use it to answer questions 11 and 12. In which one way is the above property of sound useful to bats? A: Bats use echoes to find insects / it is used to measure distance.. Reflected sound locates objects.
chunks.source: Reflected sound locates objects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way do bacteria help in the production of yoghurt? A: They ferment milk into yoghurt.. Bacteria sour the milk.
chunks.source: Bacteria sour the milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a farm animal that is castrated. A: Bull (or buck, boar).. Males are castrated to fatten them.
chunks.source: Males are castrated to fatten them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from spreading diarrheal diseases, state one other way houseflies are dangerous to man. A: They contaminate food with germs.. Flies carry germs on their bodies.
chunks.source: Flies carry germs on their bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which characteristic makes sand soil best for building houses? A: It is strong and stable.. Sand soil supports heavy buildings.
chunks.source: Sand soil supports heavy buildings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a humming bird different from other birds in terms of flight? A: It can fly backwards / hover in one place.. Hummingbirds hover like helicopters.
chunks.source: Hummingbirds hover like helicopters.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the major cause of child poisoning at home. A: Keeping paraffin and chemicals within reach of children.. Children drink from accessible bottles.
chunks.source: Children drink from accessible bottles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way an individual can participate in primary Health Care. A: Immunizing children.. Vaccination is part of PHC.
chunks.source: Vaccination is part of PHC.

chunks.subject: Science
