chunks.text: Q: Give any one way early planting is advantageous to a crop farmer. A: Crops use early rains fully.. Early planting catches the whole season.
chunks.source: Early planting catches the whole season.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger a primary six girl can face while putting on dirty Knickers. A: She can get urinary tract infections.. Dirty knickers harbour germs.
chunks.source: Dirty knickers harbour germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a dog benefit from bringing out its tongue while running? A: To cool its body (lose heat).. Panting releases heat.
chunks.source: Panting releases heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which part of the female reproductive system does conception take place? A: In the oviduct (fallopian tube).. Fertilization happens in the oviduct.
chunks.source: Fertilization happens in the oviduct.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one biological method of controlling crop pests in the garden. A: Using predators (e.g. cats eat rats).. Natural enemies kill pests.
chunks.source: Natural enemies kill pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a reproductive part of a flower. Use it to answer the questions 25 and 26. Identify the reproductive part of the flower shown above. A: Stamen. The stamen is the male reproductive part.
chunks.source: The stamen is the male reproductive part.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 26: The diagram shows a stamen. Which part produces pollen (similar to sperms in animals)? A: The anther, at the top of the stamen, produces pollen (like sperms).. Pollen is the male gamete.
chunks.source: Pollen is the male gamete.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does salting help in the preservation of meat? A: It removes water so germs cannot grow.. Salt draws out moisture.
chunks.source: Salt draws out moisture.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is boiling water considered the best method of making water safe for drinking? A: It kills germs and removes impurities.. Boiling is thorough and chemical-free.
chunks.source: Boiling is thorough and chemical-free.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the sexually transmitted diseases that can lead to madness at later stages if not treated early? A: Syphilis. Untreated syphilis can affect the brain.
chunks.source: Untreated syphilis can affect the brain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens to the weight of an object when immersed in water? A: It reduces (it weighs less).. Upthrust pushes up, reducing weight.
chunks.source: Upthrust pushes up, reducing weight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is polio vaccine given more than once to children? A: To build strong immunity.. Repeated doses strengthen protection.
chunks.source: Repeated doses strengthen protection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are the gills of a fish different from the gills of a mushroom in terms of their function? A: Fish gills are for breathing, while mushroom gills produce spores.. Fish gills exchange gases; mushroom gills make spores.
chunks.source: Fish gills exchange gases; mushroom gills make spores.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below is of a burning candle wax. Use it to answer questions 33 and 34. Why would the flame go off when the candle wax is covered with a container? A: Because it is starved of oxygen.. Fire needs oxygen to burn.
chunks.source: Fire needs oxygen to burn.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below is of a burning candle wax. Use it to answer questions 33 and 34. Give any one danger of using a candle wax at home. A: It can cause fire outbreaks.. A candle can set a house ablaze.
chunks.source: A candle can set a house ablaze.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A part from debeaking, state any one other way of preventing egg eating in poultry A: Collecting eggs regularly.. No eggs left means none to eat.
chunks.source: No eggs left means none to eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a worker Bee able to carry pollen from flowers? A: Using its pollen basket.. Bees pack pollen on their legs.
chunks.source: Bees pack pollen on their legs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the gas used to leguminous plants to make proteins. A: Nitrogen. Legumes use nitrogen to make proteins.
chunks.source: Legumes use nitrogen to make proteins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which instrument is used to measure air pressure? A: Barometer. A barometer measures air pressure.
chunks.source: A barometer measures air pressure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does salt disappear when put in water? A: Because it dissolves in water.. Salt is soluble.
chunks.source: Salt is soluble.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What structure is used by a causality to support him/her while walking in case of a fractured leg? A: Crutches. Crutches support a fractured leg.
chunks.source: Crutches support a fractured leg.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a): What type of change is evaporation? A: Physical change. No new substance is formed.
chunks.source: No new substance is formed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(1): Give any two factors that affect the rate of evaporation. A: Temperature.. Heat speeds up evaporation.
chunks.source: Heat speeds up evaporation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(2): Give any two factors that affect the rate of evaporation. A: Wind.. Wind carries vapour away.
chunks.source: Wind carries vapour away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c): State any one way in which evaporation is applied in our daily life. A: Drying clothes.. Wet clothes dry by evaporation.
chunks.source: Wet clothes dry by evaporation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a): What method of vegetative propagation is shown above? A: Grafting. Joining scion to stock is grafting.
chunks.source: Joining scion to stock is grafting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b): Name the part marked A. A: Scion. The upper joined part is the scion.
chunks.source: The upper joined part is the scion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c): Apart from the above method, state any one other method of vegetative propagation. A: Budding. A bud is another grafting method.
chunks.source: A bud is another grafting method.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(d): Give any one advantage of vegetative propagation. A: It keeps the desired qualities of the plant.. Grafted plants stay true to type.
chunks.source: Grafted plants stay true to type.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(1): Give the role of each of the following during digestion. Saliva A: It softens food and starts digestion.. Saliva moistens and digests starch.
chunks.source: Saliva moistens and digests starch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(2): Give the role of each of the following during digestion. Tongue A: It rolls food into a bolus for swallowing.. The tongue pushes food around.
chunks.source: The tongue pushes food around.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(1): State any two characteristics of enzymes. A: They are specific (each works on one food).. Each enzyme has one job.
chunks.source: Each enzyme has one job.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(2): State any two characteristics of enzymes. A: They are destroyed by heat.. High heat denatures enzymes.
chunks.source: High heat denatures enzymes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a): How does prolonged breast feeding promote family planning at home? A: It delays the return of fertility.. Breastfeeding suppresses ovulation.
chunks.source: Breastfeeding suppresses ovulation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b)(1): Apart from prolonged breast feeding, name any two other methods of family planning A: Using condoms.. Condoms prevent pregnancy.
chunks.source: Condoms prevent pregnancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b)(2): Apart from prolonged breast feeding, name any two other methods of family planning A: Using contraceptive pills.. Pills prevent ovulation.
chunks.source: Pills prevent ovulation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c): Give any one advantage of family planning. A: It reduces family expenses.. Fewer children cost less.
chunks.source: Fewer children cost less.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(1): Mention two methods of harvesting rain water at home. A: Using gutters and tanks.. Roof water is collected in tanks.
chunks.source: Roof water is collected in tanks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(2): Mention two methods of harvesting rain water at home. A: Digging a pond / well.. Ponds store rain water.
chunks.source: Ponds store rain water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b): Give any one way in which water is useful to a mechanic. A: Washing vehicles / cooling engines.. Mechanics use water for washing.
chunks.source: Mechanics use water for washing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c): State any one danger of water to people. A: It can drown people.. Floods and deep water kill.
chunks.source: Floods and deep water kill.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a): Identify the property of air shown above. A: Air exerts pressure.. Air pushed the cardboard, holding the water.
chunks.source: Air pushed the cardboard, holding the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b): Why doesn’t water pour out of the glass? A: Air pressure pushes the cardboard against the glass.. Outside air pressure is stronger than the water weight.
chunks.source: Outside air pressure is stronger than the water weight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c): State the role of the cardboard in the above experiment. A: It covers the mouth, stopping water from escaping.. The card seals the glass.
chunks.source: The card seals the glass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(d): Give any one application of the above property of air in our daily life. A: Drinking with a straw.. Sucking uses air pressure.
chunks.source: Sucking uses air pressure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(1): Name the group of invertebrates to which each of the following animals belongs. Star fish A: Echinoderms. Starfish are echinoderms.
chunks.source: Starfish are echinoderms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(2): Name the group of invertebrates to which each of the following animals belongs. Jerry fish A: Coelenterates. Jellyfish are coelenterates.
chunks.source: Jellyfish are coelenterates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(1): State any two ways in which invertebrates help to promote people’s health. A: Bees give honey (food).. Honey is nutritious.
chunks.source: Honey is nutritious.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(2): State any two ways in which invertebrates help to promote people’s health. A: Silkworms give silk.. Silk clothes come from silkworms.
chunks.source: Silk clothes come from silkworms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48: The table below shows farm practices, animals and function of the practice, Study and complete it correctly. PRACTICE ANIMAL FUNCTION OF THE PRACTICE (ii) piglets Prevents injuries on the teats of the sow (i) Docking Sheep (iv) Steaming up Cows, nanny goats, sows, ewe. (iii) Dehorning Reduces injuries among animals A: Teeth clipping: piglets – Prevents injuries on the teats of the sow; Docking: Sheep – Makes mating easy; Steaming up: Cows (and nanny goats, sows, ewes) – Prepares for birth and milk production; Dehorning: Cattle – Reduces injuries among animals. Each practice matches its animal and purpose.
chunks.source: Each practice matches its animal and purpose.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.source: No air or water means no rust.

chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(1): Mention any two examples of water cleaned diseases. A: Cholera. Cholera spreads through dirty water, washed away by clean water.

chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(2): Mention any two examples of water cleaned diseases. A: Dysentery. Clean water prevents dysentery.

chunks.source: Different crops follow each other in sequence.

chunks.source: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c): In which one way can food taboos affect the health of children? A: They may lack important nutrients.. Forbidden foods may be nutritious.
chunks.source: Forbidden foods may be nutritious.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which organ is affected by trachoma? A: Eyes. Trachoma affects the eyes.
chunks.source: Trachoma affects the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which force enables objects to weigh less in water than air? A: Upthrust (buoyancy).. Upthrust reduces weight in water.
chunks.source: Upthrust reduces weight in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is fertilization in mammals similar to that in birds? A: Both involve the fusion of male and female gametes.. Fertilization joins sperm and ovum in both.
chunks.source: Fertilization joins sperm and ovum in both.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the vector for East Coast Fever in cattle. A: Brown ear tick. Ticks spread East Coast Fever.
chunks.source: Ticks spread East Coast Fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What food deficiency can lead to kwashiorkor? A: Protein deficiency. Lack of protein causes kwashiorkor.
chunks.source: Lack of protein causes kwashiorkor.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the type of objects which require the displacement method to get their volume. A: Irregular objects. Displacement finds volume of odd shapes.
chunks.source: Displacement finds volume of odd shapes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one disease which can be controlled by boiling water for drinking. A: Cholera. Boiling kills cholera germs.
chunks.source: Boiling kills cholera germs.

chunks.source: Grasshoppers destroy leaves.

chunks.text: Q: How is burning of rubbish dangerous in the environment? A: It pollutes the air with smoke.. Burning releases harmful gases.
chunks.source: Burning releases harmful gases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one function of the liver in the body? A: It stores glycogen / produces bile.. The liver stores and secretes.
chunks.source: The liver stores and secretes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Use the diagram of the flying kite below to answer the question that follows. What type of energy does the flying kite have? A: Potential energy (and kinetic energy).. The high flying kite has potential energy.
chunks.source: The high flying kite has potential energy.

chunks.text: Q: Which element of PHC does a child promote by a mother breast feeding a baby? A: Nutrition. Breast milk feeds the baby.
chunks.source: Breast milk feeds the baby.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the similarity in function between the kink of the thermometer and the valves in the veins. A: Both prevent backflow.. Kink and valves stop reverse flow.
chunks.source: Kink and valves stop reverse flow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why crops should be thinned. A: To reduce competition for nutrients.. Fewer plants grow stronger.
chunks.source: Fewer plants grow stronger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one way in which wind is used as an energy resource. A: Driving windmills.. Wind turns turbines.
chunks.source: Wind turns turbines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is filtering of water alone not enough to make it safe for drinking? A: It does not kill germs.. Filters leave germs behind.
chunks.source: Filters leave germs behind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the main duty of the master bee in a hive. A: To mate with the queen.. The drone’s duty is mating.
chunks.source: The drone’s duty is mating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can loosening the string affect the pitch of sound? A: It lowers the pitch.. Loose strings vibrate slowly.
chunks.source: Loose strings vibrate slowly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the importance of water during seed germination. A: It softens the seed coat for germination.. Water wakes the seed.
chunks.source: Water wakes the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where does a cassava plant store its food? A: In its roots (tubers).. Cassava stores in root tubers.
chunks.source: Cassava stores in root tubers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one use of biogas at home? A: Cooking. Biogas burns for cooking.
chunks.source: Biogas burns for cooking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which liquid reduces friction in the human joints? A: Synovial fluid. Joints are lubricated by synovial fluid.
chunks.source: Joints are lubricated by synovial fluid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the function of a bulb in an electric circuit? A: It produces light.. A bulb glows in a circuit.
chunks.source: A bulb glows in a circuit.

chunks.text: Q: In the space below, draw a white blood cell. A: A white blood cell is drawn as a round cell with a stained nucleus.. WBCs have a visible nucleus.
chunks.source: WBCs have a visible nucleus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do trees clean the air around an industry? A: They absorb carbon dioxide.. Trees clean air by taking in CO2.
chunks.source: Trees clean air by taking in CO2.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State what happens when two North poles of magnets are brought together. A: They repel each other.. Like poles repel.
chunks.source: Like poles repel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What term refers to keeping too many animals on a small plot by a farmer? A: Overstocking. Too many animals overgraze.
chunks.source: Too many animals overgraze.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does bush burning lead to soil erosion? A: It leaves soil bare, so rain washes it away.. No cover means erosion.
chunks.source: No cover means erosion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one dangerous substance found in tobacco. A: Nicotine. Nicotine is addictive in tobacco.
chunks.source: Nicotine is addictive in tobacco.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one characteristic of swimming birds. A: They have webbed feet.. Webbed feet paddle water.
chunks.source: Webbed feet paddle water.

chunks.text: Q: Why are legumes included in crop rotation? A: They add nitrogen to the soil.. Legumes fix nitrogen.
chunks.source: Legumes fix nitrogen.

chunks.text: Q: Name the disease which causes abortion in cows. A: Brucellosis. Brucella causes abortion in cows.
chunks.source: Brucella causes abortion in cows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does sound travel from one place to another? A: By vibrations through air.. Sound waves travel in air.
chunks.source: Sound waves travel in air.

chunks.text: Q: Name the method of harvesting trees shown below. A: Coppicing. Cutting to stumps for regrowth is coppicing.
chunks.source: Cutting to stumps for regrowth is coppicing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way of reducing friction between moving parts of machines. A: Oiling (lubrication).. Oil reduces friction.
chunks.source: Oil reduces friction.

chunks.text: Q: Give the role played by the sun during the water cycle. A: It evaporates water into vapour.. Sun heats water to rise.
chunks.source: Sun heats water to rise.

chunks.text: Q: Which part of the skeleton protects the spinal cord? A: Vertebrae (backbone).. The spine shields the cord.
chunks.source: The spine shields the cord.

chunks.text: Q: How does the moth detect flowers in the darkness at night? A: By smell (antennae).. Moths smell flowers.
chunks.source: Moths smell flowers.

chunks.text: Q: State one role of children in a home. A: Fetching water / cleaning.. Children help at home.

chunks.source: Plants lose water as vapour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b): Mention the process by which plants absorb water from the soil. A: Osmosis. Roots absorb by osmosis.
chunks.source: Roots absorb by osmosis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c): Name the part of a plant which mainly carries out photosynthesis. A: Leaf. Leaves photosynthesize.
chunks.source: Leaves photosynthesize.

chunks.text: Q: 42(d): How is the root cap important to the root? A: It protects the root tip.. The cap shields growing roots.
chunks.source: The cap shields growing roots.

chunks.source: A is ice changing to water.

chunks.source: B is water changing to ice.

chunks.source: Freezing needs cold.

chunks.text: Q: 43(c): Name the natural process that involves processes E and F. A: Water cycle. Evaporation and condensation drive the water cycle.

Each digestive item matches its description.

chunks.text: Q: 55(c): Mention one method used to control soil erosion in an area. A: Terracing.. Terraces slow water.

chunks.source: Sunlight is useful.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one disadvantage of a free range system of rearing animals. A: Animals destroy crops / get stolen.. Free range risks losses.
chunks.source: Free range risks losses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a vent pipe on a VIP latrine useful? A: It lets out bad smells.. The pipe vents odours.
chunks.source: The pipe vents odours.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a): Name any one example of poultry. A: Hen. A hen is poultry.
chunks.source: A hen is poultry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b): Why do farmers keep dual purpose birds? A: For both meat and eggs.. Dual purpose gives two products.
chunks.source: Dual purpose gives two products.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c): Give one disadvantage of battery system of rearing birds. A: It is expensive to set up.. Batteries cost a lot.
chunks.source: Batteries cost a lot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(d): Identify a poultry disease caused by protozoa. A: Coccidiosis. Protozoa cause coccidiosis.
chunks.source: Protozoa cause coccidiosis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a): What is Dehydration? A: Loss of body water.. Dehydration is water loss.
chunks.source: Dehydration is water loss.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b): Give one sign of dehydration. A: Dry mouth / sunken eyes.. Water loss shows in the mouth.
chunks.source: Water loss shows in the mouth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c): Mention one cause of dehydration. A: Diarrhoea. Diarrhoea drains water.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea drains water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(d): How can dehydration be controlled? A: By giving ORS / plenty of fluids.. Rehydration replaces water.
chunks.source: Rehydration replaces water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a): Name the part labeled R. A: Pelvis (renal pelvis).. R is the inner collecting part.
chunks.source: R is the inner collecting part.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b): What activity is done at Q? A: Filtration of blood.. The cortex filters blood.
chunks.source: The cortex filters blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c): To which part of the body does S go? A: To the urinary bladder.. The ureter leads to the bladder.
chunks.source: The ureter leads to the bladder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(d): Give one disease which affects the kidneys. A: Kidney stones. Stones block the kidney.
chunks.source: Stones block the kidney.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(i): The diagram shows a baby who received immunization. With the help of arrows, show the immunisable sites for; DPT Vaccine A: DPT is given on the thigh.. The thigh muscle takes DPT.
chunks.source: The thigh muscle takes DPT.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(ii): The diagram shows a baby who received immunization. With the help of arrows, show the immunisable sites for; Measles Vaccine A: Measles is given on the left upper arm.. The left arm takes measles vaccine.
chunks.source: The left arm takes measles vaccine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(iii): The diagram shows a baby who received immunization. With the help of arrows, show the immunisable sites for; BCG A: BCG is given on the right upper arm.. The right arm takes BCG.
chunks.source: The right arm takes BCG.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(iv): The diagram shows a baby who received immunization. With the help of arrows, show the immunisable sites for; Polio Vaccine A: Polio is given by mouth (oral drops).. Polio drops go in the mouth.
chunks.source: Polio drops go in the mouth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a): What are Organic manures? A: Natural fertilizers from plants or animals.. Organic manure is natural.
chunks.source: Organic manure is natural.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(1): Name two types of organic manures. A: Farmyard manure. Animal waste fertilizes.
chunks.source: Animal waste fertilizes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(2): Name two types of organic manures. A: Compost manure. Rotted plants fertilize.
chunks.source: Rotted plants fertilize.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c): Mention any one disadvantage of using artificial fertilizers. A: They can burn crops / pollute soil.. Excess chemicals harm.
chunks.source: Excess chemicals harm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a)(1): Give any two ways in which animals depend on plants. A: They get food from plants.. Herbivores eat plants.
chunks.source: Herbivores eat plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a)(2): Give any two ways in which animals depend on plants. A: They get oxygen from plants.. Plants release oxygen.
chunks.source: Plants release oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b): Identify one way how plants depend on other plants. A: Climbers use other plants for support.. Vines climb trees.
chunks.source: Vines climb trees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c): Mention one way how animals depend on other animals. A: Predators eat other animals.. Lions eat zebras.
chunks.source: Lions eat zebras.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a): State one difference in germination of Monocotyledonous and Dicotyledonous plants. A: Monocots have one cotyledon; dicots have two.. Seed leaves differ.
chunks.source: Seed leaves differ.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b): Mention one condition required for a seed to germinate. A: Water. Seeds need water.
chunks.source: Seeds need water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c)(1): Apart from using chemicals, give two ways of controlling pests in a garden. A: Hand picking.. Pests can be picked off.
chunks.source: Pests can be picked off.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c)(2): Apart from using chemicals, give two ways of controlling pests in a garden. A: Crop rotation.. Rotation breaks pest cycles.
chunks.source: Rotation breaks pest cycles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a): Name pole P of magnet B. A: North pole. Like poles repel, so P is North.
chunks.source: Like poles repel, so P is North.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b): Why did magnet A and B remain apart as shown? A: Because like poles (North) repel each other.. Both facing poles are North.
chunks.source: Both facing poles are North.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c): Give one way of demagnetizing magnets. A: By heating.. Heat destroys magnetism.
chunks.source: Heat destroys magnetism.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(d): How are magnets useful in the environment? A: They are used in compasses / electric motors.. Magnets have many uses.
chunks.source: Magnets have many uses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a): Name the method for experiment set by the P.5 boy. A: Displacement method. Water displacement finds volume.
chunks.source: Water displacement finds volume.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b): Calculate the density of the stone. (2 Marks) A: 3 g/cc. Density = 24 ÷ 8 = 3.
chunks.source: Density = 24 ÷ 8 = 3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c): Name the container used in the experiment above. A: Measuring cylinder. The cylinder measures volume.
chunks.source: The cylinder measures volume.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50: Match the diseases in list A to the animals they attack in list B below correctly. LIST A LIST B Newcastle disease Cattle African swine fever Mad dogs Rabies Poultry Rinderpest Pigs (i) Newcastle disease (ii) African swine fever (iii) Rabies (iv) Rinderpest A: Newcastle disease: Poultry; African swine fever: Pigs; Rabies: Dogs; Rinderpest: Cattle. Each disease attacks its specific animal.
chunks.source: Each disease attacks its specific animal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(1): How does each of the following animals protect itself from enemies? Porcupine. A: It raises its quills.. Sharp quills deter enemies.
chunks.source: Sharp quills deter enemies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(2): How does each of the following animals protect itself from enemies? Wasp. A: It stings.. Wasps sting attackers.
chunks.source: Wasps sting attackers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(1): Name the animal that stays in a; Sty. A: Pig. Pigs live in sties.
chunks.source: Pigs live in sties.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(2): Name the animal that stays in a; Den. A: Lion. Lions live in dens.
chunks.source: Lions live in dens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(1): Use one sentence to state the meaning of each of the following; Reflection of light. A: Reflection is the bouncing of light off a surface.. Light bounces back.
chunks.source: Light bounces back.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(2): Use one sentence to state the meaning of each of the following; Refraction of light. A: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another.. Light bends in water.
chunks.source: Light bends in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(3): Use one sentence to state the meaning of each of the following; Spectrum. A: Spectrum is the band of colours formed when light splits.. Rainbow colours form a spectrum.
chunks.source: Rainbow colours form a spectrum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(d): What type of reflection is produced from rough shining surface? A: Diffuse reflection. Rough surfaces scatter light.
chunks.source: Rough surfaces scatter light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a): Name the part labelled A. A: Ligament. A joins bone to bone.
chunks.source: A joins bone to bone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b): Mike overstretched this part and tore it during an accident. What kind of injury did he get? A: Sprain. A torn ligament is a sprain.
chunks.source: A torn ligament is a sprain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c): What is the possible sign of the injury he got? A: Swelling (and pain).. Injuries swell.
chunks.source: Injuries swell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(d): Identify the first aid you would give to the above kind of injury. A: Rest, ice, compression and elevation (RICE).. RICE treats sprains.
chunks.source: RICE treats sprains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(1): State the effects of alcohol on each of the following; An individual. A: It damages health.. Alcohol harms the body.
chunks.source: Alcohol harms the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(2): State the effects of alcohol on each of the following; A family. A: It causes family neglect / poverty.. Drunks neglect families.
chunks.source: Drunks neglect families.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(3): State the effects of alcohol on each of the following; A community. A: It increases crime.. Alcohol fuels violence.
chunks.source: Alcohol fuels violence.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b): Mention any one life skill that can enable a person to get rid of alcohol. A: Assertiveness (saying no).. Refusing peer pressure helps.
chunks.source: Refusing peer pressure helps.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a): In which way are animals A, C and D similar? A: They are all vertebrates.. Frog, rat and snake have backbones.
chunks.source: Frog, rat and snake have backbones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b): How is the reproduction of the animal D different from that in C? A: The snake lays eggs while the rat gives birth to live young.. Reptiles lay eggs; mammals bear live.
chunks.source: Reptiles lay eggs; mammals bear live.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c): To which class of animal does animal B belong? A: Mollusca (mollusc).. Snails are molluscs.
chunks.source: Snails are molluscs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(d): How does animal A protect itself against its enemies? 12 End A: It hops away / uses camouflage.. Frogs escape by jumping.
chunks.source: Frogs escape by jumping.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the force that enables static electricity to be produced. A: Friction. Rubbing produces static electricity.
chunks.source: Rubbing produces static electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are red blood cells important in the human body? A: They carry oxygen.. Red cells transport oxygen.
chunks.source: Red cells transport oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one property of magnets. A: Like poles repel.. Magnets push like poles away.
chunks.source: Magnets push like poles away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the dangerous gas found in tobacco smoke. A: Carbon monoxide. Tobacco smoke has CO.
chunks.source: Tobacco smoke has CO.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can cattle farmers improve the quality of their local breeds? A: By cross-breeding.. Crosses improve breeds.
chunks.source: Crosses improve breeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the space provided below, draw a beak of a bird of prey. A: A bird of prey has a strong sharp hooked beak.. Hooked beaks tear flesh.
chunks.source: Hooked beaks tear flesh.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the smallest basic unit of matter? A: Atom. Atoms are the smallest units.
chunks.source: Atoms are the smallest units.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of an intestinal worm. A: Tapeworm. Tapeworms live in intestines.
chunks.source: Tapeworms live in intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of propagating pineapples. A: By planting crowns (tops).. Pineapple tops grow.
chunks.source: Pineapple tops grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we call the growth movement of a plant towards light? A: Phototropism. Plants bend toward light.
chunks.source: Plants bend toward light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a person suffering from gonorrhea advised to go with his or her sexual partner for treatment? A: To prevent re-infection.. Both must be cured.
chunks.source: Both must be cured.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one example of an energy resource in the environment. A: Sun. The sun is an energy source.
chunks.source: The sun is an energy source.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one modern method used to preserve food. A: Refrigeration. Cold preserves food.
chunks.source: Cold preserves food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the wind pipe made up of rings of cartilage? A: To keep it open.. Cartilage stops collapse.
chunks.source: Cartilage stops collapse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way the skin regulates body temperature on a hot day. A: It sweats.. Sweat cools the body.
chunks.source: Sweat cools the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens to the volume of water when heat is reduced from it up to below 00C? A: It decreases (then expands below 4°C / freezes).. Cooling shrinks water until freezing.
chunks.source: Cooling shrinks water until freezing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of an animal whose body temperature changes with change in the temperature of the surroundings. A: Frog (or lizard, fish).. Cold-blooded animals change with surroundings.
chunks.source: Cold-blooded animals change with surroundings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one secondary sex characteristic common to both males and females. A: Growth of pubic hair.. Both sexes grow pubic hair.
chunks.source: Both sexes grow pubic hair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one factor that affects the rate of transpiration. A: Temperature. Heat increases transpiration.
chunks.source: Heat increases transpiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest the best way of avoiding the contraction of sexually transmitted infection among teenagers. A: Abstinence. Avoiding sex prevents STIs.
chunks.source: Avoiding sex prevents STIs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is aluminum preferred to other metals in making of air craft bodies? A: It is light.. Aluminium is light for flying.
chunks.source: Aluminium is light for flying.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one natural cause of environmental degradation. A: Floods. Floods degrade land.
chunks.source: Floods degrade land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which group of underground stems does an Irish potato belong? A: Stem tubers. Irish potato is a stem tuber.
chunks.source: Irish potato is a stem tuber.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one vaccine that is administered to babies at birth. A: BCG. BCG is given at birth.
chunks.source: BCG is given at birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Convert 100C to 0F. A: 212°F. 100°C = 212°F.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the function of hydrochloric acid found inside the stomach. A: It kills germs / helps digestion.. Acid destroys germs.
chunks.source: Acid destroys germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does mulching control soil erosion? A: It covers soil, reducing runoff.. Mulch protects soil.
chunks.source: Mulch protects soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the safety equipment below and answer questions 28 and 29. Why is the above equipment painted with bright colours? A: To make it easily seen (red signals danger).. Bright colours attract attention.
chunks.source: Bright colours attract attention.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the safety equipment below and answer questions 28 and 29. Name the gas used in the above safety device. A: Carbon dioxide. CO2 puts out fires.
chunks.source: CO2 puts out fires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows the mouth parts of an insect. Use it to answer questions 30 and 31. Name the mouth part shown in the diagram. A: Piercing and sucking mouthpart (proboscis).. The long tube pierces and sucks.
chunks.source: The long tube pierces and sucks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows the mouth parts of an insect. Use it to answer questions 30 and 31. Name one insect with such a mouth part. A: Mosquito. Mosquitoes pierce and suck blood.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes pierce and suck blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the any one difference between mass and weight. A: Mass is constant while weight changes with gravity.. Mass stays; weight varies.
chunks.source: Mass stays; weight varies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which disorder of the digestive system is prevented by eating a lot of roughage? A: Constipation. Roughage prevents constipation.
chunks.source: Roughage prevents constipation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for the cabbage farmer to keep records? A: To know profit or loss.. Records track the business.
chunks.source: Records track the business.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What important role is played by the cilia in the nose? A: They trap dust and germs.. Cilia filter air.
chunks.source: Cilia filter air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the organisms that act as producers in a food chain. A: Green plants. Plants make food.
chunks.source: Plants make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one pest that destroys maize crops. A: Stalk borer. Borers attack maize.
chunks.source: Borers attack maize.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from protecting delicate body organs, give any other function of the human skeleton. A: It gives shape to the body.. The skeleton supports.
chunks.source: The skeleton supports.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one danger caused by presence of many industries in an area. A: Air pollution. Industries pollute air.
chunks.source: Industries pollute air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a component of blood. Name one disease that affects the component of blood shown above. A: Leukaemia (blood cancer).. Leukaemia affects white blood cells.
chunks.source: Leukaemia affects white blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a): Identify the type of leaf venation drawn above. A: Parallel venation. Veins run parallel.
chunks.source: Veins run parallel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b): Name the kind of root system possessed by a plant from which the leaf above was picked. A: Fibrous root system. Parallel-veined (monocot) plants have fibrous roots.
chunks.source: Parallel-veined (monocot) plants have fibrous roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c): Give one example of a plant with the above mentioned root system. A: Maize. Maize has fibrous roots.
chunks.source: Maize has fibrous roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(d): Give another type of leaf venation besides the one shown above. A: Reticulate (network) venation. Net-like veins are reticulate.
chunks.source: Net-like veins are reticulate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a): Name part labeled C. A: Left ventricle. C is the thick-walled left chamber.
chunks.source: C is the thick-walled left chamber.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b): Which type of blood is carried by blood vessel A? A: Oxygenated blood. A (aorta) carries oxygenated blood.
chunks.source: A (aorta) carries oxygenated blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c): Describe the flow of blood through the heart. A: Blood flows from the right atrium to the right ventricle to the lungs, then from the left atrium to the left ventricle to the body.. Blood goes heart→lungs→heart→body.
chunks.source: Blood goes heart→lungs→heart→body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(d): Give one way of maintaining the proper functioning of the above organ. A: By exercising regularly.. Exercise strengthens the heart.
chunks.source: Exercise strengthens the heart.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a): What is seed dispersal A: The scattering of seeds away from the parent plant.. Seeds spread to new places.
chunks.source: Seeds spread to new places.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b): How is seed dispersal useful to plants? A: It reduces competition between seedlings.. Spread seeds grow better.
chunks.source: Spread seeds grow better.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c)(1): Give any two agents of seed dispersal. A: Wind. Wind carries light seeds.
chunks.source: Wind carries light seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c)(2): Give any two agents of seed dispersal. A: Animals. Animals carry seeds.
chunks.source: Animals carry seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a)(1): Identify the items that are supposed to be constructed at A and C. A A: Kitchen. A is 10m from the latrine (kitchen).
chunks.source: A is 10m from the latrine (kitchen).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a)(2): Identify the items that are supposed to be constructed at A and C. C A: Water source (well).. C is 30m from the latrine (water).
chunks.source: C is 30m from the latrine (water).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b): Why should a pit latrine be 30metres away from C? A: To prevent contamination of the water.. Germs must not reach water.
chunks.source: Germs must not reach water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c): Mention one health problem caused by lack of proper sanitation in the community. A: Cholera. Poor sanitation spreads cholera.
chunks.source: Poor sanitation spreads cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(1): Give two examples of wood fuel. A: Firewood. Firewood is wood fuel.
chunks.source: Firewood is wood fuel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(2): Give two examples of wood fuel. A: Charcoal. Charcoal is wood fuel.
chunks.source: Charcoal is wood fuel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b): State one way of conserving wood fuel. A: Using energy-saving stoves.. Stoves save fuel.
chunks.source: Stoves save fuel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c): Why are plants called renewable resources? A: Because they can be replanted.. Trees regrow.
chunks.source: Trees regrow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a): The mass of the stone is 240g and its volume is 30cc. Calculate the density of the stone. (2 marks) A: 8 g/cc. Density = 240 ÷ 30 = 8.
chunks.source: Density = 240 ÷ 30 = 8.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b): The stone (volume 30cc) is immersed in the measuring cylinder. By how much will the water level rise? (2 marks) A: The water level will rise by 30cc (the volume of the stone).. Displaced water equals stone volume.
chunks.source: Displaced water equals stone volume.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a): How is poultry different from poultry keeping? A: Poultry are the birds; poultry keeping is rearing them.. Birds vs the activity.
chunks.source: Birds vs the activity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(1): Give two examples of poultry. A: Chicken. Chickens are poultry.
chunks.source: Chickens are poultry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(2): Give two examples of poultry. A: Duck. Ducks are poultry.
chunks.source: Ducks are poultry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c): Mention one disease that affects poultry on a farm. A: Newcastle disease. Newcastle kills poultry.
chunks.source: Newcastle kills poultry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(1): State the importance of each of the following in administration first aid. splints A: They support broken bones.. Splints hold fractures.
chunks.source: Splints hold fractures.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(2): State the importance of each of the following in administration first aid. arm sling A: It supports an injured arm.. A sling holds the arm.
chunks.source: A sling holds the arm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b): How is a sprain different from a strain? A: A sprain is a torn ligament; a strain is a torn muscle.. Ligament vs muscle.
chunks.source: Ligament vs muscle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c): Why are schools encouraged to only give first aid and not treatment to learners at school? A: Because teachers are not doctors.. Schools give first aid only.
chunks.source: Schools give first aid only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a): Identify one example of a modern hive? A: Top-bar hive (or box hive).. Modern hives are improved.
chunks.source: Modern hives are improved.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b): State the importance of a queen excluder in a hive. A: It keeps the queen out of the honey chamber.. Honey stays brood-free.
chunks.source: Honey stays brood-free.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c)(1): Give the role played by each of the following types of bees in a hive. Drone bees A: They mate with the queen.. Drones fertilize the queen.
chunks.source: Drones fertilize the queen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c)(2): Give the role played by each of the following types of bees in a hive. Worker bees A: They collect nectar and make honey.. Workers do all the work.
chunks.source: Workers do all the work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a): Name parts marked O and P. A: O is the renal vein and P is the ureter.. O carries blood; P carries urine.
chunks.source: O carries blood; P carries urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b): What important process takes place in part M? A: Filtration of blood.. The cortex filters blood.
chunks.source: The cortex filters blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c): Identify any one disease that affects the above organ. A: Kidney stones. Stones affect kidneys.
chunks.source: Stones affect kidneys.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51: How does each of the following animals protect itself against its enemies? Tortoise. A: 51: How does each of the following animals protect itself against its enemies? Tortoise. It withdraws into its hard shell.. The shell protects the tortoise.
chunks.source: The shell protects the tortoise.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51: How does each of the following animals protect itself against its enemies? Wasps. A: 51: How does each of the following animals protect itself against its enemies? Wasps. It stings attackers.. Wasps sting for defence.
chunks.source: Wasps sting for defence.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51: How does each of the following animals protect itself against its enemies? Millipede. A: 51: How does each of the following animals protect itself against its enemies? Millipede. It coils into a ball / produces bad smell.. Coiling protects the millipede.
chunks.source: Coiling protects the millipede.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51: How does each of the following animals protect itself against its enemies? Caterpillar. A: 51: How does each of the following animals protect itself against its enemies? Caterpillar. It has stinging hairs / camouflages.. Hairs deter predators.
chunks.source: Hairs deter predators.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52: Match items in list A to those in list B correctly. A B (i) Nuclear electricity Fast flowing water (ii) Geothermal electricity Burning fossil fuel (iii) Hydroelectricity Hot rocks (iv) Thermal electricity Uranium i) Nuclear electricity ii) Geothermal electricity iii) Hydroelectricity iv) Thermal electricity A: Nuclear electricity: Uranium; Geothermal electricity: Hot rocks; Hydroelectricity: Fast flowing water; Thermal electricity: Burning fossil fuel. Each electricity type matches its source.
chunks.source: Each electricity type matches its source.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a): Name the form of energy that stimulates the sense of hearing. A: Sound energy. Sound stimulates hearing.
chunks.source: Sound stimulates hearing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b): Give one importance of the form of energy named above. A: It enables communication.. Sound carries messages.
chunks.source: Sound carries messages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c): Mention one way of storing the form of energy mentioned above. A: By recording (on tapes/discs).. Sound can be stored.
chunks.source: Sound can be stored.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(d): Point out one device used to reproduce sound. A: Radio (or speaker).. Radios reproduce sound.
chunks.source: Radios reproduce sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a): Name the method of magnetization shown above. A: Electrical method. A coil with current magnetizes.
chunks.source: A coil with current magnetizes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b): Determine pole at X. A: North pole. By the right-hand rule, X is North.
chunks.source: By the right-hand rule, X is North.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c)(1): Give two ways of increasing the strength of magnet made using the above method. A: Increase the number of coils.. More coils strengthen it.
chunks.source: More coils strengthen it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c)(2): Give two ways of increasing the strength of magnet made using the above method. A: Increase the electric current.. More current strengthens it.
chunks.source: More current strengthens it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a): Name layer marked C. A: Parent rock (bedrock).. C is the bottom rock layer.
chunks.source: C is the bottom rock layer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b): Why is layer marked A regarded as the best for plant growth. A: It contains humus and nutrients.. Topsoil is fertile.
chunks.source: Topsoil is fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c): Name the microorganism that help to form layer A. A: Bacteria (decomposers).. Bacteria rot matter into humus.
chunks.source: Bacteria rot matter into humus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(d): Define the term soil profile. A: The vertical arrangement of soil layers (horizons).. Profile shows soil layers.
chunks.source: Profile shows soil layers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the sense organ for tasting. A: The tongue.. The tongue carries taste buds that detect tastes.
chunks.source: The tongue carries taste buds that detect tastes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is personal hygiene? A: Personal hygiene is the practice of keeping one's body clean to stay healthy (e.g. bathing, brushing teeth, washing hands).. Clean habits remove germs and dirt that cause disease.
chunks.source: Clean habits remove germs and dirt that cause disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the main source of heat. A: The sun.. The sun gives out heat (and light) energy to the earth.
chunks.source: The sun gives out heat (and light) energy to the earth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which class of food helps to build the body? A: Proteins (body-building foods).. Proteins are used to build and repair body tissues.
chunks.source: Proteins are used to build and repair body tissues.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest one way of preventing road accidents. A: Observing traffic rules, e.g. driving at a safe speed.. Most accidents are caused by reckless driving and ignoring road signs.
chunks.source: Most accidents are caused by reckless driving and ignoring road signs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we call manufactured food for rabbits? A: Pellets.. Pellets are manufactured (factory-made) feeds for rabbits.
chunks.source: Pellets are manufactured (factory-made) feeds for rabbits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does friction enable us to write on paper? A: Friction between the pen or pencil tip and the paper rubs ink (or graphite) off onto the paper.. Without friction the tip would slide smoothly and leave no mark.
chunks.source: Without friction the tip would slide smoothly and leave no mark.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the germ which causes malaria. A: Plasmodium.. Plasmodium is the protozoan germ transmitted by female anopheles mosquitoes that causes malaria.
chunks.source: Plasmodium is the protozoan germ transmitted by female anopheles mosquitoes that causes malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the polio vaccine given to babies at birth? A: To protect the baby against polio from the earliest time, before it can be exposed to the disease.. Newborns are vulnerable and immunity takes time to build, so vaccination starts at birth.
chunks.source: Newborns are vulnerable and immunity takes time to build, so vaccination starts at birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Below is a diagram, use it to answer the question that follows. Name the structures shown as far as beekeeping is concerned. A: Honeycombs.. The diagram shows bees on honeycombs; in beekeeping the honeycomb is the structure where bees store honey and raise young.
chunks.source: The diagram shows bees on honeycombs; in beekeeping the honeycomb is the structure where bees store honey and raise young.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mukasa wanted to plant a cactus plant for an experiment. In which environment could he find it? A: In a desert / dry (arid) environment.. A cactus is adapted to survive with very little water, as in deserts.
chunks.source: A cactus is adapted to survive with very little water, as in deserts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one exotic breed of rabbits kept in Uganda. A: New Zealand White.. The New Zealand White is a common exotic rabbit breed kept in Uganda.
chunks.source: The New Zealand White is a common exotic rabbit breed kept in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the gas that keeps a piece of wood burning. A: Oxygen.. Oxygen supports burning; without it the fire goes out.
chunks.source: Oxygen supports burning; without it the fire goes out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do some plants climb others? A: To reach sunlight for photosynthesis.. Climbing plants grow up other plants to get light where it is shaded below.
chunks.source: Climbing plants grow up other plants to get light where it is shaded below.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows an iron box. Study it and answer question 15. Give a reason why the handle on the iron box above is made of wood. A: Wood is a poor conductor of heat (an insulator), so the handle does not get hot when the iron box is heated.. A metal handle would conduct heat to the hand and burn it.
chunks.source: A metal handle would conduct heat to the hand and burn it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which mineral salt strengthens our bones and teeth? A: Calcium.. Calcium hardens bones and teeth.
chunks.source: Calcium hardens bones and teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can the quality of local breeds of chicken be improved? A: By crossbreeding them with high-quality exotic breeds (selective breeding).. Crossbreeding passes good traits like fast growth to the offspring.
chunks.source: Crossbreeding passes good traits like fast growth to the offspring.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the food value obtained from eating honey. A: Carbohydrates (energy).. Honey is a sugary food that gives the body energy.
chunks.source: Honey is a sugary food that gives the body energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is soil profile? A: Soil profile is the vertical arrangement of soil layers (horizons) from the topsoil down to the bedrock.. Digging down shows distinct layers, together called the profile.
chunks.source: Digging down shows distinct layers, together called the profile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest one cause of soil erosion. A: Deforestation (cutting down trees leaves soil bare).. Without plant cover, running water and wind carry soil away easily.
chunks.source: Without plant cover, running water and wind carry soil away easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the chief producer of food in a food path. A: Green plants.. Green plants make food by photosynthesis and start every food path.
chunks.source: Green plants make food by photosynthesis and start every food path.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the use of spiracles to a grasshopper? A: For breathing (taking in air).. A grasshopper breathes through tiny openings called spiracles on its abdomen.
chunks.source: A grasshopper breathes through tiny openings called spiracles on its abdomen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below is of a thermometer. Study it carefully and answer the questions that follow. What is the function of the part marked A? A: It holds the mercury (the liquid that expands with heat and rises up the tube).. The bulb is the reservoir of mercury at the end of the thermometer.
chunks.source: The bulb is the reservoir of mercury at the end of the thermometer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the above instrument useful to a health worker? A: It is used to measure body temperature (to detect fever).. A health worker checks temperature to know if a patient has fever.
chunks.source: A health worker checks temperature to know if a patient has fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are the petals of a flower brightly coloured? A: To attract pollinators such as insects.. Bright petals guide insects to the flower for pollination.
chunks.source: Bright petals guide insects to the flower for pollination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the space provided, draw an incisor tooth. A: A drawing of an incisor: a tooth with a broad, flat, chisel-shaped crown for cutting and biting, with a single root.. Incisors are the front teeth used for cutting food.
chunks.source: Incisors are the front teeth used for cutting food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write P.H.C in full. A: Primary Health Care.. PHC is basic health care given in the community to prevent disease.
chunks.source: PHC is basic health care given in the community to prevent disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is transpiration? A: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from plant leaves (mainly through the stomata).. Plants give off excess water as vapour into the air.
chunks.source: Plants give off excess water as vapour into the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which stage is a nymph in the life cycle of a cockroach? A: The second stage (between the egg and the adult).. A cockroach life cycle is egg → nymph → adult; the nymph is the young stage.
chunks.source: A cockroach life cycle is egg → nymph → adult; the nymph is the young stage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one quality of a good first aider. A: Being calm (and quick to act).. A calm first aider thinks clearly and helps without panic.
chunks.source: A calm first aider thinks clearly and helps without panic.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the use of ventilators in a house? A: To let fresh air in and stale air out (ventilation).. Ventilators keep air in the house fresh and cool.
chunks.source: Ventilators keep air in the house fresh and cool.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one disease which affects bananas. A: Banana bacterial wilt.. Bacterial wilt is a serious disease of bananas in Uganda.
chunks.source: Bacterial wilt is a serious disease of bananas in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are insulators put on electric wires? A: To prevent electric shock and stop current leaking to poles or people.. Insulators do not conduct electricity, so the current stays in the wire.
chunks.source: Insulators do not conduct electricity, so the current stays in the wire.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are gaps left in between railway lines? A: To leave room for the rails to expand on hot days.. Metal expands when heated; without gaps the rails would buckle.
chunks.source: Metal expands when heated; without gaps the rails would buckle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one item used to keep our environment clean. A: A dustbin (or broom).. Waste is collected in dustbins so it does not litter the environment.
chunks.source: Waste is collected in dustbins so it does not litter the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of energy is possessed by passengers in a moving car? A: Kinetic energy.. Anything moving possesses kinetic (movement) energy.
chunks.source: Anything moving possesses kinetic (movement) energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the mixture of two or more metals? A: An alloy.. An alloy is made by mixing two or more metals, e.g. brass.
chunks.source: An alloy is made by mixing two or more metals, e.g. brass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one use of ligaments in the body. A: They join bones to bones at joints.. Ligaments hold the skeleton together at movable joints.
chunks.source: Ligaments hold the skeleton together at movable joints.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest one reason why people eat food. A: To get energy and nutrients for growth, body building and staying healthy.. Food provides everything the body needs to work and grow.
chunks.source: Food provides everything the body needs to work and grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a): What do we call the process by which green plants make their food? A: Photosynthesis.. Green plants make their food by photosynthesis using sunlight.
chunks.source: Green plants make their food by photosynthesis using sunlight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b): Name one raw material used in photosynthesis (the process named in (a) above). A: Carbon dioxide (or water).. Plants take in carbon dioxide from air and water from the soil as raw materials.
chunks.source: Plants take in carbon dioxide from air and water from the soil as raw materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c): How does photosynthesis help to purify the environment? A: It absorbs carbon dioxide from the air and releases oxygen, keeping the air fresh.. This gas exchange cleans the air we breathe.
chunks.source: This gas exchange cleans the air we breathe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(d): Name the main product of photosynthesis (the process named in (a) above). A: Starch (glucose).. The main food made is glucose, stored as starch; oxygen is released as a by-product.
chunks.source: The main food made is glucose, stored as starch; oxygen is released as a by-product.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a): What does the term castration mean in cattle rearing? A: Castration is the removal (or crushing) of the testes of a bull.. Removing the testes stops the bull producing sperms and male hormones.
chunks.source: Removing the testes stops the bull producing sperms and male hormones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b)(i): State two reasons why cattle keepers castrate bulls. (i) A: To make bulls calm and easy to handle.. Castrated bulls (bullocks) are less aggressive.
chunks.source: Castrated bulls (bullocks) are less aggressive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b)(ii): State two reasons why cattle keepers castrate bulls. (ii) A: To fatten them faster for beef.. Bullocks put on weight quickly, giving more meat.
chunks.source: Bullocks put on weight quickly, giving more meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c): Give one disadvantage of artificial insemination in cattle reproduction. A: It is expensive / needs a trained technician (and correct heat detection).. AI requires equipment, skill and good timing, which small farmers may lack.
chunks.source: AI requires equipment, skill and good timing, which small farmers may lack.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(i): The diagram below is of a tapeworm. Use it to answer the questions that follow. Name the part labeled P. A: Scolex (the head).. P points to the head of the tapeworm, which has hooks and suckers.
chunks.source: P points to the head of the tapeworm, which has hooks and suckers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(ii): The diagram below is of a tapeworm. Use it to answer the questions that follow. Name the part labeled Q. A: Proglottids (the segments).. Q points to the body segments of the tapeworm.
chunks.source: Q points to the body segments of the tapeworm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b): State the use of part Q (the segments) to the tapeworm. A: They produce and carry eggs (reproduction).. Each mature segment is full of eggs that pass out to continue the life cycle.
chunks.source: Each mature segment is full of eggs that pass out to continue the life cycle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c): Mention one way a person can get tapeworms into his body. A: By eating undercooked beef or pork containing bladder worms.. The bladder worms develop into tapeworms in the intestines.
chunks.source: The bladder worms develop into tapeworms in the intestines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a)(i): State two reasons why people smoke. (i) A: Peer pressure (to copy friends).. Many start smoking to fit in with friends.
chunks.source: Many start smoking to fit in with friends.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a)(ii): State two reasons why people smoke. (ii) A: Addiction to nicotine / to relieve stress.. Nicotine is addictive, so smokers find it hard to stop.
chunks.source: Nicotine is addictive, so smokers find it hard to stop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b): Name one dangerous gas found in tobacco smoke. A: Carbon monoxide.. Carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas in tobacco smoke that reduces oxygen in blood.
chunks.source: Carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas in tobacco smoke that reduces oxygen in blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c): Why would you advise a smoker to stop the habit? A: Smoking causes deadly diseases like lung cancer and harms non-smokers nearby.. Stopping protects both the smoker's health and others from passive smoking.
chunks.source: Stopping protects both the smoker's health and others from passive smoking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a): Lwasa put four spoonfuls of sugar in a cupful of clean water. He stirred until the crystals of sugar could not be seen. What happened to the sugar crystals? A: They dissolved in the water.. Stirring spreads the sugar particles evenly until they disappear into the water.
chunks.source: Stirring spreads the sugar particles evenly until they disappear into the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b): Lwasa put four spoonfuls of sugar in a cupful of clean water. He stirred until the crystals of sugar could not be seen. What do we call a mixture of sugar and water? A: A solution.. A uniform mixture of a solute in a solvent is a solution.
chunks.source: A uniform mixture of a solute in a solvent is a solution.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c): Apart from sugar, name any other example of a solute. A: Salt (common salt).. Salt also dissolves in water like sugar.
chunks.source: Salt also dissolves in water like sugar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(d): If Lwasa wanted to get back his sugar, which method would he use? A: Evaporation (heating the solution so water escapes, leaving sugar).. Heating drives off the water and the dissolved sugar is left behind.
chunks.source: Heating drives off the water and the dissolved sugar is left behind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a): What are birds of prey? A: Birds of prey are birds that hunt and feed on other animals.. They have sharp beaks and talons for catching prey.
chunks.source: They have sharp beaks and talons for catching prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b): Give one example of birds of prey. A: An eagle (or hawk/kite).. Eagles are strong hunting birds.
chunks.source: Eagles are strong hunting birds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c): Why is a free range system of poultry keeping not good in an area where there are many preying birds? A: The preying birds would kill and eat the free-ranging chicken.. Free range birds are exposed with no protection from hunters.
chunks.source: Free range birds are exposed with no protection from hunters.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(d): How is a vulture different from an eagle in terms of feeding? A: A vulture feeds on carrion (dead animals) while an eagle hunts live prey.. Vultures scavenge; eagles are active hunters.
chunks.source: Vultures scavenge; eagles are active hunters.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a): Why is a piece of wood called matter? A: Because it has mass and occupies space.. Anything with mass and volume is matter.
chunks.source: Anything with mass and volume is matter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b): In which state of matter is ice at room temperature? A: Liquid (it melts into water).. Ice melts at room temperature, becoming liquid water.
chunks.source: Ice melts at room temperature, becoming liquid water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c): What is the effect of heat on matter? A: Heat makes matter expand and can change its state (e.g. solid to liquid).. Heating increases particle movement, causing expansion or melting.
chunks.source: Heating increases particle movement, causing expansion or melting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(d): In which state of matter does heat travel fastest? A: In solids (by conduction).. Heat conducts fastest through solids, especially metals.
chunks.source: Heat conducts fastest through solids, especially metals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(i): Study the diagram of an onion below and answer the questions that follow. Name the part labeled A. A: Leaves (foliage leaves).. A points to the green leaves growing above the bulb.
chunks.source: A points to the green leaves growing above the bulb.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(ii): Study the diagram of an onion below and answer the questions that follow. Name the part labeled B. A: Roots (adventitious roots).. B points to the roots growing beneath the bulb.
chunks.source: B points to the roots growing beneath the bulb.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b): What type of root system does the onion have? A: Adventitious (fibrous) roots.. Onions grow many thin roots from the base of the bulb, not one tap root.
chunks.source: Onions grow many thin roots from the base of the bulb, not one tap root.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c): How is an onion propagated? A: By planting onion bulbs (sets).. A bulb planted in soil grows into a new onion plant.
chunks.source: A bulb planted in soil grows into a new onion plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a): What is immunity? A: Immunity is the body's ability to resist or fight disease-causing germs.. The body defends itself using white blood cells and antibodies.
chunks.source: The body defends itself using white blood cells and antibodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(i): Identify any two types of immunity. (i) A: Natural immunity.. Immunity one is born with or gains after recovering from disease.
chunks.source: Immunity one is born with or gains after recovering from disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(ii): Identify any two types of immunity. (ii) A: Artificial immunity.. Immunity gained through vaccination.
chunks.source: Immunity gained through vaccination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c): Give any one symptom of a person whose immunity is very low. A: Falling sick very often / failing to recover from infections.. A weak immune system cannot fight germs, so illness repeats.
chunks.source: A weak immune system cannot fight germs, so illness repeats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a): What is a resource? A: A resource is anything in the environment that people use to meet their needs.. Water, soil, forests and minerals are all resources.
chunks.source: Water, soil, forests and minerals are all resources.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b): Mention one example of a living renewable resource. A: Trees (forests).. Trees are living resources that grow again (renewable).
chunks.source: Trees are living resources that grow again (renewable).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c): Give one way in which man degrades the environment. A: Through deforestation / bush burning / pollution.. Cutting trees and dumping waste spoil the environment.
chunks.source: Cutting trees and dumping waste spoil the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(d): Suggest one way man can conserve forests. A: By planting more trees (afforestation/re-afforestation).. Replacing cut trees keeps forests for the future.
chunks.source: Replacing cut trees keeps forests for the future.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a): Which part of a fertilized egg develops into a chick? A: The embryo (germinal disc).. The tiny embryo on the yolk grows into the chick.
chunks.source: The tiny embryo on the yolk grows into the chick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b): Why is an eggshell porous? A: To allow air (oxygen) to pass through to the developing embryo.. The pores let the embryo breathe by gaseous exchange.
chunks.source: The pores let the embryo breathe by gaseous exchange.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(c): Give one reason why some chicken lay eggs that have soft shells. A: Lack of calcium in the hen's diet.. Calcium hardens the shell; without enough, shells stay soft.
chunks.source: Calcium hardens the shell; without enough, shells stay soft.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(d): How do layers (in poultry) contribute to the health of people in a community? A: They provide eggs, a protein-rich food for the community.. Eating eggs improves nutrition and health.
chunks.source: Eating eggs improves nutrition and health.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a): The diagrams below show two types of blood vessels (A and B). Name the blood vessels shown above. A: A is a vein and B is an artery.. A is wider with valves (vein); B is narrower with thick walls (artery).
chunks.source: A is wider with valves (vein); B is narrower with thick walls (artery).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b): State one structural difference between vessels A and B. A: Vessel A (vein) has valves and thinner walls with a wider lumen, while vessel B (artery) has thicker muscular walls, a narrower lumen and no valves.. Veins carry blood back at low pressure; arteries carry it at high pressure.
chunks.source: Veins carry blood back at low pressure; arteries carry it at high pressure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c): What is the importance of part Y (the valves) in blood vessel A? A: The valves (Y) prevent the backflow of blood, keeping it flowing towards the heart.. Valves act like one-way doors in veins.
chunks.source: Valves act like one-way doors in veins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(i): The diagram shows a simple electric circuit. Use it to answer the questions. Name part V. A: V is a connecting wire (conductor).. V joins the components so current can flow round the circuit.
chunks.source: V joins the components so current can flow round the circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(ii): The diagram shows a simple electric circuit. Use it to answer the questions. Name part D. A: D is the (electric) bulb.. The symbol D in the circuit diagram represents the electric bulb, which gives light when current flows.
chunks.source: The symbol D in the circuit diagram represents the electric bulb, which gives light when current flows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b): The diagram shows a simple electric circuit. If Q is closed, give one reason why D would not light. A: The bulb could be faulty (fused filament) or the dry cell (battery) is used up / connections are loose.. If any part fails, no current flows and the bulb stays dark.
chunks.source: If any part fails, no current flows and the bulb stays dark.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c): How is part marked S useful in the above circuit? A: S is a fuse; it melts and breaks the circuit if the current becomes too high, protecting the other parts.. The fuse sacrifices itself to save the bulb and wires.
chunks.source: The fuse sacrifices itself to save the bulb and wires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a): What is a skeleton? A: A skeleton is the framework of bones that supports the body.. Bones joined together form the skeleton.
chunks.source: Bones joined together form the skeleton.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b): Name the longest bone in a human body. A: The femur (thigh bone).. The femur is the longest and strongest bone.
chunks.source: The femur is the longest and strongest bone.

chunks.subject: Science
