chunks.text: Q: 55(c)(i): State two uses of a skeleton in a human body. (i) A: It supports the body and gives it shape.. Without the skeleton the body would collapse.
chunks.source: Without the skeleton the body would collapse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c)(ii): State two uses of a skeleton in a human body. (ii) A: It protects delicate body organs (e.g. the skull protects the brain).. Hard bones shield soft organs from injury.
chunks.source: Hard bones shield soft organs from injury.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(i): Match the items in List M (Arachnids, Myriapods, Crustaceans, Mollusc) with those in List N (centipede, spider, snails, crabs). Which item in List M matches 'centipede'? A: Myriapods: centipede. A centipede has many legs and belongs to the myriapods.
chunks.source: A centipede has many legs and belongs to the myriapods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(ii): Match the items in List M (Arachnids, Myriapods, Crustaceans, Mollusc) with those in List N (centipede, spider, snails, crabs). Which item in List M matches 'spider'? A: Arachnids: spider. Spiders have eight legs and belong to the arachnids.
chunks.source: Spiders have eight legs and belong to the arachnids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(iii): Match the items in List M (Arachnids, Myriapods, Crustaceans, Mollusc) with those in List N (centipede, spider, snails, crabs). Which item in List M matches 'snails'? A: Mollusc: snails. Snails are soft-bodied animals grouped as molluscs.
chunks.source: Snails are soft-bodied animals grouped as molluscs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(iv): Match the items in List M (Arachnids, Myriapods, Crustaceans, Mollusc) with those in List N (centipede, spider, snails, crabs). Which item in List M matches 'crabs'? A: Crustaceans: crabs. Crabs are water animals with hard shells grouped as crustaceans.
chunks.source: Crabs are water animals with hard shells grouped as crustaceans.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the body sense that helps to tell the taste of sugar in tea. A: The sense of taste.. Taste buds on the tongue tell the taste of food and drink.
chunks.source: Taste buds on the tongue tell the taste of food and drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why farmers mulch their gardens. A: To conserve soil moisture (and fertility).. Mulch covers soil, reducing water loss and erosion.
chunks.source: Mulch covers soil, reducing water loss and erosion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does a fish die when removed out of the water? A: Its gills dry out in air, so it cannot breathe.. Fish breathe with gills that only work in water.
chunks.source: Fish breathe with gills that only work in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does refrigeration prevent milk from going bad? A: Cold slows down (stops) bacteria from multiplying.. Refrigeration keeps bacteria dormant so milk stays fresh.
chunks.source: Refrigeration keeps bacteria dormant so milk stays fresh.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Use the diagram to answer the questions that follow. Identify one bird with this type of foot. A: A duck (a swimming bird).. The diagram shows a webbed foot, found on swimming birds like ducks.
chunks.source: The diagram shows a webbed foot, found on swimming birds like ducks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How useful is such type of feet to this group of birds? A: For swimming (paddling) in water.. Webbed feet act like paddles for swimming birds.
chunks.source: Webbed feet act like paddles for swimming birds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the role of sunlight during photosynthesis? A: It provides the (light) energy needed for photosynthesis.. Sunlight supplies energy that plants convert into food.
chunks.source: Sunlight supplies energy that plants convert into food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the use of a vent pipe different from that of a screen? A: A vent pipe removes bad smell/stale air from the pit, while a screen traps houseflies.. Each part of a VIP latrine has a different job.
chunks.source: Each part of a VIP latrine has a different job.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where does the tsetse fly lay its eggs? A: Inside its abdomen (it hatches the eggs internally and lays larvae in the soil).. The tsetse fly is larviparous; larvae develop in the mother.
chunks.source: The tsetse fly is larviparous; larvae develop in the mother.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the importance of the garden tool below to a crop farmer. A: It is used to dig rocky soil / harvest root crops / narrow the garden.. A rake breaks and levels soil for the farmer.
chunks.source: A rake breaks and levels soil for the farmer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What physical process changes ice to gas? A: Sublimation.. Sublimation is the change from solid directly to gas.
chunks.source: Sublimation is the change from solid directly to gas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one disadvantage of friction in machines as a nuisance force. A: It causes wear and tear of machine parts (and wastes energy as heat).. Friction wears moving parts and slows machines.
chunks.source: Friction wears moving parts and slows machines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the use of a fuse in an electric circuit. A: It protects appliances by breaking the circuit when current is too high.. The fuse melts and stops excess current from damaging appliances.
chunks.source: The fuse melts and stops excess current from damaging appliances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram and answer the questions that follow. Name the pole of the magnet marked X. A: The North pole.. The marked pole X is the north-seeking pole.
chunks.source: The marked pole X is the north-seeking pole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the property of magnets shown above. A: A magnet is strongest at its poles.. Magnetic force is concentrated at the two poles.
chunks.source: Magnetic force is concentrated at the two poles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from bats, name one vertebrate that makes echoes in the environment. A: Whales (or dolphins).. Whales and dolphins use echoes to navigate like bats.
chunks.source: Whales and dolphins use echoes to navigate like bats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one sex offence common in schools today. A: Rape (or defilement).. These are sexual offences reported in schools.
chunks.source: These are sexual offences reported in schools.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one danger of sharing a room with potted plants at night. A: Plants use up oxygen for respiration at night, competing with the sleeper.. At night plants respire like animals, taking in oxygen.
chunks.source: At night plants respire like animals, taking in oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are electric wires fixed loosely on the poles during their connection? A: To leave room for contraction on cold days, so wires do not snap.. Wires contract when cold; loose fixing prevents breaking.
chunks.source: Wires contract when cold; loose fixing prevents breaking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one insect pest that attacks root crops. A: Potato weevils.. Weevils attack root crops like potatoes.
chunks.source: Weevils attack root crops like potatoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Calculate the density of an object whose mass is 10gm and volume 40cc. A: 0.25 g/cc.. Density = mass/volume = 10g/40cc = 0.25 g/cc.
chunks.source: Density = mass/volume = 10g/40cc = 0.25 g/cc.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from wearing shoes, suggest one other way of preventing hookworm infection. A: Washing hands after using the latrine (and washing fruits/vegetables).. Hookworm larvae enter through dirty hands and unwashed food.
chunks.source: Hookworm larvae enter through dirty hands and unwashed food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How useful are tendons at a joint? A: They join muscles to bones at joints.. Tendons transmit the pull of muscles to bones for movement.
chunks.source: Tendons transmit the pull of muscles to bones for movement.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one insect that protects itself by stinging apart from bees. A: Wasps (or soldier ants).. Wasps sting to defend themselves.
chunks.source: Wasps sting to defend themselves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the gestation period of a ewe? A: 5 months (about 150 days).. A ewe carries the lamb for about five months.
chunks.source: A ewe carries the lamb for about five months.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one health reason for ironing clothes. A: To kill germs/parasites and remove bad smell.. Heat from ironing kills germs on clothes.
chunks.source: Heat from ironing kills germs on clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a part of a flowering plant (a pumpkin). Name the importance of the part marked M to a pumpkin. A: It helps the pumpkin climb by gripping supports, reaching sunlight.. Tendrils coil around supports so the weak stem climbs up.
chunks.source: Tendrils coil around supports so the weak stem climbs up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one human activity that results into air pollution. A: Bush burning (or exhaust fumes from vehicles / industrial waste).. Burning and fumes release smoke and gases into the air.
chunks.source: Burning and fumes release smoke and gases into the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides using a child health card, how can you identify a child who has been immunized against tuberculosis? A: By checking the BCG scar on the right upper arm.. The TB vaccine leaves a scar on the upper arm.
chunks.source: The TB vaccine leaves a scar on the upper arm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one natural method of controlling rats in a home. A: Keeping a cat to eat rats.. Cats are natural predators of rats.
chunks.source: Cats are natural predators of rats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a housefly useful in a home during the larvae stage? A: The maggots break down faeces, reducing its volume in the pit latrine.. Housefly larvae feed on and decompose faeces.
chunks.source: Housefly larvae feed on and decompose faeces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one importance of PIASCY messages at school. A: To protect pupils from HIV/STDs, early pregnancies and dropping out of school.. PIASCY messages teach youth about AIDS prevention.
chunks.source: PIASCY messages teach youth about AIDS prevention.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one activity family members can do to promote personal hygiene. A: Bathing (and washing clothes / brushing teeth).. Clean bodies prevent skin diseases and germs.
chunks.source: Clean bodies prevent skin diseases and germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is lightning formed during a thunderstorm? A: By the discharge of electrons between clouds, or between clouds and the earth.. Built-up charges jump as lightning during storms.
chunks.source: Built-up charges jump as lightning during storms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is an approaching plane seen before the sound is heard when it is overhead? A: Light travels faster than sound.. Light reaches us almost instantly; sound takes longer.
chunks.source: Light reaches us almost instantly; sound takes longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you separate a mixture of sugar and powder of steel wire? A: By using a magnet to attract the iron (steel) powder.. Magnets pull magnetic materials out of mixtures.
chunks.source: Magnets pull magnetic materials out of mixtures.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the importance of a health survey to the government. A: To help the government plan social services.. Survey data guides health planning for the population.
chunks.source: Survey data guides health planning for the population.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How important is a stretcher in carrying out first aid? A: It carries casualties who cannot walk.. A stretcher moves injured people safely.
chunks.source: A stretcher moves injured people safely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the role of the part marked Q to the eye of a dog. A: It receives light and forms images (sent to the brain for sight).. Q is the retina, the light-sensitive layer of the eye.
chunks.source: Q is the retina, the light-sensitive layer of the eye.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should a baby who has swallowed jik when washing be made to vomit? A: Vomiting may damage other body organs (the corrosive burns the throat again on the way up).. Jik is corrosive; bringing it back up causes more burns.
chunks.source: Jik is corrosive; bringing it back up causes more burns.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a): What is germination? A: Germination is the development of a seed into a seedling.. A seed sprouts and grows into a young plant.
chunks.source: A seed sprouts and grows into a young plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b): Identify the type of germination undergone by groundnuts. A: Epigeal germination.. In groundnuts the cotyledons are carried above the soil.
chunks.source: In groundnuts the cotyledons are carried above the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c): Besides water and oxygen, give one other condition necessary for seed germination. A: Warmth (suitable temperature).. Seeds need warmth besides water and oxygen to sprout.
chunks.source: Seeds need warmth besides water and oxygen to sprout.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(d): What type of leaf venation does a groundnut have? A: Reticulate (network) venation.. Groundnut is a dicot, with net-like leaf veins.
chunks.source: Groundnut is a dicot, with net-like leaf veins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(i): The diagram shows the internal structure of a bird's egg. Name part W. A: Chalaza (twisted albumen).. W is the chalaza, the cord holding the yolk in place.
chunks.source: W is the chalaza, the cord holding the yolk in place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(ii): The diagram shows the internal structure of a bird's egg. Name part Z. A: Albumen (egg white).. Z points to the albumen surrounding the yolk.
chunks.source: Z points to the albumen surrounding the yolk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b): Besides protection, give one use of part X (the shell) to an egg. A: It gives the egg its shape and allows gaseous exchange (it is porous).. The shell holds the egg together while letting air through.
chunks.source: The shell holds the egg together while letting air through.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c): Why may a fertilized egg fail to hatch? A: If the air space is blocked, the embryo fails to get air (or if the egg is cracked / not incubated).. The embryo needs air and warmth to develop.
chunks.source: The embryo needs air and warmth to develop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(i): Give any two problems an adolescent girl who gets pregnant may face besides dropping out of school. (i) A: Forced / early marriage.. Pregnant girls are often forced into early marriage.
chunks.source: Pregnant girls are often forced into early marriage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(ii): Give any two problems an adolescent girl who gets pregnant may face besides dropping out of school. (ii) A: She may get STDs, face stigma/rejection, or die in delivery.. Young mothers face health and social dangers.
chunks.source: Young mothers face health and social dangers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(i): Identify any two groups of people who are vulnerable to AIDS. (i) A: Distant truck drivers / businessmen / traders.. People who travel and stay away from home are more exposed.
chunks.source: People who travel and stay away from home are more exposed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(ii): Identify any two groups of people who are vulnerable to AIDS. (ii) A: Street kids / soldiers / sex workers.. These groups face higher risk of HIV infection.
chunks.source: These groups face higher risk of HIV infection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a): Identify any one common drug of dependence. A: Alcohol (or tobacco / marijuana).. These are commonly abused drugs of dependence.
chunks.source: These are commonly abused drugs of dependence.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b): Identify any one common drug of dependence. Give one reason why people commonly abuse drugs. A: Peer pressure / to feel happy or mature.. Many abuse drugs to copy friends or escape problems.
chunks.source: Many abuse drugs to copy friends or escape problems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c)(i): State any two dangers of drug abuse to an individual. (i) A: Brain damage / loss of job / personal neglect.. Drugs harm the abuser's health and livelihood.
chunks.source: Drugs harm the abuser's health and livelihood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c)(ii): State any two dangers of drug abuse to a family. (ii) A: Loss of family income / family neglect / spouse abuse.. Drug abuse drains money and breaks families.
chunks.source: Drug abuse drains money and breaks families.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a): How is a strain different from a sprain? A: A strain is a torn/overstretched tendon (affects muscles); a sprain is a torn/overstretched ligament (affects joints).. Tendons join muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone.
chunks.source: Tendons join muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b)(i): Write down any one disorder of the muscles. (i) A: Cramp (or spasm / muscle tear).. Cramps are painful muscle contractions.
chunks.source: Cramps are painful muscle contractions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b)(ii): Write down any one disorder of the bones. (ii) A: Fracture (or crack).. A fracture is a broken bone.
chunks.source: A fracture is a broken bone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c): Give one health habit that helps to keep the skeletal system in healthy working condition. A: Eating a balanced diet (and doing physical exercise).. Good food and exercise keep bones and joints strong.
chunks.source: Good food and exercise keep bones and joints strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a): The diagram shows a vacuum flask (domestic appliance). Name part C. A: The vacuum seal (stopper).. C is the seal that closes the flask.
chunks.source: C is the seal that closes the flask.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b): How does part B work? A: It prevents heat loss or gain by radiation (the silvery walls reflect heat).. Shiny walls bounce heat back, keeping contents hot or cold.
chunks.source: Shiny walls bounce heat back, keeping contents hot or cold.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c): Name any one material used to make part A. A: Plastic (or wood / rubber).. The outer case is made of an insulating material.
chunks.source: The outer case is made of an insulating material.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(d): Give one use of the instrument above at home. A: To keep hot things hot and cold things cold.. A vacuum flask stores drinks at their temperature.
chunks.source: A vacuum flask stores drinks at their temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a): Name one natural component of soil. A: Bacteria (and earthworms / termites).. Living organisms are natural soil components.
chunks.source: Living organisms are natural soil components.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b): Apart from weathering, give one way how soil is formed. A: Through decomposition of organic matter (by organisms).. Rotting plants and animals form soil.
chunks.source: Rotting plants and animals form soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c): What role do earthworms play in soil formation? A: They aerate the soil and their droppings make it fertile.. Earthworm burrows let air in; droppings add nutrients.
chunks.source: Earthworm burrows let air in; droppings add nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(d): What is soil exhaustion? A: Loss of soil fertility from continuous cropping without rest or manure.. Overused soil loses its nutrients.
chunks.source: Overused soil loses its nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a): The diagram shows a food chain (Grass → grasshopper → bird → snake, numbered 1 to 4). Use arrows to show the relationship between the organisms numbered from 1 to 4. A: Grass → grasshopper → bird → snake.. Arrows show who is eaten by whom along the chain.
chunks.source: Arrows show who is eaten by whom along the chain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b): What name is given to this kind of relationship? A: Food chain.. A feeding series of organisms is a food chain.
chunks.source: A feeding series of organisms is a food chain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c): What is the feeding group name given to organisms labeled 3? A: Primary consumers.. Organism 3 (the grasshopper) feeds directly on the producer.
chunks.source: Organism 3 (the grasshopper) feeds directly on the producer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(d): Give the role of organism 4 in the environment. A: They make food, purify air and give out oxygen.. Organism 4 (grass) is the producer.
chunks.source: Organism 4 (grass) is the producer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a): What are inexhaustible resources? A: Resources that cannot be used up.. They remain no matter how much is used, e.g. sunlight.
chunks.source: They remain no matter how much is used, e.g. sunlight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(i): Give two ways of conserving trees as a natural resource. (i) A: Afforestation (planting trees).. Planting trees replaces those cut down.
chunks.source: Planting trees replaces those cut down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(ii): Give two ways of conserving trees as a natural resource. (ii) A: Re-afforestation / agro-forestry.. More trees are planted and protected.
chunks.source: More trees are planted and protected.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c): How does a clay stove conserve heat? A: Clay is a poor conductor of heat, so it retains heat and loses it slowly.. The clay walls keep warmth inside longer.
chunks.source: The clay walls keep warmth inside longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a): To which group of vertebrates does a tadpole belong? A: Amphibians.. Tadpoles are young amphibians (frogs).
chunks.source: Tadpoles are young amphibians (frogs).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b): Give one importance of tadpoles in our environment. A: They control malaria by eating mosquito larvae.. Tadpoles feed on larvae in water.
chunks.source: Tadpoles feed on larvae in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c): How is breathing of a tadpole different from its adult? A: A tadpole breathes with gills while the adult breathes with lungs (or moist skin).. Breathing organs change at metamorphosis.
chunks.source: Breathing organs change at metamorphosis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a): Apart from kidney, name one other excretory organ protected by the skeleton. A: The lungs (protected by the ribs).. Ribs shield the lungs in the chest.
chunks.source: Ribs shield the lungs in the chest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b): Name the excretory product secreted by the kidneys. A: Urine.. Kidneys filter blood and make urine.
chunks.source: Kidneys filter blood and make urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(c): Give one disease of the skin. A: Scabies (or eczema / ringworms).. Scabies is a common skin disease.
chunks.source: Scabies is a common skin disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(d): State one way of keeping the skin in a good working condition. A: Bathing regularly (and eating a balanced diet).. Clean skin stays healthy.
chunks.source: Clean skin stays healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a): The diagram below shows an electric bulb. Name part R. A: The glass envelope (bulb).. R is the glass outer part of the lamp.
chunks.source: R is the glass outer part of the lamp.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b): Why is oxygen gas not used in part S (inside the bulb)? A: Oxygen supports burning, so it would burn off the filament.. The filament would burn out in oxygen.
chunks.source: The filament would burn out in oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c): Give a reason why part T (the filament) is usually coiled. A: To increase its electrical resistance (and glowing surface area).. A coiled thin wire resists current and glows brightly.
chunks.source: A coiled thin wire resists current and glows brightly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(d): Identify any one gas found in part S. A: Nitrogen (or argon / neon).. Inactive gases fill the bulb so the filament lasts.
chunks.source: Inactive gases fill the bulb so the filament lasts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a): Give the importance of a pulley at school besides pulling up or down the school flag. A: For drawing curtains / lifting building materials.. Pulleys change the direction of force for lifting.
chunks.source: Pulleys change the direction of force for lifting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b): Calculate the effort needed to lift a load of 200N using a single movable pulley. A: 100 N.. Effort = Load / MA = 200N / 2 = 100N for a single movable pulley.
chunks.source: Effort = Load / MA = 200N / 2 = 100N for a single movable pulley.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c): Give one factor that may reduce the efficiency of a pulley. A: Friction (between the rope and pulley).. Friction wastes some effort as heat.
chunks.source: Friction wastes some effort as heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a): What is food preservation? A: Food preservation is keeping food free from germs or contamination (so it lasts).. Preserved food stays safe to eat longer.
chunks.source: Preserved food stays safe to eat longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(i): Name two modern methods of food preservation. (i) A: Refrigeration.. Cold keeps germs dormant.
chunks.source: Cold keeps germs dormant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(ii): Name two modern methods of food preservation. (ii) A: Canning (or pasteurization / deep frying).. Sealed tins keep food from germs.
chunks.source: Sealed tins keep food from germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c): What is food insecurity in the conservation of food? A: Food insecurity is the lack of reliable access to enough safe, nutritious food.. Without good conservation, food runs out or spoils.
chunks.source: Without good conservation, food runs out or spoils.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(d): Name one animal that belongs to the same group as a tadpole. A: A newt (or salamander).. Newts and salamanders are amphibians like frogs (tadpoles grow into frogs).
chunks.source: Newts and salamanders are amphibians like frogs (tadpoles grow into frogs).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a): Match items in A with those in B. A: (i) Storage of semen, (ii) Welding metals, (iii) Making electric bulbs, (iv) Preservation of drinks. B: Carbon dioxide, rare gases, Oxygen, Carbon monoxide, Nitrogen. Which gas in B matches 'Storage of semen'? A: Storage of semen: Nitrogen. Semen is stored frozen using liquid nitrogen.
chunks.source: Semen is stored frozen using liquid nitrogen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b): Match items in A with those in B. Which gas in B matches 'Welding metals'? A: Welding metals: Oxygen. Oxy-acetylene welding uses oxygen for a hot flame.
chunks.source: Oxy-acetylene welding uses oxygen for a hot flame.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c): Match items in A with those in B. Which gas in B matches 'Making electric bulbs'? A: Making electric bulbs: rare gases. Bulbs are filled with inactive (rare) gases like argon.
chunks.source: Bulbs are filled with inactive (rare) gases like argon.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(d): Match items in A with those in B. Which gas in B matches 'Preservation of drinks'? A: Preservation of drinks: Carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide carbonates and preserves soft drinks.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide carbonates and preserves soft drinks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one living component of the environment. A: Plants.. Plants are living things in the environment.
chunks.source: Plants are living things in the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the difference between melting and sublimation as used in heat energy. A: Melting is the change from solid to liquid; sublimation is the change from solid directly to gas.. Melting passes through liquid; sublimation skips it.
chunks.source: Melting passes through liquid; sublimation skips it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one characteristic of arthropods. A: They have jointed legs (and segmented bodies).. Jointed limbs are the key arthropod feature.
chunks.source: Jointed limbs are the key arthropod feature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one deficiency disease which affects the musculo-skeletal system. A: Rickets.. Lack of vitamin D/calcium weakens bones.
chunks.source: Lack of vitamin D/calcium weakens bones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a blubber layer useful to a sea mammal? A: It keeps the sea mammal warm (insulates against cold water).. Blubber is a fat layer that stops heat loss.
chunks.source: Blubber is a fat layer that stops heat loss.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of compound leaf illustrated below. A: Trifoliate compound leaf.. Three leaflets make it trifoliate.
chunks.source: Three leaflets make it trifoliate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does mulching keep moisture in the soil? A: It covers the soil and reduces evaporation of water.. Mulch shields soil from sun and wind.
chunks.source: Mulch shields soil from sun and wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one effect of heat on matter. A: It causes matter to expand (or change state).. Heat makes particles move faster and spread.
chunks.source: Heat makes particles move faster and spread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one functional difference between veins and arteries. A: Veins carry blood towards the heart; arteries carry blood away from the heart.. They move blood in opposite directions.
chunks.source: They move blood in opposite directions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one disorder of a digestive system. A: Constipation (or diarrhoea).. These are common digestive disorders.
chunks.source: These are common digestive disorders.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is BCG vaccine administered at birth? A: To protect the baby against tuberculosis from birth.. Early vaccination builds immunity before exposure.
chunks.source: Early vaccination builds immunity before exposure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is rainbow formed? A: By dispersion (splitting) of sunlight through raindrops.. Raindrops refract and reflect sunlight into colours.
chunks.source: Raindrops refract and reflect sunlight into colours.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one source of food in the environment? A: Plants.. Plants make food for all living things.
chunks.source: Plants make food for all living things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one factor which affects the speed of sound. A: Temperature (of the medium).. Sound travels faster in warm air.
chunks.source: Sound travels faster in warm air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does the experiment below show about soil? A: That soil contains water (moisture).. Heating drove water out of the soil as droplets on the lid.
chunks.source: Heating drove water out of the soil as droplets on the lid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one sign of a simple fracture. A: Swelling (or severe pain) at the injured part.. A simple fracture breaks bone without tearing skin.
chunks.source: A simple fracture breaks bone without tearing skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the process in plants which is similar to sweating in humans. A: Transpiration.. Plants lose water vapour like humans lose sweat.
chunks.source: Plants lose water vapour like humans lose sweat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cite any one antenatal care services you know. A: Immunizing the mother / checking her health (blood pressure).. Antenatal care keeps mother and baby safe.
chunks.source: Antenatal care keeps mother and baby safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are the root nodules useful to the leguminous plants? A: They store nitrogen-fixing bacteria that add nitrates to the soil.. The bacteria feed the plant with nitrogen.
chunks.source: The bacteria feed the plant with nitrogen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which component of air is decreased in the atmosphere during the process of photosynthesis? A: Carbon dioxide.. Plants absorb carbon dioxide during photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants absorb carbon dioxide during photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below is of a tooth. State the function of the above tooth. A: For cutting and biting food.. The diagram shows an incisor with a flat cutting edge.
chunks.source: The diagram shows an incisor with a flat cutting edge.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the dry season the best time for shearing of sheep? A: So the sheep do not catch cold (it is warm and dry).. Sheep shorn in wet cold weather would suffer.
chunks.source: Sheep shorn in wet cold weather would suffer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one primary sex characteristic in both boys and girls adolescents. A: Maturation of the reproductive organs (testes in boys, ovaries in girls).. Primary characteristics are the reproductive organs themselves.
chunks.source: Primary characteristics are the reproductive organs themselves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which form of energy is stored in a dry cell? A: Chemical energy.. A dry cell stores energy in chemicals.
chunks.source: A dry cell stores energy in chemicals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one cause of dehydration among infants. A: Diarrhoea (or vomiting).. Losing body fluids causes dehydration.
chunks.source: Losing body fluids causes dehydration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the type of cattle whose body conformation is drawn below. A: Beef cattle.. The rectangular body conformation is typical of beef breeds.
chunks.source: The rectangular body conformation is typical of beef breeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one reason why farmers thin their crops. A: To reduce competition for nutrients, water and light.. Spaced crops grow bigger and healthier.
chunks.source: Spaced crops grow bigger and healthier.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one method of applying fertilizers in the garden. A: Broadcasting (or band placement).. Fertilizer is spread over the garden.
chunks.source: Fertilizer is spread over the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one example of a harmful fungi in the environment. A: Bread mould (mucor).. Moulds spoil food and crops.
chunks.source: Moulds spoil food and crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one factor that may call for caesarian operation as a form of delivery in woman. A: When the baby is too big or wrongly positioned (breech).. A narrow pelvis or big baby blocks normal birth.
chunks.source: A narrow pelvis or big baby blocks normal birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a micropyle useful to a germinating bean seed? A: It lets water (and air) enter the seed for germination.. The micropyle is the seed's entry hole.
chunks.source: The micropyle is the seed's entry hole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one example of a percussion musical instrument. A: A drum.. Drums are hit to make sound.
chunks.source: Drums are hit to make sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one example of stem tuber crop. A: Irish potato.. Irish potatoes are stem tubers.
chunks.source: Irish potatoes are stem tubers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one importance of reproduction to living things. A: It ensures the continuity of species.. New organisms replace those that die.
chunks.source: New organisms replace those that die.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one characteristic of a physical change. A: No new substance is formed (it can be reversed).. Physical changes keep the same material.
chunks.source: Physical changes keep the same material.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which vector spreads relapsing fever to people? A: Lice.. Relapsing fever spreads through lice bites.
chunks.source: Relapsing fever spreads through lice bites.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of an egg laying mammal. A: The duck-billed platypus (or spiny anteater).. These mammals lay eggs.
chunks.source: These mammals lay eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a first aid box useful to a first aider? A: It keeps first aid materials for the first aider to use.. Everything needed is stored in one box.
chunks.source: Everything needed is stored in one box.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one cause of teenage pregnancy among girls. A: Peer pressure / lack of guidance.. Girls copy friends or lack advice.
chunks.source: Girls copy friends or lack advice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the device used by blind people to dodge obstacles on their way. A: A white cane (walking stick).. The cane feels obstacles ahead.
chunks.source: The cane feels obstacles ahead.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41: The cuboid below measures 6cm by 2cm by 4cm and its mass is 48g. Find the density of the cuboid. (4 marks) A: 1 g/cm³.. Volume = 6×2×4 = 48 cm³; density = mass/volume = 48g/48cm³ = 1 g/cm³.
chunks.source: Volume = 6×2×4 = 48 cm³; density = mass/volume = 48g/48cm³ = 1 g/cm³.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(i): In which two ways are plants used as energy resources? (i) A: As firewood.. Burning wood gives heat energy.
chunks.source: Burning wood gives heat energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(ii): In which two ways are plants used as energy resources? (ii) A: As charcoal.. Charcoal from wood is also fuel.
chunks.source: Charcoal from wood is also fuel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b)(i): Suggest two methods of harvesting trees in agroforestry. (i) A: Pollarding.. Cutting branches high up lets them regrow.
chunks.source: Cutting branches high up lets them regrow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b)(ii): Suggest two methods of harvesting trees in agroforestry. (ii) A: Coppicing.. Cutting stems near the ground for regrowth.
chunks.source: Cutting stems near the ground for regrowth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a): Name any one authorized place to get medical drugs in case you need them. A: A pharmacy / drug shop / hospital.. Licensed places sell safe drugs.
chunks.source: Licensed places sell safe drugs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b): Geoffrey was suffering from malaria and the health worker gave him Coartem prescribed (4x2). State any one factor the health worker based on to prescribe Coartem tablets to Geoffrey. A: The malaria test results (or the patient's symptoms/weight).. The worker confirmed malaria before prescribing.
chunks.source: The worker confirmed malaria before prescribing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c): According to the above information, how often should Geoffrey take the medicine? A: Twice a day (4 tablets each time).. 4×2 means four tablets, two times daily.
chunks.source: 4×2 means four tablets, two times daily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(d): Why should drugs be kept out of reach of children? A: They may poison themselves (overdose).. Children can swallow harmful drugs.
chunks.source: Children can swallow harmful drugs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a): A boy stood in front of a wall and clapped his hands. After 3 seconds, he heard the same sound from the wall. What name is given to the sound heard after 3 seconds? A: An echo.. The repeated sound is an echo.
chunks.source: The repeated sound is an echo.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b): A boy stood in front of a wall and clapped his hands. After 3 seconds, he heard the same sound from the wall. How was such a sound produced? A: By reflection of the sound off the wall.. Sound bounced back to his ears.
chunks.source: Sound bounced back to his ears.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c): A boy stood in front of a wall and clapped his hands. After 3 seconds, he heard the same sound from the wall. Mention one mammal that makes use of the above sound to move. A: A bat.. Bats use echoes to navigate.
chunks.source: Bats use echoes to navigate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(d): A boy stood in front of a wall and clapped his hands. After 3 seconds, he heard the same sound from the wall. Name any one material that can be put in theatre halls to absorb the sound you have named in (a) above. A: Soft materials like curtains, carpets or foam.. Soft surfaces absorb sound.
chunks.source: Soft surfaces absorb sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a): How do we call the finger -like structures found in the ileum? A: Villi.. Villi are finger-like absorbers in the ileum.
chunks.source: Villi are finger-like absorbers in the ileum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b): Name the digestive enzyme found in saliva. A: Ptyalin (salivary amylase).. Ptyalin in saliva digests starch.
chunks.source: Ptyalin in saliva digests starch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c)(i): Name two types of digestion. (i) A: Mechanical digestion.. Chewing and churning break food physically.
chunks.source: Chewing and churning break food physically.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c)(ii): Name two types of digestion. (ii) A: Chemical digestion.. Enzymes break food chemically.
chunks.source: Enzymes break food chemically.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a): The diagram below shows a lens. Use it to answer the questions that follow. Name the type of lens shown above. A: A concave (diverging) lens.. It is thinner in the middle.
chunks.source: It is thinner in the middle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b): Complete the light rays through the lens above (draw how the rays go). A: The rays spread out (diverge) after passing through the lens.. A concave lens diverges light rays.
chunks.source: A concave lens diverges light rays.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c): The diagram below shows a lens. Use it to answer the questions that follow. Which eye defect is corrected by the above lens? A: Short sight (myopia).. Concave lenses correct short sight.
chunks.source: Concave lenses correct short sight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(d): Besides short sight, name any other eye defect. A: Long sight (hypermetropia).. Another common eye defect.
chunks.source: Another common eye defect.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(i): Give any two examples of dairy breeds of goats. A: Saanen.. Saanen is a dairy goat breed.
chunks.source: Saanen is a dairy goat breed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(ii): Give any two examples of dairy breeds of goats. A: Toggenburg.. Toggenburg is another dairy breed.
chunks.source: Toggenburg is another dairy breed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b): Identify one disadvantage of the tethering method of rearing goats. A: It restricts the goat's movement and grazing.. Tethered goats cannot feed freely.
chunks.source: Tethered goats cannot feed freely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c): Which practice in goat keeping controls internal parasites? A: Deworming (dosing).. Regular deworming kills internal parasites.
chunks.source: Regular deworming kills internal parasites.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a): Name the type of chicken reared for egg production. A: Layers.. Layers are kept for egg production.
chunks.source: Layers are kept for egg production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b): State any one way of increasing egg production on our poultry farms. A: By proper feeding and good housing.. Well-fed hens lay more eggs.
chunks.source: Well-fed hens lay more eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c)(i): Write down two advantages of keeping farm records on a poultry farm. (i) A: They help in planning and tracking profit or loss.. Records show how the farm performs.
chunks.source: Records show how the farm performs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c)(ii): Write down two advantages of keeping farm records on a poultry farm. (ii) A: They help detect diseases and losses early.. Records reveal problems quickly.
chunks.source: Records reveal problems quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49: The table below shows immunization sites, diseases and vaccines administered. Study and complete it correctly. Rows: [Disease: ___, Vaccine: BCG vaccine, Site: Injection on the right upper arm]; [Disease: Measles, Vaccine: Measles vaccine, Site: ___]; [Disease: Diphtheria, Vaccine: ___, Site: Injection on the left upper arm]; [Disease: Hepatitis B, Vaccine: ___, Site: Injection on the left upper thigh]. A: BCG → Tuberculosis; Measles site → Injection on the left upper arm; Diphtheria → DPT vaccine; Hepatitis B → Hepatitis B vaccine.. Each disease has its vaccine and correct site.
chunks.source: Each disease has its vaccine and correct site.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a): Why are biceps and triceps called antagonistic muscles? A: Because they work in opposite directions (one contracts while the other relaxes).. Antagonistic muscles pull opposite ways.
chunks.source: Antagonistic muscles pull opposite ways.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(i): What happens to each of the following muscles when the arm is straightened: biceps? A: The biceps relaxes (extends).. Straightening needs the triceps to pull.
chunks.source: Straightening needs the triceps to pull.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(ii): What happens to each of the following muscles when the arm is straightened: triceps? A: The triceps contracts.. It pulls the arm straight.
chunks.source: It pulls the arm straight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c): Apart from feeding babies on food stuffs rich in Vitamin D, how else can rickets be prevented? A: By basking in morning sunshine (sunlight gives vitamin D).. Sunlight on skin makes vitamin D.
chunks.source: Sunlight on skin makes vitamin D.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a): What is the difference between heat and temperature? A: Heat is a form of energy; temperature is the degree of hotness of a body.. Heat is energy, temperature measures it.
chunks.source: Heat is energy, temperature measures it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(i): Mention any two importances of heat transfer by conduction in the environment. (i) A: Cooking food.. Conduction carries heat through pots to food.
chunks.source: Conduction carries heat through pots to food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(ii): Mention any two importances of heat transfer by conduction in the environment. (ii) A: Warming the house / ironing clothes.. Heat spreads by conduction in solids.
chunks.source: Heat spreads by conduction in solids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c): Why is the handle of a frying pan made of either wood or plastic? A: Wood and plastic are poor conductors (insulators), so the handle stays cool.. Insulators do not carry heat to the hand.
chunks.source: Insulators do not carry heat to the hand.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(i): Mention any two examples of wading birds. (i) A: Heron.. Herons wade in water.
chunks.source: Herons wade in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(ii): Mention any two examples of wading birds. (ii) A: Crane (or stork).. Cranes also wade.
chunks.source: Cranes also wade.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b)(i): State any two reasons why some birds are able to fly. (i) A: They have hollow (light) bones.. Light bones make flight easier.
chunks.source: Light bones make flight easier.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b)(ii): State any two reasons why some birds are able to fly. (ii) A: They have wings and streamlined bodies.. Wings lift them; streamlined shape cuts air.
chunks.source: Wings lift them; streamlined shape cuts air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a): The diagram below is of a musical instrument. Name the group of musical instrument drawn above. A: String instruments.. It is played by plucking strings.
chunks.source: It is played by plucking strings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b)(i): Which strings will produce a high pitch of sound? A: String A (the shortest string).. Short strings vibrate faster, giving high pitch.
chunks.source: Short strings vibrate faster, giving high pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b)(ii): Which strings will produce a low pitch of sound? A: String D (the longest string).. Long strings vibrate slowly, giving low pitch.
chunks.source: Long strings vibrate slowly, giving low pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c): How can the pitch of sound produced by the musical instrument above be changed? A: By tightening or loosening the pegs (changing string tension).. Tighter strings give higher pitch.
chunks.source: Tighter strings give higher pitch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a): How is melanin found in the malpighian layer of the human skin important? A: It protects the skin from strong sunlight (ultra-violet rays).. Melanin blocks harmful sun rays.
chunks.source: Melanin blocks harmful sun rays.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(i): State any one way in which the human skin regulates the body temperature during cold days. A: The skin shivers / hairs stand erect / blood vessels narrow.. These actions reduce heat loss.
chunks.source: These actions reduce heat loss.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(ii): State any one way in which the human skin regulates the body temperature during hot days. A: The skin sweats (and blood vessels widen).. Sweat evaporation cools the body.
chunks.source: Sweat evaporation cools the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(d): Give any one way of caring for the human skin. A: By bathing regularly (and applying body lotion).. Clean skin stays healthy.
chunks.source: Clean skin stays healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(i): Match sensibly. Vectors: Housefly, Female anopheles mosquito, Tsetse fly, Culex mosquito. Germs: Trypanosoma, Filaria, Plasmodia, Chlamydia. Which germ in the list is spread by the Housefly? A: Housefly: Chlamydia. Houseflies spread the germ causing trachoma (Chlamydia).
chunks.source: Houseflies spread the germ causing trachoma (Chlamydia).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(ii): Match sensibly. Which germ is spread by the Female anopheles mosquito? A: Female anopheles mosquito: Plasmodia. Female anopheles spreads malaria (Plasmodia).
chunks.source: Female anopheles spreads malaria (Plasmodia).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(iii): Match sensibly. Which germ is spread by the Tsetse fly? A: Tsetse fly: Trypanosoma. Tsetse flies spread sleeping sickness (Trypanosoma).
chunks.source: Tsetse flies spread sleeping sickness (Trypanosoma).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(iv): Match sensibly. Which germ is spread by the Culex mosquito? A: Culex mosquito: Filaria. Culex mosquitoes spread elephantiasis (Filaria).
chunks.source: Culex mosquitoes spread elephantiasis (Filaria).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a legume. A: Beans.. Beans are legumes with nitrogen-fixing nodules.
chunks.source: Beans are legumes with nitrogen-fixing nodules.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the use of a trowel to a crop farmer? A: For digging small holes and transplanting seedlings.. A trowel is a small hand digging tool.
chunks.source: A trowel is a small hand digging tool.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why a spider is not an insect. A: It has eight legs (insects have six).. Spiders are arachnids, not insects.
chunks.source: Spiders are arachnids, not insects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a worker bee able to carry pollen on its body? A: It has pollen baskets on its hind legs (and a hairy body).. Pollen sticks to the hairs and baskets.
chunks.source: Pollen sticks to the hairs and baskets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does a mushroom use to reproduce? A: Spores.. Mushrooms reproduce by tiny spores.
chunks.source: Mushrooms reproduce by tiny spores.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the danger of not brushing your teeth regularly? A: Tooth decay (cavities).. Germs rot unbrushed teeth.
chunks.source: Germs rot unbrushed teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is copper called a good conductor? A: It allows heat and electricity to pass through easily.. Copper conducts well.
chunks.source: Copper conducts well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is chlorophyll important in the process of photosynthesis? A: It traps sunlight energy for photosynthesis.. Chlorophyll captures light in leaves.
chunks.source: Chlorophyll captures light in leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a foot of a bird. Use it to answer questions 9 and 10. Name an example of a bird with this foot. A: An eagle (or hawk).. The foot has sharp talons for gripping.
chunks.source: The foot has sharp talons for gripping.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How useful is the structure of this foot to the bird? A: For gripping and catching prey.. Talons hold struggling prey.
chunks.source: Talons hold struggling prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a vacuum prevent heat loss in a flask? A: It stops heat loss by conduction and convection (no air inside).. Vacuum has no particles to carry heat.
chunks.source: Vacuum has no particles to carry heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we call a condition when a person cannot see objects that are far from him? A: Short sight (myopia).. Short-sighted people see near objects only.
chunks.source: Short-sighted people see near objects only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a type of a pulley system. How does it help to make work easy? A: It reduces the effort needed to lift the load.. Pulleys give mechanical advantage.
chunks.source: Pulleys give mechanical advantage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which substance in the ear prevents dust from entering the organ? A: Wax.. Ear wax traps dust.
chunks.source: Ear wax traps dust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from charcoal and timber, name one practice that is a danger to trees. A: Bush burning.. Fires destroy trees.
chunks.source: Fires destroy trees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a poultry farmer stop cannibalism among his birds? A: By debeaking (trimming their beaks).. Blunt beaks cannot peck hard.
chunks.source: Blunt beaks cannot peck hard.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of a stem tuber. A: Irish potato.. Irish potatoes grow as stem tubers.
chunks.source: Irish potatoes grow as stem tubers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the reproduction of a housefly different from that of a grasshopper? A: A housefly undergoes complete metamorphosis; a grasshopper undergoes incomplete metamorphosis.. Housefly: egg-larva-pupa-adult; grasshopper: egg-nymph-adult.
chunks.source: Housefly: egg-larva-pupa-adult; grasshopper: egg-nymph-adult.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of plants have a parallel leaf venation? A: Monocots (e.g. maize).. Monocot leaves have parallel veins.
chunks.source: Monocot leaves have parallel veins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the use of synovial fluid in a joint? A: It lubricates the joint (reduces friction).. Synovial fluid oils moving bones.
chunks.source: Synovial fluid oils moving bones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which organ in the body allows exchange of gases in blood? A: The lungs.. Gases exchange in the lungs' air sacs.
chunks.source: Gases exchange in the lungs' air sacs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the use of a urinary bladder? A: It stores urine.. Urine waits in the bladder.
chunks.source: Urine waits in the bladder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the use of ORS to a sick child? A: To replace lost water and salts (prevent dehydration).. ORS restores body fluids.
chunks.source: ORS restores body fluids.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does a piece of stone sink in water? A: It is denser than water.. Denser objects sink.
chunks.source: Denser objects sink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which immunisable disease paralyses limbs of human beings? A: Polio.. Polio paralyses limbs; it is preventable by vaccine.
chunks.source: Polio paralyses limbs; it is preventable by vaccine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What causes evaporation in a water cycle? A: Heat from the sun.. Sun heat evaporates water.
chunks.source: Sun heat evaporates water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which activity of sanitation will reduce the spread of malaria in a community? A: Draining stagnant water / clearing bushes.. No stagnant water means no mosquito breeding.
chunks.source: No stagnant water means no mosquito breeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the danger of water snails to human beings? A: They spread bilharzia (schistosomiasis).. Snails host the bilharzia worms.
chunks.source: Snails host the bilharzia worms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the use of prop roots on a maize plant? A: To support the maize plant upright.. Prop roots anchor tall stems.
chunks.source: Prop roots anchor tall stems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of change needs heat to take place? A: Chemical change.. Chemical changes need heat to start.
chunks.source: Chemical changes need heat to start.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why a mother must breastfeed her baby? A: Breast milk has all nutrients and protects the baby from disease.. Mother's milk is the perfect baby food.
chunks.source: Mother's milk is the perfect baby food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a bat able to avoid hitting a rock at night? A: By using echoes (echolocation).. Bats hear reflected sound to dodge objects.
chunks.source: Bats hear reflected sound to dodge objects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which practice of cultivation reduces soil erosion in hilly areas? A: Terracing (or contour ploughing).. Terraces slow running water on slopes.
chunks.source: Terraces slow running water on slopes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is passive smoking? A: Breathing in smoke from other people's cigarettes.. Non-smokers inhale nearby smoke.
chunks.source: Non-smokers inhale nearby smoke.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should garden tools be kept in a dry place? A: To prevent them from rusting.. Moisture rusts metal tools.
chunks.source: Moisture rusts metal tools.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is human skin called an excretory organ? A: It removes sweat (water, salts and urea).. Skin excretes through sweat.
chunks.source: Skin excretes through sweat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of a living house allows carbon dioxide out? A: Ventilators (or windows).. Ventilators let stale air out.
chunks.source: Ventilators let stale air out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the use of a nostril to a fish? A: For smelling.. Fish nostrils detect smells, not for breathing.
chunks.source: Fish nostrils detect smells, not for breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which blood vessels have valves? A: Veins.. Veins have valves to stop backflow.
chunks.source: Veins have valves to stop backflow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How would the seed below (a spiky burr seed) be dispersed? A: By animals (the burrs stick to animal fur/skin).. Spiky seeds hitch rides on passing animals.
chunks.source: Spiky seeds hitch rides on passing animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(i): The diagram shows part of a germinating seed (y = plumule). Name part (i). A: Cotyledon (seed leaf).. (i) is the food store of the seed.
chunks.source: (i) is the food store of the seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(ii): The diagram shows part of a germinating seed (y = plumule). Name part (ii). A: Radicle (young root).. (ii) grows down into the soil.
chunks.source: (ii) grows down into the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b): What is the function of part Y (the plumule)? A: It grows into the shoot (stem and leaves).. The plumule is the future shoot.
chunks.source: The plumule is the future shoot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c): Name one condition that would make a seed fail to germinate. A: Lack of water (or warmth / oxygen).. Seeds need water, warmth and air to sprout.
chunks.source: Seeds need water, warmth and air to sprout.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(i): Match the weather instrument in A with what it does in B. A: Windsock, Rain gauge, Sixth's thermometer, Barometer. B: atmospheric pressure, strength of wind, temperature, how much it has rained. Which function matches 'Windsock'? A: Windsock: strength of wind. A windsock shows how strong the wind blows.
chunks.source: A windsock shows how strong the wind blows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(ii): Match the weather instrument in A with what it does in B. Which function matches 'Rain gauge'? A: Rain gauge: how much it has rained. A rain gauge collects and measures rainfall.
chunks.source: A rain gauge collects and measures rainfall.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(iii): Match the weather instrument in A with what it does in B. Which function matches 'Sixth's thermometer'? A: Sixth's thermometer: temperature. It records maximum and minimum temperatures.
chunks.source: It records maximum and minimum temperatures.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(iv): Match the weather instrument in A with what it does in B. Which function matches 'Barometer'? A: Barometer: atmospheric pressure. A barometer measures air pressure.
chunks.source: A barometer measures air pressure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(i): Give the cause of kwashiorkor in the human body. A: Lack of proteins in the diet.. Kwashiorkor comes from protein deficiency.
chunks.source: Kwashiorkor comes from protein deficiency.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(ii): Give the cause of anaemia in the human body. A: Lack of iron in the diet.. Iron makes blood; without it comes anaemia.
chunks.source: Iron makes blood; without it comes anaemia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(i): Apart from refrigeration, give two other ways of conserving fish. (i) A: Smoking (drying) fish.. Smoke preserves fish.
chunks.source: Smoke preserves fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b)(ii): Apart from refrigeration, give two other ways of conserving fish. (ii) A: Salting fish.. Salt stops germs growing.
chunks.source: Salt stops germs growing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a): The diagram shows a method of magnetization (stroking a nail with a magnet). What is the method called? A: Magnetization by stroking (single touch).. Stroking with a magnet aligns the nail's domains.
chunks.source: Stroking with a magnet aligns the nail's domains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b): What would happen if point X of the nail is put at pole S? A: Point X would be attracted to pole S.. X became a north pole; opposite poles attract.
chunks.source: X became a north pole; opposite poles attract.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c): Name one activity that would make a magnet lose its magnetism. A: Heating it (or hammering / dropping it).. Heat scrambles the magnetic alignment.
chunks.source: Heat scrambles the magnetic alignment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(d): Which part of a radio uses a permanent magnet? A: The loudspeaker.. A permanent magnet drives the speaker cone.
chunks.source: A permanent magnet drives the speaker cone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a): What are energy resources? A: Energy resources are things that provide energy for use.. Wood, sun and water give energy.
chunks.source: Wood, sun and water give energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b): What is the major source of energy on earth? A: The sun.. The sun is the main source of earth's energy.
chunks.source: The sun is the main source of earth's energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c)(i): Give two ways by which water can act as a resource. (i) A: For drinking and domestic use.. Water is life's basic resource.
chunks.source: Water is life's basic resource.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c)(ii): Give two ways by which water can act as a resource. (ii) A: For generating hydro-electricity.. Falling water turns turbines.
chunks.source: Falling water turns turbines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a)(i): Name the two types of pollination in flowering plants. (i) A: Self pollination.. Pollen moves within the same flower.
chunks.source: Pollen moves within the same flower.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a)(ii): Name the two types of pollination in flowering plants. (ii) A: Cross pollination.. Pollen moves between different flowers.
chunks.source: Pollen moves between different flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b)(i): What is the use of anthers during pollination? A: They produce (and release) pollen grains.. Anthers are the male parts.
chunks.source: Anthers are the male parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b)(ii): What is the use of the stigma during pollination? A: It receives pollen grains.. The stigma is the female landing site.
chunks.source: The stigma is the female landing site.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a): The diagram shows a boy using a metallic bar to raise a sack of coffee. Which type of machine is he using? A: A lever.. The bar turning on a support is a lever.
chunks.source: The bar turning on a support is a lever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b): What can he do to lift the sack more easily? A: Move the fulcrum nearer the load (or push at the far end).. A longer effort arm needs less force.
chunks.source: A longer effort arm needs less force.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c): Name the force that slows movement in moving parts of a machine. A: Friction.. Friction opposes moving parts.
chunks.source: Friction opposes moving parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(d): How is the force in (c) useful in our daily life? A: It helps us walk without slipping / brake / write.. Friction gives grip.
chunks.source: Friction gives grip.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(i): The diagram shows a ray of light on a smooth shiny surface Z (W = normal). Name part X. A: Reflected ray.. X is the ray bouncing off the surface.
chunks.source: X is the ray bouncing off the surface.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(ii): The diagram shows a ray of light on a smooth shiny surface Z. Name part W. A: Normal.. W is the line at right angles to the surface.
chunks.source: W is the line at right angles to the surface.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b): Name an instrument where the above principle (reflection) is used. A: A periscope (or mirror).. Periscopes use reflection to see around.
chunks.source: Periscopes use reflection to see around.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(c): The angle of reflection is the angle between the reflected ray (X) and the normal (W). A: It is the angle between the reflected ray X and the normal W.. Angle of reflection equals angle of incidence.
chunks.source: Angle of reflection equals angle of incidence.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a): What is First Aid? A: First aid is the immediate help given to a casualty before a doctor arrives.. It is the first help at an accident.
chunks.source: It is the first help at an accident.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(i): Give two reasons why an injured person may need first aid. (i) A: To save life.. Quick aid can keep someone alive.
chunks.source: Quick aid can keep someone alive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(ii): Give two reasons why an injured person may need first aid. (ii) A: To prevent the injury from getting worse.. Early care stops complications.
chunks.source: Early care stops complications.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c): How is a splint useful to a person with a fractured lower leg? A: It keeps the broken bones still (immobilizes them).. A splint stops movement at the fracture.
chunks.source: A splint stops movement at the fracture.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a): What is teenage pregnancy? A: Pregnancy in girls below 18 years.. Teenage mothers are still children.
chunks.source: Teenage mothers are still children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(i): Apart from failure to have safe delivery, give two other dangers of teenage pregnancy. (i) A: Failure to complete school.. Pregnancy often ends schooling.
chunks.source: Pregnancy often ends schooling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(ii): Apart from failure to have safe delivery, give two other dangers of teenage pregnancy. (ii) A: Health risks (or death) during delivery.. Young bodies face delivery dangers.
chunks.source: Young bodies face delivery dangers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c): How can a school prevent teenage pregnancies? A: Through guidance, counselling and sex education.. Schools teach dangers and prevention.
chunks.source: Schools teach dangers and prevention.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(i): How is castration important to a cattle farmer? A: It makes bulls calm and easy to handle (and fatten faster).. Castrated bulls are docile.
chunks.source: Castrated bulls are docile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(ii): How is deworming important to a cattle farmer? A: It kills internal parasites (worms).. Dewormed cattle stay healthy.
chunks.source: Dewormed cattle stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(i): Give two systems used in grazing cattle. (i) A: Paddocking.. Cattle graze in fenced paddocks.
chunks.source: Cattle graze in fenced paddocks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(ii): Give two systems used in grazing cattle. (ii) A: Herding (or tethering).. A herdsman moves cattle to pasture.
chunks.source: A herdsman moves cattle to pasture.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(i): Give two ways of making water safe for drinking. (i) A: Boiling.. Boiling kills germs.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(ii): Give two ways of making water safe for drinking. (ii) A: Filtering (or treating with chemicals).. Filters remove dirt.
chunks.source: Filters remove dirt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(i): Write any two ways by which water can become impure. (i) A: Dumping waste into water.. Waste pollutes water.
chunks.source: Waste pollutes water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(ii): Write any two ways by which water can become impure. (ii) A: Urinating / defecating near water sources.. Human waste contaminates water.
chunks.source: Human waste contaminates water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(i): The diagram shows a simple electric circuit. Name part T. A: T is a connecting wire.. T joins the circuit parts.
chunks.source: T joins the circuit parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(ii): The diagram shows a simple electric circuit. Name part R. A: R is the bulb.. R lights when current flows.
chunks.source: R lights when current flows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b): If Q is closed, give one reason why R would not light. A: The bulb could be faulty (or the battery dead).. A broken part stops current.
chunks.source: A broken part stops current.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c): How is S useful in the above circuit? A: S is a fuse; it breaks the circuit if current is too high, protecting the parts.. The fuse guards against excess current.
chunks.source: The fuse guards against excess current.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(i): Below is part of the human alimentary canal. Give the name of part R. A: Gall bladder.. R is the small sac on the liver.
chunks.source: R is the small sac on the liver.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a)(ii): Below is part of the human alimentary canal. Give the function of part R. A: It stores bile.. Bile is kept until needed.
chunks.source: Bile is kept until needed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b): Where does food go after P (the duodenum)? A: Into the ileum (the rest of the small intestine).. Food continues along the small intestine.
chunks.source: Food continues along the small intestine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c): Give one way of preventing constipation. A: Eating foods rich in roughage (and drinking enough water).. Roughage keeps bowels moving.
chunks.source: Roughage keeps bowels moving.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a)(i): The government of Uganda has stopped the use and manufacture of polythene bags. Give two reasons why this was done. (i) A: They pollute the environment (they do not rot).. Polythene is non-biodegradable.
chunks.source: Polythene is non-biodegradable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a)(ii): The government of Uganda has stopped the use and manufacture of polythene bags. Give two reasons why this was done. (ii) A: They block drainage channels and kill animals that swallow them.. Bags choke drains and livestock.
chunks.source: Bags choke drains and livestock.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(i): Apart from controlling the spread of crop pests, give two other uses of mulching a garden. (i) A: It keeps moisture in the soil.. Mulch stops evaporation.
chunks.source: Mulch stops evaporation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b)(ii): Apart from controlling the spread of crop pests, give two other uses of mulching a garden. (ii) A: It controls soil erosion / adds nutrients.. Mulch protects and feeds soil.
chunks.source: Mulch protects and feeds soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one component of soil. A: Humus.. Humus is decayed organic matter in soil.
chunks.source: Humus is decayed organic matter in soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one function of the human skin A: It protects the body (and regulates temperature).. Skin is a protective covering.
chunks.source: Skin is a protective covering.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one epidemic disease that can breakout in your community with poor sanitation A: Cholera.. Cholera spreads fast with poor sanitation.
chunks.source: Cholera spreads fast with poor sanitation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the group of tuber crops to which a coco yam belongs A: Root tubers.. Cocoyam stores food in roots.
chunks.source: Cocoyam stores food in roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one use of snakes to man A: They eat rats (control pests).. Snakes are natural rat catchers.
chunks.source: Snakes are natural rat catchers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one part to look at when cleaning your teeth A: The gaps between the teeth (and gums).. Food hides between teeth.
chunks.source: Food hides between teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one type of mechanical energy A: Kinetic energy.. Moving objects have kinetic energy.
chunks.source: Moving objects have kinetic energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the reason why the rate of soil erosion is higher in mountainous areas A: Steep slopes make water run fast, carrying soil away.. Fast water erodes more.
chunks.source: Fast water erodes more.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why it is advisable that children participate in keeping their environment clean A: To learn responsibility and prevent disease.. Clean habits keep everyone healthy.
chunks.source: Clean habits keep everyone healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the mineral missing in the diet of a child suffering from goitre A: Iodine.. Lack of iodine causes goitre.
chunks.source: Lack of iodine causes goitre.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the state of matter in which a material with a volume but no shape belongs A: Liquid.. Liquids flow without fixed shape.
chunks.source: Liquids flow without fixed shape.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the function of the septum in the human heart. A: It prevents mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.. The septum divides the heart's sides.
chunks.source: The septum divides the heart's sides.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Below is a drawing of a garden tool (a hand trowel). Use it to answer questions 14 and 15. Name the garden tool. A: A hand trowel.. The diagram shows a small hand trowel.
chunks.source: The diagram shows a small hand trowel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the function of the garden tool A: For digging small holes and transplanting seedlings.. Trowels work soil in small spaces.
chunks.source: Trowels work soil in small spaces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one condition under which a mother may be stopped from breastfeeding the baby A: If the mother is very sick (or on certain drugs).. Illness can pass through milk.
chunks.source: Illness can pass through milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An alcoholic drink is labelled 40%. State what that means. A: It contains 40% alcohol.. The label shows alcohol content.
chunks.source: The label shows alcohol content.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Below is the structure of the root system in a plant. Use it to answer questions 18 and 19. Name the type of roots in the plant above. A: Prop (adventitious) roots.. The roots grow from the stem above ground.
chunks.source: The roots grow from the stem above ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the type of root system in the plant above. A: Fibrous (adventitious) root system.. Many thin roots spread out.
chunks.source: Many thin roots spread out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one reason why immunization is considered as a Primary Health Care practice A: It prevents disease cheaply across the community.. Prevention is a PHC principle.
