chunks.source: Prevention is a PHC principle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why physical methods of pest control are preferred to chemical methods A: They are cheap and leave no chemical residues.. Physical methods avoid poison.
chunks.source: Physical methods avoid poison.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one reason why it is advisable for men to be circumcised A: It reduces the risk of HIV/STD infection.. Circumcision lowers infection chances.
chunks.source: Circumcision lowers infection chances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one way in which a health club in schools can reduce the outbreak of diseases in the school A: By teaching hygiene and cleaning the school.. Health clubs spread health messages.
chunks.source: Health clubs spread health messages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of change that takes place when fruits ripen A: Chemical change.. Ripening makes new substances.
chunks.source: Ripening makes new substances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of bacteria to man A: They decompose organic matter (making nutrients).. Bacteria recycle nutrients.
chunks.source: Bacteria recycle nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State how the hairy body of the housefly is important in spreading diseases. A: Germs stick to the hairs and are carried to food.. Hairy bodies trap germs.
chunks.source: Hairy bodies trap germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State why in resting an arm using an arm sling, the forearm and upper arm should be rested at 90°. A: To keep the arm comfortable and well supported.. 90° rests the joint naturally.
chunks.source: 90° rests the joint naturally.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Below is an instrument (a thermometer) used to measure the temperature of a person. Record the temperature of the person. A: 42.0°C.. The thermometer display reads 42.0.
chunks.source: The thermometer display reads 42.0.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State why the doctor said the person was not normal A: 42°C is above normal body temperature (37°C); the person has a fever.. Normal is 37°C.
chunks.source: Normal is 37°C.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State why it is important to sprinkle water on plant materials when making compost manure A: To soften materials and speed up decomposition.. Moisture helps rotting.
chunks.source: Moisture helps rotting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the role of plants in a food chain A: They are producers (make food).. Plants start every food chain.
chunks.source: Plants start every food chain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the muscular organ that separates the chest cavity from the abdomen in humans A: The diaphragm.. It separates chest from abdomen.
chunks.source: It separates chest from abdomen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one importance of information gathered through a health survey in a community A: It helps plan health services for the community.. Data guides health decisions.
chunks.source: Data guides health decisions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one human activity that results into flooding of water bodies. A: Deforestation (or dumping waste in drainage channels).. Bare land and blocked drains flood.
chunks.source: Bare land and blocked drains flood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the group of arthropods to which ticks belong A: Arachnids.. Ticks have eight legs like spiders.
chunks.source: Ticks have eight legs like spiders.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An organism has the following characteristics; cannot make its own food, reproduces by the use of spores, is made up of many cells. Name the group of living things to which it belongs A: Fungi.. Fungi feed on dead matter and make spores.
chunks.source: Fungi feed on dead matter and make spores.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the magnetic method, mention any one method of storage and reproduction of sound. A: The optical method (CDs).. CDs store sound as light patterns.
chunks.source: CDs store sound as light patterns.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of immunity that a baby gets after being immunized A: Artificial immunity.. Vaccines give artificial immunity.
chunks.source: Vaccines give artificial immunity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one vaccine against COVID-19 A: AstraZeneca (or Pfizer).. These vaccines were used against COVID-19.
chunks.source: These vaccines were used against COVID-19.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State what you understand by the efficiency of a simple machine. A: The ratio of work output to work input, times 100%.. Efficiency shows how much work is useful.
chunks.source: Efficiency shows how much work is useful.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a): What is personal hygiene? A: Personal hygiene is keeping one's body clean to stay healthy.. Clean habits prevent disease.
chunks.source: Clean habits prevent disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(i): State the importance of ironing while cleaning clothes. A: It kills germs on clothes.. Heat from ironing disinfects.
chunks.source: Heat from ironing disinfects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(ii): State the importance of soaking while cleaning clothes. A: It loosens dirt for easy washing.. Soaking softens stains.
chunks.source: Soaking softens stains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c): Identify any one disease that can be spread in a school due to poor cleanliness of beddings. A: Scabies.. Dirty bedding spreads scabies.
chunks.source: Dirty bedding spreads scabies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(i): Mention any two functions of muscles. (i) A: Movement.. Muscles pull bones to move.
chunks.source: Muscles pull bones to move.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(ii): Mention any two functions of muscles. (ii) A: Support / maintaining posture.. Muscles hold the body upright.
chunks.source: Muscles hold the body upright.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44: The following are processes that lead to hearing in humans. Arrange them in their correct order: (1) The cochlea changes the vibrations into nervous impulses; (2) The pina receives sound vibrations and directs them to the eardrum; (3) Vibrations are transmitted through the ear ossicles to the inner ear; (4) Messages are sent through the auditory nerve to the brain for interpretation. A: 2 → 3 → 1 → 4: pina receives sound → eardrum → ear ossicles → cochlea → auditory nerve → brain.. Sound travels step by step to the brain.
chunks.source: Sound travels step by step to the brain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(i): In a slum in Mukono, many people live in a small area with no proper pit latrines and littered polythene bags. Identify any two environmental problems that can result from this situation. (i) A: Outbreak of diseases (e.g. cholera).. Poor sanitation spreads disease.
chunks.source: Poor sanitation spreads disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(ii): Identify any two environmental problems that can result from this situation. (ii) A: Pollution and bad smell.. Litter dirties the area.
chunks.source: Litter dirties the area.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(i): Identify any two ways in which the people in the area above can control these environmental problems. (i) A: Building proper pit latrines/toilets.. Safe disposal stops disease.
chunks.source: Safe disposal stops disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b)(ii): Identify any two ways in which the people in the area above can control these environmental problems. (ii) A: Proper waste disposal (collecting litter).. Clean surroundings stay healthy.
chunks.source: Clean surroundings stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a): Name the germ that causes COVID 19 A: Coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2).. This virus causes COVID-19.
chunks.source: This virus causes COVID-19.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b): Identify any one sign or symptom of COVID-19. A: Fever / dry cough / loss of smell.. These are common COVID signs.
chunks.source: These are common COVID signs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c)(i): Mention any two ways of controlling the spread of COVID-19 in a school. (i) A: Wearing face masks.. Masks block the virus.
chunks.source: Masks block the virus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c)(ii): Mention any two ways of controlling the spread of COVID-19 in a school. (ii) A: Washing hands / keeping distance.. Hygiene stops spread.
chunks.source: Hygiene stops spread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(i): Name the group of worms to which hookworm belongs. A: Nematodes (roundworms).. Hookworms are roundworms.
chunks.source: Hookworms are roundworms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(ii): Name the group of worms to which tapeworm belongs. A: Platyhelminthes (flatworms).. Tapeworms are flat.
chunks.source: Tapeworms are flat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(i): Identify any two ways of controlling the spread of bilharzia in a community. (i) A: Wearing shoes.. Shoes block worm entry.
chunks.source: Shoes block worm entry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(ii): Identify any two ways of controlling the spread of bilharzia in a community. (ii) A: Using clean latrines / drinking clean water.. Sanitation stops worm spread.
chunks.source: Sanitation stops worm spread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(i): Mention any two practices that can prevent contamination of food in a school. (i) A: Washing hands before handling food.. Clean hands keep food safe.
chunks.source: Clean hands keep food safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(ii): Mention any two practices that can prevent contamination of food in a school. (ii) A: Covering food.. Covers keep germs off.
chunks.source: Covers keep germs off.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b)(i): Name any two diseases that can be transmitted through contaminated food. (i) A: Cholera.. Dirty food spreads cholera.
chunks.source: Dirty food spreads cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b)(ii): Name any two diseases that can be transmitted through contaminated food. (ii) A: Typhoid.. Typhoid also spreads via food.
chunks.source: Typhoid also spreads via food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(i): Mention any two advantages of keeping pigs. (i) A: They multiply (produce many young) fast.. Pigs farrow many piglets.
chunks.source: Pigs farrow many piglets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(ii): Mention any two advantages of keeping pigs. (ii) A: They eat a wide range of foods.. Pigs are not picky eaters.
chunks.source: Pigs are not picky eaters.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(i): Identify any two advantages of keeping pigs over keeping cattle. (i) A: They mature faster than cattle.. Pigs grow quickly.
chunks.source: Pigs grow quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b)(ii): Identify any two advantages of keeping pigs over keeping cattle. (ii) A: They need less space and feed.. Pigs suit small farms.
chunks.source: Pigs suit small farms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(i): Apart from the free-range system, name two other methods of keeping poultry. (i) A: Deep litter system.. Birds live on floor litter.
chunks.source: Birds live on floor litter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a)(ii): Apart from the free-range system, name two other methods of keeping poultry. (ii) A: Battery cage system.. Birds live in cages.
chunks.source: Birds live in cages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(i): Explain why poultry easily get infected in the free-range system. (i) A: They mix with wild birds and animals.. Contact spreads disease.
chunks.source: Contact spreads disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(ii): Explain why poultry easily get infected in the free-range system. (ii) A: They eat contaminated food and water.. Dirty food carries germs.
chunks.source: Dirty food carries germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(i): Mention any two methods of extracting honey. (i) A: Centrifuging (spinning).. Spinning throws honey out.
chunks.source: Spinning throws honey out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(ii): Mention any two methods of extracting honey. (ii) A: Pressing (squeezing) combs.. Squeezing releases honey.
chunks.source: Squeezing releases honey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(i): Name any two materials that can be used to make compost manure in your community A: Plant materials (dry leaves, grass).. Plants rot into manure.
chunks.source: Plants rot into manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a)(ii): Name any two materials that can be used to make compost manure in your community A: Animal droppings.. Droppings enrich manure.
chunks.source: Droppings enrich manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(i): Identify any two advantages of organic manure over inorganic fertilizers. (i) A: They are cheap (free).. No purchase needed.
chunks.source: No purchase needed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(ii): Identify any two advantages of organic manure over inorganic fertilizers. (ii) A: They improve soil structure.. Organic matter loosens soil.
chunks.source: Organic matter loosens soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b): Explain the reason why the inner walls of the glass in a vacuum flask are painted silver. A: To reflect heat (prevent loss by radiation).. Shiny walls bounce heat back.
chunks.source: Shiny walls bounce heat back.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a): A machine lifts a load of 3000N through 0.5m when an effort of 1000N is applied through 2m. Calculate the mechanical advantage of the machine. A: 3.. MA = Load/Effort = 3000N/1000N = 3.
chunks.source: MA = Load/Effort = 3000N/1000N = 3.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b): Calculate the velocity ratio of the machine. A: 4.. VR = effort distance/load distance = 2m/0.5m = 4.
chunks.source: VR = effort distance/load distance = 2m/0.5m = 4.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Define an epidemic. A: An epidemic is the outbreak of a disease affecting many people at the same time in an area.. Epidemics spread fast, e.g. cholera or Ebola outbreaks.
chunks.source: Epidemics spread fast, e.g. cholera or Ebola outbreaks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b)(i): State what happens to the triceps when the forearm is folded. A: The triceps relaxes (extends).. Folding needs the biceps to contract, so the triceps relaxes.
chunks.source: Folding needs the biceps to contract, so the triceps relaxes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b)(ii): State what happens to the biceps when the forearm is folded. A: The biceps contracts.. The biceps pulls the forearm up when folding.
chunks.source: The biceps pulls the forearm up when folding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(i): State the importance of the queen excluder in a Kenyan top bar hive. A: It keeps the queen out of the honey chamber (so honey is not mixed with brood).. The excluder lets workers pass but blocks the queen.
chunks.source: The excluder lets workers pass but blocks the queen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(ii): State the importance of the top bar in a Kenyan top bar hive. A: Bees build their combs hanging on the top bars.. Combs attach to the bars for easy harvesting.
chunks.source: Combs attach to the bars for easy harvesting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(i): Name the state of matter in which heat travels fastest by conduction. A: Solids.. Conduction is fastest in solids, especially metals.
chunks.source: Conduction is fastest in solids, especially metals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(ii): Name the state of matter in which heat travels fastest by convection. A: Liquids (and gases).. Convection happens in fluids (liquids and gases).
chunks.source: Convection happens in fluids (liquids and gases).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43: Match the internal organs in humans in A (Kidney, Brain, liver, lungs) with their functions in B (exchange of gases, produces bile, produces urine, stores information). A: Kidney: produces urine; Brain: stores information; liver: produces bile; lungs: exchange of gases. Kidneys make urine; the brain stores information; the liver makes bile; lungs exchange gases.
chunks.source: Kidneys make urine; the brain stores information; the liver makes bile; lungs exchange gases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55: Match the plants in A (Mango, Fern, Christmas tree, Algae) with how they reproduce in B (reproduces by fragmentation; produces seeds but without flowers; produces seeds and have flowers; reproduces by the use of spores). A: Mango: produces seeds and have flowers; Fern: reproduces by the use of spores; Christmas tree: produces seeds but without flowers; Algae: reproduces by fragmentation. Mango is a flowering plant; ferns use spores; conifers make seeds without flowers; algae fragment.
chunks.source: Mango is a flowering plant; ferns use spores; conifers make seeds without flowers; algae fragment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the body organ commonly affected by scalds. A: The skin.. Scalds burn the skin.
chunks.source: Scalds burn the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which component of the environment enables man to produce hydro electricity? A: Water.. Flowing water turns turbines for HEP.
chunks.source: Flowing water turns turbines for HEP.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a fossil fuel. A: Petroleum (or coal).. Fossil fuels come from ancient remains.
chunks.source: Fossil fuels come from ancient remains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write any one way a family can care for its member who is HIV positive. A: By giving them love, care and proper feeding.. Support helps them live positively.
chunks.source: Support helps them live positively.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of preventing COVID-19 infections. A: Wearing a face mask (or washing hands).. Masks and hygiene stop the virus.
chunks.source: Masks and hygiene stop the virus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Calculate the voltage of a torch that uses three dry cells. A: 4.5 volts.. Each dry cell is 1.5V; 3 × 1.5V = 4.5V.
chunks.source: Each dry cell is 1.5V; 3 × 1.5V = 4.5V.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one way farmers can prevent and control rats from destroying their crops in the garden. A: By keeping cats (or using traps).. Cats catch rats.
chunks.source: Cats catch rats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the first aid for a snake bite. A: Tie above the bite and rush to hospital (keep the victim calm).. First aid slows poison spread.
chunks.source: First aid slows poison spread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the disease vector that spreads nagana to cattle. A: Tsetse fly.. Tsetse flies spread nagana.
chunks.source: Tsetse flies spread nagana.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a second class lever machine (a wheelbarrow). Name the part labeled L. A: The load.. L points to the soil (load) in the wheelbarrow.
chunks.source: L points to the soil (load) in the wheelbarrow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one natural method of family planning. A: Abstinence (or withdrawal method).. Natural methods avoid devices.
chunks.source: Natural methods avoid devices.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one advantage of modern bee hives over the traditional one. A: They are easy to inspect and harvest honey without killing bees.. Modern hives have removable combs.
chunks.source: Modern hives have removable combs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a magnetic field. Name pole a. A: North pole (N).. Field lines leave the north pole.
chunks.source: Field lines leave the north pole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Vulnerable groups of people are those that can easily be harmed. Give one example of such a group of people. A: Children (or the elderly / disabled).. These groups need protection.
chunks.source: These groups need protection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one use of yeast to people. A: For baking bread (making dough rise).. Yeast ferments dough.
chunks.source: Yeast ferments dough.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below shows a common latrine in urban schools. Give the use of part Q. A: It is used to flush water to wash away waste.. Q is the flushing mechanism.
chunks.source: Q is the flushing mechanism.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are animals used as energy resources in our environment? A: They are used for transport and ploughing (their dung is fuel/manure).. Animals provide draught power.
chunks.source: Animals provide draught power.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from chicken, mention any one other domestic bird. A: Duck (or turkey).. Ducks are domestic birds.
chunks.source: Ducks are domestic birds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of a long bone in the body. A: Femur (thigh bone).. The femur is a long bone.
chunks.source: The femur is a long bone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the plant shoot response shown in the diagram below. A: Phototropism.. The shoot bends towards light.
chunks.source: The shoot bends towards light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Oral health is the state of being free from any mouth and teeth infection or disorders. Name any one oral disease / infection. A: Tooth decay (or dental caries).. A common mouth infection.
chunks.source: A common mouth infection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one material that can be attracted by a magnet. A: Iron (or steel).. Magnets attract iron.
chunks.source: Magnets attract iron.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way food gets contaminated at home. A: Through dirty hands / uncovered food.. Germs reach food easily.
chunks.source: Germs reach food easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one common sign of pest and disease damage in crops. A: Yellowing / holes in leaves.. Pests damage crops visibly.
chunks.source: Pests damage crops visibly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A towel is one of the materials used in promoting personal hygiene. How is it important? A: It is used to dry the body after bathing.. Towels absorb water.
chunks.source: Towels absorb water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one factor that can increase transpiration in plants. A: Heat / wind / low humidity.. These speed up water loss.
chunks.source: These speed up water loss.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is leaching? A: Leaching is the washing away of soil nutrients by water sinking down.. Rain carries nutrients deep.
chunks.source: Rain carries nutrients deep.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of rocks in our environment. A: For building (construction).. Rocks make stones for building.
chunks.source: Rocks make stones for building.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of a seed produces the stem of a plant? A: The plumule.. The plumule grows into the stem.
chunks.source: The plumule grows into the stem.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the exotic breed of goats well known for producing large amounts of milk. A: Saanen.. Saanen goats give much milk.
chunks.source: Saanen goats give much milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one effect of poor feeding to people. A: Weakness / stunted growth.. Poor feeding harms health.
chunks.source: Poor feeding harms health.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of air to plants. A: It provides carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.. Plants need CO2 from air.
chunks.source: Plants need CO2 from air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one way you can care for the hair found on the head. A: By washing and oiling it regularly.. Clean hair stays healthy.
chunks.source: Clean hair stays healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the lifecycle of insects below (egg → larva → pupa → adult) to answer question 35. Mention any one insect that undergoes the above life cycle. A: A housefly (or bee).. They undergo complete metamorphosis.
chunks.source: They undergo complete metamorphosis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one precaution one should consider before taking any drug. A: Check the expiry date / prescription.. Wrong drugs are dangerous.
chunks.source: Wrong drugs are dangerous.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one type of soil erosion. A: Gully erosion (or sheet erosion).. Water carves soil.
chunks.source: Water carves soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the use of the human eyes when eating food? A: To see the food (look at what we eat).. Eyes guide eating.
chunks.source: Eyes guide eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one place where immunization of children can take place. A: At a health centre / hospital.. Immunization happens at clinics.
chunks.source: Immunization happens at clinics.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one difference between mass and weight. A: Mass is the amount of matter; weight is the pull of gravity on mass.. Mass is constant; weight changes.
chunks.source: Mass is constant; weight changes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(i): Give the use of the stalk to the leaf. A: It holds the leaf and transports water and food to and from the leaf.. The stalk (petiole) supports and feeds the leaf.
chunks.source: The stalk (petiole) supports and feeds the leaf.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b)(ii): Give the use of the veins to the leaf. A: They transport water and manufactured food, and support the leaf.. Veins are the leaf's transport system.
chunks.source: Veins are the leaf's transport system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a): Besides plasma, name one other component of blood. A: Red blood cells (or white blood cells / platelets).. Blood has cells besides plasma.
chunks.source: Blood has cells besides plasma.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b)(i): Write any two materials carried by plasma. (i) A: Digested food.. Plasma carries nutrients.
chunks.source: Plasma carries nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b)(ii): Write any two materials carried by plasma. (ii) A: Waste products (or hormones).. Plasma also carries wastes.
chunks.source: Plasma also carries wastes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(c): How are malaria parasites dangerous to the circulatory system? A: They destroy red blood cells, causing anaemia.. Malaria parasites feed on blood.
chunks.source: Malaria parasites feed on blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(i): Apart from wringing, give any two activities involved in cleaning clothes locally. A: Soaking.. Soaking loosens dirt.
chunks.source: Soaking loosens dirt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a)(ii): Apart from wringing, give any two activities involved in cleaning clothes locally. (ii) A: Washing (scrubbing).. Scrubbing removes dirt.
chunks.source: Scrubbing removes dirt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b): Why is it important to wring clothes before spreading them under the sun? A: To remove excess water so they dry faster.. Less water dries quicker.
chunks.source: Less water dries quicker.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c): Write the use of soap when washing clothes. A: It removes dirt and grease.. Soap lifts dirt off clothes.
chunks.source: Soap lifts dirt off clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a): The diagram below is part of the human alimentary canal. Name the part marked with letter T. A: Large intestine (colon).. T is the large intestine.
chunks.source: T is the large intestine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b): How is the part marked with letter R adapted to its function of food absorption? A: It has villi (finger-like structures) that increase surface area for absorption.. Villi absorb digested food.
chunks.source: Villi absorb digested food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c)(i): Write down one disorder of the alimentary canal. A: Constipation.. A common digestive disorder.
chunks.source: A common digestive disorder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c)(ii): Write down one disease of the alimentary canal. A: Cholera (or dysentery).. A digestive system disease.
chunks.source: A digestive system disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(i): Identify any two materials used for harvesting water at home. A: Gutters.. Gutters channel roof water.
chunks.source: Gutters channel roof water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(ii): Identify any two materials used for harvesting water at home. A: Tanks (or jerrycans).. Tanks store harvested water.
chunks.source: Tanks store harvested water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b): Identify any two materials used for harvesting water at home. Why do people harvest water? A: To have water in dry seasons.. Stored water lasts longer.
chunks.source: Stored water lasts longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(c): Name the natural cycle that helps in the production of harvested water. A: The water cycle.. Rain comes through the water cycle.
chunks.source: Rain comes through the water cycle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a): In one sentence, show the meaning of “seed dispersal”. A: Seed dispersal is the scattering of seeds away from the parent plant.. Seeds move to new places.
chunks.source: Seeds move to new places.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b): Give any one advantage of seed dispersal. A: It reduces competition between parent and young plants.. Spread seeds grow better.
chunks.source: Spread seeds grow better.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c)(i): Mention any two seeds dispersed by animals. (i) A: Blackjack.. Its seeds stick to animals.
chunks.source: Its seeds stick to animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c)(ii): Mention any two seeds dispersed by animals. (ii) A: Guava.. Animals eat and spread guava seeds.
chunks.source: Animals eat and spread guava seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a): Why is there no problem playing with a child who is infected with HIV/AIDS in your community? A: Because HIV is not spread by playing or touching.. Casual contact is safe.
chunks.source: Casual contact is safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b): How is the engagement and participation in sports activities important in the fight against HIV/AIDS among school children? A: It keeps children busy and teaches teamwork against AIDS.. Sports unite youth in prevention.
chunks.source: Sports unite youth in prevention.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(c): Name any one harmful traditional practice that may be done to school children in Uganda today. A: Female circumcision (or early marriage).. Harmful practices spread disease.
chunks.source: Harmful practices spread disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(d): Identify any one life skill that may help school children in the fight against HIV/AIDS. A: Assertiveness (saying no).. Life skills protect youth.
chunks.source: Life skills protect youth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(i): Explain in one sentence how electricity can be used to make magnets. A: By passing electricity through a coil (electromagnet).. Current makes a temporary magnet.
chunks.source: Current makes a temporary magnet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(ii): Explain in one sentence how magnets can be used to produce electricity. A: By moving a magnet in a coil (electromagnetic induction).. Moving magnets generate electricity.
chunks.source: Moving magnets generate electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b): What structures on the bee's body enable it to carry pollen grains? A: Pollen baskets (on hind legs) and hairy bodies.. Pollen sticks to hairs and baskets.
chunks.source: Pollen sticks to hairs and baskets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c): Mention the product from pollen made by bees. A: Honey.. Bees make honey from pollen/nectar.
chunks.source: Bees make honey from pollen/nectar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(a): Mention any one method of preserving skins and hides. A: Drying (in the sun).. Dried skins keep longer.
chunks.source: Dried skins keep longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(i): Mention any one method of preserving skins and hides. Write down any two items got from processed skins and hides. A: Shoes.. Leather makes shoes.
chunks.source: Leather makes shoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(b)(ii): Mention any one method of preserving skins and hides. Write down any two items got from processed skins and hides. A: Bags (or belts).. Leather goods are many.
chunks.source: Leather goods are many.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(c): Give any one cattle parasite that may affect the quality of skins and hides. A: Ticks.. Ticks damage skins.
chunks.source: Ticks damage skins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a): Study the diagram of the human skull below. Name the immovable joint at T. A: Suture (joint).. T is a suture, an immovable skull joint.
chunks.source: T is a suture, an immovable skull joint.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(i): List down any two organs protected by the skull. (i) A: The brain.. The skull protects the brain.
chunks.source: The skull protects the brain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(ii): List down any two organs protected by the skull. (ii) A: The eyes (or ears).. Skull also shields sense organs.
chunks.source: Skull also shields sense organs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(c): How is the joint marked by letter T different from the joint at S? A: Joint T is immovable (fixed) while joint S is movable.. Sutures don't move; jaw joints do.
chunks.source: Sutures don't move; jaw joints do.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(i): Name any two natural changes that can displace people in an area. A: Floods.. Floods displace people.
chunks.source: Floods displace people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a)(ii): Name any two natural changes that can displace people in an area. A: Drought (or landslides).. Dry spells also displace.
chunks.source: Dry spells also displace.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b)(i): State any two effects of the natural changes named in (a) above. (i) A: Loss of homes and property.. Disasters destroy.
chunks.source: Disasters destroy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b)(ii): State any two effects of the natural changes named in (a) above. (ii) A: Loss of lives / famine.. People suffer and die.
chunks.source: People suffer and die.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a): Study the diagrams of houses below (M = modern house, N = traditional hut). Name the type of house shown in diagram M. A: A permanent (modern) house.. M is built of bricks with an iron roof.
chunks.source: M is built of bricks with an iron roof.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b)(i): Mention any two materials used to construct house N. (i) A: Mud.. Huts are built of mud.
chunks.source: Huts are built of mud.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b)(ii): Mention any two materials used to construct house N. (ii) A: Grass (thatch).. Thatch roofs huts.
chunks.source: Thatch roofs huts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c): Give any one advantage of house M over house N. A: It lasts longer (is stronger).. Permanent houses endure.
chunks.source: Permanent houses endure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a): Name any one exotic breed of rabbits kept in Uganda. A: New Zealand White (or Californian).. Common exotic breeds.
chunks.source: Common exotic breeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b): Write down any one habit of rabbits you know. A: They burrow (dig holes).. Rabbits live in burrows.
chunks.source: Rabbits live in burrows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c): Give any one rabbit disease that can attack poultry. A: Coccidiosis.. It attacks both rabbits and poultry.
chunks.source: It attacks both rabbits and poultry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(d): State any one way in which rabbit farmers can keep their livestock healthy. A: By keeping their hutches clean.. Clean housing prevents disease.
chunks.source: Clean housing prevents disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(i): The diagram below shows part of a plant (a leaf). Name the part marked X. A: Midrib.. X is the central vein (midrib) of the leaf.
chunks.source: X is the central vein (midrib) of the leaf.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(ii): The diagram below shows part of a plant (a leaf). Name the part marked Y. A: Leaf blade (lamina).. Y is the broad flat part of the leaf.
chunks.source: Y is the broad flat part of the leaf.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b)(i): The diagrams below show ways of making temporary magnets (electromagnets). Name method (i). A: By electricity (using an electric current / electromagnet).. Passing current through a coil makes a temporary magnet.
chunks.source: Passing current through a coil makes a temporary magnet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b)(ii): The diagrams below show ways of making temporary magnets. Name method (ii). A: By stroking with a magnet.. Stroking a magnetic material makes it temporarily magnetic.
chunks.source: Stroking a magnetic material makes it temporarily magnetic.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(i): Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma. Apart from bees, mention any two other insects that help in transferring pollen grains. (i) A: Butterflies.. Butterflies visit flowers and carry pollen.
chunks.source: Butterflies visit flowers and carry pollen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(ii): Apart from bees, mention any two other insects that help in transferring pollen grains. (ii) A: Moths (or beetles).. Moths also pollinate flowers.
chunks.source: Moths also pollinate flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(i): Match A with B. A: (i) rushing to hospital, (ii) fire, (iii) making an alarm, (iv) applying cold pad. B: causes accidents, management of accidents, giving first aid, calling for help from others. Which item in B matches 'rushing to hospital'? A: rushing to hospital: management of accidents. Rushing a casualty to hospital is managing the accident.
chunks.source: Rushing a casualty to hospital is managing the accident.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(ii): Match A with B. Which item in B matches 'fire'? A: fire: causes accidents. Fire is a cause of accidents.
chunks.source: Fire is a cause of accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(iii): Match A with B. Which item in B matches 'making an alarm'? A: making an alarm: calling for help from others. Raising an alarm calls others for help.
chunks.source: Raising an alarm calls others for help.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(iv): Match A with B. Which item in B matches 'applying cold pad'? A: applying cold pad: giving first aid. A cold pad is a first aid treatment.
chunks.source: A cold pad is a first aid treatment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: SECTION A: Why do we wash our hands after garden work? A: To remove germs and dirt.. Hands pick up germs from soil.
chunks.source: Hands pick up germs from soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the space below, draw the internal structure of a bean seed and name the cotyledon. (Converted: Name the food store part of a bean seed.) A: The cotyledon.. It stores food for the seedling.
chunks.source: It stores food for the seedling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one cause of dehydration in human beings. A: Diarrhoea (or vomiting / sweating).. Fluid loss causes dehydration.
chunks.source: Fluid loss causes dehydration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one similarity between the function of spiracles of an insect and gills of a fish. A: Both are used for breathing (gaseous exchange).. Spiracles and gills take in oxygen.
chunks.source: Spiracles and gills take in oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is malaria commonly spread among people? A: By female anopheles mosquitoes.. Mosquito bites spread malaria.
chunks.source: Mosquito bites spread malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does clay soil retain (hold) water for a longer time than sand soil? A: Because it has fine particles that pack closely.. Clay holds water tightly.
chunks.source: Clay holds water tightly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens to iron when it is exposed to water and oxygen? A: It rusts.. Iron + water + oxygen = rust.
chunks.source: Iron + water + oxygen = rust.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of joint found in the neck region. A: Pivot joint.. The neck has a pivot joint.
chunks.source: The neck has a pivot joint.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do some plants shed of their leaves during dry season? A: To reduce water loss (transpiration).. Fewer leaves lose less water.
chunks.source: Fewer leaves lose less water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which structure makes a stem be used for propagation? A: The presence of buds (nodes).. Buds grow into new plants.
chunks.source: Buds grow into new plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the gland that helps in the production of saliva. A: Salivary gland.. It makes saliva.
chunks.source: It makes saliva.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What benefit do crops get from animals in mixed farming? A: They get manure (dung).. Animal dung fertilizes crops.
chunks.source: Animal dung fertilizes crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which stage of development in human beings is characterized by aggression and disobedience? A: Adolescence.. Teenagers may rebel.
chunks.source: Teenagers may rebel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important to regularly weed crops? A: To reduce competition for nutrients, water and sunlight.. Weeds steal from crops.
chunks.source: Weeds steal from crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which pigment in the skin determines the skin colour? A: Melanin.. Melanin colours the skin.
chunks.source: Melanin colours the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify one way in which the electricity produced from Jinja is used by its consumers. A: For lighting (or cooking).. Electricity powers homes.
chunks.source: Electricity powers homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the danger of improper use of the toilet/latrine. A: It spreads diseases (and smells bad).. Poor sanitation breeds germs.
chunks.source: Poor sanitation breeds germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Complete the diagram below by drawing its shadow. (Converted: Where is a shadow formed when light is blocked by an object?) A: A shadow is drawn behind the object, away from the light source.. Light blocked makes a shadow.
chunks.source: Light blocked makes a shadow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is paddock grazing system an advantage? A: It controls overgrazing (pasture rests and regrows).. Rotating paddocks rests grass.
chunks.source: Rotating paddocks rests grass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a clinical thermometer an important tool in a health centre? A: It measures body temperature to detect fever.. Fever shows illness.
chunks.source: Fever shows illness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram below is of an egg (R = shell). State the function of R besides protecting the internal parts. A: It allows gaseous exchange (air passes through its pores).. The shell is porous.
chunks.source: The shell is porous.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do objects fall downwards once thrown upwards? A: Because of gravity.. Gravity pulls things down.
chunks.source: Gravity pulls things down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one secondary sex characteristic in female adolescents. A: Development of breasts (or widening of hips).. Female bodies change at puberty.
chunks.source: Female bodies change at puberty.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Of what importance is the sugar in the oral rehydration solution? A: It gives energy (and helps the body absorb water).. Sugar restores energy.
chunks.source: Sugar restores energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By what process does food move through the alimentary canal? A: By peristalsis.. Muscles push food along.
chunks.source: Muscles push food along.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are frogs different from birds in terms of reproduction? A: Frogs lay eggs in water (external fertilization) while birds lay eggs on land (internal fertilization).. Their breeding differs.
chunks.source: Their breeding differs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What property of air is demonstrated by the diagram below? (Diagram missing in booklet; most likely: air occupies space.) A: Air occupies space.. The diagram (missing) most likely shows air taking up space.
chunks.source: The diagram (missing) most likely shows air taking up space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How best can water be made safe for drinking? A: By boiling it.. Boiling kills germs.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do car tyres rotate more than the distance they cover on a muddy ground? A: Because of friction (they slip on the mud).. Mud makes tyres spin.
chunks.source: Mud makes tyres spin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the beam of light shown below (parallel rays). A: A parallel beam.. The rays are parallel.
chunks.source: The rays are parallel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which children in P.2 can use the air to play. A: By blowing up balloons (or flying kites).. Air fills balloons.
chunks.source: Air fills balloons.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are lizards living in a residential house important? A: They eat insects (mosquitoes and flies).. Lizards control pests.
chunks.source: Lizards control pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do most babies who have been suffering from malaria become anaemic? A: Because malaria parasites destroy red blood cells.. Fewer red cells = anaemia.
chunks.source: Fewer red cells = anaemia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention one method of planting crops. A: Row planting (or broadcasting).. Crops are sown in rows.
chunks.source: Crops are sown in rows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are the feelers of an insect important in its survival? A: They feel (sense) the environment / detect food and danger.. Feelers are sense organs.
chunks.source: Feelers are sense organs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What role can a local counsellor play in promoting immunisation against killer diseases among infants in a community? A: By mobilizing / sensitizing the community.. Leaders encourage immunization.
chunks.source: Leaders encourage immunization.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which disease is common in rabbits and poultry? A: Coccidiosis.. It attacks both.
chunks.source: It attacks both.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Describe the first Aid that can be administered to a casualty with a fractured arm. A: Tie a splint and rush the casualty to hospital.. Splints stop movement.
chunks.source: Splints stop movement.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write SARS in full. A: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome.. SARS is a respiratory disease.
chunks.source: SARS is a respiratory disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a simple machine? A: A device that makes work easier.. Machines simplify work.
chunks.source: Machines simplify work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(i): In which two ways is soil considered a resource? (i) A: It is used for farming (growing crops).. Soil grows plants.
chunks.source: Soil grows plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(a)(ii): In which two ways is soil considered a resource? (ii) A: It is used for building (making bricks).. Soil builds houses.
chunks.source: Soil builds houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(b): What effect does running water have on the soil? A: It causes soil erosion (washes away topsoil).. Running water carries soil.
chunks.source: Running water carries soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 41(c): Why isn't it necessary to mulch a sweet potato garden? A: Because sweet potato leaves cover the soil (act as live mulch).. The vines shade the ground.
chunks.source: The vines shade the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(i): Complete the table below correctly. DISEASE: Polio | VACCINE: ?. Name the vaccine for Polio. A: Polio vaccine (OPV).. Polio is prevented by OPV.
chunks.source: Polio is prevented by OPV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(ii): Complete the table. VACCINE: BGC Vaccine | DISEASE: ?. Name the disease prevented by the BGC vaccine. A: Tuberculosis (TB).. BCG prevents TB.
chunks.source: BCG prevents TB.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(b): Complete the table below correctly. Describe the effect of immunisation in ones body. A: It makes the body produce antibodies (immunity) against the disease.. Vaccines build immunity.
chunks.source: Vaccines build immunity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(a): Study the diagram of two bar magnets (a suspended magnet with S end near the S end of another magnet). What will happen when the magnets are brought close together in the given arrangement? A: They will repel each other (the suspended magnet will move away).. Like poles (S and S) repel.
chunks.source: Like poles (S and S) repel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(b): Which property of magnets is shown by the above diagram? A: Like poles repel each other (unlike poles attract).. The diagram shows repulsion.
chunks.source: The diagram shows repulsion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(c): Give one method of making a magnet. A: By stroking with a magnet (or by electricity).. Stroking magnetizes.
chunks.source: Stroking magnetizes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 43(d): Mention one way an induced magnet can be produced. A: By bringing a magnet near a magnetic material (magnetic induction).. Induction magnetizes temporarily.
chunks.source: Induction magnetizes temporarily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a)(i): Name any two components of the environment. (i) A: Plants (living things).. Plants are part of the environment.
chunks.source: Plants are part of the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(a)(ii): Name any two components of the environment. (ii) A: Water (or air / soil).. Non-living components too.
chunks.source: Non-living components too.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(b): How is the use of petroleum a danger to the environment? A: It causes air pollution (and oil spills pollute water/soil).. Burning petroleum pollutes.
chunks.source: Burning petroleum pollutes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 44(c): In which way is the over exploitation of non-renewable resources a danger? A: They get finished (depleted) and cannot be replaced.. Non-renewables run out.
chunks.source: Non-renewables run out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(i): Name the three states of matter. (i) A: Solid.. Ice is solid.
chunks.source: Ice is solid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(ii): Name the three states of matter. (ii) A: Liquid.. Water is liquid.
chunks.source: Water is liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(a)(iii): Name the three states of matter. (iii) A: Gas.. Steam is gas.
chunks.source: Steam is gas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 45(b): Which metal is a liquid at room temperature? A: Mercury.. Mercury is liquid metal.
chunks.source: Mercury is liquid metal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(a): Use the diagram below (a network of tiny blood vessels) to answer the questions. Name the blood vessels shown in the diagram. A: Capillaries.. The tiny network vessels.
chunks.source: The tiny network vessels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(b): State one importance of the blood vessels in the human body. A: They transport blood (materials) around the body.. Vessels carry blood.
chunks.source: Vessels carry blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(c): Give one structural difference between veins and arteries. A: Arteries have thick walls while veins have thin walls (veins have valves).. Their walls differ.
chunks.source: Their walls differ.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 46(d): Which blood cell is affected by sickle cells? A: Red blood cells.. Sickle cell affects red cells.
chunks.source: Sickle cell affects red cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(i): Bwaise is a slum with ever dirty water flowing in its channels. Mention two diseases people in Bwaise are likely to suffer from if they use or come in contact with that water. (i) A: Cholera.. Dirty water spreads cholera.
chunks.source: Dirty water spreads cholera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(a)(ii): Mention two diseases people in Bwaise are likely to suffer from if they use or come in contact with that water. (ii) A: Typhoid (or dysentery).. Also from dirty water.
chunks.source: Also from dirty water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(i): Give two ways the diseases in (a) above can be controlled. (i) A: By boiling drinking water.. Boiled water is safe.
chunks.source: Boiled water is safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 47(b)(ii): Give two ways the diseases in (a) above can be controlled. (ii) A: By proper disposal of waste (keeping channels clean).. Clean surroundings stop disease.
chunks.source: Clean surroundings stop disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(i): The diagram below shows a female reproductive part of a flower (R = ovary, T = style, S = petal). Name part R. A: Ovary.. R is the swollen base.
chunks.source: R is the swollen base.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(ii): Name part T. A: Style.. T is the tube.
chunks.source: T is the tube.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(a)(iii): Name part S. A: Petal.. S is the petal.
chunks.source: S is the petal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 48(b): Which part in animals is similar to S? (Note: the booklet's S labels the petal; the reproductive part similar in animals is the ovary.) A: The ovary (in female animals).. Both plant ovaries and animal ovaries produce female gametes. (The booklet's S labels the petal; the reproductive part with an animal equivalent is the ovary.)
chunks.source: Both plant ovaries and animal ovaries produce female gametes. (The booklet's S labels the petal; the reproductive part with an animal equivalent is the ovary.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(i): Give the two processes involved in alcohol production by distillation. (i) A: Fermentation.. Yeast ferments sugars to alcohol.
chunks.source: Yeast ferments sugars to alcohol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(a)(ii): Give the two processes involved in alcohol production by distillation. (ii) A: Distillation (evaporation and condensation).. Distilling concentrates alcohol.
chunks.source: Distilling concentrates alcohol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(b): Where in the body is alcohol absorbed into the blood stream? A: In the small intestine (and stomach).. Alcohol passes into blood there.
chunks.source: Alcohol passes into blood there.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 49(c): State one danger of alcohol to one's health. A: It damages the liver (causes liver cirrhosis).. Too much alcohol harms health.
chunks.source: Too much alcohol harms health.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(i): Name any two types of chicken reared in Uganda. (i) A: Layers.. Layers lay eggs.
chunks.source: Layers lay eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(a)(ii): Name any two types of chicken reared in Uganda. (ii) A: Broilers.. Broilers give meat.
chunks.source: Broilers give meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(i): Which feed is given to the first type of chicken named in (a) above? A: Layers' mash.. Layers eat layers' mash.
chunks.source: Layers eat layers' mash.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 51(b)(ii): Which feed is given to the second type of chicken named in (a) above? A: Broiler starter / finisher.. Broilers eat broiler feed.
chunks.source: Broilers eat broiler feed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(a): State one product got from cattle keeping. A: Milk (or beef / hides).. Cattle give milk.
chunks.source: Cattle give milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(i): Why is washing the udder with warm water carried out during the milking process? A: To stimulate milk let-down and clean the udder.. Warm water brings milk.
chunks.source: Warm water brings milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(ii): Why is filtering milk with a strip cup carried out during the milking process? A: To detect mastitis (and remove dirt).. Strip cups show bad milk.
chunks.source: Strip cups show bad milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 52(b)(iii): Why is oiling the teats carried out during the milking process? A: To make milking smooth (prevent cracks).. Oil softens teats.
chunks.source: Oil softens teats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(a): Study the simple circuit diagram below (a cell, a bulb and wire R). With the help of an arrow, show the direction of current flow. (Converted: In which direction does current flow in the circuit?) A: From the positive terminal to the negative terminal (conventional current).. Current leaves the positive side.
chunks.source: Current leaves the positive side.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(b): Name any one material used to make R (the wire). A: Copper (or aluminium).. Wires are copper.
chunks.source: Wires are copper.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(c): How many cells are used in the circuit? A: One.. There is a single cell.
chunks.source: There is a single cell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 53(d): What form of energy is stored in the cell? A: Chemical energy.. Cells store chemical energy.
chunks.source: Cells store chemical energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(a): Use the diagram below (light reflecting off a surface; OP is the incoming ray). Name ray OP. A: The incident ray.. OP comes into the mirror.
chunks.source: OP comes into the mirror.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(b): Complete the diagram correctly. (Converted: What should be drawn to complete the reflection diagram?) A: The reflected ray should be drawn (at the same angle on the other side of the normal).. Complete the reflection.
chunks.source: Complete the reflection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(c): If i (angle of incidence) is 30°, give the value of r (angle of reflection). A: 30°.. Angle of reflection equals angle of incidence.
chunks.source: Angle of reflection equals angle of incidence.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 54(d): Give a reason for your answer in (c) above. A: Because the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.. A law of reflection.
chunks.source: A law of reflection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(a): The diagram below is a plant leaf (with many leaflets on one stalk). What type of leaf is shown? A: A compound leaf.. It has many leaflets.
chunks.source: It has many leaflets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(b): Give a reason for your answer in (a). A: Because it has many small leaflets on one leaf stalk.. Many leaflets = compound.
chunks.source: Many leaflets = compound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(c): What type of leaf is shown above? (Same as (a).) A: A compound leaf.. Same as (a).
chunks.source: Same as (a).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 55(d): How are leaves important to animals? A: They provide food (and oxygen) for animals.. Animals eat leaves.
chunks.source: Animals eat leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 42(a)(iii): Complete the table. DISEASE: Measles | VACCINE: ?. Name the vaccine for Measles. A: Measles vaccine.. Measles is prevented by the measles vaccine.
chunks.source: Measles is prevented by the measles vaccine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(i): Match A with B. A: (i) weeding, (ii) mulching, (iii) spraying, (iv) pruning. B: controls pests, removes weeds, conserves moisture, removes excess branches. Which item in B matches 'weeding'? A: weeding: removes weeds. Weeding removes unwanted plants.
chunks.source: Weeding removes unwanted plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(ii): Match A with B. Which item in B matches 'mulching'? A: mulching: conserves moisture. Mulch keeps soil moist.
chunks.source: Mulch keeps soil moist.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(iii): Match A with B. Which item in B matches 'spraying'? A: spraying: controls pests. Spraying chemicals kills pests.
chunks.source: Spraying chemicals kills pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: 50(iv): Match A with B. Which item in B matches 'pruning'? A: pruning: removes excess branches. Pruning cuts off extra branches.
chunks.source: Pruning cuts off extra branches.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A human skeleton is the ____ of bones that supports the body. A: framework. The human skeleton is made up of all the bones joined together to form a framework.
chunks.source: The human skeleton is made up of all the bones joined together to form a framework.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of a flat bone in the body is the ____. A: skull. Flat bones include the skull, ribs, sternum and shoulder blades.
chunks.source: Flat bones include the skull, ribs, sternum and shoulder blades.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Posture is the ____ in which the body is held when sitting, standing or walking. A: position. Good posture keeps the body upright and balanced.
chunks.source: Good posture keeps the body upright and balanced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the femur, the ____ also forms the joint at the knee. A: tibia. The knee joint is formed by the femur (thigh bone) and the tibia (shin bone).
chunks.source: The knee joint is formed by the femur (thigh bone) and the tibia (shin bone).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A joint is a ____ where two or more bones meet. A: point. A joint is the point where two or more bones meet to allow movement.
chunks.source: A joint is the point where two or more bones meet to allow movement.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One function of joints in the body is to allow ____. A: movement. Joints allow different parts of the body to move.
chunks.source: Joints allow different parts of the body to move.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a tendon different from a ligament? A: A tendon joins a muscle to a bone while a ligament joins a bone to a bone. Tendons attach muscles to bones; ligaments hold bones together at joints.
chunks.source: Tendons attach muscles to bones; ligaments hold bones together at joints.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The immunisable disease that affects the bones is ____. A: polio. Polio (poliomyelitis) can be prevented by immunisation, and it weakens bones and muscles.
chunks.source: Polio (poliomyelitis) can be prevented by immunisation, and it weakens bones and muscles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from protecting delicate body organs, which of these is another function of the skeletal system? A: Giving the body shape. The skeleton gives the body shape and support, and stores mineral salts.
chunks.source: The skeleton gives the body shape and support, and stores mineral salts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way of maintaining the proper working of the skeletal system is ____. A: doing regular body exercises. Body exercises, good posture and a balanced diet keep the skeleton healthy.
chunks.source: Body exercises, good posture and a balanced diet keep the skeleton healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One mineral salt stored in bones is ____. A: calcium. Bones store mineral salts such as calcium and phosphorus.
chunks.source: Bones store mineral salts such as calcium and phosphorus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which joint is formed by the femur and the tibia? A: Knee joint. The femur (thigh bone) and tibia (shin bone) meet at the knee joint.
chunks.source: The femur (thigh bone) and tibia (shin bone) meet at the knee joint.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are the biceps and triceps called antagonistic muscles? A: Because when one contracts, the other relaxes. Antagonistic muscles work in opposite directions to move bones.
chunks.source: Antagonistic muscles work in opposite directions to move bones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a strain different from a sprain? A: A strain affects muscles or tendons while a sprain affects ligaments. A strain is the overstretching of a muscle or tendon; a sprain is the tearing of ligaments.
chunks.source: A strain is the overstretching of a muscle or tendon; a sprain is the tearing of ligaments.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of the shoulder, the bone marked X (the collar bone) is the ____. A: clavicle. The clavicle, also called the collar bone, connects the shoulder to the breastbone.
chunks.source: The clavicle, also called the collar bone, connects the shoulder to the breastbone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram, the joint indicated by letter S (the shoulder joint) is a: A: Ball and socket joint. The shoulder is a ball and socket joint which allows movement in all directions.
chunks.source: The shoulder is a ball and socket joint which allows movement in all directions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from synovial fluid, ____ also prevents friction in a joint. A: cartilage. Cartilage is a smooth, slippery tissue covering bone ends that reduces friction.
chunks.source: Cartilage is a smooth, slippery tissue covering bone ends that reduces friction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of a hinge joint is the ____ joint. A: knee. Hinge joints like the knee and elbow allow movement in one direction only.
chunks.source: Hinge joints like the knee and elbow allow movement in one direction only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of an immovable joint in the body is found in the ____. A: skull. The bones of the skull are joined by immovable joints.
chunks.source: The bones of the skull are joined by immovable joints.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are cardiac muscles called involuntary muscles? A: Because they work on their own without our control. Cardiac (heart) muscles work automatically without our conscious control.
chunks.source: Cardiac (heart) muscles work automatically without our conscious control.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from cardiac muscles, another example of an involuntary muscle is found in the ____. A: stomach. Muscles of the stomach and intestines work involuntarily to move food.
chunks.source: Muscles of the stomach and intestines work involuntarily to move food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One deficiency disease of the skeleton is ____. A: rickets. Rickets is caused by lack of vitamin D, calcium or phosphorus.
chunks.source: Rickets is caused by lack of vitamin D, calcium or phosphorus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of the arm, the bone marked S (in the forearm) is the ____. A: ulna. The ulna is one of the two bones of the forearm.
chunks.source: The ulna is one of the two bones of the forearm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of the arm, what happens to the muscles marked O (triceps) when the arm is raised (straightened)? A: They contract (shorten and thicken). When the arm is straightened, the triceps contract while the biceps relax.
chunks.source: When the arm is straightened, the triceps contract while the biceps relax.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The disorder caused when bones move out of the joint is called ____. A: dislocation. Dislocation happens when bones are forced out of their normal position at a joint.
chunks.source: Dislocation happens when bones are forced out of their normal position at a joint.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A fracture is a ____ or cracked bone. A: broken. A fracture is a break or crack in a bone, usually caused by an accident.
chunks.source: A fracture is a break or crack in a bone, usually caused by an accident.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One importance of correct body posture is that it ____. A: prevents body deformities. Correct posture keeps bones growing properly and prevents deformities.
chunks.source: Correct posture keeps bones growing properly and prevents deformities.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of a voluntary muscle is the ____. A: biceps. Voluntary muscles like the biceps are controlled consciously.
chunks.source: Voluntary muscles like the biceps are controlled consciously.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One sign of rickets in children is ____. A: bow legs. Rickets causes soft, weak bones; signs include bow legs, knock knees and pigeon chest.
chunks.source: Rickets causes soft, weak bones; signs include bow legs, knock knees and pigeon chest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of a gliding joint is found in the ____. A: wrist. Gliding joints are found in the wrist and ankle, where bones slide over each other.
chunks.source: Gliding joints are found in the wrist and ankle, where bones slide over each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The movable joint shown in the diagram (with parts J, H, I, K and L) is a: A: Hinge joint. The diagram shows a hinge joint (like the knee), which moves in one direction only.
chunks.source: The diagram shows a hinge joint (like the knee), which moves in one direction only.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of the joint, the part marked K is the ____. A: ligament. Ligaments are tough bands that hold bones together at a joint.
chunks.source: Ligaments are tough bands that hold bones together at a joint.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the movement of a hinge joint different from that of a ball and socket joint? A: A hinge joint moves in one direction only while a ball and socket joint moves in all directions. Hinge joints (knee, elbow) bend one way; ball and socket joints (shoulder, hip) rotate freely.
chunks.source: Hinge joints (knee, elbow) bend one way; ball and socket joints (shoulder, hip) rotate freely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part of the skeleton that protects the spinal cord is the ____. A: vertebral column. The vertebral column (backbone) encloses and protects the spinal cord.
chunks.source: The vertebral column (backbone) encloses and protects the spinal cord.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do the biceps and triceps work in pairs? A: When the biceps contract, the triceps relax, and vice versa. They are antagonistic muscles: one contracts while the other relaxes to bend or straighten the arm.
chunks.source: They are antagonistic muscles: one contracts while the other relaxes to bend or straighten the arm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Polio in humans is caused by a ____. A: virus. Poliomyelitis is caused by the polio virus.
chunks.source: Poliomyelitis is caused by the polio virus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One sign of polio in humans is ____. A: paralysis. Polio can cause paralysis, muscle weakness and deformed limbs.
chunks.source: Polio can cause paralysis, muscle weakness and deformed limbs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Polio affects the bones by making them ____. A: weak and deformed. Polio weakens muscles and bones, leading to deformities.
chunks.source: Polio weakens muscles and bones, leading to deformities.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A pivot joint is found in the ____. A: neck. The pivot joint in the neck allows the head to turn from side to side.
chunks.source: The pivot joint in the neck allows the head to turn from side to side.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One disorder of the skeletal system is ____. A: fracture. Disorders of the skeletal system include fractures, dislocations, rickets and polio.
chunks.source: Disorders of the skeletal system include fractures, dislocations, rickets and polio.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from transporting materials, blood also ____ the body. A: defends against germs. White blood cells in blood fight disease-causing germs.
chunks.source: White blood cells in blood fight disease-causing germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One disease of blood caused by a virus is ____. A: AIDS. AIDS is caused by HIV, a virus that attacks white blood cells.
chunks.source: AIDS is caused by HIV, a virus that attacks white blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way of preventing diseases of the circulatory system is ____. A: doing regular body exercises. Exercises, a balanced diet and avoiding smoking keep the circulatory system healthy.
chunks.source: Exercises, a balanced diet and avoiding smoking keep the circulatory system healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: During blood circulation, the liver ____. A: controls the sugar level in blood. The liver regulates the amount of sugar in the blood.
chunks.source: The liver regulates the amount of sugar in the blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The blood vessel that transports digested food from the ileum to the liver is the ____. A: hepatic portal vein. The hepatic portal vein carries digested food from the intestines to the liver.
chunks.source: The hepatic portal vein carries digested food from the intestines to the liver.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Materials move out of blood capillaries by the process of ____. A: diffusion. Diffusion is the movement of substances from where they are many to where they are few.
chunks.source: Diffusion is the movement of substances from where they are many to where they are few.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Blood vessels that transport blood towards the heart are called ____. A: veins. Veins carry blood back to the heart.
chunks.source: Veins carry blood back to the heart.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does blood in veins flow at a low pressure? A: Because blood has already passed through capillaries where pressure drops. By the time blood reaches the veins, it has lost pressure passing through the tiny capillaries.
chunks.source: By the time blood reaches the veins, it has lost pressure passing through the tiny capillaries.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of blood do most arteries carry? A: Oxygenated blood. Most arteries carry oxygenated blood away from the heart (except the pulmonary artery).
chunks.source: Most arteries carry oxygenated blood away from the heart (except the pulmonary artery).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Anaemia is caused by lack of ____ in the body. A: iron. Lack of iron reduces haemoglobin in blood, causing anaemia.
chunks.source: Lack of iron reduces haemoglobin in blood, causing anaemia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why can't white blood cells carry oxygen? A: Because they lack haemoglobin. Only red blood cells contain haemoglobin, the pigment that carries oxygen.
chunks.source: Only red blood cells contain haemoglobin, the pigment that carries oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from AIDS, another disease that affects white blood cells is ____. A: leukaemia. Leukaemia is cancer of the white blood cells.
chunks.source: Leukaemia is cancer of the white blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is a structural difference between white and red blood cells? A: White blood cells have a nucleus while red blood cells do not. Mature red blood cells have no nucleus; white blood cells have one.
chunks.source: Mature red blood cells have no nucleus; white blood cells have one.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One disease of red blood cells is ____. A: sickle cell anaemia. Sickle cell anaemia makes red blood cells sickle-shaped so they carry less oxygen.
chunks.source: Sickle cell anaemia makes red blood cells sickle-shaped so they carry less oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Blood plasma is important in the body because it ____. A: transports materials round the body. Plasma is the liquid part of blood that carries dissolved food, hormones and waste.
chunks.source: Plasma is the liquid part of blood that carries dissolved food, hormones and waste.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A joint is the ____ where two bones meet. A: point. A joint is the point where two or more bones meet.
chunks.source: A joint is the point where two or more bones meet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Gliding joints are found in the ____. A: ankle. Gliding joints are found in the wrist and ankle.
chunks.source: Gliding joints are found in the wrist and ankle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from gliding joints, another type of movable joint is the ____ joint. A: hinge. Movable joints include hinge, ball and socket, pivot and gliding joints.
chunks.source: Movable joints include hinge, ball and socket, pivot and gliding joints.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Posture is the way the body is ____ when standing, sitting or walking. A: held. Posture describes how the body is held in different positions.
chunks.source: Posture describes how the body is held in different positions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tearing of ligaments is caused by a ____. A: sprain. A sprain is the overstretching or tearing of ligaments at a joint.
chunks.source: A sprain is the overstretching or tearing of ligaments at a joint.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from protection and movement, the skeleton also ____. A: stores mineral salts. Bones store mineral salts like calcium and phosphorus.
chunks.source: Bones store mineral salts like calcium and phosphorus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of the hip, the bone marked X is the ____. A: pelvis. The pelvis (hip bone) joins the legs to the backbone.
chunks.source: The pelvis (hip bone) joins the legs to the backbone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram, the joint indicated by letter B (the hip joint) is a: A: Ball and socket joint. The hip is a ball and socket joint allowing movement in all directions.
chunks.source: The hip is a ball and socket joint allowing movement in all directions.

chunks.subject: Science
