chunks.text: Q: When the arm is straightened, the triceps muscles ____. A: contract. Straightening the arm makes the triceps contract while the biceps relax.
chunks.source: Straightening the arm makes the triceps contract while the biceps relax.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from calcium, ____ is another mineral salt stored in bones. A: phosphorus. Bones store calcium and phosphorus which make them hard.
chunks.source: Bones store calcium and phosphorus which make them hard.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the function of synovial fluid similar to that of cartilage in a joint? A: Both reduce friction between bones. Synovial fluid lubricates the joint and cartilage gives a smooth surface; both reduce friction.
chunks.source: Synovial fluid lubricates the joint and cartilage gives a smooth surface; both reduce friction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A strain is the overstretching or tearing of a ____. A: muscle. A strain affects muscles or tendons, not ligaments.
chunks.source: A strain affects muscles or tendons, not ligaments.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The spinal cord is protected by the ____. A: backbone. The backbone (vertebral column) surrounds and protects the spinal cord.
chunks.source: The backbone (vertebral column) surrounds and protects the spinal cord.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Poliomyelitis is caused by a ____. A: virus. The polio virus causes poliomyelitis.
chunks.source: The polio virus causes poliomyelitis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One sign of poliomyelitis in humans is ____. A: paralysis of the legs. Polio can paralyse the limbs, especially the legs.
chunks.source: Polio can paralyse the limbs, especially the legs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from immunisation, polio can be prevented by ____. A: observing good personal hygiene. Polio spreads through contaminated food and water, so hygiene helps prevent it.
chunks.source: Polio spreads through contaminated food and water, so hygiene helps prevent it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of the kidney, the part marked R is the ____. A: ureter. The ureter is the tube that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder.
chunks.source: The ureter is the tube that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of the kidney, the function of the part marked T (cortex) is to ____. A: filter blood. The cortex of the kidney contains tiny filters where blood filtration begins.
chunks.source: The cortex of the kidney contains tiny filters where blood filtration begins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from filtering blood, the kidney also ____. A: controls the amount of water and salts in the body. The kidney balances water and salts in the body.
chunks.source: The kidney balances water and salts in the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part of the skin that produces sweat is the ____. A: sweat glands. Sweat glands in the skin produce sweat.
chunks.source: Sweat glands in the skin produce sweat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sweating is important to the body because it ____. A: cools the body. When sweat evaporates from the skin, it cools the body.
chunks.source: When sweat evaporates from the skin, it cools the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sweat is lost from the body by the process of ____. A: evaporation. Sweat evaporates from the skin surface into the air.
chunks.source: Sweat evaporates from the skin surface into the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Nitrogen is important to plants because it helps in the formation of ____. A: proteins. Plants need nitrogen to make proteins for growth.
chunks.source: Plants need nitrogen to make proteins for growth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Electricity is a form of ____. A: energy. Electricity is a form of energy produced by flowing charges.
chunks.source: Electricity is a form of energy produced by flowing charges.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The electricity obtained from flowing water is called ____ electricity. A: hydro. Hydro electricity is generated from fast-flowing water.
chunks.source: Hydro electricity is generated from fast-flowing water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One source of direct current electricity is a ____. A: dry cell. Dry cells and batteries produce direct current.
chunks.source: Dry cells and batteries produce direct current.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The electrolyte used in a wet cell is ____. A: dilute sulphuric acid. A wet cell uses dilute sulphuric acid as the electrolyte.
chunks.source: A wet cell uses dilute sulphuric acid as the electrolyte.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One advantage of secondary cells over primary cells is that they can be ____. A: recharged. Secondary cells can be recharged and reused; primary cells cannot.
chunks.source: Secondary cells can be recharged and reused; primary cells cannot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The non-metallic conductor found in the dry cell is the ____ rod. A: carbon. The carbon (graphite) rod is the positive terminal of a dry cell.
chunks.source: The carbon (graphite) rod is the positive terminal of a dry cell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A torch with two dry cells uses a total voltage of ____. A: 3 volts. Each dry cell is 1.5V, so two dry cells give 3V.
chunks.source: Each dry cell is 1.5V, so two dry cells give 3V.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these shows a difference between conductors and insulators? A: Conductors allow electricity to pass while insulators do not. Conductors (e.g. metals) let current flow; insulators (e.g. rubber) block it.
chunks.source: Conductors (e.g. metals) let current flow; insulators (e.g. rubber) block it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is distilled water not good for drinking? A: Because it lacks mineral salts needed by the body. Distillation removes the useful mineral salts from water.
chunks.source: Distillation removes the useful mineral salts from water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Energy resources are things from which we can get ____. A: energy. Energy resources like the sun, wind and wood provide energy.
chunks.source: Energy resources like the sun, wind and wood provide energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the circuit diagram with a bulb and dry cells, current flows: A: From the positive terminal, through the bulb, back to the negative terminal. Conventional current flows from the positive terminal round the circuit to the negative terminal.
chunks.source: Conventional current flows from the positive terminal round the circuit to the negative terminal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the work of a fuse different from that of a switch? A: A fuse breaks the circuit when current is too high while a switch opens or closes the circuit at will. A fuse protects against too much current; a switch controls the circuit manually.
chunks.source: A fuse protects against too much current; a switch controls the circuit manually.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In an electric bulb, electrical energy changes to ____ energy. A: light and heat. A bulb converts electrical energy into light and heat energy.
chunks.source: A bulb converts electrical energy into light and heat energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the filament of an electric bulb coiled? A: To increase resistance so it produces more light. A coiled filament has higher resistance and glows brighter.
chunks.source: A coiled filament has higher resistance and glows brighter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A circuit is a ____ path through which electric current flows. A: complete. A complete (closed) circuit allows current to flow.
chunks.source: A complete (closed) circuit allows current to flow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of an electrical appliance is a ____. A: radio. Electrical appliances include radios, televisions, flat irons and cookers.
chunks.source: Electrical appliances include radios, televisions, flat irons and cookers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One importance of electricity is that it is used for ____. A: lighting. Electricity is used for lighting, cooking, communication and running machines.
chunks.source: Electricity is used for lighting, cooking, communication and running machines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One advantage of using electricity is that it ____. A: is clean and does not pollute the air. Electricity produces no smoke, so it keeps the air clean.
chunks.source: Electricity produces no smoke, so it keeps the air clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is static electricity different from current electricity? A: Static electricity does not flow while current electricity flows. Static electricity stays in one place; current electricity flows through conductors.
chunks.source: Static electricity stays in one place; current electricity flows through conductors.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of static electricity in nature is ____. A: lightning. Lightning is a huge discharge of static electricity in the sky.
chunks.source: Lightning is a huge discharge of static electricity in the sky.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a lightning conductor protect a building? A: By conducting lightning safely to the ground. It gives lightning an easy path into the earth.
chunks.source: It gives lightning an easy path into the earth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One danger of lightning is that it can ____. A: cause death. Lightning can kill, injure people and animals, and start fires.
chunks.source: Lightning can kill, injure people and animals, and start fires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Magnetism is the force by which magnets ____ iron objects. A: attract. Magnetism is the force of attraction or repulsion shown by magnets.
chunks.source: Magnetism is the force of attraction or repulsion shown by magnets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A magnetic material is a material that can be ____ by a magnet. A: attracted. Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic materials.
chunks.source: Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Solar energy can be obtained in the environment using ____. A: solar panels. Solar panels trap the sun's energy.
chunks.source: Solar panels trap the sun's energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way the sun is used as an energy resource is for ____. A: drying clothes and food. The sun's heat dries clothes, food and other things.
chunks.source: The sun's heat dries clothes, food and other things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a renewable energy resource is ____. A: solar energy. Renewable resources like the sun, wind and water never run out.
chunks.source: Renewable resources like the sun, wind and water never run out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the earth called a magnet? A: Because it has magnetic north and south poles. The earth behaves like a huge magnet with north and south magnetic poles.
chunks.source: The earth behaves like a huge magnet with north and south magnetic poles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The main cause of short circuits is ____. A: bare wires touching each other. When naked wires touch, current takes a short path: a short circuit.
chunks.source: When naked wires touch, current takes a short path: a short circuit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A magnet is an object that ____ iron materials. A: attracts. A magnet attracts magnetic materials like iron and steel.
chunks.source: A magnet attracts magnetic materials like iron and steel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a natural fiber is ____. A: cotton. Natural fibers include cotton, sisal, wool and silk.
chunks.source: Natural fibers include cotton, sisal, wool and silk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One animal used for ploughing is the ____. A: ox. Oxen (bulls) are used to pull ploughs in the garden.
chunks.source: Oxen (bulls) are used to pull ploughs in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The source of energy for plants to make starch is the ____. A: sun. Plants use sunlight energy to make starch during photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants use sunlight energy to make starch during photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Heat energy is important in rain formation because it causes ____. A: evaporation. Heat evaporates water, which rises, condenses and falls as rain.
chunks.source: Heat evaporates water, which rises, condenses and falls as rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A short circuit is when electric current takes a ____ path. A: shorter. A short circuit happens when current flows through an unintended shorter path.
chunks.source: A short circuit happens when current flows through an unintended shorter path.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The strength of an electromagnet can be increased by ____. A: increasing the number of turns of the coil. More coils, or more cells, make a stronger electromagnet.
chunks.source: More coils, or more cells, make a stronger electromagnet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One property of magnets is that ____. A: unlike poles attract each other. Magnets have north and south poles; unlike poles attract, like poles repel.
chunks.source: Magnets have north and south poles; unlike poles attract, like poles repel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of an electrical conductor is ____. A: copper. Metals like copper and aluminium are good conductors of electricity.
chunks.source: Metals like copper and aluminium are good conductors of electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Magnetism is a force that causes magnets to attract or ____. A: repel. Magnetism makes magnets pull towards or push away from each other.
chunks.source: Magnetism makes magnets pull towards or push away from each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way man uses coal as an energy resource is for ____. A: producing thermal electricity. Coal is burnt to produce heat for thermal electricity.
chunks.source: Coal is burnt to produce heat for thermal electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Energy resources are sources from which ____ can be obtained. A: energy. Energy resources are things from which we get energy.
chunks.source: Energy resources are things from which we get energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Two energy resources from plants are ____ and ____. A: firewood and charcoal. Wood products like firewood and charcoal come from plants.
chunks.source: Wood products like firewood and charcoal come from plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of wood in our daily life is for ____. A: cooking. Wood is used for cooking, building and making furniture.
chunks.source: Wood is used for cooking, building and making furniture.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wood conservation is the ____ use of wood. A: wise and careful. Wood conservation means using wood wisely to avoid wasting it.
chunks.source: Wood conservation means using wood wisely to avoid wasting it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Two ways of conserving wood are ____ and ____. A: using energy saving stoves and planting trees. Energy-saving stoves use less wood, and planting trees replaces cut ones.
chunks.source: Energy-saving stoves use less wood, and planting trees replaces cut ones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One advantage of an energy saving stove is that it ____. A: uses less wood. Energy-saving stoves burn less wood, so fewer trees are cut.
chunks.source: Energy-saving stoves burn less wood, so fewer trees are cut.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In a water heater, ____ energy changes to heat energy. A: electrical. A water heater changes electrical energy into heat energy.
chunks.source: A water heater changes electrical energy into heat energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In an electric bulb, electrical energy changes to ____ energy. A: light. A bulb changes electrical energy into light (and heat) energy.
chunks.source: A bulb changes electrical energy into light (and heat) energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In a generator, ____ energy changes to electrical energy. A: kinetic. A generator changes kinetic (movement) energy into electrical energy.
chunks.source: A generator changes kinetic (movement) energy into electrical energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In a motor, electrical energy changes to ____ energy. A: kinetic. A motor changes electrical energy into kinetic (movement) energy.
chunks.source: A motor changes electrical energy into kinetic (movement) energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A fuel is a substance that ____ to produce energy. A: burns. Fuels like wood and petrol burn to release energy.
chunks.source: Fuels like wood and petrol burn to release energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Two examples of wood fuel are ____ and ____. A: firewood and charcoal. Firewood, charcoal and sawdust are wood fuels.
chunks.source: Firewood, charcoal and sawdust are wood fuels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a fossil fuel is ____. A: petroleum. Fossil fuels include petroleum, coal and natural gas.
chunks.source: Fossil fuels include petroleum, coal and natural gas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each form of energy in A with its correct source in B. (A: Thermal energy, Nuclear energy, Wind power, Solar energy; B: Wind, Sun, Coal, Uranium) A: Thermal energy: Coal; Nuclear energy: Uranium; Wind power: Wind; Solar energy: Sun. Thermal energy comes from burning coal; nuclear energy from uranium; wind power from wind; solar energy from the sun.
chunks.source: Thermal energy comes from burning coal; nuclear energy from uranium; wind power from wind; solar energy from the sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The container used for making biogas is called a ____. A: digester. Biogas is produced in a biogas digester.
chunks.source: Biogas is produced in a biogas digester.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Two materials used in the production of biogas are ____ and ____. A: cow dung and plant waste. Animal dung and plant materials rot to produce biogas.
chunks.source: Animal dung and plant materials rot to produce biogas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The gas produced in a biogas digester is ____. A: methane. Methane is the main flammable gas in biogas.
chunks.source: Methane is the main flammable gas in biogas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Two methods of making magnets are ____ and ____. A: stroking and the electrical method. Magnets are made by stroking, by induction, or by the electrical method.
chunks.source: Magnets are made by stroking, by induction, or by the electrical method.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Two properties of magnets are ____ and ____. A: unlike poles attract and like poles repel. Magnets always have two poles; unlike poles attract and like poles repel.
chunks.source: Magnets always have two poles; unlike poles attract and like poles repel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram, the method of making a magnet using a cell, a coil and an iron bar is the: A: Electrical method. Passing electricity through a coil round iron makes an electromagnet.
chunks.source: Passing electricity through a coil round iron makes an electromagnet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the electromagnet diagram, the pole marked X is the: A: North pole. By the clock rule, the end where current flows anticlockwise is the north pole.
chunks.source: By the clock rule, the end where current flows anticlockwise is the north pole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: When the circuit is open, the pins at P ____. A: fall off. An electromagnet loses its magnetism when the current stops, so the pins drop.
chunks.source: An electromagnet loses its magnetism when the current stops, so the pins drop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A magnet can lose its magnetism by ____. A: heating it strongly. Heating, hammering or dropping a magnet weakens or destroys its magnetism.
chunks.source: Heating, hammering or dropping a magnet weakens or destroys its magnetism.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which diagram shows a simple electric circuit with a bulb, a conductor and a dry cell? A: A complete loop with the bulb connected to both terminals of the dry cell. A simple circuit is a complete loop: cell to conductor to bulb to conductor to cell.
chunks.source: A simple circuit is a complete loop: cell to conductor to bulb to conductor to cell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Two uses of electricity are ____ and ____. A: lighting and cooking. Electricity is used for lighting, cooking, communication and transport.
chunks.source: Electricity is used for lighting, cooking, communication and transport.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Two advantages of using electricity are ____ and ____. A: it is clean and it is easy to control. Electricity is clean, fast and easy to switch on or off.
chunks.source: Electricity is clean, fast and easy to switch on or off.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram of two bar magnets with field lines, the property of magnetism shown is: A: Unlike poles attract each other. The field lines join the two magnets, showing that unlike poles attract.
chunks.source: The field lines join the two magnets, showing that unlike poles attract.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram, the pole marked X (facing the north pole of the other magnet) is the: A: South pole. Unlike poles attract, so X facing a north pole must be a south pole.
chunks.source: Unlike poles attract, so X facing a north pole must be a south pole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a natural magnet is ____. A: lodestone. Lodestone (magnetite) is a naturally magnetic rock.
chunks.source: Lodestone (magnetite) is a naturally magnetic rock.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One appliance that uses magnets is a ____. A: loudspeaker. Loudspeakers, electric bells and compasses use magnets.
chunks.source: Loudspeakers, electric bells and compasses use magnets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Two importances of solar energy are ____ and ____. A: it does not pollute and it is free. Solar energy is clean, free and renewable.
chunks.source: Solar energy is clean, free and renewable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A solar panel is painted black to ____. A: absorb more heat. Black surfaces absorb the most heat and light energy.
chunks.source: Black surfaces absorb the most heat and light energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Flowing water possesses ____ energy. A: kinetic. Moving objects possess kinetic energy.
chunks.source: Moving objects possess kinetic energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Two ways man uses wind energy are ____ and ____. A: sailing boats and generating electricity. Wind sails boats and drives windmills to make electricity.
chunks.source: Wind sails boats and drives windmills to make electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way wind is important to plants is for ____. A: dispersing seeds. Wind disperses seeds and helps in pollination.
chunks.source: Wind disperses seeds and helps in pollination.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Oxygen is important during seed germination for ____. A: respiration. The germinating seed respires to release energy for growth.
chunks.source: The germinating seed respires to release energy for growth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The ability to do work is called ____. A: energy. Energy is defined as the ability to do work.
chunks.source: Energy is defined as the ability to do work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An energy resource is anything from which ____ can be obtained. A: energy. Energy resources are sources from which we get energy.
chunks.source: Energy resources are sources from which we get energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of an energy resource in the environment is ____. A: the sun. The sun, wind, water and wood are energy resources.
chunks.source: The sun, wind, water and wood are energy resources.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The sun can be used as an energy resource for ____. A: producing solar electricity. The sun's energy is trapped by solar panels to make electricity.
chunks.source: The sun's energy is trapped by solar panels to make electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The form of electricity obtained from the sun is ____ electricity. A: solar. Solar electricity comes from the sun.
chunks.source: Solar electricity comes from the sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from hydro electricity, another energy resource from water is ____. A: tidal energy. The rise and fall of sea tides can also generate electricity.
chunks.source: The rise and fall of sea tides can also generate electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The form of electricity obtained from wind is ____ electricity. A: wind. Windmills change wind energy into wind electricity.
chunks.source: Windmills change wind energy into wind electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A fuel is a substance that is ____ to produce energy. A: burnt. Fuels release energy when they are burnt.
chunks.source: Fuels release energy when they are burnt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from petroleum, another example of a fossil fuel is ____. A: coal. Coal and natural gas are also fossil fuels.
chunks.source: Coal and natural gas are also fossil fuels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One danger caused by using petroleum to the environment is ____. A: air pollution. Burning petroleum releases smoke that pollutes the air.
chunks.source: Burning petroleum releases smoke that pollutes the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The use of solar energy is friendly to the environment because it ____. A: does not pollute the environment. Solar energy produces no smoke or waste.
chunks.source: Solar energy produces no smoke or waste.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The form of energy obtained from wind is ____ energy. A: wind. Moving air gives us wind energy.
chunks.source: Moving air gives us wind energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The form of fuel obtained from plants and used directly is ____. A: firewood. Firewood is cut from trees and burnt directly.
chunks.source: Firewood is cut from trees and burnt directly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The form of wood fuel obtained by burning wood with a limited supply of oxygen is ____. A: charcoal. Charcoal is made by burning wood with little air.
chunks.source: Charcoal is made by burning wood with little air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One danger of using wood fuel to the environment is ____. A: deforestation. Cutting down trees for wood fuel destroys forests.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees for wood fuel destroys forests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Conservation of resources means using resources ____. A: wisely without wastage. Conservation is the wise use of resources to avoid wasting them.
chunks.source: Conservation is the wise use of resources to avoid wasting them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way of conserving wood fuel is by ____. A: using energy saving stoves. Energy-saving stoves burn less wood.
chunks.source: Energy-saving stoves burn less wood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One danger created by charcoal burning to the environment is ____. A: air pollution. Charcoal burning releases smoke that pollutes the air.
chunks.source: Charcoal burning releases smoke that pollutes the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One animal kept for purposes of ploughing is the ____. A: ox. Oxen pull ploughs in the garden.
chunks.source: Oxen pull ploughs in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way of conserving non-renewable resources is by ____. A: using renewable resources instead. Using sun, wind and water saves non-renewable resources like petroleum.
chunks.source: Using sun, wind and water saves non-renewable resources like petroleum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One importance of wind energy to people is ____. A: generating electricity. Windmills use wind to make electricity.
chunks.source: Windmills use wind to make electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An energy saving stove helps conserve the environment because it ____. A: uses less firewood. Using less wood means fewer trees are cut down.
chunks.source: Using less wood means fewer trees are cut down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One advantage of using energy from water over fossil fuels is that it ____. A: does not pollute the environment. Hydro electricity is clean, while fossil fuels pollute.
chunks.source: Hydro electricity is clean, while fossil fuels pollute.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The form of electricity obtained from burning fossil fuels is ____ electricity. A: thermal. Burning fuels produces heat used to make thermal electricity.
chunks.source: Burning fuels produces heat used to make thermal electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from wood, another substance that stores chemical energy is ____. A: food. Food stores chemical energy which our bodies use.
chunks.source: Food stores chemical energy which our bodies use.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The form of electricity obtained from uranium is ____ electricity. A: nuclear. Uranium is used to produce nuclear electricity.
chunks.source: Uranium is used to produce nuclear electricity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The use of biogas is friendly to the environment because it ____. A: is made from waste and burns cleanly. Biogas turns animal and plant waste into clean fuel.
chunks.source: Biogas turns animal and plant waste into clean fuel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What form of energy enables cars to move? A: Chemical energy (from fuel). Fuel in cars stores chemical energy, which changes to kinetic energy.
chunks.source: Fuel in cars stores chemical energy, which changes to kinetic energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One animal material used in the making of biogas is ____. A: cow dung. Cow dung is the main material put in a biogas digester.
chunks.source: Cow dung is the main material put in a biogas digester.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a non-renewable energy resource is ____. A: petroleum. Petroleum, coal and natural gas cannot be replaced once used up.
chunks.source: Petroleum, coal and natural gas cannot be replaced once used up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wind is caused by ____. A: the uneven heating of the earth by the sun. The sun heats the earth unevenly, making air move as wind.
chunks.source: The sun heats the earth unevenly, making air move as wind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from carbohydrates, ____ also provide the body with energy. A: fats. Fats (lipids) are energy-giving foods.
chunks.source: Fats (lipids) are energy-giving foods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a renewable energy resource is ____. A: wind energy. Wind, sun and water are renewable and never run out.
chunks.source: Wind, sun and water are renewable and never run out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A windmill is put in an open area so that wind can flow ____. A: freely. Plants and buildings block the wind, so windmills need open space.
chunks.source: Plants and buildings block the wind, so windmills need open space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The container used in the production of biogas is the ____. A: digester. A biogas digester is where dung rots to produce gas.
chunks.source: A biogas digester is where dung rots to produce gas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The inside of a solar drier is painted black to ____. A: absorb more heat. Black absorbs heat best, so food dries faster.
chunks.source: Black absorbs heat best, so food dries faster.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Solar panels are painted black to ____. A: absorb more heat and light. Black surfaces absorb the most heat and light energy.
chunks.source: Black surfaces absorb the most heat and light energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wind can be used to generate electricity by turning ____. A: windmills. Wind turns windmill turbines which drive generators.
chunks.source: Wind turns windmill turbines which drive generators.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The energy resource that helps in sailing boats on water is ____. A: wind. Wind pushes against the sails of boats.
chunks.source: Wind pushes against the sails of boats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One importance of a solar drier in a home is ____. A: drying and preserving food. Solar driers dry food so it can be stored for longer.
chunks.source: Solar driers dry food so it can be stored for longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Simple machines are tools that ____. A: make work easier. Simple machines like levers and pulleys make work easier.
chunks.source: Simple machines like levers and pulleys make work easier.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way machines make work easy is by ____. A: reducing the effort needed. Machines let us use less force to do the same work.
chunks.source: Machines let us use less force to do the same work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ladder leaning against a wall is an example of which simple machine? A: Inclined plane. A sloping ladder works as an inclined plane.
chunks.source: A sloping ladder works as an inclined plane.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The turning point of a machine is called the ____. A: fulcrum. The fulcrum is the pivot on which a lever turns.
chunks.source: The fulcrum is the pivot on which a lever turns.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a wedge is an ____. A: axe. Wedges include axes, knives and chisels.
chunks.source: Wedges include axes, knives and chisels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of wedges at home is for ____. A: cutting and splitting. Wedges cut and split wood and other materials.
chunks.source: Wedges cut and split wood and other materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Friction is a force that ____ motion. A: opposes. Friction opposes movement between two surfaces.
chunks.source: Friction opposes movement between two surfaces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way friction is important is that it ____. A: helps us to walk without slipping. Friction between our feet and the ground lets us walk.
chunks.source: Friction between our feet and the ground lets us walk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A bottle opener is a: A: Second class lever. In a bottle opener, the load is between the fulcrum and the effort.
chunks.source: In a bottle opener, the load is between the fulcrum and the effort.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A bottle opener is a second class lever because the ____ is between the fulcrum and the effort. A: load. Second class levers have the load between the fulcrum and the effort.
chunks.source: Second class levers have the load between the fulcrum and the effort.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of screws is for ____. A: holding things together. Screws fasten objects together firmly.
chunks.source: Screws fasten objects together firmly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a wheel and axle is a ____. A: bicycle wheel. Bicycles, cars and steering wheels use wheel and axle.
chunks.source: Bicycles, cars and steering wheels use wheel and axle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way of increasing friction is by ____. A: making surfaces rough. Rough surfaces grip each other and increase friction.
chunks.source: Rough surfaces grip each other and increase friction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One negative effect of friction in moving parts of a machine is ____. A: wear and tear. Friction wears out and damages moving parts.
chunks.source: Friction wears out and damages moving parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a screw is a ____. A: bolt. Bolts are screws used to fasten things.
chunks.source: Bolts are screws used to fasten things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the lever diagram, the effort at P should be applied: A: Downwards. Pushing down at P lifts the load on the other side of the fulcrum.
chunks.source: Pushing down at P lifts the load on the other side of the fulcrum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the lever diagram, at which point should a person hold to use less force? A: P. P is farther from the fulcrum, giving a longer effort arm so less force is needed.
chunks.source: P is farther from the fulcrum, giving a longer effort arm so less force is needed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Holding at P uses less force because P is ____ from the fulcrum. A: farther. The farther the effort is from the fulcrum, the less force is needed.
chunks.source: The farther the effort is from the fulcrum, the less force is needed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An inclined plane is a sloping surface used to ____. A: raise loads easily. An inclined plane is a slope that makes lifting loads easier.
chunks.source: An inclined plane is a slope that makes lifting loads easier.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way inclined planes make work easy is by ____. A: reducing the effort needed to lift loads. Pushing a load up a gentle slope needs less force than lifting it straight up.
chunks.source: Pushing a load up a gentle slope needs less force than lifting it straight up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The simple machine used for raising flags at school is the ____. A: pulley. A pulley changes the direction of effort to raise the flag.
chunks.source: A pulley changes the direction of effort to raise the flag.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the diagram, the type of pulley shown (attached to the load) is a: A: Single movable pulley. The pulley moves up with the load, so it is a single movable pulley.
chunks.source: The pulley moves up with the load, so it is a single movable pulley.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The force needed to overcome a 100Kgf load using a single movable pulley is ____. A: 50Kgf. A single movable pulley halves the effort: 100 divided by 2 = 50Kgf.
chunks.source: A single movable pulley halves the effort: 100 divided by 2 = 50Kgf.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the pulley diagram, the direction of the load is: A: Downwards. The load pulls downwards because of gravity.
chunks.source: The load pulls downwards because of gravity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Birds have streamlined bodies to ____. A: reduce air resistance. A streamlined shape cuts through air easily.
chunks.source: A streamlined shape cuts through air easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A fishing rod is a: A: Third class lever. In a fishing rod, the effort is between the fulcrum and the load.
chunks.source: In a fishing rod, the effort is between the fulcrum and the load.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the see-saw diagram, the part marked M is the ____. A: fulcrum. The fulcrum is the pivot on which the see-saw balances.
chunks.source: The fulcrum is the pivot on which the see-saw balances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: For the see-saw to balance (50Kgf at 4m on one side, Y at 5m on the other), the weight at Y must be ____. A: 40Kgf. 50 x 4 = Y x 5, so Y = 200 / 5 = 40Kgf.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do single fixed pulleys make work easy? A: By changing the direction of the effort. A fixed pulley lets you pull down to lift a load up.
chunks.source: A fixed pulley lets you pull down to lift a load up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of a screw is a ____. A: corkscrew. A corkscrew is a screw used to open bottles.
chunks.source: A corkscrew is a screw used to open bottles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of wheel and axle in our daily lives is in ____. A: bicycles. Bicycles, cars and door knobs use wheel and axle.
chunks.source: Bicycles, cars and door knobs use wheel and axle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The machine drawn in the diagram (a sloping surface) is an: A: Inclined plane. The sloping surface in the diagram is an inclined plane (slope).
chunks.source: The sloping surface in the diagram is an inclined plane (slope).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: On the inclined plane diagram, the distance moved by the load is ____. A: 4m. The load is raised through the vertical height of 4m.
chunks.source: The load is raised through the vertical height of 4m.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One use of an inclined plane to people is ____. A: loading heavy goods onto trucks. Slopes help people load trucks and climb to heights.
chunks.source: Slopes help people load trucks and climb to heights.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part of the human body that works as a third class lever is the ____. A: forearm. The forearm acts as a third class lever with the elbow as the fulcrum.
chunks.source: The forearm acts as a third class lever with the elbow as the fulcrum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mercy (40Kgf) sits on one side of the see-saw and Praise (25Kgf) on the other. What must Mercy do to balance with Praise? A: Move closer to the fulcrum (pivot). The heavier person must sit nearer the pivot to balance the see-saw.
chunks.source: The heavier person must sit nearer the pivot to balance the see-saw.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One force that affects the working of pulleys and slopes is ____. A: friction. Friction opposes motion in pulleys and on slopes.
chunks.source: Friction opposes motion in pulleys and on slopes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Second class levers simplify work because the effort moves a ____ distance than the load. A: longer. The effort arm is longer than the load arm, so less effort is needed.
chunks.source: The effort arm is longer than the load arm, so less effort is needed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Friction is the ____ that opposes the motion of two surfaces in contact. A: force. Friction is a force that slows down or stops objects sliding over each other.
chunks.source: Friction is a force that slows down or stops objects sliding over each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Friction is always a useful force. A: False. Friction can be a nuisance force, for example it wears out the moving parts of machines.
chunks.source: Friction can be a nuisance force, for example it wears out the moving parts of machines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does oiling help to reduce friction in the moving parts of a machine? A: It makes the surfaces smooth so they slide over each other easily. Oil forms a smooth layer between moving surfaces so they slide easily with less friction.
chunks.source: Oil forms a smooth layer between moving surfaces so they slide easily with less friction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of a lubricant, apart from oil, is ____. A: grease. Grease, like oil, is a lubricant that reduces friction between moving parts.
chunks.source: Grease, like oil, is a lubricant that reduces friction between moving parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a hoe called a simple machine? A: It has few parts and makes work easier. A simple machine has few or no moving parts and helps people do work more easily.
chunks.source: A simple machine has few or no moving parts and helps people do work more easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A lever is a rigid bar that ____. A: turns about a fixed point called the fulcrum. A lever turns on a fixed point known as the ____.
chunks.source: A lever turns on a fixed point known as the ____.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which class of levers is a pair of tongs? A: Third class lever. In tongs the effort is between the fulcrum and the load, which is a third class lever.
chunks.source: In tongs the effort is between the fulcrum and the load, which is a third class lever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of an inclined plane is a ____. A: staircase. Think of what you climb to go upstairs.
chunks.source: Think of what you climb to go upstairs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Inclined planes help people to ____. A: push heavy loads to a higher level easily. Why is a ramp easier than lifting a heavy box straight up?
chunks.source: Why is a ramp easier than lifting a heavy box straight up?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of simple machine drawn in the diagram above. (Two screws, X and Y, driven into a piece of wood.) A: Screw. The diagram shows screws, which are simple machines made of an inclined plane wound round a nail.
chunks.source: The diagram shows screws, which are simple machines made of an inclined plane wound round a nail.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why it is easier to use machine Y than machine X. (Machine Y has a slot for a screwdriver; machine X has a plain smooth head.) A: Machine Y has a slot for a screwdriver, giving a better grip and more turning force. The slot in Y lets a screwdriver grip and turn it with greater force than pushing X by hand.
chunks.source: The slot in Y lets a screwdriver grip and turn it with greater force than pushing X by hand.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The skin helps to regulate body temperature by ____. A: producing sweat, which evaporates and cools the body. What comes out of your skin when you feel hot?
chunks.source: What comes out of your skin when you feel hot?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One waste removed from the body by the kidneys is ____. A: urea. It is the main nitrogenous waste in urine.
chunks.source: It is the main nitrogenous waste in urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Wastes should be removed from the body because they are ____ to the body. A: poisonous (harmful). What happens if poison stays in the body?
chunks.source: What happens if poison stays in the body?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following habits affect the proper working of the kidneys? (Choose all that apply.) A: Drinking too little water, Drinking too much alcohol, Eating too much salt. Too little water, too much alcohol and too much salt all strain the kidneys; enough clean water keeps them healthy.
chunks.source: Too little water, too much alcohol and too much salt all strain the kidneys; enough clean water keeps them healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from removing wastes, the skin also ____. A: protects the body from germs and injury. What does your skin stop from getting inside you?
chunks.source: What does your skin stop from getting inside you?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of a fungal disease of the skin is ____. A: ringworm. Its name sounds like a worm but it is a fungus.
chunks.source: Its name sounds like a worm but it is a fungus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Excretion is the removal of ____ from the body. A: waste products. What does the body get rid of through the kidneys, lungs and skin?
chunks.source: What does the body get rid of through the kidneys, lungs and skin?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of an excretory organ is the ____. A: kidney. Which organ filters blood to form urine?
chunks.source: Which organ filters blood to form urine?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name part marked Y in the diagram of the kidney above. (Y points to the funnel-shaped part in the middle of the kidney.) A: Renal pelvis. The funnel-shaped part marked Y is the renal pelvis, where urine collects before entering the ureter.
chunks.source: The funnel-shaped part marked Y is the renal pelvis, where urine collects before entering the ureter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The function of part W in the kidney diagram is to ____. A: filter waste from the blood (filtration takes place there). Part W is the outer layer of the kidney — what happens to blood there?
chunks.source: Part W is the outer layer of the kidney — what happens to blood there?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the function of blood vessel M different from that of blood vessel P in the kidney diagram? A: M carries unfiltered blood into the kidney while P carries filtered blood away from the kidney. M is the renal artery bringing blood to be filtered; P is the renal vein taking cleaned blood back to the body.
chunks.source: M is the renal artery bringing blood to be filtered; P is the renal vein taking cleaned blood back to the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of a wheel and axle is a ____. A: bicycle wheel. Think of something round that turns on a rod.
chunks.source: Think of something round that turns on a rod.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A wheel and axle is used to ____. A: draw water from a well (windlass). How do people fetch water from a deep well?
chunks.source: How do people fetch water from a deep well?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of a wedge used in the kitchen is a ____. A: knife. What sharp tool do you use to cut food?
chunks.source: What sharp tool do you use to cut food?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of pulley is shown in the diagram above? (A single wheel fixed on a support, with a rope over it lifting a 50 kgf load.) A: Single fixed pulley. The wheel is fixed to a support and only changes the direction of the effort, so it is a single fixed pulley.
chunks.source: The wheel is fixed to a support and only changes the direction of the effort, so it is a single fixed pulley.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which class of levers is the pulley machine shown above? A: First class lever. A fixed pulley acts like a first class lever because the fulcrum (axle) is between the effort and the load.
chunks.source: A fixed pulley acts like a first class lever because the fulcrum (axle) is between the effort and the load.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A single fixed pulley is useful in a school for ____. A: raising and lowering the flag on the flag pole. How is the flag raised to the top of the pole?
chunks.source: How is the flag raised to the top of the pole?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Friction can be increased by ____. A: making the surfaces rough. What is the opposite of making surfaces smooth?
chunks.source: What is the opposite of making surfaces smooth?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Part W (the trachea) in the diagram of the breathing system is kept open all the time by ____. A: rings of cartilage. What stiff rings support the windpipe?
chunks.source: What stiff rings support the windpipe?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name part marked Z in the diagram of the breathing system above. (Z points to the large muscle below the lungs.) A: Diaphragm. Part Z is the diaphragm, the large flat muscle below the lungs that helps in breathing.
chunks.source: Part Z is the diaphragm, the large flat muscle below the lungs that helps in breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Part Y (air sacs) in the diagram is adapted to its function because it ____. A: has thin walls, is many in number and is surrounded by blood capillaries. The alveoli have thin walls, are very many and are wrapped in capillaries so gases pass through easily.
chunks.source: The alveoli have thin walls, are very many and are wrapped in capillaries so gases pass through easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from carbon dioxide, the lungs also remove ____ from the body. A: water vapour. What do you see on a cold mirror when you breathe on it?
chunks.source: What do you see on a cold mirror when you breathe on it?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of a viral disease of the lungs is ____. A: influenza (flu). It is a common illness with fever and coughing, caused by a virus.
chunks.source: It is a common illness with fever and coughing, caused by a virus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sweating helps to cool the body because as sweat ____, it takes heat away from the body. A: evaporates. What happens to wet clothes hung in the sun?
chunks.source: What happens to wet clothes hung in the sun?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from filtering blood, the kidneys also ____. A: control the amount of water and salts in the body. What do the kidneys keep in balance in the blood?
chunks.source: What do the kidneys keep in balance in the blood?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Hair on the skin is important because it ____. A: traps heat and keeps the body warm. Why do animals with thick fur stay warm?
chunks.source: Why do animals with thick fur stay warm?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name part marked S in the diagram of the skin above. (S points to the thin strand sticking out of the skin.) A: Hair. Part S is the hair, the thin strand growing out of the skin.
chunks.source: Part S is the hair, the thin strand growing out of the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The function of part R in the skin diagram is to ____. A: hold the hair firmly in the skin (anchor the hair). Part R is the bulb at the base of the hair — what does it do?
chunks.source: Part R is the bulb at the base of the hair — what does it do?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which layer of the skin is marked by letter X in the diagram above? (X points to the topmost layer of the skin.) A: Epidermis. The topmost layer marked X is the epidermis, the outer protective layer of the skin.
chunks.source: The topmost layer marked X is the epidermis, the outer protective layer of the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Light energy is a form of energy that ____. A: enables us to see (makes objects visible). What can you not do in a completely dark room?
chunks.source: What can you not do in a completely dark room?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A natural source of light is the ____. A: sun. What gives us light during the day?
chunks.source: What gives us light during the day?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Light is useful to people because it ____. A: enables them to see. How do your eyes help you move around safely?
chunks.source: How do your eyes help you move around safely?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Testing the fertility of an egg using a candle is called ____. A: candling. It is named after the candle used to shine through the egg.
chunks.source: It is named after the candle used to shine through the egg.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a beam of light different from a ray of light? A: A beam is a group of rays while a ray is a single line of light. A ray is a single straight line of light; many rays together form a beam.
chunks.source: A ray is a single straight line of light; many rays together form a beam.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: During photosynthesis, sunlight energy is used by plants to ____. A: make food. What do plants make in their leaves using sunlight?
chunks.source: What do plants make in their leaves using sunlight?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The moon is not regarded as a source of light because it ____. A: does not produce its own light; it only reflects light from the sun. Where does moonlight actually come from?
chunks.source: Where does moonlight actually come from?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of lens shown in the diagram above. (The lens is thicker in the middle than at the edges.) A: Convex lens. A lens thicker in the middle than at the edges is a convex (converging) lens.
chunks.source: A lens thicker in the middle than at the edges is a convex (converging) lens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a convex lens used to correct long sightedness? A: It converges light rays so that the image is formed on the retina. In long sightedness the image forms behind the retina; a convex lens converges the rays so the image falls on the retina.
chunks.source: In long sightedness the image forms behind the retina; a convex lens converges the rays so the image falls on the retina.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Objects that do not allow light to pass through them are called ____ objects. A: opaque. What do we call objects that block all light?
chunks.source: What do we call objects that block all light?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Shadows are formed because ____. A: light travels in a straight line and is blocked by an opaque object. What happens when light meets an object it cannot pass through?
chunks.source: What happens when light meets an object it cannot pass through?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which lens is used to correct short sightedness? A: Concave lens. A concave (diverging) lens spreads light rays so the image of a short-sighted eye forms on the retina.
chunks.source: A concave (diverging) lens spreads light rays so the image of a short-sighted eye forms on the retina.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of a transparent material is ____. A: glass. What are windows made of?
chunks.source: What are windows made of?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of beam is shown in the diagram below? (The rays spread outwards as they travel.) A: Divergent beam. The rays spread apart as they travel, so it is a divergent beam.
chunks.source: The rays spread apart as they travel, so it is a divergent beam.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Reflection of light is the ____ of light rays when they hit a shiny surface. A: bouncing back. What does a ball do when it hits a wall?
chunks.source: What does a ball do when it hits a wall?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of reflection is caused when the surface is rough? A: Diffuse (irregular) reflection. A rough surface scatters light in many directions, giving diffuse (irregular) reflection.
chunks.source: A rough surface scatters light in many directions, giving diffuse (irregular) reflection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One way of caring for the eyes is ____. A: avoiding reading in dim light. Is reading in darkness good for your eyes?
chunks.source: Is reading in darkness good for your eyes?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Reflection of light is useful to people because it ____. A: enables them to see themselves in mirrors. How do you see your face in a mirror?
chunks.source: How do you see your face in a mirror?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: When the moon comes between the sun and the earth, a ____ eclipse is formed. A: solar. Which body gives out the light that gets blocked?
chunks.source: Which body gives out the light that gets blocked?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the reflection diagram above, the reflected ray should be drawn so that it ____. (Angle b between the incident ray and the normal is 40 degrees.) A: makes the same angle with the normal as the incident ray. The reflected ray leaves the mirror making the same angle with the normal as the incident ray.
chunks.source: The reflected ray leaves the mirror making the same angle with the normal as the incident ray.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: If angle b is 40 degrees in the diagram, the angle of reflection is ____. A: 40 degrees. The two angles measured from the normal are always equal.
chunks.source: The two angles measured from the normal are always equal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The angle of reflection is 40 degrees because ____. A: the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. What does the law of reflection say about the two angles?
chunks.source: What does the law of reflection say about the two angles?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Refraction of light is the ____ of light rays as they pass from one medium to another. A: bending. What happens to a straw in a glass of water?
chunks.source: What happens to a straw in a glass of water?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sound is different from light because sound ____. A: needs a material medium to travel through while light does not. Can sound travel through empty space?
chunks.source: Can sound travel through empty space?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Images formed in plane mirrors are ____. A: the same size as the object (upright and laterally inverted). How big is your image in a flat mirror compared to you?
chunks.source: How big is your image in a flat mirror compared to you?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of reflection is shown in the diagram above? (Parallel rays hit the surface and reflect as parallel rays.) A: Regular (specular) reflection. Parallel rays reflected in one direction show regular (specular) reflection from a smooth surface.
chunks.source: Parallel rays reflected in one direction show regular (specular) reflection from a smooth surface.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the ray marked X in the reflection diagram above. (X is the ray coming towards the mirror.) A: Incident ray. The ray travelling towards the mirror is the incident ray.
chunks.source: The ray travelling towards the mirror is the incident ray.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Ray Z is reflected as shown in the diagram because ____. A: the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. What law controls how a ray bounces off a mirror?
chunks.source: What law controls how a ray bounces off a mirror?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Dispersion of light is the ____ of white light into the seven colours of the spectrum. A: splitting. What does a prism do to white light?
chunks.source: What does a prism do to white light?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being inverted, images formed in a pinhole camera are also ____. A: diminished (smaller than the object). How big is the image compared to the real object?
chunks.source: How big is the image compared to the real object?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Images formed in a pinhole camera are inverted because ____. A: light travels in a straight line. Which property of light makes the rays cross at the hole?
chunks.source: Which property of light makes the rays cross at the hole?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name part marked L in the diagram of the eye above. (L points to the white part of the eye.) A: Sclera. The tough white outer coat of the eyeball marked L is the sclera.
chunks.source: The tough white outer coat of the eyeball marked L is the sclera.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The function of part K in the eye diagram is to ____. A: control the size of the pupil (regulate the amount of light entering the eye). Part K is the coloured part of the eye — what does it adjust?
chunks.source: Part K is the coloured part of the eye — what does it adjust?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An example of a bacterial disease of the eyes is ____. A: conjunctivitis. It makes the eyes red and itchy and is caused by bacteria.
chunks.source: It makes the eyes red and itchy and is caused by bacteria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A lens camera is similar to an eye because both ____. A: have a lens that focuses light to form an image. What part do they both use to focus light?
chunks.source: What part do they both use to focus light?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A ruler placed in water appears broken because of ____. A: refraction of light. Which bending of light causes this?
chunks.source: Which bending of light causes this?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The light spectrum is the ____. A: band of seven colours into which white light is split. What do we see when white light is split?
chunks.source: What do we see when white light is split?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name part marked C in the diagram of the inside of the eye above. (C points to the clear curved front part.) A: Cornea. The transparent curved front part marked C is the cornea, which lets light into the eye.
chunks.source: The transparent curved front part marked C is the cornea, which lets light into the eye.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The function of part D in the eye diagram is to ____. A: focus (refract) light rays onto the retina. Part D is the lens — what does a lens do to light?
chunks.source: Part D is the lens — what does a lens do to light?

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part where an inverted image is formed (marked E) is the ____. A: Retina. The lens focuses light to form an inverted image on the retina at the back of the eye.
chunks.source: The lens focuses light to form an inverted image on the retina at the back of the eye.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one example of a magnetic material: ____. A: Iron. Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic materials because they are attracted by magnets.
chunks.source: Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic materials because they are attracted by magnets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which method of separating mixtures is used to separate iron filings from rice? A: Using a magnet (magnetic separation). A magnet attracts the iron filings and pulls them out of the rice, leaving the rice behind.
chunks.source: A magnet attracts the iron filings and pulls them out of the rice, leaving the rice behind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are magnets useful in hospitals? A: They are used to remove iron splinters from patients' eyes. Doctors use magnets to pull out small pieces of iron from a patient's eye, and big magnets are used in scanning machines.
chunks.source: Doctors use magnets to pull out small pieces of iron from a patient's eye, and big magnets are used in scanning machines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is an eye defect? A: An eye defect is a condition of the eye in which a person cannot see clearly. In an eye defect, light is not focused properly on the retina, so the person cannot see clearly. Examples are short sight and long sight.
chunks.source: In an eye defect, light is not focused properly on the retina, so the person cannot see clearly. Examples are short sight and long sight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What property of magnets does a working compass demonstrate? A: A freely suspended magnet always points in the north-south direction. A compass needle is a small magnet. When it swings freely, it always settles pointing north-south, which is how it shows direction.
chunks.source: A compass needle is a small magnet. When it swings freely, it always settles pointing north-south, which is how it shows direction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one method of making magnets: ____. A: Stroking a magnetic material with a magnet. Artificial magnets are made by stroking, hammering, or passing an electric current through a coil around a magnetic material.
chunks.source: Artificial magnets are made by stroking, hammering, or passing an electric current through a coil around a magnetic material.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What term is given to the ability of a magnet to pull or push other magnetic materials? A: Magnetism. Magnetism is the force by which a magnet attracts (pulls) or repels (pushes) magnetic materials.
chunks.source: Magnetism is the force by which a magnet attracts (pulls) or repels (pushes) magnetic materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the eye. What type of eye defect is shown in the diagram? A: Short sightedness. In the diagram the light rays focus in front of the retina, so the person cannot see distant objects clearly. This is short sightedness.
chunks.source: In the diagram the light rays focus in front of the retina, so the person cannot see distant objects clearly. This is short sightedness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one cause of the eye defect shown in the diagram above. A: The eyeball is too long. When the eyeball is too long (or the lens is too thick), light focuses in front of the retina, causing short sightedness.
chunks.source: When the eyeball is too long (or the lens is too thick), light focuses in front of the retina, causing short sightedness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the earth, mention any other example of a natural magnet: ____. A: Lodestone. Lodestone (magnetite) is a rock found in nature that behaves like a magnet.
chunks.source: Lodestone (magnetite) is a rock found in nature that behaves like a magnet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the two bar magnets in the diagram. Which statement correctly describes the magnetic field between the two magnets? A: Magnetic field lines run from the N pole of one magnet to the S pole of the other. Magnetic field lines always leave the north pole and enter the south pole, so between the two magnets they curve from N to S.
chunks.source: Magnetic field lines always leave the north pole and enter the south pole, so between the two magnets they curve from N to S.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What energy change takes place in a dynamo? A: Mechanical energy to electrical energy. A dynamo changes the energy of motion (turning the coil) into electrical energy.
chunks.source: A dynamo changes the energy of motion (turning the coil) into electrical energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens to a ray of light when it strikes a plane mirror? A: It is reflected. When light hits a plane mirror it bounces off; this bouncing of light is called reflection.
chunks.source: When light hits a plane mirror it bounces off; this bouncing of light is called reflection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the electromagnet. Name part marked X. A: Soft iron core. Part X is the soft iron bar around which the wire is wound. It becomes a temporary magnet when current flows.
chunks.source: Part X is the soft iron bar around which the wire is wound. It becomes a temporary magnet when current flows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the electromagnet. Which pole is indicated by letter E? A: North pole. Following the direction of the current around the coil with the right-hand rule, the end marked E becomes the north pole.
chunks.source: Following the direction of the current around the coil with the right-hand rule, the end marked E becomes the north pole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the electromagnet. Which energy change takes place in part marked W? A: Chemical energy to electrical energy. Part W is the battery (cell), which changes the chemical energy stored in it into electrical energy.
chunks.source: Part W is the battery (cell), which changes the chemical energy stored in it into electrical energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can the strength of an electromagnet be increased? A: By increasing the number of coils of wire around the core. More turns of wire (or a stronger current) make the electromagnet stronger.
chunks.source: More turns of wire (or a stronger current) make the electromagnet stronger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What germ causes trachoma? A: Bacteria. Trachoma is an eye disease caused by bacteria. It spreads through dirty hands, towels and flies.
chunks.source: Trachoma is an eye disease caused by bacteria. It spreads through dirty hands, towels and flies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of the human eye works as the diaphragm of the lens camera? A: The iris. The iris controls how much light enters the eye by making the pupil bigger or smaller, just like a camera diaphragm.
chunks.source: The iris controls how much light enters the eye by making the pupil bigger or smaller, just like a camera diaphragm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the function of the retina of the human eye. A: It receives light images and changes them into nerve signals sent to the brain. The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye where images are formed before the brain interprets them.
chunks.source: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye where images are formed before the brain interprets them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram. Name the optical instrument drawn above. A: Periscope. The instrument uses two mirrors to let the observer see an object that is not in direct line of sight. It is a periscope.
chunks.source: The instrument uses two mirrors to let the observer see an object that is not in direct line of sight. It is a periscope.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: On what principle does the optical instrument drawn above work? A: Reflection of light. The periscope works by reflecting light off two mirrors (plane mirrors) placed at an angle.
chunks.source: The periscope works by reflecting light off two mirrors (plane mirrors) placed at an angle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one use of the optical instrument drawn above to people. A: It is used in submarines to see objects above the water surface. A periscope lets people see over obstacles, for example sailors in a submarine seeing ships above the water.
chunks.source: A periscope lets people see over obstacles, for example sailors in a submarine seeing ships above the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does a coin placed in water appear raised? A: Because of refraction of light. Light rays bend as they pass from water into air, so the coin appears nearer the surface (raised) than it really is.
chunks.source: Light rays bend as they pass from water into air, so the coin appears nearer the surface (raised) than it really is.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is meant by dispersion of light? A: Dispersion of light is the splitting of white light into its seven colours. When white light passes through a prism, it splits into red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. A rainbow is a natural example.
chunks.source: When white light passes through a prism, it splits into red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. A rainbow is a natural example.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are translucent materials? A: Translucent materials are materials that allow some light to pass through them. You cannot see clearly through translucent materials, but some light passes through, unlike opaque materials which block all light.
chunks.source: You cannot see clearly through translucent materials, but some light passes through, unlike opaque materials which block all light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one example of a translucent material: ____. A: Frosted glass. Frosted glass, oiled paper and thin cloth are translucent because they let some light through without giving a clear view.
chunks.source: Frosted glass, oiled paper and thin cloth are translucent because they let some light through without giving a clear view.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one law of light reflection. A: The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. When light reflects off a surface, it bounces off at the same angle at which it arrived.
chunks.source: When light reflects off a surface, it bounces off at the same angle at which it arrived.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the electric bell. Name part marked F. A: Gong. Part F is the gong, the metal dome that the hammer strikes to produce sound.
chunks.source: Part F is the gong, the metal dome that the hammer strikes to produce sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the electric bell. What happens to part E when part D is closed? A: It becomes magnetized and attracts the soft iron armature. Part D is the switch and part E is the electromagnet. When the switch is closed, current flows through the coil and E becomes a magnet that pulls the armature.
chunks.source: Part D is the switch and part E is the electromagnet. When the switch is closed, current flows through the coil and E becomes a magnet that pulls the armature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What energy change takes place in an electric bell? A: Electrical energy to sound energy. The electric bell uses electricity from the battery to make the hammer strike the gong, producing sound.
chunks.source: The electric bell uses electricity from the battery to make the hammer strike the gong, producing sound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is refraction of light? A: Refraction of light is the bending of light rays as they pass from one transparent medium to another. Light bends when it moves between air and water or air and glass, which is why a stick in water looks bent.
chunks.source: Light bends when it moves between air and water or air and glass, which is why a stick in water looks bent.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What term is given to the natural shadow formed when light from the sun is obstructed by the moon or the earth? A: An eclipse. When the moon blocks sunlight from reaching the earth it is a solar eclipse; when the earth blocks sunlight from reaching the moon it is a lunar eclipse.
chunks.source: When the moon blocks sunlight from reaching the earth it is a solar eclipse; when the earth blocks sunlight from reaching the moon it is a lunar eclipse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one use of plane mirrors to people. A: They are used for looking at ourselves when dressing. Plane mirrors give clear, same-size images, so people use them at home and in periscopes.
chunks.source: Plane mirrors give clear, same-size images, so people use them at home and in periscopes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do images formed in a pinhole camera appear inverted? A: Because light travels in straight lines, so light from the top of the object falls on the bottom of the screen. Each ray of light travels straight through the pinhole, so the top and bottom of the object swap places on the screen, making the image upside down.
chunks.source: Each ray of light travels straight through the pinhole, so the top and bottom of the object swap places on the screen, making the image upside down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of the human eye prevents internal reflections? A: The choroid. The choroid is the dark layer that lines the inside of the eye and absorbs stray light so images stay clear.
chunks.source: The choroid is the dark layer that lines the inside of the eye and absorbs stray light so images stay clear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What determines the nature of the image formed in a pinhole camera? A: The distance between the object and the pinhole. Moving the object nearer or farther from the pinhole changes the size and brightness of the image formed on the screen.
chunks.source: Moving the object nearer or farther from the pinhole changes the size and brightness of the image formed on the screen.

chunks.subject: Science
