chunks.text: Q: Mention any one use of magnets to people. A: They are used in compasses to show direction. Magnets are used in compasses, electric bells, radios, dynamos and for separating iron from mixtures.
chunks.source: Magnets are used in compasses, electric bells, radios, dynamos and for separating iron from mixtures.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram. Which method of making magnets is shown above? A: Stroking. The diagram shows a bar magnet being rubbed along an iron nail many times in one direction, which is the stroking method.
chunks.source: The diagram shows a bar magnet being rubbed along an iron nail many times in one direction, which is the stroking method.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram. What name is given to the magnet labeled X? A: An artificial (temporary) magnet. The nail X was magnetised by stroking, so it is an artificial magnet. It is temporary because it can lose its magnetism easily.
chunks.source: The nail X was magnetised by stroking, so it is an artificial magnet. It is temporary because it can lose its magnetism easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a burning candle. Name one form of energy given off at Q: ____. A: Heat energy. A burning candle gives off heat energy and light energy at the flame.
chunks.source: A burning candle gives off heat energy and light energy at the flame.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a burning candle. Name another form of energy given off at Q: ____. A: Light energy. The flame of a burning candle produces light energy which brightens the room.
chunks.source: The flame of a burning candle produces light energy which brightens the room.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a burning candle. What gas supports the burning of the candle? A: Oxygen. Oxygen supports burning. A candle goes out when covered because the oxygen inside is used up.
chunks.source: Oxygen supports burning. A candle goes out when covered because the oxygen inside is used up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What other process in living things produces the same gas as the burning candle? A: Respiration. Both burning and respiration produce carbon dioxide as a waste product.
chunks.source: Both burning and respiration produce carbon dioxide as a waste product.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows the structure of the human urinary system. Name the part marked S: ____. A: Ureter. The ureter is the tube that carries urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder.
chunks.source: The ureter is the tube that carries urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows the structure of the human urinary system. Name the part marked T: ____. A: Urinary bladder. The urinary bladder stores urine temporarily before it is passed out of the body.
chunks.source: The urinary bladder stores urine temporarily before it is passed out of the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows the structure of the human urinary system. What is the function of the part marked R? A: It filters blood and forms urine. Part R is the kidney, which removes wastes from the blood and forms urine.
chunks.source: Part R is the kidney, which removes wastes from the blood and forms urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one disease that affects the urinary system. A: Kidney stones. Diseases of the urinary system include kidney stones, bilharzia and cystitis.
chunks.source: Diseases of the urinary system include kidney stones, bilharzia and cystitis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What force makes a pencil reduce in length as one writes? A: Friction. Friction between the pencil tip and the paper wears the pencil away as you write.
chunks.source: Friction between the pencil tip and the paper wears the pencil away as you write.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one form of energy produced by friction as one writes. A: Heat energy. When two surfaces rub against each other, friction produces heat energy.
chunks.source: When two surfaces rub against each other, friction produces heat energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tick any two disadvantages of friction to a writer. A: It wears out (shortens) the pencil, It wastes energy as heat. Friction wears the pencil down quickly and wastes the writer's energy as heat.
chunks.source: Friction wears the pencil down quickly and wastes the writer's energy as heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two natural resources in the environment that enable plants to make their food: ____ and ____. A: Sunlight and water. Plants need sunlight, water and carbon dioxide from the environment to make food.
chunks.source: Plants need sunlight, water and carbon dioxide from the environment to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the process by which plants make their food? A: Photosynthesis. Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants make food using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide.
chunks.source: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants make food using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which gas is given off during photosynthesis? A: Oxygen. During photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen.
chunks.source: During photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one natural and one artificial source of light: natural ____, artificial ____. A: The sun; a candle. The sun is a natural source of light, while a candle, lamp or torch is made by people and is artificial.
chunks.source: The sun is a natural source of light, while a candle, lamp or torch is made by people and is artificial.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the moon not regarded as a source of light? A: Because it does not produce its own light; it only reflects light from the sun. A source of light must produce its own light. The moon only shines by reflecting sunlight.
chunks.source: A source of light must produce its own light. The moon only shines by reflecting sunlight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which reflection of light is important to people. A: It enables us to see objects. We see objects because they reflect light into our eyes. Mirrors also use reflection.
chunks.source: We see objects because they reflect light into our eyes. Mirrors also use reflection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The illustrations show different types of rays of light. Name the rays of light marked Q and S: Q ____, S ____. A: Q: parallel rays; S: diverging rays. Q shows rays running side by side (parallel), while S shows rays spreading out from a point (diverging).
chunks.source: Q shows rays running side by side (parallel), while S shows rays spreading out from a point (diverging).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of lens can be used to make light rays move as shown in S above? A: Concave lens. A concave lens spreads light rays apart (diverges them), as shown in S.
chunks.source: A concave lens spreads light rays apart (diverges them), as shown in S.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which eye defect can be corrected by a lens which makes rays move as shown in R? A: Long sightedness. R shows converging rays made by a convex lens, and convex lenses are used to correct long sightedness.
chunks.source: R shows converging rays made by a convex lens, and convex lenses are used to correct long sightedness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagrams show two types of simple machines labeled A and B. Name each machine: A ____, B ____. A: A: pulley; B: inclined plane. A shows a wheel with a rope (pulley) and B shows a sloping surface (inclined plane) used to raise the load.
chunks.source: A shows a wheel with a rope (pulley) and B shows a sloping surface (inclined plane) used to raise the load.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the two machines would you choose to use to lift the load X to a height of 2 metres? A: B (the inclined plane). The inclined plane is the better choice because it needs less effort to lift the load.
chunks.source: The inclined plane is the better choice because it needs less effort to lift the load.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason for your choice of machine in the question above. A: An inclined plane needs less effort to lift the load. With an inclined plane the effort moves over a longer distance, so less force is needed to lift the load.
chunks.source: With an inclined plane the effort moves over a longer distance, so less force is needed to lift the load.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows part of the human skeleton. Name the part marked J: ____. A: Ribs (rib cage). Part J points to the ribs, which form the rib cage around the chest.
chunks.source: Part J points to the ribs, which form the rib cage around the chest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tick any two delicate body organs protected by the rib cage. A: The heart, The lungs. The rib cage protects the delicate heart and lungs inside the chest.
chunks.source: The rib cage protects the delicate heart and lungs inside the chest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the rib cage used during breathing out? A: The ribs move downwards and inwards. During breathing out, the rib muscles relax and the ribs move down and in, making the chest smaller so air is pushed out.
chunks.source: During breathing out, the rib muscles relax and the ribs move down and in, making the chest smaller so air is pushed out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows the human skin. Name the layers A and B: A ____, B ____. A: A: epidermis; B: dermis. The epidermis is the outer layer of the skin and the dermis is the inner layer below it.
chunks.source: The epidermis is the outer layer of the skin and the dermis is the inner layer below it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows the human skin. State the functions of parts marked Y and Z: Y ____, Z ____. A: Y (hair): traps warm air to keep the body warm; Z (sweat gland): produces sweat which cools the body. Hairs trap a layer of warm air against the skin, while sweat glands release sweat that cools the body as it evaporates.
chunks.source: Hairs trap a layer of warm air against the skin, while sweat glands release sweat that cools the body as it evaporates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is a section of a human kidney. Name the parts marked with letters B and C: B ____, C ____. A: B: ureter; C: renal pelvis. The ureter carries urine from the kidney to the bladder, and the renal pelvis collects urine inside the kidney.
chunks.source: The ureter carries urine from the kidney to the bladder, and the renal pelvis collects urine inside the kidney.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is a section of a human kidney. What happens to blood in the part marked with letter D? A: It is filtered; wastes, excess water and salts are removed from it to form urine. In part D the blood is filtered so that waste products leave the blood and become urine.
chunks.source: In part D the blood is filtered so that waste products leave the blood and become urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is a section of a human kidney. How is part A important to the kidney? A: It is the renal vein which carries filtered (clean) blood away from the kidney to the rest of the body. After the kidney filters the blood, the clean blood leaves through the renal vein to circulate in the body.
chunks.source: After the kidney filters the blood, the clean blood leaves through the renal vein to circulate in the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which organ removes urine from the body? A: The urethra. Urine is stored in the bladder and then passed out of the body through the urethra.
chunks.source: Urine is stored in the bladder and then passed out of the body through the urethra.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which body system does the organ that removes urine from the body belong? A: The excretory (urinary) system. The organs that handle urine (kidneys, ureters, bladder, urethra) make up the excretory or urinary system.
chunks.source: The organs that handle urine (kidneys, ureters, bladder, urethra) make up the excretory or urinary system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where does urine collect before it is removed from the body? A: In the urinary bladder. Urine flows from the kidneys through the ureters and is stored in the bladder until it is passed out.
chunks.source: Urine flows from the kidneys through the ureters and is stored in the bladder until it is passed out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one substance found in urine. A: Urea. Urine contains water, urea and dissolved salts removed from the blood by the kidneys.
chunks.source: Urine contains water, urea and dissolved salts removed from the blood by the kidneys.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the process that takes place in the air sacs. A: Gaseous exchange. In the air sacs (alveoli), oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves the blood.
chunks.source: In the air sacs (alveoli), oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves the blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What prevents the trachea from closing during breathing? A: Rings of cartilage. The trachea is held open by C-shaped rings of cartilage so air can pass freely.
chunks.source: The trachea is held open by C-shaped rings of cartilage so air can pass freely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tick any two products found in the air we breathe out. A: Carbon dioxide, Water vapour. Breathed-out air contains more carbon dioxide and water vapour than breathed-in air.
chunks.source: Breathed-out air contains more carbon dioxide and water vapour than breathed-in air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the skin, give any one other example of a respiratory organ. A: The lungs. The lungs are the main respiratory organs where gaseous exchange takes place.
chunks.source: The lungs are the main respiratory organs where gaseous exchange takes place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tick any two diseases which affect the respiratory organs in humans. A: Tuberculosis, Pneumonia. Tuberculosis and pneumonia attack the lungs, while malaria and cholera affect other parts of the body.
chunks.source: Tuberculosis and pneumonia attack the lungs, while malaria and cholera affect other parts of the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one practice by humans which may lead to a respiratory disease. A: Smoking. Smoking damages the lungs and air passages and can lead to respiratory diseases.
chunks.source: Smoking damages the lungs and air passages and can lead to respiratory diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a man using a simple machine Z to load sand onto a truck. What type of simple machine is the man using? A: An inclined plane. The man pushes the wheelbarrow up a sloping plank, which is an inclined plane.
chunks.source: The man pushes the wheelbarrow up a sloping plank, which is an inclined plane.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of inclined planes: ____ and ____. A: A staircase and a slide. Staircases, slides, ladders and ramps are all examples of inclined planes.
chunks.source: Staircases, slides, ladders and ramps are all examples of inclined planes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can the man improve on the machine above in order to make his work easier? A: By using a longer plank to make the slope gentler. A longer, less steep slope needs less effort to push the load up.
chunks.source: A longer, less steep slope needs less effort to push the load up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tick any two examples of non-renewable resources in the environment. A: Petroleum, Coal. Petroleum and coal get used up and cannot be replaced quickly, while sunlight and wind are renewable.
chunks.source: Petroleum and coal get used up and cannot be replaced quickly, while sunlight and wind are renewable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two ways of conserving non-renewable resources: ____ and ____. A: Using them sparingly and using alternative renewable sources of energy. Avoiding wastage and switching to renewable sources like solar energy saves non-renewable resources.
chunks.source: Avoiding wastage and switching to renewable sources like solar energy saves non-renewable resources.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is excretion? A: Excretion is the removal of waste products from the body. The body removes poisonous wastes through the kidneys, skin, lungs and liver. This removal is called excretion.
chunks.source: The body removes poisonous wastes through the kidneys, skin, lungs and liver. This removal is called excretion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why wastes should be removed from the body. A: Wastes are poisonous and can cause diseases if they remain in the body. Waste products are harmful, so the body must remove them to stay healthy.
chunks.source: Waste products are harmful, so the body must remove them to stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the kidneys, mention any other excretory organ. A: The skin. The skin, lungs and liver are also excretory organs because they remove wastes from the body.
chunks.source: The skin, lungs and liver are also excretory organs because they remove wastes from the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one waste removed from the body by the kidneys. A: Excess water. The kidneys remove excess water, urea and salts from the blood and pass them out as urine.
chunks.source: The kidneys remove excess water, urea and salts from the blood and pass them out as urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the function of the kidneys during blood circulation. A: They filter blood and remove wastes from it. As blood circulates through the kidneys, wastes are filtered out and the clean blood continues around the body.
chunks.source: As blood circulates through the kidneys, wastes are filtered out and the clean blood continues around the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the function of the kidneys similar to that of the skin? A: Both remove wastes (excess water and salts) from the body. The kidneys remove wastes as urine while the skin removes wastes as sweat, so both are excretory organs.
chunks.source: The kidneys remove wastes as urine while the skin removes wastes as sweat, so both are excretory organs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which human body organ balances the amount of water needed in the body? A: The kidneys. The kidneys control how much water leaves the body as urine, keeping the body's water balanced.
chunks.source: The kidneys control how much water leaves the body as urine, keeping the body's water balanced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the skin help to maintain body temperature during coldness? A: Hairs stand upright to trap warm air and keep the body warm. In cold weather the hairs on the skin stand up and trap a layer of warm air, and little sweat is produced.
chunks.source: In cold weather the hairs on the skin stand up and trap a layer of warm air, and little sweat is produced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the kidney. Which part of the kidney filters blood? A: Glomerulus. Blood is filtered in the glomerulus, a tiny ball of blood vessels inside the kidney.
chunks.source: Blood is filtered in the glomerulus, a tiny ball of blood vessels inside the kidney.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the kidney. Name the blood vessel marked by letter M. A: Renal vein. The renal vein carries filtered (clean) blood away from the kidney to the rest of the body.
chunks.source: The renal vein carries filtered (clean) blood away from the kidney to the rest of the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the kidney. State the function of part marked N. A: It carries urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder. Part N is the ureter, the tube that takes urine from the kidney to be stored in the bladder.
chunks.source: Part N is the ureter, the tube that takes urine from the kidney to be stored in the bladder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does excessive alcoholism affect the normal working of the kidneys? A: It damages the kidneys and reduces their ability to filter blood properly. Too much alcohol poisons and damages the kidneys so they cannot clean the blood well.
chunks.source: Too much alcohol poisons and damages the kidneys so they cannot clean the blood well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one excretory waste removed from the body through the skin. A: Sweat (excess water and salts). The skin removes excess water and dissolved salts from the body in the form of sweat.
chunks.source: The skin removes excess water and dissolved salts from the body in the form of sweat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the outermost layer of the skin. A: The epidermis. The skin has two layers: the outer epidermis and the inner dermis.
chunks.source: The skin has two layers: the outer epidermis and the inner dermis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from removing wastes, mention one other function of the human skin. A: It protects the body from germs and injury. The skin covers the body to keep germs out and also controls body temperature.
chunks.source: The skin covers the body to keep germs out and also controls body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the function of the hair on the skin. A: It traps warm air to keep the body warm. Hairs on the skin trap a layer of warm air against the body, reducing heat loss in cold weather.
chunks.source: Hairs on the skin trap a layer of warm air against the body, reducing heat loss in cold weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from producing bile, state any other function of the liver. A: It breaks down poisonous substances in the body. The liver detoxifies poisons such as alcohol and also stores glucose as glycogen.
chunks.source: The liver detoxifies poisons such as alcohol and also stores glucose as glycogen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which organ of the body is affected by Hepatitis B? A: The liver. Hepatitis B is a viral disease that attacks the liver.
chunks.source: Hepatitis B is a viral disease that attacks the liver.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What germ causes ringworm infection in humans? A: A fungus. Ringworm is a skin infection caused by a fungus, not by a worm.
chunks.source: Ringworm is a skin infection caused by a fungus, not by a worm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one sign of ringworm infection in humans. A: Ring-shaped itchy rash on the skin. Ringworm shows as round, red, itchy patches on the skin.
chunks.source: Ringworm shows as round, red, itchy patches on the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one way of preventing ringworm infection in humans. A: Keeping the skin clean and dry. Good personal hygiene and avoiding sharing clothes or towels prevents the spread of ringworm.
chunks.source: Good personal hygiene and avoiding sharing clothes or towels prevents the spread of ringworm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Lungs are both respiratory and excretory organs. Give a reason why they are referred to as excretory organs. A: Because they remove carbon dioxide (a waste product) from the body. The lungs remove carbon dioxide and water vapour when we breathe out, so they act as excretory organs too.
chunks.source: The lungs remove carbon dioxide and water vapour when we breathe out, so they act as excretory organs too.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the breathing system. Name part marked Z. A: Diaphragm. The diaphragm is the sheet of muscle below the lungs that moves up and down during breathing.
chunks.source: The diaphragm is the sheet of muscle below the lungs that moves up and down during breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the breathing system. Mention any one disease that affects part marked X. A: Tuberculosis. Part X is in the lung, which can be attacked by tuberculosis, pneumonia or asthma.
chunks.source: Part X is in the lung, which can be attacked by tuberculosis, pneumonia or asthma.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being in the excretory system, in which other system do the kidneys belong? A: The urinary system. The kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra together make up the urinary system.
chunks.source: The kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra together make up the urinary system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of maintaining the proper working of the kidneys. A: Drinking enough clean water. Drinking enough water helps the kidneys flush out wastes, while avoiding alcohol protects them.
chunks.source: Drinking enough water helps the kidneys flush out wastes, while avoiding alcohol protects them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which human body organ regulates body temperature? A: The skin. The skin controls body temperature through sweating, hairs and blood flow near the surface.
chunks.source: The skin controls body temperature through sweating, hairs and blood flow near the surface.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does a person urinate a lot on a cold day than a sunny day? A: Because on a cold day little sweat is produced, so more wastes leave the body as urine. On hot days much water leaves as sweat, but on cold days the kidneys remove the extra water as urine.
chunks.source: On hot days much water leaves as sweat, but on cold days the kidneys remove the extra water as urine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does smoking affect the proper functioning of the lungs? A: It damages the air sacs and reduces the lungs' ability to exchange gases. Smoke harms the air passages and air sacs, making breathing difficult and causing diseases.
chunks.source: Smoke harms the air passages and air sacs, making breathing difficult and causing diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the human skin. Name part marked B. A: Hair follicle. The hair follicle is the pocket in the skin from which the hair grows.
chunks.source: The hair follicle is the pocket in the skin from which the hair grows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the human skin. State the function of part marked C. A: It produces sweat which cools the body and removes wastes. Part C is the sweat gland. Its sweat cools the body as it evaporates and carries out salts.
chunks.source: Part C is the sweat gland. Its sweat cools the body as it evaporates and carries out salts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What germ causes leprosy? A: Bacteria. Leprosy is a skin disease caused by bacteria and it can be cured with medicine.
chunks.source: Leprosy is a skin disease caused by bacteria and it can be cured with medicine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way leprosy can be spread from one person to another. A: Through prolonged close contact with an infected person. Leprosy spreads through droplets from the nose and mouth during long, close contact with an untreated person.
chunks.source: Leprosy spreads through droplets from the nose and mouth during long, close contact with an untreated person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one sign of leprosy. A: Pale patches on the skin with loss of feeling. Leprosy causes pale skin patches that feel numb, and it can damage nerves if not treated.
chunks.source: Leprosy causes pale skin patches that feel numb, and it can damage nerves if not treated.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from being spread through air, give any other way tuberculosis is spread in humans. A: Through drinking unboiled milk from infected cows. Tuberculosis germs can pass through the milk of sick cows, so milk should be boiled before drinking.
chunks.source: Tuberculosis germs can pass through the milk of sick cows, so milk should be boiled before drinking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one sign of tuberculosis in humans. A: A persistent cough. Tuberculosis causes a cough that lasts for weeks, loss of weight and sometimes coughing of blood.
chunks.source: Tuberculosis causes a cough that lasts for weeks, loss of weight and sometimes coughing of blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What communicable disease has similar signs as tuberculosis? A: Whooping cough. Whooping cough also causes severe coughing fits, similar to the persistent cough of tuberculosis.
chunks.source: Whooping cough also causes severe coughing fits, similar to the persistent cough of tuberculosis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the kidney. How is blood carried in J different from that carried in K? A: Blood in J contains wastes (is unfiltered) while blood in K has been filtered (is clean). Blood entering the filtering part still carries wastes, while blood leaving it has been cleaned by the kidney.
chunks.source: Blood entering the filtering part still carries wastes, while blood leaving it has been cleaned by the kidney.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the kidney. Name part marked M. A: Bowman's capsule. The Bowman's capsule is the cup-shaped part that collects the filtered fluid from the glomerulus.
chunks.source: The Bowman's capsule is the cup-shaped part that collects the filtered fluid from the glomerulus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the kidney. How is the function of part marked L different from that of part N? A: L filters blood while N carries urine away from the kidney. The filtering part removes wastes from blood, while the tube part takes the formed urine to the bladder.
chunks.source: The filtering part removes wastes from blood, while the tube part takes the formed urine to the bladder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one activity done during hardening off in a nursery bed. A: Reducing watering of the seedlings. During hardening off, watering is reduced and the shade is removed so seedlings get used to harsh garden conditions.
chunks.source: During hardening off, watering is reduced and the shade is removed so seedlings get used to harsh garden conditions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is transplanting? A: Transplanting is the transfer of seedlings from a nursery bed to the main garden. Seedlings are first raised in a nursery bed and later moved to where they will grow to maturity.
chunks.source: Seedlings are first raised in a nursery bed and later moved to where they will grow to maturity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should transplanting be done in the evening? A: To reduce water loss so that the seedlings do not wilt. In the cool evening there is less heat, so transplanted seedlings lose less water and survive better.
chunks.source: In the cool evening there is less heat, so transplanted seedlings lose less water and survive better.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is thinning different from pruning? A: Thinning is the removal of excess seedlings to create space, while pruning is the removal of unwanted branches from a plant. Thinning reduces crowding of young plants, while pruning shapes grown plants and removes diseased branches.
chunks.source: Thinning reduces crowding of young plants, while pruning shapes grown plants and removes diseased branches.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is mulching? A: Mulching is the covering of soil around plants with dry plant materials. Dry grass, leaves or straw are spread over the soil to keep moisture and control weeds.
chunks.source: Dry grass, leaves or straw are spread over the soil to keep moisture and control weeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one advantage of mulching gardens. A: It keeps soil moisture. Mulches stop water from evaporating, control weeds and rot to add nutrients to the soil.
chunks.source: Mulches stop water from evaporating, control weeds and rot to add nutrients to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of gap filling. A: It maintains the correct plant population in the garden. Gap filling replaces seedlings that died, so the garden keeps the right number of plants.
chunks.source: Gap filling replaces seedlings that died, so the garden keeps the right number of plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which garden tool is used for pruning? A: Secateurs. Secateurs are strong scissors-like tools used for cutting branches when pruning.
chunks.source: Secateurs are strong scissors-like tools used for cutting branches when pruning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of weeds to crops. A: Weeds compete with crops for nutrients, water and sunlight. Weeds steal what crops need to grow, so crop yields go down.
chunks.source: Weeds steal what crops need to grow, so crop yields go down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one method of controlling weeds in a garden. A: Mulching. Weeds can be controlled by mulching, uprooting, slashing or spraying herbicides.
chunks.source: Weeds can be controlled by mulching, uprooting, slashing or spraying herbicides.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does mulching help to conserve soil moisture? A: It reduces evaporation of water from the soil. The mulch cover shields the soil from direct sunshine, so less water escapes into the air.
chunks.source: The mulch cover shields the soil from direct sunshine, so less water escapes into the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one pest of pineapples. A: Mealybugs. Mealybugs and pineapple beetles attack pineapples and reduce the harvest.
chunks.source: Mealybugs and pineapple beetles attack pineapples and reduce the harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one method of harvesting trees in agroforestry. A: Selective felling. In agroforestry trees are harvested by selective felling, coppicing or pollarding so the land keeps being useful.
chunks.source: In agroforestry trees are harvested by selective felling, coppicing or pollarding so the land keeps being useful.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a woodlot? A: A woodlot is a small area where trees are grown for wood. A woodlot is planted to provide firewood, timber and poles.
chunks.source: A woodlot is planted to provide firewood, timber and poles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one factor considered when starting a woodlot project. A: The type of soil. Before starting a woodlot, a farmer considers soil type, land availability, water and the tree species to plant.
chunks.source: Before starting a woodlot, a farmer considers soil type, land availability, water and the tree species to plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one advantage of starting a woodlot project. A: It provides firewood and timber. A woodlot gives the farmer wood for fuel and building, and can also earn income.
chunks.source: A woodlot gives the farmer wood for fuel and building, and can also earn income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of wood in the environment. A: It is used as fuel (firewood). Wood is used as firewood, for building houses and for making furniture.
chunks.source: Wood is used as firewood, for building houses and for making furniture.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are farm records? A: Farm records are written information about activities carried out on a farm. Farm records show what was planted, spent and earned, helping the farmer manage the farm well.
chunks.source: Farm records show what was planted, spent and earned, helping the farmer manage the farm well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one importance of keeping records on a woodlot project. A: They help the farmer to know whether the project is making a profit or a loss. Records show income and costs, so the farmer can tell if the woodlot business is succeeding.
chunks.source: Records show income and costs, so the farmer can tell if the woodlot business is succeeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one type of records kept on a crop farm. A: Production records. Crop farms keep production records, sales records, labour records and inventory records.
chunks.source: Crop farms keep production records, sales records, labour records and inventory records.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one problem faced by a farmer who does not keep records. A: The farmer cannot tell whether the farm is making a profit or a loss. Without records the farmer cannot plan well or know which activities earn money.
chunks.source: Without records the farmer cannot plan well or know which activities earn money.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one activity done by young farmers club. A: Growing crops. Young farmers clubs grow crops, keep livestock and plant trees to learn farming skills.
chunks.source: Young farmers clubs grow crops, keep livestock and plant trees to learn farming skills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one disease of tomatoes. A: Tomato blight. Tomatoes are attacked by blight and bacterial wilt, which destroy the plants and fruits.
chunks.source: Tomatoes are attacked by blight and bacterial wilt, which destroy the plants and fruits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do mulches help to control the growth of weeds in a garden? A: They block sunlight so weeds cannot grow. Weed seeds need light to germinate, and the mulch cover denies them light.
chunks.source: Weed seeds need light to germinate, and the mulch cover denies them light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Use the food chain below. Name the secondary consumer in the food chain. Plants -> Grasshopper -> Hen -> Eagle -> Bacteria A: Hen. The grasshopper is the primary consumer (eats plants), and the hen eats the grasshopper, making the hen the secondary consumer.
chunks.source: The grasshopper is the primary consumer (eats plants), and the hen eats the grasshopper, making the hen the secondary consumer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Use the food chain below. How important are plants in the food chain? Plants -> Grasshopper -> Hen -> Eagle -> Bacteria A: Plants are the producers; they provide food (energy) for all other organisms in the food chain. Without plants there would be no food for the grasshopper, and the whole food chain would collapse.
chunks.source: Without plants there would be no food for the grasshopper, and the whole food chain would collapse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do weeds growing in a garden lower crop yields? A: They compete with crops for nutrients, water, sunlight and space. Weeds take up what crops need, so crops grow poorly and produce less.
chunks.source: Weeds take up what crops need, so crops grow poorly and produce less.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of staking tomatoes in a garden. A: It keeps the fruits off the ground so they do not rot. Staking holds tomato plants upright so fruits stay clean, get sunlight and are easy to harvest.
chunks.source: Staking holds tomato plants upright so fruits stay clean, get sunlight and are easy to harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does spacing of crops help them to grow well? A: It reduces competition for nutrients, water, sunlight and space. Well-spaced crops each get enough of what they need instead of fighting with neighbours.
chunks.source: Well-spaced crops each get enough of what they need instead of fighting with neighbours.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a tree species grown in a woodlot. A: Eucalyptus. Eucalyptus, pine and musizi are fast-growing trees commonly planted in woodlots.
chunks.source: Eucalyptus, pine and musizi are fast-growing trees commonly planted in woodlots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which soil benefits from bacteria. A: Bacteria decompose dead matter and release nutrients into the soil. Decomposer bacteria rot dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil for crops to use.
chunks.source: Decomposer bacteria rot dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil for crops to use.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from helping in germination, how else is oxygen important to plants? A: It is used by plants for respiration. Plants need oxygen to respire and release energy from food, just like animals do.
chunks.source: Plants need oxygen to respire and release energy from food, just like animals do.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does soil benefit from people? A: People add manure and fertilizers to soil to make it fertile. People improve soil by adding manure, mulching and protecting it from erosion.
chunks.source: People improve soil by adding manure, mulching and protecting it from erosion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram. Which method of harvesting wood is shown in the diagram? A: Clear felling. Clear felling is the cutting down of all trees in an area at once.
chunks.source: Clear felling is the cutting down of all trees in an area at once.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one advantage of clear felling over selective felling. A: It is faster and cheaper because a large area is harvested at once. Clear felling harvests much wood in one operation, saving time and labour.
chunks.source: Clear felling harvests much wood in one operation, saving time and labour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we call the practice of growing crops together with trees on the same piece of land? A: Agroforestry. Agroforestry combines trees and crops on the same land so the farmer gets both wood and food.
chunks.source: Agroforestry combines trees and crops on the same land so the farmer gets both wood and food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do plants benefit from agroforestry? A: Trees provide shade and their fallen leaves add nutrients to the soil. In agroforestry, trees shelter crops from strong sunshine and wind, and leaf litter enriches the soil.
chunks.source: In agroforestry, trees shelter crops from strong sunshine and wind, and leaf litter enriches the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one advantage of row planting over broadcasting method of growing crops. A: It is easy to weed and harvest crops planted in rows. Rows give crops equal spacing and leave paths for weeding, spraying and harvesting.
chunks.source: Rows give crops equal spacing and leave paths for weeding, spraying and harvesting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger caused by chemicals sprayed on crops to farmers. A: They can poison the farmers and cause health problems. Farm chemicals are poisonous, so farmers must wear protective clothing when spraying.
chunks.source: Farm chemicals are poisonous, so farmers must wear protective clothing when spraying.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one social problem in the community. A: Theft. Social problems such as theft, corruption and drug abuse disturb peace in the community.
chunks.source: Social problems such as theft, corruption and drug abuse disturb peace in the community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one type of common sickness in a home. A: Malaria. Common sicknesses in homes include malaria, flu, diarrhoea and cough.
chunks.source: Common sicknesses in homes include malaria, flu, diarrhoea and cough.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which immunisable disease affects the liver? A: Hepatitis B. Hepatitis B attacks the liver and can be prevented by immunization.
chunks.source: Hepatitis B attacks the liver and can be prevented by immunization.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are deficiency diseases? A: Deficiency diseases are diseases caused by lack of food nutrients in the body. When the body lacks nutrients like vitamins, protein or iron, deficiency diseases such as kwashiorkor and anaemia occur.
chunks.source: When the body lacks nutrients like vitamins, protein or iron, deficiency diseases such as kwashiorkor and anaemia occur.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one cause of malnutrition in adults. A: Eating an unbalanced diet. Malnutrition in adults is caused by poor feeding, poverty or diseases that reduce appetite.
chunks.source: Malnutrition in adults is caused by poor feeding, poverty or diseases that reduce appetite.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of malnutrition in children. A: It causes stunted growth. Malnourished children grow poorly, fall sick easily and may die.
chunks.source: Malnourished children grow poorly, fall sick easily and may die.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one sign of malnutrition. A: A swollen belly with thin arms and legs. Signs of malnutrition include a swollen belly, thin limbs, brown hair and always feeling tired.
chunks.source: Signs of malnutrition include a swollen belly, thin limbs, brown hair and always feeling tired.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from immunization, give any other way polio can be prevented in a home. A: Drinking boiled clean water. Polio germs spread through dirty water and faeces, so clean water and proper latrines prevent it.
chunks.source: Polio germs spread through dirty water and faeces, so clean water and proper latrines prevent it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the germ that causes polio. A: A virus. Polio is caused by a virus that attacks the nerves and can paralyse the legs.
chunks.source: Polio is caused by a virus that attacks the nerves and can paralyse the legs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from tuberculosis, mention any other bacterial immunisable disease. A: Diphtheria. Bacterial immunisable diseases include tuberculosis, diphtheria, whooping cough and tetanus.
chunks.source: Bacterial immunisable diseases include tuberculosis, diphtheria, whooping cough and tetanus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What causes anaemia? A: Lack of iron in the diet. Anaemia is caused by lack of iron, which the body needs to make red blood cells. Heavy bleeding and malaria can also cause it.
chunks.source: Anaemia is caused by lack of iron, which the body needs to make red blood cells. Heavy bleeding and malaria can also cause it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are communicable diseases? A: Communicable diseases are diseases that can spread from one person to another. Diseases like flu, tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS spread from person to person, unlike non-communicable diseases.
chunks.source: Diseases like flu, tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS spread from person to person, unlike non-communicable diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one communicable disease which is sexually transmitted. A: HIV/AIDS. Sexually transmitted diseases include HIV/AIDS, syphilis and gonorrhoea.
chunks.source: Sexually transmitted diseases include HIV/AIDS, syphilis and gonorrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are health concerns? A: Health concerns are conditions in the community that threaten people's health. Poor sanitation, dirty water and poor waste disposal are health concerns because they make people sick.
chunks.source: Poor sanitation, dirty water and poor waste disposal are health concerns because they make people sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are antisocial behaviours? A: Antisocial behaviours are behaviours that go against the accepted standards of the community. Behaviours like theft, drug abuse and fighting harm others and break community rules.
chunks.source: Behaviours like theft, drug abuse and fighting harm others and break community rules.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one antisocial behaviour among the youth. A: Drug abuse. Drug abuse, theft and gambling are antisocial behaviours common among some youth.
chunks.source: Drug abuse, theft and gambling are antisocial behaviours common among some youth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one community health concern. A: Poor sanitation. Poor sanitation, dirty drinking water and poor waste disposal threaten the health of the whole community.
chunks.source: Poor sanitation, dirty drinking water and poor waste disposal threaten the health of the whole community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one example of a non-communicable disease of the lungs. A: Asthma. Asthma and lung cancer cannot spread from person to person, so they are non-communicable.
chunks.source: Asthma and lung cancer cannot spread from person to person, so they are non-communicable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of antisocial behaviour. A: It leads to imprisonment. Antisocial behaviour can lead to imprisonment, injury, disease and death.
chunks.source: Antisocial behaviour can lead to imprisonment, injury, disease and death.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are sexual deviations? A: Sexual deviations are sexual behaviours that go against the accepted moral standards of the community. They are abnormal sexual behaviours that the community does not accept.
chunks.source: They are abnormal sexual behaviours that the community does not accept.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a sexual deviation. A: Defilement. Examples of sexual deviations include defilement, rape and homosexuality.
chunks.source: Examples of sexual deviations include defilement, rape and homosexuality.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can school-going children prevent themselves from contracting HIV/AIDS? A: By abstaining from sex. Abstinence is the surest way for school children to avoid HIV/AIDS. They should also avoid sharing sharp objects.
chunks.source: Abstinence is the surest way for school children to avoid HIV/AIDS. They should also avoid sharing sharp objects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of controlling common sicknesses in a home. A: Keeping the home clean. A clean home, clean water and proper waste disposal keep common sicknesses away.
chunks.source: A clean home, clean water and proper waste disposal keep common sicknesses away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does sleeping under a treated mosquito net help to prevent malaria? A: It prevents mosquito bites, and the insecticide on the net kills mosquitoes. The net blocks mosquitoes from reaching the sleeper, and its treatment kills mosquitoes that land on it.
chunks.source: The net blocks mosquitoes from reaching the sleeper, and its treatment kills mosquitoes that land on it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does rearing fish in a pond help to prevent the spread of malaria? A: Fish eat mosquito larvae in the water. Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water, but fish in the pond eat their larvae before they grow.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water, but fish in the pond eat their larvae before they grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is sickle cell anaemia different from anaemia? A: Sickle cell anaemia is inherited from parents while ordinary anaemia is caused by lack of iron in the diet. Sickle cell anaemia is passed from parents to children through genes, but ordinary anaemia comes from poor feeding or disease.
chunks.source: Sickle cell anaemia is passed from parents to children through genes, but ordinary anaemia comes from poor feeding or disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one activity that can be done to address health concerns. A: Health education (sensitizing the community). Teaching the community about hygiene, immunization and sanitation addresses health concerns.
chunks.source: Teaching the community about hygiene, immunization and sanitation addresses health concerns.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one life skill of avoiding social problems in youths. A: Assertiveness (saying no to bad peer pressure). Life skills like assertiveness, decision making and self-awareness help youths avoid social problems.
chunks.source: Life skills like assertiveness, decision making and self-awareness help youths avoid social problems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of smoking to a pregnant woman. A: It can cause miscarriage. Smoking harms the unborn baby and can cause miscarriage or a weak baby.
chunks.source: Smoking harms the unborn baby and can cause miscarriage or a weak baby.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of smoking to a family. A: It wastes family income. Money spent on cigarettes is wasted, and second-hand smoke sickens other family members.
chunks.source: Money spent on cigarettes is wasted, and second-hand smoke sickens other family members.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are water-borne diseases? A: Water-borne diseases are diseases spread through drinking contaminated water. Cholera, typhoid and dysentery spread when people drink dirty water.
chunks.source: Cholera, typhoid and dysentery spread when people drink dirty water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which water-borne disease is caused by amoeba? A: Amoebic dysentery. Amoeba in dirty water causes amoebic dysentery, which gives bloody diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Amoeba in dirty water causes amoebic dysentery, which gives bloody diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of sharing water sources with animals. A: Animals contaminate the water and spread diseases to people. Animals pass urine and dung into shared water, spreading diseases like bilharzia to people.
chunks.source: Animals pass urine and dung into shared water, spreading diseases like bilharzia to people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of sharing houses with domestic animals. A: Animals spread diseases and parasites to people. Animals in the house spread germs, fleas and worms to family members.
chunks.source: Animals in the house spread germs, fleas and worms to family members.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one cause of inadequate food in a home. A: Poverty. Poverty, drought, laziness and poor farming methods cause food shortage in homes.
chunks.source: Poverty, drought, laziness and poor farming methods cause food shortage in homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one way of making water safe for drinking. A: Boiling it. Boiling kills germs in water. Water can also be filtered or treated with chlorine.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs in water. Water can also be filtered or treated with chlorine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one water habitat vector. A: Mosquito. Mosquitoes, blackflies and snails live in or near water and spread diseases to people.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes, blackflies and snails live in or near water and spread diseases to people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one disease spread by water habitat vectors. A: Malaria. Water habitat vectors spread malaria (mosquitoes), bilharzia (snails) and river blindness (blackflies).
chunks.source: Water habitat vectors spread malaria (mosquitoes), bilharzia (snails) and river blindness (blackflies).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of controlling water habitat vectors. A: Draining stagnant water. Removing breeding places, spraying insecticides and rearing fish control water habitat vectors.
chunks.source: Removing breeding places, spraying insecticides and rearing fish control water habitat vectors.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does classification of animals mean? A: Grouping animals according to their similarities and differences. Classification of animals means sorting animals into groups based on characteristics they share and how they differ.
chunks.source: Classification of animals means sorting animals into groups based on characteristics they share and how they differ.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an importance of classifying animals? A: It makes animals easy to study and identify. When animals are grouped by their characteristics, scientists and learners can study and identify them more easily.
chunks.source: When animals are grouped by their characteristics, scientists and learners can study and identify them more easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are vertebrates? A: Animals with a backbone. Vertebrates are animals that have a backbone (spine) supporting their bodies.
chunks.source: Vertebrates are animals that have a backbone (spine) supporting their bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a characteristic of vertebrates? A: They have a backbone. All vertebrates have a backbone, though they differ in where they live and how they reproduce.
chunks.source: All vertebrates have a backbone, though they differ in where they live and how they reproduce.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The chart shows classification of vertebrates. Which group of animals is indicated by letter X? A: Warm-blooded vertebrates. Letter X groups birds and mammals (Y) together - these are the warm-blooded vertebrates.
chunks.source: Letter X groups birds and mammals (Y) together - these are the warm-blooded vertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which group of animals is indicated by letter Y in the chart? A: Mammals. Letter Y sits beside birds under warm-blooded vertebrates - it represents mammals.
chunks.source: Letter Y sits beside birds under warm-blooded vertebrates - it represents mammals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of an animal in group K in the chart. A: Tilapia. Group K sits among reptiles and amphibians under cold-blooded vertebrates - it represents fish, e.g. tilapia.
chunks.source: Group K sits among reptiles and amphibians under cold-blooded vertebrates - it represents fish, e.g. tilapia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a kite grouped under birds? A: Because it has feathers, lays eggs and is warm-blooded. A kite is grouped under birds because it shows bird characteristics: feathers, a beak, laying hard-shelled eggs and warm blood.
chunks.source: A kite is grouped under birds because it shows bird characteristics: feathers, a beak, laying hard-shelled eggs and warm blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows the beak of a bird. Why is a bird with this kind of beak a flesh eater? A: The beak is strong and hooked for tearing flesh. Birds of prey like eagles have strong hooked beaks that grip and tear the flesh of their prey.
chunks.source: Birds of prey like eagles have strong hooked beaks that grip and tear the flesh of their prey.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the drawings A to E (A: snake, B: bird, C: bat, D: frog, E: fly). Which of these animals lay eggs? A: A (snake), B (bird), D (frog), E (fly). Snakes, birds, frogs and flies all lay eggs. The bat (C) is a mammal and gives birth to live young.
chunks.source: Snakes, birds, frogs and flies all lay eggs. The bat (C) is a mammal and gives birth to live young.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the animals A to E are cold blooded? A: A (snake), D (frog), E (fly). The snake, frog and fly are cold blooded - their body temperature changes with the surroundings. Birds and bats are warm blooded.
chunks.source: The snake, frog and fly are cold blooded - their body temperature changes with the surroundings. Birds and bats are warm blooded.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which one of the animals A to E has no backbone? A: E (fly). The fly is an insect, which is an invertebrate - it has no backbone. The snake, bird and frog are all vertebrates.
chunks.source: The fly is an insect, which is an invertebrate - it has no backbone. The snake, bird and frog are all vertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why animal C (bat) is a mammal. A: It gives birth to live young and suckles them. Although a bat flies, it is a mammal because it has hair, gives birth to live young and feeds them on milk.
chunks.source: Although a bat flies, it is a mammal because it has hair, gives birth to live young and feeds them on milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a tadpole differ from an adult frog in the way it takes in oxygen? A: A tadpole uses gills while an adult frog uses lungs and its moist skin. A tadpole lives in water and breathes with gills; the adult frog breathes with lungs on land and through its moist skin.
chunks.source: A tadpole lives in water and breathes with gills; the adult frog breathes with lungs on land and through its moist skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fish, reptiles and birds are vertebrates that lay eggs. State one other characteristic which is common to them. A: They all have backbones. Fish, reptiles and birds are all vertebrates, so they all have backbones. (Birds are warm blooded, so cold blood is not common to all.)
chunks.source: Fish, reptiles and birds are all vertebrates, so they all have backbones. (Birds are warm blooded, so cold blood is not common to all.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a bird. What does this animal feed on? A: Dead animals (carrion). The bird in the diagram is a vulture, a scavenger that feeds on the flesh of dead animals.
chunks.source: The bird in the diagram is a vulture, a scavenger that feeds on the flesh of dead animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the animal in the diagram important in the community? A: It cleans the environment by eating dead animals. Vultures remove dead animals from the environment, which keeps surroundings clean and reduces the spread of diseases.
chunks.source: Vultures remove dead animals from the environment, which keeps surroundings clean and reduces the spread of diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is of a fish. Name the part labelled X. A: Dorsal fin. Part X is the dorsal fin, found on the back of the fish. It helps the fish stay upright in water.
chunks.source: Part X is the dorsal fin, found on the back of the fish. It helps the fish stay upright in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: On the diagram of the fish, the gills are found ____. A: on the sides of the head, under the gill cover. A fish's gills are located on both sides of its head, covered by the operculum (gill cover).
chunks.source: A fish's gills are located on both sides of its head, covered by the operculum (gill cover).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a fish take in oxygen? A: It absorbs dissolved oxygen from water using its gills. Water passes over the gills, which absorb the oxygen dissolved in the water into the blood.
chunks.source: Water passes over the gills, which absorb the oxygen dissolved in the water into the blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of part Z (the tail fin) of the fish. A: It helps the fish to swim forward and change direction. The tail (caudal) fin pushes against water to move the fish forward and steers it when turning.
chunks.source: The tail (caudal) fin pushes against water to move the fish forward and steers it when turning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one reason why a frog is able to live both on land and in water comfortably. A: It breathes with lungs on land and through its moist skin in water. An adult frog uses lungs on land and can also absorb oxygen through its moist skin, so it survives in both places.
chunks.source: An adult frog uses lungs on land and can also absorb oxygen through its moist skin, so it survives in both places.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What helps a frog to swim easily in water? A: Its webbed hind feet. The skin between a frog's hind toes (webbed feet) works like paddles, pushing water so the frog swims fast.
chunks.source: The skin between a frog's hind toes (webbed feet) works like paddles, pushing water so the frog swims fast.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Use the list: mouse, chameleon, frog, python. Which two animals can be grouped together? A: Chameleon and python. The chameleon and python are both reptiles - cold blooded vertebrates with dry scaly skins that lay eggs on land.
chunks.source: The chameleon and python are both reptiles - cold blooded vertebrates with dry scaly skins that lay eggs on land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why the chameleon and python are grouped together. A: Both are reptiles. Chameleons and pythons are both reptiles: they are cold blooded, have scales and lay eggs.
chunks.source: Chameleons and pythons are both reptiles: they are cold blooded, have scales and lay eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which animal in the list has a different mode of reproduction from the others? A: Mouse. The mouse is a mammal that gives birth to live young, while the chameleon, frog and python all lay eggs.
chunks.source: The mouse is a mammal that gives birth to live young, while the chameleon, frog and python all lay eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which environment do you find a frog? A: In water and on land near water. Frogs are amphibians found in ponds, swamps and damp places on land near water.
chunks.source: Frogs are amphibians found in ponds, swamps and damp places on land near water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows an animal commonly found in the school surroundings. To which group of animals does this animal belong? A: Reptiles. The animal is a chameleon, which is a reptile - it has dry scales and lays eggs on land.
chunks.source: The animal is a chameleon, which is a reptile - it has dry scales and lays eggs on land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the chameleon protect itself from its enemies? A: By changing its colour to match the surroundings. A chameleon changes its skin colour to blend with its surroundings (camouflage), hiding it from enemies.
chunks.source: A chameleon changes its skin colour to blend with its surroundings (camouflage), hiding it from enemies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the chameleon useful to the environment? A: It eats insects, helping to control pests. Chameleons catch and eat many insects with their long sticky tongues, which controls insect pests in the environment.
chunks.source: Chameleons catch and eat many insects with their long sticky tongues, which controls insect pests in the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagrams show beaks and feet of birds. How is the beak of bird A suitable to its mode of feeding? A: It is broad and flat for sieving food from water and mud. Bird A has a broad flat beak like a duck's, which sieves small food from water and mud.
chunks.source: Bird A has a broad flat beak like a duck's, which sieves small food from water and mud.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the bird use the claws (foot) labelled C for feeding? A: To grip and tear its prey. The sharp claws (talons) of foot C grip prey tightly and help tear flesh when the bird feeds.
chunks.source: The sharp claws (talons) of foot C grip prey tightly and help tear flesh when the bird feeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of food is suitable for the bird's beak labelled B? A: Nectar from flowers. Beak B is long and thin, suited for reaching into flowers to suck nectar.
chunks.source: Beak B is long and thin, suited for reaching into flowers to suck nectar.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How useful is the foot labelled D to the bird? A: It helps the bird to swim (paddle) in water. Foot D is webbed, so it works like a paddle that pushes water and helps the bird swim.
chunks.source: Foot D is webbed, so it works like a paddle that pushes water and helps the bird swim.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: On the diagram of the fish, label with letter P the part which enables the fish to move forward. That part is the ____. A: tail (caudal) fin. The tail (caudal) fin pushes against the water to drive the fish forward.
chunks.source: The tail (caudal) fin pushes against the water to drive the fish forward.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the function of part marked C on the fish? A: The scales protect the fish's body. Part C points to the scales, which cover and protect the fish's body and reduce water loss.
chunks.source: Part C points to the scales, which cover and protect the fish's body and reduce water loss.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the function of part marked T on the fish? A: The nostril helps the fish to smell (detect food and chemicals in water). Part T is the nostril at the top of the snout; the fish uses it to smell its surroundings.
chunks.source: Part T is the nostril at the top of the snout; the fish uses it to smell its surroundings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study list A (fish, bird, frog) and list B (man, whale, bat). How do animals in list A differ from those in B in regards to their reproduction? A: Animals in A lay eggs while animals in B give birth to live young. Fish, birds and frogs all lay eggs, while man, whale and bat are mammals that give birth to live young.
chunks.source: Fish, birds and frogs all lay eggs, while man, whale and bat are mammals that give birth to live young.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are animals in list A similar to those in list B? A: They are all vertebrates. Every animal in both lists has a backbone, so they are all vertebrates.
chunks.source: Every animal in both lists has a backbone, so they are all vertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why a bat is a mammal and not a bird. A: It gives birth to live young and suckles them. Bats have hair and feed their babies on milk, which makes them mammals even though they fly.
chunks.source: Bats have hair and feed their babies on milk, which makes them mammals even though they fly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a vertebrate. To which class of vertebrates does it belong? A: Reptiles. The animal is a tortoise, which is a reptile - cold blooded, with dry scales and a shell, laying eggs on land.
chunks.source: The animal is a tortoise, which is a reptile - cold blooded, with dry scales and a shell, laying eggs on land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the tortoise, name any other animal that belongs to the same class of vertebrates. A: Crocodile. The crocodile is also a reptile like the tortoise. Frogs are amphibians, whales are mammals and sharks are fish.
chunks.source: The crocodile is also a reptile like the tortoise. Frogs are amphibians, whales are mammals and sharks are fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does the tortoise in the diagram feed on? A: Vegetation such as grass and leaves. Tortoises are mainly herbivores that graze on grass, leaves and fruits.
chunks.source: Tortoises are mainly herbivores that graze on grass, leaves and fruits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the tortoise protect itself from enemies? A: By withdrawing its body into its hard shell. When in danger, a tortoise pulls its head, legs and tail inside its hard shell where enemies cannot reach it.
chunks.source: When in danger, a tortoise pulls its head, legs and tail inside its hard shell where enemies cannot reach it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one difference between the way humans and insects breathe. A: Humans breathe through lungs while insects breathe through spiracles. Humans take in air through lungs, while insects take in air through tiny holes called spiracles on their bodies.
chunks.source: Humans take in air through lungs, while insects take in air through tiny holes called spiracles on their bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the animals A (frog), B (mouse), C (snake) and D (snail). In which way are animals A, B and C similar? A: They are all vertebrates. The frog, mouse and snake all have backbones, so they are vertebrates. (The mouse is warm blooded, so they are not all cold blooded.)
chunks.source: The frog, mouse and snake all have backbones, so they are vertebrates. (The mouse is warm blooded, so they are not all cold blooded.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the reproduction of animal B (mouse) different from that of the other animals? A: The mouse gives birth to live young while the others lay eggs. The mouse is a mammal that gives birth to live young; the frog, snake and snail all lay eggs.
chunks.source: The mouse is a mammal that gives birth to live young; the frog, snake and snail all lay eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To what class of vertebrates does animal A (frog) belong? A: Amphibians. A frog lives part of its life in water and part on land, which makes it an amphibian.
chunks.source: A frog lives part of its life in water and part on land, which makes it an amphibian.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does animal D (snail) protect itself from enemies? A: By withdrawing its soft body into its hard shell. When danger comes, a snail pulls its soft body inside its hard shell for protection.
chunks.source: When danger comes, a snail pulls its soft body inside its hard shell for protection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are amphibians? A: Animals that live part of their lives in water and part on land. Amphibians, like frogs and toads, spend part of their life in water and part on land.
chunks.source: Amphibians, like frogs and toads, spend part of their life in water and part on land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a characteristic of amphibians? A: They lay their eggs in water. Amphibians lay soft eggs in water, where the young hatch and live before moving onto land.
chunks.source: Amphibians lay soft eggs in water, where the young hatch and live before moving onto land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another characteristic of amphibians? A: They have moist skins. Amphibians have moist skins through which they can also absorb oxygen.
chunks.source: Amphibians have moist skins through which they can also absorb oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is an example of an amphibian? A: Frog. A frog is an amphibian. A lizard is a reptile, a rat is a mammal and a fish is a fish.
chunks.source: A frog is an amphibian. A lizard is a reptile, a rat is a mammal and a fish is a fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another example of an amphibian. A: Toad. A toad is an amphibian with dry rough skin. Snakes are reptiles, bats are mammals and snails are molluscs.
chunks.source: A toad is an amphibian with dry rough skin. Snakes are reptiles, bats are mammals and snails are molluscs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following animals is warm blooded: fish, lizard, rat and snail? A: Rat. The rat is a mammal, and mammals are warm blooded - they keep a constant body temperature.
chunks.source: The rat is a mammal, and mammals are warm blooded - they keep a constant body temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason to support your answer that the rat is warm blooded. A: It is a mammal and mammals maintain a constant body temperature. As a mammal, the rat's body keeps a steady warm temperature whatever the weather.
chunks.source: As a mammal, the rat's body keeps a steady warm temperature whatever the weather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which class of vertebrates do you put a duckbilled platypus and a kangaroo? A: Mammals. Both the duckbilled platypus and the kangaroo are mammals: the platypus lays eggs but suckles its young, and the kangaroo carries its baby in a pouch.
chunks.source: Both the duckbilled platypus and the kangaroo are mammals: the platypus lays eggs but suckles its young, and the kangaroo carries its baby in a pouch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a characteristic of reptiles? A: They have dry scaly skins. Reptiles are covered with dry scales which protect them and stop their bodies from drying out.
chunks.source: Reptiles are covered with dry scales which protect them and stop their bodies from drying out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is another characteristic of reptiles? A: They lay eggs on land. Most reptiles lay leathery eggs on land, unlike amphibians which lay eggs in water.
chunks.source: Most reptiles lay leathery eggs on land, unlike amphibians which lay eggs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are mammals different from all other vertebrates? A: They give birth to live young and suckle them. Mammals are the only vertebrates that feed their babies on milk from mammary glands (most also give birth to live young).
chunks.source: Mammals are the only vertebrates that feed their babies on milk from mammary glands (most also give birth to live young).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the reproduction of reptiles different from that of amphibians? A: Reptiles lay eggs on land while amphibians lay eggs in water. Reptiles have internal fertilization and lay shelled eggs on land; amphibians have external fertilization and lay soft eggs in water.
chunks.source: Reptiles have internal fertilization and lay shelled eggs on land; amphibians have external fertilization and lay soft eggs in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the table: A (Tilapia, Frog, Crocodile, Dove), B (Rat, Goat, Lion, Whale). What is the similarity in the way animals in A reproduce? A: They all lay eggs. The tilapia, frog, crocodile and dove all reproduce by laying eggs.
chunks.source: The tilapia, frog, crocodile and dove all reproduce by laying eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: To which class of vertebrates do animals in B belong? A: Mammals. The rat, goat, lion and whale are all mammals - they give birth to live young and suckle them.
chunks.source: The rat, goat, lion and whale are all mammals - they give birth to live young and suckle them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is tilapia in A similar to a whale in list B? A: Both live in water. Both the tilapia and the whale live in water, though the whale is a warm-blooded mammal that breathes with lungs.
chunks.source: Both the tilapia and the whale live in water, though the whale is a warm-blooded mammal that breathes with lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the similarity between animals in list A and list B? A: They are all vertebrates. All animals in both lists have backbones, so they are all vertebrates.
chunks.source: All animals in both lists have backbones, so they are all vertebrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of the following is a characteristic of fish? A: They have scales covering their bodies. Fish are covered with overlapping scales that protect their bodies.
chunks.source: Fish are covered with overlapping scales that protect their bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
