chunks.source: Region T is the right side with deoxygenated blood from the body; region M is the left side with oxygenated blood from the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is of a blood cell. What type of blood cell is shown in the diagram? A: White blood cell. The cell has a nucleus and an irregular shape - a white blood cell. (Part T points to its nucleus.)
chunks.source: The cell has a nucleus and an irregular shape - a white blood cell. (Part T points to its nucleus.)

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason for your answer above. A: Because it has a nucleus (and an irregular shape). Unlike red blood cells, white blood cells have a nucleus, which is visible as part T.
chunks.source: Unlike red blood cells, white blood cells have a nucleus, which is visible as part T.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does blood move from the heart to the lungs before it moves round the body? A: To pick up oxygen and release carbon dioxide. Blood must be refreshed with oxygen in the lungs before the heart pumps it to the body.
chunks.source: Blood must be refreshed with oxygen in the lungs before the heart pumps it to the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one function of red blood cells. A: To carry oxygen around the body. Red blood cells use haemoglobin to transport oxygen to all body cells.
chunks.source: Red blood cells use haemoglobin to transport oxygen to all body cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one function of white blood cells. A: To defend the body against germs. White blood cells destroy germs that cause diseases.
chunks.source: White blood cells destroy germs that cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is an illustration of blood circulation in the body. What body organ does part T represent? A: Lungs. Part T is the lungs, where blood exchanges carbon dioxide for oxygen.
chunks.source: Part T is the lungs, where blood exchanges carbon dioxide for oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the difference in the blood carried by blood vessels marked B and C? A: B carries oxygenated blood to the heart while C carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs. Vessel B is the pulmonary vein bringing oxygenated blood from the lungs; vessel C is the pulmonary artery taking deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
chunks.source: Vessel B is the pulmonary vein bringing oxygenated blood from the lungs; vessel C is the pulmonary artery taking deoxygenated blood to the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part of the blood helps in the clotting of blood? A: Platelets. Platelets gather at a cut and form a clot that stops bleeding.
chunks.source: Platelets gather at a cut and form a clot that stops bleeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the left side of the heart able to pump blood to most body parts? A: Because it has thicker and stronger muscles. The left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall to pump blood all round the body.
chunks.source: The left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall to pump blood all round the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: When it is said that Sarah is anaemic, what is lacking from her blood? A: Red blood cells (iron). Anaemia means the blood lacks enough red blood cells (or iron to make them).
chunks.source: Anaemia means the blood lacks enough red blood cells (or iron to make them).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the function of the pulmonary vein different from that of other veins? A: It carries oxygenated blood while other veins carry deoxygenated blood. The pulmonary vein is the only vein carrying oxygenated blood (from the lungs to the heart).
chunks.source: The pulmonary vein is the only vein carrying oxygenated blood (from the lungs to the heart).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the blood vessel which takes blood from the heart to the lungs. A: Pulmonary artery. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.
chunks.source: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the chamber of the heart which pumps blood throughout the body adapted for its function? A: It has thick muscular walls. The left ventricle's thick muscles give the power to pump blood to the whole body.
chunks.source: The left ventricle's thick muscles give the power to pump blood to the whole body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which blood vessels carry blood from the heart? A: Arteries. Arteries are the vessels that carry blood away from the heart.
chunks.source: Arteries are the vessels that carry blood away from the heart.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from transporting body materials, state any other function of blood in the body. A: It distributes heat around the body. Blood also spreads heat evenly and defends the body against germs.
chunks.source: Blood also spreads heat evenly and defends the body against germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which disease of blood is caused by a virus? A: AIDS. AIDS is caused by HIV, a virus that attacks white blood cells.
chunks.source: AIDS is caused by HIV, a virus that attacks white blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What blood vessel transports digested food from the ileum to the liver? A: Hepatic portal vein. The hepatic portal vein carries nutrient-rich blood from the intestines to the liver.
chunks.source: The hepatic portal vein carries nutrient-rich blood from the intestines to the liver.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why blood in veins flows at a low pressure. A: Because veins are far from the heart's pumping force. By the time blood reaches the veins, the heart's push has weakened, so pressure is low (valves help it along).
chunks.source: By the time blood reaches the veins, the heart's push has weakened, so pressure is low (valves help it along).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why white blood cells cannot carry oxygen. A: Because they have no haemoglobin. Only haemoglobin (in red blood cells) can pick up and carry oxygen.
chunks.source: Only haemoglobin (in red blood cells) can pick up and carry oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one structural difference between a white blood cell and a red blood cell. A: A white blood cell has a nucleus while a red blood cell has none. White blood cells have a visible nucleus; mature red blood cells lose theirs.
chunks.source: White blood cells have a visible nucleus; mature red blood cells lose theirs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do arteries withstand the pressure of blood pumped by the heart? A: They have thick elastic muscular walls. The thick elastic walls stretch with each heartbeat without bursting.
chunks.source: The thick elastic walls stretch with each heartbeat without bursting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way of maintaining the proper working of the circulatory system. A: Exercising the body regularly. Regular exercise strengthens the heart and improves blood circulation.
chunks.source: Regular exercise strengthens the heart and improves blood circulation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give another way of maintaining the proper working of the circulatory system. A: Eating a balanced diet. A balanced diet keeps blood vessels healthy and prevents blockages.
chunks.source: A balanced diet keeps blood vessels healthy and prevents blockages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are red blood cells able to carry oxygen around the body? A: Because they contain haemoglobin. Haemoglobin in red blood cells picks up oxygen in the lungs and releases it to body cells.
chunks.source: Haemoglobin in red blood cells picks up oxygen in the lungs and releases it to body cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Use the diagram to answer the questions. Name the blood vessel marked H. A: Artery. Vessel H has a thick wall and narrow space - an artery carrying blood away from the heart.
chunks.source: Vessel H has a thick wall and narrow space - an artery carrying blood away from the heart.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part marked T on blood vessel I. A: Valve. Part T is a valve inside the vein, which stops blood flowing backwards.
chunks.source: Part T is a valve inside the vein, which stops blood flowing backwards.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Blood in blood vessel I (a vein) flows ____ the heart. A: towards. Veins return blood to the heart, and the valve keeps it moving in that one direction.
chunks.source: Veins return blood to the heart, and the valve keeps it moving in that one direction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one disease of the heart. A: Heart attack. A heart attack happens when blood flow to the heart muscle is blocked.
chunks.source: A heart attack happens when blood flow to the heart muscle is blocked.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one disorder of the circulatory system. A: High blood pressure. High blood pressure (hypertension) strains the heart and vessels.
chunks.source: High blood pressure (hypertension) strains the heart and vessels.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the smallest blood vessels in the body. A: Capillaries. Capillaries are the tiniest vessels, where materials pass between blood and body cells.
chunks.source: Capillaries are the tiniest vessels, where materials pass between blood and body cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: What is an essential drug? A: A drug that treats the most common diseases in a community. Essential drugs are the drugs a community needs most to treat common sicknesses.
chunks.source: Essential drugs are the drugs a community needs most to treat common sicknesses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of an essential drug. A: Paracetamol (Panadol). Paracetamol is a common essential drug used to reduce pain and fever.
chunks.source: Paracetamol is a common essential drug used to reduce pain and fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Why are prescriptions important in the treatment of sickness? A: They help the patient take the correct drug in the correct dose. A prescription tells the patient exactly which drug to take, how much and how often.
chunks.source: A prescription tells the patient exactly which drug to take, how much and how often.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: What are contraceptives? A: Drugs or devices used to prevent pregnancy. Contraceptives stop a woman from becoming pregnant when she does not want a baby.
chunks.source: Contraceptives stop a woman from becoming pregnant when she does not want a baby.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a contraceptive. A: Condoms. Condoms are a common contraceptive that also protect against HIV.
chunks.source: Condoms are a common contraceptive that also protect against HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Why is smoking of tobacco harmful to the body? A: Tobacco smoke contains poisonous substances that damage body organs. Poisons in tobacco smoke, like tar and nicotine, damage the lungs and other organs.
chunks.source: Poisons in tobacco smoke, like tar and nicotine, damage the lungs and other organs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Which poisonous substance in tobacco smoke causes lung cancer? A: Tar. Tar is the sticky black substance in tobacco smoke that causes lung cancer.
chunks.source: Tar is the sticky black substance in tobacco smoke that causes lung cancer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Which TWO are reasons why people drink alcohol? (Choose TWO.) A: To forget their worries, To enjoy themselves at parties. Some people drink to forget problems or to feel happy at celebrations, but alcohol harms the body.
chunks.source: Some people drink to forget problems or to feel happy at celebrations, but alcohol harms the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Match each effect of drinking alcohol to who is affected. A: An individual: Damages his or her liver and brain; A family: Family money is wasted and quarrels increase. Alcohol damages the drinker's body and also wastes family money and causes quarrels at home.
chunks.source: Alcohol damages the drinker's body and also wastes family money and causes quarrels at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO qualities of an essential drug. (Choose TWO.) A: It is effective against common diseases, It is affordable to most people. An essential drug must work well against common sicknesses and be affordable.
chunks.source: An essential drug must work well against common sicknesses and be affordable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO advantages of laboratory manufactured drugs over traditional drugs. (Choose TWO.) A: They have carefully measured doses, They are tested to be safe. Factory-made drugs have exact doses and are tested for safety, unlike many traditional drugs.
chunks.source: Factory-made drugs have exact doses and are tested for safety, unlike many traditional drugs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: What is the possible danger of buying drugs from local shops or markets? A: The drugs may be fake, expired or badly stored. Drugs from markets may be fake or expired and can poison you instead of curing you.
chunks.source: Drugs from markets may be fake or expired and can poison you instead of curing you.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Name the poisonous substance in tobacco smoke that causes addiction. A: Nicotine. Nicotine is the addictive poison in tobacco that makes smokers unable to stop.
chunks.source: Nicotine is the addictive poison in tobacco that makes smokers unable to stop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Which body organ is damaged when you drink a lot of alcohol? A: The liver. Too much alcohol damages the liver, the organ that cleans poisons from blood.
chunks.source: Too much alcohol damages the liver, the organ that cleans poisons from blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: What is the danger of taking drugs which are not prescribed by a health worker? A: They can poison the body or fail to cure the sickness. Unprescribed drugs may be the wrong drug or wrong dose, which can poison you.
chunks.source: Unprescribed drugs may be the wrong drug or wrong dose, which can poison you.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO ways alcohol is used in hospitals. (Choose TWO.) A: To disinfect skin and equipment, To preserve specimens in the laboratory. Hospitals use alcohol to kill germs on skin and tools, and to preserve laboratory specimens.
chunks.source: Hospitals use alcohol to kill germs on skin and tools, and to preserve laboratory specimens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: State TWO effects of alcohol to a community. (Choose TWO.) A: More accidents and crimes, Broken families and poverty. Alcohol leads to accidents, crime, wasted money and broken families in a community.
chunks.source: Alcohol leads to accidents, crime, wasted money and broken families in a community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Apart from taking a wrong dose, give one other way in which drugs are misused. A: Sharing drugs prescribed for one person with another person. Drugs prescribed for one person may be wrong or dangerous for another person.
chunks.source: Drugs prescribed for one person may be wrong or dangerous for another person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Name TWO poisonous substances found in tobacco. (Choose TWO.) A: Nicotine, Tar. Tobacco contains nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide, all of which are poisonous.
chunks.source: Tobacco contains nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide, all of which are poisonous.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO effects of cigarette smoking by pregnant women to their unborn babies. (Choose TWO.) A: Babies are born with low weight, Babies may be born too early or die before birth. Smoking in pregnancy harms the unborn baby, causing low birth weight or early birth.
chunks.source: Smoking in pregnancy harms the unborn baby, causing low birth weight or early birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO ways in which drug dependence can affect an individual. (Choose TWO.) A: Wastes a lot of money, Damages health and leads to crime. A drug-dependent person wastes money on drugs and may steal or fall sick.
chunks.source: A drug-dependent person wastes money on drugs and may steal or fall sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: State TWO ways in which an individual can avoid drug dependence. (Choose TWO.) A: Never start taking drugs, Avoid bad company that pressures you to take drugs. The best protection is never starting and keeping away from people who use drugs.
chunks.source: The best protection is never starting and keeping away from people who use drugs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why doctors prescribe drugs for patients. A: So that patients get the right drug and the right dose for their sickness. A prescription makes sure the patient takes the correct drug in the correct amount.
chunks.source: A prescription makes sure the patient takes the correct drug in the correct amount.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Name one gas contained in tobacco smoke. A: Carbon monoxide. Tobacco smoke contains the poisonous gas carbon monoxide.
chunks.source: Tobacco smoke contains the poisonous gas carbon monoxide.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of preparing alcohol and match each part to its correct answer. A: The method used in the diagram: Distillation; The arrows labelled J: Heat; Why the tube passes through cold water: To cool the alcohol vapour back into liquid; The process that forms M (the rising vapour): Evaporation. The diagram shows distillation: heat evaporates alcohol, and the cold-water tube condenses the vapour back to liquid.
chunks.source: The diagram shows distillation: heat evaporates alcohol, and the cold-water tube condenses the vapour back to liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why drugs should be kept away from children. A: Children may swallow them and get poisoned. Children do not know drugs are dangerous and may swallow them.
chunks.source: Children do not know drugs are dangerous and may swallow them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Write one bad behaviour which is a result of drug abuse. A: Stealing money to buy drugs. Drug abusers may steal, fight or become rude when they crave drugs.
chunks.source: Drug abusers may steal, fight or become rude when they crave drugs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Give the meaning of each of the following. A: Active smoking: Smoking a cigarette yourself; Passive smoking: Breathing in smoke from other people's cigarettes. An active smoker smokes directly, while a passive smoker breathes in other people's smoke.
chunks.source: An active smoker smokes directly, while a passive smoker breathes in other people's smoke.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: What piece of advice can you give to smokers to help them stop the habit? A: Stay away from smokers and places where people smoke. Avoiding smokers and smoking places removes the temptation to smoke.
chunks.source: Avoiding smokers and smoking places removes the temptation to smoke.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Match each item about making alcohol to its correct answer. A: The process that turns sugar into alcohol: Fermentation; The fungus used in this process: Yeast. Yeast is the fungus that ferments sugar into alcohol.
chunks.source: Yeast is the fungus that ferments sugar into alcohol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Apart from making alcohol, state TWO other useful things fermentation does for human beings. (Choose TWO.) A: It makes bread dough rise when baking, It is used to make yoghurt. Fermentation by yeast also makes bread rise and helps make foods like yoghurt.
chunks.source: Fermentation by yeast also makes bread rise and helps make foods like yoghurt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Apart from the brain, give any other body organ which is greatly damaged by alcohol. A: The liver. Alcohol greatly damages the liver as well as the brain.
chunks.source: Alcohol greatly damages the liver as well as the brain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: If a person enters a room and begins smoking, how does that habit affect the health of the people in the room? A: They become passive smokers and their health is harmed. Smoke in a room forces others to breathe it in, making them passive smokers.
chunks.source: Smoke in a room forces others to breathe it in, making them passive smokers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why a patient should take a drug only when it is prescribed by a medical worker. A: To make sure it is the correct drug and dose for the sickness. Only a medical worker can choose the right drug and dose for your sickness.
chunks.source: Only a medical worker can choose the right drug and dose for your sickness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: How do some people become passive smokers? A: By breathing in smoke from other people's cigarettes. Anyone who breathes in another person's cigarette smoke is a passive smoker.
chunks.source: Anyone who breathes in another person's cigarette smoke is a passive smoker.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Apart from curing diseases, give one other characteristic of essential drugs. A: They are safe to use. Essential drugs must be safe as well as effective.
chunks.source: Essential drugs must be safe as well as effective.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: State one physical change that takes place during the process of distillation of alcohol. A: The alcohol vapour cools and changes back into liquid. In distillation, vapour condenses (changes from gas to liquid) in the cold tube.
chunks.source: In distillation, vapour condenses (changes from gas to liquid) in the cold tube.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Name one disease that affects the stomach because of alcoholism. A: Ulcers. Too much alcohol can cause ulcers (sores) in the stomach.
chunks.source: Too much alcohol can cause ulcers (sores) in the stomach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: State one disease that both a passive and an active smoker may suffer from. A: Lung cancer. Both active and passive smokers can get lung cancer from tobacco smoke.
chunks.source: Both active and passive smokers can get lung cancer from tobacco smoke.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Some diseases can be treated without drugs. Match each item to its answer. A: An example of such a disease: A broken bone (fracture); How to treat it: Keep it still with a splint or plaster; Why two patients should not share drugs: They may have different sicknesses needing different drugs. A fracture is treated with a splint, not drugs, and patients should never share prescribed drugs.
chunks.source: A fracture is treated with a splint, not drugs, and patients should never share prescribed drugs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: By what process is alcohol made from fruit juice? A: Fermentation. Yeast ferments the sugar in fruit juice to make alcohol.
chunks.source: Yeast ferments the sugar in fruit juice to make alcohol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Give any one life skill that children need to develop in order to safeguard themselves against drug dependence. A: The ability to say NO to drugs (assertiveness). Children who can firmly say no to drugs protect themselves from dependence.
chunks.source: Children who can firmly say no to drugs protect themselves from dependence.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Match each statement about keeping and misusing drugs to its correct answer. A: Why drugs should be kept away from moisture and sunlight: Moisture and sunlight spoil drugs; Why drugs should be kept out of reach of children: Children may swallow them and get poisoned; One way people in a family misuse drugs (1): Sharing one person's drugs with others; One way people in a family misuse drugs (2): Taking an overdose. Store drugs in a cool dry sealed place away from children, and never share drugs or take an overdose.
chunks.source: Store drugs in a cool dry sealed place away from children, and never share drugs or take an overdose.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO factors that may lead to alcoholism. (Choose TWO.) A: Peer pressure from friends, Stress and frustrations in life. Friends' pressure and life stress can push people into drinking too much alcohol.
chunks.source: Friends' pressure and life stress can push people into drinking too much alcohol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Absorption of alcohol takes place in the ____ of the alimentary canal. A: stomach. Alcohol is absorbed into blood mainly through the stomach wall (and small intestine).
chunks.source: Alcohol is absorbed into blood mainly through the stomach wall (and small intestine).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of alcohol that causes blindness when it comes into contact with the eyes. A: Methanol. Methanol is a poisonous alcohol that can cause blindness.
chunks.source: Methanol is a poisonous alcohol that can cause blindness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why people smoke. A: Because of peer pressure from friends. Many people start smoking because friends pressure them or to look cool.
chunks.source: Many people start smoking because friends pressure them or to look cool.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: What is drug prescription? A: Written instructions from a health worker on how to take a drug. A prescription is the health worker's written order saying which drug, how much and how often.
chunks.source: A prescription is the health worker's written order saying which drug, how much and how often.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Why should drugs be stored in a sealed container? A: To keep out moisture and air that spoil them. Air and moisture spoil drugs, so sealed containers keep them effective.
chunks.source: Air and moisture spoil drugs, so sealed containers keep them effective.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: What is drug abuse? A: Using drugs in a wrong and harmful way. Drug abuse is using drugs wrongly, for example to get high instead of to cure sickness.
chunks.source: Drug abuse is using drugs wrongly, for example to get high instead of to cure sickness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: How is drug abuse different from drug misuse? A: Abuse is using drugs for wrong purposes; misuse is using the right drug in the wrong way. Abuse means using drugs for the wrong purpose (like getting high); misuse means using the correct drug wrongly (like wrong dose).
chunks.source: Abuse means using drugs for the wrong purpose (like getting high); misuse means using the correct drug wrongly (like wrong dose).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Name any TWO commonly abused drugs. (Choose TWO.) A: Alcohol, Marijuana (cannabis). Alcohol and marijuana are among the drugs most commonly abused.
chunks.source: Alcohol and marijuana are among the drugs most commonly abused.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of keeping drugs in an open place. A: Children may reach them and get poisoned. Open drugs can be reached by children or spoiled by moisture.
chunks.source: Open drugs can be reached by children or spoiled by moisture.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: What is drug dependence? A: A condition where the body cannot do without a drug. A dependent person feels sick or uneasy without the drug and must keep taking it.
chunks.source: A dependent person feels sick or uneasy without the drug and must keep taking it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Give any one life skill that safeguards against alcoholism. A: Self-control. Self-control helps a person resist the urge to drink alcohol.
chunks.source: Self-control helps a person resist the urge to drink alcohol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: A patient was given a packet of drugs labelled 'Panadol 2x3'. Study the packet and match each question to its answer. A: What is this written information called: Dosage; Why is this information important to patients: It tells them how much drug to take and how often; How many times a day should the patient take the drug: Three times a day; The patient took the drug in the morning; after how many hours should the next dose be taken: Eight hours. '2x3' means 2 tablets, 3 times a day, so doses are 8 hours apart (24 divided by 3).
chunks.source: '2x3' means 2 tablets, 3 times a day, so doses are 8 hours apart (24 divided by 3).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Alcohol, smoking and drugs in society
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the steps in the distillation of alcohol in the correct order. A: Heat the fermented mixture, Alcohol vapour rises, Vapour cools in the cold-water tube, Liquid alcohol collects. Distillation: heating makes alcohol evaporate, the vapour cools in the cold tube and condenses back to liquid.
chunks.source: Distillation: heating makes alcohol evaporate, the vapour cools in the cold tube and condenses back to liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is an accident? A: A sudden unexpected event that causes injury or damage. An accident happens suddenly without being planned and can injure people.
chunks.source: An accident happens suddenly without being planned and can injure people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A child was burnt by steam from a saucepan. Match each item to its answer. A: The kind of injury the child got: A scald; The first aid to give the child: Pour cold water on the burnt part. Steam causes scalds, and cold water cools a scald.
chunks.source: Steam causes scalds, and cold water cools a scald.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO possible ways by which such scalding accidents can be avoided. (Choose TWO.) A: Turn saucepan handles away from the edge of the stove, Keep children away from cooking fires. Turning handles in and keeping children from fires prevents scalds.
chunks.source: Turning handles in and keeping children from fires prevents scalds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What first aid would you give to a person who has got a compound fracture on his arm? A: Keep the arm still with a splint and rush the person to hospital. Never push the bone back; keep the limb still with a splint and rush to hospital.
chunks.source: Never push the bone back; keep the limb still with a splint and rush to hospital.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: John overstretched and tore a ligament on his ankle. Match each item to its answer. A: The kind of injury John got: A sprain; A possible sign of this injury: Swelling and pain at the ankle; The first aid for this injury: Rest the ankle, apply a cold compress and bandage it. A torn ligament is a sprain; rest it, cool it and bandage it.
chunks.source: A torn ligament is a sprain; rest it, cool it and bandage it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What first aid would you give to someone who has been bitten by a venomous snake? A: Keep the victim calm and still, and rush him or her to hospital. Keep the bitten part still, keep the victim calm, and rush to hospital for antivenom.
chunks.source: Keep the bitten part still, keep the victim calm, and rush to hospital for antivenom.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it not advisable to use water to put out fire caused by petrol? A: Petrol floats on water and the fire spreads. Petrol is lighter than water, so it floats and burning petrol spreads on water.
chunks.source: Petrol is lighter than water, so it floats and burning petrol spreads on water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each item about first aid to its correct answer. A: What first aid is: Immediate help given to an injured person before a doctor arrives; Why an 11-year-old boy should not pull a drowning adult from water: The adult may pull him under and both may drown. First aid is quick help before the doctor comes, but a small boy cannot safely rescue a drowning adult.
chunks.source: First aid is quick help before the doctor comes, but a small boy cannot safely rescue a drowning adult.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State TWO things the boy should do to save the drowning adult. (Choose TWO.) A: Shout loudly for help, Throw a rope or floating object to the adult. The boy should call for help and throw something that floats instead of entering the water.
chunks.source: The boy should call for help and throw something that floats instead of entering the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the first aid for high fever? A: Tepid sponging. Sponging the body with lukewarm (tepid) water cools a person with high fever.
chunks.source: Sponging the body with lukewarm (tepid) water cools a person with high fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is near drowning? A: When a person almost dies under water but is rescued alive. Near drowning means the victim was saved before dying under water.
chunks.source: Near drowning means the victim was saved before dying under water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the use of a first aid box? A: To keep first aid equipment for emergencies. A first aid box stores bandages, antiseptic and other things needed to help the injured.
chunks.source: A first aid box stores bandages, antiseptic and other things needed to help the injured.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List any TWO things found in a first aid box. (Choose TWO.) A: Bandages, Antiseptic. Bandages cover wounds and antiseptic kills germs on wounds.
chunks.source: Bandages cover wounds and antiseptic kills germs on wounds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State why every school should have a first aid box. A: So that injured pupils get quick first aid. Pupils get injured while playing, so quick first aid must be near.
chunks.source: Pupils get injured while playing, so quick first aid must be near.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a first aid box different from a first aid kit? A: A first aid box stays in one place while a first aid kit is carried around. A box is fixed (e.g., on a wall) while a kit is portable for journeys.
chunks.source: A box is fixed (e.g., on a wall) while a kit is portable for journeys.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How would you give first aid for nose bleeding? A: Let the person sit up, lean the head back slightly and pinch the soft part of the nose. Sitting up with head tilted back and pinching the nose helps the blood clot.
chunks.source: Sitting up with head tilted back and pinching the nose helps the blood clot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What causes fainting? A: Not enough blood reaching the brain. When the brain lacks blood and oxygen, a person faints.
chunks.source: When the brain lacks blood and oxygen, a person faints.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO conditions that can lead to fainting. (Choose TWO.) A: Anaemia (shortage of blood), Standing for long in hot sunshine. Anaemia and standing long in heat reduce blood reaching the brain.
chunks.source: Anaemia and standing long in heat reduce blood reaching the brain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are the legs of a person who has fainted raised higher than the head when giving first aid? A: So that blood flows back to the brain. Raising the legs lets blood flow down to the brain and the person recovers.
chunks.source: Raising the legs lets blood flow down to the brain and the person recovers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way the cause of a burn is similar to that of a scald. A: Both are caused by heat. Burns (dry heat) and scalds (wet heat) are both heat injuries.
chunks.source: Burns (dry heat) and scalds (wet heat) are both heat injuries.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A scald is caused by dry heat. True or False? A: False. A scald is caused by wet heat such as steam or hot water; dry heat causes a burn.
chunks.source: A scald is caused by wet heat such as steam or hot water; dry heat causes a burn.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should cold water be poured on the part of the body which has been scalded or burnt? A: To cool the skin and reduce pain and damage. Cold water removes heat from the burn, reducing pain and deeper damage.
chunks.source: Cold water removes heat from the burn, reducing pain and deeper damage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one activity that can help to reduce snake bites in homes. A: Clearing bushes around homes. Snakes hide in bushes, so clearing them keeps snakes away from homes.
chunks.source: Snakes hide in bushes, so clearing them keeps snakes away from homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason why people who get badly burnt are given plenty of fluids. A: They lose a lot of body fluids through the burnt skin. Bad burns make the body lose fluids, so drinking replaces them.
chunks.source: Bad burns make the body lose fluids, so drinking replaces them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one use of a tourniquet. A: To stop heavy bleeding from a limb. A tourniquet is tied above a bleeding wound to stop blood flow.
chunks.source: A tourniquet is tied above a bleeding wound to stop blood flow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the equipment and match each item to its answer. A: The name of the equipment: A fire extinguisher; Why it is painted in bright colours: So it can easily be seen in an emergency; Why such equipment is recommended in schools: To put out fire quickly and protect the many pupils; The gas contained in it: Carbon dioxide. The fire extinguisher holds carbon dioxide gas that puts out fire; its bright colour makes it easy to find.
chunks.source: The fire extinguisher holds carbon dioxide gas that puts out fire; its bright colour makes it easy to find.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a sling used when giving first aid to a person with a broken hand? A: To hold the broken bones still. A sling supports the broken hand so the bones do not move.
chunks.source: A sling supports the broken hand so the bones do not move.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it a bad practice to apply soil or cow dung on any burnt area of our skin? A: It causes infection of the wound. Soil and dung carry germs that infect burns.
chunks.source: Soil and dung carry germs that infect burns.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO reasons why the injured part with a burn or scald is dipped into cold water. (Choose TWO.) A: It cools the burnt skin, It reduces pain and swelling. Cold water takes heat out of the burn and eases pain and swelling.
chunks.source: Cold water takes heat out of the burn and eases pain and swelling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of avoiding burns while lifting hot objects. A: Use a dry cloth or pot holder. A dry cloth protects your hands from hot objects.
chunks.source: A dry cloth protects your hands from hot objects.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sarah fell off a bicycle and broke her leg. Match each item to its answer. A: The injury Sarah got: A fracture; First aid for Sarah (1): Keep the leg still with a splint; First aid for Sarah (2): Rush her to hospital; The importance of giving her first aid: It stops the injury from getting worse. A broken leg (fracture) must be kept still with a splint and the victim rushed to hospital.
chunks.source: A broken leg (fracture) must be kept still with a splint and the victim rushed to hospital.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO main causes of motor accidents in Uganda. (Choose TWO.) A: Over speeding, Drunk driving. Speeding and drunk driving are leading causes of road accidents.
chunks.source: Speeding and drunk driving are leading causes of road accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO ways in which petrol fire can be put out. (Choose TWO.) A: Smother it with a heavy blanket, Use a fire extinguisher or sand. Petrol fire is put out by cutting off air with a blanket, sand or a fire extinguisher.
chunks.source: Petrol fire is put out by cutting off air with a blanket, sand or a fire extinguisher.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a burn different from a scald? A: A burn is caused by dry heat while a scald is caused by wet heat. Dry heat (fire, hot metal) causes burns; wet heat (steam, hot water) causes scalds.
chunks.source: Dry heat (fire, hot metal) causes burns; wet heat (steam, hot water) causes scalds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a splint necessary when giving first aid to someone with a broken limb? A: To keep the broken bones still. A splint stops the broken bones from moving and causing more damage.
chunks.source: A splint stops the broken bones from moving and causing more damage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What first aid would you give to a child who has drunk paraffin? A: Give plenty of fluids and rush the child to hospital without making him vomit. Give fluids to dilute the paraffin and rush to hospital; never make the child vomit.
chunks.source: Give fluids to dilute the paraffin and rush to hospital; never make the child vomit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important to feel the pulse (heart beat) of a seriously injured victim of an accident? A: To check whether the heart is still beating. Feeling the pulse tells whether the victim is alive and the heart works.
chunks.source: Feeling the pulse tells whether the victim is alive and the heart works.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it dangerous to cause a victim who has swallowed paraffin to vomit it? A: The vomit can enter the lungs and damage them. Bringing paraffin back up can let it enter the lungs and cause serious damage.
chunks.source: Bringing paraffin back up can let it enter the lungs and cause serious damage.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is near drowning different from drowning? A: In near drowning the victim is rescued alive, while in drowning the victim dies. Near drowning ends with rescue; drowning ends with death.
chunks.source: Near drowning ends with rescue; drowning ends with death.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is tepid sponging an important first aid to a person with high fever? A: It cools the body. Lukewarm sponging takes heat away from the body and lowers the fever.
chunks.source: Lukewarm sponging takes heat away from the body and lowers the fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What kind of accident requires the use of splints in giving first aid? A: Fractures (broken bones). Splints keep broken bones still, so they are used for fractures.
chunks.source: Splints keep broken bones still, so they are used for fractures.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a safety pin in a first aid kit important? A: It fastens bandages. A safety pin holds bandages in place on a wound.
chunks.source: A safety pin holds bandages in place on a wound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the injured person. How is structure M useful to the injured person? A: It is a sling that supports the broken arm and keeps it still. The sling (M) holds the injured arm still so the break is not worsened.
chunks.source: The sling (M) holds the injured arm still so the break is not worsened.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the injury that results from tearing of muscles. A: A strain. Torn muscles cause a strain; torn ligaments cause a sprain.
chunks.source: Torn muscles cause a strain; torn ligaments cause a sprain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one type of accident whose first aid is to put the injured part of the body in cold water. A: Burns and scalds. Cold water is the first aid for heat injuries like burns and scalds.
chunks.source: Cold water is the first aid for heat injuries like burns and scalds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the fracture. What type of fracture is shown? A: A simple fracture. The bone is broken but the skin is not pierced, so it is a simple (closed) fracture.
chunks.source: The bone is broken but the skin is not pierced, so it is a simple (closed) fracture.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one sign of a compound fracture. A: The broken bone pierces through the skin. In a compound fracture the broken bone sticks out through the skin.
chunks.source: In a compound fracture the broken bone sticks out through the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why would you give plenty of water to a person who has taken rat poison? A: To dilute the poison in the body. Water dilutes (weakens) the poison while rushing the victim to hospital.
chunks.source: Water dilutes (weakens) the poison while rushing the victim to hospital.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does mouth-to-mouth breathing help a victim of near drowning? A: It gives the victim air and restores breathing. Blowing air into the victim's mouth supplies oxygen and restarts breathing.
chunks.source: Blowing air into the victim's mouth supplies oxygen and restarts breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any TWO causes of nose bleeding. (Choose TWO.) A: Picking the nose, A blow to the nose. Picking and blows injure the soft blood vessels inside the nose.
chunks.source: Picking and blows injure the soft blood vessels inside the nose.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each piece of advice for nose bleeding to its reason. A: Lean back the head: So that blood does not flow out of the nose; Pinch the soft part of the nose: To press the vessels and stop the bleeding. Leaning back keeps blood in while pinching presses the bleeding vessels shut.
chunks.source: Leaning back keeps blood in while pinching presses the bleeding vessels shut.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does cooking from a raised place help to prevent burns and scalds in a home? A: Small children cannot reach the hot food and fire. Raised stoves keep hot pots away from small children.
chunks.source: Raised stoves keep hot pots away from small children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The condition when the body temperature goes beyond the normal is called ____. A: fever. A body temperature above normal is called fever.
chunks.source: A body temperature above normal is called fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the importance of yelling for help when a person is near drowning? A: To attract people who can rescue the victim. Yelling brings rescuers who can save the drowning person.
chunks.source: Yelling brings rescuers who can save the drowning person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What first aid is given to a person with dust in the eyes? A: Wash the eyes with clean water and do not rub them. Clean water washes dust out; rubbing scratches the eyes.
chunks.source: Clean water washes dust out; rubbing scratches the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a razor blade important in giving first aid? A: It is used to cut bandages and plasters. A razor blade cuts bandages, plasters and tape to size.
chunks.source: A razor blade cuts bandages, plasters and tape to size.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of a life jacket when travelling in a boat. A: It keeps a person floating on water. A life jacket keeps you afloat if the boat capsizes.
chunks.source: A life jacket keeps you afloat if the boat capsizes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a life jacket made out of bright colours? A: So the wearer can easily be seen in water. Bright colours help rescuers spot a person in water quickly.
chunks.source: Bright colours help rescuers spot a person in water quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How important is a stretcher in giving first aid to a person with broken legs? A: It carries the victim without moving the broken bones. A stretcher moves the victim while keeping broken legs still.
chunks.source: A stretcher moves the victim while keeping broken legs still.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a strain different from a sprain? A: A strain is a torn muscle while a sprain is a torn ligament. Muscles tear in a strain; ligaments tear in a sprain.
chunks.source: Muscles tear in a strain; ligaments tear in a sprain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does anaemia lead to fainting in anaemic patients? A: Less blood and oxygen reach the brain. Anaemia means little blood, so the brain gets too little oxygen and the person faints.
chunks.source: Anaemia means little blood, so the brain gets too little oxygen and the person faints.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does keeping drugs out of reach of children help to prevent poisoning at home? A: Children cannot reach and swallow the drugs. If children cannot reach drugs, they cannot swallow and be poisoned by them.
chunks.source: If children cannot reach drugs, they cannot swallow and be poisoned by them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram demonstrates a first aid for fainting. Match each item to its answer. A: The accident that needs this first aid: Fainting; The main cause of this accident: Not enough blood reaching the brain. Raising the legs higher than the head sends blood back to the brain of a fainted person.
chunks.source: Raising the legs higher than the head sends blood back to the brain of a fainted person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is respiration? A: The release of energy from food in the body. Respiration is the chemical process in body cells that releases energy from food.
chunks.source: Respiration is the chemical process in body cells that releases energy from food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which structures enable the trachea to remain open all the time? A: Rings of cartilage. C-shaped rings of cartilage hold the trachea open so air passes freely.
chunks.source: C-shaped rings of cartilage hold the trachea open so air passes freely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Respiration takes place in the lungs. True or False? A: False. Respiration takes place in the cells of the body; the lungs only handle gaseous exchange.
chunks.source: Respiration takes place in the cells of the body; the lungs only handle gaseous exchange.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of the energy made during respiration to the body. A: It is used for body activities like movement and growth. Energy from respiration powers movement, warmth, growth and all body activities.
chunks.source: Energy from respiration powers movement, warmth, growth and all body activities.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from skin, name any one other respiratory organ. A: The lungs. The lungs are the main respiratory organs; the skin also helps in breathing.
chunks.source: The lungs are the main respiratory organs; the skin also helps in breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one difference between respiration and breathing. A: Respiration releases energy from food while breathing is moving air in and out. Breathing moves air in and out; respiration is the chemical release of energy in cells.
chunks.source: Breathing moves air in and out; respiration is the chemical release of energy in cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which property of air makes lungs expand when we breathe in? A: Air exerts pressure. Air pressure pushes into the lungs and makes them expand when we breathe in.
chunks.source: Air pressure pushes into the lungs and makes them expand when we breathe in.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of red blood cells during respiration. A: They carry oxygen to body cells. Red blood cells transport oxygen from the lungs to all body cells for respiration.
chunks.source: Red blood cells transport oxygen from the lungs to all body cells for respiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one gaseous waste transported by blood. A: Carbon dioxide. Blood carries the waste gas carbon dioxide from cells to the lungs.
chunks.source: Blood carries the waste gas carbon dioxide from cells to the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The end products of respiration are energy, carbon dioxide and ____. A: water. Respiration releases energy and produces carbon dioxide and water.
chunks.source: Respiration releases energy and produces carbon dioxide and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does the heart of a person who is running beat faster than normal? A: To supply more oxygen and food to the working muscles. Running muscles need more energy, so the heart pumps faster to deliver oxygen.
chunks.source: Running muscles need more energy, so the heart pumps faster to deliver oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of cilia in the nose. A: They trap dust and germs from inhaled air. Tiny hair-like cilia in the nose trap dust and germs before air reaches the lungs.
chunks.source: Tiny hair-like cilia in the nose trap dust and germs before air reaches the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What takes place in the lungs when one breathes in and out? A: Gaseous exchange. In the lungs, oxygen enters blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.
chunks.source: In the lungs, oxygen enters blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it more difficult to breathe in a room full of smoke than in the open compound? A: Smoke pollutes the air and irritates the breathing organs. Smoke-filled air has less clean oxygen and irritates the nose and lungs.
chunks.source: Smoke-filled air has less clean oxygen and irritates the nose and lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How important are rings of cartilage that make up the trachea? A: They keep the trachea open so air passes freely. Cartilage rings stop the trachea from collapsing when we breathe.
chunks.source: Cartilage rings stop the trachea from collapsing when we breathe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of the diaphragm during breathing out. A: It relaxes and moves up, pushing air out of the lungs. When breathing out, the diaphragm relaxes and domes upward, forcing air out.
chunks.source: When breathing out, the diaphragm relaxes and domes upward, forcing air out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How important is the rib cage during breathing in? A: It moves up and out to create space for the lungs to expand. The ribs move up and out so the chest expands and air rushes in.
chunks.source: The ribs move up and out so the chest expands and air rushes in.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one component of air breathed out. A: Carbon dioxide. Breathed-out air contains more carbon dioxide and water vapour.
chunks.source: Breathed-out air contains more carbon dioxide and water vapour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the body get the oxygen it uses for respiration? A: By breathing in air through the respiratory organs. We breathe in air, and oxygen passes from the lungs into blood.
chunks.source: We breathe in air, and oxygen passes from the lungs into blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match what happens to the rib cage during breathing. A: During breathing in: The rib cage moves up and out; During breathing out: The rib cage moves down and in. Breathing in expands the chest (ribs up and out); breathing out shrinks it (ribs down and in).
chunks.source: Breathing in expands the chest (ribs up and out); breathing out shrinks it (ribs down and in).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way in which smoking affects the human respiratory system. A: It damages the lungs and air passages. Tobacco smoke damages the lungs and can cause lung cancer and breathing diseases.
chunks.source: Tobacco smoke damages the lungs and can cause lung cancer and breathing diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Gaseous exchange takes place in the ____ in the body. A: air sacs. Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged in the tiny air sacs (alveoli) of the lungs.
chunks.source: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged in the tiny air sacs (alveoli) of the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match what happens to the diaphragm during breathing. A: During breathing in: The diaphragm contracts and moves down; During breathing out: The diaphragm relaxes and moves up. Breathing in: diaphragm contracts flat and down. Breathing out: it relaxes and domes up.
chunks.source: Breathing in: diaphragm contracts flat and down. Breathing out: it relaxes and domes up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How important is oxygen during respiration? A: It is used to release energy from food. Oxygen burns food in cells to release energy during respiration.
chunks.source: Oxygen burns food in cells to release energy during respiration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one example of a non-communicable disease of the lungs. A: Lung cancer. Lung cancer cannot spread from person to person, unlike TB or pneumonia.
chunks.source: Lung cancer cannot spread from person to person, unlike TB or pneumonia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one characteristic that makes air sacs carry out gaseous exchange. A: They have thin walls and a rich supply of blood capillaries. Thin walls and many capillaries let gases pass quickly in the air sacs.
chunks.source: Thin walls and many capillaries let gases pass quickly in the air sacs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: By what process does air move in and out of the air sacs? A: Diffusion. Gases move in and out of air sacs by diffusion, from high to low concentration.
chunks.source: Gases move in and out of air sacs by diffusion, from high to low concentration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the model experiment and match each part to what it represents. A: The system shown: The respiratory system; The balloon: The lungs; The thin rubber sheet: The diaphragm; When air fills the balloon, the rubber sheet: Moves down. The model shows breathing: the balloon is the lung and the rubber sheet is the diaphragm.
chunks.source: The model shows breathing: the balloon is the lung and the rubber sheet is the diaphragm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are lungs grouped under the respiratory system? A: Because gaseous exchange takes place in them. The lungs are where oxygen enters blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.
chunks.source: The lungs are where oxygen enters blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the function of the epiglottis in the respiratory system. A: It prevents food from entering the trachea. The epiglottis closes the windpipe when we swallow so food goes to the stomach.
chunks.source: The epiglottis closes the windpipe when we swallow so food goes to the stomach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of breathing to the body. A: It supplies oxygen needed for respiration. Breathing brings in oxygen that cells need to release energy.
chunks.source: Breathing brings in oxygen that cells need to release energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is blood important during respiration? A: It transports oxygen to cells and carbon dioxide away. Blood carries oxygen to cells and takes away carbon dioxide.
chunks.source: Blood carries oxygen to cells and takes away carbon dioxide.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from energy and carbon dioxide, ____ is a bi-product of respiration. A: water. Respiration produces energy, carbon dioxide and water.
chunks.source: Respiration produces energy, carbon dioxide and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do the lungs expand during breathing in? A: Air pressure from inhaled air pushes them open. Incoming air exerts pressure that expands the lungs.
chunks.source: Incoming air exerts pressure that expands the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State what happens to the pressure in the chest cavity during breathing in. A: It decreases (becomes lower). The expanding chest lowers air pressure inside, so outside air rushes in.
chunks.source: The expanding chest lowers air pressure inside, so outside air rushes in.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of blood capillaries in the body. A: They allow exchange of materials between blood and body cells. Thin-walled capillaries let oxygen, food and wastes pass between blood and cells.
chunks.source: Thin-walled capillaries let oxygen, food and wastes pass between blood and cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why human beings breathe in. A: To take in oxygen needed for respiration. We breathe in to get oxygen for releasing energy from food.
chunks.source: We breathe in to get oxygen for releasing energy from food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one good health habit that can improve the working of the lungs. A: Doing regular physical exercise. Exercise strengthens the lungs and improves breathing.
chunks.source: Exercise strengthens the lungs and improves breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the trachea prevent foreign bodies from reaching the lungs? A: Cilia and mucus trap dust and germs. Mucus traps dirt and cilia sweep it away from the lungs.
chunks.source: Mucus traps dirt and cilia sweep it away from the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is air we breathe in different from air we breathe out? A: Breathed-out air has less oxygen and more carbon dioxide. The body uses up oxygen and adds carbon dioxide, so exhaled air differs.
chunks.source: The body uses up oxygen and adds carbon dioxide, so exhaled air differs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is friction reduced between the lungs and the ribs? A: By the smooth pleural membranes with fluid between them. The pleural membranes with slippery fluid let the lungs slide without friction.
chunks.source: The pleural membranes with slippery fluid let the lungs slide without friction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the respiratory system and match each item to its answer. A: Part marked B: The bronchi; The function of part marked E (a lung): Gaseous exchange takes place in it; Where letter P (the heart) should be marked: Between the lungs, slightly to the left. B is a bronchus carrying air into the lung; the lungs (E) exchange gases; the heart lies between the lungs.
chunks.source: B is a bronchus carrying air into the lung; the lungs (E) exchange gases; the heart lies between the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why a person breathes a lot after an exercise. A: To supply extra oxygen to release more energy and remove carbon dioxide. Exercise uses extra energy, so the body breathes faster to get more oxygen.
chunks.source: Exercise uses extra energy, so the body breathes faster to get more oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does air breathed out contain less oxygen than air breathed in? A: The body uses up oxygen during respiration. Cells use oxygen to release energy, so exhaled air has less of it.
chunks.source: Cells use oxygen to release energy, so exhaled air has less of it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO diseases which affect the respiratory organs in humans. (Choose TWO.) A: Tuberculosis, Pneumonia. TB and pneumonia attack the lungs and air passages.
chunks.source: TB and pneumonia attack the lungs and air passages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one practice by humans which may lead to a respiratory disease. A: Smoking cigarettes. Smoking damages the lungs and causes respiratory diseases.
chunks.source: Smoking damages the lungs and causes respiratory diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A P.6 class used the lung model in an experiment. Match each item to its answer. A: What the experiment is about: How the lungs work during breathing; What happens to the balloon when air moves out: It shrinks (deflates). The model shows breathing: pulling the sheet down fills the balloon; pushing it up empties it.
chunks.source: The model shows breathing: pulling the sheet down fills the balloon; pushing it up empties it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one infectious disease of the lungs. A: Tuberculosis. Tuberculosis (TB) spreads from person to person and attacks the lungs.
chunks.source: Tuberculosis (TB) spreads from person to person and attacks the lungs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one disorder of the respiratory system. A: Asthma. Asthma is a disorder where air passages narrow and breathing becomes hard.
chunks.source: Asthma is a disorder where air passages narrow and breathing becomes hard.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can one maintain the proper working of the respiratory system? A: By avoiding smoking and doing regular exercise. Clean air, no smoking and exercise keep the respiratory system healthy.
chunks.source: Clean air, no smoking and exercise keep the respiratory system healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one viral disease of the lungs. A: Influenza (flu). Flu is caused by a virus and attacks the respiratory system.
chunks.source: Flu is caused by a virus and attacks the respiratory system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why it is not advisable to breathe through the mouth. A: The mouth does not warm, clean or moisten air like the nose does. The nose filters, warms and moistens air; the mouth does not.
chunks.source: The nose filters, warms and moistens air; the mouth does not.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Put each respiratory disease under Infectious or Non-communicable. A: Infectious: Tuberculosis,Pneumonia,Influenza; Non-communicable: Lung cancer,Asthma. Infectious diseases spread between people; non-communicable ones like cancer and asthma do not.
chunks.source: Infectious diseases spread between people; non-communicable ones like cancer and asthma do not.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Arrange the events of breathing in (inhalation) in the correct order. A: The diaphragm contracts and moves down, The rib cage moves up and out, Air pressure in the chest falls, Air rushes into the lungs. Breathing in: diaphragm flattens, ribs lift, chest pressure drops and air flows in.
chunks.source: Breathing in: diaphragm flattens, ribs lift, chest pressure drops and air flows in.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which breed of cattle is obtained by mating a pure local breed and an exotic breed? A: A cross breed. Mating local and exotic breeds produces a cross breed with qualities of both.
chunks.source: Mating local and exotic breeds produces a cross breed with qualities of both.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO reasons why farmers keep cattle. (Choose TWO.) A: To get milk, To get meat. Cattle give milk and meat, and also income, hides and labour.
chunks.source: Cattle give milk and meat, and also income, hides and labour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of colostrum to a calf. A: It protects the calf against diseases. Colostrum, the first milk, gives the newborn calf protection against diseases.
chunks.source: Colostrum, the first milk, gives the newborn calf protection against diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does paddock grazing help to control ticks in cattle? A: Moving cattle to fresh paddocks leaves ticks behind to die without hosts. Rotating cattle between paddocks breaks the tick life cycle because ticks starve without hosts.
chunks.source: Rotating cattle between paddocks breaks the tick life cycle because ticks starve without hosts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO reasons why some farmers prefer keeping local breeds of cattle to exotic breeds. (Choose TWO.) A: They resist local diseases, They need less care and feed. Local breeds survive on poor feed and resist local diseases better than exotic breeds.
chunks.source: Local breeds survive on poor feed and resist local diseases better than exotic breeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one characteristic of dairy cattle. A: They produce a lot of milk. Dairy cattle are kept mainly for high milk production.
chunks.source: Dairy cattle are kept mainly for high milk production.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a type of cattle? A: A group of cattle kept for the same purpose. Cattle are grouped into types by purpose, e.g., dairy, beef and dual purpose.
chunks.source: Cattle are grouped into types by purpose, e.g., dairy, beef and dual purpose.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name TWO types of cattle kept in Uganda. (Choose TWO.) A: Dairy cattle, Beef cattle. Uganda's cattle include dairy types for milk and beef types for meat.
chunks.source: Uganda's cattle include dairy types for milk and beef types for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of controlling in-breeding in cattle. A: Use a different bull from another farm (avoid mating related animals). Bringing in an unrelated bull prevents mating of related animals.
chunks.source: Bringing in an unrelated bull prevents mating of related animals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from ticks, name any one other cattle pest. A: Tsetse flies. Tsetse flies bite cattle and spread nagana.
chunks.source: Tsetse flies bite cattle and spread nagana.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO diseases spread by ticks to cattle. (Choose TWO.) A: East Coast fever, Redwater. Ticks spread East Coast fever and redwater (babesiosis) among cattle.
chunks.source: Ticks spread East Coast fever and redwater (babesiosis) among cattle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which tick-borne diseases can be controlled. A: Dipping or spraying cattle with acaricides. Killing ticks by dipping or spraying stops tick-borne diseases.
chunks.source: Killing ticks by dipping or spraying stops tick-borne diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the grazing system and match each item to its answer. A: The system of grazing shown: Paddock grazing; An advantage of this system (1): Pasture gets time to regrow; An advantage of this system (2): It helps control ticks and diseases; A disadvantage of this system: It is expensive to fence the paddocks. The fenced sections show paddock grazing: pasture rests, diseases are controlled, but fencing is costly.
chunks.source: The fenced sections show paddock grazing: pasture rests, diseases are controlled, but fencing is costly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one advantage of exotic breeds of cattle over local ones. A: They produce more milk and grow faster. Exotic breeds give much more milk and meat than local breeds.
chunks.source: Exotic breeds give much more milk and meat than local breeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is free range system of grazing cattle not suitable for farmers in towns? A: There is not enough land in towns. Free range needs large open land, which towns lack.
chunks.source: Free range needs large open land, which towns lack.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from feeding, give any TWO ways a farmer can care for his or her cattle. (Choose TWO.) A: Provide clean water, Treat them when sick. Good care includes clean water, treatment, clean shelter and parasite control.
chunks.source: Good care includes clean water, treatment, clean shelter and parasite control.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The type of cattle kept for milk production is called ____ cattle. A: dairy. Dairy cattle are kept mainly to produce milk.
chunks.source: Dairy cattle are kept mainly to produce milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of an exotic breed of cattle which is best for milk production. A: Friesian. The Friesian is a leading exotic dairy breed with very high milk yield.
chunks.source: The Friesian is a leading exotic dairy breed with very high milk yield.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down TWO activities a farmer should do in order to get clean milk from a cow. (Choose TWO.) A: Wash the udder before milking, Use clean milking containers. Clean udders and clean containers keep milk free from germs.
chunks.source: Clean udders and clean containers keep milk free from germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way tsetse flies are dangerous to cattle. A: They spread nagana to cattle. Tsetse fly bites spread nagana, which kills cattle.
chunks.source: Tsetse fly bites spread nagana, which kills cattle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one method of milking cows. A: Hand milking. Cows can be milked by hand or by a milking machine.
chunks.source: Cows can be milked by hand or by a milking machine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO milk products. (Choose TWO.) A: Butter, Cheese. Milk is processed into butter, cheese, yoghurt and ghee.
chunks.source: Milk is processed into butter, cheese, yoghurt and ghee.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the meaning of each word as used in cattle rearing. A: Insemination: Putting semen into the cow to make it pregnant; Cross-breeding: Mating animals of different breeds; Castration: Removing the testicles of a male animal; Heat period: The time when a female animal is ready for mating. These are key breeding terms: insemination, crossing breeds, castration and heat.
chunks.source: These are key breeding terms: insemination, crossing breeds, castration and heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO signs of heat in cows. (Choose TWO.) A: The cow is restless and bellows, The cow mounts other cows. A cow on heat is restless, bellows and mounts others.
chunks.source: A cow on heat is restless, bellows and mounts others.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State TWO advantages of artificial insemination. (Choose TWO.) A: One bull's semen can serve many cows, It controls the spread of breeding diseases. Artificial insemination spreads good genes widely and avoids disease from natural mating.
chunks.source: Artificial insemination spreads good genes widely and avoids disease from natural mating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does isolation of infected animals help to control diseases in cattle? A: It stops the disease from spreading to healthy animals. Separating sick animals keeps germs from reaching healthy ones.
chunks.source: Separating sick animals keeps germs from reaching healthy ones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one internal (endo) parasite in cattle. A: Tapeworms. Tapeworms, roundworms and liver flukes live inside cattle.
chunks.source: Tapeworms, roundworms and liver flukes live inside cattle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Semen used in artificial insemination is stored in liquid ____. A: nitrogen. Liquid nitrogen keeps semen frozen and alive until use.
chunks.source: Liquid nitrogen keeps semen frozen and alive until use.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the equipment used by farmers to inseminate their cows. A: An insemination gun (syringe). A special syringe-like gun places semen into the cow.
chunks.source: A special syringe-like gun places semen into the cow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one sign you would see on cattle suffering from each disease. A: Anthrax: Sudden death with blood from body openings; East Coast fever: Swollen lymph nodes; Nagana: Loss of weight and weakness; Foot and mouth disease: Blisters in the mouth and on the feet. Each cattle disease shows its own signs: anthrax kills suddenly, East Coast fever swells glands, nagana wastes, foot-and-mouth blisters.
chunks.source: Each cattle disease shows its own signs: anthrax kills suddenly, East Coast fever swells glands, nagana wastes, foot-and-mouth blisters.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of the equipment shown (a Burdizzo) on a cattle farm. A: It is used for castrating animals. The Burdizzo crushes the sperm tubes to castrate male animals without a wound.
chunks.source: The Burdizzo crushes the sperm tubes to castrate male animals without a wound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do you understand by 'dual purpose' cattle? A: Cattle kept for both milk and beef. Dual purpose breeds like the Sahiwal give both milk and meat.
chunks.source: Dual purpose breeds like the Sahiwal give both milk and meat.

chunks.subject: Science
