chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO local breeds of cattle kept in Uganda. (Choose TWO.) A: Ankole, Zebu (Nganda). Ankole and Zebu/Nganda are Uganda's well-known local breeds.
chunks.source: Ankole and Zebu/Nganda are Uganda's well-known local breeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why cattle keepers practise cross-breeding. A: To get animals with good qualities of both breeds. Cross-breeding combines, for example, high milk yield with disease resistance.
chunks.source: Cross-breeding combines, for example, high milk yield with disease resistance.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can foot and mouth disease be controlled in cattle? A: By vaccinating cattle and restricting movement of animals. Vaccination and quarantine stop foot-and-mouth outbreaks.
chunks.source: Vaccination and quarantine stop foot-and-mouth outbreaks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the use of a drenching gun to a cattle farmer. A: It is used to give liquid medicine (dewormers) to animals. A drenching gun forces liquid deworming medicine down the animal's throat.
chunks.source: A drenching gun forces liquid deworming medicine down the animal's throat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one reason why farmers castrate their animals. A: To control breeding and make males calm and fatten faster. Castrated males are calm, fatten well and cannot breed anyhow.
chunks.source: Castrated males are calm, fatten well and cannot breed anyhow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The product from cattle used in the leather industry is ____. A: hides. Cattle hides (skins) are processed into leather.
chunks.source: Cattle hides (skins) are processed into leather.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the cattle disease whose sign is abortion. A: Brucellosis. Brucellosis causes cows to abort (lose pregnancies).
chunks.source: Brucellosis causes cows to abort (lose pregnancies).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from pasteurizing, give any other way milk can be prevented from going bad. A: Boiling it. Boiling kills germs in milk so it stays fresh longer.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs in milk so it stays fresh longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the importance of dipping cattle? A: It kills ticks and other external parasites. Dipping in acaricide kills ticks that spread diseases.
chunks.source: Dipping in acaricide kills ticks that spread diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one difference between dosing and drenching. A: Dosing is giving solid medicine while drenching is giving liquid medicine. Dosing uses solid drugs (bolus); drenching uses liquid drugs.
chunks.source: Dosing uses solid drugs (bolus); drenching uses liquid drugs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a farmer make use of cow dung produced by his animals? A: Use it as manure or fuel (biogas). Cow dung makes good manure and can produce biogas fuel.
chunks.source: Cow dung makes good manure and can produce biogas fuel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of controlling nagana in cattle. A: Control tsetse flies by spraying or trapping. Killing tsetse flies stops the spread of nagana.
chunks.source: Killing tsetse flies stops the spread of nagana.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is steaming up? A: Feeding a pregnant cow extra well before calving. Steaming up means giving a cow extra feed shortly before it gives birth.
chunks.source: Steaming up means giving a cow extra feed shortly before it gives birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one advantage of steaming up in cattle. A: The cow produces more milk after calving. A well-fed cow before calving gives more milk and a healthy calf.
chunks.source: A well-fed cow before calving gives more milk and a healthy calf.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which cattle disease is best controlled by burying the carcass of a sick animal? A: Anthrax. Anthrax germs survive in carcasses, so burying stops their spread.
chunks.source: Anthrax germs survive in carcasses, so burying stops their spread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one method of rearing cattle used in towns. A: Zero grazing. Zero grazing (stall feeding) suits towns where land is scarce.
chunks.source: Zero grazing (stall feeding) suits towns where land is scarce.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why farmers prefer keeping cross breed cattle other than the exotic ones. A: Cross breeds resist diseases better than exotic breeds. Cross breeds combine exotic milk yield with local hardiness.
chunks.source: Cross breeds combine exotic milk yield with local hardiness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO methods used in deworming animals. (Choose TWO.) A: Drenching with liquid dewormer, Dosing with solid deworming tablets. Dewormers are given as liquid (drenching) or solids (dosing).
chunks.source: Dewormers are given as liquid (drenching) or solids (dosing).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is dehorning? A: The removal of horns from animals. Dehorning removes horns so animals do not injure each other.
chunks.source: Dehorning removes horns so animals do not injure each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one advantage of dehorning cattle. A: Dehorned cattle do not injure each other or handlers. Without horns, cattle are safer to handle and need less space.
chunks.source: Without horns, cattle are safer to handle and need less space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you increase milk production in a dairy cow? A: Feed it well with a balanced diet and plenty of water. Good feeding, clean water and proper milking raise milk yield.
chunks.source: Good feeding, clean water and proper milking raise milk yield.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do farmers control the breeding of poor-quality animals on their farms? A: By castrating or culling poor-quality males. Castrating poor bulls stops them from breeding and spoiling the herd.
chunks.source: Castrating poor bulls stops them from breeding and spoiling the herd.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What germ causes mastitis in cattle? A: Bacteria. Bacteria infect the udder and cause mastitis.
chunks.source: Bacteria infect the udder and cause mastitis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO signs of mastitis. (Choose TWO.) A: Swollen painful udder, Milk with pus or blood. Mastitis swells the udder and spoils the milk with pus or blood.
chunks.source: Mastitis swells the udder and spoils the milk with pus or blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of controlling mastitis in cattle. A: Milk with clean hands and treat infected cows. Clean milking and treating sick cows control mastitis.
chunks.source: Clean milking and treating sick cows control mastitis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The type of cattle kept to provide labour on a farm is called ____ cattle. A: work. Work oxen plough fields and pull carts.
chunks.source: Work oxen plough fields and pull carts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the government control the spread of a cattle disease when it breaks out in an area? A: By quarantine and vaccination campaigns. Quarantine stops animal movement and vaccination builds protection.
chunks.source: Quarantine stops animal movement and vaccination builds protection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one advantage of cross breeding with an exotic bull. A: The calves give more milk and grow faster. An exotic bull passes high milk yield and fast growth to calves.
chunks.source: An exotic bull passes high milk yield and fast growth to calves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any FOUR basic requirements considered when starting a livestock farm. (Choose FOUR.) A: Land, Capital (money), Labour, Good breeds of animals. A livestock farm needs land, money, workers, good breeds, water and market.
chunks.source: A livestock farm needs land, money, workers, good breeds, water and market.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it difficult to control diseases under the free-range system of grazing cattle? A: Animals mix freely and spread diseases to each other. Free-range cattle wander and mix, so diseases spread easily.
chunks.source: Free-range cattle wander and mix, so diseases spread easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO ways of controlling external (ecto) parasites in cattle. (Choose TWO.) A: Dipping in acaricide, Spraying with acaricide. Dipping and spraying kill ticks, lice and other parasites on the skin.
chunks.source: Dipping and spraying kill ticks, lice and other parasites on the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one disadvantage of inbreeding in cattle. A: It produces weak calves with poor growth. Mating related animals weakens the offspring.
chunks.source: Mating related animals weakens the offspring.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one importance of deworming animals. A: It removes worms so animals grow well and stay healthy. Dewormed animals use their feed for growth instead of feeding worms.
chunks.source: Dewormed animals use their feed for growth instead of feeding worms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of ear tagging in cattle. A: It identifies each animal for proper records. Ear tags give each animal an identity for records of health and breeding.
chunks.source: Ear tags give each animal an identity for records of health and breeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Cattle are called ruminants because they chew cud. True or False? A: True. Cattle chew cud (bring back swallowed food to chew again), so they are ruminants.
chunks.source: Cattle chew cud (bring back swallowed food to chew again), so they are ruminants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why would animals in a paddock system not easily be attacked by East Coast fever? A: Rotating paddocks leaves ticks behind to die, breaking disease spread. Paddock rotation starves ticks, so tick-borne East Coast fever spreads less.
chunks.source: Paddock rotation starves ticks, so tick-borne East Coast fever spreads less.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO exotic breeds of cattle kept for dairy. (Choose TWO.) A: Friesian, Jersey. Friesian and Jersey are famous exotic dairy breeds.
chunks.source: Friesian and Jersey are famous exotic dairy breeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one advantage of zero grazing system of grazing cattle. A: It needs only a small piece of land. Zero grazing keeps cattle in a stall, so it suits farmers with little land.
chunks.source: Zero grazing keeps cattle in a stall, so it suits farmers with little land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one cattle disease caused by each of the following germs. A: Virus: Foot and mouth disease; Bacteria: Anthrax. Foot-and-mouth is viral; anthrax is bacterial.
chunks.source: Foot-and-mouth is viral; anthrax is bacterial.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO ways of preventing cattle diseases. (Choose TWO.) A: Vaccinate animals regularly, Isolate sick animals. Vaccination and isolation keep diseases away from the herd.
chunks.source: Vaccination and isolation keep diseases away from the herd.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The structure used to hold the cow's head during vaccination is called a ____. A: crush. A crush holds the cow still so vaccination is safe.
chunks.source: A crush holds the cow still so vaccination is safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from labour, give one other requirement for starting a livestock farm. A: Land. Animals need land for housing and grazing.
chunks.source: Animals need land for housing and grazing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Put each cattle parasite under Internal or External. A: Internal (endo) parasites: Tapeworms,Roundworms,Liver flukes; External (ecto) parasites: Ticks,Tsetse flies,Lice. Internal parasites live inside the body; external parasites live on the skin.
chunks.source: Internal parasites live inside the body; external parasites live on the skin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is apiculture? A: The keeping of bees. Apiculture is the practice of keeping bees for honey and other products.
chunks.source: Apiculture is the practice of keeping bees for honey and other products.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the main reason why farmers keep bees on their farms. A: To get honey and other bee products for food and income. Bees give honey, wax and propolis which farmers eat and sell.
chunks.source: Bees give honey, wax and propolis which farmers eat and sell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name TWO types of bees in the environment. (Choose TWO.) A: Honey bees, Stingless bees. Honey bees and stingless bees are the common types around us.
chunks.source: Honey bees and stingless bees are the common types around us.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are honey bees called social insects? A: They live and work together in a colony. Honey bees live together in a hive with each doing its duty.
chunks.source: Honey bees live together in a hive with each doing its duty.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any TWO types of honey bees. (Choose TWO.) A: The queen bee, The worker bee. A hive has the queen, workers and drones.
chunks.source: A hive has the queen, workers and drones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the role of the queen bee in the hive. A: To lay eggs. The queen is the mother of the hive; she lays all the eggs.
chunks.source: The queen is the mother of the hive; she lays all the eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why can't a queen bee die after stinging its enemy? A: Her sting is smooth and does not stick in the victim. The queen's smooth sting pulls out safely, unlike the worker's barbed sting.
chunks.source: The queen's smooth sting pulls out safely, unlike the worker's barbed sting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The special food given to a queen bee is called royal ____. A: jelly. Royal jelly is the rich food fed to the queen bee.
chunks.source: Royal jelly is the rich food fed to the queen bee.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The queen bee is the most fertile bee in the hive. True or False? A: True. The queen lays all the eggs, so she is the most fertile bee.
chunks.source: The queen lays all the eggs, so she is the most fertile bee.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of bees develops from unfertilized eggs? A: Drones. Unfertilized eggs hatch into male drones.
chunks.source: Unfertilized eggs hatch into male drones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the role of a drone bee. A: To mate with the queen. Drones are male bees whose duty is to fertilize the queen.
chunks.source: Drones are male bees whose duty is to fertilize the queen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of bees do not have a sting? A: Drones. Male drones have no sting; only females (queen and workers) sting.
chunks.source: Male drones have no sting; only females (queen and workers) sting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any TWO roles of worker bees in the hive. (Choose TWO.) A: Collecting nectar and pollen, Guarding the hive entrance. Workers do all the work: collecting food, feeding larvae, guarding and cleaning.
chunks.source: Workers do all the work: collecting food, feeding larvae, guarding and cleaning.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any THREE substances collected from the environment by bees. (Choose THREE.) A: Nectar, Pollen, Water. Bees collect nectar, pollen, water and propolis from the environment.
chunks.source: Bees collect nectar, pollen, water and propolis from the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does a worker bee die soon after stinging its enemy? A: Its barbed sting sticks in the victim and tears out part of its body. The worker's barbed sting cannot pull out, so the bee dies after stinging.
chunks.source: The worker's barbed sting cannot pull out, so the bee dies after stinging.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of bee wax to bees. A: They use it to build honeycombs. Beeswax forms the honeycomb cells where honey and brood are kept.
chunks.source: Beeswax forms the honeycomb cells where honey and brood are kept.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of honey bees that produce bee wax. A: Worker bees. Young worker bees produce wax from glands on their bodies.
chunks.source: Young worker bees produce wax from glands on their bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A place where beehives are kept is called an ____. A: apiary. An apiary is a collection of beehives.
chunks.source: An apiary is a collection of beehives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of bees produce royal jelly? A: Worker bees. Nurse worker bees produce royal jelly to feed the queen and larvae.
chunks.source: Nurse worker bees produce royal jelly to feed the queen and larvae.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of propolis to bees. A: It seals cracks and keeps the hive safe from germs. Bees use sticky propolis to seal the hive and fight germs.
chunks.source: Bees use sticky propolis to seal the hive and fight germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why can't worker bees lay eggs? A: They are not fully developed females. Workers are undeveloped females, so they cannot lay eggs like the queen.
chunks.source: Workers are undeveloped females, so they cannot lay eggs like the queen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any TWO methods of harvesting honey. (Choose TWO.) A: Pressing the honeycombs, Using a honey extractor (centrifuge). Honey is harvested by pressing combs or spinning them in an extractor.
chunks.source: Honey is harvested by pressing combs or spinning them in an extractor.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any TWO products obtained from bees. (Choose TWO.) A: Honey, Beeswax. Bees give honey, beeswax, propolis and royal jelly.
chunks.source: Bees give honey, beeswax, propolis and royal jelly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one product of bee honey. A: Mead (honey wine). Honey is used to make mead and to sweeten foods and medicines.
chunks.source: Honey is used to make mead and to sweeten foods and medicines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO importance of bee wax to people. (Choose TWO.) A: Making candles, Making shoe polish. People use beeswax for candles, polish, cosmetics and crayons.
chunks.source: People use beeswax for candles, polish, cosmetics and crayons.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is nuptial flight? A: The mating flight of the queen bee with drones. During the nuptial flight, the queen mates with drones in the air.
chunks.source: During the nuptial flight, the queen mates with drones in the air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one type of bee hives. A: A traditional hive (e.g., a log or bark hive). Traditional hives are made from logs, bark or pots; modern ones from boxes.
chunks.source: Traditional hives are made from logs, bark or pots; modern ones from boxes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a modern bee hive. A: A top bar hive. Top bar and Langstroth hives are modern box hives.
chunks.source: Top bar and Langstroth hives are modern box hives.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO advantages of a modern bee hive over a traditional bee hive. (Choose TWO.) A: Honey is harvested without destroying combs, It is easy to inspect the colony. Modern hives allow inspection and honey harvest without killing bees.
chunks.source: Modern hives allow inspection and honey harvest without killing bees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it easier to collect honey in a modern bee hive than in a traditional bee hive? A: Combs can be removed without destroying the hive. Removable top bars let farmers take honey without breaking combs.
chunks.source: Removable top bars let farmers take honey without breaking combs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is stocking the hive? A: Putting bees into a new hive. Stocking means introducing a bee colony into an empty hive.
chunks.source: Stocking means introducing a bee colony into an empty hive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do farmers stock the hive? A: By trapping a swarm and placing it in the hive. Farmers catch swarming bees and settle them into the hive.
chunks.source: Farmers catch swarming bees and settle them into the hive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is setting the hive? A: Placing the hive in a suitable position. Setting means putting the hive in a good shady, safe place.
chunks.source: Setting means putting the hive in a good shady, safe place.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO factors considered before setting up beehives. (Choose TWO.) A: Nearness to flowering plants, Nearness to clean water. Hives need flowers for nectar and water nearby, away from noise.
chunks.source: Hives need flowers for nectar and water nearby, away from noise.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is swarming? A: When part of the bee colony leaves the hive with a queen. Swarming is the natural splitting of a colony to form a new one.
chunks.source: Swarming is the natural splitting of a colony to form a new one.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State TWO main reasons why bees swarm. (Choose TWO.) A: Overcrowding in the hive, A new queen is produced. Bees swarm when the hive is crowded or a new queen emerges.
chunks.source: Bees swarm when the hive is crowded or a new queen emerges.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens to bees in the hive when a new queen is produced? A: The old queen leaves with some workers (swarming). When a new queen emerges, the old queen departs with a swarm.
chunks.source: When a new queen emerges, the old queen departs with a swarm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the modern bee hive and match each part to its name. A: Part marked A: Top bar; Part marked B: Queen excluder; Part marked C: Brood chamber. The top bar covers the hive, the queen excluder is the mesh screen, and the brood chamber holds the young bees.
chunks.source: The top bar covers the hive, the queen excluder is the mesh screen, and the brood chamber holds the young bees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the bee hive. What is the function of part marked B? A: It stops the queen from entering the honey chamber to lay eggs there. The queen excluder keeps the queen in the brood chamber so honey stays free of brood.
chunks.source: The queen excluder keeps the queen in the brood chamber so honey stays free of brood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The larvae of bees are called ____. A: grubs. Bee larvae are called grubs before they become pupae.
chunks.source: Bee larvae are called grubs before they become pupae.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is poultry? A: Domestic birds kept by farmers. Poultry are tamed birds like chicken, ducks and turkeys kept on farms.
chunks.source: Poultry are tamed birds like chicken, ducks and turkeys kept on farms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one type of poultry. A: Chicken. Chicken is the most common type of poultry; others are ducks, turkeys and geese.
chunks.source: Chicken is the most common type of poultry; others are ducks, turkeys and geese.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the difference between poultry and poultry keeping. A: Poultry are the birds while poultry keeping is the rearing of the birds. Poultry = the birds; poultry keeping = the activity of rearing them.
chunks.source: Poultry = the birds; poultry keeping = the activity of rearing them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why farmers rear poultry. A: To get eggs and meat. Poultry give eggs, meat and income to farmers.
chunks.source: Poultry give eggs, meat and income to farmers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO characteristics of exotic breeds of poultry. (Choose TWO.) A: They grow fast, They lay many eggs. Exotic breeds grow quickly and lay many eggs but need good care.
chunks.source: Exotic breeds grow quickly and lay many eggs but need good care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name TWO types of chicken. (Choose TWO.) A: Layers, Broilers. Layers are kept for eggs and broilers for meat.
chunks.source: Layers are kept for eggs and broilers for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO examples of exotic breeds of poultry kept for laying eggs. (Choose TWO.) A: White Leghorn, Rhode Island Red. White Leghorn and Rhode Island Red are famous exotic layers.
chunks.source: White Leghorn and Rhode Island Red are famous exotic layers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO exotic breeds of poultry kept for meat (chicken) production. (Choose TWO.) A: Light Sussex, Cornish. Light Sussex and Cornish are exotic breeds kept for meat.
chunks.source: Light Sussex and Cornish are exotic breeds kept for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one type of feathers in birds. A: Down feathers. Birds have down, contour and flight feathers.
chunks.source: Birds have down, contour and flight feathers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO importance of feathers to birds. (Choose TWO.) A: They keep birds warm, They help birds to fly. Feathers insulate the body and enable flight.
chunks.source: Feathers insulate the body and enable flight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one advantage of local breeds of poultry over exotic breeds. A: They resist diseases better. Local breeds are hardy and resist diseases better than exotic breeds.
chunks.source: Local breeds are hardy and resist diseases better than exotic breeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Chicks under four weeks are given ____ mash. A: chick. Chick mash is the special feed for young chicks.
chunks.source: Chick mash is the special feed for young chicks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do farmers carry out de-beaking in poultry farms? A: To stop birds from pecking and injuring each other. De-beaking (cutting beak tips) prevents cannibalism and egg eating.
chunks.source: De-beaking (cutting beak tips) prevents cannibalism and egg eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the importance of including calcium in chicken feed? A: It makes strong eggshells. Calcium builds hard eggshells in laying birds.
chunks.source: Calcium builds hard eggshells in laying birds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the egg and match each part to its name or function. A: Part marked X: Yolk; Part marked Y: Albumen (egg white); The function of part W (chalaza): It holds the yolk in the centre of the egg; The function of part Z (shell): It protects the inside of the egg. The egg has yolk (X), albumen (Y), chalaza (W) holding the yolk, and shell (Z) protecting all.
chunks.source: The egg has yolk (X), albumen (Y), chalaza (W) holding the yolk, and shell (Z) protecting all.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO systems of keeping poultry. (Choose TWO.) A: Deep litter system, Free range system. Poultry are kept under deep litter, free range or battery cage systems.
chunks.source: Poultry are kept under deep litter, free range or battery cage systems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it difficult to control diseases under the free-range system of keeping poultry? A: Birds roam and mix, spreading diseases. Free-range birds wander and mix with others, spreading infections.
chunks.source: Free-range birds wander and mix with others, spreading infections.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one advantage of deep litter system of keeping poultry. A: Many birds are kept in a small house. Deep litter keeps many birds together in one house.
chunks.source: Deep litter keeps many birds together in one house.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from getting money, give any TWO other ways a farmer benefits from keeping poultry. (Choose TWO.) A: Gets eggs for food, Gets manure for gardens. Poultry give the family eggs, meat and droppings for manure.
chunks.source: Poultry give the family eggs, meat and droppings for manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is incubation? A: Keeping eggs warm until they hatch. Incubation is warming fertilized eggs so chicks develop and hatch.
chunks.source: Incubation is warming fertilized eggs so chicks develop and hatch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO conditions necessary for an egg to hatch. (Choose TWO.) A: Warmth, Fertilization of the egg. A fertilized egg needs warmth (and moisture) to hatch.
chunks.source: A fertilized egg needs warmth (and moisture) to hatch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why an egg may fail to hatch. A: The egg is not fertilized. Unfertilized eggs have no chick inside and cannot hatch.
chunks.source: Unfertilized eggs have no chick inside and cannot hatch.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is brooding? A: Keeping chicks warm until they grow feathers. Brooding provides warmth to chicks that cannot yet control body heat.
chunks.source: Brooding provides warmth to chicks that cannot yet control body heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one type of brooders. A: A charcoal brooder (lantern/jiko). Brooders like charcoal stoves, lanterns or electric brooders warm chicks.
chunks.source: Brooders like charcoal stoves, lanterns or electric brooders warm chicks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one disadvantage of a deep litter system of keeping poultry. A: Diseases spread fast among crowded birds. Crowded birds in deep litter easily pass diseases to each other.
chunks.source: Crowded birds in deep litter easily pass diseases to each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one advantage of artificial incubation over natural incubation. A: Many eggs hatch at the same time. An incubator hatches many eggs at once without a broody hen.
chunks.source: An incubator hatches many eggs at once without a broody hen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each part of an incubator to its importance. A: Thermometer: It measures the temperature in the incubator; Thermostat: It controls (regulates) the temperature in the incubator. The thermometer measures heat; the thermostat keeps it at the right level.
chunks.source: The thermometer measures heat; the thermostat keeps it at the right level.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is litter as applied in poultry keeping? A: Dry bedding material spread on the floor of a poultry house. Litter like wood shavings or straw covers the floor of the poultry house.
chunks.source: Litter like wood shavings or straw covers the floor of the poultry house.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one importance of litter in a poultry house. A: It keeps the house warm and dry. Litter absorbs droppings and keeps birds warm and comfortable.
chunks.source: Litter absorbs droppings and keeps birds warm and comfortable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one material that can be used as litter in a poultry house. A: Wood shavings. Wood shavings, straw or coffee husks make good litter.
chunks.source: Wood shavings, straw or coffee husks make good litter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down TWO poultry diseases caused by bacteria. (Choose TWO.) A: Fowl typhoid, Pullorum. Fowl typhoid and pullorum are bacterial diseases of poultry.
chunks.source: Fowl typhoid and pullorum are bacterial diseases of poultry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down TWO poultry diseases caused by virus. (Choose TWO.) A: Newcastle disease, Fowl pox. Newcastle disease and fowl pox are caused by viruses.
chunks.source: Newcastle disease and fowl pox are caused by viruses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO ways of preventing diseases in poultry. (Choose TWO.) A: Vaccinate birds regularly, Keep the poultry house clean. Vaccination and cleanliness prevent poultry diseases.
chunks.source: Vaccination and cleanliness prevent poultry diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are parasites? A: Living things that feed on other living things and harm them. Parasites live on or in a host and harm it, e.g., worms and ticks.
chunks.source: Parasites live on or in a host and harm it, e.g., worms and ticks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of each type of parasite in poultry. A: Internal parasite in poultry: Tapeworms; External parasite in poultry: Lice. Tapeworms live inside birds; lice live on their bodies.
chunks.source: Tapeworms live inside birds; lice live on their bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO ways of preventing parasites in poultry. (Choose TWO.) A: Deworm birds regularly, Dust birds against lice. Deworming and dusting keep internal and external parasites away.
chunks.source: Deworming and dusting keep internal and external parasites away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which system of rearing poultry would you recommend to a farmer who wants to keep layers? A: Battery cage system. Battery cages suit layers: eggs roll out clean and records are easy.
chunks.source: Battery cages suit layers: eggs roll out clean and records are easy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO differences between a cock and a hen. (Choose TWO.) A: A cock has a bigger comb and wattles, A cock crows while a hen clucks. Cocks are bigger, colourful and crow; hens are smaller and lay eggs.
chunks.source: Cocks are bigger, colourful and crow; hens are smaller and lay eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of heat in a brooder. A: It keeps chicks warm. Chicks need warmth until they grow feathers.
chunks.source: Chicks need warmth until they grow feathers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are poultry vices? A: Bad habits of birds like egg eating and cannibalism. Vices are bad behaviours such as egg eating, feather pecking and cannibalism.
chunks.source: Vices are bad behaviours such as egg eating, feather pecking and cannibalism.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO causes of poultry vices. (Choose TWO.) A: Overcrowding, Lack of enough feed. Crowding and hunger drive birds to peck each other and eat eggs.
chunks.source: Crowding and hunger drive birds to peck each other and eat eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from egg eating, give any TWO other examples of poultry vices. (Choose TWO.) A: Feather pecking, Cannibalism. Feather pecking and cannibalism are common poultry vices besides egg eating.
chunks.source: Feather pecking and cannibalism are common poultry vices besides egg eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one cause of egg eating in poultry. A: Lack of calcium in feed. Birds lacking calcium eat eggs to get it; strong shells also prevent it.
chunks.source: Birds lacking calcium eat eggs to get it; strong shells also prevent it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO ways of preventing egg eating vice in poultry. (Choose TWO.) A: Give feed rich in calcium, Collect eggs regularly. Calcium-rich feed and quick egg collection stop egg eating.
chunks.source: Calcium-rich feed and quick egg collection stop egg eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A farmer's chicken pass blood-stained droppings and have drooping wings. Match each item to its answer. A: The disease likely attacking the birds: Coccidiosis; How neighbours can prevent it (1): Vaccinate their birds; How neighbours can prevent it (2): Keep their poultry houses clean and dry; Why separate the sick birds: To stop the disease spreading to healthy birds. Blood-stained droppings with drooping wings point to coccidiosis; isolate, vaccinate and clean.
chunks.source: Blood-stained droppings with drooping wings point to coccidiosis; isolate, vaccinate and clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of hanging each item in a poultry house. A: Perches: Birds rest and sleep on them; Green vegetables: They provide vitamins and keep birds busy. Perches are for resting; greens give vitamins and reduce pecking.
chunks.source: Perches are for resting; greens give vitamins and reduce pecking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO disadvantages of keeping local breeds of poultry. (Choose TWO.) A: They grow slowly, They lay few eggs. Local breeds grow slowly and lay few eggs compared to exotic breeds.
chunks.source: Local breeds grow slowly and lay few eggs compared to exotic breeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do feathers help to keep birds warm? A: They trap warm air near the body. Fluffy feathers hold a layer of warm air against the bird's body.
chunks.source: Fluffy feathers hold a layer of warm air against the bird's body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one advantage of a battery cage system of keeping poultry. A: Eggs are clean and easy to collect. In battery cages, eggs roll out clean and each bird's laying is recorded.
chunks.source: In battery cages, eggs roll out clean and each bird's laying is recorded.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The type of brooding where a mother hen moves with her chicks searching for food is called ____ brooding. A: natural. In natural brooding, the mother hen cares for and warms her chicks.
chunks.source: In natural brooding, the mother hen cares for and warms her chicks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any THREE reasons why records should be kept on a poultry farm. (Choose THREE.) A: To know the profit or loss, To track egg production, To plan feeding. Records show profit, production and help plan the farm.
chunks.source: Records show profit, production and help plan the farm.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from Light Sussex, name any other exotic breed of chicken kept for meat. A: Cornish. The Cornish is another exotic breed kept for meat.
chunks.source: The Cornish is another exotic breed kept for meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name TWO systems of keeping poultry that enable a farmer to keep large numbers of birds. (Choose TWO.) A: Deep litter system, Battery cage system. Deep litter and battery cages house many birds in a small space.
chunks.source: Deep litter and battery cages house many birds in a small space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Put each poultry disease under Bacterial or Viral. A: Bacterial: Fowl typhoid,Pullorum; Viral: Newcastle disease,Fowl pox,Gumboro. Bacteria cause fowl typhoid and pullorum; viruses cause Newcastle, fowl pox and Gumboro.
chunks.source: Bacteria cause fowl typhoid and pullorum; viruses cause Newcastle, fowl pox and Gumboro.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: An egg needs warmth to hatch. True or False? A: True. Fertilized eggs only hatch when kept warm, by a hen or an incubator.
chunks.source: Fertilized eggs only hatch when kept warm, by a hen or an incubator.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any TWO products got from sheep. (Choose TWO.) A: Wool, Mutton. Sheep give wool for clothes and mutton (meat).
chunks.source: Sheep give wool for clothes and mutton (meat).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does shearing refer to in sheep rearing? A: Cutting off wool from sheep. Shearing is shaving the wool off sheep.
chunks.source: Shearing is shaving the wool off sheep.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of grazing goats and match each item to its answer. A: The method of grazing shown: Tethering; An advantage of this method (1): The goat cannot wander and destroy crops; An advantage of this method (2): It is cheap because no fencing is needed; A disadvantage of this method: The rope can tangle and injure the goat. The goat is tied to a peg: tethering keeps it in place cheaply, but the rope can harm it.
chunks.source: The goat is tied to a peg: tethering keeps it in place cheaply, but the rope can harm it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one method of rearing cattle used in towns. A: Zero grazing. Zero grazing (stall feeding) fits towns where grazing land is scarce.
chunks.source: Zero grazing (stall feeding) fits towns where grazing land is scarce.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What germ causes lamb dysentery in sheep? A: Bacteria. Bacteria cause lamb dysentery, a diarrhoea disease of lambs.
chunks.source: Bacteria cause lamb dysentery, a diarrhoea disease of lambs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO signs of lamb dysentery. (Choose TWO.) A: Bloody diarrhoea, Weakness and loss of appetite. Lamb dysentery shows as bloody diarrhoea and weak lambs.
chunks.source: Lamb dysentery shows as bloody diarrhoea and weak lambs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way a farmer can control lamb dysentery. A: Keep lambing pens clean and dry. Clean dry pens stop the germs that cause lamb dysentery.
chunks.source: Clean dry pens stop the germs that cause lamb dysentery.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of an exotic breed of goats kept in Uganda. A: Saanen. The Saanen is a well-known exotic dairy goat kept in Uganda.
chunks.source: The Saanen is a well-known exotic dairy goat kept in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One example of fibre got from goats is ____. A: mohair. Angora goats give mohair, a fibre used in textiles.
chunks.source: Angora goats give mohair, a fibre used in textiles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO reasons why some farmers would prefer rearing goats to cattle. (Choose TWO.) A: Goats need less feed and space, Goats multiply faster. Goats are cheap to keep, need little space and breed quickly.
chunks.source: Goats are cheap to keep, need little space and breed quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from tethering, give any TWO other methods of grazing goats. (Choose TWO.) A: Paddock grazing, Herding. Goats can also graze in paddocks or be herded by a herdsman.
chunks.source: Goats can also graze in paddocks or be herded by a herdsman.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of manure is got from a goat's farm? A: Goat droppings (pellets). Goat droppings are rich manure for gardens.
chunks.source: Goat droppings are rich manure for gardens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is gestation period? A: The time from conception to birth. Gestation is the pregnancy period before a baby is born.
chunks.source: Gestation is the pregnancy period before a baby is born.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The gestation period of a nanny (goat) is about ____ months. A: five. A goat carries its pregnancy for about five months.
chunks.source: A goat carries its pregnancy for about five months.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should the floor of a goat's house be made slanting? A: So that urine and water drain out. A slanting floor drains urine, keeping the house dry and clean.
chunks.source: A slanting floor drains urine, keeping the house dry and clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should milk goats be given plenty of water to drink? A: Water helps them produce more milk. Milk contains much water, so milking goats need plenty to drink.
chunks.source: Milk contains much water, so milking goats need plenty to drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down TWO exotic breeds of goats kept for milk production. (Choose TWO.) A: Saanen, Toggenburg. Saanen and Toggenburg are exotic dairy goat breeds.
chunks.source: Saanen and Toggenburg are exotic dairy goat breeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one breed of goats kept for meat production. A: Boer goat. The Boer is a famous meat goat breed.
chunks.source: The Boer is a famous meat goat breed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do farmers keep Angora goats? A: To get mohair fibre. Angora goats are kept for their soft mohair fibre.
chunks.source: Angora goats are kept for their soft mohair fibre.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention TWO methods of grazing sheep. (Choose TWO.) A: Herding, Paddock grazing. Sheep are grazed by herding or in paddocks.
chunks.source: Sheep are grazed by herding or in paddocks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is zero grazing? A: Keeping animals in a stall and bringing feed and water to them. In zero grazing, animals stay housed while the farmer brings their feed.
chunks.source: In zero grazing, animals stay housed while the farmer brings their feed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest TWO advantages of zero grazing to a farmer. (Choose TWO.) A: It needs only a small piece of land, Manure is easy to collect. Zero grazing saves land and makes manure collection easy.
chunks.source: Zero grazing saves land and makes manure collection easy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Giving birth in goats is called ____. A: kidding. A goat giving birth is kidding.
chunks.source: A goat giving birth is kidding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention TWO products from goats. (Choose TWO.) A: Milk, Meat (chevon). Goats give milk, meat (chevon) and skins.
chunks.source: Goats give milk, meat (chevon) and skins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the meaning of the term castration. A: The removal of the testicles of a male animal. Castration removes the testicles so the male cannot breed.
chunks.source: Castration removes the testicles so the male cannot breed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO dangers of castration to animals. (Choose TWO.) A: Heavy bleeding, Infection of the wound. Poor castration can cause bleeding and wound infection.
chunks.source: Poor castration can cause bleeding and wound infection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is shearing of sheep done during the dry season? A: So the sheep do not catch cold without their wool. Sheep shorn in cold rain could catch pneumonia; dry season is safer.
chunks.source: Sheep shorn in cold rain could catch pneumonia; dry season is safer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The farm tool used in shearing sheep is called ____ shears. A: wool. Wool shears (or shearing machines) cut wool off sheep.
chunks.source: Wool shears (or shearing machines) cut wool off sheep.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which product from sheep is used in the textile industry? A: Wool. Wool is spun into yarn for clothes in the textile industry.
chunks.source: Wool is spun into yarn for clothes in the textile industry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from wool, name any other animal product used in the textile industry. A: Mohair from Angora goats. Mohair and silk are other animal fibres used in textiles.
chunks.source: Mohair and silk are other animal fibres used in textiles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO advantages of docking sheep. (Choose TWO.) A: It keeps the backside clean, It prevents maggot attack. Docking (cutting the tail) keeps sheep clean and free of maggots.
chunks.source: Docking (cutting the tail) keeps sheep clean and free of maggots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is dehorning a good practice on an animal farm? A: Hornless animals do not injure each other or handlers. Dehorned animals are safer and need less space.
chunks.source: Dehorned animals are safer and need less space.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention TWO bacterial diseases common in sheep and goats. (Choose TWO.) A: Anthrax, Blackquarter. Anthrax and blackquarter are bacterial diseases of small ruminants.
chunks.source: Anthrax and blackquarter are bacterial diseases of small ruminants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What germ causes Nagana disease in farm animals? A: A protozoan (trypanosome). Trypanosomes carried by tsetse flies cause nagana.
chunks.source: Trypanosomes carried by tsetse flies cause nagana.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO external parasites in sheep. (Choose TWO.) A: Ticks, Lice. Ticks and lice live on the skin of sheep.
chunks.source: Ticks and lice live on the skin of sheep.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO effects of parasites in farm animals. (Choose TWO.) A: Loss of weight, Anaemia. Parasites suck blood and feed, causing weight loss and anaemia.
chunks.source: Parasites suck blood and feed, causing weight loss and anaemia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the meaning of each term. A: Piggery: A house where pigs are kept; Farrow: To give birth in pigs. Pigs live in a piggery; a sow farrows when giving birth.
chunks.source: Pigs live in a piggery; a sow farrows when giving birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a sow different from a boar? A: A sow is a female pig while a boar is a male pig. Sow = female pig; boar = male pig.
chunks.source: Sow = female pig; boar = male pig.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO characteristics of local breeds of pigs. (Choose TWO.) A: They resist diseases, They need little care. Local pigs are hardy and need little care but grow slowly.
chunks.source: Local pigs are hardy and need little care but grow slowly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any TWO systems of rearing pigs. (Choose TWO.) A: Intensive (housed) system, Free range system. Pigs are reared intensively in pens or free range.
chunks.source: Pigs are reared intensively in pens or free range.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one problem faced by farmers who rear pigs in Uganda. A: Lack of enough quality feed. Good pig feed is costly and hard to find.
chunks.source: Good pig feed is costly and hard to find.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What causes swine flu in pigs? A: A virus. Swine flu is a viral disease of pigs.
chunks.source: Swine flu is a viral disease of pigs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO signs of a pig with swine flu. (Choose TWO.) A: Coughing, Fever and loss of appetite. Swine flu shows as coughing, fever and dullness.
chunks.source: Swine flu shows as coughing, fever and dullness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way a farmer can control the spread of swine flu in pigs. A: Isolate sick pigs. Separating sick pigs stops the virus spreading.
chunks.source: Separating sick pigs stops the virus spreading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of grazing goats in muddy areas. A: They can get foot rot. Muddy areas rot goats' feet (foot rot).
chunks.source: Muddy areas rot goats' feet (foot rot).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Tethering is a method of grazing goats. True or False? A: True. Tethering means tying a goat to a peg so it grazes around it.
chunks.source: Tethering means tying a goat to a peg so it grazes around it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is reproduction? A: The process by which living things produce young ones. Reproduction is how organisms make more of their own kind.
chunks.source: Reproduction is how organisms make more of their own kind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention TWO types of reproduction. (Choose TWO.) A: Sexual reproduction, Asexual reproduction. Reproduction is sexual (two parents) or asexual (one parent).
chunks.source: Reproduction is sexual (two parents) or asexual (one parent).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The permanent birth control method in females is called tubal ____. A: ligation. Tubal ligation permanently blocks the oviducts so no pregnancy occurs.
chunks.source: Tubal ligation permanently blocks the oviducts so no pregnancy occurs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of reproduction do bacteria undergo? A: Asexual reproduction. Bacteria divide into two; they reproduce asexually.
chunks.source: Bacteria divide into two; they reproduce asexually.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is growth different from development? A: Growth is increase in size while development is increase in ability. Growth = getting bigger; development = becoming more able and mature.
chunks.source: Growth = getting bigger; development = becoming more able and mature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is adolescence? A: The stage between childhood and adulthood. Adolescence is the teenage stage of becoming an adult.
chunks.source: Adolescence is the teenage stage of becoming an adult.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any TWO primary sex characteristics in adolescent boys. (Choose TWO.) A: Growth of testes, Growth of the penis. Primary sex characteristics are the reproductive organs themselves.
chunks.source: Primary sex characteristics are the reproductive organs themselves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any TWO secondary sex characteristics in adolescent girls. (Choose TWO.) A: Growth of breasts, Widening of hips. Secondary characteristics appear at puberty but are not the reproductive organs.
chunks.source: Secondary characteristics appear at puberty but are not the reproductive organs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is family planning? A: Planning the number and spacing of children. Family planning helps couples choose how many children to have and when.
chunks.source: Family planning helps couples choose how many children to have and when.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO advantages of family planning to a woman. (Choose TWO.) A: Her health is protected, She has time to care for each child. Spaced births protect the mother's health and let her care well for children.
chunks.source: Spaced births protect the mother's health and let her care well for children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any TWO artificial birth control methods. (Choose TWO.) A: Using condoms, Taking birth control pills. Artificial methods use devices or drugs, e.g., condoms, pills, injections.
chunks.source: Artificial methods use devices or drugs, e.g., condoms, pills, injections.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any TWO natural birth control methods. (Choose TWO.) A: Abstinence, The calendar (rhythm) method. Natural methods use no devices: abstinence, withdrawal, calendar method.
chunks.source: Natural methods use no devices: abstinence, withdrawal, calendar method.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO disadvantages of pregnancy in adolescence. (Choose TWO.) A: The girl may drop out of school, Her health is at risk. Teenage pregnancy risks health and ends schooling.
chunks.source: Teenage pregnancy risks health and ends schooling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one effect of gonorrhoea on the female reproductive system. A: It can block the oviducts and cause infertility. Untreated gonorrhoea scars the oviducts and can make a woman unable to have babies.
chunks.source: Untreated gonorrhoea scars the oviducts and can make a woman unable to have babies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which characteristics differentiate between a grown-up boy and a girl? A: Secondary sex characteristics. Beards, breasts, voice and body shape distinguish grown males and females.
chunks.source: Beards, breasts, voice and body shape distinguish grown males and females.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State TWO problems faced by a family with many children. (Choose TWO.) A: Not enough food and money, Poor care for each child. Many children strain food, money, school fees and parental care.
chunks.source: Many children strain food, money, school fees and parental care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one health problem faced by a woman who produces many children with little spacing. A: Anaemia (shortage of blood). Frequent births drain the mother's blood and strength, causing anaemia.
chunks.source: Frequent births drain the mother's blood and strength, causing anaemia.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is spacing of children important in a family? A: It protects the mother's health and lets each child get good care. Spaced children let the mother recover and each child receive enough care.
chunks.source: Spaced children let the mother recover and each child receive enough care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention TWO secondary sex characteristics common to both adolescent boys and girls. (Choose TWO.) A: Growth of pubic hair, Growth of armpit hair. Both boys and girls grow pubic and armpit hair at puberty.
chunks.source: Both boys and girls grow pubic and armpit hair at puberty.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO emotional changes in adolescents. (Choose TWO.) A: Mood swings, Strong feelings of attraction to others. Adolescents experience mood swings and new strong emotions.
chunks.source: Adolescents experience mood swings and new strong emotions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one problem faced by adolescents. A: Peer pressure. Adolescents struggle with peer pressure, body changes and emotions.
chunks.source: Adolescents struggle with peer pressure, body changes and emotions.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is puberty? A: The stage when the body becomes able to reproduce. Puberty is when reproductive organs mature and secondary characteristics appear.
chunks.source: Puberty is when reproductive organs mature and secondary characteristics appear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one sign which is common in people with tuberculosis and those with AIDS. A: Loss of weight. Both TB and AIDS cause serious weight loss.
chunks.source: Both TB and AIDS cause serious weight loss.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The female reproductive gametes in animals are called ____. A: ova. Ova (eggs) are the female gametes produced by ovaries.
chunks.source: Ova (eggs) are the female gametes produced by ovaries.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from producing ova, state any other function of the ovary. A: It produces female hormones. Ovaries also make the female hormones that control body changes.
chunks.source: Ovaries also make the female hormones that control body changes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are Sexually Transmitted Diseases? A: Diseases spread through sexual contact. STDs like gonorrhoea, syphilis and HIV pass from person to person during sex.
chunks.source: STDs like gonorrhoea, syphilis and HIV pass from person to person during sex.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from gonorrhoea and AIDS, name TWO other sexually transmitted diseases. (Choose TWO.) A: Syphilis, Chlamydia. Syphilis and chlamydia are other common STDs.
chunks.source: Syphilis and chlamydia are other common STDs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the function of the amniotic fluid during pregnancy. A: It protects the foetus from shock and injury. The fluid cushions the baby against bumps and keeps temperature steady.
chunks.source: The fluid cushions the baby against bumps and keeps temperature steady.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is TASO (The AIDS Support Organisation) useful to AIDS victims? A: It gives them counselling, treatment and care. TASO supports people with HIV/AIDS with medicine, food and counselling.
chunks.source: TASO supports people with HIV/AIDS with medicine, food and counselling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one cause of teenage pregnancy. A: Lack of guidance and peer pressure. Poor guidance, peer pressure and abuse can lead to teenage pregnancy.
chunks.source: Poor guidance, peer pressure and abuse can lead to teenage pregnancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can teenage pregnancy be controlled in adolescents? A: By guiding them and encouraging abstinence. Guidance, abstinence and adult care protect adolescents.
chunks.source: Guidance, abstinence and adult care protect adolescents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is a person who is HIV positive different from one who has developed AIDS? A: HIV positive means carrying the virus; AIDS is the advanced disease stage. HIV is the virus; AIDS is the late stage when the body defence collapses.
chunks.source: HIV is the virus; AIDS is the late stage when the body defence collapses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any TWO things a pregnant woman must do to promote the health of her baby in the womb. (Choose TWO.) A: Eat a balanced diet, Attend antenatal visits. Good feeding and antenatal care keep mother and baby healthy.
chunks.source: Good feeding and antenatal care keep mother and baby healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO signs that show that an individual is suffering from AIDS. (Choose TWO.) A: Serious loss of weight, Long-lasting diarrhoea. AIDS shows as wasting, long diarrhoea, TB and skin rashes.
chunks.source: AIDS shows as wasting, long diarrhoea, TB and skin rashes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why would you advise a youth to abstain from sex? A: To avoid HIV/AIDS, STDs and early pregnancy. Abstinence protects youths from HIV, STDs and teenage pregnancy.
chunks.source: Abstinence protects youths from HIV, STDs and teenage pregnancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger of a blocked oviduct in a woman. A: She cannot conceive (infertility). A blocked oviduct stops the ovum meeting sperm, causing infertility.
chunks.source: A blocked oviduct stops the ovum meeting sperm, causing infertility.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fertilization in human females takes place in the ____. A: oviduct. The sperm meets the ovum in the oviduct (fallopian tube).
chunks.source: The sperm meets the ovum in the oviduct (fallopian tube).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from producing sperms, how else are the testes useful to males? A: They produce male hormones. Testes make male hormones that develop male characteristics.
chunks.source: Testes make male hormones that develop male characteristics.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one sign of syphilis. A: Sores on the private parts. Syphilis starts with painless sores on the genitals.
chunks.source: Syphilis starts with painless sores on the genitals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the germ that causes AIDS. A: The HIV virus. HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) causes AIDS.
chunks.source: HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) causes AIDS.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from having sex with an infected person, write down TWO other ways one can get the germ that causes AIDS. (Choose TWO.) A: Through infected blood transfusion, From an infected mother to her baby. HIV also spreads through infected blood and from mother to child.
chunks.source: HIV also spreads through infected blood and from mother to child.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In ABC against AIDS, A stands for ____. A: abstinence. A = Abstinence, B = Be faithful, C = use Condoms.
chunks.source: A = Abstinence, B = Be faithful, C = use Condoms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should young girls avoid getting pregnant? A: Pregnancy risks their health, schooling and future. Teenage pregnancy endangers health and stops education.
chunks.source: Teenage pregnancy endangers health and stops education.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is fertilization? A: The union of a sperm and an ovum. Fertilization is when the male sperm joins the female ovum.
chunks.source: Fertilization is when the male sperm joins the female ovum.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of fertilization do mammals undergo? A: Internal fertilization. In mammals, fertilization happens inside the female's body.
chunks.source: In mammals, fertilization happens inside the female's body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do mammals reproduce? A: Sexually, giving birth to live young. Mammals mate and females give birth to live babies.
chunks.source: Mammals mate and females give birth to live babies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the function of the epididymis on the male reproductive system. A: It stores sperms. The epididymis is a coiled tube where sperms mature and are stored.
chunks.source: The epididymis is a coiled tube where sperms mature and are stored.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The part of the male reproductive system that produces sperms is the ____. A: testes. The testes (testicles) produce sperm cells.
chunks.source: The testes (testicles) produce sperm cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of the epididymis to the male reproductive system. A: It stores sperms until they are needed. Sperms wait in the epididymis until ejaculation.
chunks.source: Sperms wait in the epididymis until ejaculation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is pregnancy? A: The period from fertilization to birth. Pregnancy is the time a woman carries the developing baby.
chunks.source: Pregnancy is the time a woman carries the developing baby.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the germ that causes gonorrhoea. A: Bacteria. Gonorrhoea is a bacterial STD.
chunks.source: Gonorrhoea is a bacterial STD.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one sign of gonorrhoea infection in a newly born baby. A: Infected (sore) eyes. Babies can catch gonorrhoea in the eyes during birth.
chunks.source: Babies can catch gonorrhoea in the eyes during birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does gonorrhoea infection increase the chances of a person getting HIV/AIDS? A: Its sores give HIV an entry into the body. Open sores from gonorrhoea let the HIV virus enter easily.
chunks.source: Open sores from gonorrhoea let the HIV virus enter easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can a person avoid getting gonorrhoea? A: By abstaining from sex or being faithful to one uninfected partner. Abstinence and faithfulness prevent gonorrhoea.
chunks.source: Abstinence and faithfulness prevent gonorrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The gestation period in humans is ____ months. A: nine. Human pregnancy lasts about nine months.
chunks.source: Human pregnancy lasts about nine months.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any TWO signs of pregnancy in women. (Choose TWO.) A: Missing monthly periods, Morning sickness (vomiting). Missed periods and morning vomiting are early signs of pregnancy.
chunks.source: Missed periods and morning vomiting are early signs of pregnancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain what ante-natal care is. A: Health care given to a pregnant woman before birth. Ante-natal care checks the mother and baby during pregnancy.
chunks.source: Ante-natal care checks the mother and baby during pregnancy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any TWO ways pregnant women benefit from antenatal visits. (Choose TWO.) A: Problems are found and treated early, They learn how to care for the baby. Clinics detect problems early and teach baby care.
chunks.source: Clinics detect problems early and teach baby care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from ante-natal care, give TWO other ways of caring for pregnant women. (Choose TWO.) A: Give them enough rest, Feed them a balanced diet. Rest and good feeding keep pregnant women healthy.
chunks.source: Rest and good feeding keep pregnant women healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way should pregnant women protect their unborn babies from malaria? A: By sleeping under treated mosquito nets. Mosquito nets stop malaria mosquitoes biting mother and baby.
chunks.source: Mosquito nets stop malaria mosquitoes biting mother and baby.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are pregnant women advised not to smoke? A: Smoke harms the unborn baby. Tobacco poisons reach the baby and can cause low birth weight or death.
chunks.source: Tobacco poisons reach the baby and can cause low birth weight or death.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which element of primary health care deals with pregnant women and their unborn babies? A: Maternal and child health. Maternal and child health covers mothers and babies.
chunks.source: Maternal and child health covers mothers and babies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any TWO diseases of the male reproductive system. (Choose TWO.) A: Gonorrhoea, Syphilis. STDs like gonorrhoea and syphilis attack the male reproductive system.
chunks.source: STDs like gonorrhoea and syphilis attack the male reproductive system.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any TWO disorders of the male reproductive system. (Choose TWO.) A: Undescended testes, Prostate problems. Undescended testes and prostate enlargement are male reproductive disorders.
chunks.source: Undescended testes and prostate enlargement are male reproductive disorders.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does gonorrhoea lead to ectopic pregnancy in women? A: It scars and blocks the oviducts so the embryo sticks there. Scarred tubes trap the fertilized egg, which then grows in the tube.
chunks.source: Scarred tubes trap the fertilized egg, which then grows in the tube.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from leading to ectopic pregnancy, how else does gonorrhoea affect women? A: It can cause infertility. Gonorrhoea damage can leave a woman unable to conceive.
chunks.source: Gonorrhoea damage can leave a woman unable to conceive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from ectopic pregnancy, state any one disorder of the female reproductive system. A: Blocked oviducts. Blocked oviducts are a common female reproductive disorder.
chunks.source: Blocked oviducts are a common female reproductive disorder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give TWO possible ways through which a baby can get HIV/AIDS from the mother. (Choose TWO.) A: During birth, Through breastfeeding. HIV passes from mother to child during birth or through breast milk.
chunks.source: HIV passes from mother to child during birth or through breast milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State TWO ways in which an HIV positive pregnant woman can protect her unborn baby from getting HIV/AIDS. (Choose TWO.) A: Take ARV drugs as advised, Deliver in a health facility. ARVs and skilled delivery greatly reduce mother-to-child HIV spread.
chunks.source: ARVs and skilled delivery greatly reduce mother-to-child HIV spread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each process in human reproduction to its correct meaning. A: Ovulation: Release of an ovum from the ovary; Implantation: Attachment of the embryo on the uterus wall; Pregnancy: The period from fertilization to birth; Fertilization: Union of a sperm and an ovum. Ovulation releases the egg, fertilization joins sperm and egg, implantation fixes the embryo, pregnancy carries it to birth.
chunks.source: Ovulation releases the egg, fertilization joins sperm and egg, implantation fixes the embryo, pregnancy carries it to birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the female reproductive organ and match each item to its answer. A: Part marked X: Ovary; Part marked Y: Cervix; The part where fertilization takes place (mark N): Oviduct (fallopian tube); One disease that affects this organ: Gonorrhoea. X is the ovary, Y is the cervix, fertilization happens in the oviduct, and STDs like gonorrhoea attack this organ.
chunks.source: X is the ovary, Y is the cervix, fertilization happens in the oviduct, and STDs like gonorrhoea attack this organ.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the function of anthers in flowers similar to that of testes in humans? A: Both produce male gametes. Anthers make pollen (male gametes) just as testes make sperms.
chunks.source: Anthers make pollen (male gametes) just as testes make sperms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: One permanent method of birth control in males is ____. A: vasectomy. Vasectomy permanently blocks the sperm tubes in males.
chunks.source: Vasectomy permanently blocks the sperm tubes in males.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the developing foetus and match each item to its answer. A: The substance marked N: Amniotic fluid; Part marked K: The placenta; A use of the placenta to the foetus (1): Food passes from the mother to the foetus through it; A use of the placenta to the foetus (2): Oxygen passes to the foetus and wastes are removed through it. N is the protective amniotic fluid and K is the placenta, which feeds the foetus and removes wastes.
chunks.source: N is the protective amniotic fluid and K is the placenta, which feeds the foetus and removes wastes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why pregnant women are advised to feed on food rich in proteins. A: Proteins build the baby's body. Protein builds the growing baby's muscles and organs.
chunks.source: Protein builds the growing baby's muscles and organs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important for a husband and his wife to be treated together if they have gonorrhoea? A: So they do not re-infect each other. Treating only one partner lets the other re-infect the treated one.
chunks.source: Treating only one partner lets the other re-infect the treated one.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which sexually transmitted disease can cause blindness in babies? A: Gonorrhoea. Gonorrhoea caught during birth can infect a baby's eyes and cause blindness.
chunks.source: Gonorrhoea caught during birth can infect a baby's eyes and cause blindness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A signpost warns that AIDS kills. In which way is this message helpful to school children? A: It reminds them to abstain from sex so they do not get HIV/AIDS. AIDS awareness messages remind children to abstain and protect themselves from HIV.
chunks.source: AIDS awareness messages remind children to abstain and protect themselves from HIV.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which the umbilical cord is important to the developing foetus in the uterus. A: It connects the foetus to the placenta for food and oxygen. The umbilical cord carries food and oxygen from the placenta to the foetus.
chunks.source: The umbilical cord carries food and oxygen from the placenta to the foetus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way in which married couples can avoid HIV/AIDS among themselves. A: Being faithful to each other. Faithfulness between uninfected partners keeps HIV away.
chunks.source: Faithfulness between uninfected partners keeps HIV away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the human reproductive system, match each process to where it takes place, and give one use of the placenta. A: Implantation: In the uterus; Production of sperms: In the testes; Production of female hormones: In the ovaries; Conception (fertilization): In the oviduct; One use of the placenta during pregnancy: It passes food and oxygen from mother to foetus. Sperms form in testes, hormones in ovaries, fertilization in the oviduct, implantation in the uterus; the placenta feeds the foetus.
chunks.source: Sperms form in testes, hormones in ovaries, fertilization in the oviduct, implantation in the uterus; the placenta feeds the foetus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the human foetus in the uterus and match each item to its answer. A: Part marked Y: Amniotic fluid; Part marked Z: The foetus; The importance of part X (placenta): Food and oxygen pass from the mother to the foetus through it; The importance of part W (amniotic sac): It holds the fluid that protects the foetus from shock. Y is the protective fluid, Z is the baby, X (placenta) feeds it, and W (sac) holds the fluid.
chunks.source: Y is the protective fluid, Z is the baby, X (placenta) feeds it, and W (sac) holds the fluid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Arrange these processes of human reproduction in the correct order. A: Ovulation, Fertilization, Implantation, Pregnancy. First the ovum is released, then fertilized, then the embryo attaches, then pregnancy continues to birth.
chunks.source: First the ovum is released, then fertilized, then the embryo attaches, then pregnancy continues to birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Fertilization takes place in the uterus. True or False? A: False. Fertilization takes place in the oviduct; the embryo later implants in the uterus.
chunks.source: Fertilization takes place in the oviduct; the embryo later implants in the uterus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down two activities that help to promote good sanitation in a home. (Select two) A: Sweeping the compound, Slashing tall bushes around the home. Sweeping the compound and slashing bushes keep the home clean and remove hiding places for germs and pests. The other choices make sanitation worse.
chunks.source: Sweeping the compound and slashing bushes keep the home clean and remove hiding places for germs and pests. The other choices make sanitation worse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two diseases that may attack a family due to poor sanitation. (Select two) A: Cholera, Typhoid. Cholera and typhoid spread through dirty water and poor disposal of faeces. Measles, tetanus and polio spread in other ways.
chunks.source: Cholera and typhoid spread through dirty water and poor disposal of faeces. Measles, tetanus and polio spread in other ways.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it not necessary for a VIP latrine to have a lid for the hole? A: The vent pipe carries away bad smell and the screen keeps out flies. The vent pipe removes bad smell and the screen at its top traps flies, so no lid is needed. A lid would block the free flow of air.
chunks.source: The vent pipe removes bad smell and the screen at its top traps flies, so no lid is needed. A lid would block the free flow of air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it not good to pour paraffin in a pit latrine? A: It kills the bacteria that break down the waste. Bacteria in the pit decompose faeces. Paraffin kills these helpful bacteria, so the pit fills up faster.
chunks.source: Bacteria in the pit decompose faeces. Paraffin kills these helpful bacteria, so the pit fills up faster.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should pit latrines be smoked from time to time? A: To kill germs and keep away flies. Smoke kills germs and drives away flies, which keeps the latrine cleaner and healthier.
chunks.source: Smoke kills germs and drives away flies, which keeps the latrine cleaner and healthier.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one advantage of a VIP latrine over an ordinary pit latrine. A: The vent pipe removes bad smell. The vent pipe carries bad-smelling air above the roof, so a VIP latrine smells less than an ordinary pit latrine.
chunks.source: The vent pipe carries bad-smelling air above the roof, so a VIP latrine smells less than an ordinary pit latrine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the recommended minimum distance between a drinking water source and a VIP latrine? A: 30 metres. A latrine should be at least 30 metres from a drinking water source so that germs from the pit do not reach the water.
chunks.source: A latrine should be at least 30 metres from a drinking water source so that germs from the pit do not reach the water.

chunks.subject: Science
