chunks.text: Q: Why should the squat hole of an ordinary pit latrine be covered? A: To prevent flies from entering and spreading germs. A cover stops flies from getting into the pit and carrying germs to food. It also reduces bad smell.
chunks.source: A cover stops flies from getting into the pit and carrying germs to food. It also reduces bad smell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one difference between an ordinary pit latrine and a VIP latrine. A: A VIP latrine has a vent pipe while an ordinary pit latrine does not. The vent pipe is the main feature that makes a latrine a VIP (Ventilated Improved Pit) latrine.
chunks.source: The vent pipe is the main feature that makes a latrine a VIP (Ventilated Improved Pit) latrine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a vent pipe help to reduce bad smell in a VIP latrine? A: It lets the bad-smelling air escape above the roof. Warm smelly air rises through the vent pipe and escapes above the roof, while fresh air enters through the squat hole.
chunks.source: Warm smelly air rises through the vent pipe and escapes above the roof, while fresh air enters through the squat hole.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is a dust bin important in a classroom? A: It collects rubbish and keeps the classroom clean. A dustbin gives litter a proper place, so the classroom stays clean and healthy.
chunks.source: A dustbin gives litter a proper place, so the classroom stays clean and healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two reasons for placing utensils on a rack. (Select two) A: To allow the utensils to dry well, To keep utensils away from dust and germs. A rack lets air dry the utensils and keeps them off the dirty ground, away from dust and germs.
chunks.source: A rack lets air dry the utensils and keeps them off the dirty ground, away from dust and germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should a rack be constructed with a stand at least 1 (one) metre above the ground? A: To keep the utensils away from dust and animals. Raising the rack keeps utensils away from dust on the ground and from animals that could dirty them.
chunks.source: Raising the rack keeps utensils away from dust on the ground and from animals that could dirty them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger of leaving utensils for a long time outside on a rack. A: Dust and germs settle on them. Utensils left outside collect dust and germs, which can contaminate food served in them.
chunks.source: Utensils left outside collect dust and germs, which can contaminate food served in them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the Ventilated Improved Pit (VIP) latrine. Name the part marked M. A: The screen (cap) at the top of the vent pipe. M labels the small screen at the very top of the vent pipe. It lets air out but keeps flies from entering or leaving through the pipe.
chunks.source: M labels the small screen at the very top of the vent pipe. It lets air out but keeps flies from entering or leaving through the pipe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the Ventilated Improved Pit (VIP) latrine. Name the part marked N. A: The vent pipe. N labels the tall pipe that carries smelly air from the pit to above the roof. That pipe is called the vent pipe.
chunks.source: N labels the tall pipe that carries smelly air from the pit to above the roof. That pipe is called the vent pipe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the Ventilated Improved Pit (VIP) latrine. Give the function of the part marked M. A: It prevents flies from entering or leaving through the vent pipe. The screen at the top of the vent pipe traps flies, so they cannot enter or leave through the pipe and spread germs.
chunks.source: The screen at the top of the vent pipe traps flies, so they cannot enter or leave through the pipe and spread germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the Ventilated Improved Pit (VIP) latrine. What do the arrows in the diagram show? A: The movement of air through the vent pipe. The arrows show air flowing: fresh air enters through the squat hole and smelly air rises out through the vent pipe.
chunks.source: The arrows show air flowing: fresh air enters through the squat hole and smelly air rises out through the vent pipe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two activities done to promote sanitation in a home. (Select two) A: Sweeping the compound, Proper disposal of rubbish. Sweeping and proper rubbish disposal keep the home clean. The other choices spread germs and diseases.
chunks.source: Sweeping and proper rubbish disposal keep the home clean. The other choices spread germs and diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What advice would you give to a person wishing to construct a pit latrine at his home? A: Build it at least 30 metres from the water source and 10 metres from the house. A latrine 30 metres from water keeps germs out of drinking water, and 10 metres from the house keeps smell and flies away.
chunks.source: A latrine 30 metres from water keeps germs out of drinking water, and 10 metres from the house keeps smell and flies away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one characteristic of a Ventilated Improved Pit latrine. A: It has a vent pipe with a fly screen at the top. The vent pipe with a screen is what makes a latrine a VIP latrine. It needs no lid because air must flow freely.
chunks.source: The vent pipe with a screen is what makes a latrine a VIP latrine. It needs no lid because air must flow freely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of draining stagnant water in a compound. A: It removes breeding places for mosquitoes. Mosquitoes lay their eggs in stagnant water. Draining it removes their breeding places and reduces malaria.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in stagnant water. Draining it removes their breeding places and reduces malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why people should use latrines properly. A: To prevent the spread of diseases. Using latrines properly keeps faeces away from people, water and food, which stops diseases from spreading.
chunks.source: Using latrines properly keeps faeces away from people, water and food, which stops diseases from spreading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two materials used while constructing a latrine. (Select two) A: Bricks, Cement. Bricks and cement make the walls and floor of a latrine strong. Paper, leaves and plastic bags are too weak.
chunks.source: Bricks and cement make the walls and floor of a latrine strong. Paper, leaves and plastic bags are too weak.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What good health habit should be practiced after visiting a latrine or toilet? A: Washing hands with soap and clean water. Hands pick up germs in the latrine. Washing with soap and clean water removes the germs before they reach food or the mouth.
chunks.source: Hands pick up germs in the latrine. Washing with soap and clean water removes the germs before they reach food or the mouth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of slashing tall bushes around our homes. A: It removes hiding and breeding places for mosquitoes and other dangerous animals. Tall bushes hide mosquitoes, snakes and other dangerous animals. Slashing them keeps the home safe.
chunks.source: Tall bushes hide mosquitoes, snakes and other dangerous animals. Slashing them keeps the home safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a Ventilated Improved Pit latrine left without a cover? A: To allow the free flow of air through the vent pipe. Air must flow freely in through the squat hole and out through the vent pipe. A cover would block this air flow.
chunks.source: Air must flow freely in through the squat hole and out through the vent pipe. A cover would block this air flow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why a latrine should be 10 metres away from the living house. A: To keep bad smell and flies away from the house. A latrine 10 metres from the house keeps its smell away and stops flies from carrying germs from the latrine to food in the house.
chunks.source: A latrine 10 metres from the house keeps its smell away and stops flies from carrying germs from the latrine to food in the house.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of water in a water borne toilet. A: It carries the waste into the septic tank. Water flushes the waste from the toilet bowl into the septic tank, where it is stored and broken down.
chunks.source: Water flushes the waste from the toilet bowl into the septic tank, where it is stored and broken down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How important is a septic tank in a home? A: It safely stores and breaks down waste from the water borne toilet. The septic tank receives waste flushed from the toilet and lets bacteria break it down safely underground.
chunks.source: The septic tank receives waste flushed from the toilet and lets bacteria break it down safely underground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one problem faced by people who use water borne toilets. A: They need a constant supply of water. A water borne toilet cannot flush without water, so homes without piped water struggle to use it.
chunks.source: A water borne toilet cannot flush without water, so homes without piped water struggle to use it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should a latrine be constructed with a strong floor? A: To prevent the floor from collapsing while in use. A weak floor can break and drop the user into the pit. A strong floor supports users safely.
chunks.source: A weak floor can break and drop the user into the pit. A strong floor supports users safely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Our school pit latrine smells a lot and is always full of flies. What measure can we take to prevent this situation? A: Smoke it regularly and always keep the squat hole covered. Smoking kills germs and drives away flies, while covering the hole stops flies entering and reduces smell.
chunks.source: Smoking kills germs and drives away flies, while covering the hole stops flies entering and reduces smell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down two activities that can be done by an individual to promote personal hygiene. (Select two) A: Bathing daily, Brushing teeth regularly. Bathing and brushing teeth keep the body clean. The other choices spread germs and dirt.
chunks.source: Bathing and brushing teeth keep the body clean. The other choices spread germs and dirt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one effect of poor disposal of human wastes in the environment. A: It leads to the spread of diseases. Poorly disposed human waste contaminates water, food and soil, spreading diseases like cholera and typhoid.
chunks.source: Poorly disposed human waste contaminates water, food and soil, spreading diseases like cholera and typhoid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one reason why people working in dirty areas should wear gumboots. A: To protect their feet from germs, cuts and harmful objects. Dirty areas hide sharp objects, germs and chemicals. Gumboots shield the feet from injury and infection.
chunks.source: Dirty areas hide sharp objects, germs and chemicals. Gumboots shield the feet from injury and infection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two signs of poor sanitation in a school. (Select two) A: Bad smell around the latrines, Rubbish scattered in the compound. Bad smell and scattered rubbish show that waste is not handled well. The other choices show good sanitation.
chunks.source: Bad smell and scattered rubbish show that waste is not handled well. The other choices show good sanitation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which proper disposal of wastes is important in our environment. A: It prevents the spread of diseases. Proper waste disposal keeps germs away from people, water and food, so diseases do not spread.
chunks.source: Proper waste disposal keeps germs away from people, water and food, so diseases do not spread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the hand washing tool used in rural areas. Name the sanitation tool drawn in the diagram. A: Tippy tap. The diagram shows a tippy tap: a water container on a stand with soap nearby, used for washing hands in rural homes.
chunks.source: The diagram shows a tippy tap: a water container on a stand with soap nearby, used for washing hands in rural homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the hand washing tool. How does the above tool help to prevent the spread of diarrhoeal diseases in a home? A: It provides water and soap for washing hands after visiting the latrine. Washing hands with soap at the tippy tap removes germs picked up in the latrine, so diarrhoeal diseases do not spread.
chunks.source: Washing hands with soap at the tippy tap removes germs picked up in the latrine, so diarrhoeal diseases do not spread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the hand washing tool. Give any two local materials that can be used for making the above tool. (Select two) A: A jerrycan (plastic container), Wooden poles. A tippy tap is made from a jerrycan hung on wooden poles. Glass, iron bars and cement blocks are not normally used.
chunks.source: A tippy tap is made from a jerrycan hung on wooden poles. Glass, iron bars and cement blocks are not normally used.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the hand washing tool. Apart from a latrine, name any other place where the above tool can be placed. A: Near the kitchen. A tippy tap near the kitchen lets people wash hands before handling food, which prevents diseases.
chunks.source: A tippy tap near the kitchen lets people wash hands before handling food, which prevents diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is Primary Health Care? A: Essential health care made available to all people in a community. Primary Health Care is basic health care that every person in the community can reach and afford.
chunks.source: Primary Health Care is basic health care that every person in the community can reach and afford.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two elements of Primary Health Care. (Select two) A: Immunisation, Water and sanitation. Immunisation and water and sanitation are core PHC elements. Roads, markets and football are not health care elements.
chunks.source: Immunisation and water and sanitation are core PHC elements. Roads, markets and football are not health care elements.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two elements of Primary Health Care. (Select two) A: Maternal and child health, Health education. Maternal and child health and health education are PHC elements. Music, farming and trading are not.
chunks.source: Maternal and child health and health education are PHC elements. Music, farming and trading are not.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write PHC in full. A: Primary Health Care. PHC stands for Primary Health Care.
chunks.source: PHC stands for Primary Health Care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two ways an individual can participate in Primary Health Care. (Select two) A: Immunising children, Keeping the home clean. Immunising children and keeping the home clean support community health. The other choices harm health.
chunks.source: Immunising children and keeping the home clean support community health. The other choices harm health.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write CDD in full. A: Control of Diarrhoeal Diseases. In Primary Health Care, CDD stands for Control of Diarrhoeal Diseases, one of the PHC elements.
chunks.source: In Primary Health Care, CDD stands for Control of Diarrhoeal Diseases, one of the PHC elements.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two ways a pregnant woman benefits from maternal and child health care. (Select two) A: She is checked for diseases during pregnancy, She is advised on proper feeding. Maternal health care checks the mother and baby for diseases and teaches proper feeding. It does not give farm tools or clothes.
chunks.source: Maternal health care checks the mother and baby for diseases and teaches proper feeding. It does not give farm tools or clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two ways the community can promote primary health care. (Select two) A: Building health centres, Immunising children. Health centres and immunisation bring health care to the community. The other choices work against health.
chunks.source: Health centres and immunisation bring health care to the community. The other choices work against health.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two ways of caring for people with special needs. (Select two) A: Feeding them, Taking them to hospital when sick. People with special needs should be fed and treated when sick, like everyone else. Neglect and heavy work harm them.
chunks.source: People with special needs should be fed and treated when sick, like everyone else. Neglect and heavy work harm them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of promoting PHC in a community. A: It helps to prevent diseases in the community. PHC focuses on preventing diseases, so fewer people fall sick.
chunks.source: PHC focuses on preventing diseases, so fewer people fall sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it advisable to brush our teeth after every meal? A: To remove food particles that cause tooth decay. Food left on teeth feeds germs that rot the teeth. Brushing removes the food remains.
chunks.source: Food left on teeth feeds germs that rot the teeth. Brushing removes the food remains.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two ways a family can promote immunization. (Select two) A: Taking babies for immunisation on time, Keeping the child health card safely. Timely immunisation and a safe health card keep the baby protected. The other choices put the baby at risk.
chunks.source: Timely immunisation and a safe health card keep the baby protected. The other choices put the baby at risk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way water sources can be protected from contamination. A: Fencing the water source. A fence keeps people and animals from stepping into or dirtying the water source.
chunks.source: A fence keeps people and animals from stepping into or dirtying the water source.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one healthy life style. A: Feeding on a balanced diet. A balanced diet keeps the body strong and healthy. Smoking, alcohol and laziness harm health.
chunks.source: A balanced diet keeps the body strong and healthy. Smoking, alcohol and laziness harm health.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why a person should have enough rest. A: It relaxes the body and keeps it healthy. Rest lets the body recover its energy and grow well.
chunks.source: Rest lets the body recover its energy and grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two people with special needs in a community. (Select two) A: The disabled, The elderly. The disabled and the elderly need extra care. Footballers, traders and drivers are not groups with special needs.
chunks.source: The disabled and the elderly need extra care. Footballers, traders and drivers are not groups with special needs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it necessary to brush teeth after every meal? A: To remove food remains that germs feed on. Germs feed on food remains and produce acids that rot teeth. Brushing removes their food.
chunks.source: Germs feed on food remains and produce acids that rot teeth. Brushing removes their food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one activity that a teacher can do during a health parade in a school to promote health. A: Inspecting pupils' nails, teeth and uniforms. During a health parade the teacher checks that every pupil is clean, which encourages personal hygiene.
chunks.source: During a health parade the teacher checks that every pupil is clean, which encourages personal hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: As a pupil and member of the school health committee, what would you do to improve health in the school? A: Ensure the compound and latrines are kept clean. A clean compound and clean latrines keep germs away from pupils.
chunks.source: A clean compound and clean latrines keep germs away from pupils.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why parents should take their children for immunization. A: To protect them against immunisable diseases. Immunisation builds immunity that protects children against killer diseases like polio and measles.
chunks.source: Immunisation builds immunity that protects children against killer diseases like polio and measles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain what ante-natal care is. A: The care given to a pregnant woman before the baby is born. 'Ante' means before and 'natal' means birth, so ante-natal care is care before birth.
chunks.source: 'Ante' means before and 'natal' means birth, so ante-natal care is care before birth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why an individual should promote personal hygiene. A: It prevents the spread of diseases. A clean body keeps germs away, so diseases do not spread.
chunks.source: A clean body keeps germs away, so diseases do not spread.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is a pool of water near a home likely to be a source of malaria to the people in that home? A: It acts as a breeding place for mosquitoes. Mosquitoes lay eggs in stagnant pools. The mosquitoes that grow there spread malaria.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes lay eggs in stagnant pools. The mosquitoes that grow there spread malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way a P.7 pupil can help in the control of polio in a community. A: Encouraging parents to take babies for polio immunisation. Polio drops protect babies. A pupil can remind parents to take babies for immunisation.
chunks.source: Polio drops protect babies. A pupil can remind parents to take babies for immunisation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why people should cut their finger nails short. A: Dirt and germs hide under long nails. Germs and dirt collect under long nails and enter food when we eat. Short nails stay cleaner.
chunks.source: Germs and dirt collect under long nails and enter food when we eat. Short nails stay cleaner.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two activities one should carry out in order to ensure proper sanitation at home. (Select two) A: Sweeping the compound, Proper disposal of rubbish. Sweeping and proper rubbish disposal keep the home sanitary. The other choices spread germs.
chunks.source: Sweeping and proper rubbish disposal keep the home sanitary. The other choices spread germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one practice in a community that can help to prevent the spread of communicable diseases. A: Immunising children. Immunisation stops communicable diseases from spreading from person to person.
chunks.source: Immunisation stops communicable diseases from spreading from person to person.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one proper way of disposing of rubbish in a home. A: Throwing it in a rubbish pit. A rubbish pit keeps waste in one place, away from people, food and water.
chunks.source: A rubbish pit keeps waste in one place, away from people, food and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does immunisation promote health in a child? A: It protects the child against immunisable diseases. Vaccines build immunity, so the child does not catch immunisable diseases.
chunks.source: Vaccines build immunity, so the child does not catch immunisable diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should communities fence open spring wells? A: To stop people and animals from contaminating the water. A fence keeps dirty feet, animals and rubbish out of the spring water.
chunks.source: A fence keeps dirty feet, animals and rubbish out of the spring water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one activity the community can do to reduce road accidents. A: Putting speed humps on the road. Speed humps force drivers to slow down, which reduces accidents.
chunks.source: Speed humps force drivers to slow down, which reduces accidents.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one Primary Health Care activity children can do to help their mothers when cooking. A: Fetching water. Fetching water is a helpful PHC activity children can do while mothers cook.
chunks.source: Fetching water is a helpful PHC activity children can do while mothers cook.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down two health care activities that can be provided to the elderly in our homes. (Select two) A: Feeding them, Washing their clothes. The elderly should be fed and kept clean. Heavy work, neglect and shouting harm them.
chunks.source: The elderly should be fed and kept clean. Heavy work, neglect and shouting harm them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: You are a health prefect in your school. Give one activity you would do during a health parade. A: Inspecting the cleanliness of fellow pupils. A health prefect checks nails, teeth, hair and uniforms to encourage cleanliness.
chunks.source: A health prefect checks nails, teeth, hair and uniforms to encourage cleanliness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which health education is important in controlling overpopulation. A: It teaches family planning methods. Health education teaches family planning, which helps families have the number of children they can care for.
chunks.source: Health education teaches family planning, which helps families have the number of children they can care for.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two reasons why it is important to wash hands before eating food. (Select two) A: To remove germs from the hands, To remove dirt from the hands. Hands carry germs and dirt that cause diseases when they reach food. Washing removes both.
chunks.source: Hands carry germs and dirt that cause diseases when they reach food. Washing removes both.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from washing hands, mention any two other activities one can do to maintain personal hygiene. (Select two) A: Bathing daily, Brushing teeth regularly. Bathing and brushing teeth keep the body clean. The other choices spread dirt and germs.
chunks.source: Bathing and brushing teeth keep the body clean. The other choices spread dirt and germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which Primary Health Care (PHC) is important to the community. A: It prevents diseases in the community. PHC prevents diseases, so the community stays healthy and spends less on treatment.
chunks.source: PHC prevents diseases, so the community stays healthy and spends less on treatment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the element of Primary Health Care promoted by this activity: Sweeping the kitchen. A: Water and sanitation. Sweeping keeps the surroundings clean, which belongs to the water and sanitation element of PHC.
chunks.source: Sweeping keeps the surroundings clean, which belongs to the water and sanitation element of PHC.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the element of Primary Health Care promoted by this activity: Putting drops of polio vaccine into the mouth of a child. A: Immunisation. Giving polio drops is immunisation: it protects the child against polio.
chunks.source: Giving polio drops is immunisation: it protects the child against polio.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the element of Primary Health Care promoted by this activity: Eating a balanced diet. A: Nutrition. Eating a balanced diet belongs to the nutrition element: food supply and proper feeding.
chunks.source: Eating a balanced diet belongs to the nutrition element: food supply and proper feeding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from pregnant mothers, young and disabled people, give any one other group of people who need special care in a family. A: The elderly. Old people are weak and need extra care, like pregnant mothers, the young and the disabled.
chunks.source: Old people are weak and need extra care, like pregnant mothers, the young and the disabled.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from ante-natal care, give two other ways of caring for pregnant women. (Select two) A: Feeding them on a balanced diet, Taking them to hospital for check-ups. Good feeding and hospital check-ups keep mother and baby healthy. Heavy work, smoking and denying food harm them.
chunks.source: Good feeding and hospital check-ups keep mother and baby healthy. Heavy work, smoking and denying food harm them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are pregnant women advised not to smoke? A: Smoking can harm the unborn baby. Chemicals in cigarette smoke reach the unborn baby through the mother and can damage its growth.
chunks.source: Chemicals in cigarette smoke reach the unborn baby through the mother and can damage its growth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one habit which helps to promote oral health. A: Brushing teeth regularly. Regular brushing removes food and germs, keeping teeth and gums healthy.
chunks.source: Regular brushing removes food and germs, keeping teeth and gums healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one disadvantage of keeping finger nails long. A: Dirt and germs collect under them. Long nails trap dirt and germs, which can enter food and cause diseases.
chunks.source: Long nails trap dirt and germs, which can enter food and cause diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State two ways community members can promote sanitation in their area. (Select two) A: Slashing bushes, Draining stagnant water. Slashing bushes and draining stagnant water remove hiding and breeding places for pests. The other choices spread disease.
chunks.source: Slashing bushes and draining stagnant water remove hiding and breeding places for pests. The other choices spread disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two ways in which Primary Health Care (PHC) is an important programme in the community. (Select two) A: It prevents diseases, It reduces death rates. By preventing diseases, PHC saves lives and reduces deaths in the community.
chunks.source: By preventing diseases, PHC saves lives and reduces deaths in the community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two roles of a school health committee. (Select two) A: Ensuring the school compound is clean, Organising health parades. A school health committee keeps the school clean and organises health parades. It does not punish pupils or collect fees.
chunks.source: A school health committee keeps the school clean and organises health parades. It does not punish pupils or collect fees.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two conditions in which women are vulnerable. (Select two) A: Pregnancy, Breastfeeding. During pregnancy and breastfeeding a woman's body needs extra care and food, so she is vulnerable.
chunks.source: During pregnancy and breastfeeding a woman's body needs extra care and food, so she is vulnerable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State two ways in which family members can care for vulnerable women. (Select two) A: Giving them enough food, Taking them to hospital when sick. Vulnerable women need enough food and medical care. Overwork, abuse and isolation harm them.
chunks.source: Vulnerable women need enough food and medical care. Overwork, abuse and isolation harm them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which element of Primary Health Care helps to prevent tooth decay? A: Nutrition. Proper nutrition, eating a balanced diet low in sugary foods, helps to prevent tooth decay.
chunks.source: Proper nutrition, eating a balanced diet low in sugary foods, helps to prevent tooth decay.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is this element of Primary Health Care important to the community: Water and sanitation? A: It helps to prevent water-borne diseases. Clean water and proper sanitation stop germs reaching people, so water-borne diseases are prevented.
chunks.source: Clean water and proper sanitation stop germs reaching people, so water-borne diseases are prevented.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way is this element of Primary Health Care important to the community: Maternal and Child health? A: It reduces deaths of mothers and babies. Care for pregnant women and babies prevents complications, so fewer mothers and babies die.
chunks.source: Care for pregnant women and babies prevents complications, so fewer mothers and babies die.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two health care services which are provided through maternal and child health. (Select two) A: Immunisation of babies, Ante-natal care for pregnant women. Maternal and child health provides immunisation and ante-natal care. Roads, adult classes and markets are not health services.
chunks.source: Maternal and child health provides immunisation and ante-natal care. Roads, adult classes and markets are not health services.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one use of a razor blade in promoting personal hygiene. A: Shaving unwanted hair. A razor blade is used for shaving unwanted hair as part of personal hygiene.
chunks.source: A razor blade is used for shaving unwanted hair as part of personal hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two reasons why physical exercises are important to our bodies. (Select two) A: They keep the body fit and strong, They improve blood circulation. Exercise strengthens the body and helps blood move well. It does not cause disease or waste time.
chunks.source: Exercise strengthens the body and helps blood move well. It does not cause disease or waste time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger of poor disposal of human wastes. A: It leads to the spread of diseases. Poorly disposed human waste spreads germs through water, food, flies and soil.
chunks.source: Poorly disposed human waste spreads germs through water, food, flies and soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State two ways water in the community gets contaminated. (Select two) A: Dumping rubbish in water sources, Animals drinking directly from the source. Rubbish and animals dirty the water. Boiling, fencing and covering protect water instead.
chunks.source: Rubbish and animals dirty the water. Boiling, fencing and covering protect water instead.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should every home have a latrine? A: To ensure proper disposal of faeces. A latrine gives every home a safe place for faeces, keeping germs away from people, food and water.
chunks.source: A latrine gives every home a safe place for faeces, keeping germs away from people, food and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one duty of the family in promoting Primary Health Care. A: Taking children for immunisation. A family's duty in PHC includes taking children for immunisation so they are protected against diseases.
chunks.source: A family's duty in PHC includes taking children for immunisation so they are protected against diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is personal hygiene? A: The practice of keeping one's body clean. Personal hygiene means keeping your own body clean through habits like bathing and brushing teeth.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene means keeping your own body clean through habits like bathing and brushing teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest any two importance of personal hygiene. (Select two) A: It prevents diseases, It makes one look smart and clean. Personal hygiene keeps germs away and makes a person look neat. It does not waste water or cause disease.
chunks.source: Personal hygiene keeps germs away and makes a person look neat. It does not waste water or cause disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two ways of keeping our bodies clean. (Select two) A: Bathing daily, Washing hands with soap. Bathing and washing hands with soap clean the body. Dirty clothes, unbrushed teeth and shared towels spread dirt and germs.
chunks.source: Bathing and washing hands with soap clean the body. Dirty clothes, unbrushed teeth and shared towels spread dirt and germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List down any two items used to promote personal hygiene. (Select two) A: Soap, Toothbrush. Soap and a toothbrush are used to clean the body and teeth. Dirty water, mud and used towels are not clean.
chunks.source: Soap and a toothbrush are used to clean the body and teeth. Dirty water, mud and used towels are not clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the habit of cutting finger nails short important to an individual? A: It prevents dirt and germs from hiding under the nails. Short nails do not trap dirt and germs, so food stays safe when we eat with our hands.
chunks.source: Short nails do not trap dirt and germs, so food stays safe when we eat with our hands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the habit of grooming hair important to an individual? A: It removes dirt and prevents parasites like lice. Groomed hair is free of dirt and lice, which keeps the scalp healthy.
chunks.source: Groomed hair is free of dirt and lice, which keeps the scalp healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the habit of washing hands before eating important to an individual? A: It removes germs that can cause diseases. Hands carry germs that cause diseases when they reach food. Washing removes them.
chunks.source: Hands carry germs that cause diseases when they reach food. Washing removes them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Suggest one reason why people iron clothes and beddings. A: To kill germs and parasites in them. The heat of the iron kills germs and parasites hiding in clothes and beddings.
chunks.source: The heat of the iron kills germs and parasites hiding in clothes and beddings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: A primary four child ate an unwashed mango in the morning. Identify any two diseases he is likely to suffer from. (Select two) A: Cholera, Typhoid. Unwashed fruit can carry germs that cause cholera and typhoid. Malaria, measles and tetanus spread in other ways.
chunks.source: Unwashed fruit can carry germs that cause cholera and typhoid. Malaria, measles and tetanus spread in other ways.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are people advised to wash their hands with soap? A: To remove germs from the hands. Soap kills and washes away germs that water alone cannot remove.
chunks.source: Soap kills and washes away germs that water alone cannot remove.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should people brush their teeth regularly? A: To prevent tooth decay. Brushing removes food and germs that rot the teeth.
chunks.source: Brushing removes food and germs that rot the teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one use of a razor blade in promoting personal hygiene. A: Shaving unwanted hair. A razor blade shaves unwanted hair, which is part of keeping the body clean.
chunks.source: A razor blade shaves unwanted hair, which is part of keeping the body clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which one way does toothpaste promote oral health? A: It removes germs and food particles from the teeth. Toothpaste cleans germs and food off the teeth and strengthens them.
chunks.source: Toothpaste cleans germs and food off the teeth and strengthens them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any two activities that can be done by an individual to promote personal hygiene. (Select two) A: Bathing daily, Brushing teeth regularly. Bathing and brushing teeth keep the body clean. The other choices spread dirt and germs.
chunks.source: Bathing and brushing teeth keep the body clean. The other choices spread dirt and germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one habit which helps to promote oral health. A: Brushing teeth after meals. Brushing after meals removes food that germs would feed on, keeping teeth healthy.
chunks.source: Brushing after meals removes food that germs would feed on, keeping teeth healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two reasons why it is important to wash hands before eating food. (Select two) A: To remove germs from the hands, To prevent diarrhoeal diseases. Washing removes germs, which prevents diarrhoeal diseases that spread through dirty hands.
chunks.source: Washing removes germs, which prevents diarrhoeal diseases that spread through dirty hands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from washing hands, mention any two other activities one can do to maintain personal hygiene. (Select two) A: Bathing daily, Cutting finger nails short. Bathing and short nails keep the body clean. Sharing toothbrushes and dirty habits spread germs.
chunks.source: Bathing and short nails keep the body clean. Sharing toothbrushes and dirty habits spread germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one item used for cleaning hands after visiting a latrine or toilet. A: Soap. Soap (with clean water) kills and removes the germs picked up in the latrine.
chunks.source: Soap (with clean water) kills and removes the germs picked up in the latrine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one piece of advice you can give to a friend in order to promote their personal hygiene. A: Always bathe daily. Daily bathing keeps the body clean and free of germs and bad smell.
chunks.source: Daily bathing keeps the body clean and free of germs and bad smell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which health parades can help to maintain personal hygiene in school children. A: They encourage pupils to keep their bodies clean. Health parades check and remind pupils to stay clean, which builds the habit of personal hygiene.
chunks.source: Health parades check and remind pupils to stay clean, which builds the habit of personal hygiene.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What good health habit should be practiced after visiting a latrine or toilet? A: Washing hands with soap and clean water. Hands pick up germs in the latrine. Washing with soap and clean water removes them.
chunks.source: Hands pick up germs in the latrine. Washing with soap and clean water removes them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one disease spread through poor personal hygiene. A: Cholera. Cholera spreads through dirty hands, water and food, which poor personal hygiene allows.
chunks.source: Cholera spreads through dirty hands, water and food, which poor personal hygiene allows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one method used to make dirty water clean. A: Filtration. Filtration passes dirty water through layers like sand and charcoal, which trap the dirt.
chunks.source: Filtration passes dirty water through layers like sand and charcoal, which trap the dirt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the method that can be used to separate fruit seeds from juice. A: Filtration. Pouring juice through a filter leaves the seeds behind while the juice passes through.
chunks.source: Pouring juice through a filter leaves the seeds behind while the juice passes through.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the method that can be used to separate millet seeds mixed with its husks. A: Winnowing. Winnowing tosses the mixture in air so the wind blows away the light husks and the heavy seeds fall down.
chunks.source: Winnowing tosses the mixture in air so the wind blows away the light husks and the heavy seeds fall down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the importance of sorting clothes before washing them at home. A: It prevents coloured clothes from staining white ones. Sorting separates white clothes from coloured ones so colours do not run and spoil other clothes.
chunks.source: Sorting separates white clothes from coloured ones so colours do not run and spoil other clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the importance of soaking clothes before washing them at home. A: It loosens dirt for easy washing. Soaking softens and loosens dirt so that less effort and soap are needed to wash.
chunks.source: Soaking softens and loosens dirt so that less effort and soap are needed to wash.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is water obtained by distillation method not good for drinking? A: It does not contain mineral salts needed by the body. Distillation removes everything from water, including the mineral salts our bodies need.
chunks.source: Distillation removes everything from water, including the mineral salts our bodies need.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which method of making water clean do you first allow the impurities to settle at the bottom of a container? A: Decantation. In decantation, dirty water is left to stand so impurities settle, then the clean water on top is gently poured off.
chunks.source: In decantation, dirty water is left to stand so impurities settle, then the clean water on top is gently poured off.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is water obtained through filtration not necessarily safe for drinking? A: Filtration does not remove germs. Filters trap dirt but tiny germs pass through, so filtered water must still be boiled before drinking.
chunks.source: Filters trap dirt but tiny germs pass through, so filtered water must still be boiled before drinking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of wringing clothes during washing. A: It can tear or weaken the clothes. Twisting clothes hard in wringing stretches and weakens the fabric, so clothes tear easily.
chunks.source: Twisting clothes hard in wringing stretches and weakens the fabric, so clothes tear easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two water borne diseases. (Select two) A: Cholera, Typhoid. Cholera and typhoid spread through dirty drinking water. Malaria spreads through mosquitoes, measles through air, and polio through contaminated food or water but is grouped as immunisable.
chunks.source: Cholera and typhoid spread through dirty drinking water. Malaria spreads through mosquitoes, measles through air, and polio through contaminated food or water but is grouped as immunisable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which two ways can water borne diseases be prevented in the community? (Select two) A: Boiling drinking water, Protecting water sources from contamination. Boiling kills germs and protected sources stay clean. The other choices contaminate water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs and protected sources stay clean. The other choices contaminate water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should communities fence open spring wells? A: To stop people and animals from contaminating the water. A fence keeps dirty feet, animals and rubbish out of the spring water.
chunks.source: A fence keeps dirty feet, animals and rubbish out of the spring water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the simple method of making water clean. Name the method used above. A: Filtration. The diagram shows dirty water passing through layers of stones, sand and charcoal, which is filtration.
chunks.source: The diagram shows dirty water passing through layers of stones, sand and charcoal, which is filtration.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the simple method of making water clean. Apart from the coarse stones, name any two other local materials placed in container T. (Select two) A: Fine sand, Charcoal. The filter layers are coarse stones, fine sand and charcoal (with cotton). Salt, sugar and oil are not filter materials.
chunks.source: The filter layers are coarse stones, fine sand and charcoal (with cotton). Salt, sugar and oil are not filter materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the simple method of making water clean. Why should the clean water obtained in container S be boiled before drinking? A: To kill the germs that filtration does not remove. Filtration removes dirt but not germs, so boiling is needed to kill the germs and make the water safe.
chunks.source: Filtration removes dirt but not germs, so boiling is needed to kill the germs and make the water safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one factor considered when sorting clothes for washing. A: Colour. Clothes are sorted by colour so that coloured clothes do not stain white ones.
chunks.source: Clothes are sorted by colour so that coloured clothes do not stain white ones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one chemical used to treat water for drinking. A: Chlorine. Chlorine kills germs in drinking water.
chunks.source: Chlorine kills germs in drinking water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one danger of hanging clothes under direct sunlight. A: Strong sunlight fades the colour of clothes. Very strong sunshine bleaches and fades the colours of clothes.
chunks.source: Very strong sunshine bleaches and fades the colours of clothes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two ways in which water gets contaminated by the community. (Select two) A: Dumping rubbish in water sources, Washing clothes in water sources. Rubbish and washing dirty the water. Boiling, fencing and covering protect water.
chunks.source: Rubbish and washing dirty the water. Boiling, fencing and covering protect water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from decanting, give any other way clean water can be obtained from contaminated water. A: Filtration. Filtration passes water through layers that trap dirt, giving clean water.
chunks.source: Filtration passes water through layers that trap dirt, giving clean water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is water pollution? A: Making water dirty with harmful substances. Water pollution is the contamination of water by sewage, chemicals, rubbish and other harmful substances.
chunks.source: Water pollution is the contamination of water by sewage, chemicals, rubbish and other harmful substances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two pollutants of water. (Select two) A: Sewage, Industrial chemicals. Sewage and industrial chemicals poison water. Clean rain, oxygen and sunlight do not pollute water.
chunks.source: Sewage and industrial chemicals poison water. Clean rain, oxygen and sunlight do not pollute water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is borehole water safer to drink than well water? A: It is drawn from deep underground where it is less contaminated. Boreholes tap water deep underground, where soil filters it and germs rarely reach.
chunks.source: Boreholes tap water deep underground, where soil filters it and germs rarely reach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does a wet cloth spread on a line inside a house dry? A: The water in it evaporates. Water in the wet cloth slowly changes into vapour and escapes into the air, so the cloth dries.
chunks.source: Water in the wet cloth slowly changes into vapour and escapes into the air, so the cloth dries.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the main source of water in the environment? A: Rain. Rain feeds wells, rivers and underground water. It is the main source of all water in the environment.
chunks.source: Rain feeds wells, rivers and underground water. It is the main source of all water in the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the force that enables rain to fall from the sky. A: Gravity. Gravity pulls everything, including rain drops, down towards the earth.
chunks.source: Gravity pulls everything, including rain drops, down towards the earth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does boiling water make it safe for drinking? A: Boiling kills the germs in water. The heat of boiling kills the germs that cause water borne diseases.
chunks.source: The heat of boiling kills the germs that cause water borne diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of washing clothes with soap. A: Soap helps to remove dirt from clothes. Soap loosens dirt and grease so they wash out of the fabric easily.
chunks.source: Soap loosens dirt and grease so they wash out of the fabric easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one disadvantage of making water safe for drinking using chlorine. A: Chlorine gives water an unpleasant taste. Water treated with chlorine can taste and smell unpleasant, though it is safe to drink.
chunks.source: Water treated with chlorine can taste and smell unpleasant, though it is safe to drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does wind help to dry clothes? A: It blows away the water vapour, speeding evaporation. Wind carries away the vapour above wet clothes, so more water evaporates quickly.
chunks.source: Wind carries away the vapour above wet clothes, so more water evaporates quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is dew formed? A: Water vapour in the air condenses on cool surfaces at night. At night, surfaces cool down and water vapour in the air condenses on them as dew drops.
chunks.source: At night, surfaces cool down and water vapour in the air condenses on them as dew drops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two causes of silting. (Select two) A: Soil erosion, Deforestation. Eroded soil and soil left bare by deforestation wash into water bodies and settle as silt. Afforestation, terracing and mulching prevent erosion.
chunks.source: Eroded soil and soil left bare by deforestation wash into water bodies and settle as silt. Afforestation, terracing and mulching prevent erosion.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two ways in which silting affects aquatic life. (Select two) A: It kills fish, It destroys breeding places of aquatic animals. Silt buries fish and their breeding places and blocks sunlight. It does not clean water or add oxygen.
chunks.source: Silt buries fish and their breeding places and blocks sunlight. It does not clean water or add oxygen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can silting be controlled from occurring along river banks? A: By planting grass and trees along river banks. Plant roots hold the soil together so rain cannot wash it into the river.
chunks.source: Plant roots hold the soil together so rain cannot wash it into the river.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How important is sunlight in water formation? A: Sunlight causes evaporation, which starts the water cycle. The sun heats water bodies and causes evaporation, the first step of the water cycle.
chunks.source: The sun heats water bodies and causes evaporation, the first step of the water cycle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are water bodies important in the process of water formation? A: They give off water vapour through evaporation. Lakes, rivers and seas release water vapour into the air, which later forms rain.
chunks.source: Lakes, rivers and seas release water vapour into the air, which later forms rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two ways in which rain helps in the growth of plants. (Select two) A: It provides water for plants, It helps dissolve nutrients in the soil. Rain gives plants water and dissolves soil nutrients so roots can absorb them. Breaking stems, floods and washing crops away are harms of too much rain.
chunks.source: Rain gives plants water and dissolves soil nutrients so roots can absorb them. Breaking stems, floods and washing crops away are harms of too much rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two ways in which rain affects the proper growth of plants. (Select two) A: Too much rain causes flooding, Heavy rain washes away fertile soil. Excess rain floods gardens and washes away fertile soil, harming crops. The other choices are benefits of rain.
chunks.source: Excess rain floods gardens and washes away fertile soil, harming crops. The other choices are benefits of rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is soil leaching? A: The loss of soil nutrients dissolved and carried away by water. When water passes through soil, it dissolves nutrients and carries them deep down where roots cannot reach.
chunks.source: When water passes through soil, it dissolves nutrients and carries them deep down where roots cannot reach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one cause of soil leaching. A: Heavy rain washing through the soil. Heavy rain dissolves soil nutrients and washes them deep into the ground.
chunks.source: Heavy rain dissolves soil nutrients and washes them deep into the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is leaching dangerous to crops? A: It removes the nutrients crops need to grow. Leaching washes plant food deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, so crops grow poorly.
chunks.source: Leaching washes plant food deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, so crops grow poorly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does dew disappear in the morning? A: The morning sun evaporates it. As the sun warms the air in the morning, dew drops evaporate back into vapour.
chunks.source: As the sun warms the air in the morning, dew drops evaporate back into vapour.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the process that makes dew disappear in the morning. A: Evaporation. Dew disappears because liquid dew changes into vapour, which is evaporation.
chunks.source: Dew disappears because liquid dew changes into vapour, which is evaporation.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are water impurities? A: Substances that make water dirty or unsafe. Impurities are unwanted substances like germs, dirt and chemicals that spoil water.
chunks.source: Impurities are unwanted substances like germs, dirt and chemicals that spoil water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two ways water gets contaminated. (Select two) A: Dumping waste in water, Defecating near water sources. Waste and faeces near water introduce germs. Boiling, filtering and chlorinating clean water.
chunks.source: Waste and faeces near water introduce germs. Boiling, filtering and chlorinating clean water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way of preventing water sources from contamination. A: Fencing the water source. A fence keeps people, animals and rubbish away from the water source.
chunks.source: A fence keeps people, animals and rubbish away from the water source.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are water habitat vector diseases? A: Diseases spread by vectors which live and breed in water. A vector is an animal that carries disease germs. Water habitat vectors, like mosquitoes, breed in water.
chunks.source: A vector is an animal that carries disease germs. Water habitat vectors, like mosquitoes, breed in water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two examples of water habitat vector diseases. (Select two) A: Malaria, Bilharzia. Malaria (mosquitoes) and bilharzia (snails) are spread by vectors that breed in water. Measles, tetanus and polio spread differently.
chunks.source: Malaria (mosquitoes) and bilharzia (snails) are spread by vectors that breed in water. Measles, tetanus and polio spread differently.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two vectors that breed in water. (Select two) A: Mosquitoes, Blackflies. Mosquitoes and blackflies lay their eggs in water. Houseflies, cockroaches and lice breed elsewhere.
chunks.source: Mosquitoes and blackflies lay their eggs in water. Houseflies, cockroaches and lice breed elsewhere.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of preventing clothes from losing colour during washing. A: Wash coloured clothes separately from white ones. Separating colours keeps dyes from running onto other clothes, so colours last longer.
chunks.source: Separating colours keeps dyes from running onto other clothes, so colours last longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from making water safe for home use, give any other use of the filtration method at home. A: Filtering juice to remove seeds. Filtration is also used at home to remove seeds from juice.
chunks.source: Filtration is also used at home to remove seeds from juice.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the experiment. What natural process in the environment does this experiment show? A: The water cycle. Heating water to vapour and cooling the vapour back to liquid models evaporation and condensation in the water cycle.
chunks.source: Heating water to vapour and cooling the vapour back to liquid models evaporation and condensation in the water cycle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the experiment. What does the source of heat represent in nature? A: The sun. In nature, the sun provides the heat that evaporates water from water bodies.
chunks.source: In nature, the sun provides the heat that evaporates water from water bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the experiment. What is the function of the bottle with cold water? A: It cools the vapour so it condenses into liquid water. Cold water cools the steam, making it condense back into liquid, like clouds forming in the sky.
chunks.source: Cold water cools the steam, making it condense back into liquid, like clouds forming in the sky.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Study the diagram of the experiment. Give any other local process that takes place in the same way. A: Local distillation of alcohol. Local brewing heats fermented liquid and cools the vapour to collect alcohol, just like the experiment.
chunks.source: Local brewing heats fermented liquid and cools the vapour to collect alcohol, just like the experiment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are resources? A: Useful things found in the environment. Resources are things in the environment, like water, plants and minerals, that people use.
chunks.source: Resources are things in the environment, like water, plants and minerals, that people use.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one type of resource in the environment. A: Living resources. Resources can be grouped into types such as living resources (plants, animals) and non-living resources (water, rocks).
chunks.source: Resources can be grouped into types such as living resources (plants, animals) and non-living resources (water, rocks).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of non-living resources in the environment. (Select two) A: Water, Rocks. Water and rocks are non-living. Plants, animals and trees are living resources.
chunks.source: Water and rocks are non-living. Plants, animals and trees are living resources.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State two ways plants are used as resources in the environment. (Select two) A: They provide food, They provide medicine. Plants give us food and medicine. They clean air and hold soil instead of polluting or destroying.
chunks.source: Plants give us food and medicine. They clean air and hold soil instead of polluting or destroying.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are renewable resources? A: Resources that can be replaced naturally when used up. Renewable resources, like water and plants, are naturally replaced after use.
chunks.source: Renewable resources, like water and plants, are naturally replaced after use.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of renewable resources. (Select two) A: Water, Plants. Water and plants are replaced naturally. Petrol, coal and natural gas cannot be replaced once used.
chunks.source: Water and plants are replaced naturally. Petrol, coal and natural gas cannot be replaced once used.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does conservation of resources mean? A: Using resources carefully to avoid wasting them. Conservation means protecting resources and using them wisely so they last longer.
chunks.source: Conservation means protecting resources and using them wisely so they last longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one characteristic of non-renewable resources. A: They cannot be replaced once used up. Non-renewable resources like petrol and coal took millions of years to form and cannot be replaced.
chunks.source: Non-renewable resources like petrol and coal took millions of years to form and cannot be replaced.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does covering food during cooking help to conserve wood fuel? A: Food cooks faster, so less firewood is used. A covered pot keeps heat in, so food cooks faster and less firewood is burnt.
chunks.source: A covered pot keeps heat in, so food cooks faster and less firewood is burnt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is water as a renewable resource replaced in the environment? A: Through rainfall in the water cycle. Used water returns to the environment as rain through the water cycle.
chunks.source: Used water returns to the environment as rain through the water cycle.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two non-renewable resources in the environment. (Select two) A: Petrol, Coal. Petrol and coal cannot be replaced once used. Water, plants and air are renewable.
chunks.source: Petrol and coal cannot be replaced once used. Water, plants and air are renewable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two ways of conserving non-renewable resources. (Select two) A: Using them sparingly, Using alternative sources of energy like solar. Using less and switching to solar saves non-renewable resources. Wasting and careless burning finish them faster.
chunks.source: Using less and switching to solar saves non-renewable resources. Wasting and careless burning finish them faster.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is water grouped under renewable resources? A: It is replaced through the water cycle. Water is renewable because the water cycle keeps returning it as rain.
chunks.source: Water is renewable because the water cycle keeps returning it as rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way does the use of biogas conserve the environment? A: It reduces the cutting of trees for firewood. Biogas from cow dung replaces firewood, so fewer trees are cut down.
chunks.source: Biogas from cow dung replaces firewood, so fewer trees are cut down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one example of a plant fibre. A: Cotton. Cotton is a soft fibre from the cotton plant. Wool and silk come from animals, nylon is man-made.
chunks.source: Cotton is a soft fibre from the cotton plant. Wool and silk come from animals, nylon is man-made.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one resource in the environment that enables plants to make their food: (i) A: Sunlight. Plants need sunlight energy to make food in photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants need sunlight energy to make food in photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one resource in the environment that enables plants to make their food: (ii) A: Water. Plants also need water to make food in photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Plants also need water to make food in photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the name given to the process by which plants make their food? A: Photosynthesis. Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food.
chunks.source: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which gas is given off during photosynthesis? A: Oxygen. Plants release oxygen as they make food. Animals then use this oxygen for breathing.
chunks.source: Plants release oxygen as they make food. Animals then use this oxygen for breathing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two water resources in Uganda that provide us with proteins. (Select two) A: Lake Victoria, River Nile. Fish from Lake Victoria and River Nile give us proteins. Mountains, deserts and forests are not water resources.
chunks.source: Fish from Lake Victoria and River Nile give us proteins. Mountains, deserts and forests are not water resources.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two human practices that can lead to the destruction of such water resources. (Select two) A: Overfishing, Polluting the water. Overfishing removes too many fish and pollution poisons the water. Protecting, cleaning and stocking help the resource.
chunks.source: Overfishing removes too many fish and pollution poisons the water. Protecting, cleaning and stocking help the resource.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which gas is used by plants to make proteins? A: Nitrogen. Plants take in nitrogen compounds to build proteins for growth.
chunks.source: Plants take in nitrogen compounds to build proteins for growth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one natural resource found under the ground and used as fuel. A: Petroleum. Petroleum is pumped from underground and used as fuel for vehicles and machines.
chunks.source: Petroleum is pumped from underground and used as fuel for vehicles and machines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two of the 5Rs in waste management. (Select two) A: Reduce, Reuse. The 5Rs are Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repurpose and Recycle. Reduce and Reuse are two of them.
chunks.source: The 5Rs are Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repurpose and Recycle. Reduce and Reuse are two of them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two effects of poor waste management in the environment. (Select two) A: It pollutes the environment, It spreads diseases. Poorly managed waste pollutes land, water and air, and spreads diseases.
chunks.source: Poorly managed waste pollutes land, water and air, and spreads diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from wood fuel, name any other type of fuel. A: Charcoal. Charcoal is another common fuel used for cooking, besides firewood.
chunks.source: Charcoal is another common fuel used for cooking, besides firewood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one way in which wood fuel can be conserved. A: Using energy-saving stoves. Energy-saving stoves use less firewood to cook the same food.
chunks.source: Energy-saving stoves use less firewood to cook the same food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is environmental degradation? A: The spoiling of the environment by harmful activities. Environmental degradation is the destruction of nature through activities like deforestation and pollution.
chunks.source: Environmental degradation is the destruction of nature through activities like deforestation and pollution.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two natural causes of environmental degradation. (Select two) A: Drought, Floods. Drought and floods are natural events that damage the environment. Afforestation, terracing and recycling protect it.
chunks.source: Drought and floods are natural events that damage the environment. Afforestation, terracing and recycling protect it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one animal fibre found in the environment. A: Wool. Wool is a fibre obtained from animals such as sheep. Cotton, sisal and flax are plant fibres.
chunks.source: Wool is a fibre obtained from animals such as sheep. Cotton, sisal and flax are plant fibres.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two practices that lead to destruction of wetlands. (Select two) A: Draining wetlands for farming, Dumping waste in wetlands. Draining and dumping waste destroy wetlands. Protecting, planting papyrus and keeping them clean preserve them.
chunks.source: Draining and dumping waste destroy wetlands. Protecting, planting papyrus and keeping them clean preserve them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is air pollution? A: Making air dirty with harmful substances. Air pollution is the contamination of air by smoke, dust, fumes and other harmful substances.
chunks.source: Air pollution is the contamination of air by smoke, dust, fumes and other harmful substances.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one activity that causes air pollution. A: Burning charcoal. Burning charcoal releases smoke that pollutes the air. Planting trees, sweeping and recycling do not pollute air.
chunks.source: Burning charcoal releases smoke that pollutes the air. Planting trees, sweeping and recycling do not pollute air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to a mixture of two or more metals? A: Alloy. An alloy is a mixture of two or more metals, like brass and bronze.
chunks.source: An alloy is a mixture of two or more metals, like brass and bronze.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two examples of a mixture of metals. (Select two) A: Brass, Bronze. Brass (copper and zinc) and bronze (copper and tin) are alloys. Iron, copper and aluminium are single metals.
chunks.source: Brass (copper and zinc) and bronze (copper and tin) are alloys. Iron, copper and aluminium are single metals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two reasons for mixing two or more metals. (Select two) A: To make them stronger, To prevent rusting. Metals are mixed to make stronger, rust-free alloys. Mixing never aims to weaken metals or waste them.
chunks.source: Metals are mixed to make stronger, rust-free alloys. Mixing never aims to weaken metals or waste them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from killing people, give two other dangers of lightning. (Select two) A: It can start fires, It can destroy buildings. Lightning can set buildings and trees on fire and destroy them. It does not water crops or cool air.
chunks.source: Lightning can set buildings and trees on fire and destroy them. It does not water crops or cool air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down two ways by which people can protect themselves from the dangers of lightning. (Select two) A: Staying indoors during storms, Avoiding standing under tall trees. Staying indoors and avoiding tall trees keeps people safe. Open fields, metal rods and tall trees attract lightning danger.
chunks.source: Staying indoors and avoiding tall trees keeps people safe. Open fields, metal rods and tall trees attract lightning danger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are people encouraged to plant trees after cutting some? A: To replace the trees that were cut. Replanting replaces cut trees, keeping the environment green and the resources renewable.
chunks.source: Replanting replaces cut trees, keeping the environment green and the resources renewable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one importance of conserving resources in the environment. A: It makes resources last for future use. Conservation ensures that resources remain available for a long time, even for future generations.
chunks.source: Conservation ensures that resources remain available for a long time, even for future generations.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way soil is used as a resource in the environment. A: Soil is used for growing crops. Soil supports plants, so it is the resource farmers use to grow food crops.
chunks.source: Soil supports plants, so it is the resource farmers use to grow food crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is recycling important in the environment? A: It reduces the amount of waste in the environment. Recycling turns waste into useful items again, so less rubbish piles up.
chunks.source: Recycling turns waste into useful items again, so less rubbish piles up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a fibre as applied in textile? A: A thread-like material used for making cloth. Fibres like cotton and wool are spun into threads and woven into cloth.
chunks.source: Fibres like cotton and wool are spun into threads and woven into cloth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way in which minerals like copper are important in the environment. A: Copper is used for making electric wires. Copper conducts electricity well, so it is used to make electric wires.
chunks.source: Copper conducts electricity well, so it is used to make electric wires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can soil as a renewable resource be replaced in the environment? A: New soil is formed by the weathering of rocks. Rocks break down slowly through weathering, forming new soil over time.
chunks.source: Rocks break down slowly through weathering, forming new soil over time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one characteristic of a renewable resource. A: It can be replaced naturally when used up. Renewable resources come back through natural processes like the water cycle and plant growth.
chunks.source: Renewable resources come back through natural processes like the water cycle and plant growth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two uses of rocks to people. (Select two) A: Building houses, Making murram roads. Rocks are crushed for building and road making. They are not food, drink or air.
chunks.source: Rocks are crushed for building and road making. They are not food, drink or air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one animal that uses water as its habitat. A: Fish. Fish live in water all their lives. Goats, dogs and hens live on land.
chunks.source: Fish live in water all their lives. Goats, dogs and hens live on land.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Under which type of resources do we find plastics? A: Non-renewable resources. Plastics are made from petroleum, which is a non-renewable resource.
chunks.source: Plastics are made from petroleum, which is a non-renewable resource.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one importance of latex that is obtained from plants. A: Latex is used for making rubber products. The milky latex from rubber trees is processed into rubber for tyres, shoes and gloves.
chunks.source: The milky latex from rubber trees is processed into rubber for tyres, shoes and gloves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the component of air used for respiration. A: Oxygen. Living things use oxygen from air for respiration to release energy.
chunks.source: Living things use oxygen from air for respiration to release energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the component of air used for putting out fire. A: Carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it is used to put out fires.
chunks.source: Carbon dioxide does not support burning, so it is used to put out fires.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two dangers of wind to people. (Select two) A: It can blow off roofs of houses, It spreads dust that causes diseases. Strong wind destroys houses and carries dust that causes diseases. Cooling, drying and winnowing are useful effects.
chunks.source: Strong wind destroys houses and carries dust that causes diseases. Cooling, drying and winnowing are useful effects.

chunks.subject: Science
