chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of preventing constipation. A: Eating foods rich in roughages. Roughages add bulk to undigested food and help it move easily through the gut.
chunks.source: Roughages add bulk to undigested food and help it move easily through the gut.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one effect of dysentery to the body. A: Loss of water leading to dehydration. Dysentery causes watery bloody stool, so the body loses a lot of water and becomes dehydrated.
chunks.source: Dysentery causes watery bloody stool, so the body loses a lot of water and becomes dehydrated.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does dysentery spread from infected people to healthy people? A: Through drinking contaminated water. Dysentery germs pass out in stool and spread when healthy people drink water contaminated with it.
chunks.source: Dysentery germs pass out in stool and spread when healthy people drink water contaminated with it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write one way of controlling the spread of dysentery. A: Boiling drinking water. Boiling kills the germs that cause dysentery in drinking water.
chunks.source: Boiling kills the germs that cause dysentery in drinking water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one disease of the digestive system. A: Cholera, Dysentery, Typhoid. Cholera, dysentery and typhoid all attack the digestive system; malaria attacks the blood.
chunks.source: Cholera, dysentery and typhoid all attack the digestive system; malaria attacks the blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows the arrangement of permanent teeth in the lower jaw. Name the type of teeth marked Q. A: Canine teeth. Teeth Q are pointed, so they are the canine teeth.
chunks.source: Teeth Q are pointed, so they are the canine teeth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the lower jaw diagram, state the function of the type of teeth labelled P. A: Biting and cutting food. Teeth P are incisors at the front, used for biting and cutting food.
chunks.source: Teeth P are incisors at the front, used for biting and cutting food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In the lower jaw diagram, state the function of the type of teeth labelled Q. A: Tearing food. Teeth Q are canines, used for tearing food.
chunks.source: Teeth Q are canines, used for tearing food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one difference between the structure of the types of teeth labelled Q and R. A: Q has a pointed tip while R has a broad flat crown. The canine (Q) has a single pointed cusp for tearing, while the molar (R) has a broad flat crown with several cusps for grinding.
chunks.source: The canine (Q) has a single pointed cusp for tearing, while the molar (R) has a broad flat crown with several cusps for grinding.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is cholera spread? A: By drinking contaminated water. Cholera germs from stool contaminate water, and drinking it spreads the disease.
chunks.source: Cholera germs from stool contaminate water, and drinking it spreads the disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of controlling the spread of typhoid. A: Boiling drinking water. Boiling drinking water kills typhoid germs and stops the disease from spreading.
chunks.source: Boiling drinking water kills typhoid germs and stops the disease from spreading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one disorder of the digestive system. A: Constipation. Constipation is a disorder of the digestive system in which passing stool becomes difficult.
chunks.source: Constipation is a disorder of the digestive system in which passing stool becomes difficult.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is part of the human digestive system. Name the part marked Y. A: Oesophagus. Part Y is the oesophagus, the tube that carries food from the mouth to the stomach.
chunks.source: Part Y is the oesophagus, the tube that carries food from the mouth to the stomach.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram is part of the human digestive system. Name the part marked W. A: Pancreas. Part W is the pancreas, which produces digestive enzymes.
chunks.source: Part W is the pancreas, which produces digestive enzymes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is nutrition? A: The process by which the body obtains and uses food. Nutrition is how the body takes in food and uses it for energy, growth and health.
chunks.source: Nutrition is how the body takes in food and uses it for energy, growth and health.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is food poisoning? A: Illness caused by eating contaminated food. Food poisoning is sickness that comes from eating food containing germs or poison.
chunks.source: Food poisoning is sickness that comes from eating food containing germs or poison.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does washing hands before eating help to prevent food contamination? A: It removes germs from the hands. Washing hands removes germs so they are not passed onto the food we eat.
chunks.source: Washing hands removes germs so they are not passed onto the food we eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two signs of food poisoning in humans. A: Vomiting, Diarrhoea. Vomiting and diarrhoea are common signs that someone has eaten poisoned food.
chunks.source: Vomiting and diarrhoea are common signs that someone has eaten poisoned food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are pregnant women considered to be vulnerable? A: They need extra food nutrients for the growing baby. Pregnant women are vulnerable because the growing baby depends on the mother's food for nutrients.
chunks.source: Pregnant women are vulnerable because the growing baby depends on the mother's food for nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should a family keep enough food? A: To have food in times of scarcity. Keeping enough food ensures the family eats well even when food is scarce.
chunks.source: Keeping enough food ensures the family eats well even when food is scarce.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of water in the body. A: It carries food nutrients round the body. Water carries dissolved food and waste round the body and cools it.
chunks.source: Water carries dissolved food and waste round the body and cools it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is malnutrition? A: Lack of enough food nutrients in the body. Malnutrition is the poor health that results when the body lacks enough food nutrients.
chunks.source: Malnutrition is the poor health that results when the body lacks enough food nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one source of food in the community. A: The garden. Families get food from gardens, markets, farms and shops in the community.
chunks.source: Families get food from gardens, markets, farms and shops in the community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one good eating habit. A: Washing hands before eating. Washing hands before eating is a good habit that keeps germs away from food.
chunks.source: Washing hands before eating is a good habit that keeps germs away from food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of chewing food before swallowing. A: It breaks food into small pieces for easy digestion. Chewing cuts food into small pieces and mixes it with saliva so it is easy to swallow and digest.
chunks.source: Chewing cuts food into small pieces and mixes it with saliva so it is easy to swallow and digest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two causes of malnutrition in adults. A: Poverty, Ignorance about feeding. Poverty and ignorance about proper feeding cause adults to lack enough food nutrients.
chunks.source: Poverty and ignorance about proper feeding cause adults to lack enough food nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two dangers of malnutrition in babies. A: Stunted growth, Weak body defence. Malnourished babies grow poorly and their bodies cannot fight diseases well.
chunks.source: Malnourished babies grow poorly and their bodies cannot fight diseases well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two importance of mineral salts in the body. A: They build strong bones and teeth, They help make blood. Mineral salts like calcium build bones and teeth, and iron helps to make blood.
chunks.source: Mineral salts like calcium build bones and teeth, and iron helps to make blood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which class of food provides the body with heat energy? A: Carbohydrates. Carbohydrates are the main source of heat and energy for the body.
chunks.source: Carbohydrates are the main source of heat and energy for the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of iodine in the body. A: It prevents goitre. Iodine keeps the thyroid gland working well and prevents goitre.
chunks.source: Iodine keeps the thyroid gland working well and prevents goitre.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two signs of a baby suffering from marasmus. A: Very thin body, Old man's face. A baby with marasmus is extremely thin with wrinkled skin like an old person's face.
chunks.source: A baby with marasmus is extremely thin with wrinkled skin like an old person's face.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What causes anaemia? A: Lack of iron in the body. Anaemia is caused by lack of iron, which the body needs to make red blood cells.
chunks.source: Anaemia is caused by lack of iron, which the body needs to make red blood cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two sources of vitamin A. A: Carrots, Pawpaw. Carrots and pawpaw are rich sources of vitamin A, which is good for the eyes.
chunks.source: Carrots and pawpaw are rich sources of vitamin A, which is good for the eyes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two signs of scurvy in children. A: Bleeding gums, Wounds take long to heal. Scurvy, caused by lack of vitamin C, makes gums bleed and wounds heal slowly.
chunks.source: Scurvy, caused by lack of vitamin C, makes gums bleed and wounds heal slowly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is food hygiene? A: Keeping food clean and safe from germs. Food hygiene is the practice of handling food in clean ways so it stays safe to eat.
chunks.source: Food hygiene is the practice of handling food in clean ways so it stays safe to eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of feeding on a balanced diet. A: It keeps the body healthy. A balanced diet gives the body all nutrients in the right amounts, keeping it healthy.
chunks.source: A balanced diet gives the body all nutrients in the right amounts, keeping it healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two signs of malnutrition in children. A: Thin body, Swollen stomach. Malnourished children may be very thin or have swollen stomachs and legs.
chunks.source: Malnourished children may be very thin or have swollen stomachs and legs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do people preserve food? A: To keep it for future use. People preserve food so it stays good for a long time and is available in times of scarcity.
chunks.source: People preserve food so it stays good for a long time and is available in times of scarcity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is food preservation? A: Methods of keeping food for a long time without going bad. Food preservation means treating food so germs do not spoil it and it lasts longer.
chunks.source: Food preservation means treating food so germs do not spoil it and it lasts longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does refrigeration help in preserving food? A: Cold slows down the growth of germs. The cold in a fridge slows germs, so food stays fresh longer.
chunks.source: The cold in a fridge slows germs, so food stays fresh longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention two methods of preserving food that involve heat energy. (The book prints 'preserving heat'.) A: Smoking, Sun-drying. Smoking and sun-drying use heat to remove moisture from food so germs cannot grow.
chunks.source: Smoking and sun-drying use heat to remove moisture from food so germs cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is breast feeding? A: Feeding a baby on breast milk. Breast feeding is giving a baby milk directly from the mother's breast.
chunks.source: Breast feeding is giving a baby milk directly from the mother's breast.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two advantages of breast feeding to a baby. A: Breast milk has all food nutrients, Breast milk is clean and warm. Breast milk contains all the nutrients a baby needs and is clean, warm and germ-free.
chunks.source: Breast milk contains all the nutrients a baby needs and is clean, warm and germ-free.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who are vulnerable groups of people? A: People who need special care in feeding. Vulnerable groups are people who need special feeding and care, like babies and pregnant women.
chunks.source: Vulnerable groups are people who need special feeding and care, like babies and pregnant women.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are convalescents different from invalids? A: Convalescents are recovering from illness while invalids are chronically sick. A convalescent is getting better after sickness, while an invalid is sick for a long time and cannot care for himself.
chunks.source: A convalescent is getting better after sickness, while an invalid is sick for a long time and cannot care for himself.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one disadvantage of bottle feeding. A: Bottle milk can easily get contaminated. Milk in bottles can easily be contaminated with germs and make the baby sick.
chunks.source: Milk in bottles can easily be contaminated with germs and make the baby sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is weaning of babies? A: Introducing babies to solid foods in addition to breast milk. Weaning is starting to give a baby soft solid foods together with breast milk.
chunks.source: Weaning is starting to give a baby soft solid foods together with breast milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important to wean babies at 6 months? A: Breast milk alone is no longer enough for the growing baby. At 6 months the baby has grown and needs more nutrients than breast milk alone can give.
chunks.source: At 6 months the baby has grown and needs more nutrients than breast milk alone can give.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of feeding a pregnant woman on food rich in proteins. A: Proteins help the baby to grow. Proteins are body-building foods, so they help the unborn baby grow well.
chunks.source: Proteins are body-building foods, so they help the unborn baby grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from pregnant women, mention any other two vulnerable groups of people. A: Babies, The sick. Babies and sick people are vulnerable because they need special feeding and care.
chunks.source: Babies and sick people are vulnerable because they need special feeding and care.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two uses of food in the body. A: Food gives the body energy, Food helps the body to grow. Food gives the body energy to work and materials to grow.
chunks.source: Food gives the body energy to work and materials to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why people eat food. A: To get energy to do work. People eat food to get energy for work, to grow and to stay healthy.
chunks.source: People eat food to get energy for work, to grow and to stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one disadvantage of breastfeeding. A: The mother must always be near the baby. A breastfeeding mother must stay close to feed the baby often, which limits her movement.
chunks.source: A breastfeeding mother must stay close to feed the baby often, which limits her movement.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How important is breastfeeding to a woman? A: It helps the womb return to its normal size. Breastfeeding helps the mother's womb shrink back to normal after delivery.
chunks.source: Breastfeeding helps the mother's womb shrink back to normal after delivery.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two conditions under which bottle feeding may be recommended. A: When the mother is dead, When the mother produces no milk. Bottle feeding is recommended when the mother has died or cannot produce enough milk.
chunks.source: Bottle feeding is recommended when the mother has died or cannot produce enough milk.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of caring for vulnerable people. A: Giving them enough nutritious food. Vulnerable people are cared for by giving them enough nutritious food and a clean environment.
chunks.source: Vulnerable people are cared for by giving them enough nutritious food and a clean environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one advantage of breastfeeding over bottle feeding to a family. A: Breast milk is free and always ready. Breastfeeding saves the family money and the milk is always at the right temperature.
chunks.source: Breastfeeding saves the family money and the milk is always at the right temperature.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two classes of food that make up a balanced diet. A: Carbohydrates, Proteins. A balanced diet is made of classes like carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, fats, mineral salts, water and roughages.
chunks.source: A balanced diet is made of classes like carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, fats, mineral salts, water and roughages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a balanced diet? A: A diet with all food nutrients in the right amounts. A balanced diet contains every class of food in the correct amounts for the body.
chunks.source: A balanced diet contains every class of food in the correct amounts for the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two importance of proteins to the body. A: Proteins help the body to grow, Proteins repair worn-out tissues. Proteins are body-building foods: they help the body grow and repair worn-out parts.
chunks.source: Proteins are body-building foods: they help the body grow and repair worn-out parts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which deficiency disease does one get due to lack of proteins in the body? A: Kwashiorkor. Lack of proteins causes kwashiorkor, marked by a swollen stomach and brown hair.
chunks.source: Lack of proteins causes kwashiorkor, marked by a swollen stomach and brown hair.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two importance of vitamins in the body. A: Vitamins protect the body against diseases, Vitamins help the body to see well. Vitamins protect the body from diseases and, like vitamin A, keep the eyes healthy.
chunks.source: Vitamins protect the body from diseases and, like vitamin A, keep the eyes healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which class of food provides the body with more energy than carbohydrates? A: Fats. Fats give more energy than the same amount of carbohydrates.
chunks.source: Fats give more energy than the same amount of carbohydrates.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of carbohydrates in the body. A: They provide heat and energy. Carbohydrates are energy-giving foods that provide heat and energy for work.
chunks.source: Carbohydrates are energy-giving foods that provide heat and energy for work.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two signs of a baby suffering from kwashiorkor. A: Swollen stomach, Brown or reddish hair. A baby with kwashiorkor has a swollen stomach and the hair turns brown or reddish.
chunks.source: A baby with kwashiorkor has a swollen stomach and the hair turns brown or reddish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are deficiency diseases? A: Diseases caused by lack of a food nutrient. Deficiency diseases come from missing a needed nutrient, like lack of vitamin C causing scurvy.
chunks.source: Deficiency diseases come from missing a needed nutrient, like lack of vitamin C causing scurvy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any two vitamin deficiency diseases. A: Scurvy, Rickets. Scurvy (lack of vitamin C) and rickets (lack of vitamin D) are vitamin deficiency diseases.
chunks.source: Scurvy (lack of vitamin C) and rickets (lack of vitamin D) are vitamin deficiency diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a food taboo? A: A cultural belief that forbids eating certain foods. A food taboo is a custom that stops people from eating particular foods.
chunks.source: A food taboo is a custom that stops people from eating particular foods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one advantage of food taboos in a community. A: They stop people from eating foods that may harm them. Food taboos can protect people from eating foods that might be harmful to them.
chunks.source: Food taboos can protect people from eating foods that might be harmful to them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way in which food taboos are a disadvantage to people in a community. A: They make people miss important food nutrients. Food taboos can stop people from eating nutritious foods, leading to malnutrition.
chunks.source: Food taboos can stop people from eating nutritious foods, leading to malnutrition.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the disease which results from the deficiency of vitamin C in human body. A: Scurvy. Lack of vitamin C causes scurvy.
chunks.source: Lack of vitamin C causes scurvy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two signs of vitamin C deficiency disease in humans. A: Bleeding gums, Wounds take long to heal. Scurvy makes the gums bleed and wounds heal very slowly.
chunks.source: Scurvy makes the gums bleed and wounds heal very slowly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of food which gives us vitamin C. A: Oranges. Oranges, lemons and other citrus fruits are rich in vitamin C.
chunks.source: Oranges, lemons and other citrus fruits are rich in vitamin C.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What deficiency disease does one get due to lack of roughages in the diet? A: Constipation. Without roughages, undigested food moves too slowly and constipation results.
chunks.source: Without roughages, undigested food moves too slowly and constipation results.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a mineral deficiency disease. A: Goitre. Goitre is caused by lack of the mineral iodine.
chunks.source: Goitre is caused by lack of the mineral iodine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any one source of roughages. A: Vegetables. Vegetables, fruits and whole grains are good sources of roughages.
chunks.source: Vegetables, fruits and whole grains are good sources of roughages.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is food contamination? A: Making food unsafe by adding germs or dirt to it. Food contamination is when germs, dirt or poison get into food and make it unfit to eat.
chunks.source: Food contamination is when germs, dirt or poison get into food and make it unfit to eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two ways food gets contaminated. A: Touching food with dirty hands, Flies landing on food. Dirty hands and flies carry germs onto food and contaminate it.
chunks.source: Dirty hands and flies carry germs onto food and contaminate it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from covering food, state any other way of preventing food from contamination. A: Washing hands before handling food. Clean hands stop germs from passing onto food.
chunks.source: Clean hands stop germs from passing onto food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What causes goitre? A: Lack of iodine in the diet. Goitre is caused by lack of iodine, which the thyroid gland needs.
chunks.source: Goitre is caused by lack of iodine, which the thyroid gland needs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which deficiency disease causes bleeding of gums? A: Scurvy. Scurvy, from lack of vitamin C, causes bleeding gums.
chunks.source: Scurvy, from lack of vitamin C, causes bleeding gums.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What causes marasmus? A: Lack of enough food (starvation). Marasmus is caused by not eating enough food over a long time.
chunks.source: Marasmus is caused by not eating enough food over a long time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two characteristics of bacteria. A: They are very tiny and seen with a microscope, They are single-celled organisms. Bacteria are microscopic single-celled living things.
chunks.source: Bacteria are microscopic single-celled living things.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two places where bacteria can be found. A: In the air, In the soil. Bacteria live almost everywhere: in air, water, soil and in our bodies.
chunks.source: Bacteria live almost everywhere: in air, water, soil and in our bodies.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one condition needed for bacteria to reproduce apart from warmth. A: Moisture. Bacteria need warmth, moisture and food to reproduce quickly.
chunks.source: Bacteria need warmth, moisture and food to reproduce quickly.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is a harmful bacterium? A: The bacterium that causes cholera. Some bacteria cause diseases; the cholera bacterium is a harmful one.
chunks.source: Some bacteria cause diseases; the cholera bacterium is a harmful one.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do bacteria reproduce? A: By binary fission. Bacteria reproduce by binary fission, where one cell splits into two.
chunks.source: Bacteria reproduce by binary fission, where one cell splits into two.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two importance of bacteria in the environment. A: They decompose dead matter, They help in making yoghurt. Bacteria rot dead plants and animals, and useful ones make foods like yoghurt.
chunks.source: Bacteria rot dead plants and animals, and useful ones make foods like yoghurt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the instrument used for seeing bacteria. A: Microscope. Bacteria are too small to see, so we use a microscope to see them.
chunks.source: Bacteria are too small to see, so we use a microscope to see them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two dangers of harmful bacteria to people. A: They cause diseases, They spoil food. Harmful bacteria cause diseases and make food go bad.
chunks.source: Harmful bacteria cause diseases and make food go bad.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two diseases caused by bacteria in humans. A: Cholera, Typhoid. Cholera and typhoid are diseases caused by bacteria spread through dirty water.
chunks.source: Cholera and typhoid are diseases caused by bacteria spread through dirty water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two ways of preventing bacterial diseases in humans. A: Boiling drinking water, Immunisation. Boiling water kills germs and immunisation protects the body against bacterial diseases.
chunks.source: Boiling water kills germs and immunisation protects the body against bacterial diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two examples of bacterial diseases in plants. A: Bacterial wilt, Blight. Bacterial wilt and blight are plant diseases caused by bacteria.
chunks.source: Bacterial wilt and blight are plant diseases caused by bacteria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are antibiotics? A: Drugs used to kill bacteria. Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria or stop them from growing.
chunks.source: Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria or stop them from growing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a disinfectant. A: Jik. Jik is a disinfectant used to kill germs on surfaces.
chunks.source: Jik is a disinfectant used to kill germs on surfaces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do bacteria help in soil formation? A: They decompose dead matter to form humus. Bacteria rot dead plants and animals, forming humus which makes soil fertile.
chunks.source: Bacteria rot dead plants and animals, forming humus which makes soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the bacteria found in the root nodules of leguminous plants. A: Rhizobium. Rhizobium bacteria live in the root nodules of beans and peas and fix nitrogen.
chunks.source: Rhizobium bacteria live in the root nodules of beans and peas and fix nitrogen.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does refrigeration help to preserve food? A: Cold slows down the growth of bacteria. The cold in a fridge slows bacteria, so food stays fresh longer.
chunks.source: The cold in a fridge slows bacteria, so food stays fresh longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does covered food rot? (Book wording kept; germs already on the food multiply.) A: Germs already present in the food multiply and rot it. Even covered food rots because germs already on it keep multiplying.
chunks.source: Even covered food rots because germs already on it keep multiplying.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are fungi? A: Living things that feed on dead decaying matter. Fungi are simple living things without chlorophyll that feed on dead decaying matter.
chunks.source: Fungi are simple living things without chlorophyll that feed on dead decaying matter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two characteristics of fungi. A: They reproduce by means of spores, They have no chlorophyll. Fungi reproduce by spores and have no chlorophyll, so they cannot make their own food.
chunks.source: Fungi reproduce by spores and have no chlorophyll, so they cannot make their own food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one difference between bacteria and fungi. A: Bacteria reproduce by binary fission while fungi reproduce by spores. Bacteria split into two to reproduce, while fungi reproduce by means of spores.
chunks.source: Bacteria split into two to reproduce, while fungi reproduce by means of spores.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do bacteria reproduce? A: By splitting into two (binary fission). Bacteria reproduce by binary fission: one cell divides into two identical cells.
chunks.source: Bacteria reproduce by binary fission: one cell divides into two identical cells.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are mushrooms different from plants in terms of their reproduction? A: Mushrooms reproduce by spores while plants reproduce by seeds. Mushrooms (fungi) make spores, while most plants reproduce by seeds.
chunks.source: Mushrooms (fungi) make spores, while most plants reproduce by seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two examples of fungi in the environment. A: Mushroom, Yeast. Mushroom and yeast are common fungi found in the environment.
chunks.source: Mushroom and yeast are common fungi found in the environment.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does yeast reproduce? A: By budding. Yeast reproduces by budding, where a small bud grows out of the parent cell.
chunks.source: Yeast reproduces by budding, where a small bud grows out of the parent cell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the importance of gills on a mushroom. A: They produce spores. The gills under the mushroom cap produce spores for reproduction.
chunks.source: The gills under the mushroom cap produce spores for reproduction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are gills of a fish different from the gills of a mushroom? A: Fish gills are for breathing while mushroom gills produce spores. Fish use gills to breathe in water, but a mushroom's gills make spores for reproduction.
chunks.source: Fish use gills to breathe in water, but a mushroom's gills make spores for reproduction.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one poisonous fungus in the environment. A: Toadstool. The toadstool looks like a mushroom but is poisonous to eat.
chunks.source: The toadstool looks like a mushroom but is poisonous to eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two importance of fungi in the environment. A: They decompose dead matter, Some are eaten as food. Fungi rot dead matter, and some like mushrooms are eaten as food.
chunks.source: Fungi rot dead matter, and some like mushrooms are eaten as food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the fungus used in fermentation of alcohol. A: Yeast. Yeast ferments sugars to make alcohol.
chunks.source: Yeast ferments sugars to make alcohol.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the fungus that normally grows on bread and leftover food. A: Mould. Mould (bread mould) grows on bread and leftover food.
chunks.source: Mould (bread mould) grows on bread and leftover food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are fungal diseases? A: Diseases caused by fungi. Fungal diseases are sicknesses caused by harmful fungi.
chunks.source: Fungal diseases are sicknesses caused by harmful fungi.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of fungal diseases in humans. A: Ringworm, Athlete's foot. Ringworm and athlete's foot are skin diseases caused by fungi.
chunks.source: Ringworm and athlete's foot are skin diseases caused by fungi.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two examples of fungal diseases in plants. A: Rust, Smut. Rust and smut are fungal diseases that attack crops.
chunks.source: Rust and smut are fungal diseases that attack crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two ways of preventing fungal diseases in humans. A: Keeping the body clean and dry, Avoiding sharing clothes and towels. Cleanliness and not sharing personal items prevent the spread of fungal skin diseases.
chunks.source: Cleanliness and not sharing personal items prevent the spread of fungal skin diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do fungi feed? A: By feeding on dead decaying matter. Fungi feed saprophytically on dead and decaying matter.
chunks.source: Fungi feed saprophytically on dead and decaying matter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the feeding of fungi different from that of plants? A: Fungi feed on decaying matter while plants make their own food. Fungi lack chlorophyll so they feed on decaying matter, while green plants make food by photosynthesis.
chunks.source: Fungi lack chlorophyll so they feed on decaying matter, while green plants make food by photosynthesis.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are fungicides? A: Chemicals used to kill fungi. Fungicides are chemicals sprayed to kill harmful fungi on crops.
chunks.source: Fungicides are chemicals sprayed to kill harmful fungi on crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a harmful bacterium. A: The bacterium that causes typhoid. The typhoid bacterium is harmful because it causes typhoid fever.
chunks.source: The typhoid bacterium is harmful because it causes typhoid fever.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two dangers of harmful fungi to people. A: They cause diseases, They destroy crops. Harmful fungi cause diseases in people and destroy crops in gardens.
chunks.source: Harmful fungi cause diseases in people and destroy crops in gardens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a mushroom obtain its food from decaying matter? A: Through the mycelium which absorbs digested food. The mushroom's mycelium spreads in decaying matter and absorbs the digested food.
chunks.source: The mushroom's mycelium spreads in decaying matter and absorbs the digested food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the fungus used to make penicillin drugs. A: Penicillium. Penicillin is made from the Penicillium mould.
chunks.source: Penicillin is made from the Penicillium mould.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a mushroom. Name the part marked A. A: Cap (pileus). Part A is the cap (pileus), the umbrella-like top of the mushroom.
chunks.source: Part A is the cap (pileus), the umbrella-like top of the mushroom.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a mushroom. Name the part marked B. A: Gills. Part B is the gills, the thin plates under the cap that produce spores.
chunks.source: Part B is the gills, the thin plates under the cap that produce spores.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a mushroom. State the function of the part marked C. A: It absorbs food and water from decaying matter. Part C is the mycelium, which absorbs digested food and water from decaying matter.
chunks.source: Part C is the mycelium, which absorbs digested food and water from decaying matter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which class of food are mushrooms? A: Vegetables. Mushrooms are counted among vegetables, giving the body vitamins and mineral salts.
chunks.source: Mushrooms are counted among vegetables, giving the body vitamins and mineral salts.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What food value is obtained from eating carrots? A: Vitamins. Carrots give the body vitamins, especially vitamin A for good eyesight.
chunks.source: Carrots give the body vitamins, especially vitamin A for good eyesight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two methods used in growing crops. A: Row planting, Broadcasting. Crops are planted by row planting or by broadcasting seeds.
chunks.source: Crops are planted by row planting or by broadcasting seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one advantage of row planting over broadcasting. A: It makes weeding easy. In rows, crops are spaced so weeding and harvesting are easy.
chunks.source: In rows, crops are spaced so weeding and harvesting are easy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is gap filling an important practice in crop growing? A: It replaces dead seedlings so the plant population stays full. Gap filling replaces seeds or seedlings that died, keeping the right number of plants for a good harvest.
chunks.source: Gap filling replaces seeds or seedlings that died, keeping the right number of plants for a good harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two crop growing practices. A: Weeding, Mulching. Weeding and mulching are practices farmers do to care for growing crops.
chunks.source: Weeding and mulching are practices farmers do to care for growing crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each term with its correct meaning. A: Harrowing: Breaking soil lumps into fine particles after ploughing; Thinning: Removing excess seedlings to give enough space; Pruning: Cutting off unwanted branches from a plant. Harrowing breaks soil after ploughing, thinning removes crowded seedlings, and pruning cuts unwanted branches.
chunks.source: Harrowing breaks soil after ploughing, thinning removes crowded seedlings, and pruning cuts unwanted branches.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one major reason for mulching crops in a garden. A: To keep moisture in the soil. Mulches cover the soil and stop water from evaporating, keeping the soil moist.
chunks.source: Mulches cover the soil and stop water from evaporating, keeping the soil moist.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does mulching improve on soil fertility? A: Mulches rot and form humus. As mulches decay they form humus, which adds nutrients to the soil.
chunks.source: As mulches decay they form humus, which adds nutrients to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is weeding? A: The removal of unwanted plants from the garden. Weeding is removing weeds, the unwanted plants that compete with crops.
chunks.source: Weeding is removing weeds, the unwanted plants that compete with crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one example of a weed in the garden. A: Black jack. Black jack is a common weed that grows among crops.
chunks.source: Black jack is a common weed that grows among crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State two ways in which weeds can lower the yield of crops. A: Weeds compete with crops for nutrients, Weeds hide crop pests. Weeds steal water, nutrients and sunlight from crops and hide pests that attack crops.
chunks.source: Weeds steal water, nutrients and sunlight from crops and hide pests that attack crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way in which the growth of weeds can be controlled in a garden. A: By mulching the garden. Mulching covers the soil so weeds do not get sunlight to grow.
chunks.source: Mulching covers the soil so weeds do not get sunlight to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from controlling weeds, give any one other way farmers can care for their crops. A: By watering the crops. Farmers also care for crops by watering, mulching, thinning and applying manure.
chunks.source: Farmers also care for crops by watering, mulching, thinning and applying manure.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one reason why farmers sort seeds before planting them. A: To remove bad seeds and plant only healthy ones. Sorting removes broken or diseased seeds so only healthy seeds that will germinate are planted.
chunks.source: Sorting removes broken or diseased seeds so only healthy seeds that will germinate are planted.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one root tuber which is propagated by use of seeds. A: Carrots. Carrots are root tubers grown by planting seeds.
chunks.source: Carrots are root tubers grown by planting seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does weeding help to control crop pests like caterpillars? A: It removes the hiding places of pests. Weeds hide pests like caterpillars, so weeding removes their shelter.
chunks.source: Weeds hide pests like caterpillars, so weeding removes their shelter.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows bags of maize flour on a raised stand in a store. Why are the bags put on such a raised stand? A: To keep the flour dry and safe from pests. The raised stand keeps bags off the damp floor, allows air flow and protects flour from pests like rats.
chunks.source: The raised stand keeps bags off the damp floor, allows air flow and protects flour from pests like rats.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does mulching of gardens help to control the growth of weeds in a garden? A: It covers the soil so weeds get no sunlight. Mulches block sunlight from reaching weed seeds, so weeds cannot grow.
chunks.source: Mulches block sunlight from reaching weed seeds, so weeds cannot grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down one activity done to seedlings during hardening off. A: Reducing watering gradually. During hardening off, watering is reduced and seedlings are exposed to sunshine to make them tough.
chunks.source: During hardening off, watering is reduced and seedlings are exposed to sunshine to make them tough.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any suitable way a farmer can control weeds in a rice garden. A: By flooding the garden. Flooding a rice garden with water kills weeds while rice, which loves water, keeps growing.
chunks.source: Flooding a rice garden with water kills weeds while rice, which loves water, keeps growing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one type of crops that are included in a crop rotation cycle. A: Legumes. Legumes like beans and peas are included in rotation because they add nitrogen to the soil.
chunks.source: Legumes like beans and peas are included in rotation because they add nitrogen to the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give a reason why leguminous crops are included in crop rotation. A: They add nitrogen to the soil. Legumes have root nodules with bacteria that fix nitrogen, enriching the soil for the next crop.
chunks.source: Legumes have root nodules with bacteria that fix nitrogen, enriching the soil for the next crop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two reasons why farmers first plant some seeds in a nursery bed. A: Small seeds need special care, Young seedlings are protected from harsh weather. Tiny seeds get special care in a nursery, and young seedlings are sheltered until strong enough.
chunks.source: Tiny seeds get special care in a nursery, and young seedlings are sheltered until strong enough.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two advantages of planting crops in rows. A: Weeding is easy, Harvesting is easy. Row planting makes weeding, harvesting and counting crops easy.
chunks.source: Row planting makes weeding, harvesting and counting crops easy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two advantages of crop rotation to crop farmers. A: It controls crop pests and diseases, It maintains soil fertility. Rotating crops breaks pest cycles and keeps the soil fertile.
chunks.source: Rotating crops breaks pest cycles and keeps the soil fertile.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a nursery bed? A: A small prepared garden where seedlings are raised before transplanting. A nursery bed is a small plot where young plants are raised with care before being moved to the main garden.
chunks.source: A nursery bed is a small plot where young plants are raised with care before being moved to the main garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any one root tuber crop which is propagated by means of seeds. A: Carrots. Carrots are root tubers that farmers grow from seeds.
chunks.source: Carrots are root tubers that farmers grow from seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of growing crops in a nursery bed first. A: Young plants get better care and protection. In a nursery, delicate seedlings get water, shade and protection until they are strong.
chunks.source: In a nursery, delicate seedlings get water, shade and protection until they are strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one way of caring for crops in a nursery bed. A: Watering the seedlings. Nursery seedlings are cared for by watering, shading and mulching.
chunks.source: Nursery seedlings are cared for by watering, shading and mulching.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the garden tool used in transplanting seedlings. A: Trowel. A trowel is the small hand tool used for digging holes when transplanting seedlings.
chunks.source: A trowel is the small hand tool used for digging holes when transplanting seedlings.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are crop pests? A: Organisms that destroy crops. Crop pests are living things, like insects and rats, that damage or destroy crops.
chunks.source: Crop pests are living things, like insects and rats, that damage or destroy crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two examples of insect pests in our gardens. A: Weevils, Caterpillars. Weevils and caterpillars are insect pests that damage crops in gardens.
chunks.source: Weevils and caterpillars are insect pests that damage crops in gardens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are root crops? A: Crops grown for their roots. Root crops are crops whose roots are harvested for food, like cassava and carrots.
chunks.source: Root crops are crops whose roots are harvested for food, like cassava and carrots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two examples of root crops. A: Cassava, Sweet potatoes. Cassava and sweet potatoes are root crops harvested for their swollen roots.
chunks.source: Cassava and sweet potatoes are root crops harvested for their swollen roots.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any two diseases that affect root tubers in the garden. A: Cassava mosaic disease, Cassava brown streak disease. Cassava mosaic and cassava brown streak are common diseases of root tubers.
chunks.source: Cassava mosaic and cassava brown streak are common diseases of root tubers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are root crop pests? A: Pests that attack root crops. Root crop pests are organisms that damage root crops like cassava and sweet potatoes.
chunks.source: Root crop pests are organisms that damage root crops like cassava and sweet potatoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two examples of root crop pests. A: Moles, Weevils. Moles and weevils attack root crops in the garden.
chunks.source: Moles and weevils attack root crops in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can root crop pests be controlled in the garden without using chemicals? A: By crop rotation. Crop rotation, hand picking and traps control root crop pests without chemicals.
chunks.source: Crop rotation, hand picking and traps control root crop pests without chemicals.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one biological way of controlling pests. A: Using predators like cats to eat rats. Biological control uses living enemies, like cats for rats or ladybirds for aphids, to reduce pests.
chunks.source: Biological control uses living enemies, like cats for rats or ladybirds for aphids, to reduce pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is harvesting? A: Collecting mature crops from the garden. Harvesting is gathering crops that are ready from the garden or field.
chunks.source: Harvesting is gathering crops that are ready from the garden or field.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two ways root tubers can be harvested. A: By uprooting, By digging them out. Root tubers are harvested by uprooting or digging them out of the soil.
chunks.source: Root tubers are harvested by uprooting or digging them out of the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are stem tubers? A: Crops that store food in swollen underground stems. Stem tubers like Irish potatoes store food in thick underground stems.
chunks.source: Stem tubers like Irish potatoes store food in thick underground stems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one characteristic of stem tubers. A: They have eyes (buds) that sprout. Stem tubers have eyes or buds from which new shoots grow.
chunks.source: Stem tubers have eyes or buds from which new shoots grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two examples of stem tubers. A: Irish potatoes, Yams. Irish potatoes and yams are stem tubers.
chunks.source: Irish potatoes and yams are stem tubers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where does an Irish potato store its food? A: In the underground stem (tuber). The Irish potato stores food in its swollen underground stem called a tuber.
chunks.source: The Irish potato stores food in its swollen underground stem called a tuber.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which food value is obtained from eating Irish potatoes? A: Carbohydrates. Irish potatoes give the body carbohydrates for energy.
chunks.source: Irish potatoes give the body carbohydrates for energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two pests that attack stem tubers in a garden. A: Weevils, Moles. Weevils and moles attack stem tubers like Irish potatoes.
chunks.source: Weevils and moles attack stem tubers like Irish potatoes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any one way of controlling pests that attack stem tubers in the garden. A: Practising crop rotation. Crop rotation breaks the life cycle of tuber pests and reduces their numbers.
chunks.source: Crop rotation breaks the life cycle of tuber pests and reduces their numbers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one economic value of crops to farmers. A: Crops are sold for income. Farmers sell harvested crops to earn money.
chunks.source: Farmers sell harvested crops to earn money.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are perennial crops? A: Crops harvested year after year. Perennial crops live for many seasons and are harvested year after year, like coffee and bananas.
chunks.source: Perennial crops live for many seasons and are harvested year after year, like coffee and bananas.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Besides digging, give any other value of the garden tool shown in the diagram. (Diagram missing in the PDF; tool assumed to be a hoe.) A: Weeding. A hoe is also used for weeding and making furrows besides digging.
chunks.source: A hoe is also used for weeding and making furrows besides digging.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the garden tool used for turning manure. A: Garden fork. A garden fork is used for turning manure and loosening soil.
chunks.source: A garden fork is used for turning manure and loosening soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is sun-drying helpful in the preservation of food crops? A: It removes moisture so germs cannot grow. Sun-drying removes water from crops, so germs cannot grow and the crops last longer.
chunks.source: Sun-drying removes water from crops, so germs cannot grow and the crops last longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are beans and peas grouped under leguminous crops? A: They have root nodules that fix nitrogen. Beans and peas are legumes because their root nodules hold bacteria that fix nitrogen into the soil.
chunks.source: Beans and peas are legumes because their root nodules hold bacteria that fix nitrogen into the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one reason for thinning crops like cotton. A: To give the remaining plants enough space to grow. Thinning removes crowded seedlings so the rest get enough space, light and nutrients.
chunks.source: Thinning removes crowded seedlings so the rest get enough space, light and nutrients.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of a fruit vegetable. A: Tomatoes. Tomatoes are fruit vegetables because they develop from the flower of the plant.
chunks.source: Tomatoes are fruit vegetables because they develop from the flower of the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What type of root system do cereals possess? A: Fibrous root system. Cereals like maize and millet have fibrous roots that spread near the soil surface.
chunks.source: Cereals like maize and millet have fibrous roots that spread near the soil surface.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Briefly explain the term seedling. A: A young plant grown from a seed. A seedling is a young tender plant that has just grown from a seed.
chunks.source: A seedling is a young tender plant that has just grown from a seed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each farming activity with its correct effect. A: Irrigation: Allows growth of crops in all seasons; Afforestation: Promotes convectional rainfall; Mulching: Preserves soil moisture; Crop rotation: Leads to death of crop pests. Irrigation waters crops in dry seasons, trees bring rain, mulches keep moisture, and rotation kills pests.
chunks.source: Irrigation waters crops in dry seasons, trees bring rain, mulches keep moisture, and rotation kills pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do some plants with weak stems climb others? A: To get support and reach sunlight. Climbers like beans climb for support so their leaves can reach sunlight.
chunks.source: Climbers like beans climb for support so their leaves can reach sunlight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is seed viability? A: The ability of a seed to germinate. Seed viability is whether a seed is alive and able to germinate.
chunks.source: Seed viability is whether a seed is alive and able to germinate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one condition under which a seed may fail to germinate. A: Lack of moisture. A seed fails to germinate without moisture, warmth or air, or if it is dead.
chunks.source: A seed fails to germinate without moisture, warmth or air, or if it is dead.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is broadcasting method of growing or planting seeds? A: Scattering seeds randomly on the garden. Broadcasting is throwing or scattering seeds by hand all over the prepared garden.
chunks.source: Broadcasting is throwing or scattering seeds by hand all over the prepared garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram of a garden tool is missing in the PDF, but the caption names it. Name the garden tool. A: Garden fork. The tool shown is a garden fork, used for turning manure and loosening soil.
chunks.source: The tool shown is a garden fork, used for turning manure and loosening soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one use of the garden fork to the farmer. A: Turning manure. Farmers use the garden fork to turn manure and to loosen or dig soil.
chunks.source: Farmers use the garden fork to turn manure and to loosen or dig soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one plant that can be pruned. A: Coffee. Coffee, tea and fruit trees are pruned to remove unwanted branches.
chunks.source: Coffee, tea and fruit trees are pruned to remove unwanted branches.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the group of crops that are harvested year after year. A: Perennial crops. Perennial crops live for many years and are harvested year after year.
chunks.source: Perennial crops live for many years and are harvested year after year.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two examples of perennial crops. A: Coffee, Bananas. Coffee and bananas are perennial crops harvested year after year.
chunks.source: Coffee and bananas are perennial crops harvested year after year.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one way in which perennial crops are harvested. A: By picking. Perennial crops like coffee are harvested by picking the ripe fruits, leaving the plant to bear again.
chunks.source: Perennial crops like coffee are harvested by picking the ripe fruits, leaving the plant to bear again.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In which way are traps useful to the crop farmers? A: They catch and kill crop pests. Farmers set traps to catch pests like rats and moles that destroy crops.
chunks.source: Farmers set traps to catch pests like rats and moles that destroy crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram of a garden tool is missing in the PDF, but the caption names it. Name the garden tool shown. A: Watering can. The tool shown is a watering can, used for watering crops.
chunks.source: The tool shown is a watering can, used for watering crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the use of the watering can to a farmer. A: Watering crops and seedlings. A watering can is used to water crops, especially seedlings in a nursery bed.
chunks.source: A watering can is used to water crops, especially seedlings in a nursery bed.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one quality of a good planting material. A: It is healthy and free from disease. Good planting materials are healthy, mature and free from pests and diseases.
chunks.source: Good planting materials are healthy, mature and free from pests and diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one disease that commonly affects the coffee plants in the community. A: Coffee berry disease. Coffee berry disease attacks the berries of coffee plants.
chunks.source: Coffee berry disease attacks the berries of coffee plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one method of harvesting root crops. A: Uprooting. Root crops are harvested by uprooting or digging them out of the soil.
chunks.source: Root crops are harvested by uprooting or digging them out of the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two ways in which weeding helps on the proper growth of root crops. A: It removes competition for nutrients, It loosens soil for tubers to expand. Weeding removes competing weeds and loosens the soil so tubers can swell easily.
chunks.source: Weeding removes competing weeds and loosens the soil so tubers can swell easily.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one advantage of planting seeds using broadcasting method. A: It is fast and covers a large area. Broadcasting is quick, so a large garden can be planted in a short time.
chunks.source: Broadcasting is quick, so a large garden can be planted in a short time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one characteristic of monocotyledonous seeds. A: They have one cotyledon. Monocotyledonous seeds, like maize, have a single seed leaf (cotyledon).
chunks.source: Monocotyledonous seeds, like maize, have a single seed leaf (cotyledon).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What name is given to the group of crops that grow and live for many seasons? A: Perennial crops. Perennial crops grow and live for many seasons, bearing harvests year after year.
chunks.source: Perennial crops grow and live for many seasons, bearing harvests year after year.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Use the crop list (conifer, coffee, cassava, groundnut): which crop is propagated by the use of stem cuttings? A: Cassava. Cassava is planted using stem cuttings stuck into the soil.
chunks.source: Cassava is planted using stem cuttings stuck into the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: From the crop list, identify one annual crop. A: Groundnut. Groundnut matures and is harvested within one season, so it is an annual crop.
chunks.source: Groundnut matures and is harvested within one season, so it is an annual crop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: From the crop list, identify one perennial crop. A: Coffee. Coffee lives for many years, so it is a perennial crop.
chunks.source: Coffee lives for many years, so it is a perennial crop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any other way in which a conifer is different from all the other crops on the list. A: A conifer does not produce flowers or fruits. A conifer is a non-flowering plant, while coffee, cassava and groundnut all produce flowers and fruits.
chunks.source: A conifer is a non-flowering plant, while coffee, cassava and groundnut all produce flowers and fruits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Sort the crops into annual crops and perennial crops. A: Annual crops: Groundnut,Cassava; Perennial crops: Coffee,Conifer. Groundnut and cassava are harvested within a season, while coffee and conifers live for many years.
chunks.source: Groundnut and cassava are harvested within a season, while coffee and conifers live for many years.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is mulching? A: Covering soil with dry plant materials. Mulching is covering the soil around crops with dry grass, leaves or other plant materials.
chunks.source: Mulching is covering the soil around crops with dry grass, leaves or other plant materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State one source of mulches in our community. A: Dry grass. Dry grass, banana leaves and coffee husks are common mulches.
chunks.source: Dry grass, banana leaves and coffee husks are common mulches.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention two advantages of mulching our garden. A: It keeps moisture in the soil, It controls weeds. Mulches keep soil moist and stop weeds from growing.
chunks.source: Mulches keep soil moist and stop weeds from growing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the farm store shown in the diagram. A: A granary. The raised traditional store for keeping harvested grain is called a granary.
chunks.source: The raised traditional store for keeping harvested grain is called a granary.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the part marked P on the granary. A: Legs. Part P is one of the legs (stand) that raise the granary above the ground.
chunks.source: Part P is one of the legs (stand) that raise the granary above the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the part marked P important on the farm structure above? A: It raises the store above the ground, keeping grain dry and safe from pests. The legs lift the granary off the damp ground and away from rats and other pests.
chunks.source: The legs lift the granary off the damp ground and away from rats and other pests.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List down one crop whose seeds can be kept in the farm structure. A: Maize. Grains like maize, millet and beans are stored in a granary.
chunks.source: Grains like maize, millet and beans are stored in a granary.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are pests? A: Living things that destroy crops or animals. Pests are organisms such as insects, rats and birds that damage crops and stored food.
chunks.source: Pests are organisms such as insects, rats and birds that damage crops and stored food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any two common insect pests in the garden. A: Weevils, Caterpillars. Weevils and caterpillars are common insect pests in gardens.
chunks.source: Weevils and caterpillars are common insect pests in gardens.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one natural method of controlling insect pests in the garden. A: Hand picking the pests. Pests can be controlled naturally by hand picking them or using their predators.
chunks.source: Pests can be controlled naturally by hand picking them or using their predators.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each crop with its method of harvesting. A: Bananas: Cutting down the bunch; Cassava: Uprooting; Coffee: Picking the ripe berries; Maize: Plucking the dry cobs. Bananas are cut as bunches, cassava is uprooted, coffee berries are picked, and maize cobs are plucked.
chunks.source: Bananas are cut as bunches, cassava is uprooted, coffee berries are picked, and maize cobs are plucked.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two advantages of planting crops in rows. A: Weeding is easy, Spacing is even. Rows make weeding easy and give crops even spacing.
chunks.source: Rows make weeding easy and give crops even spacing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from row planting method, identify any other method of planting seeds. A: Broadcasting. Besides row planting, seeds can be planted by broadcasting (scattering).
chunks.source: Besides row planting, seeds can be planted by broadcasting (scattering).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagram shows a garden tool. Name the garden tool above. A: Rake. The tool with a long handle and a toothed head is a rake.
chunks.source: The tool with a long handle and a toothed head is a rake.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is the garden tool above important to farmers? A: It is used for collecting rubbish and levelling soil. A rake gathers rubbish, leaves and levels the soil surface.
chunks.source: A rake gathers rubbish, leaves and levels the soil surface.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from millet, wheat and sorghum, give any other cereal food crop. A: Maize. Maize and rice are also cereal crops.
chunks.source: Maize and rice are also cereal crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention any one common pest that destroys cereal crops. A: Weevils. Weevils attack stored cereals like maize and millet.
chunks.source: Weevils attack stored cereals like maize and millet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two reasons why cereal crops are dried before storing. A: To prevent rotting, To prevent attack by pests. Drying removes moisture so grains do not rot and pests cannot easily attack them.
chunks.source: Drying removes moisture so grains do not rot and pests cannot easily attack them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: The diagrams show weather instruments A and B. Why is it advisable for the above instruments to be put in an open place? A: So that sunshine reaches A freely and rain falls freely into B. In the open, the sunshine recorder gets full sunshine and the rain gauge catches all the rain.
chunks.source: In the open, the sunshine recorder gets full sunshine and the rain gauge catches all the rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the difference in the functions of weather instruments A and B. A: A measures sunshine while B measures rainfall. Instrument A (sunshine recorder) records hours of sunshine; instrument B (rain gauge) measures the amount of rainfall.
chunks.source: Instrument A (sunshine recorder) records hours of sunshine; instrument B (rain gauge) measures the amount of rainfall.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each garden tool with its correct use. A: Tool A: For spraying crops; Tool B: For cutting tree branches; Tool C: For collecting rubbish; Tool D: For transplanting seedlings. Tool A is a sprayer, B is a hand saw, C is a rake, and D is a trowel.
chunks.source: Tool A is a sprayer, B is a hand saw, C is a rake, and D is a trowel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is soil? A: The top layer of the earth's surface on which plants grow. Soil is the loose top layer of the earth made of weathered rock particles, humus, air and water.
chunks.source: Soil is the loose top layer of the earth made of weathered rock particles, humus, air and water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Apart from weathering, give the other process by which soil is formed. A: Decomposition of dead plants and animals. Soil forms by weathering of rocks and by decomposition of dead plants and animals into humus.
chunks.source: Soil forms by weathering of rocks and by decomposition of dead plants and animals into humus.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any two causes of weathering of rocks. A: Rain water, Wind. Rain, wind, temperature changes and plant roots break rocks into small particles.
chunks.source: Rain, wind, temperature changes and plant roots break rocks into small particles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do living organisms in soil help to improve soil fertility? A: They decompose dead matter to form humus. Organisms like earthworms and bacteria rot dead matter into humus and aerate the soil.
chunks.source: Organisms like earthworms and bacteria rot dead matter into humus and aerate the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two importance of soil to people. A: Soil is used for growing crops, Soil is used for building houses. People use soil for growing crops and for building houses and making bricks.
chunks.source: People use soil for growing crops and for building houses and making bricks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one type of soil. A: Loam soil. The main types of soil are sand, clay and loam.
chunks.source: The main types of soil are sand, clay and loam.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Match each description with the correct type of soil. A: Highest drainage: Sand soil; Highest capillarity: Clay soil. Sand soil drains fastest because of its large particles, while clay soil pulls up the most water by capillarity.
chunks.source: Sand soil drains fastest because of its large particles, while clay soil pulls up the most water by capillarity.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two components of soil. A: Air, Water. Soil is made of rock particles, humus, air, water, mineral salts and living organisms.
chunks.source: Soil is made of rock particles, humus, air, water, mineral salts and living organisms.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which agent of soil erosion causes gullies? A: Running water. Fast running water cuts deep channels called gullies in the soil.
chunks.source: Fast running water cuts deep channels called gullies in the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does soil erosion lead to soil infertility? A: It washes away the fertile topsoil. Erosion carries off the rich topsoil, leaving poor infertile soil behind.
chunks.source: Erosion carries off the rich topsoil, leaving poor infertile soil behind.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is clay soil able to retain water much longer than the other types of soil? A: It has very small particles with small air spaces. Clay's tiny particles hold water tightly by capillarity, so water stays longer.
chunks.source: Clay's tiny particles hold water tightly by capillarity, so water stays longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which component of soil is used by plants to make their food? A: Mineral salts. Plants absorb mineral salts from the soil to make their food and grow well.
chunks.source: Plants absorb mineral salts from the soil to make their food and grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the best soil for making pots. A: Clay soil. Clay soil is sticky and can be shaped, so it is best for making pots and bricks.
chunks.source: Clay soil is sticky and can be shaped, so it is best for making pots and bricks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one example of artificial fertilizers used in a garden. A: NPK. NPK and urea are artificial (chemical) fertilizers added to improve soil fertility.
chunks.source: NPK and urea are artificial (chemical) fertilizers added to improve soil fertility.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which type of soil has rough and large particles? A: Sand soil. Sand soil is made of rough, large particles with big air spaces.
chunks.source: Sand soil is made of rough, large particles with big air spaces.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two living organisms that aerate the soil. A: Earthworms, Termites. Earthworms and termites burrow through soil, letting air in.
chunks.source: Earthworms and termites burrow through soil, letting air in.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Write down any two causes of soil erosion. A: Deforestation, Overgrazing. Cutting down trees and overgrazing leave soil bare so wind and water carry it away.
chunks.source: Cutting down trees and overgrazing leave soil bare so wind and water carry it away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any two agents of soil erosion. A: Running water, Wind. Running water and wind are the main agents that carry soil away.
chunks.source: Running water and wind are the main agents that carry soil away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give two ways in which soil erosion can be controlled in hilly areas. A: Terracing, Contour ploughing. Terracing and contour ploughing slow down running water on hills.
chunks.source: Terracing and contour ploughing slow down running water on hills.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why does water drain faster in sand soil than clay soil? A: Sand soil has large particles with large air spaces. Water passes quickly through the big air spaces between sand particles.
chunks.source: Water passes quickly through the big air spaces between sand particles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one importance of soil aeration to a farmer. A: It lets air reach plant roots for healthy growth. Aerated soil lets air reach roots and helps seeds germinate.
chunks.source: Aerated soil lets air reach roots and helps seeds germinate.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How are mineral salts important in the soil? A: Plants use them to make food and grow well. Mineral salts dissolved in soil water are absorbed by plants for making food.
chunks.source: Mineral salts dissolved in soil water are absorbed by plants for making food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Soil exhaustion is the loss of soil fertility; give any one human activity that can lead to the loss of soil fertility. A: Deforestation. Deforestation, overgrazing, monocropping and bush burning make soil lose fertility.
chunks.source: Deforestation, overgrazing, monocropping and bush burning make soil lose fertility.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any two ways of improving on soil fertility. A: Adding manure, Practising crop rotation. Manure adds nutrients and crop rotation, especially with legumes, restores fertility.
chunks.source: Manure adds nutrients and crop rotation, especially with legumes, restores fertility.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State any one way in which people use sand soil. A: For building and construction. Sand soil is used in building, for making concrete and glass.
chunks.source: Sand soil is used in building, for making concrete and glass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does leaching reduce soil fertility? A: It washes mineral salts deep beyond the reach of roots. Leaching carries dissolved mineral salts deep into the soil where plant roots cannot reach them.
chunks.source: Leaching carries dissolved mineral salts deep into the soil where plant roots cannot reach them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which experiment shows that soil contains water? A: Heating soil in a tin and seeing water droplets form on a cold lid. When soil is heated, its water turns to vapour and forms droplets on a cold surface, proving soil contains water.
chunks.source: When soil is heated, its water turns to vapour and forms droplets on a cold surface, proving soil contains water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name any two living components of soil. A: Bacteria, Earthworms. Bacteria, fungi, earthworms and small insects are living components of soil.
chunks.source: Bacteria, fungi, earthworms and small insects are living components of soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is soil fertility? A: The ability of soil to support plant growth. Soil fertility is how rich the soil is in nutrients for growing crops.
chunks.source: Soil fertility is how rich the soil is in nutrients for growing crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any two ways soil can lose its fertility. A: Soil erosion, Leaching. Erosion washes away topsoil and leaching washes nutrients deep down.
chunks.source: Erosion washes away topsoil and leaching washes nutrients deep down.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give any one danger that results from the loss of soil fertility to the environment. A: Poor crop yields leading to hunger. Infertile soil gives poor harvests, which can cause hunger and famine.
chunks.source: Infertile soil gives poor harvests, which can cause hunger and famine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Equal amounts of water were poured onto soils A and B in the diagram. From which soil did more water drop? A: Soil B. More water collected under soil B, so more water drained through it.
chunks.source: More water collected under soil B, so more water drained through it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State why more water dropped from soil B. A: Soil B has large particles with large air spaces, so water passes through quickly. Soil B is sand soil; its large particles leave big air spaces that let water drain fast.
chunks.source: Soil B is sand soil; its large particles leave big air spaces that let water drain fast.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the type of soil in B. A: Sand soil. Soil B let water through quickly, so it is sand soil.
chunks.source: Soil B let water through quickly, so it is sand soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give one use of the type of soil in A. A: Making pots and bricks. Soil A held water, so it is clay soil, which is used for making pots and bricks.
chunks.source: Soil A held water, so it is clay soil, which is used for making pots and bricks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention the types of skeleton. A: Endo skeleton, Exo skeleton, Hydrostatic skeleton. From the P7 Science notes: Endo skeleton
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Endo skeleton

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give examples of animals that have an endo skeleton. A: Human beings / people, Cows, Dogs, Cats, Goats, Lions, Elephants, Tiger. From the P7 Science notes: Human beings / people
