chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Human beings / people

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do animals with an exo skeleton increase in size or grow: ____ A: By moulting or ecdysis. From the P7 Science notes: By moulting or ecdysis
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: By moulting or ecdysis

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the functions of the skeleton. A: The skeleton gives the body shape., The skeleton helps in body movement., The skeleton protects the delicate body parts.. From the P7 Science notes: The skeleton gives the body shape.
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: The skeleton gives the body shape.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the delicate body organs protected by the following parts of the skeleton. A: skull: Brain; Tongue; Eyes; Middle and inner ear.; Back bone / spine / vertebral column: Spinal cord; Rib cage / Ribs: Heart; Lungs; Pelvis / Hip girdle: Reproductive organs; Eye Socket / Orbit: Eyes. From the P7 Science notes: skull: Brain; Tongue; Eyes; Middle and inner ear.
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: skull: Brain; Tongue; Eyes; Middle and inner ear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are babies said to have more bones than adults: ____ A: Babies are born with many cartilages which later join to form bones.. From the P7 Science notes: Babies are born with many cartilages which later join to form bones.
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Babies are born with many cartilages which later join to form bones.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the two regions of the skeleton. A: Axial region, Appendicular region. From the P7 Science notes: Axial region
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Axial region

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention the parts of the skeleton that make up the axial region. A: Skull, Back bone, Ribs. From the P7 Science notes: Skull
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Skull

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the parts that made up the appendicular region. A: Girdles, Limbs. From the P7 Science notes: Girdles
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Girdles

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the different items / substance contained in bones. A: Blood, Blood cells, Nerves. From the P7 Science notes: Blood
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Blood

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Mention the mineral salts that make bones and teeth strong A: Calcium, Phosphorous. From the P7 Science notes: Calcium
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Calcium

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify any parts of the body where we find a cartilage. A: Pinna of the ear., At the end of the nose, At the end of every bone.. From the P7 Science notes: Pinna of the ear.
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Pinna of the ear.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the functions of cartilages in the body. A: A cartilage reduces friction at a joint., A cartilage cushions bones. Types / classes / groups of bones. From the P7 Science notes: A cartilage reduces friction at a joint.
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: A cartilage reduces friction at a joint.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the longest and strongest bone in the body. A: Femur Diagrams showing the long bones in the body. From the P7 Science notes: Femur Diagrams showing the long bones in the body
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Femur Diagrams showing the long bones in the body

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the parts of a movable joint and their functions. A: Ligament: A ligament is tough elastic fibre that joins a bone to a bone.; Tendon: A tendon is tough elastic fibre that joins a bone to a muscle/tendon.; Cartilage: A cartilage cushions bones in a joint.; A cartilage reduces friction at a joint.; Synovial membrane: Synovial membrane produces synovial fluid.; Synovial fluid: Synovial fluid reduces friction at a joint.. From the P7 Science notes: Ligament: A ligament is tough elastic fibre that joins a bone to a bone.
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Ligament: A ligament is tough elastic fibre that joins a bone to a bone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the types / examples of movable joints. A: Ball and socket joint., Hinge joint, Pivot joint, Gliding joint / plane joint. 1. Ball and socket joint. From the P7 Science notes: Ball and socket joint.
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Ball and socket joint.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give the examples of the ball and socket joints in the body. A: Shoulder joint, Hip joint An illustration showing the ball and socket joint at the shoulder. From the P7 Science notes: Shoulder joint
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Shoulder joint

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the different examples of hinge joints in the body. A: Knee joint, Elbow joint, Knuckle joints A diagram showing a hinge joint at the knee. .. From the P7 Science notes: Knee joint
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Knee joint

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify examples of pivot joint in the body: ____ A: Neck vertebrae A diagram showing the pivot joints at the neck. From the P7 Science notes: Neck vertebrae A diagram showing the pivot joints at the neck
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Neck vertebrae A diagram showing the pivot joints at the neck

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Identify the examples of immovable joints in the body. A: Suture joints. A diagram showing the suture joints. From the P7 Science notes: Suture joints. A diagram showing the suture joints
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Suture joints. A diagram showing the suture joints

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the functions of joints in the body. A: Joints allow directional movement in the body., Joints allow non-directional movement in the body.. From the P7 Science notes: Joints allow directional movement in the body.
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Joints allow directional movement in the body.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are voluntary muscles? A: Voluntary muscles are muscles whose movement can be controlled., Voluntary muscles are muscles whose movement is under one’s will.. From the P7 Science notes: Voluntary muscles are muscles whose movement can be controlled.
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Voluntary muscles are muscles whose movement can be controlled.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: State the characteristics of voluntary muscles. A: Voluntary muscles are fibrous., Voluntary muscles get tired quickly., Movement of voluntary muscles is under one’s will.. From the P7 Science notes: Voluntary muscles are fibrous.
chunks.source: From the P7 Science notes: Voluntary muscles are fibrous.

chunks.subject: Science

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 1. Write O.A.U in full. A: Organisation of African Unity. The OAU was the first continental body that united independent African states. It was formed in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in 1963.
chunks.source: The OAU was the first continental body that united independent African states. It was formed in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in 1963.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 2. Give two reasons why O.A.U was formed. i. ii. A: i. To promote unity and solidarity among African states. ii. To defend the independence and territorial integrity of member states.. After independence, African leaders wanted to stay united so that no country would be re-colonised and all could develop together.
chunks.source: After independence, African leaders wanted to stay united so that no country would be re-colonised and all could develop together.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 3. Who was the first chairman of O.A.U? A: Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia. Haile Selassie hosted the founding summit of the OAU in Addis Ababa in 1963 and chaired its first meeting.
chunks.source: Haile Selassie hosted the founding summit of the OAU in Addis Ababa in 1963 and chaired its first meeting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 4. Where are the headquarters of O.A.U? A: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The OAU set up its headquarters in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia.
chunks.source: The OAU set up its headquarters in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 5. Why were the headquarters of O.A.U put in Ethiopia? A: Ethiopia was never colonised, so it was a neutral ground and a symbol of African freedom acceptable to all member states.. Because Ethiopia had defeated colonialists at Adwa, every African country respected it as a symbol of independence.
chunks.source: Because Ethiopia had defeated colonialists at Adwa, every African country respected it as a symbol of independence.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. Give four countries and their leaders who attended the first O.A.U meeting in 1963 i. ii. iii. iv. A: Ghana - Kwame Nkrumah; Egypt - Gamal Abdel Nasser; Ethiopia - Haile Selassie; Mali - Modibo Keita (also accepted: Guinea - Sekou Toure; Algeria - Ahmed Ben Bella; Nigeria - Abubakar Tafawa Balewa; Tanzania - Julius Nyerere).. Thirty-two independent African states attended the 1963 Addis Ababa summit that founded the OAU.
chunks.source: Thirty-two independent African states attended the 1963 Addis Ababa summit that founded the OAU.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 7. Why was O.A.U transformed into A.U? A: The OAU had failed to achieve economic development and stop conflicts, so it was replaced by the AU in 2002 to pursue economic integration and peace more strongly.. The AU was modelled to work more like the European Union, with stronger focus on trade, development and peacekeeping.
chunks.source: The AU was modelled to work more like the European Union, with stronger focus on trade, development and peacekeeping.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. Why was it important for member states of O.A.U to unite after independence? A: Unity gave member states a stronger common voice in world affairs and helped them support liberation movements in countries still under colonial rule.. A united Africa could bargain better and help brothers still fighting for freedom, for example in Southern Africa.
chunks.source: A united Africa could bargain better and help brothers still fighting for freedom, for example in Southern Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. Sort the founder members of the OAU into their African regions. Regions: East Africa, North Africa, West Africa, Central Africa. A: East Africa: Uganda,Kenya; North Africa: Egypt,Algeria; West Africa: Ghana,Nigeria; Central Africa: Cameroon,Democratic Republic of Congo. The OAU was founded by 32 independent states in 1963, drawn from every region of Africa.
chunks.source: The OAU was founded by 32 independent states in 1963, drawn from every region of Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10. Give any two achievements of the O.A.U. i. ii. A: i. It supported liberation movements that ended colonial rule and apartheid in Africa. ii. It promoted unity and helped settle disputes between member states.. Through the OAU liberation committee, freedom fighters got money, training and diplomatic support.
chunks.source: Through the OAU liberation committee, freedom fighters got money, training and diplomatic support.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. Write one sentence about Kwame Nkrumah. A: Kwame Nkrumah was the first president of Ghana who led it to independence in 1957 and championed the formation of the OAU.. Nkrumah called for a 'United States of Africa' and hosted the 1958 All-African People's Conference in Accra.
chunks.source: Nkrumah called for a 'United States of Africa' and hosted the 1958 All-African People's Conference in Accra.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. Give any two failures of O.A.U. i. ii. A: i. It failed to stop civil wars in member states, for example in Rwanda and Somalia. ii. It had no standing army of its own to enforce peace.. The OAU's policy of non-interference made it weak whenever members fought each other.
chunks.source: The OAU's policy of non-interference made it weak whenever members fought each other.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. Name two organs of O.A.U. i. ii. A: i. The Assembly of Heads of State and Government. ii. The Council of Ministers.. The Assembly was the supreme organ; the Council of Ministers carried out its decisions. Others were the General Secretariat and the Commission of Mediation.
chunks.source: The Assembly was the supreme organ; the Council of Ministers carried out its decisions. Others were the General Secretariat and the Commission of Mediation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 14. Why did South Africa take long to become a member of O.A.U? A: South Africa was ruled by the apartheid regime, which the OAU opposed, so it was only admitted after apartheid ended in 1994.. The OAU refused to admit racist regimes; South Africa joined after Nelson Mandela became president.
chunks.source: The OAU refused to admit racist regimes; South Africa joined after Nelson Mandela became president.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. Give any four organs of AU i. ii. iii. iv. A: i. The Assembly of the Union. ii. The Executive Council. iii. The Pan-African Parliament. iv. The AU Commission.. The AU has more organs than the OAU, including a parliament and a Peace and Security Council.
chunks.source: The AU has more organs than the OAU, including a parliament and a Peace and Security Council.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 16. Define the term decolonisation of Africa. A: Decolonisation of Africa is the process by which African colonies gained independence from European colonial rulers.. Most African countries became independent in the 1960s after nationalist struggles.
chunks.source: Most African countries became independent in the 1960s after nationalist struggles.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 17. Suggest any two objectives of AU i. ii. A: i. To promote economic development and integration among member states. ii. To promote peace, security and stability on the continent.. The AU aims to make Africa developed and peaceful, like a united family of nations.
chunks.source: The AU aims to make Africa developed and peaceful, like a united family of nations.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 18. Which organ of A.U runs day to day activities? A: The AU Commission. The AU Commission in Addis Ababa handles the daily work of the African Union.
chunks.source: The AU Commission in Addis Ababa handles the daily work of the African Union.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 19. What are common markets? A: Common markets are groups of countries that agree to trade freely with one another by reducing or removing taxes on imports and exports.. Examples are COMESA and the EAC; they make goods cheaper and markets bigger.
chunks.source: Examples are COMESA and the EAC; they make goods cheaper and markets bigger.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 20. Mention four examples of common markets in Africa. i. ii. iii. iv. A: i. COMESA. ii. EAC (East African Community). iii. ECOWAS. iv. SADC.. These regional bodies remove trade barriers so member countries can buy and sell easily.
chunks.source: These regional bodies remove trade barriers so member countries can buy and sell easily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 21. Which common market in Africa unites countries of Central Africa? A: ECCAS (Economic Community of Central African States). ECCAS unites Central African countries such as Cameroon, Chad and Congo for trade and cooperation.
chunks.source: ECCAS unites Central African countries such as Cameroon, Chad and Congo for trade and cooperation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 22. Why is Tanzania not a member of COMESA? A: Tanzania left COMESA to concentrate on the EAC and SADC, avoiding double membership and conflicting trade rules.. Belonging to many blocs with different rules is costly and confusing, so Tanzania chose the EAC and SADC.
chunks.source: Belonging to many blocs with different rules is costly and confusing, so Tanzania chose the EAC and SADC.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 23. Write three reasons why EAC was formed. i. ii. iii. A: i. To promote trade among member states. ii. To widen markets for goods produced in the region. iii. To promote economic cooperation and development.. The EAC was revived in 1999 so East Africans could trade freely and develop together.
chunks.source: The EAC was revived in 1999 so East Africans could trade freely and develop together.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 24. How can security promote trade in an area? A: Security attracts traders and investors because people do business confidently where their lives and goods are safe.. No one invests in a place full of fighting and robbery.
chunks.source: No one invests in a place full of fighting and robbery.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 25. In which two ways do common markets help to promote trade in Africa? i. ii. A: i. They remove taxes (tariffs) on goods traded between members, making goods cheaper. ii. They create a bigger market for producers to sell their goods.. Free trade means more customers and lower prices.
chunks.source: Free trade means more customers and lower prices.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 26. State any two challenges facing A.U. i. ii. A: i. Civil wars and conflicts in some member states. ii. Lack of enough funds because some members do not pay their contributions.. Wars and empty pockets slow down the AU's work.
chunks.source: Wars and empty pockets slow down the AU's work.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 27. Name the regional body that unites countries in the horn of Africa. A: IGAD (Intergovernmental Authority on Development). IGAD brings together countries of the Horn of Africa such as Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia, Somalia and South Sudan.
chunks.source: IGAD brings together countries of the Horn of Africa such as Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia, Somalia and South Sudan.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 28. Where are the headquarters of COMESA? A: Lusaka, Zambia. COMESA, the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa, is headquartered in Lusaka.
chunks.source: COMESA, the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa, is headquartered in Lusaka.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 29. In which year did the East African Community collapse? A: 1977. The first East African Community collapsed in 1977 due to disagreements and unequal benefits among Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.
chunks.source: The first East African Community collapsed in 1977 due to disagreements and unequal benefits among Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 30. How did O.A.U help to end apartheid in South Africa? A: The OAU supported liberation movements with funds and weapons, isolated the apartheid regime diplomatically, and pushed for sanctions until apartheid ended in 1994.. The OAU's liberation committee gave freedom fighters bases, money and training.
chunks.source: The OAU's liberation committee gave freedom fighters bases, money and training.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 31. Give two reasons why the EAC was revised. i. ii. A: i. To widen the market for goods within East Africa. ii. To promote economic cooperation after the collapse of the first community.. The 1999 treaty brought back the EAC so the region could trade and develop together again.
chunks.source: The 1999 treaty brought back the EAC so the region could trade and develop together again.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 32. In which two ways has AU tried to promote peace in Somali? i. ii. A: i. It sent peacekeeping troops (AMISOM) to fight terrorists and protect the government. ii. It supported dialogue and reconciliation among Somali groups.. AU soldiers from Uganda and Burundi helped stabilise Somalia under the AMISOM mission.
chunks.source: AU soldiers from Uganda and Burundi helped stabilise Somalia under the AMISOM mission.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 33. What is the role of ECOMOG in West Africa? A: ECOMOG is the military arm of ECOWAS that keeps peace in West Africa by stopping wars and protecting civilians.. ECOMOG intervened in civil wars in Liberia and Sierra Leone.
chunks.source: ECOMOG intervened in civil wars in Liberia and Sierra Leone.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 34. Write the following in full. (i) SADC (ii) ECOWAS (iii) EAC A: (i) SADC - Southern African Development Community. (ii) ECOWAS - Economic Community of West African States. (iii) EAC - East African Community.. These are regional economic communities for Southern, Western and Eastern Africa.
chunks.source: These are regional economic communities for Southern, Western and Eastern Africa.

chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 1. What is a continent? A: A continent is a very large continuous mass of land on the earth's surface.. The world has seven continents, and Africa is the second largest.
chunks.source: The world has seven continents, and Africa is the second largest.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 2. Write down any six continents of the world. A: (i) Africa (ii) Asia (iii) Europe (iv) North America (v) South America (vi) Australia. The seven continents are Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Australia and Antarctica.
chunks.source: The seven continents are Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Australia and Antarctica.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 3. Name the world’s biggest continent. A: Asia. Asia is the largest continent, followed by Africa.
chunks.source: Asia is the largest continent, followed by Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 4. Which continent is crossed by the three major latitudes? A: Africa. The Equator, the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn all cross Africa.
chunks.source: The Equator, the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn all cross Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 5. Define each of these terms (a) Latitude (b) Longitude A: (a) Latitude: imaginary lines drawn across the map from east to west used to measure distance north or south of the Equator. (b) Longitude: imaginary lines drawn from north to south used to measure distance east or west of the Prime Meridian.. Latitudes run parallel to the Equator; longitudes meet at the poles.
chunks.source: Latitudes run parallel to the Equator; longitudes meet at the poles.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 6. Why is the Equator marked 00? A: The Equator is the starting line from which all other latitudes are measured northwards and southwards.. Just like zero on a ruler, the Equator is marked 0 degrees.
chunks.source: Just like zero on a ruler, the Equator is marked 0 degrees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 7. Write down all the African countries crossed by; (a) the Equator (b) the Prime meridian (c) the Tropic of Cancer (d) the Tropic of Capricon A: (a) the Equator: Uganda, Kenya, Somalia, Democratic Republic of Congo, Republic of Congo, Gabon. (b) the Prime Meridian: Ghana, Burkina Faso, Mali, Algeria. (c) the Tropic of Cancer: Mauritania, Mali, Algeria, Niger, Chad, Libya, Egypt. (d) the Tropic of Capricorn: Namibia, Botswana, South Africa, Mozambique, Madagascar.. These imaginary lines help us locate African countries on the world map.
chunks.source: These imaginary lines help us locate African countries on the world map.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 8. State the importance of the Equator. A: The Equator divides the earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres and is the reference line for measuring latitudes.. It also marks the hottest belt of the earth where the sun is overhead twice a year.
chunks.source: It also marks the hottest belt of the earth where the sun is overhead twice a year.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 9. How are longitudes important to man? A: Longitudes help us to determine local time and to locate places east or west of the Prime Meridian.. Each 15 degrees of longitude equals one hour of time difference.
chunks.source: Each 15 degrees of longitude equals one hour of time difference.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 10. Name the longitude marked 1800. A: The International Date Line. The 180-degree longitude is where each new day begins on the calendar.
chunks.source: The 180-degree longitude is where each new day begins on the calendar.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 11. Mention two other major latitudes found outside Africa. A: The Arctic Circle and the Antarctic Circle. These two major latitudes lie near the North and South Poles, far outside Africa.
chunks.source: These two major latitudes lie near the North and South Poles, far outside Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 12. Identify any three ways of locating places on a map. A: Grid references, latitudes and longitudes, compass direction, and landmarks.. Map readers combine these methods to find exact positions.
chunks.source: Map readers combine these methods to find exact positions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 13. Write down the biggest country in Africa. A: Algeria. Algeria in North Africa is the largest country on the continent.
chunks.source: Algeria in North Africa is the largest country on the continent.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 14. Define the term ‘Grid reference’ A: A grid reference is a set of numbers used to locate a place in a grid square on a map.. Maps are divided into numbered squares to make finding places easy.
chunks.source: Maps are divided into numbered squares to make finding places easy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 15. Write down the five geographical regions of Africa. A: (i) North Africa (ii) West Africa (iii) Central Africa (iv) East Africa (v) Southern Africa. Africa is divided into five geographical regions for easy study.
chunks.source: Africa is divided into five geographical regions for easy study.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 16. Sort the countries into their African regions. Regions: North Africa, West Africa, Central Africa, East Africa, Southern Africa. A: North Africa: Egypt,Algeria,Morocco; West Africa: Nigeria,Ghana,Senegal; Central Africa: Cameroon,Chad,Democratic Republic of Congo; East Africa: Uganda,Kenya,Tanzania; Southern Africa: South Africa,Zambia,Zimbabwe. Each region groups neighbouring countries with similar location and history.
chunks.source: Each region groups neighbouring countries with similar location and history.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 1. What are physical features? A: Physical features are natural landforms on the earth's surface such as mountains, valleys, lakes and rivers.. They are formed by natural forces, not by man.
chunks.source: They are formed by natural forces, not by man.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 2. Write down any four physical features. A: (i) Mountains (ii) Valleys (iii) Lakes (iv) Rivers. Africa's physical features also include plateaus, plains and deserts.
chunks.source: Africa's physical features also include plateaus, plains and deserts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 3. Which physical feature covers the biggest part of East Africa? A: The plateau. Most of East Africa is a raised flat land called a plateau.
chunks.source: Most of East Africa is a raised flat land called a plateau.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 4. By what process were these features formed; (a) Rift valley (b) Depression lakes (c) L. Bunyonyi (d) Mt. Mufumbiro (e) Cape ranges A: (a) Rift valley - faulting (b) Depression lakes - down-warping (c) L. Bunyonyi - lava damming (volcanicity) (d) Mt. Mufumbiro - volcanicity (e) Cape ranges - folding. Faulting cracks the crust, down-warping sags it, lava can dam valleys into lakes, and folding pushes up mountain ranges.
chunks.source: Faulting cracks the crust, down-warping sags it, lava can dam valleys into lakes, and folding pushes up mountain ranges.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 5. Write down three characteristics of rift valley lakes. i. ii. iii. A: i. They are long and narrow. ii. They are deep. iii. They are salty because they have no outlet.. Rift valley lakes like Tanganyika and Turkana lie in the deep cracks of the rift valley.
chunks.source: Rift valley lakes like Tanganyika and Turkana lie in the deep cracks of the rift valley.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 6. Mention two dangers of living near a volcanic mountain. i. ii. A: i. Eruptions can destroy homes, crops and lives. ii. Hot lava and poisonous gases can kill people and animals.. Volcanic mountains are beautiful but dangerous when they erupt.
chunks.source: Volcanic mountains are beautiful but dangerous when they erupt.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 7. Define each of these terms; (a) Volcanicity (b) Active volcano A: (a) Volcanicity: the process by which magma forces its way through cracks in the earth's crust to form volcanic features. (b) Active volcano: a volcano that still erupts from time to time.. Mount Nyiragongo in DRC is an active volcano that has erupted in recent years.
chunks.source: Mount Nyiragongo in DRC is an active volcano that has erupted in recent years.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 8. Name Africa’s highest mountain. A: Mount Kilimanjaro. Kilimanjaro in Tanzania rises 5,895 metres above sea level.
chunks.source: Kilimanjaro in Tanzania rises 5,895 metres above sea level.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 9. Mention the longest lake in Africa. A: Lake Tanganyika. Tanganyika is the longest freshwater lake in Africa, shared by Tanzania, DRC, Burundi and Zambia.
chunks.source: Tanganyika is the longest freshwater lake in Africa, shared by Tanzania, DRC, Burundi and Zambia.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 10. Why are rift valley lakes salty? A: Rift valley lakes have no outlet, so salts carried in by rivers stay behind while water evaporates in the hot sun.. Without an outlet, everything dissolved in the water remains and concentrates.
chunks.source: Without an outlet, everything dissolved in the water remains and concentrates.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 11. Give the meaning of each of these; (a) Lagoon (b) Crater lake (c) Glacier lake (d) Caldera A: (a) Lagoon: a shallow body of sea water separated from the open sea by a sandbank or coral reef. (b) Crater lake: a lake formed in the crater of a volcano. (c) Glacier lake: a lake formed by the action of moving ice (glacier). (d) Caldera: a very large crater formed when a volcano collapses.. Each lake type is named after the hollow that holds its water.
chunks.source: Each lake type is named after the hollow that holds its water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 12. What is a seasonal river? A: A seasonal river is a river that flows only during the rainy season and dries up in the dry season.. Many small rivers in semi-arid areas are seasonal.
chunks.source: Many small rivers in semi-arid areas are seasonal.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 13. In relation to a river, give the meaning of each of these; (a) Confluence (b) Banks (c) Tributary (d) Mouth (e) Delta (f) Distributary (g) Estuary (h) Gorge A: (a) Confluence: the point where two rivers meet and join. (b) Banks: the sides of a river. (c) Tributary: a small river or stream that joins a bigger river. (d) Mouth: the end of a river where it pours its water into a lake, sea or another river. (e) Delta: a fan-shaped area of deposited soil at a river's mouth. (f) Distributary: a small channel that branches off from the main river. (g) Estuary: the wide mouth of a river where it meets the sea. (h) Gorge: a deep narrow valley cut by a river.. These words describe the parts and journey of a river from source to mouth.
chunks.source: These words describe the parts and journey of a river from source to mouth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 14. Why is water transport hard on most of Africa’s rivers? A: Most African rivers have waterfalls, rapids and cataracts, and many are seasonal or too shallow for boats.. The Nile's cataracts and the Congo's rapids block ships from sailing far inland.
chunks.source: The Nile's cataracts and the Congo's rapids block ships from sailing far inland.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 15. Give two reasons why R. Congo carries a big volume of water to the sea. i. ii. A: i. It flows through the heavy-rainfall equatorial region (Congo Basin). ii. It has very many tributaries joining it.. The Congo is the second most powerful river in the world after the Amazon.
chunks.source: The Congo is the second most powerful river in the world after the Amazon.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 16. Mention two problems caused by rivers. A: Rivers cause floods that destroy crops and homes, and they can drown people and animals.. Floods and drowning are the main dangers of rivers.
chunks.source: Floods and drowning are the main dangers of rivers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 17. Identify two problems facing rivers. i. ii. A: i. Pollution from factories and homes. ii. Silting caused by soil erosion.. Dirty water and mud are choking many African rivers today.
chunks.source: Dirty water and mud are choking many African rivers today.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 18. Write down four values of rivers to Africa. i. ii. iii. iv. A: i. Fishing. ii. Transport. iii. Generation of hydro-electricity. iv. Irrigation of crops.. Rivers give Africa food, power, water and transport routes.
chunks.source: Rivers give Africa food, power, water and transport routes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 19. What are multipurpose river projects? A: Multipurpose river projects are projects built on a river to serve many purposes at once, such as electricity, irrigation, fishing and transport.. The Akosombo Dam in Ghana is a multipurpose project giving power and a fishing lake.
chunks.source: The Akosombo Dam in Ghana is a multipurpose project giving power and a fishing lake.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 20. Give two factors considered before setting up a multipurpose river project. i. ii. A: i. A large and reliable volume of water. ii. A suitable narrow valley site for building the dam.. Engineers also consider the demand for power and the cost of the project.
chunks.source: Engineers also consider the demand for power and the cost of the project.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 21. Point out two disadvantages of multipurpose river projects. i. ii. A: i. People are displaced from their homes by the flooding reservoir. ii. They are very expensive to build.. Dams can also destroy farmland and disturb the environment.
chunks.source: Dams can also destroy farmland and disturb the environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 22. By what process were these features formed? (a) Volcanic mountains (b) Block mountains (c) Fold mountains A: (a) Volcanic mountains - volcanicity (b) Block mountains - faulting (c) Fold mountains - folding. Magma builds volcanic mountains, faulting lifts block mountains like Rwenzori, and folding raises ranges like the Cape Ranges and Atlas.
chunks.source: Magma builds volcanic mountains, faulting lifts block mountains like Rwenzori, and folding raises ranges like the Cape Ranges and Atlas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 23. Why is crop growing hard on the top of very high mountains? A: It is too cold on very high mountain tops, and the soils are thin and poor for crops.. Frost and steep rocky slopes make farming impossible near the peaks.
chunks.source: Frost and steep rocky slopes make farming impossible near the peaks.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 24. State four values of mountains to man. i. ii. iii. iv. A: i. They give fertile volcanic soils for farming. ii. They attract tourists. iii. They are sources of rivers. iv. They influence rainfall (relief rainfall).. Mountains are valuable for farming, tourism, water and minerals.
chunks.source: Mountains are valuable for farming, tourism, water and minerals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 25. Identify two disadvantages of mountains. i. ii. A: i. They make transport and communication difficult. ii. Their steep slopes suffer soil erosion and landslides.. It is hard to build roads and farms on steep mountainsides.
chunks.source: It is hard to build roads and farms on steep mountainsides.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 26. Write down four problems faced by people living on mountain areas. i. ii. iii. iv. A: i. Cold weather. ii. Soil erosion and landslides. iii. Poor transport on steep slopes. iv. Difficulty in farming.. Mountain life is hard because of cold, steep land and isolation.
chunks.source: Mountain life is hard because of cold, steep land and isolation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 27. Name Africa’s biggest man- made lake. A: Lake Volta (in Ghana). Lake Volta is the largest man-made lake in Africa, created by the Akosombo Dam.
chunks.source: Lake Volta is the largest man-made lake in Africa, created by the Akosombo Dam.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 28. Give one characteristic of each of these stages of a river flow. (a) Upper course (b) Middle course (c) Lower course A: (a) Upper course: fast flowing with waterfalls and rapids. (b) Middle course: slower with meanders. (c) Lower course: slow with deposition forming deltas.. A river is young and wild upstream, and old and calm near its mouth.
chunks.source: A river is young and wild upstream, and old and calm near its mouth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 29. Write down the two main tributaries of R. Congo. A: (i) River Ubangi (ii) River Kasai. These two great rivers join the Congo and add to its huge volume of water.
chunks.source: These two great rivers join the Congo and add to its huge volume of water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 30. Why does R. Nile flow northwards? A: The Nile flows northwards because the land slopes from the highlands of East Africa down towards the Mediterranean Sea.. Water always flows downhill, and northern Africa is lower than the lake region.
chunks.source: Water always flows downhill, and northern Africa is lower than the lake region.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 31. Define the term ‘Perennial river’ A: A perennial river is a river that flows throughout the year without drying up.. The Nile and the Congo are perennial rivers.
chunks.source: The Nile and the Congo are perennial rivers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 32. Name two dead volcanoes in Africa. A: (i) Mount Elgon (ii) Mount Kenya. Dead (extinct) volcanoes will never erupt again.
chunks.source: Dead (extinct) volcanoes will never erupt again.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 33. Why is there snow on the peak of some mountains? A: It is very cold at high altitudes, so the moisture freezes into snow and ice.. Temperature falls as one climbs higher.
chunks.source: Temperature falls as one climbs higher.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 34. What are coral reefs? A: Coral reefs are ridges of coral skeletons built up by tiny sea animals along warm shallow coasts.. They form beautiful underwater structures along the East African coast.
chunks.source: They form beautiful underwater structures along the East African coast.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 35. How are coral reefs of value to Africa? A: They attract tourists, provide fishing grounds, and supply coral rock for building.. Diving tourists come to see the colourful reefs of the Indian Ocean coast.
chunks.source: Diving tourists come to see the colourful reefs of the Indian Ocean coast.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 36. Give any two disadvantages of coral reefs. i. ii. A: i. They make it hard for ships to dock at the coast. ii. They can tear the bottom of boats.. Reefs are a danger to navigation even as they protect the shore.
chunks.source: Reefs are a danger to navigation even as they protect the shore.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 37. (a) Differentiate between a delta and an estuary. (b) Give any two rivers in Africa that end; (i) in a delta (ii) in an estuary A: (a) A delta is a fan-shaped deposit of soil at a river's mouth, while an estuary is a wide drowned mouth where the river meets the sea. (b)(i) Rivers ending in a delta: River Nile, River Niger. (ii) Rivers ending in an estuary: River Congo, River Orange.. Deltas build land outwards; estuaries are flooded river mouths.
chunks.source: Deltas build land outwards; estuaries are flooded river mouths.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 38. Give any two lakes which are found in the Eastern Rift Valley. A: Lake Turkana and Lake Baringo (also accepted: Lakes Nakuru, Naivasha, Bogoria, Manyara, Natron).. The Eastern (Gregory) Rift Valley holds a chain of long narrow lakes.
chunks.source: The Eastern (Gregory) Rift Valley holds a chain of long narrow lakes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 39. Name any two theories that led to the formation of the rift valley. i. ii. A: i. The tension theory (plates pulling apart). ii. The compression theory (plates pushing together).. Both theories explain how forces in the earth's crust opened the rift valley cracks.
chunks.source: Both theories explain how forces in the earth's crust opened the rift valley cracks.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 40. Explain the following terms; (a) Active volcano (b) Dormant volcano (c) Extinct volcano A: (a) Active volcano: a volcano that erupts from time to time. (b) Dormant volcano: a volcano that has not erupted for a long time but may erupt again. (c) Extinct volcano: a volcano that will never erupt again.. Nyiragongo is active, Kilimanjaro is dormant, and Elgon is extinct.
chunks.source: Nyiragongo is active, Kilimanjaro is dormant, and Elgon is extinct.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 41. Name any two active volcanoes in Africa. i. ii. A: i. Mount Nyiragongo (DRC). ii. Mount Cameroon (also accepted: Nyamuragira, Erta Ale, Ol Doinyo Lengai).. Africa's active volcanoes are found along the rift valley and in Cameroon and Ethiopia.
chunks.source: Africa's active volcanoes are found along the rift valley and in Cameroon and Ethiopia.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 1. Define the following terms. (i) climate (ii) weather (iii) meteorology A: (i) Climate: the average weather conditions of an area recorded over a long period of time. (ii) Weather: the day-to-day condition of the atmosphere at a particular time and place. (iii) Meteorology: the scientific study of the atmosphere and weather.. Climate is what you expect; weather is what you get.
chunks.source: Climate is what you expect; weather is what you get.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 2. Match each item to the weather condition for using it. List A: an umbrella, a heavy coat, a light dress. List B: rainy weather, cold weather, hot weather. A: an umbrella - rainy weather; a heavy coat - cold weather; a light dress - hot weather.. We dress according to the weather of the day.
chunks.source: We dress according to the weather of the day.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 3. Define the following terms as associated to weather; (i) isotherms (ii) isohytes (iii) isonephs (iv) isobars A: (i) Isotherms: lines drawn on a map joining places with the same temperature. (ii) Isohytes: lines joining places with the same rainfall. (iii) Isonephs: lines joining places with the same cloud cover. (iv) Isobars: lines joining places with the same air pressure.. These 'iso' lines join places sharing the same weather measurement.
chunks.source: These 'iso' lines join places sharing the same weather measurement.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 4. Draw the map symbol for the following; (a) Hill (b) Contour A: (a) Hill: a small closed contour with the height written inside or shown by a triangle with a dot. (b) Contour: a line joining places of the same height above sea level.. Contours show height; a hill appears as concentric closed contours.
chunks.source: Contours show height; a hill appears as concentric closed contours.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 5. How does weather influence people’s ways of dressing? A: People wear light clothes in hot weather, warm heavy clothes in cold weather, and raincoats or umbrellas when it rains.. Dressing suits the weather to keep the body comfortable.
chunks.source: Dressing suits the weather to keep the body comfortable.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. Which climatic region of Africa favours; (i) sheep rearing (ii) citrus fruit growing A: (i) Sheep rearing: Mediterranean climate. (ii) Citrus fruit growing: Mediterranean climate.. The Mediterranean climate with winter rainfall suits sheep and citrus fruits like oranges.
chunks.source: The Mediterranean climate with winter rainfall suits sheep and citrus fruits like oranges.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 7. Describe the tropic region. A: The tropic region is the hot zone between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn where the sun is always high in the sky.. It is the hottest part of the earth, receiving direct sunshine all year.
chunks.source: It is the hottest part of the earth, receiving direct sunshine all year.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. Name the climatic region that is; (a) Hot and dry throughout the year (b) Hot and dry (c) Hot and wet throughout the year A: (a) Hot and dry throughout the year: Desert climate. (b) Hot and dry: Semi-desert (semi-arid) climate. (c) Hot and wet throughout the year: Equatorial climate.. Deserts are dry, semi-deserts are partly dry, and equatorial lands are wet all year.
chunks.source: Deserts are dry, semi-deserts are partly dry, and equatorial lands are wet all year.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. Give any two characteristics of equatorial climate. i. ii. A: i. It is hot and wet throughout the year. ii. It receives heavy convectional rainfall, usually in the afternoon.. Equatorial regions like the Congo Basin are always warm and rainy.
chunks.source: Equatorial regions like the Congo Basin are always warm and rainy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10. What is the main economic activity carried out in areas within semi-arid climate? A: Nomadic pastoralism (cattle keeping). In dry areas people keep animals that can move in search of water and pasture.
chunks.source: In dry areas people keep animals that can move in search of water and pasture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. Which method of farming is mainly carried out in dry areas? A: Irrigation farming. Irrigation brings water to crops where rainfall is unreliable.
chunks.source: Irrigation brings water to crops where rainfall is unreliable.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. Name any two crops that can grow well in semi-arid areas. A: (i) Sorghum (ii) Millet (also accepted: cassava, groundnuts). These crops survive with little water in dry areas.
chunks.source: These crops survive with little water in dry areas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. Mention any three characteristics of Desert climate. i. ii. iii. A: i. Very hot during the day and cold at night. ii. Very little rainfall. iii. Sparse vegetation with thorny plants.. Deserts like the Sahara are harsh lands of heat and dryness.
chunks.source: Deserts like the Sahara are harsh lands of heat and dryness.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 14. Describe desert climate. A: Desert climate is very hot and dry with extremely low rainfall and big differences between day and night temperatures.. Only specially adapted plants and animals survive there.
chunks.source: Only specially adapted plants and animals survive there.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. When does a sea breeze occur? A: A sea breeze occurs during the day when the land heats up faster than the sea and cool air blows from the sea to the land.. At night the reverse happens and we get a land breeze.
chunks.source: At night the reverse happens and we get a land breeze.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 16. Which winds cause rainfall to the East African countries? A: The South-East trade winds (South-East monsoon winds). These moist winds from the Indian Ocean bring rain to East Africa.
chunks.source: These moist winds from the Indian Ocean bring rain to East Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 17. Why does the wind ward side of a mountain receive reliable rainfall? A: Moist winds are forced to rise on the windward side; as they rise they cool, condense and form rain.. Mountains block winds and squeeze rain out of them - this is relief rainfall.
chunks.source: Mountains block winds and squeeze rain out of them - this is relief rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 18. Suggest any three factors that influence the climate of Africa. i. ii. iii. A: i. Latitude (distance from the Equator). ii. Altitude (height above sea level). iii. Distance from large water bodies.. Also: prevailing winds, ocean currents and vegetation affect climate.
chunks.source: Also: prevailing winds, ocean currents and vegetation affect climate.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 19. What are prevailing winds? A: Prevailing winds are winds that blow regularly in a particular direction over an area.. The trade winds and westerlies are prevailing winds that bring rain or dryness.
chunks.source: The trade winds and westerlies are prevailing winds that bring rain or dryness.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 20. What do you call the area where two trade winds meet? A: The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), also called the doldrums. It is the low-pressure belt around the Equator where the trade winds meet and cause heavy rain.
chunks.source: It is the low-pressure belt around the Equator where the trade winds meet and cause heavy rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 21. How are the following weather instruments important? (a) Sunshine recorder (b) Hygrometer (c) Barometer (d) Wind sock (e) Anemometer A: (a) Sunshine recorder: measures the duration of sunshine. (b) Hygrometer: measures humidity. (c) Barometer: measures air pressure. (d) Wind sock: shows wind direction. (e) Anemometer: measures wind speed.. Each instrument at a weather station measures one element of weather.
chunks.source: Each instrument at a weather station measures one element of weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 22. Name any three countries in Africa that experience equatorial climate. A: Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda, Republic of Congo (also accepted: Gabon, Cameroon).. These countries lie on the Equator and receive rainfall throughout the year.
chunks.source: These countries lie on the Equator and receive rainfall throughout the year.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 23. Give any two economic activities carried out in desert climate. i. ii. A: i. Nomadic pastoralism. ii. Tourism. iii. Mining.. Desert people keep camels and goats, and tourists visit desert attractions.
chunks.source: Desert people keep camels and goats, and tourists visit desert attractions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 24. Why is Dar-es-salaam warmer than Kampala? A: Dar-es-salaam is at sea level while Kampala is on a plateau about 1,200 metres high, and temperature falls with altitude.. Low places are hotter than high places.
chunks.source: Low places are hotter than high places.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 25. Identify the main physical feature that is responsible for the formation of relief rainfall. A: Mountains (highlands). Highlands force moist winds to rise and form relief rainfall.
chunks.source: Highlands force moist winds to rise and form relief rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 26. Why is it difficult to grow clonal coffee in north eastern Uganda? A: North eastern Uganda is dry with unreliable rainfall, while clonal coffee needs plenty of reliable rainfall.. Clonal coffee is a thirsty crop that cannot survive drought.
chunks.source: Clonal coffee is a thirsty crop that cannot survive drought.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 27. Identify one advantage of the existence of a large water body to the climate of the surrounding areas. A: A large water body makes the surrounding area receive more rainfall and have moderate temperatures.. Lakes and seas cool the land by day and warm it by night.
chunks.source: Lakes and seas cool the land by day and warm it by night.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 28. Give any one use of a school weather station. A: It is used for studying and recording weather elements by pupils.. Pupils learn to read thermometers, rain gauges and wind vanes there.
chunks.source: Pupils learn to read thermometers, rain gauges and wind vanes there.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 29. What is a weather station? A: A weather station is a place where instruments for measuring weather elements are kept.. Schools and airports have weather stations.
chunks.source: Schools and airports have weather stations.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 30. Identify one way in which irrigation farming can help cotton farmers in Uganda. A: Irrigation gives cotton water during dry spells so it grows well and yields more.. Cotton needs water at the right time to produce good harvests.
chunks.source: Cotton needs water at the right time to produce good harvests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 31. What is global warming? A: Global warming is the gradual rise in the earth's temperature caused by human activities.. It leads to climate change, droughts and melting ice.
chunks.source: It leads to climate change, droughts and melting ice.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 32. Suggest any three factors that may lead to global warming. i. ii. A: i. Deforestation. ii. Burning of fossil fuels (petrol, coal). iii. Industrial gases and bush burning.. Cutting trees and burning fuels fill the air with heat-trapping gases.
chunks.source: Cutting trees and burning fuels fill the air with heat-trapping gases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 33. How does altitude influence the climate of an area? A: Temperature falls as altitude rises, so high places are cooler than low places.. That is why mountain tops are cold and can have snow.
chunks.source: That is why mountain tops are cold and can have snow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 34. Why do people in desert areas were turbans on their heads? A: Turbans protect their heads from the hot sun, heat and dust.. A turban works like a cool shade in the desert.
chunks.source: A turban works like a cool shade in the desert.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 35. How does deforestation affect the climate of an area? A: Deforestation reduces rainfall and raises temperatures because trees help form rain and cool the air.. Cutting trees makes an area hotter and drier.
chunks.source: Cutting trees makes an area hotter and drier.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 36. What does the term equinox mean? A: Equinox is the time of the year when day and night are equal all over the world.. It happens around 21st March and 23rd September when the sun is overhead the Equator.
chunks.source: It happens around 21st March and 23rd September when the sun is overhead the Equator.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 37. When is the sun overhead the following latitudes; (i) Equator (ii) Tropic of cancer (iii) Tropic of Capricorn A: (i) Equator: around 21st March and 23rd September. (ii) Tropic of Cancer: around 21st June. (iii) Tropic of Capricorn: around 22nd December.. The overhead sun moves between the tropics through the year.
chunks.source: The overhead sun moves between the tropics through the year.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 38. How does climate affect man’s activity? A: Climate determines the crops grown, the houses built, the clothes worn and the economic activities of an area.. People in deserts dress and farm differently from people in rainy highlands.
chunks.source: People in deserts dress and farm differently from people in rainy highlands.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 39. Why are areas near the Equator hotter than those that are far away? A: The sun's rays hit the Equator directly, so areas near it receive more heat than areas far away where rays are slanting.. Direct sunshine is hotter than slanting sunshine.
chunks.source: Direct sunshine is hotter than slanting sunshine.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 40. Which climatic region in Africa receives rainfall in winter? TOPIC: VEGETATION OF AFRICA A: The Mediterranean climatic region. The Mediterranean region gets its rain in winter from the westerly winds.
chunks.source: The Mediterranean region gets its rain in winter from the westerly winds.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 1. What is vegetation? A: Vegetation is the plant cover of an area.. It includes forests, grasslands and all plants growing in a place.
chunks.source: It includes forests, grasslands and all plants growing in a place.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 2. Write down the two types of vegetation? A: (i) Natural vegetation (ii) Planted vegetation. Natural vegetation grows on its own; planted vegetation is planted by people.
chunks.source: Natural vegetation grows on its own; planted vegetation is planted by people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 3. Give three characteristics of; (a) planted vegetation (b) Natural vegetation A: (a) Planted vegetation: (i) It is planted by man. (ii) Trees are of the same species and age. (iii) Trees are planted in rows. (b) Natural vegetation: (i) It grows on its own. (ii) It has mixed tree species. (iii) Trees are of different ages.. A planted forest looks neat and uniform while a natural forest is mixed and wild.
chunks.source: A planted forest looks neat and uniform while a natural forest is mixed and wild.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 4. Give any three types of trees that provide; (a) soft wood (b) Hard wood A: (a) Soft wood: pine, cypress, fir. (b) Hard wood: mvule, mahogany, teak.. Soft wood comes from coniferous trees; hard wood from broad-leaved trees.
chunks.source: Soft wood comes from coniferous trees; hard wood from broad-leaved trees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 5. Why are most game parks found in areas with savana vegetation? A: Savanna areas have plenty of grass which is food for the grazing wild animals kept in game parks.. Zebras, antelopes and buffaloes graze on savanna grass.
chunks.source: Zebras, antelopes and buffaloes graze on savanna grass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. Which type of wood is got from Mangrove forests? A: Hard wood. Mangrove trees produce strong hard wood used for building poles and charcoal.
chunks.source: Mangrove trees produce strong hard wood used for building poles and charcoal.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 7. Give two characteristics of; (a) Equatorial vegetation (b) Desert vegetation A: (a) Equatorial vegetation: (i) Trees are very tall with a dense canopy. (ii) Trees are evergreen. (b) Desert vegetation: (i) Plants have small thorny leaves. (ii) Plants have long deep roots.. Equatorial forests are tall and green all year; desert plants are small and tough.
chunks.source: Equatorial forests are tall and green all year; desert plants are small and tough.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. Why do trees in equatorial forests grow tall? A: Trees in equatorial forests grow tall to compete for sunlight under the dense canopy.. Only the tallest trees reach the light above the forest canopy.
chunks.source: Only the tallest trees reach the light above the forest canopy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. Why is there no vegetation on the top of Mt. Rwenzori? A: The top of Mount Rwenzori is too cold and permanently covered with snow and ice, so plants cannot grow there.. Above the snow line no vegetation survives.
chunks.source: Above the snow line no vegetation survives.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10. Why do trees in deserts have small leaves? A: Small leaves reduce water loss through transpiration in the hot dry desert.. Desert plants save every drop of water.
chunks.source: Desert plants save every drop of water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. Which vegetation zone in Africa mostly favour sheep rearing? A: The Mediterranean vegetation zone. Mediterranean grasslands suit sheep rearing, as in South Africa's veld.
chunks.source: Mediterranean grasslands suit sheep rearing, as in South Africa's veld.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. a) What is lumbering? (b) Give two problems facing lumbering in DRC. (c) Give one danger of deforestation. A: (a) Lumbering is the commercial cutting down of trees for timber. (b)(i) Poor transport in the thick forests. (ii) Political instability and wars. (c) One danger of deforestation is soil erosion and desertification.. Lumbering feeds the timber industry but must be controlled to protect forests.
chunks.source: Lumbering feeds the timber industry but must be controlled to protect forests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. Write down three human activities that affect vegetation; (a) negatively (b) positively A: (a) Negatively: (i) Deforestation (ii) Bush burning (iii) Overgrazing. (b) Positively: (i) Afforestation (tree planting) (ii) Agroforestry (iii) Gazetting forest reserves.. Man can destroy vegetation or protect and restore it.
chunks.source: Man can destroy vegetation or protect and restore it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 14. How does vegetation influence human settlement? A: People settle where vegetation supports their activities - farmers near fertile forested land and pastoralists near grasslands.. Vegetation shows whether land can support crops or animals.
chunks.source: Vegetation shows whether land can support crops or animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. Give any four factors that influence vegetation distribution. A: (i) Climate of the area. (ii) Altitude. (iii) Nature of soils. (iv) Drainage.. Rainfall, temperature, height, soils and water decide what grows where.
chunks.source: Rainfall, temperature, height, soils and water decide what grows where.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 16. Define each of these terms; (a) Game parks (b) Tourism (c) Poaching (d) Encroachment A: (a) Game parks: protected areas set aside for the conservation of wild animals. (b) Tourism: the business of travelling for pleasure. (c) Poaching: the illegal killing of wild animals. (d) Encroachment: the illegal settling or farming on protected land.. These terms are all connected with wildlife conservation.
chunks.source: These terms are all connected with wildlife conservation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 17. Give the main product got from the Miombo woodlands. A: Hardwood timber. Miombo woodlands of Tanzania and Zambia give valuable hardwood timber and wood fuel.
chunks.source: Miombo woodlands of Tanzania and Zambia give valuable hardwood timber and wood fuel.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 18. Name Uganda’s biggest natural forest. A: Budongo Forest. Budongo in western Uganda is the country's largest natural forest.
chunks.source: Budongo in western Uganda is the country's largest natural forest.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 19. Why do mountain gorillas live in Bwindi NGP and not Kidepo NGP? A: Bwindi has thick montane forest that gives gorillas food and shelter, while Kidepo is open savanna without such forest.. Mountain gorillas need dense forest to live in.
chunks.source: Mountain gorillas need dense forest to live in.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 20. How are forests important to the carpenters of Africa? A: Forests give carpenters timber for making furniture and building.. Without forests carpenters would have no wood to work with.
chunks.source: Without forests carpenters would have no wood to work with.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 21. Give two products got from soft wood. A: Timber for construction and wood for making paper.. Soft wood is light and easy to work with.
chunks.source: Soft wood is light and easy to work with.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 22. Give two causes of the decrease of forests in East Africa. A: (i) Deforestation for farming and settlement. (ii) Charcoal burning and firewood cutting.. Cutting trees faster than planting them shrinks forests.
chunks.source: Cutting trees faster than planting them shrinks forests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 23. State two values of forests to wild animals. A: (i) Forests give wild animals food. (ii) Forests give wild animals shelter (habitat).. Animals live and feed in forests.
chunks.source: Animals live and feed in forests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 24. How do these factors influence vegetation distribution; (a) Climate of an area (b) Altitude of an area (c) Nature of soils A: (a) Climate: heavy rainfall supports thick forests while dry areas have grass or desert plants. (b) Altitude: different heights have different vegetation belts. (c) Nature of soils: fertile soils support thick vegetation while poor soils support little.. Each factor decides which plants can survive in an area.
chunks.source: Each factor decides which plants can survive in an area.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 25. State four ways of vegetation conservation. A: (i) Afforestation (planting trees). (ii) Agroforestry. (iii) Gazetting forest reserves. (iv) Using alternative sources of energy.. Planting, protecting and using less wood conserve vegetation.
chunks.source: Planting, protecting and using less wood conserve vegetation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 26. Why are the Miombo woodlands sparsely populated? A: Miombo woodlands are infested with tsetse flies and have poor soils, so people avoid settling there.. Tsetse flies spread sleeping sickness to people and nagana to cattle.
chunks.source: Tsetse flies spread sleeping sickness to people and nagana to cattle.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 27. How can rural electrification contribute to vegetation conservation? A: Rural electrification gives people electricity for cooking and lighting, so they cut fewer trees for firewood and charcoal.. Less firewood cutting means more trees survive.
chunks.source: Less firewood cutting means more trees survive.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 28. How are trees in the Sahara able to survive the desert conditions? A: They have long deep roots to reach underground water and small leaves to reduce water loss.. Desert trees are built to survive with very little water.
chunks.source: Desert trees are built to survive with very little water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 29. Why do trees in the savana areas shed off their leaves in the dry season? A: They shed leaves to reduce water loss through transpiration during the dry season.. Bare branches lose less water in the dry heat.
chunks.source: Bare branches lose less water in the dry heat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 30. Why is cattle rearing hard in Miombo woodlands? A: Miombo woodlands have tsetse flies that spread nagana, a disease that kills cattle.. Cattle cannot survive where tsetse flies are many.
chunks.source: Cattle cannot survive where tsetse flies are many.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 31. Why are trees in the tropical rain forests evergreen? A: They receive heavy rainfall throughout the year, so they never lack water.. Constant rain keeps the forest green all year round.
chunks.source: Constant rain keeps the forest green all year round.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 32. Briefly explain why trees in the Equatorial forests grow very tall. A: The trees compete for sunlight, so only the tallest reach the light above the dense canopy.. In a crowded forest, height wins the race for light.
chunks.source: In a crowded forest, height wins the race for light.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 33. How useful are these crops to our industries in Africa? (a) Wattle trees (b) Pyrethrum (c) Cotton (d) Sisal A: (a) Wattle trees: tannin for the leather tanning industry. (b) Pyrethrum: insecticides. (c) Cotton: textile (cloth) industry. (d) Sisal: ropes, sacks and mats.. These cash crops supply raw materials to industries.
chunks.source: These cash crops supply raw materials to industries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 34. What kind of vegetation mostly provides food to mountain gorillas? A: Bamboo and other montane forest vegetation. Mountain gorillas feed mainly on bamboo shoots, leaves and stems.
chunks.source: Mountain gorillas feed mainly on bamboo shoots, leaves and stems.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 35. Name the biggest forest in West Nile. A: Zoka Forest. Zoka in Adjumani district is the largest forest reserve in the West Nile region.
chunks.source: Zoka in Adjumani district is the largest forest reserve in the West Nile region.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 36. How will tree planting help to control the water problem in the dry areas of E. Africa? A: Trees attract rainfall and their roots hold water in the soil, reducing the water shortage.. Planted trees make dry areas wetter and cooler over time.
chunks.source: Planted trees make dry areas wetter and cooler over time.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 1. Define each of these terms (a) Tribe (b) Ethnic group (c) Taboo (d) Culture A: (a) Tribe: a group of people with a common language, culture and ancestry. (b) Ethnic group: a large group of people with a common origin, language and culture. (c) Taboo: an act or behaviour forbidden by custom. (d) Culture: the way of life of a people.. These words describe how African societies are organised and live.
chunks.source: These words describe how African societies are organised and live.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 2. Why is Africa called the cradle land of mankind? A: The earliest human fossils, such as those found at Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania, were discovered in Africa.. This shows that mankind first lived in Africa before spreading to other continents.
chunks.source: This shows that mankind first lived in Africa before spreading to other continents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 3. Who were the original inhabitants of; (a) E. Africa (b) N. Africa (c) Southern Africa A: (a) E. Africa: the Bushmen (San). (b) N. Africa: the Berbers. (c) Southern Africa: the San (Bushmen) and Khoikhoi.. These early inhabitants were later displaced or absorbed by migrating groups like the Bantu.
chunks.source: These early inhabitants were later displaced or absorbed by migrating groups like the Bantu.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 4. Write down any four sources of history. A: (i) Oral tradition (ii) Archaeology (iii) Written records (iv) Linguistics. Historians also use anthropology and fossils to learn about the past.
chunks.source: Historians also use anthropology and fossils to learn about the past.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 5. How is culture important to us? A: Culture gives us identity and unity, teaches moral values, and attracts tourists.. A people without culture loses its identity.
chunks.source: A people without culture loses its identity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. Name the three major ethnic groups of East Africa. A: (i) Bantu (ii) Nilotes (iii) Cushites (Hamites). These three groups migrated into East Africa from different directions.
chunks.source: These three groups migrated into East Africa from different directions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 7. Under which ethnic group are the Bahima? A: The Highland Nilotes. The Bahima of Ankole are cattle keepers belonging to the Nilotic group.
chunks.source: The Bahima of Ankole are cattle keepers belonging to the Nilotic group.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. How were the Africans of long ago politically organised? A: They were organised in kingdoms, chiefdoms and clans under kings, chiefs and clan elders.. Each society had its own leaders and laws before foreigners came.
chunks.source: Each society had its own leaders and laws before foreigners came.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. Give any four causes of early migrations. A: (i) Wars and conflicts. (ii) Drought and famine. (iii) Search for fertile land, water and pasture. (iv) Overpopulation.. People moved to find safety, food and better land.
chunks.source: People moved to find safety, food and better land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10. Why did the Bantu settle in the lake region of East Africa? A: The lake region had fertile soils, reliable rainfall and fish, which suited the Bantu who were cultivators.. The Bantu needed good land for their crops.
chunks.source: The Bantu needed good land for their crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. Why did the Bantu settle in areas with fertile soils? A: The Bantu were cultivators and needed fertile soils to grow their crops well.. Fertile land gave them good harvests.
chunks.source: Fertile land gave them good harvests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. Mention two reasons why people of today migrate. A: (i) To look for jobs. (ii) To get better education and social services. (iii) To run away from wars and disasters.. Modern migration is driven by the search for a better life.
chunks.source: Modern migration is driven by the search for a better life.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. Give three effects of early migrations. A: (i) Intermarriage between groups. (ii) Spread of new skills like iron working. (iii) Conflicts and displacement of weaker groups.. Migrations mixed peoples and cultures across Africa.
chunks.source: Migrations mixed peoples and cultures across Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 14. What was the Trans Saharan trade? A: The Trans-Saharan trade was the trade across the Sahara desert between North Africa and West Africa, exchanging gold and salt.. Camels carried goods between the Mediterranean coast and cities like Timbuktu.
chunks.source: Camels carried goods between the Mediterranean coast and cities like Timbuktu.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. Mention two effects of the Trans Saharan trade. A: (i) It spread Islam in West Africa. (ii) It led to the growth of towns like Timbuktu.. The trade also brought new goods and intermarriage.
chunks.source: The trade also brought new goods and intermarriage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 16. Write down any three tribes in Africa that lead a nomadic life. A: (i) Fulani (ii) Tuareg (iii) Masai (also accepted: Karamojong, Turkana, Somali). Nomads move with their animals in search of water and pasture.
chunks.source: Nomads move with their animals in search of water and pasture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 17. Why did some Nilotic tribes like the Iteso change to crop growing? A: (i) They settled among the Bantu in areas with fertile soils. (ii) They learnt the skill of crop growing from their Bantu neighbours.. Settled life and good land turned some pastoralists into farmers.
chunks.source: Settled life and good land turned some pastoralists into farmers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 18. a) Name the biggest Bantu tribe in; (i) Uganda (ii) Kenya (iii) Tanzania (b) Who were the first foreigners to come to East Africa? A: (a)(i) Uganda: Baganda (ii) Kenya: Kikuyu (iii) Tanzania: Sukuma. (b) The Arabs.. The Arabs came first for trade, long before the Europeans.
chunks.source: The Arabs came first for trade, long before the Europeans.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 19. What was the original home land of the River lake Nilotes? A: Bahr-el-Ghazal in South Sudan. The River-Lake Nilotes like the Acholi, Langi and Alur migrated south from this region.
chunks.source: The River-Lake Nilotes like the Acholi, Langi and Alur migrated south from this region.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 20. a) How were the people of long ago politically organised? (b) Write down two characteristics of ancient kingdoms. (c) Who were the founders of Bunyoro Kitara? A: (a) They were organised in kingdoms, chiefdoms and clans. (b)(i) They had a centralised leadership under a king. (ii) Leadership was hereditary (passed from father to son). (c) The Bachwezi.. Long ago Africans governed themselves through their own traditional leaders before colonial rule.
chunks.source: Long ago Africans governed themselves through their own traditional leaders before colonial rule.

chunks.subject: Social
