chunks.text: Q: 21. How does a big population in a country affect each of these; (i) Market for goods (ii) Labour force (iii) Wetlands (b) State one danger of a small population to a country. A: (i) Market for goods: it becomes bigger because there are more buyers. (ii) Labour force: it increases because there are more workers. (iii) Wetlands: they get encroached on and degraded. (b) A small population gives a small market and a shortage of labour.. Population size affects the economy and the environment in good and bad ways.
chunks.source: Population size affects the economy and the environment in good and bad ways.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 22. a) Why didn’t some tribes form kingdoms? (b) Give three advantages of kingdoms. A: (a) Some tribes were small or kept moving (pastoralists), so they stayed in clans under elders instead of forming kingdoms. (b)(i) They promoted unity among people. (ii) They provided security and protection. (iii) They had organised leadership for development.. Kingdoms needed settled, united people under one strong ruler.
chunks.source: Kingdoms needed settled, united people under one strong ruler.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 23. a) Why did the early trade move in caravans? (b) How were camels useful during the Trans Saharan trade? (c) How are the Fulani related to the Turkana in terms of lifestyle? A: (a) Caravans gave traders protection against robbers and wild animals. (b) Camels carried heavy loads and could travel long distances in the desert without water. (c) Both are nomadic pastoralists who move with their cattle in search of water and pasture.. The desert journey was dangerous, so traders moved in large protected groups.
chunks.source: The desert journey was dangerous, so traders moved in large protected groups.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 24. a) Write down any two problems nomads face. (b) Suggest solutions to the above problems. A: (a)(i) Shortage of water and pasture during drought. (ii) Cattle rustling and conflicts. (b)(i) Build dams and boreholes for water. (ii) Provide security and encourage settled farming.. Nomads suffer most from drought and insecurity.
chunks.source: Nomads suffer most from drought and insecurity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 25. a) Name any three countries where the Europeans settled in Africa. (b) How did the settlers affect the natives of the countries they settled in? A: (a)(i) Kenya (ii) Zimbabwe (iii) South Africa (also accepted: Algeria, Namibia). (b) The settlers took the best land from natives, introduced forced labour and taxes, and undermined African cultures.. Europeans settled where the climate suited them and farming was good.
chunks.source: Europeans settled where the climate suited them and farming was good.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 1. What is Nationalism? A: Nationalism is the strong love for one's country and the desire for it to be free and self-governing.. Nationalism drove Africans to fight for independence from colonial rule.
chunks.source: Nationalism drove Africans to fight for independence from colonial rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 2. Differentiate between a nationalist and a patriot . A: A nationalist is one who fights for the independence of his country, while a patriot is one who loves and defends his country.. All nationalists are patriots, but not all patriots led the independence struggle.
chunks.source: All nationalists are patriots, but not all patriots led the independence struggle.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 3. What was Pan-Africanism? A: Pan-Africanism was the movement that called for the unity and solidarity of all African people worldwide.. It inspired Africans to work together against colonialism and racism.
chunks.source: It inspired Africans to work together against colonialism and racism.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 4. Name any three Pan-Africanists who attended the first Pan African Congress. A: (i) Henry Sylvester Williams (ii) W.E.B. Du Bois (iii) Bishop Alexander Walters. The first Pan-African Congress was held in London in 1900 to protest colonialism and racism.
chunks.source: The first Pan-African Congress was held in London in 1900 to protest colonialism and racism.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 5. Define the term independence? A: Independence is the freedom of a country to govern itself without being ruled by another country.. Uganda got its independence on 9th October 1962.
chunks.source: Uganda got its independence on 9th October 1962.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 6. Write short notes about the following personalities (i) Ignatius Kangave Musaazi (ii) George William Kakoma (iii) Gregory Magoba A: (i) Ignatius Kangave Musaazi: formed the Uganda National Congress (UNC) in 1952, the first political party in Uganda. (ii) George William Kakoma: composed Uganda's national anthem. (iii) Gregory Magoba: remembered as one of Uganda's early nationalists in the independence struggle.. These men are remembered for their roles in Uganda's journey to independence.
chunks.source: These men are remembered for their roles in Uganda's journey to independence.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 7. State any three ways Africans demanded for their independence. A: (i) Forming political parties. (ii) Holding peaceful demonstrations and strikes. (iii) Boycotting European goods.. Africans used both peaceful and forceful methods to demand freedom.
chunks.source: Africans used both peaceful and forceful methods to demand freedom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 8. Why did Africans demand for their independence? (Give two reasons) A: (i) They were mistreated through forced labour and heavy taxes. (ii) Their land was grabbed by colonialists.. Colonial suffering pushed Africans to fight for self-rule.
chunks.source: Colonial suffering pushed Africans to fight for self-rule.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 9. Give any two problems that Africans experienced during the struggle for independence. A: (i) They were imprisoned and tortured. (ii) Many were killed by colonial forces.. The struggle for freedom was painful and costly.
chunks.source: The struggle for freedom was painful and costly.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 10. Write the first sentence of the second stanza of the National Anthem. A: Oh Uganda! the land of freedom.. Uganda's anthem has three stanzas; the second begins with the land of freedom.
chunks.source: Uganda's anthem has three stanzas; the second begins with the land of freedom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 11. Who is a citizen by (a) descent (b) naturalisation (c) adoption A: (a) By descent: a person born to parents who are citizens. (b) By naturalisation: a foreigner granted citizenship after applying and meeting conditions. (c) By adoption: a child legally adopted by citizen parents.. Uganda's constitution gives these three ways of becoming a citizen.
chunks.source: Uganda's constitution gives these three ways of becoming a citizen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 12. State any two forceful means natives used to demand for independence. A: (i) Armed rebellions and uprisings. (ii) Riots and sabotage of colonial property.. When peaceful demands failed, some Africans took up arms.
chunks.source: When peaceful demands failed, some Africans took up arms.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 13. Why didn’t Uganda attend the Pan-African Congress that was held in Ghana? A: Uganda was still a British protectorate with restricted political activity, so it could not send an independent delegation.. The 1958 Accra conference gathered already-independent or nearly-independent states.
chunks.source: The 1958 Accra conference gathered already-independent or nearly-independent states.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 14. Why do you think Africans were defeated during their struggle for independence? A: The Europeans had superior weapons such as guns, while Africans fought with spears and arrows.. Better guns beat spears in most early resistances.
chunks.source: Better guns beat spears in most early resistances.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 15. Name the two countries in Africa that were not colonised. A: (i) Ethiopia (ii) Liberia. Ethiopia defeated Italy at Adwa; Liberia was founded by freed American slaves.
chunks.source: Ethiopia defeated Italy at Adwa; Liberia was founded by freed American slaves.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 16. In which two ways were Africans mistreated during their struggle for independence? A: (i) They were forced to do hard labour with little or no pay. (ii) They were heavily taxed and beaten.. Colonial mistreatment angered Africans into resistance.
chunks.source: Colonial mistreatment angered Africans into resistance.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 17. Suggest two reasons why Europeans were more interested in colonising African countries. A: (i) To get raw materials for their industries. (ii) To get markets for their finished goods and for national prestige.. Africa's wealth and strategic value attracted competing European powers.
chunks.source: Africa's wealth and strategic value attracted competing European powers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 18. Give any three contributions of Kwame Nkrumah towards Ghana’s independence. A: (i) He formed the CPP which led Ghana to independence in 1957. (ii) He organised the 1958 All-African People's Conference in Accra. (iii) He championed African unity and the OAU.. Nkrumah made Ghana the first sub-Saharan country to gain independence.
chunks.source: Nkrumah made Ghana the first sub-Saharan country to gain independence.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 19. Write brief notes about Nelson Mandela. A: Nelson Mandela fought apartheid, spent 27 years in prison on Robben Island, and became South Africa's first black president in 1994.. He is a world symbol of forgiveness and freedom.
chunks.source: He is a world symbol of forgiveness and freedom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 20. Why was Ethiopia not colonised? A: Ethiopia defeated the Italian army at the Battle of Adwa in 1896 under Emperor Menelik II.. The victory kept Ethiopia free and inspired the rest of Africa.
chunks.source: The victory kept Ethiopia free and inspired the rest of Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 21. Why was German rule opposed in Tanganyika? A: German rule was harsh, with forced labour, heavy taxes and cruel punishments, which sparked the Maji Maji rebellion of 1905-1907.. The Germans treated Tanganyikans brutally.
chunks.source: The Germans treated Tanganyikans brutally.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 22. Why are the following personalities remembered towards the independence struggles of their countries; (i) Nelson Mandela (ii) Kwame Nkrumah A: (i) Nelson Mandela: led the fight against apartheid and became South Africa's first black president. (ii) Kwame Nkrumah: led Ghana to independence and championed African unity.. Both are founding heroes of free Africa.
chunks.source: Both are founding heroes of free Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 23. Name any two personalities who attended the Accra conference in Ghana in 1958. A: Kwame Nkrumah (Ghana) and Julius Nyerere (Tanganyika) (also accepted: Sekou Toure of Guinea).. The 1958 Accra conference gathered Africa's leading nationalists.
chunks.source: The 1958 Accra conference gathered Africa's leading nationalists.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 24. Give any two prominent Africans that led Nigeria to independence. A: (i) Nnamdi Azikiwe (ii) Obafemi Awolowo (also accepted: Abubakar Tafawa Balewa).. These nationalists led Nigeria to independence in 1960.
chunks.source: These nationalists led Nigeria to independence in 1960.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 25. Suggest any two reasons why Africans fought for independence. A: (i) To end colonial mistreatment and exploitation. (ii) To govern themselves and control their own resources.. Africans wanted dignity, freedom and their land back.
chunks.source: Africans wanted dignity, freedom and their land back.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 26. Why should Ugandans respect the national anthem? A: Ugandans respect the anthem because it is a national symbol that expresses love and loyalty to the country.. Standing at attention during the anthem shows patriotism.
chunks.source: Standing at attention during the anthem shows patriotism.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 27. State one way the national anthem is respected. A: By standing at attention silently whenever it is played or sung.. We also sing it with pride and never disrespect it.
chunks.source: We also sing it with pride and never disrespect it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 28. Name the African nationalist who formed ANC party in 1912. A: Pixley ka Isaka Seme. Seme founded the ANC in 1912 to fight for the rights of black South Africans.
chunks.source: Seme founded the ANC in 1912 to fight for the rights of black South Africans.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 29. Give the reason why Tanganyika got independence earlier than Uganda and Kenya. A: Tanganyika was a UN trust territory which Britain prepared for independence faster, and it had no stubborn white settlers blocking African advance.. Tanganyika became independent in 1961, ahead of Uganda (1962) and Kenya (1963).
chunks.source: Tanganyika became independent in 1961, ahead of Uganda (1962) and Kenya (1963).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 30. Why was Liberia not colonised? A: Liberia was founded by freed American slaves and was protected by the USA, so European powers left it alone.. Its American connection kept colonisers away.
chunks.source: Its American connection kept colonisers away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 31. Briefly write short notes about the following personalities; (i) De-Klerk (ii) Bishop Desmond Tutu (iii) Izaka Seme A: (i) De Klerk: the last apartheid president who released Mandela and ended apartheid. (ii) Bishop Desmond Tutu: the Anglican archbishop who campaigned against apartheid. (iii) Izaka Seme: founded the ANC in 1912.. Each played a key role in South Africa's freedom story.
chunks.source: Each played a key role in South Africa's freedom story.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 32. State any two methods which people can use to choose their leaders at a polling station. A: (i) Secret ballot (ticking on a ballot paper). (ii) Lining up behind a candidate or showing hands.. Voting must be free and fair for democracy to work.
chunks.source: Voting must be free and fair for democracy to work.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 1. Why is Africa called the cradle land of man kind? A: The earliest human fossils were discovered in Africa, for example at Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania.. This proves mankind first appeared in Africa.
chunks.source: This proves mankind first appeared in Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 2. State the original inhabitants in the following regions. (i) North Africa (ii) East Africa (iii) South Africa A: (i) North Africa: the Berbers. (ii) East Africa: the Bushmen (San). (iii) South Africa: the San and Khoikhoi.. Later migrations displaced these first inhabitants.
chunks.source: Later migrations displaced these first inhabitants.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 3. Give the main ethnic groups of people in Africa. A: The main ethnic groups of Africa are the Bantu, Nilotes, Cushites, Berbers, Pygmies and the San.. Africa's people belong to several large language and culture families.
chunks.source: Africa's people belong to several large language and culture families.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 3b. What is an Ethnic group? A: An ethnic group is a large group of people with a common origin, language and culture.. The Bantu are the largest ethnic group in Africa.
chunks.source: The Bantu are the largest ethnic group in Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 4. Which source of history is commonly used in most schools? A: Oral tradition. Elders tell stories of the past, which pupils learn in school.
chunks.source: Elders tell stories of the past, which pupils learn in school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 5. Which ethnic group originated from West Africa? A: The Bantu. The Bantu originated around Cameroon/Nigeria in West Africa and spread across central, eastern and southern Africa.
chunks.source: The Bantu originated around Cameroon/Nigeria in West Africa and spread across central, eastern and southern Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. How is culture important? A: Culture gives people identity, unity and moral values, and it attracts tourists.. Through culture we know who we are.
chunks.source: Through culture we know who we are.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 7. Where in Africa do the Bushmen live today? A: In the Kalahari Desert of Botswana and Namibia. The Bushmen are hunter-gatherers of the Kalahari.
chunks.source: The Bushmen are hunter-gatherers of the Kalahari.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. Why did the movement of people between North Africa and West Africa begin? A: The movement began because of the Trans-Saharan trade between North and West Africa.. Traders crossed the desert exchanging gold and salt.
chunks.source: Traders crossed the desert exchanging gold and salt.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. What was the main cause of Ngoni migration? What is the main occupation of the hamates? A: The main cause of Ngoni migration was fleeing from the wars of Shaka Zulu (the mfecane). The Hamites' main occupation is pastoralism (cattle keeping).. The Ngoni ran south and east to escape Shaka's armies.
chunks.source: The Ngoni ran south and east to escape Shaka's armies.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10. How are the archeologists important to people? A: Archaeologists dig up and study fossils and old objects, helping us learn about the past.. Their discoveries, like early human fossils, prove Africa is the cradle of mankind.
chunks.source: Their discoveries, like early human fossils, prove Africa is the cradle of mankind.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. Give 3 problems faced by early migrants in different parts of Africa. A: (i) Attacks by wild animals and hostile tribes. (ii) Hunger, thirst and diseases on the journey. (iii) Difficult terrain of forests, deserts and rivers.. Early migrants travelled on foot through dangerous land.
chunks.source: Early migrants travelled on foot through dangerous land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. What were the San and Khoikhoi previously known as? A: The Bushmen and the Hottentots. These old names are no longer used; today we say the San and Khoikhoi.
chunks.source: These old names are no longer used; today we say the San and Khoikhoi.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. How were the people of Africa politically organised before the coming of foreigners? A: They were organised in kingdoms, chiefdoms and clans under kings, chiefs and elders.. Foreigners found Africans already governing themselves.
chunks.source: Foreigners found Africans already governing themselves.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 14. Give two reasons why people of long ago migrated. A: They migrated to search for fertile land, water and pasture, and to run away from wars, drought and epidemics.. The search for survival drove early migrations.
chunks.source: The search for survival drove early migrations.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. Identify two reasons why people migrate today. A: (i) To look for employment. (ii) To access better social services like education and health.. Today people move mainly for a better life.
chunks.source: Today people move mainly for a better life.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 16. Why did the Bantu choose to settle in areas with fertile soils? A: The Bantu were cultivators, so they settled where the soils were fertile for growing crops.. Fertile land meant good harvests.
chunks.source: Fertile land meant good harvests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 17. Give three effects of migrations in Africa. A: (i) Intermarriage and emergence of new languages. (ii) Spread of iron working and new crops. (iii) Conflicts between groups.. Migrations mixed cultures across the continent.
chunks.source: Migrations mixed cultures across the continent.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 18. Give two effects of trans-Saharan trade. A: (i) It spread Islam in Africa. (ii) It led to the growth of towns like Timbuktu and Kano.. Trade brought religion, wealth and new ideas.
chunks.source: Trade brought religion, wealth and new ideas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 19. What was the original homeland of Nilotics? A: Bahr-el-Ghazal in South Sudan. From there the Nilotes moved south into Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania.
chunks.source: From there the Nilotes moved south into Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 20. Outline two tribes in Africa who purely live a nomadic life. A: (i) Fulani (ii) Tuareg (also accepted: Masai). These groups move with their animals all year round.
chunks.source: These groups move with their animals all year round.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 21. Name three Nilotic groups who settled in East Africa. A: (i) Plain Nilotes (ii) Highland Nilotes (iii) River-Lake Nilotes. Examples are the Karamojong, the Sebei and the Acholi.
chunks.source: Examples are the Karamojong, the Sebei and the Acholi.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 22. How did the introduction of iron working encourage people to migrate? A: Iron tools helped the Bantu clear forests for farming and make better weapons, so they could move into new lands.. Iron hoes and axes opened up new settlement areas.
chunks.source: Iron hoes and axes opened up new settlement areas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 23. Why is Bunyoro Kitara Empire remembered in the economy of East Africa? A: It is remembered for introducing iron working and the long-horned cattle in East Africa.. The Bachwezi rulers of Bunyoro-Kitara advanced farming and cattle keeping.
chunks.source: The Bachwezi rulers of Bunyoro-Kitara advanced farming and cattle keeping.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 24. State two characteristics of kingdoms. A: (i) They had centralised leadership under a king. (ii) Leadership was hereditary.. Kingdoms were organised states with clear rulers.
chunks.source: Kingdoms were organised states with clear rulers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 25. Suggest two reasons why more people choose to settle in one area than another. A: (i) Fertile soils and reliable rainfall. (ii) Availability of jobs and social services.. People settle where life is easy and promising.
chunks.source: People settle where life is easy and promising.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 26. How can a high population in the country affect each of the following; (i) Market for goods (ii) labour needed to produce goods. A: (i) Market for goods: a big population gives a large market. (ii) Labour needed: a big population gives plenty of labour.. Many people means many buyers and many workers.
chunks.source: Many people means many buyers and many workers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 27. Give two reasons why the government of Uganda conducts population census. A: (i) To know the number of people for planning services. (ii) To allocate resources and plan development.. Governments count people to serve them better.
chunks.source: Governments count people to serve them better.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 28. Why didn’t some ethnic groups form kingdoms? A: Some groups were too small or kept moving as pastoralists, so they remained in clans under elders.. Kingdoms needed large settled populations.
chunks.source: Kingdoms needed large settled populations.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 29. How were camels important during the trans-saharan trade? A: Camels carried heavy loads of goods and could travel long desert distances without water.. They were called the ships of the desert.
chunks.source: They were called the ships of the desert.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 30. Why did traders move in caravans during the trans-saharan trade? A: Traders moved in caravans for protection against robbers and wild animals in the desert.. There is safety in numbers on a dangerous journey.
chunks.source: There is safety in numbers on a dangerous journey.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 31. Why are the people of Meroe remembered in the history of Africa? A: The people of Meroe are remembered for developing iron smelting, one of the earliest iron industries in Africa.. Meroe in Sudan was an ancient centre of iron working.
chunks.source: Meroe in Sudan was an ancient centre of iron working.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 33. State any one Bantu tribe in each of the following countries. (a)Tanzania (b) South Africa (c) Nigerian A: (a) Tanzania: Sukuma (b) South Africa: Zulu (c) Nigeria: Yoruba. These are among the largest tribes in their countries.
chunks.source: These are among the largest tribes in their countries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 34. Which tribe in Nigeria practices transhumance? A: The Fulani. The Fulani move seasonally with their cattle between grazing lands.
chunks.source: The Fulani move seasonally with their cattle between grazing lands.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 1. Why was Africa first described as a dark continent by the Europeans? A: Africa was called the dark continent because its interior was unknown to Europeans.. Early maps showed Africa as a blank 'dark' interior.
chunks.source: Early maps showed Africa as a blank 'dark' interior.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 2. State two reasons why the Europeans took long to know the interior of Africa. A: (i) Thick forests, deserts and diseases like malaria blocked them. (ii) Some African tribes were hostile to strangers.. The interior was hard to enter and survive in.
chunks.source: The interior was hard to enter and survive in.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 3. Give the reason why Sir Churchhill Winston described Uganda as a pearl of Africa. A: Uganda's beauty - its good climate, fertile soils, forests, lakes and wildlife - impressed Churchill during his 1907 visit.. He described Uganda as a fairy-tale land of beauty.
chunks.source: He described Uganda as a fairy-tale land of beauty.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 4. State the reason why the Europeans referred the volcanic mountains of Kisolo and Kabale as Switzerland of Africa. A: The cool climate and beautiful hilly scenery of Kisoro and Kabale reminded Europeans of Switzerland.. Both areas are cool, hilly and green.
chunks.source: Both areas are cool, hilly and green.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 5. From which continent did the first foreigners to Uganda come? A: Asia (the Arabs). Arab traders from Asia were the first foreigners to reach Uganda.
chunks.source: Arab traders from Asia were the first foreigners to reach Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. How helpful were the dhows to the first foreigners to Africa? A: Dhows carried the first foreigners (Arabs) across the Indian Ocean to the East African coast.. Without dhows the Arabs could not have crossed the ocean.
chunks.source: Without dhows the Arabs could not have crossed the ocean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 7. How were the Monsoon winds important to the Arabs during their movement to Africa? A: The monsoon winds blew the dhows to the African coast and back to Asia in different seasons.. Sailors depended on these seasonal winds for ocean travel.
chunks.source: Sailors depended on these seasonal winds for ocean travel.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. State two reasons why Arabs came to the African continent. A: (i) To trade in goods like ivory and slaves. (ii) To spread Islam.. Trade came first; religion followed the traders.
chunks.source: Trade came first; religion followed the traders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. State three reasons why Islam took long to spread fast in Africa yet the Arabs came first. (ii) (iii A: (i) The Arabs were more interested in trade than in preaching. (ii) There was a language barrier. (iii) Africans strongly held their traditional beliefs.. Few Arabs worked as missionaries, so Islam spread slowly at first.
chunks.source: Few Arabs worked as missionaries, so Islam spread slowly at first.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10. State two positive, negative, economic and social effects for the coming of Arabs in Africa. Positive effects (ii) Negative effects (ii) Economic effects A: Positive: (i) Introduced new crops like rice and cloves. (ii) Led to the growth of Kiswahili. Negative: (i) Promoted the slave trade. (ii) Caused wars and suffering. Economic: (i) Promoted trade. (ii) Led to growth of towns. Social: (i) Spread Islam. (ii) Led to intermarriage.. The Arabs changed East Africa in good and bad ways.
chunks.source: The Arabs changed East Africa in good and bad ways.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. Name two towns in Africa that developed as a result of Arab settlement in Africa. A: (i) Zanzibar (ii) Mombasa (also accepted: Kilwa, Tabora).. Arab settlement turned coastal villages into busy trade towns.
chunks.source: Arab settlement turned coastal villages into busy trade towns.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. Define the following terms; (i) slave trade (ii) slavery A: (i) Slave trade: the buying and selling of human beings. (ii) Slavery: the state of being owned by another person as property.. Millions of Africans suffered under this cruel trade.
chunks.source: Millions of Africans suffered under this cruel trade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. Give two ways how the Arabs obtained slaves from Africa. A: (i) Through raids and kidnapping. (ii) By buying captives from local chiefs.. Some chiefs exchanged their own people for guns and goods.
chunks.source: Some chiefs exchanged their own people for guns and goods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 14. State two reasons why slaves were needed by the Arabs. A: (i) To work on plantations growing cloves and sugar. (ii) To serve as domestic servants and soldiers.. Arab plantations and homes needed cheap labour.
chunks.source: Arab plantations and homes needed cheap labour.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. Which town was the largest slave market in the following; (i) World (ii) East Africa A: (i) World: Zanzibar. (ii) East Africa: Zanzibar.. Zanzibar was the biggest slave market in the world in the 1800s.
chunks.source: Zanzibar was the biggest slave market in the world in the 1800s.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 16. State three evils of slave trade on the African continent. A: (i) It caused death and suffering. (ii) It caused depopulation. (iii) It caused famine and fear.. Whole villages were destroyed by slave raiders.
chunks.source: Whole villages were destroyed by slave raiders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 17. Give one reason why it was difficult to bring slave trade to an end. A: Slave trade was very profitable, and some African chiefs collaborated with the traders.. Greed kept the cruel trade alive for years.
chunks.source: Greed kept the cruel trade alive for years.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 18. Write short notes about the following in relation to slave trade. (i) Sir Samuel Baker (ii) Dr. David Livingstone (iii) Tipu – Tipu A: (i) Sir Samuel Baker: fought and stopped slave trade in northern Uganda. (ii) Dr. David Livingstone: exposed the horrors of slave trade to the world. (iii) Tippu Tip: a notorious Arab slave trader in East and Central Africa.. Two fought the trade; one profited from it.
chunks.source: Two fought the trade; one profited from it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 19. State three treaties that were signed to stop slave trade in Africa. A: (i) The Moresby Treaty of 1822. (ii) The Hamerton Treaty of 1845. (iii) The Frere Treaty of 1873.. Britain signed these treaties with the Sultan of Zanzibar to end slave trade.
chunks.source: Britain signed these treaties with the Sultan of Zanzibar to end slave trade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 20. How did slave trade lead to the following in Africa? (i) Famine (ii) Depopulation A: (i) Famine: the able-bodied were taken away, leaving no one to farm. (ii) Depopulation: many people were captured or killed, reducing the population.. Slave raids emptied villages of their workers.
chunks.source: Slave raids emptied villages of their workers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 21. Name the first group of Europeans to come to Africa. A: The Portuguese. The Portuguese were the first Europeans to sail around Africa to India.
chunks.source: The Portuguese were the first Europeans to sail around Africa to India.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 22. State two reasons for the coming of the Portuguese. A: (i) To find a sea route to India for the spice trade. (ii) To spread Christianity.. Portugal wanted spices and converts.
chunks.source: Portugal wanted spices and converts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 23. State three reasons for Portuguese settlement at the coast. A: (i) The coast had good natural harbours for their ships. (ii) They wanted resting places to refresh on the long voyage to India. (iii) To control trade at the coast.. The coast served their ships and their trade.
chunks.source: The coast served their ships and their trade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 1. What is Nationalism? A: Nationalism is the strong love for one's country and the desire for it to be free and self-governing.. It is the spirit that drove the independence struggles.
chunks.source: It is the spirit that drove the independence struggles.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 2. What term is used to describe a person who has strong love towards his or her country? A: A patriot. A patriot loves his country deeply and is ready to serve and defend it.
chunks.source: A patriot loves his country deeply and is ready to serve and defend it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 3. How did I.K. Musaazi contribute to the struggle for independence in Uganda? A: I.K. Musaazi formed the Uganda National Congress (UNC) in 1952, Uganda's first political party, which demanded independence.. Musaazi is called the father of Uganda's nationalism.
chunks.source: Musaazi is called the father of Uganda's nationalism.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 4. Define citizenship. A: Citizenship is the state of being a recognised member of a country with rights and duties.. Citizens vote, obey laws and defend their country.
chunks.source: Citizens vote, obey laws and defend their country.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 5. Why is George William Kakoma remembered in the history of Uganda? A: George William Kakoma composed Uganda's national anthem.. His anthem is sung at all national functions.
chunks.source: His anthem is sung at all national functions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 6. The National anthem of Uganda has three parts. In which part do we find these words, “For our own dear land, we shall always stand”? A: The third stanza. The words 'For our own dear land, we'll always stand' are in the third stanza: 'The Pearl of Africa's Crown.'
chunks.source: The words 'For our own dear land, we'll always stand' are in the third stanza: 'The Pearl of Africa's Crown.'

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 7. Give one reason why the National Anthem is respected. A: The anthem is a national symbol that shows love and loyalty to Uganda.. Respecting it is a duty of every citizen.
chunks.source: Respecting it is a duty of every citizen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 8. State one way the national anthem is respected. A: By standing at attention silently when it is played or sung.. We also sing it proudly and never misuse it.
chunks.source: We also sing it proudly and never misuse it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 9. Give any two reasons why Africans fought for independence. A: (i) To end colonial mistreatment such as forced labour and heavy taxes. (ii) To win self-rule and control their own resources.. Freedom and dignity drove the struggle.
chunks.source: Freedom and dignity drove the struggle.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 10. Give any two problems that Africans experienced during the fight for independence. A: (i) They were imprisoned, tortured and killed. (ii) Their movements and meetings were banned.. Colonialists used force to crush the freedom fighters.
chunks.source: Colonialists used force to crush the freedom fighters.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 11. Give the difference between citizenship by birth and by descent. A: Citizenship by birth is gained by being born in a country, while citizenship by descent is gained through parents who are citizens even if born abroad.. Birth place versus parents' citizenship.
chunks.source: Birth place versus parents' citizenship.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 12. Define Pan Africanism. A: Pan-Africanism was the movement calling for unity and solidarity of all Africans worldwide.. It inspired the fight against colonialism and racism.
chunks.source: It inspired the fight against colonialism and racism.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 13. State two peaceful means African natives used to demand for independence. A: (i) Peaceful demonstrations. (ii) Forming political parties and using the press.. Africans also used boycotts and strikes.
chunks.source: Africans also used boycotts and strikes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 14. State two reasons why Europeans never wanted African countries to control themselves. A: (i) They wanted to keep exploiting Africa's raw materials. (ii) They feared losing prestige and power in the world.. Independence meant Europe losing wealth and pride.
chunks.source: Independence meant Europe losing wealth and pride.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 15. Why are the following personalities remembered towards the independence struggles of their countries? (i) Nelson Mandela (ii) Kwame Nkrumah A: (i) Nelson Mandela: led the fight against apartheid in South Africa. (ii) Kwame Nkrumah: led Ghana to independence and championed African unity.. Both are heroes of African freedom.
chunks.source: Both are heroes of African freedom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 16. State two possible reasons why Africans were defeated in their struggle for independence. A: (i) The Europeans had superior weapons. (ii) Africans were disunited and fought separately.. Guns plus African disunity led to defeat.
chunks.source: Guns plus African disunity led to defeat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 17. What was the main reason for the creation of the Pan African Movement? A: To unite Africans in the struggle against colonialism and racism.. A united Africa could defeat colonialism faster.
chunks.source: A united Africa could defeat colonialism faster.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 18. State three ways the African natives were oppressed during colonial era. A: (i) Forced labour. (ii) Heavy taxation. (iii) Land grabbing and racial segregation.. Colonial oppression touched every part of African life.
chunks.source: Colonial oppression touched every part of African life.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 19. Name the African nationalist who led Zambia to independence. A: Kenneth Kaunda. Kaunda led Zambia to independence in 1964.
chunks.source: Kaunda led Zambia to independence in 1964.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 20. State any one reason why persons aged 18 and above take part in National elections. A: The constitution allows every adult citizen aged 18 and above to vote and choose leaders.. Voting is a right and duty of adult citizens.
chunks.source: Voting is a right and duty of adult citizens.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 21. Define the term election. A: An election is the process by which people choose their leaders through voting.. Uganda holds general elections every five years.
chunks.source: Uganda holds general elections every five years.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 22. Give one reason why elections are conducted in a democratic government. A: Elections let people choose the leaders they want peacefully.. They are the heart of democracy.
chunks.source: They are the heart of democracy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 23. How is democracy practiced in schools today? A: Democracy is practised in schools through electing prefects and class leaders.. Pupils vote for the leaders they want.
chunks.source: Pupils vote for the leaders they want.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 24. What is patriotism? A: Patriotism is the love and devotion one has for his or her country.. Patriots serve their country faithfully.
chunks.source: Patriots serve their country faithfully.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 25. State the difference between independence and nationalism. A: Independence is the state of being free and self-governing, while nationalism is the strong desire and love that drives people to seek that freedom.. Nationalism is the spirit; independence is the result.
chunks.source: Nationalism is the spirit; independence is the result.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 26. Name two African countries that were not colonized. A: (i) Ethiopia (ii) Liberia. These two countries were never colonised.
chunks.source: These two countries were never colonised.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 27. State two reasons why Ethiopia was not colonized. A: (i) Ethiopia had a strong army that defeated Italy at Adwa in 1896. (ii) Emperor Menelik II united Ethiopians against the invaders.. The Adwa victory is celebrated across Africa.
chunks.source: The Adwa victory is celebrated across Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 28. Name the first political party in each of the following countries. (i) Ghana (ii) Uganda A: (i) Ghana: Convention People's Party (CPP). (ii) Uganda: Uganda National Congress (UNC).. Nkrumah formed the CPP; Musaazi formed the UNC.
chunks.source: Nkrumah formed the CPP; Musaazi formed the UNC.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 29. Why was Ghana called The Gold Coast before attaining its independence? A: Ghana was rich in gold, which Europeans called the 'Gold Coast'.. The name described its greatest mineral wealth.
chunks.source: The name described its greatest mineral wealth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 30. Why was Liberia not colonized? A: Liberia was founded by freed American slaves and enjoyed the protection of the United States.. America's protection kept European colonisers away.
chunks.source: America's protection kept European colonisers away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 31. How is tribalism a threat to Nationalism? A: Tribalism divides people along tribal lines and destroys the unity needed for nationalism.. A divided nation cannot stand together.
chunks.source: A divided nation cannot stand together.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 32. Give the reason why Tanganyika, the present Tanzania got independence earlier than Uganda and Kenya. A: Tanganyika was a UN trust territory which Britain prepared for independence faster, and it had few white settlers opposing African rule.. Nyerere's TANU also united Tanganyikans early.
chunks.source: Nyerere's TANU also united Tanganyikans early.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 33. Name three African Nationalists who were behind Ethiopia’s defeat to the Italians against colonialism. A: Emperor Menelik II led the Ethiopian forces; his generals and united Ethiopian warriors defeated the Italians at Adwa.. Ethiopia's victory was won under Menelik II's leadership in 1896.
chunks.source: Ethiopia's victory was won under Menelik II's leadership in 1896.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 34. Which political party led South Africa to independence? A: The African National Congress (ANC). The ANC led the long fight that ended apartheid in 1994.
chunks.source: The ANC led the long fight that ended apartheid in 1994.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 35. Name the African Nationalist who formed ANC party in 1912. A: Pixley ka Isaka Seme. Seme founded the ANC in 1912 to defend black people's rights.
chunks.source: Seme founded the ANC in 1912 to defend black people's rights.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 36. Briefly write short notes about the following personalities. (i) De-Klerk (ii) Bishop Desmond Tutu (iii) Chief Albert Luthuri A: (i) De Klerk: the last apartheid president who freed Mandela and ended apartheid. (ii) Bishop Desmond Tutu: the archbishop who campaigned against apartheid and won the Nobel Peace Prize. (iii) Chief Albert Luthuli: ANC president who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1960.. Each helped end apartheid in his own way.
chunks.source: Each helped end apartheid in his own way.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 37. State any two methods which people can use to cast their votes at a polling station. (ii) P.7 TOPICAL QUESTIONS FOR TERM II SOCIAL A: (i) Secret ballot. (ii) Lining up behind the candidate of one's choice.. Both methods let voters choose freely.
chunks.source: Both methods let voters choose freely.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 1. Write O.A.U in full. A: Organisation of African Unity. The OAU was formed in Addis Ababa in 1963.
chunks.source: The OAU was formed in Addis Ababa in 1963.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 2. Give two reasons why O.A.U was formed. A: (i) To promote unity and solidarity among African states. (ii) To defend their independence and territorial integrity.. Newly independent states wanted to protect their hard-won freedom together.
chunks.source: Newly independent states wanted to protect their hard-won freedom together.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 3. Why were the headquarters of O.A.U put in Ethiopia? A: Ethiopia was never colonised, so it was neutral and a symbol of African freedom respected by all.. No member could claim Ethiopia favoured colonisers.
chunks.source: No member could claim Ethiopia favoured colonisers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 4. Name two founder members of O.A.U in each of the following regions. (a) North Africa (b) West Africa (c) East Africa. A: (a) North Africa: (i) Egypt (ii) Algeria. (b) West Africa: (i) Ghana (ii) Nigeria. (c) East Africa: (i) Uganda (ii) Kenya.. Thirty-two states founded the OAU in 1963.
chunks.source: Thirty-two states founded the OAU in 1963.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 5. Give any two achievements of O.A.U. A: (i) It supported liberation movements that ended colonialism and apartheid. (ii) It promoted unity and settled disputes among members.. The OAU gave Africa one strong voice.
chunks.source: The OAU gave Africa one strong voice.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. Why is Kwame Nkrumah remembered in the History of Africa? A: Kwame Nkrumah is remembered as Ghana's independence hero and a great champion of African unity who pushed for the OAU.. He wanted a United States of Africa.
chunks.source: He wanted a United States of Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 7. Outline two failures of O.A.U. A: (i) It failed to stop civil wars, for example in Rwanda. (ii) It failed to promote economic development.. Without its own army and with the non-interference rule, the OAU was weak.
chunks.source: Without its own army and with the non-interference rule, the OAU was weak.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. Name two organs of O.A.U. A: (i) The Assembly of Heads of State and Government. (ii) The Council of Ministers.. The Assembly made the big decisions.
chunks.source: The Assembly made the big decisions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. Why did South Africa take long to become a member of O.A.U? A: South Africa was under the apartheid regime which the OAU opposed; it joined only after apartheid ended in 1994.. The OAU would not admit a racist government.
chunks.source: The OAU would not admit a racist government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10. Why was O.A.U transformed into AU? A: The OAU was changed into the AU to pursue economic integration and peace more effectively, like the European Union.. The AU was launched in 2002 in Durban, South Africa.
chunks.source: The AU was launched in 2002 in Durban, South Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. Why was it important for member states of O.A.U to unite after independence? A: Unity gave them a stronger voice in world affairs and helped them assist liberation struggles in remaining colonies.. Together they were stronger.
chunks.source: Together they were stronger.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. Give any three organs of the AU. A: (i) The Assembly. (ii) The Executive Council. (iii) The Pan-African Parliament.. The AU also has the AU Commission and the Peace and Security Council.
chunks.source: The AU also has the AU Commission and the Peace and Security Council.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. Define the term decolonization of Africa. A: Decolonisation is the process by which colonies gained independence from colonial rulers.. Africa's decolonisation peaked in the 1960s.
chunks.source: Africa's decolonisation peaked in the 1960s.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 14. Give two objectives of AU. A: (i) To promote economic development and integration. (ii) To promote peace and security in Africa.. The AU wants a developed, peaceful Africa.
chunks.source: The AU wants a developed, peaceful Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. What is a common market? A: A common market is a group of countries that trade freely by reducing taxes on each other's goods.. COMESA and the EAC are common markets.
chunks.source: COMESA and the EAC are common markets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 16. Give 4 examples of common markets in Africa. A: (i) COMESA (ii) EAC (iii) ECOWAS (iv) SADC. These blocs make trade easier across Africa.
chunks.source: These blocs make trade easier across Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 17. Write 3 reasons why COMESA was formed. A: (i) To promote trade among member states. (ii) To create a bigger market for goods. (iii) To encourage economic cooperation.. COMESA covers Eastern and Southern Africa.
chunks.source: COMESA covers Eastern and Southern Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 18. In which two ways do common markets help to promote trade in Africa? A: (i) They lower taxes on goods traded between members. (ii) They give producers a larger market to sell to.. Cheaper goods and more customers help trade grow.
chunks.source: Cheaper goods and more customers help trade grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 19. State two challenges facing the AU. A: (i) Civil wars in member states. (ii) Shortage of funds from unpaid contributions.. Conflict and empty treasuries slow the AU.
chunks.source: Conflict and empty treasuries slow the AU.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 20. Which regional body unites countries in the horn of Africa? A: IGAD (Intergovernmental Authority on Development). IGAD unites the Horn of Africa countries.
chunks.source: IGAD unites the Horn of Africa countries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 21. Write the following in full. (i) ADC (ii) COMESA (iii) ECOWAS A: (i) ADC - African Development Community. (ii) COMESA - Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa. (iii) ECOWAS - Economic Community of West African States.. These bodies promote regional economic cooperation.
chunks.source: These bodies promote regional economic cooperation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 22. Which city in Africa hosts the headquarters of COMESA? A: Lusaka, Zambia. COMESA's headquarters are in the Zambian capital.
chunks.source: COMESA's headquarters are in the Zambian capital.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 23. Identify the member states of E.A.C. A: Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Democratic Republic of Congo, South Sudan and Somalia.. The EAC has grown from three to eight partner states.
chunks.source: The EAC has grown from three to eight partner states.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 24. How did OAU help to end apartheid in South Africa? A: The OAU funded and armed liberation movements, isolated the apartheid regime, and pressed for sanctions until apartheid fell in 1994.. Its liberation committee supported fighters across Southern Africa.
chunks.source: Its liberation committee supported fighters across Southern Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 25. Give two reasons why the E.A.C was revived? A: (i) To expand trade and markets in the region. (ii) To promote economic and political cooperation.. The revived EAC aims at a common market and even political federation.
chunks.source: The revived EAC aims at a common market and even political federation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 26. In which two ways has AU tried to promote peace in Somalia? A: (i) It deployed peacekeeping troops (AMISOM). (ii) It supported peace talks and reconciliation.. AU soldiers helped Somalia fight terrorists.
chunks.source: AU soldiers helped Somalia fight terrorists.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 27. What is the role of ECOMOG in West Africa? A: ECOMOG keeps peace in West Africa by stopping wars and protecting civilians.. It is the military wing of ECOWAS.
chunks.source: It is the military wing of ECOWAS.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 28. Which two groups which joined together to form the O.A.U? A: (i) The Casablanca Group (ii) The Monrovia Group. These two groups of states united to form the OAU in 1963.
chunks.source: These two groups of states united to form the OAU in 1963.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 1. In which way is money important in economic development? A: Money is used as a medium of exchange, for saving and for investing in businesses.. Without money, trade would depend on slow barter exchange.
chunks.source: Without money, trade would depend on slow barter exchange.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 2. Why are rivers considered to be an economic resource? A: Rivers provide fish, water for irrigation, hydro-electricity, transport and tourist attraction.. A river is a natural economic asset to the people near it.
chunks.source: A river is a natural economic asset to the people near it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 3. Apart from coffee, mention the major cash crop grown in Ethiopia on plantations. A: Chat (khat). Ethiopia grows coffee and chat as major cash crops on plantations.
chunks.source: Ethiopia grows coffee and chat as major cash crops on plantations.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 4. How is labour important in a country’s economic development? A: Labour provides the human workforce that produces goods and services in a country.. Without workers, natural resources stay unused.
chunks.source: Without workers, natural resources stay unused.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 5. Which type of transport is most suitable in developing tourism in East Africa? A: Road transport (also accepted: air transport). Good roads let tourists reach game parks and attractions easily.
chunks.source: Good roads let tourists reach game parks and attractions easily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. Apart from Democratic Republic of Congo, identify one country in central Africa with developed timber industries. A: Republic of Congo (also accepted: Gabon, Cameroon). The Congo Basin forests support big timber industries.
chunks.source: The Congo Basin forests support big timber industries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 7. Compare Zambia and Uganda in terms of economy. A: Zambia's economy depends mainly on copper mining, while Uganda's economy depends mainly on agriculture.. Zambia is mineral-rich; Uganda is farm-rich.
chunks.source: Zambia is mineral-rich; Uganda is farm-rich.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. Give one reason why South Africa is highly industrialized. A: South Africa has abundant minerals (gold, diamonds, coal), enough capital and well-developed energy supply.. Minerals plus money plus power built its industries.
chunks.source: Minerals plus money plus power built its industries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. What do we call the type of industries that deal in provision of services in an economy? A: Tertiary industries. Banks, hotels, transport and schools are tertiary (service) industries.
chunks.source: Banks, hotels, transport and schools are tertiary (service) industries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10. State one example of a renewable energy resource apart from hydro-electricity. A: Solar energy (also accepted: wind, geothermal). The sun, wind and underground heat are renewable and never run out.
chunks.source: The sun, wind and underground heat are renewable and never run out.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. How is Egypt able to grow crops yet it’s a desert country? A: Egypt irrigates its crops with water from the River Nile, stored by the Aswan Dam.. The Nile turns desert into farmland.
chunks.source: The Nile turns desert into farmland.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. Give two reasons why Akasombo dam was constructed. A: (i) To generate hydro-electricity. (ii) To provide power for the aluminium smelting industry.. The Akosombo Dam created Lake Volta and powers Ghana's industries.
chunks.source: The Akosombo Dam created Lake Volta and powers Ghana's industries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. In which two ways has communication become easy in Uganda today? A: (i) Through mobile phones. (ii) Through the internet and FM radios.. Modern technology has made communication fast and cheap.
chunks.source: Modern technology has made communication fast and cheap.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 14. Which type of education promotes literacy and numeracy? A: Primary (basic) education. Learning to read, write and count starts in primary school.
chunks.source: Learning to read, write and count starts in primary school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. Write any two factors that have kept DRC under developed yet it has large mineral deposits. A: (i) Long civil wars and instability. (ii) Corruption and poor infrastructure.. War and bad leadership waste the country's mineral wealth.
chunks.source: War and bad leadership waste the country's mineral wealth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 16. In which two ways can land locked countries solve the problems they face in import and export trade. A: (i) By using the seaports of neighbouring countries like Mombasa and Dar-es-salaam. (ii) By keeping good relations with transit neighbours.. Landlocked countries depend on their neighbours' ports for trade.
chunks.source: Landlocked countries depend on their neighbours' ports for trade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 1. What is a challenge? A: A challenge is a difficult problem or task that needs great effort to overcome.. Africa faces challenges like poverty, wars and diseases.
chunks.source: Africa faces challenges like poverty, wars and diseases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 2. In which one way can illiteracy lead to poverty? A: Illiterate people cannot get good jobs, so they earn little and stay poor.. Without education, people miss better-paying work.
chunks.source: Without education, people miss better-paying work.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 3. State one way of improving labour force in Africa. A: By training workers through education and vocational skills.. Skilled, healthy workers produce more.
chunks.source: Skilled, healthy workers produce more.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 4. In which way can teenage pregnancies and early marriages be controlled? A: Through educating the youth about the dangers and enforcing laws against early marriage.. Keeping girls in school delays marriage and pregnancy.
chunks.source: Keeping girls in school delays marriage and pregnancy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 5. (a) Write down two economic challenges facing East African countries. (b) State the solution to each of the problems given above. A: (a)(i) Unemployment. (ii) Heavy foreign debts. (b)(i) Create jobs through industrialisation. (ii) Borrow wisely and fight corruption.. Jobs and careful borrowing reduce economic pain.
chunks.source: Jobs and careful borrowing reduce economic pain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. Give two reasons for the increasing number of refugees in Africa. A: (i) Civil wars and conflicts. (ii) Natural disasters like drought and floods.. People flee fighting and hunger across borders.
chunks.source: People flee fighting and hunger across borders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 7. State two disadvantages of foreign aid to developing countries. A: Foreign aid creates dependency and often comes with strict conditions from donors.. Aid can also delay a country from solving its own problems.
chunks.source: Aid can also delay a country from solving its own problems.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. Write short notes about the following; (i) Infant mortality rate. (ii) Maternal mortality rate. A: (i) Infant mortality rate: the number of babies who die before their first birthday out of every 1,000 born. (ii) Maternal mortality rate: the number of mothers who die during childbirth out of a given number of births.. High rates show poor health services.
chunks.source: High rates show poor health services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. Give two economic effects of AIDS in Uganda. A: (i) It kills the energetic workers, reducing the labour force. (ii) It leaves many orphans who become a burden to families and the state.. AIDS weakens the economy by striking the working age group.
chunks.source: AIDS weakens the economy by striking the working age group.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10. Give two causes of famine in Africa. A: (i) Drought and unreliable rainfall. (ii) Wars that displace farmers.. Pests and poor farming methods also cause famine.
chunks.source: Pests and poor farming methods also cause famine.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. Write one disadvantage of exporting raw materials. A: Raw materials fetch low prices compared to finished goods, so the country earns little.. Processing adds value and income.
chunks.source: Processing adds value and income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. Outline two causes of famine in Africa. A: (i) Prolonged drought. (ii) Civil wars and insecurity.. Both stop people from growing food.
chunks.source: Both stop people from growing food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. In which two ways is famine a challenge in most African countries? A: (i) It causes hunger and malnutrition. (ii) It causes death and suffering.. Famine weakens the whole nation.
chunks.source: Famine weakens the whole nation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 14. Which ministry in Uganda is responsible for refugees in Uganda? A: The Office of the Prime Minister (OPM). Uganda's OPM handles refugees and disaster management.
chunks.source: Uganda's OPM handles refugees and disaster management.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. Give two ways in which African countries can discourage civil wars. A: (i) By promoting dialogue and peaceful settlement of disputes. (ii) By practising democracy and good governance.. Talking beats fighting.
chunks.source: Talking beats fighting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 1. Which organisation was replaced by United Nations Organisation? A: The League of Nations. The League failed to stop World War II, so the UNO replaced it in 1945.
chunks.source: The League failed to stop World War II, so the UNO replaced it in 1945.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 2. How does Uganda benefit from the common wealth organisation? A: Uganda gets scholarships, technical assistance, trade opportunities and sports links through the Commonwealth.. Commonwealth membership opens doors to Britain and other members.
chunks.source: Commonwealth membership opens doors to Britain and other members.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 3. Give two reasons why UNO was formed. A: (i) To promote world peace and prevent wars. (ii) To promote human rights and development.. The UNO was born in 1945 after the destruction of World War II.
chunks.source: The UNO was born in 1945 after the destruction of World War II.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 4. Which European country ruled Rwanda as a mandate territory after World War I? A: Belgium. After World War I, the League of Nations gave Rwanda to Belgium as a mandate territory.
chunks.source: After World War I, the League of Nations gave Rwanda to Belgium as a mandate territory.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 5. Identify any two organs of UNO. A: (i) The General Assembly. (ii) The Security Council.. Other organs are the Secretariat, the ICJ, ECOSOC and the Trusteeship Council.
chunks.source: Other organs are the Secretariat, the ICJ, ECOSOC and the Trusteeship Council.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. In which two ways has UNICEF helped to improve the living standards of Ugandans? A: (i) It supports immunisation of children. (ii) It supports education and provision of clean water.. UNICEF cares for the world's children.
chunks.source: UNICEF cares for the world's children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 7. Which UNO agency is responsible for each of the following? (i) Improving working conditions of labourers. (ii) Promoting culture, Education and Scientific research. (iii) Fighting hunger and malnutrition. (iv) Population control and family life education. A: (i) ILO (International Labour Organisation). (ii) UNESCO. (iii) FAO (Food and Agriculture Organisation). (iv) UNFPA (UN Population Fund).. Each UN agency has a special job in the world.
chunks.source: Each UN agency has a special job in the world.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. What do the olive branches of on the UNO flag symbolise? A: The olive branches symbolise world peace.. The UNO's main goal is to keep peace among nations.
chunks.source: The UNO's main goal is to keep peace among nations.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. Give two achievements of UNO. A: (i) It has kept peace through peacekeeping missions in troubled countries. (ii) It has promoted human rights and helped refugees through UNHCR.. The UNO also fights hunger and disease through its agencies.
chunks.source: The UNO also fights hunger and disease through its agencies.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10. Which countries qualify to be members of the common wealth? A: Countries that were once British colonies or accept the Commonwealth's values of democracy and good governance.. Membership is now open beyond the former British Empire.
chunks.source: Membership is now open beyond the former British Empire.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. State the difference between an ambassador and high commissioner. A: An ambassador represents his country in a foreign (non-Commonwealth) country, while a high commissioner represents his country in a fellow Commonwealth country.. Same job, different title by destination.
chunks.source: Same job, different title by destination.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. In which two ways does Uganda benefit from the European Union? A: (i) Uganda gets financial aid for development projects. (ii) Uganda gets a market for its exports in Europe.. The EU supports roads, water and education in Uganda.
chunks.source: The EU supports roads, water and education in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. Give any two projects in Uganda funded by the European Union. A: (i) Road construction projects. (ii) Water and sanitation projects.. The EU funds many development projects across Uganda.
chunks.source: The EU funds many development projects across Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 14. Give two similarities between the common wealth and UNO. A: (i) Both promote world peace. (ii) Both promote cooperation and development among members.. Both bodies bring nations together for common goals.
chunks.source: Both bodies bring nations together for common goals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. In which two ways did World War II lead to independence struggle in Africa? A: (i) Africans who fought in the war learnt military skills and demanded freedom. (ii) The war weakened European powers so they could no longer hold colonies tightly.. Returning soldiers asked why they fought for freedom abroad but had none at home.
chunks.source: Returning soldiers asked why they fought for freedom abroad but had none at home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 1. Name the type of climate described as hot and wet throughout the year. A: Equatorial climate. The equatorial climate is hot and wet throughout the year.
chunks.source: The equatorial climate is hot and wet throughout the year.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 2. Mention any one place where people get spiritual guidance. A: A church (also accepted: mosque, shrine). People go to places of worship for spiritual guidance.
chunks.source: People go to places of worship for spiritual guidance.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 3. State any one factors that attracted the Bantu cultivators to settle within the lake regions. A: Fertile soils and reliable rainfall (also accepted: fishing in the lakes). The Bantu were cultivators who needed good land for crops.
chunks.source: The Bantu were cultivators who needed good land for crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 4. Give any one way sand mining can negatively affect farming in an area. A: It destroys the soil structure and fertility, and leaves pits that cannot be farmed.. Sand mining removes the useful top soil.
chunks.source: Sand mining removes the useful top soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 5. Mention the national symbol which is similar to a school badge. A: The national emblem (coat of arms). Like a school badge, the coat of arms is a small official symbol of identity.
chunks.source: Like a school badge, the coat of arms is a small official symbol of identity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. How did Dr. Albert Cook socially contribute to the life of people of Uganda? A: He built Mengo Hospital and fought diseases like sleeping sickness, improving people's health.. Dr. Albert Cook was a missionary doctor who brought modern medicine to Uganda.
chunks.source: Dr. Albert Cook was a missionary doctor who brought modern medicine to Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 7. Name the river which separates Tanzania from Uganda. A: River Kagera. The Kagera forms part of the border between Tanzania and Uganda.
chunks.source: The Kagera forms part of the border between Tanzania and Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. Why is road maintenance in rural areas still difficult? A: Heavy rains damage the murram roads, and there is little money and few machines for repairs.. Rural roads are mostly murram and wash away in rain.
chunks.source: Rural roads are mostly murram and wash away in rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. Give any one reason why people make plans of what to buy before shopping. A: To avoid impulse buying and to spend within one's budget.. A shopping list helps one buy only what is planned and affordable.
chunks.source: A shopping list helps one buy only what is planned and affordable.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10. How did Johann Ludwig Krapt make it easy for the coastal people to understand the bible? A: He translated the Bible into Kiswahili, a language the coastal people understood.. Krapf was a German missionary and explorer at the East African coast.
chunks.source: Krapf was a German missionary and explorer at the East African coast.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. What was the main reason for the signing of Moresby treaty? A: To stop the slave trade. The Moresby Treaty of 1822 was signed between Britain and the Sultan of Zanzibar against slave trade.
chunks.source: The Moresby Treaty of 1822 was signed between Britain and the Sultan of Zanzibar against slave trade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. How has prolonged drought contributed to loss of lives in Uganda? A: Prolonged drought causes famine, hunger and death of people and animals.. Without rain, crops fail and water dries up.
chunks.source: Without rain, crops fail and water dries up.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. What happens to a law breaker when the court has proved him/ her guilty? A: He or she is punished (sentenced to prison or fined).. Courts punish the guilty to keep law and order.
chunks.source: Courts punish the guilty to keep law and order.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 14. How did the Namirembe agreement bring back happiness in the Buganda kingdom? A: The Namirembe Agreement of 1955 ended the Kabaka crisis and allowed Kabaka Mutesa II to return from exile.. Its signing restored peace and happiness in Buganda.
chunks.source: Its signing restored peace and happiness in Buganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. State any one role played by civil servants. A: Civil servants implement government policies and deliver services to the people.. Teachers, nurses and administrators are civil servants.
chunks.source: Teachers, nurses and administrators are civil servants.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 16. Name the body responsible for conserving the environment. A: NEMA (National Environment Management Authority). NEMA protects Uganda's environment from degradation.
chunks.source: NEMA protects Uganda's environment from degradation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 17. Give the importance of having voluntary workers in the district. A: Voluntary workers supplement government services and promote community development.. They serve without pay for the good of the community.
chunks.source: They serve without pay for the good of the community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 18. How is a scale useful to a map reader? A: A scale helps a map reader to measure real distances on the ground from the map.. With a scale, centimetres on the map become kilometres on the ground.
chunks.source: With a scale, centimetres on the map become kilometres on the ground.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 19. Below is the number plate of Dr. Tayala’s vehicle. What does letter U stand for on the number plate? UBA 600B A: Uganda. All Ugandan number plates start with the letter U.
chunks.source: All Ugandan number plates start with the letter U.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 20. Why is tourism called an invisible trade? A: Tourism earns foreign exchange without exporting physical goods - the 'goods' are services visitors enjoy.. Money comes in, but no goods go out, so it is called invisible trade.
