chunks.source: Money comes in, but no goods go out, so it is called invisible trade.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 21. Write NEMA in full. A: National Environment Management Authority. NEMA is the body responsible for conserving Uganda's environment.
chunks.source: NEMA is the body responsible for conserving Uganda's environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 22. Give any one way the early man protected himself from danger. A: He lived in caves, used fire, and made stone tools and weapons.. Early man also lived in groups for protection.
chunks.source: Early man also lived in groups for protection.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 23. Which type of timber is used in the ship building industry? A: Hard wood (such as mvule and mahogany). Hard wood is strong and resists water, suiting ship building.
chunks.source: Hard wood is strong and resists water, suiting ship building.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 24. Why is there no hydro-electricity in Kalangala district? A: Kalangala is made of islands in Lake Victoria with a small scattered population, making HEP supply costly and difficult.. Extending the power grid to islands is very expensive.
chunks.source: Extending the power grid to islands is very expensive.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 25. What does the Golden colour on the African Union flag represent? A: Africa's mineral wealth and natural resources. The gold colour on the AU flag stands for Africa's rich resources.
chunks.source: The gold colour on the AU flag stands for Africa's rich resources.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 26. Mention any one effect of lighting on buildings. 3 Turn Over A: Lightning can strike buildings and cause fire or destroy them.. That is why tall buildings have lightning conductors.
chunks.source: That is why tall buildings have lightning conductors.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 27. How do people in rural areas benefit from the establishment of small scale industries? A: They create jobs and provide goods and markets near the people.. Small industries bring work and services to villages.
chunks.source: Small industries bring work and services to villages.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 28. What do we call the sudden increase in the number of people living in an area? A: Rapid population growth (population explosion). It can also be called a population influx when caused by migration.
chunks.source: It can also be called a population influx when caused by migration.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 29. How does a school provide market to the community? A: The school buys food and supplies from the community, and pupils buy items from local shops.. Schools are big customers of the surrounding community.
chunks.source: Schools are big customers of the surrounding community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 30. Name the leader of the Democratic party who took part in the independence elections of Uganda. A: Benedicto Kiwanuka. Kiwanuka led the Democratic Party and became Uganda's first prime minister.
chunks.source: Kiwanuka led the Democratic Party and became Uganda's first prime minister.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 31. State any one way children abuse their rights. A: By dodging school, abusing drugs, or disrespecting parents and teachers.. Children abuse their rights when they misuse their freedoms.
chunks.source: Children abuse their rights when they misuse their freedoms.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 32. How was the Royal Geographical Society important to early explorers who came to Uganda? A: It sponsored and funded the early explorers who came to Uganda.. Explorers like Speke and Grant were supported by the Society.
chunks.source: Explorers like Speke and Grant were supported by the Society.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 33. Give any one way the government benefits from people when they pay taxes promptly. A: The government gets revenue to provide services like roads, schools and hospitals.. Taxes are the government's main source of income.
chunks.source: Taxes are the government's main source of income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 34. Name the only high land Nilotes tribe found in Uganda. A: The Sebei. The Sebei live on the slopes of Mount Elgon in eastern Uganda.
chunks.source: The Sebei live on the slopes of Mount Elgon in eastern Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 35. State any one common cause of accidents on water. In questions 36 – 40, answer Either Christianity or Islam but not alternatives in a number A: Overloading boats and travelling without life jackets.. Storms and untrained operators also cause water accidents.
chunks.source: Storms and untrained operators also cause water accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 41. a) State any two indicators of a good transport network system in a country. b) Give two ways a good transport network promotes development in a country. A: a) (i) Good tarmac roads. (ii) Many means of transport (also accepted: low transport fares). b) (i) It eases the movement of goods to markets. (ii) It creates jobs and promotes trade.. Good roads and many vehicles show a good network; such a network boosts trade and jobs.
chunks.source: Good roads and many vehicles show a good network; such a network boosts trade and jobs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 42. a) Name one selfless organization in Uganda which provides shelter/ homes for orphans. b) Apart from providing homes, how else do orphans benefit from the above organization? 5 Turn Over c) Mention any two other organizations which provide similar services to people in Uganda. A: a) SOS Children's Villages. b) They get education, health care and life skills.. Such organisations care for orphans beyond just housing them.
chunks.source: Such organisations care for orphans beyond just housing them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 43. a) What title is given to the head of the Judiciary? b) Give one example of people who make up the Judiciary. c) State any two roles of the Judiciary. A: a) The Chief Justice. b) Judges and magistrates. c) (i) They interpret laws. (ii) They punish law breakers.. The Judiciary is the arm of government that handles justice.
chunks.source: The Judiciary is the arm of government that handles justice.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 44. Match each river to the dam built on it. List A: River Niger, River Orange, River Zambezi. List B: Akosombo dam, Kariba dam, Verwoerd dam, Kainji dam. (River Congo has none of the listed dams.) A: River Niger - Kainji dam; River Orange - Verwoerd dam; River Zambezi - Kariba dam. (River Congo has none of the listed dams; its great dam is Inga.). Akosombo is on the Volta, Kariba on the Zambezi, Verwoerd on the Orange and Kainji on the Niger.
chunks.source: Akosombo is on the Volta, Kariba on the Zambezi, Verwoerd on the Orange and Kainji on the Niger.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 45. a) Name the major tourist attraction found in Mgahinga National park. b) Give any two reasons why the tourism industry in Uganda has developed. ii) c) What can the government of Uganda do to attract more tourists into the country? A: a) Mountain gorillas. b) (i) Uganda has many tourist attractions. (ii) There is peace and security. c) By advertising abroad, improving facilities and keeping security.. Mgahinga in southwestern Uganda protects the endangered mountain gorillas.
chunks.source: Mgahinga in southwestern Uganda protects the endangered mountain gorillas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 46. a)State any two factors that unite members of a nuclear family. ii) b) Give any two ways how order can be created in a home. A: a) (i) Love and cooperation. (ii) Respect and good communication. b) (i) Setting family rules. (ii) Sharing duties fairly.. Unity and order make a happy home.
chunks.source: Unity and order make a happy home.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 47. a) Name the organization that unites all the former colonies of the British empire. b) Give any two ways a country like Uganda benefits as a member of the above body. ii) c) State any one challenge the above body faces today. A: a) The Commonwealth. b) (i) Scholarships and technical aid. (ii) Trade opportunities with member states.. The Commonwealth unites Britain's former colonies.
chunks.source: The Commonwealth unites Britain's former colonies.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 48. a) What is urbanization? b) Give any two roles of urban centres to rural areas. ii) c) Give one role of rural areas to urban areas. 7 Turn Over A: a) Urbanisation is the increase in the number of people living in towns. b) (i) Urban centres provide markets for rural produce. (ii) They provide jobs and social services.. Towns grow as people move in for work and services.
chunks.source: Towns grow as people move in for work and services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 49. (b) Give the reason why the colonialists encouraged railway construction in East Africa. (c) Why is railway transport not commonly used by people in Uganda today? (d) Give any two ways faulting is important to the economic development of Uganda. A: (b) To transport raw materials to the coast and ease administration. (c) It is expensive and slow, with limited routes compared to road transport. (d) (i) Faulting forms rift valley lakes used for fishing and tourism. (ii) Faulting exposes minerals.. The Uganda Railway was built by the British to link Uganda to Mombasa.
chunks.source: The Uganda Railway was built by the British to link Uganda to Mombasa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 50. a) What is relief? b) Mention any one feature that was formed through faulting. For questions 51 – 54, answer Christianity or Islam not both on each A: a) Relief is the ups and downs (shape) of the land's surface. b) The rift valley (also accepted: block mountain).. Relief describes whether land is flat, hilly or mountainous.
chunks.source: Relief describes whether land is flat, hilly or mountainous.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. Why is Africa regarded as a Cradle land of man-kind? A: Africa is regarded as the cradle land of mankind because the earliest human fossils were discovered here.. Fossils at Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania prove humans first lived in Africa.
chunks.source: Fossils at Olduvai Gorge in Tanzania prove humans first lived in Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. What factor of climate influences settlement of people in an area? A: Rainfall (also accepted: temperature). People settle where the climate favours farming and comfort.
chunks.source: People settle where the climate favours farming and comfort.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10. Write ECOWAS in full. A: Economic Community of West African States. ECOWAS unites West African countries for trade and cooperation.
chunks.source: ECOWAS unites West African countries for trade and cooperation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. How are the Masai and Karamojong similar in their occupation? A: Both are pastoralists who keep cattle.. The Masai of Kenya/Tanzania and the Karamojong of Uganda are cattle keepers.
chunks.source: The Masai of Kenya/Tanzania and the Karamojong of Uganda are cattle keepers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. State any one way soil erosion is being reduced in Kabale. A: Through terracing the hills.. Terraces slow down running water on Kabale's steep hills.
chunks.source: Terraces slow down running water on Kabale's steep hills.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. Why are school assemblies important in a school? A: School assemblies pass information and build unity and discipline among pupils.. Announcements and guidance happen at assembly.
chunks.source: Announcements and guidance happen at assembly.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 14. Which colour on the Uganda flag symbolizes brotherhood of mankind? A: Black. The black band on Uganda's flag stands for the brotherhood of African people.
chunks.source: The black band on Uganda's flag stands for the brotherhood of African people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. What is the main duty of Judiciary organ to the democratic government? A: To interpret laws and punish law breakers, protecting justice in the country.. The Judiciary keeps the government within the law.
chunks.source: The Judiciary keeps the government within the law.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 16. Name the Pan Africanist who founded the Universal Negro-Improvement Association. A: Marcus Garvey. Garvey founded the UNIA to unite black people and promote 'Back to Africa'.
chunks.source: Garvey founded the UNIA to unite black people and promote 'Back to Africa'.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 17. Why is tourism called an invisible trade? A: Tourism earns foreign exchange without exporting physical goods.. Visitors pay for services, so earnings are 'invisible'.
chunks.source: Visitors pay for services, so earnings are 'invisible'.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 18. Why are slopes of mountain Kenya densely populated? A: The slopes have fertile volcanic soils and receive reliable rainfall.. Good soils and rain attract many farmers.
chunks.source: Good soils and rain attract many farmers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 19. Mention any one characteristic of rift valley lakes. A: They are long, narrow, deep and salty.. Rift valley lakes lie in the deep cracks of the rift.
chunks.source: Rift valley lakes lie in the deep cracks of the rift.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 20. Which animal is commonly referred to as the ship of the desert? A: The camel. The camel carries loads across deserts, like a ship carries cargo across seas.
chunks.source: The camel carries loads across deserts, like a ship carries cargo across seas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 21. How did Mungo Park meet his death in West Africa? A: He drowned in the River Niger after his boat was attacked at the Bussa rapids.. Mungo Park explored the Niger in West Africa.
chunks.source: Mungo Park explored the Niger in West Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 22. Which type of land form covers the largest part of Africa? A: The plateau. Most of Africa is a high flat land.
chunks.source: Most of Africa is a high flat land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 23. In which direction will David face if he turns anti-clock wise from North through 900? A: West. Turning anti-clockwise (left) from North by 90 degrees points West.
chunks.source: Turning anti-clockwise (left) from North by 90 degrees points West.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 24. What is a bye-election? A: A bye-election is an election held to fill a vacant political seat between general elections.. It happens when a leader dies, resigns or is removed.
chunks.source: It happens when a leader dies, resigns or is removed.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 25. Name the winds that bring rains to the Mediterranean region in winter. A: The westerly winds. Westerlies bring winter rain to Mediterranean lands.
chunks.source: Westerlies bring winter rain to Mediterranean lands.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 26. Give one use of a mobile phone to the youth today. A: For communication and accessing information (also accepted: mobile money).. Phones connect the youth to people and knowledge.
chunks.source: Phones connect the youth to people and knowledge.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 27. What is decentralization? A: Decentralisation is the transfer of powers and services from the central government to local governments.. It brings services nearer to the people.
chunks.source: It brings services nearer to the people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 28. Name the most common type of fish caught in Lake Victoria. A: Tilapia. Tilapia is the main fish caught in Lake Victoria.
chunks.source: Tilapia is the main fish caught in Lake Victoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 29. How did Alexander Mackey promote Education in Uganda? A: He taught reading, writing and technical skills, and set up a printing press.. Mackay was a missionary who brought formal education to Buganda.
chunks.source: Mackay was a missionary who brought formal education to Buganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 30. Who was the founder of the Imperial British East-African Company? A: Sir William Mackinnon. He formed the company to administer British interests in East Africa.
chunks.source: He formed the company to administer British interests in East Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 31. Why was Liberia not colonized? A: Liberia was founded by freed American slaves and protected by the USA.. European powers respected America's interest in Liberia.
chunks.source: European powers respected America's interest in Liberia.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 32. Why are the Miombo woodland of Tanzania poorly inhabited? A: They are infested with tsetse flies and have poor soils.. Tsetse flies spread diseases to people and cattle.
chunks.source: Tsetse flies spread diseases to people and cattle.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 33. Name one instrument of power given to Yoweri Kaguta Museveni when he was sworn in as president of Uganda. A: The Constitution (also accepted: the presidential standard, the national seal). These symbols represent the authority of the presidency.
chunks.source: These symbols represent the authority of the presidency.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 34. State one result from the signing of the 1900 Buganda Agreement. A: Buganda lost much of its land, which was divided among chiefs as mailo land, and the Kabaka's powers were reduced.. The agreement also fixed Buganda's boundaries and introduced taxes.
chunks.source: The agreement also fixed Buganda's boundaries and introduced taxes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 35. Give one contribution of Indians to the economic development of Uganda. For each of the questions 36-40, answer either Christian or Islamic but not both alternatives in a number. A: They promoted trade and set up industries and businesses in Uganda.. Indians also helped build the Uganda Railway as labourers.
chunks.source: Indians also helped build the Uganda Railway as labourers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 41. Match each lake to the process that formed it. List A: Lake Katwe, Lake Albert, Lake Kyoga, Kabaka's lake. List B: faulting, man-made lake, volcanicity, down warping. A: Lake Katwe - volcanicity; Lake Albert - faulting; Lake Kyoga - down warping; Kabaka's lake - man-made lake.. Katwe is a crater lake, Albert lies in the rift valley, Kyoga in a down-warped basin, and Kabaka's lake was dug by men.
chunks.source: Katwe is a crater lake, Albert lies in the rift valley, Kyoga in a down-warped basin, and Kabaka's lake was dug by men.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 42. a) What is a budget? b) Give two reasons why a school needs a budget. ii) c) Which ministry prepares a National budget in Uganda? A: a) A budget is a plan of expected income and expenditure. b) (i) To plan and control spending. (ii) To avoid wasting money.. A budget helps a school use its money wisely.
chunks.source: A budget helps a school use its money wisely.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 43. a) State one of the children’s rights. b) Mention any two ways how children’s rights are violated. ii) c) Which local council I executive is responsible to protect children’s rights? A: a) The right to education (also accepted: food, health care, protection). b) (i) Through child labour. (ii) By denying them schooling. c) So that they can protect themselves and become responsible citizens.. Children should know their rights and duties.
chunks.source: Children should know their rights and duties.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 45. What role was played by the following personalities in the history of Africa? i) Dr. David Livingstone: ii) Sir Samuel Baker: iii) Dr. Kwame Nkrumah: iv) Nelson Mandela: A: i) Dr. David Livingstone: explored Africa and exposed the horrors of slave trade. ii) Sir Samuel Baker: fought slave trade in northern Uganda. iii) Dr. Kwame Nkrumah: led Ghana to independence and championed African unity. iv) Nelson Mandela: fought apartheid and became South Africa's first black president.. Two fought slave trade; two fought for freedom.
chunks.source: Two fought slave trade; two fought for freedom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 46. a) Name the chief economic activity of the following people living around: i) Lake Victoria: ii) Mabira forest: b) State two disadvantages of encroaching on forest lands. A: a) (i) Around Lake Victoria: fishing. (ii) Around Mabira forest: lumbering. b) (i) It destroys forests and wildlife habitats. (ii) It causes soil erosion and loss of rainfall.. People's work follows the resources near them.
chunks.source: People's work follows the resources near them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 47. a) What is population? b) Stat two factors that influence population growth in Uganda. A: a) Population is the number of people living in an area. b) (i) Birth rate. (ii) Migration (also accepted: death rate).. More births and in-migration raise population.
chunks.source: More births and in-migration raise population.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 48. a) Name one game park in East Africa where tourists may find each of the following: i) Flamingo birds ii) Mountain gorillas b) State any two problems facing game parks of East Africa. A: a) (i) Flamingo birds: Lake Nakuru National Park (Kenya). (ii) Mountain gorillas: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park (also accepted: Mgahinga). b) (i) Poaching. (ii) Encroachment by people.. Nakuru's soda lake attracts flamingos; Bwindi's forest shelters gorillas. Parks suffer from poachers and land grabbers.
chunks.source: Nakuru's soda lake attracts flamingos; Bwindi's forest shelters gorillas. Parks suffer from poachers and land grabbers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 49. a)What does the term ‘migration ‘ mean? b) State any two causes of migration by the early man? ii) c) What is urban-rural migration? A: a) Migration is the movement of people from one place to another to settle. b) (i) Search for food and water. (ii) Search for shelter and safety.. Early man moved to survive.
chunks.source: Early man moved to survive.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 50. a) Give any two uses of land as a major resource of people. ii) b) Apart from land, give any two other major resources in East Africa. ii) For each of the questions 51-55, answer Either the Christian or Islamic questions but not Both alternatives in a number. A: a) (i) Farming. (ii) Settlement (also accepted: grazing, mining).. Land is man's most important resource.
chunks.source: Land is man's most important resource.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. Write NEMA in full. A: National Environment Management Authority. NEMA protects Uganda's environment.
chunks.source: NEMA protects Uganda's environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 7. Which ministry in Uganda is in charge of vegetation conservation? A: The Ministry of Water and Environment. This ministry handles forests, water and environmental protection.
chunks.source: This ministry handles forests, water and environmental protection.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. How do lions benefit from vegetation in areas where they stay? A: Vegetation gives lions shade and hiding places for hunting prey.. Lions stalk their prey hidden in tall grass and bushes.
chunks.source: Lions stalk their prey hidden in tall grass and bushes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. Give any one example of a natural forest outside East Africa. A: The Congo forest (also accepted: the Amazon forest). The Congo Basin holds Africa's largest tropical rainforest.
chunks.source: The Congo Basin holds Africa's largest tropical rainforest.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10. Name the plant cover that grows mostly in the East African coast. A: Mangrove vegetation. Mangroves grow along the East African coast in salty water.
chunks.source: Mangroves grow along the East African coast in salty water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. State one reason why the above vegetation grows well in the coastal areas. A: The coastal areas are warm and receive heavy rainfall.. Heat plus rain suits the mangrove vegetation.
chunks.source: Heat plus rain suits the mangrove vegetation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. Mention any one example of tree species found in desert vegetation zones. A: Cactus (also accepted: acacia, baobab). Desert trees survive with little water.
chunks.source: Desert trees survive with little water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. What are oasis? A: An oasis is a fertile area in a desert where water is found.. Travellers rest and farm at oases in the desert.
chunks.source: Travellers rest and farm at oases in the desert.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 14. State any one way oasis promote vegetation growth in an area. A: Oasis water helps plants to grow in the dry desert.. Water is life for desert plants.
chunks.source: Water is life for desert plants.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. Write down any one factor that makes areas in Karamoja to have scattered vegetation. A: Low and unreliable rainfall. Karamoja is semi-arid, so only scattered drought-resistant plants grow.
chunks.source: Karamoja is semi-arid, so only scattered drought-resistant plants grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 16. What does the term ‘Game Park’ mean? A: A game park is a protected area set aside for the conservation of wild animals.. Animals live freely and safely in game parks.
chunks.source: Animals live freely and safely in game parks.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 17. State any one reason why school children are encouraged to conserve grass planted in the school compound. A: Grass prevents soil erosion and keeps the compound beautiful.. Grass holds the soil together with its roots.
chunks.source: Grass holds the soil together with its roots.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 18. Mention any one difference between natural and planted forests. A: Natural forests have mixed tree species while planted forests have one tree species.. Natural forests grow wild; planted forests are arranged by man.
chunks.source: Natural forests grow wild; planted forests are arranged by man.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 19. What general name is given to the group of people that extract timber from mature trees? A: Lumberjacks (lumbermen). They cut mature trees for the timber industry.
chunks.source: They cut mature trees for the timber industry.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 20. Give any one way NEMA conserves the environment. A: NEMA plants trees, enforces environmental laws and sensitises people.. It also stops wetland degradation and pollution.
chunks.source: It also stops wetland degradation and pollution.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 21. Write REMA in full. A: Rwanda Environment Management Authority. REMA does in Rwanda what NEMA does in Uganda.
chunks.source: REMA does in Rwanda what NEMA does in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 22. How does massive cutting down of tree lead to environmental hazards? A: It causes soil erosion, desertification and loss of rainfall.. Bare land washes away and dries up.
chunks.source: Bare land washes away and dries up.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 23. Why is Bwindi impenetrable forest National Game Park having many mountains gorillas? A: Bwindi has thick montane forest that gives gorillas food and shelter.. Mountain gorillas need dense forest to survive.
chunks.source: Mountain gorillas need dense forest to survive.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 24. Write down the type of timber that is mainly harvested from Mediterranean vegetation zone. A: Soft wood (pine). Mediterranean forests mainly give soft wood timber.
chunks.source: Mediterranean forests mainly give soft wood timber.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 25. State one factor that make equatorial regions to have evergreen vegetation. A: Heavy rainfall throughout the year. Constant rain keeps equatorial trees green always.
chunks.source: Constant rain keeps equatorial trees green always.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 26. What term is used to describe grasslands of South Africa? A: Veld. The veld of South Africa is a temperate grassland.
chunks.source: The veld of South Africa is a temperate grassland.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 27. Name one economic activity carried out in temperate grasslands. A: Sheep rearing (also accepted: wheat farming). Temperate grasslands suit sheep and wheat.
chunks.source: Temperate grasslands suit sheep and wheat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 28. State one factor that makes natural forests to have thick undergrowth. A: Heavy rainfall and fertile soils. Rich rain and soil grow thick plants under the big trees.
chunks.source: Rich rain and soil grow thick plants under the big trees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 29. Mention any one example of citrus fruit tree grown in Mediterranean areas. A: Oranges (also accepted: lemons). Citrus fruits love the Mediterranean winter rainfall.
chunks.source: Citrus fruits love the Mediterranean winter rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 30. Give the meaning of the term ‘global warming’. A: Global warming is the gradual rise in the earth's temperature.. It is caused by deforestation and burning of fuels.
chunks.source: It is caused by deforestation and burning of fuels.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 31. What is a sanctuary? A: A sanctuary is a protected place where wild animals are kept safe.. Rhino sanctuaries protect rhinos from poachers.
chunks.source: Rhino sanctuaries protect rhinos from poachers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 32. Name the largest sanctuary found in East Africa. Study the drawing below. Snow line (4500m) B A A: The Serengeti (one of the largest protected areas in East Africa). East Africa's great parks protect millions of wild animals.
chunks.source: East Africa's great parks protect millions of wild animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 36. State any one way the government can promote the tourism industry. A: By advertising tourist attractions abroad and improving roads, hotels and security.. More visitors come when a country is known and safe.
chunks.source: More visitors come when a country is known and safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 37. How does tourists benefit from hotels and lodges located near Game parks? A: Hotels and lodges give tourists accommodation, food and rest near the parks.. Tourists sleep and eat comfortably near attractions.
chunks.source: Tourists sleep and eat comfortably near attractions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 38. Write down any one negative effect of the tourism industry to a country. A: It can lead to poaching and environmental degradation.. Too many visitors can also spread diseases to animals.
chunks.source: Too many visitors can also spread diseases to animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 39. State any one was a craft maker in Jinja can benefit from the tourism industry. A: Tourists buy his crafts as souvenirs, giving him income.. Craft shops near tourist sites earn good money.
chunks.source: Craft shops near tourist sites earn good money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 40. What major tourist attraction in common at Tsavo National Game Park? Section B A: Elephants. Tsavo in Kenya is famous for its large red elephants.
chunks.source: Tsavo in Kenya is famous for its large red elephants.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 41. Study the table below and fill in the missing information. Tree species Product Cypress Ficus tree Wattle tree Mvule A: Cypress - timber/poles; Ficus tree - barkcloth; Wattle tree - tannin; Mvule - timber for furniture.. Each tree species gives a useful product.
chunks.source: Each tree species gives a useful product.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 42. Write down two differences between natural forests and planted forests in terms of; (i) Wood. (ii) tree species; (iii) maturity (b) Name the largest natural forest along Jinja highway on your to the East of Uganda. A: (i) Wood: natural forests give hard wood while planted forests give soft wood. (ii) Tree species: natural forests have mixed species while planted forests have one species. (iii) Maturity: natural trees take longer to mature. (b) Mabira Forest.. Planted forests are uniform and fast; natural forests are mixed and slow.
chunks.source: Planted forests are uniform and fast; natural forests are mixed and slow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 43. a) Write down any two importance of forests to the economic development of Uganda. (b) State any two ways in which forests can be a danger to people in areas where they are located. A: a) (i) Forests give timber for building and furniture. (ii) They attract tourists and give medicine. (b) (i) They hide dangerous wild animals. (ii) They hide criminals.. Forests are a natural wealth of Uganda.
chunks.source: Forests are a natural wealth of Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 44. Write down one way how each of the following factors influence the distribution of vegetation in an area. (a) Nature of the soils (b) Rainfall distribution (c) Human activities (d) Altitude A: (a) Nature of soils: fertile soils support thick vegetation while poor soils support little. (b) Rainfall distribution: heavy-rainfall areas have forests while dry areas have grass. (c) Human activities: deforestation destroys vegetation while afforestation restores it. (d) Altitude: different heights have different vegetation belts.. Soil, water and man decide what grows.
chunks.source: Soil, water and man decide what grows.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 45. a) What is swamp drainage? (b) Give any three factors that contribute to swamp drainage in Uganda. A: (a) Swamp drainage is the removal of water from swamps. (b) (i) Need for farmland. (ii) Need for settlement land. (iii) Brick making and population pressure.. People drain swamps mainly to farm and settle.
chunks.source: People drain swamps mainly to farm and settle.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 46. a) State the main reason why most parts of Africa are covered by savanna grasslands (b) Give any two ways wild animals benefit from savanna grasslands. (c) Mention the major economic activity carried out in savanna woodlands. A: a) Most of Africa has a tropical climate with alternating wet and dry seasons that favour grass. (b) (i) Wild animals get pasture. (ii) They get habitat. (c) Lumbering (timber harvesting) and charcoal burning.. Savanna grass feeds Africa's great herds.
chunks.source: Savanna grass feeds Africa's great herds.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 47. a) Mention any two vegetation zones found in central Africa. (b) State any two factors that make the above area to experience the above vegetation zones. A: a) (i) Equatorial vegetation (ii) Savanna vegetation. (b) (i) Heavy rainfall and high temperatures. (ii) Low altitude.. Central Africa is hot and wet, so forests and grasslands dominate.
chunks.source: Central Africa is hot and wet, so forests and grasslands dominate.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 49. a) Mention the game parks in East Africa that are famous for; (i) zebras (ii) lions (iii) Gorillas (iv) ostriches A: a) (i) Zebras: Lake Mburo National Park. (ii) Lions: Queen Elizabeth National Park (also accepted: Murchison Falls).. Uganda's parks are famous for different animals.
chunks.source: Uganda's parks are famous for different animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 50. a) What major economic activities are carried out in the following area. i) Great Karoos ii) Maize triangle (b) Write down any two factors that favours the above economic activities. A: a) (i) Great Karoo: sheep rearing. (ii) Maize triangle: maize (crop) farming. (b) (i) Suitable climate and grasslands. (ii) Good soils and market.. The Karoo's dry grass suits sheep; the maize triangle's fertile land suits maize.
chunks.source: The Karoo's dry grass suits sheep; the maize triangle's fertile land suits maize.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 51. a) Give the meaning of the term poaching. (b) Write down any two reasons why people carry out the above activity. (c) State the economic effect of the above activity to a country like Uganda. A: (a) Poaching is the illegal killing of wild animals. (b) (i) To get ivory and trophies. (ii) To get meat. (c) It reduces tourist numbers and kills a source of foreign income.. Poaching steals a country's wildlife wealth.
chunks.source: Poaching steals a country's wildlife wealth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 52. a) Mention any two human activities that positively affect vegetation distribution. (b) Write down any two ways the above activities influence vegetation distribution. A: (a) (i) Afforestation. (ii) Agroforestry. (b) Planting trees restores vegetation cover.. Man can heal the land he has damaged.
chunks.source: Man can heal the land he has damaged.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 53. a) How does vegetation influence animal distribution across Africa. (b) Give one reason why Miombo woodlands are sparsely populated. (c) Name the major economic activity carried out in Miombo woodlands. (d) State any one way of overcoming challenges faced in the Miombo woodlands. A: (a) Vegetation gives animals food and habitat, so animals live where suitable plants grow. (b) Miombo woodlands are infested with tsetse flies. (c) Lumbering (timber harvesting). (d) By spraying to kill tsetse flies and planting trees.. Plants decide where animals can live; tsetse control opens the woodlands.
chunks.source: Plants decide where animals can live; tsetse control opens the woodlands.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 54. a) Briefly describe each of the following kinds of animals found in Game parks. i) herbivoures ii) carnivores iii) omnivores (b) Give any one example of herbivores. A: a) Herbivores feed on plants; carnivores feed on flesh; omnivores feed on both plants and flesh. (b) Zebra (also accepted: antelope, elephant).. Game park animals are grouped by what they eat: plants, meat, or both.
chunks.source: Game park animals are grouped by what they eat: plants, meat, or both.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 55. a) Write any one method of ensuring vegetation growth in semi-arid areas. (b) State any two advantages of using the above method mentioned in (a) above. (c) Mention any one place in East Africa where the above method is used. A: (a) Irrigation. (b) (i) Crops grow even in the dry season. (ii) It increases yields. (c) The Mwea Irrigation Scheme in Kenya (also accepted: Doho rice scheme in Uganda).. Watering dry land makes it productive.
chunks.source: Watering dry land makes it productive.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 1. Name any one food crop that grows well in a swamp. A: Rice (also accepted: yams/cocoyam). Rice grows well in wet swampy soils.
chunks.source: Rice grows well in wet swampy soils.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 2. Mention the instrument that is used to measure the amount of rainfall at a weather station. A: A rain gauge. It collects and measures the millimetres of rainfall.
chunks.source: It collects and measures the millimetres of rainfall.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 3. Name the ethnic group of people that occupy the north – earthen part of Uganda. A: The Nilotes (the Karamojong). The Karamojong are Plain Nilotes living in north-eastern Uganda.
chunks.source: The Karamojong are Plain Nilotes living in north-eastern Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 4. What is the compass direction of Uganda from Rwanda? A: North. Rwanda lies to the south of Uganda, so Uganda is north of Rwanda.
chunks.source: Rwanda lies to the south of Uganda, so Uganda is north of Rwanda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 5. Apart from missionaries, which other group of foreigners helped to develop social services in Uganda? A: The British colonial government. The colonial administration built schools, hospitals and roads.
chunks.source: The colonial administration built schools, hospitals and roads.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. Give any one reason why farmers are advised to plant crops at the beginning of a rainy season. A: So that crops get enough water for germination and early growth.. Early planting catches the full rainy season.
chunks.source: Early planting catches the full rainy season.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 7. Mention any one disadvantage of building in wetlands. A: Buildings may flood or develop weak foundations in the waterlogged soil.. Wetlands are nature's water stores, not building plots.
chunks.source: Wetlands are nature's water stores, not building plots.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. Give one reason why there are many different types of natural vegetation in Africa. A: Africa has many different climates and soils, each supporting different plants.. From deserts to rainforests, each zone grows its own vegetation.
chunks.source: From deserts to rainforests, each zone grows its own vegetation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. State any one way in which labour force can be improved in Africa. A: Through education, training and better health care for workers.. Skilled healthy workers produce more.
chunks.source: Skilled healthy workers produce more.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 10. In which way is the formation of Mt. Rwenzori different from that of Mt. Elgon? A: Mount Rwenzori was formed by faulting (a block mountain) while Mount Elgon was formed by volcanicity.. Rwenzori was lifted by earth movements; Elgon was built by lava.
chunks.source: Rwenzori was lifted by earth movements; Elgon was built by lava.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. Give one reason why controlling population increase is difficult. A: Some cultures value large families and many people do not use family planning.. Tradition and low contraceptive use keep birth rates high.
chunks.source: Tradition and low contraceptive use keep birth rates high.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. Mention any one way in which the government can help the people in rural areas to increase agricultural produce. A: By providing extension workers, loans, and improved seeds.. Support services help farmers produce more.
chunks.source: Support services help farmers produce more.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 13. Name the lake that is the source of the Blue Nile. A: Lake Tana. The Blue Nile starts from Lake Tana in Ethiopia.
chunks.source: The Blue Nile starts from Lake Tana in Ethiopia.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 14. Name the type of tax charged on imported goods in Uganda. A: Customs duty. It is charged on goods entering the country.
chunks.source: It is charged on goods entering the country.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. Name the winds that bring rain to East Africa. A: The South-East trade winds. These moist winds from the Indian Ocean bring rain to East Africa.
chunks.source: These moist winds from the Indian Ocean bring rain to East Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 16. Why is Patrice Lumumba remembered in the history of Democratic Republic of Congo? A: Patrice Lumumba was the first prime minister of independent Congo who fought for its independence and was assassinated in 1961.. He is a hero of Congolese nationalism.
chunks.source: He is a hero of Congolese nationalism.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 17. Give one advantage of exporting processed goods other than raw materials. A: Processed goods fetch higher prices and earn more foreign income.. Processing adds value to raw materials.
chunks.source: Processing adds value to raw materials.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 18. Apart from being cloudy or windy, give any one other change of weather. A: Change in temperature (also accepted: rainfall, sunshine). Weather changes in temperature, rain, wind and cloud cover.
chunks.source: Weather changes in temperature, rain, wind and cloud cover.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 19. Give one problem the builders of the Uganda Railway faced in the Nandi area. A: They faced resistance from the Nandi people led by Koitalel arap Samoei.. The Nandi fought the railway builders for years.
chunks.source: The Nandi fought the railway builders for years.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 20. Why is air transport used by very few people in Africa? A: Air transport is very expensive for most Africans.. Few people can afford air tickets.
chunks.source: Few people can afford air tickets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 21. In which agreement were the boundaries of Buganda drawn? A: The 1900 Buganda Agreement. It fixed Buganda's boundaries and divided its land.
chunks.source: It fixed Buganda's boundaries and divided its land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 22. Why should a citizen obey the laws of a country? A: To keep peace and order and avoid punishment.. Laws protect everyone's rights and safety.
chunks.source: Laws protect everyone's rights and safety.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 23. State one reason why some people in Uganda do not get access to social services. A: Because of poverty, living in remote areas, or corruption.. Services do not reach everyone equally.
chunks.source: Services do not reach everyone equally.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 24. Name the element on the Uganda coat of Arms that represents Uganda’s culture. A: The drum. The drum at the base of the shield represents Uganda's culture.
chunks.source: The drum at the base of the shield represents Uganda's culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 25. How did the trade between the coastal Arabs help in the expansion of Buganda Kingdom? A: Trade gave Buganda guns and wealth, which strengthened its army and expansion.. Arab guns made Buganda the most powerful kingdom in the region.
chunks.source: Arab guns made Buganda the most powerful kingdom in the region.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 26. State one factor which has made irrigation in the Karamoja region almost impossible. A: Karamoja receives very low and unreliable rainfall.. Without enough water, irrigation is almost impossible.
chunks.source: Without enough water, irrigation is almost impossible.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 27. Why was the Nyanza province transferred from Uganda to Kenya in 1902? A: It was transferred for administrative convenience, being nearer to Kisumu and Nairobi in Kenya.. The British found it easier to administer from Kenya.
chunks.source: The British found it easier to administer from Kenya.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 28. State one problem facing effective communication in Uganda. A: Poor network coverage, illiteracy and language barriers.. Many rural areas lack phones and radios.
chunks.source: Many rural areas lack phones and radios.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 29. Why is Kapchorwa cooler than Gulu? A: Kapchorwa is on the high slopes of Mount Elgon while Gulu is on a lower plateau.. Higher places are cooler.
chunks.source: Higher places are cooler.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 30. Where is snow found in East Africa? A: On the tops of high mountains like Rwenzori, Kilimanjaro and Kenya.. Only the highest peaks are cold enough for snow.
chunks.source: Only the highest peaks are cold enough for snow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 31. Which water passage joins the Red sea to the Mediterranean sea? A: The Suez Canal. It joins the Red Sea to the Mediterranean Sea through Egypt.
chunks.source: It joins the Red Sea to the Mediterranean Sea through Egypt.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 32. State one reason why German colonial rule was resisted in Tanganyika. A: German rule was harsh, with forced labour and heavy taxes, sparking the Maji Maji rebellion.. Tanganyikans rose against German cruelty in 1905-1907.
chunks.source: Tanganyikans rose against German cruelty in 1905-1907.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 33. Which bank is jointly owned by the member countries of the East African community? A: The East African Development Bank (EADB). It is jointly owned by the EAC partner states and funds development.
chunks.source: It is jointly owned by the EAC partner states and funds development.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 34. State one cause of land fragmentation in Uganda. A: Inheritance, where land is divided among children into smaller pieces.. Each generation splits the family land further.
chunks.source: Each generation splits the family land further.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 35. Give any one way in which the people of South Africa fought against Apartheid. For questions 36 – 40, answer Christianity or Islam “BUT NOT” both. A: Through boycotts, demonstrations, strikes and the armed struggle of the ANC.. International sanctions also pressured the apartheid regime.
chunks.source: International sanctions also pressured the apartheid regime.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 41. (a) Name the two explorers who made three journeys to Africa. (b) State any two problems that were faced by the early explorers in Africa. A: (a)(i) Dr. David Livingstone (ii) Henry Morton Stanley. (b)(i) They faced hostile tribes. (ii) They suffered tropical diseases like malaria.. These explorers opened up the African interior to the world.
chunks.source: These explorers opened up the African interior to the world.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 42. (a) Name two African leaders who attended the Pan African Congress in 1958. (b) State two ways in which Marcus Garvey contributed to the development of Africa. A: (a)(i) Kwame Nkrumah (Ghana) (ii) Julius Nyerere (Tanganyika). (b)(i) He founded the UNIA to unite black people. (ii) He promoted the 'Back to Africa' movement and black pride.. The 1958 Accra conference gathered Africa's top nationalists.
chunks.source: The 1958 Accra conference gathered Africa's top nationalists.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 46(a) State any one of the children’s rights. (b) Mention any one of the children’s responsibilities. (c) State any two reasons why children should know their rights and responsibilities. A: (a) The right to education (also accepted: food, health care). (b) The duty to respect parents and do school work. (c) (i) So they can protect themselves from abuse. (ii) So they grow into responsible citizens.. Rights come with responsibilities.
chunks.source: Rights come with responsibilities.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 45. (a) What was the Great Trek? (b) Mention any two places that were occupied by the Dutch after the Great Trek. (c) State any one result of the Great Trek. A: (a) The Great Trek was the movement of the Dutch Boers from the Cape Colony into the interior of South Africa in the 1830s-1840s. (b)(i) Natal (ii) The Orange Free State (also accepted: Transvaal). (c) It led to the creation of Boer republics (also accepted: clashes with African kingdoms like the Zulu).. The Boers trekked to escape British rule at the Cape.
chunks.source: The Boers trekked to escape British rule at the Cape.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 46. (a) Which organization was replaced by the African Union (AU)? (b) Mention any two organs of the African Union (AU) (c) State any one way in which the African Union (AU) is helping member states to solve the problem of Civil wars. A: (a) The Organisation of African Unity (OAU). (b)(i) The Assembly. (ii) The Executive Council. (c) By sending peacekeeping troops and supporting dialogue.. The AU replaced the OAU in 2002.
chunks.source: The AU replaced the OAU in 2002.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 48. (a) Apart from growing crops, give one other activity carried out by man to support his family. (b) State any two ways in which man has benefited from growing crops. (c) Mention any one problem faced by people who grow crops in Uganda. A: (a) Animal rearing (also accepted: fishing, trading). (b)(i) Crops give food. (ii) Crops give income when sold. (c) Pests and diseases, or unreliable rainfall.. Farming feeds and pays the family but faces many risks.
chunks.source: Farming feeds and pays the family but faces many risks.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 49. (a) What title is given to the person who heads the Judiciary in Uganda? (b) Mention any two groups of people who are members of the Judiciary. (c) How does Parliament contribute to the work of the Judiciary? A: (a) The Chief Justice. (b)(i) Judges. (ii) Magistrates. (c) Parliament makes the laws that the Judiciary interprets.. The Judiciary interprets laws and delivers justice.
chunks.source: The Judiciary interprets laws and delivers justice.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 50. (a) Name any one place at school where waste materials can be disposed. (b) State any two problems caused by poor waste management in schools. (c) Why is recycling important in waste management? A: (a) In dustbins or a rubbish pit. (b)(i) It causes diseases. (ii) It pollutes the environment and smells badly. (c) Recycling reduces waste and saves resources.. Clean schools keep pupils healthy.
chunks.source: Clean schools keep pupils healthy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 1. Name one landlocked country in the horn of Africa. A: Ethiopia. Ethiopia in the Horn of Africa has no coastline.
chunks.source: Ethiopia in the Horn of Africa has no coastline.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 2. State one way people in a sub county community can live at peace with neighbours. A: Through dialogue, respect and cooperation with neighbours.. Peaceful communities solve disputes by talking.
chunks.source: Peaceful communities solve disputes by talking.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 3. Mention one feature in the community that helps people to find the location of the school. A: A landmark such as a church, road signpost or big tree.. Well-known features help people find places.
chunks.source: Well-known features help people find places.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 4. Give any one change the Bantu migration brought to East Africa. A: It introduced iron working and new crops in East Africa.. The Bantu also spread their languages and culture.
chunks.source: The Bantu also spread their languages and culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 5. Write down one way the British put Kenya under their rule. A: Through military conquest, treaties with chiefs, and settling white farmers.. The British used force and agreements to take control.
chunks.source: The British used force and agreements to take control.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 6. State one way citizens can help the government to promote democracy in a country. A: By voting, obeying laws and paying taxes.. Good citizens take part in national life.
chunks.source: Good citizens take part in national life.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 7. Mention a thing that may cause conflicts between a school and its neighborhood. A: Noise, or disputes over land boundaries.. Schools and neighbours clash over disturbances and land.
chunks.source: Schools and neighbours clash over disturbances and land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 8. Why are countries in East Africa today called republics? A: They are headed by elected presidents, not kings or queens.. A republic chooses its head of state by voting.
chunks.source: A republic chooses its head of state by voting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 9. State one title of Electoral commission official at a polling station. A: The presiding officer (also accepted: returning officer). He or she manages voting at the polling station.
chunks.source: He or she manages voting at the polling station.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 10. Name the independent country of Africa which is located within another country. A: Lesotho. Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa.
chunks.source: Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 10b. State one advantage of EAC to its member states. A: It gives member states a bigger market for their goods.. EAC members also enjoy free movement and cooperation.
chunks.source: EAC members also enjoy free movement and cooperation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 11. How did the Arabs lead to the origin of Kiswahili at the East African coast? A: The Arabs intermarried and traded with the coastal Bantu, mixing Arabic with Bantu languages to form Kiswahili.. Kiswahili grew from Arab-African contact at the coast.
chunks.source: Kiswahili grew from Arab-African contact at the coast.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 12. Which economic activity in Nyika plateau is similar to that of people of North Eastern Uganda? A: Pastoralism (cattle keeping). Both areas are dry, so people keep animals that move for pasture.
chunks.source: Both areas are dry, so people keep animals that move for pasture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 13. In which way can a surplus budget encourage development in a country? A: The extra money can fund development projects like roads and schools.. A surplus means income is more than spending.
chunks.source: A surplus means income is more than spending.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 14. Name one country in East Africa which meets High taxes when importing and exporting goods. A: Uganda (a landlocked country). Landlocked countries pay more to move goods through neighbours' ports.
chunks.source: Landlocked countries pay more to move goods through neighbours' ports.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 15. Why did Gipir move from Pubungu to a new land? A: Gipir moved after a quarrel with his brother Labongo over a spear and beads.. This Luo legend explains the Luo migration southwards.
chunks.source: This Luo legend explains the Luo migration southwards.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 16. State one reason why farmers like living in areas with reliable rainfall. A: Reliable rainfall gives good harvests.. Farmers depend on rain for their crops.
chunks.source: Farmers depend on rain for their crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 17. In which way does security promote development in an area? A: Security attracts investors and lets people work without fear.. Peaceful areas develop faster.
chunks.source: Peaceful areas develop faster.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 18. Mention one example of a civic leader in the district in charge of crop growing. A: The District Agricultural (Production) Officer. He or she guides farmers on better crop growing.
chunks.source: He or she guides farmers on better crop growing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 19. State one way health workers can help in controlling population growth. A: By teaching family planning methods to the people.. Fewer births mean controlled population growth.
chunks.source: Fewer births mean controlled population growth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 20. What can cause shortage of social services for people in an area? A: High population pressure, corruption, or remoteness of the area.. When people are many or leaders are corrupt, services fall short.
chunks.source: When people are many or leaders are corrupt, services fall short.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 21. State one way people become family relatives. A: Through marriage, birth (blood) or adoption.. Families grow in these three ways.
chunks.source: Families grow in these three ways.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 22. It is 2:00 pm at GMT, what is the time at town X which is 60oE. A: 6:00 pm. Every 15 degrees east adds one hour; 60 divided by 15 is 4 hours ahead of GMT.
chunks.source: Every 15 degrees east adds one hour; 60 divided by 15 is 4 hours ahead of GMT.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 23. How is a rainy weather important to farmers? A: Rainy weather gives water for crops to grow well.. Farmers need rain for good harvests.
chunks.source: Farmers need rain for good harvests.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 24. Give one cause of common accidents in a home. A: Open fires, sharp objects, or slippery floors.. Carelessness at home causes accidents.
chunks.source: Carelessness at home causes accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 25. State one reason children go to live on the streets. A: Poverty, domestic violence, or being orphaned.. Hard homes push children onto the streets.
chunks.source: Hard homes push children onto the streets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 26. How can boys and girls be treated equally? A: By giving them the same education and household duties.. Both boys and girls deserve equal chances.
chunks.source: Both boys and girls deserve equal chances.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 27. Give any one importance of activities such as pottery, carpentry and casual laboring in our community. A: They give people income and provide useful goods to the community.. Handwork feeds families and serves neighbours.
chunks.source: Handwork feeds families and serves neighbours.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 28. Mention one task Kintu was told to do before marrying Nambi. A: Kintu was given difficult tasks by Ggulu, Nambi's father, to prove he was worthy, such as building and providing for a home quickly.. The Buganda legend says Kintu passed Ggulu's tests before marrying Nambi.
chunks.source: The Buganda legend says Kintu passed Ggulu's tests before marrying Nambi.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 29. How can rivers and lakes be dangerous to people? A: People can drown in them, and floods destroy homes and crops.. Deep water and floods are the main dangers.
chunks.source: Deep water and floods are the main dangers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 30. Why did the spread of Christianity increase after the coming of colonialist to Uganda? A: The colonialists built churches and schools and protected missionaries, so Christianity reached more people.. Colonial peace and support opened the way for missionaries.
chunks.source: Colonial peace and support opened the way for missionaries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 31. A holiday is an extended period of leisure and recreation that can be away from school or work and home. Identify any one type of holiday in Uganda. A: A public (national) holiday (also accepted: religious holiday). Uganda celebrates days like Independence Day and Christmas.
chunks.source: Uganda celebrates days like Independence Day and Christmas.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 32. In which way have people of Kenya and Tanzania benefited from the Indian Ocean? A: They use it for fishing, seaport trade and tourism.. The ocean gives food, ports and visitors.
chunks.source: The ocean gives food, ports and visitors.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 33. How did Colonel Patterson contribute to the development of transport in East Africa? A: He built the Uganda Railway across Tsavo, overcoming the man-eating lions.. Patterson led the railway construction through dangerous country.
chunks.source: Patterson led the railway construction through dangerous country.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 34. Give one reason for the scramble and partition of East Africa by Europeans. From 36 answer either Christianity or Islam but not both. A: To get raw materials, markets and colonies for national prestige.. European powers competed for a share of Africa.
chunks.source: European powers competed for a share of Africa.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 41. (a) Write the means of transport you can use in the following places, (i) on a lake (ii) in a village path way (iii) in wind (b) Why is there no child in your class who comes to school in a canoe? A: (a)(i) On a lake: a boat/canoe. (ii) On a village pathway: a bicycle (also accepted: walking). (iii) In the air: an aeroplane. (b) There is no big water body near the school / canoes cannot move on land.. Each place suits its own means of transport.
chunks.source: Each place suits its own means of transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Location of Africa on the Map of the World
chunks.text: Q: 42. (a) How was Mount Elgon formed? (b) State one way Mountain Elgon has positively affected the farming activities of people living on and near it. (c) Give any two problems faced by people who live on Mountain Elgon. A: (a) Mount Elgon was formed by volcanicity. (b) Its fertile volcanic soils support farming. (c) (i) Landslides. (ii) Soil erosion.. Volcanic soils are rich for crops.
chunks.source: Volcanic soils are rich for crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Nationalism and the Road to Independence of Africa
chunks.text: Q: 43. (a) Which nationalistic party was the first to be formed in Uganda? (b) Why is Uganda considered to be an independent country? (c) State two objectives of the political party mentioned in 43(a). A: (a) The Uganda National Congress (UNC). (b) Uganda has its own government, constitution and flag since 9th October 1962. (c)(i) To win independence for Uganda. (ii) To unite Ugandans.. The UNC, formed by Musaazi in 1952, was Uganda's first party.
chunks.source: The UNC, formed by Musaazi in 1952, was Uganda's first party.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 44. (a) Name the crop grown in East Africa used for making insecticides. (b) State one benefit of the crop mentioned in 44(a) to the farmers in Kenya. (c) Give two ways lack of capital has led to low agricultural production in East Africa. A: (a) Pyrethrum. (b) It gives them income from selling it. (c)(i) Farmers cannot buy good seeds and tools. (ii) They cannot afford fertilisers.. Pyrethrum makes natural insecticides; money grows crops.
chunks.source: Pyrethrum makes natural insecticides; money grows crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 45. (a) Which type of tax is collected from imports? (b) State one way the government can encourage people to pay taxes. (c) Write one problem the government meets when collecting taxes. (d) State the importance of taxes to a country. A: (a) Customs duty. (b) By sensitising people on the value of taxes and easing payment. (c) Smuggling and tax evasion. (d) Taxes give revenue for services like roads and schools.. Taxes fund the nation's development.
chunks.source: Taxes fund the nation's development.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 46. (a) Identify any one recreation centre in your community (b) Initiation is the admission of someone into a group typically with a ritual. Give any two importance of the ritual of initiation. (c) Apart from initiation, write one other cultural festival in our community. A: (a) A playground or community hall. (b)(i) It marks one's entry into adulthood. (ii) It teaches cultural values and identity. (c) Circumcision ceremonies (also accepted: harvest festivals, naming ceremonies).. Initiation moves one from childhood to adulthood.
chunks.source: Initiation moves one from childhood to adulthood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 47. (a) Name the London based organized which sent the first missionaries to Uganda. (b) Name one of the first missionary to come to Uganda in 1877 (c) Write down two contributions of missionaries in Uganda A: (a) The Church Missionary Society (CMS). (b) Alexander Mackay (also accepted: C.T. Wilson). (c)(i) They built schools. (ii) They built hospitals.. The CMS sent the first missionaries to Buganda in 1877.
chunks.source: The CMS sent the first missionaries to Buganda in 1877.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 48. Study the climate table below from Congo Basin and answer question 4 Month J F M A M J J A S O N D TempoC 26 26 Rainfall mm 60 80 180 160 140 120 135 160 180 (a) 201 200 90 Describe the climate shown on the table. (b) Calculate the temperature range. (c) In which month was 180 mm of rainfall recorded? (d) State one factor that makes this area to receive plenty of rainfall. A: (a) Equatorial climate - hot and wet throughout the year. (b) 3 degrees Celsius (26 - 23). (c) March and September. (d) Its location near the Equator / the thick Congo forest.. The Congo Basin is always hot with heavy rain.
chunks.source: The Congo Basin is always hot with heavy rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: 50. (a) Name the Bank which is jointly run by countries in the East African Community. (b) State the services provided by the above bank to the people of East Africa. (c) Give one reason why saving is important to people. A: (a) The East African Development Bank (EADB). (b) It gives loans for development projects in member states. (c) Saving provides money for future needs and emergencies.. The bank is jointly owned by the EAC countries.
chunks.source: The bank is jointly owned by the EAC countries.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: We played ___ every evening. A: football. The word is 'football': We played football every evening.
chunks.source: The word is 'football': We played football every evening.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'waste' mean? A: use carelessly. 'waste' means use carelessly.
chunks.source: 'waste' means use carelessly.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'adventure' mean? A: an exciting experience. 'adventure' means an exciting experience.
chunks.source: 'adventure' means an exciting experience.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'visit' mean? A: to go and see someone. 'visit' means to go and see someone.
chunks.source: 'visit' means to go and see someone.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'use carelessly'? A: waste. use carelessly — that is 'waste'.
chunks.source: use carelessly — that is 'waste'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'excited' mean? A: feeling very happy and eager. 'excited' means feeling very happy and eager.
chunks.source: 'excited' means feeling very happy and eager.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'early' mean? A: before the usual time. 'early' means before the usual time.
chunks.source: 'early' means before the usual time.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'spend' mean? A: use money. 'spend' means use money.
chunks.source: 'spend' means use money.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'swimming' mean? A: moving in water. 'swimming' means moving in water.
chunks.source: 'swimming' means moving in water.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: The ___ to Jinja takes three hours. A: journey. The word is 'journey': The journey to Jinja takes three hours.
chunks.source: The word is 'journey': The journey to Jinja takes three hours.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'finally' mean? A: at the end. 'finally' means at the end.
chunks.source: 'finally' means at the end.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'photograph' mean? A: a picture taken with a camera. 'photograph' means a picture taken with a camera.
chunks.source: 'photograph' means a picture taken with a camera.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: He showed a ___ of the lake. A: photograph. The word is 'photograph': He showed a photograph of the lake.
chunks.source: The word is 'photograph': He showed a photograph of the lake.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: My aunt is a ___. A: relative. The word is 'relative': My aunt is a relative.
chunks.source: The word is 'relative': My aunt is a relative.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: I ___ not saving money. A: regret. The word is 'regret': I regret not saving money.
chunks.source: The word is 'regret': I regret not saving money.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'fail to catch or do'? A: miss. fail to catch or do — that is 'miss'.
chunks.source: fail to catch or do — that is 'miss'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'before the usual time'? A: early. before the usual time — that is 'early'.
chunks.source: before the usual time — that is 'early'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: He arrived ___. A: late. The word is 'late': He arrived late.
chunks.source: The word is 'late': He arrived late.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'experience' mean? A: something you live through. 'experience' means something you live through.
chunks.source: 'experience' means something you live through.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: She will ___ for the trip. A: save. The word is 'save': She will save for the trip.
chunks.source: The word is 'save': She will save for the trip.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'information about recent events'? A: news. information about recent events — that is 'news'.
chunks.source: information about recent events — that is 'news'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'to bring something to the receiver'? A: deliver. to bring something to the receiver — that is 'deliver'.
chunks.source: to bring something to the receiver — that is 'deliver'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'address' mean? A: the place where someone lives or works. 'address' means the place where someone lives or works.
chunks.source: 'address' means the place where someone lives or works.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'friendly' mean? A: kind and warm in manner. 'friendly' means kind and warm in manner.
chunks.source: 'friendly' means kind and warm in manner.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'to pick up something'? A: collect. to pick up something — that is 'collect'.
chunks.source: to pick up something — that is 'collect'.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'envelope' mean? A: a paper cover for a letter. 'envelope' means a paper cover for a letter.
chunks.source: 'envelope' means a paper cover for a letter.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Kato added his ___. A: signature. The word is 'signature': Kato added his signature.
chunks.source: The word is 'signature': Kato added his signature.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: What does 'stamp' mean? A: a small sticker that pays for postage. 'stamp' means a small sticker that pays for postage.
chunks.source: 'stamp' means a small sticker that pays for postage.

chunks.subject: Theme
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'a job or position'? A: post. a job or position — that is 'post'.
chunks.source: a job or position — that is 'post'.
