Things that are **different** go in separate groups. Keywords: sort: put things into groups; group: a set of things together; same: alike in some way; different: not the same; size: how big or small
chunks.source: We **sort** objects into **groups** by **size**, colour, or shape. Things that are the **same** go together. Things that are **different** go in separate groups.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What does **sort** mean? A: To put things into groups by size, colour, or shape.
chunks.source: To put things into groups by size, colour, or shape.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What do you put in one **group**? A: Things that are the **same**.
chunks.source: Things that are the **same**.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Amina has 3 red stones and 2 blue stones. How many **groups** by colour? A: Two groups.
chunks.source: Two groups.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If leaves are big and small, they are **different** in what? A: Size.
chunks.source: Size.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Kato **sorts** 5 stones by size. He makes 2 groups. What does he do? A: He puts same size stones together.
chunks.source: He puts same size stones together.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Measuring with Hands and Feet. I can measure length using hand spans, foot paces, and sticks. We **measure** **length** using hand **spans**, foot **paces**, or sticks. We count how many to know how **long** something is. Keywords: measure: find how long or big; span: distance from thumb to little finger; pace: a step when walking; length: how long something is; long: having much length
chunks.source: We **measure** **length** using hand **spans**, foot **paces**, or sticks. We count how many to know how **long** something is.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What does **measure** mean? A: To find how long or big something is.
chunks.source: To find how long or big something is.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is a **span**? A: The distance from thumb to little finger.
chunks.source: The distance from thumb to little finger.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is a **pace**? A: A step when walking.
chunks.source: A step when walking.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Amina measures a book with 4 hand **spans**. What is the **length**? A: 4 spans.
chunks.source: 4 spans.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which is **long**: a pencil or a rope? A: The rope is long.
chunks.source: The rope is long.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Adding in the Garden. I can add numbers to find the total up to 50. We **add** numbers to find the **total** or **sum**. **Altogether** means the same as total. **More** means adding to what we have. Keywords: add: put numbers together; total: the whole amount; altogether: in total; more: added to what is there; sum: the answer when you add
chunks.source: We **add** numbers to find the **total** or **sum**. **Altogether** means the same as total. **More** means adding to what we have.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What does **add** mean? A: To put numbers together.
chunks.source: To put numbers together.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Amina has 4 flowers. Kato gives her 2 **more**. How many **altogether**? A: 6 flowers.
chunks.source: 6 flowers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the **sum** of 5 and 3? A: 8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: There are 6 birds. 3 **more** come. What is the **total**? A: 9 birds.
chunks.source: 9 birds.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write an addition for: 2 stones and 4 stones. A: 2 + 4 = 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Counting Together. I can count objects up to one hundred. We **count** by making **groups** of ten. Ten **groups** make one **hundred**. Keywords: count: to say numbers in order; hundred: ten groups of ten; number: a symbol for how many; many: a large amount; group: a set of things together
chunks.source: We **count** by making **groups** of ten. Ten **groups** make one **hundred**.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many **groups** of ten make one **hundred**? A: Ten **groups**.
chunks.source: Ten **groups**.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: **Count** by tens: ten, twenty, thirty, ____? A: Forty
chunks.source: Forty

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If you have five **groups** of ten, what is the **number**? A: Fifty
chunks.source: Fifty

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Point to a **group** of ten stones. A: Child points to ten stones.
chunks.source: Child points to ten stones.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Sharing Fair Shares. I can share equally among two and four people. **Share** by making **equal** piles. **Each** gets the same. That is **fair**. **Half** is one of two **equal** parts. Keywords: share: to give parts to others; equal: the same amount for each; fair: right and just; each: every one person; half: one of two equal parts
chunks.source: **Share** by making **equal** piles. **Each** gets the same. That is **fair**. **Half** is one of two **equal** parts.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Eight sweets **shared** by two. How many for **each**? A: Four
chunks.source: Four

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Twelve groundnuts **shared** by four. How many for **each**? A: Three
chunks.source: Three

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Cut a paper circle in **half**. Are the parts **equal**? A: Yes, two **equal** parts.
chunks.source: Yes, two **equal** parts.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Is it **fair** if Amina gets six and Kato gets two? A: No, not **equal**.
chunks.source: No, not **equal**.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Telling the Time. I can tell time: o'clock and half past. Short **hand** shows **hour**. Long **hand** up is **o'clock**. Long **hand** down is **half past**. Read the **clock** to know the **time**. Keywords: clock: a tool that shows time; hour: sixty minutes; half past: thirty minutes after the hour; time: what the clock shows; hands: the pointers on a clock
chunks.source: Short **hand** shows **hour**. Long **hand** up is **o'clock**. Long **hand** down is **half past**. Read the **clock** to know the **time**.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Short **hand** on three, long **hand** up. What **time**? A: Three **o'clock**
chunks.source: Three **o'clock**

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Short **hand** past six, long **hand** down. What **time**? A: **Half past** six
chunks.source: **Half past** six

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Draw a **clock** showing seven **o'clock**. A: Child draws short **hand** on seven, long **hand** up.
chunks.source: Child draws short **hand** on seven, long **hand** up.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What **time** is lunch at your school? A: Child answers, e.g., one **o'clock**.
chunks.source: Child answers, e.g., one **o'clock**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Living Things in Our School. I can name living things in my school. **Living** things grow and breathe. **Tree**, **flower**, **grass**, and **hen** are **living**. Keywords: tree: a big plant with a trunk; flower: a pretty part of a plant; grass: short green plants on the ground; hen: a bird that lays eggs; living: something that grows and breathes
chunks.source: **Living** things grow and breathe. **Tree**, **flower**, **grass**, and **hen** are **living**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one **living** thing at school. A: **tree** or **flower** or **grass** or **hen**
chunks.source: **tree** or **flower** or **grass** or **hen**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Is a **flower** **living**? A: Yes
chunks.source: Yes

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Is a book **living**? A: No
chunks.source: No

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does **living** mean? A: Grows and breathes
chunks.source: Grows and breathes

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Point to **grass** in the picture. A: Child points to grass
chunks.source: Child points to grass

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Things That Are Not Living. I can name non-living things in my school. **Non-living** things do not grow or breathe. **Desk**, **stone**, **book** are **non-living** **thing**s. Keywords: desk: a table for writing; stone: a hard piece of rock; book: pages with words and pictures; non-living: does not grow or breathe; thing: an object you can see or touch
chunks.source: **Non-living** things do not grow or breathe. **Desk**, **stone**, **book** are **non-living** **thing**s.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one **non-living** thing in class. A: **desk** or **book** or **stone**
chunks.source: **desk** or **book** or **stone**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Is a **stone** **living**? A: No
chunks.source: No

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Is a **hen** **non-living**? A: No
chunks.source: No

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does **non-living** mean? A: Does not grow or breathe
chunks.source: Does not grow or breathe

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Point to a **desk** in the picture. A: Child points to desk
chunks.source: Child points to desk

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Keeping Our School Clean. I can help keep my school compound clean. A **clean** **compound** is healthy. Put **rubbish** in the **bin**. **Sweep** every day. Keywords: clean: free from dirt; rubbish: waste like paper and plastic; bin: a container for rubbish; sweep: to clean with a broom; compound: the school yard
chunks.source: A **clean** **compound** is healthy. Put **rubbish** in the **bin**. **Sweep** every day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do we put **rubbish**? A: In the **bin**
chunks.source: In the **bin**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What tool do we use to **sweep**? A: A broom
chunks.source: A broom

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Is a dirty **compound** good? A: No
chunks.source: No

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does **clean** mean? A: Free from dirt
chunks.source: Free from dirt

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Say one way to keep school **clean**. A: **Sweep** or use **bin**
chunks.source: **Sweep** or use **bin**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Animals at Home. I can name animals we keep at home. We keep goats, hens, dogs, and cats at home. They give us food and keep us safe. Keywords: goat: an animal that gives milk and meat; hen: a bird that lays eggs; dog: an animal that guards the home; cat: an animal that catches mice; home: the place where we live
chunks.source: We keep goats, hens, dogs, and cats at home. They give us food and keep us safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What animal gives us eggs? A: hen
chunks.source: hen

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What animal guards the home at night? A: dog
chunks.source: dog

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What animal says maa maa? A: goat
chunks.source: goat

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do the animals live? A: home
chunks.source: home

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What animal catches mice? A: cat
chunks.source: cat

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Plants at Home. I can name plants found at home. Banana plants, flowers, trees, and leaves grow in our garden. Leaves make food for plants. Keywords: banana: a plant with long leaves and fruit; flower: the colourful part of a plant; tree: a big plant with a trunk; leaf: the green part of a plant; garden: a place where plants grow
chunks.source: Banana plants, flowers, trees, and leaves grow in our garden. Leaves make food for plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What plant has big green leaves? A: banana
chunks.source: banana

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What colourful part grows on plants? A: flower
chunks.source: flower

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What big plant has a trunk? A: tree
chunks.source: tree

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What green part makes food? A: leaf
chunks.source: leaf

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do plants grow at home? A: garden
chunks.source: garden

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Water at Home. I can name water sources and uses at home. We get water from the well. We carry it in a jerrycan. Clean water is safe to drink. Keywords: water: clear liquid we need to live; well: a deep hole in the ground for water; jerrycan: a plastic container for carrying water; clean: free from dirt and germs; drink: to take liquid into the mouth
chunks.source: We get water from the well. We carry it in a jerrycan. Clean water is safe to drink.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do we get water from the ground? A: well
chunks.source: well

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we carry water in? A: jerrycan
chunks.source: jerrycan

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What must water be before we drink? A: clean
chunks.source: clean

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we do when thirsty? A: drink
chunks.source: drink

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What liquid do we need every day? A: water
chunks.source: water

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Animals in Our Community. I can name domestic animals and say how they help us. Cows, goats, pigs, and donkeys live in our community. They give milk, meat, and carry loads. We see them at the market. Keywords: cow: big animal that gives milk; goat: small animal that gives milk; pig: animal that gives meat; donkey: strong animal that carries loads; market: place where people buy and sell
chunks.source: Cows, goats, pigs, and donkeys live in our community. They give milk, meat, and carry loads. We see them at the market.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What animal gives milk? A: Cow or goat
chunks.source: Cow or goat

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What animal carries loads? A: Donkey
chunks.source: Donkey

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do people buy animals? A: Market
chunks.source: Market

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What animal likes mud? A: Pig
chunks.source: Pig

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two animals that give milk. A: Cow and goat
chunks.source: Cow and goat

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Plants in Our Community. I can name useful plants and say how we use them. Mango, cassava, maize, and sugarcane are useful **plants**. They give us fruit, roots, grains, and juice. We grow them in our community. Keywords: mango: tree with sweet yellow fruit; cassava: root crop we cook for food; maize: tall plant with yellow grains; sugarcane: tall stem we chew for juice; plant: living thing that grows in soil
chunks.source: Mango, cassava, maize, and sugarcane are useful **plants**. They give us fruit, roots, grains, and juice. We grow them in our community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What fruit grows on a tree? A: Mango
chunks.source: Mango

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What plant do we chew for juice? A: Sugarcane
chunks.source: Sugarcane

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What plant makes posho? A: Maize
chunks.source: Maize

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What root crop do we peel? A: Cassava
chunks.source: Cassava

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two plants in the garden. A: Mango and maize
chunks.source: Mango and maize

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Keeping Our Community Clean. I can keep my home and school clean and safe. We put **rubbish** in the **dustbin**. We **sweep** to make places **clean**. A **clean** community keeps us healthy. Keywords: rubbish: waste we throw away; dustbin: box for rubbish; dirty: not clean; clean: free from dirt; sweep: use a broom to clean
chunks.source: We put **rubbish** in the **dustbin**. We **sweep** to make places **clean**. A **clean** community keeps us healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do we put rubbish? A: In the dustbin
chunks.source: In the dustbin

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we use to sweep? A: A broom
chunks.source: A broom

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What makes a place dirty? A: Rubbish
chunks.source: Rubbish

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the opposite of dirty? A: Clean
chunks.source: Clean

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What should you do with a wrapper? A: Put in dustbin
chunks.source: Put in dustbin

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Parts of My Body. I can name six parts of my body. Amina and Kato learn the names of six body parts: head, eye, ear, nose, mouth, hand. Keywords: head: the top part of your body; eye: the part you see with; ear: the part you hear with; nose: the part you smell with; mouth: the part you eat and talk with; hand: the part at the end of your arm
chunks.source: Amina and Kato learn the names of six body parts: head, eye, ear, nose, mouth, hand.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is this? (point to head) A: head
chunks.source: head

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is this? (point to eye) A: eye
chunks.source: eye

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is this? (point to ear) A: ear
chunks.source: ear

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is this? (point to hand) A: hand
chunks.source: hand

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Keeping My Body Clean. I can tell how to keep my body clean. Amina and Kato learn to use soap, water, a brush, and take a bath to stay clean. Keywords: soap: a thing you use to wash; water: liquid you drink and wash with; brush: a tool to clean teeth; teeth: the white parts in your mouth; bath: washing your whole body
chunks.source: Amina and Kato learn to use soap, water, a brush, and take a bath to stay clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do you use to wash hands? A: soap
chunks.source: soap

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do you pour from a jerrycan? A: water
chunks.source: water

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do you use to clean teeth? A: brush
chunks.source: brush

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do you do to wash your whole body? A: bath
chunks.source: bath

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Food That Keeps Me Healthy. I can name foods that make me strong. Amina and Kato learn that food like banana, milk, and egg help them grow strong. Keywords: food: things you eat; banana: a yellow fruit; milk: a white drink from cows; egg: a round food from a chicken; strong: having power
chunks.source: Amina and Kato learn that food like banana, milk, and egg help them grow strong.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do you eat at lunch? A: food
chunks.source: food

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name a yellow fruit. A: banana
chunks.source: banana

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What white drink comes from cows? A: milk
chunks.source: milk

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What food comes from a chicken? A: egg
chunks.source: egg

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: The Sun. I can name what the sun gives us. The sun gives light and heat. It makes day. Our shadows show where light is blocked. Keywords: sun: the big bright ball in the sky; hot: very warm, like fire; light: brightness that helps us see; shadow: dark shape made when light is blocked; day: time when the sun shines
chunks.source: The sun gives light and heat. It makes day. Our shadows show where light is blocked.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What shines in the sky? A: The sun
chunks.source: The sun

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does the sun give us? A: Light and heat
chunks.source: Light and heat

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a dark shape on the ground? A: A shadow
chunks.source: A shadow

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: When do we see the sun? A: During the day
chunks.source: During the day

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does the sun feel? A: Hot
chunks.source: Hot

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Rain. I can tell what rain brings. Rain falls from clouds. It brings water. Things get wet. An umbrella keeps us dry. Keywords: rain: water falling from the sky; cloud: white or grey puff in the sky; water: clear liquid we drink and use; wet: covered with water; umbrella: cover held over the head in rain
chunks.source: Rain falls from clouds. It brings water. Things get wet. An umbrella keeps us dry.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What falls from clouds? A: Rain
chunks.source: Rain

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does rain bring? A: Water
chunks.source: Water

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What gets wet in rain? A: Clothes, ground, shoes
chunks.source: Clothes, ground, shoes

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we hold over our head? A: Umbrella
chunks.source: Umbrella

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What colour is a rain cloud? A: Grey or dark
chunks.source: Grey or dark

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Wind. I can feel and see wind. Wind is moving air. It blows kites and shakes trees. We feel wind but cannot see air. Keywords: wind: moving air we can feel; blow: to push air out; kite: paper toy flown in the wind; tree: big plant with trunk and branches; air: invisible gas all around us
chunks.source: Wind is moving air. It blows kites and shakes trees. We feel wind but cannot see air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is wind? A: Moving air
chunks.source: Moving air

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does wind do to a kite? A: Lifts it up
chunks.source: Lifts it up

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does wind do to a tree? A: Shakes branches
chunks.source: Shakes branches

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we breathe? A: Air
chunks.source: Air

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Can we see air? A: No, but we feel wind
chunks.source: No, but we feel wind

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Things That Can Hurt Me. I can name things at home and school that can hurt me. **Knife**, **fire**, and **sharp** things are **danger**. They can **hurt** you. Always tell an adult. Keywords: knife: a tool with a sharp edge for cutting; fire: hot flames that burn; sharp: has a thin edge that cuts easily; hurt: to feel pain in your body; danger: something that can cause harm
chunks.source: **Knife**, **fire**, and **sharp** things are **danger**. They can **hurt** you. Always tell an adult.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What can **hurt** you in the kitchen? A: A **knife** or **fire** can **hurt** you.
chunks.source: A **knife** or **fire** can **hurt** you.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What word means 'can cause harm'? A: **danger**
chunks.source: **danger**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What should you do if you see a **sharp** **knife**? A: Tell an adult.
chunks.source: Tell an adult.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two **danger** things at home. A: **knife** and **fire**
chunks.source: **knife** and **fire**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Is it safe to play with **fire**? A: No, **fire** can **hurt** you.
chunks.source: No, **fire** can **hurt** you.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Staying Safe on the Road. I can say how to cross the **road** safely. **Look** left, **look** right, wait for **car** to pass, then **cross**. Hold hands to stay **safe** on the **road**. Keywords: road: a path for cars and people; car: a vehicle with four wheels; look: to use your eyes to see; cross: to go from one side to the other; safe: free from harm or danger
chunks.source: **Look** left, **look** right, wait for **car** to pass, then **cross**. Hold hands to stay **safe** on the **road**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What must you do before you **cross** the **road**? A: **Look** left and right.
chunks.source: **Look** left and right.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What can go fast on the **road**? A: A **car** or boda boda.
chunks.source: A **car** or boda boda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we hold hands? A: To stay **safe**.
chunks.source: To stay **safe**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do we **cross** the **road**? A: At the zebra lines.
chunks.source: At the zebra lines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Is it **safe** to run on the **road**? A: No, running is not **safe**.
chunks.source: No, running is not **safe**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: First Help for Small Cuts. I can help clean a small **cut**. For a small **cut**: **wash** with water, stop the **blood**, put a **plaster**, keep it **clean**. Keywords: cut: a small opening in the skin; blood: red liquid that comes from a **cut**; wash: to clean with water and soap; plaster: a sticky cover for a **cut**; clean: free from dirt and germs
chunks.source: For a small **cut**: **wash** with water, stop the **blood**, put a **plaster**, keep it **clean**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What comes out of a **cut**? A: **blood**
chunks.source: **blood**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do you use to **wash** a **cut**? A: Clean water and soap.
chunks.source: Clean water and soap.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What keeps a **cut** **clean**? A: A **plaster**.
chunks.source: A **plaster**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What should you do first for a **cut**? A: **Wash** it.
chunks.source: **Wash** it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why put a **plaster** on a **cut**? A: To keep it **clean**.
chunks.source: To keep it **clean**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Animals That Live Together. I can name animals that live in groups. Bees, ants, and cows live in groups. A group of cows is called a herd. Keywords: bee: a flying insect that makes honey; ant: a small insect that walks in lines; cow: a big animal that gives milk; herd: a group of cows or goats; group: many animals together
chunks.source: Bees, ants, and cows live in groups. A group of cows is called a herd.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What insect makes honey? A: bee
chunks.source: bee

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we call a line of ants? A: a group
chunks.source: a group

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a group of cows called? A: a herd
chunks.source: a herd

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one animal that lives in a group. A: bee or ant or cow
chunks.source: bee or ant or cow

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Do cows live alone? A: no
chunks.source: no

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Plants Grow Together. I can name plants that grow together in a garden. Maize and beans grow together in the garden. We pull weeds so they grow well. Keywords: maize: a tall plant with yellow seeds; beans: a plant with pods we eat; garden: a place where plants grow; grow: to get bigger; weed: a wild plant that takes food
chunks.source: Maize and beans grow together in the garden. We pull weeds so they grow well.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What tall plant gives us posho? A: maize
chunks.source: maize

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What plant grows in pods? A: beans
chunks.source: beans

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do plants grow? A: in the garden
chunks.source: in the garden

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we call a wild plant that takes food? A: weed
chunks.source: weed

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do plants need to grow? A: water and soil
chunks.source: water and soil

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Sharing Water and Food. I can say how we share water and food with friends. Friends share water and food. Clean water keeps us well. Sharing is caring. Keywords: share: to give some to others; water: liquid we drink and use; food: what we eat to stay strong; clean: not dirty; friend: a person we like and trust
chunks.source: Friends share water and food. Clean water keeps us well. Sharing is caring.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What did Amina give Kato? A: water
chunks.source: water

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we say when we give some to others? A: share
chunks.source: share

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we eat to stay strong? A: food
chunks.source: food

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What kind of water do we use to wash? A: clean water
chunks.source: clean water

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who is Kato to Amina? A: friend
chunks.source: friend

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Foods from Plants. I can name foods we get from plants. We get **mango**, **matooke**, **cassava**, **groundnuts**, and other **fruit** from plants. Keywords: mango: a sweet yellow fruit; matooke: green bananas we steam; cassava: a brown root we boil; groundnuts: nuts that grow under soil; fruit: sweet food from a plant
chunks.source: We get **mango**, **matooke**, **cassava**, **groundnuts**, and other **fruit** from plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name a **fruit** from the story. A: mango
chunks.source: mango

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which food grows under the soil? A: groundnuts
chunks.source: groundnuts

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What green food do we steam? A: matooke
chunks.source: matooke

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which root do we boil? A: cassava
chunks.source: cassava

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Say two **foods from plants**. A: mango, matooke, cassava, or groundnuts
chunks.source: mango, matooke, cassava, or groundnuts

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Foods from Animals. I can name foods we get from animals. We get **egg** from a **hen**, **milk** from a cow, **meat** from goats or cows, and **fish** from water. Keywords: egg: comes from a hen; milk: white drink from a cow; meat: animal flesh we cook; fish: swims in water, we eat it; hen: bird that lays eggs
chunks.source: We get **egg** from a **hen**, **milk** from a cow, **meat** from goats or cows, and **fish** from water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does a **hen** give us? A: egg
chunks.source: egg

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What white drink comes from a cow? A: milk
chunks.source: milk

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name a food from a goat. A: meat
chunks.source: meat

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What swims in the lake? A: fish
chunks.source: fish

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Say two **foods from animals**. A: egg, milk, meat, or fish
chunks.source: egg, milk, meat, or fish

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Eating Clean Food. I can keep food clean and safe to eat. We **wash** hands to remove **germs**. We **cover** food to keep it **clean**. **Dirty** things bring **germs**. Keywords: wash: clean with water and soap; clean: free from dirt; cover: put a lid on top; dirty: not clean, has soil; germs: tiny things that make us sick
chunks.source: We **wash** hands to remove **germs**. We **cover** food to keep it **clean**. **Dirty** things bring **germs**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we do before eating? A: wash hands
chunks.source: wash hands

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What hides on **dirty** hands? A: germs
chunks.source: germs

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we put on a pot? A: a lid / cover
chunks.source: a lid / cover

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: If a spoon falls, is it **clean**? A: no, it is dirty
chunks.source: no, it is dirty

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Say one way to keep food safe. A: wash hands or cover food
chunks.source: wash hands or cover food

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Things That Move. I can name things that move. Amina and Kato see cars, buses, bicycles, and boats. All these things move people and goods. Keywords: car: a vehicle with four wheels; bus: a big vehicle for many people; bicycle: a vehicle with two wheels; boat: a vehicle that floats on water; move: to go from one place to another
chunks.source: Amina and Kato see cars, buses, bicycles, and boats. All these things move people and goods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What has four wheels and moves on the road? A: car
chunks.source: car

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What big vehicle carries many people? A: bus
chunks.source: bus

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What has two wheels and you pedal it? A: bicycle
chunks.source: bicycle

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What floats on water and moves? A: boat
chunks.source: boat

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What word means to go from one place to another? A: move
chunks.source: move

chunks.id: L-P1-Science-Moving on Land, Water and Air
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Moving on Land, Water and Air
chunks.text: Moving on Land, Water and Air. I can say where different transport moves. The train moves on the road, boats move on water, and planes fly in the air. Keywords: road: a path for cars and buses; water: where boats and ships go; air: the sky where planes fly; plane: a vehicle that flies in the air; train: a vehicle that runs on rails
chunks.source: The train moves on the road, boats move on water, and planes fly in the air.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Science-Moving on Land, Water and Air
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Moving on Land, Water and Air
chunks.text: Q: Where does a car drive? A: On the road.
chunks.source: On the road.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Science-Moving on Land, Water and Air
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Moving on Land, Water and Air
chunks.text: Q: Where does a boat sail? A: On the water.
chunks.source: On the water.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Science-Moving on Land, Water and Air
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Moving on Land, Water and Air
chunks.text: Q: Where does a plane fly? A: In the air.
chunks.source: In the air.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Science-Moving on Land, Water and Air
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Moving on Land, Water and Air
chunks.text: Q: What runs on rails and carries goods? A: A train.
chunks.source: A train.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Science-Moving on Land, Water and Air
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Moving on Land, Water and Air
chunks.text: Q: Name the three places transport moves. A: Road, water, air.
chunks.source: Road, water, air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Keeping Safe When Travelling. I can stay safe when I travel. Amina and Kato sit in their seats, wear belts, and listen to the driver. They are safe at every stop. Keywords: seat: a place to sit in a vehicle; belt: a strap that keeps you safe; safe: free from danger; driver: the person who drives the vehicle; stop: a place where the vehicle halts
chunks.source: Amina and Kato sit in their seats, wear belts, and listen to the driver. They are safe at every stop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do you sit on in a bus? A: A seat.
chunks.source: A seat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do you wear to be safe? A: A belt.
chunks.source: A belt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who drives the bus? A: The driver.
chunks.source: The driver.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where does the bus let you off? A: At the stop.
chunks.source: At the stop.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we wear a belt? A: To be safe.
chunks.source: To be safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Things Made from Plants. I can name things made from plants. We make baskets from sisal and mats from banana fibre. Both are plant materials. Keywords: basket: a container made of woven material; mat: a flat piece for sitting or sleeping; sisal: a strong fibre from a plant; banana fibre: fibre from banana plant; make: to create something
chunks.source: We make baskets from sisal and mats from banana fibre. Both are plant materials.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a basket made from? A: sisal
chunks.source: sisal

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a mat made from? A: banana fibre
chunks.source: banana fibre

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we do to create these items? A: make
chunks.source: make

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name a plant material used for weaving. A: sisal
chunks.source: sisal

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Things Made from Clay. I can name things made from clay. We make pots from clay and soil. The pot must dry in the sun. Keywords: clay: soft earth used for pots; pot: a container made from clay; soil: the top layer of earth; dry: to become without water; make: to create something
chunks.source: We make pots from clay and soil. The pot must dry in the sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a pot made from? A: clay
chunks.source: clay

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is mixed with clay? A: soil
chunks.source: soil

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens to the pot in the sun? A: it gets dry
chunks.source: it gets dry

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does the potter do? A: make a pot
chunks.source: make a pot

chunks.id: L-P1-Science-Things Made from Metal and Wood
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Things Made from Metal and Wood
chunks.text: Things Made from Metal and Wood. I can name things made from metal and wood. Wood and metal together make strong things. A hammer and nail help join them. Keywords: metal: a hard, shiny material like iron; wood: material from trees; nail: a small metal pin; hammer: a tool for hitting nails; strong: not easily broken
chunks.source: Wood and metal together make strong things. A hammer and nail help join them.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Science-Things Made from Metal and Wood
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Things Made from Metal and Wood
chunks.text: Q: What material is shiny and hard? A: metal
chunks.source: metal

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Science-Things Made from Metal and Wood
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Things Made from Metal and Wood
chunks.text: Q: What material comes from trees? A: wood
chunks.source: wood

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Science-Things Made from Metal and Wood
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Things Made from Metal and Wood
chunks.text: Q: What do you hit with a hammer? A: a nail
chunks.source: a nail

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Science-Things Made from Metal and Wood
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Things Made from Metal and Wood
chunks.text: Q: Why are wood and metal good together? A: they are strong
chunks.source: they are strong

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Things Around Us. I can name the parts of our environment. Our environment has **soil**, **water**, **air**, **plants**, and **animals**. All living things need them. Keywords: soil: the ground we walk on; water: liquid we drink and use; air: what we breathe; plant: living thing that grows in soil; animal: living thing that moves and eats
chunks.source: Our environment has **soil**, **water**, **air**, **plants**, and **animals**. All living things need them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the ground called? A: **soil**
chunks.source: **soil**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we drink? A: **water**
chunks.source: **water**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we breathe? A: **air**
chunks.source: **air**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What grows in the ground? A: **plant**
chunks.source: **plant**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What moves and eats? A: **animal**
chunks.source: **animal**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Caring for Plants and Animals. I can tell how to care for living things. We **water** and **feed** plants and animals. We **care** for them and **protect** them so they **grow**. Keywords: water: give drink to; feed: give food to; care: look after well; grow: get bigger; protect: keep safe from harm
chunks.source: We **water** and **feed** plants and animals. We **care** for them and **protect** them so they **grow**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we give a thirsty plant? A: **water**
chunks.source: **water**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we give a hungry animal? A: **feed**
chunks.source: **feed**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does 'look after' mean? A: **care**
chunks.source: **care**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does a seedling do? A: **grow**
chunks.source: **grow**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does 'keep safe' mean? A: **protect**
chunks.source: **protect**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Keeping Our Environment Clean. I can keep my place clean and safe. Put **litter** in the **bin**. **Burn** dry waste safely. A **clean** environment keeps us healthy. Keywords: litter: rubbish on the ground; bin: container for rubbish; burn: destroy with fire; dirty: not clean; clean: free from dirt
chunks.source: Put **litter** in the **bin**. **Burn** dry waste safely. A **clean** environment keeps us healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is rubbish on the ground called? A: **litter**
chunks.source: **litter**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do we put rubbish? A: **bin**
chunks.source: **bin**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we do with dry leaves? A: **burn**
chunks.source: **burn**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is the opposite of **clean**? A: **dirty**
chunks.source: **dirty**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we want our compound to be? A: **clean**
chunks.source: **clean**

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Keeping Safe at Home. I can keep safe at home by locking doors and telling adults about strangers. Lock the door, do not open to strangers, and tell an adult to report any danger. Keywords: lock: a device to fasten a door; door: the entry to a room or house; stranger: a person you do not know; safe: free from harm; report: to tell an adult about a problem
chunks.source: Lock the door, do not open to strangers, and tell an adult to report any danger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do you turn to close the door? A: lock
chunks.source: lock

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who should you tell if a stranger knocks? A: an adult
chunks.source: an adult

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What word means not in danger? A: safe
chunks.source: safe

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do you do when you see a stranger at the gate? A: report to an adult
chunks.source: report to an adult

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: People Who Keep Us Safe. I can name people who help keep me safe. Police, guard, teacher, and parent all help keep us safe. Keywords: police: officers who protect the community; guard: a person who watches a gate or building; teacher: a person who teaches and cares for pupils; parent: a mother or father who cares for a child; help: to give assistance
chunks.source: Police, guard, teacher, and parent all help keep us safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who waves from the road? A: police
chunks.source: police

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who stands at the school gate? A: guard
chunks.source: guard

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who teaches you in class? A: teacher
chunks.source: teacher

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who cares for you at home? A: parent
chunks.source: parent

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do all these people do for you? A: help
chunks.source: help

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Danger Signs Around Us. I can recognise danger signs and know what to do. Signs like stop and warning tell us about danger and poison. We stop and stay safe. Keywords: sign: a board that gives information; danger: something that can cause harm; poison: a substance that can make you very sick; warning: a notice that tells you to be careful; stop: to cease moving
chunks.source: Signs like stop and warning tell us about danger and poison. We stop and stay safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does a red sign with the word stop mean? A: stop
chunks.source: stop

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What should you do when you see a warning sign? A: stop and stay away
chunks.source: stop and stay away

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What word means a harmful substance? A: poison
chunks.source: poison

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does the word danger mean? A: something that can hurt you
chunks.source: something that can hurt you

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do you do if you see a sign that says warning? A: be careful and stay away
chunks.source: be careful and stay away

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: My School and Its Symbols. I can name the symbols of my school. Amina and Kato learn the school symbols: gate, sign post, name, flag, badge, and uniform. Keywords: school: place where we learn; flag: cloth with colours; badge: small emblem; uniform: same clothes for all; gate: entrance door; sign post: board with name; name: what something is called
chunks.source: Amina and Kato learn the school symbols: gate, sign post, name, flag, badge, and uniform.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does the sign post show? A: The sign post shows the name of the school.
chunks.source: The sign post shows the name of the school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What colour is the flag? A: The flag flies high with bright colours.
chunks.source: The flag flies high with bright colours.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do pupils wear? A: Pupils wear the uniform.
chunks.source: Pupils wear the uniform.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where is the gate? A: The gate is at the school entrance.
chunks.source: The gate is at the school entrance.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is on the badge? A: The badge has the school symbol.
chunks.source: The badge has the school symbol.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Leaders and Helpers at School. I can name the leaders and helpers at school. Amina and Kato meet the head teacher, deputy, teacher, pupil, cook, cleaner, and askari. Keywords: head teacher: school leader; deputy: assistant leader; teacher: person who teaches; pupil: child who learns; cook: makes food; cleaner: keeps place clean; askari: guard
chunks.source: Amina and Kato meet the head teacher, deputy, teacher, pupil, cook, cleaner, and askari.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who is the school leader? A: The head teacher leads the school.
chunks.source: The head teacher leads the school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who helps the head teacher? A: The deputy helps the head teacher.
chunks.source: The deputy helps the head teacher.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who teaches the class? A: The teacher teaches the class.
chunks.source: The teacher teaches the class.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who cooks the food? A: The cook prepares the food.
chunks.source: The cook prepares the food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who keeps the school safe? A: The askari guards the school.
chunks.source: The askari guards the school.

chunks.id: L-P1-Social-Rules That Keep Our School Happy
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Rules That Keep Our School Happy
chunks.text: Rules That Keep Our School Happy. I can follow the rules that keep our school happy. Amina and Kato learn to listen, share, respect, care, queue, and tidy to keep school happy. Keywords: rules: what we must do; listen: hear carefully; share: give to others; respect: treat nicely; care: look after; queue: stand in line; tidy: make clean
chunks.source: Amina and Kato learn to listen, share, respect, care, queue, and tidy to keep school happy.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-Rules That Keep Our School Happy
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Rules That Keep Our School Happy
chunks.text: Q: What must we do in class? A: We must listen to the teacher.
chunks.source: We must listen to the teacher.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-Rules That Keep Our School Happy
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Rules That Keep Our School Happy
chunks.text: Q: How do we keep the room clean? A: We tidy up after work.
chunks.source: We tidy up after work.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-Rules That Keep Our School Happy
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Rules That Keep Our School Happy
chunks.text: Q: What do we do when we wait? A: We queue in a line.
chunks.source: We queue in a line.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-Rules That Keep Our School Happy
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Rules That Keep Our School Happy
chunks.text: Q: How do we treat friends? A: We respect and care for them.
chunks.source: We respect and care for them.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-Rules That Keep Our School Happy
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Rules That Keep Our School Happy
chunks.text: Q: What do we do with toys? A: We share toys with others.
chunks.source: We share toys with others.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Who Lives in My Home. I can name the people who live in my home. Amina's home has father, mother, grandfather, grandmother, brother, sister, and baby. They all live together and help each other. Keywords: father: male parent; mother: female parent; grandfather: father's father; grandmother: mother's mother; brother: male sibling; sister: female sibling; baby: very young child
chunks.source: Amina's home has father, mother, grandfather, grandmother, brother, sister, and baby. They all live together and help each other.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who cooks the food? A: Mother
chunks.source: Mother

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who tells stories? A: Grandfather
chunks.source: Grandfather

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who helps the baby? A: Sister
chunks.source: Sister

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who plays with a ball? A: Brother
chunks.source: Brother

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Homes in Our Village. I can name parts of a home in my village. A village has houses and huts with roofs, walls, doors, windows, and compounds. Keywords: house: building for living; hut: small grass house; roof: top cover of a house; wall: side of a house; door: entry opening; window: glass opening for light; compound: open space around house
chunks.source: A village has houses and huts with roofs, walls, doors, windows, and compounds.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the top cover called? A: Roof
chunks.source: Roof

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the opening for people? A: Door
chunks.source: Door

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What lets light in? A: Window
chunks.source: Window

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the open space outside? A: Compound
chunks.source: Compound

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Work People Do at Home. I can name jobs people do at home. At home people cook, sweep, wash, fetch water, dig, care, and help each other. Keywords: cook: make food ready; sweep: clean floor with broom; wash: clean clothes with water; fetch water: get water from borehole; dig: turn soil for planting; care: look after someone; help: give assistance
chunks.source: At home people cook, sweep, wash, fetch water, dig, care, and help each other.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does mother do? A: Cook
chunks.source: Cook

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does grandmother do? A: Sweep
chunks.source: Sweep

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does sister do? A: Fetch water
chunks.source: Fetch water

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does everyone do? A: Help
chunks.source: Help

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Places That Serve Our Community. I can name places that help our community. Amina and Kato learn about places that serve their community: market, hospital, shop, church, mosque, school, and police post. Keywords: market: place to buy food; hospital: place for sick people; shop: small place to buy things; church: place for Christian prayer; mosque: place for Muslim prayer; school: place where children learn; police post: place where police work
chunks.source: Amina and Kato learn about places that serve their community: market, hospital, shop, church, mosque, school, and police post.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do we buy matooke? A: market
chunks.source: market

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do sick people go? A: hospital
chunks.source: hospital

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do Christians pray? A: church
chunks.source: church

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do children learn? A: school
chunks.source: school

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do police work? A: police post
chunks.source: police post

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Leaders Who Guide Our Community. I can name leaders who guide our community. Amina and Kato learn about leaders who guide their community: chairperson, elder, chief, priest, imam, councillor, and leader. Keywords: chairperson: leader of a village group; elder: old person with wisdom; chief: traditional leader of a clan; priest: Christian religious leader; imam: Muslim religious leader; councillor: elected leader for an area; leader: person who guides others
chunks.source: Amina and Kato learn about leaders who guide their community: chairperson, elder, chief, priest, imam, councillor, and leader.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who leads the village meeting? A: chairperson
chunks.source: chairperson

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who gives wise advice? A: elder
chunks.source: elder

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who is the traditional clan leader? A: chief
chunks.source: chief

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who leads Christian prayer? A: priest
chunks.source: priest

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who leads Muslim prayer? A: imam
chunks.source: imam

chunks.subject: Social

chunks.source: Amina and Kato learn about people and their work: farmer, shopkeeper, tailor, builder, driver, nurse, and teacher.

chunks.text: My Body Helps Me Every Day. I can name my body parts and say what they do. My body parts like head, eyes, ears, nose, mouth, hands, and legs help me every day. chunks.source: My body parts like head, eyes, ears, nose, mouth, hands, and legs help me every day.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Keeping Healthy at Home and School
chunks.text: Keeping Healthy at Home and School. I can tell how to keep clean and healthy at home and school. We stay healthy by washing with soap, brushing teeth, taking a bath, and using the latrine. Keywords: wash: clean with water; soap: thing to clean with; brush: clean with a brush; teeth: white parts in mouth; bath: wash whole body; latrine: toilet place; clean: not dirty
chunks.source: We stay healthy by washing with soap, brushing teeth, taking a bath, and using the latrine.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-Keeping Healthy at Home and School

chunks.id: L-P1-Social-People and Places That Keep Us Healthy
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: People and Places That Keep Us Healthy
chunks.text: People and Places That Keep Us Healthy. I can name the people and places that help us when we are sick. Nurses, doctors, health centres, hospitals, medicine, and immunisation help us when we are sick. Keywords: nurse: helps sick people; doctor: treats sick people; hospital: big place for sick; health centre: small place for sick; medicine: drug to heal; immunisation: shot to prevent disease; sick: not well
chunks.source: Nurses, doctors, health centres, hospitals, medicine, and immunisation help us when we are sick.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-People and Places That Keep Us Healthy
chunks.subject: Social

chunks.text: Q: Who treats you at the hospital? A: doctor

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-People and Places That Keep Us Healthy
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: People and Places That Keep Us Healthy
chunks.text: Q: What do you take to get better? A: medicine

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-People and Places That Keep Us Healthy
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: People and Places That Keep Us Healthy
chunks.text: Q: What shot keeps you from getting sick? A: immunisation
chunks.source: immunisation

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-People and Places That Keep Us Healthy

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Signs of the Weather. I can name signs of different weather. The **sun**, **cloud**, **rain**, **wind**, and **storm** are signs of weather. Weather can be **hot** or **cold**. Keywords: sun: bright light in the sky; cloud: white or grey puff in the sky; rain: water drops from the sky; wind: moving air we feel; storm: strong wind and rain together; hot: feels like fire on skin; cold: feels like ice on skin
chunks.source: The **sun**, **cloud**, **rain**, **wind**, and **storm** are signs of weather. Weather can be **hot** or **cold**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What shines bright in the sky? A: The **sun**.
chunks.source: The **sun**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What brings water from the sky? A: **Rain**.
chunks.source: **Rain**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What moves the leaves and feels cool? A: **Wind**.
chunks.source: **Wind**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we call strong wind and rain together? A: A **storm**.
chunks.source: A **storm**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: If your skin feels like fire, the weather is? A: **Hot**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Weather and What We Wear. I can match clothes to the weather. We use an **umbrella** and **gumboots** for **rain**. A **coat**, **sweater**, and **hat** keep us warm. **Shoes** are for dry ground. Keywords: umbrella: held over head to stop rain; gumboots: tall rubber boots for wet ground; coat: warm cover for the body; hat: cover for the head; sweater: knitted top for warmth; shoes: covers for feet; rain: water falling from sky
chunks.source: We use an **umbrella** and **gumboots** for **rain**. A **coat**, **sweater**, and **hat** keep us warm. **Shoes** are for dry ground.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you hold over your head in rain? A: An **umbrella**.
chunks.source: An **umbrella**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What boots keep feet dry in mud? A: **Gumboots**.
chunks.source: **Gumboots**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What warm cover goes over your clothes? A: A **coat**.
chunks.source: A **coat**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you wear on your head in the sun? A: A **hat**.
chunks.source: A **hat**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What knitted top keeps you warm? A: A **sweater**.
chunks.source: A **sweater**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Weather and Our Work. I can say how weather changes work. The **farmer** **dig**s and **plant**s in the rainy **season**. In the **dry** **season**, the **farmer** **harvest**s. Weather guides work in the **garden**. Keywords: farmer: person who grows food; dig: turn soil with a hoe; plant: put seeds in soil; harvest: cut and gather ripe crops; dry: no rain, sun bakes the ground; garden: plot where crops grow; season: time of year with certain weather
chunks.source: The **farmer** **dig**s and **plant**s in the rainy **season**. In the **dry** **season**, the **farmer** **harvest**s. Weather guides work in the **garden**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who grows food in the garden? A: A **farmer**.
chunks.source: A **farmer**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a farmer do with a hoe? A: **Dig** the soil.
chunks.source: **Dig** the soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a farmer put in the ground? A: **Plant** seeds.
chunks.source: **Plant** seeds.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: When does a farmer cut the ripe maize? A: In the **dry** **season**.
chunks.source: In the **dry** **season**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What time of year has certain weather? A: A **season**.
chunks.source: A **season**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Things That Can Hurt Us. I can name things that can hurt me at home. Knife, fire, medicine, poison, razor, matches, and hot water can hurt us. We tell an adult and stay away. Keywords: knife: a sharp tool for cutting; fire: hot flames that burn; medicine: drugs to make us well; poison: bad liquid that kills; razor: sharp blade for shaving; matches: small sticks to make fire; hot water: very warm water that burns
chunks.source: Knife, fire, medicine, poison, razor, matches, and hot water can hurt us. We tell an adult and stay away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What cuts and is sharp? A: knife
chunks.source: knife

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What burns and cooks food? A: fire
chunks.source: fire

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we take when sick? A: medicine
chunks.source: medicine

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is in a bottle and kills? A: poison
chunks.source: poison

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Staying Safe on the Road. I can cross the road safely. We walk on the side of the road. At the zebra crossing, we look left, look right, then walk across. Keywords: road: path for cars and people; look: use eyes to see; cross: go from one side to other; zebra crossing: white lines to cross safely; left: side of the body with heart; right: other side of the body; walk: move on feet
chunks.source: We walk on the side of the road. At the zebra crossing, we look left, look right, then walk across.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do cars drive? A: road
chunks.source: road

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we do with our eyes? A: look
chunks.source: look

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do we cross safely? A: zebra crossing
chunks.source: zebra crossing

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which side do we look first? A: left
chunks.source: left

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do we move across? A: walk
chunks.source: walk

chunks.id: L-P1-Social-First Help When We Are Hurt
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: First Help When We Are Hurt
chunks.text: First Help When We Are Hurt. I can help when someone gets hurt. For a cut from a fall, we wash it, put a bandage, and see a nurse or doctor if needed. Keywords: first aid: first help when hurt; bandage: cloth to cover a wound; nurse: person who helps sick people; wash: clean with water and soap; cut: open wound from sharp thing; fall: drop down to the ground; doctor: person who treats sick people
chunks.source: For a cut from a fall, we wash it, put a bandage, and see a nurse or doctor if needed.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-First Help When We Are Hurt
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: First Help When We Are Hurt
chunks.text: Q: What is first help called? A: first aid

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-First Help When We Are Hurt
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: First Help When We Are Hurt
chunks.text: Q: What covers a cut? A: bandage
chunks.source: bandage

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-First Help When We Are Hurt
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: First Help When We Are Hurt
chunks.text: Q: Who helps at the clinic? A: nurse
chunks.source: nurse

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-First Help When We Are Hurt
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: First Help When We Are Hurt
chunks.text: Q: What do we do with water and soap? A: wash
chunks.source: wash

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-First Help When We Are Hurt
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: First Help When We Are Hurt
chunks.text: Q: What happens when we drop down? A: fall

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Families and Neighbours. I can name people around me and greet them with respect. A **family** lives together. A **neighbour** lives nearby. A **friend** plays with you. An **elder** guides you. A **visitor** comes to see you. We **greet** and show **respect** to all. Keywords: family: people who live together and love each other; neighbour: person who lives near your home; friend: person you like to play with; elder: older person who guides us; visitor: person who comes to see you; greet: say hello in a kind way; respect: show care by words and actions
chunks.source: A **family** lives together. A **neighbour** lives nearby. A **friend** plays with you. An **elder** guides you. A **visitor** comes to see you. We **greet** and show **respect** to all.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who lives in your **family**? A: Mother, father, brothers, sisters, grandparents.
chunks.source: Mother, father, brothers, sisters, grandparents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you say when you **greet** a **neighbour**? A: Good morning or good afternoon.
chunks.source: Good morning or good afternoon.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one **elder** you **respect**. A: Grandmother, grandfather, teacher, uncle.
chunks.source: Grandmother, grandfather, teacher, uncle.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a **visitor**? A: A person who comes to see you.
chunks.source: A person who comes to see you.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do you show **respect** to a **friend**? A: Share, listen, say sorry.
chunks.source: Share, listen, say sorry.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Working Together in Our Community. I can name ways we work together to keep our place clean. **Communal work** is work we do together. We **share** tasks. We **help** each other. We **sweep**, **slash**, **dig**, and **clean** to keep our community tidy and safe. Keywords: communal work: work we do together as a group; share: give part of what you have to others; help: do something for someone else; sweep: clean the ground with a broom; slash: cut tall grass with a slasher; dig: turn soil with a hoe; clean: make something free from dirt
chunks.source: **Communal work** is work we do together. We **share** tasks. We **help** each other. We **sweep**, **slash**, **dig**, and **clean** to keep our community tidy and safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **communal work**? A: Work we do together as a group.
chunks.source: Work we do together as a group.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one tool for **sweep**. A: Broom.
chunks.source: Broom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do men use to **slash** grass? A: Slasher or panga.
chunks.source: Slasher or panga.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do you **help** at home? A: Sweep, fetch water, wash plates.
chunks.source: Sweep, fetch water, wash plates.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we **clean** the latrine? A: To stop diseases.
chunks.source: To stop diseases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Rules for Living Together. I can follow rules that bring peace at home and school. **Rules** guide us. We **respect**, **share**, **listen**, say **sorry**, and **forgive**. These bring **peace** to our **family**, school, and community. Keywords: rules: guides that tell us what to do; respect: treat others with care; share: let others use what you have; listen: hear and think about what is said; sorry: word we say when we make a mistake; forgive: let go of anger when someone says sorry; peace: calm and happy living together
chunks.source: **Rules** guide us. We **respect**, **share**, **listen**, say **sorry**, and **forgive**. These bring **peace** to our **family**, school, and community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one school **rule**. A: **Respect**, **share**, or **listen**.
chunks.source: **Respect**, **share**, or **listen**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you say when you hurt a **friend**? A: **Sorry**.
chunks.source: **Sorry**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **forgive** mean? A: Let go of anger.
chunks.source: Let go of anger.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do you **listen** to the teacher? A: Eyes on teacher, mouth closed.
chunks.source: Eyes on teacher, mouth closed.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **peace** feel like? A: Calm and happy.
chunks.source: Calm and happy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Where Our Food Comes From. I can name places where food comes from. Food comes from the garden, farm, market, shop, and lake. Farmers grow crops on the farm. Keywords: garden: place where crops grow; farm: big land for crops; market: place to buy food; shop: small place to buy; lake: big water with fish; farmer: person who grows food; grow: to make plants bigger
chunks.source: Food comes from the garden, farm, market, shop, and lake. Farmers grow crops on the farm.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where does maize grow? A: In the garden.
chunks.source: In the garden.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who grows food on the farm? A: The farmer.
chunks.source: The farmer.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do we buy sugar? A: At the shop.
chunks.source: At the shop.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do fish come from? A: From the lake.
chunks.source: From the lake.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one place food comes from. A: Garden, farm, market, shop, or lake.
chunks.source: Garden, farm, market, shop, or lake.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Foods Grown in Uganda. I can name foods grown in Uganda. Uganda grows matooke, posho, beans, groundnuts, sweet potatoes, millet, and cassava. These foods keep us healthy. Keywords: matooke: steamed green banana; posho: maize flour meal; beans: small seeds we cook; groundnuts: nuts that grow underground; sweet potatoes: sweet root vegetable; millet: small grain for porridge; cassava: root crop for flour
chunks.source: Uganda grows matooke, posho, beans, groundnuts, sweet potatoes, millet, and cassava. These foods keep us healthy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is matooke? A: Steamed banana.
chunks.source: Steamed banana.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is posho made from? A: Maize flour.
chunks.source: Maize flour.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name a food from the farm. A: Sweet potatoes, cassava, millet, beans, or groundnuts.
chunks.source: Sweet potatoes, cassava, millet, beans, or groundnuts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which food makes porridge? A: Millet.
chunks.source: Millet.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we boil for breakfast? A: Sweet potatoes.
chunks.source: Sweet potatoes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Good Food Keeps Us Strong. I can name meals and healthy foods. We eat breakfast, lunch, and supper every day. Fruit, vegetable, milk, and egg make us strong. Keywords: breakfast: first meal in morning; lunch: meal at midday; supper: meal in evening; fruit: sweet food from trees; vegetable: plant food like greens; milk: white drink from cows; egg: oval food from chicken
chunks.source: We eat breakfast, lunch, and supper every day. Fruit, vegetable, milk, and egg make us strong.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What meal do we eat in the morning? A: Breakfast.
chunks.source: Breakfast.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What meal do we eat at midday? A: Lunch.
chunks.source: Lunch.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What meal do we eat in the evening? A: Supper.
chunks.source: Supper.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name a fruit. A: Mango, banana, or orange.
chunks.source: Mango, banana, or orange.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What makes bones strong? A: Milk.
chunks.source: Milk.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Ways We Travel on Land. I can name ways we travel on land. We travel on land by bus, car, bicycle, motorcycle, boda boda, train, or walk. Keywords: bus: big vehicle for many people; car: small vehicle for a few people; bicycle: two wheels you pedal; motorcycle: two wheels with engine; boda boda: motorcycle taxi; train: long vehicle on rails; walk: move on foot
chunks.source: We travel on land by bus, car, bicycle, motorcycle, boda boda, train, or walk.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we call a motorcycle taxi in Uganda? A: boda boda
chunks.source: boda boda

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which vehicle has two wheels and pedals? A: bicycle
chunks.source: bicycle

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What goes on rails and says choo choo? A: train
chunks.source: train

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you do with your feet to move? A: walk
chunks.source: walk

chunks.id: L-P1-Social-Travel on Water and in the Air
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travel on Water and in the Air
chunks.text: Travel on Water and in the Air. I can name ways we travel on water and in air. We travel on water by boat, canoe, ship, ferry. We travel in air by aeroplane, helicopter. Lake Victoria is our big lake. Keywords: boat: small vessel for water; canoe: narrow boat paddled by hand; ship: very big boat for ocean; ferry: boat that carries vehicles; aeroplane: flying machine with wings; helicopter: flying machine with rotor; lake: large water surrounded by land
chunks.source: We travel on water by boat, canoe, ship, ferry. We travel in air by aeroplane, helicopter. Lake Victoria is our big lake.

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-Travel on Water and in the Air
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travel on Water and in the Air
chunks.text: Q: What do you call a big boat that carries cars? A: ferry
chunks.source: ferry

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-Travel on Water and in the Air
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travel on Water and in the Air
chunks.text: Q: Which small boat do you paddle? A: canoe
chunks.source: canoe

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-Travel on Water and in the Air
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travel on Water and in the Air
chunks.text: Q: What flies high and has wings? A: aeroplane
chunks.source: aeroplane

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-Travel on Water and in the Air
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travel on Water and in the Air
chunks.text: Q: Where does a boat float? A: lake
chunks.source: lake

chunks.id: LQ-P1-Social-Travel on Water and in the Air
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travel on Water and in the Air
chunks.text: Q: What goes choo choo on water? A: ship
chunks.source: ship

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: People Who Help Us Travel. I can name people who help us travel. A **driver** drives, a **conductor** helps passengers, a **pilot** flies, a **captain** steers a ship. Wear a **helmet** when you **travel** on a motorcycle. Keywords: driver: person who drives vehicle; passenger: person riding in vehicle; conductor: person who collects fares; pilot: person who flies aeroplane; captain: person who steers ship; helmet: hard hat for head safety; travel: go from one place to another
chunks.source: A **driver** drives, a **conductor** helps passengers, a **pilot** flies, a **captain** steers a ship. Wear a **helmet** when you **travel** on a motorcycle.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who drives the bus? A: driver
chunks.source: driver

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who collects money on the bus? A: conductor
chunks.source: conductor

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who flies the aeroplane? A: pilot
chunks.source: pilot

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who steers the ship? A: captain
chunks.source: captain

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you wear on a motorcycle? A: helmet
chunks.source: helmet

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Things Made in Our Homes. I can name things made at home. At home we make pots, baskets, mats, brooms, ropes, necklaces, and use clay. Keywords: pot: a round container for cooking; basket: a woven container; mat: a flat piece for sitting; broom: a tool for sweeping; rope: strong cord for tying; necklace: jewellery for the neck; clay: soft earth for shaping
chunks.source: At home we make pots, baskets, mats, brooms, ropes, necklaces, and use clay.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a **pot** used for? A: cooking
chunks.source: cooking

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which item is woven? A: basket
chunks.source: basket

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name a tool for sweeping. A: broom
chunks.source: broom

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you tie with? A: rope
chunks.source: rope

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Things Made at School. I can name things made at school. At school we use paper, dolls, balls, toys, hats, bags, and sticks for craft. Keywords: paper: thin sheet for writing; doll: a small toy person; ball: round object for games; toy: something to play with; hat: head covering; bag: container for carrying; sticks: thin pieces of wood
chunks.source: At school we use paper, dolls, balls, toys, hats, bags, and sticks for craft.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you fold to make a doll? A: paper
chunks.source: paper

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which toy is round? A: ball
chunks.source: ball

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you wear on your head? A: hat
chunks.source: hat

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you carry your books in? A: bag
chunks.source: bag

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: People Who Make Things. I can name people who make things. Potters, weavers, carpenters, tailors, builders, artists all use craft to make things. Keywords: potter: person who shapes clay; weaver: person who weaves mats; carpenter: person who works with wood; tailor: person who sews clothes; builder: person who builds houses; artist: person who creates art; craft: skill of making things
chunks.source: Potters, weavers, carpenters, tailors, builders, artists all use craft to make things.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who shapes clay into pots? A: potter
chunks.source: potter

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who weaves mats and baskets? A: weaver
chunks.source: weaver

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who makes wooden tables? A: carpenter
chunks.source: carpenter

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who sews clothes? A: tailor
chunks.source: tailor

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Features Around Our Home. I can name features around my home. Amina and Kato walk around their home and see a tree, hill, river, lake, road, garden, and compound. They learn the names of these features. Keywords: tree: a tall plant with a trunk; hill: high land that goes up; river: water that flows on land; lake: big water with land around; road: path for walking and cars; garden: place where crops grow; compound: area around the house
chunks.source: Amina and Kato walk around their home and see a tree, hill, river, lake, road, garden, and compound. They learn the names of these features.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What tall plant gives shade? A: tree
chunks.source: tree

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What high land is far away? A: hill
chunks.source: hill

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What water flows near the hill? A: river
chunks.source: river

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What big water has blue colour? A: lake
chunks.source: lake

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What path goes to the market? A: road
chunks.source: road

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Animals in Our Environment. I can name animals in my environment. Amina and Kato visit a farm and see a goat, cow, hen, sheep, dog, bird, and fish. They learn the names of these animals. Keywords: goat: animal with horns that eats grass; cow: big animal that gives milk; hen: bird that lays eggs; sheep: animal with wool; dog: animal that barks and guards; bird: animal with feathers and wings; fish: animal that lives in water
chunks.source: Amina and Kato visit a farm and see a goat, cow, hen, sheep, dog, bird, and fish. They learn the names of these animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What animal says meh? A: goat
chunks.source: goat

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What big animal gives milk? A: cow
chunks.source: cow

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What bird lays eggs? A: hen
chunks.source: hen

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What animal has wool? A: sheep
chunks.source: sheep

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What animal lives in water? A: fish
chunks.source: fish

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Caring for Our Surroundings. I can care for my surroundings.
