Amina and Kato learn to pick rubbish, use a bin, sweep, plant trees, water plants, protect trees, and keep the compound clean. Keywords: rubbish: waste like paper and plastic; bin: container for rubbish; sweep: clean with a broom; plant: put a seed or tree in soil; water: give water to plants; protect: keep safe from harm; clean: free from dirt
chunks.source: Amina and Kato learn to pick rubbish, use a bin, sweep, plant trees, water plants, protect trees, and keep the compound clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where does rubbish go? A: bin
chunks.source: bin

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you do with a broom? A: sweep
chunks.source: sweep

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you give to a thirsty plant? A: water
chunks.source: water

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we do to keep trees safe? A: protect
chunks.source: protect

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you do with a seed in the ground? A: plant
chunks.source: plant

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: People Who Keep Us Safe. I can name people who keep us safe. The **police officer**, **askari**, **soldier**, **guard**, **elder**, **parent**, and **teacher** keep us safe. Keywords: police officer: a person who keeps law; askari: a guard in Uganda; soldier: a person in the army; guard: a person who watches a place; elder: an older respected person; parent: mother or father; teacher: a person who teaches
chunks.source: The **police officer**, **askari**, **soldier**, **guard**, **elder**, **parent**, and **teacher** keep us safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who waves at the market? A: The police officer.
chunks.source: The police officer.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who checks the gate? A: The askari.
chunks.source: The askari.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who watches the school gate? A: The guard.
chunks.source: The guard.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who tells a story under the tree? A: The elder.
chunks.source: The elder.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who waves from home? A: The parent.
chunks.source: The parent.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Keeping Safe from Harm. I can name things that keep us safe. The **lock**, **gate**, **fence**, **thief**, **stranger**, **report**, and **safe** keep us safe. Keywords: lock: a device to close a door; gate: an entrance that opens and closes; fence: a barrier around a place; thief: a person who steals; stranger: a person you do not know; report: to tell an adult about danger; safe: free from danger
chunks.source: The **lock**, **gate**, **fence**, **thief**, **stranger**, **report**, and **safe** keep us safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you use to close a gate? A: A lock.
chunks.source: A lock.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What stands around a home? A: A fence.
chunks.source: A fence.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who do you tell if you see a thief? A: An adult.
chunks.source: An adult.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you call a person you do not know? A: A stranger.
chunks.source: A stranger.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do you feel when the gate is locked? A: Safe.
chunks.source: Safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Living Peacefully with Others. I can name ways to live in peace. With **peace**, **share**, **forgive**, **respect**, **listen**, **friend**, and **harmony** we live happily. Keywords: peace: calm and quiet; share: to give part of something; forgive: to stop being angry; respect: to treat kindly; listen: to hear carefully; friend: a person you like; harmony: living together happily
chunks.source: With **peace**, **share**, **forgive**, **respect**, **listen**, **friend**, and **harmony** we live happily.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What grows when we are kind? A: Peace.
chunks.source: Peace.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you do with a ball? A: Share.
chunks.source: Share.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you do when a friend hurts you? A: Forgive.
chunks.source: Forgive.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do you treat others kindly? A: Respect.
chunks.source: Respect.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you call a person you like? A: Friend.
chunks.source: Friend.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: My School. I can introduce myself and name places in my school. Amina visits the **classroom**, **library**, **office**, **playground**, and meets a **pupil** with many **books**. Keywords: classroom: room where pupils learn; library: room with many books; office: room where teachers work; playground: open area for play; pupil: child who goes to school; books: pages with stories
chunks.source: Amina visits the **classroom**, **library**, **office**, **playground**, and meets a **pupil** with many **books**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is Amina's name? A: Amina.
chunks.source: Amina.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where does Amina read books? A: In the library.
chunks.source: In the library.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why does Amina go to the library? A: To read books.
chunks.source: To read books.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two places in the school. A: Classroom and playground.
chunks.source: Classroom and playground.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Teacher Nankya say? A: My name is Teacher Nankya.
chunks.source: My name is Teacher Nankya.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: People at School. I can name people at school and what they wear. Amina wears a **uniform** and **badge**, meets a **teacher**, a **friend**, and a **pupil**. Keywords: pupil: child who goes to school; uniform: special clothes for school; badge: small sign on uniform; teacher: person who teaches; friend: person you like
chunks.source: Amina wears a **uniform** and **badge**, meets a **teacher**, a **friend**, and a **pupil**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina wear? A: Uniform and badge.
chunks.source: Uniform and badge.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who teaches Amina? A: Teacher.
chunks.source: Teacher.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why does the teacher wear a uniform? A: To show she is a teacher.
chunks.source: To show she is a teacher.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name Amina's friend. A: Friend.
chunks.source: Friend.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does the pupil do? A: Reads.
chunks.source: Reads.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Around Our School. I can read a simple map and name features around my school. The **map** shows the **road**, **path**, **tree**, **fence**, **symbol**, and **water**. Keywords: map: drawing of places; road: wide way for cars; path: narrow way for walking; tree: big plant with leaves; fence: wall around school; symbol: sign that means something; water: liquid we drink
chunks.source: The **map** shows the **road**, **path**, **tree**, **fence**, **symbol**, and **water**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does the map show? A: Road, path, tree, fence, symbol, water.
chunks.source: Road, path, tree, fence, symbol, water.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where does Amina walk first? A: Road or path.
chunks.source: Road or path.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is the symbol near the water? A: To mark the water place.
chunks.source: To mark the water place.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name three things on the map. A: Road, tree, fence.
chunks.source: Road, tree, fence.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina draw? A: The map.
chunks.source: The map.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: My Home and Family. I can name people in my family and say where we live. Amina's home has a house, mother, father, sister, and brother. They work and eat together. Keywords: home: the place where you live with your family; house: the building where a family lives; mother: the woman who cares for you; father: the man who cares for you; sister: a girl with the same parents; brother: a boy with the same parents
chunks.source: Amina's home has a house, mother, father, sister, and brother. They work and eat together.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who cooks food in Amina's home? A: Mother cooks food.
chunks.source: Mother cooks food.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where does Father work? A: Father works in the garden.
chunks.source: Father works in the garden.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Sister carry? A: Sister carries a jerrycan of water.
chunks.source: Sister carries a jerrycan of water.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is the home happy? A: The family works and eats together.
chunks.source: The family works and eats together.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two people in Amina's family. A: Mother and Father (or Sister and Brother).
chunks.source: Mother and Father (or Sister and Brother).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Draw your home. Label mother, father, sister, brother. A: Child draws and labels.
chunks.source: Child draws and labels.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: People Who Help Us. I can name people who help in our community. The doctor, nurse, farmer, police, shop, and market all help our community every day. Keywords: doctor: a person who treats sick people; nurse: a person who helps the doctor; farmer: a person who grows food; police: people who keep us safe; shop: a place to buy things; market: a big place with many sellers
chunks.source: The doctor, nurse, farmer, police, shop, and market all help our community every day.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where does the farmer sell maize? A: At the market.
chunks.source: At the market.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who helps sick people at the clinic? A: The doctor and nurse help.
chunks.source: The doctor and nurse help.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does the police officer do? A: The police officer directs traffic.
chunks.source: The police officer directs traffic.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need a shop? A: To buy things like sugar and soap.
chunks.source: To buy things like sugar and soap.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two helpers at the market. A: Farmer and shopkeeper.
chunks.source: Farmer and shopkeeper.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Draw a helper you like. Write their name. A: Child draws and labels.
chunks.source: Child draws and labels.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Good Behaviour at Home. I can show love, respect, and kindness at home. Love, respect, help, share, greet, and kind make our home happy. Amina shows all six every day. Keywords: love: to care deeply for someone; respect: to listen and obey elders; help: to do something for someone; share: to give part of what you have; greet: to say hello politely; kind: friendly and caring
chunks.source: Love, respect, help, share, greet, and kind make our home happy. Amina shows all six every day.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina do when she sees Mother sweeping? A: She helps.
chunks.source: She helps.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How does Amina greet Father? A: She says, "Good evening, Daddy."
chunks.source: She says, "Good evening, Daddy."

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Kato share with his sister? A: He shares a mango.
chunks.source: He shares a mango.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is sharing kind? A: It shows you love the other person.
chunks.source: It shows you love the other person.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two good behaviours at home. A: Help and greet (or share and respect).
chunks.source: Help and greet (or share and respect).

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Tell one kind thing you did this week. A: Child tells an example.
chunks.source: Child tells an example.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Parts of My Body. I can name the main parts of my body. Amina learns the names of her head, eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and hands. Keywords: head: the top part of the body; eyes: the parts we see with; ears: the parts we hear with; nose: the part we smell with; mouth: the part we eat and talk with; hands: the parts at the end of arms
chunks.source: Amina learns the names of her head, eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and hands.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name the part you use to see. A: eyes
chunks.source: eyes

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name the part you use to smell. A: nose
chunks.source: nose

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need a mouth? A: We use the mouth to eat and talk.
chunks.source: We use the mouth to eat and talk.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Point to your head. A: Head is on top of the neck.
chunks.source: Head is on top of the neck.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you do with your hands? A: We hold, write, and clap with hands.
chunks.source: We hold, write, and clap with hands.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which part helps you hear? A: ears
chunks.source: ears

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: I Use My Body. I can say how I use different body parts. Kato uses his fingers, legs, toes, arms, knees, and shoulders to move and play. Keywords: fingers: the small parts on the hand; legs: the long parts we walk on; toes: the small parts at the end of the foot; arms: the long parts from shoulder to hand; knees: the joints in the middle of the leg; shoulders: the parts where arms meet the body
chunks.source: Kato uses his fingers, legs, toes, arms, knees, and shoulders to move and play.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you use to hold a pen? A: fingers
chunks.source: fingers

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which part helps you walk? A: legs
chunks.source: legs

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do knees bend? A: Knees bend so we can sit and run.
chunks.source: Knees bend so we can sit and run.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name the part at the end of your foot. A: toes
chunks.source: toes

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you raise to wave? A: arms
chunks.source: arms

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where are your shoulders? A: Shoulders are between neck and arms.
chunks.source: Shoulders are between neck and arms.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Keeping Clean. I can name things that keep me clean. Nalongo uses soap, brush, comb, towel, bath, wash, and teeth to stay clean. Keywords: soap: a substance for washing; brush: a tool for cleaning hair or teeth; comb: a tool with teeth for hair; towel: a cloth for drying; bath: a wash of the whole body; wash: to clean with water; teeth: the hard parts in the mouth
chunks.source: Nalongo uses soap, brush, comb, towel, bath, wash, and teeth to stay clean.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you use to clean your hands? A: soap
chunks.source: soap

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you use to brush your hair? A: brush
chunks.source: brush

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do we wash our teeth? A: We wash teeth to keep them healthy.
chunks.source: We wash teeth to keep them healthy.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What dries you after a bath? A: towel
chunks.source: towel

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you use to comb your hair? A: comb
chunks.source: comb

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you do in a bath? A: wash
chunks.source: wash

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Foods We Eat. I can name common Ugandan foods. Amina learns about fruit like banana and orange, and foods like maize, rice, and beans at the market. She eats them at home with her family. Keywords: banana: a long yellow fruit; orange: a round orange fruit; fruit: food from plants like banana; maize: a yellow grain for posho; rice: white grains we cook; beans: small seeds we cook
chunks.source: Amina learns about fruit like banana and orange, and foods like maize, rice, and beans at the market. She eats them at home with her family.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name three fruit Amina saw at the market. A: Banana, orange, and mango.
chunks.source: Banana, orange, and mango.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What did Mother buy at the market? A: Mother bought banana, orange, maize, rice, and beans.
chunks.source: Mother bought banana, orange, maize, rice, and beans.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is banana a fruit? A: Because it grows on a plant and has seeds.
chunks.source: Because it grows on a plant and has seeds.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What did Amina eat for dinner? A: Amina ate rice with beans and orange for dessert.
chunks.source: Amina ate rice with beans and orange for dessert.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which food is a grain: maize or banana? A: Maize is a grain.
chunks.source: Maize is a grain.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Meals of the Day. I can name the three main meals and what we eat at each. Amina has breakfast with porridge, lunch at school with beans, and dinner with family. She drinks and eats at each meal. Keywords: breakfast: morning meal; lunch: midday meal; dinner: evening meal; porridge: thin hot cereal; drink: take liquid in mouth; eat: put food in mouth
chunks.source: Amina has breakfast with porridge, lunch at school with beans, and dinner with family. She drinks and eats at each meal.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What are the three meals of the day? A: Breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
chunks.source: Breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina drink at breakfast? A: She drinks porridge or tea.
chunks.source: She drinks porridge or tea.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do we eat lunch at midday? A: Because we need energy for the afternoon.
chunks.source: Because we need energy for the afternoon.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What did Amina eat at dinner? A: She ate rice and fish stew.
chunks.source: She ate rice and fish stew.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name a food for breakfast. A: Porridge or banana.
chunks.source: Porridge or banana.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Food Makes Us Strong. I can say how different foods help my body. Teacher Nankya teaches that meat makes us strong, cabbage and vegetable give vitamins, and healthy food helps us grow. Keywords: meat: animal flesh we eat; cabbage: green leafy vegetable; vegetable: plant food like cabbage; grow: get bigger; healthy: not sick, well; strong: has power
chunks.source: Teacher Nankya teaches that meat makes us strong, cabbage and vegetable give vitamins, and healthy food helps us grow.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two vegetable from the lesson. A: Cabbage and tomato.
chunks.source: Cabbage and tomato.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What food makes muscles strong? A: Meat makes muscles strong.
chunks.source: Meat makes muscles strong.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need healthy food? A: To grow well and be strong.
chunks.source: To grow well and be strong.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What did Mother cook with cabbage? A: Mother cooked meat stew with cabbage.
chunks.source: Mother cooked meat stew with cabbage.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina want to do? A: She wants to grow tall.
chunks.source: She wants to grow tall.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Things Around Us. I can name things around me. Amina learns to name things around her like tree, bird, grass, flower, leaf, and soil. Keywords: tree: a tall plant; grass: green ground cover; flower: a colorful plant part; leaf: a flat green part of a plant; soil: the earth where plants grow; bird: a small flying animal
chunks.source: Amina learns to name things around her like tree, bird, grass, flower, leaf, and soil.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the green ground cover called? A: grass
chunks.source: grass

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name a thing Amina sees that flies. A: bird
chunks.source: bird

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word means the top layer of earth? A: soil
chunks.source: soil

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why does Amina feel proud? A: She can name many things around her.
chunks.source: She can name many things around her.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: This is a ___. A: tree
chunks.source: tree

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: I can see a ___. A: bird
chunks.source: bird

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Animals in Our Environment. I can name animals in my environment. Kato learns to name bee, hen, sheep, mosquito, fly, and butterfly in the garden. Keywords: bee: an insect that makes honey; hen: a bird that lays eggs; sheep: an animal that gives wool; mosquito: a small biting insect; fly: a common flying insect; butterfly: a colorful flying insect
chunks.source: Kato learns to name bee, hen, sheep, mosquito, fly, and butterfly in the garden.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which animal makes honey? A: bee
chunks.source: bee

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name the bird that clucks. A: hen
chunks.source: hen

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which animal gives wool? A: sheep
chunks.source: sheep

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What small insect bites at night? A: mosquito
chunks.source: mosquito

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why does Kato feel happy? A: He learns the names of many animals.
chunks.source: He learns the names of many animals.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: This is a ___. A: bee
chunks.source: bee

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: We Care for Our Environment. I can describe ways to care for my environment. Nalongo and Peter plant, water, clean, sweep, and care for a tree to keep their school clean. Keywords: plant: put a seed in soil to grow; water: give liquid to a plant; clean: remove dirt and rubbish; rubbish: waste that is thrown away; sweep: use a broom to clear dust; tree: a tall woody plant
chunks.source: Nalongo and Peter plant, water, clean, sweep, and care for a tree to keep their school clean.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do we do to make a new tree grow? A: plant
chunks.source: plant

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do we give a tree to help it grow? A: water
chunks.source: water

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which action means picking up rubbish? A: clean
chunks.source: clean

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do we use a broom for? A: sweep
chunks.source: sweep

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do we care for the tree? A: It gives shade and clean air.
chunks.source: It gives shade and clean air.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: We will ___ the yard. A: clean
chunks.source: clean

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Things We Make at School. I can name things we make at school and the materials we use. Amina and Kato make a bead necklace, a mat, a basket, a rope, and a clay pot at school with Teacher Nankya. Keywords: bead: a small round piece with a hole for threading; mat: a flat piece for covering the floor; basket: a container made of woven strips; rope: thick strong string for tying; clay: wet earth used for shaping; pot: a round container for cooking or storing
chunks.source: Amina and Kato make a bead necklace, a mat, a basket, a rope, and a clay pot at school with Teacher Nankya.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Kato make with rope? A: A mat
chunks.source: A mat

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What material is the pot made of? A: Clay
chunks.source: Clay

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where does the bead necklace go at the end? A: On the shelf
chunks.source: On the shelf

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why does Kato use rope for the mat? A: Because rope is strong for weaving.
chunks.source: Because rope is strong for weaving.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two things Amina and Kato make. A: Bead necklace and mat (or basket, pot, rope)
chunks.source: Bead necklace and mat (or basket, pot, rope)

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does the clay pot hold? A: Water
chunks.source: Water

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Materials We Use. I can name materials we use for making things and say what they make. Amina, Kato, and Peter collect sisal, clay, stick, paper, and string for craft class. Each material is used to make different things. Keywords: sisal: a plant with long leaves for making rope; material: something used to make an object; clay: wet earth used for shaping; stick: a thin piece of wood; paper: thin sheets for writing or folding; string: thin rope for tying
chunks.source: Amina, Kato, and Peter collect sisal, clay, stick, paper, and string for craft class. Each material is used to make different things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What material makes strong rope? A: Sisal
chunks.source: Sisal

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where do they find clay? A: Near the termite mound
chunks.source: Near the termite mound

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Peter use the stick for? A: A kite frame
chunks.source: A kite frame

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is sisal good for rope? A: Because sisal is tough and strong.
chunks.source: Because sisal is tough and strong.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name three materials they collect. A: Sisal, clay, stick (or paper, string)
chunks.source: Sisal, clay, stick (or paper, string)

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What material does Amina use for beads? A: Paper
chunks.source: Paper

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: We Make Toys. I can name toys we make and say how we play with them. Amina, Kato, and Peter make a ball, a doll, a kite, a drum, and a toy car. They play with them under the mango tree. Keywords: ball: a round object for throwing or kicking; doll: a toy shaped like a person; kite: a light frame with paper that flies in wind; drum: a hollow instrument beaten with hands; toy car: a small vehicle pushed by hand; play: to do something for fun
chunks.source: Amina, Kato, and Peter make a ball, a doll, a kite, a drum, and a toy car. They play with them under the mango tree.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Peter make in the story? A: A kite or a drum
chunks.source: A kite or a drum

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina make? A: A doll
chunks.source: A doll

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Kato make? A: A toy car
chunks.source: A toy car

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why does the kite fly? A: Because the wind blows.
chunks.source: Because the wind blows.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two toys they play with. A: Ball and drum (or kite, doll, toy car)
chunks.source: Ball and drum (or kite, doll, toy car)

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where do they put the toys at the end? A: In a box
chunks.source: In a box

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Ways We Travel. I can name different ways we travel in Uganda. We **travel** on the **road** using a **bus**, **taxi**, **bicycle**, or **boat**. Keywords: bus: a large vehicle that carries many people; taxi: a small car that carries a few passengers; bicycle: a two‑wheel vehicle you pedal; boat: a vessel that moves on water; road: a path for vehicles and people; travel: to go from one place to another
chunks.source: We **travel** on the **road** using a **bus**, **taxi**, **bicycle**, or **boat**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name a vehicle that moves on the **road**. A: **bus**
chunks.source: **bus**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you call a two‑wheel vehicle you pedal? A: **bicycle**
chunks.source: **bicycle**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which vehicle moves on water? A: **boat**
chunks.source: **boat**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What word means to go from one place to another? A: **travel**
chunks.source: **travel**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a small car that carries a few passengers? A: **taxi**
chunks.source: **taxi**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: People Who Help Us Travel. I can identify the people who help us travel safely. The **driver**, **conductor**, and **passenger** help us **travel** safely with a **ticket**, **helmet**, and **seat**. Keywords: driver: the person who drives the vehicle; passenger: a person who rides in a vehicle; conductor: the person who checks tickets on a bus; helmet: a hard hat that protects the head; seat: a place to sit in a vehicle; ticket: a paper that shows you paid for the ride
chunks.source: The **driver**, **conductor**, and **passenger** help us **travel** safely with a **ticket**, **helmet**, and **seat**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who drives the **bus**? A: **driver**
chunks.source: **driver**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you call a person riding in the **bus**? A: **passenger**
chunks.source: **passenger**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who checks the **ticket** on the **bus**? A: **conductor**
chunks.source: **conductor**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What protects your head when you ride a **bicycle**? A: **helmet**
chunks.source: **helmet**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you sit on in a vehicle? A: **seat**
chunks.source: **seat**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Safety on the Road. I can explain how to cross the road safely. At a **zebra crossing** on the **road**, **look** **left**, then **right**, then **cross** safely. Keywords: zebra crossing: a marked place for pedestrians to cross; road: a path for vehicles and people; look: to use your eyes to see; cross: to go from one side of the road to the other; left: the side opposite to right; right: the side opposite to left
chunks.source: At a **zebra crossing** on the **road**, **look** **left**, then **right**, then **cross** safely.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the marked place to cross called? A: **zebra crossing**
chunks.source: **zebra crossing**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What must you do before you **cross** the **road**? A: **look** left and right
chunks.source: **look** left and right

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which side do you **look** first in Uganda? A: **left**
chunks.source: **left**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the opposite of **left**? A: **right**
chunks.source: **right**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What word means to go from one side of the **road** to the other? A: **cross**
chunks.source: **cross**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Things That Can Hurt Us. I can name things that can hurt me. Knives, fire, poison, and hot things can hurt us; we must stay away and tell an adult. Keywords: knife: a sharp tool for cutting; fire: flames that give heat; poison: a substance that makes you sick; burn: an injury from heat; sharp: having a thin edge that cuts; hot: very warm, can burn
chunks.source: Knives, fire, poison, and hot things can hurt us; we must stay away and tell an adult.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a **knife** used for? A: A knife is used for cutting.
chunks.source: A knife is used for cutting.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is **fire** dangerous? A: Fire is hot and can burn you.
chunks.source: Fire is hot and can burn you.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What should you do if you see **poison**? A: Tell an adult and do not touch it.
chunks.source: Tell an adult and do not touch it.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How do you treat a **burn**? A: Cool it with water and get help.
chunks.source: Cool it with water and get help.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why must we stay away from **sharp** things? A: Sharp things can cut you.
chunks.source: Sharp things can cut you.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: When We Get Hurt. I can explain what to do when someone gets hurt. When we get a cut or fall, we clean it, use a bandage, take medicine, and see a nurse or doctor. Keywords: cut: a wound from a sharp thing; fall: to drop down suddenly; bandage: a cloth to cover a wound; medicine: a substance to treat illness; doctor: a person who treats sick people; nurse: a person who helps the doctor
chunks.source: When we get a cut or fall, we clean it, use a bandage, take medicine, and see a nurse or doctor.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does a **bandage** do? A: A bandage covers a cut.
chunks.source: A bandage covers a cut.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need **medicine** after a cut? A: Medicine helps heal the cut.
chunks.source: Medicine helps heal the cut.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who can help a **cut** at school? A: The nurse can help.
chunks.source: The nurse can help.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What should you do after a **fall**? A: Tell an adult and get checked.
chunks.source: Tell an adult and get checked.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is it important to see a **doctor**? A: A doctor can give the right medicine.
chunks.source: A doctor can give the right medicine.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Keeping Safe. I can describe how to stay safe in daily life. Being careful, following safety rules, and asking an adult for help keeps us safe from danger. Keywords: safety: being free from danger; careful: paying attention to avoid harm; danger: something that can cause harm; safe: free from harm; help: assistance from someone; adult: a grown‑up person
chunks.source: Being careful, following safety rules, and asking an adult for help keeps us safe from danger.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **safety** mean? A: Safety means being free from danger.
chunks.source: Safety means being free from danger.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why must we be **careful** near the road? A: Because traffic can cause danger.
chunks.source: Because traffic can cause danger.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What should you do if you see **danger**? A: Tell an adult and get help.
chunks.source: Tell an adult and get help.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who can give **help** when you are unsafe? A: An adult can give help.
chunks.source: An adult can give help.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is it good to feel **safe**? A: Feeling safe lets you learn and play.
chunks.source: Feeling safe lets you learn and play.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Living in Peace. I can explain how peace grows when friends share, forgive, and say sorry. Amina and Kato show peace by sharing, forgiving, and saying sorry. Teacher Nankya sees their peace and smiles. Keywords: peace: calm and friendship; friend: a person you like; share: give part of something; forgive: stop being angry; sorry: word for regret; happy: feeling good
chunks.source: Amina and Kato show peace by sharing, forgiving, and saying sorry. Teacher Nankya sees their peace and smiles.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina want with Kato? A: She wants peace.
chunks.source: She wants peace.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina do in the garden? A: She picks matooke.
chunks.source: She picks matooke.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina say when she hurts Kato? A: She says sorry.
chunks.source: She says sorry.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do Kato and Amina feel happy at the end? A: Because they forgive and share.
chunks.source: Because they forgive and share.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Teacher Nankya see? A: She sees their peace.
chunks.source: She sees their peace.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: People Who Keep Us Safe. I can name people who keep us safe and say how they protect us. Police, soldiers, and guards give us security, safety, and protect us. Keywords: police: officers who keep order; soldier: person who defends the country; guard: person who watches a place; security: being safe from danger; safety: freedom from harm; protect: keep safe from harm
chunks.source: Police, soldiers, and guards give us security, safety, and protect us.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who directs traffic at the trading centre? A: A police officer.
chunks.source: A police officer.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does the soldier do at the market? A: He guards the market gate.
chunks.source: He guards the market gate.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does the guard check at the school gate? A: He checks bags.
chunks.source: He checks bags.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do the police and soldier work together? A: To protect the village.
chunks.source: To protect the village.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Teacher Nankya teach about? A: Security and safety.
chunks.source: Security and safety.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Keeping Safe from Thieves. I can describe how to stay safe from thieves by locking doors, reporting, and telling an adult. Lock your doors, report a thief, and tell a trusted adult to stay safe. Keywords: thief: person who steals; steal: take something not yours; lock: fasten a door; report: tell authorities; safe: free from danger; tell: inform someone
chunks.source: Lock your doors, report a thief, and tell a trusted adult to stay safe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What did Amina and Kato see? A: A thief trying to steal a jerrycan.
chunks.source: A thief trying to steal a jerrycan.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where did they run to be safe? A: Inside the house or to the neighbour's house.
chunks.source: Inside the house or to the neighbour's house.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What did they do after seeing the thief? A: They told their mother.
chunks.source: They told their mother.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why should they report the thief to the police? A: So the police can keep the area safe.
chunks.source: So the police can keep the area safe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Teacher Nankya say to do? A: Lock doors and tell an adult.
chunks.source: Lock doors and tell an adult.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: My Rights as a Child. I can name my rights and say who must keep me safe. Every child has rights to care, protection, and love, and an adult must keep them safe. Keywords: rights: things every child must have; care: looking after someone; protection: keeping someone safe from harm; adult: a grown person; safe: free from danger; love: deep caring feeling
chunks.source: Every child has rights to care, protection, and love, and an adult must keep them safe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What are three rights every child has? A: Care, protection, and love.
chunks.source: Care, protection, and love.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who must keep a child safe? A: An adult.
chunks.source: An adult.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why does Amina feel safe after learning her rights? A: Because she knows an adult must give care, protection, and love.
chunks.source: Because she knows an adult must give care, protection, and love.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name one place Amina could go to learn about rights. A: School library or community centre.
chunks.source: School library or community centre.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the sentence: Every child has the right to ___. A: care, protection, and love.
chunks.source: care, protection, and love.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Keeping My Body Safe. I can keep my body safe and know who to tell. No one may harm or abuse a child; tell a trusted adult, never keep a bad secret, and ask for help to stay safe. Keywords: harm: hurt or damage; abuse: bad treatment that hurts; tell: say something to someone; secret: something kept hidden; help: support or aid; safe: free from danger
chunks.source: No one may harm or abuse a child; tell a trusted adult, never keep a bad secret, and ask for help to stay safe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What are two things that are never allowed? A: Harm and abuse.
chunks.source: Harm and abuse.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who should Amina tell if something bad happens? A: A trusted adult.
chunks.source: A trusted adult.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why must Amina not keep a bad secret? A: Because a bad secret can cause more harm.
chunks.source: Because a bad secret can cause more harm.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What can Amina ask for to stay safe? A: Help.
chunks.source: Help.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: My body is ___. A: safe.
chunks.source: safe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Lost and Found. I can help a lost child find a trusted adult. If a child is missing or lost, find a trusted adult, say the child's name, ask for help, and call the police if needed. Keywords: missing: not able to be found; lost: unable to find the way; adult: a grown person; name: what someone is called; help: support or aid; police: officers who keep order
chunks.source: If a child is missing or lost, find a trusted adult, say the child's name, ask for help, and call the police if needed.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What are the first two steps if a child is missing? A: Find a trusted adult and say the child's name.
chunks.source: Find a trusted adult and say the child's name.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who can you call for help besides an adult? A: The police.
chunks.source: The police.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why should you not run away from a lost child? A: Running away does not help the child.
chunks.source: Running away does not help the child.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What information must you give the adult? A: The child's name.
chunks.source: The child's name.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: A lost child needs ___. A: help.
chunks.source: help.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Measuring Length. I can measure length using a ruler and metre. We measure length with a ruler for short things and a metre stick for long things. Keywords: measure: find the size of something; length: how long something is; metre: a unit for measuring length; ruler: a tool to measure short lengths; long: having much length; short: having little length
chunks.source: We measure length with a ruler for short things and a metre stick for long things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What tool do you use for a **short** thing? A: A ruler.
chunks.source: A ruler.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What tool do you use for a **long** thing? A: A metre stick.
chunks.source: A metre stick.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The door is two ___ long. A: metres
chunks.source: metres

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: The eraser is five ___ long. A: centimetres
chunks.source: centimetres

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why use a metre stick for the room? A: The room is long. A ruler is too short.
chunks.source: The room is long. A ruler is too short.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Measuring Weight. I can compare weight using a balance and kilograms. Weight tells how heavy something is. We measure it in kilograms using a balance. Keywords: weight: how heavy something is; kilogram: a unit for measuring weight; heavy: has a lot of weight; light: has little weight; balance: a tool to compare weight; mass: amount of matter in an object
chunks.source: Weight tells how heavy something is. We measure it in kilograms using a balance.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What unit do we use for **weight**? A: Kilogram.
chunks.source: Kilogram.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What tool compares **weight**? A: A balance.
chunks.source: A balance.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: A stone is ___. A feather is ___. A: heavy, light
chunks.source: heavy, light

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: One kilogram of sugar has the same ___ as one kilogram of rice. A: mass
chunks.source: mass

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why does the balance tip? A: The heavy side goes down.
chunks.source: The heavy side goes down.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Time and Money. I can tell time to the hour and count Ugandan shillings. A clock tells time in hours and minutes. We use shillings for money in Uganda. Keywords: time: when things happen; clock: a tool that shows time; hour: sixty minutes; minute: sixty seconds; money: what we use to buy things; shilling: Uganda's money unit
chunks.source: A clock tells time in hours and minutes. We use shillings for money in Uganda.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What shows **time**? A: A clock.
chunks.source: A clock.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How many **minutes** in one **hour**? A: Sixty.
chunks.source: Sixty.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is Uganda's **money** called? A: Shilling.
chunks.source: Shilling.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: School starts at eight. The short hand points to ___. A: eight
chunks.source: eight

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need **money**? A: To buy things we need.
chunks.source: To buy things we need.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Games We Play. I can name games and actions we do for fun. **Games** like football and rope skipping are **recreation**. We **play**, **run**, **jump**, and kick a **ball** to stay healthy and happy. Keywords: games: activities we play for fun; recreation: fun time after work or school; play: to do something for fun; ball: a round object for games; run: to move fast on feet; jump: to push off the ground
chunks.source: **Games** like football and rope skipping are **recreation**. We **play**, **run**, **jump**, and kick a **ball** to stay healthy and happy.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two **games** Amina played. A: Football and rope skipping.
chunks.source: Football and rope skipping.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **recreation** mean? A: Fun time after work or school.
chunks.source: Fun time after work or school.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence with **ball**. A: Kato kicked the red ball.
chunks.source: Kato kicked the red ball.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence with **jump**. A: The frog can jump high.
chunks.source: The frog can jump high.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do children need **recreation**? A: It makes bodies strong and hearts happy.
chunks.source: It makes bodies strong and hearts happy.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Festivals We Celebrate. I can tell how we celebrate festivals with music, dance, and food. A **festival** is a special happy day. We **celebrate** with **music**, **dance**, **sing** ing, and sharing **food** together. Keywords: festival: a special day of joy; celebrate: to show joy on a special day; dance: to move body to music; music: sounds that make songs; sing: to make words with tune; food: things we eat
chunks.source: A **festival** is a special happy day. We **celebrate** with **music**, **dance**, **sing** ing, and sharing **food** together.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name one **festival** you know. A: Christmas or Eid or Independence Day.
chunks.source: Christmas or Eid or Independence Day.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **celebrate** mean? A: To show joy on a special day.
chunks.source: To show joy on a special day.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence with **music**. A: The drum music is loud.
chunks.source: The drum music is loud.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence with **dance**. A: We dance at the wedding.
chunks.source: We dance at the wedding.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do people share **food** at a **festival**? A: To show love and unity.
chunks.source: To show love and unity.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Our Holiday. I can describe what we do on holiday: rest, visit, travel, and be with family. **Holiday** means no school. We **rest**, **travel**, **visit** loved ones, and enjoy **family** time. It makes us **happy**. Keywords: holiday: break from school or work; rest: to stop work and relax; visit: to go see someone; travel: to go from one place to another; family: people related to us; happy: feeling good and smiling
chunks.source: **Holiday** means no school. We **rest**, **travel**, **visit** loved ones, and enjoy **family** time. It makes us **happy**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a **holiday**? A: A break from school or work.
chunks.source: A break from school or work.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence with **rest**. A: We rest under the mango tree.
chunks.source: We rest under the mango tree.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence with **visit**. A: We visit Grandmother in the village.
chunks.source: We visit Grandmother in the village.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How did Amina **travel**? A: By boda boda and matatu.
chunks.source: By boda boda and matatu.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why was Amina **happy**? A: She was with her **family**.
chunks.source: She was with her **family**.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Counting to 200. I can count to 200 and know hundreds, tens and ones. Numbers to 200 have hundreds, tens and ones. Group in tens to count fast. The place of a digit tells its value. Keywords: hundreds: groups of one hundred; tens: groups of ten; ones: single units; place value: the value of a digit by its position; count: say numbers in order
chunks.source: Numbers to 200 have hundreds, tens and ones. Group in tens to count fast. The place of a digit tells its value.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the number: 1 hundred, 7 tens, 5 ones. A: 175

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many tens in 160? A: 16

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the place value of 8 in 183? A: tens
chunks.source: tens

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we group sticks in tens? A: It makes counting large numbers faster and shows place value.
chunks.source: It makes counting large numbers faster and shows place value.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Adding Two-Digit Numbers. I can add two-digit numbers without regrouping. To add two-digit numbers: write in columns, add ones, add tens, write the sum. No regrouping means each column stays under ten. Keywords: add: put numbers together; sum: the answer when you add; tens: groups of ten; ones: single units; total: the whole amount
chunks.source: To add two-digit numbers: write in columns, add ones, add tens, write the sum. No regrouping means each column stays under ten.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the sum of 30 and 40? A: 70

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the total: 62 + 17. A: 79

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we add ones before tens? A: Because ones are the smallest place value. We build the sum from right to left.
chunks.source: Because ones are the smallest place value. We build the sum from right to left.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Shapes and Lines Around School. I can name sides and corners of 2D shapes. 2D shapes have sides and corners. Count them to name the shape. A square has 4 equal sides and 4 corners. A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners. Keywords: shape: a flat figure; side: a straight edge of a shape; corner: where two sides meet; line: a straight mark; square: a shape with four equal sides and four corners
chunks.source: 2D shapes have sides and corners. Count them to name the shape. A square has 4 equal sides and 4 corners. A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many sides does a rectangle have? A: 4

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many corners does a triangle have? A: 3

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name a shape with 4 equal sides and 4 corners. A: square
chunks.source: square

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Draw a shape with 5 sides. What is it called? A: pentagon
chunks.source: pentagon

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why is a circle not a polygon? A: A circle has no straight sides and no corners.
chunks.source: A circle has no straight sides and no corners.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Subtracting Two-Digit Numbers. I can subtract two-digit numbers without regrouping to find the difference. We subtract two-digit numbers by taking away ones from ones and tens from tens to find the difference. Keywords: subtract: take away; difference: the answer when you subtract; minus: the sign for subtraction; tens: groups of ten; ones: single units
chunks.source: We subtract two-digit numbers by taking away ones from ones and tens from tens to find the difference.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is 56 - 24? A: 32

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the difference: 89 - 53. A: 36

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we subtract the ones first? A: Because ones are the smallest place value. We subtract ones from ones and tens from tens.
chunks.source: Because ones are the smallest place value. We subtract ones from ones and tens from tens.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the steps to subtract 72 - 41. A: 1. Write 72 above 41. 2. Subtract ones: 2-1=1. 3. Subtract tens: 7-4=3. 4. Difference is 31.
chunks.source: 1. Write 72 above 41. 2. Subtract ones: 2-1=1. 3. Subtract tens: 7-4=3. 4. Difference is 31.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A boda boda fare is 3000 shillings. Musa pays with 5000 shillings. How much change? A: 2000 shillings
chunks.source: 2000 shillings

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare: 45 - 12 and 34 - 10. Which difference is greater? A: 45-12=33, 34-10=24. 33 is greater than 24.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Ordinal Numbers and Positions. I can use ordinal numbers from first to tenth to tell position. Ordinal numbers like first, second, fifth, and tenth tell us the position of things in order. Keywords: first: number one in order; second: number two in order; fifth: number five in order; tenth: number ten in order; position: place in a line or order
chunks.source: Ordinal numbers like first, second, fifth, and tenth tell us the position of things in order.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the ordinal number for 3. A: third
chunks.source: third

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the **position** of the child after the **second**? A: third
chunks.source: third

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we use ordinal numbers in a queue? A: To know who is first, second, etc., so everyone gets a fair turn.
chunks.source: To know who is first, second, etc., so everyone gets a fair turn.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: List the first five ordinal numbers. A: first, second, third, fourth, fifth
chunks.source: first, second, third, fourth, fifth

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In a race of 8 children, Musa finishes **fifth**. How many children finished before him? A: 4 children
chunks.source: 4 children

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the ordinal number for the last day of the week (Sunday is 7th). A: seventh
chunks.source: seventh

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Comparing Numbers. I can compare and order numbers up to 200 using greater than, less than, and equal. We compare numbers by checking hundreds, then tens, then ones. We use > for greater than, < for less than, and = for equal. Keywords: greater than: bigger than; less than: smaller than; equal: the same as; compare: check which is bigger or smaller; order: arrange from smallest to largest
chunks.source: We compare numbers by checking hundreds, then tens, then ones. We use > for greater than, < for less than, and = for equal.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Compare 156 and 165. Which is **greater than**? A: 165 is greater than 156.
chunks.source: 165 is greater than 156.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the symbol: 199 ___ 190. A: >

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why is 145 **greater than** 132? A: Because the tens digit 4 is greater than 3, while hundreds are equal.
chunks.source: Because the tens digit 4 is greater than 3, while hundreds are equal.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Order these numbers from smallest to largest: 120, 102, 112. A: 102, 112, 120

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A kilo of posho costs 2500 shillings. A kilo of beans costs 3000 shillings. Which costs **less than** the other? A: Posho costs less than beans.
chunks.source: Posho costs less than beans.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write a number that is **equal** to 150. A: 150

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Counting in Twos and Fives. I can skip count in twos and fives and identify even and odd numbers. We learned to **skip count** in **twos** and **fives**, and to tell **even** from **odd** numbers. Keywords: twos: groups of two; fives: groups of five; skip count: count by jumping numbers; even: numbers ending with 0,2,4,6,8; odd: numbers ending with 1,3,5,7,9
chunks.source: We learned to **skip count** in **twos** and **fives**, and to tell **even** from **odd** numbers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the next number when you **skip count** in **twos** after 12? A: 14

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the first five numbers when you **skip count** in **fives**. A: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Is 18 an **even** or **odd** number? A: Even
chunks.source: Even

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why is 7 an **odd** number? A: Because it ends with 7, not 0,2,4,6,8.
chunks.source: Because it ends with 7, not 0,2,4,6,8.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If you have 20 mangoes and share them in **twos**, how many groups? A: 10 groups
chunks.source: 10 groups

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Measuring Our Bodies. I can measure height and length using a metre ruler. We used a **metre** ruler to **measure** **height** and **length**, and learned what **tall** means. Keywords: measure: find the size of something; metre: unit of length equal to 100 centimetres; tall: having great height; height: how high something is; length: how long something is
chunks.source: We used a **metre** ruler to **measure** **height** and **length**, and learned what **tall** means.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What tool do you use to **measure** **height** in **metre**? A: A metre ruler or tape measure.
chunks.source: A metre ruler or tape measure.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If Peter's **height** is 1 metre 20 centimetres, how many centimetres is that? A: 120 centimetres
chunks.source: 120 centimetres

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which is longer: 1 **metre** or 80 centimetres? A: 1 metre
chunks.source: 1 metre

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we use a **metre** ruler to find **length**? A: Because a metre ruler shows metres and centimetres.
chunks.source: Because a metre ruler shows metres and centimetres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the **height** of a door that is 2 **metre** tall. A: 2 metres
chunks.source: 2 metres

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Heavy and Light. I can compare heavy and light objects and weigh them. We compared **heavy** and **light** objects, used **heavier**, **lighter**, and learned to **weigh** them. Keywords: heavy: having a lot of mass; light: having little mass; heavier: more heavy than something else; lighter: less heavy than something else; weigh: find how heavy something is
chunks.source: We compared **heavy** and **light** objects, used **heavier**, **lighter**, and learned to **weigh** them.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which is **heavier**, a sack of **cassava** or a feather? A: The sack of cassava.
chunks.source: The sack of cassava.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If a bottle is **lighter** than a bag, which is **heavier**? A: The bag.
chunks.source: The bag.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What tool do we use to **weigh** objects? A: A scale.
chunks.source: A scale.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why is a stone **heavier** than a sponge? A: Because stone has more mass.
chunks.source: Because stone has more mass.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write two things that are **light**. A: Feather, paper.
chunks.source: Feather, paper.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Money: Coins and Notes. I can name Ugandan coins and notes up to 1,000 shillings. Ugandan **coins** and **notes** have different numbers, colours, and shapes. The **price** tells you the value in **shillings**. Keywords: shilling: Uganda's money unit; coin: metal money; note: paper money; money: what we use to buy; price: cost of a thing
chunks.source: Ugandan **coins** and **notes** have different numbers, colours, and shapes. The **price** tells you the value in **shillings**.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What **coin** has a crane on it? A: The 200 shilling coin.
chunks.source: The 200 shilling coin.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What colour is the 1,000 **shilling** **note**? A: Red.
chunks.source: Red.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the **price** of a 500 **shilling** **coin** in words. A: Five hundred shillings.
chunks.source: Five hundred shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we check the number on **money**? A: To know the value and not make a mistake.
chunks.source: To know the value and not make a mistake.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Put these in order from smallest to biggest: 100 **shilling**, 500 **shilling**, 1,000 **shilling**. A: 100 shilling, 500 shilling, 1,000 shilling.
chunks.source: 100 shilling, 500 shilling, 1,000 shilling.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If you have two 500 **shilling** **coins**, how many **shillings** do you have? A: 1,000 shillings.
chunks.source: 1,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Buying Food: Adding Money. I can add **money** amounts to find the **total** **cost** of food. To find the **total** **cost**, add the **price** of each item. The **total** tells you how many **shillings** to pay. Keywords: buy: get by paying; cost: what you pay; total: all added together; price: cost of one thing; shilling: Uganda's money unit
chunks.source: To find the **total** **cost**, add the **price** of each item. The **total** tells you how many **shillings** to pay.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Add 200 **shillings** + 300 **shillings**. A: 500 shillings.
chunks.source: 500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: **Price** of rice 700 **shillings**, **price** of meat 800 **shillings**. Find **total** **cost**. A: 1,500 shillings.
chunks.source: 1,500 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Amina has 1,000 **shillings**. She spends 600 **shillings**. How much left? A: 400 shillings.
chunks.source: 400 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we add **prices** when we **buy** more than one thing? A: To know the total cost before we pay.
chunks.source: To know the total cost before we pay.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the **total** of 500 **shillings** + 200 **shillings** + 100 **shillings**. A: 800 shillings.
chunks.source: 800 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Kato buys two **matooke** at 300 **shillings** each. What is the **total** **cost**? A: 600 shillings.
chunks.source: 600 shillings.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Capacity: Litres. I can **measure** **capacity** using **litre** and **half litre** containers. **Capacity** is how much a container holds. One **litre** equals two **half litres**. We **measure** liquids in **litres**. Keywords: litre: unit for liquids; capacity: how much a container holds; full: filled to the top; half litre: half of one litre; measure: find the amount
chunks.source: **Capacity** is how much a container holds. One **litre** equals two **half litres**. We **measure** liquids in **litres**.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many **half litre** cups make one **litre**? A: Two.
chunks.source: Two.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A jug holds 2 **litres**. How many **half litres** is that? A: Four.
chunks.source: Four.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the **capacity** of a **full** **half litre** cup. A: Half litre.
chunks.source: Half litre.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we use a **litre** jerrycan for water? A: It holds more so we carry fewer trips.
chunks.source: It holds more so we carry fewer trips.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If you pour two **half litre** packets into a jug, what is the **capacity**? A: One litre.
chunks.source: One litre.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Mother buys 3 **litres** of milk. She has 1 **litre** at home. How many **litres** now? A: 4 litres.
chunks.source: 4 litres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Place Value to 500. I can identify hundreds, tens, and ones and expand numbers up to 500. We use hundreds, tens, and ones to show the place value of numbers up to 500 and we can expand them. Keywords: hundreds: groups of one hundred; tens: groups of ten; ones: single units; place value: the value of a digit by its position; expand: write a number as sum of its parts
chunks.source: We use hundreds, tens, and ones to show the place value of numbers up to 500 and we can expand them.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write 276 in expanded form. A: 200 + 70 + 6

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the place value of 5 in 452? A: 50 (tens)
chunks.source: 50 (tens)

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need to know the tens place when adding? A: Because we carry groups of ten to the next column.
chunks.source: Because we carry groups of ten to the next column.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the number with 3 hundreds, 2 tens, 4 ones. A: 324

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Adding with Carrying. I can add two‑digit numbers with carrying. When adding two‑digit numbers, we add ones, carry any ten, then add tens to get the sum. Keywords: add: put numbers together; carry: move a ten to the next column; regroup: change ten ones into one ten; sum: the answer of addition; tens: groups of ten
chunks.source: When adding two‑digit numbers, we add ones, carry any ten, then add tens to get the sum.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What do you do when the ones make ten? A: Carry one to the tens column.
chunks.source: Carry one to the tens column.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we regroup when adding? A: Because ten ones become one ten.
chunks.source: Because ten ones become one ten.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the sum of 34 + 48. A: 82

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Subtracting with Borrowing. I can subtract two‑digit numbers with borrowing. When subtracting two‑digit numbers, we borrow from the tens if the ones are too small, then find the difference. Keywords: subtract: take one number away from another; borrow: take a ten from the next column; regroup: change a ten into ten ones; difference: the answer of subtraction; tens: groups of ten
chunks.source: When subtracting two‑digit numbers, we borrow from the tens if the ones are too small, then find the difference.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Subtract 64 - 28. A: 36

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Subtract 73 - 46. A: 27

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What do you do when the top ones are smaller? A: Borrow one ten from the tens column.
chunks.source: Borrow one ten from the tens column.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we borrow when subtracting? A: Because we need enough ones to take away.
chunks.source: Because we need enough ones to take away.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the difference of 81 - 34. A: 47

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Patterns and Sequences. I can continue and make number and shape patterns. A pattern repeats by a rule. You can continue number or shape sequences by finding the rule. Keywords: pattern: a design that repeats; sequence: a set of things in order; repeat: to do again; next: the one that comes after; rule: the way a pattern works
chunks.source: A pattern repeats by a rule. You can continue number or shape sequences by finding the rule.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Complete the pattern: 5, 10, 15, ___ A: 20

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Draw the next shape in the pattern: circle, square, circle, ___ A: square
chunks.source: square

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why does the pattern 3, 6, 9, 12 go up by 3? A: Because the rule is add 3 each time.
chunks.source: Because the rule is add 3 each time.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Make your own number pattern using the rule 'add 5' starting at 2. A: 2, 7, 12, 17

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the rule for the pattern: 10, 20, 30, 40? A: Add 10 each time.
chunks.source: Add 10 each time.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Solid Shapes We Make. I can name 3D shapes and count their faces. A cube has 6 square faces. A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces. A cylinder has 2 circular faces. A sphere has no flat faces. Keywords: cube: a solid with 6 square faces; cuboid: a solid with 6 rectangular faces; cylinder: a solid with 2 circular faces; sphere: a solid with no flat faces; face: a flat side of a solid
chunks.source: A cube has 6 square faces. A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces. A cylinder has 2 circular faces. A sphere has no flat faces.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Name the shape with 6 equal square faces. A: cube
chunks.source: cube

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: How many faces does a cuboid have? A: 6

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which shape has no edges and no vertices? A: sphere
chunks.source: sphere

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why does a cylinder have 2 circular faces? A: Because its top and bottom are circles.
chunks.source: Because its top and bottom are circles.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Draw a cuboid and label its faces. A: A drawing with 6 rectangular faces labeled.
chunks.source: A drawing with 6 rectangular faces labeled.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Measuring in Centimetres. I can measure length in centimetres with a ruler. Use a ruler to measure length in centimetres. Start at zero and read the number at the end. Keywords: centimetre: a unit for measuring length; ruler: a tool to measure length; measure: to find the size of something; length: how long something is; long: having great length
chunks.source: Use a ruler to measure length in centimetres. Start at zero and read the number at the end.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the length of a 30 cm ruler? A: 30 cm
chunks.source: 30 cm

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If a pencil ends at 12 on the ruler, how long is it? A: 12 cm
chunks.source: 12 cm

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we start measuring at the zero mark? A: To get the correct length.
chunks.source: To get the correct length.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Draw a line 8 cm long using a ruler. A: A line 8 cm long.
chunks.source: A line 8 cm long.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which is longer: a 25 cm stick or a 15 cm stick? A: The 25 cm stick.
chunks.source: The 25 cm stick.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Multiplication as Groups. I can multiply by making equal groups of 2 and 5. Multiply means adding equal groups. Groups of 2 and 5 are easy to count. The total is altogether. Keywords: multiply: to add the same number many times; groups: sets of things put together; times: how many groups we have; equal groups: groups with the same number in each; altogether: the total number in all groups
chunks.source: Multiply means adding equal groups. Groups of 2 and 5 are easy to count. The total is altogether.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Draw 4 groups of 2. How many altogether? A: 8 (4 times 2 = 8)
chunks.source: 8 (4 times 2 = 8)

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Draw 3 groups of 5. How many altogether? A: 15 (3 times 5 = 15)

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the multiply sentence: 5 groups of 2. A: 5 times 2 = 10
chunks.source: 5 times 2 = 10

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do equal groups help us multiply faster? A: We count in steps (2, 4, 6...) not one by one.
chunks.source: We count in steps (2, 4, 6...) not one by one.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: There are 6 boda bodas. Each carries 2 people. How many people altogether? A: 12 (6 times 2 = 12)

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A matatu has 5 rows. Each row has 2 seats. How many seats altogether? A: 10 (5 times 2 = 10)

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Telling the Time. I can tell time at o'clock, half past and quarter past. The long hand tells minutes: 12 is o'clock, 6 is half past, 3 is quarter past. The short hand tells the hour. Keywords: o'clock: the hour exactly, minutes hand at 12; half past: 30 minutes after the hour, minutes hand at 6; quarter past: 15 minutes after the hour, minutes hand at 3; clock: a tool that shows the time; hour: 60 minutes, the short hand shows it
chunks.source: The long hand tells minutes: 12 is o'clock, 6 is half past, 3 is quarter past. The short hand tells the hour.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Draw a clock showing 9 o'clock. Where are the hands? A: Short hand at 9, long hand at 12.
chunks.source: Short hand at 9, long hand at 12.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Draw a clock showing half past 4. Where are the hands? A: Short hand between 4 and 5, long hand at 6.
chunks.source: Short hand between 4 and 5, long hand at 6.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Draw a clock showing quarter past 11. Where are the hands? A: Short hand just past 11, long hand at 3.
chunks.source: Short hand just past 11, long hand at 3.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why is the short hand between numbers at half past? A: Because the hour is not finished yet.
chunks.source: Because the hour is not finished yet.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If it is 2 o'clock now, what time in one hour? A: 3 o'clock.
chunks.source: 3 o'clock.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The bus leaves at quarter past 6. You arrive at half past 6. Did you catch it? A: No, the bus left 15 minutes ago.
chunks.source: No, the bus left 15 minutes ago.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: How Far? Distances. I can compare distances using metres and kilometres. Metres measure short distances (near). Kilometres measure long distances (far). 1 kilometre = 1000 metres. Keywords: distance: how far it is from one place to another; metre: a short step, 100 centimetres; kilometre: 1000 metres, a long walk; near: a short distance away; far: a long distance away
chunks.source: Metres measure short distances (near). Kilometres measure long distances (far). 1 kilometre = 1000 metres.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which unit for the length of a bed: metre or kilometre? A: metre
chunks.source: metre

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which unit for distance from Kampala to Jinja: metre or kilometre? A: kilometre
chunks.source: kilometre

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: 1 kilometre = how many metres? A: 1000 metres
chunks.source: 1000 metres

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we use kilometres for long distances? A: Metres would be too many numbers to count.
chunks.source: Metres would be too many numbers to count.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Your school is 800 metres away. Is it near or far? A: Near (less than 1 kilometre).
chunks.source: Near (less than 1 kilometre).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: The hospital is 5 kilometres away. The shop is 300 metres. Which is nearer? A: The shop (300 metres < 5000 metres).
chunks.source: The shop (300 metres < 5000 metres).

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Number Lines and Ordering. I can put numbers in order on a number line. A number line shows order, before, after, between. Keywords: number line: A line with numbers in order.; order: The way numbers go from small to big.; before: Coming earlier than another number.; after: Coming later than another number.; between: In the middle of two numbers.
chunks.source: A number line shows order, before, after, between.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the numbers in order: 15, 3, 27. A: 3, 15, 27

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What number comes after 40? A: 41

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What number is between 50 and 60? A: 55

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we use a number line? A: It shows the order of numbers.
chunks.source: It shows the order of numbers.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Fill the blank: 12, __, 37, 48. A: 25

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Which number comes before 37? A: 25

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Addition Word Problems. I can solve addition word problems up to 100. A problem asks a question. We join numbers to find the sum and the answer. Keywords: problem: A question that needs solving.; altogether: The total when things are added.; sum: The result of adding numbers.; join: To put numbers together by adding.; answer: The final result of a problem.
chunks.source: A problem asks a question. We join numbers to find the sum and the answer.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Kato buys a shirt for 40 sh and a cap for 25 sh. What is the **altogether** cost? A: 65 sh
chunks.source: 65 sh

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Add 12 and 38. What is the **sum**? A: 50

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the addition sentence for 20 + 55. A: 20 + 55 = 75

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we add to find the total? A: Adding joins the parts to make the whole.
chunks.source: Adding joins the parts to make the whole.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If the **answer** is 90 and one part is 45, what is the other part? A: 45

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Read the **problem**: 10 + 20 = ? A: 30

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Subtraction Word Problems. I can solve subtraction word problems up to 100. A problem asks what is left. We take away to find the difference and the answer. Keywords: problem: A question that needs solving.; left: What remains after taking away.; difference: The result of subtracting one number from another.; take away: To remove a number from another.; answer: The final result of a problem.
chunks.source: A problem asks what is left. We take away to find the difference and the answer.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Nalongo had 60 bananas. She gave 22 away. How many are **left**? A: 38

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Find the **difference** between 90 and 40. A: 50

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Write the subtraction sentence for 70 - 30. A: 70 - 30 = 40

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Why do we subtract to find how many are **left**? A: Subtracting takes away the part given away.
chunks.source: Subtracting takes away the part given away.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: If the **answer** is 15 and the start was 50, how many were **take away**? A: 35

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Read the **problem**: 100 - 25 = ? A: 75

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Counting to 1000. I can count and understand place value up to 1,000. We learned to **count** to 1000 using **place value**: ones, tens, **hundreds**, and **thousand**. Keywords: thousand: a group of ten hundreds; hundreds: groups of one hundred; place value: the value of a digit by its position; count: to say numbers in order; number: a symbol for a quantity
