chunks.text: Q: Why is a farmer important? A: A farmer grows food for families.
chunks.source: A farmer grows food for families.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Living Things Around Us. I can name living things around me. Amina discovers many living things like **plant**, **tree**, **flower**, **grass**, **bird**, **bee**, and **hen** around her home and school. Keywords: plant: a living thing that grows; tree: a big plant with a trunk; flower: the colourful part of a plant; grass: short green plants covering ground; bird: an animal with feathers and wings; bee: a flying insect that makes honey; hen: a female chicken that lays eggs
chunks.source: Amina discovers many living things like **plant**, **tree**, **flower**, **grass**, **bird**, **bee**, and **hen** around her home and school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What **plant** does Amina water every day? A: She waters a small plant.
chunks.source: She waters a small plant.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which **tree** stands near the kitchen? A: A tall tree stands near the kitchen.
chunks.source: A tall tree stands near the kitchen.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What **flower** grows at the base of the tree? A: A bright flower grows there.
chunks.source: A bright flower grows there.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why does the **bee** visit the flower? A: The bee collects nectar to make honey.
chunks.source: The bee collects nectar to make honey.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two **bird** sounds Amina hears. A: She hears a bird sing and a hen cluck.
chunks.source: She hears a bird sing and a hen cluck.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What **grass** does Amina see in the garden? A: She sees green grass.
chunks.source: She sees green grass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Non-Living Things Around Us. I can name non-living things around me. Amina learns that **stone**, **soil**, **water**, **air**, **sun**, **rock**, and **road** are non-living things around us. Keywords: stone: a hard piece of earth; soil: the top layer of ground where plants grow; water: a clear liquid we drink and use; air: the invisible gas around us; sun: the star that gives light and heat; rock: a large solid stone; road: a path for walking or driving
chunks.source: Amina learns that **stone**, **soil**, **water**, **air**, **sun**, **rock**, and **road** are non-living things around us.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What **stone** did Amina see on the path? A: A smooth stone.
chunks.source: A smooth stone.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is **soil** important for plants? A: Soil gives nutrients to plants.
chunks.source: Soil gives nutrients to plants.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What **water** did Amina collect at the borehole? A: Clean water.
chunks.source: Clean water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What **air** do we breathe every day? A: We breathe fresh air.
chunks.source: We breathe fresh air.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why does the **sun** help us? A: The sun gives light and warmth.
chunks.source: The sun gives light and warmth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What **rock** is near the **road**? A: A big rock.
chunks.source: A big rock.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Protecting Our Environment. I can protect my environment. Amina and Peter show **care** by cleaning **rubbish**, using a **bin**, **sweeping**, and **plant**ing a tree for **protection**. Keywords: rubbish: waste things we throw away; protection: keeping something safe from harm; clean: free from dirt or rubbish; plant: to put a seed in soil to grow; sweep: to clear dirt with a broom; bin: a container for rubbish; care: to look after something well
chunks.source: Amina and Peter show **care** by cleaning **rubbish**, using a **bin**, **sweeping**, and **plant**ing a tree for **protection**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What **rubbish** did Amina and Peter see? A: They saw rubbish near the gate.
chunks.source: They saw rubbish near the gate.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need **protection** for our environment? A: To keep it safe and healthy.
chunks.source: To keep it safe and healthy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do they **clean** the area? A: They sweep and use a bin.
chunks.source: They sweep and use a bin.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do they **plant** near the gate? A: They plant a seed.
chunks.source: They plant a seed.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we **sweep** the compound? A: To remove rubbish and keep clean.
chunks.source: To remove rubbish and keep clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do they put the **rubbish**? A: In the bin.
chunks.source: In the bin.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Materials from Our Environment. I can name materials from our environment. We get sisal, clay, banana fibre, sticks, reeds, grass, and wood from our environment. People use them to make many crafts. Keywords: sisal: a plant with long leaves used for rope; clay: soft soil used for pots; banana fibre: strong threads from banana stem; sticks: small dry wood pieces; reeds: tall plants in wet places; grass: green plant covering ground; wood: hard material from trees
chunks.source: We get sisal, clay, banana fibre, sticks, reeds, grass, and wood from our environment. People use them to make many crafts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one material from the swamp. A: Reeds or grass.
chunks.source: Reeds or grass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What material comes from the banana plant? A: Banana fibre.
chunks.source: Banana fibre.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which material is soft when wet? A: Clay.
chunks.source: Clay.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people use sisal? A: To make strong rope.
chunks.source: To make strong rope.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do we get wood from? A: From trees.
chunks.source: From trees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Crafts People Make. I can name crafts made in Uganda. People make beads, baskets, mats, pots, ropes, necklaces, and drums from local materials. Each craft has a use. Keywords: bead: small coloured ball with a hole; basket: woven container for carrying; mat: flat woven piece for sitting; pot: clay container for cooking; rope: strong thick string; necklace: jewellery worn on neck; drum: instrument beaten for sound
chunks.source: People make beads, baskets, mats, pots, ropes, necklaces, and drums from local materials. Each craft has a use.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a basket used for? A: Carrying matooke.
chunks.source: Carrying matooke.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which craft is made from clay? A: A pot.
chunks.source: A pot.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What material makes a strong rope? A: Sisal or banana fibre.
chunks.source: Sisal or banana fibre.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people make necklaces? A: To wear for beauty.
chunks.source: To wear for beauty.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name a craft made from wood. A: A drum.
chunks.source: A drum.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Selling the Things We Make. I can explain how crafts are sold. At the market or shop, people sell and buy things. Customers pay money at a set price. Keywords: market: open place for selling; shop: building where things are sold; sell: give something for money; buy: get something by paying; money: coins and notes for paying; price: cost of something; customer: person who buys
chunks.source: At the market or shop, people sell and buy things. Customers pay money at a set price.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where can you sell crafts? A: At the market or shop.
chunks.source: At the market or shop.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who buys the crafts? A: A customer.
chunks.source: A customer.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do you use to pay? A: Money.
chunks.source: Money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why does the seller tell the price? A: So the customer knows the cost.
chunks.source: So the customer knows the cost.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What did Mother buy with the money? A: Soap and salt.
chunks.source: Soap and salt.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Means of Transport We Use. I can name different means of transport. Amina sees many types of transport like bicycle, motorcycle, bus, car, boat, aeroplane, and train. She learns how each moves. Keywords: bicycle: a vehicle with two wheels; motorcycle: a vehicle with two wheels and an engine; bus: a large vehicle for many people; car: a vehicle with four wheels; boat: a vehicle that moves on water; aeroplane: a vehicle that flies in the sky; train: a vehicle that runs on rails
chunks.source: Amina sees many types of transport like bicycle, motorcycle, bus, car, boat, aeroplane, and train. She learns how each moves.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What has two wheels? A: A bicycle.
chunks.source: A bicycle.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which transport flies in the sky? A: An aeroplane.
chunks.source: An aeroplane.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where does a boat move? A: On water.
chunks.source: On water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people wear a helmet on a motorcycle? A: To protect the head.
chunks.source: To protect the head.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name a transport that runs on rails. A: A train.
chunks.source: A train.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Road Safety for Travellers. I can follow road safety rules. Kato and Nalongo learn to use the zebra crossing, wear helmets and seat belts, and listen to the driver. They travel safely on the road. Keywords: zebra crossing: a marked place to cross the road; helmet: a hard hat for head protection; driver: person who drives a vehicle; passenger: person travelling in a vehicle; road: a path for vehicles and people; travel: to go from one place to another; seat belt: a strap that keeps you safe in a car
chunks.source: Kato and Nalongo learn to use the zebra crossing, wear helmets and seat belts, and listen to the driver. They travel safely on the road.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do you cross the road safely? A: At the zebra crossing.
chunks.source: At the zebra crossing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a driver do? A: Drives the vehicle.
chunks.source: Drives the vehicle.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why must a passenger wear a seat belt? A: To stay safe in a crash.
chunks.source: To stay safe in a crash.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What protects a motorcycle rider's head? A: A helmet.
chunks.source: A helmet.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the road used for? A: For vehicles and people to travel.
chunks.source: For vehicles and people to travel.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Moving Goods to Market. I can describe how goods move to market. The farmer, trader, truck, bicycle, and boat move loads to the market. Each transport helps goods reach people. Keywords: farmer: person who grows crops; trader: person who buys and sells goods; truck: a large vehicle for carrying heavy loads; bicycle: a vehicle with two wheels; boat: a vehicle that moves on water; load: goods carried from one place to another; market: place where goods are sold
chunks.source: The farmer, trader, truck, bicycle, and boat move loads to the market. Each transport helps goods reach people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who grows the food? A: The farmer.
chunks.source: The farmer.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a trader do? A: Buys and sells goods.
chunks.source: Buys and sells goods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which vehicle carries goods on water? A: A boat.
chunks.source: A boat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is a truck useful for a big load? A: It can carry many things.
chunks.source: It can carry many things.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where does the trader sell the load? A: At the market.
chunks.source: At the market.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Accidents at Home and School. I can name common accidents and say how to stay safe. Amina learns that fire, knives, razors, and matchboxes can cause burns, cuts, and falls. She knows to tell an adult and keep dangerous things away. Keywords: fire: hot flame; burn: skin hurt from heat; cut: skin split by sharp thing; fall: drop down suddenly; knife: sharp tool for cutting; matchbox: box with matches; razor: sharp blade for shaving
chunks.source: Amina learns that fire, knives, razors, and matchboxes can cause burns, cuts, and falls. She knows to tell an adult and keep dangerous things away.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What can **fire** do? A: Fire can burn.
chunks.source: Fire can burn.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What should you do if you see a **knife** on the floor? A: Tell an adult.
chunks.source: Tell an adult.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is a **matchbox** dangerous? A: It can start a fire.
chunks.source: It can start a fire.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What happens if you **fall**? A: You can get hurt.
chunks.source: You can get hurt.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why should you keep **razor** away? A: It is sharp and can cut.
chunks.source: It is sharp and can cut.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: First Aid for Small Hurts. I can explain simple first aid steps for a small cut. Amina learns first aid: wash, clean, bandage, and tell a nurse or doctor. She knows medicine helps healing. Keywords: first aid: basic help for injury; bandage: strip to cover a wound; wash: clean with water; nurse: health worker at school; doctor: medical professional; medicine: drug to treat illness; clean: free from dirt
chunks.source: Amina learns first aid: wash, clean, bandage, and tell a nurse or doctor. She knows medicine helps healing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the first step of **first aid** for a **cut**? A: Wash the cut with clean water.
chunks.source: Wash the cut with clean water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we put a **bandage** on a **cut**? A: To keep it clean.
chunks.source: To keep it clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who can give **medicine** for a bad cut? A: A doctor.
chunks.source: A doctor.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a **nurse** do for a small hurt? A: Checks and cleans it.
chunks.source: Checks and cleans it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why must we keep a **cut** **clean**? A: To stop germs.
chunks.source: To stop germs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Keeping Safe from Danger. I can identify dangers and say how to stay safe. Amina learns to avoid poison, unknown medicine, and strangers. She knows to report danger and follow road safety. Keywords: poison: harmful substance; medicine: drug for health; safety: being free from harm; road: path for vehicles; water: liquid we drink; stranger: person we do not know; report: tell an adult about danger
chunks.source: Amina learns to avoid poison, unknown medicine, and strangers. She knows to report danger and follow road safety.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What should you do if a **stranger** offers **water**? A: Say no and report.
chunks.source: Say no and report.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is unknown **medicine** dangerous? A: It can be poison.
chunks.source: It can be poison.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **safety** mean on the **road**? A: Look both ways before crossing.
chunks.source: Look both ways before crossing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What must you do if you see **poison**? A: Report it to an adult.
chunks.source: Report it to an adult.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why keep **water** clean? A: To avoid illness.
chunks.source: To avoid illness.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Living Together in Peace. I can explain how peace grows when we share, respect, and forgive. Amina learns that peace comes when we share, respect, care, and forgive each other. Living together in peace makes our village strong. Keywords: peace: calm and no fighting; love: deep care for others; respect: treating others well; care: looking after someone; friend: a person you like; share: give part of yours; forgive: stop being angry
chunks.source: Amina learns that peace comes when we share, respect, care, and forgive each other. Living together in peace makes our village strong.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina share with her friend? A: She shares her mango.
chunks.source: She shares her mango.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do friends forgive each other? A: Because forgiveness brings peace.
chunks.source: Because forgiveness brings peace.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one way to show respect. A: Listen when others speak.
chunks.source: Listen when others speak.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What word means to give something to others? A: Share.
chunks.source: Share.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does Amina feel when there is peace? A: She feels happy and safe.
chunks.source: She feels happy and safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does the teacher Nankya do at the gate? A: She greets the children.
chunks.source: She greets the children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Solving Disagreements Peacefully. I can describe how to solve a conflict by talking, listening, and saying sorry. Amina and Peter learn that talking, listening, and saying sorry solve conflicts peacefully. Elders and teachers can guide them. Keywords: conflict: a disagreement or fight; talk: speak to each other; listen: hear and understand; negotiation: finding a fair agreement; sorry: showing regret; elder: an older respected person; teacher: person who teaches
chunks.source: Amina and Peter learn that talking, listening, and saying sorry solve conflicts peacefully. Elders and teachers can guide them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the first step to solve a conflict? A: Talk calmly to each other.
chunks.source: Talk calmly to each other.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is listening important in a disagreement? A: It helps understand the other person.
chunks.source: It helps understand the other person.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who can help when children cannot agree? A: An elder or a teacher.
chunks.source: An elder or a teacher.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does negotiation mean? A: Sharing ideas to find a solution.
chunks.source: Sharing ideas to find a solution.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What word shows you regret your action? A: Sorry.
chunks.source: Sorry.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does the teacher react to peaceful solving? A: The teacher praises them.
chunks.source: The teacher praises them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: People Who Keep Security. I can name the people who protect us and explain how to report danger. Police, soldiers, guards, and askari work together to give us security. We must report dangers to them. Keywords: police: officers who enforce law; soldier: person who defends the country; guard: person who watches a place; askari: security officer in uniform; report: tell authorities about danger; thief: person who steals; security: safety and protection
chunks.source: Police, soldiers, guards, and askari work together to give us security. We must report dangers to them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who wears a blue uniform at the trading centre? A: A police officer.
chunks.source: A police officer.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a soldier do at the barracks? A: Stands guard at the gate.
chunks.source: Stands guard at the gate.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the job of a school guard? A: Watches the school compound.
chunks.source: Watches the school compound.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What should you do if you see a thief? A: Report to the police.
chunks.source: Report to the police.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is it unsafe to chase a thief? A: It can be dangerous.
chunks.source: It can be dangerous.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What word means safety for everyone? A: Security.
chunks.source: Security.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: My Rights as a Child. I can name my rights as a child. Every child in Uganda has rights to care, protection, food, education, health, and play. Keywords: rights: things every child should have; care: adults looking after you; protection: keeping safe from danger; food: what we eat to grow; education: learning at school; health: being well and not sick; play: games and fun time
chunks.source: Every child in Uganda has rights to care, protection, food, education, health, and play.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a right? A: A right is something every child should have.
chunks.source: A right is something every child should have.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two rights Amina learned. A: Food and education.
chunks.source: Food and education.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do children need food? A: Food gives energy to grow.
chunks.source: Food gives energy to grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who can help if a right is missing? A: A trusted adult like a parent or teacher.
chunks.source: A trusted adult like a parent or teacher.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does protection mean? A: Protection keeps you safe from danger.
chunks.source: Protection keeps you safe from danger.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Keeping Safe from Harm. I can tell how to stay safe from harm. Children must tell a trusted adult like a teacher or parent if they face harm, abuse, or a stranger. Keywords: harm: any hurt to a child; abuse: when someone hurts a child on purpose; adult: a grown person who can help; stranger: someone you do not know; report: tell a trusted person about a problem; teacher: person who teaches at school; parent: mother or father
chunks.source: Children must tell a trusted adult like a teacher or parent if they face harm, abuse, or a stranger.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is harm? A: Harm is any hurt to a child.
chunks.source: Harm is any hurt to a child.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What should Kato do if a stranger offers a gift? A: Say no and tell a trusted adult.
chunks.source: Say no and tell a trusted adult.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why must children report abuse? A: Reporting stops the abuse and keeps children safe.
chunks.source: Reporting stops the abuse and keeps children safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two trusted adults Kato can tell. A: Teacher and parent.
chunks.source: Teacher and parent.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a stranger mean? A: A stranger is someone you do not know.
chunks.source: A stranger is someone you do not know.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Trusted People Who Protect Children. I can name trusted people who protect children. Many adults like parents, teachers, police officers, elders, nurses, chairpersons, and friends protect children. Keywords: parent: mother or father; teacher: person who teaches at school; police officer: person who keeps law and order; elder: respected older person; nurse: health worker who gives medicine; chairperson: leader of the village council; friend: someone you like and trust
chunks.source: Many adults like parents, teachers, police officers, elders, nurses, chairpersons, and friends protect children.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who protects children at home? A: A parent.
chunks.source: A parent.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who protects children at school? A: A teacher.
chunks.source: A teacher.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a police officer do? A: Stops bad actions and keeps peace.
chunks.source: Stops bad actions and keeps peace.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is a nurse important for children? A: A nurse gives medicine and cares for health.
chunks.source: A nurse gives medicine and cares for health.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two trusted people a child can tell. A: Parent and teacher.
chunks.source: Parent and teacher.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Measuring in the Market. I can measure weight, length, and volume at the market. Amina learns to measure weight, length, and volume at the market. Keywords: kilogram: unit for weight; litre: unit for liquid volume; metre: unit for length; measure: to find size or amount; scale: tool that shows weight; buy: to get by paying; sell: to give for money
chunks.source: Amina learns to measure weight, length, and volume at the market.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What unit do we use for weight? A: kilogram
chunks.source: kilogram

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What unit do we use for liquid? A: litre
chunks.source: litre

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What tool shows weight? A: scale
chunks.source: scale

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we measure things before we buy? A: To know how much we need.
chunks.source: To know how much we need.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does the trader do? A: sell
chunks.source: sell

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Time in Our Community. I can tell time, weeks, months, and seasons. Amina learns to read time, weeks, months, and seasons. Keywords: clock: tool that shows time; hour: sixty minutes; minute: sixty seconds; calendar: shows days and months; week: seven days; month: four weeks; season: time of year with weather
chunks.source: Amina learns to read time, weeks, months, and seasons.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What shows the hour and minute? A: clock
chunks.source: clock

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How many days in a week? A: seven
chunks.source: seven

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What tells the month? A: calendar
chunks.source: calendar

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need a calendar? A: To know the month and week.
chunks.source: To know the month and week.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What changes with rain and sun? A: season
chunks.source: season

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Money We Use. I can identify Ugandan money, price, and change. Amina learns about Ugandan money, price, and change at the market. Keywords: shilling: unit of Ugandan money; coin: metal money piece; note: paper money piece; money: what we use to buy; price: cost of something; market: place to buy and sell; change: money returned after paying
chunks.source: Amina learns about Ugandan money, price, and change at the market.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the unit of money in Uganda? A: shilling
chunks.source: shilling

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What metal piece is money? A: coin
chunks.source: coin

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What paper piece is money? A: note
chunks.source: note

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need change? A: To get back extra money.
chunks.source: To get back extra money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do we buy things? A: market
chunks.source: market

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Games and Sports We Enjoy. I can name games and sports we play in Uganda. Amina enjoys games like football and netball. She runs, jumps, dances, and plays with friends at school. Keywords: games: activities we play for fun; football: a game kicking a ball; netball: a game throwing a ball through a net; run: move fast on feet; jump: push off the ground; dance: move to music; play: do something for fun
chunks.source: Amina enjoys games like football and netball. She runs, jumps, dances, and plays with friends at school.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What game does Amina kick? A: football
chunks.source: football

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What game uses a net? A: netball
chunks.source: netball

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do children do to music? A: dance
chunks.source: dance

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why does Amina like sports day? A: Because she can run, jump, and play with friends.
chunks.source: Because she can run, jump, and play with friends.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two games from the story. A: football and netball
chunks.source: football and netball

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does Teacher Nankya say? A: Time for games!
chunks.source: Time for games!

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Festivals in Our Community. I can describe a festival in my community. Amina enjoys a festival with music, drums, dance, and food. It is a holiday to celebrate. Keywords: festival: a big community party; celebrate: show happiness together; music: sounds that make a tune; dance: move body to rhythm; food: things we eat; drums: instruments beaten for sound; holiday: day off from work or school
chunks.source: Amina enjoys a festival with music, drums, dance, and food. It is a holiday to celebrate.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where does Amina go? A: the trading centre
chunks.source: the trading centre

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina hear? A: music and drums
chunks.source: music and drums

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina eat? A: matooke and beans
chunks.source: matooke and beans

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people celebrate? A: To show happiness together.
chunks.source: To show happiness together.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What makes the sound boom boom? A: drums
chunks.source: drums

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Is today a school day? A: No, it is a holiday.
chunks.source: No, it is a holiday.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Special Days We Remember. I can name special days in Uganda. Uganda has special days like Independence Day, Christmas, Eid, and New Year. They are holidays to celebrate with the flag. Keywords: independence day: day Uganda became free; christmas: Christian holiday on 25th December; eid: Muslim holiday after Ramadan; new year: first day of the year; holiday: day off from school or work; celebrate: do something special for a day; flag: cloth symbol of a country
chunks.source: Uganda has special days like Independence Day, Christmas, Eid, and New Year. They are holidays to celebrate with the flag.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: When is Independence Day? A: 9th October
chunks.source: 9th October

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do Christians celebrate on 25th December? A: Christmas
chunks.source: Christmas

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do Muslims celebrate after Ramadan? A: Eid
chunks.source: Eid

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we raise the flag? A: To show pride for Uganda.
chunks.source: To show pride for Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What day starts the new year? A: New Year
chunks.source: New Year

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Do you go to school on these days? A: No, they are holidays.
chunks.source: No, they are holidays.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: People in My Home. I can name the people in my home. Amina lives with her mother, father, baby, and other relatives; they share meals and visit each other. Keywords: parent: a mother or father; mother: a female parent; father: a male parent; children: sons and daughters; baby: a very young child; family: people who live together and care for each other; relative: a person connected by blood or marriage
chunks.source: Amina lives with her mother, father, baby, and other relatives; they share meals and visit each other.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina's mother do at the market? A: She sells tomatoes.
chunks.source: She sells tomatoes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who rides a boda boda to work? A: Her father rides a boda boda.
chunks.source: Her father rides a boda boda.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two children in Amina's family. A: Amina and the baby.
chunks.source: Amina and the baby.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a relative? A: A relative is a family member like an uncle or grandmother.
chunks.source: A relative is a family member like an uncle or grandmother.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what family means. A: Family means people who live together and care for each other.
chunks.source: Family means people who live together and care for each other.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where does Amina go on the weekend in the story? A: She visits her relative in the village.
chunks.source: She visits her relative in the village.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Places in Our Community. I can name places in my community. Kato walks on the road and sees the market, shop, school, hospital, church, and mosque in his community. Keywords: market: a place to buy and sell food; hospital: a place where sick people get help; church: a building for Christian prayer; mosque: a building for Muslim prayer; school: a place where children learn; shop: a small store selling goods; road: a path for vehicles and people
chunks.source: Kato walks on the road and sees the market, shop, school, hospital, church, and mosque in his community.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What can you buy at the market? A: You can buy food like matooke and tomatoes.
chunks.source: You can buy food like matooke and tomatoes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where do sick people go? A: They go to the hospital.
chunks.source: They go to the hospital.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two places of worship in the story. A: The church and the mosque.
chunks.source: The church and the mosque.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Teacher Nankya do at the school? A: She teaches children.
chunks.source: She teaches children.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why a road is important. A: A road lets people and vehicles move between places.
chunks.source: A road lets people and vehicles move between places.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which place did Kato visit first in the story? A: He went to the market or the shop.
chunks.source: He went to the market or the shop.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Leaders in Our Community. I can name leaders in my community. Nalongo's village group meets, chooses a leader, and works together to improve their village. Keywords: leader: a person who guides others; chairperson: the person who leads a meeting; village: a small community in the countryside; member: a person who belongs to a group; group: several people together; meeting: a gathering to talk and decide
chunks.source: Nalongo's village group meets, chooses a leader, and works together to improve their village.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does the chairperson do at the meeting? A: The chairperson opens the meeting with a prayer.
chunks.source: The chairperson opens the meeting with a prayer.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who is a member of the village group? A: Nalongo is a member.
chunks.source: Nalongo is a member.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing the leader does in the story. A: The leader visits the school or talks to the chairperson.
chunks.source: The leader visits the school or talks to the chairperson.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a meeting? A: A meeting is when people gather to talk and decide.
chunks.source: A meeting is when people gather to talk and decide.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what a leader does. A: A leader guides the group and helps make decisions.
chunks.source: A leader guides the group and helps make decisions.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is the village group important? A: They work together for a better village.
chunks.source: They work together for a better village.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Our Sub-County. I can name the parts of my sub-county and identify a landmark. A sub-county is made of parishes, which are split into zones. Landmarks like hills and features like rivers help us describe where we live. Keywords: sub-county: a part of a district with several parishes; parish: a smaller area inside a sub-county; zone: a small section inside a parish; landmark: a well‑known place that helps people find their way; hill: a high piece of land; feature: any natural or man‑made thing that describes a place
chunks.source: A sub-county is made of parishes, which are split into zones. Landmarks like hills and features like rivers help us describe where we live.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a **sub-county**? A: A sub-county is a part of a district that contains several parishes.
chunks.source: A sub-county is a part of a district that contains several parishes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name one **parish** in your **sub-county**. A: My parish is called Kyarusozi.
chunks.source: My parish is called Kyarusozi.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does a **zone** do? A: A zone is a small area inside a parish.
chunks.source: A zone is a small area inside a parish.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of a **landmark**. A: A big hill or a church can be a landmark.
chunks.source: A big hill or a church can be a landmark.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is a **hill** a useful **feature**? A: A hill can be seen from far away and helps people find direction.
chunks.source: A hill can be seen from far away and helps people find direction.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what a **feature** is. A: A feature is any natural or man‑made thing like a hill, river, or building that helps describe a place.
chunks.source: A feature is any natural or man‑made thing like a hill, river, or building that helps describe a place.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Physical Features Around Us. I can identify and name common physical features in my area. Physical features such as hills, rivers, lakes, valleys, and forests shape our surroundings and help us describe where we live. Keywords: hill: a high piece of land; river: a flowing body of water; lake: a large body of water surrounded by land; valley: low land between hills; forest: a large area covered with trees; feature: any natural thing that describes a place
chunks.source: Physical features such as hills, rivers, lakes, valleys, and forests shape our surroundings and help us describe where we live.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a **hill**? A: A hill is a high piece of land.
chunks.source: A hill is a high piece of land.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name a **river** you know. A: The Nile River flows through Uganda.
chunks.source: The Nile River flows through Uganda.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What makes a **lake** different from a **river**? A: A lake is still water surrounded by land; a river flows.
chunks.source: A lake is still water surrounded by land; a river flows.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Describe a **valley**. A: A valley is low land between hills.
chunks.source: A valley is low land between hills.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is a **forest** important? A: A forest gives us wood, medicine, and fresh air.
chunks.source: A forest gives us wood, medicine, and fresh air.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what a **feature** is. A: A feature is any natural thing like a hill, river, or forest that describes a place.
chunks.source: A feature is any natural thing like a hill, river, or forest that describes a place.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Directions of the Compass. I can use a compass to find north, south, east, west and describe front and behind. A compass points to north; east is sunrise, west is sunset, south is opposite north. Front is forward, behind is back. Keywords: north: the direction where the sun rises in the morning; south: the opposite direction of north; east: the direction where the sun rises; west: the direction where the sun sets; compass: a tool that shows the four main directions; direction: the way something points or moves; behind: at the back of something; front: at the forward side of something
chunks.source: A compass points to north; east is sunrise, west is sunset, south is opposite north. Front is forward, behind is back.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does a **compass** show? A: A compass shows the four main directions: north, south, east, west.
chunks.source: A compass shows the four main directions: north, south, east, west.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If you face **east**, where is **west**? A: West is behind you when you face east.
chunks.source: West is behind you when you face east.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name the direction where the sun sets. A: The sun sets in the west.
chunks.source: The sun sets in the west.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the opposite of **north**? A: The opposite of north is south.
chunks.source: The opposite of north is south.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Describe where the **front** of a house is. A: The front is the side with the main door.
chunks.source: The front is the side with the main door.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what **direction** means. A: Direction is the way something points or moves, like north or left.
chunks.source: Direction is the way something points or moves, like north or left.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Work People Do. I can name different types of work in my sub-county. People in our sub-county do different **work** like **farming**, **fishing**, **trading**, and **services**. Each **journey** brings goods to the **market**. Keywords: work: activity to earn a living; farming: growing crops for food; fishing: catching fish for food; trading: buying and selling goods; services: work that helps others; journey: travel from one place to another
chunks.source: People in our sub-county do different **work** like **farming**, **fishing**, **trading**, and **services**. Each **journey** brings goods to the **market**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **work** mean? A: Work is an activity people do to earn a living.
chunks.source: Work is an activity people do to earn a living.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which **work** involves catching fish? A: **Fishing**.
chunks.source: **Fishing**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where does a trader sell things? A: At the **market** or **trading** centre.
chunks.source: At the **market** or **trading** centre.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What **services** does a teacher give? A: A teacher teaches children.
chunks.source: A teacher teaches children.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain **farming** in your own words. A: Farming is growing crops or raising animals for food.
chunks.source: Farming is growing crops or raising animals for food.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What **work** do people do in your sub-county? A: People do **farming**, **fishing**, **trading**, and **services**.
chunks.source: People do **farming**, **fishing**, **trading**, and **services**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Growing Crops and Keeping Animals. I can explain how crops and animals help families. Farmers grow **crops** and keep **cattle** and **goats**. They **harvest** the **crops** and sell them at the **market**. The **garden** and animals work together. Keywords: crops: plants grown for food; cattle: cows kept for milk and meat; goats: small animals kept for milk and meat; harvest: gathering ripe crops; garden: place where crops grow; market: place to buy and sell
chunks.source: Farmers grow **crops** and keep **cattle** and **goats**. They **harvest** the **crops** and sell them at the **market**. The **garden** and animals work together.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What are **crops**? A: Crops are plants grown for food like maize.
chunks.source: Crops are plants grown for food like maize.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two animals Uncle Musa keeps. A: **Cattle** and **goats**.
chunks.source: **Cattle** and **goats**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **harvest** mean? A: Harvest is gathering ripe crops.
chunks.source: Harvest is gathering ripe crops.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where does Uncle Musa sell his **harvest**? A: At the **market**.
chunks.source: At the **market**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain how **cattle** help the **garden**. A: **Cattle** give manure to make the **garden** fertile.
chunks.source: **Cattle** give manure to make the **garden** fertile.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What **crops** grow in your area? A: Maize, beans, cassava, matooke.
chunks.source: Maize, beans, cassava, matooke.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Problems and Solutions at Work. I can describe challenges at work and how to solve them. Workers face **challenges** like rain. They find **solutions** using **money**, **tools**, and **group** work. Better **services** come from solving problems together. Keywords: challenges: problems that make work hard; solutions: ways to fix problems; money: coins and notes used to buy; tools: things used to do work; services: work that helps others; group: people working together
chunks.source: Workers face **challenges** like rain. They find **solutions** using **money**, **tools**, and **group** work. Better **services** come from solving problems together.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What are **challenges**? A: Challenges are problems that make work hard.
chunks.source: Challenges are problems that make work hard.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one **solution** for rain ruining goods. A: Build a shelter.
chunks.source: Build a shelter.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is a **group** helpful? A: A **group** shares **money**, **tools**, and work.
chunks.source: A **group** shares **money**, **tools**, and work.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What **tools** might traders need? A: Hammer, nails, saw, tarp.
chunks.source: Hammer, nails, saw, tarp.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain how **money** helps find **solutions**. A: **Money** buys **tools** and materials for **solutions**.
chunks.source: **Money** buys **tools** and materials for **solutions**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What **services** do traders give? A: Traders sell goods people need.
chunks.source: Traders sell goods people need.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Things Around Us. I can name natural and human things in my environment. **Natural** things like **tree**, **plant**, and **animal** come from nature. **Human** things are made by people. **Observation** helps us see the difference. Keywords: natural: made by nature, not people; human: made or done by people; observation: looking carefully to learn; tree: big woody plant; plant: living thing that grows in soil; animal: living creature that moves
chunks.source: **Natural** things like **tree**, **plant**, and **animal** come from nature. **Human** things are made by people. **Observation** helps us see the difference.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Is a mango **tree** **natural** or **human** made? A: **Natural**.
chunks.source: **Natural**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Is a school building **natural** or **human** made? A: **Human** made.
chunks.source: **Human** made.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name one **animal** you see at home. A: Goat, cow, chicken, dog, or cat.
chunks.source: Goat, cow, chicken, dog, or cat.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **observation** mean? A: Looking carefully to learn.
chunks.source: Looking carefully to learn.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one **natural** thing and one **human** thing at the market. A: **Natural**: fruits, vegetables. **Human**: stalls, scales, plastic bags.
chunks.source: **Natural**: fruits, vegetables. **Human**: stalls, scales, plastic bags.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: how do you know if something is **natural**? A: It grows or exists without people making it, like a **plant** or **animal**.
chunks.source: It grows or exists without people making it, like a **plant** or **animal**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: How People Change the Environment. I can explain how human activities cause changes in the environment. **Human activities** are things people do. Every **cause** has an **effect**. Some **changes** are **useful** like wells. Others harm the land. Each **event** teaches us to choose well. Keywords: human activities: things people do; cause: why something happens; effect: what happens because of a cause; change: to make different; useful: helps us do something; event: something that happens
chunks.source: **Human activities** are things people do. Every **cause** has an **effect**. Some **changes** are **useful** like wells. Others harm the land. Each **event** teaches us to choose well.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a **cause**? A: Why something happens.
chunks.source: Why something happens.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is an **effect**? A: What happens because of a cause.
chunks.source: What happens because of a cause.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give one **human activity** that is **useful** for the environment. A: Planting trees, digging a well, cleaning a spring.
chunks.source: Planting trees, digging a well, cleaning a spring.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What **change** happens when people cut many trees? A: Soil erosion, less rain, animals lose homes.
chunks.source: Soil erosion, less rain, animals lose homes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: how does a **human activity** become a **cause**? A: When people do something like burning rubbish, it makes something else happen like dirty air.
chunks.source: When people do something like burning rubbish, it makes something else happen like dirty air.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name one **event** in your village that **changed** the environment. A: Road building, swamp drainage, tree planting day, flood.
chunks.source: Road building, swamp drainage, tree planting day, flood.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Caring for Our Environment. I can name ways to protect the environment and keep it safe. We **protect** our environment by keeping it **clean**. Put **rubbish** in the pit. Use **waste** wisely. **Plant** trees. Make water sources **safe**. Small acts make a big difference. Keywords: protect: keep safe from harm; clean: free from dirt; rubbish: things thrown away; waste: material not wanted; plant: put seeds in soil to grow; safe: free from danger
chunks.source: We **protect** our environment by keeping it **clean**. Put **rubbish** in the pit. Use **waste** wisely. **Plant** trees. Make water sources **safe**. Small acts make a big difference.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **protect** mean? A: Keep safe from harm.
chunks.source: Keep safe from harm.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where should you put **rubbish**? A: In the rubbish pit or bin.
chunks.source: In the rubbish pit or bin.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How can food **waste** be **useful**? A: Feed animals or make compost for the garden.
chunks.source: Feed animals or make compost for the garden.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is a **clean** compound **safe**? A: No sharp things, no bad smells, fewer flies and mosquitoes.
chunks.source: No sharp things, no bad smells, fewer flies and mosquitoes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: how does **plant**ing a **tree** **protect** the environment? A: Roots hold soil, leaves clean air, shade cools the ground, birds get homes.
chunks.source: Roots hold soil, leaves clean air, shade cools the ground, birds get homes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name three things you do at home to keep the environment **clean** and **safe**. A: Sweep yard, use rubbish pit, cover well, **plant** grass, burn less, reuse bottles.
chunks.source: Sweep yard, use rubbish pit, cover well, **plant** grass, burn less, reuse bottles.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: The Weather Today. I can describe the weather using words like rain, sun, cloud, wind, hot, cold. Amina observes the **weather** and sees **sun**, **cloud**, **wind**, **rain**, and feels **hot** or **cold**. Keywords: weather: the condition outside like sun or rain; rain: water falling from the sky; sun: the bright star that gives light; cloud: white or grey mass in the sky; wind: moving air that blows; hot: high temperature, feels warm; cold: low temperature, feels cool
chunks.source: Amina observes the **weather** and sees **sun**, **cloud**, **wind**, **rain**, and feels **hot** or **cold**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What word describes water falling from the sky? A: rain
chunks.source: rain

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do we call the bright star that gives light? A: sun
chunks.source: sun

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If the air feels warm, what word do we use? A: hot
chunks.source: hot

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the weather like when a big grey cloud covers the sky? A: It might rain.
chunks.source: It might rain.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: What does wind do? A: Wind moves air and blows things like leaves.
chunks.source: Wind moves air and blows things like leaves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Yesterday was cold, today is ___. A: hot
chunks.source: hot

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Weather in the Week. I can use time words like today, tomorrow, week, day to talk about weather. Peter learns that a **week** has seven **day**s. **Today** and **tomorrow** are part of the **week**. The radio **predicted** **rain** for the **future**, not the **past**. Keywords: week: seven days together; day: twenty-four hours from morning to night; today: this day right now; tomorrow: the day after today; predicted: said what will happen before it happens; future: time that has not come yet; past: time that has already gone
chunks.source: Peter learns that a **week** has seven **day**s. **Today** and **tomorrow** are part of the **week**. The radio **predicted** **rain** for the **future**, not the **past**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How many days make a week? A: seven
chunks.source: seven

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do we call the day after today? A: tomorrow
chunks.source: tomorrow

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If the radio says rain will come, what word means they said it before? A: predicted
chunks.source: predicted

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the time that has not come yet called? A: future
chunks.source: future

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: What does 'past' mean? A: Past is time that already happened, like yesterday.
chunks.source: Past is time that already happened, like yesterday.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Today is Monday, tomorrow is ___. A: Tuesday
chunks.source: Tuesday

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Weather and Farming. I can explain how rain, sun, and seasons help plants grow and when to harvest. Nalongo teaches Kato that **rain** helps crops **grow**, **sun** dries them, and **dry** **season** is for **harvest**. Weather guides **plant**ing. Keywords: rain: water falling from the sky; sun: the bright star that gives light; dry: without water, not wet; season: a time of year with certain weather; plant: put seeds in soil to grow; grow: get bigger and stronger; harvest: cut and gather ripe crops
chunks.source: Nalongo teaches Kato that **rain** helps crops **grow**, **sun** dries them, and **dry** **season** is for **harvest**. Weather guides **plant**ing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What makes maize grow tall? A: rain
chunks.source: rain

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What dries the crops for harvest? A: sun
chunks.source: sun

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: When is the soil without water? A: dry season
chunks.source: dry season

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do we do when we put seeds in soil? A: plant
chunks.source: plant

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: Why do farmers like the dry season for harvest? A: Dry season has sun to dry crops so they do not rot.
chunks.source: Dry season has sun to dry crops so they do not rot.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: We plant when rain starts, we harvest in ___ season. A: dry
chunks.source: dry

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Animals Around Us. I can name common animals and say what they need. Amina learns that every animal needs feed, water, and shelter each day. Keywords: animal: a living thing that moves; goat: a small farm animal with horns; cow: a big farm animal that gives milk; hen: a bird that lays eggs; insect: a tiny creature with six legs; feed: food given to animals; shelter: a safe place to stay
chunks.source: Amina learns that every animal needs feed, water, and shelter each day.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is an **animal**? A: A living thing that moves and breathes.
chunks.source: A living thing that moves and breathes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two animals Amina sees. A: Goat and cow.
chunks.source: Goat and cow.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does a **cow** give us? A: Milk.
chunks.source: Milk.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do animals need **shelter**? A: To stay safe from rain and sun.
chunks.source: To stay safe from rain and sun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how Amina cares for the animals. A: She gives them feed, water, and shelter every day.
chunks.source: She gives them feed, water, and shelter every day.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which **insect** might you see in the garden? A: A butterfly or ant.
chunks.source: A butterfly or ant.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Plants Are Living Things. I can name parts of a plant and say what it needs to grow. A plant needs water, soil, and sun to grow and make leaves. Keywords: plant: a living thing that grows in soil; grow: to get bigger; leaf: the green part that makes food; seed: the small start of a plant; water: liquid that plants drink; soil: the earth where plants grow; sun: the bright star that gives light
chunks.source: A plant needs water, soil, and sun to grow and make leaves.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a **plant**? A: A living thing that grows in soil.
chunks.source: A living thing that grows in soil.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name three things a **plant** needs. A: Water, soil, and sun.
chunks.source: Water, soil, and sun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does a **seed** become? A: A new plant.
chunks.source: A new plant.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is the **leaf** important? A: It makes food using sun.
chunks.source: It makes food using sun.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how Kato helps the plant grow. A: He waters it, checks the soil, and lets the sun shine on it.
chunks.source: He waters it, checks the soil, and lets the sun shine on it.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What happens if a plant gets no **water**? A: It may dry up and die.
chunks.source: It may dry up and die.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Caring for Living Things. I can list daily care actions for animals and plants. Daily care means giving feed, water, shelter, and love to every living thing. Keywords: shelter: a safe place to stay; feed: food given to animals; water: liquid for drinking; food: what living things eat; home: a place where someone lives; care: looking after with kindness; daily: every day
chunks.source: Daily care means giving feed, water, shelter, and love to every living thing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **shelter** mean? A: A safe place to stay.
chunks.source: A safe place to stay.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two things animals need every day. A: Feed and water.
chunks.source: Feed and water.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is a **home** important for a hen? A: It keeps her warm and safe.
chunks.source: It keeps her warm and safe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **care** mean? A: Looking after something with love.
chunks.source: Looking after something with love.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how Nalongo cares for the animals daily. A: She gives them feed, water, and checks their shelter each day.
chunks.source: She gives them feed, water, and checks their shelter each day.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What could happen if Nalongo forgets to give water? A: The animals may get thirsty and sick.
chunks.source: The animals may get thirsty and sick.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Parts of a Plant. I can name the main parts of a plant. A plant has six main parts: **seed**, **root**, **stem**, **leaf**, **flower**, and **fruit**. Each part has a special job to help the plant live and grow. Keywords: seed: the small start of a new plant; stem: the part that holds the plant up; root: the part under the soil that drinks water; leaf: the green part that makes food from sun; flower: the bright part that makes seeds; fruit: the part that holds seeds after the flower
chunks.source: A plant has six main parts: **seed**, **root**, **stem**, **leaf**, **flower**, and **fruit**. Each part has a special job to help the plant live and grow.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which part takes water from the soil? A: The **root** takes water from the soil.
chunks.source: The **root** takes water from the soil.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which part carries water up the plant? A: The **stem** carries water up the plant.
chunks.source: The **stem** carries water up the plant.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which part catches sunlight to make food? A: The **leaf** catches sunlight to make food.
chunks.source: The **leaf** catches sunlight to make food.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which part grows into a **fruit** with seeds? A: The **flower** grows into a **fruit** with seeds.
chunks.source: The **flower** grows into a **fruit** with seeds.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what the **stem** does. A: The **stem** holds the plant up and moves water from the **root** to the **leaf** and **flower**.
chunks.source: The **stem** holds the plant up and moves water from the **root** to the **leaf** and **flower**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name all six parts of a plant you learned today. A: **seed**, **root**, **stem**, **leaf**, **flower**, **fruit**
chunks.source: **seed**, **root**, **stem**, **leaf**, **flower**, **fruit**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Plants We Eat. I can name food plants and say if they are fruit or vegetable. **Mango** and **banana** are **fruit** because they hold seeds. **Maize** grains are seeds. **Bean** seeds are a **vegetable** **food**. All give us energy to grow. Keywords: mango: a sweet yellow fruit with a big seed; banana: a long curved fruit that grows in bunches; maize: a tall plant with yellow grains on a cob; bean: a seed that grows in a pod, eaten as food; fruit: the sweet part of a plant that holds seeds; vegetable: a plant part we eat that is not sweet fruit; food: anything we eat to give us energy
chunks.source: **Mango** and **banana** are **fruit** because they hold seeds. **Maize** grains are seeds. **Bean** seeds are a **vegetable** **food**. All give us energy to grow.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which of these is a **fruit** with a big **seed**? A: **mango** is a **fruit** with a big **seed**.
chunks.source: **mango** is a **fruit** with a big **seed**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Is a **banana** a **fruit** or a **vegetable**? A: A **banana** is a **fruit** because it has tiny seeds inside.
chunks.source: A **banana** is a **fruit** because it has tiny seeds inside.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What **food** do we get from the **maize** cob? A: We get yellow grains from the **maize** cob to make posho.
chunks.source: We get yellow grains from the **maize** cob to make posho.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is a **bean** called a **vegetable**? A: We eat the **bean** seed, not the sweet **fruit** pod, so it is a **vegetable** **food**.
chunks.source: We eat the **bean** seed, not the sweet **fruit** pod, so it is a **vegetable** **food**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words the difference between a **fruit** and a **vegetable**. A: A **fruit** is the sweet part of a plant that holds seeds. A **vegetable** is any other plant part we eat, like seeds, leaves, or roots.
chunks.source: A **fruit** is the sweet part of a plant that holds seeds. A **vegetable** is any other plant part we eat, like seeds, leaves, or roots.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: List four plants we eat from the lesson. A: **mango**, **banana**, **maize**, **bean**
chunks.source: **mango**, **banana**, **maize**, **bean**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Plants Around Our School. I can name plants in our school **habitat** and say how they help us. Our school **habitat** has many **plant** friends: **tree** for **shade**, **grass** for ground cover, **flower** for bees, and **leaf** for food making. Each **plant** helps the **habitat** stay healthy. Keywords: habitat: the natural home where a plant or animal lives; tree: a tall plant with a woody **stem** and branches; shade: cool dark place under a plant out of the sun; flower: the bright part of a plant that makes seeds; grass: short green plants that cover the ground; plant: any living thing that grows in soil and makes food; leaf: the green part of a plant that catches sun
chunks.source: Our school **habitat** has many **plant** friends: **tree** for **shade**, **grass** for ground cover, **flower** for bees, and **leaf** for food making. Each **plant** helps the **habitat** stay healthy.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a **habitat**? A: A **habitat** is the natural home where a **plant** or animal lives.
chunks.source: A **habitat** is the natural home where a **plant** or animal lives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does a **tree** give us at school? A: A **tree** gives **shade**, clean air, and holds soil with its **root**.
chunks.source: A **tree** gives **shade**, clean air, and holds soil with its **root**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is **grass** good for the playing field? A: **Grass** covers the soil, keeps it cool, and makes a soft field.
chunks.source: **Grass** covers the soil, keeps it cool, and makes a soft field.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do **flower** and bees do together? A: **Flower** brings bees. Bees help the **plant** make seeds.
chunks.source: **Flower** brings bees. Bees help the **plant** make seeds.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why every **plant** in the school **habitat** matters. A: Every **plant** has a job: **tree** gives **shade** and air, **grass** covers ground, **flower** feeds bees, **leaf** makes food.
chunks.source: Every **plant** has a job: **tree** gives **shade** and air, **grass** covers ground, **flower** feeds bees, **leaf** makes food.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name five **plant** things you see in your school **habitat**. A: **tree**, **grass**, **flower**, **leaf**, **shade**
chunks.source: **tree**, **grass**, **flower**, **leaf**, **shade**

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Money and Prices. I can explain price, budget, and money at the market. Mother uses a budget to plan spending at the market. Knowing prices helps us buy what we need with the money we have. Keywords: money: coins and notes we use to pay; price: cost of something in shillings; shillings: Ugandan money units; budget: plan for how to spend money; buy: give money to get something; sell: give something to get money; market: place where people buy and sell
chunks.source: Mother uses a budget to plan spending at the market. Knowing prices helps us buy what we need with the money we have.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a **budget**? A: A plan for how to spend money.
chunks.source: A plan for how to spend money.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If rice costs 3,000 **shillings** and beans cost 2,000 **shillings**, how much do they cost together? A: 5,000 shillings.
chunks.source: 5,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Nalongo wants to **sell** her eggs. What does **sell** mean? A: Give something to get money.
chunks.source: Give something to get money.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Mother has 10,000 **shillings**. She spends 5,000 **shillings**. How much **money** is left? A: 5,000 shillings.
chunks.source: 5,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: In your own words, why do we need to know the **price** before we **buy**? A: Knowing the price helps us plan our budget and not spend too much money.
chunks.source: Knowing the price helps us plan our budget and not spend too much money.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write one thing you would **buy** at the **market** with 1,000 **shillings**. A: I would buy a mango or a small heap of tomatoes.
chunks.source: I would buy a mango or a small heap of tomatoes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Saving Resources. I can tell the difference between needs and wants and choose to save. Kato learns to save money for needs like a school bag. He keeps money safe and does not waste it on wants like sweets. Keywords: save: keep money for later; spend: use money to buy things; waste: use carelessly and lose; keep: hold something safe; need: something you must have; want: something you like but can live without; money: coins and notes we use to pay
chunks.source: Kato learns to save money for needs like a school bag. He keeps money safe and does not waste it on wants like sweets.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **save** mean? A: Keep money for later.
chunks.source: Keep money for later.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If you **waste** water, what happens? A: It is gone and you have less.
chunks.source: It is gone and you have less.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name one **need** and one **want**. A: Need: food. Want: toy.
chunks.source: Need: food. Want: toy.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why should we **keep** **money** safe? A: So it is not lost or stolen.
chunks.source: So it is not lost or stolen.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: In your own words, why is it better to **save** for a **need** than **spend** on a **want**? A: Saving for a need helps you get important things. Spending on wants uses up money fast.
chunks.source: Saving for a need helps you get important things. Spending on wants uses up money fast.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Draw a box where you can **keep** your savings. Say what you **save** for. A: A tin box. I save for a school bag.
chunks.source: A tin box. I save for a school bag.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Using Water Well. I can describe ways to save water and keep it clean for the future. We must use water carefully, keep it clean, and save it for the future. Sharing and fixing leaks means enough water for all. Keywords: water: liquid we drink and use; share: give part to others; clean: free from dirt; future: time that will come; use: do something with; enough: as much as needed; save: keep for later, not waste
chunks.source: We must use water carefully, keep it clean, and save it for the future. Sharing and fixing leaks means enough water for all.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **clean** **water** mean? A: Water free from dirt and germs.
chunks.source: Water free from dirt and germs.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why do we **save** **water** for the **future**? A: So there is enough for everyone later.
chunks.source: So there is enough for everyone later.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two ways to **use** less **water** at home. A: Use a cup for bathing. Fix leaky taps.
chunks.source: Use a cup for bathing. Fix leaky taps.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If we **share** one jerrycan, how do we know each gets **enough**? A: We use a cup to measure.
chunks.source: We use a cup to measure.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: In your own words, what happens if we **waste** **water** today? A: Wasting water means less for tomorrow. The future may not have enough clean water.
chunks.source: Wasting water means less for tomorrow. The future may not have enough clean water.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Draw a poster showing how to **save** **water**. Write one tip. A: Fix leaks. Use a cup. Share fairly.
chunks.source: Fix leaks. Use a cup. Share fairly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Living in Harmony. I can use polite words, share, and forgive to keep peace and harmony with friends. Amina shows that polite words, sharing, and forgiving bring harmony and peace to the village. Keywords: harmony: living together peacefully; forgive: stop being angry; share: give part to others; polite: show good manners; peace: no fighting; friend: a person you like
chunks.source: Amina shows that polite words, sharing, and forgiving bring harmony and peace to the village.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **harmony** mean? A: Living together without fighting.
chunks.source: Living together without fighting.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the polite word: 'Please' or 'Give me'. A: Please
chunks.source: Please

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If you **share** your mango, what do you do? A: Give some to a friend.
chunks.source: Give some to a friend.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How can you **forgive** a friend who took your pen? A: Say it is okay and stay friends.
chunks.source: Say it is okay and stay friends.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what **peace** means in your village. A: Peace means no fighting and everyone helps each other.
chunks.source: Peace means no fighting and everyone helps each other.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does a **friend** do when you are sad? A: A friend listens and helps.
chunks.source: A friend listens and helps.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Saying Sorry and Forgiving. I can say sorry, forgive, request, be kind, help, and stay together with friends. Peter and Musa show that saying sorry, forgiving, and helping each other keeps them together. Keywords: sorry: feeling regret; forgive: let go of anger; request: ask politely; kind: caring and gentle; help: give assistance; together: in a group
chunks.source: Peter and Musa show that saying sorry, forgiving, and helping each other keeps them together.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **sorry** mean? A: Feeling bad for a mistake.
chunks.source: Feeling bad for a mistake.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the kind action: share a sweet or push a friend. A: Share a sweet.
chunks.source: Share a sweet.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If you **request** a book, what do you do? A: Ask politely for it.
chunks.source: Ask politely for it.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How can you **forgive** someone who broke your toy? A: Tell them it is okay and stay friends.
chunks.source: Tell them it is okay and stay friends.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what **together** means when playing. A: Together means playing side by side and helping each other.
chunks.source: Together means playing side by side and helping each other.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **help** look like at home? A: Helping mother carry water.
chunks.source: Helping mother carry water.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Children's Rights and Needs. I can name my rights and needs and show respect, protection, care, and safety. Teacher Nankya teaches that every child has rights, needs, and deserves respect, protection, care, and safety. Keywords: child rights: rights every child has; needs: things a child must have; respect: treating others well; protection: keeping safe from harm; care: looking after someone; safe: free from danger
chunks.source: Teacher Nankya teaches that every child has rights, needs, and deserves respect, protection, care, and safety.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What are **child rights**? A: Rights every child has, like education and safety.
chunks.source: Rights every child has, like education and safety.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name one **need** a child has. A: Food, water, or school.
chunks.source: Food, water, or school.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How do you show **respect** to a teacher? A: Listen and follow instructions.
chunks.source: Listen and follow instructions.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does **protection** mean for a child? A: Being kept safe from harm.
chunks.source: Being kept safe from harm.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why **care** is important. A: Care means adults look after children so they grow well.
chunks.source: Care means adults look after children so they grow well.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What makes a place **safe** for children? A: No danger, clean water, and kind adults.
chunks.source: No danger, clean water, and kind adults.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Our Culture. I can name parts of my culture and explain why they matter. The festival showed the village **culture** through **custom**, **tradition**, **rites**, **values**, and **events**. Keywords: culture: the way a group of people live; custom: a special way people do things; tradition: a practice passed down from older people; rites: special ceremonies that honor beliefs; values: important beliefs that guide behaviour; events: planned happenings like festivals or meetings
chunks.source: The festival showed the village **culture** through **custom**, **tradition**, **rites**, **values**, and **events**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is **culture**? A: Culture is the way a group of people live, including their customs and traditions.
chunks.source: Culture is the way a group of people live, including their customs and traditions.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of a **custom** from the story. A: Dancing at the festival is a custom.
chunks.source: Dancing at the festival is a custom.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why are **values** important? A: Values guide how people treat each other.
chunks.source: Values guide how people treat each other.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Name two **events** at the festival. A: Dancing and storytelling are events.
