chunks.text: Q: **Skip count** by **thousands** from 1000 to 5000. Write the numbers. A: 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: What is the **pattern** when you **skip count** by **hundreds**? A: Each number ends with two zeros. The hundreds digit increases by 1.
chunks.source: Each number ends with two zeros. The hundreds digit increases by 1.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: Fill the missing numbers: 3000, __, 5000, __, 7000. A: 4000, 6000. **Skip count** by **thousands** adds 1000.
chunks.source: 4000, 6000. **Skip count** by **thousands** adds 1000.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: In your own words, how are **hundreds** and **thousands** **pattern**s different? (Model: **Hundreds** end with two zeros, **thousands** end with three zeros. Both increase by 1 in their place value.) A: **Hundreds** end with two zeros (100, 200). **Thousands** end with three zeros (1000, 2000). Both go up by 1 in the front digit.
chunks.source: **Hundreds** end with two zeros (100, 200). **Thousands** end with three zeros (1000, 2000). Both go up by 1 in the front digit.

chunks.subject: Math
chunks.text: Q: A lorry carries 1000 bricks per trip. It makes 4 trips. How many bricks total? Use **skip count** by **thousands**. A: 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000. Total 4000 bricks.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Living Things Around Our Home. I can name living things around my home. Living things around our home include hens, goats, trees, and grass. They all breathe, eat, and grow. Keywords: hen: a bird that lays eggs; goat: an animal that gives milk; tree: a tall plant with a trunk; grass: green plants that cover the ground; living: something that breathes, eats, and grows
chunks.source: Living things around our home include hens, goats, trees, and grass. They all breathe, eat, and grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a living thing? A: A living thing breathes, eats, and grows.
chunks.source: A living thing breathes, eats, and grows.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two living things Amina sees. A: Hen and goat.
chunks.source: Hen and goat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Is a stone living? A: No, a stone does not breathe or grow.
chunks.source: No, a stone does not breathe or grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does the hen give us? A: Eggs.
chunks.source: Eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does the goat eat? A: Grass.
chunks.source: Grass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why a tree is living. A: A tree is living because it grows, makes food from sunlight, and breathes.
chunks.source: A tree is living because it grows, makes food from sunlight, and breathes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Non-Living Things and Materials. I can identify materials that make non‑living things. Non‑living things are made of materials like wood, metal, plastic, and glass. Keywords: wood: hard material from trees; metal: strong shiny material; plastic: light material made in factories; glass: clear material that breaks easily; material: what things are made of
chunks.source: Non‑living things are made of materials like wood, metal, plastic, and glass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a material? A: A material is what things are made of.
chunks.source: A material is what things are made of.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two materials from the lesson. A: Wood and metal.
chunks.source: Wood and metal.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Is water a material? A: No, water is a liquid.
chunks.source: No, water is a liquid.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What material is a window made of? A: Glass.
chunks.source: Glass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What material is a jerrycan made of? A: Plastic.
chunks.source: Plastic.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why metal is useful for a roof. A: Metal is strong and does not rot, so it keeps rain out.
chunks.source: Metal is strong and does not rot, so it keeps rain out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Sanitation at Home. I can keep my home clean and healthy. Good sanitation uses a latrine, dustbin, and rubbish pit to keep germs away and the home clean. Keywords: latrine: a toilet outside the house; dustbin: a bin for rubbish; rubbish pit: a hole for burning or burying rubbish; clean: free from dirt and germs; germs: tiny things that make us sick
chunks.source: Good sanitation uses a latrine, dustbin, and rubbish pit to keep germs away and the home clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we wash hands? A: To remove germs.
chunks.source: To remove germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do we put rubbish? A: In the rubbish pit or dustbin.
chunks.source: In the rubbish pit or dustbin.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a latrine for? A: For human waste.
chunks.source: For human waste.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens if we leave rubbish on the ground? A: Germs and flies come.
chunks.source: Germs and flies come.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two ways to keep home clean. A: Sweep and wash hands.
chunks.source: Sweep and wash hands.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why covering the dustbin stops germs. A: Covering the dustbin keeps flies and germs away from food.
chunks.source: Covering the dustbin keeps flies and germs away from food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Physical Features Around Us. I can name and describe the main physical features in our sub-county. Our sub-county has hills, valleys, rivers, swamps, and plains. Each feature gives us water, land, or resources we use every day. Keywords: hill: high land that rises up; valley: low land between hills; river: water that flows in a channel; swamp: wet land with water plants; plain: flat land that spreads wide
chunks.source: Our sub-county has hills, valleys, rivers, swamps, and plains. Each feature gives us water, land, or resources we use every day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one physical feature you see near your home. A: hill or valley or river or swamp or plain
chunks.source: hill or valley or river or swamp or plain

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What feature gives us water for drinking? A: river
chunks.source: river

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which feature is low land between hills? A: valley
chunks.source: valley

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is a swamp useful? A: It holds water and stops floods.
chunks.source: It holds water and stops floods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words the difference between a hill and a plain. A: A hill is high land that rises up. A plain is flat land that spreads wide.
chunks.source: A hill is high land that rises up. A plain is flat land that spreads wide.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Animals in Our Sub-County. I can name common animals in our area and say if they are wild or not. Our sub-county has wild animals like lizards, frogs, snakes, and birds. They live free and help nature. We watch them but do not harm them. Keywords: lizard: small reptile with four legs; frog: small animal that jumps and swims; snake: long reptile with no legs; bird: animal with feathers and wings; wild: living free in nature, not kept by people
chunks.source: Our sub-county has wild animals like lizards, frogs, snakes, and birds. They live free and help nature. We watch them but do not harm them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two wild animals you see at school. A: lizard, frog, snake, or bird
chunks.source: lizard, frog, snake, or bird

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which animal eats mosquitoes? A: frog
chunks.source: frog

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does 'wild' mean? A: Living free in nature, not kept by people.
chunks.source: Living free in nature, not kept by people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What should you do if you see a snake? A: Stand still and let it go away.
chunks.source: Stand still and let it go away.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why we should not kill frogs. A: Frogs eat mosquitoes which cause malaria. They help keep us healthy.
chunks.source: Frogs eat mosquitoes which cause malaria. They help keep us healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Plants in Our Sub-County. I can name common plants and say which are crops and which are wild. Our sub-county has palms, eucalyptus, mangoes, and many crops like maize. Crops are planted by people. Wild plants grow naturally. Both are important. Keywords: palm: tall tree with fan leaves; eucalyptus: tall tree with peeling bark; mango: fruit tree with sweet yellow fruit; crop: plant grown by people for food or sale; wild: growing naturally without people planting it
chunks.source: Our sub-county has palms, eucalyptus, mangoes, and many crops like maize. Crops are planted by people. Wild plants grow naturally. Both are important.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one tree that gives sweet fruit. A: mango
chunks.source: mango

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which tree grows fast for poles? A: eucalyptus
chunks.source: eucalyptus

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a crop? A: A plant grown by people for food or sale.
chunks.source: A plant grown by people for food or sale.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of a wild plant. A: Wild grass or wild flowers.
chunks.source: Wild grass or wild flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words the difference between a crop and a wild plant. A: A crop is planted and cared for by people. A wild plant grows on its own without people planting it.
chunks.source: A crop is planted and cared for by people. A wild plant grows on its own without people planting it.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Crop Farming. I can name crops grown for food and income. Amina learns that cassava, sweet potato, and groundnuts are grown for food and income. Farmers dig soil, wait, then harvest. Keywords: cassava: a root crop for food; sweet potato: a sweet root crop; groundnuts: nuts that grow underground; harvest: gather ripe crops; dig: turn soil with a hoe
chunks.source: Amina learns that cassava, sweet potato, and groundnuts are grown for food and income. Farmers dig soil, wait, then harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What crop grows under the ground? A: Cassava and groundnuts grow under the ground.
chunks.source: Cassava and groundnuts grow under the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do farmers dig the soil? A: To make it soft for roots to grow.
chunks.source: To make it soft for roots to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two crops Amina saw. A: Cassava and sweet potato.
chunks.source: Cassava and sweet potato.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does harvest mean? A: Gathering ripe crops from the garden.
chunks.source: Gathering ripe crops from the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why crop farming is important. A: Crop farming gives food to eat and money when sold at market.
chunks.source: Crop farming gives food to eat and money when sold at market.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where does the family sell groundnuts? A: At the market.
chunks.source: At the market.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Keeping Animals for a Living. I can name animals kept for a living and their products. Peter learns that cattle, goats, and poultry graze for food and give milk, eggs, and meat for income. Keywords: cattle: cows kept for milk; goats: small animals for meat; poultry: chickens kept for eggs; graze: eat grass in the field; milk: white drink from cows
chunks.source: Peter learns that cattle, goats, and poultry graze for food and give milk, eggs, and meat for income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do cattle eat? A: Cattle graze on grass.
chunks.source: Cattle graze on grass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two products from poultry. A: Eggs and meat.
chunks.source: Eggs and meat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do goats graze on bushes? A: To get food and stay healthy.
chunks.source: To get food and stay healthy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is milk used for? A: Milk is drunk or sold for income.
chunks.source: Milk is drunk or sold for income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how animals help a family. A: Animals give milk, eggs, and meat for food and to sell for money.
chunks.source: Animals give milk, eggs, and meat for food and to sell for money.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do cattle graze? A: On fresh grass in the field.
chunks.source: On fresh grass in the field.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Fishing and Other Work. I can describe fishing and trade at the market. Musa learns that fish from the lake are caught with nets, then traded at the market for income. Keywords: fish: animal that lives in water; lake: big water body; net: tool to catch fish; trade: buy and sell goods; market: place to buy and sell
chunks.source: Musa learns that fish from the lake are caught with nets, then traded at the market for income.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where are fish caught? A: Fish are caught in the lake.
chunks.source: Fish are caught in the lake.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What tool catches fish? A: A net catches fish.
chunks.source: A net catches fish.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where are fish sold? A: Fish are sold at the market.
chunks.source: Fish are sold at the market.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does trade mean? A: Trade means buying and selling goods.
chunks.source: Trade means buying and selling goods.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how fish reach the market. A: Fishermen catch fish with nets, traders buy them, and take them to market to sell.
chunks.source: Fishermen catch fish with nets, traders buy them, and take them to market to sell.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two jobs at the landing site. A: Fisherman and trader.
chunks.source: Fisherman and trader.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Parts of Our Environment. I can name the five main parts of the environment. The environment has five main parts: **soil**, **water**, **air**, **plants**, and **animals**. They all depend on each other. Keywords: soil: the top layer of ground where plants grow; water: clear liquid that falls as rain and flows in streams; air: the invisible gas around us that we breathe; plants: green living things like trees, grass, and crops; animals: living creatures such as birds, goats, and insects
chunks.source: The environment has five main parts: **soil**, **water**, **air**, **plants**, and **animals**. They all depend on each other.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the five parts of the environment. A: The five parts are **soil**, **water**, **air**, **plants**, and **animals**.
chunks.source: The five parts are **soil**, **water**, **air**, **plants**, and **animals**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do **plants** need from the **air**? A: **Plants** need **air** to make food.
chunks.source: **Plants** need **air** to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is **water** important for **animals**? A: **Animals** drink **water** to stay alive.
chunks.source: **Animals** drink **water** to stay alive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you keep **soil** healthy? A: Plant trees, pick up litter, and avoid wasting **water**.
chunks.source: Plant trees, pick up litter, and avoid wasting **water**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why all five parts are needed. A: All five parts work together; without one, living things cannot survive.
chunks.source: All five parts work together; without one, living things cannot survive.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part do you see most at home? A: Answers vary; for example, I see **soil** in the garden.
chunks.source: Answers vary; for example, I see **soil** in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: How People Spoil the Environment. I can describe ways people damage the environment. People spoil the environment by making **pollution**, dropping **litter**, creating **smoke**, **cutting trees**, and leaving places **dirty**. Keywords: pollution: harmful substances that make air, water, or land dirty; litter: rubbish thrown on the ground; smoke: grey gas from burning things; cutting trees: removing trees from the land; dirty: not clean, covered in dust or waste
chunks.source: People spoil the environment by making **pollution**, dropping **litter**, creating **smoke**, **cutting trees**, and leaving places **dirty**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name three activities that spoil the environment. A: **Litter**, **smoke**, and **cutting trees** are three examples.
chunks.source: **Litter**, **smoke**, and **cutting trees** are three examples.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does **pollution** do to the **air**? A: **Pollution** makes the **air** harmful to breathe.
chunks.source: **Pollution** makes the **air** harmful to breathe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is **cutting trees** bad for the **soil**? A: Without trees, rain and wind wash or blow away the **soil**.
chunks.source: Without trees, rain and wind wash or blow away the **soil**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can you keep your compound clean? A: Collect **litter**, use a bin, and avoid burning waste.
chunks.source: Collect **litter**, use a bin, and avoid burning waste.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why **smoke** is a problem. A: **Smoke** adds bad gases to the **air**, causing **pollution** and health problems.
chunks.source: **Smoke** adds bad gases to the **air**, causing **pollution** and health problems.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which bad habit do you see most in your village? A: Answers vary; for example, I see a lot of **litter** near the market.
chunks.source: Answers vary; for example, I see a lot of **litter** near the market.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Caring for Our Environment. I can list ways to care for the environment. We care for our environment by **plant**ing, **recycle**ing, **clean**ing, **protect**ing, and looking after every **tree**. Keywords: plant: put a seed or seedling in the ground to grow; recycle: use old things again in a new way; clean: make something free from dirt or waste; protect: keep safe from harm; tree: a tall woody plant with a trunk
chunks.source: We care for our environment by **plant**ing, **recycle**ing, **clean**ing, **protect**ing, and looking after every **tree**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List three ways to care for the environment. A: **Plant** trees, **recycle** waste, and **clean** your compound.
chunks.source: **Plant** trees, **recycle** waste, and **clean** your compound.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does **recycle** mean? A: **Recycle** means using old things again in a new way.
chunks.source: **Recycle** means using old things again in a new way.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should we **protect** a water source? A: To keep **water** clean and safe for drinking.
chunks.source: To keep **water** clean and safe for drinking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a **tree** help the **air**? A: A **tree** takes in bad gases and gives out fresh **air**.
chunks.source: A **tree** takes in bad gases and gives out fresh **air**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why **clean**ing is important. A: **Clean**ing removes **litter** and stops **pollution** from spreading.
chunks.source: **Clean**ing removes **litter** and stops **pollution** from spreading.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which caring action do you like most? A: Answers vary; for example, I like to **plant** flowers.
chunks.source: Answers vary; for example, I like to **plant** flowers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Elements of Weather. I can name the five elements of weather and say what each means. Weather has five main elements: sunshine, rainfall, wind, temperature, and cloud. Keywords: sunshine: light and heat from the sun; rainfall: water that falls from clouds; wind: moving air; temperature: how hot or cold the air is; cloud: white or grey mass in the sky
chunks.source: Weather has five main elements: sunshine, rainfall, wind, temperature, and cloud.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the five elements of weather. A: sunshine, rainfall, wind, temperature, cloud
chunks.source: sunshine, rainfall, wind, temperature, cloud

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does temperature tell us? A: It tells how hot or cold the air is.
chunks.source: It tells how hot or cold the air is.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which element is moving air? A: Wind is moving air.
chunks.source: Wind is moving air.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do we call water falling from the sky? A: Rainfall.
chunks.source: Rainfall.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what a cloud is. A: A cloud is a mass of tiny water droplets in the sky.
chunks.source: A cloud is a mass of tiny water droplets in the sky.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: If the sky is dark and wet, which element are you seeing? A: Rainfall and cloud.
chunks.source: Rainfall and cloud.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Seasons in Uganda. I can name the two main seasons in Uganda and say what people do in each. Uganda has a wet season for planting and a dry season for harvest. Keywords: wet season: time of heavy rain; dry season: time with little rain; planting: putting seeds in the soil; harvest: gathering ripe crops; rain: water falling from clouds
chunks.source: Uganda has a wet season for planting and a dry season for harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the two main seasons in Uganda. A: wet season and dry season
chunks.source: wet season and dry season

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do farmers do in the wet season? A: They do planting of crops.
chunks.source: They do planting of crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens in the dry season? A: Crops are harvested.
chunks.source: Crops are harvested.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which season has a lot of rain? A: The wet season has a lot of rain.
chunks.source: The wet season has a lot of rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why planting is done in the wet season. A: Because the soil is wet and seeds need water to grow.
chunks.source: Because the soil is wet and seeds need water to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: If you see maize being cut, which season is it? A: It is the dry season, time for harvest.
chunks.source: It is the dry season, time for harvest.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: How Weather Affects Us. I can explain how weather changes farming, clothes, travel, and can cause flood or drought. Weather affects farming, clothes, travel, and can cause flood or drought. Keywords: farming: growing crops and raising animals; clothes: things we wear; travel: moving from one place to another; flood: too much water covering land; drought: long time with little or no rain
chunks.source: Weather affects farming, clothes, travel, and can cause flood or drought.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does rain help farming? A: Rain gives water for crops to grow.
chunks.source: Rain gives water for crops to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What problem can too much rain cause? A: Too much rain can cause a flood.
chunks.source: Too much rain can cause a flood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a drought? A: A drought is a long time with little or no rain.
chunks.source: A drought is a long time with little or no rain.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we change clothes with the weather? A: We wear light clothes when hot and warm clothes when cold.
chunks.source: We wear light clothes when hot and warm clothes when cold.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how a flood can stop travel. A: A flood covers roads and bridges, so vehicles cannot pass.
chunks.source: A flood covers roads and bridges, so vehicles cannot pass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: If there is no rain for many weeks, what may happen to crops? A: Crops may dry up and die because of drought.
chunks.source: Crops may dry up and die because of drought.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Groups of Animals. I can name the five main groups of animals. The five main animal groups are mammals, birds, insects, fish, and reptiles. Keywords: mammals: animals that have hair and give milk; birds: animals with feathers that lay eggs; insects: small animals with six legs; fish: animals that live in water and have gills; reptiles: animals with dry scales
chunks.source: The five main animal groups are mammals, birds, insects, fish, and reptiles.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the five animal groups. A: mammals, birds, insects, fish, reptiles
chunks.source: mammals, birds, insects, fish, reptiles

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which group has feathers? A: birds
chunks.source: birds

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which group lives in water and has gills? A: fish
chunks.source: fish

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which group has six legs? A: insects
chunks.source: insects

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which group has dry scales? A: reptiles
chunks.source: reptiles

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what makes a mammal different from a bird. A: Mammals have hair and give milk, while birds have feathers and lay eggs.
chunks.source: Mammals have hair and give milk, while birds have feathers and lay eggs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Groups of Plants. I can name the main groups of plants. The main plant groups are flowering, non-flowering, crop, tree, and grass. Keywords: flowering: plants that make flowers and seeds; non-flowering: plants that do not make flowers; crop: plants grown for food; tree: tall plants with a trunk; grass: short plants that cover the ground
chunks.source: The main plant groups are flowering, non-flowering, crop, tree, and grass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name the five plant groups. A: flowering, non-flowering, crop, tree, grass
chunks.source: flowering, non-flowering, crop, tree, grass

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which group makes flowers? A: flowering
chunks.source: flowering

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which group does not make flowers? A: non-flowering
chunks.source: non-flowering

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which group gives us maize? A: crop
chunks.source: crop

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which group grows tall and gives shade? A: tree
chunks.source: tree

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words the difference between a crop and a tree. A: A crop is planted for food like maize, while a tree grows tall and gives fruit or wood.
chunks.source: A crop is planted for food like maize, while a tree grows tall and gives fruit or wood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: What Living Things Need. I can list the basic needs of living things. All living things need food, water, air, shelter, and the chance to grow. Keywords: food: something that gives energy; water: liquid needed for life; air: invisible gas we breathe; shelter: a safe place to stay; grow: to become bigger and stronger
chunks.source: All living things need food, water, air, shelter, and the chance to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: List the five basic needs of living things. A: food, water, air, shelter, grow
chunks.source: food, water, air, shelter, grow

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which need helps plants make food? A: air
chunks.source: air

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which need keeps a baby goat safe from rain? A: shelter
chunks.source: shelter

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What do animals get from eating plants? A: food
chunks.source: food

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do living things need water? A: to stay hydrated and move nutrients
chunks.source: to stay hydrated and move nutrients

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why air is important for a plant. A: Air gives carbon dioxide which plants use with sunlight and water to make food.
chunks.source: Air gives carbon dioxide which plants use with sunlight and water to make food.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Parts of a Plant. I can name the parts of a plant and say what each part does. A plant has five main parts: **root**, **stem**, **leaf**, **flower**, and **fruit**. Each part has a special job to help the plant live and make new plants. Keywords: root: the part under the soil that holds the plant and takes in water; stem: the part that stands up and carries water to the leaves; leaf: the flat green part that makes food for the plant; flower: the bright part that makes seeds and fruit; fruit: the part that holds the seeds, often good to eat
chunks.source: A plant has five main parts: **root**, **stem**, **leaf**, **flower**, and **fruit**. Each part has a special job to help the plant live and make new plants.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part holds the plant in the soil? A: The **root** holds the plant in the soil.
chunks.source: The **root** holds the plant in the soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part carries water to the leaves? A: The **stem** carries water to the leaves.
chunks.source: The **stem** carries water to the leaves.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part makes food using sunlight? A: The **leaf** makes food using sunlight.
chunks.source: The **leaf** makes food using sunlight.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part makes seeds and fruit? A: The **flower** makes seeds and fruit.
chunks.source: The **flower** makes seeds and fruit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which part holds the seeds? A: The **fruit** holds the seeds.
chunks.source: The **fruit** holds the seeds.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what the **stem** does. A: The **stem** stands up and carries water from the **root** to the **leaf**.
chunks.source: The **stem** stands up and carries water from the **root** to the **leaf**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Plants We Eat. I can name vegetables we eat and say which part of the plant we eat. We eat different parts of plants: **cabbage** (**leaf**), **tomato** (**fruit**), **onion** (**stem**), **pumpkin** (**fruit** and **leaf**). Knowing the part helps us understand the plant. Keywords: cabbage: a vegetable with many layers of leaves we eat; tomato: a red fruit we eat as a vegetable; onion: a round vegetable with a strong smell; pumpkin: a big orange vegetable that grows on a vine; leaf: the flat green part of a plant, some we eat as vegetables
chunks.source: We eat different parts of plants: **cabbage** (**leaf**), **tomato** (**fruit**), **onion** (**stem**), **pumpkin** (**fruit** and **leaf**). Knowing the part helps us understand the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which vegetable is made of many leaf layers? A: **Cabbage** is made of many **leaf** layers.
chunks.source: **Cabbage** is made of many **leaf** layers.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which vegetable is a red fruit we cook? A: **Tomato** is a red **fruit** we cook as a vegetable.
chunks.source: **Tomato** is a red **fruit** we cook as a vegetable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which vegetable grows under the soil like a swollen stem? A: **Onion** grows under the soil as a swollen **stem**.
chunks.source: **Onion** grows under the soil as a swollen **stem**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which big orange vegetable grows on a vine? A: **Pumpkin** is a big orange **fruit** that grows on a vine.
chunks.source: **Pumpkin** is a big orange **fruit** that grows on a vine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two vegetables we eat the leaf of. A: We eat the **leaf** of **cabbage** and **pumpkin** (or nakati).
chunks.source: We eat the **leaf** of **cabbage** and **pumpkin** (or nakati).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: is a tomato a fruit or a vegetable? A: A **tomato** is a **fruit** because it has seeds, but we cook it like a vegetable.
chunks.source: A **tomato** is a **fruit** because it has seeds, but we cook it like a vegetable.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Growing a Plant. I can explain how a seed grows into a plant. A **seed** needs **water** to **germinate**. Then it needs **water** and **sunlight** to **grow**. The **root** drinks, the **leaf** makes food, and the plant gets bigger until it makes new **seed**s. Keywords: seed: the small part of a plant that can grow into a new plant; germinate: when a seed wakes up and starts to grow; water: the liquid that helps seeds wake up and plants grow; sunlight: the light and heat from the sun that plants need; grow: to get bigger and change from a seed into a plant
chunks.source: A **seed** needs **water** to **germinate**. Then it needs **water** and **sunlight** to **grow**. The **root** drinks, the **leaf** makes food, and the plant gets bigger until it makes new **seed**s.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a seed? A: A **seed** is the small part of a plant that can grow into a new plant.
chunks.source: A **seed** is the small part of a plant that can grow into a new plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does 'germinate' mean? A: **Germinate** means when a **seed** wakes up and starts to grow.
chunks.source: **Germinate** means when a **seed** wakes up and starts to grow.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What two things does a seed need to germinate? A: A **seed** needs **water** and warm soil to **germinate**.
chunks.source: A **seed** needs **water** and warm soil to **germinate**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does the leaf need sunlight for? A: The **leaf** needs **sunlight** to make food for the plant.
chunks.source: The **leaf** needs **sunlight** to make food for the plant.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens after the plant grows flowers? A: After **flower**s, the plant makes **fruit** with new **seed**s inside.
chunks.source: After **flower**s, the plant makes **fruit** with new **seed**s inside.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how a seed becomes a plant. A: The **seed** gets **water** and **germinate**s. A **root** grows down, a **stem** grows up. The **leaf** catches **sunlight** to make food. The plant **grow**s bigger, makes **flower**s, then **fruit** with new **seed**s.
chunks.source: The **seed** gets **water** and **germinate**s. A **root** grows down, a **stem** grows up. The **leaf** catches **sunlight** to make food. The plant **grow**s bigger, makes **flower**s, then **fruit** with new **seed**s.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Resources Around Us. I can name natural resources in my sub-county. We learned that water, wood, soil, grass are natural resources we must use wisely. Keywords: water: clear liquid we drink; wood: hard material from trees; soil: brown earth where plants grow; grass: green plants that cover the ground; resource: something useful from nature
chunks.source: We learned that water, wood, soil, grass are natural resources we must use wisely.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a **resource**? A: A resource is something we get from nature like water or wood.
chunks.source: A resource is something we get from nature like water or wood.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two natural resources from the lesson. A: Water and wood are natural resources.
chunks.source: Water and wood are natural resources.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is **soil** important? A: Soil helps plants grow food for us.
chunks.source: Soil helps plants grow food for us.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How can we keep **water** clean? A: We can boil or filter water to make it clean.
chunks.source: We can boil or filter water to make it clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what **grass** is used for. A: Grass feeds animals and covers the ground.
chunks.source: Grass feeds animals and covers the ground.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does **wood** give us? A: Wood gives us firewood and material for building.
chunks.source: Wood gives us firewood and material for building.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Using Resources Wisely. I can explain how to save, reuse, and avoid waste of resources. We learned to save, reuse, and avoid waste so firewood and charcoal last for everyone. Keywords: save: keep something for later use; waste: throw away something useful; reuse: use something again; firewood: wood cut for burning; charcoal: black fuel made from wood
chunks.source: We learned to save, reuse, and avoid waste so firewood and charcoal last for everyone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does it mean to **save** a resource? A: To save a resource means to use less so it lasts longer.
chunks.source: To save a resource means to use less so it lasts longer.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of **reuse** at home. A: Using an old jar to keep beans is reuse.
chunks.source: Using an old jar to keep beans is reuse.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should we not **waste** firewood? A: Wasting firewood destroys forests and makes cooking harder.
chunks.source: Wasting firewood destroys forests and makes cooking harder.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is **charcoal** made? A: Charcoal is made by burning wood in a kiln.
chunks.source: Charcoal is made by burning wood in a kiln.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why we must **save** water. A: Saving water keeps the borehole from drying up.
chunks.source: Saving water keeps the borehole from drying up.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What can we do with ash from the fire? A: We can reuse ash to enrich garden soil.
chunks.source: We can reuse ash to enrich garden soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Keeping Water Safe. I can describe steps to make water safe for drinking. We learned to boil, filter, and cover water to keep it clean and safe. Keywords: boil: heat water until it bubbles; filter: pass water through a cloth to remove dirt; cover: put a lid on a container; contaminate: make dirty or unsafe; clean: free from dirt and germs
chunks.source: We learned to boil, filter, and cover water to keep it clean and safe.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we **boil** water before drinking? A: Boiling kills germs that can make us sick.
chunks.source: Boiling kills germs that can make us sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does **filter** mean? A: To filter means to pass water through a cloth or sand to remove dirt.
chunks.source: To filter means to pass water through a cloth or sand to remove dirt.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a **cover** keep water safe? A: A cover stops flies and dust from contaminating the water.
chunks.source: A cover stops flies and dust from contaminating the water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What can **contaminate** water? A: Dirt, flies, and germs can contaminate water.
chunks.source: Dirt, flies, and germs can contaminate water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how to make water **clean**. A: First filter, then boil, then cover the container.
chunks.source: First filter, then boil, then cover the container.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What should you do after boiling water? A: Cover the pot and let it cool before drinking.
chunks.source: Cover the pot and let it cool before drinking.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Living Safely Together. I can name ways to stay safe and get help in my community. We stay **safe** by spotting **danger** and telling an **adult**. Reporting helps **protect** our whole community. Keywords: safe: free from harm; report: tell an adult about a problem; danger: something that can hurt you; adult: a grown-up person; protect: keep someone safe from harm
chunks.source: We stay **safe** by spotting **danger** and telling an **adult**. Reporting helps **protect** our whole community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does the word **safe** mean? A: Free from harm or danger.
chunks.source: Free from harm or danger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: If you see a **danger**, what should you do? A: **Report** it to an **adult**.
chunks.source: **Report** it to an **adult**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who is an **adult**? A: A grown-up person like a teacher or parent.
chunks.source: A grown-up person like a teacher or parent.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a fence **protect** a garden? A: It keeps goats and cows out.
chunks.source: It keeps goats and cows out.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In your own words, why is it important to **report** a **danger**? A: So adults can fix it and keep everyone **safe**.
chunks.source: So adults can fix it and keep everyone **safe**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one **danger** you might see near a road. A: A deep hole, a broken wire, or a speeding boda boda.
chunks.source: A deep hole, a broken wire, or a speeding boda boda.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Common Dangers Around Us. I can identify five common dangers in my environment and say how to avoid them. Five common **danger**s are **deep water**, **fire**, **electricity**, **poison**, and missing **warning** signs. Knowing them keeps us **safe**. Keywords: deep water: water over your head; fire: hot flames that burn; electricity: power in wires; poison: something that makes you sick if eaten; warning: a sign that tells you to be careful
chunks.source: Five common **danger**s are **deep water**, **fire**, **electricity**, **poison**, and missing **warning** signs. Knowing them keeps us **safe**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is **deep water**? A: Water that is over your head.
chunks.source: Water that is over your head.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is **fire** a **danger**? A: It burns skin, clothes, and houses.
chunks.source: It burns skin, clothes, and houses.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What should you do if you see a fallen **electricity** wire? A: Stay away and tell an adult.
chunks.source: Stay away and tell an adult.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where should **poison** be kept? A: Locked up high, away from children.
chunks.source: Locked up high, away from children.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In your own words, what does a **warning** sign tell you? A: It tells you to be careful because there is a **danger**.
chunks.source: It tells you to be careful because there is a **danger**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two **danger**s found in the kitchen. A: **Fire** and **poison** (like kerosene or cleaning liquid).
chunks.source: **Fire** and **poison** (like kerosene or cleaning liquid).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: People Who Keep Us Safe. I can name community helpers and explain how they keep us safe. The **police**, **health worker**, **leader**, and **teacher** all **help** **protect** us. Knowing their roles makes our community **safe**. Keywords: police: officers who keep law and order; health worker: person who treats sickness; leader: person who guides the community; teacher: person who helps children learn; help: give support or aid
chunks.source: The **police**, **health worker**, **leader**, and **teacher** all **help** **protect** us. Knowing their roles makes our community **safe**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does a **police** officer do? A: Keeps law and order, directs traffic.
chunks.source: Keeps law and order, directs traffic.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where does a **health worker** work? A: At a clinic, health centre, or hospital.
chunks.source: At a clinic, health centre, or hospital.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a **leader**'s job in the village? A: Solves problems and guides the community.
chunks.source: Solves problems and guides the community.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a **teacher** **help** you stay **safe**? A: Teaches about **danger**s and how to **report** them.
chunks.source: Teaches about **danger**s and how to **report** them.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: In your own words, explain how these four people **help** the community. A: The **police** stop crime, **health worker**s treat sickness, **leader**s solve disputes, **teacher**s teach safety.
chunks.source: The **police** stop crime, **health worker**s treat sickness, **leader**s solve disputes, **teacher**s teach safety.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: If you are lost at the trading centre, who should you ask for **help**? A: A **police** officer or a shop keeper (an **adult**).
chunks.source: A **police** officer or a shop keeper (an **adult**).

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Foods of Our Culture. I can name traditional Ugandan foods and explain their importance. We eat traditional foods like matooke and millet. We roast meat and share a meal together. Keywords: matooke: green banana cooked as food; millet: small grain made into flour; roast: cook over fire; traditional: from our ancestors' ways; meal: food eaten at one time
chunks.source: We eat traditional foods like matooke and millet. We roast meat and share a meal together.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is matooke? A: Matooke is a green banana that we steam and eat.
chunks.source: Matooke is a green banana that we steam and eat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do we cook millet? A: We grind millet into flour and make bread or porridge.
chunks.source: We grind millet into flour and make bread or porridge.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does roast mean? A: To roast means to cook food over fire or heat.
chunks.source: To roast means to cook food over fire or heat.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are traditional foods important? A: They are healthy and part of our culture.
chunks.source: They are healthy and part of our culture.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Describe a meal you share with your family. A: A meal is food eaten together at one time.
chunks.source: A meal is food eaten together at one time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what traditional food means. A: Traditional food is food that our ancestors ate and we still eat today, like matooke and millet.
chunks.source: Traditional food is food that our ancestors ate and we still eat today, like matooke and millet.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Plants Used in Ceremonies. I can identify plants used in ceremonies and their cultural meanings. In our culture, banana, coffee, and herb plants are used in every ceremony. Keywords: banana: plant with fruit and large leaves; coffee: beans used for a drink; herb: plant used for medicine or flavour; ceremony: special event with customs; culture: way of life of a people
chunks.source: In our culture, banana, coffee, and herb plants are used in every ceremony.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What plant leaves decorate a ceremony? A: Banana leaves decorate the ceremony.
chunks.source: Banana leaves decorate the ceremony.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How is coffee used in culture? A: Coffee beans are shared to show friendship and seal promises.
chunks.source: Coffee beans are shared to show friendship and seal promises.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one herb used for medicine. A: Mint or aloe vera are herbs used for medicine.
chunks.source: Mint or aloe vera are herbs used for medicine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does culture mean? A: Culture is the way of life of a people, including their customs.
chunks.source: Culture is the way of life of a people, including their customs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we use plants at a ceremony? A: Plants have meanings in our culture, like banana for life.
chunks.source: Plants have meanings in our culture, like banana for life.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why banana is important in ceremonies. A: Banana represents food and life, so it is used to bless events.
chunks.source: Banana represents food and life, so it is used to bless events.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Work Done at Home. I can describe home roles and explain why sharing work matters. We fetch, cook, dig, sweep, and share work at home. Everyone helps. Keywords: fetch: go get and bring back; cook: prepare food with heat; dig: turn soil with a hoe; sweep: clean floor with a broom; share: divide fairly among people
chunks.source: We fetch, cook, dig, sweep, and share work at home. Everyone helps.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does fetch mean? A: To fetch means to go get something and bring it back.
chunks.source: To fetch means to go get something and bring it back.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who cooks in your home? A: Mother, father, or children can cook.
chunks.source: Mother, father, or children can cook.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why do we dig the garden? A: We dig to prepare soil for planting crops.
chunks.source: We dig to prepare soil for planting crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: When do you sweep the house? A: We sweep in the morning and evening to keep clean.
chunks.source: We sweep in the morning and evening to keep clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does share mean? A: To share means to divide work or things fairly among people.
chunks.source: To share means to divide work or things fairly among people.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why we share work at home. A: Sharing work makes it fair and easy for everyone.
chunks.source: Sharing work makes it fair and easy for everyone.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Common Diseases. I can name common diseases in my community and say how they spread. We learned that malaria, cholera, typhoid, and diarrhoea are common diseases spread by germs and mosquitoes. We can prevent them by washing hands, drinking clean water, and using mosquito nets. Keywords: malaria: a disease from mosquito bites; cholera: a disease from dirty water; typhoid: a disease from dirty food or water; diarrhoea: loose, watery stools often; germs: tiny things that cause sickness
chunks.source: We learned that malaria, cholera, typhoid, and diarrhoea are common diseases spread by germs and mosquitoes. We can prevent them by washing hands, drinking clean water, and using mosquito nets.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What disease comes from mosquito bites? A: Malaria comes from mosquito bites.
chunks.source: Malaria comes from mosquito bites.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two diseases from dirty water. A: Cholera and typhoid come from dirty water.
chunks.source: Cholera and typhoid come from dirty water.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How do germs cause diarrhoea? A: Germs on dirty hands or in water cause diarrhoea.
chunks.source: Germs on dirty hands or in water cause diarrhoea.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What should you do before eating to stop germs? A: Wash hands with soap before eating.
chunks.source: Wash hands with soap before eating.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how to prevent malaria. A: Sleep under a mosquito net and clear bushes near home.
chunks.source: Sleep under a mosquito net and clear bushes near home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Disease Vectors. I can name disease vectors and say how they spread sickness. We learned that mosquitoes, houseflies, cockroaches, and tsetse flies are vectors that spread diseases like malaria, diarrhoea, cholera, and sleeping sickness. We can stop them by covering food, using nets, and keeping our compound clean. Keywords: mosquito: a small flying insect that bites; housefly: a common fly found in homes; cockroach: a brown insect that runs fast; tsetse fly: a fly that bites and causes sleeping sickness; vector: an animal that carries disease germs
chunks.source: We learned that mosquitoes, houseflies, cockroaches, and tsetse flies are vectors that spread diseases like malaria, diarrhoea, cholera, and sleeping sickness. We can stop them by covering food, using nets, and keeping our compound clean.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a vector? A: A vector is an animal that spreads disease.
chunks.source: A vector is an animal that spreads disease.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which vector spreads malaria? A: The mosquito spreads malaria.
chunks.source: The mosquito spreads malaria.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a housefly spread germs? A: A housefly lands on dirt then on food, leaving germs.
chunks.source: A housefly lands on dirt then on food, leaving germs.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What disease does the tsetse fly spread? A: The tsetse fly spreads sleeping sickness.
chunks.source: The tsetse fly spreads sleeping sickness.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how to stop cockroaches from spreading germs. A: Cover food, clean the kitchen, and cover rubbish bins.
chunks.source: Cover food, clean the kitchen, and cover rubbish bins.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Immunisation and Clinics. I can explain why immunisation is important and where to get it. We learned that immunisation at the health centre or clinic gives children vaccines to protect them from dangerous diseases. Keeping the immunisation card and returning on time ensures full protection. Keywords: immunisation: getting vaccines to prevent disease; clinic: a place where nurses give health care; health centre: a bigger place with doctors and nurses; vaccine: a medicine that stops you getting sick; child: a young boy or girl
chunks.source: We learned that immunisation at the health centre or clinic gives children vaccines to protect them from dangerous diseases. Keeping the immunisation card and returning on time ensures full protection.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is immunisation? A: Immunisation is when a child gets vaccines to protect against diseases.
chunks.source: Immunisation is when a child gets vaccines to protect against diseases.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Where do children go for vaccines? A: Children go to the clinic or health centre for vaccines.
chunks.source: Children go to the clinic or health centre for vaccines.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does a vaccine do? A: A vaccine helps the body fight germs so the child does not get sick.
chunks.source: A vaccine helps the body fight germs so the child does not get sick.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why is the immunisation card important? A: The card shows when to return for the next vaccine.
chunks.source: The card shows when to return for the next vaccine.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why every child needs immunisation. A: Immunisation protects children from deadly diseases like measles and polio.
chunks.source: Immunisation protects children from deadly diseases like measles and polio.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Simple Tools We Use. I can name and describe simple tools used at home and in the garden. Kato learns that each **tool** like the **hoe**, **panga**, **spade**, and **wheelbarrow** has a special job in the garden. Keywords: hoe: a tool for digging; panga: a large knife for cutting; spade: a tool for moving earth; wheelbarrow: a cart with one wheel; tool: something used to do work
chunks.source: Kato learns that each **tool** like the **hoe**, **panga**, **spade**, and **wheelbarrow** has a special job in the garden.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does a **hoe** do? A: A **hoe** digs and loosens soil.
chunks.source: A **hoe** digs and loosens soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which tool moves heavy soil? A: The **wheelbarrow** moves heavy soil.
chunks.source: The **wheelbarrow** moves heavy soil.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one tool that cuts grass. A: The **panga** cuts grass.
chunks.source: The **panga** cuts grass.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why a **spade** is useful. A: A **spade** lifts and moves earth.
chunks.source: A **spade** lifts and moves earth.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Choose the tool you would use to dig a hole for a tree. A: I would use a **hoe** or a **spade**.
chunks.source: I would use a **hoe** or a **spade**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Simple Machines. I can identify simple machines and explain how they make work easier. Amina discovers that a **lever**, **pulley**, **wheel**, and **ramp** are simple machines that make moving a **load** easier. Keywords: lever: a stiff bar that turns on a point; pulley: a wheel with a rope to lift; wheel: a round object that rolls; ramp: a sloping surface; load: something heavy to move
chunks.source: Amina discovers that a **lever**, **pulley**, **wheel**, and **ramp** are simple machines that make moving a **load** easier.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does a **lever** do? A: A **lever** lifts or moves a **load** with a pivot.
chunks.source: A **lever** lifts or moves a **load** with a pivot.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which simple machine uses a rope and a wheel? A: A **pulley** uses a rope and a wheel.
chunks.source: A **pulley** uses a rope and a wheel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name a simple machine that rolls. A: A **wheel** rolls.
chunks.source: A **wheel** rolls.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how a **ramp** helps. A: A **ramp** lets you slide a **load** up instead of lifting.
chunks.source: A **ramp** lets you slide a **load** up instead of lifting.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: If you need to lift a heavy box, which simple machine would you choose? A: I would use a **lever** or a **pulley**.
chunks.source: I would use a **lever** or a **pulley**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Energy We Use. I can name sources of energy used at home and say what they do. Nalongo learns that **firewood**, **charcoal**, **solar**, and **paraffin** are sources of **energy** used at home. Keywords: firewood: wood burned for heat; charcoal: burned wood pieces; solar: energy from the sun; paraffin: liquid fuel for stoves; energy: power to do work
chunks.source: Nalongo learns that **firewood**, **charcoal**, **solar**, and **paraffin** are sources of **energy** used at home.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What gives heat when burned? A: **Firewood** and **charcoal** give heat when burned.
chunks.source: **Firewood** and **charcoal** give heat when burned.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which energy source comes from the sun? A: **Solar** energy comes from the sun.
chunks.source: **Solar** energy comes from the sun.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name a liquid fuel used for cooking. A: **Paraffin** is a liquid fuel.
chunks.source: **Paraffin** is a liquid fuel.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why we need different energy sources. A: Different sources work for different needs like cooking or light.
chunks.source: Different sources work for different needs like cooking or light.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: If the power goes out, which energy source could you use for light? A: You could use a **solar** lamp or **paraffin** lamp.
chunks.source: You could use a **solar** lamp or **paraffin** lamp.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Sources of Energy. I can name sources of energy around me. The **sun**, **firewood**, **electricity**, and **biogas** are **source**s of energy we use every day. Keywords: sun: the big star that gives light and heat; electricity: power that runs lights and phones; firewood: wood burned for cooking; biogas: gas made from animal waste; source: where something comes from
chunks.source: The **sun**, **firewood**, **electricity**, and **biogas** are **source**s of energy we use every day.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one **source** of energy you see at home. A: **Firewood**, **electricity**, **sun**, or **biogas**.
chunks.source: **Firewood**, **electricity**, **sun**, or **biogas**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What **source** gives us light during the day? A: The **sun**.
chunks.source: The **sun**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What **source** comes from wires on poles? A: **Electricity**.
chunks.source: **Electricity**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What **source** is made from cow dung? A: **Biogas**.
chunks.source: **Biogas**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what a **source** of energy means. A: A **source** of energy is where energy comes from, like the **sun** or **firewood**.
chunks.source: A **source** of energy is where energy comes from, like the **sun** or **firewood**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which **source** do we burn to cook? A: **Firewood**.
chunks.source: **Firewood**.

chunks.id: L-P3-Science-Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.text: Heat and Light from the Sun. I can tell how we use solar energy. The **sun** gives **heat** and **light**. We use **solar** energy to **dry** things and **panel**s make **electricity**. Keywords: solar: from the sun; dry: to make something not wet; heat: warmth that makes things hot; light: brightness that helps us see; panel: a flat board that catches sun power
chunks.source: The **sun** gives **heat** and **light**. We use **solar** energy to **dry** things and **panel**s make **electricity**.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Science-Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.text: Q: What does **solar** mean? A: From the **sun**.
chunks.source: From the **sun**.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Science-Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.text: Q: What two things does the **sun** give us? A: **Heat** and **light**.
chunks.source: **Heat** and **light**.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Science-Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.text: Q: What does a **panel** do? A: Catches **sun** power to make **electricity**.
chunks.source: Catches **sun** power to make **electricity**.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Science-Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.text: Q: Why do we put wet clothes in the **sun**? A: To **dry** them with **heat**.
chunks.source: To **dry** them with **heat**.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Science-Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how **solar** energy helps us. A: **Solar** energy from the **sun** gives **heat** to **dry** things and **light** to see. A **panel** makes **electricity**.
chunks.source: **Solar** energy from the **sun** gives **heat** to **dry** things and **light** to see. A **panel** makes **electricity**.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Science-Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.subject: Science
chunks.unit: Heat and Light from the Sun
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing you **dry** at home using the **sun**. A: Clothes, cassava, maize, or dishes.
chunks.source: Clothes, cassava, maize, or dishes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Saving Energy. I can say ways to save energy at home. We **save** energy by using a good **stove** for **firewood** and when we **switch off** lights to stop **waste**. Keywords: switch off: to turn something off; save: to keep and not waste; firewood: wood burned for cooking; stove: a place to cook with fire; waste: to use more than needed
chunks.source: We **save** energy by using a good **stove** for **firewood** and when we **switch off** lights to stop **waste**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does **switch off** mean? A: To turn something off.
chunks.source: To turn something off.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does a clay **stove** help **save** **firewood**? A: It keeps **heat** inside so less wood burns.
chunks.source: It keeps **heat** inside so less wood burns.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why should we not **waste** **electricity**? A: It costs money and uses energy.
chunks.source: It costs money and uses energy.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing you can **switch off** at home. A: Light, radio, TV, or phone charger.
chunks.source: Light, radio, TV, or phone charger.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how to **save** energy when cooking. A: Use a good **stove** that keeps **heat** in. Then you burn less **firewood**.
chunks.source: Use a good **stove** that keeps **heat** in. Then you burn less **firewood**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What happens if we **waste** **firewood**? A: We cut more trees and the forest disappears.
chunks.source: We cut more trees and the forest disappears.

chunks.id: L-P3-Social-People and Families in Our Community
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: People and Families in Our Community
chunks.text: People and Families in Our Community. I can name the members of my family and community. Amina learns that a family includes parent, elder, neighbour, visitor, relative, and clan members who all help each other. Keywords: family: people who live together; parent: mother or father; elder: older person who gives advice; neighbour: person who lives near you; visitor: person who comes to visit; relative: family member; clan: large family group
chunks.source: Amina learns that a family includes parent, elder, neighbour, visitor, relative, and clan members who all help each other.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-People and Families in Our Community
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: People and Families in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: What is a family? A: A group of people who live together and care for each other.
chunks.source: A group of people who live together and care for each other.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-People and Families in Our Community
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: People and Families in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: Who is a parent? A: A mother or father who looks after a child.
chunks.source: A mother or father who looks after a child.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-People and Families in Our Community
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: People and Families in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: What does an elder do in the community? A: An elder gives advice and shares stories.
chunks.source: An elder gives advice and shares stories.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-People and Families in Our Community
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: People and Families in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: Name one neighbour you know. A: Any person who lives near you.
chunks.source: Any person who lives near you.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-People and Families in Our Community
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: People and Families in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what a clan is. A: A clan is a large group of relatives who share a common ancestor.
chunks.source: A clan is a large group of relatives who share a common ancestor.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-People and Families in Our Community
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: People and Families in Our Community
chunks.text: Q: What might a visitor bring to a home? A: A visitor may bring news or gifts.
chunks.source: A visitor may bring news or gifts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Social Services Near Our Home. I can identify the social services near my home. Kato discovers that the school, hospital, market, church, mosque, water source, and road are important social services in his community. Keywords: school: place where children learn; hospital: place for sick people; market: place to buy and sell; church: building for Christian worship; mosque: building for Muslim worship; water source: place to get clean water; road: path for walking and driving
chunks.source: Kato discovers that the school, hospital, market, church, mosque, water source, and road are important social services in his community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do children learn at school? A: They learn reading, writing, and numbers.
chunks.source: They learn reading, writing, and numbers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do sick people go? A: They go to the hospital.
chunks.source: They go to the hospital.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What can you buy at the market? A: You can buy food, clothes, and tools.
chunks.source: You can buy food, clothes, and tools.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do people pray in a church? A: Christians pray in a church.
chunks.source: Christians pray in a church.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do Muslims pray? A: Muslims pray in a mosque.
chunks.source: Muslims pray in a mosque.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why a water source is important. A: A water source gives clean water for drinking and cooking.
chunks.source: A water source gives clean water for drinking and cooking.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Leaders in Our Community. I can name the leaders in my community and their roles. The chairperson, councillor, elder, chief, priest, imam, and leader all serve the community in different ways. Keywords: chairperson: head of village council; councillor: represents village at district; elder: older person who gives advice; chief: traditional leader of village; priest: Christian religious leader; imam: Muslim religious leader; leader: person who guides others
chunks.source: The chairperson, councillor, elder, chief, priest, imam, and leader all serve the community in different ways.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who is the chairperson? A: The chairperson leads the village council meetings.
chunks.source: The chairperson leads the village council meetings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a councillor do? A: A councillor represents the village at the district level.
chunks.source: A councillor represents the village at the district level.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is an elder respected? A: An elder gives wise advice and keeps traditions.
chunks.source: An elder gives wise advice and keeps traditions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the role of a chief? A: A chief oversees the village and keeps peace.
chunks.source: A chief oversees the village and keeps peace.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where does a priest work? A: A priest works in a church.
chunks.source: A priest works in a church.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what a leader should do. A: A leader should guide, serve, and protect the community.
chunks.source: A leader should guide, serve, and protect the community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: What Is a Sub-County?. I can name the parts of a sub-county and say how they fit together. A sub-county is a group of parishes. Towns have divisions instead. Many sub-counties make a district. Keywords: sub-county: a group of parishes with one local government; division: a part of a town or city like a sub-county; parish: a group of villages that work together; village: a small place where families live near each other; zone: a small part of a village or town; boundary: a line that shows where an area ends; district: a big area made of many sub-counties
chunks.source: A sub-county is a group of parishes. Towns have divisions instead. Many sub-counties make a district.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which is smaller: a parish or a sub-county? A: A parish is smaller.
chunks.source: A parish is smaller.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do many parishes make together? A: They make a sub-county.
chunks.source: They make a sub-county.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the area that is like a sub-county but in a town. A: A division.
chunks.source: A division.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What shows where one sub-county ends? A: A boundary line.
chunks.source: A boundary line.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In your own words, explain how a village fits into a district. A: A village is in a parish, which is in a sub-county, which is in a district.
chunks.source: A village is in a parish, which is in a sub-county, which is in a district.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: If you live in a zone, what bigger area are you also in? A: You are in a village.
chunks.source: You are in a village.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Physical Features in Our Sub-County. I can name and describe the main physical features in my sub-county. Our sub-county has hills, rivers, valleys, roads, swamps, forests, and lakes. Each feature helps people in different ways. Keywords: hill: high land that rises up; river: fresh water that flows in a channel; lake: a large body of water surrounded by land; swamp: wet land with grass and reeds; forest: a big area thick with trees; valley: low land between hills; road: a path for vehicles and people
chunks.source: Our sub-county has hills, rivers, valleys, roads, swamps, forests, and lakes. Each feature helps people in different ways.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which feature has flowing fresh water? A: A river.
chunks.source: A river.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we call low land between two hills? A: A valley.
chunks.source: A valley.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name a feature that floods in the rain season. A: A swamp.
chunks.source: A swamp.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which feature is a large water body surrounded by land? A: A lake.
chunks.source: A lake.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In your own words, tell how a road helps a village. A: A road lets people reach the market, school, and health centre.
chunks.source: A road lets people reach the market, school, and health centre.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: If you stand on a hill, what might you see below? A: A valley, a road, or a swamp.
chunks.source: A valley, a road, or a swamp.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Finding Places with a Compass. I can use a compass to find the four main directions on a map. A compass always points north. Align your map with the compass, then north is up, south down, east right, west left. Keywords: north: the direction towards the top of a map; south: the direction towards the bottom of a map; east: the direction where the sun rises; west: the direction where the sun sets; compass: a tool that shows north, south, east, west; direction: the way you go to reach a place; map: a drawing that shows places from above
chunks.source: A compass always points north. Align your map with the compass, then north is up, south down, east right, west left.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What tool shows the four main directions? A: A compass.
chunks.source: A compass.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: If you face the rising sun, which direction are you facing? A: East.
chunks.source: East.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: On a map aligned with a compass, which way is south? A: Towards the bottom.
chunks.source: Towards the bottom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: The church is north of the mosque. Where is the mosque from the church? A: South.
chunks.source: South.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In your own words, explain how to use a compass with a map. A: Hold the compass flat, let the needle point north, then turn the map so its top matches north.
chunks.source: Hold the compass flat, let the needle point north, then turn the map so its top matches north.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What direction is the setting sun? A: West.
chunks.source: West.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Jobs People Do. I can name different occupations in my community. People have different occupations like farmer, trader, teacher, and nurse; each job helps the community. Keywords: occupation: a type of work people do; job: work done for pay; work: activity that uses effort; farmer: person who grows crops and raises animals; trader: person who buys and sells goods; teacher: person who teaches children; nurse: person who cares for sick people
chunks.source: People have different occupations like farmer, trader, teacher, and nurse; each job helps the community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is an **occupation**? A: An occupation is a job people do for pay.
chunks.source: An occupation is a job people do for pay.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one **job** you see in your village. A: A farmer, a teacher, or a nurse.
chunks.source: A farmer, a teacher, or a nurse.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a **farmer** do? A: A farmer grows crops and raises animals.
chunks.source: A farmer grows crops and raises animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is a **nurse** important? A: A nurse gives medicine and checks health.
chunks.source: A nurse gives medicine and checks health.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what **work** means. A: Work is any activity done to earn money or help others.
chunks.source: Work is any activity done to earn money or help others.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which **occupation** would you like to have? A: I would like to be a teacher because I like helping children learn.
chunks.source: I would like to be a teacher because I like helping children learn.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Farming and Trading. I can describe farming and trading as economic activities. Economic activities like farming, trading, and services happen at the market; they provide crops, animals, and services for the community. Keywords: economic activity: work that makes money for people; trade: buying and selling things; trading: the act of buying and selling; crops: plants grown for food; animals: livestock like cows and goats; market: place where people buy and sell; services: work that helps others like haircuts
chunks.source: Economic activities like farming, trading, and services happen at the market; they provide crops, animals, and services for the community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is an **economic activity**? A: Work that makes money for people.
chunks.source: Work that makes money for people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of **trade**. A: Buying maize from a farmer.
chunks.source: Buying maize from a farmer.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do **crops** provide? A: Food for families and the market.
chunks.source: Food for families and the market.

chunks.subject: Social
