chunks.text: Q: Why are **services** important? A: They help people with needs like haircuts.
chunks.source: They help people with needs like haircuts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what **trading** means. A: Trading is when people exchange goods for money.
chunks.source: Trading is when people exchange goods for money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which **market** do you visit with your family? A: We go to the trading centre near the borehole.
chunks.source: We go to the trading centre near the borehole.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Challenges at Work and Solutions. I can identify work challenges and suggest solutions. Challenges at work can be solved by asking for help, using the right tools, and planning for weather and transport. Keywords: challenge: a difficult problem; solution: a way to fix a problem; interview: a talk to learn from someone; transport: way to move people or goods; money: coins and notes used to buy; weather: sun, rain, wind each day; tools: items used to do work
chunks.source: Challenges at work can be solved by asking for help, using the right tools, and planning for weather and transport.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a **challenge** at work? A: A difficult problem that stops work.
chunks.source: A difficult problem that stops work.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of a **solution**. A: Using a tarp to keep wood dry.
chunks.source: Using a tarp to keep wood dry.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do people do an **interview**? A: To learn from someone with experience.
chunks.source: To learn from someone with experience.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name a type of **transport** in Uganda. A: Boda boda or matatu.
chunks.source: Boda boda or matatu.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how **weather** affects work. A: Rain can stop outdoor work and damage materials.
chunks.source: Rain can stop outdoor work and damage materials.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which **tool** would you buy first? A: I would buy a saw because it cuts wood.
chunks.source: I would buy a saw because it cuts wood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Parts of Our Environment. I can name the seven parts of our environment. The environment has seven parts: air, water, soil, plants, animals, people, and buildings. We must care for all of them. Keywords: air: the invisible gas we breathe; water: liquid from rain, boreholes, lakes; soil: the top layer of ground where plants grow; plants: living things like trees, crops, grass; animals: living creatures like goats, cows, birds; people: human beings who live and work here; buildings: structures like homes, shops, schools
chunks.source: The environment has seven parts: air, water, soil, plants, animals, people, and buildings. We must care for all of them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the seven parts of the environment. A: air, water, soil, plants, animals, people, buildings
chunks.source: air, water, soil, plants, animals, people, buildings

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do we breathe? A: We breathe air.
chunks.source: We breathe air.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do we get water in the village? A: We get water at the borehole.
chunks.source: We get water at the borehole.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is soil important? A: Soil helps plants grow.
chunks.source: Soil helps plants grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what the environment is. A: The environment is all things around us like air, water, soil, plants, animals, people, and buildings.
chunks.source: The environment is all things around us like air, water, soil, plants, animals, people, and buildings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one way to care for the environment. A: Keep water clean / do not litter / plant trees
chunks.source: Keep water clean / do not litter / plant trees

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: How People Use the Environment. I can describe ways people use the environment in Uganda. People use the environment for farming, fishing, building, grazing, trading, tourism, and brick making. All these need a healthy environment. Keywords: farming: growing crops for food and sale; fishing: catching fish from lakes and rivers; building: making houses, schools, roads; grazing: letting animals eat grass in fields; trading: buying and selling goods at markets; tourism: visitors coming to see nature and culture; brick making: making bricks from soil for building
chunks.source: People use the environment for farming, fishing, building, grazing, trading, tourism, and brick making. All these need a healthy environment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List three ways people use the environment. A: farming, fishing, building (any three from list)
chunks.source: farming, fishing, building (any three from list)

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is brick making? A: Making bricks from wet soil for building.
chunks.source: Making bricks from wet soil for building.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is trading important? A: Trading moves goods from farms to markets.
chunks.source: Trading moves goods from farms to markets.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does tourism help the village? A: Tourism brings money and jobs.
chunks.source: Tourism brings money and jobs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how your family uses the environment. A: My family uses the environment by farming / fishing / trading / etc.
chunks.source: My family uses the environment by farming / fishing / trading / etc.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one use that needs clean water. A: Fishing needs clean water.
chunks.source: Fishing needs clean water.

chunks.id: L-P3-Social-How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.text: How People Spoil and Protect Nature. I can explain how people spoil nature and how to protect it. People spoil nature with waste, pollution, and litter. We protect it by cleaning, planting, conserving, and reducing rubbish. Keywords: waste: unwanted materials thrown away; pollution: dirty air, water, or soil that harms life; protect: keep safe from harm; plant: put seeds or seedlings in soil to grow; clean: make free from dirt or rubbish; conserve: use carefully so it lasts long; rubbish: dry waste like paper, plastic, tins
chunks.source: People spoil nature with waste, pollution, and litter. We protect it by cleaning, planting, conserving, and reducing rubbish.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.text: Q: Name two things that spoil nature. A: littering, burning rubbish, pollution (any two)
chunks.source: littering, burning rubbish, pollution (any two)

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.text: Q: What does 'conserve' mean? A: Use carefully so it lasts long.
chunks.source: Use carefully so it lasts long.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.text: Q: How can you protect trees? A: Do not cut them; plant new ones.
chunks.source: Do not cut them; plant new ones.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.text: Q: Why is burning plastic bad? A: It makes toxic pollution in the air.
chunks.source: It makes toxic pollution in the air.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how you can protect the environment at school. A: I can pick up rubbish, plant trees, save water, not litter.
chunks.source: I can pick up rubbish, plant trees, save water, not litter.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Spoil and Protect Nature
chunks.text: Q: Give one way to reduce waste. A: Reuse bottles / recycle paper / compost food waste
chunks.source: Reuse bottles / recycle paper / compost food waste

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Elements of the Weather. I can name the main elements of weather. Weather has many parts like rain, sun, cloud, wind, temperature, and storm. We can observe them each day. Keywords: rain: water falling from the sky; sun: the bright star that gives light and heat; cloud: white or grey mass in the sky; wind: moving air; temperature: how hot or cold the air is; weather: the condition of the air each day; storm: strong wind with heavy rain
chunks.source: Weather has many parts like rain, sun, cloud, wind, temperature, and storm. We can observe them each day.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **weather**? A: Weather is the condition of the air like rain, sun, wind, and temperature.
chunks.source: Weather is the condition of the air like rain, sun, wind, and temperature.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two elements of weather. A: Rain and wind are two elements of weather.
chunks.source: Rain and wind are two elements of weather.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a **thermometer** measure? A: A thermometer measures temperature.
chunks.source: A thermometer measures temperature.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What happens during a **storm**? A: A storm brings heavy rain and strong wind.
chunks.source: A storm brings heavy rain and strong wind.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what **temperature** means. A: Temperature tells how hot or cold the air feels.
chunks.source: Temperature tells how hot or cold the air feels.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which tool helps us know the **temperature**? A: A thermometer helps us know the temperature.
chunks.source: A thermometer helps us know the temperature.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Reading a Weather Chart. I can read a weather chart and use tools to record weather. A weather chart, rain gauge, and thermometer help us record and predict weather for a week and across seasons. Keywords: weather chart: a board showing daily weather; rain gauge: a tool that catches rain to measure it; thermometer: a tool that shows temperature; record: write down information; predict: say what will happen later; week: seven days; season: a time of year with similar weather
chunks.source: A weather chart, rain gauge, and thermometer help us record and predict weather for a week and across seasons.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a **weather chart** used for? A: A weather chart shows daily weather like rain and temperature.
chunks.source: A weather chart shows daily weather like rain and temperature.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which tool measures **rain**? A: A rain gauge measures rain.
chunks.source: A rain gauge measures rain.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a **thermometer** tell us? A: A thermometer tells the temperature.
chunks.source: A thermometer tells the temperature.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we **record** weather each day? A: We record weather to see patterns over a week.
chunks.source: We record weather to see patterns over a week.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what **predict** means. A: Predict means to say what the weather will be like later.
chunks.source: Predict means to say what the weather will be like later.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one **season** in Uganda. A: The rainy season is one season in Uganda.
chunks.source: The rainy season is one season in Uganda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Weather and People's Work. I can explain how weather affects people's work. Farmers, fishers, and builders all need the right weather to plant, harvest, build, and travel. Keywords: farmer: person who grows crops; plant: put seeds in soil to grow; harvest: gather ripe crops; dry: without water or moisture; fish: catch fish from water; build: make something like a house; travel: go from one place to another
chunks.source: Farmers, fishers, and builders all need the right weather to plant, harvest, build, and travel.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a **farmer** do? A: A farmer grows crops and raises animals.
chunks.source: A farmer grows crops and raises animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: When do you **plant** seeds? A: You plant seeds when the soil is moist.
chunks.source: You plant seeds when the soil is moist.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **harvest** mean? A: Harvest means to gather ripe crops.
chunks.source: Harvest means to gather ripe crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why must the field **dry** before planting? A: If the field is too wet, seeds may rot.
chunks.source: If the field is too wet, seeds may rot.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what **travel** means for a farmer. A: Travel means moving from the farm to the market to sell crops.
chunks.source: Travel means moving from the farm to the market to sell crops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one job that needs good weather to **build**. A: A builder needs dry weather to build a house.
chunks.source: A builder needs dry weather to build a house.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Animals in Our Sub-County. I can name animals in our sub-county and say where they live. Our sub-county has many animals like cattle, goats, birds, insects, and fish. Each animal lives in its own habitat. Keywords: animal: a living creature that moves and breathes; birds: animals with feathers and wings; insects: small animals with six legs; fish: animals that live in water and have fins; cattle: cows and bulls kept for milk and meat; goats: animals with horns that give milk and meat; habitat: the natural home of an animal or plant
chunks.source: Our sub-county has many animals like cattle, goats, birds, insects, and fish. Each animal lives in its own habitat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is an animal? A: A living creature that moves and breathes.
chunks.source: A living creature that moves and breathes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two animals that give us milk. A: Cattle and goats.
chunks.source: Cattle and goats.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do fish live? A: Fish live in water, their habitat.
chunks.source: Fish live in water, their habitat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do birds eat? A: Birds eat insects and seeds.
chunks.source: Birds eat insects and seeds.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what a habitat is. A: A habitat is the natural home where an animal or plant lives, like a stream for fish or a tree for birds.
chunks.source: A habitat is the natural home where an animal or plant lives, like a stream for fish or a tree for birds.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which animal have you seen today? A: I saw a goat near the market.
chunks.source: I saw a goat near the market.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Plants Are Living Things. I can explain that plants are living things and what they need to grow. Plants are living things that need water, sunlight, and nutrients to feed and show growth from a seed. Keywords: living things: things that grow, breathe, and need food; growth: the process of getting bigger; feed: to give food or nutrients; water: liquid that living things need to survive; sunlight: light from the sun that plants use to make food; seed: the small part of a plant that grows into a new plant; plant: a living thing that grows in soil and has leaves
chunks.source: Plants are living things that need water, sunlight, and nutrients to feed and show growth from a seed.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Are plants living things? A: Yes, plants are living things because they grow and need food.
chunks.source: Yes, plants are living things because they grow and need food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a seed need to grow? A: A seed needs water, sunlight, and soil to grow.
chunks.source: A seed needs water, sunlight, and soil to grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is growth? A: Growth is the process of getting bigger.
chunks.source: Growth is the process of getting bigger.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do plants feed? A: Plants feed on nutrients from the soil through their roots.
chunks.source: Plants feed on nutrients from the soil through their roots.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why sunlight is important for plants. A: Sunlight helps plants make their own food so they can grow.
chunks.source: Sunlight helps plants make their own food so they can grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What did Peter plant at home? A: Peter planted a bean seed in a tin.
chunks.source: Peter planted a bean seed in a tin.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Homes of Living Things. I can name different habitats and the living things that live there. Different habitats like forest, swamp, water, and soil give shelter to living things. A nest is a shelter birds build in a tree. Keywords: habitat: the natural home of an animal or plant; shelter: a place that protects from weather and danger; nest: a home built by birds to lay eggs; water: liquid that forms streams, lakes, and rain; soil: the top layer of ground where plants grow; forest: a large area covered with trees; swamp: wet land with water and grass
chunks.source: Different habitats like forest, swamp, water, and soil give shelter to living things. A nest is a shelter birds build in a tree.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a habitat? A: A habitat is the natural home of an animal or plant.
chunks.source: A habitat is the natural home of an animal or plant.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name three habitats in our sub-county. A: Forest, swamp, and water (stream).
chunks.source: Forest, swamp, and water (stream).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a nest used for? A: A nest is a shelter for birds to lay eggs and raise babies.
chunks.source: A nest is a shelter for birds to lay eggs and raise babies.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do worms live? A: Worms live in the soil.
chunks.source: Worms live in the soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why a swamp is a good habitat for frogs. A: A swamp has water and plants where frogs can hide, lay eggs, and find food.
chunks.source: A swamp has water and plants where frogs can hide, lay eggs, and find food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What shelter do you have at home? A: A house is our shelter.
chunks.source: A house is our shelter.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Parts of a Common Plant. I can name the parts of a common plant. A plant has roots, stem, leaves, flower, fruit and seeds; each part helps the plant grow. Keywords: roots: part that holds plant in soil; stem: main stalk that carries water; leaves: green parts that make food; flower: bright part that makes fruit; fruit: sweet part with seeds inside; seeds: tiny pieces that grow new plants; plant: living thing with roots, stem, leaves
chunks.source: A plant has roots, stem, leaves, flower, fruit and seeds; each part helps the plant grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do **roots** do? A: They take water from the soil.
chunks.source: They take water from the soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does the **stem** do? A: It carries water to the leaves.
chunks.source: It carries water to the leaves.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do **leaves** do? A: They make food using sunlight.
chunks.source: They make food using sunlight.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What grows on the **stem** and becomes **fruit**? A: The flower grows on the stem and becomes fruit.
chunks.source: The flower grows on the stem and becomes fruit.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where are **seeds** found? A: Seeds are inside the fruit.
chunks.source: Seeds are inside the fruit.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how a plant grows from a seed. A: A seed gets water, grows roots, a stem, leaves, then a flower and fruit with seeds.
chunks.source: A seed gets water, grows roots, a stem, leaves, then a flower and fruit with seeds.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Plants We Use for Food. I can name food plants we eat. We eat cassava, sweet potato, banana, maize, beans, mango and pawpaw for food. Keywords: cassava: root crop used for flour; sweet potato: orange root vegetable; banana: long fruit cooked as matooke; maize: yellow grain ground into flour; beans: protein rich seeds; mango: sweet yellow fruit; pawpaw: soft orange fruit
chunks.source: We eat cassava, sweet potato, banana, maize, beans, mango and pawpaw for food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What food do we get from **cassava**? A: We get flour for posho.
chunks.source: We get flour for posho.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is **sweet potato** cooked? A: It is boiled and eaten.
chunks.source: It is boiled and eaten.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **banana** become when steamed? A: It becomes matooke.
chunks.source: It becomes matooke.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **maize** used for? A: Maize kernels are ground into flour.
chunks.source: Maize kernels are ground into flour.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do **beans** give us? A: Beans give protein.
chunks.source: Beans give protein.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why we eat many different plants. A: Different plants give us energy, protein, vitamins, and keep us healthy.
chunks.source: Different plants give us energy, protein, vitamins, and keep us healthy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: How Plants Grow. I can explain how a plant grows. A seed needs water, sunlight, soil and care to germinate and grow into a healthy plant. Keywords: germination: seed starting to sprout; seed: tiny plant beginning; water: liquid plants drink; sunlight: light from the sun; soil: earth where plants grow; growth: getting bigger and stronger; care: looking after the plant
chunks.source: A seed needs water, sunlight, soil and care to germinate and grow into a healthy plant.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **germination**? A: It is when a seed starts to grow.
chunks.source: It is when a seed starts to grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a **seed** need to begin **germination**? A: It needs water, soil, and sunlight.
chunks.source: It needs water, soil, and sunlight.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is **water** important for a plant? A: Water helps the seed swell and roots grow.
chunks.source: Water helps the seed swell and roots grow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does **sunlight** help the plant? A: Sunlight lets leaves make food.
chunks.source: Sunlight lets leaves make food.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **care** mean for a plant? A: Care means giving water, weeding, and protecting it.
chunks.source: Care means giving water, weeding, and protecting it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how a seed becomes a plant. A: A seed gets water, germinates, grows roots and stem, then leaves, and with care it grows big.
chunks.source: A seed gets water, germinates, grows roots and stem, then leaves, and with care it grows big.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Resources in Our Sub-County. I can name the main resources in my sub-county. Our sub-county has many resources like water, land, forest, money, time, and people. We must use them wisely. Keywords: resources: things we use to live; water: clean liquid we drink; land: ground for farming; forest: many trees together; money: coins and notes for buying; time: hours and minutes we have; people: men, women, children who work
chunks.source: Our sub-county has many resources like water, land, forest, money, time, and people. We must use them wisely.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a resource? A: A resource is something we use to meet our needs.
chunks.source: A resource is something we use to meet our needs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two natural resources in our sub-county. A: Water and land are natural resources.
chunks.source: Water and land are natural resources.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we need money? A: Money lets us buy things we cannot make.
chunks.source: Money lets us buy things we cannot make.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do people help as a resource? A: People work to grow food and build homes.
chunks.source: People work to grow food and build homes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why time is a resource. A: Time lets us do work and learn; we cannot get it back.
chunks.source: Time lets us do work and learn; we cannot get it back.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What can we do to keep our forest safe? A: We can plant trees and stop cutting them down.
chunks.source: We can plant trees and stop cutting them down.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Making a Simple Budget. I can make a simple budget with a plan, price, and shillings. A budget is a plan that shows price, saving, buying, selling, and shillings. Keywords: budget: a plan for money; plan: a list of steps; price: how much something costs; save: keep money for later; buying: getting something by paying; selling: giving something for money; shillings: Uganda's money
chunks.source: A budget is a plan that shows price, saving, buying, selling, and shillings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a budget? A: A budget is a plan for how to use money.
chunks.source: A budget is a plan for how to use money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we check the price before buying? A: To know if we have enough money.
chunks.source: To know if we have enough money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does it mean to save? A: To keep money for future needs.
chunks.source: To keep money for future needs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of buying and selling. A: Buying a mango and selling a banana.
chunks.source: Buying a mango and selling a banana.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why a plan helps Kato. A: A plan shows how much he can spend and save.
chunks.source: A plan shows how much he can spend and save.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What currency does Uganda use? A: Uganda uses shillings.
chunks.source: Uganda uses shillings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Using Resources Wisely. I can use resources wisely by saving, conserving, and choosing needs over wants. We use resources wisely by knowing needs, saving, doing projects, and conserving for the future. Keywords: essential items: basic things we need; saving: keeping money or resources; project: a planned task to help; future: the time coming after now; needs: things we must have; wants: things we would like; conserve: use carefully so it lasts
chunks.source: We use resources wisely by knowing needs, saving, doing projects, and conserving for the future.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are essential items? A: Things we must have like food and water.
chunks.source: Things we must have like food and water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why should we save for the future? A: To be ready for emergencies and goals.
chunks.source: To be ready for emergencies and goals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of a project that helps the community. A: Cleaning a borehole or planting trees.
chunks.source: Cleaning a borehole or planting trees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the difference between needs and wants? A: Needs are necessary; wants are nice to have.
chunks.source: Needs are necessary; wants are nice to have.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how to conserve water at home. A: Turn off taps, fix leaks, and reuse water.
chunks.source: Turn off taps, fix leaks, and reuse water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does a project help people? A: It solves a problem and uses resources well.
chunks.source: It solves a problem and uses resources well.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Living in Harmony. I can explain how to live in harmony with my neighbours. **Harmony** means living in **peace** with our **neighbours**. We **share**, stay **polite**, show **respect**, and **forgive** to keep our sub-county happy. Keywords: harmony: living together happily; share: give part of what you have; polite: showing good manners; respect: treat others well; forgive: stop being angry; peace: no fighting, calm; neighbour: person living near you
chunks.source: **Harmony** means living in **peace** with our **neighbours**. We **share**, stay **polite**, show **respect**, and **forgive** to keep our sub-county happy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **harmony** mean? A: Living together happily in peace.
chunks.source: Living together happily in peace.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two ways to show **respect** to a **neighbour**. A: Greet them politely and help them.
chunks.source: Greet them politely and help them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: If your friend takes your pencil without asking, what should you do? A: Talk calmly, then **forgive** when they say sorry.
chunks.source: Talk calmly, then **forgive** when they say sorry.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is **sharing** important for **peace**? A: It stops fights and makes everyone feel cared for.
chunks.source: It stops fights and makes everyone feel cared for.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain **harmony** in your own words. A: Harmony is when people live together kindly, share, respect each other, and forgive mistakes so there is peace.
chunks.source: Harmony is when people live together kindly, share, respect each other, and forgive mistakes so there is peace.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Children's Rights and Needs. I can name children's rights and needs. Every child has **child rights** to **food**, **shelter**, **education**, **care**, and **protection**. Adults must provide these **needs** so children grow safe and strong. Keywords: child rights: things every child must have; needs: things we must have to live; food: what we eat to grow; shelter: a safe place to sleep; education: going to school to learn; care: love and looking after; protection: being kept safe from harm
chunks.source: Every child has **child rights** to **food**, **shelter**, **education**, **care**, and **protection**. Adults must provide these **needs** so children grow safe and strong.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are **child rights**? A: Things every child must have: food, shelter, education, care, protection.
chunks.source: Things every child must have: food, shelter, education, care, protection.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List three **needs** from the lesson. A: Food, shelter, education (also care, protection).
chunks.source: Food, shelter, education (also care, protection).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is **education** a right? A: It helps children learn, read, and build a good future.
chunks.source: It helps children learn, read, and build a good future.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who provides **protection** for children? A: Parents, elders, chairperson, police, teachers.
chunks.source: Parents, elders, chairperson, police, teachers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain the difference between a **need** and a **want** in your own words. A: A **need** is something you must have to live and grow, like food and shelter. A **want** is something nice to have but not necessary, like a toy or soda.
chunks.source: A **need** is something you must have to live and grow, like food and shelter. A **want** is something nice to have but not necessary, like a toy or soda.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Solving Problems Peacefully. I can solve problems peacefully by talking and listening. Solve problems with **talk**, **listen**, **forgiveness**, and **request** help. **Report** big problems to an **elder** or **chairperson** for **peace**. Keywords: forgiveness: letting go of anger; request: asking politely; talk: speak to solve a problem; listen: hear with care; elder: older respected person; chairperson: leader of the village; report: tell a leader about a problem
chunks.source: Solve problems with **talk**, **listen**, **forgiveness**, and **request** help. **Report** big problems to an **elder** or **chairperson** for **peace**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the first step to solve a problem peacefully? A: **Talk** calmly.
chunks.source: **Talk** calmly.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **listen** mean in a dispute? A: Hear the other person with care and respect.
chunks.source: Hear the other person with care and respect.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who can help if a problem is too big for children? A: An **elder**, **chairperson**, teacher, or parent.
chunks.source: An **elder**, **chairperson**, teacher, or parent.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a **request**? A: Asking politely for something or for **forgiveness**.
chunks.source: Asking politely for something or for **forgiveness**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain how **forgiveness** brings **peace** in your own words. A: **Forgiveness** means letting go of anger after someone says sorry. When we **forgive**, hearts feel light and **peace** returns.
chunks.source: **Forgiveness** means letting go of anger after someone says sorry. When we **forgive**, hearts feel light and **peace** returns.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Our Culture and Customs. I can name parts of culture and explain why they matter. Our **culture** includes **custom**, **tradition**, **rites**, **values**, **language**, and **dress** that we share and keep alive. Keywords: culture: way of life of a group; custom: a usual way people do things; tradition: a belief or practice passed down; rites: special ceremonies or actions; values: ideas about what is good; language: words people use to talk; dress: clothes worn for special times
chunks.source: Our **culture** includes **custom**, **tradition**, **rites**, **values**, **language**, and **dress** that we share and keep alive.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **culture**? A: Culture is the way a group of people live, think, and behave.
chunks.source: Culture is the way a group of people live, think, and behave.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of a **custom** in Uganda. A: Greeting elders with a bow is a custom.
chunks.source: Greeting elders with a bow is a custom.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one **tradition** you know. A: The Imbalu circumcision ceremony is a tradition.
chunks.source: The Imbalu circumcision ceremony is a tradition.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are **values** important? A: Values guide us to do good and live together peacefully.
chunks.source: Values guide us to do good and live together peacefully.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what **language** means. A: Language is the words and sounds people use to talk and understand each other.
chunks.source: Language is the words and sounds people use to talk and understand each other.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What do people wear for a **dress** during a festival? A: They wear colourful traditional clothes.
chunks.source: They wear colourful traditional clothes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Roles of Boys and Girls. I can describe how boys and girls can share, help, and respect each other equally. Boys and girls have the same **gender** rights; they **share**, **help**, **respect**, and treat each other **equal**. Keywords: gender: being a boy or a girl; boy: a male child; girl: a female child; share: to give part to others; respect: to treat others kindly; help: to give a hand; equal: the same for everyone
chunks.source: Boys and girls have the same **gender** rights; they **share**, **help**, **respect**, and treat each other **equal**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **gender** mean? A: Gender means being a boy or a girl.
chunks.source: Gender means being a boy or a girl.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of how a **boy** can **help** at home. A: A boy can help by fetching water.
chunks.source: A boy can help by fetching water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why should a **girl** and a **boy** **share** chores? A: Sharing chores makes work fair and builds teamwork.
chunks.source: Sharing chores makes work fair and builds teamwork.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what **respect** looks like. A: Respect is listening, speaking kindly, and caring about others' feelings.
chunks.source: Respect is listening, speaking kindly, and caring about others' feelings.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **equal** mean in a game? A: Equal means everyone gets the same turn and chance.
chunks.source: Equal means everyone gets the same turn and chance.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can children **help** each other at school? A: They can help by sharing books and explaining lessons.
chunks.source: They can help by sharing books and explaining lessons.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Keeping Our Culture Alive. I can explain how preservation and promotion keep music, dance, stories, food, and festivals alive. We keep our culture alive through **preservation**, **promotion**, **music**, **dance**, **stories**, **food**, and **festivals**. Keywords: preservation: keeping something safe for future; promotion: showing and sharing something widely; music: sounds made by singing or instruments; dance: moving body to rhythm; stories: tales told to teach or entertain; food: what people eat to live; festivals: big celebrations with music and food
chunks.source: We keep our culture alive through **preservation**, **promotion**, **music**, **dance**, **stories**, **food**, and **festivals**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **preservation**? A: Preservation is keeping something safe for the future.
chunks.source: Preservation is keeping something safe for the future.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of **promotion** of culture. A: Holding a cultural festival promotes our culture.
chunks.source: Holding a cultural festival promotes our culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name a traditional **music** instrument in Uganda. A: The adungu is a traditional music instrument.
chunks.source: The adungu is a traditional music instrument.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are **stories** important for **preservation**? A: Stories carry history and values to the next generation.
chunks.source: Stories carry history and values to the next generation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what **festivals** do for a community. A: Festivals bring people together to celebrate and share culture.
chunks.source: Festivals bring people together to celebrate and share culture.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can we practice **food** **preservation** at home? A: We can dry or smoke food to preserve it.
chunks.source: We can dry or smoke food to preserve it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Health Services in Our Sub-County. I can name the health places in my sub-county and say who works there. Our sub-county has a hospital, health centre, and dispensary. Doctors and nurses work there. They give medicine and immunisation to keep us healthy. Keywords: hospital: a big place where sick people get help; health centre: a smaller place for check-ups and treatment; nurse: a person who cares for patients and gives medicine; doctor: a person who finds out what sickness you have; medicine: something you take to get well; immunisation: an injection that stops you from getting sick; dispensary: a small room where medicine is given out
chunks.source: Our sub-county has a hospital, health centre, and dispensary. Doctors and nurses work there. They give medicine and immunisation to keep us healthy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do you go for an injection that stops sickness? A: The health centre for immunisation.
chunks.source: The health centre for immunisation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who gives out medicine at the dispensary? A: The nurse gives out medicine.
chunks.source: The nurse gives out medicine.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the big building on the main road called? A: It is called the hospital.
chunks.source: It is called the hospital.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who finds out what sickness you have? A: The doctor finds out what sickness you have.
chunks.source: The doctor finds out what sickness you have.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words the difference between a hospital and a health centre. A: A hospital is big for very sick people. A health centre is smaller for check-ups and immunisation.
chunks.source: A hospital is big for very sick people. A health centre is smaller for check-ups and immunisation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a nurse do? A: A nurse cares for patients and gives medicine.
chunks.source: A nurse cares for patients and gives medicine.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Common Diseases and Prevention. I can name common diseases and say how to prevent them. Malaria comes from mosquitoes. Sleep under a net. Drink clean boiled water. Wash hands with soap. These preventions stop diseases. Keywords: diseases: sicknesses that spread from person to person; malaria: a disease from mosquito bites that causes fever; prevention: doing things to stop sickness before it starts; mosquito net: a net over the bed that keeps mosquitoes out; clean water: water that is boiled or treated so it has no germs; hygiene: keeping your body and home clean to stop germs; wash: to clean with water and soap
chunks.source: Malaria comes from mosquitoes. Sleep under a net. Drink clean boiled water. Wash hands with soap. These preventions stop diseases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What disease do mosquitoes spread? A: Malaria.
chunks.source: Malaria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do you prevent mosquito bites at night? A: Sleep under a mosquito net.
chunks.source: Sleep under a mosquito net.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we boil drinking water? A: To kill germs and make clean water.
chunks.source: To kill germs and make clean water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: When should you wash your hands with soap? A: After the latrine and before eating.
chunks.source: After the latrine and before eating.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what prevention means. A: Prevention means doing things to stop sickness before it starts, like using a mosquito net and drinking clean water.
chunks.source: Prevention means doing things to stop sickness before it starts, like using a mosquito net and drinking clean water.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two diseases stopped by good hygiene. A: Diarrhoea and cholera.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea and cholera.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Keeping Our Community Healthy. I can describe a healthy routine and name ways to keep our village clean. A community routine and timetable keep us healthy. Sanitation, safe water, covered latrine, no rubbish, and exercise stop diseases. Keywords: routine: a plan of things you do every day; timetable: a written plan showing when to do each task; sanitation: keeping the place clean and safe from germs; latrine: a toilet pit for human waste; rubbish: things we throw away like peelings and papers; safe water: water that is clean and covered for drinking; exercise: moving your body to stay strong and healthy
chunks.source: A community routine and timetable keep us healthy. Sanitation, safe water, covered latrine, no rubbish, and exercise stop diseases.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a routine? A: A plan of things you do every day.
chunks.source: A plan of things you do every day.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does sanitation mean? A: Keeping the place clean and safe from germs.
chunks.source: Keeping the place clean and safe from germs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do we put rubbish? A: In the rubbish pit and burn it.
chunks.source: In the rubbish pit and burn it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is exercise important? A: It keeps your body strong and healthy.
chunks.source: It keeps your body strong and healthy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how a timetable helps the community. A: A timetable shows when to do each task so everyone remembers and works together.
chunks.source: A timetable shows when to do each task so everyone remembers and works together.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is safe water? A: Water that is clean and covered for drinking.
chunks.source: Water that is clean and covered for drinking.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Natural and Artificial Materials. I can name natural and artificial materials and say where they come from. **Natural** materials like **wood**, **clay**, **metal**, and **grass** come from nature. **Artificial** materials like **plastic** are made by people in factories. Keywords: natural: comes from nature, not made by people; artificial: made by people, not found in nature; wood: hard material from tree trunks and branches; clay: soft, sticky earth used for making pots; metal: strong, shiny material dug from the ground; plastic: light artificial material used for many things; grass: green plants that grow on the ground
chunks.source: **Natural** materials like **wood**, **clay**, **metal**, and **grass** come from nature. **Artificial** materials like **plastic** are made by people in factories.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name three **natural** materials from the lesson. A: **Wood**, **clay**, **metal**, **grass** (any three).
chunks.source: **Wood**, **clay**, **metal**, **grass** (any three).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which material is **artificial**: **wood** or **plastic**? A: **Plastic** is **artificial**.
chunks.source: **Plastic** is **artificial**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where does **clay** come from? A: **Clay** comes from the earth/ground.
chunks.source: **Clay** comes from the earth/ground.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Is a **metal** roof **natural** or **artificial**? Explain why. A: **Metal** is **natural** because it is dug from the ground.
chunks.source: **Metal** is **natural** because it is dug from the ground.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Find one **artificial** thing in your home. What is it made of? A: Answers vary. Example: A bucket made of **plastic**.
chunks.source: Answers vary. Example: A bucket made of **plastic**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In your own words, what is the difference between **natural** and **artificial** materials? A: **Natural** materials come from nature. **Artificial** materials are made by people.
chunks.source: **Natural** materials come from nature. **Artificial** materials are made by people.

chunks.id: L-P3-Social-Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.text: Simple Tools and Machines People Use. I can name simple tools and machines used in our sub-county and say what they do. **Technology** means tools and **machines** that help us. **Hoe** and **panga** are tools. **Bicycle**, **radio**, and **phone** are **machines** with moving parts. Keywords: technology: tools and machines that help people do work; hoe: tool with a metal blade for digging soil; panga: big knife for cutting grass and branches; bicycle: two-wheeled machine people ride; radio: machine that plays news and music; phone: machine for talking to people far away; machine: thing with moving parts that does work
chunks.source: **Technology** means tools and **machines** that help us. **Hoe** and **panga** are tools. **Bicycle**, **radio**, and **phone** are **machines** with moving parts.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.text: Q: Name two simple tools from the lesson. A: **Hoe** and **panga**.
chunks.source: **Hoe** and **panga**.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.text: Q: Name two simple **machines** from the lesson. A: **Bicycle**, **radio**, **phone** (any two).
chunks.source: **Bicycle**, **radio**, **phone** (any two).

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.text: Q: What **technology** does a farmer use to dig? A: A **hoe**.
chunks.source: A **hoe**.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.text: Q: Why is a **bicycle** called a **machine**? A: It has moving parts like wheels and pedals.
chunks.source: It has moving parts like wheels and pedals.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.text: Q: How does a **phone** help people in the trading centre? A: It lets them talk to customers far away.
chunks.source: It lets them talk to customers far away.

chunks.id: LQ-P3-Social-Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Simple Tools and Machines People Use
chunks.text: Q: In your own words, what does **technology** mean? A: **Technology** means tools and **machines** that help people do work.
chunks.source: **Technology** means tools and **machines** that help people do work.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Making Useful Things. I can follow instructions to make useful things and describe their texture. We use **materials** like **grass** and **clay** to make useful things. Follow **instructions** to make a **basket**, **pot**, **broom**, or **mat**. Each has a different **texture**. Keywords: materials: things used to make other things; instructions: steps that tell you how to do something; basket: container woven from strips of material; pot: round container made of baked clay; broom: brush made of grass or twigs for sweeping; mat: flat woven piece for sitting or sleeping; texture: how something feels when you touch it
chunks.source: We use **materials** like **grass** and **clay** to make useful things. Follow **instructions** to make a **basket**, **pot**, **broom**, or **mat**. Each has a different **texture**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List three **materials** used in the lesson. A: **Grass**, **clay**, banana fibre.
chunks.source: **Grass**, **clay**, banana fibre.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What are **instructions**? A: Steps that tell you how to do something.
chunks.source: Steps that tell you how to do something.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which thing has a rough **texture**: a **mat** or a **pot**? A: A **mat** made of **grass** feels rough.
chunks.source: A **mat** made of **grass** feels rough.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two things you can make from **grass**. A: **Mat** and **broom**.
chunks.source: **Mat** and **broom**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we follow **instructions** when making things? A: So the thing turns out right and works well.
chunks.source: So the thing turns out right and works well.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: In your own words, what is **texture**? A: **Texture** is how something feels when you touch it — rough, smooth, soft, hard.
chunks.source: **Texture** is how something feels when you touch it — rough, smooth, soft, hard.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Forms of Energy We Use. I can name different forms of energy we use at home and school. **Energy** gives us **light**, **heat**, and **power**. We use **firewood**, **charcoal**, and **electricity**. Use them wisely. Keywords: energy: the power to do work; light: brightness that helps us see; heat: warmth that makes things hot; power: strength or force to make things work; firewood: wood cut for burning; charcoal: black fuel made from burnt wood; electricity: power from wires that runs lights and phones
chunks.source: **Energy** gives us **light**, **heat**, and **power**. We use **firewood**, **charcoal**, and **electricity**. Use them wisely.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name three forms of **energy** we use at home. A: **Firewood**, **charcoal**, **electricity**.
chunks.source: **Firewood**, **charcoal**, **electricity**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **energy** give us for cooking? A: **Heat**.
chunks.source: **Heat**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What gives **light** in a bulb? A: **Electricity**.
chunks.source: **Electricity**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why should we not waste **charcoal**? A: It costs money and cuts trees.
chunks.source: It costs money and cuts trees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what **energy** is. A: **Energy** is the power that makes things work, like giving **light**, **heat**, or running machines.
chunks.source: **Energy** is the power that makes things work, like giving **light**, **heat**, or running machines.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Energy from the Sun. I can explain how the sun gives us clean energy. The **sun** gives **light**. A **panel** catches it to make **solar power**. **Solar power** is **clean** and helps **saving**. Keywords: solar: from the sun; solar power: energy caught from sunlight; sun: the big star that gives light and heat; light: brightness from the sun or a lamp; panel: flat board that catches sunlight; saving: keeping something for later, not wasting; clean: not dirty, safe for air and land
chunks.source: The **sun** gives **light**. A **panel** catches it to make **solar power**. **Solar power** is **clean** and helps **saving**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **solar** mean? A: From the **sun**.
chunks.source: From the **sun**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a **panel** catch? A: **Light** from the **sun**.
chunks.source: **Light** from the **sun**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is **solar power** **clean**? A: No smoke, no burning.
chunks.source: No smoke, no burning.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does a **solar** lamp help **saving**? A: Free **light**, no fuel cost.
chunks.source: Free **light**, no fuel cost.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how the **sun** gives us **energy**. A: The **sun** shines on a **panel**. The **panel** catches **light** and makes **solar power** for **clean** **energy**.
chunks.source: The **sun** shines on a **panel**. The **panel** catches **light** and makes **solar power** for **clean** **energy**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Using Energy Safely. I can describe dangers of energy and how to use it with care. **Energy** has **dangers**. **Fire** and **electricity** need **care**. **Switch off** to stop **waste**. **Saving** **energy** keeps us safe. Keywords: dangers: things that can hurt you; waste: using more than needed; saving: keeping safe, not wasting; switch off: turn the power off; fire: hot flames that burn; use: to put something to work; care: being careful and safe
chunks.source: **Energy** has **dangers**. **Fire** and **electricity** need **care**. **Switch off** to stop **waste**. **Saving** **energy** keeps us safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two **dangers** of **fire**. A: Burns, house fire.
chunks.source: Burns, house fire.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **switch off** mean? A: Turn the power off.
chunks.source: Turn the power off.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is **waste** bad? A: Costs money, harms nature.
chunks.source: Costs money, harms nature.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do you show **care** with a hot stove? A: Keep away, use dry cloth, tell adult.
chunks.source: Keep away, use dry cloth, tell adult.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how to **use** **electricity** with **care**. A: Dry hands, do not touch broken wires, **switch off** when done, do not overload sockets.
chunks.source: Dry hands, do not touch broken wires, **switch off** when done, do not overload sockets.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Describing People. I can describe people using present simple sentences. We use present simple (I am, She is) to describe people with adjectives like tall, short, thin, smart, beautiful, kind, good. Keywords: tall: high in height; short: small in height; thin: not thick, slender; smart: clever, neat; beautiful: very pretty; kind: nice, caring; good: well behaved
chunks.source: We use present simple (I am, She is) to describe people with adjectives like tall, short, thin, smart, beautiful, kind, good.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: I ___ tall. A: am
chunks.source: am

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: She ___ kind. A: is
chunks.source: is

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct sentence: (a) I am short (b) I short (c) Am I short A: a
chunks.source: a

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct sentence for Peter: (a) Peter is smart (b) Peter smart (c) Is Peter smart A: a
chunks.source: a

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how we describe a person in present simple. A: We use I am or He/She is followed by an adjective.
chunks.source: We use I am or He/She is followed by an adjective.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Make a sentence about your friend using She is. A: She is beautiful.
chunks.source: She is beautiful.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Describing Objects. I can ask and answer questions about objects using size, shape and colour. We ask about objects with Is it ...? and What colour is it? and answer with It is ... or It is not ... Keywords: round: shaped like a circle; oval: egg shaped; triangular: three sided; rectangular: four sides with right angles; flat: level, not raised; long: having great length; colour: the hue of something
chunks.source: We ask about objects with Is it ...? and What colour is it? and answer with It is ... or It is not ...

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the question: ___ it round? A: Is
chunks.source: Is

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the question: What ___ is it? A: colour
chunks.source: colour

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose correct question: (a) Is it oval? (b) Oval it is? (c) It is oval? A: a
chunks.source: a

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Answer: Is the box rectangular? -> ___ A: Yes, it is.
chunks.source: Yes, it is.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how to ask about an object's colour. A: We say What colour is it?
chunks.source: We say What colour is it?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Make a question about a long object. A: Is it long?
chunks.source: Is it long?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Comparing People and Things. I can compare people and things using comparatives and superlatives. We compare with -er/-est: heavier/heaviest, harder/hardest, softer/softest, rougher/roughest, smoother/smoothest, blacker/blackest, browner/brownest. Keywords: heavy: weighs a lot; hard: firm, not soft; soft: easy to press; rough: not smooth; smooth: even surface; black: darkest colour; brown: colour of soil
chunks.source: We compare with -er/-est: heavier/heaviest, harder/hardest, softer/softest, rougher/roughest, smoother/smoothest, blacker/blackest, browner/brownest.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the comparative of hard. A: harder
chunks.source: harder

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write the superlative of soft. A: softest
chunks.source: softest

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose correct sentence: (a) This rock is heavier than that. (b) This rock is more heavy than that. (c) This rock is heavy than that. A: a
chunks.source: a

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The ______ seed is the blackest. A: blackest
chunks.source: blackest

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how to form the superlative of a short adjective. A: Add -est to the adjective.
chunks.source: Add -est to the adjective.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Make a comparative sentence about two brown objects. A: This twig is browner than that one.
chunks.source: This twig is browner than that one.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Where Places Are. I can say where places are using near, far, across, opposite, middle, next to, behind. We use near, far, across, opposite, middle, next to, behind to tell where places are. The pattern is: The place is location word the other place. Grown-up card: Ask your child to describe where the kitchen, latrine, and water source are at home. Keywords: near: close to; far: a long way from; across: on the other side of; opposite: facing each other; middle: in the centre; next to: beside; behind: at the back of
chunks.source: We use near, far, across, opposite, middle, next to, behind to tell where places are. The pattern is: The place is location word the other place. Grown-up card: Ask your child to describe where the kitchen, latrine, and water source are at home.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The well is in the ______ of the compound. A: middle
chunks.source: middle

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The latrine is ______ the kitchen. A: behind
chunks.source: behind

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The shop is ______ the road from the market. A: across
chunks.source: across

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The mosque is ______ the church. A: opposite
chunks.source: opposite

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The kitchen is ______ the main house. A: next to
chunks.source: next to

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The hospital is ______ from our village. A: far
chunks.source: far

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The borehole is ______ the school gate. A: near
chunks.source: near

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: What does 'opposite' mean? A: It means two things face each other, like the mosque and the church across the road.
chunks.source: It means two things face each other, like the mosque and the church across the road.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Giving Directions. I can give directions using turn left, turn right, go straight, at the corner, at the junction, follow the signpost. Give clear directions with: Go straight. Turn left at the corner/junction/signpost. Turn right at the corner/junction/signpost. Grown-up card: Ask your child to direct you from home to the trading centre or borehole using the new words. Keywords: turn: change direction; left: the side of your heart; right: the other side; straight: forward without turning; signpost: a sign showing the way; corner: where two roads meet; junction: where three or more roads meet
chunks.source: Give clear directions with: Go straight. Turn left at the corner/junction/signpost. Turn right at the corner/junction/signpost. Grown-up card: Ask your child to direct you from home to the trading centre or borehole using the new words.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: At the ______, turn left. A: junction
chunks.source: junction

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Go ______ past the signpost. A: straight
chunks.source: straight

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Turn ______ at the corner near the mosque. A: right
chunks.source: right

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Turn ______ at the junction. A: left
chunks.source: left

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Follow the ______ to the hospital. A: signpost
chunks.source: signpost

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: What is the difference between a corner and a junction? A: A corner is where two roads meet. A junction is where three or more roads meet.
chunks.source: A corner is where two roads meet. A junction is where three or more roads meet.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a direction from your home to the nearest shop using turn, left, right, straight. A: Example: Go straight from the gate. Turn left at the corner. The shop is straight ahead.
chunks.source: Example: Go straight from the gate. Turn left at the corner. The shop is straight ahead.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The school is ______ ahead. A: straight
chunks.source: straight

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Reading a Simple Map. I can read a simple map and follow a route from home to school passing the church, hospital, market, and bridge. A map shows places from above. A route is the path you follow. Landmarks like church, hospital, market, bridge help you know where to turn. Grown-up card: Ask your child to trace the route on a map and tell you the landmarks in order. Keywords: map: a drawing of places from above; route: the path you follow; church: a place of worship; hospital: where sick people go; market: where people buy and sell; bridge: a way over a river or valley
chunks.source: A map shows places from above. A route is the path you follow. Landmarks like church, hospital, market, bridge help you know where to turn. Grown-up card: Ask your child to trace the route on a map and tell you the landmarks in order.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: A ______ shows places from above. A: map
chunks.source: map

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The ______ is the path you follow. A: route
chunks.source: route

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: Pass the ______ on your left first. A: church
chunks.source: church

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The ______ is on your right at the junction. A: hospital
chunks.source: hospital

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The ______ is opposite the hospital. A: market
chunks.source: market

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: ______ the bridge to cross the river. A: Cross
chunks.source: Cross

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: How do you use a map to find your way? A: You look at the map, find your start and end points, follow the route line, and use landmarks like church, hospital, market, bridge to know where to turn.
chunks.source: You look at the map, find your start and end points, follow the route line, and use landmarks like church, hospital, market, bridge to know where to turn.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Draw a simple map from your home to school. Mark the church, market, and any bridge. A: undefined

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: What I Like. I can say what I like using I like, I enjoy, and I prefer. We use I like, I enjoy, and I prefer to talk about activities we enjoy such as reading, singing, dancing, cooking, and playing. Keywords: enjoy: to take pleasure in; prefer: to like one thing more; reading: looking at books; singing: making music with voice; dancing: moving to music; cooking: preparing food; playing: doing a game or sport
chunks.source: We use I like, I enjoy, and I prefer to talk about activities we enjoy such as reading, singing, dancing, cooking, and playing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Make a sentence using I enjoy and one activity. A: I enjoy reading.
chunks.source: I enjoy reading.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Make a sentence using I prefer and one activity. A: I prefer playing football.
chunks.source: I prefer playing football.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what I like cooking means. A: It means you find cooking pleasant.
chunks.source: It means you find cooking pleasant.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct form: I ____ dancing. (like / enjoy) A: I enjoy dancing.
chunks.source: I enjoy dancing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence with I like and an activity. A: I like singing.
chunks.source: I like singing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence with I prefer and an activity. A: I prefer cooking.
chunks.source: I prefer cooking.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Foods and Drinks I Like. I can talk about foods and drinks I like and do not like. We use I like ... but I don't like ... to talk about foods, fruits, and drinks such as soda, milk, and tea. Keywords: foods: things we eat; fruits: sweet plant foods; drinks: liquids we drink; soda: sweet fizzy drink; milk: white liquid from cows; tea: hot drink from leaves
chunks.source: We use I like ... but I don't like ... to talk about foods, fruits, and drinks such as soda, milk, and tea.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Make a sentence: I like ____ but I don't like ____. A: I like mangoes but I don't like cassava.
chunks.source: I like mangoes but I don't like cassava.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Make a sentence about a drink you like and one you don't. A: I like milk but I don't like soda.
chunks.source: I like milk but I don't like soda.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what 'I like tea but I don't like coffee' means. A: It means you enjoy tea and you do not enjoy coffee.
chunks.source: It means you enjoy tea and you do not enjoy coffee.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct word: I like ____ but I don't like ____. (soda / milk) A: I like milk but I don't like soda.
chunks.source: I like milk but I don't like soda.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence using 'I like' with a food. A: I like rice.
chunks.source: I like rice.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence using 'I don't like' with a fruit. A: I don't like pineapple.
chunks.source: I don't like pineapple.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: How I Feel. I can express my feelings using I feel and she is. We use I feel, she is, he feels, they are, we feel, I am, you are to describe feelings like happy, sad, tired, angry, scared, worried, thirsty. Keywords: happy: feeling joy; sad: feeling sorrow; tired: needing rest; angry: feeling mad; scared: feeling fear; worried: feeling anxious; thirsty: needing water
chunks.source: We use I feel, she is, he feels, they are, we feel, I am, you are to describe feelings like happy, sad, tired, angry, scared, worried, thirsty.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Make a sentence: I feel ____ when I play. A: I feel happy when I play.
chunks.source: I feel happy when I play.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Make a sentence: She is ____ when it rains. A: She is sad when it rains.
chunks.source: She is sad when it rains.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what 'He feels tired' means. A: It means he is exhausted.
chunks.source: It means he is exhausted.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct form: They ____ angry when the ball is lost. (are / is) A: They are angry when the ball is lost.
chunks.source: They are angry when the ball is lost.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence using 'I am' with a feeling. A: I am worried about the test.
chunks.source: I am worried about the test.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence using 'You are' with a feeling. A: You are thirsty after running.
chunks.source: You are thirsty after running.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: How Others Feel. I can identify how others feel and respond kindly. We identify feelings like cold, hot, ill, lazy, unhappy, hungry and respond with appropriate caring actions. Keywords: cold: feeling low temperature; hot: feeling high temperature; ill: not well, sick; lazy: not wanting to work; unhappy: not happy; hungry: needing food
chunks.source: We identify feelings like cold, hot, ill, lazy, unhappy, hungry and respond with appropriate caring actions.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match the feeling to the response: cold -> ____ A: blanket
chunks.source: blanket

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Match the feeling to the response: hungry -> ____ A: food
chunks.source: food

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what you would do if someone is ill. A: Take them to the clinic.
chunks.source: Take them to the clinic.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct response for hot: give ____ A: water
chunks.source: water

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence: She is ____ so we ____ . A: She is lazy so we encourage her.
chunks.source: She is lazy so we encourage her.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence: They are ____ so we ____ . A: They are unhappy so we listen.
chunks.source: They are unhappy so we listen.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Polite Words. I can use polite words when greeting and thanking people. Polite words **please**, **thank**, **sorry**, **excuse**, **forgive**, **welcome**, **pardon** make our days smooth and kind. Use them at home, school, and the market. Keywords: please: a polite word when asking; thank: to show gratitude; sorry: to show regret; excuse: to get attention politely; forgive: to stop being angry; welcome: a friendly greeting; pardon: to ask someone to repeat
chunks.source: Polite words **please**, **thank**, **sorry**, **excuse**, **forgive**, **welcome**, **pardon** make our days smooth and kind. Use them at home, school, and the market.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: "___ me, may I have some posho?" A: **Excuse** me, may I have some posho?
chunks.source: **Excuse** me, may I have some posho?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: "___ you for the lift on the boda boda." A: **Thank** you for the lift on the boda boda.
chunks.source: **Thank** you for the lift on the boda boda.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: "I am ___ for breaking your cup." A: I am **sorry** for breaking your cup.
chunks.source: I am **sorry** for breaking your cup.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: "___ me, I did not hear the question." A: **Pardon** me, I did not hear the question.
chunks.source: **Pardon** me, I did not hear the question.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: "You are ___ to stay for supper." A: You are **welcome** to stay for supper.
chunks.source: You are **welcome** to stay for supper.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: When do we use **forgive**? A: We use **forgive** when we want someone to stop being angry after a mistake.
chunks.source: We use **forgive** when we want someone to stop being angry after a mistake.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: What does **welcome** mean? A: **Welcome** means we are happy someone is here or we accept their thanks.
chunks.source: **Welcome** means we are happy someone is here or we accept their thanks.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Asking Politely. I can make polite requests using 'May I ... please?' and respond correctly. Polite requests use **Excuse me, may I ... please?**. **Borrow** = take, **lend** = give. **Help** and **share** make work light. Always **ask** with respect. Keywords: borrow: to take something for a short time; lend: to give something for a short time; please: a polite word when asking; excuse: to get attention politely; help: to assist someone; share: to give a part of yours; ask: to put a question
chunks.source: Polite requests use **Excuse me, may I ... please?**. **Borrow** = take, **lend** = give. **Help** and **share** make work light. Always **ask** with respect.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: "___ me, ___ I ___ your pencil, ___?" A: **Excuse** me, **may I borrow** your pencil, **please**?
chunks.source: **Excuse** me, **may I borrow** your pencil, **please**?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: "Yes, I will ___ it to you." A: Yes, I will **lend** it to you.
chunks.source: Yes, I will **lend** it to you.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: "___ I ___ you carry that box?" A: **May I help** you carry that box?
chunks.source: **May I help** you carry that box?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: "___ we ___ this pineapple?" A: **May we share** this pineapple?
chunks.source: **May we share** this pineapple?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the polite request: A) Give me the ball. B) **May I borrow** the ball, **please**? A: **May I borrow** the ball, **please**?
chunks.source: **May I borrow** the ball, **please**?

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: What is the difference between **borrow** and **lend**? A: **Borrow** is to take for a short time. **Lend** is to give for a short time.
chunks.source: **Borrow** is to take for a short time. **Lend** is to give for a short time.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words: Why do we say **Excuse me** before a request? A: **Excuse me** gets the person's attention politely before we **ask**.
chunks.source: **Excuse me** gets the person's attention politely before we **ask**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Good Behaviour. I can describe good habits using present simple (I share, we greet). Good habits use present simple: **I share**, **we greet**, **he listens**, **she helps**, **they respect**, **I am honest**, **you are kind**. Do them every day. Keywords: share: to give part of yours; help: to assist someone; respect: to treat others well; honest: to tell the truth; kind: to be caring; greet: to say hello politely; listen: to pay attention
chunks.source: Good habits use present simple: **I share**, **we greet**, **he listens**, **she helps**, **they respect**, **I am honest**, **you are kind**. Do them every day.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap with present simple: "We ___ our teachers every morning." A: We **greet** our teachers every morning.
chunks.source: We **greet** our teachers every morning.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: "I ___ when the teacher speaks." A: I **listen** when the teacher speaks.
chunks.source: I **listen** when the teacher speaks.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: "She ___ her lunch with friends." A: She **shares** her lunch with friends.
chunks.source: She **shares** her lunch with friends.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill the gap: "They ___ the elderly with respect." A: They **respect** the elderly with respect.
chunks.source: They **respect** the elderly with respect.
