chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Which breed is white with coloured ears? A: The **californian** rabbit.
chunks.source: The **californian** rabbit.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how to tell an **angora** from a **new zealand**. A: The **angora** has long soft **fur** and short **ear**s. The **new zealand** has short **fur** and long upright **ear**s.
chunks.source: The **angora** has long soft **fur** and short **ear**s. The **new zealand** has short **fur** and long upright **ear**s.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: If you want meat, which breed would you choose? A: **New zealand** or **californian**.
chunks.source: **New zealand** or **californian**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Housing and Feeding Rabbits. I can describe proper rabbit housing and feeding. A good **hutch** is raised, roofed, and has a wire floor to stay **dry** and **clean**. Feed rabbits **pellets** and **grass** twice daily with fresh **water**. Keywords: hutch: a house for rabbits; dry: not wet; pellets: special rabbit food; grass: green plants rabbits eat; water: clean liquid to drink; clean: free from dirt
chunks.source: A good **hutch** is raised, roofed, and has a wire floor to stay **dry** and **clean**. Feed rabbits **pellets** and **grass** twice daily with fresh **water**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What is a rabbit house called? A: A **hutch**.
chunks.source: A **hutch**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why must the **hutch** be **dry**? A: To stop diseases like **coccidiosis**.
chunks.source: To stop diseases like **coccidiosis**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name two foods rabbits need daily. A: **Pellets** and **grass**.
chunks.source: **Pellets** and **grass**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How often should you give **water**? A: Always — fresh **water** must be there all the time.
chunks.source: Always — fresh **water** must be there all the time.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how to keep a **hutch** **clean**. A: Remove droppings daily. Use wire mesh floor so urine falls through. Keep the **hutch** **dry**.
chunks.source: Remove droppings daily. Use wire mesh floor so urine falls through. Keep the **hutch** **dry**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Worked example: 15 rabbits eat 1 bag of **pellets** per week. How many bags for 30 rabbits for 2 weeks? A: 4 bags.
chunks.source: 4 bags.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Rabbit Diseases and Records. I can identify common rabbit diseases and keep farm records. Common rabbit diseases are **snuffles**, **ear canker**, and **coccidiosis**. Call the **vet** for **medicine**. Keep **records** of all sickness and treatments. Keywords: snuffles: a rabbit cold with runny nose; ear canker: sores inside rabbit ears; coccidiosis: a stomach disease in rabbits; records: written notes about the farm; vet: an animal doctor; medicine: drugs to treat sickness
chunks.source: Common rabbit diseases are **snuffles**, **ear canker**, and **coccidiosis**. Call the **vet** for **medicine**. Keep **records** of all sickness and treatments.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What are the signs of **snuffles**? A: Runny nose and sneezing.
chunks.source: Runny nose and sneezing.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does **ear canker** look like? A: Sores inside the **ear**, rabbit scratches and shakes head.
chunks.source: Sores inside the **ear**, rabbit scratches and shakes head.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does **coccidiosis** cause? A: Diarrhoea and weight loss.
chunks.source: Diarrhoea and weight loss.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Who should you call when a rabbit is sick? A: A **vet**.
chunks.source: A **vet**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why **records** are important. A: **Records** help track sickness, show patterns, and give the **vet** the rabbit's history.
chunks.source: **Records** help track sickness, show patterns, and give the **vet** the rabbit's history.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Worked example: 5 rabbits had **snuffles**, 2 had **ear canker**. Total sick = 7. If 3 recover, how many still sick? A: 4 rabbits.
chunks.source: 4 rabbits.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Advantages of Keeping Rabbits. I can explain the benefits of rabbit keeping. Rabbits give **meat**, **manure**, **income**, and **fur**. They grow **quick** and need **small space**, making them ideal for Ugandan homes. Keywords: meat: animal flesh used as food; manure: animal waste used as fertiliser; income: money earned from selling; fur: soft hair used for clothing; quick: fast, in a short time; small space: little room needed
chunks.source: Rabbits give **meat**, **manure**, **income**, and **fur**. They grow **quick** and need **small space**, making them ideal for Ugandan homes.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Name four products from rabbits. A: **Meat**, **manure**, **income**, **fur**.
chunks.source: **Meat**, **manure**, **income**, **fur**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Why are rabbits good for small farms? A: They need **small space** and grow **quick**.
chunks.source: They need **small space** and grow **quick**.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: How does rabbit **manure** help the farm? A: It makes soil rich for crops.
chunks.source: It makes soil rich for crops.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: What does **income** mean? A: Money earned from selling.
chunks.source: Money earned from selling.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why rabbits grow **quick**. A: Rabbits mature in 3-4 months and does have many babies per year.
chunks.source: Rabbits mature in 3-4 months and does have many babies per year.

chunks.subject: Science
chunks.text: Q: Worked example: 8 rabbits give 0.5 kg **manure** each per day. How much **manure** in one week? A: 28 kg.
chunks.source: 28 kg.

chunks.id: L-P4-Social-Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.text: Finding Our District on the Map. I can find my district on a map of Uganda using a compass. A **map** shows places from above. Use the **compass** rose to find **north**, **south**, **east**, **west**. Then you can locate your **district** on the **map** of Uganda. Keywords: map: a drawing of a place from above; district: an area with its own local government; compass: a tool that shows four main directions; north: the direction where the sun rises in Uganda; south: the direction opposite to north; east: the direction where the sun comes up; west: the direction where the sun goes down
chunks.source: A **map** shows places from above. Use the **compass** rose to find **north**, **south**, **east**, **west**. Then you can locate your **district** on the **map** of Uganda.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.text: Q: What does a **map** show? A: A drawing of a place from above.
chunks.source: A drawing of a place from above.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.text: Q: Name the four directions on a **compass**. A: North, south, east, west.
chunks.source: North, south, east, west.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.text: Q: If you face **north**, which direction is on your right? A: **East**.
chunks.source: **East**.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how to find a **district** on a **map**. A: Look at the **compass** rose, then move in the correct direction from a known place.
chunks.source: Look at the **compass** rose, then move in the correct direction from a known place.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.text: Q: What is a **district**? A: An area with its own local government.
chunks.source: An area with its own local government.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.text: Q: Where is the sun in the morning in Uganda? A: In the **east**.
chunks.source: In the **east**.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Finding Our District on the Map
chunks.text: Q: Where is the sun in the evening in Uganda? A: In the **west**.
chunks.source: In the **west**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: The Parts of Our District. I can name the sub-counties, counties, municipalities, and neighbours of my district. A **district** has **counties**, which have **sub-counties**. A **municipality** is a **town** with its own government. The **headquarters** is the main office. **Neighbours** share a **border**. Keywords: sub-county: a small area within a county; county: a group of sub-counties; municipality: a town with its own local government; town: a place where many people live and work; headquarters: the main office of a district or sub-county; neighbour: a district next to yours; border: the line between two districts
chunks.source: A **district** has **counties**, which have **sub-counties**. A **municipality** is a **town** with its own government. The **headquarters** is the main office. **Neighbours** share a **border**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a **sub-county**? A: A small area within a county.
chunks.source: A small area within a county.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a **county**? A: A group of sub-counties.
chunks.source: A group of sub-counties.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name a **municipality** in Wakiso district. A: Entebbe.
chunks.source: Entebbe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words the difference between a **town** and a **municipality**. A: A municipality is a town with its own local government; a town may not have one.
chunks.source: A municipality is a town with its own local government; a town may not have one.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where is the **headquarters** of your district? A: The main office where district leaders work.
chunks.source: The main office where district leaders work.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a **neighbour** district? A: A district next to yours.
chunks.source: A district next to yours.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What marks a **border** between districts? A: A river, road, or imaginary line.
chunks.source: A river, road, or imaginary line.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: The Story of Our District. I can tell the history, origin, population, and size of my district. Every **district** has a **history**. **Elders** know the **origin** of the name. **Population** counts people. **Size** measures land. Keywords: history: the story of what happened long ago; elders: older people who know the past; origin: where something began; population: the number of people living in a place; size: how big a place is; district: an area with its own local government
chunks.source: Every **district** has a **history**. **Elders** know the **origin** of the name. **Population** counts people. **Size** measures land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **history**? A: The story of what happened long ago.
chunks.source: The story of what happened long ago.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who are the **elders**? A: Older people who know the past.
chunks.source: Older people who know the past.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **origin** mean? A: Where something began.
chunks.source: Where something began.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how a district gets its name. A: It is named after a local feature like a hill, river, or tree.
chunks.source: It is named after a local feature like a hill, river, or tree.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **population**? A: The number of people living in a place.
chunks.source: The number of people living in a place.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **size**? A: How big a place is, measured in square kilometres.
chunks.source: How big a place is, measured in square kilometres.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why should we listen to **elders**? A: They know the history and origin of our district.
chunks.source: They know the history and origin of our district.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Important Places in Our District. I can identify the hospital, market, police station, church, mosque, post office, and roads in my district. A **district** needs a **hospital**, **market**, **police station**, **church**, **mosque**, **post office**, and **roads**. They help people live, work, and worship. Keywords: hospital: a place where sick people get treatment; market: a place where people buy and sell goods; police station: a place where police work to keep peace; church: a building where Christians worship; mosque: a building where Muslims worship; post office: a place where letters and parcels are sent; road: a path for vehicles and people to travel
chunks.source: A **district** needs a **hospital**, **market**, **police station**, **church**, **mosque**, **post office**, and **roads**. They help people live, work, and worship.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do sick people go? A: The hospital.
chunks.source: The hospital.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do people buy and sell goods? A: The market.
chunks.source: The market.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where do police work? A: The police station.
chunks.source: The police station.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why a district needs both a church and a mosque. A: People have different faiths; both need a place to worship.
chunks.source: People have different faiths; both need a place to worship.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does the post office do? A: Sends and receives letters and parcels.
chunks.source: Sends and receives letters and parcels.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What connects all important places? A: Roads.
chunks.source: Roads.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two important places near your home. A: Answers vary: e.g., market and church.
chunks.source: Answers vary: e.g., market and church.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Hills, Mountains and Valleys. I can name and describe the main land physical features in our district. Our district has hills, mountains, valleys, plains, plateaus, and the rift valley. Each landform has a special shape and use. Keywords: hill: high land with a rounded top; mountain: very high land with a steep peak; valley: low land between hills or mountains; plain: flat land that stretches far; rift valley: long valley with steep sides; plateau: high flat land like a table; landform: natural shape of the earth's surface
chunks.source: Our district has hills, mountains, valleys, plains, plateaus, and the rift valley. Each landform has a special shape and use.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name three landforms you can see near your home. A: Hill, valley, plain (or mountain, plateau, rift valley if in western Uganda)
chunks.source: Hill, valley, plain (or mountain, plateau, rift valley if in western Uganda)

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the difference between a hill and a mountain? A: A mountain is higher and steeper than a hill.
chunks.source: A mountain is higher and steeper than a hill.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where is the Albertine Rift Valley found? A: Along Uganda's western border with DR Congo.
chunks.source: Along Uganda's western border with DR Congo.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what a plateau is. A: High flat land like a table.
chunks.source: High flat land like a table.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which landform is best for grazing cattle? A: A plain because it is wide and flat.
chunks.source: A plain because it is wide and flat.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Draw a valley between two hills. Label the hill, valley, and a river. A: undefined

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Rivers, Lakes and Dams. I can identify water physical features and explain where they are found in our district. Rivers, lakes, dams, ponds, streams, waterfalls, and sources are water features. They give us water, power, fish, and beauty. Keywords: river: large natural flow of water; lake: large body of water surrounded by land; dam: wall built across a river to hold water; pond: small body of still water; stream: small narrow flow of water; waterfall: water falling from a height; source: place where a river begins
chunks.source: Rivers, lakes, dams, ponds, streams, waterfalls, and sources are water features. They give us water, power, fish, and beauty.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the largest lake in Uganda. A: Lake Victoria
chunks.source: Lake Victoria

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where does the River Nile begin? A: At its source in Jinja, on Lake Victoria.
chunks.source: At its source in Jinja, on Lake Victoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the difference between a river and a stream? A: A river is larger; a stream is small and narrow.
chunks.source: A river is larger; a stream is small and narrow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what a dam does. A: A dam holds back river water to store it or make electricity.
chunks.source: A dam holds back river water to store it or make electricity.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which water feature is made by people, not nature? A: A dam.
chunks.source: A dam.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List two waterfalls in Uganda. A: Sipi Falls and Murchison Falls (or any other known waterfalls).
chunks.source: Sipi Falls and Murchison Falls (or any other known waterfalls).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are ponds useful near homes? A: For fish farming, watering animals, or irrigation.
chunks.source: For fish farming, watering animals, or irrigation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: How Physical Features Help Us. I can explain how physical features provide resources and income for our community. Physical features give us fishing, farming land, water, minerals, stones, sand, and tourism. They support our daily life and economy. Keywords: fishing: catching fish for food or sale; farming: growing crops and keeping animals; water: clean water for drinking and cooking; minerals: valuable substances from the ground; stones: hard rocks used for building; sand: fine grains from rocks or rivers; tourism: visitors coming to see places
chunks.source: Physical features give us fishing, farming land, water, minerals, stones, sand, and tourism. They support our daily life and economy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two products we get from lakes. A: Fish and water (also transport, tourism)
chunks.source: Fish and water (also transport, tourism)

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How do hills help in building houses? A: They provide stones and sand from quarries.
chunks.source: They provide stones and sand from quarries.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is tourism? A: Visitors coming to see places, bringing money.
chunks.source: Visitors coming to see places, bringing money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why valleys are good for farming. A: They have rich soil and water collected from hills.
chunks.source: They have rich soil and water collected from hills.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which physical feature brings visitors to Bwindi? A: The mountain forest (gorillas).
chunks.source: The mountain forest (gorillas).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List three building materials from physical features. A: Stones, sand, water (for mixing)
chunks.source: Stones, sand, water (for mixing)

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does the River Nile help Jinja town? A: Source of Nile tourism, fishing, water, electricity from dams.
chunks.source: Source of Nile tourism, fishing, water, electricity from dams.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Dangers and Caring for Features. I can identify dangers from physical features and describe ways to protect them. Floods, landslides, and erosion are dangers from physical features. We protect, clean, and care for land by planting trees, terracing, and keeping water sources clean. Keywords: flood: water covering dry land; landslide: soil and rocks sliding down a slope; erosion: soil being washed or blown away; danger: something that can cause harm; protect: keep safe from harm; clean: free from dirt or rubbish; care: look after something well
chunks.source: Floods, landslides, and erosion are dangers from physical features. We protect, clean, and care for land by planting trees, terracing, and keeping water sources clean.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two dangers that happen on steep hills after heavy rain. A: Landslide and erosion
chunks.source: Landslide and erosion

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a flood? A: Water covering dry land when rivers overflow.
chunks.source: Water covering dry land when rivers overflow.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does planting trees protect a hill? A: Roots hold soil, stopping erosion and landslides.
chunks.source: Roots hold soil, stopping erosion and landslides.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why we should keep lakes clean. A: Dirty water harms fish, makes people sick, and spoils tourism.
chunks.source: Dirty water harms fish, makes people sick, and spoils tourism.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What can children do to care for a nearby spring? A: Pick rubbish, do not wash clothes in it, plant grass around it.
chunks.source: Pick rubbish, do not wash clothes in it, plant grass around it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List three ways to reduce flood danger in a valley. A: Keep wetlands, plant trees uphill, build proper drainage.
chunks.source: Keep wetlands, plant trees uphill, build proper drainage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is it dangerous to build houses at the foot of a bare hill? A: Landslides can bury the houses.
chunks.source: Landslides can bury the houses.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Forests, Grass and Swamps. I can name the main types of vegetation in my district. Our district has forests, grasslands, swamps, shrubs, savanna, and crops. Some grow naturally; people plant others. Keywords: vegetation: all plants growing in an area; forest: large area with many tall trees; grassland: open land covered mostly with grass; swamp: wet land where water stays long; shrub: small bushy plants; savanna: grassland with scattered trees; crops: plants grown by people for food
chunks.source: Our district has forests, grasslands, swamps, shrubs, savanna, and crops. Some grow naturally; people plant others.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name three types of natural vegetation in your district. A: Forest, grassland, swamp, shrub, savanna
chunks.source: Forest, grassland, swamp, shrub, savanna

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the difference between a forest and a savanna? A: A forest has many tall trees close together. A savanna has grass with scattered trees.
chunks.source: A forest has many tall trees close together. A savanna has grass with scattered trees.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of crops grown in Uganda. A: Maize, beans, matooke, cassava, sweet potatoes
chunks.source: Maize, beans, matooke, cassava, sweet potatoes

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what vegetation means. A: Vegetation means all the plants growing in an area, both natural and planted.
chunks.source: Vegetation means all the plants growing in an area, both natural and planted.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are swamps important? A: Swamps clean water, give fish, and grow papyrus for crafts.
chunks.source: Swamps clean water, give fish, and grow papyrus for crafts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which vegetation type has small bushy plants? A: Shrub vegetation has many small bushes.
chunks.source: Shrub vegetation has many small bushes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Is a maize garden natural or planted vegetation? A: A maize garden is planted vegetation because people grow it.
chunks.source: A maize garden is planted vegetation because people grow it.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: How Vegetation Helps Us. I can list the main uses of vegetation in daily life. Vegetation gives us medicine, firewood, food, timber, rainfall, oxygen, and shade. All are vital for Ugandan life. Keywords: medicine: herbs used to treat sickness; firewood: wood collected for cooking; food: plants and fruits we eat; timber: wood cut for building; rainfall: rain that falls from clouds; oxygen: clean air we breathe; shade: cool cover from the sun
chunks.source: Vegetation gives us medicine, firewood, food, timber, rainfall, oxygen, and shade. All are vital for Ugandan life.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List four things we get from vegetation. A: Medicine, firewood, food, timber, rainfall, oxygen, shade
chunks.source: Medicine, firewood, food, timber, rainfall, oxygen, shade

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which vegetation product do we use to cook posho? A: Firewood
chunks.source: Firewood

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two fruits that grow wild on trees. A: Mangoes, jackfruit, tamarind, guava
chunks.source: Mangoes, jackfruit, tamarind, guava

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how forests help rainfall. A: Trees release water vapour that rises and forms rain clouds.
chunks.source: Trees release water vapour that rises and forms rain clouds.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What would happen if we had no trees for shade? A: Compounds and markets would be very hot at noon.
chunks.source: Compounds and markets would be very hot at noon.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which use of vegetation is most important for your family? Why? A: Answers vary. Example: Firewood for cooking daily meals.
chunks.source: Answers vary. Example: Firewood for cooking daily meals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Match: timber is used for building, oxygen is for breathing. A: undefined

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: How People Harm Vegetation. I can identify human activities that damage vegetation. Burning, deforestation, overgrazing, overcultivation, brick making, charcoal burning, and clearing all harm vegetation and reduce its benefits. Keywords: burning: setting fire to bush or grass; deforestation: cutting down many trees; overgrazing: too many animals eating grass; overcultivation: farming land without rest; bricks: baked clay blocks for building; charcoal: black fuel made from wood; clearing: removing all plants from land
chunks.source: Burning, deforestation, overgrazing, overcultivation, brick making, charcoal burning, and clearing all harm vegetation and reduce its benefits.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name three human activities that harm vegetation. A: Burning, deforestation, overgrazing, overcultivation, brick making, charcoal burning, clearing
chunks.source: Burning, deforestation, overgrazing, overcultivation, brick making, charcoal burning, clearing

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is deforestation? A: Cutting down many trees without replanting.
chunks.source: Cutting down many trees without replanting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does overgrazing damage grassland? A: Animals eat grass faster than it grows, leaving bare soil.
chunks.source: Animals eat grass faster than it grows, leaving bare soil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why charcoal burning causes deforestation. A: Charcoal needs many trees cut for firewood, so forests disappear.
chunks.source: Charcoal needs many trees cut for firewood, so forests disappear.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which activity harms swamps the most? A: Clearing wetlands for rice or building.
chunks.source: Clearing wetlands for rice or building.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What happens to soil after burning? A: Soil loses organisms, gets exposed to wind and rain, and erodes.
chunks.source: Soil loses organisms, gets exposed to wind and rain, and erodes.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one reason people clear vegetation. A: To make farms, build houses, or get firewood.
chunks.source: To make farms, build houses, or get firewood.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Caring for Our Vegetation. I can describe ways to protect and improve vegetation. Caring for vegetation means planting, watering, adding manure, trimming, and raising seedlings in nurseries. Conservation protects our future. Keywords: planting: putting seeds or seedlings in soil; watering: giving water to plants; manure: animal or plant waste for soil; trimming: cutting branches to shape trees; seedlings: young plants grown from seeds; nursery: place where young plants grow; conservation: protecting nature for the future
chunks.source: Caring for vegetation means planting, watering, adding manure, trimming, and raising seedlings in nurseries. Conservation protects our future.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List four ways to care for vegetation. A: Planting, watering, adding manure, trimming, protecting from fire and grazing
chunks.source: Planting, watering, adding manure, trimming, protecting from fire and grazing

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a nursery? A: A place where young plants (seedlings) are grown until ready for planting.
chunks.source: A place where young plants (seedlings) are grown until ready for planting.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why do we add manure when planting? A: Manure adds nutrients to the soil so seedlings grow strong.
chunks.source: Manure adds nutrients to the soil so seedlings grow strong.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what conservation means. A: Conservation means protecting plants and nature so they last for future generations.
chunks.source: Conservation means protecting plants and nature so they last for future generations.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: When is the best time to water seedlings? A: Early morning or late evening to reduce evaporation.
chunks.source: Early morning or late evening to reduce evaporation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does trimming help a mango tree? A: Trimming lets light and air in, giving more and better fruit.
chunks.source: Trimming lets light and air in, giving more and better fruit.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one conservation activity you can do at school. A: Plant a tree, water seedlings, make a nursery bed, stop burning grass.
chunks.source: Plant a tree, water seedlings, make a nursery bed, stop burning grass.

chunks.id: L-P4-Social-Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.text: Tribes and Clans in Our District. I can name the tribes, clans and languages in our district and explain why we respect each other's culture. A tribe is a large group with shared language and customs. A clan is a family group with a totem. Different ethnic groups live together in our district. Respecting each other's culture brings peace. Keywords: tribe: a large group of people with shared history and language; clan: a family group within a tribe, often with a shared totem; ethnic group: people who share culture, language and ancestors; language: the words and speech used by a group of people; ancestors: family members who lived long before us; customs: the traditional ways a group does things; totem: an animal or plant symbol for a clan
chunks.source: A tribe is a large group with shared language and customs. A clan is a family group with a totem. Different ethnic groups live together in our district. Respecting each other's culture brings peace.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What is a tribe? A: A large group of people with shared history, language and customs.
chunks.source: A large group of people with shared history, language and customs.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What is a clan? A: A family group within a tribe, often with a shared totem.
chunks.source: A family group within a tribe, often with a shared totem.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.text: Q: What does 'ethnic group' mean? A: People who share culture, language and ancestors.
chunks.source: People who share culture, language and ancestors.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of a custom in Uganda. A: Greeting elders respectfully.
chunks.source: Greeting elders respectfully.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why totems are important. A: Totems give clans identity and teach respect for nature.
chunks.source: Totems give clans identity and teach respect for nature.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.text: Q: Name two tribes found in Uganda. A: Baganda and Banyankole (or any other Ugandan tribes).
chunks.source: Baganda and Banyankole (or any other Ugandan tribes).

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Tribes and Clans in Our District
chunks.text: Q: How can children show respect for different cultures at school? A: Learn greetings, share food, listen to stories from other cultures.
chunks.source: Learn greetings, share food, listen to stories from other cultures.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Legends of Our People. I can retell origin legends of Uganda's peoples and explain what they teach about migration and settlement. Legends are traditional stories that explain the origin of tribes. They describe migration, the search for pasture or land, and the first settlement. Uganda's peoples have different legends but similar patterns. Keywords: legend: a traditional story about the past, often explaining origins; origin: the beginning or source of something; migration: movement of people from one place to another; settlement: a place where people make their homes; search: to look carefully for something; pasture: land covered with grass for animals to eat; story: an account of events, real or imagined
chunks.source: Legends are traditional stories that explain the origin of tribes. They describe migration, the search for pasture or land, and the first settlement. Uganda's peoples have different legends but similar patterns.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a legend? A: A traditional story about the past, often explaining origins.
chunks.source: A traditional story about the past, often explaining origins.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does 'origin' mean in a legend? A: The beginning or source of a people or clan.
chunks.source: The beginning or source of a people or clan.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one legend from Buganda. A: Kintu and Nambi.
chunks.source: Kintu and Nambi.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one legend from Bugisu. A: Mundu and Sera.
chunks.source: Mundu and Sera.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one legend from Luo areas. A: Labong and Gipir.
chunks.source: Labong and Gipir.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why people migrate in these legends. A: They search for pasture, fertile land, water or safety.
chunks.source: They search for pasture, fertile land, water or safety.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What three things do origin legends usually include? A: Origin, migration, and first settlement.
chunks.source: Origin, migration, and first settlement.

chunks.id: L-P4-Social-Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.text: Why People Settle Where They Live. I can list and explain the factors that influence where people build settlements in our district. Six main factors influence where people settle: fertile soil, reliable rainfall, security, trade, jobs and services. These factors often work together to create and grow settlements. Keywords: settlement: a place where people live and build homes; fertile: soil that is good for growing crops; rainfall: the amount of rain that falls in a place; security: safety from danger or attack; trade: buying and selling goods; jobs: work that pays money or provides needs; services: things like schools, clinics and water points
chunks.source: Six main factors influence where people settle: fertile soil, reliable rainfall, security, trade, jobs and services. These factors often work together to create and grow settlements.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.text: Q: What is a settlement? A: A place where people live and build homes.
chunks.source: A place where people live and build homes.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.text: Q: Why is fertile soil important for a settlement? A: It allows crops to grow well for food and income.
chunks.source: It allows crops to grow well for food and income.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.text: Q: How does rainfall affect settlement? A: Reliable rainfall means crops get water, so people settle there.
chunks.source: Reliable rainfall means crops get water, so people settle there.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of security influencing settlement. A: People build on hills or in safe areas away from conflict.
chunks.source: People build on hills or in safe areas away from conflict.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how trade creates settlements. A: Markets attract buyers and sellers, so homes and shops grow around them.
chunks.source: Markets attract buyers and sellers, so homes and shops grow around them.

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.text: Q: Name two services that attract people to a settlement. A: School and health centre (or borehole, paved road).
chunks.source: School and health centre (or borehole, paved road).

chunks.id: LQ-P4-Social-Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Why People Settle Where They Live
chunks.text: Q: List all six factors that influence settlement patterns. A: Fertile soil, rainfall, security, trade, jobs, services.
chunks.source: Fertile soil, rainfall, security, trade, jobs, services.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Work and Celebrations. I can describe the main work people do in our district and the social celebrations that bring communities together. Main work in our district includes farming, fishing, pottery and trading. Key celebrations are weddings, naming ceremonies and circumcision. Work provides for celebrations; celebrations unite the community. Keywords: farming: growing crops and keeping animals for food and income; fishing: catching fish from lakes or rivers; pottery: making pots and jars from clay; trading: buying and selling goods at markets; wedding: a ceremony joining two people in marriage; naming: a ceremony to give a baby its name; circumcision: a traditional ceremony for boys becoming men
chunks.source: Main work in our district includes farming, fishing, pottery and trading. Key celebrations are weddings, naming ceremonies and circumcision. Work provides for celebrations; celebrations unite the community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is farming? A: Growing crops and keeping animals for food and income.
chunks.source: Growing crops and keeping animals for food and income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Where is fishing important in Uganda? A: On lakes like Victoria, Kyoga, Albert and on the Nile.
chunks.source: On lakes like Victoria, Kyoga, Albert and on the Nile.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is pottery? A: Making pots and jars from clay.
chunks.source: Making pots and jars from clay.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does trading help a district? A: It moves goods, creates income and links villages to towns.
chunks.source: It moves goods, creates income and links villages to towns.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what happens at a naming ceremony. A: The clan elder gives the baby a name, relatives bring gifts, and everyone shares a meal.
chunks.source: The clan elder gives the baby a name, relatives bring gifts, and everyone shares a meal.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is circumcision celebrated publicly in Bugisu? A: It marks a boy's passage to manhood and the whole community witnesses his courage.
chunks.source: It marks a boy's passage to manhood and the whole community witnesses his courage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are work and celebrations connected? A: Work provides the resources for celebrations; celebrations honour the work and bring people together.
chunks.source: Work provides the resources for celebrations; celebrations honour the work and bring people together.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Political and Civic Leaders. I can name the main political and civic leaders in my district and explain how they are chosen. Our district has political and civic leaders like the chairperson council RDC CAO and magistrates; they are chosen by election or appointment and have the duty to serve the people. Keywords: leadership: guiding others; chairperson: head of the council; council: group of elected members; civic: about the community; election: voting to choose leaders; representative: person who speaks for others; duty: responsibility
chunks.source: Our district has political and civic leaders like the chairperson council RDC CAO and magistrates; they are chosen by election or appointment and have the duty to serve the people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the role of the district chairperson? A: The chairperson leads the council and represents the people.
chunks.source: The chairperson leads the council and represents the people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How are district council members chosen? A: They are chosen by election where citizens vote.
chunks.source: They are chosen by election where citizens vote.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what civic duty means. A: Civic duty is the responsibility to help your community.
chunks.source: Civic duty is the responsibility to help your community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one appointed leader in the district. A: The RDC or CAO is appointed.
chunks.source: The RDC or CAO is appointed.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a representative do? A: A representative speaks for the voters in the council.
chunks.source: A representative speaks for the voters in the council.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is good leadership important? A: Good leadership ensures fair decisions and development.
chunks.source: Good leadership ensures fair decisions and development.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Religious and Voluntary Leaders. I can identify religious and voluntary leaders in my community and describe their roles. Religious leaders such as bishops priests pastors sheikhs and reverends guide faith while volunteers and scouts serve the community. Keywords: bishop: head of many churches; priest: leader of a parish; pastor: leader of a congregation; sheikh: Muslim religious leader; reverend: title for Christian ministers; volunteer: person who helps without pay; scout: member of a youth service group
chunks.source: Religious leaders such as bishops priests pastors sheikhs and reverends guide faith while volunteers and scouts serve the community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a bishop oversee? A: A bishop oversees many churches in a diocese.
chunks.source: A bishop oversees many churches in a diocese.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who leads a Muslim community? A: A sheikh leads the Muslim community.
chunks.source: A sheikh leads the Muslim community.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what a volunteer does. A: A volunteer helps others without expecting payment.
chunks.source: A volunteer helps others without expecting payment.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name a voluntary youth group in Uganda. A: Scouts and Guides are voluntary youth groups.
chunks.source: Scouts and Guides are voluntary youth groups.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the role of a pastor? A: A pastor leads a Christian congregation and teaches the Bible.
chunks.source: A pastor leads a Christian congregation and teaches the Bible.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why are religious leaders important? A: They guide faith promote peace and support the needy.
chunks.source: They guide faith promote peace and support the needy.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: How Leaders Are Chosen. I can explain the different ways leaders are chosen in my district. Leaders are chosen by voting appointment inheritance or volunteering; each method follows a clear process. Keywords: voting: choosing by casting a ballot; appointment: selected by a higher authority; inheritance: passed down in a family; volunteering: offering service freely; campaign: period when candidates share ideas; ballot: paper used to vote secretly; chosen: selected for a position
chunks.source: Leaders are chosen by voting appointment inheritance or volunteering; each method follows a clear process.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is voting? A: Voting is choosing leaders by casting a secret ballot.
chunks.source: Voting is choosing leaders by casting a secret ballot.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How is an RDC selected? A: An RDC is appointed by the president.
chunks.source: An RDC is appointed by the president.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what a campaign is. A: A campaign is when candidates tell people their ideas before an election.
chunks.source: A campaign is when candidates tell people their ideas before an election.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which method uses inheritance? A: Traditional chiefs often inherit their positions.
chunks.source: Traditional chiefs often inherit their positions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does volunteering mean? A: Volunteering means giving your time and effort without pay.
chunks.source: Volunteering means giving your time and effort without pay.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is a ballot important? A: A ballot keeps the vote secret and fair.
chunks.source: A ballot keeps the vote secret and fair.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Qualities of a Good Leader. I can list and explain the qualities that make a good leader in my district. A good leader is honest kind respectful responsible tolerant hardworking and cooperative; these qualities help the district develop. Keywords: honest: truthful; kind: caring; respectful: polite and considerate; responsible: does duties well; tolerant: accepts differences; hardworking: works with effort; cooperative: works well with others
chunks.source: A good leader is honest kind respectful responsible tolerant hardworking and cooperative; these qualities help the district develop.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does honest mean? A: Honest means telling the truth.
chunks.source: Honest means telling the truth.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of a kind action by a leader. A: A leader giving food to hungry families is kind.
chunks.source: A leader giving food to hungry families is kind.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what tolerant means. A: Tolerant means accepting people who are different.
chunks.source: Tolerant means accepting people who are different.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is being responsible important for a leader? A: Responsible leaders finish their duties and keep promises.
chunks.source: Responsible leaders finish their duties and keep promises.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name a situation where a leader must be cooperative. A: A leader working with the council to build a road needs cooperation.
chunks.source: A leader working with the council to build a road needs cooperation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does hard work by a leader help the community? A: Hardworking leaders inspire others and get things done.
chunks.source: Hardworking leaders inspire others and get things done.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Services That Meet Our Needs. I can name the main social services that meet people's needs in my district. Our district offers **education**, **health**, **security**, **transport**, **water**, and **electricity** to meet people's **needs**. Looking after these **services** makes life better for everyone. Keywords: needs: things people must have to live well; education: learning in school; health: care for the body; security: safety from harm; transport: moving people or goods; water: clean liquid for drinking; electricity: power for lights and machines
chunks.source: Our district offers **education**, **health**, **security**, **transport**, **water**, and **electricity** to meet people's **needs**. Looking after these **services** makes life better for everyone.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name three **services** that meet **needs** in your district. A: Education, health, water
chunks.source: Education, health, water

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a **school** provide? A: A school provides **education**.
chunks.source: A school provides **education**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which **service** keeps people safe? A: **Security** keeps people safe.
chunks.source: **Security** keeps people safe.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why clean **water** is a basic **need**. A: Clean water prevents illness and is needed for drinking and cooking.
chunks.source: Clean water prevents illness and is needed for drinking and cooking.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give one example of **transport** used in Uganda. A: Boda boda or matatu.
chunks.source: Boda boda or matatu.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **electricity** power in a home? A: Lights, phones, and small machines.
chunks.source: Lights, phones, and small machines.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: People Who Provide Services. I can match each service provider to the service they give in my district. People such as **teacher**, **doctor**, **nurse**, **police officer**, **farmer**, **driver**, and **banker** provide the **services** that meet our **needs**. Keywords: teacher: person who teaches pupils; doctor: person who treats sick people; nurse: person who helps the doctor; police officer: person who keeps law and order; farmer: person who grows food; driver: person who drives a vehicle; banker: person who works in a bank
chunks.source: People such as **teacher**, **doctor**, **nurse**, **police officer**, **farmer**, **driver**, and **banker** provide the **services** that meet our **needs**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who gives **education** to children? A: A **teacher** gives **education**.
chunks.source: A **teacher** gives **education**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which provider gives **health** care? A: A **doctor** and a **nurse** give **health** care.
chunks.source: A **doctor** and a **nurse** give **health** care.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What **service** does a **police officer** give? A: A **police officer** gives **security**.
chunks.source: A **police officer** gives **security**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words what a **farmer** does for the community. A: A **farmer** grows food that feeds people.
chunks.source: A **farmer** grows food that feeds people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the **service** a **driver** provides. A: **Transport**.
chunks.source: **Transport**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does a **banker** help people with? A: A **banker** helps people save and borrow money.
chunks.source: A **banker** helps people save and borrow money.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List two providers you see in your village. A: Example: **teacher**, **driver**.
chunks.source: Example: **teacher**, **driver**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Problems in Meeting Needs. I can identify common problems that make it hard to provide services in my district. **Poverty**, **theft**, **corruption**, **shortage**, **laziness**, and a growing **population** are **problems** that make it hard to deliver **services**. Keywords: poverty: lack of money and resources; theft: stealing things; corruption: dishonest use of power; shortage: not enough of something; laziness: not wanting to work; population: number of people in an area; problems: difficulties that need solving
chunks.source: **Poverty**, **theft**, **corruption**, **shortage**, **laziness**, and a growing **population** are **problems** that make it hard to deliver **services**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two **problems** that affect **health** services. A: **Corruption** and **shortage** of medicine.
chunks.source: **Corruption** and **shortage** of medicine.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **poverty** stop families from getting? A: **Education**, **health**, and clean **water**.
chunks.source: **Education**, **health**, and clean **water**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how **population** growth creates **shortage**. A: More people need more **water**, **health**, and **education**, so supplies run low.
chunks.source: More people need more **water**, **health**, and **education**, so supplies run low.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which **problem** involves dishonest use of power? A: **Corruption**.
chunks.source: **Corruption**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of **theft** in a school. A: Stealing textbooks or chairs.
chunks.source: Stealing textbooks or chairs.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How can **laziness** hurt a borehole? A: If no one cleans it, the borehole breaks and **water** stops.
chunks.source: If no one cleans it, the borehole breaks and **water** stops.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List one way to fight **corruption** in your district. A: Report misuse of funds to leaders.
chunks.source: Report misuse of funds to leaders.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Caring for Service Centres. I can describe ways to look after service centres in my district. Looking after every **centre** with **cleaning**, **respect**, **protect**, and **maintain** is a shared **responsibility** that keeps **services** running for the whole **community**. Keywords: centre: place where a service is given; cleaning: making something clean; respect: treating people and property well; protect: keep safe from damage; maintain: keep in good condition; community: people living together in an area; responsibility: duty to care for something
chunks.source: Looking after every **centre** with **cleaning**, **respect**, **protect**, and **maintain** is a shared **responsibility** that keeps **services** running for the whole **community**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **cleaning** a **centre** prevent? A: Germs and disease.
chunks.source: Germs and disease.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of showing **respect** at a school **centre**. A: Putting chairs back quietly.
chunks.source: Putting chairs back quietly.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words why **maintain** is important for a health **centre**. A: It keeps equipment working so patients get care.
chunks.source: It keeps equipment working so patients get care.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who shares the **responsibility** for a community **centre**? A: The whole **community**.
chunks.source: The whole **community**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one way to **protect** a **centre** from damage. A: Fix broken doors and windows.
chunks.source: Fix broken doors and windows.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What happens if a **centre** is not **maintain**ed? A: It falls into disrepair and services stop.
chunks.source: It falls into disrepair and services stop.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List two actions you can take to help your local **centre**. A: Pick up litter and report broken things.
chunks.source: Pick up litter and report broken things.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Parts of a Vehicle. I can name the main parts of a vehicle and say what each part does. A **vehicle** has an **engine**, four **tyre**s, a **windscreen**, two **headlights**, a **steering wheel**, two **side mirror**s, and **brakes**; each part has a special job. Keywords: engine: the part that makes the vehicle move; tyre: the round rubber part that touches the road; windscreen: the front glass window; headlights: the front lights for night driving; steering wheel: the wheel the driver turns; side mirror: the mirror on the side of the vehicle; brakes: the parts that stop the vehicle
chunks.source: A **vehicle** has an **engine**, four **tyre**s, a **windscreen**, two **headlights**, a **steering wheel**, two **side mirror**s, and **brakes**; each part has a special job.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the part that makes the vehicle move? A: The **engine** makes the vehicle move.
chunks.source: The **engine** makes the vehicle move.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which part touches the road? A: The **tyre** touches the road.
chunks.source: The **tyre** touches the road.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you clean so the driver can see ahead? A: You clean the **windscreen**.
chunks.source: You clean the **windscreen**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: When do you turn on the **headlights**? A: You turn on the **headlights** at night or in rain.
chunks.source: You turn on the **headlights** at night or in rain.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you hold to steer the vehicle? A: You hold the **steering wheel**.
chunks.source: You hold the **steering wheel**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which mirror shows traffic behind you? A: The **side mirror** shows traffic behind.
chunks.source: The **side mirror** shows traffic behind.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you press to stop the vehicle? A: You press the **brakes** to stop.
chunks.source: You press the **brakes** to stop.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Tools Used in a Garage. I can name common garage tools and say what each tool is used for. A garage uses a **spanner**, **screwdriver**, **pliers**, **hammer**, **jack**, **grease**, and **oil**; each tool has a special job for fixing vehicles. Keywords: spanner: a tool for turning nuts and bolts; screwdriver: a tool for turning screws; pliers: a tool for gripping and bending; hammer: a tool for hitting nails; jack: a tool that lifts a vehicle; grease: a thick oil for reducing friction; oil: a liquid that lubricates the engine
chunks.source: A garage uses a **spanner**, **screwdriver**, **pliers**, **hammer**, **jack**, **grease**, and **oil**; each tool has a special job for fixing vehicles.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which tool lifts a vehicle? A: A **jack** lifts a vehicle.
chunks.source: A **jack** lifts a vehicle.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What tool turns a screw? A: A **screwdriver** turns a screw.
chunks.source: A **screwdriver** turns a screw.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you use to grip a wire? A: You use **pliers** to grip a wire.
chunks.source: You use **pliers** to grip a wire.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which tool hits a nail? A: A **hammer** hits a nail.
chunks.source: A **hammer** hits a nail.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you put on bolts to stop rust? A: You put **grease** on bolts.
chunks.source: You put **grease** on bolts.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What liquid keeps the engine running smoothly? A: **Oil** keeps the engine running smoothly.
chunks.source: **Oil** keeps the engine running smoothly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If a nut is loose, which tool do you need? A: You need a **spanner** to tighten the nut.
chunks.source: You need a **spanner** to tighten the nut.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Repairing and Maintaining Vehicles. I can explain what a mechanic does and use must, mustn't and if‑sentences for safety. A **mechanic** works in a **garage** to do **repair** and **maintenance**; you **must** check fluids and **tyre**s, **mustn't** ignore a damaged **tube**, and always follow **safety** rules. Keywords: mechanic: a person who fixes vehicles; garage: a place where vehicles are fixed; repair: to fix something that is broken; maintenance: regular care to keep a vehicle working; tube: the inner rubber part of a tyre; safety: being protected from danger
chunks.source: A **mechanic** works in a **garage** to do **repair** and **maintenance**; you **must** check fluids and **tyre**s, **mustn't** ignore a damaged **tube**, and always follow **safety** rules.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who fixes vehicles in a garage? A: A **mechanic** fixes vehicles.
chunks.source: A **mechanic** fixes vehicles.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the place where vehicles are fixed called? A: It is called a **garage**.
chunks.source: It is called a **garage**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What word means to fix something broken? A: **Repair** means to fix something broken.
chunks.source: **Repair** means to fix something broken.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is regular care of a vehicle called? A: Regular care is called **maintenance**.
chunks.source: Regular care is called **maintenance**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the inner rubber part of a tyre? A: The inner rubber part is the **tube**.
chunks.source: The inner rubber part is the **tube**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the most important rule in a garage? A: **Safety** is the most important rule.
chunks.source: **Safety** is the most important rule.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the sentence: You ___ check the oil every week. A: You **must** check the oil every week.
chunks.source: You **must** check the oil every week.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the sentence: You ___ drive with a worn tube. A: You **mustn't** drive with a worn tube.
chunks.source: You **mustn't** drive with a worn tube.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Newspapers and Magazines. I can name parts of a newspaper and a magazine and use present simple for routines. A **newspaper** comes daily; a **magazine** comes weekly or monthly. The **editor** picks the **headline**, **article**, and **column** for readers. Keywords: newspaper: a paper printed daily with news; magazine: a book with stories and pictures that comes weekly or monthly; headline: the big title at the top of a page; article: a written piece about one topic; column: a regular section by the same writer; editor: the person who checks and decides what goes in the paper
chunks.source: A **newspaper** comes daily; a **magazine** comes weekly or monthly. The **editor** picks the **headline**, **article**, and **column** for readers.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What comes out every day: a newspaper or a magazine? A: A **newspaper** comes out every day.
chunks.source: A **newspaper** comes out every day.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the big title on the front page called? A: The big title is called the **headline**.
chunks.source: The big title is called the **headline**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who chooses the stories for the newspaper? A: The **editor** chooses the stories.
chunks.source: The **editor** chooses the stories.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do we call a regular section by the same writer? A: A regular section is called a **column**.
chunks.source: A regular section is called a **column**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: My mother reads the ______ every Sunday. A: My mother reads the **newspaper** every Sunday.
chunks.source: My mother reads the **newspaper** every Sunday.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The ______ checks the articles before printing. A: The **editor** checks the articles before printing.
chunks.source: The **editor** checks the articles before printing.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: True or false: A magazine comes out daily. A: False. A **magazine** comes out weekly or monthly.
chunks.source: False. A **magazine** comes out weekly or monthly.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write one sentence using 'headline' and 'article'. A: The **headline** says 'Rain Comes', and the **article** tells how much rain fell.
chunks.source: The **headline** says 'Rain Comes', and the **article** tells how much rain fell.

chunks.id: L-P5-English-People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.subject: English
chunks.unit: People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.text: People Who Work in Print Media. I can name print media jobs and use relative clauses with who and which. People in print media: **journalist** **who** writes, **reporter** **who** gathers news, **author** **who** writes books. Things: **cartoon** **which** amuses, **advertisement** **which** sells. To **publish** is to print and share. Keywords: journalist: a person who writes news stories; reporter: a person who goes to events and tells the news; author: a person who writes books or long articles; cartoon: a funny drawing that tells a story or joke; advertisement: a notice that tells people to buy something; publish: to print and share a book, paper, or magazine
chunks.source: People in print media: **journalist** **who** writes, **reporter** **who** gathers news, **author** **who** writes books. Things: **cartoon** **which** amuses, **advertisement** **which** sells. To **publish** is to print and share.

chunks.id: LQ-P5-English-People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.subject: English
chunks.unit: People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.text: Q: What do we call a person who writes news stories? A: A **journalist** writes news stories.
chunks.source: A **journalist** writes news stories.

chunks.id: LQ-P5-English-People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.subject: English
chunks.unit: People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The ______ who draws the cartoon is an artist. A: The **author** who draws the cartoon is an artist.
chunks.source: The **author** who draws the cartoon is an artist.

chunks.id: LQ-P5-English-People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.subject: English
chunks.unit: People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.text: Q: Choose: The advertisement ______ sells soap is on page three. (who / which) A: The **advertisement** **which** sells soap is on page three.
chunks.source: The **advertisement** **which** sells soap is on page three.

chunks.id: LQ-P5-English-People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.subject: English
chunks.unit: People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.text: Q: Choose: The reporter ______ asked questions is my uncle. (who / which) A: The **reporter** **who** asked questions is my uncle.
chunks.source: The **reporter** **who** asked questions is my uncle.

chunks.id: LQ-P5-English-People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.subject: English
chunks.unit: People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.text: Q: What does 'publish' mean? A: To **publish** means to print and share a book, paper, or magazine.
chunks.source: To **publish** means to print and share a book, paper, or magazine.

chunks.id: LQ-P5-English-People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.subject: English
chunks.unit: People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence with 'journalist who'. A: The **journalist** **who** visited our school wrote a nice **article**.
chunks.source: The **journalist** **who** visited our school wrote a nice **article**.

chunks.id: LQ-P5-English-People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.subject: English
chunks.unit: People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence with 'cartoon which'. A: The **cartoon** **which** shows a teacher made us laugh.
chunks.source: The **cartoon** **which** shows a teacher made us laugh.

chunks.id: LQ-P5-English-People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.subject: English
chunks.unit: People Who Work in Print Media
chunks.text: Q: True or false: An author writes only newspapers. A: False. An **author** writes books or long **articles**.
chunks.source: False. An **author** writes books or long **articles**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Reading the News. I can find information in a news text and use relative clauses with which. We get **news** from a **story** on the **front page**, a **poster**, or a **broadcast**. A **reader** **who** reads learns. Use **which** for things: **story** **which**, **poster** **which**, **broadcast** **which**. Keywords: news: new information about recent events; story: a written account of an event; front page: the first page of a newspaper; poster: a large printed notice put on a wall; broadcast: a radio or TV programme that sends out news; reader: a person who reads a newspaper, magazine, or book
chunks.source: We get **news** from a **story** on the **front page**, a **poster**, or a **broadcast**. A **reader** **who** reads learns. Use **which** for things: **story** **which**, **poster** **which**, **broadcast** **which**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where do you find the main headline in a newspaper? A: On the **front page**.
chunks.source: On the **front page**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do we call a person who reads the newspaper? A: A **reader**.
chunks.source: A **reader**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The ______ which announces the match is on the tree. A: The **poster** which announces the match is on the tree.
chunks.source: The **poster** which announces the match is on the tree.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose: The broadcast ______ gives the news at 7 p.m. (who / which) A: The **broadcast** **which** gives the news at 7 p.m.
chunks.source: The **broadcast** **which** gives the news at 7 p.m.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: True or false: A story is a written account of an event. A: True. A **story** is a written account of an event.
chunks.source: True. A **story** is a written account of an event.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence with 'story which'. A: The **story** **which** I read was about a new borehole.
chunks.source: The **story** **which** I read was about a new borehole.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence with 'reader who'. A: The **reader** **who** buys the paper sees the **front page**.
chunks.source: The **reader** **who** buys the paper sees the **front page**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does 'broadcast' mean? A: A **broadcast** is a radio or TV programme that sends out **news**.
chunks.source: A **broadcast** is a radio or TV programme that sends out **news**.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Getting Ready to Travel. I can name travel words and talk about my travel plans. Amina prepares her luggage, ticket, and fare, then travels to her destination with a safe departure and arrival. Keywords: luggage: bags you carry when you travel; ticket: paper that lets you travel; fare: money you pay for the trip; destination: place you are going to; departure: time you leave; arrival: time you reach the place
chunks.source: Amina prepares her luggage, ticket, and fare, then travels to her destination with a safe departure and arrival.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Amina check before she leaves? A: She checks her luggage.
chunks.source: She checks her luggage.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What paper shows the fare? A: The ticket shows the fare.
chunks.source: The ticket shows the fare.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How much is the fare to Kampala? A: The fare is 20,000 shillings.
chunks.source: The fare is 20,000 shillings.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What time is the departure? A: The departure time is 8:00.
chunks.source: The departure time is 8:00.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What time is the arrival? A: The arrival time is 12:00.
chunks.source: The arrival time is 12:00.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where does Amina sit on the bus? A: She sits near the window.
chunks.source: She sits near the window.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If you forget your ticket, who can help? A: The conductor can help.
chunks.source: The conductor can help.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: On the Journey. I can use always, usually, often to describe travel routines. On the journey, the conductor always checks tickets, passengers usually find seats, and the driver often stops at the station. Keywords: conductor: person who checks tickets on the bus; board: to get on the bus; passenger: person who rides the bus; seat: place to sit on the bus; driver: person who drives the bus; journey: the trip from start to end
chunks.source: On the journey, the conductor always checks tickets, passengers usually find seats, and the driver often stops at the station.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does the conductor always do? A: The conductor always checks tickets.
chunks.source: The conductor always checks tickets.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does a passenger usually do? A: A passenger usually finds a seat.
chunks.source: A passenger usually finds a seat.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does the driver often do? A: The driver often stops at the station.
chunks.source: The driver often stops at the station.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What word means to get on the bus? A: Board means to get on the bus.
chunks.source: Board means to get on the bus.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who drives the bus? A: The driver drives the bus.
chunks.source: The driver drives the bus.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the trip called? A: The trip is called a journey.
chunks.source: The trip is called a journey.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If the driver drives fast, who should you tell? A: Tell the conductor.
chunks.source: Tell the conductor.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Travelling Safely. I can give safety instructions for travelling. To travel safely, wait at the station, watch the road, and follow instructions to arrive safe. Keywords: travel: to go from one place to another; station: place where buses stop; arrive: to reach a place; wait: to stay until something happens; safe: free from danger; road: path for cars and people
chunks.source: To travel safely, wait at the station, watch the road, and follow instructions to arrive safe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does Musa plan to do? A: Musa plans to travel to the market.
chunks.source: Musa plans to travel to the market.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where does Musa wait for the bus? A: Musa waits at the station.
chunks.source: Musa waits at the station.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What must you do before crossing the road? A: You must wait and look left and right.
chunks.source: You must wait and look left and right.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does safe mean? A: Safe means free from danger.
chunks.source: Safe means free from danger.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the road? A: The road is the path for vehicles.
chunks.source: The road is the path for vehicles.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does arrive mean? A: Arrive means to reach a place.
chunks.source: Arrive means to reach a place.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: If you see a child on the road, what should you do? A: Tell an adult to keep the child safe.
chunks.source: Tell an adult to keep the child safe.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: At the Post Office. I can explain how to send a letter or parcel at the post office. To send a letter or parcel you need an envelope, a stamp, the correct address, and you go to the post office where the postman collects it. Keywords: letter: a written note; stamp: a small paper you buy to mail; envelope: a flat paper cover for a letter; parcel: a wrapped box or bag to send; address: the place where the mail goes; post office: the building where you send mail; send: to cause something to go to someone; postman: the person who delivers mail
chunks.source: To send a letter or parcel you need an envelope, a stamp, the correct address, and you go to the post office where the postman collects it.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where do you go to send a letter? A: You go to the post office.
chunks.source: You go to the post office.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you put on an envelope before posting? A: You put a stamp on the envelope.
chunks.source: You put a stamp on the envelope.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who delivers the mail to homes? A: The postman delivers the mail.
chunks.source: The postman delivers the mail.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What must you write on the envelope? A: You must write the address.
chunks.source: You must write the address.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a parcel? A: A parcel is a wrapped box or bag to send.
chunks.source: A parcel is a wrapped box or bag to send.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does the clerk do with a parcel? A: The clerk weighs the parcel.
chunks.source: The clerk weighs the parcel.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: How do you feel when your letter is sent? A: You feel happy.
chunks.source: You feel happy.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Talking on the Telephone. I can use polite telephone language to make and receive calls.
