The **land** provides living **resources**: **forests**, **plants**, **animals**, and **game parks**. **Cultivation** grows **crops** for food. **Wildlife** in **game parks** brings **tourism**. Wise use protects all **resources** for the future. Keywords: land: the solid ground we live on and use for farming or building; forest: a large area covered with many trees and wild plants; plants: living things that grow in soil and make their own food; animals: living creatures that move and eat other living things; wildlife: wild animals and plants living in their natural home; cultivation: preparing soil and growing crops on it; crops: plants grown by farmers for food or to sell; tourism: people travelling to see places and spending money there; game park: a protected area where wild animals live safely; resource: something useful that people get from nature
chunks.source: The **land** provides living **resources**: **forests**, **plants**, **animals**, and **game parks**. **Cultivation** grows **crops** for food. **Wildlife** in **game parks** brings **tourism**. Wise use protects all **resources** for the future.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.text: Q: What is a **resource**? Give two examples from the lesson. A: A **resource** is something useful from nature. Examples: **land**, **forest**, **plants**, **animals**, **wildlife**, **game park**.
chunks.source: A **resource** is something useful from nature. Examples: **land**, **forest**, **plants**, **animals**, **wildlife**, **game park**.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.text: Q: Name three **crops** grown in Uganda mentioned in the lesson. A: Maize, beans, cassava, coffee, matooke, tea, millet, sorghum (any three).
chunks.source: Maize, beans, cassava, coffee, matooke, tea, millet, sorghum (any three).

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.text: Q: How does a **forest** help **cultivation** on nearby **land**? A: A **forest** catches rain, keeps soil moist, stops erosion, and gives nutrients to the soil for **crops**.
chunks.source: A **forest** catches rain, keeps soil moist, stops erosion, and gives nutrients to the soil for **crops**.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.text: Q: What is **tourism** and how does a **game park** support it? A: **Tourism** is people travelling to see places. A **game park** protects **wildlife** that tourists pay to see, bringing income.
chunks.source: **Tourism** is people travelling to see places. A **game park** protects **wildlife** that tourists pay to see, bringing income.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.text: Q: Why is cutting down a whole **forest** for more **crops** a bad idea? A: It causes soil erosion, loses **wildlife** habitat, reduces rain catchment, and harms long-term **cultivation**.
chunks.source: It causes soil erosion, loses **wildlife** habitat, reduces rain catchment, and harms long-term **cultivation**.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.text: Q: Give one way farmers can protect **crops** from **wildlife** without harming **animals**. A: Build trenches, use bee fences, plant buffer crops, or use noise/light deterrents.
chunks.source: Build trenches, use bee fences, plant buffer crops, or use noise/light deterrents.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.text: Q: List two benefits of **game parks** to local communities. A: **Tourism** jobs, income for schools/roads, protecting **wildlife** for future generations.
chunks.source: **Tourism** jobs, income for schools/roads, protecting **wildlife** for future generations.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.text: Q: Explain the difference between **plants** and **crops**. A: **Plants** are all growing things. **Crops** are **plants** chosen and grown by farmers for food or sale.
chunks.source: **Plants** are all growing things. **Crops** are **plants** chosen and grown by farmers for food or sale.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: The Land and Its Living Resources
chunks.text: Q: Reasoning: A leader wants to turn half a **game park** into farm **land** for **cultivation**. Write three reasons this may hurt the district long-term. A: 1) Loses **tourism** income. 2) Destroys **wildlife** habitat. 3) Soil may degrade without **forest** cover. 4) Conflicts with **animals** increase. (Any three).
chunks.source: 1) Loses **tourism** income. 2) Destroys **wildlife** habitat. 3) Soil may degrade without **forest** cover. 4) Conflicts with **animals** increase. (Any three).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Minerals Under the Ground. I can name minerals found in East Africa, where they are located, and how traditional and modern mining methods differ. East Africa has **minerals** like **gold**, **copper**, **oil**, **diamond**, **iron**, **salt**. **Traditional** **mining** uses simple tools; **modern** uses machines. Both give **income** and **export** earnings but need careful management to avoid **pollution**. Keywords: minerals: natural substances in the ground with economic value; mining: the work of digging minerals out of the ground; gold: a shiny yellow metal used for jewellery and money; copper: a reddish-brown metal used for wires and pipes; oil: a thick black liquid used for fuel and making plastics; diamond: a very hard clear stone used for cutting and jewellery; iron: a strong magnetic metal used to make steel; salt: a white mineral used to flavour and preserve food; income: money earned from work or selling things; export: sending goods to other countries to sell
chunks.source: East Africa has **minerals** like **gold**, **copper**, **oil**, **diamond**, **iron**, **salt**. **Traditional** **mining** uses simple tools; **modern** uses machines. Both give **income** and **export** earnings but need careful management to avoid **pollution**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name four **minerals** found in Uganda and where each is located. A: **Gold**: Busia, Namayingo, Karamoja. **Copper**: Kilembe (Kasese). **Oil**: Albertine Graben (Hoima, Buliisa). **Iron**: Muko (Rubanda). **Salt**: Lake Katwe (Kasese).
chunks.source: **Gold**: Busia, Namayingo, Karamoja. **Copper**: Kilembe (Kasese). **Oil**: Albertine Graben (Hoima, Buliisa). **Iron**: Muko (Rubanda). **Salt**: Lake Katwe (Kasese).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the difference between **traditional** and **modern** **mining**? A: **Traditional** uses simple tools (pickaxes, pans) and many workers. **Modern** uses heavy machines, chemicals, and few skilled workers.
chunks.source: **Traditional** uses simple tools (pickaxes, pans) and many workers. **Modern** uses heavy machines, chemicals, and few skilled workers.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is mercury used in **traditional** **gold** **mining**, and what is the danger? A: Mercury binds to **gold** to separate it from rock. Danger: it poisons water, fish, and people who eat the fish.
chunks.source: Mercury binds to **gold** to separate it from rock. Danger: it poisons water, fish, and people who eat the fish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does **salt** **mining** at Lake Katwe work? A: Shallow pans are filled with lake water. Sun evaporates water. **Salt** crystals form and are scraped up. No machines needed.
chunks.source: Shallow pans are filled with lake water. Sun evaporates water. **Salt** crystals form and are scraped up. No machines needed.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **export** mean? Give an example of a mineral Uganda **export**s. A: **Export** means selling goods to other countries. Uganda **export**s **gold** and **copper**.
chunks.source: **Export** means selling goods to other countries. Uganda **export**s **gold** and **copper**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List two problems caused by **modern** **mining**. A: Chemical **pollution** (cyanide, acid mine drainage), displacement of communities, high water use, land degradation.
chunks.source: Chemical **pollution** (cyanide, acid mine drainage), displacement of communities, high water use, land degradation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List two problems caused by **traditional** **mining**. A: Mercury **pollution**, open pit accidents, child labour, low recovery of **minerals**, no rehabilitation.
chunks.source: Mercury **pollution**, open pit accidents, child labour, low recovery of **minerals**, no rehabilitation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why did **copper** **mining** stop at Kilembe for many years? A: World **copper** prices fell, equipment aged, and investment stopped. Recent plans aim to restart.
chunks.source: World **copper** prices fell, equipment aged, and investment stopped. Recent plans aim to restart.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Reasoning: A company wants to start **modern** **oil** **mining** near a **game park**. Write three conditions the government should set to protect the **resource** and people. A: 1) Environmental impact study. 2) No drilling in the park buffer zone. 3) Community revenue sharing. 4) Spill emergency plan. 5) Land restoration after. (Any three).
chunks.source: 1) Environmental impact study. 2) No drilling in the park buffer zone. 3) Community revenue sharing. 4) Spill emergency plan. 5) Land restoration after. (Any three).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Water Resources of East Africa. I can describe the major water bodies in East Africa, their uses, fishing methods, and how fish is preserved. East Africa's water **resources** — **lake**, **river**, **ocean**, **swamp** — provide **fish**, water, transport, power. **Fishing** uses **traditional** (canoe, traps) and **modern** (motor, sonar) methods. **Preservation** by smoking, drying, freezing, or canning stops waste. Good **drainage** prevents floods. Keywords: lake: a large body of fresh water surrounded by land; river: a natural flowing watercourse, usually fresh water; ocean: a vast body of salt water covering most of Earth; swamp: wet land with shallow water and plants like papyrus; fishing: the activity of catching fish for food or sale; fish: cold-blooded water animals with gills and fins; drainage: the system of rivers and streams carrying water away; preservation: keeping fish from spoiling so it lasts longer; traditional: methods passed down through generations; modern: new methods using technology and machines
chunks.source: East Africa's water **resources** — **lake**, **river**, **ocean**, **swamp** — provide **fish**, water, transport, power. **Fishing** uses **traditional** (canoe, traps) and **modern** (motor, sonar) methods. **Preservation** by smoking, drying, freezing, or canning stops waste. Good **drainage** prevents floods.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name the four main types of water **resources** in East Africa. A: **Lake**, **river**, **ocean**, **swamp**.
chunks.source: **Lake**, **river**, **ocean**, **swamp**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Which **lake** is the largest in Africa and the main source of **fish** for Uganda? A: **Lake** Victoria.
chunks.source: **Lake** Victoria.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **drainage**? Why is it important? A: **Drainage** is the system of **river**s carrying water away. It prevents flooding and connects **lake**s to the **ocean**.
chunks.source: **Drainage** is the system of **river**s carrying water away. It prevents flooding and connects **lake**s to the **ocean**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List three **traditional** **fishing** methods. A: Canoe with paddle, woven traps, hook-and-line, spears, cast nets, basket traps.
chunks.source: Canoe with paddle, woven traps, hook-and-line, spears, cast nets, basket traps.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List three **modern** **fishing** methods. A: Motor boat, echo-sounder/sonar, purse seine net, nylon gill nets, GPS, ice hold.
chunks.source: Motor boat, echo-sounder/sonar, purse seine net, nylon gill nets, GPS, ice hold.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two **traditional** **preservation** methods and two **modern** ones. A: **Traditional**: sun-drying, smoking, salting. **Modern**: freezing, canning, vacuum packing, fish meal.
chunks.source: **Traditional**: sun-drying, smoking, salting. **Modern**: freezing, canning, vacuum packing, fish meal.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is **traditional** **preservation** still widely used at landing sites? A: No electricity for freezers, low cost, uses local materials (firewood, sun, salt), works off-grid.
chunks.source: No electricity for freezers, low cost, uses local materials (firewood, sun, salt), works off-grid.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What **fish** species are most caught in Uganda's **lake**s? A: Nile perch, tilapia, mukene (silver fish), lungfish, catfish.
chunks.source: Nile perch, tilapia, mukene (silver fish), lungfish, catfish.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Reasoning: A new road is built through a **swamp** without culverts. Explain two effects on water **resources** and **fishing**. A: 1) Blocks natural **drainage** → flooding upstream, drying downstream. 2) Destroys **fish** breeding grounds in the **swamp** → less **fish** catch. 3) Increases silt in **lake** → harms **fish** gills.
chunks.source: 1) Blocks natural **drainage** → flooding upstream, drying downstream. 2) Destroys **fish** breeding grounds in the **swamp** → less **fish** catch. 3) Increases silt in **lake** → harms **fish** gills.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Using Our Resources Wisely. I can identify problems facing natural resources in East Africa and explain ways to conserve them for sustainable benefit. Natural **resources** face **problems**: **deforestation**, **pollution**, **overfishing**, **land** degradation, poaching. **Conservation** provides **solutions** for **sustainable** use — **protect** the **resource**, keep the **benefit**. Wise management ensures **resources** last for all generations. Keywords: problem: a difficulty that needs to be solved; solution: a way to fix a problem; conservation: protecting natural resources so they last; pollution: harmful substances put into air, water, or soil; deforestation: cutting down forests faster than they grow back; overfishing: catching fish faster than they can breed; resource: something useful from nature that people need; benefit: a good result or advantage; protect: keep safe from harm or damage; sustainable: able to continue for a long time without running out
chunks.source: Natural **resources** face **problems**: **deforestation**, **pollution**, **overfishing**, **land** degradation, poaching. **Conservation** provides **solutions** for **sustainable** use — **protect** the **resource**, keep the **benefit**. Wise management ensures **resources** last for all generations.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define **conservation** in your own words. A: **Conservation** is protecting and wisely using natural **resources** so they last for future generations.
chunks.source: **Conservation** is protecting and wisely using natural **resources** so they last for future generations.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **deforestation**? Give two causes and two effects. A: **Deforestation** = cutting **forest** faster than it regrows. Causes: charcoal, timber, **cultivation** expansion. Effects: soil erosion, loss of **wildlife**, less rain, climate change.
chunks.source: **Deforestation** = cutting **forest** faster than it regrows. Causes: charcoal, timber, **cultivation** expansion. Effects: soil erosion, loss of **wildlife**, less rain, climate change.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **overfishing**? How does a 5-inch mesh net help? A: **Overfishing** = catching **fish** faster than they breed. 5-inch mesh lets juveniles escape to grow and breed.
chunks.source: **Overfishing** = catching **fish** faster than they breed. 5-inch mesh lets juveniles escape to grow and breed.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List three types of **pollution** from **mining** and one **solution** for each. A: 1) Mercury → ban mercury, use retorts. 2) Acid mine drainage → treat water, line ponds. 3) Silt/sediment → settling ponds, re-vegetate.
chunks.source: 1) Mercury → ban mercury, use retorts. 2) Acid mine drainage → treat water, line ponds. 3) Silt/sediment → settling ponds, re-vegetate.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain the difference between **protect** and **conserve**. A: **Protect** = keep safe from harm (e.g., fence a park). **Conserve** = manage wisely for long-term use (e.g., sustainable logging).
chunks.source: **Protect** = keep safe from harm (e.g., fence a park). **Conserve** = manage wisely for long-term use (e.g., sustainable logging).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **sustainable** mean? Give an example of **sustainable** **fishing**. A: **Sustainable** = can continue long-term without running out. Example: using legal mesh, closed seasons, **fish** farming.
chunks.source: **Sustainable** = can continue long-term without running out. Example: using legal mesh, closed seasons, **fish** farming.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name two **benefits** of **conservation** to local communities. A: Long-term **income** (tourism, **fish**), clean water, fertile **land**, climate regulation, cultural heritage.
chunks.source: Long-term **income** (tourism, **fish**), clean water, fertile **land**, climate regulation, cultural heritage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is **land** degradation a **problem** for **cultivation**? A: Erosion removes topsoil. Nutrients lost. Yields drop. Farmers clear more **forest** → cycle continues.
chunks.source: Erosion removes topsoil. Nutrients lost. Yields drop. Farmers clear more **forest** → cycle continues.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Reasoning: A district has **gold** **mining**, **fishing** on a **lake**, and a **game park**. Write a **sustainable** plan with one rule for each **resource**. A: **Gold**: lined ponds, no mercury, rehabilitate after. **Fish**: 5-inch mesh, closed season, boat limits. **Game park**: anti-poaching patrols, community revenue share, buffer zones.
chunks.source: **Gold**: lined ponds, no mercury, rehabilitate after. **Fish**: 5-inch mesh, closed season, boat limits. **Game park**: anti-poaching patrols, community revenue share, buffer zones.

chunks.id: L-P6-Social-How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.text: How People Long Ago Sent Messages. I can describe traditional ways people in East Africa communicated long ago. Traditional communication in East Africa used drums, horns, smoke, trumpets, whistles and messengers to send signals and alarms. Keywords: communication: sending and receiving messages; traditional: belonging to the old customs; drum: a hollow instrument beaten to make sound; horn: an animal horn blown to make a loud call; smoke: visible gas from fire used as a sign; messenger: a person who carries a message; trumpet: a long metal instrument blown for signals; whistle: a small device that makes a sharp sound; signal: a sign that carries information; alarm: a warning of danger
chunks.source: Traditional communication in East Africa used drums, horns, smoke, trumpets, whistles and messengers to send signals and alarms.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.text: Q: What is communication? A: Sending and receiving messages.
chunks.source: Sending and receiving messages.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.text: Q: Name one traditional way to send a message. A: A drum beat.
chunks.source: A drum beat.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.text: Q: What does a messenger do? A: Carries a message from place to place.
chunks.source: Carries a message from place to place.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.text: Q: Which instrument is blown to make a loud call? A: A horn.
chunks.source: A horn.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.text: Q: What is a signal? A: A sign that carries information.
chunks.source: A sign that carries information.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.text: Q: Why did people use smoke signals? A: To warn of danger over long distances.
chunks.source: To warn of danger over long distances.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of an alarm in traditional times. A: A fast drum beat warning of attack.
chunks.source: A fast drum beat warning of attack.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.text: Q: Explain how a trumpet was used. A: It announced the chief's arrival.
chunks.source: It announced the chief's arrival.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: How People Long Ago Sent Messages
chunks.text: Q: Reasoning: If a village had no drum, what other traditional method could they use? A: They could use smoke or a horn.
chunks.source: They could use smoke or a horn.

chunks.id: L-P6-Social-Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.text: Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other. I can explain modern communication tools and their advantages and challenges. Modern communication tools like mobile phones, internet, radio, television, and post services connect people quickly but require infrastructure and skills. Keywords: telephone: a device for voice calls over wires; mobile phone: a portable phone that works without wires; radio: a device that receives broadcast sound; television: a device that shows moving pictures and sound; internet: a global network linking computers; letter: a written message sent by post; email: an electronic message sent via computer; post office: a place where letters and parcels are handled; telegram: a short message sent by telegraph; billboard: a large outdoor board for advertisements
chunks.source: Modern communication tools like mobile phones, internet, radio, television, and post services connect people quickly but require infrastructure and skills.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.text: Q: What is a mobile phone? A: A portable phone that works without wires.
chunks.source: A portable phone that works without wires.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.text: Q: How does a letter reach its destination? A: It goes to the post office, is sorted, transported, and delivered.
chunks.source: It goes to the post office, is sorted, transported, and delivered.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.text: Q: Name one advantage of the internet. A: Instant access to information and communication.
chunks.source: Instant access to information and communication.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.text: Q: What is a billboard used for? A: Large outdoor advertisements.
chunks.source: Large outdoor advertisements.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.text: Q: Which tool broadcasts sound to many listeners at once? A: Radio.
chunks.source: Radio.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.text: Q: What is the main challenge of television in rural areas? A: Need for electricity and signal.
chunks.source: Need for electricity and signal.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.text: Q: Explain how email differs from a telegram. A: Email is electronic and instant; telegram was a paid telegraph service.
chunks.source: Email is electronic and instant; telegram was a paid telegraph service.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Modern Ways of Talking to Each Other
chunks.text: Q: Reasoning: If the internet is down, which two tools could still send a message? A: Mobile phone (SMS) and radio announcement.
chunks.source: Mobile phone (SMS) and radio announcement.

chunks.id: L-P6-Social-Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.text: Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today. I can compare traditional and modern transport methods in East Africa. East Africa's transport mixes old ways like canoes and bicycles with modern roads, railways, air, water, and pipelines to move people and goods. Keywords: transport: the movement of people or goods from one place to another; road: a path for vehicles, bicycles, and walkers; railway: tracks for trains to carry passengers and goods; air: travel by aircraft through the sky; water: travel on lakes, rivers, or seas; canoe: a narrow boat paddled by hand; dhow: a traditional sailing vessel with lateen sails; bicycle: a two-wheeled vehicle powered by pedalling; aeroplane: a powered flying vehicle for passengers and cargo; pipeline: a pipe system for moving liquids or gas
chunks.source: East Africa's transport mixes old ways like canoes and bicycles with modern roads, railways, air, water, and pipelines to move people and goods.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.text: Q: What is transport? A: The movement of people or goods from one place to another.
chunks.source: The movement of people or goods from one place to another.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.text: Q: Name a traditional water vessel. A: A canoe or a dhow.
chunks.source: A canoe or a dhow.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.text: Q: What does a pipeline carry? A: Liquids or gas such as fuel.
chunks.source: Liquids or gas such as fuel.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.text: Q: Which transport is fastest for long distances? A: Air travel by aeroplane.
chunks.source: Air travel by aeroplane.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.text: Q: How does a bicycle help in rural areas? A: It carries people and goods on roads.
chunks.source: It carries people and goods on roads.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.text: Q: What is the role of a railway? A: To carry many passengers and heavy goods over land.
chunks.source: To carry many passengers and heavy goods over land.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of goods moved by water transport. A: Fish, timber, or cargo on ferries.
chunks.source: Fish, timber, or cargo on ferries.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Travelling in East Africa Long Ago and Today
chunks.text: Q: Reasoning: Why might a pipeline be better than trucks for fuel? A: It reduces road traffic, spills, and cost.
chunks.source: It reduces road traffic, spills, and cost.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Staying Safe on Our Roads. I can identify road dangers and explain safety rules and solutions. Road safety depends on drivers, passengers, and pedestrians obeying rules and using solutions like zebra crossings and speed bumps to prevent accidents. Keywords: traffic: the movement of vehicles and people on roads; accident: an unexpected event causing injury or damage; danger: a risk of harm; passenger: a person travelling in a vehicle; goods: items being transported; journey: a trip from one place to another; safety: freedom from danger; rules: official guidelines to follow; solution: a way to solve a problem; driver: the person operating a vehicle
chunks.source: Road safety depends on drivers, passengers, and pedestrians obeying rules and using solutions like zebra crossings and speed bumps to prevent accidents.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is traffic? A: The movement of vehicles and people on roads.
chunks.source: The movement of vehicles and people on roads.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define accident. A: An unexpected event causing injury or damage.
chunks.source: An unexpected event causing injury or damage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is danger present on roads? A: Speeding, ignoring rules, careless crossing.
chunks.source: Speeding, ignoring rules, careless crossing.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What must a passenger do for safety? A: Wear a seatbelt and stay seated.
chunks.source: Wear a seatbelt and stay seated.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of goods transport. A: A truck carrying maize to market.
chunks.source: A truck carrying maize to market.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What makes a journey safe? A: Following rules, using crossings, driver care.
chunks.source: Following rules, using crossings, driver care.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name a solution to speeding near schools. A: Speed bumps and clear signage.
chunks.source: Speed bumps and clear signage.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Reasoning: If a driver sees a child at the roadside, what should the driver do? A: Slow down, stop if needed, and let the child cross safely.
chunks.source: Slow down, stop if needed, and let the child cross safely.

chunks.id: L-P6-Social-Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.text: Foreigners Who Came to East Africa. I can explain who the first foreigners were, why they came, and what they did in East Africa. Explorers mapped the coast, missionaries brought religion and schools, and trade led to colonial rule. Keywords: explorer: a person who travels to unknown places to learn about them; missionary: a person sent to spread a religion; foreigner: someone from another country; journey: a long trip from one place to another; colonial: relating to a country controlling another territory; trade: buying and selling goods; religion: a system of faith and worship; coast: the land beside the sea; interior: the inland part of a country; map: a drawing that shows where places are
chunks.source: Explorers mapped the coast, missionaries brought religion and schools, and trade led to colonial rule.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Who was the first **explorer** to reach the East African **coast**? A: John Speke
chunks.source: John Speke

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What did the **explorer** draw to help later travellers? A: A **map** of the **interior**
chunks.source: A **map** of the **interior**

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Which **foreigner** came after the **explorer** to spread **religion**? A: A **missionary**
chunks.source: A **missionary**

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What goods were carried by **trade** caravans? A: Ivory and cloth
chunks.source: Ivory and cloth

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What period began after **trade** routes were established? A: **Colonial** rule
chunks.source: **Colonial** rule

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Why is it a common mistake to think **missionaries** arrived first? A: Because **explorers** mapped the **coast** before any **missionary** came.
chunks.source: Because **explorers** mapped the **coast** before any **missionary** came.

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Name one thing the **missionary** built. A: A school
chunks.source: A school

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.text: Q: What did the **colonial** government use the **map** for? A: To plan roads into the **interior**
chunks.source: To plan roads into the **interior**

chunks.id: LQ-P6-Social-Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.subject: Social
chunks.unit: Foreigners Who Came to East Africa
chunks.text: Q: Explain in your own words how a **journey** led to **colonial** control. A: The **explorer**'s **journey** produced a **map**, which enabled **trade** and later **colonial** administration.
chunks.source: The **explorer**'s **journey** produced a **map**, which enabled **trade** and later **colonial** administration.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Life Under Colonial Rule. I can describe how colonial rule worked, the hardships people faced, and how they resisted. Colonial rule imposed taxes and forced labour, leading to resistance and rebellion. Keywords: colonial rule: control of a territory by a foreign power; colony: a territory governed by another country; governor: the top official representing the colonial power; taxes: money people must pay to the government; labour: work, especially hard physical work; resistance: opposition to authority; rebellion: an armed uprising against rulers; settlement: areas where foreign settlers live; administration: the system of managing a colony; exploitation: using people or resources unfairly for profit
chunks.source: Colonial rule imposed taxes and forced labour, leading to resistance and rebellion.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a **colony**? A: A territory governed by another country
chunks.source: A territory governed by another country

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who was the top official in the **colonial administration**? A: The **governor**
chunks.source: The **governor**

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why did men have to do **labour** on railways? A: To earn cash to pay **taxes**
chunks.source: To earn cash to pay **taxes**

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one form of **resistance** used by Ugandans. A: Secret meetings and attacks on **colonial** posts
chunks.source: Secret meetings and attacks on **colonial** posts

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What was the 1900 **rebellion**? A: An armed uprising in the north against forced **labour** and high **taxes**
chunks.source: An armed uprising in the north against forced **labour** and high **taxes**

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **exploitation** mean in this context? A: Using people or resources unfairly for profit
chunks.source: Using people or resources unfairly for profit

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How did **settlement** affect local villagers? A: They were evicted from the best land
chunks.source: They were evicted from the best land

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of a worked step in tax collection. A: Chiefs count households, families sell crops to pay **taxes**
chunks.source: Chiefs count households, families sell crops to pay **taxes**

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain why **resistance** sometimes forced the **governor** to lower **taxes**. A: The **rebellion** showed the **administration** that high **taxes** caused unrest, so they reduced them.
chunks.source: The **rebellion** showed the **administration** that high **taxes** caused unrest, so they reduced them.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: The Struggle for Independence. I can explain how East African countries won independence and became republics. Political parties and leaders led a long struggle that won independence, created a republic, and gave the nation its flag and anthem. Keywords: independence: freedom from foreign control; struggle: a long effort to achieve a goal; leader: a person who guides others; political party: an organised group seeking power; republic: a country with an elected president; freedom: the right to act without oppression; president: the elected head of state in a republic; nation: a large group of people with a shared identity; flag: a symbol of a country; anthem: a patriotic song
chunks.source: Political parties and leaders led a long struggle that won independence, created a republic, and gave the nation its flag and anthem.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **independence** mean? A: Freedom from foreign control
chunks.source: Freedom from foreign control

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name one **political party** that fought for Uganda's **independence**. A: Uganda People's Congress
chunks.source: Uganda People's Congress

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who was a key **leader** in the **struggle**? A: Milton Obote
chunks.source: Milton Obote

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: When did Uganda become a **republic**? A: 1963

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the role of a **president** in a **republic**? A: Elected head of state
chunks.source: Elected head of state

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Describe the **flag** of Uganda. A: Black, yellow, and red horizontal stripes
chunks.source: Black, yellow, and red horizontal stripes

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the **anthem** used for? A: Sung at national events and school assemblies
chunks.source: Sung at national events and school assemblies

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain how a **political party** helped achieve **independence**. A: It organised rallies, petitions, and strikes to pressure the colonial government.
chunks.source: It organised rallies, petitions, and strikes to pressure the colonial government.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is it a common mistake to think **independence** brought immediate wealth? A: Because the new **republic** still had to build infrastructure and institutions.
chunks.source: Because the new **republic** still had to build infrastructure and institutions.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Citizens, Rights and Voting. I can explain what democracy means, the rights of a citizen, and how elections work in Uganda. Democracy gives citizens rights and responsibilities; the Electoral Commission runs fair elections where every vote counts. Keywords: democracy: government by the people through voting; citizen: a legal member of a country; citizenship: the status of being a citizen; rights: freedoms protected by law; election: a process where people choose leaders; vote: to cast a ballot for a candidate; electoral commission: the body that organises elections; ballot: the paper or electronic slip used to vote; responsibility: a duty to contribute to society; leader: a person chosen to guide others
chunks.source: Democracy gives citizens rights and responsibilities; the Electoral Commission runs fair elections where every vote counts.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define **democracy** in your own words. A: Government by the people through voting
chunks.source: Government by the people through voting

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **citizenship**? A: The status of being a legal member of a country
chunks.source: The status of being a legal member of a country

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List two **rights** of a Ugandan **citizen**. A: Free speech and free primary education
chunks.source: Free speech and free primary education

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the **electoral commission** responsible for? A: Organising elections and registering voters
chunks.source: Organising elections and registering voters

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How old must you be to **vote**? A: 18 years old
chunks.source: 18 years old

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a **ballot**? A: The paper or electronic slip used to cast a vote
chunks.source: The paper or electronic slip used to cast a vote

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of a **responsibility** of citizenship. A: Paying taxes
chunks.source: Paying taxes

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain why the **electoral commission** must be independent. A: To ensure fair elections without political interference
chunks.source: To ensure fair elections without political interference

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Describe one way you can participate in **democracy** besides voting. A: Join a community group or attend a local council meeting
chunks.source: Join a community group or attend a local council meeting

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Caring for Our Environment. I can explain how to use the environment sustainably in East Africa. Using the environment sustainably means meeting today's needs — farming, energy, water — while protecting nature so future generations in East Africa also have enough. Keywords: environment: all the natural things around us like land, water, air, plants and animals; afforestation: planting new forests where trees were cut down; tree planting: putting young trees in the ground to grow; farming: growing crops and keeping animals for food; energy: power used for cooking, lighting and machines; conservation: protecting natural resources so they last; sustainable: able to continue for a long time without harm; nature: the physical world including plants, animals, landscapes; protect: keep safe from harm or damage; community: people living together in one area
chunks.source: Using the environment sustainably means meeting today's needs — farming, energy, water — while protecting nature so future generations in East Africa also have enough.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define **environment** in your own words. A: All the natural things around us — land, water, air, plants and animals.
chunks.source: All the natural things around us — land, water, air, plants and animals.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is the difference between **afforestation** and **tree planting**? A: Afforestation is creating new forests on land that had none; tree planting is putting young trees in the ground anywhere.
chunks.source: Afforestation is creating new forests on land that had none; tree planting is putting young trees in the ground anywhere.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of **sustainable farming** methods. A: Crop rotation and leaving land fallow (or mulching, contour trenches, intercropping).
chunks.source: Crop rotation and leaving land fallow (or mulching, contour trenches, intercropping).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is cutting trees for firewood not **sustainable**? A: Trees take years to grow but are cut in minutes; the forest disappears faster than it regrows.
chunks.source: Trees take years to grow but are cut in minutes; the forest disappears faster than it regrows.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Name three **alternative energy** sources used in Uganda. A: Solar power, biogas, energy-saving stoves (or hydroelectricity, wind).
chunks.source: Solar power, biogas, energy-saving stoves (or hydroelectricity, wind).

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does **conservation** farming **protect** the soil? A: Trenches and mulch stop rain from washing or blowing away the topsoil.
chunks.source: Trenches and mulch stop rain from washing or blowing away the topsoil.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: If a **community** plants 500 trees but 200 die, what should they do? A: Replace the dead seedlings, mulch better, and water during dry spells — that is **sustainable** management.
chunks.source: Replace the dead seedlings, mulch better, and water during dry spells — that is **sustainable** management.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Reasoning: A farmer says, 'I cannot afford to leave land fallow; I need every harvest.' What would you tell him? A: Model answer: 'Leaving land fallow for one season or planting a cover crop like mucuna restores nutrients. The next harvest will be bigger, so you gain more in the long run.'
chunks.source: Model answer: 'Leaving land fallow for one season or planting a cover crop like mucuna restores nutrients. The next harvest will be bigger, so you gain more in the long run.'

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Managing Waste Properly. I can describe proper waste management and the role of NEMA in Uganda. Proper waste management — separating **rubbish**, composting, **recycling**, safe **sewage** and **disposal** — keeps our communities **clean** and protects **health**; **NEMA** guides and enforces the rules nationwide. Keywords: waste: unwanted materials thrown away after use; litter: waste dropped carelessly on the ground; rubbish: dry waste like paper, plastic, bottles and cans; polythene: thin plastic bags that do not rot easily; recycling: turning used materials into new products; sewage: liquid waste from toilets and drains; disposal: the act of getting rid of waste safely; dustbin: a container with a lid for holding waste; clean: free from dirt, waste or germs; health: the condition of being well in body and mind
chunks.source: Proper waste management — separating **rubbish**, composting, **recycling**, safe **sewage** and **disposal** — keeps our communities **clean** and protects **health**; **NEMA** guides and enforces the rules nationwide.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define **waste**. A: Unwanted materials thrown away after use.
chunks.source: Unwanted materials thrown away after use.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **litter**? A: Waste dropped carelessly on the ground instead of in a bin.
chunks.source: Waste dropped carelessly on the ground instead of in a bin.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is **polythene** a special problem? A: It does not rot, blocks drains, and burning it releases toxic smoke.
chunks.source: It does not rot, blocks drains, and burning it releases toxic smoke.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain **recycling** with one example from Uganda. A: Turning used plastic bottles into ropes or pellets for new products.
chunks.source: Turning used plastic bottles into ropes or pellets for new products.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is **sewage** and why must it be managed? A: Liquid waste from toilets and drains; if untreated it contaminates water sources and causes disease.
chunks.source: Liquid waste from toilets and drains; if untreated it contaminates water sources and causes disease.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Describe safe **disposal** of household **rubbish** in a village. A: Use a covered pit away from the borehole, or a community collection point managed by the local council.
chunks.source: Use a covered pit away from the borehole, or a community collection point managed by the local council.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **NEMA** do? A: Sets national environmental standards, inspects polluters, fines illegal dumpers, and guides districts on waste management.
chunks.source: Sets national environmental standards, inspects polluters, fines illegal dumpers, and guides districts on waste management.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does separating waste at home improve **health**? A: Less **litter** means fewer flies and mosquitoes; compost enriches the garden; recyclers earn income.
chunks.source: Less **litter** means fewer flies and mosquitoes; compost enriches the garden; recyclers earn income.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Reasoning: A shopkeeper says, 'NEMA fines are just harassment.' What would you reply? A: Model answer: 'NEMA fines protect everyone. When factories dump poison in the river, fish die and people get sick. The fine pays for cleanup and forces the factory to treat its waste.'
chunks.source: Model answer: 'NEMA fines protect everyone. When factories dump poison in the river, fish die and people get sick. The fine pays for cleanup and forces the factory to treat its waste.'

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: When People Harm the Environment. I can explain the consequences of irresponsible environmental actions in East Africa. **Irresponsible** actions — cutting trees, overgrazing, dumping waste, burning plastic — cause **flood**, **landslide**, **desertification**, **pollution**, **disease**, **erosion** and worsen **drought** and **climate change**; the **damage** hurts everyone. Keywords: flood: overflow of water onto normally dry land; landslide: sudden movement of soil and rock down a slope; desertification: fertile land turning into desert because of misuse; pollution: harmful substances added to air, water or soil; disease: illness caused by germs or unhealthy conditions; drought: long period with little or no rain; climate change: long-term shifts in temperature and weather patterns; erosion: wearing away of topsoil by wind or rain; irresponsible: not caring about the results of one's actions; damage: harm that makes something less valuable or useful
chunks.source: **Irresponsible** actions — cutting trees, overgrazing, dumping waste, burning plastic — cause **flood**, **landslide**, **desertification**, **pollution**, **disease**, **erosion** and worsen **drought** and **climate change**; the **damage** hurts everyone.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define **flood**. A: Overflow of water onto normally dry land.
chunks.source: Overflow of water onto normally dry land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What causes a **landslide**? A: Heavy rain on steep slopes where trees have been removed; soil slides downhill.
chunks.source: Heavy rain on steep slopes where trees have been removed; soil slides downhill.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Explain **desertification** in one sentence. A: Fertile land turning into desert because of human misuse like overgrazing and deforestation.
chunks.source: Fertile land turning into desert because of human misuse like overgrazing and deforestation.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give two examples of **pollution** in your district. A: Factory waste in the stream; burning **polythene** smoke; oil from boda bodas in roadside puddles.
chunks.source: Factory waste in the stream; burning **polythene** smoke; oil from boda bodas in roadside puddles.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does **erosion** affect a farmer's garden? A: Topsoil is lost, crops yield less, gullies make cultivation hard.
chunks.source: Topsoil is lost, crops yield less, gullies make cultivation hard.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why is **climate change** a concern for Ugandan farmers? A: Rains become unpredictable — longer **drought**s and heavier storms ruin planting seasons.
chunks.source: Rains become unpredictable — longer **drought**s and heavier storms ruin planting seasons.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What does **irresponsible** mean in environmental care? A: Acting without thinking of the harm to land, water, air or future generations.
chunks.source: Acting without thinking of the harm to land, water, air or future generations.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: List three types of **damage** caused by poor waste disposal. A: Blocked drains causing **flood**s; contaminated borehole water causing **disease**; lost soil fertility from **erosion**.
chunks.source: Blocked drains causing **flood**s; contaminated borehole water causing **disease**; lost soil fertility from **erosion**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Reasoning: A leader says, 'We cannot stop **climate change**, so why bother planting trees?' What would you answer? A: Model answer: 'Trees reduce **erosion**, give shade, absorb carbon, and bring rain locally. We cannot fix the whole world, but we can protect our own hills and gardens. Every tree counts.'
chunks.source: Model answer: 'Trees reduce **erosion**, give shade, absorb carbon, and bring rain locally. We cannot fix the whole world, but we can protect our own hills and gardens. Every tree counts.'

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Living Responsibly Every Day. I can propose solutions and responsible actions that protect the environment in East Africa. **Responsible** living means turning **solutions** into daily **action** — **campaign**s, **volunteer** work, **care** and **respect** for nature — so the **community** secures a healthy **future** for the next **generation**. Keywords: responsible: acting with care for consequences on others and nature; solution: a way to solve a problem; campaign: organised effort to promote a cause; volunteer: person who offers time and effort without pay; care: look after something with attention; respect: treat something as valuable and important; future: the time that is yet to come; generation: all people born and living at about the same time; community: people living together in one area; action: something done to achieve a result
chunks.source: **Responsible** living means turning **solutions** into daily **action** — **campaign**s, **volunteer** work, **care** and **respect** for nature — so the **community** secures a healthy **future** for the next **generation**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Define **responsible** in the context of the environment. A: Acting with care for the consequences of your actions on nature and other people.
chunks.source: Acting with care for the consequences of your actions on nature and other people.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What is a **solution** to the problem of **polythene** bags? A: Use reusable cloth bags; support the ban on single-use bags; recycle old bags.
chunks.source: Use reusable cloth bags; support the ban on single-use bags; recycle old bags.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Describe a **campaign** you could run at school. A: Example: 'Bring Your Own Bottle' week with posters, a class challenge, and a **volunteer** team to check compliance.
chunks.source: Example: 'Bring Your Own Bottle' week with posters, a class challenge, and a **volunteer** team to check compliance.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Who is a **volunteer**? A: A person who gives time and effort without pay for a cause.
chunks.source: A person who gives time and effort without pay for a cause.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: How does **care** for the school compound show **respect**? A: Picking up **litter**, not stepping on grass, watering trees — all show the place is valued.
chunks.source: Picking up **litter**, not stepping on grass, watering trees — all show the place is valued.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Why must we think of the **future** **generation** when we use resources? A: What we use now will not be there for them unless we manage it **sustainably**.
chunks.source: What we use now will not be there for them unless we manage it **sustainably**.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Give an example of a **community** **action** that protects the environment. A: Village by-law requiring **dustbin**s and compost pits; collective tree planting on public land.
chunks.source: Village by-law requiring **dustbin**s and compost pits; collective tree planting on public land.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: What small daily **action** reduces **waste** most? A: Refusing single-use plastic, carrying a reusable bottle and bag, composting food scraps.
chunks.source: Refusing single-use plastic, carrying a reusable bottle and bag, composting food scraps.

chunks.subject: Social
chunks.text: Q: Reasoning: A friend says, 'My **action** alone cannot change anything.' How do you respond? A: Model answer: 'One person inspires another. The **community** is made of individuals. If everyone thinks that way, nothing changes. Your **action** starts the ripple.'
chunks.source: Model answer: 'One person inspires another. The **community** is made of individuals. If everyone thinks that way, nothing changes. Your **action** starts the ripple.'

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Planning My Holiday. I can use 'going to' to talk about my future holiday plans. Amina makes a plan, uses 'going to' for future actions, and enjoys her vacation with relatives. Keywords: plan: a list of things you will do; vacation: a long break from school; journey: a trip from one place to another; visit: to go and see someone; trip: a short journey for a purpose; relative: a family member; relax: to rest and feel calm; scenery: the natural view around you
chunks.source: Amina makes a plan, uses 'going to' for future actions, and enjoys her vacation with relatives.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the sentence: Amina ____ visit her aunt next week. A: Answer: is going to. Reason: 'going to' shows a planned future action.
chunks.source: Answer: is going to. Reason: 'going to' shows a planned future action.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct form: We ____ travel by bus tomorrow. A: Answer: are going to. Reason: plural subject 'we' needs 'are going to'.
chunks.source: Answer: are going to. Reason: plural subject 'we' needs 'are going to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word means 'a long break from school'? A: Answer: vacation. Reason: matches the definition.
chunks.source: Answer: vacation. Reason: matches the definition.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in the blank: The ____ to Jinja takes three hours. A: Answer: journey. Reason: journey means a trip from one place to another.
chunks.source: Answer: journey. Reason: journey means a trip from one place to another.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Select the past tense of 'plan' used in a future sense: ____ A: Answer: planned (but future uses 'going to plan'). Reason: the lesson focuses on 'going to' not past.
chunks.source: Answer: planned (but future uses 'going to plan'). Reason: the lesson focuses on 'going to' not past.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does 'relax' mean? A: Answer: to rest and feel calm. Reason: definition from the lesson.
chunks.source: Answer: to rest and feel calm. Reason: definition from the lesson.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write one sentence using 'going to' and the word 'scenery'. A: Answer: I am going to enjoy the scenery on the journey. Reason: uses target structure and word.
chunks.source: Answer: I am going to enjoy the scenery on the journey. Reason: uses target structure and word.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Identify the error: 'She will going to relax.' A: Answer: Remove 'will'. Reason: 'will going to' is incorrect; use 'is going to'.
chunks.source: Answer: Remove 'will'. Reason: 'will going to' is incorrect; use 'is going to'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Holiday Activities. I can narrate past holiday activities using regular and irregular past tense verbs. Kato narrated his holiday using past tense verbs for swimming, fishing, football, games, reading, helping, chores, and stories. Keywords: swimming: moving in water; fishing: catching fish; football: a game played with a ball; games: activities for fun; reading: looking at books; helping: assisting someone; chores: small jobs at home; stories: tales told or read
chunks.source: Kato narrated his holiday using past tense verbs for swimming, fishing, football, games, reading, helping, chores, and stories.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Change to past tense: I ____ (go) swimming yesterday. A: Answer: went. Reason: irregular verb go → went.
chunks.source: Answer: went. Reason: irregular verb go → went.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct past form: She ____ (catch) a fish. A: Answer: caught. Reason: catch → caught.
chunks.source: Answer: caught. Reason: catch → caught.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in: We ____ (play) football every evening. A: Answer: played. Reason: regular verb adds -ed.
chunks.source: Answer: played. Reason: regular verb adds -ed.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Identify the error: 'He readed a book.' A: Answer: read. Reason: read is irregular, past stays read.
chunks.source: Answer: read. Reason: read is irregular, past stays read.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence in past tense using 'stories'. A: Answer: Grandfather told us stories. Reason: past tense 'told' and target word.
chunks.source: Answer: Grandfather told us stories. Reason: past tense 'told' and target word.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the past of 'help'? A: Answer: helped. Reason: regular verb.
chunks.source: Answer: helped. Reason: regular verb.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Select the irregular past verb: a) walked b) swam c) jumped A: Answer: swam. Reason: swim → swam.
chunks.source: Answer: swam. Reason: swim → swam.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: They ____ (do) chores before playing. A: Answer: did. Reason: do → did.
chunks.source: Answer: did. Reason: do → did.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Telling Others About My Holiday. I can sequence a holiday account using first, then, after that, finally. Nalongo used first, then, after that, finally to structure her holiday account in her diary. Keywords: diary: a book for personal notes; photograph: a picture taken with a camera; memory: something you remember; excited: feeling very happy and eager; suddenly: quickly and without warning; finally: at the end; adventure: an exciting experience; experience: something you live through
chunks.source: Nalongo used first, then, after that, finally to structure her holiday account in her diary.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Put the sequencing words in order: finally, first, then, after that. A: Answer: first, then, after that, finally. Reason: correct chronological order.
chunks.source: Answer: first, then, after that, finally. Reason: correct chronological order.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the word that means 'quickly and without warning': A: Answer: suddenly. Reason: definition matches.
chunks.source: Answer: suddenly. Reason: definition matches.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in: ____ I arrived, I unpacked my bag. A: Answer: Finally. Reason: indicates the last event.
chunks.source: Answer: Finally. Reason: indicates the last event.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a sentence using 'diary' and 'memory'. A: Answer: I keep a diary to save every memory. Reason: uses both target words.
chunks.source: Answer: I keep a diary to save every memory. Reason: uses both target words.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Identify the sequencing word in: 'Then we went swimming.' A: Answer: Then. Reason: shows next step.
chunks.source: Answer: Then. Reason: shows next step.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does 'excited' mean? A: Answer: feeling very happy and eager. Reason: definition.
chunks.source: Answer: feeling very happy and eager. Reason: definition.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: The trip was an ____ I will never forget. A: Answer: adventure. Reason: adventure = exciting experience.
chunks.source: Answer: adventure. Reason: adventure = exciting experience.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Select the past tense verb that fits: She ____ (write) in her diary. A: Answer: wrote. Reason: irregular past of write.
chunks.source: Answer: wrote. Reason: irregular past of write.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: If I Had Planned Better. I can express regrets about the past using the third conditional. Musa learns to use the third conditional to express regrets: if he had saved and prepared early, he would not have missed the trip. Keywords: regret: feeling sorry about something; save: keep money for later; spend: use money; waste: use carelessly; prepare: get ready; early: before the usual time; late: after the usual time; miss: fail to catch or do
chunks.source: Musa learns to use the third conditional to express regrets: if he had saved and prepared early, he would not have missed the trip.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete the third conditional: If she ____ (study), she would have passed. A: Answer: had studied. Reason: past perfect after 'if'.
chunks.source: Answer: had studied. Reason: past perfect after 'if'.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Choose the correct form: If we ____ (leave) early, we would have caught the bus. A: Answer: had left. Reason: past perfect needed.
chunks.source: Answer: had left. Reason: past perfect needed.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Identify the error: 'If I had went, I would have seen him.' A: Answer: had gone. Reason: past participle of go is gone.
chunks.source: Answer: had gone. Reason: past participle of go is gone.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Write a regret sentence using 'regret' and 'save'. A: Answer: I regret that I did not save money. Reason: uses target words.
chunks.source: Answer: I regret that I did not save money. Reason: uses target words.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Fill in: He ____ (spend) all his money, so he missed the trip. A: Answer: spent. Reason: past simple for real past action.
chunks.source: Answer: spent. Reason: past simple for real past action.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does 'waste' mean? A: Answer: use carelessly. Reason: definition.
chunks.source: Answer: use carelessly. Reason: definition.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Select the third conditional: a) If I go, I will see. b) If I had gone, I would have seen. c) If I went, I would see. A: Answer: b. Reason: matches third conditional structure.
chunks.source: Answer: b. Reason: matches third conditional structure.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Complete: If they ____ (prepare) early, they ____ (not miss) the train. A: Answer: had prepared / would not have missed. Reason: both clauses in third conditional.
chunks.source: Answer: had prepared / would not have missed. Reason: both clauses in third conditional.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Parts of a Formal Letter. I can identify and arrange the parts of a formal letter. A formal letter has the sender's address, date, receiver's address, salutation, body, closing and signature. Keywords: address: the place where someone lives or works; sender: the person who writes the letter; receiver: the person who gets the letter; salutation: the greeting at the start of a letter; signature: your signed name at the end of a letter; formal: official and polite in style; heading: the top part with addresses and date; date: the day, month and year
chunks.source: A formal letter has the sender's address, date, receiver's address, salutation, body, closing and signature.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which part of a formal letter comes first? A: The sender's address. Reason: It identifies the writer.
chunks.source: The sender's address. Reason: It identifies the writer.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What follows the sender's address? A: The date. Reason: The date shows when the letter was written.
chunks.source: The date. Reason: The date shows when the letter was written.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where is the receiver's address placed? A: On the left, below the sender's address. Reason: Formal letters use left margin for receiver.
chunks.source: On the left, below the sender's address. Reason: Formal letters use left margin for receiver.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the salutation in a formal letter when the name is unknown? A: Dear Sir, or Dear Madam,. Reason: It is the standard formal greeting.
chunks.source: Dear Sir, or Dear Madam,. Reason: It is the standard formal greeting.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which closing is used when you do not know the receiver's name? A: Yours faithfully,. Reason: Yours faithfully matches an unknown recipient.
chunks.source: Yours faithfully,. Reason: Yours faithfully matches an unknown recipient.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does the heading of a formal letter include? A: Sender's address, date, receiver's address, and salutation. Reason: These four parts form the heading.
chunks.source: Sender's address, date, receiver's address, and salutation. Reason: These four parts form the heading.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the purpose of the signature? A: To show who wrote the letter. Reason: The signature authenticates the letter.
chunks.source: To show who wrote the letter. Reason: The signature authenticates the letter.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is the layout of a formal letter important? A: It makes the letter clear and professional. Reason: Proper layout helps the receiver read easily.
chunks.source: It makes the letter clear and professional. Reason: Proper layout helps the receiver read easily.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Writing a Formal Letter. I can write a formal application letter with correct tone and structure. An application letter states the vacancy, your qualification, experience, reference, and closes with Yours faithfully. Keywords: application: a formal request for a job or place; request: asking for something politely; apply: to make a formal request; post: a job or position; vacancy: an empty job position; qualification: a skill or certificate that makes you suitable; experience: knowledge gained from doing a job; reference: a person who can tell about your character or work
chunks.source: An application letter states the vacancy, your qualification, experience, reference, and closes with Yours faithfully.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the purpose of an application letter? A: To apply for a vacancy. Reason: It shows interest in a post.
chunks.source: To apply for a vacancy. Reason: It shows interest in a post.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which word means a job opening? A: Vacancy. Reason: Vacancy refers to an available position.
chunks.source: Vacancy. Reason: Vacancy refers to an available position.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What should you include about your background? A: Qualification and experience. Reason: They prove you can do the job.
chunks.source: Qualification and experience. Reason: They prove you can do the job.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which phrase is formal for 'I want to apply'? A: I am writing to apply. Reason: It uses formal structure.
chunks.source: I am writing to apply. Reason: It uses formal structure.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a reference in a letter? A: A person who can vouch for you. Reason: Employers contact references.
chunks.source: A person who can vouch for you. Reason: Employers contact references.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which closing is correct for an application to an unknown person? A: Yours faithfully,. Reason: Used when recipient name unknown.
chunks.source: Yours faithfully,. Reason: Used when recipient name unknown.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does 'post' mean in this context? A: To send by mail. Reason: You post the letter at the post office.
chunks.source: To send by mail. Reason: You post the letter at the post office.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is formal tone important? A: It shows respect and professionalism. Reason: Formal tone meets employer expectations.
chunks.source: It shows respect and professionalism. Reason: Formal tone meets employer expectations.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Writing an Informal Letter. I can write an informal letter to a friend or relative with a friendly tone. Informal letters use friendly greetings, personal news, and are sent in an envelope with a stamp or as a postcard. Keywords: informal: not official; relaxed and personal; postcard: a card with a picture sent without an envelope; message: a short written communication; envelope: a paper cover for a letter; stamp: a small sticker that pays for postage; greetings: friendly words at the start of a letter; friendly: kind and warm in manner; news: information about recent events
chunks.source: Informal letters use friendly greetings, personal news, and are sent in an envelope with a stamp or as a postcard.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is an informal letter? A: A letter to friends or relatives with a friendly tone. Reason: It uses personal language.
chunks.source: A letter to friends or relatives with a friendly tone. Reason: It uses personal language.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What do you put on an envelope? A: Stamp and address. Reason: The stamp pays for delivery.
chunks.source: Stamp and address. Reason: The stamp pays for delivery.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is a postcard? A: A card with a picture and short message sent without an envelope. Reason: It is cheaper and quicker.
chunks.source: A card with a picture and short message sent without an envelope. Reason: It is cheaper and quicker.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Which greeting is friendly? A: Hi Nalongo, how are you? Reason: It is casual and warm.
chunks.source: Hi Nalongo, how are you? Reason: It is casual and warm.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where do you write the message in a postcard? A: On the back of the card. Reason: The front has the picture.
chunks.source: On the back of the card. Reason: The front has the picture.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does 'news' mean in a letter? A: Updates about your life. Reason: Friends share news.
chunks.source: Updates about your life. Reason: Friends share news.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is a stamp needed? A: To pay for postage. Reason: Without a stamp, the post office will not deliver.
chunks.source: To pay for postage. Reason: Without a stamp, the post office will not deliver.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the difference between formal and informal letters? A: Formal letters are official; informal letters are personal. Reason: Tone and layout differ.
chunks.source: Formal letters are official; informal letters are personal. Reason: Tone and layout differ.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Addressing and Posting a Letter. I can address an envelope correctly using abbreviations and post it. Use abbreviations like P.O. Box and c/o, seal the envelope, and post it at the post office for delivery. Keywords: abbreviation: a shortened form of a word; post office: a place where mail is sent and received; mail: letters and parcels sent by post; deliver: to bring something to the receiver; seal: to close an envelope securely; sort: to arrange mail by destination; collect: to pick up something; box: a container for mail at the post office
chunks.source: Use abbreviations like P.O. Box and c/o, seal the envelope, and post it at the post office for delivery.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does P.O. Box stand for? A: Post Office Box. Reason: It is the standard abbreviation.
chunks.source: Post Office Box. Reason: It is the standard abbreviation.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What does c/o mean? A: Care of. Reason: It shows the letter is for someone at another address.
chunks.source: Care of. Reason: It shows the letter is for someone at another address.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What must you do to an envelope before posting? A: Seal it. Reason: To keep the letter secure.
chunks.source: Seal it. Reason: To keep the letter secure.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Where is mail sorted? A: At the sorting centre. Reason: Letters are sorted by destination.
chunks.source: At the sorting centre. Reason: Letters are sorted by destination.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who delivers the mail? A: The postman delivers. Reason: Postmen bring mail to boxes.
chunks.source: The postman delivers. Reason: Postmen bring mail to boxes.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Who collects the letter from the box? A: The receiver. Reason: The receiver picks up mail from their box.
chunks.source: The receiver. Reason: The receiver picks up mail from their box.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is an abbreviation? A: A shortened form of a word. Reason: P.O. Box is an abbreviation.
chunks.source: A shortened form of a word. Reason: P.O. Box is an abbreviation.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: Why is correct addressing important? A: So the letter reaches the right person. Reason: Wrong address causes delays.
chunks.source: So the letter reaches the right person. Reason: Wrong address causes delays.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Preparing for Examinations. I can explain how to prepare well for examinations using a timetable, revision, notes and goals. Good preparation with a timetable, regular revision, clear goals and a solid plan leads to success in examinations. Keywords: preparation: getting ready; revision: studying again; candidate: person taking exam; timetable: schedule of study; success: achieving goal; notes: short written points; goal: aim; plan: method to achieve goal
chunks.source: Good preparation with a timetable, regular revision, clear goals and a solid plan leads to success in examinations.

chunks.subject: English
chunks.text: Q: What is the first step in good **preparation** for PLE? A: Write a **timetable** – it organises study time.
